abstract: A musical instrument for electronically producing music from audio segments. The musical instrument comprises: an apparatus having a first surface; a plurality of selectable elements disposed in a substantially circular geometry on the first surface; and at least one memory storing the plurality of audio segments, each of the plurality of audio segments being associated with a respective selectable element in the plurality of selectable elements, wherein, in response to detecting selection of a subset of the plurality of selectable elements, the system is configured to generate music using audio segments in the plurality of audio segments that are associated with the selected subset of the plurality of selectable elements.
reason: The patent describes a musical instrument with a circular arrangement of selectable elements and audio segments, but the mechanism is a direct input-output mapping (selecting elements triggers associated audio). This is a feature or interface design rather than a causal functional principle that solves a broader problem.

abstract: An apparatus for a hearing device includes a first voltage regulator with an output terminal; a first voltage reference; a second voltage regulator with an output terminal; a switching element; and a decoupling element; wherein the switching element and the decoupling element are operatively between the first voltage reference and the first voltage regulator; wherein the output terminal of the first voltage regulator shares a same electrical node as the output terminal of the second voltage regulator; and wherein the first voltage regulator is configured to provide a first output voltage in response to applied battery power, the second voltage regulator is configured to provide a second output voltage if a certain condition is fulfilled, and the switching element is configured to disconnect the first voltage reference from the decoupling element if the condition is fulfilled.
problem: Managing power supply to different components in a hearing device while ensuring stable voltage outputs under varying conditions.
constraint: Balancing power delivery between two regulators while maintaining electrical isolation and avoiding interference between the first and second voltage outputs.
mechanism: A conditional disconnector selectively isolates a first power regulation path from a reference element when a threshold condition is detected, enabling a second regulation path to assume control and deliver a distinct output. This establishes a dynamic power routing architecture that transitions between regulation modes based on operational demands while preserving isolation between outputs.
mechanism_raw: A switching element conditionally disconnects a voltage reference from a decoupling element when a specific condition is met, allowing a second voltage regulator to take over and provide a different output voltage. This creates a dynamic power routing system that adapts to operational states.

abstract: A tool for inserting a flame arrestor assembly into a process control device having a first passageway of a first depth and a second passageway of a second depth different from the first depth. The tool includes a head portion having a first diameter, and a tip portion having a second diameter less than the first diameter. The tip portion has a first portion, a second portion, and a third portion, the first and second portions being separated by a first notch, and the second and third portions being separated by a second notch. The first notch is arranged to indicate when the flame arrestor assembly is fully inserted into the first passageway, and the second notch is arranged to indicate when the flame arrestor assembly is fully inserted into the second passageway.
problem: Ensuring proper insertion depth of a flame arrestor into process control devices with passageways of differing depths.
constraint: Designing notches at precise positions to correspond to different passageway depths while maintaining structural integrity of the tool.
mechanism: A positioning tool incorporates spaced indicators along its length that align with target insertion depths of a component. Physical interaction between the tool and the component generates tactile or visual feedback when the component reaches full insertion at each depth, ensuring proper engagement without over-insertion.
mechanism_raw: A tool with a tip portion containing notches positioned to physically indicate when the flame arrestor is fully inserted into each passageway. The notches act as tactile/visual feedback mechanisms triggered by the physical interaction between the tool and the device.

abstract: A printer management system includes one or more printing devices having a printing area for printing according to a digital file, an access area through which a user may access the printing area, and a locking mechanism configured to lock the access area preventing access to the printing area. A management server is communicatively coupled to the one or more printing devices over a communication network and is configured to receive a print request from one or more user devices or one of the one or more printing devices to print the digital file, transmit the digital file to one of the one or more printing devices, and transmit commands to lock and unlock the locking mechanism of the one or more printing devices. In one embodiment the management system is configured to update a printing status of each of the one or more printing devices.
problem: Coordinating access control and status monitoring across multiple printing devices in a networked environment.
constraint: Synchronizing lock/unlock commands and status updates across multiple devices over a communication network without delays or conflicts.
mechanism: A central coordinator receives requests from distributed endpoints, transmits data to selected endpoints, and issues commands to actuate access control mechanisms on those endpoints. The coordinator also monitors and updates endpoint states, creating a synchronized system for managing access and status across networked hardware.
mechanism_raw: A centralized management server receives print requests, transmits digital files to devices, and remotely controls locking mechanisms to restrict or grant access. The server also updates device statuses, creating a unified system for managing distributed hardware.

abstract: A system for simultaneously supplying compressed air to the personal breathing apparatus of a firefighter and to an internal combustion engine appliance, such as a chainsaw. The supply of air intake of the chainsaw is provided by means of an adapter which is configured to attach to both the air intake of the chainsaw and to a demand valve-type regulator.
problem: Simultaneously supplying compressed air to two devices (breathing apparatus and chainsaw) with potentially varying demand levels.
constraint: Ensuring the air supply can meet peak demand from both devices simultaneously while preventing pressure imbalances or flow interference.
mechanism: A shared resource distributor dynamically allocates flow from a single source to multiple consumers by adjusting delivery rates in response to real-time demand from each consumer. This prevents pressure imbalances and ensures peak demand from all consumers is met without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: An adapter connects a single compressed air source to both devices via a demand valve-type regulator, which dynamically adjusts airflow based on the instantaneous needs of each device. This allows shared resource utilization without manual intervention.

abstract: A robot includes a joint and a drive mechanism disposed in the joint. A reducer includes an output shaft and a fixed portion. A first seal seals a gap between the output shaft and the fixed portion. A first cover is fixed to the fixed portion and covers an outer surface of the fixed portion. An intermediate portion is fixed to an output-side portion of the output shaft. A second cover is fixed to an output-side portion of the intermediate portion and covers an outer surface and an output-side edge of the first cover. A second seal seals a gap between the first cover and the intermediate portion. A groove extends approximately over a circumference of the outer surface of the first cover.
problem: Protecting a robot joint's internal components from contamination and wear while maintaining rotational movement.
constraint: Balancing contamination protection with the need for unimpeded rotational movement and structural integrity in a compact joint space.
mechanism: Multi-stage barrier system: A first flexible interface isolates relative motion between a rotating component and a stationary base, while a second flexible interface isolates motion between a fixed enclosure and an intermediate structure. Overlapping protective layers and a circumferential channel form a tortuous path barrier to block contaminant ingress while permitting rotational movement.
mechanism_raw: Layered sealing and covering system: A first seal isolates the gap between a rotating output shaft and a fixed portion, while a second seal isolates the gap between a fixed cover and an intermediate component. Overlapping covers and a circumferential groove create a labyrinth-like barrier to block contaminants while allowing motion.

abstract: The encapsulated sustained release urea fertilizer is a urea fertilizer and a stabilizer encapsulated in fumed silica. The stabilizer may be a gellan gum hydrogel or biochar. The encapsulated sustained release urea fertilizer allows for both immediate and sustained nitrogen release over time and displays reduced nitrogen volatilization and increased water holding capacity.
problem: Achieving controlled, sustained release of nitrogen from urea fertilizer while minimizing volatilization and improving water retention.
constraint: Maintaining structural stability of the encapsulated matrix while enabling both immediate and prolonged nutrient release without compromising agricultural efficacy.
mechanism: Porous matrix encapsulation: A rigid, high-surface-area scaffold physically entraps a nutrient source and a retention agent, creating controlled diffusion pathways that regulate release kinetics and minimize gaseous loss through physical confinement and selective permeability.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulation in a porous matrix: Fumed silica forms a rigid, high-surface-area scaffold that physically traps urea and a stabilizer (e.g., gellan gum or biochar), creating diffusion pathways that regulate release kinetics and reduce gaseous loss.

abstract: A Dust Mitigation System (“DMS”) is disclosed that includes a fabric-material having a front-surface and a back-surface; a plurality of conductive-fibers within the fabric-material; and a plurality of input-nodes approximately adjacent to the back-surface or the front-surface of the fabric-material. The plurality of conductive-fibers are approximately parallel in a first direction along the fabric-material and are approximately adjacent to the front-surface of the fabric-material and the plurality of input-nodes are in signal communication with the plurality of conductive-fibers and configured to receive an alternating-current (“AC”) voltage-signal from an input-signal-source. The plurality of conductive-fibers are configured to generate an electric-field on the front-surface of the fabric-material in response to the plurality of input-nodes receiving the AC voltage-signal from the input-signal-source and a traveling-wave (from the electric-field) that travels along the front-surface of the fabric-material in a second direction that is transverse to the first direction.
problem: Removing or mitigating dust accumulation on a surface without physical contact or airflow.
constraint: Optimizing fiber orientation and AC frequency to produce a coherent traveling wave while minimizing power consumption and ensuring uniform field distribution across the surface.
mechanism: Electrodynamic traveling-wave actuation: Conductive elements arranged in a pattern generate a propagating electric field when energized, creating a moving electrostatic force field that levitates and transports particulate matter along a surface without mechanical contact.
mechanism_raw: Electrodynamic traveling-wave actuation: Conductive fibers embedded in a fabric generate a transverse electric field when supplied with an AC signal, creating a traveling wave that induces electrostatic forces to levitate and transport dust particles along the surface.

abstract: An aircraft rotor mast assembly that includes a composite rotor mast and a rotor housing surrounding the rotor mast. The rotor mast includes a first end, a second end, and a length therebetween. The rotor mast includes a plurality of circular openings proximate the first end to accommodate bolts for the fixation of a rotor hub to the rotor mast. The second end of the rotor mast includes a flange, wherein the flange defines a plurality of openings therethrough to accommodate the attachment of the rotor mast to a transmission.
problem: Attaching a rotor hub and transmission to a rotor mast while maintaining structural strength and minimizing weight in aerospace applications.
constraint: Balancing mechanical load-bearing capacity with weight reduction and ensuring precise alignment between the rotor hub, mast, and transmission under dynamic rotational forces.
mechanism: Material-geometry co-design: A lightweight structural component uses strategically placed apertures for mechanical coupling at one end and a flanged interface with aligned apertures at the other end, leveraging material properties and load-path optimization to balance strength and mass.
mechanism_raw: Strategic material and geometry integration: A composite rotor mast uses circular openings near the hub end for bolt fixation and a flanged second end with aligned openings for transmission attachment, leveraging composite materials' strength-to-weight ratio and tailored load paths.

abstract: A needle assembly for use in carpeting includes a handle having a first longitudinal axis running from a forward end to a rear end, a shaft section running along the first longitudinal axis with a first portion having a first outer diameter and a second portion, where the second portion has a second outer diameter representing a maximal outer diameter of the second portion, and the second outer diameter is less than the first outer diameter, a first bore a first maximal diameter and a front-end opening. The needle assembly includes a needle having a shank with a second maximal diameter permitting insertion of the shank in the first bore. The needle includes a blade disposed between the shank and the front end, and a tip section disposed between the blade and the front end, having a transverse opening, and terminating with a pointed tip.
problem: Designing a needle assembly for carpeting that allows smooth insertion into a shaft while enabling precise stitching and thread manipulation.
constraint: Ensuring the needle's shank diameter permits insertion into the shaft bore while maintaining sufficient strength in the blade and tip to penetrate carpet materials without deformation.
mechanism: Segmented functional geometry: A tool with a stepped profile allows insertion into a receiving bore via a reduced-diameter section, while a separate working segment with a transverse aperture enables controlled material manipulation during operation.
mechanism_raw: Stepped diameter and functional segmentation: A handle with a shaft featuring a larger first diameter and a smaller second diameter permits needle insertion into a bore, while a blade and tip section with a transverse opening enable controlled thread passage and penetration during carpet stitching.

abstract: Illumination device, in particular in a vehicle, wherein certain areas in the interior of the vehicle, such as center console, dashboard, and/or side doors, are at least partially covered by real wood elements that are translucent. Illumination units are arranged on the underside of the wood elements and the wood elements can be used to produce differently shaped illuminations with a defined orientation in the vehicle interior. The wood elements have a thickness such that the illumination units are not visible to an occupant when switched off, i.e., not emitting light.
problem: Integrating illumination into a vehicle interior without visible hardware when the lights are off.
constraint: Balancing material thickness to hide light sources without compromising light output when illuminated.
mechanism: Using a translucent material with controlled thickness to conceal light sources when inactive while allowing light transmission when active.
mechanism_raw: Using translucent material (e.g., wood) with controlled thickness to conceal light sources when inactive while allowing light transmission when active.

abstract: The subject matter disclosed herein provides methods for controlling loads in an IP network that is divided into one or more zones and/or subzones. In one aspect, there is provided a method that can associate a plurality of controllers with one of a plurality of zones. Each controller can be connected to one or more loads. The method can associate each controller with an address. The address can include a network address and a host identifier. The network address for each controller in a first zone can be the same. The method can transmit over a network a control message to each controller in the first zone. The control message can cause one or more operational parameters of the loads connected to each controller in the first zone to change. Related apparatus, computer program products, systems, techniques, and articles are also described.
problem: Efficiently managing and controlling loads across an IP network divided into zones.
constraint: Ensuring zone-based addressing avoids conflicts while enabling scalable, localized control of distributed devices.
mechanism: Grouping controllers into zones with shared network addresses and transmitting targeted control messages to collectively adjust operational parameters of connected loads.
mechanism_raw: Grouping controllers into zones with shared network addresses and transmitting targeted control messages to collectively adjust operational parameters of connected loads.
residual_terms: ["zones", "shared network addresses", "targeted control messages", "operational parameters", "connected loads"]

abstract: A mole trap includes a molded housing with first and second portions. One of the portions includes two molded posts. A trigger and release plate are each pivotally mounted on one of the two posts, and are substantially encased within the housing. The trap may include a first shaft connected to a trigger pad, and a spring loaded second shaft. The first shaft is slideable with respect to the second shaft, which is connected to a plurality of tines. A release is operative to hold a trigger in a set position, and thereby hold the spring loaded second shaft in the set position. The first shaft is operable to displace the release in response to an upward force applied to the trigger pad, wherein the release is operable to release the trigger in response to the displacement, wherein the trigger is operable to release the spring loaded outer shaft.
problem: Creating a mechanical trap that triggers a spring-loaded mechanism in response to an animal's movement.
constraint: Calibrating trigger sensitivity to ensure activation by target movement without false triggers from external forces.
mechanism: A trigger pad displaces a release mechanism via a sliding shaft, which in turn releases a spring-loaded shaft connected to tines, converting upward force into a trapping action.
mechanism_raw: A trigger pad displaces a release mechanism via a sliding shaft, which in turn releases a spring-loaded shaft connected to tines, converting upward force into a trapping action.
residual_terms: ["trigger pad", "release mechanism", "sliding shaft", "spring-loaded shaft", "tines", "upward force", "trapping action"]

abstract: A foam for use in a lost-foam casting process utilized in the manufacture of a component for a gas turbine engine, the foam having a void fraction less than or equal to ninety five percent, is disclosed. The foam may include a first layer comprising polymer foam having an open-cell structure and a void fraction greater than ninety five percent. A second layer, comprising adhesive, may be adhered to the first layer. A third layer comprising particulate material may be adhered to the second layer.
reason: The patent describes a specific material composition (layered foam with controlled void fractions) for a casting process, but does not describe a generalizable functional mechanism beyond material layering for a niche industrial application.

abstract: A drive mechanism is presented for tightening a skewer of a bicycle fork anchor upon a prong of a bicycle fork by delivering a predetermined drive-force to the skewer. The drive mechanism draws a head of the skewer against the prong thereby pinch-securing the bicycle fork to the bicycle fork anchor. The drive mechanism can include a manually operable actuator and a transmission. The manually operable actuator can be coupled to the transmission. The transmission can include a slip mechanism that only transmits driving forces to the skewer of the bicycle fork anchor that are less than the predetermined drive-force.
problem: Tightening a bicycle skewer to a precise force without over-tightening or damaging components.
constraint: Setting the slip threshold accurately to prevent over-tightening while ensuring sufficient clamping force.
mechanism: A slip mechanism in the transmission limits force transmission to a predetermined threshold, ensuring only forces below the threshold are applied to the skewer.
mechanism_raw: A slip mechanism in the transmission limits force transmission to a predetermined threshold, ensuring only forces below the threshold are applied to the skewer.
residual_terms: ["slip mechanism", "transmission", "force transmission", "predetermined threshold", "forces below the threshold", "skewer"]

abstract: A concrete composition is obtained by dry mixing cement and an aggregate, adding thereto a water dispersion which is preformed by dispersing a low substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose having a hydroxypropoxy substitution of 5-16 wt % in the form of fibrous particles having an aspect ratio of 4-7 in water, and mixing the ingredients. Because of reduced drying shrinkage, only a little drop of fluidity, and proper flow, the concrete composition is useful to form concrete buildings having frost damage resistance.
problem: Achieving concrete with reduced drying shrinkage, maintained fluidity, and frost damage resistance for durable construction materials.
constraint: Balancing the cellulose substitution level (5-16 wt%) and particle aspect ratio (4-7) to avoid excessive fluidity loss while ensuring structural integrity and frost resistance.
mechanism: Dispersing fibrous particles with controlled substitution and aspect ratio into a binding matrix to modulate hydration kinetics and microstructure, thereby reducing drying shrinkage while preserving flowability and frost resistance through balanced rheological and mechanical interactions.
mechanism_raw: Using fibrous particles of low-substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose (with specific hydroxypropoxy substitution and aspect ratio) dispersed in water to control hydration and microstructure, balancing shrinkage reduction with flow properties.

abstract: A slab bridge structure having improved rigid connection strength between bridge girders and concrete piers. The slab bridge structure has a rigid connection structure in which slab concrete (3) is poured between side surfaces of bridge girders (1) arranged in line in a bridge width direction, throughout a longitudinal direction of the bridge girders, connection concrete (12) in which bridge girder portions (1′) supported by a bridge seat (2a) of a concrete pier (2) that supports the bridge girders are embedded is further added onto the bridge seat, and the slab concrete and the concrete pier are concrete-joined through the connection concrete, the slab bridge structure further includes: a connecting rod (13) embedded in the concrete pier and projecting upward from the bridge seat of the pier; and a connecting plate (14) connecting upper end portions of the adjacent bridge girder portions.
problem: Ensuring rigid and durable connections between bridge girders and concrete piers in slab bridge structures under dynamic loads.
constraint: Maintaining load transfer efficiency while accommodating thermal expansion/contraction and minimizing stress concentrations at the girder-pier interface.
mechanism: Embedding a secondary binding medium around structural elements at an interface and integrating mechanical fasteners to form a load-transferring joint that distributes stresses across the connection while accommodating differential movement.
mechanism_raw: Embedding connection concrete around girder portions on pier seats and using mechanical connectors (rods and plates) to create a monolithic joint that distributes stresses across the interface.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to an electronic vaping system. In an embodiment, the electronic vaping system may be paired (e.g., communicate, exchange data, integrate, have a symbiotic relationship, share, etc.) with a computing device. In an embodiment, an electronic vapor (eVapor) device may be built into a computing device. In an embodiment, the eVapor device may be a portable device separate from the computing device. In an embodiment, the computing device may comprise an application, wherein the application may allow the eVapor device and the computing device to share functionality. In an embodiment, the application may allow personalized login information, and a profile and settings may be associated with the personalized login information. In an embodiment, the profile and settings may be associated with vapor settings, flavors, attributes, etc. In an embodiment, the application may comprise security features, such as password protection, encryption/decryption, etc.
problem: Providing personalized, secure, and integrated control of vapor delivery in electronic vaping systems through computing device pairing.
constraint: Balancing user accessibility and personalization with robust encryption and authentication to prevent unauthorized access or data breaches.
mechanism: Linking a vapor delivery device to a remote computing system through a software interface that manages user-specific configurations, operational parameters, and cryptographic safeguards to enable synchronized, authenticated control.
mechanism_raw: Linking vapor device functionality to a computing device via an application that manages user profiles, settings, and security protocols, enabling synchronized data exchange and customized operation.

abstract: A wire tightening apparatus includes a housing having a ratchet gear formed in its inner periphery in a circumferential direction. A winding member is rotatably inserted into the housing, with a wire being wound therearound. A support part radially protrudes from the upper portion of a coupling shaft coupled to the housing. An intermediate member includes an engagement restriction part that is engaged with the ratchet gear and is restricted from rotating. The intermediate member has a resilient coupling hole in its center, with a resilience restriction part on the periphery thereof. The engagement restriction part is provided on an end of a blade extending from a body and having a resilient support force. The resilience restriction part is elevated by an external force coupled to the upper portion of the winding member and is supported by the outer periphery of the support part in lifted and lowered states.
problem: Achieving precise, controlled tightening of wires or cables with reliable locking and adjustable tensioning in mechanical systems.
constraint: Ensuring the resilient coupling hole and blade mechanism can withstand repeated stress cycles without failure while maintaining smooth operation under varying load conditions.
mechanism: Combining a unidirectional motion-limiting mechanism with a compliant coupling interface and blade-based engagement to enable incremental rotation under load while permitting manual override through external force application.
mechanism_raw: Combining a ratchet gear with a resilient coupling hole and blade-based engagement restriction to allow incremental rotation while enabling manual override via external force on the winding member.

abstract: A paint edging tool that deliver paint with sharp, clear edges at wall junctions. The paint edging tool includes a base wherein the base may include a handle, at least one wheel, a painting pad, a built-in-deflector, and at least one pad ejector. The handle may be configured to allow rotation between multiple positions. The handle may further include an adapter wherein the adapter is configured to be mounted on the handle, thereby allowing a pivoting motion in relation to the wall. The base may include at least one lobe, wherein the lobe is configured to be located on each side of the base, and is further configured to connect with the at least one wheel. The painting pad may be configured to be notched around the at least one deflector and the at least one wheel in order to allow painting inside a corner area of a wall.
problem: Delivering sharp, clean paint edges at wall junctions and corners during coating applications without manual touch-ups.
constraint: Balancing the tool's maneuverability in tight spaces with the precision of the deflector and pad geometry to avoid paint bleed while maintaining consistent coverage.
mechanism: Integrating rolling guides, flow-directing barriers, and patterned contact surfaces into a coating tool to mechanically constrain material spread and define edge boundaries during application, eliminating post-application correction.
mechanism_raw: Integrating wheels, deflectors, and notched painting pads into a tool base to mechanically guide paint flow and physically block excess material from spreading beyond the target area.

abstract: Robotic surface-cleaning assemblies include a base configured to be operatively coupled to a robotic arm; a supply of cleaning fabric supported relative to the base; an applicator supported relative to the base, wherein the applicator is configured to support a portion of cleaning fabric from the supply of cleaning fabric and operatively and selectively position the portion into engagement with a surface to be cleaned; and a source of cleaning fluid supported relative to the base, wherein the source of cleaning fluid is configured to operatively and selectively (i) deliver cleaning fluid directly to the portion of cleaning fabric supported by the applicator and/or (ii) deliver cleaning fluid directly to the surface to be cleaned. Methods of cleaning a surface with a robotic surface-cleaning assembly also are disclosed.
problem: Automating surface cleaning with a robotic system while enabling flexible application of cleaning fabric and fluid delivery.
constraint: Balancing precise control of fabric positioning and fluid delivery timing to avoid over-saturation or ineffective cleaning while maintaining robotic mobility.
mechanism: Coordinated integration of a manipulator's motion, an applicator that selectively positions a cleaning medium into contact with a surface, and a fluid delivery system that can target either the medium or the surface directly, enabling adaptive cleaning strategies through synchronized control of positioning and fluid application timing.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated integration of a robotic arm's movement, an applicator that selectively positions cleaning fabric into engagement with a surface, and a fluid delivery system that can target either the fabric or the surface directly, allowing adaptive cleaning strategies.

abstract: A multi-mode aerial vehicle hybrid wing includes a fixed wing configured to extend from a side of an elongated fuselage and double over its longitudinal axis, a tilt wing attached at a first side to a free end of the fixed wing wherein the tilt wing is rotatable ninety degrees about its axis, and a duct attached to a second side of the tilt wing. The duct includes a plurality of pivotal control surfaces positioned at a top entrance of the duct, dual counter-rotating rotors positioned at an underside of the duct, a plurality of cross stators positioned at a back entrance of the duct, and a plurality of stator pivotal control surfaces within each of the cross stators of the duct. The multi-mode aerial vehicle hybrid wing also includes a winglet attached to the duct opposite to the tilt wing.
problem: Enabling a single aerial vehicle to operate in multiple flight modes (e.g., fixed-wing and rotary-wing) with structural adaptability.
constraint: Structural complexity and weight distribution must accommodate dual-mode operation without compromising stability or performance in either configuration.
mechanism: Structural reconfiguration of aerodynamic surfaces and internal airflow control elements, where a primary lifting surface rotates to alter orientation and secondary control surfaces dynamically adjust to manage airflow and lift across distinct operational modes.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical reconfiguration of a tilt wing and duct system, where the tilt wing rotates ninety degrees to alter aerodynamic orientation, and the duct's internal control surfaces and rotors dynamically adjust to manage airflow and lift across modes.

abstract: The present invention provides a seal comprising an elastomeric composite, said composite comprising an elastomeric polymer and a negative thermal expansion (NTE) filler, the NTE filler has a coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) lower than −6×10-6 K-1 within a temperature range of 220-293 K and is present in an amount of 0.01-50 volume % based on the total volume of the elastomeric composite at 20° C.
problem: Maintaining dimensional stability of an elastomeric seal under temperature fluctuations to prevent leakage or failure.
constraint: Optimizing filler volume percentage and thermal expansion coefficient to ensure compatibility with the elastomer's properties and the operational temperature range.
mechanism: Incorporation of a material with opposing thermal expansion characteristics into a compliant matrix, whose dimensional response to temperature counteracts the matrix's inherent expansion, thereby stabilizing the composite's overall dimensions across a temperature range.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a negative thermal expansion (NTE) filler into the elastomer matrix, whose contraction with temperature offsets the elastomer's expansion, thereby stabilizing the composite's overall dimensions.

abstract: A zip slider has: a slider body having upper and lower elements providing two entry channels through which zip teeth pass and slider un/mating; a pull tab having a cam; a biasing spring having a locking prong and a follower surface bearing against the cam. The cam on the follower surface biases the tab into a closed position in which it lies against the upper element. When the tab is in a lifted position, the cam action on the follower surface raises the prong above the mated teeth, enabling relative motion of the teeth and body; when the tab is in the closed position, the prong bears against the teeth to prevent unwanted relative slider and teeth motion. The slider has a counter bias, acting between the upper element and the tab to apply a biasing force on the tab acting against the action of the cam and follower surface.
problem: Creating a zip slider that reliably locks and unlocks teeth while maintaining user control over the tab position.
constraint: Balancing the cam's mechanical advantage and spring tension to ensure smooth operation without unintended unlocking or excessive force requirements.
mechanism: A mechanical engagement system with a primary biasing element that maintains a default engaged state, and a secondary manual input that overcomes the bias to enable controlled disengagement, allowing selective relative motion between interlocked components.
mechanism_raw: A cam-follower system with a biasing spring that automatically biases the tab into a closed position, while a counter bias allows manual lifting to disengage the prong from the teeth, enabling controlled relative motion.

abstract: A sanitary fitting includes a pipe section which has a valve seat and which receives a valve upper part which bears against the valve seat and which includes a head piece which is traversed centrally by a spindle which is rotatably and/or pivotably mounted in the head piece and via which a control disc can be moved relative to an inlet disc within the head piece, wherein the valve upper part is releasably connected to the pipe section, wherein a device for the defined positioning of the valve upper part within the pipe section in at least two rotary positions offset by an angle of orientation is arranged.
problem: Allowing a sanitary valve to be positioned in multiple rotary orientations for different flow configurations while ensuring secure sealing.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and sealing integrity across all rotary positions while maintaining ease of installation and removal.
mechanism: A releasable mechanical interface between a valve component and a flow pathway, combined with a positioning mechanism that locks the valve in predefined angular orientations, enabling mode switching while maintaining sealing integrity across all positions.
mechanism_raw: A releasable connection between the valve upper part and pipe section, combined with a positioning device that mechanically locks the valve in predefined rotary positions via angular offsets, enabling mode switching without leakage.

abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including instructions encoded on storage media, for performing reduction of gradient vectors and similarly structured data that are generated in parallel, for example, on nodes organized in a mesh or torus topology defined by connections in at least two dimension between the nodes. The methods provide parallel computation and communication between nodes in the topology.
problem: Efficiently performing parallel reduction of gradient vectors or structured data across nodes in a mesh or torus topology without excessive communication overhead.
constraint: Balancing computational parallelism with communication bandwidth limitations in the network topology to avoid bottlenecks during data reduction.
mechanism: Distributing computation and communication tasks across a network of nodes with structured connectivity to enable parallel processing while minimizing redundant data transfers through coordinated inter-node communication.
mechanism_raw: Leveraging the inherent connectivity of a multi-dimensional mesh or torus topology to distribute computation and communication tasks across nodes, enabling parallel processing of gradient vectors while minimizing redundant data transfers through structured inter-node coordination.

abstract: A lighting control system for controlling a cumulative light emitted by a lighting fixture having a plurality of LED light sources may comprise a plurality of LED drivers adapted to be coupled to a respective one of the LED light sources and configured to control an intensity of the respective LED light source, and a controller configured to transmit a single digital message for controlling the cumulative light emitted by the lighting fixture. Each of the plurality of LED drivers is configured to adjust the intensity of the respective LED light source to a preset intensity in response to the single digital message transmitted by the controller.
problem: Controlling cumulative light output from multiple LED sources in a lighting fixture using a single digital command without requiring individualized control signals for each LED.
constraint: Ensuring precise synchronization of LED intensities across drivers while minimizing signaling complexity and avoiding overcurrent or inconsistent brightness.
mechanism: Broadcasting a shared command to multiple autonomous units that independently adjust their output based on the command, ensuring synchronized control of cumulative output without individualized signaling.
mechanism_raw: Broadcasting a single digital message to multiple LED drivers, each of which autonomously adjusts its respective LED to a preset intensity based on the shared message, enabling decentralized yet synchronized control of cumulative light output.

abstract: A printer includes a printer body and a lid. The printer body includes a recording paper holder configured to accommodate a roll of recording paper and a projection provided on a bottom surface of the recording paper holder that contacts the recording paper. The lid is attached to the printer body to be opened and closed relative to the printer body.
reason: The patent describes a structural design (projection on a paper holder and a hinged lid) without a causal mechanism that solves a broader problem beyond the specific printer's physical configuration. The mechanism is tied to the printer's form factor rather than a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A ground engaging tooth assembly for a cutting edge of a ground engaging implement may include an adapter and a ground engaging tip. The adapter may have a forward extending adapter nose having an inverted or reverse keystone-shaped contour, with the ground engaging tip having a nose cavity for receiving the adapter nose and exterior surfaces having complementary shapes to the adapter nose. The adapter nose and an adapter cavity of the tip may also be configured with complimentary surfaces that increase retention between the adapter nose and the tip when downward forces are applied to the tip. In other embodiments, the surfaces of the tip may include reliefs extending inwardly into the body of the tip to reduce weight and facilitate penetration of the tip into work material as wear material wears away from a front edge of the tip.
problem: Achieving secure mechanical retention between a ground-engaging tip and an adapter under dynamic downward forces while reducing weight and improving penetration into work material.
constraint: Balancing retention strength under load with weight reduction and wear resistance to maintain performance over time.
mechanism: Using a mechanical interface with interlocking surfaces that increase retention force under applied load, combined with structural features that reduce weight and enhance performance during wear.
mechanism_raw: Using a reverse keystone-shaped adapter nose and complementary tip cavity with interlocking surfaces that tighten retention when downward forces are applied, combined with inward reliefs in the tip to reduce weight and enhance penetration as wear occurs.
residual_terms: ["reverse keystone-shaped adapter nose", "inward reliefs in the tip"]

abstract: Embodiments of the present invention provide a control channel resource transmission method including: obtaining, by a user equipment, a configuration parameter in a candidate control channel set according to a preset protocol and/or higher-layer signaling sent by a base station, where the higher-layer signaling is used to notify the configuration parameter; determining an antenna port according to the obtained configuration parameter; receiving, by using the antenna port, a control channel or a control channel element sent by the base station; and determining, by the base station, the antenna port according to the same configuration parameter as that of the user equipment, and sending, by using the antenna port, the control channel or the control channel element to the user equipment. The embodiments of the present invention are applicable to control channel resource transmission.
problem: Coordinating antenna port selection between a base station and user equipment for control channel resource transmission without requiring explicit real-time negotiation.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between base station and user equipment configurations while minimizing signaling overhead and adapting to dynamic network conditions.
mechanism: Deriving a shared configuration parameter via higher-layer signaling or a preset protocol, which both endpoints independently use to select the same resource for transmission or reception, ensuring synchronized allocation without real-time negotiation.
mechanism_raw: Deriving a shared configuration parameter via higher-layer signaling or a preset protocol, which both the base station and user equipment use to independently determine the same antenna port for transmitting or receiving control channels, ensuring synchronized resource allocation.

abstract: An erase operation includes one or more erase depth checks to detect the occurrence of shallow erased memory cells at the end of an erase process. Memory cells are subjected to erase and erase verification until erase verification success is achieved. At the end of successful erase verification, a subset of memory cells is read to detect an erase depth or level of the memory cells. If the erase depth check indicates that the subset memory cells are in a shallow erased condition, additional erasing and verification is performed.
problem: Ensuring memory cells are sufficiently erased without over-erasing, as initial erase verification may miss shallow erased cells.
constraint: Balancing thoroughness (avoiding incomplete erasure) with efficiency (preventing unnecessary over-erasing or process delays).
mechanism: A feedback loop where initial verification of a target state is followed by a secondary check on a subset of elements. If incomplete states are detected, additional corrective action and re-verification are triggered, creating a self-correcting process that adapts to edge cases.
mechanism_raw: A feedback loop where erase verification is followed by a post-verification erase depth check on a subset of cells. If shallow erasure is detected, additional erasing and re-verification are triggered, creating a self-correcting process that adapts to edge cases.

abstract: Apparatus and process are described for forming projections on a substrate for use as hook-type fasteners in touch fastening systems, wherein vibration energy may be used to soften a substrate which may be positioned between a mold and a source of vibration. The mold may include a plurality of cavities into which the softened substrate may be forced to form the projections. The substrate may comprise a film, sheet, web, composite, laminate, etc. and be useful as an attachment strip for temporary or permanent fastening. The source of vibration may be an ultrasonic horn. The process to form such projections may be operated in a continuous, semi-continuous or intermittent manner.
problem: Forming precise projections on substrates (e.g., hook fasteners) without relying on high heat or pressure, which could damage the material.
constraint: Selecting vibration parameters (frequency, amplitude) and mold design to achieve consistent shaping without degrading the substrate.
mechanism: Applying oscillatory energy to a deformable substrate to locally reduce its stiffness, then forcing it into a shaped cavity under pressure. The oscillatory energy enables forming at lower energy inputs while preserving structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using vibration energy (e.g., ultrasonic) to locally soften a substrate, then forcing it into mold cavities under pressure. The vibration reduces material stiffness, enabling shaping at lower energy inputs while maintaining structural integrity.

abstract: In some preferred embodiments, the present invention provides an improved system and apparatus for cleaning the clipper blades at an intermediate step of hair cutting, to avoid hindrance of the hair sticking the blades. This ensures better handling and operation of the hair cutting tools. The apparatus can be removably worn any of the fingers of the Barber, as per the comfort and ease of operations felt by him. The invention suggests a cleaning barber brush apparatus that is conveniently adjusted to be worn in different fingers of different sizes, using elastic and rubber holding means.
problem: Maintaining tool functionality (e.g., clipper blade cleanliness) during active use without interrupting workflow or requiring manual intervention.
constraint: Ensuring the tool remains securely positioned during dynamic movements while allowing quick removal or repositioning.
mechanism: A wearable, adjustable tool integrated into a user’s hand via a flexible holding mechanism. The tool’s position and grip adapt to different users, enabling real-time maintenance of a primary tool’s functionality during active operation.
mechanism_raw: A wearable, adjustable cleaning tool integrated into the user's hand via elastic/rubber holding means. The tool’s position and grip adapt to different finger sizes, enabling real-time cleaning while the primary task (hair cutting) continues.

abstract: An oral cavity apparatus includes a body portion having first and second ends and a grip portion; an oral tool coupled to the first end of the body portion; and a touch-sensitive (TS) sensor which is located on the body portion and outputs a sensor value indicative of a force applied thereto by a user. In addition, a controller is configured to compare the sensor value with at least one threshold value, and to actuate the oral tool based upon the results of the comparison.
problem: Controlling an oral tool’s operation based on user-applied force to prevent excessive pressure or unintended actuation.
constraint: Calibrating sensor sensitivity and response time to distinguish intentional user input from incidental contact.
mechanism: A sensor measures applied force, which is compared to predefined thresholds by a controller. The controller actuates a device only when force exceeds a minimum threshold and halts operation if force exceeds a maximum, creating a closed-loop force-regulated system.
mechanism_raw: A touch-sensitive sensor measures applied force, which is compared to predefined thresholds by a controller. The controller actuates the tool only when force exceeds a minimum threshold and stops it if force exceeds a maximum, creating a closed-loop force-regulated system.

abstract: A rotor comprises a disk having a rim. The rim has an axial face facing one of a forward or rearward direction. The rim defines a circumferential groove. A damper engages with the rim at both the axial face and the circumferential groove. The disk includes a rotor hub having a hub inner surface facing a longitudinal axis about which the rotor hub rotates. The rim is spaced radially outwardly relative to the hub inner surface. The axial face extends radially inwardly from the rim to the hub inner surface. The circumferential groove is formed within the hub inner surface. The damper comprises a split ring damper with a first leg mounted within the circumferential groove and a second leg that extends from the first leg, surrounds a radial lip of the hub inner surface, and extends radially outwardly to contact the axial face. An integrally bladed rotor is also disclosed.
problem: Damping vibrations in a rotating rotor component to reduce noise, wear, and mechanical stress without impeding rotational motion.
constraint: Designing the damper’s geometry and material to fit within the rotor’s confined space while maintaining effective damping across operational speeds.
mechanism: A damper engages a rotating component at two distinct geometric interfaces: one providing radial constraint and another providing axial constraint. The dual-point contact distributes damping forces across the component’s geometry, counteracting vibrations through controlled friction and structural coupling.
mechanism_raw: A split ring damper engages the rotor at two points: a circumferential groove (radial constraint) and an axial face (axial constraint). The dual-point contact distributes damping forces across the rotor’s geometry, counteracting vibrations through controlled friction and structural coupling.

abstract: A spinning forming device according to one aspect, a receiving jig supporting a central portion of a plate to be formed is attached to a rotating shaft, and a transform target portion of the plate is pressed by a processing tool and locally heated by a heater that performs induction heating. The heater includes an electric conducting pipe in which a cooling liquid flows. The electric conducting pipe includes: a coil portion extending in a circumferential direction of the rotating shaft and having a doubled circular-arc shape facing the plate; and a pair of lead portions extending from the coil portion outward in a radial direction of the rotating shaft. Each of the pair of lead portions is retreated father away from the plate than the coil portion at its end portion adjacent to the coil portion.
problem: Localizing heat application during rotational forming of a plate without interfering with mechanical processing or cooling efficiency.
constraint: Balancing electromagnetic field concentration for effective induction heating against mechanical clearance and cooling liquid flow within the rotating system.
mechanism: Shape a conductive heating element as a curved segment oriented toward a rotating surface to concentrate electromagnetic energy at a localized region. Extend and withdraw connecting leads radially away from the surface to maintain electrical connectivity while avoiding electromagnetic and physical interference with the heating zone. This geometric separation enables simultaneous localized heating and mechanical forming during rotation.
mechanism_raw: The heater's coil portion is shaped as a doubled circular arc facing the plate, enabling concentrated induction heating at the target area. The lead portions are radially extended and retreated away from the plate, preventing electromagnetic and physical interference with the coil's heating zone while maintaining electrical connectivity. This geometric separation allows simultaneous localized heating and mechanical forming during rotation.
residual_terms: ["induction heating", "electromagnetic field concentration", "circular arc", "coil", "lead portions", "radial extension"]

abstract: A self-closing device is configured to retract a unit capable of being pulled out with respect to an apparatus main body, to the apparatus main body. The self-closing device includes a plurality of retracting modules configured to retract the unit from a retracting start position towards a retracting end position. The plurality of retracting modules are provided such that retracting strokes from the retracting start position to the retracting end position partially overlap each other and the retracting start positions are different from each other in the retracting direction.
problem: Retracting a pull-out unit smoothly and completely to its end position using multiple independent actuation modules.
constraint: Coordinating stroke overlap and start positions to avoid mechanical conflicts while maximizing retraction reliability and minimizing response time.
mechanism: Arrange multiple independent actuation modules with overlapping stroke ranges and staggered initiation points. As each module begins motion at a different time, their combined output ensures continuous force application across the entire retraction path. The stroke overlap compensates for timing or force variations between modules, preventing gaps in retraction and ensuring full engagement of the unit into the apparatus main body.
mechanism_raw: Multiple retracting modules are arranged with overlapping strokes and staggered starting positions. As each module begins retraction at a different point, their combined motion ensures continuous force application across the entire retraction path. The overlap compensates for timing or force variations between modules, preventing gaps in retraction and ensuring full engagement of the unit into the apparatus main body.

abstract: Embodiments provide a method and apparatus for upgrading a hydrocarbon feedstock. According to at least one embodiment, the method includes (a) supplying a hydrocarbon feedstock to an oxidation reactor, where the hydrocarbon feedstock is oxidized in the presence of a catalyst under conditions sufficient to selectively oxidize sulfur compounds present in the hydrocarbon feedstock; (b) separating the hydrocarbons and the oxidized sulfur compounds by solvent extraction; (c) collecting a residue stream that includes the oxidized sulfur compounds; (d) supplying the residue stream to a coker to produce coker gases and solid coke; and (e) supplying spent adsorbent including residual oils from the adsorption column to the coker for disposing the spent adsorbent after completion of an adsorption cycle.
problem: Upgrading hydrocarbon feedstock by removing sulfur compounds while efficiently managing multiple waste streams generated during processing.
constraint: Maintaining chemical compatibility and thermal stability across interconnected oxidation, extraction, and coking stages to prevent process interference.
mechanism: Integrate sequential processing stages where waste output from one stage serves as input for another. Oxidized contaminants are separated via solvent extraction, and the residue stream is co-processed in a coking stage alongside spent material from a prior treatment cycle. This cascading use of the coking stage for both residue and spent material disposal consolidates waste handling and reduces the need for separate treatment pathways.
mechanism_raw: The method integrates sequential processing steps where waste from one stage becomes input for another. Oxidized sulfur compounds are separated via solvent extraction, and the residue stream is co-processed in a coker alongside spent adsorbent from a prior adsorption cycle. This cascading use of the coker for both residue and adsorbent disposal consolidates waste handling and reduces the need for separate treatment pathways.

abstract: Technical solutions are described for measuring fuel injection to an engine of a vehicle. For example, an engine control unit (ECU) that controls the operation of the engine, is equipped with a first direct memory address channel to store rail pressure values that are received from the engine in a first buffer. The ECU further includes a second direct memory address channel configured to copy a first subset of the rail pressure value from the first buffer to a filter module in response to an angle-based interrupt request. The ECU further includes a third direct memory address channel configured to copy filtered pressure values from the filter module to a second buffer. The ECU also includes a processor that computes a pressure drop based on the filtered pressure values from the second buffer, and compute a quantity of fuel injected into the engine based on the pressure drop.
problem: Accurately measuring fuel injection quantity in real-time using high-frequency pressure data without overloading the central processor.
constraint: Synchronizing angle-based interrupts with engine timing to ensure filtered pressure values reflect relevant injection events while minimizing CPU workload.
mechanism: Use autonomous data transfer channels to move sensor measurements into buffers without processor intervention. A filtering stage processes subsets of data triggered by angle-based interrupts synchronized to rotational position. A secondary autonomous transfer channel moves filtered values to another buffer, allowing the processor to compute derived quantities from pre-processed data without interrupting ongoing sensor data acquisition.
mechanism_raw: Direct memory access (DMA) channels autonomously transfer rail pressure data from sensors to buffers, bypassing the CPU. A filter module processes subsets of data triggered by angle-based interrupts synchronized to engine rotation. A third DMA channel moves filtered values to a secondary buffer, allowing the processor to compute pressure drops and fuel quantities from pre-processed data without interrupting sensor data acquisition.
residual_terms: ["direct memory access", "DMA", "angle-based interrupts", "engine timing", "pressure data", "buffers", "filter module", "CPU"]

abstract: An extracorporeal reservoir device including a housing, a venous inlet sub-assembly, and a venous filter. The venous sub-assembly is mounted to the housing and includes a downtube and a luer port connector body. The connector body extends from the downtube and forms a passageway open to a lumen of the downtube. The connector body is arranged such that fluid flow from the passageway merges with a flow path of fluid along the primary lumen at an angle of less than 90°. Secondary blood flow through the port connector body is less likely to induce turbulent flow into venous blood flow within the downtube, and is thus less likely to break up any bubbles carried by the venous blood. For example, at port flow rates of less than 500 mL/minute, fluid flow from the port connector body does not induce turbulent flow into fluid flowing through the primary lumen.
problem: Introducing secondary fluid flow into a primary flow path without inducing turbulence that could disrupt sensitive components (e.g., bubbles in blood).
constraint: Maintaining flow rates below a threshold (e.g., 500 mL/minute) to ensure the angled merging does not transition into turbulent regimes.
mechanism: Merge a secondary fluid flow into a primary flow path at an angle less than 90 degrees. This angled merging reduces shear forces and flow separation at the junction, preventing turbulent eddies that would otherwise disrupt laminar flow or damage sensitive components in the primary stream. The geometric constraint of the angle ensures smooth fluid dynamics even at low flow rates.
mechanism_raw: The connector body merges secondary fluid flow into the primary lumen at an angle less than 90 degrees. This angled merging reduces shear forces and flow separation at the junction, preventing turbulent eddies that would otherwise break up bubbles or disrupt laminar flow in the primary stream. The geometric constraint of the angle ensures smooth fluid dynamics even at low flow rates.
residual_terms: ["angled merging", "laminar flow", "turbulence", "shear forces", "flow separation", "eddy currents", "primary lumen", "secondary fluid"]

abstract: The present disclosure relates to the alignment of moieties (e.g., nanoparticles and/or nanowires) into prescribed architectures on two- and/or three-dimensional substrates (e.g., nucleic acid nanostructures/crystals). The present disclosure also relates to a nucleic acid (e.g., DNA) lithography method that includes, in some embodiments, adsorbing a bare nucleic acid nanostructure onto a surface of a substrate, and etching the surface of the substrate containing the bare nucleic acid nanostructure, thereby producing a patterned substrate.
problem: Precisely aligning nanoscale moieties (e.g., nanoparticles, nanowires) into prescribed architectures on substrates without manual intervention or high-cost lithography.
constraint: Balancing the resolution of the nucleic acid's self-assembled structure with the etching process's ability to faithfully replicate fine features without damaging the substrate or the template.
mechanism: Using a self-assembling structure as a template to guide a material removal process, where the template's inherent structural specificity directs the removal to produce ordered arrangements on a substrate surface. The template's resolution is balanced against the removal process's fidelity to replicate fine features without damaging the substrate.
mechanism_raw: Using a bare nucleic acid nanostructure as a self-assembled template that adsorbs onto a substrate surface, then etching the substrate to transfer the nanostructure's pattern into the substrate, thereby creating a patterned architecture. The nucleic acid's inherent structural specificity guides the etching process to produce ordered arrangements.

abstract: An approach is provided for routing an aerial drone while preserving privacy. The approach involves processing model data depicting at least one structure to determine one or more privacy-sensitive features of the at least one structure. The approach also involves calculating line-of-sight data between a route of an aerial drone and the one or more privacy-sensitive features. The approach further involves configuring a routing of the aerial drone based on the line-of sight data when the aerial drone is traveling near the at least one structure.
problem: Routing an aerial drone through or near structures while avoiding exposure of privacy-sensitive features (e.g., private spaces, restricted areas).
constraint: Maintaining route efficiency and navigational feasibility while ensuring sufficient distance or occlusion between the drone and privacy-sensitive features to prevent unintended observation.
mechanism: Analyzing environmental model data to identify privacy-sensitive regions, computing visibility vectors between a planned trajectory and those regions, and dynamically adjusting the trajectory to enforce spatial separation or occlusion. The visibility analysis acts as a spatial filter to satisfy privacy constraints while maintaining navigational efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Processing environmental model data to identify privacy-sensitive features, computing line-of-sight vectors between the drone's planned path and those features, and dynamically adjusting the route to avoid direct visibility of sensitive areas. The line-of-sight analysis acts as a spatial filter to enforce privacy constraints.

abstract: A method for producing a ceramic circuit board comprising the steps of bonding a metal sheet to a ceramic substrate via a brazing material containing Ag to form a bonded body; etching the bonded metal sheet to form a circuit pattern; and removing an unnecessary brazing material from the substrate provided with the circuit pattern, by etching with an acidic solution comprising carboxylic acid and/or carboxylate and hydrogen peroxide.
problem: Creating a ceramic circuit board with a defined metal circuit pattern while selectively removing excess brazing material without damaging the circuit or substrate.
constraint: Optimizing the etchant's chemical composition and concentration to achieve selective dissolution of the brazing material without attacking the metal circuit or the ceramic substrate.
mechanism: Bonding a conductive layer to a substrate via an intermediate material, forming a circuit pattern through selective material removal, then using a chemically selective etchant to dissolve the intermediate material without attacking the conductive layer or substrate. The etchant's composition enables targeted removal of the intermediate layer while preserving the circuit and substrate.
mechanism_raw: Bonding a metal sheet to a ceramic substrate via a silver-containing brazing material, etching the metal to form the circuit pattern, and then using a carboxylic acid/carboxylate and hydrogen peroxide-based acidic solution to selectively dissolve the remaining brazing material. The chemical composition of the etchant enables targeted removal of the brazing layer while preserving the circuit and substrate.

abstract: An optical cable including a load bearing core includes a longitudinally and radially extending slot housing at least one optical fiber, wherein the slot has a width providing a low clearance for the optical fiber(s) housed therein and preventing two optical fibers being stuck to one another; and the slot has a depth equal to or lower than a radius of the core.
problem: Preventing optical fibers within a cable from adhering to one another while maintaining structural integrity and alignment within a load-bearing core.
constraint: Balancing the slot width to minimize fiber-to-fiber contact without compromising the core's load-bearing capacity or fiber positioning stability.
mechanism: Incorporating a physical separation structure within a load-bearing core, where the structure's geometry provides controlled clearance to prevent contact between adjacent elements while maintaining structural integrity. The separation width is constrained to balance element retention stability against core strength.
mechanism_raw: Designing a longitudinally and radially extending slot in the core with a width that provides low clearance for the fibers, physically separating them to prevent contact and adhesion. The slot depth is constrained to be equal to or less than the core's radius to preserve structural strength while enabling fiber retention.

abstract: A belt rotating device includes: a meandering correction roller that is rotatably supported within a support frame and is one of a plurality of rollers that stretch an endless belt; a supporting portion that is provided at the support frame and supports a rotating shaft of the meandering correction roller so as to be able to incline the rotating shaft of the meandering correction roller in a one direction; a collar member that is provided on the rotating shaft of the meandering correction roller, contacts the side end of the endless belt in which meandering has occurred, and moves in an axial direction; and an inclination guide portion that is supported by the support frame and has an inclined surface downward and inclined with respect to the shaft of the meandering correction roller, in a position in which the contact portion of the collar member contacts the inclination guide portion.
problem: Correcting lateral misalignment (meandering) of an endless belt during rotation in a belt-driven system.
constraint: Ensuring the collar-guide interaction generates sufficient corrective force to realign the belt without introducing excessive friction or mechanical wear that could destabilize the system.
mechanism: Mounting a pivoting element with a contact interface that interacts with a moving belt's edge during misalignment, where displacement of the contact interface along an inclined surface induces rotational adjustment of the pivoting element to realign the belt. The mechanical coupling between contact displacement and pivoting motion provides automatic corrective feedback.
mechanism_raw: Mounting a meandering correction roller on a pivotable shaft, with a collar that contacts the belt's side edge when misalignment occurs. The collar's axial movement along the belt edge interacts with an inclined guide surface, causing the roller's shaft to tilt and realign the belt. The mechanical coupling between collar displacement and roller inclination provides automatic corrective feedback.

abstract: Methods, devices, and systems are provided that determine analyte trends according to different methods depending on whether a change-resistant state is active or not active. The method used when the change-resistant state is activated provides for different requirements for a resulting analyte trend to transition between states (e.g., level to non-level). Furthermore, in some aspects, methods, devices, and systems of selecting or modifying a response rate of an analyte monitoring device for an individual user are provided. User instructions for selecting or modifying a response rate of the device or system is received externally via a user interface or communication channel. The response rate of the analyte monitoring device or system is then selected or modified to the first response rate, and the device or system operated with the first response rate.
problem: Managing analyte trend transitions and response rates in monitoring systems to balance stability and responsiveness under varying physiological states.
constraint: Balancing the need for stable operation during change-resistant states with the requirement for timely responses to genuine analyte shifts, while accommodating user-defined preferences for response speed.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting transition thresholds between operational states based on a detected resistance-to-change condition, and enabling external input to modulate system response dynamics, thereby balancing stability and reactivity to environmental shifts.
mechanism_raw: Adapting transition criteria between analyte trend states (e.g., level to non-level) based on an active change-resistant state, and allowing external user input to select or modify the device's response rate, which dynamically adjusts how quickly the system reacts to detected changes.

abstract: The invention provides a motor-driven chimney draft system with a flue gas inlet, a flue gas outlet, a flue gas compartment in fluid communication with the flue gas inlet and with the flue gas outlet, the flow of flue gases in the flue gas compartment having a flow direction from the flue gas inlet to the flue gas outlet, a motor compartment with motor having a motor shaft extending through a separating wall of the flue gas compartment, the motor shaft carrying an impeller for driving the received flow of flue gases in the flow direction; each of the separating wall of the flue gas compartment and the separating wall of the motor compartment extends parallel to the flow direction of flue gases, and they are arranged facing each other so as to define an air space therebetween, where the air space has openings allowing ambient air to flow through the air space.
problem: Maintaining efficient flue gas flow in a motor-driven chimney draft system while preventing overheating of the motor compartment.
constraint: Ensuring the motor compartment remains thermally isolated from the flue gas compartment while maintaining structural integrity and airflow efficiency through the air space.
mechanism: Employing a driven impeller to establish directional gas flow within a primary compartment, while a thermally isolated secondary compartment is cooled via ambient airflow through an intervening air gap, decoupling thermal management from the primary flow path.
mechanism_raw: Using a motor-driven impeller to actively drive flue gas flow in a defined direction, combined with an air space between parallel separating walls that allows ambient air to flow through and cool the motor compartment, decoupling thermal management from the primary gas flow path.

abstract: The present invention provides a conveyor belt tracking system for a dryer having a web of a mesh material having a protrusion extending along the length proximal one lateral edge and above a flat surface and a first generally cylindrical roller having a three-tiered slot for receiving the protrusion and two flanking shallow tracks for receiving base flanges.
problem: Maintaining alignment of a conveyor belt in a dryer system to prevent lateral drift and ensure consistent material transport.
constraint: Achieving precise alignment without introducing friction or jamming risks, while accommodating thermal expansion and mechanical wear in a high-temperature drying environment.
mechanism: Integrating a lateral guide feature on a moving belt with a multi-tiered mechanical interface that constrains motion through geometric engagement, enabling self-correcting alignment via physical constraint without introducing friction-dependent forces.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a protrusion along the belt's edge with a three-tiered roller slot that mechanically guides the belt by engaging the protrusion and flanking base flanges, creating a self-correcting alignment mechanism through geometric constraint.

abstract: The invention relates to ignition sets comprising initial explosive substances selected from the group consisting of compounds, in particular compounds of lead, which are derived from trinitropolyphenols, such as trinitrophenol, trinitroresorcinol or hydrazoic acid, for example, in mixture with oxygen-generating substances, wherein further included are initial explosive substances made of alkali metal and/or alkaline-earth metal salts of dinitrobenzofuroxanes and oxygen-generating substances made from nitrates of ammonium, guanidine, aminoguanidine, triaminoguanidine, dicyanodiamidine and from the elements of sodium, potassium, magnesium, calcium, cerium and/or from multivalent metal oxides.
problem: Creating a reliable ignition system that sustains combustion through controlled oxygen generation and tailored explosive initiation.
constraint: Balancing the energetic output of the initial explosives with the oxygen release rate to ensure complete combustion without premature or incomplete ignition.
mechanism: Sequencing energetic initiation materials with oxidizer sources to first trigger combustion and then sustain it via staged release of reactive species, ensuring complete energy release through temporal coordination of ignition and oxygen generation.
mechanism_raw: Combining initial explosive substances (e.g., lead-derived trinitro compounds or dinitrobenzofuroxane salts) with oxygen-generating materials (e.g., nitrates of ammonium or alkali metals) to sequentially trigger ignition and maintain sustained combustion via staged release of oxygen.

abstract: A method for measuring and displaying the track geometry of a track system uses a track-driveable permanent-way machine, comprising a control measurement system measuring the track position to be corrected before a lifting and lining device, an acceptance measurement system measuring the corrected track position after it, and output units displaying the measured values. The lifting and lining device is controlled depending on the measured values of the control measurement system and the acceptance measurement system to achieve a specified target track geometry. A three-dimensional position image is calculated from the curvature image (k(s)), longitudinal level image (h(s)) and superelevation image (u(s)) of the target track geometry, put into a perspective display, and displayed by the output unit, supplemented by measured error curves for track parameters of track direction, superelevation, twist, and longitudinal level.
problem: Accurately measuring and correcting track geometry in real-time during railway maintenance to achieve target alignment specifications.
constraint: Ensuring real-time synchronization between measurement and correction systems to avoid over-adjustment, while providing intuitive visual feedback for operators to validate corrections.
mechanism: Implementing a dual-measurement feedback system where pre-correction and post-correction assessments drive actuator adjustments, combined with real-time visualization of geometric parameters to synchronize correction actions and prevent over-adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Using a control measurement system to assess track position before correction, an acceptance measurement system to verify post-correction alignment, and a feedback loop that adjusts lifting/lining devices based on both measurements, supplemented by 3D visualization of curvature, level, and superelevation data.

abstract: The invention relates to a locking device, in particular for a motor vehicle, having a catch mechanism and a coupling device for connecting to a motor drive. The coupling device comprises a coupling lever, which by virtue of a plurality of engagement lugs is able to pivot a coupling lever.
