The engagement lugs can be detected in succession by the coupling lever and are arranged in this respect one behind the other. The invention further relates to a plastics component for the locking device. An engagement lug is formed by an element protruding from a main face of the coupling lever in order to simplify production and to keep material costs and installation space to a minimum.
problem: Simplifying production and minimizing material costs and installation space in a mechanical locking device.
constraint: Balancing minimal material usage and compact design while maintaining reliable mechanical engagement.
mechanism: A pivoting lever with sequentially arranged engagement points that enable incremental mechanical locking through controlled rotational movement, allowing discrete stable positions without complex actuation.
mechanism_raw: A coupling lever with sequentially arranged engagement lugs that pivot the lever in a controlled manner, enabling incremental engagement without complex components.

abstract: Polycrystalline diamond constructions include a diamond body comprising a matrix phase of bonded together diamond crystals formed at high pressure/high temperature conditions with a catalyst material. The sintered body is treated remove the catalyst material disposed within interstitial regions, rendering it substantially free of the catalyst material used to initially sinter the body. Accelerating techniques can be used to remove the catalyst material. The body includes an infiltrant material disposed within interstitial regions in a first region of the construction. The body includes a second region adjacent the working surface and that is substantially free of the infiltrant material. The infiltrant material can be a Group VIII material not used to initially sinter the diamond body. A metallic substrate is attached to the diamond body, and can be the same or different from a substrate used as a source of the catalyst material used to initially sinter the diamond body.
problem: Creating a polycrystalline diamond body with spatially controlled material properties for enhanced performance.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the diamond matrix while achieving targeted material distribution.
mechanism: Selective removal of a first material from a matrix structure followed by infiltration of a second material into specific zones, creating regions with distinct compositions while preserving overall structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Selective removal of catalyst material from interstitial regions followed by infiltration of a different material into specific zones, creating regions with distinct compositions.

abstract: An arrangement in a cardboard creasing machine, for forming structured patterns of creasing lines in a material comprising a cardboard web fed to the machine, comprising a system of at least two rollers. The first roller is provided with a male die, having at least two envelope surfaces, each with a structured pattern of lines, of which at least one has an open end. In order to prevent wild creasing lines with open ends are provided with crease stoppers, extending perpendicularly to the open line. The second roller is provided with a female die corresponding to the male die.
problem: Preventing unintended 'wild' creasing lines in structured cardboard patterns during manufacturing.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment of stoppers with open lines without disrupting the overall structured pattern.
mechanism: Barriers positioned perpendicular to linear features on a deformable substrate, physically interrupting uncontrolled propagation of deformation along the linear features.
mechanism_raw: Crease stoppers positioned perpendicular to open-ended crease lines, physically blocking uncontrolled propagation of the crease.

abstract: This invention serves as the fundamental design for a space-based, nuclear-powered spacecraft for deep space journeys. Nuclear energy is used as the motive power for the propulsion. The spacecraft propellant is a gas (such as helium or hydrogen), which is also the coolant for the onboard nuclear reactor. Nuclear energy is converted to thermal energy in the reactor, which heats up the propellant gas. That superheated gas then expands through the spacecraft nozzle and creates the thrust. The nuclear fuel consists of high enriched uranium. The amount of fuel is mission dependent, and requires declaration of payload, and desired speed, which is limited to sub-light for the first generation of this invention. The spacecraft will be assembled in, and launched from low earth orbit. The spacecraft final assembly consists of modular components delivered to low earth orbit from earth by conventional chemical rockets.
problem: Providing propulsion for deep-space missions with high energy density and modularity.
constraint: Limiting speed to sub-light velocities and requiring pre-declaration of mission parameters for fuel optimization.
mechanism: A heat source transfers thermal energy to a propellant, causing expansion through a directed outlet to generate thrust, with modular subsystems enabling assembly in a remote environment.
mechanism_raw: Nuclear thermal energy heats a propellant gas, which expands through a nozzle to generate thrust, with modular assembly enabling in-orbit construction.

abstract: A sanitary washing device according to an embodiment includes a toilet seat, a main part, and a radio wave sensor. The toilet seat is provided on a toilet. The toilet seat is pivotally supported by the main part. When the toilet seat is closed, the user in front of the main part is detected by the radio wave sensor in a first region, and in a second region higher than the first region. When the toilet seat is open, the user in front of the main part is not detected in the first region by the radio wave sensor, but the user in front of the main part is detected in the second region by the radio wave sensor. The position of the radio wave sensor is not changed between the state in which the toilet seat is open and the state in which the toilet seat is closed.
problem: Accurately detecting user presence in varying toilet seat configurations without repositioning sensors.
constraint: Maintaining sensor position while adapting detection logic to account for physical obstructions caused by the seat.
mechanism: A fixed electromagnetic sensor detects presence in distinct spatial regions by leveraging geometric occlusion caused by a movable obstruction, differentiating detection zones without physical sensor relocation.
mechanism_raw: A fixed radio wave sensor detects users in distinct regions depending on seat position, leveraging geometric occlusion to differentiate detection zones.

abstract: A sludge lance for a tube and shell steam generator that has a central divider plate that extends substantially the length of a central tube lane substantially bisecting a hand hole through which the tube lane can be accessed. The sludge lance has a nozzle with a spring biased, reciprocally movable plunger that extends against the divider plate and is locked in position by a stream of high pressure cleaning fluid that traverses the nozzle and exits through jets to clean sludge from between the tubes. An alignment tool with a swing arm indexes the jets to assure they are properly aligned with the tube rows and spaced from the divider plate.
problem: Cleaning sludge from confined spaces between tubes in a steam generator while maintaining precise alignment of cleaning jets.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise jet alignment with the limited accessibility of the tube lane, requiring a mechanism that can both stabilize and adjust within a constrained space.
mechanism: A fluid-pressure-actuated positioning element is selectively locked in place by a pressurized medium, enabling controlled movement and stabilization within a confined workspace. A mechanical indexing system with a pivoting linkage adjusts the orientation of working elements to maintain alignment with target structures, combining dynamic fluid forces for positioning and mechanical constraints for precision.
mechanism_raw: A spring-biased plunger is locked in position by a high-pressure fluid stream, enabling controlled movement and stabilization during cleaning. An alignment tool with a swing arm indexes the jets to ensure proper alignment with tube rows, combining fluid pressure for positioning and mechanical indexing for precision.

abstract: The present application relates to a steamer which has a steam generator (11) with a steam outlet (33). A steam path extends from the steam outlet to convey steam, and a filter unit (7) is positioned in the steam path. The filter unit has a filter cartridge (24) removably mounted along the steam path having a cartridge housing, a filter medium received in the cartridge housing. The filter unit also has a cartridge inlet and a cartridge outlet which are at or towards a first end (32) of the cartridge housing (34), and a barrier (20) configured to guide the steam to flow in the cartridge housing to a second end (17). The filter unit is spaced from the steam outlet (33), to filter impurities from steam passing along the steam path. The present application also relates to a filter cartridge for a steamer.
problem: Filtering impurities from steam in a steamer while maintaining efficient steam flow through the filter unit.
constraint: Maintaining steam flow velocity and pressure while ensuring thorough filtration, requiring a balance between flow guidance and filter medium exposure.
mechanism: A flow-directing barrier within a filter housing channels the fluid stream toward a downstream end of the filter medium, ensuring uniform exposure and preventing bypass flow. The filter medium is removably positioned and spaced from the outlet to optimize contact time and filtration efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A barrier within the filter cartridge housing directs steam flow toward the second end of the cartridge, ensuring uniform contact with the filter medium and preventing bypass flow. The cartridge is removably mounted and spaced from the steam outlet to optimize filtration efficiency.

abstract: The invention aims to improve the manufacture of flexible goods, such as garments, through the temporary modification of the physical properties of the components to be assembled, facilitating their handling and manipulation later on in the manufacturing process. Attributes that can be affected by this process are the stiffness of the material, the presence of mechanical or physical markings, the density of the material, the air or fluid permeability of the material, the responsiveness of the material to magnetic fields, or the adhesive nature of the material.
problem: Handling and manipulating flexible materials (e.g., garments) during manufacturing without damaging their final properties.
constraint: Ensuring the temporary modification does not permanently alter the material's functional or aesthetic properties, requiring precise control over the duration and intensity of the property change.
mechanism: A reversible property-modification process temporarily alters material characteristics (e.g., stiffness, permeability) during assembly to enable controlled handling, with the modification being reversed post-processing to restore original attributes. The process applies time-limited and intensity-controlled changes to avoid permanent structural or aesthetic degradation.
mechanism_raw: Temporarily modifying material properties (stiffness, permeability, density, etc.) through a process that alters physical characteristics during assembly, enabling easier handling and manipulation. The modification is reversible, preserving the material's original attributes post-processing.

abstract: A device for laying floor and wall covering for outside corners includes two portions, namely a rigid “central” first portion that is substantially in the shape of a hollow tetrahedron or of a quarter of a truncated cone, and a flexible “peripheral” second portion that is substantially triangular in shape and that extends from the periphery of the central portion. The peripheral portion comes to bear against the floor portion and against the wall portions that are disposed facing the device.
problem: Covering outside corners where floor and wall surfaces meet, requiring both structural stability and conformability to irregular geometries.
constraint: Balancing rigidity for structural support with flexibility for surface conformity, ensuring the device remains stable yet adaptable to different corner configurations.
mechanism: A hybrid structural element combines a rigid core (e.g., polyhedral or conical geometry) for load-bearing support with a flexible periphery that adapts to irregular surface contours. The rigid core maintains corner integrity while the flexible periphery conforms to varying angles and surface geometries, balancing stability and adaptability.
mechanism_raw: A rigid central portion (tetrahedron or truncated cone shape) provides structural support, while a flexible peripheral portion conforms to the floor and wall surfaces. The combination allows the device to adapt to varying angles and surfaces while maintaining integrity at the corner.

abstract: An apparatus includes a display panel. In one example, the display panel includes an array of subpixels in a first, a second, and a third colors. Subpixels in the first, second, and third colors are alternatively arranged in every three adjacent rows of the array of subpixels. Every two adjacent rows of the array of subpixels are staggered with each other. A first subpixel in one of the first, second, and third colors and a second subpixel in a same color as the first subpixel are offset by 3 units in the horizontal axis and 4 units in the vertical axis. The first and second subpixels have a minimum distance among subpixels in the same color.
problem: Optimizing subpixel arrangement in a display panel to maximize color accuracy and resolution while minimizing visual artifacts.
constraint: Maintaining consistent color balance and pixel density across the display while adhering to manufacturing tolerances for subpixel placement and spacing.
mechanism: A subpixel array uses staggered row alignment with controlled horizontal and vertical offsets between same-color elements to enforce minimum spacing and reduce color mixing. The arrangement enhances spatial uniformity and color accuracy by distributing subpixels in a pattern that minimizes visual artifacts while maintaining consistent pixel density.
mechanism_raw: Subpixels of three colors are arranged in alternating rows with staggered alignment between adjacent rows. Specific horizontal and vertical offsets (3 units horizontal, 4 units vertical) between same-color subpixels ensure minimum spacing, enhancing uniformity and reducing color mixing errors.

abstract: A creased sticky note with a sticky body, an adhesive layer and at least one crease is provided. The sticky body has an adhesion portion and a flexible portion disposed adjacent to the adhesion portion. The adhesive layer is disposed on the adhesion portion. The at least one crease is disposed on the adhesion portion, or is disposed between the adhesion portion and the flexible portion, or is disposed on a stress hinders area of the flexible portion which is near the adhesion portion.
problem: Sticky notes are difficult to handle or reposition without losing adhesion or causing unintended sticking due to uniform stiffness and adhesion across the entire surface.
constraint: Balancing adhesion strength and flexibility so the note can be easily manipulated without compromising its ability to stick or leave residue.
mechanism: Varying local mechanical compliance across a surface by introducing controlled discontinuities in stiffness, enabling selective bending or separation in predefined regions while preserving functional properties (e.g., adhesion) in other regions.
mechanism_raw: Strategic placement of creases in specific regions (adhesion portion, flexible portion, or stress-hindering areas) allows controlled bending or separation, enabling localized flexibility while maintaining adhesion where needed.

abstract: Methods of making sintered articles from powder metal carbide compositions by additive manufacturing techniques are described herein. Sintered carbide articles fabricated by such additive manufacturing techniques, in some embodiments, exhibit densities equaling articles formed according to conventional techniques employed in powder metallurgy. For example, a method of manufacturing an article comprises providing sintered cemented carbide powder comprising a hard particle phase including tungsten carbide and a metallic binder phase and forming the sintered cemented carbide powder into a green article by one or more additive manufacturing techniques. The green article is sintered to provide a sintered article having density greater than 90% theoretical full density, wherein the green article has a density less than 50% theoretical full density prior to sintering.
problem: Additive manufacturing of powder metal carbide articles typically results in low-density 'green' parts that cannot achieve the structural integrity required for industrial applications without conventional sintering methods.
constraint: Maintaining uniform density and structural integrity during sintering while starting from a fragile, low-density green part.
mechanism: Forming a fragile, low-density precursor structure via additive deposition, then applying thermal energy to induce controlled densification of particulate material, achieving structural integrity through phase transformation or sintering.
mechanism_raw: Forming a low-density green article via additive manufacturing, then sintering it to achieve high density (>90% theoretical) by leveraging controlled densification of the powdered material during thermal processing.

abstract: In the multilayer bottle of the present invention, an outermost layer and an innermost layer are each composed of a polyester (Z1); a barrier layer is composed of a resin composition containing 40 to 99 parts by mass of a polyamide (X) and 1 to 60 parts by mass of a polyester (Z2); an alkali compound (A) is blended in the resin composition; and furthermore, the resin composition satisfies the following formulae (1) to (3). 0.01≤P≤6.5 (1)3.2≤M≤73.1 (2)M≥29.2−0.218α (3) In the formulae, P represents a molar concentration (μmol/g) of phosphorus atoms; M represents a molar concentration (μmol/g) of alkali (earth) metal atoms; and α represents the parts by mass of the polyamide (X) contained in the resin composition.
problem: Multilayer packaging requires barrier layers that effectively block gas/moisture permeation while maintaining structural compatibility with adjacent layers.
constraint: Balancing barrier effectiveness with material processability and adhesion between layers to avoid delamination or brittleness.
mechanism: Combining chemically distinct polymeric materials in precise stoichiometric ratios to optimize interfacial compatibility and barrier performance through molecular-level interactions, ensuring structural cohesion between layers.
mechanism_raw: Blending a polyamide with a polyester and an alkali compound in precise molar ratios (governed by formulas for phosphorus and alkali metal concentrations) to optimize barrier properties through chemical interaction and phase compatibility.

abstract: The present invention relates to a agave syrup product having a low water content. The agave syrup product retains the physical and palatable properties of untreated agave syrup while having a prolonged shelf-life. It can be advantageously used to sweeten beverages (such as hot beverages) and in the manufacture of pharmaceutical compositions (such as throat lozenges) and/or confectionary.
problem: Agave syrup's high water content leads to microbial growth and degradation, shortening shelf-life without altering its palatable properties.
constraint: Achieving sufficient water reduction to extend shelf-life without denaturing sugars or altering viscosity and sweetness.
mechanism: Applying controlled thermal or mechanical energy to reduce volatile component content while maintaining compositional stability, thereby inhibiting biological degradation without altering functional characteristics (e.g., viscosity, sweetness).
mechanism_raw: Reducing water content through controlled dehydration while preserving the syrup's physical and chemical composition, thereby inhibiting spoilage organisms without compromising taste or texture.

abstract: A compressed natural gas storage and dispensing system having descending pressure bulk storage banks in fluid communication with a supply source for CNG and dispensing storage banks in fluid communication with the descending pressure bulk storage bank, both banks being in fluid communication with fuel dispensers, wherein the delivery pressure of the CNG during, simultaneous refueling of CNG powered vehicles is equalized.
problem: Simultaneous refueling of multiple CNG vehicles causes pressure imbalances in storage systems, leading to inconsistent delivery pressure and potential system inefficiency.
constraint: Maintaining pressure equilibrium across interconnected storage and dispensing banks while accommodating variable refueling rates and vehicle demand.
mechanism: Interconnecting multiple storage units with descending pressure states to dynamically redistribute fluidic energy across a network, ensuring uniform delivery pressure despite variable demand through passive pressure equilibration.
mechanism_raw: Using descending pressure bulk storage banks in fluid communication with dispensing banks to dynamically equalize pressure across the system during refueling, ensuring uniform delivery pressure regardless of demand fluctuations.

abstract: The present invention relates to a door (3) of a domestic cooking oven (1), in particular of the pyrolytic type. The door (3) comprises at least a first and a second plate (31, 32) and a first and a second upright beam (8, 9). The first plate (31) defines an outer surface of the door (3) and the two upright beams (8, 9) receiving at least the second plate (32) are fixed internally relative thereto. The door (3) further comprises a first and a second locking element (14, 15) removably engaged to the first and second upright beams (8, 9) and configured to be selectively movable between an operating position, wherein they are engaged to the respective upright beams (8, 9) in such a way as to lock at least the second plate (32) in a mounting position, and at least one unlocked position, wherein they enable the second plate (32) to be extracted from the door (3).
problem: Securely locking a removable inner plate in a high-temperature oven door while enabling safe extraction for maintenance or replacement.
constraint: Balancing secure locking under high-temperature conditions with ease of manual unlocking and plate extraction without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A pair of selectively movable locking elements engage with upright beams to fix the inner plate in place during operation, and disengage to allow extraction when unlocked. The mechanical interlock ensures positional stability under thermal stress while permitting controlled access.
mechanism_raw: A pair of selectively movable locking elements engage with upright beams to fix the inner plate in place during operation, and disengage to allow extraction when unlocked. The mechanical interlock ensures positional stability under thermal stress while permitting controlled access.

abstract: An article of water resistant clothing that includes a water resistant underlay layer. The water resistant underlay layer includes at least one compression panel to compress a portion of a body of a user wearing the water resistant clothing. The article of swimwear includes a water resistant overlay layer disposed over the water resistant underlay layer. The water resistant overlay layer exposes at least a portion of the water resistant underlay layer through material of the water resistant overlay layer. The article of water resistant clothing includes a set of fasteners embedded in at least one of the water resistant underlay layer or the water resistant overlay layer to couple the water resistant underlay layer to the water resistant overlay layer.
problem: Combining water resistance with targeted body compression in wearable clothing without sacrificing adjustability or waterproofing.
constraint: Maintaining water resistance across the entire garment while enabling variable compression and selective exposure of the underlay through the overlay.
mechanism: A layered system uses a water-resistant underlay with embedded compression panels and an overlay layer with openings that expose the underlay. Fasteners couple the layers, allowing the overlay to dynamically adjust compression zones while maintaining a sealed barrier against water ingress.
mechanism_raw: A layered system uses a water-resistant underlay with embedded compression panels and an overlay layer with openings that expose the underlay. Fasteners couple the layers, allowing the overlay to dynamically adjust compression zones while maintaining a sealed barrier against water ingress.

abstract: A system and method which allows for a pre-constructed article of clothing to having printing on substantially all of its external surface area. Specifically, an image may be simultaneously printed across multiple components of a clothing article. The method generally provides for transfer of a digital image, such as a digital photograph, to be applied to an article of clothing in a manner that prints an entire two-dimensional surface of the clothing with a coherent image, that maintains coherency when the article of clothing is worn. There is also provided an article of clothing produced using the systems and methods.
problem: Applying a coherent digital image across multiple pre-existing components of a 3D clothing article without distortion when the garment is worn.
constraint: Preserving image coherency across non-planar, multi-component surfaces while accommodating movement and deformation of the garment during wear.
mechanism: Simultaneous printing across all external surfaces of a pre-constructed garment using aligned transfer techniques, ensuring image continuity by accounting for component geometry and spatial relationships during the printing process.
mechanism_raw: Simultaneous printing across all external surfaces of a pre-constructed garment using aligned transfer techniques, ensuring image continuity by accounting for component geometry and spatial relationships during the printing process.

abstract: Flares with consumable weights connected to a forward end of the grain of the flare are disclosed. Also disclosed are consumable weight components for flares. The consumable weight components include a metal material within a matrix. Also disclosed are methods for fabricating a flare and methods for using a flare. Use of the consumable weights in the flares may reduce the amount of debris falling to ground.
problem: Reducing ground debris from flares during operation while maintaining their functional performance.
constraint: Ensuring the consumable weights fully combust without altering the flare's trajectory, burn rate, or safety characteristics.
mechanism: Consumable weights composed of a metal matrix are attached to the forward end of the flare grain. These weights burn away during ignition, reducing the mass of non-combusted debris that falls to the ground.
mechanism_raw: Consumable weights composed of a metal matrix are attached to the forward end of the flare grain. These weights burn away during ignition, reducing the mass of non-combusted debris that falls to the ground.

abstract: A defibrillator system optimizes the timing and manner of applying a defibrillator charge to a patient based upon data provided to the defibrillator from a utility module or one or more external devices. A parameter module on the utility module provides the defibrillator with patient parameter information. Devices external to the utility module may provide the utility module with coaching data that the utility module may pass through to the defibrillator as a proxy to the external devices. The utility module may also provide external devices with patient data that the utility module may pass through to the external devices as a proxy to the defibrillator on a scheduled or other basis. The utility module may additionally provide a reserve of power to enable defibrillators to be used where power is unavailable and to enable defibrillators to deliver multiple charges more readily anywhere, anytime.
problem: Optimizing defibrillator charge delivery timing and ensuring reliable power availability in emergency scenarios with variable external device inputs.
constraint: Maintaining low-latency data synchronization and power delivery reliability across heterogeneous external devices and critical defibrillation workflows.
mechanism: A utility module acts as a bidirectional proxy, relaying patient data and coaching inputs between external devices and the defibrillator while providing a reserve power source. This enables real-time parameter optimization and sustained operation even in power-limited environments.
mechanism_raw: A utility module acts as a bidirectional proxy, relaying patient data and coaching inputs between external devices and the defibrillator while providing a reserve power source. This enables real-time parameter optimization and sustained operation even in power-limited environments.
residual_terms: ["bidirectional proxy", "patient data", "coaching inputs", "reserve power source", "parameter optimization"]

abstract: A cleaning system can be used on an intermediate bulk container. The cleaning system includes a chemical tank, filled with a chemical liquid. A first chemical pump and a second chemical pump, are mechanically coupled to the chemical tank and configured to pump the contents of the chemical tank. A dispensing valve is mechanically coupled to the first chemical pump and the second chemical pump and configured to dispense the chemical liquid. A water tank, is filled with water. A first water pump and a second water pump are mechanically coupled to the water tank and configured to dispense the water. A topside washing assembly is attached to the chemical tank and mechanically coupled to the first chemical pump and the second chemical pump. The topside washing assembly disperses water from the water tank in order to clean the chemical tank.
problem: Effective cleaning of an intermediate bulk container using multiple fluids (chemical and water) while preventing cross-contamination and ensuring thorough coverage.
constraint: Balancing flow rates between chemical and water systems to avoid mixing while ensuring sufficient pressure and coverage for cleaning.
mechanism: Two independent fluid delivery systems are coordinated through a control valve to manage sequential or simultaneous flow of distinct fluids, preventing cross-contamination while ensuring coverage. A distribution assembly disperses one fluid to clean a containment vessel, leveraging the dual-system architecture to balance pressure and timing between the fluids.
mechanism_raw: Dual pumps for each fluid (chemical and water) are mechanically coupled to their respective tanks and coordinated via a dispensing valve to control flow rates and timing. A topside washing assembly disperses water from the water tank to clean the chemical tank, leveraging the dual-pump system to manage sequential or simultaneous delivery of fluids.

abstract: A prefiner (28) is described and includes a chamber (34) for receiving molten glass exiting a submerged combustion melter. The prefiner (28) also includes a foam breaker (36) and an exit conduit (38). The molten glass holding chamber includes a top portion (42), a bottom portion (40), and an enclosing sidewall (44). The top portion (42) includes an opening to accommodate the foam breaker (36), which is positioned to break the glass bubbles within the chamber. The exit conduit (38) resides within the chamber (34) and is in fluid communication with an outlet (68) in the sidewall (44). The exit conduit (38) is positioned to permit molten glass to flow from the lower section of the chamber to the outlet (68) and to the next stage of processing, typically a finer.
problem: Removing gas bubbles (foam) from molten glass exiting a submerged combustion melter to ensure a defect-free final product.
constraint: Maintaining optimal positioning of the foam breaker and exit conduit to ensure efficient bubble removal without disrupting the molten glass flow or introducing thermal gradients.
mechanism: A physical disruption element positioned at the upper region of a containment chamber collapses gas bubbles within a viscous medium. A submerged exit pathway in the lower region allows degassed material to flow out while retaining residual bubbles in the upper portion, enabling staged separation based on buoyancy and spatial positioning.
mechanism_raw: A foam breaker positioned at the top of a holding chamber physically disrupts and collapses bubbles within the molten glass. An exit conduit submerged in the lower section of the chamber allows degassed molten glass to flow out while retaining residual bubbles in the upper portion, enabling staged separation.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a specific class on pigment reactive silicone polymers that contain both higher alkyl groups and reactive trialkoxy silanes present in the backbone of a specific silicone polymer. By carefully selecting the proper reactive silicone polymer and treating the pigment with said polymer a surprisingly stable and efficient coating is applied the pigment, most importantly ZnO and TiO2 as to render photo stability and alter solubility of the pigment in a variety of solvents.
problem: Applying a stable, efficient coating to pigments (e.g., ZnO, TiO₂) to enhance photo stability and alter solubility in solvents.
constraint: Selecting the precise ratio of alkyl groups to trialkoxy silanes to balance reactivity, stability, and solubility without compromising the pigment's functional properties.
mechanism: A reactive polymer with dual functional groups (hydrophobic and hydrolyzable moieties) forms a covalent or strong physical bond with a particulate surface. The molecular structure enables controlled reactivity during application, creating a durable coating that resists environmental degradation and modulates solubility through tailored surface chemistry.
mechanism_raw: A reactive silicone polymer containing both higher alkyl groups and trialkoxy silane moieties in its backbone forms a covalent or strong physical bond with the pigment surface. The specific molecular structure enables controlled reactivity during application, creating a durable coating that resists photodegradation and modulates solubility.

abstract: To overcome defects in the supply of pressurized lubricant, a hydrodynamic bearing for guiding a shaft (14) includes a stationary outer annular wall, a rotatable inner annular wall (20), and a space (22) between the walls. The outer annular wall comprises an opening for supplying pressurized lubricant to the space so as to form a film of load-bearing fluid. The bearing includes a cavity (30) externally defined by the inner annular wall (20) and axially defined by two transverse annular walls (31A, 31B) secured to the shaft (14) and arranged on both sides of the cavity. The inner annular wall (20) comprises fluid connection orifices (32) connecting the cavity (30) to the space (22). The cavity (30) is divided into compartments (50, 52) by a partition wall (48) configured such that the cavity forms a lubricant supply for a transient operational phase.
problem: Ensuring a continuous supply of pressurized lubricant to a hydrodynamic bearing during transient operational phases (e.g., startup, shutdown) when external lubricant supply may be insufficient.
constraint: Designing the partition and orifice geometry to balance lubricant distribution between compartments and the load-bearing space, ensuring adequate supply during both steady-state and transient conditions.
mechanism: A partitioned reservoir within a load-bearing structure, divided into compartments by a barrier, maintains localized lubricant storage. Fluid communication pathways connect the compartments to the load-bearing space, allowing lubricant redistribution during transient phases while preserving pressure and film integrity through geometric constraints.
mechanism_raw: A partitioned cavity within the bearing, divided by a wall into compartments, acts as a localized reservoir. Fluid connection orifices link the cavity to the bearing's load-bearing space, allowing lubricant to flow from the compartments during transient phases while maintaining pressure and film integrity.

abstract: A combination for a firearm which creates an improved firearm. An upper chassis is created which is formed from a first housing and a second housing which, once independently formed, are permanently secured to each other. The upper chassis provides a first opening through which a spent cartridge is discharged and a second opening which permits a variety of attachments to be selectively attached to the upper chassis to customize the firearm to the user and activity.
problem: Customizing a firearm to accommodate user-specific attachments and activities while maintaining structural integrity and reliable cartridge discharge.
constraint: Ensuring the permanent joint between the two housings maintains structural rigidity and alignment while enabling modular attachment compatibility across diverse accessories.
mechanism: A modular structural assembly formed by permanently joining two independently configured housings creates standardized attachment interfaces while maintaining rigidity. The dual-housing design enables selective accessory integration through predefined connection points, balancing structural integrity with functional adaptability across diverse operational requirements.
mechanism_raw: A modular upper chassis formed by permanently securing two independently molded housings creates a first opening for spent cartridge discharge and a second opening for selective attachment of accessories. The dual-housing design allows for standardized attachment points without compromising the structural or functional requirements of the firearm.

abstract: The present invention provides novel watermelon line 74WA002 and plant parts, seed, and tissue culture therefrom. The invention also provides methods for producing a watermelon plant by crossing the watermelon plants of the invention with themselves or another watermelon plant. The invention also provides watermelon plants produced from such a crossing as well as plant parts, seed, and tissue culture therefrom. Further provided are methods of producing triploid watermelon seed and plants and seedless watermelon fruit produced therefrom as well as the triploid watermelon seed and plants and the seedless fruits produced by such methods.
problem: Producing seedless watermelon fruit and triploid plants with viable reproduction.
constraint: Balancing genetic stability and fertility in triploid plants to ensure viable fruit production without compromising seedlessness.
mechanism: Combining organisms with differing chromosome sets through controlled breeding to induce triploidy, using chromosomal imbalance to suppress reproduction while maintaining viability.
mechanism_raw: Inducing triploidy through controlled cross-breeding of polyploid and diploid watermelon lines, leveraging chromosomal imbalance to suppress seed development while maintaining fruit viability.

abstract: A pneumatic tire includes: an annular structure that is cylindrical and metal where at least an outer side surface in the radial direction is a rough surface; a tread rubber layer that will become a tread portion provided along a circumferential direction of the annular structure on an outer side of the annular structure; and a carcass portion including fibers covered with rubber, provided on at least both sides in a direction parallel to a center axis of the cylindrical structure including the annular structure and the tread rubber layer.
reason: The invention primarily describes material and structural combinations (metal annular structure, rough surface, fiber-reinforced rubber) without a causal functional mechanism that can be abstracted beyond tire design.

abstract: A tank fitting apparatus and method is provided. The tank fitting apparatus includes a bottom plate apparatus. The bottom plate apparatus includes a bottom plate having a bottom surface, a top surface, and a bottom plate passageway. The bottom plate apparatus further includes a bolt connected to the bottom plate and extending from the top surface of the bottom plate. The tank fitting apparatus further includes a valve apparatus. The valve apparatus includes a pipe and a valve integrally formed with the pipe. The valve is movable between an open valve position and a closed valve position. A top plate integrally formed on the pipe and extends outwardly from the pipe. The valve apparatus has a connected tank fitting position where the bolt of the bottom plate apparatus extends through the top plate of the valve apparatus to connect the valve apparatus with the bottom plate apparatus.
problem: Reliably connecting a valve assembly to a tank while enabling adjustable positioning and secure sealing during operation.
constraint: Ensuring the bolt-top plate interface maintains structural integrity and sealing while permitting valve actuation.
mechanism: Employing a single mechanical linkage through a plate to connect components, enabling both assembly and movement between operational states while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using a bolt extending through a top plate to mechanically link the valve apparatus to the bottom plate, allowing assembly and valve movement between open/closed positions via a single connection point.

abstract: A variable inlet device for a vehicle includes a first pipe and a second pipe arranged in parallel to each other, and a variable injection pipe configured to allow an exit thereof to be selectively connected to an entrance of the first pipe or an entrance of the second pipe by a rotation movement and a back and forth movement.
problem: Selectively directing fluid flow between two parallel paths in a vehicle inlet system.
constraint: Achieving precise alignment and sealing between the variable pipe and target pipe entrances during movement.
mechanism: Using coordinated rotational and translational motion of a variable conduit to dynamically align its exit with one of two target inlets, enabling selective path connection without manual adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Combining rotational and translational movement of a variable injection pipe to dynamically connect its exit to either the first or second pipe entrance, enabling path selection without manual reconfiguration.

abstract: A control valve device includes a valve body having an actuator port connected to an actuator and a relief passage configured to allow the actuator port to communicate with a return passage, a spool slidably assembled into the valve body and configured to allow the actuator port to selectively communicate with a supply side or a return side, a relief valve configured to open/close the relief passage to control pressure of the actuator port, and an on/off valve assembled into an assembling hole which is formed in the valve body. The on/off valve configured to allow the actuator port to communicate with the relief passage through the assembling hole at the time of valve open.
problem: Controlling actuator port pressure and flow direction in a hydraulic/pneumatic system while enabling fail-safe pressure relief.
constraint: Coordinating the spool, relief valve, and on/off valve timing to ensure pressure stability and safe operation during transitions.
mechanism: Combining a directional flow controller, a pressure regulator, and a safety valve that activates during operation to prevent overpressure, ensuring coordinated control of fluid dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a spool for flow direction, a relief valve for pressure regulation, and an on/off valve that opens the relief passage during valve operation to prevent overpressure.

abstract: An example method includes positioning a thermal bus bar into a bus bar support channel of a cooling wall, the cooling wall comprising a plurality of thermal bus bars. The positioning comprises removably connecting first portions of at least two dripless connectors coupled to a fluid flow path of the thermal bus bar to second portions of the dripless connectors coupled to coolant transport lines that receive and return coolant from a coolant source. The method further includes flowing coolant received from the coolant transport lines through the fluid flow path and returning the coolant to the coolant transport lines. The thermal bus bar is positioned while coolant provided by the coolant transport lines is flowing through other thermal bus bars of the cooling wall.
problem: Replacing or installing a thermal bus bar in a cooling wall without interrupting coolant flow through other bus bars.
constraint: The connectors must maintain a leak-free seal during connection/disconnection while coolant flows through adjacent bus bars.
mechanism: A coupling mechanism enables removable connection of fluid lines to a heat transfer element while maintaining a sealed interface, allowing maintenance of one element without interrupting fluid flow through adjacent elements.
mechanism_raw: Dripless connectors allow removable coupling of coolant lines to a thermal bus bar while other bars remain operational, enabling maintenance or replacement without system shutdown.

abstract: A portable cutting tool includes a blade and a motor for driving the blade to rotate. The motor has a motor output shaft. A guard assembly includes an upper guard and a lower guard which is used for receiving the motor. A base is connected to the upper guard. The base further includes a front portion connected to the upper guard, a rear portion extending longitudinally, and a gripping portion disposed between the front portion and the rear portion. The blade shaft is perpendicular to the motor output shaft.
reason: The perpendicular blade and motor shaft arrangement is a structural design choice for ergonomic or mechanical layout, not a causal mechanism solving a problem through a functional relationship.

abstract: This invention relates to a nose assembly for a chainsaw guide bar for wood harvesting and a chainsaw guide bar having the same. The nose assembly (400) comprising: a pair of nose side plates (410, 420; 470); and a sprocket and bearing assembly adapted to be clamped between the pair of nose side plates (410, 420; 470) and comprising an idler sprocket (450); wherein at least one of the pair of the nose side plates (410, 420; 470) is provided at an inside surface thereof facing to the sprocket and bearing assembly with one or more lubricant conveying channels for lubricating the sprocket and bearing assembly. The chainsaw guide bars according to the present invention enable flow of lubricant to moving parts in order to reduce friction of these moving parts as a saw chain rotates though the guide bar.
problem: Reducing friction and wear in moving parts of a chainsaw guide bar nose assembly during chain rotation.
constraint: The channels must be positioned within the structural side plates without compromising their clamping or load-bearing integrity.
mechanism: Embedded fluid-conveying pathways within structural components deliver lubricant directly to moving mechanical interfaces, ensuring continuous lubrication without external routing while preserving structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Integrated lubricant-conveying channels in the nose side plates deliver lubricant directly to the sprocket and bearing assembly, ensuring continuous lubrication without external routing.

abstract: A counterweight attachment and removal device which can connect lifting assemblies and a counterweight without precisely adjusting the construction machine position and the counterweight position, and which can attach the counterweight to adjust lateral direction. The device (18) includes a link (28) which is connected pivotally to the rear end of the construction machine, and a pair of coupling units (32, 32) which are connected to the leading end of the link (28). Each coupling unit (32) has a pair of coupling pieces (38, 40), a connecting pin (42) and a position adjustment member (44, 45). The coupling pieces (38, 40) extend from the link (28) and are able to tilt and move pivotally around the central axis (O). The connecting pin (42) is detachably connected to the extension ends between the connecting pieces (38, 40). Each adjustment member (44, 45) is disposed on the inner surface of the connecting piece (38, 40).
problem: Attaching a counterweight to a construction machine without requiring precise alignment of the machine or counterweight positions.
constraint: The coupling units must balance flexibility for adjustment with sufficient rigidity to securely fasten the counterweight under load.
mechanism: A multi-axis adjustable coupling system with pivotally connected units and position-adjustment elements accommodates misalignment during attachment of a balancing mass, balancing flexibility with load-bearing rigidity.
mechanism_raw: Pivotally connected coupling units with tilting coupling pieces and adjustable position members allow lateral and angular adjustment during counterweight attachment, accommodating misalignment.
residual_terms: ["multi-axis adjustable coupling system", "pivotally connected units", "position-adjustment elements", "load-bearing rigidity"]

abstract: An internal combustion engine comprising: a plurality of cylinders; at least one intake manifold, which receives fresh air from the outside; a plurality of intake channels, each connecting a cylinder to the intake manifold; and an intake sound amplification device, which is provided with an amplification pipe, an insulating element sealing the amplification pipe in a tight manner, a plurality of amplification channels, each originating from a corresponding intake channel, and an amplification manifold, which, on one side, is connected to all amplification channels and, on the other side, is connected to the amplification pipe.
problem: Amplifying intake sound in an internal combustion engine for noise tuning or performance feedback.
constraint: The amplification channels and pipe must be tuned to target frequencies without disrupting engine airflow or performance.
mechanism: A resonant amplification system uses a manifold connected to multiple tuned channels and a resonant pathway to selectively amplify specific acoustic frequencies from a fluid flow without disrupting flow dynamics.
mechanism_raw: An amplification manifold connected to multiple channels originating from intake channels and an amplification pipe creates a resonant pathway that amplifies specific sound frequencies.
residual_terms: ["resonant amplification system", "tuned channels", "resonant pathway", "fluid flow dynamics"]

abstract: A lamp includes a base unit and a shade unit. The base unit includes a case body, push button and rotary switches, and an interconnect member connected to the rotary switch. The shade unit includes a shade body connected to the interconnect member, a light module and a connect member. The shade unit is slidable along the interconnect member between a switch-on position, where the connect member is spaced apart from the pushbutton switch so that the light module is switched on and the shade body is rotatable to rotate the rotary switch to adjust brightness of the light module, and a switch-off position, where the connect member abuts against the pushbutton switch so that the light module is switched off.
problem: Mechanically controlling the power state and brightness of a lamp through physical positioning of its shade unit.
constraint: The physical geometry of the interconnect member and the spacing between the connect member and pushbutton switch must precisely define the switch-on and switch-off positions without requiring external power or complex electronics.
mechanism: A mechanical positioning system translates linear and rotational movement of a shade unit into discrete electrical contact states (on/off) and variable resistance for brightness control, using the geometry of a positioning element and mechanical switches to define precise actuation points without external power.
mechanism_raw: Sliding movement of the shade unit along an interconnect member translates positional changes into electrical contact states: moving the connect member away from a pushbutton switch activates the light, while abutting it deactivates the light. Rotational motion of the shade body further adjusts brightness via a rotary switch.

abstract: A monofilament having, in cross section, a first width and a second width being orthogonal to the first width and being greater than the first width is helically wound about the circumference surface of the mandrel. Each helical unit included in the configured helix of the monofilament includes a pair of legs, a first coupling portion coupled between said pair of legs, and a second coupling portion coupled between one leg of said pair of legs and the other leg of a pair of legs in an adjacent helical unit. The second width of said first coupling portion is oriented along the axial direction of the mandrel. The first coupling portion in each helical unit in the helix is pressed such that the second width of the first coupling portion is widened in its width direction, thereby forming an engagement head.
problem: Creating a helical structure with interlocking engagement features from a single monofilament material.
constraint: The cross-sectional dimensions of the monofilament (first width < second width) and the controlled deformation of coupling portions must balance structural strength with the ability to form reliable engagement heads without material failure.
mechanism: A helical structure formed by winding a filament with varying cross-sectional dimensions, where selective deformation of coupling regions during winding creates mechanical interlocks between adjacent helical units, maintaining structural integrity along the axis.
mechanism_raw: Helical winding of a monofilament with orthogonal width dimensions allows coupling portions to be selectively deformed (widened) during winding, forming engagement heads that mechanically lock adjacent helical units together. The axial orientation of the coupling portions ensures structural integrity along the mandrel's length.

abstract: A device for the cyclonic separation of solid particles contained in a fluid, comprising a primary cyclone chamber, a secondary cyclone chamber, an inlet channel for fluid loaded with solid particles opening into the primary cyclone chamber, an outlet channel for fluid cleaned of the solid particles connected to the secondary cyclone chamber, and a ducting unit connecting the primary cyclone chamber to the secondary cyclone chamber and surrounded by the primary cyclone chamber. The ducting unit comprises a core delimiting the secondary cyclone chamber and having at least one helical groove having a bottom which diverges away from an axis of the secondary cyclone chamber in a direction towards the latter, and a cap covering a part of the core in such a way as to delimit, with the groove, a channel connecting the primary cyclone chamber to the secondary cyclone chamber.
problem: Efficiently separating solid particles from a fluid using cyclonic action in a compact, multi-stage system.
constraint: The divergence angle of the groove and the cap-core geometry must optimize fluid velocity and particle trajectory to maximize separation without causing excessive pressure drop or structural weakness.
mechanism: A multi-stage separation system where a helical flow path, created by a diverging channel between primary and secondary chambers, increases centrifugal force on particles in a fluid stream, enhancing separation efficiency while maintaining structural integration between chambers.
mechanism_raw: A helical groove on the core of the ducting unit diverges away from the secondary cyclone chamber axis, creating a channel that directs fluid flow between the primary and secondary chambers. This helical path increases centrifugal force on particles, enhancing separation efficiency while maintaining structural integration between chambers.

abstract: System-on-chip (SOC) products using high frequency, wideband, highly linear, CMOS and BiCMOS processes will be the next evolution of wireless and wireline communications integrated circuits. Aspects described herein can provide enhanced overall performance over existing prior art single-ended, wideband RF amplifier topologies. A single-ended third order intermodulation distortion nulling circuit can extend the dynamic range for wideband amplifiers up to an order-of-magnitude, without a DC power or noise figure (NF) penalty. The application of distortion nulling can be extended to all the building blocks used in CMOS/BiCMOS RF transceivers to improve performance. The application of this concept to all of the building blocks in an RF transceiver will allow the dynamic range of the transceiver to be increased without suffering a DC power dissipation increase or a significant noise increase.
problem: Reducing intermodulation distortion in wideband RF amplifiers without increasing power consumption or noise.
constraint: The nulling circuit must maintain signal integrity and phase alignment across wide bandwidths while operating within the power and noise constraints of CMOS/BiCMOS processes.
mechanism: A distortion compensation system that generates an inverse distortion signal to cancel out third-order intermodulation components produced by a main amplifier, using a circuit topology that balances linearity and signal paths to extend dynamic range without additional power or noise penalties.
mechanism_raw: A third-order intermodulation distortion nulling circuit generates an inverse distortion signal that cancels out distortion components produced by the main amplifier. This is achieved through precise circuit topology that balances linearity and signal paths, extending dynamic range without additional DC power or noise figure penalties.

abstract: A total runway safety system (TRSS) and method measures, monitors, manages, and informs flight crew on the progress of takeoffs and landings and of any hazardous runway conditions. In some embodiments, the TRSS measures, monitors, and informs flight crew of longitudinal and lateral runway tracks thus preventing overruns and veer-offs during takeoffs and landings. In some embodiments, backscatter of infrared laser beams emitted by the aircraft is used to evaluate groundspeed and the reflectivity of the runway surface to make estimates of the surface conditions, roughness and contamination, which affects rolling and braking efforts and acceleration. In some embodiments TRSS evaluates runway surface and predicts tire-surface rolling and braking coefficient of friction. In some embodiments, GPS and similar navigation data, and ATC/airport reported runway braking conditions are evaluated along with the infrared laser, ultrasound and digital images to find best estimates of the runway remaining, current speed, acceleration, and jerk.
problem: Preventing runway overruns and veer-offs by dynamically assessing runway surface conditions and aircraft state during takeoff/landing.
constraint: The system must integrate heterogeneous sensor inputs with varying update rates and accuracy into a unified model that operates reliably under diverse environmental conditions (e.g., rain, ice, darkness) without false alarms.
mechanism: A predictive safety system that integrates heterogeneous sensor inputs (e.g., surface reflectivity, position, acceleration, roughness) to estimate real-time tire-surface friction coefficients, informing models for remaining runway length and hazard detection under diverse environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: Sensor fusion combines infrared laser backscatter (for surface reflectivity and groundspeed), GPS/navigation data (for position and acceleration), and digital imaging/ultrasound (for surface roughness) to estimate real-time tire-surface friction coefficients. These estimates inform predictive models for remaining runway length and hazard detection.

abstract: A phase interpolator includes a current generating circuit, a current controlling circuit and a signal generating circuit, wherein the current generating circuit is arranged to generate a current; and the current controlling circuit is arranged to generate a control signal to the current generating circuit to control a current value of the current. The signal generating circuit includes a capacitor, wherein the signal generating circuit generates a phase interpolation signal by using the capacitor to receive the current, wherein a phase of the phase interpolation signal is varied according to the current.
problem: Need to generate a phase-interpolated signal with precisely controllable phase in an electrical circuit.
constraint: The phase must be precisely controlled by the current value, requiring stable current generation and consistent capacitor charging characteristics to maintain accuracy across operating conditions.
mechanism: A variable current source charges a capacitive element, and the phase of the output signal is directly proportional to the current value, enabling phase interpolation through current-controlled charging characteristics.
mechanism_raw: A control signal adjusts the current value delivered by a current generating circuit; this variable current charges a capacitor in a signal generating circuit, and the phase of the resulting signal varies directly according to the current value, enabling phase interpolation through current-controlled capacitor charging.

abstract: A method for making ice cream including the following steps, performed in the following order: heating the side walls of the processing container to a preset preheating temperature; placing a basic ice cream mixture in the processing chamber after the step of heating the side walls of the processing container to a preset preheating temperature; deactivating any infectious agents which may be present in the basic mixture by activating the thermal treatment system in heating mode for a predetermined time in order to pasteurize the basic mixture inside the processing chamber; keeping the basic mixture, previously subjected to the thermal treatment inside the processing chamber, for a predetermined hold time.
problem: Need to effectively pasteurize a food mixture (ice cream) inside a processing chamber while ensuring uniform heat transfer and microbial safety.
constraint: The preheating temperature must be set appropriately to ensure effective pasteurization without overheating or damaging the mixture, and the hold time must be sufficient to achieve the desired microbial reduction.
mechanism: A containment surface is preheated to a target temperature before introducing the material, ensuring immediate and uniform thermal contact; the material is then subjected to rapid thermal treatment followed by a controlled hold period to achieve pathogen deactivation.
mechanism_raw: The side walls of the processing container are preheated to a preset temperature before the mixture is introduced, ensuring immediate and uniform thermal contact; when the mixture is placed inside, the preheated walls enable rapid and effective thermal treatment for pasteurization, followed by a controlled hold time to complete pathogen deactivation.

abstract: A material sorting system sorts materials, such as scrap pieces composed of unknown metal alloys, as a function of their detected x-ray fluorescence. The x-ray fluorescence may be converted into an elemental composition signature that is then compared to an elemental composition signature of a reference material in order to identify and/or classify each of the materials, which are then sorted into separate groups based on such an identification/classification. The material sorting system may include an in-line x-ray tube having a plurality of separate x-ray sources, each of which can irradiate a separate stream of materials to be sorted.
problem: Need to automatically sort materials of unknown composition (e.g., scrap metal alloys) into groups based on their chemical identity.
constraint: The system must accurately match measured elemental signatures to reference signatures in real-time while handling multiple material streams simultaneously, requiring reliable X-ray sources and fast signature comparison.
mechanism: Each material is irradiated to induce characteristic emission, the emission is converted into an elemental signature, the signature is compared to reference data to classify the material, and the material is directed into sorted groups based on the classification.
mechanism_raw: Each material is irradiated with X-rays, causing X-ray fluorescence emission; the fluorescence is converted into an elemental composition signature, which is compared to reference signatures to identify or classify the material, and the material is then sorted into separate groups based on the identification result.

abstract: The present invention relates to aqueous compositions of associative polyelectrolyte complexes (PECs), optionally containing surfactants, biocidal agents and/or oxidants, which can provide a cleaning benefit and surface protection to treated articles including reduced soiling tendency, reduced cleaning effort and improved soil repellency, as well as providing bacteriostatic properties to treated surfaces that thereby gain resistance to water, environmental exposure and microbial challenge. Treatment means and compositions are provided that employ associative polyelectrolyte complexes formed by combining a water soluble cationic first polyelectrolyte with a water soluble second polyelectrolyte bearing groups of opposite charge to the first polyelectrolyte under suitable mixing conditions and at least one oxidant selected from the group: alkaline metal salts and/or alkaline earth metal salts of hypochlorous acid, hypochlorous acid, solubilized chlorine, any source of free chlorine, acidic sodium chlorite, active chlorine generating compound and any combinations or mixtures thereof. Also provided are means to form stable associative polyelectrolyte complexes with at least one oxidant in aqueous solutions having R values from about 0.10 to 20.
problem: Need to provide simultaneous cleaning, soil repellency, and bacteriostatic properties to treated surfaces using an aqueous composition.
constraint: The R value (ratio of components) must be maintained between 0.10 and 20 to form stable associative complexes with the oxidant in aqueous solution, ensuring both cleaning efficacy and long-term stability.
mechanism: A cationic and anionic polyelectrolyte are combined to form associative complexes, which are stabilized with an oxidizing agent at a controlled ratio to provide cleaning, soil repellency, and antimicrobial surface protection.
mechanism_raw: A water-soluble cationic polyelectrolyte is combined with a water-soluble oppositely charged polyelectrolyte under suitable mixing conditions to form associative polyelectrolyte complexes; these complexes are stabilized with oxidants (e.g., hypochlorite salts) at a controlled R value, providing cleaning, soil repellency, and antimicrobial surface protection.

abstract: An assembly for mounting a door with a vehicle compartment includes an arm coupled with the compartment and with the door and a constant-force spring having a coil coupled with one of the door and the compartment and an end coupled with the other of the door and the compartment such that a contraction of the spring causes the door to move with rotation of the arm.
problem: Need to mount a door on a vehicle compartment with controlled, smooth movement during opening and closing.
constraint: The spring must provide a constant force to ensure smooth, controlled door movement regardless of door position, and the arm geometry must be designed to produce the desired motion profile.
mechanism: A constant-force element is coupled between the door and the compartment, and a mechanical linkage connects the door to the compartment; contraction of the element causes the door to move with rotation of the linkage, providing controlled, smooth movement through the combination of constant force and rotational mechanics.
mechanism_raw: A constant-force spring is coupled between the door and the compartment, and an arm connects the door to the compartment; contraction of the spring causes the door to move with rotation of the arm, providing controlled, smooth door movement through the combination of constant spring force and rotational arm mechanics.

abstract: LED lighting apparatus defining a longitudinal axis and including a lens, an element holder for holding the lens and having at least one guide pin, a fixture body for receiving the element holder and having at least a first plurality of slots extending transverse the longitudinal axis of the apparatus. The guide pin is received in at least one of the slots corresponding to a first beam angle of the lens, the element holder being configured to be selectively movable to one of the plurality of slots for selecting a projection beam angle of the LED lighting apparatus. A second plurality of slots is provided extending along the longitudinal axis and connecting the horizontal slots, such that the guide pin is repositioned from one of the first slots to another of the first slots by traveling along one of the second plurality of slots.
problem: Adjusting the projection beam angle of an LED lighting apparatus without requiring complex reconfiguration or multiple discrete components.
constraint: The need to maintain precise alignment and structural integrity of the lens while allowing smooth repositioning between discrete angular settings.
mechanism: A positioning system where a guided element moves through a network of intersecting pathways to select discrete positions, enabling controlled repositioning between stable states without continuous actuation.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical system where a guide pin on an element holder engages with a first plurality of transverse slots to set a beam angle, and a second plurality of longitudinal slots connects the transverse slots, allowing the guide pin to travel along the longitudinal slots to reposition between transverse slots. This enables selective adjustment of the lens position relative to the LED, thereby changing the beam angle.

abstract: A wearable device made by amorphous alloy with antibacterial function includes a functional part adapted for implementing using functions of the wearable device; and an amorphous alloy housing configured out of the functional part and adapted for cladding the functional part to prevent the functional part from directly contacting with a user. Since the wearable device has the amorphous alloy housing covering on the functional part, thus the amorphous alloy housing rather than the functional part will contact with the user skin directly. As the amorphous alloy has excellent bactericidal capability, thus user wearing such a wearable device will get a good user experience.
reason: The patent primarily describes a material choice (amorphous alloy) with inherent antibacterial properties to prevent direct skin contact. While the material's bactericidal capability is functional, the mechanism is a static property of the material rather than a dynamic causal operation that can be transferred to other systems.

abstract: The invention relates to a method of authentication of a contactless communication circuit, PICC, by a contactless communication terminal, PCD. Within the PICC, a first number is generated by encryption of a second random number, and the first number is sent to the PCD. Within the PCD, a third number is generated by decryption of the first number. Also within the PCD, a fourth number is determined and encrypted to generate a fifth number. The fifth number has first and second portions. Back within the PICC, a sixth number is determined, which is used in the determination of a seventh number. The seventh number is determined by encryption by a cipher block chaining operating mode of the sixth number with an initialization vector equal to the first portion. If the seventh number is different from the second portion, the authentication is interrupted.
reason: The authentication method relies on standard cryptographic operations (encryption, decryption, cipher block chaining) applied in a specific sequence. While the sequence is novel in its application, the underlying mechanisms (e.g., CBC mode, initialization vectors) are well-established in cryptography and not a transferable problem-solving principle beyond their existing use cases.

abstract: A subject for the invention is to diminish the occurrence of streak-type segregation in producing a material comprising a Ni-based superalloy. The invention relates to a Ni-based superalloy having excellent unsusceptibility to segregation, characterized by comprising: 0.005 to 0.15 mass % of C; 8 to 22 mass % of Cr; 5 to 30 mass % of Co; equal or greater than 1 and less than 9 mass % of Mo; 5 to 21 mass % of W; 0.1 to 2.0 mass % of Al; 0.3 to 2.5 mass % of Ti; up to 0.015 mass % of B; and up to 0.01 mass % of Mg, with the remainder comprising Ni and unavoidable impurities.
problem: Minimizing streak-type segregation during the production of Ni-based superalloys, which degrades material quality and performance.
constraint: Balancing the concentrations of multiple elements to achieve desired mechanical and thermal properties while avoiding unintended interactions or brittleness.
mechanism: A controlled elemental composition that modulates solidification dynamics to optimize microstructure formation, reducing susceptibility to segregation through balanced phase distribution and grain growth regulation during cooling.
mechanism_raw: A specific elemental composition (e.g., controlled ranges of C, Cr, Co, Mo, W, Al, Ti, B, Mg) that influences solidification behavior and microstructure formation. By balancing these elements, the alloy's susceptibility to segregation is reduced through optimized phase distribution and grain growth control during cooling.

abstract: In an embodiment of this invention, a carriage includes a first lever that is operated by an operator to attach or detach a printhead and rotates about a first rotating shaft. The carriage also includes a second lever that rotates about a second rotating shaft parallel to the first rotating shaft and, if the printhead is attached, contacts part of the printhead and presses the printhead in accordance with the rotation. The carriage further includes a spring having one end hung on an end portion of the second lever and the other end hung on part of the carriage. If the printhead is attached, the press force of the spring acts to press the printhead against the carriage in accordance with the rotation of the first lever. If the printhead is detached, no press force acts.
problem: Automatically applying a controlled press force to a printhead when it is attached to a carriage, while ensuring no residual force remains when the printhead is detached.
constraint: Ensuring the mechanical linkage between the levers and spring provides consistent pressure without manual adjustment, while allowing easy detachment without residual force.
mechanism: A two-stage mechanical linkage where a primary actuator drives a secondary element to apply force via a resilient component, which disengages automatically upon reversal of the primary actuator to eliminate residual force.
mechanism_raw: A dual-lever system where a first operator-controlled lever rotates to initiate attachment/detachment, and a second lever (rotated by the first) contacts the printhead to press it against the carriage. A spring connected to the second lever amplifies and maintains the press force during attachment, but disengages when the first lever is rotated to detach the printhead, eliminating the force.

abstract: A formaldehyde-free sizing composition for products based on fibers, in particular mineral fibers, such as glass or rock fibers, which includes: at least one non-reducing sugar, at least one catalyst for the dehydration of the non-reducing sugar, at least one amine, and at least one compound including activated ethylenic unsaturation(s).
problem: Creating strong, durable binders for mineral fiber products without using formaldehyde, which is toxic and carcinogenic.
constraint: The chemistry must achieve sufficient binding strength and thermal stability for fiber processing while completely eliminating formaldehyde emissions, and all components must be compatible within the same curing reaction.
mechanism: A carbohydrate source undergoes catalytic dehydration to produce reactive intermediates, which then participate in cross-linking reactions with a nitrogen-containing compound and a compound bearing activated ethylenic unsaturation, forming a cured polymeric network that binds fibers together without generating toxic byproducts.
mechanism_raw: A non-reducing sugar is dehydrated by a catalyst to generate reactive intermediates (e.g., furan derivatives), which then undergo cross-linking reactions with an amine and a compound bearing activated ethylenic unsaturation, forming a cured polymeric network that binds fibers together.
residual_terms: ["carbohydrate source", "catalytic dehydration", "reactive intermediates", "cross-linking reactions", "nitrogen-containing compound", "activated ethylenic unsaturation", "cured polymeric network"]

abstract: A gas turbine shroud ring segment assembly (36) with an outer structural block (32A) having cooling channels (72) between inlets (60) on a front face and outlets (74, 76) on a front hanger rail (48). The outlets may be positioned on a radially inner surface (77) of the front rail for impingement and forced convection cooling of backsides of radially inner front lips (44) of adjacent shroud ring segments (30A, 30B) mounted on front and rear rails (48, 50) of the block. The outlets may enter a pocket (86) on the inner surface configured to allow coolant flow in all positions of the ring segments (32A, 32B). The cooling channel may form a main channel (72A) and tributary channels (72B, 72C). These channels may be drilled upward from the rail to the inlet. The tributaries may have offset intersections (72E, 72D) with the main channel.
problem: Cooling rotating gas turbine shroud ring segments, particularly the radially inner front lips of adjacent segments, in a high-temperature engine environment.
constraint: Must deliver effective cooling to moving and rotating components while preserving structural integrity of the shroud and accommodating variable angular positions of the ring segments during operation.
