The water reservoir includes a top that is at least partially open to capture water falling from the evaporator. The bracket is coupled to a compressor and covers a portion of the open top of the water reservoir in order to prevent the water from spilling when the portable dehumidifier is tilted at an angle.
problem: Preventing water spillage from a portable dehumidifier's reservoir when the device is tilted during transport or use.
constraint: Balancing the bracket's coverage area and tilt-angle sensitivity to prevent spillage without restricting airflow or dehumidification performance during normal operation.
mechanism: A mechanically coupled cover element dynamically adjusts the accessible opening area of a liquid reservoir in response to tilt. The cover restricts spillage by reducing open area when tilted beyond a threshold, while maintaining normal operation in upright positions through passive mechanical coupling.
mechanism_raw: A bracket mechanically coupled to the compressor covers a portion of the reservoir's open top when the device tilts, dynamically adjusting the open area to retain water while allowing normal operation in upright positions.

abstract: A pen structure with a glass smasher has the glass smasher mounted at the front end of a pen. When a user holds the pen and presses the front end (i.e., the smashing cone) of the smashing rod of the glass smasher forcibly against a glass obstacle, an impact block will strike the rear section of the smashing rod vigorously such that the smashing cone is instantly driven to smash the glass obstacle. A ballpoint/rollerball refill is detachably provided in the pen and is at least 6 cm long in order to contain enough ink. The overall length of the pen is at least 10 cm so that the pen can be easily held while the user writes or draws with the ballpoint/rollerball tip and while the user applies a force to a glass obstacle through the front end of the smashing rod to smash the glass obstacle.
problem: Creating a compact tool that combines writing functionality with the ability to generate high-impact force for breaking glass obstacles.
constraint: Designing the pen's length and internal mechanics to accommodate both writing ergonomics and sufficient impact force generation without compromising portability or structural integrity.
mechanism: A striking mechanism transfers kinetic energy from a moving impact element to a pointed rod, amplifying force applied to a target surface. The rod's geometry concentrates the transferred energy to fracture brittle obstacles through localized stress concentration.
mechanism_raw: A smashing rod with a front cone is struck by an impact block when the rod is pressed against a glass obstacle. The impact block transfers kinetic energy to the rod, amplifying the force applied to the cone to fracture the glass.

abstract: An apparatus for gripping a tubular includes a body. A slip carrier is coupled to an inner surface of the body. The slip carrier is configured to pivot between an open position and a closed position. A tubular is configured to be introduced laterally into the body when the slip carrier is in the open position. A slip is coupled to the slip carrier. The slip is configured to move radially between a first position that is spaced apart from the tubular and a second position that contacts and grips the tubular.
problem: Gripping a tubular that must be introduced laterally into a confined space without pre-alignment.
constraint: The pivot and radial movement must be synchronized to ensure the slip engages the tubular only after full insertion, avoiding damage during lateral entry.
mechanism: A two-stage gripping system uses a movable carrier to enable lateral insertion of an object into a confined space, transitioning between an open configuration for entry and a closed configuration for engagement. A secondary actuation element converts the carrier's motion into a radial gripping force that activates only after the object is fully inserted, ensuring damage-free engagement through synchronized movement.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting slip carrier enables lateral insertion of the tubular by transitioning between open and closed positions, while a radially movable slip converts the carrier's pivot motion into a gripping force that contacts and secures the tubular.

abstract: A water jets cutting machine includes a first rotating seat driven by a first motor to rotate about a first rotation axis, a second rotating seat driven by a second motor to rotate about a second axis, a water jets cutting head, an inertial measurement unit (IMU) for detecting an inclination angle of the water jets cutting head, and a controller connecting the first and second motors and the IMU. The controller is able to control the first and second motors to instantaneously conduct compensation for angular deviation of the water jets cutting head according to attitude and position signals which are fed back to the controller by the IMU.
problem: Maintaining cutting accuracy of a water jet head despite angular deviations caused by external forces or mechanical play.
constraint: The compensation must occur without interrupting the cutting process, requiring high-speed sensor feedback and motor response to maintain precision.
mechanism: A real-time feedback control system continuously monitors orientation deviations of a moving tool using a sensor array, and a controller dynamically adjusts multiple independent axes of motion to counteract detected angular displacements, maintaining operational precision without interrupting the process.
mechanism_raw: An inertial measurement unit (IMU) continuously detects the cutting head's inclination, and a controller uses this feedback to instantaneously adjust two independent rotational axes, compensating for angular deviations in real time.

abstract: A gas tank arrangement for an internal combustion engine is provided, the gas tank arrangement including a gas tank configured to contain a combustible gas, and a first additional gas tank positioned in downstream fluid communication with the gas tank, wherein the gas tank arrangement further includes a second additional gas tank positioned in downstream fluid communication with the gas tank and in upstream fluid communication with the first additional gas tank. A vehicle including such a gas tank arrangement is also provided.
reason: The patent describes a static arrangement of gas tanks in fluid communication but does not specify a causal mechanism for solving a problem. The configuration appears to be a system layout rather than a functional principle that can be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A bore cleaning device is configured to clean a bore of a firearm. The device includes a cylindrically shaped cleaning pad including a solid, non-hollow core. The device further includes a propellant providing a force to push the cleaning pad down the bore of the firearm and a payload located in a bore-forward position of the cleaning pad. The device can optionally include a lower charge cap situated between the propellant and the cleaning pad.
problem: Cleaning the interior of a narrow, elongated bore (e.g., a firearm barrel) without manual intervention or mechanical scrubbing.
constraint: The propellant charge must be calibrated to provide sufficient force to move the pad through the bore without causing damage to the bore or the pad itself.
mechanism: A self-propelled cleaning element is driven through a confined passage by a calibrated propellant force, with a forward payload ensuring complete traversal of the passage. The propellant force is regulated to move the cleaning element without exceeding safe operational limits for both the element and the passage.
mechanism_raw: A propellant generates force to push a solid, non-hollow cleaning pad through the bore, with a payload positioned forward of the pad to ensure complete traversal and debris removal.

abstract: Provided herein are compositions (e.g., pharmaceutical compositions, nutraceutical compositions, foods, beverages, cosmetic compositions, diet supplements) comprising deuterated caffeine. The provided compositions may be useful for treating and/or preventing various diseases and conditions, such as obesity, causing weight loss, increasing metabolic rate, reducing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, increasing urine output, increasing sodium excretion, reducing edema, a pain disorder, apnea, hypotension, an encephalopathy, a neurological or psychiatric disorder, and an inflammatory disorder.
problem: Modifying the pharmacokinetic or metabolic behavior of caffeine to enhance therapeutic effects or reduce side effects for medical applications.
constraint: The degree of deuteration must balance enhanced efficacy with potential toxicity, ensuring the modified compound remains safe for human consumption or medical use.
mechanism: A chemical modification strategy substitutes specific atomic groups within a bioactive molecule to alter its metabolic degradation rate and chemical stability, thereby modulating its biological activity duration and physiological effects. The degree of substitution is optimized to balance therapeutic enhancement with safety constraints.
mechanism_raw: Deuterium substitution in the caffeine molecule alters its chemical stability and metabolic degradation rate, prolonging its biological activity and enabling targeted modulation of physiological processes such as metabolism or neurotransmitter activity.

abstract: A tool for machining materials has a main part and one or more blades. The main part is made of a low-alloy steel. The socket is welded to the main part, and the blade edges are made of a hard metal. The hard metal contains at least 82 vol. % of tungsten carbide and a metallic binder made of a cobalt-nickel-based alloy. The hardness of the hard metal is greater than 1350 HV10. The socket has a sintered composite, and 40 vol. % to 60 vol. % of the composite is composed of a metal carbide and a metallic binder. At least 95 vol. % of the metallic binder is made of nickel, and the hardness of the composite is less than 800 HV10.
problem: Balancing hardness and structural integrity in machining tools to optimize wear resistance and durability.
constraint: The socket composite must have a hardness below 800 HV10 and 40-60 vol.% carbide, while the blade edges exceed 1350 HV10 with at least 82 vol.% tungsten carbide, requiring precise material composition control.
mechanism: Using a composite structure with a graded hardness profile, where a lower-hardness base region provides structural support and a higher-hardness edge region delivers localized wear resistance. The compositional gradient between regions balances toughness and durability without compromising overall mechanical integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using a composite socket with a metallic binder (nickel-rich) and metal carbide to provide a tough, lower-hardness base, while blade edges use a harder tungsten carbide-cobalt-nickel composite. The graded hardness between components allows localized wear resistance without compromising overall structural support.

abstract: A management computer (equipment information acquisition unit) includes an equipment information acquisition unit that acquires production information from a plurality of pieces of production equipment and a display that displays a production status of a production line (component mounting line) and manages the production status of the production line where a work (board) is operated with a plurality of pieces of production equipment in order to produce a product (mounting board). Then, the display displays a plurality of equipment information sections respectively displaying the equipment information of a plurality of pieces of production equipment in order according to the production order and further displays the number of stocks of the work in a corresponding one of the plurality of pieces of production equipment in each of the plurality of work information sections to be displayed for the plurality of pieces of production equipment.
problem: Visualizing and managing real-time production status across multiple pieces of equipment in a workflow-dependent manufacturing line.
constraint: The display must maintain synchronization between equipment information sections and work information sections, ensuring stock counts are mapped to the correct equipment in the production sequence.
mechanism: Synchronizing data from distributed equipment into a sequence-aligned visualization layout, where each equipment's operational status and associated work-in-progress quantities are displayed in production order. This enables dynamic tracking of workflow continuity and bottleneck identification.
mechanism_raw: Aggregating production data from distributed equipment and displaying it in a sequence-aligned layout, where each equipment's status and work-in-progress stock levels are shown in production order. This enables operators to track bottlenecks and workflow continuity dynamically.

abstract: Provided is a semiconductor pressure sensor that can maintain high reliability and measure pressure with high accuracy without increasing the size thereof and that has hydrogen permeation prevention performance.The semiconductor pressure sensor includes: a first semiconductor substrate having a recess formed thereon; a second semiconductor substrate joined to the first semiconductor substrate with an oxide film interposed therebetween; a reference pressure chamber formed as a space surrounded by the recess of the first semiconductor substrate and the second semiconductor substrate; a piezoresistor formed on a surface of the second semiconductor substrate that receives pressure, along an outer periphery of the reference pressure chamber; and a protective film formed on the surface of the second semiconductor substrate that receives pressure, and side surfaces of the second semiconductor substrate and the oxide film.
problem: Maintaining sensor accuracy and reliability in harsh environments (e.g., hydrogen exposure) without increasing device size.
constraint: The protective film must cover all exposed surfaces of the second substrate and oxide film without adding bulk, requiring precise deposition and material selection to avoid interfering with pressure transmission.
mechanism: Encapsulating sensitive components with a conformal protective layer covering active surfaces and edges, combined with a hermetically sealed reference chamber formed by substrate bonding. This isolates the sensor from environmental contaminants while maintaining mechanical responsiveness.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating the piezoresistor and sensitive surfaces with a protective film that covers both the active surface and side edges, while using a hermetically sealed reference chamber formed by substrate bonding. This isolates the sensor from external contaminants while preserving mechanical integrity.

abstract: A method for producing a solid catalyst component includes bringing a magnesium compound, a titanium halide compound, and one or more internal electron donor compounds into contact with each other to effect a reaction; washing the resulting product with a first inert organic wash solvent that does not have reactivity with the titanium halide compound, and has a solubility parameter (SP) of 8.0 to 9.0; washing the resulting intermediate product in the absence of the titanium halide compound with a second inert organic wash solvent that includes a hydrocarbon compound and does not have reactivity with the titanium halide compound, but has a solubility parameter (SP) of more than 9.0; and washing the resulting product in the absence of the titanium halide compound with a third inert organic wash solvent that does not have reactivity with the titanium halide compound, and has a solubility parameter (SP) of less than 8.0.
problem: Optimizing catalyst component synthesis by selectively removing unreacted or byproduct materials during multi-step washing processes.
constraint: The solvents must be inert to titanium halide compounds and applied in a specific order to avoid redepositing contaminants, with SP thresholds tightly controlled to ensure selective removal.
mechanism: Applying solvents with progressively varying solubility parameters in sequential washing steps, where each solvent targets specific substances based on their solubility characteristics. The ordered sequence ensures selective removal of residual reactants, non-polar impurities, and polar residues without redeposition.
mechanism_raw: Using solvents with progressively varying solubility parameters (SP) in sequential washing steps: first a mid-SP solvent (8.0–9.0) to remove residual reactants, then a high-SP solvent (>9.0) to eliminate non-polar impurities, and finally a low-SP solvent (<8.0) to strip remaining polar residues. Each step targets specific substances based on their solubility characteristics.

abstract: A yarn comprising a plurality of bicomponent filaments having a first region comprising a first polymer composition and a second region comprising a second polymer composition, each of the first and second regions being distinct in the bicomponent filaments; each bicomponent filament comprising 5 to 60 weight percent of the first polymer composition and 95 to 40 weight percent of the second polymer composition; wherein the first polymer composition comprises aramid polymer containing 0.5 to 20 weight percent discrete homogeneously dispersed carbon particles and the second polymer composition comprises modacrylic polymer being free of discrete carbon particles; the yarn having a total content of 0.1 to 5 weight percent discrete carbon particles.
problem: Creating a yarn with tailored electrical or mechanical properties by integrating conductive particles into a polymer matrix without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: The first polymer must constitute 5–60 wt% of each filament and contain 0.5–20 wt% carbon particles, while the total yarn carbon content remains below 5 wt%, requiring precise control over particle dispersion and polymer ratios.
mechanism: Structuring filaments with distinct regions: a first region containing a polymer matrix with dispersed conductive particles for localized property enhancement, and a second region of a complementary polymer free of particles. The bicomponent architecture balances functional performance with structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Structuring bicomponent filaments with a first region (aramid polymer with dispersed carbon particles) and a second region (modacrylic polymer free of particles). The distinct regions allow localized property enhancement (e.g., conductivity) while the overall yarn maintains flexibility and strength through the complementary polymer blend.

abstract: The present invention relates to an improved process for producing chemical cellulose pulp wherein biopolymers are added immediately before, during or after a bleaching step, depending on pulp characteristics and on process conditions used. The biopolymers according to the present invention are starches chemically modified by an etherification reaction. This treatment results in a differentiated pulp having improved physical, chemical and mechanical properties when compared with cellulose pulps obtained by traditional processes. The use of said biopolymer alters the relations between important pulp properties rendering their application in papermaking process advantageous. This differentiation increases the possibilities of use and also of new applications, including for the substitution of pulps produced from other cellulose sources. Thus, the present invention also relates to methods of making paper, such as printing, writing, decorative, special or tissue-type papers, through the use of the cellulose pulps modified by the above process.
problem: Improving physical, chemical, and mechanical properties of chemical cellulose pulp for papermaking applications
constraint: The timing of biopolymer addition must be precisely matched to pulp characteristics and process conditions; adding at the wrong stage relative to the bleaching step could be ineffective or could degrade pulp quality rather than improve it
mechanism: Introducing a chemically modified additive into a material processing sequence at a stage temporally coordinated with a chemical treatment step, where the timing is dynamically matched to material characteristics and environmental conditions to alter intermolecular interactions and produce a material with enhanced functional properties
mechanism_raw: Timing the introduction of chemically modified biopolymers (etherified starches) relative to a bleaching or chemical treatment step, where the timing is matched to pulp characteristics and process conditions, to alter the interrelationships between pulp properties and produce a differentiated pulp with enhanced characteristics

abstract: A smart window-based security system is provided. The system includes a plurality of smart windows, each smart window of the plurality of smart windows having at least one electrochromic window and at least one sensor integrated into the smart window. The plurality of smart windows are coupled together in a system having at least one processor configured to detect a personal or property security threat, such as an intruder or fire based, on information from sensors of the plurality of smart windows.
reason: The patent describes a system integration of sensors and electrochromic windows with centralized processing for threat detection. This is an application-specific combination of known technologies (sensors, smart glass, processors) rather than a novel causal mechanism. The underlying concept of distributed sensing networks is well-established and does not constitute a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A method of manufacturing a semiconductor device, the method including forming dummy gate structures on a substrate; forming spacers on sidewalls of the dummy gate structures; forming a preliminary first interlayer insulation pattern to fill a gap between adjacent spacers; etching an upper portion of the preliminary first interlayer insulation pattern through a first etching process to form a preliminary second interlayer insulation pattern; implanting an ion on the dummy gate structures, the spacers, and the preliminary second interlayer insulation pattern through an ion-implanting process; etching an upper portion of the preliminary second interlayer insulation pattern through a second etching process to form an interlayer insulation pattern having a flat upper surface; and forming a capping pattern on the interlayer insulation pattern to fill a gap between the spacers.
reason: The patent describes a specific semiconductor manufacturing process involving dummy gates, spacers, sequential etching, and ion implantation. While the process involves interesting fabrication steps, it is a highly specialized technique specific to semiconductor device manufacturing. The mechanism of using ion implantation to modify etch characteristics is a known technique in the field and does not represent a broadly transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: With the pharmaceutical injection system in an embodiment, pharmaceutical injection amount setting conditions for setting a pharmaceutical injection amount are inputted to a portable terminal (300), and the pharmaceutical injection amount setting conditions are transmitted to a health care worker-use information terminal (500). The portable terminal (300) receives the pharmaceutical injection amount set on the basis of the pharmaceutical injection amount setting conditions transmitted from the health care worker-use information terminal (500), and transmits the pharmaceutical injection amount to a pharmaceutical injection device (100). The health care worker-use information terminal (500) receives the pharmaceutical injection amount setting conditions transmitted from the portable terminal (300), and the pharmaceutical injection amount set on the basis of the pharmaceutical injection amount setting conditions is inputted. The health care worker-use information terminal (500) transmits the inputted pharmaceutical injection amount to the portable terminal (300). The pharmaceutical injection device (100) receives the pharmaceutical injection amount transmitted from the portable terminal (300), and a piston drive mechanism (101) is driven on the basis of the pharmaceutical injection amount.
problem: Safely and accurately setting and delivering pharmaceutical injection amounts in a system involving multiple parties (patient, healthcare worker, injection device)
constraint: The system requires coordination among multiple intermediaries (patient terminal, healthcare worker terminal, injection device), creating potential for communication failures, delays, or desynchronization; the execution device must only accept parameters that have been properly authorized through the entire chain
mechanism: Establishing a hierarchical authorization chain where a parameter-setting condition is input by a first entity, transmitted to a second authorized entity that validates and sets the final parameter value, and this validated parameter is then relayed through an intermediary to an execution device that only accepts parameters bearing explicit authorization from the qualified entity
mechanism_raw: Using a multi-stage communication chain where injection amount setting conditions are input by one party (patient), transmitted to an authorized party (healthcare worker) who sets the actual injection amount based on those conditions, and this authorized amount is then transmitted through an intermediary (portable terminal) to the execution device, creating a verification chain where the device only acts on parameters that have been explicitly authorized by a qualified party

abstract: A system, method, and articles of manufacture for a surface-modified transition metal cyanide coordination compound (TMCCC) composition, an improved electrode including the composition, and a manufacturing method for the composition which may include multiple chelation species (Che_x). The composition, compound, device, and uses thereof according to AxMn(y-k)Mjk[Mnm(CN)(6-p-q)(NC)p(Che_I)rq]z.CHE_GROUP (Vac)(1-z).nH2O, wherein CHE_GROUP includes one or more chelation materials selected from the group consisting of (Che_I)rw, (Che_II)sv, and combinations thereof, and wherein 0<j≤4, 0≤k≤0.1, 0≤(p+q)≤6, 0<x≤4, 0<y≤1, 0<z≤1, 0<w≤0.2; −3≤r≤3; 0<v≤0.2; −3≤s≤3; and 0≤n≤6; wherein x+2(y−k)+jk+(m+(r+1)q−6)z+wr+vs=0.
problem: Creating improved electrode materials with modified surface properties for better electrochemical performance
constraint: The composition must satisfy a charge balance equation (x+2(y−k)+jk+(m+(r+1)q−6)z+wr+vs=0), which constrains the possible combinations and ratios of all components, requiring precise stoichiometric control to maintain material stability while achieving the desired surface modification
mechanism: Incorporating multiple functional modifier species into a crystalline framework structure, where the modifiers alter surface and interface properties, and their concentrations are constrained by a mathematical balance equation to maintain structural integrity while achieving targeted surface modification
mechanism_raw: Incorporating multiple chelation species into a transition metal cyanide coordination compound framework, where the chelation species modify the surface and interface properties of the material, and their concentrations are constrained by a charge balance equation to maintain structural integrity while achieving the desired surface modification

abstract: A method is disclosed for recovering lipids from microbial biomass, and for producing lipids. In the method, an aqueous suspension includes fermentation broth containing oleaginous yeast biomass which is subjected to hydrothermal treatment and lipids are recovered from the biomass by solvent extraction.
problem: Efficiently extracting lipids from microbial biomass without degrading their quality.
constraint: Balancing hydrothermal treatment intensity to maximize lipid accessibility while avoiding thermal degradation of sensitive lipid compounds.
mechanism: A controlled thermal and pressure environment disrupts a structural matrix to increase permeability, enabling extraction of intracellular materials via solvent penetration. The intensity of the treatment is balanced to maximize accessibility while avoiding degradation of sensitive compounds.
mechanism_raw: Hydrothermal treatment disrupts the structural integrity of microbial biomass, increasing permeability and accessibility of intracellular lipids to solvent extraction. The controlled thermal and pressure conditions break down cell walls and matrix components, enabling solvent penetration and lipid recovery.

abstract: In one embodiment, a fixture for supporting a body in an oven includes a plurality of support ribs to support the body, and a support element to support and connect the plurality of support ribs. Each support rib has a length, a width, a thickness, and a first end. The length extends from the support element to the first end, and the width extends perpendicular to the length. The length varies across the width of at least one support rib. In another embodiment, a fixture for supporting a body in an oven includes a plurality of connected support ribs to support the body. Each support rib is spaced from at least one other support rib. The length differs for at least a first support rib of the plurality of support ribs with respect to at least a second support rib of the plurality of support ribs.
problem: Supporting objects in high-temperature environments (e.g., ovens) without deformation or structural failure due to thermal expansion.
constraint: Optimizing rib geometry to balance thermal expansion compensation with sufficient mechanical support under load.
mechanism: Variable geometry in support elements creates a gradient in thermal expansion tolerance and stress distribution. Differing dimensions across the elements accommodate localized thermal gradients, preventing uniform stress buildup and maintaining structural integrity under load.
mechanism_raw: Varying the length and width of support ribs across their span creates a gradient in thermal expansion tolerance and stress distribution. Ribs with differing dimensions accommodate localized thermal gradients, preventing uniform stress buildup and maintaining structural integrity.

abstract: A light-emitting device includes: a light-emitting stack including a first active layer emitting a first light having a first peak wavelength; a diode emitting a second light having a second peak wavelength between 800 nm and 1900 nm; and a tunneling junction between the diode and the light-emitting stack, wherein the tunneling junction includes a first tunneling layer and a second tunneling layer on the first tunneling layer, the first tunneling layer has a band gap and a thickness of the first tunneling layer is greater than a thickness of the second tunneling layer.
problem: Efficiently injecting charge carriers between semiconductor layers with mismatched band gaps in optoelectronic devices.
constraint: Matching layer thicknesses and band gaps to maximize tunneling efficiency without introducing resistive losses or carrier recombination.
mechanism: A junction with a thicker first layer (larger band gap) and a thinner second layer (smaller band gap) enables carrier transport via quantum tunneling. The thickness differential ensures sufficient tunneling probability while minimizing voltage drop across the junction.
mechanism_raw: A tunneling junction with a thicker first tunneling layer (larger band gap) and a thinner second tunneling layer (smaller band gap) enables carrier transport via quantum tunneling. The thickness differential ensures sufficient tunneling probability while minimizing voltage drop across the junction.

abstract: An assembly for rotationally friction driving the wheel of an airplane provided with a driving track. The assembly has a base intended to be fixed to a lower part of the landing gear, two arms mounted to pivot on the base, and rollers so mounted as to rotate at the end of each arm, with each roller being associated with a pinion for rotationally driving the roller. A central pinion is mounted so as to rotate along the arms pivot axis so that the rollers driving pinions engage with the central pinion. A drive actuator acts on the arms of the assembly so as to position the assembly either in a disengaged position in which the rollers are separated from the driving track, or in an engaged position in which the rollers are held to rest on the driving track.
problem: Engaging and disengaging a drive mechanism with a moving surface (e.g., airplane wheel track) while maintaining rotational force transmission.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and force distribution between rollers, pinions, and the central pinion to prevent slippage during engagement while allowing rapid disengagement.
mechanism: Pivoting contact elements with gear interfaces are actuated to move between disengaged (separated) and engaged (pressed against a surface) positions. A central gear transfers rotational force to the contact elements via mechanical engagement, enabling controlled friction-driven motion.
mechanism_raw: Pivoting arms with rollers and pinions are actuated to move between disengaged (rollers separated) and engaged (rollers pressed against the track) positions. A central pinion transfers rotational force to the rollers via gear engagement, enabling controlled friction-driven motion.

abstract: The present invention relates to an apparatus for supplying hot water and, more particularly, to a hot water supply apparatus using a revolving magnetic body, wherein the apparatus is driven with low power consumption while being environment-friendly and having excellent safety when hot water and heating are supplied, the apparatus including: a heat exchange body containing water, and including a circular heating pipe circumferentially provided in the heat exchange body; a stator provided to encompass an outside of the heat exchange body and wound with a plurality of coils, the stator being magnetized when an electric current is applied thereto, wherein the heating pipe includes therein a magnetic body that revolves along the circumference of the heating pipe due to a magnetic field formed by the stator, so that water is heated by frictional heat generated when the magnetic body revolves.
problem: Heating water efficiently with low power consumption while avoiding direct contact between moving parts and the fluid.
constraint: Maintaining stable magnetic body motion and heat transfer efficiency while minimizing energy input to the stator coils.
mechanism: A magnetic element is moved along a conductive surface by a rotating magnetic field, generating frictional heat through contactless motion. The heat transfers to an adjacent fluid medium, enabling efficient heating without mechanical wear between moving parts.
mechanism_raw: A magnetic body revolves along a heating pipe due to a rotating magnetic field generated by a stator. Frictional heat from the magnetic body's movement transfers to the surrounding water, enabling contactless heating without mechanical wear.

abstract: An accessory for catching a fastener responsive to operation of a power tool having a working assembly for driving or removing the fastener may include a working end, a coupling end opposite the working end, and a catch portion disposed between the working end and the coupling end. The coupling end may be configured to be operably coupled to the power tool to be fixed rotationally and axially relative to an axis of the working assembly. The catch portion may extend substantially coaxial with the axis of the working assembly away from the coupling end to the working end. The working end may be configured to extend beyond a distal end of the working assembly.
problem: Efficiently catching a fastener during power tool operation without disrupting the tool's rotational or axial function.
constraint: Maintaining rotational and axial alignment with the tool's working assembly while ensuring the catch portion extends beyond the tool's distal end to intercept the fastener.
mechanism: A coaxial capture element is positioned between a fixed coupling point and a working end that extends beyond the tool's distal end, enabling interception of a fastener during operation while preserving rotational and axial alignment with the tool's working assembly.
mechanism_raw: A coaxial catch portion is positioned between a coupling end (fixed to the tool's axis) and a working end (extending beyond the tool's distal end), allowing the catch to capture the fastener as the tool operates while maintaining alignment with the tool's working assembly.

abstract: Provided is a method that enables a crystal-free glass material to be stably produced by a containerless levitation technique. A glass material 30 has a first surface 31 facing a forming surface 10a and a second surface 32 located on a side opposite to the forming surface 10a. The first surface 31 includes a central portion 31a and a peripheral portion 31b located outside of the central portion 31a. Gas is jetted through a gas jet hole at a flow velocity and a flow volume at which a glass material satisfying R2<R3<R1 is formed where R1 represents a radius of curvature of the central portion 31a, R2 represents a radius of curvature of the peripheral portion 31b, and R3 represents a radius of curvature of the second surface 32.
problem: Producing crystal-free glass via containerless levitation without defects caused by uncontrolled surface curvature.
constraint: Balancing gas flow parameters to achieve the required curvature hierarchy without inducing structural defects in the glass.
mechanism: Gas flow parameters are dynamically adjusted to shape opposing surfaces of a levitated object such that their radii of curvature satisfy a hierarchical relationship (R2 < R3 < R1), suppressing nucleation sites that induce structural defects.
mechanism_raw: Gas jet velocity and volume are controlled to shape the glass's first and second surfaces such that the radii of curvature satisfy R2 < R3 < R1, preventing nucleation sites that lead to crystallization.

abstract: The present invention relates to a marker associated with resistance to smut which is a quantitative trait of sugarcane. Specifically, a marker associated with resistance to sugarcane smut, which consists of a continuous nucleic acid region existing in a region sandwiched between the nucleotide sequence shown in SEQ ID NO: 1 and the nucleotide sequence shown in SEQ ID NO: 14 or a different similar region, is provided.
problem: Identifying a reliable genetic marker for resistance to sugarcane smut, a quantitative trait.
constraint: Ensuring the marker region is consistently linked to the resistance trait across diverse genetic backgrounds to avoid false positives or negatives.
mechanism: A nucleic acid region bounded by two conserved sequences is employed as a genetic marker, exploiting its stable linkage to a quantitative resistance trait across diverse genetic backgrounds for selective identification or breeding.
mechanism_raw: A specific nucleic acid region located between two known sequences (SEQ ID NO: 1 and SEQ ID NO: 14) is used as a marker, leveraging its consistent association with the resistance trait for selective breeding or genetic testing.

abstract: A laundry machine includes first and second washing units including first and second tubs, respectively. First and second drums are mounted inside the first and second tubs, and first and second drive units drive rotations of the first and second drums around first and second rotational shafts, respectively. The second washing unit is arranged above the first washing unit and has a smaller laundry treating capacity than the first washing unit. The first rotational shaft is not parallel to the second rotational shaft. A first recess projects downward from a rear lower surface of the second tub and is configured to heat wash water in the second tub. A metal plate member is provided on an outside lower surface of the second tub, and partially extends to the rear of the second tub to expose a bottom surface of the first recess.
problem: Optimizing space and functionality in a dual washing unit laundry machine with non-parallel rotational axes.
constraint: Balancing the vertical stacking and non-parallel orientation of the units to fit within a compact footprint while maintaining independent drum rotation and heating efficiency.
mechanism: A secondary processing unit is vertically stacked above a primary unit with non-parallel rotational axes, and a recessed thermal transfer element coupled with a conductive plate enables efficient heat distribution to wash water while minimizing spatial overlap.
mechanism_raw: The second washing unit is arranged above the first with non-parallel rotational shafts, and a recessed heating element combined with a metal plate on the second tub enables efficient heat transfer to wash water while minimizing spatial overlap.

abstract: A window blind includes a fixed rail and a plurality of slats hang below the fixed rail through a ladder tape. The slats are controlled by an output adjustment mechanism to change between a first state and a second state. In addition, an output clutch mechanism is provided to collect or to expand the window blind. Said output adjustment mechanism and said output clutch mechanism are both controlled by an input mechanism. Whereby, it requires only one single control module to adjust shielding of the slat assembly composed of the slats, and to expand or collect the slat assembly.
problem: Simplifying the control of a window blind's slat angle and overall position with a single input mechanism.
constraint: Ensuring the two mechanisms operate without mechanical interference while maintaining precise control over both slat angle and blind position.
mechanism: A single actuation input is mechanically or logically coupled to two independent output systems—one for angular adjustment and one for positional extension—ensuring coordinated operation without mechanical interference between the two functions.
mechanism_raw: A single input mechanism simultaneously actuates an output adjustment mechanism (for slat angle) and an output clutch mechanism (for blind expansion/contraction), coordinating their operation through mechanical linkage or control logic.

abstract: A semiconductor memory device includes a memory cell array including a plurality of dynamic memory cells, an ECC engine configured to correct at least one error in a read data from the memory cell array, and a test circuit which performs a test on the memory cell array in a test mode of the semiconductor memory device by writing a test pattern data in the memory cell array and by reading, from the memory cell array, test result data corresponding to the test pattern data. When the test result data includes at least one error bit, the test circuit subtracts a second number from a first number of the at least one error bit and is configured to output the subtracted result to an outside of the semiconductor memory device. The second number corresponds to a number of error bits that the ECC engine is capable of correcting.
problem: Accurately assessing the true error rate of a memory array beyond the correction capability of an ECC engine during testing.
constraint: The ECC engine's correction limit is a fixed, known value, so the subtraction must be based on this predefined threshold rather than dynamic error analysis.
mechanism: A measurement system subtracts a predefined correction capacity from total detected errors to isolate residual failures beyond a known correction threshold, enabling assessment of inherent failure rates independent of correction masking.
mechanism_raw: The test circuit subtracts the ECC engine's maximum correctable error count from the total detected error bits, outputting only the residual uncorrectable errors to external systems. This isolates the memory's inherent failure rate from the ECC's masking effect.

abstract: A sterilization process transition method of switching from an SIP process to a product sterilization process in an apparatus including piping that feeds a product into a filling machine through a heating sterilization part. The process sterilizes the piping before a filling operation, and the product sterilization process sterilizes the product to be filled. An F value is calculated from temperature and flowrate data on a fluid flowing in the heating sterilization part that are obtained from temperature sensors and flowmeters disposed in the product filling apparatus at predetermined time intervals. The temperature and flowrate at two or more predetermined positions in the product filling apparatus are adjusted from a set temperature and a set flowrate for the SIP process to a set temperature and a set flowrate for the product sterilization process while preventing the F value from becoming lower than a predetermined value.
problem: Transitioning between sterilization processes (SIP to product sterilization) without compromising the critical F-value (a measure of sterilization efficacy) during the switch.
constraint: The F-value must not drop below a predetermined safety threshold at any point during the transition, requiring coordinated adjustment of multiple variables rather than sequential changes.
mechanism: Multiple process variables are adjusted simultaneously during a transition between operational states while continuously monitoring a critical efficacy metric to ensure it remains above a minimum threshold throughout the change.
mechanism_raw: Temperature and flowrate at multiple positions in the system are adjusted simultaneously from SIP to product sterilization setpoints, while continuously monitoring and constraining the F-value to remain above a minimum threshold throughout the transition.

abstract: A decoration pattern data generating apparatus includes: a controller, the controller being configured to control the decoration pattern data generating apparatus to select an embroidery pattern to be sewn, specify an outline of the embroidery pattern, based on embroidery pattern data for sewing the selected embroidery pattern; set an area outside the specified outline, as a decoration area; and generate decoration pattern data for sewing a decoration pattern in the set decoration area.
reason: The mechanism is a static spatial definition process (selecting a pattern, defining its outline, and setting an area outside it as decoration). It lacks a causal functional relationship that solves a broader problem beyond the specific embroidery design context.

abstract: A display unit of the disclosure includes a unit pixel and a driving section that drives the unit pixel. The unit pixel includes a light-emitting device, a capacitor section having a first capacitor and a second capacitor that are coupled in series through a first node, a drive transistor that supplies a drive current corresponding to a potential difference across both ends of the capacitor section to the light-emitting device, and a first transistor that delivers a first voltage to the first node by turning on.
reason: The mechanism describes a specific circuit topology for driving a pixel (capacitor configuration, transistor arrangement) without a generalizable causal principle. The functional relationship is tightly coupled to display hardware design rather than a transferable problem-solving approach.

abstract: Systems and apparatus may include converter device(s), a matrix switch, processor(s), and memory(s), where one or more of the converter devices provide video input signals to the matrix switch. A processor may determine if one of a plurality of video signals input to the matrix switch includes data representative of identification information overlain on a video image derived from one of the plurality of video signals. The determination may be based on a flag value stored in the converter device(s). The flag value may be retrieved by a server coupled to the matrix switch. If the information is included in the video signal, the video signal may be passed through a path in a matrix switch configured by the processor. If the information is not included in the video signal, the data representative of identification information may be retrieved from the converter device and then overlain on the video image.
problem: Determining whether a video signal contains overlain identification data and routing or modifying the signal accordingly without redundant processing.
constraint: The flag must be reliably stored and retrieved from the converter device to avoid false positives/negatives, and the matrix switch configuration must be dynamically adjusted based on the flag's state.
mechanism: A stored state indicator is checked to determine whether a signal already contains embedded data. If present, the signal is routed through a preconfigured path; if absent, the data is retrieved and combined with the signal before routing.
mechanism_raw: A flag stored in a converter device is checked to determine if identification data is already present in the video signal. If present, the signal is routed through a preconfigured matrix switch path; if absent, the data is retrieved from the converter and overlain on the video image before routing.

abstract: Provided are a dip coating device which minimizes attachment of a coating material to a member to which a member to be coated is fixed, thereby facilitating coating of the member to be coated and a method for producing a coated member which is obtained by dip coating a member to be coated with a coating material. The dip coating device 10 of the present invention for coating a member to be coated 20 with a coating material 70, comprises a reservoir 30 that stores a coating material 70, a first fixing part 40 that holds a member to be coated 20, and a second fixing part 50 directly or indirectly provided on a wall 31 of the reservoir 30, wherein the first fixing part 40 and the second fixing part 50 magnetically attract to each other.
problem: Minimizing unwanted adhesion of coating material to the holder during dip coating of a member.
constraint: Requires magnetic materials and precise alignment to ensure sufficient holding force without interfering with the coating process.
mechanism: A magnetic holding system uses opposing magnetic forces to retain a movable component in a fixed position without direct physical contact, preventing adhesion of processed material to the holder during surface treatment operations.
mechanism_raw: Magnetic attraction between two fixing parts (one holding the coated member, the other fixed to the reservoir wall) allows the member to be held without physical contact that could cause coating material to stick to the holder.

abstract: The present invention relates to increasing longevity of the nitrogen content of soil through improved liquid delivery formulations of nitrification inhibitors. The liquid formulation can also be comprised of nitrification inhibitors and optionally urease inhibitors that are blended solutions of each. The nitrification inhibitors are present in a mixture that comprises both a protic and an aprotic solvent system. The novel formulations are designed to be applied to fertilizers, especially urea and manure based fertilizers. The delivery formulations provide an environmentally sound and inherently safe solvating system that improves the storage stability of the urease inhibitors by utilizing liquid organic non-water containing solvents, maintains the nitrification inhibitors in solution to storage temperatures of at least 10° C., and provides improved application to fertilizer of nitrification inhibitors. These delivery formulations enable safe storage, transport and subsequent application or blending with urea-based or manure-based fertilizers that can be applied to soil in either a liquid or granular form to provide improved nitrogen retention in the soil for uptake for plant life.
problem: Maintaining stability and solubility of nitrification/urease inhibitors in liquid delivery formulations for fertilizers under storage and application conditions.
constraint: Balancing the proportions of protic and aprotic solvents to optimize solubility, stability, and compatibility with fertilizer substrates.
mechanism: A dual-solvent formulation combines polar and non-polar solvent classes to create a non-aqueous medium that maintains chemical stability and solubility of active agents under varying temperature and storage conditions.
mechanism_raw: A solvent system combining both protic and aprotic solvents creates a non-water-based medium that keeps inhibitors in solution and prevents degradation at low temperatures, enabling safe storage and effective application.

abstract: A worm gear has a worm wheel, a drive shaft, and a flexible shaft. The worm wheel meshes with a worm shaft, which is driven by the drive shaft. The flexible shaft can be arranged in the drive shaft with a radial gap between at least a portion of the flexible shaft and the drive shaft. The flexible shaft can be coupled to the drive shaft such that a first spring constant is provided for displacement of the flexible shaft in a radial direction within a first range and a second spring constant is provided for displacement of the flexible shaft in the radial direction within a second range.
problem: Providing variable stiffness characteristics in a mechanical drive system to accommodate different operational loads or displacements.
constraint: Designing the flexible shaft geometry and material to achieve the desired dual spring constant behavior without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A compliant mechanical element with a controlled geometric discontinuity exhibits two distinct stiffness regimes: a low-resistance mode for minor displacements and a high-resistance mode for larger displacements, enabling adaptive load response.
mechanism_raw: A flexible shaft arranged with a radial gap within a drive shaft exhibits two distinct spring constants: a lower stiffness for small displacements and a higher stiffness for larger displacements, enabling adaptive mechanical response.

abstract: A feedback control method accounts for noise emissions of a centrifuge for the operation of a centrifuge, in particular a separator or a decanting centrifuge, for the centrifugal processing of a product, in particular for clarifying a product and/or for separating a product into different liquid phases using the drum.
problem: Controlling centrifuge operation while accounting for noise emissions that may interfere with performance or environmental compliance.
constraint: Ensuring the noise monitoring system is sufficiently responsive and integrated with the control loop to avoid delays or overcorrection.
mechanism: A closed-loop control system continuously monitors environmental noise levels and dynamically adjusts operational parameters of a rotating processing unit to maintain performance while minimizing acoustic emissions.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control loop integrates real-time noise emission data into the centrifuge's operational parameters, dynamically adjusting processing conditions to minimize noise while maintaining separation efficiency.
residual_terms: ["feedback control loop", "noise emission data", "closed-loop control system"]

abstract: A grinding wheel for grinding a wafer held on a holding table includes: a first circular annular plate mounted to a mount of a grinding apparatus; a tubular body extending downward from an outer circumference of the first circular annular plate; a second circular annular plate connected to a lower end of the tubular body; a plurality of grindstones arranged in an annular pattern on a lower surface of the second circular annular plate; an annular ultrasonic oscillation section disposed on an upper surface of the second circular annular plate so as to surround an opening; and an ultrasonic reception section that receives an ultrasonic vibration transmitted from the ultrasonic oscillation section to the grindstones.
problem: Achieving precise and consistent grinding of wafers while monitoring and maintaining ultrasonic vibration performance.
constraint: Maintaining uniform ultrasonic energy distribution across all grindstones and ensuring the reception section accurately captures vibration data without disrupting the grinding process.
mechanism: An ultrasonic energy delivery system transmits vibrational energy to multiple processing elements arranged in a ring configuration, while a separate sensing subsystem detects energy transmission characteristics to verify and regulate consistency during operation.
mechanism_raw: An ultrasonic oscillation section transmits vibrations to grindstones arranged in an annular pattern, while a separate reception section detects transmitted ultrasonic energy to verify and regulate vibration consistency during grinding.

abstract: Catalyst compositions and polymerization systems include at least one thioguanidine complex according to Formula (I): MQaX4_a (I) in which M is Ti, Zr, or Hf; a is 1 or 2; each group Q of the thioguanidine complex is a bidentate thioguanidine ligand bound to the metal center and having Formula (1a) or Formula (1b), In Formulas (1a) and (1b), each group R1, R2, and R3 is independently chosen from alkyl groups or aryl groups; each group Z1 is independently chosen from alkylene groups. If a=2, groups R3 of the two groups Q are optionally linked to each other through at least one covalent bond. Each X is covalently bonded or coordinated to the metal center and is independently chosen from alkyl groups or halides. The polymerization systems may be configured to copolymerize ethylene and α-olefins.
problem: Controlling the copolymerization of ethylene and α-olefins with precise molecular architecture.
constraint: Balancing ligand rigidity and metal coordination strength to prevent catalyst deactivation while allowing monomer access.
mechanism: A stabilizing element with dual-point coordination binds to a catalytic center, enabling selective monomer insertion during polymerization while preventing deactivation through controlled rigidity and coordination strength.
mechanism_raw: A bidentate thioguanidine ligand stabilizes a transition metal center (Ti/Zr/Hf) through coordinated bonding, enabling selective insertion of monomers during polymerization while maintaining catalyst activity.

abstract: A floating drilling platform for offshore oil/gas drilling and exploration in ice-infested polar areas comprises a deck module, a hard compartment, and a soft compartment sequentially connected from top to bottom. The bottom of the deck module is connected to the top of the hard compartment by evenly distributed column. Both the hard and the soft compartments are cylinders centrally arranged with center wells. The deck module is also centrally arranged with a center well. The hard compartment, the soft compartment and the deck module are coincident with a centerline. The outer diameter of the soft compartment, as well as that of the deck module, is larger than that of the hard compartment. The top of the hard compartment is designed with a circular inclined plane upwardly and outwardly arranged at the outer edge. The top of the circular inclined plane is connected to the bottom of the deck module.
problem: Maintaining structural integrity and operational stability of offshore platforms in ice-infested environments.
constraint: Optimizing the stiffness gradient between compartments to balance ice resistance with structural weight and cost.
mechanism: A hierarchical structural system with a stiffness gradient between rigid and flexible zones absorbs and redistributes external forces, while an angled load-transfer surface redirects concentrated stresses outward to prevent localized failure.
mechanism_raw: A layered compartment system with a rigid inner cylinder (hard compartment) and flexible outer cylinders (soft/deck modules) absorbs and redistributes ice-induced forces, while an inclined plane at the hard compartment's top transfers loads outward to prevent localized failure.

abstract: A portable rechargeable lighting device uses software in a microcontroller to turn on a charger protection circuit when a charging circuit is activated, to monitor at least one electrical characteristic relative to a rechargeable battery, to control at least one charging parameter of the charging circuit, and to alert a user of a low battery condition before light emitted from the device terminates.
problem: Preventing unexpected power loss in portable devices by proactively managing battery health and user awareness.
constraint: Integrating sensor feedback and control logic without increasing power consumption or device complexity.
mechanism: A feedback control system continuously monitors electrical parameters, dynamically adjusts operational settings to optimize performance, and triggers preemptive alerts when critical thresholds are approached.
mechanism_raw: A microcontroller monitors battery electrical characteristics in real-time, dynamically adjusts charging parameters to optimize longevity, and triggers alerts before critical voltage thresholds are reached.

abstract: A method for identifying a patient that is at risk for developing a thyroid disorder that occurs subsequent to treatment with a regimen that depletes lymphocytes, comprising determining whether antibodies directed against thyroid peroxidase or thyroid microsomes are present in the patient, wherein if the antibodies are present in the patient then the patient is at increased risk for developing a thyroid disorder. A particular embodiment is a method for identifying a patient with multiple sclerosis that is at risk for developing a thyroid disorder that occurs subsequent to treatment with a regimen that depletes CD52-positive cells, comprising determining whether antibodies directed against thyroid peroxidase or thyroid microsomes are present in the patient, wherein if the antibodies are present in the patient then the patient is at risk for developing the thyroid disorder.
problem: Predicting adverse thyroid effects in patients undergoing lymphocyte-depleting therapies.
constraint: Ensuring antibody detection specificity to avoid false positives while capturing subclinical autoimmune predisposition.
mechanism: A biomarker detection system identifies pre-existing immune markers to predict susceptibility to a specific physiological dysfunction, enabling risk stratification before therapeutic intervention.
mechanism_raw: Detecting pre-existing autoantibodies (anti-TPO or anti-thyroid microsomes) as biomarkers to identify patients whose immune systems are primed for post-treatment thyroid dysfunction.

abstract: Systems, methods, and apparatus for fiber optic lighting panels that produce twinkling star patterns by means of a light engine and specialized optics are disclosed. In one or more embodiments, a disclosed panel for creating a lighted scene comprises a substrate comprising a first surface, a second surface spaced from the first surface, and a plurality of apertures through the first and second surfaces. The panel further comprises an optical lens disposed on the first surface within each of the apertures. Also, the panel comprises a light distribution unit (LDU) comprising a plurality of light sources coupled to the second surface. Further, the panel comprises a bundle of optical fibers coupled to each of the light sources, where each of the optical fibers is in communication with one of the optical lenses for transferring light emitted by the light sources to create the lighted scene.
problem: Creating dynamic, spatially distributed light patterns (e.g., twinkling stars) with uniform brightness and controlled variability.
constraint: Aligning fiber-lens pairs to maintain light efficiency while allowing scalable, modular panel configurations.
mechanism: A distributed light management system uses guided transmission elements and focusing components to redirect and independently control discrete light points, enabling spatially varied patterns with uniform output.
mechanism_raw: Optical fibers coupled to discrete light sources transfer and spatially redirect light through lenses embedded in a perforated substrate, enabling independent control of individual light points to simulate motion or randomness.

abstract: A sheet processing device has a binding unit that applies water to a crimping range of sheets and then crimps the sheets. The sheet processing device includes a processing tray on which sheets are placed, a pair of pressure teeth (pressure teeth and receiving teeth) that crimps the sheets placed on the processing tray at a crimping position with the sheets interposed therebetween, and a water application member (cylinder and piston) that applies water to the crimping position before crimping by the pressure teeth. When the number of sheets placed on the processing tray is equal to or less than a predetermined number, the sheets are crimped by the pressure teeth without water application; while when the number of sheets placed on the processing tray exceeds the predetermined number, the sheets are crimped by the pressure teeth after water application.
problem: Ensuring effective crimping of sheets when the number of sheets varies, as excessive sheets may not bind properly without additional treatment.
constraint: The threshold number of sheets determines whether water is applied, balancing resource usage (water) against the need for effective crimping under varying loads.
mechanism: Applying a treatment substance to a processing region only when an input quantity exceeds a threshold, enabling adaptive processing based on input size to improve output quality.
mechanism_raw: Conditionally applying water to the crimping region only when the number of sheets exceeds a threshold, enabling adaptive processing based on input size to improve binding quality.

abstract: A reinforcement apparatus for reinforcing a structure comprising at least one pier bearing on foundations, a cross-beam bearing on said pier and at least one structure element located above the cross-beam, the reinforcement apparatus comprising at least one column (20) destined to surround the pier at least partly, to be mechanically coupled to the pier and to bear on said foundations, and at least one transverse beam (22) fixed relative to the column and destined to be mechanically coupled to the cross-beam, and at least one load transfer element (36) arranged on an upper face of said at least one transverse beam (22) to take up at least part of the load of the structure element.
reason: The patent describes a structural reinforcement design using specific mechanical components (columns, beams, load transfer elements) without a novel causal principle that generalizes beyond structural engineering contexts.

abstract: An LED lamp includes: a lamp shell; a passive heat dissipating element having a heat sink, wherein the heat sink comprises fins and a base; a power source; a light emitting surface connected to the heat sink of the passive heat dissipating element and comprising LED chips; a first heat dissipating channel formed in a first chamber of the lamp shell; a second heat dissipating channel formed in the heat sink and between the fins and the base of the heat sink; and a lamp cover connected with the heat sink and having a light output surface and an end surface; wherein the base of the heat sink has a projecting portion protrudes from the light emitting surface in an axial direction of the LED lamp, the projecting portion protrudes from the light emitting surface in the axial direction of the LED lamp, the projecting portion is configured to be annular and a concave structure is defined by both the projecting portion and the base for receiving and protecting both the light emitting surface and the light cover, the base has a first inner surface and the lamp cover has a peripheral wall, the first inner surface corresponds to the peripheral wall, a gap is kept between the first inner surface and the peripheral wall, the first inner surface is configured to be a slant and an angle is formed between the first inner surface and the light emitting surface, the angle is an obtuse angle.
problem: Managing heat dissipation and protecting internal components in a compact LED lamp while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: The geometry must balance heat dissipation efficiency with physical protection, requiring precise angles and spacing between the heat sink and lamp cover.
mechanism: Using shaped structural features to create a protective cavity and thermal pathways, enabling passive heat dissipation and component shielding through geometric design.
mechanism_raw: Using a projecting annular structure and concave geometry to create a protective cavity and thermal channels, enabling passive heat dissipation and component shielding through shaped structural features.
residual_terms: ["protective cavity", "thermal pathways", "passive heat dissipation", "geometric design", "shaped structural features"]

abstract: A system includes a non-transitory computer-readable medium containing computer-executable instructions for providing a method related to rapid reporting of meaningful use in electronic health records. The method includes storing patient encounter data in a database, pre-calculating data related to at least one meaningful use measure, storing the pre-calculated data in a plurality of small staging tables, and compiling the pre-calculated and stored data from the small staging tables into a single table that is adapted to be accessed by reporting software.
problem: Rapidly generating meaningful use reports from large, complex electronic health record datasets without overloading the system during query compilation.
constraint: The staging tables must be small and pre-processed to minimize runtime aggregation overhead while maintaining data accuracy for reporting software.
mechanism: Pre-calculating and storing data in small intermediate tables, then aggregating them into a single table for reporting, decoupling computation from query time to optimize performance.
mechanism_raw: Pre-calculating and storing data in small staging tables, then aggregating them into a single table for reporting, decoupling computation from query time to optimize performance.

abstract: An elastic wave device includes a lamination layer film including a piezoelectric thin film on a support substrate. The lamination layer film is not partially present in a region located in an outer side portion of a region where IDT electrodes are provided. A first insulation layer extends from at least a portion of a region where the lamination layer film is not present to an upper portion of the piezoelectric thin film. A wiring electrode has a width of about 6 μm and extends from the upper portion of the piezoelectric thin film to an upper portion of the first insulation layer, and extends onto a section of the first insulation layer in the region.
reason: The patent specifies a highly technical design for an elastic wave device with precise layer dimensions and electrode widths, but does not describe a generalizable causal principle applicable outside its specific domain.

abstract: A comfort device comprising a plurality of elongate inserts is disclosed herein. The comfort device can include one or more compartments configured to store the plurality of elongate inserts. The plurality of elongate inserts can have a length and a cross-section, where the cross-section has a cross-sectional area and a plurality of dimensions. The length of the inserts can be at least eight inches and at least eight times a greatest dimension of the cross-sectional area. The comfort device can include one or more openings and fastening mechanism corresponding to the one or more openings. The plurality of elongate inserts can generate tensional force in response to a force applied to the comfort device, thus providing improved elasticity for the comfort device.
problem: Providing adjustable elasticity in a comfort device while maintaining structural integrity under applied forces.
constraint: Insert dimensions must be at least eight inches in length and at least eight times the greatest cross-sectional dimension to ensure sufficient tensional force generation without structural failure.
mechanism: Geometric structural elements with controlled length-to-cross-sectional ratios generate tensional resistance in response to applied forces, converting mechanical deformation into elastic compliance through shape-dependent stiffness.
mechanism_raw: Elongate inserts with specific length-to-cross-sectional ratios generate tensional force in response to applied forces, converting mechanical deformation into elastic resistance through geometric compliance.

abstract: There is provided a method for producing a multicore optical fiber while depressurizing holes in a common cladding tube. A production method for a multicore optical fiber includes a preform forming step of forming a common cladding tube having a plurality of holes extending between a first end and a second end, an end-face working step of digging the common cladding tube from the second end to a predetermined depth to forming a third end, a connection step of connecting a glass tube to the second end, an insertion step of inserting core rods into the holes to the third end, a sealing step of sealing the first end, and a drawing step of spinning the multicore optical fiber while depressurizing the holes through the glass tube and combining the common cladding tube and the core rods from the first end.
problem: Manufacturing multicore optical fibers with precise core alignment while avoiding structural defects during the drawing process.
constraint: The depressurization must be synchronized with the spinning/drawing process to maintain structural cohesion between the cladding tube and core rods without collapsing the holes.
mechanism: Controlled pressure differentials in a shared surrounding structure during a forming process draw internal components into alignment, enabling simultaneous formation of multiple aligned cores within a single composite structure.
mechanism_raw: Depressurizing holes in a common cladding tube during the drawing step creates controlled pressure differentials that draw core rods into alignment with the cladding, enabling simultaneous formation of multiple cores in a single fiber structure.

abstract: Disclosed herein are viral vectors for use in recombinant molecular biology techniques. In particular, the present disclosure relates to self-limiting viral vectors comprising genes encoding site-specific endonucleases as well as recognition sequences for site-specific endonucleases such that expression of the endonuclease in a cell cleaves the viral vector and limits its persistence time. In some embodiments, the viral vectors disclosed herein also carry directives to delete, insert, or change a target sequence.
problem: Controlling the persistence time of viral vectors in target cells to limit unintended genetic modification or immune responses.
constraint: The endonuclease expression and cleavage must occur after sufficient delivery of the therapeutic gene but before prolonged persistence, balancing efficacy with safety.
mechanism: Expression of internally encoded cleavage agents triggers self-destruction of the delivery vehicle's genetic material after sufficient cargo transfer, limiting persistence through timed degradation of the vector itself.
mechanism_raw: Expression of site-specific endonucleases encoded by the viral vector cleaves the vector's own genome after delivery, triggering self-destruction and limiting its persistence time in a dose- and time-dependent manner.

abstract: A method of fabricating an opto-pyrotechnic initiator, includes a) forming a body having a cavity in which a pyrotechnic charge is to be received, the body also having an internal passage extending between the cavity containing the pyrotechnic charge and an inlet opening out in an outside face of the body; b) placing a first portion of an optical fiber in the internal passage of the body, with a second portion of the optical fiber extending beyond the inlet of the body, and a glass preform being interposed between the optical fiber and the inlet of the body; and c) applying heat treatment to the glass preform to raise the glass preform to a temperature higher than the melting point of the glass preform so as to form a hermetic sealing element made of glass between the optical fiber and the inlet of the body.
problem: Creating a hermetic seal between an optical fiber and a pyrotechnic initiator body to ensure reliable light transmission without leakage.
constraint: The heat treatment must precisely control temperature and duration to melt the preform without damaging the optical fiber's core or the pyrotechnic charge.
mechanism: Thermal energy applied to a fusible material interposed between two components causes flow and solidification into a unified bond, creating a leak-proof interface through material fusion.
mechanism_raw: Heating a glass preform interposed between the fiber and the body to a temperature exceeding its melting point causes the glass to flow and form a monolithic seal, bonding the fiber and body through thermal fusion.

abstract: A standard musical score represented in digital format is analyzed for its constituent parts in order to identify notational directives for traversing through the musical score. A linearized version of the musical score is generated that is in substantially the same visual format but allows the reader to traverse through the musical score exclusively in a forward direction and without need for jumps in a reverse direction or forward jumps beyond the subsequent consecutive page. In certain embodiments, forward jumps may be minimally limited to a page within the musical score while in other embodiments a forward jump may be minimally limited to a line or a measure. In yet other embodiments, reverse jumps may be entirely eliminated while in still other embodiments, reverse jumps within pages may remain unchanged.
problem: Enabling forward-only traversal of a digital musical score to reduce cognitive load and eliminate disorienting jumps during reading.
constraint: The linearization must preserve the original visual format while altering traversal logic, requiring precise mapping of jumps to maintain musical coherence.
mechanism: Analysis of navigational directives in a structured document generates a transformed version that enforces sequential traversal by restricting reverse navigation and bounding forward navigation to predefined intervals.
mechanism_raw: Analyzing the score's notational directives and generating a linearized version that enforces sequential page/line/measure traversal by restricting reverse jumps and limiting forward jumps to predefined boundaries.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a lubricating oil additive containing a vicinal diol and a particular detergent blend typically is low viscosity base oils whereby exhibiting improved fuel economy.
