In this respect, disclosed is a lubricating oil composition comprising: a major amount of base oil of lubricating viscosity; a friction modifier which is selected from the group consisting of C10-C30 alkane 1,2-diols and C10-C30 alkene 1,2-diols; an overbased alkyl alkaline earth metal hydroxybenzoate detergent having a metal ratio less than 3.0; and an overbased alkyl calcium sulfonate or an overbased alkyl calcium hydroxybenzoate having a metal ratio of 3.5 or greater.
problem: Improving fuel economy in lubricating oils by balancing friction reduction and detergency in low-viscosity base oils.
constraint: The metal ratio thresholds (less than 3.0 and 3.5 or greater) must be precisely maintained to ensure the detergents do not counteract the friction modifier’s benefits or compromise base oil stability.
mechanism: Combining a friction-reducing agent with two detergent systems having distinct threshold values to balance friction reduction and deposit control. The friction-reducing agent directly lowers resistance, while the detergents with differing thresholds balance between preventing sludge and avoiding excessive viscosity increases.
mechanism_raw: Combining a vicinal diol friction modifier with two detergent blends having distinct metal ratios (one below 3.0 and another at 3.5 or higher) to synergistically reduce friction while maintaining deposit control. The diol directly lowers friction, while the detergents with differing metal ratios balance between preventing sludge and avoiding excessive viscosity increases.

abstract: The present disclosure is directed to climbing wall assemblies having a variety of improvements. For instance, the climbing wall assemblies may include connectors to attach the surface panels to the framework, in which the connectors may be mounted substantially anywhere along the front of the framework and at substantially any angle, providing for the securement of climbing panels in various geometries. The climbing wall assemblies may also include braces that may easily be adjusted to a desired length and configuration during construction of a climbing wall. The climbing wall assemblies may also include variable-angle, integral front posts, which provide for the easy and stable securement of climbing panels in various geometries. These improvements provide climbing wall assemblies that may be easily assembled to produce a desirable climbing wall structure having few framework components.
problem: Creating a climbing wall assembly that can be easily reconfigured into variable geometries without requiring custom framework components.
constraint: The connectors and braces must provide sufficient rigidity to support climbing loads while remaining simple enough to adjust during assembly without specialized tools.
mechanism: Using adjustable connectors and braces that allow surface panels to be mounted at arbitrary positions and angles on a framework. The variable-angle supports and length-adjustable braces enable secure attachment of panels in non-uniform configurations while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using adjustable connectors and braces that allow surface panels to be mounted at arbitrary positions and angles on a framework. The variable-angle front posts and length-adjustable braces enable secure attachment of panels in non-uniform configurations while maintaining structural integrity.

abstract: A propulsion system for an aircraft includes an electric propulsion engine. The electric propulsion engine includes an electric motor and a fan rotatable about a central axis of the electric propulsion engine by the electric motor. The electric propulsion engine also includes a bearing supporting rotation of the fan and a thermal management system. The thermal management system includes a lubrication oil circulation assembly and a heat exchanger thermally connected to the lubrication oil circulation assembly. The lubrication oil circulation assembly is configured for providing the bearing with lubrication oil. Such an electric propulsion engine may be a relatively self-sufficient engine.
problem: Managing heat dissipation in an electric propulsion engine to maintain self-sufficient operation without external cooling systems.
constraint: The lubrication oil must maintain adequate viscosity and flow properties across operating temperatures to simultaneously lubricate bearings and transfer heat effectively.
mechanism: Integrating a thermal management system that uses a fluid medium (e.g., lubrication oil) to transfer heat from critical components to a heat rejection unit. The fluid acts as a coolant, absorbing heat from bearings and other components and rejecting it via the heat exchanger, eliminating the need for separate cooling loops.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a thermal management system that uses the engine’s existing lubrication oil circulation to transfer heat from bearings to a heat exchanger. The oil acts as a coolant, absorbing heat from critical components and rejecting it via the heat exchanger, eliminating the need for separate cooling loops.

abstract: A sensor assembly for detecting material loss of a vessel transporting flowing media, the sensor assembly having at least one sensor positioned between a pair of annular plates such that the radially innermost surface of the sensor is in open communication with the flowing media. A series of parallel resistors spaced along the sensor and transmit a signal. As the material of the annular plates is worn away by corrosion and/or erosion, the outermost resistor becomes exposed to the flowing media and breaks the circuit as to that resistor, thus changing the signal.
problem: Detecting progressive material loss (corrosion/erosion) in a vessel transporting flowing media without interrupting operations.
constraint: The resistors must be spaced and positioned so that wear progression reliably exposes them in a predictable sequence, ensuring accurate signal changes without false triggers from transient media contact.
mechanism: Positioning a sensor with a series of parallel resistors between annular plates such that wear of the plates exposes resistors sequentially to the flowing media. Each exposed resistor breaks its circuit, altering the transmitted signal in a way that correlates to the extent of material loss.
mechanism_raw: Positioning a sensor with a series of parallel resistors between annular plates such that wear of the plates exposes resistors sequentially to the flowing media. Each exposed resistor breaks its circuit, altering the transmitted signal in a way that correlates to the extent of material loss.

abstract: A multi-functional, multi-directional wearable safety lighting device is disclosed herein that includes a main light housing and a magnetic mounting assembly coupleable to a bottom surface of the main light housing. The mounting assembly is configured to secure the wearable safety lighting device to a user. The main light housing includes warning light elements coupled front and rear side surfaces. A directional work light is coupled to the front side surface of the main housing and is distinct from the warning light elements. A power source supplies power to the warning light elements and the work light. A controller is programmed to energize the warning light elements in select subgroups following depression of a first control button or a second control button, and energize the directional work light following depression of a third control button.
problem: Providing both warning and directional work lighting in a wearable device while allowing user-selectable operational modes.
constraint: The controller must ensure that activating one lighting mode does not interfere with another, and the power source must supply sufficient current to all elements simultaneously during overlapping operations.
mechanism: Using a controller to activate distinct subgroups of warning lights (front/rear) and a separate work light based on input from multiple control buttons. The controller maps specific button presses to predefined lighting configurations, enabling mode switching without physical reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: Using a controller to activate distinct subgroups of warning lights (front/rear) and a separate work light based on input from multiple control buttons. The controller maps specific button presses to predefined lighting configurations, enabling mode switching without physical reconfiguration.

abstract: A method of generating a three-dimensional physical map using different data sources includes receiving, at a computing device, topographic data, e.g., digital surface model data and/or digital elevation model data, for a geographic area and also receiving map area data, e.g., coordinates, scaling, and/or resolution data, for a subset area of the geographic area. The computing device generates map data, such as computer-readable three-dimensional (3D) printer data, based on the topographic data and the map area data, which can be used by a 3D printer or other additive manufacturing process to generate a three-dimensional physical map that depicts the topographic features of the subset area.
problem: Converting heterogeneous digital geographic data into a physical, manufacturable three-dimensional representation of a specific sub-region.
constraint: The generated physical map must accurately represent the topographic features of the specified subset area while being constrained by the resolution and scaling parameters of both the input data and the additive manufacturing process.
mechanism: Combining spatial data sources representing terrain and boundary constraints, then computationally transforming the combined data into a physical structure definition that maps the terrain features into a manufacturable three-dimensional object.
mechanism_raw: Receiving topographic data (elevation/surface models) and map area data (coordinates, scaling, resolution) for a subset area, then computationally synthesizing these two data sources into fabrication-ready 3D printer data that maps the topographic features of the subset area into a physical object definition.

abstract: A motherboard substrate, a motherboard panel, a display panel, a display device and a method for manufacturing the display panel are provided. The motherboard substrate comprises a plurality of display substrates arranged in an array and regions provided between adjacent display substrates. Each display substrate includes a region to be packaged; a first reflection structure is provided at the region to be packaged; a second reflection structure is provided on the outside of the display substrate and in the region between adjacent display substrates; and the second reflection structure and the first reflection structure are spaced apart from each other.
reason: The abstract primarily describes a structural arrangement of reflection structures at specific locations (packaging region and inter-substrate region) without explaining a causal functional relationship that produces a useful effect. It lists component placement rather than articulating how the spacing or arrangement solves a problem through a transferable mechanism.

abstract: In an example embodiment, an atomizer for dispensing cleaning solution from a capsule is provided. The atomizer comprises a handle, a base, and an atomizer pipette extending from the nozzle to the base. The handle comprises a nozzle, a trigger, a lever, the atomizer pipette, and a capsule chamber. The base comprises a reservoir portion configured for receiving cleaning solution from the capsule. The handle is configured to be secured to the base. When the capsule is positioned within the capsule chamber and the lever is moved from an open position to a closed position, the cleaning solution is provided to the reservoir portion. When the capsule is positioned within the capsule chamber, the handle is secured to the base, and the trigger is activated, the cleaning solution is dispensed from the reservoir portion through the atomizer pipette and out of the nozzle.
problem: Controlled dispensing of cleaning solution from a replaceable capsule in a handheld atomizer, ensuring solution is available for dispensing only when properly loaded.
constraint: The capsule-loading action (lever closure) and the dispensing action (trigger activation) must be mechanically separated so that solution transfer to the reservoir is completed before dispensing, preventing dry dispensing or incomplete transfer.
mechanism: A two-stage mechanical process where a first action transfers material from a replaceable container into a storage chamber, and a second action dispenses the stored material through an outlet, with mechanical decoupling ensuring the second action cannot occur until the first action is fully completed.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage mechanical sequence: first, closing a lever actuates transfer of cleaning solution from the capsule into an internal reservoir (preparation/loading phase); second, activating a trigger dispenses the stored solution from the reservoir through a pipette and out the nozzle (dispensing phase). The two actions are mechanically decoupled so that dispensing cannot occur unless the capsule has been properly loaded and the reservoir filled.

abstract: There are provided an ultrasonic imaging apparatus, an ultrasonic probe apparatus, a signal processing apparatus, and a method for controlling an ultrasonic imaging apparatus. The ultrasonic imaging apparatus may include at least one first ultrasound element installed in a first ultrasound element installation unit; at least one second ultrasound element installed in a second ultrasound element installation unit that is separate from the first ultrasound element installation unit and such that the second ultrasound element forms a gap with the first ultrasound element; and a processor configured to estimate one or two or more virtual ultrasound signals that correspond to the gap based on a first ultrasound signal output from the at least one first ultrasound element and a second ultrasound signal output from the at least one second ultrasound element.
problem: Achieving continuous sensing coverage across a region where physical sensor elements cannot be placed due to a gap, such as between two separate sensor installation units.
constraint: The accuracy of the estimated virtual signals depends on the spatial relationship and signal correlation between the two physically separated sensor groups; the gap size must be within a range where reliable interpolation is possible.
mechanism: Using two spatially separated sensor groups to measure signals in a region, then computationally estimating one or more virtual signals corresponding to a gap between the groups based on the correlation and spatial relationship between the measured signals from both groups.
mechanism_raw: Using two spatially separated groups of ultrasound elements that flank a physical gap, receiving actual ultrasound signals from both groups, and computationally estimating one or more virtual ultrasound signals that correspond to the gap region based on the relationship between the real signals from the two groups. This fills the sensing gap without requiring physical elements in the gap region.

abstract: A system for cryogenic cooling of a remote cooling target comprising a cryogenic cooling device and a flexible cold fluid discharge interface, said flexible cold fluid discharge interface further comprising a flexible outer hose, a flexible middle recirculation line, a flexible inner hose, a flexible cryogen supply line, a first annular vacuum insulating area disposed between said flexible outer hose and said middle recirculation line, and a second annular vacuum insulating area disposed between said flexible inner hose and said flexible supply line. Said outer flexible hose, first evacuated annular segment, recirculation line, inner hose, second evacuated annular segment and supply line are arranged substantially concentrically. The system further comprising a first connecting means for connecting a first terminal end of the flexible cold fluid discharge interface to said cryogenic cooling device and a second connecting means comprising a rigid insertion member disposed at the second terminal end of the flexible cold fluid discharge interface for inserting into a remote cooling location.
problem: Delivering cryogenic cooling to a remote location through a flexible interface while minimizing heat transfer from the ambient environment into the cold fluid.
constraint: The system must balance thermal insulation performance (requiring sufficient vacuum gap width and layer count) against mechanical flexibility (requiring thin, bendable materials), and the concentric arrangement must maintain vacuum integrity across all insulating gaps during flexing.
mechanism: A concentric multi-layer system with vacuum-insulated gaps between adjacent flexible layers to minimize heat transfer through conduction and convection, while maintaining mechanical flexibility through bendable materials that preserve vacuum integrity during deformation.
mechanism_raw: Using a concentrically arranged multi-layer flexible conduit system where vacuum-insulated annular gaps are disposed between adjacent flexible hose layers (supply line, recirculation line, and outer hose). The vacuum gaps provide thermal insulation by eliminating convective and conductive heat transfer paths, while the flexible hose materials maintain mechanical flexibility for routing to the remote location.

abstract: Techniques for suppression of program disturb in flash memory devices are described herein. In an example embodiment, a method for suppression of program disturb in a flash memory array is provided. The flash memory array comprises rows and columns of memory cells, where the memory cells in each row are coupled to a source line and to a select-gate (SG) line, and the memory cells in each column are coupled to a respective bit line (BL). During a program memory operation, a first voltage, of a selected SG line, and a second voltage, of an unselected BL, are regulated independently of a power supply voltage of the flash memory array, where the first voltage is regulated in a first range of 0.9V to 1.1V and the second voltage is regulated in a second range of 0.4V to 1.2V.
problem: Program disturb in flash memory arrays during programming operations, where unintended voltage coupling affects unselected memory cells.
constraint: The regulated voltages must be maintained within specific narrow ranges (0.9V-1.1V for SG line, 0.4V-1.2V for BL) while remaining independent of the power supply voltage, requiring local regulation circuits that can override or bypass the global supply.
mechanism: Local voltage regulation on specific nodes by decoupling their control from a global power supply, allowing each node to be maintained within a precise target range to prevent disturbance propagation to adjacent components.
mechanism_raw: Independently regulating voltages on specific signal lines (selected SG line and unselected BL) by decoupling their control from the main power supply voltage, allowing each node to be held within a precise target range that prevents disturbance propagation to neighboring cells.

abstract: A head (14) for an oral care implement (10) has a mounting surface (20) comprising at least one tuft of a first type (16) and at least one tuft of a second type (18), the at least one tuft of the first type (16) and the at least one tuft of the second type (18) each having a cross-sectional area extending in a plane substantially perpendicular to a longitudinal axis. The cross-sectional area of the tuft of the first type (16) is smaller than the cross-sectional area of the tuft of the second type. The at least one tuft of the first type (16) comprises filaments having a substantially circular cross-sectional area extending in a plane perpendicular to the longitudinal axis and having an end-rounded free end, and the at least one tuft of the second type (18) comprises flagged filaments having split free ends.
reason: The patent describes a static product design with different tuft geometries (circular vs. flagged filaments) on a toothbrush head. It lists physical features rather than explaining a causal functional relationship that solves a problem through a transferable mechanism.

abstract: A method of controlling an electrosurgical HF apparatus, as well as an HF apparatus, includes an electrosurgical instrument and an HF generator for generating an HF current. The HF generator is in a locked state in which its activation is not possible. An application to be carried out is to be selected prior to a user-side activation of the HF generator, whereby the HF generator is unlocked.
problem: Preventing accidental or unauthorized activation of an electrosurgical HF generator, which could cause unintended tissue damage.
constraint: The application selection must occur prior to user-side activation, creating a mandatory sequence where the precondition gates the activation pathway, ensuring the generator cannot be activated without first specifying the intended use.
mechanism: Implementing a lock state that prevents activation until a precondition is explicitly satisfied, ensuring activation is only permitted after the intended procedure is selected, thereby gating the activation pathway through a mandatory sequence.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a lock state on the HF generator that prevents activation, and requiring a precondition (selection of a specific application) to be completed before user-side activation is permitted, thereby unlocking the generator only when the intended procedure is explicitly chosen.

abstract: Methods and apparatus for reacting rotary actuator and control surface loads into a wing structure using reaction links. The apparatus incorporates a structural interface feature that can facilitate a change of the component(s) in the load loop, such as the path connecting a control surface to a fixed aircraft structure via a rotary actuator. In particular, the structural interface between the rotary actuator and the rear spar of a wing can be tuned for stiffness to achieve an optimized load path that reacts actuator and control surface loads back into the wing structure. An actuator integration objective can be met for any rotary actuator using an integration method which tolerates wing and/or hinge line deflection.
problem: Reacting rotary actuator and control surface loads into a wing structure while accommodating structural deflection and optimizing the load path.
constraint: The stiffness tuning of the structural interface must balance optimized load transfer against the need to accommodate wing and/or hinge line deflection, requiring a design that can be adjusted to achieve the desired load path without over-constraining the structure.
mechanism: A structural interface with adjustable stiffness between a moving component and a supporting structure, enabling optimized load transfer while accommodating deflection through a compliant yet controllable connection that balances force transmission against structural flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Using a structural interface feature between the rotary actuator and the wing structure that can be tuned for stiffness, allowing the load path to be optimized for force transfer while tolerating deflection in the wing or hinge line through a compliant yet controllable connection.

abstract: A valve connector comprises a body including an inlet port, an outlet port defining a longitudinal axis, at least one aperture extending between an exterior surface of the body and the outlet port. The valve connector also comprises a sleeve arranged about the exterior surface of the body and movable relative to the body between a clamping position and a release position and a biasing member applying a biasing force against the sleeve towards the clamping position. The valve connector further comprises a clamping mechanism including at least one clamping member arranged at least partially within the aperture. When the valve is received in the outlet port, the clamping member is inwardly displaceable into the outlet port in response to the biasing force biasing the sleeve toward the clamping position, such that the clamping member engages the valve.
problem: Securely connecting a valve to a valve connector with reliable clamping engagement upon insertion.
constraint: The clamping member must be positioned within the aperture such that it is inwardly displaceable into the outlet port in response to the biasing force, ensuring that the insertion motion directly triggers the clamping engagement without requiring separate actuation steps.
mechanism: A biasing element that applies a force to a clamping member positioned within an aperture, where insertion of a component directly displaces the clamping member inwardly via the biasing force, automatically engaging the component as a direct result of the insertion motion without requiring separate actuation.
mechanism_raw: Using a biased sleeve that applies a biasing force toward a clamping position, where insertion of the valve into the outlet port causes at least one clamping member positioned in an aperture to be inwardly displaced by the biasing force, automatically engaging the valve as a direct result of the insertion action.

abstract: A filament accumulator assembly is provided containing a filament inlet for receiving a continuous filament from the filament source and a filament outlet for receiving the continuous filament from the filament inlet, the continuous filament forming a filament loop between the filament exiting the filament inlet and entering the filament outlet. The filament accumulator assembly further comprises a filament track defining at least part of an inner boundary and an outer boundary of a circuitous filament route between the filament inlet and the filament outlet, and the filament loop is bound by the filament track. The filament loop has a diameter that varies across a range of potential diameters within the filament track.
problem: Accumulating variable amounts of continuous filament between a source and an outlet while maintaining a continuous loop and a controlled filament path.
constraint: The filament must remain bound within the track boundaries while allowing diameter variation, balancing storage capacity with a controlled and predictable filament path.
mechanism: A guided loop system with fixed boundary constraints allows a continuous filament to expand or contract within a defined path, enabling variable storage capacity while maintaining a controlled trajectory. The loop diameter adjusts dynamically within the boundaries to accommodate filament accumulation without exceeding the track limits.
mechanism_raw: A filament track with defined inner and outer boundaries creates a circuitous route, and the filament loop is bound within this track. The loop diameter varies across a range of potential diameters within the track, allowing the loop to expand or contract to store more or less filament while remaining constrained by the track boundaries.

abstract: A body structure for a rail vehicle that includes a frame with at least one support element made at least predominantly of steel alloy, at least one equipment element made predominantly of aluminum alloy, at least one first plate having at least one longitudinal edge and a first surface delimited by the longitudinal edge, and at least one longitudinal batten of steel alloy, which is integral with the support element, wherein the longitudinal batten is fixed flat to the first face by way of friction melt bonding.
problem: Joining dissimilar metal alloys (steel and aluminum) in a structural rail vehicle body while maintaining structural integrity despite differing thermal expansion coefficients and metallurgical properties.
constraint: Must join materials with different thermal expansion coefficients and metallurgical properties while maintaining structural integrity and load-bearing capacity at the joint.
mechanism: A thermal fusion process joins materials with mismatched thermal expansion coefficients by generating localized heat at the interface, causing material melting and re-solidification to form a metallurgical bond. The process accommodates differential thermal behavior while maintaining structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Friction melt bonding is used to fix a steel alloy longitudinal batten flat to a face of a plate, creating a strong metallurgical bond between the dissimilar materials by melting and re-solidifying material at the interface under frictional heat.

abstract: A drilling assembly includes a straight housing in which a mud motor assembly is mounted. The mud motor includes a rotor that rotates within a stator. The rotor has an axial centerline substantially parallel with the housing. A drivetrain is coupled between the rotor and a driveshaft. The driveshaft is coupled to a drill head. The driveshaft has a centerline that is non-coincident with (i.e., offset or angled) the axial centerline. The angle between the driveshaft centerline and the axial centerline may be fixed or variable. The angle may be variable in response to an axial force, imparted to the rotor, that is transferred to the driveshaft through the drivetrain. Additional apparatus, systems, and methods are disclosed.
problem: Transmitting rotational motion from a motor to a drill head when their axes are not aligned, with the need for variable angular offset that responds to operational forces.
constraint: Must transmit torque through a non-aligned axis while allowing the angular offset to vary responsively to axial forces, without losing torque transmission efficiency.
mechanism: A variable-angle coupling transmits rotational motion between non-aligned axes by dynamically adjusting the angular offset in response to axial forces. The coupling maintains torque transfer efficiency while allowing responsive reorientation of the driven component.
mechanism_raw: A drivetrain couples a rotor with one axial centerline to a driveshaft whose centerline is non-coincident (offset or angled) with the rotor's centerline. The angle between the driveshaft and the rotor centerline is variable in response to an axial force imparted to the rotor, which is transferred to the driveshaft through the drivetrain.

abstract: A clamping device for a bone-in limb meat according to an embodiment includes a pair of clamp pieces including a first clamp piece and a second clamp piece, and being openable/closable so as to hold a bone-in limb meat, and rotation suppressing portions for suppressing a rotation of the bone-in limb meat, the rotation suppressing portions being disposed at positions deviated with respect to the pair of clamp pieces in a direction perpendicular to a plane including an opening/closing direction of the pair of clamp pieces. The rotation suppressing portions include a projection portion disposed so as to protrude from the first clamp piece into a space between the pair of clamp pieces and configured to contact the bone-in limb meat when viewed from the direction perpendicular to the plane.
problem: Holding irregularly shaped bone-in limb meat during processing while preventing rotation of the workpiece relative to the clamping device.
constraint: Must hold irregularly shaped bone-in meat with sufficient grip force while preventing rotation, with anti-rotation elements positioned outside the main clamping plane to avoid interference with the gripping action.
mechanism: A dual-element clamping system grips irregular workpieces using opposing clamp pieces, while dedicated anti-rotation elements positioned outside the primary clamping plane engage the workpiece to resist rotational displacement. A projection from one clamp piece extends into the gap between clamps to provide additional rotational constraint.
mechanism_raw: A pair of clamp pieces open and close to grip the meat, while rotation suppressing portions are positioned deviated from the clamp pieces in a direction perpendicular to the clamping plane. A projection from one clamp piece extends into the space between the clamps and contacts the bone-in meat to resist rotational movement.

abstract: The present invention relates to a composition for preventing and treating cancer-related fatigue, characterized by containing a new processed ginseng powder or a new processed ginseng extract having an increased amount of a ginsenoside constituent, which was previously minute, by preparing a saponin-decomposing enzyme and subsequently using hydrolysis by the prepared saponin-decomposing enzyme and an organic acid. The composition according to the present invention can be very effectively used for preventing and treating cancer-related fatigue, the most destructive and universal side effect, which is caused by cancer itself or occurs in association with the treatment of cancer.
problem: Increasing specific beneficial ginsenoside compounds in ginseng that are normally present in minute amounts, for the purpose of preventing and treating cancer-related fatigue.
constraint: Must selectively increase specific ginsenoside compounds through enzymatic hydrolysis while preserving the overall composition and avoiding degradation of other beneficial constituents.
mechanism: A two-stage biochemical enhancement process selectively amplifies target compounds by first applying enzymatic hydrolysis to break down precursor molecules, followed by chemical treatment with an organic acid to stabilize and increase the concentration of specific beneficial constituents while preserving other components.
mechanism_raw: A saponin-decomposing enzyme is prepared and used to perform hydrolysis on the ginseng, followed by treatment with an organic acid, which selectively increases the amount of previously minute ginsenoside constituents in the processed ginseng powder or extract.

abstract: Embodiments described herein provide an automatic lid opener comprising a base section, a top section, a middle section, at least one motor and a control panel. The base section comprises a base cavity capable of receiving a base portion of a jar, an inflatable grip within the base cavity, and a pump configured to inflate the inflatable grip, the inflatable grip configured to extend in a radially inward direction of the base cavity upon inflation and engage the base portion of the jar to form a grip, when the jar is positioned in the base cavity. The top section comprises a lid gripping mechanism and a lid rotation mechanism. The at least one motor is configured to operate at least one of the pump, the lid gripping mechanism, the rotation mechanism, or the height adjustment mechanism, and the control panel is configured to power the at least one motor.
problem: Opening containers (e.g., jars) without manual gripping or slippage, requiring stable base fixation during lid rotation.
constraint: Balancing inflation pressure to achieve sufficient grip strength without damaging the container or exceeding material limits of the inflatable element.
mechanism: An expandable element within a base structure applies inward radial force to secure a target object, decoupling rotational input from translational motion of the object. This creates a stable platform for manipulating a connected component.
mechanism_raw: Inflatable grip within a base cavity expands radially inward to engage and secure the container base, decoupling rotational forces on the lid from translational movement of the container. This creates a stable platform for lid manipulation.

abstract: A micromechanical sensor includes a first functional layer, a second functional layer, and a third functional layer The second functional layer is situated between the first and third functional layers. The second and third functional layers are connected to each other by a connecting area of the third functional layer. The second functional layer is underneath the connecting area at a defined distance from the first functional layer. The first functional layer is underneath the connecting area on an oxide that is situated on a substrate.
problem: Creating a micromechanical sensor structure capable of detecting mechanical displacement or force through layered interactions.
constraint: Maintaining precise interlayer spacing and connection geometry to ensure repeatable mechanical response without structural failure under stress.
mechanism: A multi-layer structure with a defined gap between layers enables controlled relative displacement between layers, mediated by a connecting region. External forces induce measurable deflection or strain in the layered system.
mechanism_raw: A sandwiched functional layer system with a defined vertical gap between layers allows controlled relative movement between the first and second layers, mediated by a connecting area in the third layer. This enables measurable deflection or strain in response to external forces.

abstract: A helmet detects shear force impacts. Indicator elements in the helmet or protective gear provides a visual indication, an audio indication, or a combination is contained in the surface of the outer shell of the helmet and detects when there is a mechanical force imparted on the helmet. One or more sensors are embedded in the helmet and detect when a shear force is imparted on the helmet. In other embodiments, the sensors can detect that there was a mechanical force on the helmet and also measure the energy of the force. The outer surface of the helmet may have a lining that changes appearance with a shear impact force hits the surface of the helmet.
problem: Detecting and quantifying shear force impacts (non-axial forces) on protective gear, which are often missed by traditional impact sensors.
constraint: Distinguishing shear forces from axial impacts while minimizing false positives, requiring sensor placement and signal processing tuned to directional force discrimination.
mechanism: Distributed sensors detect lateral force vectors across a surface, converting non-axial mechanical impacts into measurable energy values. Feedback indicators provide real-time information on impact severity and location.
mechanism_raw: Embedded sensors distributed across the helmet surface detect lateral or tangential force vectors, converting mechanical shear into measurable energy values. Visual/audio indicators provide real-time feedback on impact severity and location.
residual_terms: ["distributed sensors", "lateral force vectors", "non-axial mechanical impacts", "measurable energy values", "feedback indicators"]

abstract: A tactual finger grip device and method provides increased tactual and visual sensory awareness of finger pressure and alignment especially for the left-handed user. The grip device provides a conically shaped sleeve of resilient material for inserting and adjustably securing a hand-held implement, such as a writing implement. A plurality of raised surface projections circumferentially positioned about the grip device outer surface provide tactual friction with a user's fingers, enabling user tactile sensory awareness, causing the user to adaptably minimize the tactual friction by conforming fingers and hand to natural placement, when the user grasps the sleeve secured to the hand-held implement. The device provides visual indicia for the forefinger, index finger, and thumb placement forming a natural hand position. Alternatively, the raised surface projections positioned about the inner surface create tactual friction or pressure between the device and a wearer's received finger when pressure is applied to a surface.
problem: Improving tactile and visual feedback for finger pressure and alignment during gripping tasks, particularly for users with atypical hand orientation (e.g., left-handed individuals).
constraint: Optimizing projection geometry and material resilience to balance friction feedback with comfort and fatigue reduction during prolonged use.
mechanism: Surface projections on a resilient element create controlled friction against contacting surfaces, forcing adaptive conformation of the contacting body. This provides tactile feedback enabling self-correction of applied pressure and alignment.
mechanism_raw: Raised surface projections on a resilient conical sleeve create controlled friction against the user's fingers, forcing adaptive hand conformation. This provides tactile sensory awareness that enables self-correction of grip pressure and alignment.

abstract: A vehicle having a front trunk and a method of controlling a vehicle to access the trunk may include raising a hood from a closed position adjacent body structure to a fully open position with the hood oriented horizontally to provide access to a front trunk, raising a grille with the hood; and pivoting the grille about a hinge affixed to the hood. Front trunk lighting and bins maybe included in the vehicle.
problem: Accessing a front trunk compartment in a vehicle without obstruction from the hood or grille during opening.
constraint: Synchronizing the motion paths of the hood and grille to avoid collision or interference while maintaining structural integrity of the vehicle's front assembly.
mechanism: Coordinated pivoting of two components via a shared mechanical linkage allows one component to move along a path that avoids interference with the other component's motion. The movement of the second component is mechanically coupled to the first.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated pivoting of the hood and grille via a shared hinge system allows the hood to move horizontally while the grille pivots independently, creating unobstructed access to the trunk cavity. The grille's movement is mechanically linked to the hood's motion.

abstract: Compositions that include polymerases with features for improving entry of nucleotide analogues into active site regions and for coordinating with the nucleotide analogues in the active site region are provided. Methods of making the polymerases and of using the polymerases in sequencing and DNA replication and amplification as well as kinetic models of polymerase activity and computer-implemented methods of using the models are also provided.
problem: Improving the efficiency of nucleotide analogue entry into polymerase active sites during DNA sequencing or replication.
constraint: Balancing the need for enhanced analogue entry with the requirement to maintain precise coordination during the catalytic cycle to avoid disrupting fidelity or processivity.
mechanism: Structural features of a catalytic region are optimized to enhance interaction with target molecules through geometric and chemical compatibility, enabling coordinated binding and catalysis while maintaining fidelity during the catalytic cycle.
mechanism_raw: Structural features of the polymerase enzyme are engineered to enhance the physical interaction between the active site region and nucleotide analogues, enabling coordinated binding and catalysis through optimized geometric and chemical compatibility.

abstract: Provided is a vertical roller mill equipped with a rotary classifier for causing a plurality of classification blades provided above a rotary table and positioned around an axis to rotate about the axis, wherein: of a solid fuel pulverized by a roller, the rotary classifier guides solid fuel fine powder from an outer-circumferential-side space to an inner-circumferential-side space surrounded by the plurality of classification blades, and suppresses, by collision with the plurality of classification blades, an intrusion of solid fuel coarse powder into the inner-circumferential-side space; and each of the plurality of classification blades is shaped in a manner such that there is no interference between a scattering direction in which the coarse powder that collided with the classification blades scatters and an intake direction in which the fine powder is guided to the inner-circumferential-side space, and the scattering direction is oriented upward relative to a horizontal direction.
problem: Separating fine and coarse solid fuel particles in a vertical roller mill while preventing coarse particles from contaminating the fine powder stream.
constraint: Maintaining separation efficiency while preventing re-entrainment of coarse particles into the fine powder stream through controlled collision dynamics and directional flow management.
mechanism: A rotating element with angled surfaces directs particles via centrifugal flow, where fine particles follow inward trajectories while coarse particles collide with the surfaces and scatter outward, with surface orientation preventing interference between intake and scattering directions.
mechanism_raw: A rotary classifier uses angled classification blades to guide fine particles inward via centrifugal flow while coarse particles collide with the blades and scatter upward, with blade orientation ensuring no interference between intake and scattering directions.

abstract: A sandwiching device for creating pocket sandwich-type food, the sandwiching device having a stand, a lever mechanism attached to the stand, a punch attached to the lever mechanism, a die attached to the stand and positioned below the punch, and a sealer seated within the die. The lever mechanism is used to lower the punch and press the punch against the die and the sealer. When foodstuff is placed on the die, pressing the punch against the die and the sealer simultaneously cuts the crust off the foodstuff while sealing the edges of the foodstuff to create a pocket sandwich. To facilitate the sealing, the perimeter edge of the sealer may have a scalloped edge.
problem: Creating pocket sandwiches by simultaneously cutting crusts and sealing edges in a single mechanical operation.
constraint: Ensuring synchronized cutting and sealing forces to avoid misalignment or incomplete sealing, while accommodating variable foodstuff thicknesses.
mechanism: A compressive mechanism simultaneously applies cutting and sealing forces through a punch and die assembly, where a sealer's perimeter edge deforms and bonds material edges to form a sealed pocket while accommodating variable thickness.
mechanism_raw: A punch and die assembly with an integrated sealer applies compressive force to cut foodstuff while the sealer's perimeter edge (e.g., scalloped) deforms and bonds the edges to form a sealed pocket.

abstract: The present application provides a manufacturing method and a spinneret assembly that includes a nozzle body, an outer spinning solution channel formed inside the nozzle body, and at least one inner spinning solution channel formed inside the nozzle body. A nozzle outlet formed at an end of the nozzle body is immersed in a solidification liquid. The outer spinning solution channel includes an outer liquid outlet, and the at least one inner spinning solution channel includes an inner liquid outlet. The outer liquid outlet and the inner liquid outlet communicate with the nozzle outlet and are confluent at the nozzle outlet. A diameter of the inner liquid outlet is smaller than a diameter of the outer liquid outlet. An outer-layer dope spinned from the outer liquid outlet covers an inner-layer dope spinned from the inner liquid outlet so as to generate a solid filamentary fiber with multi-layer materials.
problem: Producing multi-layer synthetic fibers with controlled layer thickness and composition during wet spinning.
constraint: Balancing flow rates and viscosity between inner and outer layers to maintain structural integrity and prevent interlayer mixing during coagulation.
mechanism: Concentric flow paths with differing outlet diameters converge at a nozzle, where an outer-layer material flows around an inner-layer material to form a layered filament as they solidify in a solidification medium.
mechanism_raw: Concentric spinning solution channels with differing outlet diameters converge at a nozzle immersed in solidification liquid, where the outer-layer dope flows around the inner-layer dope to form a layered filament as they solidify.

abstract: A dough dividing device has a housing. Arranged therein is a feed chamber, for feeding dough, and a delivery chamber, which is arranged downstream and in delivery communication with the feed chamber. A delivery piston is arranged in a displaceably driven manner inside the delivery chamber for delivering dough. A measuring chamber is arranged downstream of the delivery chamber. In an extended delivery position a face of the delivery piston is arranged in a passage chamber between the delivery chamber and the measuring chamber. The passage chamber is delimited by a wall which extends circumferentially around the piston face. At least one degassing channel serves for degassing the measuring chamber. In the delivery position of the delivery piston the degassing channel is arranged between the piston face and the passage-chamber wall and creates a gas connection between the measuring chamber and a surrounding area.
problem: Delivering precise dough quantities while removing entrapped gas during the division process to ensure consistent product quality.
constraint: Maintaining gas permeability during delivery while preventing dough leakage or pressure imbalances that could affect measurement accuracy.
mechanism: A piston's extended position creates a degassing channel between its face and a circumferential wall, allowing gas to escape from a measuring chamber during material transfer without disrupting flow or measurement accuracy.
mechanism_raw: A delivery piston's extended position creates a degassing channel between its face and a circumferential wall, allowing gas to escape from the measuring chamber during dough transfer without disrupting material flow.

abstract: An electrochemical cell 10 is provided that includes first and second electrodes 13, 15, an electrolyte medium 17 in electrolytic communication with the first and second electrodes 13, 15, a chemical substance capable of undergoing an electrochemical reaction, and a voltage source 19 in electrolytic communication with the first and second electrodes 13, 15. The first electrode 13 includes a layer of an active catalyst material 25, and graphene coating 27 at least partially covering the layer of the active catalyst material 25. Methods for making and using the graphene coated electrode are further provided.
problem: Catalyst degradation or inefficiency in electrochemical cells due to direct exposure to reactive environments.
constraint: Balancing protection of the catalyst with sufficient conductivity and accessibility for electrochemical reactions.
mechanism: A conductive barrier layer partially covers an active catalytic region, creating a selective interface that permits ion/electron transport while isolating the catalyst from a reactive environment. The barrier preserves catalytic activity by limiting direct exposure to degradation-inducing conditions.
mechanism_raw: A graphene coating partially covers the active catalyst layer, acting as a protective barrier that preserves catalytic activity while maintaining electrolytic communication. The graphene layer allows ion/electron transport while shielding the catalyst from degradation.

abstract: The present invention is directed toward an automatic connected vehicle subsequent owner method and system for automatically wiping personal data from the vehicle, transitioning remote services access to a subsequent owner, and delinking the vehicle from their smartphone or other interactive communication link. In one more embodiments, a computer implemented method provides for delinking customers and deregistering vehicles from original owners where those vehicles have been subsequently sold, discontinued, or otherwise transferred for the customer's ownership.
problem: Personal data retention in vehicles during ownership transfer, risking privacy breaches.
constraint: Ensuring complete data removal while preserving non-personal system functionality and avoiding false triggers during non-transfer events.
mechanism: A detection module identifies ownership transition events (e.g., sale, deregistration) and triggers automated removal of user-specific data while preserving non-personal system configurations. The mechanism decouples personal data from the system without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: A system detects ownership transfer events (e.g., sale, deregistration) and automatically triggers data wiping and delinking of remote services. This decouples user-specific data from the vehicle without manual intervention.

abstract: One variation of a system for forming a meat patty includes: a cylinder operable in a upright position and an inverted position; a piston running within the cylinder and defining a set of gas ports; a grinder configured to grind meat and to dispense a quantity of ground meat into the cylinder, in the upright position, during a grind cycle; an actuator system configured to transition the cylinder from the upright position to the inverted position during a dispense cycle to dispense the quantity of ground meat from the cylinder; and a gas supply configured to supply gas to the cylinder behind the piston at a first pressure during the grind cycle to limit ingress of ground meat into the gas ports and at a second pressure greater than the first pressure during the dispense cycle to dislodge the quantity of ground meat from the piston.
problem: Clogging or inefficient dispensing of ground meat in automated patty-forming systems.
constraint: Maintaining pressure differentials sufficient to prevent clogging without over-pressurizing the system or damaging the meat structure.
mechanism: A pressure modulation system dynamically adjusts gas pressure: a lower pressure during material processing prevents ingress into mechanical ports, while a higher pressure during dispensing actively dislodges accumulated material. This ensures continuous flow across operational cycles.
mechanism_raw: Gas pressure is dynamically adjusted: a lower pressure during grinding prevents meat ingress into piston ports, while a higher pressure during dispensing actively dislodges meat from the piston. This pressure modulation ensures smooth operation across cycles.

abstract: A filter element has a filter medium body enclosing an inwardly positioned flow space and having a center axis. A support frame is arranged at an inner side of the filter medium body. At least one circumferentially extending sealing ring lip is arranged at the filter medium body and projects axially in an axial direction relative to the center axis past an end face of the filter medium body. The sealing ring lip is designed to seal relative to a housing component of a receiving filter housing. A support ring is arranged at the end face of the filter medium body at a radial distance to the sealing ring lip in a radial direction relative to the center axis. The support ring is supported in the radial direction at the support frame and is formed as one piece together with the support frame.
problem: Filter element collapse or seal failure under fluid pressure in filtration systems.
constraint: Balancing sealing flexibility to accommodate housing tolerances with sufficient radial support to prevent filter medium deformation under flow pressure.
mechanism: A flexible sealing element forms a dynamic interface against a housing to accommodate dimensional tolerances, while a structurally independent support component maintains radial rigidity. The design separates compliance requirements from load-bearing functions to prevent medium deformation under pressure.
mechanism_raw: A circumferential sealing ring lip flexes to form a dynamic seal against the housing, while a radially spaced support ring (integrated with the support frame) maintains structural integrity. The design decouples sealing compliance from structural rigidity.

abstract: The invention includes a solid rinse aid that is particularly designed for extrusion solid formation and which is effective for creating spotless surfaces after rinsing. According to the invention, application has identified the critical combination of solid surfactants, coupling agents, hydrotrope, and hardening agents that is acceptable in the extrusion process to create a solid. The hydrotrope includes one or more short-chain alkylbenzene and/or alkyl naphthalene sulfonates. The composition hardens quickly but not so quick as to negatively impact the extrusion process. The compositions may also be used to form pressed or cast solids.
problem: Achieving controlled solidification in extruded rinse aid compositions without disrupting manufacturing or performance.
constraint: Optimizing the hardening rate to align with extrusion process timing while ensuring the final solid dissolves cleanly without residue.
mechanism: A composition with a controlled solidification rate balances manufacturing timing constraints: it hardens sufficiently to maintain structural integrity during shaping but not so rapidly as to obstruct forming processes. The formulation ensures clean dissolution post-use without residual byproducts.
mechanism_raw: A specific combination of solid surfactants, coupling agents, hydrotropes (short-chain alkylbenzene/alkyl naphthalene sulfonates), and hardening agents creates a composition that hardens rapidly enough for extrusion but not so fast as to clog dies or compromise dissolution efficacy.

abstract: The present disclosure provides methods of activating an enzyme, such as error prone or template independent polymerase, using electricity to alter pH of a reaction zone and reaction site from an inactivating pH at which the enzyme is inactive to an activating pH at which the enzyme is active to add a nucleotide to an initiator or growing polymer chain. The activating pH can then be changed back to an inactivating pH and the process repeated as many times as desired to produce a target nucleic acid sequence.
problem: Controlling enzyme activity in a reaction to enable precise, repeatable synthesis of target nucleic acid sequences.
constraint: Maintaining enzyme stability and reaction specificity while cycling pH rapidly and repeatedly without degrading the enzyme or introducing errors.
mechanism: Using an electrical signal to reversibly shift the chemical environment of a reaction zone between states that deactivate and activate a catalyst, cycling the environment to trigger synthesis steps during active phases and halt activity during inactive phases.
mechanism_raw: Using electricity to reversibly alter the pH of a reaction zone between an inactivating pH (enzyme inactive) and an activating pH (enzyme active), cycling the pH to trigger nucleotide addition during active phases and halt activity during inactive phases.

abstract: An information handling system may include a network interface device; an antenna communicatively coupled to the network interface device to communicatively couple the information handling system to a wireless network device; and an antenna optimization system to selectively switch the antenna between an omni-directional antenna electromagnetic radiation pattern during listening periods for channel occupancy during collision avoidance protocol to a directed electromagnetic radiation pattern emission during data transmissions directed to the wireless network device.
problem: Optimizing wireless communication efficiency by balancing channel listening (collision avoidance) and directed data transmission.
constraint: Timing the antenna pattern switch to align with protocol phases (listening vs. transmitting) without introducing latency or signal degradation.
mechanism: Dynamically switching an antenna between a broad radiation pattern during listening periods (to detect channel occupancy) and a focused radiation pattern during data transmission (to direct energy toward a target device), reducing interference and improving throughput.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically switching an antenna between an omni-directional radiation pattern during listening periods (to detect channel occupancy) and a directed radiation pattern during data transmission (to focus energy toward a target device), reducing interference and improving throughput.

abstract: A hair brush that has a circular head or bristle portion with a circular hollow support member that has apertures that accommodate first and second bristles. Each bristle has a triangular hollow shape so that when positioned through the apertures, air can flow through (a) the hollow in the triangular bristles, (b) the apertures in the support member, and (c) outward through a non-bristle side of the support member.
reason: The patent describes a specific product design (hollow bristles and apertures for airflow) but does not articulate a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a broader problem beyond the brush's structural features.

abstract: According to one embodiment, a glass-ceramic composition may include from about 60 mol. % to about 75 mol. % SiO2; from about 5 mol. % to about 10 mol. % AI2O3; from about 2 mol. % to about 20 mol. % alkali oxide R2O, the alkali oxide R2O including Li2O and Na2O; and from 0 mol. % to about 5 mol. % alkaline earth oxide RO, the alkaline earth oxide RO including MgO. A ratio of Al2O3 (mol. %)) to the sum of (R2O (mol. %)+RO (mol. %)) may be less than 1 in the glass-ceramic composition. A major crystalline phase of the glass-ceramic composition may be Li2Si2O5. A liquidus viscosity of the glass-ceramic composition may be greater than 35 kP. The glass-ceramic composition may be used to form the glass clad layer(s) of a laminated glass article.
reason: The patent specifies a material composition with defined chemical ratios and properties but does not describe a functional mechanism for achieving an effect beyond the material's inherent characteristics.

abstract: Airfoils including a plurality of nozzles and venturi. The airfoils may include a body including an inner wall defining a high pressure fluid chamber, and a plurality of high pressure nozzles extending through the inner wall. Each high pressure nozzle may be in fluid communication with the high pressure fluid chamber. The airfoil body may also include an intermediate wall positioned adjacent to and surrounding the inner wall to define a low pressure fluid chamber formed between the intermediate wall and the inner wall, and a plurality of low pressure venturi extending through the intermediate wall. Each low pressure venturi may be in fluid communication with the low pressure fluid chamber. Additionally, the airfoil body may include an outer wall positioned adjacent to and surrounding the intermediate wall to define a cooling channel formed between the intermediate wall and the outer wall.
problem: Managing fluid pressure and cooling in an airfoil to maintain structural integrity and performance under varying operational conditions.
constraint: Balancing fluid pressure distribution across multiple chambers to avoid structural failure while maintaining effective cooling and airflow management.
mechanism: Integrating high-pressure flow directors and low-pressure suction elements within concentric chambers of a structural body to direct fluid flow, creating controlled pressure gradients that enhance cooling and aerodynamic stability.
mechanism_raw: Integrating high-pressure nozzles and low-pressure venturis within concentric chambers of the airfoil body to direct fluid flow, creating controlled pressure gradients that enhance cooling and aerodynamic stability.

abstract: A cartridge is disclosed that has a base with a first base portion with a first inlet opening for a first of the cold and hot fluids to be mixed, and a second base portion with a second inlet opening for the second fluid and an outlet opening for a mixture of the cold and hot fluids. The cartridge also has a thermostatic element, as well as a control spool for controlling the temperature of the mixture. The control spool defines a spool axis that is parallel to the base axis. In order to maximize the flow sections of the fluids through the base, the spool axis is offset relative to the base axis.
problem: Maximizing flow cross-sections for multiple fluids through a mixing cartridge while maintaining thermostatic temperature control of the mixture.
constraint: The spool must remain functionally capable of temperature regulation despite being offset, creating a tradeoff between maximizing flow area and maintaining precise thermostatic control.
mechanism: Positioning an actuating element off-axis relative to the main flow conduit so that the element is displaced from the primary fluid channels, enabling the inlet and outlet openings to retain larger cross-sectional areas without constriction by the element, while the element still moves to modulate mixture temperature through interaction with a temperature-responsive regulator.
mechanism_raw: Offsetting the control spool axis relative to the base axis so that the spool is positioned away from the primary flow paths, allowing the fluid inlet and outlet openings to maintain larger cross-sectional areas without being constricted by the spool, while the spool still traverses to regulate temperature via the thermostatic element.

abstract: There is provided a method and apparatus for manufacturing filters for smoking articles. The method comprises providing hollow tubes (309) of filter material. Each hollow tube has an outer diameter and an inner diameter. The method further comprises providing filter inserts (205). Each filter insert (205) has a first portion having a cross sectional dimension larger than the inner diameter of the hollow tube. The method further comprises inserting each filter insert (205) into a hollow tube (309) of filter material. During inserting, the first portion of the filter insert (205) engages with the hollow tube (309) to retain the filter insert in the hollow tube.
problem: Retaining a filter insert securely within a hollow tube of filter material during manufacturing of smoking article filters.
constraint: The insert must be large enough to create sufficient engagement for retention but small enough to allow insertion without damaging or rupturing the hollow tube material.
mechanism: Employing an interference engagement where a segment of the inserted component has a transverse dimension exceeding the internal passageway of the receiving tube, so that during placement the enlarged segment presses against the tube wall, generating frictional retention that secures the component without auxiliary fastening or bonding agents.
mechanism_raw: Using an interference fit where a portion of the filter insert has a cross-sectional dimension larger than the inner diameter of the hollow tube, so that during insertion the oversized portion engages with the tube wall material, creating frictional retention that holds the insert in place without additional fasteners or adhesives.

abstract: The composite pultruded products either in “I” profile or “Plate” profile of higher cross sectional area where said products consisting essentially synthetic polyester felts as core impregnated with a resin system comprises of at least one resin, curing system comprising a curing agent and an accelerator, a filler, a thinner, pigment or any other additives; encapsulated between bi-directionally and/or uni-directionally oriented synthetic fabric selected from polyester, carbon, aramid, glass, basalt and mixtures thereof impregnated with said resin system are provided. In another composite pultruded products either in “I” profile or “Plate” profile of higher cross sectional area where said products consisting of plank of short fibers bagasse premixed with the said resin system as core is enclosed between the synthetic polyester felts impregnated with the resin system which is further enclosed between bi-directionally and/or uni-directionally oriented synthetic fabric selected from polyester, carbon, aramid, glass, basalt and mixtures thereof impregnated with the resin system. The system and method for the preparation of said composite pultruded products are also illustrated herein. These products lead to a significant reduction in weight and reduction in density with higher stiffness and bending strength. The present composite products are encapsulated by fabrics in the peripheral area bringing more integrity uniformity of synthetic polyester felt materials. This leads to a significant cost reduction without sacrificing much tensile strength.
problem: Creating lightweight composite materials with high stiffness and bending strength while reducing material cost.
constraint: Balancing weight reduction and cost savings against the need to maintain sufficient tensile strength, as the core materials are lower-cost but lower-strength compared to the reinforcing fabrics.
mechanism: Sandwiching a low-density core material between layers of directionally oriented reinforcing fabric, where the outer fabric layers supply tensile and flexural reinforcement while the encapsulated core provides internal support and uniformity, with peripheral fabric wrapping binding the core into a unified composite structure.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating a low-density core material (synthetic polyester felt or short fiber plank) between layers of bi- or uni-directionally oriented reinforcing fabric, where the outer fabric layers provide tensile and bending reinforcement while the encapsulated core contributes structural integrity and uniformity, with the peripheral fabric encapsulation binding the core into a cohesive composite structure.

abstract: The present invention pertains to a glass for a data storage medium substrate which contains a specific amount of each of SiO2, Al2O3, MgO, CaO, SrO, BaO, Li2O, Na2O, and K2O, in molar percentage based on the oxides, and does not substantially contain B2O3 or ZrO2, wherein the sum of the Li2O, Na2O, and K2O contents (R2O), the molar ratio of the SiO2 content to the Al2O3 content (SiO2/Al2O3), and the molar ratio of the sum of the SiO2 and Al2O3 contents (SiO2+Al2O3) to R2O[(SiO2+Al2O3)/R2O] fall within their specific ranges, formula (1): 90<[SiO2]+2×[Al2O3]+0.8×[RO]−0.5×[R2O] [in formula (1), RO represents the sum of the MgO, CaO, SrO, and BaO contents] is satisfied, and the glass transition point Tg, the alkali resistance, and the acid resistance fall within their specific ranges.
problem: Creating glass compositions with specific properties (low density, high stiffness, chemical resistance) suitable for data storage medium substrates.
constraint: The glass must avoid B2O3 and ZrO2 while simultaneously satisfying multiple property targets (Tg, chemical resistance) and the compositional formula constraint, limiting the available formulation space.
mechanism: Adjusting the proportional composition of network-forming and network-modifying oxides within defined ranges, including a stoichiometric constraint that balances each oxide group's contribution to the material structure, to produce a substance with targeted thermal transition temperature, chemical inertness, and mechanical stiffness while excluding specific constituents that would impair performance.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the molar ratios of network formers (SiO2, Al2O3) and network modifiers (alkaline earth oxides RO, alkali oxides R2O) within specific ranges, including a formula constraint that balances the contributions of each oxide group to the glass structure, to achieve a glass with targeted glass transition temperature, alkali resistance, and acid resistance while excluding certain components that would degrade performance.
residual_terms: ["network formers", "network modifiers", "molar ratios", "glass transition temperature", "chemical resistance"]

abstract: An optimal sample size for experiments targeting units having specific static criteria is determined, based on one or more iterations of a performed experiment. The sample size to use for subsequent experiments targeting units having the specific static criteria is calculated based on target effect of the performed experiment. Multiple iterations can be performed to refine the sample size. Each iteration uses the previously calculated sample size as a parameter. The calculated sample size is then used to determine an optimal treatment. Separate experiments using separate treatments are performed on separate group sets of the calculated sample size. For each separate performed experiment, a score is calculated for the corresponding specific treatment, taking into account actual effect size, statistical significance and homogeneity of effect. Depending upon the score, the given treatment can be accepted for production usage or discarded, or the experiment can be replicated to validate effect.
problem: Determining optimal sample sizes for experiments and selecting treatments for production usage based on experimental results.
constraint: Balancing statistical power (larger sample sizes for detecting effects) against experimental cost and resource constraints, while also balancing multiple potentially conflicting evaluation criteria (effect size, significance, homogeneity) in the treatment scoring.
mechanism: Iteratively updating sample size determinations using measured effect magnitudes from preceding experimental cycles, then applying the computed sample size to execute concurrent trials with distinct treatments, evaluating each treatment through a weighted assessment of observed effect magnitude, statistical confidence, and consistency of effect, and employing the resulting evaluation to choose whether to adopt, reject, or repeat the trial for confirmation.
mechanism_raw: Iteratively refining sample size calculations using observed effect sizes from prior experiment iterations, then deploying the calculated sample size to run parallel experiments with separate treatments, scoring each treatment based on a composite evaluation of actual effect size, statistical significance, and homogeneity of effect, and using the score to decide whether to accept, discard, or replicate the experiment for validation.

abstract: The present invention discloses a thermally activated delayed fluorescence material and application thereof in an organic electroluminescence device. The thermally activated delayed fluorescence material is a compound having the general structure of Formula I or Formula II:In Formula I and Formula II, R1 is a cyano, p is 1, 2 or 3, q is 1, 2 or 3, m is 1 or 2, n is 1 or 2, and X is bromine or iodine. The present invention further discloses application of the thermally activated delayed fluorescence material as a host material or a luminescent dye of a luminescent layer of an organic electroluminescence device.
problem: Need to efficiently harvest both singlet and triplet excitons for light emission in organic electroluminescence devices, since triplet excitons are normally non-emissive and wasted as heat.
constraint: The singlet-triplet energy gap must be small enough for thermal activation at practical operating temperatures, but large enough to maintain proper electronic properties and prevent quenching.
mechanism: A material with a controlled energy gap between two electronic states enables thermal activation at operational temperatures to convert non-emissive states into emissive states. This thermal upconversion process recovers energy that would otherwise be lost, increasing the efficiency of a light-emitting system by utilizing both electronic pathways.
mechanism_raw: A compound with a small singlet-triplet energy gap allows thermal energy at operating temperature to activate reverse intersystem crossing, converting non-emissive triplet excitons into emissive singlet states. This thermal upconversion harvests energy that would otherwise be lost, effectively doubling the internal quantum efficiency by utilizing both singlet and triplet pathways.

abstract: An apparatus includes a MEMS wafer with a device layer and a handle substrate bonded to the device layer. A complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (“CMOS”) wafer includes an oxide layer, and a passivation layer overlying the oxide layer. A bonding electrode overlies the passivation layer. A eutectic bond is between a first bonding metal on the bonding electrode and a second bonding metal on the MEMS wafer. A sensing electrode overlies the passivation layer. A shield electrode is adjacent to the sensing electrode. A sensing gap is positioned between the sensing electrode and the device layer, wherein the sensing gap is smaller than a shield gap positioned between the shield electrode and the device layer.
problem: Need to sense mechanical displacement in a MEMS device bonded to a CMOS wafer while simultaneously providing electromagnetic shielding to prevent interference with the sensing electrode.
constraint: Gap sizes must be precisely controlled during fabrication to achieve the desired sensitivity differential, while the eutectic bond between the wafers must maintain structural integrity and electrical connectivity.
mechanism: A geometric differential arrangement uses varying separation distances between a sensing element and a shielding element relative to a reference surface. The shielding element, positioned with a larger separation, provides electromagnetic isolation while remaining mechanically insensitive to small displacements. The sensing element, positioned with a smaller separation, exhibits greater sensitivity to mechanical movement. This spatial configuration enables selective sensitivity while maintaining shielding.
mechanism_raw: Different gap distances between the sensing electrode and the shield electrode relative to the device layer create a differential sensitivity arrangement. The shield electrode, positioned with a larger gap, is mechanically less sensitive to small displacements but provides electromagnetic isolation. The sensing electrode, positioned with a smaller gap, is more sensitive to mechanical movement. This geometric differential allows selective sensitivity while maintaining shielding.

abstract: A fid is made of separate components that can be easily assembled and disassembled by the user. In this manner the fid components can be easily stored or transported and then assembled when needed to create a fid of sufficient length to splice a synthetic rope or other types of rope. The fid includes an elongate shaft or needle with a first that tapers to a point. The opposing end of the shaft may be machined to form a connection structure. A coupler may have an elongate form with two opposing ends along a center axis. One end of the coupler removable attaches to the needle at the connection structure. The second end of the coupler permanently attaches to a rope holder, which may take the form of a cylindrical, helically wound braid of thin wire cable forming a wire basket.
problem: Need for a rope splicing tool (fid) that can be compactly stored and transported, yet assembled to sufficient length when needed for splicing operations.
constraint: The quick-connect interface must be strong enough to withstand splicing forces without accidental disconnection, yet easily releasable by hand without tools for repeated assembly and disassembly.
mechanism: A modular tool uses a detachable mechanical interface between an elongate working element and a handle component. The working element features a structured connection point that engages with a complementary coupling on the handle. This allows the tool to be disassembled into shorter segments for storage and reassembled by the user when needed, with the detachable connection providing both portability and functional length extension.
