mechanism_raw: A modular fid uses a removable quick-connect coupling between an elongate needle (with a machined connection structure at one end) and a coupler. The coupler permanently attaches to a rope holder, while the needle detachably connects to the coupler. This allows the fid to be disassembled into shorter components for storage and reassembled by the user when needed, with the removable connection providing both portability and functional length extension.

abstract: An apparatus for producing a printed circuit board on a substrate, has a table for supporting the substrate, a function head configured to effect printing conductive and non-conductive materials on the substrate, a positioner configured to effect movement of the function head relative to the table, and a controller configured to operate the function head and the positioner to effect the printing of conductive and non-conductive materials on the substrate. The apparatus optionally has a layout translation module configured to accept PCB multilayer circuit board files and convert multilayer circuit board layout data of the PCB multilayer circuit board files to printing data files for controlling the function head to print conductive material and nonconductive material onto the substrate to produce a printed circuit effecting functionality of the multilayer circuit board layout data.
problem: Need to produce functional printed circuit boards by directly depositing both conductive and non-conductive materials in precise patterns on a substrate, translating digital design data into physical circuit structures.
constraint: The material deposition must achieve sufficient precision in trace width and spacing to create electrically functional circuits, while the function head and positioner must coordinate to handle both conductive and non-conductive materials without cross-contamination.
mechanism: A digital-to-physical translation system converts design data into controlled material deposition patterns. A deposition element, coordinated with a positioning mechanism relative to a substrate, applies multiple material types in precise spatial arrangements according to translated layout instructions. This closed-loop process transforms digital specifications directly into physical structures through synchronized material placement.
mechanism_raw: A layout translation module converts multilayer PCB circuit board files into printing data files that control a function head. The function head, moved by a positioner relative to a substrate-supporting table, deposits conductive and non-conductive materials in precise patterns according to the translated layout data. This closed-loop system transforms digital circuit designs directly into physical printed structures through controlled material deposition.

abstract: A scroll compressor is provided capable of supplying oil stored in an oil storage chamber upward through a rotary shaft to supply the oil to a compression device and to lubricate a bearing portion. The scroll compressor may include a casing, a drive motor, a rotary shaft, a main frame, a fixed scroll, and an orbiting scroll. A medium pressure chamber may be formed in or at a middle of the main frame, the fixed scroll, and the orbiting scroll. A pocket groove configured to guide oil discharged through the oil hole to the medium pressure chamber may be formed in an upper surface of the orbiting scroll, and a differential pressure path configured to guide the oil guided to the medium pressure chamber to the compression chamber may be provided in the fixed scroll.
problem: Need to supply oil from a storage chamber through a rotating shaft to lubricate bearings and deliver oil to the compression chamber in a scroll compressor, despite relative motion between the orbiting and fixed scrolls.
constraint: The oil routing passages must maintain proper pressure differentials and flow continuity despite the orbital motion of the scroll, while the pocket groove and differential pressure path must be precisely aligned to guide oil effectively during rotation.
mechanism: A rotating system routes fluid through a guided pathway that maintains flow continuity despite relative motion between components. A collection chamber formed by multiple moving parts acts as an intermediate reservoir, receiving fluid from a rotating source. A pressure-driven redistribution path then directs the fluid to a target location based on differential pressure gradients, ensuring delivery despite orbital movement.
mechanism_raw: Oil is discharged through an oil hole in the rotary shaft, then guided by a pocket groove on the orbiting scroll's upper surface to a medium pressure chamber formed in the main frame, fixed scroll, and orbiting scroll. From this intermediate collection point, a differential pressure path in the fixed scroll routes the oil to the compression chamber. The medium pressure chamber acts as a stable intermediate reservoir that collects oil from the rotating system and redistributes it via pressure differentials to the target location.

abstract: An inspecting and repairing device of additive manufacturing technology and a method thereof are provided. The inspecting and repairing device has a powder bed unit, a repairing unit, and an inspection unit. The powder bed unit has a powder platform, a powder spreading mechanism and a laser unit. The repairing unit has a processing mechanism. The inspection unit has a camera and a controller. According to an image of the powder platform captured by the camera, the controller can determine whether spreading powders, whether being overcome a powder spreading defect, or whether driving the processing mechanism to repair a surface of a workpiece.
problem: Detecting and correcting defects during additive manufacturing (e.g., powder spreading defects, surface imperfections) without interrupting the build process.
constraint: The controller must make accurate defect-detection and repair decisions from image data in real-time during the manufacturing process, balancing inspection thoroughness against process throughput.
mechanism: A real-time closed-loop feedback system where an imaging sensor continuously captures images of a work surface during a manufacturing process, a controller analyzes the images to detect anomalies, and based on the analysis, autonomously decides whether to adjust the material deposition process or activate a corrective mechanism to fix the workpiece surface. The visual inspection directly drives corrective action without human intervention.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop feedback system where an imaging sensor captures real-time images of the powder bed, a controller analyzes the images to detect anomalies, and based on the analysis, autonomously decides whether to adjust the powder spreading process or activate a repair mechanism to fix the workpiece surface. The visual inspection directly drives corrective action without human intervention.

abstract: A coiled tubing injector apparatus for inserting and/or removing coiled tubing from a well head comprising a first injector column and a second injector column forming a central pathway within a frame. The first and second injector columns each comprise an inner and outer band, the outer band containing a plurality of rolling elements for engaging the coiled tubing and the inner band creating drive force to energize the outer band. The inner band further comprises a wear plate designed to sustain the majority of wear for less costly maintenance and repair of injection heads.
problem: Managing wear in a coiled tubing injector drive system to reduce maintenance costs and downtime while maintaining reliable gripping and driving force on the tubing.
constraint: The wear plate must be designed to fail or degrade preferentially over the outer band components, requiring it to be easily replaceable while still maintaining sufficient structural integrity to transmit drive forces.
mechanism: A dual-band drive system where an inner band generates the primary drive force that energizes an outer band, and the outer band's rolling elements engage the workpiece. A sacrificial wear component is integrated into the inner band to absorb the majority of mechanical wear, protecting the more complex and costly outer band and rolling elements from degradation.
mechanism_raw: A dual-band drive system where an inner band generates the primary drive force that energizes an outer band, and the outer band's rolling elements engage the coiled tubing. A sacrificial wear plate is integrated into the inner band to absorb the majority of mechanical wear, protecting the more complex and costly outer band and rolling elements from degradation.
residual_terms: ["dual-band drive system", "inner band", "outer band", "rolling elements", "sacrificial wear component", "drive force"]

abstract: A drive mechanism deforms two diaphragms to perform alternate increase and decrease in volume of a supply chamber. At this time, the two diaphragms are provided for the single supply chamber. This leads to possibility of suction and feed out of a desired amount of liquid even with limited deformation of the diaphragms. In addition, the two diaphragms achieve suppression in deformation thereof upon suction and feed out of a desired amount of liquid. This allows selection of the diaphragms each with a short stroke, yielding suppressed stagnation and quality degradation of the liquid.
problem: Achieving precise suction and dispensing of liquid with limited diaphragm stroke, while minimizing fluid stagnation and quality degradation.
constraint: Each diaphragm must have a short stroke (limiting individual displacement), so the system relies on coordinated dual-actuation to achieve the required total volume change, trading mechanical complexity for improved fluid quality and reduced stagnation.
mechanism: Two diaphragms cooperate on a single supply chamber, deforming alternately to increase and decrease chamber volume. The dual-diaphragm arrangement allows the system to achieve the desired fluid displacement even when each individual diaphragm has only a short stroke, and the cooperative action suppresses excessive deformation of either diaphragm during operation.
mechanism_raw: Two diaphragms cooperate on a single supply chamber, deforming alternately to increase and decrease chamber volume. The dual-diaphragm arrangement allows the system to achieve the desired fluid displacement even when each individual diaphragm has only a short stroke, and the cooperative action suppresses excessive deformation of either diaphragm during operation.

abstract: A mechanical parking garage includes a plurality of pallets, a parking system including a rail track unit and a plurality of tower units, and a transporting system. Each tower unit is mounted on and slidable along the rail track unit, and has a plurality of first parking spaces, each of which is disposed for storing one of the pallets. The transporting system includes a rail mechanism mounted above the parking system, and a transporting mechanism mounted to the rail mechanism and being horizontally movable. Any adjacent two of the tower units are movable relative to each other between approximate state and a distal state. At the distal state, the adjacent two of the tower units define a transporting aisle therebetween.
problem: Efficiently accessing and transporting vehicles to/from storage locations in a mechanical parking system without requiring permanent aisles that waste space.
constraint: The towers must be mechanically movable along the rail track, adding complexity to the structure, but this enables dynamic aisle creation that maximizes storage density compared to fixed-aisle systems.
mechanism: Storage units are mounted on a rail track and can move relative to adjacent units between a closed (proximate) state and an open (distal) state. When adjacent units move apart, they create a temporary transporting aisle between them, allowing a rail-mounted transport mechanism to access stored items in those units. The aisles are formed on-demand only where and when needed.
mechanism_raw: Storage tower units are mounted on a rail track and can move relative to adjacent towers between a closed (proximate) state and an open (distal) state. When adjacent towers move apart, they create a temporary transporting aisle between them, allowing a rail-mounted transport mechanism to access pallets stored in those towers. The aisles are formed on-demand only where and when needed.
residual_terms: ["storage units", "rail track", "adjacent units", "transporting aisle", "rail-mounted transport mechanism", "stored items", "on-demand"]

abstract: A schedule data acquisition requestor requests and acquires schedule data from a sub controller. When a modification to the acquired schedule data is made, a schedule data update requestor sends the modified schedule data to the sub controller and requests an update. A schedule data update processor sends a permission notification to a main controller in response to the update request and writes the modified schedule data onto its own flash memory. Conversely, when a rejection notification is sent from the sub controller, the schedule data update requestor displays a warning message and new schedule data on a screen.
problem: Synchronizing schedule data updates between a main controller and distributed sub-controllers while handling both successful updates and rejected modifications gracefully.
constraint: The system must maintain local copies of schedule data and coordinate state between multiple controllers, requiring reliable communication and local storage, but this enables continued local operation even when the central controller is unavailable.
mechanism: A hierarchical update protocol where a local system acquires schedule data from a sub-controller, and when modifications are made, sends the updated data to the sub-controller for approval. Upon receiving permission, the local system writes the data to its own memory and notifies the main controller. If the sub-controller rejects the update, the local system displays a warning and presents the new schedule data on a display, ensuring the user is informed of the conflict.
mechanism_raw: A hierarchical update protocol where a local system acquires schedule data from a sub-controller, and when modifications are made, sends the updated data to the sub-controller for approval. Upon receiving permission, the local system writes the data to its own flash memory and notifies the main controller. If the sub-controller rejects the update, the local system displays a warning and presents the new schedule data on a screen, ensuring the user is informed of the conflict.
residual_terms: ["hierarchical update protocol", "local system", "sub-controller", "main controller", "schedule data", "approval", "flash memory", "warning", "display"]

abstract: The invention generally relates to sequencing library preparation methods. In certain embodiments, two or more template nucleic acids are joined together by a linking molecule, such as a PEG derivative. Identical copies of a nucleic acid fragment or both strands of a duplex fragment may be linked together. The linked nucleic acids are amplified, creating linked amplicons. Emulsion PCR with linked primers creates linked template nucleic acids for seeding sequencing clusters and errors can be readily identified by their presence on only one of the linked fragments.
problem: Errors in sequencing cannot be reliably distinguished from true genetic variants when amplifying individual nucleic acid fragments.
constraint: The linking chemistry must preserve the physical association of fragments through amplification and sequencing steps without disrupting their structural integrity or introducing bias.
mechanism: Create paired entities from a target molecule by linking identical or complementary copies through a connecting agent, such that discrepancies between the paired entities during analysis indicate errors while consistent features represent true variants. The linking preserves physical association through processing steps without disrupting structural integrity or introducing bias.
mechanism_raw: Linking identical copies or complementary strands of a nucleic acid fragment via a linking molecule (e.g., PEG derivative) creates paired amplicons. During sequencing, errors introduced in one fragment are detected because they appear only on one of the linked fragments, while true variants are present on both.

abstract: An intermediate casing for a turbine engine, comprising at least one central hub and one shroud (12) which are positioned concentrically, and mutually mechanically connected by structural arms (11), with such casing comprising at least one sealing part (13) attached between the shroud (12) and a structural arm (11), with the sealing part (13) including at least one metal core and one seal.
reason: The patent describes a static structural arrangement of components (hub, shroud, arms, sealing parts) without explaining a causal functional relationship that produces an effect beyond the specific mechanical design.

abstract: An article of footwear includes a sole structure including a chamber for receiving a pressurized fluid, the chamber having a top portion, a bottom portion, and side portions around a periphery of the chamber. The sole structure also includes a central structure located in a central portion of the chamber between opposing side portions of the chamber, such that the chamber is devoid of additional structures in a surrounding region around the central structure and extending from the central structure to the side portions of the chamber. On all sides of the central structure, a dimension of the surrounding region between the central structure and the nearest side portion is one third or more of a span across the chamber between opposing side portions.
problem: Balancing cushioning and structural support in a pressurized fluid chamber for footwear or similar applications.
constraint: The central structure must be sized and positioned to ensure the surrounding regions meet the minimum dimensional threshold without compromising the chamber's ability to contain pressurized fluid.
mechanism: Position a central structural element within a containment volume such that surrounding regions on all sides maintain a minimum proportional dimension relative to the overall span. This spatial arrangement distributes applied forces across the volume while preserving structural support, enabling controlled deformation and energy absorption.
mechanism_raw: A central structure is positioned within the chamber, with surrounding regions on all sides having a dimension of at least one-third of the chamber's span. This spatial arrangement distributes forces across the chamber while maintaining structural support, enabling controlled deformation and energy absorption.

abstract: A continuous flow reactor includes a shell, wherein the shell is provided with a shell pass inlet and a shell pass outlet which are communicated with an inner cavity of the shell, tube plates and communication devices are connected to upper and lower ends of the shell, a reaction tube bank is arranged in the shell and includes a plurality of reaction tubes, upper and lower ends of each reaction tube are fixedly connected to the tube plates in a penetrating manner, and all the reaction tubes are sequentially communicated in series through the communication devices.
reason: The patent describes a conventional reactor configuration (shell, tube plates, serially connected tubes) without explaining a novel causal mechanism beyond standard continuous-flow reactor design principles.

abstract: A present robot operation apparatus operates a robot including a plurality of joints, and includes an operation unit that transmits a signal corresponding to an operation by an operator to a control unit of the robot, and the operation unit is configured to be detachably attached to an attachment member fixed to an arm member of the robot arranged closer to a base than the joint closest to a tip among the plurality of joints.
problem: Enabling detachment of a robot control unit without interfering with the robot's joint operations or requiring complex reconfiguration.
constraint: The attachment point must be positioned sufficiently close to the base to avoid mechanical interference with the robot's articulation while remaining accessible for detachment.
mechanism: Attach a detachable component to a fixed point on a multi-joint articulated system positioned closer to the base than the most distal joint. This placement enables independent attachment/detachment of the component without requiring reconfiguration of distal joints, preserving operational continuity during detachment.
mechanism_raw: The operation unit is attached to a fixed member on the robot's arm closer to the base than the tip-most joint. This placement allows the control unit to be detached or reattached independently of the robot's distal joints, preserving operational continuity during detachment.

abstract: In some examples, a track comprises a plurality of members coupled to one another. The plurality of members comprises a first member, a second member, and a third member. The first member is operable to couple the track to an aircraft. The second member forms a first rail. The third member forms a second rail. In addition, the third member comprises at least a portion of an outer mold line of the aircraft. Moreover, the third member is operable to support a step load. The first rail and the second rail are operable to guide movement of an aircraft component along the track.
problem: Need to guide an aircraft component along a track while simultaneously maintaining aircraft structural integrity, aerodynamic performance, and load-bearing capacity without adding redundant separate components.
constraint: The member must balance structural load-bearing requirements, aerodynamic surface smoothness, and rail guidance precision within a single integrated component, limiting design freedom in each individual function.
mechanism: A single structural element is configured to simultaneously fulfill multiple distinct functional roles—providing a guided path for component movement, forming part of an external aerodynamic surface, and bearing structural loads—by integrating these functions into one physical member, thereby eliminating the need for separate dedicated components for each function.
mechanism_raw: A single structural member is designed to serve multiple functions simultaneously: it forms a rail for guiding component movement, constitutes part of the aircraft's outer mold line (aerodynamic surface), and provides structural support for step loads. This multi-functional integration eliminates the need for separate rail, skin, and structural components by making one member fulfill all three roles.

abstract: A device for adapting a flusher for toilet tanks to a flush valve base provided with a lateral overflow pipe, includes a fastening element for fastening to the overflow pipe, the fastening element having a ring or cylinder shape with a low height and which includes a pair of cut-outs able to house lugs arranged in the overflow pipe; and a support element of a casing of a flusher of toilet tanks, including a fastening arrangement with the casing of the flusher, and may include a part for adapting the diameter of the fastening element to the diameter of the overflow pipe.
problem: Need to connect a flusher assembly to a flush valve base that has a lateral overflow pipe with existing lugs, when the flusher and valve base have incompatible geometries and potentially different pipe diameters.
constraint: The adapter must maintain a low profile (low height) while providing secure lug engagement and accommodating diameter variations, limiting the available space for engagement features and adjustment mechanisms.
mechanism: An interface element with geometric cut-outs selectively engages pre-existing mechanical features on a target component, creating a positive coupling without requiring modification of the target. A variable-dimension accommodation feature allows the same interface to bridge components with differing geometries or sizes through compliant geometric adaptation.
mechanism_raw: An adapter element with cut-outs engages pre-existing lugs on the overflow pipe, providing positive mechanical coupling without modifying the valve base. A diameter-adapting feature allows the same adapter to accommodate different overflow pipe diameters, creating a universal interface that bridges mismatched components through geometric compliance and selective engagement.

abstract: A method of drying (sublimation or desorption) a frozen product stored in a container, comprising: a) capturing a thermal IR image of the container wall using a thermal IR camera; b) processing the thermal IR image by calculating temperature values of points located on the outer surface of the container wall; c) calculating a maximum temperature of the product in the container using a mathematical model that models heat flow and that models progress of the drying process; d) controlling an amount of power supplied to the container based on the calculated maximum product temperature and on a temperature safety_margin. A freeze drying apparatus for performing said method. A container having a specific shape for use in such a process.
problem: Need to control a freeze-drying process to prevent product overheating without directly measuring internal product temperature, which is difficult or damaging to access during the process.
constraint: The mathematical model must accurately predict internal temperatures from external surface measurements while accounting for changing thermal properties and drying progress, requiring the model to be both precise and adaptive to process dynamics.
mechanism: External sensing captures surface condition data, which is processed by an adaptive mathematical model that simulates internal state evolution based on the surface measurements and known process dynamics. The model estimates an internal condition parameter, and an actuator is controlled based on this estimated parameter plus a safety margin, preventing direct internal measurement while maintaining process safety.
mechanism_raw: External thermal IR imaging captures surface temperature data on the container wall, which is then fed into a mathematical model that simulates heat flow through the container and models the progress of the drying/sublimation process. The model estimates the maximum internal product temperature from these surface measurements, and power supplied to the container is controlled based on this estimated temperature plus a safety margin.

abstract: A device for separating a metalliferous, lumpy mixture, with a conveyor belt and with a rotating drum in which a fixed magnet system with at least one magnet line is arranged. The separating effect of the device is improved and its complexity is reduced where it is provided that the magnets of the at least one magnet line are arranged such that their poles have the sequence NS SN or SN NS in the circumferential direction, as a result of which the ratio of the maximum radial magnetic flux density to the maximum tangential magnetic flux density on the belt surface, facing the material, in the region of the magnet system is greater than one and, owing to this, the electrically conductive particles are separated out into the first partial stream by radial force action (repulsion).
problem: Need to separate electrically conductive particles from a metalliferous mixture using magnetic forces, where conventional magnetic separation may not effectively distinguish conductive from non-conductive particles.
constraint: The pole arrangement must produce a radial-to-tangential magnetic flux density ratio greater than one to ensure effective radial repulsion, while the magnet configuration must be compatible with the rotating drum geometry and material transport mechanics.
mechanism: A field-generating element array is arranged to produce a directional field where one component dominates another (ratio greater than one), inducing responsive forces in target particles that cause directional displacement. Non-responsive particles remain unaffected, achieving separation based on material response to the dominant field component.
mechanism_raw: Permanent magnets are arranged in a specific circumferential pole sequence (NS SN or SN NS) around a rotating drum, creating a magnetic field where the radial flux density component dominates over the tangential component (ratio > 1). This radial field orientation induces eddy currents in conductive particles, generating repulsive forces that push them outward, separating them from non-conductive materials that are not affected by eddy current repulsion.

abstract: A display device is disclosed. The display device of the present invention comprises: a display panel; a frame positioned at the back of the display panel; a main optical assembly positioned on the frame between the display panel and the frame; and a side optical assembly positioned on the frame between the display panel and the frame, and positioned adjacent to the main optical assembly, wherein the frame comprises: a bottom forming a lower surface; and a side support extending from the bottom toward one side of the display panel, wherein: the side support is closer to the display panel than the bottom; the main optical assembly is positioned on the bottom; and the side optical assembly can be positioned on the side support.
problem: Need to position multiple optical assemblies at different distances from a display panel within a compact display device, where different optical components require different depths for proper optical function.
constraint: The frame must provide sufficient structural support for both optical assemblies while maintaining the precise height difference between the bottom and side support, and the side support must not interfere with the main optical assembly's function.
mechanism: A mounting structure incorporates multiple support surfaces at different distances from a reference plane, creating a tiered configuration. Different components are mounted on different support surfaces, allowing each to be positioned at a distinct depth relative to the reference plane using a single integrated structure.
mechanism_raw: A frame is designed with a bottom surface and a side support that extends from the bottom toward the display panel at a greater distance than the bottom itself, creating a tiered mounting structure. The main optical assembly is mounted on the bottom surface (farther from the display panel), while the side optical assembly is mounted on the side support (closer to the display panel), allowing different components to be positioned at precisely different depths using a single integrated frame.

abstract: A guest management system configured to facilitate the provision of services to guest. A guest's personal computing device, and provided computing devices, are used to request and receive products and services. The services provided may be tacked and scored based on either feedback from guests and/or objective measurements of the performance of service providers. Services are optionally dependent on an automatically determined location of a guest and may include access to third party accounts of the guests.
problem: Efficiently providing personalized services to guests in dynamic environments while balancing automated location-based triggers and subjective/objective performance metrics.
constraint: Balancing automation (location-based service selection) with user feedback and performance data to avoid conflicting or irrelevant service adjustments.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting service delivery by determining a user's position to modify service dependencies, while integrating real-time feedback and performance metrics to score and adapt service delivery, balancing automated triggers with subjective/objective data to avoid conflicting adjustments.
mechanism_raw: Automatically determining a guest's location to dynamically adjust service dependencies, while integrating real-time feedback and objective performance measurements to score and adapt service delivery.

abstract: A display substrate of an electronic device and a method for manufacturing the display substrate are provided. The display substrate includes: a base; a thin film transistor formed on a side of the base; an organic light emitting layer, formed on a side of the thin film transistor facing away from the base; and a touch electrode layer, formed in the organic light emitting layer.
problem: Integrating touch-sensing functionality into a display without increasing thickness or degrading display performance.
constraint: Maintaining material compatibility and structural integrity between the touch electrode and the organic light-emitting layer to avoid performance degradation.
mechanism: Integrating a sensing layer directly within an emissive display layer to enable touch detection without adding separate structural layers, maintaining material compatibility and structural integrity between the sensing and emissive components.
mechanism_raw: Embedding a touch electrode layer directly within the organic light-emitting layer, enabling touch detection without adding separate structural layers.

abstract: A burner arrangement (1), for a mobile heater operated with liquid fuel, is provided; having a combustion chamber (2) for converting fuel with combustion air in a flaming combustion, which combustion chamber (2) extends along a longitudinal axis (Z) in a main flow direction (H); a pre-mixing chamber (3), which is arranged fluidicly upstream of the combustion chamber (2), for generating a fuel-combustion air-mixture, which pre-mixing chamber (3) comprises a side wall (4); a fuel evaporation surface (O) arranged in the pre-mixing chamber; a fuel supply (10) for supplying liquid fuel; and a first combustion air supply (6) having a swirl body (7) for supplying a combustion air flow into the pre-mixing chamber (3) with a swirl such that the combustion air is guided along the fuel evaporation surface (O) with a tangential flow component. A neck portion (5) is formed at a transition from the pre-mixing chamber (3) to the combustion chamber (2) at which the flow cross-section abruptly widens in the main flow direction (H).
problem: Achieving efficient and stable combustion of liquid fuel in a mobile heater while managing airflow and fuel evaporation.
constraint: Balancing turbulent mixing (via swirl) and flow expansion (via the neck) to maintain stable combustion without excessive pressure loss or flame instability.
mechanism: Inducing a tangential airflow component along a fuel evaporation surface using a swirl-inducing element, combined with a flow expansion section that abruptly widens the cross-section to stabilize combustion dynamics while managing pressure loss.
mechanism_raw: Using a swirl body to induce a tangential airflow component along a fuel evaporation surface, combined with a neck portion that abruptly widens the flow cross-section to stabilize combustion dynamics.

abstract: A vapor compression system includes a compressor, a first heat exchanger, an expansion valve and a second heat exchanger arranged serial refrigerant flow path; a first fan configured to direct air over the first heat exchanger; a controller coupled to the first fan and the compressor, the controller configured to: set a compressor discharge superheat limit; determine a compressor discharge superheat; compare the compressor discharge superheat to the compressor discharge superheat limit; and when the compressor discharge superheat is less than the compressor discharge superheat limit, the controller reducing at least one of a compressor speed and a first fan speed.
problem: Preventing compressor damage in a vapor compression system caused by excessive discharge superheat while maintaining operational efficiency.
constraint: Maintaining system cooling capacity and energy efficiency while avoiding compressor damage through dynamic speed adjustments based on thermal feedback.
mechanism: Monitoring thermal output in real-time and dynamically reducing operational speed (e.g., compressor or fan) when a predefined thermal threshold is breached to prevent component damage while maintaining system efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring compressor discharge superheat in real-time and reducing compressor speed or fan speed when superheat falls below a predefined limit to prevent overheating.

abstract: Smart processing devices and systems for controlling functionality of smart processing devices are provided. In some examples, a smart processing device may include a central segment and a plurality of removable segments. The removable segments may be connected to the central segment in a plurality of different configurations. In some examples, each configuration may enable or disable functionality associated with the smart processing device. Further, a system may receive data associated with a current physical configuration of a smart processing device. The current physical configuration data may be compared to pre-stored configuration data in order to identify one or more functions to be enabled or disabled for the smart processing device. The system, computing platform, or the like, may generate an instruction, command or signal enabling or disabling functionality and may transmit the signal to the smart processing device for execution and control of functions provided by the smart processing device.
problem: Dynamically enabling or disabling device functionality based on physical hardware configuration without manual reconfiguration.
constraint: Ensuring accurate detection of physical configurations and correct mapping to functional profiles to avoid unintended behavior or system errors.
mechanism: Detecting the physical arrangement of removable components relative to a central component and mapping the detected configuration to pre-stored functional profiles to enable/disable corresponding features without manual reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: Detecting the physical arrangement of removable segments relative to a central segment and mapping the detected configuration to pre-stored functional profiles to enable/disable corresponding features.

abstract: A woven geosynthetic fabric having a weft direction and a warp direction, includes weft yarns woven in the weft direction and warp yarns woven in the warp direction interweaving the weft yarns to form a fabric having comparable modulus; the warp yarns including a high modulus monofilament yarn having a tenacity of at least 0.75 g/denier at 1% strain, at least 1.5 g/denier at 2% strain, and at least 3.75 g/denier at 5% strain as determined in accordance with ASTM International Standard 4595.
problem: Achieving a woven geosynthetic fabric with balanced modulus in both weft and warp directions despite differing yarn properties.
constraint: The high-modulus yarn must meet precise tenacity requirements (e.g., 0.75 g/denier at 1% strain, 3.75 g/denier at 5% strain) to ensure structural balance without compromising flexibility or durability.
mechanism: Interweaving two sets of elongated tensile elements with differing mechanical properties, where one set incorporates elements with defined strength thresholds at multiple strain levels, to produce a composite structure with balanced directional stiffness and flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Interweaving weft and warp yarns, where the warp yarns include high-modulus monofilaments with specific tenacity thresholds at varying strain levels, to create a fabric with comparable modulus across directions.

abstract: Additives containing a filler, and an emissivity agent are combined for thermal enhancement, which may further include a reflectivity agent, a stabilizer, or combinations thereof. The additive is used in the production of cloth or the modification of cloth including clothing, home goods, and temporary shelters, and may be used in screen printing and three dimensional applications. More than one type of filler, emissivity agent, reflective agent, and stabilizer may be used.
problem: Enhancing thermal properties (e.g., emissivity, reflectivity) of cloth for applications like clothing, shelters, or home goods.
constraint: The additive must balance multiple agents (filler, emissivity, reflectivity) to avoid trade-offs between thermal enhancement and other properties like flexibility or printability.
mechanism: Formulating a composite additive containing multiple functional agents (e.g., filler, emissivity modifier, reflectivity modifier) to synergistically alter thermal behavior of a fibrous substrate during processing or finishing, while maintaining compatibility with mechanical and surface properties.
mechanism_raw: Combining a filler, emissivity agent, and optionally a reflectivity agent or stabilizer in a single additive formulation to synergistically modify thermal behavior of the cloth during production or post-production processes.

abstract: A variety of methods and arrangements for reducing noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) in a skip fire engine control system are described. In one aspect, a firing sequence is used to operate the engine in a skip fire manner. A smoothing torque is determined that is applied to a powertrain by an energy storage/release device. The smoothing torque is arranged to at least partially cancel out variation in torque generated by the skip fire firing sequence. Various methods, powertrain controllers, arrangements and computer software related to the above operations are also described.
problem: Reducing noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) caused by irregular torque output in a skip fire engine control system.
constraint: The energy storage/release device must respond rapidly enough to match the frequency and magnitude of torque fluctuations while maintaining overall powertrain efficiency.
mechanism: Introducing a dynamic counter-torque from an energy storage and release system that actively opposes cyclical variations in rotational force output, thereby attenuating periodic disturbances in a mechanical power transmission system.
mechanism_raw: Applying a smoothing torque from an energy storage/release device that actively counteracts torque variations generated by the skip fire firing sequence, thereby canceling out cyclical powertrain disturbances.
residual_terms: ["energy storage and release system", "counter-torque", "rotational force", "power transmission system"]

abstract: A method for use in a dispersed storage network (DSN) includes receiving a data access request at a DSN memory that controls storage of encoded data slices in multiple storage units. The data access request is capable of being serviced using either of at least two different storage units. The DSN memory determines wear levels associated with the two different storage units, and selects one of them as a preferred storage unit based, at least in part, on the wear levels. The DSN memory fulfills the data access request using the preferred storage unit.
problem: Managing wear and extending lifespan of storage units in a dispersed storage network (DSN) while maintaining data accessibility.
constraint: The selection process must balance wear leveling with performance requirements, ensuring data retrieval latency and reliability are not compromised by prioritizing less-worn units.
mechanism: Continuously monitoring operational wear metrics across a distributed array of storage devices and dynamically prioritizing access to less-worn devices to distribute usage and prevent localized degradation of system reliability.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring wear levels of multiple storage units and dynamically selecting a preferred unit for data access based on wear metrics, thereby distributing usage to prevent premature failure of individual units.

abstract: A system and method for inspecting a rail is provided. The system includes an ultrasonic transducer positioned to emit an ultrasonic beam onto the rail and receive a refraction beam, the ultrasonic transducer being movable between a first position and a second position. A sensor is operable to measure an angle of a carriage, the carriage being positioned on the rail. A controller is operably coupled to the sensor, the controller having a processor that is responsive to executable computer instructions when executed on the processor to cause the ultrasonic transducer to move to receive refraction beam in response to the measured angle indicating a rail radius of less than a predetermined first threshold.
problem: Accurately inspecting rails for defects, particularly at varying radii or curvatures, using ultrasonic testing.
constraint: The system must synchronize real-time angle measurements with precise transducer movement to maintain inspection accuracy across dynamic rail geometries without interrupting the inspection process.
mechanism: Coupling real-time geometric sensing of a curved surface with automated repositioning of an ultrasonic probe to maintain optimal beam alignment for signal reception when surface curvature exceeds a predefined threshold.
mechanism_raw: Using a sensor to measure the rail's angle and automatically repositioning an ultrasonic transducer to optimize beam alignment for receiving refraction signals when the rail radius falls below a threshold.

abstract: The present invention relates to a piston cylinder system for a working device, wherein the piston cylinder system comprises at least one tubular element and at least one piston which is guided in the at least one tubular element. The piston cylinder system is characterized in that at least one tubular element consists of high-manganese-steel and the inner side of the at least one tubular element is machined.
problem: Wear and degradation in piston-cylinder systems under high-stress operational conditions.
constraint: Balancing material cost and work-hardening properties against the need for precise machining to ensure long-term performance without excessive maintenance.
mechanism: A material that dynamically increases surface hardness under frictional stress, combined with precision surface finishing to maintain dimensional accuracy and minimize abrasive degradation over repeated mechanical interaction.
mechanism_raw: Using high-manganese steel, which work-hardens under friction to increase surface durability, combined with precision machining of the inner surface to maintain tight tolerances and reduce abrasive wear.

abstract: Methods and systems for designing a volumetric model of a construct at a user interface through use of a 3-D design, fabrication and assembly system comprising a modeling component, a robotic assembly workstation component, and a workflow configuration module to generate, through the workflow configuration module, a 3-D print bill of materials for a rendered volumetric model; generate a workflow configuration model based on the 3-D print bill of materials, the model including an automated robot control scheme of a series of assembly order instructions to direct a multi-axis robot of the robotic assembly workstation component to print and/or assemble a construct; transmit the workflow configuration model to the robotic assembly workstation component with a print and/or assembly command in accordance with the automated robot control scheme; and print and/or assemble the construct with the multi-axis robot in accordance with the print and/or assembly command.
problem: Inefficient translation of 3D design models into automated robotic assembly workflows, leading to manual intervention and errors.
constraint: Ensuring seamless integration between design software, material planning, and robotic control systems to avoid mismatches in assembly order or material usage.
mechanism: An automated translation layer that converts a three-dimensional digital model into a material allocation plan and a sequence of robotic actuation instructions, which are then executed by a multi-axis robotic system without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: A workflow configuration module that automatically generates a 3D print bill of materials and a robot control scheme from a rendered model, then transmits this to a multi-axis robotic workstation to execute print/assembly commands without human oversight.

abstract: A semiconductor light emitting device includes a light-emitting structure including a first conductivity-type semiconductor layer, an active layer, and a second conductivity-type semiconductor layer, a first transparent electrode layer on the second conductivity-type semiconductor layer, a first insulating layer on the first transparent electrode layer, the first insulating layer including a plurality of through-holes, a reflective electrode layer on the first insulating layer and connected to the first transparent electrode layer through the plurality of through-holes, and a transparent protection layer covering upper and side surfaces of the reflective electrode layer, the transparent protection layer being on a portion of the first insulating layer.
problem: Trade-off between electrical conductivity and optical transparency in semiconductor light-emitting devices.
constraint: Optimizing hole density and layer thickness to maximize both electrical connectivity and light output efficiency.
mechanism: A multi-layer structure with conductive pathways through an insulating layer to enable electrical connectivity between electrodes while permitting unobstructed light emission, with a protective barrier layer to isolate sensitive components from environmental exposure.
mechanism_raw: A layered structure with through-holes in an insulating layer that connect a transparent electrode to a reflective electrode, enabling electrical contact without blocking light emission, while a transparent protection layer shields the reflective electrode from environmental damage.

abstract: A steam generator for generating a superheated fluid from a working fluid using a stream of heated gas, the steam generator comprising: a housing, which defines a gas flow path having an inlet at one, upstream end thereof into which a stream of heated gas is delivered and an outlet at the other, downstream end thereof; and a steam generation module which is disposed within the gas flow path of the housing, the steam generation module comprising a heat exchanger which receives a working fluid and is operative to raise the temperature of the working fluid to provide a saturated fluid, and a superheater which receives the saturated fluid from the heat exchanger and is operative to raise the temperature of the saturated fluid and provide a supersaturated fluid.
problem: Inefficient heat transfer in steam generators, leading to suboptimal superheated fluid production.
constraint: Managing heat distribution between stages to avoid overheating the working fluid or underutilizing the heated gas stream.
mechanism: A staged thermal energy transfer system where a first stage brings a working fluid to its phase-change threshold, and a subsequent stage further elevates its temperature using residual heat from the same energy source, optimizing cumulative thermal absorption.
mechanism_raw: Sequential heat exchange stages: a heat exchanger first raises the working fluid to saturation, then a superheater further increases its temperature, leveraging staged thermal energy absorption to achieve superheated output efficiently.

abstract: An ammunition tray is provided for containing a plurality of bullet cartridges within an ammunition box container having a stowage volume. The tray includes a substantially rectangular template having a horizontal surface bounded by first and second opposing longitudinal edges and opposing lateral edges joined at four corners. Each longitudinal edge includes a first tab bent substantially perpendicular to the surface in a vertical direction to form a rib. Each lateral edge includes a second tab bent substantially perpendicular to the surface to form a wall. The surface includes a first row of interior pockets that point towards the first longitudinal edge as a proximal orientation. The surface further includes a second row of interior pockets that point towards the second longitudinal edge as a distal orientation. The template has longitudinal and lateral edges bent to form the respective ribs and walls fits within the stowage volume as a vertical stack of plural templates. Each first interior pocket in the first row can cradle a cartridge on the surface along the proximal orientation, can fit the cartridge from an adjacent second row, and has lateral edges bent to curl in said vertical direction. Each second interior pocket in the second row can cradle the cartridge on the surface along the distal orientation, can fit the cartridge from an adjacent first row, and has lateral edges bent to curl opposite said vertical direction.
problem: Inefficient use of stowage volume in ammunition storage systems, limiting cartridge capacity and accessibility.
constraint: Balancing the structural rigidity of bent edges against the need for flexible pocket orientations to maximize storage density.
mechanism: A modular storage unit with alternating internal cavity orientations and integrated structural ribs formed by bent edges, allowing vertical stacking of units that interlock to maximize volumetric density while preserving mechanical stability.
mechanism_raw: A template with alternating interior pocket orientations and bent edges forming ribs and walls, enabling a vertical stack of templates that cradle cartridges in opposing directions while maintaining structural integrity and compact nesting.

abstract: A chemical sensor and a system and method for sensing a chemical species. The chemical sensor includes a plurality of nanofibers whose electrical impedance varies upon exposure to the chemical species, a substrate supporting and electrically isolating the fibers, a set of electrodes connected to the plurality of fibers at spatially separated points to permit the electrical impedance of the plurality of fibers to be measured, and a membrane encasing the fibers and having a thickness ranging from 50 μm to 5.0 mm. The system includes the chemical sensor, an impedance measuring device coupled to the electrodes and configured to determine an electrical impedance of the plurality of fibers, and an analyzer configured to identify the chemical species based on a change in the electrical impedance. The method measures at least one change in an electrical impedance between spatially separated electrodes connected to a plurality of fibers upon exposure of the fibers to the chemical species, and identifies the chemical species based on the measured change in the electrical impedance.
problem: Detecting and identifying a chemical species based on its interaction with a sensor.
constraint: The membrane encasing the fibers must balance sensitivity (allowing chemical interaction) with structural integrity (thickness between 50 μm and 5.0 mm).
mechanism: A material whose electrical impedance changes upon exposure to a target substance is positioned between spatially separated measurement points. The impedance variation is monitored and correlated to a characteristic signature to identify the target substance.
mechanism_raw: Nanofibers with variable electrical impedance upon exposure to a chemical species are measured between spatially separated electrodes. The impedance change is analyzed to identify the chemical species.

abstract: The drive assembly includes annular drive magnets extending around a top end of a drive shaft and annular drive coils extending around the drive magnets, separated by a pressure boundary. A latch assembly is coupled to the drive magnets and engages with the drive shaft in response to actuation of the drive assembly. The drive coils also rotate the drive magnets and the engaged latch assembly to axially displace the drive shaft. Deactivating the drive coils disengages the latch assembly from the drive shaft, dropping a connected control rod assembly via gravity into a nuclear fuel assembly.
problem: Remotely actuating and releasing a control rod in a high-pressure or hazardous environment (e.g., nuclear reactor).
constraint: The pressure boundary between the drive coils and magnets must maintain isolation while enabling magnetic coupling and rotational motion.
mechanism: A magnetic coupling transmits rotational motion through a pressure boundary to engage a mechanical latch, axially displacing a component. Disengaging the coupling removes the mechanical constraint, allowing a restoring force to act on the component.
mechanism_raw: Annular drive magnets and coils rotate to engage a latch assembly with a drive shaft, axially displacing it. Deactivating the coils disengages the latch, allowing gravity to drop the control rod.

abstract: A shirt collar attachment includes a first support, a second support, at least one design body, a first collar attachment, and a second collar attachment. The first support and the second support are terminally connected to each other at an angle, wherein the angle can be an acute, right, or obtuse angle. The at least one design body is adjacently connected to the first support and the second support thus providing the design element for the shirt collar attachment. The first collar attachment is terminally connected to the first support, opposite of the second support. The second collar attachment is terminally connected to the second support, opposite of the first support. Collectively, the first collar attachment and second collar attachment are able to secure the shirt collar attachment to the corners of the shirt collar, providing an alternative to necktie and variants neckwear.
reason: The design is a specific product configuration for attaching to shirt collars, relying on fixed geometric arrangements (angled supports and terminal attachments) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism.

abstract: A driver cabin for an urban railway vehicle, the driver cabin extending in a longitudinal driving direction and including: a cabin chassis including at least one main shock-absorbing area having a longitudinal extend defined between a front plane oriented transversally to the longitudinal driving direction and a rear plane oriented transversally to the longitudinal driving direction, the main shock-absorbing area being able to deform in case of a shock between an initial state and a shock-absorbed state, so that in the shock-absorbed state the longitudinal extend of the main shock-absorbing area is reduced about a predefined compression distance; an electrical equipment compartment storing at least one stiff electrical element carrying electronic components. The electrical equipment compartment is located inside the main shock-absorbing area.
problem: Protecting sensitive electrical equipment in a vehicle during impact or shock events.
constraint: The compression distance and placement of stiff elements must balance energy absorption with equipment protection.
mechanism: A deformable structure undergoes controlled longitudinal compression during a shock event, absorbing kinetic energy through plastic or elastic deformation. Stiff components positioned within the deformation zone are shielded from direct shock loading by the energy-absorbing material.
mechanism_raw: A deformable shock-absorbing structure reduces its longitudinal extent during a shock, absorbing energy while shielding stiff electrical components located within the deformation zone.

abstract: An information processing apparatus includes a memory and a processor coupled to the memory and configured to extract data having x times y bits from genome data in which a mutation pattern at each gene mutation position is represented as x bits, such that the extracted data is constituted by y data pieces each having x bits at y respective mutation positions, x and y being integers greater than or equal to 1, respectively, to refer to an addend table that stores a plurality of addend data associated with respective x-times-y-bit data to identify addend data corresponding to the extracted data, and to use an SIMD instruction to add the identified addend data to count data at positions corresponding to the y mutation positions in the genome data, the count data indicating counts of occurrences of mutation patterns in the genome data.
problem: Efficiently counting mutation patterns in large genomic datasets.
constraint: The use of SIMD requires data to be structured in fixed-size chunks (x*y bits) to enable parallel processing without branching overhead.
mechanism: Data is partitioned into fixed-size chunks, each mapped to precomputed values via a lookup table. Parallel processing units simultaneously update aggregate counts for all chunks, eliminating branching overhead through vectorized operations.
mechanism_raw: Data is extracted in x*y-bit chunks, mapped to precomputed addend values via a lookup table, and aggregated using SIMD instructions to parallelize count updates across mutation positions.

abstract: An exercise apparatus allowing freedom of movement of an exercise bar is provided. The exercise apparatus comprises one or more base assemblies; a pair of spaced vertical members mounted to the one or more base assemblies; and a first bar member mounted to the spaced vertical members, wherein the first bar member is at least partially rotatable relative to the longitudinal axes of the vertical members. The one or more base assemblies may facilitate multidirectional horizontal movement of the vertical members, whereby the first bar member is rotatable relative to the longitudinal axes of the vertical members.
problem: Traditional exercise bars are fixed in orientation, limiting natural multidirectional movement during exercise.
constraint: Balancing structural stability of the base assemblies with the need for unrestricted multidirectional movement of the bar.
mechanism: A movable element is coupled to a support structure through a combination of translational and rotational degrees of freedom, enabling multidirectional motion by allowing the element to shift position along multiple axes while maintaining mechanical linkage to the support.
mechanism_raw: A bar is mounted to vertically movable members that can translate horizontally, while the bar itself is rotatably coupled to the vertical members. This allows the bar to rotate relative to the vertical axes as the base assemblies move, enabling simultaneous horizontal translation and rotational freedom.

abstract: An acid steam cleaning apparatus for cleaning vessels using acid steam, comprising: a raw acid liquid container (1), a heater (2), a cleaning cavity (3), a double-walled tube, and a controller. The double-walled tube is installed in the cleaning cavity and has an inner tube (200) and an outer tube (300), wherein the inner tube (200) and the outer tube (300) closely contact each other; acid steam exit holes (230, 330) are provided around and/or at the upper portions of the inner tube (200) and the outer tube (300), the acid steam exit holes (230, 330) extending through the outer tube and the inner tube; the acid steam exit holes (230, 330) are in communication with the interior (220) of the inner tube (200); the interior (220) of the inner tube (200) is connected with an acid steam entry channel for forming an acid steam path; grooves (210) extending axially are provided on the outer surface of the inner tube (200); water/air entry holes (310) for water/air to enter are provided at the bottom of the outer tube (300), and water/air exit holes (320) for discharging water/air are distributed on the outer tube (300); the grooves (210) on the inner tube (200) are in communication with the water/air entry holes (310) and are in communication with the water/air exit holes (320) on the outer tube (300); the water/air entry holes (310) are connected with a water/air entry pipe for forming a water/air path. When vessels are being cleaned using acid steam, the vessels are fitted over the double-walled tube, and clean acid liquid and pure water pass through the acid steam path and the water/air path, so as to be separated from waste acid liquid, waste water, and waste air, such that the cleaning effect is improved, and the trouble of mounting and detaching components after cleaning is avoided.
problem: Cleaning vessels with acid steam requires efficient separation of clean and waste fluids to avoid contamination and reduce post-cleaning maintenance.
constraint: Maintaining tight integration between the inner and outer tubes to ensure fluid separation without compromising flow efficiency.
mechanism: A dual-channel conduit system separates two fluid streams by maintaining distinct flow paths through nested tubular structures, with controlled discharge points that preserve stream isolation while enabling regulated outflow.
mechanism_raw: A double-walled tube with inner and outer tubes creates two distinct flow paths: an acid steam path through the inner tube and a water/air path through grooves on the inner tube connected to the outer tube. Exit holes in both tubes allow controlled discharge while maintaining separation of streams.

abstract: Disclosed is a three-branched six-degree-of-freedom parallel mechanism with curved sliding pairs, which includes a base, a moving platform, and three identical kinetic branches. The kinetic branches are radially and evenly distributed and arranged between the base and the moving platform. Each kinetic branch includes a first curved link assembly, a first motor, and a support link. One end of the support link is hinged to the moving platform. One end of the first curved link assembly is hinged to the support link. The first motor is disposed on the base and is configured for driving the first curved link assembly to rotate, where an arc length of the first curved link assembly is changed as the first curved link assembly is driven to rotate.
problem: Achieving complex multi-axis motion in mechanical systems while maintaining compactness and precision.
constraint: Ensuring synchronized motion across all three branches to maintain platform stability while achieving full spatial mobility.
mechanism: A platform is connected to a base via multiple geometrically coupled actuation branches, where coordinated motion of the branches through arc-length variation enables synchronized multi-axis displacement of the platform.
mechanism_raw: Three identical curved sliding pair branches radially arranged between a base and moving platform. Each branch uses a curved link assembly driven by a motor, where rotation changes the arc length of the link, enabling coordinated six-degree-of-freedom motion through geometric coupling.

abstract: Coating method for arc coating or arc ion plating coating of substrates in a vacuum chamber in which using an arc evaporator solid material that functions as cathode is evaporated, during arc evaporation the motion of the cathode spot on the solid material surface is accelerated using a magnetic field for avoiding ejection of a large amount of macro-particles or droplets from the solid material surface, negative charged particles resulted from the arc evaporation flow from the cathode to an anode, characterized by the motion of the negative charged particles from the cathode to the anode fundamentally doesn't cause an additional increase of the absolute value of the potential difference between cathode and anode allowing a lower increment of the substrate temperature during coating.
problem: Arc evaporation coating processes generate macro-particles that degrade coating quality and increase substrate temperature.
constraint: Balancing magnetic field strength to control spot motion without disrupting the overall arc discharge stability.
mechanism: A directed energy beam interacts with a material surface under the influence of a controlled magnetic field, which modulates particle trajectory to distribute energy input and suppress undesirable particle ejection.
mechanism_raw: A magnetic field accelerates the motion of the cathode spot across the solid material surface during arc evaporation, preventing localized overheating and reducing macro-particle ejection. The magnetic control ensures charged particles flow from cathode to anode without increasing the potential difference.

abstract: An overflow drain assembly includes a housing configured to be installed at a bottom of a basin. A plug assembly is configured to be disposed within the housing and has an upper and lower plug body translatable to each other. A fluidic seal is attached to the upper plug body and configured to removably engage in a water tight manner with a top side water inlet of the housing. A single compression spring is disposed between and biases apart the upper and lower plug body. A first permanent magnet attached to the lower plug body is above a second permanent magnet attached to the upper plug body. The upper plug body is configured to be manually pushed downward a first time by a user to automatically lock into an open position and manually pushed downward a second time to automatically raise and lock into a closed position.
problem: Creating a drain assembly that can be manually toggled between open and closed states with automatic locking, without requiring tools or complex mechanisms.
constraint: Ensuring reliable magnetic latching without unintended disengagement under fluid pressure or vibration.
mechanism: A dual-state mechanical system uses opposing forces from a resilient element and magnetic interaction between two components to create stable positions, where manual input shifts magnetic alignment to toggle between states with automatic latching.
mechanism_raw: A dual-plug body system with a compression spring biasing the upper and lower plugs apart. A first permanent magnet on the lower plug interacts with a second magnet on the upper plug, creating a toggle effect: manual depression of the upper plug shifts magnetic alignment to lock into open or closed positions.

abstract: In some embodiments, a crossbow comprises a stock, a fire control assembly and a bow portion. In some embodiments, the bow portion comprises a prod, a first limb, a second limb, a first rotatable member and a second rotatable member. The crossbow comprises a drawn orientation wherein the first rotatable member overlaps with the stock. In some embodiments, a reference line oriented orthogonal to a shooting axis intersects the stock and the first rotatable member. In some embodiments, the reference line is parallel to a rotation axis of the first rotatable member.
problem: Ensuring a crossbow can be drawn and held in a ready position without mechanical interference between the bow portion and the stock.
constraint: Balancing the need for compact mechanical overlap with the requirement to maintain structural support and precise alignment during energy storage and release.
mechanism: A movable component with rotational degrees of freedom is configured to overlap with a structural base in a loaded state, while a reference axis orthogonal to the primary operational direction is aligned parallel to the rotation axis of the movable component. This alignment ensures that rotational motion of the movable component does not compromise the structural integrity or operational alignment of the base during energy storage and release.
mechanism_raw: The bow portion's rotatable members are designed to overlap with the stock in the drawn orientation, and a reference line orthogonal to the shooting axis is aligned parallel to the rotation axis of the first rotatable member. This alignment ensures that rotational movement of the bow components does not disrupt the stock's structural integrity or the crossbow's operational alignment.
residual_terms: ["rotational degrees of freedom", "reference axis", "loaded state", "energy storage and release"]

abstract: Methods, systems, and devices for protecting stored data in a memory device are described. In one example, a memory device may include a set of memory cells coupled with a digit line and a plate line. A method of operating the memory device may include performing an access operation on a selected memory cell of the set of memory cells, and performing an equalization operation on a non-selected memory cell of the plurality of memory cells based on performing the access operation. The equalization operation may include applying an equal voltage to opposite terminals of the non-selected memory cell via the digit line and the plate line, which may allow built-up charge, such as leakage charge resulting from the access operation, to dissipate. Such an equalization operation may reduce a likelihood of memory loss in non-selected memory cells after access operations.
problem: Preventing data loss in non-selected memory cells caused by charge leakage during access operations on selected cells.
constraint: Balancing the timing and voltage levels of the equalization operation to avoid disrupting the access operation while effectively neutralizing leakage effects.
mechanism: Following an access operation on a target node, an equalization process applies a common potential to opposing terminals of non-target nodes via shared conductive pathways. This neutralizes accumulated leakage charge, preventing unintended interference from the access operation on non-target nodes.
mechanism_raw: After performing an access operation on a selected memory cell, an equalization operation applies an equal voltage to opposite terminals of non-selected cells via shared digit and plate lines. This dissipates built-up leakage charge, mitigating unintended interference from the access operation.
residual_terms: ["access operation", "equalization process", "common potential", "shared conductive pathways", "leakage charge"]

abstract: The present invention provides a mascara container including: a pouch-shaped inner container of a film material; and an outer container of an elastic material that covers the outside of the inner container. According to the present invention, highly-viscous mascara content can easily be transferred to an application member when a user lightly squeezes a container, so that the residual mascara content inside the container can easily be discharged to increase the usable amount of content after the mascara is opened, regardless of the duration of use. Accordingly, the effect can be realized of improving eyelash volume by applying a sufficient amount of mascara content.
problem: Efficiently dispensing high-viscosity mascara content while minimizing residual waste inside the container.
constraint: Maintaining the structural integrity of the inner pouch while ensuring the elastic outer layer provides sufficient compression for consistent dispensing.
mechanism: An elastic external casing applies uniform compressive force to a flexible internal reservoir when externally actuated. The elastic deformation of the external casing transfers pressure evenly to the internal reservoir, expelling viscous content toward a dispensing interface without requiring excessive input force.
mechanism_raw: An elastic outer container compresses a pouch-shaped inner container made of flexible film when squeezed. The elastic material's deformation transfers pressure uniformly to the inner pouch, forcing viscous content toward the applicator without requiring excessive force.
residual_terms: ["elastic external casing", "flexible internal reservoir", "compressive force", "viscous content"]

abstract: A fiber-reinforced plastic component includes a three-dimensional component plastic member and at least one reinforcement fiber rod. The three-dimensional component plastic member determines at least parts of a shape of the plastic component. The three-dimensional component plastic member has at least one void which is open to at least one side and in which the at least one reinforcement fiber rod is placed.
problem: Creating a fiber-reinforced plastic component with targeted structural strength while preserving a complex three-dimensional shape.
constraint: Balancing the placement and density of reinforcement fibers to maximize strength without compromising the component's geometric complexity or manufacturing feasibility.
mechanism: A three-dimensional structural framework with predefined cavities is formed first, and reinforcement elements are inserted into these cavities. The framework determines the component's geometric form, while the reinforcement elements provide localized strengthening in regions subjected to critical stress.
mechanism_raw: A three-dimensional plastic member with predefined voids is formed first, and reinforcement fiber rods are inserted into these voids. The plastic member determines the component's shape, while the fibers provide localized reinforcement in critical stress regions.
residual_terms: ["three-dimensional structural framework", "predefined cavities", "reinforcement elements", "critical stress regions"]

abstract: An electrophotographic photosensitive member (1) includes a conductive substrate (2) and a photosensitive layer (3) disposed directly or indirectly on the conductive substrate (2). The photosensitive layer (3) has a charge generating layer (3a) and a charge transport layer (3b) disposed in order from the conductive substrate (2). The charge generating layer (3a) contains a charge generating material. The charge transport layer (3b) contains a charge transport material, a binder resin, and a pigment that absorbs light having an irradiation wavelength. The binder resin includes a polyarylate resin including a repeating unit represented by general formula (1):
problem: Optimizing light absorption in the charge transport layer of an electrophotographic photosensitive member to improve performance.
constraint: Selecting a pigment and binder resin combination that maximizes light absorption without degrading the electrical properties of the charge transport layer.
mechanism: A light-absorbing agent that selectively absorbs radiation at a target wavelength is incorporated into a charge transport medium. This agent reduces unwanted optical interference, thereby enhancing the efficiency of charge generation and transport processes within the medium.
mechanism_raw: A pigment that absorbs light at the irradiation wavelength is incorporated into the charge transport layer. This pigment reduces unwanted light interference, enhancing the efficiency of charge generation and transport processes in the photosensitive layer.
residual_terms: ["light-absorbing agent", "target wavelength", "charge transport medium", "charge generation and transport processes"]

abstract: A semiconductor device includes a first plurality of stacked nanowire structures extending in a first direction disposed over a first region of a semiconductor substrate. Each nanowire structure of the first plurality of stacked nanowire structures includes a plurality of nanowires arranged in a second direction substantially perpendicular to the first direction. A nanowire stack insulating layer is between the substrate and a nanowire closest to the substrate of each nanowire structure of the first plurality of stacked nanowire structures. At least one second stacked nanowire structure is disposed over a second region of the semiconductor substrate, and a shallow trench isolation layer is between the first region and the second region of the semiconductor substrate.
