constraint: Ensuring the interlocking components maintain tight tolerances and structural stability under thermal or mechanical stress during semiconductor processing, without compromising the alignment or introducing contamination.
mechanism: A mechanically interlocked multi-component assembly using complementary geometric features to maintain precise relative positioning and distribute loads across the structure during processing, while permitting localized access or adjustment.
mechanism_raw: An interlocking modular design where an upper ring plate with concentric walls and a bridge is mechanically coupled to a lower ring with a complementary wall, allowing precise alignment and load distribution while enabling localized adjustments or maintenance.

abstract: A cold crucible structure according to an embodiment of the present invention includes a cold crucible structure according to an embodiment of the present invention includes: a cold crucible unit including hollow top and bottom caps, a plurality of segments connecting the top cap and the bottom cap, slits disposed between the segments, and a reaction area surrounded by the segments; and an induction coil unit disposed to cover the outer side of the cold crucible unit and disposed across the longitudinal directions of the segments and the slits, in which the diameter of the reaction area is defined as a crucible diameter, the crucible diameter is 100 to 300 mm, and a width of each of the slits is defined by (mm)(where dslit is the width of each of the slits and Ø is the crucible diameter).
problem: Managing thermal expansion and material flow in a high-temperature reaction area of a cold crucible while maintaining structural integrity and process efficiency.
constraint: Balancing the slit width-to-diameter ratio to prevent excessive heat loss or structural weakness while ensuring sufficient flexibility for thermal expansion and material flow during processing.
mechanism: A segmented containment structure with gaps between segments whose dimensions scale proportionally with the overall structure size, allowing controlled dimensional change and material movement during thermal cycling while maintaining structural continuity through external energy application.
mechanism_raw: A segmented crucible design with slits between segments, where the slit width is proportionally scaled relative to the crucible diameter, allowing controlled thermal expansion and material movement while the induction coil spans across the segments to provide uniform heating.
residual_terms: ["segmented containment structure", "gaps between segments", "dimensional change", "thermal cycling", "external energy application"]

abstract: The invention relates to a method of improved ammunition production, more specifically to an improved pressed metal head component suitable for a polymer tube cartridge The invention relates to a method of drawing and forming a metal head unit for use with a polymer case to form a polymer cartridge for use in a rifled barrel, comprising the steps of
problem: Forming a pressed metal head component that is compatible with a polymer tube cartridge for use in a rifled barrel, ensuring structural integrity and proper fit.
constraint: Achieving the required dimensional accuracy and material compatibility between the metal head and polymer case during forming, while avoiding defects such as cracking or delamination under high-pressure conditions.
mechanism: A plastic deformation process that shapes a first component to match the physical dimensions and mechanical characteristics of a second component, creating a mechanically compatible interface capable of withstanding operational stresses.
mechanism_raw: A drawing and forming process that shapes a metal head unit to precisely match the dimensions and mechanical properties of a polymer case, enabling reliable integration and performance under firing stresses.
residual_terms: ["plastic deformation process", "physical dimensions", "mechanical characteristics", "mechanically compatible interface", "operational stresses"]

abstract: In a general aspect, a customized surgical profile is validated for execution on a surgical system. In some aspects, a customized ophthalmic surgical profile, which includes a surgical pattern and at least one parameter associated with the surgical pattern, is obtained. A pattern definition file executable by a laser-based ophthalmic surgical system is generated based on the customized ophthalmic surgical profile. Execution of the customized ophthalmic surgical profile on the laser-based ophthalmic surgical system is simulated based on the pattern definition file, and the pattern definition file is validated based on an output of the simulation. The validated pattern definition file is provided for execution on the laser-based ophthalmic surgical system.
problem: Ensuring a customized surgical profile is safe and effective for execution on a laser-based surgical system without risking patient harm during actual surgery.
constraint: Balancing the fidelity of the simulation with the need for rapid validation to avoid delays in surgical procedures.
mechanism: Validating a procedural plan by simulating its execution and using the simulation output as a gatekeeping step to determine approval before real-world deployment.
mechanism_raw: Simulating the execution of a pattern definition file derived from the surgical profile to validate its behavior before real-world deployment, using the simulation output as a gatekeeping step for approval.

abstract: The present invention provides a 4D printed component that uses the photoisomerization stimulus as a method of activation. Other 4D printing methods use heat, moisture, a combination of heat and stress, and the heat from a light source as methods of activation. The present invention takes advantage of 3D printing capability and adds the capability of providing a printable material that dynamically changes shape over time when exposed to an external stimulus. The invention reduces the number of required 3D printed parts to create a moving object. This characteristic reduces the amount of onboard weight of the 3D printed components by reducing the number of parts required to create motion. The present invention removes the need for onboard sensors, processors, motors, power storage, etc. This characteristic will allow for manufacturing of, inter alia, novel medical devices, automated actuators, packaging, smart textiles, etc.
problem: Creating dynamically shape-changing objects without requiring onboard sensors, processors, motors, or power storage.
constraint: Achieving precise and repeatable shape changes through controlled light exposure while maintaining structural integrity of the printed component.
mechanism: A material that undergoes a physical transformation when exposed to an external light stimulus, enabling autonomous actuation without embedded components.
mechanism_raw: Using a 4D-printed material that undergoes photoisomerization (shape change) when exposed to an external light stimulus, enabling autonomous actuation through material-level response.

abstract: A nested segment assembly and a method of additively manufacturing the same are provided. In one example aspect, the nested segment assembly includes a first component segment and a segment component segment positioned adjacent the first component segment. The first component segment has an end face and a tongue projecting outwardly from the end face. The second component segment defines a groove. The groove is defined at an end face of the second component segment that is adjacent the end face of the first component segment. The first component segment and the second component segment are additively printed such that at least a portion of the tongue of the first component segment is nested within the groove defined by the second component segment. Segmented components having a tesla valve formed therebetween are also provided.
problem: Manufacturing segmented components with interlocking functional features (e.g., tesla valves) as a single integrated unit via additive manufacturing.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and fit between nested segments during printing to maintain structural and functional integrity.
mechanism: Designing adjacent segments with complementary interlocking geometries that are fabricated in a nested configuration, enabling mechanical integration without post-assembly.
mechanism_raw: Designing adjacent segments with complementary tongue-and-groove geometries that are additively printed in a nested configuration, enabling mechanical interlocking and fluidic functionality without post-assembly.

abstract: An enclosure for a nacelle of a wind turbine is connected to a substructure in a manner that allows the enclosure to move relative to the substructure. An imaginary straight line extends over the panel and is aligned with an edge of the panel. The imaginary straight line defines a first sub-portion of the panel, said first sub-portion comprising the edge. The first sub-portion butts against the substructure. The first sub-portion is retained against the substructure by a tension element acting in a direction of tension. The first sub-portion can be displaced relative to the substructure in a direction which intersects the direction of tension. The invention facilitates the operation of assembling the enclosure.
problem: Facilitating assembly of a wind turbine nacelle enclosure by allowing controlled movement of panels relative to the substructure during installation.
constraint: Balancing the tension force to securely hold the panel in place while allowing sufficient mobility for assembly adjustments.
mechanism: A tension element that retains a component against a structure while permitting displacement in a direction intersecting the tension axis, enabling alignment adjustments during assembly.
mechanism_raw: Using a tension element to retain a panel portion against the substructure while permitting displacement in a direction intersecting the tension axis, enabling alignment adjustments during assembly.

abstract: Provided are a metal-base circuit board having excellent solder crack resistance, thermal conductivity, adhesive property, and insulation property and a resin composition for a circuit board used for the metal-base circuit board. A resin composition for a circuit board comprises a vinylsilyl group-containing polysiloxane (having a vinylsilyl group equivalent of 0.005 to 0.045 mol/kg) comprising (A) a dual-end type vinylsilyl group-containing polysiloxane having a weight average molecular weight of 30,000 to 80,000 and (B) a side-chain dual-end type vinylsilyl group-containing polysiloxane having a weight average molecular weight of 100,000 or more, a hydrosilyl group-containing polysiloxane (having a hydrosilyl group equivalent of 6 mol/kg or more), and an inorganic filler at 60 to 80% by volume. The mass ratio of (A) to (B), (A)/(B), is 80/20 to 30/70, and the molar ratio of (C) a hydrosilyl group to (D) a vinylsilyl group, (C)/(D), is 2.5 to 5.0.
reason: The patent primarily describes a specific material composition (resin with defined polysiloxane ratios and filler percentages) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. While the composition addresses material property tradeoffs, it is a formulation-specific solution tied to circuit board manufacturing.

abstract: An aircraft light for a foldable wing tip of an aircraft includes a first lighting structure, including at least one first light source and a first optical system, with the at least one first light source and the first optical system in operation generating a first light output; a second lighting structure, including at least one second light source and a second optical system, with the at least one second light source and the second optical system in operation generating a second light output; wherein the first light output and the second light output are of the same color and wherein the first light output and the second light output are angled with respect to each other; and wherein the aircraft light is configured to control the at least one first light source and the at least one second light source depending on a wing tip orientation signal, which is indicative of an orientation of the foldable wing tip.
problem: Maintaining consistent visual signaling or illumination from an aircraft light regardless of the orientation of a foldable wing tip.
constraint: Balancing the angular separation of light outputs to cover necessary viewing angles while avoiding overlap or gaps in illumination as the wing tip moves.
mechanism: Multiple light sources with angularly separated output directions are selectively activated based on a positional signal from a movable component, ensuring continuous coverage of a target viewing region as the component changes orientation.
mechanism_raw: Two light sources with the same color output are angled relative to each other, and their activation is dynamically controlled based on a wing tip orientation signal. This ensures the light output direction adapts to the wing's position, maintaining visibility or signaling effectiveness.

abstract: In the system and method disclosed, an ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) scanning tunneling microscope (STM) tip is used to selectively desorb hydrogen atoms from the Si(100)-2X1:H surface by injecting electrons at a negative sample bias voltage. A new lithography method is disclosed that allows the STM to operate under imaging conditions and simultaneously desorb H atoms as required. A high frequency signal is added to the negative sample bias voltage to deliver the required energy for hydrogen removal. The resulted current at this frequency and its harmonics are filtered to minimize their effect on the operation of the STM's feedback loop. This approach offers a significant potential for controlled and precise removal of hydrogen atoms from a hydrogen-terminated silicon surface and thus may be used for the fabrication of practical silicon-based atomic-scale devices.
problem: Achieving precise, simultaneous control of hydrogen atom desorption for lithography without disrupting the scanning tunneling microscope's feedback loop.
constraint: Matching the frequency and energy delivery to the desorption threshold while ensuring filtering does not attenuate the STM's operational signals.
mechanism: A high-frequency signal is combined with a base voltage to deliver energy for a material modification process, while a filtering mechanism isolates the process signal from a concurrent measurement system's operational frequencies.
mechanism_raw: A high-frequency signal is superimposed on a negative sample bias voltage to deliver sufficient energy for hydrogen removal. The resulting current harmonics are filtered to isolate the STM's feedback loop from interference, enabling concurrent imaging and desorption.

abstract: An apparatus for forming filter rods for aerosol-generating articles is provided, including a first source and a second source, the first source being configured to supply filter material in a form of a first tow, and the second source being configured to supply filter material in a form of a second tow; a single driven delivery roller configured to advance the first tow and the second tow; and an extrusion tool configured to process the first tow and the second tow, the delivery roller being arranged such that the first and the second tows are advanced from the first and the second sources toward the extrusion tool only by the delivery roller, and the extrusion tool is further configured to process several sources of filter material simultaneously to create one filter rod. A method for forming filter rods for aerosol-generating articles is also provided.
problem: Efficiently combining multiple streams of filter material into a single filter rod without requiring separate processing steps for each material.
constraint: Ensuring synchronized advancement of both tows through the single roller to prevent misalignment or uneven material flow during extrusion.
mechanism: A single driven advancement mechanism synchronously transports multiple distinct material streams toward a forming tool, which integrates them into a unified output structure without requiring separate delivery systems per stream.
mechanism_raw: A single driven delivery roller advances two distinct tows of filter material simultaneously toward an extrusion tool, which processes them together to form one integrated filter rod. This eliminates the need for separate delivery systems per material.
residual_terms: ["driven advancement mechanism", "material streams", "forming tool", "unified output structure"]

abstract: A method dresses one polishing cloth or two polishing pads simultaneously, in which a polishing cloth has been applied to a polishing plate, with at least one dresser (4), which is equipped with at least one dressing element (8), this at least one dressing element (8) being in contact with the at least one polishing cloth (11, 12) to be dressed, wherein the at least one polishing plate (21, 22) is rotated with a relative rotational speed and the at least one dresser (4) is rotated with a relative rotational speed and at least two different combinations of directions of rotation of the two pairs of polishing plates (21, 22) and pin wheels (31, 32) are executed during the simultaneous dressing of two polishing pads (11, 12) or during the dressing of one polishing cloth (11) of the polishing plate (21) and of the at least one dresser (4).
problem: Maintaining consistent surface texture on polishing cloths or pads by dressing them efficiently, even when processing multiple pads simultaneously.
constraint: Coordinating rotational speeds and directions to achieve uniform dressing without causing uneven wear or mechanical interference between components.
mechanism: A dressing element rotates in a direction opposing a polishing surface, with coordinated rotational speed and direction combinations applied across multiple polishing surfaces to ensure uniform abrasion distribution during simultaneous dressing.
mechanism_raw: A dresser with dressing elements rotates at a relative speed and direction opposite to the polishing plate(s), with multiple combinations of rotational directions executed during simultaneous dressing. This ensures uniform abrasion across the polishing surface(s).

abstract: The present invention relates to a method for synthesizing and collecting, in a single step, nanoparticles of different materials, and for producing coatings thereof on materials with simple or complex geometries, both in a controlled atmosphere and in ambient conditions, by means of the combined application of a laser beam and high-intensity electric fields.
problem: Synthesizing and collecting nanoparticles of different materials in a single step, including forming coatings on complex geometries under varying environmental conditions.
constraint: Balancing laser intensity and electric field strength to achieve precise nanoparticle size and composition while accommodating ambient or controlled atmosphere conditions.
mechanism: A directed energy beam and electric field are combined to induce localized material ablation and ionization, enabling controlled nucleation and growth of particles while directing their formation and collection under varying environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: A laser beam and high-intensity electric fields are combined to induce localized material ablation and ionization, enabling controlled nucleation and growth of nanoparticles. The interaction between the laser and electric field directs particle formation and collection.

abstract: A method (and the associated system) for risk evaluation in a vascular region of interest V are provided, making it possible, based on a fluidic study and/or on a treatment algorithm using a learning method, to generate risk models MR predictively indicating the risk level NR for the occurrence of events such as: occurrence and rupture of an aneurysm, coarctation, etc., and the associated anatomical areas. The models MR are intended to serve as an assistance support for the medical decision-making of a physician.
problem: Predicting the risk of vascular events (e.g., aneurysm rupture, coarctation) in a specific vascular region of interest to support physician decision-making.
constraint: The mechanism must balance the accuracy of fluidic modeling with the generalization capability of the learning-based treatment algorithm, ensuring the risk models are both predictive and clinically interpretable for medical decision support.
mechanism: Combining a physics-based simulation of fluid dynamics with a data-driven learning model to generate predictive risk assessments that map physiological conditions to event likelihood, where the simulation provides mechanistic accuracy and the learning model provides generalization across patient-specific variations.
mechanism_raw: Combining a fluidic study (hemodynamic simulation) with a treatment algorithm based on a learning method to generate predictive risk models that map vascular conditions to event risk levels.
residual_terms: ["fluid dynamics", "learning model", "predictive risk assessments", "physiological conditions", "event likelihood", "mechanistic accuracy", "generalization"]

abstract: A film bulk acoustic wave resonator includes a piezoelectric film disposed over a cavity. The cavity is shaped as partial ellipse including first, second, and third vertices. The film bulk acoustic wave resonator further includes three release ports in positions that minimize etch time to remove all sacrificial material from within the cavity.
problem: Efficiently removing all sacrificial material from within a cavity of a film bulk acoustic wave resonator without leaving residue that could impair device performance.
constraint: The mechanism must balance minimizing etch time (for manufacturing efficiency) with ensuring complete sacrificial material removal (for device reliability), while maintaining the acoustic performance of the resonator through the specific cavity and port geometry.
mechanism: Configuring an internal cavity geometry with multiple strategically placed access ports to enable complete removal of sacrificial material through optimized spatial distribution of etching pathways, balancing processing time against removal completeness while preserving functional performance characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Shaping the cavity as a partial ellipse with three release ports positioned to minimize etch time, enabling complete removal of sacrificial material through optimized geometric placement of access points.
residual_terms: ["cavity geometry", "access ports", "sacrificial material", "etching pathways", "spatial distribution", "processing time", "removal completeness", "functional performance"]

abstract: A portable storage container includes a body and a lid. The body has a bottom and sides that define an interior storage volume. The lid is attachable to the body for closing the interior storage volume and includes a lid base, a first lid member, and a second lid member. The first lid member is hingeably attached to the lid base on a first side and the second lid member is hingeably attached on a second side. Each of the lid members includes a handle recess and an attached handle. The handle of the first lid member is positioned at least partially in the handle recess of the second lid member and the handle of the second lid member is positioned at least partially in the handle recess of the first lid member when the first lid member opened and the second lid member is closed.
problem: Creating a portable storage container lid that is both easy to handle and securely closed when one lid member is opened and the other remains closed.
constraint: Balancing accessibility of the handles with secure retention of the lid members in their respective open/closed states without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Interlocking handles between two hinged lid members: when one lid member is opened, its handle is positioned partially within the handle recess of the other (closed) lid member, and vice versa. This interaction ensures the handles remain accessible and the lid members stay functionally coupled during use.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking handles between two hinged lid members: when one lid member is opened, its handle is positioned partially within the handle recess of the other (closed) lid member, and vice versa. This interaction ensures the handles remain accessible and the lid members stay functionally coupled during use.

abstract: Methods of treating contaminated groundwater having recalcitrant organic contaminants are disclosed. The methods include pretreating the contaminated groundwater to remove iron, introducing a persulfate to the contaminated groundwater, and exposing the contaminated groundwater to irradiation. The methods may also include extracting the contaminated groundwater from a feed stream. The methods may also include preparing the persulfate with high purity water. Systems for treating contaminated groundwater having recalcitrant organic contaminants are also disclosed. The systems include a pretreatment subsystem, a source of persulfate, and an irradiation source.
problem: Effectively removing recalcitrant organic contaminants from contaminated groundwater that are resistant to conventional treatment methods.
constraint: Maintaining the correct sequence and conditions to avoid interference from iron and ensure effective activation of persulfate via irradiation without degrading the treatment system.
mechanism: A sequential multi-step process: (1) pretreatment to remove interfering substances, (2) introduction of a strong oxidizing agent, and (3) activation of the oxidizing agent via irradiation to enhance degradation of recalcitrant contaminants. The pretreatment step ensures optimal conditions for subsequent activation.
mechanism_raw: A sequential multi-step process: (1) pretreatment to remove iron (which could interfere with subsequent steps), (2) introduction of persulfate as a strong oxidizing agent, and (3) irradiation to activate the persulfate, enhancing its ability to degrade recalcitrant contaminants. The pretreatment step ensures optimal conditions for persulfate activation.

abstract: A composition for use as a pressure-tolerant dual-crosslinker gel in a fracturing fluid that comprises polymer, the polymer operable to increase the viscosity of a fluid; boron-containing crosslinker, the boron-containing crosslinker operable to crosslink the polymer; and a transition metal oxide additive, the transition metal oxide additive operable to crosslink the polymer.
problem: Creating a pressure-tolerant gel for fracturing fluids that maintains viscosity and structural integrity under high-pressure conditions.
constraint: Balancing the concentrations and interactions of the two crosslinkers to avoid over-crosslinking (which could reduce viscosity) or under-crosslinking (which could compromise pressure tolerance).
mechanism: A dual-crosslinker system: two distinct crosslinking agents both crosslink the polymer matrix. The combination provides redundant crosslinking pathways, enhancing structural integrity and pressure tolerance compared to single-crosslinker systems.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual-crosslinker system: a boron-containing crosslinker and a transition metal oxide additive both crosslink the polymer. The combination provides redundant crosslinking pathways, enhancing gel stability and pressure tolerance compared to single-crosslinker systems.

abstract: The invention provides a lysis reagent for lysing red blood cells, thereby releasing a target, such as RNA from a parasitic organism, in a form suitable for analysis. The reagent includes at least ammonium chloride and an anionic detergent, and may include an anti-coagulant. The reagent serves to lyse red blood cells, protect the released target from degradation in the lysate, and is compatible with subsequent steps for analysis of the target such as target capture, amplification, detection, or sequencing.
problem: Lysing red blood cells to release target molecules (e.g., RNA from parasites) while preserving their integrity and compatibility with downstream analytical processes.
constraint: Ensuring the reagent composition does not degrade the target molecule (e.g., RNA) while maintaining compatibility with downstream steps like amplification or sequencing.
mechanism: A reagent combining a cell-lysing agent (to disrupt target cells), a membrane-disrupting agent (to release intracellular components), and optionally a stabilizing agent (to preserve target molecule integrity). The components work synergistically to lyse cells, release targets, and maintain compatibility with downstream processes.
mechanism_raw: A reagent combining ammonium chloride (to lyse red blood cells), an anionic detergent (to disrupt cell membranes), and optionally an anti-coagulant (to prevent degradation of the target). The components work synergistically to lyse cells, release targets, and stabilize them for subsequent analysis.

abstract: An exemplary electromagnetic shielded dry bag with magnetic closure system includes an outer bag, an inner shielding liner, and a pair of embedding strips having magnets embedded therein. The outer bag is preferably comprised of water-proof material and has a fluid-sealed floor portion and an access mouth disposed oppositely thereof. First and second bag panels are disposed oppositely of one another and extend from the floor portion to the access mouth. The inner shielding liner is comprised of electromagnetic shielding material and defines an electromagnetic shielding compartment within the bag. The embedding strips are secured to respective bag panels. This securement may be by way of heat fusing of respective securement elements to the inner faces, thereby forming pockets with which the strips reside. When the closure section is magnetically retained in closed configuration, the access mouth is thereby retained in an RF-sealed and fluid-sealed configuration to protect the shielding compartment.
problem: Creating a protective enclosure that is both waterproof and electromagnetically shielded, with a closure mechanism that maintains both seals.
constraint: Ensuring the magnetic closure does not compromise the electromagnetic shielding effectiveness or the waterproof integrity of the bag during sealing and use.
mechanism: A magnetic closure system: opposing panels are retained via embedded magnetic elements, creating a dual-seal interface that maintains both fluid-tight integrity and electromagnetic shielding when the closure is engaged.
mechanism_raw: Magnetic closure system: embedding strips with magnets are secured to opposing bag panels. When the closure is magnetically retained, the access mouth is sealed both fluid-tightly (via waterproof material) and RF-sealed (via the electromagnetic shielding liner), ensuring dual protection.

abstract: An object is to provide lactic acid bacteria that can be applicable to feed, fertilizers, live bacterial preparations, probiotics, etc. The lactic acid bacteria are identified and deposited under the accession numbers of NITE (National Institute of Technology and Evaluation) P-02313, NITE P-02314, NITE P-02490, NITE P-02491, and NITE P-02492. In addition, another object is to provide feed, fertilizers and live bacterial preparations containing the lactic acid bacterium/bacteria of the invention. According to studies, it is confirmed that the lactic acid bacteria are proliferated in animals including human, plants, etc. without being destroyed. According to studies, it is also confirmed that the lactic acid bacteria are proliferated in water, soil, etc. without being destroyed. Therefore, the lactic acid bacteria can be widely applicable in feed, fertilizers, live bacterial preparations, etc.
reason: The abstract describes the outcome (bacteria surviving in diverse environments) but does not explain the causal mechanism enabling this survival. It focuses on application rather than a functional principle.

abstract: Swellable metal sealing elements and methods for forming a seal in a wellbore using said swellable metal sealing elements. An example method comprises providing a swellable metal sealing element selected from the group consisting of an O-ring, a gasket, or a seal stack; wherein the swellable metal sealing element is disposed in or around a downhole tool disposed in the wellbore. The method further comprises exposing the swellable metal sealing element to a brine and allowing or causing to allow the swellable metal sealing element to swell.
problem: Creating a reliable seal in a wellbore that adapts to environmental conditions without mechanical intervention.
constraint: The material must swell predictably and maintain structural integrity under downhole pressure and chemical exposure.
mechanism: A responsive material element undergoes controlled volumetric expansion when exposed to an environmental trigger, generating a conformal interface through material-driven shape change that adapts to surrounding conditions without external actuation.
mechanism_raw: A swellable metal sealing element undergoes volumetric expansion when exposed to a specific chemical trigger (e.g., brine), generating a conformal seal through material-driven shape change.

abstract: An assembly for a gas turbine engine according to an example of the present disclosure includes, among other things, a gas turbine engine component that has a first interface portion, and a support that has a mounting portion and a second interface portion, the mounting portion attachable to an engine static structure, a first retention feature that releasably secures the first interface portion to the support in a first installed position of the gas turbine engine component, and a second retention feature dimensioned to secure the first interface portion to the second interface portion in a second installed position of the gas turbine engine component. The first installed position differs from the second installed position, and one of first and second retention features is dimensioned to carry the gas turbine engine component in response to release of another one of the first and second retention features. A method of sealing for a gas turbine engine is also disclosed.
problem: Securing a gas turbine component in multiple positions while ensuring load-bearing redundancy during installation or maintenance.
constraint: The retention features must balance ease of installation with fail-safe load distribution under high-temperature and vibrational conditions.
mechanism: A redundant retention architecture employs two distinct mechanical coupling interfaces: one for initial positioning and another for load transfer, enabling load-bearing continuity when one interface is disengaged through selective engagement of the alternate interface.
mechanism_raw: A dual retention system uses two distinct mechanical interfaces: one for initial positioning and another for load transfer, allowing one feature to carry the component if the other is disengaged.

abstract: In one example, a lighting assembly includes a housing to hold an elongated lamp and an elongated device attached to or integral with the housing and configured to, when an lamp is held in the housing, convert light from the lamp having a first irradiance that is non-uniform along a length into light having a second irradiance that is uniform along the length.
problem: Achieving uniform light irradiance along the length of an elongated lamp despite inherent non-uniformity in light emission.
constraint: The device must maintain uniformity across the entire length while accommodating the lamp's geometry and thermal expansion.
mechanism: An elongated optical redistribution element interacts with non-uniform emitted radiation to spatially transform input irradiance into uniform output across its length through geometric and optical coupling effects.
mechanism_raw: An elongated structural device (e.g., diffuser or light guide) interacts with the lamp's emitted light to redistribute irradiance spatially, converting non-uniform input into uniform output.
residual_terms: ["optical redistribution element", "spatial transformation", "geometric and optical coupling"]

abstract: A device includes a first amplifier and a second amplifier. The first amplifier includes an inverting input configured to be coupled to a feedback node of an output of a power converter, a first non-inverting input configured to couple to a first voltage node, a second non-inverting input, and an output. The second amplifier includes an inverting input coupled to the output of the first amplifier, a non-inverting input coupled to a second voltage node, and an output. The device also includes a first transistor coupled to the output of the first amplifier and having a control terminal coupled to the output of the second amplifier, a capacitor coupled to a ground node and to the second non-inverting input of the first amplifier, and a current node coupled to the capacitor.
problem: Precisely regulating the output of a power converter while maintaining stability under dynamic load conditions.
constraint: The amplifiers must operate without oscillation or delay, balancing response speed with noise immunity in high-frequency power systems.
mechanism: A hierarchical feedback control system uses cascaded signal conditioning stages to sense and adjust output voltage, with one stage stabilizing an intermediate node and another stage modulating a switching element to maintain regulation under dynamic load conditions.
mechanism_raw: A cascaded amplifier-transistor feedback loop uses two amplifiers to sense and adjust the converter's output voltage, with one amplifier stabilizing the feedback node and the other controlling the transistor's gate.
residual_terms: ["feedback control system", "cascaded signal conditioning", "switching element", "intermediate node"]

abstract: The invention relates to a light module for a motor vehicle headlamp, comprising: at least one light source (1) and at least one projection device (2), the projection device (2) having an entry optical unit (21) and an exit optical unit (22), the entry optical unit (21) being designed to form an intermediate image from light emitted by the at least one light source (1) in an intermediate image plane, which lies between the entry optical unit (21) and the exit optical unit (22) and is substantially perpendicular to an optical axis of the projection device (2), and the exit optical unit (22) being designed to image the intermediate image into a region in front of the light module in the form of a light distribution of a first predefined type, at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) being provided, which at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) is designed to emit light between the entry optical unit (21) and the exit optical unit (22); the exit optical unit (22) being designed to image the light emitted by the at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) into the region in front of the light module in the form of a light distribution of a second predefined type; the entry optical unit (21) and the at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) being designed in such a way and being associated with each other in such a way that neither the at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) nor the light emitted by the at least one additional light source (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d) changes the intermediate image.
problem: Need to project multiple distinct light distributions from a single headlamp module without additional light sources interfering with the main light source's optical processing.
constraint: The additional light sources must not change the intermediate image, requiring careful spatial and optical design to avoid interference with the intermediate image plane while still allowing the exit optical unit to image their light output.
mechanism: Multiple light sources are arranged along a shared optical path such that their emitted outputs are spatially separated from a primary light source's intermediate image plane. A downstream optical element combines the intermediate image and the additional sources' outputs into a common output region, enabling distinct distributions to be projected through controlled spatial separation of optical paths.
mechanism_raw: Additional light sources are positioned in the optical path between the entry and exit optical units and designed in association with the entry optical unit so that their emitted light does not alter the intermediate image formed by the main light source. The exit optical unit then images both the intermediate image and the additional sources' light into the output region, allowing multiple light distributions to be produced from a shared projection device through spatial separation of optical paths.

abstract: A method for detecting a leak, having at least the following steps: a) capturing a flow volume of a liquid through a liquid line during a multiplicity of liquid removal processes; b) comparing the flow volumes of the liquid in the respective liquid removal processes with an alarm value; c) outputting an alarm signal if the flow volume of the liquid in a liquid removal process exceeds the alarm value; d) adapting the alarm value on the basis of a frequency of the occurrence of the flow volumes of the liquid in the liquid removal processes above an adaptation value.
problem: Need to detect leaks in a liquid line by monitoring flow volumes, but fixed alarm thresholds may be too sensitive or insufficient depending on varying operating conditions.
constraint: The adaptation must balance detection sensitivity against false alarms, using the frequency of threshold exceedances as the sole basis for adjusting the alarm value.
mechanism: A detection threshold is dynamically adjusted via a feedback loop that monitors the frequency of measured values exceeding a reference level. When exceedances occur frequently, the threshold is recalibrated to balance sensitivity against false alarms, creating an adaptive system that tunes its response to observed operating conditions.
mechanism_raw: The alarm value is dynamically adapted based on the frequency of flow volumes exceeding an adaptation value. When flow volumes frequently exceed the adaptation value, the alarm value is adjusted to maintain appropriate detection sensitivity, creating a feedback loop that tunes the detection threshold to the observed operating environment.

abstract: An electronic timepiece improves operability when manually adjusting the time. The electronic timepiece includes: a time display configured to indicate the time; a rotatable crown that can be pulled out to multiple stop positions, including a first position and a second position; a stop position detector configured to detect the stop position of the crown; an operation detector configured to detect an operation rotating the crown; and a time setter configured to change the time displayed by the time display according to an adjustment amount that differs according to the stop position at each detected operation when the stop position is the first position or the second position and the operating detector detects the operation.
problem: Need to improve operability when manually adjusting time on an electronic timepiece, as a single adjustment rate may be too slow for large changes or too coarse for fine adjustments.
constraint: The adjustment amount must differ according to the stop position, requiring the system to detect both the operational state (stop position) and the input action (rotation) to determine the appropriate adjustment magnitude.
mechanism: An input device with multiple discrete operational states modulates the magnitude of a control action based on the detected state and the applied input. Each state corresponds to a different adjustment granularity, allowing the user to select precision by choosing the operational configuration before initiating the input action.
mechanism_raw: The crown has multiple stop positions, and the time setter changes the displayed time by an adjustment amount that varies according to the detected stop position. Different stop positions provide different adjustment granularity, allowing the user to select appropriate precision by choosing how far to pull the crown.

abstract: A foliage shredder that can shred inputted foliage matter into uniform sized particles without pulverizing the inputted foliage matter includes a housing, a shredding axle, a motor, a stand, a digital timer, a power cord, and a lid. The shredding axle is concentrically positioned within a cylindrical compartment of the housing and rotatably coupled to a rotor of the motor. A stator of the motor is externally connected to the housing and electrically connected to the power cord through the digital timer. The lid is terminally attached to the housing thus closing the cylindrical compartment. The cylindrical compartment functions as a container unit for the inputted foliage as the electrically powered shredding axle shreds the inputted foliage into uniform sized particles.
reason: The abstract describes a list of components (housing, shredding axle, motor, stand, timer, power cord, lid) without explaining a causal mechanism for achieving uniform particle size without pulverization. No functional relationship is described that explains how the arrangement produces the desired effect.

abstract: Provided is an optical laminate capable of contributing to reduction in weight and improvement in impact resistance of a display apparatus. The optical laminate includes a thin glass having a thickness of 100 μm or less and a polarizing plate arranged on one side of the thin glass, in which the polarizing plate includes a polarizer and a protective film arranged on a surface of the polarizer on a thin glass side. In one embodiment, the optical laminate of the present invention further includes an adhesion layer between the thin glass and the polarizing plate.
reason: The abstract describes a material composition (thin glass with polarizing plate and protective film) without explaining a causal functional mechanism beyond using thin materials for weight reduction. No transferable causal operation is described.

abstract: A disc for use in a disc screen is disclosed. The disc includes a longitudinal disc axis and a hub extending a length along the longitudinal disc axis. The hub further includes a hub surface and a helical ridge structure extending away from the hub surface and twisting about the longitudinal axis at least 360 degrees. A cross-section of the hub taken perpendicularly to the longitudinal disc axis is non-circular.
problem: Inefficient material separation or screening in disc screens due to limited interaction between the disc and materials being processed.
constraint: Balancing structural integrity of the disc with the need for sufficient helical twist and non-circular geometry to avoid mechanical failure while maximizing material movement.
mechanism: A helical structure extending from a rotating hub surface creates rotational and lifting motion as the hub turns. The non-circular cross-sectional geometry of the hub forces materials along a complex trajectory, increasing contact duration and interaction with the surface for enhanced separation.
mechanism_raw: A helical ridge structure extending from the hub surface and twisting around the longitudinal axis creates a rotational and lifting motion as the disc rotates. The non-circular cross-section of the hub ensures that materials are moved along a complex path, increasing contact time and interaction with the disc surface for improved separation.

abstract: A system for cementing a wellbore having a casing string disposed in the wellbore is provided. The system includes a cement tool, a fiber optic cable, and a computing device. The cement tool is operable to be deployed down the wellbore through a casing string from a surface during cementing process of the wellbore. The cement tool includes a tool sensor. The fiber optic cable is coupled with the cement tool such that the fiber optic cable spans the wellbore from the cement tool to the surface. The fiber optic cable is communicatively coupled with the tool sensor. The computing device is communicatively coupled with the fiber optic cable and is operable to receive and process signals from the tool sensor via the fiber optic cable during the cementing process.
problem: Inability to monitor real-time conditions during a cementing process in a wellbore, leading to potential inefficiencies or failures in sealing the well.
constraint: Ensuring reliable signal transmission through the fiber optic cable in a high-pressure, high-temperature downhole environment without signal degradation or physical damage to the cable.
mechanism: A signal transmission medium physically coupled to a downhole tool relays sensor measurements from the tool to a surface computing device. This enables continuous, real-time monitoring of operational parameters during a process, allowing immediate adjustments to maintain performance.
mechanism_raw: A fiber optic cable physically coupled to a downhole cement tool transmits sensor data from the tool to a surface computing device. This allows continuous, real-time monitoring of parameters like pressure, temperature, or flow during cementing, enabling immediate adjustments to the process.

abstract: A heat exchanger header includes a first stage with a first unit and a second stage with second units. The first unit includes a first branched region, a first common axis, and first fluid channels. Each of the first fluid channels includes a first end and a second end, wherein each of the first fluid channels defines a first spiral path with respect to the first common axis. Each of the second units includes a second branched region, a second common axis, and second fluid channels. Each of the second fluid channels includes a first end and a second end, wherein each of the second fluid channels defines a second spiral path with respect to the second common axis. Each of the second ends of the first fluid channels is connected to one of the second branched regions.
problem: Inefficient heat transfer in heat exchanger systems due to limited surface area and suboptimal fluid flow patterns.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the spiral channels under thermal and pressure stresses while optimizing the balance between turbulence-induced heat transfer and pressure drop across the system.
mechanism: Spiral flow paths in a heat exchange system increase effective surface area for thermal transfer. The spiral geometry induces controlled turbulence in fluid flow, enhancing convective heat transfer while maintaining compactness through staged branching of flow channels.
mechanism_raw: Spiral fluid channels in each stage of the heat exchanger header increase the effective surface area for heat exchange. The spiral paths induce controlled turbulence in the fluid flow, enhancing convective heat transfer while maintaining a compact design through staged branching.

abstract: A power supply unit for an aerosol inhaler includes: a first element connected in series to a load and having a first electric resistance value; a second series circuit including a second element having a second electric resistance value and a third element connected in series to the second element and having a third electric resistance value, and connected in parallel with a first series circuit including the load and the first element; and an operational amplifier in which one of a non-inverting input terminal and an inverting input terminal is connected to the first series circuit, and the other of the non-inverting input terminal and the inverting input terminal is connected to the second series circuit. Each of the first to third electric resistance values is larger than the electric resistance value of the load at a normal temperature or a temperature in a predetermined temperature range.
problem: Unstable power delivery to an aerosol inhaler load due to temperature-dependent resistance variations, risking inconsistent performance or safety issues.
constraint: Selecting resistor values that are large enough to dominate temperature effects but small enough to avoid excessive power dissipation or voltage drop, while ensuring the op-amp can maintain stable feedback across the operating temperature range.
mechanism: A resistor network with values significantly higher than a load's resistance is configured in series and parallel with a feedback-controlled amplifier. The amplifier adjusts output to stabilize voltage/current delivery to the load, compensating for temperature-induced resistance variations in the resistors.
mechanism_raw: A resistor network with values significantly higher than the load's resistance is used in series and parallel configurations with an operational amplifier. The op-amp provides feedback control to stabilize the voltage/current delivered to the load, compensating for temperature-induced resistance changes in the resistors.

abstract: Provided herein is an improved spin coating system and a method of using the spin coating machine to produce an optical article. The system includes at least one dispensing arm assembly. The holder assembly is moveable along a substantially vertical axis. The dispensing arm assembly has a base and at least one arm having a first end and a second end and is moveable along a horizontal axis. The at least one arm is operably coupled to the base at the first end and operably coupled to at least one applicator at the second end, and the applicator is capable of being positioned along the substantially vertical axis. The method includes depositing a primer layer onto a lens using the dispensing arm assembly, followed by a hard coating, and drying and cooling the substrate using a drying/cooling station that is positioned substantially along the substantially vertical axis.
problem: Inconsistent or imprecise application of multi-layer coatings (e.g., primer, hard coat) on substrates like lenses due to limited positional control during spin coating.
constraint: Achieving synchronization between vertical and horizontal movements to maintain alignment and prevent cross-contamination between layers, while minimizing process time and mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A dual-axis positioning system coordinates movement between an applicator and a substrate holder. Horizontal and vertical motion axes are synchronized to enable precise sequential deposition of multiple material layers without manual intervention or cross-contamination between layers.
mechanism_raw: A dispensing arm assembly with horizontal-axis mobility is coordinated with a vertically movable holder assembly. This dual-axis movement allows precise positioning of the applicator relative to the substrate, enabling sequential deposition of different coating layers without manual intervention or contamination between layers.

abstract: A sewing machine includes a thread cutter. The thread cutter includes a cutter blade having a blade edge configured to cut a thread, and a movable member. The movable member includes a guide having a guide surface adjacent to the cutter blade. The guide is configured to receive force from the thread at the guide surface during the course of cutting the thread with the cutter blade and to move in a moving direction which is a longitudinal direction of the blade edge.
problem: Efficiently cutting a thread while maintaining control over the cutting process to avoid tangling or misalignment.
constraint: The guide must move in precise synchronization with the blade's cutting motion without introducing lateral forces that could disrupt the thread or blade.
mechanism: A dynamically responsive guide element interacts with the material being processed during a cutting operation, translating forces generated by material movement into coordinated motion that adjusts the cutting trajectory to maintain alignment and prevent misalignment-induced disruptions.
mechanism_raw: A movable guide adjacent to the cutter blade receives force from the thread during cutting and translates that force into longitudinal movement along the blade edge, dynamically adjusting the cutting path to maintain alignment and tension.

abstract: A hydraulic system includes a hydraulic pump, a first hydraulic actuator, a second hydraulic actuator, a first control valve to control the first hydraulic actuator, a second control valve to control the second hydraulic actuator, the second control valve being arranged on a downstream side of the first control valve, and a discharge fluid tube in which the operation fluid flows. The hydraulic system further includes a first fluid tube in which a return fluid flows toward the second control valve. The hydraulic system further includes a second fluid tube in which a supply fluid flows toward the first hydraulic actuator, a third fluid tube coupling the first fluid tube to the discharge fluid tube, and a fourth fluid tube in which the return fluid flows toward the second fluid tube, the fourth fluid tube being connected to the first fluid tube.
problem: Managing fluid flow and pressure distribution in a hydraulic system with multiple actuators to ensure coordinated operation.
constraint: The system must maintain pressure integrity and flow directionality across multiple parallel paths without cross-interference or pressure drops that could destabilize actuator performance.
mechanism: A branched fluid distribution network employs sequenced valve arrangements and cross-coupled pathways to regulate pressure equilibrium and directional flow allocation across parallel operational branches, preventing cross-interference while maintaining system-wide pressure integrity.
mechanism_raw: A network of interconnected fluid tubes and control valves routes supply and return fluids in a specific sequence, using downstream valve arrangements and cross-coupling tubes to balance pressure and direct flow to the correct actuators.

abstract: An array substrate and a manufacturing method thereof, a display panel, and a display device are provided. The array substrate includes a base substrate, gate lines and data lines, switch circuits, a common electrode layer, and a light shielding conductive layer. The gate lines and the data lines are on the base substrate and cross with each other to define pixel regions; the switch circuits are in the pixel regions; the common electrode layer is on a side of the switch circuits away from the base substrate; and the light shielding conductive layer is on the side of the switch circuits away from the base substrate and is electrically connected to the common electrode layer. At least a portion of an orthographic projection of the gate lines, the data lines and the switch circuits is within an orthographic projection of the light shielding conductive layer on the base substrate.
problem: Preventing light leakage in display pixels while maintaining electrical connectivity for common electrode functionality.
constraint: The layer must align precisely with underlying components to avoid gaps in shielding or electrical discontinuities, while remaining compatible with the pixel's structural and optical requirements.
mechanism: A multifunctional shielding layer is spatially arranged to overlap critical component projections, utilizing its material properties to simultaneously block unwanted radiation and establish electrical continuity with a shared conductive network.
mechanism_raw: A light-shielding conductive layer is positioned to overlap the orthographic projections of gate lines, data lines, and switch circuits, using its conductive properties to both block light and electrically couple to the common electrode layer.

abstract: A floor electrical outlet cover may be disposed over and coupled to a floor electrical outlet, the floor electrical outlet cover comprising a first color and further comprising at least one opening aligned with the floor electrical outlet, and at least one flap coupled to the floor electrical outlet cover, the flap configured to move from a closed position that restricts access to the floor electrical outlet to an open position that provides access to the floor electrical outlet. A colored electrical plate cover may comprise a second color different from the first color and a structural element coupled to the floor electrical outlet cover. The colored electrical plate cover may further comprise at least one opening aligned with the at least one opening in the floor electrical outlet cover. At least one colored flap cover may be coupled to the flap.
reason: The patent describes a color-coded outlet cover with flaps and covers, but the mechanism is purely a physical design feature (flap movement and color coding) without a deeper causal functional relationship that solves a technical problem beyond basic accessibility and aesthetics.

abstract: Methods of making a foamed article include: (a) milling a block or sheet of thermoplastic polymer to form a precursor; (b) crosslinking the thermoplastic polymer; (c) heating the precursor to a first temperature to soften the thermoplastic polymer; (d) infusing the thermoplastic polymer with at least one inert gas at a first pressure that is sufficient to cause the at least one inert gas to permeate into the softened thermoplastic polymer; and (e) while the thermoplastic polymer is softened, reducing the pressure to a second pressure below the first pressure to at least partially foam the precursor into a foamed article, wherein the foamed article is substantially the same shape as the precursor.
problem: Creating a foamed thermoplastic article with controlled expansion while preserving the precursor's shape during the foaming process.
constraint: The timing and magnitude of pressure reduction must be precisely controlled to ensure uniform foaming without collapsing the structure or causing uneven expansion.
mechanism: A material shaping process involves sequential thermal conditioning, gaseous saturation under elevated pressure, and controlled depressurization to induce internal phase expansion while preserving the precursor's geometric form through timed pressure modulation.
mechanism_raw: The precursor is heated to soften the polymer, infused with inert gas under high pressure to saturate the material, then rapidly depressurized while still softened, causing the gas to expand and form a foam structure that retains the original shape.

abstract: A formulation for a photopolymer composite material for a 3D printing system includes an acrylate monomer or an acrylate oligomer, an inorganic hydrate, a reinforcing filler, a co-initiator, a thermal initiator, and an ultraviolet (UV) initiator. In the formulation the acrylate monomer or the acrylate oligomer may be between about 10.0-30.0 w % of the formulation. The thermal initiator may be between about 0.001-0.05 w %, the co-initiator may be between about 0.001-0.05 w %, and the UV initiator may be between about 0.001-0.2 w % of the formulation. A method of generating a formulation of a photopolymer composite material for use in a 3D printing system includes using an acrylate monomer or an acrylate oligomer, an inorganic hydrate, a reinforcing filler, a co-initiator, a thermal initiator, and an ultraviolet (UV) initiator.
problem: Achieving controlled curing and structural integrity in photopolymer composites for 3D printing under varying environmental conditions.
constraint: Balancing initiator concentrations to prevent interference between thermal and UV activation pathways while ensuring sufficient curing speed and material stability.
mechanism: Combining two energy-responsive agents with distinct activation thresholds enables sequential or simultaneous curing under different energy inputs, allowing polymerization to proceed via multiple pathways while maintaining compatibility between components.
mechanism_raw: Combining thermal and UV initiators with distinct activation thresholds allows sequential or dual-mode curing, enabling the material to polymerize under different energy inputs (heat and light) while maintaining compatibility between components.

abstract: The present invention provides a stable, aqueous injectable solution comprising epinephrine or its pharmaceutically acceptable salt, a sulfite antioxidant, butylated hydroxyl anisole, an organic acid and a chelating agent, wherein the solution is free of an inorganic acid and an inorganic base. The invention also provides a method of treating the septic shock by intravenous administration of stable aqueous injectable solution comprising epinephrine or its pharmaceutically acceptable salt, a sulfite antioxidant, butylated hydroxyl anisole, an organic acid and a chelating agent, wherein the solution is free of an inorganic acid and an inorganic base.
problem: Stabilizing labile pharmaceutical compounds (e.g., epinephrine) in aqueous injectable solutions without using inorganic acids or bases, which may cause adverse reactions.
constraint: Selecting antioxidant and chelator combinations that do not interact deleteriously with the active pharmaceutical ingredient or each other, while avoiding inorganic components that compromise biocompatibility.
mechanism: A combination of oxidative inhibitors, metal-deactivating agents, and an organic pH-buffering compound suppresses degradation pathways (oxidative and metal-catalyzed) while maintaining chemical stability through complementary stabilization mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: Using a combination of antioxidants (sulfite, BHA) and a chelating agent with an organic acid to suppress oxidative degradation and metal-catalyzed decomposition, while maintaining pH stability through organic acid buffering.

abstract: A horse training device which is adjustable to fit various sizes of horse heads and neck sizes. The training device includes a generally U-shaped bosal-like member having a forward end and first and second legs extending rearwardly therefrom. A first ring is secured to the rearward ends of the first and second legs. A first U-shaped strap has its lower ends secured to second and third rings secured to the first and second legs respectively. A second strap has one end thereof secured to a cross-member which extends between the first and second legs. The other end of the second strap has a fourth ring member secured thereto. The lower ends of a U-shaped third strap are secured to the fourth ring. A U-shaped fourth strap is connected to the first and third straps and extend around the head of the horse below the ears of the horse.
problem: Creating an adjustable animal training device that accommodates varying anatomical dimensions while maintaining secure, consistent contact pressure.
constraint: Ensuring mechanical stability and load distribution across all adjustment configurations to prevent localized pressure points or structural failure during use.
mechanism: A modular mechanical interface with distributed attachment points enables incremental geometric reconfiguration, allowing the device to conform to varying anatomical dimensions while maintaining uniform load distribution and structural integrity across all configurations.
mechanism_raw: A modular strap-and-ring system with multiple attachment points allows incremental adjustment of tension and geometry, enabling the device to conform to different head/neck sizes without slippage.

abstract: A clock comprises a dial comprising two or more positions. Each position has an associated time value and the associated time values of the two or more positions increase in a first clock direction around the dial. An indicator provided in combination with the dial indicates a position on the dial with respect to the two or more markings that represents a time. An actuator provides a motive force to move the indicator from one position to another position on the dial under the control of a controller so that the indicator transitions from a first time to a later second time by moving the indicator in a second clock direction opposite the first clock direction around the dial. The clock can comprise one or more indicators, actuators, and sensors for sensing the position of each indicator. Indicators can be clock hands, for example minute, hour, or second hands.
problem: Displaying time progression on a dial-based interface using non-traditional indicator movement to enhance visual intuitiveness or aesthetic appeal.
constraint: Synchronizing the reverse-direction movement with precise time intervals to avoid ambiguity in time interpretation while maintaining mechanical reliability of the actuator system.
mechanism: A control system actuates an indicator to move in a direction opposing the numerical sequence on a dial, creating a visual contrast that emphasizes temporal progression through reverse motion synchronized with precise time intervals.
mechanism_raw: A controller actuates an indicator to move in a direction opposite to the numerical sequence on the dial, creating a visual contrast that emphasizes temporal progression through reverse motion.

abstract: A flying disc smoking pipe apparatus is provided wherein a flying disc, having a central opening, has a centrally mounted smoking pipe insert within the central opening, having a plurality of draw pipes extending radially from the insert to and through the flying disc shaped housing lip. The distal end of the draw pipes is flush with the outside circumference of the flying disc. A smoking bowl is provided in the top of the insert and is in direct pneumatic communications with the draw pipes. The flying disc housing facilitates passing the pipe amongst multiple users at a distance by gliding the pipe from user to user. A single user may draw smoke through a draw pipe and selectively adjust the smoke temperature by throttling air flow into other draw pipes. Multiple users may also smoke simultaneously. The flying disc smoking pipe apparatus further provides entertainment and recreation to smoking.
problem: Enabling multi-user access and temperature control in a portable smoking device while maintaining structural integrity during shared use.
constraint: Balancing airflow resistance and structural rigidity across the radial pipes to ensure even smoke distribution and prevent mechanical failure during repeated handling and gliding motions.
mechanism: A central chamber with radially distributed access ports allows simultaneous interaction by multiple users, with individual flow regulation mechanisms to control per-user parameters while maintaining structural integrity during repeated mechanical engagement.
mechanism_raw: Radially distributed draw pipes connected to a central chamber allow simultaneous inhalation by multiple users, with selective airflow throttling through individual pipes to regulate smoke temperature per user.
residual_terms: ["radially distributed access ports", "individual flow regulation", "structural integrity"]

abstract: Systems and methods are provided in which a speaker profile-data inquiry is transmitted to a mobile device associated with a first speaker. In response to the speaker-profile-data inquiry, speaker profile data associated with the first speaker is received. Audio data representing a voice input is received. The first speaker is identified as providing the voice input, the identification being based on a comparison of characteristics of the received audio data with the speaker profile data of a plurality of speakers for whom speaker profile data is stored. An instruction, which includes a speaker-relative signifier, is determined from the received audio data, and determining the instruction includes determining a referent of the speaker-relative signifier based on the first speaker profile data. An action indicated by the instruction is performed.
problem: Accurately identifying a speaker and interpreting speaker-relative commands (e.g., 'my device') in voice-based systems without ambiguity.
constraint: Balancing real-time speaker identification accuracy with computational efficiency and minimizing false positives in multi-speaker environments.
mechanism: Profile data is dynamically retrieved and compared against incoming signal characteristics to identify the source. The identified profile is then used to resolve relative references by determining their referent based on stored context, enabling personalized command execution.
mechanism_raw: Speaker profile data is dynamically retrieved and compared against incoming audio characteristics to identify the speaker. The speaker's profile is then used to resolve speaker-relative signifiers (e.g., 'my') by determining their referent based on the speaker's stored context, enabling personalized command execution.

abstract: A blade outer air seal assembly includes a blade outer air seal that has a plurality of segments that extend circumferentially about an axis and are mounted in a carrier. At least two of the plurality of segments have a first wall and a second wall circumferentially spaced from one another and a base portion that extends from the first wall to the second wall. The base portion extends circumferentially outward past the first and second walls to form first and second sealing surfaces. An intersegment seal has a curved surface. The curved surface is engaged with the first and second sealing surfaces between the at least two segments.
problem: Maintaining a dynamic seal between adjacent segments of a rotating or thermally expanding component (e.g., turbine blades) while allowing relative movement.
constraint: Ensuring the seal remains effective under high temperatures and mechanical stress without impeding segment mobility or requiring frequent maintenance.
mechanism: Adjacent segments with spaced walls and extending base portions form sealing surfaces. A flexible intersegment seal engages these surfaces, accommodating relative motion and thermal expansion while maintaining continuous contact to prevent leakage.
mechanism_raw: Segments with circumferentially spaced walls and outward-extending base portions create sealing surfaces. A curved intersegment seal engages these surfaces, accommodating relative motion and thermal expansion while maintaining continuous contact to prevent leakage.

abstract: An apparatus for encoding audio information is provided. The apparatus for encoding audio information includes a selector for selecting a comfort noise generation mode from two or more comfort noise generation modes depending on a background noise characteristic of an audio input signal, and an encoding unit for encoding the audio information, wherein the audio information includes mode information indicating the selected comfort noise generation mode.
problem: Efficiently encoding audio signals with varying background noise characteristics while preserving perceptual quality and minimizing bandwidth usage.
constraint: Balancing noise synthesis quality with computational complexity and bandwidth constraints, particularly in low-bitrate or real-time communication systems.
mechanism: A selector dynamically chooses a noise synthesis mode based on real-time analysis of the input signal's background noise. The selected mode is encoded with the audio data, allowing the decoder to synthesize appropriate background noise during silent or low-energy segments.
mechanism_raw: A selector dynamically chooses a comfort noise generation mode based on real-time analysis of the input signal's background noise. The selected mode is encoded alongside the audio data, allowing the decoder to synthesize appropriate background noise during silent or low-energy segments.

abstract: There is provided a projection apparatus which includes a projection unit configured to project an image, an acquisition device configured to acquire a distance between an apparatus main body and a projection target, a ranging device including a ranging axis which is substantially parallel to a projection optical axis of the projection unit, and a controller configured to control a projection operation, based on a result of ranging of the ranging device with reference to the distance acquired by the acquisition device.
problem: Automatically adjusting projection parameters (e.g., focus, brightness, keystone correction) based on the distance between the projector and the projection surface.
constraint: Achieving accurate distance measurement and projection adjustment without introducing latency or requiring manual recalibration in dynamic environments.
mechanism: A distance measurement device, aligned with the projection axis, measures the distance to the target surface. A controller uses this measurement, combined with pre-acquired data, to dynamically adjust projection parameters (e.g., focus, scaling) to optimize image quality.
mechanism_raw: A ranging device, aligned parallel to the projection axis, measures the distance to the target surface. A controller uses this measurement, combined with pre-acquired distance data, to dynamically adjust the projection operation (e.g., lens focus, image scaling) to optimize image quality.

abstract: The present invention makes a rotary movement smooth, the rotary movement allowing direct detection of the movement of an output member of a rotary clamp. In a clamp, an output member is accommodated in a cylinder hole. A first valve chamber, to which compressed air is supplied, is provided between a lower wall of a housing and the output member. A second valve chamber is a hollowed out portion of the output member so as to be provided open toward the first valve chamber. A valve rod is inserted into the second valve chamber from the lower wall. A valve rod passage that allows the second valve chamber to communicate with outside air is provided in the valve rod, and a seal section is provided in a peripheral gap where the valve rod and the second valve chamber move relatively to one another. The gap is formed so that, as the valve rod and the second valve chamber are in relative movement, there is a region which is sealed by the seal section against movement of the compressed air through the gap between the valve rod and the second seal chamber and the there is a region which is open from the seal.
problem: Enabling smooth rotary motion of an output member in a pneumatic clamp while allowing direct detection of its position or movement.
constraint: Maintaining a reliable seal between the valve rod and output member despite continuous relative motion, while ensuring sufficient airflow for responsive control.
mechanism: A valve rod with a peripheral passage and seal section is inserted into a hollow output member. Relative motion between the rod and member creates alternating sealed and open regions in the gap, regulating airflow to control pressure differentials and enable smooth motion while permitting position sensing via pressure or flow changes.
mechanism_raw: A valve rod with a peripheral passage and seal section is inserted into a hollowed output member. As the rod and member move relatively, the seal creates alternating sealed and open regions in the gap, regulating airflow to control pressure differentials and enable smooth motion while permitting position sensing via pressure or flow changes.

abstract: A display system displays the progress of processing in an additive manufacturing device.
