The additive manufacturing device manufactures an object with a three-dimensional shape by processing of adding material on the basis of CAD data that is design data. The display system includes an obtaining unit to obtain position data that indicates the present position of a processing point where the processing is performed. The display system includes a display unit to display a trace of the processing point superimposed over the three-dimensional shape based on the design data.
problem: Visualizing the real-time progress of an additive manufacturing process relative to the intended 3D object geometry.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between the processing point's position data and the displayed trace without disrupting the manufacturing process.
mechanism: Capture real-time positional coordinates of an active processing element and continuously render a trajectory trace of those coordinates onto a digital representation of a target structure, enabling concurrent visual comparison between the executed path and the intended geometry.
mechanism_raw: Obtaining live position data of the processing point and dynamically overlaying its trace onto the CAD-derived 3D model, enabling direct comparison between actual and intended states.

abstract: An electronic device that obtains a set of remote-control commands is described. During operation, the electronic device may receive an image associated with a second electronic device, where a brand and a model of the second electronic device are initially unknown to the electronic device. Then, the electronic device may perform image analysis on the image to determine at least the brand of the second electronic device. Moreover, the electronic device may access, based at least in part on the determined brand, the set of remote-control commands that are associated with the second electronic device. Next, the electronic device may store the set of remote-control commands in memory. Subsequently, when the electronic device receives user-interface activity information associated with a portable electronic device that specifies selection of the second electronic device, the electronic device may provide the set of remote-control commands to the second electronic device.
problem: Automatically identifying an unknown remote-controlled device's brand/model and retrieving its specific command set without prior configuration.
constraint: Accuracy of image-based brand identification and availability of a comprehensive command database for all possible brands/models.
mechanism: Acquire a visual representation of an unknown device, apply pattern recognition to infer its identity from the representation, and use the inferred identity to select a corresponding pre-stored operational instruction set from a structured collection.
mechanism_raw: Analyzing an image of the device to infer its brand via pattern recognition, then using the brand to index into a database of pre-stored command sets for that brand.

abstract: Methods and devices including implantable micro-sensors used to detect tissue-dissolved inert gas and to detect microbubble formation to avoid Caisson disease are described. The disclosed methods and devices are based on measuring the refractive index changes in hydrophobic liquids after absorbing an inert gas such as nitrogen. The changes in the refractive index are based on implementing one of an interferometry, optical microcavity resonance shift, a photonic crystal resonance, a beam deflection, a resonance tuning or detuning, an amplitude change, or an intensity change method.
problem: Detecting dissolved inert gas concentrations and microbubble formation in biological tissue to prevent decompression sickness (Caisson disease).
constraint: Biocompatibility of the sensor materials and sensitivity of the optical detection method to small refractive index shifts in a dynamic biological environment.
mechanism: Monitor refractive index variations within a fluid medium caused by dissolved gas uptake, and convert those variations into measurable optical signals using light-based detection techniques, thereby determining gas concentration and bubble formation in a biological context.
mechanism_raw: Measuring refractive index changes in a hydrophobic liquid medium caused by inert gas absorption, using optical methods (e.g., interferometry, photonic resonance) to transduce gas concentration into detectable signals.
residual_terms: ["refractive index", "fluid medium", "dissolved gas", "optical signals", "light-based detection", "biological context"]

abstract: A layboy includes an upper belt section with a plurality of transversely spaced upper belts that extend in a longitudinal direction such that bottom portions of the upper belts lie in a first plane that defines an upper boundary of a transport path through the layboy and a lower belt section having a plurality of transversely spaced lower belts that extend in the longitudinal direction such that top portions of the lower belts lie in a second plane that defines an upper boundary of the transport path. The bottom portion of one of the top belts and/or the top portion of one of the bottom belts extends away from the transport path to define a gap in the transport path at which scrap moving through the layboy can fall out of the transport path.
problem: Removing scrap material from a continuous transport path in a conveyor system without interrupting the flow of non-scrap material.
constraint: Balancing the size and placement of gaps to ensure scrap removal without compromising the structural integrity or throughput of the transport path.
mechanism: Arrange two opposing transport surfaces so that their adjacent paths form a gap at a specific location, causing unwanted material to exit the transport path at that location while continuous support is maintained for desired material elsewhere along the path.
mechanism_raw: Positioning upper and lower belt sections such that their bottom/top portions create localized gaps in the transport path, allowing scrap to fall out while maintaining support for non-scrap material.

abstract: The present invention provides a changeable linear speed reduction clutch, which is formed by connecting a changeable linear speed double-layer planetary gear train and a brake, and is transmission machinery with functions of both a speed reducer and a clutch. A planetary carrier of the changeable linear speed double-layer planetary gear train is used as an input end, one central gear as an output end, the other central gear as a braking end, and the braking end is directly connected to the brake; and the changeable linear speed double-layer planetary gear train adopts one of two types of planetary gear trains. The brake at least has two states, that is, braking and non-braking states, wherein the braking state of the brake is equivalent to an engaged state of the clutch, and the non-braking state of the brake is equivalent to a disengaged state of the clutch. The method of setting the changeable linear speed double-layer planetary gear train, and the application method of the present invention are provided herein. Compared with a device in which a multi-stage speed reducer and a clutch are arranged independently, the changeable linear speed reduction clutch in the present invention is small and light and has a simple structure.
problem: Integrating speed reduction and clutching functions into a single compact mechanical system to replace separate multi-stage reducers and clutches.
constraint: Achieving mechanical simplicity and compactness while maintaining torque capacity and precise control over both speed reduction and clutch engagement states.
mechanism: Employ a multi-stage gear assembly with a shared central component acting as output and a selectively engageable braking element connected to another central component, where actuation of the braking element toggles between speed-reducing operation and disengaged (clutch) states.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual-layer planetary gear train where one central gear serves as output, another as a braking end connected to a brake, and the planetary carrier as input. Brake engagement/disengagement directly controls clutch state while the gear train provides variable speed reduction.
residual_terms: ["multi-stage gear assembly", "central component", "output", "braking element", "speed-reducing operation", "disengaged state", "clutch state"]

abstract: An actuation apparatus for actuating a component of a switchable valve train device of an internal combustion engine includes: a support body for mounting on a cylinder head cover of the internal combustion engine; an actuation lever mounted to the support body for pivotal movement of the actuation lever between a first position for actuation of the component and a second position for allowing de-actuation of the component; and a biasing means for urging the actuation lever from the second position towards the first position. In use, the biasing means becomes biased when an actuation source causes the actuation lever to pivot to the second position. When the actuation source attempts to actuate the component when the component is non-actuatable, the biasing means causes the actuation lever to pivot from the second position to the first position, thereby to actuate the component when the component becomes actuatable again.
problem: Managing actuation of a switchable valve train component when the component is temporarily non-actuatable, preventing unintended engagement or mechanical stress.
constraint: The biasing force must be sufficient to reset the lever without interfering with normal actuation or causing excessive wear during repeated cycles.
mechanism: A resilient element stores potential energy when an external force moves a lever to a secondary position. When the external force becomes unavailable, the stored energy in the resilient element automatically returns the lever to its primary position, ensuring the lever is actuated only when the external force is available.
mechanism_raw: A biasing means stores energy when an external actuation source moves the lever to a secondary position. When the component becomes non-actuatable, the stored energy in the biasing means automatically resets the lever to its primary position, ensuring the component is actuated only when it is ready.

abstract: A heat exchanger includes a first collecting pipe, a second collecting pipe and a number of flat tubes connected between the first collecting pipe and the second collecting pipe. The first collecting pipe includes a first upper main board and a first lower main board. A first channel and a second channel are formed between the first upper main board and the first lower main board. The second collecting pipe includes a third channel and a fourth channel. The third channel is communicated with the first channel through a row of the flat tubes. The fourth channel is communicated with the second channel through another row of the flat tubes.
reason: The patent describes a structural arrangement of channels and tubes in a heat exchanger but does not present a novel causal mechanism beyond standard heat exchanger design principles. The problem (efficient heat transfer) is addressed through physical layout rather than a transferable functional mechanism.

abstract: A catadioptric high-aperture optical element includes a substrate made of a transparent material; and a lens formed on the substrate. The lens includes, plural refractive features formed on a central portion of the lens, and plural reflective features formed on a ring portion of the lens. The plural refractive features are shaped to refract light incoming from the substrate and the plural reflective features are shaped to achieve total internal reflections with the light incoming from the substrate.
problem: Creating a high-aperture optical element that efficiently directs light using a combination of refraction and reflection in a single substrate.
constraint: The refractive and reflective features must be shaped and positioned to balance light bending and reflection without causing unwanted scattering or loss of optical efficiency.
mechanism: A first optical feature on the central portion of a light-transmissive substrate bends incoming light through refraction, while a second optical feature on the peripheral portion redirects light through total internal reflection. This hybrid approach allows precise control of light paths within a compact structure.
mechanism_raw: Refractive features on the central portion of the lens bend incoming light, while reflective features on the ring portion use total internal reflection to redirect light. This hybrid approach allows precise control of light paths within a compact structure.

abstract: An auto-rack bridge plate locking assembly including a support bracket, a guide tube, a slidable locking pin partially positioned in the guide tube, a handle assembly removably attachable to the locking pin, a fixed pivot pin partially positioned in the guide tube, and a spring positioned in the guide tube between the pivot pin and the locking pin. An auto-rack railroad car bridge plate may include a plate configured to extend from one auto-rack railroad car to an adjacent auto-rack railroad car with the locking assembly connected to the plate and configured to pivotally attach the plate to one of the auto-rack rail road cars.
problem: Securing a bridge plate between adjacent auto-rack railroad cars while allowing manual release and automatic re-engagement under vibration.
constraint: The spring force must be strong enough to maintain engagement under dynamic loads but weak enough to allow manual override without excessive effort.
mechanism: A resilient element positioned between a fixed pivot and a slidable locking member provides a restoring force that maintains engagement of the locking member. A removable manual interface allows disengagement, while the resilient element ensures automatic re-engagement when the manual interface is removed.
mechanism_raw: A spring positioned between a fixed pivot pin and a slidable locking pin provides a restoring force that keeps the locking pin engaged. A removable handle allows manual disengagement, while the spring ensures automatic re-engagement when the handle is removed.

abstract: An apparatus comprises data processing circuitry to perform data processing operations in response to a sequence of instructions, where the sequence of instructions comprises branch instructions. Trace generating circuitry generates a trace stream of trace items indicative of the data processing operations. The trace generating circuitry is responsive to one or more not-taken branch instructions followed by a taken branch instruction in the sequence of instructions to: include at least one not-taken trace item corresponding to the one or more not-taken branch instructions followed by a taken trace item in the trace stream when a current status condition of the apparatus is met, and to include a source address associated with the taken branch instruction in the trace stream when the current status condition of the apparatus is not met. A hybrid approach between tracing not-taken branch instructions and tracing a source address associated with the taken branch instruction is thus provided.
problem: Efficiently generating a trace stream for data processing operations involving branch instructions without excessive data overhead or loss of critical execution context.
constraint: The status condition must accurately reflect the execution context to balance trace completeness with data size, avoiding both information loss and unnecessary verbosity.
mechanism: Trace generation circuitry conditionally includes either not-taken branch trace items or source addresses of taken branches based on a status condition. When the status condition is met, not-taken branches are traced; when not met, the source address of the taken branch is traced instead, reducing redundant data.
mechanism_raw: Trace generation circuitry conditionally includes not-taken branch trace items or source addresses of taken branches based on a status condition. When the status condition is met, not-taken branches are traced; when not met, the source address of the taken branch is traced instead, reducing redundant data.
residual_terms: ["trace generation circuitry", "status condition", "not-taken branch trace items", "source address of taken branches", "taken branch"]

abstract: The present disclosure provides an eye-protection mode processing method, device, terminal, and medium in a fingerprint recognition mode. The method can include acquiring eye-protection parameters of each one of current constituent windows in the case of that a mobile terminal is in a fingerprint recognition mode, and, if the eye-protection parameters of the constituent window are preset values and the constituent window is a constituent window corresponding to fingerprint recognition, then setting the eye-protection parameters of the constituent window corresponding to the fingerprint recognition as a value of zero.
problem: Balancing eye protection with the need for a fingerprint sensor to function through a display during fingerprint recognition mode.
constraint: Maintaining eye protection in non-fingerprint regions while ensuring the fingerprint sensor receives unobstructed optical or capacitive input.
mechanism: Selectively disabling a display's light output in a region corresponding to an optical or capacitive sensor window while maintaining ambient protection settings in surrounding regions, enabling the sensor to receive unobstructed input during its active mode.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting display parameters (e.g., blue light emission) to zero in the specific window corresponding to the fingerprint sensor area, while maintaining eye-protection settings in other windows. This allows the fingerprint sensor to operate without interference from the display's light output.

abstract: A first wafer of semiconductor material has a surface. A second wafer of semiconductor material includes a substrate and a structural layer on the substrate. The structural layer integrates a detector device for detecting electromagnetic radiation. The structural layer of the second wafer is coupled to the surface of the first wafer. The substrate of the second wafer is shaped to form a stator, a rotor, and a mobile mass of a micromirror. The stator and the rotor form an assembly for capacitively driving the mobile mass.
problem: Integrating a radiation detector with a micromirror actuator on a single semiconductor structure without compromising either component's functionality.
constraint: Achieving precise mechanical coupling between the stator/rotor/mobile mass assembly and the detector layer without introducing parasitic interference or structural conflicts.
mechanism: Forming mechanical and sensing structures from a shared substrate by shaping one portion to provide actuation components and integrating a detector layer on the same substrate, allowing independent mechanical and electrical functions to coexist without structural interference.
mechanism_raw: Shaping the substrate of the second wafer to form the stator, rotor, and mobile mass of the micromirror, while the structural layer on the same substrate integrates the detector device. This allows the detector and actuator to share a common substrate while maintaining independent mechanical and electrical functions.

abstract: The present invention includes improvements to a device with bristles that makes it possible to perform oral hygiene tasks to remove quickly impurities in the oral cavity, in particular when the user is travelling and does not carry a toothbrush and, due to time constraints, requires quick and effective cleaning. The cleaning device may also include luffa sponges, water-soluble films, spheres with toothpaste or channels that provide flexibility to a membrane which, when bending, generates a vacuum and is placed on the tongue in order to be used as a toothbrush handle. The device provides a better fitting and handling in the mouth of a user, since it avoids the generation of vacuum when actuated, and also has a membrane surrounded by a cylindrical section that allows its handling since it adapts to the tongue.
problem: Enabling quick and effective oral cleaning without a traditional toothbrush, particularly in constrained environments like travel.
constraint: Avoiding vacuum generation during actuation to prevent discomfort, while ensuring the device conforms to oral anatomy for effective cleaning.
mechanism: Using a deformable membrane enclosed by a compliant structure that adapts to anatomical contours, where bending the membrane generates a temporary pressure differential for handling while surface features deliver cleaning action to target areas.
mechanism_raw: Using a flexible membrane surrounded by a cylindrical section that adapts to the tongue's shape, with channels or luffa sponges providing structural compliance. When bent, the membrane generates a vacuum for handling, while bristles or films deliver cleaning agents directly to teeth surfaces.

abstract: Disclosed is a method for treating a grained material. A nonlimiting example of the method includes the operations of providing a workpiece having grains, exasperating a surface of the workpiece to open the grains, applying at least one coat of a base paint to the exasperated surface, applying at least one layer of clear coat on the base paint, applying at least one of a glaze and a paint on the clear coat, and surface treating to reveal grains of the workpiece. Disclosed also are items of furniture and sheet materials treated by the aforementioned process.
problem: Enhancing the visual appearance of grained materials (e.g., wood) by selectively exposing underlying grain patterns through layered surface treatments.
constraint: Balancing the thickness and composition of each layer to ensure selective removal reveals grains without damaging the underlying material or obscuring the desired aesthetic effect.
mechanism: Applying successive layers of material to a textured surface and then selectively removing outer layers through surface treatment to expose underlying patterns, with layer thickness and composition controlling the degree and precision of exposure.
mechanism_raw: Exasperating the material surface to open grains, applying base paint, clear coat, and glaze in sequence, then surface treating (e.g., sanding) to selectively remove top layers and reveal the grains. The layered approach ensures controlled exposure of the grain structure while protecting the material.

abstract: Reverse flow reactor (RFR) apparatuses exhibiting asymmetric feed profiles and improved purge mode efficiency, and methods of using same to transform a hydrocarbon feed into a pyrolysed hydrocarbon product are disclosed. The RFR apparatus includes an RFR body with a reaction zone having at least one bed. The RFR body has a central vertical axis and flanked by first and second void spaces. The method utilizes at least two oxygen-containing feeds, a combustion fuel feed, a purge feed, and a hydrocarbon pyrolysis feed. The RFR apparatus can cycle between an exothermic heating mode (heated to ≥700° C. while maintaining a pressure drop across the reaction zone of ≤100 kPag), a purge mode (purging oxygen using <6 bed volumes of purge gas to achieve a residual oxygen level of ≤20 ppm while maintaining a pressure drop of ≤35 kPag), and an endothermic pyrolysis mode (feeding pyrolysis hydrocarbons through the reaction zone to form pyrolysis products, while maintaining a pressure drop across the reaction zone of ≤70 kPag).
problem: Improving the efficiency of hydrocarbon pyrolysis in a reverse flow reactor while managing oxygen levels and pressure drops during cyclic operation.
constraint: Maintaining low pressure drops across all modes while achieving rapid oxygen purging and efficient heat transfer during exothermic and endothermic phases.
mechanism: Cycling a reactor through distinct operational phases—exothermic heating, purge, and endothermic processing—each with controlled thresholds for temperature, gas volume, oxygen concentration, and pressure drop, using asymmetric input profiles to optimize efficiency across all phases.
mechanism_raw: Cycling the reactor between exothermic heating (≥700°C, ≤100 kPag pressure drop), purge mode (<6 bed volumes of purge gas to achieve ≤20 ppm oxygen, ≤35 kPag pressure drop), and endothermic pyrolysis (≤70 kPag pressure drop). Asymmetric feed profiles and controlled oxygen management optimize each phase's efficiency.
residual_terms: ["reactor", "exothermic heating", "purge mode", "endothermic pyrolysis", "oxygen concentration", "pressure drop", "bed volumes", "purge gas"]

abstract: Some embodiments relate to a vibration sensor. The vibration sensor comprises: a sensor base to couple to a vibration source; a piezoelectric transducer coupled on a first side of the transducer to the sensor base; at least one conductor coupled to the piezoelectric transducer; and a seismic weight positioned on a second side of the piezoelectric transducer; wherein the sensor base, the piezoelectric transducer and the seismic weight are aligned along an axis and arranged so that relative movement between the sensor base and the seismic weight arising from the vibration source causes a current to be generated in the piezoelectric transducer and an output signal corresponding to the generated current is detectable on the at least one conductor.
problem: Detecting vibrations and converting them into a measurable electrical signal without requiring external power.
constraint: The alignment of components along a single axis ensures directional sensitivity and efficient energy transfer, but limits detection to vibrations along that axis.
mechanism: A deformable transducer is positioned between a fixed base and a movable mass aligned along a single axis. Relative motion between the base and mass caused by vibrations applies mechanical strain to the transducer, generating an electrical signal proportional to the strain. Conductors extract the signal from the transducer.
mechanism_raw: A piezoelectric transducer is positioned between a fixed sensor base and a seismic weight aligned along an axis. Relative movement between the base and weight caused by vibrations deforms the piezoelectric material, generating a current proportional to the mechanical strain. The output signal is extracted via conductors coupled to the transducer.

abstract: An electronic cigarette includes a microprocessor, a battery module and a heating element. The battery module is electrically connected to the heating element and supplies power to the heating element with a first output parameter. The electronic cigarette further includes a sensing module, connected to the microprocessor and disposed in a smoke outlet passage of the electronic cigarette, for detecting the concentration of an analyte and sending it to the microprocessor. The microprocessor stores a preset threshold, the microprocessor receives the concentration of the analyte detected by the sensing module, and further determines the relationship between the concentration of the analyte and the preset threshold. When the concentration of the analyte is higher than or equal to the preset threshold, the microprocessor controls the battery module to supply power to the heating element with a second output parameter, wherein the second output parameter is smaller than the first output parameter.
problem: Maintaining safe or optimal operating conditions in a heating device by dynamically adjusting power output based on real-time analyte concentration.
constraint: The system relies on a fixed threshold and binary adjustment (first vs. second output parameter), which may not account for gradual or non-linear relationships between analyte levels and desired power adjustments.
mechanism: A sensor detects a parameter in a process stream and transmits data to a controller. The controller compares the parameter to a preset threshold and adjusts an output parameter of a power source when the threshold is exceeded, thereby modifying the system's operational state.
mechanism_raw: A sensing module detects analyte concentration in the vapor stream and sends data to a microprocessor. The microprocessor compares the concentration to a preset threshold and reduces the battery module's output parameter (e.g., voltage/current) when the threshold is exceeded, thereby lowering heating power.

abstract: An process for the on-line quenching of seamless steel tube using residual heat, a method for manufacturing a seamless steel tube, and a seamless steel tube. The process for the on-line quenching of a seamless steel tube comprises the following steps: when the temperature of a tube is higher than Ar3, evenly spraying water along a circumferential direction of the tube so as to continuously cool the tube to be not higher than T° C., the cooling rate being controlled to be E1° C./s to E2° C./s to obtain a microstructure with martensite as the main composition, wherein T=Ms−95° C., Ms represents the martensitic phase transition temperature, E1=20×(0.5−C)+15×(3.2−Mn)−8×Cr−28×Mo−4×Ni−2800×B, and E2=96×(0.45−C)+12×(4.6−Mn), and the C, Mn, Cr, Ni, B and Mo in the equations each represents the mass percentages of corresponding elements in the seamless steel tube.
problem: Controlling the microstructure of a steel tube during on-line quenching to achieve desired mechanical properties without interrupting production.
constraint: The cooling rate must balance between achieving martensite formation and avoiding thermal stresses or cracking, which depends on precise control of spray distribution and composition-dependent formulas.
mechanism: A coolant is applied to a workpiece at a rate determined by composition-dependent formulas. The cooling rate is constrained between two thresholds derived from the material's composition, ensuring the temperature drops to a target value to produce a specified microstructure.
mechanism_raw: Water is sprayed circumferentially at a cooling rate calculated using formulas dependent on the steel's elemental composition (C, Mn, Cr, etc.). The cooling rate is constrained between E1 and E2 values derived from the composition, ensuring the temperature drops to T = Ms - 95°C to produce a martensitic microstructure.

abstract: The livestock halter may comprise a headstall, a noseband, a throatlatch, a connecting strap, a left cheekpiece, a right cheekpiece, coupled via a plurality of connecting rings to form headgear adapted to be worn by livestock. As non-limiting examples, the livestock may be equines or camelids. The headstall may be adapted to be detachable at one end for donning the halter such that the headstall is not forced over ears of the livestock. A crown buckle for adjusting the fit of the headstall may be located on the right side of the halter such the crown buckle does not interfere with the operation of a closure snap. A tie ring for connecting a lead rope may be a tie-down ring instead of a traditional ring and triangle for increased strength and easier sliding.
problem: Creating a livestock halter that can be quickly and safely applied without forcing it over the animal's ears or interfering with closure mechanisms.
constraint: The design must balance adjustability (via buckles and detachable components) with structural integrity and non-interference between functional elements (e.g., buckle and snap).
mechanism: A detachable component allows positioning around an object without sliding over sensitive regions. Functional elements are arranged to avoid mutual interference, with adjustable fasteners and reinforced connection points for structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A detachable headstall allows the halter to be opened and positioned around the animal's head without sliding over the ears. A crown buckle is placed on the right side to avoid interfering with a closure snap, and a tie-down ring replaces traditional rings for increased strength and sliding ease.

abstract: A reactor system may comprise a housing; and a condensation catalyst layer within the housing comprising a condensation catalyst comprised of at least one of a base-substituted zeolite, a stannous salt, or a phosphonitrile chloride. The condensation catalyst layer may be configured to catalyze a condensation reaction of a plurality of silane diols in water flowing through the housing into a plurality of siloxanes.
problem: Efficiently catalyzing the condensation of silane diols into siloxanes in an aqueous environment within a continuous flow reactor.
constraint: The catalyst composition must remain stable and active in aqueous conditions while being compatible with continuous flow dynamics to avoid clogging or deactivation.
mechanism: A catalytic layer provides active sites within a flow path. As a fluid passes through, the catalyst facilitates molecular rearrangement and bond formation between reactants, enabling a condensation reaction to produce a target product.
mechanism_raw: A catalyst layer containing base-substituted zeolites, stannous salts, or phosphonitrile chlorides is positioned within a reactor housing. As water flows through, the catalyst facilitates the condensation reaction of silane diols into siloxanes by providing active sites for molecular rearrangement and bond formation.

abstract: The invention discloses a special equipment and a method for surface microcrystallization of cementitious materials. The specialized equipment includes a vibrator, a vibration signal generator, a power amplifier and a vibration transmitting body. A signal output terminal of the vibration signal generator is connected to a signal input terminal of the power amplifier, a signal output terminal of the power amplifier is connected to a signal input terminal of the vibrator, the vibrator is connected to the vibration transmitting body, and the vibration transmitting body is to be in contact with the cement product after initial setting. The surface microcrystallization method for cement product: after the casting and before the final setting of the cement product, vibration is applied to its outer or inner surface, the vibration frequency is greater than or equal to 1 KHz, and the vibration time is greater than or equal to 5 minutes. The surface layer of the cement product prepared by the present invention forms a structured layer with a certain thickness, high density, low permeability and relatively uniform surface coverage of granular crystal or gel phase, so that the cement product has excellent anti-aging performance.
problem: Improving surface density, permeability, and crystallization uniformity in cementitious materials to enhance anti-aging performance.
constraint: Vibration must be applied within a narrow time window (before final setting) and with specific frequency/duration parameters to avoid disrupting the material's structural integrity while maximizing crystallization.
mechanism: Applying controlled mechanical agitation within a critical processing window to induce structured phase transformation, creating a surface layer with enhanced physical properties through regulated nucleation and gel formation.
mechanism_raw: Applying high-frequency vibration (>=1kHz) during the critical post-casting, pre-final-setting phase to induce controlled microcrystallization and gel phase formation, creating a structured surface layer with enhanced physical properties.

abstract: An acid phosphatase mutant, and method for preparing nicotinamide riboside by same. The mutant is a protein of the following (a), (b) or (c): (a) a protein, having an amino acid sequence shown in SEQ ID NO: 3; (b) a protein, derived from (a), having catalytic activity higher than an acid phosphatase parent having an amino acid sequence shown in SEQ ID NO: 2, obtained by substituting, deleting or adding several amino acids in the amino acid sequence shown in SEQ ID NO: 3, using nicotinamide mononucleotide as a substrate; (c) a protein, having catalytic activity higher than the acid phosphatase shown in SEQ ID NO: 2, having 90% or more homology with the amino acid sequence of the protein defined by (a) or (b), and using nicotinamide mononucleotide as a substrate. It is used to prepare nicotinamide riboside and the conversion rate can be 99%.
problem: Increasing catalytic efficiency of acid phosphatase for high-yield production of nicotinamide riboside from nicotinamide mononucleotide.
constraint: Modifications must maintain sufficient homology (>=90%) to the parent enzyme to retain structural stability and catalytic function while achieving higher activity.
mechanism: Modifying a biocatalyst's structural framework through targeted molecular alterations to enhance reaction efficiency while preserving substrate recognition and functional stability.
mechanism_raw: Engineering enzyme variants through targeted amino acid substitutions, deletions, or additions to enhance catalytic activity while preserving substrate specificity, enabling near-complete conversion rates.

abstract: The invention provides a gas turbine combustor having structural reliability against vibration of fuel nozzles caused by fluid force and high environmental performance by uniform combustion in a combustion chamber. The gas turbine combustor comprises a fuel nozzle configured to inject fuel, and a fuel nozzle plate including a hole section into which an insertion section located in a root part of the fuel nozzle is inserted. The fuel nozzle includes a male screw section at least on an outer circumferential surface of a downstream portion viewed from a flowing direction of the fuel in the insertion section. The fuel nozzle plate includes a female screw section in the hole section. The female screw section screws with the male screw section. The fuel nozzle includes the insertion section. An upstream end portion of the insertion section is metallurgically joined to an upstream end portion of the fuel nozzle plate.
problem: Ensuring structural reliability of fuel nozzles in gas turbine combustors under high-vibration conditions while maintaining uniform combustion.
constraint: The threaded connection must balance mechanical strength and thermal expansion compatibility, while the metallurgical joint must avoid introducing stress concentrations that could propagate cracks.
mechanism: Combining a precision mechanical interface with a secondary joining method to achieve alignment, vibration resistance, and structural integrity under dynamic loading conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using a threaded male/female screw interface between the nozzle and mounting plate to provide precise alignment and vibration resistance, combined with metallurgical joining at the upstream end to prevent loosening or fatigue failure.

abstract: A method of making a portion of a microfluidic channel includes lithographically patterning a first pattern into a first layer of photoresist disposed on a substrate, the first pattern representative of morphology of a reservoir rock; etching the first pattern into the substrate to form a patterned substrate; disposing a second layer of photoresist onto the patterned substrate; lithographically patterning a second pattern into the second layer of photoresist to reveal portions of the patterned substrate; and depositing calcite onto the exposed portions of the patterned substrate.
problem: Creating microfluidic channels that replicate reservoir rock morphology for accurate fluid flow simulation in research or industrial applications.
constraint: The lithography and etching steps must achieve sub-micron precision to replicate complex pore geometries, while calcite deposition must selectively coat exposed regions without obscuring critical structural details.
mechanism: Transferring complex topographical patterns into a substrate via precision fabrication, followed by selective material deposition to create durable, chemically stable microstructures that replicate natural porous media.
mechanism_raw: Combining lithographic patterning and etching to transfer rock-like topographies into a substrate, followed by selective calcite deposition to form durable, chemically stable microstructures that mimic natural porous media.

abstract: Systems and methods of storing phase history, and enhancing and restoring phase accuracy for a embedded Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver include storing a phase history of the GNSS receiver output; determining an expected value of phase of the GNSS receiver output based on the phase history; and, responsive to a degradation of the GNSS receiver output, adjusting the GNSS receiver output utilizing the expected value of phase. The systems and method can further include, responsive to degradation being a loss of the GNSS receiver output, utilizing a holdover output from a physical frequency reference and with a phase adjusted based on the expected value of phase, and, responsive to the variation, utilizing the phase history to re-generate the GNSS receiver output for performance enhancement.
problem: Maintaining phase accuracy and operational continuity in GNSS receivers during signal degradation or loss.
constraint: The system must balance computational latency for real-time phase prediction against the need for high-resolution phase history storage, while ensuring the holdover reference remains stable enough to bridge signal loss periods.
mechanism: Storing historical operational data to predict expected states, using a reference source adjusted by these predictions to sustain accuracy during interruptions, and reconstructing degraded signals via temporal data interpolation.
mechanism_raw: Storing historical phase data to predict expected phase values, then using a holdover frequency reference adjusted by these predictions to sustain output accuracy during outages, and regenerating degraded signals via phase history reconstruction.

abstract: A display device for a machining program has a function of displaying a modal state. The display device includes a program analysis unit that inputs the machining program and that identifies an attention block in the machining program, a modal effective range analysis unit that identifies a modal state that is effective in the attention block and an effective range of the modal state, and a modal effective range display unit that visually displays the effective range of the modal state along with the machining program.
problem: Understanding the effective range of modal states in a machining program to avoid unintended behavior during execution.
constraint: Balancing the granularity of modal state analysis with the need for clear visual representation to avoid overwhelming the user while maintaining accuracy.
mechanism: Analyzing a program to identify critical segments, determining the scope of state transitions within those segments, and visually presenting the transition boundaries alongside the program to clarify operational states.
mechanism_raw: Analyzing the machining program to identify attention blocks, determining the modal state's effective range within those blocks, and visually displaying the range alongside the program to clarify state transitions.

abstract: Method and apparatus for predicting clinical trial eligibility for patients. Embodiments include determining a current value for each of a plurality of attributes of a first patient. Embodiments include identifying a cohort of patients that are clinically similar to the first patient, based on the plurality of attributes. Embodiments include analyzing data associated with the cohort of patients to determine an attribute trend for at least a first attribute the plurality of attributes. Embodiments include generating a predicted value for the first attribute, based on the current value of the first attribute and the attribute trend for the first attribute. Embodiments include identifying a plurality of clinical trials based on the first attribute. Embodiments include generating a probability that the first patient will be eligible for each of the plurality of clinical trials at a future time, based on the predicted value for the first attribute.
problem: Predicting whether a patient will meet eligibility criteria for clinical trials at a future time based on evolving attributes.
constraint: Ensuring the cohort's trends accurately reflect individual patient variability while avoiding overfitting to historical data that may not generalize.
mechanism: Using current attributes to select a similar group, analyzing group trends to project future attribute values, and computing eligibility probabilities based on projected outcomes.
mechanism_raw: Using current patient attributes to identify a clinically similar cohort, analyzing cohort data to determine attribute trends, and projecting future attribute values to calculate eligibility probabilities for trials.

abstract: Quick Release Buckle (QRB) is an automated seatbelt system. QRB utilizes a power source and control unit software incorporated into pre-existing components within the vehicle's transmission or by micro-switch. QRB automatically disengages the seatbelt upon placing the vehicle in “park”, regardless of the ignition setting for law enforcement/military vehicles. While in “park”, an electrical signal energizes a solenoid releasing the buckle. The control unit contains proprietary software that records every engage/disengage of the seatbelt. Electronic records can be downloaded at any time, using an integrated micro-scan disk (SD) module/card. During a collision, the system ceases to record activity, showing electronic proof the seatbelt was engaged/disengaged. Civilian application includes accident investigations, insurance inquiries, and private company regulation compliance. Civilian QRB differs slightly as the transmission must be placed in “park” and the ignition must be in “off” for system operation.
problem: Automatically disengaging a seatbelt in law enforcement/military vehicles when the vehicle is in 'park' to ensure rapid egress while maintaining compliance records.
constraint: Ensuring reliable operation across varying vehicle states (ignition on/off) while maintaining tamper-proof electronic records for compliance and accident investigations.
mechanism: Actuating a release mechanism in response to a specific system state, ensuring operation across varying conditions, and logging all actuation events for compliance tracking.
mechanism_raw: Triggering a solenoid release via a control unit when the vehicle enters 'park', regardless of ignition state, and recording all engage/disengage events electronically for later retrieval.

abstract: Provided are continuous filament-based elongate bodies having improved durability and bending fatigue performance. The elongate bodies are formed from a plurality of fibers where at least one component fiber is a multifilament ultra-high molecular weight polyolefin fiber having a filament intrinsic viscosity (IVf) of from 15 dl/g to about 45 dl/g when measured in decalin at 135° C., wherein said at least one multifilament ultra-high molecular weight polyolefin fiber has a tenacity of at least 32 g/denier, a denier of greater than 800, and a denier per filament of greater than 2.0. The high tenacity combined with high fiber denier and high filament denier (dpf) enhances the cyclic bend over sheave (CBOS) durability when the elongate body is incorporated in a multi-fiber construction such as a rope.
problem: Improving the bending fatigue performance of continuous filament-based elongate bodies (e.g., ropes) under cyclic loading.
constraint: Balancing fiber tenacity, denier, and filament count to optimize structural support and throughput without compromising flexibility or increasing material costs excessively.
mechanism: Combining fibers with specified mechanical properties (tenacity, denier, filament count) to enhance resistance to cyclic bending in multi-fiber constructions.
mechanism_raw: Combining multifilament ultra-high molecular weight polyolefin fibers with high tenacity, high denier, and high filament denier to enhance cyclic bend over sheave (CBOS) durability in multi-fiber constructions.

abstract: A method cleans surfaces in an internal volume of an aircraft component through which a medium flows. The method includes: connecting the internal volume to be cleaned to a steam generator; generating a cleaning steam having a predetermined vapour pressure and temperature by the steam generator; applying the cleaning steam to the surfaces to be cleaned in the internal volume; maintaining the vapour pressure and the temperature within the internal volume for the duration of a predetermined condensation time; generating a pressure drop in the internal volume of the aircraft component, in order to vaporise the portion of the cleaning steam that condensed during the condensation time; and removing the cleaning steam from the internal volume via a discharge device.
problem: Cleaning internal surfaces of aircraft components through which a medium flows, ensuring thorough removal of contaminants without damaging the component.
constraint: Managing steam parameters and pressure changes to ensure complete cleaning while preventing thermal or mechanical damage to the aircraft component during the process.
mechanism: Applying a controlled thermal medium at predetermined pressure and temperature to internal surfaces, maintaining conditions for condensation, then inducing a pressure change to vaporize and remove condensed material.
mechanism_raw: Applying controlled steam at a predetermined vapor pressure and temperature to the internal surfaces, maintaining these conditions for a condensation period, then inducing a pressure drop to vaporize condensed steam and remove it via a discharge device.

abstract: A computer-implemented method of generating scan instructions for forming a product using additive layer manufacture as a series of layers is provided. The method comprises determining a beam acceleration voltage to be used when forming the product; for each hatch area of layers of the product, determining a respective beam current to be used when forming the hatch area and providing a respective beam current value to the hatch area description in the scan pattern instruction file; and for each line of each hatch area, determining a respective beam spot size to be used when scanning the beam along the line and providing a respective beam spot size value to the line description in the scan pattern instruction file, and determining a respective series of beam step sizes and beam step dwell times to be used when scanning the beam along the line, and providing a respective series of beam position values and beam step dwell times to the line description in the scan pattern instruction file thereby defining how the beam is to be scanned along the line. Also provided are a file of scan instructions, an additive layer manufacture apparatus, and a method of forming a product using the additive layer manufacturing apparatus.
problem: Optimizing beam parameters for additive layer manufacturing to ensure precise and efficient formation of complex 3D structures.
constraint: Balancing scanning speed and precision by tailoring beam parameters to specific regions without compromising overall build quality or throughput.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting energy delivery parameters based on the geometric characteristics of each region in the layers, enabling localized control of energy intensity during scanning to balance speed and precision.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically adjusting beam acceleration voltage, current, spot size, and step dwell times based on the geometric characteristics of each hatch area and line in the product's layers, enabling localized control of energy delivery during scanning.

abstract: A vehicle includes an electrified propulsion system powered by a traction battery. The vehicle also includes an electrical distribution system (EDS) to pass current to and from the traction battery. The EDS is provided with at least one flexible electrical distribution component (FEDC) including a plurality of individual conductor paths. At least one of the individual conductor paths defines a typical width and a reduced width narrowed portion sized to operate as a fuse and thereby break an electrical circuit of the at least one individual conductor path in response to heat generated from conducting an electrical current greater than a predetermined threshold.
problem: Protecting electrical circuits in flexible distribution systems from overcurrent damage while maintaining normal operation under standard conditions.
constraint: Ensuring the fuse segment triggers only at predefined current thresholds while maintaining flexibility and conductivity under normal operating conditions.
mechanism: A conductor segment designed to fail when current exceeds a predefined threshold, breaking the circuit without affecting adjacent paths through localized thermal failure.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a narrowed conductor path segment designed to act as a fuse, where heat generated by excessive current causes localized failure, breaking the circuit without affecting adjacent paths.

abstract: The invention belongs to the field of vehicles, and particularly relates to a mobile cabin, a rail, and a three-dimensional rail transit system. The mobile cabin includes a mobile cabin chassis, wherein a transparent housing is arranged on the mobile cabin chassis, two or more seats are arranged in a cavity defined by the transparent housing and the mobile cabin chassis, front rubber steering wheels and a rubber driving wheel are arranged on the mobile cabin chassis, the front rubber steering wheels are guide wheels, and the rubber driving wheel is used for driving the whole mobile cabin. The invention has the remarkable effects of improving the traffic capacity and the comfort of personal travel and realizing intelligent traffic.
reason: The patent describes a structural design for a mobile cabin with rubber wheels and a transparent housing but does not present a causal mechanism for solving a problem beyond component arrangement. The solution is specific to a 3D rail transit system and lacks a generalizable functional principle.

abstract: A method for constructing an assembled recyclable rectangular working well with preset detachable door openings comprises steps of: (I) designing according to functional requirements for a rectangular working well; (II) constructing by supporting piles; (III) installing prefabricated top beam; (IV) edge protection construction; (V) alternate construction of earthwork excavation, retaining slabs and internal support breast beams; (VI) installing the ladder entering the rectangular working well; (VII) rectangular working well back cover; (VIII) demolition of the detachable subsection support piles in the door part and completing the construction of the assembled recyclable rectangular working well in the preset detachable door hole; (IX) after the operation in the well is completed, during the backfilling process of the rectangular working well, gradually recovering the working well components such as the retaining slab, the internal support girder, the prefabricated crown beam and the supporting piles.
problem: Constructing a recyclable rectangular working well that can be assembled, used, and disassembled for repeated deployment without permanent structural modifications.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity during operation while ensuring components can be easily disassembled and recovered without damaging the surrounding environment.
mechanism: Using detachable, prefabricated structural components that are sequentially installed during assembly and gradually recovered during disassembly, enabling modular reuse without permanent modifications.
mechanism_raw: Using detachable, prefabricated components (e.g., support piles, retaining slabs, beams) that are sequentially installed during construction and gradually recovered during backfilling, enabling modular reuse of structural elements.

abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including computer programs encoded on computer storage media, for determining a suitable building layout for a property. One of the operations is performed by optionally, receiving building module parameters for section of qualifying building modules. displaying, via a user interface, a graphical representation of two or more building modules. A user may customize a building layout from the two or more building modules. The system displays an assembled building layout including two or more building modules. The system receives a confirmation of the assembled building layout for 3D printing. Based on the assembled building layout, instructions are generated and transmitted to one or more 3D printers to manufacture one or more building structures based on the selected building layout with potential subsequent modification of the preconfigured positions of windows, doors and walls of the building.
problem: Generating customized building layouts for 3D printing that balance user-defined design preferences with manufacturability constraints.
constraint: Ensuring user flexibility in design while maintaining compatibility with 3D printing capabilities and structural feasibility of the final building.
mechanism: Allowing interactive customization of building modules through a graphical interface, then translating the assembled layout into manufacturing instructions with iterative adjustments to preconfigured elements.
mechanism_raw: Allowing interactive customization of building modules through a graphical interface, then translating the assembled layout into machine instructions for 3D printers, with iterative adjustments to preconfigured elements like windows and walls.

abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including medium-encoded computer program products, for computer aided design of physical structures using generative design processes. A method includes obtaining a design space for a modeled object, one or more design criteria, one or more in-use load cases, and one or more specifications of material, wherein the design criteria comprise a required number of loading cycles for the modeled object; iteratively modifying a generatively designed three dimensional shape of the modeled object, comprising: performing numerical simulation of the modeled object, finding a maximized stress or strain element for each of the one or more in-use load cases, determining an expected number of loading cycles for each of the one or more in-use load cases, redefining a fatigue safety factor inequality constraint for the modeled object, computing shape change velocities in accordance with at least the fatigue safety factor inequality constraint, and updating the level-set representation.
problem: Designing physical structures that can withstand repeated loading cycles without failure while optimizing shape and material usage.
constraint: Balancing computational efficiency of simulations with the need to accurately model fatigue behavior across multiple load cases.
mechanism: Iteratively modifying a geometric representation by performing numerical simulations, identifying critical stress/strain elements, computing fatigue safety factors, and adjusting shape change velocities to update a level-set representation. This creates a feedback loop where structural geometry evolves to balance load-bearing requirements and fatigue resistance.
mechanism_raw: Iteratively modifying a 3D shape by performing numerical simulations, identifying critical stress/strain elements, computing fatigue safety factors, and adjusting shape change velocities to update a level-set representation. This creates a feedback loop where structural geometry evolves to balance load-bearing requirements and fatigue resistance.

abstract: A carcass cleaning system. Specifically, a system for cleaning an animal carcass using potable water passed through an offline treatment system and the application of this treated water to the surface of the carcass, for example, by running through a bath or by spraying or nebulisation at or onto the surface of the carcass. The invention finds utility in the fields of butchery and slaughtering of animals in the preparation for sale as meat.
reason: The mechanism is a straightforward application of water treatment and spraying/nebulization for cleaning, which is a direct process rather than a causal principle. It lacks a deeper functional relationship that can be abstracted beyond the specific cleaning context.

abstract: A ring-type wearable device is disclosed. The disclosed ring-type wearable device comprises: an outer ring member; an inner ring member separably inserted into the outer ring member; a sensor unit disposed in the outer ring member; and a control unit disposed in the outer ring member so as to be electrically connected to the sensor unit, wherein the sensor unit can maintain constant sensitivity in correspondence to the thickness of the inner ring member.
reason: The mechanism is a specific sensor calibration method tied to physical dimensions of a wearable device. While it involves maintaining sensitivity, it does not describe a generalizable causal operation beyond the niche application of ring-type wearables.

abstract: The invention relates to a device for treating the hair including a housing for receiving a cosmetic product refill, a heating element for the hair to be treated, and a device that prevents the reception of the cosmetic product refill in the housing, depending on the temperature of the heating element.
problem: Preventing unsafe use of a cosmetic product refill in a heated device when the heating element is at a temperature that poses a risk.
constraint: Ensuring the temperature sensing and interlock mechanism is responsive enough to prevent unsafe conditions without overly restricting normal operation.
mechanism: Using a temperature-dependent mechanical or electrical interlock that physically blocks or disables the insertion/reception of a refill when the heating element exceeds a safe temperature threshold. This creates a causal link between thermal state and access control.
mechanism_raw: Using a temperature-dependent mechanical or electrical interlock that physically blocks or disables the insertion/reception of a refill when the heating element exceeds a safe temperature threshold. This creates a causal link between thermal state and access control.

abstract: The invention involves an automatic shut-off waste disposer that may be activated with a control module, which utilizes a programmable automatic shut-off routine. This enables a user to turn on the garbage disposer and walk away without having to turn the disposer off. In exemplary embodiments, activation of the disposer includes actuation of a solenoid valve for injecting a stream of water flow into the dispenser chamber in order to facilitate a proper water flow while the disposer is actively disposing of food waste. In some exemplary embodiments, activation of the disposer may be achieved via a user-activated pneumatic actuator, which may be installed in proximity to the sink to which the disposer is coupled. In some exemplary embodiments, the disposer implements a sensor for automatically shutting of a motor of the disposer upon a predetermined event.
problem: Automatically managing a waste disposer to ensure safe and efficient operation without requiring constant user supervision.
constraint: Balancing the sensitivity of event detection to avoid false shutdowns while ensuring safety thresholds are met.
mechanism: Implementing a programmable control routine that activates a fluid injection mechanism during operation and uses sensors to detect predetermined events (e.g., motor overload, completion of grinding) to trigger automatic shutdown. This creates a closed-loop system where external inputs and internal states govern operation.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a programmable control routine that activates a solenoid valve to inject water flow during operation and uses sensors to detect predetermined events (e.g., motor overload, completion of grinding) to trigger automatic shutdown. This creates a closed-loop system where external inputs and internal states govern operation.
residual_terms: ["programmable control routine", "fluid injection mechanism", "predetermined events", "automatic shutdown", "closed-loop system"]

abstract: In an example, a composite stringer is described. The composite stringer includes a skin flange having a first gage, a top flange having a second gage, and a web having a third gage and extending between the skin flange and the top flange. The skin flange is configured to be coupled to a support structure. The support structure includes at least one of a skin of a vehicle or a base charge. The second gage of the top flange is greater than the first gage of the skin flange and the third gage of the web. The skin flange, the top flange, and the web include a plurality of plies of composite material.
problem: Balancing structural strength, weight, and material efficiency in composite load-bearing components.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity under load while reducing overall weight and material usage.
mechanism: Adjusting material distribution across structural regions by varying local thickness to align stiffness and load-bearing capacity with stress requirements, reducing material in low-demand areas while preserving integrity in high-demand zones.
mechanism_raw: Varying the thickness (gage) of composite plies across different structural regions (skin flange, top flange, web) to locally optimize stiffness and load distribution while minimizing excess material in low-stress areas.

abstract: A process and an apparatus for drying and consolidating an optical fibre preform in a furnace tube comprising a heating chamber, wherein an extension tube having an extension chamber configured to house at least a length portion of the preform is removably joined to the furnace tube and the drying process starts with the preform not completely inserted into the furnace tube, an upper length portion of the preform being surrounded by the extension tube joint to the furnace tube.
problem: Preventing thermal shock and ensuring uniform heating during the drying and consolidation of heat-sensitive optical fiber preforms.
constraint: Balancing heating efficiency with the need to prevent thermal stress-induced defects in the preform.
mechanism: Introducing an object into a thermal processing zone through a controlled transitional pathway, enabling staged exposure of different sections to temperature changes to mitigate abrupt thermal gradients and associated stress.
mechanism_raw: Gradually introducing the preform into the heating zone via an extension tube, allowing controlled thermal exposure of different preform sections to avoid abrupt temperature gradients.

abstract: A SiC epitaxial growth apparatus according to an embodiment includes a mounting stand on which a SiC wafer is mounted, and a furnace body which is configured to cover the mounting stand, and the furnace body includes a raw material gas supply port which is positioned so as to face the mounting stand and is configured to supply a raw material gas to the growth space, a first purge gas supply port which surrounds a vicinity of the raw material gas supply port and is configured to supply a purge gas to the growth space, and a second purge gas supply port which surrounds a vicinity of the first purge gas supply port and is configured to supply a purge gas to the growth space.
problem: Achieving uniform gas distribution and preventing contamination during SiC epitaxial growth processes.
constraint: Maintaining precise gas flow dynamics to ensure uniform deposition without introducing impurities.
mechanism: Establishing concentric flow barriers around a primary material inlet to create layered gas dynamics, isolating and directing reactive streams toward a target surface while displacing contaminants through peripheral sweeping flows.
mechanism_raw: Using concentric purge gas supply ports surrounding the raw material gas inlet to create layered gas flow barriers, isolating and directing the reactive gas stream toward the growth surface while sweeping away contaminants.

abstract: Methods and systems for charging, retaining, and cooling a mobile device in a vehicle. The system includes a tray configured to receive the mobile device, the tray having a plurality of apertures. The system also includes a wireless charger coupled to the tray and configured to wirelessly charge the mobile device. The system also includes a suction device configured to draw air through the plurality of apertures of the tray and create a suction force for reducing lateral movement of the mobile device and cooling the mobile device.
problem: Securing a mobile device in place and actively cooling it during wireless charging in a vehicle environment.
constraint: Balancing suction force for secure retention with sufficient airflow for effective cooling without obstructing charging.
mechanism: Generating negative pressure through distributed apertures to simultaneously anchor an object against displacement and induce convective airflow for thermal regulation, merging retention and cooling functions via a shared fluidic mechanism.
mechanism_raw: Generating suction through apertures in the tray to both physically retain the device against lateral movement and drive airflow for convective cooling, integrating mechanical retention and thermal management into a single system.

abstract: What is disclosed herein are embodiments of an enclosed manufacturing system configured to provide a controlled process environment for various articles of manufacture requiring a controlled process environment, and additionally to contain a process environment within the enclosure during periods of external access to the interior of the enclosed manufacturing system. Various embodiments of manufacturing systems of the present teaching can contain the environment within a manufacturing enclosure so as to minimize the interaction of an environment external to a manufacturing enclosure with the internal enclosure environment.
problem: Maintaining a controlled internal process environment within an enclosure while allowing external access to its interior.
constraint: Balancing accessibility requirements with the need to minimize contamination or environmental disruption during access.
mechanism: Implementing decoupling barriers or regulated airflow systems between an internal environment and external access points to maintain environmental integrity during ingress/egress events, preventing uncontrolled exchange of contaminants or conditions.
mechanism_raw: Designing an enclosed system with isolation mechanisms that decouple the internal environment from external conditions during access events, preserving environmental integrity through controlled barriers or airflow systems.

abstract: Apparatuses and methods to manufacture integrated circuits are described. A method of forming film on a substrate is described. The film is formed on a substrate by exposing a substrate to a diamond-like carbon precursor having an sp3 content of greater than 40 percent. Methods of etching a substrate are described. Electronic devices comprising a diamond-like carbon film are also described.
problem: Creating a diamond-like carbon film with a high sp3 bonding content (>40%) on a substrate to achieve specific mechanical or chemical properties.
constraint: Maintaining the sp3 bonding content above 40% during the deposition process to ensure the desired film properties without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Controlling the bonding configuration of a deposited film by exposing the substrate to a precursor whose bonding state is regulated during formation, so that the resulting film retains a target proportion of high-energy bonds that govern its structural and functional characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Exposing the substrate to a precursor with a controlled sp3 bonding content during film formation, which directly determines the resulting film's structural and functional characteristics.

abstract: It discloses to a device and a method for controlling pollutants in metal mine water resources cycling utilization. The device includes a multi-stage inflow constructed wetland (3), in which one or more layers of the filler are laid, and water distribution pipes (4) are buried at different height levels in the filler layers for multi-stage inflow, so that the received basin water is allowed to flow through each layer of the filler to degrade or remove the pollutants. In the multi-stage inflow constructed wetland, the types of fillers, dosage ratio, particle size and filling height of fillers in each layer are specifically selected. Therefore, heavy metal adsorption, suspended matter filtration, organic matter degradation, dephosphorization and denitrification can be effectively realized in the multi-stage inflow constructed wetland.
problem: Removing multiple types of pollutants (heavy metals, suspended solids, organics, phosphorus, nitrogen) from contaminated water in a single system.
constraint: Balancing the selection and arrangement of fillers across layers to enable simultaneous but non-interfering pollutant removal mechanisms.
mechanism: Arranging multiple treatment zones with distinct material compositions and physical properties so that a contaminant stream passes through each zone in sequence, with each zone applying a different removal mechanism that operates independently of the others.
mechanism_raw: Using a multi-stage layered wetland with fillers of varying compositions, dosages, particle sizes, and heights to sequentially target different pollutants through distinct physicochemical and biological processes.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to the field of display, in particular to a composition for an overcoat layer, a preparation method for the same, an overcoat layer material, and a display substrate and a display device including the overcoat layer material. The composition for the overcoat layer comprises: 10 to 30% by weight of styrene, 10 to 30% by weight of an epoxy resin, 1 to 3% by weight of a crosslinking agent, 0.1 to 0.5% by weight of a photoinitiator and/or a thermal initiator, 1 to 3% by weight of a surfactant, and 40 to 77% by weight of a solvent. The composition for the overcoat layer has styrene as a main monomer component, and may be initiated to cure by an initiator to obtain the overcoat layer material.
problem: Formulating an overcoat layer material that cures efficiently to provide protective or functional properties for display substrates.
constraint: Optimizing the weight ratios of components to ensure proper curing kinetics, mechanical strength, and compatibility with the substrate.
mechanism: Combining a base polymerizable compound with crosslinking agents, curing initiators, and solvents in optimized proportions to enable controlled polymerization and formation of a cross-linked network that provides protective or functional properties to a substrate.
mechanism_raw: Designing a composition with a primary monomer (styrene) combined with crosslinking agents, initiators, and solvents to enable controlled curing and formation of a cross-linked polymer network.

abstract: A heating device includes a surface heater unit including a heater portion that generates heat in a region extending in a longitudinal direction, the surface heater unit heating a heating object; and a heat conducting unit having a hollow space in which working fluid is sealed and including a working-fluid transport unit that transports the working liquid in the longitudinal direction, the heat conducting unit being in contact with the surface heater unit. The working-fluid transport unit is provided unevenly in a direction crossing the longitudinal direction in the hollow space.
problem: Efficiently transferring heat along a longitudinal direction using a working fluid in a heat-conducting unit.
constraint: Maintaining the uneven distribution of the transport unit to optimize fluid flow patterns without disrupting overall thermal performance.
mechanism: Positioning fluid transport pathways in a non-uniform pattern across a cross-sectional plane that intersects the primary heat flow direction, so that the working fluid follows a tortuous path that enhances convective heat transfer along the desired axis.
mechanism_raw: Arranging a working-fluid transport unit unevenly in a direction crossing the longitudinal axis within a hollow space, directing fluid flow to enhance heat transfer in the desired direction.

abstract: A diffusion component for impregnating molten steel with a gas includes a barrier having a first side and a second side, a through-hole formed within the barrier, the through-hole connecting the first side to the second side, and a porous element arranged within the through-hole such that the flow of molten steel passes over the porous element. At least one flow disrupter is arranged relative to the porous element and configured to promote non-laminar flow of molten steel passing through the through-hole.
problem: Promoting effective gas-liquid contact between a gas and molten steel in a high-temperature diffusion process.
constraint: Ensuring the flow disrupter generates sufficient turbulence without causing structural damage to the barrier or porous element under extreme thermal conditions.
mechanism: Placing a flow disturbance element adjacent to a permeable barrier so that the motion of a high-temperature fluid over the barrier surface is rendered non-laminar, thereby increasing interfacial contact area and mass transfer between the fluid and a dispersed phase.
mechanism_raw: Using a flow disrupter positioned relative to a porous element to induce non-laminar flow of molten steel over the porous surface, increasing interfacial contact and mass transfer efficiency.

abstract: The percentage of a height of each undulation with respect to a length of the undulation is a unit steepness. A steepness is an average value of unit steepnesses of all undulations in a longitudinal direction at each of different positions in a width direction of a metal sheet. The maximum value of steepnesses in a center section in the width direction is less than or equal to 0.3%. The maximum value of steepnesses in a first edge in the width direction and a maximum value of steepnesses in a second edge section in the width direction are less than or equal to 0.6%. The maximum value of steepnesses in at least one of the first edge section and the second edge section in the width direction is less than the maximum value of steepnesses in the center section in the width direction.
problem: Controlling surface texture gradients in metal sheets to prevent localized stress concentrations or deformation during forming or use.
constraint: Maintaining a trade-off between structural integrity in high-stress edge regions and minimizing deformation risks in the central region, while ensuring the gradient does not exceed specified steepness thresholds.
mechanism: Varying the steepness of surface undulations across a sheet's width to create a controlled gradient, where edge regions have higher steepness for structural support while the center has lower steepness for formability, with at least one edge having lower steepness than the center to balance stress distribution.
