mechanism_raw: Varying the steepness of undulations across the width of a metal sheet by reducing center-section steepness while allowing higher edge steepness, with at least one edge having lower steepness than the center. This creates a controlled gradient that balances structural support and formability.

abstract: A network of microfibers are fabricated with a core-shell construction from sustainable materials, where the core includes a phase-change material, such as coconut oil, and the shell includes a biomass, such as cellulose. The microfibers are made via a wet-wet electrospinning process utilizing a coaxial spinneret with an inner conduit and an outer conduit. The biomass and the phase-change material are coaxially extruded into a coagulation bath including a mixture of ethanol and water. The collected microfibers exhibit a beaded structure of PCM aggregates and biomass connecting regions between the aggregates and are effective to aid in the thermoregulation of the immediate environment surrounding the network. The microfibers are suitable for use in a variety of sustainable products such as wearable thermoregulating textiles, wall/ceiling panels, insulation, packaging material, and more.
problem: Achieving thermoregulation in sustainable materials without compromising structural integrity or material sustainability.
constraint: Balancing the thermal capacity of the PCM core with the mechanical stability of the biomass shell, ensuring the beaded structure does not disrupt the phase-change functionality or material cohesion.
mechanism: Coaxially forming a core-shell microfiber structure by extruding a thermally responsive core material concentrically within a mechanically stable shell material, where the shell maintains structural connectivity while the core enables localized thermal regulation through phase transitions.
mechanism_raw: Coaxially extruding a phase-change material (core) and biomass (shell) via wet-wet electrospinning to form microfibers with a beaded structure. The core-shell design enables localized thermal regulation through PCM phase transitions while the biomass shell maintains structural connectivity and sustainability.

abstract: According to one embodiment of the present invention, a method of decoding, by a user equipment, a downlink signal in a wireless communication system comprises the steps of: receiving a semi-persistent zero power-channel state information reference signal (SP ZP CSI-RS) resource configuration from a base station; and decoding a downlink signal according to the SP ZP CSI-RS resource configuration. The SP ZP CSI-RS resource configuration includes a plurality of SP ZP CSI-RS resources and information on whether or not each of a plurality of the SP ZP CSI-RS resources is used can be indicated or configured by the base station.
problem: Efficiently decoding downlink signals in wireless systems while minimizing resource allocation overhead and adapting to dynamic network conditions.
constraint: Balancing the persistence of resource configurations (to reduce signaling) with the need for dynamic adjustments to accommodate varying channel conditions and user demands.
mechanism: Configuring a set of reference signal resources with partial persistence, where a base station dynamically indicates which resources are active, allowing user equipment to decode signals based on a flexible configuration that reduces signaling overhead while adapting to changing conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using semi-persistent zero-power CSI-RS resources configured by a base station, where the base station dynamically indicates which resources are active. This allows the user equipment to decode signals based on a flexible, partially persistent configuration that reduces signaling overhead.

abstract: A fire-protection system comprising two elements is disclosed: 1) A retractable fire-protection covering or mat that may be automatically deployed over a building and stowed after the threat has passed; and, 2) A water fire spray system for wetting the lower aspects of a building to protect the lower and uncovered aspects of a building from fire. Using these systems simultaneously allows the user to mitigate forest and brush fire threats that may periodically threaten a building.
problem: Protecting buildings from wildfire threats that simultaneously endanger both upper and lower structural regions.
constraint: Coordinating deployment timing and coverage areas of the two systems to ensure no gaps in protection, while minimizing resource usage during non-emergency conditions.
mechanism: Deploying two complementary protection systems simultaneously—one providing overhead shielding coverage and another providing targeted wetting of lower regions—to ensure continuous protection across both upper and lower structural areas while minimizing resource usage during non-emergency conditions.
mechanism_raw: Combining a retractable fire-protection covering (deployed over the building) with a water spray system targeting lower aspects. The dual systems operate simultaneously to shield vulnerable regions while wetting exposed areas to prevent ignition.

abstract: Various multifunctional dispensing systems with overhead fuel/air delivery and methods for using the same are provided. Such a system can include a dispenser system and an overhead delivery unit suspended on tracks above a vehicle drive aisle at a fueling station. The overhead delivery unit can include a fuel dispensing nozzle and an air dispensing nozzle that can be moved about the tracks so as to optimally position the nozzles to be approximately overhead the fuel doors and tires, respectively. Such an arrangement allows a customer to refuel their vehicle and inflate their tire(s) without moving their car between each transaction.
problem: Enabling customers to perform multiple vehicle maintenance tasks (e.g., refueling and tire inflation) without repositioning the vehicle between operations.
constraint: Optimizing spatial arrangement and nozzle mobility to accommodate diverse vehicle sizes and configurations while maintaining operational efficiency and safety.
mechanism: Suspending multiple dispensing nozzles on overhead mobile tracks above a service aisle, allowing independent positioning of each nozzle to align with different vehicle service points, eliminating the need for vehicle repositioning between tasks.
mechanism_raw: Suspending fuel and air dispensing nozzles on overhead tracks above a vehicle aisle, allowing independent positioning of nozzles to align with fuel doors and tires. This eliminates the need for vehicle movement between tasks.

abstract: A method for generating a fault tree of a multi-component system is provided. The multicomponent system includes a logical-functional system layer and a physical system layer as different layers of abstraction. The physical system layer may correspond, for example, to software and/or hardware implementing the functional aspects of the logical-functional system layer. The method first provides a logical-functional fault tree for the logical-functional system layer and a physical fault tree for the physical system layer, the latter having elements corresponding to elements in the logical-functional fault tree. Next, a mixed-layer fault tree is generated by combining aspects of both fault trees in a systematic way. The disclosed is particularly relevant for analyzing safety-critical systems. However, the present concepts are not limited to these applications and may be applied to general use cases where fault tree analysis is applicable.
problem: Analyzing faults in multi-component systems that span multiple abstraction layers (logical-functional and physical), where faults can propagate between layers but each layer has its own distinct fault characteristics and failure modes.
constraint: The combination must maintain the distinct fault characteristics of each layer while enabling cross-layer analysis through systematic element correspondence, balancing layer-specific detail with integrated cross-layer visibility.
mechanism: Creating separate hierarchical models for each abstraction layer, then systematically integrating them into a unified model that preserves element correspondence across layers, enabling cross-layer propagation analysis while retaining layer-specific failure characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Creating separate fault trees for each abstraction layer and then systematically combining them into a mixed-layer fault tree that preserves the correspondence between elements across layers, enabling cross-layer fault propagation analysis while maintaining the distinct fault characteristics of each layer.

abstract: A filter assembly has an outer housing having an open first end and an open second end. An inner filter housing is within the outer housing adjacent the second end, and a gasket is provided at the first end of the outer housing. An internal chamber is provided between the first end of the outer housing and the inner filter housing, where during use, fluid from the within the internal chamber is drawn out the second end of the outer housing by way of the inner filter housing. A filter is provided within the inner filter housing. The gasket forms a gasketed opening smaller than the open first end of the outer housing. The gasket may extend axially adjacent a wall of the outer housing and abut the inner filter housing, such that the internal chamber is defined by the gasket and the inner filter housing.
reason: This is a standard mechanical filter assembly design using a gasket to define a flow chamber. The mechanism is a conventional sealing and chamber-forming approach with no novel problem-solving principle that transcends the specific mechanical context.

abstract: Systems that are used to support a plurality of frames arranged in a specific configuration are contemplated. The system comprises outer frame panels that removably couple to the plurality of frames. It is contemplated that the outer frame panels collectively couple to the plurality of frames to thereby provide additional stability to maintain the plurality of frames in the specific configuration, such that the risk of the plurality of frames losing their specific configuration during transport is reduced.
reason: This describes a basic mechanical bracing system using removable external panels to stabilize internal frames during transport. The mechanism is a standard clamping/bracing approach with no novel problem-solving principle beyond conventional mechanical support.

abstract: An object of the present invention is to provide a chemical liquid purification method which makes it possible to obtain a chemical liquid having excellent defect inhibition performance. The chemical liquid purification method according to an embodiment of the present invention is a chemical liquid purification method including obtaining a chemical liquid by filtering a substance to be purified containing an organic solvent by using two or more kinds of filters having different pore sizes, in which a supply pressure P1 of the substance to be purified supplied to a filter Fmax having a maximum pore size X1 among the two or more kinds of filters and a supply pressure P2 of the substance to be purified supplied to a filter Fmin having a minimum pore size X2 among the two or more kinds of filters satisfy P1>P2.
problem: Obtaining a chemical liquid with excellent defect inhibition performance through multi-stage filtration using filters with different pore sizes, where uniform pressure application would compromise either flow rate or filtration quality.
constraint: The pressure differential must be controlled so that larger pore filters receive higher pressure to maintain flow rate while smaller pore filters receive lower pressure to prevent damage or excessive clogging, balancing throughput with filtration quality across stages.
mechanism: Applying variable pressure differentials to sequential filtration stages, where larger pore stages receive higher pressure to maintain flow rate and smaller pore stages receive lower pressure to prevent damage or clogging, optimizing throughput and quality across stages.
mechanism_raw: Applying different supply pressures to filters based on their pore sizes — higher pressure to larger pore filters and lower pressure to smaller pore filters (P1 > P2) — ensuring adequate flow through each filtration stage while preventing damage or excessive clogging of finer filters, thereby optimizing both throughput and defect inhibition.

abstract: The present disclosure discloses an emblem structure in which an emblem is coupled to a part in an integral form, thereby minimizing the amount of protrusion and an image is implemented in a distorted form, and advancing the quality of a product. The emblem structure includes a base layer, an image layer disposed on an outer surface of the base layer or to be spaced apart from the outer surface, and a transparent layer deposited on the base layer to cover the image layer. The transparent layer is configured such that light is transmitted and refracted and that the light reflected by the base layer and the image layer is lost, thereby improving visual recognition of the image layer.
problem: Improving visual recognition of an image on an emblem while minimizing protrusion and enhancing product quality, where unwanted reflections from underlying layers reduce image contrast and visibility.
constraint: The transparent layer must balance light transmission and refraction to optimize visual recognition while maintaining structural integrity and minimizing protrusion, ensuring that beneficial light manipulation does not compromise the physical form factor.
mechanism: Using a transparent layer configured to manipulate light transmission and refraction such that reflected light from underlying layers is directed away or attenuated, reducing glare and enhancing contrast of the intended visual element.
mechanism_raw: Using a transparent layer configured to transmit and refract light in a way that causes light reflected by the base layer and image layer to be directed away or lost (scattered/absorbed), thereby reducing glare and unwanted reflections and enhancing the contrast and visibility of the intended image layer.

abstract: A rotor assembly is provided for a piece of rotational equipment. This rotor assembly includes a rotor disk, a rotor blade and a seal element. The rotor disk is configured to rotate about a rotational axis. The rotor disk extends axially along the rotational axis to a rotor disk end face. The rotor blade includes an attachment. The attachment attaches the rotor blade to the rotor disk. The seal element is configured to seal a gap between the rotor disk and the attachment. The seal element has a longitudinal centerline that extends along an interface between the rotor disk and the attachment at the rotor disk end face.
problem: Sealing a dynamic gap between rotating components (e.g., rotor disk and blade attachment) while maintaining operational integrity under rotational stress.
constraint: Balancing sealing effectiveness against wear, friction, and material fatigue caused by continuous rotational forces.
mechanism: A flexible sealing element is positioned along the interface between two rotating components, with its longitudinal axis aligned to the interface. This allows the seal to maintain continuous contact and adapt to axial movement or misalignment caused by rotation, preventing leakage without impeding motion.
mechanism_raw: A seal element is positioned along the interface between two rotating components, with its longitudinal centerline aligned to the interface. This allows the seal to maintain continuous contact and adapt to axial movement or misalignment caused by rotation, preventing leakage without impeding motion.

abstract: A method for grasping a row of multiple separate blocks of frozen food originating from a plate freezer, the row extending in a longitudinal direction corresponding to the longitudinal direction of the plate freezer, includes the steps of grasping the row of blocks along its opposing lateral edges by closing a clamp (1) having two grasping elements (2, 20) that extend along the opposing lateral edges of the row, wherein at least one of the grasping elements along its length includes multiple separate pinching elements (4, 40), each element for pinching one or more of the blocks, the pinching elements being individually movable with respect to the at least one grasping element in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal direction of this grasping element, the method further including adjusting the lateral position of each pinching element when closing the clamp, by individually moving each pinching element.
problem: Grasping a row of discrete objects (e.g., frozen food blocks) with variable lateral positioning or spacing along a linear axis.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient gripping force per element while allowing independent movement, and ensuring coordination between elements to avoid uneven pressure distribution.
mechanism: A clamp employs multiple independently movable gripping elements along its grasping surface. Each gripping element adjusts its lateral position during clamping to conform to the specific position of an individual object in the row, enabling adaptive gripping of non-uniform or misaligned items.
mechanism_raw: A clamp uses multiple independently movable pinching elements along its grasping surface. Each pinching element adjusts its lateral position during clamping to conform to the specific position of an individual object in the row, enabling adaptive gripping of non-uniform or misaligned items.

abstract: A drying apparatus can include, in some aspects, an ultrasonic transducer and an infrared heater positioned proximate to the ultrasonic transducer and configured to emit infrared light. The drying apparatus can include a plurality of ultrasonic transducers. The drying apparatus can include a delivery enclosure defining a bottom wall, the bottom wall defining a plurality of air outlets; the ultrasonic transducer mounted to the delivery enclosure; and the drying apparatus can include an air mover mounted to the delivery enclosure.
problem: Efficiently drying materials (e.g., food, chemicals) by combining rapid heat transfer with moisture removal.
constraint: Optimizing the spatial and temporal coordination of ultrasonic and infrared energy to maximize drying efficiency without overheating or damaging the material.
mechanism: Simultaneous application of mechanical agitation (to dislodge moisture) and thermal energy (to evaporate moisture). The energy sources are positioned in proximity to create synergistic delivery, accelerating drying through combined mechanical and thermal effects.
mechanism_raw: Simultaneous application of ultrasonic vibrations (to agitate and dislodge moisture) and infrared radiation (to directly heat and evaporate moisture). The ultrasonic transducers and infrared heaters are positioned in proximity to create synergistic energy delivery, accelerating drying through mechanical and thermal effects.

abstract: A computer system receives a request to locate a vehicle within a facility. The computer system parses the request to identify one or more characteristics of the vehicle. The computer system identifies a sensor corresponding to the vehicle based on the one or more characteristics of the vehicle. The computer system identifies a most recent location of the vehicle based on the last registered position of the vehicle within the facility. The computer system transmits a signal to a parking spot sensor at the most recent location of the vehicle in the facility. The computer system receives the unique identification. The computer system determines that the unique identification of the vehicle sensor co-located with the parking spot sensor matches the sensor of the requested vehicle. The computer system reports to the user a current location of the vehicle within the facility based on a location of the parking spot sensor.
problem: Locating a specific asset (e.g., vehicle) within a large facility using sparse sensor data and historical tracking information.
constraint: Ensuring accuracy of historical data and sensor coverage to avoid false negatives, while minimizing computational overhead from repeated queries.
mechanism: A system parses a query to identify asset characteristics, uses historical position data to narrow the search to a likely area, then activates a localized sensor at that area to verify the asset's presence via unique identification. This combines predictive querying with targeted real-time verification to reduce search scope.
mechanism_raw: A system parses a query to identify asset characteristics, uses historical position data to narrow the search to a likely area, then activates a localized sensor at that area to verify the asset's presence via unique identification. This combines predictive querying with targeted real-time verification to reduce search scope.

abstract: A semiconductor structure may include a vertical field effect transistor, the vertical field effect transistor may include a top source drain, a bottom source drain, and an epitaxial channel and a resistive random access memory below the vertical field effect transistor. The resistive random access memory may include an epitaxial oxide layer, a top electrode, and a bottom electrode. The top electrode, which may function as the bottom source drain of the vertical field effect transistor, may be in direct contact with the epitaxial channel of the vertical field effect transistor. The epitaxial oxide layer may separate the top electrode from the bottom electrode. The top source drain may be arranged between a dielectric material and the epitaxial channel. The dielectric material may be in direct contact with a top surface of the epitaxial channel. The epitaxial oxide layer may be composed of a rare earth oxide.
problem: Integrating memory and logic components in a semiconductor structure to minimize footprint and improve performance.
constraint: Ensuring material compatibility and electrical isolation between the FET and RAM components to prevent cross-interference or degradation of performance.
mechanism: A vertical field-effect transistor and resistive memory are stacked such that the memory's top electrode serves as the transistor's bottom terminal. An insulating layer separates the memory electrodes, while the transistor's channel and dielectric are arranged to share structural layers, enabling monolithic integration without compromising individual functionality.
mechanism_raw: A vertical field-effect transistor (FET) and resistive random-access memory (RAM) are stacked such that the RAM's top electrode serves as the FET's bottom source/drain. An epitaxial oxide layer separates the RAM electrodes, while the FET's channel and dielectric are arranged to share structural layers, enabling monolithic integration without compromising individual functionality.

abstract: The invention relates to a method and forest work machine (1) making use of it, by means of which the control of the forest work machine is assisted. In the forest work machine, a light source (2) is adapted, which may be directed to one or more different parts of the surroundings around it, forming the working area of the forest work machine. This is adapted to produce at least one specifically defined specified-form light pattern (3) on said working area. With such a light pattern, visual information content may be produced on the working area to support an operator of the forest work machine in their work. As content of such information, it is possible to define control measures for the forest work machine, performed in any working area or their restrictions.
problem: Assisting an operator in controlling a forest work machine by providing actionable visual guidance in the working area.
constraint: The light pattern must be precisely defined and projected onto the working area without interfering with the machine's physical operations or the operator's visibility.
mechanism: Projecting a spatially defined visual pattern onto a target area to encode operational constraints or guidance, enabling an operator to interpret and act on the encoded information within their field of view without disrupting physical operations.
mechanism_raw: Projecting a specifically defined light pattern onto the working area to encode control measures or restrictions, enabling the operator to interpret and act on visual information directly within their field of view.

abstract: The present invention provides an adhesive resin composition that has excellent adhesiveness and durability, a method for bonding adherends, and an adhesive resin film More specifically, the present invention relates to an adhesive resin composition containing more than 50 parts by mass and 99.5 parts by mass or less in a solid content of an acid-modified polyolefin resin having a melting point of 50 to 100° C., 0.5 parts by mass or more and less than 50 parts by mass in a solid content of an epoxy resin having a novolac structure, and an organic solvent; a method for bonding adherends including forming an adhesive layer on a first adherend by applying the adhesive resin composition and drying, and then bonding a second adherend to the adhesive layer by laminating the second adherend on the adhesive layer; and an adhesive resin film including a first adhesive layer, a substrate layer, and a second adhesive layer in that order, in which any one or both of the first adhesive layer and the second adhesive layer include(s) the adhesive resin composition.
reason: The patent primarily describes a specific material composition (acid-modified polyolefin, epoxy resin, solvent) with defined mass ratios. While the combination may produce adhesion and durability, the mechanism is rooted in chemical interactions between specific materials rather than a generalizable functional principle.

abstract: A MEMS device is provided. The MEMS device includes a substrate having at least one contact, a first dielectric layer disposed on the substrate, at least one metal layer disposed on the first dielectric layer, a second dielectric layer disposed on the first dielectric layer and the metal layer and having a recess structure, and a structure layer disposed on the second dielectric layer and having an opening. The opening is disposed to correspond to the recess structure, and the cross-sectional area at the bottom of the opening is smaller than the cross-sectional area at the top of the recess structure. The MEMS device also includes a packaging layer, and at least a portion of the packaging layer is disposed in the opening and the recess structure. The second dielectric layer, the structure layer, and the packaging layer define a chamber.
problem: Creating a sealed chamber in a MEMS device while maintaining structural integrity and enabling packaging integration.
constraint: The cross-sectional area difference between the opening and recess must be precisely controlled to ensure the packaging layer forms a hermetic seal without structural failure.
mechanism: Forming a sealed chamber through a layered structure where a recess in one layer and a corresponding opening in another layer have mismatched cross-sectional areas, enabling a packaging material to geometrically interlock and create a hermetic seal via controlled area transitions.
mechanism_raw: Using a layered structure with a recess in a dielectric layer and a corresponding opening in a structure layer, where the cross-sectional area at the bottom of the opening is smaller than the top of the recess. This allows a packaging layer to be disposed in both features, forming a sealed chamber through geometric interlocking.

abstract: A method and a serial communicator facilitating multiple and synchronous communication with three-dimensional (3D) printers are disclosed. The serial communicator establishes serial communication with a plurality of 3D printers. The serial communicator concurrently sends and receives commands, instructions and status message from each of the plurality of 3D printers. The serial communicator provides multiple and synchronous dimensionality for a user to execute 3D printing. A user accesses the serial communicator using a user device or user management system (UMS) for managing multiple series connections to multiple 3D printers. The serial communicator receives 3D modelling data containing a tool path (Gcode) from the UMS. The serial communicator assigns the 3D modelling data to available 3D printer for executing the 3D printing using the serial communication.
problem: Enabling synchronous, concurrent communication and task execution across multiple 3D printers from a single user interface.
constraint: The system must manage multiple serial connections simultaneously without data collision or timing conflicts, ensuring synchronized execution across heterogeneous printers.
mechanism: Managing concurrent communication and task distribution across multiple devices by establishing parallel serial connections, dynamically routing data streams to available devices, and synchronizing command execution to prevent timing conflicts.
mechanism_raw: A serial communicator that establishes parallel serial connections to multiple printers, concurrently sends/receives commands and status messages, and dynamically assigns 3D modeling data (Gcode) to available printers based on availability.

abstract: A waste disposal system with a waste receiver for receiving pharmaceutical waste material. A locking assembly is secured to a fixed surface and actuated from a locked configuration to an unlocked configuration. A lock cylinder of the locking assembly may extend forward of a front wall of a receiver body of the waste receiver to engage a locking feature of the cover in the locked configuration. A cover retention feature may prevent axial decoupling of the cover from the receiver body. An engagement feature is moved to be disengaged from the receiver body, and the receiver body is moved away from the fixed surface to disengage the locking assembly from the cover. The cover is decoupled from the cover retention feature, and coupled with the receiver body to seal the pharmaceutical waste material. The locking assembly may be removed from a lock passageway for disposal of the waste receiver.
problem: Securely sealing pharmaceutical waste in a receiver while allowing controlled removal of the receiver for disposal.
constraint: The locking and retention features must balance secure engagement during use with controlled disengagement for disposal, ensuring no accidental release of hazardous material.
mechanism: Securing a containment system using a dual-stage mechanism: a primary locking element engages a cover to prevent unauthorized access, while a secondary retention element prevents unintended decoupling. Disengaging the primary lock enables controlled removal of the containment body while maintaining resealing capability.
mechanism_raw: A locking assembly with a lock cylinder that engages a cover's locking feature in a locked configuration, combined with a cover retention feature that prevents axial decoupling. Disengaging the locking assembly allows the receiver body to move away from the fixed surface, decoupling the cover and resealing the waste.

abstract: A process for growing carbon nanotubes includes making carbon nanotubes by flowing methane into a tube. The process also includes increasing pressure to a high predefined pressure for the carbon nanotubes and maintaining temperature at a low predefined temperature for the carbon nanotubes. The high pressure and low temperature produce carbon nanotubes within minutes.
problem: Rapid synthesis of carbon nanotubes without compromising structural quality.
constraint: Balancing high pressure and low temperature to avoid structural defects while maintaining reaction kinetics for rapid synthesis.
mechanism: Applying a combined pressure and temperature regime to manipulate reaction kinetics and selectivity, where pressure forces reactant proximity to accelerate nucleation while temperature suppresses parasitic pathways, enabling rapid synthesis with structural fidelity.
mechanism_raw: Applying a high pressure and low temperature combination to accelerate chemical reactions, where the pressure forces reactant molecules into close proximity while the low temperature suppresses unwanted side reactions, enabling rapid nucleation and growth within minutes.

abstract: The present invention relates to functional fibers, that is, sweat-absorptive quick-drying fibers through which moisture, such as sweat discharged from the skin, is quickly discharged to the outside to be dried. A sweat-absorptive quick-drying composition including a water repellent for fibers as a material applied on the fibers further includes water-repellent microcapsules and wasabi antibacterial microcapsules respectively obtained by performing micro-encapsulation of the water repellent for fibers and wasabi oil. Accordingly, it is possible to ensure a very stable water-repellent function by using a water-repellent-functional-processing agent subjected to micro-encapsulation treatment, unlike conventional fibers subjected to sweat-absorptive quick-drying treatment.
problem: Maintaining stable water-repellent and antibacterial functionality in sweat-absorptive fibers during repeated use and washing.
constraint: Designing microcapsules that remain intact during fiber processing and use while allowing targeted release of functional agents.
mechanism: Encapsulating functional agents within protective barriers to isolate them from environmental degradation during processing and use, while enabling triggered release through mechanical or chemical stimuli to sustain performance over repeated cycles.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating water repellents and wasabi oil in microcapsules to protect active agents from degradation and enable controlled release, ensuring sustained performance over time.

abstract: The present disclosure discloses an infrared sensor structure, comprises a cantilever switch array, the cantilever switch array comprises cantilever switches, and each cantilever switch comprises a cantilever beam and a switch corresponding to the cantilever beam, vertical heights from the cantilever beams to the switches in different cantilever switches are different from each other, when the cantilever beams are deformed towards the switches and connect to the switches, the switches turn on; wherein, deformations of different cantilever beams produced by absorbing infrared signal are different from each other, the intensity of the infrared signal can be quantified by number of the switches on, so as to realize detection of the infrared signal. The manufacturing of the infrared sensor structure in the present disclosure can be compatible with the existing semiconductor CMOS process.
problem: Quantifying infrared signal intensity using a mechanical sensor array compatible with semiconductor manufacturing.
constraint: Calibrating beam heights and material properties to ensure discrete, non-overlapping activation thresholds for accurate intensity measurement.
mechanism: Deploying an array of mechanically responsive elements with distinct activation thresholds, where each element undergoes displacement proportional to incident energy and triggers a discrete state change at a unique threshold, converting continuous intensity into a quantized count.
mechanism_raw: Using cantilever beams of varying heights that deform proportionally to absorbed infrared energy, where each beam triggers a switch at a distinct deformation threshold, converting intensity into a countable number of activated switches.

abstract: A cookware assembly comprises a lid including an underside and a plurality of basting projections. The underside has a center and extending toward a perimeter of the lid. Each of the plurality of basting projections protrudes downwardly from the underside of the lid. Each of the plurality of basting projections includes an interior concave surface, an exterior concave surface, and a drip ridge. The interior concave surface extends downwardly away from the underside to form a bay adjacent to the interior concave surface. The drip ridge is formed along a border between the interior concave surface and the exterior surface and defines a vertex along the drip ridge. During use of the lid, condensate formed on the underside collects along the interior concave surface, which funnels the condensate to the vertex for droplet formation and release from a corresponding one of the plurality of basting projections.
problem: Efficiently collecting and redistributing condensate during cooking to baste food without manual intervention.
constraint: Optimizing the geometry of concave surfaces and drip ridges to maximize condensate collection and controlled droplet release without disrupting heat distribution.
mechanism: Shaping interior surfaces with converging geometries to direct fluid flow toward a collection vertex, where accumulated mass forms discrete droplets and releases them at defined points through surface tension thresholds, enabling passive redistribution without external actuation.
mechanism_raw: Structuring concave interior surfaces on downward-projecting basting projections to funnel condensate toward a drip ridge vertex, where accumulated liquid forms droplets and releases them at specific points for targeted basting.

abstract: Provided are valve devices and flow heads for a valve device. A valve device can include a valve body (30) that opens and closes a valve hole (15a) to allow communication between a primary flow path (17a) and a secondary flow path (17b), a back pressure chamber (7) defined at the back side of the valve body, a small hole (51) that is provided in the valve body to allow the primary flow path of and the back pressure chamber to communicate with each other, and a pin (6) that has a straight portion inserted into the small hole to clean the small hole by relative motions of the small hole and the straight portion. A flow head (34) may be annular and include one or more notches along a perimeter and be configured to engage with an inner peripheral surface of an upper end portion of an inner barrel of the valve device.
problem: Preventing clogging of a small communication hole between a primary flow path and a back pressure chamber in a valve device.
constraint: Ensuring the pin's motion is synchronized with valve movement to clean the hole without introducing wear or leakage.
mechanism: Integrating a reciprocating cleaning element synchronized with primary mechanical motion to maintain unobstructed communication between flow paths, where the element traverses a critical orifice during operation to remove obstructions without introducing leakage paths.
mechanism_raw: Inserting a straight pin into the small hole that moves relative to the hole during valve operation, mechanically scraping away debris to maintain unobstructed flow communication.

abstract: A semiconductor memory device and a method of manufacturing the semiconductor memory device are provided. The semiconductor memory device includes a doped semiconductor pattern including a body portion and a first protrusion protruding from the body portion in a first direction, a first channel pattern disposed on a top surface of the first protrusion and extending in the first direction, a first memory pattern surrounding a sidewall of the first channel pattern and extending on a sidewall of the first protrusion, and interlayer insulating layers and conductive patterns alternately stacked on each other in the first direction.
problem: Increasing semiconductor memory density while maintaining reliable electrical connections and structural integrity in a 3D-stacked architecture.
constraint: Balancing structural support from the protrusion and body against the need for dense vertical stacking and precise alignment of conductive and insulating layers.
mechanism: A vertical conductive structure extends from a base, with a first functional pattern on its upper surface and a second functional pattern on its lateral surface. This spatial arrangement enables three-dimensional integration of components around the conductive structure, increasing density without lateral expansion while maintaining alignment between layers.
mechanism_raw: A doped semiconductor protrusion extends vertically from a body, with a channel pattern on its top surface and a surrounding memory pattern on its sidewall. This vertical arrangement allows 3D integration of memory elements around the channel, enabling higher density without lateral expansion.

abstract: A sheet feeding apparatus includes a stacking member having a separation unit and an opening portion disposed upstream from the separation unit, a feeding member, and a moving device that includes a slope portion having a slope along which sheets are guided toward the separation unit. The moving device moves the stacking member between a first position where the feeding member and sheets stacked on the stacking member are in contact with each other, and a second position where the feeding member and the sheets are not in contact with each other. When the stacking member is at the first position, the slope portion is disposed at a position lower than the separation unit in a vertical direction. When the stacking member is at the second position, the slope portion is disposed to protrude via the opening portion to be higher than a stacking surface of the stacking member.
problem: Efficiently feeding sheets from a stack while preventing misfeeds or jams during separation.
constraint: Timing and positional accuracy of the slope relative to the separation unit to ensure smooth sheet flow without mechanical interference.
mechanism: A movable guide surface shifts between a first position where it directs sheets toward a separation mechanism and a second position where it retracts through an opening to avoid mechanical interference. This positional adjustment dynamically controls sheet flow and separation timing.
mechanism_raw: A moving device shifts a stacking member between two positions: one where a slope guides sheets toward a separation unit (lower position) and another where the slope retracts via an opening to avoid interference (higher position). This positional adjustment dynamically controls sheet guidance and separation.

abstract: The present disclosure provides a page browsing method and apparatus, an electronic device, and a machine readable medium, which belong to the field of touch technologies. The page browsing method includes: in a scenario of sliding for browsing a page, enabling browsing mode configuration according to a first touch operation received from a user; performing the browsing mode configuration in response to the user input; and automatically browsing consecutive pages according to a result of the browsing mode configuration.
problem: Enabling intuitive and efficient page browsing on touch-enabled devices without requiring repetitive user input.
constraint: Ensuring the automated browsing aligns with user intent and allows interruption or adjustment without unintended behavior.
mechanism: A first input gesture configures parameters for a continuous action sequence, which then executes automated sequential navigation based on the configured parameters. This converts a single user input into a sustained process that can be interrupted or adjusted.
mechanism_raw: A first touch operation configures a browsing mode (e.g., speed, direction), which then triggers automated sequential page navigation based on the configured parameters. This converts a single gesture into a continuous action sequence.

abstract: A method of transmitting and receiving a data channel by a user equipment (UE) in a wireless communication system is disclosed. The method includes receiving downlink control information (DCI) including information related to a resource region for a physical downlink shared channel (PDSCH) or a physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH), acquiring a resource indication value (RIV) from the DCI, acquiring a first length of allocated resource blocks based on the RIV, scaling the first length of allocated resource blocks to a second length of allocated resource blocks, based on a scaling factor and receiving the PDSCH or transmitting the PUSCH based on the second length of allocated resource blocks, wherein the scaling factor may be 2n, and n may be non-negative integer.
problem: Optimizing resource block allocation in wireless communication systems to balance efficiency and flexibility.
constraint: Selecting scaling factors that avoid over-allocation or underutilization of resources while maintaining compatibility with system-wide resource management.
mechanism: An initial allocation value determines a base quantity of resources, which is then scaled by a multiplicative factor to adjust the allocation dynamically. This scaling allows adaptation of resource usage to varying transmission demands while maintaining system-wide compatibility.
mechanism_raw: A resource indication value (RIV) determines an initial length of allocated resource blocks, which is then scaled by a factor (2^n) to adjust the allocation. This scaling allows dynamic adaptation of resource usage to varying transmission needs.

abstract: A coupling device (16, 116, 216, 316) configured optimally to communicate between a first and a second admittance controller and actuator assembly, the first and the second admittance control and actuator assembly respectively having a first and a second admittance controller (12a, 12b) configured to drive a respective first and a second actuator and each of the first and the second actuator being respectively connected to a first body having a first mass and a second body having a second mass, wherein the coupling device (16, 116, 216, 316) comprises: an input port having a first input for receiving a first input force signal (f1) from the first admittance controller and actuator assembly (12a) and a second input for receiving a second input force signal (f2) from the second admittance controller and actuator assembly (12b), and a processor adapted to derive a first output force signal for output to the first admittance controller and actuator assembly based on a Lagrange multiplier dependent on a comparison of the first input force signal and the second input force signal.
problem: Coordinating forces between two independent admittance-controlled actuators to achieve synchronized motion or force application.
constraint: Maintaining stability and responsiveness in the coupled system despite potential delays or discrepancies in force feedback between the two actuators.
mechanism: A coupling mechanism computes output forces by comparing input force signals from two independent actuators using a mathematical constraint variable. This coordination ensures synchronized motion or force application while maintaining system stability despite feedback discrepancies.
mechanism_raw: A coupling device uses a Lagrange multiplier derived from comparing input force signals from both actuators to compute output forces. This mathematical coordination ensures the actuators work in harmony while respecting physical constraints.

abstract: A machine including a first deck, a second deck, a first blank transfer assembly, and a second blank transfer assembly is provided. The first and second decks are coupled to a frame. The first blank transfer assembly extends from a first end to a second end and includes a first pick-up assembly moveable between the first end, proximate the second deck, and the second end, proximate the first deck. The second blank transfer assembly extends from a third end to a fourth end and includes a second pick-up assembly moveable between the third end, proximate the second deck, and the fourth end, proximate the first deck. The first blank transfer assembly and the second blank transfer assembly are operationally offset when moving between the first and second ends and the third and fourth ends, respectively.
problem: Transferring blanks between two decks without mechanical interference between the two transfer assemblies operating in parallel.
constraint: Must maintain transfer throughput and cycle time while ensuring the two assemblies never collide during their reciprocating motion between decks.
mechanism: Coordinating two parallel transfer operations with temporal and spatial offsets to prevent collision while maintaining continuous throughput. The offset timing and spatial positioning of the parallel assemblies ensures non-interfering paths during reciprocating motion between endpoints.
mechanism_raw: Two blank transfer assemblies are operationally offset relative to each other when moving between their respective ends, so that their pick-up assemblies traverse non-interfering paths while still completing transfers between the decks. The offset timing and spatial positioning of the parallel assemblies prevents collision while maintaining continuous transfer capability.

abstract: Examples are disclosed herein that relate to electronically functional textile articles. One example provides a knitted textile article comprising a first conductive thread and a second conductive thread knit into the article in such a manner as to form a conductive junction separated by a gap. The knitted textile article further comprises a knitted surface texture feature formed at a location that defines an opening over the gap, and an electronic component connecting the gap to form a circuit with the first conductive thread and the second conductive thread.
problem: Integrating discrete electronic components into a knitted textile structure to form functional circuits without disrupting the textile's integrity or manufacturability.
constraint: Must maintain the textile's flexibility, drape, and manufacturability while creating gaps narrow enough for component integration yet accessible through the surface texture, and precise enough for reliable electrical connection.
mechanism: Forming conductive pathways with precisely positioned gaps and surface access features during a textile manufacturing process, enabling component insertion and electrical connection. The manufacturing process simultaneously creates conductive junctions and surface texture features that align with gaps, providing physical access for component integration.
mechanism_raw: The knitting process itself simultaneously creates conductive thread junctions with precisely positioned gaps and surface texture features (e.g., raised loops or openings) at locations that align with those gaps. The surface texture feature provides physical access to the gap, allowing an electronic component to be inserted and connected to bridge the gap, forming a circuit with the conductive threads.

abstract: A cutting device is disclosed. The cutting device has a first housing member, a second housing member that is removably attachable to the first housing member to form a housing, and a carriage that is movably disposed in the housing, the carriage including a first attachment portion, which is disposed at a first portion of the carriage, and a second attachment portion, which is disposed at a second portion of the carriage that is disposed away from the first portion of the carriage. The cutting device also has an exterior member disposed at an exterior of the housing and attached to the carriage via an aperture disposed in one of the first housing member and the second housing member, and a cutting member that is removably attachable to the first attachment portion at the first portion of the carriage.
problem: Providing a cutting device with a replaceable cutting member while maintaining a persistent external connection (e.g., biasing or guidance) to the carriage.
constraint: Must maintain positional precision and structural stability of the cutting member during operation while enabling tool replacement without losing the external member's connection or function.
mechanism: Decoupling a replaceable functional element from a persistent external connection by using separate attachment points on a shared support structure. A first attachment portion interfaces with the replaceable element while a second attachment portion maintains a persistent connection to an external member through a housing aperture.
mechanism_raw: A carriage carries two separate attachment portions at different locations: a first attachment portion for the removable cutting member and a second attachment portion connected to an exterior member through a housing aperture. This decouples the replaceable cutting element from the persistent external connection, allowing the cutting member to be swapped without disturbing the exterior member's function.

abstract: Prestressed carbon fibers of at least one textile structure comprising carbon fibers are embedded in a concrete matrix. At least one textile structure comprising carbon fiber bundles is laid in a mold at a distance from one another, into two accommodation elements which are arranged at two diametrical end faces of the mold. Hollow spaces within the accommodation element are filled with a rapid-curing viscous composition having a mineral basis or rapid-curing polymer. After curing the composition or of the polymer, tensile forces act on the accommodation element(s) in the longitudinal direction of the carbon fiber bundles with a tensioning device. During the tensile force the interior of the mold is subsequently filled completely with viscous concrete. After curing of the concrete, the tensile forces on the prestressed carbon fiber bundles are largely transferred to the cured concrete and the concrete component can then be removed from the mold.
problem: Applying and retaining prestressing tension in carbon fiber bundles embedded in concrete, where the tension must be maintained during concrete placement but ultimately transferred to the cured concrete matrix.
constraint: Must coordinate the curing timing between the rapid-curing temporary composition and the concrete so that tension is maintained during concrete placement but properly transferred to the cured concrete without loss of prestress.
mechanism: Temporarily retaining tension in reinforcement elements using a rapidly curing composition, then transferring the tension to a cured matrix after the matrix has set. The temporary composition holds reinforcement under tension during matrix placement, and curing coordination ensures tension transfer to the final structure without prestress loss.
mechanism_raw: Temporary rapid-curing compositions fill hollow spaces in accommodation elements at the mold ends, holding the carbon fiber bundles under tension during the tensile force application. After the temporary composition cures and the concrete is poured and cured, the prestressing forces are largely transferred from the accommodation elements to the cured concrete matrix, and the component is removed from the mold with the prestress retained in the final structure.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method of manufacturing a cellulose product having a flat or non-flat product shape by a pressure moulding apparatus comprising a forming mould. The forming mould has a forming surface defining said product shape, The method comprises the steps of: arranging a cellulose blank containing less than 45 weight percent water in said forming mould; heating said cellulose blank to a forming temperature in the range of 100° C. to 200° C.; and pressing said cellulose blank by means of said forming mould with a forming pressure acting on the cellulose blank across said forming surface, said forming pressure being in the range of 1 MPa to 100 MPa.
problem: Forming cellulose blanks into flat or non-flat product shapes without material degradation or steam-related forming defects.
constraint: Must balance moisture content, temperature, and pressure so that fibers soften sufficiently for forming without burning or charring, while moisture is low enough to prevent steam disruption but not so low as to make the material brittle.
mechanism: Balancing moisture content, thermal softening, and pressure application to enable plastic deformation of a fibrous material without causing vaporization-induced defects. Controlled low moisture prevents steam formation, while heat and pressure enable shaping across a forming surface with shape retention.
mechanism_raw: A cellulose blank with controlled low moisture content (below 45 wt%) is heated to a temperature range (100–200°C) that softens the cellulose fibers without causing residual water to vaporize and disrupt forming, then pressed with controlled pressure (1–100 MPa) across a forming surface to shape the material. The low moisture content prevents steam formation that would create voids or surface defects, while the heat-pressure combination enables plastic deformation and shape retention.

abstract: A pressure vessel is disclosed having an inner vessel made of an inner-vessel material and an outer layer applied thereon as well as a valve-connection piece with a two-part sealing cone and outer piece, the sealing cone being positioned on an inner face of a protrusion of the inner vessel and the outer piece for generating a sealing pressure being positioned between the two-part sealing cone, the protrusion and the outer piece on an outer face of the protrusion. The outer piece includes a suitably shaped groove having a first and a second edge for receiving a sealing ring that seals under the sealing pressure, wherein the groove and the sealing ring are dimensioned such that, under the sealing pressure and due to the plastic deformability, first and second sealing beads project at least into two gaps between the sealing ring and form the first and second edge.
problem: Creating a reliable seal in a pressure vessel that maintains or improves sealing integrity under internal pressure without requiring external clamping forces.
constraint: The sealing ring must be dimensioned and made of a material with sufficient plastic deformability to form sealing beads under pressure, but not so much that it over-deforms and loses structural integrity or fails to maintain the seal.
mechanism: A deformable sealing element is positioned within a constrained space such that applied pressure induces controlled plastic deformation, causing the element to form protruding features that engage with adjacent surfaces. This creates a self-reinforcing seal whose integrity increases with internal pressure, as the deformation amplifies contact forces between the element and the surfaces.
mechanism_raw: Applied sealing pressure causes plastic deformation of a dimensioned sealing ring within a groove, forcing the ring to form sealing beads that project into gaps between the ring and the groove's first and second edges, creating a self-reinforcing seal that tightens as pressure increases.

abstract: A robotic system is provided for repeatedly and reproducibly applying a sealant to a seam in an assembled heating, ventilation and air conditioning (“HVAC”) duct component. The applied sealant has a predetermined location on the assembled HVAC duct component to seal the seam. An assembled HVAC duct component is thus provided having a robot applied sealant on at least one seam in the assembled HVAC duct component, wherein the applied sealant has at least one of a predetermined location, thickness or coverage. The robotically applied sealant can be applied to a blank for forming the assembled HVAC duct component, wherein the sealant is located at locations forming a seam in the assembled HVAC duct component.
problem: Achieving consistent, reproducible sealant application to HVAC duct seams, where manual application leads to variability in location, thickness, and coverage.
constraint: The robotic system must balance precision and speed to achieve reproducible results in an industrial manufacturing environment without significantly slowing production throughput.
mechanism: A programmable actuation system applies a substance to predefined locations on a target surface using stored parameters that specify spatial coordinates, material distribution, and coverage metrics. The system autonomously replicates identical application patterns across multiple targets, ensuring uniformity through closed-loop control of actuation variables.
mechanism_raw: A robotic system applies sealant to predetermined locations on the duct component based on programmed parameters for location, thickness, and coverage, ensuring each application is identical and reproducible across multiple units.

abstract: Methods, apparatus, and processor-readable storage media for generating context-based question-answer pairs by applying artificial intelligence techniques to context-related data are provided herein. An example computer-implemented method includes obtaining multi-modal data pertaining to a given event, and removing noise from the multi-modal data by applying filtering techniques to the multi-modal data, thereby generating filtered multi-modal data; creating a comprehensive set of multi-modal data pertaining to at least a portion of the given event by aggregating the filtered multi-modal data in accordance with topic modelling techniques and removing any items of duplicate filtered multi-modal data; dynamically generating question-answer pairs related to the given event by applying machine reading comprehension-based artificial intelligence models to the comprehensive set of multi-modal data; and outputting at least a portion of the questions from the question-answer pairs to one or more participants of the given event.
problem: Generating relevant and comprehensive question-answer pairs from complex, noisy multi-modal data related to a given event, where raw data contains irrelevant information and duplicates.
constraint: The system must balance noise removal and data aggregation to retain sufficient context for meaningful QA generation while avoiding information overload and redundancy from duplicate or irrelevant data.
mechanism: A multi-stage processing pipeline first removes irrelevant data from heterogeneous inputs, then aggregates the remaining data using semantic clustering to form a coherent dataset. Duplicate entries are eliminated, and context-aware generative models are applied to the cleaned dataset to dynamically produce question-answer pairs that reflect the aggregated information.
mechanism_raw: A processing pipeline filters noise from multi-modal data, aggregates the filtered data using topic modeling to create a comprehensive dataset, removes duplicates, and then applies machine reading comprehension AI models to dynamically generate context-based QA pairs from the cleaned and organized data.

abstract: A method of generating a tessellated output file comprising receiving a computer-aided design (CAD) model file defining a CAD model including a plurality of vertices, a plurality of curves, a plurality of surfaces, and at least one volume; generating base polygon data defining the CAD model for additive manufacturing, the base polygon data including a plurality of connected polygons, each polygon including a plurality of nodes, a plurality of edges, and a face; generating data for a vertex metadata container including a listing of CAD model vertices and one polygon node associated with each CAD model vertex; generating data for a curve metadata container including a listing of CAD model curves and at least one polygon edge associated with each CAD model curve; and generating data for a surface metadata container including a listing of CAD model surfaces and at least one polygon face associated with each CAD model surface.
problem: Converting CAD models to tessellated polygon data for additive manufacturing while preserving the semantic associations between original CAD model elements (vertices, curves, surfaces) and their tessellated representations.
constraint: The mapping must accurately preserve the relationship between high-level CAD features and their tessellated counterparts without losing information or introducing ambiguity, while keeping the metadata overhead manageable.
mechanism: A bidirectional mapping system associates high-level structural elements of a source model with corresponding elements in a tessellated representation. Metadata containers explicitly link each source vertex, curve, and surface to their tessellated counterparts, preserving semantic relationships through a hierarchical correspondence framework that maintains feature-level traceability.
mechanism_raw: Metadata containers are generated that explicitly map each CAD model vertex to a corresponding polygon node, each CAD model curve to corresponding polygon edges, and each CAD model surface to corresponding polygon faces, maintaining the structural and semantic correspondence between the original CAD model and the tessellated output.

abstract: A body part protector includes an inner layer defining an interior space that is configured to be occupied by a human body part, an outer layer connected to the inner layer and forming at least one chamber therebetween, and a plurality of separate dampers. A damper is at least partially disposed in the chamber. Each damper extends into the interior space along a respective longitudinal axis. Each damper has an outer end disposed at a fixed position relative to the outer layer and an inner end disposed longitudinally opposite the outer end in the interior space. The protector includes a plurality of separate engagement members corresponding to the plurality of dampers. Each engagement member is disposed at the inner end of the corresponding damper and is configured to engage the body part of the user. Each damper includes a plurality of compressible damper elements concentrically arranged about the longitudinal axis.
problem: Protecting body parts from impact forces while allowing movement, maintaining comfort, and ensuring consistent contact between the protector and the body part.
constraint: The damper elements must balance impact absorption capacity with flexibility to allow movement, while the engagement members must maintain consistent body contact without causing discomfort during dynamic motion.
mechanism: An array of independently compressible elements arranged concentrically about a central axis compresses locally in response to impact forces, while engagement structures at the inner periphery maintain continuous contact with a target surface. The independent compression allows localized energy absorption without disrupting overall contact consistency, enabling movement while preserving protective engagement.
mechanism_raw: Concentrically arranged compressible damper elements about a longitudinal axis compress independently upon impact, while engagement members at the inner end of each damper maintain consistent contact with the body part, allowing localized compression at impact points without losing overall body contact.

abstract: The method includes the step of pulling the corrugated board along hot plates by means of an upper flexible member and a lower flexible member driven by two electric motors. By at least one electric parameter of the drive motor of the lower flexible member, the correct operation of the traction device and in particular the correct ratio of the linear feeding speeds of the two flexible members is checked. The method provides an iterative check of the controlled electric parameter and a possible correction of the speed of the flexible members to maintain the desired speed ratio.
problem: Maintaining the correct linear feeding speed ratio between two flexible members in a traction device to ensure proper operation of a corrugated board pulling system.
constraint: Balancing the need for real-time adjustment of motor speeds while avoiding slippage or misalignment of the flexible members during the pulling process.
mechanism: Using a feedback signal derived from one drive's operational parameter to iteratively adjust another drive's speed, maintaining a synchronized speed ratio between two flexible traction members without slippage.
mechanism_raw: Using an electric parameter (e.g., motor current or speed) from the lower flexible member's drive motor as a feedback signal to iteratively monitor and correct the speed ratio between the two flexible members, ensuring synchronized operation.

abstract: A respiratory system and method comprise a tracker module adaptable to be secured to a variety of inhalers, the tracker module sensing activation of the medication canister of the inhaler for delivery of medication to a user. The tracker module also senses the rate of inhalation air flow of the user when inhaling medication for determination of proper inhaler use. Upstream and downstream sensors provide flow information to determine quality of the inhalation. A flow sensor is an integral part of the tracking module and can be used on multiple inhalers. Other sensors are provided that monitor user presence at the inhaler, user technique in using the inhaler, and the attitude of the inhaler when it was used. Low power devices are used to conserve battery power. A spirometer provides user lung function data.
problem: Ensuring proper inhaler use by accurately assessing inhalation technique, flow quality, and user behavior across diverse inhaler types.
constraint: Achieving accurate flow measurement and user behavior monitoring while maintaining low power consumption for battery-operated devices.
mechanism: Integrating multiple sensors positioned at different points in a flow path to cross-validate measured airflow characteristics, enabling determination of inhalation quality and actuation timing.
mechanism_raw: Integrating upstream and downstream flow sensors within a universal tracker module to cross-validate inhalation airflow data, enabling determination of inhalation quality and proper inhaler actuation timing.

abstract: Light boards including one or more light emitting elements (e.g. light emitting diode (LED) devices) for use in lighting fixtures are disclosed. In one example implementation, a light board includes a first layer having a first surface and an opposing second surface. The light board includes one or more light emitting elements disposed on the first surface of the first layer. The light board includes one or more circuit elements located on the second surface of the first layer. The one or more circuit elements are associated with powering the one or more light emitting elements. The light board includes a second layer disposed on the second surface of the first layer such that the one or more circuit elements are located between the second surface of the first layer and the second layer.
reason: The patent describes a static layered structure for component placement and protection, which is a design choice rather than a functional mechanism that produces a useful effect through causal interaction.

abstract: A premix burner for combusting premixed gas containing fuel and air mixed in advance includes a plurality of combustion nozzles including a first nozzle having an ignition rod disposed therein and a second nozzle other than the first nozzle, a first premixed gas passage for supplying the premixed gas to the first nozzle, and a second premixed gas passage for supplying the premixed gas to the second nozzle. The first premixed gas passage and the second premixed gas passage are fluidically isolated from each other.
problem: Achieving reliable ignition and combustion in a premix burner while preventing cross-interference between combustion zones.
constraint: Maintaining combustion efficiency and ignition reliability while ensuring gas passages remain isolated to avoid unintended interactions between combustion zones.
mechanism: Fluidically isolating separate gas passages for each combustion nozzle, with one nozzle dedicated to housing an ignition element, ensuring independent gas flow paths to prevent flame propagation or interference between nozzles.
mechanism_raw: Fluidically isolating separate gas passages for each combustion nozzle, with one nozzle dedicated to housing an ignition rod, ensuring independent gas flow paths to prevent flame propagation or interference between nozzles.

abstract: Disclosed is an elevator system for a multilevel architectural structure, the system having: a system controller, an elevator and an elevator controller, wherein the system controller and elevator controller communicate over a network, multi-level hoistway in which the elevator travels, the multi-level hoistway including a plurality of egress levels, including a first egress level, the first level being a primary egress level, wherein during an alarm condition the system, when the primary level is inaccessible, performs an emergency assessment of identifying a safe level of the plurality of levels at which to discharge passengers, the assessment comprising obtaining a smoke density profile for the egress levels, the profile illustrating a distribution of smoke within the multilevel structure, analyzing the smoke density profile, identifying a safe level having a smoke density that is safe, and instructing the elevator to discharge passengers on the safe level.
problem: Safely discharging elevator passengers during an emergency when the primary egress level is inaccessible due to hazards like smoke.
constraint: Balancing the need for rapid emergency decision-making with the requirement to accurately assess environmental hazards (e.g., smoke distribution) to ensure passenger safety.
mechanism: Analyzing a real-time environmental hazard profile across multiple egress levels to dynamically identify a safe discharge level meeting predefined safety thresholds, then actuating movement to that level.
mechanism_raw: Analyzing a real-time smoke density profile across multiple egress levels to dynamically identify a safe discharge level with acceptable smoke density, then instructing the elevator to move passengers to that level.

abstract: An engine hoist attachment assembly for hoisting a vehicle component includes a tube, a bar, and a pair of rods. The tube has a first end that is configured to slidably insert a terminus of a boom of an engine hoist to removably couple the tube to the boom. The bar has a back face that is coupled to and extends bidirectionally and perpendicularly from a second end of the tube so that the bar is substantially parallel to a surface upon which the engine hoist is positioned. The pair of rods is coupled to and extends in parallel from a front face of the bar. The rods are configured to position under a vehicle component, positioning a user to utilize the engine hoist to selectively lift and lower the vehicle component.
problem: Adapting a standard engine hoist to lift specific vehicle components without permanent modification.
constraint: Balancing removability of the attachment with structural stability during lifting operations.
mechanism: A removable coupling mechanism enables selective attachment to a lifting apparatus, while a stable platform with adjustable positioning elements provides structural support for lifting operations without permanent modification.
mechanism_raw: A slidable coupling (tube) allows removable attachment to the hoist boom, while a perpendicular bar and parallel rods provide a stable, adjustable platform to position under the component, enabling selective lifting and lowering.

abstract: A storage tank system features a tank made of rigid material and an insulation assembly. The insulation assembly includes an inner membrane and an outer membrane wherein the inner membrane is located within the outer membrane and at least one of the inner membrane and outer membrane is made of a flexible material. An insulation medium is located in a space between the inner membrane and the outer membrane and a vacuum is applied to the space.
problem: Providing effective thermal insulation for a rigid storage tank while accommodating structural or environmental flexibility.
constraint: Maintaining vacuum integrity in the insulation medium while preserving the flexibility of the membranes.
mechanism: A dual-membrane insulation system with a vacuum medium between flexible barriers reduces heat transfer via conduction and convection, while the flexible material allows the insulation to conform to or accommodate structural movement.
mechanism_raw: A dual-membrane insulation system with a vacuum between flexible inner and outer membranes reduces heat transfer via conduction and convection, while the flexible material allows the insulation to conform to the tank's shape or absorb movement.

abstract: A micro-combustion device generating electrical power raises global performance of the system, is compact, and reduces losses by utilizing an induced helical path. The device includes: injection ducts inserting a combustion agent, a fuel and/or a mixture thereof wherein the injection of the combustion agent takes place tangentially to the internal cylindrical wall, inducing a helical combustion path, the internal cylindrical walls of the chamber having a deposition of catalytic material to accelerate the combustion reaction; a turbo compressor group, including a compressor, feeding under pressure the combustion chamber through the injection ducts, and a turbine, receiving the flue gases from the discharge duct, compressor and turbine being keyed on the same axis, whereon a generator of electrical power, in turn, is keyed; and a fuel cell, fed by the flue gases through the turbine and by an oxidizing agent, implementing an electrochemical process generating additional electrical power.
problem: Improving efficiency and compactness of micro-combustion-based power generation systems.
constraint: Balancing energy extraction between the turbine and fuel cell to avoid overexploitation of flue gas energy before the fuel cell stage.
mechanism: A helical flow path induced by tangential injection enhances mixing and reaction completeness, while catalytic surfaces accelerate combustion. Sequential energy extraction via a shared-axis turbine and downstream energy recovery stage maximizes power output from a single combustion process.
mechanism_raw: Inducing a helical combustion path via tangential fuel injection enhances mixing and reaction completeness, while catalytic wall coatings accelerate combustion. A shared-axis turbine-generator and downstream fuel cell sequentially extract energy from flue gases, maximizing power output from a single combustion process.

abstract: A method of remediation of a water-bearing formation is disclosed. A first solution containing a nitrogen-containing compound and a second solution containing a nitrite-containing compound are introduced into the water-bearing formation. The two solutions intermix within the formation such that a foam is generated within the formation.
problem: Remediating a water-bearing subsurface formation by generating a stabilizing or mobilizing foam in situ.
constraint: Ensuring the two solutions intermix effectively within the formation to trigger foam generation without premature reaction in surface equipment.
mechanism: Two separate reactive chemical solutions are injected into a subsurface formation, where they intermix and react to form a foam that alters flow dynamics or enhances contaminant removal within the porous medium.
