mechanism_raw: Injecting two separate chemical solutions (a nitrogen-containing compound and a nitrite-containing compound) into the formation allows them to intermix and react, forming a foam that alters flow dynamics or enhances contaminant removal within the porous medium.

abstract: A solenoid valve system includes a supply solenoid valve, a plurality of exhaust solenoid valves, and a valve control section controlling opening and closing operation of the supply solenoid valve and the plurality of exhaust solenoid valves using PWM or PFM. The plurality of exhaust solenoid valves are disposed in parallel with each other. The supply solenoid valve and the plurality of exhaust solenoid valves have substantially identical flow rate characteristics. The number of the plurality of the exhaust solenoid valves is twice the number of the supply solenoid valve.
problem: Achieving precise control of fluid flow rates in a solenoid valve system with balanced supply and exhaust operations.
constraint: Maintaining matched flow rate characteristics between supply and exhaust valves to ensure balanced system operation under dynamic control.
mechanism: A supply valve and multiple parallel exhaust valves with matched flow characteristics are controlled via pulse-modulated signals, enabling fine-grained flow rate modulation by adjusting active valve count and duty cycles.
mechanism_raw: A supply solenoid valve and multiple parallel exhaust solenoid valves with identical flow characteristics are controlled via PWM/PFM, enabling fine-grained modulation of flow rates by adjusting the number of active exhaust valves and their duty cycles.

abstract: An electro-optical device includes an electro-optical panel including first to n-th (n is an integer of 2 or greater) data line blocks with each data line block including a first data line group and a second data line group, a first circuit device, and a second circuit device. The first circuit device drives, in an i-th phase of phase development drive, the first data line group of an i-th data line block of the first to n-th data line blocks, and the second circuit device drives, in the i-th phase of the phase development drive, the second data line group of the i-th data line block of the first to n-th data line blocks.
problem: Efficiently driving multiple data line groups in an electro-optical panel while minimizing interference and ensuring synchronized operation during phase-based activation.
constraint: Balancing timing coordination between the first and second circuit devices to avoid overlap or conflict during phase transitions while maintaining signal integrity.
mechanism: Sequential activation of distinct groups using separate control units, where each phase activates a subset to distribute electrical load and reduce interference through temporal coordination.
mechanism_raw: Phased sequential activation of distinct data line groups using separate circuit devices, where each phase drives a specific subset of lines to distribute electrical load and reduce crosstalk.

abstract: A vibration actuator has a movable body and a fixing body. The movable body includes: a disk-shaped magnet; annular cores each having an opening at a center thereof; and spring stopper weight parts, and stacked such that the magnet is disposed at a center of the movable body, the annular cores is fixed on front and rear surfaces of the magnet in its axial direction, and the spring stopper weight parts are joined with the annular cores at the opening. Each spring stopper weight part includes: a spring fixing part connecting to one of the elastic support parts; a joining protrusion part inserted into the opening of one of the annular cores; and a weight body part provided between the spring fixing part and the joining protrusion part, having a larger diameter, and disposed to face and join with an annular surface of one of the annular cores.
problem: Generating controlled, precise mechanical vibrations in a movable body using magnetic and elastic components within a compact actuator design.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and precise alignment of the magnet, cores, and spring components to ensure consistent vibration amplitude and frequency without mechanical failure.
mechanism: Converting electromagnetic forces into controlled mechanical motion through magnetic-elastic coupling, using a central magnet and elastic elements to regulate vibration amplitude and frequency.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a central magnet with annular cores and spring stopper weight parts to convert electromagnetic forces into controlled axial or radial motion through magnetic-elastic coupling.

abstract: A card-type solid state drive (SSD) including: a substrate that has a first surface and a second surface facing each other; a memory controller and a nonvolatile memory device that are on the first surface; a plurality of functional terminals on the second surface; and a plurality of thermal terminals on the second surface, wherein the functional terminals include first-row functional terminals, second-row functional terminals, and third-row functional terminals, wherein at least one of the first-row functional terminals, at least one of the second-row functional terminals, and at least one of the third-row functional terminals are electrically connected to the memory controller or the nonvolatile memory device, and wherein the thermal terminals are not electrically connected to the memory controller or the nonvolatile memory device.
problem: Managing heat dissipation in a compact solid-state drive while maintaining reliable electrical connectivity and avoiding thermal-electrical interference.
constraint: Ensuring physical separation and material compatibility between thermal and electrical pathways to avoid signal degradation while maximizing heat dissipation efficiency.
mechanism: Separating thermal and electrical pathways on a shared substrate to prevent cross-interference while optimizing heat dissipation efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Separating thermal terminals from functional terminals on a shared substrate, with thermal terminals dedicated to heat transfer and functional terminals handling electrical signals, preventing cross-interference.

abstract: Apparatus, systems, and methods for protecting a vehicle from a radiation source (e.g., the sun) are provided. One apparatus includes a set of first wires and a set of second wires located proximate to the set of first wires. The set of first wires maintains a positive voltage and the set of second wires maintains a negative voltage. The set of first wire and the set of second wires are arranged to generate an electrostatic field (ESF) between the vehicle and the radiation source. A system includes a spacecraft and a field generator that generates an ESF between the spacecraft and a radiation source. A method includes tracking a location of a spacecraft relative to a radiation source and generating an ESF between the spacecraft and the radiation source.
problem: Protecting a vehicle or spacecraft from harmful radiation (e.g., solar radiation) by creating a localized electrostatic barrier.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient voltage and field strength to effectively shield against radiation while minimizing power consumption and avoiding interference with onboard electronics.
mechanism: Generating an electrostatic field between a protected object and a radiation source using oppositely charged elements to deflect charged particles through electrostatic repulsion.
mechanism_raw: Generating an electrostatic field between the vehicle and radiation source using oppositely charged wire arrays, deflecting or neutralizing charged particles through electrostatic repulsion.

abstract: Methods of controlling olefin polymerization reactor systems are provided herein. In some aspects, the methods include a) selecting n input variables, each input variable corresponding to a process condition for an olefin polymerization process; b) identifying m response variables, each response variable corresponding to a measurable polymer property; c) adjusting one of more of the n input variables in a plurality of polymerization reactions using the olefin polymerization reactor system, to provide a plurality of olefin polymers and measuring each of the m response variables as a function of the input variables for each olefin polymer; d) analyzing the change in each of the response variables as a function of the input variables to determine the coefficients; e) calculating a Response Surface Model (RSM) using general equations for each response variable determined in step d) to correlate any combination of the n input variables with one or more of m response variables; f) applying n selected input variables to the calculated Response Surface Model (RSM) to predict one or more of m target response variables, each target response variable corresponding to a measurable polymer property; and g) using the n selected input variables Is1 to Isn to operate the olefin polymerization reactor system and provide a polyolefin product.
problem: Optimizing the olefin polymerization process to produce polyolefins with target properties by correlating input process conditions with measurable responses.
constraint: Accurately modeling complex, nonlinear chemical interactions while ensuring the RSM remains computationally tractable and experimentally validated across varying process conditions.
mechanism: Statistically modeling relationships between input variables and response variables to predict and control process outcomes through empirical correlation.
mechanism_raw: Using a Response Surface Model (RSM) to statistically map relationships between input variables (e.g., temperature, pressure) and response variables (e.g., polymer molecular weight), enabling predictive control of the reactor system.

abstract: In a duct device that includes a duct body 9 having: an air flow path 90 defined thereinside; and a first divisional body 1 and a second divisional body 5 combined in a combining direction in which the first and second divisional bodies 1 and 5 approach each other, at time of positioning when a first duct portion 2 and a second duct portion 6 oppose each other, and an engagement portion 33 and an engagement projection 7 do not engage with each other, an outer wall portion 65 covers, from an outer side, a tip portion 21 that is a front end of the first duct portion 2, and the engagement portion 33 contacts with the engagement projection 7 in the combining direction, and covers a second engagement surface 72 that is a rear end of the engagement projection 7, with an engagement wrap portion 35, from the outer side.
problem: Ensuring proper alignment and secure engagement between two duct body components during assembly without misalignment or incomplete connection.
constraint: Balancing the combining direction and engagement geometry to prevent premature or incomplete engagement while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism: Staged mechanical interlocking where a first component's tip is covered by an outer wall portion during initial positioning, followed by a secondary engagement feature wrapping around a projection in a combining direction to ensure sequential and secure connection.
mechanism_raw: Sequential engagement where an outer wall portion covers the tip of the first duct portion during positioning, followed by an engagement wrap portion covering the rear end of the engagement projection in the combining direction, ensuring staged mechanical interlocking.
residual_terms: ["outer wall portion", "engagement wrap portion", "engagement projection", "combining direction"]

abstract: Systems and methods for authenticating identification information are disclosed. For example, an Automated Teller Machine (ATM) may comprise a user interface. The user interface may comprise a card reader. The card reader may be configured for card rotation about an axis of a bank card. The user interface may be configured to receive card rotation input from a user. The ATM may comprise at least one memory storing instructions. The ATM may comprise at least one processor configured to execute the instructions to perform operations. The operations may comprise receiving identification information from the user. The operations may comprise receiving the card rotation input. The operations may comprise extracting a card rotation sequence from the card rotation input. When the card rotation sequence is within a predetermined threshold from a stored card rotation sequence corresponding to the identification information, the operations may comprise authenticating the user for an ATM operation.
problem: Authenticating a user for an ATM operation using a physical card rotation input as a secure, non-traditional biometric-like identifier.
constraint: Accurately detecting and interpreting card rotation input while setting a threshold that balances security (preventing false positives) and usability (allowing natural user variation).
mechanism: Capturing a physical rotational input from a user, extracting a rotational sequence, and comparing it to a stored reference sequence within a predetermined threshold to authenticate the user.
mechanism_raw: Capturing card rotation input from a user, extracting a rotation sequence, and comparing it to a stored sequence within a predetermined threshold to authenticate the user.

abstract: Included are a first mobile terminal testing device that operates as an LTE base station, a second mobile terminal testing device that operates as an NSA 5G NR base station, and a test control device that controls the first mobile terminal testing device and the second mobile terminal testing device. The test control device includes a command input unit into which a control command for controlling the first mobile terminal testing device and the second mobile terminal testing device is input, a command transmission determination unit that determines a mobile terminal testing device of a transmission destination of the control command, and a command transmission unit that transmits the control command to a transmission destination determined by the command transmission determination unit. The command transmission determination unit determines the transmission destination of the control command according to the type of the control command.
problem: Efficiently routing control commands to heterogeneous mobile terminal testing devices (e.g., LTE and 5G NSA base stations) from a single test control device.
constraint: Correctly categorizing command types and ensuring reliable routing without cross-device interference or command misinterpretation.
mechanism: Classifying a control command based on its type, determining a target destination from the classification, and routing the command to the appropriate device via a transmission unit configured for heterogeneous device types.
mechanism_raw: Determining the transmission destination of a control command based on its type, then routing the command to the appropriate testing device via a command transmission unit.

abstract: A method for forming a laterally-grown group III metal nitride crystal includes providing a substrate, the substrate including one of sapphire, silicon carbide, gallium arsenide, silicon, germanium, a silicon-germanium alloy, MgAl2O4 spinel, ZnO, ZrB2, BP, InP, AlON, ScAlMgO4, YFeZnO4, MgO, Fe2NiO4, LiGa5O8, Na2MoO4, Na2WO4, In2CdO4, lithium aluminate (LiAlO2), LiGaO2, Ca8La2(PO4)6O2, gallium nitride, or aluminum nitride (AlN), forming a pattern on the substrate, the pattern comprising growth centers having a minimum dimension between 1 micrometer and 100 micrometers, and being characterized by at least one pitch dimension between 20 micrometers and 5 millimeters, growing a group III metal nitride from the pattern of growth centers vertically and laterally, and removing the laterally-grown group III metal nitride layer from the substrate. A laterally-grown group III metal nitride layer coalesces, leaving an air gap between the laterally-grown group III metal nitride layer and the substrate or a mask thereupon.
problem: Forming a high-quality, laterally-grown group III metal nitride crystal layer with controlled coalescence and minimal defects.
constraint: Balancing growth center dimensions (1–100 μm) and pitch (20 μm–5 mm) to achieve uniform lateral growth and coalescence without structural defects.
mechanism: Using a patterned substrate with defined growth centers to guide vertical and lateral crystal growth, causing lateral expansion and coalescence of the crystal layer, resulting in an air gap between the crystal layer and substrate.
mechanism_raw: Using a patterned substrate with growth centers of specific minimum dimensions and pitch ranges to guide vertical and lateral crystal growth, resulting in coalescence and an air gap between the crystal layer and substrate.

abstract: An inner coating layer for solid-propellant rocket engines, constituted by a material comprising from 45% to 55% wt. of a a cross-linkable, unsaturated-chain polymer base, from 11% to 13% wt. of silica, from 15% to 25% wt. of vulcanizing agents and plasticizers, from 5% to 7% wt. of aramid fiber and from 10% to 15% wt. of microspheres made of a material selected among glass, quartz and nano clay, having diameter lower than 200 μm, density comprised between 0.30 and 0.34 g/cc and resistance to hydrostatic pressure greater than, or equal to, 4500 psi.
problem: Creating a durable, heat-resistant inner coating layer for solid-propellant rocket engines that withstands extreme operational stresses.
constraint: Optimizing weight percentages (e.g., 45–55% polymer, 10–15% microspheres) and material properties (density 0.30–0.34 g/cc, >4500 psi pressure resistance) to meet performance requirements.
mechanism: Composing a composite material with a cross-linkable polymer base, reinforcing fillers, and low-density microspheres to balance structural strength, thermal resistance, and pressure tolerance for use in high-stress environments.
mechanism_raw: Composing a composite material with a cross-linkable polymer base, silica, vulcanizing agents, aramid fibers, and low-density microspheres to balance structural strength, thermal resistance, and pressure tolerance.
residual_terms: ["cross-linkable polymer base", "reinforcing fillers", "low-density microspheres", "structural strength", "thermal resistance", "pressure tolerance"]

abstract: A system may include a seat assembly. The seat assembly may include a seat base, a seat portion mounted to the seat base, and an armrest assembly configured to be in an up position or a down position. The armrest assembly may include a handle operable by a user to lock or unlock at least one functionality of at least one adjustable seat assembly feature. Operation of the handle may be configured at least to: unlock the at least one functionality of at least one adjustable seat assembly feature while locking the armrest assembly from moving between the up position and the down position.
problem: Managing the interaction between an armrest's positional state and a seat's adjustable features to prevent unintended movement during adjustment.
constraint: The armrest's positional lock and the seat feature's unlock must be mechanically coupled so that one action directly enforces the other's state.
mechanism: A single actuation input drives two mechanically coupled state transitions: one component's release is directly enforced by another component's fixation, ensuring that enabling one function simultaneously disables the other through a shared mechanical linkage.
mechanism_raw: A single handle operation simultaneously triggers two mechanically linked state changes: unlocking a seat feature while locking the armrest's position, ensuring coordinated control of interdependent components.

abstract: A machine to work a box-like element or similar includes a cutting unit to cut a strip-like element on a corresponding lying plane in a first substantially plane configuration; a loading unit with a thrust blade translatable in a first direction; a folding and insertion unit having a housing seating of the strip-like element that is directed substantially orthogonally to said lying plane, so that after translation of the thrust blade in said first direction the strip-like element is introduced into said housing seating, assumes a “U” shape and has flaps and a connection part; said folding and insertion unit being translatable in a second direction to at least partly insert said flaps in a slit in the box-like element; and an attachment unit of part of said flaps inside said box-like element on which the slit is made, so that the connection part protrudes from the box-like element.
problem: Automating the formation of a box-like structure with integrated flaps and connection parts from a flat strip-like element.
constraint: Each mechanical stage must align with the previous step's output, requiring orthogonal motion paths and synchronized timing to avoid misalignment during insertion and attachment.
mechanism: A sequence of directionally constrained mechanical operations—separating, advancing, bending into a U-shape, inserting extensions through an aperture, and securing them—transforms a flat element into a three-dimensional structure through precisely timed, orthogonal movements.
mechanism_raw: A sequence of orthogonal mechanical operations—cutting, thrusting, folding into a U-shape, inserting flaps into a slit, and attaching them—transforms the strip into the final structure through precisely timed, directionally constrained movements.

abstract: A method for manufacturing pouches made of at least partly thermoplastic material, including the steps of superimposing at least two webs of at least partly thermoplastic material, joining the webs at adhesion regions or lines, and cutting the webs at cutting regions or lines in order to provide pouches. In a condition in which the webs are superimposed, the method further includes the step of mutually aligning the webs by causing the elongation of at least one of the two webs via the application of heat.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment of superimposed thermoplastic webs before joining them to form pouches.
constraint: Heat application must be precisely regulated to achieve sufficient elongation for alignment without causing material degradation or uneven deformation.
mechanism: Applying heat to one layer induces controlled thermal elongation, dynamically adjusting its length to match the other layer's dimensions during the superimposed state, enabling precise alignment before joining.
mechanism_raw: Applying heat to one web induces controlled thermal elongation, dynamically adjusting its length to match the other web's dimensions during the superimposed state.

abstract: Provided is an electric work vehicle having a simple configuration, yet allowing a hydraulic cylinder to function appropriately even in a low-temperature environment. An electric work vehicle includes a first hydraulic cylinder, a second hydraulic cylinder and a third hydraulic cylinder and includes also a hydraulic system for feeding work oil to these hydraulic cylinders and a traveling motor. The hydraulic system includes an oil heating circuit for heating the work oil using heat generated from the traveling motor.
problem: Maintaining hydraulic fluid performance in low-temperature environments without adding dedicated heating components.
constraint: The heating circuit must efficiently transfer motor waste heat to the oil without compromising the motor's primary function or introducing thermal inefficiencies.
mechanism: Waste heat generated by a moving mechanical element is captured and transferred via an integrated thermal circuit to warm a working fluid, sustaining its viscosity and functionality without dedicated heating components.
mechanism_raw: Waste heat generated by the traveling motor is repurposed via an integrated oil heating circuit to warm the hydraulic work oil, sustaining its viscosity and functionality.

abstract: Methods and systems for providing an availability status associated with a facility. One system includes a visual indicator associated with a facility subsystem of the facility and a sensor configured to detect data associated with the facility subsystem. The system also includes a controller communicatively coupled to the visual indicator and the sensor. The controller is configured to receive a data from the sensor. The controller is also configured to determine a current availability status associated with the facility subsystem based on the data received from the sensor. The controller is also configured to control the visual indicator to indicate the current availability status associated with the facility subsystem.
problem: Providing real-time, localized visual feedback about the operational status of a facility subsystem.
constraint: The controller must process sensor data and update the indicator rapidly enough to reflect real-time status changes without introducing latency or ambiguity.
mechanism: A sensor detects subsystem data, a controller processes it to determine availability status, and a visual indicator directly reflects that status, creating a closed-loop feedback system that provides real-time, localized operational visibility.
mechanism_raw: A sensor detects subsystem data, a controller processes it to determine availability status, and a visual indicator directly reflects that status, creating a closed-loop feedback system.

abstract: A combustion-resistant branch assembly for an artificial tree, the branch assembly including a first branch portion including a first rod having a main portion intermediate a first end portion and a second end portion; a first group of sub-branches attached to the first branch portion, each sub-branch of the first group of sub-branches including a member having a first end portion; and a first winding, including a combustion-resistant strand, wrapped about the first end portion of the first rod of the first branch portion and the first end portion of each sub-branch of the first group of sub-branches, thereby attaching the first group of sub-branches to the first branch portion.
problem: Attaching sub-branches to a main branch in an artificial tree while providing combustion resistance.
constraint: Balancing structural integrity of the branch assembly with the need for uniform distribution of combustion-resistant material without compromising attachment strength.
mechanism: A continuous filament of fire-resistant material is helically wound around the intersection of a primary support member and secondary support members, simultaneously forming a mechanical bond that resists tensile separation and depositing flame-retardant material at the stress-concentrated junction where failure is most likely to propagate.
mechanism_raw: A winding composed of a combustion-resistant strand is wrapped around the junction points of the main branch and sub-branches, simultaneously securing them mechanically and embedding fire-resistant material at critical connection points.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to a voltage regulating circuit, including an impedance circuit, a control unit and a power supply circuit. The impedance circuit has a first node and a second node, wherein the second node is electrically coupled to a load. The control unit is electrically coupled to the first node and configured to control a first voltage value of the first node according to a control signal. An input terminal of the power supply circuit is electrically coupled to the second node. An output of the power supply circuit is electrically coupled to the load. The power supply circuit is configured d to output a control voltage to the load according to a second voltage value of the second node.
problem: Regulating voltage delivered to a load in a power supply circuit despite varying load conditions.
constraint: Maintaining stability and responsiveness in the control loop while avoiding oscillations or delays caused by interactions between the two voltage regulation stages.
mechanism: A hierarchical feedback control architecture employs two nested control loops: an outer loop adjusts a primary control variable based on a reference signal, and an inner loop regulates a secondary variable closer to the output load, with the inner loop responding faster to disturbances so that the outer loop sees a stabilized intermediate condition, thereby decoupling steady-state accuracy from transient response.
mechanism_raw: A dual-node feedback control system where a control unit adjusts the voltage at a first node based on a control signal, and a power supply circuit responds to the voltage at a second node (closer to the load) to dynamically adjust its output, creating a cascaded regulation loop.
residual_terms: ["hierarchical feedback control architecture", "nested control loops", "outer loop", "inner loop", "intermediate condition"]

abstract: A method of preparing a superabsorbent polymer, which enables the preparation of the superabsorbent polymer exhibiting an improved absorption rate while maintaining excellent absorption performances is provided. The method of preparing the superabsorbent polymer includes carrying out a crosslinking polymerization of a water-soluble ethylene-based unsaturated monomer having acidic groups which are at least partially neutralized, in the presence of an internal crosslinking agent having a predetermined chemical structure to form a water-containing gel polymer, gel-pulverizing the water-containing gel polymer, drying, pulverizing, and size-sorting the gel-pulverized water-containing gel polymer to form a base polymer powder, and carrying out a surface crosslinking of the base polymer powder by a heat treatment in the presence of a surface crosslinking agent, wherein the gel-pulverizing is carried out by extruding the water-containing gel polymer through a porous plate having a plurality of holes using a screw extruder mounted inside a cylindrical pulverizer under a condition that a chopping index is 28 (/s) or more.
problem: Improving the absorption rate of a superabsorbent polymer while maintaining its absorption capacity.
constraint: Achieving sufficient mechanical energy input during extrusion to structure the polymer without degrading its molecular integrity or causing excessive heat damage.
mechanism: A polymer gel is subjected to high-shear mechanical comminution through a perforated barrier under controlled energy input, fragmenting the gel into smaller particles while preserving molecular structure, thereby increasing surface-area-to-volume ratio and creating a more open pore network that accelerates liquid acquisition without reducing total absorbent capacity.
mechanism_raw: Controlled mechanical processing of the gel polymer via screw extrusion through a porous plate under a specified chopping index (≥28/s), which creates a base polymer with optimized pore structure and surface area for faster liquid absorption.
residual_terms: ["polymer gel", "high-shear mechanical comminution", "perforated barrier", "surface-area-to-volume ratio", "pore network", "absorbent capacity"]

abstract: A vehicle-mounted equipment control device includes a controller configured to cause equipment of any of a headlight, a wiper, and an air-conditioning device to continue a visual securing operation for securing visibility of a driver of a vehicle even after driving control of the vehicle is switched from automated driving control to manual driving control regardless of an operation mode of the equipment specified by an operation switch for setting an operation of the equipment when an operation mode executed by the equipment immediately before driving control of the vehicle is switched from automated driving control to manual driving control is an operation mode corresponding to the visual securing operation.
problem: Ensuring continued visibility for a driver when transitioning vehicle control from automated to manual driving.
constraint: Preventing unintended deactivation of critical visibility systems during control transitions while allowing manual override when the driver intentionally adjusts settings.
mechanism: A state-aware override controller monitors the operational mode of a vehicle subsystem prior to a control-transition event; if the subsystem was in a safety-critical visibility mode, the controller inhibits manual input from changing that mode, maintaining the safety-critical function until an explicit driver command is received to alter it, thereby preventing inadvertent deactivation during the transition.
mechanism_raw: A controller overrides the equipment's operation mode specified by a switch if the pre-transition mode was a 'visual securing operation' (e.g., headlights, wipers), forcing the equipment to maintain that mode regardless of manual input until the driver explicitly changes it.
residual_terms: ["state-aware override controller", "control-transition event", "safety-critical visibility mode", "inhibits manual input", "explicit driver command"]

abstract: An integrated energy optimizer having an edge side and a cloud side. The edge side may incorporate an energy optimizer, a building management system connected to the energy optimizer, a controller connected to the building management system, and equipment connected to the controller. The cloud side may have a cloud connected to the energy optimizer and to the building management system, and a user interface connected to the cloud. Data from the field sensor may go to the optimizer and the building management system. The data may be processed at the optimizer and the building management system for proper settings at the building management system.
problem: Optimizing energy usage across building systems with distributed sensors and actuators.
constraint: Balancing latency-sensitive local control decisions with computationally intensive cloud-based analytics to avoid delays in critical energy adjustments.
mechanism: A distributed processing framework partitions sensor data analysis between a local processing node colocated with actuators and a remote centralized processor; the local node executes time-critical control decisions with minimal latency, while the remote processor performs computationally intensive optimization and long-horizon planning, with results communicated back to refine local control targets, creating a latency-tolerant hierarchical control system.
mechanism_raw: Data from field sensors is processed both locally (at an edge optimizer and building management system) and remotely (at a cloud server), with local processing enabling rapid adjustments and cloud processing enabling long-term optimization and user interface feedback.
residual_terms: ["distributed processing framework", "local processing node", "remote centralized processor", "time-critical control decisions", "long-horizon planning", "hierarchical control system"]

abstract: Described herein are transistor arrangements fabricated by forming a metal gate cut as a trench that is non-selective to the gate sidewalls, in an etch process that can remove both the gate electrode materials and the surrounding dielectrics. Such an etch process may provide improvements in terms of accuracy, cost-efficiency, and device performance, compared to conventional approaches to forming metal gate cuts. In addition, such a process may be used to provide power rails, if the trench of a metal gate cut is to be at least partially filled with an electrically conductive material. Because the electrically conductive material is in the trench and may be in between the fins, as opposed to being provided over the fins, such power rails may be referred to as “recessed.” Providing recessed power rails may provide improvements in terms of reduced metal line resistance and reduced voltage droop.
problem: Inaccurate, costly, or performance-limited formation of metal gate cuts and power rails in transistor arrangements.
constraint: Balancing etch selectivity to remove multiple materials without damaging adjacent structures while maintaining cost-efficiency and device performance.
mechanism: Employing a non-selective removal process to create a trench that eliminates multiple material types in a single step, followed by depositing a conductive filler to form recessed conductive pathways between structural elements.
mechanism_raw: Using a non-selective etch process to create a trench that removes both gate electrode materials and surrounding dielectrics in a single step, then filling the trench with conductive material to form recessed power rails between fins.

abstract: An electronic device includes a substrate layer having a front surface and a back surface opposite the front surface, a plurality of ultrasonic transducers formed on the front surface of the substrate layer, wherein the plurality of ultrasonic transducers generate backward waves during operation, the backward waves propagating through the substrate layer, and a plurality of substrate structures formed within the back surface of the substrate layer, the plurality of substrate structures configured to modify the backward waves during the operation.
problem: Uncontrolled or inefficient propagation of backward waves in ultrasonic transducers through a substrate, limiting device functionality.
constraint: Designing substrate structures that effectively alter wave propagation without interfering with transducer operation or introducing unwanted signal distortion.
mechanism: Integrating structural elements within a surface of a medium to alter wave propagation characteristics during operation, enabling controlled modification of backward wave behavior without disrupting primary functionality.
mechanism_raw: Integrating substrate structures within the back surface of the substrate to modify backward wave propagation during operation, enabling tailored wave behavior for improved performance.

abstract: Methods, apparatus, systems and articles of manufacture are disclosed that provide an apparatus to analyze vehicle perspectives, the apparatus comprising a profile generator to generate a first profile of an environment based on a profile template and first data generated by a first vehicle; a data analyzer to: determine a difference between the first profile and a second profile obtained from a first one of one or more nodes in the environment; and in response to a trigger event, update the first profile based on the difference; and a vehicle control system to: in response to the trigger event, update a first perspective of the environment based on one or more of second data from the first one of the one or more nodes or the updated first profile; update a path plan for the first vehicle based on the updated first perspective; and execute the updated path plan.
problem: Static or outdated environmental perspectives in autonomous vehicles, leading to suboptimal path planning and navigation.
constraint: Ensuring timely and accurate integration of node data with the baseline profile to avoid instability or delays in path execution.
mechanism: Generating a reference environmental model, continuously comparing it with real-time data from distributed sensing nodes, and dynamically adjusting a navigation plan in response to detected trigger events.
mechanism_raw: Generating a baseline environmental profile, comparing it with real-time data from distributed nodes, and dynamically updating the vehicle's perspective and path plan in response to trigger events.

abstract: A TDC (Time-To-Digital Converter) includes: a DLL (Delay Locked Loop) to delay a stop signal applied from an external element and to output a multi-phase signal; a synchronizer to synchronize the stop signal with a clock signal by using the multi-phase signal, and to output a synchronized stop signal; a counter to output a counter value by using the synchronized stop signal applied from the synchronizer; and a time information calculator to calculate time information of the stop signal based on the counter value and the multi-phase signal.
problem: Inaccurate or low-resolution time-to-digital conversion in timing measurement systems.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization accuracy and minimizing phase drift to ensure precise time measurement across varying operating conditions.
mechanism: Using a phase-aligned signal generator to synchronize a timing reference with a target signal, then deriving time measurement data from counter values and phase alignment states.
mechanism_raw: Using a delay-locked loop to generate multi-phase signals, synchronizing a stop signal with a clock via these phases, and calculating time information based on counter values and phase alignment.

abstract: A braided vaso-occlusive member formed out of first plurality of filaments interwoven with a second plurality of filaments, wherein filaments of the first plurality are helically wound in a first rotational direction along an elongate axis of the braided member, and filaments of the second plurality are wound in a second rotational direction opposite the first rotational direction, such that filaments of the first plurality cross over and/or under filaments of the second plurality at each of a plurality cross-over locations axially spaced along the elongate axis of the braided member, wherein at each cross-over location, the filaments of the first plurality cross over at least two consecutive filaments of the second plurality, then cross under only a single filament of the second plurality, and then cross over at least two additional consecutive filaments of the second plurality.
problem: Inconsistent mechanical properties (e.g., flexibility, strength) in braided structures due to uniform or random filament crossover patterns.
constraint: Achieving precise crossover spacing and filament alignment to balance structural integrity with desired flexibility or compressibility.
mechanism: Helically winding two filament groups in opposing rotational directions with a repeating crossover sequence to control mechanical behavior through structured interlocking patterns.
mechanism_raw: Helically winding two sets of filaments in opposite directions with a repeating crossover pattern (over two, under one, over two) to control mechanical behavior through structured interlocking.

abstract: A portable pet door is provided. The portable pet door includes a plurality of panels (101) connected in such a manner that allows the pet door to be folded for portability when not in use. The portable pet door may be installed in a sliding door jamb and configured to be held in place via friction from the sliding door (110) and an adjacent door jamb. The portable pet door has a removable flap (102) located at the bottom of the portable pet door. The portable pet door may have a connector (401) located on a top portion of a top panel of the plurality of panels that allows the pet door to be removably secured to a door jamb.
problem: Creating a portable pet door that can be temporarily installed in a sliding door jamb without permanent modifications.
constraint: Balancing portability (foldable panels, removable flap) with the need for stable installation via friction and connector engagement.
mechanism: Using existing structural friction and a detachable mechanical interface to temporarily secure a device in place without permanent attachment, enabling portability while maintaining installation stability.
mechanism_raw: Using friction from an existing structure (the sliding door) and a removable connector to hold the device in place, allowing portability while maintaining secure installation.

abstract: A conveyance roller is configured to convey a sheet having passed through a fixing device toward a photosensitive drum. A gear train is switchable between a transmission state in which the gear train transmits power from a motor to the conveyance roller and a transmission release state in which the gear train does not transmit the power from the motor to the conveyance roller. A movement member is movable between a first position at which the movement member causes the gear train to be in the transmission state and a second position at which the movement member causes the gear train to be in the transmission release state. A cam is configured to cause a development roller to move between a contact position and a separation position. The movement member is movable between the first position and the second position in conjunction with movement of the cam.
problem: Coordinating the state of a gear train (transmission vs. release) with the movement of a development roller in a printing/fixing system.
constraint: Ensuring precise synchronization between gear train state transitions and roller positioning to avoid mechanical interference or timing errors.
mechanism: Mechanically coupling a cam-driven actuator to both a gear train and a roller system so that state transitions in the gear train occur in direct synchronization with the roller's positional changes via a shared mechanical pathway.
mechanism_raw: Mechanically linking a cam-driven movement member to both the gear train and the development roller, ensuring that the gear train state changes in direct conjunction with the roller's position via a shared movement path.

abstract: Instructions (108) cause a processor (104) to: classify a clinical report for a subject under evaluation by one of anatomical organ or disease; identify and retrieve clinical reports for the same subject from the healthcare data source(s); group the retrieved clinical report by one of anatomical organ or disease; select a group of the clinical report, wherein the group includes reports for a same or related one of the anatomical organ or the disease; build a model that predicts semantic relationships between nodes in the reports in the selected group of reports based on one or more of extracted parameters or keywords; compare one of the parameter values or the keywords across the reports using the model; construct a graphical timeline of the reports; highlight differences in the parameter values or the keywords based on a result of the compare; and visually present the graphical timeline with the highlighted differences.
problem: Organizing and visualizing heterogeneous clinical data to highlight temporal changes in parameters or keywords across related reports.
constraint: Accurately modeling semantic relationships across diverse data types while maintaining temporal coherence in the visualization.
mechanism: Grouping heterogeneous data by shared semantic attributes, applying a predictive model to compare parameter variations across grouped data, and constructing a temporal visualization that highlights differences based on model-derived comparisons.
mechanism_raw: Grouping reports by shared attributes (organ/disease), building a predictive model to compare parameters/keywords across reports, and constructing a timeline with highlighted differences based on model outputs.

abstract: A general-purpose engine is provided with an engine body having an exhaust system part connected to a cylinder, and also with a cooling mechanism for cooling the engine body. The cooling mechanism is provided with a cooling fan which rotates to generate a cooling air flow, a discharge section which discharges the cooling air flow generated by the rotation of the cooling fan and a cooling air flow opening which is disposed in the upper part of a partition for separating a cylinder chamber having the cylinder provided therein from a muffler chamber having a canister muffler provided therein, connects the cylinder head side of the cylinder chamber and the upper side of the muffler chamber, and causes a cooling air flow to flow from the cylinder head side of the cylinder chamber to the muffler chamber.
problem: Cooling an engine body efficiently while integrating with existing exhaust and muffler systems without adding separate cooling components.
constraint: Balancing cooling efficiency with structural integration, ensuring airflow does not interfere with exhaust or muffler functions.
mechanism: Routing fluid flow through a partitioned pathway between two chambers of an integrated system, using one chamber as part of the flow path to enhance cooling efficiency without adding separate components.
mechanism_raw: Routing cooling airflow through a partition between the cylinder and muffler chambers, leveraging the muffler chamber as part of the cooling path to enhance airflow from the cylinder head.

abstract: An ultrasonic diagnosis apparatus according to an embodiment includes a transmission unit, a reception unit, a generator, and a display controller. The transmission unit causes an ultrasonic probe to transmit a displacement-producing ultrasonic wave and causes the probe to transmit a displacement-observing ultrasonic wave. The reception unit generates reflected-wave data based on a reflected wave received by the probe. The generator calculates displacement at each of a plurality of positions in the scan area over a plurality of time phases, based on the reflected-wave data, determines a time phase when the calculated displacement is substantially maximum, for each of the positions, and generates image data representing positions where the determined time phases are substantially the same as each other, among the positions. The display controller superimposes an image based on the image data on a medical image corresponding to an area including the scan area.
problem: Visualizing tissue displacement dynamics during ultrasonic imaging to highlight regions with synchronized mechanical behavior.
constraint: Accurately capturing and synchronizing displacement data across multiple spatial positions and time phases to avoid artifacts in the final image.
mechanism: Analyzing temporal displacement data across spatial positions to identify phase alignment of maximum displacement events, then generating a composite image highlighting regions with synchronized mechanical behavior.
mechanism_raw: Calculating displacement over time phases, identifying the phase of maximum displacement for each position, and generating an image based on positions where these phases align, then superimposing this on a medical image.

abstract: A weight lifting support shirt includes a chest support portion, a first arm support portion, a second arm support portion, a neck relief portion, a torso support portion, a first lateral extension, and a second lateral extension. A grid plate is disposed about a center of the chest support portion. The grid plate resists stretching of material of the chest support portion when a weight is lowered by a lifter and stores energy of the weight when the weight is lowered during a workout. The grid plate rebounds the stored energy into a chest portion and arms of the lifter when the weight is lifted by the lifter during the workout. The grid plate comprises a figure eight stitching. The figure eight stitching directs load and energy received from multiple angles during the workout, towards the center of the chest support portion.
problem: Providing dynamic support and energy return during weightlifting to reduce strain on the lifter's chest and arms.
constraint: Balancing energy storage capacity with flexibility to allow natural movement while maintaining structural integrity under variable loads.
mechanism: A resilient network structure stores energy when deformed under load and releases stored energy to support adjacent body regions during movement. The network directs multidirectional forces toward a central region to optimize energy transfer efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A grid plate with figure-eight stitching stores energy when the material is stretched during weight lowering and rebounds the stored energy into the lifter's chest and arms during lifting. The stitching directs multidirectional loads toward the center of the chest support portion, enabling efficient energy transfer.

abstract: A substrate processing method is provided. In the method, a substrate is provided. A monomer that is chemically bonded to the substrate is supplied onto the substrate. An initiator for polymerizing the monomer is supplied to the substrate having the supplied monomer thereon, thereby forming a polymer film.
problem: Forming a uniform polymer film on a substrate with controlled chemical bonding and polymerization.
constraint: Ensuring the monomer adheres to the substrate before initiator application to prevent delamination or uneven polymerization.
mechanism: A surface treatment applies a bonding agent to a substrate, followed by localized activation of a polymerization trigger to form a cohesive film. The sequential application ensures adhesion precedes structural formation to prevent premature curing or delamination.
mechanism_raw: A monomer chemically bonds to the substrate surface, followed by localized application of an initiator to trigger polymerization. This sequential bonding and polymerization ensures adhesion and film formation without premature curing.

abstract: A high frequency ultrasound array having a number of transducer elements that are formed in sheet of piezoelectric material. A frame having a coefficient of thermal expansion similar to that of the piezoelectric material surrounds the piezoelectric material and is separated from the piezoelectric material by an epoxy material. Kerf cuts that define the individual elements in the sheet of piezoelectric material extend across a full width of the sheet. In some embodiments, sub-dice kerf cuts that divide a single transducer element into two or more sub-elements also extend all the way across the width of the sheet. A lens positioned in front of the transducer elements can have a radius machined therein to focus ultrasound signals. The frame, transducer elements and lens are bent or curved with the desired radius to focus ultrasound signals.
problem: Creating a high-frequency ultrasound array with precise focusing and thermal stability.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the piezoelectric sheet during kerf cutting and bending while ensuring acoustic focusing accuracy.
mechanism: A thermally matched support structure maintains dimensional stability during temperature fluctuations. Precision cuts define discrete functional elements, while geometric alignment between a focusing element and the cut structure ensures acoustic energy concentration.
mechanism_raw: A frame with a thermal expansion coefficient matching the piezoelectric material minimizes stress during temperature changes. Kerf cuts define individual transducer elements, while sub-dice cuts enable sub-element segmentation. A curved lens focuses ultrasound signals by aligning with the bent/curved transducer and frame geometry.

abstract: Offshore terminal apparatus which in various examples comprises a floating storage vessel which is spread-moored in fixed heading orientation to a seabed offshore by spread mooring lines, the floating storage vessel comprising a hull having bow and stern ends and which at either or both the bow end and the stern end is fitted with an extension section and includes coupling means on the extension section to couple spread mooring lines to the floating storage vessel.
problem: Maintaining a floating storage vessel in a fixed heading orientation offshore despite environmental forces.
constraint: Balancing mooring line tension and hull extension design to resist dynamic offshore forces without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Distributed tensioning elements attached to extended structural sections counteract rotational forces by balancing opposing loads. The extended sections distribute forces through coupling points to maintain a fixed orientation under dynamic environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: Spread mooring lines attached to extension sections at the bow and stern ends of the hull allow controlled tensioning to counteract rotational forces. The fixed-heading orientation is maintained by distributing mooring forces through the extension sections and coupling points.

abstract: A combined microalgae and mycorrhizal fungi granular formulation includes a microalgae inoculant combined with a mycorrhizal fungi inoculant with demineralized water to maintain moisture and applied to carrier granules such as a natural clay-based or mineral-based material. The coated granules are dried and may be applied to agricultural areas in dried granular form.
problem: Combining two distinct biological inoculants (microalgae and mycorrhizal fungi) into a stable, transportable granular formulation.
constraint: Ensuring compatibility between the two biological agents and the carrier material to prevent degradation during drying and storage.
mechanism: A moisture-retaining coating process encapsulates biological agents onto a porous carrier substrate. The carrier provides structural integrity and controlled release, while a drying phase preserves agent viability until deployment.
mechanism_raw: Demineralized water maintains moisture for both organisms during coating onto carrier granules. The clay- or mineral-based carrier provides structural support and controlled release, while drying preserves viability of both inoculants until application.

abstract: A monolithic attitude control motor frame includes a monolithic structure including an outer surface of revolution and a plurality of side walls defining a plurality of cavities extending radially from the outer surface of revolution. Adjacent cavities of the plurality of cavities share a side wall or side wall portion therebetween. Each of the cavities is configured to receive an attitude control motor. A monolithic attitude control motor system includes a monolithic frame including an outer surface of revolution and a plurality of side walls defining a plurality of cavities extending radially from the outer surface of revolution. The system further includes a plurality of attitude control motors corresponding to the plurality of cavities, such that an attitude control motor of the plurality of attitude control motors is disposed in each cavity of the plurality of cavities.
problem: Integrating multiple attitude control motors into a compact, structurally sound system without increasing part count or compromising mechanical integrity.
constraint: Balancing cavity density (to maximize motor count) against structural rigidity (to maintain frame integrity under operational loads).
mechanism: A single structural unit with interconnected chambers arranged around a central axis allows each component to occupy a dedicated chamber while relying on shared walls between chambers to provide structural support, reducing assembly complexity and maintaining integrity under operational loads.
mechanism_raw: A monolithic frame with radially extending cavities that share side walls allows each motor to be housed in its own cavity while using the shared walls as structural support, reducing weight and assembly complexity compared to discrete mounting structures.

abstract: An example operation may include one or more of receiving, by a retailer node, an encrypted inventory of goods data from a plurality of supplier nodes over a blockchain network, computing, by the retailer node, an ordering proportion based on the encrypted inventory of goods data, generating, by the retailer node, an ordering policy based on the ordering proportion, and executing a smart contract to order goods from the plurality of the supplier nodes based on the ordering policy.
problem: Enabling a retailer to autonomously determine and execute optimal ordering quantities from multiple suppliers while preserving data privacy and trust in a decentralized environment.
constraint: Maintaining data confidentiality (via encryption) while ensuring the computed ordering policy remains accurate and executable without real-time supplier coordination.
mechanism: A decentralized system receives encrypted data from multiple sources, computes a policy based on that data without exposing raw information, and uses an automated execution mechanism to enforce the policy, ensuring decision-making remains accurate while preserving data confidentiality.
mechanism_raw: Receiving encrypted inventory data from suppliers over a blockchain, computing an ordering proportion based on that data, and using a smart contract to automatically execute orders according to a derived policy, thereby decoupling decision-making from direct data exposure.

abstract: The present invention provides a conductive fabric comprising base cloth and a conductive metallic circuit structure formed on the surface of the base cloth. The conductive metallic circuit structure comprises at least one metallic seed layer and at least one chemical-plating layer. The metallic seed layer is an evaporation-deposition layer or a sputter-deposition layer and has a circuit pattern. The chemical-plating layer is applied over the surface of the metallic seed layer. The conductive fabric has improved conductivity and heat generation efficiency.
problem: Creating a flexible fabric with high electrical conductivity and efficient heat generation without sacrificing mechanical flexibility or durability.
constraint: Ensuring adhesion and continuity between the seed layer and plating layer while preserving the fabric's flexibility and resistance to cracking during use.
mechanism: A layered approach deposits a conductive pattern onto a flexible base material, then builds up conductive pathways through a secondary deposition process, combining precise patterning with bulk conductivity while maintaining mechanical flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Depositing a metallic seed layer with a defined circuit pattern onto a base cloth, then applying a chemical-plating layer over it to build up conductive pathways, combining the precision of deposition with the bulk conductivity of plating.

abstract: A mascara brush having a centre made of at least two wire sections twisted together along a longitudinal axis of the wire core, and having a bristle covering made of plastic bristles formed by filaments, each of which bristles is held in a clamping manner between the two wire sections, and which bristles are formed with a wedge-shaped bristle tip or without a wedge-shaped bristle tip on their free ends. At least one portion of the bristles has a bristle coating made of a first softer material, and a bristle core that is joined to the bristle coating and made of a second harder material, and at least these bristles have a transverse cut, in the form of a simple wedge, on one side or on two sides, at least partially on their radially outward free ends, and comprise a wedge-shaped bristle tip having at least one cut surface forming a wedge.
problem: Achieving effective application and grooming of mascara using a brush that balances gentle contact with precise product delivery.
constraint: Balancing the softness of the bristle coating (for gentle application) with the hardness of the core (for structural integrity and defined tip geometry).
mechanism: A multi-material bristle design incorporates a rigid internal core surrounded by a softer outer layer, with geometric features such as tapered tips and segmented cuts to create variable stiffness and surface texture for controlled product delivery and application pressure.
mechanism_raw: Twisting two wire sections to form a core with bristles clamped between them, where individual bristles have a softer outer coating and harder core, combined with wedge-shaped tips and transverse cuts to create variable stiffness and surface texture for controlled product release and application.
residual_terms: ["multi-material bristle design", "rigid internal core", "softer outer layer", "variable stiffness"]

abstract: A turning thread automatic diagnosing method includes collecting a spindle actual speed and a feeding shaft actual speed of a lathe; based upon the spindle actual speed and the feeding shaft actual speed, continuously calculating thread errors to obtain a thread error curve; and analyzing an error cause according to the thread error curve. In addition, a turning thread automatic diagnosing system is disclosed, using the method. A data processing system and a storage medium are also disclosed. The technology of the embodiments can automatically identify the problem causing a thread error and provide a corresponding solution.
problem: Automatically identifying the root cause of thread errors in lathe machining without manual inspection or operator intervention.
constraint: Accurately mapping dynamic error signatures to specific failure modes in real time while filtering out noise from normal operational variations.
mechanism: A real-time monitoring system continuously collects operational parameters, generates a dynamic error signature from those parameters, and correlates the signature with predefined failure patterns to identify root causes without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Continuously collecting spindle and feed shaft speeds, calculating real-time thread errors to generate an error curve, and analyzing that curve to correlate error patterns with specific mechanical or operational causes, enabling automated diagnosis and corrective action.

abstract: Disclosed is a device for the automatic removal of rejected eggs from an incubation tray, whereby the device includes a suction power above the egg to suck up the egg, and the device further includes a blowing power against the bottom of the egg to blow away the egg, whereby the blowing power blows an air flow or overpressure against the bottom of the egg. Also disclosed is a method for the automatic removal of one or more rejected eggs from an incubation tray.
problem: Automatically removing rejected eggs from an incubation tray without damaging them.
constraint: Balancing suction and blowing forces to avoid crushing the egg while ensuring reliable removal.
mechanism: Apply opposing attractive and repulsive forces to an object so the attractive force holds the object while the repulsive force displaces it from a surface, with the forces balanced to avoid damaging the object.
mechanism_raw: Using opposing suction and blowing forces to lift and propel the egg, where suction holds the egg while blowing displaces it from the tray.

abstract: A luminaire module (100) includes light-emitting elements (LEEs) (110) arranged to provide light; a light guide (130) including a receiving end (131a) and an opposing end (131b), the receiving end (131a) arranged to receive light provided by the LEEs (110), a core (134) including a first transparent material with a first refractive index (n1), the core (134) having a pair of opposing side surfaces (132a, 132b) extending along a length of the light guide (130) between the receiving and opposing ends (131a, 131b), and a cladding (136) including a second material having a second smaller refractive index (n2), the cladding (136) extending across and being in contact with at least a portion of the opposing side surfaces (132a, 132b) forming a cladding-core interface. The cladding-core interface is optically smooth. Additionally, the luminaire module (100) includes an optical extractor (140) arranged to receive guided light from the opposing end (131b) of the light guide (130) and configured to output into the ambient environment at least some of the received guided light.
reason: The mechanism relies on standard waveguide principles (core-cladding structure and optical extraction) without a novel causal operation beyond known optical design.

abstract: Systems, methods, and non-transitory computer-readable storage media for a fast power network simulator. A system configured per this disclosure can use identify a power network, the power network comprising generators, transmission lines, and loads, and receive a model of the power network. The model of the power network can include: models of the generators modeled as differential equations, and models of the transmission lines and the loads modeled as algebraic equations. The system can convert, via a processor, the algebraic equations of the models of the transmission lines and the loads to additional differential equations, then combine, via the processor, the differential equations and the additional differential equations, to yield combined differential equations. The system can then iteratively solve linear equations, via the processor, associated with the combined differential equations, to yield solutions, and output the solutions as part of a power simulation of the power network.
problem: Efficiently simulating power networks with mixed differential and algebraic equations.
constraint: Maintaining accuracy while reducing computational complexity through equation type unification.
mechanism: Transform a system of mixed equation types into a unified equation type so that iterative linear solving can be applied to reduce computational complexity while maintaining accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Converting algebraic equations (transmission lines, loads) into differential equations to unify the system, enabling iterative linear solving for faster computation.

abstract: A support plate for supporting a package during filling with a food product is disclosed. The support plate can include a wall defining a cavity for receiving a top portion of the package. The wall has a slanted interior surface that is complementary to the top portion of the package. The support plate also comprises a support projection extending in a parallel direction to and away from the wall, the support projection being complementary to and for abutting the top portion of the package, wherein the top portion can include a concave top surface and a second concave surface. A system that can include the support plate for use in a filling machine and a filling machine that can include a plurality of the systems are also disclosed.
reason: The mechanism is a shape-specific mechanical design tailored to a particular package geometry, lacking a generalizable causal principle.

abstract: A lighting system for providing uniform bright lighting of products within in a glass door refrigerated cabinet. The lighting system has a frame member with an angled wing extending therefrom that wraps around a side edge of a light-transmitting optical shield, and a LED lighting strip positioned between the frame member and the optical shield. The LED lighting strip has a plurality of spaced-apart LED lights mounted therealong with a coined reflective facet optic mounted around each LED light. The angled wing(s) reflects light emitted laterally outwards from the at least one LED lighting strip such that the light can be re-directed to evenly illuminate products in a refrigerated cabinet. The angled wing(s) also protects a user's fingers from cracking the plastic optical shield which can become brittle in the cool or cold temperatures of the refrigerated cabinet.
problem: Providing uniform bright lighting in a refrigerated cabinet while protecting the optical shield from physical damage.
constraint: Balancing light redirection efficiency with structural protection to avoid brittleness-related damage.
mechanism: Use angled reflective surfaces to redirect laterally emitted light back into a target volume to increase uniformity, while a protective barrier shields the reflective surfaces from physical damage.
mechanism_raw: Using angled reflective wings to redirect laterally emitted light back into the cabinet, increasing uniformity, while physically shielding the optical component.

abstract: A helmet stabilization system and apparatus for reducing the incidence of whiplash and neck injuries while wearing a helmet, such as in contact sports. The invention includes a helmet mount; a base mount configured for attachment to a shoulder harness; and a flex rod interconnectable between the helmet mount and the base mount. The flex rod, when interconnected between the helmet mount and the base mount provides a resistance to an extension or a compression sequence responsive to a contact imparted on the helmet. An oobleck may be provided in a coupling between the flex rod and the base mount to permit voluntary head movements of the user and to provide a resistance responsive to an impact force.
problem: Reducing whiplash and neck injuries from impacts while allowing voluntary head movement during normal use.
constraint: Balancing voluntary head mobility with sufficient impact resistance to prevent injury.
mechanism: Use a rate-sensitive coupling between two components that provides low resistance to slow relative motion but high resistance to rapid relative motion, combined with a resilient element that resists sudden displacement, so that voluntary movement is permitted while impact forces are dynamically opposed.
mechanism_raw: A flex rod provides resistance to sudden extension/compression forces, while an oobleck coupling allows slow voluntary movements but stiffens under rapid impact forces, creating a dynamic resistance that adapts to the rate of applied force.

abstract: An exhaust gas/reactant mixing arrangement is for an exhaust system of an internal combustion engine for mixing exhaust gas and reactant. The mixing arrangement includes an exhaust gas guide housing extending in the direction of a housing longitudinal axis and a housing wall. The housing wall surrounds and defines an exhaust gas duct accommodating a flow of exhaust gas. A mixing zone is formed between an upstream end wall and a downstream end wall arranged downstream of the upstream end wall. The mixing zone includes a first chamber and a second chamber as well as a reactant dispensing unit carried on the exhaust gas guide housing for dispensing reactant into the first chamber in a reactant main dispensing direction oriented substantially along a reactant dispensing line.
problem: Efficiently mixing exhaust gas and reactant in an exhaust system without disrupting flow dynamics.
constraint: Maintaining exhaust gas flow continuity while achieving thorough mixing of reactant and exhaust gas.
mechanism: Introduce a reactant into a first chamber of a multi-chamber housing along a defined flow path, generating controlled turbulence that promotes staged mixing with a primary gas stream before the combined flow exits downstream, ensuring homogenization through spatial and directional separation of injection and mixing zones.
mechanism_raw: A multi-chamber housing directs reactant dispensing along a specific line into a first chamber, creating controlled turbulence and staged mixing with exhaust gas before downstream flow, ensuring homogenization through spatial and directional separation of injection and mixing zones.

abstract: A method for extracting naturally occurring oil bodies (oleosomes) from a material containing naturally occurring oil bodies (oleosomes) includes the steps of dispersing the material containing oleosomes in an aqueous composition to thereby obtain an aqueous dispersion of material containing oleosomes, extracting oleosomes from the aqueous dispersion of material containing oleosomes to thereby obtain a crude oleosome extract and isolating crude oleosomes from the extract by drying the crude oleosome extract. The dried oleosome powder may be used with a personal care product, a pharmaceutical product or a food product.
problem: Isolating naturally occurring oil bodies (oleosomes) from a material matrix while preserving their structural integrity.
constraint: Preventing degradation of oleosomes during dispersion, extraction, and drying processes.
mechanism: Disperse a material containing target structures in an aqueous medium to form a suspension that selectively releases the target structures, followed by extraction and drying to isolate intact structures, leveraging aqueous phase interactions to preserve structural integrity throughout the process.
mechanism_raw: Dispersing the material in an aqueous medium to separate oleosomes into a suspension, followed by extraction and drying to isolate intact oleosomes, leveraging aqueous phase interactions to selectively release and concentrate the target structures.

abstract: Disclosed herein are nonwoven webs comprising a nonwoven substrate and a binder comprising a polysaccharide. In one embodiment, the polysaccharide can comprise poly alpha-1,3-glucan, a poly alpha-1,3-glucan ether compound as disclosed herein, a poly alpha-1,3-glucan ester compound as disclosed herein, a graft copolymer comprising a backbone comprising dextran and poly alpha-1,3-glucan side chains, a crosslinked graft copolymer comprising a backbone comprising dextran and poly alpha-1,3-glucan chains, or a mixture thereof. Also disclosed are articles comprising the nonwoven webs, and methods of making the nonwoven webs.
reason: The patent describes specific polysaccharide materials (e.g., poly alpha-1,3-glucan) used as binders in nonwoven webs. While the materials have unique properties, the mechanism is primarily a material composition choice rather than a causal functional process that can be generalized to other fields.

abstract: A two-layer multi-strand cord (60) has a modulus EC such that 50 GPa≤EC≤160 GPa. The cord comprises: (a) an internal layer (CI) of the cord made up of J>1 internal strands (TI) wound in a helix having a modulus EI, each internal strand (TI) comprising: an internal layer (C1) made up of Q≥1 internal threads (F1), and an external layer (C2) made up of N>1 external threads (F2) wound around the internal layer (C1), and (b) an external layer (CE) of the cord made up of L>1 external strands (TE) wound around the internal layer (CI) of the cord, each external strand (TE) comprising: an internal layer (C1′) made up of Q′≥1 internal threads (F1′), and an external layer (C2′) made up of N′>1 external threads (F2′) wound around the internal layer (C1′).
problem: Achieving a controlled modulus (50–160 GPa) in a multi-strand cord while maintaining structural integrity and flexibility.
constraint: Balancing modulus requirements with the mechanical limits of individual thread and strand components.
mechanism: Construct a hierarchical layered structure composed of nested helical thread layers arranged in internal and external strands, distributing mechanical stress across multiple structural tiers to achieve a target modulus through geometric and material synergy while maintaining flexibility.
mechanism_raw: A hierarchical layered structure with internal and external strands, each composed of nested thread layers wound in helices, distributes mechanical stress across multiple structural tiers to achieve the target modulus through geometric and material synergy.
residual_terms: ["hierarchical layered structure", "helical thread layers", "strands", "modulus", "geometric and material synergy", "flexibility"]

abstract: Retention of events of an ordered event stream is disclosed. Expiration of events stored in a segment of an ordered event stream (OES) can be desirable. New events are added to a head of an OES segment, and pruning events from a tail of the OES segment can be valuable. Processing applications can register a processing scheme for a segment, e.g., at-least-once processing, exactly-once processing, etc., and can generate checkpoints indicating a degree of advancement in processing events of the segment. The ordered event stream can determine a cut point indicative of a progress point, that before which, events of an OES can be marked as ready for expiration.
