constraint: The tension must remain even throughout the knitting process to ensure consistent loop formation and prevent chain breakage or irregular fabric structure, while the weighting step must achieve the desired fabric characteristics without over-compacting the knitted architecture.
mechanism: At least one chain of flexibly linked elements is fed into a knitting machine while maintaining even tension on the chain; the knitting machine then interloops the chain links together according to a knitting pattern, transforming the one-dimensional chain into a two-dimensional knitted fabric structure, which is subsequently weighted to set its final form and properties.
mechanism_raw: At least one metal chain of flexibly linked elements is fed into a knitting machine while maintaining even tension on the chain; the knitting machine then interloops the chain links together according to a knitting pattern, transforming the one-dimensional chain into a two-dimensional knitted fabric structure, which is subsequently weighted to set its final form and properties.
residual_terms: ["chain of flexibly linked elements", "knitting machine", "even tension", "interloops", "knitting pattern", "weighted"]

abstract: A pilot burner for a combustor includes an inner conduit configured to deliver a fuel, and an outer conduit concentric with the inner conduit and configured to deliver air. An inner wall defines an inner plenum, and a partition wall is radially outward of the inner wall and defines an intermediate plenum with at least a portion of the inner wall. Exit passages fluidly couple the inner plenum to the intermediate plenum. An outer wall defines an outer plenum with at least a portion of the partition wall. A crossover section includes passages fluidly coupling the inner conduit to the outer plenum, and passages fluidly coupling the outer conduit to the inner plenum. An end plate includes openings to direct fuel, air for combustion, and air for cooling from the respective plenums.
problem: Delivering fuel, combustion air, and cooling air to appropriate locations in a combustor in a controlled manner to ensure proper mixing, combustion, and thermal management.
constraint: The crossover passages and concentric wall arrangement must balance fluid mixing efficiency, pressure drop, and structural integrity while maintaining thermal isolation between streams.
mechanism: A multi-stream fluid routing system uses concentric pathways and cross-coupling passages to exchange different fluid streams between inner and outer conduits. This enables each fluid to be directed to its intended destination (combustion vs. cooling) through dedicated exit passages, allowing staged mixing and targeted thermal management without separate routing hardware.
mechanism_raw: Concentric conduit and plenum architecture with crossover passages that cross-couple different fluid streams: fuel from the inner conduit is routed to the outer plenum, while air from the outer conduit is routed to the inner plenum. This controlled exchange allows each fluid to be directed to its intended destination (combustion vs. cooling) through dedicated exit passages, enabling staged mixing and targeted cooling without separate routing hardware.

abstract: A filling valve for filling a container with a filling product, e.g., a beverage in a beverage filling system, includes a valve base body. The valve base body includes an outlet configured to discharge the filling product into the container; a swirl chamber configured to receive the filling product and is able to be brought into a fluidic connection with the outlet; and a main inlet, which feeds into the swirl chamber and is configured to introduce at least one main component of the filling product into the swirl chamber such that the filling product is swirled in the swirl chamber, whereby after exiting from the outlet the filling product flows downwardly in a spiral movement in the container. The swirl chamber has an annular shape, the cross-sectional contour thereof having a rounded shape, substantially without corner points, in the direction of extent and perpendicular to the direction of extent.
problem: Filling containers with a liquid product (e.g., beverage) in a controlled manner that produces a desired flow pattern (spiral/downward flow) inside the container to minimize splashing, foaming, or uneven filling.
constraint: The annular swirl chamber geometry must balance smooth flow (rounded, corner-free contour) with sufficient swirl generation to achieve the desired spiral flow pattern in the container.
mechanism: A swirl-inducing chamber with an annular geometry and smooth, corner-free internal contour receives a fluid and imparts a rotational motion. The streamlined shape preserves the swirl with minimal turbulence, enabling the fluid to exit in a controlled spiral trajectory for targeted distribution within a receiving vessel.
mechanism_raw: A swirl chamber with an annular shape and rounded cross-sectional contour (substantially without corner points) receives the filling product and imparts a swirling motion. The smooth, corner-free geometry maintains the swirl with minimal turbulence and energy loss, so that upon exiting the outlet, the product continues in a controlled spiral movement downward through the container.

abstract: A cushioning mat comprises a plurality of cushioning bumps arranged in a plurality of rows, the bumps of each row alternating with substantially flat bottom portions. Each bump comprises a top wall and a side wall which extends from a mat base identified by the bottom portions. The top wall and the side wall define an inner bump cavity. The bumps of adjacent rows are staggered with each other. In at least a portion of the side wall a vent opening is made which places in communication the inner cavity of the bump with the outside of the bump.
problem: Providing cushioning with controlled compression characteristics and airflow management to absorb impact while maintaining structural support and consistent performance across the mat surface.
constraint: The vent opening size and placement must balance controlled air escape (for desired damping/compression rate) with sufficient structural integrity of the bump walls to maintain cushioning performance.
mechanism: A compressible cushioning structure incorporates vent openings in its structural elements to regulate airflow during compression. The controlled air escape rate governs compression speed and force, while a staggered arrangement of load-bearing elements distributes applied forces evenly to maintain surface stability.
mechanism_raw: Cushioning bumps with vent openings in their side walls create a controlled airflow path between the inner bump cavity and the outside environment. During compression, air escapes through these vents at a regulated rate, controlling the compression speed and force. The staggered arrangement of bumps with alternating flat bottom portions distributes load evenly and maintains mat stability.

abstract: An injection molding machine includes a screw inserted in an injection cylinder and configured to be movable in an axial direction of the screw, a motor configured to move the screw, a torque detection unit configured to detect a torque of the motor, a position detection unit configured to detect a position of the screw, a motor drive control unit configured to drive the motor to thereby advance the screw to a foremost position in a direction of injection, a processor, and a memory. The processor and memory are configured to determine that unmelted resin remains inside the injection cylinder if the torque of the motor becomes equal to or greater than a limit torque while the screw is advancing to the foremost position.
problem: Detecting whether unmelted resin remains inside an injection cylinder during the injection molding process, which can cause defects in the molded part.
constraint: The torque limit threshold must be calibrated to distinguish between normal screw advancement resistance (fully melted resin) and elevated resistance caused by unmelted resin, avoiding false positives while ensuring reliable detection.
mechanism: A resistance-monitoring system tracks real-time mechanical load during a linear actuation process. By comparing detected load against a calibrated threshold, the system identifies abnormal resistance caused by incomplete material processing and triggers corrective action.
mechanism_raw: Motor torque is monitored in real-time as the screw advances toward its foremost injection position. Unmelted resin increases resistance to screw movement, causing motor torque to rise. By comparing detected torque against a predetermined limit threshold, the system can determine if unmelted resin is present and take corrective action.

abstract: The present invention provides new methods for preparing compound 5, and pharmaceutically acceptable salts thereof, of structure Compound 5, or a pharmaceutically acceptable salt thereof, is an important intermediate in the synthesis of carfilzomib. The invention further provides methods of making a useful manganese catalyst that may be used in the epoxidation step of the present invention.
reason: The abstract only names specific compounds (Compound 5, carfilzomib intermediate) and mentions a manganese catalyst for epoxidation without describing any underlying causal mechanism or generalizable principle. It is a list of chemical synthesis targets and catalyst types rather than an explanation of how a problem is solved through a transferable functional mechanism.

abstract: A mono-crystalline silicon growth apparatus is provided. The mono-crystalline silicon growth apparatus includes a furnace, a support base disposed in the furnace, a crucible disposed on the support base, and a heating module. The support base and the crucible do not rotate relative to the heating module, and an axial direction is defined to be along a central axis of the crucible. The heating module is disposed at an outer periphery of the support base and includes a first heating unit, a second heating unit, and a third heating unit. The first heating unit, the second heating unit, and the third heating unit are respectively disposed at positions with different heights corresponding to the axial direction.
problem: Achieving controlled axial temperature distribution during mono-crystalline silicon growth, where uniform or graded thermal profiles are needed along the crucible height to ensure consistent crystal quality.
constraint: The heating units must be positioned at different heights along the axial direction to control the temperature profile, while the crucible and support base remain stationary relative to the heating module to maintain stable, position-specific heating.
mechanism: Using multiple heat sources positioned at different axial locations around a stationary object to independently control temperature at specific axial positions, creating a tailored axial temperature gradient without requiring relative motion between the object and the heat sources.
mechanism_raw: Using multiple heating units disposed at different axial heights around the crucible, with the crucible and support base held stationary relative to the heating module. This spatial distribution of heat sources at specific heights allows independent control of the temperature at different axial positions, creating a tailored axial temperature gradient without requiring mechanical rotation of the crucible relative to the heaters.

abstract: An ironing panel and an ironing device are related to clothes ironing appliances. The temperature distribution of existing ironing panels is non-uniform during ironing. The ironing panel of the invention comprises a panel body provided with a patch having a patch ironing surface, the patch ironing surface and a main ironing surface are continuous to form a complete ironing surface, and a gap is reserved between the patch and the panel body to form a heat homogenizing cavity. When the ironing panel works, an electric heater transfers heat to the panel body, the main ironing surface away from the electric heater is maintained at a low temperature, and heat from the electric heater is indirectly transferred to the patch ironing surface via the main ironing surface and the heat homogenizing cavity rather than being directly transferred to the patch ironing surface.
problem: Non-uniform temperature distribution across an ironing panel surface during operation, where the region far from the heat source becomes cooler and creates inconsistent ironing performance.
constraint: The gap forming the heat homogenizing cavity must be sized to allow sufficient lateral heat diffusion for temperature homogenization while still maintaining adequate thermal conductivity through the main ironing surface to deliver heat to the patch.
mechanism: Introducing a thermal spreading medium between a heat source and a working surface, where the medium allows lateral heat diffusion to homogenize temperature distribution across the surface before heat is delivered to the target area.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a heat homogenizing cavity (an air gap) between a patch and the main panel body. Heat from the electric heater is transferred to the patch indirectly via the main ironing surface and the heat homogenizing cavity, rather than directly. The cavity acts as a thermal spreading medium that allows heat to diffuse laterally before reaching the patch surface, resulting in a more uniform temperature distribution across the entire ironing surface.

abstract: A heat exchange device includes a core and a housing. The core includes a first collecting part and a second collecting part, and a flat tube part is provided between the two. The flat tube part includes a first flat tube group and a second flat tube group. The first collecting part includes first and second collecting portions, and a separator is formed between the two. Each flat tube of the first flat tube group is communicated with the collecting cavity of the first collecting portion. The collecting cavity of the first collecting portion is communicated with the collecting cavity of the second collecting portion through the first flat tube group, the collecting cavity of the second collecting part, and the second flat tube group.
problem: Achieving efficient heat exchange with controlled fluid flow distribution through collecting parts in a compact heat exchanger configuration.
constraint: The separator must effectively partition the collecting portion into distinct cavities, and the flat tube groups must be arranged to connect these cavities in the desired flow pattern while maintaining structural integrity and minimizing pressure loss.
mechanism: Partitioning a chamber into distinct cavities using a divider, then connecting these cavities through multiple independent flow pathways to create controlled fluid distribution and heat exchange within a compact core structure.
mechanism_raw: Using a separator within a collecting part to divide it into multiple collecting portions with separate cavities, and then connecting these portions through distinct flat tube groups. The first flat tube group connects the cavity of the first collecting portion to the cavity of the second collecting portion, while the second flat tube group provides an additional flow path. This partitioning and selective interconnection creates controlled flow distribution and heat exchange pathways within the core structure.

abstract: A removable module and a housing for an attachment system of a consumer product is described. The removable module includes a locking mechanism comprising a first portion having a substantially planar top surface and second portion that comprises a substantially non-planar bottom surface. The first portion and the second portion are coupled together. The locking mechanism also includes a first spring mechanism coupled between the first portion and the second portion. The first spring mechanism causes the first portion to be biased away from the second portion. The locking mechanism also includes a second spring mechanism. The second spring mechanism causes the substantially planar top surface of the first portion to be biased substantially flush with respect to the removable module and also causes the substantially non-planar bottom surface of the second portion to be biased proud with respect to the removable module.
problem: Creating a removable module attachment system that provides secure locking, proper surface alignment, and easy removal without manual adjustment of individual components.
constraint: The two spring mechanisms must be tuned to work in concert: the first spring provides the separation force needed for the locking action, while the second spring provides the positioning force to ensure proper surface alignment, and both must operate within the mechanical tolerances of the attachment system.
mechanism: Using dual resilient elements acting on different regions of a locking component to simultaneously generate separation force for engagement and positioning force for surface alignment, creating a self-adjusting attachment mechanism that automatically seats surfaces correctly during insertion.
mechanism_raw: Using two spring mechanisms acting on different portions of a locking element. The first spring biases a first portion (with a planar top surface) away from a second portion (with a non-planar bottom surface), creating a separation force. The second spring independently biases the planar top surface to be flush with the module and the non-planar bottom surface to be proud relative to the module. Together, these dual spring forces create a self-aligning, spring-loaded attachment that automatically positions the surfaces correctly when the module is inserted.

abstract: A compound for use in oil recovery includes a quantum dot and a zwitterionic surfactant. The quantum dot has a diameter no greater than 25 nm and the quantum dot is bonded to the zwitterionic surfactant. A nanofluid for use in oil recovery includes the compound described above and a fluid carrier. A method for recovering oil from a formation includes flooding the formation with a nanofluid. The nanofluid has a quantum dot diameter no greater than 25 nm bonded to a zwitterionic surfactant and a fluid carrier.
problem: Enhancing oil recovery efficiency by improving the ability of a fluid to mobilize trapped oil in a formation, where conventional surfactants alone may not provide sufficient penetration or wettability alteration.
constraint: The quantum dot must have a diameter no greater than 25 nm to ensure adequate penetration into the formation pores, and it must be chemically bonded to the zwitterionic surfactant to ensure the hybrid compound functions as a unified agent rather than separate components that may separate during transport.
mechanism: Chemically bonding a nanoscale agent (with size constrained to enable pore penetration) to a surface-active compound to form a unified functional unit that combines enhanced surface interaction properties with surfactant action for synergistic fluid-based material mobilization.
mechanism_raw: Chemically bonding a quantum dot (with diameter no greater than 25 nm) to a zwitterionic surfactant to form a hybrid compound. The quantum dot provides nanoscale properties such as enhanced surface interaction or wettability alteration, while the zwitterionic surfactant provides surface-active properties. The covalent bonding ensures the two components act as a single functional unit, combining their effects synergistically when delivered as a nanofluid to the oil-bearing formation.

abstract: A system to remotely detect and identify an airborne drone presenting a flight risk to piloted aircraft. A warning of the hazardous drone is presented to the piloted aircraft. An airborne drone is observed by any of several means, to include receipt of drone location or identification data broadcast by the drone or broadcast by a ground-based system, or through a piloted aircraft airborne sensor. The safety warning and real-time observation of a hazardous drone may be shared among other piloted aircraft, in particular to other subscribing aircraft approaching the airspace of the hazardous drone.
problem: Detecting and warning about hazardous airborne drones to piloted aircraft, and sharing this information among multiple aircraft in real-time.
constraint: Must operate in real-time with potentially incomplete or delayed information from heterogeneous sources, and must selectively share warnings only with aircraft approaching the relevant airspace to avoid overwhelming recipients with irrelevant alerts.
mechanism: Aggregating observations of a potential hazard from multiple independent sources to identify flight-risk drones, then selectively propagating safety warnings and real-time observations to other aircraft that are approaching the hazard's airspace, creating a distributed early-warning network.
mechanism_raw: Aggregating observations of a potential hazard from multiple independent sources (broadcast data, ground-based systems, aircraft sensors) to identify flight-risk drones, then selectively propagating safety warnings and real-time observations to other aircraft that are approaching the hazard's airspace, creating a distributed early-warning network.

abstract: A system (400) configured to generate an expanded query for an electronic health database, the system comprising: a user interface (410) configured to receive a query comprising a search string and information about a clinical context in which the search is being performed; and a processor (460) comprising: (i) a model creation module (420) configured to generate a clinical information model comprising one or more clinical concepts; (ii) a prioritization module (430) configured to prioritize the one or more clinical concepts identified in the generated clinical information model based on the received information about the clinical context in which the search is being performed and a clinical guideline or management plan for the patient; (iii) a query expansion module (440) configured to create an expanded query using the prioritized clinical concepts; and (iv) a query module (450) configured to query the electronic health database using the expanded query.
problem: Generating effective search queries for electronic health databases that account for the clinical context of the search.
constraint: The concept expansion must remain relevant to the specific clinical context and adhere to clinical guidelines, balancing query comprehensiveness (capturing all relevant results) against precision (avoiding irrelevant results), while operating within the constraints of structured clinical knowledge models.
mechanism: Context-aware query expansion: receiving a user query along with clinical context, generating a domain-specific information model containing relevant concepts, prioritizing those concepts based on the clinical context and established clinical guidelines, expanding the original query using the prioritized concepts, and then executing the expanded query against the database.
mechanism_raw: Context-aware query expansion: receiving a user query along with clinical context, generating a domain-specific information model containing relevant concepts, prioritizing those concepts based on the clinical context and established clinical guidelines, expanding the original query using the prioritized concepts, and then executing the expanded query against the database.

abstract: Provided herein are semiconductor structures that include germanium and have a germanium nitride layer on the surface, as well as methods of forming the same. The described structures include nanowires and fins. Methods of the disclosure include metal-organic chemical vapor deposition with a germanium precursor. The described methods also include using a N2H4 vapor.
reason: This patent describes a specific materials processing technique (metal-organic CVD with N2H4 vapor) for forming germanium nitride layers on semiconductor structures. The mechanism is entirely tied to the specific chemical precursors, materials, and semiconductor fabrication domain, with no generalizable problem-solving principle that can be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A sheet suction device includes a drum including multiple suction holes in a circumferential surface of the drum, the drum configured to bear a sheet on the circumferential surface and rotate, a suction device configured to suck the sheet through the multiple suction holes, a rotary valve between the multiple suction holes of the drum and the suction device, the rotary valve configured to rotate relative to the drum to change a number of the multiple suction holes communicating with the suction device, and a driver configured to relatively rotate the drum and the rotary valve.
problem: Controlling suction force on a sheet borne by a rotating drum, allowing variable suction application during sheet handling operations.
constraint: The system must maintain continuous sheet contact and handling capability while varying suction, requiring precise mechanical coordination between drum rotation and valve rotation to ensure smooth transitions in suction force without losing grip on the sheet.
mechanism: Using a rotary valve positioned between the drum's suction holes and the vacuum source, where relative rotation between the valve and drum selectively connects a variable number of suction holes to the suction device at any given time, thereby modulating the total active suction area and the resulting suction force on the sheet.
mechanism_raw: Using a rotary valve positioned between the drum's suction holes and the vacuum source, where relative rotation between the valve and drum selectively connects a variable number of suction holes to the suction device at any given time, thereby modulating the total active suction area and the resulting suction force on the sheet.

abstract: A heat pipe operating noiselessly by preventing, or reducing the effects of, the mixing of working fluid at different temperatures includes a hollow tube, a capillary structure, a working fluid, and a bushing. The porous capillary structure able to carry the fluid is disposed on an inner wall of the tube. The bushing is hollow, and the bushing is disposed on a surface of the capillary structure away from the tube. The heat pipe is divided into evaporation, adiabatic, and condensation sections, the capillary structure being at all sections. The working fluid is disposed in the capillary structure of the evaporation section, the bushing is disposed on a side of the capillary structure of the adiabatic section.
problem: Operating a heat pipe noiselessly by preventing or reducing the mixing of working fluid at different temperatures within the pipe.
constraint: The bushing must allow heat transfer and fluid transport through the capillary structure while preventing bulk fluid mixing, and the capillary structure must be maintained continuously across all sections including through the bushing to ensure proper fluid return and heat pipe operation.
mechanism: Placing a hollow bushing in the adiabatic section of the heat pipe, positioned on the capillary structure, to act as a physical barrier that prevents working fluid at different temperatures from mixing while still allowing heat transfer through the capillary structure that is maintained continuously across all sections (evaporation, adiabatic, and condensation).
mechanism_raw: Placing a hollow bushing in the adiabatic section of the heat pipe, positioned on the capillary structure, to act as a physical barrier that prevents working fluid at different temperatures from mixing while still allowing heat transfer through the capillary structure that is maintained continuously across all sections (evaporation, adiabatic, and condensation).

abstract: An electronic device displays a first user interface that includes a plurality of icons of a first type and at least one icon of a second type. While a focus selector is on a first icon of the first type, the device detects movement of a contact in a drag gesture, and, in response, moves the first icon across the display. In accordance with a determination that the first icon moves over one or more other icons of the first type during the drag gesture, the device outputs one or more tactile outputs of a first type. In accordance with a determination that the drag gesture moves the first icon over an icon of the second type at the end of the drag gesture, the device displays a second user interface that corresponds to the icon of the second type and outputs a tactile output of a second type.
problem: Providing contextually appropriate tactile feedback during drag-and-drop interactions in a user interface with multiple icon types.
constraint: Balancing tactile feedback distinctness to avoid user confusion while ensuring the feedback is perceptible and not overwhelming during rapid interactions.
mechanism: Varying tactile feedback intensity and pattern based on contextual interaction state during a continuous gesture, where feedback distinctness is modulated by the relationship between the moving element and target elements, with a transition signal triggered when a contextual boundary is crossed.
mechanism_raw: Differentiating tactile outputs based on the type of icon being interacted with during a drag gesture. When dragging an icon over others of the same type, a first tactile output is generated, while dragging over a different type at the end triggers a second tactile output and a UI transition.

abstract: A system may enable control of one or more output devices in response to input received from one or more activators. An activator may transmit a unique identifier that corresponds to the output device to be controlled. A control unit may receive the unique identifier and enable control of the output device in response to one or more additional inputs. The inputs may be provided by a flex sensor or capacitive touch sensor of a wearable device. In response to the additional inputs, control may be permitted for the output device identified by the unique identifier of the activator.
problem: Enabling selective control of specific output devices using activators that may be spatially or contextually separated from the devices they control.
constraint: Ensuring the unique identifier and sensor inputs are reliably correlated to prevent unintended control of non-target devices while maintaining low latency.
mechanism: Decoupling device selection from activation by first establishing a target via a transmitted identifier, then enabling control only when a secondary sensor condition is met, ensuring control authority is restricted to the pre-selected target.
mechanism_raw: Using a unique identifier transmitted by an activator to pre-select a target device, then permitting control of that device only when additional sensor inputs (e.g., flex or capacitive touch) are detected, decoupling device selection from activation.

abstract: A robot system includes a robot arm, a vehicle being movable and supporting the robot arm, and a tilt sensor configured to detect a tilt relative to a reference direction of at least one of the robot arm and the vehicle. The control method includes controlling the robot arm to sequentially position a control point of the robot arm to a plurality of target points. The controlling of the robot arm includes, when the control point is located at the target point where the control point is to be located one point previously to an object target point of the plurality of target points, resetting a control parameter for positioning the control point at the object target point based on the tilt from the reference direction, and positioning the control point at the object target point using the reset control parameter.
problem: Maintaining accurate positioning of a robot arm on a movable vehicle despite environmental tilt or orientation changes.
constraint: Balancing the frequency and magnitude of parameter adjustments to avoid overcorrection or instability while ensuring sufficient compensation for tilt effects.
mechanism: Adjusting operational parameters of a manipulator system in real-time based on environmental orientation data prior to executing a movement command, to compensate for positional errors induced by external tilt or displacement.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically resetting control parameters for the robot arm based on real-time tilt sensor data before executing a movement to a target point, compensating for tilt-induced positional errors.

abstract: The present disclosure discloses a device for centrifuge testing of a driven pile in different installation and pull-out modes, including a supporting system, a pile driving system, a pile-soil system and a measurement and acquisition system. The present disclosure further provides a method for operating the device for centrifuge testing of a driven pile in different installation and pull-out modes. The present disclosure can perform geotechnical centrifuge testing of a driven pile through penetration in different installation modes and pull-out in different pull-out modes, and provide the effective test device and method for study of a pile-soil mutual dynamic response during a whole process of penetration and a process of pull-out of the driven pile. Moreover, pile-soil deformation characteristics and the like during the processes of penetration and pull-out can be visually observed through a high-speed camera or a digital camera, and the pull-out and penetration can be tested separately.
problem: Studying dynamic pile-soil interaction during both installation and pull-out phases under realistic stress conditions.
constraint: Maintaining accurate scaling of stress and strain conditions during centrifuge rotation while allowing independent observation of installation and pull-out processes.
mechanism: Simulating scaled environmental forces on a test specimen using rotational acceleration to replicate gravitational effects, enabling independent observation of opposing operational phases (e.g., insertion and extraction) under controlled stress conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using a geotechnical centrifuge to simulate scaled gravitational forces, enabling separate testing of penetration and pull-out modes while observing deformation characteristics via high-speed or digital imaging.

abstract: An effect device easy to mount includes an annular frame, effect sheets and fixing assemblies for pivoting the effect sheets in the annular frame. The fixing assembly has a first insertion pin and a second insertion pin respectively mounted at two ends of the effect sheets and used for pivoting. The first insertion pin is sleeved with an elastic element and an end portion of the first insertion pin penetrates through a mounting hole in the annular frame. A first protruding portion protrudes out of an end, close to the effect sheets, of the first insertion pin. One end of the elastic element abuts against the first protruding portion, and the other end of the elastic element abuts against an inner side wall of the annular frame. The second insertion pin is fixed in a pivoting mode.
problem: Mounting effect sheets in an annular frame such that they can pivot freely while remaining securely retained.
constraint: Ensuring the elastic element provides sufficient retention force to prevent unintended dislodging while allowing smooth pivoting without excessive friction.
mechanism: Using a resilient biasing element on a first axis to maintain contact pressure between a flexible sheet and a frame, while a second fixed axis provides a stable rotational pivot, allowing motion without disengagement.
mechanism_raw: Using an elastic element sleeved on a first insertion pin to bias the effect sheet against the frame, allowing pivoting motion while maintaining retention, with a second fixed pin providing a stable pivot axis.

abstract: A vapor management system includes a monitoring service system configured to communicate one or more system parameters with at least one vapor mitigation system. The monitoring service system is further configured to generate a user interface. The user interface is configured to display and permit adjustment of the one or more system parameters.
reason: The abstract describes only a generic monitoring and user-interface system for displaying and adjusting parameters of vapor mitigation systems. There is no specific causal mechanism that transforms monitoring into a useful physical effect; it is merely a supervisory control interface without any novel feedback, actuation, or physical interaction principle.

abstract: A microelectromechanical (MEMS) microphone with membrane trench reinforcements and method of fabrication is provided. The MEMS microphone includes a flexible plate and a rigid plate mechanically coupled to the flexible plate. The MEMS microphone includes a stoppage member affixed to the rigid plate and extending perpendicular relative to a surface of the rigid plate opposite the surface of the flexible plate. The stoppage member limits motion of the flexible plate. The rigid plate includes a reverse bending edge that include a first lateral etch stop that includes a first corner radius and a second lateral etch stop that includes a second corner radius. The first corner radius is more than 100 nanometers and the second corner radius is more than 25 nanometers. Further, a lateral step width between the first corner radius and the second corner radius is less than around 4 micrometers.
problem: Preventing mechanical damage to a delicate flexible membrane in a MEMS device from over-deflection or contact with opposing surfaces, while preserving acoustic sensitivity and fabrication yield.
constraint: The stop gap must be small enough to prevent damaging over-travel yet large enough to avoid interfering with normal acoustic deflection; corner radii must be large enough to prevent stress-induced fracture but small enough to satisfy fabrication resolution limits.
mechanism: A mechanical stop with stress-relief features is positioned between a flexible membrane and an opposing surface. The stop physically limits the membrane's deflection range to prevent collision or adhesion, while geometric features (e.g., controlled corner radii, lateral step widths) distribute stress concentrations during both fabrication and operation, ensuring the stop structure itself does not fail under cyclic loading.
mechanism_raw: A stoppage member rigidly affixed to a stationary plate extends perpendicularly toward the flexible membrane, physically capping its travel range so that excessive deflection is mechanically prevented before the membrane can collide with or adhere to the opposing surface. The reverse-bending edge geometry with controlled corner radii and lateral step widths manages stress concentration during both fabrication (etching) and operation, ensuring the stop structure itself does not become a failure point.

abstract: A vehicle escape ramp arresting system that includes a narrowed internal width and includes housing connection that limits the peak initial load that can be applied to a metal tape during a vehicle impact with a net and allows a housing associated with the system to rotate about both the vertical and horizontal axes to aid in slowing an errant vehicle.
problem: Arresting an errant vehicle on an escape ramp in a way that limits the peak initial impact load transmitted to the energy-absorbing metal tape, preventing structural damage to the arresting system and avoiding unsafe deceleration spikes for the vehicle.
constraint: The rotational compliance must be sufficient to limit peak load but not so loose that the housing fails to engage the vehicle or allows excessive vehicle displacement before deceleration begins.
mechanism: A multi-axis compliant coupling connects an energy-absorbing element to a support structure, allowing rotational movement in multiple directions during impact. This decouples the initial transient force from the energy-absorbing element, distributing the load over time and spatial orientation to limit peak force transmission while maintaining engagement with the impacting object.
mechanism_raw: A compliant housing connection allows the arresting housing to rotate about both vertical and horizontal axes in response to impact forces. This multi-axis rotational compliance decouples the initial impact transient from the metal tape, distributing the load over time and direction rather than applying a sudden peak force, thereby limiting the maximum load seen by the tape while still extracting kinetic energy from the vehicle.

abstract: A method for controlling a flow of one or more fluids from a formation into a production tubing, includes measuring fluid properties of the one or more fluids passing through one or more fluidic oscillators of a flowmeter device disposed on the production tubing, adjusting the flow in a flow area based on the fluid properties through an inflow control device coupled to the production tubing and is in fluid communication with the flow meter device, and controlling, in response to change in the fluid properties, actuation of the inflow control device to adjust the flow by a controller coupled to the inflow control device.
problem: Controlling the flow rate of fluids produced from a subsurface formation into a production tube based on real-time measurements of fluid properties, without requiring surface intervention or direct human control.
constraint: The system must operate reliably in a harsh downhole environment with limited power and no surface access, requiring the sensing, communication, and actuation to be fully autonomous and robust to varying fluid compositions and pressures.
mechanism: A closed-loop feedback system autonomously regulates fluid flow by integrating passive fluid property sensing (via oscillatory flow behavior), real-time communication of sensed parameters, and actuation of a flow-area adjustment mechanism. The controller directly modulates the adjustment mechanism in response to sensed fluid properties, enabling autonomous operation without surface intervention.
mechanism_raw: Fluidic oscillators integrated into a flowmeter on the production tubing passively sense fluid properties (such as composition or flow characteristics) through their oscillation behavior. These measurements are communicated to an inflow control device that adjusts the effective flow area, and a controller actuates the inflow control device in direct response to changes in the sensed fluid properties, forming a closed-loop feedback system that autonomously regulates flow based on downhole conditions.
residual_terms: ["closed-loop feedback system", "oscillatory flow behavior", "flow-area adjustment mechanism"]

abstract: Wind turbine systems with wind directors are disclosed. The wind director is configured to simultaneously reduce drag force applied to a returning blade and increase force applied to an advancing blade. In some embodiments, the wind director includes an inlet having an inlet width configured to receive wind at a proximal end, and an outlet having an outlet width on a distal end opposite the proximal end. The wind director is configured to position near a wind turbine such that wind exiting the outlet is applied to an advancing blade of the wind turbine. Furthermore, the wind director provides a barrier to a returning blade opposite the first blade, thereby reducing drag force applied thereto. The wind director may further comprise a secondary duct which has an angled outlet and is configured to apply an additional force to the returning blade.
problem: Improving the aerodynamic efficiency of a wind turbine by increasing driving force on the advancing blade while simultaneously reducing drag on the returning blade, without disrupting the turbine's normal rotation or adding excessive parasitic load.
constraint: The wind director must enhance the force differential between advancing and returning blades without creating excessive turbulence, structural loading, or interference with the turbine's natural airflow patterns.
mechanism: A directional airflow management system enhances torque asymmetry by channeling incident airflow onto an advancing blade via a directed outlet, while simultaneously shielding a returning blade from opposing airflow using a barrier structure. A secondary airflow director applies an additional directed force to the returning blade, optimizing net torque without disrupting natural rotational dynamics.
mechanism_raw: A wind director with an inlet and outlet is positioned near the turbine so that wind exiting the outlet is channeled onto the advancing blade, increasing its effective driving force. The same wind director acts as a barrier to the returning blade on the opposite side, shielding it from oncoming wind and thereby reducing drag. A secondary duct with an angled outlet can apply an additional directed force to the returning blade to further optimize the net torque.
residual_terms: ["directional airflow management system", "directed outlet", "barrier structure", "secondary airflow director"]

abstract: A liquid removal device is for removing a liquid from a surface. The liquid removal device includes a chassis comprising a handle and an absorber drum and an extractor drum both rotationally coupled with the chassis. The absorber drum includes a cylinder, where an absorbent layer is positioned on an outer drum surface of the absorber drum. The extractor drum includes a reservoir configured to retain the liquid absorbed from the surface, an outer extractor surface, and a plurality of apertures defined by the outer extractor surface in fluid communication with the reservoir. The extractor drum is movable between a first position and a second position. In the first position, at least a first portion of the plurality of apertures are in contact with the absorbent layer. In the second position, the first portion of the plurality of apertures are not in contact with the absorbent layer.
problem: Efficiently transferring absorbed liquid from a surface to a collection reservoir without manual intervention or over-saturation of the absorbent material.
constraint: Balancing contact duration and pressure between the extractor drum apertures and absorbent layer to maximize liquid transfer while minimizing residual saturation on the absorbent layer.
mechanism: A movable perforated surface alternately contacts and disengages from an absorbent layer on a rotating surface, mechanically transferring liquid from the absorbent layer to an internal reservoir through the perforations during positional transitions.
mechanism_raw: A movable extractor drum with apertures alternately contacts and disengages from an absorbent layer on a rotating absorber drum, mechanically transferring liquid from the absorbent layer to an internal reservoir via the apertures during positional transitions.

abstract: A heating, ventilation, and/or air conditioning (HVAC) packaged unit includes a first refrigerant circuit component configured to change a temperature or a pressure of a refrigerant flowing through the first refrigerant circuit component and a second refrigerant circuit component configured to change a temperature or a pressure of the refrigerant flowing through the second refrigerant circuit component. The first and the second refrigerant circuit components are within a common refrigerant circuit that is disposed within a common support structure. The HVAC packaged unit also includes an interconnection conduit having a length formed from aluminum, a first end segment coupled to a first end of the length, and a second end segment coupled to a second end of the length. The first end segment and the second end segment are each formed from copper, and the interconnection conduit extends between the first refrigerant circuit component and the second refrigerant circuit component.
problem: Optimizing thermal conductivity and structural integrity in a refrigerant conduit that connects components with differing material requirements.
constraint: Balancing thermal performance, material cost, and galvanic corrosion resistance when joining dissimilar metals in a refrigerant pathway.
mechanism: A composite interconnection conduit uses a central segment of one material for thermal conductivity and end segments of another material for corrosion resistance and compatibility with connected components, enabling efficient heat transfer while maintaining structural reliability.
mechanism_raw: A composite interconnection conduit uses a central aluminum segment for lightweight thermal conductivity and copper end segments for corrosion resistance and compatibility with refrigerant components, enabling efficient heat transfer while maintaining structural reliability.

abstract: The invention discloses an image detection method, apparatus, device and a medium. The method includes: determining one or more edge points in an input image and gradient directions thereof; generating an initial matrix with the same size as the input image, and assigning the same initial value to all matrix elements in the initial matrix; for each pixel point located in an accumulation region of each edge point, assigning a corresponding accumulation value to a matrix element in the initial matrix corresponding to the pixel point, to obtain an accumulation matrix; determining one or more circle-center positions in the input image based on the accumulation matrix; wherein, the accumulation region of each edge point includes a first direction line for accumulation along the gradient direction of the edge point and a second direction line for accumulation along the direction opposite to the gradient direction of the edge point.
problem: Detecting circular or curved features in images with computational efficiency despite noise or partial occlusion.
constraint: Trade-off between computational complexity of accumulation across multiple directions and accuracy in distinguishing true circle centers from noise-induced false peaks.
mechanism: Edge points and their gradient directions are used to accumulate evidence in a parameter space matrix along lines aligned with the gradient direction and its opposite, enabling identification of circular feature centers through peak accumulation values.
mechanism_raw: Edge points and their gradient directions are used to accumulate evidence in a parameter space matrix along lines aligned with the gradient direction and its opposite, enabling identification of circle centers through peak accumulation values.
residual_terms: ["edge points", "gradient directions", "parameter space matrix", "circle centers", "peak accumulation"]

abstract: This application provides a data transmission method and a related apparatus. The method includes: A network device generates a first physical layer protocol data unit PPDU. The first PPDU includes a first universal-Signaling field U-SIG field and a first extremely high throughput-Signaling field EHT-SIG field, a sum of a quantity of information bits of the first U-SIG field and a quantity of information bits of the first EHT-SIG field is less than or equal to 78 information bits, and at least one of the first U-SIG field and the first EHT-SIG field includes an identifier indication field, where the identifier indication field is used to uniquely identify one station. The network device sends an encoded first PPDU to a station.
problem: Efficiently encoding station-specific identifiers within a fixed-bit signaling field in high-throughput wireless communication protocols.
constraint: Allocating limited bit capacity between signaling overhead and station identification to maintain protocol efficiency without exceeding hardware or regulatory bit constraints.
mechanism: A signaling protocol data unit incorporates a universal signaling field and a high-throughput signaling field, with at least one field containing an identifier indication field to uniquely identify a station while adhering to a total bit limit.
mechanism_raw: A physical layer protocol data unit (PPDU) incorporates a universal signaling field and an extremely high throughput signaling field, with at least one field containing an identifier indication field to uniquely identify a station while adhering to a total bit limit of 78.
residual_terms: ["PPDU", "universal signaling field", "extremely high throughput signaling field", "identifier indication field", "78 bits"]

abstract: Disclosed is a mounting system for mounting one or more accessory devices to a helmet. The system including a pair of mounting rails for attachment on respective sides on exterior of the helmet shell; and a clamping arrangement for attachment on exterior of the helmet shell between the pair of mounting rails substantially in the back portion of the helmet shell, wherein the clamping arrangement is coupled to at least one of the mounting rails via a coupling having an adjustable length for enabling attachment to helmet shells having various properties.
problem: Attaching accessories to helmets of varying shapes, sizes, and surface properties using a single mounting system.
constraint: Maintaining secure attachment and load-bearing capacity across diverse helmet designs while enabling tool-free or rapid adjustment of the coupling length.
mechanism: Adjustable-length couplings between mounting rails and a clamping arrangement allow the system to conform to different geometries by dynamically modifying the spacing and tension between components during installation.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable-length couplings between mounting rails and a clamping arrangement allow the system to conform to different helmet geometries by dynamically modifying the spacing and tension between components during installation.

abstract: An additively manufactured header for a heat exchanger includes a header body. The header body includes a base and a top opposite the base. The base is open and configured for connection to a heat exchanger core. The additively manufactured header further includes a tube extending from the top of the header body and a flange formed on the tube. The header body, the tube, and the flange are all additively manufactured together.
problem: Traditional heat exchanger headers require multiple manufacturing steps and assembly, increasing complexity, cost, and potential failure points.
constraint: Balancing design freedom from additive manufacturing with material properties and thermal stress resistance required for heat exchanger operation.
mechanism: A fabrication process forms a fluid-handling component as a single integrated structure by depositing material layer-by-layer according to a digital model, eliminating discrete assembly steps and enabling internal passages with non-standard geometries that enhance heat transfer efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Additive manufacturing integrates the header body, tube, and flange into a single monolithic structure, eliminating assembly steps and enabling complex internal geometries that improve thermal performance.

abstract: A semiconductor device includes a substrate having a memory region and a logic region. A first dielectric layer is disposed on the substrate. A first conductive structure and a second conductive structure are respectively formed in the first dielectric layer on the memory region and the logic region. A memory cell is formed on the first dielectric layer and directly contacts a top surface of the first conductive structure. A first cap layer continuously covers a top surface and a sidewall of the memory cell and directly contacts a top surface of the second conductive structure. A second dielectric layer is formed on the first cap layer. A third conductive structure penetrates through the second dielectric layer and the first cap layer to contact the memory cell.
problem: Integrating memory and logic regions on a single semiconductor substrate while maintaining electrical connectivity and minimizing interference between regions.
constraint: Managing layer thickness and material compatibility to prevent electrical crosstalk while ensuring reliable contact between memory and logic regions.
mechanism: A protective overlayer spans across multiple functional regions on a substrate and establishes direct electrical contact with conductive elements in one region, while a separate conductive pathway extends through the overlayer to connect with another region, enabling stacked integration without lateral wiring.
mechanism_raw: A continuous cap layer covers the memory cell and directly contacts a second conductive structure, enabling vertical integration of memory and logic through a third conductive structure that penetrates the cap layer.

abstract: A gaming system compatible with patron-controlled portable electronic devices, such as smart phones or tablet computers, is described. The gaming system can include electronic gaming machines that are compatible to receive both virtual ticket vouchers and printed ticket vouchers that are redeemable for credits on the electronic gaming machines. Information associated with a virtual ticket voucher can be stored on a patron-controlled portable electronic device and then can be wireless transmitted to the electronic gaming machines. The electronic gaming machines can be configured to issue virtual ticket vouchers and printed ticket vouchers that can be redeemed for cash or additional game play on another electronic gaming machine. In one embodiment, the electronic gaming machine can be configured to issue a virtual ticket voucher to a patron-controlled portable electronic device.
problem: Enabling seamless interoperability between virtual (device-stored) and physical (printed) ticket vouchers in gaming systems to support diverse patron preferences.
constraint: Ensuring secure, real-time synchronization of voucher data across devices and machines without compromising transaction integrity or user experience.
mechanism: A transaction terminal accepts and issues two distinct forms of digital entitlement—one stored electronically on a portable device and one encoded on a physical medium—by reading both formats and synchronizing their data states in real time to enable cross-terminal redemption.
mechanism_raw: The gaming machine accepts both voucher types by wirelessly receiving virtual voucher data from portable devices and processing printed vouchers, while also issuing either type for cross-machine redemption.

abstract: Methods and apparatuses for in situ synthesis of SiC, CMCs, and MMCs are disclosed, comprising: providing an apparatus having: an electromagnetic energy source; an autofocusing scanner; a powder system for SiC and one or more powders; a powder delivery system; a shielding gas comprising argon and/or nitrogen; and a computer coupled to and configured to control the energy source, scanner, powder system, and powder delivery system to deposit layers of the sample; programming the computer with specifications of the sample; using the computer to control electromagnetic radiation, mixing ratio, and powder deposition parameters based on the specifications of the sample; and using the autofocusing scanner to focus and scan the electromagnetic radiation onto the sample while the powders are concurrently deposited by the powder delivery system onto the sample to create a melting pool to deposit one or more layers onto the sample. Other embodiments are described and claimed.
problem: Precisely synthesizing complex material structures (e.g., SiC, CMCs, MMCs) with controlled composition and layer deposition in situ.
constraint: Maintaining real-time coordination between radiation focus, powder delivery, and layer deposition to ensure structural integrity and compositional accuracy.
mechanism: A control system dynamically adjusts energy delivery, material composition, and deposition rate in real time during a layer-by-layer fabrication process, using feedback from a focusing mechanism to maintain a stable interaction zone that produces material layers with precisely controlled properties.
mechanism_raw: A computer-controlled system synchronizes electromagnetic radiation focusing (via an autofocusing scanner), powder mixing ratios, and deposition parameters to create a melting pool that deposits layers with specified material properties.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to consortia of bacteria strains and composition comprising one or more bacterial strains disclosed herein. These consortia of isolated bacteria cultures and compositions comprising said cultures, having greater activity than would be observed for the individual bacteria cultures and compositions. A composition of the disclosure may advantageously be used for enhancing the availability of soil phosphorus and other macronutrients and/or micronutrients to plants, and thereby enhancing their growth and yield.
problem: Enhancing soil nutrient availability to plants beyond what individual bacterial strains can achieve.
constraint: Selecting and balancing bacterial strains to ensure compatibility, sustained coexistence, and optimal nutrient-release kinetics in the soil environment.
mechanism: A mixed population of microorganisms is combined such that their collective biochemical activities interact to produce a combined effect greater than the sum of their individual contributions, enhancing the availability of essential nutrients to plants through complementary metabolic pathways.
mechanism_raw: A consortium of bacterial strains is formulated such that their combined metabolic activities produce synergistic effects, increasing nutrient solubilization and plant uptake more effectively than individual cultures.

abstract: A laminated glass includes first and second glass plates arranged on vehicle interior and exterior sides, respectively; and an intermediate film located between the glass plates, and configured to be bonded to the glass plates. The laminated glass has a display area used for a head-up display. The display area includes an area having a cross section with a wedge shape. A thickness of an upper edge side portion of the display area is greater than that of a lower edge side. In at least a part of the area having a cross section with a wedge shape, a value of the wedge angle varies depending on a position of measurement in the vertical direction. A viewing angle of the display area is 2 degrees or more. A maximum amount of deviation in measured values of the wedge angles from a linear approximation line is 0.2 mrad or less.
problem: Optimizing the viewing angle and image quality of a head-up display in laminated glass while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: The wedge angle deviation from a linear approximation must remain within 0.2 mrad to preserve image quality and prevent distortion.
mechanism: Adjust the angular orientation of an optical element across a surface to control light refraction and distribution, enabling a wider viewing angle by dynamically modifying the optical path through a gradient structure. The angular deviation from a linear approximation must remain within a specified threshold to preserve image quality.
mechanism_raw: Varying the wedge angle across the display area to control light refraction and distribution, enabling a wider viewing angle by dynamically adjusting the optical path through a gradient wedge structure.

abstract: Described are systems and methods for enabling voice interaction with appliances, services (e.g., media streaming services, gaming services, news feed services, social platform services, etc.), and the like by way of appropriate supplied apps (also referred to as “skills,” “actions,” or the like) which may be presented or downloaded to a smart device having associated therewith one or more cloud-based voice service platforms. Also described are systems that utilize one or more microphones to provide sound metering for control purposes.
reason: The patent describes a system architecture for voice interaction using cloud platforms and apps, but does not specify a causal functional mechanism beyond component integration and connectivity.

abstract: A display device includes: a substrate including a first display area, a second display area, and a third display area which are arranged along a row direction; a first pixel row on the substrate, extending in the row direction, and including first pixel circuit portions overlapping the second and third display areas; a second pixel row extending in the row direction and including second pixel circuit portions overlapping the second display area; display elements overlapping the first display area; and bridge lines adjacent to the second pixel circuit row, overlapping the second display area, and connecting the first pixel circuit portions and the display elements.
problem: Routing electrical signals in a display device with multiple display areas without interference or signal degradation.
constraint: The bridge lines must overlap specific display areas and align with pixel circuit rows to ensure connectivity without disrupting adjacent display regions.
mechanism: Position conductive elements adjacent to circuit rows to connect components in different regions, enabling signal transmission across overlapping areas while maintaining structural separation. The conductive elements must align with specific circuit rows and overlap designated regions to ensure connectivity without disrupting adjacent areas.
mechanism_raw: Using bridge lines positioned adjacent to pixel circuit rows to connect pixel circuits in one area to display elements in another area, enabling signal transmission across overlapping regions while maintaining structural separation.

abstract: Methods for fabricating an interconnect for a fuel cell stack that include providing a protective layer over at least one surface of an interconnect formed by powder pressing pre-alloyed particles containing two or more metal elements and annealing the interconnect and the protective layer at elevated temperature to bond the protective layer to the at least one surface of the interconnect.
problem: Fabricating durable interconnects for fuel cell stacks that can withstand high-temperature annealing processes without degradation.
constraint: The protective layer material and annealing temperature must be compatible to ensure effective bonding without compromising the interconnect's structural or electrical properties.
mechanism: Apply a protective layer over a component before subjecting it to a high-temperature process, where the layer bonds to the component during the process to shield it from environmental damage and form a durable composite structure. The protective layer material and process temperature must be compatible to ensure effective bonding without compromising the component's properties.
mechanism_raw: Applying a protective layer over the interconnect before annealing, which bonds to the interconnect surface during the high-temperature process to shield it from oxidation or damage while forming a durable composite structure.

abstract: A steering control apparatus for a marine vessel that is able to automatically reduce chine walk includes a processor to obtain behavior information on a hull, including one or more of a behavior relating to a shift of the hull in a roll direction, a shift of the hull in a yaw direction, a shift of the hull in crosswise direction, a steering load, and a helm operation load. When judging that one or more conditions to change a steering mode to a counter steering mode are satisfied, the processor changes the steering mode to the counter steering mode. In the counter steering mode, the processor controls steering of the marine vessel by performing counter steering so as to reduce at least some of one or more of the behaviors of the hull based on the obtained behavior information.
problem: Automatically reducing chine walk (lateral hull oscillation) in marine vessels during steering operations.
constraint: The system must process sensor data and execute mode transitions rapidly enough to counteract hull movements without introducing steering lag or instability.
mechanism: Monitor operational parameters of a system using sensors and dynamically switch to a corrective mode that applies counteracting inputs based on real-time feedback, enabling automatic adjustment to counteract unwanted movements. The system must process sensor data and execute mode transitions rapidly enough to avoid introducing lag or instability.
mechanism_raw: Detecting hull behavior parameters (roll, yaw, crosswise shift, steering load) via sensors and dynamically switching to a counter-steering mode that applies corrective steering inputs based on real-time behavioral feedback.

abstract: The present invention provides methods for uniform growth of nanostructures such as nanotubes (e.g., carbon nanotubes) on the surface of a substrate, wherein the long axes of the nanostructures may be substantially aligned. The nanostructures may be further processed for use in various applications, such as composite materials. For example, a set of aligned nanostructures may be formed and transferred, either in bulk or to another surface, to another material to enhance the properties of the material. In some cases, the nanostructures may enhance the mechanical properties of a material, for example, providing mechanical reinforcement at an interface between two materials or plies. In some cases, the nanostructures may enhance thermal and/or electronic properties of a material. The present invention also provides systems and methods for growth of nanostructures, including batch processes and continuous processes.
problem: Growing nanostructures uniformly and aligned on a substrate surface, and then transferring them to enhance the mechanical, thermal, or electronic properties of a target material.
constraint: The growth process must maintain both uniformity and alignment simultaneously, and the transfer step must preserve the aligned structure while integrating the nanostructures with the target material without disrupting their orientation.
mechanism: A controlled growth process produces elongated elements with long axes substantially aligned and uniformly distributed on a substrate. The aligned array is transferred, either in bulk or to another surface, where the alignment enables the elements to bridge and reinforce interfaces between materials or plies, providing directional property enhancement (mechanical reinforcement, thermal/electronic conductivity) at those interfaces.
mechanism_raw: A controlled growth process (batch or continuous) produces nanostructures with long axes substantially aligned and uniformly distributed on a substrate. The aligned nanostructure array is then transferred, either in bulk or to another surface, where the alignment enables the nanostructures to effectively bridge and reinforce interfaces between materials or plies, providing directional property enhancement (mechanical reinforcement, thermal/electronic conductivity) at those interfaces.

abstract: A compressed gas storage system that includes a pressure vessel. The pressure vessel includes a first vessel portion and a second vessel portion in fluid communication with the first vessel portion. The pressure vessel includes a third vessel portion in fluid communication with the second vessel portion. The compressed gas storage system includes a first valve positioned between the first vessel portion and the second vessel portion and a second valve positioned between the second vessel portion and the third vessel portion. The first valve allows and impedes fluid flow between the first and the second vessel portions. The second valve allows and impedes fluid flow between the second and the third vessel portions.
reason: The patent describes a pressure vessel divided into three chambers with two valves controlling flow between them. This is a straightforward component arrangement (compartmentalized vessel with controllable valves) without a deeper causal mechanism that solves a specific problem beyond basic gas storage with flow control.

abstract: A tool holder includes a body having a posterior arm with a first longitudinal axis extending from a posterior arm proximal portion to a posterior arm distal end. The body includes an anterior arm having a second longitudinal axis extending from an anterior arm proximal portion to an anterior arm distal end. The anterior arm proximal portion includes an anterior arm offset portion having a third longitudinal axis that intersects the first longitudinal axis at or below a midpoint of the posterior arm. The body also includes a u-shaped portion joining the posterior arm distal end and the anterior arm distal end. At least one magnet is positioned on the anterior arm to connect to a paintbrush or other tool.
problem: Holding a tool such as a paintbrush at a specific position and orientation relative to a holder body, enabling precise tool placement and manipulation.
constraint: The offset intersection point and u-shaped connector geometry must be precisely configured to achieve the intended tool positioning angle while maintaining structural rigidity and allowing the magnetic connection to engage and release as needed.
mechanism: A holder body uses a geometric configuration where an anterior arm with an offset portion intersects the posterior arm's longitudinal axis at or below the posterior arm's midpoint, and a u-shaped portion joins the distal ends of both arms. This geometric relationship creates a specific leverage and positioning geometry that orients a tool at a desired angle, while a magnetic element on the anterior arm provides a detachable connection to the tool.
mechanism_raw: The tool holder body uses a geometric configuration where an anterior arm with an offset portion intersects the posterior arm's longitudinal axis at or below the posterior arm's midpoint, and a u-shaped portion joins the distal ends of both arms. This geometric relationship creates a specific leverage and positioning geometry that orients the tool at a desired angle, while a magnet on the anterior arm provides a detachable connection to the tool.

abstract: The soft magnetic alloy of the present disclosure is represented by a composition formula of FeaSibBcCudMe where M is at least one type of element selected from a group consisting of Nb, Mo, V, Zr, Hf, and W, and the formula satisfies 82.5≤a≤86, 0.3≤b≤3, 12.5≤c≤15.0, 0.05≤d≤0.9, and 0≤e<0.4 in at %. The soft magnetic alloy includes a structure that has a crystal grain with a grain diameter of 60 nm or less in an amorphous phase.
reason: The patent specifies a soft magnetic alloy composition with particular elemental ratios and a grain size constraint. This is a materials composition specification rather than a problem-solving mechanism describing how a functional relationship produces a useful effect.

abstract: The fertilizer composition is an algae-based, biodegradable and compostable fertilizer composition. The fertilizer composition includes an algal biomass, ground fenugreek seeds, and a binder for molding the fertilizer into pellets. In some embodiments, the fertilizer composition includes Enteromorpha prolifera (E. prolifera), ground and sieved fenugreek seeds and mastic gum. E. prolifera contains numerous nutrients, including vitamins, minerals and a variety of bioactive compounds. Fenugreek seeds have antimicrobial and antioxidant activities, and also have natural insect repellant properties. Mastic gum exhibits antimicrobial activity. Thus, the fertilizer composition provides a variety of nutrients to plants and also provides protection against pathogens. In the fertilizer composition, a ratio of the E. prolifera to the ground fenugreek seeds to the mastic gum by weight may be 6:3:1.
problem: Creating a fertilizer composition that simultaneously provides comprehensive plant nutrition and protection against pathogens, insects, and oxidative stress.
constraint: The weight ratio must balance nutrient provision against pathogen protection while ensuring the mastic gum functions effectively as both a binder for pellet formation and an antimicrobial agent, without compromising the bioavailability of nutrients or the efficacy of protective compounds.
mechanism: A composition combines a nutrient-dense component (rich in vitamins, minerals, and bioactive compounds), a protective component (providing antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insect repellent properties), and a multifunctional binder (serving as both a structural agent for pellet formation and an antimicrobial agent) in a specific weight ratio. The ratio balances nutrient provision against protective functions so that the binder contributes to both structural integrity and pathogen inhibition, and the molded pellet form factor enables controlled delivery of both nutrition and protection.
mechanism_raw: The composition combines algal biomass (a nutrient source rich in vitamins, minerals, and bioactive compounds), ground fenugreek seeds (providing antimicrobial, antioxidant, and insect repellent properties), and mastic gum (a binder with antimicrobial activity) in a specific weight ratio (6:3:1). The ratio balances the nutrient-dense component with the protective components so that the binder also serves as a functional antimicrobial agent, and the molded pellet form factor enables controlled delivery of both nutrition and protection.

abstract: There are provided a semiconductor memory device and a manufacturing method thereof. The semiconductor memory device includes: a cell stack structure surrounding a first channel structure and a second channel structure; a first source select line overlapping with a first region of the cell stack structure and surrounding the first channel structure; and a second source select line overlapping with a second region of the cell stack structure and surrounding the second channel structure. Each of the first source select line and the second source select line includes a first select gate layer overlapping with the cell stack structure, a second select gate layer disposed between the first select gate layer and the cell stack structure, and a third select gate layer disposed between the first select gate layer and the second select gate layer.
problem: Improving semiconductor memory device structure to enable better electrical control and integration of multiple channel structures within a confined space.
constraint: Balancing the vertical stacking of gate layers to maintain structural integrity while optimizing electrical performance and minimizing interference between adjacent channel structures.
mechanism: A multi-tiered control system using overlapping layered elements to manage conductive pathways, enabling selective activation and isolation between adjacent functional units through spatially arranged electrical interfaces.
mechanism_raw: Layered select gate structures (first, second, third gate layers) arranged to overlap and surround channel structures, creating a multi-tiered electrical control system that manages current flow and isolation between components.

abstract: Various embodiments of a combination lamp are provided, which combine a plurality of different lamp functions in a unitary configuration, and can reduce the total amount of space taken up for at least substantially the same amount of illumination produced.
