The combination lamps can be configured for use on vehicles, light fixtures, free standing lamps, decorative articles, etc. In some embodiments, each lamp component may have a power connection element independent from the other lamp components.
problem: Reducing spatial footprint of multi-function lighting systems while maintaining illumination output and functional independence of individual lamp components.
constraint: Ensuring independent power delivery and thermal management for each lamp component within a shared compact enclosure without compromising performance or durability.
mechanism: A modular integration approach where multiple functional units are combined within a shared enclosure, each maintaining independent operational pathways for power and heat dissipation to prevent cross-interference.
mechanism_raw: Unitary integration of multiple lamp components with independent power connections, allowing each component to operate without physical or electrical interference from others despite shared housing.

abstract: A fishing apparatus including a shank, a hook extending from the shank, one or more extendable barbs, and a spring. Each extendable barb has first and second ends and is disposed for angular movement with respect to the hook from the first end, from a first barb position in which the barb second end is proximate the hook to a second barb position in which the second end of the barb extends outwardly from the hook. The spring forcibly urges each extendable barb from first to second barb positions. A band may be included, circumferentially encircling the hook, slidably movable from first to second band positions. When in the first band position, each barb is held in a slot by the band. When in the second band position, each barb is urged by the spring into its second barb position. Fixed barbs may also be included.
problem: Automatically deploying barbs to secure a caught fish while preventing premature activation during handling or casting.
constraint: Maintaining reliable deployment force from the spring while ensuring the band can securely retain barbs in the retracted position under dynamic conditions.
mechanism: A spring-loaded retention system using a sliding restraining element to hold deployable components in a compressed state; movement of the restraining element releases stored energy to actuate the components outward.
mechanism_raw: Spring-urged extendable barbs held in a retracted position by a circumferential band; sliding the band releases the barbs, allowing the spring to deploy them outwardly from the hook.

abstract: A cutting assembly and corresponding workpiece processing for cutting a workpiece, the cutting assembly including a first cutting tool adapted to cut the workpiece along a first cutting plane, and a second cutting tool adapted to cut the workpiece along a second cutting plane, the first and second cutting planes defining an inner angle therebetween, the cutting assembly being adapted to cut the workpiece along the first and second cutting planes in a single operation.
problem: Efficiently cutting a workpiece along two distinct planes to create a defined inner angle without requiring multiple separate cutting operations.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment and synchronization between the two cutting planes to ensure the resulting angle matches the desired geometry without overcutting or misalignment.
mechanism: A synchronized dual-axis cutting system with geometrically fixed tool orientations, enabling simultaneous material removal along two distinct planes through coordinated motion control.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated dual cutting tools arranged at a fixed inner angle, enabling simultaneous cutting along both planes in a single operation through synchronized tool movement or workpiece positioning.

abstract: An air-conditioning garment includes a garment main part that is worn on the upper body of a wearer, and two fans that are attached to a lower part of a back part of a garment main part, and configured to feed outside air into the inside of the garment main part. Each of the two fans includes a fan main body and a case that houses the fan main body and includes two air outlets. The two air outlets are formed so that their blowing directions are restricted to being upward or obliquely upward. The two air outlets are formed in such a manner that their blowing directions have an upwardly-opened V-shape.
problem: Effectively cooling the upper body of a wearer using minimal airflow energy while directing air to maximize thermal comfort.
constraint: Optimizing fan placement and outlet geometry to balance airflow volume, directionality, and energy consumption while avoiding obstruction from the wearer's movement or clothing.
mechanism: A directional airflow generation system using multiple outlets arranged to create a diverging pattern, strategically positioned to envelop a target surface and enhance convective heat transfer through controlled air distribution.
mechanism_raw: Two fans with upwardly-directed V-shaped air outlets positioned on the back, creating a diverging airflow pattern that envelops the torso and enhances convective cooling through strategic directional control.

abstract: A fire protection system includes a plurality of fluid distribution devices coupled to the fluid supply pipes to define four fluid distribution devices above a floor. The fluid distribution devices generate a spray pattern overlapping one another to define a rectangular fluid distribution area 2.5 ft. The rectangular area having a first pair of edges extending parallel to the fluid supply pipes and a second pair of edge extending perpendicular to the first edge. The fluid distribution devices are axially aligned above a corner of the rectangular area, the fluid distribution area defined by a grid of one square foot areas totaling an area no more than 12 ft.×8 ft., the rectangular area of fluid distribution having a total fluid density of at least 60 gpm/sq. ft., the rectangular area including a first zone of fluid distribution of a 4 ft.×4 ft. area.
reason: The abstract describes a static arrangement of spray nozzles positioned to create overlapping coverage patterns over a rectangular area. While overlapping distribution zones is a known technique, the patent does not describe a novel causal mechanism or functional relationship that produces an effect beyond standard spray coverage layout. It reads as a component list and geometric specification rather than a transferable problem-solving principle.

abstract: A 3D printing machine includes a first spinning part moving in directions of three axes, i.e., X-, Y-, and Z-axes, to melt and spin a base material; and a second spinning part moving along a moving direction of the first spinning part to spin reinforcing fiber onto an upper surface of the spun base material, and moving clockwise or counterclockwise so that the reinforcing fiber is spun onto the upper surface of the base material at a moment when the first spinning part changes a moving direction thereof to the X- or Y-axis direction.
problem: Depositing reinforcing fiber onto a base material surface during 3D printing in a way that integrates the fiber at structurally critical transition points where the print head changes direction.
constraint: The fiber application must be precisely timed to coincide with the primary print head's directional changes while both elements are in motion, requiring coordination between two independently controlled spinning mechanisms.
mechanism: A secondary dispensing element is coordinated to move with a primary deposition head and releases reinforcing material at the precise instant the primary head changes its directional trajectory along one of its motion axes. This synchronization aligns material placement with directional transition points, enhancing structural integrity at corners and path-change locations during additive fabrication.
mechanism_raw: A secondary spinning element moves along with the primary print head and applies reinforcing fiber at the precise moment the primary head changes its X or Y axis direction, synchronizing fiber placement with directional transitions to enhance structural integrity at corners and direction-change points.
residual_terms: ["secondary spinning element", "primary print head", "reinforcing fiber", "X or Y axis direction", "spinning mechanisms"]

abstract: A system and a method for treating biomass with a gas includes at least one conduit having at least one biomass inlet and at least one biomass outlet, at least one gas inlet and at least one gas outlet. The system further includes a transport unit configured to move the biomass through the conduit from the at least one biomass inlet to the at least one biomass outlet thereby defining a biomass transport direction. The system is configured such that gas flowing from the at least one gas inlet to the at least one gas outlet crosses the biomass transport direction.
problem: Treating biomass with a gas in a continuous process where effective contact between the moving solid biomass and the flowing gas is needed for efficient mass transfer.
constraint: The gas flow direction must cross the biomass transport direction within the shared conduit to maximize contact efficiency, while the biomass transport must remain continuous and unidirectional to maintain throughput.
mechanism: A solid material is conveyed through a shared conduit in a defined transport direction by a driving mechanism, while a fluid is introduced through a separate inlet and flows through the same conduit in a direction that intersects the solid transport direction. This creates a cross-flow interaction zone where continuous mass exchange occurs between the moving solid and the crossing fluid stream.
mechanism_raw: Biomass is transported through a conduit in a defined direction by a transport unit, while gas is introduced through a separate inlet and flows through the same conduit in a direction that crosses the biomass transport direction, creating a cross-flow interaction zone where gas and biomass continuously exchange mass as the biomass moves.

abstract: Disclosed herein in a system for positioning a sub-assembly for installation. The system comprises a tool comprising a base and a sub-assembly support. The sub-assembly support is positioned above the base and pivotably mounted to the base at a pivot axis. The tool is positioned adjacent to an interior surface of an assembling body and configured to support a sub-assembly. The system also comprises at least one actuator that is selectively operable to tilt a first surface of the sub-assembly support toward an opening in the assembling body and adjust an angle of the sub-assembly support, relative to the base. The system further comprises an interior conforming device attached to the tool and configured to interface with the interior surface of the assembling body. The system additionally comprises an exterior conforming device configured to interface with the exterior surface of the assembling body.
problem: Positioning a sub-assembly for installation into an assembling body that has both interior and exterior surfaces, where precise alignment is needed despite geometric constraints.
constraint: The system must conform to both interior and exterior surfaces at the same time while independently adjusting the sub-assembly angle, requiring coordinated mechanical compliance and actuation.
mechanism: Conforming elements interface with opposing surfaces of a target structure simultaneously to establish a positional reference frame, while an adjustable support mechanism applies controlled angular displacement to align a component relative to the reference frame, enabling precise placement within a constrained cavity.
mechanism_raw: Interior and exterior conforming devices interface with the body's interior and exterior surfaces simultaneously to establish a positional reference frame, while a pivotably mounted sub-assembly support is tilted by an actuator to adjust the sub-assembly angle relative to the base, enabling precise placement within the cavity.
residual_terms: ["conforming elements", "adjustable support mechanism", "angular displacement", "positional reference frame"]

abstract: A system and process for collecting aerosol matter samples is disclosed. The system includes a circular sample cartridge holder that contains a plurality of sample cartridges. Each sample cartridge contains a filter media for collecting aerosol matter samples. The system further includes a docking device for receiving an aerosol-generating system. The docking device places the aerosol-generating system in engagement with one of the sample cartridges. The aerosol matter collecting system further includes an aerosol withdrawing device that causes a controlled puff volume to flow through a sample cartridge for collecting an aerosol matter sample. The system can be completely automated and can collect samples on a puff by puff basis. The system and process are well suited to analyzing aerosols collected heated tobacco product system, but can also be used to test smoking articles, such as cigarettes, or any other device or product such as e cigarette that produces an aerosol.
problem: Collecting aerosol matter samples automatically and on a discrete, puff-by-puff basis from various aerosol-generating devices.
constraint: The system must operate completely automated while maintaining controlled, reproducible puff volumes for each individual sample collection cycle.
mechanism: An automated docking interface engages a discrete sample container with a fluid source, and a controlled suction mechanism withdraws a predetermined volume of fluid through the container, capturing particulate matter for sequential sample collection.
mechanism_raw: A docking device mechanically engages an aerosol-generating system with a specific sample cartridge containing filter media, and an aerosol withdrawing device draws a controlled puff volume through the cartridge, capturing aerosol on the filter for automated discrete-sample collection.
residual_terms: ["automated docking interface", "controlled suction mechanism", "discrete sample container", "predetermined volume"]

abstract: Devices, methods, and systems are provided for extracting particles from a ferrofluid. Such methods may comprise receiving a flow of ferrofluid comprising target particles and background particles and generating a first, focusing magnetic field to focus the target particles towards a capture region. The capture region may capture the target particles and a plurality of background particles. A second, defocusing magnetic field may be configured to remove background particles from the capture region. A detector may be used to detect the target particles bound to the target region.
problem: Separating target particles from background particles in a ferrofluid where both types of particles are magnetically responsive.
constraint: The two magnetic fields must be sequentially applied with opposing effects—focusing to attract targets and defocusing to repel background—without disturbing the captured targets during the defocusing step.
mechanism: A first magnetic field concentrates target particles toward a capture zone, then a second opposing magnetic field is applied to displace non-target particles from the capture zone, leaving purified target particles for analysis.
mechanism_raw: A first focusing magnetic field concentrates target particles toward a capture region, then a second defocusing magnetic field is applied to remove background particles from the same capture region, leaving purified target particles behind for detection.
residual_terms: ["magnetic field", "target particles", "capture zone", "opposing magnetic field", "non-target particles"]

abstract: A carrying device (1) for the frontal removal of a roll body from a roll frame, comprising a main frame (2) and a receiving section (3) for the roll body. The receiving section (3) can be transferred from an introduction position (E) into a supporting position (S). The receiving section (3) has a profile which at least partially encloses the roll body in the supporting position (S), and the carrying device (1) can be pushed in below the roll body with the receiving section (3) in the introduction position (E), and the roll body is carried with the receiving section (3) in the supporting position (S).
problem: Removing a roll body from a roll frame via frontal access, where the roll body must be lifted from below without lateral clearance.
constraint: The receiving section must change shape from open to enclosing while already positioned under the roll body, requiring a profile that can both slide in and then capture the roll body in a single motion sequence.
mechanism: A shape-adaptive receiver transitions from an open configuration to an enclosing configuration while positioned beneath an object, enabling the receiver to slide into position and then grip the object for frontal extraction without lateral clearance.
mechanism_raw: A receiving section transitions from an introduction position (open profile, allowing the device to be pushed in below the roll body) to a supporting position (enclosing profile, partially surrounding the roll body to grip and carry it), enabling frontal extraction.

abstract: A programmable motion system is disclosed that includes a dynamic end effector system. The dynamic end effector system includes an end effector that is coupled via a dynamic coupling to the programmable motion system, wherein the dynamic coupling provides that at least a portion of the end effector may spin with respect to an other portion of the end effector.
reason: The abstract only describes a component-level feature (a dynamic coupling that allows part of an end effector to spin) without explaining a specific problem-solving causal mechanism, how the spinning is achieved, or what functional effect it produces beyond the stated capability.

abstract: A power tool including a sensor attachment, a housing, a motor, and a power tool controller. The power tool controller is operable or configured to control power provided to the motor. The sensor attachment is coupled to the power tool's housing and includes a first non-contact sensor and a sensor controller. The sensor controller receives signals from the first non-contact sensor related to distance to a work surface and determines a fastener depth based on the signals from the first non-contact sensor. If the fastener depth is greater than or equal to a desired fastener depth, the sensor controller generates and sends a control signal to the power tool controller. In response, the power tool controller turns off or cuts power to the motor.
problem: Automatically controlling the depth of a fastener driven by a power tool to avoid over-penetration.
constraint: Real-time sensing and immediate power cutoff must occur without physical contact, requiring precise calibration and rapid response to avoid overshoot.
mechanism: A feedback system measures distance to a target surface in real-time, calculates the position of a driven element relative to the surface, and interrupts power delivery to an actuator when a predetermined positional threshold is reached, preventing over-penetration through closed-loop control.
mechanism_raw: A non-contact sensor measures distance to a work surface, calculates fastener depth, and triggers a control signal to cut power to the motor when the desired depth is reached, creating a closed-loop feedback system.

abstract: The present invention relates to a composition comprising an aqueous dispersion of submicron-sized polymer particles and micron-sized polymer beads, wherein the polymer particles or beads or both are functionalized with phosphorus acid groups. The composition of the present invention is useful for providing a matte finish on substrates, such as leather, textiles, wallboard, decorative coatings, concrete, and wood, with improved stain resistance. The present invention also relates to a leather substrate coated with a clear matte finish comprising an acrylic or styrene-acrylic polymer film and micron-sized polymer beads, wherein the film or the beads or both are functionalized with a phosphorus acid monomer.
problem: Achieving a matte finish on substrates with improved stain resistance using a single coating composition.
constraint: Balancing particle size ratios and functional group density to maintain both optical matte properties and stain resistance without compromising adhesion or durability.
mechanism: A coating composition combines particles of differing size distributions and surface-functionalized groups to simultaneously create microscale surface texture (via size disparity) and chemical resistance (via functional groups), producing a matte finish with enhanced stain resistance through synergistic physical and chemical interactions.
mechanism_raw: Combining submicron-sized polymer particles and micron-sized polymer beads functionalized with phosphorus acid groups creates a surface texture (via particle size distribution) and chemical resistance (via functional groups) that synergistically produce a matte, stain-resistant finish.
residual_terms: ["particles of differing size distributions", "surface-functionalized groups", "microscale surface texture", "chemical resistance"]

abstract: A gutter assembly comprising: a gutter having a front gutter wall having a front inner lip; and a gutter cover comprising: a front cover mounting portion including: a rim abutting segment superposable to the front inner lip; and a lip retaining member resiliently and deflectably connected to the rim abutting segment, the lip retaining member extending downwardly and including a lip retaining segment extending forwardly from a rearward segment end of the rim abutting segment to define a lip receiving recess thereinbetween for receiving the front inner lip of the gutter, the lip retaining member further comprising a guiding member extending rearwardly and downwardly from the lip retaining segment, the lip retaining member being resiliently deflectable rearwardly by the guiding member abutting the front inner lip upon engagement of the gutter cover with the gutter.
problem: Securely attaching a gutter cover to a gutter in a removable, tool-free manner while accommodating misalignment during installation.
constraint: The resilient material must provide sufficient deflection force for easy installation while maintaining long-term retention under environmental stress.
mechanism: A resiliently deformable retention element deflects during engagement with a mating surface feature, then returns to a stable configuration to form a self-locking mechanical interlock that guides alignment and maintains connection under environmental stress through stored elastic energy.
mechanism_raw: A resiliently deflectable lip retaining member snaps over the gutter's front inner lip when the cover is engaged, using the material's elasticity to create a self-locking mechanical interlock that guides and retains the connection.
residual_terms: ["resiliently deformable retention element", "self-locking mechanical interlock", "elastic energy"]

abstract: A ventilation system for a space includes an air supply partition configured to cause filtered air to flow into an area of the space, and an air exhaust partition in spaced-apart relationship with the air supply partition and configured to cause air to be drawn in and filtered from the area. The air supply partition and the air exhaust partition create a “push-pull” air flow across the area. A ventilation partition includes air inlets in a first portion of the housing, air outlets in a second portion of the housing, a filter, and a fan configured to draw air in through the air inlets, through the filter, and out through the air outlets. The partition is a portable, free-standing structure configured to be supported by a surface, such as a floor of a room in which the partition is located.
problem: Efficiently ventilating a localized area of a space with filtered air while maintaining portability and adaptability to different room layouts.
constraint: The partitions must be free-standing and portable while maintaining sufficient spacing and alignment to sustain the push-pull airflow dynamics.
mechanism: Two spatially separated partition elements establish opposing airflow directions—one introducing filtered fluid into a target zone and the other extracting contaminated fluid from the same zone—creating a directional flow gradient that enhances localized ventilation efficiency through push-pull dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Two spaced-apart partitions (supply and exhaust) create a 'push-pull' airflow pattern across the target area, with one partition forcing filtered air in and the other drawing contaminated air out, enhancing directional flow and filtration efficiency.
residual_terms: ["spatially separated partition elements", "push-pull dynamics", "directional flow gradient"]

abstract: A system of obtaining an aluminium melt including SiC particles for use when moulding vehicle parts, e.g. brake disks, the system comprises a pre-processing tank (2), configured to receive SiC particles and to apply a pre-processing procedure to pre-process the SiC particles; a SiC particle transport member (4) configured to transport the pre-processed SiC particles from the pre-processing tank (2) to a crucible (6) of a melting furnace device (8), and the melting furnace device (8) is configured to receive and melt solid aluminium, e.g. aluminium slabs, and to hold an aluminium melt (10) and to receive said pre-processed SiC particles (12). The system also comprises a tube-like SiC particle mixing arrangement (14) defining and enclosing an elongated mixing chamber (16), the mixing arrangement (14) is configured to be mounted in said crucible (6) and structured to receive into said mixing chamber (16) said pre-processed SiC particles (12) via a first inlet (18) and said aluminium melt (10) via at least one second inlet (20), and to apply a mixing procedure by rotating a rotatable mixing member (22) arranged in said mixing chamber (16) about said longitudinal axis A, wherein said pre-processed SiC particles are mixed together with the aluminium melt in said mixing chamber. The mixing arrangement (14) is provided with at least one outlet (26) to feed out the mixture from said mixing chamber into said crucible.
problem: Uniformly dispersing SiC particles into a molten aluminum melt for consistent composite material properties in molded vehicle parts.
constraint: The mixing process must prevent particle clumping and degradation while maintaining temperature control and throughput for industrial-scale production.
mechanism: A conditioning stage prepares particulate material, which is then introduced into a mixing chamber containing a fluid medium where a rotating agitation element continuously disperses the particles throughout the medium, ensuring uniform distribution before recirculating the mixture back into the primary processing vessel.
mechanism_raw: A pre-processing step conditions SiC particles, which are then transported to a crucible-mounted mixing chamber where a rotating member agitates the particles and melt together, ensuring homogeneous distribution before feeding the mixture back into the crucible.
residual_terms: ["conditioning stage", "rotating agitation element", "uniform distribution", "recirculating the mixture"]

abstract: The invention relates to a Prodrug activation method, for therapeutics, wherein use is made of abiotic reactive chemical groups that exhibit bio-orthogonal reactivity towards each other. The invention also relates to a Prodrug kit comprising at least one Prodrug and at least one Activator, wherein the Prodrug comprises a Drug and a first Bio-orthogonal Reactive Group (the Trigger), and wherein the Activator comprises a second Bio-orthogonal Reactive Group. The invention also relates to targeted therapeutics used in the above-mentioned method and kit. The invention particularly pertains to antibody-drug conjugates and to bi- and trispecific antibody derivatives.
problem: Need to activate therapeutic prodrugs specifically at target sites (e.g., disease tissue) without causing systemic side effects from premature drug release.
constraint: The reactive groups must be sufficiently bio-orthogonal (non-reactive with biological molecules) to avoid off-target activation, while still being reactive enough under physiological conditions to release the drug at the target site. This requires balancing reactivity and selectivity.
mechanism: A delivery system carries a therapeutic agent linked via a first reactive group, and a separate activator carries a complementary second reactive group. These two groups selectively react with each other only when they encounter each other at a target site, triggering release of the active agent. The reactive groups are chosen to be inert toward biological components but reactive toward each other, enabling site-specific activation through a controlled interaction that balances reactivity and selectivity.
mechanism_raw: A prodrug carries a drug linked via a first bio-orthogonal reactive group (Trigger), and a separate activator carries a complementary second bio-orthogonal reactive group. These two groups selectively react with each other only when they encounter each other at the target site, triggering release of the active drug. The bio-orthogonal groups are chosen to be inert toward biological components but reactive toward each other, enabling site-specific activation.

abstract: A systemic dual motor framing for a watercraft is provided as is the overall system. The systemic dual motor framing is movable between a folded condition and an unfolded condition for attaching with the assistance of strapping to a stern of the watercraft, sleeve-like, either by sliding over the stern end or strapping around the stern. In the unfolded condition, the systemic dual motor framing facilities the strapping while maintaining a motor on each side of the watercraft, wherein the two motors can be selectively powered in conjunction remotely.
problem: Need to mount dual motors on a watercraft in a configuration that is portable for transport/storage yet functional when deployed, with symmetric positioning and independent motor control.
constraint: The frame must be compact and structurally sound in the folded state for transport, while maintaining rigidity and proper motor alignment in the unfolded state. The strapping attachment mechanism must function reliably in both states.
mechanism: A frame system transitions between a compact condition and an operational condition. In the operational state, the frame deploys to create symmetric mounting points on each side of a watercraft's stern, using a securing mechanism to attach the assembly. Each motor is independently controllable via remote selective powering, allowing differential thrust for steering or stabilization. The frame maintains structural integrity in both conditions while enabling portability and functional deployment.
mechanism_raw: A frame system transitions between a folded (compact) condition and an unfolded (operational) condition. In the unfolded state, the frame deploys to create symmetric mounting points on each side of the watercraft's stern, using strapping to secure the assembly. Each motor is independently controllable via remote selective powering, allowing differential thrust for steering or stabilization.

abstract: A phosphorus production method can include reducing feed containing phosphate ore and providing a silica ratio from 0.3 to 0.7 in a reaction chamber from 1250 to 1380° C. Less than 20% of the phosphate remains in the residue. Another phosphorus production method includes continuously moving a reducing bed through the reaction chamber with the feed agglomerates substantially stable while in the reducing bed. Reaction chamber temperature can be from 1250 to 1380° C. A phosphorus production system includes a barrier wall segmenting the reaction chamber into a reduction zone differentiated from a preheat zone. The bed floor is configured to move continuously from the preheat zone to the reduction zone during operation. A method for producing a reduction product includes exothermically oxidizing reduction/oxidation products in the reaction chamber, thereby adding heat to the reducing bed from the freeboard as a second heat source.
problem: Need to efficiently produce phosphorus from phosphate ore in a high-temperature reaction chamber while managing heat distribution, material flow, and residue minimization.
constraint: Reaction temperature must be maintained within a narrow range (1250–1380°C), the silica ratio in feed must be controlled (0.3–0.7), less than 20% of phosphate must remain in residue, and the moving bed must remain agglomerate-stable while traversing zones.
mechanism: A moving bed of feed material continuously traverses a segmented reaction chamber, passing through distinct thermal zones. Heat is supplied from two sources: a primary endothermic reaction in the bed and secondary exothermic oxidation of byproducts in the region above the bed. The bed floor moves from a preheat zone to a reduction zone during operation, with heat from the secondary source supplementing the primary reaction to maintain temperature within a controlled range. The bed remains structurally stable while traversing the zones.
mechanism_raw: A reducing bed of feed material continuously moves through a reaction chamber segmented by a barrier wall into a preheat zone and a reduction zone. The bed floor moves from preheat to reduction zone during operation. Heat is supplied from two sources: the primary endothermic reduction reaction and secondary exothermic oxidation of reduction/oxidation byproducts in the freeboard above the bed, which adds heat from above to supplement the reducing bed.

abstract: An apparatus for an architectural opening comprises a plurality of panels pivotably connected together. At least one of the plurality of panels comprises a frame comprising a plurality of first frame members connected to a plurality of second frame members at respective interfaces to define at least one opening. The interfaces are defined by ends of the plurality of first frame members positioned at least partially within respective apertures defined in the plurality of second frame members. Each of the first and second frame members comprise an internal cavity filled with a gas having a thermal conductivity between 2 mW/(m·K) and 25.5 mW/(m·K) at 25 degrees Celsius. The at least one of the plurality of panels also comprises an inset panel secured within the at least one opening.
problem: Need to create architectural panels that provide thermal insulation while being pivotably connectable for flexible installation configurations.
constraint: The insulating gas must have thermal conductivity within a specific range (2–25.5 mW/(m·K) at 25°C), the interlocking joints must maintain gas seals while allowing pivoting motion, and the structure must support the inset panel within the frame opening.
mechanism: Frame members are connected at interfaces where ends of first frame members are inserted into apertures defined in second frame members, creating sealed internal cavities. These cavities are filled with a gas having specific thermal conductivity properties. Panels are pivotably connected together, allowing articulation while maintaining the gas-filled insulating cavities. An inset panel is secured within the opening defined by the frame, enabling flexible installation configurations while preserving thermal insulation.
mechanism_raw: Frame members are connected at interfaces where ends of first frame members are inserted into apertures defined in second frame members, creating sealed internal cavities. These cavities are filled with gas having specific thermal conductivity. The panels are pivotably connected together, allowing articulation while maintaining the gas-filled insulating cavities. An inset panel is secured within the opening defined by the frame.
residual_terms: ["apertures", "sealed internal cavities", "thermal conductivity", "pivotably connected", "inset panel", "gas-filled insulating cavities"]

abstract: A pathogen detection and display system is configured to discover and display the location of substances of interest, particularly pathogens that can spread infection. The detection and display system can be used in healthcare facilities on surfaces, medical equipment and devices, patients, and staff, for example.
reason: The abstract only states that the system 'is configured to discover and display the location of substances of interest' but does not describe any specific detection mechanism, sensing method, or display mechanism. No causal functional relationship is explained.

abstract: Devices and methods for mobile monitoring of a drainage catheter are provided. A device may be configured to perform an operation of rendering a user interface. The user interface may be configured to provide an output interface configured to prompt a user to input catheter use information, catheter use information being information related to using the catheter to drain fluid from the patient. The user interface may be configured to provide an input interface for the user to input catheter use information. The device may be further configured to receive catheter use information input by the user through the user interface. The device may be further configured to generate catheter management information based upon the received catheter use information. A method for mobile monitoring of a drainage catheter may include using a processor to perform the steps the device is configured to perform.
reason: The patent describes a standard data collection and processing system for catheter monitoring, which lacks a novel causal mechanism beyond conventional user interface and data aggregation techniques.

abstract: A resource allocation device includes: a course estimation unit that estimates a course of each mobile terminal based on a location of a mobile terminal acquired from a network device, and estimates a probability that each mobile terminal is located in each area at time of prediction; a determination unit that calculates, for each area, the number of mobile terminals in the area using the probability and determines whether the maximum value of an overcommit ratio for each area exceeds an upper limit; and an execution unit that executes the allocation or release of resources to an MEC server group located in each area when the maximum value of the overcommit ratio is equal to or less than the upper limit, and refrains from executing the allocation or release of the resources to the MEC server group when the maximum value of the overcommit ratio exceeds the upper limit.
problem: Efficiently allocating network resources to mobile terminals while avoiding overcommitment of edge computing resources.
constraint: Balancing resource utilization efficiency against the risk of overcommitting resources when predicted demand exceeds capacity.
mechanism: Predictive demand estimation across spatial regions enables dynamic allocation of shared computing resources to distributed endpoints, with allocation decisions constrained by real-time overcommit thresholds to prevent resource exhaustion.
mechanism_raw: Probabilistic location estimation predicts terminal distribution across areas, enabling dynamic resource allocation to MEC servers only when overcommit ratios remain within safe thresholds.

abstract: A grain oriented electrical steel sheet includes a base steel sheet, an oxide layer, and a tension-insulation coating. When a glow discharge spectroscopy is conducted in a region from a surface of the tension-insulation coating to an inside of the base steel sheet, a sputtering time Fe0.5 at which a Fe emission intensity becomes 0.5 times as compared with a saturation value thereof and a sputtering time Fe0.05 at which a Fe emission intensity becomes 0.05 times as compared with the saturation value satisfy (Fe0.5−Fe0.05)/Fe0.5≥0.35. A maximal point of a Cr emission intensity is included between the Fe0.05 and the Fesat. Moreover, a magnetic flux density B8 in a rolling direction of the grain oriented electrical steel sheet is 1.90 T or more.
problem: Achieving high magnetic flux density in grain-oriented electrical steel through controlled material composition and layer structure.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the steel sheet while achieving the required magnetic performance parameters (B8 ≥ 1.90 T).
mechanism: Controlled compositional gradients within a layered material structure optimize directional property alignment, where precise modulation of layer formation parameters creates a spatially varying internal architecture that enhances target performance metrics while preserving structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Precise control of oxide layer sputtering times and chromium distribution creates a gradient structure that optimizes magnetic domain alignment and reduces core losses.

abstract: A laundry treatment machine including: a cabinet; a tub within the cabinet; a horizontal axis fluid pervious drum within the tub rotatable about a horizontal axis, wherein the drum has a diameter orthogonal to the horizontal axis and an average width in line with the horizontal axis and a ratio of diameter to average width from 1.5:1 to 3.25:1; a circumferential entry section into the tub that spans at least across an intermediate range of from 30 degrees to 60 degrees above and rotationally about the horizontal axis and is bounded within a front position of more than 2 degrees above and rotationally about the horizontal axis and a top position less than 90 degrees above and rotationally about the horizontal axis; and a door in the cabinet, the door sealingly engaged with the entry section.
problem: Optimizing laundry drum geometry to improve washing efficiency and mechanical interaction with laundry loads.
constraint: Balancing drum size and entry angle to maximize mechanical agitation while maintaining structural stability and user accessibility.
mechanism: A geometric aspect ratio combined with a partial circumferential access opening modulates mechanical interaction forces between a rotating containment vessel and its load, where the dimensional relationship and entry angle govern load distribution and inertial dynamics during cyclic motion.
mechanism_raw: A diameter-to-width ratio (1.5:1 to 3.25:1) combined with a circumferential entry section spanning 30–60 degrees enhances load distribution and rotational dynamics during washing cycles.

abstract: An extendable drain configured to move between a retracted position and an extended position includes a housing and a drain member. The housing includes a top, a bottom, and a sidewall including an annular stretchable sleeve. The housing defines an interior volume configured to be at least partially filled by a fluid causing the annular sleeve to stretch axially, thereby increasing a distance between the top of the housing and the bottom of the housing. The drain member includes an open top fixed to the top of the housing, an open bottom, and a sidewall extending between the top and the bottom of the drain member through the interior volume of the housing. At least partially filling the interior volume of the housing moves the drain member axially causing the sleeve to stretch, thereby increasing the distance between the top of the housing and the bottom of the housing.
problem: Creating an extendable drain system that can reversibly adjust its length while maintaining fluid flow capability.
constraint: Ensuring the sleeve material can withstand repeated stretching without failure while maintaining a sealed fluid path during extension.
mechanism: Pressure-induced deformation of an expandable barrier element axially displaces a flow-control member, where controlled volumetric expansion of a flexible sleeve reversibly adjusts the effective length of a fluid pathway while maintaining a sealed interface.
mechanism_raw: Fluid pressure within a housing stretches an annular sleeve, axially displacing a drain member to extend or retract the drain length through controlled volumetric expansion.

abstract: A system and method for sports gaming and wagering. A game system includes a game server and user gaming devices in communication over a network. A wagering game involves multiple players in virtual gaming rooms, each player must complete a series of bets over a predefined time period or over a predefined sporting event or tournament, with the participating players competing against each other to achieve the highest score, winnings, or ranking.
reason: The patent describes a standard multiplayer gaming and wagering system with virtual rooms and time-based betting. The mechanism is not a novel causal operation but rather a conventional online gaming architecture, lacking a unique problem-solving principle transferable to other fields.

abstract: Curable resin compositions having extended open times at ambient temperatures and short cure times at elevated temperatures are prepared using a curable resin, a combination of room-temperature-stable liquid peroxides (including at least one perketal), a promoter salt, a thiol-functionalized organic accelerator and a free radical trap. The curable resin compositions are useful in pultrusion, cure-in-place pipe and resin transfer molding applications, among others.
problem: Creating curable resin compositions that remain stable (extended open time) at ambient temperatures but cure rapidly when exposed to elevated temperatures.
constraint: Balancing ambient-temperature stability (open time) with rapid curing at elevated temperatures without premature activation.
mechanism: A temperature-responsive curing system comprising a thermally labile initiator that remains dormant at ambient conditions but activates at elevated temperatures, combined with a kinetic modulator that suppresses premature reaction at lower temperatures while accelerating curing once initiated. The modulator balances stability and cure speed by controlling radical generation and termination rates.
mechanism_raw: A combination of room-temperature-stable liquid peroxides (including a perketal), a promoter salt, a thiol-functionalized accelerator, and a free radical trap. The perketal decomposes at higher temperatures to initiate curing, while the thiol accelerator and free radical trap modulate reaction kinetics to balance stability and cure speed.

abstract: A real-time diagnosis aid method including: (a) providing a decision-support system for autonomous medical diagnosis to a user of a medical system, the system comprising a display module and software modules embodied on a computer readable medium; (b) generating on the display module an ordered list of diagnostic clues to look at by the user according to the diagnostic clues already filled in as absent or present, the ordered list being based on the relevance of looking at respective diagnostic clues to quickly lead to a diagnosis by the user; (c) receiving from the user, information on presence or absence of one or more diagnosis clues listed in the ordered list; and (d) processing the received information to update the ordered list and provide on the display module an indication of the probability of each possible diagnosis.
problem: Providing real-time diagnostic assistance to medical professionals by dynamically prioritizing diagnostic clues and updating diagnosis probabilities based on user input.
constraint: Maintaining real-time responsiveness while ensuring the ordered list remains clinically relevant and computationally efficient.
mechanism: A dynamic prioritization engine that ranks diagnostic hypotheses based on relevance to user-provided evidence, recalculating confidence scores in real time through a feedback loop. The system adaptively narrows candidate diagnoses by iteratively updating rankings as new inputs are received, maintaining computational efficiency through relevance-weighted pruning.
mechanism_raw: A decision-support system that generates an ordered list of diagnostic clues based on relevance to quickly narrow down diagnoses. User input updates the list and recalculates probabilities, creating a feedback loop that adaptively guides the diagnostic process.

abstract: Belts have an elongated portion having opposed first and second ends configured for connection to each other, the first end including a planar body defining a first aperture and a second aperture spaced apart from the first aperture, and the second end including a buckle having a body with a first protrusion configured to be received in the first aperture and a second protrusion configured to be received in the second aperture. The first end may have a first free end. The second aperture may be closer to the first free end than is the first aperture. The second end may have a second free end. The first protrusion may be closer to the second free end than is the second protrusion. The first aperture may have a first limit surface away from the second aperture. The second aperture may have a second limit surface away from the first aperture.
problem: Creating a belt with a secure, adjustable fastening system that maintains stability during use while allowing easy adjustment.
constraint: Balancing adjustability (ease of fastening/unfastening) with mechanical stability (preventing unintended loosening during use).
mechanism: A dual-point mechanical interlock where two spaced engagement elements on a fastening component insert into corresponding apertures on a strap, with geometric constraints on the apertures preventing disengagement under load. The system balances adjustability with stability by requiring simultaneous alignment of both points for release while maintaining positional integrity during use.
mechanism_raw: A dual-point engagement system where a buckle's two protrusions align with and insert into two spaced-apart apertures on the belt's first end. The apertures have limit surfaces that constrain movement, ensuring the belt remains locked in place after adjustment.

abstract: A screen device intended for a window or a door in a building or vehicle. The device includes a first elongated frame part having two ends; a further frame part and a third one, respectively, being arranged at each end of the first frame part at right angles to the first frame part and connected to a first one of its two ends. Two crossbars are arranged in parallel to the fixedly arranged first frame part and movable independently of each other along the two further frame parts. A pleated screen element is arranged between the first crossbar and the second crossbar, and the crossbars are guided by guide cords. At least one of the crossbars is formed by two profiles that are arranged in parallel to each other and leave a space between them in which a strip provided with holes for respective ones of the guide cords is received.
problem: Designing an adjustable screen device for windows or doors that allows independent movement of crossbars to control coverage while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Ensuring independent crossbar movement does not compromise the screen's alignment or durability under repeated adjustments.
mechanism: An independently adjustable tensioning system where two parallel guide elements slide along a frame, connected by a flexible screen material. At least one guide element incorporates a split-profile design with a guided actuation mechanism, enabling localized adjustment of screen position and tension without disrupting alignment of the opposing guide element.
mechanism_raw: Two parallel crossbars move independently along frame parts, with a pleated screen element between them. At least one crossbar is split into two profiles with a cord-guided strip, enabling smooth, independent adjustment of the screen's position and tension.

abstract: Provided is an aerosol generating device including at least one component accommodating space having an opening on an outer surface of the aerosol generating device and allowing a removable component to be accommodated therein through the opening; a controller configured to periodically generate a test signal; a detection signal generator configured to generate a flooding detection signal based on the test signal when a liquid is introduced through the opening; and a detection signal transmitter configured to receive a generated flooding detection signal and transmit the received flooding detection signal to the controller, wherein the controller determines whether the aerosol generating device is flooded based on the flooding detection signal.
problem: Detecting whether an aerosol generating device is flooded due to liquid intrusion through its component accommodation opening.
constraint: The test signal must be designed to reliably detect liquid presence without false positives, while the detection system must operate within the physical constraints of the device's opening and internal component layout.
mechanism: A controller periodically applies a test signal to a component accommodation opening and evaluates the signal's response to detect liquid presence, determining a flooding status based on deviations from expected signal characteristics.
mechanism_raw: A controller periodically generates a test signal, which is used to produce a flooding detection signal when liquid is introduced through the opening. The detection signal is transmitted back to the controller, which evaluates the signal to determine flooding status.

abstract: A method and system for providing cooling to a part formed using high-temperature additive manufacturing process. Infrared sensors or cameras are used to measure sidewall temperatures and, optionally, top layer temperature. Coolant nozzles provide cooling to the sidewalls of the finished layers and, optionally, to the top layer. The coolant intensity of the coolant nozzles is controlled in order to reduce temperature gradients between layers and/or to maintain temperatures in each layer below preferred maximum temperature.
problem: Managing temperature gradients and overheating in parts produced by high-temperature additive manufacturing processes.
constraint: Balancing cooling intensity to avoid thermal shock while ensuring uniform temperature control across layers, constrained by the spatial and temporal resolution of sensors and nozzle placement.
mechanism: Real-time temperature sensors monitor spatial regions of a manufactured part, and a feedback-controlled cooling system dynamically adjusts cooling intensity across those regions to reduce temperature gradients and maintain thermal thresholds.
mechanism_raw: Infrared sensors measure sidewall and top layer temperatures in real time, and coolant nozzles dynamically adjust cooling intensity based on sensor feedback to reduce inter-layer temperature gradients and maintain temperatures below maximum thresholds.

abstract: A chalk box including a housing (110) having an aperture (140), a reel assembly (120) enclosed within the housing, a string (140) having a first end operably coupled to an end hook (170) and configured to extend from the housing through the aperture and having a second end configured to be wound on the reel assembly, a chalk reservoir (160) in which the string is retained or through which the string passes prior to extending out of the aperture, and a seating assembly (180) configured to extend around at least fifty percent of the length or volume of the end hook when the string is fully withdrawn into the housing.
problem: Ensuring consistent chalk retention and string deployment in a chalk box mechanism during full string withdrawal.
constraint: The seating assembly must cover sufficient surface area to ensure retention without impeding smooth string extension or retraction, constrained by the hook's geometry and housing aperture size.
mechanism: A contact element extends to cover a portion of a hook's surface area during full string withdrawal, maintaining physical contact between the string and hook to retain material and stabilize deployment.
mechanism_raw: A seating assembly extends around at least 50% of the end hook's length or volume when the string is fully withdrawn, maintaining physical contact between the string and hook to retain chalk and stabilize deployment.

abstract: An augmented reality device includes an illuminator, a camera, a memory, and a processor, wherein the processor is configured to execute one or more instructions stored in the memory to turn on a light source of the illuminator to obtain a first image from the camera, turn off the light source to obtain a second image from the camera, estimate depth information, based on the first image, and estimate posture information, based on the second image.
problem: Accurately estimating depth and posture information in augmented reality systems using a single camera and illuminator.
constraint: Timing and synchronization of image capture must avoid motion blur between the two states, while the illuminator's activation must not interfere with ambient light conditions during posture estimation.
mechanism: A processor captures two image states—one with an illuminator active and one without—to decouple depth estimation from orientation calculation, improving accuracy by separating light-dependent and ambient measurements.
mechanism_raw: The processor captures two images: one with the illuminator on (for depth estimation) and one with it off (for posture estimation), decoupling depth and orientation calculations to improve accuracy.

abstract: A level shifter and a chip with the level shifter are shown. Between the input pair and the cross-coupled output pair, there are a first protection circuit and a second protection circuit. An overdrive voltage, which is double the nominal voltage of the level shifter plus a delta voltage, is applied to the level shifter. The first protection circuit has a first voltage-drop circuit that compensates for the delta voltage. The second protection circuit has a second voltage-drop circuit that compensates for the delta voltage.
problem: Protecting a level shifter from overvoltage conditions while maintaining signal integrity during voltage level transitions.
constraint: The voltage-drop circuits must precisely offset the delta voltage without introducing signal distortion, constrained by the level shifter's input/output voltage tolerances and power supply limitations.
mechanism: Voltage-compensation circuits offset an overvoltage delta relative to a nominal threshold, ensuring a signal-level interface operates within safe voltage ranges without distorting transitions.
mechanism_raw: First and second protection circuits with voltage-drop components compensate for a delta voltage added to the nominal overdrive voltage, ensuring the level shifter operates within safe voltage ranges.

abstract: A drive cap uses snap fasteners to couple with the housing assembly of a hair clipper. The drive cap uses joining structures, such as protrusions and recesses, to align with the upper and lower housings of the housing assembly. Once correctly aligned, snap fasteners enable a snug fit and enhance the fit and finish of the hair clipper. The snap fasteners can be located on an inner surface of the drive cap, lower housing, and/or upper housing. A snap detent is located on the inner surface of an adjacent surface to receive the snap fastener. Using a combination of protrusions, extensions, voids, and recesses, in addition to the snap fasteners ensures a secure fit for the drive cap between the upper and lower housings. The snap fasteners couple the drive cap to upper and lower housings seamlessly along the outer surface of the hair clipper and facilitate quick release of the drive cap for maintenance or cleaning.
problem: Attaching and detaching a drive cap to a hair clipper housing assembly requires both secure coupling and quick release for maintenance, while ensuring proper alignment between parts.
constraint: The mechanism must balance secure attachment (snug fit, enhanced fit and finish) with quick release capability (for maintenance and cleaning), while preventing misalignment that could cause improper snap engagement.
mechanism: A two-stage coupling process where alignment features first ensure correct relative positioning between components, then a secondary fastening mechanism engages to create a secure connection. The alignment stage precedes and enables the fastening stage, so the fastening mechanism only activates when components are correctly positioned, allowing tool-free assembly and quick release.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage coupling process where alignment structures (protrusions, recesses, extensions, voids) first ensure correct relative positioning of the drive cap and housings, then snap fasteners engage with snap detents on adjacent surfaces to create a secure, snug fit. The alignment stage precedes and enables the fastening stage, so the snap fasteners only engage when parts are correctly positioned, allowing tool-free assembly and quick release.

abstract: A freehub of a bicycle contains: a body fitted and rotating on a rotary shaft. A receiving sleeve is connected with the body and fitted on the rotary shaft, and the receiving sleeve includes an accommodation holder configured to accommodate a freewheel. A ratchet assembly is mounted between the body and the receiving sleeve, the ratchet assembly includes multiple chutes, and a central axis of a respective chute is not parallel to a central axis of the rotary shaft. A toothed ring is fitted between the fixing element and the body. The ratchet assembly includes multiple teeth, multiple engagement elements, and multiple resilient elements. A respective resilient element abuts against the respective chute and a respective engagement element, such that the respective engagement element is urged by the respective resilient element to linearly move toward the respective tooth so as to engage with the respective tooth.
problem: Creating a freewheel mechanism that allows rotation in one direction while locking in the other, with reliable and consistent engagement of the ratchet elements.
constraint: The non-parallel chute angle must balance smooth engagement and disengagement with sufficient holding force, while the resilient elements must provide enough bias to maintain engagement without causing excessive friction or wear.
mechanism: A directional locking mechanism uses angled pathways whose orientations are non-parallel to a rotational axis. Biased engagement elements are constrained to move along these angled pathways, converting rotational motion into controlled linear engagement with locking teeth. The non-parallel pathway orientation ensures engagement only occurs in one rotational direction, while biasing maintains consistent contact between engagement elements and teeth despite wear or tolerances.
mechanism_raw: A ratchet assembly uses chutes whose central axes are oriented at non-parallel angles to the rotary shaft axis. Resilient elements bias engagement elements to linearly move along these angled chutes toward teeth, creating a directional locking action. The non-parallel chute orientation converts rotational motion into controlled linear engagement movement, while the resilient biasing ensures consistent contact between engagement elements and teeth regardless of wear or manufacturing tolerances.

abstract: A method of characterising particles in a sample, comprising: obtaining a scattering measurement comprising a time series of measurements of scattered light from a detector, the scattered light produced by the interaction of an illuminating light beam with the sample; producing a corrected scattering measurement, comprising compensating for scattering contributions from contaminants by reducing a scattering intensity in at least some time periods of the scattering measurement; determining a particle characteristic from the corrected scattering measurement.
problem: Accurately determining particle characteristics from light scattering measurements when contaminants distort the scattering signal and obscure the true particle response.
constraint: The method must balance removing contaminant contributions while preserving the actual particle scattering signal, requiring accurate identification of which time periods contain contaminant-dominated data without discarding valid particle measurements.
mechanism: A time-series signal correction method identifies temporal intervals where contaminant contributions dominate a measurement stream. The signal intensity in those intervals is adjusted to compensate for contaminant effects, producing a corrected signal. Target characteristics are then derived from the corrected signal, separating the desired response from contaminant interference based on temporal variation patterns.
mechanism_raw: A time series of scattered light measurements is obtained, then temporal analysis identifies time periods where contaminant contributions dominate. The scattering intensity in those periods is reduced to compensate for contaminant effects, producing a corrected scattering measurement. Particle characteristics are then determined from this corrected measurement, separating the desired particle signal from contaminant interference based on how each varies over time.

abstract: The present disclosures discloses a method of target feature extraction based on millimeter-wave radar echo, which mainly solves the problems that techniques in the prior art cannot fully utilize raw radar echo information to obtain more separable features and cannot accurately distinguish targets with similar physical shapes and motion states. The method is implemented as follows: acquiring measured data of targets, generating an original RD map, and removing ground clutter of the map; sequentially performing target detection, clustering and centroid condensation on the RD map after the ground clutter removal; acquiring a continuous multi-frame RD maps and carrying out the target tracking; according to the tracking trajectory, selecting candidate areas and extracting features based on a single piece of RD map and features based on two successive RD maps, respectively.
problem: Extracting features from radar echo data that can accurately distinguish between targets with similar physical shapes and motion states, when single-frame analysis is insufficient.
constraint: The method must balance computational complexity of multi-frame processing with the improved feature separability gained from temporal analysis, while ensuring that tracking and feature extraction remain robust across varying target dynamics.
mechanism: A multi-frame data processing method generates spatial-temporal representations of input data, applies noise filtering and feature extraction to individual frames and frame pairs. Targets are tracked across consecutive representations, and complementary static and dynamic features are extracted from single-frame and multi-frame data. The combination of static and dynamic features enhances discriminability between similar targets by leveraging both instantaneous and temporal information.
mechanism_raw: Multi-frame radar data is processed to generate range-Doppler maps, with ground clutter removal, target detection, clustering, and centroid condensation applied. Targets are tracked across continuous multi-frame maps, and features are extracted from both single-frame RD maps and pairs of successive RD maps. The combination of static (single-frame) and dynamic (multi-frame) features provides complementary information that enhances separability between similar targets.
residual_terms: ["spatial-temporal representations", "noise filtering", "feature extraction", "static and dynamic features"]

abstract: An avionic system for a rotorcraft includes a data source and an enhanced ground proximity warning system. The data source has terrain data and obstacle data stored therein. The enhanced ground proximity warning system can be selectively switched, by a pilot, to operate in either a normal mode or a desensitized mode. The enhanced ground proximity warning system receives flight data, retrieves terrain data and obstacle data from the data source, evaluates the retrieved terrain data and the obstacle data to determine variations in elevations of terrain and obstacles in predetermined area that is a predetermined distance ahead of the current position and along the flight path, and based at least in part on the determined variations, selectively generate a prompt that suggests that the pilot switch the ground proximity warning system to the desensitized mode.
problem: Providing ground proximity warnings to pilots without generating excessive nuisance alerts that could lead to pilot desensitization or disregard of the warning system.
constraint: The system must balance safety (providing warnings when genuinely needed) with usability (avoiding nuisance warnings), requiring accurate prediction of when terrain/obstacle profiles will trigger excessive alerts without compromising detection of actual hazards.
mechanism: A predictive alert system analyzes environmental hazard profiles along a trajectory and selectively adjusts detection sensitivity based on anticipated hazard characteristics. The system proactively modifies its response threshold before entering regions where nuisance alerts would likely occur, maintaining detection capability for genuine hazards while reducing false alarms through anticipatory adaptation.
mechanism_raw: The system analyzes terrain and obstacle elevation variations in a predetermined area ahead of the aircraft along the flight path. Based on the determined variations, it selectively generates a prompt suggesting the pilot switch the warning system to a desensitized mode. This proactive adaptation uses predictive environmental analysis to adjust system sensitivity before entering areas where nuisance warnings would be likely, maintaining alert effectiveness while reducing false alarms.

abstract: Interconnect structures and corresponding techniques for forming the interconnect structures are disclosed herein. An exemplary interconnect structure includes a conductive feature that includes cobalt and a via disposed over the conductive feature. The via includes a first via barrier layer disposed over the conductive feature, a second via barrier layer disposed over the first via barrier layer, and a via bulk layer disposed over the second via barrier layer. The first via barrier layer includes titanium, and the second via barrier layer includes titanium and nitrogen. The via bulk layer can include tungsten and/or cobalt. A capping layer may be disposed over the conductive feature, where the via extends through the capping layer to contact the conductive feature. In some implementations, the capping layer includes cobalt and silicon.
problem: Ensuring reliable electrical connections in semiconductor interconnects while preventing material diffusion and electromigration.
constraint: Balancing conductivity, adhesion, and thermal stability across multiple material interfaces without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Layered barrier structures with distinct material compositions create sequential diffusion barriers, while a capping layer provides mechanical and chemical stability for conductive features.
mechanism_raw: Layered barrier structures with distinct material compositions (e.g., titanium and titanium nitride) create sequential diffusion barriers, while a cobalt-silicon capping layer provides mechanical and chemical stability for conductive features.

abstract: In an embodiment method for growing a rare earth oxide crystal, a surface of a Si substrate is cleaned by carrying out treatments using chemical solutions such as a mixed sulfuric acid-hydrogen peroxide solution, hot nitric acid, or diluted hydrofluoric acid several times to remove impurities on the surface of the Si substrate. A silicon oxide layer including amorphous SiOx is formed on the Si substrate. A metal layer including a rare earth metal is formed in contact with an upper surface of the silicon oxide layer. The silicon oxide layer is reacted with the metal layer through heating to form a first crystal layer including a rare earth oxide crystal obtained by oxidizing the rare earth metal on the Si substrate.
problem: Growing high-quality rare earth oxide crystals on silicon substrates with minimal lattice mismatch and impurity contamination.
constraint: Achieving precise surface cleaning and thermal conditions to ensure uniform crystal growth without introducing defects or secondary phases.
mechanism: A pre-formed oxide layer acts as a reactive intermediate, enabling controlled oxidation of a metal layer through thermal reaction to nucleate and grow a crystalline oxide layer on the substrate.
mechanism_raw: A pre-formed silicon oxide layer acts as a reactive intermediate, enabling controlled oxidation of a rare earth metal layer through thermal reaction to nucleate and grow a crystalline oxide layer on the substrate.

abstract: Embodiments of the knife cut resistant sleeve comprise a spring enclosed by a cut resistant material. The knife cut resistant sleeve is configured to be placed onto a rope of varying sizes and protect the rope from sharp objects. Embodiments of the knife cut resistant sleeve use cut resistant material and can be capable of rotation when hit by a knife in order to prevent the rope from being cut. The sleeve is configured to provide the correct amount of coverage on the rope depending on the length of the rope.
problem: Protecting flexible elongated objects (e.g., ropes) from sharp cutting forces while maintaining adaptability to varying sizes.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient flexibility and coverage across variable rope diameters while ensuring the protective material resists cutting under dynamic loads.
mechanism: A resilient core enclosed in cut-resistant material allows rotational movement when struck by a cutting force, distributing the force circumferentially to prevent localized penetration of the underlying object.
mechanism_raw: A spring core enclosed in cut-resistant material allows rotational movement when struck by a knife, distributing the cutting force circumferentially to prevent localized penetration of the underlying object.

abstract: A distributor for a plate heat exchanger includes a tube part having a tube wall and having a first end and a second end; a first flange formed at the first end; and a connecting protrusion. The connecting protrusion projects from the tube wall of the tube part in a direction away from an axis of the tube part, and projects from the first flange at the inside of the outer edge of the first flange in a direction towards the second end of the tube part; the connecting protrusion has a connecting protrusion wall, which has an axial connecting protrusion wall that faces in the axial direction of the tube part and is remote from the first flange, the axial connecting protrusion wall being between the first end and the second end of the tube part, and having at least one through-hole.
problem: Distributing fluid evenly across a plate heat exchanger while maintaining structural alignment and flow directionality.
constraint: Balancing flow rate uniformity with mechanical strength and minimizing pressure drop across the distributor structure.
mechanism: A connecting protrusion with an axial wall and through-holes directs fluid flow from the tube part into the heat exchanger plates, using geometric constraints to control distribution patterns.
mechanism_raw: A connecting protrusion with an axial wall and through-holes directs fluid flow from the tube part into the heat exchanger plates, using geometric constraints to control distribution patterns.

abstract: Systems, methods and computer programs for transferring data in a communication system are described. The communication system has a first node arranged to send data to a plurality of second nodes using a first protocol. The first protocol allows the transfer of data of a first type. At least one of the second nodes additionally requires data of a second type, which is not included in the data sent according to the first protocol. First data, of the first type, is transferred to a plurality of the second nodes using the first protocol. Second data, of the second type, is stored in a memory. Subsequently, in response to a request, access to the second data is provided to the second node.
problem: Transferring data of a second type not supported by an existing communication protocol without modifying the protocol itself.
constraint: Ensuring timely access to buffered data while avoiding conflicts with ongoing first-type data transfers over the shared communication channel.
mechanism: Storing the second data type in a memory buffer and providing on-demand access via a separate request-response mechanism, decoupling protocol limitations from data delivery requirements.
mechanism_raw: Storing the second data type in a memory buffer and providing on-demand access to it via a separate request-response mechanism, decoupling protocol limitations from data delivery requirements.

abstract: This invention provides a method for operating an automotive arrangement with a lighting device and a vehicle sensor. This method comprises the steps of providing a plurality of auxiliary sensors, configured to provide some device data, provide a control unit configured to estimate a vehicle sensor temperature using the device data and controlling an operation parameter of the automotive lighting device using the estimated vehicle sensor tem-perature. The invention also provides a data processing element and a computer program to carry out this method and an automotive lighting device comprising a control unit which carries out this method.
problem: Managing automotive lighting device operation parameters without direct temperature sensing of the vehicle sensor.
constraint: Reliance on indirect sensor data rather than a dedicated temperature sensor for the target component.
mechanism: Using auxiliary sensor data to estimate a target component's temperature and adjusting an operational parameter of a device based on the estimated temperature.
mechanism_raw: Using auxiliary sensor data to estimate a target sensor's temperature and adjusting the lighting device's operation parameter based on the estimated temperature.

abstract: A power converter and a corresponding method of converting power are presented. The power converter includes a ground port, an input port for receiving an input voltage and an output port for providing an output voltage; an inductor; a flying capacitor; a network of switches; and a driver to drive the network of switches with a sequence of states during a drive period. The sequence of states includes a first state and a second state. In the first state one of the input port and the output port is coupled to the ground port via a first path comprising the inductor. In the second state the remaining state among the input port and the output port is coupled to the ground port via a second path and a third path, the second path comprising the flying capacitor and bypassing the inductor, and the third path comprising the inductor.
problem: Efficiently converting power between input and output ports while managing energy transfer through inductive and capacitive elements.
