constraint: The length-to-diameter ratio must balance sufficient residence time for complete carbonization against excessive pressure drop and uneven heat distribution; the auxiliary metal compound must generate combustible gases at a rate that sustains temperature without causing runaway exotherms or introducing contaminants.
mechanism: An auxiliary reactant is co-fed with organic material and reacts to generate additional combustible gases beyond the primary distilled volatiles. These gases are burned in situ, and the resulting hot combustion products are uniformly circulated through the furnace to maintain a consistent temperature throughout the reaction zone. The furnace geometry (length-to-diameter ratio) ensures adequate residence time and promotes uniform gas flow patterns that distribute heat evenly.
mechanism_raw: An auxiliary reactant (metal oxide, carbonate, or hydroxide) is co-fed with organic material and reacts to generate additional combustible gases (e.g., CO) beyond the primary distilled volatiles. These gases are burned in situ, and the resulting hot combustion products are uniformly circulated through the furnace to maintain a consistent reduction temperature throughout the reaction zone. The furnace geometry (length-to-diameter ratio of 1:1 to 10:1) ensures adequate residence time and promotes uniform gas flow patterns that distribute heat evenly.
residual_terms: ["combustible gases", "in situ", "combustion products", "furnace", "residence time", "gas flow patterns", "heat distribution", "length-to-diameter ratio"]

abstract: An improved method for the continuous production of stable aqueous ammonium polyphosphate compositions which are useful as fertilizers and fire retardants. Wet-process superphosphoric acid which is primarily in the orthophosphate form and anhydrous ammonia vapor are combined in a pipe reactor wherein the exothermic ammoniation of the acid and the conversion of a portion of the orthophosphate to polyphosphate caused by the heat liberated in the exothermic ammoniation reaction occur. A stream of the acid is introduced into the interior of a stream of ammonia vapor in the pipe reactor in order to avoid corrosion of the pipe reactor. Water is added to the reaction mixture to quench the conversion reaction and to provide the amount of water that is required in the desired final composition. The resulting stream is combined with a cooler stream of the desired final stable aqueous ammonium polyphosphate wherein the polyphosphate is cooled and the ammoniation is completed rapidly.
problem: Continuously producing stable aqueous ammonium polyphosphate compositions while preventing corrosion of the reaction equipment and controlling the extent of polyphosphate conversion.
constraint: The spatial arrangement of reactants (acid inside ammonia vapor) must prevent acid contact with cold pipe surfaces while ensuring thorough mixing; the timing and amount of water addition must quench the conversion reaction precisely without over-diluting or under-completing the ammoniation; the cooler stream temperature and flow rate must complete the reaction without initiating further conversion.
mechanism: The exothermic reaction of a reactant generates heat that simultaneously drives a conversion reaction in the same reactor. To prevent corrosion, the corrosive reactant stream is introduced into the interior of the other reactant stream, ensuring that corrosive material contacts the pipe wall only where it is immediately neutralized by excess of the other reactant. After the reaction, a quenching agent is added to stop the conversion reaction at the desired point, and the hot product is rapidly mixed with a cooler stream of the final composition to complete the reaction and control temperature.
mechanism_raw: The exothermic ammoniation of superphosphoric acid generates heat that simultaneously drives the conversion of orthophosphate to polyphosphate in the same reactor. To prevent corrosion, the acid stream is introduced into the interior of the ammonia vapor stream, ensuring that corrosive acid contacts the pipe wall only where it is immediately neutralized by excess ammonia. After the reaction, water is added to quench the conversion reaction at the desired point, and the hot product is rapidly mixed with a cooler stream of the final composition to complete ammoniation and control temperature.

abstract: A multiple switch automatic reset timer in which the switches are located in the back of the timer and have operators angularly spaced about a main bearing axis. A clutch operator is also angularly spaced from the switch operators. A spring return timing gear on the main bearing axis drives a spring tensioner also carried on the main bearing axis. This stores power in the spring which is released at the timed-out point for driving a cam wheel carried on the main bearing axis. This actuates the switch operators and also releases the clutch allowing the timing gear to reset. The cam wheel is maintained in the timed-out position by a latch engaging the spring tensioner. This latch is released by a solenoid operated wheel carried on the main bearing axis. This wheel may also operate the clutch and one or all of the switches. The wheel configuration determines the type of action given by the timer. Provision is made for on delay, off delay, interval, instantaneous switch operation and many other combinations.
problem: Providing a multi-function timer capable of performing various timing operations (on delay, off delay, interval, instantaneous) with automatic reset and multiple switch actuations from a single timing cycle.
constraint: The spring must store sufficient energy to drive all switch operations and the reset mechanism in a single release; the latch must hold the cam wheel reliably under load until solenoid release; the wheel configuration must be mechanically changeable to provide different timing functions without redesigning the entire mechanism.
mechanism: Energy is stored mechanically in a spring during the timing period via a spring-return timing gear. At the timed-out point, the stored spring energy is released to drive a cam wheel that simultaneously actuates multiple switch operators and releases a clutch to allow the timing gear to reset. A latch mechanism holds the cam wheel in the timed-out position until a solenoid-operated release mechanism disengages it. The configuration of this control wheel determines which switches are actuated and whether the clutch is engaged, thereby selecting the timer function.
mechanism_raw: Energy is stored mechanically in a spring during the timing period via a spring-return timing gear. At the timed-out point, the stored spring energy is released to drive a cam wheel that simultaneously actuates multiple switch operators and releases a clutch to allow the timing gear to reset. A latch mechanism holds the cam wheel in the timed-out position until a solenoid-operated wheel releases it. The configuration of this control wheel determines which switches are actuated and whether the clutch is engaged, thereby selecting the timer function.
residual_terms: ["spring", "timing gear", "cam wheel", "switch operators", "clutch", "latch mechanism", "solenoid", "control wheel", "timer function"]

abstract: A circular water ski device an upper and lower surface and having a revolving platform on the upper surface. There is a space between the upper and lower surface filled with buoyant material. The lower surface in a first embodiment has a general concave cross-section which may capture an air bubble, and provide a relief for the escape of entrapped water in another embodiment.
problem: Reducing hydrodynamic drag and managing water entrapment on a water ski device while maintaining buoyancy and structural support.
constraint: The concavity must be sufficient to reliably trap an air layer under dynamic conditions but not so deep as to cause hydrodynamic instability or catch water; the buoyant material must be distributed to maintain structural integrity while complementing the air-trapping effect.
mechanism: A concave lower surface geometry passively traps an air bubble between the device and the water surface, creating a low-friction air layer that reduces drag. The same concave geometry provides relief channels that allow entrapped water to escape rather than being trapped, preventing instability. Buoyant material disposed between the upper and lower surfaces provides structural support and flotation independent of the trapped air layer.
mechanism_raw: A concave lower surface geometry passively traps an air bubble between the ski and the water surface, creating a low-friction air layer that reduces drag. The same concave geometry provides relief channels that allow entrapped water to escape rather than being trapped, preventing instability. Buoyant material disposed between the upper and lower surfaces provides structural support and flotation independent of the trapped air layer.
residual_terms: ["concave lower surface", "air bubble", "air layer", "hydrodynamic drag", "relief channels", "entrapped water", "buoyant material", "structural support", "flotation"]

abstract: Cutting or shearing structure wherein cutter or shearing blades are revolvably mounted yet pinned to hubs keyed to a central shaft. The shaft of hub structure is constructed for elimination of broken shear pin points. The shear pins themselves are disposed transversely relative to the shaft and are so positioned as to prevent lateral play of the blade ends as these pass through the spaces between operatively associated cutter blades.
problem: Preventing blade failure at shear pin attachment points and eliminating lateral play of revolving cutting or shearing blades as they pass through gaps between opposing blades.
constraint: The transverse pin positioning must prevent lateral play without restricting the necessary rotational movement of the blades; the hub construction must eliminate stress concentrations while maintaining sufficient structural strength to transmit cutting forces through the shear pins.
mechanism: Shear pins are oriented transversely relative to the central shaft and positioned at specific locations along the blade-to-hub interface to constrain lateral movement of blade ends as they pass through spaces between operatively associated cutter blades. The hub and shaft structure is designed with a geometry that eliminates stress concentration points at the shear pin attachment locations, preventing premature pin failure. The blades remain revolvably mounted on the hubs while being pinned to transmit torque through the shear pins.
mechanism_raw: Shear pins are oriented transversely relative to the central shaft and positioned at specific locations along the blade-to-hub interface to constrain lateral movement of blade ends as they pass through spaces between operatively associated cutter blades. The hub and shaft structure is designed with a geometry that eliminates stress concentration points at the shear pin attachment locations, preventing premature pin failure. The blades remain revolvably mounted on the hubs while being pinned to transmit torque through the shear pins.
residual_terms: ["shear pins", "transverse orientation", "central shaft", "blade-to-hub interface", "lateral movement", "stress concentration", "hub and shaft structure", "revolvably mounted", "torque transmission"]

abstract: A greatly extended plenum chamber, comprising a plenum or exhaust chamber and a plenum extension connected thereto, is employed in combination with grease filters which operate by impingement and by centrifugal action. Furthermore, a stream of air is directed against the upstream surfaces of the filters. The result of the combination is a surprisingly effective removal of grease and smoke from cooking fumes, with consequent minimization of grease coatings on the surfaces of the plenum chamber and of the exhaust blower connected thereto. When space does not permit vertical installation of a large extended plenum chamber, portions of such chamber may be inclined from the vertical and/or may be replaced by a plurality of smaller plenum extensions. In an additional embodiment, the effect of a very large plenum extension is obtained by a single and much smaller plenum extension. This is achieved by (a) using a duct (to the exhaust blower) which has a diameter larger than the depth of the plenum extension, and (b) placing a relatively small air deflector below the connection between such duct and the plenum extension. Other features of the apparatus and method include (a) a unitary construction which is substantially completed at the factory and is easily and unitarily installed at the job site by dropping it into a hole in the ceiling, and (b) an electrostatic precipitator which is sometimes employed where smog regulations are particularly stringent.
problem: Efficiently removing grease and smoke from cooking fumes while minimizing surface contamination in confined spaces.
constraint: Balancing filtration effectiveness with installation space limitations, requiring adaptable geometry or duct sizing to maintain performance in constrained environments.
mechanism: A variable-geometry flow chamber with directed airflow creates impingement and centrifugal forces to separate particulates from a gas stream, enabling enhanced filtration volume within spatial constraints through adjustable internal geometry.
mechanism_raw: Combining an extended plenum chamber with directed airflow against filter surfaces to enhance impingement and centrifugal separation, allowing larger effective filtration volume within spatial constraints by inclining or subdividing the plenum.

abstract: A multiple low pressure selector relay having a housing provided with a plurality of low pressure relays each having an exhaust port. A movable selector is carried by the housing and has means for closing all of the exhaust ports except two thereof when the selector is in one position thereof, the selector having the means thereof opening other of the exhaust ports when the selector is moved to other positions thereof whereby the desired number of exhaust ports in addition to the two thereof can be opened.
problem: Selectingively activating a variable number of exhaust ports in a low-pressure relay system.
constraint: Ensuring reliable mechanical linkage between selector position and port states while maintaining pressure integrity across all configurations.
mechanism: A mechanically linked selector element dynamically adjusts the number of active exhaust pathways by selectively closing or opening ports in discrete positions, maintaining pressure integrity through direct mechanical coupling between selector position and port states.
mechanism_raw: A movable selector mechanically closes all exhaust ports except two in one position, and opens additional ports in other positions, enabling dynamic control of active exhaust pathways.

abstract: A method and apparatus for casting a plurality of ingots by forming a pool of molten metal in a main mold section which is in direct, open communication with a plurality of ingot mold sections by flowing the molten metal from the pool into the ingot mold sections. An electrode and a conductor establish an electrical current path, through the molten metal pool, which does not enter the ingot mold sections, and the cast ingots are electrically isolated at their lower ends.
problem: Casting multiple isolated ingots from a shared molten metal pool while maintaining electrical isolation of the ingots.
constraint: Preventing current leakage into the ingot sections while maintaining open communication between the pool and molds for molten metal flow.
mechanism: An electrical bypass path is established through a shared conductive medium to isolate individual mold sections, allowing independent solidification of each section without electrical interference while maintaining fluid communication between the medium and molds.
mechanism_raw: Establishing an electrical current path through the molten pool that bypasses the ingot mold sections, allowing independent solidification of each ingot without electrical interference.

abstract: A fire protection system including a plurality of suppressor units activatable to suppress a detected fire; a plurality of electrical current responsive activators, one associated with each of the suppressor units and adapted to induce activation thereof; a control circuit connecting the activators in series and including an actuator for initiating activating current flow to the activators; and an auxiliary circuit for connecting the activators parallel in response to the initiation of activating current flow by the actuator, the auxiliary circuit including a plurality of electronic switches, one connected between the supply and each of the junctions between each pair of series connected activators.
problem: Activating multiple fire suppressors in parallel when a fire is detected, while maintaining series connectivity for normal operation.
constraint: Ensuring fail-safe transition between series and parallel configurations without disrupting the control circuit during activation.
mechanism: A switching network transitions between series and parallel configurations of actuators via triggered electronic switches, ensuring simultaneous activation of all actuators upon detection of a condition while preserving circuit continuity during normal operation.
mechanism_raw: Switching from a series configuration of activators to a parallel configuration via electronic switches triggered by an actuator, ensuring simultaneous activation of all suppressors.

abstract: A machine has a movable boom for lifting a load, and an overload sensing device mounted on the boom to sense boom deflection. The overload sensing device includes a rigid beam having one end secured to a vertical side plate of the boom only by anchors spaced widely apart, welded preferably on opposite sides of the centroid or neutral axis of the boom side plate. The beam has a free end, on which an adjustable contact plate is carried, to engage a switch adjustably carried on a mounting plate secured to the beam side plate.
problem: Detecting overload conditions in a lifting boom by measuring deflection without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Positioning anchors to avoid interfering with the boom's neutral axis while ensuring accurate deflection measurement across varying load conditions.
mechanism: A rigid displacement translator anchored at spaced points on a structural member converts deflection into mechanical motion, actuating a switch via an adjustable contact element positioned to avoid interference with the member's neutral axis.
mechanism_raw: Using a rigid beam anchored at spaced points on the boom's side plate to translate deflection into mechanical displacement, which actuates a switch via an adjustable contact plate.

abstract: A translatory shock absorber is provided for mounting an attitude sensor thereon for isolating a sensor from translatory vibrations. The translatory shock absorber includes a hollow block structure formed as one piece to form a parallelogram. The absorber block structure includes a movable top plate for supporting the attitude sensor and a fixed base plate with opposed side plates interposed therebetween. At the junctions of the side plates, and the base and top plates, there are provided machined-out grooves which act as flexible hinges for attenuating translatory vibrations. A damping material is supported on a pedestal which is carried on the base plate between the side plates thereof. The top of the damping material rests against the bottom surface of the top plate for eliminating the resonant peaks of vibration.
problem: Isolating a sensor from translatory vibrations while maintaining structural support.
constraint: Balancing vibration isolation with structural rigidity to prevent sensor misalignment or mechanical failure.
mechanism: Use a compliant element to permit controlled displacement while a damping element absorbs vibrational energy through contact with a moving surface, balancing isolation with structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Flexible hinges (machined grooves) allow controlled movement to attenuate vibrations, while damping material absorbs resonant energy by pressing against the moving plate.

abstract: Refining with the requirements that a mixing rate of powder ore to lump ore is prepared in the range of 20 to 50%, the amount of SiO.sub.2 in the charging raw materials is readjusted to which the amount of SiO.sub.2 in the slag is in the range of 35 to 45% and impedance of volt-ampere between the electrode and the bottom of furnace is more than 1.6 .times. 10.sup..sup.-3.OMEGA. carbon-unsaturated system ferro-chromium of which both S and Si are low can be easily and stably obtained without desulfurizing out of the furnace.
problem: Producing carbon-unsaturated ferro-chromium with low sulfur and silicon content without external desulfurization.
constraint: Maintaining precise compositional and electrical thresholds to avoid destabilizing the furnace environment or requiring post-processing.
mechanism: Adjust material composition ratios and electrical parameters to control chemical reaction pathways, suppressing impurity retention during high-temperature processing.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting raw material ratios (powder-to-lump ore, SiO2 content) and electrical impedance parameters to control chemical reactions and prevent sulfur retention during smelting.

abstract: Metal oxides are directly reduced by charging metal oxide-carbonaceous agglomerates to a shaft furnace, passing said pellets downwardly countercurrent to a flow of hot gases in a reduction zone, wherein the agglomerates are heated to 2000.degree.-2400.degree.F. and reduction effected while the agglomerates maintain their integrity, and then transferring the reduced pellets to a melting zone. In the melting zone, having a controlled atmosphere, the pellets melt and a mass of molten metal and slag is formed and then discharged from the melting zone.
problem: Efficiently reducing metal oxides to molten metal while preserving pellet integrity during high-temperature processing.
constraint: Preventing pellet disintegration during reduction while managing atmospheric conditions to avoid unwanted oxidation or contamination.
mechanism: Apply staged thermal treatment in a countercurrent reactive medium to reduce metal oxides while maintaining structural integrity of agglomerates, followed by controlled-atmosphere phase transformation to separate molten product and residue.
mechanism_raw: Sequential heating of agglomerates in a countercurrent gas flow to reduce oxides at high temperatures, followed by controlled-atmosphere melting to form molten metal and slag.

abstract: An extraction tower for the counter-current leaching of sugar beets cossettes or crushed sugar cane. The elements which convey the material to be leached through the tower, especially the conveyor screw means and/or the baffle means which are arranged for cooperating with the conveyor screw means are provided with load sensor means, such as strain gauge elements which through control amplifier means control the drive means for the conveying elements to adapt the through-put and thus the conveying to the loads occurring throughout the tower. Even the pump and valve means may be controlled in response to such strain gauge means.
problem: Adapting material throughput in a counter-current leaching tower to variable loads without manual intervention.
constraint: Ensuring sensor accuracy and response speed to prevent overloading or underutilization of the tower components.
mechanism: Deploy real-time sensor feedback from load-bearing elements to dynamically adjust actuation systems, modulating material flow rates to match variable input conditions without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Strain gauge sensors on conveyor and baffle elements feed real-time load data to control amplifiers, which adjust drive motors and pumps to dynamically match throughput to load conditions.

abstract: The present invention introduces a heat engine, or a heat pump, in which the working medium used is subjected alternatively to solidification and melting operations. A working medium so used is referred to as an S/L type working medium. In a new heat engine, an S/L type working medium is subjected to cyclic operations, each cycle comprises of a high temperature melting step conducted under a first pressure, and a low temperature solidification step conducted under a second pressure. In a new heat pump, each cycle comprises of a high temperature solidification step conducted under a first pressure and a low temperature melting step conducted under a second pressure. When a non-aqueous medium is used, the first pressure and the second pressure are a relatively high pressure and a relatively low pressure, respectively. When an aqueous medium is used the two pressures are a relatively low pressure and a relatively high pressure, respectively. it is noted that the operation of a heat pump is the reverse operation of a heat engine.
problem: Creating a heat engine or heat pump that leverages phase changes of a working medium for thermal energy transfer.
constraint: Matching pressure and temperature conditions to the medium's phase behavior to sustain cyclic operation without external energy penalties.
mechanism: Cycle a phase-change medium between melting and solidification states under differential pressure conditions, using thermodynamic work from pressure differentials to drive thermal energy transfer.
mechanism_raw: Cycling a solid/liquid (S/L) medium between melting (high temperature, first pressure) and solidification (low temperature, second pressure) steps, with pressure differentials driving thermodynamic work.

abstract: A stepladder with a sturdy plate mounted on its top surface and a pair of wheels mounted near the top of the ladder is provided so that upon folding the legs together and inverting the ladder, it becomes a dolly which rides on said wheels and employs the plate as a carry plate. Additional wheels or casters are added to the other end of the ladder to convert same to a wheeled flat bed.
problem: A single piece of equipment (stepladder) needs to serve two distinct functional roles — climbing and cargo transport — without requiring separate dedicated devices.
constraint: The design must maintain structural integrity and load-bearing capacity in both the ladder and dolly configurations while using minimal additional components, so the placement of the plate and wheels must be compatible with both orientations.
mechanism: A single structural assembly incorporates load-bearing elements and transport elements positioned at a specific region of the structure. By changing the orientation and configuration state of the assembly, the same physical elements are repositioned through geometric reconfiguration: one element becomes a horizontal load-bearing surface and the other elements become rolling supports, transforming the assembly from a climbing structure into a cargo transport structure. The mechanism relies on changing the configuration state of the structure to repurpose existing components for a new function.
mechanism_raw: The ladder incorporates a sturdy top plate and wheels positioned near the top. By folding the legs together and inverting the ladder, the same physical components are repositioned through geometric reconfiguration: the plate becomes a horizontal carry surface and the wheels become the rolling support, transforming the ladder into a dolly. Additional wheels at the opposite end convert it to a flatbed. The mechanism relies on changing the configuration state of the structure to repurpose existing components for a new function.

abstract: A rotary pump includes a plurality of rotor driven radial vanes pivotally supported on a cantilevered pivot pin located centrally of a cylindrical pump housing by a first end fixed to a closure plate of the pump and a free end spaced with respect to the end plate of a cylindrical rotor. A pilot sleeve is press fit within a vane hub and the sleeve includes a bearing surface for rotatably supporting the pilot sleeve on the free end of the pivot pin and the sleeve further includes means for guiding the pilot sleeve within a grooved track in the end plate of the rotor so as to prevent deflection of the pivot pin and resultant wear of pump vane tips on the inner surface of a pump chamber.
problem: In a rotary vane pump, the cantilevered pivot pin supporting the vanes can deflect under operational loads, causing the vane tips to wear against the inner surface of the pump chamber.
constraint: The pilot sleeve must allow free rotation of the vane hub on the pivot pin while simultaneously constraining lateral deflection, requiring precise press-fit tolerances and groove geometry that balance bearing support with minimal friction.
mechanism: An intermediate guided bearing element is press-fit within a rotating hub and rotatably supported on the free end of a cantilevered support member via a bearing surface. The element also engages a grooved track in a fixed structure, providing lateral guidance that constrains the cantilevered member from deflecting. The element acts as an intermediate guided bearing that maintains rotational freedom while preventing lateral displacement of the cantilevered member.
mechanism_raw: A pilot sleeve is press-fit within the vane hub and rotatably supported on the free end of the pivot pin via a bearing surface. The sleeve also engages a grooved track in the rotor's end plate, providing lateral guidance that constrains the pivot pin from deflecting. The sleeve acts as an intermediate guided bearing element that maintains rotational freedom while preventing lateral displacement of the cantilevered pin.
residual_terms: ["guided bearing element", "press-fit", "rotatably supported", "bearing surface", "grooved track", "lateral guidance", "cantilevered member"]

abstract: This is an improved smokeless flare powered by air supply to the burner at substantial velocity. The flare includes an air flow-operated damper for the purpose of preventing the back flow of flame and hot gases under adverse wind conditions. The damper consists of two semicircular plates which are hinged along the diameter of the air supply pipe and are held in a closed (transverse) position by means of tension springs. Another feature of this flare is that in the sectors between the spider arms of the burner there are baffles which are triangular in shape and have substantial longitudinal dimension. There are narrow passages between the baffles and each of the adjacent spider arms so that the air flow from the blower must pass through these restricted passages and therefore will move at a higher velocity. A third feature involves openings through the side wall of the air flow pipe opposite the baffles so that there is induced flow of air through these openings into the baffle space and up through the triangular wall of the baffle to prevent accumulation of soot.
problem: A smokeless flare must prevent backflow of flame and hot gases under adverse wind conditions while also preventing soot accumulation in the baffle spaces.
constraint: The damper spring tension must be calibrated so it opens reliably under normal airflow but closes quickly against backflow, while the baffle geometry must increase air velocity enough for soot prevention without excessively restricting primary combustion airflow.
mechanism: Two opposing barrier elements are hinged along a flow path and held closed by resilient elements. Flow pressure overcomes the resilient force to open the barrier in the normal direction, but reverses to close it against backflow. Constriction elements with narrow passages between them and support arms reduce the cross-sectional area of the flow path, increasing velocity through the Bernoulli effect. Openings opposite the constriction elements induce secondary flow through the constriction walls, sweeping away accumulated material before it can settle.
mechanism_raw: Two semicircular damper plates are hinged along the air supply pipe diameter and held closed by tension springs. Airflow pressure overcomes spring tension to open the damper in the normal direction, but reverses to close it against backflow. Triangular baffles with narrow passages between them and spider arms constrict airflow, increasing velocity through the Bernoulli effect. Openings opposite the baffles induce secondary airflow through the baffle walls, sweeping away soot before it can accumulate.

abstract: An apparatus is provided for use as a suspension device for suspending one or more anodes and one or more reference cells inside metallic water tanks as a portion of a cathodic protection system for the water tank for the inhibition of corrosion in the tank. The apparatus is particularly adapted for use in the northern reaches of the earth's temperate zones, where ice forms in outdoor water tanks during the winter season. The apparatus is designed to maintain the anodes and reference cells suspended therefrom in the liquid portion of the water tank as ice forms at the top of the water, the bottom of the water and at the sides of the tank and to allow the anodes and reference cells to retain the ability to perform their function despite the ice.
problem: Corrosion-inhibiting anodes and reference cells in metallic water tanks must remain suspended in the liquid portion of the water even as ice forms simultaneously at the top, bottom, and sides of the tank during winter.
constraint: The suspension must accommodate ice formation at multiple surfaces (top, bottom, sides) simultaneously while keeping the electrodes electrically coupled to the liquid water, requiring compliance in multiple degrees of freedom without losing the electrodes from the water entirely.
mechanism: A flexible mounting system allows monitoring elements to move with the receding liquid interface as solidification occurs at multiple boundaries. The mounting system maintains the elements in contact with the remaining liquid by accommodating the changing three-dimensional geometry of the liquid/solid boundary, rather than fixing them at a static position that would become isolated by the solid phase.
mechanism_raw: The suspension apparatus uses a flexible or adaptive mounting system that allows the anodes and reference cells to move with the receding liquid interface as ice forms at multiple boundaries. The suspension maintains the electrodes in contact with the remaining liquid water by accommodating the changing three-dimensional geometry of the water/ice boundary, rather than fixing them at a static position that would become isolated by ice.
residual_terms: ["flexible mounting system", "monitoring elements", "liquid interface", "liquid/solid boundary", "solid phase"]

abstract: A single-sideband radiotelephone system includes a single-sideband transmitter which initially broadcasts two frequency-spaced tones simultaneously for a predetermined time interval, and thereafter broadcasts the two tones alternately in a unique code pattern to access a predetermined receiver. Each single-sideband receiver in the system includes a pair of detectors each having a narrow bandpass, the center frequencies of which are spaced apart by the difference in frequency of the transmitted tones. The center frequencies of the detectors are simultaneously varied relative to the initial two-tone broadcast while maintaining the frequency differential therebetween; and simultaneous detection of both tones will terminate the frequency varying mode of operation. The subsequently transmitted unique code pattern is then sensed by the detectors, the code pattern decoded, and the selected receiver is enabled to receive any subsequently broadcasted information.
problem: A single-sideband radiotelephone system needs to selectively access a predetermined receiver from multiple receivers, overcoming frequency uncertainty and providing coded addressing.
constraint: The paired detectors must maintain their exact frequency differential during sweeping to correctly identify the tone pair, and the system must distinguish between the initial synchronization tone burst and the subsequent coded access pattern to avoid false triggering.
mechanism: A transmitter first broadcasts two frequency-spaced signals simultaneously to establish a reference. Each receiver has paired narrow-band detectors whose center frequencies are simultaneously swept while maintaining their fixed frequency differential. When both detectors simultaneously sense the transmitted signals, the sweep terminates, indicating frequency acquisition. The transmitter then sends a unique coded pattern of alternating signals, which the now-frequency-locked detectors decode to selectively enable only the target receiver.
mechanism_raw: The transmitter first broadcasts two frequency-spaced tones simultaneously to establish a reference. Each receiver has paired narrow-band detectors whose center frequencies are simultaneously swept while maintaining their fixed frequency differential. When both detectors simultaneously sense the transmitted tones, the sweep terminates, indicating frequency acquisition. The transmitter then sends a unique coded pattern of alternating tones, which the now-frequency-locked detectors decode to selectively enable only the target receiver.

abstract: Means for retarding the spread of fire from a building space, comprising an upwardly extending duct, the cross-sectional area of which is related by formulae to the cross-sectional area for air intake to the space, and has an access gate at the lower end for connecting the duct with the building space, and preferably a release gate at the upper end for connecting the duct with the outside atmosphere. Preferably the access gate and release gate are thermally actuated by having heat destructible components which are destroyed by flames from a fire in the space. The cross-sectional area of the duct and of the air intake are determined by design to i) drain away flames and smoke, ii) produce a depression in the building space thereby retarding the spread of fire, and iii) draw sufficient air to the building space to ensure relatively low fire temperature and a relatively short fire duration. The same ducts may serve a number of building spaces above one another at different floor levels. Open plan buildings and corridors may have drop curtains which isolate the or each building space in the event of fire, but leave openings for the designed air intake.
problem: Preventing uncontrolled spread of fire and smoke between building spaces during a fire event.
constraint: Balancing duct and air intake dimensions to achieve sufficient depression and airflow without compromising structural integrity or over-restricting air supply.
mechanism: A heat-responsive system creates controlled pressure differentials across interconnected pathways to passively redirect and dissipate combustible materials, using automatic actuation triggered by thermal thresholds to regulate airflow and reduce thermal energy during a fire event.
mechanism_raw: Using a thermally actuated duct system with cross-sectional areas designed to create controlled pressure differentials, draining flames/smoke, and regulating airflow to lower fire temperature and duration. Gates open automatically in response to heat, enabling passive suppression.

abstract: A spraying device for a bottle cleaning machine in which bottles are conveyed in inverted position. The spraying device reciprocates in the machine beneath the bottles and includes upwardly directed nozzles that follow respective bottles in succession for a predetermined distance. A cam drive is provided for the device with a guide return. The frame for the spraying device is supported and guided in the machine on antifriction elements. The antifriction elements may include balls rollingly supported by channels in the machine and rollingly engaged by the frame of the spraying device.
problem: Achieving precise, low-wear reciprocating motion for spray nozzles in a bottle cleaning machine.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and durability of rolling elements under repeated reciprocation while minimizing friction and wear.
mechanism: A rotating input drives a reciprocating component via a shaped mechanical interface, while rolling elements constrained in channels reduce friction and maintain alignment between the moving component and a target surface during repeated linear motion cycles.
mechanism_raw: Combining a cam-driven reciprocating frame with antifriction rolling elements (balls in channels) to guide smooth, aligned movement while maintaining nozzle-to-bottle contact over a predetermined distance.

abstract: Logs or tree limb sections to be debarked and a plurality of smaller, higher density impact objects are disposed in a series of interfaced, open-ended cylindrical sections, alternate ones of which have different diameters and are rotated in opposite directions about generally horizontal axes. The cylindrical sections are generally tangent about a point above their rotational axes and their upper ends are inclined slightly to promote migration of the impact objects and wood sections in series through the chambers and for discharging the same from the final chamber. At least the larger diameter sections include conveyers for carrying the impact objects upwardly and for releasing the same for impacting engagement against the wood sections to be debarked and an external conveyer recycles the impact objects from the final to the initial cylindrical section. An air delivery system discharges dislodged bark and other foreign material from the cylindrical sections.
problem: Efficiently removing bark from logs using mechanical impact and material transport.
constraint: Balancing rotational speeds, cylinder diameters, and conveyor timing to ensure effective debarking without damaging wood or jamming the system.
mechanism: Alternating rotational forces and variable geometry surfaces generate a tumbling environment where high-inertia impact objects repeatedly strike and dislodge material, while synchronized transport mechanisms lift and reposition objects to enable repeated interactions and debris evacuation.
mechanism_raw: Rotating cylindrical sections of alternating diameters and opposing directions create a tumbling action with high-density impact objects, while conveyors lift and release objects for repeated impacts. Inclined upper ends and air systems facilitate material migration and debris removal.

abstract: An apparatus for sorting silverware including a hopper for collecting the silverware in bulk amounts and a vibrating bed for gradually discharging the silverwave and conveying it to a sorting stage for dividing the different types of silverware. The sorting stage includes a table defining a barrier against which the silverware is directed. Laterally extending openings are defined by the barrier, and these openings permit the passage of knives past the barrier means. Forks and spoons are held by the barrier means as they are moved over the table and are then dropped onto a structure which separates the forks and spoons. Receptacles are provided for collecting the different types of silverware.
problem: Separating mixed silverware types (knives, forks, spoons) based on shape differences.
constraint: Designing barrier openings and vibration parameters to reliably differentiate items by shape without jamming or misrouting.
mechanism: Vibratory motion conveys items along a surface toward a barrier with openings sized and shaped to permit passage of specific geometries while blocking others, with blocked items diverted to a secondary sorting stage based on additional shape discrimination.
mechanism_raw: Using a vibrating bed to convey items to a barrier with laterally extending openings that allow knives to pass while blocking forks/spoons, which are then dropped onto a secondary separator for further sorting.

abstract: A method for avoiding cracking of the molded body during the decompression step in an isostatic pressing method of molding. The powders to be molded are housed in a shaping rubber mold, are molded under pressure, and the improvement is characterized by supplying forcibly gas between the outer peripheral surface of a molded body or a shaping thin rubber bag where the molded body is housed and the inner peripheral surface of the shaping rubber mold, the gas having a pressure higher than the isostatic pressure applied to the shaping rubber mold at the time when the shaping rubber mold begins to restore to its original state during the decompression step of the method. An apparatus for the said compression molding which is equipped with a specially designed pressure gas inletting device.
problem: Preventing cracks in molded bodies during decompression in isostatic pressing.
constraint: Timing gas injection to exceed isostatic pressure precisely during decompression without over-pressurizing or disrupting the molding process.
mechanism: A pressurized medium is injected between a forming surface and a molded object during decompression to counteract collapsing forces, with timing synchronized to exceed ambient pressure precisely as the mold restores its shape, preserving structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Injecting gas at higher pressure between the molded body and shaping rubber mold during decompression to counteract collapsing forces, maintaining structural integrity as the mold restores.

abstract: A multiple ply wood article having a first wood veneer ply defining a generally tubular shape, which may be generally cylindrical, with a pair of confronting ends providing a first seam. A second wood veneer ply defining a generally tubular shape generally similar to the shape of the first wood veneer ply with a pair of confronting ends providing a second seam. The second wood veneer ply being disposed exteriorly of the first wood veneer ply in general surface to surface adjacency. The grain orientations of the first and second wood veneer plies being oriented generally parallel with respect to each other. Adhesive means securing the wood veneer plies to establish a multiple ply tubular body. The first and second seams are preferably in generally relative nonaligned position. Additional wood veneer plies having similar structural features may be secured over the first two plies. Closure elements may be secured to one or both ends of the tubular body in order to establish a container. A method of manufacturing the multiple ply wood article described above including preforming the first and second wood veneer plies into the desired general shape, applying adhesive to at least one of the two surfaces to be bonded and securing the two plies in surface to surface adjacency with the grains being oriented generally parallel. Additional plies may be preformed and simultaneously or sequentially bonded to create additional plies in the tubular body.
problem: Creating a structurally robust tubular wood article from multiple veneer plies while maintaining integrity during forming and use.
constraint: Balancing structural strength and seam offsetting to avoid weak points while allowing preforming of the tubular shape without delamination.
mechanism: Orienting reinforcement directions of adjacent layers in parallel alignment while staggering interface lines between layers to distribute stress concentrations and prevent failure along a single interface, combined with a binding agent to lock the layered structure together.
mechanism_raw: Aligning grain orientations of adjacent plies in parallel and offsetting seams between plies to distribute stress and prevent failure along a single seam line, combined with adhesive bonding to lock the layered structure.

abstract: To maintain centering of the axis of a machine movable along a tube and rotatable relative to the tube, the machine is associated with a weight compensating device which provides a weight compensation sufficient to compensate for the weight of the machine regardless of the attitude of the machine in the tube. The device comprises at least one closed chamber for liquid and communicating with at least three radially extending, equally angularly spaced cylinders and pistons, the pistons of which are fixed to the chamber and the cylinders of which carry rollers bearing against the wall of the tube.
problem: Maintaining the centered position of a machine moving along and rotating within a tube, regardless of its orientation or attitude.
constraint: Ensuring equal angular spacing of pistons and sufficient liquid incompressibility to provide real-time, passive compensation for weight variations across all orientations.
mechanism: Using a closed incompressible fluid chamber connected to radially extending pistons with contact elements that bear against a surrounding surface, automatically adjusting fluid pressure distribution to counteract gravitational and inertial forces and maintain central positioning across all orientations.
mechanism_raw: Using a closed liquid-filled chamber connected to radially extending pistons with rollers that bear against the tube wall, automatically adjusting liquid pressure distribution to counteract gravitational and inertial forces on the machine.

abstract: This invention relates to a diver's re-breathing apparatus of a closed circuit type. The gas circuit is provided with a solenoid valve coupled to an oxygen cylinder and arranged to be energised to introduce oxygen into the breathable atmosphere when the oxygen content therein drops below a certain proportion. The electrical circuit comprises a pair of transducers in the gas circuit, one of which is sensitive to oxygen partial pressure and the other sensitive to total pressure, the outputs of the two transducers being amplified and fed into an analogue divider, the output of the divider being responsive to percentage of oxygen in the breathable atmosphere and being effective to energise the solenoid to thereby maintain the oxygen content of the breathable atmosphere within limits of percentage, rather than within limits of partial pressure.
problem: Maintaining safe oxygen concentration in a closed-circuit rebreathing system by controlling gas composition rather than absolute partial pressure.
constraint: Achieving real-time computation of gas ratios with minimal latency while ensuring sensor accuracy and valve responsiveness to avoid hypoxia or oxygen toxicity.
mechanism: Using two transducers to measure a target gas partial pressure and total pressure, feeding their outputs into an analogue divider to compute gas percentage, and using this ratio to trigger a control valve for precise gas replenishment based on composition rather than absolute pressure.
mechanism_raw: Using two transducers to measure oxygen partial pressure and total pressure, feeding their outputs into an analogue divider to compute oxygen percentage, and using this ratio to trigger a solenoid valve for precise oxygen replenishment.

abstract: Fatty acid ester mixtures liquid at low temperatures comprising (A) alkylene oxide adducts to train-oil fatty acids, or mixtures, esterified with unsaturated fatty acids, or mixtures, which are substantially free of any polyunsaturated train-oil fatty acids; or (B) alkylene oxide adducts to unsaturated fatty acids, or mixtures, which are substantially free of any polyunsaturated train-oil fatty acids, esterified with train-oil fatty acids, or mixtures; as well as compositions for using and the processes of preparing and using these esters.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical composition (fatty acid esters with defined adducts and esterification) to achieve low-temperature fluidity, but does not describe a functional mechanism for solving a broader problem beyond material formulation.

abstract: Hollow semiconductor bodies having an outer surface composed of a doped semiconductor material and an inner surface composed of a pure semiconductor material are formed by sequential deposition from a gaseous thermally decomposable semiconductor compound onto a heated carrier member. The multi-layer hollow semiconductor bodies are directly heatable during diffusion of dopants into semiconductor elements.
reason: The patent describes a semiconductor manufacturing process (sequential deposition to form hollow bodies with doped and pure layers) but does not articulate a transferable functional mechanism beyond the specific technical domain of semiconductor doping and structure formation.

abstract: A remote control system for the jack cylinders of a hydraulically operated crane includes a plurality of regulating valves for controlling respective jack cylinders, the regulation of each valve being controlled by the movement of a respective valve spool connected to a respective lever forming part of a linkage including an arm mounted on a rotatable shaft and connectable to the shaft by a respective electromagnetically operated clutch so that by engagement of one said clutch and rotation of the shaft to a predetermined position the corresponding valve spool may be correspondingly positioned to move the associated jack cylinder accordingly. Engagement of the clutches and rotation of the shaft can be controlled by a portable actuating unit connected to the rest of the system by an electrical cable, the system including a control means which adjusts the position of the shaft to correspond with the setting of a control member on the actuating unit.
problem: Remote control of multiple hydraulic jack cylinders on a crane with a single portable actuating unit.
constraint: The system must balance selective engagement of clutches with precise shaft positioning to avoid unintended valve movements while maintaining remote operability.
mechanism: A central control unit selectively engages discrete mechanical pathways through a clutch mechanism, enabling a single input to actuate multiple independent output devices. The clutch mechanism allows selective coupling between a shared rotational input and individual output linkages, with positional feedback ensuring precise alignment of each output device.
mechanism_raw: Electromagnetic clutches selectively engage a rotatable shaft connected to valve spools via a linkage, allowing a central shaft rotation to position individual valve spools when a clutch is engaged. The portable actuating unit controls clutch engagement and shaft rotation to map control inputs to specific jack cylinders.

abstract: Apparatus and method for forming hemmed curtains including advancing a continuous length of fabric while simultaneously carrying adhesive filaments across the fabric, then stopping the fabric and performing a series of operations thereon at an operating station, including cutting the fabric along a transverse line adjacent the adhesive filaments, then folding the fabric end pieces with a double folded hem extending over the adhesive filaments and with the cut edge of the fabric contained within the fold so as not to be exposed, then heating the adhesive filaments to melt them and thereby secure the folded hems in place, and finally advancing the fabric again to present another part thereof for similar processing. Preferably, two adhesive filaments are carried across one of the fabric pieces whereby the folded hem thereof will be secured in place along spaced parallel securing lines so as to provide a curtain rod pocket in such hem.
problem: Creating a hemmed curtain with an integrated curtain rod pocket using a continuous fabric web.
constraint: The fabric must remain stationary during cutting, folding, and heating to ensure precise alignment of the hem and adhesive placement.
mechanism: A synchronized multi-stage process applies material advancement, adhesive deposition, cutting, folding, and energy-induced bonding in a repeating sequence. Each stage operates on a stationary workpiece to ensure alignment accuracy, with incremental progression forming discrete secured sections.
mechanism_raw: A synchronized sequence of advancing fabric, applying adhesive filaments, cutting, folding the fabric end over the adhesive, and heating to bond the hem. The process repeats incrementally to form discrete hems with parallel securing lines.

abstract: In a mold for casting an annular rim member for use in a vehicle wheel for mounting a pneumatic tire, the mold cavity is formed so that the casting has at least one of a radial overdimension or a radial underdimension and its outer surface which faces the tire has an unsegmented annular area. After the casting is solidified and removed from the mold, it is plastically deformed by radially directed cold forming or working to remove the radial overdimension or underdimension. An iron-carbon melt is used for the casting to provide a ductile structure whose yield point is exceeded in carrying out the plastic deformation.
problem: Achieving precise radial dimensions in a cast annular rim for a vehicle wheel.
constraint: The material must have sufficient ductility to exceed its yield point during cold working without structural failure.
mechanism: A two-phase dimensional correction process involves forming a component with intentional geometric deviations, followed by controlled plastic deformation to achieve target dimensions. The material's ductility enables deformation beyond its yield point without structural failure.
mechanism_raw: Casting the rim with intentional radial over/under-dimensioning, then using cold working (plastic deformation) to correct the dimensions. The ductile iron-carbon melt allows deformation without fracturing.

abstract: A drapery table having a clamp bar extending the width thereof and supported thereon parallel to the forward table edge, or to a reference line of the table, clamp devices for securing one edge of a large sheet of fabric to the clamp bar, and a power device for moving said bar laterally to draw said fabric sheet across the table, so as to insure that the line of the fabric at the table edge, or at the reference line, is precisely parallel to the clamped fabric edge. Devices are provided for automatically stopping the bar at the limits of its travel, for adjusting the limits at which bar travel is stopped, for adjusting the bar into precise parallelism with the table edge, or the reference line thereof, and providing for allowing individual application of the clamp devices, but for simultaneous release of all of the clamp devices from a single station.
problem: Precisely aligning a fabric sheet's edge parallel to a reference line on a drapery table.
constraint: The system must allow individual clamp engagement while enabling simultaneous release of all clamps from a single station.
mechanism: A movable clamping system engages a workpiece edge and translates it across a surface using a powered actuator. Integrated positional constraints and adjustable stops maintain alignment relative to a reference during movement, with selective clamp engagement enabling individual control.
mechanism_raw: A clamp bar secures one fabric edge, and a power device moves the bar laterally to draw the fabric across the table. Automatic stops and adjustments ensure the fabric edge remains parallel to the reference line during movement.

abstract: A dry-process method and apparatus for producing archival microform records from light reflecting hard copy utilize a dry-process mask film strip which is photosensitive to and microimaged by light reflected and reduced or condensed from the hard copy and developed by heat to provide microimaged transparencies therein as the mask film strip is moved to an imaging and developing station. It also utilizes a dry-process microform film which has archival properties and which is sensitive to and microimaged and developed by short pulses of electromagnetic energy above a threshold value applied thereto through the microimaged transparencies of the superimposed mask film strip when it is moved to an image transferring station to provide in the microform film imaged microform records which conform to the transparent microimages in the dry-process mask film strip and, hence, the hard copy and which have achival properties. The microform film is preferably in the form of a microfiche.
problem: Producing archival microform records from light-reflecting hard copy without wet chemical processing.
constraint: The films must respond selectively to specific energy thresholds to avoid unintended exposure or degradation during imaging and development.
mechanism: A dual-stage imaging process uses energy-responsive media to capture and transfer images without liquid development. A first medium records an image via reflected energy, then selectively exposes a second medium through controlled energy pulses above a threshold, creating a transparency without chemical processing.
mechanism_raw: A dry-process mask film is microimaged by reflected light, then heat-developed to create transparencies. A second dry-process microform film is exposed through the mask via short electromagnetic pulses above a threshold, transferring the image without liquid development.

abstract: In a process for the preparation of tannable pelts from animal skins or hides wherein concurrent soaking, unhairing, opening up of the hide structure, and bating are effected in a single procedural step by treatment with enzymes in an aqueous bath containing enzymes, the improvement wherein the enzymatic treating bath is free of amines and comprises dissolved therein: PA1 A. an effective amount of at least one member selected from the group consisting of a fungus protease whose optimum efficacy towards casein is at a pH above 7.0, trypsin, papain, and a bacterial protease whose optimum efficacy is at a pH between 6 and 9; PA1 B. an effective amount of a bacterial protease having an optimum efficacy against hemoglobin at a pH above 9; and PA1 C. an effective amount of thioglycolic acid or a salt thereof.
problem: Efficiently performing multiple sequential leather-processing steps (soaking, unhairing, opening, bating) in a single enzymatic bath without damaging hide structure or requiring amines.
constraint: The enzymes must operate within non-overlapping pH ranges to avoid mutual inhibition, and the absence of amines prevents unwanted chemical interactions that could disrupt enzymatic efficacy or hide integrity.
mechanism: Using multiple agents with non-overlapping operational ranges to execute sequential processes in a single environment, avoiding mutual inhibition and structural damage. The agents are selected such that their activity thresholds (e.g., pH ranges) prevent interference while enabling simultaneous or staged actions.
mechanism_raw: Combining a cocktail of enzymes with specific pH optima (fungal protease above pH 7, bacterial protease between pH 6-9, and another bacterial protease above pH 9) alongside thioglycolic acid in an amine-free aqueous bath. This enables simultaneous enzymatic actions to execute multiple processing steps in one procedural stage, leveraging pH-dependent enzyme activity to avoid interference and structural damage.

abstract: A rotary engine includes a tri-lobular casing provided an elliptical piston having two opposite faces alternately cooperating to define one of three firing chambers with a segment of the casing wall. Gearing and eccentric means supporting the piston within the casing and connected to side plates translate the location of the center axis of the piston 120.degree. relative the center of the casing during each firing stroke thereof as one nose of the piston travels a distance substantially three times that of the opposite nose whereby six firing strokes take place during each 360.degree. revolution of the piston.
problem: Achieving a high number of power strokes in a compact rotary engine without increasing rotational speed or mechanical complexity.
constraint: The piston's shape and the casing's tri-lobular design must precisely coordinate with the gearing to maintain continuous contact between piston faces and casing walls, ensuring smooth translation of motion without mechanical interference.
mechanism: Employing a geometric arrangement of a multi-faced moving element within a multi-lobed casing, coordinated via eccentric motion conversion, to generate multiple power strokes per revolution. The shape and spatial relationship between the moving element and casing walls ensure continuous contact and motion translation without mechanical interference.
mechanism_raw: Using an elliptical piston with two opposite faces and a tri-lobular casing. Eccentric gearing and side plates translate the piston's center axis 120 degrees relative to the casing during each firing stroke, causing one nose to travel three times the distance of the opposite nose. This geometric arrangement converts rotational motion into six firing strokes per 360-degree revolution.

abstract: A method of pelletizing glass batch materials including commercially available sand, soda ash, salt cake, other minor glass forming materials, dolomite having an average (statistical mean) particle size less than 15 microns, and limestone having an average (statistical mean) particle size less than 250 microns is disclosed. The process involves the steps of mixing the glass batch materials together. A pelletizing regime is established on a rotating, pelletizing disc in which three zones of pelletization exist in the form of a pellet nucleation zone, a pellet growth zone, and a pellet tumbling zone. Each of the zones exists generally from the top of the pelletizing disc downwardly in a curved fashion over an area of the pelletizing disc with each zone having a discernable width. A prescribed amount of water is added to a portion of a pellet growth zone established on the pelletizing disc. A prescribed amount of a caustic soda solution is also added to a portion of the pellet growth zone spaced downwardly from the top of the pellet growth zone. The caustic addition is in the form of a wide stream generally centered with respect to the centerline of the pellet growth zone and spread across a substantial portion of the width of the pellet growth zone. A prescribed amount of the mixed glass batch materials are added to a portion of the pellet growth zone spaced downwardly from the caustic addition position. The batch materials addition stream is in the form of a wide stream generally centered with respect to the centerline of the pellet growth zone. The stream of batch materials is spread across a substantial portion of the width of the pellet growth zone. The caustic addition stream has a width in the range from slightly less than the width of the batch materials addition stream to a width of about 70% of the batch materials addition stream. Both the addition streams are centered with repsect to one another.
problem: Producing uniform glass batch pellets efficiently by controlling nucleation, growth, and tumbling phases in a rotating pelletizing disc.
constraint: The width and positioning of the caustic soda and batch material streams must be precisely coordinated (caustic stream width between 70% and slightly less than the batch stream) to ensure uniform chemical interaction without disrupting pellet formation dynamics.
mechanism: Establishing distinct spatial zones on a rotating surface to sequentially manage nucleation, growth, and tumbling phases. Controlled addition of materials in specific zones, with stream widths coordinated to ensure uniform interaction, prevents over-wetting and promotes controlled agglomeration.
mechanism_raw: Establishing three distinct zones (nucleation, growth, tumbling) on a rotating disc. Water and caustic soda solution are added as wide, centered streams in the growth zone, with the caustic stream narrower than the batch material stream. This staged addition optimizes moisture and chemical distribution to promote controlled pellet growth while preventing over-wetting or uneven agglomeration.

abstract: The disclosure relates to a method of upgrading metallurgical grade silicon to semiconductor grade for making low cost silicon devices and particularly solar cells. This is accomplished by passing conductive fibers such as graphite or the like which are compatible with the later processing steps through an area which is cooled below 700.degree. C and which contains silicon difluoride and a proper N-type dopant. At these temperatures, the silicon difluoride gas will break down into pure silicon which will deposit onto the fiber with the formation of silicon tetrafluoride gas which is then recycled into a further chamber. In the further chamber, the gaseous silicon tetrafluoride is mixed with the impure metallurgical grade silicon at temperatures above 700.degree. C to form the silicon difluoride gas which is then fed into the former chamber for deposition of pure silicon onto the continuously moving fibers of graphite or the like. A p-type layer can then be formed over the n-type layer in any standard manner, such as by then passing the coated fibers through a further reaction chamber wherein p-type dopant is diffused into the top surface of the n-type layer that has been formed. The dopants alternatively could be added in the gas stream of SiF.sub.4 or the p-layer formed by ion implantation. In this way, relatively inexpensive p-n junction devices are formed without the requirement of purifying, cutting and polishing a silicon slice in the standard manner.
problem: Upgrading metallurgical-grade silicon to semiconductor-grade purity without traditional purification, slicing, or polishing steps.
constraint: Temperature control is critical: the deposition chamber must remain below 700°C to prevent SiF2 decomposition into non-depositable forms, while the recycling chamber must exceed 700°C to drive the reverse reaction with impure silicon.
mechanism: Implementing a continuous gas-phase deposition and recycling loop with temperature-controlled chambers. A substance is deposited in a cooled chamber and regenerated in a heated chamber, enabling purity enhancement through selective decomposition and recombination without bulk purification.
mechanism_raw: Passing conductive fibers through a cooled chamber (<700°C) containing silicon difluoride (SiF2) gas and dopants. SiF2 decomposes to deposit pure silicon onto the fibers, forming SiF4 gas that is recycled to a high-temperature chamber (>700°C) where it reacts with impure silicon to regenerate SiF2. This continuous gas-phase deposition and recycling loop enables pure silicon coating on fibers, bypassing bulk purification.

abstract: A circular knitting machine for stockings, particularly for the manufacture of stockings closed at the toe directly on the machine, having a coupling joint for disengaging the lower needle cylinder from the upper needle cylinder or from the welt dial. The coupling joint consists of a substantially flanged element rigid with the shaft driving the lower needle cylinder and of a gear wheel mounted idly and axially displaceable on the shaft. The gear wheel engages with a corresponding crown gear for rotation of the upper needle cylinder or the welt dial. The flanged element and the gear wheel have means for mutual engagement and the machine further comprises means for the axial displacement of the gear wheel to disengage it from the flanged element, these means being responsive to the machine program.
problem: Automatically disengaging mechanical components (e.g., needle cylinders) in a circular knitting machine to enable seamless toe-closing operations without manual intervention.
constraint: The gear wheel must be precisely aligned with the flanged element during engagement to transmit torque without slippage, and the axial displacement mechanism must respond reliably to the machine's program to avoid unintended disengagement during operation.
mechanism: Using program-controlled axial displacement of a mechanical coupling element to selectively engage or disengage components. The displacement mechanism ensures precise alignment during engagement and reliable disconnection based on operational requirements, enabling automated transitions between functional phases.
mechanism_raw: A flanged element rigidly attached to the driving shaft engages with an idly mounted, axially displaceable gear wheel. Program-controlled axial displacement of the gear wheel disengages it from the flanged element, decoupling the upper/lower needle cylinders or welt dial. This allows selective mechanical disconnection based on the knitting program, enabling automated transitions between knitting phases.

abstract: An apparatus for slicing a meat product in which the cutting edge of a rotating involute slicing blade is advanced in synchronism with the feed of the meat product during the cutting of a slice from the meat product. There is also means for either mounting an involute slicing blade or arranging the cutting edge of an involute slicing blade.
problem: Achieving consistent, clean slices of a deformable material (e.g., meat) without tearing or irregular thickness during high-speed cutting.
constraint: Maintaining precise temporal and spatial coordination between two independent mechanical motions (blade rotation and material feed) to avoid misalignment or inconsistent slice quality.
mechanism: Coordinating the periodic cutting action of a moving blade with the continuous advancement of material so that the blade's cutting trajectory remains synchronized with the material's displacement, thereby maintaining uniform slice geometry and preventing deformation-induced irregularities.
mechanism_raw: Synchronizing the rotational motion of an involute slicing blade's cutting edge with the linear feed rate of the material being sliced, ensuring the blade's cutting path matches the material's movement to maintain uniform slice geometry.
residual_terms: ["involute slicing blade", "rotational motion", "linear feed rate", "cutting path"]

abstract: A ram-borer apparatus is described which comprises a tubular housing, a percussion piston which is movable axially to and fro in the housing, and a striker-tip which is arranged to slide in an axial direction relative to the housing and which bears against the housing in the working direction via a resilient member. In accordance with the invention, there is attached to the rear end of the housing a drag-sock for coupling a tube or cable, etc. to the housing, and/or an expander-cone for enlarging the bore formed by the apparatus, and/or a steering tube for steering the apparatus along a straight or preselected arcuate path.
problem: Enabling directional control, bore enlargement, and cable/coupling attachment in a confined or curved subsurface environment during ram-boring operations.
constraint: Balancing the need for modular adaptability with structural integrity and operational efficiency in a high-force, confined-space drilling environment.
mechanism: Mounting interchangeable functional modules onto a tubular structure positioned behind the primary boring element, enabling selective activation of directional control, bore enlargement, and coupling functions without interrupting the main drilling operation.
mechanism_raw: Attaching modular functional components (drag-sock, expander-cone, steering tube) to the rear of a tubular housing, allowing independent steering, bore expansion, and coupling without disrupting the primary boring action.

abstract: A method of making a covered article such as an automobile seat cushion is disclosed. The method includes the steps of forming covering members from a covering material which is impervious to a foam material formed by reacting a foamable composition. The covering members are sewed together along sew lines to form a cover. A peripheral edge of the cover is joined to an interior peripheral edge of a locating member. A plurality of small openings are formed along the sew lines of the cover in the sewing operation. These openings are sealed so that the foam material produced upon the foaming of the foamable composition cannot flow therethrough. The cover and attached locating member are positioned in a foaming mold. The locating member aligns the cover properly with respect to the foaming mold so that a vacuum can be drawn on a die surface of the mold to draw a surface of the cover into contact with the die surface. A charge of the foamable composition is placed in an interior volume of the cover and the foaming mold is closed. The foamable composition is reacted to fill the interior volume of the cover with the foam material. The foam mold is opened and the cover is removed therefrom. The locating member is removed from the cover.
problem: Precisely positioning a flexible, impermeable cover within a mold cavity during foam injection while preventing foam leakage through sewing-induced openings.
constraint: Ensuring the locating member's alignment accuracy and the sealing integrity of micro-openings under vacuum pressure without compromising the cover's structural or aesthetic properties.
mechanism: Using a detachable alignment fixture connected to the edge of a flexible barrier to position it within a cavity under negative pressure, while sealing all apertures created by fastening processes to prevent egress of injected material.
mechanism_raw: Using a removable locating member attached to the cover's periphery to align it with the mold via vacuum suction, while sealing all sew-line openings to contain foam expansion within the cover's interior volume.

abstract: A method of making a series of wire strand sizes bracketing the most frequently requested strand sizes from a limited number of predetermined wire sizes such as two or three stock wire sizes by combining the stock wires together into a predetermined pattern to make any required strand size in the series. By producing wire strands in accordance with the invention the inventory of wire normally kept on hand in a production facility is decreased and the promptness with which orders for strands may be supplied is increased.
problem: Reducing inventory complexity and lead time for producing a wide range of wire strand sizes from a minimal set of standardized stock wire diameters.
constraint: Balancing the trade-off between minimizing stock wire variety and achieving sufficient flexibility to produce all required strand sizes without compromising mechanical performance.
mechanism: Selecting a minimal set of base component sizes and arranging them in specific spatial configurations to synthesize any required output size within a target range, exploiting combinatorial combinations of standardized inputs.
mechanism_raw: Combining a limited number of predetermined stock wire sizes into specific geometric patterns (e.g., twisting, braiding) to synthesize any required strand size in a target series, leveraging combinatorial arrangements of base components.

abstract: A die closing unit for injection molding machines producing articles with embedded insert parts, where the injection molding die includes several identical transfer sections which are movable between a closing station in alignment with the other die sections and a loading station in which the insert parts are placed into the transfer section of the die.
