A vertically movable die carrier, positioned just below the closing station, receives a transfer section of the die from a transfer station, as the transfer section is shifted horizontally into the closing station in a first embodiment, or lifted vertically into the closing station in a second embodiment. In each case, the transfer section thereby becomes independent of the transfer platen which moves the transfer sections between the transfer and loading stations.
problem: Efficiently embedding insert parts into molded articles while maintaining precise alignment and enabling rapid die reconfiguration between molding cycles.
constraint: Coordinating horizontal and vertical movements of die sections and the carrier to ensure seamless transitions between stations without disrupting the molding process or insert positioning.
mechanism: Separating die segments from a transfer platform so they can move independently between a placement location and a forming location, while a vertically actuated carrier manages alignment and insertion of components during the molding cycle.
mechanism_raw: Decoupling die sections (transfer sections) from a transfer platen by moving them independently between a loading station (for insert placement) and a closing station (for molding), using a vertically movable die carrier to facilitate alignment and insertion.

abstract: Hydrogen is produced by reacting carbon monoxide with steam at a temperature of at least 200.degree.F. in the presence of a supported catalyst containing: (1) at least one alkali metal compound derived from an acid having an ionization constant below 1 .times. 10.sup..sup.-3, (2) a metallic hydrogenation-dehydrogenation material, and (3) a halogen moiety. The ratio of metal component to alkali metal compound, each calculated on the basis of the oxide thereof, ranges from 0.0001 to about 10 parts by weight per part by weight of the alkali metal compound. The halide constituent is present in amounts in excess of about 0.01 weight %, based on total catalyst. A preferred catalyst composition comprises potassium carbonate, a mixture of cobalt and molybdenum oxides and combined chlorine contained on an alumina support.
problem: Efficiently producing hydrogen from carbon monoxide and steam at elevated temperatures while maintaining catalyst stability and reactivity.
constraint: The ratio of metal to alkali metal compound (0.0001–10 parts per part) and halide content (>0.01 wt%) must be tightly controlled to balance catalytic activity, structural integrity, and resistance to deactivation.
mechanism: A multi-component catalytic system combines a stabilizing agent (from a weak acid source), a primary catalytic material, and a dispersion-enhancing moiety on a support structure. The stabilizing agent maintains structural integrity of the primary material, while the dispersion-enhancing moiety prevents agglomeration, enabling synergistic catalytic activity for a chemical conversion process.
mechanism_raw: A multi-component catalyst combines an alkali metal compound (from a weak acid), a metallic hydrogenation-dehydrogenation material, and a halogen moiety on a support. The alkali metal compound stabilizes the metallic component, while the halogen moiety enhances dispersion and prevents sintering, enabling synergistic catalytic activity for the water-gas shift reaction.

abstract: A fabric positioning holder is automatically moved by computer directed first and second stepper motors. A force generating means urges the jaws of the fabric positioning holder against the throat plate with total pressures which exceed 10 lbs. The stepper motors are, therefore, mounted such that their mass can be employed to overcome the shock forces associated with rapid movement of the holder.
problem: Achieving precise fabric positioning under high pressure while mitigating shock forces from rapid movement.
constraint: The motor mounting must balance sufficient mass to counteract shock forces without compromising positional accuracy or introducing excessive inertia during acceleration/deceleration.
mechanism: Actuation elements are mounted with sufficient mass to dynamically counteract inertial forces generated during rapid movement of a workpiece. The total applied force ensures firm contact with a reference surface, while the actuation element mass absorbs shock forces through opposing inertial resistance.
mechanism_raw: Stepper motors are mounted such that their mass acts as a counterweight to absorb shock forces generated during rapid movement of the fabric holder. The total pressure (exceeding 10 lbs) ensures firm contact with the throat plate, while the motor mass dynamically offsets inertial forces.

abstract: An automatic switching arrangement in electric fuses for projectiles which can be set on at least three different operational functions, for example proximity fuse function and inpact fuse function with two different sensitivities. The electric fuse comprises at least two separate ignition circuits each having an inhibition control terminal connected to the respective ignition circuit so that this circuit functions normally when the associated control terminal is connected to ground and is deactivated when the ground connection is interrupted. The inhibition control terminals are connected to ground through individual fusible wires. Each fusible wire is connected to an electric contact which is accessible from the outside of the projectile through individual different polarity dependent or amplitude dependent impedance elements. To set the electric fuse on a desired function, the projectiles are moved successively past a setting station comprising a voltage generator. The generator has an output terminal adapted to successively contact said contacts on the projectiles as they move past the generator. Depending on its setting, the generator delivers voltage pulses of different polarity or amplitude whereby selective melting of the fusible wires can be effected by means of the voltage generator for setting the electric fuse.
problem: Selectively configuring a projectile's electric fuse to operate in multiple modes (e.g., proximity, impact) without physical switches or manual intervention.
constraint: The impedance elements must respond exclusively to the intended polarity or amplitude to avoid unintended circuit activation, requiring precise voltage control and impedance design.
mechanism: Selective circuit activation is achieved by melting fusible connections via voltage pulses of specific electrical characteristics. The pulses break ground paths for non-selected circuits while preserving connections for the desired operational mode, enabling mode configuration without physical switches.
mechanism_raw: Fusible wires connected to impedance elements (polarity/amplitude-dependent) are selectively melted by a voltage generator. The generator delivers pulses of specific polarity or amplitude as the projectile passes by, breaking ground connections to deactivate non-selected circuits and enabling only the desired operational mode.

abstract: An earth borehole instrument having a plurality of pad members adapted to engage the borehole walls are pivotally connected through mechanical arms to a spring-loaded slidable collar on the instrument. Each of the pad assemblies has a bow spring on its inner surface which is fixedly attached to one of the mechanical arms and slidably attached to another of the mechanical arms supporting the pad. The hidden bow spring maintains the pad, serving as a wear link, in flat contact with the borehole wall. In alternative embodiments, hidden bow springs maintain one or more borehole wall-engaging wheels against the borehole wall.
problem: Maintaining consistent contact between borehole instrument pads and irregular or dynamic borehole walls during operation.
constraint: The bow spring must balance flexibility to adapt to wall variations with sufficient stiffness to maintain contact pressure, while resisting wear and fatigue over extended use.
mechanism: Flexible elements are attached to mechanical arms with one fixed and one sliding connection, creating adaptive contact mechanisms. The flexible elements bend to accommodate surface variations while maintaining consistent pressure, with concealed placement reducing direct exposure to wear.
mechanism_raw: Bow springs are fixedly attached to one mechanical arm and slidably attached to another, acting as 'wear links' that flex to accommodate wall irregularities while maintaining flat contact. The spring's hidden placement ensures continuous pressure without direct exposure to wear.

abstract: A microwatt thermoelectric generator suitable for implanting in the body. The disclosed generator utilizes a nuclear energy source. Provision is made for temporary electrical connection to the generator for testing purposes, and for ensuring that the heat generated by the nuclear source does not bypass the pile. Also disclosed is a getter which is resistant to shrinkage during sintering, and a foil configuration for controlling the radiation of heat from the nuclear source to the hot plate of the pile.
problem: Directing heat from a nuclear source through a thermoelectric pile in an implantable generator while preventing heat bypass and ensuring material stability during fabrication.
constraint: The getter must retain structural integrity during sintering, and the foil must balance thermal conductivity with radiation control to avoid overheating or energy loss.
mechanism: A thermally conductive pathway is established between a heat source and energy conversion elements using a dimensionally stable material and a radiation-controlling barrier. The stable material maintains thermal contact during fabrication, while the barrier directs heat flow through the conversion elements rather than bypassing them.
mechanism_raw: A getter resistant to shrinkage during sintering is used to maintain thermal contact, while a foil configuration between the nuclear source and hot plate controls heat radiation. This ensures heat flows through the pile rather than bypassing it, maximizing energy conversion efficiency.

abstract: An accessory instrument panel adapted to be mounted on an angular surface in a vehicle. The panel consists of a one piece molding having an upper mounting bracket that is fastened to the angular surface in the vehicle with arcuate flanges projecting downwardly from the bracket and having arcuate serrations on the outer surfaces thereof that interengage arcuate serrations on the sides of an instrument mounting panel. The mounting panel is pivotally mounted with respect to the mounting bracket so that the angular position of the mounting panel with respect to the mounting bracket and the mounting surface may be adjusted as desired.
problem: An instrument panel must be mounted on an angular vehicle surface while allowing the viewing angle of the instruments to be adjusted after installation to suit different drivers or viewing preferences.
constraint: The adjustment range is limited by the arcuate travel of the serrations, and the locking force must be strong enough to hold the panel in place under vibration yet allow manual repositioning.
mechanism: A pivotally mounted panel engages discrete angular positions on a fixed support via interlocking surface features, so that rotating the panel causes the features to slide past one another and lock into a new angular position when released, mechanically retaining the adjusted orientation without additional fasteners.
mechanism_raw: A pivotally mounted instrument panel engages arcuate serrations on a fixed bracket, so that rotating the panel causes the serrations to slide past one another and lock into a new angular position when released, mechanically retaining the adjusted orientation without additional fasteners.

abstract: A coating composition is provided which comprises (a) 10% to 90% by weight of at least one thermoplastic aromatic polysulphones preferably having a reduced viscosity of at least 0.3 (measured at 25.degree.C on a solution in dimethyl formamide containing 1 g of polymer in 100 cm.sup.3 of solution) and (b) 90% to 10% by weight of at least one fluorocarbon polymer.
problem: A coating composition must combine chemical resistance and mechanical durability in a single material system without phase separation or loss of performance.
constraint: The blend ratio must balance the competing demands of mechanical strength (favored by higher polysulphone content) and chemical resistance (favored by higher fluorocarbon content), while maintaining processability and phase stability.
mechanism: A first polymer matrix is blended with a second polymer in complementary weight ratios, so that the first polymer provides structural integrity and adhesion while the second polymer contributes chemical inertness and low surface energy, forming a co-continuous or compatible phase morphology that yields both properties simultaneously.
mechanism_raw: A thermoplastic aromatic polysulphone matrix is blended with a fluorocarbon polymer in complementary weight ratios, so that the polysulphone provides structural integrity and adhesion while the fluorocarbon contributes chemical inertness and low surface energy, forming a co-continuous or compatible phase morphology that yields both properties simultaneously.

abstract: Canteen with water color painting accessories comprising through one side wall of a canteen, a cylindrical central recess to take a cup for brush washing, on the surface of the said wall, a tray with radial disposed compartments being provided to hold tubes of water color, a cover of the tray with a central opening of the same diameter as the said central recess of the canteen and also with multi-sections serving as color mixing pallet, the washing cup being inversely screwed into the central recess to retain the cover on the tray.
problem: A portable painting kit must integrate a water container, brush-washing cup, paint storage, and a mixing palette in a compact, self-contained unit that remains assembled during transport.
constraint: The threading and cover geometry must allow the cup to be removed for use while keeping the palette cover retained, and the compartments must be sized to hold standard paint tubes without spilling during transport.
mechanism: A central recess in a container wall receives a reversely threaded cup that, when screwed in, simultaneously seals the recess and clamps a cover with a mixing surface onto a tray of compartments, so that a single rotational action both secures the washing cup and locks the palette cover in place.
mechanism_raw: A central recess in the canteen wall receives an inversely threaded cup that, when screwed in, simultaneously seals the recess and clamps a cover with a mixing palette onto a tray of paint compartments, so that a single rotational action both secures the washing cup and locks the palette cover in place.

abstract: There is disclosed a locking device for securing a conventional freight cart within a vehicle such as a truck, train or trailer and which locking device includes a hook-like clasp member which is rotatably mounted relative to the vehicle structure, and a locking member that is operative to immobilize the clasp in the locked position thereof. A plurality of locking devices may be conveniently attached to or provided integrally with a side rail of the vehicle at spaced intervals corresponding to the size of the carts to be secured. Simple and quick engagement and disengagement of the locking devices facilitate efficient loading and unloading of the carts.
problem: Freight carts must be quickly and securely fastened inside a vehicle to prevent movement during transit while allowing rapid loading and unloading.
constraint: The clasp and lock must be positioned at intervals matching cart dimensions, and the locking mechanism must be robust enough to resist vibration-induced loosening while remaining operable without tools.
mechanism: A rotatably mounted hook-like clasp is positioned over a feature and then locked in place by a separate locking member that immobilizes the clasp's rotation, so that engagement is a single swing motion and securing is a separate, positive locking action that prevents accidental release.
mechanism_raw: A rotatably mounted hook-like clasp is positioned over a cart feature and then locked in place by a separate locking member that immobilizes the clasp's rotation, so that engagement is a single swing motion and securing is a separate, positive locking action that prevents accidental release.

abstract: A water level monitor and alarm indicates when the drain valve in a toilet flush tank is improperly seated and water is not filling the flush tank as required. The monitor can also be adjusted to indicate when water is overfilling the flush tank. A hollow tube contains a float and fills with water as the tank fills, lifting the float. If water continues filling the tank after a predetermined level is reached, a portion of the float will trip a switch and indicating devices outside the tank will signal the overfill. When the flush tank empties, water is metered from the hollow tube through a variable size opening and gradually lowers the float contained therein, causing the float to descend at a slower rate than the tank water level. If the tank does not begin filling with water at a proper time to intercept the float, the float will continue to descend, and, at a predetermined level, trigger an alarm to signal that the flush tank is not filling.
problem: A flush tank must be monitored to detect both failure to fill (drain valve leak) and overfilling, using a single sensing mechanism that responds to the water level dynamics of the tank.
constraint: The variable drain opening and float travel must be calibrated so that the float's descent rate differs sufficiently from the tank's normal fill rate to distinguish between proper operation and malfunction, without false triggering during normal cycling.
mechanism: A float inside a hollow tube rises with the liquid level during filling and descends as liquid drains from the tube through a variable opening; if the float rises past the expected level it trips an overfill switch, and if it descends below the expected level before the system refills it triggers an underfill alarm, using the differential timing between system liquid level and tube liquid level to detect abnormal conditions.
mechanism_raw: A float inside a hollow tube rises with the tank water level during filling and descends as water drains from the tube through a variable opening; if the float rises past the expected level it trips an overfill switch, and if it descends below the expected level before the tank refills it triggers an underfill alarm, using the differential timing between tank water level and tube water level to detect abnormal conditions.

abstract: A heel cushion having a resilient and compressible pad formed by a pair of surfaces which diverge to a thickness from 3/4 inches to 13/4 inches, inclusive. The resilient and compressible pad is formed of flexible and compressible material having a density in the range of 2.50 to 4.50 pounds per cubic foot, inclusive, and a compression in the range of 25 to 80 RMA, inclusive.
reason: The patent describes specific material properties (density, compression range) for a heel cushion but does not explain a causal mechanism for how these properties produce the cushioning effect. It is a product specification rather than a transferable problem-solving principle.

abstract: In this application there is presented a mechanical dust collector which includes an elongated cylindrical housing at the bottom of which a dirty gas stream enters through a primary volute which directs the incoming stream to a cup shroud mounted in the housing axially thereof and generally centrally of the volute, this volute being closed at the bottom and open at the top only to the shroud, whose center is closed so that the inlet stream is given a helical upward draft which throws the solid particles out of the stream toward the interior wall of the housing. Then a secondary volute is provided at the opposite end of the housing leading tangentially from a secondary inlet, this secondary volute being closed at the top and open at the bottom only at an annular space adjacent the inner wall of the housing so that a secondary stream is provided there driving smoothly down the inner wall of the housing and causing the fine solid particles to pass downwardly and below a solid ground which extends horizontally outwardly beyond the cup shroud and which terminates short of the inner wall of the housing. The clean gas passes out the top of the housing through a central outlet.
problem: Separating solid particles from a gas stream in a dust collection system.
constraint: Balancing the helical upward draft and secondary downward flow to ensure efficient particle separation without disrupting gas flow dynamics.
mechanism: A primary flow director channels a gas stream into a helical upward draft, using centrifugal force to drive particles toward a containment boundary. A secondary flow director generates a counteracting downward flow along the boundary, transporting particles to a collection zone while permitting cleaned gas to exit through a central pathway. The opposing flow directions and geometric constraints create staged separation by balancing particle migration and gas dynamics.
mechanism_raw: A primary volute directs the gas stream into a helical upward draft, throwing particles toward the housing wall via centrifugal force. A secondary volute creates a downward flow along the wall, driving particles below a ground plate while allowing clean gas to exit through a central outlet. The opposing flow directions and geometric constraints enable staged particle separation.
residual_terms: ["centrifugal force", "helical upward draft", "secondary downward flow", "geometric constraints"]

abstract: A method for producing water gel explosives by solubilizing a nitroparaffin sensitizer having 1-3 carbon atoms, preferably nitromethane, in an aqueous oxidizer perchlorate salt solution by incorporating in the composition a nitroparaffin solubilizing agent, such as ethylene glycol, and the product so produced.
problem: Stabilizing a nitroparaffin sensitizer in an aqueous oxidizer solution to produce water gel explosives.
constraint: Selecting a solubilizing agent that effectively dissolves the sensitizer without destabilizing the oxidizer solution or compromising explosive performance.
mechanism: A compatibilizing agent is introduced into a primary solution to dissolve a hydrophobic component, enabling uniform dispersion and preventing phase separation. The agent acts as an intermediate bridge between hydrophobic and hydrophilic phases, maintaining solution stability while preserving functional performance of the active components.
mechanism_raw: A nitroparaffin solubilizing agent (e.g., ethylene glycol) is incorporated into the oxidizer solution to dissolve the sensitizer (e.g., nitromethane), enabling uniform dispersion and preventing phase separation. The solubilizing agent acts as a bridge between hydrophobic and hydrophilic components.

abstract: Production of cord fabrics by continuous, melt spun polyamide or polyester filaments which are plied and twisted and then are formed into a tire cord layer or fabric consisting essentially of planar, parallel, longitudinal cord yarns with or without weft yarn interweaving, characterized by multifilament melt spinning with a predraw at more than 3000 meters/minute, cooling, plying and twisting into cord yarns without further stretching, and then residual stretching of less than 2.4:1 at 50.degree.-130.degree. C of the filaments before or after incorporation into the web or fabric.
problem: Producing high-strength cord fabrics with consistent structural properties for tire reinforcement.
constraint: Maintaining precise temperature and stretching ratios to avoid filament degradation while achieving optimal molecular orientation and mechanical properties.
mechanism: A high-speed continuous forming process aligns polymer chains through controlled mechanical deformation and thermal conditioning. Sequential stretching at elevated temperatures reduces internal stresses while optimizing molecular orientation, ensuring uniform mechanical properties without structural degradation. Precise parameter control maintains filament integrity during subsequent processing steps.
mechanism_raw: Multifilament melt spinning at high speed (>3000 m/min) followed by controlled residual stretching (<2.4:1) at elevated temperatures (50–130°C) aligns polymer chains and reduces internal stresses. This sequential process ensures uniform tensile strength and dimensional stability without over-stretching during plying or twisting.

abstract: A clip for earrings comprising separate jaw members pivotally attached. One jaw is adapted to display a decoration and is provided with contact means adapted to contact one side of an ear lobe. The other jaw is movable towards and away from the first jaw and is provided with a generally C-shaped terminal loop portion for transverse receipt of a screw member having a contact adapted to contact the other portion of an ear lobe so that the spacing between the contacts may be altered to change the pressure applied to mount the earring. The C-shape of the loop for receiving the screw member enables the use of a shorter movable jaw which in turn enables the presentation of an overall lower profile of the resultant earring. Additionally, two-point contact between the screw member and the loop is provided so as to increase the ease in which such members may be repositioned.
problem: Creating an adjustable earring clip that balances secure attachment with comfort and low profile.
constraint: Ensuring the C-shaped loop and screw interface provide sufficient mechanical advantage for adjustment while maintaining compactness and preventing slippage under varying pressure settings.
mechanism: A curved mechanical interface on a movable component engages a threaded adjustment element, enabling transverse displacement of contact points. The dual-point interaction between the interface and adjustment element provides incremental force modulation while the curved geometry accommodates compact positioning, balancing secure attachment with low-profile operation.
mechanism_raw: A C-shaped loop on the movable jaw engages a screw member, allowing transverse adjustment of the contact points. The two-point contact between the screw and loop enables incremental pressure changes while the C-shape accommodates a shorter jaw design, reducing the earring's overall profile.

abstract: Stable sludge-free ammonium polyphosphate fertilizer solution is prepared by introducing ammonia and a blend of impure wet process phosphoric acid having a P.sub.2 O.sub.5 content of 58 to 68% and solvent extracted wet process phosphoric acid of reduced Fe.sub.2 O.sub.3, Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, MgO and free H.sub.2 O content into a reactor wherein the mixed reactants are retained for at least about 0.10 second after which the reaction product is immediately quenched and the resulting solution aged to effect precipitation and nucleation of suspended insoluble metallic phosphates and insoluble organic matter, and filtered.
problem: Producing a stable, sludge-free ammonium polyphosphate fertilizer solution by preventing unwanted precipitation and degradation during synthesis.
constraint: Balancing reaction duration and quenching timing to prevent over-reaction or incomplete precipitation, while maintaining throughput and solution stability.
mechanism: A reaction is arrested at a target state by terminating it after a controlled duration, followed by a settling phase that allows suspended impurities to aggregate and separate, enabling their removal. A blend of reactants with differing purity levels balances reaction kinetics against product stability.
mechanism_raw: Controlled reaction time (0.10 second retention) followed by immediate quenching arrests the reaction at a desired state, while aging allows suspended impurities to precipitate and nucleate, enabling subsequent filtration. The blend of impure and solvent-extracted phosphoric acid balances reactant purity and reaction kinetics.

abstract: A disc-like reflector, in addition to preventing excessive cooking of the food in a region immediately adjacent the probe housing, functions as a spring to hold the handle and reflector assembly together. The assembly remains tightly together despite different coefficients of thermal expansion of the various component parts.
problem: Maintaining structural integrity of a multi-component assembly under varying thermal expansion coefficients during operation.
constraint: Material and geometric design must simultaneously satisfy thermal reflectivity and mechanical spring requirements without failure under cyclic thermal stress.
mechanism: A compliant element provides both thermal reflection and mechanical biasing, maintaining contact pressure between components despite differential thermal expansion. This dual-function element passively compensates for dimensional changes without external adjustment.
mechanism_raw: A disc-like reflector serves a dual function: reflecting heat to prevent localized overheating and acting as a spring to mechanically bias components together. The spring-like property compensates for differential thermal expansion, ensuring tight assembly without manual adjustment.

abstract: A household flatplate ironer comprising two cooperating pressing plates, the upper one of which is lowerable onto the lower one by means of a supporting arm and a counterpoise, is provided with means for re-opening the ironer automatically after it has remained closed for a predetermined period of time, thus affording an article of laundry being ironed to cool off without suffering damage from overheating.
problem: Preventing damage to laundry from overheating during pressing while allowing safe cooling without manual intervention.
constraint: Timing must balance sufficient pressing duration with safe cooling intervals, while mechanical simplicity ensures reliability in household use.
mechanism: A timed release mechanism lowers a pressing element using a counterbalanced support, then automatically reopens after a predetermined interval. This decouples the pressing action from manual control, ensuring safe cooling occurs without user intervention.
mechanism_raw: A timed automatic reopening mechanism uses a counterpoise and supporting arm to lower the upper pressing plate, then triggers reopening after a predetermined period. This decouples the pressing action from manual control, ensuring cooling occurs without user oversight.

abstract: An apparatus for handling compacted blocks of compost, soil or the like material comprising a chamber defined by two relatively movable plates in which a batch of material is compacted at a compacting station. The chamber is moved to a depositing station at which the block is removed by firstly retracting one of the plates while the other plate holds the block, and then by retracting the other plate, leaving the block deposited on a platform. The apparatus desirably is in the form of a wheel assembly having plates defining a number of chambers radiating from the wheel axis and there is means for indexing the wheel so that each chamber moves in turn from the compacting station to the depositing station.
problem: Efficiently transferring and depositing compacted blocks of material (e.g., compost) from a compaction chamber to a platform without manual handling.
constraint: Coordination of plate retraction sequence and wheel indexing must ensure block stability during transfer while minimizing mechanical complexity and energy use.
mechanism: A rotating transfer wheel with radial chambers moves batches between a compaction station and a deposition station. Sequential retraction of retaining elements releases the batch at the destination, while indexed positioning ensures each chamber cycles through the stations.
mechanism_raw: A rotating wheel with radiating chambers moves batches from a compaction station to a depositing station. Sequential retraction of one plate (holding the block) followed by the other plate (releasing it) deposits the block precisely on a platform. Indexing ensures each chamber cycles through stations.

abstract: Disclosed is a bipolar electrolyzer having an anolyte equalizer between adjacent electrolytic cells. The electrolyte equalizer includes a conduit which passes through the cathode of one cell and through the catholyte chamber of that cell to a first aperture in the peripheral wall around the electrolyzer. The equalizer also includes a second aperture which passes through the electrolyzer peripheral wall to the anolyte chamber of the next adjacent cell in the electrolyzer. Finally, a channel carrier having an outer wall with a bearing surface and an inner wall with a bearing surface, the inner and outer walls forming a channel communicating with each of the apertures, and the bearing surfaces bearing against the peripheral wall, provides the equalizing channel between the adjacent cell.
problem: Equalizing electrolyte (anolyte) between adjacent cells in a bipolar electrolyzer to maintain uniform electrochemical performance.
constraint: Channel geometry and sealing must maintain electrolyte flow while withstanding electrochemical and mechanical stresses over prolonged operation.
mechanism: A passive fluidic network with apertures and sealing surfaces connects adjacent electrochemical cells, allowing electrolyte to flow between them and equalize levels. The sealing interface maintains fluid integrity while enabling automatic balancing without disrupting the electrochemical process.
mechanism_raw: A conduit system with apertures connects adjacent cells' catholyte and anolyte chambers via a channel carrier. The carrier's bearing surfaces seal against the peripheral wall, creating a fluid path that passively balances electrolyte levels between cells without disrupting the electrolysis process.

abstract: A cylindrical pressure chamber, designed to contain a hot expanding fluid in a nuclear reactor, has a refractory peripheral wall provided with a cooled metal lining surrounding a ceramic insulating layer which is shielded from the fluid by an inner metallic shell. The shell is separated from the ceramic layer, in the nonoperating state, by an annular clearance allowing its expansion under internal fluid pressure to pretension that shell so as to reduce the thermally induced stress to less than the yield point of the metal. The ceramic layer is anchored to the lining by radial bolts and has radial bores slidably engaged by guide studs welded to the shell. PAC FIELD OF THE INVENTION My present invention relates to a cylindrical pressure chamber designed to contain a hot expanding fluid, more specifically a pressure chamber used in a nuclear reactor. PAC BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION Conventional pressure chambers of this kind comprise a cylindrical structure forming a refractory peripheral wall, this wall being internally provided with a first metallic lining surrounding a ceramic insulating layer of low thermal conductivity. The insulating layer, in turn, is provided with a second, inner metallic lining protecting it from the confined fluid. The insulating layer may consist of concrete, for example; the tubular linings coaxially bracketing that layer are usually made of steel. In operation, the inner lining undergoes considerable heating and tends to expand radially as well as axially. Its radial distension is blocked, however, by the insulating layer whose thermal coefficient of expansion is substantially lower than that of steel. This places the inner lining under considerable stress, often exceeding its yield point and leading to an early destruction thereof, particularly if the pressure chamber is repeatedly taken out of service so that the lining undergoes recurrent cooling and heating. PAC OBJECT OF THE INVENTION The object of my present invention, therefore, is to provide an improved construction for such a pressure chamber which avoids the aforestated disadvantages and increases the service life of its peripheral wall structure. PAC SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION I realize this object, pursuant to my present invention, by replacing the conventional inner metallic lining with a metal shell or tube separated from the insulating layer, in an unoperated state of the assembly, by an annular clearance enabling radial expansion of the shell under pressure of the confined fluid as soon as operations are started. This expansion is, of course, limited by the depth of the clearance, which is sufficient to enable pretensioning of the shell in peripheral direction for reducing the thermally induced stresses therein to less than the yield point of the metal. If the outer peripheral wall surrounding the insulating layer is provided with a cooled metallic lining as in conventional nuclear reactor chambers, this lining may carry anchor means engaging that layer. On the other hand, the layer is provided with countersunk guide means bridging the intervening clearance and engaging the inner metallic shell to facilitate its radial displacement relative to the layer. The guide means may comprise a number of sleeves seated in radial bores of the layer and a corresponding number of studs slidably received in these sleeves, the studs preferably having retaining heads of larger diameter than the sleeves limitedly displaceable in extensions of the bores beyond the sleeves. The insulating layer may be axially subdivided into tiers of sectoral blocks with interlocking trapezoidal profiles in an axial plane, the profiles of adjoining tiers converging alternately toward the periphery and toward the axis. In such a case I prefer to anchor the outwardly converging blocks firmly to the outer wall, advantageously via its cooled lining as mentioned above, and to provide the inwardly converging blocks with lost-motion couplings of the aforedescribed kind linking them with the inner metallic shell to act as the aforementioned guide means. In order to facilitate thermal distension of the shell in an axial direction, the same may be subdivided into axially separated sections interconnected by expansion joints.
problem: Thermal stress in the inner metallic lining of a pressure chamber exceeds the metal's yield point due to differential thermal expansion between the steel lining and the ceramic insulating layer, causing premature failure especially under repeated thermal cycling.
constraint: The annular clearance depth must be precisely sized: sufficient to allow enough radial expansion for beneficial pretensioning, but not so large as to compromise structural integrity or permit excessive movement that could damage the shell or its guides.
mechanism: A movable inner component is separated from an outer structure by a clearance in the non-operating state. When internal pressure is applied during operation, the inner component expands within the clearance, inducing a pretensioning force in the peripheral direction. This pretension counteracts thermally induced stresses, reducing them below the material's yield point. Alignment guides enable controlled displacement while maintaining positional stability.
mechanism_raw: The inner metallic shell is separated from the ceramic insulating layer by an annular clearance in the non-operating state. When internal fluid pressure is applied during operation, the shell expands radially within the clearance, and this pressure-induced expansion pretensions the shell in the peripheral direction. This pretension counteracts the thermally induced stresses, reducing them to below the yield point of the metal. Guide studs and sleeves allow controlled radial displacement while maintaining alignment.

abstract: Air cooling means useful in conjunction with UV processors, i.e. apparatus for treating products with ultraviolet light, is adapted to impinge relatively high velocity cooling air onto the product being treated while minimizing contact of the cooling air with the lamp providing the ultraviolet light. The air cooling means comprises oppositely spaced slot-like nozzles and an exhaust channel to remove the air without contacting the ultraviolet lamp. In preferred embodiments, the nozzles direct the air angularly away from the ultraviolet lamp and toward a longitudinal exhaust channel positioned between and above the nozzles. It is preferred that the UV processor have a plurality of ultraviolet lamps with air cooling means adjacent to and following each such lamp.
problem: Need to cool a product being treated with ultraviolet light while preventing cooling air from contacting and potentially cooling or damaging the UV lamp.
constraint: The angular direction of the nozzles and the position of the exhaust channel must balance effective product cooling with minimal lamp contact and efficient air removal, requiring precise geometric coordination between nozzle angle, spacing, and exhaust placement.
mechanism: Oppositely positioned airflow outlets direct a cooling medium angularly away from a sensitive component and toward a collection channel positioned between and above the outlets. The medium impinges on the target surface for effective cooling while being deflected away from the sensitive component. The strategically placed collection channel captures and removes the medium without it contacting the sensitive component, maintaining a directed airflow path that cools the target but isolates the sensitive component.
mechanism_raw: Oppositely spaced slot-like nozzles direct high-velocity cooling air angularly away from the UV lamp and toward a longitudinal exhaust channel positioned between and above the nozzles. The air impinges on the product for effective cooling while being deflected away from the lamp. The strategically placed exhaust channel captures and removes the air without it contacting the lamp, maintaining a clean airflow path that cools the product but protects the lamp.

abstract: An improved liquid-dispensing nozzle and more specifically, an improved vapor recovery means for a nozzle comprising a vapor collector (such as a flexible bellows) surrounding a portion of the discharge spout in spaced relation thereto, one end of which is sealed to the upper portion of the nozzle spout and/or housing; and at the other end of the vapor collector, a compressible cellular plastic material such as foamed plastic associated therewith. When the discharge spout is inserted into, e.g., an automobile fillpipe, the compressible cellular plastic material forms a vapor seal with the upper end of the fillpipe whereby the vapors escaping from the fillpipe are directed into the interior chamber formed between the exterior of the discharge spout and the inside of the vapor collector thereby minimizing the escape of vapors to the atmosphere. The vapors are then removed from this chamber.
problem: Vapors escaping from a fillpipe during fuel dispensing need to be captured and removed to minimize atmospheric release of volatile substances.
constraint: The compressible material must form an effective vapor seal with fillpipes of varying diameters while allowing easy insertion and removal, requiring a balance between compliance for sealing and structural integrity for repeated use.
mechanism: A flexible collector with a compressible sealing element surrounds a discharge conduit. When the conduit is inserted into a receiving port, the compressible element deforms to form a vapor-tight interface with the port's opening. This creates a sealed volume between the exterior of the conduit and the interior of the collector, capturing escaping vapors and directing them into the collection system where they are removed through the collector.
mechanism_raw: A vapor collector (flexible bellows) surrounds the discharge spout with a compressible cellular plastic material at its open end. When the spout is inserted into the fillpipe, the compressible material deforms to form a vapor seal with the fillpipe's upper end. This creates a sealed chamber between the exterior of the spout and the interior of the vapor collector, capturing escaping vapors and directing them into the collection chamber where they are removed through the vapor collector.

abstract: The invention relates to a device for spreading or scattering granular substances and is provided with a container, a delivery tube connected thereto and a distributor which is secured to the free end of the delivery tube. According to the invention the distributor comprises a flat or substantially flat plate, which on one side is provided with a multiplicity of protrusions distributed over the plate area. The protrusions are preferably cylindrical pins which extend perpendicular to the plate.
reason: This patent describes a simple mechanical component — a flat plate with perpendicular cylindrical pins distributed over its surface — used to scatter granular material. There is no deeper causal problem-solving mechanism; the pins merely physically interact with flowing granular material through direct contact. The device is a static architecture without a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A control valve for selectively establishing connections between the spring applied parking brake in an air braked vehicle and either the parking brake air reservoir or the exhaust port of the control valve, and incorporating a lock which enables the operator to secure the control valve in the position in which the parking brakes are applied.
reason: This patent describes a conventional control valve with a mechanical lock. The valve selectively connects a parking brake to either an air reservoir or an exhaust port, and a lock secures it in the applied position. This is a standard mechanical component combining two well-known functions (valve selection and mechanical locking) without a deeper causal problem-solving mechanism that would be transferable to other fields.

abstract: An axial gap synchronous dynamoelectric machine consists essentially of a disc-shaped rotor having axially oriented permanent magnet pole bodies with faces lying in an annular surface; a stator core spaced axially from the pole faces; and a discoidal AC winding linked with the pole bodies and the core. The winding consists of a plurality of coils laid overlapping in an annular array and bonded together with a resinous material into a unitary structure having an annular disc portion containing the coil sides and inner and outer ring portions containing the coil end-heads. It is supported by the stator with its disc portion in the space between the stator core and the pole faces, and its disc portion is spaced axially from the pole faces.
problem: Efficiently arranging AC windings in a compact axial space between a rotor and stator while maintaining structural integrity and electrical performance.
constraint: Balancing the axial spacing between the rotor and stator to accommodate the winding structure while ensuring sufficient structural support and minimizing electrical losses.
mechanism: Bond overlapping conductive elements together using a structural adhesive into a rigid, annular configuration, enabling the conductive assembly to occupy a constrained radial gap between rotating and stationary components while preserving mechanical integrity and electromagnetic functionality.
mechanism_raw: Overlapping coils are bonded together with resinous material into a unitary annular disc structure, allowing the winding to occupy the limited axial space between the stator core and rotor pole faces without compromising mechanical stability or electromagnetic function.

abstract: A method and apparatus for texturing continuous filament yarn wherein the yarn is fed at a controlled rate and under controlled tension by a pair of feed rolls into a confined crimping zone against a mass of crimped yarn therein, causing the yarn to collapse longitudinally to form crimps which become part of such mass. Heat and pressure are applied to the yarn mass in the crimping zone to plastically deform the yarn and partially set the crimps. The crimped yarn mass is then fed at a controlled rate by means of toothed rolls from the crimping zone into a setting zone. Heat and pressure are applied to the yarn mass in the setting zone to fully set the crimps. The yarn mass is moved through the setting zone by an endless belt having upstanding teeth that positively engage the yarn mass. The pressure applied to the yarn mass in the setting zone is substantially sufficient only to keep the crimps closed during the final setting thereof. The crimped yarn mass is then fed from the setting zone into a cooling zone. The yarn mass is cooled in the cooling zone to a temperature below that at which the yarn undergoes any molecular structural alteration in the absence of the application of a substantial force thereto. Finally, the yarn is withdrawn at a controlled rate from the cooling zone in continuous filament form. One of the feed rolls is mounted on one end of a yoke, the other end of which has an eccentric mounting shaft, the movement of which allows the feed rolls to be perfectly aligned in skewness and parallelism. Proper alignment of the crimping and setting chamber with respect to the other elements is accomplished by providing the frame with a number of alignment shoulders against which the chamber is set upon installation.
problem: Consistently texturing continuous filament yarn by applying controlled crimping, heat-setting, and alignment during continuous processing.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment and tension across multiple processing zones to avoid yarn defects while enabling continuous operation.
mechanism: Apply sequential controlled forces (tension, heat, pressure) across distinct processing zones, combined with mechanically precise alignment of feed mechanisms using adjustable geometric constraints, to maintain material quality during continuous deformation and stabilization.
mechanism_raw: Sequential application of controlled tension, heat, and pressure in distinct crimping and setting zones, combined with mechanically precise alignment of feed rolls and chambers via an eccentric yoke and alignment shoulders to maintain yarn quality.

abstract: An accumulator for a flexible metal strip has a rotatable annular plate for supporting spiral wound turns of the strip and an outer and inner crown of rollers disposed at the outer and inner peripheries thereof. A deflecting device is disposed inside the inner crown of rollers to guide the inner turn of the strip out of the accumulator and over the spiral wound turns of the strip. The deflecting device has a series of rollers with fixed axes which are tilted with respect to the plate axis at varying angles which preferably increase directly with decreasing distance from the accumulator outlet. The intersections of the axes of the deflecting rollers with the plane are preferably on a circle having an axis displaced with respect to the plane axis and the projections of the deflecting roller axes on the plate plane preferably form a constant angle with the tangents of the circle at each of these intersections.
problem: Guiding a flexible metal strip smoothly through an accumulator with spiral-wound turns without causing stress, misalignment, or damage.
constraint: Ensuring the strip follows a smooth, stress-free path through the accumulator while accommodating varying radial positions of the spiral turns.
mechanism: Arrange a series of pivoting guide elements with fixed axes oriented at varying angles, positioned such that their axis intersections form a displaced circular path and their projections maintain a constant angular relationship with local tangents, creating a stress-minimized trajectory for the flexible strip.
mechanism_raw: A series of deflecting rollers with fixed axes tilted at varying angles, arranged such that their axis intersections form a displaced circle and their projections maintain a constant angle with tangents, creating a geometrically optimized path for the strip.

abstract: A method of continuous precipitation of insoluble solids formed by the reaction of a liquid solution and a reactant by hydrodynamic agitation of the solution and the reactant in a continuous hydrodynamic precipitation apparatus. The apparatus comprises vertically standing elongated tank means; liquid level control means for maintaining tank liquid at a predetermined level in the tank means; hydrodynamic agitator means in the tank means for receiving and agitating the solution, the reactant and recirculated tank liquid; conduit means for supplying predetermined quantities of solution and reactant to the agitator means; pressure pump means for recirculating at least a portion of the liquid under pressure from the bottom portion of the tank means to the hydrodynamic agitator means; whereby the solution, the reactant and the recirculated tank liquid are thoroughly mixed by the hydrodynamic agitator means; and means for removing at least a portion of the precipitated solids from the bottom portion of the tank means.
problem: Continuously mixing reactants and precipitating insoluble solids in a controlled, scalable hydrodynamic system.
constraint: Balancing recirculation pressure and agitation intensity to achieve uniform mixing without disrupting liquid level control or precipitate removal.
mechanism: Combine fluid-driven agitation with pressure-induced recirculation of tank contents to ensure homogenization of reactants and suspended solids, enabling continuous precipitation while maintaining liquid level control and facilitating solid removal from the system base.
mechanism_raw: Hydrodynamic agitation combined with pressure-driven recirculation of tank liquid to ensure thorough mixing of solution, reactant, and recirculated fluid, enabling continuous precipitation while maintaining liquid level and removing solids from the tank bottom.

abstract: There are prepared fuel elements for high temperature reactors from which the fuel zone can be removed from the structural graphite after the burnup of the fissile material has taken place so that the fuel element can be filled with new fuel and again placed in the reactor by having the strength of the matrix in the fuel zone sufficient for binding the embedded coated fuel particles but substantially less than the strength of the structural graphite whereby by the action of force it can be easily split up without destroying the particles.
problem: Enabling reuse of structural graphite components in high-temperature reactors after fuel burnup by removing the spent fuel zone without damaging embedded fuel particles.
constraint: Matching the matrix strength to the structural graphite strength to ensure operational integrity while enabling selective removal of the fuel zone post-burnup.
mechanism: Design a sacrificial matrix with controlled cohesive strength sufficient to retain embedded functional particles during operation but below the structural substrate strength, enabling selective mechanical separation of the matrix without compromising the substrate or damaging the particles.
mechanism_raw: Designing the fuel matrix with strength sufficient to bind coated fuel particles during operation but substantially less than the structural graphite, allowing mechanical splitting of the fuel zone without destroying the particles or the structural support.

abstract: A combined electrical receptacle type adaptor and night light providing both multiple electrical sockets and subdued illumination, comprising a wall plate in the form of a truncated pyramid with four sloped faces and a pair of conductor prongs protruding from the rear of the wall plate and adapted to be received in openings of an existing wall outlet for establishing electrical contact with the circuits thereof. The wall plate carries a pair of two-conductor sockets, the conductors of which are connected respectively to the back prongs. The plate additionally has a pair of electric lamps respectively disposed at non-adjacent faces of the pyramid, for illuminating areas on opposite sides thereof. Also carried by the wall plate is a switch connected with the lamps, providing control of their energization. In a preferred embodiment, the switch is disposed in a third face of the pyramid and enables the lamps to be selectively energized at either half or full brilliance. The arrangement is such that the adaptor can be readily installed over the existing wall outlet, to provide subdued illumination without sacrifice or loss of the duplex function of the outlet.
reason: The patent describes a product design integrating multiple components (sockets, lamps, switch) into a geometric wall plate. While it solves the problem of providing illumination without losing outlet functionality, the mechanism is a static arrangement of parts rather than a causal functional principle that can be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A method of continuously casting metal comprising feeding molten metal into an open-ended mold to form a billet, cooling the molten metal in the mold to form a solidified skin on the billet, withdrawing the billet from the mold, and applying external fluid pressure to the withdrawn portion of the billet. The external fluid pressure is sufficient to prevent breakout of molten metal through the skin, and the magnitude of the external pressure applied to one region of the billet is less than the magnitude of the external pressure applied to another region of the billet.
problem: Preventing molten metal breakout through a solidified skin during continuous casting while accommodating variable billet regions.
constraint: Balancing pressure magnitudes across regions to prevent breakout without over-pressurizing adjacent areas, which could cause deformation or failure.
mechanism: Applying spatially varying external pressure to different regions of a moving solidified structure, where the pressure magnitude in each region is adjusted to counteract localized stress or weakness in the surface layer, ensuring structural integrity during withdrawal.
mechanism_raw: Applying variable external fluid pressure to different regions of the billet, where the pressure magnitude is adjusted to counteract localized stress or weakness in the skin, ensuring structural integrity during withdrawal.

abstract: A flame resistant cloth or fabric comprising synthetic fibers prepared from resin condensation products of phenols and aldehydes which can be fiberized and cured. These fabrics may include blends of phenolic resin fibers with other fire resistant fibers such as wool, silk, polyamide fibers, polyacrylonitrile fibers, mineral and glass fibers, among others.
reason: The patent focuses on material composition (phenolic resin fibers and blends) for flame resistance. While useful, it does not describe a causal functional mechanism beyond listing materials and their properties, which are not transferable as a problem-solving principle.

abstract: Uniform heat treatment of particulate material of nonuniform gradation in a vertical heat treating vessel such as a vertical kiln or retort is affected by regulating the heat input to a heat treating zone in the vessel in response to changes in specific gravity of the mass of particles passing into the heat treating zone as detected by measurements such as differential pressure changes of combustion supporting fluid and process gas flowing into and from the heat treating zone to result in a balance between particulate mass flow and heat input and substantially uniformly heat treated particulate material. Furthermore, uniform oxygen conversion within a heat treating zone in a vertical heat treating vessel is maintained by measuring the oxygen content in the effluent gases passing from the gas outlet of the heat treating vessel and controlling the flow of air into the heat treating vessel in response to variations of the oxygen content in the effluent stream to maintain a constant oxygen content in the effluent gas stream.
problem: Achieving uniform heat treatment of particulate material with nonuniform gradation in a vertical vessel, while maintaining consistent oxygen conversion.
constraint: Maintaining a balance between particulate mass flow and heat input while keeping oxygen levels constant, which requires precise sensor integration and responsive control systems.
mechanism: Using real-time measurements of material density and reactant concentration to dynamically adjust heat input and flow rate, creating a feedback loop that balances mass flow and heat input to ensure uniform treatment of nonuniform material.
mechanism_raw: Using real-time measurements (differential pressure for specific gravity, oxygen content in effluent gases) to dynamically adjust heat input and air flow, creating a feedback loop that balances mass flow and heat input to ensure uniform treatment.
residual_terms: ["real-time measurements", "differential pressure", "specific gravity", "oxygen content", "effluent gases", "feedback loop", "mass flow", "heat input", "uniform treatment"]

abstract: In the method of this invention a substantially linear polyurethane filament is elongated a number of times its original length and heated at a temperature above its "fiber stick temperature" for a sufficient time so that the filament permanently retains that elongation and does not recover any substantial amount of the length to which it has been elongated.
problem: Creating a polyurethane filament that permanently retains elongation without recovery after stretching.
constraint: Selecting the correct temperature and duration to achieve permanent deformation without degrading the material or causing unintended structural changes.
mechanism: Heating an elongated polymer filament above a critical temperature for a sufficient duration to induce permanent molecular alignment or cross-linking, thereby locking in the deformed shape without recovery.
mechanism_raw: Heating the elongated filament above its 'fiber stick temperature' for a sufficient time to induce permanent molecular alignment or cross-linking, thereby locking in the deformed shape.

abstract: A method of and system for controlling the temperature of a continuous furnace through which steel bodies are transported at a constant speed, in which the temperature is controlled so as to keep the distance from the entry port of the furnace to a position in the furnace where the furnace temperature is substantially equal to the desired delivery temperature of a steel body to be heated at a predetermined value which is determined in accordance with the dwell time, shape and size of the steel body.
problem: Controlling the temperature profile in a continuous furnace so that steel bodies reach their desired delivery temperature despite varying dwell times, shapes, and sizes, while the bodies move at constant speed.
constraint: The transport speed of the steel bodies is held constant, so temperature control must be achieved entirely through spatial adjustment of the temperature profile rather than through speed modulation, requiring precise coordination between the body's characteristics and the furnace's thermal zones.
mechanism: Using the spatial distance from the entry point to the position where the temperature equals the desired delivery temperature as the primary control variable. This distance is dynamically set based on the physical characteristics of the body being processed, creating a feedback loop that adjusts the temperature profile along the processing path to ensure the body reaches the target temperature at the correct spatial position.
mechanism_raw: Using the spatial distance from the furnace entry port to the position where the furnace temperature equals the desired delivery temperature as the primary control variable. This distance is dynamically set based on the physical characteristics (dwell time, shape, size) of the steel body being processed, creating a feedback loop that adjusts the temperature profile along the furnace to ensure the body reaches the target temperature at the correct spatial position.

abstract: A training aid which is especially adapted to the equine body for the purpose of developing, in training, suppleness, flexion, balance and impulsion. The essential details comprise a combination upright check rein stanchion and yoke, which is disposed rearwardly adjacent the shoulders and withers of the equine and includes flexible crupper extension, stabilizing and connecting the stanchion to the equine quarters. The stanchion and yoke are adapted to secure plural check reins at one end, said check reins respectively being adapted to engage the single bit portion and the curb portion of a double or full bridle. The anchors of the stanchion are vertically adjustable for the snaffle check rein and associated normal bridle reins and the anchors of the yoke extension provide for adjustable disposition of the curb check rein, relative to the shoulders and withers of the equine. The invention is especially adapted to longeing or driving of the equine.
problem: Developing suppleness, flexion, balance, and impulsion in a horse during training by guiding proper posture and movement patterns through controlled resistance applied at specific anatomical reference points.
constraint: The system must provide enough constraint to guide proper biomechanics without restricting natural movement or causing discomfort, requiring a balance between corrective resistance and the horse's freedom of motion.
mechanism: An adjustable multi-point constraint system positioned at specific anatomical reference points that applies controlled, customizable resistance through adjustable tensioning elements engaging different parts of the restraint. The vertical adjustability of anchors allows independent tuning of resistance for different restraint types, enabling progressive training adaptation based on the subject's anatomy and training stage.
mechanism_raw: An adjustable multi-point constraint system positioned at specific anatomical reference points (behind the shoulders and withers) that applies controlled, customizable resistance through check reins engaging different parts of the bridle. The vertical adjustability of anchors allows independent tuning of resistance for different rein types (snaffle vs. curb), enabling progressive training adaptation based on the subject's anatomy and training stage.
residual_terms: ["anatomical reference points", "controlled resistance", "adjustable tensioning elements", "progressive training adaptation"]

abstract: A two stage continuous process and apparatus for crystallization of a solute or solvent from a solution comprising, first, passing the solution through a precrystallization zone with simultaneous cooling and/or rapid evaporation of the solvent resulting in the formation of small crystal nuclei, second, mixing the suspension from the precrystallization zone in a recrystallization zone with a suspension containing crystals of a much greater size than the crystal nuclei formed in the precrystallization zone wherein the crystal nuclei dissolve in the solution of the recrystallization zone and recrystallize on the larger crystals, the recrystallization step being carried out substantially adiabatic, and selectively recirculating part of the solution from the crystallization zone substantially crystal free to the precrystallization zone. Selective recirculation techniques provide a shortened residence time in the precrystallization zone without concurrently shortening the resistance time of the crystals in the crystallization zone.
problem: Controlling crystal size distribution in a continuous crystallization process by independently managing nucleation (formation of small crystal nuclei) and crystal growth (enlargement of crystals), which are naturally coupled processes that would otherwise interfere with each other.
constraint: The recirculation rate must be carefully balanced — too much recirculation shortens nucleation residence time excessively, while too little allows crystal fines to accumulate and disrupt the growth zone, requiring selective control of the crystal-free stream.
mechanism: Selective recirculation of substantially crystal-free solution from the crystallization zone back to the precrystallization zone. This maintains high nucleation conditions in the precrystallization zone without diluting or disrupting the crystal growth environment in the recrystallization zone, where small nuclei dissolve and recrystallize onto larger crystals. The recirculation decouples the two processes: nucleation rate is controlled by the precrystallization conditions, while crystal growth time is preserved independently.
mechanism_raw: Selective recirculation of substantially crystal-free solution from the crystallization zone back to the precrystallization zone. This maintains high nucleation conditions (short residence time, rapid cooling/evaporation) in the precrystallization zone without diluting or disrupting the crystal growth environment in the recrystallization zone, where small nuclei dissolve and recrystallize onto larger crystals. The recirculation decouples the two processes: nucleation rate is controlled by the precrystallization conditions, while crystal growth time is preserved independently.
residual_terms: ["crystal-free solution", "crystallization zone", "precrystallization zone", "nucleation conditions", "crystal growth environment", "nucleation rate", "crystal growth time"]

abstract: Apparatus for transferring information between an electronic display device and means for transmitting and receiving information and for supplying operating current to the electronic display device. The operating current is provided by a battery and the apparatus includes an operating circuit having an energizing means which charges the battery when the apparatus is not in use. The energizing means includes first inductive means located inside the fuel dispensing nozzle and second inductive means for coupling electromagnetically with the first inductive means located outside the nozzle. Conductors are arranged between the display device and the information transmitting and receiving means to provide safe transfer of information between them.
problem: Transferring information and supplying operating power to an electronic display device in a hazardous environment (e.g., fuel dispensing nozzle) where direct electrical connections pose safety risks, while ensuring reliable data communication.
constraint: The system must balance the efficiency and range of inductive power transfer against the safety requirements of the hazardous environment, while ensuring that the wired information path does not compromise the safety benefits of contactless power delivery.
mechanism: Combining two distinct transfer mechanisms in a single system: electromagnetic coupling for contactless power transfer to charge the battery, and physical conductors for safe, reliable information transfer between the display and the communication electronics. The electromagnetic coupling eliminates the need for direct electrical contacts for power, while the conductors ensure data integrity that electromagnetic data transfer might not provide.
mechanism_raw: Combining two distinct transfer mechanisms in a single system: inductive (electromagnetic) coupling for contactless power transfer to charge the battery (first inductive means inside the nozzle, second outside), and physical conductors for safe, reliable information transfer between the display and the communication electronics. The inductive coupling eliminates the need for direct electrical contacts for power, while the conductors ensure data integrity that inductive data transfer might not provide.

abstract: An improved racket weighting device for use with any existing racket having a shaft with a throat connected to a frame during warm-up, practice or actual play in sports such as tennis, badminton, squash or the like. The device includes a non-continuous flexible member adapted to be wrapped at least one time around the throat of the racket, supplemental weight integrally associated with the member, the hooks, Self-adhering synthetic fabric fasteners or the like for securely attaching the member to the racket. The improved racket weighting device is particularly useful for temporarily adding supplemental weight to a racket in order to develop a better shot by strengthening the critical parts of the arm.
problem: Temporarily increasing the resistance and modifying the dynamic properties of a sports racket during training to strengthen the arm and develop better shot technique, without permanently altering the racket.
constraint: The attachment must be secure enough to withstand dynamic forces during use while being easily removable and adjustable, requiring a balance between attachment strength and convenience of installation/removal.
mechanism: A non-continuous flexible member wrapped around a specific structural reference point with integrally associated supplemental weight. The flexible member and various fastening options allow the weight to be temporarily and adjustably attached at a strategic location that maximizes the moment of inertia change, providing progressive resistance training that can be quickly added or removed as needed.
mechanism_raw: A non-continuous flexible member wrapped around a specific structural reference point (the throat where the shaft meets the frame) with integrally associated supplemental weight. The flexible member and various fastening options (hooks, self-adhering synthetic fabric) allow the weight to be temporarily and adjustably attached at a strategic location that maximizes the moment of inertia change, providing progressive resistance training that can be quickly added or removed as needed.
residual_terms: ["flexible member", "structural reference point", "supplemental weight", "moment of inertia", "progressive resistance training"]

abstract: An assembly includes a face plate which is mounted to an exposed wall stud in an enclosure such as a garage. The ends of a U-shaped locking member formed from a bar of hardened steel extend through transverse openings in the face plate and encircle a portion of a bicycle frame. An eye is formed on one end of the locking member and a padlock is placed through the eye to prevent withdrawal of the locking member from the face plate. In a first embodiment of the invention the face plate is mounted to the exposed edge of the wall stud on the interior of the enclosure, and in a second embodiment the face plate is mounted to the outside surface of the wall defined by the wall stud.
reason: The patent describes a specific mechanical locking assembly with a U-shaped member and padlock. While functional, it does not present a generalizable causal mechanism beyond the product's static design. The problem (securing a bicycle) is solved by component arrangement rather than a transferable operational principle.

abstract: An arrangement for protecting the wall of a vapor generator from stresses due to thermal expansion of duct end sections and plenums associated therewith, and including support plate means which abut the plenum ends and transmit the stresses to rigid support members to be balanced by similar stresses from the opposite end of the plenum.
problem: Managing thermal expansion stresses in vapor generator walls caused by duct end sections and plenums.
constraint: Requires symmetrical stress application from opposing ends to maintain equilibrium without over-constraining the structure.
mechanism: Apply balanced opposing forces from both ends of a thermally expanding structure to external anchors, so that expansion-induced stresses are symmetrically distributed and net force on the structure is neutralized without over-constraining the system.
mechanism_raw: Opposing support plates transmit and balance thermal expansion stresses from both ends of the plenum to rigid supports, neutralizing net stress on the wall.

abstract: A protective helmet having an internal integral layer of reflective material and the method of constructing the same is disclosed. A first layer of catalyzed clear gel coat is sprayed under pressure into a helmet mold and allowed to dry. A second fog layer of clear gel coat is sprayed over the first layer to form a tacky surface upon which small double sided reflective chips can be sprinkled and brushed flat. The second gel coat is then dried thoroughly. A third backing layer of clear gel coat containing metal flakes is then sprayed over the second layer and completely dried. A layer of saturated fiber-glass mat is applied over the third layer to seal in the reflective chips and to eliminate any air pockets. Layers of fiberglass cloth are then applied over the mat and the fiberglass is completely dried. The helmet is popped from the mold, sanded and finished.
reason: The patent details a layered manufacturing process for embedding reflective materials in a helmet. The mechanism is a specific material application technique (gel coat layering with chips/flakes) rather than a causal principle applicable to other domains.

abstract: An ultrasonic transducer employs a ceramic disc which, when excited by a d-c pulse, vibrates in its planar resonant frequency mode. The sensitivity is selectively increased for the second positive half cycle of the transient oscillation of the disc and a method is described for using the selectively improved transient response to greatly increase the precision of measurement of the time interval for a transient pulse of ultrasonic energy to travel the distance between an ultrasonic transmitter and an ultrasonic receiver.
problem: Improving precision in measuring time intervals for ultrasonic pulse travel between transmitter and receiver.
constraint: Balancing sensitivity enhancement with the need to avoid signal distortion or interference in transient response.
mechanism: Selectively amplify the response of a sensing element during a specific portion of its transient oscillation cycle to enhance measurable signal characteristics for timing precision, while avoiding distortion of the overall transient response.
mechanism_raw: Selectively enhancing the sensitivity of a ceramic disc's transient oscillation during its second positive half-cycle to amplify measurable signal characteristics for timing precision.

abstract: An electric motor incorporating an internally powered DC magnet armature. The motor includes a field winding powered from a DC source but polarity controlled to produce an advancing magnetic field. Power is delivered from a DC source to the field windings by current amplifiers. The amplifier input is controlled by the signals from an optical encoder sensor. The encoder sensor detects the passage of light coded segments on an optical encoder disc rotating with the armature. The relative position of the encoder sensor determines the direction of rotation. The power output of the motor is varied by a variable pulse length generator which converts the pulses from the encoder sensors into a train of pulses of variable length.
problem: Controlling motor direction and power output in a DC motor with an internally powered armature.
constraint: Requires precise synchronization between encoder feedback and pulse modulation to maintain stable operation across varying loads.
