mechanism: Use position sensing feedback from a rotating element to modulate drive signal characteristics (polarity and pulse duration) in a closed-loop system, enabling synchronized directional and power control of the motor across varying loads.
mechanism_raw: Using an optical encoder to detect armature position and modulate field winding polarity and pulse length, creating a closed-loop feedback system for directional and power control.
residual_terms: ["closed-loop feedback", "position sensing", "polarity", "pulse duration", "directional control", "power control", "varying loads"]

abstract: An adjustable wrench having two jaws movable in relation to one another. Each jaw having one short wrenching face and an adjacent longer wrenching face. The short wrenching faces engaging diametrically opposite sides of a nut and the longer wrenching faces engaging diametrically opposite sides of a nut. A recess is cut into one jaw to accommodate the longer wrenching face of the other jaw.
problem: Achieving reliable gripping of nuts of varying sizes with a single adjustable wrench while maintaining contact on diametrically opposite sides.
constraint: The recess must be sized to accommodate the longer wrenching face without compromising the structural integrity of the jaw or reducing the effective gripping range.
mechanism: Two opposing gripping elements with complementary engagement lengths are arranged so that shorter engagement portions contact one pair of opposite sides of a workpiece while longer engagement portions contact another pair. A clearance opening in one element permits the longer engagement portion of the opposing element to pass through, enabling symmetric closure around workpieces of varying sizes while maintaining dual-point contact on diametrically opposite sides.
mechanism_raw: Two jaws with complementary short and long wrenching faces are positioned so that the short faces engage one pair of opposite nut sides and the long faces engage another pair. A recess in one jaw allows the long face of the opposing jaw to pass through, enabling the jaws to close symmetrically around nuts of different sizes while preserving dual-point contact on opposite sides.
residual_terms: ["complementary engagement lengths", "clearance opening", "dual-point contact", "diametrically opposite sides"]

abstract: A foam generating unit is adjustably mounted for longitudinal movement on a liquid sprayer having an orifice which provides a diverging liquid stream directed into the inlet of the foam generating unit. The foam generating unit includes a foam-generating section most advantageously having a pressure-reducing inlet passageway section including a preferably sharply outwardly tapering portion leading to a throat portion. Air inlet ports are provided communicating with the pressure-reducing passageway, through which ports air is drawn by the reduced pressure caused by the pressure-reducing passageway. The desired foaming action is achieved by adjusting the points of the pressure-reducing passageway section struck by the stream by moving the foam generating unit relative to the orifice.
problem: Generating consistent foam by controlling the interaction between a liquid stream and air entrainment in a foam-producing device.
constraint: The taper angle and throat geometry must balance pressure reduction and flow stability to avoid excessive turbulence or insufficient air intake, while the adjustable positioning must maintain precise alignment to ensure consistent foam quality.
mechanism: A flow channel with a diverging section transitioning to a constricted throat generates a localized pressure drop. Ambient fluid is introduced through inlet ports into the low-pressure region via the resulting pressure differential. An adjustable interface between the liquid supply and the flow channel allows the entry point of the liquid stream into the channel to be varied, thereby modulating the pressure reduction and ambient fluid entrainment to control mixture consistency.
mechanism_raw: A pressure-reducing passageway with a sharply outward-tapering section leading to a throat creates a localized low-pressure zone. Air is drawn through inlet ports into this zone via the pressure differential. The foam-generating unit is adjustably positioned relative to the liquid orifice, allowing the point where the liquid stream enters the passageway to be varied, thereby controlling the degree of pressure reduction and air entrainment to optimize foaming.

abstract: Stabilizer apparatus for use with a vehicle such as a tractor supporting load handling equipment such as a backhoe in which foot members disposed at opposite sides of a vehicle are engageable with the ground to stabilize the vehicle and are movable to an elevated position for transport by the vehicle. In the ground engaging position the foot members are positioned with their outer extremities projecting beyond some maximum predetermined width of the vehicle and in their transport position occupy a position in which the outer extremities are disposed within the confines of the maximum predetermined width of the vehicle.
problem: Stabilizing a vehicle during load-handling operations while ensuring the stabilizer components remain within transport width constraints when not in use.
constraint: The maximum predetermined width of the vehicle imposes a strict spatial boundary that the stabilizer must respect in both operational and transport configurations.
mechanism: Deployable stabilizing members are configured to extend beyond a fixed spatial envelope in an operational state and retract within that envelope in a transport state. This dual-position movement allows the stabilizer to provide lateral stability during operation while avoiding spatial conflicts during transit.
mechanism_raw: Foot members are designed to extend beyond the vehicle's maximum predetermined width in the ground-engaging position and retract within that width during transport. This dual-position movement allows the stabilizer to provide lateral stability during operation while avoiding spatial conflicts during transit.

abstract: A method for forming a closed end on a tubular knitted fabric, such as a stocking, on a circular knitting machine, in which two annular tubular layers are formed as continuations of the tubular knitted fabric at separate stages by needles operating in the same cylinder of the machine. The two layers are supported on separate circles of support members while a relative rotation through at least 180.degree. between the circles of support members is effected, and a final few rows of substantially run-proof close knitting are made before the fabric is cast-off from the needles.
problem: Creating a closed, run-proof end on a tubular knitted fabric (e.g., a stocking) without compromising structural integrity or requiring complex manual finishing.
constraint: The need to rotate the support circles relative to each other introduces a mechanical coordination requirement that must be precisely controlled to avoid misalignment or fabric damage.
mechanism: Two annular tubular layers are formed as continuations of the fabric, supported on separate circles of support members. Relative rotation of at least 180 degrees between the support circles interlocks the layers, followed by close-knitting rows to finalize the closure. This rotational alignment and mechanical interlocking ensure a secure, self-supporting end.
mechanism_raw: Two annular tubular layers are formed as continuations of the fabric, supported on separate circles of support members. Relative rotation of at least 180 degrees between the support circles interlocks the layers, followed by close-knitting rows to finalize the closure. This rotational alignment and mechanical interlocking ensure a secure, self-supporting end.

abstract: An improved leg construction is disclosed for jackup barges. The barge leg is typically of triangular construction. The members of a leg including the three verticals extending along the leg are preferably constructed of tubular members. The vertical tubular members include on the inside a rack formed of teeth to engage an elevating gear drive unit. Adjacent to the teeth, an undercut on both sides of the slot in the exterior of the tubular member is formed, locking the guide mechanism to the tubular member. This construction measurably improves the profile of the jackup leg to impinging wave action from any direction, thereby reducing the resistance of the leg to water and permitting a reduction in the leg weight and hull size.
problem: Improving the hydrodynamic profile of jackup barge legs to reduce wave resistance and structural weight while maintaining load-bearing capacity.
constraint: The leg must balance structural rigidity (via the rack and guide system) with hydrodynamic efficiency, requiring precise geometric optimization to avoid stress concentrations.
mechanism: The leg uses a triangular tubular design with internal racks for gear engagement and undercut slots on the exterior to lock guide mechanisms. The undercut geometry allows the guide to clamp securely while the tubular shape minimizes water resistance from any direction, distributing forces efficiently.
mechanism_raw: The leg uses a triangular tubular design with internal racks for gear engagement and undercut slots on the exterior to lock guide mechanisms. The undercut geometry allows the guide to clamp securely while the tubular shape minimizes water resistance from any direction, distributing forces efficiently.

abstract: A vibratory feeder, conveyor, separator, screen, or other vibratory equipment used in materials handling and related fields of the tuned two mass type in which one mass is an imbalance generator of the type using eccentric weights on a rotating shaft uses helical coil springs for coupling the imbalance generator to the trough or the like without clamping of the ends of the springs or constraining them to remain parallel to each other. Decoupling of the lateral oscillatory forces from the trough is achieved by using at least two pairs of collinear springs, one of each pair on each side of a wall member secured to the trough, and each held in compression between the wall member and a pair of vibrator plates held in fixed spaced apart relationship on each side of the wall member. The imbalance generator is secured to one of the vibrator plates so as to be well outside the spring system thus giving a low natural lateral frequency to the two mass system.
problem: Controlling lateral oscillatory forces in vibratory materials-handling equipment (e.g., feeders, screens) to decouple unwanted vibrations from the trough or support structure.
constraint: The springs must remain unconstrained and parallel to avoid introducing parasitic stiffness or damping, which could disrupt the tuned frequency response.
mechanism: A tuned two-mass system uses pairs of collinear helical coil springs on either side of a wall member, with the imbalance generator positioned outside the spring system. This configuration decouples lateral oscillations by allowing independent spring compression and maintaining a low natural lateral frequency without clamping or constraining the springs.
mechanism_raw: A tuned two-mass system uses pairs of collinear helical coil springs on either side of a wall member, with the imbalance generator positioned outside the spring system. This configuration decouples lateral oscillations by allowing independent spring compression and maintaining a low natural lateral frequency without clamping or constraining the springs.

abstract: A device for facilitating the saddling of a horse by making easier and more flexible the fastening of the strap between the rigging ring on the saddle and the cinch strap under the belly of the horse, is further improved by the addition of a novel wrench device. The rotary winch or roller which effects the tightening of the strap takes the form of a hollow cylinder and includes in its interior a novel cylindrical ratchet with an engaging pawl and a retractable, telescoping handle permanently positioned therein to provide ready and convenient access for operation, freedom from interference, and avoidance of loss or misplacement of the handle.
problem: Facilitating efficient and reliable tightening of a strap (e.g., for saddling a horse) while ensuring the tightening mechanism's handle is always accessible and not prone to loss or interference.
constraint: The handle must remain permanently positioned within the cylinder to avoid loss, yet extend smoothly without interfering with the ratchet or strap during operation.
mechanism: A hollow cylindrical winch houses a retractable, telescoping handle within its interior, connected to a ratchet mechanism. The handle extends for use and retracts into the cylinder when not in operation, eliminating the need for external storage or manual retrieval.
mechanism_raw: A hollow cylindrical winch houses a retractable, telescoping handle within its interior, connected to a ratchet mechanism. The handle extends for use and retracts into the cylinder when not in operation, eliminating the need for external storage or manual retrieval.

abstract: A mounting member for an extractor hold down apparatus permits the extractor to exert both extraction and insertion forces at different angles to, for example, an electronic unit on an avionic rack. The mounting member is provided with a pair of elongated slots that accommodate a cross bar and retaining disks mounted on the power shaft of the extractor. The slots provide an angle range of at least 18.degree. plus or minus 15.degree..
problem: An extractor mechanism needs to apply both extraction and insertion forces at different angles to an electronic unit mounted on an avionic rack, where a fixed-angle coupling would limit operational flexibility.
constraint: The angular range is mechanically limited to at least 18 degrees plus or minus 15 degrees, which balances the need for angular flexibility against the structural integrity and precision of the force transmission path through the slot and cross bar interface.
mechanism: A mechanical interface uses an elongated slot with a cross bar and retaining elements to create angular compliance between a rotating drive shaft and a target unit. The slot geometry constrains the cross bar to slide within a defined angular range, so rotational motion of the drive shaft translates into linear extraction or insertion force at whatever angle the slot permits, automatically accommodating angular misalignment between the applied force direction and the target unit.
mechanism_raw: Elongated slots in a mounting member accommodate a cross bar and retaining disks on the extractor's power shaft, creating a mechanical interface that allows angular compliance. The slot geometry constrains the cross bar to slide within a defined angular range, so rotational motion of the power shaft translates into linear extraction/insertion force at whatever angle the slot permits, automatically accommodating angular misalignment between the applied force direction and the target unit.

abstract: A high-strength parallel yarn rope comprises a series of multi-filament rope yarns which are bounded together in parallel relation along their lengths by a binder distributed only on the surfaces of the yarns to form a flexible rope core. The core is surrounded by a braided jacket, and a flexible layer of water-impervious material adhesively and mechanically bonds the core to the jacket. A method is also disclosed for manufacturing the rope.
problem: Creating a rope that simultaneously achieves high tensile strength, flexibility, and water impermeability, where traditional binding methods that saturate the entire yarn bundle would stiffen the rope and full encapsulation would add excessive bulk.
constraint: The surface-only binder distribution preserves flexibility but limits the total binding force, while the water-impervious layer must provide both adhesive and mechanical attachment without adding stiffness that would reduce the rope's overall flexibility.
mechanism: Multi-filament yarns are bound together in parallel using a binder applied only to their outer surfaces, forming a flexible core that retains inter-filament mobility. A braided jacket surrounds this core, and a separate flexible water-impervious layer is bonded to both the core and jacket through dual attachment—adhesive bonding for sealing and mechanical interlocking for structural integrity—creating a composite structure where each layer contributes a distinct function without compromising the others.
mechanism_raw: Multi-filament yarns are bound together in parallel using a binder applied only to their outer surfaces, forming a flexible core that retains inter-filament mobility. A braided jacket then surrounds this core, and a separate flexible water-impervious layer is bonded to both the core and jacket through dual adhesion—adhesive bonding for sealing and mechanical interlocking for structural integrity—creating a composite structure where each layer contributes a distinct function without compromising the others.

abstract: Multi-purpose clamp comprised of tubular clamp elements which contain releaseably secured clamping devices built into its walls, to hold inserts in place. The inserts being tubular and containing releaseably secured clamping devices, housed within and forming part of the tubular clamp elements. These inserts containing jaws at their extremities to exert biting or holding force at the point where they meet or come together.
problem: Need a reconfigurable clamping system that can hold inserts in place with biting force at the point of contact, where a single fixed clamp would not accommodate different insert sizes or positions.
constraint: The releaseable securing of clamping devices enables reconfiguration but limits the maximum force that can be transmitted through the interface, and the nested tubular design must balance the number of clamping stages against the overall compactness of the assembly.
mechanism: Nested tubular clamp elements contain releaseably secured clamping devices built into their walls, with tubular inserts that also house their own clamping devices and feature jaws at their extremities. When the tubular elements and inserts are assembled, the jaws meet and exert biting force at the contact point, and the releaseable securing mechanism allows the clamping devices to be repositioned or replaced, enabling the same clamp body to adapt to different insert configurations.
mechanism_raw: Nested tubular clamp elements contain releaseably secured clamping devices built into their walls, with tubular inserts that also house their own clamping devices and feature jaws at their extremities. When the tubular elements and inserts are assembled, the jaws meet and exert biting force at the contact point, and the releaseable securing mechanism allows the clamping devices to be repositioned or replaced, enabling the same clamp body to adapt to different insert configurations.

abstract: A roughing machine for roughing the margin of an upper of a shoe assembly comprised of a last having an insole on its bottom and the upper mounted thereon with the upper margin lying against and being secured to the insole periphery. The machine is so constructed as to enable a roughing tool to engage the upper margin a relatively great or a relatively small distance inwardly of the periphery of the shoe assembly bottom during movement of the upper margin past the roughing tool and the machine incorporates an automatically operable mechanism for placing the roughing tool in one or the other of these positions.
problem: Roughing the margin of a shoe upper at a selectable distance from the periphery during manufacturing, where a fixed-position tool would only work for one specific margin width and manual adjustment would slow production.
constraint: The tool position is binary (two discrete distances) rather than continuously variable, and the automatic switching mechanism must operate reliably during continuous movement of the workpiece, limiting the system to pre-set positions rather than arbitrary adjustment.
mechanism: A working tool is automatically positioned at one of two selectable distances from a moving workpiece edge as the workpiece passes the tool. An automatically operable mechanism shifts the tool between positions during the workpiece's movement, so the tool engages the workpiece at either a relatively great or relatively small distance inwardly of the edge, with the switching occurring without stopping the process.
mechanism_raw: A roughing tool is automatically positioned at one of two selectable distances from the periphery as the upper margin moves past the tool. An automatically operable mechanism shifts the tool between positions, so the tool engages the upper margin at either a relatively great or relatively small distance inwardly of the periphery, with the switching occurring during the workpiece's movement past the tool without stopping the process.

abstract: The pressure measurement system utilizes two bourdon tubes with an active side connected to a test specimen and a reference side connected to an outside source. The tubes are attached to a single extensometer measuring relative displacement. The active side deflects when gases vent a specimen failure. The reference side is independently pressurized to a test pressure and provides a zero reference while providing a pressure calibration reference for the active side. The deflection noted by the active side at specimen failure is duplicated on the reference side by venting until an appropriate magnitude of pressure versus deflection is determined. In this way the pressure which existed inside the specimen prior to failure can be determined.
problem: Determining the pressure that existed inside a test specimen immediately prior to its failure, where direct measurement inside the specimen is not possible and the failure event destroys the measurement opportunity.
constraint: A single extensometer measures both tubes, requiring the reference tube to be calibrated against the active side and the matching process to be performed by venting the reference tube until deflections align, which means the measurement is retrospective rather than real-time and depends on the mechanical similarity of the two tubes.
mechanism: Two pressure-responsive elements—an active side connected to the specimen and a reference side connected to an external source—are attached to a single displacement sensor that measures their relative movement. When the specimen fails and gases vent, the active element deflects. The reference element is independently pressurized to a known test pressure to provide a zero and calibration reference. The deflection recorded by the active element at failure is then duplicated on the reference side by adjusting the reference until its deflection matches the active element's failure deflection, at which point the known pressure of the reference element reveals the pre-failure pressure of the specimen.
mechanism_raw: Two bourdon tubes—an active side connected to the specimen and a reference side connected to an external source—are attached to a single extensometer that measures their relative displacement. When the specimen fails and gases vent, the active tube deflects. The reference tube is independently pressurized to a known test pressure to provide a zero and calibration reference. The deflection recorded by the active tube at failure is then duplicated on the reference side by venting the reference until the reference tube's deflection matches the active tube's failure deflection, at which point the known pressure of the reference tube reveals the pre-failure pressure of the specimen.

abstract: Solar energy conversion is provided by a structure formed of a plurality of photovoltaic sources. An electrolyte wets the sources. Upon exposure to light the photovoltaic sources cause a current to flow in the electrolyte producing an electrochemical reaction. The products of this reaction may then be collected and stored. In a preferred embodiment the electrolyte is an aqueous solution of hydrogen iodide, and the hydrogen produced by the electrochemical reaction may be stored, burned as a fuel or used in a fuel cell to produce electrical energy.
problem: Converting solar energy into a storable chemical form for later use.
constraint: The electrolyte must remain chemically stable and conductive under prolonged light exposure while enabling efficient charge transfer to sustain the reaction without degradation.
mechanism: A light-responsive medium converts photonic energy into chemical energy by enabling sustained charge transfer reactions, where the medium facilitates redox processes to store energy in reaction products.
mechanism_raw: Photovoltaic sources generate a current in an electrolyte upon light exposure, driving an electrochemical reaction whose products (e.g., hydrogen) are collected and stored. The electrolyte acts as a medium to translate photonic energy into chemical energy via sustained redox reactions.

abstract: 1. A solid composite type propellant composition comprising as a base propellant an oxidizer, a metallic fuel and fuel binder and between 0.1 and 10% by weight of a ferrocene plasticizer that is selected from the group consisting of mono- and di-substituted ferrocenes wherein the substituents are selected from the group consisting of --R, --COR, --CO.sub.2 R, --CH(OH)R, and --CH(R'CO.sub.2)R wherein R and R' are selected from the group consisting of alkyl, cycloalkyl, alkenyl and cycloalkenyl radicals, the carbon chains of which may be interrupted by oxygen.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical composition (ferrocene plasticizer in a propellant) rather than a causal functional mechanism. The mechanism is limited to material selection, not a process or system that solves a problem through a generalizable principle.

abstract: A foamed or aerated water gel explosive composition devoid of any self-explosive sensitizer is provided which is sensitive to detonation in charge diameters greater than 5.1 cm. The explosive composition retains sensitivity for long periods. The migration or collapse of air or gas entrained in the composition is substantially prevented by incorporating a blend of a foaming surfactant and a stabilizing surfactant in chosen proportions.
problem: Maintaining sensitivity and structural integrity of a foamed explosive composition over time without relying on self-explosive sensitizers.
constraint: The surfactant blend must be proportioned to balance bubble formation and stability without compromising the explosive's detonation properties.
mechanism: A dual-component agent system controls bubble formation and structural reinforcement, where one component generates and maintains bubbles while another stabilizes their walls to preserve sensitivity and integrity.
mechanism_raw: A blend of foaming and stabilizing surfactants is incorporated to control bubble morphology, preventing gas migration or collapse. The foaming surfactant creates and maintains bubbles, while the stabilizing surfactant reinforces bubble walls to preserve sensitivity.

abstract: A reproducible mounting for use in conjunction with prealigned optional assemblies. The mounting comprises a base member and a mating member attached thereto by fastening means cooperating with first, second and third noncollinerly disposed mounting holes whereby all six degrees of freedom between the base and the mating member are eliminating.
problem: Achieving precise, repeatable alignment of components while eliminating all six degrees of freedom (translation and rotation) in a mechanical mounting system.
constraint: The mounting holes must be positioned noncollinearly to avoid overconstraint, which could introduce stress or misalignment.
mechanism: A geometric constraint system uses three noncollinear contact points to eliminate all translational and rotational degrees of freedom, enforcing a single stable positional configuration through deterministic spatial relationships.
mechanism_raw: Three noncollinear mounting holes on a base and mating member enforce kinematic constraints. The geometric arrangement of three points inherently limits movement to a single stable configuration, ensuring deterministic positioning.

abstract: A method of simulating small spherical voids in metal is provided. The method entails drilling or etching a hemispherical depression of the desired diameter in each of two sections of metal, the sections being flat plates or different diameter cylinders. A carbon bead is placed in one of the hemispherical voids and is used as a guide to align the second hemispherical void with that in the other plate. The plates are then bonded together with epoxy, tape or similar material and the two aligned hemispheres form a sphere within the material; thus a void of a known size has been created. This type of void can be used to simulate a pore in the development of radiographic techniques of actual voids (porosity) in welds and serve as a radiographic standard.
problem: Creating a precisely sized, reproducible spherical void within a material to simulate porosity for radiographic testing standards.
constraint: The carbon bead must be sized to fit both hemispheres precisely, and the bonding material must maintain structural integrity without distorting the void geometry.
mechanism: A precision alignment method forms a controlled void by joining two complementary concave surfaces using a sizing guide, ensuring geometric conformity to create a reproducible spherical cavity.
mechanism_raw: Two hemispherical depressions are drilled into separate material sections, aligned using a carbon bead guide, and bonded together. The alignment ensures the hemispheres form a perfect sphere, creating a controlled void with known dimensions.

abstract: A high precision timepiece pace measuring device wherein a first mask circuit inhibits the entry of a first signal of the timepiece so as to initiate a measurement of the pace of the timepiece from a second signal of the timepiece, while a second mask circuit inhibits the entry of timepiece signals, external noises and the like during a period from a time at the initiation of the measurement to a time immediately before the termination thereof, wherein a counter circuit which receives the timepiece signals as its inputs is connected to a nine's complement presetting circuit, to a carry detecting circuit and to normal and nine's complement circuits which are respectively selected in accordance with the presence and absence of a carry in the counter circuit, and wherein output pulses of the counter circuit are fed back via a counter matrix circuit so as to set the mask period of the second mask circuit.
problem: Accurately measuring the pace of a timepiece while filtering out external noise and unwanted signals during the measurement period.
constraint: Balancing noise suppression during measurement with the need to capture valid timepiece signals, while maintaining counter accuracy through nine's complement and carry detection logic.
mechanism: A feedback loop dynamically adjusts a noise-filtering window by monitoring real-time output from a counting mechanism. This ensures measurement initiation and termination align with valid signal periods while suppressing external interference through adaptive masking.
mechanism_raw: A feedback loop adjusts the mask period of a second mask circuit by feeding back output pulses from a counter circuit via a counter matrix. This dynamically tunes the noise-filtering window based on real-time counter behavior, ensuring precise measurement initiation and termination.

abstract: A cooling box for a metallurgical furnace comprising an independent and outermost first cooling water channel turning back in the front end part of the cooling box to form itself into a loop, a second cooling water channel turning back to form itself into a loop along the inner side of said first cooling water channel and a third cooling water channel turning back along the inner side of the second cooling water channel and communicating with the second cooling water channel at one end thereof.
problem: Efficiently dissipating heat in a high-temperature metallurgical furnace while maintaining structural integrity of the cooling system.
constraint: Ensuring structural stability of the cooling box under extreme thermal stress while optimizing heat transfer efficiency through channel geometry and flow communication.
mechanism: A layered thermal management system uses nested, concentric flow channels arranged in a cascading configuration. Each inner channel communicates with its outer neighbor at one end, creating sequential heat transfer stages that maximize dissipation while maintaining structural integrity under thermal stress.
mechanism_raw: Nested, concentric cooling water channels arranged in a layered configuration, where each inner channel communicates with its outer neighbor at one end. This creates a cascading heat transfer path that maximizes thermal dissipation through sequential cooling stages.

abstract: An injection molded safety pin particularly for use as a laundry net pin or for attachment of hunting tag holders to jackets and the like, said pin including a free shaft having a pointed first end with a groove which is transverse the shaft and adjacent the pointed end, a fixed shaft integrally connected at one end by a U-shaped portion to the second end of the free shaft, a head assembly integral with the second end of the fixed shaft and having a slot which is narrower than the free shaft to receive said first free end of the free shaft with a protrusion extending into the slot to engage the transverse groove on the shaft, said head assembly may include a spring biased clip or a wall which prevents the free shaft from deflecting out of the slot.
reason: The mechanism is a specific mechanical interlock design (groove-and-protrusion fastening) with no generalizable causal principle beyond standard mechanical fastening. The problem and solution are tightly bound to the physical structure of the pin.

abstract: Apparatus for handling cartons of paperboard and the like has at least two diametrically opposite holders, means for moving the holders in a circular path and means for moving same into and out of unfolded cartons to fix and carry the cartons. The diametrically opposed holders are arranged to be controlled for movement in opposite directions by a common control device.
problem: Handling and carrying unfolded cartons in a manufacturing process without damaging them, while ensuring synchronized movement of gripping elements.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between opposing holders to prevent uneven forces that could deform cartons, while accommodating variable carton sizes and shapes.
mechanism: Opposing gripping elements are mechanically linked to move in coordinated, diametrically opposed directions along a circular path. This ensures balanced force application and synchronized insertion/removal actions, preventing deformation of handled objects through equalized gripping pressure.
mechanism_raw: Diametrically opposed holders are controlled by a common device to move in opposite directions along a circular path. This opposing motion ensures balanced gripping forces and coordinated insertion/removal from cartons, enabling stable handling during transport.

abstract: A sufficient amount of alumina is initially digested in aqueous hydrochloric or hydrofluoric acid to provide from about 5 to about 25 wt. % of the aluminum content of the desired alumina sol, and a finely divided aluminum is subsequently digested therein to provide the remaining required amount of alumina. The method enables the digestion reaction to be effected at an increased rate, and affords a sol of improved homogeniety and reproducibility.
problem: Accelerating the digestion of alumina in acid to produce a homogeneous sol with consistent properties.
constraint: Optimizing the ratio of pre-digested alumina to finely divided aluminum to balance reaction rate enhancement with sol homogeneity and reproducibility.
mechanism: A staged reaction process first creates a reactive medium by partially dissolving a base material, then introduces a secondary reactant to accelerate completion. The pre-conditioned medium enhances dissolution kinetics of the remaining base material, ensuring homogeneity and reproducibility.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage digestion process: first dissolving a portion of alumina in acid to create a reactive medium, then introducing finely divided aluminum to rapidly complete the reaction. The staged addition leverages the pre-existing solution to accelerate dissolution of the remaining alumina.

abstract: This specification is directed to a method of producing oil from an oil-containing subterranean formation by a caustic waterflood. Oil containing carboxylic acids is passed through an ion-exchange resin to selectively remove the carboxylic acids therefrom. The removed carboxylic acids are injected into the formation in conjunction with the caustic waterflood to enhance the production of oil from the formation.
problem: Enhancing oil recovery from subterranean formations by improving the effectiveness of caustic waterfloods.
constraint: Balancing the selective removal of acids without depleting critical components of the oil, while ensuring the re-injected acids do not cause formation plugging or chemical incompatibility.
mechanism: A selective removal medium captures specific molecular species from a fluid stream, which are then reintroduced into a secondary fluid flow to alter interfacial properties and enhance mobilization of trapped material within a porous medium.
mechanism_raw: Selective removal of carboxylic acids from oil via ion-exchange resin, followed by re-injection of the removed acids into the formation alongside the caustic waterflood to reduce interfacial tension and mobilize trapped oil.

abstract: An improved blade clamping mechanism for a motor grader blade which has blade support rails carried in pivoted blade support means for lateral sliding movement, and in which confining surfaces in the blade support means restrict both vertical and fore-and-aft movement of the rails in the support means. A clamp lever is pivoted on the circle of the motor grader and has a clamp arm which can be turned in a vertical plane against the bottom of the lower support rail with a high mechanical advantage to force the rail against an overlying confining surface; and a single action hydraulic cylinder and piston unit which turns the lever simultaneously presses a clamp shoe against the rear of the upper support rail. The clamps are normally locked by hydraulic pressure on the piston, and released by moving a manually controlled valve to a drain position so that a return spring acting on the clamp shoe can move the shoe and the lever to a release position.
problem: Securing a motor grader blade in a fixed position with high mechanical advantage while enabling rapid release.
constraint: Achieving synchronized clamping of multiple rails with a single actuator while maintaining sufficient mechanical advantage for both clamping and release operations.
mechanism: A single actuation source drives coordinated mechanical displacement across multiple contact points, using pressurized force for locking and a resilient element for release, enabling synchronized clamping with variable mechanical advantage.
mechanism_raw: A single hydraulic cylinder simultaneously actuates a lever to clamp the lower rail against a confining surface and a clamp shoe to press the upper rail, using hydraulic pressure for locking and a return spring for release.

abstract: A toy which expels a liquid from the wrist area of a glove by applying pressure to the palm portion of the glove has a compressible bulb disposed at the palm portion of the glove and connected to a tube which extends into an aperture provided in a gauntlet provided on the glove. The tube terminates in a nozzle directed toward the palm portion of the glove so as to spray the liquid onto the hand of a person grasping the user's glove hand, or toward an object upon the user's making a fist with the glove hand. A valve connected to the compressible bulb is provided in the palm portion of the glove for permitting refilling of the bulb with the medium to be sprayed.
problem: Creating a wearable device that expels liquid on demand through user-initiated pressure.
constraint: Ensuring the nozzle direction and valve design allow both spraying during use and refilling without leakage or unintended discharge.
mechanism: A compressible chamber integrated into a wearable interface connects to a directional outlet; manual compression of the chamber forces contained fluid through the outlet toward a target surface.
mechanism_raw: A compressible bulb in the palm area is connected to a tube terminating in a nozzle; squeezing the palm compresses the bulb, forcing liquid through the nozzle toward the hand or target object.

abstract: Wind motor comprising one or more sets of rotors, arranged each to project outwardly with respect to the adjacent one in the direction of the wind, such that only the useful part of the subsequent rotor is exposed to the wind flow. The vertical axis rotors are, in aligned arrangement on oblique V-like extending radial arms, pivotally mounted to a common and fixed vertical shaft for self-orientation in the direction of the wind and for angular self-adjustment by bringing the "V" arranged arms closer to each other.
problem: Optimizing wind energy capture by dynamically aligning rotors with wind direction and adjusting their angular exposure.
constraint: Maintaining structural stability and rotational efficiency while allowing continuous self-adjustment to varying wind directions and speeds.
mechanism: Self-aligning rotational elements mounted on articulated support arms dynamically adjust their angular orientation relative to a flow direction, with arm geometry modulating exposure of subsequent elements to optimize energy capture.
mechanism_raw: Vertical axis rotors are mounted on oblique V-shaped radial arms that pivotally self-orient into the wind, with the arms adjusting their angle by moving closer together to expose only the useful portion of subsequent rotors.

abstract: To maintain the cutting wire of a wire saw properly bowed with a substantially constant cutting pressure on the stone, an automatic power controller is utilized consisting of a meter with relay contacts. The meter measures the current flowing to the main power motor for the wire saw which drives the wire. When this current falls below a selected value, the meter through the relay means turns on a slow speed wire saw dolly feed down motor which down feeds the wire into the stone. This increases wire cutting pressure and restores wire bow to the optimum degree for efficient and rapid cutting. The increase in wire pressure and resulting drag increases current consumption to the main wire saw drive motor. When this current is increased to its original value, the meter turns off the slow speed down feed motor for the dolly.
problem: Maintaining consistent cutting pressure in a wire saw to ensure efficient and uniform cutting of stone.
constraint: Balancing response speed and precision to avoid over-correction or delayed adjustments that could damage the wire or reduce cutting efficiency.
mechanism: A closed-loop control system monitors a proxy variable representing operational force, automatically adjusting mechanical positioning to maintain a target threshold and prevent over-correction or delayed response.
mechanism_raw: A feedback loop monitors motor current (as a proxy for cutting pressure); when current drops, a secondary motor automatically down-feeds the wire to increase pressure, and stops when current returns to the target level.

abstract: An attachment for ground-engaging pads of stabilizer arms of material-handling apparatus. The pad has a ground-engaging plate and at least one bracket normal with respect to the ground-engaging plate which is welded or otherwise rigidly secured thereto. The bracket (or a pair of brackets) is pivotally connected to the free end of the stabilizer arm in a conventional manner. The ground-engaging plate has at least one slit. A smooth-terrain engaging attachment (preferably rubber-faced) is adapted to be mounted on the pad by having a portion projecting through said slit in the plate and having a bar, spaced from said slit and rigidly secured to the attachment which is adapted to be slid over the ground-engaging plate. A pin is removably mounted in the projecting portion of the attachment for holding the attachment in operating position on the pad, so that when the pin is removed, the attachment can be easily slid out of and dismounted from the ground-engaging pad.
problem: Quickly and securely attaching/removing a ground-engaging pad to a stabilizer arm without tools or complex operations.
constraint: The attachment must remain rigidly secured during operation but allow rapid manual removal without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A sliding engagement between a movable component and a base structure, secured by a removable fastener that allows axial insertion and retention until manually released, enabling rapid attachment and detachment without external tools.
mechanism_raw: A slotted plate with a removable pin allows a rubber-faced attachment to slide onto the plate via a projecting portion through the slit, while a bar on the attachment slides over the plate. Removing the pin releases the attachment for easy dismounting.

abstract: A removable washer attachment providing a closed system for use in washing containers such as chemical or pesticide drums including an insert secured to a formed opening in one wall of the container. The insert has a first portion extending exteriorly of the container, a second portion depending interiorly of the container, and a bore extending axially therethrough for receiving a suction tube. The insert is fluid-tight sealingly engaged with the formed opening. Another seal is provided between the bore and a suction tube inserted therein. When it is desired to wash material from a container, washing fluid is admitted into the bore and is channeled through passages into curved notches disposed in a lower segment of the interiorly depending portion. The washing fluid is sprayed upwardly and contacts the inside top and side walls of the container or a disposable bag if the container utilizes such. Residue material is washed downwardly to the bottom of the container where it is removed through the suction tube.
problem: Washing residue from sealed containers (e.g., chemical drums) without opening the container or causing spillage.
constraint: The system must maintain a leak-proof seal during washing while enabling efficient fluid flow and residue removal.
mechanism: A sealed interface with internal fluid channels directs pressurized washing medium through geometric flow paths to impinge on interior surfaces, while a separate extraction conduit removes dislodged residue, maintaining system integrity through complementary sealing elements.
mechanism_raw: A fluid-tight insert with internal passages directs washing fluid upward through curved notches to spray the container interior, while a suction tube removes residue. Seals at the insert and tube maintain a closed system.

abstract: A six-wheel railway motor truck for swivelly supporting a locomotive body is connected to the same for the effective transmission thereto of draft and braking forces at a level at or near that of the rail whereby the vertical moment arm through which traction forces might act to tip the truck frame and thereby cause load transference from axle to axle is minimized, with corresponding minimization of such load transference. The truck comprises a rigid frame resiliently supported on the three axles, a body support bolster comprising longitudinally spaced transversely extending end members and transversely spaced longitudinally extending side members defining an open central portion above the middle axle for providing unobstructed access to the middle axle motor and sufficient vertical clearance therefor while maintaining the bolster and overall truck height relatively low. One of the bolster transverse members is supported through a swivel center plate at its center on the longitudinal center line of the truck and the other bolster transverse member is supported near its ends on the sides of the truck frame to provide a stable three point support for the bolster and the locomotive body is carried on springs mounted respectively on the end portions of the respective bolster transverse members. For transmitting longitudinal forces from the truck to the supported body substantially at rail level, the bolster is connected to the vehicle body at each side by a pair of longitudinally upwardly and outwardly inclined links arranged so that their axial projections intersect at track level.
problem: Minimizing load transfer between axles and tipping moments in a railway truck during traction or braking forces.
constraint: The design must balance structural stability, low overall height, and unobstructed access to the middle axle motor.
mechanism: A multi-point support system with angled force-transmitting elements arranged so their load paths converge at a reference plane, reducing moment arms by aligning force application with the plane of reaction forces.
mechanism_raw: A three-point bolster support with links inclined so their axial projections intersect at rail level transmits longitudinal forces at the rail's elevation, reducing vertical moment arms and load redistribution.

abstract: An improved engine for burning a lean air-fuel mixture includes a main combustion chamber into which the air-fuel mixture is introduced and an auxiliary combustion chamber wherein the air-fuel mixture is initially ignited. A spark plug in the auxiliary combustion chamber has central and side electrodes which define a spark gap. A corona discharge is established in an electrostatic field between the central electrode and a field electrode. The ions in the corona discharge collect on fuel particles in the air-fuel mixture so that these particles are electrically charged and deposited on the field electrode, the walls of the auxiliary combustion chamber, and the side electrode. The fuel particles which come toward the central electrode are electrostatically atomized by the corona discharge and accelerated away. As this is occurring, the electrically charged air-fuel mixture accelerates away from the entrance to the auxiliary combustion chamber with a resulting increase in flow rate and turbulence in the auxiliary combustion chamber. Upon establishment of an electrical arc across the spark gap, the rich air-fuel mixture in the auxiliary combustion chamber is ignited and the resultant flame is directed by the entrance passageway or nozzle into the main chamber in such a manner as to insure ignition and complete burning of the relatively lean mixture in the main chamber during a comparatively longer while.
problem: Efficiently igniting and combusting a lean air-fuel mixture in an engine to ensure complete burning.
constraint: The system must generate sufficient turbulence and charge density to ignite the lean mixture without excessive energy input or pre-ignition.
mechanism: An electrostatic charging stage increases fuel particle dispersion and kinetic energy to enhance mixture turbulence, followed by an electrical discharge initiation stage that triggers combustion in a controlled region to propagate flame into the primary combustion volume.
mechanism_raw: Corona discharge charges fuel particles, electrostatically atomizing and accelerating them to increase turbulence. The charged mixture is ignited via a spark gap, directing flame into the main chamber for sustained combustion.

abstract: An appointment calendar comprises a ring-type binder, at least one page having a pocket and a flap which partially slips into the pocket, and an insertion having two leaves, one of the leaves being received in the pocket to hold the insertion in place in the calendar and the other leaf, which contains printed promotional, decorative or informative matter, overlying the pocket so that the printed matter is visible. The pocket is closed along all margins except along an opening adjacent the edge of the page that is engaged in the binder. The binder rings engage the flap and a part of the page which is non-pocketed but do not engage the pocket or the insertion.
reason: The mechanism is a static product design feature specific to calendars, relying on physical pocket/flap geometry rather than a generalizable causal principle for solving a broader problem.

abstract: An ultrasonic track testing carriage for movement along rails in operative relationship with a test vehicle is disclosed and includes a pair of wheel frames each having guide means for following the gauge side of the rail and ultrasonic sensing means mounted in working relationship with a portion of the rail for detecting changes in the rail and the position of the sensing means relative to the rail with a main frame disposed between the wheel frames and adapted to be coupled to the test vehicle for movement therewith. Interconnecting means extends between the main frame and each of the wheel frames so as to permit each wheel frame independent freedom of motion relative to the main frame in a plane substantially perpendicular to the gauge side of the rail while simultaneously maintaining parallelism between the wheel frames. The ultrasonic sensing means associated with each wheel frame is adapted to be adjusted in a vertical, lateral and angular plane relative to the rail being inspected.
problem: Maintaining proper ultrasonic sensing contact and orientation with rails that have local surface variations while the testing carriage moves along the rails.
constraint: Maintaining parallelism between the two wheel frames while permitting independent vertical/lateral/angular motion of each frame relative to the main frame.
mechanism: Each sensing element is provided with independent degrees of freedom in a plane perpendicular to the target surface, while a constraint mechanism simultaneously maintains alignment between the elements. This decouples local surface irregularities from the global orientation of the system, allowing each sensor to self-adjust to local geometry while preserving overall system alignment.
mechanism_raw: Each wheel frame is given independent freedom of motion relative to the main frame in a plane perpendicular to the gauge side of the rail, while interconnecting means simultaneously maintain parallelism between the wheel frames. This decouples local rail irregularities from the global alignment of the system, allowing each ultrasonic sensor to self-adjust to local rail geometry while the overall carriage remains properly oriented.

abstract: An improved process and apparatus for production of synthetic multifilamentary yarns having uniform quality. The method comprises extruding a molten synthetic polymer downwardly through a spinneret, advancing the extruded filaments downwardly through a substantially stationary column of heated air, and subsequently advancing the filaments downwardly through a quenching zone wherein they are in contact with cooling air introduced into the path of the filaments under controlled conditions of air velocity and direction of flow. The apparatus for carrying out the process comprises an extrusion spinneret for extruding a number of filaments directly into a heated sleeve having walls that are imperforate, said heated sleeve leading to a quenching chamber having opposite, essentially vertical inlet and outlet panels for allowing cooling air to pass through the chamber, and means for regulating the stream of cooling air whereby both the velocity of the air stream going through the quenching chamber and its general direction as it contacts the descending filaments may be regulated.
problem: Producing synthetic multifilamentary yarns with uniform quality by ensuring consistent thermal treatment of continuously moving filaments.
constraint: Balancing air velocity and direction in the quenching zone to achieve uniform cooling without disrupting or misaligning the descending filaments.
mechanism: Filaments are advanced sequentially through a sealed heating zone with uniform thermal distribution and then through a controlled cooling zone where fluid velocity and flow direction are regulated to contact the moving filaments. The coordinated regulation of fluid stream properties ensures uniform thermal treatment across all filaments.
mechanism_raw: Filaments are advanced sequentially through a sealed heated sleeve with imperforate walls (ensuring uniform convective heating) and then through a quenching chamber where cooling air is introduced under controlled velocity and direction. The regulation of both air stream velocity and flow direction as it contacts the descending filaments allows precise control of the cooling profile, achieving uniform quenching across all filaments.

abstract: A sintered alloy for cutting tools comprising 60 to 90% by weight of a carbide comprising Mo.sub.2 C, WC and TiC in the proportions shown by the tetragonal region surrounded by points A, B, C and D in the ternary composition diagram of FIG. 1, the proportion of the sum of WC and Mo.sub.2 C with a WC/Mo.sub.2 C weight ratio of 35:65 to 65:35 being 50 to 75% by weight, and the proportion of TiC being 25 to 50% by weight, 3 to 20% by weight of a nitride selected from the group consisting of TiN, TaN or a mixture of TiN and TaN, and 5 to 20% by weight of Ni, Co or a mixture of Ni and Co as a binder metal, And further comprising a solid solution phase of the carbide and nitride with a grain size of not more than 1.3 .mu. and a binder metal phase.
reason: This patent primarily discloses a specific materials composition (ranges of carbides, nitrides, and binder metals) rather than a novel problem-solving mechanism. The underlying principle of combining hard phases with a ductile binder is a well-established materials science concept (cemented carbide), and the patent does not describe a new causal operation beyond specifying particular proportions.

abstract: This invention concerns processes for the regeneration of carbonylation catalysts consisting of dispersions of ligand-stabilized palladium(II) halide complexes in quaternary ammonium, phosphonium and arsonium salts of trihalostannate(II) and trihalogermanate(II) using organic peroxides as the regenerating agent. PAC STATEMENT OF THE INVENTION This invention pertains to the art of regenerating spent palladium carbonylation catalysts useful for the carbonylation of olefins. More particularly, this invention concerns the regeneration of certain carbonylation catalysts consisting of dispersions of ligand-stabilized palladium(II) halide complexes in quaternary ammonium, phosphonium and arsonium salts of trihalostannate(II) and trihalogermanate(II) using substantially anhydrous organic peroxide reagents. PAC BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION This invention concerns a process for regenerating certain palladium catalysts used in the carbonylation of olefins. Carbonylation refers here to the reaction of .alpha.-olefins with carbon monoxide and active-hydrogen-containing compounds selected from the group consisting of alkanols or water. The major products of carbonylation are fatty(carboxylic) acids and their esters. The preparation of the fatty acids or fatty acid esters using metal carbonyls or carbonyl precursors to catalyze the carbonylation of olefins is old in the literature, originally involving Reppe and his coworkers and contemporaries. Reviews by C.W. Bird [Chem. Rev.62, 283 (1962)] document this work. Unfortunately, many of these carbonyl or carbonyl-type catalysts have the disadvantages of inherent toxicity, they require stringent reaction conditions which in turn lead to competing side reactions such as olefin isomerization, polymerization and reduction, and they exhibit poor selectivity to the desired linear acid ester. Recently, more acceptable homogeneous catalyst systems have been developed which offer substantially improved selectivity in converting olefins to primarily linear fatty acids or linear fatty esters, in good yield, under moderate reaction conditions of temperature and pressure. As is usually the case, after much more extensive usage, certain drawbacks in the catalysts have become more evident. These include difficulty in maintaining high conversions, high selectivities and high yields after recycling the catalyst several times. These problems are due to catalyst degradation as well as catalyst decomposition, mechanical losses and further catalyst decomposition during the separation of the products from the homogeneous catalysts and the inert solvents of the reaction mixture. Thermal instability of the catalyst is particularly troublesome in the recovery and working-up of certain ligand-stabilized homogeous palladium catalyst reaction mixtures. In order to avoid or minimize these problems, the use of molten quaternary ammonium, phosphonium and arsonium salts of trihalostannate(II) and trihalogermanate (II) as both solvent and part of the catalytic entity has been disclosed, particularly in the two U.S. patents of G.W. Parshall, U.S. Pat. Nos. 3,657,368 and 3,565,823, which are known in the art as well as in applicant's Ser. No. 526,867 filed 11/25/74 in the U.S. Patent Office. More recently, two procedures, involving distillation and solvent extraction, for isolating product fatty acids/esters from palladium carbonylation catalysts consisting of dispersions of ligand-stabilized palladium(II) halides in quaternary ammonium, phosphonium and arsonium salts of trihalostannate(II) and trihalogermante(II) have been set forth in Ser. No. 581,320 and Ser. No. 581,395 both filed May 27, 1975. Following the separation of the catalyst and fatty acid ester products by these methods the palladium catalyst is suitable for recycle with fresh olefin/alcohol feed. Claims to the regeneration of the same palladium catalysts after multiple cycling by chlorination or treatment with mineral acid are also set forth in the above two applications. Each of these applications also discloses that a useful carbonylation must have: 1. A simple and efficient means of separating catalysts from the products, 2. The ability to recycle the catalyst without its substantial deactivation. This is particularly important since the palladium catalysts are thermally sensitive, and 3. A capability of operating at high concentrations of catalyst in the feed stream, thereby minimizing capital costs. PAC DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION The innovative and claimed aspect of this application is the discovery that the loss of catalytic activity of the above mentioned spent palladium carbonylation dispersion catalysts, can be restored by treatment of the catalysts with substantially anhydrous organic peroxides. The use of the latter (alternatively referred to as hydroperoxides) reagents is exemplified in Example 1, described infra. Here the octene, ethanol mixture is carbonylated by the procedure described, the ethyl nonanoate ester recovered by distillation, and after five cycles, the solid catalyst regenerated as follows: 1. The recovered catalyst is treated with organic peroxide reagent, preferably in the presence of an inert solvent, and the mixture heated under an inert atmosphere. 2. Excess liquid is removed by distillation under reduced pressure. 3. Additional stabilizing ligand, such as triphenylphosphine, is added to the cooled melt catalyst after peroxide treatment in the mole ratio of 1-10 mole ligand per mole Pd. The regenerated catalyst is then ready for recycle to the carbonylation reactor with fresh olefin/alcohol feed. Generally speaking, a wide range of peroxide and hydroperoxide reagents may be employed to regenerate said palladium carbonylation catalysts, Suitable hydroperoxide reagents include tert-butylhydroperoxide, cumene hydroperoxide, p-menthane hydroperoxide and 2,5-dimethylhexyl-2,5-dihydroperoxide. Suitable peroxide reagents include carprylyl peroxide, lauroyl peroxide, acetyl peroxide, benzoyl peroxide, p-chlorobenzoyl peroxide, dicumyl peroxide, di-t-butyl peroxide, t-butyl peracetate, t-butyl perbenzoate, and methyl ethyl ketone peroxide. At least a stoichiometric amount of peroxide reagent should be added to the spent palladium catalyst in order to achieve satisfactory regeneration, that is at least one mole of peroxide regent per gram atom of palladium present in the catalyst. Preferably, an excess of peroxide reagent should be employed, from 1 to 10.sup.4 moles of peroxide reagent per gram atom of palladium. Regeneration is judged to have occurred when a sample of treated catalyst delivers a selectivity to the desired linear fatty (carboxylic) acid or ester of between 70 and 95%, and a yield of total ester of from 20 to 95%. The peroxide or hydroperoxide regenerating reagents may be added to the spent catalyst neat, but preferably they are added in dilute form in the presence of a dried, inert solvent. Suitable inert solvents include among others, paraffinic solvents such as petroleum ethers, heptane, hexane and n-octane etc., ketones such as methyl isobutyl ketone, acetone and methyl ethyl ketone, chlorinated solvents such as o-dichlorobenzene, methylene chloride, and chloronaphthalenes, sulphones such as dimethylsulphone, aromatics such as benzene, toluene and xylenes, and mixtures thereof. The quatity of solvent used to dilute the organic peroxide or hydroperoxide reagent is not critical as to volume, for convenience sake about 0.1 parts by volume to 10.sup.4 parts by volume of inert solvent may be employed for each volume part of peroxide reagent. Likewise the time and temperature of regeneration are not initial, and temperatures of 20.degree. to 150.degree. C may be employed for 0.01 to 48 hours, according to the choice of palladium catalyst to be regenerated, and the choice of peroxide reagent. Catalyst regeneration is normally carried out in the presence of an inert atmosphere. This may be nitrogen, helium, argon, neon, carbon dioxide, or mixtures thereof, or the regeneration may be carried out in vacuo. Regeneration of palladium carbonylation catalysts with peroxide reagents is exemplified infra in Example 1 for the melt complex [(C.sub.2 H.sub.5).sub.4 N][SnCl.sub.3 ]-PdCl.sub.2 [P(C.sub.6 H.sub.5).sub.3 ].sub.2. Other palladium carbonylation catalysts beyond [(C.sub.2 H.sub.5).sub.4 N] [SnCl.sub.3 ]-PdCl.sub.2 [P(C.sub.6 H.sub.5).sub.3 ].sub.2 may also be generated by this technique. These catalysts generally consist of ligand-stabilized palladium(II) halide complexes dispersed in quaternary ammonium, phosphonium and arsonium salts of trihalostannate(II) and trihalogermanate(II). They are illustrated, but not limited by, the carbonylation catalysts described in Examples 8 to 14. Other substrate mixtures beyond the 1-octene, ethanol used in Example 1 may also be carbonylated by the regenerated palladium carbonylation catalysts. Some typical examples are given in Examples 15 to 20, described infra. Generally, for the carbonylation of .alpha.-olefins, as exemplified in equation 1, R.sub.1 and R.sub.2, individually, may by hydrogen, alkyl up to 12 carbon atoms, alkenyl up to 12 carbon atoms, or aryl up to 12 carbon atoms, or mixed alklaryl or arylalkyl groups. Suitable alkanols (ROH) ##STR1## include primary and secondary alcohols of 1 to 12 carbon atoms, phenols, substituted alcohols and polyols. The major products of the carbonylation reaction are fatty (carboxylic) acids and their esters.
problem: Restoring catalytic activity of spent palladium carbonylation catalysts after multiple reaction cycles, where the catalyst degrades or decomposes during separation and working-up of reaction products.
constraint: Regeneration must be performed under substantially anhydrous conditions and an inert atmosphere to prevent unwanted side reactions and catalyst decomposition during the peroxide treatment.
mechanism: A spent catalytic complex is treated with a regenerating agent under controlled environmental conditions (anhydrous, inert atmosphere) and elevated temperature. The regenerating agent restores active catalytic species by reversing deactivation pathways, followed by removal of excess reagent and reintroduction of stabilizing ligands to reform the active complex.
mechanism_raw: Treating the spent catalyst with substantially anhydrous organic peroxides (or hydroperoxides) under an inert atmosphere and elevated temperature. The peroxide reagent acts as a regenerating agent that restores the active palladium species, likely by re-oxidizing or re-ligating deactivated palladium complexes. After treatment, excess liquid is removed and stabilizing ligand is added to re-form the active catalytic complex.

abstract: An attachment for a conventional toilet bowl in a commode. The arcuate device for diverting and directing the swirling water created by flushing, into the exit waste conduit of the toilet bowl. A non-corrosive curved baffle, capable of deflecting and diverting water. The baffle is securely positioned below the still water level of a conventional toilet bowl to direct and force swirling water directly into the outlet conduit means at the base of a conventional commode for the purpose of saving water.
problem: Conserving water in conventional toilet bowls by efficiently directing swirling flush water into the exit waste conduit rather than allowing it to swirl ineffectively in the bowl.
constraint: The baffle must be positioned below the still water level to intercept the swirling flow, and must be made of non-corrosive material to withstand continuous exposure to waste water.
mechanism: A curved flow-director element is positioned within the fluid path of a containment vessel below the static fluid level. The element intercepts and redirects swirling flow generated during discharge, guiding it along a controlled trajectory into an exit conduit. The curvature provides a smooth deflection surface to minimize turbulence and backpressure.
mechanism_raw: A non-corrosive curved baffle is positioned below the still water level of the toilet bowl. The arcuate shape of the baffle intercepts the swirling water flow created by flushing and redirects it along a controlled path directly into the outlet conduit at the base of the bowl. The curvature of the baffle provides a smooth deflection surface that guides the water without creating excessive turbulence or backpressure.

abstract: A retainer of generally U-shape having slightly diverging legs detachably secures the proximal part of an excavating tooth within a complementary recess in its holder. The proximal end of the tooth has a generally rectangular cross-section with opposed outward extending ears and rearwardly thereof is formed with a spindle having a shoulder at the back. In the operative position of the retainer, a portion of the retainer straddles the spindle immediately in front of the shoulder. At least one leg of the retainer is formed with an upper offset leg portion and with oppositely offset lower leg portion with an interconnection there-between. The upper offset portion fits ahead of the shoulder to retain the tooth in place when the retainer is in operative position; but when the retainer is retracted to inoperative position, the upper offset portion of the leg clears the shoulder of the spindle of the tooth. The tooth holder is formed with an opening in which the retainer slides and the opening has an inward protuberance which engages the connecting portion to prevent unintentional complete withdrawal of the retainer so that it is not lost when it has been moved to retracted position. An improved distal tooth shape is disclosed wherein the blade has a body of substantially uniform thickness from front to rear with a central rib whereby the tooth remains sharp during its life. At the rear of the distal portion of the tooth is an abrupt shoulder which inhibits use of the tooth after its cutting life is exhausted and prevents excessive use from damaging the holder.
problem: Detachably securing a tool (excavating tooth) in a holder while allowing controlled removal without losing the retainer.
constraint: Balancing secure retention during use with easy detachment, while ensuring the retainer remains physically connected to the holder to avoid loss.
mechanism: A resilient element with a locking feature engages a protrusion on a tool to retain it in a holder. The locking feature can be selectively disengaged to allow removal, while a physical stop on the holder prevents full withdrawal of the resilient element, ensuring it remains connected.
mechanism_raw: A U-shaped retainer with offset legs straddles a spindle on the tool. When engaged, the upper offset locks behind the spindle's shoulder to retain the tool; when retracted, the offset clears the shoulder, enabling removal. A protuberance in the holder's opening prevents full withdrawal of the retainer.

abstract: A lunch bucket having a food compartment and a separate, unconnected compartment for a beverage bottle, so that liquid possibly leaking from the bottle cannot damage the food, both compartments having closure doors, the bottle compartment door operating a friction device operable to secure said door frictionally in either its open or its closed position, and to secure the bottle in position when said door is closed.
problem: Preventing liquid leakage from a beverage bottle from damaging stored food in a shared container.
constraint: Maintaining accessibility to both compartments while ensuring the bottle is immobilized and the door remains in a chosen position without additional latches.
mechanism: Separate, unconnected compartments with independently operable closures. A friction-based retention system secures each closure in a selected position and immobilizes a container within its compartment, preventing movement and leakage contact with adjacent contents.
mechanism_raw: Separate, unconnected compartments with closure doors. A friction device on the bottle compartment door allows it to be secured in open or closed positions, and when closed, frictionally holds the bottle in place to prevent movement and leakage contact with food.

abstract: Books are produced by feeding juxtaposed webs of printed matter, obtained from rolls, to a knife which cuts the webs to provide juxtaposed sheets in paginated relation; a delivery cylinder may be optionally set to feed the paginated sheets to one of two folders, which respectively fold signatures of different form. The signatures are then delivered to a conveyor which is preferably a saddle conveyor in which event the fold is so made as to result in a lap margin.
problem: Producing books with paginated sheets folded into signatures of different forms while maintaining proper alignment and margins.
constraint: Accommodating different folding methods (e.g., varying signature forms) while maintaining consistent sheet alignment and margin formation during high-speed production.
mechanism: Cut sheets are conveyed through a shaped path that induces folding into signatures. The path geometry forces folds to create lap margins, ensuring proper alignment and pagination of signatures during high-speed production.
mechanism_raw: Juxtaposed webs are cut into sheets and delivered to a saddle conveyor. The conveyor's geometry forces folds to create lap margins, ensuring proper pagination and alignment of signatures as they are conveyed to downstream processing.

abstract: A brick press is disclosed having a turntable carrying a plurality of molds angularly spaced from each other and having equipment associated therewith establishing a plurality of series of operating stations, each series including at least a precompression station, a compression station and an ejection station. The molds carried by the turntable are provided with replaceable liners. A material handling and feed system is also disclosed, providing for preparation of particulate or granular materials to be charged into the molds.
problem: Efficiently producing bricks with consistent compression and ejection while enabling maintenance and material handling.
constraint: Balancing continuous operation with replaceable components and synchronized material feeding to avoid process interruptions.
mechanism: A rotating platform carries processing units through sequential stations. Replaceable components within the units allow maintenance without downtime, while a synchronized feeding system delivers material into the units during rotation to maintain continuous operation.
mechanism_raw: A rotating turntable carries molds through sequential stations (precompression, compression, ejection). Replaceable liners in the molds allow maintenance without downtime, and a material handling system prepares and feeds granular material into the molds during rotation.

abstract: The air flow in one zone of a gypsum wallboard dryer involves removal of the air from the wallboard drying section at one end of the elongate wallboard drying section, followed by directing a major portion of this air through fans to accelerate the air flow, next heating the air in an elongate plenum, through which the air passes, by directing high intensity flame angularly into the air flow from the periphery of the elongate section, thus creating agitation within the air flow to create uniformity of temperature therethroughout prior to directing the heated, thoroughly mixed air back into the wallboard drying section, at an end of the section opposite to the end from which it was originally removed.
problem: Achieving uniform temperature distribution in a gypsum wallboard dryer to prevent localized overheating or under-drying.
constraint: Maintaining airflow velocity and heat intensity to ensure mixing without excessive energy consumption or thermal degradation of the wallboard.
mechanism: Air is drawn from one end of a drying section, accelerated, heated by directed energy sources, and agitated to mix the air. The thoroughly mixed, heated air is then redirected back into the drying section at the opposite end to ensure uniform temperature distribution.
mechanism_raw: Air is removed from one end of the drying section, accelerated by fans, heated via high-intensity flames directed angularly into the airflow, and agitated to mix the air. The thoroughly mixed, heated air is then redirected back into the drying section at the opposite end.
