abstract: In a continuous sugar evaporator-crystallizer having a plurality of evaporating-crystallizing vessels as stages, each evaporating-crystallizing stages being communicated one to another in series and being provided with a means for feeding an aqueous sugar solution, a heating means and a means for withdrawing generated steam, by feeding an aqueous sugar solution to each evaporating-crystallizing stage, heating the aqueous sugar solution in each evaporating-crystallizing stage, thereby evaporating water off the aqueous sugar solution and crystallizing sugar crystals, and withdrawing the generated steam from each of the stages, while feeding seed sugar crystals to the first evaporating-crystallizing stage and withdrawing the resulting sugar crystal slurry from the last evaporating-crystallizing stage, sugar crystals of high quality is obtained in the slurry with an effective suppression of occurrence of conglomerated sugar grains by providing sugar crystal distances of 0.26 to 0.59 mm in the solution in the first evaporating-crystallizing stage, and feeding the aqueous sugar solution to each of intermediate evaporating-crystallizing stages excluding the first and last evaporating-crystallizing stages at a substantially equal feed rate, and making the feed rate of the aqueous sugar solution to the first evaporating-crystallizing stage at least 1.5 times the feed rate to each of the intermediate evaporating-crystallizing stages.
problem: Preventing conglomeration of sugar crystals and maintaining high-quality crystal slurry in a multi-stage evaporator-crystallizer.
constraint: Balancing feed rate ratios and spatial crystal distribution to avoid overcrowding while maintaining throughput.
mechanism: Regulating nucleation and growth dynamics by controlling inter-particle spacing in a primary processing stage and adjusting feed rate ratios between stages to suppress unwanted aggregation while maintaining throughput.
mechanism_raw: Controlling crystal spacing in the first stage (0.26–0.59 mm) and adjusting feed rates (first stage ≥1.5× intermediate stages) to regulate nucleation and growth dynamics, suppressing unwanted crystal aggregation.

abstract: A method and apparatus for forming a drawn container from a metallic blank are disclosed wherein the blank is drawn over the outer surface of a stationary forming ring by an annular forming die to form a tubular wall portion which is thereafter completely redrawn by a forming punch in co-operation with a forming die, a reverse redrawn annular wall portion of the blank being positioned for engagement by a curling ring to form an inwardly curled rim at the peripheral edge of the open end of the container.
problem: Forming a drawn metallic container with a curled rim from a blank in a single continuous process.
constraint: Coordinating tool geometry and deformation sequence to avoid material failure while achieving precise final shape.
mechanism: Executing a sequence of forming operations on a workpiece using coordinated tool geometries, where initial shaping, complete redrawing, and rim curling are performed in a continuous process without intermediate handling to avoid material failure.
mechanism_raw: Sequential forming steps: initial drawing over a stationary ring, complete redrawing via punch-die cooperation, and curling via a dedicated ring to shape the rim without intermediate handling.

abstract: In an embroidery machine, especially an area embroidery machine, the embroidering heads of embroidering stations, which are arranged one above the other, are adjustably mounted on basic guides which extend over the entire height of the embroidering field, in such a manner that the embroidering tools on the needle side and on the shuttle side of each embroidering station are movable synchronously to each other relative to the embroidery field, individually, in groups, or in their entirety. The basic guides on the needle side and on the shuttle side are movable relative to the embroidery field. The embroidering tools are mounted on the basic guides by interconnecting adjustment bars; the relative position of the adjustment bars in view of the basic guides is adjustable on the needle side and on the shuttle side.
problem: Precisely positioning embroidering tools relative to a work field in an area embroidery machine.
constraint: Maintaining positional synchronization between opposing tool sides during independent or collective adjustments.
mechanism: Mounting tools on shared guide structures with interconnecting elements to enable synchronized, grouped, or independent movement while maintaining alignment between opposing tool sides during positioning adjustments.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable mounting of tools on shared basic guides via interconnecting bars, enabling synchronized, grouped, or individual movement while maintaining alignment between needle and shuttle sides.

abstract: Fish are oriented by laying them in random arrangement in the central portion of a vibrating trough, the opposite ends of which form passages slightly wider than the widest fish being sorted. Fish move headfirst toward the trough ends, and the movement of fish discharged in single file from such trough ends is accelerated to propel fish past detector means. Such detector means include a radiant-energy source and fish-sorting means responsive to energy from such source operable to deflect fish leaving such source for channeling the fish corresponding to a characteristic detected by the detector. Such characteristic may be sex, length or sidewise orientation. Alternatively, fish can be subjected to detector means for energizing a signal simply to indicate a characteristic of the fish without sorting the fish, such as by placing a fish on an energy-transmitting surface, applying an energy-responsive element to the opposite side of the fish and actuating a signal in response to operation of the energy-responsive element.
problem: Orienting and sorting irregularly shaped objects (e.g., fish) based on physical characteristics.
constraint: Balancing vibration frequency and acceleration speed to ensure reliable orientation and detection without damaging objects.
mechanism: Inducing headfirst orientation of irregularly shaped objects via vibrational excitation, propelling objects past sensors for trait detection, and applying responsive deflection to channel sorted items based on detected characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Vibratory trough induces headfirst orientation, acceleration propels objects past detectors, and responsive deflection channels sorted items based on detected traits.

abstract: A high temperature water (HTW) space heating system in which the direct source of HTW is an automatic electrode steam boiler having electrodes, adapted to be connected in an electrical distribution system. The electrodes are positioned in corresponding steam generating compartments surrounded by a control compartment. A corresponding water spout directs water toward the tip of each electrode. A regulating valve allows only a limited steam output, which is used for control purposes. Water is taken from the boiler and mixed with water from an outside source. A boiler water circulating group feeds the mixed water to the spouts with sufficient velocity for it to flow up the surface of the electrodes to the water level in the steam generating compartments. The system has a heated space circuit including a pump for circulating HTW. An HTW supply circuit connects the boiler with the heated spaces circuit and provides unrestricted flow of HTW from the boiler to the heated spaces circuit so that the boiler serves as a pressurized expansion tank for the heating system. A diversion circuit is connected between the heated spaces circuit and the inlet of the boiler water circulating pump. A control valve arrangement diverts a controlled amount of HTW from the heated spaces circuit to the pump inlet through the diversion circuit. Such diverted HTW constitutes water from an outside source and is replaced in the heated spaces circuit by HTW from the boiler through HTW supply circuit.
problem: Integrating a high-temperature water boiler into a space heating system while maintaining pressure and flow stability.
constraint: Ensuring the boiler acts as a pressurized expansion tank without disrupting the heated spaces circuit’s unrestricted flow.
mechanism: Balancing system pressure and flow by using a regulated steam output for control, mixing boiler fluid with external fluid, and routing diverted high-temperature fluid through a diversion circuit to maintain stability without disrupting the main heated spaces circuit.
mechanism_raw: Using a regulated steam output for control, mixing boiler water with external water, and routing diverted HTW through a diversion circuit to balance system pressure and flow.

abstract: An aircraft instrument with an acceleration compensation device comprises at least a capsule, a rocking axle, a link mechanism to transmit displacements of a free end of the capsule to the rocking axle, a first gear integrally provided with the rocking axle, a second gear meshed with the first gear and being rotatable, and weights. The weights are provided on the first gear and the second gear each correspondingly, and rotative force of the weights caused by an acceleration force works on the rocking axle so as to cancel the rotative force of the rocking axle by the displacements, due to the acceleration, of the free end of the capsule.
problem: Acceleration forces cause unwanted displacement in aircraft instruments, leading to inaccurate readings.
constraint: The system must balance opposing forces precisely without introducing mechanical complexity or hysteresis that could degrade accuracy.
mechanism: A force-balancing system uses opposing torques generated by movable masses on interlocking mechanical elements to counteract displacement caused by external acceleration, achieving cancellation through equilibrium of rotational forces.
mechanism_raw: Weights mounted on intermeshing gears generate a rotative force opposing the capsule's acceleration-induced displacement, mechanically canceling the error through opposing torque.

abstract: An illustrative embodiment of the invention eliminates the circumferential thermal stresses found in a feedwater inlet nozzle of a once-through-vapor generator that are caused by the presence of steam in the nozzle during a low flow load condition. Specifically, The cold inlet feedwater is directed upwardly to fill and overflow the nozzle conduit and prevent steam entrance and collection in the nozzle, and then, impinges on a shroud which re-directs the flow downward into fluid flow contact with the nozzle conduit and through the vapor generator.
problem: Steam ingress into a feedwater inlet nozzle during low-flow conditions creates circumferential thermal stresses that damage the nozzle.
constraint: The flow direction and pressure must be maintained to ensure the nozzle remains filled with liquid, preventing vapor accumulation without disrupting overall system hydraulics.
mechanism: A liquid barrier is maintained by directing a cold fluid upward to fill and overflow a conduit, physically blocking vapor ingress, while a secondary flow path redirects the fluid downward to preserve system hydraulics.
mechanism_raw: Cold feedwater is directed upward to fill and overflow the nozzle conduit, physically blocking steam entry, then redirected downward via a shroud to maintain continuous flow through the vapor generator.

abstract: A material pleater embodying a plurality of parallel, longitudinally extending plate-like members carried by an elongated member with adjacent plate-like members spaced from each other to receive a pleat of material therebetween. An elongated pleat depresser has longitudinally extending, spaced apart depresser elements with each being disposed to move between adjacent plate-like members and depress a pleat of material therebetween. Detachable means connects the pleats thus formed to each other whereby they remain in the formed position after removal of the plate-like members and the pleat depresser.
problem: Forming and retaining consistent pleats in materials after mechanical forming tools are removed.
constraint: The spacing between plates and the depresser's movement must be precisely coordinated to form uniform pleats without damaging the material or requiring continuous tool contact.
mechanism: Parallel surfaces spaced to receive material are paired with a moving compression element that shapes the material into discrete folds, while separable fasteners permanently retain the fold geometry after tool removal.
mechanism_raw: Parallel plates spaced to receive material pleats are paired with a moving depresser element that compresses the material between plates, while detachable connectors permanently fix the pleat geometry after tool removal.

abstract: A process for preparing a free-flowing lactulose-containing powder from a solution containing lactose, by adding calcium hydroxide to the solution to adjust the pH of said solution to from 9.4 to 11.2; heating the resulting solution so that the pH is reduced to from 7.5 to 9.0; the homogenizing, concentrating and drying.
problem: Converting a lactose-containing solution into a stable, free-flowing powder without clumping or degradation.
constraint: The pH adjustment and heating steps must occur within specific ranges to avoid over-processing or destabilizing the lactulose compound during drying.
mechanism: A multi-stage chemical and thermal process adjusts pH through sequential reagent addition and heating, followed by homogenization, concentration, and solidification to lock in powder properties via controlled phase transitions.
mechanism_raw: Calcium hydroxide adjusts the solution pH to a high range, heating reduces pH to a lower range, and subsequent homogenization, concentration, and drying lock in the desired powder properties through controlled chemical and thermal transitions.

abstract: A counter-current leaching or extraction tower for comminuted vegetable matter such as sugar beet cossettes, or crushed sugar cane, is provided with conveying elements, the longitudinal dimension of which may be altered in response to the operating condition in the material or matter being leached. Especially, the baffle members in the tower and, if desired, also the conveyor screw wings which are arranged to cooperate with the baffle members, are adjustable in their length in response to control signals derived from sensors, such as strain gauges, attached to the conveying elements. The angular position of the conveying elements in a plane parallel to the motion of the screw wings and relative to a radial direction may also be adjustable in response to the same type of control signals. The conveying elements may be constructed to include telescoping members which are longitudinally and thus radially extendable and retractable relative to the volume of the extraction tower. The combination of the several adjustabilities of the conveying elements provides an efficient localized control of the operating conditions throughout the tower volume.
problem: Inefficient localized control of operating conditions in a counter-current leaching tower due to fixed conveying elements.
constraint: The adjustments must balance real-time responsiveness with mechanical durability, ensuring sensors and actuators can adapt to varying loads without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A feedback-controlled system dynamically adjusts flow-directing and material-handling elements in response to real-time sensor data, altering their geometry and orientation to optimize contact efficiency and extraction performance.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable baffles and conveyor screw wings respond to real-time sensor data (e.g., strain gauges) by telescoping or rotating, dynamically altering their length and angular position to optimize material contact and extraction efficiency throughout the tower.

abstract: Particular zones are given a distinctive appearance with respect to surrounding areas on a surface such as a printed-circuit board to be drilled in an automatic process. The surface is automatically scanned in a system of two rectilinear perpendicular coordinates by a reader comprising at least one detector which is responsive to the distinctive appearance. The coordinates of the surface points for which the detector delivers a signal representing the presence of the distinctive appearance during the scanning are recorded in a coded form which can be utilized by the automatic machine.
problem: Automatically identifying and recording the coordinates of specific zones on a surface for use by a machine (e.g., drilling).
constraint: The detector must reliably distinguish the distinctive zones from surrounding areas during scanning, and the recorded coordinates must be precise enough for automated machine operations.
mechanism: Scanning a surface along two orthogonal axes with a detector sensitive to distinctive visual markers, then recording the detected marker positions in a coded format for use by an automated machine.
mechanism_raw: Scanning a surface in a rectilinear coordinate system with a detector responsive to distinctive visual markers, then recording the coordinates of detected markers in coded form for downstream machine use.

abstract: Manufacture of grain and split leather is simplified by pre-tanning hide with a chromium-free tan until its shrinkage temperature is about 170.degree. to about 185.degree. F, splitting the pre-tanned hide to provide a grain intermediate and a split intermediate, shaving at least one of these intermediates, and chrome-tanning the shaved intermediate. Shavings contain no chromium and can be disposed of by dumping, without significant environmental impact. Before splitting, the hide can also be pickled to improve the splitting and shaving and make the unfinished hide better suited for shipping to remote geographical areas. Entire hide treatment sequence can be effected with two stages in which batches of hides are loaded in a container such as tumbling drum; unhairing, bating and pre-tanning with or without a pickle, all in one stage, and final tanning, coloring and fat-liquoring in another stage. Final chrome-tanned product has very good physical characteristics including unusually high slot tear and is recovered in higher yield.
problem: Simplifying leather manufacturing while reducing environmental impact from chromium-containing waste.
constraint: The pre-tanning must achieve sufficient structural integrity for splitting and shaving without chromium, while the final chrome-tanning must preserve product quality and yield.
mechanism: Treating a material with a chromium-free agent to achieve a controlled shrinkage temperature sufficient for mechanical processing, separating the treated material into layers, mechanically reducing one layer without introducing contaminants, then applying a final treatment to the reduced layer in a subsequent stage.
mechanism_raw: Pre-tanning hide with a chromium-free agent to a controlled shrinkage temperature, splitting the pre-tanned hide into grain and split intermediates, shaving intermediates without chromium contamination, then chrome-tanning the shaved intermediate in a separate stage.

abstract: A fireplace for use in mobile homes is disclosed. The fireplace has a plurality of doors which seal the combustion chamber. An air duct leads from the combustion chamber of the fireplace through the floor of the mobile home so as to provide an external source of combustion air for the fireplace when the doors close and seal the fireplace combustion chamber from the interior of the mobile home.
problem: Providing combustion air for a fireplace in a mobile home without depleting indoor air quality or creating safety hazards.
constraint: The air duct must maintain a sealed path from the external environment to the combustion chamber without compromising the structural integrity of the mobile home floor.
mechanism: Creating a sealed pathway from an external environment through a structural surface to a combustion chamber, supplying external air directly to support combustion without exchanging indoor air.
mechanism_raw: Sealing the combustion chamber with doors and routing an external air duct through the floor to supply combustion air directly from outside the mobile home.

abstract: Method and apparatus for treating sugar-works molasses wherein the third stage part of the mother liquid-hot saccharate suspension is reheated in a heat exchanger before mixing the same with the cool filtrate of the second stage to increase the temperature of the mixture to the precipitation temperature of hot saccharate.
problem: Optimizing the temperature of a mixed liquid suspension to achieve efficient precipitation in sugar processing.
constraint: The reheating must precisely adjust the temperature of the mixed suspension without overheating, which could degrade the saccharate or reduce yield.
mechanism: Transferring heat to a portion of a mixed liquid suspension in a heat exchange device, then combining the heated portion with a cooler portion of the suspension to raise the overall temperature to a target precipitation level.
mechanism_raw: Reheating a portion of the mother liquid-hot saccharate suspension in a heat exchanger before mixing it with a cooler filtrate, thereby raising the combined mixture to the desired precipitation temperature.

abstract: Burner installation in a steam generator having means for firing pulverized coal as well as gas, includes a combustion chamber of substantially rectangular cross section, at least three pulverized coal-burners disposed mutually adjacent one another in cross-sectional direction of the combustion chamber on a first wall of the combustion chamber at least one of the pulverized coal-burners being located between others thereof, gas burners located on at least another wall of the combustion chamber located adjacent the first wall thereof, the pulverized coal burners being located at an elevation of the combustion chamber above the gas burners, the at least one of the pulverized coal-burners being operable only if gas is not being burned simultaneously therewith by the gas burners.
problem: Efficiently operating a steam generator with both pulverized coal and gas burners without conflicting combustion dynamics.
constraint: The spatial separation and interlock must ensure that coal and gas combustion do not interfere with each other, maintaining stable flame patterns and heat distribution.
mechanism: Positioning first and second combustion devices on opposing walls of a chamber, with a control system that prevents simultaneous operation of both devices to maintain stable combustion dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Arranging pulverized coal burners above gas burners on adjacent walls of a rectangular combustion chamber, with an interlock system that disables coal burners when gas burners are active to prevent simultaneous operation.

abstract: For lapping the surfaces defining a hole in a wiredrawing die of diamond or artificial material, one or more transducers are excited by respective ultrasonic generators to produce mechanical vibrations imparted to lapping needles. Turntables arranged opposite to the tips of the lapping needles are rotated from a common drive shaft and, simultaneously, each rolled or swayed about an axis passing through the die mounted thereon. A cam or crank mechanism driven from the common drive shaft is employed for the rolling motion of each turntable. The apparatus further comprises means for fine adjustment of the position of each turntable relative to the lapping needle in a plane at right angles therewith, and means for yieldably urging the die on the turntable against the lapping needle under adjustable pressure.
problem: Achieving precise and uniform lapping of a small, hard surface (e.g., a die hole) while maintaining structural integrity and throughput.
constraint: Balancing the intensity of ultrasonic vibrations with the precision of mechanical positioning to avoid over-lapping or uneven wear while maintaining consistent contact pressure.
mechanism: Combining high-frequency energy input with multi-axis mechanical motion and adjustable contact force to achieve uniform material removal across a target surface while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Combining ultrasonic vibrations (via transducers) with controlled mechanical motion (rotation and rolling of turntables) and adjustable pressure to create a multi-axis lapping action that ensures uniform material removal across the target surface.

abstract: A door latch arrangement is disclosed to prevent a door from popping open when the door is subjected to pressure from the inside. Means are provided to restrain movement of the door latch until the door and latch have moved partially open, thereafter the door is free to manipulated to a fully open position.
problem: Preventing unintended door opening under internal pressure while allowing manual override once partial opening is achieved.
constraint: Ensuring the restraint is strong enough to resist pressure-induced forces but weak enough to allow manual override once the door begins to open.
mechanism: A restraint system that blocks a locking mechanism until the door's own motion triggers a release, after which manual override becomes possible. The release is mechanically linked to the door's partial opening.
mechanism_raw: A restraint system that blocks latch movement until the door has moved partially open, after which the latch is released to allow full manual manipulation. The door's own motion triggers the release.

abstract: A preforming apparatus for stranding machines for imparting to the wires or strands the helical wave shape the wires have to assume in the finished rope. For each wire or strand to be wound into the rope one particular preforming device is provided on a common base plate. Each preforming device comprises rollers around which the wires are guided. At least one roller in each preforming device is adjustable in its position relative to the other rollers of the device in order to vary the wave shape of the wires; and setting means are provided on the base plate for simultaneously and jointly setting all adjustable rollers in one single operating step.
problem: Imparting a consistent helical wave shape to multiple wires or strands simultaneously during rope manufacturing.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization of adjustments across multiple independent devices to avoid variability in the final rope structure.
mechanism: Using synchronized adjustment of multiple independent shaping elements via a centralized control mechanism to ensure uniform deformation of all strands in a single step.
mechanism_raw: Using adjustable rollers in each preforming device, with a centralized setting mechanism that jointly adjusts all rollers in a single step to ensure uniform wave shaping across all wires.

abstract: Intake arrangement of an internal combustion engine comprises an air intake passageway and an air-fuel mixture intake passageway with its port arranged radially inwardly of the air intake passageway. Port opening period of the air-fuel mixture intake port is full overlapped with and shorter than port opening period of air intake port of the air intake passageway.
problem: Optimizing air-fuel mixture intake timing in an internal combustion engine to improve combustion efficiency.
constraint: Balancing the overlap duration to maximize air intake while preventing excessive fuel dilution or incomplete combustion.
mechanism: Overlapping the opening periods of two intake pathways with different durations to control the timing and proportion of air versus fuel entering a combustion chamber.
mechanism_raw: Overlapping the opening period of the air-fuel mixture intake port with the air intake port, but shortening the mixture port's duration to control the timing and proportion of air versus fuel entering the cylinder.

abstract: Subject device is automatically tripped by manually opening the door of the mailbox. The device includes a frame which is intended to be attached to the lower edge of the mailbox. Pivotally attached to the frame is a signalstaff adapted for pivotal movement between an upright position and a recumbent cocked position. Attached to the upper end of the signalstaff is an omnidirectional signalhead which provides conspicuous evidence from any angle of view that the door of the mailbox has been opened. The signalstaff is held in the cocked position and/or selectively released therefrom by a novel trigger mechanism which includes an actuating lever disposed adjacent the door for operable engagement therewith and whereby the trigger mechanism is operated to enable biasing apparatus to carry the signalstaff to the upright position as the door is opened.
problem: Providing a conspicuous, omnidirectional visual signal when a mailbox door is opened.
constraint: Ensuring the trigger mechanism reliably engages and disengages with the door's motion while maintaining the signalstaff's stability in the upright position.
mechanism: A pivotally mounted signal element held in a cocked position by a trigger linked to the door's motion. Opening the door actuates the trigger, releasing the signal element to swing upright via a biasing mechanism, making it visible from any angle.
mechanism_raw: A pivotally mounted signalstaff held in a cocked position by a trigger mechanism linked to the door. Opening the door actuates the trigger, releasing the signalstaff to swing upright via biasing apparatus, making the signalhead visible from any angle.

abstract: A guide for a motorized handsaw which guide includes a track member and clamps which fixedly engage the track and clamp to the underside adjacent edges of the workpiece to be cut by the saw. The clamps include sawable workpiece edge engaging members which extend into the area of the expected saw cut so that they indicate the guided saw line therebetween.
problem: Ensuring a motorized handsaw follows a precise cutting path while maintaining alignment with the workpiece.
constraint: Balancing secure clamping to the workpiece without obstructing the saw's cutting path or introducing misalignment during operation.
mechanism: Clamping elements engage a workpiece at opposing edges and extend into the expected cut zone, with their relative positioning defining a physical reference line that constrains the cutting tool to follow the intended path. The clamping force and reference line are co-located to ensure alignment is maintained during operation.
mechanism_raw: Clamps engage the workpiece edges and extend into the expected cut area, physically marking the guided saw line between them. This dual function of clamping and line indication ensures the saw follows the intended path.

abstract: Glass compositions of the SiO.sub.2 -ZrO.sub.2 -alkali metal oxide-alkaline earth oxide system containing 70-82 mole percent SiO.sub.2 and 2-8 mole percent ZrO.sub.2 and alkali metal oxides and alkaline earth oxides, and optionally Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, in specified amounts, such glasses being resistant to water, acids and alkalies, having a low to medium thermal coefficient of expansion and a low liquidus temperature.
problem: Creating a glass composition resistant to water, acids, and alkalies while maintaining low thermal expansion and low liquidus temperature.
constraint: Optimizing the oxide ratios to achieve multiple performance criteria (chemical resistance, thermal expansion, liquidus temperature) without compromising structural integrity or manufacturability.
mechanism: A chemical composition is formulated using a specific molar ratio of network-forming oxides, high-refractive-index stabilizers, and fluxing agents to simultaneously achieve chemical durability, controlled thermal expansion, and reduced processing temperature. The ratios balance structural stability against multiple performance criteria through compositional optimization.
mechanism_raw: A specific molar ratio of SiO₂-ZrO₂-alkali metal oxide-alkaline earth oxide (with optional Al₂O₃) is formulated to stabilize the glass structure, leveraging ZrO₂'s high refractive index and alkali/alkaline earth oxides to balance chemical durability and thermal properties.
residual_terms: ["molar ratio", "network-forming oxides", "high-refractive-index stabilizers", "fluxing agents", "chemical durability", "thermal expansion", "processing temperature"]

abstract: An improved feed adjusting apparatus for sewing machines having a control device which reduces to a minimum the displacement between the actual path and the optimum path of travel of a slider during its intended function of transforming the oscillating movement of the feed advance shaft to reciprocating movement of the bar that supports the machine's feed dogs.
problem: Minimizing displacement between the actual and optimal path of a slider in a sewing machine feed mechanism during oscillating-to-reciprocating motion conversion.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical simplicity and responsiveness while reducing displacement errors across varying operational loads and speeds.
mechanism: A feedback-driven control system continuously compares the actual trajectory of a moving element to its ideal path during motion conversion, dynamically adjusting actuation inputs to minimize deviations. The system compensates for load- and speed-dependent errors in real-time to maintain precise output motion.
mechanism_raw: A control device actively adjusts the slider's path by dynamically compensating for deviations between its actual trajectory and the ideal path, ensuring precise reciprocating motion of the feed bar.
residual_terms: ["feedback-driven control system", "trajectory comparison", "motion conversion", "actuation inputs", "deviations", "load-dependent errors", "speed-dependent errors"]

abstract: A catalytic process is provided for the selective production of para-xylene by contacting, under conversion conditions, a charge stock containing, as a major reactant, at least one hydrocarbon selected from the group consisting of toluene, a C.sub.3 -C.sub.10 olefin, a C.sub.5 -C.sub.10 naphthene, a C.sub.3 -C.sub.10 paraffin, and mixtures of the foregoing with a catalyst comprising a composite of a crystalline aluminosilicate zeolite and antimony oxide, said zeolite having a silica to alumina ratio of at least about 12 and a constraint index, as hereinafter defined, within the approximate range of 1 to 12.
problem: Selectively producing para-xylene from hydrocarbon feedstocks while suppressing undesired byproducts.
constraint: Balancing catalytic activity and selectivity to maximize para-xylene yield while preventing catalyst deactivation or over-conversion of reactants.
mechanism: A porous crystalline catalyst structure with controlled pore geometry and acid site distribution selectively promotes target molecular transformations by restricting reactant/product diffusion and stabilizing intermediate species. The catalyst's framework composition and topology enforce reaction pathway selectivity while resisting deactivation.
mechanism_raw: A catalyst composed of a crystalline aluminosilicate zeolite (high silica-to-alumina ratio, constraint index 1–12) combined with antimony oxide selectively promotes the formation of para-xylene by controlling molecular diffusion and reaction pathways within the zeolite structure.
residual_terms: ["porous crystalline catalyst", "pore geometry", "acid site distribution", "diffusion restriction", "intermediate species stabilization", "reaction pathway selectivity", "deactivation resistance"]

abstract: A boom for an excavator or the like is constructed to have a generally L-shape when viewed in side elevation and have a circular cross section tapering downward from a maximum diameter at the apex of the boom to each end. The boom is made up of a central body portion consisting of a cast-form elbow and a pair of tapered tubular members formed of rolled plate welded along a longitudinal seam extending from the elbow outward to the outer ends of the boom. A pair of cast-formed connecting members are then welded to the end of the boom. The method of fabrication includes the cast-forming of the elbow and the respective end connecting means and forming the tapered body members by rolling and connecting the entire assembly by welding.
problem: Constructing a durable, structurally efficient boom for heavy machinery (e.g., excavators) with complex geometry and load-bearing requirements.
constraint: Achieving structural integrity and fatigue resistance while minimizing material waste and manufacturing complexity through hybrid forming techniques (casting, rolling, welding).
mechanism: A hybrid structural assembly combines formed components with differing manufacturing processes (e.g., casting and rolling) to create a continuous load path. High-stress regions use localized reinforcement through one process, while intermediate sections use optimized geometry from another process, distributing stress and minimizing material waste through process-specific shaping.
mechanism_raw: Combining cast-formed components (elbow and end connectors) with rolled tapered tubular sections, welded together to create a seamless load path. The tapered design distributes stress while the cast joints provide localized strength at high-stress regions.
residual_terms: ["hybrid structural assembly", "formed components", "manufacturing processes", "load path", "high-stress regions", "localized reinforcement", "process-specific shaping"]

abstract: Sulfone copolymeric oil additives having utility as a lubricating oil pour point depressant, viscosity index improver, dispersant, load carrying agent, rust inhibitor and/or antioxidant, or as a cold flow improver for heavy distillates and residual fuels, comprise the hydrocarbon soluble copolymers of an ethylenically unsaturated polar monomer and sulfur dioxide. This sulfone copolymer may contain one or more additional monomers including: C.sub.2 to C.sub.50, preferably at least C.sub.6, substantially linear alpha olefins; C.sub.2 to C.sub.12, preferably C.sub.2 to C.sub.9, cyclic olefins; and, C.sub.4 to C.sub.6 conjugated diolefins.
problem: Improving multiple performance properties (e.g., pour point, viscosity, dispersancy) of lubricating oils and fuels using a single additive.
constraint: Balancing the composition of monomers to achieve multiple functionalities (e.g., solubility, thermal stability, and reactivity) without compromising the additive's effectiveness or compatibility with the base fluid.
mechanism: Combine multiple monomers with differing polarities and chain structures through copolymerization to create a single additive that interacts with a base fluid to simultaneously modify its physical and chemical properties. The varying monomer compositions enable the additive to address multiple performance requirements without compromising compatibility or effectiveness.
mechanism_raw: Copolymerizing an ethylenically unsaturated polar monomer with sulfur dioxide and additional monomers (e.g., alpha olefins, cyclic olefins, diolefins) to create a hydrocarbon-soluble sulfone copolymer. The combination of monomers with varying polarities and chain structures allows the copolymer to interact with the base fluid to modify its physical and chemical properties simultaneously.

abstract: In a power and free conveyor system which comprises a train of free trolleys including a leading trolley and one or more following trolleys, one of the following trolleys is provided with a transfer dog that remains fully retracted within the trolley track and out of contact therewith until conveying of the train is to be transferred from a first to a second powered conveying chain. To initiate the transfer, a power dog on the first chain disengages from a drive dog on the leading trolley, and the transfer dog is raised out of the following trolley for engagement with another power dog on the first chain. Engagement of the transfer dog with the power dog is maintained preferably throughout the transfer area until the leading trolley is adjacent to the second conveyor chain for engagement of a power dog thereon with the drive dog of the leading trolley.
problem: Transferring a train of free trolleys from one powered conveyor chain to another without disrupting the movement of the leading trolley or losing synchronization.
constraint: Ensuring precise timing and mechanical coordination between the retraction/extension of the transfer dog and the engagement/disengagement of power dogs to avoid collisions or misalignment during transfer.
mechanism: Use a sequential engagement mechanism where a transfer element on a following unit remains inactive until a power element on the first system disengages from the leading unit's drive element. The transfer element then activates to maintain continuous engagement with the first system until the leading unit is ready to interface with the second system, enabling controlled, synchronized transfer of a sequence of units.
mechanism_raw: A transfer dog on a following trolley remains retracted until a power dog on the first chain disengages from the leading trolley's drive dog. The transfer dog is then raised to engage with the first chain's power dog, maintaining engagement throughout the transfer area until the leading trolley is ready to engage with the second chain. This allows controlled, sequential transfer of the trolley train.

abstract: A seat supporting assembly for resiliently supporting a vehicle seat which finds particular utility in tractors or other off-the-road vehicles. The seat supporting assembly includes an adjusting means, readily accessible to the operator and by which he can adjust both the height of the seat and the up-stop limit of the seat. A spring loaded mechanism is provided for the adjusting means which includes a pair of arms that have interengaging means that equalize movement of the adjusting mechanism.
problem: Providing an adjustable vehicle seat that allows the operator to simultaneously modify seat height and up-stop limit while maintaining balanced movement.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical balance and smooth operation of the interengaging arms under varying load conditions (e.g., operator weight, vibration) to prevent binding or uneven movement.
mechanism: Employ a mechanically linked adjustment system with interengaging components that equalize movement forces during actuation. The interengagement ensures synchronized motion between multiple adjustment axes, allowing a single control input to modify both height and positional limits while maintaining balanced operation under varying load conditions.
mechanism_raw: A spring-loaded adjusting mechanism with a pair of interengaging arms equalizes movement during adjustment. The arms' interengagement ensures synchronized motion, allowing the operator to adjust both height and up-stop limit through a single accessible control without requiring separate adjustments.

abstract: One or more pulsating streams of liquid material may be transformed into streams of essentially constant velocity with use of a counterweighted tundish that tilts in response to variations in liquid input. The dispensing system is particularly suited for use as a feeding source of liquid metal for continuous strip casting processes due to its ability to provide a constant low velocity teeming stream.
problem: Converting pulsating liquid streams into a steady, constant-velocity flow for processes requiring uniform material delivery (e.g., continuous strip casting).
constraint: Calibrating the counterweight's mass and pivot point to match the specific pulsation frequency and amplitude of the input stream, ensuring responsiveness without overcorrection.
mechanism: Implement a passive feedback system where a counterbalanced reservoir tilts in response to input flow variations, dynamically adjusting outlet geometry to dampen pulsations. The counterbalance provides mechanical stabilization that opposes transient pressure changes, converting irregular input into a steady, low-velocity output stream.
mechanism_raw: A counterweighted tundish tilts in response to variations in liquid input, dynamically adjusting the outlet geometry to dampen pulsations. The counterweight provides passive feedback to stabilize the flow rate, ensuring a consistent low-velocity stream despite upstream fluctuations.

abstract: A micro information reader defined by a thin container open at one side. The open side receives a micro information carrier. The carrier and the thin container are provided with interengaging ridges which function as detents to index the micro information carrier with respect to fixed illumination sources and projection lenses on the reader.
problem: Precisely indexing a micro information carrier (e.g., a microform) relative to fixed illumination sources and projection lenses in a reader without external alignment mechanisms.
constraint: Designing the ridge geometry and spacing to ensure repeatable, high-precision alignment while allowing easy insertion and removal of the carrier without jamming.
mechanism: Use complementary mechanical constraints on both the carrier and its receptacle to passively position and align the carrier relative to fixed components. The interengaging features act as self-aligning detents that constrain movement in multiple axes, ensuring precise registration without external adjustment mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: Interengaging ridges on both the thin container and the micro information carrier act as passive detents. These ridges mechanically constrain the carrier's position, automatically aligning it with the fixed optical components when inserted into the reader.

abstract: A game in which a plurality of game pieces are moved about a smooth endless track in a random manner by tilting the track cyclicly to provide a downhill racing surface in advance of the game pieces. The track is oval in shape and is tilted or wobbled by means of a pair of eccentric cams which cyclicly raise and lower weight-supporting arms at one end of the track, to tilt it about a centrally located pivot point. Each game piece includes a base portion having a substantially flat bottom with a number of ball bearings mounted therein to facilitate random movement of the game pieces along the track, and to enhance the random nature of the movement of the game pieces with respect to the track and with respect to each other.
problem: Creating a game that produces unpredictable, random movement of game pieces on a track.
constraint: Balancing tilt amplitude and frequency to maintain randomness while preventing pieces from stalling or moving too predictably.
mechanism: Apply periodic oscillatory motion to a surface so that objects resting on it experience alternating gravitational gradients, inducing stochastic displacement. The amplitude and frequency of oscillation are tuned to sustain motion without allowing objects to settle into stable positions.
mechanism_raw: Cyclic tilting of the track via eccentric cams generates a moving downhill surface, causing pieces with low-friction bases (e.g., ball bearings) to roll randomly. The tilt direction and speed are controlled to ensure continuous, chaotic motion without jamming.

abstract: Apparatus and method are disclosed for efficient harvesting of fruits or nuts from trees. Picking tines extend radially from a vertically disposed drive shaft and move horizontally through the foliage of a fruit or nut bearing tree by rotation of the shaft. During rotation, the drive shaft is also reciprocated vertically for upward and downward movement of the tines in the foliage while they also move horizontally therein. Also, the rotational velocity of the shafts is varied rhythmically so that horizontal travel of the tines on upward movement becomes zero or else is much slower than during downward movement. By upward and downward movement of the tines, while also varying their horizontal travel rhythmically, the harvesting rate can be increased and the damage to tree foliage can be reduced.
problem: Efficiently harvesting fruits/nuts from trees while minimizing damage to foliage and fruit.
constraint: Synchronizing rotational speed and vertical motion to optimize fruit detachment without excessive force on branches or foliage.
mechanism: Combine rotational movement of flexible tines with reciprocating vertical motion, modulating rotational speed between upward and downward strokes. During upward motion, reduced rotational speed allows tines to gently engage and dislodge targets; during downward motion, increased rotational speed facilitates debris clearance and repositioning.
mechanism_raw: Combining rotational motion of tines with vertical reciprocation and rhythmic variation of rotational speed. During upward movement, horizontal speed is reduced or halted, allowing tines to dislodge fruit gently; during downward movement, faster horizontal speed clears debris or repositions tines.
residual_terms: ["rotational movement", "reciprocating vertical motion", "rotational speed", "tines", "upward motion", "downward motion"]

abstract: In a clothes washer an agitator that is also a water pump draws water from the zone between the basket and the tub of the clothes washer and pumps it to the inside of the basket thereby raising the water level in the area where washing occurs during agitation and also promoting good clothes roll-over action in the treatment zone. A method of laundering articles includes the step of pumping laundering liquid into a treatment zone and radially outwardly along a lower portion of the zone during agitation to obtain a desired level of laundering liquid in the part of the zone where laundering occurs.
problem: Improving washing efficiency by ensuring adequate water distribution in the treatment zone during agitation.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient water flow to the treatment zone without disrupting the mechanical agitation's effectiveness or overloading the pump.
mechanism: Integrate a fluid transfer mechanism within an agitating element to draw liquid from a secondary zone and direct it into the primary treatment zone during mechanical agitation. This enhances fluid-assisted material movement and ensures adequate liquid distribution without interrupting the agitation process.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a pump into the agitator to draw water from the outer zone and inject it radially outward into the basket during agitation. This raises water levels in the active washing area and enhances clothes roll-over action through fluid-assisted mechanical movement.
residual_terms: ["fluid transfer mechanism", "agitating element", "liquid", "secondary zone", "primary treatment zone", "mechanical agitation", "fluid-assisted material movement"]

abstract: A coke briquette for use in iron foundries in which coke fines screened from coke being fed to the cupola are recycled into briquette form to be used in place of raw coke in the iron making process. A mix for making the briquettes employs an 80-10-10 percentage by weight ratio of coke fines, high early cement and fly ash respectively to which water is added in a two-step process. The fines have their external surfaces prewetted prior to the adding of the fly ash, cement and additional water for activating the cement. The resulting mix is then formed and cured into cylindrical briquettes by conventional block-making apparatus.
problem: Recycling coke fines into structurally sound briquettes for industrial use without compromising material integrity.
constraint: Achieving the correct moisture balance to activate cement hydration without over-saturating the mix, which could weaken the final briquette structure.
mechanism: Apply controlled moisture addition to particulate material in a staged process to activate binding agents through chemical hydration. The moisture level is regulated to ensure uniform mixing and curing, enabling the particles to cohere into a structurally stable form via optimized chemical reactions.
mechanism_raw: Prewetting coke fines to activate binding agents (cement and fly ash) in a two-step hydration process. The controlled addition of water ensures uniform mixing and curing, enabling the fines to bind into durable briquettes via optimized chemical reactions.
residual_terms: ["moisture addition", "particulate material", "binding agents", "chemical hydration", "moisture level", "chemical reactions"]

abstract: A mounting panel for technical instruments consisting of a number of smaller panel elements which are provided with instrument holes and which form a system of modules. The panel is provided with weakenings so that elements of the panel may be broken away for adapting the panel to the desired size. Weakenings are also provided in the panel which run between adjacent holes so that the middle portion between four or more of the holes may be knocked out to obtain a larger opening to fit larger instruments.
problem: Adapting a mounting panel to fit varying instrument sizes and configurations without requiring custom manufacturing.
constraint: Designing weakening patterns that ensure clean, predictable breakage without unintended damage to adjacent areas or compromising load-bearing capacity.
mechanism: Incorporate predefined structural discontinuities in a panel to enable controlled separation of sections. This allows modular adaptation of the panel geometry while preserving structural integrity in regions not subject to separation.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating predefined weakening lines in the panel structure to allow controlled breakage of sections. This enables modular resizing and hole expansion while maintaining structural integrity in unmodified regions.

abstract: Stylus, having a conductive electrode, is mounted at one end of a pivoted stylus support arm within a pickup cartridge body of non-conductive material, removably received in a conductive housing. A conductive spring, with one end in electrical contact with the stylus electrode, is secured at its opposite end to the cartridge body. A printed circuit board, mounted within the conductive housing, comprises a dielectric substrate bearing a conductive coating in several elongated surface regions. The conductive coating in two of said regions defines first and second conductors, lying substantially parallel to each other. When the cartridge is received in the housing, electrical contact is established between the body-secured spring end and one end of the first conductor. Capacitive elements couple the other end of the first conductor to the housing. The spring, first conductor, and housing form a transmission line, which resonates with the end-loading capacitive elements and a variable capacitance formed between stylus electrode and the disc record, at frequencies in a selected range. UHF oscillations at a frequency adjacent said range are inductively coupled to the transmission line. AM detector, connected to second conductor, recovers recorded information.
problem: Recovering recorded information from a disc record while maintaining signal fidelity across a selected frequency range.
constraint: Balancing resonance frequency stability with variable stylus-disc capacitance while enabling inductive coupling of UHF oscillations without disrupting the transmission line's operation.
mechanism: A resonant transmission line structure formed by a conductive element, a first conductor, and a housing interacts with end-loading capacitive elements and a variable capacitance between a probe and a target surface. High-frequency oscillations are inductively coupled to this system, and amplitude modulation detection via a second conductor recovers the recorded information.
mechanism_raw: A resonant transmission line formed by a conductive spring, first conductor, and housing interacts with end-loading capacitive elements and a variable stylus-disc capacitance. UHF oscillations are inductively coupled to this system, and AM detection via a second conductor recovers the recorded information.
residual_terms: ["resonant transmission line", "conductive element", "first conductor", "housing", "end-loading capacitive elements", "variable capacitance", "probe", "target surface", "inductively coupled", "high-frequency oscillations", "amplitude modulation detection", "second conductor", "recorded information"]

abstract: A carrying case for transporting an article in an upright condition is described including a deep box having a front wall, a rear wall, a pair of side walls, a bottom, and defining an upwardly opening chamber therein. Advantageously, the case includes a laterally positionable holding apparatus which is secured to the box within the chamber for engagement with the opposite edges of the article and for holding it in spaced relation away from the front and rear walls. The case also includes a handle for carrying it and supporting it as a working surface, and a removable cover that serves as a tray.
reason: The mechanism is a static structural design for positioning an article within a case, lacking a causal functional principle that produces an effect through dynamic interaction or feedback.

abstract: A valve block assembly for use in glassware forming machines is disclosed. The valve block has at least two rows of valve stations arranged parallel to one another. An air supply manifold and an air exhaust manifold communicates with each row of valve stations. A cartridge valve is disposed at each of the valve stations for controlling the air flow through a respective valve station. An outlet conduit, having a needle valve disposed within it, forms a flow path away from the cartridge valve. A check valve is also disposed within at least one of said outlet conduits. All of the valves are mounted in a vertical front face of the valve block.
reason: The mechanism is a modular arrangement of valves and manifolds for airflow control, which is a structural configuration rather than a causal functional principle that generates a useful effect through dynamic interaction.

abstract: A centrifuge apparatus, primarily for use in the continuous or semi-continuous separation of blood, has a disposable separation unit which is orbited on a centrifuge rotor. The separation unit has a sealed jacket which is held against rotation during the orbiting and communicates with a stationary and nonrotatable liquid inlet and outlet connector on the rotor axis. A separation vessel rotatably mounted in the jacket communicates with liquid inlet and outlet passages in the jacket and is rotationally unbalanced to orient itself relative to the rotor during the orbiting of the jacket.
problem: Achieving continuous or semi-continuous separation of blood components while maintaining a sealed, sterile system during orbital centrifugation.
constraint: Balancing rotational imbalance to ensure self-orientation without disrupting the sealed system or introducing mechanical instability during high-speed orbiting.
mechanism: A sealed containment is held against rotation during orbiting, while a separation vessel mounted within it is rotationally unbalanced to self-orient relative to the rotor. This imbalance causes the vessel to align dynamically during operation, enabling continuous separation without manual adjustment.
mechanism_raw: A sealed jacket is held against rotation during orbiting, while a separation vessel mounted within it is rotationally unbalanced to self-orient relative to the rotor. This imbalance causes the vessel to align dynamically during operation, enabling continuous separation without manual adjustment.

abstract: Process for the production of latices of conjugated diene polymers and conjugated diene copolymers with vinyl compounds by emulsion polymerization comprising PA1 (a) a first polymerization stage in the presence of the monomer as a phase separate from the polymer being formed, PA1 (b) an intermediate stage in which the monomer is added in quantities such that the conversion of the monomer at the end of each individual addition exceeds 45%, and PA1 (c) a final stage in which the reaction is carried to completion.
problem: Producing latices of conjugated diene polymers with controlled molecular structure and properties through emulsion polymerization.
constraint: Maintaining phase separation during the first stage while ensuring sufficient conversion in intermediate stages to prevent uncontrolled polymerization or structural defects.
mechanism: A multi-stage process: (1) phase-separated monomer polymerization, (2) intermediate monomer addition with greater than 45% conversion per addition to control chain growth, and (3) final completion. This staged approach balances phase separation and conversion rates to regulate polymer architecture.
mechanism_raw: A three-stage process: (1) phase-separated monomer polymerization, (2) intermediate monomer addition with >45% conversion per addition to control chain growth, and (3) final completion. This staged approach balances phase separation and conversion rates to regulate polymer architecture.
residual_terms: ["multi-stage process", "phase-separated monomer polymerization", "intermediate monomer addition", "greater than 45% conversion", "chain growth", "final completion", "phase separation", "conversion rates", "polymer architecture"]

abstract: A bailer pump designed for securing to a well head comprising an elongated stan pipe projecting upward from the well head supporting a motor driving a reel for cable through a drive train incorporating a magnetic brake, when the current to the motor is interrupted the magnetic brake is activated. A bailer is propelled into and out of the well in a repititious controlled manner. The electrical control mechanisms operate in conjunction with a pivot arm mounted at the top of the stan pipe on an axle. Pillow blocks retain the pivot arm in a tilting position. Tension or lack of tension on the cable passing over the top pulley causes a reciprocal tilting of the pivot arm and the pulley. The tilting arm contacts a micro switch which through time delay and relays start, stop, and reverse the electric motor operating the cable reel. The short delay in the well permits filling of the bailer and a long delay at the well head permits unloading of the bailer. The long delay is energized by the bailer striking a bailer stop contacting the top micro switch stopping the motor and activating the long delay. The unloading function is accomplished mechanically by the bailer contacting the bailer stop pulling an actuating rod which through a trough linkage tilts the unloading trough under the bailer striking a dart at the bottom of the bailer emptying the contents of the bailer into an oil receiver.
problem: Automating the reciprocating motion of a bailer to fill and unload materials in a well while maintaining controlled timing between operations.
constraint: Balancing the timing of filling and unloading cycles to ensure efficient operation without overloading the motor or bailer, while maintaining mechanical reliability of the pivot arm and linkage system.
mechanism: A feedback system where physical tension variations in a moving component tilt a mechanical lever, actuating sensors that trigger time-delayed control signals to regulate motor operation. The delays correspond to different operational phases (filling and unloading), creating a closed-loop between physical movement and motor control.
mechanism_raw: Cable tension variations caused by bailer movement tilt a pivot arm, which actuates micro switches. These switches trigger time-delay relays to start, stop, or reverse the motor driving the cable reel. A short delay allows bailer filling, while a long delay (activated by the bailer striking a stop) enables mechanical unloading via a linkage-driven trough. The system creates a closed-loop feedback between physical cable tension and motor control.

abstract: A support device for an independent tank, wherein a first support member secured to the tank is adapted to be supported on the top surface of a second support member attached to a ship's hold. Particularly in the case of a spherical tank, a horizontal ring projecting from adjacent the equator of the spherical tank is adapted to be supported on a support deck installed around the inner periphery of a ship's hold, with a pressure-resistant heat insulating material interposed between the ring and the support deck. In such support device, an anti-floating member is provided on and projects from either the first support member or the second support member through the other member without touching the same. When the tank tends to float up, the free end of the anti-floating member and the mating member engage each other with the pressure-resistant heat insulating material interposed therebetween, thereby preventing the floating up of the tank.
problem: Securing a floating tank (e.g., a spherical tank on a ship) against buoyancy forces while maintaining thermal insulation and structural support.
constraint: Ensuring the anti-floating mechanism activates only under buoyancy forces while allowing normal support and thermal expansion, without compromising the insulating material's integrity.
mechanism: A mechanical interlock that engages under upward buoyancy forces, using a projecting member that contacts a mating surface with an insulating material interposed. This blocks upward movement while preserving thermal insulation.
mechanism_raw: An anti-floating member projects from one support component through another without contact. When the tank tends to float, the free end of the anti-floating member engages a mating surface on the opposing component, with the pressure-resistant insulating material interposed between them. This mechanical engagement physically blocks upward movement while preserving insulation.

abstract: A monitoring apparatus for a textile machine comprising a feeler coupled with an evaluation circuit, the feeler possessing two spaced electrodes, each of which delivers an electrode signal when textile material moves therepast. The electrodes are offset in the direction of movement of the textile material and the evaluation circuit comprises a logic circuit responsive to electrode signals having a time displacement corresponding at least approximately to the transit time of the textile material from the one electrode to the other electrode.
problem: Detecting the presence, speed, or direction of textile material movement in a machine using non-contact sensing.
constraint: Precisely spacing the electrodes and calibrating the time-delay logic to account for material speed variations and sensor response times, ensuring accurate detection without false triggers.
mechanism: A time-based detection system using spaced sensors to measure the transit time of material between them, determining movement characteristics through signal timing.
mechanism_raw: Two electrodes are spaced and offset along the direction of material movement. Each electrode generates a signal when material passes it. The evaluation circuit measures the time displacement between the signals, which corresponds to the transit time of the material between the electrodes. This time-based logic determines movement characteristics.

abstract: A non-elastomeric sensor holding fixture using metal-to-sensor contact friction in a wheel slip control system maintains a wheel speed sensor in intimate contact with an exciter wheel without the excessive sensor wear which otherwise happens when the wheel speed sensor is held in place with resilient elastomeric holder. The use of metal-to-sensor frictional contact in the holding fixture avoids the hardening and seizing normally occurring in elastomeric-to-sensor frictional contact due to time and allows readjustment of sensor position after extended use.
problem: Maintaining a wheel speed sensor in consistent contact with an exciter wheel without excessive wear or degradation over time.
constraint: Balancing the frictional force to ensure sufficient contact pressure for accurate sensing while minimizing wear on the sensor and exciter wheel surfaces.
mechanism: A friction-based contact mechanism using a durable material to maintain sensor pressure against a moving surface, allowing repositioning after wear without degradation.
mechanism_raw: A non-elastomeric holding fixture uses metal-to-sensor contact friction to press the sensor against the exciter wheel. Unlike elastomeric materials, metal friction avoids hardening, seizing, or degradation from prolonged use, allowing the sensor to be repositioned after extended operation.

abstract: In an analog to digital converting circuit used in a pulse height analyzer or in a time to digital converting circuit used in a time analyzer, the first binary in a scaler for counting clock pulses is switched over to use the true state and the complementary state each of the reset circuit and the output circuit, alternately. By switching over the reset circuit and the output circuit, no substantial variation in counting the scaler is induced and any odd-even unbalance phenomena due to the binary constitution of the scaler is statistically equilibrated.
problem: Reducing odd-even unbalance errors in binary counting systems (e.g., scalers in analog-to-digital converters) caused by the binary constitution of the scaler.
constraint: Ensuring the switching between true and complementary states does not introduce timing delays or disrupt the scaler's counting process, while maintaining synchronization with the clock pulses.
mechanism: A dynamic state selection mechanism that alternates between two states of a binary stage to statistically balance errors over time.
mechanism_raw: The first binary stage of the scaler is alternately switched between using its true state and complementary state for reset and output circuits. By dynamically toggling which state is used for these functions, the system statistically averages out the odd-even imbalance over time, minimizing counting errors.
residual_terms: ["binary stage", "true state", "complementary state", "reset and output circuits"]

abstract: Powder detergent compositions for machine dish washing which are effective in hard water in the absence of phosphates are provided based on a combination of low foaming nonionic surfactant, bleaching agent, and from 8-70% of ammonium sulfate, ammonium borate, ammonium carbonate, ammonium bicarbonate, or a mixture thereof. The composition is required to provide a pH in the range of pH 7.0 to pH 8.5 measured in 1% water solution.
problem: Creating an effective phosphate-free detergent composition that functions in hard water without compromising cleaning performance.
constraint: Maintaining pH within 7.0–8.5 to ensure compatibility between components and prevent precipitation of hardness ions, while balancing ammonium salt concentration (8–70%) for optimal ion sequestration and cleaning.
mechanism: Combining a buffering/sequestering agent with active cleaning agents (e.g., surfactant, oxidizer) to maintain pH within a specified range and bind hardness ions, enabling cleaning efficacy in high-mineral-content water.
mechanism_raw: Combining ammonium salts (e.g., ammonium sulfate, borate) with a low-foaming nonionic surfactant and bleaching agent to buffer pH (7.0–8.5) and sequester hardness ions, enabling surfactant and bleach efficacy in hard water.

abstract: An electronic timepiece having a time alarm. The timepiece includes a time counter circuit for developing a progressively increasing count representative of time. A single alarm counter and a repeat alarm counter both store respective counts representative of respective times. The single alarm counter is responsive to a reset signal for clearing the count stored therein. A coincidence detecting circuit compares the respective counts stored in the single and repeat alarm counter circuits with the count developed by the time counting circuit, and develops an output signal when the compared counts coincide. An alarm responds to this output signal to indicate when the time represented by the compared counts coincide. A gate circuit is effective for alternately applying the respective counts stored in the alarm counter circuits to the coincidence detecting circuit to alternately compare the count developed by the time counter circuit with the respective counts stored in the alarm counter circuits. The gate circuit applies the coincidence detecting circuit output signal as a reset signal to reset the single alarm counter circuit when the count developed by the time counting circuit coincides with the count stored in the single alarm counter circuit.
problem: Efficiently managing multiple alarm events (single and repeat) in an electronic timepiece using minimal hardware.
constraint: The gate circuit must synchronize alternation between the two alarm counters and reset the single alarm counter upon coincidence, ensuring no overlap or missed comparisons.
mechanism: Using a switching network to alternately route stored event counts from two independent counters to a shared comparison unit, enabling time-multiplexed evaluation against a reference signal.
mechanism_raw: Using a gate circuit to alternately route stored alarm counts from two separate counters to a shared coincidence detector, enabling time-multiplexed comparison against a time counter signal.

abstract: An apparatus for dispensing liquid from a container is locked to the container rim and comprises an air inlet for delivering air under superatmospheric pressure to the interior of the container above the liquid level therein, a check valve in the inlet for preventing air from escaping, a tap standpipe defining an air channel arranged for connection to the inlet, a liquid outlet in communication with the bottom of the chamber, and a shutoff valve for closing the outlet.
problem: Dispensing liquid from a container without manual pumping or risk of spillage, while maintaining pressure integrity.
constraint: The check valve must prevent air escape to maintain pressure, while the shutoff valve ensures controlled dispensing and prevents unintended flow.
mechanism: Applying pressurized fluid to a sealed reservoir via a one-way inflow valve, forcing liquid discharge through an outlet when a controlled release valve is opened, while maintaining system pressure integrity.
mechanism_raw: Applying superatmospheric air pressure via an inlet with a check valve to create a sealed system that forces liquid out through an outlet when a shutoff valve is opened.

abstract: A device for displacing a body along a guiding column which is particularly suitable for the projection head of an enlarging or reproducing apparatus. The device comprises in a conventional manner a guiding column and, on the body, a friction wheel which presses against the column and which is disposed on a shaft. The shaft of the friction wheel is mounted in the sleeve-like body which surrounds the column except in the vicinity of the friction wheel. The friction wheel is sub-divided into two wheel portions and means are provided for exerting a force upon the wheel portions along the axis of the friction wheel. These means act upon a guiding surface of the column disposed at an angle of up to 90.degree. with respect to the friction wheel axis.
problem: Achieving precise, controlled movement of a body along a guiding column (e.g., a projection head) using friction-based actuation.
constraint: The guiding surface angle (up to 90° relative to the wheel axis) and axial force magnitude must balance friction to allow smooth movement without slippage or binding.
mechanism: Splitting a friction-based actuator into two segments and applying variable axial force to modulate contact pressure against an angled surface, enabling controlled displacement through friction adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Splitting a friction wheel into two portions and applying axial force to modulate contact pressure against an angled guiding surface, enabling fine adjustment of friction for controlled displacement.

abstract: A method for treating a sour petroleum distillate is disclosed. The distillate is treated in contact with a catalyst in the presence of an alkaline reagent at oxidation conditions, said catalyst having been prepared by forming an aqueous dispersion of a metal phthalocyanine comprising a soluble acid amide, contacting a solid adsorptive support with said dispersion at conditions to adsorb at least a catalytic amount of said metal phthalocyanine thereon. The resulting composite is subsequently dried.
problem: Preparing a stable, effective catalyst for treating sulfur-containing (sour) petroleum distillates via catalytic oxidation.
constraint: The acid amide must stabilize the phthalocyanine during adsorption to prevent aggregation, while drying conditions preserve the catalyst's active sites and support adhesion.
mechanism: Forming a stabilized dispersion of a catalytic complex with a stabilizing agent, adsorbing it onto a porous substrate, then removing solvent under controlled conditions to preserve active sites and structural adhesion.
mechanism_raw: Forming an aqueous dispersion of a metal phthalocyanine with a soluble acid amide to stabilize the complex, then adsorbing it onto a solid support before drying, ensuring catalytic activity and structural integrity.

abstract: 2. An article of manufacture useful as a gas generator and comprising a container having an outlet and supported and adapted to burn within said container and adhered to the walls of said container a mixed, shaped and cured composition of matter characterized by generating large volumes of gas on combustion and, except for minor amounts of compounding ingredients, consisting essentially of from about 70 to 87% by weight of finely-divided dried ammonium perchlorate, from about 0.5 to 5.0% by weight of at least one high surface area finely-divided essentially anhydrous inorganic silicon and oxygen-containing burning rate modifier selected from the group consisting of silicon monoxide, fume silica, arc silica and silicon oxyimide, and the balance a combustible organic elastomeric polymeric binder selected from the group consisting of a cured polyesterurethane of an organic diisocyanate and a hydroxyl terminated polyester of a dibasic acid and a glycol and a polymer comprising predominantly linear carbon chains cured through at least a portion of its combined curable acid groups selected from the class consisting of COOH, SO.sub.3 H, SO.sub.2 H and PO.sub.3 H.sub.2 radicals.
problem: Need a solid gas generator composition that produces large volumes of gas with a controlled burning rate while maintaining structural integrity and adhesion to the container walls during combustion.
constraint: The burning rate modifier must be present in a narrow range (0.5-5.0% by weight) to achieve the desired burning rate without destabilizing the composition or compromising mechanical integrity; the binder must simultaneously provide adhesion, structural support, and clean combustion.
mechanism: A solid fuel matrix incorporates dispersed reactive particles to increase available reaction sites, thereby controlling and increasing the burning rate. A polymeric binder simultaneously provides structural cohesion, adhesion to containment surfaces, and contributes combustible material to gas generation. The burning rate modifier is constrained to a narrow concentration range to balance reaction kinetics with mechanical integrity.
