mechanism_raw: Dispersing high surface area inorganic silicon-containing particles (silicon monoxide, fume silica, arc silica, or silicon oxyimide) within a solid fuel/oxidizer matrix (ammonium perchlorate) to increase available reaction sites and thereby control and increase the burning rate. An elastomeric polymeric binder holds the composition together, adheres it to the container walls, and contributes combustible material to the gas generation process.
residual_terms: ["burning rate modifier", "polymeric binder", "solid fuel matrix", "reactive particles"]

abstract: Disclosed is a buckle for a belt in which parts of the buckle are provided in two interrelated, yet separate, parts. The first part, secured to one end of the belt, comprises a plate having two extending tangs. The first tang extends downwardly and through the end of the belt to which it is affixed. It engages an aperture in a rigid loop. The second tang extends upwardly so as to engage the apertures in the free end of the belt, after the belt has been inserted through the rigid loop. The rigid loop has an implement formed as an integral part thereof. The implement is inserted into a pouch in the belt.
reason: This is a specific mechanical design for a belt buckle with an integrated tool feature. It describes a two-part latching mechanism and an integral implement, but does not embody a deeper causal principle or problem-solving mechanism that transfers to other fields beyond the immediate mechanical design of belt fasteners.

abstract: A yarn is provided which has zero twist and random lengths of tightly entangled fibers as nodes having substantially zero twist and comprising an average of about 20%-70% of a representative length of yarn, said nodes having a retentivity of at least 75% and alternating with random lengths of substantially unentangled asymmetrically splayed fibers in intervals having an average length of about 3-12 mm. A fraction of the fibers in the yarn can be broken to provide effect yarns.
problem: Need to create a yarn with good mechanical integrity and retentivity without using twist, which can interfere with certain textile applications or fiber properties.
constraint: The entanglement node density and length must be balanced against the unentangled section length to achieve sufficient retentivity (≥75%) while maintaining zero twist and acceptable processability; too much entanglement reduces flexibility, too little reduces strength.
mechanism: A zero-twist yarn is formed by alternating localized entanglement regions (comprising a specified fraction of total length) where fibers are tightly interlocked to provide structural integrity and retentivity, with unentangled sections of asymmetrically splayed fibers that enable flexibility and processability. Mechanical properties arise from discrete entanglement nodes rather than continuous structural modification.
mechanism_raw: Creating a zero-twist yarn by forming random entanglement nodes (comprising 20-70% of the yarn length) where fibers are tightly entangled to provide structural integrity and retentivity (at least 75%), alternating with random lengths of unentangled, asymmetrically splayed fibers that provide flexibility and processability. The mechanical properties arise from localized entanglement rather than continuous structural modification.

abstract: A method of making a core yarn in which a pair of flattened slubbings or fiber-fleece strips are passed through a stretching arrangement comprising a plurality of pairs of rollers, the slubbing being engaged in the nips of the rollers, with the core thread being fed to each of the slubbing strips in the nip of the last roller pair. According to the invention, the two slubbing strips are passed directly adjacent one another (either in contact or with a small spacing) through the nip of the last roller pair and immediately downstream thereof, the combination of strips and the respective core threads are spun together.
problem: Need to efficiently and reliably combine core threads with fiber-fleece carrier strips to produce a core yarn with consistent structure and proper core positioning.
constraint: The slubbing strips must be precisely positioned adjacent to each other at the final nip to ensure the core threads are properly introduced to both strips simultaneously; any misalignment or excessive spacing would result in uneven core distribution or failed combination.
mechanism: Two core elements are fed to adjacent carrier strips at a critical convergence point where the strips are positioned in direct proximity, ensuring simultaneous introduction of both cores to the strips at the same junction. The combined elements are then subjected to a single downstream consolidation process, synchronizing their integration before final formation.
mechanism_raw: Feeding two core threads to two adjacent slubbing strips at the nip of the last roller pair in a stretching arrangement, where the strips are positioned directly adjacent (in contact or with small spacing) so that the core threads are simultaneously introduced to both strips at the same critical junction point. The combined strips and core threads are then spun together in a single downstream operation, ensuring synchronized combination before final yarn formation.

abstract: A method and apparatus for controlling and transferring the cut end of a weft to a subsequent sliding shuttle clamp. The weft end is retained in the guide slot of the shuttle supply drum which was occupied by the previous shuttle before it was shot through the shed. A storage lever retracts the cut end of the weft to the intake side of the drum and the weft is then pivoted to the new shuttle.
problem: Need to reliably capture, retain, and transfer the cut end of a weft thread from one shuttle to a subsequent shuttle in a weaving operation without breaking the thread or losing tension.
constraint: The capture-retract-pivot sequence must be precisely coordinated with shuttle movement timing to avoid breaking the weft thread or losing tension; the guide slot and storage lever must reliably retain the thread end while allowing smooth retraction and pivoting to the new shuttle.
mechanism: A sequential capture-retract-transfer operation retains a thread end in a guided retention feature, retracts it to an intake position via a mechanical repositioning element, and pivots it to a receiving shuttle. The timing of each phase is coordinated with shuttle movement to maintain tension and prevent thread failure.
mechanism_raw: Retaining the weft end in a guide slot on the shuttle supply drum (previously occupied by the departing shuttle), then using a storage lever to retract the cut end to the intake side of the drum, and finally pivoting the weft to the new shuttle for transfer. This creates a sequential capture-retract-transfer operation using guided retention and mechanical repositioning.
residual_terms: ["guided retention feature", "mechanical repositioning element", "capture-retract-transfer", "shuttle movement timing"]

abstract: In the chrome-tanning of skins with a chromium (III) salt and an acid-binding agent, the improvement which comprises effecting the chrome-tanning in the presence of a water-soluble partial ester of a polycarboxylic acid containing 4 to 11 carbon atoms which ester hydrolyzes into the free acid or its salt. The partial ester is advantageously present in about 0.5 to 2, preferably 1,3 to 1.8, times the molar amount of the chromium salt expressed as Cr.sub.2 O.sub.3. The tanning composition can be formed by dissolving the desired ingredients and the solution spray dried to provide a properly formulated powder which can thereafter by employed to re-formulate the solution.
problem: Improving the efficiency and control of chrome-tanning processes by managing acidity and reaction conditions during skin treatment.
constraint: The partial ester must be present in a specific molar ratio (0.5–2× the chromium salt) to balance hydrolysis rate and acid availability without destabilizing the tanning chemistry.
mechanism: Using a hydrolyzable precursor that releases acidity in a controlled manner through chemical decomposition, enabling modulation of reaction conditions in a metal salt-based treatment process. The precursor's molar proportion relative to the metal salt is constrained to balance hydrolysis kinetics and acid availability without destabilizing the treatment chemistry.
mechanism_raw: Using a water-soluble partial ester of a polycarboxylic acid that hydrolyzes into the free acid or its salt, providing a controlled release of acidity. This allows precise modulation of the tanning environment while maintaining compatibility with chromium (III) salts, enabling optimized reaction kinetics and product consistency.

abstract: An ultrasonic probe particularly suitable for ultrasonic diagnostic equipments of the electronic scanning type is made up of a multiplicity of piezoelectric transducer elements, each in the shape of a rectangular plate with electrode films coated on both sides, arranged in a row at intervals and an acoustic impedance matching layer placed on the row of the transducer elements. The width-to-thickness ratio of each piezoelectric plate takes a value not greater than 0.8 and preferably between 0.4 and 0.7 so that the plate can vibrate in width expansion mode. It is highly preferable that the impedance matching layer has a laminated structure given by two layers which are different in acoustic impedance of the respective materials and individually have definite thicknesses.
problem: Optimizing ultrasonic transducer performance for diagnostic equipment by enabling efficient vibration modes and acoustic energy transmission.
constraint: The width-to-thickness ratio must remain within 0.4–0.7 to ensure stable width expansion mode operation, and the impedance layers must have precisely controlled thicknesses to match the acoustic properties of the transducer and target medium.
mechanism: Configuring a vibrating element with a geometric aspect ratio to induce a specific vibration mode, combined with a multi-layer interface system having distinct acoustic properties to minimize energy loss at boundaries. The aspect ratio and layer thicknesses are constrained to ensure stable mode operation and impedance matching between the vibrating element and a target medium.
mechanism_raw: Designing piezoelectric plates with a width-to-thickness ratio ≤0.8 to induce width expansion vibration mode, combined with a two-layer acoustic impedance matching system. The layered materials with distinct impedances reduce energy loss at interfaces, improving signal fidelity and directional control of ultrasonic waves.

abstract: A novel and industrially feasible method of producing microcapsules, which comprises dissolving an oil-and-fat in an organic solvent by heating, dispersing a core material in the resultant solution, cooling the dispersion with stirring to coacervate the oil-and-fat on the core material, and separating and drying the resultant encapsulated particulate products.
problem: Producing microcapsules with uniform encapsulation of core materials using a scalable, industrially feasible method.
constraint: The cooling rate and stirring intensity must be carefully balanced to ensure uniform coacervation without disrupting particle integrity or causing premature solidification of the encapsulating material.
mechanism: Inducing phase separation of a dispersed material through controlled thermal and mechanical energy input during a coacervation process. The cooling rate and agitation intensity are balanced to ensure uniform shell formation around core particles without disrupting structural integrity or causing premature solidification of the encapsulating material.
mechanism_raw: Dissolving an oil/fat in an organic solvent, dispersing the core material, then cooling the mixture with stirring to induce coacervation. The controlled cooling causes the oil/fat to phase-separate and form a cohesive shell around the core particles, which are then separated and dried to yield encapsulated products.

abstract: A method and apparatus for continuous supervision of both a vehicle's speed and deceleration over a track, provides overspeed detection in one set of conditions and under-deceleration detection under other conditions. The apparatus does not provide automatic driving, but is used in conjunction with either automatic driving equipment or manual driving of the vehicle. The process involved comprises the steps of transmitting to the vehicle an exit speed, defined as a speed limit to be observed on leaving a particular block section of the track upon which the vehicle travels. The exit speed is stored in the vehicle, and comparisons are made with a stored exit speed for the preceding block section. The process further includes a continuous measurement of both actual speed and deceleration of the vehicle, and provides for initiation of emergency braking dependent upon the results of the comparison and measurement steps. Specifically, where the present exit speed equals or exceeds the exit speed of the preceding section, emergency braking is initiated subsequent to a predetermined delay where the actual speed exceeds the exit speed for the particular block section. Where the present exit speed is less than the exit speed for the preceding section, emergency braking is initiated when the measured deceleration is less than a predetermined deceleration.
problem: Ensuring vehicle safety by dynamically monitoring speed and deceleration to trigger emergency braking when deviations from safe operating parameters occur.
constraint: The system must reconcile real-time speed/deceleration measurements with stored exit speed data to avoid false triggers while maintaining responsiveness to genuine safety risks.
mechanism: Comparing real-time operational parameters of a moving system against stored reference thresholds using conditional logic to determine actuation timing. The system delays or initiates corrective action based on whether the reference thresholds are increasing or decreasing, ensuring responsiveness to genuine deviations while avoiding false triggers.
mechanism_raw: Transmitting and storing exit speeds for sequential track sections, then continuously comparing the vehicle's actual speed and deceleration against these thresholds. Emergency braking is initiated based on conditional logic: delayed braking if speed exceeds the current exit speed (when exit speeds are non-decreasing), or immediate braking if deceleration falls below a minimum threshold (when exit speeds are decreasing).

abstract: A die closing unit for an injection molding machine having either the stationary die carrier plate or the movable die carrier plate so connected to the tie rods, or to the piston rods, respectively, that the space between the two die carrier plates is adjustable, the adjustment mechanism including adjustment sleeves and rotationally coupled adjustment nuts seated on threaded tie rod portions, a clamping flange creating a rigid tie rod connection by abutting the sleeves and by clamping their threads, the sleeves having drive teeth for synchronous adjustment rotation after release by means of either an internally geared adjustment ring or a gear chain, with the aid of a drive arbor.
problem: Adjusting the spacing between die carrier plates in injection molding machines to enable precise, repeatable die alignment while maintaining structural rigidity.
constraint: The adjustment mechanism must balance ease of rotation (via drive teeth and gears) with sufficient clamping force from the flange to prevent loosening under operational stresses.
mechanism: Using mechanically coupled adjustment elements with synchronized rotational input to maintain uniform spacing between opposing surfaces. A clamping mechanism applies compressive force to secure the adjusted positions, balancing ease of adjustment with resistance to loosening under operational stresses.
mechanism_raw: Using threaded tie rods with adjustment sleeves and rotationally coupled nuts, combined with a clamping flange that rigidly secures the sleeves. Drive teeth on the sleeves enable synchronized rotation via a gear ring or chain, allowing simultaneous adjustment of multiple tie rods to maintain uniform spacing and alignment.

abstract: A flash evaporator to be used for purposes such as distilling sea water has a series of evaporator stages in which vapor derived from liquid flowing through the successive evaporator stages is condensed to form a distillate. A wall structure situated in each evaporated stage defines therein an elongated narrow gap the length of which is substantially greater than the width of each evaporator stage with this gap forming an orifice through which the liquid is compelled to issue while flowing from an inlet to an outlet of each evaporator stage. Between the inlet and the gap in each evaporator stage the wall structure defines an upstream flow path the cross section of which decreases from the inlet toward the gap. From the gap toward the outlet of each stage the wall structure defines a downstream flow path the cross section of which increases from the gap toward the outlet. Each evaporator stage has an interior space communicating with the liquid flowing along the downstream flow path to receive vapor therefrom, and in this space is situated a condenser for condensing the vapor, this condenser being situated at an elevation lower than the free surface of the liquid flowing along the downstream flow path. The vapor flowing toward the condenser in each stage is directed centrifugally against the inner surface of an outer shell of each stage so that any liquid droplets entrained with the vapor deposit themselves against the inner surface of the shell, and troughs are carried by the inner surface of the shell to collect the droplets so that the latter cannot travel with the vapor to the condenser.
problem: Efficiently separating vapor and liquid phases in a multi-stage flash evaporator while minimizing droplet carryover to the condenser.
constraint: Balancing flow velocity and pressure gradients to maintain efficient vapor generation while ensuring droplet separation without excessive energy loss.
mechanism: Accelerate liquid flow through a converging-diverging path to generate vapor, then direct the vapor centrifugally against a surface where geometric features collect entrained droplets, preventing their transport to a downstream condensation zone.
mechanism_raw: The evaporator stages use converging-diverging flow paths and a narrow gap to accelerate liquid flow, creating vapor. The vapor is directed centrifugally against the shell's inner surface, where troughs collect entrained droplets, preventing them from reaching the condenser. This geometric and centrifugal separation ensures clean vapor condensation.

abstract: A fluid valve apparatus having a stationary semicylindrical member through which a fluid port extends is characterized by a valve band which is flexibly movable from a first, closed, to a second, open, position in response to an actuating force. In the closed position, the flexible valve band is pulled taut about the surface of the cylindrical member and covers the fluid port. When closed, the valve band is subjected to a compressive force on the first surface thereof adjacent to the stationary cylindrical member and a tensile force on a second surface thereof. While in the open position, in which the fluid port is uncovered, the flexible valve band is subjected only to a tensile force tangentially directed relative to the surface of the cylindrical member. A rocker actuating member is operably connected to the flexible valve band and transmits an actuating force thereto by pivoting about a pivot point instantaneously defined by the intersection of the tangential direction of the tensile force on the flexible valve band and a second direction tangentially disposed relative to the surface of the cylindrical member.
problem: Creating a fluid valve that transitions between open and closed states with controlled force distribution to avoid mechanical failure or leakage.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the valve band under alternating compressive and tensile forces while ensuring smooth pivoting of the rocker arm.
mechanism: Tension a flexible band around a cylindrical member to close a port, and use a pivoting lever whose pivot point is defined by the intersection of tangential force directions to translate actuation into controlled flexing of the band, dynamically shifting compressive and tensile forces during operation.
mechanism_raw: A flexible valve band is tensioned around a cylindrical member to close a port. A rocker arm pivots at a point defined by the intersection of tangential force directions, translating actuation into controlled flexing of the band. The compressive and tensile forces on the band shift dynamically during operation, enabling precise valve control.
residual_terms: ["flexible band", "cylindrical member", "rocker arm", "tangential force directions", "compressive and tensile forces"]

abstract: Vibration isolated sensor apparatus with minimized air stream obstruction for external mounting on an aircraft. An elongated multi-gimbaled sensor assembly disposed within a cylindrical pod housing for extension along a longitudinal axis of an aircraft is resiliently supported for vibration isolation by a circumferential array of cantilevered longitudinally-extending leaf springs. By actuation of crank arms at the supported ends of the leaf springs, the direction and extent of such resilient support can be made to match g forces created by maneuvering of the aircraft, thereby maintaining minimal radial-wise spring travel clearance-way and minimal transverse section size.
problem: Isolating a sensor from aircraft vibrations while adapting to dynamic g-forces during maneuvers without compromising sensor alignment or airflow.
constraint: Achieving real-time adjustment of spring orientation to match varying g-forces without introducing mechanical lag or excessive component size.
mechanism: Support a sensor with cantilevered flexible elements and use adjustable linkages to reorient the flexible elements in real-time to align with varying acceleration forces, minimizing transverse displacement and profile while maintaining vibration isolation and airflow.
mechanism_raw: Cantilevered leaf springs support the sensor, and crank arms adjust the spring orientation to align with g-forces. This dynamically minimizes radial spring travel and transverse profile, maintaining vibration isolation while reducing airflow obstruction.

abstract: This invention is concerned with a method of tanning or retanning leather or pelts by treating them with an aqueous liquor containing water-soluble oligourethanes having ionic groups. The oligourethanes have a molecular weight of from 300 to 20,000 and they may be methylolated. The oligourethanes may be water-soluble owing to their ionic groups or they may contain hydrophilic segments to aid in their solubility in the aqueous liquor. The liquor may also contain up to an equal amount of formaldehyde or compounds which split off formaldehyde.
reason: The patent describes a chemical composition (oligourethanes with ionic groups) for leather tanning rather than a functional mechanism. The 'mechanism' is limited to material solubility and chemical interaction, which is specific to the tanning process and not a transferable causal operation.

abstract: An immobilized glucose isomerase is obtained by mixing microbial cells of the microorganism having glucose isomerase activity with an aqueous solution of a natural water insoluble gel-forming substance. Glucose is isomerized to fructose by contacting an aqueous solution of glucose with said immobilized glucose isomerase more favorably than the usual isomerization method.
problem: Improving the efficiency and reusability of glucose isomerase in converting glucose to fructose by immobilizing the enzyme on a solid support.
constraint: Balancing gel porosity and mechanical stability to ensure sufficient substrate access while maintaining structural integrity during repeated use.
mechanism: Mix active biocatalyst-containing cells with a water-insoluble gel-forming substance to create an immobilized biocatalyst where the gel matrix physically traps the cells while allowing substrate diffusion, enhancing reaction efficiency and enabling reuse.
mechanism_raw: Microbial cells containing glucose isomerase are mixed with a water-insoluble gel-forming substance, creating an immobilized biocatalyst. The gel matrix physically traps the cells while allowing substrate diffusion, enhancing reaction efficiency and enabling enzyme reuse.

abstract: A foundation for supporting a superstructure in which the foundation comprises precast concrete beams mounted on and supported by at least two non-precast pier elements. Each of the pier elements is poured in place in specially formed vertical holes in the ground at the construction site and have an axially aligned reinforcing rod which extends upward above the top of the pier. Each precast beam has at least two spaced-apart apertures which overlie the respective pier elements. In one embodiment, these apertures receive the reinforcing rods of the pier elements when the beam is mounted upon the piers during construction, and cementing material is introduced into each aperture to effect a bond between the beam and each pier element associated therewith. Each precast beam is thereby supported in an upright position with the beam parallel to the ground. In another embodiment, a tubular pedestal is affixed to the top of the pier and the reinforcing rod of the pier extends into but not above the tubular pedestal. The beams are mounted on the pedestal with a beam aperture positioned above each pedestal and a second reinforcing rod is inserted into and positioned to extend between each beam aperture and its associated pedestal. A cementing material is introduced into the sleeve aperture and pedestal to bond each beam and pier elements associated therewith together. It is preferred that hollow sleeves be used to define each of the apertures formed in the beams.
problem: Creating a secure structural connection between precast and cast-in-place concrete elements while maintaining alignment and load-bearing capacity during construction.
constraint: The system must balance precise alignment of apertures with pier elements during assembly, while ensuring the cementitious bond achieves sufficient strength without compromising the structural integrity of either component.
mechanism: Using apertures in one structural element that receive extending reinforcement from another element, combined with a bonding medium introduced into the apertures to form a monolithic connection. The alignment of apertures with the reinforcement elements ensures positional stability, while the bonding medium transfers loads between the elements.
mechanism_raw: Using apertures in precast beams that receive reinforcing rods from in-situ piers, combined with cementitious bonding material introduced into the apertures to form a monolithic connection. The alignment of apertures with pier elements ensures positional stability, while the cementing material transfers loads between the beam and pier.

abstract: The invention relates to a method of and an installation for the heat treatment of steels, such as heating before hardening, annealing, and carburization, which heat treatment is carried out in a furnace in the presence of a protection or carbon-enrichment atmosphere which flows continuously through the furnace, the atmosphere being obtained by the mixture, before its introduction into the furnace, of a carrier gas including nitrogen and possibly hydrogen, and an active gas constituted by a hydrocarbon, the mixture containing at least 0.2% by volume of hydrocarbon. The active gas may be constituted by ethylene, ethane or acetylene and the treatment is carried out at a temperature between 850.degree. and 1050.degree. C. The installation includes a device for analyzing the atmosphere at the furnace outlet, this analyzer actuating a regulating valve for the inlet flow of active gas through a servo-mechanism, in dependence on the proportion of carbon in the treated steel.
problem: Maintaining a consistent protective or carbon-enrichment atmosphere composition during steel heat treatment processes to ensure uniform material properties.
constraint: The system must maintain a minimum hydrocarbon concentration (≥0.2% by volume) and operate within a specific temperature range (850–1050°C) while responding quickly enough to prevent deviations that could compromise the heat treatment quality.
mechanism: A closed-loop feedback system where an outlet sensor measures a process parameter in the exhaust stream, dynamically adjusting the inlet flow of an active constituent via a regulated valve. This ensures the process atmosphere remains within target parameters despite variations in material composition or process conditions.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop feedback system where an outlet gas analyzer measures carbon content in the furnace exhaust, dynamically adjusting the inlet flow of active gas (hydrocarbon) via a servo-regulated valve. This ensures the atmosphere composition remains within target parameters despite variations in steel composition or process conditions.
residual_terms: ["closed-loop feedback system", "outlet sensor", "exhaust stream", "inlet flow", "active constituent", "regulated valve", "process atmosphere", "target parameters"]

abstract: A filling material for pillows, cushions and upholstery or the like is cut from a soft plastic foam material in the shape of a plurality of short four-sided rods, each having a body of polygonal shape. The bodies are each cut in such a manner that all side surfaces form surfaces of cut to reduce lumping and tearing of the bodies. Each body is formed with its height smaller than its breadth and its length in the range of one and a half times to five times the breadth, which breadth does not exceed a value of 10 mm. The bodies are each further cut to be rhomboidal in at least transverse cross section to provide surfaces joined at edges to form acute angles so as to enhance resilient properties thereof.
problem: Designing a resilient filling material for pillows and upholstery that minimizes clumping, tearing, and uneven distribution while maintaining comfort and durability.
constraint: The foam dimensions must balance resilience (via acute angles and aspect ratios) against manufacturing feasibility, while the size limitation (≤10mm breadth) ensures compatibility with standard upholstery applications.
mechanism: Shaping resilient elements with non-uniform transverse cross-sections and specific length-to-breadth ratios to create acute-angle edges that enhance resilience through controlled deformation. The geometric configuration distributes stress evenly and reduces inter-particle friction that causes clumping.
mechanism_raw: Shaping foam rods with rhomboidal transverse cross-sections and specific length-to-breadth ratios (1.5–5x breadth, ≤10mm breadth) to create acute-angle edges that enhance resilience through controlled deformation. The geometric configuration distributes stress evenly and reduces inter-particle friction that causes clumping.
residual_terms: ["resilient elements", "transverse cross-sections", "length-to-breadth ratios", "acute-angle edges", "controlled deformation", "stress distribution", "inter-particle friction", "clumping"]

abstract: A dart is made with a body that breaks away from the point upon impact and/or vanes or flights that break away from the body upon impact. The objective is to minimize the size of the embedded dart in a target so that subsequent darts can be thrown to the high score area of the prior darts. The breakaway is accomplished by relative movement upon impact between point and body and by the force of gravity breaking apart a magnetic hold between body and point. Springs are also used to separate the point and other parts and/or to hold the point in projected position during flight and to allow telescoping upon impact.
problem: Minimizing the embedded size of darts in a target to allow subsequent throws to hit high-score areas without obstruction from prior darts.
constraint: The retention forces must be strong enough to maintain component integrity during flight but weak enough to allow separation upon impact, requiring precise calibration of magnetic, spring, or gravitational forces.
mechanism: Designing projectiles with breakaway components that separate upon impact via inertial forces overcoming retention mechanisms. The separation is triggered by impact forces, which overcome the retention mechanisms (magnetic hold, spring tension, gravitational retention) that keep parts attached during flight.
mechanism_raw: Designing darts with breakaway components (point, vanes) that separate upon impact via gravity, springs, or magnetic release. The separation is triggered by inertial forces during impact, which overcome the retention mechanisms (magnetic hold, spring tension) that keep parts attached during flight.
residual_terms: ["projectiles", "breakaway components", "inertial forces", "retention mechanisms", "magnetic hold", "spring tension", "gravitational retention", "impact forces"]

abstract: A metallized plastic molding comprises a plastic substrate, a primer layer having a gel percentage of at least 80% and a swelling degree of 20% or less deposited on said substrate and a metallic film deposited on the primer layer. The metallized plastic molding is prepared by coating a plastic substrate with a primer forming material containing at least one compound having a molecular weight of 150 - 2000 and containing at least two polymerizable unsaturated groups in one molecule, curing the primer forming material so that it has a gel percentage of at least 80% and a swelling degree of 20% or less to form a primer layer and then depositing a metallic film layer by a dry type method on the primer layer.
problem: Achieving strong adhesion between a metallic film and a plastic substrate in metallized moldings without delamination or degradation during processing or use.
constraint: The primer must balance cross-linking density (to achieve ≥80% gel) with flexibility (to avoid brittleness), while the molecular weight range (150–2000) ensures compatibility with both the plastic substrate and the metallic film deposition process.
mechanism: Depositing an intermediate layer containing polymerizable compounds that cure to form a highly cross-linked network. This creates a stable, low-swelling interface that enhances adhesion between dissimilar material layers during deposition processes.
mechanism_raw: Depositing a primer layer containing polymerizable unsaturated compounds (MW 150–2000) that cure to form a highly cross-linked network (≥80% gel percentage, ≤20% swelling). This creates a stable, low-swelling interface that enhances adhesion between the plastic and metal layers during dry deposition processes.
residual_terms: ["intermediate layer", "polymerizable compounds", "cross-linked network", "gel percentage", "swelling", "adhesion", "dissimilar material layers", "deposition processes"]

abstract: A re-usable envelope having a zip closure which can be locked closed by a sealing device. The sealing device is of plastics material, one part being mounted to the envelope and the other part being engageable therewith, the sealing device only being operable by breaking said other part. The zip tag includes a part for manual engagement to facilitate closing of the sealing device.
problem: Need to provide a reusable closure for an envelope that is both convenient to use and tamper-evident, so that unauthorized opening is detectable.
constraint: The seal must be secure enough to prevent casual opening, yet the breakable component must be reliably destroyed upon opening, while the underlying zip closure remains reusable.
mechanism: A dual-component closure system combining a reusable continuous fastening mechanism with a single-use destructible security element; the destructible element is permanently affixed to one surface and engages with a complementary structure on another surface, such that opening the closure requires breaking the destructible element, thereby providing visual evidence of tampering while preserving the reusable fastening mechanism.
mechanism_raw: A two-part mechanical seal where one part is permanently mounted to the envelope and the other part engages with it; the engaging part is designed to be destructively broken to open, making tampering evident. The zip closure allows reuse of the envelope body while the breakable seal provides single-use security.

abstract: Drafts of preselected weight are sliced into a preselected number of slices by passing the material to be sliced through a curtain of radiation to measure the density of the material, and this measurement is used to calculate the length of each draft, which measurement is stored and subsequently read out to control the operation of a stepping hydroelectric motor which pushes the material through a cutting station at the proper speed.
problem: Need to slice a draft of material into a preselected number of slices, each of a preselected weight, despite variations in material density.
constraint: The system must account for real-time variations in material density to maintain consistent slice weight, requiring closed-loop feedback from density measurement to cutting speed control.
mechanism: A closed-loop control system that measures a material property (density) in real-time as the material moves through a processing zone, uses the measured property to calculate a target dimension (length) for discrete segments, stores the calculated target, and adjusts the material transport speed accordingly so that each segment has a predetermined mass despite variations in the measured property.
mechanism_raw: A radiation curtain measures the density of the material as it passes through; this density measurement is used to calculate the required length of each slice, which is stored and then used to control a stepping motor that drives the material through a cutting station at a speed that produces slices of the correct weight.

abstract: Tetradecahydroundecaborate compounds, MB.sub.11 H.sub.14, wherein M represents a monovalent cation are prepared by the reaction of the corresponding octahydroborate compounds, MB.sub.3 H.sub.8, with boron trifluoride. The reaction is carried out at a temperature of 100.degree. C. to 120.degree. C., preferably in an inert solvent medium.
reason: This patent describes a specific chemical synthesis method for producing a particular class of boron hydride compounds. The mechanism is a standard chemical reaction (reacting octahydroborate with boron trifluoride at a controlled temperature) and does not represent a generalizable problem-solving principle that can be transferred to other fields.

abstract: Thermostat metal compositions are disclosed which have a substantially uniform flexivity over a broad range of operating temperatures and which respond rapidly to changes in ambient temperatures. These results are achieved by using, as an intermediate layer, a major portion by volume of a thermostat metal that has a thermal conductivity in excess of 2,400 BTU in/ft.sup.2 hr.degree. F.
problem: Need thermostat metal compositions that maintain uniform flexivity over a broad temperature range and respond rapidly to ambient temperature changes.
constraint: The intermediate layer must have a thermal conductivity exceeding a specific threshold to achieve the desired uniform flexivity and rapid response, while still being compatible with the overall thermostat metal structure.
mechanism: A multi-layer composite structure with an intermediate layer having thermal conductivity above a threshold value, positioned between two active layers, such that heat transfer through the intermediate layer ensures uniform thermal response across the entire structure, enabling consistent and rapid flexural actuation over a broad temperature range.
mechanism_raw: An intermediate layer with high thermal conductivity (>2400 BTU in/ft² hr°F) is incorporated into the thermostat metal composition, ensuring rapid and uniform heat transfer across the material so that the entire structure responds consistently and quickly to temperature changes.

abstract: A short sleeve is provided for telescoping over a switch toggle and an elongated lever arm has one end thereof pivotally attached to one end of the sleeve for angular displacement relative thereto about an axis extending transversely of the sleeve and the lever arm. The sleeve and lever arm include coacting structure operative to releasably retain the lever arm in predetermined angular position relative to the sleeve with the arm defining an endwise outward extension of the aforementioned one end of the sleeve, the other end of the sleeve being open for telescoping over an associated switch toggle.
problem: Need to extend the operating lever of a switch toggle to make it more accessible, while maintaining a secure and releasable connection.
constraint: The lever arm must be releasably retained in a fixed angular position during operation to prevent slippage, yet the entire assembly must be easily removable from the switch toggle when needed.
mechanism: An extendable lever assembly comprising a sleeve that coaxially receives a base actuator element and a lever arm pivotally coupled to the sleeve; a coacting retention interface between the sleeve and lever arm selectively fixes the angular orientation of the lever arm relative to the sleeve during operation, while allowing axial removal of the entire assembly from the base actuator element when the retention interface is disengaged.
mechanism_raw: A sleeve telescopes over the switch toggle, and a lever arm is pivotally attached to the sleeve at one end. Coacting retention structure between the sleeve and lever arm holds the arm in a predetermined angular position, with the arm extending endwise outward from the sleeve end, effectively lengthening the toggle lever while remaining removable.

abstract: In a method of producing iron by direct reduction of the ore, compaction into agglomerates and fusion, where the ore is reduced by a gaseous process with pre-reduction to monoxide FeO at 1000.degree. C, followed by a final reduction at 700.degree.C. The resultant powder is compacted into agglomerates and dumped, in successive loads after each pour, into an induction melting furnace and melted by contact and mixing with a preexistent charge of liquid metal. An amount equivalent to the newly-melted charge is poured into a refining ladle, after skimming off the slag.
problem: Efficiently melting reduced iron powder while minimizing slag contamination and thermal shock during direct iron production.
constraint: Balancing the rate of powder addition and furnace temperature to maintain consistent molten metal quality while preventing excessive slag entrapment or thermal stress.
mechanism: Sequentially introducing a material into a molten bath to enable controlled direct-contact melting through mixing, followed by removing surface impurities and transferring a measured volume of the molten product.
mechanism_raw: Sequential addition of compacted powder into an induction furnace containing a preexistent molten metal charge, enabling controlled melting through direct contact and mixing, followed by skimming slag and ladling an equivalent volume of molten metal.

abstract: Methods and apparatus for mounting a device and adjusting its position employ a mount for the device and provide spaced isthmi located on a predetermined axis. The portion of the mount between the spaced isthmi is rendered tiltable about the mentioned axis. The device is mounted on the tiltable portion and its position is adjustable by tilting such portion about the mentioned axis.
problem: Precisely adjusting the position of a mounted device while maintaining structural stability during movement.
constraint: Ensuring the isthmi geometry provides sufficient structural support to the tiltable segment while enabling smooth, repeatable tilting without backlash or mechanical play.
mechanism: Using spaced structural elements on a pivot axis to create a tiltable segment of a mount, allowing controlled angular adjustment of a device by pivoting the segment about the axis while maintaining structural support.
mechanism_raw: Using spaced isthmi on a predetermined axis to create a tiltable segment of the mount, allowing controlled angular adjustment of the device by pivoting the segment about the axis.

abstract: The presence and absence of an inserted weft yarn are sensed respectively by, in moving a sensor body having an aperture opening externally of the body and two contacts located in the aperture and engaged with each other by an elastic force from a first position in which the inserted weft yarn is passed through the aperture during insertion into a second position in which the inserted weft yarn is taken out from the aperture by disengaging the contacts, sensing the contacts being disengaged and remaining engaged.
problem: Reliably detecting the presence or absence of a moving inserted weft yarn during textile manufacturing.
constraint: Maintaining consistent elastic force and contact alignment to ensure reliable disengagement/engagement without false triggers from yarn movement or environmental vibrations.
mechanism: Employing a sensor with an aperture and two elastically biased contacts that disengage when a moving element passes through the aperture during insertion, and re-engage when the element is withdrawn, mechanically sensing the element's position.
mechanism_raw: Employing a sensor body with an aperture and two elastically biased contacts that disengage when the yarn passes through the aperture during insertion, and re-engage when the yarn is withdrawn, mechanically sensing the yarn's position.

abstract: A transfer tube and seal structure for a hydraulic unit for connecting a pair of flow passages in a housing to flow passages in a valve plate which is floatingly mounted and engageable against a cylinder block in an axial piston hydraulic unit with ports in the valve plate communicating with axially-extending bores in the cylinder block, each of which carries a piston movably mounted therein. A transfer tube is loosely positioned in coaxial flow passages to span the gap between the valve plate and the housing and maintain a sealed flow relation therebetween while permitting movement of the valve plate relative to the housing. The transfer tubes each have an outwardly-opening groove adjacent each end thereof mounting a metallic seal ring and with the outer face of the seal ring being of substantially reduced width for a limited area of sealing contact with the walls of the flow passages.
problem: Maintaining a sealed fluid flow path between a floating valve plate and a housing in a hydraulic unit while accommodating relative movement.
constraint: Balancing the seal ring's flexibility and contact width to maintain pressure integrity under dynamic movement while minimizing wear and leakage.
mechanism: Positioning a transfer element loosely within coaxial flow passages to span a gap between a movable component and a housing, using seal rings with reduced-width outer faces to create limited-area sealing contact that accommodates relative movement.
mechanism_raw: Positioning a transfer tube loosely within coaxial flow passages to span the gap between the valve plate and housing, using metallic seal rings with reduced-width outer faces to create limited-area sealing contact that accommodates movement.

abstract: To defrost a selected evaporator, in a system including at least two evaporators, the system condenser is isolated from the compressor and the selected evaporator receives hot, compressed refrigerant vapor directly from the compressor. The liquid refrigerant formed in the defrosting evaporator flows to the other evaporators in the system to permit them to continue in the refrigeration mode. A pressure regulated control system is provided which causes excess liquid refrigerant in the defrosted evaporator to be pumped out of that evaporator before the evaporator is reconnected to the compressor suction line. In a preferred embodiment, each evaporator includes a coil having a plurality of circuits connected between its inlet and outlet and each circuit is disposed in a horizontal plane at a different elevation from any of the other circuits. During the defrost cycle, hot compressed refrigerant vapor flows through either the normal inlet or outlet of the evaporator after passing through a hot gas inlet line which is arranged to pre-heat the lowermost circuits of the evaporator, thereby equalizing the defrosting rate of circuits located at different elevations.
problem: Defrosting a selected evaporator in a multi-evaporator refrigeration system without disrupting the operation of other evaporators.
constraint: Equalizing the defrosting rate across evaporator circuits at different elevations by pre-heating lowermost circuits via hot gas flow, ensuring uniform melting without overcooling or refrigerant starvation in non-defrosting circuits.
mechanism: Isolating a heat exchanger and directing heated fluid directly to a target unit, allowing byproduct liquid formed during heating to flow to other units, while a pressure-regulated system removes excess liquid before reconnecting the target unit to a suction path.
mechanism_raw: Isolating the condenser and directing hot compressed refrigerant vapor directly to the target evaporator, allowing liquid refrigerant formed during defrosting to flow to other evaporators, while a pressure-regulated system pumps out excess liquid before reconnecting the evaporator to the suction line.

abstract: Improved apparatus for forming hollow cylindrical pipes of reinforced concrete wherein the pipe is formed in a vertical position and the principle components for forming the pipe comprise a bottom pallet and saddle, an outer jacket, a core positioned concentrically in spaced relationship within the outer jacket and a reinforcing cage positioned between the center core and the jacket and sealing means are provided for sealing the relationship between the bottom pallet, the outer jacket and the inner core. Use is made of movable elastic seals on the lower ends of the outer jacket and the core. The seals can be expanded inwardly toward the pallet by means of a positive pressure until the concrete has been poured into the form and compacted by vibration. Negative pressure is then utilized to withdraw the elastic seals from the formed pipe and the inner core and outer jacket are subsequently removed from the green pipe.
problem: Forming and releasing hollow cylindrical concrete pipes without damaging the structure during the molding process.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the green pipe while allowing reversible sealing and release of the mold components.
mechanism: Using a pressure differential to reversibly expand and contract resilient sealing elements against a forming surface during material deposition and densification, enabling controlled engagement and disengagement of mold components from the formed structure.
mechanism_raw: Using positive pressure to expand elastic seals inward against a pallet during concrete pouring and compaction, then applying negative pressure to withdraw the seals, enabling controlled separation of the mold components from the formed pipe.

abstract: A chip breaker includes an abutment surface having geometry generally corresponding in profile to the geometry on the cutting edge of the associated thread chaser to permit such abutment surface to be uniformly spaced from respective roots and crests of the thread chaser and in close proximity thereto when the chaser and breaker are clampingly juxtaposed. The juxtaposed or trailing surface of the chip breaker has angularly biased, parallel grooves therein to deliver coolant past the chaser body and then into the cutting area along the respective flanks of the chip breaker and chaser geometry.
problem: Managing chip removal and coolant delivery in precision cutting operations to prevent tool wear and surface damage.
constraint: Balancing close proximity of the chip breaker to the cutting edge with unobstructed coolant delivery and chip evacuation.
mechanism: Matching a contacting surface geometry to a cutting edge profile to maintain uniform spacing, combined with directional flow channels on a trailing surface to guide fluid delivery into a cutting zone along adjacent surfaces.
mechanism_raw: Matching the abutment surface geometry to the cutting edge profile to maintain uniform spacing, combined with angularly biased parallel grooves on the trailing surface to direct coolant flow into the cutting area along the flanks.
residual_terms: ["contacting surface geometry", "cutting edge profile", "uniform spacing", "directional flow channels", "trailing surface"]

abstract: An apparatus for controlling the generation of sound in the loudspeakers of intercommunicating telephone sets in response to pulse-code modulated speech signals from the microphones of the telephone sets. A digital comparator compares speech signals received from each microphone and delivers a binary control signal to a dividing circuit through which the speech signal having the highest maximum value passes. The dividing circuit responds to the control signal by dividing the speech signal by a desired factor. A loudspeaker, contained in the same telephone set as the microphone from which the speech signal having the highest maximum value emanated, is in circuit with a control unit. The same binary control signal causes the control unit to suppress the generation of sound in the loudspeaker.
problem: Preventing acoustic feedback and interference in intercommunicating telephone systems during simultaneous speech transmission.
constraint: Real-time signal processing and suppression without disrupting the communication of other participants.
mechanism: Comparing signals from multiple input transducers, selecting the signal with the highest amplitude, attenuating it by a scaling factor, and inhibiting output generation from the associated transducer to prevent feedback loops.
mechanism_raw: Digitally comparing speech signals from multiple microphones, selecting the signal with the highest maximum value, dividing it by a factor, and suppressing sound generation in the loudspeaker associated with that signal to avoid feedback loops.

abstract: Herbicidal tetrahydroindazoles of the formula: ##STR1## where Q is chlorine, bromine or methyl; PA1 X is hydrogen, methyl, chlorine, methoxy, ethoxy, or bromine; PA1 Y is hydrogen, methyl, chlorine or methoxy; PA1 V is hydrogen, methyl or chlorine; and PA1 Z is hydrogen or methyl; with the proviso that PA2 (a) when Y and Z are methyl, X must be hydrogen, methyl, chlorine, or bromine; PA2 (b) when Y is hydrogen or chlorine and V is hydrogen or chlorine and Z is hydrogen, X must be hydrogen, methyl, or ethoxy; and PA2 (c) at least one of X, Y, V or Z must be hydrogen.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical compound with herbicidal properties. While the structure-activity relationship is scientifically significant, it does not describe a generalizable problem-solving mechanism applicable across different fields.

abstract: A single-control lever mounted in a pivot assembly is movable in an arc in first and second directions in one plane to impart motion through a cam arrangement to a first push rod and cable assembly so that the first push rod and cable assembly moves equal amounts in the same direction upon movement of the lever in either the first or second direction. The same single-lever is movable in an arc in third and fourth directions in a second plane normal to the first plane to impart longitudinal motion to a second push rod and cable assembly affixed to the pivot assembly. A plate member affixed to the bracket supporting the pivot assembly limits travel of the single-control lever to a predetermined path.
problem: Controlling multiple mechanical outputs (e.g., push rods) with a single input lever across orthogonal planes.
constraint: Ensuring precise mechanical linkage between the lever's motion and the push rods while restricting movement to a defined path.
mechanism: Using a pivot-mounted lever with a cam arrangement to convert multi-directional rotational motion into linear displacement of two output assemblies, with a constraint member limiting the lever's motion to a predefined range.
mechanism_raw: Using a pivot-mounted lever with a cam arrangement to translate multi-directional arc motion into linear motion of two push rod assemblies, with a plate member limiting the lever's travel path to a predetermined range.
residual_terms: ["pivot-mounted lever", "cam arrangement", "multi-directional rotational motion", "linear displacement", "constraint member", "predefined range"]

abstract: A boat dock assembled from portable sections hingedly connected to each other and provided with foldable and adjustably extensible leg assemblies. Each section is formed from tread retaining decking members made of extruded metal sections interconnected in close parallel spaced relation by interlocking elements. Pivotally separable half-shell foot elements are connected to the leg assemblies for stabilized support of the dock sections.
problem: Creating a portable, stable boat dock that can adapt to uneven terrain while maintaining structural integrity during assembly and use.
constraint: Balancing portability (lightweight, foldable components) with structural stability (load distribution, terrain adaptability) without compromising the dock's ability to remain assembled under dynamic loads.
mechanism: Modularly connect portable structural segments using articulated joints to enable assembly/disassembly, while adjustable stabilization elements with separable contact points adapt to uneven terrain. Interlocking load-bearing members distribute forces across parallel structural elements, balancing portability with load capacity.
mechanism_raw: Hingedly connecting portable dock sections allows modular assembly and disassembly, while foldable and adjustably extensible leg assemblies with pivotally separable foot elements enable localized stabilization on irregular surfaces. The interlocking decking members distribute load across parallel extruded metal sections, balancing portability with load-bearing capacity.

abstract: A recording medium comprises a photographic plate and an aperture-raster plate parallel to but spaced from the photographic plate. The aperture-raster plate is provided with a honeycombed pattern of small apertures. Light emanating from an illuminated object is directed toward the side of the recording medium provided with the aperture-raster plate, and the constituent light rays pass through the apertures and are registered upon the photographic plate both with respect to intensity and direction. Thereafter, the photographed object is three-dimensionally reproduced by illuminating the recording medium with incoherent light incident upon the recording medium in the direction opposite to that in which the observer of the reproduction views the recording medium.
problem: Capturing three-dimensional spatial information of an object using a two-dimensional recording medium and reconstructing it for viewing.
constraint: Precise alignment between the aperture-raster plate and photographic plate to ensure accurate directional encoding, while maintaining compatibility with incoherent light for practical reconstruction.
mechanism: Spatially filter incoming radiation through a structured aperture array to encode directional information onto a recording medium alongside intensity data. Reconstruct depth cues by projecting radiation in the reverse observation direction, leveraging encoded directional data to recreate parallax effects.
mechanism_raw: A honeycombed aperture-raster plate with small apertures spatially filters incoming light rays, encoding directional information onto a photographic plate alongside intensity data. Reconstruction uses incoherent light projected in the reverse direction of observation, leveraging the encoded directional data to recreate depth cues through parallax and light scattering effects.

abstract: The bimetallic material comprises a laminate of two materials, one having a high coefficient of thermal expansion, one with a low coefficient of thermal expansion. The material with the high coefficient of expansion is a corrosion resisting and heat resisting austenitic chromium-nickel steel, while the material with the low coefficient of expansion is a heat hardenable alloy of iron, nickel, cobalt and titanium and/or aluminium. It is found that this combination of materials gives rise to a bimetallic material capable of heavy duty applications without the disadvantages normally associated with such heavy duty materials.
problem: Creating a durable bimetallic material for heavy-duty applications that avoids thermal stress failure and corrosion issues common in traditional bimetallic systems.
constraint: Matching thermal expansion coefficients and material compatibility between layers to prevent delamination or fatigue failure under cyclic thermal loading.
mechanism: Laminate a high-expansion corrosion-resistant layer with a low-expansion hardenable alloy layer to create a composite that resists cracking under thermal cycling. Differential expansion between layers generates controlled bending or stress distribution, enabling structural resilience in demanding environments.
mechanism_raw: Laminating a high-thermal-expansion corrosion-resistant steel layer with a low-thermal-expansion hardenable iron-nickel-cobalt-titanium/aluminum alloy layer creates a composite that resists cracking under temperature fluctuations. The differential expansion between layers generates controlled bending or stress distribution, enabling structural resilience in demanding environments.

abstract: The present invention involves a high-frequency heating apparatus of the type which comprises a heating chamber for accommodating an object to be heated, a door openably and closably provided for an opening of the heating chamber, a high-frequency energy generator for supplying high-frequency energy to the interior of the heating chamber, a fan for forcibly ventilating the interior of the heating chamber, and a heating chamber air-outlet cooperative with the fan to effect the forcible ventilation for the interior of the heating chamber. Temperature of air flowing out of heating chamber through the heating chamber air-outlet is detected by a temperature sensor to actuate an automatic heating control unit for controlling the supply of high-frequency energy. The apparatus is also provided with a manual heating control unit for manually controlling the heating time. In response to a selective operation of one of the automatic heating control unit and the manual heating control unit, an air flow path changer is actuated to change a part of the flow path of the air for ventilating the interior of the heating chamber.
problem: Automatically controlling high-frequency heating processes to maintain consistent temperature while allowing manual override for specific heating durations.
constraint: Ensuring seamless switching between automatic and manual modes without disrupting the heating process, while maintaining airflow path integrity to avoid uneven heating or overheating.
mechanism: Monitor output conditions via a sensor to trigger automatic adjustment of energy input, while a manual override allows user-defined operation durations. Dynamically reconfigure airflow pathways based on operational mode to optimize heat distribution and cooling efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A temperature sensor monitors airflow exiting the heating chamber, triggering an automatic control unit to adjust high-frequency energy supply. A manual control unit allows user-defined heating times, and an airflow path changer dynamically redirects ventilation routes based on whether automatic or manual mode is active, optimizing heat distribution and cooling efficiency.

abstract: Apparatus for removing underwound yarn wraps from the spindle of a spinning frame, including a carrier member mounted for driven movement along the spinning frame, and a pair of rotating brushes which are independently driven and independently arranged for movement toward and away from the spindles. A non-rotatable brush may also be associated with the carrier member, behind the rotatable brushes, to remove any wraps not removed by the rotatable brushes. A suction source is provided for collecting removed yarn wraps. The carrier member includes floor engaging wheels, and means for engaging rails extending along the spinning frame, and the carrier member permits vertical adjustment of the rail engaging means to facilitate mounting the carrier member on the rails. The apparatus is designed so as not to interfere with the movement of the traverse ring of the spinning frame, or with the fixed structure of the spinning frame during operation of the apparatus or during mounting of the apparatus on the rails. A cut-off switch is provided to engage the end of the spinning frame at the completion of the movement of the apparatus therealong and to stop further movement of the apparatus.
problem: Removing underwound yarn wraps from spinning frame spindles without interfering with the frame's traverse ring or fixed structure during operation or installation.
constraint: Achieving precise positional control and vertical adaptability to accommodate varying spindle heights and frame geometries without mechanical interference during operation.
mechanism: Position a mobile carrier with independently actuated removal elements along guided rails, using vertical adjustment to target specific locations. Independent movement of removal elements avoids collision with moving components, while a debris collection system captures dislodged material and a limit switch halts motion at boundaries.
mechanism_raw: A carrier member with independently driven rotating brushes and a non-rotatable brush moves along rails via floor-engaging wheels and adjustable rail engagement. The independent brush movement and vertical adjustment allow precise targeting of yarn wraps while avoiding collision with the spinning frame's moving components. A suction source collects debris, and a cut-off switch halts movement at the frame's end.
residual_terms: ["mobile carrier", "independently actuated removal elements", "guided rails", "limit switch"]

abstract: In a spark ignition internal combustion engine with power output controlled by a throttle, a throttle switch provides a wide open throttle signal and a knock sensor provides a knock level signal. A normal spark pulse train, corrected for intake manifold vacuum, engine speed and dwell angle, is fed through a shift register which delays each spark pulse by a fixed number of counts. A pulse train generator responsive to crankshaft rotation produces a crankshaft reference angle pulse each fixed number of degrees of crankshaft rotation; and these pulses are counted by the shift register to provide a normal spark timing. First and second up-down counters are responsive to the knock detector, the first up-down counter counting up with excessive knock and being effective to delay the counting of the shift register by a period proportional to its count, the second up-down counter being responsive to the wide open throttle switch to count downward with excessive knock and insert extra pulses between the pulses of the pulse train generator in number proportional to its count to advance spark from the normal setting.
problem: Optimizing spark ignition timing in an internal combustion engine under varying load (throttle) and knock conditions to balance performance and knock suppression.
constraint: Balancing knock suppression (via delayed timing) and engine performance (via advanced timing) while maintaining stable operation across varying load and speed conditions.
mechanism: A dual feedback control system uses two counters to dynamically balance opposing adjustments: one counter increases a delay based on detected knock levels, while another counter advances timing by inserting extra pulses when high-demand conditions are detected. A delay element modulates output timing proportionally to the first counter's value, while the second counter controls pulse insertion to advance timing, creating a dynamic balance between suppression of adverse conditions and operational efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A dual feedback control system uses two up-down counters: one adjusts spark timing delay based on knock levels, and another advances timing by inserting extra pulses when wide-open throttle is detected. The shift register delays spark pulses proportionally to the first counter's count, while the second counter modulates pulse insertion to advance timing, creating a dynamic balance between knock suppression and engine efficiency.

abstract: A juicy, self-basting sausage-like food product is prepared by the following steps: (a) forming a protein binder slurry containing 20 to 32% water, 3 to 8% albumen, 0.5 to 4% caseinate and 0 to 2.5% vegetable protein isolate; (b) adding 3 to 15% vegetable oil to the slurry; (c) vigorously agitating the oil-containing slurry to form a protein-oil emulsion; (d) forming a textured protein mixture containing 30 to 40% cooked gluten, 1 to 14% textured vegetable protein and 0 to 4% water; (e) blending the protein-oil emulsion and the textured protein mixture together; (f) blending 3 to 15% vegetable oil with the combined mixture; (g) shaping the resulting mixture to a desired form; and (h) heating the shaped mixture to set the protein in a stable, physical form, said percents being weight percent based on the total weight of the product.
reason: The patent describes a specific food product formulation and processing steps (e.g., protein binder slurries, emulsification, and heating) tailored to a sausage-like product. While the combination of emulsification and protein matrix formation may retain moisture, the mechanism is tightly coupled to food-specific ingredients and processes, lacking a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: Apparatus and method are disclosed to prevent melted yarn when stopped in a high temperature texturing jet device utilizing high temperature fluid such as steam. The device of this invention is attached to the prior art texturing jet device. The attachment comprises a sleeve around the yarn ejector. The sleeve has at least two orifices communicating with a conduit for high pressure fluid having a valve actuated by a sensor to detect yarn stoppage. The high pressure fluid, such as air, blows the yarn plug and yarn from the texturing jet device. The method comprises sensing yarn stoppage with a sensor and actuating the valve in the high pressure fluid conduit communicating with at least two orifices in the sleeve surrounding at least the down stream portion of the injector and blowing any yarn in the texturing chamber out of the chamber with high pressure fluid.
problem: Preventing damage to yarn (e.g., melting or sticking) in a high-temperature texturing jet device when the yarn stops moving during operation.
constraint: Ensuring rapid and reliable clearing of the yarn without disrupting ongoing operations, while minimizing fluid usage and mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A detection element senses when a moving material stops progressing through a processing chamber. Upon detection, a valve is actuated to release pressurized fluid through orifices surrounding the chamber, creating a fluid jet that clears the blocked material from the chamber without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: A sensor detects yarn stoppage and actuates a valve to release high-pressure fluid (e.g., air) through orifices in a sleeve surrounding the jet. The fluid jet clears the yarn plug from the chamber, automatically resolving the blockage without manual intervention.

abstract: A bimetallic element in which a bimetallic strip of two bands of different metals is wound helically into an elongated body, said body having in its center a free space, the diameter of which is smaller than the thickness of the bimetallic strip and preferably is essentially zero. By winding said elongated body into a helical spring, the outer diameter of which is substantially greater than the outer diameter of the elongated body, an element is obtained that can be used as a thermostatic actuating means in a thermostatic device.
problem: Creating a compact thermostatic actuating element that provides large rotational or linear displacement from thermal expansion in a confined space.
constraint: Achieving significant displacement from minimal thermal expansion while maintaining structural integrity and compactness in the actuator design.
mechanism: A thermally responsive element with differential expansion coefficients is configured in a helical winding geometry that amplifies small linear thermal expansion into larger rotational or axial displacement. The helical configuration converts minimal thermal movement into significant mechanical displacement while maintaining structural integrity in a compact form factor.
mechanism_raw: A bimetallic strip is helically wound into an elongated body with a central free space, then coiled into a spring. The helical winding amplifies the linear thermal expansion of the bimetallic strip into a larger rotational or axial movement, enabling precise actuation in thermostatic devices.
residual_terms: ["thermally responsive element", "differential expansion coefficients", "helical winding geometry", "thermal expansion", "rotational or axial displacement"]

abstract: An X-Y plotter is provided having an automatic pen changer comprising a pen repository, a memory for storing data identifying a pen selected by a user, a plot head for automatically fetching pens from and depositing pens into the repository, a processing means having a routine stored in a read-only-memory for providing head-movement coordinates, and a control means for moving the head to said coordinates, the pen-changing action (fetching and depositing) being performed solely by movement of the head to said coordinates. Deposited pens are automatically capped to prevent drying-out, fetched pens are automatically uncapped prior to use.
problem: Automatically changing tools (e.g., pens) in an X-Y plotter without manual intervention, while preventing tool degradation (e.g., drying out).
constraint: Performing tool changes solely through coordinated head movement and memory-driven positioning, without additional actuators or manual steps, while maintaining tool readiness.
mechanism: A memory stores user-selected tool identities, and a positioning mechanism moves to predefined coordinates to fetch or deposit tools from a repository. The positioning mechanism's movement alone performs tool changes, with automatic capping/uncapping mechanisms ensuring tools remain usable between operations.
mechanism_raw: A memory stores user-selected pen identities, and a plot head moves to predefined coordinates to fetch or deposit pens from a repository. The head's movement alone performs pen changes, with automatic capping/uncapping mechanisms ensuring pens remain usable between operations.

abstract: Processes for the treatment of textile fabrics which comprises applying to the fabrics a finishing agent of the group consisting of (a) phosphoric acid esters of poly(oxyethylene) alkanols and salts thereof having the formulae EQU [R--O--(CH.sub.2 CH.sub.2 O).sub.n ].sub.3 P.dbd.O or ##STR1## OR MIXTURES OF THESE COMPOUNDS, IN WHICH FORMULAE R is a straight-chain alkyl radical having at least 16 and at most 18 carbon atoms, n is an integer of at least 10 and at most 14, and Me is a monovalent metal ion, and (b) monoglycerides and diglycerides of saturated aliphatic straight-chain fatty acids having at least 12 and at most 14 carbon atoms, and (c) mixtures of the said finishing agents at (a), (b) and (c).
reason: The patent describes specific chemical compositions for textile finishing, which are tailored to a narrow application. The mechanism is a chemical interaction (e.g., ester/glyceride coatings) that is not easily transferable to other fields without significant adaptation of the chemical structure.

abstract: There is disclosed a probe assembly suitable for mounting in a pressure vessel and the like which has an elongated probe member with a continuous and unbroken insulation coating that is received within an assembly body. The latter has attachment means to secure the body in an aperture of a pressure vessel. The elongated probe member has an outwardly deflecting radial bend, and reverse and straightening radial bends which are received within and bear against supporting shoulders in the assembly body. The probe has its elongated portions projecting from opposite ends of the body, substantially coaxially. The aforedescribed construction securely retains the probe member within the assembly body, preventing its forced dislodgement therefrom under the pressure within the pressure vessel or misalignment during installation or use while, nevertheless, providing a continuous unbroken electrical insulation, thereby insuring against malfunctions that can occur when process fluids leak into the assembly body.
problem: Securing a probe in a high-pressure environment while maintaining electrical insulation and preventing dislodgement or misalignment.
constraint: Balancing mechanical retention strength with the need to preserve an unbroken insulation coating under pressure.
mechanism: Controlled geometric deformation of a probe creates a mechanical interlock with complementary structural features in an assembly body. This interlock maintains coaxial alignment and resists displacement forces while preserving a continuous insulating layer under external pressure.
mechanism_raw: A probe with controlled radial bends (outward deflection, reverse bends, and straightening bends) engages with supporting shoulders in an assembly body. This mechanical interlock retains the probe coaxially while allowing continuous insulation, resisting pressure-induced forces.

abstract: A nail driver having a rod that telescopes within a hollow elongated tube. One end of the rod is designed to strike the nails and a weighted handle is attached to the other end. The tube has at least one chamber for holding the nails in position to be struck by the driver, and the chamber has a slot for receiving the nails. There are means for feeding nails through the slot. Preferably there are two such chambers and two such feeding means, one chamber and feeding means adapted for flat headed nails and the other chamber and means adapted for finishing nails. The impacting end of the rod is bifurcated, and one portion is designed to drive finishing nails in one chamber and the other portion is designed to drive flat headed nails in the other chamber. The impacting end of the rod and the chamber are changeable so that the invention may be used to drive a wide variety of nail sizes and types.
