problem: Driving multiple nail types (e.g., flat-headed and finishing nails) efficiently without manual tool adjustments.
constraint: Maintaining compatibility with diverse nail sizes/types while ensuring reliable feeding and impact alignment.
mechanism: A selectively extendable dual-path actuator engages discrete chambers containing different fastener types. Each chamber incorporates a dedicated feeding mechanism, enabling tool-free switching between fastener types through the actuator's bifurcated configuration.
mechanism_raw: A telescoping rod with a bifurcated impacting end drives nails from separate chambers. Each chamber and feeding mechanism is dedicated to a specific nail type, enabling selective operation via the bifurcated rod design.

abstract: The disclosure relates to a locking device for an automatic scraper in a centrifuge. The locking device has an automatic safety device in the form of insertable and withdrawable pins which are arranged to prevent unintentional axial movement when the scraper is in an initial position and to prevent unintentonal rotation of the scraper when it is in operative position.
problem: Preventing unintentional axial movement or rotation of a centrifuge scraper during operation.
constraint: Ensuring fail-safe engagement of the pins without interfering with the scraper's operational motion.
mechanism: A dual-state mechanical locking system uses insertable elements to selectively immobilize a component in two distinct operational positions. The first position prevents axial displacement while the second prevents rotational movement, ensuring fail-safe engagement without impeding intended motion.
mechanism_raw: Insertable/withdrawable pins mechanically lock the scraper in its initial position (preventing axial movement) and operative position (preventing rotation). The pins act as a dual-state safety interlock.

abstract: A one-piece carriage is proportioned for sliding engagement with an elongated guide which mounts an elongated micrometer screw laterally thereof and parallel thereto. An integral, lateral extension of the carriage overlies the screw and is provided with a slot perpendicular to the screw, the slot freely receiving the latch portion of a lever which is secured pivotally in the slot by a pivot pin disposed parallel to the screw. The outer portion of the lever forms a lever actuator for engagement with the screw, a spring interengaging the lever and carriage for urging the latch portion resiliently into engagement with the screw. The carriage also supports a block which mounts an archery bow sight.
problem: Achieving precise, repeatable adjustments of an archery bow sight relative to a micrometer screw.
constraint: Maintaining backlash-free engagement between the lever latch and screw while enabling smooth manual actuation.
mechanism: A pivoting lever with a constrained engagement feature converts rotational input from a precision screw into controlled linear displacement. Spring biasing and slot-based interaction between the lever and screw enable backlash-free incremental adjustments for fine positional control.
mechanism_raw: A lever with a latch portion engages the micrometer screw via a slot. The lever's pivot and spring bias allow incremental screw rotation, translating rotational motion into controlled lateral carriage movement for fine sight adjustment.

abstract: A temperature sensitive member, such as used in a thermostat, is formed of an elongated metal strip coated with a layer of polymer material. Holes are formed through the metal strip over its length and the layer of polymer material extends into the holes. The polymer material layer has a greater thickness than the metal strip. In one embodiment, the member can be formed by helically slitting a tubular member with the ends of the slit spaced inwardly from the ends of the tubular member. The polymer material layer is coated on the interior surface of the tubular member.
problem: Achieving precise temperature sensitivity in a thermostat-like device using a metal strip and polymer coating.
constraint: Balancing polymer thickness and hole spacing to optimize thermal sensitivity while maintaining structural integrity of the metal strip.
mechanism: A composite structure combines two materials with differing thermal expansion coefficients, where one material is mechanically constrained within recesses of the other. This constraint amplifies bending deformation in response to temperature changes, enabling precise actuation through controlled differential expansion.
mechanism_raw: Holes through the metal strip allow the thicker polymer layer to extend into them, creating differential thermal expansion between the polymer and metal. This structural interaction amplifies bending in response to temperature changes, enabling precise actuation.

abstract: An envelope opener comprising first, second and third shear stations for shearing three edges of an envelope in sequence one edge at a time. Each shear station sequentially aligns the envelope by contacting the edge to be sheared, shears the contacted edge, and then releases the envelope. A microcomputer monitors the advance of the envelope through and between the shear stations and causes the shear stations to cyclically align, shear and release the envelope. A peel back station downstream of the shear station peels back a panel of the envelope to expose the contents thereof. If an envelope is jammed at or between any of the stations, the microcomputer actuates a display to indicate a jam condition. The microcomputer also shuts off power to the opener to prevent damage to the envelope.
problem: Efficiently opening envelopes sequentially without jamming or damaging contents.
constraint: Synchronizing alignment, shearing, and release timing across stations to handle variable envelope sizes and prevent mechanical interference.
mechanism: A controller orchestrates sequential operations across multiple stations, each performing a distinct mechanical action (alignment, shearing, release) in a synchronized cycle. Real-time feedback detects disruptions and interrupts actuation to prevent damage, ensuring controlled sequential processing of variable-sized items.
mechanism_raw: A microcomputer coordinates three shear stations to cyclically align, shear, and release the envelope edge-by-edge. Real-time monitoring detects jams and halts power to prevent damage, ensuring controlled sequential processing.

abstract: A process for recovery of reusable chromic acid from waste chromic acid solution containing impurities, which process comprises a first step in which the solution containing chromic acid is introduced into the cathode compartment in an electro-dialysis process and free chromic acid or chromate ions in the above solution are transferred to the anode compartment, a second step in which H.sub.2 SO.sub.4 is added in at least equivalent amounts to the heavy metallic ion contained in the outlet solution, in which chromic acid ion concentration is reduced, in order to convert chemical species of the contained metallic ion and increase the H.sup.+ ion concentration and then chromate ions in the resultant solution are extracted into an organic phase with contact of an organic solvent (A), and a third step in which residual amounts of chromic acid ion remaining in the aqueous raffinate from the second step are extracted into an organic phase with contact of an organic solvent (B). Organic solvents A and B are regenerated by stripping the organic phase with a suitable strip reagent.
problem: Recovering reusable chromic acid from waste solutions containing impurities.
constraint: Managing chemical compatibility and ion selectivity across electrochemical and solvent extraction stages to maximize purity and recovery efficiency.
mechanism: A multi-stage separation process combines electrochemical ion transfer, chemical precipitation to remove contaminants, and solvent-based isolation to recover a target substance. Regeneration of the solvent enables reuse, maintaining purity and efficiency across stages.
mechanism_raw: A three-step process combines electrodialysis to transfer chromate ions, chemical precipitation via sulfuric acid to remove heavy metals, and sequential organic solvent extraction to isolate residual chromic acid. Solvent regeneration enables reuse.

abstract: The invention disclosed provides a new improved slurry detergent and to a method of using same. The slurry detergent may be formulated with alkali metal hydroxides and/or silicates, condensed phosphates, sodium hypochlorite and sodium polyacrylate, or the like. The new improved slurry is found to have significant advantages over both liquid detergents and powder detergents in dispensing as well as in use.
reason: The abstract lists detergent components (alkali metal hydroxides, silicates, phosphates, etc.) but does not describe a causal mechanism for how these components interact to solve a specific problem. It focuses on formulation rather than a functional process or structural principle.

abstract: A rotary scraping or abrading tool in which a rotatable disc has a multiple of guiding bores through which scraping elements are axially arranged. The scraping elements have outer active ends extending beyond the face of the disc facing the workpiece to be treated. Inner ends of the scraping elements bear against a disc of elastic material. The scraping elements are provided with axial play within the bores which are arranged as coacting sets of holes in at least two adjacent parallel discs. The scraping elements are in the form of circular cylindrical tubular studs with a scraping end cross-cut and with an inner end thereof having a head. The cross section of the head exceeds the cross section of the remainder of the stud. The bores, moreover, have an axis at an acute angle relative to the direction of rotation of the discs.
problem: Maintaining consistent scraping contact on a workpiece surface during rotary abrasion despite surface irregularities.
constraint: Balancing axial play and bore angle to maintain scraping force without excessive wear or loss of precision.
mechanism: Mechanical compliance is achieved through elements with axial play within angled mounting features, allowing independent movement to adapt to surface irregularities. Parallel apertures in coacting components enable dynamic pressure adjustment, maintaining consistent contact force during rotary motion.
mechanism_raw: Scraping elements with axial play within angled bores allow independent movement, while coacting sets of holes in parallel discs enable adaptive positioning. The angled bore orientation relative to rotation ensures dynamic contact pressure adjustment.

abstract: This specification discloses an identification tag for designating a container with either of two indicia. The tag includes a generally planar body which can be folded double along an axis so that either of two indicia can be displayed by reversing the fold, one of the messages being on one side and the other message being on the other side of the tag. The body of the tag can be attached to the container by an elongated strap extending from one edge of the body and passing through a pair of aligned holes in the body which are generally symetric with respect to the axis of folding. The strap has a barb-like protrusion at the end which facilitates insertion of the strap into the holes and resists removal of the strap. When the indicia is to be changed, the strap is removed from the holes, the body folded in reverse and attached to the container with the other indicia showing.
problem: Need to reversibly change displayed indicia on a container tag without replacing the tag.
constraint: The tag must remain securely attached to the container yet allow easy removal and reattachment when changing indicia.
mechanism: A reversible display element with two distinct indicia on opposing surfaces enables switching between messages by inverting the element's orientation. A detachable fastening mechanism with a resilient engagement feature allows secure attachment to a target surface while permitting removal for reorientation.
mechanism_raw: A foldable planar body with two indicia on opposite sides allows switching between messages by reversing the fold direction. An elongated strap with a barb-like protrusion enables secure attachment to a container while permitting removal for re-folding.

abstract: An improved process for forming cast articles of plaster reinforced with fibers is disclosed wherein low consistency plaster slurries that include a fluidizing agent and fibrous reinforcing materials are co-sprayed onto a sectionalized casting bed having a flexible membrane section connecting rigid sheet forming bed portions; allowed to stand in a horizontal position through initial stiffening; and then before the slurry has set, the sectionalized casting bed is reformed so as to produce a contoured shape to the gypsum cement sheet.
problem: Forming contoured shapes in fiber-reinforced plaster cast articles while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: The reshaping must occur after initial stiffening but before the slurry fully sets to avoid structural failure.
mechanism: A composite material application process deposits a reinforcing phase and a binding phase onto an adjustable mold surface. The mold is shaped during an intermediate stiffening stage of the composite, before full curing, to achieve a contoured form while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Co-spraying low-consistency plaster slurries with fibrous reinforcement onto a sectionalized casting bed with a flexible membrane allows initial stiffening in a horizontal position, followed by reshaping the bed before full setting to produce a contoured form.
residual_terms: ["composite material application", "adjustable mold surface", "intermediate stiffening stage"]

abstract: An optical system for use with apparatus for grading articles of produce according to color. The simplified system is comprised of an aspherical lens, a field stop and an end of a fiber optic bundle at the image plane of the lens. Color filters and photoelectric detectors are positioned from the opposite end of the bundle at a distance so as to be uniformly illuminated by light emanating from each fiber of the bundle upon which a portion of the image is present.
problem: Accurately grading produce by color using an optical system with uniform illumination across the image.
constraint: The optical components must be positioned to maintain uniform illumination across the entire image plane for accurate color grading.
mechanism: An optical system focuses an image onto a light-transmitting medium with a field stop to ensure uniform illumination. Color-selective filters and detectors positioned at the medium's output enable consistent color-based classification of objects.
mechanism_raw: An aspherical lens focuses the image onto a fiber optic bundle's end, with a field stop ensuring uniform light distribution. Color filters and photoelectric detectors positioned at the opposite end of the bundle are uniformly illuminated by light from each fiber, enabling consistent color detection.

abstract: A sugarcane pith and rind separation unit comprising a power driven rind gripping roll, a power driven pith milling roll in close spaced relation, said rolls having surface indentation and being driven at such rotational speeds so as to accept incoming longitudinally split sugarcane stalk halves, flatten them, and mill out the pith away from the rind, and a pith deflecting plate or shroud positioned at the output of the two rolls, said plate having shaped surfaces for causing the rind and pith to travel further on separate paths and having, adjacent the leading edge and closely positioned in the output side of the pinch between the rolls, an elongated cylindrical roller of relatively small diameter and adapted to be driven at a rotational speed such as to effectively move any fibrous material that might cause clogging and binding out of the confined region between the rolls and the deflecting plate and pass to the output. In the preferred embodiment, the roller has formed on its surface, a series of elongated grooves defining sharp gear-like teeth inclined in the rotation direction and effective to cut, shred, break-up, and move the said fibrous material.
problem: Separating pith from sugarcane rind while preventing clogging and binding in the processing mechanism.
constraint: The rotational speeds and surface features of the rolls and roller must balance material separation efficiency with anti-clogging action.
mechanism: A material processing system uses counter-rotating elements with surface features and differential motion to mechanically separate components of a fibrous article. A directed deflection element routes separated materials along distinct paths, while an active cutting element removes residual material from the processing zone.
mechanism_raw: Power-driven rolls with surface indentations and differential speeds flatten and mill sugarcane halves, while a pith deflecting plate directs separated materials along distinct paths. A driven cylindrical roller with gear-like grooves at the output actively cuts, shreds, and moves fibrous material away from the confined region between the rolls and deflecting plate.
residual_terms: ["counter-rotating elements", "differential motion", "directed deflection element", "active cutting element"]

abstract: A process for reducing the hydrogen sulfide content of geothermal steam during a drilling operation by injecting hydrogen peroxide and an alkali metal hydroxide or calcium hydroxide into a flowing stream containing geothermal steam. Environmentally harmless reaction products are thus formed and the emission of hydrogen sulfide during drilling operations is substantially abated.
problem: Reducing hydrogen sulfide emissions during geothermal steam drilling operations.
constraint: The chemical reagents must be introduced in sufficient quantities and react effectively within the flowing stream to ensure complete hydrogen sulfide conversion.
mechanism: A chemical injection system introduces reactive agents into a flowing process stream to trigger a conversion reaction that neutralizes a target contaminant. The agents are delivered in stoichiometric proportion to ensure complete reaction within the stream's residence time.
mechanism_raw: Injecting hydrogen peroxide and an alkali metal hydroxide or calcium hydroxide into the flowing geothermal steam stream triggers a chemical reaction that converts hydrogen sulfide into environmentally harmless products, thereby abating emissions.

abstract: To eliminate the noisy milling machines for cutting grooves in articulation pieces of innersoles, a machine is provided which comprises a series of pairs of forwarding rollers, one of the rollers of the first few pairs of rollers has a double knife formed on at least a part of its circumference so that a piece passing between such a pair has two longitudinal cuts formed thereon which are to become the side walls of the groove; a transverse skinning knife is pivotally mounted so as to be moveable into and out of the path of this piece as it passes a subsequent pair of rollers, this knife has the width of the groove and is pivoted into the path of the piece to remove the material between the longitudinal cuts. Preferably, a bracket device is associated with the skinning knife to maintain the straight path of the piece as the skinning knife works on it.
problem: Eliminating noisy milling machines for cutting grooves in innersole articulation pieces while maintaining precision and continuous operation.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise, simultaneous longitudinal and transverse cuts while ensuring the workpiece remains aligned and undamaged during the operation.
mechanism: A workpiece is advanced through a sequence of cutting elements: first, paired cutting tools create parallel longitudinal incisions while the workpiece moves along a guided path, then a secondary cutting element removes material between the incisions. A guiding structure constrains the workpiece to a straight trajectory during both cutting phases, enabling continuous operation without manual repositioning.
mechanism_raw: Using pairs of forwarding rollers with integrated double knives to create longitudinal cuts, followed by a transverse skinning knife that removes material between the cuts. A bracket maintains the workpiece's straight path during cutting, enabling a continuous, noise-free process.

abstract: Centrifugal separator having control valves 12 in the concentrated phase discharge passageway 10 for control of the concentration of solids in the concentrated phase. The control valves are hydraulically operated and have a control chamber 12c for the control fluid. The control fluid is clear phase obtained by communicating the control chamber 12c with the paring chamber 6 for the clear phase. Desirably the closing device of the valves is a resilient deformable tube membrane 12b.
problem: Controlling the concentration of solids in the concentrated phase of a centrifugal separator without introducing external control fluids.
constraint: Ensuring the control fluid (clear phase) remains uncontaminated and compatible with the valve components while maintaining responsive hydraulic control.
mechanism: A closed-loop control system uses a process output stream as its own actuation medium, where a deformable membrane regulates fluid flow to modulate valve closure. The system's inherent output (clear phase) directly drives the control mechanism, eliminating external fluid dependencies while maintaining hydraulic responsiveness.
mechanism_raw: Hydraulically operated control valves use clear phase fluid (obtained directly from the separator's paring chamber) as the control medium, with a resilient deformable tube membrane regulating valve closure. This creates a closed-loop system where the separator's own output drives its control mechanism.

abstract: A synthesis of four (4) factors is applied, through a test approach, to eliminate wire fractures, and fractures and overstressing of other cable components. This approach shows this "crucial flaw" is prevented from occurring amidst other flaws within the "flaw state" of the complex structure of work performing cable. These other flaws prove to be minor during the cable's service life. Non-frangible, ductile aluminum (al) and titanium (ti) wire are used in the cable assembly wherein their high dynamic properties and other attributes prevent wire fractures, and neutralize or reduce wire wear, depending upon load level, to change and improve the cable's "flaw state" so that a "fail-safe" cable may be designed to provide a protracted service life. Steel and copper wire fail to qualify for "fail-safe" cable constructions due to their low dynamic properties and other flaws in the cable structure.
problem: Preventing wire fractures and overstressing in cables to achieve a fail-safe design with extended service life.
constraint: Balancing material ductility and dynamic performance against structural integrity and load-bearing requirements to avoid catastrophic failure under varying conditions.
mechanism: A multi-factor synthesis approach selects materials with high ductility and dynamic response characteristics to absorb stress variations and tolerate structural flaws. Testing evaluates material properties, load adaptability, flaw tolerance, and dynamic behavior to shift the system's failure state toward controlled degradation rather than catastrophic fracture.
mechanism_raw: Selecting non-frangible, ductile materials (aluminum and titanium) with high dynamic properties to neutralize wear and absorb stress variations. A synthesis of four factors (material properties, load-level adaptability, structural flaw tolerance, and dynamic response) is applied through testing to shift the cable's 'flaw state' toward fail-safe operation.

abstract: A holder for forming and cooking a tortilla within a frying pan. The holder includes an apertured plate of generally U-shaped transverse configuration upon the exterior surfaces of which is removably clipped a tortilla. A handle is slidably connected to a pair of bars that connect the outer ends of the plate. The handle slides relative to the bars when the plate is inverted during a tortilla cooking operation to clear the sides of the frying pan.
problem: Forming and cooking a tortilla in a frying pan without sticking or deformation during inversion.
constraint: Ensuring the sliding handle mechanism provides sufficient clearance during inversion while maintaining structural stability and ease of use.
mechanism: A gripping element with an adjustable handle allows inversion of a flexible item while maintaining its shape. The handle's sliding motion automatically repositions the gripping element to clear surrounding surfaces during inversion, ensuring the item remains secured without manual adjustment.
mechanism_raw: A U-shaped apertured plate with a slidably connected handle allows the tortilla to be clipped onto the plate and inverted. The handle slides relative to the bars during inversion, automatically adjusting the plate's position to clear the pan's sides and maintain the tortilla's shape.

abstract: A tractor of width acceptable for highway travel having a narrow rear body portion between the rear wheels, the width of the body portion being less than the width of each pneumatic tire mounted on the rear wheels. Four or six rear tires which are rotatable on the same axis have the narrow body portion disposed centrally and closely between them, such body portion extending forwardly relatively to the rear wheels with the forward portion of the body, which is substantially wider than the rear portion, mounting an engine near the front wheels. A power transmitting linkage connects the engine with the rear wheels through the rear body portion which, with lateral projections, houses a differential and the necessary shaft bearings. A lifting device extends rearwardly from the rear body portion to behind the rear wheels and then extends laterally where it functions to scrape mud or the like from the treads of the rear tires. A tow bar also extends aft from the rear body portion which is sufficiently wide to scrape mud or the like from the interior sides of the closest rear wheels.
problem: Designing a tractor that meets highway width restrictions while accommodating a wide front engine compartment and functional rear attachments.
constraint: Balancing the tractor's overall width for highway compliance with the need to house critical components and attachments in a compact, functional layout.
mechanism: A compact layout uses a narrower rear section to comply with width restrictions while integrating critical components through lateral projections. A rearward-extending mechanism leverages the vehicle's geometry to perform dual functions: component integration and surface cleaning during operation.
mechanism_raw: A narrow rear body portion (wider than the tires but narrower than the front) houses the differential and bearings, with lateral projections for component integration. A rearward-extending lifting device and tow bar scrape mud from tire treads and interior wheel sides, leveraging the tractor's geometry for dual functionality.

abstract: The arrangement is mainly designed for transporting solid minerals from the floor of the ocean to a support vessel. The arrangement comprises an endless flexible carrier which is made of interconnected container sections. Each section has two chambers -- a load chamber and a float chamber. The arrangement also has means for batched loading of the chambers with solid mineral and compressed gas. During operation of the arrangement, the load chambers are loaded with solid mineral and the float chambers are filled with gas so that the loaded sections of the carrier acquire a positive buoyancy thus enabling displacement of the entire carrier.
problem: Transporting heavy solid minerals from the ocean floor to a support vessel requires overcoming gravitational and hydrodynamic resistance while maintaining controlled displacement.
constraint: Balancing the weight of the solid mineral load with the buoyancy provided by compressed gas to ensure net positive displacement without structural failure of the flexible carrier.
mechanism: Batched loading of discrete chambers with solid material and a buoyant medium creates variable buoyancy across interconnected carrier sections, enabling selective positive buoyancy in loaded sections to displace the entire carrier through controlled differential lift.
mechanism_raw: Batched loading of chambers with solid minerals and compressed gas creates variable buoyancy in interconnected carrier sections, enabling selective positive buoyancy in loaded sections to displace the entire carrier.

abstract: An improved archery bowstring release device is provided which includes a housing having a rear finger-receiving portion and a front portion, the latter with forwardly projecting flanges disposed in vertically spaced relation to define a longitudinal space therebetween. A bowstring draw cord defining a loop is preferably secured to the flanges and projects from the housing. A draw cord loop retainer is pivotally secured in the space to the flanges for movement between a locked bowstring-retaining position and an unlocked bowstring-releasing position. If desired, the retainer can be used directly to draw the bowstring rather than utilizing the draw cord, and the draw cord can then be removed from the device. The retainer projects laterally and rearwardly from the housing when in the locked position. A trigger mechanism is provided which comprises a coupler extending longitudinally in the space and pivotally connected to the flanges adjacent its rear end and to a link adjacent its front end, the link in turn being pivotally secured to the loop retainer. An elongated trigger arm extends longitudinally of the housing and is pivoted thereto so that its front end engages the rear end of the coupler. The arm's rear end extends rearwardly from the housing and is urgeable transversely of the housing by the archer's thumb to cause the front end thereof to force the coupler and link to rotate the retainer from the locked (cocked) position to the unlocked position, thus releasing the bowstring. The retainer can be easily manually moved back to the locked position. The device is inexpensive, durable and efficient, permitting easy, sure and highly accurate and reproducible drawing and shooting of archery arrows.
problem: Achieving a reliable, precise, and reproducible release of a bowstring in an archery device while allowing manual control and durability.
constraint: Ensuring the mechanical linkage system provides consistent force transmission and positional accuracy without introducing play or wear that compromises release timing.
mechanism: A manual actuator applies transverse pressure to a mechanical linkage system that converts the input force into rotational motion, selectively moving a retention element between locked and unlocked states to enable controlled release.
mechanism_raw: A thumb-actuated trigger arm pivots a coupler-link system that rotates a loop retainer between locked and unlocked positions, mechanically translating transverse thumb pressure into rotational release motion.

abstract: A device comprises a slider mounted fo reciprocations in guides extending along the axis of pulling an article. A mechanism for clamping dies comprises a double-arm level articulated to the slider and to a piston rod of an actuating cylinder having its piston chamber communicating with a passage for a slide valve having a drive means. A lower die is rigidly fixed to the slider and an upper block is secured to the free end of the lever.
problem: Applying controlled clamping or pulling force to an article along a linear axis using mechanical actuation.
constraint: Coordinating the slider's reciprocation with the lever's articulation to maintain uniform pressure distribution and avoid misalignment during clamping.
mechanism: A multi-arm lever system articulated to a reciprocating slider and linear actuator amplifies and directs input force along a defined axis, coordinating motion between components to maintain uniform pressure distribution during clamping.
mechanism_raw: A double-arm lever articulated to a slider and piston rod amplifies and directs actuation force from the cylinder to a lower die and upper block, creating synchronized clamping motion.

abstract: What may be termed a low-boy machine is provided with a side-positioned air-supplying blowing chamber, an air heating and upwardly and directing chamber-defining base part, a centrally disposed upright support post or column, an upright steam burst and heat-applying pipe assembly, an upper platform frame on the column that carries cap-finishing means, and a non-permeable bag positioned to extend upwardly between the base part and the upper frame to define a fluid-directing and mixing chamber for supplying steam and hot air to the cap-finishing means. The cap-finishing means has a pair of perforated cap-receiving and stretching parts through which steam and heated air is supplied to the inside of a fabric cap to be finished. The pair of parts have means for relatively moving them towards and away from each other to release and stretch a cap that is positioned thereon.
problem: Efficiently finishing fabric caps by applying steam and heated air internally while stretching the material to achieve a desired shape.
constraint: Maintaining consistent temperature and airflow distribution through the perforated parts while enabling controlled relative movement to stretch the cap without damaging it.
mechanism: A sealed mixing chamber combines steam and heated gas, which are directed through perforated components that move relative to each other to stretch and finish the article while maintaining consistent thermal and flow conditions.
mechanism_raw: A non-permeable bag defines a mixing chamber that combines steam and hot air, which are directed through perforated cap-receiving parts that move relative to each other to stretch and finish the cap.
residual_terms: ["sealed mixing chamber", "perforated components", "steam and heated gas"]

abstract: Disclosed herein is an adjustable hat for protecting one from the rays of the sun. The hat is comprised of a collapsible body portion adjustably mounted on an upper support band and a head and chin band assembly. The head and chin band assembly includes a pair of upper headbands which are preferably integrally formed with an adjustable chin strap. The head and chin band assembly is in turn adjustably mounted on the upper support band such that the hat can be adjusted to any desired angular position on the wearer's head to block the sun's rays.
problem: Providing adjustable sun protection that can be positioned at any desired angular orientation on a wearer's head.
constraint: Balancing adjustability with structural integrity to ensure the hat remains securely positioned during movement without compromising comfort or protection.
mechanism: An adjustable interface connects a collapsible body to a head-mounted support structure, enabling angular repositioning of the body relative to the wearer's head through a sliding or pivoting mechanism while maintaining structural stability.
mechanism_raw: An adjustable mounting system connects a collapsible body to a head and chin band assembly, allowing angular repositioning of the hat relative to the wearer's head via a sliding or pivoting interface.

abstract: Titanium aluminum, non-frangible structural wire, when assembled into axially symmetric and contrahelically wrapped cable has high fatigue strength and loading linearity for uniquely high work efficiency. Dynamic stresses are moderated by more suitable mechanical, physical and dynamic properties so that stress and fatigue control are passively achieved. Structural wire is specially processed from selected titanium base alloys having high drop test tear energy, wherein new construction designs and specifications are then suitable and used during cable assembly to substantially advance work performance and increase service life. Work characteristics are basically improved and changed by (1) adding elastic and constructional stretch, (2) materially reducing mass density, and (3) loading cable with hard and soft spring. These cable attributes translate into much higher fatigue strength, mainly by absorbing, storing and dissipating induced work loads at rapid rates. A new construction characteristic is enlarged cores for both structural and electrical reasons wherein stress stratification, stress transfer and distribution between layers, and stress propagation and vibration are changed, wherein stretch is increased and loading dynamically counterbalanced. Internal stresses are also reduced in the interrelated process by greater component compliance. Variably designed core and outer strand constructions including composite cable are used to increase work capacity and service life, and to reduce cost. Non-frangible, aluminum wire may be used as components in cable constructions, interchangeably with titanium wire as conductor and structural components in many cases in this invention.
problem: Achieving high fatigue strength and dynamic stress moderation in structural cables under rapid loading while maintaining work efficiency and service life.
constraint: Balancing structural support and load-bearing capacity with sufficient compliance to absorb dynamic stresses without compromising cable integrity or increasing mass density.
mechanism: Passively managing dynamic stresses in load-bearing structures by integrating material compliance (elastic deformation, reduced mass density) and structural design (enlarged cores, composite configurations, variable stiffness elements) to absorb, store, and dissipate induced work loads at rapid rates, thereby reducing internal stresses and enabling stress stratification and dynamic counterbalancing.
mechanism_raw: Passively managing dynamic stresses by integrating material compliance (elastic/constructional stretch, reduced mass density) and structural design (enlarged cores, composite strand configurations, hard/soft spring loading) to absorb, store, and dissipate induced work loads at rapid rates, thereby reducing internal stresses and enabling stress stratification and dynamic counterbalancing.

abstract: A container for a wire spool adapted to be stacked one on top of the other without damage thereto or to its contents. The container comprises a spool housing having a side wall, a bottom wall and an open top end. A cover is provided for the open top end and is engageable about an outer peripheral edge of the open top end. A cover having load transfer ribs converging into a ring which is formed therein and which extends within the housing. The load transfer ring rests on an upper end of a wire spool, when provided in the housing, whereby external loads on the cover will be transmitted to the bottom wall of the housing through the load transfer ring and a core of the spool.
problem: Enabling safe stacking of wire spool containers without damaging the container or its contents under external loads.
constraint: Ensuring the load transfer path is robust enough to handle stacking forces while maintaining the structural integrity of the spool and its contents during handling and storage.
mechanism: Transferring external loads through a dedicated load transfer path (formed by converging structural elements) that directs forces directly to a central core structure, channeling forces through the core to a base support, bypassing the primary container structure to preserve its integrity.
mechanism_raw: Transferring external loads from the cover through a load transfer ring (formed by converging ribs) that rests directly on the spool core, channeling forces through the spool's core to the bottom wall of the housing, bypassing the spool itself.
residual_terms: ["load transfer path", "central core structure", "bypassing the primary container structure"]

abstract: A method for treating nonferrous metal hydroxide sludge waste to separate and recover the nonferrous metals therein wherein the waste is first mixed with an alkali hydroxide or carbonate, dried, and then roasted and the water-insoluble residue in the roasted material is treated with sulfuric acid to produce an acid-insoluble residue and a sulfuric acid solution containing copper, aluminum and chromium and thereafter, separating the copper from this solution by liquid-liquid extraction and thereafter, separating the aluminium, chromium, zinc and nickel from the remaining solution by separate liquid-liquid extraction steps.
problem: Separating and recovering nonferrous metals (copper, aluminum, chromium, zinc, nickel) from hydroxide sludge waste efficiently and selectively.
constraint: Achieving selective separation of multiple metals in a single process stream while minimizing cross-contamination and optimizing reagent usage across sequential extraction steps.
mechanism: Sequential chemical processing: applying alkali treatment to stabilize feedstock, thermal conversion to alter solubility, acid leaching to dissolve target components, followed by staged liquid-liquid extraction to isolate individual substances based on solubility and chemical affinity.
mechanism_raw: Sequential chemical processing: alkali treatment to stabilize sludge, roasting to convert water-insoluble residues, sulfuric acid leaching to dissolve target metals, followed by staged liquid-liquid extraction to isolate individual metals based on solubility and chemical affinity.

abstract: A shaped body of calcium silicate characterized by being composed of globular secondary particles interconnected with one another and each made up of lath-like xonotlite or foshagite crystals having been three-dimensionally interlocked with one another and having an index of crystallite antigrowth of at least 15, the globular secondary particles having had an outside diameter of about 10 to about 80 .mu.m and an apparent density of up to 0.13 g/cm.sup.3 and having been in the form of a shell with a hollow interior space and a thickness of about 0.3 to about 10 .mu.m before being shaped into the body.
problem: Creating a lightweight, high-strength calcium silicate material with controlled porosity and thermal stability for industrial applications.
constraint: Balancing the formation of hollow, low-density particles with sufficient crystal interlocking to prevent structural collapse during shaping and use.
mechanism: Engineering globular secondary particles with hollow interiors and lath-like crystals interlocked three-dimensionally, combined with controlled crystallite antigrowth (index ≥15), to achieve low apparent density (≤0.13 g/cm³) while maintaining structural integrity through interlocked crystal networks.
mechanism_raw: Engineering globular secondary particles with hollow interiors and lath-like xonotlite/foshagite crystals interlocked three-dimensionally, combined with controlled crystallite antigrowth (index ≥15), to achieve low apparent density (≤0.13 g/cm³) while maintaining structural integrity through interlocked crystal networks.
residual_terms: ["hollow interiors", "lath-like crystals", "controlled crystallite antigrowth", "interlocked crystal networks"]

abstract: A safety razor intended to be discarded after use, comprising a cutting head and a handle. The cutting head includes two oppositely disposed longitudinal surfaces with cutting edges disposed thereon. In order that both cutting edges may be used, the cutting head is rotatably disposed in an extension piece adjoining the handle.
problem: Allowing both cutting edges of a disposable safety razor to be used without requiring complex mechanical adjustments or additional components.
constraint: Maintaining simplicity and low cost for disposability while ensuring the rotational mechanism is durable enough to allow repeated edge switching without failure.
mechanism: Rotatably mounting a dual-edge cutting element within an extension piece adjoining a handle, enabling selective exposure of either of two oppositely disposed cutting edges through rotational adjustment without requiring additional mechanical components.
mechanism_raw: Rotatably mounting the cutting head within an extension piece adjoining the handle, enabling the user to rotate the head to expose either of the two oppositely disposed cutting edges for use.

abstract: A sewing machine is disclosed wherein positioning of the work feeding regulator is controlled by a digital actuator responsive to digital signals applied thereto. The positioning of the work feeding regulator is thereby adjustable in discrete increments. A manual override and feed balance mechanism is provided for effecting continuous positioning of the work feeding regulator.

constraint: Balancing discrete incremental precision (digital control) with continuous analog flexibility (manual override)
mechanism: A digital actuator responds to digital signals to position a work feeding regulator in discrete increments, while a manual override mechanism enables continuous positioning, allowing the system to switch between discrete digital control and continuous manual control as needed
mechanism_raw: A digital actuator responds to digital signals to position the work feeding regulator in discrete increments, while a manual override mechanism enables continuous positioning, allowing the system to switch between discrete digital control and continuous manual control as needed

abstract: Fire retardant generally non-caking compositions of intimately intermixed ammonium phosphate, e.g. mono- and/or diammonium phosphate; sodium tetraborate containing molecularly bound water, e.g. the decahydrate, borax; and fractured finely ground solid powder particles of soda-containing silicate glass which have a high and irregular surface area and an active dry moisture absorbent surface condition for maintaining the particles of ammonium phosphate and sodium tetraborate in moisture protected disposition and for inhibiting the tendency of such particles to adhere to one another; the three components having an average particle size below about 4 mesh, the ammonium phosphate and sodium tetraborate being present in a combined predominant amount effective for imparting an active fire retarding property to cellulosic materials, and the resulting admixture being substantially dry and free flowing with the individual particles thereof in substantially uniform and non-caking distribution; PA1 Corresponding combinations of such compositions with fibers of cellulosic material forming composite fire retardant products in which the three components are in substantially uniform distribution throughout the cellulosic material and in intimate association with the corresponding fibers thereof, and particularly loose fill structural products in which the individual particles of glass, borax and phosphate are disposed in situ in entwined relation with the adjacent cellulosic fibers; and PA1 Methods of preparing such composition in the substantial absence of moisture and of autogenous mixing heat, and in turn methods of preparing such composite fire retardant products.
problem: Maintaining fire retardant powder compositions in a dry, free-flowing, non-caking state while protecting moisture-sensitive active components
constraint: Maintaining fire-retardant effectiveness of the active components while preventing caking and moisture degradation through the use of moisture-absorbent carrier particles
mechanism: Fractured silicate glass particles with high irregular surface area and active dry moisture-absorbent surfaces are intermixed with hygroscopic fire retardant components, where the glass particles absorb ambient moisture and create a protective barrier that keeps the active components in moisture-protected disposition and inhibits particle-to-particle adhesion
mechanism_raw: Fractured silicate glass particles with high irregular surface area and active dry moisture-absorbent surfaces are intermixed with hygroscopic fire retardant components (ammonium phosphate, sodium tetraborate), where the glass particles absorb ambient moisture and create a protective barrier that keeps the active components in moisture-protected disposition and inhibits particle-to-particle adhesion
residual_terms: ["fractured silicate glass particles", "irregular surface area", "moisture-absorbent surfaces", "hygroscopic fire retardant components", "protective barrier", "moisture-protected disposition", "particle-to-particle adhesion"]

abstract: A kettle having a chamber sealed from the ambient atmosphere and designed to receive a plurality of tires retreaded with precured treads. Steam and air are supplied to the chamber in such a way that they are thoroughly mixed within the chamber to eliminate any hot or cold spots previously encountered in devices wherein the steam and air are each supplied to the chamber through a single inlet.
problem: Eliminating temperature non-uniformities (hot or cold spots) in a sealed chamber during steam-air heating processes for tire retreading
constraint: Achieving uniform mixing of steam and air within a sealed chamber without creating temperature gradients or dead zones
mechanism: Steam and air are introduced into the chamber in a manner that promotes thorough mixing within the chamber itself, rather than being supplied through separate single inlets as in prior devices, ensuring uniform temperature distribution throughout the chamber volume
mechanism_raw: Steam and air are introduced into the chamber in a manner that promotes thorough mixing within the chamber itself, rather than being supplied through separate single inlets as in prior devices, ensuring uniform temperature distribution throughout the chamber volume

abstract: This invention relates to herbicidal active compounds and their use. The compounds of this invention correspond to the formula: ##STR1## wherein R is selected from cyclopropyl, ethyl, furyl, benzyl, methyl, and 3,4-methylenedioxy-benzyl; R.sub.1 is selected from chloro and trifluoromethyl; R.sub.2 is selected from hydrogen, 4-chloro, 4-propargyloxy, and 5-chloro; R.sub.3 is selected from ethyl, chloroethyl, isobutyl, allyl and propargyl.

abstract: An articulated spindle as used for example in a rolling mill drive has a shank the ends of which are connected to sleeves through gear-type couplings. Liquid is continually passed through each gear-type coupling for cooling and lubrication. The liquid is supplied under pressure through the shank to the couplings, passes through the couplings, and is withdrawn under suction through return conduits which rotate with the shank. The liquid is supplied by a delivery pump through a rotating joint to the shank and is withdrawn from the return conduits through the rotating joint by a suction pump.
problem: Providing continuous cooling and lubrication to rotating gear-type couplings in an articulated spindle while maintaining rotation through a fixed interface
constraint: Maintaining continuous fluid flow through a rotating interface while the spindle articulates and rotates, requiring sealed rotating joints for both pressure supply and suction return
mechanism: Pressurized liquid is supplied through a rotating joint to the rotating shank, flows through the gear-type couplings for cooling and lubrication, and is then withdrawn under suction through return conduits that rotate with the shank, with both supply and return passing through the same rotating joint to maintain continuous fluid circulation despite rotation
mechanism_raw: Pressurized liquid is supplied through a rotating joint to the rotating shank, flows through the gear-type couplings for cooling and lubrication, and is then withdrawn under suction through return conduits that rotate with the shank, with both supply and return passing through the same rotating joint to maintain continuous fluid circulation despite rotation

abstract: A binary frequency divider stage comprises eleven insulated gate field effect transistors and a capacitor, all of which may be fabricated as an integrated circuit. The stage has an input, an output, two supply lines, and two clock lines for receiving two sets of out-of-phase clock pulses. Pulses are supplied to the input synchronously with one of the sets of clock pulses and the divider stage produces at its output pulses of half the frequency of the input pulses.
problem: Dividing an input pulse frequency by two (or more generally, performing binary frequency division) using a minimal number of components that can be integrated on a single chip.
constraint: The circuit must operate reliably with only two out-of-phase clock signals and a fixed number of transistors, requiring precise phase relationships and balanced switching thresholds to avoid race conditions or metastability.
mechanism: A bistable switching network that alternates between two stable states on successive input clock transitions, so each complete input cycle produces exactly one output state change, thereby halving the output frequency relative to the input.
mechanism_raw: A bistable switching network (multiple FETs configured as a toggle flip-flop) that alternates between two stable states on successive input clock transitions, so each complete input cycle produces exactly one output state change, thereby halving the output frequency relative to the input.
residual_terms: ["bistable switching network", "stable states", "clock transitions", "output state change", "frequency"]

abstract: The invention relates to a process for the utilization of waste substances containing combustible components and showing fluctuations in their composition and properties and to a device for carrying out the process. The improvement comprises effecting the volatilization, decomposition and incomplete combustion of the waste substances in a first process step which is immediately followed by a second process step in which formed pyrolysis gases are burned in a heating device for burning starting materials for building materials or inorganic binders.
problem: Utilizing waste substances with fluctuating composition and properties in a downstream thermal process (e.g., burning them to produce heat for building-material manufacturing) without destabilizing the downstream process.
constraint: The two stages must be tightly coupled in time and heat integration so that the pyrolysis gases are immediately available for combustion, while the first stage must tolerate wide swings in waste composition without producing off-spec intermediates.
mechanism: Decoupling the variable input from the fixed-output process by splitting the operation into two sequential stages: a first stage that volatilizes, decomposes, and partially combusts the heterogeneous waste into a more uniform intermediate, and a second stage that burns those intermediates in a controlled heating device, so the downstream process receives a stabilized fuel stream regardless of upstream variability.
mechanism_raw: Decoupling the variable input from the fixed-output process by splitting the operation into two sequential stages: a first stage that volatilizes, decomposes, and partially combusts the heterogeneous waste into a more uniform intermediate (pyrolysis gases), and a second stage that burns those gases in a controlled heating device, so the downstream process receives a stabilized fuel stream regardless of upstream variability.

abstract: An inherent tendency for particulate wheat gluten to agglomerate when introduced into an aqueous medium is inhibited by mixing the gluten with an edible material, which is rich in protein capable, when interposed between the gluten particles, of interfering with and preventing the hydrogen bonding between protein molecules of the gluten which would otherwise cause the gluten particles to agglomerate. Soy flour is particularly effective as the agglomeration-inhibiting additive and can be introduced by pre-mixing with the gluten. The invention is particularly useful in inhibiting agglomeration of vital wheat gluten in the production of yeast-leavened baked goods.
problem: Preventing particulate protein (wheat gluten) from agglomerating when dispersed in an aqueous medium, which would degrade texture and processing in food products like yeast-leavened baked goods.
constraint: The interposing agent must itself be edible and must be present in sufficient quantity and with compatible molecular dimensions to effectively occupy the interfacial space, while not altering the functional properties of the final food product.
mechanism: Introducing a secondary particulate material whose molecules interpose themselves between the primary particles, physically disrupting the intermolecular bonding network that would otherwise form between the primary particles and cause them to clump together.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a secondary protein-rich material (e.g., soy flour) whose molecules interpose themselves between the primary protein particles, physically disrupting the hydrogen-bonding network that would otherwise form between the primary protein molecules and cause them to clump together.

abstract: A stick holder is an accessory having an elongated body rectangular in cross-section, and having support brackets at each end including extending arms and transverse legs. The holder body includes transverse passages for receiving and clamping sticks, which are ejected from an adjacent stick box or hopper and urged into food articles or other articles retained in an article holder on the opposite side of the stick holder. To locate the stick holder in desired relation to the stick box, the stick holder and the apparatus have coacting structure to prevent relative movement. Guide blocks are mounted on the sides of the apparatus, adjacent to the ends of the stick box, and coact with the stick holder support brackets to provide a broader support base eliminating rocking movement of the stick holder about a longitudinal axis, to prevent movement of the stick holder away from the stick box, and to locate the stick holder laterally with some precision relative to the stick box.
problem: Precisely positioning and stabilizing a stick-holding accessory relative to a stick-feeding hopper in a food-processing (or general article-insertion) machine, preventing misalignment, rocking, and lateral drift during operation.
constraint: The positioning mechanism must allow the stick holder to be quickly installed and removed (for maintenance or changeover) while still providing repeatable, high-precision alignment, and must resist dynamic forces generated during stick ejection and insertion without loosening.
mechanism: Using coacting mechanical interfaces — complementary locating structures on both the accessory and the host apparatus — that engage to constrain relative movement in multiple degrees of freedom, combined with guide blocks and support brackets that create a broad, stable base eliminating rocking about the longitudinal axis.
mechanism_raw: Using coacting mechanical interfaces — complementary locating structures on both the stick holder and the host apparatus — that engage to constrain relative movement in multiple degrees of freedom, combined with guide blocks and support brackets that create a broad, stable base eliminating rocking about the longitudinal axis.

abstract: A wear part for sliding gates used for the outlet of vessels which contain metal melts therein, the wear part being for example a sliding plate, a base plate, an inlet tube or an outlet tube. The wear part includes a refractory material surrounded by a metal mantle, where a fireproof refractory concrete is poured into a mold and hardened therein so that the mold serves as the metal mantle when the concrete has hardened. A lining surrounding a through-bore in the wear part may be cast therewith. The wear part is preferably clamped in a supporting frame.
problem: Fabricating a durable, high-temperature wear part (for sliding gates in metal-melt vessels) that combines a refractory core with a metal outer shell, without requiring complex multi-step assembly or bonding processes.
constraint: The mold material must withstand the thermal and mechanical stresses of both the casting process and subsequent service in contact with molten metal, while the refractory core and metal mantle must have compatible thermal expansion characteristics to avoid cracking or delamination during temperature cycling.
mechanism: Using the forming mold itself as the permanent outer shell of the finished part: a refractory material is poured into the mold and allowed to harden in place, so the mold walls become the shell surrounding the cured refractory core, producing a monolithic composite structure in a single casting step.
mechanism_raw: Using the forming mold itself as the permanent metal mantle of the finished part: refractory concrete is poured into the mold and allowed to harden in place, so the mold walls become the metal jacket surrounding the cured refractory core, producing a monolithic composite structure in a single casting step.

abstract: A drive system for a movable closure member movable along rail sets carried on opposed sides of the frame of a structure includes a rail set on each side of at least one pair of opposed sides of the frame. Each rail set includes first and second laterally offset toothed sections. Each first section includes a horizontal segment and an inclined segment whereas each second segment includes a vertical segment and an inclined segment which has at least a portion thereof in juxtaposed side-by-side relation with the inclined segment of the first section. An electric motor has a drive shaft that extends transversely of the rail sets and carries a first gear wheel coaxially therewith at each end. Each first gear wheel carries a second and smaller gear wheel eccentrically thereon. The first and second gear wheels have a common point of tangency. The first gear wheels are cooperable with the first sections of the respective rail sets and the second gear wheels are cooperable with the second sections of the respective rail sets. The respective rail sections and gear wheels are dimensioned to provide for transfer of driving force between the first and second gear wheels when the common point of tangency therebetween falls within the juxtaposed side-by-side portions of the respective inclined segments of the rail sets.
problem: Transmitting driving force to a closure member moving along rails on opposed sides of a frame, where the drive must engage two separate rail sections simultaneously and transfer force between gear elements at different positions.
constraint: The force transfer between gear wheels is only effective within a specific geometric overlap zone of the inclined rail segments, requiring precise dimensional matching between rail sections and gear wheels to ensure coupling occurs at the correct position.
mechanism: Two rotationally coupled elements with offset axes engage separate track sections. Mechanical power transfer between the elements is selectively enabled only when their mutual contact point lies within a specific geometric overlap region of the track segments, creating a position-dependent coupling that activates force transmission between the elements based on relative alignment.
mechanism_raw: A pair of eccentrically mounted gear wheels on a common shaft engage separate rail sections. Force transfer between the two gear wheels is selectively enabled only when their common point of tangency falls within juxtaposed side-by-side portions of inclined rail segments, creating a position-dependent coupling that activates mechanical power transmission between the gears based on relative alignment.

abstract: There is disclosed a composite web of pressure sensitive labels and method of making and using same. The composite web has a web of supporting material and a series of two-part labels releasably secured by pressure sensitive adhesive to the supporting material web. One part of the label is detachably connected to the other part by a line of partial severing. The adhesive is preferably coated onto only the one label part and the other label part is preferably free of adhesive. The label parts that are adhesive-free are detachably connected to each other by frangible portions which prevent the adhesive-free label parts from moving away from the supporting material web until the labels are delaminated from the supporting material. There is also disclosed method of making such composite webs and method of using such composite webs in label printing and applying machines.
problem: Retaining an adhesive-free portion of a two-part label on a supporting web during handling and processing, without using adhesive on that portion, until deliberate delamination is applied.
constraint: The frangible connections must be strong enough to retain the adhesive-free parts during normal handling and machine processing, yet weak enough to break cleanly when the intended delamination force is applied, balancing retention strength against release force.
mechanism: Non-adhesive regions of a multi-part label are temporarily bound to neighboring non-adhesive regions on a carrier substrate through breakable connections. These connections retain the non-adhesive regions during handling and processing until an external separation force exceeds their strength, at which point the connections fail and permit deliberate delamination.
mechanism_raw: The adhesive-free label parts are detachably connected to each other by frangible portions that temporarily bind them to neighboring adhesive-free parts on the supporting web. These frangible connections prevent the adhesive-free parts from moving away from the web until an external delamination force is applied, at which point the frangible links break and allow separation.

abstract: A method of irradiating a collection of particles by ultrashort pulses of light with isotopic selectivity having application in various methods of isotope separation (two step photoionization, photochemical separation or radiation pressure). In particular there is disclosed a method and apparatus for the efficient acceleration and collection of particles by means of radiation pressure, exemplified by separating a preselected isotope species from a gaseous mixture of isotopes. The gaseous mixture is irradiated with ultrashort, repetitious pulses of coherent light, each pulse having an intensity, frequency and duration selected to create momentum changes in the preselected gaseous isotope whereby to spatially isolate the isotope. Preferably, irradiation is carried out in the cavity of a mode-locked laser into which the gaseous mixture is injected. The pulses traverse and reflect back through the cavity so that the selected isotope is initially excited by a pulse, then restitutes its energy to the reflected pulse by stimulated emission. Means are provided for collecting the spatially isolated isotope.
problem: Spatially isolating and collecting a preselected isotope species from a gaseous mixture using radiation pressure from light pulses, with isotopic selectivity and efficient energy utilization.
constraint: The pulse parameters (intensity, frequency, duration) must be precisely tuned to the target isotope's excitation characteristics, and the isotope must remain in the cavity during both forward and reflected pulse traversal to enable the stimulated emission energy recovery.
mechanism: Pulsed radiation traverses a resonant cavity containing a mixture of species, first exciting a preselected species and then, upon reflection back through the cavity, receiving energy back from the excited species via stimulated emission. This bidirectional interaction creates a net momentum change in the selected species that differs from other species, causing spatial isolation. The reflected pulse recovers energy from the species, enhancing efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Ultrashort light pulses traverse a laser cavity containing the gas mixture, first exciting the target isotope and then, upon reflection back through the cavity, receiving energy back from the excited isotope via stimulated emission. This bidirectional pulse interaction creates a net momentum change in the selected isotope that differs from other species, causing spatial isolation. The reflected pulse effectively recovers energy from the isotope, enhancing efficiency.

abstract: A wetted parallel plate collecting electrode arrangement which increases the maximum electric field intensity possible without having water draining off the lower edges of the collecting electrodes forming small droplets which are accelerated towards the opposite electrodes. An electrically conductive partition plate maintained at a voltage intermediate the voltages on the electrodes is disposed between the lower edges of oppositely charged electrodes and extends above and below the lower edges of the electrodes. Preferably, the partition plate is electrically "floating" and receives its voltage due to the effects of the electric field between the collecting electrodes.
problem: Increasing the maximum electric field intensity in a wetted parallel plate electrode arrangement without causing conductive liquid (water) to drain off electrode edges and form droplets that are accelerated toward opposite electrodes.
constraint: The floating partition plate must self-bias to an appropriate intermediate voltage through field effects alone, without external voltage control, while still providing sufficient field gradient modification to counteract droplet acceleration.
mechanism: A conductive element is disposed between the lower edges of oppositely charged electrodes and is maintained at a voltage intermediate between them. The element is electrically floating, self-biasing to the intermediate voltage through the surrounding electric field. This creates a controlled field gradient near the electrode edges that prevents conductive liquid droplets from forming and being accelerated across the gap.
mechanism_raw: A conductive partition plate is disposed between the lower edges of oppositely charged electrodes and is maintained at a voltage intermediate between them. The partition plate is electrically floating, self-biasing to the intermediate voltage through the surrounding electric field. This creates a controlled field gradient near the electrode edges that prevents water droplets from forming and being accelerated across the gap.
residual_terms: ["parallel plate electrode arrangement", "conductive liquid", "water", "droplets", "floating partition plate", "intermediate voltage", "electric field"]

abstract: A label is provided for a bottle in the form of a heat shrinkable sleeve made of oriented polyethylene. The label is made as a laminate having inner and outer layers. The outer layer has a coefficient of friction of less than about 0.15. The inner layer has a coefficient of friction of greater than about 0.4. The inner layer includes ethylene vinyl acetate. The layers are about 0.001 inches. The layers are connected by an adhesive, which is about 0.00005 inches thick. A plurality of sleeves can be formed from a planar strip wherein first halves of the sleeves are formed adjacent each other along half of the strip and complementary halves of the sleeves are formed adjacent each other along the other half of the strip, whereafter the strip is folded in half to bring the first halves into alignment with the complementary halves and the thusly constituted portions of the sleeves are heat sealed or welded together.
problem: Efficiently manufacturing and applying heat-shrinkable sleeve labels to bottles, where the label must slide on easily during application but grip the bottle securely after shrinking.
constraint: The friction differential between layers must be sufficient to enable easy application while ensuring secure post-shrinkage grip, and the complementary half-pairing must maintain precise alignment during folding and sealing to produce properly formed sleeves.
mechanism: The label laminate uses a friction gradient: a low-friction outer layer enables easy sliding during insertion, while a high-friction inner layer grips the surface. Manufacturing is enabled by forming complementary sleeve halves on opposite halves of a planar strip, then folding the strip to align the halves and sealing them together, allowing batch production of paired components from a single flat substrate.
mechanism_raw: The label laminate uses a friction gradient: a low-friction outer layer (<0.15 coefficient) enables easy sliding during bottle insertion, while a high-friction inner layer (>0.4 coefficient) with ethylene vinyl acetate grips the bottle surface. Manufacturing is enabled by forming complementary sleeve halves on opposite halves of a planar strip, then folding the strip to align the halves and heat-sealing them together, allowing batch production of paired components from a single flat substrate.

abstract: A valve for controlling fluid flow is disclosed in which a fluid outlet is controlled by two separate components, one being tubular in shape and located inside the other hollow component. Both the hollow and the tubular components may either be the valve body and closing element respectively, or vice-versa. The two components are reciprocally slidable through elastic sealing rings along their common longitudinal axis, and are also rotatable about that same axis, whence the path of fluid flow may be readily controlled in a gradual manner from the fully shut position to the fully open position, depending upon the longitudinal position of a plunger element with respect to the valve body. The plunger is in a state of static balance with respect to any existing pressure or friction, as well as with respect to its own weight.
problem: Gradually controlling fluid flow from fully shut to fully open while maintaining stable positioning of the control element without external actuating forces, despite varying pressure, friction, and gravitational loads.
constraint: The components must maintain elastic sealing integrity while simultaneously enabling both axial sliding and rotational motion, and the static balance must account for pressure, friction, and weight forces concurrently so that no single force dominates the positioning.
mechanism: Two coaxial components are both axially translatable and rotatable relative to each other, enabling continuous modulation of a flow path from closed to open. The relative motion combines axial displacement and rotation to gradually vary the flow area. The control element is statically balanced so that pressure, friction, and gravitational forces cancel, allowing it to remain in a selected position without external holding force. Elastic sealing is maintained between the components despite both axial sliding and rotational motion.
mechanism_raw: Two concentric hollow/tubular components are both reciprocally slidable and rotatable about a common longitudinal axis. The combined sliding and rotational motion of one component relative to the other provides continuous, gradual modulation of the fluid flow path from shut to open. The plunger element is designed to be in static balance with respect to existing pressure, friction, and its own weight, so it naturally maintains its selected position without requiring external force to hold it in place.

abstract: A two lens group type of miniaturized zoom lens system having a minimum wide end viewing angle of 76.degree. and a zoom ratio at least 2.3. The first or object side lens group includes at least two positive and two negative lenses with the image side lens being positive. The second or image side lens group includes at least two positive lenses facing the object. The variable aperture is mounted in front of the second lens group and the fixed aperture, which may be proportionally movable, is mounted behind the second lens group. The overall lens system satisfies the following conditions: ##EQU1## wherein: Z is the zoom ratio (Z=f.sub.T /f.sub.W), PA1 f.sub.1 is the focal length of the first lens groups, PA1 f.sub.2 is the focal length of the second lens group, PA1 f.sub.W is the focal length in the wide angle position, PA1 f.sub.T is the focal length in the telescopic or narrow angle position, and PA1 r.sub.I is the radius of curvature of the lens surface facing the object of the positive lens nearest to the image in the first lens group.
reason: The patent discloses a specific optical lens design defined by mathematical conditions (zoom ratio, focal length ratios, curvature constraints) that are inherently field-specific to optical engineering. While the lens group arrangement and aperture placement are described, these represent standard optical design techniques rather than a generalizable problem-solving mechanism applicable to other fields.

abstract: A device enabling the operator of an internal combustion engine to visually inspect the quality and level of a fluid held within an associated fluid sump of the engine, transmission, or other adjacent fluid sump. The device operates directly from the vacuum system of the associated engine to selectively draw fluid from the sump upwardly into a viewing chamber. A lamp behind the chamber illuminates the fluid to facilitate visual inspection. If the fluid is below a prescribed level, no fluid will be drawn into the chamber, thereby indicating to the operator that the fluid level is below a specified minimum. The device may also be provided with a continuous monitoring system whereby fluid may be initially drawn into the visual inspection chamber and held there indefinitely or until the fluid drops below a prescribed level. When this happens, the continuous monitoring system may function to activate an annunciator giving warning to the engine operator that the fluid level is low.
problem: Visually inspecting the quality and level of fluid in an enclosed engine sump without manual sampling, and providing automatic warning when fluid drops below a prescribed minimum level.
constraint: The device must operate directly from the engine's vacuum system without external power, and the level threshold is mechanically fixed by the relative positioning of the chamber intake and the sump fluid surface.
mechanism: A vacuum-driven system draws fluid from a reservoir into a transparent viewing chamber for visual inspection. The fluid level threshold is determined by the relative positioning of the chamber intake and the reservoir fluid surface: when the reservoir level is above the intake, fluid is drawn in and becomes visible; when below, no fluid enters the chamber, signaling a low-level condition. A continuous monitoring mode can retain drawn fluid and trigger an indicator when the level drops below the threshold.
mechanism_raw: The device taps into the engine's existing vacuum system to draw fluid upward from the sump into a transparent viewing chamber. A lamp illuminates the chamber for visual inspection. The fluid level threshold is mechanically self-indicating: if the fluid level in the sump is above the chamber's intake point, fluid is drawn in and visible; if below, no fluid enters the chamber, immediately signaling a low-level condition. A continuous monitoring mode can hold drawn fluid indefinitely and trigger an annunciator when the level drops below the threshold.
