residual_terms: ["vacuum system", "transparent viewing chamber", "chamber intake", "fluid level threshold", "annunciator"]

abstract: Apparatus for controlling the closing limit of a carburetor throttle valve in a motor vehicle having an automatic transmission with a shift control that includes a governor producing a speed-dependent pressure. The apparatus comprises a vacuum-actuated device for varying the closing limit of the throttle valve in dependence upon the vacuum applied thereto; a vacuum line connecting the vacuum actuated device with a source of intake manifold vacuum downstream of the throttle valve; a hydraulic or solenoid valve arranged in the vacuum line for controlling the vacuum transmitted by the line; and a hydraulic or electrical circuit for controlling this valve in dependence upon the speed-dependent pressure produced by the governor.
problem: Adjusting the closing limit of a throttle valve in a motor vehicle based on vehicle speed, so that engine performance is coordinated with automatic transmission shift behavior.
constraint: The system must coordinate the speed-dependent governor pressure with the vacuum actuation of the throttle using the transmission's existing governor as the speed sensor, and the vacuum line valve must respond proportionally to the governor pressure to achieve smooth throttle modulation.
mechanism: A speed-dependent hydraulic pressure source controls a valve positioned in a vacuum line. This valve modulates the vacuum transmitted to an actuation device that varies the closing limit of a control element. The system creates a cascade: speed → hydraulic pressure → valve modulation → vacuum variation → control element position adjustment, coordinating engine performance with transmission behavior.
mechanism_raw: A governor produces a speed-dependent hydraulic pressure that controls a valve (hydraulic or solenoid) positioned in a vacuum line. This valve modulates the vacuum transmitted from the intake manifold to a vacuum-actuated device that varies the throttle valve's closing limit. Thus, vehicle speed indirectly adjusts the throttle's control range through a cascade: speed → governor pressure → valve modulation → vacuum variation → throttle position adjustment.
residual_terms: ["governor pressure", "vacuum line", "vacuum-actuated device", "throttle valve closing limit", "proportional response"]

abstract: A tunnel oven of elongated configuration and having at least one movable carriage therein for transporting ceramic products to be baked through the tunnel, is provided with a reversible blower operative to generate a stream of gas having reciprocating movement which passes through the tunnel in a direction opposite to the direction of movement of the carriage. The opposing sides of the tunnel are provided with inwardly extending projections and intervening recesses which give the overall tunnel a zig-zag or wave configuration; and fire stations are located adjacent the various projections or recesses for heating the reciprocating stream of gas and for producing cross currents which cause the stream to flow along a generally sinuous path through the tunnel in a flow direction opposite to the direction of movement of the carriage.
problem: Uniformly heating ceramic products as they move through a tunnel oven, ensuring thorough and even thermal treatment despite the continuous motion of the products.
constraint: The gas flow direction must be opposite to the carriage movement direction, and the tunnel geometry (projections, recesses, fire station placement) must be precisely arranged to create the sinuous flow path and cross currents without impeding the reciprocating gas stream or the moving carriage.
mechanism: A reversible flow generator creates a gas stream that moves through a tunnel in the direction opposite to a product-carrying carriage. The tunnel walls are configured with inwardly extending projections and intervening recesses, creating a sinuous flow path. Heating elements positioned adjacent to these projections and recesses heat the reciprocating gas stream and produce cross currents, causing the gas to follow a generally wave-like path through the tunnel. This counter-flow combined with geometric sinuosity ensures that the gas repeatedly crosses the product path from multiple angles, providing uniform heating.
mechanism_raw: A reversible blower generates a gas stream that flows through the tunnel in the direction opposite to the product-carrying carriage movement. The tunnel walls are configured with inwardly extending projections and intervening recesses, creating a zig-zag or wave geometry. Fire stations positioned adjacent to these projections and recesses heat the reciprocating gas stream and produce cross currents, causing the gas to follow a generally sinuous path through the tunnel. This counter-flow combined with geometric sinuosity ensures that the gas repeatedly crosses the product path from multiple angles, providing uniform heating.
residual_terms: ["reversible blower", "gas stream", "tunnel geometry", "projections", "recesses", "fire stations", "cross currents", "sinuous path", "counter-flow"]

abstract: This invention relates to a tensioning device for a drive belt for controlling the rotation of aligned members such as spindles of textile machines. According to the invention, a pressing roller is mounted at one movable end of an elastic support formed by two parallel tapes of hardened steel the confronting ends of which are fixed in equi-spaced relation by two spacers, while the other end of the support is rigidly fastened to the machine, so that the axis of the pressing roller is displaceable parallel to itself.
problem: Maintaining consistent belt tension and pressing force on a drive belt while allowing controlled displacement of the pressing roller parallel to itself.
constraint: The support must be elastic enough to permit displacement while maintaining structural integrity and consistent pressure; the parallel tape and spacer arrangement must preserve alignment during deflection.
mechanism: An elastic support structure composed of two parallel compliant elements, with their ends fixed in a spaced relationship, provides a compliant yet aligned mounting for a moving component. The elastic deformation of the elements allows the component's axis to displace parallel to itself while the parallel arrangement and spacing maintain consistent alignment and pressure application.
mechanism_raw: An elastic support formed by two parallel hardened steel tapes, with their confronting ends fixed in equi-spaced relation by spacers, provides compliant yet aligned mounting for a pressing roller. The elastic deformation of the tapes allows the roller axis to displace parallel to itself while the parallel tape structure and spacers maintain consistent spacing and alignment, ensuring uniform pressure application.

abstract: A composite magnetic core assembly for a magnetic head comprises first and second substantially C-shaped portions which are symmetrically arranged with respect to each other. Each of the first and second C-shaped portions comprises a substantially L-shaped back core, a substantially oblique prism shaped head chip and at least one side plate which is made of nonmagnetic and electrically conductive material. The side plate is fixedly attached on one side of the head tip and a portion of one side of the back core for reinforcing the adhesive strength between the head tip and the back core.
problem: Reinforcing the adhesive bond between a magnetic head tip and back core to prevent delamination or separation under mechanical and thermal stress.
constraint: The reinforcement material must be nonmagnetic and electrically conductive to avoid disrupting magnetic performance, while still providing sufficient structural strength to reinforce the bond.
mechanism: A reinforcing element made of nonmagnetic and electrically conductive material is attached to both sides of a joint between two components, bridging the interface. This element distributes mechanical and thermal stress across the joint, while its nonmagnetic and conductive properties ensure it does not disrupt magnetic flux or introduce energy losses.
mechanism_raw: A side plate made of nonmagnetic and electrically conductive material is fixedly attached to both the head tip and the back core, bridging the junction between them. This plate mechanically reinforces the adhesive joint by distributing stress across the interface, while its nonmagnetic and conductive properties ensure it does not interfere with the magnetic flux path or introduce eddy current losses.

abstract: Automobile door lock assembly of push-button type including a rotatable element axially movable with a push-button and an annular element co-axial with the rotatable element. The rotatable element is formed with an axially extending slot having a shoulder defined by a wide and narrow portions of the slot. The annular element has a lug adapted to be placed in the slot of the rotatable element so that, when the lug is placed in the position engageable with the shoulder, the axial movement of the rotatable element is prohibited but, when the rotatable element is rotated to place the lug out of the path of the shoulder, the axial movement of the rotatable element is allowed to release the latch in the lock assembly. The annular element has manually actuatable lever so that it can be actuated into locking position without using a key.
problem: Creating a mechanical interlock that selectively permits or prohibits axial movement of a push-button through combined rotational and axial actuation, without requiring a key.
constraint: The mechanism must reliably lock under axial force while allowing selective release through rotation; the geometric relationship between the lug, slot, and shoulder must ensure positive engagement and disengagement.
mechanism: A mechanical interlock uses a protruding lug on a coaxial annular element positioned within an axially extending slot on a rotatable element. The slot contains a shoulder formed by wide and narrow sections. When the lug engages the shoulder in the narrow section, axial movement is blocked. Rotating the annular element shifts the lug into the wide section, clearing the shoulder and permitting axial movement to release the latch. A manually actuatable lever on the annular element enables locking without a key.
mechanism_raw: A lug on a coaxial annular element is positioned within an axially extending slot on a rotatable element. The slot has a shoulder formed by wide and narrow portions. When the lug engages the shoulder in the narrow portion, axial movement is blocked. Rotating the annular element moves the lug into the wide portion of the slot, clearing the shoulder and allowing axial movement to release the latch. A manually actuatable lever on the annular element enables locking without a key.

abstract: A forced-flow boiler installation and method of operating the same comprising a series circuit of a feed pump, an economizer, an evaporator and a water separator as well as a recirculation line or system containing therein a circulating pump and leading from the water outlet of the separator to the evaporator inlet. Between the feed pump and a subsequently connected closure valve there branches-off a filling line or conduit having a valve and bypassing the economizer and leading to the evaporator inlet. The economizer, at the region of its maximum geodetic height, contains venting means.
problem: Managing water flow distribution and gas venting in a forced-flow boiler system to ensure proper filling, circulation, and operation of the evaporator and economizer.
constraint: The system must balance flow between the main circuit and bypass line while ensuring proper venting at high points; valves must coordinate to control flow routing and prevent undesirable pressure or temperature conditions.
mechanism: A fluid system uses a bypass line branching between a pump and a closure valve to route flow directly to a downstream component while bypassing an intermediate component. Venting means at the highest point of the intermediate component allow trapped gas to be expelled, preventing gas locking. A recirculation line returns fluid from a separator to the downstream component for continuous circulation, enabling selective flow routing during filling or specific operating conditions.
mechanism_raw: A bypass filling line branches off between the feed pump and a closure valve, routing water directly to the evaporator inlet while bypassing the economizer. This allows selective flow routing around the economizer during filling or specific operating conditions. Venting means at the maximum geodetic height of the economizer allow trapped air or steam to be expelled, preventing gas locking. A recirculation line returns water from the separator outlet to the evaporator inlet for continuous circulation.

abstract: An apparatus and method for clamping louvered window panes in the window frame sections of a louvered window structure. The louvered window structure usually includes a plurality of pivotably movable pane supporting elements which have elongate slots to receive the panes. The apparatus comprises a clamping device in the nature of a band having a pair of overlapping terminal portions, which form an envelope section and this band is capable of being disposed over a portion of each window pane supporting element and a portion of the pane which extends beyond the slot formed in the pane supporting element. An individual clamping device is located at each of the opposite ends of each or certain of the window panes. The clamping device includes a locking mechanism which is capable of causing locking engagement of the two terminal portions of the band, such that the clamping device can be clamped about the window frame section and the pane to lockably hold the pane in the window frame structure. In the preferred aspect, the locking mechanism comprises a worm having a screw head which is engageable to be turned only in the locking direction. In this way, the louvered window structure is protected against unauthorized removal of the various louvered window panes.
problem: Clamping and securing louvered window panes in a window frame structure in a manner that prevents unauthorized removal of the panes.
constraint: The clamping force must be sufficient to securely hold the pane while the one-way locking mechanism prevents unauthorized loosening; the band must conform to the geometry of both the supporting element and the pane.
mechanism: A clamping band with overlapping terminal portions is wrapped around a supporting element and a portion of a panel extending beyond a slot. A one-way actuation mechanism engages the overlapping terminals, tightening the band to clamp the panel and supporting element together. The one-way mechanism prevents loosening, creating a tamper-resistant securement that requires specific directional input to release.
mechanism_raw: A band with overlapping terminal portions is disposed over both the pane supporting element and the portion of the pane extending beyond the slot. A worm drive with a screw head that can be turned only in the locking direction engages the overlapping terminal portions, tightening the band to clamp the pane and supporting element together. The one-way screw head prevents the worm from being turned in the loosening direction, creating a tamper-resistant securement.
residual_terms: ["clamping band", "overlapping terminal portions", "one-way actuation mechanism", "tamper-resistant securement"]

abstract: A composition of matter is provided comprising a polyurethane latex and a polymer of at least one vinyl monomer, said polymer having been obtained by free radical polymerization of said monomer in the presence of the latex and being characterized as a hard, resinous material at temperatures below about 60.degree. C.
problem: Creating a composite material with enhanced hardness and thermal stability at specific temperatures.
constraint: The polymerization must occur within the latex phase to ensure compatibility and avoid phase separation, while maintaining the material's integrity below 60°C.
mechanism: In-situ polymerization of monomers within a dispersed polymer phase forms a reinforcing polymer network that enhances mechanical and thermal properties of the matrix, while maintaining structural integrity below a critical temperature threshold to prevent phase separation.
mechanism_raw: In-situ free-radical polymerization of vinyl monomers in the presence of a polyurethane latex, forming a hard, resinous polymer phase that reinforces the latex matrix below a critical temperature threshold.

abstract: An axial-piston machine such as an axial-piston motor or, preferably, an axial-piston pump, has a cylinder drum rotatable in a chamber defined by the machine housing, the cylinder bores at low pressure communicating with the interior of the housing. Only part of the end of the cylinder drum turned toward a displacing slide covers the surface of this slide which is provided with an arcuate groove for communication with the cylinder bores under elevated pressure while the control surface of this slide only covers the high-pressure portion of the surface of the cylinder drum so that the latter overhangs the slide.
problem: Managing pressure communication and flow in an axial-piston machine to optimize displacement efficiency.
constraint: The slide's geometry must balance pressure sealing and mechanical clearance to prevent leakage while allowing smooth rotational movement.
mechanism: A controllably shaped moving element with a variable-geometry groove selectively exposes pressurized fluid ports while isolating low-pressure regions during rotational motion, enabling regulated fluid exchange between chambers.
mechanism_raw: A displacing slide with an arcuate groove and overhanging control surface selectively exposes high-pressure cylinder bores while isolating low-pressure regions, enabling controlled fluid exchange during rotation.

abstract: A monitoring system for a water scalping sand classifying tank, comprising timers for measuring the cumulative total discharge times for at least two key classification stations of the tank over an extended period of time which may include many reblend cycles for the tank. Tolerance limits are established by use of at least two timers for each key station. Any extended variation in the desired ratio of total discharges for the key stations, indicating an input change requiring correction, is signalled by an indicator system coupled to the timers.
problem: Detecting deviations in the operational ratio of key stations in a sand classifying tank over extended periods.
constraint: The system must account for reblend cycles and long-term variability while maintaining sensitivity to meaningful deviations without false alarms.
mechanism: Time-accumulating measurement devices track operational durations for multiple stations, and a comparison system evaluates these values against predefined tolerance thresholds to trigger corrective signals when deviations exceed acceptable limits.
mechanism_raw: Cumulative timers measure discharge durations for multiple stations, and an indicator system compares these values against predefined tolerance limits to signal input changes requiring correction.

abstract: The panels are disposed in parallel to one another and are held in contact with the lower surface of a tabular iceberg by arms or cables attached to anchor points on the upper surface of the iceberg and by gas-filled chambers attached to the panels. The panels are stretched by ballast weights attached to their lower edges.
problem: Maintaining contact between flexible panels and the lower surface of a floating or submerged structure (e.g., an iceberg) under dynamic environmental conditions.
constraint: The buoyancy-to-ballast ratio must be precisely balanced to ensure consistent contact pressure without overcompressing or destabilizing the panels.
mechanism: Adjustable buoyancy elements press flexible panels against a submerged surface, while tensioning weights and anchor points balance contact pressure and stabilize the system under dynamic environmental forces.
mechanism_raw: Gas-filled chambers provide buoyancy to press panels against the structure, while ballast weights stretch the panels and anchor points secure the system to the upper surface.
residual_terms: ["adjustable buoyancy elements", "tensioning weights", "anchor points", "dynamic environmental forces"]

abstract: A heat exchanger of the regenerative type comprising a rotor constructed of corrugated strip layers providing transverse channels extending therethrough. The device is arranged to have separate gas streams directed through different parts of the rotor so that on rotation of the rotor the storage mass effects the exchange of sensible heat between the streams.
problem: Transferring sensible heat between two separate gas streams in a regenerative heat exchanger.
constraint: The rotor's rotation speed and storage mass must be optimized to maximize heat transfer efficiency while minimizing pressure drop across the gas streams.
mechanism: A rotating thermal storage medium alternately absorbs heat from one gas stream and releases it to another during successive cycles, enabling continuous heat transfer through periodic storage and release phases.
mechanism_raw: A rotating rotor composed of corrugated strip layers stores heat from one gas stream as it passes through, then releases it to the other stream during subsequent rotation, enabling continuous heat exchange.
residual_terms: ["rotating thermal storage medium", "successive cycles", "periodic storage and release phases"]

abstract: In the bottom blown process for the refining of molten steel, additional heat is generated for melting greater amounts of scrap, by injecting at least one secondary stream of an oxygen-containing gas to the space above the molten metal bath so as to combust the CO and H.sub.2 evolving therefrom. The excess heat so generated is absorbed both by the bath and the furnace lining, causing overheating and rapid deterioration of the lining. For a given quantum of heat so generated the ability of the molten metal to absorb a greater portion of that heat and thereby maintain the temperature of the furnace lining within the practical limits has been found to depend to a significant extent on the design of the furnace itself. The invention is directed to conducting the refining process in vessels which provide, for a given bath capacity, greater top surface areas than has heretofore been employed.
problem: In bottom-blown molten steel refining, secondary oxygen gas injection generates excess heat that overheats and rapidly deteriorates the furnace lining, limiting the amount of scrap that can be melted.
constraint: The vessel must provide greater top surface area for a given bath capacity without compromising structural integrity or bath containment.
mechanism: Increasing the ratio of exposed surface area to contained volume in a reaction vessel allows the processed material to absorb a greater portion of internally generated thermal energy, thereby reducing heat transfer to the vessel walls and maintaining wall temperature within practical limits.
mechanism_raw: Increasing the top surface area of the refining vessel relative to bath capacity allows the molten metal to absorb a greater portion of the generated heat, thereby reducing heat transfer to the furnace lining and maintaining its temperature within practical limits.

abstract: A method and means for burning corn and corncobs is described. The apparatus includes a conical or pyramidal shaped perforated floor having a central opening formed therein which is in communication with a first conveyor which supplies the material to be burned thereto. A second conveyor extends around the periphery of the floor for carrying away the ashes of the burned material. The first conveyor forces the corncobs or corn upwardly through the central opening to form a mound or pile of material thereon. The mound of material is ignited and air is forced upwardly through the perforated floor to enhance combustion so that the material is substantially completely burned. The products of combustion are passed upwardly through a heat exchanger and filtered through the material delivered to the first conveyor before being exhausted to the atmosphere.
problem: Burning irregular biomass fuels like corn and corncobs requires complete combustion while managing ash removal and heat recovery in a single integrated system.
constraint: The system must balance upward air flow for combustion enhancement with controlled fuel mound geometry to ensure complete burning and efficient heat recovery without disrupting ash removal.
mechanism: A shaped perforated support structure forms a mound of combustible material that is ignited, while upward gas flow through the perforations enhances combustion; residue is continuously removed by a peripheral transport mechanism while combustion gases pass through a heat recovery unit and are filtered through the fuel bed before exhaust.
mechanism_raw: A conical/pyramidal perforated floor with a central opening forms a mound of fuel that is ignited, while upward air flow through the perforations enhances combustion; ash is continuously removed by a peripheral conveyor while combustion gases pass through a heat exchanger and are filtered through the fuel bed before exhaust.

abstract: A process for preserving process cheese which comprises admixing with natural cheese during the steps of preparing process cheese from natural cheese sorbic acid-containing powder or granules having particle diameter of 300 microns or more comprising 5-90% by weight of finely divided sorbic acid and 10-95% by weight of an easily water-soluble substance which is a solid at normal temperature.
problem: Preserving process cheese from microbial spoilage while maintaining its texture and quality during processing.
constraint: The sorbic acid formulation must have sufficiently large particle size and appropriate carrier composition to ensure controlled release without adversely affecting the texture or processing characteristics of the cheese.
mechanism: An antimicrobial agent is delivered as solid particles with a minimum size threshold, composed of a concentrated active component and a water-soluble carrier matrix, allowing controlled release of the agent during material processing.
mechanism_raw: Sorbic acid is delivered as solid powder or granules with particle diameter of 300 microns or more, composed of 5-90% finely divided sorbic acid and 10-95% water-soluble solid carrier, allowing controlled release of the antimicrobial agent during cheese processing.

abstract: The automobile security lock is of the kind having a body in which is rotatable a cylinder having pistons radially movable therein by a cylindrical key having notches formed therein. The body also has pistons which cooperate with the pistons in the cylinder. The pistons of the cylinder are slidable into radial cylindrical bores formed in the cylinder. Likewise the pistons in the body slide into radial slots in the body. On entry of the correct key the external extremities of the cylinder pistons lie flush with the external surface of the cylinder in such a manner as to permit rotation of the cylinder in relation to the body. However, on entry of an incorrect key where the corresponding notch is either insufficiently deep or too deep the extremities of the cylinder pistons enter said radial slots in said body or the internal extremities of the body pistons said radial bores in the cylinder to effect locking of the cylinder in relation to the body.
problem: Preventing unauthorized rotation of a cylinder in an automobile security lock when an incorrect key is used, while allowing rotation with the correct key.
constraint: The piston and slot geometry must be precisely matched so that only the correct key aligns all pistons flush while any key deviation causes engagement with the locking slots.
mechanism: Movable elements in both the rotating and stationary components cooperate such that with the correct input, element extremities lie flush with the rotating surface permitting rotation; with an incorrect input, mismatched depths cause elements to enter opposing radial receptacles, mechanically locking the rotating component to the stationary component.
mechanism_raw: Radial pistons in both the cylinder and body cooperate such that with the correct key, piston extremities lie flush with the cylinder surface permitting rotation; with an incorrect key, mismatched notch depths cause pistons to enter opposing radial slots/bores, mechanically locking the cylinder to the body.

abstract: Fiber containing plaster boards are prepared by superimposing a plurality of board blanks one on top of the other such that the direction of the fiber orientation in the superimposed blanks deviates one from the other. The board blanks are formed in a conventional manner from a suspension of calcium sulfate capable of setting, reinforcing fibers and a quantity of water beyond the quantity of water necessary for setting the calcium sulfate capable of setting. After mechanically removing excess water from the suspension to form the board blanks, two or more of these blanks are placed one on top of the other and are connected under pressure and dried. Thereafter, a predetermined number of board blanks having a direction of the fiber orientation deviating one from the other, are placed one on top of the other and are pressed together prior to or during the setting of the calcium sulfate.
problem: Producing fiber-reinforced plaster boards with improved structural properties by controlling fiber orientation across multiple layers.
constraint: The fiber orientation directions must deviate sufficiently between layers to provide multidirectional reinforcement while maintaining adequate bonding between layers during pressing and setting.
mechanism: Multiple layered structures with reinforcement elements oriented in different directions are superimposed and compressed together, either before or during material setting, creating a composite structure with multidirectional reinforcement.
mechanism_raw: Multiple board blanks with fibers oriented in different directions are superimposed and pressed together under pressure, either before or during calcium sulfate setting, creating a composite structure with multidirectional fiber reinforcement.

abstract: A time detecting switch for an alarm clock comprises phase detecting type slide switches between rotatable coaxially mounted pairs of time wheels and detecting wheels which are rotated to the phases corresponding to an alarm signalling time according to an alarm signalling time setting. One of the pair of the two kinds of wheels comprises a disk of electrically insulating material having a hole therethrough, and an electrically conductive switch plate mounted on one face of the disk has an electric contacting portion which extends through the hole in the disk and bent to form a contacting face in the same plane with the other face of the disk.
problem: Creating a reliable mechanical-electrical time-based switch that triggers an alarm at a precise setting.
constraint: Requires precise mechanical alignment of wheels and conductive components to ensure accurate phase detection without slippage or misalignment.
mechanism: A rotational mechanism where aligned positions of coaxial components create an electrical connection, translating angular alignment into a triggering signal. Conductive elements bridge a circuit when rotational phases match, mechanically converting positional alignment into an electrical output.
mechanism_raw: Coaxially mounted time wheels and detecting wheels with phase-aligned conductive contacts: rotation of the wheels to a specific phase causes a conductive switch plate to bridge an electrical circuit through a hole in an insulating disk, mechanically translating rotational alignment into an electrical signal.

abstract: Fluid control valve apparatus is provided having a directional control valve for metering passage of fluid from a supply passage to a feeder passage for first actuator. A pressure compensating valve is provided for regulating flow through the directional control valve and for delivering excess fluid to a compensating valve output port for power operation of a second actuator. A main relief valve is connected to the first actuator feeder passage downstream from a metering portion of the directional control valve for sensing a first actuator stall condition. The main relief valve, when actuated, delivers fluid to a tank from a supply passage, through the metering portion of the directional control valve, and a relief passage including the main relief valve upon sensing an overload condition. The rate of flow through the relief passage is subject to limitation only by the metering portion of the direction control valve.
problem: Managing fluid flow to two actuators while protecting against overload conditions in a hydraulic system.
constraint: The relief flow rate is constrained by the metering valve's capacity, creating a trade-off between overload protection and system responsiveness.
mechanism: A fluid control system that directs flow to primary and secondary actuators via a metering valve, with pressure compensation and relief flow through the same metering component to balance overload protection and responsiveness. Excess pressure is routed to a reservoir through the metering valve's inherent restriction when overload is detected.
mechanism_raw: A directional control valve meters fluid to a primary actuator and routes excess fluid to a secondary actuator via a pressure compensating valve, while a main relief valve bypasses fluid to a tank through the same metering portion when overload is detected, using the metering valve's inherent flow restriction to limit relief flow.

abstract: A hair cutting appliance includes a hair handling and vacuuming device having a hair passageway extending through the device from a forward intake portion to a rearward exhaust portion thereof. A barber's shear is positioned fixedly with respect to the device to have its cutting teeth disposed transversely of an intermediate portion of the hair passageway. A vacuum cleaner hose is attached to the rearward portion of the hair handling device. The hair handling device includes a first inclined hair ramp disposed between a forward edge of the forward portion of the device and the barber's shear cutting teeth, the interior end of this ramp terminating adjacent to but forwardly of the shear cutting teeth. A second inclined hair ramp is disposed between the forward edge of the forward portion of the hair handling device, and an interior end of this second ramp terminates in parallel spaced relation to the interior end of the first ramp and in spaced relation to and in alignment with the cutting teeth of the shear blades of the barber's shear. A paddle wheel is mounted inside of the passageway to have paddles which pass from closely adjacent the interior end of the second ramp to closely adjacent the cutting teeth to carry hair passing between the interior ends of the ramps into the cutting teeth. A plurality of hair length determining sleeves of various lengths are provided to be attached to the forward portion of the hair handling device to be placed in contact with the scalp of a customer to receive a haircut, thus determining and fixing the minimum distance between the shear blades and the scalp.
problem: Efficiently cutting hair while simultaneously removing cut material and maintaining consistent cutting length.
constraint: The cutting length is constrained by the physical spacing of the sleeves, requiring precise mechanical adjustment to maintain consistent results.
mechanism: A transport system moves material into a cutting zone with transversely positioned blades, while a removal mechanism extracts cut material and adjustable spacing elements maintain consistent cutting length. Inclined guides direct material into the cutting zone, and a vacuum or airflow removes debris.
mechanism_raw: A conveyor system (paddle wheel) transports hair into cutting teeth positioned transversely to a passageway, while inclined ramps guide hair into the cutting zone and a vacuum removes cut hair. Length-determining sleeves fix the distance between the cutting teeth and the scalp.

abstract: A thermostat metal characterized by low cost has a substantially linear temperature response over a wide temperature range from 0.degree. to 800.degree. F. and is adapted for wide use for temperature control purposes in a whole variety of electrical cooking appliances, particularly when used in combination with integral but thermally-inactive support means for the thermostat metal. The thermostat metal comprises a layer of metal of relatively high coefficient of thermal expansion having a nominal composition by weight of 72 percent manganese, 18 percent copper and 10 percent nickel metallurgically bonded to a layer of metal of relatively lower coefficient of thermal expansion comprising 430 Stainless Steel, whereby the bimetal material displays a sufficiently high and linear flexivity over a wide temperature range to be useful in the various different types of thermostats used in cooking appliances.
problem: Achieving a low-cost thermostat with a linear thermal response over a wide temperature range for cooking appliances.
constraint: The material composition must balance thermal expansion coefficients to avoid non-linear deformation or hysteresis over the operating range.
mechanism: A thermal actuator using bonded materials with differing thermal expansion coefficients to produce linear deformation across a temperature range, enabling precise actuation without calibration. The differential expansion of layered materials generates predictable mechanical displacement in response to temperature changes.
mechanism_raw: A bimetallic strip composed of a high-expansion alloy (manganese-copper-nickel) bonded to a low-expansion alloy (stainless steel) produces linear flexivity across a wide temperature range, enabling precise thermal actuation without complex calibration.

abstract: Method and apparatus for heat treatment of comminuted raw material of the type used, for example, for the production of cement in which the material is preheated in a preheater by means of hot exhaust gases from a kiln, the material is separately calcined for the deacidification of a portion of the calcium carbonate present and is subsequently burnt to completion in the kiln. The specific improvement of the present invention involves utilizing undispersed coarse pieces of fuel for the separate calcination and conducting the separate calcination at the material inlet end to the kiln.
problem: Improving energy efficiency and material processing in cement kiln heat treatment by optimizing fuel use and calcination timing.
constraint: The calcination process must occur at the material inlet to avoid disrupting downstream kiln operations, requiring precise control of fuel particle size and combustion timing.
mechanism: A staged combustion process where coarse fuel is combusted in a separate preheating zone to drive material processing before final burning, utilizing exhaust gases for preheating and controlling fuel particle size for timing. Heat release is sequenced to optimize energy transfer and material transformation.
mechanism_raw: Using undispersed coarse fuel in a separate calcination step at the kiln inlet allows staged heat release, preheating raw material with exhaust gases while combusting coarse fuel to drive calcination before final burning in the kiln.

abstract: Method of low-loss thermal energy storage in and withdrawal from a heat accumulator connected with an energy source and a heat consumer in a circulatory system through which a heat-carrying flow medium circulates which includes passing the flow medium through the energy source so as to withdraw thermal energy from the energy source and effect absorption of the thermal energy by the flow medium, guiding the flow medium in respective layers within the heat accumulator in a direction from the center of the heat accumulator toward the periphery thereof so as to store the thermal energy in a heat storage mass disposed in the heat accumulator; and guiding the flow medium in the layers thereof through the heat accumulator in a direction from the periphery of the heat accumulator to the center thereof, and passing the flow medium from the heat accumulator through the consumer so as to withdraw thermal energy therefrom and transfer it to the consumer; and apparatus therefor.
problem: Efficiently storing and retrieving thermal energy in a heat accumulator while maintaining low losses during charge and discharge cycles.
constraint: Balancing radial flow directionality with structural integrity of the heat storage mass to prevent thermal short-circuiting or uneven energy distribution.
mechanism: A bidirectional flow medium is directed through a storage mass in a controlled radial pattern: during energy input, the medium flows outward from a central inlet to an outer periphery, embedding thermal energy within the storage mass; during energy extraction, the medium flows inward from the periphery to the center, retrieving stored heat. This directional layering of flow ensures controlled thermal energy distribution and minimizes mixing losses between charge and discharge cycles.
mechanism_raw: Directional layering of flow medium within the heat accumulator: during storage, the medium flows radially outward from the center to the periphery, embedding thermal energy in the storage mass; during retrieval, the medium flows radially inward from the periphery to the center, extracting stored heat. This bidirectional layered flow ensures controlled thermal energy distribution and minimizes mixing losses.

abstract: A heating apparatus for the vaporization of a mixture of two liquefied gases in chemical equilibrium with a binary compound thereof includes a vertically disposed enclosed vessel having a lower liquid zone to which the mixture to be vaporized is supplied as a liquid from an external supply source and an upper vaporized gas zone from which gas can be removed for use. A vertically disposed heating element, which may be an electric heating element, steam tube, and the like, extends downwardly in the vessel through the vaporized gas zone and terminates above the portion of the liquid zone communicating with the liquid supply and is adapted to supply sufficient heat to vaporize a gaseous mixture from the liquid zone. A housing is disposed about the heating element in spaced relationship thereto and a heat transfer medium is contained within the space. The heating element is controlled by a control unit responsive to a thermal sensing element disposed in the interior of the housing and arranged to monitor the temperature of the portion of housing in contact with the vaporized gas zone.
problem: Precisely controlling the vaporization of a liquefied gas mixture in a vertical vessel while preventing overheating or incomplete vaporization.
constraint: Maintaining thermal isolation between the heating element and liquid zone while enabling responsive temperature feedback to avoid overheating or inefficient vaporization.
mechanism: A heating element is positioned within a vapor zone and thermally coupled to a heat transfer medium that is isolated from the liquid zone. A temperature sensor monitors the vapor zone and adjusts the heating element's output via a feedback loop, ensuring optimal heat delivery to the liquid zone without direct contact between the heating element and the liquid.
mechanism_raw: A vertically disposed heating element is positioned within the vapor zone and surrounded by a housing containing a heat transfer medium. A thermal sensor inside the housing monitors the temperature of the vapor zone and adjusts the heating element's output via a feedback loop, ensuring optimal heat delivery to the liquid zone without direct contact between the heating element and the liquid.

abstract: A coin packaging machine in which different kinds of coins are packaged is provided. The coin packaging machine is provided with a mechanism for supplying coins, a mechanism for transporting the supplied coins while selecting a kind of coins out during transportation, a mechanism for accumulating transported coins, a delivery mechanism for receiving accumulated coins and delivering the coins from receiving position to packaging position, a mechanism for supplying a web of paper within packaging zone and a mechanism for clamping the packaged coins. The coin packaging machine may further include a mechanism for making adjustments of various kinds of the above mechanisms in accordance with the thickness and the width of the coins to be packaged.
problem: Automatically sorting and packaging different types of coins with varying dimensions without manual reconfiguration.
constraint: Achieving rapid and precise mechanical adjustments during transport and packaging to accommodate varying coin dimensions without disrupting throughput.
mechanism: A transport mechanism dynamically adjusts its configuration (e.g., width, thickness) in real-time based on detected characteristics of items being conveyed, selecting item types during movement. Accumulated items are then transferred to a packaging zone where a clamping mechanism adapts to the specific dimensions of the selected items, enabling seamless handling of diverse item sizes without manual reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A transport mechanism dynamically selects coin types during movement by adjusting its configuration (e.g., width, thickness) in real-time based on detected coin characteristics. Accumulated coins are then transferred to a packaging zone where a clamping mechanism adapts to the specific dimensions of the selected coins, enabling seamless handling of diverse coin sizes.

abstract: A power generator utilizing the full volumetric expansion of water upon its change from the liquid phase to the solid phase (ice). The generator includes a chamber having heat transmitting, fluid impervious, flexible walls. The chamber is filled with water. A pressure-containing housing has an internal cavity in which the chamber is located in spaced relation to the housing. The space between the housing and the flexible walls of the chamber is filled with a fluid which is circulated through the cavity. A conduit connected to the housing provides flow communication between the cavity and means for utilizing moving fluid, such as a fluid driven motor. The phase of the water in the chamber is changed from liquid to solid so that the water expands in volume. Expansion of the water expands the flexible walls of the chamber to displace a proportional amount of fluid from the housing through the conduit, the moving displaced fluid serving as a power medium to drive the motor to do work.
problem: Converting the volumetric expansion of water during freezing into usable mechanical work for power generation.
constraint: Managing the timing and magnitude of phase change expansion to ensure consistent fluid displacement and motor operation without structural failure of the flexible walls.
mechanism: A flexible-walled chamber filled with a phase-change material is enclosed in a fluid-filled cavity. When the material undergoes a phase change that causes volumetric expansion, the flexible walls displace the surrounding fluid, which is then directed through a conduit to drive a fluid-powered motor. The phase change directly translates into mechanical displacement of the fluid medium.
mechanism_raw: A flexible-walled chamber filled with water is enclosed in a fluid-filled cavity. When water freezes and expands, the flexible walls displace the surrounding fluid, which is then directed through a conduit to drive a fluid-powered motor. The phase change from liquid to solid directly translates into mechanical displacement of the fluid medium.

abstract: A method and apparatus is disclosed for use in converting heat to electrical energy and comprises a plurality of capacitors which have a temperature dependent capacitance. Heat is used to decrease the dielectric constant in the capacitors causing charge to expand from the capacitors into an associated circuit and do electrical work. The invention also includes reeds which are caused to vibrate by the flow of vapor carrying heat between stages. These reeds serve as thermal switches which pulse heat at the proper frequency and phase through a large number of stacked capacitors. The efficiency of the apparatus is optimized by operating the individual capacitors through cycles approximating Carnot cycles.
problem: Efficiently converting low-grade thermal energy into electrical energy using temperature-dependent capacitive effects.
constraint: Synchronizing the thermal switching frequency and phase across multiple capacitors to approximate Carnot cycle efficiency while minimizing heat loss between stages.
mechanism: Capacitors with temperature-dependent dielectric constants are stacked and thermally switched by vibrating elements that pulse heat between stages. As heat decreases the dielectric constant, charge expands from the capacitors into an external circuit, performing electrical work. The vibrating elements act as synchronized thermal switches to optimize the timing and phase of heat transfer across the capacitor array.
mechanism_raw: Capacitors with temperature-dependent dielectric constants are stacked and thermally switched by vibrating reeds that pulse heat between stages. As heat decreases the dielectric constant, charge expands from the capacitors into an external circuit, performing electrical work. The reeds act as synchronized thermal switches to optimize the timing and phase of heat transfer across the capacitor array.

abstract: A drafting set, including a drawing board and a T-square, the board having a foldable easel on its rear side for supporting the board in various adjustable positions, the T-square including a slidable shoe on its outward end for bearing against an edge of the board which is opposite an edge against which the T-square crosshead bears, and permanent magnet means holding the shoe and crosshead from falling away from the board edges.
problem: Maintaining adjustable positioning of drafting tools (T-square shoe and crosshead) against board edges without unintended displacement during use.
constraint: Balancing the need for secure retention during operation with the requirement for manual adjustability of the T-square components.
mechanism: Use a passive retention element to apply a holding force against opposing surfaces so a sliding component remains in a selected position during operation while still permitting manual repositioning.
mechanism_raw: Permanent magnets provide passive retention force to hold the slidable shoe and crosshead against opposing board edges, enabling stable alignment while allowing manual repositioning.
residual_terms: ["passive retention element", "holding force", "opposing surfaces", "sliding component", "manual repositioning"]

abstract: A telescope made only of spherical mirrors including a first mirror system comprising a first, concave spherical mirror and a second, convex spherical mirror have a common center of curvature, the ratio of the radius of said first, concave mirror to said second convex mirror being approximately .sqroot.5+1:.sqroot.5-1, said first mirror arranged to intersect input rays of collimated light and to direct them to said second mirror, said first and second mirrors arranged off axis so as to not obstruct the light path to said first mirror; and a second mirror system comprising at least a third, concave mirror and a fourth, convex mirror having a common center of curvature, the radius of said third mirror being approximately twice the radius of said fourth mirror, said third mirror positioned to intersect light reflected from said second mirror and to reflect it to said fourth mirror, said fourth mirror reflecting light back to said third mirror from which it is reflected to form a real image, the optical axis of said system being defined by a line between the centers of curvature of said first and second systems.
problem: Correcting spherical aberration in telescopes constructed solely from spherical mirrors, which are easier to manufacture than aspherical alternatives.
constraint: Achieving aberration correction using only spherical mirrors, which inherently introduce aberrations, while avoiding light path obstruction.
mechanism: Arrange reflective elements with specific geometric proportions and off-axis positioning so that wavefront distortions introduced by each element are redirected and superimposed in a manner that causes mutual cancellation, producing a corrected output.
mechanism_raw: Arranging spherical mirrors with specific radius ratios (e.g., √5+1:√5−1 and 2:1) and off-axis positioning to redirect light paths such that aberrations from individual mirrors cancel out, forming a corrected optical system.

abstract: A construction system comprises a lattice girder reinforcement and a formwork for producing double-skinned concrete ceiling or wall slabs, with two frames separated from each other. The rising reinforcement of the inner skin is bent towards the outer skin so that the top inner skin support edge remains undisturbed and extends to the top outer skin edge. It comprises a reinforced haunched concrete slab each end of which defines a slot through which an interconnecting tie bar extends. Abutting prefabricated slabs are aligned with respective connecting bars inserted into slots and joints between two abutting wall elements. A board with an open hole is slid on the rear end of the connecting bar and bears on the other surface of the wall elements and a turnbuckle at this end bears on the free surface of the board. For thermal insulation of the joints, thermal insulating mats adjacent thereto are so profiled as to produce a continuous space in the longitudinal direction of the joints, the profile of the outside of the space being broader than the inside. A thermally insulating bar with the same profile as the space is inserted therein.
problem: Creating thermally insulated joints between prefabricated double-skinned concrete slabs while maintaining structural continuity and alignment.
constraint: Balancing structural load transfer and joint alignment with the need for uninterrupted thermal insulation across the joint.
mechanism: Interlock thermally resistive elements with complementary profiles and insert connecting members into continuous channels, then use adjustable mechanical fasteners to align and secure adjacent structural units while preserving an uninterrupted thermal barrier.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking profiled thermal insulating mats with matching bars inserted into continuous longitudinal spaces, combined with mechanical fasteners (tie bars, turnbuckles, and boards) to align and secure abutting slabs without disrupting insulation.
residual_terms: ["thermally resistive elements", "complementary profiles", "continuous channels", "adjustable mechanical fasteners", "thermal barrier"]

abstract: Process and apparatus for stress relieving steel sheet, strip, strapping, wire and the like involves the use of high intensity shortwave infrared radiation to heat the steel to the desired stress relieve temperature. The apparatus comprises a furnace having opposing spaced-apart parallel banks of infrared radiation lamps. An electronic programmable controller controls the intensity of the lamps along the banks' length. A roller arrangement is used in passing such steel through the furnace. A device measures the linear speed of the steel. The controller adjusts lamp intensity, as determined by a program based on the signal received from the line speed measuring device. The controller, according to its program, maintains a minimum lamp intensity when the steel is stationary. The controller increases the lamp intensity to a predetermined level to preheat the steel to ensure on line start-up that the steel emerges at the desired stress relieve temperature. The responsiveness of the infrared heating unit provides significant advances in the art of stress relieving steel and economines.
problem: Achieving precise, energy-efficient stress relief in continuously moving steel sheets by maintaining uniform temperature despite variable line speeds.
constraint: Optimizing heating responsiveness and energy use while avoiding overheating or temperature gradients in the steel during variable-speed processing.
mechanism: Dynamically modulate radiant energy output in response to real-time movement rate measurements, applying elevated input during initial acceleration and sustaining a minimum level during idle states to maintain uniform thermal exposure despite variable processing speeds.
mechanism_raw: Using a programmable controller to dynamically adjust infrared lamp intensity based on real-time line speed measurements, preheating during start-up, and maintaining minimum intensity when stationary to ensure consistent thermal treatment.
residual_terms: ["radiant energy output", "movement rate measurements", "elevated input", "minimum level", "thermal exposure"]

abstract: Motor fuel composition comprising a mixture of hydrocarbons in the gasoline boiling range containing in combination a minor amount of a substituted asparagine containing the formula: ##STR1## in which R and R' each represent a secondary or tertiary alkyl or alkylene radical having from about 7 to about 20 carbon atoms and a minor amount of a carbonic acid ester having the formula: EQU R'O(CH.sub.2 CH.sub.2 O).sub.n OCO--(RO).sub.x --CO(OCH.sub.2 CH.sub.2).sub.n OR' in which R is a divalent aliphatic hydrocarbon radical, containing 2 to 10 carbon atoms, R' is hydrogen or an aliphatic hydrocarbon radical containing 2 to 18 carbon atoms, x has a value from 1 to 4 and n has a value from 0 to 4.
reason: The patent describes a chemical fuel composition with specific additives but does not disclose a causal functional mechanism beyond the chemical interaction of the listed compounds. The problem (improving fuel performance) is addressed by material selection rather than a transferable process or structural principle.

abstract: A wide-band vibration damper for damping sound propagating in a solid body includes at least one horn member having a broad end or side and a tapering end. The broad horn side or end is rigidly connected to the solid body which is to be dampened in its vibration. The tapering end of the horn member is connected to a supporting rigid point through a damping material such as a foam material or the like.
problem: Damping sound or vibration energy propagating through a solid body without compromising the body's structural function
constraint: The horn must be rigidly coupled at the broad end to efficiently extract vibrational energy from the body, while the narrow end must connect through compliant damping material to a rigid support point — balancing energy extraction efficiency against the need to avoid over-constraining the vibrating body
mechanism: A rigidly coupled, tapered energy-directing member is attached to a vibrating body at its broad end and connected at its narrow end to a compliant energy-dissipating element, which interfaces with a rigid support. The tapering geometry acts as an impedance transformer, concentrating vibrational energy toward the narrow end where the compliant element converts it into dissipated energy, extracting energy from the system at the point of highest stress concentration while preserving the body's structural function.
mechanism_raw: A tapered horn member is rigidly attached at its broad end to the vibrating solid body and connected at its narrow end to a rigid support through damping material. The tapering geometry acts as an acoustic impedance transformer, concentrating and channeling vibrational energy toward the narrow end where the damping material converts it into dissipated energy (heat), effectively extracting energy from the system at the point of highest stress concentration

abstract: A method of precipitating calcium borates from an aqueous mixture of calcium chloride and borax is disclosed. The yield of calcium borate precipitates can be increased by increasing the concentration of borax. Preferably, an increase in the calcium concentration also is employed. In general, it was found that properties of compacted glass batch produced from these calcium borates compare favorably with those compacted from standard glass batches.
reason: The patent describes simply increasing reactant concentration to drive a precipitation reaction forward, which is a basic application of chemical equilibrium principles (Le Chatelier's principle) rather than a novel causal mechanism. No underlying functional relationship is described beyond standard concentration-dependent solubility.

abstract: The present invention relates to a plating bath for electroplating various metals with chromium, prepared from 100 g to 1600 g chromium trioxide per liter, 0.3 weight percent to 15 weight percent Cl (chlorine or chloride ions) calculated on the chromium trioxide, and/or 0.3 to 10 weight percent I (iodine and/or iodide ions) calculated on the chromium trioxide said plating bath optionally containing also from 0.3 weight percent to 2 weight percent sulfate ions calculated on the chromium trioxide, and to a process of electroplating of metals from such plating baths, which is effected at a temperature between room temperature and about 60.degree. C. at a current density from 10 A/dm.sup.2 to about 270 A/dm.sup.2.
reason: The patent specifies composition ranges and operating parameters for a known electroplating process. The use of halide ions as catalysts/conductivity enhancers in electroplating is a well-established chemical principle, and the patent merely optimizes parameter ranges rather than describing a novel causal mechanism.

abstract: Relatively fine materials are separated from bulky materials by a two-tier screen assembly mounted on springs and shaken by an off balance drive. The screen assembly spans the space between two parallel plates which are joined by staggered crossbeams. An upper screen is supported by longitudinal bars which rest across upper crossbeams, and two lower screens rest on lower crossbeams. The crossbeams are joined by a longitudinal center plate. In use, the forces of heavy weights tending to bend a given crossbeam are transmitted through the center plate to the joined crossbeams to reduce the strain on the single beam.
problem: Separating fine materials from bulky materials using a shaken screen assembly while maintaining structural integrity under heavy loading without excessive bending or failure of individual support beams
constraint: The center plate must be rigid enough to effectively transfer and distribute bending forces between crossbeams, but must not overly stiffen the assembly to the point where it impedes the shaking motion necessary for material separation
mechanism: A longitudinal structural linking member connects and distributes forces between spaced-apart support beams of a shaken screen assembly. When external loads induce bending forces on one beam, the linking member transmits these forces to adjacent beams, distributing the load across multiple structural members and reducing peak strain on any single beam, while permitting sufficient flexibility to allow the shaking motion required for material separation.
mechanism_raw: Crossbeams supporting the screen tiers are structurally linked by a longitudinal center plate. When heavy material loads cause bending forces on one crossbeam, the center plate transmits these forces to adjacent joined crossbeams, distributing the load across multiple structural members and reducing peak strain on any single beam

abstract: A drawing apparatus provided with calculative function of a calculation portion. A universal parallel ruler in which operating keys and a calculation result display portion for operating the calculative function are disposed on the surface of a member, the base of which is connected with an operating grip of a head portion to project sideways of the member, the head portion being disposed to be moved and set to any position on a drawing board by guide rail members or jointed arm members and supporting a vertical scale and a horizontal scale to be set to any angle.
reason: The patent describes integrating a calculator into a drafting tool by mounting electronic components on a ruler-like member. This is a product feature combination (co-locating computation and drafting) rather than a novel causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through an underlying functional relationship.

abstract: High crimp, high strength, hollow rayon fibers or filaments which maintain their hollowness after being immersed in water and subsequently dried, and have a crimped configuration such that there is in excess of about 20 crimps per inch, preferably between about 25-30 crimps per inch, are provided by an in-line process whereby a viscose solution containing a blowing agent is extruded into an aqueous acid coagulating bath. The conditions of the process result in hollow filaments that are substantially irreversible since they remain hollow and do not collapse even after repeated washing and drying cycles. The hollow filaments possess high crimp, such as about 25-30 crimps per inch, which will permit ease in carding and blending with other fibers. The high crimp hollow fibers also possess high strength nearly equivalent to that of high wet modulus rayon fibers.
problem: Creating synthetic fibers that maintain structural integrity (hollowness and crimp) after repeated exposure to moisture and drying cycles, while balancing strength and processability.
constraint: Balancing crimp density (for processability) with structural stability (to prevent collapse) while maintaining tensile strength comparable to high-wet-modulus fibers.
mechanism: A continuous forming process generates internal voids within elongated polymeric structures using a volatile expansion medium, followed by a chemical setting step that permanently fixes the hollow geometry through molecular cross-linking or phase separation. Controlled mechanical deformation during the setting phase introduces periodic structural undulations, creating a high-density surface texture that enables downstream fiber processing while maintaining tensile integrity comparable to high-modulus materials.
mechanism_raw: An in-line extrusion process uses a blowing agent in a viscose solution to generate hollow filaments, combined with controlled coagulation in an aqueous acid bath. The process conditions (e.g., temperature, bath composition) stabilize the hollow structure irreversibly by cross-linking or phase-separation effects, preventing collapse during washing/drying. The high crimp density (20-30 crimps/inch) is achieved through controlled deformation during coagulation, enabling carding compatibility.

abstract: A method for controlling exhaust gases emitted from a direct arc furnace melting furnace. Prior to cleaning the temperature of the gases is sensed and the arc power is regulated in response to the sensed exhaust gas temperature. Also, the cleaning process of the gases is changed depending upon the sensed gas temperature.
problem: Controlling exhaust gas composition and temperature in a direct arc furnace to optimize emission cleanup efficiency and prevent equipment damage.
constraint: Maintaining arc stability and energy efficiency while ensuring cleanup systems operate within optimal temperature ranges to avoid corrosion or incomplete pollutant removal.
mechanism: A sensing element monitors a process parameter that correlates with combustion completeness and contaminant load, and a controller uses this measurement to simultaneously adjust energy input to the reaction zone and modify the operation of downstream purification stages. The controller implements a feedback strategy that maintains the process parameter within an optimal range, ensuring efficient energy utilization while preventing equipment degradation from excessive temperatures or incomplete pollutant removal.
mechanism_raw: A feedback loop senses exhaust gas temperature and dynamically adjusts arc power (to modulate combustion temperature) and alters the gas cleaning process (e.g., scrubber parameters, filtration stages) in real-time. The temperature serves as a proxy for combustion completeness and particulate load, enabling adaptive control of both energy input and cleanup intensity.
residual_terms: ["arc furnace", "arc power", "combustion temperature", "scrubber parameters", "filtration stages", "particulate load"]

abstract: A shopping cart theft prevention system which includes signal sending means and a receiver carried by the cart for receiving a cart-immobilizing or cart-mobilizing signal from the transmitter. The cart includes a frame and a sub-frame pivoted to the frame and bearing spaced cart-supporting wheels, the sub-frame being connected to the frame by a latch. The latch is opened whenever a signal is received from the transmitter by a receiver attached to the cart. Alternatively, a signal can be sent to keep the latch closed, and upon removal of the signal, the latch can be opened. The cart may carry a battery operated solenoid triggered by the radio signal. The plunger of the solenoid may comprise or activate a crossbar on the latch. Thus, when the solenoid is operated, the crossbar is moved so that the latch is open or closed, allowing the sub-frame and associated wheels to automatically swing out of operative position when open, thereby immobilizing the cart.
problem: Preventing unauthorized removal of shopping carts from a designated area by remotely immobilizing or mobilizing them via a mechanical latch system.
constraint: Ensuring reliable signal reception in varied environments while maintaining mechanical robustness and low power consumption for battery-operated components.
mechanism: A wireless receiver detects a control signal and converts received electromagnetic energy into mechanical motion that actuates a latching mechanism. The latching mechanism directly controls the position of a movable sub-frame, which alters the contact state between support elements and a load-bearing surface. The system operates in a fail-safe manner where the presence or absence of the control signal determines whether the support elements are engaged or disengaged, thereby controlling mobility.
mechanism_raw: A radio-frequency signal triggers a solenoid-actuated latch that releases a pivoted sub-frame, causing wheels to swing out of contact with the ground (immobilizing the cart). The system uses a fail-safe design where signal absence or presence directly controls latch state, converting electromagnetic energy into mechanical displacement to alter the cart's mobility.

abstract: A removable sign post holding apparatus including a body portion having a post-receiving opening, a plurality of retaining members disposed around the periphery of the body portion, the retaining members extending along the length of the body portion from a point adjacent the post-receiving opening thereof, a plurality of ground-engaging members associated with the retaining members and extending from adjacent the post-receiving opening of the body portion beyond the opposite end of the body portion a significant distance, each of the ground-engaging members having an enlarged portion adjacent the end thereof closest to the post-receiving opening.
problem: Securing a sign post or similar vertical member in the ground while allowing rapid, tool-free removal and reinstallation.
constraint: Balancing grip strength (to resist wind/vibration) with ease of manual removal, while ensuring the ground-engaging elements do not dislodge during normal use.
mechanism: A body incorporates flexible gripping elements that create frictional engagement with an inserted member, and ground-penetrating elements with enlarged retention features that resist upward displacement. The gripping elements are designed to maintain engagement under normal operating loads while allowing manual release when a threshold force is exceeded. The ground-penetrating elements anchor the body in a substrate, with their enlarged features preventing extraction during routine use.
mechanism_raw: A body with peripheral retaining members and ground-engaging spikes (with enlarged tips) creates a friction-based anchor. The retaining members grip the post, while the spikes penetrate soil and resist upward pull via their enlarged ends. Removal requires overcoming static friction between the post and retaining members, which is designed to be achievable manually but not accidentally.
residual_terms: ["peripheral retaining members", "ground-engaging spikes", "enlarged tips", "static friction", "friction-based anchor"]

abstract: A frame-positioning device for mounting and stretching canvas and like materials that must be stretch-mounted to a supporting stretcher-frame structure, generally comprising a four-sided wooden frame member, whereby the canvas is stapled thereto. The frame-positioning means includes a pair of stretcher bar holders which are arranged to be slidably received on the structural-beam member of a canvas-stretching-and-mounting apparatus, so as to be adjustable in vertical and horizontal planes along the beam to accommodate various sizes of frames.
problem: Mounting and tensioning canvas or similar materials onto frames of varying sizes using a standardized stretching apparatus.
constraint: Achieving sufficient clamping force to hold stretched material without slippage while maintaining smooth adjustability across a range of frame sizes.
mechanism: Adjustable mounting elements slide along a structural member in multiple degrees of freedom, allowing precise positioning to accommodate varying dimensions. The mounting elements selectively lock into position through friction or mechanical interlocks, transferring tension forces from a flexible sheet material to the structural member. The system enables incremental adjustments during installation while maintaining sufficient clamping force to prevent slippage of the stretched material.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable stretcher bar holders slide along a structural beam in both vertical and horizontal planes, allowing precise positioning to accommodate different frame dimensions. The holders lock into place via friction or mechanical clamps, transferring tension forces from the canvas to the beam while enabling incremental adjustments during installation.
residual_terms: ["stretcher bar holders", "structural beam", "friction or mechanical clamps", "tension forces", "canvas"]

abstract: A metal vapor discharge lamp includes a cathode comprising a reservoir of liquid cesium. Metallic cesium which is eroded from the cathode surface by the action of the discharge is returned to the reservoir by the combined effects of gravity, evaporation, condensation, and diffusion to provide a highly stable, long-lived lamp. The intense infrared pulse output of cesium vapor discharge lamps of the present invention is well suited for triggering light-activated semiconductor switches through dielectric pipe networks and for pumping neodymium glass or neodymium-YAG lasers.
problem: Maintaining stable, long-lived operation of a metal vapor discharge lamp despite material erosion from the cathode surface.
constraint: Balancing the rate of material erosion with the efficiency of recovery mechanisms to ensure continuous operation without external replenishment.
mechanism: A self-sustaining material recovery loop counteracts loss from a discharge process by returning eroded material to its source through multiple concurrent pathways: gravitational return, phase-change-driven transport (evaporation-condensation cycles), and molecular migration (diffusion). This balances erosion rate with recovery efficiency to maintain operational continuity without external replenishment.
mechanism_raw: Eroded cesium is actively returned to the cathode reservoir through a combination of gravity-driven flow, evaporation-condensation cycles, and diffusion, creating a self-sustaining material recovery loop that counteracts loss from the discharge process.

abstract: 1. An electronic proximity fuze for a projectile comprising transducer me for converting infrared radiation to an electrical signal, amplifying means connected to said transducer for amplifying said signal, said amplifying means including automatic gain control means for decreasing the gain of said amplifying means upon occurrence of a slowly rising signal, electronic switch means, a source of electrical energy, a detonator, means connecting said switch means said source and said detonator in electrical series circuit, means connecting said amplifying means and said electronic switch means for closing said switch means upon occurrence of a rapidly rising signal of predetermined magnitude, said last named means operating to reduce said predetermined magnitude of the signal when said automatic gain control has decreased the gain of said amplifying means.
problem: Distinguishing between target signals (rapidly rising) and false triggers (slowly rising) in an electronic proximity fuze to ensure accurate detonation timing.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient sensitivity to detect valid targets while suppressing false triggers from gradual environmental changes.
mechanism: Dynamic signal discrimination adjusts detection thresholds based on input rate-of-change: a feedback-controlled sensitivity reduction suppresses responses to slowly varying inputs while preserving responsiveness to rapidly changing inputs, creating a rate-dependent trigger mechanism that distinguishes valid targets from gradual environmental noise.
mechanism_raw: Automatic gain control reduces amplifier sensitivity for slowly rising signals, which lowers the effective threshold for triggering on rapidly rising signals, creating a dynamic discrimination mechanism based on signal rise rate.

abstract: A method for separating copper sulphides from lead sulphides contained in particulate copper lead sulphide concentrates by a flotation process in which an aqueous alkali metal silicate-alkali metal dichromate reagent solution is added in the flotation step to depress the lead bearing sulphides. The copper lead sulphide concentrate may be obtained from a complex copper-lead-zinc ore, in which case the majority of the zinc is first removed by conventional flotation techniques and the copper lead sulphide concentrate treated with activated carbon prior to addition of the silicate-dichromate reagent solution.
problem: Separating copper sulphides from lead sulphides in a complex ore concentrate to enable selective recovery of valuable metals.
constraint: Achieving chemical selectivity without interfering with downstream processing or introducing toxic residues.
mechanism: Selective surface modification enables preferential separation of target materials from non-target materials in a mixture: a chemical agent alters surface properties of non-target components to reduce their reactivity with a separation medium, allowing target components to be selectively isolated while non-target components remain in the bulk phase.
