mechanism_raw: A chemical reagent (alkali metal silicate-dichromate) selectively depresses lead-bearing sulphides by altering their surface properties, allowing copper sulphides to be preferentially floated while lead remains in the pulp phase.

abstract: A process for baking bread by separating a portion of the flour to be used into a wet gluten phase and a starch slurry phase, converting the starch slurry phase into sugar, combining the wet gluten phase and the sugar into a dough including the remaining flour or other weaker flours and treating and baking the resulting dough to produce a bread product.
problem: Optimizing bread texture and composition by processing flour components (gluten and starch) separately before recombination.
constraint: Balancing the timing and conditions of starch conversion and gluten isolation to preserve functional properties during recombination.
mechanism: Independent optimization of distinct material fractions enables controlled recombination into a composite structure: one fraction undergoes chemical transformation (e.g., enzymatic conversion) while another is physically isolated (e.g., wet-phase separation), allowing each fraction's functional properties to be tuned separately before integration into a final product with tailored characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Starch is enzymatically converted to sugar while gluten is isolated as a wet phase, enabling independent optimization of each component's properties before combining them into a dough with controlled structure and sweetness.

abstract: Gymnastic apparatus designed to strengthen the muscles of the abdomen at waist level, those located in the small of the back and in the buttocks and to exercise and maintain all of the rest of the body's muscles, including a base, a bar which can be moved in any direction, one of whose ends is fitted with a sleeve, and whose other end is connected to the base by means of a connection mechanism. The connection mechanism includes a ball holding the end of the bar which is housed in a tube whose upper end is shaped to match the upper end of the ball, with the lower end of the tube being secured to the base. Said ball can move in all directions in response to movement imparted to the ball, within a space limited by the upper end of the tube and by a part forming a seat for the ball mounted on the base by means of an adjustment mechanism making it possible to adjust friction of the ball.
problem: Providing multi-directional resistance exercise for core and full-body muscle strengthening with adjustable intensity.
constraint: Maintaining smooth, unrestricted motion across all axes while providing consistent, user-adjustable resistance without mechanical binding.
mechanism: Omnidirectional motion with user-adjustable resistance is achieved through a multi-axis joint with controllable interface pressure: a mechanical adjustment mechanism modulates contact force between a spherical element and its housing, creating variable friction that provides consistent resistance across all movement directions without restricting range of motion.
mechanism_raw: A ball-and-socket joint with adjustable friction allows omnidirectional movement of the bar while enabling resistance tuning via a mechanical seat that modulates contact pressure between the ball and its housing.

abstract: This invention is of a process and an intermediate alloy for making an oriented-low-alloy iron (primarily recrystallized) which obtains maximum (110) [001] texture and improved magnetic properties by controlling the sulfur, carbon, manganese, and oxygen contents in the intermediate alloy to certain critical narrow ranges. With alloys containing the 0.01-0.15 percent manganese normally found in commercially available iron, the optimum intermediate (prior to final anneal) sulfur level has been found to be 0.004-0.008 percent. This sulfur level is appropriate for such manganese contents for a wide variety of silicon and chromium content. Similarly an intermediate carbon level of between 0.002 and 0.020% has been shown to give the maximum texture and best properties. The oxygen level must be 0.005 percent or lower and should be held as low as practicable. With these levels of sulfur, carbon, manganese, and oxygen, the alloy can be processed by hot rolling at 900.degree.-1200.degree. C. (usually between 1000.degree.-1100.degree. C.), followed by either two or three cold rolling stages with the final cold rolling providing a 50-75 percent reduction, and with annealing at between 750.degree. C. and the A.sub.Cl temperature of the material between cold rollings. The alloy can also contain 0-3% cobalt and up to total of 2% chromium and silicon.
problem: Achieving maximum crystallographic texture and improved magnetic properties in an iron alloy requires precise control of chemical composition and processing steps to avoid suboptimal microstructural development.
constraint: The sulfur and carbon levels must be tightly constrained (e.g., sulfur 0.004-0.008%, carbon 0.002-0.020%) to balance texture development and avoid brittleness, while oxygen must remain below 0.005% to prevent oxidation interference during processing.
mechanism: Precisely controlling elemental composition within critical narrow ranges during material processing, followed by a sequence of mechanical deformation and thermal treatments, to induce a desired recrystallized microstructure with optimal crystallographic orientation.
mechanism_raw: Controlling sulfur, carbon, manganese, and oxygen contents within critical narrow ranges during alloy processing, followed by a sequence of hot rolling, cold rolling, and annealing at specific temperatures, to induce a desired recrystallized microstructure with optimal [001] texture.

abstract: A signal-generating system for a striker clock comprises a clockwork-driven hour disk (12) having conductor tracks which coact with respective contact springs of an hour switch (13) whose pattern of energization changes from one quarter hour to the next, thereby calling forth different numerical values which are stored in a first read-only memory (18) and determine the number of strikes to be emitted in any 15-minute interval when a switch (8) coupled with the minute shaft of the clock is briefly closed. A flip-flop (23) set upon such closure starts a periodically pulsed binary counter (25) which works into a comparator (20) also receiving the numerical value read out from the first memory (18); when the count matches that value, the comparator resets the flip-flop and the counter. The reading of the counter is further transmitted to a decoder (30) addressing a second read-only memory (31) which actuates selected sound emitters (37a-37f) the requisite number of times. The selection of the sound emitters proceeds under a program stored in the second memory (31 ) which could be modified, periodically under the control of the first memory (18) or manually, to vary the acoustic effect. The flip-flop, pulse counter and comparator could be replaced by a microcomputer with input connections to the clockwork-driven minute and hour switches (8, 13) and to the two memories (18, 31) and with outputs for the selective actuation of the sound emitters (37a-37f).
problem: Generating a variable number of strikes in a mechanical clock based on time intervals requires translating mechanical time signals into electronic control of sound emitters.
constraint: The system must synchronize mechanical clock movements (e.g., minute and hour switches) with electronic components to ensure accurate strike counts without disrupting the clock's mechanical operation.
mechanism: Encoding time intervals mechanically via a rotating element with conductive segments, combined with electronic counting and comparison circuits to tally pulses and trigger acoustic emitters through programmable memory, enabling dynamic sound output synchronized to mechanical timekeeping.
mechanism_raw: Using a clockwork-driven hour disk with conductor tracks to encode time intervals, combined with a flip-flop, binary counter, and comparator to count pulses and trigger sound emitters via a programmable memory, enabling dynamic acoustic output based on time.

abstract: A material for use in resilient conforming pads, cushions and the like and cushions filled with such material as described. The material comprises elastic gas-filled hollow microparticles cohered to a mass by a thermoplastic bonding agent semi-liquid at body temperature. The material is useful for providing contour-conforming resilient padding for garments, athletic equipment, prosthetic devices, surgical or vehicular cushions and the like. The gas-filled hollow particles each have a resilient gas-impermeable thermoplastic shell enclosing a quantity of a gas.
problem: Creating a resilient padding material that conforms to body shapes while maintaining structural integrity and comfort requires balancing flexibility and recovery.
constraint: The bonding agent must transition between semi-liquid and solid states at body temperature to enable contouring without permanent deformation, while the microparticle shells must remain gas-impermeable to preserve cushioning over time.
mechanism: Cohering elastic gas-filled hollow microparticles with a thermoplastic bonding agent that transitions between semi-liquid and solid states at body temperature, allowing the material to deform under pressure and recover its shape when cooled, while maintaining gas impermeability for long-term resilience.
mechanism_raw: Cohering elastic gas-filled hollow microparticles with a thermoplastic bonding agent that is semi-liquid at body temperature, allowing the material to deform under pressure and recover its shape when cooled, while maintaining gas impermeability for long-term resilience.

abstract: Apparatus is disclosed herein which detects breaks in spinning yarns in ring spinning frames or the like and in particular senses vibrations inherent to a yarn guide disposed on a bobbin when the yarn guide comes into contact with the spinning yarns. The apparatus achieves quick inspection of whether breaks occur with the spinning yarns by the presence and absence of the vibrations, thereby monitoring joints in the spinning yarns and the operating state of the spinning machine.
problem: Detecting breaks in spinning yarns during ring spinning requires real-time monitoring of mechanical disruptions without interrupting the production process.
constraint: The vibration sensor must be positioned to detect subtle changes in yarn tension and motion without introducing additional friction or interference with the spinning process.
mechanism: Sensing mechanical vibrations generated by a guide element in contact with a moving filament, where the presence or absence of these vibrations indicates whether a break has occurred, enabling real-time detection without disrupting the production process.
mechanism_raw: Sensing vibrations generated by a yarn guide in contact with the spinning yarn, where the presence or absence of these vibrations indicates whether a break has occurred, enabling immediate detection and response.

abstract: A filter for a cigarette includes a porour filter rod circumscribed by a non-porous or smoke impervious wrapper wherein the filter rod with the non-porous wrapper therearound is provided with grooves extending from one end thereof a preselected distance longitudinally therealong. Tipping material circumscribes the non-porous wrapper and is provided with flow-through openings therein in flow communication with the grooves. The grooves may be oriented to extend to the mouth end of the filter when connected to a cigarette, to the tobacco end of the filter when connected to the cigarette, or non-connecting grooves which extend from each end of the filter element a preselected distance therealong.
problem: Controlling airflow and filtration efficiency in a cigarette filter requires directing smoke through structured pathways to balance resistance and particle capture.
constraint: The groove orientation and opening placement must be optimized to direct airflow toward the mouth or tobacco end without compromising the filter's structural integrity or creating uneven pressure drops.
mechanism: Structuring a porous filter element with longitudinal channels circumscribed by a non-porous barrier, combined with apertured tipping material aligned to the channels, to direct airflow through defined pathways and regulate passage while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating longitudinal grooves in a porous filter rod circumscribed by a non-porous wrapper, with tipping material containing flow-through openings aligned to the grooves, to channel airflow and regulate smoke passage.
residual_terms: ["longitudinal grooves", "porous filter rod", "non-porous wrapper", "tipping material", "flow-through openings"]

abstract: Cyclone separator for separating solid particles from particle laden gas having an outlet pipe assembly which includes a pair of co-axial outlet pipes radially spaced apart from each other to form an annular passage therebetween. A plurality of accelerating air supplying nozzles are provided around the outer pipe of the outlet pipe assembly. A blower is provided to supply air under pressure to the annular passage and the nozzles. The air under pressure is discharged from the nozzles along the outer surface of the outlet pipe assembly in the same direction as that of a spiral downward flow of particle laden gas thereby accelerating the spiral downward flow and disturbing the outer surface of the outlet pipe assembly to prevent formation of a boundary layer. The air under pressure is also discharged from the annular passage to blow down the outermost portion of a spiral upward gas flow in the outlet pipe assembly which includes a substantial part of particles contained in the spiral upward flow, so that only the central portion of the spiral upward gas flow containing a less amount of particles is exhausted through the inner pipe of the outlet pipe assembly.
problem: Separating solid particles from particle-laden gas in a cyclone separator while preventing boundary layer formation on the outlet pipe and improving separation efficiency of the upward gas flow.
constraint: The auxiliary air flow must be directed to both accelerate the downward spiral flow and disrupt the boundary layer without destabilizing the overall cyclonic flow pattern, while also selectively stripping the particle-rich outer annulus of the upward flow without losing the particle-lean core.
mechanism: A coaxial flow passage directs a primary particle-laden gas stream into a spiral motion. A secondary fluid flow is introduced along the outer surface of the passage in the same direction as the spiral, simultaneously accelerating the downward spiral and disrupting boundary layer formation. The secondary fluid also impinges on the outermost annular region of the upward gas flow, selectively stripping particle-rich outer layers while preserving a particle-lean core for exhaust through an inner passage.
mechanism_raw: Co-axial outlet pipes create an annular passage; pressurized air is discharged from nozzles along the outer surface of the outlet pipe in the same direction as the spiral downward flow, simultaneously accelerating that flow and disturbing the pipe surface to prevent boundary layer formation. The same pressurized air is also discharged from the annular passage to blow down the outermost portion of the spiral upward gas flow—which carries a substantial portion of entrained particles—so that only the central, particle-lean portion is exhausted through the inner pipe.
residual_terms: ["spiral motion", "annular passage", "boundary layer", "particle-rich outer annulus", "particle-lean core"]

abstract: Apparatus for simultaneously treating the surfaces of a plurality of exposed photopolymer printing plates supported one above another by racks on a trolley. The trolley may be moved by a conveyor 18 from a first compartment 6 to a second compartment 7 separated by a curtain door 11. The first compartment has a series of ultra-violet sources 26 interdigitating with the plates to expose these and a hot air supply 34, 35 for driving solvent from the plates. The second compartment has spray means 29 interdigitating with the plates to spray detackifying solution thereon and a hot air supply 34, 35 for drying the plates after detackifying.
reason: The patent describes a multi-compartment treatment apparatus with UV exposure, hot air drying, and detackifying spray stations arranged sequentially on a moving trolley. While it enables simultaneous batch processing of multiple plates, it does not contain a deeper causal mechanism beyond sequential mechanical transport between treatment zones. The 'interdigitating' of sources with plates is a spatial arrangement, not a functional principle that produces an emergent effect.

abstract: A method of operating a vapor generating system, including a once-through vapor generator, wherein wet vapor is generated in the upper portion of the load range and superheated vapor is generated in the lower portion of the load range is disclosed. Generated vapor is passed through an external and remote moisture separator. Superheated vapor is desuperheated by liquid injection as it passes from the vapor generator to the moisture separator.
problem: Controlling the moisture content and thermal state of vapor produced by a once-through vapor generator across varying load conditions, ensuring dry vapor output while managing heat input efficiently.
constraint: The system must balance load-dependent vapor quality (wet vs. superheated) with the need for consistent moisture separation, requiring desuperheating via liquid injection only when superheated vapor is generated, without over-cooling or introducing excess moisture into the separator.
mechanism: A vapor generation system operates in two modes: producing wet vapor at higher loads and superheated vapor at lower loads. Generated vapor is routed through a remote moisture separation stage. When superheated vapor is produced, a controlled liquid injection process desuperheats the vapor during transit to the separator, conditioning it to a state suitable for moisture removal. The system dynamically adjusts liquid injection based on vapor state to avoid over-cooling or excess moisture introduction.
mechanism_raw: The vapor generator operates in two modes: producing wet vapor in the upper load range and superheated vapor in the lower load range. Generated vapor is routed through an external, remote moisture separator. When superheated vapor is produced, it is desuperheated by controlled liquid injection as it passes from the generator to the separator, conditioning the vapor to an appropriate state for moisture removal before final use.

abstract: A roving formed from a first kind of staple fibers, each of which is at least 3 denier, is interposed with a randomly mixed sliver formed from a second kind of staple fibers, each of which is between 1.5 denier and 3 denier, and a third kind of staple fibers, each of which is at most 1.5 denier, the thermal shrinkage of the second kind of staple fibers being higher than that of the third kind of staple fibers. The roving and the randomly mixed sliver are twisted together so that the sliver wraps around the roving in order to form a double layered roving. After the double layered roving is subjected to fine spinning, it is then subjected to a heat treatment. As a result, a multi-layered bulky spun yarn is obtained.
problem: Creating a multi-layered bulky spun yarn with controlled texture and structural integrity from staple fibers of different properties.
constraint: The fiber denier ranges and thermal shrinkage differentials must be precisely balanced so that the second-kind fibers shrink sufficiently to create bulk while the third-kind fibers provide structural support, and the twist level must be sufficient to maintain the double-layered structure during heat treatment without causing excessive compaction.
mechanism: A multi-layered fiber assembly is formed by twisting together a first fiber bundle with a second fiber bundle containing fibers of differing thermal shrinkage properties. The twist configuration wraps the second bundle around the first, creating a double-layered structure. Subsequent heat treatment induces differential dimensional changes between the fiber types, where higher-shrinkage fibers contract more than lower-shrinkage fibers, generating bulk through controlled structural distortion while maintaining integrity via the twist level.
mechanism_raw: A roving of first-kind staple fibers (≥3 denier) is interposed with a randomly mixed sliver of second-kind fibers (1.5–3 denier, higher thermal shrinkage) and third-kind fibers (≤1.5 denier, lower thermal shrinkage). The roving and sliver are twisted together so the sliver wraps around the roving, forming a double-layered structure. Fine spinning and subsequent heat treatment cause the second-kind fibers to shrink more than the third-kind fibers, creating differential dimensional changes that generate bulk in the final multi-layered yarn.
residual_terms: ["thermal shrinkage differentials", "heat treatment", "twist level", "double-layered structure", "differential dimensional changes"]

abstract: A side shiftable railway car in which the bolsters resting on the wheeled trucks engage a movable center plate on the underside of the car. The center plate may be slid sideways along retaining flanges welded to the underside of the car and locked in place by heavy keeper pins adapted to be inserted and extracted manually with levers.
problem: Enabling lateral (sideways) shifting of a railway car relative to its trucks for alignment or positioning purposes, while providing a secure and releasable locking mechanism to hold the car in the desired shifted position.
constraint: The sliding interface between the center plate and retaining flanges must allow smooth lateral movement under load while maintaining structural integrity, and the keeper pin locking system must be robust enough to withstand dynamic train forces yet manually operable for position adjustment.
mechanism: A sliding interface between a vehicle body and its support structure allows lateral displacement under load. The interface includes constrained motion guides that permit sideways movement while maintaining structural continuity. A manually operable locking mechanism engages discrete positions along the motion path, using a releasable pin system that withstands dynamic forces when engaged but allows position adjustment when disengaged via lever actuation.
mechanism_raw: Bolsters resting on wheeled trucks engage a movable center plate mounted on the underside of the car. The center plate slides sideways along retaining flanges that constrain lateral motion, allowing the car body to shift relative to the trucks. Heavy keeper pins are manually inserted through aligned holes to lock the center plate in the selected lateral position, and extracted with levers to release the lock for further shifting.
residual_terms: ["lateral displacement", "constrained motion guides", "releasable pin system", "dynamic forces", "lever actuation"]

abstract: A storm window is made of two or more panes of non-shatterable plastic hinged together so that the window can be reduced in one dimension sufficiently to permit the edges to enter permanent channels in the frame. The panes are straightened and held in a plane position by latches operated from the inside.
problem: A storm window must be reduced in size to fit into permanent frame channels while maintaining structural integrity and planar alignment.
constraint: The reduction must be sufficient to enter the channels, but the panes must remain non-shatterable and retain alignment under latching forces.
mechanism: A foldable connection between adjacent sections enables dimensional adjustment for insertion into a fixed receptacle, while a mechanical locking system applies corrective forces to align and rigidly secure the sections into a planar configuration once positioned.
mechanism_raw: Hinged panes allow dimensional reduction for insertion into fixed channels, while internal latches mechanically straighten and lock the panes into a planar configuration once positioned.

abstract: An automatic optoelectronic inspection device is located at a position downstream from a cigarette making machine and upstream from cigarette packaging machinery, and cigarettes are conveyed in groups to the inspection device where each group is inspected. The inspection device includes a plurality of photodetectors arranged so that there is a one-to-one correspondence between the position of a photodetector and the position occupied by each cigarette in a normally formed group. Each photodetector includes a light-emitting source for illuminating the end portion of a cigarette and a photoelectric transducer for sensing light reflected from the end portion of a cigarette in registration with the photodetector. The power to the light-emitting sources is controlled in such a way that the intensity of the light emanating from each light-emitting source is modulated at a high frequency. The signal produced by each photoelectric transducer is AC-coupled to circuitry for comparing each photoelectric transducer signal with a preset threshold signal, thereby substantially eliminating the effects of varying ambient light on the accuracy with which missing and improperly filled cigarettes are detected. If the intensity of reflected light is such that the photoelectric transducer signal is less than the threshold signal, the comparison circuitry indicates that a cigarette is missing from the group or is improperly filled, and the group of cigarettes is rejected. Other features are also disclosed.
problem: Detecting missing or improperly filled cigarettes in a group under varying ambient light conditions without false positives.
constraint: The modulation frequency must be high enough to distinguish target signals from ambient light variations, while maintaining one-to-one positional correspondence between photodetectors and cigarette positions.
mechanism: A modulated energy emission source and synchronized signal processing isolate target reflections from environmental noise, enabling position-specific threshold comparisons to identify anomalies in a discrete item array.
mechanism_raw: Modulated high-frequency light sources and AC-coupled photodetector signals isolate the target reflection signal from ambient light noise, enabling threshold-based defect detection.

abstract: A method and apparatus are disclosed for cleansing a matrix of a magnetic separator and more particularly a wet-magnetic separator having adherent magnetic material. The matrix is cleansed both with a liquid medium and an additional gaseous compressible medium. The introduction of the compressible medium is controlled in accordance with a measure of the adherent magnetic material present.
problem: Removing adherent magnetic material from a separator matrix that resists removal by liquid alone.
constraint: The gas flow rate must be balanced to avoid disrupting the liquid medium while ensuring sufficient force to dislodge material, with feedback control preventing over- or under-cleaning.
mechanism: A dual-medium delivery system combines liquid and gaseous phases for surface treatment, with real-time sensing of residual contaminant levels dynamically adjusting the gas-to-liquid ratio to maintain cleaning efficacy without disrupting the liquid environment.
mechanism_raw: Combining liquid and gaseous compressible media for matrix cleansing, with gas introduction dynamically controlled based on real-time measurements of residual adherent material.

abstract: A method for concentrating and dewatering fine-grained materials wherein the material is delivered by a feeder to the central portion of a pressing chamber in an arcuately shaped housing. A profiled sieve is mounted in the housing. An electric motor imparts a vertical-elliptical oscillatory motion to the housing at a frequency up to 160 Hz and at an amplitude from up to 5 mm. An apparatus for performing the aforementioned method, comprising a frame on which an electric motor is secured. A housing is supported by springs on the frame. The housing is arcuately shaped and a sieve extends along the whole length of the arcuately shaped housing. The sieve divides the housing into a pressing chamber and a dewatering chamber. In the bottom portion of the dewatering chamber there is provided a pipe for discharging liquid from the dewatering chamber. In the axes of the springs supporting the housing there are provided regulator bolts for limiting the amplitude of the vibratory motion of the housing.
problem: Concentrating and dewatering fine-grained materials efficiently without clogging or uneven separation.
constraint: The vibration frequency (up to 160 Hz) and amplitude (up to 5 mm) must be tuned to the material's particle size and density, with the sieve profile balancing throughput and separation efficiency.
mechanism: An oscillatory motion generator imparts controlled multi-axis vibration to a shaped containment vessel with a gradient surface profile, while adjustable mechanical stops regulate amplitude to optimize particle migration and fluid expulsion.
mechanism_raw: Vertical-elliptical oscillatory motion of an arcuately shaped housing with a profiled sieve creates controlled vibration-induced particle movement, while regulator bolts limit amplitude to optimize dewatering and material transport.
residual_terms: ["oscillatory motion generator", "multi-axis vibration", "gradient surface profile", "adjustable mechanical stops"]

abstract: A tubular nib having a beak-shaped section at one end of a tube, a slit formed in the beak-shaped section, and a slit-widening inhibiting section having a radius of curvature larger than that of the tubular part of the tubular nib at least at the section across the innermost end of the slit in the beak-shaped part of the tubular nib.
problem: Preventing slit widening in a tubular nib during use, which would compromise material flow control.
constraint: The radius of curvature must be sufficiently larger than the tubular section to prevent stress concentration, while preserving the nib's overall structural integrity and functional beak shape.
mechanism: A stress-distributing geometric transition with a progressively increasing radius at a critical junction redirects operational loads away from a vulnerable opening, preserving its functional geometry under applied forces.
mechanism_raw: A slit-widening inhibiting section with a larger radius of curvature at the slit's innermost end distributes stress and resists deformation, maintaining slit geometry under operational loads.

abstract: This invention relates to a method and apparatus for the separation of finely divided solid particles dissimilar in size and/or density, such as platelets and other blood cells. The separation of, for instance, platelets is accomplished by subjecting the blood sample to centrifugal force in the chamber while displacing the platelets from the blood sample by injecting a relatively small volume of saline into the centrifugally outer end of the chamber. In the preferred apparatus, the saline is injected into che blood sample by driving the chamber supporting the blood sample into a saline filled cavity under the influence of centrifugal force.
problem: Separating particles of dissimilar size and/or density (e.g., platelets and blood cells) from a sample.
constraint: Balancing the volume of injected saline to avoid disrupting the centrifugal stratification while ensuring sufficient displacement of target particles.
mechanism: Applying a radial acceleration field to stratify particles by size/density, then introducing a secondary fluid at the outer periphery to selectively displace target particles along the gradient, enabling separation based on differential mobility under the field.
mechanism_raw: Combining centrifugal force with controlled displacement of a fluid (saline) injected at the centrifugally outer end of the chamber. The centrifugal force stratifies particles by density/size, while the saline injection selectively displaces target particles from the sample, leveraging the radial gradient of centrifugal force to drive separation.

abstract: A fire and explosion suppression system which is operative for suppressing an explosion within 100 milliseconds of the existence of a high energy ignition and within 200 milliseconds of the existence of a low energy ignition. Respective output signals from a detector of ultraviolet radiation and a detector of infrared radiation are fed to a logical AND circuit to provide a third output signal indicative of simultaneous receipt of ultraviolet and infrared radiations. Actuation apparatus responsive to the third output signal then actuates extinguishing agent distribution apparatus for discharging an extinguishing agent into the volume to be protected, such as the troop compartment and/or the engine compartment of an armored vehicle.
problem: Rapidly and accurately detecting an explosion or fire to trigger suppression within critical time windows (100ms for high-energy ignition, 200ms for low-energy).
constraint: Achieving sub-200ms response time while maintaining detection accuracy to avoid false triggers from non-explosive UV/IR sources.
mechanism: Employing two distinct radiation sensors with different spectral sensitivities and requiring concurrent detection of both signals via logical conjunction to confirm an event, thereby suppressing false triggers while meeting strict temporal response thresholds.
mechanism_raw: Using dual-sensor detection (UV and IR) with logical AND circuitry to confirm simultaneous presence of both radiation types, reducing false positives. The combined signal triggers suppression only when both sensors confirm an ignition event, ensuring high reliability under time constraints.
residual_terms: ["radiation sensors", "spectral sensitivities", "concurrent detection", "logical conjunction", "temporal response thresholds"]

abstract: This invention relates to integral heater follower plates designed primarily for use with hot melt dispensing apparatus. Two basic embodiments, with several variations of each of the two basic embodiments, are disclosed. The first of the two basic embodiments of the integral heater follower plate comprises a follower plate shaped to fit inside a container in which hot melt material is stored and at least one spiral heater is embedded in one surface of the follower plate. The second of the two basic embodiments of the integral heater follower plate of this invention comprises a follower plate shaped to fit inside a container in which the hot melt material is stored and a plurality of cartridge heaters housed in holes cut in the follower plate. In addition to the combination heater follower plate, optional fins that may be used with the combination heater follower plates of this invention are disclosed.
problem: Maintaining consistent temperature of hot melt material in a container during dispensing operations.
constraint: Ensuring even heat distribution across the material surface without interfering with the follower plate's mechanical movement or causing localized overheating.
mechanism: Mounting thermal energy sources on a movable interface that tracks the material level, applying heat directly at the boundary between the source and the material to maintain uniform temperature with minimal thermal lag during dispensing.
mechanism_raw: Integrating heating elements (spiral or cartridge) directly into a follower plate that moves with the material level. This ensures heat is applied at the interface between the heater and the material, dynamically adjusting to the material's position while minimizing thermal lag.

abstract: A feedwell comprises two parallel circular channels side by side or superimposed. In the case of side by side channels they have apertures in their floors and device is provided for adjusting the sizes of the apertures. When the channels are superimposed, the apertures face radially inwardly and also have a device for adjusting their sizes. In the case of two side by side channels downward flow below the apertures is baffled by two series of superimposed and spaced apart baffle plates of different angularity to the radii of the feedwell.
problem: Controlling and stabilizing fluid flow distribution in a feedwell for processes like mineral processing or slurry handling.
constraint: Balancing flow adjustment flexibility with structural integrity and minimizing energy loss from excessive baffling.
mechanism: Distributing flow through multiple parallel pathways with variable openings and flow-directing structures to dynamically balance distribution, suppress turbulence, and minimize energy loss while maintaining structural coherence.
mechanism_raw: Using parallel channels with adjustable apertures and baffles to dynamically regulate flow patterns. The adjustable apertures allow real-time control of flow rates between channels, while baffles direct downward flow to prevent turbulence and ensure uniform distribution.

abstract: Methods and apparatus are described for the manufacture of particle board in which a fleece of particle material with admixed binder is formed on an endless belt 1 at a forming station and is subsequently passed through a series of presses and heating devices where it is consolidated into particle board. The lower, and preferably also the upper, covering layers of the fleece are selectively warmed at the forming station to activate the cold binding capability of the admixed binder and endow the fleece with sufficient stability to withstand the handling stresses as it is passed from one endless band conveyor to another. pa The selective warming is conveniently achieved by means of respective heating devices each of which incorporates a number of pairs of oppositely poled capacitor plates arranged alternately side by side along the length of the fleece and extending over the full width thereof. In this way longitudinally extending field lines pass between the capacitor plates and penetrate to a required depth in the associated covering layer. In an alternative embodiment, in which the fleece is conveniently deposited in sequential layers on the endless band fleece carrier, the first layer, which forms the lower covering layer is warmed by passing it between a pair of capacitor plates.
problem: Stabilizing a particle-filled fleece during handling prior to consolidation into particle board.
constraint: Controlling the depth of electric field penetration to avoid activating binder in unintended regions while ensuring sufficient surface stability.
mechanism: Applying an electric field between opposing electrodes positioned along a transport path to induce selective heating in surface layers of a particle-laden medium, activating a binding agent only within a controlled penetration depth to stabilize the surface without affecting the interior.
mechanism_raw: Selective capacitive heating of outer fleece layers using oppositely poled capacitor plates arranged along the conveyor. The electric field penetrates to a controlled depth, activating binder only in the surface layers to provide structural integrity without overheating the core.

abstract: The invention relates to alkylborane complexes with aromatic amines of the formula: ##STR1## in which R.sup.1 and R.sup.2 are the same or different (1-4C)-alkyl radicals, or together with the adjacent nitrogen atom are morpholino, piperidino or pyrrolidino radicals; R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 are independently selected from hydrogen, (1-4C)-alkyl, (1-4C)-alkoxy, di-(1-4C)-alkylamino, morpholino, piperidino and pyrrolidino; thexyl stands for 1,1,2-trimethylpropyl; and n is the integer 1 when R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 are other than nitrogen containing radicals, or the integer 1 or 2 when one of R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 is a nitrogen containing radical, or the integer 1, 2 or 3 when both R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 are nitrogen containing radicals. The complexes are more stable than thexylborane tetrahydrofuran complex, but are sufficiently reactive to be valuable as hydroborating and reducing agents. The invention also provides solutions of the complexes of formula I in organic solvents for convenient storage or subsequent synthetic use, and a process for manufacturing said complexes. A particularly convenient complex of the invention is thexylborane N,N-diethylaniline complex.
problem: Creating chemically stable yet sufficiently reactive alkylborane complexes for use as hydroborating and reducing agents in organic synthesis.
constraint: The trade-off between stability (preventing decomposition during storage/use) and reactivity (maintaining sufficient activity for hydroboration/reduction reactions) is controlled by the choice of amine substituents and their spatial arrangement.
mechanism: Ligands with tunable electronic and steric properties are coordinated to a reactive core, modulating its electron density and accessibility to balance stability against premature decomposition and reactivity for target chemical transformations.
mechanism_raw: The aromatic amine ligands in the complex structure stabilize the borane core through electronic and steric effects, balancing reactivity by modulating the borane's electron density and accessibility while preventing premature decomposition.

abstract: An improved long vertical shaft bioreactor for the treatment of degradable waste is provided wherein the head tank or basin surmounting the vertical downcomer and riser chambers is surrounded by a foam oxidation vessel. Conduits are provided between the head tank and the foam vessel through which (a) foam accumulated in the head tank is passed to the foam vessel and (b) through which excess fluid in the head tank may be vented.
problem: Managing foam accumulation and fluid overflow in a vertical shaft bioreactor to maintain efficient waste degradation without operational disruption.
constraint: The system must balance foam removal efficiency with minimal disruption to the bioreactor's hydraulic flow and microbial activity, requiring conduit sizing and vessel placement to avoid backpressure or clogging.
mechanism: A secondary processing vessel is integrated around a primary chamber, connected via passive transfer pathways that divert accumulated byproduct material to the secondary vessel while maintaining hydraulic continuity and avoiding backpressure in the primary system.
mechanism_raw: A dedicated foam oxidation vessel is integrated around the head tank, connected via conduits that passively transfer accumulated foam to the vessel and vent excess fluid, decoupling foam management from the main reactor chamber.

abstract: A weft cutting device in a shuttleless loom is provided with a plate-like cutting member which after completion of beating is caused to move between a pair of weft guide members and across the weft held in position by stepped portions provided for the guide members. Escapement of the weft from the stepped portion is prohibited by an escapement preventing member located near the guide members. Weft is sufficiently tensioned by a tensioning member disposed near the cutting member and engaging weft earlier than the cutting member.
problem: Achieving precise weft cutting and tensioning in a shuttleless loom without weft slippage or misalignment during the cutting process.
constraint: The timing and spatial coordination between the cutting member, tensioning member, and escapement prevention must be synchronized to avoid cutting errors while maintaining high-speed loom operation.
mechanism: A cutting element is moved along a guided path between fixed reference points to sever a tensioned filament, while a tensioning element applies controlled force ahead of the cut and a positional constraint prevents lateral displacement, ensuring synchronized cutting and stabilization.
mechanism_raw: A plate-like cutting member moves between stepped guide members to sever the weft, while a tensioning member engages the weft ahead of the cut and an escapement preventing member blocks lateral movement, ensuring controlled tension and positional stability during cutting.

abstract: The invention pertains to an apparatus for extracting a cork from a bottle comprising a cork-engaging member, including a corkscrew, and a holder for aligning and guiding the corkscrew, via its own diameter, with respect to the bottle. The cork-engaging member is completely removable from the holder for independent use, and to permit the corkscrew point to be used to sever the metal foil, which covers the bottle top, and both the holder and cork engaging member to be more easily cleaned. The holder includes a plurality of longitudinally extending circumferentially spaced, radially deflectable gripping elements connected to and spaced downwardly from a guide which receives the corkscrew, and are all approximately equally resiliently biased to a normal unflexed radial position. One embodiment is capable of two alternative modes of operation. The corkscrew itself is improved by the provision of an outer layer of friction reducing material.
problem: Aligning and guiding a corkscrew for reliable cork extraction while enabling independent tool use and hygienic cleaning.
constraint: The gripping elements must balance sufficient radial compliance for alignment with enough rigidity to prevent misalignment during extraction, while the removable design must not compromise structural integrity or cleaning accessibility.
mechanism: A removable tool is retained by a holder with compliant gripping elements that self-align via resilient biasing, allowing detachment for standalone use while maintaining positional accuracy when reinserted through radial compliance and structural rigidity.
mechanism_raw: A removable corkscrew is guided by a holder with radially deflectable gripping elements that self-align via resilient biasing, allowing the corkscrew to be detached for standalone use (e.g., foil severing) while maintaining precise alignment when reinserted.

abstract: Apparatus for recirculating combustion exhaust gases to the burner region of a Stirling cycle hot-gas engine to lower combustion temperature and reduct NO.sub.x formation includes a first wall separating the exhaust gas stream from the inlet air stream, a second wall separating the exhaust gas stream from the burner region, and low flow resistance ejectors formed in the first and second walls for admitting the inlet air to the burner region and for entraining and mixing with the inlet air portion of the exhaust gas stream. In a preferred embodiment the ejectors are arranged around the periphery of a cylindrical burner region and oriented to admit the air/exhaust gas mixture tangentially to promote mixing. In another preferred embodiment a single annular ejector surrounds and feeds the air/exhaust gas mixture to a cylindrical burner region. The annular ejector includes an annular plate with radially-directed flow passages to provide an even distribution of the air/exhaust gas mixture to the burner region.
problem: Reducing NOx formation in a Stirling cycle hot-gas engine by recirculating combustion exhaust gases to lower burner region temperature.
constraint: The ejector geometry and flow orientation must balance efficient gas entrainment and mixing with minimal pressure loss to avoid compromising engine performance, while maintaining even distribution across the burner region.
mechanism: Momentum-driven flow devices in separating structures entrain and mix a secondary gas stream with a primary gas flow, using the secondary stream's kinetic energy to induce recirculation and uniform distribution across a reaction zone while minimizing pressure loss.
mechanism_raw: Low-resistance ejectors in separating walls entrain and mix inlet air with exhaust gas streams, using the exhaust's momentum to drive recirculation and tangential/annular flow patterns that enhance mixing uniformity before combustion.

abstract: A telescoping, U-shaped straight through, primary flow invert form may be lenghtened or shortened to meet the diameter of the cylindrical manhole and is mounted at opposite ends to the aligned main flow inlet and outlet pipes of the manhole. Longitudinally projecting bottom and opposed side invert tabs located at the ends of the straight through invert form contact the insides of the inlet and outlet pipes, respectively, to center the form. Slide guides, each carrying a retainer tab, adjust the retaining tabs longitudinally to position them within respective pipes at respective ends of the form for preventing lifting of the invert form during concrete pouring within the manhole. An angularly adjustable, intersecting side flow invert form projects from another pipe opening to the manhole at some angle to the straight through form and includes interlocking, axially slidable, opposed section halves. Straps fixed at one end to the section halves permit clip locking or latching of the invert form leading edges in contact with the outside wall of the straight through form. Inverted U-shaped telescoping struts between the opposed interlocking, slidable section halves latch the side flow invert to the side of the through form opposite that receiving the clip borne by the strap.
problem: Ensuring a form structure remains centered, stable, and properly positioned within a cylindrical manhole during concrete pouring while accommodating variable diameters and intersecting pipe connections.
constraint: Balancing adjustability for variable diameters and angles with structural rigidity to prevent lifting or misalignment during concrete pouring.
mechanism: Use adjustable, interfitting segments with sliding and hinged connections to dynamically conform a support structure to varying internal geometries, while mechanical retention features prevent displacement during a casting process.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable telescoping and interlocking components with sliding retainers and hinged section halves allow dynamic sizing and alignment of the form to the manhole and pipe geometry, while mechanical latching and tab systems prevent displacement during concrete pouring.

abstract: A starting method for an electro-pneumatically actuated wet-settling machine, for the separation of mineral mixtures, particularly coal, into their constituent components, in which the separation of the mineral mixture takes place through the pulsation of a separating liquid which is energized and controlled by means of compressed air in pulsation chambers which have electrically controlled air inlet and outlet valves, and in which the initiation of the wet-settling process takes place after a standstill, at least partially automatically, particularly through an electrically or electronically operating automatic starter, which starts at least some settling machine apparatus and/or their components in a predetermined dependency upon one another.
problem: Initiating a wet-settling separation process safely and efficiently after a standstill, ensuring interdependent components start in a controlled sequence to avoid operational failure.
constraint: Ensuring precise timing and dependency between component startups to prevent mechanical stress or process inefficiency during initiation.
mechanism: Employ a sequenced startup controller that activates components in a predetermined dependency order, using timed control signals and pulsating actuation to synchronize the initiation of interdependent processing stages.
mechanism_raw: An automatic starter initiates components in a predetermined dependency order, using electrically controlled valves and compressed air pulsation to synchronize the energization of settling machine apparatus.
residual_terms: ["automatic starter", "electrically controlled valves", "compressed air pulsation", "settling machine apparatus"]

abstract: A screw press for extracting liquids from materials such as fruits, vegetables, or the like having a cylindrical barrel having a concentric variable-speed helical feed and compression screw. The rearward portion of the cylindrical barrel comprises a cage section having perforate filter screens for passing extracted liquids and filtering out undesired solids from the material being pressed. The cage section is formed by at least one pair of open semicircular frames having a plurality of spaced apart ribs which support replaceable filter screens. The repair of frames is attached along its bottom edge to a set of interleaved hinge blocks which are hingedly attached to the frame of the press. The pair of frames is removably joined along the upper edges of the frame. When the press is nonoperating, the frames are separated at the upper edges and the hinged blocks permit the frames to open in a book-like manner and swing downward and outward completely clear of the feed and compression screw. The wide open position permits cleaning of the screens and screw, or replacement of the screens. A feed portion of the press barrel has an opening limited to 11/2 times the feed screw pitch and an inlet chamber enclosing 50% to 75% of the circumference of the feed and compression screw. The feed and compression screw is driven by an adjustable hydraulic drive system to permit control for optimum throughput of the press.
problem: Enabling rapid access for cleaning and maintenance of a screw press's cage screens and internal components without full disassembly of the press.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the press during operation while enabling quick, tool-free access for maintenance.
mechanism: Implement a hinged, book-like opening mechanism for frame structures that allows major components to swing away from a central rotating element, while removable connections and adjustable drives enable maintenance access and performance tuning.
mechanism_raw: Hinged, book-like opening of cage frames via interleaved hinge blocks allows the frames to swing clear of the screw, while removable upper-edge connections and adjustable hydraulic drives facilitate screen replacement and throughput optimization.

abstract: Apparatus for selectively interconnecting different pieces of audio electrical equipment, such as an amplifier and a tuner, for the purpose of demonstrating the same to a potential purchaser. Units to be demonstrated are connected to different address-assigned ports in the apparatus, and a keyboard is operated to address the particular ports for the units desired to be connected. The apparatus includes an electronic memory which stores the addresses of the addressed ports, and which then effects a connection between such ports.
problem: Dynamically interconnecting different pieces of audio equipment for demonstration without manual rewiring, based on user-selected configurations.
constraint: Managing multiple simultaneous connections efficiently while ensuring reliable address-based routing without signal interference.
mechanism: Utilize addressable connection points linked to a programmable memory that stores user-defined port combinations, triggering automated switching to establish interconnections between selected points based on stored configurations.
mechanism_raw: Address-assigned ports linked to an electronic memory store user-selected port combinations, which then trigger automated connections between the addressed ports to establish the desired equipment interconnections.

abstract: The invention provides a razor assembly comprising a shaving unit and a handle. The shaving unit has a platform, a blade, pivotal mounting for pivotally connecting the shaving unit to the handle, and apparatus for receiving a biasing force from the handle. The handle includes two flexible arms which at one end have pivotal mounting apparatus complementary to the shaving unit's pivotal mounting apparatus, the flexible arms being secured to the handle in a region spaced from the handle's pivotal mounting apparatus. A movable button engages the flexible arms and is movable for flexing the arms to disengage the handle's pivotal mounting apparatus from the shaving unit's pivotal mounting apparatus and for reverse movement which frees the flexible arms for engagement of the handle's pivotal mounting apparatus with the shaving unit's pivotal mounting apparatus. The handle also includes apparatus for exerting a biasing force on the shaving unit's apparatus for receiving a biasing force.
problem: Allowing a razor shaving unit to pivot freely relative to the handle while maintaining a consistent biasing force and enabling secure attachment/detachment.
constraint: Balancing flexibility for pivoting with sufficient mechanical retention to prevent accidental disengagement during shaving.
mechanism: Incorporate flexible coupling elements with complementary pivot mounts and a movable actuation mechanism to enable controlled engagement and disengagement, while a separate force-applying system maintains consistent pressure during operation.
mechanism_raw: Flexible arms with complementary pivotal mounts and a movable button mechanism enable controlled flexing to engage or disengage the shaving unit, while a separate biasing system maintains consistent pressure during use.

abstract: This invention relates to an apparatus of regenerating fluidizing medium employed in a fluidized-bed incinerator, wherein the sticking matter attached to the fluidizing medium employed in the incinerator in the process of burning up in the incinerator the ash collected from power plant boiler exhaust gases (EP ash) is removed from the fluidizing medium chemically and physically.
problem: Fluidizing medium in a fluidized-bed incinerator becomes fouled with ash and sticking matter during operation, reducing efficiency and requiring frequent maintenance.
constraint: Must maintain continuous operation of the incinerator while effectively cleaning the medium without degrading its structural or functional properties.
mechanism: In-situ regeneration of a particulate medium using simultaneous chemical and physical processes removes accumulated deposits while maintaining continuous operation, preserving the medium's structural integrity and functional properties.
mechanism_raw: Chemical and physical regeneration of the fluidizing medium removes accumulated ash and sticking matter, restoring its functionality without interrupting the incineration process.

abstract: A cantilever mounted wind turbine having an interior stationary support column and a concentrically mounted rotatable rotor and having a first bearing between the support column and the rotor and a second flexibly coupled bearing between the support column and the rotor where the second bearing includes bearing surfaces and a flexible coupling between one of the bearing surfaces and the rotor in order to provide bending moment decoupling between the rotor and its support column.
problem: Wind loads on a cantilever-mounted turbine rotor induce bending moments that stress the support column and bearings, risking structural failure.
constraint: Must balance structural rigidity for power generation with flexibility to absorb dynamic loads without compromising bearing lifespan.
mechanism: A compliant mechanical interface between a rotating component and a support bearing allows independent pivoting motion to decouple external bending forces while maintaining rotational alignment through elastic deformation.
mechanism_raw: A flexible coupling between the rotor and one bearing decouples bending moments, allowing the rotor to pivot independently while maintaining rotational alignment.

abstract: A sealing body member for attaching into an edge beam having upwardly extending arms, wherein at least one of the upwardly extending arms and the adjacent sealing body have respective mirror image longitudinal recesses, and a dowel part for inserting into the recesses, where the sealing body has a longitudinal cut above the recesses and approximately adjacent the upper edge of the upwardly extending wall to permit the sealing body upper part to be folded for inserting the dowel part from above into the recesses.
problem: Sealing body members must be securely attached to edge beams with upwardly extending arms, but installation requires precise alignment of dowel parts in recesses.
constraint: Must ensure a leak-proof seal after installation while permitting assembly from a single direction without disassembling adjacent components.
mechanism: A deformable section in a sealing component enables temporary geometric reconfiguration, allowing insertion of alignment features from a single direction into complementary recesses formed in adjacent structural elements.
mechanism_raw: A longitudinal cut in the sealing body allows folding of the upper part, enabling dowel insertion from above into mirror-image recesses formed in the arms and sealing body.

abstract: An improved grain bin floor support system utilizes a plurality of independent floor supports for supporting interlocking flooring elements. Each floor support has curvilinear lower and upper rails, the lower serving as a base member for bearing against a subfloor or other supporting surface. Each support has plural spacers which extend between the upper and lower rails to maintain them in spaced, parallel relationship. The lower rail or base member defines a curvilinear path on the supporting surface. Similarly, the upper rail supports the flooring elements along a curvilinear path coincident with that established by the base member.
problem: Grain bin flooring requires independent supports that distribute load evenly while accommodating interlocking flooring elements in a modular system.
constraint: Must maintain parallel spacing between rails under load while allowing modular assembly and disassembly of flooring elements.
mechanism: Curved load-transfer surfaces on modular supports define continuous engagement paths, ensuring uniform load distribution and maintaining parallel spacing between interlocking flooring elements under applied forces.
mechanism_raw: Curvilinear lower and upper rails on each support define matching paths, ensuring aligned load transfer and interlocking flooring engagement along a continuous curve.

abstract: Object of the invention are new diisatoic acid and triisatoic acid derivatives of the general formula I ##STR1## wherein n represents 2 or 3, X stands for oxygen or sulfur and R for a group of the general formula II EQU Y--Z--B].sub.m, (II) in which m stands for 1 or 2, Y for B when m is 1 and Y further represents a di- or trivalent alkyl group with 1 to 5 carbon atoms when m is 2, B represents alkylene with 1 to 4 carbon atoms and Z stands for phenylene-1,4-dioxy or diphenylene-4,4'-dioxy optionally singly or multiply substituted by Cl, NO.sub.2 or alkyl or for a 5- to 7-membered heterocyclic ring which is optionally substituted by one or more of said substituents and has one or more atoms selected from the group consisting of N, S and O as members of the ring, with a benzene nucleus optionally being annulated to said ring, and a process for the production of these compounds which is characterized in that a compound of the general formula III EQU R--XH).sub.n (III) wherein R, X and n have the meaning defined above is reacted with at least two equivalents of isatoic acid anhydride, preferably in the presence of strong bases, as well as the use of these new compounds for the preparation of plastic materials.
problem: Need to synthesize novel diisatoic acid and triisatoic acid derivatives with tailored properties for plastic material production.
constraint: Must control reaction stoichiometry and base strength to achieve desired substitution patterns without over-reacting or degrading the product.
mechanism: Controlled stoichiometric excess of a reactive anhydride species in the presence of strong bases drives selective multi-site substitution on a molecular scaffold, enabling tailored substitution patterns through reaction kinetics and base-mediated activation.
mechanism_raw: Reacting a compound of formula R–XH with at least two equivalents of isatoic acid anhydride in the presence of strong bases drives the formation of complex multi-substituted derivatives.

abstract: To avoid the passage of contamination from one bird to another at a poultry inspection station in a poultry processing shackle line and to eliminate the necessity for the inspector to touch the birds during the inspection, each bird in succession at the inspection station is automatically engaged and tilted to a breast-up, back-down generally horizontal position with the eviscerated body cavity facing the inspector. In such position, the body cavity is automatically expanded to a wide open condition for easy visual inspection while each bird traverses the inspection station, following which the bird tilting and body cavity expanding units are removed from contact with the birds and thoroughly cleansed near the back of the inspection station prior to automatically engaging other oncoming birds at the inspection station.
problem: Contamination transfer between birds during poultry inspection and the need to avoid direct inspector contact with the birds.
constraint: Balancing continuous throughput with thorough cleansing between operations to prevent cross-contamination.
mechanism: Sequentially engage, manipulate, and release each item at a processing station, then cleanse the handling elements between operations to prevent cross-contamination while maintaining continuous throughput.
mechanism_raw: Automated sequential engagement, tilting, and body cavity expansion of each bird at the inspection station, followed by disengagement and cleansing of the handling units before engaging the next bird. This ensures continuous processing while maintaining hygiene and eliminating manual contact.

abstract: A document clamping device formed from a series of pivotally interconnected links. Adjacent pairs of links are movable between a first position of mutual alignment and a second position at right angles to one another about a pivot. Locking means are provided to hold the links firmly in the second position and preferably also in the first position. This locking means may be in the form of spring-loaded ball catches or resilient bosses on one link locating within recesses on the other link of a pair. Pivoting may be achieved either by means of a pivot pin or by mutually engaging configurations on the interconnected ends of two adjacent links.
problem: Need for a flexible yet secure clamping mechanism for documents or similar objects that can adapt to varying sizes or shapes.
constraint: Maintaining structural rigidity in the locked position while enabling smooth pivoting and reconfiguration.
mechanism: Interconnected articulated segments capable of reconfiguring between extended and angular orientations, with selective retention elements to fix the segments in a chosen geometry for adjustable clamping.
mechanism_raw: A series of pivotally interconnected links that can shift between aligned and right-angle positions, with locking mechanisms (e.g., spring-loaded catches or resilient bosses) to hold the links in the desired configuration. This allows adjustable clamping force and geometry.

abstract: A control system for hydraulic servomechanisms comprising a double-acting jack the working chambers of which are selectively and alternately connectable to a source of pressurized fluid and to a fluid discharge through a reactive switching valve which itself is operated by a control member. According to the invention, there are provided between the valve and each working chamber of the jack means for intercepting the passage of fluid toward said chamber as long as the upstream pressure does not reach a predetermined threshold value. The application may be advantageously used in power-assisted steering systems for automotive vehicles.
problem: Uncontrolled or premature actuation of hydraulic servomechanisms, particularly in systems like power-assisted steering where precise pressure-dependent responses are critical.
constraint: Ensuring the threshold pressure is reliably detected and the interception mechanism does not introduce lag or failure in the control system.
mechanism: Delaying actuation of a fluid-powered actuator until upstream pressure reaches a predetermined threshold by intercepting fluid flow via a pressure-responsive switching valve.
mechanism_raw: Intercepting fluid flow to a hydraulic jack chamber until upstream pressure reaches a predetermined threshold, using a reactive switching valve operated by a control member. This delays actuation until sufficient pressure is achieved, ensuring controlled operation.

abstract: A sled for transportation of passengers or cargo, especially small children and infants, comprises a passenger receiving enclosure having a base and a cover, and a laterally presented side access opening. The enclosure can swivel about a vertical axis relative to the runners of the sled, so that the access aperture can be presented in any chosen direction, e.g., away from the wind, to afford additional protection to the rider.
problem: Exposure of passengers or cargo to environmental elements (e.g., wind, snow) during transport on a sled or similar vehicle.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and stability of the enclosure during swiveling and transport.
mechanism: Mounting an enclosed compartment on a rotatable interface relative to a transport base, allowing the compartment's access opening to be oriented independently of the base's direction of travel to shield occupants from environmental exposure.
mechanism_raw: A swiveling passenger enclosure mounted on a base, allowing the access opening to be oriented in any direction relative to the sled's runners. This enables the access to face away from the wind or other environmental hazards while maintaining structural stability.

abstract: A process is provided for the manufacture of titanium compounds and particularly titanium dioxide wherein excess titaniferous bearing material is reacted with dilute sulfuric acid having a concentration of between about 25% and about 60% by weight at a temperature below about 140.degree. C., and in the presence of a reducing agent which affects the reduction of ferric iron to ferrous iron. Thereafter, the titanium sulfate may be recovered or further processed to provide titanium dioxide hydrate accompanied by recycling the spent acid for reaction with the titaniferous bearing material charged to the process. The titanium hydrate may be calcined to provide titanium dioxide.
problem: Efficient and cost-effective production of titanium dioxide from titaniferous materials while managing impurities and recycling process chemicals.
constraint: Controlling reaction temperature and acid concentration to optimize yield while preventing degradation of the reducing agent or acid during recycling.
mechanism: Reacting a metal-bearing feedstock with acid in the presence of a reducing agent at controlled temperature to convert a target metal into a recoverable form, then recycling the spent acid back into the reaction to close the chemical loop.
mechanism_raw: Reacting titaniferous material with dilute sulfuric acid at low temperature in the presence of a reducing agent to convert ferric iron to ferrous iron, followed by recovery of titanium sulfate or further processing to titanium dioxide hydrate. Spent acid is recycled back into the reaction, closing the chemical loop.

abstract: The device includes a main flow control valve and associated packings designed for effective operation under extreme conditions associated with the pumping of high viscosity asphaltic crude wherein the formation includes toxic gases, and where the formation is produced using steam flooding techniques. The main valve seat and the associated valve closure, consisting of a reciprocating ram and packing plug, are coaxial with the pump polished rod. The valve seat includes tapered walls defining a shoulder which partially confronts the ram plug; and the ram plug is formed of a compressible material formed to the shape of the valve seat. The packing plug is retained on the end of the ram by axial tie rods and a retaining ring, which ring may engage the valve seat shoulder to effect axial compression of the packing plug between the retaining ring and ram face, and consequent radial expansion into sealing engagement. The ram is reciprocated axially, either manually or hydraulically relative to the ram body; and a packing gland, suitable to seal against toxic gases, is provided between the ram and valve body. A rod packing, at the upper end of the ram, includes a primary adjustable packing gland for effective sealing between the ram and the reciprocating polished rod; and may also include a positive shutdown gland for positive sealing at the polished rod in the event of the failure of the primary gland. The positive shutdown is designed for hydraulic operation, to enable automatic operation in response to detection of a gas leak at the primary gland.
problem: Sealing a valve under extreme conditions involving high-viscosity fluids, toxic gases, and steam flooding while maintaining operational integrity.
constraint: Balancing axial compression force to achieve radial sealing without over-tightening, while maintaining compatibility with reciprocating motion and toxic gas containment.
mechanism: Axial compression of a compressible element between opposing surfaces converts axial force into radial expansion, creating a seal against a tapered interface. Coaxial alignment of components ensures uniform force distribution, while a secondary sealing mechanism activates automatically in response to detected leakage.
mechanism_raw: Axial compression of a compressible packing plug between a retaining ring and ram face causes radial expansion into sealing engagement with a tapered valve seat. The coaxial alignment of the valve seat, ram, and pump polished rod ensures consistent sealing forces, while a secondary shutdown gland activates automatically in response to detected gas leaks.

abstract: A seed and method for epitaxial solidification of materials, a preferred seed having at least a portion with a melting point 20.degree.-45.degree. C. depressed from that of the alloy being solidified into an article. Boron and silicon are preferably added to nickel superalloys seeds when directionally solidified columnar grain and single crystal articles are formed. Improved seeds also have surface compositions which promote the dissolution of surface contamination films that interfere with epitaxy.
problem: Promoting epitaxial solidification of materials (e.g., nickel superalloys) by overcoming surface contamination films that inhibit crystal growth.
constraint: Maintaining the melting point depression within a narrow range to ensure nucleation control without destabilizing the alloy's structural properties.
mechanism: A nucleation seed with a controlled thermal property enables epitaxial growth by lowering the energy barrier for crystal formation, while surface-active agents dissolve contamination layers to expose clean substrate for alignment. The thermal property is maintained within a defined range to balance nucleation control and material stability.
mechanism_raw: A seed with a melting point depressed by 20–45°C relative to the alloy enables controlled nucleation, while surface compositions (e.g., boron and silicon additives) actively dissolve contamination films to facilitate epitaxial alignment during solidification.

abstract: The invention provides a method of, and apparatus for, controlling the fuel to air ratio of the fuel mixture to an internal combustion engine which includes a fuel mixture feed system having a known type of carburettor. In the method the fuel mixture is supplemented with air and exhaust gas by utilizing pressure controlled air and exhaust gas valves operated by pressure changes in the fuel feed system and/or intake manifold of the engine so that the valves open when the fuel to air ratio of the fuel mixture supplied by the carburettor is in excess of a predetermined value.
problem: Automatically adjusting the fuel-to-air ratio in an internal combustion engine when the carburetor-supplied mixture exceeds a desired threshold.
constraint: Ensuring valve actuation timing and pressure thresholds align with engine operating conditions to avoid overcorrection or delayed response.
mechanism: Pressure variations in a fluid system directly actuate valves to adjust a mixture ratio, forming a closed-loop feedback system. Valve timing and pressure thresholds are synchronized with operational conditions to prevent overcorrection or delayed response.
mechanism_raw: Pressure changes in the fuel feed system or intake manifold directly actuate air and exhaust gas valves, opening them to supplement the mixture when the fuel-to-air ratio is too high. This creates a closed-loop feedback system driven by inherent engine pressures.

abstract: A modular spacer concept is disclosed for use in centrifuge bores. The arrangement is such that various sizes of tubes are available to allow for different amounts of fluid which may be inserted therein for centrifugation. A plurality of substantially identical spacers are provided, each of which has an effective length equal to a predetermined standard difference in tube sizes. The lower surface of each spacer has a concave center portion adapted to fit the convex center portion of the upper surface of a tube, and the upper surface of each spacer has a convex center portion adapted to fit the concave center portion of the lower surface of a substantially identical spacer.
problem: Accommodating variable tube sizes in centrifuge bores using standardized components while maintaining structural and functional consistency.
constraint: Standardizing spacer dimensions to cover a range of tube sizes while preserving mechanical integrity and alignment during centrifugation.
mechanism: Modular components with complementary geometric interfaces stack to adjust effective length, accommodating variable sizes while maintaining alignment and structural integrity. Standardized dimensions enable compatibility across a range of configurations without custom parts.
mechanism_raw: Modular spacers with complementary concave/convex surfaces stack to adjust effective length, allowing different tube sizes to be accommodated without custom parts. Each spacer’s geometry ensures alignment and stability between adjacent components.

abstract: An apparatus and method for folding and crushing empty cylindrical cans such that after being folded and crushed the can end faces are essentially coplanar. The apparatus comprises a flat stationary anvil and a flat parallel reciprocable platen defining therebetween a folding compartment into which an empty can is inserted, an independently reciprocable creasing element or plunger slidably inserted in an aperture through the center of the reciprocable platen such as to enter and leave said folding compartment, and a drive arrangement simultaneously advancing the reciprocable platen and reciprocable creasing element into said folding compartment towards the can, the creasing element being advanced more rapidly than or ahead of the platen, and drive retracting the creasing element after the creasing element has nearly passed through the can without stopping the advance of the platen, and subsequently retracting the platen.
