mechanism: Using opposing powered rollers with parallel axes positioned on either side of the workpiece, with complementary engagement features that interface with connector elements. As the workpiece is compressively driven through the roller nip, both rollers simultaneously apply and compress the connector elements onto both sides of the workpiece, ensuring synchronized bilateral attachment with aligned pressure.
mechanism_raw: Using opposing powered rollers with parallel vertical axes positioned on either side of the workpiece, with complementary V-webs that engage the connector plates. As the prefabricated wood frame is compressively driven through the roller nip, both rollers simultaneously apply and compress the connector plates onto both sides of the workpiece, ensuring synchronized bilateral attachment with aligned pressure.

abstract: An apparatus is disclosed for securing a two component lining to the inside shell of a rotary kiln or the like. The apparatus includes a plurality of standoffs each having a bottom portion for connection to the inside shell of the kiln, a middle portion, and a top portion. A grid is connected to each of the top portions by means of a weld. A layer of a lightweight first castable material having high insulative properties is gunned or cast along the inside shell of the kiln to a depth less than the height of the standoffs. A second castable material having abrasion resistive properties is gunned or cast onto the surface of the first castable material at a depth substantially level with the surface of the grid. The standoffs serve as an anchor to secure the two layers of castible material into position . The grid connected to the top portion of the standoffs is preferably a honeycomb grid which aids the second castable material in protecting the first castable material from damage due to abrasion.
problem: Securing a two-component lining (insulative inner layer and abrasion-resistant outer layer) to the inside shell of a rotary kiln so that each layer maintains its position and function despite the harsh, abrasive environment.
constraint: The standoff height must exceed the first layer depth to allow the second layer to reach the grid level, balancing insulation thickness against abrasion protection and structural anchoring.
mechanism: A multi-stage anchoring system uses discrete physical anchors extending from a base surface to mechanically lock successive material layers in position. A boundary-defining structure connected to the anchors establishes a reference plane, with a first layer applied below the anchor height and a second layer applied to the boundary level. The anchors create interlocking engagement with both layers, while the boundary structure shields the inner layer from direct exposure to external abrasive forces.
mechanism_raw: Standoffs anchored to the kiln shell act as physical anchors extending upward; a grid connected to the tops of the standoffs defines a boundary and structural reference. The first castable insulative layer is applied to a depth below the standoff height, and the second abrasion-resistant layer is applied to the level of the grid. The standoffs mechanically lock both layers in place, while the grid (preferably honeycomb) shields the inner insulative layer from direct abrasive wear by the outer layer and environment.

abstract: A sewing machine for sewing workpieces, comprises a stationary bottom part with an arm which has one end pivotally mounted on the bottom part and an opposite end overlying the bottom part. The arm is movable from a fixed sewing position to an inoperable position away from the point of stitch formation. A revolving looper is mounted on the end of the opposite arm and it has a thread exit opening and a needle is mounted for upward and downward movement in the bottom part for cooperation with the looper. The workpiece is clamped between the base part and the arm and the needle traverses the workpiece upwardly. The construction includes a looper thread guide member mounted on the opposite arm adjacent the looper and has a thread deflector located between the needle path and the thread exit opening of the looper and extending above the point of stitch formation directly laterally of the needle path crosswise to the axis of the looper.
problem: Maintaining proper thread path alignment between the needle and the revolving looper as the sewing arm pivots between an operative sewing position and an inoperative position away from the stitch formation point.
constraint: The thread deflector must be positioned to maintain proper thread path geometry throughout the full pivoting range of the arm, without interfering with needle movement or stitch formation.
mechanism: A co-moving thread guidance assembly is mounted directly on a pivoting mechanical arm to maintain alignment between a moving element and a stationary element throughout the arm's full range of motion. A deflector positioned between the moving element's path and the stationary element's exit point redirects the thread along a consistent trajectory, ensuring geometric continuity of the thread path regardless of the arm's angular orientation.
mechanism_raw: A looper thread guide member is mounted directly on the pivoting arm adjacent to the looper, so it moves with the arm throughout its range of motion. A thread deflector on this guide is positioned between the needle path and the looper's thread exit opening, extending above the stitch formation point and laterally across the needle path. This ensures the thread is properly deflected and guided regardless of the arm's angular position, maintaining consistent stitch formation.

abstract: There is disclosed an axial flow fan having blades which are made up of metallic inner portions attached to the hub of the fan, and outer plastic portions whose inner ends are secured to the outer ends of the metallic portion. The plastic portions are hollow and have an exterior surface of air foil cross section, and seal discs on one side of the hub extend outwardly therefrom to approximately the intersection of the metallic and plastic portions.
problem: Creating axial flow fan blades that combine structural integrity at the hub attachment with lightweight, aerodynamically optimized outer portions.
constraint: The interface between the metallic and plastic portions must securely transfer loads while maintaining the airfoil profile and aerodynamic continuity of the blade.
mechanism: A composite blade structure transitions between material properties along its radial length, with a high-strength inner segment for load transfer and a lightweight outer segment optimized for aerodynamic performance. An intermediate sealing element extends from the attachment point to the material interface, maintaining aerodynamic continuity while enabling each segment to fulfill distinct structural and functional requirements.
mechanism_raw: Each blade is constructed as a composite along its radial length: a metallic inner portion is attached to the hub for structural strength and load transfer, while a hollow plastic outer portion with an airfoil-shaped exterior surface is secured to the outer end of the metallic portion. Seal discs extend outward from the hub to approximately the interface between the metallic and plastic portions, providing aerodynamic sealing. This material transition allows each segment to fulfill its specific functional requirement.

abstract: An open-fronted container 1 has a base 2, side walls 3 and a back wall 4 and is capable of supporting an identical overlying container, in column stacking relationship therewith. The container is provided with a pivotable frame member 9', having a generally U-shaped portion and integral cranked legs, for supporting an overhanging cantilevered end of the overlying container. The frame has an inoperative position 9 in which it can rest on the upper edge of the rear wall and in the rebate defined by integral extension 8, when not supporting an overlying container, and abuts extensions 10 and 11 when in the supporting position.
problem: Creating a container that can support an identical overlying container in column stacking while having a non-interfering, stable position when used standalone.
constraint: The frame geometry and pivot point must allow automatic transition between the resting and supporting positions based solely on the presence or absence of an overlying load, without manual intervention.
mechanism: A load-responsive pivoting frame automatically switches between a resting state and a supporting state based on the presence or absence of an external force. The frame's geometry includes a U-shaped engagement portion and offset support legs that pivot around a fixed axis. In the resting state, the frame is constrained by surface features, while applied force from an overlying load rotates the frame to deploy the support legs into a load-bearing configuration.
mechanism_raw: A pivotable frame member with a U-shaped portion and integral cranked legs is mounted on the container. When no overlying container is present, the frame rests in an inoperative position on the upper edge of the rear wall and within a rebate defined by an integral extension. When an overlying container is placed, its cantilevered end applies force that pivots the frame into a supporting position where the cranked legs abut extensions, providing structural support for the stacked load.

abstract: A tanning process comprising pickling a hide which has previously subjected to beamhouse works such as depilation if necessary, decalcification and beating, in the presence of urotropin and at least one tanning improver selected from chromium and aluminum salts as well as from phenolic compounds, organic compounds containing nitrogen and sulphur or halogen atoms, organic carboxylic acids, organotin compounds, copper compounds and arsenic compounds.
reason: The abstract describes a chemical tanning process by listing the compounds used (urotropin and various tanning improvers) but does not explain the causal mechanism of how these chemicals interact to produce the tanning effect. It is a formulation list rather than a description of a functional principle.

abstract: Metal sheet (cold-rolled steel sheet) contaminated with rolling oil is heated at a temperature higher than its recrystallization temperature in a naked flame furnace, e.g. of the incomplete combustion type. The heated sheet is then rapidly cooled by contact with an aqueous medium. The resulting sheet has considerably improved suitability for phosphate coating and painting, compared with sheet which is annealed after alkaline degreasing. The sheet is preferably treated with formic acid.
problem: Metal sheet contaminated with rolling oil has poor suitability for phosphate coating and painting after conventional alkaline degreasing and annealing.
constraint: The heating temperature must exceed the recrystallization temperature to activate the desired metallurgical transformation, while the cooling must be rapid enough (quenching) to preserve the altered surface state rather than allowing equilibrium annealing to occur.
mechanism: Subjecting a contaminated surface to a controlled thermal cycle: heating beyond a critical phase-transformation threshold to activate metallurgical restructuring, followed by rapid cooling to arrest equilibrium recovery and preserve an altered surface state that enhances subsequent coating adhesion.
mechanism_raw: Heating the contaminated sheet above its recrystallization temperature in a flame furnace, then rapidly quenching it by contact with an aqueous medium. The rapid thermal cycle alters the surface condition and microstructure, removing or transforming oil contamination residues and creating a surface state that is more receptive to phosphate coating and painting.

abstract: A high yield technique to convert normally-unusable round logs of balsa or other species of wood whose diameter is less than about 4 inches into large rectangular panels that are contourable.The raw logs are first peeled to expose the wood and are then cut into round pieces of a desired length. The pieces, after being kiln-dried, are stacked to form a dry assembly in which the pieces are separated from each other to define a matrix of intersticial spaces. The pieces in the assembly are then interlaminated in a mold by filling the matrix with an elastomeric plastic solution which, when cured, functions as an adhesive to provide an integrated stock block. The stock block is then divided into panels of the desired thickness, each panel being constituted by an array of round wood tiles joined together by elastomeric hinges, whereby the resultant panel is contourable and may be conformed to a curved surface.
problem: Small-diameter round logs (less than about 4 inches) that are normally unusable are to be converted into large rectangular panels that can conform to curved surfaces.
constraint: The interstices must be sized and positioned so that the cured elastomer provides sufficient adhesion to hold the elements together as a unified block while remaining flexible enough to function as hinges, and the elements must be dried before assembly to prevent moisture-related degradation of the bond.
mechanism: Arranging discrete rigid elements in a stacked configuration with intentional gaps, then filling the gaps with a compliant bonding medium that cures to simultaneously rigidize inter-element connections and retain localized flexibility, enabling the assembly to conform to curved geometries while maintaining structural coherence.
mechanism_raw: Discrete wood elements are arranged in a stacked matrix with intentional interstices between them, then the interstices are filled with an elastomeric material that cures to simultaneously bond the elements and act as flexible hinges. This creates an integrated composite block where each element remains individually articulable through the elastomeric hinges, enabling the final panel to be contoured to curved surfaces.

abstract: A method of repairing cracks in a concrete structure to prevent leakage wherein rods are inserted in the crack at spaced intervals to extend outwardly therefrom. A surface seal is applied to extend partially into the crack near the structure outer surface from which the rods extend, and to the structure outer surface adjacent to the crack and around the rods so that the surface seal acts as a surface barrier for the filler to be injected. Port members, having hollow shaft portions, and a flange portion are placed over the rods with the flange portions approximately adjacent the structure outer surface. Substantially the entire flange portion is embedded in the surface seal. The surface seal is allowed to cure to define a surface barrier for the filler, and the rods are removed from the crack and port members such that the ports communicate with the crack cavity behind the surface seal. After the surface seal cures, a filler is injected through the port members and into the crack cavity, and the port members are plugged. A port and plug assembly for use in sealing the cracks has a hollow shaft portion and a flange portion at one end thereof. The flange defines the base of the port member and is generally flat with the shaft extending from only one side of the base, the base being adapted to be embedded in a surface seal in the crack sealing method.
problem: Cracks in concrete structures must be sealed to prevent leakage, requiring filler to be injected into the crack cavity without surface spillage.
constraint: The surface seal must fully cure to form a reliable barrier before rod removal, and the port flanges must be embedded in the seal so that withdrawal of the rods creates clean hollow channels without breaking the surface barrier.
mechanism: Establishing temporary hollow channels within a defect using removable inserts, forming a cured barrier over the defect that embeds the channel inlets, then injecting filler through the channels into the defect cavity while maintaining barrier integrity during insert removal.
mechanism_raw: Removable rods are inserted into the crack to temporarily establish hollow port channels. A surface seal is applied over the crack and around the rods, embedding port members with flanges. After the seal cures into a barrier, the rods are withdrawn, leaving hollow pathways that communicate with the crack cavity behind the seal. Filler is then injected through these ports and into the cavity, and the ports are plugged.

abstract: A side bearing comprises integrally bonded pieces including an elastomeric cushion member secured to top and bottom plates and flexible leveling means secured to the bottom plate. The bearing is designed for connection between the bolster and truck side frames of a railway car. The elastomeric member includes progressively larger openings therein extending from its center to its ends to provide varying flexibility to permit articulation of the truck side frames relative to the bolster during operation.
problem: A railway car side bearing must allow articulation between the bolster and truck side frames during operation while maintaining load-bearing support.
constraint: The opening size progression must be calibrated so that flexibility increases gradually toward the ends without compromising the structural integrity of the elastomer, and the elastomer must be integrally bonded to the top and bottom plates to ensure load transfer while permitting the desired articulation.
mechanism: Implementing a compliant load-bearing element with spatially varying stiffness regions, where reduced constraint zones enable controlled articulation at high-motion areas while maintaining structural rigidity at load-transfer regions through a gradient of mechanical compliance.
mechanism_raw: An elastomeric cushion member with progressively larger openings extending from its center toward its ends provides a graded flexibility profile. The varying aperture sizes create regions of differing compliance, allowing controlled articulation at the ends where motion is greatest while maintaining stiffness and support at the center where load transfer is critical.

abstract: In a method for gathering a ring shaped wire rod, particularly a wire rod made of steel, the wire rod is continuously conveyed and gathered in the form of a coil by means of a gathering apparatus including a gathering tub and a coil plate. In accordance with the present invention, the lowering speed of the coil plate is controlled in such a manner that piling position of said rings is always within a predetermined range. In addition, the ring shaped wire rod is dropped, while imparting a movement having a horizontal component to the ring shaped wire rod so as to increase the filling ratio over that of the prior art. The coils gathered in the present invention are more compact than in the prior art.
problem: Ring-shaped wire rod coils must be gathered more compactly than prior art methods to increase filling ratio and reduce storage volume.
constraint: The lowering speed control and horizontal motion must be coordinated so that the piling position remains within the target range while the horizontal movement enhances packing density without causing misalignment or jamming of the coils.
mechanism: Coordinating vertical displacement rate with lateral motion during deposition of helical elements to dynamically adjust pile positioning within a target zone, causing overlapping trajectories that increase packing density through interleaved layering rather than simple vertical accumulation.
mechanism_raw: The lowering speed of the coil plate is actively controlled to keep the piling position of the wire rings within a predetermined range, preventing uncontrolled accumulation. Simultaneously, the ring-shaped wire rod is dropped while imparting a horizontal component of motion, causing the rings to interleave and pack more densely than simple vertical stacking.
residual_terms: ["lowering speed control", "horizontal component of motion", "ring-shaped wire rod"]

abstract: A mounting and actuating apparatus for the tongs of a grapple wherein a pair of pulleys carrying the tongs are interconnected by cable means extending between the pulleys in generally figure eight configuration, one embodiment teaching driving one pulley by a fluid pressure cylinder positioned between the pulleys and utilizing axially offset cable links, the other embodiment including a multiplying linkage between the two tongs.
problem: Coordinating the movement of two tongs in a grapple to achieve synchronized opening/closing while maintaining mechanical efficiency.
constraint: Balancing compact mechanical design with sufficient force transmission and synchronization between the two tongs.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system uses opposing cable routing between two driven elements so that actuating one element causes the other to move in the opposite direction through a continuous loop. Force amplification or synchronization is achieved through offset connection points or compound linkages that distribute motion and torque between the elements.
mechanism_raw: Interconnected pulleys with cables arranged in a figure-eight configuration, where driving one pulley causes the other to move in opposition via the cable linkage, enabling coordinated tong motion. Axially offset cable links or multiplying linkages amplify or synchronize force application.

abstract: A combined stand and volume meter for round bottom flasks which functions regardless of the flask neck orientation. Interlocking planes of material create a greater than hemispheric cavity encircling the flask. Horizontal parallel lines, calibrated in volumetric units pass across the cavity, allowing for flask orientation compensation by Visual correlation of the fluid level and volumetric lines.
problem: Measuring fluid volume in a container (e.g., round-bottom flask) regardless of its orientation relative to gravity.
constraint: Ensuring the cavity geometry and calibration lines remain effective across all possible orientations of the container.
mechanism: A reference volume is defined by a rigid cavity surrounding the container, with calibrated visual indicators positioned across the cavity. The cavity geometry is designed to maintain a consistent relationship between fluid level and volume measurement across all orientations of the container, allowing visual correlation of fluid position to volumetric units.
mechanism_raw: A cavity formed by interlocking material planes creates a greater-than-hemispheric enclosure around the container. Horizontal calibrated lines across the cavity allow visual correlation of fluid level to volumetric units, compensating for orientation changes.

abstract: An apparatus for crushing articles, such as aluminum beverage cans. The crushing apparatus comprises a rotatable, polygonal-shaped drum having blades mounted on each flat outer surface of the drum which project outwardly beyond the respective surface. The articles to be crushed are introduced into the area between the drum and a spring-loaded pressure plate, and on rotation of the drum, the blades engage the articles and move them into the nip between the drum and pressure plate to crush and flatten the articles. The apparatus also includes a quick release mechanism in which the pressure plate can be readily released to correct a jamming situation.
problem: Efficiently crushing deformable articles (e.g., aluminum cans) while addressing mechanical jamming during operation.
constraint: Maintaining consistent crushing force and throughput while enabling rapid recovery from jamming conditions.
mechanism: A rotating multi-faced element with radially extending projections moves articles into a compression zone between the rotating element and a resiliently biased opposing surface. The geometry of the rotating element ensures progressive deformation of articles, while a selective disengagement mechanism allows rapid separation of the compression surfaces to clear obstructions.
mechanism_raw: A rotating polygonal drum with outward-projecting blades moves articles into a nip between the drum and a spring-loaded pressure plate. The drum's rotation and blade geometry ensure progressive crushing, while a quick-release mechanism allows rapid disengagement to resolve jams.

abstract: A pneumatic piston assembly wherein a first apertured piston having a piston well is secured by a diaphragm to a pneumatic chamber. A load-supporting element is received in and pivotally engages the floor of the piston well. The load to be isolated directly engages the load-supporting element. Vibrational forces acting on the chamber are primarily absorbed by the piston in a gimbal-like fashion, thereby effectively isolating the supported load from such forces.
problem: Isolating a supported load from vibrational forces transmitted through a mounting structure.
constraint: Balancing vibration isolation effectiveness with the need to stably support the load under varying force directions.
mechanism: A flexible membrane connects a movable barrier to a load-supporting element that can pivot in multiple axes. The load engages the pivoting element directly, while the flexible membrane absorbs vibrational forces by allowing relative motion between the barrier and the mounting structure, decoupling the load from transmitted vibrations.
mechanism_raw: A diaphragm-secured apertured piston with a gimbal-like load-supporting element allows the piston to pivot and absorb vibrational forces in multiple axes. The load directly engages the pivoting element, decoupling it from chamber vibrations.

abstract: A unitary portable flashlight assembly incorporating a hand operated generator and rechargeable batteries, such as the pressure vented nickel-cadmium type with welded electrodes. The generator is designed and operated to charge th batteries at a high rate for a short time to provide extended operation of the load during a later discharging mode. The batteries also serve to regulate the voltage during the charging mode thus protecting the load if it be connected during the charging period. The battery assembly can provide the necessary energy to operate such devices as radio receivers and transmitters, electric fire starters, etc., as well as providing a mechanical output.
problem: Providing extended operational time for portable devices using a hand-powered generator and rechargeable batteries.
constraint: Optimizing charge rate and battery capacity to maximize stored energy while preventing overcharging or voltage instability.
mechanism: An energy harvesting source charges an intermediate storage element at an elevated rate for a brief period, accumulating energy rapidly. The storage element then supplies regulated voltage to a load during discharge, sustaining operation over an extended duration. Voltage regulation during both charging and discharging protects connected devices from overcharging or voltage instability.
mechanism_raw: The generator charges batteries at a high rate for a short duration, storing energy quickly. The batteries then regulate voltage during discharge, enabling sustained operation of loads. Voltage regulation during charging protects connected devices.
residual_terms: ["energy harvesting source", "intermediate storage element", "elevated charge rate", "voltage regulation", "sustained operation"]

abstract: This invention provides a metal bonded diamond abrasive article of nickel-copper basis. The sintered metal bond, which consists essentially of 2 to 30% by weight of copper, 1 to 40% by weight of tin, 0.2 to 3% by weight of phosphorous, and at least 50% by weight of the remainder nickel, well disperses and retains diamond grits and minimizes the clogging and the variation in rate of stock removal.
problem: Minimizing clogging and variation in rate of stock removal in metal bonded diamond abrasive articles.
constraint: Balancing the proportions of alloying elements to achieve optimal diamond retention and abrasive efficiency without compromising structural integrity or increasing material costs.
mechanism: A controlled composition of binding elements with specific proportions of alloying components creates a sintered matrix that disperses and retains abrasive particles more effectively, reducing clogging and maintaining consistent performance by balancing retention strength and material efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A specific nickel-copper alloy composition with controlled percentages of copper, tin, phosphorus, and nickel creates a sintered metal bond that disperses and retains diamond grits more effectively, reducing clogging and maintaining consistent abrasive performance.

abstract: A carriage drive system for a metal working machine wherein the carriage supports the metal working tool. The carriage drive comprises a worm gear rotatably engaged with a rack arrangement, driven by a motor and gear box on the carriage. The rack arrangement comprises a pair of rack sections opposed to one another along the sides of the worm gear. The carriage drive is pivotably supported on the carriage by a pivot pin which permits slight rocking and self centering motion in the carriage drive as it propels the carriage on its ways.
problem: Maintaining stable and self-centering motion of a carriage drive system in a metal working machine despite mechanical tolerances or misalignment.
constraint: Allowing sufficient flexibility for self-alignment while maintaining rigid enough contact between the worm gear and rack to ensure precise propulsion and minimize wear.
mechanism: A pivotably mounted drive assembly allows limited rotational movement to enable self-centering alignment, ensuring continuous engagement between a rotating drive element and a linear track while propelling a platform along guided pathways.
mechanism_raw: A pivotably supported carriage drive with a pivot pin allows slight rocking and self-centering motion, enabling the worm gear and rack arrangement to maintain consistent engagement while propelling the carriage along its ways.

abstract: Concrete pipe including a hollow tube of concrete with a grid of reinforcing bars embedded therein. A plurality of inserts are embedded in the concrete pipe in between the bars of the grid and have passageways therethrough to form slots between the interior of the concrete pipe and the exterior thereof at predetermined locations to form slotted concrete pipe. The inserts are attached to the grid of reinforcing bars during formation of the pipe and the concrete is introduced to surround the grid and inserts and is permitted to set. Thereafter, the formed concrete pipe contains embedded reinforcing bars and inserts in predetermined locations resulting in a slotted reinforced concrete pipe.
problem: Creating reinforced concrete pipes with precisely positioned slots between the interior and exterior surfaces without compromising structural reinforcement.
constraint: Positioning inserts accurately within the reinforcing grid to form slots at desired locations without disrupting the load-bearing capacity of the rebar framework.
mechanism: Embedded formative elements with internal channels are positioned within a reinforcing framework during fabrication, allowing a binding medium to solidify around them and create predefined apertures that connect internal and external regions while preserving structural continuity through surrounding reinforcement.
mechanism_raw: Embedding inserts with passageways into the reinforcing bar grid during pipe formation allows concrete to set around them, creating predefined slots that connect the interior and exterior while maintaining structural integrity through the surrounding reinforcement.

abstract: The connecting part for electrical warp stop motions on weaving machines has two rectangular housing shells (2,3) pressed against each other at their open sides by means of a threaded pin (10) screwed into the first housing shell (2). The screw-head of the threaded pin is in the shape of a knob (11) and presses against the second housing shell (3). In the longitudinal sides (4,6) of both housing shells (2,3) are supporting slots (9) at equal distances to take up the contact bars. On the interior base (12,15) of each housing shell (2,3) is a strip (13,16) of elastic material and on each strip a contact foil (14,17) for conducting electricity to all the contact bars, the narrow edges of which have perfect contact with the contact foils, even at varying height resulting from deviations in manufacture, due to the elastic material under them. A plug pin (18), in the second housing shell (3) is in direct electrical contact to the contact foil (17) in this housing shell and a further plug pin (19) is electrically connected to the contact foil (14) in the first housing shell (2) by means of a rod (23) on the exterior of the longitudinal side of the second housing shell and by means of the screw-head (11) and the threaded pin (10).
problem: Maintaining reliable electrical contact in connectors despite manufacturing tolerances or dimensional variations in component height.
constraint: Selecting an elastic material with sufficient compliance to accommodate variations while maintaining durable contact pressure over repeated use cycles.
mechanism: Compliant material layers interposed between conductive surfaces and contact elements enable adaptive deformation to accommodate dimensional deviations, maintaining consistent electrical interface pressure through elastic recovery forces.
mechanism_raw: Elastic material strips placed beneath contact foils allow the foils to flex and conform to variations in contact bar height, ensuring consistent electrical contact even when components deviate from nominal dimensions.
residual_terms: ["compliant material layers", "conductive surfaces", "contact elements", "elastic recovery forces"]

abstract: A hoisting attachment for a tilt-up wall slab is provided with a remotely operable quick release mechanism which is under the control of the positional attitude of a hoisting cable-attached shackle. An improved assemblage of wall slab insert anchor, support stand for the insert anchor, and a recess former frictionally attached to the upper end of the anchor is also provided.
problem: Enabling remote, position-dependent release of a hoisting attachment for tilt-up wall slabs without manual intervention.
constraint: Ensuring the release mechanism activates only at the correct positional threshold to prevent accidental disengagement during lifting or positioning operations.
mechanism: A position-sensitive release system activates disengagement of a lifting coupling when a suspended component reaches a predetermined orientation, using gravitational or inertial forces to trigger separation only at the correct operational threshold.
mechanism_raw: A quick release mechanism controlled by the positional attitude of a hoisting cable-attached shackle automatically triggers release when the shackle reaches a specific orientation, allowing hands-free operation based on the load's position.

abstract: A drive system for a yarn false twisting apparatus is disclosed which may be readily converted to produce either S or Z twist, and which insures adequate tension of the drive belt. The apparatus comprises a pair of twist imparting members, and a drive belt system for rotating the twist imparting members which comprises a drive whorl positioned to engage a tangential belt, and a series of pulleys having a drive belt entrained thereabout for rotatably interconnecting the whorl and twist imparting members. The whorl and one of the pulleys are mounted coaxially on a whorl support member, which may be selectively positioned in one of two operating positions to place the whorl on opposite sides of the tangential belt. Another of the pulleys is an idler pulley, which is adjustably mounted for movement in a direction perpendicular to the yarn path of travel and so as to permit maintenance of an adequate tension on the drive belt.
problem: Converting between S and Z twist directions in yarn false twisting while maintaining consistent drive belt tension.
constraint: Balancing twist direction conversion with belt tension requires precise mechanical positioning without compromising structural integrity or operational stability.
mechanism: Coaxial mounting of a rotational element and a tensioning element on a shared support allows selective repositioning to reverse the rotational element's orientation relative to a moving belt, enabling directional conversion. An adjustably mounted tensioning element moves perpendicular to the material path to dynamically regulate belt tension.
mechanism_raw: Coaxial mounting of the whorl and pulley on a support member allows selective positioning to reverse the whorl's side relative to the tangential belt, enabling twist direction conversion. An adjustably mounted idler pulley moves perpendicular to the yarn path to dynamically maintain belt tension.

abstract: A blowing nozzle for a shuttleless weaving machine, in the shape of a hollow needle with a single blowing aperture or a plurality of elementary apertures in its side wall. The mouth of each aperture is recessed with respect to a surface surrounding it in order to prevent scraping material from warp threads moving past the nozzle. Such material could otherwise block the aperture.
problem: Preventing blockage of blowing apertures in a shuttleless weaving nozzle by material scraped from warp threads during high-speed operation.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient airflow through the aperture while ensuring the recessed design does not impede the nozzle's structural or aerodynamic performance.
mechanism: Recessing an aperture mouth relative to a surrounding surface creates a geometric barrier that prevents direct contact between moving material and the aperture edge, reducing material accumulation and subsequent blockage.
mechanism_raw: Recessing the aperture mouth relative to the surrounding surface creates a geometric barrier that prevents direct contact between moving warp threads and the aperture edge, reducing material scraping and subsequent blockage.

abstract: A discharge electrode and discharge electrode assembly having longer more reliable service life than conventional tensioned wires wherein the electrode is categorized as rigid because its mechanical behavior more closely resembles that of a structural beam than a wire of equal length and the electrode in the preferred embodiment has a flattened ellipsoidal configuration with corona members projecting substantially along a plane passing through the long axis of the ellipsoidal electrode.
problem: Extending the service life of discharge electrodes beyond conventional tensioned wires prone to mechanical failure under operational stress.
constraint: Achieving sufficient electrical performance (e.g., corona discharge efficiency) while maintaining structural rigidity to withstand mechanical loads over extended use.
mechanism: Designing an electrical discharge element as a rigid structural beam with a flattened ellipsoidal shape and planar discharge surfaces distributes mechanical stress more evenly, reducing localized strain and failure points compared to flexible conductors.
mechanism_raw: Designing the electrode as a rigid structural beam with a flattened ellipsoidal shape and planar corona members distributes mechanical stress more evenly, reducing localized strain and failure points compared to flexible wires.
residual_terms: ["rigid structural beam", "flattened ellipsoidal shape", "planar discharge surfaces"]

abstract: A multi-cylinder pump for a cryogenic liquid is provided with an unloading system in which the inlet valve of each cylinder can be selectively held open or permitted to close. In the closed position, the operation of the cylinder is normal; while, in the open position, the liquid fails to attain sufficient pressure to exit through the outlet valve, thereby deactivating the cylinder. Preferably, the unloading system comprises several plunger assemblies which may be extended in order to engage the inlet valve and hold it in the open position. Each plunger assembly may be activated by means of a manual thumb screw or in accordance with the change in a pressure differential acting on the plunger. Alternatively, the plunger assembly may be activated electronically by means of a solenoid.
problem: Selectively deactivating individual cylinders in a multi-cylinder cryogenic pump to control output pressure and flow without disrupting overall system operation.
constraint: Ensuring reliable valve engagement and disengagement while maintaining precise pressure control and minimizing mechanical wear in cryogenic conditions.
mechanism: Plunger assemblies engage inlet valves to hold them open, preventing pressure buildup in selected chambers and effectively deactivating them. Activation can be manual, pressure-differential-driven, or electronic via solenoids.
mechanism_raw: Plunger assemblies engage inlet valves to hold them open, preventing pressure buildup in selected cylinders and effectively deactivating them. Activation can be manual, pressure-differential-driven, or electronic via solenoids.

abstract: A process for making asphalt concrete comprises mixing starting materials including aggregate and binder material and optionally, other additives, to a final temperature of about 60.degree. C. to about 150.degree. C. in an indirectly heated mixing chamber which is sealed. The moisture content of the asphalt concrete mixture is controlled as a function of the moisture content of the starting materials. Apparatus for performing the process in a continuous or batch operation is also set forth.
problem: Controlling moisture content in asphalt concrete mixtures during continuous or batch mixing to ensure consistent material quality and performance.
constraint: Balancing temperature control (60–150°C) with moisture regulation to prevent overheating or under-mixing while accommodating variable input material properties.
mechanism: Monitoring the moisture content of input materials and dynamically adjusting the mixing process (e.g., temperature, timing, or additive introduction) in a sealed chamber maintains target moisture levels throughout production.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring the moisture content of starting materials and dynamically adjusting the mixing process (e.g., temperature, timing, or additive introduction) in a sealed chamber to maintain target moisture levels throughout production.

abstract: Waste thermoplastic resin film is cleaned to reclaim raw material for subsequent recycling by crushing a mass of the waste film into pieces and then feeding the pieces onto a moving mesh conveyor immersed in a wash tank which is filled with a cleaning liquid; the liquid being at a temperature sufficient to soften the pieces. Cleaning is promoted by irradiating the pieces on the conveyor with ultrasonic energy from positions located on opposite lateral sides of and just above the upper surface of the conveyor while simultaneously forcing liquid in the tank to flow in the same direction as the conveyor while directing jets of additional liquid into the tank in the opposite direction to produce a forced circulatory flow pattern within the tank.
problem: Effective cleaning of waste thermoplastic resin film to reclaim raw material for recycling.
constraint: Balancing ultrasonic energy application and liquid flow directions to maintain a stable circulatory flow pattern without disrupting the conveyor's movement or piece transport.
mechanism: Applying vibrational energy from opposing lateral directions to a moving support surface while establishing a counteracting fluid flow pattern to create a stable circulatory cleaning action on softened thermoplastic pieces.
mechanism_raw: Combining ultrasonic irradiation applied from opposite lateral sides of a moving mesh conveyor with a forced circulatory flow pattern created by opposing liquid jets and conveyor-direction flow to enhance cleaning action on softened thermoplastic pieces.

abstract: A process for the production of reinforced rubber articles formed from polyester yarn embedded into rubber stock is disclosed. The process comprises the steps of: (1) treating the yarn with a finish composition which comprises water and a silane having the structural formula: ##STR1## wherein n=2 to 5, and (2) including from about 2 to 50 parts, per hundred parts of rubber, of silica particles in the rubber stock. The reinforced rubber article is preferably a pneumatic passenger tire which has excellent adhesion of tire cord to rubber.
problem: Achieving strong adhesion between polyester yarn and rubber stock in reinforced rubber articles like tires.
constraint: Optimizing the silane treatment concentration and silica particle loading to maximize adhesion without degrading rubber elasticity or processability.
mechanism: Introducing a chemical coupling agent to promote interfacial bonding between a fiber and a matrix material, combined with incorporating particulate reinforcement to enhance mechanical interlocking and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Treating the yarn with a silane coupling agent to improve chemical bonding at the fiber-rubber interface, combined with incorporating silica particles into the rubber stock to enhance mechanical interlocking and matrix reinforcement.

abstract: A wood splitting maul includes a maul head having two inclined blade faces that meet to form a sharpened blade edge. A plurality of elongated, cylindrical roller bearing elements are rotatably disposed in respective recesses in each of the blade faces and extend outwardly from the blade faces to force the walls of a split being formed in a log to move away from a portion of the blade faces, reducing friction between the walls of the split and the blade faces.
problem: Reducing friction between split log walls and blade faces during wood splitting to improve cutting efficiency.
constraint: Positioning and sizing the rollers to ensure they engage the split walls effectively without interfering with the blade's penetration or splitting force.
mechanism: Mounting rotating elements on opposing surfaces of a cutting tool so that contact with a workpiece causes rotation, actively displacing separated material away from the tool to reduce frictional resistance during penetration.
mechanism_raw: Mounting rotatable cylindrical roller bearings on the blade faces so that as the blade enters the log, the rollers rotate and actively push the split walls away from the blade, minimizing contact friction.

abstract: An anti-soiling treating agent comprising PA0 (a) a perfluoroalkyl-containing hybrid urethane compound (I) resulting from the addition reaction of two perfluoroalkyl-containing alcohols which have a difference in melting point of at least 20.degree. C. and are selected from compounds of the following formula EQU Rf--A--B--OH PA1 wherein Rf represents a linear or branched perfluoroalkyl group, A is the group --CH.sub.2 --.sub.l in which l is an integer of 0 to 5, the group ##STR1## in which R is a hydrogen atom, an alkyl group having not more than 12 carbon atoms or a substituted alkyl group, the group ##STR2## in which R is as defined above, a phenylene group, an ether linkage, or an ester linkage, and B represents an alkylene or aralkylene group having not more than 12 carbon atoms, or a derivative thereof containing an ether linkage, PA0 the mole ratio between the two alcohols being 33-67:67-33, with a polyisocyanate, or PA0 (b) a composition comprising the perfluoroalkyl-containing hybrid urethane compound (I) and a fluorine-free vinyl polymer (II) having a Rockwell hardness of 90 to 130, or PA0 (c) a composition comprising the perfluoroalkyl-containing hybrid urethane compound (I) and a perfluoroalkyl-containing vinyl polymer (III), or PA0 (d) a composition comprising the perfluoroalkyl-containing hybrid urethane compound (I), the perfluoroalkyl-containing vinyl polymer (III) and the fluorine-free vinyl polymer (II), and if desired, water and/or an organic solvent.
problem: Creating a durable anti-soiling coating with balanced surface properties for long-lasting performance.
constraint: Controlling the mole ratio of the two alcohols (33-67:67-33) and the Rockwell hardness of the vinyl polymer (90-130) to achieve optimal coating integrity and anti-soiling efficacy.
mechanism: Blending a hybrid compound with low surface energy properties and a polymer matrix with controlled hardness to create a coating that balances anti-soiling efficacy, chemical resistance, and mechanical durability.
mechanism_raw: Blending a perfluoroalkyl-containing hybrid urethane compound (formed from two alcohols with a ≥20°C melting point difference) with fluorine-free or fluorinated vinyl polymers to combine low surface energy, hardness, and chemical resistance.

abstract: A method and apparatus for forming rings that is particularly suited for forming plow rings from elongated lengths of stock having irregular cross sectional shape. A length of stock (12) is positioned against a mandrel (20), the end of the stock being pre-bent from a previous bending operation, with the free end of the stock extending beyond the mandrel. A movable bending element (24) is brought into contact with the stock opposite the point of contact with the mandrel, and advanced around the mandrel partially bending the stock. A clamp (82) clamps the partially bent stock against the mandrel and a cutter (98) then cuts the stock, leaving a partial bend in the newly formed free end of the stock, the cut portion of stock being clamped to the mandrel. The length of stock is moved away from the mandrel so that the bending of the cut portion around the mandrel can be completed.
problem: Forming closed rings from elongated stock with irregular cross-sectional shapes.
constraint: Coordinating the timing and positioning of bending, clamping, cutting, and post-cut bending steps to accommodate irregular stock geometry without misalignment or incomplete closure.
mechanism: Executing a sequential forming process involving partial deformation around a shaping element, temporary fixation of the deformed geometry, material removal, and completion of the deformation to achieve a closed-loop structure from irregular stock.
mechanism_raw: Using a sequential process of partial bending around a mandrel, clamping the partially bent stock, cutting it to length, and then completing the bend by moving the clamped stock away from the mandrel to form a closed ring.

abstract: A plurality of containers are interconnected in side by side generally parallel relationship by flexible substantially non-expandable belts so that such containers may be in abutting relationship when in stored position and may be spaced a predetermined distance apart when in use and such belts have limited axial movement while the axes remain substantially parallel with each other.
problem: Need to store multiple containers compactly while allowing them to be deployed at a controlled spacing for use, without losing parallel alignment between them.
constraint: The belts must be flexible enough to allow relative movement between containers yet non-expandable enough to maintain controlled spacing; axial movement is limited to preserve parallel alignment of all container axes.
mechanism: Flexible, non-extensible linkages connect parallel containers, permitting transition between a compact abutting arrangement and a spaced-apart arrangement. The linkages allow limited axial displacement while constraining the container axes to remain substantially parallel, ensuring controlled, reversible spacing change without loss of parallel alignment.
mechanism_raw: Flexible but substantially non-expandable belts interconnect parallel containers, allowing them to transition from an abutting (stored) configuration to a spaced-apart (use) configuration. The belts permit limited axial movement while constraining the container axes to remain substantially parallel, so the spacing change is controlled and reversible.

abstract: An in-hole motor drill assembly has the rotor of the motor which may be connected to the drill bit through a shaft connected to the rotor, and a housing which may be connected to the running string, and a normally disengaged clutch between said housing and said shaft. Means are provided for engaging the clutch by exerting a negative force on said housing, which is applied to the shaft by a pick-up bearing, if the bit is stuck against upward movement. The shaft can be rotated by rotation of the running string. In normal operation, during drilling, the clutch is disengaged to permit the shaft to rotate relative to the housing. The bearing which picks up the shaft and bit, during normal off-bottom circulation or retrieval of the assembly, is constructed to permit longitudinal movement of the housing relative to the shaft, when the bit is stuck, to engage the clutch.
problem: When a drill bit becomes stuck against upward movement, the drill string rotation cannot be transmitted to the bit, preventing recovery or continued drilling.
constraint: The clutch must remain disengaged during normal drilling to permit independent shaft rotation, yet engage reliably when upward force is applied; the pick-up bearing must allow longitudinal movement of the housing relative to the shaft to enable clutch engagement under stuck conditions.
mechanism: A normally disengaged coupling between a housing and a shaft automatically engages when an upward force is applied to the housing. A force-transfer element transmits this force to the shaft, causing the coupling to connect the housing's rotation to the shaft, thereby transmitting input rotation to the stuck component. During normal operation, the coupling remains disengaged to allow independent shaft rotation.
mechanism_raw: A normally disengaged clutch between the housing and shaft automatically engages when a negative (upward) force is applied to the housing. A pick-up bearing transfers this force to the shaft, causing the clutch to couple the housing rotation to the shaft, thereby transmitting drill string rotation to the stuck bit. During normal drilling, the clutch remains disengaged to allow independent shaft rotation.
residual_terms: ["normally disengaged coupling", "upward force", "force-transfer element", "housing rotation", "shaft rotation"]

abstract: Crown corks are conveyed from a supply source along an aligning track to a helically shaped guide track and then on to a capping device. A conveying disc rotates about a central axis and has a planar surface extending transversely of the central axis adjacent to the guide track. The conveying disc moves individual crown corks from the aligning track through the guide track to receiving pockets in the capping device. The receiving pockets travel along a circular path which has a transfer point disposed tangentially to the circumferential edge of the planar surface of the conveying disc.
problem: Need to transfer individual discrete items (crown corks) from a linear/helical feed track to rotating receiving pockets on a capping device without jamming or misalignment.
constraint: The transfer point must be precisely tangentially disposed relative to the disc's circumferential edge to ensure smooth handoff without impact or misalignment; the disc must rotate about a fixed central axis to maintain consistent transfer timing.
mechanism: A rotating transfer element with a planar surface bridges between a linear feed path and a circular receiving path. Items are moved from the feed path onto the transfer element's surface and carried to a handoff point disposed tangentially to the transfer element's circumferential edge, where they are transferred to receiving pockets traveling along their circular path. The tangential geometry ensures smooth, continuous transfer between the two moving systems.
mechanism_raw: A rotating conveying disc with a planar surface bridges between the guide track and the circular path of receiving pockets. Items are moved from the guide track onto the disc's planar surface and carried to a transfer point disposed tangentially to the disc's circumferential edge, where they are handed off to the receiving pockets traveling along their circular path. The tangential geometry ensures smooth, continuous transfer between the two moving systems.
residual_terms: ["rotating transfer element", "planar surface", "linear feed path", "circular receiving path", "tangential handoff point", "circumferential edge"]

abstract: A bird action toy in which a bird toy body capable of inclining forward and returning to the upright position on a perch and of performing such actions simultaneously as opening and closing its bill, producing chirping sounds and swinging its tail is detachably fitted over the supporting member through an adapter. The bird toy body comprises cam and a motor for driving the cam, the cam being engaged with the engagement rod projecting from the perch so as to incline the body forwardly and return it to the upright position. The perch serves as a case for storing batteries to drive the motor installed in the toy body.
problem: Need to produce multiple coordinated mechanical actions (forward inclination, bill opening/closing, tail swinging, sound production) from a single motor in a compact, detachable toy.
constraint: The cam profile and engagement rod geometry must be designed to produce multiple coordinated motions from a single motor input; the toy body must be detachable from the perch while maintaining mechanical engagement with the cam and engagement rod.
mechanism: A single motor drives a shaped profile that engages with an extended linkage. The shaped profile converts the motor's rotary motion into coordinated oscillatory motion of the linkage, which simultaneously drives multiple mechanical actions including forward inclination and return, opening and closing, and swinging. The profile geometry and linkage engagement ensure all actions are synchronized from one power source.
mechanism_raw: A single motor drives a cam that engages with an engagement rod projecting from the perch. The cam converts the motor's rotary motion into coordinated oscillatory motion of the engagement rod, which simultaneously drives the bird body's forward inclination and return, bill opening/closing, and tail swinging. The cam profile and engagement geometry ensure all actions are synchronized from one power source.
residual_terms: ["single motor", "shaped profile", "extended linkage", "rotary motion", "oscillatory motion", "coordinated mechanical actions"]

abstract: An apparatus for producing and collecting a liquid extract and a pressed dry by-product from a mash of fibrous material includes an extraction chamber and a mechanism for compressing the mash of fibrous material within the extraction chamber to extract the liquid and form a pressed dry product therefrom. The extraction chamber includes a material inlet opening for filling the chamber with the mash, a liquid outlet opening for collecting the liquid extract, and a by-product outlet opening for collecting the dry by-product. The compressing mechanism expells the dry by-product from the extraction chamber once the liquid has been extracted from the mash. The mash is compressed within a movable work station, and the dry-product is expelled from the extraction chamber by moving the work station and discharging the dry product in accordance therewith.
problem: Need to extract liquid from a fibrous mash and separately collect both the liquid extract and the pressed dry by-product in a single processing operation.
constraint: The work station must be movable to perform both compression (for liquid extraction) and expulsion (for dry by-product removal) within the same chamber; the chamber must have separate outlets for liquid and dry product to prevent cross-contamination.
mechanism: A movable work station within a processing chamber first compresses material to extract liquid, which exits through a first outlet. The same work station then continues moving to expel the residual solid by-product through a second outlet. The sequential movement of the single work station performs both compression and expulsion in a coordinated cycle within the same chamber.
mechanism_raw: A movable work station within the extraction chamber compresses the fibrous mash to extract liquid, which exits through a liquid outlet. Once liquid extraction is complete, the same work station continues moving to expel the dry by-product through a separate by-product outlet. The sequential movement of the single work station performs both compression and expulsion in a coordinated cycle.
residual_terms: ["movable work station", "processing chamber", "compresses material", "liquid outlet", "residual solid by-product", "second outlet", "sequential movement"]

abstract: A hydraulic excavator having first and second booms pivoted end to end, plus an arm pivotally connected to a swinging end of the second boom. A bucket is pivotally mounted at the leading end of the arm. A boom operating linkage mechanism including a lever and hydraulic cylinders is mounted on a full-revolving base for swinging the first boom with respect to the base. The arm is adapted to rotate with respect to the second boom and therefore the bucket is capable of providing both back hoe and front loading operations.
problem: An excavator needs to perform both back hoe and front loading operations without requiring separate machines or manual reconfiguration.
constraint: Each additional pivot joint and hydraulic actuator increases mechanical and control complexity, but provides greater versatility in reach and functional modes; the trade-off is between system complexity and operational flexibility.
mechanism: Multiple serially connected articulated segments, each with an independently controllable joint, are configured so that the angular state of each joint determines the pose of a terminal effector. By coordinating the angular states across all joints, a single terminal effector attains multiple distinct functional configurations from one fixed base platform.
mechanism_raw: Serial articulated links (first boom, second boom, arm, bucket) are each pivotally connected and independently actuated, so the angular configuration of each joint determines the position and orientation of the end-effector (bucket). By coordinating the pivot angles of multiple sequential joints, a single end-effector achieves multiple functional configurations (back hoe vs. front loading) from one base platform.

abstract: A suction arrangement for removing labels from bottles comprising a label-softening container adapted to contain a liquid, a plurality of elongated bottle-receiving cells having each an open end for insertion and withdrawal of bottles into and from the cell and provided at its opposite end with a plurality of openings, a conveyor for transporting the cells closely adjacent each other and closely past an opening in a bottom portion of a wall defining a suction compartment within the container while liquid is continuously sucked out of the suction compartment and returned into the container so that a stream of liquid passes from the container through that cell which is located at any instant adjacent the opening in the bottom portion of the wall defining the suction compartment to thus remove the labels from the bottles and transport the labels through the opening into the suction compartment while transversely spaced bars extend in the suction compartment over the opening to prevent the bottles to pass together with the labels out of their cells.
problem: Labels need to be removed from bottles efficiently while preventing the bottles themselves from being drawn into or passing through the suction system along with the labels.
constraint: The system requires continuous liquid circulation and pumping to maintain the removal stream, trading energy and fluid handling costs against the selective removal of labels while retaining bottles.
mechanism: A moving carrier transporting a target object passes adjacent to a fluid extraction opening while a continuous fluid stream is drawn through the carrier, generating a flow that detaches and transports a lightweight contaminant. Transversely positioned barrier elements within the extraction zone permit passage of the lightweight detached contaminant but block the heavier target object, achieving separation by differential transport resistance.
mechanism_raw: A moving cell carrying a bottle passes adjacent to a suction opening while a continuous stream of liquid is drawn through the cell, creating a flow that detaches and carries away the label. Transversely spaced bars positioned in the suction compartment act as a selective barrier: they allow the lightweight detached label to pass through the opening but block the heavier bottle from following, achieving separation by differential transport.
residual_terms: ["fluid extraction opening", "continuous fluid stream", "lightweight contaminant", "heavier target object", "differential transport resistance", "barrier elements"]

abstract: Disclosed are dry mixes for the preparation of baked goods having yeasty flavor that do not require dough kneading or lengthy fermentation steps. Such mixes comprise flour, chemical leavening agents, active dry yeast, and a selected gum mixture comprising propylene glycol alginate, and a member selected from the group consisting of karaya gum, guar gum, xanthan gum, carboxymethyl cellulose, carregeenan gum, and mixtures thereof. Baked goods prepared from doughs made from the dry mixes herein require no kneading step. After a shortened fermentation step, the doughs can be baked in a conventional manner. The resultant baked goods are characterized by high specific volume and a bread-like consistency and texture.
problem: Baked goods with yeasty flavor and bread-like texture need to be produced without the time-consuming steps of dough kneading and lengthy fermentation.
constraint: The specific combination and ratio of gums must be carefully selected to achieve the right balance of dough handling properties, gas retention, and texture, trading ingredient specificity and cost against processing time savings.
mechanism: A formulated hydrocolloid matrix forms a viscoelastic network within a malleable substrate that entraps gas bubbles from multiple leavening sources. This network provides structural integrity and gas retention without mechanical working, while a combined chemical and biological leavening system delivers rapid expansion and flavor development in a shortened processing interval.
mechanism_raw: A specific hydrocolloid gum mixture (propylene glycol alginate combined with one of several secondary gums) forms a viscoelastic matrix in the dough that traps gas bubbles from both chemical leavening agents and active dry yeast. This matrix provides structural integrity and gas retention without mechanical kneading, while the dual leavening system (chemical + biological) achieves rapid rise and yeasty flavor in a shortened fermentation time.
residual_terms: ["hydrocolloid matrix", "viscoelastic network", "malleable substrate", "gas bubbles", "leavening sources", "chemical and biological leavening"]

abstract: This can opener opens and empties cans of their contents rapidly, especially paint and similar cans. The opener has a knife edge dimensioned and configured to penetrate an end, especially the bottom, of the can. There is a positioning means for disposing a can having two ends with one end over the knife edge. A means urges the can downward against the knife edge with sufficient force to cause the knife edge to penetrate the one end of the can. A means for receiving contents from the can is disposed beneath the knife edge. Cans may be opened and emptied in rapid sucession with this opener. An emptied can is moved forward by the positioning of a second can for opening and slides down into a can crusher. A piston operated can crusher cylinder is activated electro/pneumatically to come down and crush the emptied can and remove any remaining contents. When the piston retracts the crushed can drops out of the crusher.
problem: Cans need to be opened and emptied rapidly in succession, and the emptied cans need to be efficiently disposed of by crushing without interrupting the continuous operation.
constraint: The system requires precise coordination of positioning, cutting force, and crushing force in a continuous sequence, trading mechanical complexity and timing precision against throughput speed.
mechanism: An automated sequence positions a container over a cutting edge and applies sufficient force to penetrate the container end, while a receiver collects the contents. After opening, the emptied container is advanced by the positioning of the next container into a compression station where a piston applies compressive force to reduce the container volume, then retracts to eject the compressed container.
mechanism_raw: The system uses sequential automated positioning: a can is positioned over a knife edge and forced downward with sufficient force to penetrate the can end, while a receiver collects the contents. After opening, the emptied can is automatically advanced forward by the positioning of the next can, sliding it into a crusher station where a piston applies compressive force to crush the can, then retracts to eject the crushed can.

abstract: In an needle bar drawing device or gill box comprising needle bars carried by chains is arranged a bristle mat consisting of one or few layers of bristles extending along the whole needle field up to the proximity of a clamping gap formed between a pair of exit rollers. The bristle mat is penetrated by the needles of the needle field and creates a stripping effect at the disappearing position of the needles in the region of the nip, this stripping effect avoiding the conveying of fibers freely swimming in the sliver, and thus the danger and disadvantage of any lap forming.
problem: During needle bar drawing of fibers, fibers can detach from the needles and freely swim in the sliver, leading to lap formation and quality defects.
constraint: The bristle mat must be positioned precisely at the needle retraction point to be effective without interfering with the normal fiber drawing and clamping action, trading positioning precision against stripping effectiveness.
mechanism: A compliant fibrous stripping element is positioned along a needle field and penetrated by the needles. At the needle retraction point near the clamping gap, the compliant element creates a mechanical stripping action that removes fibers from the retracting needles before they can detach and disperse, directing them into the proper fiber stream.
mechanism_raw: A bristle mat is positioned along the needle field and penetrated by the needles. At the point where the needles retract near the nip (clamping gap between exit rollers), the bristle mat creates a mechanical stripping action that removes fibers from the needles before they can detach and freely swim in the sliver. The compliant bristles contact the retracting needles and strip off adhered fibers, directing them into the proper fiber stream rather than allowing them to disperse.
residual_terms: ["compliant fibrous stripping element", "needle field", "needle retraction point", "clamping gap", "mechanical stripping action"]

abstract: A worm press, especially for pressing vegetable matter, e.g. in the pressing of oil from oil-bearing seeds and fruits, comprises a worm having a plurality of worm sections and a housing within which the worm rotates and which is formed with rings defining axially spaced constrictions for the pressed mass between the worm sections. The worm has annular frustoconical shoulders juxtaposed with frustoconical flanks of the respective rings so that the flanks of each ring and shoulder define a respective constriction which is of a width adjustable by relative axial displacement of the worm and the housing, the rings being fixed in the housing and the shoulders being fixed on the worm.
problem: Need to press oil from oil-bearing seeds/fruits with adjustable compression to optimize extraction efficiency across varying material characteristics.
constraint: Rings are fixed in the housing and shoulders are fixed on the worm, so adjustment requires axial displacement of the entire worm relative to the housing; this trades individual component adjustability for structural simplicity and robustness under high pressure.
mechanism: Interlocking tapered surfaces on a rotating member and stationary housing rings create adjustable constrictions; relative axial displacement between the rotating member and housing changes the width of each constriction, thereby controlling the compression applied to the material being processed as it progresses through the device.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking frustoconical shoulders on the worm and frustoconical flanks on housing rings create adjustable constrictions; relative axial displacement of the worm and housing changes the width of each constriction, thereby controlling the compression applied to the pressed mass as it progresses through the press.

abstract: In an anvil assembly for powder-compacting press wherein an article is compacted of powder material against the face of the anvil clamped in position over a die cavity filled with powdered material, a reciprocable punch being disposed at the bottom of the die cavity for compacting the powdered material against the anvil face, the anvil is provided with a movable face portion which, during compaction of the powder material, is displaced away from the die cavity, compressing an elastomeric return spring.
problem: Need to compact powder material against an anvil face while accommodating variations in powder volume, density, or compressibility during the compaction cycle.
constraint: The elastomeric spring provides a controlled, proportional return force; the tradeoff is between sufficient compliance to accommodate powder variations and sufficient stiffness to achieve the required compaction density.
mechanism: A movable surface portion displaces away from a cavity during compaction, compressing a resilient return element; this compliance allows the surface to yield under pressure, maintaining contact with the material while absorbing volumetric variations, then the resilient element returns the surface after compaction.
mechanism_raw: A movable anvil face portion displaces away from the die cavity during compaction, compressing an elastomeric return spring; this compliance allows the anvil face to yield under pressure, maintaining contact with the powder while absorbing volumetric variations, then the spring returns the face after compaction.

abstract: A process of purifying silica sand comprises grinding sandstone, washing and desliming the ground sandstone to remove the major part of the clay-type binder, attrition-scrubbing the deslimed sand particles to release further amounts of binder therefrom, washing and desliming to remove said binder, drying and heating the sand particles, treating the hot sand with sulfuric acid to convert the iron oxides, ferrosilicates and ferro-aluminous impurities into water soluble compounds, attrition-scrubbing the hot suspension of the chemically treated sand to release the strongly adhering stains of said impurities, washing with cold water and desliming, conditioning the sand suspension with fatty acids or petroleum sulfonate collectors, a polyalcohol frothing agent and, if necessary, a mineral acid to bring the pH to from 1.5 to 7.0, carrying out a first froth-flotation to remove the remaining ferrosilicates and iron oxides, and carrying out a second froth-flotation with a fatty amine collector in the presence of sulfuric acid and/or hydrofluoric acid to activate the aluminosilicates and to remove the same at a pH of from 1.5 to 3.5.
problem: Need to purify silica sand by removing multiple distinct types of impurities (iron oxides, ferrosilicates, ferro-aluminous compounds) that require different treatment conditions.
constraint: Specific pH ranges (1.5-7.0 for first flotation, 1.5-3.5 for second) and chemical combinations are required for each stage; the tradeoff is between thorough multi-stage purification and increased process complexity and cost.
mechanism: Sequential application of different chemical treatments: acid treatment converts impurities into water-soluble compounds, mechanical agitation releases adhered contaminants, then different selective separation agents at different chemical conditions remove different impurity types; each stage targets impurities that respond to specific chemical conditions.
mechanism_raw: Sequential application of different chemical treatments: acid treatment converts impurities into water-soluble compounds, attrition-scrubbing releases adhered stains, then different flotation collectors at different pH levels selectively remove different impurity types; each stage targets impurities that respond to specific chemical conditions.

abstract: A counterweight arrangement for mobile vehicles including a pair of transversely spaced support members having notches formed therein. The counterweight has a pair of transversely spaced rod members secured thereto which are selectively received in the notches. A pair of transversely spaced cables are secured to the counterweight to raise and lower the counterweight. The cables are received around corresponding sheaves which may be repositioned to control the movement of the rod members into and out of the notches and around the support members.
problem: Need to raise, lower, and selectively position a counterweight on a mobile vehicle to balance the vehicle during operation.
constraint: Notched engagement provides discrete positioning but requires cable/sheve coordination to engage/disengage; the tradeoff is between precise discrete positioning and the mechanical complexity of coordinating multiple cable and sheave movements.
mechanism: Engagement members on the counterweight selectively interface with discrete positioning features on transversely spaced support members for step-wise positioning; tension elements raise and lower the counterweight, while repositionable guidance elements control the movement of engagement members into and out of the positioning features, coordinating lifting with engagement.
mechanism_raw: Rod members on the counterweight selectively engage notches on transversely spaced support members for discrete positioning; cables raise and lower the counterweight, while repositionable sheaves control the movement of rod members into and out of the notches, coordinating lifting with engagement.

abstract: A vertically adjustable pedestal trestle for theater stages or the like which includes a platform carried by a top frame and lockable supporting scissors are articulated to corners of the top frame as well as a vertical adjustment device which may be driven by motor power or manually. The vertical adjustment device includes one or more additional lifting scissors arranged centrally below the platform. The lifting scissors are provided at respective leg ends with runners or sliding elements and are adapted to be extended toward the underside of the platform.
problem: Need to vertically adjust a theater stage platform with stable, load-bearing support that can be locked at the desired height.
