constraint: The combination of distributed corner support scissors and centralized lifting scissors balances load distribution with adjustability; the tradeoff is between structural stability from corner support and the adjustability provided by the central lifting mechanism.
mechanism: Distributed corner support mechanisms provide stable load-bearing support; a central vertical adjustment device with additional lifting mechanisms arranged below the platform uses sliding runners at leg ends that extend toward the platform underside, providing the lifting force; a locking feature secures the position once adjusted.
mechanism_raw: Corner scissors mechanisms provide stable distributed support; a central vertical adjustment device with additional lifting scissors arranged below the platform uses sliding runners at leg ends that extend toward the platform underside, providing the lifting force; the lockable feature secures the position once adjusted.
residual_terms: ["distributed corner support", "central vertical adjustment", "sliding runners", "locking feature"]

abstract: Extruders are widely used to transform solid plastic materials into molten plastic materials. Because of the low thermal conductivity of plastic materials and the inefficient mixing of the plastic materials inside an extruder, the heat is not evenly distributed in the material being processed and some portion of the material emerges from the extruder with excessive heat. This invention discloses a new screw with a novel mixing section which promotes mixing of the hot, molten material with the cold, unmolten material inside the screw channel by its unique geometry, thereby improving the heat transfer from the hot, molten material to the cold, unmolten material and increasing the energy efficiency of the extruder.
problem: Uneven heat distribution in plastic materials during extrusion due to low thermal conductivity and inefficient mixing.
constraint: The screw geometry must balance mixing efficiency with structural integrity and throughput to avoid excessive pressure drop or mechanical failure.
mechanism: A rotating helical element with a specially configured mixing zone induces forced intimate contact between high-temperature and low-temperature regions of a material, enabling conductive energy transfer through enhanced physical mixing while maintaining structural continuity and flow characteristics.
mechanism_raw: A screw with a uniquely shaped mixing section forces intimate contact between hot molten and cold unmolten material, enabling conductive heat transfer from the molten to the unmolten regions through enhanced physical mixing.
residual_terms: ["helical element", "mixing zone", "conductive energy transfer", "physical mixing", "structural continuity", "flow characteristics"]

abstract: An apparatus is provided for conveying animals to be stunned. The apparatus comprises two sets of endless conveyor belts. Each set of belts defines a substantially V-shaped passageway. Animals are wedged between the V-shaped belts and conveyed into contact with stunning electrodes. The conveyor belts include a plurality of curved plates hinged together at their edges to form a gap free and uninterrupted operating surface to contact the animals's skin. The trailing edge of each plate partly surrounds the leading edge of the following plate. The outer surface of each plate is curved so that the surface is generally concentric with the axis of the reversing wheel. The gap between the first set of conveyor belts and the second set of conveyor belts is bridged by guide rollers positioned tangentially to the operating surface of the conveyor belts.
problem: Conveying animals into controlled contact with stunning electrodes while maintaining safe, gap-free contact with their skin.
constraint: The system must maintain consistent pressure and alignment to avoid injury while ensuring reliable conveyance into the stunning zone.
mechanism: Two opposing V-shaped transport surfaces converge to wedge an object between them, using articulated curved elements with matching contours to form a continuous contact interface, while alignment guides bridge the gap between transport sections to maintain positional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Two V-shaped conveyor belt sets wedge animals between them, using hinged curved plates with concentric surfaces to form a continuous contact surface, while guide rollers bridge the gap between belt sets to maintain alignment.
residual_terms: ["V-shaped transport surfaces", "articulated curved elements", "continuous contact interface", "alignment guides", "positional accuracy"]

abstract: An adhesive applicator has a nozzle through which adhesive can be dispensed to sheets of a set as the sheets are driven seriatim past the nozzle. Adhesive is furnished in a cartridge which is pressurized so that the adhesive is delivered from the cartridge to the nozzle under pressure. A valve controls the flow of adhesive from the nozzle, and the valve is under control of a logic and control unit. The logic and control unit receives signals from various sensors or detectors indicating, inter alia, the presence of an adhesive cartridge, the level of adhesive in the cartridge, the flow of adhesive from the nozzle, and the amount of adhesive in a collection bottle which receives surplus adhesive dispensed from the nozzle but not applied onto a sheet. The logic and control unit is capable of operating the valve that controls flow of adhesive from the nozzle so that adhesive is selectively dispensed from the nozzle to all but one sheet of a set of sheets. A purge cycle is initiated if adhesive does not flow from the nozzle when commanded to flow by the logic and control unit.
problem: Selective adhesive application to sheets in a set while detecting and recovering from flow failures.
constraint: The control system must balance real-time sensor feedback with precise valve timing to ensure consistent application and fault recovery without wasting adhesive.
mechanism: A control system monitors multiple sensor inputs representing operational states and selectively actuates a dispensing element to apply material to all but one target, initiating a recovery cycle if flow is obstructed.
mechanism_raw: A logic control unit monitors sensor inputs (cartridge presence, adhesive level, flow rate, surplus collection) and selectively actuates a valve to dispense adhesive to all but one sheet, initiating a purge cycle if flow is blocked.
residual_terms: ["control system", "sensor inputs", "operational states", "dispensing element", "recovery cycle", "flow obstruction"]

abstract: A carton for suspending an article within the carton and a blank for forming same has a collapsible arrangement for automatically forming the suspension support. This arrangement includes two parallel bridge panels, each of which is hingedly coupled at its opposite side edges to the front and back panels at locations spaced from the side panels of the carton. The upper edges of the bridge panels form a support surface which is substantially perpendicular and between the carton panels for supporting an edge of a cap of an article to suspend the article between the bridge panels and within the carton. Front flaps pivotedly mounted at the opposite side edges of the front panel may be formed in the front panel and located behind the cap of the article to create a shadow effect.
problem: Automatically forming a suspension support within a carton to suspend an article during packaging.
constraint: The bridge panel geometry must collapse flat during carton formation yet deploy reliably into a stable support structure without external intervention.
mechanism: Articulated bridge panels, connected to opposing surfaces at spaced intervals, deploy into a perpendicular support configuration when the structure is formed, using their upper edges to cradle and suspend an article.
mechanism_raw: Hinged bridge panels, coupled to front and back panels at spaced locations, deploy into a perpendicular support surface when the carton is erected, using their upper edges to cradle the article's edge.
residual_terms: ["articulated bridge panels", "opposing surfaces", "perpendicular support configuration", "upper edges", "cradle and suspend"]

abstract: A semiconductor memory is provided with a hook structure composed of first to fourth regions and is capable of non-destructive readout. The third and fourth regions of the hook structure are both made floating and each form one of main electrode regions of each of a write and/or refresh transistor and a readout transistor. Carriers which are injected from the other main electrode region of the write transistor are stored as excess majority carriers in the third region and majority carriers of the fourth region flow out therefrom into the first region via the third and second regions, in consequence of which the fourth region lacks in the majority carrier and voltages of the floating third and fourth regions vary. The voltage variation of the fourth region is read out by the readout transistor. The excess majority carriers stored in the third region flow out therefrom into the other main electrode region of the write transistor and become extinct when it operates as a refresh transistor.
problem: Non-destructive readout of stored data in a semiconductor memory while maintaining charge integrity.
constraint: The charge transfer and voltage sensing must occur without fully depleting the stored carriers, balancing readout sensitivity with data retention.
mechanism: A charge storage structure with isolated regions holds excess majority carriers in one region, which migrate through intermediate regions to alter voltages in another isolated region; this voltage variation is detected via a sensing element, and the stored charge is restored during a refresh cycle.
mechanism_raw: A hook structure with floating regions stores excess majority carriers in one region, which flow through intermediate regions to alter voltages in another floating region; this voltage variation is read out via a transistor, and the stored charge is replenished during a refresh cycle.
residual_terms: ["charge storage structure", "isolated regions", "majority carriers", "voltage variation", "sensing element", "refresh cycle"]

abstract: A viewing system with automatic correction of the reading distance as a function of the inclination of the screen housing. In accordance with the invention, the viewing system comprises a screen housing axially suspended on a U shape base. The screen housing is adjustable by inclination on its axis of suspension. For each inclination two pins carried by the screen housing and sliding in two angled slots carried by the base carry out an automatic correction of the distance separating the operator from the front face of the screen housing.
problem: Maintaining optimal viewing distance between an operator and a screen as the screen's inclination changes.
constraint: The system must maintain structural stability while allowing smooth adjustment through the pin-slot mechanism without manual intervention.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system translates angular displacement of a surface into controlled linear displacement of its position relative to a base, maintaining a geometric relationship between tilt angle and viewing distance through constrained sliding motion of pins within angled slots.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical linkage where pins sliding in angled slots automatically adjust the screen's axial position relative to the base in response to inclination changes, creating a direct geometric relationship between tilt angle and viewing distance.

abstract: A semi-automatic, semi-continuous method is provided for the manufacture of cast explosive boosters. The method makes us of a mold assembly which is transported through filling, cooling and disassembly stations in a substantially continuous manner with little or no manual intervention. The method is adaptable to the manufacture of sheath/core or multiple layer boosters employing two explosives of different sensitivities. The method results in reduced operating costs and improved safety.
problem: Reducing operating costs and improving safety in the manufacturing of cast explosive boosters through automation.
constraint: The mold assembly must be compatible with all processing stations and maintain integrity during transport to ensure consistent quality and safety.
mechanism: A continuous transport system moves a workpiece through a sequence of discrete processing stations, enabling semi-automated production flow with minimal manual intervention while maintaining compatibility and structural integrity across all stages.
mechanism_raw: Continuous transport of a mold assembly through discrete processing stations (filling, cooling, disassembly) with minimal manual intervention, enabling semi-automated production flow.

abstract: Risk of fracture of an optical fibre in an overhead stranded electric conductor having an optical fibre loosely housed in an elongate compartment extending throughout the length of the conductor when the conductor is subjected to a tensile load greater than that which the optical fibre is designed to withstand is substantially reduced by supporting the stranded conductor from each of two opposite sides of a tower by suspension means incorporating a weak link designed to fracture at a tensile load less than that which the optical fibre can withstand before fracturing. An excess length of the stranded conductor extends between fittings at which the suspension means are secured to the conductor, is arranged sinuously down one side face of the tower and, where the stranded conductor is an earth conductor, is detachably secured to the tower at spaced positions along its length by releasable clips. When the tensile load on the stranded conductor increases to a value greater than that which the weak links can withstand, a weak link will fracture and the excess length of stranded conductor will be detached from the tower to reduce the load on the stranded conductor and thereby reduce risk of optical fibre fracture.
problem: Preventing fracture of an optical fiber housed in an overhead conductor when tensile loads exceed the fiber's design limits.
constraint: The weak link's fracture threshold must be precisely calibrated to fail before the optical fiber reaches its tensile limit while maintaining overall conductor stability.
mechanism: A sacrificial element with a calibrated failure threshold is integrated into a load-bearing system, fracturing at a predetermined load below the critical component's limit to redistribute tension and protect the primary element from exceeding its tensile capacity.
mechanism_raw: A sacrificial weak link in the suspension system fractures at a predetermined load threshold below the fiber's breaking point, allowing excess conductor length to detach and redistribute tension away from the fiber.
residual_terms: ["sacrificial element", "calibrated failure threshold", "predetermined load", "tensile capacity", "redistribute tension"]

abstract: A composition comprising an agricultural fertilizer and pellets is disclosed. The fertilizer and the pellets are predominantly in the minus six plus thirty mesh size. The pellets consist essentially of at least one hydroxide, oxide or carbonate of calcium, magnesium or both, and constitute from 5 to 90 percent by weight of the composition. The pellets contain at least 2 percent by weight of calcium, magnesium or both in the form of the oxide, the hydroxide or both, calculated as the oxide.
reason: The patent describes a static material composition (fertilizer pellets with specific particle sizes and chemical compounds) without a dynamic causal mechanism or process that produces a functional effect through interaction between components.

abstract: Steel products may be coated with an insulating composition by a process which involves coating a uniform layer of finely ground glass powder on the steel and burning it at temperatures ranging from 700.degree.-1000.degree. C. Following, a paste comprising a mixture of the afore-mentioned glass, aluminum oxide and an evaporable liquid are deposited upon the burned coating, dried and burned again at 700.degree.-1000.degree. C. The resultant coatings adhere well to steel and resist temperatures as high as 860.degree. C., so suggesting then use for coating steel destined as a substitute for ceramic supports in electronic and hybrid microelectronic applications.
problem: Creating a durable, heat-resistant insulating coating on steel substrates for use in high-temperature electronic applications.
constraint: The process must balance temperature ranges (700–1000°C) and material composition to ensure adhesion, thermal stability, and resistance to degradation at operational temperatures up to 860°C.
mechanism: A multi-stage thermal bonding process sequentially applies and fuses layers of glass-based materials onto a substrate, using controlled temperature cycles to create a durable, heat-resistant coating with graded composition and adhesion properties.
mechanism_raw: Sequential application and thermal bonding of glass layers: first burning a glass powder layer, then applying a paste containing glass and aluminum oxide, followed by a second burn to form a multi-layered, adherent coating.
residual_terms: ["glass-based materials", "aluminum oxide", "thermal bonding", "multi-layered coating", "temperature cycles", "adhesion properties"]

abstract: The present invention concerns a method for processing a fiber sliver in a drafting arrangement, and a drafting arrangement for implementing the method. The objective for a drafting arrangement, which can be adapted to a wide range of staple lengths, to draft a fiber sliver at high speeds, has led to the following features of the invention: PA0 (a) The fiber sliver is deflected simultaneously in the drafting process systematically in such a manner that, the fiber sliver can be inserted into the subsequently arranged funnel and the subsequently arranged pair of calender rolls without further deflection. PA0 (b) All bottom rolls are fixedly arranged. PA0 (c) The first pressure rolls limiting the pre-drafting zone and the main drafting zone, respectively, are arranged to be shiftable along an arc about the rotational axis of the corresponding bottom roll in such a manner that the drafting zones are adaptable to the fiber length. PA1 In order to position these pressure rolls accurately in parallelism with respect to the corresponding bottom roll on the arc, there are provided arresting devices co-axially arranged with respect to the arc for taking-up bearing block pairs supporting the pressure rolls. PA0 (d) All pressure rolls as well as the pressure roll mounted on a double arm are jointly pivotable from a lifted-off threading-in position to a working position and vice versa.
problem: Drafting a fiber sliver at high speeds while adapting to a wide range of staple fiber lengths without requiring additional deflection steps or losing alignment between pressure and bottom rolls.
constraint: Balancing high-speed drafting operation with adaptability to varying staple lengths while maintaining parallel roll alignment and enabling quick transition between threading and working states.
mechanism: A fiber sliver is deflected simultaneously during drafting to maintain alignment with downstream processing elements. Adjustable mounting systems position drafting components along arc-shaped paths relative to their corresponding base elements, enabling repositioning to accommodate varying input characteristics. Locking mechanisms on the same arc paths secure components in precise parallel alignment. A shared actuation system transitions all components between a non-operational state and a working state.
mechanism_raw: The fiber sliver is deflected simultaneously during drafting so it enters the funnel and calender rolls without further deflection. The first pressure rolls are mounted on arc-shaped paths about the rotational axis of their corresponding bottom rolls, allowing the drafting zones to be repositioned to match fiber length. Co-axial arresting devices on the same arc take up bearing block pairs to lock the pressure rolls in precise parallel alignment with the bottom rolls. All pressure rolls are jointly pivotable between a threading position and a working position.

abstract: An apparatus for cutting tires is disclosed that employs: a base on which there is disposed two upstanding shafts (one rotatable), and first and second plates to sandwich therebetween the tire casing. Both plates have upstanding teeth members, an off-center hole and a center hole. The rotatable shaft is disposed in the center hole of both plates and the other shaft is disposed in the off-center hole of the first plate. On the same side of the first plate on which the upstanding teeth means are disposed, there is affixed an upstanding member which is received in the off-center hole of the second plate. A cutter bar is provided that has a cutting means and a rotatable handle on one terminal portion. The cutting bar also has a handle and it contains an elongated rectangular shaped slot. The terminal portion of the rotatable shaft is rectalinear in cross section and is disposed in the cutter bar slot so that upon rotation of the shaft, the cutter bar also rotates.
problem: Cutting tire casings efficiently by converting a single rotational input into a controlled cutting motion through a mechanical linkage that accommodates the irregular geometry of tires.
constraint: Achieving controlled cutting motion from a single rotational input while accommodating the non-uniform geometry of tire casings and maintaining structural stability during cutting.
mechanism: A rotational input is converted into controlled linear motion through a non-circular mechanical interface between a rotating element and a slot in a secondary component. The geometric mismatch between the rotating element and the slot forces the secondary component to move in a predetermined path. Offset mounting features in associated plates provide mechanical advantage and positional control for the resulting motion.
mechanism_raw: A rotatable shaft with a rectilinear (non-circular) cross-section terminal portion is disposed in an elongated slot in a cutter bar. When the shaft rotates, the non-circular interface between the shaft and the slot forces the cutter bar to rotate in a controlled manner, converting rotational input into cutting motion. The off-center hole arrangement in the plates provides the mechanical advantage and positioning needed for the cutting action.

abstract: A wafer baking oven has a set of baking tongs which move through the oven to effect baking of the wafers. The oven is particularly for wafer products such as flat wafers, low hollow wafers, sugar cones, wafer cups and wafer figures. There is a baking chamber through which the baking tongs move and a front end at which baked wafers are discharged from the baking tongs and fresh batter is poured into the tongs for baking. The region in which this takes place is referred to as a front port. The front port includes a batter pouring station and a discharge station with a chute and at least one discharge spider. To reduce loss of heat and to reduce the noise level of the wafer oven, the front port is surrounded by a housing which comprises, at least in part, an enclosure attached to a frame. The housing has two passage openings at the side which face the baking chamber, and the baking tongs pass through these passage openings as they move in a circuit between the baking oven and the front port. There is also an outlet opening in the enclosed housing of the front port for the discharge of baked wafers.
problem: Reducing heat loss and noise from a wafer baking oven's front port where baking tongs continuously enter and exit the oven chamber for batter pouring and wafer discharge.
constraint: Allowing continuous bidirectional movement of baking tongs through the enclosure while maintaining effective heat retention and noise reduction at the oven port.
mechanism: An enclosure with apertures allows continuous bidirectional movement of tools through a port while maintaining environmental isolation. The apertures are positioned to permit tool passage without compromising the enclosure's ability to retain heat and suppress noise. An additional outlet aperture enables product discharge while preserving the isolation properties of the enclosure.
mechanism_raw: The front port is enclosed by a housing with side passage openings that allow the baking tongs to pass through in a continuous circuit while maintaining an enclosed environment around the port. The housing isolates the front port from the baking chamber, reducing heat escape and noise emission. An outlet opening in the housing allows discharged wafers to exit while preserving the enclosure's thermal and acoustic isolation.
residual_terms: ["side passage openings", "enclosed environment", "thermal and acoustic isolation", "outlet opening"]

abstract: Dust is controlled on roads, in mines, on mineral and tailings piles, surfaces of pulverized coal and mineral piles contained within open transit cars such as coal cars or trucks, and other surfaces containing coal particles, rock dust, clay, soil particles and other finely divided particles subject to dusting by applying thereto a dust inhibiting amount of a liquid dispersion of watery consistency of highly branched water swellable polymer of acrylamide or an acrylamide-acrylic acid copolymer, branched and/or cross-linked with a multifunctional unsaturated monomer containing more than one ethylenically unsaturated group, said cross-linked polyer or copolymer having a three-dimensional structure and being in the form of microgelatinous particles having a particle size not exceeding approximately one micron in an oil containing emulsion form, and having the properties of swelling dramatically in water and binding dust particles upon adsorption from solution.
problem: Controlling dust on diverse surfaces (roads, mines, piles, transit cars) by applying a treatment that binds fine particulate matter without requiring complex application equipment or causing runoff issues.
constraint: Creating a stable, easily-applied liquid dispersion with sub-micron particles that can swell and bind dust upon application while remaining compatible with an oil emulsion carrier for broad surface adhesion.
mechanism: A liquid dispersion containing sub-micron swelling particles in an oil-based carrier is applied to surfaces. The particles absorb moisture and expand, creating a binding matrix that immobilizes particulate matter through adsorption. The oil carrier ensures broad surface adhesion while maintaining the dispersion's stability during application.
mechanism_raw: A liquid dispersion of watery consistency containing microgelatinous polymer particles (≤1 micron) in an oil-containing emulsion is applied to dusty surfaces. The highly branched, cross-linked polyacrylamide or acrylamide-acrylic acid copolymer particles swell dramatically upon contact with water/moisture and bind dust particles through adsorption from solution, effectively immobilizing them.

abstract: A pawl and ratchet assembly for use in socket drive wrenches or the like which includes a pair of arcuate pawls that encircle a ratchet gear means. A single control is provided for positioning the pawls so that either of the pawls can individually engage the ratchet gear means to provide clockwise and counterclockwise ratcheting, both of the pawls can engage the ratchet gear means to provide a lockup mode and so that both of the pawls can be disengaged from the ratchet gear means to permit a freewheeling mode. In one embodiment, the pawl control means is mounted on the handle of the socket drive wrench to enhance its accessibility in confined areas of use.
problem: Providing a ratcheting mechanism in a socket drive wrench that can selectively operate in clockwise ratcheting, counterclockwise ratcheting, lockup, or freewheeling modes through a single control, especially in confined spaces.
constraint: Achieving four distinct operational modes (two ratcheting directions, lockup, freewheeling) through a single control point while maintaining reliable pawl engagement and accessibility in tight workspaces.
mechanism: A pair of arcuate engagement elements encircles a rotating gear. A single control system selectively positions both elements to enable independent engagement for unidirectional motion, simultaneous engagement for a locked state, or full disengagement for free rotation. The control is positioned on an extended handle to facilitate operation in restricted spaces.
mechanism_raw: A pair of arcuate pawls encircle the ratchet gear. A single control mechanism positions both pawls so that either pawl can individually engage the gear for unidirectional ratcheting, both pawls can engage simultaneously for a locked state, or both pawls can be disengaged for freewheeling. The control is mounted on the wrench handle to enhance accessibility in confined areas.

abstract: A phenolic cation exchange resin with a chelating group has been prepared by reacting resorcinol with iminodiacetic acid in the presence of formaldehyde at a molar ratio of about 1:1:6. The material is highly selective for the simultaneous recovery of both cesium and strontium from aqueous alkaline solutions, such as, aqueous alkaline nuclear waste solutions. The organic resins are condensation polymers of resorcinol and formaldehyde with attached chelating groups. The column performance of the resins compares favorably with that of commercially available resins for either cesium or strontium removal. By combining Cs.sup.+ and Sr.sup.2+ removal in the same bed, the resins allow significant reduction of the size and complexity of facilities for processing nuclear waste.
problem: Efficiently recovering both cesium and strontium ions simultaneously from aqueous alkaline nuclear waste solutions without requiring separate processing steps.
constraint: Maintaining high selectivity and adsorption capacity for both ions in harsh alkaline conditions while ensuring the resin's structural integrity and compatibility with existing column processing systems.
mechanism: A functionalized polymer matrix incorporates multiple complementary binding sites that selectively capture distinct target ions through coordination chemistry, enabling simultaneous recovery of multiple species in a single processing stage under harsh chemical conditions.
mechanism_raw: A chelating group (iminodiacetic acid) is chemically attached to a phenolic cation exchange resin matrix, enabling the resin to selectively bind both Cs+ and Sr^2+ ions through complementary coordination chemistry, allowing simultaneous recovery in a single column.

abstract: A furnace producing a precisely controlled temperature gradient within a central bore by a plurality of heating elements sandwiched between respective insulating layers with each heating element loosely thermally coupled to a thermally conductive ring extending concentrically outward from the furnace bore. Thermal sensors at each layer provide data to data processing equipment which controls and moves temperature gradients within the furnace by program.
problem: Achieving precise spatial and temporal control of a temperature gradient within a central bore of a furnace for applications requiring uniform thermal processing.
constraint: Balancing thermal coupling between elements and rings to avoid cross-interference while maintaining rapid response and spatial resolution of the gradient.
mechanism: A plurality of thermal actuators are arranged in spatially separated zones, each coupled to a conductive element with controlled thermal resistance. Distributed temperature sensors provide feedback to a controller that independently modulates power to each actuator, enabling dynamic positioning and stabilization of a temperature profile within a target region.
mechanism_raw: Multiple heating elements are arranged in concentric insulating layers, each loosely thermally coupled to a conductive ring. Thermal sensors at each layer feed data to a processor that dynamically adjusts power to individual elements, enabling controlled movement and stabilization of the temperature gradient.

abstract: This disclosure relates to an insulating system which is particularly adapted for insulating the walls, floors, ceilings and like structure of buildings and includes a panel having a hollow chamber or interior under negative pressure (vacuum) and being of a variety of external peripheral sizes and shapes to fit within areas defined by wall and/or floor and/or ceiling studs, beams, or the like, a plurality of springs, chains or the like for supporting the panel in generally spaced relationship to an associated building wall, ceiling, floor or like structure, and a plurality of pin-like elements of relatively small cross-sectional configuration normally spaced from the exterior surface of the panel for contacting a limited exterior surface area of the panel only upon the springs, chains or the like becoming inoperative which would in the absence of the pin-like elements result in direct contact between the panel and the associated building wall, ceiling, floor or like structure and thus reduce the insulating efficiency thereof.
problem: Providing effective thermal insulation for building structures while preventing direct contact between the insulating panel and the structure, which would degrade vacuum insulation performance.
constraint: Ensuring the suspension system maintains sufficient spacing under varying environmental loads while the pin-like elements remain inactive until failure occurs.
mechanism: A vacuum-insulated panel is maintained in spaced relation to a supporting structure by a compliant suspension system. Backup contact-prevention elements are positioned to engage only upon failure of the primary suspension, preserving insulation performance by preventing direct conductive contact during normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A vacuum-insulated panel is suspended via springs or chains to maintain spacing from the structure. Pin-like elements are positioned to engage only if the suspension system fails, preventing direct contact and preserving insulation efficiency during normal operation.

abstract: The invention is concerned with a construction of a rod holder fixing means comprising a rod holder and a cylinder detachably pivoted thereon, wherein a spacer is suspended on a side of the cylinder, and adapted to be adjustably pressed against the inside of a rod hole by screwably moving a bolt through the cylinder so that the means is slidably insertible into any rod hole regardless of the diameter, position and inclination thereof with respect to the gunnel surface of a fishing boat and fixedly mountable on or above the gunnel regardless of the width and shape thereof.
problem: Creating a universal rod holder mounting system that can adapt to varying hole diameters, positions, and inclinations on a fishing boat gunnel without requiring custom fitting.
constraint: Achieving sufficient clamping force through the screw mechanism while maintaining compatibility with diverse hole geometries and gunnel shapes.
mechanism: A self-adjusting mounting assembly uses a movable spacer element pressed against an interior surface by an adjustable force-applying member. The assembly accommodates geometric variation in the receiving aperture through compliant positioning, enabling secure attachment regardless of aperture size, position, or orientation.
mechanism_raw: A spacer is suspended on one side of a cylinder and pressed against the interior of a rod hole via a screwable bolt. This allows the assembly to self-adjust to the hole's geometry when inserted, enabling secure mounting regardless of the hole's size or orientation.

abstract: A venetian blind mechanism having a lead and a plurality of auxiliary carriers supported for traversing movement along a header between a retracted and an extended position and vane supports mounted on the auxiliary carriers for turning about an upright axis for light control. An operating chain is connected intermediate its ends to the lead carrier and has first and second chain portions extending lengthwise of the header in meshing engagement with sprockets on the auxiliary carriers to control spacing between the auxiliary carriers. Chain operating means is associated with the ends of the first and second chain portions for moving them in relatively opposite directions to effect rotation of the vane supports. A chain locking device is provided for automatically locking the chain to the sprocket on an auxiliary carrier when the carriers are retracted, to restrain movement of the operating chain by the chain operating means.
problem: Coordinating the movement of multiple vane supports in a venetian blind to achieve precise light control while enabling automatic locking when the system is retracted.
constraint: Maintaining synchronized spacing between carriers during traversal while ensuring reliable locking engagement without interfering with normal operation.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system transmits coordinated motion from a primary carrier to multiple secondary carriers through a continuous flexible drive element routed around rotatable sprockets. The drive element's opposing motion segments induce synchronized rotation of vane supports, while a selective engagement mechanism locks the sprockets during retraction to prevent unintended movement.
mechanism_raw: An operating chain is connected to a lead carrier and routed through sprockets on auxiliary carriers. Opposite-direction movement of chain portions rotates the vane supports, while a locking device engages the sprockets during retraction to prevent unintended chain movement.

abstract: A timekeeping signal source for an electronic timepiece produces a highly accurate timekeeping signal which is stable in frequency with respect to both temperature variations and long-term drift. The timekeeping signal is produced by phase lock control using a high frequency reference signal from a crystal-controlled high-frequency oscillator. Phase lock control can be performed continuously or on an intermittent basis, in order to reduce power consumption. In addition, the timekeeping rate can be adjusted with a resolution within one period of the high frequency reference signal, by variation of a numeric value stored in digital memory means.
problem: Producing a highly accurate and stable timekeeping signal that resists temperature variations and long-term drift, while also allowing fine adjustment and minimizing power consumption.
constraint: Balancing accuracy and stability against power consumption — intermittent phase lock control trades continuous correction for power savings while maintaining long-term stability through the high-frequency reference.
mechanism: A feedback control system compares a periodic output signal against a high-frequency reference signal to maintain synchronization, with intermittent correction cycles to reduce power consumption, and a digitally stored value is adjusted to fine-tune the output period with sub-cycle resolution.
mechanism_raw: Phase lock control of the timekeeping signal using a high-frequency reference signal from a crystal oscillator, with intermittent phase lock operation to reduce power consumption, and digital memory-based fine adjustment of the timekeeping rate achieving sub-period resolution by varying a stored numeric value.

abstract: A process for desensitizing sensitive explosives materials such as RDX or HMX involves stirring a paste of the explosives material in a liquid medium, usually water, with a wax which will soften below the safe decomposition temperature of the explosives material, heating the mixture to drive off the liquid and soften the wax which is then coated onto the explosives material as the liquid evaporates. On cooling, explosive material particles substantially entirely encapsulated in wax are obtained. When warm or after cooling, aluminum powder can be mixed with the desensitized material. As little as 1% of added wax can improve the F of I of RDX from 73 to around 100 and the wax coating is quite stable even when the explosive is pressed, e.g. when making charges.
problem: Sensitive explosives materials (RDX, HMX) have low friction/impact resistance and need to be desensitized for safer handling while maintaining their explosive properties.
constraint: The wax must soften at a temperature below the decomposition temperature of the explosive material, limiting the processing temperature range and requiring careful selection of the softening agent.
mechanism: A coating process encapsulates particles by mixing them with a temperature-sensitive material in a liquid medium, heating to evaporate the liquid and soften the material so it flows around the particles, then cooling to solidify the material into a protective shell.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulation of explosive particles using a wax that softens below the safe decomposition temperature of the explosive: the wax is stirred into a paste with the explosive in a liquid medium, heated to evaporate the liquid and soften the wax, allowing the softened wax to coat the explosive particles as the liquid evaporates, then cooling to solidify the wax encapsulation.

abstract: The vapor generator is constructed with an evaporator of vertical tubes about the combustion chamber and a final evaporator which is disposed between the economizer and at least one superheater within the flue of the generator. The first superheater tubes are vertically disposed and are welded to the tubes of the evaporator in a seamless manner and connect with the vapor outlet of the water separator.
reason: This patent describes the physical arrangement and structural features of tubes and components in a vapor generator (vertical tube placement, seamless welding between evaporator and superheater, positioning relative to economizer). It is a static architectural description of construction details rather than a causal functional mechanism that produces a useful effect through a transferable principle.

abstract: A timer apparatus is provided such that an operation of switches for setting a timer working hour makes it possible to memorize the timer working hour in a timer circuit and also to display this timer working hour in a digital time display device, and, to obtain an output when this timer working hour arrives. In this timer apparatus, the switches for setting a timer working hour are composed of twelve switches disposed at a positional relation corresponding to 1 o'clock to 12 o'clock on the dial plate of a clock.
reason: This patent describes a timer apparatus with switches arranged at clock-face positions (1-12 o'clock) for setting a timer working hour. The underlying concept of setting a time and producing an output when it arrives is generic, and the specific arrangement of switches is a user interface design choice rather than a causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A material for steel wool is disclosed which essentially consists of 0.05 to 0.20% of C, up to 0.10% of Si, 0.50 to 1.30% of Mn, 0.035 to 0.10% of P, up to 0.04% of S,0.05 to 0.15% of N and the balance Fe. In this material, Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 inclusions with sizes not smaller than 3 microns are suppressed to a level not greater than 20 ppm and when the content of the Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 inclusions (3 microns and over) is in the range of 5 to 20 ppm, Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 inclusions with a size ranging from 3 to 10 microns is contained in an amount not smaller than 30% of the total content of Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 inclusions with sizes not smaller than 3 microns.
reason: This patent specifies a chemical composition for steel wool with particular ranges of C, Si, Mn, P, S, N, and Fe, along with requirements for Al2O3 inclusion size and concentration. It is a materials specification listing composition ranges and desired outcomes without explaining the causal mechanism by which the composition achieves the inclusion characteristics. No underlying causal operation is described.

abstract: A method for continuous saccharification of plant raw material by feeding the raw material as such or prehydrolyzed and a dilute sulphuric acid solution into a flow reactor in order to hydrolyze the raw material under pressure and at a high temperature, discharging dry solids and liquid from the reactor by expansion and separating liquid and solids, wherein the raw material and sulfuric acid solution are led through the reactor at equal rate, which is the same as required by the more easily hydrolyzable particles of the raw material, the solids and liquid together are discharged into the same blow tank and at least part of the separated coarse solid is returned into the reactor.
problem: Efficiently hydrolyzing plant raw material under high pressure and temperature while maintaining throughput and minimizing unreacted residue.
constraint: Balancing flow rates to avoid overloading the reactor while maintaining sufficient residence time for hydrolysis, and managing energy costs from recycling unreacted solids.
mechanism: Adjusting input rates of raw material and reactive agent to match processing demands of the most resistant components, combined with recycling unprocessed solids back into the system to ensure complete conversion of residual material.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the feed rate of raw material and acid to match the hydrolysis requirements of the most recalcitrant particles, combined with recycling coarse solids back into the reactor to ensure complete processing of residual material.

abstract: Pulverized coal is converted by means of a gaseous mixture and partial oxidation into synthesis gas which is subsequently utilized as a feedstock for the production of hydrocarbons. A gaseous mixture containing non-converted synthesis gas and low boiling hydrocarbons is separated from the higher boiling hydrocarbons and recycled to the coal conversion step.
problem: Optimizing the conversion of pulverized coal into hydrocarbons by maximizing the utilization of synthesis gas and minimizing waste of unreacted intermediates.
constraint: Achieving efficient separation of components with different boiling points while maintaining stable reaction conditions during recycling.
mechanism: Separating non-converted gaseous intermediates and low-boiling products from higher-boiling outputs, then recycling the separated gases back to the conversion step to drive further reactions.
mechanism_raw: Separating non-converted synthesis gas and low-boiling hydrocarbons from higher-boiling products, then recycling the separated gases back to the coal conversion step to drive further reactions.

abstract: A shirt collar is described which eliminates the need for stays, but yet lies flat and maintains a crisp and neat appearance with time. The disclosed collar includes a flexible lining material characterized in that it is relatively stiff in the transverse direction of the collar and relatively flexible in the longitudinal direction.
problem: Maintaining a crisp, flat collar shape over time without rigid stays while allowing flexibility for wear and movement.
constraint: Balancing transverse stiffness and longitudinal flexibility to ensure durability and comfort without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Using a flexible material with directional stiffness properties—relatively rigid in one axis to resist deformation and maintain shape, and compliant in another axis to allow bending and movement.
mechanism_raw: Using a flexible lining material with anisotropic stiffness—relatively stiff in the transverse direction to resist deformation and maintain shape, and flexible in the longitudinal direction to allow bending and movement.

abstract: Novel radiation-curable, liquid vinyl organosilicon polymers and coating compositions which are free of volatile solvent(s) and which are adapted to be applied to a substrate and cured rapidly by exposure to radiation to form release coatings having good release properties with respect to adhesives, and methods for producing such polymers and compositions and for applying and curing such release coatings. The vinyl polysiloxane may be prepared from dimethyl dichlorosilane, vinyl methyl dichlorosilane, and tetrachlorosilane or trichloromethylsilane. It may be mixed with a polymethyl hydrogen polysiloxane and a photosensitizer and cured by ultraviolet or electron beam radiation.
problem: Creating a fast-curing, solvent-free release coating with consistent adhesive-release properties for industrial applications.
constraint: Ensuring the polymer composition allows for rapid curing without compromising the release properties or requiring toxic solvents.
mechanism: Formulating a polymer composition that undergoes rapid crosslinking when exposed to radiation, eliminating volatile solvents while achieving consistent release characteristics through controlled curing.
mechanism_raw: Formulating a vinyl organosilicon polymer composition that undergoes rapid crosslinking when exposed to radiation (UV or electron beam), eliminating the need for volatile solvents while achieving desired release characteristics.

abstract: This invention is a small light weight underwater transducer that operates at low frequencies. The foregoing is accomplished by embedding piezoelectric material in the wall of an oval shell between the shell's nodal points. When an alternating voltage is applied to the piezoelectric material, the piezoelectric material expands and contracts causing large circumferential strains in the shell of the transducer. The aforementioned strains cause the shell to vibrate and energy to be radiated into the water. This invention may also be used as a receiving type of transducer.
problem: Generating efficient low-frequency underwater acoustic energy radiation or reception in a lightweight, compact transducer.
constraint: Positioning piezoelectric elements at nodal points to maximize strain amplification while minimizing added mass and maintaining structural integrity of the shell.
mechanism: Positioning energy-conversion elements at points of maximum strain amplification within a deformable structure to convert electrical energy into mechanical vibrations that radiate efficiently into a surrounding medium.
mechanism_raw: Embedding piezoelectric material at nodal points of an oval shell to amplify circumferential strain during expansion/contraction, converting electrical energy into mechanical vibrations that radiate efficiently into water.

abstract: A method and apparatus for separating cells according to differences in sedimentation velocity comprises a vessel preferably constructed from a cylindrical body of ring formation, the height of which is substantially less than its diameter, and from top and bottom plates sealingly and removably attached to the ring. The vessel is preferably mounted on a tiltable platform for controlled movement between tilted and horizontal positions and has a small horizontal cross-sectional area in the tilted position relative to such area in the horizontal position. The vessel is provided with two ports; a lower port communicating with a lowermost level of the vessel while in the tilted position and an upper port communicating with the uppermost level in the tilted position. Flow distributing structure is provided preferably between each port and the interior of the vessel whereby the force of liquid flowing into the vessel through a port is dissipated. A gradient liquid and a cell suspension are loaded into the vessel while it is in a tilted position. Thereafter, the vessel is rotated to the horizontal position for cell separation. After separation, the vessel is reoriented to the tilted position, and the gradient liquid containing separated cells is collected as various fractions.
problem: Separating cells based on differences in sedimentation velocity while minimizing cross-contamination and maximizing fraction purity.
constraint: Balancing tilt angle and vessel geometry to optimize sedimentation velocity differences without causing shear-induced cell damage or mixing of fractions.
mechanism: Dynamic reorientation of a containment vessel between inclined and level attitudes modulates the effective settling cross-section, producing staged gravitational separation of particulate populations by differential settling rate. The inclined attitude suppresses convective disturbance during introduction, while the level attitude promotes laminar stratification. Collection apertures positioned at extreme elevations in the inclined orientation enable selective extraction of separated fractions.
mechanism_raw: Controlled reorientation of a vessel between tilted and horizontal positions dynamically alters the effective cross-sectional area for sedimentation, enabling staged separation of cell populations by velocity. The tilt position reduces flow turbulence during loading, while the horizontal position allows gravity-driven stratification. Ports at extreme levels in the tilted orientation facilitate selective collection of separated fractions.
residual_terms: ["sedimentation velocity", "tilt angle", "vessel geometry", "shear-induced cell damage", "cross-sectional area", "gravity-driven stratification", "selective collection"]

abstract: A motor controller for a three phase AC motor (10) which is adapted to operate bidirectionally from signals received either from a computer (30) or a manual control (32). The controller is comprised of digital logic circuit means which implement a forward and reverse command signal channel (27, 29) for the application of power through the forward and reverse power switching relays (16, 18, 20, 22). The digital logic elements are cross coupled to prevent activation of both channels simultaneously and each includes a plugging circuit (65, 67) for stopping the motor upon the removal of control signal applied to one of the two channels (27, 29) for a direction of rotation desired. Each plugging circuit (65, 67) includes a one-shot pulse signal generator (88, 102) which outputs a single pulse signal of predetermined pulsewidth which is adapted to inhibit further operation of the application of power in the channel which is being activated and to apply a reversal command signal to the other channel which provides a reversed phase application of power to the motor for a period defined by the pulse-width output of the one-shot signal generator to plug the motor (10) which will then be inoperative until another rotational command signal is applied to either of the two channels.
problem: Safely stopping a bidirectional motor and preventing conflicting power signals when switching directions or removing control input.
constraint: Pulse width must be precisely calibrated to fully decelerate the motor without overdriving the reversal phase, while maintaining fail-safe inhibition of further power application until a new command is received.
mechanism: Directional pulse generation in each drive channel produces a transient opposing signal upon command removal, inducing regenerative braking through controlled phase reversal. Interlocked logic enforces mutual exclusion between opposing drive states, while pulse duration governs the braking interval before system lockout.
mechanism_raw: A one-shot pulse generator in each direction channel creates a temporary reversal command to the opposing channel upon signal removal, mechanically braking the motor via phase reversal. Cross-coupled logic ensures mutual exclusion of forward/reverse activation, while the pulse width defines the duration of the braking action before lockout.
residual_terms: ["bidirectional motor", "phase reversal", "mutual exclusion", "pulse width", "braking action", "lockout", "fail-safe inhibition"]

abstract: Apparatus for conveying cigarettes by means of one or more fluted drums has a frame including spaced front and back walls defining between them a suction manifold; a fluted drum in front of the frame; a tubular drum-carrying member which extends through an opening in the front wall of the frame, engages and seals in or around an aperture in the rear wall of the frame, and has a flange by which it is secured to the front wall of the frame, the drum being rotatable around the tubular member; and a drive shaft which extends axially through the tubular member, is secured to the front end of the drum, is supported by bearings carried by the tubular member, and carries at its rear end behind the rear wall of the frame a gear or other means by which it is driven; suction being transmitted to ports in the flutes of the drum from the manifold via a passage contained within the thickness of the wall of the tubular member in the region where it extends through the front wall of the frame.
problem: Transmitting suction to rotating fluted drums in a cigarette conveyor while maintaining structural integrity and minimizing maintenance.
constraint: Maintaining a vacuum-tight seal between the rotating tubular member and stationary frame walls under continuous mechanical stress and thermal expansion.
mechanism: An integrated tubular structural element provides a continuous internal flow path for vacuum transmission to a rotating perforated surface, eliminating discrete flexible couplings. The element traverses a stationary boundary with a compliant sealing interface, preserving pressure integrity during rotation. Internal apertures in the rotating surface connect to the flow path through the wall of the tubular element.
mechanism_raw: A tubular drum-carrying member integrates a sealed internal passage for suction delivery, eliminating external hoses or rotary joints. The member extends through the frame walls with a flange seal, allowing rotation while maintaining vacuum integrity. Suction ports in the drum flutes connect to the internal passage via the tubular member's wall thickness.
residual_terms: ["vacuum-tight seal", "rotating tubular member", "stationary frame walls", "continuous mechanical stress", "thermal expansion", "fluted drums", "suction ports", "flange seal"]

abstract: The fastness properties of basic dyeings on cellulosic substrates are improved by treating the substrate with a fixing agent comprising a precondensate or mixture of PA1 (A) the reaction product of an amine with cyanamide, dicyandiamide, guanidine or biguanidine, or, PA1 (B) a quaternary polyalkylene polyamine with PA1 (C) formaldehyde and/or, PA1 (D) an N-methylol compound optionally together with PA1 (E) a catalyst, e.g. MgCl.sub.2. The fixing agents are normally applied as an aftertreatment, with a subsequent heat-curing step.
problem: Improving the fastness of basic dyes on cellulosic substrates without compromising fabric hand or requiring excessive chemical usage.
constraint: Optimizing the molar ratio of amine to crosslinking agents to achieve maximum dye retention without excessive fabric stiffening or thermal degradation during curing.
mechanism: A pre-reacted amine-crosslinker matrix forms a chemically active network that covalently binds chromophore molecules to cellulosic fibers. Subsequent thermal curing activates formaldehyde-based crosslinking agents, creating an insoluble polymeric structure that immobilizes dye within the fiber matrix.
mechanism_raw: A precondensate formed by reacting amines with cyanamide/dicyandiamide/guanidine/biguanidine creates a reactive matrix that chemically bonds dye molecules to cellulose fibers. Formaldehyde and N-methylol compounds crosslink the matrix during heat curing, forming a durable, insoluble network that traps dye within the fiber structure.
residual_terms: ["basic dyes", "cellulosic substrates", "amine to crosslinking agent molar ratio", "formaldehyde", "N-methylol compounds", "heat curing", "thermal degradation", "fabric hand", "dye retention", "fabric stiffening"]

abstract: A process of producing a tufted pile fabric comprises providing a primary backing which may be woven, non-woven or knitted fabric and containing for example polypropylene, polyester, polyamide, jute or viscose rayon, applying a meltable fibrous layer to both sides of the primary backing, preferably by needling fibres into the backing, inserting pile tufts into the primary backing so that parts of the pile tufts extend through backing and the meltable fibrous layers and melting the fibrous layer which is on the side of the backing opposite the pile forming surface of the tufts to secure the tufts to the backing and provide an anchor coat for the fabric. The meltable fibre may be polyamide fibre with a melting point in the range 80.degree.-150.degree. C. and may conveniently be Grilon K115 (Grilon is a Registered Trade Mark). The process may be used to provide mother and daughter tufted pile fabrics by applying a second primary backing with meltable fibrous layers applied thereto to the pile forming surface of the first fabric and melting the fibrous layers of the second primary backing to adhere the latter to the pile forming surface of the tufts, and thereafter slitting the tufts intermediate the two primary backings.
problem: Securing pile tufts to a backing in tufted fabric while enabling selective slitting to produce mother/daughter fabric configurations.
constraint: Matching the melting point of the fibrous layer to the thermal tolerance of the primary backing and pile material to avoid unintended deformation during the melting step.
mechanism: A selectively meltable fibrous interlayer applied to opposing surfaces of a primary substrate temporarily anchors projecting fiber elements. Thermal activation of the non-projecting side fixes the fiber elements via localized fusion, while the projecting side remains dimensionally stable. An additional substrate with a complementary meltable layer may be joined and fused to form a composite structure prior to division.
mechanism_raw: A meltable fibrous layer applied to both sides of a primary backing acts as a temporary anchor. Selective melting of the non-pile-side layer fixes tufts in place via thermal bonding, while the pile-side layer remains intact. A second backing with its own meltable layer can be added and melted to create a dual-layer structure before slitting.
residual_terms: ["pile tufts", "backing", "meltable fibrous layer", "primary backing", "thermal bonding", "melting point", "thermal tolerance", "pile-side layer", "non-pile-side layer", "slitting", "mother/daughter fabric"]

abstract: A method for thermal treatment, especially drying, of finely particulated bulk material comprises the steps of stirring the material in a reactor by means of a rotating stirrer while simultaneously discharging a heated gas under pressure through openings in a hollow arm of the stirrer so as to form in the reactor a whirling fluidized bed from the material, and introducing the necessary amount of heat for the thermal treatment of the material at least in part through a heat exchanger extending into the whirling fluidized bed. The apparatus for carrying out the method mainly comprises an arrangement for feeding the material through an inlet into a reactor forming a whirling chamber in which a rotating stirring device is arranged having at least one hollow stirring arm provided with openings through which a preferably heated gas under pressure is discharged into the material so as to form a whirling fluidized bed in the reactor, a heat exchanger extending through the fluidized bed, and an outlet for discharging the gas and treated material from the reactor. The reactor may also include an arrangement extending into the whirling fluidized bed for retarding flow of the material from the inlet to the outlet of the reactor, which arrangement may be constituted by a heat exchanger of lamellar construction so that the material will pass in cascades through the reactor.
problem: Efficiently transferring heat to and drying finely particulated bulk material without clogging or uneven thermal treatment.
constraint: Balancing gas pressure, stirrer rotation speed, and heat exchanger geometry to sustain a stable fluidized bed without disrupting material flow or causing localized overheating.
mechanism: A mechanical agitator with hollow elements discharges pressurized gas to create a dynamically suspended particle bed, while a heat transfer element positioned within the bed directly exchanges thermal energy with the suspended particles. Coordinated gas pressure, rotational speed, and geometric arrangement maintain stable suspension and maximize thermal contact surface area.
mechanism_raw: A rotating stirrer with hollow arms discharges heated gas under pressure to create a whirling fluidized bed, while a heat exchanger extends into the bed to directly transfer heat to the suspended particles. The mechanical agitation and gas flow synergistically maintain particle suspension and maximize heat exchange surface area.

abstract: An apparatus for applying a coating of an atomizable material, such as a phosphor slurry, to the inside surface of a glass tube comprises a rotatable member having a surface for receiving material, a device for rotating the member and conduct for delivering material to the surface of the member. The rotating and delivery mechanisms are preferably situated along the same direction as the extension of the axis of rotation through the surface of the member. The apparatus may include a device for electrically charging the material prior to coating. A method for applying the coating of atomizable material to the inside surface of a glass tube comprises positioning a rotatable member within the tube, delivering the material to a surface of the member adapted to receive the material, and rotating the member at a predetermined velocity to atomize the material and inpact the surface of the tube with at least a portion of the atomized material. A potential differnce may be established between the atomized material and the surface of the tube to improve coating efficiency. The surface of the tube may be maintained at an electrical potential, and multiple coatings may be produced.
problem: Applying a uniform coating to the interior surface of a narrow, elongated tube (e.g., glass tubing) without manual intervention or overspray.
constraint: Controlling rotational velocity and electrical potential to achieve atomization and adhesion without excessive material waste or uneven thickness.
mechanism: A rotating internal member atomizes coating material via centrifugal force, propelling droplets onto a surrounding surface. Electrical charging of the material enhances adhesion and distribution, while coaxial alignment of rotation and delivery ensures consistent material flow and uniform coverage.
mechanism_raw: A rotating member within the tube atomizes coating material via centrifugal force, propelling droplets onto the tube wall. Electrical charging of the material enhances adhesion and distribution, while coaxial alignment of rotation and delivery ensures consistent material flow.

abstract: A linkage for actuating a pair of suction cups that are located adjacent the other end of the guide rails and that can fold an upwardly inclined blank on the guide rails; the suctions cups being adapted to hold by suction two adjacent side panels of the blank, that are contiguous to the lower guide rail and on vertically opposite sides of the blank, and to rotate in opposite directions about the lower guide rail until the suction cups are 90.degree. apart, so that the two adjacent side panels are folded 90.degree. apart about the lower guide rail and thereby the blank is folded into a rectangular tube.
problem: Folding a flat blank into a precise rectangular tube shape with minimal manual adjustment or complex tooling.
constraint: Synchronizing the rotational motion of the suction cups to maintain precise angular alignment and avoid misalignment during folding.
mechanism: Two opposing elements, positioned on opposite sides of a guide, rotate in coordinated directions to fold adjacent panels at a fixed angular relationship. The synchronized rotational motion ensures precise alignment and formation of a rectangular cross-section as the elements move into position.
mechanism_raw: Two suction cups, positioned on opposite sides of a guide rail, rotate in opposing directions to fold adjacent panels 90 degrees relative to each other. The coordinated rotation ensures the blank folds into a rectangular cross-section as the cups move into alignment.

abstract: A retainer for attaching a rotating band to a projectile during handling ramming of the projectile. The retainer cooperates with a groove on the projectile and is discarded during firing of the projectile by the force of the charge. An interlocking double split ring forms the retainer with an outer ring having an L-shaped cross-section and an inner ring shaped to fit into the L-shape of the outer ring. Each ring is provided with a split or opening to allow for expansion of the ring over the projectile and into the projectile groove. The outer ring split may be cut at an angle of less than 90.degree. to minimize deflection of the outer ring. The inner and outer rings are assembled with their splits together and then clocked 180.degree. apart. The inner ring is then locked to the outer ring by a locking notch. Hoop stress of the outer ring prevents the inner ring from deflecting at the split such that the retainer is forced to behave as a continuous single ring.
problem: Temporarily securing a rotating band to a projectile during handling and ramming, while ensuring automatic release during firing.
constraint: Designing the split geometry and material properties so the retainer remains intact under handling stresses but fails predictably under firing acceleration.
mechanism: An interlocking dual-component retainer uses radial compression stress in an outer element to clamp an inner element, preventing deflection at a split interface. The assembly behaves as a continuous structure until external forces exceed the compression threshold, causing the retainer to fail and detach.
mechanism_raw: An interlocking double split ring uses hoop stress in the outer ring to clamp the inner ring, preventing deflection at the split. The assembly behaves as a continuous ring until firing forces overcome the hoop stress, causing the retainer to fail and detach.

abstract: A process for artificially coloring fruit wherein an aqueous medium containing the fruit is treated with a dye and an edible calcium salt at an elevated temperature until the desired quantity of dye penetrates the fruit tissue, then the pH is lowered at least to a value at which the dye becomes substantially insoluble, after which the pH is raised gradually while ensuring that the pH of the inner parts of the fruit does not exceed 7, and finally the fruit is separated from the aqueous medium.
problem: Achieving uniform dye penetration into fruit tissue while preventing over-penetration or chemical residue in the fruit's interior.
constraint: Controlling pH and temperature profiles to balance dye solubility, penetration depth, and fruit safety without exceeding a pH of 7 in the fruit's core.
mechanism: Elevated temperature and chemical additives accelerate molecular diffusion of a dye into a substrate. Subsequent pH adjustment precipitates the dye to lock it in place, while controlled chemical profiles ensure safety thresholds are maintained. Physical separation from the treatment medium finalizes the process.
mechanism_raw: Elevated temperature and calcium salt accelerate dye diffusion into the fruit. Lowering pH precipitates the dye, locking it in place, while gradual pH adjustment ensures the fruit's internal pH remains safe. Separation from the medium finalizes the process.

abstract: A brush (10) is provided. The brush (10) includes a housing (12) which includes an aperture (28). Bristles (42) are mounted within the housing (12) and extend through the aperture (28). A cover (50) is provided and includes an aperture (52). Cover (50) is slidably mounted to the housing (12) and housing (12) is selectively rotatable within the cover (50). Housing (12) is rotatable to a first position exposing bristles (42) through the aperture (52) of the cover (50) for use of the brush (10). Housing (12) is rotatable to a second position for covering the aperture (28) and the bristles (42) when the brush (10) is not in use.
problem: Protecting bristles of a brush during non-use while enabling easy access for use.
constraint: The mechanism must enable single-motion switching between exposed and covered states without requiring disassembly or complex actuation.
mechanism: Relative rotational movement between a housing and a slidable cover selectively aligns or misaligns their respective openings, enabling single-motion switching between exposed and enclosed states without disassembly.
mechanism_raw: Rotational movement of a housing relative to a slidable cover allows bristles to be selectively exposed or fully enclosed by aligning or misaligning their respective apertures.

abstract: A material feed control mechanism for a wood or brush chipper having an upright stop gate vertically movable to a material obstructing position extended transversely across and within the feed housing, and forwardly of the cutter to a material non-obstructing position projected upwardly from the housing. A latch assembly for releasably holding the stop gate in the material non-obstructing position associated with a release mechanism actuated by a lever system operable independently by any one of a plurality of handles one of which is arranged forwardly of the feed housing and a pair of which are located at opposite sides of the feed housing, to permit the fall of the gate to the material obstructing position therefor.
problem: Controlling material feed into a chipper safely and allowing independent operator intervention from multiple positions.
constraint: The release mechanism must be operable independently from multiple locations to ensure accessibility and safety without compromising the gate's default obstructing position.
mechanism: A movable gate is releasably held in a non-obstructing position, with a lever system enabling release from any of multiple remote actuation points while maintaining the gate's default obstructing state.
mechanism_raw: A vertically movable stop gate is releasably latched in a non-obstructing position, with a lever system enabling release from any of multiple handles positioned around the feed housing.
residual_terms: ["movable gate", "releasably latched", "lever system", "multiple actuation points", "default obstructing position"]

abstract: This relates to a plastic material closure which is provided with deformable sealing flaps and cooperating abutments wherein when the closure is drawn down onto a container, the flaps will deform in accordance with the cross section of the sealing surface area of the container including down inside of the mouth of the container and down alongside the exterior surface of the neck finish to provide effective sealing contact with the container sealing area. Separate seals between the flaps and the container neck finish permit the same closure to be used to form gas-tight seals both with respect to high internal pressures and vacuum packs. The seals are liquid-tight and the closure may be used for reclosing the container against liquid loss.
problem: Achieving a reliable gas-tight and liquid-tight seal on containers with varying neck geometries using a single closure design.
constraint: The flaps must deform sufficiently to accommodate diverse geometries while maintaining seal integrity under both high internal pressure and vacuum conditions.
mechanism: Deformable sealing elements conform to a container's sealing surface when compressed, creating adaptive contact both within the opening and along the exterior surface to maintain seal integrity under varying pressure conditions.
mechanism_raw: Deformable sealing flaps conform to the container's sealing surface when compressed, creating adaptive contact both inside the mouth and alongside the exterior neck finish.
residual_terms: ["deformable sealing flaps", "sealing surface", "adaptive contact", "high internal pressure", "vacuum conditions"]

abstract: Aluminum salts of aromatic sulfonic acid formaldehyde condensates are useful cement additives and leather retanning agents. These salts prepared by reaction of freshly precipitated aluminum hydroxide with aromatic sulfonic acid formaldehyde condensate are of higher purity than aluminum salts obtained by prior art processes.
problem: Producing aluminum salts of aromatic sulfonic acid formaldehyde condensates with higher purity than prior art methods.
constraint: The reaction must be timed to coincide with the precipitation of aluminum hydroxide to maximize purity, requiring precise control over reactant freshness and mixing conditions.
mechanism: Reacting a freshly precipitated intermediate with a condensate ensures minimal contamination and higher purity compared to using pre-formed or aged reactants, with timing coordinated to coincide with precipitation.
mechanism_raw: Reacting freshly precipitated aluminum hydroxide with the condensate ensures minimal contamination and higher purity compared to using pre-formed or aged aluminum sources.
residual_terms: ["freshly precipitated", "aluminum hydroxide", "condensate", "pre-formed or aged aluminum sources", "precipitation timing"]

abstract: A seismic testing apparatus is provided in which linear motion or excitation of a horizontally disposed table is achieved simultaneously along three mutually orthogonal axes by means of independently operable hydraulic-actuator assemblies. Rotational or torsional motion of the table about the linear excitation axes is resisted by separate, mechanical rotation-inhibiting means each consisting of a torsionally rigid structure disposed parallel to the table and perpendicularly to their respective associated axes of excitation. The torsionally rigid structures are each connected to the table at two spaced-apart points, with all four points of connection lying in the same plane.
problem: Achieving precise linear motion along three orthogonal axes while resisting unwanted rotational or torsional movement of the table.
constraint: The torsional resistance structures must be rigid enough to prevent rotation without interfering with the linear motion, requiring all connection points to lie in the same plane for stability.
mechanism: Independent actuators provide linear excitation along each axis, while torsionally rigid structures connected at four coplanar points mechanically inhibit rotational motion about those axes without interfering with linear movement.
mechanism_raw: Independent hydraulic actuators provide linear excitation along each axis, while torsionally rigid structures connected at four coplanar points mechanically inhibit rotational motion about those axes.
residual_terms: ["hydraulic actuators", "linear excitation", "torsionally rigid structures", "four coplanar points", "rotational motion"]

abstract: An action play toy which includes a housing having a plurality of apertures therein and a plurality of action elements and three dimensional elements which are detachably received in the apertures.
