A gear assembly in the housing interconnects the action elements for simultaneous rotation and a bell assembly in the housing produces interesting sound in response to rotation of the gear assembly. The toy is adapted for assembly by a child with action and three dimensional elements of a variety of configurations, as desired.
problem: Creating an engaging, customizable toy that produces synchronized visual and auditory feedback through user-assembled components.
constraint: Balancing the variety of detachable element configurations with the need for a unified mechanical linkage that ensures synchronized motion and sound generation.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage interconnects detachable elements, causing simultaneous movement of all elements when any one is moved. This movement drives a sound-producing element, linking physical interaction to sensory feedback.
mechanism_raw: A gear assembly mechanically interconnects detachable action elements, causing simultaneous rotation of all elements when any one is moved. This rotation drives a bell assembly to produce sound, linking physical interaction to sensory feedback.

abstract: A fixing means for attachment to a base (1), e.g. to a level concrete roof, of a thermal lagging (3), e.g. a mineral wool mat, said fixing means consisting of a screw (2) or other nail binding to the base and a washer (4) located on top of the lagging, this washer carrying a tubular recess (5) partly penetrating into the lagging (3) and the bottom (6) of which is pierced by the screw and within which the head of the screw (2) resides. To the end of the tubular recess (5) has been connected by stays (7) a plug (8) fitting into a hole drilled in the base (1) and into which the screw (2) can be screwed.
problem: Securing thermal insulation to a base surface (e.g., concrete roof) while maintaining insulation integrity and allowing screw tightening.
constraint: Ensuring the washer and plug assembly provides sufficient holding force without compressing or damaging the insulation material during installation.
mechanism: A two-part anchoring system secures an insulation layer to a base surface. One component partially penetrates the insulation to house a fastener head, while a second component engages a pre-formed opening in the base to lock the insulation in place, enabling adjustment without compromising integrity.
mechanism_raw: A washer with a tubular recess partially penetrates the insulation, housing the screw head. A plug connected via stays fits into a pre-drilled hole in the base, creating a two-part anchoring system that locks the insulation in place while enabling screw adjustment.

abstract: Mounting for telescopic energy absorbing steering column for vehicles in which a guide bracket carries column release capsules on opposite sides of the column and has vertically oriented tongue and groove slide connection with column mounted capsule bracket for optimized column mounting stiffness and improved column guidance on release.
problem: Optimizing stiffness and guidance in a telescopic steering column mount during vehicle collision-induced release.
constraint: Balancing vertical slide mobility with lateral rigidity to prevent misalignment while enabling energy absorption during collapse.
mechanism: A sliding connection between two components allows controlled vertical movement while maintaining lateral stiffness. A tongue-and-groove interface ensures precise alignment and guidance during motion, balancing mobility with structural rigidity.
mechanism_raw: A vertically oriented tongue-and-groove slide connection between the guide bracket and column-mounted capsule bracket allows controlled vertical movement while maintaining lateral stiffness, ensuring precise column guidance during release events.

abstract: A fish holding and cleaning device containing two frame members that are attached to one another by a hinge for folding to a closed carrying position and unfolding to an open, cleaning position. When opened to a cleaning position the ends of the frame members pinch together so that a fish tail can be captured therebetween. The head of a fish so captured can be secured to an outside end of one of the frame members by a hook and a biasing element such as a rubber band. Each frame member has a grooved cleaning surface upon which a fish resides when being cleaned on that side. By using the hook a fish can be moved to and secured to the opposite cleaning surface while its tail remains captured between the frame member ends. Pockets are attached below the frame members for the storage of cleaning tools.
problem: Efficiently securing, positioning, and cleaning fish in a portable device without requiring manual readjustment between operations.
constraint: Maintaining secure clamping of the fish tail while allowing smooth repositioning of the head between cleaning surfaces without slippage.
mechanism: A clamping mechanism secures one end of an object while a biasing system allows the other end to move between operational positions. Hinged frame members apply compressive force to the clamped end, and an elastic biasing element maintains contact with a working surface during repositioning.
mechanism_raw: Hinged frame members pinch the fish tail when unfolded, while a hook-and-rubber-band system biases the fish head to one cleaning surface. The fish can then be moved to the opposite surface for cleaning while the tail remains clamped, enabling bidirectional access.

abstract: An upsetter of the horizontal type which has in a horizontal row a plurality of split dies which include upper movable dies and lower fixed dies each having a clamp die section and an upset die section, the upsetter including a number of piece dies separately constituting the clamp die sections of the movable dies and hydraulic cylinders for operating the clamp die sections independently of each other.
problem: Forming complex metal parts with precise upset features using a horizontal die system.
constraint: Coordinating independent hydraulic actuation across multiple die sections to ensure synchronized clamping and forming without mechanical interference.
mechanism: Independent actuation of multiple die sections enables selective clamping and forming of material. Separate hydraulic cylinders control clamp and forming die segments, decoupling clamping force from forming force to achieve localized precision without mechanical interference.
mechanism_raw: Independently operated hydraulic cylinders control separate clamp die sections within split dies, allowing selective clamping of workpieces while adjacent upset die sections form material. This decouples clamping force from forming force for localized precision.

abstract: A vehicle body of the convertible or targa type and the method of converting such a body from a sedan type vehicle body in which a reinforcing structure is disposed within the passenger compartment and is fastened thereto to form a centrally extending structural channel member extending longitudinally within the passenger compartment and having forward and rearward transverse portions fastened to the forward and rearward suspension supports of the body to transmit torsional and beaming loads imposed on the vehicle body by the ground engaging wheels.
problem: Maintaining structural rigidity (torsional and beaming load paths) in a vehicle body when converting from a closed sedan configuration to an open convertible/targa configuration, where removing the roof eliminates critical structural elements.
constraint: The reinforcing structure must be integrated within the passenger compartment without significantly compromising interior space or comfort, while still providing sufficient structural rigidity to match or approach the torsional stiffness of the original sedan body.
mechanism: An internal load-bearing frame is integrated within the passenger compartment, fastened to form a longitudinally extending structural channel with transverse connections to the front and rear suspension mounting points. This frame transmits torsional and beaming loads through the passenger compartment structure to the suspension supports, compensating for structural loss caused by removing the roof.
mechanism_raw: A reinforcing structure is disposed within the passenger compartment and fastened to form a centrally extending structural channel member running longitudinally, with forward and rearward transverse portions that connect to the front and rear suspension supports. This creates an internal load-bearing frame that transmits torsional and beaming loads through the passenger compartment structure to the suspension mounting points, compensating for the structural loss caused by removing the roof.

abstract: The invention relates to an apparatus for producing a preform for constituting an optical fiber. This apparatus essentially comprises a glass maker's lathe and a motor which holds and rotates a hollow silica tube, a torch making it possible to heat a cross-section of the tube and which can be translated along the tube and means for supplying the gaseous compounds consisting of silicon chloride, oxygen and doping agents decomposing under the action of the heat. Part of the products obtained is deposited on the walls of the tube. The supply means comprise a pipe entering the tube in axial manner and at the end of which are provided two radially directed arms, which terminate with an outlet normal to the pipe and arm, said pipe moving in translation integrally with the torch.
problem: Delivering gaseous reactants (silicon chloride, oxygen, doping agents) to the correct deposition zone on a rotating silica tube during optical fiber preform manufacturing, where the heating and deposition zone moves along the tube via torch translation.
constraint: The gas supply system must maintain consistent flow rates and directional control as it moves with the torch, while the rotating tube and translating components create mechanical complexity in routing and sealing the gas delivery path.
mechanism: A gas delivery conduit enters the deposition tube axially and translates integrally with the heating zone, so the gas delivery point travels with the moving deposition zone. The conduit terminates in two radially directed arms, each ending with an outlet oriented normal to both the conduit and the arm, ensuring consistent gas flow direction relative to the moving deposition zone regardless of position along the tube.
mechanism_raw: The gas supply pipe enters the tube axially and moves in translation integrally with the torch, so the gas delivery point travels with the heating zone. The pipe terminates in two radially directed arms, each ending with an outlet oriented normal to both the pipe and the arm, ensuring consistent gas flow direction relative to the moving deposition zone regardless of torch position along the tube.

abstract: A folding apparatus for a sewing machine which includes a first guide for folding a marginal edge portion of fabric to define a pocket or hem and a second guide for directing a relatively narrow web or strip from an area remote to an operator work area to an area partially within the first guide. A portion of the first guide defines a slot which permits a portion of the narrow web to extend into abutment with fabric defining the pocket such that the fabric and web feed to the sewing machine as one component.
problem: Coordinating the feeding of two separate material streams (fabric with a folded edge and a narrow web/strip) into a sewing machine as a single unified component, where the web originates from a remote location relative to the operator work area.
constraint: The slot geometry and guide positioning must precisely align the web with the fabric fold so they merge correctly without misalignment, while accommodating the different feed dynamics of the two separate material streams.
mechanism: A first guide folds the fabric's marginal edge to form a pocket or hem, and a second guide directs the narrow web from a remote area to a position partially within the first guide. A slot defined in the first guide allows a portion of the narrow web to extend into abutment with the fabric, so both materials feed together into the sewing machine as one component.
mechanism_raw: A first guide folds the fabric's marginal edge to form a pocket or hem, and a second guide directs the narrow web from a remote area to a position partially within the first guide. A slot defined in the first guide allows a portion of the narrow web to extend into abutment with the fabric, so both materials feed together into the sewing machine as one component.

abstract: An electronic sewing machine with a computer (10) for the sewing of a selected fancy seam has electronic circuits to bring about a breaking of a control circuit of the motor (11) of the machine, when the selected seam is completed, and further to detect the "O"-position of a motor control (16) and in this position to re-engage the control circuit and initiate starting codes in the computer for repetition of the selected fancy seam, when the motor is restarted.
problem: Automatically repeating a selected fancy seam pattern on an electronic sewing machine without manual intervention, ensuring the motor is in the correct rotational position before restarting the pattern to avoid errors.
constraint: The system must wait for the motor to reach the exact reference position before re-engaging, which introduces a delay but ensures the pattern starts from a consistent, known position each time.
mechanism: Electronic circuits interrupt the motor control circuit when the selected seam is completed, then detect a reference position of the motor control. Once the motor reaches this reference position, the control circuit is re-engaged and starting codes are initiated in the computer to repeat the selected seam pattern.
mechanism_raw: Electronic circuits break the motor control circuit when the selected seam is completed, then detect the 'O'-position (reference position) of the motor control. Once the motor reaches this reference position, the control circuit is re-engaged and starting codes are initiated in the computer to repeat the selected fancy seam pattern.

abstract: The present invention relates to a process for recovering uranium from raffinate which is obtained by extracting phosphoric acid from a uranium-containing wet-process phosphoric acid with the aid of organic extractants and separating the resulting organic phosphoric acid extract from residue not taken up by the extract. To this end, the raffinate residue is subjected to thermal treatment and thereby freed from dissolved or emulsified residual extractant. Next, the raffinate is treated with a water-immiscible solvent to extract the uranium, and the extracted uranium is separated from the undissolved raffinate portion.
problem: Recovering uranium from raffinate residue that remains after phosphoric acid extraction using organic extractants, where dissolved or emulsified residual extractant interferes with subsequent uranium recovery.
constraint: The thermal treatment must remove residual extractant without degrading the uranium or the raffinate matrix, and the water-immiscible solvent must selectively extract uranium while leaving the undissolved raffinate intact for separation.
mechanism: The residue is first subjected to thermal treatment to remove dissolved or emulsified residual extractant, then treated with a water-immiscible solvent to extract the target material, and finally the extracted material is separated from the undissolved residue portion through phase separation.
mechanism_raw: The raffinate residue is first subjected to thermal treatment to remove dissolved or emulsified residual extractant, then treated with a water-immiscible solvent to extract the uranium, and finally the extracted uranium is separated from the undissolved raffinate portion through phase separation.

abstract: The invention is a new type of diffraction crystal designed for sagittally focusing photons of various energies. The invention is based on the discovery that such focusing is not obtainable with conventional crystals because of distortion resulting from anticlastic curvature. The new crystal comprises a monocrystalline base having a front face contoured for sagittally focusing photons and a back face provided with rigid, upstanding, stiffening ribs restricting anticlastic curvature. When mounted in a suitable bending device, the reflecting face of the crystal can be adjusted to focus photons having any one of a range of energies.
problem: Conventional diffraction crystals cannot focus photons sagittally because anticlastic curvature distorts the crystal during bending, preventing precise focusing across different photon energies.
constraint: The crystal must remain monocrystalline and bendable enough for focus adjustment, while the ribs must be rigid enough to prevent unwanted distortion but not so massive as to prevent the required bending.
mechanism: Structural stiffening elements on a deformable surface counteract secondary distortion caused by bending, enabling the primary surface to maintain its intended shape while the material is flexed for focus adjustment. The stiffeners act as constraints that decouple the desired primary curvature from unwanted secondary deformation.
mechanism_raw: Rigid stiffening ribs on the back face of the crystal counteract the anticlastic curvature that would otherwise distort the front (reflecting) face, allowing the front face to maintain its desired focusing contour while the crystal is bent to adjust focus for different photon energies. The ribs act as a structural constraint that decouples the desired primary curvature from the unwanted secondary distortion.

abstract: Baked products comprising from about 12% to about 60% of a non-absorbable, non-digestible liquid polyol polyester and from about 25% to about 85% microcrystalline cellulose or a mixture of microcrystalline cellulose and flour in a weight ratio cellulose:flour of at least 1:1 have good texture, good mouthfeel, are highly palatable and have a low caloric content.
reason: This is a composition/formulation patent specifying ingredient ratios (polyol polyester and microcrystalline cellulose) to achieve desired baked good properties. It describes what ingredients to combine and in what proportions, but does not describe a causal functional mechanism that produces an effect through a generalizable principle.

abstract: A centrifugal cleaner and assembly thereof for separating solids from a fluid suspension. Each cleaner has an accepts plenum chamber, a slurry inlet plenum chamber adjacent thereto, a rejects plenum chamber disposed in alignment with and spaced from the accepts and slurry inlet chambers, and an axially elongated tubular shell for defining a centrifugal separating chamber disposed between the accepts chamber and rejects chamber. A multiplicity of cleaners are nested in side-by-side alignment so that the slurry inlet chambers, the accepts chambers, and the rejects chambers are interconnected with their respective counterparts to form a longitudinally elongated accepts plenum, a longitudinally elongated slurry inlet plenum, and a longitudinally elongated rejects plenum which serve to provide fluid communication between each of the cleaners and the accepts collection tank, the slurry supply tank and the rejects collection tank.
problem: Efficiently separating solids from fluid suspensions using multiple centrifugal cleaners while ensuring uniform distribution of slurry input and collection of accepts and rejects across all units.
constraint: The cleaners must be precisely aligned so that corresponding chambers interconnect, and the elongated plenum design must maintain uniform pressure and flow distribution across all units to prevent some cleaners from being starved or overloaded.
mechanism: Multiple parallel processing units are interconnected via shared distribution and collection networks that balance input and output flows across all units. The shared manifolds act as parallel pathways that maintain uniform pressure and flow distribution to prevent starvation or overloading of individual units.
mechanism_raw: Multiple centrifugal cleaners are nested side-by-side with their corresponding plenum chambers (slurry inlet, accepts, rejects) interconnected to form elongated shared plenum chambers that distribute fluid across all cleaners and collect outputs uniformly. The shared manifolds act as distribution and collection networks that parallelize the separation process while maintaining balanced flow to each unit.

abstract: Apparatus is disclosed for attachment to shoes to create tap dancing shoes, including heel and toe attachments. Each of the attachments has two pieces, one of which is fixedly attached to the shoe along respective outer edges, having a center cutout with a bridging member proximate one end. The second piece loosely fits within the center cutout of the first piece, and has a pair of projecting ears which loosely nest within cross axis grooves in the first piece, the second piece also having a forward lip and surface for contacting against the bridging member of the first piece for creating a tapping sound.
reason: This is a specific mechanical attachment design for tap dancing shoes. It describes a particular two-piece component geometry with cutouts, ears, grooves, and bridging members tailored to produce a tapping sound on a shoe. While it involves mechanical interaction, the mechanism is too application-specific and does not embody a generalizable causal principle beyond the immediate product.

abstract: A device for clamping the adjustment ring 3 of a cone crusher with respect to a support ring 1 mated therewith by means of threads 2 comprises a check nut 4 and hydraulic cylinders 7 with spring-actuated piston rods 6 whose tips 8 are arranged in a groove 9, one of the surfaces of the groove being formed by a taper recess 5 of the clamping ring 4 and the other surface thereof being formed by the end surface 10 of the support ring 1. The piston rods 6 of the hydraulic cylinders 7 are arranged radially with respect to the axis of the check nut 4.
problem: Clamping an adjustment ring to a support ring in a cone crusher with uniform force around the entire circumference, despite the need for repeated adjustment and release.
constraint: The piston rods must be arranged radially and the groove geometry (taper recess plus end surface) must match the piston rod tips to ensure uniform force distribution and proper self-centering, while the spring actuation must provide sufficient return force without interfering with the hydraulic clamping action.
mechanism: Radially arranged actuators apply uniform clamping force around a circular interface through a self-centering mechanism. Actuator tips engage a groove formed between a tapered recess and a surface, where pressurization drives engagement and a return mechanism ensures release. The radial symmetry ensures even force distribution around the full circumference.
mechanism_raw: Radially arranged hydraulic cylinders with spring-actuated piston rods apply clamping force uniformly around the circular interface. The piston rod tips fit into a groove formed between a taper recess in the clamping ring and the end surface of the support ring, creating a self-centering clamping action where hydraulic pressure pushes the pistons into the groove to clamp, and springs ensure return when pressure is released. The radial arrangement ensures even force distribution around the full circumference.

abstract: A combined toothpaste dispenser and toothbrush device comprising an elongate container for receiving or containing toothpaste and forming a handle member, a toothbrush member connected or connectable to said container and supporting bristles, ducting leading or capable of leading from the container to the bristles of said brush member, and a device for urging toothpaste through the ducting from the container to the bristles, characterized by the feature that the toothbrush member is adapted to be displaced relative to the elongate container so that in an inoperative position the brush member is juxtaposed or lies along the container while in the operative position the brush member extends from the end of the container and away from it to permit teeth-cleaning operations to be effected.
problem: Combining toothpaste storage, dispensing, and brushing into a single compact device without compromising usability during operation.
constraint: Balancing compactness for storage with sufficient extension of the brush for effective teeth-cleaning operations.
mechanism: A movable component is mechanically displaced relative to a storage unit between a stowed position (aligned with the unit) and an operative position (extended away from the unit), enabling dual functionality of storage and active use through positional reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A toothbrush member is mechanically displaced relative to an elongate container between a stowed position (aligned with the container) and an operative position (extended away from the container), enabling dual functionality of storage and active use through positional reconfiguration.

abstract: A carrying or transporting tube for artistic prints, sheets, or canvas materials features a backing liner that protects the wound print within the tube and prevents the unwinding of the wound print. The liner is comprised of a rectilinear section having a pouch on opposite ends thereof. The print to be transported is placed in the pouch of the liner, and the liner is wound and inserted into the carrying tube.
problem: Protecting rolled artistic prints during transport while preventing unintended unwinding of the rolled material.
constraint: Ensuring the liner's pouch design allows easy insertion/removal of the print while maintaining secure retention during transport.
mechanism: A rectilinear backing structure with anchoring elements at both ends secures the rolled material during winding into a containment tube, using the anchoring elements to fix the material and the structure to maintain tension and prevent unwinding.
mechanism_raw: A rectilinear backing liner with pouches at both ends secures the print during winding into a tube, using the pouches to anchor the print and the liner's structure to maintain tension and prevent unwinding.

abstract: In a sheet stacking apparatus, especially a recirculating document handler for recirculating document sheets for precollation copying at a copier platen to and from a stack in a document tray without obstructing access to the document tray, with restacking edge guides repositionable to accommodate stacking different sheet sizes and a restacking feeder for restacking the document sheets in the tray within the restacking edge guides by feeding each document in over the top of the stack from one edge and releasing the document to restack, there is provided automatically varying corrugation restacking apparatus enabling controlled restacking for recirculative copying of large flimsy documents such as Japanese B4 size sheets compatibly with normal document sizes having sheet corrugating members repositioned by movement of a repositionable restacking edge guide into a position to restack such large sheets and automatically providing in coordination therewith additional sheet corrugation in response to the flimsiness and size of the sheet.
problem: Restacking varying sizes and stiffness of document sheets (e.g., large flimsy Japanese B4 sheets) in a recirculating document handler without obstructing tray access.
constraint: Synchronizing edge guide repositioning with corrugation adjustments to handle diverse sheet properties without manual intervention.
mechanism: Automatically adjusting material deformation in coordination with repositionable edge guides, where movement of the guides triggers additional deformation to accommodate material flexibility and size, enabling adaptive restacking.
mechanism_raw: Automatically adjusting sheet corrugation in coordination with repositionable edge guides, where movement of the guides triggers additional corrugation to accommodate sheet flimsiness and size, enabling adaptive restacking.

abstract: Apparatus for preheating scrap material, e.g. scrap metal, comprises heaters, such as air preheaters, scrap containers and air or gas conduits for conveying heated gas from the heaters to the scrap container(s) and back from the scrap container(s). The apparatus is characterized in that the conduit to the scrap container(s) is provided with valve means for diverting the flow of hot air or gas to the container(s), for example during replacement of container(s).
problem: Maintaining continuous preheating of scrap material while replacing scrap containers in a heating system.
constraint: Ensuring valve actuation and flow diversion occur seamlessly during container replacement to avoid thermal disruption.
mechanism: Valve means divert flow away from a container during replacement, allowing uninterrupted operation of the system by rerouting the flow path.
mechanism_raw: Valve means divert hot gas flow away from a container during replacement, allowing uninterrupted operation of the heating system by rerouting the flow path.

abstract: An optical weft sensor for a loom in which the light-receiving and light receiving elements are fixed to the loom frame and only the flexible optical fibers are disposed on the reed frame. Since no shock or vibration is applied to these electronic elements, it is possible to obtain a relatively long life time, thus improving the sensor reliability. Additionally, since the weft sensor according to the present invention is supported by a sensor holder, it is possible to readily adjust the sensor position along the reed frame or reed holder when the width of the cloth is required to change. The optical weft sensor comprises a LED, a phototransistor, optical fibers, and a detection circuit, in addition to the sensor holder.
problem: Protecting sensitive optical/electronic components in a vibrating loom environment while enabling adjustable positioning of the sensor.
constraint: Maintaining signal integrity through flexible fibers while allowing positional adjustment of the sensor along the reed frame.
mechanism: Fixed sensitive components are isolated from vibration by mounting them to a rigid frame, while flexible transmission elements on a movable frame transmit signals, decoupling sensitive components from mechanical stress.
mechanism_raw: Fixed electronic elements (LED, phototransistor) are isolated from vibration by mounting them to the loom frame, while flexible optical fibers on the reed frame transmit light signals, decoupling sensitive components from mechanical stress.

abstract: A three-dimensional circuit structure suited for a routing type electronic switcher matrix, for analog or digital signals, in which internal wire interconnections are not required. Plural parallel-disposed zero-insertion-force connectors are orthogonally related on opposite sides of mother-boards that divide tiers in the structure. Selected conductive pins of the connectors are electrically connected to make necessary interconnections. Printed circuit cards are inserted in the zero-insertion-force connectors for carrying a large plurality of solid-state, or equivalent, cross points, and are inter-connected by the selected conductive pins.
problem: Reducing the need for internal wire interconnections in a three-dimensional circuit structure while enabling modular signal routing.
constraint: Balancing physical tier separation with electrical connectivity while maintaining signal integrity across orthogonal connector arrays.
mechanism: Orthogonal connector arrays on opposing surfaces of structural tiers enable modular electrical coupling between components across separated layers without internal wiring, using selectively engaged conductive elements to bridge orthogonal interfaces.
mechanism_raw: Orthogonal zero-insertion-force connectors on opposite sides of mother-boards divide tiers, and selected conductive pins are used to electrically connect components across tiers without internal wiring, enabling modular and reconfigurable interconnections.

abstract: A damper operator for use with a damper having a frame and a damper blade pivotally associated with the frame, which damper operator comprises a drive rod; a pair of lever arms which are pivotally associated with each and which extend between the drive rod and a pivoting mechanism associated with the blade of the damper; and a latching mechanism which extends between portions of each of the lever arms, and which permits selective engagement and disengagement between those portions of the lever arms, and accordingly, selective respective rotation of the lever arms, so that the blade of the damper can be urged toward a predetermined orientation.
problem: Achieving selective and controlled rotation of a damper blade to a predetermined orientation without continuous force application.
constraint: Maintaining precise blade positioning while allowing repeated engagement/disengagement cycles without mechanical wear or loss of control.
mechanism: A releasable mechanical coupling between linked actuation elements allows selective engagement to transfer motion for blade positioning, and disengagement to permit independent adjustment without continuous force application.
mechanism_raw: A latching mechanism between lever arm portions allows selective engagement/disengagement, enabling independent rotation of lever arms to drive the blade toward a desired position when latched and permitting manual or automatic adjustment when unlatched.

abstract: A cloth tentering device wherein the tentering force for spreading cloth is produced magnetically between a permanent magnet member accommodated within a tubular cloth or engaged with the selvages of a flat cloth and rows of electromagnets in position separate from and parallel to the cloth. The tentering force can be freely adjusted in the course of the tentering operation by controlling the energizing current of the electromagnets.
problem: Adjustably controlling the tentering force applied to cloth during spreading operations without mechanical contact or fixed-force systems.
constraint: Ensuring uniform force distribution across the cloth while allowing continuous adjustment without physical contact or mechanical wear.
mechanism: Dynamic modulation of magnetic field strength between a fixed magnetic element and controllable electromagnetic elements generates and adjusts a repulsive or attractive force in real time without physical contact.
mechanism_raw: Magnetic interaction between a permanent magnet member and electromagnet rows generates tentering force, which is dynamically adjusted by varying the electromagnet energizing current to modulate the magnetic field strength in real time.

abstract: A hair brush has features for placing waves in the hair with the use of a hot air blower. The brush has a body with a filament carrier portion and a handle portion. The filament carrier portion has at least one stationary section and one movable section. Each section has at least one longitudinal row of filaments. The movable section is movable with respect to the stationary section. In one position, the filaments align, and in the other position, the filament are moved out of alignment. A spring urges the movable section to the first position.
problem: Creating controlled waves or texture in hair using a hot air blower by dynamically adjusting the interaction between brush filaments and hair strands.
constraint: Maintaining consistent filament positioning during operation while allowing rapid transitions between aligned and misaligned states for styling variability.
mechanism: A movable contact element shifts between aligned and misaligned configurations relative to a stationary contact element, altering interaction patterns with a target surface to vary pressure and fluid flow effects, with a restoring force biasing the movable element to a default state.
mechanism_raw: A movable filament section shifts between alignment and misalignment with a stationary section, altering the contact pattern between filaments and hair to create varying pressure and airflow effects, with a spring biasing the movable section to the aligned position.

abstract: Carbonaceous raw material, such as lignite coal, having first been passed successively through a moving grate stoker furnace, a shaft furnace and a quench chamber is screened so as to remove from the end product substantially all +12 mesh and larger particles which are then crushed to -12 mesh screen size and recirculated into the stream of raw material enroute through the moving grate stoker.
problem: Efficiently processing carbonaceous raw material to achieve a consistent particle size distribution while minimizing waste and energy consumption.
constraint: Balancing recirculation efficiency with energy costs of crushing and screening while avoiding over-processing of already-sized particles.
mechanism: A closed-loop process separates oversized particles via screening, subjects them to size reduction, and reintroduces them into the upstream material stream, ensuring only appropriately sized particles proceed to a finishing stage while maintaining throughput through continuous recirculation.
mechanism_raw: Screening removes oversized particles, which are crushed and recirculated into the upstream raw material stream, ensuring only appropriately sized particles proceed to the quench chamber while maintaining throughput through closed-loop particle size control.

abstract: In the froth flotation of coal, especially coking coal, improved results are observed when using as a collector an oil distillate cut within the range 80.degree. to 250.degree. C., containing less than 20% by weight of naphthenes, less than 20% by weight of aromatic content and more than 60% by weight of n-alkanes and branched-alkanes. Preferably, the collector is used with a polyglycol ether "frother".
reason: The patent specifies a chemical composition for a collector in coal flotation, which is a domain-specific solution rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The problem and solution are tightly coupled to the chemical properties of the materials used in this particular separation process.

abstract: The invention provides a spiral separator of the type for use in separating a pulp of water and minerals into mineral fractions of differing densities and having a helical trough (30) supported with its axis upright. The shape of the trough working surface profile (30) varies (FIGS. 2A-2D) from place to place along the trough. The profile has a point of maximum displacement (32A, 32B, 32C, 32D) at which profile (30) is at a maximum spacing below a notional straight line (40) joining the inner end (31) and outer end (22) of the trough working surface profile (30). The distance of the point of maximum displacement (32A, 32B, 32C, 32D) from one end (31 or 22) of the profile varies along the trough. A method for manufacture of troughs according to the invention is also described and claimed.
problem: Separating minerals of differing densities in a pulp requires optimizing flow dynamics along a spiral trough to enhance separation efficiency.
constraint: The trough geometry must balance structural integrity with the need to create spatially varying flow conditions that maximize separation efficiency without causing mechanical failure.
mechanism: Varying the geometric profile of a transport channel along its length creates controlled flow patterns that differentially move particles based on density, with a point of maximum displacement shifting along the channel to balance separation forces and throughput.
mechanism_raw: Varying the geometric profile of the trough along its length creates controlled flow patterns that differentially move particles based on density, with a point of maximum displacement shifting along the trough to balance separation forces and throughput.
residual_terms: ["density", "pulp", "spiral trough", "minerals", "separation efficiency", "flow dynamics", "geometric profile", "transport channel", "flow patterns", "particles", "separation forces", "throughput"]

abstract: A method of extruding and shaping thermoplastic material in which a constant amount of thermoplastic material is continuously fed from a screw extruder to a die by means of a metering pump. The extruder is arranged to continuously receive a constant amount of the thermoplastic material. The metering pump is adjusted to the correct rotational frequency to maintain the pressure of the molten thermoplastic material between the extruder and the metering pump within a predetermined range.
problem: Maintaining consistent pressure and flow rate during thermoplastic extrusion to ensure uniform shaping and prevent process instability.
constraint: The system must reconcile the extruder's constant feed rate with the pump's variable speed to avoid pressure fluctuations that could disrupt the extrusion process.
mechanism: A metering device adjusts its operational frequency in response to real-time pressure measurements between a material source and the device, creating a feedback loop that dynamically balances material feed rate and pressure within a target range.
mechanism_raw: A metering pump adjusts its rotational frequency in response to real-time pressure measurements between the extruder and pump, creating a feedback loop that dynamically balances material feed rate and pressure within a target range.
residual_terms: ["pressure", "flow rate", "thermoplastic extrusion", "uniform shaping", "process instability", "extruder", "constant feed rate", "pump", "variable speed", "pressure fluctuations", "metering pump", "rotational frequency", "feedback loop", "material feed rate", "target range"]

abstract: A side terminal lead alloy is provided which is a composition of lead, 3 wt-% antimony and 10 wt-% brass. The alloy is capable of use in conjunction with resistance welding techniques. The terminal created thereby exhibits sufficient structural integrity to permit a mechanical connection to be made directly thereto without any additional threaded inserts and exhibits sufficient electrical current conductivity to permit direct electrical connection thereto.
reason: The patent describes a specific alloy composition (lead, antimony, brass) tailored for a niche application (side terminal leads). The mechanism is material-specific and does not generalize to a broader causal principle applicable across fields.

abstract: Methods and apparatus are disclosed for preventing a missile's rocket exhaust gases from contacting and adversely affecting, such as by overheating, the launch rails from which a missile may be launched. Such apparatus includes orifices and pressure/flow controls in association with the rails in order to produce a cold gaseous stream directed in opposition to the exhaust gases during at least the initial phase. The stream creates a boundary plane or barrier between the rails and the exhaust gases, thereby shielding the rails from damage due to overheating. Arrangements are provided to control the time and duration of the stream so that it may be limited to the period of actual need.
problem: Preventing high-temperature rocket exhaust gases from damaging launch rails during missile launch.
constraint: The gas stream must be precisely timed and limited to the initial launch phase to conserve resources while ensuring sufficient protection during peak thermal exposure.
mechanism: A controlled stream of cooling medium is directed in opposition to a high-temperature gas flow, creating a dynamic barrier plane that physically separates the gas from a protected surface and absorbs thermal energy before it reaches the surface.
mechanism_raw: A controlled stream of cold gas is directed in opposition to the exhaust flow, creating a dynamic barrier plane that physically separates the exhaust from the rails and absorbs thermal energy before it reaches the surface.
residual_terms: ["high-temperature", "rocket exhaust gases", "launch rails", "missile launch", "gas stream", "cold gas", "exhaust flow", "dynamic barrier plane", "thermal energy", "surface", "precisely timed", "initial launch phase", "peak thermal exposure"]

abstract: A mechanical device imparts a circular rotational movement to a liquid and at various stages of the movement exerts variable vacuum and pressure effects on the rotating liquid to convert potential energy into heat energy. Preferably employs a centrifugal energy drum (B) and a channelled guide disc (C) arranged in a device body (A) and supported by a chassis (D).
problem: Converting potential energy of a rotating liquid into usable heat energy efficiently.
constraint: The pressure and vacuum stages must be precisely timed and spatially arranged relative to the rotational position to maximize energy extraction without disrupting flow continuity.
mechanism: A rotating medium is subjected to alternating pressure and vacuum zones arranged circumferentially around its path, causing cyclic expansion and compression of the medium to convert kinetic energy into thermal energy through repeated work on the fluid.
mechanism_raw: A rotating liquid is subjected to staged variable vacuum and pressure effects at different points in its circular path, causing controlled expansion and compression of the liquid that converts its potential energy into heat energy through repeated cyclic work on the fluid.

abstract: An economizer (16) located in the rear pass (12) of a steam generator having a vertical tube panel containing a plurality of parallel, vertically spaced horizontal tube portions (22) and a support therefor including a pair of plates (32, 34), one positioned on either side of the tube panel. First tabs or bars (46) which are integral at one end (50) with the first plate (32) extend horizontally beneath and support every other, or alternate horizontal tube portions (22), and are welded (52) to the second plate (34) at their other ends. Second tabs or bars (44) which are integral at one end (48) with the second plate (34) extend horizontally beneath and support the remaining, alternate horizontal tube portions (22) not supported by the first bars (46), and are supported at their other ends by ledges (54) contained on the first plate (32).
problem: Supporting a vertical tube panel in an economizer while accommodating thermal expansion and maintaining structural integrity across all tubes.
constraint: The tab spacing must align with every other tube to ensure full coverage while the interlocking welds and ledges must accommodate differential thermal expansion between the plates and tubes.
mechanism: A dual-plate support system employs complementary interlocking elements on opposing plates, where each plate's elements support components not supported by the other, creating mutual reinforcement and self-stabilization while accommodating differential thermal expansion.
mechanism_raw: Two parallel plates with complementary interlocking tab arrays are positioned on either side of the tube panel; each plate's tabs support the tubes not supported by the other plate, and the tabs are anchored to the opposing plate, creating a self-stabilizing dual-plate support structure where each plate reinforces the other.

abstract: A press for compacting comminuted material in the manufacture of pressedboard comprising a pair of steel pressing bands which are backed up in the pressing zone by roller bodies on endless chains carried through this zone between respective press platens and the bands. The chains have links which are folded into a zigzag configuration as they enter the zone and are drawn out into an extended configuration outside the zone.
problem: Providing continuous backing support for pressing bands in a pressing zone while allowing the drive chains to flex and navigate around sprockets outside that zone.
constraint: The transition between zigzag and extended configurations must occur smoothly at the zone boundaries to avoid shock loads and maintain consistent pressing pressure.
mechanism: A chain or link assembly transitions between a compact, rigid configuration in a pressing zone and a flexible configuration outside that zone, with smooth boundary transitions to maintain consistent pressure application while enabling articulation around sprockets.
mechanism_raw: Chain links are designed to fold into a zigzag configuration as they enter the pressing zone, creating a compact, rigid backing structure for the roller bodies, and then unfold into an extended configuration outside the zone, allowing normal chain articulation around sprockets.

abstract: A system and method for handling and storing spent reactor fuel and other solid radioactive waste, including canisters to contain the elements of solid waste, storage racks to hold a plurality of such canisters, storage bays to store these racks in isolation by means of shielded doors in the bays. This system also includes means for remotely positioning the racks in the bays and an access tunnel within which the remotely operated means is located to position a rack in a selected bay. The modular type of these bays will facilitate the construction of additional bays and access tunnel extension.
reason: The patent describes a system architecture composed of modular shielded bays, storage racks, canisters, and remote handling equipment arranged in a facility layout. It lists components and their spatial relationships rather than describing a causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through a functional principle.

abstract: In order to improve the fatigue resistance of a cable, particularly a rubber adherable cable for reinforcing rubber articles such as vehicle tires, substantially uniformly distributed residual compressive stress is induced in substantially the complete peripheric zone of the wires making up the cable. The stress may be induced by submitting lengths of the cable to a number of elementary bending--unbending operations in considerably different planes and simultaneously tensioning the cable.
problem: Improving fatigue resistance of cables, particularly rubber-adherable cables for reinforcing rubber articles, by inducing uniform residual compressive stress in the wire periphery.
constraint: The bending-unbending operations must be performed in sufficiently different planes and with controlled tension to ensure uniform stress distribution without causing localized damage or compromising the rubber-adhesion properties of the cable surface.
mechanism: A cable or wire assembly undergoes repeated bending-unbending cycles in multiple distinct orientations under controlled tension, inducing plastic deformation in the peripheral region to create a substantially uniform distribution of residual compressive stress across the surface.
mechanism_raw: Lengths of cable are subjected to multiple elementary bending-unbending cycles in substantially different planes while simultaneously being tensioned, causing the outer peripheral zone of the wires to experience repeated plastic deformation in varied orientations, resulting in a substantially uniform distribution of residual compressive stress across the entire periphery.

abstract: The microstructure of titanium alloy castings is improved by a process which comprises beta-solution heat treating the cast article at or near the beta-transus temperature of the alloy, cooling the article to room temperature at a rate in excess of air cooling and aging the article at a temperature about 0.8 to 0.9 of the beta-transus.
problem: Improving the microstructure of titanium alloy castings to achieve desired mechanical properties and phase distribution.
constraint: The specific temperature ranges relative to the beta-transus and the cooling rate must be precisely controlled — too slow cooling or incorrect aging temperature causes unwanted phase growth or coarsening, while too rapid cooling may induce stress or cracking.
mechanism: A multi-stage thermal treatment process where a first heating step establishes a target phase state near a critical transformation temperature, a rapid cooling step locks in a non-equilibrium microstructure, and a subsequent aging step at a controlled sub-transformation temperature drives controlled precipitation and phase refinement, collectively producing the desired microstructure through precisely sequenced temperature and cooling rate control.
mechanism_raw: A sequential thermal treatment process where beta-solution heat treating near the beta-transus temperature establishes a phase state, rapid cooling (faster than air cooling) locks in a non-equilibrium microstructure, and aging at 0.8-0.9 of the beta-transus temperature drives controlled precipitation and phase refinement, collectively producing the target microstructure.

abstract: A protective carrier for holding a loaded spare magazine in a position of readiness for immediate insertion into operative engagement with a firearm. A latch release mechanism is operable simultaneously with the operation of the magazine release mechanism of the firearm, permitting an empty magazine and a loaded spare magazine to be released together, the empty magazine being allowed to fall clear of the firearm while the loaded spare magazine is grasped and inserted into the weapon for use in a minimum amount of time. The spare magazine carrier of the invention protectively surrounds the open upper end of the spare magazine to shield cartridges held therein against contamination by dirt, mud, and the elements, in order to help avoid malfunction or damage of the weapon.
problem: Enabling rapid magazine swap in a firearm while protecting the spare magazine from contamination and ensuring the empty magazine clears the weapon.
constraint: The coupling must trigger reliably with the firearm's existing magazine release without interfering with normal operation, while the protective shroud must shield against contamination yet allow sufficiently quick access for insertion.
mechanism: A dual-release coupling mechanism mechanically linked to an existing actuation point so that a single input simultaneously disengages two retained objects, allowing one to be passively cleared while the other is immediately grasped and repositioned, with a protective barrier shielding the retained object from environmental contamination while permitting rapid access.
mechanism_raw: A latch release mechanism mechanically coupled to the firearm's magazine release so that a single actuation simultaneously releases both the empty magazine and the loaded spare magazine from the carrier, allowing the empty to fall clear while the spare is immediately grasped and inserted, with the carrier's protective shroud shielding the spare's cartridges from dirt and elements.

abstract: A tablecloth having a central portion on which serving pieces may be placed, with a series of individual dining portions of the tablecloth projecting outwardly from the central portion at spaced locations and having individual place settings on these different portions, and with the tablecloth having cutaway areas between the individual dining portions and at which the table top is directly visible to give the overall assembly a unique and pleasing appearance.
reason: This patent describes a tablecloth with a specific layout of fabric portions and cutaway areas for aesthetic appearance. There is no causal functional mechanism — it is a static design arrangement of material, not a problem-solving mechanism that produces an effect through a functional relationship.

abstract: A tool is provided for pressure forming teeth in the periphery of a cylindrical, tubular workpiece such as a power transmission member by rolling. The tool has an improved tooth generating configuration which improves the flow characteristics of the metal in the workpiece and develops uniformity of tooth wall thickness during the tooth generating process.
problem: Forming uniform teeth on the periphery of a cylindrical tubular workpiece by rolling while ensuring consistent tooth wall thickness and good material flow.
constraint: The tool geometry must balance material flow characteristics with uniformity of tooth wall thickness — overly aggressive geometry causes uneven flow or stress concentrations, while insufficient forming action fails to achieve the desired tooth profile.
mechanism: A forming tool with a configured geometry controls material displacement in a workpiece during a rolling process, directing flow to develop uniform wall thickness and improved material characteristics as features are formed on a cylindrical surface.
mechanism_raw: A tool with a specifically configured tooth-generating geometry controls the flow of metal in the workpiece during the rolling process, directing material displacement to develop uniform tooth wall thickness and improved flow characteristics as the teeth are formed.

abstract: A method and apparatus for processing elongate brush cuttings, such as those resulting from the pruning of almond trees. The method comprises collecting the cuttings, loading them into the compaction chamber of a packer, moving a plunger longitudinally through the chamber to compress the cuttings and force them into an orientation extending generally normal to the direction of plunger travel, and discharging the cuttings from one end of the chamber while maintaining said orientation. The apparatus comprises a wheel supported chassis which carries a transfer packer and a crane supported grapple for loading cuttings into the packer. The packer has an open topped hopper into which the cuttings are charged. The plunger moves through the hopper to compress cuttings received therein and force said cuttings through a discharge opening in one side of the hopper.
problem: Processing elongate brush cuttings (such as from pruning) by compacting them and reorienting them from their elongated state into a more manageable cross-oriented configuration for discharge.
constraint: The plunger compression force and chamber geometry must be sufficient to reorient the cuttings without excessive force that would damage the material or jam the mechanism, while the discharge must maintain the reoriented state without reverting to the original elongated configuration.
mechanism: A longitudinal compression element moves through a confinement chamber, compressing elongate material and forcing it into an orientation extending generally normal to the direction of compression travel, with the discharge maintaining this reoriented configuration, thereby transforming bulky elongated material into a compact, cross-oriented output stream.
mechanism_raw: A plunger moves longitudinally through a compaction chamber, compressing the elongate cuttings and forcing them into an orientation extending generally normal to the direction of plunger travel, with the discharge maintaining this reoriented configuration, thereby transforming bulky elongated material into a compact, cross-oriented discharge stream.

abstract: An improved construction for a percussion fuse. The fuse function has a firing pin rigidly mounted in an ignition head an adapted to coact with a percussion cap mounted in an impact member. This impact member is securedly maintained in a first position by means of at least one blocking sphere which is partially mounted in an annular groove of the impact member and partially mounted in a bore of the cylindrical forward portion of the percussion fuse body. A movable inertial sphere is disposed in a chamber between the impact member and the ignition head. In order to improve the fail-safety there is mounted in this chamber a housing between the impact member and ignition head which is coaxially movable with respect to the firing pin. When the projectile is accelerated forwardly the housing moves against the impact member and the movable inertial sphere is clamped between the impact member and housing to thereby prevent a further relative motion between firing pin and percussion cap and to thereby prevent detonation of the percussion cap. During normal deceleration prior to target impact, the housing moves back from the impact member and allows the inertial sphere to roll into the annular chamber of the housing. This allows the impact member to move forward and thereby allows the percussion cap to impact the firing pin when the projectile impacts the target.
problem: Ensuring a percussion fuse does not detonate prematurely but reliably detonates on impact.
constraint: Balancing fail-safety (preventing accidental detonation) with reliable detonation on impact.
mechanism: Use an inertial element restrained during acceleration to prevent motion between a triggering component and a detonator, and released during deceleration to allow the triggering component to move and initiate detonation.
mechanism_raw: Inertial sphere clamped between impact member and housing during acceleration prevents motion between firing pin and percussion cap; during deceleration, housing moves back, allowing inertial sphere to roll into an annular chamber, enabling the impact member to move forward and trigger detonation.

abstract: An improved process for the electrolysis of an aqueous electrolyte in an electrolytic membrane cell is provided. The membrane cell is comprised of an anode compartment having at least one anode and containing the aqueous electrolyte and a cathode compartment containing at least one cathode and a concentrated catholyte liquor. A vertically positioned cation exchange membrane separates the anode compartment from the cathode compartment. The process improvement comprises exposing a substantial portion of the cathode to a gaseous atmosphere, this substantial portion of the cathode is not immersed in the concentrated catholyte liquor produced. The concentrated aqueous catholyte liquor is removed from the cathode compartment to prevent a substantial accumulation of catholyte liquor in the cathode compartment. The improved process can be carried out in a novel electrolytic cell in which the cathode compartment is substantially reduced in size to permit a material savings as well as provide a higher production capacity per unit of floor space.
problem: Improving efficiency and production capacity in electrolysis of aqueous electrolytes in membrane cells.
constraint: Maintaining optimal catholyte concentration and gas exposure for maximum reaction efficiency.
mechanism: Expose a portion of an electrode to a gaseous environment instead of full immersion in electrolyte, while actively removing electrolyte to prevent accumulation, thereby optimizing the electrochemical reaction interface.
mechanism_raw: Exposing a substantial portion of the cathode to a gaseous atmosphere instead of immersing it in catholyte, while removing catholyte to prevent accumulation, optimizing the electrochemical reaction interface.

abstract: The present invention relates to novel facultative methylotrophic microorganisms of the genus Pseudomonas, or of a genus Pseudomonas-type genus, to protein-containing biomass, and to a process for the microbiological purification of aqueous solutions, e.g. wastewater solutions, which contain methanol, ethanol, acetate, glucose, alkylammonium compounds, e.g., trimethylethylammonium chloride, or alkylamine oxides, e.g. trimethylamine oxide, as pollutants.
reason: The mechanism is primarily the use of specific biological agents (microorganisms) to degrade pollutants, which is application-specific and not a generalizable process mechanism.

abstract: The disclosed arrangement refers specifically to a smelting arrangement which includes two metallurgical vessels serviced by a common, electrode carrying lid which is pivoted about a vertical axis as between one or the other position in relation to the two vessels. The current feed arrangement is designed such that beginning with a bus system extending from the transformer, conductors are run in a triangular arrangement down to a first plane, in freely sagging suspension and up again to the electrodes in such a manner that the conductors undergo a slight displacement only in the vertical suspension region near the transformer, equivalent to a slight torsion of a triangular prism, while the suspended portions of the conductors remain invarient during the pivoting about an axis that runs through the center of the triangle defined by the connect points at the transformer.
problem: Maintaining electrical connectivity in a smelting arrangement with a pivoting lid between two vessels.
constraint: Ensuring minimal conductor displacement during pivoting to maintain stable electrical feed.
mechanism: Suspend a conductor in a freely sagging configuration near a power source, using a geometric arrangement that allows pivoting motion while maintaining invariant suspended portions to minimize displacement in the vertical suspension region.
mechanism_raw: Triangular conductor arrangement suspended in freely sagging form near the transformer, allowing pivoting of the lid while keeping suspended conductor portions invariant, minimizing displacement in the vertical suspension region.

abstract: An adjustable friction hinge assembly of thermoplastic material comprises a first hinge leaf having spaced apart non-adjustable knuckles having non-circular through holes, and a second hinge leaf having a single knuckle which fits into the space between the spaced-apart non-adjustable knuckles. The hinge pin has non-circular portions which are received with the corresponding non-circular through holes of said spaced-apart knuckles, and which prevent rotation of said hinge pin in said knuckles. The inside diameter of the middle knuckle is adjustable by an adjustment screw, thereby to control the frictional torque resistance of the knuckle on the hinge pin. Provision is made for squeezing some of the plastic material into the threads of said adjustment screw, thereby to maintain the adjustment at its initially set position despite repeated openings and closings of the hinged door, cover or lid.
problem: Maintaining a desired frictional torque in a hinge assembly despite repeated mechanical cycling and environmental exposure.
constraint: The material must deform sufficiently to lock the adjustment without compromising structural integrity or requiring excessive torque during initial setting.
mechanism: A deformable material is displaced into a threaded interface during adjustment, creating a self-locking interference that resists loosening under dynamic loads. A non-circular geometric constraint between interconnected components prevents rotational slippage, while the material's plastic deformation at the interface permanently retains the adjusted position without requiring continuous actuation.
mechanism_raw: A deformable thermoplastic material is intentionally displaced into the threads of an adjustment screw during tightening, creating a self-locking interference that resists loosening under dynamic loads. The non-circular hinge pin and knuckle geometry prevent rotational slippage, while the material's plastic deformation at the screw interface permanently retains the adjusted position.

abstract: A methanation reactor utilizing an improved catalyst for the conversion of CO, CO.sub.2 and mixtures thereof to CH.sub.4 is disclosed. The catalyst comprises a monolithic mesh type structure of a nickel alloy having an integral Beta phase Raney coating on its outer surfaces. When used, substantially higher reactant flow rates and lower operating temperatures are possible as compared to conventional fluidized bed granular catalysts.
problem: Achieving efficient catalytic conversion of CO/CO₂ to CH₄ at higher flow rates and lower temperatures than conventional granular catalysts.
constraint: The catalyst must maintain structural stability and coating adhesion under thermal cycling and high-velocity gas flow without sacrificing surface area or catalytic activity.
mechanism: A structured scaffold with an integrated catalytic coating provides a high-surface-area pathway for reactants, enabling uniform distribution and reduced pressure drop. The monolithic geometry allows higher flow velocities while maintaining intimate contact between reactants and active sites, avoiding attrition and channeling issues inherent in particulate systems.
mechanism_raw: A monolithic mesh structure provides a high-surface-area scaffold with an integral catalytic coating, enabling uniform reactant distribution and reduced pressure drop. The structured geometry allows higher flow velocities while maintaining intimate contact between reactants and active sites, and the monolithic form avoids the attrition and channeling issues of granular beds.

abstract: A pontoon assembly for floating bridges includes four pivotally interconnected articulable floats providing a pontoon assembly having a folded and an unfolded position. Each of the floats is generally rectangularly shaped. In the unfolded position the pontoon assembly has an inner two floats and an outer two floats and the outer two floats are lengthwise connected to an outer edge of the inner two floats. The inner two floats each have an upper surface which provides a vehicular roadway. A rectangular recess is disposed in each of the outer two floats and the recess has a size sufficient to permit a ramp part to be removably positioned in there. The ramp parts have a height corresponding to the depth of the recess in order to provide a flush upper surface with the upper surface of the associated outer float. Each of the ramp parts includes lugs to permit connection with an inner float to thereby provide a closed rampway.
problem: Creating a floating bridge structure that can transition between compact folded and expanded operational configurations while maintaining a continuous, load-bearing roadway.
constraint: The pivot connections and ramp interfaces must balance flexibility for folding with sufficient rigidity to support vehicular loads and environmental forces when deployed.
mechanism: Interconnected segments with pivot points allow transition between folded and expanded configurations. Nested inner and outer segments with recessed channels accommodate removable bridge sections, which are mechanically linked to maintain a continuous, load-bearing surface when deployed. The articulation enables folding without disconnection, while the recessed design preserves structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Pivotally interconnected rectangular floats are arranged in nested inner and outer pairs, with recessed channels in the outer floats accommodating removable ramp sections. The ramps are mechanically linked to the inner floats via lugs, forming a closed, flush roadway when deployed. The articulation allows folding without disconnecting components, while the recessed design preserves structural continuity.

abstract: This invention relates to a process for servo-controlling a magnitude TI depending on a parameter .theta., whereby: the variations in time of a second magnitude TG which varies as a function of the parameter .theta. and to which the magnitude TI is related are monitored; a control signal TGE=TDS+TER is provided, TER being a function of the deviation between the reference value TR and the real value TI of the first magnitude, and the value of TDS being equal to the arithmetical mean between maximum and minimum values, TGEMX and TGEMN respectively, of the second magnitude TG determined previously; and the value of the parameter .theta. is adjusted to servo-control the second magnitude TG by the calculated value TGE.
problem: Servo-controlling a system parameter to maintain a target value of a monitored magnitude despite deviations caused by external disturbances.
constraint: The system must balance responsiveness to deviations with stability to avoid oscillations, requiring careful tuning of the corrective term relative to the baseline signal.
mechanism: A control signal is synthesized by combining a baseline value (derived from the arithmetic mean of previously determined maximum and minimum values of the monitored magnitude) with a corrective term proportional to the deviation between the target and actual values. The parameter is adjusted to drive the monitored magnitude toward the synthesized control signal, centering the system within its operational envelope while compensating for disturbances.
mechanism_raw: A control signal is synthesized by combining a baseline value (the arithmetic mean of previously determined maximum and minimum values of the monitored magnitude) with a corrective term proportional to the deviation between the target and actual values. The parameter is adjusted to drive the monitored magnitude toward the synthesized control signal, effectively centering the system within its operational envelope while compensating for disturbances.

abstract: A method of manufacturing railway switchpoint concrete sleeper blocks of varying lengths and having different number of attachment means located in mutually different positions for the attachment of rails. A plurality of steel matrix plates 102 whose respective lengths correspond to the desired lengths of the various sleeper blocks and which exhibit detachably mounted dowels 109 are placed end to end in an elongate mould bed with the dowels facing upwardly, whereafter reinforcing rods 5 are tensioned and concrete is poured into the mould bed and permitted to harden. The thus formed coherent concrete body is then removed from the mould and the matrix plates removed, with the dowels remaining cast in the concrete block. The concrete body is then cut into sleeper blocks of desired length. The dowels are accurately mounted in predetermined positions in frame members 111 affixed to the matrix plates. Upon casting and hardening of the sleeper blocks the frame members are disengaged from the plates and the in-cast dowels for renewed use in a subsequent casting operation.
problem: Manufacturing concrete railway sleepers with variable lengths and precisely positioned attachment hardware in a single, efficient production process.
constraint: The matrix plates and frames must maintain dimensional accuracy and durability across repeated use while allowing rapid engagement and disengagement of the dowels during casting and removal.
mechanism: Reusable mold components with detachably mounted hardware elements are arranged in a modular configuration, allowing precise positioning of attachment features independent of the final product geometry. After material casting and hardening, the mold components are removed, leaving hardware embedded in the cured body. The cured body is then segmented into individual units, and the mold components are disengaged for reuse, decoupling hardware placement from product dimensions.
mechanism_raw: Reusable steel matrix plates with detachably mounted dowels are arranged end-to-end in a mold, with dowels positioned in frames affixed to the plates. After concrete casting and hardening, the plates are removed, leaving dowels embedded in the concrete. The cured body is then cut into individual sleepers, and the frames are disengaged from the dowels for reuse. This decouples hardware positioning from sleeper geometry, enabling mass customization.

abstract: A calculator for determining postage or shipping fees which has a bus-oriented microprocessor structure having several memories, including a read only memory with programmed quadrangles corresponding to geographic areas represented by the three most significant digits of ZIP codes. This memory allows a computation of a distance-related value to be performed for each shipment between a destination ZIP code and an originating ZIP code. The distance-related value is converted to a zone by means of a look-up table. The zone, as well as a carrier selection, define a piece-wise linear curve to be used for fee calculation. Using an equation related to distance and having weight of a parcel defined by a scale, on which the parcel rests, the shipping fee may be calculated. Once the fee is calculated, special services may be added. The calculator may be changed from a calculating mode to a load mode wherein cost and weight numbers are entered by a user to define the break point or end point of linear segments which make up rate curves for each zone for a particular carrier. Each carrier may have different types of service, all having different rate curves for different zones. All may be defined by means of end points and break points for linear segments or complete straight lines with end points.
problem: Calculating shipping fees based on geographic zones and carrier-specific rate structures.
constraint: Balancing computational efficiency with the flexibility to redefine rate curves for multiple carriers and zones without disrupting ongoing calculations.
mechanism: Mapping input data to predefined categories using lookup tables, then applying piecewise functions with user-adjustable parameters to compute results. This allows dynamic configuration of calculation rules for different categories without disrupting ongoing computations.
mechanism_raw: Mapping geographic data (e.g., ZIP codes) to zones via lookup tables, then applying piecewise linear functions defined by user-adjustable breakpoints to compute fees. This allows dynamic rate curve configuration for different carriers and zones.

abstract: Disclosed is a display device including a transparent piezoelectric element having transparent electrodes coated on both surfaces thereof, bonded by transparent adhesive material on an inner surface of a transparent cover to be arranged in front of a display panel of the display device. The transparent cover works as a vibration generator of a sound source. The thickness of the transparent electrodes are selected to serve as an anti-reflection layer of the near ultraviolet light. Relative dimensions of and positional relation between the transparent cover and the piezoelectric element are limited in predetermined ranges to assure high quality of display characteristic and sufficient volume of sound.
problem: Integrating sound generation into a display device without compromising display quality or sound volume.
constraint: Optimizing electrode thickness to satisfy both anti-reflective optical properties and mechanical vibration requirements for sound generation.
mechanism: A component serves dual functions: one part generates sound via vibration while another part provides optical properties. Precise dimensional and positional constraints ensure both functions are optimized simultaneously.
mechanism_raw: Using a transparent cover as a dual-function component: its vibration generates sound while its thickness and electrode coatings serve as an anti-reflective layer. Precise dimensional and positional constraints ensure both optical clarity and acoustic performance.

abstract: An arrangement for calendering bands of paper and like materials has one or more inelastic calendering rollers. Elastically deformable working rollers are associated with the calendering roller or rollers and are movable between operative positions in which they cooperate with the calendering roller or rollers to calender the bands and inoperative positions. Each of the rollers is rotated at a predetermined peripheral speed at which it calenders the bands. At least one of the working rollers has a drive capable of rotating it at a peripheral speed which is a small fraction of the predetermined peripheral speed.
