This working roller serves as a spare and is held in its inoperative position during a calendering operation while being rotated at a lower peripheral speed. When one of the working rollers in use becomes damaged or worn, the spare working roller is accelerated to the speed of the other rollers and is then moved to its operative position in order to assume the function of the damaged or worn working roller. The damaged or worn working roller is simultaneously moved to its inoperative position so that it may be repaired or replaced.
problem: Maintaining continuous calendering operations despite roller wear or damage.
constraint: Minimizing downtime during roller replacement while ensuring mechanical synchronization of speed transitions between active and spare rollers.
mechanism: A redundant system with a standby component that can be accelerated to operational speed and swapped into position when the active component fails, while the failed component is moved to a standby state for repair. Mechanical synchronization ensures smooth transitions between active and standby components.
mechanism_raw: A redundant system where a spare roller is kept in an inoperative position at reduced speed. When a primary roller fails, the spare is accelerated to operational speed and swapped into position, while the damaged roller is moved to an inoperative state for repair.

abstract: A foam-applying nozzle assembly (N) having adjustable flow rates for applying a foam made up from a supply of a foam-forming liquid composition (F) and a flowing liquid stream (W) includes an inner barrel (I) having an axial bore (10) for communicating the liquid stream (W) from a hose. Eductor means (E) with the inner barrel (I) extracts the foam-forming liquid composition (F) from the supply of the foam-forming composition. The eductor means (E) inducts the extracted foam-forming liquid composition (F) into a first portion (W1) of the liquid stream (W) flowing through the eductor means (E). The eductor (E) has a discharge opening (22o) in proximity to the outlet (10m) of the inner barrel (I) for mixing the foam-forming composition (F) with the liquid stream (W) from the inner barrel (I) in proximity to the discharge of the liquid stream, whereby a foam is created. A deflection plate (32) is mounted inwardly and spaced apart of a mixing plate (12) which is mounted substantially perpendicular to the longitudinal axis (A) of the axial bore of the inner barrel (I). The deflection plate (32 ) is formed having slanting ducts (32a) to communicate a second stream portion (W2) to a mixing chamber 13. Ducts (32a) slant at an angle whereby second stream portion (W2) reflects from the mixing plate (12) to a slanted reflection edge (58) of the inner barrel (I).
problem: Efficiently creating foam with adjustable flow rates by mixing a foam-forming liquid with a liquid stream.
constraint: Balancing the timing and pressure of the primary and secondary streams to ensure consistent foam quality while allowing adjustable flow rates.
mechanism: Inducing a secondary fluid into a primary stream using a suction device, combined with a deflection structure that redirects part of the secondary stream to a mixing chamber. This enables controlled mixing with variable flow rates by balancing timing and pressure of the streams.
mechanism_raw: Using an eductor to induct foam-forming liquid into a primary liquid stream, combined with a deflection plate featuring angled ducts that redirect a secondary stream portion to a mixing chamber. This enables controlled foam generation with variable flow rates.

abstract: The present invention relates to an improved toothbrush which permits the user to brush both sides of his teeth at the same time. Through use of the Twin Dental Brush, the user can effectively brush the rear face of each tooth to thereby remove plaque and other unwanted matter from the rear face as well as the front face of the tooth. In addition to permitting effective and efficient cleaning of both sides of a tooth at the same time, the present invention enables the user to effectively clean and remove plaque in a very rapid manner.
problem: Effectively cleaning both the front and rear surfaces of teeth simultaneously.
constraint: Optimizing bristle geometry and spacing to reach both surfaces of teeth in the oral cavity while maintaining user comfort and maneuverability.
mechanism: A tool with opposing contact elements arranged to engage both surfaces of a target during a single motion. The configuration ensures mechanical access to opposing surfaces without requiring repositioning, while optimizing geometry for user comfort.
mechanism_raw: A dual-bristle design arranged to contact both sides of a tooth during a single brushing motion. The bristle configuration ensures mechanical access to opposing surfaces without requiring manual repositioning.

abstract: A bypass valve assembly is disclosed for use with a fluid flow meter of the type having a housing, an inlet, an outlet, a fluid passage which fluidly connects the inlet to the outlet and a flow rate responsive member within the fluid passage. The bypass valve assembly comprises a tubular body open at one end in which is secured to the flow meter housing so that the open end of the tube registers with the flow meter inlet. A valve member is contained within the tube and is urged to a closed position by a helical spring. In its closed position, the valve member directs all of the influent to the flow meter through the passage. When the fluid flow rate into the flow meter exceeds a predetermined amount, the valve member moves to an open position against the force of the helical spring thus bypassing the influent directly to the flow meter outlet.
problem: A fluid flow meter can be damaged or give inaccurate readings when the flow rate exceeds its measurement capacity.
constraint: The spring force must be calibrated so that normal operating flow rates keep the valve closed for accurate measurement, while excessive flow rates overcome the spring to open the bypass; the tradeoff is between measurement accuracy at normal rates and protection at high rates.
mechanism: A pressure-responsive element is automatically displaced by flow-induced pressure when the flow rate exceeds a predetermined threshold, opening a diversion path that bypasses excess fluid directly to the outlet, while a biasing element maintains closure during normal flow so all fluid passes through the measurement device. The biasing element's force is calibrated to balance measurement accuracy at normal rates against protection at high rates.
mechanism_raw: A spring-loaded valve member is automatically displaced by flow-induced pressure when the flow rate exceeds a predetermined threshold, opening a bypass path that diverts excess fluid directly to the outlet, while the spring keeps the valve closed during normal flow so all fluid passes through the meter.

abstract: In the disintegration of a chromite or chromium-containing residue, wherein the chromium-containing material is disintegrated with an alkaline compound in the presence of oxygen and a diluent at a temperature above about 800.degree. C. and thereafter leached, the improvement which comprises pre-roasting the chromium-containing material prior to addition of the alkaline compound. Pre-roasting can be effected at 400.degree. to 1200.degree. C. with addition of certain amounts of silica dioxide and/or aluminum oxide and such additives, depending on the chromium containing material, if still required, are added--prior to disintegration and leaching--in such a quantity to establish a ratio of SiO.sub.2 : AL.sub.2 O.sub.3 of about 2:1 and further a ratio, calculated on the basis of NaOH as the alkaline compound, of SiO.sub.2 : Na.sub.2 O of about 1:0.5 plus a Cr.sub.2 O.sub.3 : Na.sub.2 O ratio of about 1:2 to 1:4. Residues from previous leaching cycles can be present during disintegration as solid diluents but their contents of SiO.sub.2 and/or Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 are not taken into account in calculating the SiO.sub.2 :AL.sub.2 O.sub.3 ratios. The process gives excellent results even with starting materials relatively high in SiO.sub.2 which are difficult to disintegrate to materials of desirable properties by other methods.
problem: Chromium-containing residues are difficult to disintegrate with alkaline compounds, particularly when the starting material is high in SiO2.
constraint: The pre-roasting temperature (400–1200°C) and the additive ratios (SiO2:Al2O3 ≈ 2:1, SiO2:Na2O ≈ 1:0.5, Cr2O3:Na2O ≈ 1:2 to 1:4) must be precisely controlled; the tradeoff is between achieving sufficient chemical modification for disintegration and managing the energy cost and complexity of the high-temperature pre-treatment.
mechanism: The material undergoes a thermal pre-treatment to alter its structural and chemical reactivity before exposure to an alkaline environment, and chemical modifiers are introduced in controlled ratios to establish conditions that enable successful disintegration and extraction. The pre-treatment temperature and modifier ratios are coordinated to balance chemical modification efficacy against energy and process complexity.
mechanism_raw: The material is pre-roasted at high temperature to modify its structure and reactivity before alkaline treatment, and specific additives (SiO2, Al2O3) are introduced in controlled ratios to establish chemical conditions that enable successful alkaline disintegration and leaching.

abstract: A top for a pill or other medicine bottle having an externally threaded upper portion which receives the top. The top includes a cover which defines a recess having an internally threaded section for receiving the externally threaded portion of the bottle. The cover is proportioned for closing the upper portion of the bottle. Indicia in the form of numbers from one to twelve in the preferred embodiment are carried by the cover. A dial member rotatably mounted on the cover is moved by the user to indicate the time when the next dosage of medicine contained in the bottle is to be taken. In another embodiment means are provided to child proof the top such that children cannot inadvertently gain access to the bottle contents.
reason: The patent describes a rotatable dial with time markings mounted on a medicine bottle cap — a straightforward application of a standard mechanical pointer interface to a new context. No novel causal mechanism is disclosed; it is essentially a product feature combination rather than a problem-solving principle.

abstract: An improved envelope tracking and control system for a mail sorting machine of the type which reads a sorting code imprinted on each envelope and deposits the envelope in the proper sorting bin by deflecting a diverter gate associated with the bin. Each diverter mechanism has two sets of photo sensors which sense the presence of an approaching envelope. Tracking circuitry processes the sort code obtained from the envelope and transfers the processed data to the tracking circuit for the next diverter if the data does not coincide with a code that has been preassigned to the diverter. The processed data is held in a latch circuit and is passed on only if the envelope is sensed by the second set of photo sensors. If there is coincidence of the data, a one shot pulse applied to a solenoid deflects the appropriate gate for a predetermined time period that avoids possible damage to the solenoid or to the circuit components. Existing components are used in a self test system which includes an astable oscillator that simulates successive envelopes passing through the machine.
problem: A mail sorting machine must accurately track envelopes through a cascade of diverters and actuate the correct diverter gate without damaging solenoids or misrouting items.
constraint: The timing between the two sensor sets must be calibrated so data is held long enough for confirmation but released promptly, and the solenoid pulse width must be long enough to divert the envelope but short enough to prevent component damage; the tradeoff is between sorting accuracy and mechanical reliability.
mechanism: Each diverter employs sequential sensing elements to detect an approaching item and process its identification code, latching the data and propagating it to subsequent diverters only if a confirmation sensor validates the item's presence and the code does not match the current diverter. When a code match occurs, a timed actuation signal triggers a deflection mechanism for a precisely limited duration to redirect the item without exceeding component stress thresholds.
mechanism_raw: Each diverter has two sets of photo sensors; the first detects an approaching envelope and the tracking circuit processes the sort code, latching the data and passing it to the next diverter only if the second sensor confirms the envelope's presence and the code doesn't match the current diverter. When a code match occurs, a one-shot pulse actuates the solenoid for a precisely limited duration to deflect the gate.

abstract: In a method for compacting compactable soils by vibration while using a compacting apparatus comprising an elongate member having a vibrator mounted on one end thereof, and further having laterally projecting fins arranged along at least part of the length thereof, the elongate member is inserted to a given depth into soil to be compacted and there vibrated to densify and compact soil surrounding said elongate member while withdrawing the elongate member from a compacted location when the load required to lift the elongate member together with the vibrator from said location, while the member is vibrating, is at least equal to a previously established set-point value corresponding to a desired degree of compaction.
problem: Soil compaction must achieve a target density without over-compacting, which wastes energy and may damage the surrounding structure.
constraint: The set-point must be calibrated to the target compaction density for the specific soil type, and the vibration frequency and load measurement must be coordinated so that resistance accurately reflects compaction state; the tradeoff is between achieving sufficient compaction and avoiding unnecessary energy expenditure or over-compaction.
mechanism: A vibrating tool with lateral surfaces is inserted into the material and oscillated to densify it; the resistance force required to extract the tool while it vibrates is continuously monitored, and when this force reaches a set-point value corresponding to the desired compaction level, the tool is automatically withdrawn. The set-point and vibration parameters are coordinated to balance compaction sufficiency against energy expenditure and over-compaction risk.
mechanism_raw: A vibrating tool with lateral fins is inserted into the soil and vibrated to densify it; the resistance force required to lift the tool while it vibrates is continuously monitored, and when this force reaches a set-point value corresponding to the desired compaction level, the tool is automatically withdrawn.

abstract: A tail breaker cam assembly for use with a shrimp processing machine for aiding in the fracturing of the tail of a shrimp from the main shrimp shell, the tail breaker cam assembly including a first, fixed cam member and a second cam member pivotal about the first cam member with a biasing means to urge the pivoting cam member to move in one direction and means for limiting the amount of travel of the pivotable second cam member.
problem: Fracturing the tail of a shrimp from the main shell in a controlled, repeatable manner during automated processing without damaging the rest of the shrimp.
constraint: The biasing force and travel limit must balance between applying sufficient force to fracture the tail while preventing excessive displacement that would damage the shrimp body or fail to cleanly separate the tail.
mechanism: A two-element cooperative cam system where a stationary cam and a pivoting cam work together: a resilient element continuously biases the pivoting cam toward the workpiece to apply fracturing force, while a displacement limiter constrains the maximum pivoting motion, ensuring the force is applied within a controlled range that fractures the target region without over-travel.
mechanism_raw: A two-part cam system where a fixed cam member and a pivotal cam member work together: the biasing means continuously urges the pivoting cam toward the workpiece to apply fracturing force, while the travel-limiting means constrains the maximum pivoting displacement, ensuring the force is applied within a controlled range that fractures the target region without over-travel.

abstract: A needle clamp, fixed at the lower end of the needle bar of a sewing machine. A guide member is provided in the lower portion of the needle clamp locating a sewing needle in a predetermined position in the needle clamp. The guide member has a cylindrical opening in its upper portion coupling with the extreme lower portion of the needle bar and in its lower portion a guide hole whose section has substantially the shape of the transverse section of the needle shank.
problem: Precisely positioning a sewing needle in a predetermined location within a needle clamp that is driven by a reciprocating needle bar.
constraint: The guide must allow the needle to be inserted and the needle bar to rotate while simultaneously constraining the needle's transverse position, requiring the cylindrical upper section to permit rotation but the shaped lower section to prevent lateral movement.
mechanism: A dual-geometry guide member that uses different constraint profiles in different axial sections: the upper cylindrical opening allows rotational coupling with the driving element while permitting axial insertion, and the lower guide hole with a cross-section matching the workpiece's transverse profile constrains the workpiece's lateral position, ensuring precise alignment.
mechanism_raw: A dual-geometry guide member that uses different constraint profiles in different axial sections: the upper cylindrical opening allows rotational coupling with the needle bar while permitting axial insertion, and the lower guide hole with a cross-section matching the needle shank's transverse profile constrains the needle's lateral position, ensuring precise alignment.

abstract: A fluid system (10) having a directional control valve (12) operated by a pilot valve (11) having a manually operable control handle (22) for selectively controlling a fluid motor (14) in positioning a load (17). The pilot valve (11) includes a spool (31) cooperating with associated portions of the pilot valve to provide a pressure regulated pilot signal to the directional control valve during normal operation of the system. Spool (31) includes a recess (98) which is placed in communication with the high pressure portion of the motor cylinder (16) during a dead engine condition by manipulation of handle (22) to provide pressure regulated delivery of the fluid from the motor (14) through recess (98) and to the conduit normally controlling the directional control valve for effecting a controlled lowering or retraction of the load. A single pilot valve is utilized for effecting the pressure regulated control in both normal and dead engine conditions.
problem: Controlling a fluid motor to position a load with pressure-regulated operation during both normal running conditions and dead engine (failure) conditions using a single control valve.
constraint: The single spool must provide both normal pressure regulation and fail-safe pressure regulation through the same physical valve, requiring the recess to be positioned and sized so it can serve as an alternative pressure-regulated path without interfering with normal operation.
mechanism: A single pilot valve spool with a recess that serves dual functions: during normal operation, the spool provides a pressure-regulated pilot signal through its standard cooperation with valve ports; during failure conditions, the recess is placed in communication with the high-pressure portion of the fluid motor, creating an alternative fluid path that delivers pressure-regulated fluid through the recess to the conduit normally controlling the directional valve, enabling controlled lowering or retraction of the load.
mechanism_raw: A single pilot valve spool with a recess that serves dual functions: during normal operation, the spool provides a pressure-regulated pilot signal through its standard cooperation with valve ports; during dead engine conditions, the recess is placed in communication with the high-pressure portion of the motor cylinder, creating an alternative fluid path that delivers pressure-regulated fluid through the recess to the conduit normally controlling the directional valve, enabling controlled lowering or retraction of the load.

abstract: A damper control is provided which extends the control arm to the lintel. It is a support bracket comprised of a first angle which is secured to the lintel and a second angle which is secured to the first by a set collar and screw. A right angle bell crank is pivotally connected to the support bracket. One end of the bell crank is connected by a horizontal connecting rod, adjustable connecting link and upright connecting rod to the damper control arm. A stop projects downward into the path of the control lever to limit its rotational movement.
problem: Transmitting and limiting rotational motion from a control lever to a damper control arm that is positioned away from the control point (extended to the lintel).
constraint: The linkage must transmit sufficient force to control the damper while the adjustable link allows calibration for proper damper positioning, and the stop must limit travel to prevent over-rotation without restricting the necessary control range.
mechanism: A motion-redirecting linkage system where a pivoting lever translates and redirects input motion through a multi-link chain (horizontal connecting rod, adjustable connecting link, upright connecting rod) to a remote output arm. The adjustable link allows calibration of the motion ratio, and a travel stop limits the rotational range of the input lever to prevent over-rotation without restricting the necessary control range.
mechanism_raw: A bell crank pivotally connected to a support bracket, with a multi-link linkage system (horizontal connecting rod, adjustable connecting link, upright connecting rod) connecting one end of the bell crank to the damper control arm. The bell crank translates and redirects the control lever's motion, the adjustable link allows calibration of the motion ratio, and a stop limits the rotational travel of the control lever.

abstract: The improved hoist includes a direct current brake and a control therefor. In the brake control, the AC current is rectified with DC current being sent to the brake solenoid. When the hoist is operating, the brake solenoid is energized to hold the brake in the unactivated position. A timer and power reducer are utilized to reduce the power on the solenoid while the hoist is in operation, thus reducing the energy expended while the hoist is in operation. The operating speed of the brake is increased since less power must be dissipated from the solenoid before the brake can be actuated.
problem: Reducing energy consumption of an electromagnetic brake solenoid during sustained hoist operation while also increasing the speed at which the brake can be actuated when needed.
constraint: The reduced holding power must remain sufficient to keep the brake disengaged during operation, requiring the timer and power reducer to balance energy savings against reliable brake holding, while the reduced power level must still allow rapid release when the brake is commanded to engage.
mechanism: A timed power modulation system that lowers the electrical power delivered to an electromagnetic actuator after initial engagement: when the system is operating, the actuator is initially fully energized to release the brake, then a timer triggers a power reducer to lower the holding power, which simultaneously reduces energy consumption and reduces the amount of power that must be dissipated from the actuator before the brake can be re-actuated, thereby increasing brake operating speed.
mechanism_raw: A timer and power reducer that lower the electrical power delivered to the brake solenoid after initial engagement: when the hoist is operating, the solenoid is initially fully energized to release the brake, then the timer triggers the power reducer to reduce the holding power, which simultaneously reduces energy consumption and reduces the amount of power that must be dissipated from the solenoid before the brake can be re-actuated, thereby increasing brake operating speed.

abstract: Disclosed is a method of reversibly immobilizing sulfate ash at least about 20% of which is sulfates of transuranic elements. The ash is mixed with a metal which can be aluminum, cerium, samarium, europium, or a mixture thereof, in amounts sufficient to form an alloy with the transuranic elements, plus an additional amount to reduce the transuranic element sulfates to elemental form. Also added to the ash is a fluxing agent in an amount sufficient to lower the percentage of the transuranic element sulfates to about 1% to about 10%. The mixture of the ash, metal, and fluxing agent is heated to a temperature sufficient to melt the fluxing agent and the metal. The mixture is then cooled and the alloy is separated from the remainder of the mixture.
problem: Safely immobilizing radioactive sulfate ash containing transuranic elements for disposal or storage.
constraint: The process requires precise temperature control to melt the fluxing agent and metal without causing unintended reactions or structural degradation of the alloy.
mechanism: Introduce a reactive element to form a metallurgical bond with target constituents, reducing their chemical state while a fluxing medium lowers impurity content. Controlled heating enables phase separation between the bonded alloy and residual materials, achieving immobilization through physical isolation.
mechanism_raw: A metal (e.g., aluminum, cerium) is added to form an alloy with transuranic elements, reducing their sulfates to elemental form. A fluxing agent lowers sulfate content, and heating melts the mixture to enable physical separation of the alloy from residual materials.

abstract: A method is provided for semiconductor ribbon-to-ribbon conversion in a rigid edge mode. A combination carrier and mask is provided by which the ribbon is secured during the conversion process. The carrier holds the ribbon and simultaneously masks the edges of the ribbon from the heating effects of an impinging energy beam. The energy beam, such as a laser or electron beam, impinges on the ribbon and creates a molten zone which extends through the thickness of the ribbon. During the growth process, the molten zone is caused to move along the length of the ribbon. The mask prevents melting of the extreme edge portions of the ribbon and thus allows a rapid growth rate and a stable molten zone without sophisticated electronic equipment to gate the energy beam at the ribbon edges.
problem: Controlling molten zone propagation during semiconductor ribbon processing to avoid edge damage and ensure stable growth.
constraint: The mask material must withstand the energy beam's intensity while maintaining structural integrity during the process.
mechanism: Use a protective barrier to shield vulnerable regions of a workpiece from a directed energy source, enabling controlled propagation of a molten zone along a defined path. The barrier maintains structural integrity of non-target areas while eliminating the need for dynamic energy modulation.
mechanism_raw: A carrier/mask combination secures the ribbon and shields its edges from an energy beam (e.g., laser), allowing a molten zone to traverse the ribbon while preventing edge melting. This eliminates the need for complex beam-gating systems.

abstract: Inosiplex has been found to be useful as an anti-inflammatory agent, e.g., to treat rheumatoid arthritis. There is no need to employ known anti-inflammatory agents, e.g., indomethacin or aspirin, with it and, in fact, the anti-inflammatory action of inosiplex is reduced if either of these two drugs are present.
reason: The patent describes a specific compound (Inosiplex) and its anti-inflammatory use, but does not disclose a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a broader problem. The interaction with other drugs is a property of the compound, not a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A sorter for grains, pulses and the like having a perforated sorting plate mounted on a frame and both longitudinally and laterally inclined with respect to the horizontal plane and adapted to be vibrated in the longitudinal direction while being intermittently lifted toward the upper side. The perforated sorting plate overlies an air chamber into which pressurized air is introduced by a blower through an air duct. The perforated sorting plate is provided with a corrugated upper surface to define a multiplicity of ribs oriented in the direction perpendicular to the direction of vibration of the sorting plate and in parallel rows at a pitch not less than the size of the material to be sorted. A set of discharge openings for receiving the sorted material is provided at the lower end of the perforated sorting plate where the ribs terminate. Auxiliary air passages communicating with the space above the sorting plate are provided to permit removal of dust and other granular material of lower specific gravity than the grains being sorted.
problem: Separating granular materials (e.g., grains, pulses) by specific gravity and size using mechanical vibration and airflow.
constraint: The rib pitch must match the material size to prevent clogging while enabling efficient separation of lighter fractions.
mechanism: Apply oscillatory motion to an inclined perforated surface with spatially varying geometry to induce differential particle transport. A fluid stream removes lighter fractions while geometric constraints enforce size-based segregation through selective passage.
mechanism_raw: A vibrated, inclined perforated plate with corrugated ribs oriented perpendicular to vibration direction creates controlled particle movement. Pressurized air and auxiliary passages remove lighter materials, while rib pitch ensures size-based separation.

abstract: A boiler control utilizing a pressure sensor is provided that operates the system in the low fire mode if the load is light and can be satisfied in that mode. If the low fire operation is inadequate to hold the load, and the pressure drops, the boiler is then operated in a modulating mode which includes a high fire limit.
problem: Optimizing boiler operation under varying load conditions to balance efficiency and responsiveness.
constraint: The pressure threshold for switching modes must be calibrated to avoid oscillation between states under fluctuating loads.
mechanism: Monitor system demand via a pressure-responsive sensor and switch between discrete operational states based on a calibrated threshold. This adaptive control balances energy efficiency against response speed while preventing oscillatory behavior under fluctuating conditions.
mechanism_raw: A pressure sensor detects load demand, switching the boiler between low-fire mode (for light loads) and modulating high-fire mode (when pressure drops below a threshold). This adaptive control avoids unnecessary energy use while maintaining system stability.

abstract: The invention concerns a method for controlling a bidirectional stepping motor having two windings and three pole faces. The invention comprises applying current pulses alternately to only one of the motor windings to cause it to rotate in one direction and to only the other of the motor windings to cause it to rotate in the other direction. The invention is used for controlling bidirectional motors which are employed in particular in timepieces.
problem: Controlling the rotational direction of a bidirectional stepping motor efficiently without complex switching between multiple windings.
constraint: Only one winding is energized at a time to avoid interference or conflicting magnetic fields, requiring precise timing and sequencing of pulses.
mechanism: Sequentially energizing one of two actuation elements in a controlled temporal pattern induces directional motion in a multi-pole system, where the spatial arrangement of poles determines the resulting rotational direction.
mechanism_raw: Alternating current pulses are applied selectively to one of two motor windings to induce rotation in a specific direction, leveraging the motor's pole-face configuration to achieve bidirectional control with minimal circuitry.

abstract: An electromagnetic device of the type having a rotor and a stator with magnetically coacting peripheries, with the stator having toothed pole structures, has the stator pole teeth set at nonuniform spacing to improve the operating characteristics of the device. When the device is a stepping motor, improved step accuracy is attained through reduction of residual (or detent) torque. Reduction of airborne noise is reduced in all motor types.
problem: Reducing residual (detent) torque and airborne noise in electromagnetic devices like stepping motors caused by uniform stator pole tooth spacing.
constraint: Spacing must be optimized to balance torque ripple reduction with structural integrity and manufacturing feasibility of the stator.
mechanism: Varying the spatial period of interacting magnetic structures disrupts periodic force variations that produce steady-state torque and acoustic emissions, thereby smoothing output characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Nonuniform spacing of stator pole teeth disrupts periodic magnetic interactions that generate residual torque and noise, smoothing torque output and minimizing acoustic vibrations.

abstract: A system for analyzing destination addresses on pieces of mail transported serially past an optical scan area to determine whether the address is machine imprinted or handwritten. Based on the determination, an output is generated to control sorting the mail into either one grouping with printed or typed addresses (readable by machine) or another grouping with handwritten addresses (unreadable by machine). High intensity lamps are focused on each side of the scan area angled at a predetermined angle to the path of transport of the mail to illuminate the address. Arrays of photocells are positioned in vertical alignments, one array on each side of the transport path. The array on the side of the piece of mail bearing the address is activated by a piece of mail reaching the scan area to cyclically generate signals based on the characteristics of the addresses scanned. The signals are processed to reach the decision as to whether the addresses are imprinted or handwritten.
problem: Automatically distinguishing between machine-imprinted and handwritten addresses on mail for sorting purposes.
constraint: Illumination angle and sensor activation timing must align precisely with mail transport speed to ensure consistent signal quality and classification accuracy.
mechanism: Directional illumination enhances surface feature contrast, while time-aligned sensor arrays capture spatial patterns to classify input based on edge and texture characteristics.
mechanism_raw: High-intensity angled illumination enhances contrast on the address surface, while synchronized photocell arrays capture and process optical signals to classify address type based on edge and texture characteristics.

abstract: A molded pole-type sandpapering tool (10) comprises a molded body member (12) having a flat backing surface (14) for the sandpaper (210) and a handle mounting surface (16) on the opposite side thereof which includes a two-piece resilient molded universal joint (18) to which a molded handle mount (22) is attached and two pairs of spaced apart pheripherally disposed molded contoured guide ramps (200a-200b, 200c-200d) adjacent opposite sides of the universal joint (18) and defining a pair of substantially orthogonally disposed slots (202a-202f) for the universally mounted handle (18) for enabling planar positioning thereof for applying optimum positive pressure to the abrasive surface. The contoured guide ramps comprise sloped contoured surfaces which positively guide the handle (20) on a contoured path between the orthogonal slots during universal movement of the handle (20) substantially in the plane of the abrasive surface (210) while maintaining optimum pressure. A pair of resilient wire spring clips (204, 206) are pivotally mounted to the guide ramps (200a-200d) for removably securing the ends of the sandpaper (210) to the body member (12) to hold the sandpaper (210) against the backing surface (14). The contoured guide ramps (200a-200f) have retention notches (212a-212d) therein for removably locking the spring clips (204, 206) in a sandpaper securing position against the handle mounting surface (16).
problem: Maintaining consistent pressure and planar alignment of an abrasive surface during sanding motions across uneven workpieces.
constraint: The guide ramp geometry must balance flexibility for planar motion with rigidity to maintain pressure, requiring precise contouring to avoid binding or uneven force application.
mechanism: A flexible coupling allows motion in the plane of a working surface, while contoured constraint guides with orthogonal paths maintain consistent pressure distribution across uneven geometries.
mechanism_raw: A two-piece resilient universal joint allows handle movement in the plane of the abrasive surface, while contoured guide ramps with orthogonal slots constrain motion to predefined paths, ensuring optimal pressure distribution.

abstract: A pallet tray for transporting and storing workpieces in an automatic feed system attached to a machine tool includes an elongated metallic base member 1 having a plurality of plastic inserts 2 mounted thereon. Each insert has one or more holding pockets 3 for the individual workpieces. The base member has an inverted U-shaped profile defining a recessed guide groove 7 in the longitudinal direction which cooperates with a guide rail of the workpiece feeding system. With such construction different inserts can be provided to accommodate variously configured workpieces to thereby avoid the separate injection molding of a number of differently dimensioned, complete pallet trays.
problem: Accommodating workpieces of varying shapes and sizes in a pallet tray system without manufacturing entirely new trays for each configuration.
constraint: Inserts must interface mechanically and dimensionally with the base and guide rail system to ensure reliable transport and alignment during automated operations.
mechanism: Interchangeable modular elements with configurable retention features are selectively attached to a standardized base platform, enabling rapid adaptation to varying geometries while maintaining system compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Modular plastic inserts with customizable holding pockets are detachably mounted onto a standardized metallic base, enabling rapid reconfiguration for different workpiece geometries while maintaining compatibility with feeding systems.

abstract: A single integrally injection molded container or compact made of any suitable thermoplastic synthetic polymer composition material has an elongated base assembly which defines a storage compartment and a fully enclosed side compartment in general alignment and communication therewith. A cover is pivotally connected to the base assembly by a first living hinge and is movable from an open position to overlie and close the storage compartment in the base assembly, an end closure is pivotally connected to the base assembly by a second living hinge and is movable from an open position to close the end of the side compartment remote from the storage compartment, the side compartment is provided with bracket means to hold a brush or applicator and when the cover is in the closed position an aligned opening permits the holder of the brush or applicator to extend into and to overlie the storage compartment to enable the brush or applicator to be stored in the container when not in use.
problem: Organizing a brush or applicator and its storage in a compact container while maintaining accessibility and integration.
constraint: Balancing compactness with accessibility, ensuring the brush/applicator can be stored without requiring additional space or separate compartments.
mechanism: Using flexible hinge connections to join a movable cover and end closure to a base structure, with aligned openings that permit an elongated tool to extend into an internal storage region when the cover is closed, enabling combined storage and access through a single closure motion.
mechanism_raw: Using living hinges to connect a cover and end closure to a base assembly, with aligned openings that allow the brush/applicator to extend into the storage compartment when the cover is closed, enabling dual functionality (storage and access) through a single closure action.

abstract: A method of treating aqueous liquid and semi-liquid wastes to render them fit for ultimate disposal in a sedentary mass, by admixing with the waste a solidification agent, encapsulating the admixture before solidification in an elongate, pliable, tubular membrane, sealing the ends of the membrane, and allowing the admixture to set to a sedentary mass.
problem: Safely disposing of aqueous liquid or semi-liquid wastes by converting them into a stable, solid mass for long-term containment.
constraint: Maintaining containment integrity while allowing the solidification process to proceed without mechanical interference or premature rupture of the membrane.
mechanism: Encapsulating a waste-solidification agent mixture within a flexible tubular membrane, sealing its ends, and allowing it to solidify into a stationary mass, thereby isolating the material during the solidification process and preventing leakage or environmental contamination.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating the waste-solidification agent mixture in a pliable tubular membrane, sealing its ends, and allowing it to set into a sedentary mass, which isolates the material during solidification and prevents leakage or environmental contamination.

abstract: A chimney lining system is disclosed, in which a membrane, typically 60 mils thick, of corrosion-resistant alloy material is suspended within an external skeletal frame-work of less-expensive carbon steel. Hangers provide for radial expansion of the liner. However, inward movement of the hangers is restrained. Axially spaced circumferential corrugations located midway axially between where two membrane sections are stiffened, joined and connected to the framework, provide for axial expansion. The external framework is disposed within a tubular concrete chimney column. At several levels, grillages support the external framework from the wall of the chimney column. The structural grillages may bear upon load cells equipped to signal the build-up of sludge on the interior of the liner.
problem: Managing thermal expansion and structural integrity in a chimney lining system exposed to high temperatures and corrosive environments.
constraint: Balancing directional expansion (radial and axial) with structural support to prevent failure while minimizing material costs and maintenance.
mechanism: Suspending a corrosion-resistant membrane within a structural framework using supports that permit radial expansion while restraining inward movement, combined with axially spaced corrugations to accommodate axial expansion, thereby decoupling thermal movement from structural stress.
mechanism_raw: Suspending a corrosion-resistant membrane within a steel framework using hangers that allow radial expansion but restrain inward movement, combined with axially spaced corrugations to accommodate axial expansion, decoupling thermal movement from structural stress.

abstract: A slide valve, in particular the piston of a switching valve, is actuated in both directions of adjustment by a pressure medium which acts on the annular face and/or the circular face of a regulating piston fixed one-sidedly to the slide valve. The equalization of the differing controlling forces, determined by the different sized surfaces of the regulating piston that are subjected to pressure, is achieved by means of a spring or by an hydraulic counterforce.
problem: Actuating a slide valve bidirectionally using a pressure medium while compensating for unequal forces caused by differing piston surface areas.
constraint: Achieving precise force equilibrium to ensure smooth valve operation without over-reliance on external power sources or complex feedback systems.
mechanism: Applying pressure to a regulating piston connected to a sliding valve element, with a resilient or hydraulic counterforce balancing the net force resulting from unequal pressure-exposed surface areas, enabling controlled bidirectional actuation despite force imbalances.
mechanism_raw: Applying pressure to a regulating piston fixed to the slide valve, with a spring or hydraulic counterforce balancing the net force from the unequal pressure-exposed surfaces, enabling controlled bidirectional actuation despite force imbalances.

abstract: Apparatus that offers its users high intensity exercise through a leg operated, rotary motion mode of exercise in which the rotary motion is selectively interrupted so as to allow a beneficial, stand-up, body lifting, method of exercise. The body-lift rotary-motion apparatus includes pedals and cranks in a fixed 180.degree. relationship, a braking mechanism, and controls for operating the braking mechanism to provide that once the "down" pedal has moved past bottom dead center on its way up, it is momentarily braked to provide a step-up platform to permit the user to raise his body as he steps up onto the "up" pedal. In one embodiment, there is a frame to support the user while pedalling in a stand-up position and to hold the pedalling, braking, and control components, with braking accomplished by solenoid applied friction modulated by timers and voltage level controls available to the user to adjust exercise intensity and comfort, these controls being keyed to rotary pedal position by a cam-actuated switch.
problem: Providing a body-lifting exercise through a rotary motion mode while allowing intermittent interruptions to enable stand-up stepping.
constraint: Coordinating braking timing with pedal position to ensure safety and effectiveness, while allowing user-adjustable intensity through modulated controls.
mechanism: Using a braking mechanism triggered by pedal position (via a cam-actuated switch) to momentarily stop the down pedal after bottom dead center, creating a step-up platform that allows the user to lift their body while pedaling in a stand-up position.
mechanism_raw: Using a braking mechanism triggered by pedal position (via a cam-actuated switch) to momentarily stop the down pedal after bottom dead center, creating a step-up platform that allows the user to lift their body while pedaling in a stand-up position.

abstract: A device intended to provide sound reports similar to those occuring when firing with live ammunition when firing small arms. The device is implemented as a magazine which can be fitted to a weapon instead of its ordinary magazine. In the device there is a pressurized gas container (11), e.g. for compressed air, the gas being used to fill a dosing chamber (13) with the aid of a valve means (16,14) actuable by the weapon trigger. The dosing chamber can be opened momentarily so that the compressed air enclosed therein streams out and expands with a report.
problem: Simulating realistic gunfire sounds without live ammunition while maintaining compatibility with standard weapon systems.
constraint: Balancing gas pressure, valve timing, and chamber volume to replicate the transient pressure wave of real gunfire without overcomplicating the mechanical interface.
mechanism: A pressure-actuated release mechanism triggered by a mechanical input controls the sudden discharge of stored energy through a calibrated volume, producing a transient acoustic event that mimics a reference signature.
mechanism_raw: A trigger-actuated valve controls the release of pressurized gas from a dosing chamber, creating a sudden expansion of gas to mimic the acoustic signature of live firing.
residual_terms: ["pressure-actuated release", "mechanical input", "stored energy", "calibrated volume", "transient acoustic event", "reference signature"]

abstract: One or a mixture of compounds of the formula: EQU X--(PX.sub.2 .dbd.N).sub.n --POX.sub.2 wherein X is a halogen atom and n is an integer, usually below about 15 is heated with a suitable phosphorus reactant such as PX.sub.5 ; PX.sub.3 +X.sub.2 ; P+X.sub.2 ; or oligomer of the formula EQU [X--(PX.sub.2 .dbd.N).sub.n --PX.sub.3 ].sup.+ [R].sup.- wherein X is a halogen atom, R is PX.sub.6 or X, and n is an integer usually below about 15; or a mixture of two or more such phosphorus reactants so that a halophosphazene having a --PX.sub.3.sup.+ end group is formed as one of the co-products of the reaction. This co-product is a substance having the general formula EQU [X--(PX.sub.2 .dbd.N).sub.n --PX.sub.3 ].sup.+ [R].sup.- wherein X, R and n are as defined above. The other co-product is phosphoryl trihalide, POX.sub.3. In a second stage the resultant reaction product is heated with at least a stoichiometric amount (preferably, an excess) of a nitrogen source (e.g., NH.sub.3 ; NH.sub.4 Cl; etc.) so that hydrogen halide is evolved and halophosphazene polymer of a suitably high molecular weight is formed.
problem: Producing high molecular weight halophosphazene polymers with controlled end-group functionality.
constraint: Controlling reaction stoichiometry and temperature to avoid side reactions while ensuring sufficient end-group reactivity for the second-stage polymerization.
mechanism: A sequential chemical transformation process uses a first-stage intermediate with a reactive terminal group to enable a second-stage chain-extension reaction via a nitrogen-containing reagent, driving molecular weight growth through controlled stoichiometric addition.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage reaction where a first-stage co-product with a reactive --PX3+ end group enables a second-stage polymerization via nitrogen source addition, driving molecular weight growth through sequential chemical transformations.
residual_terms: ["sequential chemical transformation", "first-stage intermediate", "reactive terminal group", "second-stage chain-extension reaction", "nitrogen-containing reagent", "molecular weight growth", "stoichiometric addition"]

abstract: A rotatable unitary ball valve is provided, comprising, in combination: PA0 (1) a unitary valve housing of plastic material defining a ball valve chamber, intercommunicating first and second fluid ports and first and second fluid passages, and a threaded end connector socket in one passage; PA0 (2) an externally threaded end connector integral with the valve housing, permanently fixed in the end connector socket, and adapted for attachment to a fluid line; and the other fluid passage being adapted for attachment to a fluid line; PA0 (3) a ball valve having a through fluid passage intercommunicating the first and second fluid passages of the valve housing only in the open position of the valve, and disposed in the valve chamber for rotation between open and closed positions; closing off intercommunication between the first and second fluid passages via the ball valve chamber and the ball valve through fluid passage in the closed position, and making such intercommunication in the open position; PA0 (4) at least one sealing means sealingly disposed between the ball valve and the valve chamber wall, maintaining a fluid-tight seal therewith at least in the closed position of the valve; and PA0 (5) means extending to the outside of the valve housing for rotating the valve between open and closed positions.
problem: Creating a durable, fluid-tight ball valve with integrated attachment points for fluid lines while minimizing assembly complexity.
constraint: Material selection (plastic) must balance chemical resistance, thermal expansion, and mechanical strength to maintain sealing under varying operating conditions.
mechanism: A monolithic structural element integrates a flow-control aperture with attachment interfaces, eliminating separable joints, while a conformal sealing surface between a rotating barrier and a fixed chamber wall maintains fluid integrity during rotational actuation.
mechanism_raw: Unitary construction of the valve housing and end connector eliminates mechanical joints, while a sealing interface between the rotating ball and chamber wall maintains fluid integrity during operation.
residual_terms: ["monolithic structural element", "flow-control aperture", "attachment interfaces", "separable joints", "conformal sealing surface", "rotating barrier", "fixed chamber wall", "fluid integrity", "rotational actuation"]

abstract: An improved method for melting silica material in a crucible and drawing off a fused silica tube therefrom having reduced air lines or striations. Bubble formation in the silica melt in the crucible is considerably reduced by supplying the exterior of the crucible with an atmosphere of hydrogen in a carrier gas of argon or certain other noble gases. The fused silica melt is discharged from the crucible around a hollow mandrel and a gas mixture of hydrogen in argon is fed within the hollow mandrel to the interior of the issuing silica tubing while the above atmosphere of hydrogen in argon is passed over the exterior of such silica tubing to form a silica tube product with markedly reduced striations.
problem: Reducing bubble formation and striations in fused silica tubing during crucible melting and mandrel-based extrusion.
constraint: Maintaining precise gas mixture ratios and flow rates to prevent oxidation while ensuring uniform gas distribution across the melt and forming region.
mechanism: A dual-zone inert-reactive gas environment applies a hydrogen-containing atmosphere both externally around a containment vessel and internally within a forming mandrel to suppress nucleation events and stabilize material flow during shaping operations.
mechanism_raw: A hydrogen-containing gas atmosphere (hydrogen in argon) is applied both externally around the crucible and internally within the mandrel to suppress bubble nucleation and stabilize the melt flow during tube formation.
residual_terms: ["dual-zone gas environment", "hydrogen-containing atmosphere", "containment vessel", "forming mandrel", "nucleation events", "material flow", "shaping operations"]

abstract: A novel method for improving the quality of wheat flour, wherein the novelty resides in bringing the wheat flour into contact with a non-equilibrium plasma. The dough prepared from the wheat flour processed by this method exhibits an improved viscoelasticity, and the starch in this wheat flour shows a greater water holding capacity. Appearance and texture of the secondary products from this wheat are also improved remarkably.
problem: Improving viscoelastic properties and water retention in wheat flour for enhanced food product quality.
constraint: Controlling plasma parameters (energy, duration, species concentration) to induce beneficial structural changes without degrading flour components or introducing harmful byproducts.
mechanism: A non-equilibrium reactive species treatment modifies biopolymer molecular structures through controlled exposure to energetic species, altering intermolecular interactions to enhance hydration and mechanical property characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Non-equilibrium plasma treatment modifies starch and protein molecular structures through reactive species interaction, altering cross-linking and hydration behavior to enhance functional properties.
residual_terms: ["non-equilibrium reactive species treatment", "biopolymer molecular structures", "energetic species", "intermolecular interactions", "hydration", "mechanical property characteristics"]

abstract: A building structure including a primary structure, secondary structural members supported on the primary structure, diagonal bracing means connected to and extending obliquely from the primary structure and the secondary structural members to increase the load carrying capacity of the secondary structural members. Bracing means also extend between secondary structural members.
problem: Increasing the load-carrying capacity of secondary structural members in a building structure without redesigning the primary structure.
constraint: The bracing geometry must be positioned to create effective load paths without interfering with the functional use of the structure, and the brace connections must transfer forces reliably at both ends while the overall system remains constructable within standard building practices.
mechanism: Diagonal tension-compression elements are interconnected between primary and secondary structural members to form a triangulated load-transfer network. These elements convert lateral and bending loads into axial forces that structural members resist more efficiently, redistributing loads across multiple parallel paths to stiffen the assembly and increase overall load-carrying capacity without modifying the primary structure.
mechanism_raw: Diagonal bracing elements are connected obliquely between the primary structure and secondary members, as well as between secondary members themselves. These braces convert lateral and bending loads into axial tension and compression forces along the brace length, which structural members handle more efficiently. The triangulated bracing network redistributes loads across multiple load paths, effectively stiffening the assembly and increasing overall capacity.

abstract: A jet-type grinding mill wherein particles are entrained in a circulating gaseous vortex and caused to pulverize each other during their passage through the mill, the mill having a classifier or separator section wherein there are a pair of coaxial tubular nozzles, one within and radially spaced from the other, the two nozzles forming an auxiliary cyclone-type separator means whereby the lightest of the ground particles pass through the inner nozzle as final product while the heavier ground particles are recycled back for further processing.
problem: Separating ground particles by size during jet grinding while recycling oversized particles for further processing, without interrupting the grinding cycle.
constraint: The nozzle diameters, spacing, and gas flow rates must be tuned so that the cyclonic separation force differential matches the particle size distribution, ensuring that only properly sized particles exit while oversized particles are reliably redirected for further grinding.
mechanism: A coaxial flow-field separator creates a centrifugal classification zone within a grinding vortex. Particles entrained in a circulating fluid experience radial force differentials based on mass; lighter particles follow an inner flow path and exit as product, while heavier particles are forced to an outer flow path and redirected back into the grinding zone for additional size reduction. The coaxial arrangement provides continuous size-based separation and automatic recirculation without interrupting the grinding cycle.
mechanism_raw: A pair of coaxial tubular nozzles creates an auxiliary cyclone-type separator within the grinding mill's vortex. Particles entrained in the circulating gas experience centrifugal forces in the cyclonic flow field; lighter particles follow the inner flow path and exit through the inner nozzle as final product, while heavier particles are forced outward and recycled back into the grinding zone for additional pulverization. The coaxial nozzle arrangement provides continuous size-based classification and automatic recirculation.

abstract: An electronic sound generating circuit for an electronic device having standard signal generator including a first audio frequency signal generating circuit generating a first audio frequency signal, a second audio frequency signal generating circuit generating a second audio frequency signal having a frequency which differs from said first audio frequency signal, a mixing circuit mixing said first audio frequency signal and said second audio frequency signal to provide a mixed signal, and a tone generating circuit generating an audible tone in response to said mixed signal.
problem: Generating a selectable audible tone in an electronic device using standard signal generation circuitry.
constraint: The two input frequencies must differ by an amount that produces a beat frequency within the desired audible range, and the mixing circuit must preserve the difference frequency component while suppressing unwanted harmonics or noise that could distort the output tone.
mechanism: Two signals with different frequencies are generated independently and combined in a mixing stage. The mixing produces sum and difference frequency components; the difference frequency (beat frequency) is selected as the output tone. By varying the frequency difference between the two input signals, different audible tones are produced. A selection stage isolates the difference frequency component while suppressing unwanted harmonics or noise.
mechanism_raw: Two audio frequency signals with different frequencies are generated independently and then mixed together. The mixing process produces sum and difference frequencies; the difference frequency (beat frequency) falls within the audible range and is selected as the output tone. A tone generating circuit then converts this mixed signal into an audible sound. By varying the frequency difference between the two input signals, different audible tones can be produced.

abstract: The apparatus forms fiberboard hollow ducts from fiberboard and comprises means for collapsing or partially collapsing the fiberboard into a flat collapsed fiberboard or partially collapsed fiberboard for advancing the collapsed or partially collapsed fiberboard through a preheating and heating stage while heat sensitive tape is applied to the linear seam of the advancing fiberboard. After tape is applied, means for applying pressure and cooling operate to permanently set the tape.
problem: Forming fiberboard into hollow duct shapes with a sealed longitudinal seam, using heat-sensitive tape as the seam closure method.
constraint: The heating temperature must be sufficient to activate the heat-sensitive tape without damaging the fiberboard, and the pressure and cooling must be applied at the correct timing and intensity to ensure the tape bonds permanently while the fiberboard retains its formed shape.
mechanism: A sheet material is collapsed into a flat configuration for advancement, then passed through a forming and sealing station. Heat-activated closure material is applied to a linear seam where duct walls will join. Simultaneous pressure and cooling are applied to permanently set the closure material, creating a sealed longitudinal seam that maintains the hollow duct shape. The preheating and heating stages activate the closure material without damaging the base material.
mechanism_raw: The fiberboard is first collapsed or partially collapsed into a flat or semi-flat configuration for easy advancement. As the advancing collapsed board passes through a preheating and heating stage, heat-sensitive tape is applied to the linear seam where the duct walls will join. After tape application, pressure and cooling are applied simultaneously to permanently set the tape, creating a sealed seam that maintains the hollow duct shape.

abstract: A method is described for the production of composite materials from layers of wood veneer and fibres bonded together and impregnated with resin. The method includes the steps of (a) impregnating at least one layer of reinforcement fibres with a first resin, (b) coating surfaces of at least one layer of wood veneer with a second resin, (c) stacking the at least one resin impregnated reinforcement fibre layer with the at least one layer of resin coated wood veneer and (d) bonding the layers together under conditions of pressure and temperature appropriate to the resins employed in step (a) and step (b) to produce a laminate. Examples of composites are given using carbon fibres and hard wood veneers together with properties thereof.
problem: Producing a composite material that combines the properties of wood veneer with reinforcement fibers, using a single lamination process despite the different material characteristics of each layer.
constraint: The pressure and temperature conditions must be compatible with both resin systems—high enough to cure both resins effectively but not so extreme as to degrade either the reinforcement fibers or the wood veneer, and the layer stacking sequence must ensure proper resin distribution and interlayer adhesion.
mechanism: Reinforcement layers are treated with a first bonding agent optimized for fiber adhesion, while veneer layers are treated with a second bonding agent optimized for wood adhesion. The treated layers are stacked in a predetermined sequence and bonded together under controlled pressure and temperature conditions compatible with both bonding agents simultaneously. This co-curing process creates a unified laminate where each bonding agent performs optimally for its respective substrate while the layers are integrally bonded.
mechanism_raw: Reinforcement fibers are impregnated with a first resin optimized for fiber bonding, while wood veneer layers are coated with a second resin optimized for wood adhesion. The resin-impregnated fiber layers and resin-coated veneer layers are then stacked and bonded together under controlled pressure and temperature conditions that are appropriate for both resin systems simultaneously. This co-curing process creates a unified laminate where each resin type performs optimally for its respective substrate while the layers are integrally bonded.

abstract: The present invention is directed to an improved clip and supporting rack therefor. The clip is constructed with rigid outwardly diverging arms to eliminate the need to force the stamp handle through a throat, and does not require spring loading. Furthermore, the clip easily accommodates stamps having handles of numerous sizes and shapes. One embodiment of supporting rack is free standing and provides circular clip supports forming storage bins for small items such as paper clips and the like. The load from the clips and stamps on the supports is carried down through a central post. Another embodiment of rack is adapted to be straight and wall mounted with spaces provided to permit snap-on of the clips.
problem: Creating a clip that can be easily attached to stamps of various sizes without requiring spring loading or forcing through a throat.
constraint: Balancing rigidity of the arms to maintain structural integrity while allowing flexibility to accommodate various handle sizes.
mechanism: Use rigid diverging structural elements that flex to accommodate varying external dimensions while maintaining positional stability through inherent stiffness, eliminating the need for separate biasing components.
mechanism_raw: Rigid outwardly diverging arms that allow the clip to self-adjust to different handle sizes and eliminate the need for springs.

abstract: Water-soluble disazo compounds of the formula (1) ##STR1## and diamino compounds serving as starting compounds (tetrazo components), of the formula (4) ##STR2## in which the formulae moieties occurring twice, namely Z, K and X, in each case have a meaning identical to one another and the groups Z are bonded to the two benzene nuclei in each case in the ortho- or in each case in the para-position relative to the ethylenedioxy substituent, and the azo groups or amino groups and the groups Z in the benzene nuclei are in each case bonded in the meta-position relative to one another and K is the radical of a coupling component containing a sulfato, carboxy or sulfo group, X denotes a hydrogen atom or a fiber-reactive group and Z is a group of the formula --SO.sub.2 --CH.dbd.CH.sub.2 or --SO.sub.2 --CH.sub.2 --CH.sub.2 --Y in which Y denotes a radical which can be eliminated in aqueous medium under alkaline or acidic conditions or the hydroxy group. Disazo compounds of the formula (1) can be used as dyestuffs having fiber-reactive properties for dyeing, for example, cellulose fiber material and wool and be prepared by tetrazotizing diamines of the formula (4) and coupling with coupling components evident from the formula (1). Diamino compounds of the formula (4) are obtained by acetylating a 1,2-di-(o- or p-aminophenoxy)-ethane, chlorosulfonating this bis-acetylamino compound and reducing the sulfonyl chloride groups to sulfinic acid groups, which are then oxyethylated to give .beta.-hydroxyethylsulfonyl groups, which, after deacetylation of acetylamino groups, can be converted in a manner which is in itself known into one of the abovementioned groups Z, for example into the .beta.-sulfatoethylsulfonyl group by means of a sulfating agent.
problem: Creating water-soluble disazo compounds with fiber-reactive properties for dyeing cellulose and wool.
constraint: Precise positioning of substituents (ortho, para, meta) on the benzene nuclei to ensure the desired chemical reactivity and solubility.
mechanism: Apply a sequence of chemical transformations to introduce specific reactive functional groups at defined positions on molecular frameworks, enabling targeted interaction with substrate materials through controlled substituent placement.
mechanism_raw: A sequence of chemical modifications (acetylation, chlorosulfonation, reduction, oxyethylation, deacetylation) to introduce specific functional groups (e.g., β-sulfatoethylsulfonyl) that enable fiber reactivity.

abstract: An insulating material for an insulated article and a method for making same are provided. The article comprises goose down or similar insulation, together with an excess of submicron finely divided hydrophobic particulate metal or metalloid oxide pigment contained in an envelope. The envelope is tightly woven (or similar) fabric which is permeable to gas, but retains the pigment. An envelope having good breathability and, hence, dryability is provided together with improved insulation and resistence to water penetration and absorption. In addition, the envelope may be compressed when not in use and still recover its loft thereafter when the pressure is released.
problem: Providing an insulating material that is breathable, water-resistant, and compressible yet retains loft.
constraint: Balancing the envelope's permeability to gas with its ability to retain the particulate and maintain structural integrity under compression.
mechanism: Combine a loft-retaining fibrous matrix with hydrophobic particulate dispersed within a gas-permeable containment structure to balance thermal resistance, moisture management, and mechanical integrity under compression.
mechanism_raw: Combining goose down with submicron hydrophobic particulate in a gas-permeable envelope to enhance insulation and water resistance while allowing breathability.

abstract: Apparatus for the production of fixed point multifilament yarns with a whirling unit provided with a passage (15) through which the filaments to be whirled are driven and whirled together as at least one blasting nozzle injects gas into said passage. To obtain high filament feed rates and provide for the desired fixed points the blasting nozzle is in the form of a De Laval nozzle (20) whose jet is directed at an angle or perpendicularly to the longitudinal direction of the passage (15).
problem: Producing fixed-point multifilament yarns with high filament feed rates.
constraint: Optimizing the nozzle design and gas jet direction to achieve efficient whirling without damaging the filaments.
mechanism: Direct a high-velocity fluid stream through a converging-diverging flow channel at an oblique angle relative to filament movement, inducing controlled rotational motion to achieve rapid and stable filament positioning.
mechanism_raw: Using a De Laval nozzle to direct a gas jet at an angle or perpendicular to the filament passage, creating controlled whirling for high feed rates and fixed points.

abstract: A metal or metal compound coating 6 is deposited on a face of a hot, freshly formed ribbon 1 of glass during the ribbon's forward travel through a coating station 5 between a forming installation 3 and an annealing lehr 4 by contacting the ribbon face with fluid coating precursor material e.g. sprayed from nozzle 17. Preparatory to the coating step, the ribbon 1 is passed through successive thermal conditioning zones comprising a zone 19 in which temperature gradients across the ribbon are reduced and a following zone in which heat is supplied substantially entirely to a surface layer of the glass at the face to be coated by exposing that face to one or more radiant heaters 22 having a black body temperature below 1100.degree. C. to compensate at least partially for the cooling effect of the coating step on the ribbon 1.
problem: Coating a hot glass ribbon without causing excessive cooling during the coating process.
constraint: Maintaining precise temperature control to prevent thermal stress and ensure uniform coating adhesion.
mechanism: Pass a thermally sensitive substrate through staged temperature regulation zones to minimize thermal gradients, while applying directed radiant energy to counteract localized cooling during surface treatment.
mechanism_raw: Passing the ribbon through thermal conditioning zones to reduce temperature gradients and using radiant heaters below 1100°C to supply heat to the surface layer, compensating for cooling from the coating step.
residual_terms: ["staged temperature regulation zones", "directed radiant energy", "thermal gradients"]

abstract: A drum-shaped grate of an incinerator includes a plurality of cylindrical drums, the grate covering of which is formed of a plurality of suspended middle grate bars which are combined in segments and arrested by fixed grate bars. The adjacent grate bars in the circular direction are suspended on bar carriers and the lateral faces of each two adjacent grate bars are spaced from each other by spacers. The surfaces of the spacers positioned between each two adjacent grate bars and abutting against each other are flat and smooth. Due to a possible relative displacement of the middle grate bars in their longitudinal direction owing to the placing of the spacers between the adjacent bars a clogging of the air slots formed between the grate bars would be prevented.
problem: Preventing clogging of air slots in an incinerator grate caused by thermal expansion or movement of grate bars during operation.
constraint: Balancing the need for airflow through the grate with the structural support required to maintain the grate's shape under thermal and mechanical stress.
mechanism: Elements with low-friction, planar interfaces are positioned between adjacent structural members to permit controlled relative longitudinal displacement while preserving structural integrity. This displacement prevents particulate accumulation from obstructing airflow through gaps between the members.
mechanism_raw: Spacers with flat, smooth surfaces are placed between adjacent grate bars, allowing controlled relative longitudinal displacement of the bars while maintaining structural integrity. This displacement prevents particulate buildup from blocking airflow through the slots.

abstract: A manipulator for rotatably moving a test specimen in an ultra-high vacuum chamber includes a translational unit movable in three mutually perpendicular directions. A manipulator frame is rigidly secured to the translational unit for rotatably supporting a rotary shaft. A first copper disc is rigidly secured to an end of the rotary shaft for rotary movement within the vacuum chamber. A second copper disc is supported upon the first disc. The second disc receives a cryogenic cold head and does not rotate with the first disc. A sapphire plate is interposed between the first and second discs to prevent galling of the copper material while maintaining high thermal conductivity between the first and second discs. A spring is disposed on the shaft to urge the second disc toward the first disc and compressingly engage the interposed sapphire plate. A specimen mount is secured to the first disc for rotation within the vacuum chamber. The specimen maintains high thermal conductivity with the second disc receiving the cryogenic transfer line.
problem: Preventing galling (adhesive wear) between two copper discs in a high-vacuum, cryogenic environment while maintaining high thermal conductivity between them.
constraint: Selecting a material that simultaneously satisfies the conflicting requirements of low friction (to prevent wear) and high thermal conductivity (to enable cryogenic cooling).
mechanism: A material with high thermal conductivity and low friction is interposed between two moving surfaces and compressed by a biasing element. The material provides a wear-resistant interface that allows relative motion without adhesive wear, while maintaining heat transfer between the surfaces.
mechanism_raw: A sapphire plate is interposed between the rotating and stationary copper discs, compressed by a spring. The sapphire provides a low-friction, wear-resistant interface that allows relative motion without galling, while its high thermal conductivity maintains heat transfer between the discs.

abstract: This method involves the deposition of free metal atoms (4) from the apex (5) of a pointed tip (1) supported at a distance of 10 to 20 nm from a substrate (2). The atoms (4) are being field-desorbed under the influence of a strong electric field existing between the tip (1) and the substrate (2). With the tip (1) being moved across the substrate (2), a narrow trace (6) of metal atoms will be deposited on the substrate.
problem: Precisely depositing free metal atoms onto a substrate to form narrow conductive traces for microelectronic or nanoscale devices.
constraint: Maintaining the tip-substrate distance within a narrow range (10–20 nm) to ensure sufficient electric field strength for desorption while avoiding physical contact that would damage the tip or substrate.
mechanism: A strong electric field is generated between a pointed element and a surface, desorbing material from the element's apex via field-induced emission. The element is scanned across the surface, depositing desorbed material in a controlled pattern as the field's spatial modulation is governed by the element's position.
mechanism_raw: A strong electric field is generated between a pointed tip and a substrate, field-desorbing metal atoms from the tip apex. The tip is scanned across the substrate, depositing atoms in a controlled trace pattern as the field-induced desorption is spatially modulated by the tip's position.

abstract: A capsize prevention device for a multihull vessel which may be mounted to an existing vessel or be integrally manufactured therewith.
