The device includes first and second tubes disposed longitudinally along the lower portion of the keel of the vessel through which seawater flows during the sailing of the vessel. Each of the tubes includes forward and rearward watertight valves. When the valves are open, water is free to flow through the tubes. When the valves are closed, water will be trapped within the tubes, thus adding the mass of the trapped water to the keel. The mass of the water within the tubes serves to prevent capsize about one of the outriggers of the vessel.
problem: Preventing capsizing of a multihull vessel by dynamically adjusting the vessel's center of gravity and stability.
constraint: Balancing the need for rapid, selective ballast adjustment with the requirement to maintain watertight integrity and avoid adding excessive weight during normal operation.
mechanism: A system of watertight chambers along the vessel's keel incorporates controllable valves to selectively admit or retain fluid. Closing the valves adds mass to the keel, lowering the center of gravity and increasing the righting moment to resist capsizing.
mechanism_raw: Longitudinal tubes along the keel contain watertight valves that can be opened to allow seawater flow or closed to trap water. Closing the valves adds mass to the keel, lowering the center of gravity and increasing righting moment to resist capsizing.

abstract: A push key and blade-receiving cartridge are provided for removing, inverting and reinserting an injector blade into a razor. Preferred embodiments of the cartridge include pivotally mounted guides for separating the clamping members of a razor head and guiding the razor head into position with respect to the cartridge.
reason: The patent describes a specific mechanical tool for razor blade handling with pivotally mounted guides, but does not disclose a generalizable causal mechanism beyond conventional mechanical guidance and clamping. The solution is highly application-specific with no clear underlying principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: In a staking machine for staking leather, skins or furs a rotatable work roll carrying staking blades or grindstones is arranged against a flexible pressing device with an adjustable gap. A workpiece is pulled through the gap by a rotary feed roll and a rotary clamping roll also arranged at an adjustable clearance. The workpiece is fed through the gap between the feed roll and the clamping roll when the feed roll cooperates with the clamping roll.
problem: Achieving controlled staking of leather/skins/furs by balancing pressure application and material movement through a processing gap.
constraint: Balancing pressure and feed rate to avoid over-processing or misalignment while maintaining consistent material throughput.
mechanism: A system with adjustable pressure application and material transport that dynamically balances force and movement to process materials without damage, using coordinated control of gap geometry, feed rate, and clamping to maintain consistent throughput while preventing over-processing.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable gap between a work roll (with blades/grindstones) and a flexible pressing device, combined with coordinated rotary feed and clamping rolls with independent adjustable clearances. This allows dynamic control of material path, pressure distribution, and feed rate to perform staking without damaging the workpiece.

abstract: Apparatus for growing hollow tubular crystalline bodies from the melt includes, in a preferred embodiment, a capillary die of the desired shape, a seed holder having a cross section of similar shape and to which a plurality of elongate seeds may be attached, and an inner after heater of substantially similar shape but smaller size supported from the die by an inner radiation shield.
problem: Growing hollow tubular crystalline bodies with precise shape and structural integrity from a melt.
constraint: Maintaining uniform temperature and shape fidelity during growth to prevent defects or uneven crystallization.
mechanism: A thermal shaping system that uses a mold to define geometry, a nucleation point to initiate crystallization, and controlled heating to maintain temperature gradients for structured growth, ensuring uniform solidification direction and shape fidelity.
mechanism_raw: Using a capillary die to define the outer shape of the melt, a seed holder with matching cross-section to initiate crystallization, and an inner after heater (shielded by radiation shields) to maintain temperature gradients. This combination controls solidification direction and thermal profile to grow structured crystals.

abstract: A phosphor having formed on its surface generally spherical or semi-spherical surface treating substance composed of silicon dioxide, an aluminum compound and a zinc compound, at least 70% by weight of the surface treating substance being in the form of particles having an average particle size within a range of from 60 to 300 m.mu.m.
problem: Enhancing phosphor performance (e.g., light emission efficiency or durability) through surface modification.
constraint: Achieving at least 70% of particles within the specified size range while maintaining the required chemical composition for optimal surface interaction.
mechanism: A surface treatment process using particles with controlled size distribution and chemical composition to alter surface characteristics for improved performance, where particle morphology and composition modify interaction properties.
mechanism_raw: Applying a surface treating substance composed of silicon dioxide, aluminum, and zinc compounds in spherical/semi-spherical particles with controlled size distribution (60–300 mμm). The particle morphology and composition modify surface properties to improve functional performance.

abstract: A clock has a face comprising a rigid base layer, an overlaying layer of resilient padding and an enveloping film layer. The clock movement may be conveniently supported from the face, the sounding board effect of the base layer being diminished by the foam layer. The base may formed of hardboard or the like, the film layer providing both a decorative and protective function therefor.
problem: Reducing the sounding board effect (unwanted vibration/resonance) in a clock face while maintaining structural and functional integrity.
constraint: Selecting foam thickness and material properties to sufficiently dampen vibrations without compromising the clock's structural support or aesthetic function.
mechanism: A multi-layered damping system with a rigid base, resilient intermediate layer, and protective outer layer to absorb vibrations while maintaining structural integrity, where the intermediate layer dissipates energy without reintroducing resonance.
mechanism_raw: Layering a rigid base (e.g., hardboard) with a resilient foam padding and an enveloping film. The foam layer dampens vibrations from the base layer, while the film provides protection and decoration without reintroducing resonance.

abstract: This invention reveals a steel wire element useful in the reinforcement of rubber articles in which the steel wire is provided with an adhesive coating comprising a ternary brass alloy containing about 55 percent to about 75 percent by weight copper, about 15 to about 45 percent by weight zinc, and about 0.1 to about 10 percent by weight iron. Preferably this ternary brass alloy will contain about 1 to 5 percent by weight iron. The ternary alloy may be formed by sequentially electroplating layers of copper, iron and zinc followed by heating to promote the diffusion of the copper, iron and zinc layers. The steel wire elements of this invention are useful in the reinforcement of vehicle tires, power transmission belts, conveyor belts, hoses, and the like.
problem: Improving adhesion between steel wires and rubber matrices in reinforced articles (e.g., tires, belts).
constraint: Optimizing the alloy composition (e.g., 1–5% iron) and diffusion process to ensure uniform bonding without compromising wire strength or rubber compatibility.
mechanism: A coating process involving sequential deposition of metal layers followed by diffusion to form an alloy that enhances adhesion between materials, creating a metallurgical bond through controlled composition and thermal activation.
mechanism_raw: Forming a ternary brass alloy coating (Cu-Zn-Fe) on steel wires via sequential electroplating of copper, iron, and zinc layers, followed by heating to promote interdiffusion. The resulting alloy creates a metallurgical bond that enhances adhesion to rubber during vulcanization.

abstract: With a cylinder saw arranged rotatably in a machine frame, only circular profiles are sawed out of boards and beams. This cylinder saw possesses a toothed arrangement, at least on the front side, and is rotatably supported by support and guide rollers in the machine frame. The outside circumference of the cylinder saw is embraced by a continuous, driven belt. A planing fixture is arranged behind the device for sawing out circular profiles with the aid of the cylinder saw and with this planing fixture any desired concave, convex or straight profile shapes can be milled into circular wooden pieces or boards. The planing fixture consists of four profile planing shafts arranged uniformly distributed on the outer circumference, the axes of which are adjustable relative to the longitudinal central axis of the wooden beam to be processed.
problem: Cutting circular profiles from boards and milling variable concave, convex, or straight profiles on wooden pieces.
constraint: Balancing adjustability of planing shafts to achieve diverse profiles while maintaining structural support and alignment.
mechanism: Combine a rotating cutting tool with a driven belt for circular profile generation, and arrange adjustable planing elements around a central axis to mill variable profiles via positional adjustment of their axes.
mechanism_raw: Combining a cylinder saw with a driven belt for circular cutting and adjustable planing shafts arranged around the circumference to mill desired profiles via positional adjustment of their axes.
residual_terms: ["rotating cutting tool", "driven belt", "adjustable planing elements", "central axis"]

abstract: An extrusion die for a ceramic honeycomb structure having a plurality of different wall thicknesses and at least two through-hole comprises discharge slots corresponding to the cross-sectional shape of the ceramic honeycomb structure and feed passageways formed in communication with said discharge slots. The hydraulic diameters of the feed passageways which communicates with discharge slots which result in thinner wall in the honeycomb structure are comparatively larger than the hydraulic diameters of the feed passageways which communicate with discharge slots which result in thicker walls in the honeycomb structure. The invention can also include a replaceable perforated plate attached on inlet portions of the feed passageways of an extrusion die. The completely novel extrusion die is suitable for use in obtaining a ceramic honeycomb structure having at least two difference types of wall thicknesses and defining through-holes of complex shapes.
problem: Uneven flow distribution in an extrusion die causes inconsistent wall thickness when forming a ceramic honeycomb structure with multiple wall thicknesses and complex through-hole shapes.
constraint: The hydraulic diameter of each feed passageway must be precisely tuned to the flow characteristics of its corresponding discharge slot and wall thickness, balancing flow resistance against throughput to maintain uniform extrusion pressure and avoid defects such as thickening, thinning, or incomplete filling.
mechanism: Each feed channel is assigned a hydraulic diameter that is inversely related to the material volume required at its corresponding discharge outlet: channels feeding outlets that produce thinner sections have larger hydraulic diameters, and channels feeding outlets that produce thicker sections have smaller hydraulic diameters. This differential sizing compensates for the varying flow resistance and flow demand of each discharge path, balancing the material flow rate across all outlets so that each section receives the correct amount of material despite geometry differences, thereby maintaining uniform extrusion pressure and avoiding defects such as thickening, thinning, or incomplete filling.
mechanism_raw: Feed passageways are sized with hydraulic diameters that are inversely related to the desired wall thickness at their corresponding discharge slots: larger hydraulic diameters feed slots that produce thinner walls, and smaller hydraulic diameters feed slots that produce thicker walls. This compensates for the differing flow resistance and flow demand of each discharge path, balancing the material flow rate across all slots so that each wall receives the correct amount of material despite the geometry differences.
residual_terms: ["hydraulic diameter", "flow resistance", "flow rate", "discharge outlet", "extrusion pressure", "feed channel", "material volume"]

abstract: The combination of an electric furnace and a slag retaining pouring spout thereon in registry with a modified tap hole is disclosed. The tap hole located in one end of the electric furnace communicates with the interior thereof and the slag retaining pouring spout is positioned on the electric furnace and in communication with the tap hole. The slag retaining pouring spout is angled upwardly and outwardly with respect to the tap hole and positioned above of the molten metal and slag in the operating electric furnace and receives molten metal from the electric furance when the same is tilted to pour the molten metal through the tap hole. The slag retaining pouring spout has a secondary tap hole therein normally closed with a consumable plug during the operation of the electric furnace and the early tap of the molten metal therefrom into the slag retaining pouring spout. A lever arm on the pouring spout carries a plate forming a gate for the secondary tap hole and a circular Argon delivering shroud is positioned around the secondary tap hole. The combination acts to deliver only slag-free molten metal, such as steel, from the electric furnace.
problem: Delivering only slag-free molten metal (e.g., steel) from an electric furnace while retaining slag and preventing re-oxidation during pouring.
constraint: The mechanism depends on the density difference between slag and molten metal, and the secondary tap hole must be positioned at the correct height relative to the slag-metal interface; the consumable plug, gate, and argon shroud must all function reliably at high temperatures.
mechanism: Density-based phase separation with controlled outlet positioning and inert atmosphere protection: when a vessel containing two immiscible phases of different density is tilted, the denser phase flows toward a first outlet positioned below the interface level, while the less-dense phase collects at an upper region. A secondary outlet positioned at a height corresponding to the interface level allows the denser phase to exit while retaining the less-dense phase. A controllable barrier at the secondary outlet regulates flow initiation and cessation, and an inert gas curtain surrounding the secondary outlet prevents atmospheric interaction with the exiting denser phase.
mechanism_raw: Density-based separation using an angled spout: when the furnace is tilted, molten metal and slag enter the spout; the upward/outward angle causes less-dense slag to collect at the upper end while denser molten metal flows to a secondary tap hole positioned below the slag level. A gate and consumable plug control the secondary outlet, and an inert gas (argon) shroud around the secondary tap hole prevents atmospheric contamination of the exiting metal.

abstract: A prefabricated building unit is formed as an integrally moulded body of fibre-reinforced concrete. The body has a wall, a beam extending along the top or bottom of the wall, and a floor or roof extending from the beam perpendicularly to the wall at the bottom or top thereof respectively. The beam is reinforced by reinforcing bars extending there along and an elongated reinforcing member extending helically around the reinforcing bars.
problem: Creating a structurally sound prefabricated building unit that integrates wall, beam, and floor/roof elements into a single molded body with adequate reinforcement.
constraint: The helical reinforcement must be properly positioned around the longitudinal bars to provide optimal confinement without interfering with the integral molding process, and the fiber-reinforced concrete must cure uniformly around all reinforcement elements.
mechanism: Integrated reinforcement architecture combining axial tension members with circumferential confinement elements: primary load-bearing elements aligned along the principal stress direction provide tensile strength, while a secondary element extending helically around the primary elements applies radial compression to the surrounding matrix material. This helical confinement enhances multi-directional strength, shear resistance, and structural stability by maintaining intimate contact between the matrix and all reinforcement elements within a unified molded structure.
mechanism_raw: Combining longitudinal reinforcement bars (providing primary tensile load-bearing capacity along the beam axis) with a helically extending reinforcing member that wraps around the longitudinal bars. The helical wrapping confines the concrete and bars, providing multi-directional strength, shear resistance, and stability, all integrated into a single fiber-reinforced concrete molded body.

abstract: A plug for closing the opening in the bottom of a top pouring ingot mold is comprised of a preformed plug body having top and bottom ends and an outer peripheral surface providing a contour generally corresponding with that of the mold opening to be plugged. The lower portion of the outer peripheral surface is provided with a coating of a thermally curable sealing composition having a heavy paste-like consistency, and the plug body and coating are enclosed in a heat shrinkable plastic film. In use, the plug is pushed into a plug opening in the bottom of an ingot mold which generally is hot from a previous casting operation, the plastic film disintegrates, the sealing material is squeezed so as to spread and fill the space between the mold opening and plug body, and the heat of the mold cures the sealing material to secure the plug in place and seal the peripheral space between the plug body and mold opening.
problem: Sealing the opening in the bottom of a hot ingot mold to prevent metal leakage during casting, using the mold's residual heat to activate the sealing mechanism.
constraint: The sealant must have the right consistency to flow under pressure when the film disintegrates but cure to a strong seal; the mold must be sufficiently hot to disintegrate the film and cure the sealant, and the timing of film disintegration and sealant curing must be coordinated with plug insertion.
mechanism: Thermally triggered sequential sealing process: a removable protective barrier enclosing a flowable sealing material is selectively removed upon exposure to elevated temperature from a heated surface. The released sealing material is then displaced by mechanical insertion pressure to fill an annular gap between an inserted plug and a receiving opening. Residual thermal energy from the heated surface then induces a curing transformation in the sealing material, establishing a durable seal that prevents leakage through the opening.
mechanism_raw: Heat-activated multi-stage sealing: a protective heat-shrinkable film enclosing a paste-like thermally curable sealant disintegrates when exposed to the hot mold surface; the sealant is then squeezed by insertion pressure to flow and fill the annular gap between the plug body and mold opening; residual mold heat cures the sealant in place, creating a secure, durable seal.

abstract: A manually operable needle threading device comprises a housing having a recess for positioning the eye of a needle to be threaded in alignment with the path of a displaceable thread pusher member in the housing, whereby displacement of the pusher member from a retracted to an extended position pushes a portion of a thread between the needle and pusher member through the needle eye. The pusher member displaces the portion of thread between gripping fingers on the housing which hold the thread portion upon displacement of the pusher member from the extended to the retracted position. The portion of thread remains attached to the threading device upon separation of the needle therefrom until a loose end of the thread passes through the needle eye to complete the threading operation, after which the thread portion is released from the threading device. In one embodiment the housing is of pistol-like configuration facilitating handling and operation of the threading device.
problem: Threading a needle by manually pushing a thread through the needle eye, with controlled gripping and release of the thread.
constraint: The pusher extension, gripping finger engagement, and release mechanism must be precisely coordinated so that the thread is pushed through the eye, gripped during retraction, and released only when the loose end has passed through; the housing geometry must align the needle eye with the pusher path.
mechanism: Coordinated reciprocating advancement with selective gripping and timed release: a linearly actuated pusher element advances to propel a flexible filament through an aperture in a workpiece. Gripping elements engage the filament during pusher retraction, maintaining filament position relative to the workpiece. The gripping elements selectively disengage only after a predetermined filament length has passed through the aperture, ensuring complete threading without premature release or slippage during the reciprocating cycle.
mechanism_raw: Reciprocating pusher with coordinated gripping fingers: the pusher extends to push a thread portion between the needle and pusher through the needle eye; gripping fingers on the housing then hold the thread as the pusher retracts; the thread remains gripped until a loose end passes through the eye, at which point the gripping fingers release the thread, completing the threading operation.

abstract: Metal oxides are applied to the surface of urea particles and chemically bonded to the urea by a heat-induced reaction. The product of this reaction is a free-flowing, relatively non-hygroscopic nitrogenous chemical fertilizer. By selecting metal oxides corresponding to a particular soil deficiency, beneficial micronutrients can be supplied simultaneously with nitrogen. Other materials, such as elemental sulfur, can be incorporated into the metal oxides prior to coating or can be liquefied and applied as a separate additional coating to the metal oxide-urea particles. In another embodiment, fertilizer particles are coated with metal oxides, covered with molten urea, and heated to induce a reaction. The formed reaction product remains as a layer on the exterior of the particle.
problem: Creating a free-flowing, non-hygroscopic nitrogenous fertilizer that can simultaneously deliver tailored micronutrients based on specific soil deficiencies.
constraint: The heat-induced reaction must create a stable chemical bond between the metal oxide and urea without degrading the urea core; the coating thickness and composition must be controlled to maintain the desired release profile and nutrient delivery while preserving the free-flowing, non-hygroscopic properties.
mechanism: Thermally induced chemical bonding for functional coating formation: reactive coating materials are applied to discrete core particles and chemically bonded via heat-induced reaction, forming a stable exterior layer. This layer serves dual functions: providing a protective barrier that reduces moisture absorption and enhances flow characteristics, and acting as a delivery matrix for beneficial agents. The coating composition can be selectively varied to match specific environmental or nutritional requirements while maintaining the core particle's structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Heat-induced chemical bonding to form a functional coating layer: metal oxides are applied to urea particles and chemically bonded via heat-induced reaction, forming a stable layer on the particle exterior that acts as both a protective barrier (reducing hygroscopicity and improving flowability) and a delivery vehicle for beneficial micronutrients; the metal oxide composition can be selected to match specific soil deficiencies.

abstract: Magnetic devices are described which include a sheet of magnetic material having a relieved groove/ridge configuration, all the grooves and ridges being straight and parallel, and evenly spaced apart. Such devices can form part of apparatus for use in connection with a dry transfer sheet in assisting setting out a correctly spaced and aligned legend on a desired receptor surface. The apparatus can comprise a base member which, e.g. may be attachable to a designed receptor surface and a sheet-holder member. The sheet-holder member can consist of a bar to which a sheet of dry transfer material may be attached. One side of the bar of the sheet-holder member has a rib which may engage in the base member in one of the parallel grooves therein. The lateral spacing of the parallel grooves and the vertical spacing of lines of letters on the dry transfer sheet correspond to ensure accurate horizontal alignment of letters transferred from different rows on the transfer sheet to the final receptor. Convenient transfer sheet layouts are described.
problem: Accurately aligning letters transferred from different rows on a dry transfer sheet to a receptor surface without manual adjustment.
constraint: Grooves and ridges must remain straight, parallel, and evenly spaced to maintain alignment accuracy while allowing smooth movement of the transfer sheet.
mechanism: A structured surface with parallel elements whose spacing matches the pitch of discrete features on a movable sheet, enabling automatic alignment through lateral movement of the sheet across the surface.
mechanism_raw: Matching the lateral spacing of parallel grooves in a magnetic base member to the vertical spacing of letter rows on the transfer sheet, ensuring automatic horizontal alignment when the sheet is moved across the grooves.

abstract: In the manufacture of a flared ferromagnetic annular core for a television deflection unit in which a moulding (13) consisting of compressed starting material is supported in a hollow holder (11) having an inclined inner wall (12) on which a considerable part of the flared outer surface of the moulding (13) bears during sintering. Allows compression and expansion of the moulding to take place.
problem: Allowing compression and expansion of a flared ferromagnetic core during sintering without damaging the molding or losing structural integrity.
constraint: The inclined wall must balance support for the molding during sintering with sufficient clearance to accommodate dimensional changes without inducing stress fractures.
mechanism: A support structure with an angled internal surface that provides radial clearance for dimensional changes during a thermal process while maintaining contact pressure against a component during deformation.
mechanism_raw: Using a hollow holder with an inclined inner wall that supports the molding during sintering while permitting radial movement caused by thermal expansion or compression.

abstract: A portable cephalostat is shown as having a frame-like base subassembly which provides for an area upon which a patient's head is to rest and a support for supporting locating arms which serve to locate the patient's head in a selected position; the base subassembly provides for the placement of a first film, to be exposed, below the patient's head and for the placement of additional film, also to be exposed, generally to one side of the patient's head and generally parallel to the mid-sagittal plane of the patient's head; and a dial indicator is provided for, upon attaining the desired location of the patient's head, automatically indicating the elevation of the axis of the patient's auditory canals with respect to the first film.
problem: Automatically indicating the elevation of a patient's auditory canal axis relative to a reference film during head positioning for medical imaging.
constraint: The system must remain portable while maintaining mechanical precision to ensure accurate elevation readings without manual recalibration.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage connecting a positioning device's adjustable arms to a displacement sensor, translating relative movement of the arms into a direct readout of vertical alignment.
mechanism_raw: Linking a dial indicator to the locating arms of the cephalostat so that movement of the patient's head directly translates to a mechanical readout of the auditory canal axis elevation.

abstract: A color-developing ink containing at least one color developer selected from the group consisting of phenolic resins, aromatic carboxylic acids and metal salts thereof as well as a higher chain ether having total carbon atoms of 10 to 40, has various advantages such as the density of the developed image is high, fading of the developed image with time is at a low level, blurring of the developed letters is also at a low level, there is no abnormal tinting by the developed image, there is no swell of rubber rolls of a printer, and printability on a printer is excellent.
reason: The patent describes a chemical composition (ink formulation) optimized for specific print quality metrics. The mechanism is a material-level solution (chemical interactions between components) rather than a functional process or system that can be abstracted and applied to other fields.

abstract: A steering system including a first member, and a second member movable relative to the first member, and a hydraulic assistance device comprising a valve portion including a first valve port, and a second valve port. The valve portion communicates with a fluid pressure source and a hydraulic cylinder assembly, and is connected to the first member and movable in response to movement of the first member relative to the second member for selectively supplying fluid from the fluid pressure source to the second valve port and for transmitting fluid to the hydraulic cylinder assembly from the first valve port in response to movement of the first member in one direction relative to the second member, and for supplying fluid from the fluid pressure source to the first valve port and for transmitting fluid to the hydraulic cylinder assembly from the second valve port in response to movement of the second member in the opposite direction relative to the first member. The hydraulic assistance device further includes a slave hydraulic cylinder assembly communicating with the first valve port and the second valve port, connected to the second member, and movable in response to movement of the first member relative to the second member for supplying fluid to the first valve port and receiving fluid from the second valve port in response to movement of the first member in the one direction relative to the second member, and for supplying fluid to the second valve port and receiving fluid from the first valve port in response to movement of the first member in the opposite direction relative to the second member.
problem: Providing bidirectional hydraulic assistance in a steering system to amplify driver input forces regardless of the direction of steering movement.
constraint: The valve must switch fluid paths instantaneously and reliably in response to bidirectional input without cross-contamination or delay in pressure transmission.
mechanism: A bidirectional flow control system that reverses fluid communication paths between a pressure source and an actuator in response to opposing directional inputs, enabling force amplification in both directions.
mechanism_raw: A valve portion that reverses fluid flow paths between a pressure source and a hydraulic cylinder based on the relative movement direction of the steering members, enabling assistance in both clockwise and counterclockwise steering.
residual_terms: ["bidirectional flow control", "fluid communication paths", "pressure source", "actuator", "directional inputs"]

abstract: An inertial air cleaner characterized by comprising an intake pipe, a first air chamber, a second air chamber, a third air chamber, a first funnel-shaped air disturber, a second funnel-shaped air disturber, a first dust chamber, a second dust chamber and an exhaust pipe, and being capable of making the intake smoke or air with carbon rotate therein, and effectively removing the carbon particles by centrifugal force without need of any filtering materials.
problem: Efficiently removing particulate matter (e.g., carbon) from intake air or smoke without relying on disposable filtering materials.
constraint: Balancing airflow throughput and rotational velocity to maximize particle separation efficiency while minimizing pressure drop and avoiding clogging of the dust chambers.
mechanism: Inducing a controlled vortical flow regime within a multi-stage chamber system to generate centrifugal acceleration that displaces particulates radially outward from a moving fluid stream. Sequential chamber geometry and internal flow disruptors amplify rotational velocity, directing separated particles to dedicated collection zones while maintaining continuous fluid throughput.
mechanism_raw: Creating a controlled rotational airflow path through a series of interconnected chambers and funnel-shaped disturbers, which induces centrifugal force to separate particles from the air stream. The sequential chamber geometry and disturber shapes amplify rotational velocity, forcing particles outward against chamber walls for collection in dedicated dust chambers.

abstract: An anodic assembly immersible in a fluoborate electrolytic bath in an electroplating process for plating tin and similar metals. The assembly is constituted by a cylindrical basket containing a replenishable pile of solid pieces of the plating metal, the basket being formed by a perforated carbon tube closed at its bottom by a carbon plug. The outer surface of the tube is impregnated with a resin acting as a reinforcing skin to prevent cracking when the tube is drilled to create the required perforations.
problem: Maintaining structural integrity of a perforated container (e.g., a carbon tube basket) during drilling operations without cracking, while allowing replenishable solid plating metal pieces to remain contained.
constraint: Selecting a resin material that provides sufficient mechanical reinforcement without compromising the electrical conductivity of the carbon tube or interfering with the electroplating process.
mechanism: Applying a reinforcing material layer to a perforated structural substrate to absorb mechanical stresses during high-force operations. The material layer acts as a compliant buffer that prevents crack propagation through the substrate while maintaining open pathways for fluid or ionic transport through the perforations.
mechanism_raw: Impregnating the outer surface of the carbon tube with a reinforcing resin skin that acts as a structural buffer. The resin skin absorbs mechanical stresses during drilling, preventing crack propagation while the perforations allow electrolyte and metal ion flow for electroplating.

abstract: An instantaneous desired cutting position of a milling cutter or circular saw blade in a mobile apparatus for cutting hard materials, such as a concrete highway surface, is maintained even if the mobile apparatus travels over irregular or slanted surfaces. For this purpose the saw blade position is adjustable either by varying the position of the saw blade mounting in a machine frame or by varying the position of the entire machine frame. The position correction is accomplished by a sensor which produces control signals for a position correction power drive in response to pendulum movements which represent cutter or blade deviations from the desired cutting position. The position of the entire machine frame may be varied by raising or lowering a wheel remote from the cutter or blade. Thus, a binding or jamming of the cutter or blade is prevented.
problem: Maintaining a consistent cutting position of a blade or cutter on a mobile apparatus when traversing uneven or slanted surfaces, to prevent binding or jamming.
constraint: Ensuring the sensor-actuator feedback loop responds quickly enough to surface variations while maintaining precise positional control under dynamic cutting loads.
mechanism: Implementing a gravitational reference sensor coupled to a feedback-controlled actuator system. The sensor detects positional deviations of a cutting element relative to a target plane, generating corrective signals that drive the actuator to adjust either the cutting element's orientation or the supporting structure's elevation, dynamically compensating for surface irregularities.
mechanism_raw: Using a pendulum-based sensor to detect deviations in the cutter's position relative to the desired cutting plane. The pendulum's movement generates control signals that drive a power actuator to adjust either the blade's mounting position or the entire machine frame's elevation, dynamically compensating for surface irregularities.

abstract: A pen-like instrument for dispensing correction fluid comprising an elongate housing, a bag of thin flexible polymeric film material containing correction fluid within a cavity in the housing, and an applicator tip assembly comprising a body secured to the housing and the bag and having a through opening through which the correction fluid is dispensed when an applicator member positioned within the through opening separated from a lip on the body against the bias of a spring.
problem: Controlling the dispensing of correction fluid from a pen-like applicator without leakage or unintended flow during storage or transport.
constraint: Balancing spring force and applicator geometry to ensure reliable sealing under varying temperatures and fluid viscosities while allowing smooth dispensing on demand.
mechanism: Establishing a normally-closed fluid interface maintained by a resilient biasing element. Applied pressure overcomes the biasing force to displace a sealing member from a mating surface, creating an open flow path. Removal of pressure allows the biasing element to restore the sealing member to its original position, reestablishing a leak-tight closure.
mechanism_raw: A spring-biased applicator member is held in sealing contact with a lip on the dispenser body. When pressure is applied to the fluid bag, the applicator member is forced away from the lip against the spring bias, opening a flow path. Removing pressure allows the spring to reseat the applicator, resealing the system.

abstract: Apparatus for controlling the working stoke of the hydraulic props of a mine roof support unit is disclosed. The control apparatus comprises a control valve whose input side is connected to a hydraulic pressure line, and whose output side is connected to a working chamber of each of the props via a respective supply line. A sequence valve is provided in the supply line leading to one of the props. The sequence valve is such as to open the associated supply line when subjected to a predetermined hydraulic pressure, this predetermined hydraulic pressure being at least approximately equal to the hydraulic pressure necessary to overcome the resistance to the working stroke of another of the props. The sequence valve has a tubular valve body, a valve closure element mounted within the valve body, and a valve seat positioned within the valve body. A spring is provided for biassing the valve closure element towards the valve seat. A control piston carries the valve seat, the control piston having a piston face which, when subjected to hydraulic pressure in the biassing direction of the spring, is effective to displace the control piston so as to move the valve seat away from the valve closure element, thereby opening the sequence valve.
problem: Coordinating the working strokes of multiple hydraulic props in a mine roof support unit to ensure sequential or synchronized operation based on pressure thresholds.
constraint: Calibrating the sequence valve's pressure threshold and spring bias to match the operational resistance of the props, ensuring reliable sequential activation without premature or delayed triggering.
mechanism: Configuring a pressure-responsive valve assembly with a spring-biased closure element and a hydraulically actuated control member. When upstream pressure exceeds a calibrated threshold (corresponding to resistance in a secondary system), the control member displaces the closure element from its seat, enabling fluid communication to a downstream actuator. This establishes a pressure-dependent sequencing relationship between multiple actuators.
mechanism_raw: A sequence valve with a spring-biased valve closure element and a hydraulically actuated control piston. When pressure in the supply line reaches a threshold (corresponding to overcoming resistance in another prop), the control piston displaces the valve seat away from the closure element, opening the valve and enabling flow to the associated prop. This creates a pressure-dependent sequencing mechanism.
residual_terms: ["pressure-responsive valve assembly", "spring-biased closure element", "hydraulically actuated control member", "pressure threshold"]

abstract: A garment is constructed from flexible and joined panels, such as waterproofed cloth panels. The garment has a top portion, a bottom portion and a foldable lengthening panel which is folded once and hidden behind the bottom portion when the garment is shortened. The foldable lengthening panel extends completely around the garment and a long zipper also extends completely around the garment. One side of the zipper is attached to the lower edge of the bottom portion and the other side of the zipper is attached to the upper edge of the bottom portion or the lower edge of the lengthening panel.
problem: Adjustable garment length while maintaining structural integrity and concealment of the adjustment mechanism.
constraint: Balancing adjustability with the need to hide the lengthening panel and maintain a continuous waterproof seal around the garment.
mechanism: A foldable extension element is integrated with a full-perimeter fastening system that connects both the main garment portion and the extension element. The extension element is positioned behind the main portion when in a shortened configuration, and the fastening system enables length adjustment by selectively exposing or concealing the extension element, maintaining a continuous seal around the garment perimeter throughout the adjustment range.
mechanism_raw: A foldable lengthening panel, hidden behind the bottom portion when shortened, is integrated with a full-perimeter zipper. The zipper's attachment to both the bottom portion and the lengthening panel allows the garment to be shortened by folding the panel into a concealed position, enabling length adjustment without compromising the garment's form or waterproofing.

abstract: A machine for manufacturing foam building blocks (39) and the like wherein a plurality of two-piece forming molds (21) are continuously moved by a conveyor mechanism along a closed path-of-travel (22) is disclosed. Filling, curing and injection stations (31, 32 and 33) are located along the path-of-travel (22). As a mold (21) enters the filling station (31), the nozzle (37) of a foam gun (35) enters a hole (34) in the top of the mold (21) and moves with the mold (21) as that mold continues to move along the path-of-travel (22). At the end of the filling station (31), after the foam gun (35) has injected a suitable amount of resin, curing and foaming agent materials into the mold (21), the nozzle (37) rises from the hole (34). Thereafter, a cap-latch (36) is moved into a hole closed position. In addition to closing the hole (34), the cap-latch (36) forms one of two latches that latch the two mold pieces (21a and 21b) together. The other latch (38) is located on the opposite side of the forming molds (21). After leaving the filling station (31), the forming molds pass through the curing station (32) where they are heated to a suitable temperature. After leaving the curing station (32), the forming molds (21) enter the ejection station (33) where the latches (36, 38) are opened, the forming mold pieces (21a and 21b) are split apart and the finished foam block (39) is ejected. Then, the forming mold pieces (21a and 21b) are brought back together and the latch (38) is closed. Thereafter, the forming molds (21) are moved to the filling station (31) and the cycle is repeated.
problem: Continuous, synchronized filling, curing, and ejection of foam blocks in a manufacturing line without interrupting mold movement.
constraint: Maintaining mold integrity and sealing during continuous movement while coordinating multiple operations (filling, latching, curing, ejection) on a moving conveyor.
mechanism: A dispensing element moves in coordination with a containment vessel along a transport path during material introduction. A dual-function closure mechanism simultaneously seals the vessel's filling aperture and joins the vessel's components together. This combined sealing and joining action maintains vessel integrity during processing and discharge phases, enabling continuous cycling of vessels through multiple operational stations without interrupting transport movement.
mechanism_raw: A nozzle moves in tandem with the mold along a conveyor path during filling, then a cap-latch simultaneously closes the mold's filling hole and latches the two mold halves together. This dual-function latch ensures the mold remains sealed and intact during curing and ejection, enabling uninterrupted cycling of the molds through the process stations.

abstract: A slitter mechanism for use in a double fold bottomer apparatus employed in making bags from starting flush cut tubes is described which gives precise, high speed side marginal tube slitting in order to permit subsequent downstream gluing and folding operations. In preferred forms, the slitter mechanism includes a bag-end separating assembly having a vacuum manifold and a cooperating adjacent deflector bar serving to separate end portions of the sidewalls of a moving tube. A sequentially rotatable blade is also provided which first enters the open end of the moving tube between separated wall portions, overtakes and slits the leading side margin of the tube, and then stops with a trailing slitting edge situated within the tube open end; subsequent bag movement causes the trailing tube side margin to engage and be slit by the stationary blade edge.
problem: Precise, high-speed slitting of moving tubes for downstream folding/gluing operations without damaging the material.
constraint: Achieving high-speed operation while maintaining precise alignment and avoiding material deformation during slitting.
mechanism: A separation mechanism creates an opening between flexible material layers using differential pressure and a deflecting element. A cutting tool enters the created opening to sever the leading edge, then retracts with its trailing edge positioned within the material. Subsequent material movement causes the trailing edge of the material to engage the stationary cutting tool, completing the separation through sequential cutting action in a single pass.
mechanism_raw: A vacuum manifold and deflector bar separate the tube's sidewalls, creating an open gap. A rotating blade enters the separated gap, slits the leading edge, and stops with its trailing edge inside the tube. Subsequent tube movement causes the trailing edge to engage the stationary blade, completing the slit. This sequential blade action ensures both leading and trailing edges are cut efficiently in one pass.

abstract: The adjustment provides for three degrees of freedom, in which in addition to varying the distance of the rolls from the rolling axis an adjustment axis is provided generally parallel to the rolling axis and about which the roll mount can be tilted. This adjustment axis itself may also be tilted for changing the speeding of the rolls.
problem: Precisely adjusting the position, tilt, and speed of rolls in a rolling apparatus to accommodate varying material requirements.
constraint: Balancing the complexity of multi-axis adjustments with the need for precise, repeatable control in industrial rolling operations.
mechanism: Three independent degrees of adjustment are provided: (1) varying the radial distance of processing elements from the central axis, (2) tilting the mounting system about an axis parallel to the central axis, and (3) adjusting the orientation of the adjustment axis itself to control rotational velocity. This multi-axis system enables independent control of element positioning, angular orientation, and rotational speed to optimize material processing parameters.
mechanism_raw: Three degrees of freedom are provided: (1) varying the distance of the rolls from the rolling axis, (2) tilting the roll mount about an axis parallel to the rolling axis, and (3) tilting the adjustment axis itself to control roll speed. This multi-axis adjustment system allows independent control of roll positioning, angling, and rotational speed to optimize material processing.

abstract: A heated sand spreader apparatus has an inclined elongated screw conveyor mounted at the rear end of a mobile chassis for receiving and conveying sand in a rearward direction along a spiraling path. A plurality of heat generators are attached to the conveyor for directing heat on the sand grains moving within the conveyor. The grains are heated to such a degree that upon subsequent contact with ice on a road surface the grains will melt the ice and deposit in it. After the ice refreezes the grains form a granular surface on the ice. The apparatus includes a broadcast-type spreader supported from the auger conveyor which receives heated sand therefrom and is operated to uniformly broadcast the sand grains on the road surface at the rear of the mobile chassis.
problem: Efficiently heating and uniformly spreading granular material (e.g., sand) to melt ice and create a traction surface on roadways.
constraint: Ensuring consistent heating of sand grains without clogging the conveyor or spreader, while maintaining uniform distribution across the road surface.
mechanism: An inclined conveying system transports granular material while integrated heating elements raise the material temperature during transit. A distribution mechanism receives the heated material and disperses it uniformly across a target surface. The heated particles interact with surface conditions upon contact, then undergo phase change to form a textured traction layer with enhanced surface friction properties.
mechanism_raw: An inclined screw conveyor transports sand rearward while heat generators attached to the conveyor heat the grains during transit. A broadcast spreader, supported by the auger, receives the heated sand and distributes it uniformly on the road surface. The heated grains melt ice on contact, then refreeze to form a granular traction layer.

abstract: A disturbance alarm comprising a hollow tubular case having upper and lower electrical contact plates fixedly positioned therein. A pendulum assembly includes a lower weight which rests upon the flat upper surface of the lower contact plate, an upper weight and a rigid shaft fixed to the weights and spacing the weights from each other. The upper electrical contact plate encircles the pendulum shaft and is adapted to make electrical contact therewith to close an electrical circuit through an alarm device. A collar is slidable within the case for clamping the lower weight onto the contact plate such that the pendulum is balanced thereon out of electrical contact with the upper contact plate. A magnet encircles the pendulum shaft adjacent to the upper weight for attracting and holding the pendulum in electrical contact with the upper plate when such balance is disturbed and an alarm condition is thereby detected.
problem: Detecting mechanical disturbances (e.g., vibrations or tilting) in a stable system.
constraint: The system must remain stable under normal conditions (balanced pendulum) while reliably triggering an alarm when external forces disturb the equilibrium.
mechanism: A balanced element maintains a stable state through equilibrium, and a disturbance disrupts this balance, triggering a switch via a magnetic attraction to close a circuit.
mechanism_raw: A pendulum is balanced on a contact plate using a clamping collar, maintaining electrical isolation. When a disturbance disrupts this balance, a magnet attracts the pendulum into contact with an upper plate, closing an alarm circuit.

abstract: Fish and crustacean bait consisting essentially of (a) from about 5 to about 50 wt. % of a water insoluble polymer having a melting point below about 110.degree. C. (e.g., polyamides and copolymers of ethylene with at least one ethylenically unsaturated comonomer); (b) from about 45 to about 95 wt. % of fish meal; and (c) from 0 to about 20 wt. % of fish oil.
reason: The patent describes a composition of materials (polymer, fish meal, oil) without explaining a causal functional relationship or mechanism for how the components interact to solve a problem.

abstract: A high-frequency oscillator including an oscillation circuit (1) having a quartz crystal (X) and an amplifying element (Q.sub.2), a power amplifying circuit (3) for amplifying the output of the oscillation circuit, and a control system (Q.sub.7, 6) for varying a bias voltage of the amplifying element to thereby control the output power of the power amplification circuit. The control system comprises an FET (Q.sub.7) connected at the drain thereof to the amplifying element, and a control circuit (6) for applying a control signal to the gate of the FET.
problem: Controlling the output power of a high-frequency oscillator while maintaining stable oscillation.
constraint: The control system must dynamically adjust the bias without destabilizing the oscillation circuit or introducing unwanted noise.
mechanism: A feedback control system dynamically adjusts a bias parameter of an amplifying element in response to a control signal, modulating output power while maintaining oscillation stability.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control system uses an FET connected to the amplifying element to adjust its bias voltage in response to a control signal, thereby modulating the output power of the power amplification circuit.

abstract: An internal combustion engine has n member of cylinders, a piston in each cylinder connected to a crankshaft (2), each piston being in phase or out of phase with the others by A.degree. or a multiple thereof (A=720/n), cams for actuating inlet and exhaust valves to each cylinder, and a cam drive mechanism (5) which rotates the cams in phased relationship with the crankshaft (2) to open the valves in sequence for a desired angle of rotation of the crankshaft. The cam drive mechanism also includes means for combining the rotational movement of the cams with a phased oscillatory movement of the camshaft (3) and cams of variable amplitude about the axis of rotation at a frequency f times the crankshaft frequency so that over the period which the valves are opened and/or their timings variable, f has the following values: PA1 f=2n when the number of cylinders n=1; PA1 f=n or n/2 when n=2; PA1 and f=n/2 when n=3 or more. The selection of the frequency of the oscillations allows all the cams to be mounted on the same camshaft.
problem: Achieving variable valve timing in an internal combustion engine with multiple cylinders while minimizing mechanical complexity.
constraint: The oscillatory motion must be precisely synchronized with the crankshaft rotation to ensure proper valve timing across all cylinders without mechanical interference.
mechanism: A drive mechanism combines rotational motion with a phased oscillatory motion of variable amplitude, synchronized to a reference frequency, enabling adjustment of timing across multiple components on a single shaft.
mechanism_raw: The cam drive mechanism combines the rotational movement of the camshaft with a phased oscillatory motion of variable amplitude, synchronized to the crankshaft frequency, enabling all cams to be mounted on a single shaft while adjusting valve timing.

abstract: Bayer process liquors derived from the digestion of bauxites with a caustic solution are purified by removing at least a portion of the organic impurities present in the liquors. Removal of these impurities is accomplished by treating liquor containing dispersed therein solids generated by the Bayer process or added thereto, such as red mud particles, alumina trihydrate, oxalate salt, or filter aid with an organic polymeric, water-soluble cationic quaternary ammonium salt (POLYQUAT salt) which due to its cationic nature will adhere to the surface of the dispersed solids. The organic coating or layer adhered to the solids provides a receptive surface for the organic impurities, thus allowing formation of a solid-Polyquat-organic Adduct which is easily removed from the Bayer system.
problem: Removing organic impurities from Bayer process liquors during alumina production.
constraint: The polymer must selectively bind to solids without interfering with the Bayer process chemistry, while the adduct must remain separable from the liquor phase.
mechanism: A charged polymer selectively binds to dispersed solids, creating a charged surface that attracts and binds impurities, forming a removable solid-polymer-impurity complex.
mechanism_raw: A cationic quaternary ammonium polymer adheres to dispersed solids (e.g., red mud, alumina trihydrate), forming a charged surface that attracts and binds organic impurities, creating a removable solid-Polyquat-organic adduct.

abstract: A steam generator for burning a normally-solid fuel which produces non-combustible solid residues, including, an elongated combustion chamber, a fuel introduction means to introduce fuel adjacent the axis of the combustion chamber as a centrally-disposed stream moving in a downstream direction, a combustion-supporting gas introduction means for introducing the gas as an annular, rotating stream about the fuel stream and which, together with the fuel introduction means forms a rotating, toroidal vortex of the fuel and the combustion-supporting gas moving in a downstream direction. The combustion chamber has a volume sufficient to burn all of the fuel and, together with the fuel introduction means and the combustion-supporting gas introduction means, cause the vortex to collapse and form plug flow thereafter. Water introduction means introduces water into the flue gas at the downstream end of the combustion chamber as a plurality of peripherally-arranged jets. Preferably the water is introduced from the vena contracta of a nozzle-type orifice. A vaporization chamber, coupled to the combustion chamber, has a volume sufficient to vaporize a major portion of the water to steam and a separator separates solid residues from the flue gas-steam mixture.
problem: Efficiently combusting solid fuels with non-combustible residues while managing heat transfer and solid separation in a steam generator.
constraint: Balancing vortex stability and collapse timing to avoid residue buildup while maintaining sufficient combustion chamber volume for complete fuel burnout.
mechanism: Generating a rotating flow structure of fuel and combustion gas to enhance mixing and combustion, then transitioning the flow to a linear regime to ensure complete burnout. Introducing a fluid medium at a constricted flow region to maximize phase-change efficiency, followed by separating solid particulates from the gas stream.
mechanism_raw: Creating a rotating toroidal vortex of fuel and combustion gas to enhance mixing and combustion, then collapsing the vortex into plug flow to ensure complete burnout. Water is introduced as peripheral jets at the vena contracta to maximize vaporization efficiency, followed by solid-gas separation.

abstract: A scalloped stream of paper sheets is intermittently transported from a feeding unit to a reservoir wherein one portion of a flexible elastic band convolutes the sheets around a core. The sheets are then transported over a switchover device and onto another portion of the band which convolutes the sheets around a hub while the core pays out the one portion of the band. If the sheets are needed at one or more consuming stations, the hub pays out the other portion of the band and the switchover device directs successive sheets from the other portion of the band to a removing unit. The switchover device and the one portion of the band define a first station where the sheets arriving from the feeding unit reach the one portion of the band and where the sheets leave the one portion of the band on their way to the other portion of the band. The other portion of the band and the switchover device define a second transfer station. The elasticity of the band is such that its length is increased by at least 0.1% in response to the application of a tensional stress of at least 0.25 kg/mm.sup.2 .
problem: Intermittently transporting and storing flexible sheet materials (e.g., paper) between feeding and consumption stations without continuous mechanical drive.
constraint: Maintaining band elasticity (≥0.1% elongation under ≥0.25 kg/mm² stress) to ensure reliable winding/unwinding without slippage or material damage.
mechanism: Using an elastic tensioning element to convolutely wind flexible sheets around a core, combined with a path-switching mechanism that redirects material flow between storage and delivery routes. The elasticity enables dynamic tension adjustment during transfer operations.
mechanism_raw: Using an elastic band with controlled tension to convolutely wind sheets around a core/hub, combined with a switchover device that redirects sheet flow between storage and delivery paths. The elasticity allows dynamic tension adjustment during transfer.

abstract: A method of backing carpeting material 19 with hot-melt compositions such as atactic polypropylene or bitumen comprises carefully doctoring selected thicknesses of the composition to the undersurface of the material 19 with the wear surface of the material uppermost. In one arrangement this is achieved using a lick roll arrangement 20 incorporating a doctor blade, cooling the backed product at cooling zones 28, 29 and applying the material to a nip formed by rollers 21. In another arrangement this is achieved by doctor box 16 applying the composition to a carrier 13, the carpeting material 19 then being laminated at roll 21 to the layer of composition, the laminate then being cooled before being stripped from the carrier 13. In a further arrangement the carrier is in the form of sheet material 15 which is supported by endless belt 13 and which is bonded into the hot-melt composition to become an integral part thereof.
problem: Applying uniform hot-melt compositions to carpet backing without damaging the material or compromising adhesion during cooling.
constraint: Balancing composition viscosity, cooling rate, and carrier material compatibility to prevent delamination or uneven thickness.
mechanism: Applying a viscous material to a substrate using controlled shearing elements, followed by cooling zones and compression rollers to laminate the material. A secondary support sheet may be integrally bonded to the material during processing to maintain structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Controlled doctoring of hot-melt material onto the carpet undersurface using precision blades or boxes, followed by cooling zones and nip rollers to laminate the composition. A carrier sheet may be integrally bonded to the composition for structural support during processing.

abstract: A leading edge arrangement includes a fixed wing portion 10, a slat member 18 slidably mounted with respect thereto by an arm 14. The arm 14 is provided with an internal trackway 15 and external cam surfaces 16' and 16", the trackway co-operating with roller bearings 12 on the fixed wing portion and the cam surfaces co-operating with respective roller bearings 13' and 13" on the fixed wing portion. The profiles of the trackway and cam surface are selected so that from a stowed cruise condition the slat member initially moves to a take-off setting along a path in which the ratio of downward deflection to extension movement is low, and subsequently moves to a landing setting along a path in which the said ratio is high. A modification is also described in which the rearward heel of the slat member which is exposed when the slat is extended is formed of a flexible panel portion, so that it may blend smoothly with the remainder of the rearward surface of the slat member.
problem: Optimizing aerodynamic performance of a leading edge slat across varying flight conditions (cruise, takeoff, landing).
constraint: Designing cam and track profiles to achieve smooth transitions between settings while minimizing mechanical complexity and weight.
mechanism: Using an articulated linkage with internal guide tracks and external profile surfaces to direct a movable component along a trajectory that adjusts the ratio of angular deflection to linear displacement. Profile geometries encode distinct movement paths for different operational modes.
mechanism_raw: Using an articulated arm with internal trackways and external cam surfaces to guide the slat along a path that adjusts the ratio of downward deflection to extension. Cam profiles encode distinct movement trajectories for different flight settings.

abstract: The invention provides a conversation device having a space key for instructing feeding of a printing tape without printing, a pulse oscillator for producing pulses of predetermined period upon depression of the space key, a counter for counting the pulses generated from the pulse oscillator, a one-shot multivibrator for producing a pulse to indicate that the count value has reached a predetermined value, a flip-flop which is set by the pulse from the one-shot multivibrator and allows the pulses from the pulse oscillator to be supplied to a motor driver for amplifying the pulses and which is reset when the predetermined number of pulses from the pulse oscillator is received and prohibits the supply of the pulse oscillator to the motor driver, and a pulse motor for feeding the printing tape without printing. Therefore, when the flip-flop is set, the motor driver causes the pulse motor to drive the printing tape for a predetermined length corresponding to a plurality of characters. The device further includes a CPU for discriminating a depressed key and for supplying a signal to the motor driver which causes the pulse motor to drive the printing tape for a length corresponding to one character.
problem: Precisely controlling incremental tape feed length in a printing device without manual intervention or mechanical calibration.
constraint: Ensuring pulse period accuracy and flip-flop reset timing to maintain consistent feed lengths across varying operational states.
mechanism: Generating a fixed number of timing pulses corresponding to a desired displacement length, with a bistable control circuit that enables/disables actuator pulses. A processor discriminates input signals to adjust pulse counts for single-unit or multi-unit feed operations.
mechanism_raw: Using a pulse oscillator and counter to generate a fixed number of pulses corresponding to a desired tape length, with a flip-flop circuit that enables/disables motor driver pulses. The CPU discriminates key inputs to adjust pulse counts for single-character or multi-character feeds.

abstract: A mobile binding is provided comprising holding elements or S shaped clips and formed from two sheets of cardboard, or a similar semi rigid material, which extends over the whole length of the binding and which are bonded together, except at least in the end portions of the back, the inner sheet having an opening in which one of the end legs of the S shaped element may be engaged, the other end then being engaged in the middle of a review to be bound. The improvement consists in providing said holding elements with a notch on the inner face of their portion situated opposite said opening when they are in position in the binding; it also comprises a plate which may be engaged in said opening between said two sheets of the back and which is provided with an outwardly turned flange adapted for engagement in the notches of said elements.
problem: Creating a mobile binding that securely holds pages while allowing adjustable engagement and release using semi-rigid materials.
constraint: The binding must use semi-rigid materials (e.g., cardboard) that balance flexibility for adjustment with structural integrity to maintain the interlock under load.
mechanism: A resilient interlocking system uses a deformable element with a protruding feature and a complementary receptacle: the protrusion engages a retention structure to lock the component in place, while the material's controlled flexibility enables insertion, positional adjustment, and release without continuous external force.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical interlock between a notched holding element and a plate with an outward flange: the flange engages the notch to lock the plate in place, while the semi-rigid material allows controlled flexing for insertion/removal and positional adjustment.
residual_terms: ["resilient interlocking system", "deformable element", "protruding feature", "complementary receptacle", "retention structure", "controlled flexibility"]

abstract: Disclosed is an improved process wherein coal particles are beneficiated by froth flotation under coal froth flotation conditions to separate the desired coal particles from remaining unwanted ash and like gangue material. The improvement of the present invention comprises conducting the froth flotation in the presence of an effective proportion of a promoter which is at least C.sub.10 aliphatic carboxylic acid or an aliphatic ester thereof which is devoid of nitrogen atoms; the hydroxylated, oxidized, or alkoxylated derivative of said acid or ester promoters; and mixtures thereof.
problem: Separating coal particles from ash and gangue during froth flotation by enhancing the hydrophobicity of coal surfaces.
constraint: The promoter must lack nitrogen atoms to avoid interfering with coal's surface chemistry and remain effective under coal flotation conditions (pH, temperature, and reagent compatibility).
mechanism: A surface-modifying agent selectively adsorbs onto target particles, altering their interfacial properties to enhance preferential attachment to a dispersed phase (e.g., gas bubbles) during separation, while chemical composition constraints ensure compatibility with the target material's surface chemistry.
mechanism_raw: A chemical promoter (C10+ aliphatic carboxylic acid or ester without nitrogen) selectively adsorbs onto coal particles, increasing their hydrophobicity and enabling preferential attachment to air bubbles during flotation, while hydroxylated/alkoxylated derivatives further tune surface interactions.
residual_terms: ["surface-modifying agent", "selective adsorption", "interfacial properties", "dispersed phase", "chemical composition constraints"]

abstract: Method of manufacturing an injection-molded ski plate comprising steps of disposing a lower side member in a lower mold, disposing an upper side member in the lower mold, disposing an upper mold formed with a concaved portion corresponding to a roof-like shape with the widthwise central part of the ski plate and injecting a foaming synthetic resin into a hollow space between the lower and upper members and harding after foaming, whereby the upper member is molded following the roof-like concaved portion so that a convexed roof-like portion is formed on the upper member.
problem: Forming a ski plate with a convex roof-like upper surface using injection molding of foaming synthetic resin.
constraint: The foaming resin must expand uniformly within the mold cavity while maintaining adhesion to the upper/lower side members, requiring precise timing of injection, foaming, and hardening phases.
mechanism: A shaping process uses a contoured mold cavity to direct the expansion and solidification of a foaming material, forcing adjacent structural elements to conform to a geometrically optimized profile through synchronized control of material flow, expansion, and hardening phases.
mechanism_raw: A concaved upper mold cavity shapes the expanding foaming resin as it hardens, forcing the upper side member to conform to the mold's roof-like geometry, creating a structurally optimized convex profile through controlled expansion and solidification.
residual_terms: ["contoured mold cavity", "foaming material", "expansion and solidification", "geometric optimization", "synchronized control"]

abstract: A pin for holding and/or cooling of a ceramic coating in hot reaction chambers has a pin shaft and a pin cap connected with one another in firm and heat-conductive manner, wherein the pin shaft is composed of material corresponding to the reaction conditions in the hot reaction chamber, and the pin cap is composed of a material corresponding to the material of the wall of the hot reaction chamber.
problem: Maintaining and cooling a ceramic coating in a hot reaction chamber where the coating and chamber wall face different thermal and chemical environments.
constraint: The pin must transition between two distinct material systems (shaft and cap) without compromising heat transfer or structural integrity, requiring a firm, heat-conductive bond between dissimilar materials.
mechanism: A composite interface component transitions between two material systems: one side resists environmental degradation from a reactive medium, while the other side matches the thermal and chemical properties of a substrate, enabling stable heat transfer and structural continuity across dissimilar environments.
mechanism_raw: A composite pin design: the pin shaft is made of material resistant to the chamber's reaction conditions, while the pin cap matches the chamber wall material, enabling thermal and chemical compatibility at both the coating interface and the chamber wall interface.
residual_terms: ["composite interface component", "material systems", "environmental degradation", "thermal and chemical properties", "structural continuity"]

abstract: A signaling device for firing signaling cartridges in an emergency. The signaling cartridges are adapted to emit light, noise and or smoke signals. The device includes a grip which is manually grasped and which includes a firing lever adapted to be pressed inwardly. The firing lever when in a normal inoperative position forms part of the grip contour. When the firing lever is pressed inwardly it lifts off a rotatably mounted hammer from a firing pin. The hammer then snaps back via the force exerted by a spring to actuate the firing pin. Simultaneously with actuation of the hammer the firing lever also effects a rotational advance of a cartridge magazine of the signaling device. Alternately, the cartridge magazine can be rotationally advanced with the thumb of the user of the device. When the signaling device is held in its "natural" position it is vertically upwardly oriented so that signaling cartridges are fired in that direction.
problem: Firing signaling cartridges and advancing a cartridge magazine in a handheld signaling device with minimal user effort.
constraint: The lever must integrate both functions (hammer release and magazine rotation) without requiring separate user actions, while maintaining safety by ensuring the lever only actuates when pressed inward in the natural grip position.
mechanism: A single actuation input drives two mechanically linked operations in sequence: a first motion releases stored energy to perform an impact action, while a second motion (via a cam or linkage) converts the same input into rotational indexing of a component feed mechanism, ensuring synchronized operation without separate user actions.
mechanism_raw: A single mechanical input (pressing the firing lever) triggers two sequential actions: (1) lifting the hammer to release spring-driven impact on the firing pin, and (2) rotating the magazine via a cam or linkage connected to the lever's motion, ensuring synchronized firing and cartridge indexing.
residual_terms: ["actuation input", "mechanically linked operations", "stored energy", "impact action", "cam or linkage", "rotational indexing", "component feed mechanism"]

abstract: This invention relates to a device for making cabled yarns of considerable regularity wherein a first yarn is firstly braked by a progressive brake, then it is subjected to a false twist. A second yarn is braked in order to impose a very regular tension thereon. The two yarns pass through a rotating system comprising two pulleys coupled with each other which ensure that the advance of these two yarns is identical. The composite or cabled yarn then passes through a system for stopping the progression of the twist. Finally, the cabled yarn arrives at a distribution device, care being taken to provide a large distance d between the distribution device and the last point of guiding of the yarn which is located opposite the center of the stroke of the yarn distribution device. The invention is more particularly applicable to the manufacture for cabled yarns for pneumatic tires.
problem: Producing cabled yarns with consistent twist distribution and regularity, particularly for high-performance applications like pneumatic tires where uneven twisting causes structural weakness.
constraint: The coupled pulley system must ensure identical advancement of both yarns while maintaining independent tension control, and the spacing distance d must be large enough to allow twist stabilization without introducing slack or instability in the composite yarn.
mechanism: Two filaments are independently subjected to controlled resistive forces to impose regular tension, then advanced through a mechanically coupled rotational system that synchronizes their feed rates, ensuring identical advancement. A twist-arresting mechanism halts progression of the twist at a defined location, and a large spacing between the final guide and the distribution point allows the twist to stabilize before distribution, preventing irregular twist propagation.
mechanism_raw: Two yarns are independently braked to impose controlled, regular tension, then advanced through a coupled rotating system that mechanically synchronizes their feed rates, ensuring identical advancement. A twist-stopping system arrests progression of the twist at a defined point, and a large spacing between the final yarn guide and the distribution device allows the twist to stabilize before distribution, preventing irregular twist propagation.
