abstract: A portable drum set is provided by utilizing a pre-tuned head which is clamped to an arcuate member. The arcuate member has a pair of floor-engaging legs on either side which are releasably clamped to the arcuate member. Other percussion instruments such as drums or cymbals may be mounted to the top of the arcuate member or the legs to provide a full kit. Also, a resilient pad is placed on the bottom surface of the bass drum pedal to help isolate the set and vibrations from the supporting surface. The clamps may be formed either of a resilient material such as rubber or may be formed of metal to rigidly clamp the pre-tuned head rim to the arcuate member.
problem: Creating a portable, quickly deployable drum set that maintains tuning stability and isolates vibrations from the supporting surface during transport and use.
constraint: The clamps must provide sufficient holding force to maintain tuning and structural integrity during play, yet be releasable enough for quick setup and teardown, while the resilient pad must isolate vibrations without compromising pedal responsiveness.
mechanism: A pre-tuned flexible membrane is clamped to a curved structural member using releasable fasteners, allowing rapid assembly and disassembly while preserving tension. Surface-engaging supports are also releasably attached to the curved member, enabling modular configuration. A compliant isolation element on the actuation pedal decouples vibrations from the supporting surface, preventing energy transfer and noise coupling.
mechanism_raw: A pre-tuned drum head is clamped to an arcuate member using releasable clamps, allowing rapid assembly and disassembly while preserving tuning. Floor-engaging legs are also releasably clamped to the arcuate member, enabling modular configuration. A resilient pad on the bass drum pedal isolates vibrations from the supporting surface, preventing energy transfer and noise coupling.

abstract: This invention presents apparatus and a method for controlling the contents and the filling of a distribution tank for pulverized material. The apparatus and method include structure for and the steps of weighing the distribution tank and an intermediate tank and structure for and the steps of sealing the connection between the tanks for transfer of material and separating the tanks for weighing.
problem: Accurately controlling the contents and filling of a distribution tank for pulverized material, where precise measurement and transfer are needed without contamination or loss.
constraint: The connection between tanks must be sealable to prevent material loss during transfer, yet separable to allow independent weighing, and the weighing system must accurately measure each tank's contents without interference from the transfer mechanism.
mechanism: A distribution vessel and an intermediate vessel are weighed independently to determine material content, and a sealable connection between the vessels allows controlled transfer of material. The vessels are separated for weighing, ensuring that each measurement reflects only the contents of that specific vessel, while the sealed transfer prevents spillage or contamination during movement of material.
mechanism_raw: The distribution tank and an intermediate tank are weighed independently to determine material content, and a sealed connection between the tanks allows controlled transfer of material. The tanks are separated for weighing, ensuring that each measurement reflects only the contents of that specific tank, while the sealed transfer prevents spillage or contamination during movement of material.

abstract: A tamper indicating closure cap of the type having a pivotable stopper closing a cap top orifice. The stopper has an integral flange overlying portions of the top and extending behind the pivotable member to preclude pivoting of the pivotable member. The flange is removable from the pivotable member and indicia formed in the container top underlying the flange is made visible by removal of the flange.
problem: Providing tamper evidence on a closure cap that clearly indicates unauthorized access or opening, while maintaining normal closure function.
constraint: The flange must be removable only by an action that simultaneously enables pivoting of the stopper and exposes the indicia, ensuring that any attempt to open the cap necessarily produces a visible tamper signal.
mechanism: A pivotable closure element seals the container orifice and has an integral blocking member that overlies and mechanically prevents the closure element from pivoting open. The blocking member covers visual indicators on the container, and removal of the blocking member to enable pivoting also exposes the indicators, creating a visible tamper signal that is directly linked to the act of opening the closure.
mechanism_raw: A pivotable stopper closes the cap orifice and has an integral flange that overlies and mechanically blocks the pivotable member from pivoting open. The flange covers indicia on the container top, and removal of the flange to enable pivoting also exposes the indicia, creating a visible tamper indicator that is directly linked to the act of opening the closure.

abstract: A vacuum dewar for infrared detectors is disclosed, in which unitary Kovar leads are used to reduce heat load and improve reliability and ruggedness. The Kovar leads are encapsulated in the glass walls of the hollow stem which carries the sensor array and supplies cryogenic fluid for cooling the array. The Kovar leads extend throughout the entire length of the stem to form both the electrical feed-through and the contact points at each end of the stem for the attachment of wire leads or cables, and to form a reinforcing structure for the stem. A fabrication method is also disclosed, in which a unitary Kovar leadframe is held under tension while two concentric glass tubes, between which the leadframe is vacuum-sandwiched, are fused together to form a stem encapsulating continuous Kovar leads throughout its length, while preventing excessive oxidation of the Kovar leads.
problem: Providing reliable electrical feed-throughs in a vacuum dewar for infrared detectors while minimizing heat load, maximizing structural integrity, and preventing oxidation of conductive leads during fabrication.
constraint: The Kovar leads must remain under controlled tension during glass fusion to prevent oxidation and ensure hermetic sealing, while the leadframe must be unitary to serve as both electrical conductor and structural reinforcement without introducing thermal bridges or mechanical failure points.
mechanism: A unitary conductive leadframe is held under tension while two concentric insulating tubes are fused together around it, vacuum-sandwiching the leadframe to form a hollow stem. The continuous conductive leads serve simultaneously as electrical feed-throughs, contact points at each end, and reinforcing structure for the stem. The tension during fusing prevents excessive oxidation of the leads while ensuring a hermetic seal.
mechanism_raw: A unitary Kovar leadframe is held under tension while two concentric glass tubes are fused together around it, vacuum-sandwiching the leadframe to form a hollow stem. The continuous Kovar leads serve simultaneously as electrical feed-throughs, contact points at each end, and reinforcing structure for the stem. The tension during fusing prevents excessive oxidation of the Kovar leads while ensuring a hermetic seal.

abstract: A method of manufacturing an identification card whereby information is printed on a sheet of plastic material. A raised pattern is formed on a different sheet of material to create a holographic image. The resultant raised pattern sheet is attached to the surface of the sheet of plastic material by pressure sensitive adhesive. The surface of the plastic material is overlaminated with a transparent layer to form a sandwich and heat and pressure is applied to fuse overlaminated layers. The pattern sheet has a high melting point so that the image is viewed as three-dimensional through an overlaminated layer.
problem: Creating a durable, three-dimensional holographic image on an identification card without degrading the image during lamination.
constraint: Balancing the melting points of the pattern sheet and overlaminate to ensure fusion of the overlaminate without compromising the structural integrity or visual clarity of the holographic image.
mechanism: Using a first layer with a higher thermal threshold than a second layer, so that applying heat and pressure fuses the second layer without deforming the first layer's structured pattern, preserving its three-dimensional appearance.
mechanism_raw: Using a pattern sheet with a high melting point relative to the overlaminate layer, so that heat and pressure during lamination fuse the overlaminate without deforming the holographic pattern, preserving its three-dimensional appearance.

abstract: Method of manufacturing core yarns from fiber bands. A part of the fibers of a fiber band is released from the fiber band and is deflected. These deflected fibers do not participate in the spinning process, but are wrapped around the twisted core in a plurality of reinforcing winds. The method of the invention overcomes the problems of manufacturing yarns without requiring expensive and complicated mechanical elements.
problem: Manufacturing reinforced core yarns from fiber bands without requiring complex mechanical systems.
constraint: Managing the release and deflection of fibers to ensure consistent wrapping around the core without disrupting the spinning process or requiring additional mechanical components.
mechanism: Redirecting a portion of fibers from a continuous band away from a central twisting element, causing them to wrap around the twisted core in reinforcing winds through controlled deflection, without additional mechanical components.
mechanism_raw: Deflecting a portion of fibers from the fiber band so they are not incorporated into the core spinning process, instead wrapping them around the twisted core in reinforcing winds through controlled fiber redirection.

abstract: An explosion proof vault for housing electrical equipment is isolated from ambient air by the provision of an auxiliary expansion chamber. The auxiliary expansion chamber is coupled to the explosion proof casing and an inelastic bladder is located in the auxiliary expansion chamber in fluid communication with the explosion proof casing. An airtight seal around the mouth of the bladder prevents the passage of air between the explosion proof casing and the auxiliary expansion chamber except within the bladder.
problem: Isolating electrical equipment in an explosion-proof vault from ambient air while managing pressure changes during an explosion.
constraint: Ensuring the bladder's inelasticity and airtight seal balance pressure relief during expansion with the need to fully isolate the equipment from ambient air.
mechanism: Using an inelastic, sealed flexible barrier in an auxiliary chamber connected to a main enclosure, allowing controlled expansion of internal gases through the barrier while maintaining an airtight isolation of enclosed equipment from ambient air.
mechanism_raw: Using an inelastic bladder in an auxiliary expansion chamber connected to the main casing, allowing controlled expansion of gases through the bladder while maintaining an airtight seal to prevent air ingress.

abstract: The radial plunger pump has a rotor in which a plurality of plungers are radially slidingly received and have their outer ends in engagement with a guide ring which is provided so as to be eccentric from the rotor, so that the plungers reciprocate in their cylinders as the rotor rotates. The eccentric amount is controlled by the movement of a controlling piston, and the movement of the controlling piston is controlled by a pilot valve. The pilot valve which has a sleeve and a shaft member, switches the pressure in a chamber formed behind the controlling piston in order to control the movement of the controlling piston. The position of the shaft member of the pilot valve is further controlled by an electrical control, so that the critical point at which the pilot valve switches the pressure is controlled by the electrical control.
problem: Controlling the displacement of a radial plunger pump by adjusting the eccentricity of the plungers.
constraint: Coordinating the electrical control of the pilot valve's switching point with the mechanical movement of the controlling piston to achieve smooth and accurate eccentricity adjustment.
mechanism: Using a pressure-switching valve to alter fluid pressure in a chamber that repositions a mechanical linkage, which adjusts the offset of working elements, with an external controller overriding the valve's actuation point for precise regulation.
mechanism_raw: Using a pilot valve with a sleeve and shaft to switch pressure in a chamber behind a controlling piston, which adjusts the eccentric position of the plungers, with electrical control overriding the pilot valve's switching point for precise displacement regulation.

abstract: An electrophotographic recording material is described which comprises an electrically conductive support and a photoconductive layer comprising a photoconductor, a binder, and at least one bis-benzothiazole-pentamethine-cyanine having a particular structure. The aforementioned recording material displays a sensitization peak in the range between about 680 nm and 710 nm, and can be processed under visual control using bright safelights.
problem: Achieving a specific spectral sensitization range (680–710 nm) in an electrophotographic recording material while enabling processing under bright safelights.
constraint: Designing the dye's molecular structure to balance spectral sensitivity in the target range with sufficient safelight tolerance to avoid unintended exposure during processing.
mechanism: Incorporating a dye with a molecular structure tuned to absorb light in a specific wavelength range into a light-sensitive layer, providing targeted spectral sensitivity while maintaining resistance to unintended exposure under bright ambient lighting conditions.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a bis-benzothiazole-pentamethine-cyanine dye with a tailored molecular structure into the photoconductive layer, which provides the desired sensitization peak and compatibility with bright safelights.

abstract: An ultrasonic transducer comprising a network of parallel piezoelectric transducer elements having a width W or in the form of a parallelepipedon having a length H and a width W, characterized in that the thickness T of the said transducer elements is equal to half the wavelength corresponding to a frequency F which is equal to the average value of at least two of the successive piezoelectric resonance frequencies of the piezoelectric material concerned, the products of the thickness and the resonance frequencies framing at least two successive vibratory modes of this material in the bidimensional diagram of the curves F.multidot.T=f(W/T) of the spread of the resonance frequencies relating to the piezoelectric material concerned or in the tridimensional diagram of the curves F.multidot.T=f(W/T, H/T).
problem: Achieving efficient ultrasonic transduction by optimizing the vibratory modes of piezoelectric transducer elements.
constraint: Balancing the thickness, width, and length of the transducer elements to frame at least two successive vibratory modes without interference, while maintaining structural integrity and operational bandwidth.
mechanism: Adjusting the physical dimensions of vibratory elements to align with at least two successive natural frequencies of the material, ensuring dimensional parameters correspond to half-wavelength relationships in a multidimensional parameter space to prevent modal interference while preserving structural and operational constraints.
mechanism_raw: Tuning the thickness of the transducer elements to half the wavelength of a frequency corresponding to the average of two successive resonance frequencies, ensuring the physical dimensions align with the material's vibratory modes in a bidimensional or tridimensional parameter space.

abstract: A coal-water mixture (CWM) burner includes a conically shaped rotating cup into which fuel comprised of coal particles suspended in a slurry is introduced via a first, elongated inner tube coupled to a narrow first end portion of the cup. A second, elongated outer tube is coaxially positioned about the first tube and delivers steam to the narrow first end of the cup. The fuel delivery end of the inner first tube is provided with a helical slot on its lateral surface for directing the CWM onto the inner surface of the rotating cup in the form of a uniform, thin sheet which, under the influence of the cup's centrifugal force, flows toward a second, open, expanded end portion of the rotating cup positioned immediately adjacent to a combustion chamber. The steam delivered to the rotating cup wets its inner surface and inhibits the coal within the CWM from adhering to the rotating cup. A primary air source directs a high velocity air flow coaxially about the expanded discharge end of the rotating cup for applying a shear force to the CWM in atomizing the fuel mixture for improved combustion. A secondary air source directs secondary air into the combustion chamber adjacent to the outlet of the rotating cup at a desired pitch angle relative to the fuel mixture/steam flow to promote recirculation of hot combustion gases within the ignition zone for increased flame stability.
problem: Improving combustion efficiency and flame stability in a coal-water mixture burner.
constraint: Coordinating steam delivery, air velocity, and rotational speed to balance atomization, adhesion prevention, and recirculation without excessive cooling or turbulence.
mechanism: Applying rotational force to disperse a fluid into a thin layer, introducing a secondary medium to counteract surface adhesion, and directing coaxial gas flows to fragment the dispersed material and induce recirculation of heated gases for sustained combustion stability.
mechanism_raw: Using centrifugal force from a rotating cup to spread fuel into a thin sheet, steam to inhibit adhesion, and coaxial air flows to atomize the mixture and promote hot gas recirculation for stable ignition.
residual_terms: ["rotational force", "surface adhesion", "coaxial gas flows", "recirculation of heated gases"]

abstract: A control system for a belt-drive infinitely variable transmission. The transmission is connected to a crankshaft of an engine through an electromagnetic clutch. The control system is provided with an engine speed signal producing circuit, a vehicle speed producing circuit and an arithmetic circuit for controlling the clutch current flowing through the coil of the clutch in dependency on the engine speed signal and vehicle speed signal. The arithmetic circuit is so arranged as to cut off the clutch current when the engine speed decreases to a predetermined value which is slightly higher than an engine speed at which the engine stalls during shiftdown operation of the transmission.
problem: Preventing engine stall during downshifts in a belt-drive infinitely variable transmission.
constraint: Setting the engine speed threshold precisely to avoid stalling while maintaining smooth clutch engagement and transmission responsiveness under varying load conditions.
mechanism: Implementing a closed-loop control system that continuously compares measured rotational speeds against a predefined threshold, actuating a disengagement mechanism when the threshold is breached to prevent torque overload during rapid speed transitions.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a feedback control loop that monitors engine and vehicle speeds to cut clutch current when engine speed drops below a threshold slightly above stall speed, preventing torque overload during shiftdown.

abstract: A noble metal-containing zeolitic catalyst having cracking activity and hydrogenation activity is pretreated by contacting the catalyst with a nitrogen-containing compound to decrease the cracking activity of the catalyst followed by treatment with hydrogen to recover the hydrogenation activity of the catalyst. The pretreated catalyst is used in a process for the hydrogenation of aromatic hydrocarbons.
problem: Optimizing a zeolitic catalyst's balance between cracking and hydrogenation activities for aromatic hydrocarbon processing.
constraint: Controlling the sequence, duration, and conditions of nitrogen and hydrogen treatments to achieve the desired activity balance without degrading the catalyst structure.
mechanism: Sequentially exposing a catalytic medium to a nitrogen-containing agent to suppress one reaction pathway, followed by exposure to a hydrogen-rich environment to restore a competing reaction pathway, thereby selectively modifying active sites to balance catalytic activities.
mechanism_raw: Pretreating the catalyst with a nitrogen-containing compound to suppress cracking activity, followed by hydrogen treatment to restore hydrogenation activity, selectively modifying active sites for targeted reactions.

abstract: A method for constructing an optical filter for use in a holographic scanner includes exposing a photographic film to a laser, developing the film and reinserting the developed film into the unexpanded output beam of the laser to provide a uniform illumination of the outputted beam. The filter is positioned in the reference beam in the construction of a hologram used in the holographic scanner.
problem: Constructing an optical filter with uniform illumination properties for use in holographic scanners.
constraint: Ensuring the film's exposure and development process produces consistent optical density variations that align with the laser's beam profile to achieve uniform illumination without introducing artifacts.
mechanism: Recording a spatial modulation pattern onto a light-sensitive medium using a coherent radiation source, then repositioning the medium within the same radiation field to generate a uniform intensity distribution that compensates for beam profile irregularities during holographic reconstruction.
mechanism_raw: Exposing and developing photographic film to a laser beam, then reinserting the developed film into the unexpanded laser output to create a spatially uniform filter that modulates the reference beam during hologram construction.
residual_terms: ["light-sensitive medium", "coherent radiation source", "spatial modulation pattern", "uniform intensity distribution"]

abstract: A DC arc furnace including a hearth adapted to contain a melt and having a melt electrode which is only effective when covered by the melt, an enclosure for the hearth including a roof over the hearth, at least one arcing electrode depending downwardly through the roof and adapted to initially melt a charge of solid metal on the hearth and thereafter the resulting melt, and at least one starting electrode through which electric power is transmitted to the charge of solid metal until it is melted down by the arcing electrode to enough melt to cover the melt electrode; the starting electrode or electrodes depending downwardly through the roof at a position horizontally offset from the arcing electrode and being adapted to be moved downwardly so as to press on the charge of solid scrap on the hearth until the charge is melted down by the arcing electrode so as to cover the melt electrode and thereafter to be moved upwardly free from the charge.
problem: Initiating and sustaining an arc melt in a DC furnace when the primary melt electrode is initially ineffective due to lack of melt coverage.
constraint: The arcing electrode must remain inactive until covered by melt, requiring precise timing and positioning of the starting electrode to avoid interference.
mechanism: A temporary secondary component is activated to initiate a process in a primary component that is initially non-functional. The secondary component is positioned to interact with the input material until the primary component becomes operational, after which the secondary component is disengaged to allow the primary component to assume control. This bridges the initial non-operational state of the primary component until it becomes functional.
mechanism_raw: A temporary starting electrode, horizontally offset from the arcing electrode, is pressed onto the solid charge to initiate melting. Once sufficient melt forms to cover the arcing electrode, the starting electrode is retracted, allowing the arcing electrode to take over. This bridges the initial non-operational state of the main electrode until it becomes functional.

abstract: Cutlery apparatus with readily interchangeable cutting tools such as knives, the cutting tools being either double ended or a plurality of single ended tools pivotally mounted in a handle, either directly between the handle sides or on a generally U-shaped tool holding member which is in turn pivotally movable in and out of a slotted handle, the apparatus being further provided with lock arm means also pivotally mounted on the handle, forming a part of the handle when closed and retaining the tool rigidly in the handle without use of spring means when the tool is locked in the handle in a position of use. The apparatus which in certain embodiments is of a type commonly called swap blade knives, is readily disassembleable for tool interchange or cleaning. Double ended knives embodying the invention have the strength of a full tang knife with the versatility of a multi-bladed folding knife. Like handle sides, like lock arms, and cutting tools of like construction insofar as the pivot component and locking component portions thereof, are utilized in certain forms of the apparatus, to simplify fabrication and facilitate interchangeability of parts.
problem: Achieving both structural rigidity and tool interchangeability in a cutting tool handle without relying on spring-based retention.
constraint: The locking mechanism must maintain rigidity under load while allowing quick release for tool changes, requiring precise alignment of pivot and locking components.
mechanism: A pivotally mounted component is mechanically locked into a handle structure via a lock arm that engages the component's pivot point. The lock arm integrates with the handle's structure when closed, using the handle's rigidity to secure the component without resilient elements. This enables tool interchange or maintenance through mechanical disengagement.
mechanism_raw: A pivotally mounted tool is locked into the handle via a lock arm that mechanically engages the tool's pivot component. The lock arm forms part of the handle when closed, using the handle's own structure to rigidly secure the tool without springs, enabling tool interchange or cleaning through disassembly.

abstract: The device comprises two or more cover plate members (14), whose lengths are submultiples of the lengths of a range of platen rollers (12) and such that two or more plate members disposed in side-by-side relationship cover the entire length of the platen roller. Each plate member (14) comprises a lower guide portion (16) of part-cylindrical shape and two wall portions (17, 18) which are substantially planar and set at different angles of inclination, being connected to the lower guide portion in such a way to lead in a sheet of paper (19) towards the guide portion. Each plate member (14) is pivotally mounted on a control shaft (22) which is parallel to the axis of the roller (12) and capable of preventing transverse movements of the plate member with respect to the roller, and carries the usual paper pressing rollers (34, 36) which are disposed in two parallel rows. A leaf spring (26) co-operates with a lug (24) on the plate member (14) to hold the paper pressing rollers pressed against the platen roller. The control shaft comprises opening cams (57) arranged to co-operate with the leaf springs to disengage same from the respective lugs and to permit the respective plate members to drop away from the platen roller (12), whereby the paper pressing rollers (34, 36) are disengaged from the platen roller to assist in introducing the sheet of paper.
problem: Maintaining consistent paper pressure against a platen roller during operation while enabling easy sheet insertion without jamming.
constraint: The cam and spring system must balance sufficient pressure during operation with reliable disengagement for loading, requiring precise mechanical coordination.
mechanism: Pivotally mounted pressure elements with resilient members apply force to a surface. Coordinated actuation of release mechanisms disengages the resilient members from the pressure elements, temporarily reducing applied force to allow insertion of a sheet. Re-engagement restores pressure once the sheet is positioned.
mechanism_raw: Pivotally mounted cover plates with leaf springs press paper against the platen roller. Opening cams on a control shaft disengage the leaf springs from lugs on the plates, allowing the plates to drop away from the roller. This temporarily releases pressure to facilitate paper insertion, then re-engages pressure once the sheet is in place.

abstract: Apparatus and method for the electrochemical reduction of a nitroaromatic to a dye includes a housing divided into two sections by membrane. An electrolyte solution including a non-aqueous electrolyte dimethylformamide and a supporting electrolyte is provided to the two sections of the housing. A cathode is located in one section of the housing while an anode is located in the other section. A nitroaromatic is provided to the section having the cathode. A direct voltage is provided to the cathode and to the anode so that a current can pass and cooperate in a reaction between the nitroaromatic and the electrolyte solution to provide a dye.
problem: Efficiently converting nitroaromatic compounds to dyes via electrochemical reduction while isolating incompatible reaction environments.
constraint: The membrane must selectively permit ion flow while blocking reactant crossover, and the non-aqueous electrolyte must stabilize the reaction without interfering with electron transfer.
mechanism: A selective barrier divides a system into two distinct reaction zones, permitting ion transport while preventing bulk mixing of reactants. A non-aqueous medium supports electron transfer in one zone, with direct voltage driving a reduction process. The barrier maintains chemical isolation between incompatible environments.
mechanism_raw: A membrane divides the housing into anode and cathode chambers, allowing ion transport while preventing bulk mixing of reactants. A non-aqueous electrolyte (dimethylformamide) supports the reaction, with the cathode chamber receiving the nitroaromatic. Direct voltage drives the reduction, leveraging the membrane to maintain distinct chemical environments.

abstract: A load control system is disclosed for preventing the uncontrolled lowering of a load should a line failure occur in a hydraulic system. The system is designed to be used with a hydraulic cylinder having a movable piston therein which divides the cylinder into a head end and a rod end. Attached to the piston and extending out of the hydraulic cylinder is a piston rod which has a load secured to its free end. The load control system includes a source of pressurized fluid, the flow of which is selectively controlled to the hydraulic cylinder by a control valve. Positioned between the control valve and the head and rod ends of the hydraulic cylinder, respectively, are first and second valves each of which is normally biased towards a closed position by a common pressure. The first and second valves are urged toward an open position by fluid pressure taken between the control valve and the first valve and are movable by this fluid pressure in a proportional manner with the second valve being opened first. The second valve is also physically mounted directly to the hydraulic cylinder such that if a line breakage occurs, the load will still be unable to drop.
problem: Preventing uncontrolled lowering of a hydraulic load during line failure while enabling proportional flow control during normal operation.
constraint: The valves must open proportionally under normal pressure while closing automatically during failure, requiring precise pressure biasing and mechanical mounting to ensure reliability.
mechanism: Normally closed flow control elements, biased by system pressure, open proportionally in response to pressure differentials during normal operation. A redundant element physically coupled to the load ensures automatic closure during upstream failure, creating a fail-safe state that prevents uncontrolled movement.
mechanism_raw: Normally closed valves, biased by system pressure, open proportionally in response to fluid pressure between the control valve and the cylinder. The second valve is physically mounted on the cylinder, ensuring fail-safe closure even if upstream lines rupture. This creates redundant pressure-dependent control that defaults to a safe state.

abstract: A gas burner capable of heating a gas to a high temperature and pressure is isclosed. The burner utilizes a mixing canal to mix the fuel and oxidiser gases and a conically enlarging recess at the exit of the mixing canal. In the recess are both several intake openings for the gas to be heated which openings extend from feeder canals that are parallel to the mixing canal and a side canal leading to an ignition mechanism. The intake openings provide a gas-dynamic blockage of the fuel and oxidiser gas mixture.
problem: Achieving efficient high-temperature and high-pressure gas heating in a burner while maintaining stable gas flow and combustion.
constraint: Balancing gas-dynamic blockage intensity to avoid excessive pressure drop while ensuring sufficient mixing and flame stabilization.
mechanism: A diverging flow channel with controlled apertures at its exit creates a localized flow restriction that stabilizes a mixed fluid stream and directs it toward an ignition region. The geometric expansion and regulated apertures balance pressure and velocity to optimize combustion efficiency while maintaining stable flow.
mechanism_raw: A conically enlarging recess at the mixing canal exit creates a gas-dynamic blockage via intake openings, which stabilizes the fuel-oxidizer mixture and directs flow toward the ignition zone. The geometric expansion and controlled intake openings balance pressure and velocity to optimize combustion efficiency.
residual_terms: ["diverging flow channel", "controlled apertures", "flow restriction", "ignition region", "geometric expansion", "pressure and velocity balance"]

abstract: An activity toy, having a spherical housing which is flattened at its poles so as to be supportable at two places on a support surface, has an elongated helical member which extends within the interior from one of the poles to the other. A bushing is fitted around the helical member and is sized so as to very lightly frictionally engage the helical member whereby when it moves along the longitudinal axis of the helical member, the friction between it and the helical member rotates it on the helical member. A collar is located around the bushing. The collar is free to spin independent of the bushing. However, during travel of the bushing along the helical member, the rotation of the bushing is communicated to the collar. The collar includes a plurality of axles which extend away from the collar, each of which carries an object on its end. Upon inversion of the toy, the combination bushing, collar, and objects on the collar spin down the helical member, with the collar and the objects attached thereto further spinning on the bushing upon the bushing reaching its downward limit of travel.
problem: Creating a mechanical toy that converts linear motion into rotational motion with visually engaging, self-sustaining movement.
constraint: Maintaining minimal friction to allow smooth bushing movement while ensuring sufficient engagement to induce rotation without jamming.
mechanism: A rotating interface with frictional coupling on a helical guide converts translational motion into rotational motion. A freely rotating transfer element transmits this rotation to connected components, enabling cascading motion when the device is inverted. The friction-to-motion coupling generates and transmits rotational energy during linear travel.
mechanism_raw: A bushing with frictional engagement on a helical member rotates as it translates along the helix. A freely spinning collar transfers this rotation to attached objects, enabling cascading motion when the toy is inverted. The friction-to-motion coupling ensures rotational energy is generated and transmitted during linear travel.
residual_terms: ["rotating interface", "frictional coupling", "helical guide", "freely rotating transfer element", "friction-to-motion coupling"]

abstract: An actuator of the type used in aircraft flight controls and similar applications is combined with a fail-passive electrohydraulic control system (11) that affords the usual actuator response to electrical input commands during normal operation, and responds to any of a number of possible failure conditions to dispose the actuator in a passive or neutral failure mode. The passive-failure mode allows the actuator (15) to remain in the last-known valid position or move in response to an external force such as provided by a redundant backup actuator thereby avoiding a possibly dangerous flight condition that can result from a "hard over" actuator response to a failure condition. First and second unbalanced eletrohydraulic servo actuator controls (14 and 16) are connected in back-to-back closed control loops bewteen the actuator (15) and electrical command inputs (14e and 16e) to form a balanced actuator configuration, and the separate control loops are synchronized by a synchronizing piston and associated electrical position transducer (24) that enable normal actuator operation so long as a predetermined relationship exists between the supply pressure Ps and the sum of the fluid pressure Pc1 and Pc2 applied to opposite sides of the actuator. Any failure condition results in unsynchronizing the separate control loops and equalizing the pressures at opposite sides of the actuator, thereby producing the fail-passive mode.
problem: Preventing dangerous "hard over" actuator responses during system failures in electrohydraulic control systems.
constraint: Ensuring synchronization under normal conditions while enabling rapid, reliable failure detection and pressure equalization.
mechanism: Two synchronized unbalanced actuators in closed-loop configurations maintain normal operation through pressure equilibrium. Upon failure, the control loops desynchronize and equalize pressures across the actuator, transitioning it to a passive state that permits external forces to reposition it safely.
mechanism_raw: Two synchronized unbalanced servo actuators in closed-loop configurations maintain normal operation via pressure balance. On failure, the loops unsynchronize and equalize pressures across the actuator, transitioning it to a passive mode that allows external forces to reposition it safely.
residual_terms: ["synchronized unbalanced actuators", "closed-loop configurations", "pressure equilibrium", "control loops", "pressure equalization", "passive state"]

abstract: A vacuum pump and trap combination in which the trap is configured in the manner of a siphon and comprises a tube immersed in trap liquid but having an opening lying above the trap liquid level. The tube has a wall section lying below the trap liquid level and having perforations therein to admit different amounts of trap liquid in relation to the rate of discharge gas flow, thereby preventing frothing of the trap liquid.
problem: Preventing frothing of trap liquid in vacuum systems caused by high-velocity gas discharge.
constraint: Matching perforation size and placement to gas flow rates to balance liquid intake and froth suppression without overfilling.
mechanism: A siphon-like trap with perforations below the liquid surface admits variable amounts of liquid proportional to gas flow rate. This dynamically adjusts the liquid-gas interface to suppress froth formation while maintaining effective trapping.
mechanism_raw: A siphon-like trap tube with perforations below the liquid level admits variable amounts of liquid proportional to gas flow rate. This dynamically adjusts the liquid-gas interface to suppress froth formation while maintaining effective trapping.
residual_terms: ["siphon-like trap", "perforations below liquid surface", "liquid-gas interface", "froth suppression"]

abstract: A high strength, high ductility, low carbon, dual phase steel wire, bar or rod and process for making the same is provided. The steel wire, bar or rod is produced by cold drawing to the desired diameter in a single multipass operation a low carbon steel composition characterized by a duplex microstructure consisting essentially of a strong second phase dispersed in a soft ferrite matrix with a microstructure and morphology having sufficient cold formability to allow reductions in cross-sectional area of up to about 99.9%. Tensile strengths of at least 120 ksi to over 400 ksi may be obtained.
problem: Producing high-strength, high-ductility steel with low carbon content through cold working processes.
constraint: Achieving sufficient cold formability to enable extreme reductions without fracture while maintaining phase stability.
mechanism: Cold drawing a dual-phase material (matrix with dispersed strong second phase) to extreme reductions induces strain hardening and microstructural refinement. The duplex morphology enables simultaneous strength and ductility by distributing deformation across phases.
mechanism_raw: Cold drawing a dual-phase steel (ferrite matrix with dispersed strong second phase) to extreme reductions (up to 99.9%) induces strain hardening and microstructural refinement. The duplex morphology allows simultaneous strength and ductility by distributing deformation across phases.
residual_terms: ["cold drawing", "dual-phase material", "strain hardening", "microstructural refinement", "duplex morphology", "extreme reductions"]

abstract: Horizontal supporting rolls disposed at a lateral side of the work rolls support the work rolls in the direction of travel of the rolled material, and horizontal back-up rolls disposed at a lateral side of the horizontal supporting rolls back-up the horizontal supporting rolls. Frames rotatably hold the horizontal supporting rolls and the horizontal back-up rolls at both axial ends of these rolls, and a first driving mechanism causes a movement of the frames in the direction of travel of the material to be rolled and to impart to the work rolls desired pressing force acting in the direction of travel of the rolled material. A second driving mechanism restrains the position of the frames thus setting the work rolls at predetermined offset positions, provided on the face of the housing confronting the holding means and adapted to guide the movement of the holding member in the direction of travel of the rolled material. With this arrangement, it is possible to prevent any horizontal deflection of the work roll thus affording a highly precise crown and shape control on the rolled product, while facilitating the setting of the work rolls at a designated offset position, as well as replacement of the work rolls.
problem: Achieving precise crown and shape control in rolled products while preventing horizontal deflection of work rolls during rolling operations.
constraint: Balancing the application of pressing force with precise positional restraint to avoid horizontal deflection while maintaining operational flexibility for roll replacement and adjustment.
mechanism: A dual-actuation system where a first actuator applies pressing force to a frame and a second actuator selectively locks the frame position to maintain work rolls at predetermined offset positions, enabling controlled force application without horizontal deflection through coordinated force and restraint.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual driving system where a first mechanism moves frames to apply pressing force and a second mechanism restrains frame position to lock work rolls at predetermined offset positions, enabling controlled force application without deflection.

abstract: A process is disclosed for preparing a suede leather product from animal hides. The hide is scalded before tanning and the finished product can be washed and ironed in a manner similar to a woolen garment. The hide is pretanned in formaldehyde, neutralized in sodium bicarbonate, tanned with a basic chrome solution, neutralized with sodium sulfate, and dyed with a direct color dye. More specifically, an outer suede product is obtained from the external corium of the skin, instead of the flesh side, with the result that less expensive sheepskin acceptable to the trade can be used in place of top grade kidskin and goatskin suedes. In a preferred practice of the method, the hide is burnt twice in scalding steps carried out in a swelling state, soon after first and second fleshing steps and, prior to a bating step. The burning affects the entire thickness of the fibrous grain layer by exposing the upper layer of the corium by soaking the hide in the third solution of sodium sulfide after a third fleshing step. The process obtains a soaped-water washable skin capable of maintaining a soft condition and avoiding fading of the dye. The washable condition is obtained by soaking the dyes, greased with egg yolk, in hot water.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical and physical process tailored to leather processing, with no generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: Collecting electrodes extend vertically in dust-collecting electrostatic precipitators, which are horizontally traversed by gas. Each collecting electrode comprises a plurality of profiled sheet metal strips which are suspended from the roof structure and are hooked into each other at their vertical longitudinal edges. The collecting electrodes also comprise at least one lower transverse connector. Two adjacent collecting electrodes define a gas passage which contains centrally disposed corona electrodes. Each sheet metal strip is substantially W-shaped in cross-section defining shallow dust-collecting pockets and comprises portions which are inclined alternately in opposite directions with respect to the direction of gas flow and portions which are parallel to the direction of gas flow and disposed between the inclined portions. The edge portions extend also parallel to the direction of gas flow and are reversely bent through 180.degree. at their extreme ends to form U-shaped strips which are adapted to be hooked into each other.
problem: Efficiently collecting dust in electrostatic precipitators while maintaining structural integrity and gas flow dynamics.
constraint: Optimizing surface geometry to maximize dust collection efficiency while ensuring structural stability and unimpeded gas passage through the electrode array.
mechanism: A geometric surface configuration with profiled structures forming shallow collection zones and flow-guiding features, where the interaction between gas flow and electrode surfaces enhances particle capture efficiency through optimized spatial relationships between gas movement and collection surfaces.
mechanism_raw: Using profiled W-shaped sheet metal strips with reversely bent U-shaped edges to create shallow dust-collecting pockets and guide gas flow, enhancing particle capture through geometric interaction between gas and electrodes.

abstract: A vacuum conveyor system including a conveyor having plural mounting portions on which workpieces are mounted in spaced-apart relation along an endless track, comprising: plural enclosure devices provided on the plural mounting portions of the conveyor, respectively, for forming air-tight enclosed chambers in which the workpieces mounted on the mounting portions are accommodated, respectively; a vacuum source for drawing an atmosphere from the enclosed chambers; and a suction piping assembly disposed along the conveyor and travelling together with the conveyor along the endless track, the suction piping assembly being connected to the vacuum source and having connections which are adapted to communicate with the enclosed chambers to evacuate the enclosed chambers to a predetermined reduced pressure.
problem: Maintaining a vacuum on moving workpieces in a conveyor system without interrupting continuous operation.
constraint: Ensuring airtight connections between the moving suction piping and stationary vacuum source while accommodating the endless motion of the conveyor track.
mechanism: A continuously moving vacuum interface system that dynamically maintains airtight connections between a stationary vacuum source and enclosed chambers on a moving conveyor, enabling uninterrupted evacuation through synchronized motion and sealed coupling mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a traveling suction piping assembly that moves with the conveyor and dynamically connects to enclosed chambers, allowing continuous evacuation from a stationary vacuum source.

abstract: A device for tightening chains, cables or ropes is disclosed. Previously, turnbuckles or load binders, the latter operating on the principle of the lever, have been used to tighten two ends of a chain or cable around an object, or the ends of two chains which have been secured at their other ends. Such devices are hand-operated and accordingly can only apply limited tension to the chain or cable. The present invention provides a device whereby an air-gun or pneumatic wrench or other power tool can be used to tighten the chain or cable to much greater tension. The device utilizes a threaded bolt which is secured to one end of the chain and which, by the rotation of a threaded socket, is drawn through a sleeve to which the other end of the chain is secured, thereby tightening the chain.
problem: Applying high tension to chains, cables, or ropes using a power tool instead of manual hand-operated devices.
constraint: Translating high-torque rotational input into controlled linear displacement to achieve greater tension than manual systems while maintaining mechanical reliability.
mechanism: A rotational-to-linear conversion mechanism that translates high-torque rotational input into controlled linear displacement by engaging a threaded interface between a rotating component and a fixed element, thereby generating tension through mechanical advantage.
mechanism_raw: Converting rotational motion from a power tool into linear tension by rotating a threaded socket to draw a threaded bolt through a fixed sleeve, thereby tightening the chain or cable.

abstract: A hydraulic cylinder device for power multiplication includes a cylinder (1) containing a single-stage piston (2) having a piston rod (4) and a two-stage secondary piston (3), the piston rod (4) extending through a bore in the secondary piston. The cylinder (1) is closed by a cylinder cover (16) through which the piston rod (4) also extends. Two stop-pistons (22, 24) with different strength springs (21, 23) are located in projection (20) integral with cylinder (1) and opposite the stop-pistons are two opening-pistons (33, 34).
problem: Achieving controlled power multiplication in a hydraulic system where a single input must drive multiple amplification stages in a sequenced manner.
constraint: The spring strengths must be calibrated so that each stage activates at the correct pressure threshold, balancing the need for sequential operation with the requirement for overall power multiplication without uncontrolled simultaneous activation.
mechanism: A multi-stage amplification system uses pressure thresholds to sequence activation of stages with differential effective areas, where weaker thresholds trigger earlier stages and stronger thresholds trigger later stages, ensuring controlled sequential force multiplication without simultaneous activation.
mechanism_raw: A primary single-stage piston with a piston rod extends through a bore in a two-stage secondary piston, mechanically coupling the primary piston's motion to the secondary piston which has a larger effective area. Spring-biased stop-pistons with different spring strengths and opposing opening-pistons create a sequencing mechanism: the weaker spring engages first to initiate one stage, and the stronger spring engages later to activate the next stage, ensuring staged force amplification occurs in a controlled order.

abstract: A loose leaf chewing tobacco product is prepared from leaf tobacco by removing the stems and major veins, then cutting the leaves across the grain of the remaining veins in a uniform manner with the cuts being spaced no greater than 1/4 inch apart, then casing the leaves with a casing mixture and finally drying the cased leaves.
reason: This patent describes a specific product preparation method for chewing tobacco involving stem removal, cross-grain cutting at fixed spacing, casing, and drying. The operations are material-specific processing steps rather than a generalizable problem-solving mechanism with causal functional principles applicable across fields.

abstract: A molding machine has a valve assembly that includes means for selectively heating or cooling a mold by controlling flow of gas through an array of gas impingement jets disposed adjacent the backside of a mold surface to regulate the temperature over respective first and second areas of the mold surface. Gas heating and cooling circuits include two drive cylinder regulated plate valves for supplying gas at the gas impingement jet nozzles associated with the mold.
problem: Independently regulating temperature over different areas of a mold surface during molding to achieve spatially controlled thermal conditioning.
constraint: The gas flow to each impingement jet must be independently regulated while maintaining precise temperature control, requiring the valve assembly to balance rapid response with stable thermal regulation across multiple zones simultaneously.
mechanism: An array of independently controlled fluid delivery elements provides selective thermal conditioning to distinct zones of a surface, with each element's flow rate and temperature regulated by separate actuators to enable spatially resolved heating or cooling.
mechanism_raw: An array of gas impingement jets is positioned adjacent the backside of the mold surface, with each jet supplying heated or cooled gas to a specific mold area. Drive cylinder-regulated plate valves independently control gas flow to each jet circuit, allowing selective heating or cooling of first and second mold areas by directing gas at controlled flow rates and temperatures through the impingement jets.

abstract: A nonreinforced microfiber fabric is disclosed. The fabric has minimum grab tensile strength to weight ratio greater than 0.8N per gram per square meter and a minimum Elmendorf tear strength to weight ratio greater than 0.04N per gram per square meter. The fibers in the fabric have an average length greater than 10 centimeters and at least 80% of the fibers have a diameter of 7 microns or less. The fabric is made by thermally embossing a microfiber web which is made with a minimum of degradation to the polymer and employing high velocity secondary air to maintain air flow uniformity and fiber length.
problem: Creating a strong, tear-resistant nonreinforced microfiber fabric from very fine fibers without degrading the polymer or losing fiber length during processing.
constraint: The thermal embossing temperature and pressure must be sufficient to bond fibers without degrading the polymer, while the high-velocity secondary air must provide enough flow uniformity to preserve fiber length but not so much as to disrupt the web structure during bonding.
mechanism: A fibrous web is bonded through thermal activation while a controlled airflow field maintains structural integrity during processing, balancing inter-fiber adhesion with preservation of fiber length and diameter through managed air velocity and thermal exposure.
mechanism_raw: A microfiber web is thermally embossed to bond fibers together, while high-velocity secondary air is introduced during the process to maintain airflow uniformity through the web. This airflow management prevents fiber displacement and breakage, preserving the long fiber length (>10 cm) and fine diameter (≤7 microns) while the thermal embossing creates sufficient inter-fiber bonding to achieve the required tensile and tear strength ratios without polymer degradation.

abstract: An offshore bulk liquid discharge system and method for its deployment are disclosed. The system is adapted for rapid deployment and facilitates rapid unloading of liquids from an ocean tanker to a shore location. The system includes a base, a mooring buoy tethered to the base and floodable buoyancy tanks which may be flooded causing the base to land on the sea floor. A product swivel mounted on the base provides fluid communication between a tanker hose and a flexible pipeline.
problem: Rapidly deploying an offshore fluid transfer system that can transition between a floating state for deployment and a seabed-resting state for operation, while maintaining continuous fluid communication despite vessel movement.
constraint: The system must transition reliably between floating and seabed-resting states using only ballast flooding, while the swivel coupling must maintain leak-tight fluid communication under dynamic loading from wave action and vessel movement.
mechanism: A buoyancy-controlled transition system shifts between floating and resting states via selective fluid displacement in chambers, while a rotational coupling maintains continuous fluid communication between moving components despite external dynamic forces.
mechanism_raw: Floodable buoyancy tanks on the base allow controlled ballasting: flooding the tanks causes the base to descend and land on the sea floor, while the mooring buoy keeps the system tethered during deployment. A product swivel mounted on the base provides a rotational fluid coupling between the tanker hose and the flexible pipeline, allowing continuous fluid transfer even as the tanker moves relative to the seabed-resting base.

abstract: A propellant charge and method of manufacture thereof by which the increase in maximum gas pressure within the upper use temperature range which occurs upon firing can be influenced until eliminated. The propellant charge is manufactured by compacting a first portion of the propellant charge which corresponds to between 50-80% of the total mass of the propellant charge, and then adding the balance of the propellant charge as loose powder on top of the first portion.
problem: The maximum gas pressure generated during firing of a propellant charge increases significantly at upper use temperatures, potentially causing unsafe or undesirable pressure spikes.
constraint: The ratio of compacted to loose powder must be maintained between 50-80% compacted to balance structural integrity of the charge with the desired pressure modulation effect.
mechanism: A multi-density reactive medium is formed by compacting a first portion of the medium to create a dense region, then depositing the remaining portion as a less-dense layer. The differing burn rates of the dense and loose regions produce a controlled temporal pressure profile that counteracts temperature-induced pressure variations.
mechanism_raw: A dual-density propellant structure is created by compacting a first portion (50-80% of total mass) to form a dense core, then layering the remaining mass as loose powder on top. The compacted portion burns at a different rate than the loose powder, creating a controlled pressure modulation profile that counteracts the temperature-induced pressure increase.

abstract: A slider supplying apparatus, for use with a slide-fastener finishing machine, includes a rail for slidingly supporting a number of sliders in succession from a reservoir, with the opposite wings of each slider body astride of the rail and with a pull tab hanging from the slider body, and a chute defining a guide channel for passage therethrough of the slider bodies and having an upper end portion disposed adjacent to a free end portion of the rail for receiving the successive sliders therefrom. The upper end portion of the chute has a sloping edge engageable with the pull tab of each slider, as the latter slides forwardly on the free end portion of the rail, so as to raise the pull tab perpendicularly to the slider wing. The chute also has a guide slit coextensive with the guide channel for receiving the pull tab of each slider in such raised posture while the slider body is in the guide channel.
problem: Slider pull tabs on slide-fastener sliders need to be reoriented to a perpendicular posture as the sliders pass through a guide channel in a finishing machine, to ensure proper positioning for subsequent processing.
constraint: The slope angle of the edge and the position of the guide slit must be precisely coordinated with the slider geometry and rail positioning to ensure reliable tab lifting without jamming.
mechanism: A sloped surface engages a flexible tab as a carrier moves along a rail, converting the carrier's horizontal motion into vertical displacement that reorients the tab. A guide opening then captures and retains the tab in its reoriented position as the carrier enters a downstream channel.
mechanism_raw: A sloping edge on the chute engages the pull tab of each slider as it slides forward on the rail, converting the horizontal sliding motion into vertical lifting motion that raises the tab perpendicular to the slider wings. A coextensive guide slit then captures and maintains the tab in this raised posture as the slider body enters the guide channel.

abstract: A portable system for making harped, reinforced concrete beams includes a series of inverted T-shaped concrete bed sections, with aligned longitudinally extending holes for receiving tensioning cables to hold the sections together, to provide two beds, one on either side of the center wall of the sections, to make the concrete beams. At points near the center of each beam to be formed, arrangements for "harping" or depressing the longitudinally extending tensioning steel strands or cables are provided. The harping arrangements include a lever pivotally mounted on the central wall of the concrete sections to pivot in either direction to alternatively harp beams on either side, with intermediate lever actuated arrangements including a harping fork for engaging the steel strands, and screw threaded arrangements at the outer end of the lever for pulling the lever down toward the outer edge of the concrete bed, thereby depressing and harping the tensioning steel strands which are to be embedded in the concrete beams.
problem: Tensioning steel strands in reinforced concrete beams need to be selectively depressed (harped) at specific points near the center of each beam to achieve desired structural properties, and this must be done in a portable, reversible manner.
constraint: The lever must pivot freely in both directions while the screw mechanism provides controlled, precise depression force, and the harping fork must engage the strands without slippage during the depression operation.
mechanism: A pivoting lever with a gripping element engages tensioned members, and a threaded actuation mechanism applies controlled displacement force to the lever, mechanically deflecting the members. Bidirectional pivoting of the lever enables deflection on either side of a central reference plane.
mechanism_raw: A lever is pivotally mounted on the central wall of the concrete bed sections and can pivot in either direction. A harping fork at the lever engages the steel strands, and screw-threaded arrangements at the outer end of the lever pull the lever down toward the outer edge of the bed, mechanically depressing the strands. The bidirectional pivot allows harping on either side of the center wall.

abstract: A helmholtz resonator is driven by a piezoelectric element and is suited for mounting to a printed circuit board. The resonator includes a resonant chamber defined by bottom, top, and side walls, and at least two ports that provide access to the chamber. The ports are contiguous to the bottom and side walls so that any liquid entering the chamber during the printed circuit board cleaning process can exit via the ports. This arrangement overcomes the contamination problem existing in prior art resonators having a single port.
problem: Liquid entering a Helmholtz resonator chamber during PCB cleaning processes becomes trapped, causing contamination and degradation of resonator performance.
constraint: The ports must be positioned at the lowest points of the chamber walls relative to typical cleaning orientations, and their size and number must balance acoustic performance with effective drainage.
mechanism: Multiple drainage openings are positioned at the lowest regions of a resonant cavity relative to expected operational orientations, providing redundant exit pathways for entrapped fluid. This ensures fluid evacuation regardless of the cavity's orientation during use.
mechanism_raw: Multiple ports are positioned contiguous to both the bottom and side walls of the resonant chamber, creating multiple exit pathways for any liquid that enters. This ensures that regardless of the chamber's orientation during cleaning, liquid can drain out through the ports rather than accumulating inside.

abstract: A fume hood is fabricated of three or four like modules to a desired partial or full cylindrical structure having a reaction chamber therein. Each module has an upstanding, arcuate circumferential outer wall and an upper wall and base extending inwardly therefrom in coincidence above and below one another. The top wall and base have the shape of a sector of a circle with their apexes opposite the outer wall and the outer wall being the arc of the sector. An inner wall spaced interior of the outer wall defines an exhaust passageway therebetween with movement of gases and air being through exhaust ports through the inner wall. The exhaust ports are spaced apart between the top wall and base and are at constant certain distances from the top wall and base.
problem: A fume hood with a reaction chamber needs to be constructed in a scalable, modular manner while providing uniform exhaust of gases and air through the structure.
constraint: The modules must be geometrically identical to allow scalable assembly, and the exhaust ports must be positioned at constant distances from the walls to maintain uniform airflow distribution while preserving structural integrity of the cylindrical form.
mechanism: A plurality of identical arcuate segments are assembled to form a cylindrical reaction chamber. Each segment contributes outer and inner walls that define an annular exhaust passage between them, with exhaust openings positioned at uniform intervals along the passage to ensure consistent gas extraction throughout the chamber length.
mechanism_raw: Three or four identical arcuate modules are assembled to form a partial or full cylindrical structure. Each module contributes an upstanding outer wall, upper wall, and base that together define the reaction chamber. An inner wall spaced interior to the outer wall creates an exhaust passageway between them, with exhaust ports spaced apart at constant distances from the top wall and base to ensure uniform gas extraction along the entire length.

abstract: A stern tube seal device providing a seal about a rotatable shaft includes an annular case member arranged about the outer periphery of a shaft, a gap between the annular case member and the shaft sealed by a plurality of lip seals, a floating ring seal or a pressure type hollow ring is arranged in the middle of the lip seal, and pressure fluid is charged into the rear portion of the floating ring seal or into the pressure type hollow ring to enhance the sealing effect by the pressure of the fluid.
problem: Sealing a rotatable shaft in a stern tube while maintaining effective sealing under dynamic conditions.
constraint: Balancing fluid pressure to improve sealing without causing excessive friction or damage to the seal components.
mechanism: Apply pressurized fluid to a movable sealing element positioned around a rotating shaft to dynamically increase contact force against the shaft surface, compensating for wear, misalignment, or dynamic displacement.
mechanism_raw: Applying pressurized fluid to a floating ring or hollow ring seal to dynamically enhance sealing force against the shaft, compensating for wear or misalignment.

abstract: The ski binding comprises a toe iron 1 and a rear soleholding device 2. The toe iron is shiftable between a position for ski touring and a position for downhill skiing. A U-shaped bearing bracket 7 and a plug-in pivot 12 are provided. By the two legs 8 and 9 of the bearing bracket the pivot is spaced from the ski a distance which somewhat exceeds the thickness of the sole of the boot. As a result, the plug-in pivot 12 can be used as a holding-down member and as an abutment. The edge portion of the sole is adapted to extend under the plug-in pivot and to be forced against the plug-in pivot 12 by the rear soleholding device. The rear soleholding device comprises a holding-down member 3 for effecting a release in a vertical direction and also comprises a slide 5 for effecting a release in a lateral direction under an overload. In that position the ski binding is used as a downhill binding. Alternatively, the sole of the boot can be connected to the bearing bracket 7 by the plug-in pivot 12 if the latter extends through a bearing bushing 20 provided in the sole 17 of the boot and is held by the legs 8 and 9 at the same time. In that case the boot is pivotable on the plug-in pivot. In such touring position of the ski binding the rear soleholding device is inactive.
problem: Switching between a flexible touring mode and a rigid downhill mode in a ski binding while ensuring secure boot attachment in both states.
constraint: Ensuring the pivot can withstand both rotational forces in touring mode and vertical/lateral release forces in downhill mode without failure.
mechanism: Implement a dual-mode pivot component that switches between a fixed retention function in one operational state and a rotational pivot function in another state, enabled by a structural bracket that spatially separates the pivot from the base surface.
mechanism_raw: A dual-function pivot component that acts as a holding-down member in downhill mode and a pivot point in touring mode, enabled by a U-shaped bracket spacing the pivot from the ski.

abstract: A process for manufacturing an enriched fructose syrup, which is characterized in that dextrose is crystallized from a relatively high solids feed syrup containing fructose and dextrose and then another relatively dilute (or lower solids) fructose containing diluent syrup is added to enhance separation of the dextrose crystals from the mother liquor. Process can be adjusted to yield dextrose monohydrate or anhydrous alpha dextrose crystalline product in addition to an enriched fructose syrup.
problem: Separating dextrose crystals from a fructose-containing syrup to produce an enriched fructose product.
constraint: Optimizing the timing and proportion of dilution to maximize crystal recovery while minimizing energy or processing costs.
mechanism: Perform sequential crystallization of a target compound from a high-solids feed, followed by controlled dilution with a secondary syrup to reduce viscosity and enhance separation of crystals from the mother liquor.
mechanism_raw: Crystallizing dextrose from a high-solids feed syrup, then introducing a dilute fructose syrup to reduce viscosity and enhance crystal-mother liquor separation.

abstract: A multiple use hand tool comprises an elongated housing defining a handle having a longitudinal through bore in which is slideably mounted a tool holding member for holding a utility knife blade at one end and a marking crayon at the other end for selective extension from the respective end of the handle for use. The tool holding member is releasable for sliding from the housing for removal and replacement of a tool.
reason: The mechanism is a straightforward mechanical design (slideable, removable tool holder) without a deeper causal principle that generalizes beyond the specific tool application.

abstract: A process for producing an instant starch based pie filling mix by premixing natural sweetener and fat, subsequently dry mixing remaining sweetener, starch and maltodextrin with the pre-mixed fat and sweetener until a flowable powder results. The no-bake pie filling upon hydration sets to a firm glossy, smooth and creamy texture.
problem: Creating a no-bake starch-based pie filling mix that forms a firm, smooth texture upon hydration.
constraint: Controlling the mixing sequence and ingredient ratios to balance flowability of the powder with the desired texture development during hydration.
mechanism: Premix a hydrophobic binder and a cohesive additive to form a structured base, then dry-blend with a water-absorbing polymer and a viscosity-modifying agent to ensure uniform dispersion and controlled hydration behavior.
mechanism_raw: Premixing fat and natural sweetener to create a cohesive base, then dry-mixing with starch and maltodextrin to ensure uniform dispersion and prevent clumping during hydration.

abstract: A filament jet entangler comprising a supporting bracket and a jet insert mounted thereon, the jet insert including a cylindrical yarn confining passage extending therethrough and intersected by a pair of coplanar fluid jet ports whose axes intersect at the cylindrical wall defining the yarn confining passage and define an included angle of about 48.degree..
problem: Entangling filaments using fluid jets in a confined space while maintaining structural integrity of the yarn.
constraint: The included angle of the jet ports must balance entanglement efficiency with minimal structural damage to the yarn, while the cylindrical confinement ensures localized interaction.
mechanism: Multiple fluid streams are directed to intersect within a confined passage at an angle that creates controlled collision zones, where the interaction between the streams and the passing material causes entanglement while the confinement limits the interaction to a localized region.
mechanism_raw: Intersecting fluid jet ports at a specific angle (48 degrees) within a cylindrical passage create controlled turbulence and collision zones that entangle filaments as they pass through the confined space.

abstract: An improved model steam generator for simulating the conditions within a nuclear steam generator in order to monitor the condition of the heat exchange tubes and tubesheet of the nuclear steam generator is disclosed herein. The improved model steam generator includes a highly effective separator assembly for separating water droplets entrained within the steam flowing out of the outlet of the secondary side of the generator formed from a plurality of separator grids, each of which includes an array of semi-cylindrical deflector members. The grids are vertically stacked with the deflector members transversely disposed to the flow of steam generated by the model steam generator. Each of the parallel arrays of deflector members in each grid is angularly disposed approximately 45.degree. to the deflector members in the grids above it and below in order to provide a tortuous path for the flow of steam ascending therethrough. The separator assembly removes proportionately more water droplets from the steam generated by the model steam generator, which in turn allows it to accurately simulate the sludge accumulation characteristics of the nuclear steam generator being monitored. The model steam generator also includes a bankable condenser assembly which greatly enhances its turn-down ratio, as well as a feedwater pre-heater which allows it to accurately simulate the thermohydraulic conditions at a variety of points on the tubesheet of the nuclear steam generator.
problem: Separating water droplets from steam in a model steam generator to accurately simulate nuclear steam generator conditions.
constraint: The angular offset between grids and vertical stacking must maximize droplet removal while maintaining steam flow efficiency and minimizing pressure drop.
mechanism: A series of transversely oriented flow-deflecting elements are arranged in a vertical stack with angular offsets between adjacent elements, creating a tortuous flow path that forces the continuous phase to repeatedly change direction, causing the dispersed phase to separate due to differential inertia.
mechanism_raw: Vertically stacked separator grids with transversely disposed deflectors angled 45 degrees relative to adjacent grids create a tortuous flow path that forces steam to change direction repeatedly, causing entrained droplets to separate due to inertia.

abstract: Flexible non-distortable handcraft sheet materials, including needlework fabrics, adaptable for receiving printed designs, patterns, photographs and craft instructional information and the methodology for producing the materials with the designs, patterns and photographs and instructional information printed thereon. Material alignment and feed features are located along the parallel edges of the materials for moving same through a computer-directed printer. In accordance with the methodology visual information in the form of designs, patterns, photographs, flat art work, still objects, live objects, etc. is converted into digital information through a digitizer with the digitized image information thereafter fed to a computer for manipulation and editing by software and keyboard direction and for conversion to visual image information for CRT display and for utilization by a computer printer as imprinted graphic information. The flexible handcraft sheet materials bearing printer feed features include: paper and paper laminates; leather, suede, simulated leather, paper-leather and plastic-leather laminates; paper-thin woods, wood veneers and wood alminates with paper or plastic; laminates including non-woven, spun-bonded random fiber plastic sheet; plastic and paper-plastic laminates; foils and foil laminates; and like craft materials.
reason: The patent describes a product design (flexible sheet materials with printed information and edge feed features) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The digital conversion and printing methodology are standard processes, and the material alignment features are specific to printer hardware.

abstract: An embroidery hoop fixture for releasably retaining a fabric swatch between a base member having an opening with a beveled edge on which a fabric swatch is supported in cooperation with a pair of clamping sectors positioned on the base member and fabric swatch for releasably retaining the fabric swatch with the sectors forming a coincident opening with the base member opening.
