The sectors are provided with depending base member beveled lugs for cooperative releasable engagement with the base member beveled edge. The pair of sectors is yieldably connected together for releasable clamping engagement of the sectors to the base member by means of the depending lugs.
reason: The patent describes a mechanical clamping fixture using beveled lugs and sectors for fabric retention. While functional, this is a standard mechanical interlock design without a novel causal principle that could transfer to other fields.

abstract: This transport is effected by means of an injector, e.g. while inserting a weft thread into a weaving machine. In order to therewith keep the air consumption as low as possible the diameter of the discharge tube is made as small as possible. For nevertheless increasing the force imparted to the thread and thereby its directional stability the invention uses with an injector for subsonic inlet flow of the gas a discharge tube which widens along a very small conical angle, such that over its full length the gas obtains the speed of sound. With an injector for supersonic flow of the inlet gas this supersonic velocity is maintained along the full length of the discharge tube likewise by widening the discharge tube along a very small conical angle. The directional stability of the thread is further increased if, by keeping constant the cross-sectional area of the discharge tube, it is flattened in the direction perpendicular to the plane of the warp threads.
problem: Reducing air consumption in a pneumatic thread injector while maintaining directional stability of the thread during insertion into a weaving machine.
constraint: The conical expansion angle and cross-sectional flattening must balance air consumption reduction with sufficient force and directional control for the thread.
mechanism: A discharge conduit that gradually expands along a small angle maintains supersonic flow velocity over its length to maximize momentum transfer to the conveyed element. Cross-sectional flattening of the conduit perpendicular to the target orientation constrains the flow geometry to stabilize the element's direction.
mechanism_raw: A discharge tube that widens along a small conical angle maintains sonic gas speed over its full length, maximizing force transfer to the thread. Flattening the tube perpendicular to warp threads further stabilizes the thread's direction by constraining airflow geometry.

abstract: The exterior of successive filter cigarettes, filter rod sections or other rod-shaped articles of the tobacco processing industry is monitored for the presence of various defects including absence or improper orientation of filter mouthpieces, improperly applied or outwardly projecting uniting bands, absence of roundness and/or others by directing a beam of radiation along successive articles while they move sideways in the flutes of a drum-shaped conveyor. The beams of radiation are influenced by defects and are thereupon monitored for the purposes of generating signals which are indicative of defects, if any. The beam of radiation extends all the way along the full length of each article and can also extend partially or around the entire circumference of each article.
problem: Detecting defects (absence or improper orientation of filter mouthpieces, improperly applied or outwardly projecting uniting bands, absence of roundness, etc.) in successive rod-shaped articles as they move along a production line.
constraint: The articles move sideways in flutes of a drum-shaped conveyor, so the detection system must operate on high-speed moving objects while providing full-length and circumferential coverage without stopping the articles.
mechanism: A radiation beam is directed along each moving article such that defects modulate the beam's intensity or pattern. The modulated beam is monitored to generate electrical signals indicative of specific defects. The beam geometry extends along the full length of each article and can also extend partially or around the entire circumference, enabling multi-dimensional defect detection on continuously moving objects.
mechanism_raw: A radiation beam is directed along each moving article such that defects modulate the beam's intensity or pattern. The modulated beam is monitored to generate electrical signals indicative of specific defects. The beam geometry extends along the full length of each article and can also extend partially or around the entire circumference, enabling multi-dimensional defect detection on continuously moving objects.

abstract: A constant speed hydraulic drive comprising a variable displacement hydraulic pump controlled to maintain a constant flow of hydraulic fluid even though a prime mover therefor is subject to speed variations. The constant flow rate delivered by the hydraulic pump is at a rate sufficient to drive a load hydraulic motor at a predetermined speed when the load hydraulic motor is subject to any given load. A pilot operated relief valve proportionally bleeds hydraulic fluid from ahead of the hydraulic motor in accordance with the speed and load of the hydraulic motor. And an electrical means provides a varying control signal to the pilot operated relief valve which is responsive to the total pulse error between those representative of motor speed and a predetermined speed to provide a first speed command signal greater than the predetermined speed, and a second speed command signal which modifies the first speed command signal by the difference in the actual speed from the first speed command signal, whereby the speed of the hydraulic motor is maintained at the predetermined speed.
problem: Maintaining a hydraulic motor at a predetermined constant speed despite speed variations in the prime mover and varying load conditions on the motor.
constraint: The system must compensate simultaneously for both upstream prime mover speed variations and downstream load variations while keeping the output speed constant, requiring a dual-error feedback loop with cascaded command signals.
mechanism: A variable displacement pump maintains constant hydraulic fluid flow. A pilot-operated relief valve proportionally bleeds fluid based on motor speed and load. An electrical control system generates a first speed command signal greater than the predetermined speed based on total pulse error between motor speed and the target, then generates a second speed command signal that modifies the first by the difference between actual speed and the first command, creating a two-stage feedback correction that drives the relief valve to maintain constant motor speed.
mechanism_raw: A variable displacement pump maintains constant hydraulic fluid flow. A pilot-operated relief valve proportionally bleeds fluid based on motor speed and load. An electrical control system generates a first speed command signal greater than the predetermined speed based on total pulse error between motor speed and the target, then generates a second speed command signal that modifies the first by the difference between actual speed and the first command, creating a two-stage feedback correction that drives the relief valve to maintain constant motor speed.
residual_terms: ["variable displacement pump", "pilot-operated relief valve", "proportionally bleeds", "two-stage feedback correction", "cascaded command signals"]

abstract: An apparatus for hardening cores and/or molds made of sand with the addition of hardenable binding agents, which are used for casting molded bodies from flowable substances, is described, whereby an amount, predetermined by metering devices controlled via control valves, of the substance which causes the binding agent to harden is introduced into the core or mold by aid of compressed air the rate of flow of which is regulatable by a regulating valve, whereby this substance is mixed with this compressed air, and the regulating valve is automatically controlled according to a predetermined schedule. The apparatus can be carried out with considerably fewer components and the necessary control means can in particular be designed much more simply if, according to one embodiment, the regulating valve is controlled by means of a proportional pressure regulating valve which is operated by an external control means which also controls the other control valves. As an alternative to this, the regulating valve can be controlled, according to a second embodiment, via a preadjustable pressure regulating valve and a directional valve which is controlled electrically or pneumatically.
problem: Introducing a controlled, predetermined amount of a hardening substance into sand cores or molds to cure binding agents, with automatic regulation according to a predetermined schedule.
constraint: The apparatus must achieve precise, scheduled delivery of the hardening substance using compressed air as a carrier while minimizing the number of components and simplifying the control means.
mechanism: Compressed air is mixed with the hardening substance and delivered through a regulating valve whose flow rate is automatically controlled according to a predetermined schedule. The regulating valve is controlled by either a proportional pressure regulating valve driven by an external control means (which also controls other control valves), or by a preadjustable pressure regulating valve combined with an electrically or pneumatically controlled directional valve. Metering devices controlled via control valves determine the predetermined amount of hardening substance introduced.
mechanism_raw: Compressed air is mixed with the hardening substance and delivered through a regulating valve whose flow rate is automatically controlled according to a predetermined schedule. The regulating valve is controlled by either a proportional pressure regulating valve driven by an external control means (which also controls other control valves), or by a preadjustable pressure regulating valve combined with an electrically or pneumatically controlled directional valve. Metering devices controlled via control valves determine the predetermined amount of hardening substance introduced.
residual_terms: ["compressed air", "hardening substance", "regulating valve", "proportional pressure regulating valve", "predetermined schedule", "metering devices"]

abstract: A chuck has a rear chuck part centered on a rear axis and adapted to be secured to the spindle of a drill for rotation about the rear axis, a front chuck part centered on a front axis, and a universal joint interconnecting the two parts for joint rotation about the rear axis with the front axis movable between a position on the rear axis and a position with the front axis intersecting and skew, that is nonparallel, to the rear axis. Jaws on the front chuck part can be radially displaced thereon relative to the front axis to clamp a tool--a tap or drill bit--at the front axis in the front part. A locking element carried on one of the parts is engageable with the other part for holding the parts with the axes coaxial and nondisplaceable relative to each other.
problem: Holding and driving a tool (tap or drill bit) at a front axis that can be positioned at various angles relative to the spindle axis, while also allowing the axes to be locked coaxial when needed.
constraint: The tool must be clamped at the front axis while the front axis can be angularly misaligned relative to the rear axis for operation, yet the system must be capable of locking the axes coaxial to eliminate misalignment when precision is needed.
mechanism: A rear chuck part is secured to the spindle for rotation about a rear axis. A front chuck part, centered on a front axis, is connected to the rear part via a universal joint that allows the front axis to move between a coaxial position (aligned with the rear axis) and a skew position (intersecting and nonparallel to the rear axis). Jaws on the front chuck part are radially displaced relative to the front axis to clamp the tool. A locking element selectively engages between the parts to hold them with axes coaxial and nondisplaceable when precise alignment is required.
mechanism_raw: A rear chuck part is secured to the spindle for rotation about a rear axis. A front chuck part, centered on a front axis, is connected to the rear part via a universal joint that allows the front axis to move between a coaxial position (aligned with the rear axis) and a skew position (intersecting and nonparallel to the rear axis). Jaws on the front chuck part are radially displaced relative to the front axis to clamp the tool. A locking element selectively engages between the parts to hold them with axes coaxial and nondisplaceable when precise alignment is required.
residual_terms: ["universal joint", "coaxial position", "skew position", "radially displaced jaws", "locking element", "spindle"]

abstract: An evaporative cooler is disclosed incorporating a horizontally disposed hollow cylindrical pad mounted for rotation above a water tray. The cylindrical pad extends into water placed in the tray and is rotated to continuously immerse a portion of the pad. The pad is supported through a plurality of rollers contacting circumferential bands positioned thereon; the rollers providing all of the support and all of the rotational force to the cylindrical pad.
problem: Providing evaporative cooling by continuously exposing fresh wetted surface area of a pad to the air stream while maintaining the pad in a water reservoir.
constraint: The pad must be continuously immersed in water while rotating, and all support and rotational force must be delivered through rollers contacting circumferential bands on the pad, eliminating the need for internal bearings or submerged drive mechanisms.
mechanism: A horizontally disposed hollow cylindrical pad is mounted for rotation above a water tray. The pad extends into the water in the tray and is rotated to continuously immerse a portion of the pad, ensuring that wetted surface is constantly renewed as the pad turns. The pad is supported entirely through a plurality of rollers that contact circumferential bands positioned on the pad, with the rollers providing both all structural support and all rotational driving force to the cylindrical pad.
mechanism_raw: A horizontally disposed hollow cylindrical pad is mounted for rotation above a water tray. The pad extends into the water in the tray and is rotated to continuously immerse a portion of the pad, ensuring that wetted surface is constantly renewed as the pad turns. The pad is supported entirely through a plurality of rollers that contact circumferential bands positioned on the pad, with the rollers providing both all structural support and all rotational driving force to the cylindrical pad.
residual_terms: ["hollow cylindrical pad", "water tray", "circumferential bands", "rollers", "structural support", "rotational driving force"]

abstract: Apparatus for dehydrating slurries such as water based drilling fluids heavily laden with drill cuttings and other earth solids comprising a rotating drum which is heated by combustion of a fuel air mixture to generate relatively large quantities of combustion products for heating in an enclosed chamber defined by said drum. The slurry to be dehydrated is injected into the interior of the drum or against the outer sidewall thereof for rapid exposure and substantially flash evaporation of the slurry liquids. An outer housing may be constructed around the drum and in one embodiment the drum is arranged inclined to the horizontal with the slurry introduced into the interior of the drum and the combustion chamber formed between the outer housing and the drum. In another embodiment the combustion chamber is formed on the interior of the drum and the evaporation chamber is formed between the drum and the outer housing. The exhaust flues for the evaporation chamber and the combustion chamber are interconnected to provide for induced flow of gases through a stack portion of one of the flues and to dilute the vapor flow stream to minimize the generation of condensation clouds or ice fogs during operations in cold environments.
problem: Efficient dehydration of slurries (e.g., drilling fluids) in cold environments while minimizing condensation clouds or ice fogs during operation.
constraint: Balancing heat generation from combustion with induced gas flow rates to avoid condensation without compromising evaporation efficiency.
mechanism: A heat source generates hot gases to evaporate liquid from a moving material, while a flow management system induces gas movement to dilute vapor streams and maintain temperature gradients, preventing condensation by balancing heat generation with gas flow rates.
mechanism_raw: Combustion-heated rotating drum generates hot gases for flash evaporation of slurry liquids, while interconnected exhaust flues induce gas flow through a stack to dilute vapor streams and prevent condensation by maintaining temperature gradients.

abstract: A contact or spectacle or implant lens has positive diffractive power which introduces negative longitudinal chromatic aberration that more than counteracts, and is preferably greater than twice, the natural positive longitudinal chromatic aberration of the eye. The residual negative longitudinal chromatic aberration enables the eye/brain system to perform tasks by concentrating on the appropriate color component at the different respective distances without need to accommodate.
problem: Correcting chromatic aberration in vision without requiring the eye to accommodate for different focal distances.
constraint: The lens's negative chromatic aberration must exceed twice the eye's natural positive aberration to ensure residual correction across all focal ranges.
mechanism: An optical element with opposing chromatic aberration introduces a corrective effect that counteracts the eye's natural aberration, enabling selective focus on color components across varying distances without requiring accommodation.
mechanism_raw: A lens with positive diffractive power introduces negative longitudinal chromatic aberration that counteracts the eye's natural positive aberration, enabling the brain to select appropriate color components for focus at varying distances.

abstract: A heat exchanger using heat of exhaust gas has a housing, through which the exhaust gas passes, and is provided with a heat storage insert positioned in the housing. Tubes containing air or water receiving heat from the exhaust gas are also located within the housing. The heat storage insert is formed of a plurality of bricks having hollows which form passages for the exhaust gas. The bricks at least in the regions of the passages are formed of a material which adsorbs surfur compounds contained in the exhaust gas.
problem: Recovering heat from exhaust gases while simultaneously removing sulfur pollutants in a heat exchanger system.
constraint: Material composition must balance thermal storage capacity with sulfur adsorption efficiency without degrading under high-temperature exhaust conditions.
mechanism: A dual-function material with porous pathways simultaneously adsorbs pollutants from a gas stream and stores thermal energy, transferring heat to a fluid medium while maintaining structural integrity under high-temperature conditions.
mechanism_raw: Heat storage bricks with hollow gas passages adsorb sulfur compounds from exhaust gases, while the same bricks store thermal energy to transfer heat to air or water tubes within the housing.

abstract: A plurality of music number data records of several hundreds of music numbers are sequentially recorded on a magnetic tape, such as a compact cassette tape with a blank space therebetween. The recorded music number data records are continuously and randomly reproduced and stored in digital form in a RAM so as to continuously auto-play a plurality of music numbers by means of a tone generator.
problem: Continuously auto-playing multiple music numbers from a sequential magnetic tape medium while enabling random access to individual tracks.
constraint: RAM storage capacity must accommodate continuous data streaming from tape while maintaining real-time playback without buffer underflow.
mechanism: A sequential data medium is read continuously into a buffer storage, decoupling the sequential reading process from non-linear playback by enabling random access to buffered data segments while maintaining real-time streaming.
mechanism_raw: Music data records are sequentially recorded on tape with blank spaces, then continuously reproduced and stored in digital RAM for random access playback via a tone generator, decoupling sequential tape reading from non-linear playback.

abstract: A cutter apparatus is disclosed for cutting elongated food products such as french fry potato strips, to cut them in two or to remove defects. The cutter apparatus includes two independently operated knives which are actuated by pneumatic cylinders controlled by solenoid valves that apply air pulses to such cylinders for fast operation. The valves are operated in response to control signals produced by light sensor means which senses the defect and causes a central processing unit of a computer to produce the control signals. The knife blades are each connected to the piston rod of the cylinder by a flexible resilient connector for causing the blade to move in a non-linear manner downward in response to linear movement of the piston rod for cutting the defect from the food product while such product is moving along a conveyor belt beneath such cutter, without arresting movement of the food product. The knife blade is returned to a raised static position by a rubber band strap member secured to the lower end of the piston rod. Two independently controlled knives are employed to enable the cutter to remove defects of different lengths with little waste or to cut product to different lengths.
problem: Cutting defects or dividing elongated food products (e.g., french fries) without halting their movement along a conveyor belt.
constraint: Coordinating dual knife actuation timing and blade flexibility to handle variable defect lengths or cut positions without waste or product stoppage.
mechanism: Two independently actuated cutting elements with flexible motion converters transform linear actuator movement into non-linear blade motion, enabling precise cuts on moving products via sensor-triggered coordination without halting product flow.
mechanism_raw: Two independently controlled pneumatic knives with flexible resilient connectors convert linear piston motion into non-linear blade movement, enabling precise cuts on moving products while light sensors trigger CPU-controlled actuation.

abstract: The present invention relates to the field of compound pyrotechnic products. The invention relates to a three-step, solvent-free process for the manufacture of compound pyrotechnic products containing a thermosetting binder obtained by reaction of a polyhydroxylated prepolymer with a diisocyanate, which process is characterized in that: PA1 in a first step the said prepolymer is mixed with an energetic charge and with a quantity of diisocyanate representing 50 to 90% of the required stoichiometric quantity, PA1 in a second step the remainder required to attain the said stoichiometric quantity is added and, after mixing, the pasty mixture thus obtained is extruded, PA1 in a third step the crosslinking of the thermosetting binder is completed hot. The invention makes it possible to obtain industrially, by extrusion, small-diameter pyrotechnic products containing a thermosetting binder without restriction on the "pot life" period. The invention is particularly suitable for the production of compound propellent powders for arms.
problem: Manufacturing small-diameter pyrotechnic products with thermosetting binders without restricting the usable working time (pot life) during extrusion.
constraint: Balancing stoichiometric diisocyanate addition (50-90% initially) to maintain workable viscosity during extrusion while ensuring complete crosslinking in the final step.
mechanism: Staged reaction control in a thermosetting binder system: a portion of a diisocyanate reactant is mixed initially to enable shaping via extrusion while maintaining workable viscosity, with the remaining diisocyanate added post-shaping to complete crosslinking and curing under heat, thereby decoupling the shaping phase from the final curing phase.
mechanism_raw: Staged reaction control: partial prepolymer-diisocyanate mixing allows initial shaping via extrusion before full crosslinking, with the remaining diisocyanate added post-extrusion to complete curing under heat. This decouples shaping from final curing.

abstract: A predrying tower serves for heat-treating a vertically conducted length of material. In addition to infrared heating rods arranged on each side of the length of material and over the treatment height of the drying tower, respectively one air supply box is arranged bilaterally of the length of material. The air supply box extends over the height and width of the drying tower, with air slots oriented to direct air toward the length of material. In order to obtain a circulating air system, the air is exhausted above the treatment zone over the width of the length of material and conducted to a fan arranged at the end face of the drying tower, this fan blowing the treatment air downwardly in an air recycle chamber arranged likewise at the end face of the drying tower. An air ramming or air collecting chamber is arranged on the underside of the drying tower over the operating width, wherein the accelerated air is laterally introduced and exits upwardly via a heating device into the air conducting box.
problem: Efficiently heat-treating vertically conducted material in a drying tower while maintaining uniform temperature and airflow distribution.
constraint: Coordinating air slot orientation, fan placement, and heating device positioning to ensure consistent heat transfer across the entire treatment height and width without dead zones.
mechanism: A closed-loop airflow system integrating convective and radiant (infrared) heating: lateral air supply directs airflow toward the material, while exhaust and fan-driven recycling chambers create a recirculating path that combines convective heat transfer from airflow with radiant heat from infrared sources to ensure uniform temperature distribution across the treatment zone.
mechanism_raw: Integrated infrared heating and circulating air system: lateral air supply boxes direct airflow toward the material, while exhaust and fan-driven recycling chambers create a closed-loop airflow path that combines convective and radiant heating.
residual_terms: ["infrared heating", "convective heating", "radiant heating", "closed-loop airflow", "air supply", "exhaust", "fan-driven recycling"]

abstract: This invention relates to a manufacturing process for plate or forging (bar, stamp work or the like) of ferrite-austenite two-phase stainless steel, containing C at 0.03% or below, Si at 2.0% or below, Mn at 2.0% or below, Cr at 25 to 35%, Ni at 6 to 15%, N at 0.35% or below, and Fe and inevitable impurity for the remainder with or without adding B at 0.001 to 0.030% with the following nickel balance value specified at -3 to -9 and comprising an average crystal grain size at 0.015 mm or below from heating an ingot of the above mentioned ferrite-austenite two-phase stainless steel at 1,200.degree. C. or below and keeping a forging ratio by hot working at 5 or over. EQU Ni balance value=Ni %+0.5 Mn %+30.times.(C+N) %-1.1(Cr %+1.5 Si %)+8.2
problem: Achieving a fine grain structure (≤0.015 mm) in ferrite-austenite two-phase stainless steel while maintaining specific compositional and processing parameters.
constraint: Maintaining the nickel balance formula (Ni% + 0.5 Mn% + 30(C+N)% - 1.1(Cr% + 1.5 Si%) + 8.2) within the specified range to prevent unwanted phase transformations during hot working.
mechanism: Controlled thermomechanical processing of a ferrite-austenite two-phase stainless steel: heating the material to a temperature ≤1200°C followed by hot working with a forging ratio ≥5 refines the grain size to ≤0.015 mm, while maintaining a nickel balance value (-3 to -9) ensures phase stability during processing.
mechanism_raw: Controlled thermomechanical processing: heating an ingot to ≤1200°C followed by hot working with a forging ratio ≥5 refines grain size, while a calculated nickel balance value (-3 to -9) ensures phase stability during processing.
residual_terms: ["ferrite-austenite two-phase stainless steel", "nickel balance formula", "hot working", "forging ratio", "grain size", "phase stability", "thermometallurgical processing"]

abstract: An electro-chemical electric power generating apparatus characterized by first and second electro-chemical fuel cells. Each cell includes a case containing spaced anode and cathode plates, an electrolyte between the plates and an external electric circuit connected therebetween. The apparatus next includes a steam-methane reformer to reform steam and methane to hydrogen enriched gas fuel. The cathode and anode fuels of the first cell are methanol and hydrogen and the byproducts of chemical reaction thereof are water and methane gas. The cathode and anode fuels of the second cell are oxygen and hydrogen and the byproduct of chemical reaction thereof is water. The methane gas byproduct of the first cell and the water byproduct of both cells are conducted to the steam-methane reformer and are reformed thereby into hydrogen enriched fuel gas which is conducted to and feeds the anodes of both of the cells.
problem: Efficiently generating electrical power using electrochemical fuel cells while recycling byproducts to sustain fuel supply.
constraint: Balancing the chemical reactions in both fuel cells and the reformer to ensure continuous hydrogen production without accumulating unreacted byproducts or depleting key reactants.
mechanism: Closed-loop byproduct recycling in an electrochemical power generation system: methane and water produced in a first fuel cell (methanol-hydrogen reaction) are fed back into a steam-methane reformer to regenerate hydrogen-rich fuel, which is reused in both the first and second fuel cells to sustain continuous hydrogen production.
mechanism_raw: Closed-loop byproduct recycling: methane and water produced in the first fuel cell (methanol-hydrogen reaction) are fed back into a steam-methane reformer to regenerate hydrogen-rich fuel, which is reused in both cells.

abstract: A vertical progressive lumber dryer has a plurality of vertically spaced functional zones through which lumber formed into units pass. Each unit rests atop a base and each layer of boards in the stack is separated by sticker means. Predetermined appropriate operating conditions are selected for the drying medium as well as other parts of the process. After a car has completed the last step within the dryer, it is removed and the dryed lumber sent for further processing.
reason: The patent describes a generic vertical progressive lumber dryer with functional zones and sticker separation, but does not specify a novel causal mechanism for solving a unique problem. The zoning and sticker arrangement are standard practices in lumber drying, lacking a transferable functional principle beyond conventional drying techniques.

abstract: An arrangement for transporting, storing, and blending tobacco employs a plurality of ventilated containers, each containing bales of a designated grade of tobacco. Containers are stored side-by-side and stacked several containers high, and rows of stacked containers are placed back-to-back so that all of the doors face outwardly. Following storage, the containers with various grades of tobacco are moved to a blending conveyor belt, and bales from the various containers are combined on the belt to form moxules of tobacco of a desired blend.
problem: Efficiently storing and accessing multiple grades of tobacco bales for blending while maintaining spatial organization.
constraint: Balancing storage density (stacking and back-to-back rows) with accessibility (all doors facing outward for retrieval).
mechanism: Modular storage units arranged in a grid configuration with accessible interfaces on all sides, enabling sequential retrieval and transport of contents while maintaining spatial organization through stacking and adjacent placement.
mechanism_raw: Modular ventilated containers arranged side-by-side and stacked in rows with outward-facing doors, enabling sequential access and transport to a blending conveyor for combining bales of different grades.

abstract: A light sensing apparatus comprising a solid-state photocell responsive to low levels of light connected to an impedance matching buffer stage, a gain controlled amplifier stage and an output amplifier stage; a gain control network controlled by a temperature sensor for receiving an amplified signal from said output stage, the gain being adjustable to compensate for temperature dependance of the photocell signal.
problem: Maintaining accurate light sensing signals despite temperature-induced variations in photocell output.
constraint: Achieving real-time compensation without introducing signal distortion or excessive complexity in the feedback loop.
mechanism: A feedback control system dynamically adjusts signal amplification based on environmental conditions to counteract sensor output drift, maintaining measurement accuracy without introducing distortion.
mechanism_raw: A temperature sensor monitors environmental conditions and dynamically adjusts the gain of an amplifier stage to counteract temperature-dependent signal drift in the photocell.
residual_terms: ["feedback control system", "signal amplification", "environmental conditions", "sensor output drift"]

abstract: A towable dolly comprises a platform for supporting an object either alone or on a standard dolly, a wheel assembly pivotally secured to the forward end of the platform, and a lifting or tilting assembly for tilting the platform upwardly at its rear end relative to the wheel assembly so that it is raised from the ground in its towing position. A tow bar assembly projects forwardly from the wheel assembly for connection to a standard vehicle tow bar connector.
problem: Towing a platform while keeping it elevated off the ground to avoid dragging during transport.
constraint: Ensuring stable towing orientation without compromising the platform's ability to return to a horizontal position when stationary.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system couples the position of a pivoting support element to the orientation of a platform, automatically adjusting the platform's angle during towing to maintain elevation while allowing return to a neutral position when stationary.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting wheel assembly and rear tilting mechanism mechanically link the platform's angle to the wheel position, automatically lifting the rear end when the dolly is towed.
residual_terms: ["mechanical linkage system", "pivoting support element", "platform orientation", "neutral position"]

abstract: An electrostatic precipitator is fed high voltage pulses by a pulse generating circuit including a high voltage transformer and a first thyristor switch connected in series with a primary winding of the transformer. Magnetic saturation of the core of the high voltage transformer is prevented by recurrently short circuiting the primary winding of the transformer by means of a second thyristor switch connected in parallel to the primary winding. The second thyristor switch is closed for a period of time extending from a first instant following a high voltage pulse crest to a second instant at or before the start of a pulse generating cycle subsequent to the pulse crest.
problem: Preventing magnetic core saturation in a high-voltage transformer during repetitive pulsed operation.
constraint: Timing the short-circuit duration to fully reset the core without disrupting the subsequent pulse generation cycle.
mechanism: A switching circuit periodically creates a controlled discharge path across a magnetic energy storage element after each operational cycle, resetting its state to prevent cumulative flux saturation without interrupting subsequent cycles.
mechanism_raw: A secondary thyristor switch periodically short-circuits the transformer's primary winding after each pulse, resetting the magnetic core to avoid residual flux buildup.
residual_terms: ["switching circuit", "controlled discharge path", "magnetic energy storage element", "flux saturation"]

abstract: A forming assembly for automatic machines for forming boxes from semi-finished flat blanks, comprises a plate support with associated suction means for the semi-finished blanks and a forming mould for the erection of the parts of the semi-finished blank intended to constitute the side walls of the box. The forming mould has simplified longitudinal and transverse forming elements which are adjustable in length, width and height, and the plate support has spring feet supported by modular blocks releasably fixed to the sides of the plate. The plate support also has suction members connectible by a system of external tubing to a vacuum source.
problem: Forming boxes of varying dimensions from flat blanks using a single forming assembly.
constraint: Maintaining structural rigidity and suction effectiveness while enabling rapid adjustment of forming dimensions.
mechanism: Adjustable forming surfaces and reconfigurable support elements with compliant mounting systems enable rapid dimensional adaptation of a forming process while maintaining structural integrity and operational effectiveness.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable longitudinal and transverse forming elements combined with modular spring-mounted blocks allow reconfiguration of the forming mold and plate support to accommodate different box sizes.
residual_terms: ["adjustable forming surfaces", "reconfigurable support elements", "compliant mounting systems", "dimensional adaptation"]

abstract: A process is disclosed for recovering fats and oils from oil fruits and oil seeds, wherein the oil fruits and oil seeds are cleaned, immediately thereafter pressed cold in a screw press without prior mechanical conditioning, and then extracted. In this process, the extraction is effected immediately after pressing by treating the oil fruits and oil seeds with countercurrently flowing carbon dioxide, ethane, ethene and/or propane at a temperature of from 40.degree. to 110.degree. C. and at a pressure of from 250 to 750 bar, for a time period of from 0.5 to 2.5 hours, with the solvent ratio lying between 5 and 30 kg solvent per 1 kg pressed cake. The separation of the extracted fats and oils from the separated solvent phase is effected by pressure reduction and/or temperature change. The invention also includes an apparatus for implementing the process.
problem: Recovering fats and oils from oil fruits and seeds efficiently without degrading the product, while maximizing yield from both mechanical pressing and solvent extraction steps.
constraint: The process must operate within a narrow window of temperature (40-110°C), pressure (250-750 bar), time (0.5-2.5 hours), and solvent-to-cake ratio (5-30 kg/kg) to achieve effective extraction without thermal or pressure-induced degradation of the oils.
mechanism: Sequential processing where material undergoes an initial mechanical extraction step without prior conditioning, followed by countercurrent flow of compressed solvent gases under controlled temperature and pressure to extract residual oils, and subsequent separation of extracted oils from solvent via pressure reduction and/or temperature change. The countercurrent flow and immediate transition between steps prevent degradation and maximize extraction efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Sequential processing where material is cold-pressed immediately without prior conditioning, then subjected to countercurrent flow of compressed solvent gases (CO2, ethane, ethene, propane) under controlled temperature and pressure to extract residual oils, followed by separation of extracted oils from solvent via pressure reduction and/or temperature change. The countercurrent flow and immediate transition between steps prevent degradation and maximize extraction efficiency.

abstract: A mounting assembly 4 is provided for a feed tube 12 of a high-temperature fluid-wall reactor of the type having a vertically oriented reactor tube heated to incandescence for emitting radiation radially inward to a reaction zone. The mounting assembly 4 comprises a tube support 34 having an opening 42 through which the feed tube 12 can pass, and a pivot seat member 30 secured to the reactor. The assembly 4 further comprises a retainer 52 for selectively fixing the orientation of the feed tube relative to the reactor, and a releasable attachment mechanism 70 for allowing the axial position of the feed tube to be adjusted relative to the assembly 4. According to the method of the invention, undesirable conditions within the reactor are detected, and the orientation of the feed tube is pivotably adjusted in response thereto for reducing undesirable reactor operating conditions.
problem: Maintaining stable operation of a high-temperature fluid-wall reactor by preventing undesirable conditions (e.g., uneven heating, poor reactant distribution, hot spots) that arise during operation.
constraint: The pivotable adjustment mechanism must function reliably in a high-temperature environment where the reactor tube is heated to incandescence, requiring materials and design that can withstand thermal stress while maintaining precise positional control.
mechanism: A feedback-controlled positioning system where undesirable reactor conditions are detected, and in response, the feed tube is pivotably adjusted relative to the reactor to redirect the flow of reactants and reduce the detected undesirable conditions. The feed tube's axial position can also be independently adjusted via a releasable attachment mechanism, allowing dynamic reconfiguration of the reactant delivery geometry.
mechanism_raw: A feedback-controlled positioning system where undesirable reactor conditions are detected, and in response, the feed tube is pivotably adjusted relative to the reactor to redirect the flow of reactants and reduce the detected undesirable conditions. The feed tube's axial position can also be independently adjusted via a releasable attachment mechanism, allowing dynamic reconfiguration of the reactant delivery geometry.

abstract: A multi-section overhead door having an impact-proof bottom panel for improved safety and durability is disclosed. The door is displaced vertically along parallel tracks to which it is coupled by means of rollers. Impact with the bottom panel of the door when in a raised position results in the disengagement of the track rollers from the bottom panel and the displacement of the bottom panel from alignment with the tracks. With the impact force removed, the bottom panel resumes its original position between the tracks to which it can be remounted by conveniently repositioning the track rollers thereon. The bottom panel includes front and rear rubber surfaces with a urethane filler therebetween and a flexible bottom nosing seal.
problem: Protecting an overhead door and its tracking system from damage caused by impact forces when the door is in a raised position, while maintaining normal operation and allowing easy recovery after impact.
constraint: The panel must be designed with sufficient flexibility and resilience to self-reset after disengagement, while maintaining enough structural integrity to function as a door panel during normal operation and to be easily remounted after impact.
mechanism: A self-resetting disengagement coupling where impact on the bottom panel causes the track rollers to disengage from the panel and the panel to displace out of alignment with the tracks, absorbing the impact energy through controlled disengagement. When the impact force is removed, the panel's inherent resilience causes it to resume its original position between the tracks, allowing remounting by repositioning the rollers.
mechanism_raw: A self-resetting disengagement coupling where impact on the bottom panel causes the track rollers to disengage from the panel and the panel to displace out of alignment with the tracks, absorbing the impact energy through controlled disengagement. When the impact force is removed, the panel's inherent resilience (rubber surfaces with urethane filler) causes it to resume its original position between the tracks, allowing remounting by repositioning the rollers.

abstract: Process for the preparation of oligosaccharides-containing products from biomass involving the use of hydrochloric acid for partly hydrolyzing biomass to easily fermentable oligosaccharides-containing products and easy recovery of the hydrochloric acid and the oligosaccharides containing products. The oligosaccharides-containing products themselves and use of the latter for the preparation of useful products like ethanol and penicillin by fermentation.
problem: Converting complex biomass into easily fermentable oligosaccharide products while enabling recovery and reuse of the hydrolysis acid, avoiding complete degradation of sugars into non-fermentable byproducts.
constraint: The hydrolysis must be carefully controlled to achieve partial rather than complete breakdown, producing oligosaccharides of the appropriate chain length for fermentation while avoiding over-hydrolysis that would yield non-fermentable byproducts or require excessive acid consumption.
mechanism: Controlled partial hydrolysis of biomass using an acid to produce specific oligosaccharide-range products that are readily fermentable, combined with a recovery system that separates and reclaims both the acid and the oligosaccharide products from the reaction mixture. The partial nature of the hydrolysis ensures the products remain in a fermentable intermediate state rather than being fully broken down into monosaccharides or degraded.
mechanism_raw: Controlled partial hydrolysis of biomass using hydrochloric acid to produce specific oligosaccharide-range products that are readily fermentable, combined with a recovery system that separates and reclaims both the hydrochloric acid and the oligosaccharide products from the reaction mixture. The partial nature of the hydrolysis ensures the products remain in a fermentable intermediate state rather than being fully broken down into monosaccharides or degraded.

abstract: A rinse aid formulation containing a low foam non-ionic surfactant, a low molecular weight poly(meth)acrylic acid and high molecular weight stabilizing polymer is provided. The stabilizing polymer, when at least about 85 percent neutralized, compatibilizes the low foam surfactant with the low molecular weight poly(meth)acrylic acid in water producing a stable, homogeneous aqueous dispersion. The neutralized low molecular weight poly(meth)acrylic acid improves wetting of the substrate by the rinse water and reduces spotting. The stabilizer and poly(meth)acrylic acid do not increase the foam or interfere with the defoaming properties of the surfactant.
problem: Formulating a stable aqueous rinse aid dispersion that combines a low-foam surfactant with a low molecular weight polyelectrolyte for improved wetting, without the components destabilizing each other or increasing foam.
constraint: The stabilizing polymer must be at least 85% neutralized to effectively compatibilize the components, and the formulation must maintain low foam characteristics without the stabilizer or poly(meth)acrylic acid interfering with the surfactant's defoaming properties.
mechanism: Using a high molecular weight stabilizing polymer as a compatibilizer that, when at least 85% neutralized, bridges and stabilizes the otherwise incompatible low-foam non-ionic surfactant and low molecular weight polyelectrolyte in an aqueous dispersion. The compatibilizer allows the mixture to remain homogeneous and stable while each component retains its function: the surfactant provides low-foam properties, and the polyelectrolyte improves wetting and reduces spotting.
mechanism_raw: Using a high molecular weight stabilizing polymer as a compatibilizer that, when at least 85% neutralized, bridges and stabilizes the otherwise incompatible low-foam non-ionic surfactant and low molecular weight poly(meth)acrylic acid in an aqueous dispersion. The compatibilizer allows the mixture to remain homogeneous and stable while each component retains its function: the surfactant provides low-foam properties, and the poly(meth)acrylic acid improves wetting and reduces spotting.

abstract: A process for the extraction of contaminants from plastics is disclosed. A plastic surface is contacted with an alcohol to extract any contaminants which have been absorbed by or adsorbed on the plastic surface. Thereafter, the plastic surface is rinsed with water to remove any remaining alcohol. The process has particular applicability in cleaning plastic bottles and plastic post-mix beverage dispensing lines.
problem: Removing contaminants that have been absorbed by or adsorbed on plastic surfaces (e.g., plastic bottles, beverage dispensing lines).
constraint: The solvent must be effective at extracting contaminants from plastic while also being water-miscible so it can be completely removed by a simple aqueous rinse, avoiding residue or secondary contamination.
mechanism: Applying a substance that simultaneously dissolves or carries away trapped material from a porous substrate and is also miscible with water, followed by an aqueous rinse that removes both the substance and the carried material, leaving no residual contamination.
mechanism_raw: Contacting the plastic surface with a solvent (alcohol) that can extract absorbed/adsorbed contaminants, then rinsing with water to remove the solvent and any remaining contaminants. The alcohol serves a dual role: it is both an effective extractant for contaminants trapped in the plastic matrix and a water-miscible fluid that can be readily flushed away in the subsequent rinse step.

abstract: Sewing machine with a control for the movement of a workholder. For the formation of edge parallel seams when sewing on labels with seam sections extending parallel to the movement axes of a cross slide system carrying the work holder, there are arranged at uniform distance from the stitch hole four transmitted light sensors, of which always only the one which can recognize the crosswise extending following edge of a seam section is switchable into readiness for operation. After a signal has been given by a sensor, the respective drive motor of the cross slide system is controlled by means of a microcomputer in such a way that the respective seam section ends exactly in the intended corner. Because of the work related feed control, a sewing program is not needed. Besides, the control automatically adapts itself to different label dimensions.
problem: Forming edge-parallel seams when sewing labels, where seam sections extend parallel to the movement axes of a cross-slide system, requiring precise termination of each seam section at intended corners.
constraint: The sensors must be positioned at a precisely known distance from the stitch point so that edge detection translates directly into positional control, and only one sensor is active at a time to avoid ambiguity in edge recognition.
mechanism: Positioning detection elements at a fixed, known displacement from a working point to sense boundaries of a moving object, activating only the detection element aligned with the relevant boundary, and using the known displacement to compute the working point's position so that motion stops precisely at a target boundary. The system adjusts automatically to varying object dimensions without pre-stored motion profiles.
mechanism_raw: Using transmitted light sensors positioned at a known fixed offset from the stitch point to detect edges of the workpiece. Only the sensor capable of recognizing the relevant crosswise-extending edge is activated at any given time. When that sensor detects the edge, a microcomputer uses the known sensor-to-tool offset to calculate the exact position and controls the drive motor to stop the feed so the seam section ends precisely at the intended corner. The system automatically adapts to different label dimensions without a pre-programmed sewing routine.
residual_terms: ["fixed displacement", "working point", "detection elements", "motion stops", "pre-stored motion profiles"]

abstract: Coordination compounds for use in therapy, the compounds having the general empirical formula EQU [Rh.sup.m X.sub.x Y.sub.y ].sup.a in which m is the oxidation state of Rh, X is at least one anionic ligand, Y is at least one neutral ligand, with the proviso that at least one of X and Y is a nitrogen donor ligand, x is an integer from 1 to 6, y is an integer from 1 to 5 or may be equal to zero, and a is a positive or negative integer from -3 to +3 or may be equal to zero. Such compounds are useful inter alia as radiosensitizers in the treatment of cancer. A preferred compound is [RhenCl.sub.4 ][enH.sub.2 ].
reason: This patent discloses a specific chemical compound (a rhodium coordination complex with nitrogen donor ligands) for use as a radiosensitizer in cancer therapy. The mechanism is a chemical/biological interaction specific to the compound's molecular structure and its interaction with biological tissue under radiation. There is no generalizable engineering or operational principle that can be transferred to a different field; it is a material/compound discovery rather than a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: An efficiency Photo-mailer item, uniquely conifigured in a special unitary panel Di-scored/Tri-sectioned format, so that Senders preferred photograph is presented through a protective glazed-aperture at the central front panel adjacent to the address indicia-space, yet the novel arrangement enables said photo to again reappear in proper orientation to view as one unfolds the panel to read the accompanying personal-letter portion, contained in relative privacy within the confines of the inside back-panel section during mailing; plus, the provision of a uniquely attractive display-modality, through result of a natural `splay-leg` effect achieved via said scored deformation of the card-stock material, in conjunction with an auxiliary retension provision for use on slick surfaces; the said aggregate folded panel sections being maintained closed during mailing via provisionary `stays`.
problem: Creating an efficient photo-mailer item that presents a sender's photograph and personal letter in a compact format suitable for mailing, while also providing an attractive display when opened.
constraint: The scored fold lines must be precisely positioned so that the photo appears in correct orientation in both the folded (mailing) and unfolded (display) configurations, while the material's natural deformation from scoring provides self-standing display capability without additional hardware.
mechanism: Forming a single sheet with multiple controlled fold lines to create distinct functional zones, where the fold lines enable controlled deformation that allows the unfolded sheet to self-support as a display. A visual element is presented through an aperture in one zone during a closed configuration and reorients into proper viewing alignment when the sheet is unfolded to reveal a secondary zone. Retaining elements hold the sheet in the closed configuration during transport.
mechanism_raw: Using a unitary panel with di-scored/tri-sectioned fold lines to create multiple functional sections from a single sheet. The scoring allows the material to deform in a controlled way, creating a natural 'splay-leg' effect that enables the unfolded panel to self-support as a display. The photo is visible through a protective glazed aperture in the central front panel during mailing, and reappears in proper orientation when the panel is unfolded to read the letter portion in the back section. Stays keep the panel closed during mailing.

abstract: This invention relates to an improved van body which is used with a container car, a freight car, and a truck and comprises inverse L-shaped side frames located at the right and left side walls of the front and the back of the floor, said side frames being so constructed that the top right and left ends thereof can contact each other at the top center when closed and separate when opened. Shields, each bridging the inverse L-shaped side frames on the same side, provide the vane opening and closing operations at both top ends.
problem: Creating a van body that can be used interchangeably with container cars, freight cars, and trucks, requiring a structure that can be opened for loading/unloading and closed to form a sealed enclosure.
constraint: The inverse L-shaped frames must be constructed so that their top ends can contact each other at the top center when closed while also being able to pivot apart when opened, and the bridging shields must provide the opening/closing force transmission without compromising the structural connection between frames.
mechanism: Using pivoting frame structures with complementary geometries that meet at a central point when closed to form an enclosed volume and separate when opened to allow access. Bridging elements connect the frames and transmit forces to move the frames between open and closed positions while maintaining structural continuity through the frame-and-bridge arrangement.
mechanism_raw: Using inverse L-shaped side frames at the front and back of the floor that can pivot to bring their top ends together at the top center when closed (forming a sealed enclosure) and separate when opened. Shields bridge between the side frames on each side, providing vane-like opening and closing operations at both top ends. The frames' geometry allows the entire structure to open and close while maintaining structural integrity through the frame-and-shield arrangement.
residual_terms: ["pivoting frame structures", "complementary geometries", "central point", "bridging elements", "structural continuity"]

abstract: Variations in pump capacity of gear pumps due to varying leakage paths occurring in otherwise identical pumps as a result of the manufacturing operation are minimized without unduly hindering the fitting of the bearings through the pump housing by maintaining the distance "TBD" between the center of the bearing journal and the bearing flat closely within tolerances and by providing a relief in the bearing periphery diametrically opposite of the flat.
problem: Variations in pump capacity of gear pumps due to manufacturing-induced leakage path inconsistencies.
constraint: Balancing precise geometric tolerances to reduce leakage variability without hindering the bearing's mechanical fit or assembly process.
mechanism: Controlling the relative positioning and surface geometry between two mechanically coupled components within tight tolerances, combined with a diametrically opposed relief feature on one component's periphery, to minimize unintended fluid pathways while preserving mechanical fit and assembly compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the geometric relationship between the bearing journal and bearing flat within tight tolerances, combined with a diametrically opposed relief on the bearing periphery, to minimize unintended leakage paths while preserving bearing fit.

abstract: A cement fluid-loss composition and its use in a well cementing process are disclosed. The cement fluid loss composition comprises an aqueous slurry of about 35 to about 90 weight percent of water based on weight percent of dry cement; and about 0.1 to about 2 weight percent of a terpolymer based on weight percent of dry cement, said terpolymer having the formula: ##STR1## wherein x is about 40 to about 98 mole %, more preferably about 50 to about 95 mole %, and most preferably about 80 to about 90, y is about 1 to about 50 mole %, more preferably about 2 to about 20 mole %, and most preferably about 5 to about 10 mole %, and z is about 1 to about 50 mole %, more preferably about 2 to about 20, and most preferably about 5 to about 10, y is equal to z, B is about 1 to about 50 mole %, more preferably about 2 to about 20 mole %, and most preferably about 5 to about 10 mole %, wherein B, y and z are less than 60 mole %.
problem: Excessive fluid loss in well cementing slurries, leading to poor cement placement and integrity.
constraint: Maintaining compatibility between the terpolymer composition and the cement slurry's water content and setting characteristics to avoid adverse reactions or performance degradation.
mechanism: Introducing a polymer with a specific monomer composition to alter the flow characteristics of a fluid system, increasing viscosity and stabilizing internal structure to reduce fluid loss through controlled rheological modification.
mechanism_raw: Using a terpolymer with a specific molar ratio of monomers (x, y, z, B) to modify the rheological properties of the cement slurry, reducing fluid loss by increasing viscosity and stabilizing the slurry structure.

abstract: A weapon for use in simulated war games, such weapon being particularly usable in situations where targets or opposing pesonnel are out of a direct line of sight or where weapon use in a conventional manner would be otherwise dangerous and should be avoided. Such weapon includes a frangible chamber and a slurry contained within such chamber. The slurry contains a dispersing agent and a plurality of particles serving as a marking agent. Further, a storage container is provided for receiving the slurry-containing frangible chamber to protect the chamber from accidental rupture. In use, the slurry-containing chamber is removed from the container and delivered toward the target by being manually tossed in an arcuate path to strike a target or the vicinity thereof. On striking such target, or its vicinity, the frangible chamber ruptures and the dispersing agent disperses the marking particles against such target thereby identifying the target as being eliminated from the game. As such the weapon emulates a manually deliverable grenade.
problem: Marking targets in simulated war games when direct line of sight is unavailable or conventional weapon use is unsafe.
constraint: Ensuring the frangible chamber is robust enough to survive handling and delivery but reliably ruptures upon impact to disperse the marking agent effectively.
mechanism: Encapsulating a dispersible marking agent within a breakable containment structure that ruptures upon impact, releasing a dispersing medium to spread marking particles onto a target area when direct access is unavailable.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating a dispersible marking slurry in a frangible chamber that ruptures on impact, releasing a dispersing agent to spread marking particles onto the target area.

abstract: A method and an apparatus for constructing a roof on a structure using elongated roofing members, as well as the elongated roofing members. Elongated roofing members are produced, preferably near or on the structure, by continuously forming suitable male and female flanges on sheet metal material and periodically cutting the sheet metal material to predetermined lengths. The male and female flanges of adjacent elongated roofing members are interconnected by deflecting a portion of the female flange about the male flange to crimp the male flange between portions of the female flange. A plurality of clips having flanges may be interconnected with the structure, whereby the flanges are engageable, together with the male flanges, with the female flanges to provide for rapid simultaneous interconnection of both the female flange and the male flange with the structure.
problem: Rapid and secure interconnection of elongated roofing members during construction without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Achieving quick assembly through self-locking flange interlocks while maintaining sufficient mechanical strength to withstand environmental loads.
mechanism: Forming complementary interlocking profiles on adjacent elongated members and mechanically deforming them together, while using auxiliary fasteners with gripping elements to simultaneously secure both profiles to a supporting structure during assembly.
mechanism_raw: Forming complementary male and female flanges on adjacent roofing members and mechanically crimping them together, while using clips with flanges to simultaneously anchor both flange types to the underlying structure.
residual_terms: ["complementary male and female flanges", "clips with flanges"]

abstract: A process for the separation of phosphate minerals from a phosphate-carbonate ore, by flotation, wherein a phenol polymer such as a resol or a novolak, which improves the yield and selectivity of the phosphate minerals with respect to the carbonate minerals, is used in addition to a collector agent in the flotation.
problem: Low yield and selectivity in phosphate mineral separation from phosphate-carbonate ores during flotation processes.
constraint: Optimizing the polymer's chemical structure and dosage to maximize selectivity without interfering with the primary collector's function or increasing processing costs.
mechanism: Introducing a secondary chemical agent with a specific polymeric structure to enhance the selectivity of a primary binding agent, improving the preferential attachment of target minerals over non-target minerals during separation processes.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a phenol polymer (resol or novolak) as a secondary agent to enhance the collector's ability to selectively bind phosphate minerals, improving their flotation efficiency relative to carbonate minerals.

abstract: A circuit for controlling a rice cooker has at least one heater used for heating a cooking pot. This circuit comprises a temperature detection element capable of detecting the temperature of the pot; a converter, connected to receive a detection signal from the temperature detection element, for converting the received signal to a specified electrical signal; a selector, connected to receive an electrical signal from the converter, for producing a first or second selection signal based on whether the value of the electrical signal is or is not within a specified range; and a display capable of displaying a plurality of cooking operation states. This circuit further includes a first controller which receives the first selection signal and supplies to the heater specified turn-on control signals for dividing the cooking operation into a plurality of states and sequentially performing each cooking operation. The controller also supplies display control signals for dividing the cooking operation into a plurality of states corresponding to the turn-on control signals and sequentially indicating these states. A second controller receives the second selection signal and supplies to the display model display control signals which divides the cooking operation into a plurality of states and displays the states.
problem: A rice cooker needs to automatically progress through multiple distinct cooking stages (e.g., heating, warming, keeping warm) based on the thermal state of the pot, while providing visual feedback of the current stage to the user.
constraint: The system must reliably distinguish between cooking stages using a single temperature threshold range, balancing the need for accurate state detection against the simplicity of a binary range check, while ensuring that heating control and display indication remain synchronized across all states.
mechanism: A thermal state signal is converted to an electrical value and evaluated against a specified range by a selector. Depending on whether the value falls within or outside that range, different controllers are activated. Each controller executes a predefined sequence of turn-on control signals that divide the operation into discrete states and sequentially performs each state's action, while simultaneously generating display control signals that indicate the corresponding state on a display. This creates an automatic state-machine-like progression where the sensed thermal state determines the operational state, and each state triggers both the appropriate action control and the matching visual indication.
mechanism_raw: A temperature sensor signal is converted to an electrical value and evaluated against a specified range by a selector. Depending on whether the value falls within or outside that range, different controllers are activated. Each controller executes a predefined sequence of turn-on control signals that divide the cooking operation into discrete states and sequentially performs each state's heating action, while simultaneously generating display control signals that indicate the corresponding state on a display. This creates an automatic state-machine-like progression where the sensed temperature determines the operational state, and each state triggers both the appropriate heating control and the matching visual indication.

abstract: A garment for shielding from an infant's head and hands intravenous and gastrostomy lines infused into the infant during invasive therapy. The garment accomplishes its shielding objectives without restraining the infant's head or limbs while promoting mental health and development through free movement and play. The garment generally speaking is a sleeveless wrap-around type vest provided with a clotch tab attached to the interior side of the front of the vest for anchoring a portion of the infused line located underneath the vest when it is positioned on the infant. The vest is also uniquely provided with an opening for permitting portions of the infused line to exit from beneath the vest and with cooperating components attached to the exterior side of the vest for further anchoring portions of the infused line which have exited from beneath the vest via the opening. Since the vest is of the wrap-around type, it conforms comfortably to the torso of the infant, shields the infused lines from the infant's head and limbs and encourages the infant to engage in free movement and play.
problem: An infant undergoing invasive therapy with IV and gastrostomy lines needs protection from accidentally dislodging or damaging the lines with head and hand movements, but traditional restraint methods harm mental health and development by limiting free movement.
constraint: The garment must simultaneously provide sufficient shielding and line anchoring to prevent accidental dislodgement while remaining loose enough to allow unrestricted limb movement and natural development, requiring a balance between protective coverage and mobility.
mechanism: A sleeveless wrap-around garment conforms to the torso and uses a dual-point anchoring system: an interior clasp tab secures the portion of the line running underneath the garment, while exterior cooperating components anchor the portion that exits through a dedicated opening. The wrap-around design allows the garment to shield lines from the wearer's head and hands without enclosing or restricting the limbs, enabling free movement and activity while keeping the lines positioned safely away from the wearer's reach.
mechanism_raw: A sleeveless wrap-around vest conforms to the infant's torso and uses a dual-point anchoring system: an interior clasp tab secures the portion of the line running underneath the vest, while exterior cooperating components anchor the portion that exits through a dedicated opening. The wrap-around design allows the garment to shield lines from the infant's head and hands without enclosing or restricting the limbs, enabling free movement and play while keeping the lines positioned safely away from the infant's reach.

abstract: A fixture for rectifying one of several different types of repairable and irreparable damage to the upper end portions, or insert sleeves, of the guide thimbles of a fuel assembly held in a work station includes a base having a plurality of tool positioning openings defined therein in a pattern matched with that of the guide thimbles and several aligning holes for mounting the base on guide members of the work station such that the tool positioning openings are disposed in alignment with the guide thimbles. Also, a plurality of different tools are selectively mountable in the openings of the base. Each tool is adapted to operate to rectify a different one of the types of repairable and irreparable damage to the insert sleeves of the guide thimbles. Movement of the base toward the guide thimbles causes engagement with a guide thimble, and concurrently therewith operation, of each of the tools being mounted to the base which is adapted to rectify a respective one of the different types of guide thimble insert sleeve damage which is repairable. In addition, movement of the base toward the guide thimbles causes placement at an operative position, relative to a guide thimble, of each of the tools being mounted to the base which is adapted to rectify a respective one of the different types of guide thimble insert sleeve damage which is irreparable. Finally, a group of positioning elements is mounted in selected ones of the base openings for precisely locating the fixture relative to the guide thimble insert sleeves for accurate performance of repairable damage rectifying operations by the tools as the fixture is moved toward the guide thimbles.
problem: Different types of damage to guide thimble insert sleeves in a nuclear fuel assembly require different repair tools, and performing these repairs accurately and efficiently in a constrained work station environment is challenging.
constraint: The fixture must accommodate multiple different tool types in a single pass while maintaining precise positioning accuracy for each tool relative to its specific guide thimble, requiring the base movement to be both a transport mechanism and a simultaneous actuation mechanism for all tools.
mechanism: A single fixture base with multiple tool-positioning openings is aligned with target locations via mounting holes and positioning elements. Different specialized tools are selectively mounted in the openings. A single movement of the base toward the target locations causes all mounted tools to simultaneously engage their respective targets and perform their specific operations—some rectifying repairable damage through direct tool action, others positioning irreparable-damage tools at operative locations. The positioning elements ensure precise alignment so that each tool operates accurately on its target as the base advances.
mechanism_raw: A single fixture base with multiple tool-positioning openings is aligned with the guide thimbles via mounting holes and positioning elements. Different specialized tools are selectively mounted in the openings. A single movement of the base toward the guide thimbles causes all mounted tools to simultaneously engage their respective thimbles and perform their specific repair operations—some rectifying repairable damage through direct tool action, others positioning irreparable-damage tools at operative locations. The positioning elements ensure precise alignment so that each tool operates accurately on its target as the base advances.

abstract: There is provided a method and apparatus for detecting the position of an embroidery machine after power failure. A position encoder is connected to each frame drive actuator on each axis of the embroidery machine. The computer which controls the actuators is equipped with a non-volatile memory. The encoders indicate to the computer the current position of the actuators and thus the frame. When power returns, the current position value from each encoder is compared with the required position value in the computer memory. If the values are not equal, machine start-up is inhibited and the computer commands the actuators to cause the frame to be moved to its proper position.
problem: After a power failure, an embroidery machine's frame may be left at an unknown or incorrect position, and resuming operation without knowing the true position could damage the embroidery or the machine.
constraint: The system must reliably store the required position in non-volatile memory and accurately compare it with the current sensed position, balancing the need for automatic recovery against the requirement to prevent any operation until the correct position is restored.
mechanism: Position encoders on each axis continuously report the current position of the frame to a computer with non-volatile memory that stores the last required position. When power is restored, the computer compares the current encoder-reported position with the stored required position. If they differ, the computer inhibits machine startup and automatically commands the actuators to move the frame back to its correct position before allowing operation to resume. This creates a self-correcting recovery mechanism that restores the system to a known-good state before permitting continued operation.
mechanism_raw: Position encoders on each axis continuously report the current position of the frame to a computer with non-volatile memory that stores the last required position. When power is restored, the computer compares the current encoder-reported position with the stored required position. If they differ, the computer inhibits machine startup and automatically commands the actuators to move the frame back to its correct position before allowing operation to resume. This creates a self-correcting recovery mechanism that restores the system to a known-good state before permitting continued operation.
