abstract: Stove for burning solid fuels, particularly wood. The stove has a pedestal which has a primary air inlet and an ash drawer; an upright rectangular main housing which is divided internally into a fire box section and a section for combustion products; a housing for electrical components on the back of the main housing; and a flue. The partition between the fire box and the top portion has a first passageway with a catalyst therein and a damper-controlled bypass passageway. Primary air is admitted beneath the grate and passes upwardly therethrough. Secondary air is admitted to the fire box near the glass-panelled charging doors for solid fuel. The stove has a catalyst chamber for completing combustion of the incompletely burned gases in the fire box. A substantially uniform fire box temperature and fuel combustion rate are maintained, regardless of the amount of fuel in the stove (unless fuel is nearly out) by means of a thermocouple in the fire box and an electronic control instrument which controls a valve for admission of primary air. Secondary air is admitted full time although the rate can be varied.
problem: A wood-burning stove must maintain a substantially uniform fire box temperature and consistent fuel combustion rate regardless of how much fuel is present, while ensuring complete combustion of incompletely burned gases.
constraint: The control system must maintain uniform temperature and combustion rate across varying fuel loads using only temperature feedback to modulate primary air, while the catalyst and bypass damper handle secondary combustion and flow balancing, requiring coordination between multiple air and gas pathways.
mechanism: A sensor in the combustion chamber continuously measures temperature and feeds this signal to a control instrument, which adjusts a valve controlling primary air admission beneath the grate. By modulating primary air based on real-time temperature feedback, the system maintains consistent combustion conditions. Secondary air is admitted near the charging doors, and a catalyst in a dedicated chamber completes combustion of incompletely burned gases. A damper-controlled bypass passageway provides additional flow management, creating a closed-loop feedback system that automatically regulates air intake to stabilize temperature and combustion rate.
mechanism_raw: A thermocouple in the fire box continuously measures temperature and feeds this signal to an electronic control instrument, which adjusts a valve controlling primary air admission beneath the grate. By modulating primary air based on real-time temperature feedback, the system maintains consistent combustion conditions. Secondary air is admitted near the charging doors, and a catalyst in a dedicated chamber completes combustion of incompletely burned gases. A damper-controlled bypass passageway provides additional flow management, creating a closed-loop feedback system that automatically regulates air intake to stabilize temperature and combustion rate.

abstract: An apparatus useful for introducing an additive material into a pipeline in which a primary material is flowing in a direction generally parallel to the centerline of the pipeline comprises: a probe located at least partially in the pipeline and in communication with an additive material source; and at least one first aperture and at least one second aperture located in the probe in the pipeline and acting as passageways for additive material from the additive source and the probe to the interior of the pipeline, provided that the first and second apertures are located away from the centerline of the pipeline and are oriented to face substantially downstream relative to the general flow of the primary material in the pipeline.
problem: Introducing an additive material into a pipeline without disrupting the primary flow or causing poor mixing.
constraint: Balancing aperture placement and orientation to avoid disrupting the primary flow while achieving effective additive distribution.
mechanism: Positioning injection points away from the central axis of a flowing medium and directing them along the flow direction utilizes the medium's inherent momentum to entrain and distribute an additive, achieving dispersion while minimizing disruption to the primary flow.
mechanism_raw: Positioning apertures away from the pipeline centerline and orienting them downstream leverages the primary flow's momentum to entrain and mix the additive material into the main stream, ensuring dispersion while minimizing turbulence or blockage.

abstract: An apparatus for simultaneously cutting and beveling plastic pipe such as water or sewer pipe is described. This apparatus includes a rotatable cutting head on which inclined and protruding cutting edges are provided to cut and bevel the pipe. The cutting head is mounted in a housing the lower surfaces of which include two convex pipe engaging regions positioned on either side of the cutting head which are contoured to contact the pipe and maintain the cutting head in proper cutting and beveling relation to the pipe when the housing is moved laterally or angularly relative to the pipe. Concave pipe engaging regions flank the convex regions to maintain the housing in contact with the pipe. The cutting bits are tapered to aid in retaining them in position in the cutting head.
problem: Simultaneously cutting and beveling a pipe while maintaining consistent tool alignment during lateral or angular movement.
constraint: Ensuring the housing remains in contact with the pipe during movement without introducing misalignment or inconsistent cutting depth.
mechanism: Geometric features on a tool housing with opposing curvature profiles maintain continuous contact with a workpiece surface during lateral or angular motion, ensuring stable alignment and consistent engagement of cutting elements through adaptive surface conformity.
mechanism_raw: Convex pipe-engaging regions on the housing maintain the cutting head's position relative to the pipe surface, while concave regions flank them to keep the housing in contact, enabling stable cutting and beveling even as the tool moves laterally or angularly.

abstract: A nozzle dam for providing a fluid-tight seal across a primary fluid nozzle in the plenum of a nuclear steam generating vessel includes two fluid-impermeable seals, each comprising a circular three-section foldable seal plate covered with a flexible diaphragm and circumferentially encompassed by an inflatable seal member disposable in frictional sealing engagement with the inner surface of the nozzle. The center sections of the two seals are interconnected by tubular coupling means. The diaphragms are disposed on the high pressure sides of the seal plates, and the sections of each seal plate are hinged on the high pressure side. The center section of each seal plate carries two pairs of support tabs attached to the low pressure side thereof and respectively projecting from opposite ends thereof in cantilever fashion for supported engagement with a frustoconical portion of the inner surface of the nozzle.
problem: Creating a fluid-tight seal across a nozzle in a high-pressure environment while accommodating geometric irregularities.
constraint: Balancing flexibility for sealing adaptability with the need to withstand high-pressure forces without failure.
mechanism: A deformable sealing assembly with articulated segments and pressure-responsive elements conforms to irregular surfaces under compression, using structural supports positioned on the high-pressure side to preserve integrity during shape adaptation.
mechanism_raw: Hinged, foldable seal plates with support tabs and inflatable seals allow the assembly to conform to the nozzle's inner surface under pressure, with diaphragms and hinges positioned on the high-pressure side to maintain structural integrity during deformation.

abstract: A device for treating a surplus warp yarn drawn from a warp beam of a loom consists of a drive member rotatable by the warp beam. A rotational force of the drive member is transmitted through a transmission device to a driven member. The driven member is secured to a take-up reel disposed separate from the warp beam. The surplus warp yarn drawn from the warp beam is wound up on the take-up reel rotatable with the driven member, thereby preventing the surplus warp yarn from getting entangled with regular warp yarns drawn from the warp beam.
problem: Preventing surplus warp yarn from tangling with regular warp yarns during loom operation.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between the warp beam's rotation and the take-up reel's speed to prevent tension imbalances or slack in the yarn.
mechanism: Decoupling the rotational motion of a surplus material collection system from the primary supply mechanism via an independent drive path enables synchronized yet autonomous winding, preventing entanglement through controlled tension management.
mechanism_raw: Transmitting rotational force from the warp beam to a separate take-up reel via a transmission device allows independent winding of surplus yarn, decoupling its motion from the main warp beam to avoid entanglement.

abstract: A bifocal contact lens blank having a front surface portion which is subdivided into distant and near vision front surface segments. The distant vision segment surface is defined by a partially spherical front surface with a first radius of curvature, and the near vision segment surface is defined by a spherical segment front surface portion with a smaller radius of curvature. The distant vision segment lies in the upper part of the lens blank and the near vision segment in the lower half; the surfaces meet along a locus of tangent points lying generally centrally of the lens and joined to each other on either side of this locus by a pair of offsetting front surfaces which extend between the lowermost edges of the distant vision segment surface and the uppermost edges of the near vision segment surface. These offsetting surfaces lie generally perpendicular to at least one of the segment surfaces, substantially along a meridian of the lens front surface.
problem: Creating a smooth optical transition between distant and near vision segments in a bifocal lens without distortion.
constraint: Ensuring the transition surfaces do not introduce optical aberrations or discontinuities that degrade vision quality.
mechanism: Gradual optical power transition between adjacent vision zones is achieved through controlled geometric bridging surfaces that maintain tangential continuity between curvatures, ensuring smooth refractive progression without introducing discontinuities.
mechanism_raw: Offsetting front surfaces perpendicular to the segment surfaces bridge the gap between the two curvatures, using a locus of tangent points and controlled geometry to ensure gradual transition while maintaining optical clarity.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a low bulk pin-type seam for use with the flat woven fabric. The preferred fabric is woven with continuous or monofilament yarns in the machine direction. The seam is formed by interconnecting loops constructed from the machine direction warp yarns. In constructing the seam loops, a portion of the fabric is made free of cross machine direction yarns and the warp yarns are selected out as either a loop forming yarn or as binder yarns. The fabric is then folded back upon itself in hem like fashion with the selected yarns being retained as loop forming yarns and the binder yarns being drawn back through the hem portion of the fabric to bind the hem and body portion of the fabric. If desired, a stitch pattern may be added to further secure the hem area.
problem: Creating a strong yet low-bulk seam for flat woven fabric without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing seam strength and bulk reduction while maintaining compatibility with continuous or monofilament yarns in the machine direction.
mechanism: Assigning different functional roles to yarns within a woven structure—one set forming loops and another acting as binders—then folding the edge and mechanically drawing the binders through the fold to interlock layers, creating a seam that is strong yet low-profile.
mechanism_raw: Selective yarn assignment (loop-forming vs. binder yarns) combined with hem-folding and mechanical drawing of binders through the hem to interlock the fabric layers, enabling a secure seam with minimal thickness.

While the concept of substituent groups enhancing inhibitor performance is a principle, it is deeply tied to molecular chemistry and lacks a generalizable causal operation beyond chemical formulations.

abstract: A kayak or similar water craft includes a releasable deck that allows the operator to easily evacuate the craft during an emergency. A plurality of large headed pins are preferably employed to attach the releasable deck plate to the upper surface of the hull of the vessel. The head of the pin is received in the large opening of a key hole which includes a slotted groove portion. When the pin is received in the groove portion the deck plate is securely fastened to the kayak. Forward pressure exerted by the operator causes the pins to slide out of the key holes, thereby releasing the deck plate from the craft. The deck plate is held in place by a holding handle or a clip and detent arrangement until it is ready for release. The purpose of the invention is to make it safer for water craft operators to safely and effectively evacuate a vessel during an emergency.
problem: Enabling rapid, controlled release of a deck plate during emergencies while maintaining secure attachment under normal operating conditions.
constraint: Ensuring the deck remains securely fastened during normal use but releases predictably under emergency pressure without unintended disengagement.
mechanism: Using a geometric interface where a component is secured by pins seated within slots, and forward pressure causes the pins to slide out of the slots, releasing the component only when a threshold force is applied in a specific direction.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical keyhole-and-pin interface where forward pressure on the deck plate slides large-headed pins out of slotted grooves, decoupling the deck via a force-dependent geometric interaction.

abstract: The present invention relates to a scroll type fluid displacement compressor, and more particularly, to an axial sealing mechanism for sealing the scrolls in an axial direction. A scroll type fluid displacement compressor includes a housing, a pair of scrolls each comprising an end plate and scroll element projecting from one surface of the end plate. Both scroll elements are interfitted at an angular and radial offset to make a plurality of line contacts. A groove is formed on the end surface of each scroll element and a seal element is placed within each groove. The axial thickness of one seal element is equal to or greater than the depth of the groove. The axial thickness of the other seal element is less than the distance between the bottom surface of the other groove and the end plate of the opposing scroll. Thus, one seal element is fixed in the axial direction and the other seal element is movable in the axial direction to effect a proper axial sealing of the scrolls while making it possible to more easily manufacture and assemble the scroll compressor.
problem: Achieving proper axial sealing between interfitted scrolls in a fluid displacement compressor while simplifying manufacturing and assembly.
constraint: Balancing sealing effectiveness with manufacturing tolerances and assembly ease by leveraging asymmetric seal dimensions.
mechanism: Employing seal elements of differing axial thicknesses within complementary grooves—one thicker than its groove (fixed) and one thinner than the gap to the opposing surface (movable)—so that dynamic movement between interfitted components causes adaptive sealing through controlled compression and clearance.
mechanism_raw: Differential axial thickness of seal elements in grooves—one fixed (thicker than groove depth) and one movable (thinner than opposing groove-to-endplate gap)—allowing adaptive sealing under dynamic scroll movement.
residual_terms: ["axial thickness", "grooves", "fixed seal element", "movable seal element", "adaptive sealing", "dynamic scroll movement"]

While molecular design principles for stability are a concept, the mechanism is tightly bound to chemical structure and lacks a transferable causal operation beyond chemical applications.

abstract: A device for suspending a bundle of horizontal tubes in a vertical plane (1), the device comprising pairs (4, 5, 6) of vertical tubes (7, 8) provided with half-fins on their facing sides. The half-fins have a profile including notches of circular shape, having a radius slightly larger than the radius of the tubes in the bundle and being at the same spacing as said tubes, the notches being separated by tongues (16, 18, 20, 17, 19, 21) which project from the vertical tubes by a distance which is long enough to provide good support for the tubes of the bundle and which is short enough to ensure good thermal conduction from their projecting ends to their weld zones on the corresponding vertical tubes.
problem: Supporting a bundle of horizontal tubes in a vertical plane while maintaining efficient thermal conduction between the tubes and their mounting structure.
constraint: Tongue projection length must be long enough for structural support but short enough to minimize thermal resistance between the supported tubes and the vertical tubes.
mechanism: A support structure uses paired elements with complementary geometric features (e.g., notches and projecting tongues) to physically interface between a first set of components and a second set, where the projecting elements' length is constrained to balance mechanical load-bearing capacity against thermal energy transfer efficiency between the components.
mechanism_raw: Pairs of vertical tubes with half-fins on facing sides use notches (matching tube spacing) and projecting tongues to physically support the horizontal tubes. The tongues' length is optimized to balance mechanical support against thermal conduction efficiency, as their projecting ends are welded to the vertical tubes.

abstract: A sandmill outlet screen is formed by a stack of rings which have projections and corresponding recesses stamped into them. The projections provide a gap between rings whereby flow passages between the rings are created. These passages permit the liquid being processed by the sandmill to flow out of the sandmill, but keep a grinding media in the mill. With the projections of one ring nested in the recesses of an adjacent ring, a small gap is provided. With the rings oriented to prevent nesting, a larger gap is provided. With the rings arranged so that the projections of adjacent rings abut each other, a still larger gap is obtained. This variable flow passage capability is further enhanced by varying the height of the projections.
problem: Controlling the flow rate of liquid exiting a sandmill while retaining grinding media inside the mill.
constraint: Gap size must balance liquid flow rate against retention of grinding media, with orientation and projection height providing discrete or continuous flow control.
mechanism: A multi-element flow control system uses rotatable or reconfigurable components with interlocking geometric features (e.g., projections and recesses) to create variable-sized gaps. Relative positioning of these components adjusts the gap size to modulate flow rate while maintaining retention of particulate matter within the system.
mechanism_raw: A stack of rings with stamped projections and recesses creates variable flow gaps. By rotating or orienting adjacent rings to nest projections in recesses (small gap), prevent nesting (larger gap), or abut projections (largest gap), the flow passage size is adjusted. Projection height further modulates flow capacity.

abstract: A webbing useful for safety belts having an excellent impact energy absorption and a superior impact strength, comprises a webbing made by weaving warps and wefts, at least the warps consisting of polyester filaments which have an intrinsic viscosity of 0.7 or more, a birefringence of 0.08 to 0.15, a tensile strength of 4 g/denier or more, an ultimate elongation of from 50% to 80%, and an elongation value of 5% or less at a point A in a stress-strain curve of the filaments, which point A denotes an intersection point of an extension of a steeply sloped portion of the curve appearing at the initial stage of the elongation of the filaments with an extension of a substantially horizontal or gently sloped portion of the curve appearing at the middle stage of the elongation of the filaments.
problem: Designing a safety belt webbing that absorbs high impact energy without catastrophic failure.
constraint: Filament properties must be tuned so that the transition from steep to horizontal slope occurs at an elongation value ≤5%, ensuring energy absorption without exceeding ultimate elongation limits.
mechanism: A deformable material is engineered with a stress-strain profile that transitions from a steep initial slope to a plateau at a predetermined elongation threshold. This transition enables controlled energy dissipation through progressive yielding without exceeding material failure limits.
mechanism_raw: Polyester filaments are engineered with a stress-strain curve featuring a steep initial slope (high modulus) followed by a horizontal plateau. This is achieved by controlling intrinsic viscosity, birefringence, tensile strength, and elongation properties so that the material undergoes controlled deformation at a specific stress point (point A), absorbing energy through progressive yielding.

abstract: An improvement is provided for a retractable tip marking pen whereby the tip, in its retracted position, is enclosed in a chamber which prevents drying of the marking fluid. The chamber is provided by an elastomeric sealing member positioned within the outer sheath of the pen adjacent the lower extremity thereof. The sealing member automatically opens when the tip is pushed to its writing position, and closes when the tip is retracted to its stored position.
problem: Preventing drying of marking fluid in a retractable-tip pen while allowing automatic exposure of the tip during use.
constraint: The elastomer must reliably deform to open/close the chamber without permanent damage, balancing flexibility for actuation against durability for repeated use.
mechanism: A deformable sealing element forms a closed chamber around a retractable component. Mechanical displacement of the component during extension induces deformation of the sealing element to open the chamber, while retraction allows the sealing element to recover its original shape and reseal the chamber.
mechanism_raw: An elastomeric sealing member within the pen sheath forms a closed chamber around the retracted tip. Mechanical displacement of the tip during extension automatically stretches or deforms the elastomer to open the chamber, while retraction allows the elastomer to return to its original shape, resealing the chamber.

abstract: A process for separation of a high pressure gas stream such as refinery gas in which the starting gas mixture is cooled and separated into a first vapor portion and a first liquid portion which is expanded to an intermediate pressure. The first vapor portion is further cooled and separated into a second vapor portion which may be further processed for ultimate recovery of, for example, a methane-rich product gas and a second liquid portion which is expanded to essentially the same intermediate pressure and combined with the expanded first liquid portion. The resulting mixed intermediate pressure stream or a portion thereof is then employed as refrigerant.
problem: Efficiently separating components of a high-pressure gas stream (e.g., refinery gas) while minimizing energy consumption.
constraint: Pressure and temperature conditions must be precisely managed across stages to ensure effective phase separation and refrigerant reuse without compromising product purity or system stability.
mechanism: A multi-stage separation process cools a gas stream to induce phase separation into vapor and liquid phases at successive stages. Liquid fractions are expanded to intermediate pressures and reused as a working fluid in subsequent cooling stages, creating a closed-loop energy recovery cycle that leverages phase transitions and pressure differentials.
mechanism_raw: The gas is cooled and separated into vapor and liquid phases at multiple stages. Liquid portions are expanded to intermediate pressures and reused as refrigerant in subsequent cooling stages, creating a closed-loop refrigeration cycle that leverages phase separation and expansion for energy recovery.

abstract: This invention provides a carrying case made up of two sections of molded plastic which are identical except at their outer edges which meet when the case is closed. One edge includes a tongue with reinforcing ribs which enters a groove in the outer edge to engage a gasket and form a fluid seal as well as strengthening the case. Nothing penetrates the wall of the case, the latches being connected to supports spaced outwardly from the case wall. Sockets on the bottom of the case receive spaced support members projecting from a luggage cart, and can receive connecting elements to enable the cart to carry more than one case. The sockets also can receive wheel units so that a single case may be mounted on wheels, or a plurality of cases may be connected and supported on a set of wheels. The case includes integral feet on the bottom wall to support it, and bosses on the inner walls for connecting items to the interior of the case.
problem: Creating a durable, sealable carrying case that can be structurally reinforced without compromising its fluid-tight integrity or modularity for cart/wheel integration.
constraint: Balancing the need for a fluid-tight seal with structural reinforcement, while ensuring modularity (e.g., cart/wheel integration) does not compromise the case's integrity or sealing performance.
mechanism: Fasteners are positioned on supports spaced outwardly from the main structural surface, avoiding penetration of the surface itself. This preserves structural integrity while enabling a fluid-tight seal via a gasket interface. Modular attachment points on the base allow scalable connectivity without compromising the sealed enclosure.
mechanism_raw: Latches are positioned on supports spaced outwardly from the case wall, avoiding penetration of the wall itself. This maintains structural integrity while enabling a fluid seal via a tongue-and-groove gasket interface. Sockets on the bottom allow modular attachment of support members or wheels, enabling scalable connectivity.

abstract: The invention is a reboiler-condenser which increases the efficiency of heat transfer between boiling and condensing fluids, such as oxygen and nitrogen in air separation or similar cryogenic applications. The exchanger is built up from individual plates, the opposite sides of which have enhanced condensing and boiling surfaces. The condensing channels are inclined slightly downward so that condensate can be removed at many elevations in the exchanger.
problem: Improving heat transfer efficiency in cryogenic reboiler-condenser systems where condensate removal and surface enhancement are critical for performance.
constraint: Optimizing the inclination angle and surface enhancement to maximize heat transfer without causing flow maldistribution or excessive pressure drop.
mechanism: Inclined flow channels allow condensate to drain at multiple elevations, preventing pooling and maintaining thermal contact. Enhanced surface textures on opposing sides of a heat transfer medium increase effective area, while modular assembly enables scalable heat exchange configurations.
mechanism_raw: Inclined condensing channels allow condensate to drain at multiple elevations, preventing pooling and maintaining thermal contact. Enhanced boiling/condensing surfaces on opposing plate sides increase heat transfer area, while the modular plate construction enables scalable assembly.

abstract: The coating of surfaces to impart gloss and protect from weathering, and the use of solvents in paint formulations, are disclosed; the following being exemplary: Compounds having the formula: ##STR1## wherein R.sub.1, R.sub.2, and R.sub.3 are saturated alkyls having from 2 to 20 carbon atoms therein. R.sub.1 and R.sub.2, or R.sub.2 and R.sub.3, alternatively, may be the same and form a nitrogen heterocyclic compound such as that derived from, for example, a pyrrolidine, a piperidine or a hexahydroazepine. Exemplary compounds include: N,N-diethyldodecanamide; N,N-di-n-propyldodecanamide; 1-dodecly-2-pyrrolidone; 1-dodecyl-2-piperidone; 1-dodcylhexahydro-2H-azepin-2-one; 1-dodecanoylpiperidine; 1-dodecanoylpyrrolidone; 1-dodecanoylhexahydroazepine; N,N-diethylhexadecanamide; N,N-di-n-propylhexadecanamide; 1-hexadecyl-2-pyrrolidone; 1-hexadecyl-2-piperidone; 1-hexadecylhexahydro-2H-azepin-2-one; 1-hexadecanoylpyrrolidine; 1-hexadecanoylpiperidine; 1-hexadecanoylhexahydroazepine; N,N-dioctylbutanamide; N,N-didodecylbutanamide. N-dodecyl-N-butylethanamide and N-ethyl-N-hexadecylpropanamide.
problem: Developing coating compositions that provide long-lasting gloss and weather resistance while maintaining compatibility with solvent-based formulations.
constraint: Balancing the length and branching of alkyl chains to achieve optimal solubility in solvents without sacrificing durability or weather resistance.
mechanism: Molecular structures combine a stable heterocyclic core with variable-length hydrophobic chains to balance solubility in solvents, adhesion, UV resistance, and film-forming properties. The core provides thermal and chemical stability, while chain length modulates compatibility and durability.
mechanism_raw: Heterocyclic compounds (e.g., pyrrolidone, piperidone) with long alkyl chains create a molecular structure that enhances adhesion, UV resistance, and hydrophobicity. The nitrogen heterocycle core provides thermal and chemical stability, while the alkyl chains modulate solubility and film-forming properties.

abstract: A filling or packing body has an annular cell structure. All walls surrounding each cell are normal to the main plane along which the annular structure extends. Dividing walls between the cells transverse to an outer wall closed upon itself are parallel with each other at least for a row of adjacent cells or for all of them. The ring constituted by the row of cells having the outer wall in common can be of round, in particular of circular or elliptic configuration, or its configuration can be polygonal, especially triangular. The height of the cell walls, normal to the main plane, can be constant or it can be higher at the center than at the periphery of the ring structure.
problem: Designing a structured packing or filling body that maximizes surface area for fluid interaction while maintaining structural integrity and uniform flow distribution.
constraint: Balancing cell geometry (height, parallelism) to maximize surface area and flow efficiency without causing turbulence or structural weakness.
mechanism: Cell walls oriented normal to a primary plane, with parallel dividers creating uniform flow channels. Variable wall height (higher at the center) optimizes fluid distribution and contact time, while a closed outer boundary ensures structural stability under flow conditions.
mechanism_raw: Annular cell walls are oriented normal to the main plane, with parallel dividing walls creating uniform flow channels. Variable cell wall height (higher at the center) optimizes fluid distribution and contact time, while the closed outer wall ensures structural stability.

abstract: A fitting having a weakened section therein is positioned between a flow control device and a water outlet such as a sprinkler head so that if the sprinkler head is subjected to a lateral blow, the fluid conduit will break at the weakened section, but yet the flow out of the broken conduit will be restricted by the flow control device.
problem: Preventing uncontrolled fluid discharge from a sprinkler system when the outlet is subjected to lateral impact, while maintaining normal operation under standard conditions.
constraint: Calibrating the weakened section's failure threshold to ensure it activates under impact without triggering during normal operation or minor disturbances.
mechanism: A stress-sensitive failure zone is positioned between a flow control element and an outlet. Under lateral force exceeding a calibrated threshold, the failure zone ruptures, but the flow control element limits outflow to prevent uncontrolled discharge. The threshold ensures activation only under impact conditions.
mechanism_raw: A weakened section in the conduit is positioned between the flow control device and the outlet. Under lateral force, the conduit breaks at the weakened section, but the flow control device restricts outflow, preventing flooding or damage. The weakened section is designed to fail only under specific stress thresholds.

abstract: A method of instant photography is disclosed wherein graphics are reproduced on a photographic print along with the image of an object whose photograph is taken using a camera. The method includes the steps: PA1 (a) producing a light flash, PA1 (b) and channeling at least some of the light to a zone proximate the camera lens and extending about the direct path of light that travels from said object through the lens to film in the camera, PA1 (c) whereby light channeled to that zone also passes through the lens and operates to illuminate the film, forming a light modulated background to the image of the object and also to the reproduced graphics.
problem: Reproducing graphics on a photographic print alongside the object image in instant photography, where both the primary image and secondary graphics must appear on the same print.
constraint: The channeled secondary light must pass through the lens and illuminate the film without disrupting or overwhelming the primary image formation, requiring precise spatial and intensity control of the secondary light relative to the direct optical path.
mechanism: A secondary light path is merged with a primary optical pathway such that both information channels propagate through a shared focusing element, creating a composite illumination pattern on a photosensitive medium. The secondary light is spatially and intensity-controlled to overlay graphics information without disrupting the primary image formation.
mechanism_raw: A secondary light source is channeled into a zone adjacent to the camera lens that overlaps with the primary optical path, causing the secondary light to pass through the same lens and illuminate the film. This creates a light-modulated background that carries the graphics information while the primary image is simultaneously formed, effectively overlaying two information channels through a shared optical pathway.

abstract: The present invention relates to the foundry industry and solves the problem of extended service life of valve closure gate assemblies for foundry ladles. The valve closure gate assembly of the present invention comprises two mutually slidable heat-resistant gates furnished with a protecting layer of an oxide refractory material and having flow-through rings made from an oxide refractory material disposed in the openings of the gates. The respective upper and lower surfaces of the rings are coated with a layer of refractory material.
problem: Extending the service life of valve closure gate assemblies used in foundry ladles, which operate in extreme high-temperature and abrasive environments that cause rapid degradation of sealing and sliding components.
constraint: The protective refractory layers must withstand extreme temperatures and corrosive conditions while remaining thin enough to allow the gates to slide relative to each other and maintain proper sealing engagement.
mechanism: Sacrificial protective layers are applied to sliding surfaces of mechanical components to absorb environmental degradation, preserving the structural integrity and mobility of the underlying functional elements. Integrated flow channels maintain material transport capability through the protected components.
mechanism_raw: Protective refractory layers are applied to the sliding gate surfaces to shield the underlying functional components from thermal and abrasive wear, while flow-through rings integrated into the gate openings maintain material flow capability. The refractory layers act as sacrificial barriers that absorb degradation, preserving the structural integrity and slidability of the gates.

abstract: A spark spectroscopic high-pressure gas analyzer including a spark chamber, having a pair of electrodes, for receiving a sample of the pressurized gas to be analyzed. A voltage is provided across the electrodes for generating a spark in the pressurized gas sample. A selected wavelength band of radiation emitted from the spark discharge in the pressurized gas corresponding to a component to be sensed in the gas is detected. The intensity of the emission in the wavelength band is integrated during the afterglow time interval of the spark emission and a signal representative of the integrated intensity of the emission in the selected narrow wavelength band is employed to determine the proportion of the component in the gas.
problem: Accurately determining the proportion of a specific component in a pressurized gas sample, where spectral interference and transient emission characteristics complicate measurement.
constraint: The detection must be precisely synchronized to the afterglow time interval to capture the relevant emission characteristics, and the wavelength band must be selected to correspond to the specific component being analyzed while avoiding interference from other species.
mechanism: A transient excitation event generates emission from a sample, and detection is temporally gated to a specific post-excitation interval where target-specific spectral characteristics dominate. The integrated emission intensity within a selected wavelength band during this interval is correlated to determine component proportion.
mechanism_raw: A spark discharge is generated in the pressurized gas sample, and the emission spectrum is monitored during the afterglow time interval following the spark. The intensity of emission in a selected wavelength band is integrated over this specific temporal window, where the spectral characteristics are most representative of the target component concentration, and the integrated signal is correlated to determine the proportion of the component.

abstract: A method is disclosed for extruding thin-walled ceramic bodies. The method involves mixing into a homogenized batch a granular ceramic, a binder, a soluble oxidizing agent and a matrix precursor in amounts sufficient to provide a substantially water-free extrudable mixture. The batch is extruded into an atmosphere containing SO.sub.2 which permeates the extrudate and reacts with the oxidizing agent to form SO.sub.3 in situ. The SO.sub.3 catalyzes polymerization of the furfuryl alcohol to a rigid solid which prevents deformation of the extrudate.
problem: Preventing deformation of thin-walled ceramic extrudates during the extrusion process, where the freshly extruded material lacks sufficient structural integrity to maintain its shape.
constraint: The mixture must be formulated to be substantially water-free and contain specific reactive components that respond to the environmental trigger, and the reaction must occur rapidly enough to prevent deformation before the material gains sufficient structural integrity.
mechanism: An extrudable mixture contains reactive components that undergo rapid in-situ polymerization when exposed to an environmental trigger during processing. The reaction forms a rigidizing agent that hardens the material structure before deformation can occur, preserving shape integrity during extrusion.
mechanism_raw: The extrudable mixture contains a soluble oxidizing agent and a matrix precursor that react with an environmental trigger (SO₂ in the surrounding atmosphere) as the material is extruded. The SO₂ permeates the extrudate and reacts with the oxidizing agent to form SO₃ in situ, which catalyzes rapid polymerization of the furfuryl alcohol binder into a rigid solid, hardening the extrudate during processing.

abstract: A scroll compressor can be provided with different wrap thicknesses to compensate for the different material properties of the orbiting and fixed scroll elements. The concept of different wrap thicknesses also aids in the select-fitting of parts and in the provision of and adjustment of a clearance or spacing between the wrap elements. Additionally, in the manufacture of a scroll compressor, the total wrap thickness of the two wraps is kept constant within narrow tolerances while the individual wrap thicknesses are allowed to vary over a predetermined range. The cutting tools used are sized such that even if they differ in their cutting diameters, the combined cutting diameters, and therefore the total wrap thicknesses, are constant within narrow tolerances. This permits the tools to be used and resharpened until their cutting diameters fall below the minimum acceptable diameter.
problem: Compensating for different material properties (such as thermal expansion or wear characteristics) between orbiting and fixed scroll elements in a scroll compressor, while maintaining proper clearance and enabling selective part fitting.
constraint: Individual wrap thicknesses can vary over a predetermined range to accommodate material property differences, but the total wrap thickness must remain constant within narrow tolerances, and the cutting tools must be sized so that their combined diameters maintain this constant total even as they wear.
mechanism: Complementary adjustable elements with variable individual dimensions are configured such that their combined effective dimension remains constant within tight tolerances. This compensates for differential material behavior between interacting components while maintaining uniform interface clearance and enabling selective part interchangeability.
mechanism_raw: The orbiting and fixed scroll elements are manufactured with different individual wrap thicknesses to compensate for their differing material properties, but the total combined wrap thickness is maintained constant within narrow tolerances. Complementary cutting tools with different diameters are used such that their combined cutting diameters always sum to the same total, ensuring the constant total wrap thickness even as individual tools wear and are resharpened.

abstract: An inflatable and collapsible dam arrangement including a flexible membrane weir element positioned so that when it is inflated, it will block a flow of water. The control chamber for the weir is divided into upper and lower sections. The upper section has at least a portion above ground and contains an apparatus for inflating the dam and making the weir element self-supporting. The lower control section includes at least a portion positioned underground and includes an apparatus for collapsing the dam.
problem: Creating a temporary, controllable barrier to block water flow that can be rapidly deployed and retracted without permanent infrastructure.
constraint: Balancing structural integrity when inflated against the need for rapid collapse and retraction, requiring compartmentalized pressure control to avoid uneven stress or failure.
mechanism: A deployable barrier system uses a flexible, inflatable structure divided into independently controlled chambers. Selective pressurization of chambers creates a self-supporting barrier to block flow, while controlled depressurization enables rapid collapse and retraction. Compartmentalization allows localized stress management to maintain structural integrity during deployment and recovery.
mechanism_raw: A flexible membrane is inflated to form a self-supporting barrier, with separate upper and lower control chambers enabling independent inflation (to block flow) and collapse (to release flow). The division of chambers allows localized pressure management for structural stability during inflation and controlled deflation.

abstract: A pyrotechnic composition for producing a screen for blocking the passage of infra-red radiation and of light, comprises phosphorus, preferably red amorphous phosphorus, dispersed in a binding agent, for example rubber. The composition is produced by forming the binding agent into a gel with solvent, dispersing the phosphorus into the gel, evaporating off solvent, and comminuting the resulting solid material.
problem: Producing a pyrotechnic composition with uniform dispersion of light-blocking particles in a binding matrix while maintaining mechanical cohesion.
constraint: Selecting a solvent and binding agent that allow sufficient particle dispersion without premature solidification, while ensuring the final composition retains structural integrity for pyrotechnic use.
mechanism: A particulate-laden composition is formed by creating a temporary gel matrix through solvent interaction with a binding agent, embedding dispersed particles within the gel phase, then solidifying the matrix via solvent removal. The gel phase enables homogeneous particle distribution before solidification, followed by size reduction to achieve uniform particulate consistency.
mechanism_raw: Forming a binding agent into a gel via solvent, dispersing particulate phosphorus into the gel matrix, evaporating the solvent to solidify the mixture, and comminuting the result to achieve a consistent particulate distribution. The gel phase enables homogeneous embedding of particles before solidification.

abstract: The present invention is the method of manufacturing BaPb.sub.1-x Bi.sub.x O.sub.3 single crystal utilized as a super-conductor. In this method, the starting material and the growing substrate are mounted inside an autoclave, in which an aqueous solution comprised of acid, alkali aqueous solution or peroxide is charged. With the hydrothermal synthesis that applies necessary temperature and pressure to the starting material, the BaPb.sub.1-x Bi.sub.x O.sub.3 single crystal is obtained and the composition reappearance characteristic is improved. The strain is removed by growing at a temperature below the transition point. Also, by removing such defects as heat strain, the crystallization ability and super-conducting are improved.
problem: Growing high-quality single crystals of a superconducting material with minimal defects and strain-induced performance degradation.
constraint: Maintaining a narrow temperature-pressure window to avoid decomposition or phase instability, while ensuring the solution chemistry supports defect-free crystal growth.
mechanism: A crystalline material is synthesized in a sealed, chemically controlled environment where precise temperature and pressure regulate dissolution and recrystallization. Growth occurs below a critical phase boundary to minimize strain, while solution chemistry ensures compositional uniformity and defect suppression during nucleation and lattice formation.
mechanism_raw: Hydrothermal synthesis in a controlled aqueous environment (acid/alkali/peroxide) applies precise temperature and pressure to dissolve and recrystallize the material. Growing below the transition temperature removes strain, while the solution composition enhances compositional uniformity and defect reduction.
residual_terms: ["sealed, chemically controlled environment", "critical phase boundary", "solution chemistry"]

abstract: A woven fabric which has been woven on a needle loom wherein the weft loops are secured by a knitted thread construction, the secured weft loops being located in board of the warp thread defining the opposite edge of the fabric to the edge whereat weft insertion has taken place and the knitted thread construction being woven between warp threads positioned adjacent opposite said edge.
problem: Securing loose weft loops in a woven fabric to prevent unraveling without compromising the fabric's structural continuity.
constraint: Positioning the knitted construction far enough from the insertion edge to avoid disrupting the weaving process, while ensuring sufficient tension and thread density to hold the loops securely.
mechanism: A localized anchoring structure is integrated into a woven fabric by introducing a knitted thread network between warp threads at a distance from the insertion edge. The interlooped knitted structure mechanically binds loose loops through tension and thread density, preventing unraveling without disrupting the primary weaving process.
mechanism_raw: A knitted thread construction is woven between warp threads at the edge opposite the weft insertion point, mechanically locking the weft loops in place. The knitted structure acts as a localized anchor, binding the loops through interlooping with adjacent warp threads.

abstract: A process for separating a monosaccharide from an aqueous solution comprising monosaccharides and a second component comprising a polysaccharide. The mixture is contacted with a mixed matrix membrane comprising a adsorbent or molecular sieve material dispersed in an organic polymer in which the monosaccharide has a greater steady state permeability than the polysaccharide. The monosaccharide passes through the membrane, and is recovered. Particular mixed matrix membranes found to be useful in separating mono from polysaccharides are silicalite, gamma-alumina, activated carbon or a calcium exchanged Y-zeolite dispersed in cellulose acetate or polyelectrolyte complex polymers.
problem: Separating monosaccharides from polysaccharides in aqueous solutions based on differential permeability through a membrane.
constraint: Selecting an adsorbent-polymer pair that maximizes permeability differences between the two components without degrading the membrane’s structural integrity under operational conditions.
mechanism: A selective barrier combines a porous adsorbent dispersed within a polymer matrix to exploit differential permeability. Smaller or more soluble molecules preferentially permeate through the polymer phase, while larger or less compatible molecules are sterically excluded or retained by the adsorbent, enabling size- or affinity-based separation.
mechanism_raw: A mixed matrix membrane combines a molecular sieve or adsorbent (e.g., silicalite, zeolite) dispersed in a polymer matrix. The monosaccharide’s smaller size or higher solubility in the polymer allows it to permeate preferentially, while the polysaccharide is excluded due to steric hindrance or lower affinity.

abstract: The present invention relates to a vertically oriented frame for embroidery, quilting, rug making, needlepointing or the like. The frame may be attached to a stationary surface, such as a wall panel. It may also be attached to a moveable support which optionally has wheels or casters to be rolled from one place to another. The frame comprises a support frame having multiple securing means which provide a horizontal adjustable retaining area at work space height, and an area above for vertical storage of the quilt. As each portion of the quilt is completed at the horizontal work station formed by a lower retaining bar, adjustable opposite outwardly projecting side bars and adjustable front bar, the quilt is easily stored and displayed vertically until it is complete. Upper horizontal storage support means for the quilt are provided extending over the work station area.
problem: Managing large-scale projects (e.g., quilts) that require incremental work and storage without disrupting the workspace.
constraint: Balancing accessible workspace height with vertical storage capacity to avoid interfering with ongoing work.
mechanism: A vertical support structure with adjustable retention elements and upper storage interfaces integrates a horizontal working surface with overhead storage, enabling completed portions to be stored above while ongoing work proceeds on the remaining sections without disrupting the workspace.
mechanism_raw: A vertically oriented frame with adjustable retaining bars and upper storage supports integrates a horizontal workspace with vertical storage, allowing completed sections to be stored above while work continues on the remaining portions.

abstract: A progressive hydraulic distributor with a slide for controlling a hydraulic actuator. The distributor has an internal load sensing passage that detects the operating pressure in the hydraulic fluid inlet or outlet passage and superimposes this pressure on the action of the spring of a feed valve. Thus, the difference between the up-flow and the down-flow of progressivity in the slide of the distributor is constant.
problem: Maintaining consistent control in a hydraulic system despite varying operating pressures in the fluid inlet or outlet.
constraint: Maintaining a fixed pressure differential while accommodating dynamic load variations without compromising system responsiveness.
mechanism: A pressure-sensing feedback loop detects dynamic operating pressure and modulates a control element's biasing force to maintain a constant pressure differential across a progressive flow system, accommodating load variations without compromising responsiveness.
mechanism_raw: A load-sensing passage detects operating pressure and superimposes it on a feed valve's spring, ensuring the pressure differential between up-flow and down-flow progressivity remains constant.

abstract: An oxindol compound of the formula (I) ##STR1## wherein A represents a lower alkylene group; PA0 R represents a hydrogen atom, a lower alkyl group, a phenyl-lower alkyl group, a phenoxy-lower alkyl group, a benzoyl-lower alkyl group, a lower alkoxycarbonyl group, a lower alkanoyl group, a benzoyl group which may be substituted with 1 to 3 of a lower alkyl group, a lower alkoxy group and a halogen atom on the benzene ring thereof, or a benzoyl group which is substituted with a lower alkylenedioxy group on the benzene ring thereof; and PA0 m and n, which may be the same or different, each represents an integer of 0 or 1, with proviso that when n is an integer of 1, then m is an integer of 1, PA0 when A is an ethylene group and m is an integer of 1, then R should not be 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoyl group, and when A is a group of the formula: --C(R.sup.1)(R.sup.2)--(where R.sup.1 and R.sup.2 are, the same or different, a hydrogen atom or a lower alkyl group) and m is an integer of 1, then R should not be a hydrogen atom; or its pharmaceutically acceptable salt, composition containing the compound and processes for preparing the same are disclosed. The compound is useful as a cardiotonic agent.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical compound with defined substituents for cardiotonic use. While molecular design principles are general, the mechanism here is tied to a particular chemical structure and biological target, lacking a broadly transferable causal operation.

abstract: An improved electric stringed instrument which can produce "banjo" sounds. The instrument has a banjo head including a taut flexible membrane mounted on a ring which is mounted on a solid material (preferably wood) body. The ring and body are connected in a conventional manner to a fretted neck extending away from the head. A plurality of strings extend from adjustable securing means at the end of the neck over the flexible membrane to a tailpiece secured to the body. A bridge is positioned between the strings and membrane. One or more recesses in the body below the membrane contain electric pickups. The spaces between the sides and bottoms of the pickups and the adjacent surfaces of the recesses are at least partially filled with resilient foam. The foam beneath the pickups is compressed slightly to keep the upper pickup surface in resilient contact with the membrane. Closing in the chamber under the head where the pickups are located restricts the airflow in the chamber and reduces the vibration of the head sufficiently to allow high volume without the feedback problems normally associated with prior amplified banjos. Amplifying the signal generated by the pickup under the bridge will give one sound, while amplifying the forward pickup signal will produce another different sound, providing a variety of banjo sounds.
problem: Producing banjo-like sounds on an electric stringed instrument without feedback at high volumes.
constraint: Balancing vibration suppression (to prevent feedback) with sound quality and the ability to produce distinct tonal characteristics.
mechanism: A flexible surface is tensioned over a confined chamber with embedded sensors, and a resilient contact element maintains continuous interface between the sensors and the surface, suppressing feedback-inducing vibrations while enabling tonal variation through surface compliance.
mechanism_raw: A flexible membrane (banjo head) is mounted over a restricted chamber with recessed pickups, and resilient foam maintains contact between pickups and the membrane, suppressing vibrations that cause feedback while enabling varied sound profiles.

abstract: Apparatus and method is disclosed for determining position with light by providing input light at an input light port of an optical cavity having a variable length dimension and detecting light which has traversed the variable length dimension at an output light port of the optical cavity and determining the present length of the variable length dimension using the detected light as a measure.
problem: Determining position or length changes using light in a system with a variable physical dimension.
constraint: Maintaining measurement accuracy despite dynamic changes in the cavity's length and potential environmental interference.
mechanism: A variable-dimension optical cavity allows input radiation to propagate through its length, and detected output radiation is analyzed to determine the cavity's current dimension, enabling precise measurement of position or length changes.
mechanism_raw: An optical cavity with a variable length dimension allows input light to traverse the cavity, and the output light is detected to calculate the current length, enabling precise position measurement.

abstract: A method of feedback-controlling the air-fuel ratio of a mixture, supplied to an internal combustion engine, by at least one of proportional control and integral control in dependence upon the results of a comparison between the output of an exhaust gas concentration sensor and a predetermined reference value. The method includes obtaining the ratio of a first time period required for an output value from the exhaust gas concentration sensor to make a transition from a peak value on a rich side to a predetermined reference value with respect to the predetermined reference value, and a second time period required for the output value to make a transition from a peak value on a lean side to the predetermined reference value with respect to the predetermined reference value, and altering, in dependence upon the ratio obtained, at least one predetermined control factor applied to control of the air-fuel ratio.
problem: Maintaining optimal air-fuel ratio in an internal combustion engine under dynamic operating conditions.
constraint: Balancing responsiveness and stability by adapting control parameters based on the relative speed of rich vs. lean transitions, avoiding overcorrection or sluggish response.
mechanism: Monitor bidirectional transitions of a sensed parameter to compute a timing ratio, then use this ratio to dynamically adjust feedback control parameters (e.g., proportional/integral gains) to balance responsiveness and stability in a closed-loop system.
mechanism_raw: Using the ratio of time periods for rich-to-lean and lean-to-rich transitions of exhaust gas sensor output to dynamically adjust control factors (e.g., proportional/integral gains) in a feedback control loop.

abstract: A slim knife unit includes a guide member having an L-shaped body which supports an elongated fluid actuator comprising a piston connected by piston rods to a base member having a sliding track connection to a removable knife holder. The knife holder has spaced walls defining a slot which receives a circular knife supported by a bearing mounted on a spacer bushing clamped between the walls by a center support screw. The guide member has a linear track which cooperates with the rods to guide the knife holder, and a releasable latch secures the knife holder to the base member. The guide member also has a linear track which guides a clamp member movable by a screw for securing the knife unit to a support bar.
problem: Achieving precise, repeatable linear motion for cutting operations while enabling quick tool replacement and secure mounting.
constraint: Integrating fluid power (for actuation) with mechanical guidance (for precision) without compromising tool accessibility or system rigidity.
mechanism: Integrate a powered actuator for motion with a mechanical guidance system and a releasable securing mechanism to enable controlled linear movement, precise positioning, and rapid tool exchange while maintaining rigidity.
mechanism_raw: Combining a fluid actuator for powered movement with mechanical tracks and latches to guide and stabilize a removable knife holder, ensuring controlled motion and secure attachment/detachment.

abstract: A system and method for adjusting the camber of an airfoil extending from an aircraft for optimum flight performance. In the method, a velocity signal is produced that represents the longitudinal velocity of the aircraft. Utilizing the velocity signal, it is determined if a change in camber of the airfoil can increase the aircraft's flight performance. Thereafter, the camber of the airfoil is changed until an optimum flight performance is achieved.
problem: Optimizing aircraft airfoil performance in real-time based on varying flight conditions.
constraint: Balancing real-time responsiveness with structural limitations of the airfoil, ensuring adjustments do not exceed mechanical or aerodynamic thresholds.
mechanism: Use a velocity-dependent signal to trigger iterative shape modifications of a deformable surface, adjusting its geometry until predefined performance metrics (e.g., lift/drag ratio) are satisfied within structural and aerodynamic limits.
mechanism_raw: Using a velocity signal to trigger camber adjustments on an airfoil, iteratively modifying its shape until optimal performance metrics (e.g., lift/drag ratio) are achieved.

abstract: Particulate heavy duty detergent compositions, particularly for imparting improved softness and detersive effects to fabrics laundered therewith, include in addition to conventional builder and principally anionic surfactant components, particulate cationic softener of the di-lower-di-higher alkyl quaternary ammonium and/or heterocyclic imide type, e.g. imidazolinium, in admixture with an ethoxylated tertiary amine softener/dispersing agent, such as N-tallow tertiary amine ethoxylated with from about 2 to 15 moles of ethylene oxide. The cationic softener-ethoxylated amine mixture is in the form of a spaghetti, flake, or other shape and is present in the product composition as substantially homogeneously dispersed, discrete particles. A process of laundering fabrics using the above-mentioned composition is also described.
problem: Achieving uniform dispersion of functional additives in particulate detergent compositions to enhance fabric softness and cleaning efficacy.
constraint: Maintaining physical stability and homogeneity of the mixture during storage and use, avoiding phase separation or clumping.
mechanism: Combine two chemically distinct additives in a specific physical morphology to form discrete, homogeneously dispersed particles that synergistically enhance functional properties of a particulate mixture while maintaining physical stability.
mechanism_raw: Combining a cationic softener with an ethoxylated tertiary amine in a specific physical form (e.g., spaghetti, flake) to create homogeneously dispersed discrete particles that synergistically improve performance.
residual_terms: ["chemically distinct additives", "physical morphology", "homogeneously dispersed particles", "synergistically enhance functional properties"]

abstract: A classifying cyclone efficient at removing very fine particles. In preferred embodiments, the cyclone employs an annular bevel ring positioned along the interior wall to redirect separated particles from the wall back into the path of classifying air. A control air deflector is placed in the path of the classifying airstream and adjusted vertically to provide adjustment of the annular orifice through which the classifying air passes. The air deflector is positioned at approximately the height of the bevel ring.
problem: Efficiently separating very fine particles from a gas stream in a classifying cyclone.
constraint: Positioning the air deflector at the height of the bevel ring to balance particle redirection efficiency with airflow adjustment, minimizing re-entrainment of fine particles.
mechanism: Redirect separated particulates from a containment surface back into a primary airflow using a shaped annular element, while a vertically positionable flow modifier adjusts an orifice to optimize particulate trajectory and minimize re-entrainment.
mechanism_raw: Using an annular bevel ring to redirect separated particles from the cyclone wall back into the classifying airflow, combined with a vertically adjustable air deflector to control the annular orifice and optimize particle trajectory.
residual_terms: ["shaped annular element", "containment surface", "primary airflow", "vertically positionable flow modifier", "orifice", "particulate trajectory", "re-entrainment"]

abstract: An improved electric field dependent fluid and method of preparing the same for use at temperatures in excess of 100.degree. C. (typically 120.degree. C.) without releasing water comprising: a nonconductive liquid phase; and a dispersed particulate crystalline zeolite phase (e.g., M.sub.(x/n) [AlO.sub.2).sub.x (SiO.sub.2).sub.y ] wH.sub.2 O where M is a metal cation or mixture of metal cations of average valence charge n, x and y are integers and the ratio of y to x is from about 1 to about 5, and w is a variable). Such field dependent fluids are particularly useful in automotive and/or other high temperatures applications.
problem: Maintaining electric field dependent fluid performance at high temperatures without releasing water.
constraint: Balancing thermal stability of the zeolite-water interaction against the need for sufficient ionic conductivity in the fluid for electric field responsiveness.
mechanism: Dispersing particulate materials with a porous crystalline structure into a nonconductive liquid phase stabilizes the fluid by retaining a volatile component within the particulate lattice even at elevated temperatures, preventing phase separation or conductivity loss.
mechanism_raw: Dispersing particulate crystalline zeolites (with a specific aluminosilicate structure and variable water content) into a nonconductive liquid phase stabilizes the fluid by retaining water within the zeolite lattice even at elevated temperatures, preventing phase separation or conductivity loss.

abstract: An X-ray lithography system, in which an X-ray beam is separated from synchrotron radiation beams and reflected by a scanning mirror which vertically scans the reflected X-ray beam. The X-ray is irradiated into an exposure chamber via a beryllium window, which is vertically oscillated in such a manner that the beryllium window is shifted up and down in synchronization with the scanning operation of the X-ray beam.
problem: Precisely controlling and directing an X-ray beam during lithography exposure to ensure accurate patterning.
constraint: Maintaining exact temporal and spatial synchronization between the mirror and window movements to avoid beam misalignment or exposure errors.
mechanism: Synchronizing oscillatory motion of a beam-deflecting element with oscillatory motion of a beam-gating element ensures coordinated control of beam position and transmission during scanning.
mechanism_raw: Synchronizing vertical oscillation of a scanning mirror (which deflects the X-ray beam) with vertical oscillation of a beryllium window (which gates the beam's path into the exposure chamber), ensuring the beam's position and transmission remain coordinated during scanning.

abstract: Transaction processing enclosures for containment of electronic data processing equipment, banking apparatus and the like incorporating a housing comprising a composite laminate composed of reflective, refractory and structural elements to provide an enclosure of unique structural integrity, and protection to the environment within and outside said enclosure against adverse factors such as impact and fire, and insulation against wide variations in temperature exterior to said enclosure while sustaining a stable environment within said enclosure.
problem: Protecting sensitive electronic equipment from environmental threats like fire, impact, and temperature fluctuations while maintaining internal stability.
constraint: Balancing the thickness and composition of each layer to achieve sufficient structural integrity without compromising thermal or fire protection performance.
mechanism: Constructing an enclosure from a layered composite structure, where each layer provides a distinct protective function (e.g., reflective barrier, thermal insulation, structural reinforcement) through its material properties and arrangement.
mechanism_raw: Constructing an enclosure from a composite laminate combining reflective (heat/fire barrier), refractory (thermal insulation), and structural (impact resistance) layers, each contributing distinct protective functions through their layered arrangement.

abstract: A circular knitting machine includes needles and loop-sinking sinkers longitudinally movable relative to each other in opposite directions. Each needle is provided with a non-movable slide. The movements of the needles and the sinkers are controlled by cams. Each slide has a tip. The control cam for the needle head and the control cam for the sinker and the height of the needle slide tip are selected so that the tips of the needle slides lie in the region which extends between the point of crossing of said control cams and the maximal vertical level of the knockover edge of the sinker.
problem: Coordinating needle and sinker movements in a circular knitting machine to produce consistent loop formation without mechanical interference.
constraint: Matching cam geometry and slide tip height to the sinker's vertical travel range to avoid collisions while maintaining loop consistency.
mechanism: Using shaped mechanical guides to control the relative longitudinal motion of two interlocked components, while positioning fixed contact points within a defined vertical range relative to a reference edge on the second component, ensuring precise timing of interaction and avoiding collisions.
mechanism_raw: Using cam profiles to control the relative longitudinal motion of needles and sinkers, while positioning non-movable needle slide tips within a specific vertical range relative to the sinker's knockover edge, ensuring precise timing of loop creation and transfer.

abstract: A dye-donor element for thermal dye transfer comprising a support having on one side thereof a near-infrared absorbing dye comprising a dithiolene-nickel(II) complex dispersed in a polymeric binder, and on the other side thereof a slipping layer comprising a lubricant, the dye having the formula: ##STR1## wherein each R.sup.1, R.sup.2, R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 independently represents a substituted or unsubstituted alkyl group having from 1 to about 10 carbon atoms; a substituted or unsubstituted aryl group having from about 6 to about 10 carbon atms; a substituted or unsubstitutted heterocyclic group; or R.sup.1 and R.sup.2 may be combined together with the carbon atoms to which they are attached to form a 5- or 6-membered carbocyclic or heterocyclic ring; or R.sup.3 and R.sup.4 may be combined together with the carbon atoms to which they are attached to form a 5- or 6-membered carbocyclic or heterocyclic ring.
problem: Achieving efficient near-infrared (NIR) light absorption for thermal dye transfer printing without degrading the dye or support structure.
constraint: Optimizing the substituent groups and binder composition to balance NIR absorption efficiency, thermal stability, and mechanical release properties during printing.
mechanism: Incorporating a molecular complex with tailored substituent groups into a polymer matrix on a support layer, where the complex's structure enables strong electromagnetic absorption while the matrix and release layer prevent adhesion and thermal degradation during transfer.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a dithiolene-nickel(II) complex with tailored substituent groups (R1-R4) into a polymer binder on a support layer, where the complex's molecular structure enables strong NIR absorption while the binder and slipping layer prevent adhesion and thermal degradation during transfer.

abstract: A method of obtaining a reinforcing assembly comprising reinforcement threads and a solid matrix is characterized by the fact that reinforcement threads surrounded individually by a sheathing of organic material I and furthermore surrounded by another sheathing of organic material II are grouped together, by the fact that the material II is caused to migrate into voids between the threads sheathed with material I and by the fact that the material II is caused to solidify.
problem: Creating a reinforcing composite assembly of threads and solid matrix with uniform structural integrity and strong thread-matrix bonding.
constraint: The two organic materials must be compatible — material II must be able to flow into interstitial spaces between material I-sheathed threads and then solidify to form a coherent matrix without degrading material I.
mechanism: Sequential dual-material application: a first material individually coats each reinforcement element, then a second material is caused to migrate into the voids between the individually coated elements and solidify, forming a continuous matrix that binds all elements together while each retains its individual coating.
mechanism_raw: Sequential dual-material application: a first organic material individually sheathes each reinforcement thread, then a second organic material is caused to migrate into the voids between the individually sheathed threads and solidify, forming a continuous matrix that binds all threads together while each thread retains its individual coating.

abstract: Improvements are disclosed for liquid flow drainage control in gravity type systems such as sewage septic tank systems. A plastic cap which is insertable into the ends of the drainage pipes that project into a distribution box is formed with an end face and a cylindrical body. The end face is generally circular having a larger diameter than the outer diameter of the drainage pipes into which the cap is to be inserted. The outer periphery of the end face is provided with an interdigital or scalloped pattern to facilitate easy gripping even in the most adverse conditions. The end face is further provided with an eccentric discharge hole which is located along a diameter of the end face so that the hole is always some distance from the interior surface of the cylindrical body so that the hole forms a weir to the inlet of the drainage pipe into which the end cap is inserted. The eccentric hole is provided with an outwardly projecting flange which, in cooperation with a spirit level, is used for rough leveling. The cylindrical body is made of a pliant material allowing it to conform to the irregular internal diameter of a plastic drainage pipe. The projecting end of the cylindrical body is provided with a radially extending sealing flange which also conforms to the internal diameter of the plastic drainage pipe.
problem: Controlling liquid flow drainage in gravity-fed systems (e.g., septic tank distribution boxes) where pipe internal diameters are irregular and precise flow regulation is needed.
constraint: The cap material must be sufficiently pliant to conform to irregular pipe geometries while maintaining the structural integrity needed for the eccentric hole to function as a weir.
mechanism: Eccentric aperture placement on a circular end face creates a weir effect that regulates flow into the drainage conduit, while a pliant cylindrical body and sealing flange conform to irregular internal geometries to maintain a seal and proper positioning.
mechanism_raw: Eccentric hole placement on a circular end face creates a weir effect that regulates flow into the drainage pipe, while a pliant cylindrical body and sealing flange conform to irregular internal pipe diameters to maintain a seal and proper positioning.

abstract: An electrical trigger mechanism for a gun 1 has a relatively small and lightweight firing pin 5 which is held in its stationary position shown in outline 5.sup.1 by a permanent magnet 2 or the like and in which position the firing pin is spaced apart from a solenoid coil 4. A capacitive discharge circuit discharges through the solenoid coil upon operation of the gun trigger, the movement of or pressure on the gun trigger being detected by any suitable triggering means such as an optical interrupter, a microswitch or a strain gauge. The energizing of the solenoid coil 4 is for a sufficiently short time that the magnetic field has decayed or substantially decayed by the time the firing pin reaches the coil 4. The firing pin is therefore not restrained as it passes through the coil 4 into an abuttment member 6 which has a substantially central aperture through which the firing pin 4 can project in impacting against the bullet or cartridge 9 in position within the barrel 8. After firing, the permanent magnet 2 or the like will attract the firing pin 5 back into the stationary position ready for the next firing.
problem: Electrically triggering a gun firing pin with reliable, repeatable operation and automatic reset without mechanical linkages.
constraint: The solenoid energization duration must be precisely controlled to be shorter than the time it takes the firing pin to travel from its rest position to the coil, ensuring the magnetic field has decayed or substantially decayed by the time the pin reaches the coil.
mechanism: A lightweight element is held stationary by a permanent magnetic field and spaced from an electromagnetic coil; upon activation, a capacitive energy storage circuit energizes the coil for a precisely timed duration shorter than the element's travel time to the coil, so the magnetic field decays before the element arrives, allowing unimpeded passage; the permanent magnetic field then returns the element to its rest position.
