mechanism_raw: A lightweight firing pin is held stationary by a permanent magnet and spaced from a solenoid coil; upon trigger activation, a capacitive discharge circuit energizes the coil for a precisely timed duration shorter than the pin's travel time to the coil, so the magnetic field decays before the pin arrives, allowing unimpeded passage; the permanent magnet then attracts the pin back to its rest position.

abstract: Solid propellant is first placed in a closed container with a solution of ter and detergent. A water slurry is then created by injecting compressed air in superheated steam into the solution to place the propellant and solution under several atmospheres of pressure and at the same time to raise the temperature of the solution to 400.degree.-600.degree. F. This results in oxidation of the propellant into such constituents as carbon dioxide, water, nitrous oxide and etc. These constituents are then removed by absorption.
problem: Oxidizing solid propellant into useful gaseous constituents (CO2, water, nitrous oxide) while removing reaction products from the system.
constraint: Temperature must be maintained at 400–600°F and pressure at several atmospheres to achieve effective oxidation while keeping the system closed for subsequent absorption-based product removal.
mechanism: Solid propellant is placed in a closed chamber with a liquid medium, then compressed gas is injected through heated vapor to create a pressurized, heated mixture that drives oxidation of the propellant, after which oxidation products are removed by absorption.
mechanism_raw: Solid propellant is placed in a closed container with a water-detergent solution, then compressed air is injected through superheated steam to create a pressurized, heated slurry that drives oxidation of the propellant, after which the oxidation products are removed by absorption.

abstract: An aluminum alloy-core material for brazing, having improved secular corrosion resistance is provided, by a composition of 0.5.about.1.0% of Cu, 0.5.about.1.0% of Mn, 0.10.about.0.30% of Ti, 0.3% or less of Fe, less than 0.10% of Si, and balance of Al, and contains, occasionally at least one element selected from the group consisting of from 0.05 to 0.4% of Mg, from 0.05 to 0.4% of Cr, and from 0.05 to 0.4% of Zr. The alloy is free of an Al-Fe intermetallic compound, has an improved resistance to pitting corrosion and exhibits only a slight reduction in mechanical strength after brazing.
reason: This patent discloses a specific aluminum alloy composition with defined elemental ranges and the absence of Al-Fe intermetallic compounds. It is a material specification rather than a causal mechanism — it states what composition works but does not explain how the composition produces the corrosion resistance or strength retention effect through a functional relationship.

abstract: A soil amendment material and an associated process for the preparation thereof, comprising a water swellable hydrophilic polymer infused with high concentrations of plant nutritive salts. The amendment is prepared by repeated soaking of hydrophilic swellable polymer particles in a solution of nutritive salts in water, followed by heat application to drive off the entrained water, leaving the nutrients entrapped in the polymer particles.
problem: Delivering plant nutrients to soil in a controlled, sustained manner while maintaining their availability and minimizing leaching.
constraint: Balancing nutrient loading capacity with the polymer's swelling rate and structural integrity to ensure controlled release without premature depletion or physical degradation.
mechanism: A swellable matrix infused with active agents is dehydrated and applied to a target medium. Upon rehydration, the matrix expands, creating a controlled release pathway for the entrapped agents as the matrix interacts with environmental moisture. The release rate is governed by the matrix's swelling kinetics and structural stability, balancing loading capacity with sustained availability.
mechanism_raw: A water-swellable hydrophilic polymer is infused with nutrients via repeated soaking in a salt solution, followed by dehydration. When applied to soil, the polymer rehydrates and swells, gradually releasing the entrapped nutrients as the polymer matrix expands and interacts with soil moisture.

abstract: A furnace water cooled tube wall portion (10) is separated from heated gasses by cast refractory material (12). A metal isolation plate (14) against the tubes (18) separates the tubes from the refractory material (12) and has projecting elongated anchors (30) with shanks (32) attached at spaced locations to mechanically join the refractory material to isolation plate (14). Anchors (30) have conical chamber washers welded to shanks (32) to shield the locations from cast refractory material at the spaced locations. This permits bending of shanks (32) to accommodate thermal expansion force created movement between isolation plate (14) and the refractory material (12).
problem: Managing thermal expansion mismatches between water-cooled tubes and refractory materials in high-temperature industrial furnaces to prevent structural failure.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical coupling between materials while accommodating differential thermal expansion rates, ensuring durability under cyclic heating and cooling.
mechanism: A mechanical coupling system uses deformable anchors and protective elements to join two materials with differing thermal expansion coefficients. The anchors bend under differential thermal stress, while the protective elements shield critical attachment points from infiltration, enabling controlled deformation without compromising structural integrity during cyclic heating and cooling.
mechanism_raw: Metal isolation plates with projecting anchors and conical washers mechanically join refractory material to the tubes. The anchors are designed to bend under thermal stress, while the washers shield critical attachment points from refractory material infiltration, allowing controlled deformation without compromising structural integrity.
residual_terms: ["deformable anchors", "protective elements", "thermal expansion coefficients", "cyclic heating and cooling"]

abstract: A method is disclosed for preparing coated, frozen comestibles which are stable when stored for extended periods and which, when reconstituted by microwave heating, have a texture and appearance organoleptically equivalent or superior to that of fat fried coated comestibles. According to the method, the comestibles are enrobed with a first coating of a batter including wheat flour and shortening, placed in a heated water bath for up to sixty seconds, fried, given a second coating, fried a second time and frozen.
reason: The mechanism is a specific food-processing sequence (multiple coatings and fryings) tailored to a narrow application. While it addresses texture and stability, the causal principle (layered coating to mimic fried texture) is not broadly transferable beyond comestibles.

abstract: A method of providing a normalized indication of the printing ink supply to a printing station of a printing machine, which includes main and ductor roller motors respectively operating at a first and a second speed, comprises generating first and second pulse trains having first and second pulse frequencies respectively proportional to the first and second speeds; forming a ratio of the first and second frequencies at predetermined time intervals; storing the thus formed ratio; and displaying the stored ratio. An arrangement for performing the above method includes first and second incremental digital transducers, a first counter having a counting input connected through a first gate circuit to an output of the first transducer and an output which is activated when a settable counting volume has been reached, a second counter having a counting input connected through a second gate circuit to the output of the second transducer and an output connected to a digital storage device, and a triggering circuit having inputs connected to the outputs of the first transducer and of the first counter, the triggering circuit generating a start/stop signal and a resetting signal which are respectively supplied to control inputs of the first and second gate circuits and to resetting inputs of the first and second counters.
problem: Accurately monitoring the ink supply level in a printing station despite variations in motor speeds and mechanical wear.
constraint: Ensuring the ratio calculation remains accurate over time despite potential sensor degradation, mechanical backlash, or asynchronous motor behavior.
mechanism: A feedback system generates pulse trains proportional to the operational speeds of two moving components. These pulse trains are sampled at intervals, and their frequency ratio is computed and stored to provide a normalized measurement of a target parameter. The ratio inherently compensates for speed fluctuations and mechanical drift, maintaining accuracy over time despite sensor degradation or asynchronous behavior.
mechanism_raw: Pulse trains proportional to the speeds of the main and ductor roller motors are generated and sampled at intervals. A ratio of these pulse frequencies is computed, stored, and displayed, providing a normalized indication of ink supply that inherently compensates for speed fluctuations and mechanical drift.

abstract: An oxonated poly (alkylene oxide) substantially devoid of hydrocarbon chains of 5 or more carbon atoms is used to treat substances bearing negative electrostatic charges, so as to reduce such charges without rendering the substance hyrophobic. In this manner static electricity can be reduced in textiles, paper or plastic film; glass or glass fibers can be lubricated; wood pulp can be debonded; anti-self sizing or water-dispersible paper can be made; clays, pigments and other minerals can be hydrophilized; bitumen can be recovered from oil or tar sands; and petroleum can be recovered from underground wells by secondary or tertiary recovery techniques.
problem: Reducing static electricity in materials (e.g., textiles, paper, plastics) without compromising their hydrophilic properties or functional performance.
constraint: Achieving sufficient charge dissipation while maintaining the material's original wetting, adhesion, or processing characteristics across diverse substrates.
mechanism: A surface treatment applies a conductive compound with minimal hydrophobic character to create a charge-dissipative layer. The compound adsorbs onto the material surface via electrostatic interaction, neutralizing static charges while preserving the material's original wetting and adhesion properties. The treatment avoids forming a hydrophobic barrier, ensuring functional performance across diverse substrates.
mechanism_raw: A chemical treatment using oxonated poly(alkylene oxide) with minimal hydrocarbon chains neutralizes static charges through electrostatic interaction while preserving hydrophilicity. The compound adsorbs onto surfaces, creating a conductive layer that dissipates charge without forming a hydrophobic barrier.

abstract: A vandal-proof cross bar assembly for securing the door of a refrigerated storage vault or similar chamber includes first and second mounting members secured on opposing sides of the door, and a cross bar each end of which is secured to a mounting member by a respective shackle lock. The locks attach to pivot posts extending from the mounting members. The posts pivot freely about a first axis, and the shackles each define a loose hinge about a second orthogonal axis, so that with one lock detached, the cross bar hangs freely and moves in a multi-axis articulated motion which prevents vandalism by prying and forcing the bar. In a preferred embodiment the mounting members are placed on adjacent exterior walls of the chamber and an L-shaped cross bar having a main bar and a shorter leg portion fits about a corner to engage the members and secure the door. The main bar pivots about the longitudinal axis of the shorter leg portion.
problem: Preventing vandalism by prying or forcing a cross bar used to secure a door or chamber.
constraint: Balancing security (resistance to forced entry) with the need for the bar to move freely when unlocked, while maintaining structural integrity under normal use.
mechanism: Articulated joints enable multi-directional movement of a securing element, allowing it to shift unpredictably when one attachment point is released. This distributes applied forces across multiple axes and structural paths, preventing concentrated prying or forcing actions from compromising the element's position.
mechanism_raw: Multi-axis articulated motion enabled by pivot posts and loose hinges allows the cross bar to hang freely and move unpredictably when one lock is detached, making it difficult to apply concentrated prying forces. The L-shaped design and pivoting leg further distribute forces around a corner.

abstract: A method is provided for checking the operability of protective instruction transmission systems in on-line operation in which at least two stations, particularly multi-instruction equipment, are connected to one another by transmission links and communication channels. The stations each comprise instruction input and output lines for checking the protective instructions and a first station controlling and checking of the operability transmits a test signal to a second station to be tested, the second station returning the signal to the first station unaltered. Upon receipt of the test signal, the respective inhibit of the instruction input and output lines is effected in the first and second stations. Simultaneously, the first station emits the first test instruction which the second station returns to the first station immediately after receipt and, therefore, effects the transmission of further test instructions in the first station. A test function sequence formed of a plurality of test instructions is terminated by transmission of an idle instruction which cancels the inhibit of the instruction input and output lines in the first station and in the second station.
problem: Verifying the operability of protective instruction transmission systems during online operation without disrupting normal communication.
constraint: Ensuring the test process does not interfere with ongoing communication or introduce false inhibits during normal operation.
mechanism: Test signals are transmitted in a closed loop between stations while temporarily suppressing normal input/output activity. Cascading test instructions verify signal integrity and system responsiveness, and a termination signal restores standard operation once verification is complete.
mechanism_raw: Test signals are transmitted between stations in a loop, with simultaneous inhibition of input/output lines and cascading test instructions to confirm signal integrity and system responsiveness. An idle instruction terminates the test sequence and restores normal operation.

abstract: To avoid, after excessive shocks in the underframe in the forestructure and at the coupling of a traction/thrust pivoted joint or device of a vehicle, deformations of a central buffer coupling at the underframe of the vehicle is proposed. Arranged between the carrier plate for the support of the traction/thrust device and the coupling uptake at the underframe in each instance is a shock absorber which in case of excessive shocks becomes deformed elastically and/or plastically and permits a deformation path preset for the force acting at the time.
problem: Preventing deformation of a central buffer coupling in a vehicle underframe during excessive shocks.
constraint: Allowing the shock absorber to deform sufficiently to absorb energy while maintaining structural support under normal operating conditions.
mechanism: A deformable energy-absorbing element is positioned between two structural components. Under excessive force, the element undergoes controlled elastic or plastic deformation, diverting energy away from the primary structure and preserving its integrity during normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A shock absorber placed between the carrier plate and coupling uptake deforms elastically or plastically under excessive force, providing a controlled deformation path that absorbs energy and protects the main coupling structure.

abstract: Finely divided, clean coal or other carbonaceous material is provided by forming a slurry of coarse coal in aqueous alkali solution and heating the slurry under pressure to above the critical conditions of steam. The supercritical fluid penetrates and is trapped in the porosity of the coal as it swells in a thermoplastic condition at elevated temperature. By a sudden, explosive release of pressure the coal is fractured into finely divided particles with release of sulfur-containing gases and minerals. The finely divided coal is recovered from the minerals for use as a clean coal product.
problem: Reducing carbonaceous material like coal to finely divided particles while removing sulfur-containing gases and minerals.
constraint: Controlling the timing and magnitude of pressure release to achieve desired particle size and impurity separation without excessive energy input.
mechanism: A pressurized fluid infiltrates and expands a material in a thermally conditioned state, then a rapid pressure reduction induces internal stress fractures. The sudden depressurization simultaneously releases trapped impurities and fragments the material into smaller particles.
mechanism_raw: Supercritical fluid penetrates and swells the coal in a thermoplastic state, then a sudden pressure release causes explosive fracturing into fine particles. The rapid depressurization also releases trapped impurities.

abstract: A toothbrush having a pad of bristles, a neck region and a handle is disclosed. The bristle pad has three longitudinally arranged columns of bristles, except at the distal end of the pad where there are two additional columns of bristles. The handle is short, so as to bring the user's hand into a closer relation to the mouth and teeth. The reverse side of the bristle pad has a concavity for receiving the user's finger.
reason: The patent describes specific product features (bristle column arrangement, short handle, concavity) tailored to toothbrush ergonomics and cleaning, but does not describe a generalizable causal mechanism that could be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A biofeedback system to train an exerciser while he carries out athletic activity in which his arm or feet members move rhythmically, the system translating this movement into an audible musical rhythm which makes it possible for the exerciser to being his activity into harmony with a musical rhythm conducive to optimal conditions of exercise. The system includes a compact electronic music synthesizer having a settable rhythm section, the output of the system being fed to a headset worn by the exerciser so that the music heard by the exerciser has a beat determined by the setting. The arm or feet members having sensors attached thereto which yield pulses whose rate is determined by the movement of these members, the pulses being applied to the rhythm section to control the beat setting of the music so that it is in synchronism with the movement of the members.
problem: Enabling an exerciser to synchronize their rhythmic physical activity with an optimal musical beat in real time.
constraint: The system must maintain real-time synchronization between movement and musical beat without perceptible delay, requiring precise sensor-to-audio latency control.
mechanism: A closed-loop feedback system where movement-derived signals dynamically modulate an audio output's temporal pattern, creating a self-synchronizing loop that guides rhythmic activity toward alignment with the output signal.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop feedback system where sensors on the exerciser's moving body parts generate pulses proportional to their movement, which dynamically adjust the beat of synthesized music delivered via a headset. This creates a self-synchronizing loop where the exerciser's own motion directly modulates the feedback signal, guiding them toward harmonious activity.

abstract: An aqueous electrolytic machining electrolyte for iron-boron-neodymium/praseodymium alloys consisting essentially of alkali metal chlorates and dichromates wherein the chlorate ion concentration is at least about 2.5 molar and the ratio of the molar concentrations of the dichromate ion to the chlorate ion is about 0.033 to about 0.12.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical composition for an electrolyte solution, which is a material formulation rather than a generalizable functional mechanism. The mechanism is tied to the chemical properties of the ions and their concentrations for a narrow application in electrolytic machining.

abstract: For the continuous pressing of sheet material in a reaction zone between two endless, heated press belts of a double band press at increased process temperatures, the capability for operating at process temperatures which are higher than critical, permissible operating temperatures of the double band press is achieved by heating the press belts in such a way that they have the highest temperature at their outsides facing the sheet material with heat flow through the press belt being effected from the hot outer side to the opposite inner side of the press belt. The heat flow direction in the reaction zone which otherwise leads from a pressure plate to the press belt outer side is thus reversed and, heating members are arranged in the vicinity of the press belt on the outer side thereof shortly before the reaction zone.
problem: Achieving higher process temperatures in a double band press without exceeding the thermal limits of the press belts.
constraint: The heating elements must be positioned and controlled to maintain a precise temperature gradient across the belt thickness, ensuring heat flows inward without causing thermal degradation of the belt or press structure.
mechanism: A thermal management system that establishes a controlled temperature gradient by maintaining a higher temperature on an outer surface relative to an inner surface, directing heat flow inward to enable elevated operational temperatures while protecting internal components from thermal degradation.
mechanism_raw: Reversing the natural heat flow direction by heating the outer surface of the press belt (facing the sheet material) to a higher temperature than the inner surface, forcing heat to flow inward. This allows the reaction zone to operate at temperatures above the critical threshold of the press structure while protecting internal components.

abstract: A buckle of a type comprised of two identical members, which can be releasably interlocked to each other. Each member has first and second cantilevered arms, one of which is resiliently flexible and has a locking tab, and which are adapted to wedge against an internal wedge formed in the outer member so as to cause the members to spring apart when released. The locking tabs can be manually pressed by a user to release the members.
problem: Creating a releasable mechanical interlock between two identical components that can be manually released without tools.
constraint: The resilience and geometry of the arms and wedge must balance secure locking under load with reliable manual release, requiring precise material selection and dimensional tolerances.
mechanism: A symmetric mechanical interlock using resilient arms with engagement features that wedge against a complementary structure when connected, with manual actuation on the engagement features disengaging the wedge to allow the arms to return to a released state.
mechanism_raw: Using resilient cantilevered arms with locking tabs that wedge against an internal wedge structure when interlocked. Manual pressure on the tabs disengages the wedge, allowing the arms to spring apart and release the connection. The symmetry of the two identical members ensures bidirectional compatibility.

abstract: A helicopter weight and torque advisory system for connection to cargo hook load sensors, fuel flow, air temperature and altitude indicating systems of a helicopter. The advisory system provides the flight crew of the helicopter information as to available engine torque, gross weight, gross weight center of gravity condition, and weight supported by each cargo hook as an external sling load is raised and supported by the helicopter. Also information as to required engine torque for maximum helicopter range and endurance performance is provided.
problem: Providing real-time advisory information to helicopter flight crews about weight, torque, and center of gravity during cargo operations.
constraint: The system must process and reconcile data from physically and logically diverse sensors in real time, requiring robust data fusion algorithms and fail-safe communication protocols.
mechanism: A data fusion system that aggregates inputs from physically and logically diverse sensors into a centralized computational framework, deriving and presenting correlated operational parameters as real-time advisories by reconciling heterogeneous data streams.
mechanism_raw: Integrating data from multiple heterogeneous sensors (cargo hook load cells, fuel flow meters, temperature, altitude) into a centralized computational system that derives and displays critical flight parameters. This enables dynamic situational awareness by correlating disparate inputs into actionable advisories.

abstract: A method for measuring the type of motion and configuration of objects by observation of the objects and evaluation of the observation results, including the steps of: producing data representative of an image of the objects in a selected plane at successive time intervals; deriving, from the data, for each time interval, a representation of only one pair of coordinate values in the plane for each object; producing, from the coordinate values, representations of motion paths for the objects during a plurality of the time intervals; and producing, from the motion path representations, representations of the path traversed by each object, and the average local position, the period of dwell and number of reversals of direction of motion of each object during the plurality of time intervals.
problem: Efficiently tracking and analyzing the motion characteristics of multiple objects over time without excessive computational overhead.
constraint: Balancing data reduction (to minimize computational load) with sufficient fidelity to accurately capture motion dynamics and object interactions.
mechanism: Reducing multi-dimensional observational data to a minimal set of scalar values per tracked entity per sampling interval, then reconstructing trajectories and deriving temporal behavioral statistics from these reduced representations. This preserves essential dynamic information while minimizing computational processing requirements.
mechanism_raw: Reducing image data to a single pair of coordinate values per object per time interval, then deriving motion paths and statistical properties (e.g., dwell periods, direction reversals) from these simplified representations. This avoids processing full image data while retaining essential motion information.

abstract: The apparatus has at least one cam plate driven by a drive shaft in a piston pump or hydraulic pressure generator. The cam plate has a cam track or surface with at least two substantially sinusoidal protrusions and recesses or depressions on its circumference or perimeter. The rotation of this cam plate drives a crankshaft of a hydraulic piston and cylinder drive unit or motor by means of at least one plunger or cam follower or tappet and a piston through at least one transmission pipeline or conduit filled with a hydraulic medium. This transmission pipeline is attached without valves to the cylinder of the piston and is connected by means of an also valveless cylinder with a piston of the hydraulic piston and cylinder drive unit or motor. The cam track or surface is so structured that during uniform rotation of the cam plate of the piston pump or hydraulic pressure generator and the crankshaft of the hydraulic piston and cylinder drive unit or motor, the volume of that part of the system filled with the hydraulic medium, i.e. the total volume including the pump piston displacement, cylinder dead space and the volume of the transmission pipeline or conduit, plus the volume of the motor piston displacement, remains constant over time.
problem: Maintaining consistent hydraulic pressure and flow in a valveless system during rotational motion, avoiding pressure fluctuations caused by volume changes.
constraint: Designing the cam track profile to precisely balance volume changes across all system components while maintaining mechanical simplicity and durability.
mechanism: Configuring a rotating mechanical interface with complementary volumetric features such that the aggregate displacement volume of all connected chambers remains invariant throughout a complete rotation cycle. This maintains constant medium volume without requiring active flow control elements.
mechanism_raw: Structuring the cam track geometry (e.g., sinusoidal protrusions/recesses) such that the total volume of hydraulic medium in the system (pump displacement, cylinder dead space, transmission lines, motor displacement) remains constant over time during uniform rotation. This eliminates the need for valves by ensuring volume conservation.

abstract: In a fuel injection system with an acceleration enrichment and a deceleration leaning, in which the transition compensation is determined by means of the throttle valve change speed in connection with the throttle valve change path. By means of the measurement of the throttle valve position the cause for the change of the air quantity is determined so that the information concerning a change of the operating state is present more quickly and a fuel leaning or fuel enrichment can accordingly also be effected more quickly. An intermediate injection threshold, which activates an intermediate injection calculation when exceeded, is built in, in addition, for the acceleration enrichment.
problem: Rapidly adjusting fuel injection in response to sudden changes in engine operating conditions (e.g., throttle position changes) to maintain optimal air-fuel ratios.
constraint: Balancing response speed (to avoid lean/rich spikes) with fuel efficiency and emission compliance during dynamic engine operation.
mechanism: Monitoring an input control signal and its temporal derivative to detect rapid state transitions, then applying a threshold-based activation scheme that triggers supplementary corrective actions when the rate of change exceeds a predetermined limit. This enables anticipatory adjustments to transient conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using throttle valve position and its rate of change (change speed) to trigger fuel enrichment or leaning adjustments. An intermediate injection threshold activates additional fuel calculations when acceleration exceeds a predefined limit, enabling faster response to transient conditions.
residual_terms: ["throttle valve position", "change speed", "fuel enrichment", "leaning adjustments", "intermediate injection threshold", "predefined limit"]

abstract: With the object of providing a glass run channel which can accommodate the curvature in both front elevation and plan, and also some degree of twisting, in this invention a glass run channel comprises a metal core of general S shape, the metal core having a continuous unbroken strip and a plurality of transversely extending slits forming between them bars or ribs extending transversely from the unbroken strip, the core being covered with an elastomer.
problem: Creating a flexible structural element (e.g., a window channel) that accommodates multi-axis curvature and twisting while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Optimizing slit geometry and elastomer properties to balance flexibility (for curvature accommodation) with strength (to resist mechanical stress and wear).
mechanism: Integrating a segmented flexible substrate with strategically placed discontinuities covered by a continuous compliant overlay. The discontinuities permit controlled multi-directional deformation while the overlay and remaining substrate segments maintain structural continuity and environmental sealing.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a slitted metal core (with transverse slits forming flexible ribs) covered by an elastomer. The slits allow controlled deformation in multiple directions, while the unbroken strip and elastomer coating preserve structural continuity and sealing.

abstract: A carding machine includes a licker-in and a main carding cylinder cooperating therewith; a feed roller arranged immediately upstream of the licker-in as viewed in a direction of material feed into the carding machine; and a feed table cooperating with the feed roller for advancing fiber material to the licker-in. The feed table is arranged for executing excursions towards and away from the feed roller as a function of the material quantity passing between the feed roller and the feed table and a measuring device operatively connected with the feed table for generating signals representing the excursions. There is provided a motor connected to the feed roller for rotating the same. The motor receives setting signals as a function of the excursions. The feed table has a movable first part operatively connected with the measuring device and a second part situated between the movable first part and the licker-in.
problem: Maintaining consistent fiber feed rate to a carding machine despite variations in material quantity or density.
constraint: Ensuring the feedback loop responds quickly enough to material changes without causing overcorrection or mechanical instability in the feed system.
mechanism: Implementing a closed-loop control system where a movable sensing element detects variations in material quantity, generating feedback signals proportional to these variations that modulate the actuation speed of a feeding mechanism. This dynamically compensates for input inconsistencies through continuous monitoring and adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Using a movable feed table segment connected to a measuring device to detect material quantity fluctuations. The table's excursions generate feedback signals that adjust the feed roller motor speed, creating a closed-loop system that dynamically compensates for material variations.
residual_terms: ["movable feed table segment", "measuring device", "feed roller motor", "feedback signals", "closed-loop system"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for preparing cast composite materials of nonmetallic particles in a metallic matrix, wherein particles are mixed into a molten metallic alloy to wet the molten metal to the particles, and the particles and metal are sheared past each other to promote wetting of the particles by the metal. The mixing occurs while minimizing the introduction of gas into the mixture, and while minimizing the retention of gas at the particle-liquid interface. Mixing is done at a maximum temperature whereat the particles do not substantially chemically degrade in the molten metal during the time required for processing, and casting is done at a temperature sufficiently high that there is no solid metal present in the melt. Mixing is preferably accomplished with a dispersing impeller, or a dispersing impeller used with a sweeping impeller.
problem: Achieving uniform wetting of nonmetallic particles by a molten metallic alloy without introducing gas defects or degrading the particles during processing.
constraint: Balancing temperature to prevent particle degradation and gas retention while maintaining sufficient fluidity for wetting and casting.
mechanism: Apply controlled mechanical shearing between particulate and molten material phases at a temperature optimized to maximize interfacial bonding while minimizing gas entrapment and thermal degradation, followed by casting under conditions ensuring complete fluidity of the molten phase.
mechanism_raw: Controlled mechanical shearing of particles and molten metal past each other at a temperature optimized to maximize wetting while minimizing gas entrapment and chemical degradation, combined with casting at a temperature ensuring no solid metal is present in the melt.

abstract: A toy musical playset having a teapot with xylophone keys which is filled with styrene plastic beads, a number of pots with xylophone keys and a pan with a xylophone key, tambourine symbols and musical ribs. The pots, pan and teapot may be stacked on top of each other. The toy pan may be used like a tambourine, or the musical ribs may be used with a toy spatula or spoon to make musical sounds. In addition, the toy teapot filled with beads may be shook to produce musical sounds. A child may strike the xylophone keys with a spoon producing musical sounds during play when the pots, pan and teapot are in a stacked configuration, or when they are spread out on top of a table. The pots or pan may also be hung on a child's belt.
reason: The patent describes a toy with multiple sound-producing elements but does not present a causal mechanism beyond combining components; it is a product feature list rather than a functional principle.

abstract: A cord cutter head for use in, for example, a cord cutter type grass trimmer has a housing having a downward opening, a spool mounted substantially in the center of the housing and carrying a flexible cutter cord wound thereon. An aperture is formed in the wall of the housing so as to allow the portion of the cutter cord unwound from the spool to pass therethrough. The cross-sectional shape of said spool has a longer axis and a shorter axis.
problem: Efficiently and reliably feeding a flexible cutter cord from a spool in a cord cutter head without tangling or uneven tension during operation.
constraint: Maintaining cord tension and preventing tangling while allowing smooth, controlled dispensing during cutting operations.
mechanism: Use a spool with a non-uniform cross-sectional geometry to regulate the unwinding dynamics of a flexible elongated element, ensuring consistent tension and preventing entanglement during dispensing through a constrained aperture.
mechanism_raw: Using a spool with an asymmetric cross-sectional shape (longer and shorter axes) to control the unwinding dynamics of the cutter cord, ensuring consistent cord release through the housing aperture.

abstract: A process is described for manufacturing laminated pieces, such as tiles and wall tiles, by means of successive independent extrusion of mortars or concretes, process in which mortar is deposited on some molds, said mortar is extruded and compacted and is dislodged from a transversal strip in the zone of contact of two consecutive molds. Thereafter a complete sheet of mortars is shaped on the first layer, filling in turn the emptied transversal zone and the limited sides and lastly the thickness of the piece is cut in its entirety in a vertical transversal plane. An installation is also described for carrying out the abovementioned process which in essence includes a molding bench with a series of molding heads, a lower pushing train of the molds, a bevelling mechanism inserted between the heads and which is provided with incisor blades and with devices for evacuating and returning the mortar, as well as with a cutting mechanism provided after the last head. Finally, a concrete tile is also described manufactured by double or by multiple extrusions, composed of two or of various layers of different mortars with a homogeneous external appearance.
problem: Manufacturing laminated tiles with multiple layers of different mortars/concretes while achieving a homogeneous external appearance and structural integrity.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and bonding between successive layers while avoiding mixing of different mortars during the extrusion and compaction steps.
mechanism: Perform sequential independent forming and densification of discrete material layers onto a substrate, with interlayer adhesion promoted by selective displacement and redistribution of material between adjacent layers, followed by thickness adjustment through transverse cutting.
mechanism_raw: Successive independent extrusion and compaction of mortar layers onto molds, with transversal strip dislodging and filling to ensure layer adhesion and uniform shaping, followed by vertical cutting to finalize thickness.

abstract: Apparatus and an associated method for inspecting translucent containers to determine whether haze or pearlescence exists include a light source and associated photodetectors which are in spaced relationship to permit passage of containers to be inspected therebetween. A processing unit determines whether a particular predetermined linear array of photodetectors has been illuminated to indicate the presence of pearlescence, whether a conical light beam has illuminated a circular array to indicate the presence of haze or whether neither defect exists. In a preferred embodiment, individual portions of the container less than the full circumference are tested with the results being cumulatively determined so as to minimize the likelihood that minor defects will provide a false reading of the presence of either haze or pearlescence. Counters, which are preferably electronic in nature to afford adequate speed of response may be used to total separately the number of sensors illuminated in the haze category, pearlescence category or no defect category and a comparison made to determine which of the characteristics exist for a particular container.
problem: Detecting haze or pearlescence defects in translucent containers with high accuracy while minimizing false readings from minor defects.
constraint: Balancing inspection speed and accuracy by testing sub-regions of the container and aggregating data to avoid misclassification of minor defects as significant flaws.
mechanism: Employ distinct illumination configurations to selectively activate sensor regions corresponding to different defect types, combined with cumulative evaluation of partial surface areas to aggregate detection signals and suppress false positives from minor anomalies.
mechanism_raw: Using distinct optical patterns (linear array for pearlescence, conical beam for haze) to illuminate specific sensor arrays, combined with cumulative testing of partial container regions to aggregate results and reduce false positives.

abstract: A consolidated metal-ceramic composite comprises a first phase of particles of aluminum oxide or a solid solution based on aluminum oxide uniformly distributed in a second matrix phase wherein the second matrix phase is non-reactive with aluminum oxide and contains a sufficient amount of titanium carbide at the interface between the first and second phase to prevent a chemical reaction at the interface during consolidation at the liquidus temperature and which exhibits good mechanical properties with regard to strength and toughness at high temperatures up to about 1200.degree. C.
problem: Preventing chemical reactions at the interface between aluminum oxide particles and a matrix phase during high-temperature consolidation of metal-ceramic composites.
constraint: Balancing the titanium carbide content to prevent reactions without compromising the composite's strength and toughness at temperatures up to 1200°C.
mechanism: Introducing a controlled amount of a chemical barrier material at the interface between two phases to suppress interfacial reactions during high-temperature consolidation, while preserving mechanical integrity through balanced compositional constraints.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a controlled amount of titanium carbide at the interface between the first and second phases to act as a chemical barrier, preventing interfacial reactions during consolidation at the liquidus temperature while maintaining mechanical properties.

abstract: An embedded track construction for a transit railway including first and second parallel, spaced rails extending an indefinite length in a first longitudinal direction. A composite insert assembly extends along the indefinite length of the rails to electrically insulate the track rails from the surrounding ground surface. The composite insert also provides a positive water seal and allows lateral movement of the rail. The inserts include a first generally rigid channel and an elastomeric member received thereon. The rigid channel preferably defines an inverted, generally U-shaped configuration in which one leg is interposed between the top and bottom flanges of the rails. A second leg abuttingly engages conventional support ties that are perpendicularly disposed to the transit rails. Gauge side inserts include a cut-out formed in the elastomeric member to receive an associated wheel flange. The inserts facilitate crossing of the railway in a transverse direction, as well as travel in the longitudinal direction by emergency vehicles or the like.
problem: Electrically insulating transit railway rails from the ground while providing water sealing, lateral movement accommodation, and enabling transverse vehicle crossings.
constraint: Combining rigid structural support with elastomeric flexibility to handle both longitudinal rail movement and transverse vehicle loads without compromising insulation or sealing.
mechanism: Using a composite structure combining rigid and elastomeric elements to mechanically decouple a conductive member from a grounded surface, enabling lateral movement accommodation and transverse load passage while maintaining electrical isolation and environmental sealing.
mechanism_raw: Using a composite insert with a rigid U-shaped channel and an elastomeric member to mechanically decouple the rails from the ground, with cut-outs in the elastomer to allow wheel flange passage and emergency vehicle travel.
residual_terms: ["composite structure", "rigid and elastomeric elements", "mechanical decoupling", "electrical isolation", "environmental sealing"]

abstract: An energy-conserving light-transmitting thermal barrier is disclosed in the form of a packet consisting of two light-transmitting plastic or fiberglass translucent panels between which is sandwiched a multi-layered light-transmitting insulation which consists of clear thermally-insulating flexible plastic sheets on which there are flat air-filled bubbles. The panels may have inner ribs which press on the multi-layered insulation, and the ribs may have barbs to pierce and hold the insulation place. The packets are employed to cover light-transmitting openings in a building. When the packets are supported in rigid frames, such frame assemblies can be used as openable light-transmitting barriers to cover windows, doors and skylights.
problem: Providing thermal insulation for light-transmitting building openings while maintaining structural integrity and light transmission.
constraint: Maintaining light transmission and structural rigidity while maximizing air-filled bubble insulation density without collapsing the layered structure.
mechanism: Forming a multi-layered insulation assembly by sandwiching flexible sheets with enclosed gas-filled voids between rigid translucent panels, using internal mechanical fasteners to compress and secure the layers, creating a sealed thermal barrier that maintains structural rigidity and light transmission.
mechanism_raw: Sandwiching multi-layered flexible plastic sheets with flat air-filled bubbles between translucent panels, using inner ribs with barbs to press and pierce the insulation layers into place, creating a sealed thermal barrier.

abstract: A residual quantity filler is described in which a cylindrical filling tube is used in place of a filling funnel, with a lid arrangement being provided in the filling tube and with the lid arrangement moving during the dispensing step with the dispensed material as a result of the differential pressure between the atmosphere and the vacuum prevailing at inside the filling tube, thus ensuring that the entire residual quantity can be continuously and completely processed.
problem: Ensuring complete dispensing of residual material from a filling container without manual intervention or waste.
constraint: Maintaining a consistent pressure differential to ensure the lid moves reliably without jamming or allowing air ingress that would disrupt the vacuum.
mechanism: Employing a pressure-responsive movable barrier within a containment vessel that automatically translates due to a pressure differential between an external environment and an internal vacuum, continuously expelling residual contents during dispensing without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Using a cylindrical filling tube with a pressure-responsive lid that moves automatically due to the differential pressure between atmospheric pressure and the vacuum inside the tube, continuously pushing residual material out during dispensing.

abstract: Surfactants consisting of esters of di- or tri-carboxylic hydroxyacids having the formula: ##STR1## wherein: X=H, --CH.sub.2 COOR; PA1 Y=H, OH, with the proviso that Y=H when X=--CH.sub.2 COOR; PA1 R, R.sub.1, R.sub.2, which may be the same or different, are H an alkali or alkaline-earth metal, --NH.sub.4, a cation of an ammonium organic base, or an A radical selected from the group consisting of etherified (C.sub.6 -C.sub.16) alkyl polysaccharides containing from 2 to 6 saccharide units and etherified (C.sub.6 -C.sub.16) hydroxyalkyl aliphatic polyalcohols containing from 2 to 16 hydroxyl groups; and wherein at least one of said R, R.sub.1, R.sub.2 is an A radical.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical composition of surfactants with defined molecular structures and functional groups. While the chemical structure may enable certain properties, the mechanism is primarily a list of material components and their chemical relationships rather than a causal functional operation that can be abstracted to other fields.

abstract: The opening cylinder comprising a cylindrical ring serving as a needle support and being provided with needle-housing bores extending from the inner ring surface to the outer one is designed to carry needles comprising a point section of generally tapered shape and a shaft section, the latter being pressed into and seated with force fit in a radially inner section of a corresponding one of said bores. A radially outer section of the bore surrounds a portion of said needle point section so as to form an annular groove therearound at the orifice of the bore in the outer ring surface. The radially inner section of the bore or at least part thereof has a diameter which is at least as great as the diameter of the outer section of the bore in the range of its orifice in the outer ring surface. This ensures having a simple and inexpensive needle mounting which a precise positioning of the needle tips protruding above the outer ring surface and with a secure holding of the needle shaft sections not only by press fit, but also by form fit connection due to the expansion of the inner bore section receiving the needle shaft section and the correspondingly lesser diameter of the outer bore section. The latter thus forms a bead or shoulder in front of the radially outer end edge of the needle shaft section establishing said form fit connection.
problem: Securely mounting needles on a rotating cylinder while ensuring precise positioning of needle tips and preventing loosening during operation.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise needle tip positioning with the requirement for a robust, low-cost mounting method that avoids complex machining or additional fasteners.
mechanism: A dual-region mounting interface where a first region provides interference-based retention and a second region creates a mechanical interlock, enabling both radial compression and axial constraint to secure a component without additional fasteners.
mechanism_raw: A bore with a radially inner section of larger diameter (for force-fit insertion of the needle shaft) and a radially outer section of smaller diameter (forming a bead/shoulder that creates a form-fit connection). This dual-diameter design allows both press-fit and mechanical interlocking to hold the needle securely.

abstract: Dressing of grinding wheels is performed by a dressing tool which is displaced first to be brought into contact with a grinding wheel and the contact is determined by measuring an electrical voltage of a piezoelectric element connected with the dressing tool, and then feeding of the dressing tool relative to the grinding wheel for dressing is performed by applying an electrical voltage to the piezoelectric element.
problem: Accurately detecting contact between a dressing tool and a grinding wheel, and then precisely controlling the tool's feed rate for effective dressing.
constraint: Ensuring the piezoelectric element can reliably perform both sensing and actuation without signal interference or mechanical hysteresis.
mechanism: A bidirectional transducer that converts mechanical stress into electrical signals for contact detection and converts electrical input into mechanical displacement for actuation, enabling real-time feedback control of a process through a single element.
mechanism_raw: Using a piezoelectric element connected to the dressing tool to both sense contact (via voltage changes from mechanical stress) and actuate movement (via applied voltage causing expansion/contraction). This dual functionality enables closed-loop control of the dressing process.

abstract: A reader printer includes a rotatable scanning mirror disposed in an optical path formed between a projection lens and a printer section in correspondence with a printer mode, the scanning mirror being rotated to perform scanning of an image and a movable mirror disposed near such a printer mode optical path for movement between an inserted position where it is inserted in the optical path and a retracted position to which it is retracted from the optical path. Movement of the movable mirror causes mutual switching between the printer mode optical path and the reader mode optical path.
problem: Switching between two distinct optical paths (reader mode and printer mode) in a single device without manual reconfiguration.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment of the mirror in both positions to avoid optical distortion or signal loss during switching.
mechanism: A repositionable optical element that physically shifts between two discrete positions to selectively block or unblock an optical path, enabling mode switching by altering the routing of light without manual reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A movable mirror positioned near the optical path that physically shifts between an inserted position (blocking one path) and a retracted position (allowing another path). This mechanical redirection enables mode switching by altering the optical routing.

abstract: An apparatus for the manufacture of perforated pita bread is disclosed. The apparatus includes a cylindrical roller having disposed on the surface thereof substantially circular blades with a sawtooth blade disposed along the diameter of each circular blade. The blades cut from a flattened sheet of pita dough traveling along the conveyor belt a plurality of perforated pita loaves having perforations therein for convenient tearing, which perforated pita loaves do not rupture during the baking process.
problem: Creating perforations in a fragile material (pita dough) that allow convenient tearing but do not cause structural failure during subsequent processing (baking).
constraint: Balancing the depth and spacing of perforations to ensure tearability without compromising the structural integrity of the dough during thermal expansion.
mechanism: A cutting element with a stress-distributing edge geometry that creates controlled discontinuities in a material while limiting crack propagation through a patterned edge profile, balancing localized failure with overall structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using circular blades with sawtooth edges arranged along their diameters on a rotating roller. The blade geometry cuts controlled perforations while the sawtooth pattern distributes stress to prevent crack propagation during baking.

abstract: The invention provides a full flow vaporizer for use in a refrigeration system employing hot gas from the compressor to periodically defrost the cooling coil, or coils where multiple coils are employed. The vaporizer usually consists of three concentric circular cross-section tubes forming a first inner passage, a concentric second annular passage, and a concentric third annular passage. The inner tube receives the fluid from the coil and has one end blocked. It is provided in its wall with a plurality of fine bores directing the fluid forcefully radially outwards under the action of the high velocity gas component of the fluid against the inner wall of the middle tube, which is heated by the hot gas that is passed through the third annular passage before being fed to the coil to perform the defrost function. The flow capacities of the passages and the bores are chosen to be in a specific range of flow capacities relative to one another, usually in the range 0.5 to 1.5, preferably in the range 0.9 to 1.2, so that when not in use the vaporizer has no appreciable effect on the remainder of the system. An orifice or restriction is provided at the outlet for the hot gas from the third annular passage and increases the back-pressure applied to the compressor by an amount of between 20% and 70%, preferably by between 40% and 60%, rendering the device self-balancing to prevent compressor motor overload.
problem: Defrosting cooling coils in a refrigeration system using hot gas without overloading the compressor or disrupting normal operation when the vaporizer is inactive.
constraint: Maintaining flow capacity ratios and back-pressure levels within narrow ranges to ensure the vaporizer has negligible impact on the system during non-defrost cycles.
mechanism: A multi-passage flow system with matched flow capacities and an outlet restriction that regulates back-pressure, enabling selective heating via a secondary flow path while maintaining system stability during non-active cycles.
mechanism_raw: Three concentric tubes with flow capacities matched to a specific range (0.5–1.5) create a self-balancing system. Hot gas flows through the outer annular passage, heating the middle tube, while an orifice at the outlet increases back-pressure to regulate compressor load.

abstract: A plastic clip to be tightened against a bolt comprises a base having a through hole to be penetrated vertically by the bolt, an upright post extending upright from the top of the base adjacent to the through hole, a cylindrical portion united to the outer end of the upright post and having a hole formed above and coaxial with the through hole in the base for receiving the bolt, a pair of flexible arms one extending in a curved fashion from each side of the upright post betwen the base and the cylindrical portion to slightly project with respect to the outer shape of the cylindrical portion and having a curved concave inner surface provided with a thread to be meshed with the male thread of the bolt, and a bifurcated pivotable member vertically rockably united via a reduced thickness hinge portion to the outer periphery of the cylindrical member, the bifurcated pivotable member serving to urge the pair of flexible arms sidewise against the bolt when rocked downwards.
problem: Creating a secure, tool-free fastening mechanism that can be tightened against a bolt while maintaining adjustability and grip.
constraint: Balancing the force applied by the pivotable member against the flexibility of the arms to ensure sufficient grip without over-tightening or structural failure.
mechanism: A pivoting element translates its motion into lateral displacement of flexible arms, which engage with a threaded surface to create a self-tightening grip through the interaction of the pivot's movement and the arms' flexibility.
mechanism_raw: A pivotable bifurcated member rocks downward, mechanically translating its motion into lateral displacement of flexible arms. The arms, equipped with threads, are urged against the bolt's male thread, creating a self-tightening grip through the interaction of the pivotable member's movement and the arms' flexibility.

abstract: An apparatus for pretreating and debarking logs wherein the log is debarked by a plurality of cutting elements disposed at an angle to the longitudinal extent of the log and offset with respect to each other. The cutting elements include top and bottom cutting elements between which the log is rolled, imparting helical slits thereto.
problem: Efficiently removing bark from logs while minimizing damage to the underlying wood.
constraint: Optimizing the angle and offset of the cutting elements to ensure effective helical slitting without excessive force that could damage the wood or reduce throughput.
mechanism: Cutting elements arranged at an angle and offset relative to the log's axis create helical slits as the log rotates between rollers, enabling controlled peeling through rotational motion and directional cutting forces.
mechanism_raw: Cutting elements angled and offset relative to the log's longitudinal axis are arranged between top and bottom rollers. As the log rolls between the cutters, the angled, offset configuration creates helical slits in the bark, enabling controlled peeling through rotational motion and directional cutting forces.

abstract: Novel 1-aryloxy-4-amino-2-butanols of the formula EQU ArO--CH.sub.2 --CHOH--CH.sub.2 --CH.sub.2 --NR.sup.1 R.sup.2 wherein Ar is 1-naphthyl, 2-naphthyl, indene-4(or 5-)yl, 3-(or 5-)chloro-2-pyridyl, phenyl, monosubstituted phenyl or di-substituted phenyl, R.sup.1 is lower alkyl, phenyl, phenylalkyl, 2-hydroxymethyl-2-propyl, adamantyl or lower-cycloalkyl, R.sup.2 is hydrogen or lower alkyl, wherein R.sup.1 and R.sup.2 together with the adjacent nitrogen from a heterocyclic residue and the pharmaceutically acceptable acid addition salts thereof having local anesthetic, beta-adrenergic blocking, antihypertensive and antiarrhythmic properties are disclosed. The compounds are prepared by reacting novel 1-aryloxy-4-chloro-2-butanols with amines. Methods for the preparation of the novel 1-aryloxy-4-chloro-2-butanol intermediates are also disclosed.
reason: The patent describes specific chemical compounds with defined molecular structures and their pharmaceutical applications. The mechanism is inherently tied to molecular interactions and chemical synthesis, lacking a generalizable functional principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: This invention relates to a process for preparing highly active hydrotreating catalysts prepared by incoporating an element selected from the group consisting of nickel, cobalt and mixtures thereof, a heavy metal selected from the group consisting of molybdenum, tungsten and mixtures thereof, and a stabilizing amount of phosphorus into an alumina hydrogel. The final calcined catalysts have surface areas at least about 300 m.sup.2 /g, at least about 20% of the pore volume in pores having diameters greater than about 350 .ANG. and at least about 20% of the pore volume in pores having diameters less than about 70 .ANG..
problem: Producing a hydrotreating catalyst with high activity and controlled pore structure to optimize catalytic reactions.
constraint: Balancing the concentrations of active metals and phosphorus to achieve the required surface area and pore volume distribution without compromising structural integrity or catalytic activity.
mechanism: Active components are incorporated into a matrix during synthesis, followed by a treatment to create a tailored surface area and bimodal pore distribution, enhancing catalytic efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating nickel/cobalt, molybdenum/tungsten, and phosphorus into an alumina hydrogel matrix during synthesis. The controlled incorporation and calcination process creates a catalyst with a tailored surface area and bimodal pore distribution (large pores for reactant access and small pores for active site density), enhancing catalytic efficiency.

abstract: The device, in a first embodiment, has utility for operation on a dual pulse missile including a booster segment for launching and includes several main components, as follows: an inertial mass, a shaft with a zig zag channel, a gearless electric motor, a switch deck and blocking rotor, another blocking rotor, and a spring which provides a restoring force which acts against the inertia of the inertial mass. In a second embodiment, the device has utility for operation on a triple pulse missile including a booster segment for launching and includes several main components, as follows: two inertial masses, a shaft with a unique zig zag channel, two gearless electric motors, two switch decks with blocking rotors, two springs which provide restorative forces which act against the inertia of the inertia masses. In each of the embodiments, the blocking rotors have notches which interface with the associated inertial mass or masses and lock the rotors against rotative movement unless the inertial masses are in the proper positions.
problem: Sequencing the activation of multiple pulse motors in a missile system with precise timing based on inertial forces.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment of inertial masses with the notches on the blocking rotors to maintain timing accuracy while accommodating the dynamic forces during missile operation.
mechanism: Inertial masses interact with a channel and rotors featuring notches, which mechanically gate the activation of motors based on mass positions, with springs providing restoring forces to reset the system after each pulse.
mechanism_raw: Inertial masses interact with a zig-zag channel shaft and blocking rotors featuring notches. The rotors lock or unlock based on the inertial masses' positions, mechanically gating the activation of gearless motors. Springs provide restoring forces to reset the system after each pulse, ensuring sequential operation through inertial and mechanical interlocks.

abstract: A composite article includes a compressively stressed plating which provides increased static strength and fatigue life. In particular, a fan exit guide vane (1), made of a graphite fiber reinforced composite material and including a conductive plating (7), achieves a 380% increase in static load capability over an unplated composite vane and a low cycle fatigue life of over 1 million cycles through the application of a compressively stressed nickel plating (8) which produces a residual compressive stress state of between -5,000 and -15,000 psi.
problem: Composite materials (e.g., graphite fiber reinforced composites) lack sufficient static strength and fatigue resistance under cyclic loading, leading to premature failure in high-stress applications like turbine components.
constraint: The plating must generate a residual compressive stress within a specific range (-5,000 to -15,000 psi) to balance strength enhancement without inducing delamination or other failure modes in the composite substrate.
mechanism: Applying a pre-stressed layer with inherent compressive forces to a substrate surface generates a residual compressive stress state. This stress counteracts operational tensile loads, delaying crack initiation and propagation to enhance static and fatigue performance.
mechanism_raw: Applying a compressively stressed plating (e.g., nickel) to the composite surface creates a residual compressive stress state in the material. This compressive stress counteracts tensile stresses during operation, delaying crack initiation and propagation, thereby increasing static load capacity and fatigue life.

abstract: A strand for reinforcing objects made of polymer material comprising at least one core wire and less than six outside wires arranged round it, the core wire having an outside diameter larger than the diameter of the circle tangent to each of the outside wires in the hollow space that remains free when their cross-sections have the highest packing density and smaller than the diameter of the outside wires, whereby the outside wires are made of carbon steel wire with a tensile strength of at least 2250-1130 log d N/mm.sup.2, d being the wire diameter in mm. The core wire has a tensile strength less than 2250-1130 log d N/mm.sup.2.
problem: Reinforcing strands for polymer materials require optimal load distribution between core and sheath wires to maximize tensile strength while maintaining flexibility and manufacturability.
constraint: The number of outside wires must be limited (less than six) to maintain the geometric relationship and prevent overcrowding, which would reduce the effectiveness of load distribution.
mechanism: A central element with a diameter intermediate between the spacing of surrounding elements creates controlled void geometry. Combined with differential strength properties, this geometry directs load transfer to the stronger surrounding elements while the central element maintains alignment and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A core wire with a larger diameter than the tangent circle of surrounding outside wires (but smaller than the outside wires themselves) creates a controlled void space. This geometry, combined with differential tensile strengths (core weaker than outside wires), ensures load transfer prioritizes the stronger outside wires while the core provides structural support and alignment.

abstract: A portable bullet trap device for catching bullets fired at the device comprising a box having a bottom, a top, and front, back, and opposing sides. The front has an opening for the passage of bullets fired at the device. A plurality of vertically oriented resilient panels are provided in the box aligned with the opening in the front. The panels are spaced from each other to form spaces between the central portions of the panels through which spent bullets can fall if they cannot penetrate the next successive panel. The panels may be provided as a replaceable cell having spacers between the marginal edges of the panels. Alternatively, the panels may be separately mounted in slots in the opposing sides of the box. A target means is provided to spread shots over the panels. This target means comprises at least two target sheets, each sheet adapted to be positioned over the forwardmost panel of the device and having at least one target thereon located over a different portion of the panel than the target on the other sheet when the sheets are positioned on the panels.
problem: Portable bullet traps need to safely arrest projectiles without requiring bulky or single-use materials, while allowing for maintenance and adaptability to varied shot patterns.
constraint: Panel spacing must balance projectile capture efficiency with the need for bullets to fall freely through gaps, while the resilient material must withstand repeated impacts without catastrophic failure.
mechanism: Spaced resilient barriers allow progressive energy dissipation as projectiles either embed in or pass through successive barriers. Replaceable segments enable localized maintenance, while distributed target surfaces spread wear across the system.
mechanism_raw: Vertically oriented resilient panels spaced apart allow bullets to pass through gaps if they fail to penetrate the next panel. Progressive energy absorption occurs as bullets either embed in or pass through successive panels, with replaceable cells enabling localized repair. Target sheets spread shots across panels to distribute wear.

abstract: Heavy metals and compounds thereof and other toxic materials in industrial wastes, sludges, soils, incinerated ashes and the like are fixed and stabilized in a char residue, obtained by critical region pyrolyzing techniques and appropriate proportions of carbonaceous materials intimately mixed with the sludge, to encapsulate the heavy metals with carbon bonded thereto which effectively detoxifies the residue and renders it immune to any substantial leaching out or later exposure to the toxic metals, such that the same is environmentally safe for such uses as landfill and the like.
problem: Toxic heavy metals in industrial waste pose environmental and health risks if leached into soil or groundwater during disposal or landfill use.
constraint: The pyrolysis process must occur in a controlled 'critical region' with precise temperature and carbon-to-waste ratios to ensure complete encapsulation without volatilizing toxic compounds.
mechanism: Controlled thermal decomposition of carbon-rich feedstock mixed with waste forms a stable matrix that chemically immobilizes contaminants. Precise process parameters ensure complete encapsulation without releasing volatile toxins.
mechanism_raw: Critical region pyrolysis of carbonaceous materials mixed with waste creates a char residue that chemically bonds heavy metals into a stable, encapsulated matrix. This carbon-metal bonding prevents leaching by immobilizing toxins within the char structure, rendering the residue environmentally safe.

abstract: A method and device for releasing defectively inserted weft threads in weaving machines by reversing the machine to expose the defectively inserted thread in the open shed, initially releasing the weft thread from the ends of the fell by moving the weft thread away from the fell at its ends, positioning releasing elements between the released portion of the weft thread and the fabric fell, releasing an additional portion of the weft thread from the fell by moving the releasing elements away from the fabric fell toward the machine reed, positioning an additional releasing element between the seft thread and the fabric fell, releasing an additional portion of weft thread from the fell by moving the additional releasing element away from the fell and toward the reed, and containing the positioning of the releasing elements across the shed of the weaving machine until the weft thread is released over the entire length of the shed.
problem: Defective weft threads in weaving machines disrupt fabric quality and require manual intervention, halting production and increasing downtime.
constraint: The releasing elements must be precisely coordinated to move in sequence from the fell toward the reed, ensuring uniform release without entangling adjacent threads or misaligning the fabric structure.
mechanism: Sequential actuation of release elements positioned between a defect and a reference point progressively frees the defect across an extended region. Staged movement avoids abrupt tension changes that could propagate damage to adjacent components.
mechanism_raw: Reversing the machine exposes the defective thread in the open shed. Sequential releasing elements are positioned between the thread and fabric fell, then moved toward the reed to progressively free the thread across the entire shed length. This staged release avoids abrupt tension changes that could damage the fabric or thread.

abstract: An improved process for tanning leather by treating animal skins with a water-soluble melamine-formaldehyde resin in the presence of an acid catalyst towards the end is improved by using a melamine-formaldehyde resin which is at least partially etherified with a glycol ether, alkyl glycol ether, or both.
problem: Improving the penetration and bonding of tanning agents into animal skins during leather processing.
constraint: Balancing the degree of etherification to maintain resin stability while achieving optimal interaction with the leather without excessive reactivity or solubility loss.
mechanism: Modifying a material's structural composition through partial chemical substitution to adjust solubility and reactivity under specific environmental conditions, enabling enhanced interaction with a substrate through deeper penetration and stronger adhesion.
mechanism_raw: Modifying the resin structure by partial etherification with glycol ethers to enhance solubility and reactivity under acidic conditions, enabling deeper penetration and stronger bonding with the substrate.

abstract: The weft threads (10) are clamped in weft thread hooks (12) supported on longitudinal conveyors (43, 44) extending perpendicular to and adjacent opposite ends of a row of knitting needles (42) by means of clamping slides (20) mounted on the longitudinal conveyors (43, 44). The clamping slides (20) are supported for sliding movement in a perpendicular direction relative to the movement of the longitudinal conveyors (43, 44) and are movable between an inactive, retracted position away from the hooks (12) through a placement zone (E) and an active position pressed against the hooks (12) and the weft threads (10) as the longitudinal conveyors (43, 44) move through a clamping zone (K) extending both upstream and downstream of the row of knitting needles (42).
problem: Precisely positioning and clamping weft threads in a knitting machine without interfering with the knitting needles.
constraint: Coordinating the timing and range of perpendicular sliding with conveyor movement to avoid mechanical interference while ensuring accurate thread placement and clamping.
mechanism: Decoupling placement and clamping actions by employing independent orthogonal motion systems, allowing separate control of positioning and force application to avoid mechanical interference while ensuring precise thread handling.
mechanism_raw: Using perpendicular sliding movements of clamping slides relative to longitudinal conveyors to decouple placement and clamping actions, allowing independent control of thread positioning and clamping force application.

abstract: An oxide bronze host material is a solid solution of a first oxide component comprising molybdenum oxide (MoO.sub.3), tungsten oxide (WO.sub.3), zirconium oxide (ZrO), niobium oxide (Nb.sub.2 O.sub.5) or any two or more thereof and a second oxide component comprising vanadium oxide (V.sub.2 O.sub.5) and/or titanium oxide (TiO.sub.2), the formula ratio of the first and second oxide components being selected such that the host material is capable of accepting guest atoms when incorporated in an electrochemical cell, said guest atoms altering the spectral characteristics of the host material without producing substantial visible color change in thin layers of the host material. Such a material may be used as a thin layer (12) in an electrochemical variable optical density window further including electrode layers (11, 15) on glass supports (10, 16) and an electrochromic oxide bronze layer (14) spaced from the layer (12) by an electrolyte layer (13a, 13b).
problem: Creating a material that reversibly alters spectral characteristics in electrochemical devices without visible color change in thin layers.
constraint: Selecting oxide ratios to balance guest atom acceptance capacity with structural stability and minimal visible color shift during ion insertion/extraction cycles.
