mechanism: Designing a composite material with a controlled solid solution of specific oxide components to enable reversible guest atom insertion that alters spectral properties while maintaining optical transparency through structural stability.
mechanism_raw: Designing a solid solution of specific oxide components (e.g., MoO3, WO3, ZrO, Nb2O5) with vanadium or titanium oxides to enable guest atom insertion that modifies spectral properties while maintaining optical transparency.
residual_terms: ["oxide components", "guest atom insertion", "vanadium or titanium oxides"]

abstract: A suction tube for a fly frame, roving frame, ring spinning machine or the like for collecting broken ends of yarn at the outlet rollers of the machine. The suction tube is connected to a collection chamber through a flexible sealing sleeve that permits the suction tube to pivot between its operative and inoperative positions. The suction tube comprises a suction end disposed under the bottom roller of the outlet rollers that has a body portion formed with a suction opening therein, an opposite end connected to the flexible sealing sleeve, and a pair of side walls projecting upwardly from the suction end body portion toward the bottom roller and longitudinally beyond the suction opening on opposite sides of the yarn for confining the suction substantially to the bottom roller and the yarn path. The side walls also have upper edges which are arcuately shaped to correspond approximately to the shape of the bottom roller so that the upper edges will contact the bottom roller and space the suction tube from the roller when the suction tube is unintentionally forced upwardly toward the bottom roller, thereby preventing damage to the suction tube.
problem: Protecting a suction tube from damage when unintentionally forced upward toward a rotating roller in a textile machine.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient suction confinement to the yarn path while ensuring the arcuate edges provide reliable spacing without compromising the tube's operative position.
mechanism: Incorporating shaped edge geometries on a suction element to create a physical spacing gap when in proximity to a moving surface, preventing direct contact and damage while maintaining functional confinement of the target medium.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating arcuately shaped upper edges on the suction tube that contact the roller to create a physical spacing gap, preventing direct contact and damage while maintaining suction effectiveness.

abstract: In the production of an article of extremely pure synthetic silicon dioxide, wherein silicon tetrachloride is mixed with water to effect hydrolysis, the resulting hydrolysis product is dried, and the resulting dried particulate product is further processed into the desired article, the improvement which comprises employing a ratio of silicon tetrachloride to water so that the hydrolysis product is in the form of a gel, distilling by-product hydrochloric acid out of the gel, preliminarily drying the gel at 100.degree. to 1000.degree. C. to produce an initial product, milling the initial product into a fine granulate at room temperature, separating from the milled granulate a fraction with a particle size of about 40 to 1000 .mu.m, and drying the screened-out granulate fraction while slowly heating to no more than 1400.degree. C. to form the resulting dried particulate product that is further processed into the desired article. As a result, high quality bubble free articles are produced.
problem: Producing high-quality, bubble-free synthetic silicon dioxide articles during hydrolysis and drying processes.
constraint: Balancing the rate of acid removal and temperature increases during drying to prevent bubble formation while achieving complete dehydration and structural integrity of the final product.
mechanism: Controlling phase transitions through precise reactant management, removing reaction by-products via selective separation, and applying staged thermal processing with gradient profiles to eliminate trapped gases and ensure uniform structural formation.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the hydrolysis-to-gel transition via precise reactant ratios, removing by-product acid via distillation, and applying staged drying with temperature gradients to eliminate trapped gases and ensure uniform particle formation.

abstract: A recording and readout information system having atomic scale densities comprises a recording medium having a carrier and means to form a pattern of atomic particles on the surface of the carrier. The atomic particles having an affinity for the carrier and can adhere to the surface to form a relatively adhesive and stable bond. The pattern of atomic particles produced on the carrier are representative of recorded information, e.g. binary represented information, of ultra high density based upon the size and spacing of such particles, which is in the range, for example, of 5 .ANG. (0.5 nm) to 10 .ANG. (1 nm). A preferred embodiment of the invention comprises a recording medium with an adsorbent carrier, means to form a pattern of adsorbate atomic particles on the surface of the adsorbent carrier, the adsorbate atomic particles having an adsorptive affinity for the adsorbent carrier. The adsorptive particles having an adsorptive affinity for the adsorbent carrier due, at least in part, to electrical attraction characteristics between the adsorbate atomic particles and the adsorbent carrier. Readout means, utilizing the tunnel current effect, is employed to determine the presence or absence of the atomic particles on the surface of the carrier and produce an electrical signal representative of the pattern of recorded information on the recording medium.
problem: Achieving ultra-high density data storage at atomic scales while maintaining stable and readable information patterns.
constraint: Particle size and spacing must remain within 5–10 Å (0.5–1 nm) to balance data density with physical stability and readout sensitivity.
mechanism: Using particles with affinity to adhere to a surface in a controlled pattern, enabling data encoding via presence/absence. Readout is performed via a detection method that senses the physical presence of particles at atomic resolution.
mechanism_raw: Using atomic-scale particles with electrical affinity to adhere to a carrier surface in a controlled pattern, enabling data encoding via particle presence/absence. Readout is performed via tunnel current detection, which senses the physical presence of particles at atomic resolution.

abstract: A method of manufacturing glass yarns includes the steps of: forming a large number of glass filaments by drawing molten glass through a large number of orifices formed on the bottom of a bushing; forming a plurality of strands by separately gathering the large number of glass filaments after a sizing agent has been applied thereto with a plurality of gathering rollers aligned in such a manner that they are separated from each other by a predetermined gap; winding the plurality of strands on one winding tube mounted on a collet while traversing the strands by one traverse motion thereby forming one cake; drawing out the ends of the plurality of strands from the outer periphery of the cake and rewinding the cake in the state wherein the strands are separated from each other by a rewinder after the cake has been air dried; and winding each of the strands as a glass yarn on a bobbin while twisting it. In this method, the gap between adjacent gathering rollers, the drawing speed, and the rotational speed and shape of the traverse motion are set such that they ensure that the plurality of strands which are wound on the winding tube so as to form the cake are separated from each other by 2 to 3 mm, and that the average length of the adhered portions of the strands which are formed by being passed through the turns of the traverse motion is between 150 and 350 mm, thereby solving the problems involving the generation of fluffs and breakage of filaments and enabling glass yarns of good quality to be manufactured efficiently.
problem: Preventing fluffs and filament breakage during high-speed manufacturing of glass yarns from molten glass.
constraint: Balancing roller gap, speed, and traverse motion parameters to avoid over-adhesion or insufficient separation, which would cause breakage or fluffs.
mechanism: Controlling the spacing between moving elements during a winding process by adjusting mechanical parameters to maintain precise separation, preventing entanglement and breakage through predictable adhesion patterns.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the gap between gathering rollers, drawing speed, and traverse motion to maintain precise separation (2–3 mm) between strands during winding. This ensures adhered portions of strands (150–350 mm) are formed predictably, reducing mechanical stress and entanglement.

abstract: A liquid/gas bypass line bypasses an expansion device of a refrigeration apparatus. An inlet of the bypass line is connected slightly above the bottom of a condenser so that it can pass either liquid refrigerant or vaporous refrigerant, depending on the level of liquid refrigerant in the condenser. The other end of the bypass line is connected to discharge into the evaporator, bypassing the expansion device. The bypass line functions as a conventional hot gas bypass during low load conditions when the level of liquid refrigerant is below the line's inlet. When the level rises above the inlet, often occurring when the condenser coolant temperature is low and the compressor is fully loaded, the bypass line returns excess accumulated liquid refrigerant to the evaporator. Maintaining the proper levels of liquid refrigerant in both the condenser and the evaporator not only provides the most effective use of their heat transfer surfaces, but also promotes the proper return of oil to the compressor.
problem: Maintaining optimal liquid refrigerant levels in both condenser and evaporator of a refrigeration system under varying load and coolant temperature conditions.
constraint: Inlet position must be calibrated relative to condenser liquid level to ensure correct fluid phase routing without disrupting normal refrigerant flow.
mechanism: A dynamic fluid routing system that adjusts between liquid and vapor phases based on system load and fluid levels to stabilize heat transfer surfaces and ensure proper fluid distribution.
mechanism_raw: A bypass line with an inlet positioned near the condenser bottom dynamically routes either liquid or vapor refrigerant to the evaporator. During low load, it acts as a hot gas bypass; during high liquid levels, it returns excess liquid to the evaporator, stabilizing heat transfer surfaces and oil return.

abstract: A method of preparing vegetables for marketing which involves the steps of: PA0 (a) vacuum conditioning of the comestible in its raw state in plastic pouches, i.e. a vacuum packing thereof; PA0 (b) a first pasteurization at a temperature ranging from above 85.degree. C. and up to 95.degree. C.; PA0 (c) a bacterial development or incubation treatment for a period of 24 to 27 hours at a temperature comprised between 25.degree. and 30.degree. C.; PA0 (d) a second pasteurization for 20 to 40 minutes at a temperature comprised between 85.degree. and 93.degree. C.; and PA0 (e) refrigeration of the packaged product. The method is especially applicable to fruits and vegetables which are sensitive to heat and, particularly, onions, leeks, garlic, shallots and the like.
problem: Preserving heat-sensitive produce (e.g., onions, garlic) while controlling microbial activity and maintaining shelf life.
constraint: Temperature and timing must be tightly controlled to avoid over-processing heat-sensitive produce while enabling desired microbial activity during incubation.
mechanism: A multi-stage thermal processing sequence that combines vacuum treatment, sequential heating steps, and controlled incubation to kill pathogens, enable beneficial microbial activity, and stabilize the product before storage.
mechanism_raw: A multi-stage process combining vacuum conditioning, two sequential pasteurization steps (85–95°C and 85–93°C), and a controlled incubation period (24–27 hours at 25–30°C). This sequence kills pathogens, allows beneficial bacterial development, and stabilizes the product before refrigeration.

abstract: A powderized material supply system comprises a plurality of reservoir tanks, each containing a different type of powder, and is associated with a metering means for metering the material into an individual supply line. Each individual supply line is associated with a carrier fluid source which supplies, carrier fluid at a controlled pressure for transferring the metered material with the carrier fluid. The individual material suppply lines, each associated with the corresponding reservoir tank, are connected to a post-mixing chamber into which the metered materials are introduced. The post-mixing chamber is connected to a mixture supply line. Each metering means can be controlled for metering a controlled amount of the material in its associated reservoir tank, independently of others. The powderized material supply system is applicable in various industrial or laboratory level processes which require supply of a plurality of powder state fluid material at a variable rate. The system is specifically applicable for flux injection in hot metal pre-treatment process in smelting process of metal industries. For example, the system is applicable for sequential operation or simultaneous operation for desiliconization, dephosphorization and/or desulfurization during hot metal pre-treatment.
problem: Supplying variable rates of multiple powdered materials simultaneously or sequentially in industrial processes (e.g., flux injection in metal smelting).
constraint: Each metering system must operate independently without cross-contamination, and carrier fluid pressure must be controlled to maintain consistent transport of all powders.
mechanism: A system for independently controlling the flow rate of multiple materials into a carrier fluid, followed by mixing to ensure homogeneous delivery while preventing cross-contamination between material streams.
mechanism_raw: Independent metering of each powder reservoir into a carrier fluid line, followed by post-mixing in a shared chamber. This allows precise, decoupled control of each material’s flow rate while ensuring homogeneous mixing before delivery to the process.

abstract: A comminuting machine for comminuting waste, recycleable material, ores, stones, coal and the like, comprises a rotor carrying comminuting tools and mounted for rotation about a horizontal axis in a housing. The housing has an inlet and at least one outlet region for discharging comminuted material. First and second layers are mounted for independent movement to the housing over the outlet region. One layer is provided with a grate for the passage of comminuted material. The other layer is provided with a plurality of punches which are insertable into openings through the grate for modifying or closing the openings.
problem: Controlling the size or flow rate of comminuted material discharged from a comminuting machine.
constraint: Balancing throughput efficiency with precise control over particle size or flow rate during operation.
mechanism: Two independently adjustable barriers with complementary apertures dynamically regulate the size or flow rate of discharged material by modulating the effective opening area in real time.
mechanism_raw: Two independently movable layers over the outlet: one with a grate and another with punches that dynamically adjust or close grate openings, enabling real-time modulation of material discharge characteristics.

abstract: A metal plate particularly of precious metal, for personalizing a bracelet, such as a metal watchband, formed by side-by-side rows of tubular links, comprising a plate member having two opposite edges from which two pairs of teeth extend inwardly and at least one tab perpendicular to the opposite edges. The teeth and the tab engage between adjacent links. Fastening means are provided for securing the plate member to the bracelet.
problem: Securing a decorative plate to a flexible bracelet without disrupting its structural integrity or flexibility.
constraint: Ensuring secure attachment without permanent modification or restriction of the bracelet's natural movement.
mechanism: Mechanical interlocking elements on the plate engage between adjacent flexible links, enabling reversible attachment while preserving the bracelet's natural flexibility and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical engagement via teeth and tabs on the plate that interlock between adjacent links of the bracelet, allowing reversible attachment while maintaining flexibility.

abstract: Tablets having a broad solubility profile containing a mixture of sodium metasilicate nonahydrate and anhydrous sodium metasilicate with a grain size of from 0.2 to 0.8 mm in a ratio by weight of from 1:0.75 to 1:1.2, anhydrous pentasodium triphosphate having a grain diameter of 0.2 to 0.3 mm, and 0.5 to 5% by weight of an active chlorine donor. The ratio by weight of pentasodium triphosphate to metasilicates is about 1:1 to 1:1.7, based on anhydrous substances. The tablets are used in automatic dishwashing machines where they are introduced into a free zone of the machine before the start of the prerinse cycle, at least 10% of the tablets being dissolved by inflowing cold water and at least another 70% being available in the main-wash cycle.
problem: Achieving staged dissolution of a detergent tablet across different phases of a dishwasher cycle (prerinse and main wash).
constraint: Optimizing chemical composition and particle size to ensure sufficient dissolution in cold prerinse water while retaining active ingredients for the main wash.
mechanism: A blend of hydrated and anhydrous compounds with controlled particle sizes and ratios, combined with a temperature-sensitive active agent, enables staged dissolution in cold and warm water phases by differential solubility.
mechanism_raw: A controlled mixture of hydrated and anhydrous sodium metasilicate with specific grain sizes and ratios, combined with an active chlorine donor, to enable differential dissolution rates in cold and warm water phases.

abstract: Composition (M) having a base of a cellulose ester having formate groups, this composition being an anisotropic solution containing: PA0 (a) the cellulose ester; PA0 (b) formic acid; PA0 (c) at least one phosphoric acid. A process for obtaining this composition by dissolving the cellulose and a process for obtaining articles by transformation of this composition, and, for example, regenerating the cellulose of these articles. A cellulose fiber is provided in which a degree of substitution of the cellulose by formate groups is either at least equal to 2% or is zero or less than 2%.
problem: Producing cellulose fibers with tailored solubility and mechanical properties through controlled chemical modification.
constraint: Balancing solubility in the solvent system with the structural integrity of the regenerated cellulose fiber during processing.
mechanism: An anisotropic solution of a cellulose derivative in a dual-acid solvent system, where the degree of substitution by specific functional groups modulates solubility and structural integrity during regeneration.
mechanism_raw: An anisotropic solution of cellulose ester with formic acid and phosphoric acid, where the degree of substitution by formate groups (either ≥2% or ≤2%) determines fiber regeneration behavior and material characteristics.

abstract: Shooter's hat comprising a crown portion and an integral bill and side blinder assembly, in which the bill is characterized as being short and wide, and the side blinders are rigid but bendable forms to suit the needs of the shooter. The side blinders are characterized by having forward and rearward relieved arcuate portions, the forward portion providing wider visible flight path and the rearward portion preventing side vision distractions and light blockage without interfering with facial anatomy. The side blinders also have a lower lobe approximately coordinate with the eye position, in a front-to-back orientation, that extends below the eye socket to approximately the level of the cheek bone. As compared to the long bill loose fabric flaps of the prior art, the hat provides necessary shielding from sun and distracting peripheral light or activities, yet does not unduly restrict the angle of vision of the target flight path. The prior art hat loose side flaps can blow in the wind and move with the motion of the shooter's head, thus causing distractions and blocking the vision, which are avoided by the construction of the invention.
problem: Shielding a shooter's eyes from distracting peripheral light or movement without obstructing the target flight path or facial anatomy.
constraint: Maintaining a wide forward field of view while minimizing side interference and ensuring compatibility with head movement and facial structure.
mechanism: A geometric shield with forward and rearward relieved arcuate portions and a lower lobe aligned with eye position blocks lateral distractions while preserving a wide forward field of view and compatibility with head movement.
mechanism_raw: Rigid yet bendable side blinders with forward and rearward relieved arcuate portions and a lower lobe aligned with eye position, creating a geometric shield that blocks lateral distractions while preserving forward visibility.

abstract: A method, apparatus and system for use in drying particulate matter employing a drier comprising a cylindrical upper section, a frustoconical lower section, a rotatable shaft extending substantially the entire length of the interior of the drier, a plurality of axially spaced arrays of circumferentially spaced, radially extending stirring arms appended to the shaft, and at least two perforated frustoconical separators mounted within the drier in fixed, inverse and spaced apart relation to each other, and means for introducing a heated gas into the drier for contacting and drying the particulate matter, the stirring arms and separators cooperating to retard agglomeration of the particulate matter.
problem: Preventing agglomeration of particulate matter during drying in a cylindrical dryer.
constraint: Balancing agitation intensity and separator spacing to avoid over-processing or structural damage to particles while ensuring uniform drying.
mechanism: Intermittent mechanical disruption and controlled particle transport through a confined path, where agitation elements periodically disturb accumulated material while spaced barriers regulate particle flow to prevent re-agglomeration.
mechanism_raw: Cooperation between axially spaced stirring arms and perforated separators to continuously agitate and separate particles, disrupting clumping while maintaining controlled particle movement through the dryer.

abstract: Batter coated, pre-fried microwaveable foodstuffs characterized by improved freeze/thaw stability are provided by employing as a dry predust, prior to batter application, a composition comprising greater than 20%, by weight, of an hydroxypropylmethyl cellulose ether having a methoxyl content greater than 22% and an hydroxypropyl content of at least 5%, by weight.
problem: Maintaining structural integrity of batter-coated foodstuffs during freeze/thaw cycles without compromising microwaveability.
constraint: Optimizing polymer composition (methoxyl >22%, hydroxypropyl ≥5%) to achieve freeze/thaw stability without interfering with batter adhesion or microwave heating efficiency.
mechanism: A moisture-retaining barrier formed by a polymer matrix with specific compositional thresholds, creating a stable interface that resists phase transitions during temperature cycling while maintaining surface adhesion and energy coupling.
mechanism_raw: Using a hydroxypropylmethyl cellulose ether predust with specific methoxyl and hydroxypropyl content to form a stable, moisture-retaining barrier that resists phase changes during freezing and thawing.

abstract: A pressure vessel assembly includes a pressure vessel with a vessel wall having a connection stub with a stub wall. A thermal protector for the connection stub in the form of a first tube extends substantially parallel to the stub wall. The first tube has an inner surface, one end disposed at the stub wall and another free end extending into the pressure vessel. Brackets are disposed on the inner surface of the tube between the other free end and the stub wall. A second tube extends into the connection stub beyond the one end of the first tube. The second tube has slits formed therein defining prongs therebetween connected to the brackets.
problem: Protecting a pressure vessel's connection stub from thermal stress and mechanical deformation under high-pressure conditions.
constraint: Designing the tube geometry and bracket/prong connections to accommodate thermal expansion without compromising pressure sealing or structural integrity.
mechanism: A dual-element load management system where a first compliant structure absorbs differential thermal displacement and a second load-bearing structure transfers mechanical forces while permitting controlled relative motion between connected components.
mechanism_raw: A dual-tube thermal protector system where a first tube with brackets absorbs thermal expansion and a second tube with slits and prongs transfers mechanical loads while allowing controlled movement between the stub and vessel wall.

abstract: A curbing module having interconnected sections as provided by body members interconnectable to provide a row of sections of curbing. The body members are preferably cast, and have embedded within each body member a generally U-shaped retainer member extending longitudinally and outwardly of each of the body members. Each end of the retainer member of one body member co-operates with a recess of the adjacent body member, providing, also with an associated stake-pin, the functions of both hold-down and alignment, providing and assuring a continuously attractive straightness and orderliness of the curbing as composed by a plurality of such sections.
problem: Creating a modular curbing system that maintains straightness and alignment across interconnected sections without external fasteners.
constraint: Ensuring retainer geometry and stake-pin placement provide sufficient hold-down force and alignment precision while allowing easy modular assembly and disassembly.
mechanism: Self-aligning mechanical interlocks with integrated retention features, where geometric constraints in mating components simultaneously enforce positional accuracy and secure engagement during modular assembly without external fastening.
mechanism_raw: Embedding U-shaped retainers with stake-pins and recesses in cast body members, enabling self-aligning interlocks that simultaneously secure and position adjacent sections during assembly.

abstract: A data display system in which input-output display devices are connected to a central processor, and users select application programs that are run on the central processor. The control system of the central processor includes a display manager control system and a windowing control mechanism which allows a plurality of tasks to be performed concurrently and the results displayed in areas of a display screen. The windowing control mechanism includes, a task manager control program which runs as an application in the display manager control system and includes means to interact, via the display manager, with the operator to allow applications to be initiated, means to create tasks to control the processing of the application in such a way that the applications can be suspended or resumed according to whether the operator is ready for them, and means to identify to the display manager a coordination controller that the display manager can call to allow the task manager to suspend and resume applications. The display manager includes, means to combine data from each application and build a display representation that shows many windows into the various applications onto a single screen, and means to call the coordination controller identified by the task management application so that the task manager can suspend applications that are waiting for input and resume those applications which have input available.
problem: Managing concurrent execution of multiple application tasks and dynamically displaying their outputs on a single screen in a centralized processor system.
constraint: Balancing task suspension/resumption timing with display rendering to prevent input starvation or screen overcrowding while maintaining responsive user interaction.
mechanism: Coordinated task scheduling and output multiplexing, where a control layer dynamically suspends/resumes concurrent processes based on readiness signals while a rendering layer partitions active outputs into distinct visual regions under shared display arbitration.
mechanism_raw: A task manager control program that suspends/resumes applications based on operator readiness, coordinated with a display manager that combines data from active tasks into separate windows via a coordination controller.

abstract: A movable rip fence is adapted for installation on the work table having a planar surface with a pair of rails on opposite sides that are provided with a series of evenly spaced apart holes, and with a cutting tool between the rails that extends above the table surface. The fence comprises an elongated main frame unit that extends between the rails including movable pins at opposite ends for holding the main frame unit generally perpendicular to both rails. A first control device on the main frame which enables the pins to be inserted and retracted into and out from a preselected pair of holes in the rails to first hold the main frame firmly in a predetermined fixed position and thereafter release it for movement to another position. An elongated guide member having an outer planar surface is positioned adjacent and parallel to the main frame and is yieldably attached to it. A second control device is provided for moving the guide member laterally relative to said main frame in a precise manner so as to position its outer planar surface a desired distance from the cutting tool on the rack table. A storage rack is provided at one end of the table to receive and retain the rip fence when it is not in use.
problem: Accurately and repeatably positioning a movable fence relative to a cutting tool on a work table while allowing quick repositioning.
constraint: Balancing rapid coarse repositioning with high-precision fine adjustment, while maintaining structural rigidity during cutting operations.
mechanism: A dual-mode positioning system: first, discrete mechanical engagement elements rigidly fix a component in a coarse position by interfacing with predefined positional references; second, a resiliently coupled adjustment element enables precise fine-tuning of the component's spatial relationship to a reference point. This separates gross positioning (via mechanical engagement) from precision adjustment (via resilient coupling), maintaining rigidity during operation while allowing rapid reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage positioning system: first, a pair of movable pins engage preselected holes in rails to rigidly fix the fence in a coarse position; second, a laterally adjustable guide member, yieldably attached to the main frame, allows precise fine-tuning of the fence's distance from the cutting tool. This decouples gross positioning (via pins) from precision adjustment (via the guide member).
residual_terms: ["mechanical engagement elements", "predefined positional references", "resiliently coupled adjustment element"]

abstract: A method of recycling a portion of the overhead vapor stream to enhance ethane recovery from a demethanizer. After the overhead vapor stream is discharged from the demethanizer, a portion of it, reflux, is compressed in a cyrogenic compressor to a pressure greater than that of the demethanizer. Afterwards the pressurized reflux is chilled in a heat exchanger causing at least a portion of it, and preferably all of it, to condense to a liquid. The pressure of this condensed reflux is then equalized to that of the demethanizer across a recycle valve so that a liquid reflux can be fed back to the top of the demethanizer. This recycling of a liquid reflux enhances ethane recovery as a column bottoms product from the demethanizer.
problem: Enhancing ethane recovery from a demethanizer by optimizing the reflux stream's properties before recycling.
constraint: Managing compression, cooling, and pressure equalization steps to ensure the reflux is in the correct phase and pressure for effective reintroduction without destabilizing the column.
mechanism: A multi-stage reflux optimization process: first, a vapor stream is pressurized beyond a separation column's operating pressure; second, the pressurized stream undergoes controlled cooling to induce phase transition into a liquid phase; third, the condensed liquid is pressure-matched to the column via regulated flow control before reintroduction. This leverages pressure differentials and phase-change thermodynamics to enhance separation efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A portion of the overhead vapor is compressed to a pressure exceeding the demethanizer, then chilled to induce full or partial condensation into a liquid reflux. The condensed reflux is pressure-equalized to the demethanizer via a recycle valve, enabling liquid-phase reintroduction to the column top. This leverages phase change and pressure management to improve separation efficiency.

abstract: A projector type headlight is disclosed, which comprises a concave reflector having first and second focuses on an optical axis thereof; a light source located on or at least near the first focus of the concave reflector; a shade plate positioned in front of the concave reflector, the shade plate having an upper edge located in the vicinity of the second focus of the concave reflector; and a converging lens located in front of the shade plate in such a manner that a focus of the lens is positioned on the upper edge of the shade plate, wherein the optical axis of the concave reflector is inclined with respect to an optical axis of the converging lens.
problem: Controlling the shape and direction of a projected light beam to achieve a desired illumination pattern (e.g., cutoff line for automotive headlights).
constraint: Precisely aligning the shade plate, reflector, and lens focal points while maintaining the angular relationship between optical axes to achieve the desired beam pattern.
mechanism: An optical beam sculpting system: an occluding element is positioned at a first focal region of a reflective concentrator, with its edge aligned to a focal point of a downstream refractive element. The optical axes of the concentrator and refractive element are angularly offset, causing the occluding element's edge to cast a sharp shadow that defines a beam boundary. This uses dual focal-point alignment and axis misalignment to control light distribution.
mechanism_raw: A shade plate is positioned at the second focus of a concave reflector, with its upper edge aligned to the focal point of a downstream converging lens. The optical axes of the reflector and lens are inclined relative to each other, causing the shade's edge to cast a sharp shadow that defines the beam cutoff. This uses dual focal-point alignment and axis inclination to sculpt the light distribution.

abstract: A catalytically dewaxed lubricating oil of improved oxidation stability is produced by catalytically dewaxing and hydrotreating the dewaxed product with a hydrotreating catalyst which has been oxidatively regenerated. The use of oxidative regeneration provides a hydrotreating catalyst which effectively sorbs aromatic components, especially the polycyclic aromatic liquids formed during the hydrogen activation of the dewaxing catalyst which pass out of the dewaxing reactor during the initial stages of each dewaxing cycle.
problem: Improving oxidation stability of catalytically dewaxed lubricating oils by removing polycyclic aromatic contaminants formed during dewaxing.
constraint: Balancing oxidative regeneration conditions to maximize sorption capacity without deactivating the catalyst or introducing new contaminants.
mechanism: A cyclic sorbent regeneration and contaminant removal process: a sorbent material undergoes periodic oxidative treatment to restore its adsorption capacity; during each processing cycle, the regenerated sorbent selectively captures polycyclic aromatic compounds that would otherwise degrade product stability. This couples regenerative capacity restoration with in-cycle contaminant sequestration to improve output quality.
mechanism_raw: Oxidative regeneration of the hydrotreating catalyst enhances its sorptive capacity for aromatic components. During each dewaxing cycle, the regenerated catalyst effectively adsorbs polycyclic aromatics that would otherwise degrade oxidation stability, thereby purifying the oil product.

abstract: The invention comprises a method and apparatus for recovering oil from so-called depleted oil fields and also from tar sands. A pressurized, heated, non-aqueous gas, such as carbon dioxide, is continuously flowed through a channel which is in heat exchange relationship with an oil-bearing matrix, thus reducing the viscosity and mobilizing the oil in the sensible boundary region. Mobilized oil flows to a collection reservoir from which it is then produced.
problem: Mobilizing and recovering oil from low-permeability or depleted reservoirs and tar sands where conventional methods are ineffective.
constraint: Maintaining optimal gas pressure and temperature to ensure effective viscosity reduction and mobilization without causing reservoir damage or excessive energy consumption.
mechanism: A combined thermal-pressure mobilization system: a pressurized, heated non-aqueous fluid flows through a defined flow path in thermal contact with a hydrocarbon-bearing medium. The fluid transfers thermal energy to reduce hydrocarbon viscosity while pressure differentials drive displacement of mobilized hydrocarbons toward a collection point. This integrates viscosity reduction via heat transfer with pressure-driven flow to overcome permeability constraints.
mechanism_raw: A pressurized, heated non-aqueous gas (e.g., CO₂) is continuously flowed through a channel in heat-exchange contact with the oil-bearing matrix. The gas reduces oil viscosity via thermal energy transfer and pressure-driven displacement, mobilizing oil toward a collection reservoir. This combines thermal viscosity reduction with gas-driven flow to overcome permeability limitations.

abstract: A new weft yarn is supplied to a predetermined position in case when the weft yarn in a control unit, particularly in a loom, is broken. Conventionally, the supply of the new weft yarn is effected by a weaver. The present invention provides a yarn guide device for positioning, holding, and transferring a yarn to a predetermined position. The yarn in then drawn inside of a guide tube located in a predetermined position, and thereafter the yarn is automatically guided to a required device such as a measuring and storing device for the weft yarn.
problem: Automatically supplying a new weft yarn to a predetermined position in a loom when the existing yarn breaks, eliminating manual intervention by a weaver.
constraint: The mechanism must balance precise positioning of the yarn within the guide tube and seamless transfer to downstream equipment while operating in the dynamic environment of a loom.
mechanism: Automatically detect a material break, draw in a replacement material through a fixed-position guide, and precisely direct it to a receiving unit via internal guidance, ensuring seamless transfer without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: A yarn guide device uses a guide tube positioned at a fixed location to draw in the new yarn, then automatically directs it to a downstream device (e.g., measuring/storing unit) via controlled internal guidance, ensuring precise positioning and transfer without human involvement.

abstract: This invention relates to a container for feeding a bar shaped article such as an erasing gum, a pencil lead, a crayon, a pastel, or an eyebrow stick, especially for advancing or retracting the bar shaped article. A bar shaped article (8) is inserted into an inner sleeve (2) from the rear end with the outer sleeve (1) being held by the hand, then the rear end of the inner sleeve (2) is pressed. Inner sleeve (2) moves forward and rearward against the resilient force of an elastic biasing member (3). A chuck (4) at the end of the inner sleeve (2) opens and closes repeatedly and the end of the bar shaped article (8) is fed out and can be used. When the chuck (4) holds the bar shaped article (8) in an unused state a chuck open means opens the chuck 4 slightly and loosens the securing force preventing encroachment of the chuck (4) into the article (8) allowing the chuck (4) to easily separate from the article (8) when the article (8) is fed out. Therefore feeding of the article (8) is performed accurately and smoothly.
problem: Accurately and smoothly advancing or retracting a bar-shaped article (e.g., pencil lead) while preventing damage to the article during feeding.
constraint: The system must maintain sufficient gripping force to advance the article while allowing controlled release to avoid deformation or jamming during operation.
mechanism: A gripping mechanism with a spring-biased actuator that moves axially, where a chuck opens and closes via mechanical interaction with the article. A release mechanism slightly disengages the chuck when idle to reduce friction and prevent jamming during feeding.
mechanism_raw: An inner sleeve with a chuck moves axially against a spring's resilient force. The chuck opens and closes via mechanical interaction with the article, and a 'chuck open means' slightly releases the article when idle, reducing friction and preventing encroachment during feeding.

abstract: Fiberboard shims are manufactured which contain blocked isocyanates. The blocked isocyanates are blended with the other shim components to ensure complete distribution of the isocyanate into the shim, thereby improving the strength characteristics of the shim while simultaneously simplifying the manufacturing procedure. Further, the need for hazardous solvent-based isocyanates in the workplace is eliminated.
reason: The patent describes a material composition (blending blocked isocyanates into fiberboard shims) rather than a functional or mechanical mechanism. While it solves a problem (strength and safety), the solution is a chemical/material formulation, not a transferable causal operation.

abstract: The invention relates to a device for heating billets, strip or sheet-metal, the device including one or more inductive edge heaters to heat the edges of a billet on its way from a continous casting machine, or strip or sheet-metal coming from a hot-rolling mill, arranged to surround the outer parts of the edges in order to heat them. The induction heater(s) comprises(s) one or more flat spiral element(s) (1) bent around the side edges of the billet, etc, and also at least one vertically placed, flat coil (4), located substantially parallel with the side edge (5) of the billet, etc.
problem: Heating the edges of metal billets, strip, or sheet-metal (e.g., from continuous casting or hot-rolling) to a desired temperature without overheating the entire workpiece.
constraint: The coil arrangement must ensure uniform edge heating while minimizing energy waste and avoiding unintended heating of adjacent areas.
mechanism: Localized electromagnetic induction heating using shaped conductive elements arranged to create targeted heating zones that focus energy on specific edge regions of a workpiece.
mechanism_raw: Inductive edge heaters use flat spiral elements bent around the edges and vertically placed flat coils positioned parallel to the edges, creating localized electromagnetic heating zones that target only the outer edge regions.

abstract: A separable bottom end stop includes first and second end stop members mounted on respective stringer tapes of a slide fastener at lowermost ends of the rows of coupling elements. The first end stop member has a first finger on an end thereof and a tooth remote from the first finger, and the second end stop member has a second finger on an end thereof for interfitting engagement with the first finger and an elastic wall remote from the second finger and positioned for being elastically deformable by pressed engagement with the tooth. The first and second end stop members having a combined width normally greater than the smallest distance between flanges of a slider to be mounted on the rows of coupling elements. When the elastic wall is elastically deformed by pressed engagement with the tooth at the time the end stop members are forcibly passed through the slider between the flanges, the combined width is reduced to an extent smaller than the smallest distance between the slider flanges.
problem: Creating a separable end stop for a slide fastener that can be passed through a slider during installation but then securely locks in place to prevent slider displacement.
constraint: The elastic deformation must be sufficient to allow passage through the slider while maintaining enough restoring force to ensure a secure lock after installation.
mechanism: A locking mechanism with two interlocking members connected by an elastic wall. When compressed, the elastic wall deforms to reduce the combined width, allowing passage through a slider. Upon release, the elastic wall restores, increasing the width to lock the members in place.
mechanism_raw: Two end stop members with interlocking fingers and an elastic wall are designed so that when pressed through the slider, the elastic wall deforms, temporarily reducing the combined width below the slider's flange gap. Once released, the elastic wall returns to its original shape, increasing the width to lock the stop in place.

abstract: A drive for a pilger cold-rolling mill with mass and torque balancing, where the driven crank, rotating around a vertical axis, is connected via a coupler with a roller frame guided horizontally in a guide and where the coupler assumes, with its total mass, the balancing of momentum and where the crank, with its total mass, assumes the mass balancing. An additional mass M.sub.z, which is movable synchronously and parallel to the roller frame and where the center of gravity (S.sub.M) is lower than the virtual engagement point (S.sub.AG) of the centrifugal force of the crank balancing mass (MA), where the product of the force of inertia for accelerating the mass (M.sub.z) and of the vertical distance (b) between the center of gravity (S.sub.M) and of the mass (M.sub.z) and the engagement point (S.sub.AG) of the centrifugal force of the mass (MA) corresponds to the balancing mass moment obtained as a product of the force of inertia engaging at the center of gravity (S.sub.AG) at the roller frame and its vertical distance (a) to the point of engagement (S.sub.AG) of the centrifugal force for improving conventional drives such that the mass moment or moment of inertia is balanced.
problem: Dynamic vibration and unbalanced moments in a rotating/reciprocating mechanical drive system (pilger mill) caused by the centrifugal forces of the crank balancing mass and the inertial forces of the moving roller frame.
constraint: The compensating mass must move synchronously and parallel to the roller frame, and its center of gravity must be positioned at a specific vertical distance relative to the crank's centrifugal force engagement point such that the product of its inertial force and vertical offset equals the unbalanced mass moment of the crank. The geometric relationship (vertical distances a and b) must be precisely maintained to achieve moment balance.
mechanism: A compensating mass is moved synchronously and parallel to a driven component, positioned so that its center of gravity is vertically offset relative to the virtual engagement point of a rotating component's centrifugal force. The inertial force of this compensating mass, multiplied by its vertical distance to the rotating component's centrifugal force engagement point, generates a counter-moment that exactly cancels the unbalanced moment produced by the rotating component's centrifugal force acting on the driven component. This creates a net zero dynamic moment without requiring the compensating mass to counteract the full inertial force directly.
mechanism_raw: A compensating mass (Mz) is moved synchronously and parallel to the roller frame, positioned so that its center of gravity is vertically offset below the virtual engagement point of the crank's centrifugal force. The inertial force of this compensating mass, multiplied by its vertical distance to the crank's centrifugal force engagement point, generates a counter-moment that exactly cancels the unbalanced moment produced by the crank's centrifugal force acting on the roller frame. This creates a net zero dynamic moment without requiring the compensating mass to counteract the full inertial force directly.
residual_terms: ["inertial force", "centrifugal force", "center of gravity", "moment balance", "vertical offset", "synchronous movement", "counter-moment", "unbalanced moment"]

abstract: A pixel preheat system for a thermal transfer device in which a selected image is transferred from a strip of color carrying ribbon to a strip of image carrying tape achieves precise control of the temperature of the individual pixel heating elements in a thermal printhead by combining the pixel data values just printed with the pixel data values to be printed to generate a pixel preheat value whenever either of the pixel data values is off or white. The present invention maintains the temperature of the individual pixel heating elements closer to the transition temperature of the thermal transfer ribbon and uses fewer circuit components.
problem: Maintaining precise temperature control of individual pixel heating elements in a thermal transfer device while minimizing circuit complexity.
constraint: Achieving temperature precision with fewer circuit components by leveraging temporal pixel data correlation.
mechanism: Use temporal correlation of data from adjacent cycles to predict a target parameter, adjusting a system's output closer to a threshold by dynamically modifying actuation based on prior and subsequent state information.
mechanism_raw: Combining pixel data values from adjacent print cycles (just-printed and to-be-printed) to generate a predictive preheat value, dynamically adjusting heating element temperatures closer to the thermal ribbon's transition temperature.

abstract: A remote monitoring and controlling system in which time information from a secondary clock in each slave station is transmitted in coded signal form to a master station in response to a time inquiry command issued from the master station. The transmitted time information and the time information of the primary clock of the master station are compared in the master station by taking into account the length of the coded signal and a transmission delay time from the corresponding slave station. The difference found by the comparison is temporarily stored in memory as time correction data to be used to correct the time information of the respective slave stations.
problem: Synchronizing time information across distributed slave stations with a master clock despite variable transmission delays.
constraint: Balancing accuracy of time correction against variability in transmission delay and signal encoding length.
mechanism: Transmit coded signals from distributed stations to a reference clock, compare them with the reference while accounting for signal length and transmission delay, then store correction data for iterative synchronization to reduce temporal drift.
mechanism_raw: Transmitting coded time signals from slave stations to a master, comparing them with the master clock while accounting for signal length and transmission delay, then storing correction data for iterative synchronization.

abstract: An oil-in-water type emulsified fat composition which contains cheese and shows stable emulsification can be prepared by adding 0.1 to 5% by weight, based on the fat, of monoacyl glycero phospholipid(s) as at least an emulsifier component and 0.5 to 5% by weight, based on the cheese, of molten salt(s) in the emulsification of cheese, fat and water.
reason: The mechanism is specific to food chemistry (emulsifier ratios for cheese-based compositions) and does not describe a generalizable causal operation beyond material formulation.

abstract: A thermal recording head includes heating elements which are provided in one array on the front surface of a base plate, and a radiating plate which is fixed to the rear surface of the base plate. The radiating plate has a thickness 1 satisfying 1.gtoreq.2d where d denotes the diameters of mounting holes formed in the radiating plate, some of the mounting holes are disposed at predetermined intervals at positions substantially corresponding to the heating element array, and the spacing 1.sub.2 between the base plate and the bottom of each of the mounting holes satisfies 1.sub.2 .gtoreq.d.
problem: Managing heat dissipation and structural integrity in a thermal recording head with an array of heating elements.
constraint: Geometric trade-off between minimizing thermal resistance and maintaining structural support through hole placement and plate thickness.
mechanism: Design a heat-dissipating structure with geometric constraints on thickness and hole spacing relative to hole diameters to balance thermal conductivity and mechanical stability, ensuring structural integrity while minimizing thermal resistance.
mechanism_raw: Designing a radiating plate with thickness and mounting hole spacing constrained relative to hole diameters (1 ≥ 2d, spacing ≥ d) to balance thermal conductivity and mechanical stability.
residual_terms: ["radiating plate", "mounting hole spacing", "hole diameters", "thermal conductivity", "mechanical stability"]

abstract: When molded plates of aluminum nitride obtained by molding a ceramic powder formed preponderantly of aluminum nitride powder are superposed on a support base with a ceramic powder interposed between the support base and the superposed plates and between the superposed plates and are fired in a non-oxidative atmosphere, the sintered plates consequently produced are prevented from sustaining crack or fracture. When warped and undulated sintered plates of aluminum nitride are superposed on a support base with a ceramic powder interposed between the support base and the superposed plates and between the superposed plates and are heated in a non-oxidative atmosphere, the heated plates are relieved of warp and undulation. The sintered plates of aluminum nitride are enabled to acquire improved adhesiveness to a metal film or foil when they are subjected to a heat treatment adapted to reduce the surface roughness to or below 10 .mu.m (Rmax).
problem: Preventing cracks and warpage in sintered aluminum nitride plates during high-temperature processing.
constraint: Balancing stress relief via sacrificial interlayers against the need for precise dimensional control during sintering.
mechanism: Interpose sacrificial powder layers between stacked components and a support base during high-temperature processing in a controlled atmosphere, allowing controlled movement to relieve internal stresses and surface roughness through stress redistribution.
mechanism_raw: Interposing ceramic powder layers between stacked plates and a support base during firing in a non-oxidative atmosphere, allowing controlled movement to relieve internal stresses and surface roughness.

abstract: An amplifier arrangement with controllable gain comprising two differential amplifiers which are connected in parallel at their inputs and outputs and which have different gain factors which can be varied oppositely. The gain of one of said differential amplifiers is reduced in that a first resistor is connected between its input terminals and a second resistor is connected between at least one of said input terminals and the corresponding input terminal of the other differential amplifier. As a result, the input signal to this amplifier is subject to a voltage division enabling the input swing to be increased.
problem: Limited input signal swing range in a controllable-gain amplifier, where the input signal amplitude is constrained by the amplifier's voltage headroom, preventing larger input signals from being processed without distortion.
constraint: The two amplifiers must have gains that vary in opposition (one increases as the other decreases), and the resistor values must be chosen to create the desired voltage division ratio without degrading the gain control range or introducing excessive noise or offset errors.
mechanism: Two differential amplifiers are connected in parallel at both inputs and outputs, with their gain factors varied in opposition. A resistor network is inserted at the input of one amplifier: a first resistor across its input terminals and a second resistor between one input terminal and the corresponding input of the other amplifier. This creates a voltage division at the input of the first amplifier, effectively attenuating the signal seen by that amplifier while the parallel amplifier sees the full signal. The opposing gain variation compensates for the attenuation, maintaining overall gain control while increasing the effective input swing range.
mechanism_raw: Two differential amplifiers are connected in parallel at both inputs and outputs, with their gain factors varied in opposition. A resistor network is inserted at the input of one amplifier: a first resistor across its input terminals and a second resistor between one input terminal and the corresponding input of the other amplifier. This creates a voltage division at the input of the first amplifier, effectively attenuating the signal seen by that amplifier while the parallel amplifier sees the full signal. The opposing gain variation compensates for the attenuation, maintaining overall gain control while increasing the effective input swing range.
residual_terms: ["differential amplifier", "gain factor", "voltage division", "resistor network", "input swing range", "voltage headroom", "attenuation", "opposing gain variation"]

abstract: A combination paint roller wiper and paintbrush holder comprises a wiping surface with a plurality of hooks to hang the wiping surface in a paint bucket. The wiping surface is connected to a projection that engages the wall of the bucket when a paint roller is wiped on the wiping surface. The combination also includes a support structure for a paintbrush or the like that is attached to the wiping structure on the side opposite from the wiping surface. The support structure may be attached permanently to the wiping portion, or it may be made removable. The bottom portion of the paintbrush holder is made of a solid material with drain holes to support a standing paintbrush without damage to the bristles. The paintbrush holder also has a perforated front wall, perforated side walls and a perforated rear wall.
reason: This patent describes a combined paint roller wiper and paintbrush holder tool. It is a product combining two existing functions (roller wiping and brush holding) into a single device with hooks, a wiping surface, and a perforated brush support. There is no underlying causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through a functional relationship; it is merely a physical combination of features (hooks for hanging, perforations for drainage, a projection for bucket wall engagement) without a deeper problem-solving principle that transfers to other fields.

abstract: An abrasion and fine resistant permanent press fabric or fabric structure comprising a batting or yarn consisting of an intimate blend of oxidized polyacrylonitrile and at least two fibers selected from the group consisting of polyvinyl halide, polybenzimidazole, p-aramid, m-aramid, fire resistant polyester and fire resistant rayon, said oxidized polyacrylonitrile comprising about 25 to 85% by weight of said yarn and p-aramid comprises less than 35% by weight of said yarn or batting.
reason: This patent describes a specific materials composition—a blend of oxidized polyacrylonitrile with other fire-resistant fibers in specific weight percentages. While the combination of fibers may produce desirable properties, the patent does not describe a causal functional mechanism that produces an effect through a dynamic relationship. It is a static materials recipe specifying component percentages rather than a mechanism explaining how the components interact to solve a problem. The underlying principle of blending materials for combined properties is too generic and well-known to constitute a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: An electric furnace includes a furnace vessel covered by a furnace lid liftable and lowerable by a lid lifting mechanism and pivotable from a position above the furnace vessel into a position lateral of the furnace vessel and back by a lid pivoting mechanism. A lid supporting framework is pivotably mounted lateral of the furnace vessel and includes at least one lid bracket extending over the furnace vessel for lifting, lowering and pivoting the furnace lid. In order to be able to pivot the lid bracket without furnace lid and without necessitating manipulations to be carried out at the furnace lid for the purpose of exchanging the lid or the lid core, the lid bracket is detachably connected to the furnace lid by at least one coupling means, with a coupling piece of the coupling means being arranged on the lid bracket and a coupling counter piece of the coupling means being arranged on the furnace lid. The coupling piece or the coupling counter piece includes a lateral recess extending in the pivoting direction of the lid supporting framework, through which the coupling counter piece is capable of being assembled with the coupling piece from aside.
problem: Need to exchange or service a furnace lid (or lid core) without directly manipulating the lid itself, and without requiring the lid-supporting bracket to carry the lid's weight during pivoting operations, which complicates maintenance and lid replacement.
constraint: The lateral recess must be oriented in the pivoting direction of the lid-support framework, and the coupling must allow side-assembly while maintaining sufficient engagement force to securely hold the lid during furnace operation. The coupling geometry must balance ease of attachment/detachment with operational security.
mechanism: A quick-connect coupling system detachably links a support bracket to a removable component via a coupling piece on the bracket and a coupling counter piece on the component. One of these components includes a lateral recess extending in the pivoting direction of the support framework. This lateral recess allows the coupling counter piece to be assembled with the coupling piece from the side—i.e., the component can be attached to or detached from the bracket by a lateral sliding motion rather than requiring vertical alignment or direct manipulation of the component. Once engaged, the coupling maintains a secure connection during normal lifting, lowering, and pivoting operations, but allows the component to be separated from the bracket for exchange while the bracket pivots independently.
mechanism_raw: A quick-connect coupling system detachably links the lid bracket to the furnace lid via a coupling piece on the bracket and a coupling counter piece on the lid. One of these components includes a lateral recess extending in the pivoting direction of the lid-support framework. This lateral recess allows the coupling counter piece to be assembled with the coupling piece from the side—i.e., the lid can be attached to or detached from the bracket by a lateral sliding motion rather than requiring vertical alignment or direct manipulation of the lid. Once engaged, the coupling maintains a secure connection during normal lifting, lowering, and pivoting operations, but allows the lid to be separated from the bracket for exchange while the bracket pivots independently.
residual_terms: ["quick-connect coupling", "lateral recess", "pivoting direction", "coupling piece", "coupling counter piece", "side-assembly", "lateral sliding motion", "engagement force"]

abstract: Apparatus for separating waste particles from a textile fiber flow is disclosed which includes a housing (2, 22, 34) with a deviation zone (4) and separation zone (6). Following the deviation zone is a fiber flow discharge channel (5). Following a separation means (10, 11, 23) is a waste chamber (7) for removing large and small particles of waste. The waste particle separation device includes a plurality of rod elements (10, 11) which are curved to guide lighter particles upwardly to prevent adherence to the separating element. Larger particles pass through openings between the rod-like elements to the collection chamber. Communication between the fiber flow and the waste flow may be had by using a valve member (27, 35) to intermittently connect a collection channel (25) with a suction removal source (8) via waste chamber (7).
problem: Separating waste particles of varying sizes and weights from a flowing textile fiber stream without disrupting fiber flow or causing clogging.
constraint: Balancing separation efficiency for particles of different sizes while maintaining continuous fiber flow and preventing clogging in the rod gaps or suction system.
mechanism: Curved guide elements create aerodynamic lift on lighter particles while allowing heavier particles to pass through gaps into a collection zone. An intermittent valve connects the collection zone to a suction source, enabling controlled removal of separated material without disrupting the main flow.
mechanism_raw: Curved rod elements guide lighter particles upward via aerodynamic forces, while larger particles fall through gaps between rods into a collection chamber. A valve intermittently connects the waste chamber to a suction source, enabling controlled removal of separated waste without interrupting the main fiber flow.

abstract: A hybrid electrothermal/electromagentic arcjet thruster has a cylindrical body with a longitudinal central axis, a plurality of electro-thermal propulsion mechanisms defined in the body in radially and circumferentially spaced relation about and extending along the central axis, and an electromagnetic propulsion mechanism defined in the body coaxially along the central axis thereof, between the electrothermal propulsion mechanisms and extending downstream thereof. Each electrothermal propulsion mechanism has tandemly-arranged constriction and expansion zones and are operable to concurrently receive a flow of gaseous propellant through the constriction zone and generate an electric arc therethrough to the expansion zone. The arcs interact with the propellant flows such that the latter are partially ionized and electrothermally accelerated through the expansion zones. The electromagnetic propulsion mechanism has an expansion chamber which communicates with, and extends downstream of, the expansion zones. The electromagnetic propulsion mechanism is operable to concurrently receive the flows of electrothermally-accelerated partially-ionized propellant in the expansion chamber and generate a radial current flux and an azimuthal magnetic field which interact with one another and with the flow of propellant such that the latter is electromagnetically accelerated at a higher rate than the electrothermal acceleration thereof.
problem: Achieving higher acceleration rates for propellant in a thruster to improve specific impulse and thrust efficiency.
constraint: Managing the interaction between electrothermal and electromagnetic stages to avoid energy loss and ensure the ionized propellant remains stable during sequential acceleration.
mechanism: A first stage ionizes and accelerates propellant through constriction and expansion zones, then a second stage further accelerates the partially ionized flow via interaction between radial current flux and an azimuthal magnetic field, creating a staged acceleration process.
mechanism_raw: Electrothermal propulsion stages first ionize and accelerate propellant through arc-driven constriction/expansion zones, then an electromagnetic stage further accelerates the partially ionized flow via radial current flux and azimuthal magnetic field interaction, creating a staged acceleration process.
residual_terms: ["ionization", "constriction/expansion zones", "radial current flux", "azimuthal magnetic field", "partially ionized flow"]

abstract: A coupling arrangement between a manifold having nipples and a solar panel having nipple receiving orifices. Each nipple is formed with a plurality of primary circumferential projections adjacent to the free forward end and a supplemental circumferential projection adjacent to the manifold. The primary projections have radial surfaces as well as surfaces inclined in a first direction while the supplemental projection has a radial surface as well as a surface inclined in the opposite direction. The coupling arrangement further includes a circumferential recess in each interior orifice of the solar collector, shaped and located for receiving its associated additional projection. Also disclosed is an improved arrangement for coupling together manifolds or grooves and recesses.
problem: Creating a reliable, leak-proof mechanical coupling between a manifold and a solar panel that can withstand thermal expansion and mechanical stress.
constraint: Maintaining a secure seal and mechanical integrity across temperature variations and mechanical vibrations without requiring external fasteners.
mechanism: Opposing circumferential projections with inclined surfaces engage corresponding recesses to create a self-locking interference fit. Primary projections provide initial alignment while supplemental projections ensure retention under stress.
mechanism_raw: Opposing circumferential projections (primary and supplemental) with inclined surfaces engage corresponding recesses in the solar panel orifices, creating a self-locking interference fit. The primary projections provide initial alignment, while the supplemental projections ensure retention under stress.

abstract: A surface of ceramic plate is roughened uniformly by immersing in a mixed solution comprising NH.sub.4 F, (NH.sub.4).sub.2 SO.sub.4, H.sub.2 SO.sub.4 and H.sub.2 O, followed by immersion in molten NaOH, and the resulting surface roughened ceramic plate can be used for producing a ceramic wiring board.
problem: Uniformly roughening a ceramic surface to enhance adhesion for subsequent processes like ceramic wiring board production.
constraint: Achieving uniform etching depth and roughness without over-etching or damaging the ceramic substrate, requiring precise control of chemical composition, temperature, and immersion time.
mechanism: Chemical etching via immersion in a mixed solution followed by a secondary treatment creates controlled surface roughness through selective dissolution and reaction, producing a textured surface with consistent topography.
mechanism_raw: Chemical etching via immersion in a mixed solution (NH4F, (NH4)2SO4, H2SO4, H2O) followed by molten NaOH treatment creates controlled surface roughness through selective dissolution and reaction, producing a textured surface with consistent topography.

abstract: Device for preventing thermal stratification for a steam generator feed pipe. A fixed helix (14) downstream of a rising break (12) of the pipe subdivides its interior into twisted channels. The cold water entering at a low flame rate is blocked upstream until a predetermined height (h) is reached and completely fills an upstream part (11) to be protected against thermal gradients.
problem: Preventing thermal stratification and associated thermal gradients in a steam generator feed pipe caused by cold water entering at low flow rates.
constraint: Balancing the helical geometry and flow rate to ensure the upstream section fills completely before cold water reaches it, while maintaining adequate throughput for the steam generator.
mechanism: A fixed helical element downstream of a pipe bend subdivides the interior into twisted channels, blocking flow until a predetermined height fills the upstream section. This delays flow entry until the protected zone is fully filled, preventing thermal shock.
mechanism_raw: A fixed helix downstream of a pipe bend subdivides the interior into twisted channels, blocking cold water flow until a predetermined height fills the upstream section. This delays cold water entry until the protected zone is fully filled, preventing thermal shock.

abstract: An explosive with maximum energy yield for warheads and solid rocket propellants comprises a high-energy secondary explosive with inorganic perchlorate and metal component with a high affinity for oxygen as well as desensitizing and binding agents. The oxygen balance sheet of the secondary explosive is balanced by the perchlorate component approximately to provide a complete reaction to give carbon dioxide and water. Those explosive gases are reduced by the metal component, supplying energy, in accordance with the requirements made on the explosive.
problem: Maximizing energy yield in explosive compositions while ensuring complete reaction products.
constraint: Maintaining a precise oxygen balance to avoid incomplete combustion or excess residue, which would reduce energy efficiency or destabilize the explosive.
mechanism: Balancing reactant supply and demand to achieve stoichiometric completeness, thereby optimizing energy release through controlled gas-phase reduction.
mechanism_raw: Balancing the oxygen supply from perchlorate with the oxygen demand of the secondary explosive and metal components to achieve stoichiometric completeness, thereby optimizing energy release through controlled gas reduction.

abstract: For improving controllability and simplifying the circuit arrangement, there is disclosed a random access memory device comprising a nibble decoder circuit operative to control nibble switching transistors and a read/write control circuit operative to control read/write switching circuits and data amplifier circuits independent from the nibble decoder circuit, and three data bits read out from memory cell arrays are transferred to the same memory cell arrays when a new data bit is written into the a memory cell of the other memory cell array directly accessed by an external processor, thereby preventing the data bits from destruction.
problem: Improving controllability and simplifying circuit arrangements in random access memory devices while preventing data destruction during write operations.
constraint: Balancing independent circuit control with the need to maintain data coherence across multiple memory arrays during simultaneous access.
mechanism: Decoupling control circuits to enable independent operation, and using redundant data transfer to preserve data integrity during simultaneous access.
mechanism_raw: Decoupling the nibble decoder and read/write control circuits to allow independent operation, and using redundant data transfer (three bits) to a memory array during writes to preserve data integrity.

abstract: Wax-base or emollient-base cosmetic compositions may be provided as samples on carrying sheets by providing the carrying sheet with a window sheet having a hole therein to expose said cosmetic composition, and a cover sheet over said window sheet to protect said exposed composition from incidental contact.
problem: Protecting exposed cosmetic samples on a carrying sheet from incidental contact while allowing user access.
constraint: Ensuring the cover sheet can be easily removed without damaging the sample or the underlying carrying sheet, while maintaining structural integrity during transport.
mechanism: Using a layered structure with a removable cover sheet and a window to shield an exposed area until access is required.
mechanism_raw: Using a layered structure with a window sheet (containing a hole to expose the sample) and a removable cover sheet to shield the exposed area until use.

abstract: The present invention refers to a temple for holding or for laterally tensioning a woven fabric, in particular on weaving looms, comprising endless guide means having displaceably arranged therein members provided with needles for engagement with said woven fabric, said guide means extending and being arranged in such a way that the needles of at least two members are simultaneously in engagement with the edge of the woven fabric and that, in the course of the needling-in operation, the needles brought into engagement with the woven fabric, are located at a greater distance from the longitudinal axis of the width of woven fabric than in the course of the de-needling operation. The failures occurring in the case of such a temple are now eliminated by providing an appropriate amount of play between the individual members and by guaranteeing at the same time that the members are returned to the point of needling-in in an appropriate manner.
problem: Eliminating mechanical failures in weaving loom temples during needling-in and de-needling operations.
constraint: Balancing the amount of play to prevent misalignment or failure during operation while maintaining precise needle positioning for consistent fabric tensioning.
mechanism: Introducing controlled mechanical play between interacting components and ensuring their return to a reference position to accommodate positional variance while maintaining alignment.
mechanism_raw: Introducing controlled play between needle-carrying members and ensuring their return to the correct position during needling-in, allowing simultaneous engagement with the fabric edge while accommodating positional variance.

abstract: A paraffin conversion process for hydroisomerizing a nitrogen and wax-containing hydrocarbon feedstock comprising contacting the feedstock with a catalyst including a ZSM-11 zeolite characterized by an alpha value from about 10 to 50, in combination with a Group VIII metal hydrogenation-dehydrogenation component of platinum or palladium at a temperature of about 400.degree. F. to about 850.degree. F. and at a pressure of from about 200 to about 2000 psig.
problem: Hydroisomerizing nitrogen and wax-containing hydrocarbon feedstocks efficiently using a catalyst system.
constraint: Optimizing catalyst composition and reaction conditions to balance activity, selectivity, and resistance to nitrogen poisoning while avoiding overcracking or thermal degradation.
mechanism: Combining a porous material with controlled acidity and a metal component to enable selective catalytic reactions under specific thermal and pressure conditions.
