Then a nozzle is moved and positioned by a mechanical structure along an appropriate adhesive path. The mechanical structure includes a tracer mechanism the includes an adjustable U-shaped cam track and a linkage connected to the nozzle at one end and to a cam follower at the other end thereof such that the cam follower is positioned within the cam track; a driver mechanism is connected to propel the cam follower along the track in the X-Y directions (the nozzle can move in the Z-direction as well to follow contours of the footwear). The heel pad is preferably an inflatable pad. The mechanical tracer mechanism, as a unit, has a predetermined and fixed position relative to the heel pad. The heel laster operates in two steps: first, the pad is pressed against the heel of the upper and, second, the pad is inflated to press into any crevices a the upper surface at the heel region (and the shank region). Then the upper is wiped onto the insole of the assembly.
problem: Precisely applying adhesive along a contoured surface (e.g., a footwear heel) during manufacturing.
constraint: Maintaining positional accuracy of the nozzle relative to the contoured surface while allowing independent Z-axis adjustment for surface irregularities.
mechanism: Using a mechanical tracer with an adjustable cam track and linkage system to guide a dispensing element along a predefined path, translating cam follower motion into controlled multi-axis movement for contour-following application.
mechanism_raw: Using a mechanical tracer with an adjustable U-shaped cam track and linkage system to guide a nozzle along a predefined path, translating cam follower motion into controlled X-Y-Z movement for contour-following adhesive application.

abstract: A rotor module (2) for a shapemeter comprising a central arbor (7) to a non-rotatable ring (10) surrounding the arbor (7) by at least one web (9) and an outer cylinder (12) rotatable on bearings (13) on the ring (10) and means, (16, 17) carried by the arbor (7) to cooperate with the inner surface of the ring (10) to detect relative movements between the arbor and ring in response to a force applied to the cylinder (12) at a pre-determined position in order to provide output signals representative of such movements.
problem: Detecting and measuring forces applied to a rotating cylinder in a shapemeter or similar device.
constraint: Isolating rotational motion of the outer cylinder from the arbor while enabling precise detection of minute relative displacements under load.
mechanism: Converting applied force into relative rotational movement between a non-rotatable element and a central arbor via a web-connected outer cylinder, with sensors detecting these movements to generate output signals proportional to the applied force.
mechanism_raw: Converting applied force into relative rotational movement between a non-rotatable ring and a central arbor via a web-connected outer cylinder, with sensors detecting these movements to generate output signals proportional to the applied force.

abstract: An adjustable oven for mass cooking of food products comprising an essentially sealed enclosure having a conveyor received therethrough for conveying food through the oven. A heated gaseous cooking medium is applied to the food product during conveyance through the oven by impingement of the cooking medium at high velocity through spaced duct fingers disposed above and below the conveyor system. The gaseous cooking medium is heated and circulated through the oven at high velocity and subsequently recirculated for continuous cooking of food products in the oven. The cooking oven enables optimization of the cooking process by allowing at least certain of the duct fingers to be vertically adjustable relative to the food product so as to maximize heat transfer therefrom for any particular food product. The elevation of the duct fingers from the food product may be continuously varied automatically during operation of the oven or during a cooking cycle giving the food processor great flexibility in use of the oven.
problem: Optimizing heat transfer efficiency for different food products during mass cooking in a sealed oven environment.
constraint: Maintaining continuous high-velocity circulation of the gaseous cooking medium while enabling real-time or cycle-based adjustability of duct positions without disrupting the sealed enclosure or conveyor operation.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting the position of flow-directing elements within a sealed enclosure to control the spacing between a high-velocity gaseous medium and a moving product, thereby optimizing heat transfer efficiency for varying product types without interrupting the sealed environment or product transport.
mechanism_raw: Vertically adjusting duct fingers positioned above and below a conveyor system to dynamically control the distance between high-velocity gaseous cooking medium and the food product, thereby maximizing heat transfer for any specific food type.

abstract: Disclosed is a panel which includes a pan having at least one side member with an upper edge portion, the pan having contained therein a fluid based cementitious material pressed for removal of water while within the pan, and at least one trim member attached to the upper edge portion of the side member of the pan, the trim member undergoing telescoping action upon pressing of the material in the pan so as to be rigidly secured to the upper edge portion of the side member of the pan. Also disclosed is an apparatus and process for production of the pan.
problem: Rigidly securing a trim member to a pan after pressing a fluid-based cementitious material within the pan, ensuring structural integrity during and after the pressing process.
constraint: Ensuring the telescoping action reliably engages and secures the trim member under variable pressing pressures while maintaining compatibility with the pan's structural design and material properties.
mechanism: Employing a telescoping mechanical interface that deforms or interlocks under compressive forces during a pressing operation, creating a self-locking connection between a trim component and a structural edge while accommodating variable pressure conditions.
mechanism_raw: Designing the trim member to undergo telescoping action in response to compressive forces applied during pressing, which mechanically locks the trim member to the pan's upper edge through deformation or interlocking geometry.

abstract: Synthesis gas, reducing gas, or fuel gas is produced by the partial oxidation of bituminous coal at an autogenous temperature in the range of about 2000.degree. F. to 2700.degree. F. and at a pressure in the range of about 17 to 100 atmospheres to produce a raw effluent gas stream containing entrained molten slag and carbon-rich particulate material. After cooling, course slag and carbon-rich particulate material are separated. A fuel mixture comprising about 20 to 100 wt. % of said carbon-rich particulate material and the remainder comprising a supplemental fuel is reacted by partial oxidation at an autogenous temperature of about 2000.degree. F. to 2700.degree. F. and at a reduced pressure e.g. in the range of about 1 to 16 atmospheres and at least 16 atmospheres below the pressure in the partial oxidation reaction used to produce said carbon-rich particulate material. By reducing the pressure less carbon-rich particulate material is produced in the second partial oxidation reaction at a significant cost savings and improved process efficiency.
problem: Reducing the production of carbon-rich particulate material in a secondary partial oxidation reaction to achieve cost savings and improved process efficiency.
constraint: Balancing pressure and temperature conditions between the two stages to maintain autogenous reaction conditions while ensuring the second stage's reduced pressure does not compromise overall gas yield or reaction stability.
mechanism: Implementing a staged reaction process where a first stage operates at elevated pressure to generate carbon-rich byproducts, and a subsequent stage introduces these byproducts into a reduced-pressure environment with a fuel mixture, suppressing further particulate formation while maintaining autogenous reaction conditions.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a two-stage partial oxidation process where the first stage operates at high pressure to generate carbon-rich particulate, and the second stage uses a fuel mixture containing this particulate at a significantly reduced pressure, thereby minimizing further particulate formation.

abstract: This invention relates to refractory coatings and their use. The refractory coating comprises: PA1 (1) a carrier, generally water; PA1 (2) an alpha alumina monohydrate; PA1 (3) an aluminum hydroxyhalide; and PA1 (4) a refractory material. The refractory coatings are used for coating patterns which are used to make refractory shells.
reason: The patent describes a static composition of materials (carrier, alpha alumina monohydrate, aluminum hydroxyhalide, refractory material) without explaining a causal functional relationship or dynamic process that produces a useful effect beyond the material's inherent properties.

abstract: A method for contactless profiling is performed while tilting an optic axis of a distance measuring probe (PB), which is capable of measuring a distance optically, by an angle .theta. from the vertical axis. When a point (P.sub.1) at which distance measurement is impossible is reached and measurement of distance the thus becomes impossible, the movement of the distance measuring probe (PB) is halted and the distance measuring probe is rotated to tilt the optical axis thereof from the vertical axis by the angle .theta. in the opposite direction, after which contactless profiling is resumed. Thereafter, when the points (P.sub.2, P.sub.3) at which distance measurement is impossible are reached, the distance measuring probe (PB) is made to perform the same operations so that contactless profiling may continue.
problem: Continuing contactless profiling of a surface when the distance measuring probe encounters points where optical measurement is impossible due to geometric or surface obstructions.
constraint: Ensuring the probe's rotational adjustment and resumption of movement do not introduce measurement errors or disrupt the overall profiling trajectory, while minimizing downtime during reorientation.
mechanism: Interrupting a surface-profiling operation upon detecting an optically inaccessible region, reorienting a measurement probe to redirect its sensing axis away from the obstruction, and resuming profiling along an adjusted trajectory to maintain measurement continuity and minimize positional error.
mechanism_raw: Halting probe movement upon detecting an unmeasurable point, rotating the probe to tilt its optic axis in the opposite direction, and resuming profiling to bypass the obstruction while maintaining measurement continuity.

abstract: To facilitate program control modification and troubleshooting in a sequence control system in spite of simple processing programs, sequence control processes are linked in a chain fashion. A unit process for activating an actuation member in both forward and reverse directions forms a ring so as to be activated in sequence cyclically, and these unit process rings are linked between an actuation start side activator for the present process and an actuation end side activator for the preceding process, both activated simultaneously whenever one of them is activated. Therefore, any process can be stopped at, restarted and reversed from any process steps in both the forward and reverse directions through the linked actuation start and end side activators, after the automatic operation has been switched to the manual operation or vice versa.
problem: Managing program control modification and troubleshooting in a sequence control system with simple processing programs.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between forward and reverse operations while ensuring seamless transitions between automatic and manual modes.
mechanism: A chain of interconnected control elements is configured such that each element's activation triggers the next in sequence, enabling cyclic operation. Bidirectional coupling between adjacent elements allows any step to be halted, restarted, or reversed without disrupting synchronization between forward and reverse modes.
mechanism_raw: Linking unit process rings in a chain fashion, where actuation start and end side activators are interconnected to enable cyclic activation. This allows any process step to be stopped, restarted, or reversed in both forward and reverse directions by leveraging the linked activators.

abstract: Hydrolyzable substrates comprise blocked moieties which, when cleaved from the substrate during hydrolysis, provide electron transfer agents. The released electron transfer agents can be recycled between a reductant and a reducible compound that upon reduction provides a detectable species. Alternatively, they can be recycled between an oxidant and an oxidizable compound that upon oxidation provides a detectable species. These substrates are useful in analytical compositions, elements and methods for the determination of hydrolytic analytes, such as hydrolytic enzymes or biological cells containing such enzymes.
problem: Detecting hydrolytic analytes (e.g., enzymes or biological cells) through controlled release of electron transfer agents during hydrolysis.
constraint: Ensuring the released agents are selectively cleaved only during hydrolysis and can be efficiently recycled without interfering with the detection process.
mechanism: Cleavable linkers on substrates release signaling agents during a chemical reaction. These agents participate in a redox cycle between a donor/acceptor pair and a target compound, generating a measurable output proportional to analyte concentration.
mechanism_raw: Blocked moieties on hydrolyzable substrates are cleaved during hydrolysis to release electron transfer agents. These agents are recycled between a reductant/oxidant pair and a reducible/oxidizable compound to generate a detectable species, enabling quantifiable analysis.

abstract: A piggy back evaporator includes a drip pan having an oblique condensate drain sheet extending over the major length of the same. A steam hole within the condensate drain sheet allows steam to reach the lower surface of a bottom wall of a piggy back pan. The piggy back pan bottom wall is corrugated to define a series of laterally spaced troughs on its upper face and flues on its lower face. Maple sap is fed into the piggy back pan to a level covering the corrugations of the bottom wall. A hood overlies the piggy back pan and seals off the interior thereof. A high pressure air blower is mounted to the hood and feeds air under pressure into a plenum chamber and downwardly through the downpipes into individual horizontal sparging tubes which extend the length of the piggy back pan and are located within the bottoms of individual troughs defined by the corrugations. Air under pressure passes through pin holes within the sparging tubes with the bubbles formed thereby scouring the metal surfaces of the troughs within the piggy back bottom wall and additionally creating an effective frothing action for the sap within the piggy back pan. The air passing through the sap is effectively heated and saturated with moisture with the resulting evaporation of the moisture captured by the air consuming a large quantity of heat to maintain a temperature differential between the sap/air mixture and condensing steam under the pan such that almost all of the steam is condensed in the area between the drip pan and the piggy back pan to increase the liquid concentration of the sap being processed.
problem: Efficiently evaporating liquid (e.g., maple sap) to increase solute concentration while minimizing energy waste.
constraint: Balancing the pressure and flow rate of air to optimize bubble formation, heat transfer, and steam condensation without overheating or under-saturating the system.
mechanism: A pressurized gas is introduced through apertures into a liquid medium, creating dispersed bubbles that enhance surface contact and mass transfer. The gas absorbs moisture, consumes thermal energy during evaporation, and maintains a temperature gradient to drive condensation and concentration.
mechanism_raw: Pressurized air is forced through sparging tubes with pin holes, creating bubbles that scour metal surfaces and induce frothing. The air absorbs moisture from the liquid, becomes heated and saturated, and evaporates moisture by consuming heat, maintaining a temperature differential to condense steam and enhance concentration.

abstract: Filaments are produced from polymers having an inherent viscosity of at least 0.7 measured in concentrated sulfuric acid and containing in the polymer chain at least 50 percent of the repeating units. ##STR1## by melting the polymer and heating the melt to a temperature of from about 20.degree. C. to about 80.degree. C. above the melting point of the polymer, passing the melt through a filter pack having a filtering area of at least about 8 in.sup.2 and a total volume of at least about 1.2 in.sup.3 per pound of polymer extruded per hour, and containing inert, irregularly shaped particles having a mesh size of about 25 to 140 to provide a pressure drop at least about 800 psig., and extruding the melt through spinning openings of desired shape to form filaments. The process is capable of producing fibers and yarns having a dpf of about 15 to 100, a tenacity of about 1 to 2 grams per denier, an elongation at break of about 50 to 160 percent and a modulus of about 20 to 30 grams per denier.
problem: Producing high-tenacity polymer filaments with controlled mechanical properties (e.g., tenacity, elongation, modulus).
constraint: Maintaining a pressure drop of at least 800 psig while ensuring the filter pack volume and particle mesh size do not excessively restrict throughput or degrade polymer quality.
mechanism: A viscous fluid is filtered through a porous medium with irregular particulate packing to establish a controlled pressure differential. This removes contaminants and regulates flow rate before the fluid is shaped into continuous filaments via extrusion.
mechanism_raw: Melting a high-viscosity polymer and passing it through a filter pack with inert, irregular particles to create a controlled pressure drop. This filtration step removes impurities and regulates melt flow before extrusion through spinning openings to form filaments.

abstract: The feeding of pigs or other animals is improved by the provision of a tray member which sits underneath the conventional feeder trough and extends out in the front edge of the trough so the material dropped by the animal over the front edge in the feeding action tends to collect on the tray rather than be wasted. The tray has upstanding ribs which define compartments in the area on which the feed falls to maintain the feed in place and to allow feeding of specialized materials.
problem: Reducing feed waste in animal feeding systems by capturing material dropped over the front edge of a trough.
constraint: Designing rib geometry to balance spill containment with accessibility, ensuring feed remains accessible without excessive accumulation or blockage.
mechanism: A collection tray with upstanding barriers is positioned to intercept spilled material from a primary dispensing surface. The barriers compartmentalize the collected material, maintaining accessibility while preventing uncontrolled accumulation or blockage.
mechanism_raw: A tray with upstanding ribs is positioned beneath the trough to collect spilled feed. The ribs compartmentalize the collected material, keeping it in place while allowing animals to access specialized feeds within the compartments.

abstract: A robot cleaner for insertion between parallel platens for cleaning the platens. A body having first and second sections movable away and toward each other by an air bladder. Said sections include gripping and scraping blades, each of the sections includes sides movable transversely toward the plate by a bladder. One of the sections grips the platens while the second section traverses across the plates and scrapes and cleans the plates.
problem: Cleaning parallel platens in a confined space without manual intervention.
constraint: Limited space between platens requires simultaneous stabilization and mobility without mechanical interference.
mechanism: A two-part system with independently mobile sections performs sequential gripping and cleaning: one section stabilizes a surface via transverse engagement, while the second section traverses across the surface to remove material. Flexible actuation enables each section to move without mechanical interference, allowing coordinated operation within confined spatial constraints.
mechanism_raw: A dual-section robot uses coordinated gripping and scraping actions: one section grips the platens via transverse blade movement, while the second section traverses across the plates to scrape and clean. Air bladders enable independent movement of each section, allowing sequential gripping and cleaning within tight spatial constraints.

abstract: A multi-disk clamp end effector carries around a tubular member a plurality of disks with a center hole like wafers and releases them sequentially one at a time. Each disk is attached to the tubular member by means of a holder which not only supports the disk but also is pressed to the tubular member by an elastic ring. As the tubular member is gradually retracted and its front end passes the position of each holder, the contracting force of the spring disengages the holder from the disk to which it is attached and the corresponding disk is released.
problem: Sequentially releasing multiple disks from a tubular member without manual handling.
constraint: Disks must be released in a precise order while maintaining attachment until triggered by the retraction motion.
mechanism: A series of holders, each biased by a resilient element, retain components until a retracting member sequentially disengages each holder. The retraction motion triggers release by overcoming the bias, ensuring ordered, one-at-a-time detachment through controlled mechanical interaction.
mechanism_raw: Each disk is attached to a holder with an elastic ring that biases it against the tubular member. As the tubular member retracts, its front end passes each holder, causing the elastic ring to disengage the holder from its disk, releasing it. The sequential retraction ensures controlled, one-at-a-time release.

abstract: A composite sheet material which is particularly useful as a backing material for carpet underlay is a stitched crepe paper sheet 5 with rows of apparent projections 13 formed therein between parallel rows of stitches 10 by deforming the crepe paper sheet without puncturing the paper. The stitches 10 substantially restrict the extensibility of the crepe paper sheet 5 and the apparent projections 13 are formed at a position in the crepe paper sheet 5 directly in line with the ends 11 of the stitches 10. According to the preferred method described, each apparent projection 13 is in reality a depression between two projections formed in the opposite surface of the crepe paper sheet without puncturing the paper. In an alternative embodiment there is a pair of apparent projections 13 formed in the crepe paper sheet 5 between adjacent rows of stitches 10.
problem: Creating structured projections in a flexible sheet material without puncturing or compromising integrity.
constraint: The material must retain structural integrity while forming projections, requiring a balance between localized deformation and global strength.
mechanism: Parallel constraints are applied to a deformable material to restrict extensibility in localized regions. Subsequent deformation between these constraints redistributes material into structured projections or depressions, leveraging the constraints to control deformation patterns without compromising global integrity.
mechanism_raw: Stitching parallel rows into a crepe paper sheet restricts extensibility in those regions. Subsequent deformation between the stitches creates apparent projections (or depressions) by redistributing material without puncturing, leveraging the stitching as a constraint to localize and control the deformation pattern.

abstract: A control motor for a servo valve is provided. The control motor comprises a control element which can carry out a pivotal movement due to an electric input signal supplied to said motor. The movement of the control element causes a corresponding change of hydraulic resistances and, as a consequence, changes in hydraulic output signals of an hydraulic amplifier actuated by said motor.
problem: Converting an electrical input signal into a proportional hydraulic output signal for servo control.
constraint: The system must achieve precise, proportional control between electrical input and hydraulic output without mechanical hysteresis.
mechanism: An electrically driven pivotal element directly modulates fluid flow paths in a connected amplifier, translating electrical energy into proportional hydraulic pressure changes. The pivot movement mechanically alters resistance, enabling precise signal conversion without mechanical hysteresis.
mechanism_raw: A pivotal control element, driven by an electric input, mechanically alters hydraulic resistance in a connected amplifier. The pivot movement directly modulates fluid flow paths, translating electrical energy into hydraulic pressure changes that serve as the output signal.

abstract: A bulk material container comprising a flexible liner with a bottom outlet fitting. The bottom outlet fitting of the flexible liner is inserted by means of an installing tool into a bottom opening of the shell of the container. The bottom outlet fitting has a substantially square internal pocket shape that is adapted for receiving fingers of the insertion tool for installation in the shell.
problem: Securely installing a flexible liner's outlet fitting into a rigid container shell without complex tools.
constraint: The fitting must be installed reliably in a single motion while accommodating the flexibility of the liner material.
mechanism: A tool with shaped engaging elements mates with a corresponding pocket on a flexible component during insertion. The engagement ensures alignment and force application to seat the component into a rigid opening, accommodating material flexibility through a single-motion installation process.
mechanism_raw: The outlet fitting has a square internal pocket that mates with corresponding fingers on an insertion tool. The tool's fingers engage the pocket during insertion, ensuring alignment and force application to seat the fitting into the container's bottom opening.

abstract: A two-part jack system includes a mechanical jack stand with a ratchet mechanism and a ratchet release, and a power unit that may be selectively aligned with and attached to the jack stand for raising or lowering it. A unitary control mechanism carried by the power unit is adapted to selectively lock the power unit in an aligned position relative to the jack stand, and also to selectively release the ratchet release of the jack stand. A locking mechanism is carried in part by the jack stand and in part by the power unit. The unitary control mechanism has three different operating positions. In one operating position the locking mechanism is kept locked while the ratchet release is left in an unreleased state; in a second operating position the locking mechanism is kept locked while the ratchet release is released; and in the third operating position the locking mechanism is held in an unlocked condition while the ratchet release is left in an unreleased state. The power unit has an operating handle, and a single lever which operates the unitary control mechanism is carried on the power unit operating handle for convenient access and easy control by a human operator.
problem: Coordinating the alignment, locking, and ratchet release of a mechanical jack stand and power unit through a single control mechanism to ensure safe and efficient operation.
constraint: The mechanism must ensure precise alignment between the power unit and jack stand while preventing conflicting states (e.g., unlocking while ratchet is released), requiring a single lever to manage multiple mechanical linkages without ambiguity.
mechanism: A multi-state control system with discrete operating positions that coordinate interdependent mechanical actions through a single input, ensuring mutually exclusive states to prevent conflicting operations. Each position selectively engages or disengages mechanical subsystems to enforce a defined sequence of alignment, locking, and release functions.
mechanism_raw: A multi-state control system with three discrete operating positions that independently coordinate two interdependent actions: (1) maintaining a locked connection while keeping the ratchet unreleased, (2) maintaining a locked connection while releasing the ratchet, and (3) unlocking the connection while keeping the ratchet unreleased. This allows sequential or conditional activation of mechanical subsystems based on operator input.

abstract: A centrifuge includes a drive which revolves a rotor whose speed is controlled by a sensor located on a mounting plate which is immovably fixed in a recess of a ring installed on the mounting surface of the drive casing. The ring has a hole accommodating a movable element installed with a provision for touching over the radius of curvature upon said mounting surface of the drive casing and ensuring the movement of said ring relative to the lower surface of the rotor for installing the sensor at a certain distance from said surface at which the optimum sensitivity to the rotation speed of the rotor is ensured.
problem: Maintaining optimal sensor positioning relative to a rotating component (e.g., a centrifuge rotor) to ensure accurate speed measurement despite dynamic movement.
constraint: The sensor must remain at a precise distance from the rotor surface to avoid signal degradation, while the mounting system must accommodate rotational motion without introducing mechanical interference or calibration drift.
mechanism: A sensor mounting system with an adjustable element constrained within a ring structure that maintains a fixed spatial relationship to a moving surface. The adjustable element compensates for dynamic displacement of the surface to preserve consistent sensing proximity, enabling stable signal acquisition despite rotational motion.
mechanism_raw: A sensor is mounted on a movable element within a ring structure that can shift relative to the rotor's surface. The movable element adjusts the sensor's radial position to maintain a fixed distance from the rotor surface, ensuring consistent sensitivity. The ring's hole and curvature-matching design enable passive or active repositioning of the sensor as the rotor moves.

abstract: A system for the processing and handling of products including the method and apparatus therefor. A conveyor includes rocker elements fixed thereto which may be selectively tipped by means of an actuator and camming surface to off-load products conveyed in a single file arrangement. The rocker elements are positioned on a chain to form an elongate support for the conveyed products. Two conveyors positioned side by side for receiving product in series may be used to provide a full view of the surface of the product for sensing by multiple sensors.
problem: Offloading products from a conveyor in a single-file arrangement while enabling full-surface inspection of each product using multiple sensors.
constraint: The rocker tipping mechanism must precisely align with product positions to avoid misfeeds, while the dual-conveyor arrangement must maintain synchronization to ensure no gaps in sensor coverage during offloading.
mechanism: A product transfer and inspection system using selectively actuated tipping elements synchronized with a dual-conveyor arrangement. The tipping elements align with product positions to offload items, while the parallel conveyors expose opposing surfaces of each product to sensors for complete inspection coverage without gaps.
mechanism_raw: Rocker elements mounted on a chain conveyor are selectively tipped via actuators and camming surfaces to offload products at designated points. Two parallel conveyors positioned side by side allow products to be conveyed in series, with each conveyor exposing a different surface of the product to sensors for complete inspection coverage.

abstract: A method in accordance with the invention comprises passing through a zeolite catalyst as described below, a gaseous stream containing nitrogen oxides, ammonia and oxygen to selectively catalyze the reduction of nitrogen oxides and, if excess or unreacted ammonia is present, to oxidize the excess of unreacted ammonia with oxygen to hydrogen and water. The method includes the use of a zeolite catalyst composition which comprises a metal (e.g., iron or copper) promoted zeolite, the zeolite being characterized by having a silica to alumina ratio of at least about 10 and a pore structure which is interconnected in all three crystallographic dimensions by pores having an average kinetic pore diameter of at least about 7 Angstroms. Promoted zeolites of the above type have demonstrated high tolerance for sulfur poisoning, good activity for the selective catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides with ammonia, good activity for the oxidation of ammonia with oxygen, and the retention of such good activities even under high temperature operations, e.g., 400.degree. C. or higher, and hydrothermal conditions.
problem: Efficiently reducing nitrogen oxides (NOx) with ammonia while simultaneously oxidizing excess unreacted ammonia under high-temperature and hydrothermal conditions without catalyst degradation.
constraint: The catalyst must balance pore size and interconnectivity to facilitate diffusion of reactants and products while maintaining structural integrity under high temperatures (≥400°C) and hydrothermal conditions, which typically degrade conventional catalysts.
mechanism: A catalytic system with a porous structure and compositional promotion that enables sequential chemical reactions in a single pass. The structure balances diffusion pathways and thermal stability to facilitate both reactant conversion and byproduct oxidation while resisting degradation under harsh environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: A metal-promoted zeolite catalyst with a high silica-to-alumina ratio and three-dimensionally interconnected pores (≥7 Å) enables two sequential reactions: (1) selective catalytic reduction of NOx with ammonia, and (2) oxidation of excess ammonia to hydrogen and water. The catalyst's pore structure and composition provide tolerance to sulfur poisoning and thermal stability, allowing both reactions to occur in a single pass.

abstract: In a process in which a non-woven strip is needled to a revolving endless carrier web, adjacent convolutions of the non-woven strip should exactly adjoin each other. For that purpose each convolution of the non-woven strip is initially needled to the carrier web with the exception of a marginal portion, which constitutes a free longitudinal edge, and that marginal portion is needled after the position and direction of the free longitudinal edge have been detected.
problem: Ensuring adjacent convolutions of a non-woven strip needled onto a revolving carrier web exactly adjoin each other without gaps or overlaps.
constraint: The detection system must accurately determine the free edge's position and direction in real-time to ensure precise needling, while the carrier web's rotation must be synchronized with the needling steps to avoid misalignment during the two-stage process.
mechanism: A two-stage attachment process where initial fixation secures a majority of a moving substrate while leaving a marginal region unbound. Subsequent detection of the marginal region's position and orientation enables precise final fixation, decoupling alignment from completion to correct positional errors before full bonding.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage needling process: (1) initial needling secures all portions of the strip except a marginal free edge, and (2) after detecting the position and direction of the free edge, the marginal portion is needled to complete attachment. This sequential approach decouples alignment from final fixation, allowing correction of positional errors before the final bond.

abstract: A decorative article is assembled using a plurality of pre-cut wood pieces. The wood pieces are of three types, a square, triangle and parallelogram, and are sized relative to one another, such that a variety of different designs and patterns can be achieved. The wood pieces are assembled on a disposable sheet having a rectangular grid to effect the desired pattern. Four wood frame members are then temporarily attached to the corresponding border surfaces of a wood substrate having the same rectangular grid pattern as the disposable sheet to define a wooden frame around the grid pattern. Wood glue is applied to individual squares of the grid pattern on the wood substrate and the wood pieces are sequentially moved from the disposable sheet to the wood substrate where they are secured in their respective proper positions on the substrate by the glue. After the decorative pattern has been assembled on the substrate, the wood frame members are glued to the border surfaces thereof to provide a rectangular frame for the decorative pattern.
problem: Creating a decorative pattern with precise placement of individual components on a substrate.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment between the temporary layout and the final substrate while enabling sequential transfer without disturbing already-placed pieces.
mechanism: Use a temporary spatial reference structure to establish precise positional correspondence between discrete components and a target surface, enabling sequential transfer of components while maintaining alignment through geometric matching between the temporary and target reference systems.
mechanism_raw: Using a temporary grid-based layout (disposable sheet) to transfer pre-cut pieces to a final substrate with matching grid alignment, ensuring accurate positioning through spatial correspondence between the temporary and final grids.

abstract: A method and apparatus for detecting and utilizing the bobbin circumference of cross-wound bobbins or cheeses in a textile machine producing the bobbins includes determining and evaluating the attained circumference of the cheese from measured values produced by sensors detecting the growth of the cheese. The measured values are continuously detected and processed and optionally stored in memory in at least one computer for further evaluation. A mathematical linkage symbolizing the current bobbin circumference cleansed of randomness in the current measured value pickup at very short time intervals based on the measured values for each winding station is continuously and repeatedly performed anew in the further evaluation. A parameter from the group consisting of current bobbin circumference, bobbin radius or bobbin diameter is calculated from the linkage. The linkage result is used with as little delay as possible for at least one purpose from the group consisting of displaying the result, and/or affecting the winding process, and/or detecting the yarn length and/or terminating the winding process.
problem: Accurately determining and dynamically adjusting the winding process of cross-wound bobbins in real-time despite random measurement noise.
constraint: Balancing the need for real-time responsiveness with the requirement to filter out measurement noise and variability inherent in short-interval sensor readings.
mechanism: Continuously acquire sensor measurements at high frequency, apply a statistical filtering process to suppress random fluctuations and derive a smoothed operational parameter, then use the filtered parameter with minimal latency to adjust a dynamic process, display information, or trigger termination.
mechanism_raw: Continuously sampling sensor data at short intervals, applying a mathematical linkage to filter randomness and compute a smoothed parameter (e.g., circumference), and using the result with minimal delay to control the winding process, display data, or terminate operations.

abstract: Organosilane polymers having recurring silylene-1,3-butadiyne and/or disilylene-1,3-butadiyne units are prepared in a one-pot synthesis from hexachlorobutadiene. Depending on the organic substituents (R and R'), these polymers have useful film-forming properties, and are converted to the ceramic, silicon carbide upon heating a very uniform high char yields. They can also be pulled into fibers. The polymers are thermally crosslinked above 100.degree. C.
problem: Producing organosilane polymers with useful film-forming properties and high thermal conversion to ceramic materials.
constraint: Achieving a balance between thermal stability (for crosslinking and char formation) and processability (e.g., fiber formation or film casting) through controlled polymer structure.
mechanism: Synthesize a polymer via a single-reaction-step process from a starting compound, producing a structure with repeating functional units that enable thermal crosslinking at elevated temperatures and yield a ceramic material with uniform high char formation upon heating.
mechanism_raw: One-pot synthesis from hexachlorobutadiene to create polymers with recurring silylene-1,3-butadiyne units, enabling thermal crosslinking above 100°C and uniform high char yields upon heating.

abstract: A bonding device for manufacturing a vehicle seat, in which a foam cushion member secured on an upper die is pressed against a top cover member placed on a lower die for bonding those two members together. In the upper die, provided are main and auxiliary pressing mechanisms in such a manner that the cushion member is bodily pressed by the main pressing mechanism against the top cover member and then additionally pressed by the auxiliary pressing mechanism at a local area of the cushion member where a pressure of the main pressing mechanism is not sufficiently applied. In this way, the top cover member is positively bonded to the cushion member.
problem: Ensuring complete bonding between a foam cushion and a top cover in vehicle seat manufacturing, particularly in areas where uniform pressure is insufficient.
constraint: Avoiding over-compression of the cushion while ensuring full adhesion in regions with insufficient initial pressure.
mechanism: Apply a two-stage pressure system: a primary pressure application mechanism delivers overall compressive force to join two surfaces, followed by a secondary localized pressure mechanism that targets regions where the primary pressure was insufficient to achieve complete bonding.
mechanism_raw: Two-stage pressing: a main pressing mechanism applies overall pressure to the cushion against the cover, followed by an auxiliary pressing mechanism that targets localized areas where the main pressure was inadequate.
residual_terms: ["two-stage pressure system", "primary pressure application mechanism", "secondary localized pressure mechanism"]

abstract: An improvement is provided for a retractable tip marking pen whereby the tip, in its retracted position, is enclosed in a chamber which prevents drying of the marking fluid. The chamber is provided by an elastomeric sealing member positioned within the outer sheath of the pen adjacent the lower extremity thereof. The sealing member automatically opens when the tip is pushed to its writing position, and closes when the tip is retracted to its stored position.
problem: Preventing drying of marking fluid in a retractable tip pen when the tip is not in use.
constraint: Ensuring the seal opens and closes reliably with minimal friction or wear while maintaining a tight enclosure to prevent fluid evaporation.
mechanism: Position a flexible sealing element within a protective sheath that automatically transitions between open and closed states in response to movement of a working element, creating a variable-volume enclosure that isolates the working element from environmental exposure when not in use.
mechanism_raw: An elastomeric sealing member positioned in the pen sheath automatically opens when the tip is extended to the writing position and closes when retracted, creating a sealed chamber around the tip.

abstract: A method for retreading and partially replacing the belt of a pneumatic vehicle tire, possibly accompanied by the interposition of binder layers and the use of coatings. First the replacement belt ply or plies, and then the finish-vulcanized profiled tread strip, are placed upon the tire body. A pressure treatment, possibly at an elevated temperature, is then effected. In order, along with a relatively short vulcanizing or processing time in the vulcanizing apparatus, to be able to dispense with the use of steel bandages or sleeves, the replacement belt ply or plies are vulcanized prior to placing these plies on the tire body.
problem: Reducing vulcanizing time and eliminating the need for external steel bandages during tire retreading by ensuring proper bonding of replacement belt plies to the tire body.
constraint: Balancing the pre-vulcanization step to ensure sufficient initial bonding without over-curing, which could compromise adhesion during the final vulcanization or reduce processing efficiency.
mechanism: Partially curing a replacement material before applying it to a substrate, so that the final bonding step requires reduced time and pressure while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Pre-vulcanizing the replacement belt plies before placing them on the tire body, so that the final vulcanization step requires less time and pressure, as the plies are already partially cured and structurally stable.

abstract: A shredded tobacco leaf pellet is composed of tobacco leaf shreds bound together with a nicotine-non-absorptive thermoplastic binder while retaining air permeability. The pellet is produced by mixing tobacco leaf shreds and a nicotine-non-absorptive thermoplastic binder, forming the resultant mixture into a desired shape while retaining air permeability, and then subjecting the thus-formed mixture to a heat treatment. A cigarette-like snuff is composed of at least one shredded tobacco leaf pellet of the above-described type and an outer envelope surrounding the pellet therein.
problem: Binding shredded tobacco leaf shreds into a cohesive pellet while retaining air permeability and avoiding absorption of nicotine by the binder.
constraint: Selecting a binder material that is both thermoplastic (for shaping and heat treatment) and non-absorptive (to preserve nicotine content), while ensuring the mixture retains air permeability after forming.
mechanism: Using a thermoplastic binder that does not absorb the active component to bind shredded material into a cohesive form during shaping, while preserving permeability of the final structure.
mechanism_raw: Using a nicotine-non-absorptive thermoplastic binder that binds the shreds together during heat treatment without interfering with nicotine retention, allowing the pellet to maintain structural integrity and air permeability.

abstract: A tack-in selvage forming apparatus for tacking in the end portion of a picked weft yarn to form a selvage structure in weaving a towel. The tack-in selvage forming apapratus is comprised of a tack-in needle which is controllably driven by a driving mechanism including a cylindrical grooved cam rotatable in timed relation to a main shaft of a loom. The grooved cam is formed at its periphery with generally annular shallow and deep cam grooves. The shallow cam groove is parallel with a plane perpendicular to the axis of the grooved cam, while the deep cam groove is curved relative to the same plane. A part of the shallow cam groove and a part of the deep cam groove is common and the same in depth. The shallow cam groove has a profile corresponding to a resting state of the tack-in needle, while the deep cam groove has a profile corresponding to a tack-in operational state of the tack-in needle. A cam follower drivingly connected to the tack-in needle is selectively put into the shallow and deep cam grooves. Thus, the tack-in needle is rested when the cam follower is in the shallow cam groove and operated to accomplish tack-in of a weft yarn end portion when the cam follower is in the deep cam groove.
problem: Automatically controlling the movement of a tack-in needle in a weaving loom to form a selvage structure by precisely timing its rest and operational states.
constraint: Ensuring the cam's groove profiles and rotational timing are synchronized with the loom's main shaft to achieve precise needle actuation without disrupting the weaving cycle.
mechanism: Employing a rotating cam with varying groove depths to selectively position a follower, thereby controlling the actuation state of a mechanical element in synchronization with a main drive.
mechanism_raw: Using a cylindrical grooved cam with shallow and deep annular grooves to selectively position a cam follower, which drives the tack-in needle into resting or operational states based on the cam's rotation relative to the loom's main shaft.

abstract: Surface layers of the earth contaminated with precipitates of alkaline earth metal sulfates including radium sulfate derived from subterranean waters brought to the surface of the earth, are decontaminated using an aqueous chemical composition including a polyaminopolycarboxylic acid such as ETDA or DTPA in combination with a synergist, preferably oxalate or monocarboxylic acid anion such as salicylate. The surface layers may be decontaminated in situ by applying the solvent to the earth to bring the precipitates into dissolved form after which the dissolved precipitates are leached into lower layers of the earth by percolation with water. Alternatively, the earth may be removed from its original site and decontaminated in a tank or lined pond after which the decontaminated earth may be returned to its approximate original site.
problem: Removing alkaline earth metal sulfates, including radium sulfate, from contaminated soil surfaces using a chemical composition that dissolves precipitates and facilitates their leaching.
constraint: Optimizing the chemical composition to effectively dissolve the sulfates while minimizing environmental impact, and ensuring the leaching process does not spread contamination beyond the target area.
mechanism: Applying a chelating agent combined with a synergist to dissolve contaminants, followed by percolation to leach the dissolved substances into lower layers.
mechanism_raw: Applying a polyaminopolycarboxylic acid (e.g., EDTA) combined with a synergist (e.g., oxalate or salicylate) to dissolve the sulfates, followed by percolation with water to leach the dissolved contaminants into lower soil layers.

abstract: A combined bracelet and pendant in which the major ornamental and artistic component forms a part of and is attached to a bracelet in a manner enabling it to be removed and connected to a necklace to form a pendant suspended from the necklace thereby forming an article of jewelry which can be converted from an arrangement forming a bracelet to an arrangement forming a pendant supported from a neck encircling member. The interchangeable major component of the article of jewelry includes a structure which enables it to be connected to a wrist encircling bracelet in a secure and stable manner and also enables it to be connected to a necklace in the form of a flexible member, chain or the like.
problem: Creating a modular jewelry component that can be securely and stably attached to either a bracelet or a necklace, enabling conversion between the two configurations.
constraint: Ensuring the attachment mechanism is robust enough to maintain secure connections under different mechanical stresses (e.g., wrist movement vs. pendant suspension) while allowing easy reconfiguration.
mechanism: Designing an ornamental component with two distinct attachment interfaces that mechanically engage with different support structures, allowing secure connection in multiple configurations.
mechanism_raw: Designing an interchangeable ornamental component with a dual-attachment structure that mechanically interfaces with both a wrist-encircling bracelet and a neck-encircling chain, using a connection system that ensures stability in both configurations.

abstract: A method of generating a quasi-complex hologram using incoherent light and a conoscope system comprising a birefringent crystal (30) inserted between two circular polarizers (10, 20), the method comprising the following steps: (i) recording a plurality of different conoscopic holograms of the same object without relative displacement thereof and with respective different polarization configurations; and (ii) combining the various conoscopic holograms obtained in this way in order to remove the bias and the conjugate image. The invention also relates to a device for implementing the method.
problem: Generating a quasi-complex hologram using incoherent light while eliminating bias and conjugate image artifacts.
constraint: Requires precise alignment of polarization states and birefringent crystal orientation to ensure artifact removal without relative motion of the object during recording.
mechanism: Recording multiple holograms with distinct polarization configurations without object displacement, then combining them to cancel out bias and conjugate image components through differential interference or phase cancellation.
mechanism_raw: Recording multiple conoscopic holograms with distinct polarization configurations without object displacement, then combining them to cancel out bias and conjugate image components through differential interference or phase cancellation.

abstract: This invention relates to an inflatable intelligence album including an inflatable ring formed with a check valve through which air may be blown therein to expand the inflating ring thereby enabling the inflatable ring to float on water surface and a plurality of leaves each of them completely sealed by a plastic bag with a sheet of sponge therein, whereby the children may play and read the album even in a bath tub.
reason: The invention is a product design combining buoyancy (inflatable ring) and waterproofing (sealed plastic leaves) for a specific use case (bath-time reading). No generalizable causal mechanism beyond the physical integration of these features.

abstract: A method for dispersing an oil spill on sea water, which method comprises applying to the oil spill surface an effective amount of: (i) a blend of one or more hydrophilic and one or more lipophilic surfactants so balanced that they will form microemulsions with the sea water and the oil to be dispersed; (ii) a solvent which is miscible with the oil to be dispersed and in which the blend of surfactants is substantially soluble; and (iii) from 0 to about 10 weight percent water, wherein the blend of surfactants is such that it lowers the interfacial tension between the oil to be dispersed and the sea water to less than about 250 mdynes/cm when the blend is used at a treat rate of less than about 1 to 100 by weight, based on the oil to be dispersed, wherein the solvent is a hydrocarbon solvent selected from the group consisting of No. 2 diesel fuel oil, kerosene and white oil.
problem: Dispersing oil spills on seawater efficiently at low treat rates while minimizing environmental impact.
constraint: The surfactant blend must be precisely balanced to achieve microemulsion formation at low concentrations, and the solvent must be compatible with both oil and seawater without excessive toxicity.
mechanism: Balancing hydrophilic and lipophilic surfactants to form microemulsions with oil and seawater, combined with a solvent that solubilizes the surfactant blend and reduces interfacial tension below a critical threshold, enabling spontaneous oil dispersion.
mechanism_raw: Balancing hydrophilic and lipophilic surfactants to form microemulsions with oil and seawater, combined with a solvent that solubilizes the surfactant blend and reduces interfacial tension below 250 mdynes/cm, enabling spontaneous oil dispersion.

abstract: A hydraulic control valve and sensing mechanism for controlling flow between a motor and a pump and container that includes a slide mounted in a housing bore for movement between a neutral position and two operative position. The slide has a central collar separated from end collars by slide grooves, profilings on diametric opposite sides of the slide grooves intersecting each groove. The housing bore has a pump groove supplied with pressure medium, axially opposite motor grooves connectable to motor conduits, and axially opposite the motor grooves from the pump grooves there are container grooves connectable to the container. The pressure sensing mechanism includes at least one pressure sensing orifice that is connected to the pressure to be sensed in an operative position of the slide but not being fluidly connected thereto when the slide is in its neutral position.
problem: Controlling hydraulic flow between a motor, pump, and container while enabling pressure sensing only during active operation.
constraint: The slide's geometry and groove alignment must ensure precise fluid path switching and pressure sensing activation without leakage or unintended connections during neutral or transitional states.
mechanism: A sliding valve element with grooves and profiled surfaces that selectively connect pressure medium, motor, and container conduits based on slide position, while pressure sensing orifices are fluidly connected only when the slide is in an operative position.
mechanism_raw: A sliding valve element with grooves and profiled surfaces that selectively connect pressure medium, motor, and container conduits based on slide position, while pressure sensing orifices are fluidly connected only when the slide is in an operative position.

abstract: Apparatus and method for separating intermixed particles of differing densities including a separator bowl rotatable about an axis inclined to the horizontal plane and having a base wall and a peripheral wall, and a plurality of radially-spaced chambers disposed around the peripheral wall and extending from adjacent the base wall to the upper edge of the peripheral wall, each of the chambers having chamber walls converging with one another away from the axis to a discharge port at a height intermediate the base wall and the upper edge. The bowl is rotated and a mixture of the particles is fed into the lower portion of the bowl and the mineral particle fraction discharged from the discharge port of the bowl is collected.
problem: Separating intermixed particles of differing densities using centrifugal force in a rotating system.
constraint: The bowl's inclination angle and chamber convergence rate must balance centrifugal force distribution and particle trajectory to achieve efficient separation without clogging or cross-contamination of fractions.
mechanism: Rotating an inclined bowl with radially spaced chambers that have converging walls, causing denser particles to migrate outward and lighter particles inward, with chamber geometry directing separated fractions to distinct discharge ports based on density.
mechanism_raw: Rotating an inclined bowl with radially spaced chambers that have converging walls, causing denser particles to migrate outward and lighter particles inward, with chamber geometry directing separated fractions to distinct discharge ports based on density.

abstract: A method for lengthening of normal hair includes the preparation of filaments which match the color of the normal hair, the attachment of the filaments to the normal hair by braiding the filaments with portions of normal hair, wrapping the braids with portions of filaments and applying a heat hardenable sealer to the wrapped braid. Heat is applied to the wrapped braid using an apparatus which includes a pair of tip members which are adapted for mounting on the arms of a conventional heated curling iron. The tip members include pointed portions and opposing flat surfaces which facilitate the application of heat to limited and selected areas.
problem: How to permanently and securely attach extension filaments to normal hair while matching hair color and minimizing thermal damage to surrounding hair
constraint: Heat must be applied selectively to avoid damaging surrounding hair tissue, while the braiding and wrapping must provide sufficient mechanical interlock for the sealer to create a durable bond that withstands normal hair handling
mechanism: Create a mechanical interlock between extension filaments and natural hair through braiding and wrapping, then apply a heat-activated bonding agent, using selectively shaped thermal applicators that contact only limited areas to form localized bonds exclusively where the mechanical interlock and bonding agent are present, thereby minimizing thermal exposure to surrounding tissue
mechanism_raw: Combining mechanical interweaving (braiding filaments with hair strands) with additional wrapping and a heat-activated sealer, then using shaped heat applicators with pointed and flat surfaces to selectively apply heat to limited and selected areas, creating localized bonds only where the sealer and mechanical interlock are present

abstract: A centrifugal separator for extracting heavy metals from a slurry comprises a centrifuge bowl having an inwardly facing surface over which the slurry runs. A dam at a discharge end of the surface forms a shallow layer of particles which separate preferentially the heavy metals. The surface includes a portion formed by a plurality of annular membrane portions spaced axially and separated by radial rings extending from the surface to a supporting metal bowl. The membranes are deflated or retracted to gradually form annular cups for receiving the separated metals. The membranes are then inflated to discharge the collected materials while the feed is temporarily halted and the bowl continues to rotate.
problem: How to separate heavy metals from a slurry using centrifugal force and efficiently collect and discharge the separated materials without interrupting the separation process
constraint: The membrane geometry must transition between collection (deflated) and discharge (inflated) states without stopping bowl rotation, and the feed must be temporarily halted during discharge to prevent remixing of separated materials
mechanism: Use a rotating separation surface with dynamically reconfigurable geometry — selectively deflating and inflating annular chambers along the surface to transition between forming collection regions that capture separated materials and discharging those materials, while temporarily halting feed flow during discharge to prevent remixing of separated components
mechanism_raw: Using inflatable/deflatable annular membranes spaced along the centrifuge bowl surface to dynamically reconfigure the geometry of the separation surface — deflating the membranes gradually forms annular collection cups that capture separated heavy metals, then inflating the membranes discharges the collected materials while the bowl continues to rotate

abstract: A pop-up landscape light has a cylindrical housing adapted for mounting below the surface of the ground in an outdoor environment. A light compartment is mounted for axial extension and retraction through an open top end of the housing to provide selective illumination. In a first embodiment of the present invention, a lead screw mechanism is utilized to extend and retract the light compartment from within the housing. In a second embodiment, a telescopic extensible member is connected to the light compartment and is actuated by winding or unwinding a coil of a flexible material driven by a motor through a bevel gear arrangement. In a third embodiment, a motorized swing arm mechanism is operative to rotate the light compartment through a predetermined angular increment, into and out of the housing, to provide selective illumination.
reason: The patent describes three standard mechanical actuation approaches (lead screw, telescoping coil, swing arm) for extending/retracting a light fixture. These are conventional mechanical engineering solutions without a novel causal relationship or underlying principle that transfers to other fields.

abstract: For detachable mounting onto a storage system including a pair of rodlike mounting elements mounted onto a common base and lying along an axis, a loose leaf holder comprising a planar member and apparatus associated with an edge of the planar member for detachably mounting the planar member onto the rodlike mounting elements by applying to the planar member a force having a component at right angles to the axis.
reason: The patent describes a very abstract and generic mounting concept — applying a force perpendicular to rod-like mounting elements to detachably secure a planar member. No specific novel mechanism or causal relationship is described beyond basic mechanical interference/friction principles.

abstract: Described are 2-methyl-1-nitrilo- or 2-methyl-1-hydroxylamino-3-(methoxyphenyl) propanes defined according to the generic structure: ##STR1## wherein R.sub.1 is selected from the group consisting of: (i) cyanide having the structure: ##STR2## (ii) hydroxylaminomethyl having the structure: uses thereof in augmenting or enhancing the aroma of perfume compositions, colognes and perfumed articles including but not limited to bleach compositions, solid or liquid anionic, cationic, nonionic or zwitterionic detergents, perfumed polymers, fabric softener compositions, fabric softener articles, cosmetic powders and hair preparations. Also described are processes for preparing such 2-methyl-1-nitrillo- or 2-methyl-1-hydroxylamino-3-(methoxyphenyl) propanes by means of reacting a methoxy benzyl halide with ethyl cyanide in the presence of a basic catalyst such as sodamide.
reason: The patent describes specific chemical compounds with particular molecular structures for aroma enhancement and their synthesis method. This is a compound-specific chemical discovery rather than a generalizable problem-solving mechanism that transfers across fields.

abstract: A fluid jet shredder apparatus includes a conveyor for conveying a stream of material to be shredded. The conveyor has openings formed therein. A shredding station in position adjacent the conveyor and includes a fluid jet cutting nozzle directing a high pressure jet of fluid onto the stream of material. As a result, portions of the material are separated from the stream of material. The separated portions of material pass through the openings in the conveyor. A subsequent shredding station can be positioned downstream of the initial shredding station for directing a second and higher pressure jet of fluid onto the stream of material. The subsequent shredding station can therefore shred material which the initial, relatively lower pressure fluid jet failed to shred from the stream. Sequential shredding stations of incrementally increased pressure can progressively shred material of increased hardness from the stream. The fluid jets can selectively include an abrasive material.
problem: Shredding material of varying hardness from a continuous stream in a single processing line
constraint: Pressure must be incrementally increased across stations to match material hardness, and the conveyor openings must be sized to allow separated portions to pass through while still supporting the remaining material stream
mechanism: Sequential stations apply progressively increasing energy to process materials of increasing hardness, where each station handles material that prior lower-energy stations could not separate, while a conveyor with sized apertures allows separated portions to pass through and be removed from further processing
mechanism_raw: Sequential stations apply incrementally increasing fluid jet pressure, where each station processes progressively harder material that previous lower-pressure stations could not separate, while a perforated conveyor allows already-separated portions to fall through and be removed from further processing

abstract: A method is disclosed for repositioning an adsorbate atom or molecule on a substrate surface by moving the tip of a STM to a position adjacent the atom to be moved and subsequently increasing the attraction between the tip and atom by moving the tip closer to the substrate, and then, while the atom remains bound to the surface, moving the tip laterally to drag the atom to a desired position on the surface. The tip is then moved away from the substrate, reducing the attraction between the atom and tip and leaving the atom bound at the desired position. The atom may be repositioned in close proximity to an atom of the same or another type on the same or a different substrate to create a desired multi-atom structure or synthesize a molecule. Atoms may also be repositioned to write indicia on a storage medium by dragging atoms into the desired information bearing pattern, for example, by dragging selected atoms out of a respective one of a plurality of parallel atom rows using the tip of a STM to thereby write indicia at locations denoted by the removed atoms.
problem: Precisely repositioning individual atoms or molecules on a substrate surface to create desired structures or patterns
constraint: The target must remain bound to the surface during lateral movement, and the attractive force must be precisely controlled for both pickup and release without dislodging the atom prematurely
mechanism: Controlled temporary adhesion using a manipulator: increasing attractive force to engage the target, moving the manipulator laterally while the target remains bound to the surface, then decreasing attractive force to release the target at the desired position
mechanism_raw: Controlled temporary adhesion using a manipulator tip: increasing attractive force to engage the target atom, moving the manipulator laterally while the target remains bound to the surface (dragging it to a new location), then decreasing attractive force to release the target at the desired position

abstract: A hide skiving machine adapted to skive a hide in one pass constituted by a frame which supports, at its sides, a rotatable support cylinder upon which the hide is fed and is held in place by a slidable presser roller. A lower oscillating frame having a rotating lower blade cylinder and an upper oscillating frame having a rotating upper blade cylinder are furthermore provided which skive the hide. The oscillating frames are independently movable between a raised non-working position and a lowered working position by respective actuators. Each blade cylinder is provided with a sharpening assembly which maintains the blade sharpness for more effective skiving. An adjustable, flexible front shield and a feed table are furthermore provided. The oscillating frames which support the blade cylinders are also provided with play recovery elements which help maintain the position of the blade cylinders with respect to the hide. The support cylinder can also be provided with supporting elements which allow for the inclination of the axis of the support cylinder relative to the axes of the blade cylinders, thereby providing more effective sharing of hides with variable thicknesses.
problem: Skiving hides of variable thickness in a single pass while maintaining cutting effectiveness and blade sharpness
constraint: The oscillating frames must be independently movable between working and non-working positions, and the blade cylinders must maintain both sharpness and positional accuracy despite variable material thickness and oscillation forces
mechanism: Independent mechanical compliance through resilient elements that maintain blade position relative to the material despite thickness variations, combined with adjustable geometric alignment between support and blade elements to accommodate thickness differences across the material width
mechanism_raw: Independent mechanical compliance through play recovery elements that maintain blade cylinder position relative to the hide despite thickness variations, combined with adjustable geometric alignment (inclination) between the support cylinder and blade cylinders to accommodate thickness differences across the material width

abstract: A process and apparatus for rapidly filling a pressure vessel such as a fuel storage tank with highly pressurized gas by initially inserting into the tank, a measured quantity of liquefied natural gas (LNG) or some other type of cryogenic liquid and permitting the temperature of the liquid to rise within the tank to vaporize it into a gas under a pressure which at least approaches the design working pressure of the tank. The storage tank maintains the gas under sufficiently high pressure that automotive fuel tanks or other small tanks can be rapidly filled from the storage tank without compressors due to the high internal pressure of the storage tank.
problem: Rapidly filling a pressure vessel with high-pressure gas without using mechanical compressors
constraint: The amount of cryogenic liquid must be precisely measured to achieve the target pressure, and the vaporization process must reach sufficient pressure to enable rapid transfer without additional mechanical compression
mechanism: Introducing a measured quantity of phase-change material into the vessel and allowing it to vaporize, where the vaporization pressure naturally approaches the design working pressure, creating a high-pressure gas reservoir that enables rapid filling of downstream vessels through natural phase-change pressure generation
mechanism_raw: Introducing a measured quantity of cryogenic liquid into the vessel and allowing it to vaporize, where the vaporization pressure naturally approaches the design working pressure, creating a high-pressure gas reservoir that enables rapid filling of downstream vessels through natural phase-change pressure generation

abstract: A chewing gum product having a core portion including chewable gum base, sweetener and flavoring. The core portion has deposited on its surface a rolling compound including a powdered ingredient selected from the group consisting of sucrose, mannitol, starch, calcium carbonate, talc, lactitol, palatinit, lactose, and combinstions thereof. The rolling compound further includes between about 0.1 and about 2.5 weight percent of a liquid flavor. The rolling compound is substantially free of anti-caking agents and flow agents.
problem: Creating a chewing gum product with controlled surface flavor delivery and release
constraint: The liquid flavor content must be between 0.1 and 2.5 weight percent to ensure proper integration without excess migration, and the coating must be substantially free of anti-caking agents and flow agents that would prevent direct liquid-powder integration
mechanism: Depositing a powder coating (without anti-caking agents) onto a core, where a precisely controlled amount of liquid flavor directly integrates with the powder matrix, creating a surface layer that releases flavor in a controlled manner as the powder dissolves or interacts with moisture
mechanism_raw: Depositing a powder coating (without anti-caking agents) onto a gum core, where a precisely controlled amount of liquid flavor directly integrates with the powder matrix, creating a surface layer that releases flavor in a controlled manner as the powder dissolves or interacts with moisture

abstract: A small watercraft embodying an improved exhaust system that is substantially completely watercooled by a cooling jacket. The exhaust system includes an elastic joint that is also completely surrounded by the cooling jacket so as to insure adequate cooling under all running conditions. A damming arrangement is incorporated so as to insure that all of the exhaust portions being cooled will be completely encircled with cooling water even when low amounts of water are being circulated and a drain system is also provided so as to insure that the cooling jackets will be drained when the watercraft is removed from a body of water.
problem: Ensuring adequate cooling of exhaust components in a watercraft under all running conditions, including low water circulation.
constraint: Balancing complete cooling coverage with the need to drain water to prevent stagnation or damage when not in use.
mechanism: A flow control element within a fluid circuit directs coolant to fully surround target surfaces even at low flow rates, while a drainage pathway removes residual fluid when the system is inactive to prevent stagnation.
mechanism_raw: A damming arrangement within the cooling jacket forces cooling water to fully encircle exhaust portions even at low flow rates, while a drain system removes residual water when the watercraft is removed from water.

abstract: A support structure for a vertically arranged combination household appliance, more particularly a front loading dryer assembly arranged above a top loading washer assembly, includes vertical main support members, horizontal members and other members. The structure adequately supports both appliance assemblies of the combination appliance during transportation and usage, provides improved operating performance during off balance washer spin conditions or dryer tumbling, and maintains unitary appliance characteristics by being an integral part of the combination appliance design and by being located entirely interior to the appliance cabinetry.
reason: The mechanism is a standard structural engineering approach (internal supports for dynamic loads) without a novel causal principle beyond conventional design integration.

abstract: A system for sorting lumber using a scanning camera that generates separate red, green and in some cases blue outputs to scan selected length increments along the surface of a piece of lumber and such data collected for each color is each separately histogrammed to produce a frequency distribution of color intensity. The data is analyzed to determine the mean values for each color in the selected lengths and the lengths characterized based on these mean values into specific colors. The lumber pieces may be automatically severed into pieces having significant differences in color and the pieces of significantly different colors may be automatically collected in different groupings. In an alternative arrangement the histogram for selected color is analyzed to determine the frequency distribution and degree of frequency variability to determine if it is to be classified as vertical or flat grained. The lumber pieces may be automatically severed into pieces whenever their classification changes between flat and vertical grain and the pieces of flat grain may be automatically collected separate from those of vertical grain.
problem: Automatically classifying and sorting lumber based on color and grain orientation without manual intervention.
