constraint: Accurately distinguishing subtle color/grain differences while maintaining throughput during high-speed sorting operations.
mechanism: Multi-channel sensors capture visual data from a moving surface, statistical analysis of channel distributions classifies segments based on pattern variations, and actuation occurs when classification transitions are detected.
mechanism_raw: Scanning with RGB outputs, generating histograms for each color channel, and analyzing statistical distributions (mean values or frequency variability) to classify segments, triggering automatic severing when classifications change.

abstract: The structure of the present invention comprises a self-cooling container in which a segregating wall is used to divide the container into a beverage chamber and a cooling chamber, the latter having a reaction chamber mounted therein, which in a preferred embodiment is of an elongated cylindrical shape. The reaction chamber cylinder of the present invention provides an inverted funnel-shaped bottom surface for receiving the flow of beverage from the beverage chamber portion of the container through a feed-through at the bottom of the segregating wall thereof. The funnel leads to a flow tube which is positioned in axial alignment with the cylinder, preferably through the center thereof and defining an inner wall of the reaction chamber. The reaction chamber houses a combination of chemical materials separated by a readily broken sealing device from a selected volume of distilled water, which rfeleased into the chemical constituents, initiates an endothermic reaction which extracts heat from the beverage.
problem: Cooling a beverage on demand using a self-contained system without external power or ice.
constraint: Initiating the reaction reliably on demand while ensuring efficient heat transfer between the beverage and reaction chamber.
mechanism: A segregated reaction chamber contains separated reactants isolated by a breakable barrier; activation releases the barrier, initiating an endothermic reaction that transfers heat via conductive flow through aligned thermal pathways.
mechanism_raw: A segregated reaction chamber houses chemicals separated from water by a breakable seal; when activated, the released water triggers an endothermic reaction that extracts heat from the beverage via conductive flow through an aligned funnel and tube.
residual_terms: ["segregated reaction chamber", "breakable barrier", "endothermic reaction", "conductive flow", "thermal pathways"]

abstract: Disclosed is a device for positioning an injector in its circumferential direction so that a plurality of nozzle holes formed at one end of the injector connected at the other end to a delivery pipe in an internal combustion engine can be accurately directed toward corresponding intake ports respectively. The device comprises a clip non-rotatably mounted on part of the delivery pipe, and the clip includes retaining portions extending along diametrically opposite wall portions of the injector and having confronting projections adapted to engage mating holes bored in the diametrically opposite wall portions respectively of the injector thereby positioning the injector.
problem: Precisely aligning an injector's nozzle holes with corresponding intake ports in an internal combustion engine to ensure optimal fuel delivery.
constraint: Achieving accurate alignment without rotational slippage while accommodating manufacturing tolerances in the injector and pipe components.
mechanism: A non-rotatable mechanical constraint with engagement features fixes angular orientation between two components by interfacing with complementary geometric features on each, preventing rotational slippage while accommodating dimensional variations.
mechanism_raw: A non-rotatable clip with diametrically opposed projections engages matching holes on the injector, mechanically fixing its angular orientation relative to the delivery pipe.
residual_terms: ["non-rotatable mechanical constraint", "engagement features", "complementary geometric features", "dimensional variations"]

abstract: A chip component handling and loading system for orienting and transporting a plurality of generally rectangular chip components includes a storage and feed location which, by means of vibratory action, randomly shakes out the chip components into or onto a series of twenty-five substantially parallel, generally rectangular channels. These channels are sized and arranged to receive the chip components in only one proper orientation. Any chip component which is not properly oriented either will not fit in the channel, or will fit in the channel as to its width and not height and downstream from the entry into the channels is a brush-back station where any improperly oriented chip component is either brushed away from the top surface of the channels or is brushed into a proper orientation. The channel dimensions represent the most likely orientation for the randomly vibrated chip components though not the necessary orientation for electrical testing of the components and loading these components into the clear plastic strip which will ultimately be used by the circuit board manufacturer. Consequently, a roll-over insert block is provided so as to transform the orientation of the chip components as initially loaded into the channels into a different orientation which corresponds to that required for electrical testing and component loading.
problem: Orienting and transporting rectangular chip components into a single proper orientation for electrical testing and loading, despite random initial placement.
constraint: Channel dimensions favor the most likely orientation from vibration but not the necessary orientation for testing, requiring a secondary mechanical adjustment step.
mechanism: Apply oscillatory agitation to randomly oriented objects within parallel constrained pathways sized to passively accept only one orientation. Use a secondary mechanical element to remove or reorient misaligned objects, and employ a physical transformation interface to convert the accepted orientation into a target orientation required by downstream processes.
mechanism_raw: Vibratory action randomly agitates components into parallel channels sized to accept only one orientation. Misoriented components are mechanically brushed away or reoriented, and a roll-over insert block physically transforms the orientation to match downstream requirements.

abstract: A method of preparing high integrity natural nitrogenous granules for agriculture by heating natural nitrogenous materials under alkaline conditions until the materials develop adhesive properties, forming the materials into granules by mechanical means, and heating the natural nitrogenous granules until they harden; and the compositions formed by this method. The granules for agriculture include natural fertilizers, secondary nutrients, micronutrients, and natural animal feed protein supplements. The method also provides natural based plant food and animal feed supplement granules containing natural or synthetic additive substances which are useful in agriculture. The natural materials used in the method include poultry waste, poultry feather meal, hair meal, seafood meal, blood meal, bone meal, soybean meal, food waste, and grain by-products. The method provides natural nitrogenous granules which are free of disagreeable odor by admixing reactive aldehyde compounds with the natural nitrogenous materials prior to granule formation.
problem: Creating high-integrity granules from natural nitrogenous materials while eliminating disagreeable odors during processing.
constraint: Balancing chemical treatment (alkaline heating) and odor control (aldehyde addition) without degrading the natural material properties or introducing synthetic contaminants.
mechanism: Subject natural materials to chemical treatment under elevated temperature and alkaline conditions to induce adhesive properties, enabling mechanical consolidation into granules. Apply a subsequent hardening step to stabilize the formed granules. Introduce reactive agents prior to consolidation to neutralize volatile compounds that cause undesirable odors.
mechanism_raw: Heating materials under alkaline conditions induces adhesive properties, enabling mechanical granule formation. Subsequent hardening stabilizes the granules. Reactive aldehydes are admixed prior to granulation to neutralize odor-causing compounds.

abstract: A laminated wood panel manufacturing device is provided for use with daylight presses. A pressure strip is arranged in a longitudinal direction of the press. Parallel upper and lower lids are attached to the pressure strip and extend in a transverse direction toward the press. The lids are vertically adjustable by means of adjusting screws. The pressure strip assembly is moved in a transverse direction of the press so that, during pressing, the upper and lower lids abut upper and lower board layers of a laminated stack to press the board layers together in a transverse direction of the press.
problem: Applying uniform transverse pressure to laminated board layers in a daylight press while accommodating variable layer thicknesses.
constraint: Maintaining consistent pressure application across variable layer thicknesses while enabling transverse movement of the pressure strip.
mechanism: Deploy a longitudinally extending pressure-applying element with independently adjustable contact surfaces at opposing ends. Move the pressure element transversely across layered materials while the adjustable contact surfaces maintain consistent pressure application despite variations in layer thickness.
mechanism_raw: A longitudinally arranged pressure strip with vertically adjustable upper and lower lids is moved transversely to press against board layers. The adjustable lids ensure contact pressure is maintained across varying layer dimensions during pressing.
residual_terms: ["longitudinally extending pressure-applying element", "adjustable contact surfaces", "transverse movement"]

abstract: This invention relates to a suspension apparatus for control devices which can be assembled from a connection flange or connection rotary joint, support beam sections, elbow joints, or intermediate joints which can be connected with a wall or the body of a machine, and a coupling unit which can be connected to the control device. The support beam section comprises an essentially U-shaped base profile section and a cover profile section closing the same. The base profile section is divided, by means of a separating bar parallel to its crossbar, into a support part constructed as a closed hollow profile and an open U-shaped mounting part opposed to the bar. The connection bars, which proceed in a longitudinal direction in the support part and in the mounting part, are integrally formed with screw mountings. The intermediate joint comprises two joint parts which can be bolted directly to the front sides of the base profile section acting on one another, without impairing the positioning of the connection lines and the guiding of the same with the intermediate joint.
problem: Assembling modular suspension components for control devices without disrupting existing positioning or guiding of connection lines.
constraint: Ensuring bolted connections between joint parts do not interfere with the positioning or guiding of connection lines within the profile.
mechanism: Form a base structure with a closed support region and an open mounting region separated by an internal barrier. Integrate connection elements with fastening points that allow bolted attachment of intermediate components directly to the base structure, preserving the alignment and guidance of internal routing lines within the support region.
mechanism_raw: A U-shaped base profile is divided into a closed hollow support part and an open mounting part by a separating bar. Integrally formed connection bars with screw mountings allow bolted attachment of intermediate joints directly to the base profile, preserving alignment of internal lines.
residual_terms: ["closed support region", "open mounting region", "internal barrier", "bolted attachment", "internal routing lines"]

abstract: The present invention is drawn to a combination microwave/infrared oven heating a box-like structure in which a plurality of chambers are defined. A microwave heating source is associated with at least one of the chambers for generating microwaves therein, an infrared short-wave radiation source is associated with at least another one of the chambers for generating short-wave infrared radiation therein, and a medium-wave infrared radiation source is associated with at least yet another one of the chambers for generating medium-wave infrared radiation therein. A rotary conveyor is rotatably supported in the oven within the box-like structure and conveys foodstuffs in the oven successively through the chambers. An electronic circuit including a central logic system controls the operation of the rotary conveyor to set the time periods during the foodstuffs conveyed in the oven remain in respective ones of the chambers. The central logic system may also control the operation of the microwave heating source, the short-wave infrared radiation source and the medium-wave infrared radiation source.
problem: Efficiently heating foodstuffs using multiple heating modalities (microwave, short-wave IR, medium-wave IR) in a single integrated system.
constraint: Coordinating variable heating durations and modalities across chambers while maintaining continuous conveyor movement and preventing cross-contamination of heating methods.
mechanism: Transport objects sequentially through discrete processing zones using a moving carrier system. Associate each zone with a distinct energy application source. Coordinate carrier timing and source activation through a central control system to optimize energy delivery profiles for each processing modality while preventing overlap of treatment methods.
mechanism_raw: A rotary conveyor moves foodstuffs sequentially through discrete chambers, each associated with a specific heating source. A central logic system controls conveyor timing and source activation to optimize heating profiles for each modality.
residual_terms: ["moving carrier system", "discrete processing zones", "energy application source", "central control system", "energy delivery profiles"]

abstract: According to the present invention there is provided an article of headwear, namely a hat, which has an opened position and a closed position. The hat has a forwardly projecting brim and a domed portion which extends rearwardly from the brim. The domed portion has a lower opening to accommodate a wearer's head therein. The domed portion includes a rear stationary portion and a foldable top portion. The foldable top portion is foldable downwardly and forwardly along first and second fold axes to form a top opening in the domed portion. In this manner, the article may assume the opened position. In a further embodiment, the foldable top portion may be releasably secured in the folded position, and in the unfolded or closed position may be releasably secured to the rear stationary portion.
problem: A hat needs to transition between an open configuration (for ventilation or compact storage) and a closed configuration (for normal wear), while maintaining structural integrity and shape in both states.
constraint: The folding must occur along precisely defined axes to preserve the domed structure's integrity, and the securing mechanism must reliably hold both positions without unintended deployment.
mechanism: A flexible portion is connected to a rigid portion through two defined fold axes. Controlled folding along these axes transforms the structure between a domed closed state and an open state with a top opening. Releasable latching mechanisms independently secure the flexible portion in either the folded or unfolded position, enabling stable state transitions while preserving structural integrity in both configurations.
mechanism_raw: A foldable top portion is connected to a stationary rear portion via two fold axes. Folding the top portion downwardly and forwardly along these axes creates a controlled transformation from a domed closed shape to an open configuration with a top opening. Releasable securing mechanisms hold the foldable portion in either the folded (open) or unfolded (closed) position, enabling stable state transitions.

abstract: A cover unit for covering an external face of a machine tool. The cover unit is formed with small opening for allowing a workpiece to pass therethrough. The cover unit is also formed with a large opening for facilitating maintenance to the machine tool. The small opening is selectively closed by a first closure means to avoid scattering of the cutting chips and machining liquid toward outside during machining to the workpiece. The large opening is selectively closed by a second closure means during machining to the workpiece.
problem: A machine tool cover must allow a workpiece to pass through and provide maintenance access, while preventing scattering of cutting chips and machining liquid during operation.
constraint: Each closure must operate independently and be selectively openable for its intended purpose (workpiece passage or maintenance) while both are reliably closed during machining to prevent chip and liquid escape.
mechanism: Two openings of different sizes are each provided with an independent closure mechanism. The smaller opening permits workpiece passage and is closed during machining to contain debris. The larger opening permits maintenance access and is also closed during machining. The dual independent closures enable selective access for different operational modes while maintaining environmental containment during cutting operations.
mechanism_raw: Two openings of different sizes are provided, each with an independent closure mechanism. The small opening allows workpiece passage and is closed during machining to contain debris. The large opening allows maintenance access and is also closed during machining. The dual independent closures enable selective access for different operational modes while maintaining environmental containment during cutting operations.

abstract: An edge tracing sewing machine includes a reciprocable needle bar having a needle at a lower end, a needle position sensor for detecting needle-down position, a presser bar having a presser foot at a lower end, a presser foot switch for detecting an upper position of the presser foot, a vertical feed driving device, a forward feed driving device for feeding a work fabric in a sewing direction, a lateral feed driving device for feeding the work fabric in a lateral direction perpendicular to the sewing direction, a fabric-edge position detector, a tracing width setting device, and a control device. The control device controls the lateral feed driving device based on signals from the fabric-edge position detector and the tracing width setting device, so as to carry out a tracing sewing with the tracing width set by the tracing width setting device. The control device nullifies the forward feed driving device and controls the lateral feed device based on signals from the needle position sensor and the presser foot switch. Accordingly, the difference between a distance from an edge of a work fabric to the needle and the tracing width set by the tracing width setting device is reduced after the work fabric is rotated in a vicinity of a corner of the work fabric to change the sewing direction.
problem: When edge-tracing a fabric with a set tracing width, the fabric must be rotated at corners to change direction, and positional error between the actual fabric edge and the desired tracing width must be corrected after rotation.
constraint: Forward feed must be fully nullified during corner rotation to allow pure lateral correction, and the correction must be synchronized with needle and presser foot positions to avoid fabric damage or stitching errors.
mechanism: During corner rotation, forward feed is fully nullified and lateral feed is driven by signals from a needle position sensor and a presser foot switch. This coordinated sensor-based control reduces the difference between the actual edge-to-needle distance and the set tracing width after the fabric is rotated, effectively correcting positional error through synchronized lateral adjustment while forward motion is paused.
mechanism_raw: During corner rotation, the control device nullifies forward feed and uses lateral feed driven by signals from a needle position sensor and a presser foot switch. This coordinated sensor-based control reduces the difference between the actual edge-to-needle distance and the set tracing width after the fabric is rotated, effectively correcting positional error through synchronized lateral adjustment while forward motion is paused.
residual_terms: ["forward feed", "lateral feed", "needle position sensor", "presser foot switch"]

abstract: A process for the dyeing or printing of leather with anionic metal complex dyes wherein the metal complex dyes are metal complexes of metallizable monoazo dyes or metallizable monoazomethine dyes or both metallizable monoazo and monoazo methine dyes and before the application of the dye or after the application of the dye or both before and after the application of the dye the leather is treated with a product (P) or a mixture of products (P) or an acid addition product thereof, product (P) being a polymer obtainable by reaction of PA0 (.alpha.) a mono-functional or poly-functional amine containing one or more amino groups of the group consisting of primary, secondary and tertiary amino groups with PA0 (.beta.) cyanamide, dicyanodiamide, guanidine or biguanide or a mixture in which up to 50 mole percent of the cyanamide, dicyanodiamide, guanidine or biguanide are replaced by a di-carboxylic acid or a mono- or diester thereof with cleavage of ammonia or a further reaction product thereof with reactant PA0 (.gamma.) selected from the group consisting of: PA1 (1) (.gamma..sub.1) a N-methylol derivative of a urea, a melamine, a guanamine, a triazine, a urone, a urethane or an acid amide, PA1 (2) (.gamma..sub.2) an epihalohydrin or an epihalohydrin precursor, PA1 (3) (.gamma..sub.3) formaldehyde or a formaldehyde yielding product, PA1 (4) (.gamma..sub.2) followed by (.gamma..sub.1) and PA1 (5) (.gamma..sub.3) followed by (.gamma..sub.1).
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical formulation and reaction sequence for a polymer treatment product (P) used in leather dyeing. While it details the reactants and their ratios, it does not describe a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a problem — it is essentially a chemical recipe specifying particular amines, cyanamides, and cross-linking agents. The underlying principle of substrate pretreatment is too chemistry-specific to transfer as a problem-solving mechanism to other fields.

abstract: A process and apparatus for fabricating expandable honeycomb materials disclosed. The continuous length of material is folded along opposite side portions thereof into a generally flat tubular form having upper lower layers. Adhesive is then applied along the length of the continuous material by first heating the material, applying the adhesive in a liquid state to the heated material, and then cooling the material to solidify the adhesive. The folded tubular material with solidified adhesive lines thereon is then wound about a rack in such a manner that the tubular material is deposited in a plurality of continuous layers one on another with the lines of adhesive being disposed between adjacent layers. The wound layers are then radially cut and placed in a vertically aligned stack while they are removed the rack. The vertically stacked layers are then heated to a temperature sufficient to activate the lines of adhesive and bond the layers together. Finally, the stacked tubular material is cooled to form a unitary stack of tubular, expandable honeycomb material. A device for performing the process as described above is also disclosed.
problem: Expandable honeycomb structures need to be fabricated from a continuous length of material in a controlled, scalable process that produces a unitary bonded stack.
constraint: The adhesive must be applied and solidified before winding to maintain line integrity during layer deposition, and the final activation heating must occur after stacking to ensure all interlayer adhesive lines are simultaneously activated for uniform bonding.
mechanism: The continuous material is folded into a tubular form, then adhesive lines are applied in a controlled sequence (heating, applying liquid adhesive, cooling to solidify). The tubular material with solidified adhesive lines is wound into multiple layers with adhesive lines between adjacent layers. The wound layers are radially cut and vertically stacked, then heated to activate the adhesive and bond all layers simultaneously, followed by cooling to form a unitary stack.
mechanism_raw: The continuous material is folded into a tubular form, then adhesive lines are applied in a controlled sequence (heating, applying liquid adhesive, cooling to solidify). The tubular material with solidified adhesive lines is wound into multiple layers with adhesive lines between adjacent layers. The wound layers are radially cut and vertically stacked, then heated to activate the adhesive and bond all layers simultaneously, followed by cooling to form a unitary stack.

abstract: A mixed-solid solution tri-metallic oxide/sulfide catalyst having the formula: EQU M.sub.I O.sub.a S.sub.b .multidot.M.sub.II O.sub.c M.sub.III O.sub.d wherein M.sub.I is vanadium, neodymium, tantalum, chromium, molybdenum, tungsten, and mixtures thereof; O is oxygen; S is sulfur; a is selected from zero and a number up to a positive real number representing the stoichiometric requirement, and b is selected from zero and a number up to a positive real number representing the stoichiometric requirement, provided one of a and b is a positive real number; M.sub.II is titanium, zirconium, hafnium, and mixtures thereof; c is a positive real number up to the stoichiometric requirement; M.sub.III is lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, cesium, francium, beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium, radium, zinc, cadmium, mercury, scandium, yttrium, lanthanum, actinium, and mixtures thereof; and d is a positive real number up to the stoichiometric requirement; and wherein M.sub.I O.sub.a S.sub.b is mixed in a solid solution of M.sub.II O.sub.c M.sub.III O.sub.d. A process for production of the above catalyst and its use in hydroforming reactions is taught.
problem: Improving catalytic efficiency in hydroforming reactions through optimized material composition.
constraint: The stoichiometric ratios of oxygen and sulfur (a, b) and the proportions of the three metal groups must be carefully controlled to maintain the solid solution structure while maximizing catalytic performance.
mechanism: A multi-component solid solution is formed by combining three distinct metallic phases in controlled stoichiometric ratios. The synergistic interaction between the phases balances electronic and structural properties across the mixed composition, enhancing catalytic activity through optimized charge transfer and surface reactivity.
mechanism_raw: A mixed-solid solution of tri-metallic oxide/sulfide components (M_I, M_II, M_III) is formed, where the synergistic interaction between the metals in the solid solution enhances catalytic activity by balancing electronic and structural properties across the mixed phases.

abstract: Low density silicon nitride ceramics having improved bending an specific strengths over known silicon nitride ceramics derived from silicon nitride powder and polysilazane precursors are prepared by (A) intimately mixing about 50-80% by weight of silicon nitride powder with about 15-50% by weight of perceramic polysilazane binder, (B) pulverizing the mixture to form particles having a particle size smaller than 105 micrometers, (C) separating from those particles any particles having a particle size larger than about 105 micrometers, (D) molding the resultant composition having a particle size not larger than about 105 micrometers, and (E) pyrolyzing the molded composition in an inert atmosphere to a temperature of about 1200.degree.-1450.degree. C.; said preceramic binder being at least one polysilazane prepared by reacting an organodihalosilane with ammonia, treating the ammonolysis product with a basic catalyst which is capable of deprotonating an NH group that is adjacent to an SiH group, and quenching the resultant product with an electrophilic quenching reagent.
problem: Achieving low-density silicon nitride ceramics with improved mechanical strength and specific strength.
constraint: The particle size of the mixture must be controlled (≤105 micrometers) and the pyrolysis temperature (1200–1450°C) must be precisely maintained to ensure proper binder decomposition and ceramic densification without structural defects.
mechanism: A decomposable precursor material is uniformly dispersed within a ceramic powder matrix. During high-temperature processing, the precursor undergoes chemical transformation and integrates into the ceramic structure, forming a dense, reinforced microstructure that improves mechanical properties through enhanced interparticle bonding.
mechanism_raw: A preceramic polysilazane binder is intimately mixed with silicon nitride powder, then pyrolyzed at high temperature. The binder decomposes and integrates into the ceramic matrix, forming a dense, reinforced microstructure that enhances mechanical properties compared to pure silicon nitride.

abstract: A vacuum toilet system comprises a waste-receiving bowl defining an interior space for receiving waste material. A sewer pipe defines an interior space that can be placed at a pressure that is lower than that in the interior space of the waste-receiving bowl, and a discharge valve is connected between the outlet of the waste-receiving bowl and the sewer pipe for controlling passage of material between the waste-receiving bowl and the sewer pipe. A rinse liquid valve controls supply of rinse liquid to the waste-receiving bowl. A controller is responsive to a user stimulus to open and close the discharge valve in accordance with a predetermined cycle, and to open the rinse liquid valve during at least the interval during which the discharge valve is being opened.
problem: Efficiently removing waste material from a vacuum toilet bowl while minimizing clogging and optimizing rinse liquid usage.
constraint: The timing of valve actuation must balance sufficient discharge duration for waste removal with minimal rinse liquid consumption, while maintaining pressure differentials between the bowl and sewer pipe.
mechanism: A control system coordinates the sequential actuation of two fluid pathways: a discharge pathway and a rinse pathway. The timing of actuation ensures that rinse fluid flows concurrently with waste discharge, creating a pressure-driven flushing action that removes residual material while minimizing fluid consumption through predetermined cycle durations.
mechanism_raw: A controller synchronizes the opening of the discharge valve (to a low-pressure sewer pipe) with the rinse liquid valve, ensuring that rinse liquid flows during discharge to flush residual waste through the system. The predetermined cycle ensures timed coordination between valve operations.

abstract: A hydrobrush of the type incorporating a small Pelton turbine actuated by a water jet at the pressure of the water main and which causes the rotation of a brush. The impeller (4) of said turbine is provided with a co-axial small toothed wheel (504) which is in mesh with two or more toothed wheels or satellites (5) of larger diameter, which in turn are in mesh with a crown gear (303) which surrounds them and is secured to the body (3) of said hydrobrush.
problem: Converting high-speed rotational energy from a water-driven turbine into usable brush rotation speed and torque.
constraint: The gear ratios between the turbine's small wheel, the larger satellites, and the crown gear must be optimized to achieve the desired speed-torque conversion without overloading the turbine or brush mechanism.
mechanism: A multi-stage gear train converts high-speed rotational input into lower-speed, higher-torque output. A small driving gear meshes with intermediate gears, which in turn drive a larger output gear. The gear ratio cascade enables speed reduction and torque amplification while maintaining mechanical power transfer efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A small toothed wheel on the turbine shaft meshes with larger satellite gears, which in turn mesh with a crown gear attached to the brush. This planetary gear system reduces rotational speed while increasing torque, enabling effective brushing action.

abstract: A resin composition comprising an amorphous polymer as component (1), a crystalline polymer as component (2) and a rubber like polymer as component (3), wherein component (1) is dispersed in component (2) and component (3) is dispersed in component (2) in network form is disclosed. The resin composition has excellent mechanical properties such as impact strength, flexural modulus, etc.
problem: Enhancing mechanical properties (e.g., impact strength, flexural modulus) of a resin composition through phase morphology control.
constraint: The relative proportions and compatibility of the three polymer components must be balanced to maintain structural integrity while achieving the desired dispersion morphology and mechanical performance.
mechanism: A continuous polymer matrix incorporates two dispersed phases with contrasting mechanical properties. The dispersed phases create a network structure that absorbs energy through deformation and distributes stress across the material, improving toughness and stiffness through controlled phase morphology and interfacial interactions.
mechanism_raw: An amorphous polymer (component 1) and a rubber-like polymer (component 3) are both dispersed in a continuous crystalline polymer matrix (component 2) in a network structure. The dispersed phases absorb energy and distribute stress, improving toughness and stiffness.

abstract: A connection between the ends of two discrete signal transmission devices allows signal propagation between the ends of the devices. The ends of the devices are axially aligned at a close distance from one another within an alignment sleeve. A length of heat-shrink tubing having a sealant on its inner surfaces is placed over the alignment sleeve and the ends of the devices. The tubing is heated and provides axially compressive and radially compressive forces on the alignment sleeve and device ends thereby providing a high tensile strength connection between the device ends.
problem: Joining two discrete signal transmission device ends to enable signal propagation while providing high tensile strength and environmental sealing
constraint: Must balance mechanical tensile strength with signal continuity and environmental sealing, while maintaining precise alignment of the device ends during the heat-shrink process
mechanism: A compressible sleeve with an internal sealing material is positioned over two axially aligned ends of signal transmission devices within a positioning fixture; when externally energized, the sleeve simultaneously applies axial and radial compressive forces, mechanically joining the device ends and sealing the connection while the positioning fixture maintains proper alignment during the joining process
mechanism_raw: Heat-shrink tubing with inner sealant is placed over axially aligned device ends within an alignment sleeve; when heated, the tubing simultaneously applies axial and radial compressive forces, mechanically joining the ends and sealing the connection while the alignment sleeve maintains proper positioning during the joining process
residual_terms: ["compressible sleeve", "sealing material", "positioning fixture", "compressive forces", "signal transmission devices"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for impregnating a porous substrate with foam, the method comprising transporting the porous substrate through a nip region defined by a rotating foraminous drum and a foam discharge head, the foam discharge head comprising one or more discharge openings, supplying foam to the discharge head with pressure sufficient to discharge foam through the discharge openings to impregnate the porous substrate, and urging the foam discharge head and the foraminous drum toward each other to compress the porous substrate as it passes the discharge openings. The foam discharge head is mounted to a hinged plate to enable the urging of the discharge head toward the foraminous drum.
problem: Uniformly impregnating a porous substrate with foam without damaging the substrate or causing uneven saturation
constraint: Must balance foam discharge pressure and substrate compression force to achieve uniform impregnation depth without over-saturating or damaging the porous substrate structure
mechanism: A discharge element is mounted on a pivoting support that allows it to be urged toward a rotating perforated surface, creating a compression zone where the substrate is simultaneously compressed against the surface while material is discharged under pressure through openings, forcing material into the substrate pores through controlled mechanical compression
mechanism_raw: A foam discharge head is mounted on a hinged plate that allows it to be urged toward a rotating foraminous drum, creating a nip region where the substrate is simultaneously compressed against the drum while foam is discharged under pressure through openings, forcing foam into the substrate pores through controlled mechanical compression

abstract: The composition comprises highly nutritious powder of gourd fruit which is available as solid nutritious food or nutritious beverages. The gourd powder composition contains the powder of gourd fruit, creaming syrup and/or L-ascorbic acid. The other nutritious ingredient can be added if necessary. When supplied as beverages, the foaming agents can be added thereto. The L-ascorbic acid is used mainly for the purpose of removing the grassy-smelling peculiar to the gourd. The creaming syrup is used to have the powder of gourd fruit deflocculated in the liquid. If the foaming agents are added thereto, the powder of gourd fruit is more easily deflocculated in the liquid and the cooling beverage like cream soda can be made.
reason: This patent describes a food composition using standard, well-known food science additives (L-ascorbic acid for odor removal, creaming syrup for deflocculation, foaming agents for texture). These are conventional formulation techniques without a novel causal mechanism that would transfer to other fields.

abstract: Following the application of plastic extrudate to transmission medium being moved along a path of travel to provide an insulative covering, the covered medium is moved through a cooling medium and then through an air wipe device (20). The air wipe device, which is effective to remove any of the cooling medium remaining on an outer surface of the cover, comprises a helically extending manifold (42). Spaced along inner surfaces (51, 52) of the manifold are a plurality of sets of orifices (50--50) from which air is directed into engagement with the moving transmission medium. Each set of orifices is arranged to direct streams of air toward the path of travel and hence into engagement with the transmission medium in a manner such that cooling medium is removed from the entire outer surface of the transmission medium. Also each set of orifices is such that the air which is directed toward the moving transmission media does not reengage the air wipe device. A plurality of single orifices (60--60) alternate with the sets of orifices and cooperate with the sets to maintain the transmission medium disposed along the path of travel substantially adjacent to the focal point of the streams of air from each set of orifices.
problem: Removing residual cooling medium from the entire outer surface of a moving covered transmission medium while maintaining the medium's position along its path of travel
constraint: Must balance thorough surface cleaning coverage with maintaining consistent medium positioning and avoiding air recirculation that would reduce wiping effectiveness
mechanism: A helical distribution channel contains alternating sets of outlets and individual outlets; the sets direct fluid streams toward the moving medium to remove residual material from the entire surface, while the individual outlets cooperate with the sets to maintain the medium at the focal point of the fluid streams, and the outlet arrangement prevents fluid from re-engaging the device
mechanism_raw: A helical manifold contains alternating sets of orifices and single orifices; the sets direct air streams toward the moving medium to remove cooling medium from the entire surface, while the single orifices cooperate with the sets to maintain the medium at the focal point of the air streams, and the orifice arrangement prevents air from re-engaging the device

abstract: Mechanical properties of short test specimens are tested in tension and fatigue using an improved electrical resistance heating furnace having a short length that mounts between the grips of a typical testing machine. The furnace includes a ceramic inner liner having an oval cross-section to reduce heat loss at the ends. The furnace is divided into a plurality of individually controlled heating zones. Provision is made to supply an inert gas to the volume around the specimen in the center of the furnace.
problem: Testing mechanical properties of short specimens at elevated temperatures while minimizing heat loss and maintaining an inert atmosphere
constraint: Must balance compact furnace length (to fit between testing machine grips) with effective thermal insulation, precise temperature control, and inert atmosphere maintenance
mechanism: A compact heating chamber with a non-circular cross-section thermally insulating inner liner reduces heat loss at the ends compared to a circular cross-section, while the chamber is divided into individually controlled heating zones for precise temperature profiling, and an inert gas is supplied around the specimen to prevent oxidation during testing
mechanism_raw: A short furnace with an oval cross-section ceramic inner liner reduces heat loss at the ends compared to a circular cross-section, while the furnace is divided into individually controlled heating zones for precise temperature profiling, and an inert gas is supplied around the specimen to prevent oxidation during testing
residual_terms: ["heating chamber", "non-circular cross-section", "thermally insulating inner liner", "heating zones", "inert gas", "specimen"]

abstract: A method of replicating a color photograph (11) onto a leather surface by transferring the photograph (11) to a xerographic copy (20), tracing the copy (20) onto the surface of the leather (50), using specialized leather working tools (30) to cut and raise the surface of the leather (50) and then applying colored leather dyes (81) to selected portions of the leather surface in accordance with the color scheme of the color photograph (11).
problem: Transferring a color photograph onto a textured leather surface while preserving color accuracy and surface detail.
constraint: Requires specialized leather-working tools and dyes, and depends on precise manual tracing and surface manipulation to align texture with color.
mechanism: Using an intermediate medium to transfer the image onto the target surface, then modifying the surface geometry to match the image's texture, followed by applying color in accordance with the original color scheme.
mechanism_raw: Using a xerographic copy as an intermediate to trace the image onto leather, then employing specialized tools to cut and raise the leather surface to match the image's texture, followed by applying dyes in accordance with the original color scheme.

abstract: A bomblet projectile includes a projectile body, a fuse housing on the body at the rear end thereof; and an unwindable stabilization band for stabilizing the position of the projectile while dropping. The band forms, in the deployed state, a loop having leg portions terminating in fastening regions secured to the fuse housing and a dome portion flanked by the leg portions. The band has a length and different widths along the length. The band has its greatest width in the dome portion and its smallest width in the leg portions, externally of the fastening regions.
problem: Stabilizing a projectile's orientation during descent to ensure accurate deployment or targeting.
constraint: The band's length and width distribution must balance structural integrity with aerodynamic responsiveness to avoid over-stabilization or tumbling.
mechanism: A variable-geometry aerodynamic element with differential widths along its length forms a loop that dynamically adjusts aerodynamic forces, creating passive stabilization through geometric asymmetry.
mechanism_raw: An unwindable stabilization band with variable widths (greatest in the dome, smallest in the legs) forms a loop that dynamically adjusts aerodynamic forces, creating passive stabilization through geometric asymmetry.

abstract: The combination bookmark and writing instrument holder includes a generally planar marking strip and an integrally molded retaining clip at one end of the marking strip. In the preferred embodiment, the retaining clip includes a pair of generally symmetrical, outwardly jaws that together present a writing instrument retaining channel. The channel includes a writing instrument retaining portion, and an outwardly flared mouth portion for guiding the writing instrument into the retaining portion.
problem: Retaining a writing instrument on a bookmark while allowing easy insertion and removal.
constraint: The flared mouth angle and channel width must be optimized to prevent slippage without requiring excessive force for insertion.
mechanism: A tapered retention channel with a flared entry guides the writing instrument into a narrower channel, using geometric tapering to balance insertion ease with secure retention.
mechanism_raw: A flared mouth on the retaining clip guides the writing instrument into a narrower retaining channel, using geometric tapering to balance insertion ease with secure retention.

abstract: A thermostat control for use in conjunction with a boat dock de-icer, wherein the thermostat control includes an electrical outlet, a plug for connecting the control to a source of electrical energy, a set point controller for controlling the operation of the thermostat, and a temperature sensor for sensing a fluid. A conventional boat dock de-icer is plugged into the thermostat control and the thermostat control is connected to a source of electrical energy. The temperature sensor is placed in water in the vicinity of a boat dock, and the set point is set to any desired temperature, but preferably to a temperature about freezing. When the control temperature of the water is reached, the thermostat control permits operation of the boat dock de-icer, so that the de-icer operates only when needed, instead of continuously.
problem: Operating a boat dock de-icer only when necessary to conserve energy and prevent over-operation.
constraint: The sensor must be positioned to accurately reflect ambient water temperature, and the set point must balance ice prevention with energy efficiency.
mechanism: A feedback control system with a temperature sensor activates the de-icer when the ambient temperature reaches a set point, linking environmental conditions to device operation.
mechanism_raw: A thermostat with a temperature sensor placed in water activates the de-icer when the water temperature reaches a set point (near freezing), creating a feedback loop that links environmental conditions to device operation.

abstract: Novel firm, natural yoghurt compositions made by fermentation of a fermentation mixturte comprising about 15 percent to about 70 percent fresh cowmilk or ewemilk and about 85 percent to about 30 percent soymilk using yoghurt culture organisms are provided. Use of a sweetener and a thickener is unnecessary to provide a natural yoghurt composition having a taste and consistency like or substantially indistinguishable from that of a corresponding yoghurt composition made from the fresh milk used in making the novel yoghurt compositions. Flavoring agents and fruit preparations suitable as additives in preparation of yoghurt composition can be added in conventional manner. The provided compositions have an enhanced protein content with a PER value of at least 2.6 and a reduced animal fat content as compared to the corresponding compositions using 100 percent fresh milk. Also provided are methods of preparation of the novel firm, natural yoghurt compositions.
problem: Creating a firm, natural yogurt with enhanced protein and reduced animal fat without additives.
constraint: The milk ratio must balance protein content and fat reduction while maintaining fermentation compatibility and sensory qualities indistinguishable from traditional yogurt.
mechanism: Fermenting a controlled ratio of two protein sources with cultures leverages synergistic interactions to achieve desired texture and nutritional profile without additives.
mechanism_raw: Fermenting a controlled ratio of cowmilk and soymilk (15-70% cow, 30-85% soy) with yogurt cultures leverages synergistic protein interactions to achieve desired texture and nutritional profile without thickeners or sweeteners.

abstract: An apparatus for opening and mixing staple cotton comprises two cotton supply chambers, having parallel vertical axes, at the bottom of each chamber being provided a first and a second opposite cooperating cylinders for gripping the cotton staples, and supplying the gripped staples to a respective cotton carding plate and cleaning blade.
problem: Processing staple fibers (e.g., cotton) without damaging their structure during opening, mixing, and cleaning.
constraint: Balancing gripping force and fiber damage to avoid breakage while ensuring efficient transport and processing.
mechanism: Opposing elements grip and transport fibrous materials to processing surfaces through controlled contact pressure, enabling sequential mechanical treatment while preserving structural integrity via regulated gripping and release cycles.
mechanism_raw: Opposing cylinders grip and transport fibers to carding/cleaning surfaces, enabling sequential mechanical processing while maintaining fiber integrity through controlled gripping and release.

abstract: In a method for the disposal and recovery of environmentally harmful substances, especially refrigerant from refrigerant systems, in which the refrigerant is aspirated from the refrigeration system with the aid of a compressor and liquefied, and after passing through an oil filter supplied to a disposal container, the invention provides that on its way to the compressor, the refrigerant is kept in the gaseous state by heating and is freed of foreign substances such as oil, water and dirt, which are collected in separate containers, and on its way from the compressor to the disposal container, in the liquid state, is subjected to further cleaning to remove the aforementioned substances.
problem: Safely recovering and purifying refrigerants contaminated with oil, water, and dirt during disposal.
constraint: Maintaining refrigerant in the correct phase (gaseous/liquid) during each cleaning stage to optimize contaminant removal without phase-change inefficiencies.
mechanism: Sequential phase-dependent separation: pre-compression gaseous-phase filtration removes volatile contaminants, followed by post-compression liquid-phase filtration for residual substances, exploiting state-specific contaminant removal efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Two-stage separation: gaseous-state filtration before compression removes volatile contaminants, while post-compression liquid-state filtration removes residual substances, leveraging state-dependent cleaning efficiency.

abstract: A method is provided for separating an inert solid substantially inorganic fraction comprising sand or soil from a tarry or oily organic matter in a feedstock. The feedstock may be contaminated soil or tarry waste. The feedstock is combined with pulverized coal and water. The ratio (oil or tar to dry weight of coal) of about 1.0:10 to about 4.0:10 at a temperature in the range of 60.degree.-95.degree. C. The mixture is agitated, the coarse particles are removed, and up to about 0.10% by weight (based on weight of coal) of a frothing agent is added. The mixture is then subjected to flotation, and the froth is removed from the mixture.
reason: The mechanism described (froth flotation with coal/water mixture) is a standard industrial separation technique. While effective, it does not introduce a novel causal principle beyond existing froth flotation methods.

abstract: A high density, substantially oxide-free metal layer is deposited by spray deposition on a substrate in an atmosphere containing ambient air having an oxygen content above about 0.1% by weight. This is accomplished by directing a supersonic-velocity jet stream of hot gases carrying metal particles at the substrate through an inert gas shroud. The layer is useful as a corrosion barrier and for repairing metal substrates.
problem: Depositing oxide-free metal layers in ambient environments where oxygen would otherwise react with molten or semi-molten particles.
constraint: Balancing supersonic particle velocity and shroud gas flow rate to ensure particle trajectory accuracy while maintaining oxidation protection.
mechanism: High-velocity propulsion of particulate material toward a substrate is combined with a protective gas barrier that isolates the material from reactive ambient conditions during transit, preventing unwanted chemical interaction.
mechanism_raw: Supersonic gas jet propels metal particles toward a substrate while an inert gas shroud isolates them from ambient oxygen, preventing oxidation during deposition.
residual_terms: ["supersonic gas jet", "inert gas shroud", "particle trajectory accuracy"]

abstract: A meat patty molding machine having a base plate with an opening therethrough and a fill plate rotatably mounted in the base plate opening. A meat feeder forces meat up through openings in the fill plate. A mold plate defines a disk-shaped mold cavity and is mounted to move laterally between a fill position with its disk-shaped mold cavity in communication with the fill plate and a patty discharge position with the disk-shaped mold cavity away from the fill plate. A drive means rotates the fill plate relative to the mold plate, and the fill plate rotated relative to a stationary cutting blade positioned to cut meat fibers at the upstream surface of the fill plate during filling. By forming the patty while rotating the fill plate relative to the remainder of the mold, a meat patty is formed having longitudinal strands of meat disposed in a substantially circular pattern around the patty axis.
problem: Forming meat patties with controlled internal fiber orientation to achieve specific textural properties.
constraint: Synchronizing rotational speed and lateral mold movement to maintain consistent fiber orientation without disrupting material flow.
mechanism: Synchronized rotational and translational motion of a containment element relative to a cutting mechanism during material filling induces controlled internal alignment patterns, creating structured anisotropic material properties.
mechanism_raw: Rotating the fill plate relative to the mold cavity and cutting blade during filling induces longitudinal fiber alignment in a circular pattern, creating structured meat patties.

abstract: A fuze for a bomblet projectile of the type including a primary firing pin mounted in a housing for axial displacement in the longitudinal direction and a detonation charge carried by a slide disposed in the housing for displacement in a direction transverse to said longitudinal direction of the housing, between a safety position, wherein the detonation charge is not aligned with the primary firing pin, and an armed position, wherein the detonation charge is aligned with primary firing pin. To further improve the firing and safety devices of such fuzes and permit safe pick-up of duds, a lateral recess is provided in a side surface of the slide in the form of a longitudinal groove so that the movement of the slide, if minimum centrifugal forces are no longer present, can be arrested in an intermediate position by renewed engagement of a spring tensioned safety pin in the recess. In this intermediate position the detonation charge remains off center or non-aligned with the primary firing pin, in an interrupted line of ignition. Moreover, in the intermediate position, the slide and in particular ignition element for a self-destruct charge carried by the slide, remains spaced from second firing pin disposed laterally in the housing at the armed position.
problem: Ensuring a bomblet fuze remains safe (cannot detonate) even when it ends up in an intermediate state between safety and armed positions, such as when picked up as a dud after centrifugal forces have dropped below the arming threshold.
constraint: The safety mechanism must allow arming under proper spin conditions (centrifugal force present) while guaranteeing that any intermediate or partial state maintains a non-aligned, interrupted ignition path, balancing operational arming with fail-safe safety for dud recovery.
mechanism: A normally-engaged safety element is held in a disengaged state by an activation force during normal operation, allowing a movable component to reach an active configuration. When the activation force drops below a threshold, a resilient element returns the safety element toward engagement, but instead of restoring the movable component to its original position, the safety element engages a lateral retention feature on the movable component, arresting it in an intermediate configuration. In this arrested state, the energy delivery pathway remains physically misaligned and interrupted, preventing any activation sequence from completing.
mechanism_raw: A spring-tensioned safety pin is normally held retracted by centrifugal force during arming, allowing a slide to move to the armed position. When centrifugal forces drop below a threshold, the spring drives the safety pin back into engagement, but instead of returning the slide to its original safety position, the pin catches a lateral recess (longitudinal groove) on the slide, arresting it in an intermediate position. In this arrested state, the detonation charge remains off-center/non-aligned with the primary firing pin (interrupted ignition line), and the self-destruct ignition element on the slide remains spaced from the second firing pin, preventing any detonation path from forming.
residual_terms: ["resilient element", "activation force", "threshold", "lateral retention feature", "intermediate configuration", "energy delivery pathway", "misaligned", "interrupted"]

abstract: A rolling fire door consists of a plurality of interconnected fireproof slats forming a curtain which is received by a pair of tracks along the sides of an opening to be secured. A torsion spring assembly assists in the raising and lowering of the curtain during normal operation. A torsion spring tube, rotated by raising and lowering of the curtain, is connected to a hydraulic pump. Upon the sensing of smoke, fire or the like, the torsion spring mechanism is disengaged and the curtain begins to fall by its own weight within the pair of tracks. The falling of the curtain rotates the torsion spring tube and accordingly drives the hydraulic motor which includes a restriction providing a load to the rotation of the torsion spring tube, thereby restricting the rate of descent of the curtain.
problem: Controlling the descent rate of a fire door curtain that falls under its own weight during a fire emergency, preventing dangerously rapid descent while ensuring the curtain closes to seal the opening.
constraint: The system must allow sufficient gravitational force to close the curtain (fire safety) while the self-powered hydraulic damping must limit descent speed to a safe rate, all without external power or manual intervention during a fire emergency.
mechanism: A gravitational load drives a closing element toward a sealed position. The motion of the closing element is mechanically coupled to a damping mechanism that converts kinetic energy into controlled resistance. A flow restriction within the damping mechanism creates a load proportional to the motion, regulating the descent rate. The closing motion itself provides the energy to power the damping mechanism, requiring no external power source.
mechanism_raw: When fire is detected, the torsion spring mechanism is disengaged, allowing the curtain to fall by gravity. The falling curtain rotates a torsion spring tube, which is mechanically coupled to a hydraulic pump/motor. The hydraulic system includes a restriction that creates a controlled load (resistance) on the rotation of the torsion tube. This resistance converts the kinetic energy of the falling curtain into controlled hydraulic damping, thereby regulating the rate of descent. The falling motion itself powers the damping mechanism.
residual_terms: ["gravitational load", "kinetic energy", "flow restriction", "damping mechanism", "controlled resistance", "descent rate"]

abstract: An elevator car and a counterweight is suspended on a sheave by means of a rope in a well-rope faashion. In dependence on the number of passengers on the car, the sheave is applied with an unbalance torque making appearance between the car and counterweight. Upon starting of the elevator operation by releasing a brake, upward or backward bouncing of the car takes place due to the unbalance torque. For preventing such bouncing of the car, a start compensation is performed by generating a motor torque which can cancel out the unbalance torque in precedence to the releasing of the brake. The brake is installed swingably on a winding equipment. Displacement of the brake during actuation thereof indicates the presence of the unbalance torque. By taking advantage of this displacement, the start compensation is carried out by increasing the motor torque progressively in the direction depending on the displacement and by holding the motor torque constant at a value attained when the displacement becomes smaller than a predetermined value.
problem: Preventing bouncing or jerking of an elevator car when starting, caused by an unbalance torque between the car and counterweight that varies with passenger load.
constraint: The compensation must be applied preemptively (before full brake release), must adapt progressively to varying load imbalances, and must stabilize once equilibrium is reached, using the brake's own mechanical displacement as both the sensing element and the trigger for compensation.
mechanism: A braking element is mounted with limited rotational freedom on a drive mechanism, so load imbalance causes physical displacement of the brake during actuation. This displacement serves as a feedback signal that triggers a compensation mechanism. Before the brake fully releases, a corrective torque is progressively applied in proportion to the brake displacement, counteracting the load imbalance preemptively. Once the displacement falls below a threshold indicating equilibrium, the corrective torque is held constant, enabling smooth engagement without transient motion.
mechanism_raw: The brake is mounted swingably on the winding equipment, so the unbalance torque between car and counterweight causes the brake to physically displace during actuation. This displacement is used as a feedback signal: before the brake fully releases, a motor torque is progressively increased in proportion to the brake displacement, canceling out the unbalance torque preemptively. Once the displacement drops below a predetermined threshold (indicating the unbalance is compensated), the motor torque is held constant, allowing smooth brake release without car bouncing.
residual_terms: ["braking element", "rotational freedom", "load imbalance", "physical displacement", "feedback signal", "compensation mechanism", "corrective torque", "threshold", "equilibrium", "smooth engagement"]

abstract: An instrument for determining the concentration of a particular gas that might be present in a sample has no moving parts and is extremely compact. The instrument uses as a source of radiation a device that has a radiating element whose temperature is alternated between T.sub.1 and T.sub.2 and whose spectrum approximates that of a blackbody. Radiation from this source is passed through a dual pass band filter that has two non-overlapping pass bands, one of which is centered at a wavelength at which the gas absorbs and the other of which is centered at a wavelength at which the sample does not absorb radiation. After passing through this filter, the radiation passes through the sample chamber and then is intercepted by a detector which produces an electrical signal determined by the radiation intercepted. The electrical signal is processed to provide an indication of the concentration of the gas.
problem: Determining the concentration of a specific gas in a sample using a compact instrument with no moving parts, while distinguishing the gas absorption signal from background radiation and source intensity variations.
constraint: The instrument must be extremely compact with no moving parts while achieving accurate gas concentration measurement, requiring the dual-band self-referencing approach and temperature modulation to compensate for source intensity variations and background interference without mechanical scanning or complex calibration.
mechanism: A radiation source is temperature-modulated between two values, creating a time-varying signal. The radiation passes through a dual-band filter with non-overlapping wavelength bands: one at an absorption wavelength and one at a reference wavelength. After filtering, the radiation traverses a sample chamber and is detected by a sensor capturing both bands simultaneously. The detected signal is processed by comparing the absorption-band signal against the reference-band signal, with the temperature modulation enabling discrimination of the target-specific signal from steady background interference and source drift.
mechanism_raw: A blackbody-spectrum radiation source has its temperature alternated between two values (T1 and T2), creating a modulated thermal radiation signal. This radiation passes through a dual pass-band filter with two non-overlapping bands: one centered at the gas absorption wavelength and one at a non-absorption reference wavelength. After filtering, the radiation passes through the sample chamber and is detected. The detector captures both wavelength bands simultaneously. The electrical signal is processed by comparing the absorption-band signal (attenuated by the gas) against the reference-band signal (unaffected by the gas), with the temperature modulation providing a time-varying component that enables discrimination of the gas-specific signal from steady background radiation and source drift.
residual_terms: ["temperature-modulated", "radiation source", "dual-band filter", "non-overlapping wavelength bands", "absorption wavelength", "reference wavelength", "sample chamber", "detector", "absorption-band signal", "reference-band signal", "temperature modulation", "background interference", "source drift"]

abstract: An article and method for use in making stuffed food products with at least one flat end has a plurality of annular discs connected one to another by a long tubular membrane which passes through the central opening in each disc. The membrane is transversely circumferentially perforated between each disc and stuffing pressures cause the tubular membrane to longitudinally extend and tear at the preforations so that discs can be longitudinally separated and introduced one at a time into the stuffed food product for flattening an end of the product.
problem: Sequentially dispensing individual annular discs one at a time from a connected chain for insertion into stuffed food products to flatten their ends, using stuffing pressure as the driving force.
constraint: The perforations must be strong enough to keep discs connected during handling and transport but weak enough to tear sequentially under stuffing pressure, and the longitudinal extension of the membrane must provide sufficient tensile force to drive the progressive tearing without releasing all discs simultaneously.
mechanism: Multiple discrete elements are connected in a chain by a flexible elongated member that passes through a central opening in each element. The member is transversely perforated at spaced intervals between adjacent elements. When a driving pressure is applied, the elongated member extends longitudinally, creating tensile stress concentrated at the perforated points. The member tears progressively at the first perforation, releasing the first element. Continued extension and pressure buildup causes sequential tearing at subsequent perforations, releasing each element one at a time for individual insertion.
mechanism_raw: Multiple annular discs are connected in a chain by a long tubular membrane that passes through the central opening of each disc. The membrane is transversely circumferentially perforated between each pair of adjacent discs. When stuffing pressure is applied, the tubular membrane longitudinally extends under the pressure differential. This longitudinal extension creates tensile stress concentrated at the pre-perforated points between discs. The membrane tears progressively at the first perforation, releasing the first disc. Continued extension and pressure build-up causes the membrane to tear at the next perforation, releasing the next disc, and so on. Each disc is thus separated and introduced one at a time into the food product for end flattening.
residual_terms: ["discrete elements", "flexible elongated member", "central opening", "transversely perforated", "spaced intervals", "driving pressure", "longitudinal extension", "tensile stress", "perforated points", "progressive tearing", "sequential tearing", "individual insertion"]

abstract: A gasifier system for obtaining relatively clean combustible gaseous products from solid fuel materials, such as processed sewage sludge, comprises a gasifier reactor which communicates a raw, combustible gas to a cyclone separator, a gas scrubbing device and a gas cooling and drying device. Gas which exits the system is relatively clean and may be used in a prime mover for the production of energy. The gasifier reactor of the present invention is a down-draft fixed bed gasifier. The gasifier is constructed of several interconnected modular units. Moreover, the gasifier is constructed so as to efficiently gasify fuel materials while maintaining excellent horizontal temperature control.
problem: Obtaining clean combustible gas from variable solid fuel materials (e.g., sewage sludge) while maintaining controlled temperature distribution across the gasifier reactor.
constraint: Balancing efficient gasification of heterogeneous fuel materials with maintaining uniform horizontal temperature distribution across the reactor bed.
mechanism: A plurality of spatially distributed processing zones are interconnected to enable localized thermal regulation within a continuous reaction environment. Each zone contributes to overall temperature control, allowing heterogeneous input materials to undergo conversion without localized overheating or incomplete processing. The distributed architecture decouples fuel variability from thermal uniformity.
mechanism_raw: Modular interconnected down-draft fixed bed gasifier units distribute heat management spatially across the reactor, enabling horizontal temperature control. The modular construction allows each unit to contribute to overall thermal regulation, so that diverse and inconsistent fuel materials can be gasified efficiently without localized overheating or incomplete conversion.

abstract: An assembly including a flexible vest, including a first harness ring loop positioned about an upper portion of the vest and secured thereto, with a second harness ring loop secured to a lower end of the vest, with the first harness ring loop including a first and second forward vertical belt secured between the first and second harness loops forwardly of the vest, with a first and second rear vertical belt secured to a rear portion of the vest, wherein the first rear and first forward vertical belts are securable overlying the vest, with the second rear and second vertical belts securable together overlying the vest, wherein the first harness ring loop includes a forward and rear support belt securable to forward and rear rings secured to an associated saddle pommel and a saddle seat ridge. Right and left support belts are secured to diametrically opposed side portions of the second harness ring loop securable to a "Y" strap, in turn secured to a "D" ring of an associated saddle. Thigh straps are further utilized securable about each thigh of an individual, and also secured to a "Y" strap mounted to each side of the saddle. A foam cushion insert is provided captured between the rider and the saddle seat to frictionally enhance engagement of the rider with the associated saddle seat.
problem: Securely attaching a rider to a saddle with adjustable positioning, load distribution, and frictional engagement, while maintaining comfort.
constraint: Balancing secure engagement and load distribution with adjustability and rider comfort across dynamic riding conditions.
mechanism: A multi-point load distribution system with interconnected tension elements engages multiple body contact points to balance secure attachment with comfort. Each connection point allows independent adjustment, and the interconnection creates a coupled tension network where adjustment at one point influences overall fit. A compliant interface element creates frictional engagement between the user and the support surface.
mechanism_raw: A multi-point harness system with interconnected straps (forward/rear vertical belts, support belts, thigh straps) that distribute load across multiple body contact points. Each strap connection point allows independent adjustment, and the foam cushion insert creates frictional engagement between rider and saddle. The interconnection of straps means that tension at one point influences the overall fit, enabling customized, secure positioning.

abstract: A high density high strength ceramic article is disclosed having from about 70% to about 100% of its crystalline phases as alpha sialon, having less than about 20% by weight of its crystalline phases as beta sialon, having a density of greater than about 94% of the theoretical density, and having a flexural strength of greater than about 70 kpsi at about room temperature, a Knoop hardness of greater than about 14 GPa, and a Rockwell A hardness of greater than about 94. The process for producing the article is disclosed. The process involves forming a powder mixture consisting essentially of in percent by weight from about 48 to about 88 silicon nitride, from about 8 to about 30 aluminum nitride, from about 2 to about 16 of an oxygen containing compound of an element selected from the group consisting of yttrium, lithium, magnesium, calcium, scandium, cerium, rare earths, and combinations thereof, and from about 2 to about 12 of oxygen containing compounds of one or more metals as additives to aid densification, forming a green article from the mixture, and densifying the green article by one or more methods selected from the group consisting of sintering, sintering followed by hot isostatic pressing, and encapsulated hot isostatic pressing, at a temperature of from about 1600.degree. C. to about 2000.degree. C.
problem: Achieving simultaneously high density, high strength, and controlled crystalline phase composition in ceramic articles.
constraint: Optimizing multiple mechanical properties (density, strength, hardness) simultaneously through precise control of crystalline phase composition during densification.
mechanism: Specific compositional additives are incorporated into a base powder mixture to control phase transformation kinetics during high-temperature densification. These additives modify sintering behavior and promote dominance of a target crystalline phase over competing phases, resulting in simultaneous optimization of multiple mechanical properties at high density.
mechanism_raw: Specific oxygen-containing additive combinations (yttrium, lithium, magnesium, calcium, rare earths, etc.) are incorporated into a silicon nitride/aluminum nitride powder mixture to control phase transformation during high-temperature densification. These additives modify sintering behavior and promote alpha sialon phase dominance over beta sialon, resulting in optimized mechanical properties (flexural strength, hardness) at high density.
residual_terms: ["oxygen-containing additives", "yttrium", "lithium", "magnesium", "calcium", "rare earths", "silicon nitride", "aluminum nitride", "alpha sialon", "beta sialon", "flexural strength", "hardness", "densification"]

abstract: A slide-fastener stringer half has a coupling coil having a row of turns defining a longitudinal passage and each formed with a coupling head, an upper leg and a lower leg extending transversely from the head and flanking the passage, and a bight extending from one of the respective legs to the other leg of the adjacent turn. A knitted tape against which the lower legs engage and from a longitudinal edge of which the heads project is formed of a plurality of outer warp chains adjacent the coil, an upper warp chain overlying both the upper and lower legs of the coils, and a lower warp chain overlying only the lower legs of the coil and extending along the passage between the upper and lower legs of the coil. Thus with this system the group of filaments forming the lower warp chain takes the place of the normally provided filling cord.
problem: Constructing slide-fastener tape with integrated structural elements that eliminate the need for a separate filling cord while maintaining mechanical integrity.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and proper coil engagement while eliminating a separate filling cord component through integrated textile construction.
mechanism: A textile tape structure incorporates three strategically positioned structural elements where one element is positioned to occupy the longitudinal passage between coupling features, thereby integrating the function of a normally separate internal support member directly into the tape's construction. This eliminates a discrete component while maintaining mechanical integrity of the coupling system.
