mechanism_raw: A knitted tape with three strategically positioned warp chains (outer, upper, lower) where the lower warp chain is positioned to occupy the longitudinal passage between the upper and lower legs of the coupling coil, thereby taking the place of a normally provided filling cord. This integrates the filling cord's structural function directly into the tape's knit structure, eliminating a separate component.
residual_terms: ["knitted tape", "warp chains", "coupling coil", "filling cord", "longitudinal passage", "upper leg", "lower leg"]

abstract: The independent unit for heat exchange particularly for the ventilation of a room or premises is configured like a box (12) wherein are formed two passages (40 and 42) having an undulated shape and wherein circulate in counter-current air drawn in the room and rejected to the outside and outer air introduced into the room. The invention applies particularly to the ventilation and air conditioning of the premises or rooms of a building.
problem: Achieving efficient heat exchange for building ventilation in a compact, self-contained unit.
constraint: Achieving high heat exchange efficiency in a compact, self-contained unit suitable for building ventilation applications.
mechanism: Counter-current flow through two undulated passages within a single enclosure configuration. The undulated geometry increases effective surface area for heat transfer and promotes turbulent mixing of the fluid streams, while the counter-current arrangement maintains maximum temperature driving force along the entire flow path. This enables high heat exchange efficiency in a compact, independent unit.
mechanism_raw: Counter-current flow through two undulated passages within a single box configuration. The undulated shape increases effective surface area for heat transfer and promotes turbulent mixing of the air streams, while the counter-current arrangement maintains a maximum temperature driving force along the entire flow path. This enables high heat exchange efficiency in a compact, independent unit.
residual_terms: ["undulated passages", "box configuration", "counter-current flow", "turbulent mixing", "temperature driving force", "heat exchange efficiency"]

abstract: A method of and a device for sub-micron deforming a surface (15) is described, for example for the purpose of inscribing information. During scanning of the surface the tip (14) of a scanning tunneling microscrope is held at a constant distance from the surface by means of a negative feedback control loop (18) which is controlled by a tunneling current (It) between the tip and the surface, and for forming a pit (21) in the surface (15). The control loop is deactivated and a tip height drive member (8) is energized by means a control voltage (Vpz) whose amplitude increases as a function of time and which has a predetermined final value, such that the tip is lowered into the material.
problem: Precisely inscribing sub-micron features on a surface without damaging the tool or losing positional accuracy.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise tip positioning during scanning with the requirement to apply sufficient force for material deformation without destabilizing the system.
mechanism: A feedback system maintains a precise gap between a tool and a surface using proximity sensing during scanning, then switches to a controlled actuation mode to drive the tool into the surface for localized material modification, preserving tool integrity.
mechanism_raw: A feedback loop maintains tip-surface distance via tunneling current during scanning, then is deactivated to allow a controlled voltage-driven tip descent into the material, enabling localized deformation while preserving tip integrity.

abstract: A method and apparatus are described for injecting material into a waste sludge lagoon and mixing the material in the lagoon to solidify and stabilize the waste in-situ. The apparatus includes a slotted bucket adapted to be secured to the articulated arm of a backhoe or like equipment. The bucket has a manifold in the upper interior portion thereof which is coupled to a source of the additive or reagent material to be dispensed under pressure. In a preferred embodiment the material is a dry powder which is dispensed pneumatically through the manifold into the bucket and the waste as the bucket is moved back and forth through the waste lagoon. The manifold preferably is a cylinder having mutually spaced holes, slots or nozzles. The bucket also may have a vane structure across the scoop opening for further agitation of the sludge as it enters or leaves the bucket.
problem: Solidifying and stabilizing waste in a sludge lagoon in-situ without manual intervention or inefficient mixing.
constraint: Achieving effective mixing and additive dispersion across a large, heterogeneous volume while operating with mobile heavy machinery.
mechanism: A mobile container equipped with a pressurized dispersion system is moved through the volume, pneumatically distributing additives while internal agitation elements mix the contents, ensuring uniform chemical reaction.
mechanism_raw: A slotted bucket with a pressurized manifold is moved through the sludge, pneumatically dispersing dry powder additives while the bucket's motion and internal vanes agitate the mixture, ensuring uniform distribution and chemical reaction.

abstract: The easy pour spout described herein is designed to facilitate the pouring of a fluid from its container, such as oil for the engine, power steering and transmission of an automobile as well as radiator antifreeze, without the use of a funnel. The spout is designed as a totally self-contained unit that facilitates fast delivery into the desired part of the automobile without spilling. This spout is screwed onto the individual fluid container and after the spout and container are positioned for delivery, the delivery is actuated by a downward thrust on the container and spout.
problem: Pouring fluids from containers without spilling or requiring external tools like funnels.
constraint: Maintaining a sealed, directed flow path during actuation while ensuring compatibility with diverse container geometries and fluid viscosities.
mechanism: A self-contained flow director attached to the container is mechanically engaged by the container's movement, creating a sealed path to direct fluid flow during pouring.
mechanism_raw: A self-contained spout attached to the container directs fluid flow through a controlled path, actuated by downward pressure on the container, which mechanically engages the spout to initiate and regulate pouring.

abstract: A conical crusher designed for high yield, low waste crushing includes a head mantle with a crushing surface having a uniform radius of curvature and a bowl liner with a crushing surface having a uniform radius of curvature, the radius of curvature of the head mantle being distinct from the radius of curvature of the bowl liner.
problem: Achieving high-yield, low-waste crushing of materials in a conical crusher.
constraint: Balancing the geometry of the crushing surfaces to maximize throughput and product quality while reducing wear and energy consumption.
mechanism: Variable curvature profiles on opposing crushing surfaces create a controlled compression zone that optimizes material breakdown and particle size distribution while minimizing energy use and wear.
mechanism_raw: Distinct radii of curvature on the head mantle and bowl liner create a controlled crushing zone that optimizes material compression and particle size distribution while minimizing over-crushing and energy loss.

abstract: Submicron structures are written on a surface by positioning in nanometer range proximity, preferably within current tunneling range, of the surface a scanning tip of a material that emits atoms upon application of an applied voltage of low magnitude. While the tip is maintained within said range, it is moved relative to the surface, and a series of short voltage pulses are concurrently applied between the tip and surface. These pulses cause atoms of tip material to directly transfer to the surface and concurrently cause remaining atoms of tip material to migrate to the tip and continuously reform the tip and maintain its sharp configuration, thereby insuring uninterrupted writing ability. Various tip materials exhibiting low field evaporation potentials may be used; however, gold is preferred if deposition is to be under ambient conditions. Heating the tip enhances the ability of the material to emit atoms. The deposited structures may be selectively sensed or erased by application of appropriate voltages.
problem: Writing submicron structures on a surface with continuous tip maintenance to ensure uninterrupted operation.
constraint: Maintaining tip sharpness and deposition accuracy under ambient conditions while managing the trade-off between atom emission energy and surface interaction precision.
mechanism: Short energy pulses induce atom transfer from a tool to a surface, while residual atoms on the tool migrate to restore its shape, enabling sustained operation without manual maintenance.
mechanism_raw: Short voltage pulses between a scanning tip and surface induce atom transfer from the tip to the surface, while residual tip atoms migrate to reform the tip's sharp shape, enabling sustained deposition without manual resharpening.

abstract: An elevating bearing for a large-caliber weapon accommodated in the turret of a tank, with a slant-ring bearing around the tube. The tube is mounted in a bearing ring that rotates around the axis of the tube and is itself mounted on another bearing ring and rotates around an axis at an angle to the axis of the tube. The second bearing ring rotates in the turret around another axis at an angle to the first axis. The angle between the first and the second axes of rotation equals the angle between the first axis of rotation and the axis of the tube. Both bearing rings can be driven around their axes of rotation. The slant-ring bearing is a subassembly inside the turret and the flange that secures the second bearing ring is secured stationary to the turret. The flange that the tube is mounted on and that secures the first bearing ring is secured non-rotating to the turret. At least one mechanism that rotates the bearing rings at the same time and to the same extent but in opposite directions is also secured non-rotating to the turret.
problem: Enabling multi-axis rotational movement of a weapon tube within a confined turret space while maintaining structural support and coordinated motion.
constraint: The angular relationships between rotation axes must be precisely maintained to ensure synchronized movement without mechanical interference.
mechanism: Coordinated rotation of multiple rotational elements with axes at specific angular relationships, driven in opposing directions to achieve compound motion while maintaining structural support.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated rotation of multiple bearing rings with axes at specific angular relationships, driven in opposite directions to achieve compound elevation and traverse motion.

abstract: A product stabilizer for fruits and vegetables on a moving belt includes a very flexible rubber bladder, forming an airtight chamber between two hubs which are mounted for rotation astride the conveyor belt. The bladder is inflated to relatively low pressure less than 1 psi. When the product passes under the pliable surface of the inflated bladder, the bladder conforms to the product and serves to stabilize the product.
problem: Stabilizing irregularly shaped, fragile objects (e.g., fruits/vegetables) on a moving conveyor without causing damage.
constraint: Balancing stabilization effectiveness with minimal contact pressure to avoid deforming or damaging the object.
mechanism: A flexible, low-pressure interface that passively conforms to an object's shape, creating a stabilizing contact with minimal deformation force.
mechanism_raw: A flexible, low-pressure inflatable bladder that passively conforms to the object's shape, creating a stabilizing interface through pliant contact.

abstract: An ironing board tray bracket for use in all modern ironing boards having a track that directs the extension and retraction of the ironing board legs. The bracket fits within the track and is adjustable to conform the width of the track. An arm attaches to the bracket on one end and a tray on the other end. The tray can be used for temporary storage of the iron or other ironing accessories. An iron clip is provided on the tray to hold the iron in place.
reason: The bracket is a specific mechanical adapter for a narrow product category (ironing boards) with no generalizable functional principle beyond its immediate application.

abstract: In a process for applying a partial surface coating to a textile substrate, the textile substrate is unwound from a supply roll, preheated to a preheating zone and partly coated in a coating station by a coating head having coating nozzles. The coating compound is melted and supplied to the coating head. The heated coating head is provided within a perforated cylinder. The nozzles of the coating head apply melted coating compound through the perforations in the cylinder onto the substrate. Hot air is applied in the vicinity of a rising portion of the perforated cylinder facing the substrate to provide a clean breaking off of the melted compound from the surface of the perforated cylinder during the application of the coating onto the substrate.
problem: Applying a partial surface coating to a textile substrate with clean detachment of the coating compound from the applicator.
constraint: Maintaining precise temperature and airflow control to prevent residue buildup while ensuring consistent coating transfer.
mechanism: Heated applicators with perforations deposit a coating material, while directed airflow ensures clean separation of the material from the applicator surface during transfer.
mechanism_raw: Heated coating nozzles within a perforated cylinder apply melted compound, while directed hot air ensures clean separation of the compound from the cylinder surface during application.

abstract: A multizone intruder detection system comprises a supervisory circuit for verifying, while the system is disarmed, that each of a plurality of intrusion sensors is, indeed, functional. The supervisory circuit inhibits rearming of a disarmed system until it determines that each sensor has successfully operated within a relatively brief time interval just prior to the time an attempt is made to arm the system. A timing circuit, activated by a preliminary arm signal, operates to establish a time window (e.g. 10 minutes) within which the operability of each sensor must be verified (i.e. walk-tested) as a precondition to system arming. Preferably, the timing circuit is reset by each sensor alarm output, whereby the system user is given the full time window to walk-test each sensor. By virtue of the invention, sensor sabotage in a disarmed system can be mitigated.
problem: Ensuring all intrusion sensors in a disarmed security system are functional before rearming, to mitigate undetected sensor sabotage.
constraint: Balancing the verification time window length to allow thorough testing while preventing indefinite delays in system arming.
mechanism: A timed sequential validation process where each sensor must be tested within a verification window that resets upon each successful activation, requiring all sensors to pass before rearming.
mechanism_raw: A timing circuit establishes a verification window during which each sensor must be walk-tested; the window resets with each successful sensor activation, requiring sequential validation of all sensors.
residual_terms: ["timed sequential validation", "verification window", "resets on success", "sequential activation"]

abstract: An overwrap machine for sealing packaging for a foodstuff comprises a conveyor belt, heating elements, and pluralities of modules holding rollers which contact the packaging as individual foodstuffs are conveyed by the modules. The modules, and thus the rollers, are heated by the heating elements. There are two different roller types, which are the cylindrical first rollers and the ellipsoidal second rollers. The pluralities of rollers include substantial numbers of the first rollers with fewer numbers of the second rollers interspersed therein. The ellipsoidal second rollers are effective to insure the sealing of the ends of the foodstuff being overwrapped by bearing against the unsealed ends as each foodstuff traverses the gap between opposing second rollers.
problem: Ensuring complete sealing of the ends of foodstuffs during overwrapping while maintaining throughput.
constraint: Balancing the number of rollers to maintain high throughput while ensuring sufficient ellipsoidal rollers are present to address all end-seal gaps.
mechanism: Using a combination of rollers with varying geometries, where non-uniform rollers apply targeted pressure against specific regions of a moving object as it traverses gaps between opposing rollers, ensuring localized sealing integrity without requiring additional processing steps.
mechanism_raw: Using a combination of cylindrical and ellipsoidal rollers, where the ellipsoidal rollers are positioned to apply targeted pressure against the unsealed ends of the foodstuff as it traverses gaps between opposing rollers, ensuring end-seal integrity without requiring additional sealing steps.

abstract: An apparatus for gripping tubes of yarn packages in a textile machine includes a pressurized fluid drive member. The pressurized fluid drive member is fixedly mounted to a support frame and, in one aspect of the invention, extends interiorly of a generally cylindrical fixed component having a pair of diametrically opposed projections formed on its outer surface. A movable component comprising a tube receiving housing for receiving a yarn package tube therein has a pair of detents compatibly configured with the projections on the fixed component for releasably securing the tube receiving housing to the fixed component. In the event of a collision between the tube gripping apparatus and another object, the movable component is non-destructively released from its normal operating position, thereby minimizing the risk that potentially damaging forces will be transmitted to the pressurized fluid member.
problem: Protecting a pressurized fluid drive member from damage during collisions in a textile gripping apparatus.
constraint: Maintaining normal operational engagement between the detents and projections while ensuring release occurs only under excessive collision forces.
mechanism: A mechanical interface with interlocking features between a movable component and a fixed component allows the movable part to non-destructively disengage under excessive collision forces, preventing transmission of damaging forces to a pressurized system.
mechanism_raw: A releasable mechanical connection between a movable component (with detents) and a fixed component (with projections) allows the movable part to non-destructively detach under collision forces, preventing transmission of damaging forces to the pressurized fluid member.

abstract: Continuous filament tow is partially deregistered, preferably by passing over threaded rolls; and, after being partially deregistered, fully bloomed in an air-blooming mechanism. The air-blooming mechanism draws the partially deregistered tow into a turbulent air flow, maximizing bloom; and then carries the tow after blooming directly into a casing for formation of pillows, cushions, or the like articles. The process is simple and economical.
problem: Efficiently blooming continuous filament tow to form articles like pillows or cushions in a simple and economical process.
constraint: Achieving sufficient bloom without over-processing, while maintaining a continuous and streamlined workflow from deregistration to casing.
mechanism: A sequential process where partial mechanical separation of a continuous material is followed by full dispersion via a high-velocity fluid stream, which maximizes fiber separation and directly transfers the dispersed material into an enclosing structure for article formation.
mechanism_raw: A two-step process where partial deregistration of the tow (via threaded rolls) is followed by full blooming in a turbulent air flow, which maximizes fiber separation and directly transfers the bloomed tow into a casing for article formation.

abstract: An indoor unit of an air conditioner includes a heat exchanger, through which room air circulates in a predetermined direction, and an air cleaner, The air cleaner includes an electric duct collecting portion for capturing fine duct in the circulating air, a filter portion for absorbing the odor from the circulating air, and a control unit for controlling the operations of the indoor unit and the collecting portion. The collecting portion, filter portion, and control unit are arranged side by side in a direction intersecting the predetermined direction so that filter portion is situated between the collecting portion and the control unit.
problem: Optimizing airflow and component functionality in an air cleaner for an indoor air conditioning unit.
constraint: Fitting all components in a compact configuration while ensuring airflow directionality and component accessibility for maintenance.
mechanism: Arranging treatment components in a side-by-side configuration intersecting an airflow path, positioning a filtration element between a particulate capture unit and a secondary treatment unit to ensure sequential air processing (dust removal, contaminant absorption) without disrupting flow or accessibility.
mechanism_raw: Arranging the electric duct collector, filter, and control unit side by side in a direction intersecting the airflow path, positioning the filter between the collector and control unit to ensure sequential air treatment (dust capture, odor absorption) without disrupting airflow or component operation.

abstract: A bridle bit for horses comprises a mouthpiece to be received in the mouth of a horse. A head stall ring member rotatably mounted through the outward ends of the mouthpiece member has a portion extending through the mouthpiece outward ends secured to a cylindrical cheek piece member which rotates therewith. The cheek piece members extend forwardly from the outward ends of the mouthpiece member and reside closely adjacent the cheek of the horse and a rein ring member is rotatably mounted on each cheek piece member extending forwardly therefrom and the forward end is adapted to receive rein apparatus. The head stall ring member may also have a slot adapted to receive a curb chain. The mouthpiece members move independently of one another, the head stall and cheek piece members rotate about their longitudinal axis as a unit relative to the mouthpiece members, and the rein ring members and cheek piece members rotate about their longitudinal axis as a unit relative to the mouthpiece members and the head stall members rotate partially about their longitudinal axis relative to the cheek piece members. The fully rotatable shank may be used with any suitable mouthpiece, including mouthpieces of a fixed construction and two and three part snaffle mouthpieces.
problem: Creating a bridle bit for horses that allows independent movement of the mouthpiece while maintaining controlled rein tension and rotational articulation.
constraint: Balancing independent mouthpiece movement with sufficient rotational coupling to maintain rider control and prevent unintended disengagement.
mechanism: Using articulated joints between a mouthpiece, head stall ring, cheek pieces, and rein rings to enable independent movement of the mouthpiece and coordinated rotation of connected components, reducing pressure concentration and distributing forces across multiple articulation points.
mechanism_raw: Using rotational joints between the mouthpiece, head stall ring, cheek pieces, and rein rings to enable independent movement of the mouthpiece and coordinated rotation of connected components, reducing pressure points and distributing forces across multiple articulation points.

abstract: A tobacco filter stock capable of being molded into a filter only be entanglement of filaments with one another without any adhesion means, whereby the resulting filter has a suitable hardness and a superior whiteness. A tobacco filter and a production process thereof are provided, whereby the tobacco filter stock comprises a ton of crystalline polyolefin filaments, preferably crystalline polypropylene filaments, having a single filament denier of 1 to 6 d/f, a total denier of 30,000 to 60,000 D 40 to 60 crimps/25 mm filament, a crimp elastic modulus of 2.5 to 5.0, a frictional coefficient between filaments of 0.20 to 0.37 and a height ratio (height/width) of 0.01 to 0.1.
problem: Creating a tobacco filter with suitable hardness and whiteness without using adhesion means.
constraint: Balancing filament stiffness, friction, and geometric parameters to achieve structural integrity and optical properties without adhesives.
mechanism: Interweaving elongated elements with tunable physical characteristics (stiffness, surface friction, geometric ratios) to form a cohesive, self-retaining structure through mutual mechanical entanglement, eliminating the need for binding agents.
mechanism_raw: Entangling filaments with controlled physical properties (denier, crimp, frictional coefficient, height ratio) to form a self-supporting structure through mechanical interlocking rather than chemical bonding.

abstract: Shims are selectively added to, in one form of the invention, or removed from, in another form of the invention, the space between a cutter body and a circular saw blade in a cutter tool assembly for cutting a round on wood products, to compensate for the change in cutting radius that occurs when the tool is sharpened.
problem: Maintaining a consistent cutting radius in a tool assembly as the blade wears during sharpening.
constraint: Ensuring precise manual adjustment of shims to match wear-induced radius changes without disrupting tool alignment.
mechanism: Inserting or removing adjustable spacing elements between a cutting component and its support structure to dynamically compensate for dimensional changes caused by wear, maintaining a predetermined cutting profile.
mechanism_raw: Adjustably inserting or removing shims between the cutter body and blade to compensate for dimensional changes caused by wear, preserving the cutting geometry.

abstract: An air flow/check valve for an exhaust emission system combines flow and check functions into a single valve which is especially well-suited for use with an electric motor driven air pump. The valving mechanism is operated by a fluid actuator, and pressure conditions in the actuator are controlled by sensing the pressure differential across the valving mechanism to close the valving mechanism when exhaust back pressure is indicative of causing potentially damaging backflow to the air pump. Several embodiments of the invention are disclosed.
problem: Preventing damaging backflow to an air pump in an exhaust emission system caused by high back pressure.
constraint: Responding to dynamic pressure conditions in real-time without manual intervention while maintaining flow efficiency under normal operation.
mechanism: Employing a pressure-responsive actuation system that detects differential pressure across a flow path and automatically engages a closure mechanism when reverse pressure exceeds a defined threshold, preventing reverse flow while permitting forward flow.
mechanism_raw: Using a fluid actuator controlled by pressure differential sensing across the valve to automatically close the valve when back pressure exceeds a threshold.

abstract: Silica colloids having a spherical form, a mean diameter of between about 10 and 100 nm and a polydispersity index between about 1 and 4. A process for making silica colloids is also provided comprising a) forming a reaction medium by simultaneously adding an acidifying agent and an alkaline silicate solution to a reaction vessel, b) reacting the acidifying agent and alkaline silicate solution, and c) maintaining a constant volume of the reaction medium by drawing off the reaction medium.
problem: Producing silica colloids with uniform spherical morphology and controlled size distribution.
constraint: Balancing reaction stoichiometry, mixing rates, and volume control to prevent uncontrolled particle aggregation or size variation.
mechanism: Co-introducing reactive agents into a reaction medium while dynamically regulating the medium's volume through concurrent removal, synchronizing addition rates and volume control to stabilize particle formation dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Simultaneously adding acidifying agent and alkaline silicate to a reaction vessel while maintaining constant volume by removing reaction medium, stabilizing nucleation and growth kinetics.

abstract: A mill (10) according to the preferred teachings for grinding garbage is disclosed including an octagonal shaped grinding chamber (26) formed by side plates (14-17) interconnected to have a square cross section with its corners closed by corner plates (20-23). Planar shelves (32, 34, 36) having centrally located apertures (38) divide the grinding chamber (26). Grinding rotors (48-50) are rotatably fixed to a rotatable shaft (44) and are located complementary to, parallel, and above the shelves (32, 34, 36). The grinding rotors (48-50) include planar arms (64) which radially extend from and are circumferentially spaced on a planar disc (54) fixed to the shaft (44). An impeller rotor (51) is also rotatably fixed to the shaft (44) below the grinding rotors (48-50) and includes angle iron arms (76) which radially extend from and are circumferentially spaced on a planar disc (54) fixed to the shaft (44). The arms (64) of the grinding rotors (48-50) may include pusher bars (96) located on top of the arms (64) and within the radial extent of the discs (54) and/or may include flap blades (88) located on the bottom of the arms (64) intermediate the discs (54) and the centrally located apertures (38) of the shelves (32, 34, 36). The radial spacing between the free ends of the arms (64) and the grinding chamber (26) and between the discs (54) and the centrally located apertures (38) and the axial spacing between the grinding rotors (48-50) and the shelves (32, 34, 36) decrease from the grinding rotor (48) adjacent the inlet opening (40) of the grinding chamber (26) to the grinding rotor (50) adjacent the outlet opening (42) of the grinding chamber (26).
problem: Efficiently grinding heterogeneous waste materials (e.g., garbage) in a single-pass mill.
constraint: Optimizing clearance gradients to balance grinding intensity, material flow, and structural durability under abrasive loading.
mechanism: Establishing a gradient of processing gaps between rotating elements and stationary surfaces that progressively decrease along the material flow path, creating sequential size reduction stages and directional material transport.
mechanism_raw: Progressively decreasing radial and axial clearances between grinding rotors and chamber walls/shelves from inlet to outlet, creating staged size reduction and material transport.
residual_terms: ["gradient of processing gaps", "sequential size reduction", "directional material transport"]

abstract: There is disclosed a plant for treating and melting metals, metal compounds and/or metal alloys or for producing calcium carbide. It includes a burden-receiving shaft and a melting furnace arranged below the shaft and including a heating means. A passage opening is provided between the shaft and the melting furnace, which passage opening serves to introduce the burden present within the shaft into the melting furnace. In order to be able to introduce the hot burden into the melting furnace without difficulties and without operational failures due to charging means, a gas-permeable supporting plate rigidly arranged on the melting furnace is provided at the passage opening, corresponding to at least the shaft cross section by its cross section. A clearance is provided beside the supporting plate. The shaft is designed as a structural unit separate from the melting furnace. The shaft and the melting furnace are relatively movable with respect to each other in the direction of the clearance and back.
problem: Introducing hot burden from a shaft into a melting furnace without operational failures caused by charging mechanisms.
constraint: Balancing gas permeability of the supporting plate with structural support and the need for controlled relative movement to prevent operational failures.
mechanism: A gas-permeable barrier arranged at a material transfer interface allows substance flow while maintaining structural integrity, with a gap enabling relative motion between connected components to accommodate thermal expansion or misalignment.
mechanism_raw: A gas-permeable supporting plate rigidly arranged at the passage opening allows material transfer while maintaining structural integrity, with a clearance enabling relative movement between the shaft and furnace to accommodate thermal expansion or misalignment.

abstract: A double lift dobby for controlling the movement of the heddle frames of a weaving machine which includes coupling members pivotally connected at each end of double swinging levers which coupling elements are selectively engaged to oscillating plates by reading and transmission elements controlled by extendable members of an actuating mechanism.
problem: Precisely controlling the movement of heddle frames in a weaving machine to achieve desired fabric patterns.
constraint: Ensuring precise synchronization between the actuating mechanism's extendable members and the oscillating plates to maintain accurate heddle frame control.
mechanism: Pivoting coupling elements on articulated levers selectively engage oscillating components through synchronized actuation, enabling coordinated mechanical motion via linked force transmission.
mechanism_raw: Pivotally connected coupling members at the ends of double swinging levers selectively engage oscillating plates via reading and transmission elements controlled by extendable actuating members, enabling coordinated mechanical motion.

abstract: A differential pressure regulator is provided having a single piece pressure balanced flow spindle. The differential pressure regulator also includes a spring biased diaphragm assembly which acts against the pressure balanced flow spindle which is spring biased to the closed position. The upper surface of the diaphragm assembly is exposed to the signal pressure, and the lower surface of the diaphragm assembly is exposed to the outlet pressure. An adjustable spring is situated above the upper diaphragm to provide an additional or additive downward force on the upper diaphragm necessitating a greater force on the outlet side to close the valve. A vent is provided through the central bolt and spacer rings. The upper end of the flow spindle blocks the vent in the central bolt so long as the signal pressure plus the spring pressure is greater than or equal the outlet pressure.
problem: Regulating differential pressure in a system while maintaining balance between signal pressure and outlet pressure.
constraint: Balancing the forces from signal pressure, spring bias, and outlet pressure to ensure the vent is blocked only when equilibrium is achieved, preventing unintended valve operation.
mechanism: A pressure-balanced element interacts with opposing force sources (signal pressure, outlet pressure, and adjustable bias) to modulate valve closure, blocking venting only when equilibrium is achieved.
mechanism_raw: A single-piece pressure-balanced flow spindle interacts with a spring-biased diaphragm assembly, where the upper diaphragm surface responds to signal pressure and the lower surface to outlet pressure, with an adjustable spring adding force to modulate valve closure.

abstract: A method and apparatus for transmitting extended aspect ratio pictures is described. The transmitted pictures can be viewed on an extended aspect ratio high definition screen but can also be viewed on a reduced number of lines on a conventional receiver. The lines not used in the picture viewed on the conventional receiver contain non-visible data relating to picture information. The transmitter comprises a high definition television (HDTV) camera (42) providing a high definition video signal to a standards down-convertor (44). This has a video output with a reduced number of lines coupled to a frame store (46) and a data output connected to a buffer (48). Means (54) combines the data from the buffer (48) with the video signal from the frame store (46). A controller (50) responsive to synchronizing information ensures that the data is combined with blank portions of the video signal. The combined signal is then fed to transmitter (53). At an HDTV receiver the front end circuitry (54) receives the video signal. A switch (56) under the control of a data/video detector (58) selects between sending video information to a frame store (60) and sending data to a standards up-converter (64). The data is used to enhance picture information from the frame store (64), the resultant picture being displayed on an HDTV display.
problem: Transmitting extended aspect ratio pictures compatible with both high-definition and conventional receivers.
constraint: Ensuring data is combined with blank portions of the video signal without interfering with visible content and maintaining synchronization between data and video components.
mechanism: Non-visible data is embedded in unused segments of a reduced-resolution signal, combined with the primary signal using synchronization aligned to non-display intervals, enabling reconstruction of enhanced information at receiving devices.
mechanism_raw: Non-visible data is embedded in unused lines of a reduced-line video signal, combined with the video signal using a controller synchronized to blanking intervals, enabling reconstruction of enhanced picture information at HDTV receivers.

abstract: A grinding machine for grinding outer and/or inner surfaces of a workpiece which is provided on its indexable wheel head with an outer surface grinding wheel, inner surface grinding wheel and a measuring device having a touch probe engagable with a reference surface of the workpiece. A numerical controller having a memory for memorizing data indicating positional and angular relationships between the outer surface grinding wheel, the inner surface grinding wheel and the touch probe is provided. The numerical controller first indexes the measuring device to a location facing the workpiece, and moves the workpiece along its rotational axis until the measuring device outputs a touch signal. After that, the numerical controller calculates a moving amount of the workpiece for an outer grinding operation based upon data memorized in the memory, and moves the table by the calculated amount in order to grind the outer surface of the workpiece. When a inner surface of a workpiece is machined, the inner grinding wheel is indexed to a position facing the workpiece based upon the data indicating angular relationship, after the workpiece is positioned based upon the touch signal from the measuring device. Thereafter, the table is moved based upon data indicating positional relationship between the inner surface grinding wheel and the touch probe in order to locate the inner surface grinding wheel to a predetermined grinding starting position of the inner grinding operation.
problem: Accurately positioning grinding wheels relative to a workpiece based on measured reference points and stored calibration data.
constraint: Maintaining accuracy in stored positional/angular data and ensuring precise indexing of wheels after measurement to avoid misalignment during grinding operations.
mechanism: A measurement probe establishes a reference point, then a controller calculates tool positions using stored positional relationships, indexing tools to precise operational start points based on the reference and calibration data.
mechanism_raw: A touch probe measures a reference surface to establish a workpiece position, then a numerical controller calculates wheel positions using stored positional and angular relationships, indexing wheels to precise grinding start points.

abstract: Moist, warm, clean air from a vapor treatment system is injected into wells which are screened only at the contaminated depth forcing vapor flow only through the contaminated region. Intermediate the injection wells is an extraction well which is also screened only at the contaminated depth. A vacuum is drawn on the extraction well drawing the flushing vapors from the injection wells and toward the extraction well through the contaminated soil thereby entraining some of the contaminants. The contaminants are preferably non-volatile hydrocarbons such as diesel fuel, aviation and jet fuel, crude oil or pesticides. The contaminated, flushing vapor is then treated and recycled. An MW/RF heating system heats the earth's surface and the contaminated soil, thereby enhancing volatilization of the contaminants and their removal via the vapor flushing system. By screening the wells only through the contaminated zone and controlling the flow of clean, moist, warm air through only the contaminated zone, thereby maintaining the contaminated zone in a moist state, the entire energy of the system is focussed on the contaminated region.
problem: Efficiently removing non-volatile contaminants (e.g., hydrocarbons, pesticides) from a localized soil region without wasting energy on uncontaminated zones.
constraint: Balancing energy input (heating) and vapor flow control to maintain the contaminated zone in a moist state while preventing vapor migration to non-contaminated regions.
mechanism: A localized treatment zone is isolated from surrounding regions using a barrier that restricts flow to the target area. Energy is applied to enhance contaminant volatilization within the zone, while a pressure differential drives vapor flow through the zone, entraining contaminants. The system maintains moisture in the target zone to sustain volatilization efficiency while preventing vapor migration to non-target areas.
mechanism_raw: Selective well screening at the contaminated depth forces vapor flow exclusively through the contaminated zone, while MW/RF heating enhances volatilization. A vacuum on an extraction well draws flushing vapors through the targeted region, entraining contaminants. The system focuses energy and airflow on the contaminated area by maintaining its moisture and restricting flow to that zone.

abstract: An improved ammunition data transmission system includes alternately applied parallel sources of high frequency of alternating current (AC) voltage and direct current (DC) voltage. The high frequency AC voltage is applied first to provide updated data and to activate the electronic control package for the round in the projectile. the DC voltage then activates the electric primer system for igniting the propellant charge to fire the round. Both the electronics control package and the electric primer system are connected in parallel with the source of AC voltage and, in the preferred embodiment, the parallel connected circuitry contains a capacitor to prevent DC voltage from reaching the electronics control package and an inductor for preventing AC voltage from reaching the electric primer system.
problem: Sequencing activation of an electronic control package and an electric primer in an ammunition system without cross-interference between high-frequency AC and DC signals.
constraint: Ensuring temporal separation of AC and DC signals while using passive components to block cross-coupling without disrupting the sequential activation sequence.
mechanism: Two distinct signal types are applied in temporal sequence to separate subsystems, with passive filtering elements interposed between the subsystems to prevent cross-coupling of signals. The first signal type configures or activates a control subsystem, while the second signal type triggers a downstream action, ensuring sequential operation without interference.
mechanism_raw: Alternating application of high-frequency AC (to update data and activate electronics) followed by DC (to ignite the primer). Passive components (capacitor and inductor) isolate the two circuits, preventing DC from reaching the control package and AC from reaching the primer.

abstract: A wet pump for pumping fish from a first fish receptacle to a second receptacle displaced from the first receptacle. The wet pump includes a wet pump tank into which the fish are initially pumped, a pump suction line connected to the side of the tank and communicating the tank with the first receptacle, a pump discharge line for pumping the fish from the tank, a pump system for initially creating a low pressure vacuum in the tank and for thereafter creating a high pressure in the tank, an inlet valve for opening the pump suction line when the pump creates the vacuum in the tank and for closing the pump suction line when the pump creates the high pressure in the tank, a discharge valve for closing the pump discharge line when the pump creates the vacuum and for opening the pump discharge line when the pump creates the high pressure, and a hood surrounding the inlet valve for preventing water from flowing proximate the inlet valve such that the fish do not interfere with the closing of the inlet valve when the pump is switched from the vacuum mode to the high pressure mode. When the pump creates the vacuum, the fish are suctioned through the pump suction line into the tank, and when the pump creates the high pressure, the fish are pumped from the tank through the discharge line into the second receptacle.
problem: Gently transferring live fish between receptacles without physical harm or valve malfunction caused by fish interference during mode transitions.
constraint: Maintaining valve integrity and fish viability during rapid pressure transitions while preventing water ingress that could disrupt valve operation.
mechanism: A transfer chamber alternates between two pressure states (e.g., sub-atmospheric and super-atmospheric) to move contents between receptacles. Valves synchronize with pressure transitions to direct flow, while a protective shield prevents intrusion of contents or fluid into valve mechanisms during mode changes, ensuring reliable operation and content viability.
mechanism_raw: Alternating between vacuum and high-pressure modes in a wet pump tank. Inlet and discharge valves synchronize with pressure changes to suction fish into the tank and then expel them. A hood shields the inlet valve from water and fish, ensuring reliable valve closure during mode switches.

abstract: Oral hygiene compositions effective for preventing the adherent deposition of cariogenic bacteria on teeth comprise as active constituents polymers having defined repeating units comprising hydrocarbyl groups with pendant carboxyl and pendant polyalkylene oxide groups in defined ratio. The polymers themselves, their prepartion, and a process for treating teeth with the compositions are also claimed.
problem: Preventing adherent deposition of cariogenic bacteria on tooth surfaces using a polymer-based oral hygiene composition.
constraint: Balancing the ratio of carboxyl and polyalkylene oxide groups to maximize anti-adhesive efficacy while maintaining biocompatibility and stability in an oral environment.
mechanism: A polymeric material with a backbone and pendant functional groups in a defined ratio creates a surface barrier that inhibits adhesion of target agents. The ratio of functional groups balances anti-adhesive efficacy with compatibility in the intended environment, optimizing performance through structural or electrostatic interactions.
mechanism_raw: Polymers with hydrocarbyl backbones and pendant carboxyl and polyalkylene oxide groups in a defined ratio create a structural or electrostatic barrier that inhibits bacterial adhesion to teeth. The specific ratio of functional groups optimizes anti-adhesive properties.

abstract: The present invention consists in that printed patterns on a printed circuit board and component information near the printed patterns are photographed, that the type of an electronic component to be mounted and the mounting position and mounting attitude of the electronic component are recognized from the photographed image, and that the predetermined electronic component is mounted on the predetermined position of the printed circuit board at the predetermined attitude on the basis of the above information items. Further, a program for the mounting order of all the electronic components to be mounted on the printed circuit board is generated on the basis of the image processing information items.
problem: Accurately and efficiently mounting diverse electronic components on printed circuit boards (PCBs) at correct positions and orientations without manual intervention.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment between recognized component data and physical mounting actions while dynamically generating an optimized mounting sequence from image-derived information.
mechanism: An imaging subsystem captures positional and attribute data of target locations and components. A processor derives a mounting sequence and alignment parameters from the data, directing an automated actuator to place components at specified positions and orientations in a dynamically optimized order.
mechanism_raw: Photographing PCB patterns and nearby component information, then using image processing to recognize component type, position, and attitude. A program generated from this data directs automated mounting of components in the correct order and orientation.

abstract: An apparatus for repairing a yarn break includes a housing which is first positioned roughly by being guided towards the stop motion wire belonging to the broken warp yarn. After the broken warp yarn has been removed, a fresh separate warp yarn is introduced into the stop wire and a heddle by a pair of laterally slotted threading in tubes. In the process, the fresh warp yarn travels from a blowing opening of one tube into a suction opening in the other tube while passing through an opening in the respective stop motion wire or heddle. During this operation, the tubes are moved stepwise in the warp direction of the weaving machine until reaching a guide inserted through the reed and into which the fresh warp yarn is finally threaded.
problem: Repairing a broken warp yarn in a weaving machine without disrupting the ongoing weaving process.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment of the fresh yarn through the stop wire and heddle while avoiding further disruption to the weaving process during stepwise tube movement.
mechanism: Stepwise advancement of a slotted guide element along a fixed track, using fluid flow to direct a replacement filament through the guide and adjacent alignment structures during repair.
mechanism_raw: Stepwise movement of laterally slotted tubes guided by a stop motion wire, using suction and blowing to thread a fresh yarn through the wire and heddle while maintaining alignment during repair.

abstract: A method for making a composite material including a discontinuous phase of cellulosic fiber encapsulated in and bonded to a continuous phase of a polymeric component containing a major portion of polyethylene by mixing the cellulosic fiber and polymeric component while raising the temperature of the mixture to the encapsulation point, maintaining the encapsulated material within the encapsulation range while reducing the particle size, and thereafter extruding the material while controlling its temperature within the encapsulation range and substantially aligning the fibers in the flow direction until the material contacts a heated die.
problem: Creating a composite material with cellulosic fibers encapsulated in a polymer matrix while ensuring fiber alignment and bonding.
constraint: Maintaining the encapsulation temperature range throughout processing steps to prevent premature bonding or misalignment of fibers during extrusion.
mechanism: Regulating thermal conditions during mixing, size reduction, and shaping to encapsulate fibers within a matrix, followed by orienting fibers in the flow direction during forming.
mechanism_raw: Controlling temperature during mixing, particle size reduction, and extrusion to maintain encapsulation of fibers within the polymer phase, followed by aligning fibers in the flow direction during extrusion through a heated die.

abstract: In a vapor degreasing apparatus solvent vapor provided by a boiling sump is subjected to further heating for producing superheated solvent vapor to which a workpiece in the process of being cleaned is exposed. The superheated solvent vapor raises the temperature of the workpiece in order to minimize solvent adhering to the workpiece surface as the workpiece is removed from the apparatus to ambient. Further heating is achieved by heating means interposed in the natural convection flow path of the solvent vapor provided by a boiling sump to a vapor zone area in the degreasing apparatus.
problem: Minimizing solvent adherence to a workpiece surface during vapor degreasing when the workpiece is removed to ambient conditions.
constraint: Balancing superheating to raise workpiece temperature sufficiently to minimize solvent residue without causing thermal damage or excessive energy consumption.
mechanism: Applying superheated vapor in a natural convection flow path to preheat a workpiece, thereby reducing residual solvent adhesion during removal.
mechanism_raw: Using superheated solvent vapor generated by further heating in the natural convection flow path to preheat the workpiece, reducing residual solvent adhesion during removal.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method and an arrangement for influencing the interaction between a layer of earth and a structure situated in association with the layer of earth. What is characteristic of the invention is that a casing filled with a medium and introduced into a layer of earth is introduced into a material surrounding the casing, which material preferably consists of a bentonite or a bentonite mixture.
problem: Influencing the interaction between a structure and an adjacent layer of earth to improve stability or performance.
constraint: Selecting a medium and bentonite mixture that provide the desired interaction properties while maintaining structural integrity and compatibility with the surrounding earth.
mechanism: Inserting a casing containing a selected medium into the earth and encasing it with a bentonite mixture to establish a controlled interface that modifies soil-structure interaction.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a casing filled with a medium into the earth and surrounding it with a bentonite mixture to create a controlled interface that modifies soil-structure interaction.

abstract: A sliding gate structure for controlling discharge of material from openings defined at a lower end of a railroad hopper car. The openings are covered by a pair of gates which linearly move in guide tracks to discharge the material inside or outside of the rails depending on which gate is operated. Each gate is independently operated by an operative mechanism including a control system operable from a side of the hopper car. Each operative mechanisms include a pair of linkage assemblies which are operated by a linearly distendable driver. The linkage assemblies are connected to opposite sides of the respective gate to inhibit skewing of the gate relative to the guide tracks during gate movement. Movement of each gate is independently controlled through actuation of the control system from the side of the hopper car.
problem: Controlling discharge of material from a railroad hopper car while preventing gate misalignment during operation.
constraint: Ensuring independent gate operation from a single control point while maintaining alignment through mechanical linkages to prevent binding or uneven discharge.
mechanism: Employing independently actuated sliding gates with opposing linkage assemblies to maintain alignment during linear displacement in guide tracks.
mechanism_raw: Using independently operated sliding gates with linkage assemblies connected to opposite sides of each gate to inhibit skewing during linear movement in guide tracks.

abstract: A trading card holder constructed from semi rigid, or rigid, clear material is used to protect valuable trading cards from wear. In one embodiment, the trading card holder includes a back plate and a plurality of cover plates. The cards to be displayed by the holder are sandwiched between the cover plate and the back plate thereby rendering them immovable. In a second embodiment the card display holder includes a single back plate and a single cover plate. The two plates are connected by way of a hinge member which allows the two plates to be separated for removing or installing cards into the holder system. A plurality of holes or Velcro strips are fitted along one edge of the card holder thereby allowing multiple card holders to be inserted into a binder system.
problem: Protecting valuable trading cards from wear while enabling display and organized storage in a binder system.
constraint: Balancing card immobilization (rigid plates) with accessibility (hinge) and modularity (attachment points) without compromising structural integrity or visibility.
mechanism: A hinged enclosure with rigid transparent panels that immobilize a flat item between them, enabling access through a flexible joint and modular integration via standardized connection points for system-wide organization.
mechanism_raw: A hinged sandwich structure with rigid transparent plates that immobilize the card between them, combined with a constricted access mechanism (hinge) and modular attachment points (holes/Velcro) for integration into a larger storage system.

abstract: Aqueous formulations containing a copolymer of monoolefinically unsaturated monomers having an acid number of 5 to 150 mg of KOH/g of substance and/or a polyurethane having an acid number of 5 to 150 mg of KOH/g of substance as the binder and a triglycidyl isocyanurate having an epoxy value of 0.5 to 1.01 as the cross-linker are suitable for dressing fill grain, buffed or split leathers.
problem: Creating a durable, cross-linked coating for leather dressing that adheres well and withstands wear.
constraint: Maintaining the acid number and epoxy value within specified ranges to ensure optimal cross-linking density without over-curing or under-curing, which would degrade adhesion or durability.
mechanism: A polymer matrix formed by combining a binder with a controlled reactive group density and a cross-linker with a complementary reactive group density, enabling stoichiometric network formation through precise chemical ratio matching.
mechanism_raw: Using a copolymer or polyurethane binder with a controlled acid number (5–150 mg KOH/g) paired with a triglycidyl isocyanurate cross-linker (epoxy value 0.5–1.01) to enable precise stoichiometric cross-linking, forming a robust polymer network.
residual_terms: ["reactive group density", "stoichiometric network formation", "chemical ratio matching"]

abstract: A direct-current motor that facilitates the assembly and mounting of components of the motor, including a front bracket made of synthetic resin and defining recesses. A plurality of metallic brushholders are located in the recesses. The protection of the motor is improved by the waterproofing construction of the motor, including motor cords, and has a sturdy construction.
problem: Improving assembly, mounting, and waterproofing of a DC motor while maintaining component protection.
constraint: Balancing the non-conductive, lightweight properties of the resin bracket with the need for precise metallic component alignment and robust waterproofing in a compact motor design.
mechanism: A non-conductive structural bracket with recessed cavities that position conductive components while integrating sealing elements to isolate internal components from environmental ingress.
mechanism_raw: A synthetic resin front bracket with recessed cavities that house metallic brushholders, enabling modular component placement and sealing against moisture ingress through integrated waterproofing of motor cords and internal structure.

abstract: A container for adding to a liquid metal of known density and melting point an additive metal of lower density. The container comprises a tube portion of defined cross-section formed of a metal having a melting point higher than the melting point of the liquid metal and which can alloy with the liquid metal without being a source of pollution, and an insert comprising the additive metal placed within the tube portion. The tube portion has at least one end portion constricted so as to leave a passage with a cross-section smaller than the defined cross-section of the tube, the ratio of the passage cross-section to the tube cross-section being from 1:10 to 1:1000. The container overall has a density greater than the density of the liquid metal, so that it sinks when placed within a bath of the liquid metal. This invention finds application in modifying aluminum-silicon alloys with sodium, and additive metal which is lighter than and floats on a bath of liquid aluminum-silicon alloy.
problem: Delivering a reactive additive metal (e.g., sodium) to a liquid metal bath (e.g., aluminum-silicon alloy) without contamination or uncontrolled release.
constraint: Controlling the release rate via the passage-to-tube cross-section ratio to ensure gradual, uniform dispersion of the additive without premature leakage or structural failure.
mechanism: A dense containment vessel with a restricted flow passage that sinks in a liquid medium, enabling controlled release of a reactive substance through dimensional ratio constraints between the passage and vessel cross-section.
mechanism_raw: A high-density container with a constricted passage (cross-section ratio 1:10 to 1:1000) that sinks in the bath, gradually releasing the additive through the narrow passage while the tube material alloys safely with the liquid metal.

abstract: A cap construction including an exterior layer coextensive with an interior layer defining an cap-shaped structure including an elastomeric band to enhance securement of the structure overlying a swimmer's head portion. Sandwiched between the layers are a matrix of enclosed pneumatic chambers to afford a protective covering to the swimmer in use. A modification of the instant invention includes a plurality of coaxially aligned pneumatic chambers directed exteriorly through the opposed layers defining an elongate chamber defined by an ellipse of revolution. A further modification of the instant invention includes a series of spherical chambers captured between the layers including interconnecting conduits, wherein the conduits are secured at intersections with each pneumatic sphere defining a medial axis about each intersection with apertures directed through the conduits interiorly of the pneumatic chambers, or spheres to permit equalization of pressure throughout the matrix of spheres.
problem: Providing a protective head covering for swimmers that balances cushioning, secure fit, and pressure equalization.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and impact absorption while ensuring pressure equalization through precisely placed apertures and interconnecting conduits to avoid localized pressure differentials.
mechanism: A multi-layered structure with interconnected pressurized chambers and distributed apertures that equalize internal pressure gradients while transferring impact forces through a compliant network.
mechanism_raw: A layered structure with enclosed pneumatic chambers (spherical or coaxial) interconnected by conduits with apertures, allowing pressure equalization across the matrix while distributing impact forces through the elastomeric band and chamber network.

abstract: A centrifugal apparatus including an annular shell of flexible material with annular end rings and means for driving the shell in rotation through the end rings, an external discharge roller in engagement with the outer surface of the shell and directing material toward a discharge nozzle within the shell with the nozzle leading outwardly for delivery of the material from the shell. In one form, the ends of the shell are connected to the rigid ends by rings of flexible material. An arrangement is provided for applying axial tension to the flexible material of the shell.
problem: Efficiently moving material in a centrifugal apparatus while maintaining structural integrity of the rotating shell under high-speed rotation.
constraint: Balancing flexibility of the shell material with sufficient structural support to withstand centrifugal forces without rupture.
mechanism: Applying axial tension to a flexible annular structure maintains its geometric integrity during high-speed rotation, enabling an external directing element to channel material into an internal pathway without structural deformation or failure.
mechanism_raw: Axial tension applied to the flexible annular shell maintains its shape during rotation, enabling an external discharge roller to direct material into an internal nozzle without shell deformation or failure.
residual_terms: ["axial tension", "flexible annular shell", "centrifugal forces", "discharge roller", "internal nozzle"]

abstract: The present invention provides a refractory coating composition comprising: PA1 (i) 100 parts by weight of a hydraulic cement, PA1 (ii) 3 to 50 parts by weight of a re-emulsion type powdery resin, PA1 (iii) 50 to 600 parts by weight of a mixture of 15 to 85% by weight of aluminum hydroxide powder and 85 to 15% by weight of carbonate decomposable at a temperature of 300.degree. to 1000.degree. C., and PA1 (iv) 20 to 300 parts by weight of a lightweight aggregate having open cells at a ratio of at least 50% based on the total cells.
reason: The patent describes a material composition optimized for thermal resistance rather than a functional mechanism that produces an effect through a causal process.

abstract: Disclosed is a process for preparing a radiation image storage panel having a phosphor layer containing an activated stimulable phosphor, characterized in that applying a heat treatment that can secure the content of an activator in the activated stimulable phosphor. Disclosed is also a process for preparing a radiation image storage panel having a layer of a stimulable phosphor layer activated with an activator, wherein a stimulable phosphor matrix layer is formed, and thereafter the activator is diffusion added to the layer to form a stimulable phosphor layer.
problem: Ensuring uniform and stable activator content in stimulable phosphors for radiation image storage panels to maintain consistent radiation storage performance.
constraint: Maintaining activator concentration and distribution without degrading the phosphor matrix during thermal processing.
mechanism: Thermal processing induces uniform distribution or fixation of an additive within a matrix layer, optimizing functional properties of the matrix by controlling concentration and spatial arrangement without degrading the base material.
mechanism_raw: Heat treatment or diffusion-based addition of an activator to a phosphor matrix layer secures or distributes the activator uniformly, optimizing the phosphor's stimulability and retention properties.

abstract: A magnetic clasp having first and second magnetized portions, each with a hole disposed in the center thereof. The two portions are magnetically attractive to each other but are divided with a gap at their interface to permit easy separation thereof. A third magnetic portion is sized to fit within the hole in the first and second rings. The magnetic prevents lateral movement of the two portions at their interface. The male portion has attached to its opposite ends a chain, each end of the chain being further attached to a stop sized larger than the hole in the rings.
problem: Creating a magnetic clasp that allows easy separation of two components while preventing lateral misalignment during use.
constraint: Balancing magnetic strength to enable easy separation while maintaining sufficient lateral stability to prevent unintended displacement.
mechanism: A third magnetic element positioned within complementary recesses in two components provides lateral constraint at the interface while permitting axial separation through magnetic attraction forces.
mechanism_raw: A third magnetic portion positioned within holes in the two clasp halves acts as a stabilizer, preventing lateral movement at the interface while allowing axial separation via magnetic attraction.

abstract: A method for reconditioning diamond abrasive generator wheels having a layer of diamond particles brazed to the grinding surface involves heating the braze, binding the diamond particles above the liquid melting point, reorienting the diamond particles to increase their abrasive effect, then cooling the braze with the reoriented diamond particles until it resolidifies.
problem: Restoring the abrasive effectiveness of diamond generator wheels with worn or misaligned diamond particles.
constraint: Precisely controlling heating and cooling rates to avoid thermal damage to diamonds or degradation of the braze material.
mechanism: Heating a binding medium above its phase-transition threshold enables repositioning of embedded abrasive particles to enhance contact geometry, followed by controlled cooling to re-solidify the medium with particles in reoriented positions.
mechanism_raw: Heating the braze material above its melting point allows reorientation of diamond particles to increase abrasive contact, followed by controlled cooling to resolidify the braze with the reoriented particles in place.

abstract: The invention relates to surface-active compounds of the general formula (I) ##STR1## in which Ar is an aromatic system which is optionally substituted by C.sub.1 -C.sub.18 -alkyl, C.sub.1 -C.sub.18 -alkoxy, C.sub.2 -C.sub.5 -alkanoyl, C.sub.6 -C.sub.10 -aryl, (C.sub.6 -C.sub.10 -aryl)-C.sub.1 -C.sub.4 -alkyl, A has the formula --(X--O).sub.n --Y, wherein n denotes 1 to 50, X denotes ethylene or methylethylene and all or some of Y denote an acyl radical of a non-modified or modified natural resin acid and the other radicals Y denote radicals from the group comprising hydrogen, acyl radicals of saturated C.sub.1-24 -carboxylic acids, unsaturated C.sub.3-24 -carboxylic acids, C.sub.2-24 -hydroxy-fatty acids or C.sub.8-18 -alkyl-, -alkenyl- and -alkylidene-succinic acids, maleic acid, fumaric acid, sulfosuccinic acid, sulfuric acid, benzodicarboxylic acids and C.sub.1-16 -n-alkanedicarboxylic acids, W is a group --CHR-- or --CHR--N(R*)--T--N(R*)--CHR--, wherein R*is hydrogen, C.sub.1 -C.sub.4 -alkyl, C.sub.2 -C.sub.4 -hydroxyalkyl, a radical A or --C.sub.2 -C.sub.4 -alkylene-O--A and R is H or C.sub.1-9 -alkyl, T is C.sub.2 -C.sub.12 -alkylene, which is optionally interrupted by --O-- or --NR'--, R' is H, C.sub.1 -C.sub.4 -alkyl, C.sub.2 -C.sub.4 -hydroxyalkyl, A or C.sub.2 -C.sub.4 -alkylene-O--A, W* is H or --CHR--N(R*)--T--N(R*)A and m is 1 to 16. The compounds are prepared on the basis of oxyalkylated novolaks of the formula (I) in which all the radicals Y denote hydrogen. The polyalkylene glycol chains are now terminally esterified or half-esterified in a one- or multi-stage reaction in accordance with the definition of A. The resulting surface-active products are suitable as emulsifiers and dispersing agents for the most diverse fields of applications.
problem: Creating surface-active compounds with tunable amphiphilic properties for use as emulsifiers and dispersing agents across diverse applications.
constraint: The substituent types (e.g., natural resin acids, fatty acids) and chain lengths (n=1–50) must be carefully selected to maintain structural integrity while optimizing solubility and interfacial activity.
mechanism: Controlled chemical modification of polymer chains via terminal esterification or half-esterification with specific acyl radicals, enabling precise balancing of hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions to achieve desired surface activity.
mechanism_raw: Controlled chemical modification of polyalkylene glycol chains via terminal esterification or half-esterification with specific acyl radicals, enabling precise balancing of hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions to achieve desired surface activity.

abstract: Disclosed is a heat exchanger assembled of a plurality of oval heat exchanging pipes whose end portions are mounted in a leakage proof manner in oval openings of top and bottom plates. The ratio of maximum and minimum diameters of intermediate portions of the pipes if 2.5:1 through 8:1 whereas the ratio of the maximum and minimum diameters of the oval openings in the end plates is 1.2:1 through 3:1. A method of mounting the pipe end portions in the oval openings is based on a preliminary shaping of the end portions by the application of pressure from the outside toward the center axis of the end portions in the direction of their maximum diameter. The preshaped end portions are inserted into sealing collars surrounding the edges of respective plate openings. Thereafter the end portions are expanded by means of mandrels to sealingly close the openings.
problem: Achieving leak-proof mounting of heat exchange pipes in a heat exchanger while maintaining efficient thermal performance.
constraint: The diameter ratios (2.5:1–8:1 for pipes, 1.2:1–3:1 for openings) must balance structural support and thermal expansion compatibility to prevent seal failure under operational stress.
mechanism: Pre-shaping a pipe end via external pressure application to align with a shaped opening, followed by mandrel expansion into a sealing collar to create a tight, leak-proof seal without compromising pipe geometry.
mechanism_raw: Pre-shaping pipe end portions via external pressure application to align with oval openings, followed by mandrel expansion into sealing collars to create a tight, leak-proof seal without compromising pipe geometry.

abstract: This invention relates to a chemical method of effectively decontaminating metallic wastes that have been contaminated by radioactive substances and which have resulted from the demolition of nuclear power plants or reactors in operation. The method is that when the increase in the amount of dissolution of metal ions from the wastes causes the potential of the aqueous sulfuric acid to increase beyond a certain level, the dissolved metal ions are reduced electrolytically to control the potential of said aqueous sulfuric acid to become lower than said certain level.
problem: Preventing excessive dissolution of metal ions from radioactive waste during sulfuric acid decontamination, which could destabilize the process.
constraint: The reduction process must be precisely timed and controlled to maintain the acid potential below the critical level without over-consuming energy or introducing secondary contamination.
mechanism: Electrolytically reducing dissolved metal ions when a process parameter exceeds a threshold, thereby lowering the parameter and suppressing further metal dissolution through real-time feedback control.
mechanism_raw: Electrolytically reducing dissolved metal ions when the acid potential exceeds a threshold, thereby lowering the potential and suppressing further metal dissolution through real-time feedback control.

abstract: Apparatus and method for producing shaped products from granular materials, in particular food products from cereals such as rice, corn, wheat or the like, which are pressure-baked and afterwards expanded in a heatable mold defined in a fixed upper mold and a movable lower mold (punch). Preferably the mold comprises a peripheral mold element which is individually movable. Driving means are provided for actuating the movable punch which are in the form of two aligned, separately controlled hydraulic cylinders of which one cylinder defines a precise expansion and the other cylinder controls the compression in combination with separate end switch means.
problem: Producing shaped food products with precise expansion and compression profiles during molding.
constraint: The hydraulic pressure and timing between the two cylinders must be synchronized to avoid uneven expansion or compression that could deform the product or damage the mold.
mechanism: Independent hydraulic control of two aligned actuators—one for precise expansion and one for compression—combined with position sensors to coordinate sequential or simultaneous actuation for controlled shaping.
mechanism_raw: Independent hydraulic control of two aligned cylinders—one for precise expansion and one for compression—combined with end switches to coordinate sequential or simultaneous actuation for controlled shaping.

abstract: A snap-fit fastener assembly including a receptacle member and a post member. The receptacle member is attachable to a first body such as a section of canvas or the like and the post member is attachable to a second body such as the side of a boat or the like. The receptacle member is a unitary single piece body integrally formed of a suitable plastic material and the post member includes an attachment portion and a head portion. Post engaging portions are integrally formed on the inside of the receptacle member for consistently, repeatably and securely engaging the post member in a snap-fit action such that the section of canvas may be retainably attached across the sides of the boat for covering the boat. A flexible arm with an upstanding protrusion is formed on the inside of the receptacle member for engaging a cooperatively formed groove formed on an underside of the head portion of the post member. A finger tab is formed on the outside of the receptacle member to facilitate engagement and disengagement of the receptacle portion to the post portion. The receptacle member is formed with a body portion and a cap portion connected by an integrally formed strap portion.
problem: Securely and repeatably attaching flexible materials (e.g., canvas) to rigid surfaces (e.g., boat sides) using a fastener that allows easy engagement and disengagement.
constraint: The arm's flexibility and protrusion geometry must balance insertion force and retention strength to ensure reliable locking without excessive wear or difficulty in operation.
mechanism: A flexible element with an upstanding protrusion on a receptacle deflects during insertion to engage a groove on a post head, then returns to lock the protrusion into the groove, with a manual release tab enabling disengagement.
mechanism_raw: A flexible arm with an upstanding protrusion on the receptacle deflects during insertion to engage a groove on the post head, then returns to lock the protrusion into the groove, with a finger tab enabling manual release.

abstract: The degree of rigor in a bird or animal carcass is measured.
