The carcass is carried on a carrier which runs along a rail and over a slight step or drop, which subjects the carcass to a mechanical shock. A sensor monitors the variation with time of the force exerted by the carcass on the support means which arrests its fall. Circuitry analyzes the response to determine the degree of rigor. The carcass is then subjected to appropriate treatment, e.g., by its further processing being delayed to allow rigor to develop further. This can be done by providing a switch in the rail to route the carcass along a short path or a long path. The particular feature of the response which is monitored by the circuitry may, for example, be the time of fall, the amplitude of oscillation after the carcass has been arrested by the support means, the frequency of that oscillation, the rate at which that oscillation is damped, or some combination of those features.
problem: Determining the degree of rigor in animal carcasses to decide appropriate processing steps.
constraint: Balancing accurate rigor measurement with mechanical handling without damaging the carcass or disrupting throughput.
mechanism: Inducing a controlled mechanical perturbation to a transported object, then measuring dynamic response parameters (e.g., displacement, velocity, acceleration, damping characteristics) to infer its structural rigidity state.
mechanism_raw: Inducing a controlled mechanical shock via a step/drop during transport, then analyzing the dynamic force response (e.g., time of fall, oscillation amplitude, frequency, damping rate) of the carcass to assess its rigidity state.

abstract: A material extraction nozzle for separating a mixture of materials having different densities, comprising: a nozzle body shell having an outer surface with a tangentially located material inlet at an upper portion thereof and an inner surface defining in part a frustrum of a cone; a substantially conical diffuser section having an outer surface terminating in an apex, the diffuser section axially aligned within the nozzle body shell in a spaced relation therewith so as to form an extraction chamber with the inner surface of the nozzle body shell and the outer surface of the substantially conical diffuser section; an extracted material outlet port positioned axially through the substantially conical diffuser section; and at least one rejected material capillary outlet located below the apex of the diffuser section.
problem: Separating a mixture of materials with different densities.
constraint: Maintaining flow dynamics to ensure efficient separation without clogging or loss of throughput.
mechanism: Creating a spiral flow regime within a diverging flow channel to generate centrifugal forces that direct components of a material mixture to distinct outlets based on their density differences.
mechanism_raw: Using a conical diffuser section within a nozzle to create a spiral flow, where denser materials are directed to one outlet and lighter materials to another via centrifugal forces.

abstract: Compounds UCF1 and derivatives thereof exhibit anti-bacterial and anti-tumor activities and may be used for the preparation of anti-bacterial and anti-tumor agents. Compounds UCF1 may be produced by fermentation of a microorganism of the genus Streptomyces capable of producing compounds UCF1, preferably Streptomyces sp. UOF1 (FERM BP-2844) and recovering the desired compounds from the cultured broth. The compounds UCF1 have the formula ##STR1## wherein R represents either ##STR2## The compounds may be oxidized to obtain derivatives of formula ##STR3## which exhibit similar pharmacological activities.
reason: The patent describes a specific biotechnological process for producing a compound (UCF1) using a particular microorganism. While fermentation is a standard technique, the mechanism is not generalizable beyond producing this specific compound and does not involve a novel causal operation applicable to other fields.

abstract: A method is disclosed for making a brushing tool having a hub and a plurality of bristles extending from the hub. A mold defines a cavity which is divided into a closable mold cavity and a bristle cavity. At least one bristle locating pin is disposed within the bristle cavity. At least one bundle of bristles is inserted into the bristle cavity adjacent to the at least one bristle locating pin so that one end of the bristles is disposed within the mold cavity. The mold cavity is then closed so that the ends of the bristles within the mold cavity are generally clamped together near the interface of the mold cavity and the bristle cavity. A thixotropic material in liquid form is injected into the mold cavity so that a portion of each bristle disposed within the mold cavity is surrounded by the thixotropic material. When the thixotropic material hardens, the portion of each bristle on the mold cavity becomes embedded in the hardened material, the hardened material thereby forming the hub of the brushing tool. In a preferred embodiment, the method is applied to a rotary brushing tool having a central hub and a plurality of bristles extending from the hub.
problem: Efficiently embedding bristles into a hub during brush manufacturing.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and clamping of bristles during injection to avoid misalignment or incomplete embedding.
mechanism: Using a partitioned mold assembly with alignment features to position and retain discrete elements, then introducing a flowable material into the mold cavity to encapsulate the retained elements and form a composite structure.
mechanism_raw: Using a two-part mold with locating pins to position and clamp bristle bundles, then injecting a thixotropic material into the mold cavity to form the hub around the clamped bristles.

abstract: Bakery oven for a continuous baking process which includes a baking chamber provided with a charging opening and a discharging opening, and containing a spiral conveying device provided with a helicoidal path for conveying the bakery products arranged on trays, plates, racks or the like from the charging opening to the discharging opening. This bakery oven is provided with frames ensuring the individual picking-up of the plates, trays, racks or the like outside the baking chamber to convey them by means of the spiral conveying device, and the spiral conveying device includes a mechanism for individually conveying and guiding the frames along the helicoidal path.
problem: Continuously baking bakery products while individually handling trays or racks.
constraint: Balancing individual tray control with the need for continuous, uninterrupted baking in a helical path.
mechanism: Employing a helical transport pathway with independently actuated carriers that sequentially engage and guide individual items along the path, enabling continuous motion while maintaining discrete item handling.
mechanism_raw: Employing a spiral conveyor with frames that independently pick up and guide trays along a helicoidal path, enabling continuous movement while maintaining individual product handling.
residual_terms: ["helical transport pathway", "independently actuated carriers", "discrete item handling"]

abstract: A servo controlled trolling motor steering system provides improved speed and steering control. The system includes apparatus for mounting the motor on a boat for rotation about an axis to effect steering of the boat. A foot pedal includes a base and a foot pad pivotally mounted to the base, the foot pad being pivotal by a user to command a desired steering direction. A membrane potentiometer senses rotational position of the motor to develop an electrical signal representative of the rotational position, the signal comprising a steering feedback signal. A second membrane potentiometer senses pivotal position of the foot pad relative to the base to develop an electrical signal representative of the pivotal position, the signal comprising a steering command signal. A steering control is mounted to the mounting apparatus for steering the trolling motor, including a servo driven gear set for rotating the trolling motor and an electrical control responsive to the steering command signal and the steering feedback signal for actuating the servo to rotate the trolling motor to steer the boat.
problem: Achieving precise and responsive steering control of a trolling motor based on user input, while accounting for real-time positional feedback of the motor.
constraint: The system must balance rapid response to user input with stable operation, avoiding overshoot or oscillation in the servo-driven gear set while maintaining real-time synchronization between command and feedback signals.
mechanism: A closed-loop feedback control system compares a desired input signal with a real-time measured output signal, and uses the resulting error to drive an actuator until the output matches the desired input, enabling responsive and stable control.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop feedback control system uses two independent position sensors: one to measure the user's desired steering command (via foot pedal pivot angle) and another to measure the motor's actual rotational position. The difference between these signals drives a servo-driven gear set to rotate the motor until the actual position matches the commanded position, enabling accurate steering.

abstract: The chromic anhydride contained in soluble form (chromic acid) in exhausted, polluted chromium plating baths is recovered by alkalizing the exhausted chromium plating liquid to a pH comprised between 3 and 7 at a temperature of 70.degree. C. with a commercial sodium hydroxide solution, keeping the mass in reaction at this temperature for an hour and filtration separating the precipitate obtained. The filtered solution having a specific gravity of 1.25 kg/l, contains CrO.sub.3 (22% in weight) which is then reduced with sulphur dioxide to obtain a solution containing basic chromium sulphate and sodium sulphate, suitable for use as a tanning bath; in this manner pollution is avoided and the waste chromium is exploited. The solution containing CrO.sub.3 can also be introduced into a hexavalent chromium salt production cycle.
problem: Recovering valuable chromic anhydride (chromic acid) from exhausted, polluted chromium plating baths to prevent environmental pollution and exploit waste chromium.
constraint: The pH must be maintained between 3 and 7 and the temperature at 70°C to achieve selective precipitation; the filtered solution must have a specific gravity of 1.25 kg/l with 22% CrO3 by weight for effective downstream reduction.
mechanism: Controlled precipitation via pH and temperature regulation followed by chemical reduction: adjusting the pH of a contaminated solution within a defined range while maintaining a specific temperature causes target compounds to precipitate and separate through physical filtration, then a reducing agent converts residual concentrated solution into chemically modified byproducts suitable for reuse in industrial cycles.
mechanism_raw: pH-controlled precipitation at elevated temperature followed by chemical reduction: alkalizing the waste liquid to a specific pH range (3-7) at 70°C causes targeted compounds to precipitate and separate by filtration, then sulfur dioxide reduction transforms the remaining CrO3-rich solution into chemically useful basic chromium sulfate and sodium sulfate suitable for reuse in tanning or salt production cycles.

abstract: Novel synthetic lubricants having high viscosity index are made from lower olefins. These materials have a viscosity above about 2 cS at 100.degree. C. and viscosity index above about 130 and are characterized by internal methyl groups attached to side chain tertiary carbon atoms. Hydrocarbon lubricant can be based on propene feedstock with the resulting oligomer containing less than 2.5 methyl groups per 12 carbon atoms.
problem: Producing synthetic lubricants with high viscosity index from lower olefin feedstocks.
constraint: The oligomer must contain fewer than 2.5 methyl groups per 12 carbon atoms to balance viscosity index performance with molecular weight and processability.
mechanism: Molecular architecture control during polymerization: polymerizing feedstock molecules such that branching occurs at specific carbon positions, creating a molecular structure that resists viscosity changes across temperature ranges, yielding lubricants with defined viscosity and viscosity index properties.
mechanism_raw: Molecular architecture control during oligomerization: polymerizing lower olefins (e.g., propene) such that internal methyl groups are positioned on side-chain tertiary carbon atoms, creating a branched molecular structure that resists viscosity changes across temperature ranges, yielding lubricants with viscosity above 2 cS at 100°C and viscosity index above 130.

abstract: A railless refrigerator display door constructed with two or more glass panels and having a peripheral door frame extending around the sides of the door and at the inside of the door without covering the outside glass surface of the door. Sealant is used to bond the glass panels to peripheral spacers separating the panels and to C-section structures which extend peripherally around the sides of the door. The door frame is also bonded to the C-section structures and glass panels by the sealant. Rubber bumpers attached to the C-section structures reduce heat transfer from the inside glass panel to the outside glass panel. As such, mechanical fasteners such as nuts, bolts or screws are not needed for the purpose of holding the refrigerator door together.
problem: Constructing a thermally insulated refrigerator display door without mechanical fasteners that could compromise insulation or create thermal bridges.
constraint: The peripheral door frame must extend around the sides and inside of the door without covering the outside glass surface, and the C-section structures must extend peripherally around the sides to maintain structural integrity while preserving the thermal break function.
mechanism: Adhesive bonding with integrated thermal isolation: using sealant to join components without mechanical fasteners, and incorporating insulating elements at junctions to reduce conductive heat transfer between adjacent surfaces while maintaining structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Adhesive bonding with integrated thermal breaks: using sealant to bond glass panels to peripheral spacers and C-section structures, and bonding the door frame to these components, eliminating mechanical fasteners entirely; rubber bumpers attached to the C-section structures provide thermal breaks that reduce conductive heat transfer between inner and outer glass panels.

abstract: A suitcase incorporates a foldable handle assembly (22) and wheels (15,16) which are automatically moved into protruding positions when the handle assembly is extended. With the extended handle upright, a major face of the case is substantially horizontal and further cases can be stacked on the case, which serves as a trolley.
problem: Creating a suitcase that can automatically deploy wheels and reorient itself for stacking and trolley-like use when the handle is extended.
constraint: The wheels must deploy automatically as a direct consequence of handle extension, and the handle must be foldable to allow the case to return to a closed, non-protruding configuration when not in use.
mechanism: Kinematic coupling of handle motion to wheel deployment and case reorientation: extending a foldable handle assembly automatically actuates a mechanical linkage to position wheels into operational orientation, and when the handle is upright, the case reorients to enable stable stacking through direct mechanical dependency between handle position and case geometry.
mechanism_raw: Kinematic coupling of handle extension to wheel deployment and case orientation: extending the foldable handle assembly automatically moves the wheels into protruding positions through a mechanical linkage, and when the handle is upright, the case reorients so its major face becomes substantially horizontal, enabling stable stacking of additional cases.

abstract: A framework assembly that can be selectively manipulated to a variety of configurations for leisure activity, hand and finger exercise and as a teaching aid for shape recognition. Respective circular frame members have a plurality of semi-circled frame members rotatably attached at their ends to the circular frame members in successively overlapping engagement along the lengths of the circular frame members. Two of the semi-circled frame members are rotatably attached to each other thereby providing a framework assembly that can be configured in virtually an infinite variety of shapes.
problem: Creating a framework assembly that can be reconfigured into a virtually infinite variety of shapes for leisure, exercise, and educational purposes.
constraint: The semi-circular frame members must be rotatably attached at their ends to the circular frame members in overlapping engagement, and the mutual rotatable attachment between two semi-circular members must be maintained to preserve structural continuity across all configurations.
mechanism: Rotatable joint coupling between curved segments: curved frame members are connected at their ends via rotatable joints in overlapping engagement, and additional rotatable connections between adjacent curved segments allow the framework to adopt variable configurations through rotation at the joints while preserving structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Rotatable joint coupling between curved frame segments: circular frame members have semi-circular frame members rotatably attached at their ends in successively overlapping engagement along the circular members, and two semi-circular members are rotatably attached to each other, allowing the entire framework to adopt different configurations through simple rotation of the segments at their joints.

abstract: The wiper plate is designed for ue with a variety of five gallon pails including both straight and tapered pails as well as with either cart applications or with rams. One unit allows a variety of pails to be utilized with the one device. Primary and secondary wipers provide continued contact with a tapered pail. For straight sided pails, a reversible tapered spacer provides varying wiper flexibility depending on whether the unit is going to be used with the ram or cart-mounted pail.
problem: Adapting a wiper mechanism to maintain consistent contact with pails of varying geometries (straight or tapered) in different mounting configurations (ram or cart).
constraint: Balancing wiper flexibility and contact pressure across different pail shapes while maintaining structural integrity and avoiding over-flexing that could compromise cleaning effectiveness.
mechanism: A variable compliance mechanism adjusts the flexibility of a contact element by altering its positional or orientational relationship, enabling primary and secondary contact surfaces to conform to both straight and non-straight geometries through mechanical reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A reversible tapered spacer adjusts the flexibility of the wiper assembly by altering its position or orientation, enabling primary and secondary wipers to conform to both straight and tapered pail surfaces through mechanical reconfiguration.

abstract: A dual transducer probe for measuring blood flow by Doppler effect measurement in which quantitative flow data can be compiled and flow constriction points as small as 10% and less can be pinpointed with relative ease. The probe is formed with two transducers, oriented at about 45.degree. from a bottom contacting surface of the probe so that transmission signals diverge at an angle of about 90.degree.. A first transducer directs pulsed sound waves into the direction of blood flow and a second transducer directs pulsed sound waves with the direction of blood flow. The transducers act as receivers for the respective pulses. Fluid velocity can be calculated due to the Doppler effect. By analyzing the signal frequency shifts from the two transistors the blood flow at a very minute region between the transducers, can be determined. Constrictions, corresponding to changes in flow can be pinpointed by moving the probe along the blood vessel.
problem: Pinpointing constrictions or flow variations in blood vessels with high spatial resolution using Doppler-based measurements.
constraint: Achieving sufficient angular separation between transducers to focus on a minute region while maintaining signal coherence and avoiding interference from adjacent areas.
mechanism: Two sensors oriented at complementary angles emit and receive energy waves, enabling triangulation of signal variations to isolate characteristics in a specific region between the sensors while maintaining coherence and minimizing interference from adjacent areas.
mechanism_raw: Two transducers oriented at complementary angles (e.g., 45° from a common surface, diverging at 90°) emit and receive pulsed sound waves, enabling triangulation of frequency shifts to isolate flow characteristics in a specific region between the transducers.

abstract: The present invention is a variable blending dispenser for fluids, particularly for fuel dispensers. The dispenser controls variable valves according to volumetric data observed by flow meters on input lines to the dispenser, by calculating measuring error as the difference between desired blend ratio and the observed blend ratio calculated from volumes of blend components dispensed. The dispenser successively corrects the settings of the valves after dispensing predetermined volumes, the corrections determined by a volume based PID error function so that the total amount of each blend component is separately and accurately measured while providing the desired blend ratio.
problem: Accurately maintaining a desired blend ratio of multiple fluid components during dispensing, despite measurement errors or component variability.
constraint: Balancing real-time correction speed with system stability to avoid oscillations while ensuring total component volumes remain precisely measured and the blend ratio converges to the target.
mechanism: A feedback control system continuously calculates deviations between desired and observed ratios using cumulative volume measurements, adjusting output actuators incrementally after predetermined volume thresholds to correct errors while balancing correction speed and stability.
mechanism_raw: A volume-based PID error function continuously calculates deviations between desired and observed blend ratios, adjusting valve settings incrementally after dispensing predetermined volumes to correct cumulative errors.

abstract: A boring bar has a body formed with an axial cut at the portion near its tip to define a pair of cut-apart portions. Insert mounting portions are provided on mutually opposite ends of the cut-apart portions at a tip end of the cut. A dimension adjusting mechanism is provided at an intermediate portion of the cut-apart portions. A dimension adjusting mechanism is provided at an intermediate portion of the cut-apart portions to change a boring diameter between the tips of cutting edges of inserts mounted on the insert mounting portions by moving the cut-apart portions along surfaces of the cut. A fixing screw is provided between a tip of the cut-apart portions and the dimension adjusting mechanism to fix the cut-apart portions together after adjusting the dimensions. In another arrangement, another cut is formed in the bar body at its end opposite from the end on which the inserts are mounted. A covering member is mounted on the bar body to cover this cut. It carries adjusting screws on both sides of the cut to press the bar body in a diametric direction.
problem: Adjustably controlling the boring diameter of a cutting tool to accommodate varying workpiece dimensions while maintaining precision and rigidity.
constraint: Maintaining structural rigidity and cutting force transmission during adjustment while ensuring the locking mechanism prevents unintended movement under operational loads.
mechanism: A split-component system uses an axial separation to create movable portions, which are shifted along the separation interface via an adjustment mechanism to alter spacing between functional elements, then locked in place with a securing mechanism to prevent unintended movement under load.
mechanism_raw: An axial cut divides the boring bar into movable portions, which are shifted along the cut surfaces via a dimension-adjusting mechanism to alter the spacing between cutting edges, then locked in place with a fixing screw.

abstract: A method and apparatus for manufacturing innerspring constructions for mattresses, cushions and the like, consisting of strings of jackets encasing each one coil spring, whcih are fixed side to side by means of an adhesive; the apparatus consisting of at least: PA1 a moving means or conveyor for moving a string of a particular size according to its longitudinal direction; PA1 a fixed applicator mounted in front of the conveyor, for depositing adhesive to a string moving along on said conveyor and PA1 means for positioning the coated side of said string to a similar string and pushing it into contact.
problem: Assembling flexible innerspring coils into a cohesive string structure with consistent spacing and adhesion for mattress or cushion construction.
constraint: Synchronizing adhesive application timing and positioning accuracy with conveyor speed to ensure uniform bonding without disrupting the continuous movement of the coil strings.
mechanism: A synchronized assembly process moves a first element longitudinally while a stationary applicator deposits a bonding agent onto the element, followed by a positioning mechanism that aligns and presses the coated element into contact with a second element, creating a bonded structure.
mechanism_raw: A conveyor moves a coil string longitudinally while a fixed applicator deposits adhesive onto the coils, followed by a positioning mechanism that aligns and presses the coated coils into contact with an adjacent string, creating a bonded assembly.

abstract: A nuclear energy plant housing a boiling water reactor utilizes an isolation condensers with nearly horizontal condenser tubes for both isolation condenser (IC) mode and passive containment cooling system (PCCS) mode, which is entered in response to a loss-of-coolant accident (LOCA). These tubes extend between a cylindrical distributor and a cylindrical collector. In either mode, the reactor vessel is coupled to the cylindrical distributor. Steam reaching the condenser is condensed to water, which flows back to the vessel, providing a cooling effect. In PCCS mode, gas exiting the tubes is trapped and diverted into a wet well. This diversion path is not avialable in IC mode. As a result water exits the tubes more slowly in IC modes in PCCS mode. The water remaining in the tubes during IC mode renders the condenser less efficient. This lower efficiency partially offsets the greater heat exchange in IC mode due to higher temperature differentials and the relatively absence of noncondensable gases. Accordingly, a larger percentage of the condenser area used during PCCS mode can also be used during IC mode. This amounts to a relatively thorough hybrid utilization of the condenser. The result is a dual-function condenser that is smaller, less expensive, more reliable, and more easily maintained than alternative dual-function condensers.
problem: Efficiently and reliably cooling a nuclear reactor during both normal operation and loss-of-coolant accidents (LOCAs) using a single condenser system.
constraint: The system must balance higher heat exchange efficiency in IC mode (due to temperature differentials) against reduced efficiency from retained water, while ensuring gas diversion paths are only available in PCCS mode.
mechanism: A shared heat exchange component operates in two distinct modes, with fluid pathways selectively routed through the component based on operational state. In one mode, gas is diverted to a secondary containment region, while in the other mode, condensed fluid exits through the same component with reduced flow velocity due to retained material. The component's geometry enables partial functional overlap between modes, trading off heat transfer efficiency against operational flexibility.
mechanism_raw: A dual-function condenser uses the same tubes for both isolation condenser (IC) and passive containment cooling system (PCCS) modes. In PCCS mode, gas is diverted into a wet well, while in IC mode, water exits more slowly due to retained condensate. This hybrid utilization allows a larger percentage of the condenser area to be shared between modes, balancing heat exchange efficiency and operational requirements.
residual_terms: ["heat exchange component", "fluid pathways", "condensed fluid", "gas diversion", "retained material"]

abstract: According to the present invention, the inside of a crucible in which a molten raw material is placed is partitioned off with a partition ring so that a pulled single crystal is surrounded and the molten raw material may be moved and granular silicon is supplied to the outside of the partition ring, thereby to form the whole surface of outside molten liquid as a granular silicon soluble region so as to maintain the molten liquid surface on the inside of the partition ring at almost a constant level, and also to set the temperature of the molten liquid on the outside of the partition ring higher than the temperature of the inside thereof at least by 10.degree. C. or higher by covering the partition ring and the molten liquid surface on the outside thereof with a heat keeping board.
problem: Maintaining a stable molten liquid surface level and temperature gradient during single-crystal growth to ensure uniform crystal quality.
constraint: The temperature differential between internal and external regions must be maintained (≥10°C) while preventing surface level fluctuations that could disrupt crystal growth.
mechanism: A physical barrier divides a processing chamber into regions with differing thermal and material properties. A granular buffer zone outside the barrier stabilizes the surface level of a molten material inside the barrier by maintaining mass balance through solubility. A thermal insulator covers the barrier and external surface, enforcing a minimum temperature differential between internal and external regions to preserve a controlled gradient.
mechanism_raw: A partition ring divides the crucible interior, creating a granular silicon region outside the ring. This granular region acts as a soluble buffer that maintains the molten liquid surface level inside the partition at a constant height. A heat-insulating board covers the partition and external molten surface, ensuring the external temperature remains at least 10°C higher than the internal region.
residual_terms: ["physical barrier", "granular buffer zone", "molten material", "thermal insulator", "temperature differential"]

abstract: Transparent image-recording elements that contain ink-receptive layers that can be imaged by the application of liquid ink dots. The ink-receptive layers contain a combination of: PA1 (i) a vinyl pyrrolidone; PA1 (ii) particles of a polyester, namely a poly(cyclohexylenedimethylene isophthalate-co-sodiosulfobenzenedicarboxylate); PA1 (iii) a homopolymer or a copolymer of an alkylene oxide containing from 2 to 6 carbon atoms; PA1 (iv) a polyvinyl alcohol; PA1 (v) nonylphenoxypolyglycidol; and PA1 (vi) inert particles. A printing method which employs the transparent image-recording elements also is described.
reason: The patent describes a specific material composition (a combination of polymers and particles) without explaining a causal functional relationship beyond the material's properties. It is a list of components rather than a mechanism.

abstract: A composition comprising: PA1 (a) isotactic polypropylene; and PA1 (b) a copolymer of ethylene and an alpha-olefin having at least 3 carbon atoms and having a density equal to or less than 0.915 gram per cubic centimeter and a molecular weight of at least about 250,000 wherein the ratio of flow indices of component (a) to component (b) is in the range of about 60:1 to about 200:1.
reason: The patent specifies a polymer blend with a defined flow index ratio but does not describe a causal functional mechanism beyond material property optimization. It is a material composition, not a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: An improved snow thrower and specifically an improved blower therefor that improves efficiency and reduces the likelihood of snow accumulation. The blower casing is connected to the auger housing by an exit opening that is disposed and sized so that snow blown by the blower will not reenter the auger housing. The peripheral edge of the blower casing is curved so as to reduce the likelihood of snow accumulation.
problem: Improving snow thrower efficiency and reducing snow accumulation in the blower casing and auger housing.
constraint: The exit opening must balance airflow efficiency with preventing re-entry, while the curved edge must minimize accumulation without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A material transfer system incorporates a controlled exit aperture between two chambers, sized and positioned to prevent backflow of ejected material into the upstream chamber. A geometric feature on the downstream chamber's periphery reduces surface area where material can accumulate, using curvature to direct flow away from critical regions while maintaining structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: The blower casing is connected to the auger housing via an exit opening sized and positioned to prevent blown snow from reentering the auger housing. The peripheral edge of the blower casing is curved to minimize surface area where snow can accumulate, leveraging geometric design to control material flow and prevent unwanted buildup.

abstract: Disclosed is a rubber composition having high damping capacity as well as other excellent performances, for example, dependence of elastic modulus on temperature, shear deformation, etc., which is suitable for the laminated vibrationproofing structure. The rubber composition contains carbon black for use in rubber having an iodine adsorption of 70 to 115 mg/g and DBP adsorption (method A) of 115 to 70 ml/g in an amount of 30 to 70% by weight based on 100 parts by weight of a base rubber. The rubber composition is characterized by further containing: PA1 an aromatic petroleum resin having a softening point of 70.degree. to 140.degree. C. and a bromine value of 0 to 0.2; and PA1 cumarone-indene resin and/or rosin in the ratio which satisfies the relation: ##EQU1## wherein A is a total amount of cumarone-indene resin and rosin formulated, B is an amount of an aromatic petroleum resin formulated and B is not 0.
problem: Balancing high damping capacity with other performance properties (e.g., temperature-dependent elastic modulus, shear deformation resistance) in a rubber composition used for vibrationproofing structures.
constraint: The ratio of total second-resin amount (A) to first-resin amount (B) must satisfy a specific formula, and B must be non-zero, ensuring the first resin is always present to provide the baseline mechanical properties while the second resin modulates damping.
mechanism: Adjusting the proportional amounts of two distinct additive classes within a composite material to optimize a target property (e.g., energy dissipation) while preserving other baseline mechanical characteristics. Each additive class contributes differently to the material's viscoelastic response, and their ratio is constrained by a mathematical relationship ensuring the presence of a baseline additive to maintain structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Tuning the ratio of two classes of resin additives — a first resin (aromatic petroleum resin) and a second resin (cumarone-indene resin and/or rosin) — according to a defined mathematical relationship. The ratio controls how the damping behavior is enhanced while the other mechanical properties are preserved, because each resin class contributes differently to the viscoelastic response of the composite.

abstract: A hydraulic servovalve is controlled electrically through electromagnetic means. Electrical currents applied to force motors determine the relative position of a single, displaceable control assembly within the valve. Displacive movement of the control assembly changes, in reciprocal proportion, the inlet and outlet flow-metering clearances in each of the chambers of this open-passage type valve. The position of the control assembly determines the inlet and outlet flows within, and, therefore, the net flow through, each chamber. Moreover, since the chambers are each connected (either directly, or through a flow-impeding orifice) to one of the control ports, the position of the control assembly thereby determines the control flow delivered by the valve. Generally, both hydrostatic and hydrodynamic forces within the valve are balanced against corresponding forces, all acting upon the control assembly. However, any internal unbalanced hydrodynamic forces--which arise in proportion to control flow--are compensated by opposing hydrostatic forces, creating a naturally stable servovalve over a wide range of operating conditions.
problem: Maintaining stable operation of a hydraulic servovalve over a wide range of operating conditions despite internal unbalanced forces that arise during fluid flow.
constraint: The compensation must be proportional to the control flow so that the opposing hydrostatic force matches the unbalanced hydrodynamic force across the entire operating range, and the force balancing must work for both inlet and outlet flow-metering clearances simultaneously.
mechanism: Establishing a self-correcting force equilibrium in a fluid control system by opposing hydrostatic forces generated by a pressure source against hydrodynamic forces arising from fluid flow. Residual unbalanced forces, which scale proportionally with control flow, are actively compensated by adjusting the opposing hydrostatic forces to maintain balance across varying operating conditions.
mechanism_raw: Balancing hydrostatic and hydrodynamic forces within the valve against corresponding forces acting on the control assembly. Any residual unbalanced hydrodynamic forces — which scale proportionally with control flow — are actively compensated by opposing hydrostatic forces, creating a self-correcting force balance that drives the system toward equilibrium.

abstract: This invention relates to a high browning liquid smoke composition made from the condensable liquids of pyrolyed wood or cellulose. The high browning liquid smoke composition has the capability to flavor and to impart characteristic smoke color to a foodstuff and has a brix less than about 50, a browning index greater than about 30, and a transmittance value of greater than about 50% at 590 nm. A method of making the high browning liquid smoke composition and the use of the composition with a food product is also disclosed.
reason: The abstract specifies target performance metrics (brix < 50, browning index > 30, transmittance > 50% at 590 nm) but does not explain the causal mechanism by which the composition achieves these properties. It describes what the composition should do rather than how it produces the effect.

abstract: A double action mechanical press, especially for cupping operations in which an outer slide is provided within which an inner slide is reciprocally mounted on a common crankshaft. According to the present invention, a single dynamic balancer, out of phase from both the inner and outer slides, is provided on the crankshaft in order to counterbalance the inertial forces generated by the inner and outer slides during press operation.
problem: Counterbalancing inertial forces generated by two reciprocally moving slides (inner and outer) driven by a common crankshaft in a double-action mechanical press, where separate balancing of each slide would be complex or impractical.
constraint: The single balancer must be out of phase with both slides at the same time, meaning its angular position on the crankshaft is fixed relative to both slide motions, and it must generate a force magnitude sufficient to counterbalance the sum of both slides' inertial forces.
mechanism: Using a single dynamic counterbalance element mechanically coupled to a rotating drive member to cancel the combined inertial forces of multiple reciprocating components. The counterbalance element is positioned at a fixed angular phase offset relative to all reciprocating components, generating an opposing inertial reaction force that neutralizes their aggregate inertial effects in a single element.
mechanism_raw: Using a single dynamic balancer mounted on the crankshaft and positioned out of phase with both the inner and outer slides. Because the balancer's phase is offset from both slides simultaneously, its inertial reaction force cancels the combined inertial forces of both slides in one element, rather than requiring two separate balancers.
residual_terms: ["dynamic counterbalance element", "inertial forces", "rotating drive member", "angular phase offset"]

abstract: An assembly ties together a plurality of boiler tubes to increase their mechanical stability and maintain a uniform spacing between adjacent tubes. A tie bar has a plurality of periodically spaced fingers extending from a cross member to form openings between adjacent fingers with in which the boiler tubes tightly fit. A retainer projects orthogonally from ends of some of the fingers. A locking bar has wedges spaced along one edge which engage the retainers clamping the boiler tubes between the fingers of said locking bar. Stops and brackets attach to the boiler tubes to support the fingers and cross member, thereby holding the tie bar in place during assembly.
problem: Tying together a plurality of parallel boiler tubes to increase their collective mechanical stability and maintain uniform spacing between adjacent tubes during assembly and operation.
constraint: The retainers must project orthogonally from the fingers so that the wedge engagement direction is perpendicular to the tube axis, and the stops and brackets must support the fingers and cross member to hold the tie bar in place during assembly before the locking bar is engaged.
mechanism: Creating a mechanically interlocked assembly using a primary bar with spaced engagement features and a secondary locking bar with complementary features. The engagement features grip and clamp the target objects between the two bars, while orthogonal projections on the primary bar interact with the secondary bar to lock the assembly in place during and after installation.
mechanism_raw: Using an interlocking mechanical system where a tie bar with periodically spaced fingers forms openings that grip the tubes tightly, retainers projecting orthogonally from some fingers engage with wedges on a locking bar, and the wedge engagement clamps the tubes between the fingers of the locking bar and the tie bar fingers, locking the entire assembly in place.

abstract: For cleaning at least one of the sides of the essentially vertical heat-transmitting walls between two fluids in a heat exchanger, solid particles are introduced into a stream of fluid, which particles are smaller than the distance between opposite walls defining the flow of fluid, said fluid with particles being introduced into part of a collection or distribution space above said walls and said particles being collected below said vertical walls and discharged from the heat exchanger. The particles are so heavy that they move downwards in the fluid even if this has an upward direction of flow between the walls. The particles are introduced above only part of the transverse plane above the vertical walls and switch means allow switching of said introduction to other parts of said transverse plane periodically. Thereby, the normal operation of the heat exchanger can continue with hardly any pressure loss during cleaning.
problem: Cleaning heat-transmitting walls between two fluids in a heat exchanger without significant pressure loss during normal operation.
constraint: Particles must be smaller than the distance between opposite walls (to pass through the flow channel) yet heavy enough to move downward against the fluid flow direction; the switching of injection points must be periodic to ensure complete surface coverage without disrupting normal operation.
mechanism: Solid particles denser than a fluid are introduced into the fluid stream above a portion of a transverse plane adjacent to vertical surfaces separating two fluids. The particles move downward (even against upward fluid flow) due to their weight, scrubbing the surfaces as they pass. The injection point is periodically switched to different portions of the transverse plane, so over time the entire surface is cleaned while normal fluid exchange operation continues with minimal pressure loss.
mechanism_raw: Solid particles heavier than the fluid are introduced into the fluid stream above only part of the transverse plane above vertical walls. The particles move downward (even against upward fluid flow) due to their weight, scrubbing the walls as they pass. The injection point is periodically switched to different parts of the transverse plane, so over time the entire wall surface is cleaned while normal heat exchange operation continues with minimal pressure loss.

abstract: A plurality of index members are arranged at desired positions on an end portion of a platen glass, the members being movable in a scanning direction of a scanner. A black mark is provided on a rear surface of each index member, and the mark as well as the original are read by an image reader, so that the positions of the index members can be detected. When one of the index members is detected as the scanner is moved, the image signals of the original included in the scanning region of the scanner are not outputted until the next index member is detected. In this manner, by continuously outputting image signals only of the desired areas of the original, the column skip edition can be readily and surely carried out.
problem: Selectively outputting only desired areas of an original during scanning (column skip editing) without manual post-processing.
constraint: Index members must be positioned at the desired locations and their marks must be detectable by the same image reader used for the original; the system must reliably gate output signals between detected markers without losing synchronization.
mechanism: Index members with detectable marks are placed at desired positions on a scanning surface and moved in the scanning direction. During scanning, an image reader detects both the original and the index marks. When an index mark is detected, image signal output is suppressed until the next index mark is detected, so only the regions between consecutive marks are outputted as desired areas.
mechanism_raw: Index members with detectable marks are placed at desired positions on a platen glass and moved in the scanning direction. During scanning, the image reader detects both the original and the index marks. When an index mark is detected, image signal output is suppressed until the next index mark is detected, so only the regions between consecutive marks are outputted as desired areas.

abstract: This invention pertains to a protective helmet having a plurality of vents therein and air supply tubing and filtration element for supplying filtered air to a user. The air supply tubing is connected to the filtration element mounted in the helmet and delivers this filtered air through an inlet one-way valve and a mouthpiece to the user upon demand. The inlet and an exit one-way flow valve maintain the proper flow direction during the inhale and exhale phases and prevent any back-flow from occurring.
problem: Supplying filtered air to a user in a protective helmet while maintaining proper flow direction during inhalation and exhalation and preventing backflow of contaminated air.
constraint: The valves must respond to the pressure differentials of the breathing cycle with appropriate timing; the inlet valve must prevent backflow from the exit side, and the exit valve must prevent backflow into the filtered air supply.
mechanism: Paired one-way valves (inlet and exit) automatically open and close based on pressure differentials created by the user's breathing cycle. During inhalation, the pressure drop opens the inlet valve and closes the exit valve, directing filtered air in. During exhalation, the pressure rise closes the inlet valve and opens the exit valve, directing exhaled air out. This automatic switching maintains unidirectional flow in each phase of the cycle.
mechanism_raw: Paired one-way valves (inlet and exit) automatically open and close based on pressure differentials created by the user's breathing cycle. During inhalation, the pressure drop opens the inlet valve and closes the exit valve, directing filtered air in. During exhalation, the pressure rise closes the inlet valve and opens the exit valve, directing exhaled air out. This automatic switching maintains unidirectional flow in each phase of the cycle.

abstract: In a sheet-fed offset press having at least one printing unit in which the blanket cylinder can be thrown on and off the impression cylinder and plate cylinder by a pressure-medium-energized actuating arrangement, the pressure medium energization is triggered by a control unit in accordance with the position of grip edge zones of the cylinders being in registration. In order to ensure that throwing on and throwing off take place when the grip edge zones of the cylinders are positioned immediately opposite one another, the control unit detects the position of the printing unit cylinders relatively to one another by way of an angular position sensor and also detects the actual speed of the press via a speed sensor. The control unit forms speed-dependent throw-on and throw-off actuating times which are advanced in the direction of rotation of the printing unit cylinders so that the reaction time is outside the time slot for grip edge zone registration. The invention reduces the very substantial constructional outlay needed in the case of pressure-medium-energized actuating arrangements to ensure reliable throw-on and throw-off at high printing speeds.
problem: Ensuring reliable engagement and disengagement of cylinders in a high-speed sheet-fed offset press when grip edge zones of the cylinders must be in registration, despite inherent mechanical reaction delays.
constraint: The timing advance must be proportional to the press speed so that faster speeds receive greater advancement; the angular position sensing and speed detection must be accurate enough to predict the correct actuation trigger point.
mechanism: The control unit detects the angular position of mechanical elements relative to each other and the actual operational speed. It then computes speed-dependent actuation times that are advanced in the direction of motion, so that the mechanical reaction (which has inherent delay) occurs precisely when critical zones are in registration. The advancement compensates for the system's reaction time.
mechanism_raw: The control unit detects the angular position of the printing unit cylinders relative to each other and the actual press speed. It then computes speed-dependent throw-on and throw-off actuation times that are advanced in the direction of rotation, so that the mechanical reaction (which has inherent delay) occurs precisely when the grip edge zones are in registration. The advancement compensates for the system's reaction time.
residual_terms: ["angular position sensing", "operational speed", "actuation times", "reaction time", "mechanical elements"]

abstract: A method and structure in which an adsorbate atom or molecule is repositioned on a substrate surface by moving the tip of an STM to a position adjacent to the atom to be moved and causing the atom to be attracted to the tip. While the atom remains bound to the surface (or, alternatively, is lifted), the tip is moved laterally to drag (or carry) the atom to a desired position at which it is bound to the surface. The atom may be repositioned in close proximity to an atom of the same or another type on the same or a different substrate to create a desired multi-atom structure or synthesize a molecule, or an atom may be removed to cleave a multi-atom structure, or a change in state of a multi-atom structure may be effected. Atoms may also be repositioned to write indicia on a storage medium by dragging or carrying atoms into the desired information-bearing pattern, for example, by dragging or carrying selected atoms out of a respective one of a plurality of parallel atom rows using the tip of an STM to thereby write indicia at locations denoted by the removed atoms.
problem: Repositioning individual atoms on a substrate surface to create desired multi-atom structures, synthesize molecules, or write information patterns with atomic precision.
constraint: The tip-to-atom interaction must be controlled to attract the atom without fully detaching it (or to lift and carry it stably); the lateral movement must be precise enough to place the atom at the exact desired location on the substrate.
mechanism: A probe tip is moved to a position adjacent to a target atom, causing the atom to be attracted to the tip via electronic forces. While the atom remains bound to the surface (or is lifted), the tip is moved laterally to drag or carry the atom to a desired position where it re-binds to the surface. This allows precise placement of individual atoms to form structures or patterns.
mechanism_raw: The tip of a scanning tunneling microscope (STM) is moved to a position adjacent to a target atom, causing the atom to be attracted to the tip via electronic forces. While the atom remains bound to the surface (or is lifted), the tip is moved laterally to drag or carry the atom to a desired position where it re-binds to the surface. This allows precise placement of individual atoms to form structures or patterns.

abstract: A cage-type stranding machine includes a rotatably mounted supporting pipe (6) and radially outwardly oriented longitudinal webs (7) attached to the supporting pipe and distributed uniformly around its circumference, resulting in greater stiffness which permits higher rpm. Spool carriers (9) are rotatably supported by supporting shields (12), which are attached to the longitudinal webs. The supporting shields and the rotation axes (13) of the spool carriers are arranged at an angle to the supporting pipe to reduce the rotation circle diameter, which again permits an increased rpm in operation so that the production output can be increased.
problem: Increasing production output in a cage-type stranding machine by enabling higher rotational speeds (RPM) without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing increased stiffness from the webs against the need to reduce the rotation circle diameter to avoid excessive centrifugal forces.
mechanism: Structural rigidity is increased through distributed load-bearing elements arranged circumferentially around a central support, while component orientation is adjusted to reduce rotational radius. This dual approach minimizes mechanical stress and rotational inertia, enabling higher-speed operation without structural failure.
mechanism_raw: Structural stiffness is enhanced by radially oriented longitudinal webs distributed uniformly around a supporting pipe, increasing rigidity. Spool carriers are arranged at an angle to the supporting pipe, reducing the rotation circle diameter. This combination allows higher RPM operation by minimizing rotational inertia and mechanical stress.

abstract: A yarn feed assembly for circular knitting machines for presenting one or more yarns chosen from a plurality of available yarns into the needle path under the control of a microprocessor. An arcuately movable sector-shaped yarn guide includes a plurality of openings therein for positioning a plurality of yarns in spaced parallel position with each other. A toggle clamp for each yarn located downstream from the yarn guide keeps the yarns taut in their normal stored position. To select a yarn for feeding to the feed station, a transfer arm selects the yarn positioned in a pickup position by the yarn guide. As the transfer arm begins to move, the corresponding toggle clamp releases, and the yarn is then fed onto its yarn feed location.
problem: Selecting and feeding a specific yarn from a plurality of available yarns into a circular knitting machine's needle path under microprocessor control.
constraint: Maintaining tension in non-selected yarns while ensuring precise release timing of the toggle clamp to avoid yarn slack or misalignment.
mechanism: Multiple yarns are positioned in parallel and maintained under tension by selectively engaged retention mechanisms. A coordinated actuation system releases tension in a target yarn at a precise moment relative to a transfer movement, allowing selective feeding while non-target yarns remain taut.
mechanism_raw: A sector-shaped yarn guide positions yarns in parallel, while toggle clamps downstream maintain tautness. When a transfer arm selects a yarn, the corresponding toggle clamp releases in coordination with the arm's movement, allowing the selected yarn to feed while others remain taut.

abstract: For acid copper plating baths containing a brightener used to produce smooth copper coatings of high brilliancy, it has been found that the "break-in" period normally needed after a brightener is added to the plating bath, has been virtually eliminated by use of the brightener of this invention. This brightener consists essentially of a peroxide oxidation product of a dialkylamino-thioxomethyl-thioalkanesulfonic acid wherein each alkyl and alkane group individually contains 1 to 6 carbon atoms and wherein the peroxide oxidation of the dialkylamino-thioxomethyl-thioalkane-sulfonic acid is carried out in an acid, aqueous medium having a pH of not more than about 1. In an added embodiment of this invention the acid copper plating bath also contains hydrolysis products of the peroxide oxidation product of a dialkylamino-thioxomethyl-thioalkanesulfonic acid.
reason: The mechanism is a specific chemical composition (peroxide oxidation product of a dialkylamino-thioxomethyl-thioalkanesulfonic acid) tailored to acid copper plating baths. While it solves the problem of eliminating a break-in period, the solution is inherently tied to the chemical structure and pH conditions of the plating process, limiting its transferability to other fields.

abstract: Bulk form of superconducting materials are produced by pouring a melt a O.sub.2 -containing superconducting material into a heated mold, cooling the mold until solidification begins, removing the cast object from the mold, gradually cooling the cast object to prevent the development of thermal stresses, and then annealing the cast, cooled object to restore O.sub.2 to near equilibrium levels. The bulk form produced according to the present invention may be used as a sputtering target in the production of wires, or as a bulk form semiconductor.
problem: Producing bulk superconducting materials without thermal stress or oxygen depletion during solidification.
constraint: Balancing rapid initial cooling to initiate solidification with gradual cooling to avoid thermal stress, while precisely controlling oxygen content during annealing.
mechanism: A material is subjected to a two-stage thermal process: initial rapid cooling to initiate solidification, followed by gradual cooling to prevent thermal stress. A post-solidification treatment restores material composition to equilibrium levels, ensuring structural stability and functional properties.
mechanism_raw: A melt is poured into a heated mold, cooled until solidification begins, then removed and gradually cooled to prevent thermal stress. Annealing restores oxygen to near-equilibrium levels, ensuring material stability and usability as a sputtering target or semiconductor.
residual_terms: ["two-stage thermal process", "rapid cooling", "gradual cooling", "post-solidification treatment", "equilibrium levels"]

abstract: A crimping system for crimping electrical connectors to cables. The system can automatically sense the size of a connector and can automatically determine a minimum acceptable distance of work travel in relation to the size of a connector. The system can crimp articles and control the movement of an indentor by use of a computer. The system can sense predetermined crimping information and at least partially record crimping information. The system can determine the occurrence of a bad crimp. The system can monitor predetermined characteristics of the crimping system. The system can sense free travel movement of an indentor and determine appropriate work travel movement of the indentor relative to sensed free travel movement. The system can sense free travel movement of an indentor and compare sensed free travel movement to a stored memory of potential free travel movements and connector sizes. The system can have a computer controller for, at least partially controlling a hydraulic drive system. The system can have a diagnostic monitor for use in evaluating both past and present operation of the system. A method of is disclosed for determining indentor work travel movement of crimping apparatus and a method of controlling a system for hydraulically crimping electrical connectors is also disclosed.
problem: Ensuring proper crimping of electrical connectors to cables by adaptively determining work travel based on connector size and system diagnostics.
constraint: Accurately correlating free travel measurements to connector sizes and maintaining real-time feedback control to prevent under- or over-crimping.
mechanism: Displacement of an actuating element is measured and compared to stored mappings between displacement values and target parameters. A controller adjusts actuation force in real-time based on this comparison, while a diagnostic system evaluates historical and current performance data to identify deviations from acceptable crimping outcomes.
mechanism_raw: The system senses free travel movement of an indentor, compares it to stored data mapping free travel to connector sizes, and calculates the minimum acceptable work travel. A computer controller adjusts hydraulic actuation in real-time, while a diagnostic monitor evaluates past and present performance to detect bad crimps.
residual_terms: ["displacement measurement", "stored mappings", "actuation force", "real-time adjustment", "diagnostic system", "performance data"]

abstract: A reactor for epitaxial growth wherein a susceptor on which semiconductor wafers are placed is heated by a heater, while rotating around a vertically provided gas feed pipe in a bell jar and a gas introduced through the gas feed pipe into the bell jar is decomposed to deposite a crystalline semiconductor material on the wafers, the susceptor having a plurality of pockets for positioning the wafers in which the pockets are arranged on the uniform temperature region of the susceptor other than the temperature-unstable peripheral portion thereof, thereby preventing production of defective products due to dislocation in crystal growth.
problem: Preventing defects in crystal growth caused by temperature instability during epitaxial deposition.
constraint: Balancing the need for uniform temperature distribution with the geometric limitations of the heating and gas distribution system.
mechanism: Selectively positioning workpieces within spatially defined zones of a temperature-controlled surface to avoid regions with thermal gradients, ensuring process uniformity through geometric alignment with stable thermal conditions.
mechanism_raw: Positioning substrates in regions of uniform temperature on a heated surface, avoiding thermally unstable peripheral areas, to ensure consistent crystal formation.

abstract: An electrical connector includes a spring contact member mounted in a housing which has an opening for receiving an edge of a printed circuit card. The spring contact member has a contact area urged into electrical connection with a contact pad on the printed circuit card as the edge of the board is inserted into the opening. The spring contact member has a dog-legged portion extending from the contact area in the direction of insertion of the printed circuit card to define a recessed area of the spring contact member facing the board in the opening. The recessed area of the spring contact member is aligned with the contact pad when the printed circuit card is fully inserted into the opening in the housing.
problem: Ensuring reliable electrical contact alignment during insertion of a circuit board into a connector.
constraint: Maintaining contact force and alignment accuracy while accommodating manufacturing tolerances in board insertion.
mechanism: Employing a deformable conductive element with a geometrically constrained interface that adapts its shape during insertion to achieve self-alignment and maintain contact pressure against a target surface.
mechanism_raw: Using a shaped spring contact with a recessed area that self-aligns with the contact pad when the board is fully inserted, leveraging mechanical deformation during insertion.
residual_terms: ["deformable conductive element", "geometrically constrained interface", "contact pressure", "target surface"]

abstract: The invention utilizes a hydrogen atmosphere during the heat treatment of an Al-Li alloy. The presence of such a reducing atmosphere prevents the reaction of surface lithium atoms with atmosphere components that would cause a diffusion and subsequent depletion of lithium atoms in the region near the surface. As a result, the present invention suppresses lithium loss and consequently prevents the formation of agglomerated lithium atom vacancies which would otherwise develop into microscopic metallic porosity. The prevention of such a condition maintains high fatigue resistance and corrosion resistance in association with metallic strength.
problem: Preventing lithium depletion and porosity in Al-Li alloys during high-temperature processing.
constraint: Controlling atmosphere composition and temperature to avoid unintended chemical interactions while maintaining process efficiency.
mechanism: Introducing a reactive gaseous environment to suppress surface-level chemical reactions that would otherwise drive selective atom depletion, thereby preserving bulk composition during high-temperature processing.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a reducing atmosphere (e.g., hydrogen) to suppress surface reactions that would otherwise deplete lithium atoms and create vacancies.
residual_terms: ["reactive gaseous environment", "surface-level chemical reactions", "atom depletion", "bulk composition"]

abstract: An apparatus for forming filled dough products. The apparatus includes a first belt conveyor and a second belt conveyor located below and at the end of the first belt conveyor. A first air jet stream is discharged through a thin rectangular orifice against the underside of a sheet of dough carrying a cylindrical filling as the sheet of dough leaves the first belt conveyor to support the leading edge of the sheet of dough. A deflector engages the leading edge of the sheet of dough to bend the corner thereof upwardly. A second air jet stream discharges through a thin rectangular orifice against the sheet of dough to reversely fold the leading corner of the sheet of dough against the cylindrical filling and also bends the trailing edge of this sheet of dough onto the second conveyor belt after the sheet of dough and the filling have dropped to the second belt conveyor. Rollers crease the sheet of dough outwardly of the cylindrical filling. A third air jet stream discharges through perforations positioned on opposite sides of the second belt conveyor to lift the opposite corners of the sheet of dough about the creases and to fold the corners inwardly over the filling. A paddle blade creases the folded dough rearwardly of the filling. An overhead belt conveyor moving opposite to the second belt conveyor completes the rolling of the dough and filler.
problem: Automatically folding dough around a filling to form sealed, shaped food products.
constraint: Synchronizing airflow pressure, mechanical deflection timing, and conveyor movement to avoid tearing or misalignment of the dough.
mechanism: Coordinating temporally sequenced fluidic forces and mechanical barriers to progressively manipulate a deformable material through controlled bending, folding, and sealing actions via synchronized spatial actuation.
mechanism_raw: Sequencing directed air jets and mechanical deflectors to progressively bend, fold, and crease the dough around the filling through coordinated spatial and temporal control.

abstract: Disclosed is a matrix material for implantation in a mammalian host comprising biocompatible mineral-free type I bone collagen, xenogenic to the host, and biodegradable therewithin. The matrix is manufactured from protein-extracted bone powder treated with certain swelling agents to increase its surface area and porosity. The matrix may be combined with osteogenic protein to induce reliably and reproducibly endochondral bone formation. It also can be used as a surface coat around implantable prosthetic devices to promote cellular ingrowth or as a carrier for sustained release of various therapeutic compositions.
problem: Promoting cellular ingrowth and bone formation in implantable biomedical materials.
constraint: Balancing increased porosity with structural integrity and controlled biodegradation rates to match tissue regeneration timelines.
mechanism: Modifying a biocompatible matrix structure through controlled expansion to increase surface-area-to-volume ratio and interconnected void spaces, enhancing interaction with biological tissue while maintaining structural coherence.
mechanism_raw: Modifying surface area and porosity of biocompatible collagen matrices using swelling agents to enhance interaction with host tissue.

abstract: Novel phenol derivatives of the general formula: ##STR1## wherein R.sup.1, R.sup.2, R.sup.3, R.sup.4, R.sup.5, X, Y and n are as defined in the specification, which have therapeutic and prophylactic activities against cerebral, cardiac, renal and pulmonary circulatory system diseases, respiratory diseases, allergy, anaphylactic shock, endotoxin shock, inflammation and the like as well as inhibiting activities against vascularization by oncocytes.
reason: The abstract describes a chemical compound's therapeutic application without specifying a causal mechanism beyond the chemical structure's interaction with biological systems. The mechanism of action (e.g., receptor binding, enzyme inhibition) is not detailed, making it too specific and non-transferable.

abstract: A polyurethane polyamide self-crimping conjugate fiber having eccentric conjugate form, comprises a high hardness polyurethane having a Shore hardness D of 58 to 75 and a polyamide having a melting point of at least 200.degree. C., which has a excellent extension stress properties and excellent heat resistance. The conjugate fiber is suitable for hosiery products and tricot products, having excellent transparent of fabric and a high level of fitting properties.
problem: Creating a fiber with high hardness, heat resistance, and extension stress while enabling self-crimping for textile applications.
constraint: Balancing the hardness and flexibility of the two materials to achieve self-crimping without compromising structural integrity or heat resistance.
mechanism: Combining two materials with differing thermal/mechanical properties in a structured arrangement. During processing, differential shrinkage or expansion between the materials induces self-texturing, creating a composite with enhanced structural and thermal characteristics without external mechanical action.
mechanism_raw: Combining two materials with differing thermal/mechanical properties (polyurethane and polyamide) in an eccentric conjugate structure. During processing, differential shrinkage or expansion between the materials induces self-crimping, creating a textured fiber without external mechanical action.

abstract: A delay fuse for a warhead (1) including at least two charges (3, 8) for sequential detonation disposed inside a casing (2). The delay fuse comprises a screen (6) movable in a longitudinal axial direction inside the casing (2) and under the effect of the first charge detonating, from a starting position to a destination position in which it acts on control means (12) for firing a second charge. The fuse includes a component of compressible material (13) disposed inside the casing between the screen (6) and the control means (12). The invention is applicable to shells, rockets, or missiles.
problem: Creating a reliable delay between sequential detonations in a warhead fuse to control timing of explosive charges.
constraint: Ensuring precise delay timing and mechanical reliability under extreme conditions (e.g., shock, temperature) while maintaining compactness.
mechanism: A movable element within a casing is displaced by the force of a first actuation, which then triggers a secondary actuation. A compressible medium between the movable element and the secondary trigger modulates the delay duration by absorbing and transmitting force over time, enabling controlled sequential activation.
mechanism_raw: A movable screen inside a casing is displaced by the force of a first charge, which then actuates control means to fire a second charge. A compressible material between the screen and control means modulates the delay duration by absorbing and transmitting force over time.

abstract: System and method for low temperature treatment of organic wastes containing potentially toxic concentrations of metals is described which comprises forming the waste material into pellets of preselected size, mixing the pellets with inert material, incrementally heating the mixture in air from about 200.degree. C. to about 600.degree. C. in order to oxidize the pellets to the corresponding ash containing the metals, collecting the ash, and combining the ash with inert material and binder to form a solidified compact for disposal.
problem: Safely disposing of organic waste containing toxic metals by separating and stabilizing the hazardous components.
constraint: Controlling temperature to avoid volatilization of toxic metals while ensuring complete oxidation of organics and structural stability of the final compact.
mechanism: Incremental heating of a composite material in an oxidizing environment separates organic components into gaseous byproducts while retaining inorganic constituents. The retained inorganic material is then combined with stabilizing agents to form a solidified matrix, isolating hazardous components from environmental exposure.
mechanism_raw: Incremental heating of pelletized waste mixed with inert material in air oxidizes organic components into ash while retaining metals. The ash is then combined with inert material and binder to form a solidified compact, isolating the metals from environmental exposure.

abstract: A warp tension control apparatus includes a tension detector for detecting the tension of a warp and an operation mode controller for generating a control signal to drive a motor so as to minimize the deviation between the detected tension and a normal target tension. A long period stop mode controller is included for controlling the tension so that a target slack tension is set to be less than the normal target tension when a loom stop signal has been issued. A selector switch is provided for selectively switching to a contact connected to an output of the long period stop mode controller before entering a long unmanned operating period of the loom, the switch being disposed in a circuit between an input terminal of the long period stop mode controller which receives a loom stop signal and a warp tension slack device. A switch is provided for stopping the output of the operation mode controller when the long period stop mode controller outputs the slack tension control signal such that the warp tension when the loom is stopped is said to be less than that at the time of normal operation only when the selector switch is selectively switched to a contact connected to the output of the long period stop mode controller.
problem: Maintaining proper warp thread tension during normal loom operation and long unmanned stops to prevent thread damage or slack.
constraint: Switching between modes without disrupting ongoing operations and ensuring rapid tension restoration when normal operation resumes.
mechanism: A dual-mode control system employs a sensor to monitor tension and two distinct controllers: one for active operation and one for reduced tension during idle periods. A switching mechanism activates the idle mode prior to unmanned intervals and disables the active controller during idle mode, ensuring tension is dynamically adjusted without disrupting ongoing processes.
mechanism_raw: A dual-mode control system uses a tension detector and two controllers: one for normal operation and one for slack tension during stops. A selector switch activates the slack mode before unmanned periods, and a switch disables the normal controller when slack mode is active, ensuring tension is reduced only during stops.

abstract: A clothes washing machine includes an agitator driven for agitating clothes to be washed, a dc brushless motor for driving the agitator and a microcomputer-based control device. A voltage applied to the motor can be varied in accordance with a voltage value command delivered from the control device. The number of revolution of the motor is detected and compared with a reference number of revolution for determination of whether the motor is locked or not. When the control device sequentially detects at a predetermined number of times that the number of revolution of the motor is equal to or below the reference number of revolution or below, it is determined that the motor is locked.
problem: Detecting motor lock conditions in a washing machine to prevent damage or malfunction.
constraint: Balancing sensitivity to detect genuine lock events while avoiding false positives from transient speed fluctuations.
mechanism: Repeatedly measuring rotational speed of a driven element and comparing it to a reference threshold to detect stall conditions, using a control system to trigger corrective action when the measured speed falls below the threshold.
mechanism_raw: Repeatedly measuring motor speed and comparing it to a reference threshold to determine if the motor is stalled, using a microcomputer-based control system to trigger corrective action.

abstract: A lifting platform for motor vehicles having two vertically movable columns in which additional lifting elements are disposed is disclosed.
