The lifting elements are connected to a common drive means via traction means and guide rollers in such a way that the two lifting elements can be driven synchronously with a single drive means.
problem: Synchronizing the movement of two vertically movable lifting elements in a vehicle platform using a single drive source.
constraint: Maintaining precise synchronization without requiring independent drives, which adds complexity and cost.
mechanism: Mechanically coupling two movable elements via a flexible traction medium and guided contact points to enforce synchronized motion from a single drive source, distributing force evenly across both elements.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical coupling of lifting elements via traction means (e.g., belts, chains) and guide rollers to ensure simultaneous motion from a single drive, distributing force evenly.
residual_terms: ["mechanical coupling", "traction medium", "guided contact points", "synchronized motion", "single drive source"]

abstract: The invention relates to a cross-connector of plastic material for hollow profiled window grill bars introduced into the insulating space of an insulated window assembly consisting of two panes. Such a cross-connector consists of four legs positioned perpendicularly to one another and being configured such that they be inserted into the ends of the hollow profiled window grill bars in order to become fixed with these bars which are fixed to the peripheral frame of the window at their other ends. The present invention achieves the advantages of increased flexure and torsional strengths, and lower weight, while using a plastic material containing break-throughs, or alternatively, recesses. In addition, angled pins positioned oblique to the direction of insertion of the cross-connector legs result in a tighter, more permanent connection.
problem: Increasing flexural and torsional strength of a structural connector for hollow window grill bars while minimizing weight.
constraint: Achieving sufficient structural integrity with lightweight plastic material without compromising durability.
mechanism: Enhancing structural integrity of a lightweight connector through geometric interlocking features that mechanically engage with mating components, increasing resistance to flexural and torsional loads without adding mass.
mechanism_raw: Using a plastic cross-connector with angled pins and recessed break-throughs to mechanically interlock with the bars, enhancing connection strength through geometric features.
residual_terms: ["geometric interlocking features", "lightweight connector", "flexural and torsional loads", "mating components"]

abstract: A protective cover for use with a riding saddle includes a flexible central panel having side panels depending from its respective opposite sides for enclosing the stirrup leathers of the riding saddle. The flexible central panel has a sleeve attached to a front portion for receiving a saddle horn. According to this arrangement, the cover adjusted about the saddle by a drawstring inserted therethrough a casing defined by a folded edge of the flexible central panel, which permits the protective cover to be fitted onto riding saddles of different sizes. In order to maintain a snug fit of the flexible central panel to the riding saddle, the flexible central panel also includes elastic webbing, allowing the protective cover to conform to the complex curvature of the saddle.
problem: Creating a protective cover that adapts to varying saddle geometries while maintaining a snug fit.
constraint: Balancing adjustability for different sizes with consistent contact pressure to avoid looseness or over-tightening.
mechanism: Combining an adjustable casing with elastic elements to dynamically conform to varying surface geometries, maintaining consistent contact pressure through tension-based adaptation.
mechanism_raw: Combining a drawstring-adjustable casing with elastic webbing to dynamically conform to complex curvatures and sizes of saddles.

abstract: The present invention relates generally to paints and paint bases, and, more specifically to a process for providing a stable gel-free dispersion of copper pyrithione or pyrithione disulfide plus cuprous oxide biocide in paint. The resulting paint is storage stable and remains gel-free after several months of storage at room temperature.
problem: Maintaining long-term stability of a biocidal paint dispersion containing reactive or settling-prone compounds.
constraint: Preventing chemical degradation or phase separation of active ingredients during storage without compromising efficacy.
mechanism: Stabilizing a dispersion by controlling interparticle interactions and sedimentation dynamics through specific mixing or stabilization processes, preventing phase separation and chemical degradation of active ingredients during storage.
mechanism_raw: Formulating a gel-free dispersion by controlling particle interactions and sedimentation through specific mixing or stabilization processes.

abstract: A commercial grade cutlery sharpening machine of the hand-reciprocated type employs several novel features. Work-positioning is accomplished without the use of blade clamping structure by a pair of guide pins against which the back edge of the work is guided. An abrasive-material cartridge system is disclosed that allows rapid tool change. The tool holder includes a ramp and plastic stop that cooperate to allow full, even use of the abrasive material. The work table is adjustable in inclination for operator comfort and mounts readily by means of a common suction base.
problem: Achieving precise blade positioning and even abrasive usage in a sharpening machine without clamping mechanisms, while enabling rapid tool changes.
constraint: Balancing operator convenience (no clamping, rapid tool changes) with precision alignment and even abrasive wear to avoid uneven sharpening.
mechanism: Physical guides constrain a moving part's alignment during reciprocation, ensuring uniform contact between an abrasive surface and the workpiece. A modular component system enables rapid replacement of wear elements without manual adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Guide pins physically constrain the blade's back edge to maintain consistent alignment during reciprocation, eliminating the need for clamping. A ramp and plastic stop in the tool holder ensure full, even contact between the abrasive material and the blade surface, while a cartridge system allows quick replacement of abrasive components.

abstract: A halogenated organic compound is introduced into a plasma. In the plasma state, substances are very reactive and chemical substances which are not readily decomposed such as halogenated organic compounds are decomposed in a short time. Specifically, in a high-temperature plasma exceeding 10,000.degree. C., almost all molecules are considered to dissociate into atoms. A reactive substance such as water is introduced into a plasma together with a halogenated organic compound. The decomposed halogenated organic compound is caused to react with the reactive substance, for preventing the decomposed organic compound from returning to its original state.
problem: Decomposing recalcitrant halogenated organic compounds that resist conventional chemical breakdown methods.
constraint: Maintaining plasma temperatures exceeding 10,000°C while ensuring sufficient interaction between decomposed atoms and the reactive substance to achieve complete decomposition.
mechanism: A high-energy environment dissociates target molecules into reactive species, which are then directed to interact with an introduced reactive agent to drive irreversible chemical transformation and prevent reformation of the original compound.
mechanism_raw: High-temperature plasma dissociates molecules into reactive atoms, which are then forced to react with an introduced reactive substance (e.g., water) to prevent reformation of the original compound. The plasma environment ensures complete dissociation, while the reactive substance drives irreversible chemical transformation.

abstract: This invention relates to a method of fixing an inside panel of a car, and its fixing structure. In a structure for fixing an inside panel by employing an interior decoration material to form a passenger room of a car, the present invention relates to a method and a structure for fixing an inside panel of a car, particularly suitable for a railway car. An inside frame which is press-formed is fixed to frames of a car, and an inside panel is fixed to the inside frame through fasteners. Since the inside panel is fixed to the press-formed inside frame, surface uneveness does not occur on the inside panel even if any unevenness exists on the frames of the car. A cushion material is attached to the inside frame at the joint portion of two inside panels along the joint portion. The inside panel has a decoration sheet bonded to its surface, and this decoration sheet is bent back at the edge portions of the inside panel. Therefore, the appearance of the joint portion can be improved.
problem: Attaching interior panels to vehicle frames without creating surface unevenness caused by irregularities in the underlying structure.
constraint: Balancing structural rigidity of the intermediate frame with cost and weight considerations while maintaining aesthetic joint coverage.
mechanism: A rigid intermediate structure is affixed to a base frame, decoupling a surface panel from underlying irregularities. The panel is attached to this intermediate structure via mechanical fasteners, while compliant and decorative elements mask seam discontinuities.
mechanism_raw: A press-formed intermediate frame is fixed to the vehicle's structural frames, decoupling the panel from base-frame unevenness. The panel is then attached to this rigid intermediate frame via fasteners, ensuring a smooth surface. Cushion material at joints and bent decoration sheets mask seam irregularities.

abstract: Low temperature heat curable arylene sulfide copolymer compositions which are particularly suitable for use in coating applications are provided. The compositions basically comprise a first arylene sulfide copolymer having unsubstituted para- and ortho-aromatic sulfide repeating units in the polymer chain, and a second arylene sulfide copolymer having unsubstituted para-aromatic sulfide repeating units and alkyl-substituted aromatic sulfide repeating units in the polymer chain.
problem: Developing heat-curable polymer coatings that cure effectively at low temperatures without compromising performance.
constraint: Optimizing the ratio of copolymers to balance low-temperature curability with mechanical and chemical resistance in the final coating.
mechanism: Blending two polymer compositions with complementary structural units creates a material system with tailored thermal activation properties. The synergistic interaction between the polymers enables crosslinking at reduced temperatures while maintaining performance characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Blending two arylene sulfide copolymers—one with unsubstituted para- and ortho-aromatic sulfide units, and another with para-aromatic sulfide units plus alkyl-substituted aromatic sulfide units—creates a composition with tailored thermal curing properties. The copolymer synergy enables crosslinking at reduced temperatures.

abstract: A seat of a bicycle including a pair of rods disposed on the bottom, a plate disposed above the rods, a bracket disposed below the rods and fixed to the plate so as to fix the rods between the plate and the bracket, the bracket including two flanges formed on the bottom portion, a bag including a member disposed on the upper portion and having a pair of channels for engagement with the flanges of the bracket so that the member can be coupled to the bracket and so that the bag can be coupled to the seat.
problem: Securely attaching a bag to a bicycle seat in a manner that allows quick coupling and decoupling without complex hardware.
constraint: Ensuring the flange-channel interface provides sufficient retention force to prevent accidental disengagement during use while allowing easy manual release.
mechanism: A mechanical interlocking interface between a mounting bracket and a bag member enables tool-free attachment through lateral sliding engagement. The interface provides retention force sufficient to resist accidental disengagement during use while allowing manual release.
mechanism_raw: Flanges on the bracket engage with channels in the bag's upper member, creating a mechanical interlock that holds the bag in place. The channels allow lateral sliding engagement with the flanges, enabling tool-free attachment and removal.

abstract: An adjustable glarefoil assembly is provided for mounting to a median barrier which divides opposing lanes of a highway and operates to reduce the glare of headlights from oncoming vehicles. The glarefoil assembly includes a plurality of glarefoil blades which are adjustably coupled for angular movement with respect to a base runner section in an appropriate light blocking orientation. The base runner section is rigidly mounted to the top of the median barrier at between three and five spaced points, thereby preserving some latitude for vibrational movement within the base runner section. The glarefoil blades are each adjustable about a vertical, longitudinal axis so as to optimally provide sight obstruction for a variety of different road curvatures, as well as maintaining the best possible angle to prevent wind build-up.
problem: Reducing glare from oncoming vehicle headlights on highways while accommodating varying road curvatures and wind conditions.
constraint: Balancing blade adjustability for optimal glare reduction with structural rigidity to withstand wind loads and vibrational movement.
mechanism: Adjustably coupling light-blocking elements to a base structure allows angular repositioning for optimal orientation. The base is mounted at spaced intervals to maintain structural rigidity while permitting dynamic adjustment under varying environmental loads.
mechanism_raw: Adjustably coupling glarefoil blades to a base runner section allows angular repositioning of the blades to optimize light-blocking orientation. The base runner is rigidly mounted at spaced points to preserve vibrational flexibility, enabling dynamic adjustment without compromising structural integrity.

abstract: A mechanism for applying adhesive to a sheet comprising a plurality of glue applicators comprising valves or nozzles adapted to form a charge of adhesive at the tip of each. The sheet is moved toward the nozzles to permit adhesive spots to be deposited on the sheet. The nozzles have periods of deactivation after which they are reactivated. A cleaning and moistening sponge (or a tray with appropriate fluids) is provided to maintain the adhesive in the nozzles in usable condition during periods of deactivation so that the adhesive may be immediately used and deposited on the sheet upon reactivation of the nozzles.
problem: Maintaining adhesive usability in nozzles during periods of deactivation to ensure immediate functionality upon reactivation.
constraint: Ensuring the maintenance system does not interfere with active adhesive deposition while effectively preserving nozzle readiness.
mechanism: A maintenance element interacts with dispensing nozzles during inactive periods to prevent material solidification, preserving flow properties for immediate reactivation without recalibration.
mechanism_raw: A cleaning/moistening sponge or fluid tray interacts with the nozzles during deactivation periods, preventing adhesive solidification or clogging. This preserves the adhesive's flow properties, enabling rapid redeployment without recalibration.

abstract: An insulated building panel for use in residential or commercial construction comprising a core of expanded polystyrene (EPS) bonded to at least two exterior skins of oriented strand board by a urethane laminating adhesive and treated with a sodium borate, such as disodium octaborate tetrahydrate, to preserve and protect the building panels from attack by many types of insects, molds, and fungi is disclosed. In an alternative embodiment, EPS for a variety of construction and insulating uses so protected are disclosed.
problem: Protecting building panels from biological degradation (insects, mold, fungi) while maintaining thermal insulation and structural performance.
constraint: Balancing the concentration of sodium borate to ensure efficacy against pests without compromising the panel's insulating properties or structural adhesion.
mechanism: A chemical treatment is applied to the core material to create a barrier against biological agents, while an adhesive layer bonds the core to exterior skins, integrating protection into the composite structure.
mechanism_raw: Treating the expanded polystyrene core with sodium borate creates a chemical barrier that inhibits biological attack. The urethane adhesive bonds the core to exterior skins, integrating protection into the composite structure.

abstract: This invention is in the field of clinical neurology and relates specifically to compounds, compositions and methods for treatment of patients with generalized epilepsy or partial (symptomatic) epilepsy using compounds of the formula: ##STR1## This invention also relates to compounds, compositions and methods of treatment for drug craving in patients addicted to cocaine.
problem: Treating neurological conditions such as epilepsy and cocaine addiction through targeted pharmacological intervention.
constraint: Achieving therapeutic efficacy while minimizing off-target effects and ensuring metabolic stability in the body.
mechanism: Compounds are designed to selectively interact with specific biological targets involved in neurological pathways, modulating activity to treat conditions while minimizing off-target effects.
mechanism_raw: Compounds of a specific formula interact with neurological pathways to modulate seizure activity or drug craving. The chemical structure enables selective binding to receptors or enzymes involved in these conditions.

abstract: A clock, a calendar, and a two dimensional model of the earth viewed looking at the polar axis as the earth is rotated during a twenty-four hour period thus showing day and night, dawn and dusk. The shadow cast on the earth by the absence of the sun's rays are also shown. The changing of said shadow to show the seasons of the year is also shown as the shadow is rotated once every 365 days. The disc containing the rotating shadow has a pointer that tells the observer the month of the year and the day of the month along with the sign of the zodiac. The rotating earth map has symbols to represent the major cities of the earth and a symbol to represent the pole.
problem: Visually representing complex astronomical phenomena (day/night cycles, seasons) in an intuitive, mechanical format for educational purposes.
constraint: Accurately synchronizing rotational speeds of the Earth model and shadow disc to reflect real-world astronomical ratios within a compact mechanical system.
mechanism: A rotating shadow-casting element around a stationary model simulates astronomical cycles through the interplay of light and shadow, with symbols providing geographic context.
mechanism_raw: Rotating a disc with a shadow-casting pointer around a stationary Earth model simulates the Earth's rotation and orbit. The interplay of light and shadow dynamically illustrates diurnal and seasonal changes, while symbols on the Earth map provide geographic context.

abstract: A duckweed slurry is recovered from a body of water. The duckweed slurry includes duckweed and water from the body of water. The duckweed slurry is transported to a dewatering station. A majority of the water from the duckweed slurry is removed at the dewatering station. Water removed from the duckweed slurry is returned to the body of water.
reason: The patent describes a standard separation and recycling process (dewatering and returning water) without a novel causal mechanism. The steps are conventional and lack a unique functional relationship that generalizes beyond typical resource recovery workflows.

abstract: A method of making a golf club head includes a step of making a slot located at a ball-striking face of a metal head body. The slot is filled with a fiber bulk molding compound preimpregnated in an epoxy resin and is then covered with a prefabricated ball-striking plate. Such head body is placed in a mold cavity of a molding tool, which is subsequently subjected to a treatment under heat and pressure for a predetermined period of time. Upon the completion of the curing of the epoxy resin of the head body, the molding tool is opened to have the club head removed therefrom.
problem: Creating a durable, high-performance golf club head with localized reinforcement and structural integration of composite materials.
constraint: Balancing the curing time and pressure to ensure full resin polymerization without damaging the metal substrate or compromising the composite's fiber alignment.
mechanism: Embedding a fiber-reinforced composite into a precisely shaped cavity within a substrate, then applying heat and pressure to cure and integrate the composite with the surrounding structure. This enables localized mechanical property enhancement at a contact surface while maintaining overall structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Embedding a fiber-reinforced composite (preimpregnated in epoxy) into a precisely machined slot in a metal head body, then using heat and pressure molding to cure and integrate the composite with the surrounding structure. This allows targeted mechanical property enhancement (e.g., stiffness, energy transfer) at the ball-striking face while maintaining structural integrity.
residual_terms: ["fiber-reinforced composite", "heat and pressure molding", "curing", "resin polymerization", "fiber alignment"]

abstract: A multi-strand nylon rope having improved abrasion resistance comprised of a plurality of strands. Each strand is comprised of a plurality of yarns wherein each yarn is formed of a predetermined number of filaments. The filaments of each yarn are twisted together to form a yarn of a predetermined size, the twist direction being opposite that of the final ply yarn direction. For a right lay rope a sufficient number of filaments are twisted together in the left or "S" direction to produce a yarn of a predetermined size. Three or more yarns prepared in this manner are then plied or twisted together in the opposite or right direction. The cover for each strand is formed of alternate yarns of standard and oblong filaments, respectively, the oblong filaments having a modification ratio of three, forming a rope having increased abrasion resistance, a hand and feel that is not stiff or unmanageable and which resists strand-to-strand wet abrasion.
problem: Achieving high abrasion resistance in a multi-strand rope while maintaining flexibility and manageable hand feel.
constraint: Optimizing the modification ratio of oblong filaments and twist direction to avoid stiffness or unmanageable handling while maximizing abrasion resistance.
mechanism: Combining opposing twist directions in filament assembly to stabilize yarn structure, and integrating non-circular cross-section filaments into the strand cover. The non-circular shape increases surface contact area for abrasion resistance, while the twist opposition prevents unraveling and maintains flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Combining opposing twist directions (filaments twisted in one direction, then plied in the opposite) to stabilize yarn structure, and integrating oblong filaments (with a 3:1 modification ratio) into the strand cover. The oblong shape increases surface contact area for abrasion resistance, while the twist opposition prevents unraveling and maintains flexibility.
residual_terms: ["twist direction", "oblong filaments", "modification ratio", "surface contact area", "abrasion resistance"]

abstract: Wrappings from thin pleated sheets are made from a continuous thin paper tape and the like by first making transversal folds in the tapes to form pleats, fixing the edges of the pleats and then folding the fixed edges to form hems. The hemmed pleated tape may then be cut into individual wrappings. The paper tape is coated with heat-setting material so that the pleats can be fixed by melting and resetting this material.
problem: Creating structured, durable wrappings from thin pleated sheets while enabling mass production and individual customization.
constraint: Ensuring the heat-setting material's melting and resetting properties align with the tape's thermal tolerance to avoid deformation during pleat fixation and hemming.
mechanism: Sequentially folding a continuous tape into transversal pleats, fixing the pleat edges with a thermally activated bonding material, then folding the fixed edges into hems to lock the pleat geometry. This creates a self-supporting three-dimensional structure that can be cut into individual units without losing shape or integrity.
mechanism_raw: Sequentially folding a continuous tape into transversal pleats, fixing the pleat edges with heat-setting material, then folding the fixed edges into hems to lock the pleat geometry. This creates a self-supporting 3D structure that can be cut into individual units without losing shape or integrity.

abstract: The apparatus for removing investment material from an investment flask casting includes a spring-biased seating assembly, a centering assembly having spring-biased shoulder mounts, a vertical impact assembly, and a pair of opposing horizontal impact assemblies. The vertical and horizontal impact assemblies work simultaneously and in combination with the spring-biased seating assembly and the spring-biased shoulder mounts to transmit linear dynamic and high frequency vibratory impact energy to the investment flask casting wherein the apparatus effectively and quickly removes virtually all of the investment material therefrom. The investment apparatus further includes an investment collection system for collecting waste investment material for subsequent disposal.
problem: Rapidly and thoroughly removing investment material from a casting flask without damaging the casting or requiring manual intervention.
constraint: Calibrating the frequency and amplitude of vibrations to match the material's resonance while avoiding excessive force that could deform the casting.
mechanism: Applying multi-axis mechanical energy combining linear dynamic impact with high-frequency vibratory excitation, synchronized with spring-biased positioning systems. The simultaneous application of directional force vectors and resonant frequencies disrupts and dislodges contained material without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Combining linear dynamic impact (vertical and horizontal assemblies) with high-frequency vibratory energy, synchronized with spring-biased seating and centering systems. The multi-axis, simultaneous application of mechanical energy disrupts and dislodges investment material through resonant frequencies and directional force vectors.
residual_terms: ["linear dynamic impact", "high-frequency vibratory energy", "resonant frequencies", "directional force vectors", "spring-biased seating"]

abstract: A self-regulating mixing valve has a main housing having hot- and cold-water inlets and provided with an externally threaded stem defining an axis, a valve body displaceable axially in the housing between hot and cold end positions blocking flow from the inlets and through intermediate positions permitting flow from both inlets, and a thermostat in the housing connected to the valve body. An abutment ring fixed on the housing around the stem is provided with a stop. An adjustment nut threaded on the stem adjacent the ring is axially operatively engaged with the thermostat so that rotation of the nut in one direction about the axis axially displaces the thermostat in one direction and opposite rotation axially oppositely displaces it. A protective sleeve centered on the axis and fixed on the ring extends axially outward from the ring coaxially around the sleeve and projects axially outward past the sleeve. An adjustment knob having an annular skirt engaging coaxially between the protective sleeve and the knob is provided with another stop angularly engageable with the stop of the abutment ring to limit angular displacement of the knob on the stem. Interengaging axially extending formations on and between the knob and the nut rotationally couple same together while permitting same to move axially relative to each other. A screw engaged axially between the knob and the nut and fixes the knob axially to the nut.
problem: Automatically regulating water temperature in a mixing valve while allowing manual adjustment.
constraint: Balancing manual adjustability with self-regulation requires decoupling rotational and axial movements while maintaining positional stability.
mechanism: Rotational motion of an adjustment element is converted into axial displacement of a temperature-responsive component via interengaging formations that allow rotational coupling while enabling axial movement. A fastening element secures the adjustment element to the component, enabling precise axial positioning to control fluid mixing.
mechanism_raw: Rotational motion of an adjustment nut is converted into axial displacement of a thermostat via interengaging formations between the knob and nut, which are rotationally coupled but axially movable. A screw fixes the knob to the nut, enabling precise axial positioning of the thermostat to control valve body movement.

abstract: The present invention provides an inoculation wire consisting of a hollow wire, containing powdered ferrosilicon, with a sheeth of steel, copper, nickel or aluminum alloy, for the production of cast iron with spheroidal graphite or vermicular graphite, wherein the filling contains 1 to 50% by volume of powdered magnesium silicide.
problem: Producing cast iron with controlled graphite morphology (spheroidal or vermicular) during casting.
constraint: Optimizing magnesium silicide concentration (1-50% by volume) to balance inoculation efficiency with material cost and process stability.
mechanism: A hollow delivery element introduces a controlled mixture of nucleation agents directly into molten material. The nucleation agents modify solidification behavior through localized chemical interaction, altering microstructure morphology during cooling.
mechanism_raw: A hollow inoculation wire delivers a controlled mixture of ferrosilicon and magnesium silicide powders directly into molten metal. The magnesium silicide acts as a nucleation agent, modifying graphite structure through localized chemical interaction during solidification.

abstract: The lip-type seal for the inlet opening (2) for the dagger board housing and the dagger board (3) exhibits two supporting strips (5) countersunk into the board hull (4) on both sides of the inlet opening (2) as well as two mounting strips (7) with a sealing lip (8) for clamping onto the supporting strips (5), these mounting strips terminating with the profile (6) of the underwater hull and being fashioned as clamping strips. The mounting strip (7) is designed as an L-profile. Respectively one short, perpendicularly bent-away clamping leg (11, 12) is formed at the end edges of the long (9) and of the short leg (10) of the mounting strip (7). The sealing lip (8) adjoining the long leg (9) of the mounting strip (7) is formed, on its longitudinal side facing away from the mounting strip, into a rounded sealing edge (13) passing over into an elastic supporting leg (14) that is oriented obliquely upwardly, this supporting leg being attached to the end edge of the short leg (10) of the mounting strip (7). The sealing lip (8), together with the supporting leg (14) and the short leg (10) of the mounting strip (7), forms an elastic hollow-profile strip (23).
problem: Sealing a dynamic interface (dagger board housing) against water ingress while accommodating movement.
constraint: Maintaining sealing integrity under dynamic movement and hydrostatic pressure without compromising structural support.
mechanism: A deformable sealing element with an elastic contact surface is secured to a structure via clamping features. The elastic surface maintains dynamic contact with a moving component under pressure, while the clamping features ensure structural attachment without compromising sealing integrity.
mechanism_raw: An L-profile mounting strip with clamping legs and an elastic sealing lip forms a hollow-profile strip. The sealing lip deforms elastically under pressure, maintaining contact with the dagger board while the clamping legs secure the seal to the hull structure.

abstract: A differential amplifier has a pair of inputs and a pair of outputs. Each of the outputs is connected between a high potential source and a low potential source through a pair of FETs, respectively. These FETs have the same conduction type. A gate of one of the FETs is connected to one of the inputs, and a gate of the other FET is connected to the other input. This arrangement suppresses output offset and realizes a wide sensitivity range.
problem: Suppressing output offset and achieving wide sensitivity in a differential amplifier.
constraint: Achieving precise FET matching to eliminate offset while maintaining thermal and electrical symmetry in the circuit layout.
mechanism: Symmetrically arranged matched components of the same conduction type are connected between high and low potential sources, with control terminals linked to differential inputs. Component matching minimizes offset voltage, while symmetric topology ensures balanced signal amplification across a wide input range.
mechanism_raw: Symmetrically arranged FETs of the same conduction type are connected between high and low potential sources, with gates linked to differential inputs. Matching FET characteristics minimizes offset voltage, while the symmetric topology ensures balanced signal amplification across a wide input range.

abstract: A reciprocating device for a movable member includes: a stationary member; a movable member held by the stationary member in such a manner as to be able to reciprocate; a biasing device provided between the movable member and the stationary member and adapted to bias the movable member in at least one of the reciprocating directions of the movable member; and a lock device for stopping the movable member in the course of its reciprocation, the lock device including: a cam groove formed on either the stationary member or the movable member and extending around a heart-shaped island; a lock pin having a base end section rotatably supported by either the stationary member or the movable member on which the cam groove is not formed and a tip end section bent toward the bottom of the cam groove; and a pressing device for pressing the tip end section of the lock pin toward the bottom of the cam groove, the pit section of the heart-shaped island of the lock device being equipped with a tapered surface inclined toward the bottom of a stop section of the cam groove, the tip end section of the lock pin being bent at an angle corresponding to the inclination of the tapered surface of the pit section of the heart-shaped island.
problem: Stopping a reciprocating movable member at a desired position during operation.
constraint: Ensuring reliable engagement between the pin and cam groove under dynamic motion while enabling quick release via rotational actuation.
mechanism: A shaped cam groove with a tapered locking section guides a spring-biased pin. The pin's bent tip engages the tapered surface, allowing a reciprocating member to lock at a specific position when the cam rotates into alignment, and release upon rotational actuation.
mechanism_raw: A heart-shaped cam groove with a tapered pit section guides a lock pin, which is pressed toward the groove bottom. The pin's bent tip engages the tapered surface, allowing the member to lock at a specific position when the cam rotates into alignment.

abstract: A pressure sealer for sealing pressure sensitive adhesive strips on business forms has only a single set of sealing rollers forming a nip. One roller is gear driven by a D.C. motor, and a spring applies a biasing force to press the rollers into contact with each other. A forward sensor and a reverse sensor are positioned just before the nip of the rollers, in or above a support surface for business forms, and cooperate with a computer chip to control the motor to drive a business form in a first direction between the rollers, until it has almost completely passed through the nip. Then the motor is reversed to drive the business form through the nip again in a second direction opposite the first direction. The business form is manually fed to, and removed from, the nip.
problem: Ensuring complete and uniform sealing of pressure-sensitive adhesive strips on business forms as they pass through a single nip formed by sealing rollers.
constraint: The reversal must be precisely timed (just before complete passage through the nip) to ensure full sealing without over-processing, and the form is manually fed and removed, requiring the mechanism to work with intermittent manual handling.
mechanism: Detection-triggered bidirectional traversal through a single processing zone: detection elements sense when a manually handled item has nearly completed passage through a nip, actuating reversal so the item re-passes through the same zone in the opposite direction, ensuring full treatment from both directions.
mechanism_raw: Sensor-controlled bidirectional actuation through a single processing zone: forward and reverse sensors detect when the form has almost completely passed through the nip, triggering motor reversal so the form traverses the same nip again in the opposite direction, ensuring the adhesive receives complete pressure treatment from both directions.

abstract: A pressure control chamber of a reactor containment vessel for receiving the atmosphere of the reactor containment vessel containing leakage steam developing in the event of an accident includes a pressure control pool, and a wet well disposed above the pressure control pool. The wet well is divided into an inner peripheral portion and an outer peripheral portion. The inner and outer peripheral portions are communicated with each other via the pressure control pool. An outlet port for flowing the atmosphere of the reactor containment vessel containing the leakage steam is provided at the inner peripheral side of the pressure control pool. When the atmosphere of the reactor containment vessel containing the leakage steam is introduced into the pressure control pool in the event of the accident, this atmosphere is condensed by the water in the pressure control pool, and the gas of this atmosphere not condensed is accumulated in the inner peripheral portion of the wet well. As a result, the pressure within the inner peripheral portion is increased to increase the water level of the pressure control pool at the outer peripheral portion, so that the area of contact of a reactor containment vessel wall with the pressure control pool water is increased, thereby enhancing a heat radiation performance of the reactor containment vessel.
problem: Managing pressure buildup and enhancing heat radiation from a reactor containment vessel wall during an accident involving leakage steam.
constraint: The system operates passively relying solely on the physics of condensation and pressure differentials, with the inner/outer wet well geometry creating the necessary pressure gradient to drive water level changes without active controls.
mechanism: Condensation-driven pressure redistribution via a multi-chambered containment system: gas introduced into a liquid-filled pool condenses, reducing volume. Accumulated gas in an inner chamber increases local pressure, displacing liquid in an outer chamber to expand heat transfer contact area.
mechanism_raw: Condensation-driven pressure redistribution: leakage steam atmosphere is introduced into a water-filled pressure control pool where steam condenses, reducing gas volume. Uncondensed gas accumulates in an inner peripheral chamber of a wet well, increasing local pressure, which raises the water level in an outer peripheral chamber, thereby increasing the contact area between the reactor vessel wall and the cooling water to enhance heat radiation.

abstract: Improved plastic flame spray coating apparatus and methodology are disclosed. An inert gas is configured to shroud or envelop the pneumatically-conveyed stream of powdered plastic which is carried through the combustion flame. The polyolefin coating has increased adhesion and coating smoothness and thicker coatings without thermally-induced embrittlement, discoloration and poor mechanical properties are obtained.
problem: Achieving thicker, smoother, better-adhering plastic flame spray coatings without thermally-induced embrittlement, discoloration, and poor mechanical properties.
constraint: The inert gas must be configured to shroud the powder stream without disrupting the pneumatic conveyance or spray pattern, balancing thermal protection with coating application quality and throughput.
mechanism: Protective gas shrouding of a conveyed material stream through a high-temperature zone: a gas envelope surrounds a pneumatically-conveyed material as it traverses a thermal processing region, shielding it from degradation while maintaining trajectory and deposition.
mechanism_raw: Protective gas shrouding of a conveyed material stream through a high-temperature zone: an inert gas envelope surrounds the pneumatically-conveyed powdered plastic as it traverses the combustion flame, shielding it from oxidative and thermal degradation while maintaining the spray trajectory and deposition process.

abstract: Surfaces of stone materials, marble, sandstone, bricks, concrete and articles manufactured therefrom are consolidated and protected from atmospheric agents and pollutants by applying onto said surfaces a mixture consisting of: PA0 (a) 2-40% by weight of polyvinylidene fluoride, or 1-20% by weight of a polyalkylmethacrylate wherein the alkyl group contains from 1 to 4 carbon atoms; PA0 (b) an elastomeric copolymer of vinylidene fluoride, constituting the balance to 100% and being, in moles, 55-85% of vinylidene fluoride, 15-45% of hexafluoropropene and 0-30% of tetrafluoroethylene.
reason: This patent discloses a specific chemical composition/formulation (polyvinylidene fluoride or polyalkylmethacrylate combined with an elastomeric copolymer) for protecting stone surfaces. The 'how' is simply applying this material mixture, which relies on standard chemical adhesion and film formation rather than a novel causal functional relationship or engineering mechanism that can be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A molded plastic cap buckle and adjustment strap are provided for adjusting the circumference of the head band of a cap to adjust the cap to the head of a user. The buckle is secured to one end of the head band of the cap and the adjustment strap is secured at the other end of the head band. The buckle is made from a unitary member having parts hinged together along an elongated axis that lies generally parallel to the longitudinal axis of the adjustment strap. The buckle and strap have cooperating recesses and projections for securing the buckle and strap in selected adjusted position. The recesses and projections are constructed to provide for one-way longitudinal movement of the strap relative to the buckle in one direction when the buckle and strap are assembled to reduce the effective circumference of the head band, but preclude longitudinal movement in the opposite direction.
problem: Providing adjustable, self-locking circumference control for a cap's headband to fit different head sizes without manual fasteners or complex mechanisms.
constraint: The entire mechanism must be moldable as a single unitary member with hinged parts, requiring the recess/projection geometry to be simple enough for manufacturing while still providing reliable one-way locking and sufficient holding force.
mechanism: One-way mechanical interlocking via cooperating recesses and projections on a hinged buckle: hinged parts and interlocking elements allow longitudinal movement in one direction (tightening) through ratcheting engagement, while the same geometry prevents reverse movement (loosening), creating a self-locking adjustment.
mechanism_raw: One-way mechanical interlocking via cooperating recesses and projections on a hinged buckle: the buckle's hinged parts and the strap's recesses/projections allow longitudinal movement in one direction (tightening) through ratcheting engagement, while the same engagement geometry prevents reverse movement (loosening), creating a self-locking adjustment that maintains the selected circumference.

abstract: A steam generator comprises a distribution means, positioned between the shell and the wrapper in the annular downcomer region of the steam generator, for uniformly mixing the colder feedwater with the warmer recirculating water in the downcomer region of the steam generator so that the colder feedwater is not introduced directly into any steam regions of the steam generator and does not contact any pressure boundaries for preventing water hammer and thermal shock to the steam generator. The distribution means has a downwardly directing means for discharging the substantially evenly distributed feedwater from the distribution means into the downcomer region in a descending direction and away from any pressure boundaries for minimizing flow resistance and for preventing thermal shock to the pressure boundaries. The feedwater and the recirculating water are substantially uniformly mixed in the mixing zone of the downcomer region of the steam generator prior to the mixture of feedwater and recirculating water entering the tube bundle or contacting any pressure boundaries, thereby preventing thermal shock and water hammer to the steam generator.
problem: Cold feedwater introduced directly into steam regions or contacting pressure boundaries in a steam generator causes water hammer and thermal shock.
constraint: The mixing must occur in the downcomer region prior to the mixture entering the tube bundle or contacting any pressure boundaries, and feedwater must be discharged in a descending direction away from pressure boundaries.
mechanism: A mixing zone within a fluid circulation path where colder input fluid is uniformly blended with warmer recirculating fluid before the mixture reaches heat exchange surfaces, combined with directional discharge of the input fluid away from pressure boundaries to minimize flow resistance and prevent thermal shock.
mechanism_raw: Uniformly mixing colder feedwater with warmer recirculating water in a designated mixing zone within the downcomer region before the mixture enters the tube bundle or contacts any pressure boundaries, combined with downwardly directional discharge of feedwater away from pressure boundaries to minimize flow resistance and prevent thermal shock.

abstract: A leather adjustable stirrup strap having a plurality of apertures in a first strap portion and plate-like fastener attached to a second strap portion. The fastener has two inverted U-shaped projections for fitting in selected apertures of the plurality of apertures to form the strap into a closed loop of desired length. A locking strap sized to fit under the U-shaped projections is also provided.
problem: Need for an adjustable stirrup strap that can be set to a desired loop length and maintained at that length without slippage.
constraint: The locking strap must be sized to fit under the U-shaped projections while the projections are engaged in the selected apertures, ensuring the fastener cannot disengage from the chosen aperture.
mechanism: A two-stage mechanical fastening system where engaging elements on a plate-like fastener select discrete positions along a strap to set a desired configuration, and a separate locking element fits under the engaging elements to prevent disengagement and maintain the set configuration.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage mechanical fastening system where U-shaped projections on a plate-like fastener engage selected apertures in the strap to set the desired loop length, and a separate locking strap fits under the projections to prevent disengagement and maintain the set length.

abstract: This invention relates to a process for producing stigma-like tissues of saffron in a large scale by cutting the tissues of stigma (c), style (d, e, f), ovary (h, i, k), ovule (j), and petal (r) of saffron flower, and subculturing them on a liquid or solid LS medium or B5 medium containing a cytokinin and an auxin as main hormones.
problem: Need to produce stigma-like tissues of saffron in large scale for commercial propagation.
constraint: The culture medium must contain both cytokinin and auxin as the main hormones, as their specific ratio and presence are required to induce the desired tissue differentiation pathway.
mechanism: Culturing tissue explants from target plant structures on a growth medium containing specific hormone combinations to direct cellular dedifferentiation and redifferentiation into desired specialized tissues.
mechanism_raw: Cutting tissue explants from various parts of saffron flowers (stigma, style, ovary, ovule, petal) and subculturing them on a medium containing specific hormone combinations (cytokinin and auxin) to direct cellular dedifferentiation and redifferentiation into stigma-like tissues.

abstract: A heater of a vehicle includes a pair of tank units with fluid tube passes and air centers formed therebetween. The tank units include a separate tank extrusion and header. The tank extrusion comprises a generally U-shaped extrusion with recesses provided on the exterior side of the side walls of the U-shaped extrusion. A mounting flange extends from one side wall of each tank extrusion. The header includes deformable tabs which extend over the recesses to allow clinching of the header to the tank extrusion. The mounting flanges slide within notches of a plastic case in the air module for sealing and securing the heater to the module.
problem: Need to mount and seal a heater unit to a vehicle air module with both mechanical attachment and fluid sealing.
constraint: The mounting flanges must slide within the notches of the plastic case to achieve both sealing and securing simultaneously, requiring precise dimensional coordination between the flanges and notches.
mechanism: A multi-point attachment system using deformable engagement elements that clinch over recesses on opposing components to join them together, and mounting elements that slide within complementary slots on a housing to provide both sealing and securing in a single engagement motion.
mechanism_raw: A multi-point attachment system using deformable tabs on a header that clinch over recesses on tank extrusions to join components together, and mounting flanges that slide within notches of a plastic case to provide both sealing and securing in a single engagement motion.

abstract: A conical portion growth control method and an apparatus used in the method grow a conical portion 32B of a single crystal rod 32 by pulling the crystal rod from a melt 16 heated by a heater 14 in the Czochralski method, and aim to enhance reproducibility of the shape of the conical portion 32B and shorten the conical portion 32B. The control method has the steps of presetting a target value pattern 66 of the temperature of a concave portion 46 formed on a heat-insulating material 18 and a target value pattern 64 of the diameter change rate of a growing portion of the crystal rod, measuring the diameter of the crystal growing portion, calculating the change rate of the diameter, measuring the temperature of the concave portion, correcting the target temperature based on a difference between the calculated value and the target value of the diameter change rate, and controlling the amount of electricity supplied to the heater so that the measured temperature becomes equal to the corrected target temperature.
problem: Need to enhance reproducibility of the shape of a conical portion of a single crystal rod and shorten the conical portion in the Czochralski crystal growth method.
constraint: The system must simultaneously track both the diameter change rate of the crystal and the temperature of the concave portion on the heat-insulating material to adjust heater power accordingly.
mechanism: A cascaded feedback control system where a measured dimensional change rate of a growing structure is compared to a target value, the difference is used to adjust a target temperature of a region on a heat-insulating material, and power to a heating element is adjusted so the measured temperature matches the corrected target temperature, thereby controlling growth geometry.
mechanism_raw: A cascaded feedback control system where the measured diameter change rate of the growing crystal is compared to a target value, the difference is used to correct the target temperature of a concave portion on heat-insulating material, and heater power is adjusted so the measured temperature matches the corrected target temperature, thereby controlling crystal growth geometry.

abstract: An extended nip press for the dewatering of a fiber web has an endless flexible press element, like a press jacket or press belt. A press shoe has a concave slide surface for the flexible press element, and the slide surface is adapted to the curve of a backing roll. The shoe is displaceable toward the backing roll in order to press the pressing element against it. A stationary shoe bed, which is detachably connected to a stationary support, has a depression which is provided with a packing and receives the press shoe to form a pressure chamber so that the shoe bed and the press shoe form a cylinder-piston unit. The press shoe is coupled to the shoe bed by means of at least one connecting element. The connecting element is spring biased with respect to the shoe bed and may itself be flexible or be flexibly moved to permit the radial displacement as well as the tilting of the press shoe relative to the shoe bed.
problem: Efficiently dewatering a fiber web in an extended nip press while accommodating dynamic movement and pressure variations.
constraint: Balancing controlled pressure application with the need for mechanical adaptability to prevent uneven dewatering or damage to the press element.
mechanism: A pressure-applying system with a resilient coupling between two rigid components, enabling adaptive displacement and angular adjustment to maintain uniform force distribution despite dynamic movement or misalignment.
mechanism_raw: A cylinder-piston unit formed by a press shoe and stationary shoe bed, with a spring-biased flexible connecting element allowing radial displacement and tilting of the shoe relative to the bed. This maintains uniform pressure application despite web movement or misalignment.

abstract: An improved method for monitoring the parameters of a nuclear core reactor, analyzing the monitored parameters using modified two neutron group diffusion equations that have been subjected to space-time factorization such that the factorized shape functions are approximated, and determining the core neutronics in constant time steps, for example, about 0.25 seconds, thereby to provide analysis and simulations in full range of core neutronics in real-time continuously.
problem: Real-time monitoring and simulation of nuclear reactor core neutronics without computational delays.
constraint: Maintaining accuracy in neutronics modeling while achieving computational efficiency for real-time performance.
mechanism: A computational method that decomposes multi-dimensional equations into separable spatial and temporal components using approximated basis functions, enabling fixed-interval analysis for real-time evaluation without iterative delays.
mechanism_raw: Space-time factorization of two-group neutron diffusion equations with approximated shape functions, enabling constant-time-step analysis (e.g., 0.25 seconds) for continuous real-time core neutronics evaluation.

abstract: A two-stage separation process for separating highly unsaturated triglycerides from an interesterification reaction product by sequential chromatographic separations wherein triglycerides are separated from saturated fatty acids in the first stage and unsaturated fatty acids are recovered in the second stage for recycle to the interesterification reaction zone. In a preferred embodiment using silica gel and silicalite in the two stages, respectively, and heptanone as desorbent in both stages, triglyceride product is removed as the first stage raffinate and the unsaturated fatty acid recycle product stream is removed as the raffinate in the second stage. In another embodiment, using silicalite adsorbent in both stages and 2-heptanone and acetone in the first and second stages, respectively, saturated fatty acids are removed as the extract in the first stage and triglycerides and unsaturated fatty acids are separated as raffinate product and extract product for recycle, respectively.
problem: Separating highly unsaturated triglycerides from interesterification reaction products while recycling unsaturated fatty acids.
constraint: Optimizing adsorbent and desorbent combinations to achieve high-purity separation without cross-contamination between stages.
mechanism: A multi-stage separation process using distinct material pairs in sequence, where each stage selectively retains or releases target compounds based on differential affinity, enabling isolation of desired products and recovery of intermediates for reuse.
mechanism_raw: Sequential chromatographic stages using tailored adsorbent/desorbent pairs (e.g., silica gel/silicalite with heptanone/acetone) to isolate triglycerides in the first stage and recover unsaturated fatty acids for recycle in the second stage.

abstract: A boat lift is arranged to include spaced rectilinear frameworks having leg members splayed exteriorly of a first framework extending to the second framework. The legs may optionally include telescoping extensions, with the extensions and legs having foot plates for mounting the frameworks to a support surface. Flexible webs are mounted at opposed ends between the frameworks to position and lift a boat therebetween.
problem: Lifting and positioning a boat between different water levels using a stable, adaptable mechanical system.
constraint: Ensuring structural stability and adaptability to varying boat sizes and water level differences without compromising lifting force distribution.
mechanism: A structural framework with diverging support elements and tension-adjustable flexible interfaces at opposing ends, allowing load distribution adaptation to varying geometries while maintaining stability through anchored base elements.
mechanism_raw: Rectilinear frameworks with splayed legs and flexible webs at opposed ends, allowing the webs to adjust tension and position the boat while the legs provide stable anchoring to the support surface.

abstract: A cyclone separator formed by a plurality of parallel tubes and a plurality of fins. Each tube is configured in a multitude of segments. One segment of the tubes forms a cylindrical section, one segment is bent inwardly to form a roof section, and one segment is bent inwardly to form a conically-shaped hopper section. As the circumference and diameter of the hopper section decreases from top to bottom, at least a portion of the tubes are configured, either by being extracted or swaged, to accommodate the decreasing circumference and diameter, which results in an increase in the heat recovery of the water-cooled heat transfer tubes without the need for an intermediate ring header.
problem: Enhancing heat recovery in a cyclone separator without intermediate ring headers.
constraint: Balancing structural adjustments to the tube geometry with the need for optimal heat recovery and fluid dynamics in the cyclone.
mechanism: A heat exchange structure composed of discrete segments with varying cross-sectional profiles, where geometric adjustments (e.g., extraction or compression) compensate for changing flow path dimensions while preserving structural continuity and thermal efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Segmented parallel tubes with cylindrical, roof, and conically-shaped hopper sections, where tubes are extracted or swaged to accommodate decreasing circumference, maintaining structural integrity while increasing heat transfer efficiency.

abstract: A novel oxide-dispersion strengthened type heat-resistant alloy is provided for use of preparing furnace members such as a skid rail. The alloy consists essentially of up to about 0.2% C+N, up to about 2.0% Si, up to about 2.0% Mn, about 15 to 35% Ni and about 0.2 to 4% Ta, and the balance of Fe, and contains about 0.1-2% of fine particles of high melting point metal oxide such as Y.sub.2 O.sub.3 dispersed in the austenite matrix. The alloy exhibits excellent properties of anti-hot deformation, oxidation resistance, abrasion resistance and thermal shock resistance.
problem: Creating a material that maintains structural integrity and performance under extreme thermal, oxidative, and mechanical stress in high-temperature environments (e.g., furnace components).
constraint: Balancing alloy composition (e.g., C+N, Ni, Ta content) to achieve sufficient particle dispersion without compromising ductility or manufacturability.
mechanism: Dispersing fine high-melting-point particles within a matrix to physically impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding, thereby enhancing high-temperature strength, oxidation resistance, and thermal shock tolerance.
mechanism_raw: Dispersing fine high-melting-point oxide particles (e.g., Y₂O₃) within an austenite matrix to physically impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding, thereby enhancing high-temperature strength, oxidation resistance, and thermal shock tolerance.

abstract: A radiation image storage panel having a stimulable phosphor layer and an improved protective film is disclosed. The improved protective film is produced from a mixture of a film-forming resin and an oligomer having a polysiloxane skeleton or a perfluoroalkyl group. The improved protective film can be a coated layer containing a fluorocarbon resin which is soluble in an organic solvent. Otherwise, the improved protective film can be produced by coating on the phosphor layer a mixture of a film-forming resin composition containing a fluorocarbon resin which is soluble in an organic solvent, and a powdery resin of perfluoroolefin or silicone.
problem: Protecting a stimulable phosphor layer in radiation imaging systems from physical damage, chemical degradation, and environmental exposure while maintaining functional compatibility.
constraint: Ensuring the film-forming chemistry provides adequate protection while remaining compatible with the phosphor layer's material properties and the imaging process.
mechanism: Forming a durable, chemically resistant barrier from a resin blended with a polymer additive to adhere to a sensitive layer without interfering with its functional properties.
mechanism_raw: Using a protective film formed from a resin blended with a polysiloxane or perfluoroalkyl-containing oligomer, or a fluorocarbon resin soluble in organic solvents, to create a durable, chemically resistant barrier that adheres to the phosphor layer without interfering with its stimulability.
residual_terms: ["chemically resistant barrier", "adhere to a sensitive layer", "resin", "polymer additive"]

abstract: The twin-cylinder circular knitting machine with knitted fabric tensioning device having members for retaining the fabric proximate to a knitting forming region. A first fluid-activated piston is accommodated in the upper needle cylinder and is provided with a hollow stem which is open at its ends. The lower end of the stem is engageable, by means of the sliding of the piston parallel to the axis of the needle cylinders, with the knitted fabric being formed in order to apply tension thereto. The retention members have dimensions for allowing the stem to slide outside of the retention members. The tensioning device also has an auxiliary actuation piston which acts on the piston to achieve its descent at a controlled rate at least until the lower end of the stem of the piston makes contact with the fabric in the region comprised between the retention members and the knitting forming region.
problem: Maintaining consistent tension in knitted fabric during production on a twin-cylinder circular knitting machine to prevent defects and ensure uniform fabric quality.
constraint: Coordinating the fluid pressure and mechanical geometry to apply tension without damaging the fabric or disrupting the knitting process.
mechanism: Using a fluid-activated mechanical actuator with a hollow stem that moves parallel to a rotating surface axis to engage and tension a material, combined with a secondary actuator that modulates the primary actuator's movement rate to ensure controlled contact.
mechanism_raw: Employing a fluid-activated piston with a hollow stem that slides parallel to the needle cylinder axis to engage and tension the fabric, combined with an auxiliary piston that controls the descent rate of the main piston to ensure smooth, controlled contact with the fabric.
residual_terms: ["fluid-activated mechanical actuator", "hollow stem", "parallel to a rotating surface axis", "secondary actuator"]

abstract: Non-dyed and non-finished cotton woven fabric is contacted with a cellulase solution with agitation under conditions so as to produce a cascading effect of the solution over the cotton woven fabric. When so conducted, the treated cotton woven fabric has improved feel and appearance characteristics as compared to the fabric prior to treatment. Additionally, such methods result in the removal of dead and immature cotton from the fabric.
problem: Improving the feel and appearance of cotton woven fabric by removing dead or immature fibers while enhancing surface texture through enzymatic treatment.
constraint: Optimizing agitation intensity and enzyme concentration to maximize fiber modification without over-degrading the fabric's structural integrity.
mechanism: Agitating a solution containing a biocatalyst to create a cascading flow over a fibrous material, increasing biocatalyst-substrate contact to accelerate the breakdown of non-viable components and modify surface texture.
mechanism_raw: Agitating a cellulase solution to create a cascading flow over the fabric, which increases enzyme-fiber contact and accelerates the breakdown of non-viable cotton fibers, thereby smoothing the fabric surface and removing impurities.

abstract: The present invention relates to methods for controlling insect populations and for protecting living plants from insect attack by applying to said plants or to the soil in which they are growing an insecticidally-effective amount of a substituted benzoic acid 1 or 2-alkyl or 2-cycloalkylhydrazide. Novel substituted benzoic acid 1 and 2-alkyl and 2-cycloalkylhydrazides effective as insecticides or intermediates for the preparation of insecticidal diacylhydrazides also are presented.
problem: Controlling insect populations and protecting plants from insect attack using a targeted, environmentally compatible chemical agent.
constraint: Designing the compound to achieve high insecticidal efficacy at low concentrations while minimizing off-target effects on plants and non-pest organisms.
mechanism: Applying a chemical agent that acts as a biochemical inhibitor, selectively disrupting critical physiological processes in target organisms while minimizing effects on non-target species.
mechanism_raw: Applying a substituted benzoic acid hydrazide that acts as a biochemical inhibitor, disrupting critical physiological processes in insects (e.g., molting, reproduction) while remaining selective for pests over plants.

abstract: A slidable room having an improved slide-out assembly and an improved liquid sealing assembly at an interface between an opening in the recreational vehicle and an exterior wall of the room is provided. The slide-out assembly includes a stationary main frame assembly having a pair of support members held in a fixed parallel relationship, a single transmission mechanism fixedly interposed between the support members, and a slidable support assembly slidably retained in the pair of support members for extending and contracting the room. The liquid sealing assembly is disposed around the interface between the slidable room and the opening in the recreational vehicle's exterior wall. A first flange member is affixed to a top edge and side edges of the slidable room's exterior wall. A second complementary flange member is affixed to a top edge and side edges of the opening in the recreational vehicle. The flange members include adjacent protrusions for inhibiting the flow of liquid therebetween when the slidable room is fully retracted into the recreational vehicle.
problem: Maintaining a liquid-tight seal at the interface between a slidable room and a fixed structure during extension/retraction while allowing smooth movement.
constraint: The sealing mechanism must balance tight liquid inhibition with minimal friction to allow repeated sliding motion without jamming.
mechanism: Interlocking protrusions on adjacent flexible sealing members create a physical barrier against fluid flow when the movable element is in a retracted position. The sealing members are positioned at edges and dynamically adapt to maintain contact during sliding motion, balancing sealing effectiveness with minimal resistance to movement.
mechanism_raw: Adjacent protrusions on complementary flange members interlock when the room is fully retracted, creating a physical barrier that inhibits liquid flow. The flanges are positioned at edges to dynamically adapt to movement while maintaining sealing contact.

abstract: A vehicle fuel system for a vehicle which has a fuel tank remote from the engine of the vehicle and a fuel pump remote from said tank and a canister in said tank to receive return fuel from a pressure regulator in said system. A fuel flow passage carries fuel from the main fuel tank to the pump. Under conditions of low fuel in the main fuel tank, a valve associated with the canister opens in response to side swerving motion of the vehicle to allow flow of fuel from the canister to the fuel flow passage leading to the pump to prevent starving of the engine due to low flow from the main tank.
problem: Preventing engine fuel starvation during low-fuel conditions and dynamic vehicle maneuvers (e.g., swerving).
constraint: The valve must activate only under specific motion conditions to avoid unintended fuel flow during normal operation.
mechanism: A motion-responsive valve activates under specific inertial conditions to supplement a primary supply from a secondary reservoir. The valve's activation is triggered by dynamic motion rather than manual control, ensuring fuel availability during low-supply conditions without interfering with normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A motion-responsive valve in the fuel canister opens due to lateral acceleration during swerving, allowing fuel from the canister to supplement the main tank supply. The valve activation is directly triggered by vehicle dynamics rather than manual intervention.

abstract: An air conditioning system comprises a room divider extending upwardly from a floor, the room divider having first and second sides for supplying conditioned air to an area. The room divider comprises a first panel integrally connected to a second panel to form the room divider. The first and second panels are spaced apart a predetermined distance to define an air flow area therebetween for allowing air to flow between the panels. The first and second panels include a bottom portion positioned proximate a first side of the floor, the bottom portion including a generally imperforate bottom member adjacent the second panel and sized to complement the air flow area such that air cannot flow directly through the bottom portion from or to the air flow area. At least one air outlet is integral with one of the first or second panels and is elevated a predetermined distance from the floor for allowing air within the air flow area to flow therethrough to an area surrounding the room divider. A flow direction controller is provided for directing conditioned air on a second side of the floor into the air flow area, whereby air flows from the second side of the floor through the first panel into the air flow area and through the air outlet to the surrounding area.
problem: Efficiently distributing conditioned air in a partitioned space while maintaining structural integrity of the divider.
constraint: The divider must balance structural support (via imperforate bottom sections) with airflow capacity (via spaced panels and outlets) without compromising either function.
mechanism: A partitioning element integrates spaced structural panels with an internal flow channel and elevated outlets, directing conditioned fluid through the channel between panels and expelling it via outlets. The design balances structural support from imperforate sections with fluid distribution capacity from spaced panels.
mechanism_raw: A room divider integrates spaced panels with an internal airflow channel, elevated outlets, and a flow direction controller. Air is directed through the channel between panels and expelled via outlets, leveraging the divider's structure to both partition space and guide airflow.
residual_terms: ["partitioning element", "spaced panels", "internal flow channel", "elevated outlets", "imperforate sections", "conditioned fluid"]

abstract: An apparatus for cleaning and sterilizing objects, such as pharmaceutical caps, plugs and the like includes an autoclave chamber and a cleaning device having a cleaning drum mounted for a free rotation on a frame. The frame runs on rollers and can be moved in and out of the autoclave chamber. The cleaning drum has a hollow shaft provided within the drum with spray nozzles and mounted axially in line with a hollow drive shaft passing through one sidewall of the autoclave chamber free to turn and sealed. The drum shaft and the drive shaft may be coupled together by a coupling device. The frame may be released from the drum introduced into the autoclave chamber so that it is not located during the cleaning process in the autoclave chamber and thus will not constitute an additional source of contamination.
problem: Preventing contamination of sterilized objects during cleaning/sterilization processes by isolating non-sterile components.
constraint: The system must enable precise movement and coupling/decoupling of components without introducing contamination during transfer.
mechanism: A sterilizable element is moved into a treatment chamber while its supporting structure is released and positioned outside the chamber. This decouples the element undergoing treatment from the supporting structure, ensuring only the element is exposed to sterilization conditions while maintaining contamination isolation.
mechanism_raw: A cleaning drum is moved into an autoclave chamber while its supporting frame is released and positioned outside the chamber. This decouples the drum (subject to sterilization) from the frame (a contamination source), ensuring only the drum undergoes sterilization.

abstract: A composite beam having high compressive and tensile strength is disclosed. The beam is also very lightweight, has a high modulus of elasticity, and is able to support heavy loads in applications such as in use in aerial lift devices. High dielectric resistance is also a very important property exhibited by the beam. There are three structural layers in the beam including an inner layer comprising a wound filament, a middle layer comprising a plurality of plates, and an outer layer also comprising a woven or a non-woven material.
problem: Achieving a lightweight structural beam with high compressive/tensile strength and dielectric resistance for demanding applications.
constraint: The layered design must balance conflicting material properties (e.g., strength vs. weight, conductivity vs. dielectric resistance) without delamination or performance degradation.
mechanism: A multi-layer composite structure combines a filament-wound inner layer for tensile strength, a middle layer of plates for compressive strength, and an outer layer for dielectric properties. Each layer contributes distinct mechanical and electrical characteristics to the composite, balancing conflicting performance requirements.
mechanism_raw: A three-layer composite structure combines a wound filament inner layer (for tensile strength), a middle layer of plates (for compressive strength), and an outer woven/non-woven layer (for dielectric properties). Each layer contributes distinct mechanical/electrical properties to the composite.
residual_terms: ["multi-layer composite", "filament-wound inner layer", "tensile strength", "middle layer of plates", "compressive strength", "outer layer", "dielectric properties", "delamination"]

abstract: Apparatus for slicing tobacco bales comprising a plurality of parallel sharp prongs or lances (1) which can be moved to penetrate the bale (7) in a horizontal plane while the bale is supported on a lift device (14). A retractable pusher (9) is arranged to be movable parallel to the prongs so as to separate the slice from them after cutting and has downwardly dependent sharpened teeth (10) attached to its lower edge so as to extend between the prongs.
problem: Efficiently slicing a bale into a clean slice without the slice adhering to the cutting elements or deforming the bale structure.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the bale during cutting while ensuring the pusher teeth can navigate between closely spaced prongs without jamming.
mechanism: A reciprocating separation element with interdigitated engagement features moves parallel to a cutting surface, inserting between the cutting elements after penetration to mechanically displace the cut material away from the cutting elements, using coordinated linear motion to maintain structural integrity during separation.
mechanism_raw: A retractable pusher with downwardly dependent sharpened teeth moves parallel to the prongs, inserting between them to mechanically separate the cut slice from the prongs after penetration, leveraging coordinated linear motion and interdigitated cutting/separation elements.

abstract: Improving commingling two or more continuous multiple filament yarns into a single yarn by rubbing one yarn against a static charge-inducing body that is supported in an electrically isolated manner to apply static charge to the yarn to tend to cause separation of its individual multiple filament.
