Also disclosed is commingling apparatus in which individual filaments of a multiple filament yarn are spread from each other in an enclosure that contains a source of the multiple filament yarn and has a yarn exit opening through which the filaments leave the enclosure in a separated state, a vacuum source being to connected to an air removal opening so that air flows through and around the yarn at a direction transverse to the yarn to cause spreading of the filaments, the yarn from the source passing through a guide and a weighted dancer whose movements up and down (in response to changes in tension in the yarn) control a positive feed drive for the yarn source. Also disclosed is apparatus for commingling different multiple filament yarns that includes a plurality of sources of one kind of multiple filament yarn and a plurality of tension adjustment devices for each individual yarn to reduce differences in tension among the yarns as they are presented as a flattened ribbon and combined with a flattened ribbon of a different type of yarn.
problem: Commingling multiple filament yarns into a single yarn while managing tension differences and ensuring uniform filament separation for effective blending.
constraint: Balancing static charge intensity and airflow velocity to achieve consistent filament separation without damaging the yarn or introducing excessive tension variability.
mechanism: An electrostatic field induces filament separation while a fluid flow source generates transverse airflow to spread filaments; tension-regulating feedback elements adjust feed rates to balance yarn tensions and ensure uniform blending.
mechanism_raw: Static charge induction via an electrically isolated body causes filament separation, while a vacuum source generates transverse airflow to spread filaments; tension-adjusted dancer arms regulate feed rates to balance yarn tensions.

abstract: A fiber coating which allows ceramic or metal fibers to be wetted by molten metals is disclosed. The coating inhibits degradation of the physical properties caused by chemical reaction between the fiber and the coating itself or between the fiber and the metal matrix. The fiber coating preferably includes at least a wetting layer, and in some applications, a wetting layer and a barrier layer between the fiber and the wetting layer. The wetting layer promotes fiber wetting by the metal matrix. The barrier layer inhibits fiber degradation. The fiber coating permits the fibers to be infiltrated with the metal matrix resulting in composites having unique properties not obtainable in pure materials.
problem: Allowing molten metal to wet ceramic or metal fibers for composite infiltration while preventing chemical degradation of the fibers caused by reactions with the coating or metal matrix.
constraint: Selecting materials for the wetting and barrier layers that maintain thermal stability and chemical inertness under molten metal conditions while enabling effective infiltration.
mechanism: A multi-layer coating system applies a first layer that promotes material adhesion and a second layer positioned between the substrate and the first layer that inhibits chemical reactions, enabling controlled infiltration while preventing substrate degradation.
mechanism_raw: A dual-layer coating system: a wetting layer promotes metal adhesion, and a barrier layer between the fiber and wetting layer inhibits chemical reactions, enabling controlled infiltration without fiber degradation.

abstract: The invention relates to a folding top for vehicles having a dimensionally stable rear window which, when the top is pushed back, can be folded down from an upright position of use into a stowed position displaced to the rear. Sliding control of the rear window during the stowing operation is provided via a strut of the top frame. The central region of the strut rests against the underneath of the top cover in front of the rear window when the top is closed and overlaps the rear window in its swung-back end position. A coupling device is provided for transmitting movement by means of which the rear window and the strut are connected to one another, in each case at a distance from their pivot axis. In order to make possible a rearward displacement of the rear window when stowing the folding top, largely independently of the lowering of the rear window relative to a material retaining profile, the coupling device includes tie members unstable under bending loads, which connect the rear window in the region of its front window edge to the central region of the strut. After a free movement the tie members are stable under tension only when a final phase of the rearward swinging movement of the strut is reached, after which the rear window participates in the rearward transverse advance of the central region and is moved positively into its pushed-back end position.
problem: Stowing a folding vehicle top with a dimensionally stable rear window in a coordinated manner, ensuring the window moves rearward independently of its vertical lowering during the folding process.
constraint: Timing the transition of the tie members from bending instability to tension stability to ensure the window's rearward movement aligns with the strut's motion without premature or delayed engagement.
mechanism: A coupling mechanism with load-responsive linkages connects a moving component to a structural element; these linkages transition from bending instability to tension stability during a specific phase of the structural element's motion, enabling delayed positive displacement of the moving component.
mechanism_raw: A coupling device with tie members unstable under bending loads connects the rear window to a strut; these tie members transition to tension stability only during the final phase of the strut's rearward swing, enabling delayed positive displacement of the window.

abstract: A heat-adhesive paper sheet suitable for use as fusuma paper and shoji paper in a Japanese style house, wallpaper, ceiling paper, liner for paintings and calligraphic works, and liner for plywood, and which is adhered to the object with heat by ironing. The heat-adhesive paper sheet is composed of a paper sheet material having a projection-depression pattern formed on the surface thereof by creping or embossing or the like and a layer of a thermoplastic thermal shrinking pressure-sensitive adhesive provided on one surface of the paper sheet material. Even though the surface of the object to which the paper sheet is stuck is somewhat rough and uneven, the heat-sensitive adhesive layer may easily be fused so that the paper sheet may be well applied to the object under light pressure without forming wrinkles on the applied sheet. Steam ironing, which has heretofore been unacceptable, is applicable to this paper sheet for sticking it to an object.
problem: Adhering a heat-activated paper sheet to rough or uneven surfaces without forming wrinkles or requiring excessive pressure during application.
constraint: Optimizing the projection-depression pattern depth and adhesive shrinkage properties to balance conformability and adhesion strength without compromising the sheet's structural integrity.
mechanism: A surface texture pattern with alternating projections and depressions combined with a thermally activated adhesive layer allows the sheet to conform to surface irregularities when heat is applied, with the adhesive flowing under light pressure to eliminate wrinkles.
mechanism_raw: A projection-depression surface pattern (via creping or embossing) combined with a thermoplastic thermal-shrinking pressure-sensitive adhesive layer allows the sheet to conform to surface irregularities when heat-fused, with the adhesive flowing under light pressure to eliminate wrinkles.

abstract: A mechanism for feeding weft yarn stock bobbins to a loom includes a bobbin frame (3) for at least two stock bobbins (4) which may be fitted to bobbin holders (38) having longitudinal axes (L) which may be aligned on a common yarn guide member (6). The bobbin holders (38) are each formed on a bobbin carrier (10, 10') intended for receiving one of the stock bobbins (4) and able by means of a holder (30) of a charging mechanism to be fastened to the bobbin frame (3) and removed from the bobbin frame, the bobbin carrier having a yarn guide unit (45) for feeding the piece (A) at the start of the weft yarn (5) wound onto this stock bobbin (4) to the common yarn guide member (6). The yarn guide unit (45) is formed on a carrier part (44) able to swing between a normal position suitable for seizing the starting piece (A) and a deflected position in which in an operating position of the bobbin carrier (10, 10') predetermined on the bobbin frame (3) and aligned with the yarn guide member (6), the yarn guide unit (45) may be set in a definite yarn delivery position and may be brought together with the yarn guide member (6). A simplification of the charging process and delivery of the yarn is accordingly achievable.
problem: Simplifying the process of charging weft yarn bobbins onto a loom and ensuring reliable yarn delivery during operation.
constraint: The swingable movement must precisely transition between positions without disrupting the bobbin carrier's mounting/removal process or yarn tension during operation.
mechanism: A movable guide element transitions between discrete positions to automatically align a yarn delivery path with a stationary guide system, ensuring continuous material flow during repositioning of a carrier mechanism. The positional switching synchronizes alignment without interrupting tension or mounting processes.
mechanism_raw: A swingable yarn guide unit on a bobbin carrier moves between a 'normal' position to grasp the yarn start and a 'deflected' position where it aligns with a common yarn guide member when the carrier is in its operating position on the bobbin frame. This mechanical repositioning automatically synchronizes yarn delivery alignment with the loom's guide system.

abstract: A method of enhancing the compostability of waste products (i.e., products which have been discarded after use such as diapers) containing one or more propylene polymer materials by exposure to high-energy ionizing radiation in an oxidizing atmosphere, such as air, to improve the rate of the biological degradation of the propylene polymer material(s). The irradiated waste product is then contacted with living microorganisms in the presence of sufficient moisture for their growth and of an oxygen-containing gas to produce a useful compost humus.
problem: Accelerating the biological degradation of non-biodegradable propylene polymer waste (e.g., diapers) to produce compost.
constraint: The radiation dose and oxidizing environment must be balanced to sufficiently degrade the polymer without over-processing, which could reduce the material's utility as compost.
mechanism: Exposure to high-energy radiation in an oxidizing environment induces molecular bond cleavage, generating reactive sites that enable subsequent biological metabolism. The controlled degradation lowers material resistance to enzymatic breakdown, accelerating decomposition into compost.
mechanism_raw: High-energy ionizing radiation in an oxidizing atmosphere breaks molecular bonds in the polymer, creating reactive sites that microorganisms can metabolize. The radiation-induced structural modification lowers the polymer's resistance to enzymatic attack, enabling subsequent biological decomposition.

abstract: A boot shell (10) has a part (46) which overlaps the forefoot, in which there is a longitudinal opening (48) in the instep region of the foot. This opening is spanned twice by a cable (54) in a meander-shaped arrangement in the transverse direction. The cable (54) is anchored on the boot shell (10) by means of its one end (58) in the region of the toe (38) of the boot and furthermore guided via deflection elements (60, 62). The cable (54) is a component of a BOWDEN pull-wire (56) and ends with its other end in a tensioning device (18) which is arranged on the rear shaft part (12). By means of a rotary knob (16) of the tensioning device (18), the front part of the boot shell (10) can be optimally adapted to the foot of the wearer by drawing together the region (46) which overlaps the forefoot.
problem: Adaptively tightening the forefoot region of a boot shell to conform to the wearer's foot shape.
constraint: The cable's deflection elements and anchoring points must maintain consistent tension distribution while allowing sufficient adjustment range for different foot geometries.
mechanism: A tensioned flexible element routed in a distributed path across a target region applies compressive force when actuated, causing adjacent structural sections to converge. The path geometry ensures uniform force distribution while accommodating variable geometries through adjustable tensioning.
mechanism_raw: A cable routed in a meander pattern across the instep opening is tensioned via a rear-mounted knob, causing the overlapping forefoot region to draw together. The cable's path distributes tension evenly across the target area, enabling localized compression without rigid mechanical joints.

abstract: An epitaxial growth of a first component of a multilayer stack for use in optical, electro-optical and electronic or magnetic components, e.g. on a silicon wafer, can be formed by depositing a second component in a form in which that second component produces a precipitate or inclusions in the first component which with continued deposition may be partly replaced by a third component so that the precipitate itself is buried in a monocrystalline structure and, after a thermal treatment in which the precipitate coalesces, a buried layer is formed of the second component or a compound thereof with, say, the first component, in that monocrystalline structure.
problem: Forming a buried layer of a secondary component within a monocrystalline structure for use in optical/electronic devices.
constraint: The deposition rate, thermal treatment temperature, and material compatibility must be precisely controlled to ensure precipitates coalesce uniformly without disrupting the monocrystalline matrix.
mechanism: Controlled phase separation during layered material growth creates discrete inclusions, which are subsequently buried by continued deposition. Thermal energy then drives coalescence of these inclusions into a continuous subsurface structure, leveraging migration dynamics to form integrated layers.
mechanism_raw: During epitaxial deposition, a secondary component forms precipitates or inclusions within the primary layer. Continued deposition buries these inclusions, and subsequent thermal treatment causes them to coalesce into a continuous buried layer. The process leverages controlled phase separation and thermal migration to create subsurface structures.

abstract: The present disclosure is directed to a seven-way combination tool allowing for separate use of each of seven different functional portions of the tool and having a central blade, with upper and lower surfaces one of which has a concave surface and its blade tip is beveled at the end opposite the handle. The tool handle has upper and lower portions, both of which are independently rotatable 360.degree. and each of which has a polygonal opening to accommodate polygonal shafted screwdrivers of different head types. At the tip of the central blade are located tip angle edge portions of different areas. One of which is located adjacent to the concave surface of the blade.
reason: The patent describes a multi-tool with independently rotatable handle portions and a central blade with multiple functional edges. While it combines seven tools into one device, the mechanism is a static integration of components rather than a causal process that solves a problem through functional interaction. The 'problem' (combining tools) is addressed by physical arrangement, not a transferable operational principle.

abstract: A liner or wrap for use in the scroll or discharge housing of a centrifugal separator device. The wrap comprises a one-piece, elongated strip of material which is releasably secured to the interior wall which is replaceable in the event of excessive wear. The wrap is compressible and can be placed into the separator device without having to remove the blade assemblies. The releasable wrap is seated against the discharge housing wall contiguous to blades which are rotatable in the discharge housing.
problem: Excessive wear in the discharge housing of a centrifugal separator requires frequent maintenance and blade assembly removal.
constraint: The wrap must balance compressibility for installation ease with structural integrity to withstand operational forces, and the attachment method must allow repeated removal/replacement without damaging the housing or blades.
mechanism: A resilient, replaceable barrier element is conformably positioned against a housing interior using a releasable attachment mechanism, enabling installation without disassembling adjacent components. The barrier's compressibility allows geometric conformity during placement, while the attachment method permits repeated removal/replacement without structural damage to the housing or components.
mechanism_raw: A compressible, one-piece replaceable wrap is releasably secured to the interior wall, allowing installation without removing blade assemblies. The compressibility enables the wrap to conform to the housing geometry during placement, while the releasable attachment permits rapid replacement when wear occurs.

abstract: In a combination of a finger ring and a size adjustment insert, the finger ring and the insert are provided with complementary interengaging portions that permit the insert to be twist received in frictional engagement adjacent the back side of the head of the ring. The insert is formed from a resilient plastic material and includes a male protrusion which is adapted to be twist-received into a complementary female opening formed in the back side of the decorative head of the finger ring.
problem: Fixed-size finger rings cannot accommodate variations in finger diameter, requiring multiple rings or permanent resizing.
constraint: The insert material must provide sufficient resilience for secure frictional engagement while allowing manual rotation, and the interengagement geometry must prevent unintended disengagement during normal wear.
mechanism: An adjustable circumference system uses a resilient insert with a male protrusion twist-locked into a complementary female receptacle on a base structure. Rotational manipulation of the insert changes the effective circumference by frictionally engaging the insert's geometry with the base's internal structure, while interengagement features prevent unintended disengagement.
mechanism_raw: A resilient plastic insert with a male protrusion is twist-locked into a complementary female opening on the ring's head. Rotating the insert changes the effective ring circumference by frictionally engaging the insert's geometry with the ring's internal structure.

abstract: This invention relates to a deactivating device for deactivating shoplifting detection labels of an electronic shoplifting detection system. These labels comprise a resonant circuit with a coil and a capacitor and the deactivating device comprises an antenna circuit comprising an antenna coil tuned with at least one capacitor to the resonant frequency of the resonant circuit. By means of this arrangement, sufficient energy can be induced in a resonant circuit of a label to effect electrical breakdown in the capacitor thereof. According to the invention, the antenna coil of the deactivating device is coupled, on the one hand, to a supply source and, on the other, to earth via a switch. Circuitry is provided for supplying at intervals control pulses to the switch in order to bring the switch into the conductive state. The duration of each control pulse is chosen such that at the end of a control pulse, when the switch returns to the blocking state, the energy necessary for deactivation is stored as magnetic energy in the antenna coil. This energy is subsequently converted into an electromagnetic oscillation when the switch is in the blocking state.
problem: Shoplifting detection labels must be deactivated without damaging adjacent products or requiring physical contact with the label.
constraint: The control pulse duration must precisely time the energy storage and release cycle to ensure sufficient energy transfer for capacitor breakdown while avoiding excessive energy that could damage nearby components.
mechanism: A switch-controlled energy storage and release circuit accumulates magnetic energy in an inductive element during conductive states, then converts the stored energy into electromagnetic oscillations during blocking states. The oscillations induce electrical breakdown in a target component by resonantly coupling energy at the component's natural frequency, with pulse duration controlling energy transfer magnitude.
mechanism_raw: A switch-controlled antenna circuit stores magnetic energy in an antenna coil during conductive states, then converts this stored energy into electromagnetic oscillations during blocking states. The oscillations induce electrical breakdown in the label's capacitor by resonantly coupling energy at the label's natural frequency.

abstract: A pressure sorter for a suspension flow includes a cylindrical housing having at least one inlet opening and at least one outlet opening with a defined pressure drop therebetween. A rotationally symmetric screen basket defining an axis is disposed within the housing. The screen basket has a plurality of openings defining a total screen perforation passage area. The axis of the screen basket is positioned offset a distance of 6 to 12% of the diameter of the screen basket. The axis of the screen basket is disposed in a plane which extends through the housing axis and is perpendicular to the housing outlet opening. A rotor and suspension sorting space are disposed centrically within the screen basket. An accepts space is disposed radially outward of the screen basket between the screen basket and the housing. The accepts space has a cross section causing a pressure drop between the suspension sorting space and the accepts space resulting in a suspension flow through the screen openings having a maximum velocity of 2.5 m/s, and a deviation to higher suspension flow velocity values from an arithmetic mean value based on the total screen perforation passage area across the entire screen basket circumference amounting to a maximum of 25% of the mean value.
problem: Inefficient particle separation in suspension flows due to uneven velocity distribution across a screen basket.
constraint: The offset distance and accepts space geometry must balance pressure drop requirements with structural integrity, ensuring uniform flow distribution without exceeding velocity thresholds that could damage particles or reduce separation efficiency.
mechanism: An offset geometry between a screening element and its housing creates a controlled pressure differential between adjacent flow regions. The spatial offset and cross-sectional design of the downstream region enforce maximum flow velocity limits while constraining velocity deviation across the screening surface, balancing pressure drop with particle integrity.
mechanism_raw: An offset screen basket axis (6-12% of diameter) creates a controlled pressure drop between the sorting space and accepts space. The offset geometry and cross-sectional design of the accepts space enforce a maximum flow velocity of 2.5 m/s while limiting velocity deviation to 25% of the mean across the screen circumference.

abstract: An apparatus for thickening liquids with solid contents has a container receiving the liquid and a vapor outlet and a heater, which is positioned in the liquid column in the container. The heater is constructed as a rotor rotating in the container and is formed from a plurality of substantially parallel plates arranged with a limited axial spacing and extending outwards from the rotor axis, every second space between adjacent plates forming a heating chamber sealed with respect to the liquid, while the spaces located between the same close to the rotor axis and on the circumference thereof are open towards the container interior.
problem: Inefficient thickening of liquids with solid contents due to poor heat transfer and mixing in static systems.
constraint: The axial spacing between plates must balance heat transfer efficiency in sealed chambers with mixing effectiveness in open spaces, while rotational speed must ensure uniform heat distribution without causing excessive shear forces on the solid particles.
mechanism: A rotating element with alternating sealed and open chamber configurations creates distinct thermal and mixing zones. The sealed chambers concentrate heat application to the fluid medium, while the open zones near rotational axis and periphery enable continuous circulation and mixing of the fluid-solid mixture, with axial spacing balancing heat transfer and shear forces.
mechanism_raw: A rotating heater with parallel plates creates alternating sealed heating chambers and open mixing spaces. The sealed chambers concentrate heat application to the liquid, while the open spaces near the rotor axis and circumference allow continuous mixing and circulation of the liquid-solid mixture.

abstract: A biological denitrification is provided in which ammonium ion is used as an electron donor in the denitrification. The process may advantageously be used under conditions of high ammonium ion concentrations in waste water or to remove ammonium ion from manure, soil or surface water. Microorganisms are described which may be used in these processes.
problem: Removing ammonium ion from wastewater, manure, soil, or surface water under high ammonium concentrations.
constraint: Maintaining microbial activity and process efficiency under high ammonium ion concentrations, which can be toxic or inhibitory to conventional denitrification processes.
mechanism: Employ a biological process where a target ion is metabolized by specialized agents as an electron donor, enabling its removal through microbial metabolic pathways while mitigating toxicity-induced inhibition of the process.
mechanism_raw: Using microorganisms that utilize ammonium ion as an electron donor in a biological denitrification process, enabling targeted removal of ammonium while leveraging microbial metabolic pathways.

abstract: A fire door closure reset system including a fire door movable between an opened position and a closed position relative to an opening through a wall; a lock for being pivotally attached relative to the wall for movement between a locked position and an unlocked position and for allowing the fire door to move to the closed position when in the unlocked position; a spring for urging the lock to the unlocked position; a cable having a first end for being attached to the lock and having a second end for being fixedly attached relative to the wall; the lock being held in the locked position when the cable is taut; the spring urging the lock to the unlocked position when slack is placed in the cable; occurrence responsive structure for placing slack in the cable in the event of a predetermined occurrence; and a test-reset mechanism for allowing the operation of the fire door closure reset system to be tested by placing slack in the cable and for allowing the slack in the cable to be subsequently removed after the operation of the fire door closure reset system is tested to reset the fire door closure reset system.
problem: Ensuring fire doors close automatically during emergencies while allowing manual testing and resetting of the closure system.
constraint: Balancing the need for fail-safe operation (door closes during emergencies) with the requirement for manual testing and resetting without compromising safety.
mechanism: Implement a fail-safe retention system using a tensioned element to hold a locking mechanism in place; an event-responsive trigger introduces slack to release the lock via a resilient element, enabling automatic closure. A manual override temporarily introduces slack for testing and restores tension to reset the system.
mechanism_raw: A tensioned cable holds a lock in a closed position; introducing slack in the cable (via an event-responsive trigger) allows a spring to release the lock, enabling door closure. A test-reset mechanism temporarily introduces slack for testing and then restores tension to reset the system.

abstract: A cigarette includes a charge or roll of smokable material (e.g., tobacco cut filler) circumscribed by two layers of paper wrapping materials. The first or inner wrapping material includes an inorganic filler material and tobacco material within the web. The inner wrapping material also can include a water soluble salt burn chemical and a carbonaceous material within the web. The second or outer wrapping material circumscribes and overwraps the first wrapping material, has a cellulosic base web and inorganic filler material, and exhibits a low inherent air permeability. The outer wrapping material can include a magnesium hydroxide filler, and exhibits an inherent air permeability of below about 15 CORESTA units and a net air permeability above about 40 CORESTA units. The cigarette is capable of sustaining smolder under FTC smoking conditions while yielding very low levels of visible sidestream smoke.
problem: Reducing visible sidestream smoke from cigarettes while sustaining smolder under standardized smoking conditions.
constraint: Achieving a balance between low air permeability (to control burn) and sufficient net permeability (to sustain smolder) while minimizing sidestream smoke emissions.
mechanism: Utilize a multi-layer containment system where an inner layer modulates combustion chemistry through controlled material composition, and an outer layer regulates airflow and burn rate via differential permeability, balancing sustained smolder with reduced emissions.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual-layer wrapping system: an inner layer with inorganic filler, tobacco, and chemical additives (e.g., water-soluble salts, carbonaceous materials) to control combustion chemistry, and an outer layer with low inherent air permeability to regulate airflow and burn rate.

abstract: Tri- and tetra-substituted guanidines which exhibit a high binding affinity to phencyclidine (PCP) receptors and, more preferably, low affinity to the brain sigma receptors. These guanidine derivatives act as non-competitive inhibitors of glutamate induced responses of the NMDA receptor by acting as blockers for the ion channel of the NMDA receptor-ion channel complex. These compounds thus exert neuroprotective activity and are useful in the therapeutic treatment of neuronal loss in hypoxia, hypoglycemia, brain or spinal cord ischemia, and brain or spinal chord trauma as well as being useful for the treatment of epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, Down's Syndrome, Korsakoff's disease and other neurodegenerative disorders.
problem: Treating neurodegenerative disorders by selectively blocking NMDA receptor ion channels without off-target effects on sigma receptors.
constraint: Optimizing molecular structure to achieve high affinity for NMDA/PCP receptors while minimizing affinity for sigma receptors to reduce side effects.
mechanism: Design molecular structures with high binding affinity for a target receptor complex while minimizing interaction with non-target receptors, using selective inhibition to block pathological signaling pathways and reduce off-target effects.
mechanism_raw: Designing tri- and tetra-substituted guanidine derivatives with high binding affinity to PCP receptors and NMDA ion channels, acting as non-competitive inhibitors to block glutamate-induced responses and provide neuroprotection.
residual_terms: ["binding affinity", "target receptor complex", "non-target receptors", "selective inhibition", "non-competitive inhibitors"]

abstract: A process useful for the reversible storage of information units involves the targeted, positionally selective and time-stable labeling of individual atomic positions or groups of such positions on the surface of a solid by chemical reaction with foreign atoms or molecules or by chemisorption, with the lateral atomic order of the surface in each case being retained, even on a local level.
problem: Storing information units reversibly on a solid surface without disrupting the material's structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining the surface's lateral atomic order during labeling to ensure structural stability and reversibility of the stored information.
mechanism: Apply position-selective chemical modification or adsorption to a solid surface, enabling reversible labeling of discrete sites while preserving the surface's structural order through localized, non-disruptive reactions.
mechanism_raw: Using positionally selective chemical reactions or chemisorption to label individual atomic positions or groups on a solid surface, retaining lateral atomic order even locally, enabling stable and reversible data storage.

abstract: A vertical screening apparatus in which the board to be screened is reciprocally shuttled into and out of the print zone before and after vertical reciprocation of the flood blades and print squeegees. A mechanism is provided to horizontally locate each board and to jog each board between successive sequences of flood and print strokes. Means are provided for tilting the print squeegee between successive print strokes.
problem: Achieving precise alignment and positioning of a board during sequential printing and flood strokes in a vertical screening apparatus.
constraint: Balancing the timing and synchronization of horizontal board movement, vertical blade/squeegee motion, and squeegee tilting to avoid disrupting the print zone or compromising coating uniformity.
mechanism: Coordinated horizontal displacement and angular adjustment of a spreading element between successive operations, enabling dynamic repositioning of the substrate to maintain alignment while allowing vertical reciprocation of opposing elements.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated horizontal jogging and tilting of the squeegee between successive print/flood strokes, enabling dynamic repositioning of the board to maintain alignment while allowing vertical reciprocation of flood blades and print squeegees.

abstract: The thread tension regulating apparatus comprises; thread tension setting means for selecting and setting thread clamping pressure to the right pressure coping with plural kinds of the stitches; thread tension fine-adjusting means for allowing fine-adjustment of thread clamping pressure in the thread tension regulating apparatus by moving clamping pressure of the thread tension regulating apparatus from the original position to a higher position; said clamping pressure having been adjusted by said thread tension setting means; and home-position resuming means for returning the thread tension fine-adjusting means to the home position from another position when selecting and setting another thread tension by using the thread tension setting means.
problem: Maintaining consistent thread tension across varying stitch types while enabling rapid adjustments and automatic resets to a baseline configuration.
constraint: Ensuring the fine-adjustment mechanism does not interfere with the coarse setting's stability while allowing seamless transitions between different tension requirements.
mechanism: Combining a primary tension adjustment mechanism with a secondary fine-tuning mechanism, coupled with a reset system that returns the secondary mechanism to a baseline when switching operational modes.
mechanism_raw: Combining coarse thread tension setting (via clamping pressure selection) with fine-adjustment capability, coupled with a home-position resuming mechanism that resets the fine-adjustment component when switching stitch types.

abstract: The present invention uses a cold temperature activated batter composition to coat chilled portions of a food substrate. The latent cold temperature of the chilled food, which is preferably fish, is in the range of approximately -10.degree. to 38.degree. F. and activates the batter so as to cause it to gel or set on the food portions. As a result, the batter coating adheres evenly and uniformly to each food portion. After coating with the batter, the chilled food portions may also be coated with a toasted bread crumb mixture, before the batter sets, to form a bread coating mixture, in-situ, on the chilled food portions. The bread crumbs may also include flavored oils derived from frying battered and fried fish or fried battered and breaded chicken in vegetable oils for the purpose of imparting savory and fried food flavor characteristics to the non-fried food.
problem: Achieving uniform adhesion of a batter coating to chilled food substrates without external heating or mechanical agitation.
constraint: Maintaining the substrate's temperature within a specific range (-10°F to 38°F) to ensure activation without premature setting or uneven gelation.
mechanism: Utilizing the inherent temperature of a substrate to activate a temperature-sensitive coating composition, causing it to gel upon contact for even application and subsequent layering.
mechanism_raw: Leveraging the latent cold temperature of the food substrate to activate a temperature-sensitive batter composition, causing it to gel/set in situ upon contact, enabling even coating and subsequent layering with bread crumbs.

abstract: The present invention relates to a novel compound tetrahydrocurcumin and a substance containing the same, which are produced from curcumin or a substance containing it as a material. This substance has characteristic properties such as strong antioxidative activity and yellowish color generated from reducing the original color of curcumin. The curcumin is being produced from a Zingiberaceae plant classified into Curcuma longa as a tropical product and is used for a spice and a yellow pigment for curry powder and pickles. The present invention further relates to the production method.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical compound (tetrahydrocurcumin) and its production method, focusing on altering curcumin's properties through reduction. The mechanism is tied to a particular chemical synthesis process rather than a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: A protective face guard for use in baseball and other sports and which comprises a mask piece, an impact cushioning forehead pad, an impact cushioning mouth pad, a strap and a mouth guard. The mask piece includes a front protective portion extending from a point just above the player's head to a point below the player's chin and also includes two side protective portions extending from opposite sides of the front portion. The mask piece is formed with a visor aperture to accommodate the visor of a cap worn by a player and a vision aperture which provides the player with an unobstructed front and peripheral view. The mask piece is illustrated in a first embodiment as being formed from a sheet of molded thermoplastic material and in a second embodiment as being formed from a matrix of interconnected rod members.
problem: Providing facial protection in sports while maintaining unobstructed vision and comfort through a lightweight, impact-resistant structure.
constraint: Balancing structural integrity and impact absorption with minimal material usage to avoid obstructing the player's field of view or adding excessive weight.
mechanism: Designing a protective structure with strategically placed apertures and a network of interconnected members to distribute impact forces while preserving visibility.
mechanism_raw: Designing a mask with strategically placed apertures (visor and vision windows) and a matrix of interconnected rod members or molded thermoplastic to distribute impact forces while preserving peripheral and frontal visibility.

abstract: The method is founded on the GUAZZO algorithm and is adaptive as it does not require any prior statistical knowledge of source of message to be coded. The message is comprised of a sequence of symbols of the source which are represented by the indication of the direction "0" or "1" chosen at each node of a binary tree. According to the invention, the adaptiveness is obtained by associating with each node two finite-sized counters that count the "0"s and "1"s according to the routing of the tree. The contents of these counters enable the conditional probability of each of the elements "0" and "1" to be estimated at the node.
problem: Adaptive data compression or encoding without prior statistical knowledge of the source message.
constraint: Finite counter size limits memory usage but introduces a trade-off between estimation accuracy and resource efficiency.
mechanism: Dynamically tracking symbol frequencies using bounded memory elements arranged in a hierarchical structure to enable adaptive encoding without prior statistical knowledge of the source.
mechanism_raw: Associating finite-sized counters at each node of a binary tree to dynamically track symbol occurrences ('0'/'1') based on routing, enabling real-time estimation of conditional probabilities for adaptive coding.

abstract: The electronic musical instrument, which is suitable for generating sustaining tone of a rubbed string instrument, has a manipulator for achieving performance manipulation in a linear manipulation region or in a plane manipulation region to simulate the motion of a bow of the rubbed string instrument, and a processing circuit for applying smoothing treatment to signals given by the manipulator. The musical tone generated by the electronic musical instrument can be prevented from being contaminated with discordant sound caused by noise produced in performance manipulation.
problem: Preventing discordant noise in electronic musical tones caused by performance manipulation signals.
constraint: Balancing noise reduction with retention of performance nuance to avoid over-smoothing and loss of expressive control.
mechanism: Filtering noise from performance input signals while preserving intended expressive characteristics through signal smoothing, balancing noise reduction with retention of nuance.
mechanism_raw: Applying signal smoothing to manipulator-generated performance inputs to filter out noise while preserving intended tonal characteristics.

abstract: Apparatus and method are disclosed for monitoring catalytic converter efficiency in treating exhaust gas from an internal combustion engine having fuel control means for controlling the air to fuel ratio at which fuel is supplied to the engine in response to a fuel flow control signal. During a normal operation mode, the control signal means generates the fuel flow control signal based at least in part on output signals from first and second EGO sensors exposed to the exhaust gas upstream and downstream, respectively, of the catalytic converter. The normal operation mode is periodically interrupted by a test operation mode, preferably initiated during substantially steady state operation of the engine, during which the engine is controlled in response to the output signal from the first EGO sensor without the signal from the second EGO sensor. Air to fuel ratio perturbations about a mean value corresponding to stoichiometry are introduced, comprising an initial lean interval of air to fuel ratio higher than stoichiometry, typically for about 5 seconds, followed by a series of rich intervals alternating with lean intervals. An efficiency value for the catalytic converter corresponding to its emissions treatment efficiency is determined based on the number of perturbations detected by the upstream EGO sensor versus the number detected by the downstream EGO sensor.
problem: Monitoring catalytic converter efficiency without disrupting normal engine operation.
constraint: Test mode must occur during steady-state conditions to avoid interference with dynamic engine operation.
mechanism: Introducing controlled perturbations in a system parameter during steady-state operation and comparing upstream and downstream sensor responses to quantify emissions treatment efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Introducing controlled air-to-fuel ratio perturbations during steady-state operation and comparing upstream/downstream sensor responses to quantify emissions treatment efficiency.

abstract: A device for safely collecting and transporting solvents in a manner that can be wheeled rather than carried, including a main tank for storing the solvent, and a neck member for transferring the solvent from the storage tank to the main tank. The device has a grounding strap for safety and a sight glass for viewing the solvent.
reason: The device combines standard safety (grounding strap) and visibility (sight glass) components for solvent transport. No novel causal mechanism is described beyond conventional product design.

abstract: A statically and dynamically self-adjusting and orthopedically-correct saddle and tree which are also anatomically correct for a rider. There are a pair of flat first bars which support the weight distributed on the horse's back. There is also a seat portion comprising a seat and a cantel with a pair of flat second bars extending forward from the seat. The seat with the seat center positioned at a point under the center of gravity of a rider and over the low point in the horse's back. Elastomeric members connect the seat portion to the pair of first bars. A girth is attached to the seat portion by a connecting harness and a pair of stirrup straps are attached to respective ones of the pair of flat second bars at a distance in front of the center of gravity of a rider equal to a distance between the rider's ankle and the ball of the rider's foot. The padding material over the first bars adjacent the horse's back dynamically adjusts to the horse's back at times of greatest dynamic motion.
problem: Creating an orthopedically correct saddle that dynamically adapts to rider and horse motion while maintaining anatomical alignment.
constraint: Balancing structural support, comfort, and anatomical correctness under varying dynamic loads during riding.
mechanism: Using flexible elements to connect a load-bearing surface to a support structure, enabling dynamic adjustment of pressure distribution and alignment in response to motion-induced forces while balancing structural support and comfort.
mechanism_raw: Using elastomeric members to connect the seat to support bars, enabling dynamic adjustment of pressure distribution and alignment based on motion-induced forces.

abstract: The sensor assembly includes a sensor tube in communication with the inner tank. A flush line extending from the liquid cryogen fill line is connected to the sensor tube at a three-way valve. The three way valve also connects the sensor tube to a pressure transducer. During normal operation, the sensor tube is in communication with the pressure transducer such that the level of liquid in the dewar can be monitored. When the liquid level falls below a predetermined level, the pressure transducer activates the three-way valve to connect the sensor tube to the flush line and opens a solenoid located in the fill line. As the cryogen liquid enters the fill line, a portion of it is diverted through the flush line, is vaporized and is passed through the sensor tube. The relatively warm gas flow in the sensor tube prevents the formation of ice and eliminates the problems associated therewith. A timer reverses the three-way valve to reconnect the sensor tube to the pressure transducer so that the pressure transducer can close the second solenoid and terminate the fill operation when the predetermined maximum liquid level has been reached.
problem: Ice formation in sensor tubes that monitor liquid cryogen levels in dewars, which blocks pressure sensing and prevents accurate level monitoring.
constraint: The flushing must be temporary and the system must return to sensing mode to continue monitoring; the warm gas flow must be sufficient to prevent ice but not disrupt normal operation, and the timer must coordinate the transition between flushing and sensing modes.
mechanism: Periodic temporary diversion of a warm gas flow to a sensing line to prevent ice blockage, coordinated by a timer that switches between a flushing mode and a sensing mode. The warm gas flow is sourced from an existing system line, and the timer ensures the transition between modes restores normal pressure monitoring without continuous actuation.
mechanism_raw: Automatic periodic flushing of the sensor line using a diverted warm gas flow from the fill line. When liquid level drops below a threshold, a three-way valve connects the sensor tube to a flush line and a solenoid opens in the fill line, diverting warm cryogen gas through the sensor tube to prevent ice formation. A timer then reverses the valve to reconnect the sensor tube to the pressure transducer, restoring normal sensing operation.

abstract: An aluminum-nitrogen polymer is prepared by reacting an organic nitrile with a dialkylaluminum hydride to form an organoaluminum imine, and heating the imine to a temperature of 50.degree. to 200.degree. C. for at least 2 hours. The polymeric product can be subjected to an additional heat treatment to form a more highly cross-linked polymer. After either heat treatment the polymeric product can be further reacted with a primary amine or ammonia. The organoaluminum imine as well as the aminated or non-aminated polymers can be pyrolyzed to form an aluminum nitride-containing ceramic.
problem: Synthesizing aluminum nitride-containing ceramics or polymers from organic precursors with controlled material properties.
constraint: Temperature control (50-200°C) and timing (at least 2 hours) for each step; the imine intermediate must be formed before polymerization, and thermal treatment windows must be controlled to tune cross-linking without degrading the intermediate.
mechanism: Multi-step chemical synthesis using a controlled intermediate formation to bridge organic precursors to a target material. A first reaction creates a reactive intermediate under specific temperature and timing constraints, followed by thermal treatment to build material structure. Optional post-treatments modify properties before a final conversion step, with process windows tuned to balance cross-linking and intermediate stability.
mechanism_raw: Multi-step chemical conversion using an intermediate imine formation to bridge organic nitriles to aluminum-containing polymers. An organoaluminum imine is formed by reacting an organic nitrile with a dialkylaluminum hydride, then heated to build polymer structure. Optional post-treatments (additional heat treatment for cross-linking, reaction with amine/ammonia) modify properties before final pyrolysis to form the ceramic.

abstract: A method for deforming, splitting and chopping of contaminated, or potentially contaminated, heat exchanger tubes into short tubes segments that easily may transported to an off-site location for decontamination or disposal. The method has particular utility in dismantling potentially contaminated tubes from a tube bundle that is part of a condenser for a BWR or PWR nuclear power plant. The method involves first gripping and deforming the exterior periphery of a potentially contaminated tube with opposed transverse forces sufficient to travel the tube longitudinally out of the tubesheets in a deformed condition, and then splitting the deformed tube into first and second wall sections which are chopped into short length wall segments. The deformation preferably flattens the tube so that the short wall segments are substantially planar, with exposed inner and outer surfaces.
problem: Safely dismantling and segmenting contaminated elongated objects (heat exchanger tubes) from fixed assemblies for transport and disposal without spreading contamination.
constraint: The deformation must be sufficient to extract the tube from tubesheets but controlled enough to enable clean splitting; the deformation must produce planar segments suitable for chopping without generating uncontrolled fragments.
mechanism: Sequential mechanical processing where deformation precedes segmentation. Opposed forces grip and longitudinally deform an elongated object to extract it from a fixed assembly, then the deformed object is split into planar segments and further divided into shorter pieces. The deformation step serves dual purposes: enabling extraction and creating geometrically stable segments for controlled downstream processing.
mechanism_raw: Sequential mechanical processing where deformation precedes cutting. First, opposed transverse forces grip and deform the tube longitudinally to extract it from tubesheets in a deformed condition. Then the deformed tube is split into wall sections, which are chopped into short segments. The deformation step serves dual purposes: extraction from the fixed assembly and creating planar segments with exposed inner and outer surfaces for easier handling.

abstract: A tool for assisting people in opening pull tab actuated cans of two types. The tool is provided with structural features for engaging a pull tab ring to facilitate pivotal movement of a pull tab. The tool is also provided with structural features including a hook for engaging a pull tab ring of a pull tab to facilitate substantially linear movement of the pull tab for removing tear-away lids of cans so equipped.
reason: This is a simple mechanical tool with two different engagement geometries (one for pivotal movement, one for linear movement) for different can types. It is a basic multi-interface adapter without any interesting causal mechanism, automatic behavior, or feedback loop. It represents a product feature rather than a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A process for the pyrolysis of carbonation materials such as wood which comprises directly or indirectly heating the carbonaceous material with flue gases. When carbonization commences the direct heating is stopped while indirect heating continues until carbonization is complete. There is also described an application for effecting the process.
problem: Efficient and controlled pyrolysis/carbonization of carbonaceous materials (such as wood) using waste heat from flue gases.
constraint: The transition from direct to indirect heating must be timed to coincide with the onset of carbonization; direct heating must stop when carbonization begins to avoid over-heating or uncontrolled combustion, while indirect heating must continue to complete the process.
mechanism: Staged thermal processing using a heat source with a method transition at a critical reaction milestone. Initially, the material is heated via direct contact with the heat source. When a primary reaction phase begins, direct heating is halted while indirect heating continues until the reaction completes. This staged approach optimizes energy efficiency and prevents over-heating by changing the heating mechanism at the onset of the main reaction.
mechanism_raw: Staged thermal processing using flue gas heat with a transition from direct to indirect heating at a specific process milestone. Initially, the material is heated directly or indirectly with flue gases. When carbonization commences, direct heating is stopped while indirect heating continues until carbonization is complete. This staged approach optimizes energy use and process control by changing the heating method at the onset of the main reaction phase.

abstract: For the manufacture of curved insulating glazing panes having close tolerances of form, surface and thickness, the curved single glass sheets (2; 22) are brought to their desired shape via rigid suction mold plates (1; 21) and are glued together in this condition. A device suitable for carrying out this method consists of a press having two rigid plates (3; 23), template strips (4, 5; 24, 25) and positioning stops (8, 10; 28, 30) corresponding to the theoretical shape of the glass sheets, and also retractable suckers (15; 26) disposed between the template strips (4, 5; 24, 25), being mounted on the rigid plates (3; 23).
problem: Shaping curved insulating glazing panes with close tolerances of form, surface, and thickness while maintaining structural integrity during assembly.
constraint: Balancing the rigidity of the mold plates to maintain shape accuracy against the need for retractable suction to enable part removal without deforming the cured assembly.
mechanism: A vacuum-assisted molding system uses rigid mold plates to maintain a curved shape of a deformable sheet while a press applies alignment elements and bonding pressure. Selective release mechanisms enable part removal without distorting the cured assembly by temporarily decoupling the vacuum force.
mechanism_raw: Rigid suction mold plates hold individual glass sheets in the desired curved shape via vacuum, while a press with template strips and positioning stops ensures precise alignment and gluing in the molded condition. Retractable suckers between template strips allow controlled release after bonding.
residual_terms: ["vacuum-assisted molding", "rigid mold plates", "alignment elements", "bonding pressure", "selective release mechanisms"]

abstract: An insertion station for a mail-handling machine includes a driving lever 25 and a means for swivelling the driving lever 25 back-and-forth according to an operating cycle. Axle members 18, 19 have a cam 20 mounted therebetween and a spring 26 extends between the driving lever 25 and the cam. A base plate 1 includes grooves 2, 3, 4 and finger-roller guides 28 have front and rear ends mounted above the base plate. Insertion ramps 35, 36, 37 are located below the rear ends of the finger-roller guides; and, inserting arm means 8, 9, 10 and 14, 15, 16 have fingers 5, 6, 7 and finger rollers 27, 38, 39 attached thereto. The inserting arm means 8, 9, 10 and 14, 15, 16 are connected to the axles 18, 19; the fingers 5, 6 and 7 are mounted on the insertion arms which are adapted to slide the fingers 5, 6, and 7 forwardly in an input direction in the grooves 2, 3, 4 of the base plate 1; and, the finger rollers 27, 38, 39 are in engagement with the finger-roller guides 28 for movement backwardly and upwardly above the base plate under control of the finger-roller guides, wherein, upon reaching the rear end of the finger-roller guides, the finger rollers 27, 38, 39 fall onto the insertion ramps 35, 36, 37 for the gradual insertion of the input fingers into the corresponding grooves 2, 3, 4 of the base plate 1. Rotary tension-adjustment means are connected between the axles 18, 19 and the inserting arm means for reducing bounce of the inserting-arm means.
problem: Accurately inserting input fingers into grooves of a base plate in a mail-handling machine while minimizing mechanical bounce and misalignment.
constraint: Synchronizing the upward/downward motion of fingers and rollers via guides and ramps to ensure precise insertion timing while reducing dynamic instability (bounce) through tension control.
mechanism: Coordinated insertion elements with guided motion follow a path defined by ramps and guides to position components into recesses. Dynamic instability during insertion is reduced by applying controlled tension to counteract oscillatory forces.
mechanism_raw: A coordinated system of inserting arms with fingers and finger rollers engages with finger-roller guides and insertion ramps. The rollers follow the guides to lift and position the fingers above the base plate, then fall onto ramps to gradually insert the fingers into grooves. Rotary tension adjustment dampens bounce during operation.

abstract: This invention relates generally to portable drawing surfaces and more particularly to a base structure with interchangeable components. The invention permits the manufacture of a base structure that can be combined with an accessory unit and a working surface to create either a lighted drawing surface or a drawing surface with a utensil accessory tray. This results in substantial savings in manufacturing costs as tooling requirements are substantially lowered. The lighted drawing surface includes a working surface, a lighting accessory unit and a base structure to provide a backlit surface for tracing and drawing. The portable drawing surface replaces the lighting accessory unit with a utensil accessory unit and thereby provides a drawing surface with a tray for displaying and organizing utensils.
reason: The patent describes a modular product architecture (interchangeable components) but does not specify a functional mechanism that produces a useful effect through causal interactions. The 'mechanism' is limited to static design choices (e.g., swapping accessory units) rather than a dynamic process or system behavior.

abstract: In a dobby drawing device in a weaving loom, the vertical displacement of a heddle frame is obtained with the aid of a single cable which is guided over first and second actuating levers to a set of springs. Two support shafts selectively support the actuating levers so the device may have a lifting or descending action.
problem: Achieving controlled vertical displacement of a heddle frame in a weaving loom using a single actuation source while enabling selective lifting or descending actions.
constraint: Balancing the tension in the single cable and the selective engagement of support shafts to ensure precise vertical positioning without overcomplicating the mechanical linkage.
mechanism: A single actuation source drives a cable-based linkage system with spring-biased levers. Selective engagement of support elements determines whether the linkage converts input motion into lifting or descending output, enabling bidirectional vertical displacement from a unidirectional input.
mechanism_raw: A single cable is guided over two actuating levers connected to springs. Selective support of the levers by support shafts determines whether the cable tension causes lifting or descending motion of the heddle frame. The cable-lever-spring system converts linear input into vertical displacement.

abstract: Ceramics having principal phases of aluminum iron titanate and mullite corresponding to the overall chemical composition: PA0 50 to 62% by weight Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, PA0 36 to 49.5% by weight titanium oxide, expressed as TiO.sub.2, PA0 0.5 to 10% by weight SiO.sub.2, and PA0 0.2 to 15% by weight iron oxide, expressed as Fe.sub.2 O.sub.3, PA0 up to 1% by weight impurities, PA0 with the sum of Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, TiO.sub.2 and SiO.sub.2 being 100%, wherein the sum of the crystalline phases Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, TiO.sub.2, SiO.sub.2 (other than the principal phases) is less than 6% by weight, based on the sintered body, are useful where a ceramic having a high thermal-shock-resistance is required, such as exhaust port liner internal combustion engines, for example.
reason: The patent specifies a material composition (chemical phases and oxide ratios) optimized for thermal-shock resistance but does not describe a functional mechanism that produces an effect through causal interactions. The 'mechanism' is limited to material properties rather than a process or system behavior.

abstract: A set of golf club irons, each iron including a striking face, a cavity in the back of the club, and a vibration dampening support bar extending between the lower and upper edges and within the cavity. The distance between the center of the support bar to the end of the cavity at the heel of the iron decreases from the less-lofted irons through the more lofted irons. The center of gravity of all of the clubs is substantially at the center of the striking face of the club.
problem: Balancing vibration dampening and center of gravity control in golf club irons with varying loft angles.
constraint: Maintaining a consistent center of gravity position while varying the support bar's placement to accommodate different loft angles without compromising structural integrity or dampening effectiveness.
mechanism: A dampening element is positioned within a structural cavity and systematically relocated relative to a reference edge across different configurations, enabling a mass distribution point to remain aligned with a functional surface while optimizing energy absorption and weight allocation for each configuration's performance requirements.
mechanism_raw: The position of the vibration dampening support bar within the cavity is systematically adjusted relative to the heel edge across different lofted irons, allowing the center of gravity to remain centered on the striking face while optimizing dampening and weight distribution for each club's specific performance requirements.

abstract: The invention relates to a flotation column including a plurality of controlled recycle chambers intentionally introduced into the column to cause the non-float fraction or gangue to drop down in the main float stream while the desired float fraction travels in the opposite direction by recycling to continually mix the pulp while coursing through the column. Recycle zones are positioned on the periphery of the main passage or flotation zone within chambers located in series along the column. A portion of the slurry is drawn into a recycle zone where it passes downwardly to return to the flotation zone or the main passage through the column to again be swept through the column.
problem: Efficiently separating desired float fractions from non-float gangue in a flotation column while maintaining continuous mixing and throughput.
constraint: Balancing the number and positioning of recycle zones to ensure sufficient mixing and directional reversal without excessive energy consumption or flow disruption.
mechanism: Strategically placed reprocessing zones along a separation column periphery create opposing flow directions: material is drawn into reprocessing zones, redirected to re-enter the primary separation region, causing undesired fractions to settle while target fractions migrate upward, enhancing separation through iterative mixing and directional reversal.
mechanism_raw: Controlled recycle chambers are strategically placed along the column periphery to create counter-current flow: slurry is drawn into recycle zones, forced downward to re-enter the main flotation zone, causing non-float material to settle while desired float fractions travel upward, enhancing separation efficiency through repeated mixing and directional reversal.
residual_terms: ["flotation column", "slurry", "recycle chambers", "flotation zone", "non-float material", "desired float fractions"]

abstract: Liquid dispensing apparatus includes a tank for storing liquid to be dispensed, a fill line communicating with an interior of the tank and adapted to be coupled to a source of the liquid, a heating element for heating the liquid, a heating control device for controlling the heating element to heat the liquid to a predetermined temperature, a dispensing device for dispensing liquid from the tank under pressure and a dispensing control device for selectively controlling the dispensing of the liquid by the dispensing device. The fill line is adapted to be connected to existing plumbing, such as a toilet water supply line behind a wall adjacent the toilet. The tank is adapted to be housed in a recessed wall cabinet adjacent the toilet so that the entire apparatus is hidden from view when not in use. The tank includes a sump portion defining a lowermost portion of the tank, to facilitate complete evacuation of liquid from the tank. An electrically operable pump is preferably located at the bottom of the sump portion for discharging liquid therefrom. A sight gauge is located on the front of the tank to permit visual observation of the level of liquid in the tank. User-operable switches are provided to allow a user to manually control the pump and the heating element. A thermostat is provided for automatic control, of the heating element.
problem: Providing a hidden, efficient liquid dispensing system that integrates with existing plumbing while ensuring complete evacuation of liquid from the tank.
constraint: Ensuring the sump design and pump placement facilitate full evacuation without residual liquid, while maintaining compatibility with standard plumbing and user accessibility.
mechanism: A recessed containment vessel with a lowest-point fluid extraction mechanism and visual monitoring enables complete evacuation by positioning the extraction component at the vessel's base, while user-accessible controls allow manual and automated operation. The vessel integrates with existing infrastructure through concealed connections.
mechanism_raw: A sump-shaped tank with a bottom-mounted pump and sight gauge enables complete liquid evacuation by positioning the pump at the lowest point, while user-operable switches and thermostatic controls allow manual and automatic operation. The tank is recessed into a wall cabinet to remain hidden, leveraging existing plumbing connections.

abstract: The objects of the present invention are achieved by a method and means for temporarily suspending sonar beam transducer means on a dihedral wing body at a first underwater location within sonar beam range of said scoured area; scanning a first portion of said scoured area with said sonar beam in a first substantially vertical plane that points in a first azimuth direction, so as to generate signals indicative of the range and bearing of said scanned first portion from said transducer means; and scanning at least a second different portion of said scoured area with said sonar beam in a second different substantially vertical plane that points in a second different azimuth direction, so as to generate signals indicative of the range and bearing of said scanned second portion from said transducer means. In actual practice, scanning by the sonar beam occurs in many different vertical planes and also can be done from different underwater locations.
problem: Systematically scanning a submerged area (e.g., a scoured region) from multiple underwater locations to generate comprehensive range and bearing data.
constraint: Coordinating transducer positioning and scanning angles to ensure full area coverage without redundant overlaps or gaps, while maintaining operational efficiency in underwater environments.
mechanism: A detection transducer is temporarily positioned at multiple locations and scanned across varying angular planes to sequentially cover a target region. The transducer's spatial coordinates and scanning parameters are coordinated to synthesize a composite representation of the region through overlapping data acquisition.
mechanism_raw: A sonar transducer is temporarily suspended at different underwater locations and scanned in multiple vertical planes with varying azimuth directions, allowing sequential coverage of the target area. The transducer's position and scanning angles are coordinated to build a composite map of the area through overlapping data collection.

abstract: The suspension of a door hinged within a frame for swinging movements in a horizontal plane includes an elongated metal cable with blocks secured upon its ends, with spaced apertures within the frame and door and with blocks projected into said apertures and supportably interlocked with the frame and door.
problem: Suspending a door for smooth horizontal swinging motion within a frame while maintaining structural stability and alignment.
constraint: Ensuring the cable and block system provides sufficient tension and alignment to prevent slack or binding during door movement, while accommodating variations in door weight and frame geometry.
mechanism: A flexible tensioning system with interconnected load-distributing elements is threaded through frame and moving component apertures, enabling controlled horizontal displacement while maintaining alignment and load balance. The interlocked elements accommodate weight variations and geometric tolerances without rigid mechanical constraints.
mechanism_raw: An elongated cable with blocks secured at its ends is threaded through apertures in the frame and door, creating a flexible suspension system. The interlocked blocks allow the door to swing horizontally while distributing load evenly along the cable, enabling controlled movement without rigid hinges.

abstract: A trackside device for closing hopper doors (14) has an eccentrically rotatable wheel (18). The wheel (18) rotates upon contacting a hopper door (14) to move it inward to a closed position. In a preferred embodiment, two devices are positioned on opposite sides of a railroad track to simultaneously close doors (14) on both sides of the hopper car.
problem: Automatically closing hopper doors on railroad cars without manual intervention or external power.
constraint: The mechanism must operate passively using only the contact force from the door, requiring precise eccentric geometry to ensure reliable closure without jamming or requiring external energy.
mechanism: An eccentrically mounted element converts linear contact force from a moving surface into rotational motion, which is mechanically translated into inward linear movement to close the surface. The eccentric geometry ensures that initial contact triggers a self-sustaining rotational action that completes the closing motion without external energy.
mechanism_raw: An eccentrically rotatable wheel converts contact force from a moving hopper door into rotational motion, which mechanically translates into inward linear movement to close the door. The eccentric geometry ensures that contact triggers a self-sustaining rotational action that completes the closing motion.

abstract: A process and apparatus for the remediation of soil is provided with a plug flow of soil and counter-current wash of water. The contaminant-containing soil with water is first treated to disengage the contaminant from the soil and form a liquid phase containing water and contaminant. The treated soil and liquid phase is continuously introduced into a wash zone at a first end of the wash zone, and the soil and the liquid phase are conveyed in successive and discrete portions through the wash zone between the first end of the wash zone and a second end of the wash zone to provide an essentially plug-flow of the soil through the wash zone. Wash water is introduced into the wash zone by continuously adding water to the discrete portions at the second end of the wash zone, and the wash water is conveyed through the wash zone between adjacent wash cells toward the first end counter to the plug flow conveyance of the soil and the liquid phase, such that contaminants in the liquid phase are removed from the liquid phase by the wash water. The soil and liquid phase with contaminants removed are continuously withdrawn from the wash zone as each discrete portion reaches the second end of the wash zone. The wash water containing removed contaminants is withdrawn from the discrete portions at the first end of the wash zone.
problem: Efficiently removing contaminants from soil using minimal water and processing time.
constraint: Maintaining discrete plug-flow segments and counter-current water flow requires precise control of material conveyance and water addition rates to prevent mixing and ensure continuous processing.
mechanism: Counter-current flow between discrete material-liquid segments and wash fluid maximizes contaminant transfer. The material and liquid move in segmented plug-flow through a processing zone, while wash fluid flows in the opposite direction through adjacent regions, creating a gradient that drives contaminant removal from the material phase into the wash fluid.
mechanism_raw: Counter-current flow between discrete soil-liquid portions and wash water maximizes contaminant transfer. Soil and liquid move in plug-flow segments through a wash zone, while wash water flows in the opposite direction through adjacent cells, creating a gradient that drives contaminant removal from the liquid phase into the wash water.

abstract: A process for producing via patterns in a ceramic sheet which includes the steps of forming an array of vias and then selectively filling in at least a portion of the vias with a non-conductive filler material, such as a ceramic, to create a custom via pattern. The process is particularly useful for fabricating grid transformers and ceramic printed circuit boards. The present invention also relates to ceramic devices produced by the process, and a universal tool adapted for carrying out the process.
problem: Creating custom via patterns in ceramic sheets for electronic or electromagnetic devices.
constraint: The filling process must precisely target specific vias without affecting adjacent ones, requiring alignment accuracy and material compatibility between the filler and ceramic substrate.
mechanism: Forming an array of voids in a substrate and selectively filling a subset with non-conductive material allows creation of a custom conductive pathway pattern. The unfilled voids serve as conductive paths, while filled voids block or redirect current flow.
mechanism_raw: Forming an array of vias in a ceramic sheet and selectively filling a subset with non-conductive material allows creation of a custom conductive pathway pattern. The unfilled vias serve as conductive paths, while filled vias block or redirect current flow.

abstract: A process is disclosed for making metal plated PPD-T fibers wherein the plating is durable and highly conductive. The process involves contacting the fibers with an 80 to 90% sulfuric acid solution, neutralizing and washing the fibers with water, and then plating the fibers by an electroless plating process. The acid treatment of the fibers promotes adhesion between the metal and the fiber and high electrical conductivity for the plated metal.
problem: Achieving durable, highly conductive metal plating on polymer fibers without delamination.
constraint: The acid concentration (80-90%) and exposure time must be tightly controlled to avoid fiber degradation while ensuring sufficient surface activation for plating adhesion.
mechanism: A chemical treatment modifies the surface chemistry of a substrate, creating reactive sites that enhance adhesion between a deposited material and the substrate. The treatment also cleans and activates the surface, enabling a deposition process to form a uniform, conductive layer.
mechanism_raw: Sulfuric acid treatment modifies the fiber surface chemistry, creating reactive sites that enhance adhesion between the metal and fiber. The acid treatment also cleans and activates the surface, enabling electroless plating to form a uniform, conductive layer.

abstract: A method is described for providing a body of first material and a body of second material in a chemical environment wherein the first material contains first constituents having a lower and higher oxidation state and wherein the second material contains constituents having an oxidation state of energy greater than lower oxidation state of the first constituent.
