The environment is further provided with first cations energetically disposed for receiving electrons from the first constituents but not energetically disposed for receiving electrons from the second constituents. Electrons transfer from the first constituents to the first cations which are transformed thereby into second cations of lower oxidation state resulting in first body releasing into the environment third cations which are cations of the first (lower) oxidation state of the first constituent. The environment is further provided with an agent which consumes the second and third cations thereby permitting release into the environment additional ones of the third cations resulting in the first body being preferably etched with respect to the second body. The method is useful to etch copper in the presence of more highly reactive materials such as chrome, lead, tin, titanium, aluminum, iron, cobalt, and galvanically more active gold and nickel. The method is useful for forming structures containing copper having an overlying layer of the more highly reactive material without the requirement of the use of a resist material.
problem: Selectively etching copper in the presence of more galvanically active materials (e.g., chrome, aluminum, gold) without using resist materials.
constraint: The cation selection and chemical environment must be precisely tuned to ensure electron transfer occurs only from copper, requiring control over oxidation states and reactivity thresholds of all materials involved.
mechanism: Cations in a chemical environment preferentially accept electrons from a target material (lower oxidation state) but not from more reactive materials. This drives target material oxidation and dissolution while leaving other materials intact. A secondary agent consumes dissolved cations, maintaining the electron transfer gradient to sustain selective etching.
mechanism_raw: Cations in the chemical environment preferentially accept electrons from copper (lower oxidation state) but not from more reactive materials. This drives copper oxidation and dissolution while leaving other materials intact. A secondary agent consumes dissolved cations, maintaining the electron transfer gradient to sustain selective etching.

abstract: In the case of an arrangement for the cleaning of the circumferential surface of a delivery roller pair of a drafting unit of a spinning machine, devices are provided for the reinforcing of the cleaning effect while the drafting unit starts up again after a stoppage. Heating devices are also disclosed for heating the pressure rollers before a piecing operation is started.
problem: Maintaining cleaning effectiveness of a delivery roller pair during restart of a drafting unit after a stoppage.
constraint: Balancing heating duration and temperature to avoid damaging rollers while ensuring effective cleaning during transient startup phases.
mechanism: Pre-heating a surface to alter the physical state of accumulated material, facilitating its removal during a subsequent operation by reducing adhesion or structural integrity of the material.
mechanism_raw: Heating pressure rollers before a piecing operation to reinforce cleaning by softening or dislodging debris during startup.

abstract: Improved burner constructions for gas-fired infra-red generators having ceramic fiber matrix through the thickness of which gaseous combustion mixture is passed and as it emerges it is burned to heat emerging surface to incandescence. Burner matrix can be loaded with silicon carbide particles to improve its emissivity, can be made water repellent and its uniformity can be improved. Burner body can be casting, with sheet metal addition to form a baffle and air seal and to grip matrix edges. Combustion mixture plenum can have movable partition assembly separating it from air seals, to adjust portion of matrix at which incandescence is generated. Metal screen can be stretched in front of incandescent surface to assist with low-temperature operation. Large size matrix can have central support fitted and secured to back of burner body. Air seal can be provided by narrow curtain of air extending around internal faces of burner body. Annealing lehr is desirably provided with gas-fired infra-red irradiation, and can have heat losses reduced by diminishing amount of metal used as in a conveyor to move workpieces through.
problem: Achieving uniform and controllable incandescence in gas-fired infrared burners for consistent heating.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and thermal efficiency of the matrix while allowing adjustable partitioning for variable heat distribution.
mechanism: Employing a porous matrix with adjustable partitions to dynamically modify combustion regions, enabling localized control of thermal emission while maintaining structural and thermal efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Using a ceramic fiber matrix with a movable partition to dynamically adjust the combustion zone, enabling localized control of incandescence while maintaining uniformity.

abstract: Two-wire, electronic switch which performs sensing functions, measurement functions, and output-control functions for an electrical load without receiving power from a power source, external or internal, other than the power source for the electrical load that is controlled by the switch. Electronic components of a two-wire, electronic switch which is fabricated in accordance with the present invention obtain power: (a) when the switch is off, from a power source which drives a load which is controlled by the switch and (b) when the switch is on, from an output of devices which convert current to voltage and which receive at least a portion of a current through the load as input.
problem: Powering electronic sensing and control functions in a two-wire switch without an external power source.
constraint: Ensuring harvested power does not disrupt the load's normal operation or exceed voltage/current thresholds during energy extraction.
mechanism: Extracting energy from a load's current during both active and inactive states, using state-dependent conversion methods to sustain electronic functions without disrupting the load.
mechanism_raw: Harvesting energy from the load's current during both on and off states—using direct power when off and a current-to-voltage converter when on—to sustain operation.

abstract: A machine is provided for piercing a taphole for a shaft furnace for applying the piercing rod method. The machine comprises a mounting, with a support for supporting the rod at the front of the mounting, a sliding support for supporting the rod at the rear of the mounting and a clamp, mounted in a sliding manner on the mounting and designed for gripping the rod at any place between the front support and the rear support. A travel multiplier is connected between a jack and the clamp so that the clamp may be moved. Means for controlling the jack make it possible to move the clamp in a to-and-fro motion between a position (B) at the front of the mounting and a position (A) which is located at a distance L from the position (B).
problem: Precisely controlling the position of a piercing rod along a shaft furnace taphole during piercing operations.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical stability and precision over the travel distance L while accommodating variable positioning requirements.
mechanism: Implementing a mechanical linkage with a travel multiplier to enable precise bidirectional adjustment of a component's position over a defined range while maintaining stability.
mechanism_raw: Using a sliding clamp with a travel multiplier connected to a jack, enabling controlled bidirectional movement of the clamp between fixed positions to adjust rod placement.

abstract: Contour data representing the contour of an embroidering area to be covered up with stitches formed by an embroidery machine is read from a contour data storage means and the contour of the embroidering area is displayed on a display on the basis of the contour data. A desired stitching direction for at least one point in the embroidering area is specified by the operator. The embroidering area is divided into a plurality of embroidering sections by dividing line segments parallel to the specified desired stitching direction. A reference point is set for each embroidering section. Each embroidering section is divided into blocks so that the respective contours of all the blocks are convex, and then embroidery data is produced.
problem: Efficiently covering an embroidering area with stitches while accommodating operator-specified stitching directions.
constraint: Balancing the number of divisions and block convexity to minimize stitching complexity while preserving coverage accuracy.
mechanism: Partitioning an area into convex regions aligned with a specified direction to optimize path planning for coverage while minimizing complexity.
mechanism_raw: Dividing the embroidering area into convex blocks using lines parallel to the desired stitching direction, ensuring all block contours are convex for optimized path planning.

abstract: An electric steam humidifier of the type which includes electrodes (58, 59) immersed in a tank containing water (5) includes an upper portion (10) consisting of a housing (3) closed by a cover (2), a lower portion (11) consisting of a housing (6) placed on a base (7), with the housings (3) and (6) being identical and positioned symmetrically in relation to a horizontal plane. The housings are joined to a structural element (4) made of aluminum and approximately U-shaped, with the arms of the U forming a space (40) for receiving the tank. The housing (3) contains a compartment (36) into which water is supplied and which includes an aperture (37) for evacuation of steam and an aperture (35) which is fitted to a filling aperture (54) on the upper surface of the tank (5). The tank includes on one of its side surfaces below the medial plane of the tank but above its bottom with a drainage aperture (55). The drainage aperture is extended outwardly by a well (550) which is connected to a solenoid drainage valve (49) housed within a space which forms an extension of the tank receiving space (40).
problem: Need to drain excess water from a steam humidifier tank while maintaining sufficient water level for electrode operation and proper steam generation, within a compact modular housing design.
constraint: The drainage aperture must be positioned to maintain sufficient water for electrode operation while allowing excess drainage, and the well extension must route drainage to the valve without interfering with steam evacuation or water filling. The symmetric housing design must simultaneously accommodate steam evacuation, water filling, drainage, and structural integrity.
mechanism: A drainage aperture is positioned at a specific height within a containment vessel to establish a minimum fluid level, with a conduit extending from the aperture to route excess fluid to a controllable valve. The aperture height sets the operational fluid threshold, while the valve provides active control over drainage timing. A symmetric modular housing with a structural element creates an alignment and receiving space that accommodates multiple functional apertures for fluid handling and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A drainage aperture is positioned at a specific strategic height within the tank (below the medial plane but above the bottom), extended outwardly by a well that connects to a solenoid valve. This creates a controlled drainage system where the aperture height sets the minimum operational water level, while the solenoid valve provides active control over when drainage occurs. The symmetric modular housing design with a U-shaped structural element creates a receiving space that ensures proper tank alignment and assembly while accommodating steam evacuation and water filling apertures.
residual_terms: ["drainage aperture", "solenoid valve", "symmetric modular housing", "U-shaped structural element"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for an FCC process uses dissipator plates at the outlet of a disengaging vessel to provide a quick separation of catalyst from product vapors and to prevent reentrainment of catalyst into the disengaging vessel. The process and apparatus use a riser for the conversion of an FCC feedstock and direct the effluent from the riser directly into a disengaging vessel to separate catalyst from the product vapors. Catalyst is directed downwardly out of the outlet of the disengaging vessel and through a series of dissipator plates that eliminate the tangential velocity that would be otherwise introduced by the vortex and would lead to reentrainment of catalyst. A stripping vessel is located immediately below the disengaging vessel outlet to receive catalyst as it leaves the dissipator plates. The apparatus and process are specifically suited for operation without a reactor vessel for containment of the disengaging vessel and cyclones.
problem: Catalyst particles reentering the disengaging vessel with product vapors after initial separation in FCC processes, reducing separation efficiency and contaminating the vapor stream.
constraint: The system must operate without a reactor vessel for containment, so the dissipator plates must provide sufficient velocity dissipation and phase separation using only staged plate geometry, without additional containment structure.
mechanism: A series of staged dissipation elements positioned at the outlet of a separation vessel eliminate the tangential velocity component of a downwardly flowing particulate stream. As particulate passes through the staged elements, the vortex-induced velocity that would cause reentrainment is stripped away, allowing clean separation of particulate from vapor. A receiving vessel immediately below collects the particulate after it exits the dissipation elements.
mechanism_raw: A series of dissipator plates positioned at the outlet of the disengaging vessel eliminate the tangential (vortex-induced) velocity component of the downwardly flowing catalyst stream. As catalyst passes through the staged dissipation elements, the problematic tangential velocity that would cause reentrainment is stripped away, allowing clean separation of catalyst from product vapors. A stripping vessel immediately below receives the catalyst after it exits the dissipator plates.

abstract: A method and apparatus for attaching a collarette, display, and label incorporating the use of a sewing machine having a sewing head, a collarette feed means, a display feeder, a label feeder, leading and trailing edge detectors, a stitch counter, and a controller to control each device and perform necessary calculations is disclosed.
reason: The patent describes a coordinated automation system that combines standard, well-known components (multiple feeders, edge detectors, stitch counter, controller) to perform a specific sewing task. There is no novel problem-solving mechanism or causal principle that transcends the specific domain of garment attachment; it is an application of conventional industrial control and sensing techniques.

abstract: A safety system including a surface controlled subsurface safety valves for use in a well having annulus fluid flow. One of the safety valves has a valve closure member, and a small diameter offset piston actuator to move the valve closure member in response to control fluid pressure conducted from the well surface to its open position which allows annulus fluid flow. A spring biases the valve closure member to block annulus fluid flow. The annulus safety valve has an enlarged flow area for use in high volume gas injection wells. The annulus safety valve has metal-to-metal sealing systems to improve valve life under harsh downhole well environments.
problem: Need for reliable fail-safe shut-off in wells with annulus fluid flow, particularly in high-volume gas injection wells operating under harsh downhole conditions where valve failure could lead to uncontrolled flow.
constraint: The valve must provide fail-safe operation (spring-closed when control pressure is lost), high flow capacity (enlarged flow area for high-volume gas injection), and long service life (metal-to-metal sealing) while operating in harsh downhole environments with a compact offset piston actuator design.
mechanism: A compact offset piston actuator moves a valve closure member in response to control fluid pressure, while a biasing element forces the closure member to the safe position. When control pressure is lost, the biasing element automatically closes the valve, providing fail-safe operation. Sealing systems improve valve life under harsh environments, and an enlarged flow area accommodates high volume fluid injection.
mechanism_raw: A small diameter offset piston actuator moves the valve closure member in response to control fluid pressure conducted from the surface, while a spring biases the valve closure member to the closed (safe) position. When control pressure is lost or fails, the spring automatically closes the valve, providing fail-safe operation. Metal-to-metal sealing systems improve valve life under harsh downhole well environments, and an enlarged flow area accommodates high volume gas injection.
residual_terms: ["offset piston actuator", "metal-to-metal sealing", "enlarged flow area", "fail-safe operation"]

abstract: A method and an apparatus for controlling weft inserting without depending on any operation skill, such control being on the basis of at least two kinds of information having mutually different frequencies for correcting weft inserting. A plurality of control rules prepared according to control algorithms, a plurality of data tables for weft inserting prepared according to the control algorithms or approximate expressions are used for calculating the control conditions of an actuator for weft inserting, and the weft inserting actuator is controlled on the basis of the calculated control conditions.
problem: Need to control weft inserting in weaving processes without depending on operator skill, requiring precise and consistent control that adapts to varying conditions.
constraint: The system must use multiple information sources with different frequencies that provide complementary rather than redundant correction data, and must operate independently of operator skill through automated control rules and data tables that translate multi-frequency inputs into precise actuator commands.
mechanism: Multiple information sources with different frequencies provide complementary correction data for controlling a material insertion actuator. Pre-computed control rules and data tables translate the multi-frequency inputs into precise actuator commands based on control algorithms. The actuator is controlled according to these calculated conditions, eliminating dependence on manual operation skill.
mechanism_raw: Using at least two kinds of information with mutually different frequencies to correct weft inserting, where the different frequency information sources provide complementary correction data. Pre-computed control rules and data tables (prepared according to control algorithms or approximate expressions) are used to calculate the control conditions for the weft inserting actuator based on the multi-frequency information. The actuator is then controlled on the basis of these calculated control conditions, eliminating dependence on manual operation skill.

abstract: A rescue chute suitable for attachment to a fixed structure or to an aerial ladder is disclosed. The chute has two concentric fabric chutes (2,4) supported by a multi-purpose mounting bracket (6). The chutes (2, 4) are made of a heat-resistant material. The outer chute has guying rings (8) along its length and is closed with snap hook-and-ring closures (14). The inner chute (4) has a zipper (18) running the entire length of the chute. Zipper-stops and zipper-pulls allow the inner chute to be opened at the different points to allow people to exit the chute. A snap hook (20) at the end of each zipper (18) ensures that the zipper remains closed as the chute is used. An elastic panel (24) runs the entire length of the chute. The elastic (104) may be sandwiched to protect it from heat. The rescue chute includes a non-abrasive entry flap (26). The multipurpose bracket (6) is adaptable to support the chute on a building wall or on an aerial ladder. The bracket (6) is made of coated tubular aluminum and includes an adjustable clamp (34-40) for securing the rescue chute to a wall or balcony. To secure the rescue chute to an aerial ladder, clamp arms (48) and a leveling arm (50) are provided. A metal spoked adjusting wheel (52) allows the rescue chute to be leveled. Hook clamps (58) are used to grasp the ladder rungs. The chutes (2) and (4) are secured to the multi-purpose bracket by means of grommets, reinforced nylon webbing, bolts, and aluminum strips.
problem: Providing a safe, adaptable rescue chute that can be securely attached to varied structures (e.g., walls, ladders) while allowing controlled egress for users.
constraint: Balancing heat resistance, structural stability, and rapid deployment while accommodating variable attachment points and user egress requirements.
mechanism: A dual-layer chute system where an outer stabilization layer provides structural integrity through distributed anchoring points, and an inner egress layer enables controlled user exit via variable openings. An adaptable mounting interface dynamically adjusts to heterogeneous attachment surfaces while maintaining load distribution.
mechanism_raw: A dual concentric chute system with an outer chute stabilized by guying rings and snap closures, and an inner chute with a full-length zipper and elastic panel. The zipper allows users to exit at different points, while the elastic panel maintains structural integrity under dynamic loads. The multipurpose bracket adapts to different mounting surfaces via adjustable clamps and hook clamps.
residual_terms: ["dual-layer chute system", "distributed anchoring points", "variable openings", "adaptable mounting interface", "load distribution"]

abstract: A backstop device of a carrier in a trolley conveyor having the carrier riding on a traveling rail in and out of engagement with a travelling chain. The carrier has traveling rollers with backstop rings fixedly and interiorly mounted thereupon. Each of the backstop rings has a multitude of backstop holes on the circumference of the peripheral surface of the backstop rings for engagement with a pawl.
problem: Preventing unintended reverse movement of a carrier in a trolley conveyor system while allowing forward motion.
constraint: Ensuring reliable pawl engagement without jamming in a high-speed, dynamic conveyor environment.
mechanism: A unidirectional motion control system using a pawl engaging a ratcheted element with periodic engagement features. The pawl blocks reverse motion through mechanical interference while permitting forward movement, with the ratcheted element mounted on a moving component to ensure consistent engagement.
mechanism_raw: Backstop rings with circumferential holes engage a pawl to create a ratchet-like mechanism. The interiorly mounted rings on traveling rollers ensure consistent engagement with the pawl, blocking reverse motion while permitting forward movement.
residual_terms: ["unidirectional motion control", "pawl", "ratcheted element", "periodic engagement features", "mechanical interference"]

abstract: Coffee aroma gases are conveyed to a cryogenic collector in which liquid nitrogen is sprayed directly into the aroma gas stream to rapidly condense the aroma gas and form finely divided particles of coffee aroma frost suspended in a stream of nitrogen gas, while minimizing contact of the cooled gas with the walls of the collector. The suspension of aroma frost particles in gaseous nitrogen is passed through a tubular porous filter to remove the aroma frost particles which collect on the outer surface of the tubular filter, with the nitrogen gas passing through the porous filter and being exhausted from the collector. The porous filter is periodically back pulsed to dislodge aroma frost particles collected on the outer surface of the tubular filter, with the particles being recovered for incorporation in soluble coffee products. Condensation of aroma components present in the aroma gas may be carried out in several stages to effect fractionation of the aroma gas.
problem: Efficiently capturing and recovering volatile aroma compounds from gas streams while minimizing thermal degradation and wall contact.
constraint: Maintaining particle suspension and filter efficiency while preventing wall contact and enabling periodic cleaning without system shutdown.
mechanism: A cryogenic particle capture system where a cooling medium directly interacts with a gas stream to form suspended solid particles. A porous collection surface captures particles, and a reverse-flow cleaning mechanism periodically dislodges accumulated material. Multi-stage cooling enables selective separation of components.
mechanism_raw: Cryogenic condensation using liquid nitrogen spray directly into the gas stream forms suspended aroma frost particles. A porous tubular filter collects particles on its outer surface, and periodic back-pulsing dislodges them for recovery. Multi-stage condensation enables fractionation of aroma components.
residual_terms: ["cryogenic particle capture", "cooling medium", "porous collection surface", "reverse-flow cleaning", "multi-stage cooling"]

abstract: A cosmetic preparation dispenser is provided that has a resilient tab formed on the lower end of the innerbody that presses against the cam sleeve to provide a desirable swivel drag, and which tab is prevented from undesirable deformation that reduces the swivel torque by providing a relaxation zone in the cam sleeve where the tab can recall its original shape. The relaxation zone is preferably a thin walled section of the cam sleeve that is formed by the combination of a flat outer wall and a circular inner wall, which thin walled section is deformable by pressure from the tab when the tab is seated against the thin walled section. The tab presses against the cam sleeve which causes the cam sleeve to move up a bevelled shoulder to enhance swivel drag between the cam sleeve and a retaining lip on the innerbody. The bevelled shoulder also engages the cam sleeve when force is applied to the elevator.
problem: Maintaining consistent swivel torque in a cosmetic dispenser without permanent deformation of the resilient tab.
constraint: Balancing swivel drag force with material fatigue resistance in a compact, high-cycle mechanical interface.
mechanism: A torque regulation system using a resilient element interacting with a deformable zone to create controlled friction. The deformable zone allows temporary shape change under load, while a recovery mechanism restores the element's original geometry, preventing permanent deformation and maintaining consistent torque output.
mechanism_raw: A resilient tab presses against a cam sleeve with a thin-walled relaxation zone. The tab deforms the thin-walled section to enhance swivel drag, while the relaxation zone allows the tab to return to its original shape, preventing torque reduction from plastic deformation.

abstract: A toothbrush for use by wearers of orthodontic appliances comprises an elongated handle, a neck and a head. The bristles are designed so that the outermost rows are relatively soft and of long length, the bristles in the pattern gradually shortening in length and becoming stiffer, with the shortest and stiffest bristles being positioned along the center rows of the brush's longitudinal centerline axis. Also, the center rows of bristles are formed to be angled at their ends to reduce the pressure required to deflect the bristles beneath brace elements thus reducing undue pressure against the gums. Furthermore, a flexible member compressibly supports the center rows of bristles. The toothbrush also comprises an outer bumper protectively surrounding the toothbrush head. Moreover, a further embodiment of the invention has a lower tuft of bristles projecting from the lower portion of the handle.
problem: Cleaning teeth and gums effectively around orthodontic appliances without causing tissue damage or excessive pressure.
constraint: Optimizing cleaning efficacy across varying anatomical contours while minimizing gum trauma and brace interference.
mechanism: A variable-stiffness cleaning interface with spatially graded bristle properties to adapt to anatomical contours. A flexible support structure maintains bristle orientation, while a protective bumper element limits pressure application during use.
mechanism_raw: Graduated bristle stiffness and length: outer rows are soft and long, center rows are stiff and short, with angled ends to reduce deflection pressure. A flexible member supports center bristles, and an outer bumper protects the head during use.
residual_terms: ["variable-stiffness cleaning interface", "spatially graded bristle properties", "flexible support structure", "protective bumper element"]

abstract: An optical recording structure comprises a thermally stable substrate and a polymeric layer deposited on the substrate comprised of a poly(ester-amide). Laser beams are directed at the deposited polymeric layer to record or erase information. The recording structure has an excellent dimensional and mechanical stability on storage, readily and easily records information, and has an ability to be easily and completely erased.
problem: Creating a stable optical recording medium that allows reversible data storage (recording and erasing) without dimensional or mechanical degradation over time.
constraint: Balancing the polymer's thermal stability to prevent permanent deformation during laser exposure while ensuring sufficient sensitivity for reversible recording and erasing.
mechanism: Using a thermally responsive polymeric layer deposited on a dimensionally stable substrate, where controlled thermal energy input induces reversible physical state changes in the polymer enabling data recording and erasing while maintaining structural integrity through the material's inherent thermal stability.
mechanism_raw: Using a poly(ester-amide) polymeric layer deposited on a thermally stable substrate, where laser-induced thermal changes in the polymer enable reversible data recording while maintaining structural integrity due to the material's inherent thermal stability.

abstract: An assembly member includes a rod having at one end thereof a head for driving the rod in rotation, a threaded part at an opposite end and, between the threaded part and the head, a smooth part the diameter of which is markedly larger than a threadroot diameter of the threaded part. Such member is used for the fastening of insulating layers of facade coverings or claddings.
problem: Fastening insulating layers of facade coverings or claddings without damaging the material or compromising the fastening strength.
constraint: Maintaining a diameter difference between the smooth section and thread root to ensure controlled insertion and secure fastening without over-tightening or material damage.
mechanism: Designing a fastening element with a smooth leading section of larger diameter than the threaded section, allowing rotational driving into the material before thread engagement, which distributes insertion force and prevents localized stress concentration on the material.
mechanism_raw: Designing a rod with a smooth section of larger diameter than the threaded part, allowing rotational driving of the rod into the material before threading, which distributes force and prevents localized stress on the insulation.

abstract: Self-propelled mobile apparatus for aerating water includes a vessel configured for movement across a body of water, and a mechanism contained entirely on the vessel for propelling the vessel across a body of water. A water aerating device is disposed on the vessel for aerating water as the vessel is propelled across a body of water. A method of aerating a body of water includes placing an entirely self-propelled vessel on a body of water to be aerated, propelling the self-propelled vessel across the body of water, and activating an aeration device disposed on the vessel.
problem: Aerating large bodies of water efficiently without requiring external propulsion or fixed infrastructure.
constraint: Ensuring the vessel's propulsion and aeration systems are entirely self-sufficient and compact enough to operate independently without external support.
mechanism: Integrating a self-sufficient propulsion system and fluid aeration mechanism on a mobile platform, enabling autonomous traversal across a liquid surface while performing in-situ aeration without external support or fixed infrastructure.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a self-contained propulsion system and water aeration device on a mobile vessel, enabling autonomous movement across the water surface while performing aeration tasks in situ.

abstract: The invention relates to a method of establishing and maintaining in sealed tents or the like mobile units, an environment which is independent of the surroundings with regard to temperature and contamination. The invention is characterized by taking air from the surroundings, extracting contaminated particles and gas from the air by filtration, and causing the air to pass into the mobile unit so as to establish a predetermined air pressure which is higher than the air pressure of the surroundings. The filtered air is mixed with air recycled from within the mobile unit when the aforesaid predetermined air pressure has been reached and mixing of the filtered air with recycled air is continued for as long as the internal air pressure is equal to or greater than the predetermined air pressure. The air mixture is heated or cooled to a predetermined temperature and is then distributed essentially uniformly in the mobile unit and filtered, in conjunction therewith, so as to extract any remaining particles and gas. The invention also relates to an arrangement for carrying out the method.
problem: Maintaining a sealed mobile unit's internal environment (temperature and contamination control) independently of external conditions.
constraint: Balancing air pressure, filtration efficiency, and temperature control to prevent contamination ingress while minimizing energy consumption and maintaining system autonomy.
mechanism: Combining external air filtration, internal pressure regulation to maintain higher pressure than surroundings, controlled mixing of filtered external air with recycled internal air, and uniform thermal conditioning to create a stable, contaminant-free internal environment.
mechanism_raw: Combining filtration of external air, pressure regulation to maintain higher internal pressure than surroundings, mixing filtered air with recycled internal air, and uniform temperature conditioning to create a stable, contaminant-free environment.

abstract: Rotative inserting unit for documents and sheets of paper for use, in particular, with automatic equipment for the printing and the inserting of said materials into envelopes. The unit comprises a drum (14) for the feeding of the already folded sheets, rotating intermittently, on the side surface (14a) of which transport seats are formed for the paper sheets, on subsequent angular portions of the surface, as well as fixed guide means (19) inside which said surface rotates. A conveyor (21) for the envelopes is also provided for, located at the exit of an automatic distributor box (24) of the envelopes and converging towards the exit of said guide means (19) in a position substantially tangent to the surface of said drum and in correspondence with the opening of a mobile pocket (33) for the temporary collection of the envelopes. There are further provided means (41) for lifting at least one edge delimitating the mouth of the envelope periodically contained inside said pocket in order to allow the insertion of the sheet exiting said guide means.
problem: Automatically inserting folded sheets into envelopes in high-speed printing and inserting equipment without jams or misalignment.
constraint: Coordinating the drum's intermittent rotation, envelope delivery, and lifting mechanism timing to avoid mechanical interference while maintaining high throughput.
mechanism: Synchronizing a rotating transport element with sheet retention positions, a conveyor system for envelope delivery, and a periodic lifting mechanism for envelope openings, ensuring precise temporal coordination and alignment for smooth sheet insertion at the point of envelope opening.
mechanism_raw: Synchronizing a rotating drum with transport seats for sheets, a conveyor for envelopes, and a periodic lifting mechanism for envelope mouths, ensuring precise timing and alignment for smooth insertion at the point of envelope opening.
residual_terms: ["rotating transport element", "sheet retention positions", "conveyor system", "periodic lifting mechanism", "temporal coordination", "sheet insertion"]

abstract: Disclosed is a novel method for cleaning an electrostatic precipitator by directing a stream of cleaning gas through a flexible tube positioned inside the electrostatic precipitator. The stream of gas causing the flexible tube to move randomly directing the stream of gas at the precipitator plates with sufficient force to dislodge particles adhered to such plates.
problem: Cleaning particles adhered to electrostatic precipitator plates without manual intervention or complex mechanical systems.
constraint: The system must rely on the gas stream's pressure and the tube's flexibility to achieve random motion without external control mechanisms, balancing coverage efficiency with structural simplicity.
mechanism: A flexible conduit is positioned within a particle collection surface and actuated by a fluid stream's pressure, generating uncontrolled motion that redirects the stream across the surface to dislodge accumulated material through stochastic coverage.
mechanism_raw: A flexible tube is positioned inside the precipitator and moved randomly by a stream of cleaning gas. The random motion of the tube directs the gas stream across the precipitator plates, dislodging particles through dynamic, uncontrolled coverage of the surface.

abstract: An apparatus on an aircraft provides external aircraft lighting which incorporates a coding system to facilitate visual identification of the aircraft. The lighting apparatus includes a plurality of optically-coupled components for generating, transmitting and projecting a laser beam. The components are installed in an interior compartment of the aircraft and are operable to generate the laser beam, to transmit the generated laser beam to a location adjacent to an exterior portion of the aircraft fuselage, and to project the transmitted laser beam in a predetermined direction from the exterior portion of the aircraft and in a predetermined pattern. The coding system incorporated by the pattern is based upon the properties of beam color, beam portion number and beam pulse frequency. Different values are assigned for these properties to code the different characteristics which can be used to identify the aircraft.
problem: Visually identifying aircraft in low-visibility or high-traffic airspace using external lighting.
constraint: The coding system must operate within the constraints of existing aircraft interior components and laser technology, requiring multi-parameter encoding without additional hardware complexity.
mechanism: A directed energy beam is emitted from a platform with systematically varied output characteristics (spectral composition, temporal modulation, and spatial distribution) to encode distinguishable identifiers for visual differentiation.
mechanism_raw: A laser beam is generated, transmitted, and projected in a predetermined pattern from the aircraft's exterior. The beam's properties (color, pulse frequency, and beam count) are systematically varied to encode unique identification codes, enabling visual differentiation of aircraft.

abstract: A method of locating properly and comfortably a protective helmet on the head of a person. A fit, locating and comfort band is mounted around the persons head, namely adjacent the ears and the back of the head and over the forehead. Thereafter, a protective plastic helmet having a foam lining is mounted over the band as a separate and distinct operation. The method further comprises employing a harness above the band to aid in keeping it in place while the helmet is subsequently mounted, and to protect the top of the head from discomfort caused by a central foam element of the helmet. The apparatus comprises the band and harness and helmet employed in combination with each other, but with no need for the band or harness to be connected to the helmet. In accordance with another aspect of the method and apparatus, an inflatable bladder is employed to aid in maintaining the band and helmet in the desired positions.
problem: Properly and comfortably positioning a protective helmet on a person's head while maintaining stability during movement.
constraint: The system must decouple the helmet's positioning from the band's adjustment to avoid mechanical interference while ensuring stability and comfort through inflation-based customization.
mechanism: A support structure is adjusted independently from a protective shell using a deformable interface, allowing positional decoupling between the shell and adjustment mechanism while maintaining stability through inflation-based customization.
mechanism_raw: A fit band is mounted around the head independently of the helmet, with a harness and inflatable bladder providing adjustable support. The helmet is then placed over the band as a separate step, allowing the band and bladder to maintain position and comfort without direct mechanical linkage to the helmet.

abstract: A method for drying wood strands and the like is shown and described. In a preferred embodiment, the strands are fed onto a conveyor which then moves the strands as a bed through a dryer housing. The housing may be partitioned into various zones and levels, depending on the desired configuration. A volume of drying air is heated and then passed through the bed of strands to reduce the moisture content of the strands. In a preferred embodiment, the strands are agitated to promote the even exposure of the strands to the drying heat. The strands are then conveyed through a conditioning zone before being discharged from the dryer housing.
problem: Drying wood strands uniformly to reduce moisture content without uneven exposure to heat or airflow.
constraint: The process must balance agitation intensity and airflow distribution to prevent strand damage while achieving uniform drying across variable moisture content and material geometry.
mechanism: Material is conveyed through a segmented chamber with controlled thermal airflow, where mechanical agitation during transport ensures uniform exposure to the drying medium, enabling staged moisture reduction through zoned environmental control.
mechanism_raw: Strands are conveyed through a partitioned dryer housing with heated air passed through the bed. Agitation of the strands during conveyance ensures even exposure to the drying air, while zoned configurations allow staged moisture reduction before conditioning.

abstract: A process for the selective modification and reversible removal of extremely fine structures having dimensions of down to the nanometer and subnanometer range from the surface of a solid, comprises moving the fine tip of a probe, for example a surface-sensitive scanning probe, which is located at a distance in the .ANG.ngstrom range above the surface or is in contact with the surface, over the structure at essentially the same height and thus causing a change in this structure.
problem: Precisely modifying or removing nanoscale structures on a solid surface without damaging surrounding areas.
constraint: The mechanism requires maintaining subnanometer precision in tip positioning and height control to avoid unintended alterations to adjacent structures while achieving the desired modification.
mechanism: A precision probe tip is maintained at a controlled separation distance from a target surface, with coordinated motion enabling localized interaction that selectively modifies surface features while preserving adjacent structures through sub-scale positional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: A scanning probe tip is moved at a controlled distance (angstrom range) over the target structure at a consistent height, inducing localized changes through direct interaction. The probe's proximity and motion enable selective modification at the nanometer scale.
residual_terms: ["precision probe tip", "controlled separation distance", "sub-scale positional accuracy"]

abstract: A method of sorting plastic items by measuring the effect an item has on light directed at a stream of items from a light source, then selectively removing items from the stream based on a comparison of the light measured and the light emitted from the detector is provided. The invention also includes an apparatus for separating plastic items which comprises a light source, a detector for measuring the effect an individual item has on light emitted from the detector, and sortation means for selectively removing items from the stream based on a comparison of the light emitted by the light source and that measured at the detector. A method for separating single plastic bottles from engaged interlocked bottle clusters comprising directing an air jet at an item sufficiently forceful to displace a single bottle to a collection means but insufficiently forceful to displace an interlocked bottle cluster is also provided.
problem: Need to separate individual plastic items from interlocked clusters in a continuous stream without manual intervention.
constraint: The applied force must be precisely calibrated: strong enough to displace a single bottle to collection means but insufficient to displace an interlocked cluster, requiring a narrow operating window between the two thresholds.
mechanism: Applying a stimulus whose effect depends on the target's structural state — a single item is displaced by the stimulus while an interlocked cluster resists displacement due to greater mass and structural integrity, enabling selective separation based on differential mechanical response.
mechanism_raw: Applying a controlled stimulus (air jet) whose effect varies based on the target's structural state — a single bottle is displaced by the jet while an interlocked cluster resists displacement due to its greater mass and structural integrity, enabling selective separation based on differential mechanical response.

abstract: An air conditioning system circulates a mixture of refrigerant fluid and lubricating oil. An accumulator is disposed upstream of a compressor to separate gaseous refrigerant from liquid refrigerant and oil. The accumulator includes an outer case, an inner case, an upstanding pipe, and a baffle plate disposed in the outer case and above the inner case. Gaseous refrigerant exits the accumulator through the pipe. Oil and possibly liquid refrigerant collect in the inner case around the pipe. Liquid refrigerant and possibly oil collect outside of the inner case. Each of the pipe and inner case include vertically spaced oil-return holes.
problem: Need to separate gaseous refrigerant from liquid refrigerant and lubricating oil in a circulating refrigeration system while allowing oil to return to the compressor.
constraint: The vertical spacing of oil-return holes must balance oil return efficiency against maintaining phase separation integrity, preventing liquid carryover while ensuring adequate oil circulation.
mechanism: Using gravity-driven phase separation within a nested chamber geometry — an outer case, inner case, and baffle plate create distinct collection zones where denser liquids and oil settle in different regions, while gaseous refrigerant rises and exits through a central pipe, with vertically spaced holes enabling staged oil return.
mechanism_raw: Using gravity-driven phase separation within a nested chamber geometry — an outer case, inner case, and baffle plate create distinct collection zones where denser liquids and oil settle in different regions, while gaseous refrigerant rises and exits through a central pipe, with vertically spaced holes enabling staged oil return.
residual_terms: ["gravity", "phase separation", "nested chamber geometry", "outer case", "inner case", "baffle plate", "central pipe", "vertically spaced holes"]

abstract: A binding mechanism for holding yarns of circular knitting machines during yarn changeover and when yarns are moved to inactive positions includes an elastomeric member having deformable when engaged with a flat surface and having pliable surfaces for simultaneously receiving and individually gripping multiple yarns, the member being of silicone rubber having a durometer hardness range of 45-70.
problem: Need to hold multiple yarns simultaneously during yarn changeover and when yarns are moved to inactive positions in circular knitting machines without damaging the yarns.
constraint: The durometer hardness (45-70 Shore A) must be within a narrow range: soft enough to conform and grip yarns individually without damage, yet firm enough to maintain gripping force and structural integrity under repeated engagement cycles.
mechanism: Using a compliant elastomeric member that deforms when compressed against a flat surface, where the material's pliability creates multiple individual gripping points along its surface — the deformation distributes contact pressure while the elastomer's resilience provides gripping force to each yarn independently.
mechanism_raw: Using a compliant elastomeric member that deforms when compressed against a flat surface, where the material's pliability creates multiple individual gripping points along its surface — the deformation distributes contact pressure while the elastomer's resilience provides gripping force to each yarn independently.

abstract: A heat exchanger includes a heat exchanger body and at least one bracket attached thereto. The bracket has a resin portion mechanically joined with the heat exchanger body. The bracket can be easily secured to the heat exchanger body by an injected and cured resin forming the resin portion without using mechanical fasteners, such as bolts. Moreover, the bracket and, ultimately, the heat exchanger, can be designed and manufactured to be lightweight.
problem: Need to attach brackets to a heat exchanger body securely without mechanical fasteners (bolts) while achieving a lightweight assembly.
constraint: The resin must cure to sufficient mechanical strength to replace bolted connections while remaining lightweight, requiring a balance between cure shrinkage, bond strength, and thermal expansion compatibility with the heat exchanger body.
mechanism: Using in-situ material transformation — injecting a curable resin that mechanically interlocks with the surface and cures to form a solid structural bond, eliminating the need for separate fasteners by creating the joint through the material's phase change from liquid to solid.
mechanism_raw: Using in-situ material transformation — injecting a curable resin that mechanically interlocks with the heat exchanger body surface and cures to form a solid structural bond, eliminating the need for separate fasteners by creating the joint through the resin's phase change from liquid to solid.

abstract: An improved extrusion process is provided for the production of freezeable breadings which can be applied to frozen food products and which essentially eliminates the problem of "frosty tips", i.e., the tendency of prior extruded breadings to exhibit an unappealing whitish color when breaded products were fried or baked. The process of the invention involves first preparing a moisturized breading mixture containing a major proportion of wheat flour, together with water and active yeast; this mixture is then passed into and through an extruder under moderate conditions of temperature, pressure and shear, followed by shredding and drying of the extrudate to a moisture content of from about 8-12% by weight.
problem: Need to produce freezeable breading that does not develop unappealing whitish discoloration ('frosty tips') when applied to frozen food products and subsequently fried or baked.
constraint: The extrusion conditions must remain moderate (not excessive heat, pressure, or shear) to preserve yeast viability and structural formation, while the final moisture content must be precisely controlled (8-12%) to maintain the anti-frosty-tip structure without compromising freezeability.
mechanism: Using controlled extrusion with active yeast under moderate temperature, pressure, and shear conditions — the yeast creates a specific internal structure during extrusion that prevents the formation of frosty tips, followed by shredding and controlled drying to achieve the target moisture content that preserves this structure.
mechanism_raw: Using controlled extrusion with active yeast under moderate temperature, pressure, and shear conditions — the yeast creates a specific internal structure during extrusion that prevents the formation of frosty tips, followed by shredding and controlled drying to achieve the target moisture content that preserves this structure.

abstract: The sequential forming of a wood product from lumber including the steps of and a system for sawing the lumber into lengths, sawing the lengths into elongate units, applying glue to the units and overlying the units in groups of at least two units to each group with the glue therebetween, stacking the groups, banding the stack of groups to preclude movement between the units in the groups, and drying the banded groups and curing the glue between the units in the individual groups.
problem: Efficiently forming a multi-layered wood product while maintaining structural integrity during curing.
constraint: Balancing mechanical constraint (banding) to prevent movement without damaging the units or inhibiting glue curing.
mechanism: Sequentially dividing raw material into discrete units, assembling them into layered groups with an adhesive, mechanically constraining the assembly to prevent inter-unit displacement during curing, and then curing the adhesive under controlled environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: Sequentially cutting lumber into units, gluing them in grouped layers, mechanically constraining the stack via banding to prevent inter-unit movement, and then drying/curing the glue under controlled conditions.

abstract: An apparatus for producing an edible, hand held food product which may be used as a container for ice cream and other frozen confections in which the apparatus includes, in combination, a baking mold for baking the food product and a vacuum removal plug which is selectively insertable into a female portion of the baked food product for removing the food product by means of vacuum. The removal plug has an exterior surface with a configuration corresponding substantially to the inner surface of the container and includes a plurality of vacuum ports opening to the exterior surface. The apparatus also includes a vacuum assembly for creating a vacuum within the vacuum ports.
problem: Removing a fragile baked food product from a mold without causing structural damage.
constraint: Matching the plug's surface configuration to the product's shape while maintaining sufficient vacuum pressure for adhesion without deformation.
mechanism: Using a vacuum-based extraction element with a surface configuration matching the target object's geometry and distributed vacuum ports to create uniform suction for non-destructive removal.
mechanism_raw: Using a vacuum removal plug with a surface geometry matching the product's interior and distributed vacuum ports to create uniform suction for non-destructive extraction.

abstract: Fireproofing compositions are provided. The compositions comprise a hydratable cementitious binder and polystyrene aggregate falling within particular particle size distribution limits. The compositions can also include an air entraining agent and a fibrous material. On addition of water, the compositions form settable, sprayable slurries which can be pumped to the point of application. The slurries are capable of spray application to steel structural members and adhere to the member in the slurried state and after setting. Excellent fire and heat protection is provided to the member despite the organic nature of the polystyrene aggregate.
problem: Creating a sprayable fireproofing material that adheres to steel surfaces while resisting high temperatures despite containing organic components.
constraint: Balancing sprayability and adhesion (via air entrainment and particle size) with fire resistance despite the organic polystyrene content.
mechanism: Combining a hydratable binding matrix with a lightweight particulate filler of controlled size distribution and an air-entraining agent to enable pumpable mixtures that adhere and cure into thermally stable coatings.
mechanism_raw: Combining a hydratable cementitious binder with polystyrene aggregate of controlled particle size distribution and an air-entraining agent to enable pumpable slurries that adhere and cure into thermally stable coatings.

abstract: A rotary cutter having a handle, a cylindrical head formed on one end of the handle and having a planar surface on each side of the head, an actuating member pivotally mounted in the head, a circular blade mounted on the actuating member and having a pinking or wave shaped cutting edge offset from the blade to form a hub, the blade being secured to one side of the actuating member with the hub located in a parallel relation to one of the planar surfaces, and a finger guard formed as an integral part of the handle and head.
problem: Performing safe, precise cutting with a rotary blade while protecting the user's hand from accidental contact.
constraint: Ensuring the guard does not impede blade access for cutting while providing sufficient coverage to prevent injury.
mechanism: Integrating a protective barrier as a monolithic component of the tool's structural assembly, positioned to block contact with the cutting edge during operation while maintaining access for intended use.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a finger guard as a monolithic part of the handle and head structure, positioned to block contact with the blade's cutting edge during operation.

abstract: A process for the specific, location-selective and time-stable modification of surfaces of solids in the nanometer range without destruction of the atomic order of the surface at the location of the structure or in the vicinity thereof, where a local delamination is caused at the surface of solids having a layered structure due to the action of a local probe. This process is used for the storage of information.
problem: Modifying solid surfaces at the nanoscale with spatial and temporal precision without disrupting surrounding atomic structure.
constraint: Achieving precise delamination at the nanoscale while preserving atomic order in adjacent regions to avoid structural collapse.
mechanism: Using a localized probe to induce controlled delamination at specific surface regions of layered materials, enabling targeted structural changes for information storage while preserving atomic order in adjacent regions.
mechanism_raw: Using a localized probe to induce controlled delamination at specific surface regions of layered materials, enabling targeted structural changes for information storage.

abstract: A flexible wrap is arranged for securement about the side wall portion of a beverage keg, wherein the wrap includes a row of parallel pockets extending from the sides of the beverage keg to accommodate gel packs containing a freezable gel therewithin. The wrap is arranged for securement about the beverage keg, and further employs a lid and floor arranged to overlie the top and bottom walls of an associated beverage keg.
problem: Need to provide uniform thermal management (cooling) around a beverage keg without interfering with its structure or accessibility.
constraint: The wrap must be flexible enough to conform to the keg geometry while maintaining securement, and the pockets must be arranged to accommodate gel packs without interfering with each other or the keg's structural integrity.
mechanism: A flexible enclosure with distributed thermal storage compartments conforms to a curved object's geometry, positioning thermal elements in parallel alignment along the surface. A sealed top and bottom complete a full thermal barrier, ensuring no region of the object remains exposed. The parallel compartment arrangement maintains orientation of thermal elements while preventing mutual interference, and the sealed enclosure ensures uniform thermal regulation across the entire object.
mechanism_raw: A flexible wrap with parallel pockets distributed along the side wall holds gel packs in conformal contact with the curved surface, while a lid and floor overlie the top and bottom walls to complete a full thermal enclosure. The parallel pocket arrangement allows thermal storage elements to be positioned along the cylindrical surface while maintaining their orientation, and the end caps ensure no region is left uncovered, creating uniform temperature control around the entire object.
residual_terms: ["flexible enclosure", "thermal storage compartments", "parallel alignment", "sealed top and bottom"]

abstract: A refuelling equipment (7) may be connected via an adjustable loading valve (30) to three groups of intermediate stores (4, 5, 6) in which natural gas is stored at different storage pressures. The loading valve (30) contains three inlets, each of which is connected via a feedline (13a, 14a or 15a respectively) to one of the intermediate stores (4, 5 or 6 respectively), and one outlet which is connected via an outlet line (24) to the refuelling equipment (7). The loading valve (30) further contains a cyclically adjustable valve body (31) which may be switched respectively from a first blocking position blocking all of the inlets, into a first flow position connecting the supply line (13a) to the outlet line (24), past a second blocking position into a second flow position connecting the supply line (14a) to the outlet line (24) and past a third blocking position into a third flow position connecting the supply line (15a) to the outlet line (24) and finally in the same direction of rotation back into the first blocking position. During each refuelling process the refuelling equipment (7) is accordingly directly connected first to the intermediate store at the lowest storage pressure, then to the intermediate store (5) at the middle storage pressure and finally to the intermediate store (6) at the highest storage pressure.
problem: Need to efficiently transfer gas from multiple storage sources at different pressures to a refueling equipment, optimizing flow rate and pressure matching throughout the process.
constraint: The valve body must cycle through discrete positions in a fixed rotational sequence and must block all inlets during transitions to prevent cross-connection between stores at different pressures.
mechanism: A cyclically positionable flow control element sequentially connects a target system to multiple supply sources in ascending order of stored energy potential. By initiating transfer from the lowest-potential source, the system exploits maximum differential driving force initially, then transitions to higher-potential sources as the target's energy level increases. During transitions, all connections are blocked to prevent cross-contamination between sources at differing potentials.
mechanism_raw: A cyclically adjustable valve body sequentially connects the refueling equipment to intermediate stores in order of increasing storage pressure (lowest first, then middle, then highest). By starting with the lowest-pressure source, the system achieves high initial flow rates due to the large pressure differential, and progressively switches to higher-pressure sources as the target pressure increases, maintaining efficient transfer throughout the entire refueling process.
residual_terms: ["cyclically positionable flow control element", "ascending order of stored energy potential", "differential driving force", "cross-contamination"]

abstract: Trichloroacetic and dichloroacetic acid are dehalogenated to give monochloroacetic acid by electrolyzing aqueous solutions of these acids in divided electrolysis cells using carbon cathodes; the aqueous electrolytic solutions also contain one or more metal salts having a hydrogen overvoltage of at least 0.4 volt (at a current density of at least 4000 A/m.sup.2) and specific ammonium and/or phosphonium salts. In this process, there is an extremely small evolution of hydrogen at the cathode, even at a very low concentration of the polychlorinated acetic acid, without the high selectivity of conversion of the electrolysis being impaired in continuous operation.
problem: Need to dehalogenate polychlorinated acetic acids via electrolysis without excessive hydrogen evolution at the cathode, which would impair reaction selectivity and safety.
constraint: The additives must provide a hydrogen overvoltage of at least 0.4 volt at current densities of at least 4000 A/m², and the process must maintain continuous operation without degrading conversion selectivity.
mechanism: An electrolytic medium incorporates additives that elevate the activation barrier for a competing parasitic reaction while promoting a target electrochemical transformation. The additives establish a kinetic preference by increasing the energy threshold required for the parasitic reaction, thereby shifting reaction selectivity toward the desired pathway. This enables sustained operation at high current densities without degrading conversion efficiency.
mechanism_raw: The electrolytic solution contains metal salts with high hydrogen overvoltage (>0.4V at >4000 A/m²) and specific ammonium/phosphonium salts that kinetically suppress the competing hydrogen evolution reaction at the carbon cathode. This shifts the electrochemical selectivity toward the desired dehalogenation reaction, allowing high conversion efficiency even at low concentrations of the target compound, while minimizing parasitic hydrogen production.

abstract: This invention relates to an improved process of surface sizing of paper and paperboard. The process consists of: PA1 a) Preparing an aqueous surface sizing compound by combining and mixing an aqueous solution of at least one water soluble or dispersible polymer or interpolymer, a solution or dispersion of auxiliary materials, and an aqueous solution of a metal salt, selected from the group of metals consisting of zirconium, hafnium or titanium, to the polymer solution; PA1 b) Adjusting the pH of the aqueous sizing compound from about 5 to about 10.5 by the addition of alkali, thereby increasing the molecular weight of the polymer or interpolymer by chemically or physically reacting the polymer or interpolymer with the salt of zirconium, hafnium or titanium, resulting in an increase in viscosity of the aqueous sizing compound; PA1 c) Applying the aqueous surface sizing compound to the surface of the paper or paperboard by means of a coating device, where the aqueous surface sizing compound is immobilized in the wet state, thereby preventing penetration of the aqueous surface sizing compound into the paper or paperboard; and PA1 d) Drying and curing the aqueous surface sizing compound by applying heat to the treated paper or paperboard thereby crosslinking the polisher or interpolymer contained in the surface sizing compound, and also forming bonds with the pigment particles and fiber present at the surface of the paper or paperboard, and thereby anchoring the polymer or interpolymer to the surface of the paper or paperboard.
problem: Need to apply surface sizing to paper or paperboard without penetration into the substrate, while achieving strong surface anchoring of the polymer.
constraint: The pH must be adjusted within the range of about 5 to about 10.5 to trigger the polymer-metal reaction, and the compound must be immobilized during application to prevent penetration into the paper or paperboard.
mechanism: A surface treatment composition undergoes a pH-triggered in-situ polymerization reaction that increases viscosity and molecular weight. The composition is applied in a constrained state to prevent substrate penetration. Subsequent energy input induces crosslinking and bonding between the polymerized material and surface features, creating permanent surface anchoring without altering substrate integrity.
mechanism_raw: The pH of the sizing compound is adjusted (5–10.5) to trigger in-situ reaction between the polymer and a metal salt (Zr, Hf, or Ti), increasing molecular weight and viscosity. The compound is applied while immobilized in the wet state to prevent penetration into the paper. Subsequent thermal curing crosslinks the polymer and forms bonds with pigment particles and fibers at the surface, permanently anchoring the polymer to the substrate.

abstract: A dental brush comprises two intertwisted wire sections between which fibers for cleaning the teeth and tooth gaps are arrested by the twisting. To achieve an increased retaining force acting on the fibers, it is provided in such a dental brush that at least one of the wire sections has a fin extending in the longitudinal direction.
problem: Need to increase the retaining force on cleaning fibers in a twisted-wire dental brush so that fibers do not slip out or become dislodged during use.
constraint: The fin must extend in the longitudinal direction on at least one wire section, and the fibers must be arrested by the twisting of the two wire sections together to achieve the increased retention.
mechanism: A helical wire assembly incorporates a protruding structural feature on at least one wire strand that extends along its length. When the strands are twisted together, the protrusion increases contact area between the wire and entrapped filaments, creating enhanced mechanical interlock through friction and geometric constraint. This prevents filament displacement under operational loads.
mechanism_raw: At least one of the two intertwisted wire sections includes a longitudinal fin that extends along the wire's length. When the wires are twisted together, the fin increases the contact surface area between the wire and the trapped fibers, creating a higher mechanical interlock and friction force that resists fiber pull-out under load.
residual_terms: ["helical wire assembly", "protruding structural feature", "mechanical interlock", "geometric constraint"]

abstract: A method for refinishing vehicle wheels includes removing the wheels with the tires thereon from the vehicle. The locations of the wheel weights are then marked on the tire and the weights are removed. The wheel and tire are then placed in a blast cabinet and the existing coatings on a face surface of the wheel are removed using a plastic blast media. Thereafter corrosion of the metal of the face surface is removed by blasting with rigid glass blast media. The tire is removed from the cabinet and any excess media is removed with an air blast. The tire is masked to prevent overspray. Thereafter the wheel is coated with one or more layers of coating. The coated wheel is then heated to facilitate curing, and the wheel weights are reinstailed prior to the coating being fully cured. The method of the present invention is particularly well-adapted for performance in a mobile service vehicle that can travel to the vehicle whose wheels are to be refinished.
problem: Efficiently removing multiple surface layers (coatings and corrosion) from a substrate without damaging adjacent materials (e.g., tires) in a mobile service environment.
constraint: Balancing media selection and process timing to avoid damage to non-target materials (e.g., tires) while ensuring complete removal of all layers within the constraints of a mobile service setup.
mechanism: Sequential application of distinct processing agents, each optimized to remove a specific surface layer, enabling selective removal without affecting adjacent materials through targeted interaction with each layer's properties.
mechanism_raw: Sequential application of different blast media types, where each media is optimized to target a specific layer (e.g., plastic media for coatings, rigid glass media for corrosion), allowing selective removal without damaging underlying or adjacent components.

abstract: A mechanism for rapping the electrodes of an electrostatic precipitator for the purpose of dislodging dust deposited on the electrodes is disclosed. The rapping mechanism incorporates a pair of impact beams (1, 1') between which collecting electrodes are suspended. The impact beams are so arranged that the beams slide on the upward-facing edges of a pair of support carriers (2, 2') secured to the precipitator housing. A drop hammer (7) rotatable about a horizontal shaft raps an anvil (6) secured to the impact beam pair (1, 1'), thereby causing a horizontal vibration of the impact beam pair (1, 1') without imparting any impact energy to the precipitator housing. A pair of springs (12) secured to the precipitator housing, one at each end of the impact beam pair, act against the horizontal movement of the impact beam pair and restore the impact beam pair to its original position.
problem: Dislodging particulate deposits from electrodes in an electrostatic precipitator without transferring impact energy to the precipitator housing.
constraint: Achieving sufficient vibration amplitude to dislodge deposits while preventing mechanical energy transfer to the precipitator housing structure.
mechanism: A mechanical system that generates localized vibration through impact-driven motion and spring-based restoration, isolating energy transfer to the surrounding structure by confining vibrational energy to a target zone.
mechanism_raw: A sliding beam system suspended on support carriers, where a drop hammer impacts an anvil attached to the beams to generate horizontal vibration. Springs restore the beams to their original position, isolating vibration energy from the housing.

abstract: A gauge block assembly for use in conjunction with the refilling of high pressure gaseous oxygen cylinders. The gauge block is used in an oxygen transfill header or manifold and includes a gas transfer control unit that allows rapid evacuation of the spent oxygen cylinder but that prevents rapid refilling of the oxygen cylinder with fresh oxygen. The gas transfer control unit includes a valve assembly having a restricted orifice therethrough. During the evacuation process, the check valve opens, bypassing the restricted orifice, to allow rapid evacuation of the oxygen cylinder at a first rate of flow. During the refilling process, the check valve closes. The incoming oxygen must flow through the restricted orifice at a second rate of flow less than the first rate of flow thereby regulating the flow of oxygen.
problem: Controlling fluid flow rates asymmetrically during bidirectional processes (e.g., rapid evacuation and controlled refilling) in a gas transfer system.
constraint: Maintaining distinct flow rates in each direction without requiring active control systems, relying solely on passive valve mechanics.
mechanism: A directional flow control assembly that permits unrestricted flow in one direction via a bypass mechanism and enforces regulated flow in the opposite direction through a passive restriction, achieving asymmetric flow rates without active control.
mechanism_raw: A valve assembly with a check valve and restricted orifice: the check valve bypasses the orifice during evacuation for high flow, and closes during refilling to force flow through the orifice for regulated low flow.

abstract: A process for the production of surface-active alkyl glycosides which is carried out by the transacetalization method with butanol, leads to a new alkyl glycoside as end product which is characterized by high color-stability in alkaline medium; besides a high proportion of alkyl monoglycoside, the product also contains polyglycoside on polyglycose and butyl glucoside.
reason: The mechanism is a specific chemical synthesis process (transacetalization with butanol) tailored to produce a particular alkyl glycoside composition. The underlying principle is not generalizable beyond similar chemical reactions.

abstract: A method of control of the supply of lubricating oil to a two stroke cycle internal combustion engine comprising supplying fuel to a fuel injector from a fuel reservoir having a fuel capacity greater than the maximum fuel requirement of the engine per cycle. The fuel in the reservoir being maintained at a substantially steady pressure. Delivering oil to the engine by a positive displacement pump having a delivery capacity per pump cycle greater than the maximum oil requirement of the engine per cycle. The oil pump being activated in response to the consumption of fuel from the fuel reservoir to maintain a substantially uniform predetermined ratio between the fuel consumption rate and the oil delivery rate.
problem: Maintaining a uniform fuel-to-oil ratio in a two-stroke engine despite variable fuel consumption rates.
constraint: Decoupling supply capacity from instantaneous demand to enable stable ratio control while avoiding over- or under-delivery during transient engine operation.
mechanism: A ratio maintenance system that decouples supply capacity from instantaneous demand using oversized reservoirs and a feedback loop, ensuring proportional delivery of two substances regardless of transient operational conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using oversized fuel and oil reservoirs/pumps (capacity exceeding per-cycle demand) and linking oil delivery to fuel consumption via a feedback control system, ensuring proportional delivery regardless of engine load.

abstract: A process for obtaining bimaterial parts by casting an aluminum alloy onto an insert coated with a metal film. In this process, the oxide layer is removed from the insert by treatment under vacuum, and then the insert is coated with a titanium based film by physical vapor deposition, and the insert is placed in a mold which is filled with a casting alloy.
problem: Achieving strong adhesion between an aluminum alloy casting and a metal insert in a bimetallic part, while preventing oxide interference during bonding.
constraint: Vacuum environment is required to prevent re-oxidation during coating, limiting the process to controlled atmospheric conditions.
mechanism: Sequentially preparing a surface in a controlled atmosphere to remove contaminants and prevent re-oxidation, followed by depositing a reactive coating layer to enable subsequent material bonding.
mechanism_raw: Sequential surface preparation under vacuum (oxide removal) followed by controlled physical vapor deposition of a titanium-based film, ensuring a clean, reactive surface for subsequent casting alloy bonding.
