abstract: This invention relates to a novel horizontal fluid bed reactor, which in a single unit, provides for the polymerization of monomer to polymer and mixed monomers to co-polymers. Within one reactor shell the reactor contains a plurality of polymerization stages which permit the achievement of narrow residence time distribution of the produced polymer. This arrangement also creates a sufficiently tight subdivision of the reactor volume which permits a plurality of gas circulation stages of different gas compositions, as well as, polymerization temperatures.
problem: Achieving narrow residence time distribution and precise control over polymerization conditions (gas composition, temperature) in a single reactor unit.
constraint: Balancing the number of subdivisions to maintain tight process control without sacrificing throughput or structural integrity of the reactor.
mechanism: Partitioning a processing volume into multiple sequential stages with independently adjustable environmental parameters, enabling staged control of reaction conditions within a single containment structure.
mechanism_raw: Subdividing the reactor volume into multiple sequential polymerization stages with independently controlled gas compositions and temperatures, enabling staged processing within a single shell.

abstract: A method and apparatus in a selective call receiver allow a user to receive maildrop message without losing access to previously received but unread maildrop messages in the same message slot. The selective call receiver comprises an address correlator (107) which determines whether received selective call signals comprise an individual or maildrop address assigned to the selective call receiver. A message memory (122) comprises an individual message portion (126) having an individual memory directory (127) and a maildrop message portion (128) having a maildrop memory directory (129). A processor (112) determines whether the decoded selective call message is an individual message or a maildrop message (204), determines whether a previously received maildrop message stored in the maildrop portion of the memory and having a maildrop address equivalent to the maildrop address of the decoded selective call message is "read" or "unread" (216), and provides identification information corresponding to the previously received one of the maildrop messages from the maildrop memory directory means to the individual memory directory means (222) if the previously received one of the maildrop messages is "unread".
problem: Allowing a user to receive new maildrop messages without losing access to previously received but unread maildrop messages in the same message slot.
constraint: Memory allocation must balance directory size and processing overhead to avoid performance degradation during message management.
mechanism: Separating data storage into distinct directories for individual and shared access, and dynamically migrating identification metadata of unread shared entries to the individual directory to maintain accessibility during updates.
mechanism_raw: Separating message storage into individual and maildrop memory directories, and dynamically relocating identification information of unread maildrop messages to the individual directory to preserve accessibility.

abstract: A barge cover is wound on a roller, mounted on a trolley which may be moved from one end to the other end of a barge hold, deploying or taking up the cover as it moves. The cover may then be sealed around the barge coaming in a weather proof manner. The roller is mounted on trolleys so that two men may deploy or take up the cover with only their muscle power, without requiring either special docking facilities or an independent power source.
problem: Deploying or retracting a barge cover over a hold without requiring specialized docking facilities or external power sources.
constraint: Trolley mobility must be sufficient to cover the entire hold length while maintaining structural stability under load.
mechanism: Mounting a rolling element on a manually guided mobile support system that traverses a linear path, enabling human-powered actuation of a cover mechanism along the entire length of a containment area.
mechanism_raw: Mounting a roller on a manually movable trolley system that traverses the length of the barge hold, enabling muscle-powered deployment or retraction of the cover as the trolley moves.

abstract: An article and method for marking elastomeric articles, such as tires, floor mats, and the like, includes an elastomeric sheet which is marked with indicia using a solvent based ink which contrasts with the elastomeric sheet. The indicia is cured with a clear thermoset layer such as a polyurethane. This is then applied to an uncured elastomeric article and the elastomeric article is cured. The heat and the pressure of curing causes the elastomeric sheet to bond to the elastomeric article. The indicia remains discernible and is not easily marred or dulled. After curing, the transfer can be further marked by heat transferring indicia in the form of a sublimation dye through the clear polyurethane layer.
problem: Permanently marking elastomeric articles (e.g., tires) with durable, visible indicia that resist wear and degradation during curing.
constraint: Thermal and pressure conditions during curing must be precisely controlled to ensure ink visibility and adhesion without damaging the thermoset layer.
mechanism: Transferring a pre-marked elastomeric layer with cured indicia onto an uncured article, then bonding the layer to the article via simultaneous application of heat and pressure during the article's curing process.
mechanism_raw: Transferring a pre-marked elastomeric sheet (with solvent-based ink cured under a thermoset layer) onto an uncured article, then bonding it via heat and pressure during the article's curing process.

abstract: A pin locking device for preventing an involuntary unlocking of a pin which is bent back on itself to form a spring, the pin having a pointed end section and a clasp mechanism mutually adjacent each other, the clasp mechanism retaining the pointed end section in a clasped condition against the urging of the spring. The pin locking device includes an elongated lock member having a body of a finite length made of a non-compressible material and having first and second spaced and parallel holes extending transversely through the body. An axially outwardly opening slot is provided in one end face of the lock member and extends entirely across the end face parallel to and opens into the first one of the transversely extending holes. The pointed end section of the pin extends through the second hole. The first hole receives therein a part of the pin extending between the clasp mechanism and the spring through the axially outwardly opening slot to thereby prevent the pointed end section of the pin from being able to move toward the aforesaid part of the pin between the clasp mechanism and the spring in order to effect an unclasping of the pointed end section from the clasp member.
problem: Preventing involuntary unlocking of a spring-loaded pin that is bent back on itself to form a clasp mechanism.
constraint: The lock member must be made of a non-compressible material to maintain structural integrity under spring force, and the geometry of the holes and slot must precisely align with the pin's components to allow assembly while blocking unintended movement.
mechanism: A rigid constraint element with aligned openings physically blocks relative motion between a spring-biased component and a clasp structure, preventing unintended disengagement by mechanically restricting movement along a critical axis.
mechanism_raw: A non-compressible lock member with transversely extending holes and an axially opening slot physically blocks the pin's pointed end from moving toward the spring-clasp region, mechanically preventing unclasping by constraining relative motion between the pin and the lock member.

abstract: A helmet has attached to its lower rim an inflatable bag which normally is folded so as not to restrict normal head and neck movements of the wearer but on inflation will fill the gap between the helmet rim and shoulders of a wearer. Carried by the helmet and preferably packed with the bag is a package including a conventional gas generator, igniter and battery. A switch to operate the igniter is located on the crown area of the exterior surface of the helmet and is closable on an impact with a predetermined force on the crown of the helmet. When closed the bag is almost instantaneously inflated and fills the gap to transfer most if not all of the impact force to the shoulders and relieve the cervical spine of a damaging axial compressive force. In another version, shoulder pads are provided in which there is an attachment in the form of an inflatable bag on the inner rim encircling the neck of the wearer. The inflatable bag inflates upon the impact upon the crown area of the exterior surface of the helmet to extend inwards, just enough to instantaneously broaden the foundation on which the helmet attachment can rest when deployed upon impact without harming the wearer's neck.
problem: Protecting the cervical spine from damaging axial compressive forces during impact to the crown of a helmet.
constraint: The bag must remain compact and non-restrictive during normal use while being capable of near-instantaneous inflation to a sufficient volume to bridge the gap, requiring precise triggering force thresholds and gas generator response times.
mechanism: A rapidly deployable cushioning element, normally compacted to avoid interference, expands upon impact-triggered activation to fill a spatial gap between a protective shell and a body region, redirecting forces away from a vulnerable anatomical structure.
mechanism_raw: An inflatable bag, normally folded to avoid restricting movement, rapidly deploys upon impact-triggered gas generation to fill the gap between the helmet rim and the wearer's shoulders, redirecting impact forces away from the spine and transferring them to the shoulders.

abstract: A clothes dryer designed to rest over the register of a floor duct delivering hot air from a forced hot air heating system. The dryer is a vertical hollow column, closed at the top and open at the bottom, to which are attached one or more foldable drying racks on which the clothes are hung for drying. Openings in the column at specified levels are fitted with baffles which direct the hot air toward the clothes. A flat base stabilizes the unit so it can remain in vertical orientation. A second embodiment has a housing beneath the base dimensioned to fit within the hot air duct when the register is removed. The drying racks can be easily folded down for storage.
problem: Efficiently drying clothes using hot air from an existing forced-air heating system without requiring a separate heat source.
constraint: The column must be dimensioned to fit over the duct register while maintaining structural stability, and the baffles must be positioned to optimize airflow distribution across the racks without impeding the natural convection of hot air.
mechanism: A vertical airflow-directing structure with internal baffles channels forced hot air through strategically placed openings, ensuring distributed contact with suspended articles while maintaining structural stability in a vertical orientation.
mechanism_raw: A vertical hollow column with baffles directs hot air from the duct upward through openings at specified levels, ensuring airflow contacts clothes on foldable racks while a flat base stabilizes the unit for vertical orientation.

abstract: A rail guard for monitoring the limits of transverse inclination and extension between the rails of a railroad track and transmitting an indication when these limits are breached. The rail guard has a plurality of tension switches, each switch being coupled between the outer edge of a railroad track and a penetrable surface near the railroad track. The tension switches are coupled in series and in turn are coupled to a relay. The relay controls a warning signal when one or more of the switches is in an open position.
problem: Monitoring transverse inclination and extension limits between railroad rails and transmitting an indication when these limits are breached.
constraint: The switches must be arranged in series so that any single breach interrupts the circuit, and the penetrable surface must allow sufficient movement to detect over-extension while remaining durable enough to avoid false triggers under normal rail vibrations.
mechanism: A series of displacement sensors coupled between adjacent structural elements detect movement beyond predefined thresholds; when any sensor triggers, a series circuit breaks, activating a warning system to indicate limit breach.
mechanism_raw: A series of tension switches coupled between the rail edges and a penetrable surface detect displacement beyond thresholds; when any switch opens, the series circuit breaks, triggering a relay to activate a warning signal.

abstract: A method for controlling the gas recycle loop of an ozone bleaching process wherein an ozone generator produces an ozone containing gas from an oxygen containing feed gas and delivers the ozone containing gas to an ozone reactor at a variable flow rate responsive to reactor ozone demand. Pulp is bleached with the ozone containing gas, thereby producing an exhaust gas having a flow rate that varies in response to the flow rate of the ozone containing gas delivered to the ozone reactor. The exhaust gas is then recovered and its flow rate is modified within the recycle loop so that an amount equivalent to reactor ozone demand is returned to the ozone generators. The oxygen content of the oxygen containing feed gas is monitored at or near the inlet of the ozone generator and an amount of fresh oxygen is supplied to the oxygen containing feed gas to obtain a predetermined level of oxygen therein. Additionally, an amount of exhaust gas may be purged at a rate substantially equivalent to the rate fresh oxygen is supplied. However, the pressure at the ozone generator is also monitored and the purge rate is adjusted in order to maintain constant pressure at the ozone generator.
problem: Controlling the gas recycle loop of an ozone bleaching process to match reactor ozone demand while maintaining constant pressure at the ozone generator.
constraint: The system must balance three interdependent variables—ozone demand, oxygen concentration, and generator pressure—requiring real-time adjustments to purge rates and fresh oxygen supply without destabilizing the ozone generation process.
mechanism: A multi-variable feedback control system dynamically adjusts exhaust flow rates, fresh gas supply, and purge parameters based on real-time measurements of demand, composition, and pressure to maintain equilibrium across interdependent process variables.
mechanism_raw: A feedback system adjusts the exhaust gas flow rate in the recycle loop to match ozone demand, monitors oxygen content at the generator inlet to supply fresh oxygen, and modulates purge rates based on pressure measurements to maintain constant generator pressure.

abstract: Printing is conducted at the transparent conducting film unnecessary portion on a substrate 1 with a masking ink having a higher thermal decomposition temperature than that of the transparent conducting film forming composition, and the ink is dried and cured by heat or light to form a masking pattern 2. The portion where a transparent conducting film is to be formed is preferably subjected to ozone cleaning and then coated with a transparent conducting film forming composition comprising an indium compound and/or a tin compound and a solvent to form a transparent conducting film forming composition layer 3. The thus worked substrate is subjected to a heat treatment, causing thermal decomposition of the masking pattern 2 after formation of a transparent conducting film. Then the residues of the masking ink and the transparent conducting film are removed to finally obtain a desired patterned transparent conducting film 4.
problem: Creating a patterned transparent conducting film without damaging the desired conductive regions during masking and removal steps.
constraint: The thermal decomposition temperature differential between the masking ink and the conductive film must be sufficient to enable selective removal without degrading the conductive layer.
mechanism: Using a masking material with a higher thermal decomposition temperature than the conductive layer, enabling selective removal of the mask via thermal decomposition while preserving the conductive layer in unmasked regions through temperature differential-based selectivity.
mechanism_raw: Using a masking material with a higher thermal decomposition temperature than the conductive film composition, allowing selective removal of the mask after thermal decomposition, while preserving the conductive layer in unmasked regions.

abstract: A multilayer plastic pipe having improved barrier action against diffusion of the substance being transported, particularly methanol-containing fuels, dimensional stability, resistance to mechanical stress, and particularly improved adhesion between layers is provided comprising: PA1 (A) an inner layer and an outer layer, each of which comprise a polyamide-based molding composition, wherein the inner layer and outer layer may be the same or different, and (B) at least one intermediate layer comprising PA2 a) 95 to 60% by weight of a linear, crystalline polyester and PA2 b) 5 to 40% by weight of a polymer containing reactive groups other than epoxide groups, wherein the reactive groups are contained in a concentration of from 4 to 95 mmol/kg based on the total amount of component (B); and wherein the layers are intimately bonded to one another.
problem: Achieving strong adhesion between dissimilar polymer layers in a multilayer pipe while maintaining barrier properties against substance diffusion.
constraint: The concentration of reactive groups must balance sufficient bonding strength with maintaining the barrier properties of the intermediate layer.
mechanism: Introducing an intermediate layer containing reactive groups that chemically bond with adjacent polymer layers, creating interlayer adhesion through controlled reactive group interactions that balance bonding strength with barrier integrity.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a polymer with reactive groups in an intermediate layer to chemically bond with adjacent polyamide-based layers, creating intimate interlayer adhesion through reactive group interactions.

abstract: A lightweight block useful as a patio tile, a border piece or a landscaping component, which has a density of 800 to 1,200 kg/m.sup.3 and is made from a concrete mix comprising stabilized wood aggregates prepared by sterilization of wood chips by thermal treatment, followed by a chemical treatment with a calcium salt first and then with at least one soluble silicate, the concrete mix also comprising, based on 750 liters of the stabilized wood aggregates: from 200 to 350 kg of sand; from 200 to 350 kg of cement, such as silica fume or Portland cement; from 8 to 15 kg of polymer additive, preferably a melamine-based polymer; from 80 to 175 kg of water; and optionally, at least one pigment such as iron oxide. This block is particularly interesting in that it is lightweight, it has a high bending resistance; it has a pronounced and decorative texture; and it is very porous, thereby making it self-draining and efficient as a sound absorber.
problem: Producing a lightweight, structurally sound, and porous concrete-like material with self-draining and sound-absorbing properties.
constraint: The ratio of wood aggregates, cement, polymer additive, and water must balance density, mechanical strength, and porosity for optimal performance.
mechanism: Combining treated porous aggregates with a polymer additive to form a composite structure that balances structural integrity, low density, and porosity through synergistic reinforcement and controlled void distribution.
mechanism_raw: Using sterilized and chemically treated wood aggregates to provide structural integrity and porosity, combined with a polymer additive to enhance bending resistance while maintaining low density.

abstract: A storage and retrieval machine comprising a base adapted to move horizontally along a supporting surface, a generally vertical mast supported by the base, a carriage supported for generally vertical movement along the mast, and an extendable and retractable shuttle mechanism supported by the carriage, the shuttle mechanism including an upper plate fixed against horizontal movement relative to the carriage, an intermediate plate which is located below the upper plate and which is supported by the upper plate for horizontal movement relative thereto, a lower plate which is located below the intermediate plate and which is supported by the intermediate plate for horizontal movement relative thereto, and hoops on the lower plate for selectively engaging a load, the shuttle mechanism being operable between a retracted condition wherein the intermediate plate is located directly below the upper plate and the lower plate is located directly below the intermediate plate, and an extended condition wherein the intermediate plate extends outwardly in one direction relative to the upper plate and the lower plate extends outwardly in the one direction relative to the intermediate plate.
problem: Efficiently extending a load-handling mechanism into confined storage spaces while maintaining stability and precision.
constraint: The mechanical coordination between the plates must ensure synchronized movement without jamming, while maintaining load stability during extension and retraction.
mechanism: Implementing staged extension of nested components that move sequentially relative to one another, enabling incremental outward displacement to access confined spaces while maintaining synchronized movement and load stability.
mechanism_raw: Staged extension of nested plates (upper, intermediate, lower) that move sequentially relative to one another, allowing incremental outward movement to reach deep storage positions.

abstract: An interchangeable clasp is formed from a body having at least one recess, a connector configured to fit within this recess and a member for retaining the connector within the recess. This clasp is aesthetically appealing to the viewer and may be used in numerous applications. Through the use of this interchangeable clasp, jewelry variations can be geometrically multiplied, while reducing the cost to the consumer.
problem: Creating a versatile, aesthetically appealing connection system that allows rapid interchange of components while maintaining secure attachment.
constraint: The connector and retaining member must balance ease of interchange with sufficient retention force to prevent unintended disconnection under normal use.
mechanism: Designing a modular clasp system with a recess, connector, and retaining member that enables tool-free mechanical interlocking between components through controlled engagement and disengagement forces.
mechanism_raw: A modular clasp design with a recess, connector, and retaining member that enables tool-free coupling and decoupling of components through mechanical interlocking.

abstract: A paper tail ripper having a pair of rotatably mounted knives, air motors which counter-rotate the knives and a deflector which deflects the paper tail toward the knives. The knives traverse closely spaced overlapping circles as they counter-rotate. The deflector sweeps the paper tail onto a transfer mechanism, which transfers the paper tail away from the ripper, so that the tail may be threaded through a calender stack, etc. The ripper is pivotally mounted on the transfer mechanism for movement between storage and operating positions.
problem: Efficiently separating and transferring a flexible material (paper tail) from a processing station without disrupting downstream operations (e.g., threading through a calender stack).
constraint: The overlapping knife paths and synchronized deflector motion must balance cutting speed with material integrity, while the pivot mounting must enable reliable positioning without mechanical interference.
mechanism: Two cutting elements with overlapping trajectories traverse paths to sever the material, while a sweeping element redirects the separated portion onto a downstream transfer path. A pivot-mounted assembly enables repositioning between storage and operational configurations to maintain alignment and prevent mechanical interference during material handling.
mechanism_raw: Counter-rotating knives traverse overlapping circular paths to cut the material, while a deflector sweeps the separated tail onto a transfer mechanism. The pivotally mounted system allows movement between storage and operating positions, ensuring precise alignment and controlled material handling.

abstract: A bicycle comprises a wheel-supporting frame member, a swing arm mounted on the frame member to pivot about a pivot axis, and a wheel mounted on the pivot arm for rotation about a rotation axis spaced apart from, to the rear of and substantially below the pivot axis. The pivot axis is located relative to the rotation axis such that upward vertical displacements of the rotation axis relative to the pivot axis upon rotation of the swing arm from a neutral position are accompanied by substantial rearward horizontal displacements of the rotation axis relative to the pivot axis. In the case of a rear wheel suspension, the drive chain passes over an idler sheave, which is mounted for rotation on the rear wheel support member generally below the pivot axis with its circumferential support surface for the chain located such that a tangent to it is proximate to the pivot axis.
problem: Managing vertical and horizontal displacements of a wheel in a suspension system to optimize ride quality and mechanical stability while maintaining drive chain tension.
constraint: The geometric relationship between the pivot and rotation axes must ensure desired suspension kinematics, while the idler sheave placement must avoid disrupting chain dynamics during wheel movement.
mechanism: A pivoting linkage connects the wheel's rotation axis to a pivot axis such that vertical displacement of the wheel produces a controlled horizontal displacement. A tension-maintaining element, positioned relative to the pivot axis, preserves chain tension by aligning its force application near the pivot axis during wheel movement.
mechanism_raw: A swing arm pivots about an axis positioned relative to the wheel's rotation axis such that upward vertical displacement of the wheel induces rearward horizontal displacement. An idler sheave, positioned below the pivot axis, maintains chain tension by aligning its tangent near the pivot axis.

abstract: A method of applying a Cr-bearing layer to a substrate, comprises introducing an organometallic compound, in vapor or solid powder form entrained in a carrier gas to a plasma of an inductively coupled plasma torch or device to thermally decompose the organometallic compound and contacting the plasma and the substrate to be coated so as to deposit the Cr-bearing layer on the substrate. A metallic Cr, Cr alloy or Cr compound such as chromium oxide, nitride and carbide can be provided on the substrate. Typically, the organometallic compound is introduced to an inductively coupled plasma torch that is disposed in ambient air so to thermally decompose the organometallic compound in the plasma. The plasma is directed at the substrate to deposit the Cr-bearing layer or coating on the substrate.
problem: Depositing a chromium-bearing layer on a substrate with controlled composition and minimal environmental constraints.
constraint: The plasma must decompose the organometallic compound efficiently without requiring inert gas environments, while maintaining substrate temperature and coating uniformity.
mechanism: A precursor compound is carried in a gas stream and introduced into a high-energy excitation field where thermal decomposition occurs. The excitation field is directed at the substrate to deposit the target layer, utilizing atmospheric compatibility of the excitation generation process.
mechanism_raw: An organometallic compound is entrained in a carrier gas and introduced into an inductively coupled plasma, where thermal decomposition occurs. The plasma is directed at the substrate to deposit the Cr layer, leveraging ambient air compatibility for the plasma generation.

abstract: A method for converting attapulgite clay which has never been heat treated sufficiently to destroy the natural colloidal properties of the clay to attrition resistant, low surface area, essentially catalytically inert particles adapted for use as a blending agent with particles of active zeolitic cracking catalyst. The clay, preferably mixed with an alkaline cementitious material (such as, for example, portland cement or sodium silicate) is sintered at a temperature above 1350.degree. F., preferably in the range of 1500.degree. F. to 1800.degree. F., to reduce surface area to a value below about 15 m.sup.2 /g, preferably below 5 m.sup.2 /g, and decrease apparent bulk density to a value below 1.1. The material is sized to form an essentially dustless, free flowing powder.
problem: Converting naturally colloidal clay into attrition-resistant, catalytically inert particles suitable for blending with active catalysts without generating dust.
constraint: The sintering temperature must balance surface area reduction and structural integrity, while the binder choice must ensure compatibility with downstream catalyst blending.
mechanism: A naturally colloidal material is subjected to thermal treatment in the presence of a binding agent to reduce surface area and bulk density, destroying colloidal characteristics and stabilizing the structure. Subsequent sizing forms a free-flowing particulate product resistant to attrition and dust generation.
mechanism_raw: The clay is sintered at high temperatures (1500–1800°F) with an alkaline binder to reduce surface area and bulk density, then sized to form a free-flowing powder. The thermal treatment destroys colloidal properties and stabilizes the material structure.

abstract: In an electronic article surveillance (EAS) system, a frequency-dividing transponder that responds to detection of electromagnetic radiation of a first predetermined frequency by transmitting electromagnetic radiation of a second predetermined frequency that is a frequency-divided quotient of the first predetermined frequency, includes an active strip of amorphous magnetic material having a transverse uniaxial anisotropy defining a magnetomechanical resonant frequency in accordance with the dimensions of the strip at the second predetermined frequency when magnetically biased to be within a predetermined magnetic field intensity range so as to respond to excitation by electromagnetic radiation of the first predetermined frequency by transmitting electromagnetic radiation of the second predetermined frequency; and a tripole strip of magnetic material of such coercivity and so disposed in relation to the active strip of magnetic material as to create a magnetomechanical resonance in the active strip at the first predetermined frequency when the active strip is magnetically biased to be within the predetermined magnetic field intensity range. The transponder may also include a bipolar bias strip of such coercivity and so disposed in relation to the active strip as to cause the active strip to be within the predetermined magnetic field intensity range at which the active strip has magnetomechanical resonance at the first and second predetermined frequencies.
problem: Creating a frequency-dividing transponder that reliably responds to a specific excitation frequency by transmitting a divided frequency, while maintaining magnetic stability.
constraint: The magnetic strips' coercivity and spatial arrangement must precisely control resonance conditions without cross-interference, while the bias strip must maintain field stability across temperature and environmental variations.
mechanism: A magnetically anisotropic element with transverse anisotropy resonates at a divided frequency when biased within a specific field range. A secondary magnetic element induces resonance at the original frequency, while a bias element maintains the active element within the required magnetic field range for dual-frequency operation.
mechanism_raw: An active magnetic strip with transverse anisotropy resonates at the divided frequency when biased within a specific field range. A tripole strip induces resonance at the original frequency, and a bipolar bias strip ensures the active strip remains within the required magnetic field range for dual-frequency operation.
residual_terms: ["magnetically anisotropic element", "transverse anisotropy", "divided frequency", "secondary magnetic element", "bias element", "magnetic field range"]

abstract: Landfill waste is transferred to a controlled composting plant where it is aerated, moistened and mixed to enhance and accelerate the composting of the landfill which is then returned to the landfill. When the existing landfill is unlined the returned composted landfill material is placed on a liner which is progressively expanded as the composting process is continued.
problem: Managing landfill waste in an environmentally safe manner, particularly when the landfill is unlined, to prevent contamination while reducing waste volume.
constraint: The liner must be expanded progressively to match the rate of composting, balancing containment integrity with the need to avoid overfilling or structural failure.
mechanism: Progressive containment during decomposition: introducing aeration, moisture, and mechanical agitation to accelerate organic waste breakdown, then depositing the processed material onto a flexible barrier that is incrementally expanded in synchronization with the decomposition rate. This maintains containment integrity by dynamically adjusting the barrier's capacity to match the volume of processed material, eliminating the need for pre-existing infrastructure.
mechanism_raw: Progressive containment during composting: aerating, moistening, and mixing landfill waste to accelerate decomposition, then returning the composted material onto a liner that is expanded incrementally as the composting process continues. This allows the liner to grow in tandem with the processed material, maintaining containment without requiring pre-existing infrastructure.

abstract: Non-woven fabrics and methods and apparatus for their manufacture are disclosed. The fabrics have excellent mechanical strength and hand, and have a substantial uniformity of constituent fibers even at low basis weights. The fabric comprises chopped fibers of a synthetic polymeric thermoplastic material, which serve as binder fibers, and chopped fibers of a synthetic polymeric material which need not be a thermoplastic, which serve as bonded fibers. No extraneous binder materials need be present in the fabric. During manufacture, the binder fibers are uniformly dispersed in an aqueous liquid with the bonded fibers. The fibers are wet laid to form a web which is subsequently dried. During drying, the web is physically supported to prevent fracture. Also, during drying, the web is heated sufficiently to cause the binder fibers to bond to the bonded fibers, thereby forming the finished fabric.
problem: Creating non-woven fabrics with high mechanical strength and uniformity at low basis weights without relying on extraneous binder materials.
constraint: The drying process must balance sufficient heat to activate the binder fibers while maintaining physical support to prevent structural failure of the web during solidification.
mechanism: Binder-activated fiber bonding: dispersing thermoplastic binder fibers within a matrix of structural fibers suspended in a liquid medium, forming a web via wet-laying. During solidification, the web is physically supported to prevent structural collapse while heat activates the binder fibers to melt and adhere to adjacent fibers, creating a self-supporting fabric without extraneous adhesives.
mechanism_raw: Using thermoplastic binder fibers dispersed with bonded fibers in an aqueous medium, then wet-laying the mixture into a web. During drying, the web is physically supported to prevent fracture while heat causes the binder fibers to melt and bond to the bonded fibers, forming a self-supporting fabric without additional adhesives.

abstract: A method is described for manufacturing of normal as well as ultra-fine cement on the basis of cement materials, such as cement clinker, gypsum, slag, limestone, pozzolana, flyash etc. in a plant comprising at least a mill (1), a classifying separator (3), a separation cyclone (5) and a dust collector (7). By this method some of the dust-laden conveying gas which is extracted via the cyclone gas outlet duct (11) is diverted to and dedusted in the dust collector (7), and the dust from the dust collector (7) is utilized as the basis for ultra-fine cement, whereas the cyclone material from the material outlet (9) of the cyclone is utilized as normal cement. Hence it is possible to manufacture ultra-fine cement in existing grinding plants in a mechanically simple and operationally inexpensive way, while normal cement is simultaneously manufactured, without having any significant impact on the mill operation.
problem: Manufacturing ultra-fine cement in existing grinding plants without significant mechanical modifications or operational disruption to normal cement production.
constraint: The diversion of gas and dust must not significantly alter the mill's operational parameters, requiring precise control of flow rates and separation efficiency.
mechanism: Stream splitting for dual-product generation: diverting particulate-laden gas from a primary separation unit to a secondary collection device, where the particulates are isolated as a first product. The residual gas and remaining particulates from the primary unit are directed to form a second product, enabling concurrent production of distinct materials using shared upstream processing equipment.
mechanism_raw: Splitting the output streams of a cement grinding plant by diverting dust-laden gas from the cyclone outlet to a dust collector. The collected dust from the dust collector is used as the basis for ultra-fine cement, while the cyclone material is used for normal cement. This allows simultaneous production of two products using existing equipment.

abstract: This invention relates to an apparatus for separating two fluids having different specific gravities. The invention also relates to a method for using the separating apparatus of the present invention. This invention particularly relates to the skimming of molten lithium metal from the surface of a fused salt electrolyte in the electrolytic production of lithium metal from a mixed fused salt.
problem: Separating molten lithium metal from a fused salt electrolyte in high-temperature electrolytic production processes.
constraint: The separation must function reliably in high-temperature, chemically corrosive environments without degrading the separating apparatus or contaminating the product.
mechanism: Density-driven phase separation: exploiting differences in specific gravity between two immiscible fluids in a high-temperature environment to enable passive stratification. A mechanical interface interacts with the stratified layers to selectively remove the desired phase, leveraging gravitational settling without active energy input for separation.
mechanism_raw: Exploiting differences in specific gravity between two fluids (molten lithium and fused salt) to enable passive separation via skimming. The denser molten lithium sinks or floats relative to the electrolyte, allowing mechanical removal of the desired phase.

abstract: A self-adjusting storage rack for holding vertically stationery, envelopes, letters, file folders, cards, photos, magazines and similar flat surface articles. The device comprises of two upright ends mounted on a base of two flat telescopic rods; a third central telescopic rod acts as a guide for a elastic, expandable and continuous multi-coil; each end coil is attached to an upright end so that one upright may be manually pulled out, extending the length of the rack to the full length permitted by the telescopic rods or any length in between. The elastic coil between the two uprights adjust itself accordingly.
problem: Creating a storage rack that can adjust to hold flat-surface articles of varying widths while maintaining structural stability and tension.
constraint: The elastic coil must provide sufficient tension to hold items securely without overextending the telescopic rods or causing structural instability.
mechanism: Adjustable tension via elastic compliance: employing a resilient element constrained within a pair of telescoping guides, with end attachments to opposing structural members. Manual displacement of one member extends the system to a target span, while the resilient element automatically applies restoring force to maintain contact pressure with stored items, balancing tension against structural stability.
mechanism_raw: Using a central elastic multi-coil guided by telescopic rods, with end coils attached to upright ends. Manually pulling one upright extends the rack to the desired length, while the elastic coil automatically adjusts tension to maintain contact with stored items.

abstract: A leg retainer for use with a half of a body of eviscerated poultry having a leg with a hock. The leg retainer comprises a unitary substantially coplanar thin plastic member which includes a first hook portion adapted for attachment to the body and a second hook portion adapted for hooking the leg. A connector joins the first hook to the second hook. The plastic member serves to pull the leg close to the body.
problem: Keeping a detached poultry leg positioned close to the eviscerated body during processing, without complex fastening or manual adjustment.
constraint: The member must be thin, coplanar, and made of a flexible plastic so that it can both flex to apply pulling force and remain unitary (no separate springs or hinges), while being strong enough to hold the leg against the body.
mechanism: A single unitary flexible member with two engagement portions joined by a compliant connector. When the first engagement portion is anchored to a target surface, the inherent flexibility and geometry of the connector automatically draws the second engagement portion (and thus the attached object) toward the surface, converting the act of attachment into a pulling action through the member's elastic deformation.
mechanism_raw: A single unitary flexible member with two hook portions joined by a connector. When the first hook is anchored to the body, the inherent flexibility and geometry of the connector automatically draws the second hook (and thus the leg) toward the body, converting the act of attachment into a pulling action through the member's elastic deformation.

abstract: A clip-on wear plate to protect the downwardly facing flat surface of the pedestal opening of a railway truck is provided. The wear plate has a first flat surface in contact with the downwardly facing flat surface of the pedestal and an opposed second surface in contact with the bearing adaptor. The first surface is provided with a relatively high coefficient of friction relative to the second surface to an minimize movement of the wear plate.
problem: Protecting a stationary pedestal surface from wear caused by a moving bearing adaptor, while ensuring the protective plate itself does not shift or become dislodged during operation.
constraint: The friction differential must be large enough to prevent plate migration under vibration and load, yet the low-friction side must still allow the bearing adaptor to move freely without binding or excessive resistance.
mechanism: A selectively anchored protective element with deliberately mismatched friction coefficients on its two opposing surfaces: the surface contacting the stationary part has a high coefficient of friction to grip and resist movement, while the surface contacting the moving part has a lower coefficient of friction to allow sliding. This differential friction selectively anchors the element to the stationary part while permitting relative motion at the dynamic interface.
mechanism_raw: A clip-on plate with deliberately mismatched friction coefficients on its two opposing surfaces: the surface contacting the stationary pedestal has a high coefficient of friction to grip and resist movement, while the surface contacting the moving bearing adaptor has a lower coefficient of friction to allow sliding. This differential friction selectively anchors the plate to the stationary part while permitting relative motion at the dynamic interface.

abstract: A cinch or girth assembly for attaching a saddle to an animal includes a cinch or girth having structure secured thereto for connecting to a saddle. The assembly also includes an elastomeric sheet of non-rub material that is positioned to lie between the animal and the cinch or girth to help reduce abrasive contact between the cinch or girth and the animal. The assembly further includes a protective guard with a wear-resistant sheet made from a different material than that of the elastomeric sheet. Structure is provided for attaching the guard to the elastomeric sheet so that the guard lies away from the animal and extends adjacent a longitudinal length of the cinch or girth. In preferred embodiments, the elastomeric sheet is made of neoprene and the protective guard is made from leather, nylon, or jersey material.
problem: Reducing abrasive wear between a tightened strap (cinch/girth) and an animal's skin, while simultaneously protecting the cushioning material from degradation caused by the strap's movement.
constraint: The guard must be made of a different, more wear-resistant material than the elastomeric sheet, and must be attached in a way that it lies away from the animal (avoiding additional pressure points) while still covering the strap's contact region.
mechanism: A layered protection system where a soft compliant cushioning layer is placed between a moving tensioning element and a biological surface to absorb abrasive contact, and a separate wear-resistant guard is attached to the cushioning layer but positioned to extend alongside the tensioning element away from the biological surface. The guard shields the cushioning layer from direct wear by the tensioning element, while the cushioning layer shields the biological surface from abrasion, creating a cascaded protection scheme with material specialization.
mechanism_raw: A layered system where a soft elastomeric cushioning sheet is placed between the animal and the strap to absorb abrasive contact, and a separate wear-resistant guard is attached to the cushioning sheet but positioned to extend alongside the strap away from the animal. The guard shields the elastomeric sheet from direct wear by the strap, while the elastomeric sheet shields the animal from abrasion, creating a cascaded protection scheme with material specialization.

abstract: Dense superalloy foils are prepared by hot isostatically pressing a mixture of low melting alloy powders and high melting alloy powders at a temperature at least equal to or greater than three-quarters of the melting point of the low melting point alloy powder and below the melting point of the high melting point alloy powder, at a pressure of at least 10 thousand pounds per square inch for about one to five hours.
problem: Densifying a mixture of high-melting-point superalloy powders into a dense foil without melting or degrading the high-melting structural phase.
constraint: The temperature must be high enough to activate the low-melting alloy as an effective binder (≥3/4 of its melting point) but strictly below the melting point of the high-melting alloy to prevent structural collapse or compositional degradation of the primary material.
mechanism: Consolidating a blend of low-melting-point material particles (acting as a transient liquid binder) and high-melting-point material particles under elevated pressure and temperature, where the temperature is maintained at least 3/4 of the low-melting material's melting point but below the high-melting material's melting point. The low-melting material becomes sufficiently mobile to flow and fill voids between the high-melting particles, driving densification, while the high-melting material remains solid and retains its structural integrity. The applied pressure ensures complete pore elimination.
mechanism_raw: Hot isostatic pressing a blend of low-melting-point alloy powders (acting as a transient liquid binder) and high-melting-point alloy powders at a temperature that is at least 3/4 of the low-melting alloy's melting point but below the high-melting alloy's melting point. The low-melting alloy becomes sufficiently mobile to flow and fill voids between the high-melting particles, driving densification, while the high-melting alloy remains solid and retains its structural integrity. The applied pressure (≥10 ksi) for 1–5 hours ensures complete pore elimination.
residual_terms: ["hot isostatic pressing", "transient liquid binder", "melting point", "densification", "pore elimination"]

abstract: A method for making vanadium dioxide (V.sub.2 or V.sub.2 O.sub.4) powders from vanadyl sulfate without using SO.sub.2 gas, comprises evaporative decomposition of a vanadyl sulfate hydrate spray, entrained in a nitrogen atmosphere at O.sub.2 partial pressures that would normally predict V.sub.2 O.sub.5 V.sub.2 O.sub.3. The yield of VO.sub.2 (also identified as V.sub.2 O.sub.4) is substantially improved, and occurs at lower temperatures, by the addition of hydrogen gas into the atmosphere. Surprisingly, there is no production of V.sub.2 O.sub.3. Minor amounts of a suitable dopant salt dissolved in the spray provide improved low transition temperature powders.
problem: Producing vanadium dioxide (VO₂ / V₂O₄) powders from vanadyl sulfate without using toxic SO₂ gas, while achieving higher yield and lower processing temperature, and avoiding formation of unwanted oxidation states (V₂O₅ or V₂O₃).
constraint: The oxygen partial pressure and hydrogen concentration must be precisely balanced: enough hydrogen to reduce V₂O₅ to VO₂ and prevent V₂O₃ formation, but not so much as to over-reduce to V₂O₃; the temperature must be lowered by the hydrogen effect but still sufficient for complete decomposition of the vanadyl sulfate feed.
mechanism: Evaporative decomposition of a metal sulfate hydrate spray in an inert carrier atmosphere, with controlled oxygen partial pressure, into which a reducing gas is deliberately introduced. The reducing gas acts as a mild reducing agent that shifts the oxidation equilibrium toward an intermediate oxidation state, suppressing both higher and lower oxidation states. The inert carrier ensures uniform spray transport and prevents unwanted oxidation, while the reducing gas addition lowers the effective decomposition temperature needed to reach the target phase.
mechanism_raw: Evaporative decomposition of a vanadyl sulfate hydrate spray in a nitrogen carrier atmosphere, with controlled oxygen partial pressure, into which hydrogen gas is deliberately introduced. The hydrogen acts as a mild reducing agent that shifts the oxidation equilibrium toward the intermediate VO₂ state, suppressing both the higher oxidation state (V₂O₅, which would form at higher O₂ partial pressures) and the lower oxidation state (V₂O₃, which would form under stronger reduction). The nitrogen carrier ensures uniform spray transport and prevents unwanted oxidation, while the hydrogen addition lowers the effective decomposition temperature needed to reach the target phase.
residual_terms: ["oxidation state", "oxygen partial pressure", "reducing agent", "oxidation equilibrium", "inert carrier"]

abstract: A process for the manufacture of anti-regurgitation infant milk is disclo wherein the milk is preheated, homogenized, and treated at ultra high temperatures and wherein a thickening agent, such as carob, guar, carrageenans, or pectins, is added prior to the homogenization step in an amount of between 0.3% and 1.0% by weight of the milk. The milk is then packaged under aseptic conditions in sterile packages.
problem: Preventing regurgitation in infants consuming milk by modifying the milk's physical properties.
constraint: The thickener concentration must balance efficacy (0.3–1.0% by weight) to avoid excessive viscosity that could impede flow or nutritional absorption.
mechanism: Introducing a viscosity-modifying agent into a fluid medium at a controlled concentration range (0.3–1.0% by weight) prior to homogenization, ensuring uniform dispersion and rheological modification. This increases resistance to flow, slowing transit through a biological conduit and reducing expulsion events. The timing of agent introduction before homogenization optimizes distribution and long-term stability of the modified fluid.
mechanism_raw: Adding a thickening agent (e.g., carob, guar, carrageenans, pectins) prior to homogenization ensures even dispersion and viscosity enhancement, which slows gastric emptying and reduces regurgitation. The timing of thickener addition before homogenization optimizes distribution and stability.

abstract: A submerged arc welding method for a high strength (2.25%-3%)Cr-3% Mo-V steel, to obtain a weld metal excellent in strength at room temperature and high temperature, toughness, and creep strength, after SR, temper brittleness resistance, cold crack resistance and SR crack resistance. The Cr-Mo steel contains: 2.00 to 3.25% of Cr, 0.90 to 1.20% of Mo, and V as essential components, and Nb, Ti, B and Ca as needed. A welding heat input is in the range of from 20 to 50 kJ/cm. The solid wire contains 0.09 to 0.19% of C, 0.30% or less of Si, 0.50 to 1.40% of Mn, 2.00 to 3.80% of Cr and 0.90 to 1.20% of Mo. The bonded flux contains 5 to 20% of SiO.sub.2, 20 to 40% of MgO, 2.4 to 12% of a metal fluoride (F-converted value) and 3 to 12% of a metal carbonate (CO.sub.2 -converted value). A weld metal contains 0.08 to 0.15% of C, 0.05 to 0.30% of Si, 0.50 to 1.20% of Mn, 0.030 to 0.060% of O, 0.10 to 0.50% of V and 0.005 to 0.035% of Nb. P and Ti in the weld metal are restricted to 0.010% or less and 0.012% or less, respectively. The components of C, Si, Mn, O, P, Ti are added from the solid wire and the bonded flux, and the components of V and Nb are added from at least one of the wire and the bonded flux. Moreover, the welding is performed such that Ps is 3.50 to 5.50, Ps being expressed by EQU Ps= 10.times.[ C].sub.D + 10.times.[ Si].sub.D +[Mn].sub.D + 50.times.[ P].sub.D + 20.times.[ O].sub.D where [X].sub.D is wt % of the component X in weld metal.
problem: Achieving optimal mechanical properties (strength, toughness, creep resistance) in weld metal for high-strength Cr-Mo-V steel.
constraint: Elemental concentrations and heat input must stay within narrow ranges to avoid temper brittleness, cold cracking, or solidification cracking while maintaining strength and toughness.
mechanism: Controlling material composition by selectively sourcing alloying elements from either a consumable feedstock or a bonded coating, while regulating thermal energy input (20–50 kJ/cm) during deposition. A predictive formula balances detrimental elemental concentrations (e.g., carbon, silicon, phosphorus) to maintain microstructural integrity and prevent failure modes such as cracking or brittleness.
mechanism_raw: Controlling weld metal composition by sourcing specific elements (e.g., V, Nb) from either the solid wire or bonded flux, while regulating heat input (20–50 kJ/cm) and using a formula (Ps) to balance detrimental elements (C, Si, Mn, P, O) ensures microstructural stability and resistance to cracking.

abstract: A conveyor system for transporting and aligning articles to be sorted in an automated bulk processing system is disclosed. The conveyor comprises one or more product-carrying lanes, each lane comprising two side belts separated by a central product-carrying belt. Each of the side belts is raised with respect to the product-carrying belt, thereby guiding articles on to the product-carrying belt. In a preferred embodiment, the product-carrying belt has two product-carrying surfaces and is provided with a 180.degree. lengthwise twist whereby the product-carrying surfaces are alternately presented on the upper surface of the conveyor system for each complete belt travel cycle. The 180.degree. lengthwise twist is maintained in position by a belt guide or comb located on the underside of the conveyor system.
problem: Transporting and aligning articles in an automated sorting system while ensuring consistent orientation for downstream processing.
constraint: The belt guide or comb must maintain the twist geometry to prevent belt deformation, ensuring reliable surface alternation without disrupting article transport.
mechanism: A conveying surface incorporates a lengthwise rotational deformation (180-degree twist) to alternate its functional orientation during each transport cycle. Secondary guiding elements, positioned above the primary surface, direct articles onto the twisted region, ensuring consistent alignment through geometric constraint and surface alternation.
mechanism_raw: A 180-degree lengthwise twist in the central product-carrying belt alternates the presentation of its two surfaces during each cycle, enabling automatic alignment and orientation of articles. Side belts raised relative to the central belt guide articles onto the twisted belt.

abstract: The invention provides a transfer paper which comprises a releasable base and as disposed successively thereon at least one picture printing layer, a thermosetting adhesive layer and a release layer, and a transfer process employing the above transfer paper which comprises peeling off the releasable base from the paper, transferring the printing layer and thermosetting adhesive layer as a unit to a substrate and curing the adhesive layer at a temperature of 80.degree.-170.degree. C.
problem: Transferring a printed image and adhesive layer to a substrate while preserving print quality and ensuring strong adhesion.
constraint: The curing temperature range must be controlled to avoid degrading the print layer or substrate while ensuring full adhesive crosslinking for durable bonding.
mechanism: A releasable substrate enables peeling of a printed layer and thermally activatable adhesive as a unified composite. The composite is transferred to a target surface, where controlled thermal energy (80–170°C) induces crosslinking in the adhesive, permanently bonding the layers while activating its thermoset properties.
mechanism_raw: A releasable base allows peeling off the printing and thermosetting adhesive layers as a unit, which are then transferred to the substrate. Curing the adhesive at 80–170°C bonds the layers permanently while activating the adhesive's thermoset properties.

abstract: An improved saddle tree is provided, which flexibly confirms to a horse's back to accommodate the physically characteristics of a given horse, and incorporates a damping system to preclude excessive vibrations in the flexible materials. The saddle tree includes a pair of laterally spaced apart, flexible synthetic skirts connected by a spanning member and a seat element. The seat element is coupled with the respective skirts at two forward pivot mountings, and the spanning member extends between the skirts at a rearward position. The seat element carries a skid assembly at a position just rearward of the pommel, and this assembly deforms under compressive loading to provide damping action. The cantle portion of the seat element slidably and frictionally engages the top of the spanning member.
problem: Creating a saddle that conforms to a horse's back anatomy while minimizing vibrations and maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: The balance between skirt flexibility and damping effectiveness must prevent excessive movement or vibration without compromising load-bearing capacity or rider stability.
mechanism: Flexible elements connected by a load-distributing member allow dynamic conformity to an irregular surface. A compressible damping assembly deforms under applied force to absorb vibrational energy, while a frictionally engaged adjustable component enables positional tuning without compromising structural load-bearing capacity.
mechanism_raw: Flexible synthetic skirts connected by a spanning member and seat element allow dynamic conformity to the horse's back. A skid assembly deforms under compressive loading to dampen vibrations, while the cantle's frictional engagement with the spanning member enables adjustable positioning.
residual_terms: ["load-distributing member", "compressible damping assembly", "frictionally engaged adjustable component"]

abstract: Concentrated tobacco extracts or essences are provided by first extracting water soluble components from tobacco. The aqueous extract then is contacted with supercritical carbon dioxide, and certain tobacco components in turn are extracted from the aqueous extract. Alternatively, the aqueous extract is subjected to a spray drying step, and the spray dried extract is contacted with supercritical carbon dioxide in order that certain tobacco components are extracted from the spray dried extract. The resulting extracted components are separated from the supercritical fluid in order to yield a tobacco essence. The essence has a homogeneous, viscous character and exhibits a tobacco aroma. The essence is useful as a flavoring agent for cigarettes and other smoking articles.
problem: Efficiently extracting and concentrating specific tobacco components while maintaining homogeneity and aroma.
constraint: Precise control of pressure and temperature to target specific components while preserving the chemical integrity and viscosity of the final essence.
mechanism: Using a medium with tunable solvent properties under controlled pressure and temperature to selectively isolate target compounds from a matrix, where the medium's adjustable characteristics enable component-specific extraction without thermal degradation of sensitive materials.
mechanism_raw: Using supercritical carbon dioxide as a selective solvent to extract target compounds from an aqueous tobacco extract or spray-dried matrix, leveraging the tunable solvent properties of supercritical fluids under controlled pressure and temperature to isolate desired components without thermal degradation.

abstract: A portfolio is formed from a blank of relatively rigid sheet material that includes front and rear covers hingedly connected for enclosing a multiple-page document. A document securement flap extends as an integrally formed member from the top edge of the rear cover. The document securement flap includes multiple panels defined by parallel fold lines. Folding of the panels about the fold lines creates a pocket for receiving and securing the upper marginal edge of the multiple-page document, and creates a structure that permits the document so secured to pivot about the fold line at which the document securement flap joins the rear cover.
problem: Securing a document within a portfolio while allowing it to pivot for easy access.
constraint: Balancing material rigidity and fold-line design to ensure secure retention without restricting pivotal movement.
mechanism: A flexible retention structure with defined fold lines that creates a gripping pocket for an object's edge while incorporating a hinge-like base to permit rotational access to the secured object.
mechanism_raw: A multi-panel flap with parallel fold lines that, when folded, creates a flexible pocket to grip the document's edge and a hinge-like structure at the flap's base to enable pivoting motion of the secured document.

abstract: The present invention provides a method of preparing a support for a filtration medium comprising passing a sheet of nonwoven fibrous polymeric material having first and second sides through a calender which comprises a nondeformable roll and a resilient roll, the nondeformable roll being maintained at a temperature below the melting temperature of the material, so as to increase the smoothness of the first side of the material which contacted the resilient roll. A filtration medium support material prepared in accordance with the method of the present invention, as well as a filter comprising a filtration medium and that filtration medium support material, are also provided by the present invention.
problem: Increasing the smoothness of one side of a nonwoven polymer sheet without deforming the material.
constraint: Maintaining temperature below the material's melting point to prevent deformation while achieving sufficient surface smoothing.
mechanism: Applying controlled pressure between a rigid surface and a deformable surface at a temperature below the material's phase-change threshold, where the deformable surface adapts to irregularities while the rigid surface enforces planar contact to smooth one side without bulk deformation.
mechanism_raw: Calendering the material between a nondeformable roll and a resilient roll at a temperature below the polymer's melting point, where the resilient roll conforms to surface irregularities while the nondeformable roll applies controlled pressure to smooth the contacted side.

abstract: An aeraulic separator for automatically separating materials into three batches of different weights or shapes having a chamber under a slight depression with an inlet opening, two perforated inclined planes with an inclination of angle .alpha. and .beta.,.beta. being greater than or equal to .alpha., supplied with air under pressure, three outlet openings for the three batches, and a deflector. The heavy materials drop through the first opening adjacent the second inclined plane. The materials of intermediate weight are projected above the deflector and drop in the second opening, while the light materials are sucked through the third opening connected to a suction system. The separator is preferably mounted on a system for vibrating at low frequency and high elongation.
problem: Automatically separating materials into three distinct batches based on weight or shape using aerodynamic forces.
constraint: Precise control of air pressure, suction, and incline angles to achieve consistent separation across three distinct weight classes.
mechanism: Using multiple inclined surfaces with differing angles, combined with directed airflow and suction, to separate objects into distinct streams based on their response to aerodynamic forces and gravitational pull, where angle differences and airflow control determine trajectory-based classification.
mechanism_raw: Using two perforated inclined planes with differing angles (.beta. ≥ .alpha.) supplied with pressurized air, combined with a suction system and deflector, to direct heavy materials downward, intermediate materials upward over the deflector, and light materials into a suction-driven outlet.

abstract: Five xylanases are purified from the microorganism, Microtetraspora flexuosa,preferably strain ATCC 35864. Each biochemically unique xylanase is thermostable and has optimal activity in alkaline conditions. These enzymes are excellent candidates for enhancing the delignification and bleaching of pulp. Furthermore, treating the pulp with the above enzymes prior to bleaching may reduce the amount of chlorine containing and/or peroxide chemicals required in the bleaching process.
problem: Reducing the use of harsh chemicals in pulp bleaching while enhancing delignification and brightness.
constraint: Ensuring enzyme stability and activity under high-temperature, alkaline conditions typical of industrial pulp processing.
mechanism: Introducing a catalyst that remains active under harsh environmental conditions to pre-treat a substrate, thereby increasing accessibility of target substances to subsequent processing agents and reducing the required dosage of aggressive chemicals.
mechanism_raw: Applying thermostable, alkaline-active xylanases to break down xylan in pulp prior to bleaching, thereby increasing accessibility of lignin to chemical agents and reducing the required dosage of chlorine-based or peroxide chemicals.

abstract: A surface wellhead system for a subsea well utilizes a two-piece casing hanger. The casing hanger has an inner member that secures to a string of casing that extends from the sea floor to a surface casing head. The outer member of the casing hanger is axially adjustable relative to the inner member and will hold tension in the casing. The outer member lands on a load shoulder in the casing head. An annulus outer seal seals between the exterior of the outer member and the bore of the casing head. An inner seal seals between the inner member and the bore of the outer member.
problem: Maintaining tension in a subsea casing string while allowing axial adjustment during installation and operation.
constraint: Balancing axial adjustability for tensioning with maintaining structural integrity and pressure sealing in a subsea environment.
mechanism: A two-part adjustable coupling with a fixed inner component and an axially movable outer component. The outer component transfers tension via a load shoulder and maintains pressure isolation through seals between the components and the surrounding structure.
mechanism_raw: A two-piece casing hanger with an inner member fixed to the casing and an outer member that is axially adjustable relative to the inner member. The outer member lands on a load shoulder in the casing head to transfer tension loads, while seals between the outer member and casing head, and between the inner and outer members, maintain pressure isolation during adjustment.

abstract: A method for controlling a hydraulic motor with a hydraulic valve comprising an inlet section which includes a pump and tank connection and a maneuvering section having a slide (B1) and a load signal system (L1, L2, L3). The hydraulic valve also includes two regulating constrictions (S3, S4) which can be connected to and from a motor (C), such as a hydraulic piston-cylinder device. The maneuvering slide (B1) also includes a load level detecting constriction (S2) and a load signal drain (S5), and the pump generates an idling pressure. When maneuvering the maneuver slide (B1), the load signal Ps of the load signal system is increased by a further constriction (S1) located between the pump connection and that side of the load detecting constriction (S2) that has the higher pressure during the maneuvering process.
problem: Controlling a hydraulic motor efficiently under varying load conditions without overloading the system.
constraint: Maintaining stable pressure feedback and avoiding excessive pressure spikes while ensuring responsive control under variable loads.
mechanism: A pressure feedback system using constrictions to modulate a control valve's response. The feedback pressure increases through a constriction between the pump and load detection point, enabling proportional control based on real-time load demands.
mechanism_raw: Using a load signal system with pressure feedback through constrictions (S1, S2) to dynamically adjust the hydraulic valve's response. The load signal pressure (Ps) increases via a constriction between the pump and the load detecting constriction during maneuvering, enabling proportional control based on real-time load demands.

abstract: Aqueous emulsions of graft copolymers comprising acrylate esters of alkanols having 2-24 carbon atoms grafted onto a backbone polymer comprising monomers of acrylate esters of alkanols having 2-24 carbon atoms are disclosed, as is the finishing of surfaces such as tanned leather by applying such emulsions thereto.
problem: Creating a durable, adherent surface finish for materials like leather using aqueous emulsions.
constraint: Balancing the molecular weight and graft density of the copolymer to achieve optimal adhesion, flexibility, and durability without compromising emulsion stability.
mechanism: A graft copolymer structure where grafted chains of the same monomers as the backbone enhance adhesion and film-forming properties through molecular compatibility with the substrate.
mechanism_raw: Grafting acrylate esters of alkanols (2-24 carbons) onto a backbone polymer of the same monomers to form a graft copolymer emulsion. The graft structure enhances adhesion and film-forming properties when applied to surfaces, leveraging molecular compatibility between the grafted chains and the substrate.

abstract: A mine removal vehicle comprises a tracked vehicle, a frontal assembly operatively connected with the tracked vehicle in a liftable and lowerable manner, and a box connected to the frontal assembly which has a scarifying drum arranged in it transversely to the driving direction. The scarifying drum is lowered into the soil, rotating against the driving direction, transporting a mine toward the front of the scarifying drum and exploding it there by the application of pressure.
problem: Safely removing buried mines or explosive objects from soil without premature detonation.
constraint: Ensuring the drum's rotation and soil engagement reliably move mines to the detonation zone without accidental triggering during transport.
mechanism: A counter-rotating transverse drum that engages and lifts buried objects, transporting them to a controlled detonation zone. The drum's rotation direction and position isolate the explosion from the vehicle.
mechanism_raw: Using a transverse scarifying drum rotated against the vehicle's driving direction to engage and lift mines from the soil. The drum's rotation transports mines toward its front end, where mechanical pressure triggers controlled detonation, isolating the explosion from the vehicle.

abstract: To provide a recovery plant for surplus water paint in paint-spraying booths comprising a circuit of water circulating in the booth, wherein such problems with sedimenting water paint particles no longer arise, it is proposed that a volume flow of water circulating in the booth flow from the circuit of water circulating in the booth through a branch pipe to a preconcentration stage, that the preconcentration stage comprise a ring circuit with an ultrafiltration unit for continuously producing a preconcentrate in the ring circuit and a permeate which leaves the ring circuit, that the permeate flow into the circuit of water circulating in the booth and the preconcentrate into a final concentration stage, that the final concentration stage comprise a ring circuit with an ultrafiltration unit which increases the concentration of the preconcentrate in batches to the final concentrate and produces a permeate which flows into the circuit of water circulating in the booth.
problem: Recovering surplus water-based paint from spray booth water circuits without sedimentation or clogging.
constraint: Maintaining continuous ultrafiltration operation without membrane fouling while balancing permeate recycling and concentrate production rates.
mechanism: A multi-stage ultrafiltration system with preconcentration and final concentration stages. Permeate is recycled to the circuit, while concentrate is further processed to prevent particle settling.
mechanism_raw: Routing a portion of the circulating water through a preconcentration stage with ultrafiltration to continuously produce a preconcentrate and permeate. The permeate is recycled to the booth circuit, while the preconcentrate flows to a final concentration stage with batch ultrafiltration to produce a final concentrate, preventing particle settling.

abstract: A control system for a clothes dryer is disclosed. A microprocessor monitors the heated inlet air temperature and the exhaust temperature. If the inlet temperature exceeds a high limit value a given number of times, an air blockage indicator is activated. Degrees of dryness are measured by the number of times the inlet temperature has dropped below a threshold value while the heater is off because the exhaust temperature has exceeded a desired value. An estimated drying time is calculated and displayed to the user based on a linear function of the inlet and exhaust temperatures measured at the beginning of the cycle and again a short time later.
problem: Diagnosing air blockage and degree of dryness in a clothes dryer, and estimating drying time, without direct measurement of internal airflow or moisture content.
constraint: The system relies on counting discrete threshold-crossing events rather than continuous measurement of airflow or moisture, trading measurement precision for robustness and simplicity. The linear time estimation assumes a roughly linear relationship between temperature evolution and drying progress, which may not hold under all conditions.
mechanism: Monitoring observable signal threshold-crossing events to infer unobservable internal system states. A counter accumulates discrete events when a measured signal crosses predefined thresholds, where each crossing corresponds to a specific internal condition. The accumulated count is then used to estimate a target outcome through a linear relationship between initial and subsequent signal measurements. The causal chain is: signal threshold events → count accumulation → state inference and outcome prediction.
mechanism_raw: Using threshold-crossing event counting on observable temperature signals to infer hidden system states. Each time the inlet temperature crosses a high threshold, a blockage counter increments; each time it drops below a threshold while the heater is off (indicating exhaust temperature exceeded a desired value), a dryness counter increments. A linear function of initial and later temperature measurements estimates drying time. The causal chain is: temperature threshold events → count accumulation → state inference and time prediction.

abstract: Synthetic resins contain, as essential components, A) from 20 to 95% by weight of a crosslinkable binder selected from the group consisting of the polymers, polyadducts or polycondensates having reactive centers in the form of hydroxyl, thio, primary and/or secondary amino groups and/or hydrophilic centers in the form of ammonium, sulfonium and/or phosphonium groups and B) from 5 to 80% by weight of polymers consisting of a core and one or more shells and furthermore C) from 0 to 10% by weight of one or more crosslinking agents and D) from 0 to 10% by weight of a pigment formulation consisting of one or more pigments and a resin having surfactant properties and E) from 0 to 10% by weight of additives and/or assistants.
reason: This patent discloses a chemical formulation specifying weight percentages of various components (crosslinkable binder, core-shell polymers, crosslinking agents, pigments, additives). The 'mechanism' is essentially a recipe of what to mix in what proportions, not a causal functional relationship that produces a useful effect through a generalizable principle.
