It is a list of materials and their ratios rather than an operational mechanism.

abstract: A solid state, bipolar, ignition exciter for gas turbine engines is described for delivering high energy pulses to one or more igniter plugs. A storage capacitor is charged with typically 12 to 20 Joules of stored energy and discharged through a solid state switch and a series-connected ignitor plug. The solid state switch consists of a plurality of silicon controlled rectifiers (SCRs) connected in series, in combination with other components connected in parallel with each SCR. Protection is provided against transients in voltage by means of resistance-capacitance snubber circuits connected in parallel with each SCR. Protection is provided against transients in current by means of inductance connected externally, and in series with, the solid state switch. Protection is provided against damage from reverse voltages by means of a reverse current path through the solid state switch, typically by means of a diode or series-connected diode chain connected in parallel with the SCRs. Thus, the solid state switch of the present invention conducts current alternately in forward and reverse directions once the SCRs are switched to their conducting state, providing bipolar current flow to the igniter plug. Controlling means and short circuit protection circuits are also described.
problem: Delivering high-energy electrical pulses to igniter plugs in gas turbine engines using solid-state switches, while protecting the switches from voltage transients, current transients, and reverse voltage damage.
constraint: The protection circuits must be individually connected in parallel with each SCR, and the inductance must be external and in series with the entire switch string. This adds component count and complexity, and the external inductance introduces additional parasitic effects that must be managed.
mechanism: Providing individual parallel protection circuits for each switching element in a series string, where each protection circuit is tailored to mitigate a specific failure mode. Parallel RC networks absorb voltage transients, external series inductance limits current transients, and parallel reverse-current paths protect against reverse voltage. The causal chain is: each switch in the series string has dedicated parallel protection → different transient types are independently mitigated → the switch string can conduct bipolar current safely and reliably.
mechanism_raw: For a series string of switching elements (SCRs), providing individual parallel protection circuits tailored to each failure mode: RC snubber circuits in parallel with each SCR to absorb voltage transients, external series inductance to limit current transients, and parallel reverse-current paths (diodes) to protect against reverse voltage. The causal chain is: each switch in the series string has dedicated parallel protection → different transient types are independently mitigated → the switch string can conduct bipolar current safely and reliably.
residual_terms: ["parallel protection circuits", "RC networks", "series inductance", "reverse-current paths", "switch string"]

abstract: There is disclosed an apparatus, for mounting a combined roof plumbing vent, and a safety stanchion element, on a roof with its roof covering, the elements having a mounting bracket, in conjunction with the roof beam element, being formed by fixedly connecting with a least one roof beam or rafter element, a substantially vertical tubular element, and having a fixably attached in a known manner, a roof covering.
reason: This patent describes a specific mechanical mounting apparatus for attaching a roof vent and stanchion to roof beams. The 'mechanism' is simply attaching a tubular element to structural roof beams through the roof covering. This is a basic structural attachment method without a generalizable causal functional principle. It is essentially a product design for a specific mounting scenario, not a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A dispenser is programmed to automatically dispense a beverage into a plurality of different size containers by storing therein a volume designation for each size container. The flow rate of beverage through the dispenser is determined. To do so, a user manually operates the dispenser to fill a given container with the beverage while the dispenser measures the filling time. The dispenser calculates a beverage flow rate from the volume designation for the given container and the filling time. Then the flow rate and volume designations are used thereafter by the dispenser to derive a dispensing time for each different size container. Thus the dispenser is able to derive dispensing times for each container size from filling only one of the containers. A unique dispenser valve also is disclosed.
problem: Automatically dispensing beverages into containers of different sizes without pre-calibrating or pre-programming dispensing times for each container size.
constraint: The method assumes the flow rate remains consistent between the calibration fill and subsequent automatic dispenses. Any variation in flow rate (due to temperature, pressure, viscosity changes, or equipment wear) will introduce errors in all derived dispensing times. The system also requires accurate volume designations to be pre-stored for each container size.
mechanism: Calibrating a system parameter using a single reference measurement, then applying the calibrated parameter to derive target values for multiple configurations. A user performs one manual operation while the system measures the associated time, allowing the system to calculate a rate parameter from the known quantity and measured time. This rate parameter is then combined with stored quantity designations for all other configurations to derive target values for each. The causal chain is: single manual calibration → rate parameter determination → rate parameter combined with stored quantities → automatic target value calculation for all configurations.
mechanism_raw: Calibrating a system parameter (flow rate) using a single reference measurement: a user manually fills one container while the dispenser measures filling time, then the dispenser calculates flow rate from the known volume and measured time. This calibrated flow rate is then combined with stored volume designations for all other container sizes to derive dispensing times for each. The causal chain is: single manual calibration → flow rate determination → flow rate combined with stored volumes → automatic dispensing time calculation for all container sizes.

abstract: An apparatus for breaking solid objects includes a box-shaped support (6) open at the top and at the bottom, a substantially horizontal rotor (6) mounted in the box and carrying at least one knife which turns with it while passing between backing knives, an active face of which is turned toward the rotor, and preferably has teeth, the backing knives being movable independently of each other and having their own return means, for example by oscillating the backing knives on a pivot parallel to the rotor. The knives may be set in forced oscillation, and may be individually removable.
problem: Efficiently breaking solid objects while maintaining consistent cutting action and avoiding jamming or uneven fragmentation.
constraint: Balancing the oscillation frequency and force of each backing knife to avoid over-stressing the system while maintaining sufficient interaction with the rotor knives for effective material breakdown.
mechanism: Independent adaptive elements, each with their own restoring mechanism, respond to a primary moving cutting surface and varying material resistance. This ensures continuous, uniform force application during material breakdown, even as the material shifts or deforms.
mechanism_raw: Independent oscillation of backing knives, each with their own return means, allows them to adaptively respond to the rotor's motion and material resistance. This ensures continuous, uniform cutting force application even as the material shifts or deforms during the breaking process.

abstract: For loading a processing machine with band-like material from a coil, a rotatable support, on which the coil rests with its axis substantially vertical, is driven by a motor. Since the circumference of the coil decreases during unwinding, a sensor is provided for controlling the motor to maintain a desired constant band speed.
problem: Maintaining a constant output speed of band-like material being unwound from a coil, despite the decreasing circumference of the coil during unwinding.
constraint: Achieving precise sensor feedback and motor control to avoid overshooting or lagging adjustments, which could cause material slack or tension irregularities.
mechanism: A feedback system monitors the changing geometry of a rotating supply and dynamically adjusts the driving force to maintain a constant output speed of the delivered material, compensating for variations in effective circumference.
mechanism_raw: A sensor monitors the coil's rotational speed or diameter in real-time and dynamically adjusts the motor's driving force to compensate for the changing circumference, ensuring the band speed remains constant regardless of the coil's state.

abstract: A method is disclosed for improving the stability of Vitamin D in liquid nutritional products which contain hydrolyzed protein or free amino acids as nitrogen sources. Vitamin C is added before or after a preliminary heat treatment of the liquid nutritional product and at a concentration exceeding 300 mg/l, such that the initial concentration of Vitamin C is at least 300 mg/l during the shelf-life of the liquid nutritional product. An emulsifier is added to the liquid nutritional product prior to preliminary heat treatment, the emulsifier being a diacetyltartaric acid ester of monoglycerides and diglycerides. Cystine is added following the preliminary heat treatment.
problem: Preventing degradation of Vitamin D in liquid nutritional products containing hydrolyzed proteins or free amino acids, which are prone to destabilizing reactions during storage.
constraint: Sequencing and concentration of additives must avoid interfering with the nutritional product's palatability, viscosity, or heat-sensitivity while maximizing synergistic stabilization effects.
mechanism: A multi-component stabilization strategy applies an antioxidant before or after thermal processing, an emulsifier to stabilize dispersed phases, and a post-processing radical scavenger to collectively reduce oxidative and chemical degradation pathways of a sensitive nutrient.
mechanism_raw: Adding Vitamin C as an antioxidant before or after heat treatment, combined with a diacetyltartaric acid ester emulsifier to stabilize lipid phases, and post-treatment cystine to scavenge free radicals, collectively reduces oxidative and chemical degradation pathways for Vitamin D.

abstract: A nonwoven fiber and fabric are provided wherein the fabric has comparable strength characteristics to conventional fabrics yet is softer. The fibers are are a blend of a high crystallinity polypropylene polymer and a random block copolymer of polypropylene and polyethylene. The fabric of this invention may be laminated to other spunbond layers, meltblown nonwoven fabrics or films. The nonwoven fabric of this invention may be used in products such as, for example, garments, personal care products, medical products, protective covers and outdoor fabrics.
problem: Creating a nonwoven fabric that combines high tensile strength with softness, which are typically opposing material properties.
constraint: Optimizing the ratio and compatibility of the two polymers to prevent delamination or phase separation during processing while achieving the desired mechanical and sensory properties.
mechanism: A composite material is formed by blending a high-stiffness polymer with a flexible copolymer, creating a phase-separated structure that balances mechanical strength and surface softness through controlled morphological interaction between the two components.
mechanism_raw: Blending a high-crystallinity polypropylene polymer (for structural rigidity) with a random block copolymer of polypropylene and polyethylene (for flexibility and surface softness) creates a composite fiber structure that balances strength and tactile comfort through phase-separated morphology.

abstract: A magnetic scale is formed by a plurality of non-magnetic parts arranged at equidistant intervals in all axial direction on a magnetic rod which displaces in the axial direction. The non-magnetic parts consist of first non-magnetic parts having a constant depth, and second non-magnetic parts having a different depth. A magnetic sensor which outputs a signal according to the depth and positional change of the non-magnetic parts is installed at a fixed position opposite the magnetic scale. Further provided are a mechanism for identifying a second non-magnetic part which has passed the magnetic sensor based on the output of the sensor, a memory for individually storing the absolute positions of the second non-magnetic parts, and a mechanism for calculating the displacement of the rod from the identified second non-magnetic part to its current position based oil the sensor output. The absolute position of the rod is detected, in terms of a small displacement from its stationary position, by computing it from the absolute position of the identified second non-magnetic part stored in the memory and the displacement of the rod from this second non-magnetic part. This assembly comprises only a single magnetic scale having several types of non-magnetic parts, and is therefore more economical to manufacture than the conventional assembly having a plurality of magnetic scales.
problem: Accurately detecting the absolute position of a linearly moving rod using a single magnetic scale, rather than multiple scales, to reduce manufacturing costs.
constraint: Ensuring the sensor can reliably distinguish between the two types of non-magnetic segments and that the memory accurately maps their positions to avoid cumulative error in displacement calculations.
mechanism: Absolute positional information is encoded into a single sensing medium by varying the physical characteristics of non-responsive segments. A fixed detector reads these variations, and stored reference data maps their positions, enabling displacement calculation from the nearest known reference point.
mechanism_raw: Encoding absolute positional information into a single magnetic scale by varying the depth of non-magnetic segments (first type with constant depth, second type with variable depth). A fixed magnetic sensor detects these depth variations, and a memory stores the absolute positions of the variable-depth segments, enabling displacement calculation from the nearest known reference point.

abstract: A fluidized bed combustion system and method in which a recycle heat exchanger is located adjacent the furnace section of the recycle heat exchanger. Heat exchange surfaces are provided in a compartment of the recycle heat exchanger for removing heat from the solids, and a bypass compartment is provided through which the solids directly pass to the furnace during start-up and low load conditions. The flow of solids between compartments is selectively controlled and an L-valve connects one of the compartments to the furnace section. Air is passed into the L-valve to promote the flow of the separated materials from the latter compartment to the furnace. The flow rate of the air is modulated to vary the duty of the recycle heat exchanger.
problem: Managing solid material flow and heat recovery in a fluidized bed combustion system across different operational modes (start-up, low load, normal operation) where the heat exchanger duty and solid transport requirements vary.
constraint: Balancing heat recovery from solids (via the heat exchanger) against direct solid transport to the furnace (via bypass) during different operational conditions; the system must maintain proper solid flow while modulating heat exchange duty through a single control variable (air flow rate).
mechanism: Selective routing of solid materials through parallel processing paths — a heat exchange path for normal operation and a bypass path for start-up/low load — with flow between paths actively controlled. A modulated gas flow rate drives material transfer to the processing chamber, where the gas flow rate directly modulates the heat exchange duty, coupling material transport control with thermal duty control.
mechanism_raw: Selective routing of solid materials through parallel processing paths — a heat exchange compartment for normal operation and a bypass compartment for start-up/low load — with flow between compartments actively controlled. An L-valve uses modulated air flow to drive material transfer to the furnace, where the air flow rate directly modulates the heat exchanger duty, coupling solid transport control with thermal duty control.

abstract: A self-propelled elevator car for vertical and horizontal travel in an elevator shaft has a plurality of driven friction wheels which are pressed against associated running surfaces by a passive contact force which produces the necessary friction and is influenced by a load-dependent gravitational force and an additional regulated active force. The friction wheels are rotatably mounted at free ends of guide arms having opposite ends pivotally connected to a lifting carriage attached to the bottom of the car. The guide arms extend downwardly and outwardly at a defined angle to the horizontal of a straight line between the pivot point and a contact point of the friction wheels with the running surface such that the gravitational force acting on the car forces the wheels outwardly. The active force can be applied by setting elements connected between the carriage and the guide arms. A force sensor mounted at the pivot point senses the passive force and is connected to a processor control which controls the active force applied by the setting elements in accordance with the value of the passive force.
problem: Maintaining proper friction contact force between driven wheels and running surfaces in a self-propelled elevator car that travels both vertically and horizontally, where the load on the car varies and precise friction control is needed.
constraint: Balancing the passive mechanical advantage of gravity-based force scaling (which provides baseline pressure proportional to load) with the precision of active force regulation; the system must avoid over-compensation while ensuring sufficient friction for both vertical and horizontal travel under varying loads.
mechanism: Combining a passive load-dependent gravitational force (which naturally scales contact pressure with load) with an actively regulated force applied through adjustable elements. Mechanical linkages pivot to translate the load's gravitational force into outward pressure. A force sensor at the pivot point measures the passive force component, and a processor adjusts the active force in real-time to achieve the desired total contact force.
mechanism_raw: Combining a passive load-dependent gravitational force (which naturally scales contact pressure with car weight) with an actively regulated force applied through setting elements. Guide arms pivot to mechanically translate the car's gravitational force into outward wheel pressure. A force sensor at the pivot point measures the passive force component, and a processor adjusts the active force in real-time to achieve the desired total contact force.

abstract: Breast meat is stripped from a poultry carcass, after the shoulder joints have been separated and preliminary cuts have been made in the shoulder area with a cutter designed to leave the wings attached to the breast meat, by pulling the wings and breast meat attached thereto downward on the carcass. The breast fillets and wings remain attached to the carcass, facilitating visual inspection of the product. An apparatus for performing this method comprises special devices operating at four successive stations of an inline machine; the inspection is done at a fifth station.
problem: Efficiently stripping breast meat from a poultry carcass while keeping the wings attached to the breast meat for visual inspection of the product.
constraint: Balancing efficient meat removal with keeping the product attached for inspection; the wings must remain connected to the breast meat (serving as handles) while the breast meat is separated from the carcass, requiring cuts that selectively disconnect shoulder joints without disconnecting wings from breast meat.
mechanism: Using a connected portion of the product (the wings) as a mechanical handle and lever to perform separation on another portion (breast meat). Preliminary cuts selectively disconnect joints while intentionally leaving the handle portion attached. The handle is then pulled downward on the carcass, using its attachment point as a fulcrum and its structure as a grip, to strip the target portion from the carcass.
mechanism_raw: Using a connected portion of the product (the wings) as a mechanical handle and lever to perform separation on another portion (breast meat). Preliminary cuts separate shoulder joints while intentionally leaving wings attached to the breast meat. The wings are then pulled downward on the carcass, using their attachment point as a fulcrum and their structure as a grip, to strip the breast fillets from the carcass.

abstract: A non-toxic primer composition for center-fire cartridges which provides improved ballistic data and is void of metallic oxidizing compounds. It is comprised of a mixture of about 10-30% by weight of nitrocellulose and/or a double based propellant such as Hercules Fines, approximately 30-75% by weight of two percussion-sensitive compounds such as DDNP and tetracene, and approximately 10-30% by weight of calcium silicide. The mixture provides improved propellant ignition and non-toxic ignition products, and minimizes misfires in that it contains no hygroscopic compounds.
reason: This patent describes a specific chemical formulation (a mixture of nitrocellulose, DDNP/tetracene, and calcium silicide) to achieve non-toxic primer properties. While it combines compounds with complementary ignition characteristics, the core disclosure is a material composition rather than a causal functional mechanism that transfers across fields. The 'mechanism' is simply mixing specific chemicals to achieve desired properties, which is formulation science, not a transferable engineering principle.

abstract: In a temperature controlling method of a kitchen-heating apparatus having a temperature sensor at a certain place in the heating area, the temperature control is performed by comparing a temperature detected by the temperature sensor with a set temperature. In this case, an acceleration of the temperature ascent and descent at each certain interval is required and the temperature of the above heating portion is controlled with a duty ratio which corrects the duty ratio of the above heating portion of each interval with the acceleration of the temperature ascent and descent in the front step. In another temperature control method, the point of time where the ascent of the sensor detecting temperature due to the heater being on turns to descend together with a time lag due to the heater being off is detected, and performs the control again by turning the heater on at an earlier point of time than the point where at least the sensor detecting temperature comes down to the set value of the sensor detecting temperature.
problem: Controlling temperature in a heating apparatus to achieve faster temperature ascent/descent while preventing overshoot of the set temperature, particularly accounting for thermal lag between heater operation and sensor response.
constraint: Balancing response speed with temperature stability; the system must predict thermal behavior to avoid overshoot while achieving faster temperature changes, requiring accurate detection of inflection points and proper compensation for the time lag between heater state changes and sensor temperature response.
mechanism: Predictive thermal control using two complementary techniques: (1) acceleration-based duty ratio correction, where the duty cycle of each interval is adjusted based on the measured acceleration of temperature change to speed up response, and (2) inflection-point detection, where the system identifies the moment the temperature curve transitions from ascending to descending (due to heater being off) and uses this timing information to turn the heater back on earlier than the point where temperature reaches the set value, compensating for thermal lag.
mechanism_raw: Predictive thermal control using two complementary techniques: (1) acceleration-based duty ratio correction, where the duty cycle of each interval is adjusted based on the measured acceleration of temperature change to speed up response, and (2) inflection-point detection, where the system identifies the moment the temperature curve transitions from ascending to descending (due to heater being off) and uses this timing information to turn the heater back on earlier than the point where temperature reaches the set value, compensating for thermal lag.

abstract: A glove having a wrist portion that contains a removable protective cover over a gripping means. The cover is impermeable to contamination and protects the gripping means from exposure to any infectious substance that may come into contact with the glove during use. After use, the glove is taken off by first removing the protective cover and then using the clean gripping means to pull the glove off. If at least one glove in a pair is equipped with the protective cover of the invention and both gloves comprise gripping means, both gloves can be removed without contact by unprotected fingers with contaminated portions of either glove.
problem: Contamination of gripping surfaces during glove use and unsafe removal of contaminated gloves without exposing unprotected fingers.
constraint: The cover must be impermeable to contaminants and removable without contaminating the gripping means, while the gripping means must remain functional and clean after cover removal.
mechanism: A removable barrier isolates a functional surface from contamination during operation. After use, the barrier is detached first, revealing an uncontaminated functional surface that can engage with a contaminated item without direct contact between the user's grip and the contaminated region.
mechanism_raw: A removable impermeable protective cover shields the gripping means during use. After use, the cover is removed first, exposing a clean gripping surface that can safely pull off the contaminated glove without direct finger contact with contaminated areas.

abstract: An air bag module comprises an inflatable air bag, an inflator and a container for housing the inflator and the air bag. The container comprises an elongated reaction canister having a closed housing formed of a U-shaped body with end walls defining a rectangular top gas discharge opening. An air bag deployment chute comprises a rectangular body having a bottom gas transfer opening mating with the canister opening and a top air bag deployment opening. Cooperating flanges on the top side of the canister and on the bottom side of the chute are interengageable upon endwise sliding to assemble the chute to the canister. Surfaces on the chute and canister engage to locate the chute bottom opening in registry with the canister opening. Cooperating tabs on the canister are received in slots formed in the chute upon assembly and are deformed to lock the chute to the canister. The air bag is attached via loops to two rods which are received in closed channels formed by the cooperating flanges to secure the air bag to the module. Surfaces on the chute and canister engage to prevent endwise rod removal. The inflator has a pair of mounting lugs extending from one end and a single lug at the other end. These lugs may be formed on adapter end caps. The lugs are inserted into grooves in the canister end walls and are slid or rotated past spring barriers into mounting apertures where they are retained against removal.
problem: Securely and efficiently assembling an air bag module's components (canister, chute, inflator, air bag) without complex tools while ensuring structural integrity under deployment forces.
constraint: Balancing ease of assembly (tool-free sliding/rotation) with retention strength under high-stress deployment conditions.
mechanism: A tool-free assembly system using cooperative mechanical interfaces that allow sliding/rotational engagement to self-locate components, with deformable locking elements that transition between a low-resistance assembly state and a high-retention locked state under deployment forces. Closed-channel retention and surface geometry prevent unintended disengagement while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical interlocking via cooperating flanges that slide to engage, tabs/slots that deform to lock, and rods with loops secured in closed channels formed by the flanges. Surfaces on mating parts self-locate and prevent unintended removal.

abstract: A zoom lens barrel has at least front and rear lens groups and a linear movement guide device which guides the linear movement of the front and rear lens groups in an optical axis direction. The barrel includes a rotatable cam ring which has a first helicoid and at least one cam groove, a front lens barrel which supports the front lens group and which has a second helicoid which is engaged by the first helicoid of the cam ring. A rear lens frame which supports the rear lens group and which has at least one cam pin which can be fitted in the associated cam groove of the cam ring is provided.
problem: Achieving precise linear motion of lens groups along an optical axis for zoom functionality in a compact mechanical system.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment and smooth motion while minimizing mechanical play and space requirements.
mechanism: A motion conversion mechanism that transforms rotational input into controlled linear displacement along a defined axis through helical engagement between a rotating element and a translating component, combined with guided slot/pin interactions to maintain precise alignment and minimize play during movement.
mechanism_raw: Converting rotational motion of a cam ring into linear movement via helicoid engagement between the cam ring and front lens barrel, and cam pins/slots between the cam ring and rear lens frame.

abstract: In a power plant having a boiler for heating a fluid to form a gaseous phase, a power generator for generating electrical power from the gaseous phase, a condenser for condensing the gaseous phase after the gaseous phase has passed through the power generator, a liquid ring pump for evacuating uncondensed gaseous phase from the condenser, and a chiller for cooling seal liquid discharged from the liquid ring pump for re-use in the liquid ring pump, apparatus is provided for utilizing the heat generated during the operation of the chiller to heat a predetermined portion of the fluid supplied to the boiler, thereby reducing the amount of heat which must be provided by the boiler to form a gaseous phase of the fluid so that electricity can be generated. The efficiency of the power plant is thereby increased.
problem: Improving power plant efficiency by reducing the energy required to heat fluid to a gaseous phase in a boiler.
constraint: Managing heat transfer pathways to avoid disrupting existing cooling/condensation processes while maximizing energy recovery.
mechanism: A heat recovery system that captures thermal energy from a cooling process and redirects it to preheat a working fluid upstream of a primary heating stage, reducing the energy required for phase change by utilizing waste heat that would otherwise be rejected to the environment.
mechanism_raw: Recovering waste heat from a chiller (used to cool seal liquid in a liquid ring pump) and redirecting it to preheat boiler feed fluid, thereby reducing the boiler's energy input.

abstract: A rare earth metal-nickel hydrogen occlusive alloy ingot contains 90 vol % or more of crystals having a crystal grain size of 1 to 50 .mu.m as measured along a short axis of the crystal and 1 to 100 .mu.m as measured along a long axis of the crystal. A method for producing the rare earth metal-nickel hydrogen occlusive alloy ingot involves melting a rare earth metal-nickel alloy and uniformly solidifying the alloy melt to have a thickness of 0.1 to 20 mm under cooling conditions of a cooling rate of 10.degree. to 1000.degree. C./sec and a sub-cooling degree of 10.degree. to 500.degree. C.
problem: Producing a rare earth metal-nickel hydrogen occlusive alloy with optimized crystal grain size for hydrogen absorption/desorption performance.
constraint: Balancing cooling rate and sub-cooling to achieve uniform microstructure without introducing defects or excessive energy costs.
mechanism: A solidification control process that regulates cooling dynamics during material formation by adjusting thermal extraction rates and sub-cooling levels to produce uniform crystalline structures with specified dimensional characteristics, balancing microstructure quality against energy consumption.
mechanism_raw: Controlling solidification parameters (cooling rate of 10–1000°C/sec and sub-cooling degree of 10–500°C) during alloy melting to uniformly form crystals with specified short-axis (1–50 μm) and long-axis (1–100 μm) grain sizes.

abstract: A light-duty, multi-purpose lubricant particularly formulated for use on the diverse bearing surfaces of a bicycle chain and other similar low-speed and low-temperature mechanisms operating in a dusty environment. The lubricant comprises an insoluble soap, preferably Calcium Stearate in suspension in a volatile solvent-based solution of paraffin wax and Petrolatum. After application and evaporation of the solvent the composite dry lubricant exhibits good penetration and load bearing properties without the dirt-retaining character of greases. The undissolved particles of soap combine with dirt particles to break-down portions of the lubricant into a dry flaky dust which is sloughed off the mechanism.
problem: Lubricating low-speed, dusty mechanisms (e.g., bicycle chains) without attracting or retaining dirt that degrades performance.
constraint: Maintaining load-bearing and penetration properties of the lubricant while ensuring dirt is shed rather than retained.
mechanism: A lubrication system that applies a volatile carrier solution containing solid lubricating particles, which evaporates post-application to leave a dry film. Insoluble particulate additives interact with contaminants to form a self-shedding layer that prevents accumulation while maintaining load-bearing performance.
mechanism_raw: Using a volatile solvent-based solution of paraffin wax and petrolatum that evaporates after application, leaving a dry lubricant. Insoluble soap particles (e.g., calcium stearate) combine with dirt to form a sloughing dry dust, preventing buildup.

abstract: A resin composition comprising (A) a polyphenylene ether resin, (B) a polyolefin resin, and optionally (C) an elastomer, and (D) an aliphatic polycarboxylic acid derivative represented by the following general formula: EQU (R.sub.1 O).sub.m R(COOR.sub.2).sub.n (CORN.sub.3 R.sub.4).sub.s wherein R represents a saturated hydrocarbon group having 2 to 20 carbon atoms with a linear or branched chain; R.sub.1 represents a hydrogen atom or an alkyl, aryl, acyl or carbonyldioxy group having 1 to 10 carbon atoms; each R.sub.2 represents a hydrogen atom or an alkyl or aryl group having 1 to 20 carbon atoms; R.sub.3 and R.sub.4 each represents a hydrogen atom or an alkyl or aryl group having 1 to 10 carbon atoms; m represents a number equal to 1 or 2; (n+s) is larger than or equal to 2 and, n and s are each larger than or equal to 0; (OR.sub.1) is in an alpha or beta position with respect to a carbonyl group, and in which at least two carbonyl groups are separated by 2 to 6 carbon atoms.
problem: Incompatible or poorly blended polymer resins (e.g., polyphenylene ether and polyolefin) leading to suboptimal material properties such as heat resistance, mechanical strength, or processability.
constraint: Balancing the amount and structure of the acid derivative to avoid over-plasticization or degradation of the resin blend while maintaining thermal and mechanical stability.
mechanism: A functionalized compatibilizing agent with reactive groups is introduced between dissimilar polymer resins to enhance interfacial adhesion and reduce phase separation. The agent's functional groups interact with both resins, creating a stable blend that improves thermal and mechanical properties through molecular-level compatibility.
mechanism_raw: The aliphatic polycarboxylic acid derivative acts as a compatibilizer or coupling agent between the polyphenylene ether and polyolefin resins, enhancing interfacial adhesion and phase compatibility through its functional groups (e.g., ester, amide) interacting with both resins. This reduces phase separation and improves the overall material performance.
residual_terms: ["functionalized compatibilizing agent", "reactive groups", "interfacial adhesion", "phase separation", "molecular-level compatibility"]

abstract: Improved nautical clock apparatus and methods are provided. The nautical clock apparatus is basically comprised of a clock base and a tide state indicator attached to the base. Means are attached to the tide state indicator and to the base for causing the indicator to indicate the tide state based on a time of about 12 hours and 25.235 minutes between high tides and a continuous correction to such time which lengthens and shortens such time on a cycle whereby it is longer during one or more portions of each lunar month and shorter during one or more other portions of each lunar month.
problem: Accurately predicting and indicating tidal states over a lunar month, where the interval between high tides varies due to lunar orbital dynamics.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization with the lunar cycle while avoiding cumulative drift in the base interval, requiring precise calibration of the correction algorithm.
mechanism: A base time interval is continuously adjusted using a feedback loop that modulates the interval length according to a longer-term astronomical cycle. The system dynamically lengthens or shortens the interval to account for periodic variations in external forces, maintaining synchronization without cumulative drift.
mechanism_raw: A base time interval (12 hours 25.235 minutes) is continuously adjusted using a feedback loop that modulates the interval length on a lunar-month cycle, lengthening or shortening it to account for periodic variations in tidal forces. This creates a dynamic correction mechanism tied to a longer-term astronomical cycle.
residual_terms: ["feedback loop", "base time interval", "astronomical cycle", "cumulative drift", "dynamic correction"]

abstract: A method for processing a single food product through a food processing plant. The method comprises the steps of providing a length of casing, wherein the casing has a first end and a second end. The casing further has sufficient inherent strength as provided to support a selected food product. The first end of said casing is then capped and a food product is provided. The food product is of selected size to fill approximately three-quarters of the length of the casing. The food product is inserted into the casing through the second end and a pair of clips are provided. The first clip and the second clip are each radially receivable over the exterior surface of the casing. The casing is then clipped proximate the second end of the casing utilizing the first clip and the casing is clipped proximate the food product utilizing the second clip. The casing is then cut longitudinally between the first and second clip to create handling means. A means for transporting the food product is then provided and the food product suspended by said handling means and transported through the stages of a food processing plant.
reason: The method is highly specific to food product processing with casing and clips, lacking a generalizable causal mechanism. The steps (capping, clipping, cutting) are procedural and tied to the physical properties of food casings and handling requirements, with no clear transferable functional principle beyond the food industry.

abstract: Lubricant is applied to the rolls of the size press to lubricate the rolls prior to moving the coating heads into their coating position by substantially simultaneously applying a lubricating film to each of the rolls of the size press in stripes symmetrically positioned relative to the center line of the web passing through the size press to in stages symmetrically relative to the axis of the web substantially equally increase the surface area of the roll to which the lubricating film is applied until the full surface corresponding to the full width of the web on each of the rolls is lubricated and then a metering rod type coating head apply coating to each of the size press rolls are simultaneously moved into coating position.
problem: Uneven lubrication of size press rolls prior to coating head engagement, which could cause friction, wear, or inconsistent coating application across the web width.
constraint: Balancing the timing and symmetry of stripe expansion to avoid over-lubrication in some areas while ensuring complete coverage before coating heads are moved into position.
mechanism: Lubricant is applied in symmetrical zones that progressively expand relative to a central reference line, increasing the lubricated surface area in stages until full-width coverage is achieved. This staged application ensures uniform lubrication without disrupting the continuous movement of the substrate.
mechanism_raw: Lubricant is applied in symmetrical stripes that progressively expand relative to the web's centerline, increasing the lubricated surface area in stages until full-width coverage is achieved. This staged application ensures uniform lubrication without disrupting the web's movement.
residual_terms: ["symmetrical zones", "central reference line", "staged application", "full-width coverage", "continuous movement"]

abstract: An interleaved power converter is constructed so as to substantially equalize the power output of individual converter slices or phases. In an embodiment of the invention an interleaved power control system (110) includes a power bus (114) having a battery (116) coupled thereto and a plurality of slices (112) operating in a phased relationship with one another for causing the battery to source current to the power bus or to sink current from the power bus. Each of the slices includes an inductor (L) that is switchably coupled to the power bus and a controller (146) for controlling the switching of the inductor. The switching of the inductor is controlled as a function of (a) a difference between a magnitude of a voltage potential (V.sub.B) of the power bus and a predetermined voltage potential magnitude (Voltage Setpoint); (b) a difference between a magnitude of a current flowing through the power bus (I.sub.T) and a predetermined current magnitude (Charge Current Setpoint); and (c) a signal that indicates both of (i) a predetermined proportion of a total amount of current that the power converter system is supplying and, (ii) a magnitude of a peak current flowing through the inductor.
problem: Uneven power output or current sharing among individual converter slices in an interleaved power converter system, leading to inefficiencies or component stress.
constraint: Achieving real-time balance across slices without introducing oscillations or delays, requiring precise coordination of switching timing and feedback responsiveness.
mechanism: Each converter slice is controlled using a multi-parameter feedback loop that adjusts switching timing based on three inputs: (1) deviation of the power bus voltage from a setpoint, (2) deviation of total bus current from a charge current setpoint, and (3) peak inductor current relative to a proportion of total system current. This coordinated control equalizes power output across slices operating in a phased relationship.
mechanism_raw: Each converter slice is controlled using a feedback loop that adjusts switching based on three parameters: (1) the difference between the power bus voltage and a setpoint, (2) the difference between total bus current and a charge current setpoint, and (3) the peak inductor current relative to a proportion of total system current. This multi-parameter control equalizes power output across slices operating in a phased relationship.
residual_terms: ["multi-parameter feedback loop", "switching timing", "power bus voltage", "charge current setpoint", "peak inductor current", "phased relationship"]

abstract: A process for producing a grain-oriented electrical steel sheet having a low watt loss, in which a steel strip consisting, in wt %, of 0.8 to 4.8 Si, 0.012 to 0.050 acid-soluble Al, 0.01 or less N, and the balance consisting of Fe and unavoidable impurities is cold-rolled to a final thickness of 0.15 mm or less, primary-recrystallization annealed, applied with a annealing separator containing magnesia as a major component by electrostatic spray painting, and then final-texture annealed.
problem: Achieving low watt loss in grain-oriented electrical steel by controlling grain structure during annealing.
constraint: Balancing silicon content (0.8–4.8 wt%) and annealing steps to optimize grain structure while avoiding defects from excessive or insufficient separator coverage.
mechanism: Applying a particulate barrier layer between a deformable substrate and an annealing environment via electrostatic deposition prevents interfacial adhesion, enabling controlled recrystallization and texture development during sequential thermal processing steps to achieve desired microstructural orientation without defect formation.
mechanism_raw: Electrostatic spray application of a magnesia-based annealing separator prevents adhesion between the steel strip and the annealing environment, enabling controlled primary-recrystallization and final-texture annealing to develop the desired grain orientation without defects.

abstract: A conveying arrangement for the dosed conveyance of bulk material from one metallurgical vessel into another through a conveying channel. The conveying channel has an entry opening and a discharge opening. A conveyor worm is rotatably located in the conveying channel, extending at least from the entry opening to the discharge opening and including a first flight formed by a plurality of paddles. In order to be able to configure the conveyor worm as short as possible and to minimize gas streaming through the conveying channel, the conveyor worm, on its end associated with the discharge opening, has a second flight that is formed by a continuous helix extending at least over half a convolution.
problem: Minimizing gas streaming through a conveying channel while efficiently transporting bulk material between metallurgical vessels.
constraint: Optimizing the length of the helical flight (at least half a convolution) to balance gas sealing effectiveness against material conveyance efficiency.
mechanism: Integrating two distinct helical flight geometries on a single rotating shaft—one optimized for material transport and another for gas sealing—creates a composite conveying element that simultaneously minimizes gas leakage through a channel while maintaining bulk material throughput via differential pitch and coverage patterns.
mechanism_raw: Combining a paddle-based first flight (for material conveyance) with a continuous helical second flight (for gas sealing) on a single conveyor worm reduces gas leakage while maintaining material throughput in a compact design.

abstract: Products and methods particularly useful for activating and analyzing the nuclei and nucleic acids of human fetal red blood cells or cells found in amniotic fluid thereby facilitating prenatal screening are described. The featured products include activating egg extracts, cytostatic factor (CSF) extracts, kits containing these extracts, and a microchamber microscope slide useful in analyzing nucleus activation.
problem: Enabling prenatal screening by activating and analyzing nuclei/nucleic acids in fetal cells or amniotic fluid cells.
constraint: Ensuring the extracts effectively activate nuclei without damaging cellular integrity, preserving nucleic acid viability for accurate analysis.
mechanism: Introducing biochemical activators derived from egg cytoplasmic extracts into target cells triggers nuclear activation through cytostatic factor-mediated pathways, rendering dormant genetic material analyzable via standard detection methods without requiring mitotic progression or cellular replication.
mechanism_raw: Using egg extracts and cytostatic factor (CSF) to biochemically activate dormant nuclei in target cells, rendering them analyzable via standard techniques without requiring cell division.

abstract: The invention is directed to a table game, such as table soccer that includes a unitary ball cup. The unitary ball cup includes a quarter-sphere receiving structure, a flange and barbed tangs for releasably securing the ball cup to the game table. The function of the unitary ball cup is to put a game ball into play. The invention also enhances the aesthetics of the game table, and eases installation and assembly.
problem: Securely attaching a game ball cup to a table while enabling easy installation, removal, and aesthetic integration.
constraint: Balancing the barbed tangs' grip strength to ensure secure attachment without excessive force during installation/removal, while maintaining structural integrity under gameplay stress.
mechanism: A monolithic coupling element with resilient protrusions and a stabilizing base creates a reversible mechanical interlock: insertion forces the protrusions past a surface to engage retention features, while the base provides structural support and aesthetic continuity during dynamic loading conditions.
mechanism_raw: A unitary ball cup with barbed tangs and a flange allows releasable mechanical interlocking with the table surface: the barbed tangs grip the table when inserted, while the flange provides a stable base for ball release and aesthetic continuity.

abstract: A method for the manufacture of one-piece tape tabs to be used with disposable absorbent articles. The first step is to provide a backing substrate upon which the pressure-sensitive adhesive of the tape tab can be applied. Once the backing is provided, the pressure-sensitive adhesive is applied to regions of one side of the backing substrate. The backing substrate is then slit in a direction parallel to the machine direction forming tape tab stock that is preferably fed directly to the taper unit of the absorbent article manufacturing line. The taper unit cuts the tape tab stock comprising the pressure-sensitive adhesive into individual tape tabs, each having a fixed end and releasable end. The fixed end of each tape tab is joined to the chassis of an absorbent article by means of mechanically bonding the fixed end to the absorbent article. The mechanical bonding not only joins the fixed end of the tape tab to the absorbent article, but also forms a region on the outwardly facing surface of the fixed end of the tape tab that acts as a release surface for the pressure-sensitive adhesive. In preferred embodiments, an area of the absorbent article adjacent to the fixed end of the tape tab is also subjected to mechanical bonding. The mechanical bonding forms a region on the surface of the absorbent article that acts a release surface for the pressure-sensitive adhesive disposed on the releasable end of each tape tab.
problem: Creating a one-piece tape tab that securely bonds to an absorbent article yet allows controlled releasable fastening.
constraint: Ensuring mechanical bonding patterns do not compromise the structural integrity of the tab or article while precisely defining release zones for consistent adhesive performance.
mechanism: Creating controlled surface topography through patterned mechanical bonding at a fixed attachment zone generates defined release regions on both the tab and substrate, enabling pressure-sensitive adhesion at a separable end while maintaining structural continuity under operational stress.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical bonding of the tape tab's fixed end to the article creates a textured release surface on both the tab and the article, enabling the pressure-sensitive adhesive on the releasable end to adhere firmly but peel off cleanly when needed.

abstract: A stabilizer bar or a similar metallic tube product for vehicles, has a central portion and at least two bent portions forming legs. The bar includes a thick-walled metallic tube having in the central portion a wall thickness and outside diameter in a ratio amounting to at least 1/10. This tube has an outside wall portion bent with a restricted thinning, ranging from about 5 to 15%. The bent portions are bent with an average bending radius of curvature in the range from about 1.4 to 2.1 times the outside diameter of the tube. Apparatus and methods can manufacture stabilizer bars or similar tubular metallic products of the foregoing type. For example, a method includes the steps of fitting to a bending arm one end of the thick-walled metallic tube. An inside wall portion of the tube has a radial spacing from a bending center of curvature, no greater than the length of the bending arm. The tube and the heating zone move relatively, with the heating zone advancing along the tube. Circular movement of the bending arm is resisted with a force sufficient to displace the flexure plane (separating compression zone from tension zone) radially outward from the center of curvature and to thin the outside wall of the metallic tube by about 5 to 15%. Resistance of the circular movement can be preformed with a gear and gear rack.
problem: Controlling the bending of thick-walled metallic tubes to achieve precise wall thinning without compromising structural integrity during manufacturing of stabilizer bars or similar tubular products.
constraint: The bending radius must remain within 1.4–2.1 times the tube's outside diameter to maintain structural support while enabling the required wall thinning.
mechanism: Constraining rotational motion of a bending element while progressively applying energy input along a tubular workpiece displaces the deformation plane radially outward, causing controlled thinning of the outer wall by balancing compression and tension zones during deformation.
mechanism_raw: Resisting circular movement of the bending arm while advancing a heating zone along the tube displaces the flexure plane radially outward, causing controlled thinning of the outer wall (5-15%) by balancing compression and tension zones during deformation.

abstract: A method of flushing a closed loop hydraulic system utilizes a pair of adapters temporarily disposed between a drive motor and a pair of hoses during the flushing procedure. The adapters block communication between the hoses and the motor and cover the inlet/outlet ports of the motor. By connecting a case drain line to one of the adapters and running the engine to drive a charge pump, oil is circulated through the hose connected to that adapter, the case drain line, a case drain line filter and is returned to a tank. The case drain line is then switched to the other adapter so that oil from the charge pump is circulated through the other hose.
reason: The mechanism is highly specific to hydraulic system maintenance and lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond redirecting fluid flow in closed-loop systems.

abstract: It is an object of the present invention to provide a molded semiconductor device which allows its package to be mounted on an external circuit even if the width of the conductor of a high-frequency signal transmission line on a packaging substrate of an external circuit is large, when the molded semiconductor device is to be connected to the external circuit. A semiconductor chip 3 is mounted on a first metal member 2 by mounting solder of AuSn or the like by bonding. The semiconductor chip 3 has a high-frequency signal terminal connected to a second metal member 1 by a metal wire 4 of Au or the like by bonding. The second metal member 1 is branched in a mold area 6 into two central conductors 1a, 1b which extend out of the mold area 6. The first metal member 2 has two ground conductors 2a, 2b which are disposed one on each side of the central conductors 1a, 1b. If an existing semiconductor package has a lead pitch P and a lead width M, then the distance L.sub.2 between the ground conductors 2a, 2b may be determined by (3.times.P-M), and is typically 1.73 mm. Since the distance L.sub.2 is greater than the width B (1.3 mm) of a conductor 10 on a packaging substrate of an external circuit, the central conductors 1a, 1b can be mounted on the conductor 10 on the packaging substrate.
problem: Enabling reliable mounting of semiconductor packages on external circuits with large conductor widths while maintaining signal integrity in high-frequency applications.
constraint: The distance between ground conductors must exceed the external conductor width to accommodate varying packaging substrate dimensions without signal degradation.
mechanism: Branching a conductive member into a central conductor flanked by ground conductors, with spacing determined by lead pitch and width, ensures compatibility with external circuit conductors by spatially decoupling impedance mismatches.
mechanism_raw: Branching a metal member into central conductors flanked by ground conductors, with spacing determined by lead pitch and width (L2 = 3×P - M), ensures compatibility with external circuit conductors by spatially decoupling impedance mismatches.

abstract: A shoe construction employs straps formed of plastic material whereby separate areas of the shoe straps have different characteristics of elasticity, flexibility and rigidity. The construction of the strap provides areas connected to the shoe with greater elasticity and flexibility characteristics and a lesser rigidity characteristic than a second area of the strap that has greater rigidity characteristics and is connected to closure members of the shoe.
problem: Providing variable mechanical properties (elasticity, flexibility, rigidity) in a single strap to balance comfort and structural support in footwear or similar wearable devices.
constraint: The transition between zones must maintain structural continuity while achieving the desired balance of flexibility and rigidity for functional performance.
mechanism: Zoning a flexible strap into regions with distinct mechanical properties—greater elasticity/flexibility near attachment points and greater rigidity near closure members—by varying the material composition or structure along the strap's length.
mechanism_raw: Zoning a plastic strap into regions with distinct material characteristics—greater elasticity/flexibility near attachment points and greater rigidity near closure members—by varying the material composition or structure along the strap's length.

abstract: A rechargeable photographic camera includes an interlock circuit that automatically inhibits operation of the camera flash when the camera is mated with a charging cradle, regardless of the condition of a manual on-off flash switch. The rechargeable battery of the camera therefore is assured of receiving a full charging current even if the flash unit is left on when the camera is mated with the charging cradle.
problem: Ensuring a battery receives full charging current in a device with a manually operable peripheral function (e.g., a flash) that could otherwise drain power during charging.
constraint: The override must activate reliably based on physical mating with the cradle, independent of user input, to guarantee uninterrupted charging.
mechanism: An interlock circuit automatically disables a peripheral function when the device is physically mated with a charging cradle, overriding manual switch states to prioritize charging current delivery.
mechanism_raw: An interlock circuit automatically disables the peripheral function (flash) when the device is mated with a charging cradle, overriding manual switch states to prioritize charging current delivery.

abstract: The tanning of skins is carried out using a titanium-based compound in a percentage of 5% to 10% and especially of 6% with respect to the pelt weight of the skins; a washing treatment is carried out between a basification phase and a further tanning phase; in said washing phase a sodium (or potassium) salt is introduced in the dry state prior to the water.
problem: Achieving effective tanning of skins while controlling chemical reactions and solubility during sequential treatment phases.
constraint: Balancing the percentage of titanium compound (5-10%) and the timing of salt addition to avoid over-saturation or incomplete reactions.
mechanism: Sequencing the introduction of a chemical agent in a dry state followed by a solvent during a transitional phase between two treatment stages, enabling controlled dissolution and reaction kinetics to optimize the efficacy of a reactive compound.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a sodium/potassium salt in the dry state before water during a washing phase between basification and tanning, enabling controlled dissolution and reaction kinetics to optimize titanium-based compound efficacy.

abstract: Method for the multiple receipt and discharge of rolled sections onto a cooling plate, the method being suitable to handle simultaneously groups of two or more rolled sections (11) arriving simultaneously from an intake channel, whereby at least one multigroove equipped channel (10) receives the sections (11) simultaneously and discharges them while another group of sections (11) arrives in separate distinct grooves, such discharge taking place in cooperation with specific acceptance seatings (19) on the cooling plate (18), the cooling plate (18) advancing in each forward movement cycle by a number of acceptance seatings (19) equal to "n" times the pitch ("i") of the cooling plate (18), the number "n" being a function of the number of rolled sections arriving at the same time. Device to receive and discharge a multiple of rolled sections (11) onto the cooling plate (18), the device being suitable to handle groups of a plurality of rolled sections (11) at the same time and including a supporting bar (14) positioned above the cooling plate (18) and determining vertically a first guide groove (12a-12c) and a second guide groove (12b-12d) on each side, the guide grooves (12) being defined by panels (15) able to move perpendicularly to the supporting bar (14).
problem: Efficiently handling simultaneous groups of rolled sections arriving from an intake channel onto a cooling plate.
constraint: Coordinating panel movement and cooling plate displacement to match the number of incoming sections while maintaining structural alignment.
mechanism: Dynamically accommodating variable input quantities by synchronizing the movement of adjustable partitioning elements with a supporting structure, where the partitioning elements move perpendicular to the structure and the supporting structure advances proportionally to the input pitch.
mechanism_raw: Using multigroove channels with adjustable panels that move perpendicular to a supporting bar, synchronized with cooling plate advancement by 'n' times the pitch to dynamically accommodate variable input quantities.

abstract: A cold cathode vacuum discharge tube is used in a circuit for generating pulsed autoelectronic emissions which are particularly intense and frequent in the abnormal glow discharge region, and involve much lower current densities than predicted by the Fowler-Nordheim vacuum arc discharge region law. The discharge tube is characterized by a large electrode area at least of the cathode, and a large interelectrode gap. The electrodes are preferably spaced at least 2 cm apart in a parallel relationship. A probe may be introduced between the electrodes to reduce still further the field required to generate the emissions. In another configuration the probe forms the anode and two plates form cathodes. The circuit is driven from a direct current source of having an impedance sufficient to prevent establishment of a vacuum arc discharge.
problem: Generating intense and frequent autoelectronic emissions in the abnormal glow discharge region without forming a vacuum arc.
constraint: Balancing electrode area, interelectrode gap, and circuit impedance to maintain stable glow discharge without transitioning to arcing.
mechanism: Maintaining stable gas discharge by controlling electrode spacing and circuit impedance to suppress arcing, while optionally reducing the electric field threshold for emission initiation through localized field modification.
mechanism_raw: Employing large electrode spacing (≥2 cm) and a high-impedance DC source to suppress vacuum arc formation, while optionally using a probe to reduce the required electric field for emission initiation.

abstract: A sawing process and apparatus cuts a log longitudinally along a radius curve to produce boards. The sawing apparatus includes a continuous flexible band saw blade, provided with teeth at one or both edges. A support exposes a section of saw blade that is curved and stabilized by the use of electromagnetic fields in cooperation with rollers. The saw is then configured to make a cut of a desired thickness in a curve parallel the growth rings of a log, in an arc which minimizes the number of knot defects in the board. With each pass of the log through the saw, or vice-versa, a new arc section is cut, and the log or the saw is rotated and positioned for the next arc section cut. Plural sawing stations may be used in series, and the process may be run bi-directionally when using double-edged saw blades. Once the board sections are cut, they are flattened under pressure in a kiln. Triangular grooves may be cut prior to delivery to the kiln, and adhered together afterwards to facilitate the flattening operation for small radius boards.
problem: Cutting logs along curved paths to minimize knot defects while maintaining blade stability and precision.
constraint: Maintaining blade curvature and electromagnetic stabilization during cutting while adapting to varying log geometries and cut depths.
mechanism: Stabilizing a flexible cutting element using electromagnetic fields and mechanical supports to enable curved cuts along a predetermined path, with iterative repositioning of the workpiece or cutting element for sequential arc sections.
mechanism_raw: Stabilizing a flexible band saw blade using electromagnetic fields and rollers, enabling curved cuts parallel to growth rings, with iterative repositioning of the log or saw for sequential arc sections.

abstract: A regrind deflector for an apertured screen in a hammermill has a plate extending along substantially the entire length of the screen and having a straight surface smoothly blending to a curved surface, the straight surface beginning at an inner surface of the screen and substantially tangent thereto and extending outwardly to the curved surface which curves back inwardly to the inner surface of the screen and intersects therewith at an angle of less than 90 degrees. The number of deflectors required depends on hammermill size and operating conditions as well as characteristics of the feed material to be processed.
problem: Optimizing material flow and regrind efficiency in a hammermill with an apertured screen.
constraint: Scaling deflector quantity and geometry based on hammermill size, operating conditions, and feed material characteristics to balance flow dynamics and wear resistance.
mechanism: Redirecting material flow within a processing chamber using a shaped surface that transitions from a straight to curved profile, smoothly blending with the chamber's inner surface to redirect material inwardly at an angle less than 90°, reducing blockage and improving throughput.
mechanism_raw: Using a regrind deflector with a straight-to-curved surface transition, smoothly blending from the screen's inner surface to redirect material flow inwardly at an angle <90°, reducing blockage and improving throughput.

abstract: A linear actuator for carrying read/write heads into engagement with a recording medium includes a carriage and a subcarriage. Flexible springs mount the subcarriage to the carriage. A voice coil motor has a coil mounted on the subcarriage. Initial energization of the coil causes linear movement of the carriage flexing the springs to produce small incremental movement of the heads. Further energization of the coil causes movement of the subcarriage on the bushings to provide coarse adjustment of the actuator.
problem: Precise positioning of read/write heads relative to a recording medium requires both fine and coarse adjustments without complex or bulky systems.
constraint: Balancing fine and coarse adjustment in a single compact system without sacrificing speed or precision.
mechanism: A dual-stage actuation system employs a primary actuator to flex flexible elements between two components for fine incremental adjustments, then a secondary actuator to move a component along guided paths for larger-scale positioning, enabling precise control without complex systems.
mechanism_raw: A dual-stage actuator uses a voice coil motor to first flex flexible springs between a carriage and subcarriage for small incremental movements (fine adjustment), then energizes the coil further to move the subcarriage on bushings for larger-scale positioning (coarse adjustment).

abstract: Sheath-core bicomponent fibers comprising a core of a low-cost, high strength, thermoplastic material, preferably polypropylene, completely covered with a sheath formed preferably of plasticized cellulose acetate, ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer, polyvinyl alcohol or ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer, are produced, preferably melt blown to an average diameter of 10 microns or less, and formed into tobacco smoke filters. The resultant filters retain the desirable taste properties and processing capabilities of conventional cellulose acetate filter elements, but are substantially less expensive. Because the core material is non-absorbent, less plasticizer or additive is required for comparable properties, and a web, roving or filter made of such materials has a longer shelf-life. The very fine fibers can be formed of various cross-sections, providing higher surface area and requiring less air in the melt blowing and manufacturing processes. With sheaths of polyvinyl alcohol or ethylene-vinyl alcohol copolymer, the filter element readily disintegrates when subjected to environmental conditions leaving behind only a multiplicity of very fine, substantially unnoticeable, fibers as residue.
problem: Reducing the cost of tobacco smoke filters while maintaining taste properties, processing capabilities, and shelf-life.
constraint: Balancing cost reduction, material compatibility, and environmental disintegration without compromising filter performance.
mechanism: A composite fiber structure uses a non-absorbent, high-strength core to minimize additive requirements, while a dissolvable sheath enables functional performance and environmental disintegration through material compatibility and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A sheath-core fiber structure uses a non-absorbent, high-strength core (e.g., polypropylene) to minimize plasticizer requirements, while a dissolvable sheath (e.g., polyvinyl alcohol) enables environmental disintegration. The core provides structural integrity, and the sheath enables functional performance and disposal.

abstract: A method, apparatus, and related dye compositions for dyeing textiles which operates at atmospheric pressures, is open to the atmosphere, and does not require the steaming of the textile to set or fix the dye to the textile; specifically, a multi-temperature textile dyeing method which achieves a more complete and even dyeing of the textile in a shorter period of time.
problem: Achieving faster, more even dyeing of textiles without requiring high-pressure equipment or post-dye steaming.
constraint: Maintaining dye uniformity and fixation efficiency while eliminating pressure and steaming steps.
mechanism: A multi-stage temperature-controlled process operates at atmospheric pressure by varying temperatures during dye application, allowing penetration and fixation without post-treatment steaming through open-atmosphere conditions.
mechanism_raw: A multi-temperature dyeing process operates at atmospheric pressure by varying temperatures during dye application, allowing dye penetration and fixation without steaming. Open-atmosphere conditions reduce energy use and equipment complexity.

abstract: Method and apparatus for recovering and utilizing thermal energy from subterranean hot rock by means of a self-powered closed system which transfers heat from the hot rock to a relatively cool liquid, e.g. water, flowing in a heat-conducting pipe that extends in a loop descending from the earth's surface to and through the hot rock to a depth, e.g., in the range of 5,000 to 50,000 feet, and connects to the bottom of a heat-insulated riser in which the heated liquid flow ascends to the surface. The heated flow is processed at the surface to utilize recovered thermal energy and is cooled, and the cooled liquid is recycled to the hot rock. A plurality of descending pipe loops are disposed radially a horizontal distance away from said riser and each is connected to the riser. A manifold connecting said pipes at the surface permits rotation of the descending liquid among the pipe loops for continuous operation. The natural temperature of the subterranean hot rock increases with depth causing the temperature of the liquid in the pipes to increase as it descends. The heated flow in the riser ascends to the surface by thermo-siphon circulation which results from the hydraulic head difference between the descending higher density relatively cool liquid flow and the ascending lower density flow of heated liquid and flashed vapor. At the surface, the thermal energy of the heated flow in the riser is recovered and utilized, e.g., by heat exchange and/or by use of flashed vapor in a condensing power cycle, and the cooled liquid flow therefrom is recycled to the manifold and pipes for another heat gathering circuit.
problem: Efficiently recovering and utilizing thermal energy from subterranean hot rock without external power or complex machinery.
constraint: Sustaining natural circulation and heat transfer over extreme depths (5,000–50,000 feet) without mechanical pumps or external energy input.
mechanism: A closed-loop system uses density-driven circulation between descending cool fluid and ascending heated fluid/vapor, with radially arranged loops connected to a central riser and a rotating manifold to sustain flow among loops for continuous heat extraction.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop system uses thermo-siphon circulation driven by density differences between descending cool liquid and ascending heated liquid/vapor. Radially arranged pipe loops connected to a central riser enable continuous heat extraction, with a manifold rotating flow among loops for sustained operation.

abstract: A press machine having side frames which are effectively reinforced so as to appreciably reduce the noise generated during operation of the machine and improve the working accuracy of the machine without installing any special device on the outside thereof, significantly increasing the weight of the entire press machine, or obstructing a space between the side frames of the press machine. The side frames of the press machine are C-shaped in side view and are reinforced by at least one reinforcing member fixedly secured to each of the side frames at at least one predetermined place. The reinforcing members function to suppress the deformation of the opening of the C-shaped side frames to reduce noise and improve accuracy. The reinforcing members convert the vibrational energy of the side frames into heat energy which is then absorbed into the side frames.
problem: Reducing noise and improving working accuracy in press machines without adding external damping devices, excessive weight, or obstructing frame space.
constraint: Achieving noise reduction and accuracy improvement through structural design alone, without compromising machine weight or workspace.
mechanism: Structural reinforcement within C-shaped frames incorporates internal members that convert vibrational energy into heat, absorbed by the frame structure to reduce noise and enhance rigidity without external damping devices.
mechanism_raw: C-shaped side frames are reinforced with internal members that suppress deformation of the frame opening. These members convert vibrational energy into heat, which is absorbed by the frame structure, reducing noise and enhancing structural rigidity.

abstract: A method of determining the concentrations of at least two of plural kinds of known free acids and ions contained in a solution, wherein these known free acids and ions are known beforehand to be different from each other in temperature changes and conductivity changes which are to occur in response to a titrant. The method includes a step of generating a differential temperature curve and an electric conductivity curve, which are obtained from a thermometric titration and a conductometric titration respectively and are used complementarily so that an end point which is hardly ascertained by one method of titration may be ascertained by the other method.
problem: Determining the end point of a titration when a single method (e.g., thermometric or conductometric) cannot reliably ascertain it due to overlapping or ambiguous response curves.
constraint: The free acids and ions must exhibit distinct temperature and conductivity response profiles to ensure the methods are truly complementary.
mechanism: Combining data from two distinct measurement techniques with complementary response profiles to cross-validate and resolve ambiguities in end-point detection. The differential response curves from each technique are used synergistically, where one method compensates for the limitations of the other.
mechanism_raw: Combining complementary data from two distinct measurement techniques (thermometric and conductometric titration) to cross-validate and resolve ambiguities in end-point detection. The differential temperature curve and conductivity curve are used synergistically, where one method compensates for the limitations of the other.

abstract: The invention is a fiber-optic communication network, including a fiber-optic coupler having multiple fiber-optic ports and multiple optical transceivers which are individually connected to one of the fiber-optic pods.
