Each optical transceivers includes apparatus for transmitting to and receiving from the fiber-optic coupler, optical pulse signals in accordance with a predetermined code sequence of the transceiver, and optical amplifiers for amplifying the optical pulse signals. Each optical transceivers also includes apparatus for spectrally phase encoding/decoding, in accordance with the predetermined code sequence, optical pulse signals being transmitted to and received from its associated fiber-optic port, and apparatus for reconfiguring the code sequence in accordance with a user select signal. Each optical transceivers further includes detection apparatus for detecting a received optical pulse signal transmitted from another of the optical transceivers. The detector apparatus includes apparatus for magnifying the amplitude of the received optical pulse signal. Additionally, each of the optical transceivers includes apparatus for selecting an optical carrier center frequency at which the optical transceiver receives and transmits optical pulse signals within a predetermined frequency band in accordance with a user center frequency select signal. The different carrier center frequencies are selectable from a set of non-overlapping carrier frequency bands. This allows communications on the network between different user pairs at different carrier center frequencies.
problem: Enabling simultaneous communication between multiple user pairs in a fiber-optic network without interference, while allowing dynamic reconfiguration of communication parameters.
constraint: The carrier frequency bands must be non-overlapping to prevent interference, and the code sequences must be reconfigurable to adapt to user requirements.
mechanism: Assigning non-overlapping carrier frequency bands to different communication channels and using spectrally phase-encoded code sequences that can be dynamically reconfigured. This allows independent communication channels to coexist by separating signals in both frequency and code domains.
mechanism_raw: Assigning non-overlapping carrier frequency bands to different user pairs and using spectrally phase-encoded code sequences that can be dynamically reconfigured. This allows independent communication channels to coexist by separating signals in both frequency and code domains.
residual_terms: ["carrier frequency bands", "code sequences", "frequency and code domains"]

abstract: The present invention provides a process for the manufacture of a moulded article which comprises introducing a curable epoxy resin composition to a mould which is at a temperature high enough to initiate curing of the resin and supplying further resin under pressure to compensate for shrinkage of the composition, the epoxy resin containing coarse decorative particles therein, wherein the epoxy resin is introduced into the mould through a gap having a length which is 30 to 100% of that dimension of the moulded product being made which is adjacent to the gap and a width which is at least twice the maximum size of the decorative particles.
problem: Manufacturing molded articles with coarse decorative particles without causing blockages or defects during resin flow and curing.
constraint: The gap dimensions must be precisely scaled to the mold size and particle size to balance flow efficiency and structural integrity.
mechanism: Controlling the geometry of the material introduction gap relative to the mold dimensions and particle size. The gap length (scaled to a percentage of the adjacent mold dimension) and width (at least twice the maximum particle size) ensure unobstructed flow while preventing particle entrapment.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the geometry of the resin introduction gap relative to the mold dimensions and particle size. The gap length (30–100% of the adjacent mold dimension) and width (at least twice the maximum particle size) ensure unobstructed flow while preventing particle entrapment.

abstract: A replacement drawstring for use in garments or drawstring bags and designed to easily be threaded through the drawstring tunnel around the opening of said garment or bag. Breakably molded as a part of an aglet at one end of the drawstring is an elongated wand or bodkin to simplify threading. After threading, the wand is broken off and may be discarded.
problem: Simplifying the threading of a drawstring through a narrow tunnel in garments or bags, which is typically difficult due to the flexibility and small size of the drawstring.
constraint: The wand must be breakable at a predetermined location without damaging the drawstring or the garment during or after threading.
mechanism: Integrating a temporary, rigid guide element molded as part of the aglet at one end of the drawstring. The guide facilitates threading by providing a stiff, pointed path, and is intentionally weakened so it can be broken off and discarded after use.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a temporary, rigid wand (bodkin) molded as part of the aglet at one end of the drawstring. The wand facilitates threading by providing a stiff, pointed guide, and is intentionally weakened so it can be broken off and discarded after use.

abstract: A rotatable flow control valve mechanism is provided having a valve body having a valve chamber and straight through flow passages intersecting the valve chamber. A rotatable valve element, which may be of straight, spherical or tapered configuration, is positioned for rotation within the valve chamber and is sealed with respect to the valve body by sealing elements that surround the flow passages. The rotary valve element defines a straight through flowway that is aligned with the flow passages of the valve body in the fully open condition of the valve and permits unobstructed flow through the valve and, when the flowway has a dimension at least as great as the dimension of the flow passage, permits objects such as pigs and scrapers to pass through the valve. For flow controlling activity the rotary valve element defines flow controlling passages in the form of holes or contoured slots which intersect the flowway and the outer peripheral surface thereof and incorporates anti-cavitation and noise abatement trim. The ratio of flow control slot length to flowway diameter is in the range of from 2.0 to 1.0 to 4.0 to 1.0 and is determinative of valve diameter. The noise abatement and anti-cavitation trim may be located at least partially within the flowway as well. The rotary valve element is of sufficient diameter relative to the diameter of the flowway that rotational movement between the fully open and fully closed positions is achieved in about 90.degree.. The flow control valve may also be of the top entry variety, thus permitting it to be repairable while installed in a flow line.
problem: Designing a flow control valve that simultaneously enables precise flow regulation, noise/cavitation suppression, and the ability to pass maintenance tools (e.g., pigs or scrapers) through the valve.
constraint: The slot length-to-flowway diameter ratio and rotational range must be optimized to balance flow control precision, noise reduction, and tool passage capability.
mechanism: Using a rotary valve element with a straight-through flowway aligned with the valve body passages in the open position, combined with flow control slots whose length-to-diameter ratio determines noise and cavitation behavior. The rotational range and geometric ratios allow unobstructed passage of tools while maintaining control.
mechanism_raw: Using a rotary valve element with a straight-through flowway aligned with the valve body passages in the open position, combined with flow control slots whose length-to-diameter ratio (2.0:1 to 4.0:1) determines noise and cavitation behavior. The 90-degree rotation range and geometric ratios allow unobstructed passage of tools while maintaining control.
residual_terms: ["rotary valve element", "flow control slots", "length-to-diameter ratio", "rotational range"]

abstract: An optical shutter which responds to temperature may be caused to respond to an electrical current by placing a transparent conductor of electricity parallel to and in thermal contact with it, and by running an electrical current through the transparent conductor, such that the transparent conductor is resistively heated, and thereby heats the optical shutter. The above transparent conductor may be used simultaneously as a component of a transparent insulation. The electrical current may be controlled by a photosensor, a temperature sensor, a thermostat, and/or a manual switch.
problem: Controlling a temperature-responsive optical shutter using electrical input instead of direct thermal changes.
constraint: The transparent conductor must simultaneously function as both a heating element and a component of transparent insulation, requiring materials that balance conductivity, transparency, and thermal coupling.
mechanism: A conductive element in thermal contact with a temperature-responsive component is resistively heated by an electrical current, converting electrical energy into controlled thermal actuation of the component.
mechanism_raw: A transparent conductor is placed in thermal contact with the shutter and resistively heated by an electrical current, converting electrical energy into controlled thermal actuation of the shutter.

abstract: The delivery unit includes a transfer member in the form of two aligned plungers that act to transfer controlled amounts of lubricant from a loading chamber to a delivery chamber for delivery by air pressure to the casting apparatus. The volume of lubricant transferred is controlled by a charge control mechanism interconnecting the plungers for adjusting the distance between the plunger ends.
problem: Precisely metering and delivering controlled amounts of lubricant to a casting apparatus.
constraint: The system must maintain mechanical simplicity and alignment between plungers while allowing fine adjustment of the transferred volume.
mechanism: Two aligned displacement elements transfer material between chambers, with their relative spacing adjusted by a control mechanism to regulate the volume transferred per cycle.
mechanism_raw: Two aligned plungers transfer lubricant between chambers, with their relative spacing adjusted by a charge control mechanism to regulate the volume transferred per cycle.

abstract: A semiconductor laser device which allows high speed correction of the position of a laser spot on an optical disk is disclosed. The semiconductor laser device comprises an active layer which oscillates a laser beam when electric current is supplied thereto, and a plurality of independent electrodes for varying the current density distribution in the active layer to vary the intensity distribution of the laser beam to be emitted from an emergent face of the semiconductor laser device. With the semiconductor laser device, by supplying electric currents individually from the plurality of independent electrodes to vary the current density distribution in the active layer, the beam spot position can be corrected within the frequency bandwidth of several tens MHz by direct modulation of the semiconductor laser device. Also a driving method for the semiconductor laser device and a tracking servo system in which the semiconductor laser device is incorporated are disclosed.
problem: Correcting the position of a laser spot on an optical disk at high speed during read/write operations.
constraint: The correction must occur within a frequency bandwidth of several tens of MHz, requiring rapid and precise control of current distribution without compromising laser stability.
mechanism: Multiple independent electrodes modulate current density across an active layer, altering the emitted beam's intensity distribution to steer the spot position via direct modulation.
mechanism_raw: Multiple independent electrodes modulate current density across the laser's active layer, altering the emitted beam's intensity distribution to steer the spot position via direct modulation.

abstract: A tumbler is pivotably mounted in a sash lock housing. In an extended position, an end of the tumbler limits movement of a window sash. A post in the housing extends through an eccentric bore in the tumbler. The bore defines a shelf or protrusion that urges the tumbler into engagement with the housing, thereby preventing over-rotation of the tumbler in the extended position. A spring urges the tumbler toward the extended position and cooperates with the protrusion to urge the tumbler into engagement with the housing.
problem: Preventing over-rotation of a tumbler in a sash lock while maintaining reliable engagement with the housing.
constraint: The design must ensure the tumbler remains engaged under mechanical stress while allowing smooth pivoting and preventing unintended disengagement.
mechanism: An eccentric interface in a pivoting element interacts with a post and biasing element to create a self-engaging mechanism that limits rotation and biases the element into a stable extended position.
mechanism_raw: An eccentric bore in the tumbler interacts with a post and spring to create a self-engaging mechanism that limits rotation and biases the tumbler into a stable extended position.

abstract: The outside perimeter contact surface is molded with a continuously varying outer radius as measured relative to the axis of rotation and concentric circles of contrasting color disposed on the lateral surface of the thumbwheel with centers located at axis of rotation thereby providing visual and tactile feedback to the user of the character of output signal.
problem: Providing intuitive visual and tactile feedback to a user about the character of an output signal controlled by a thumbwheel.
constraint: The feedback must be seamlessly integrated into the thumbwheel's physical form without compromising ergonomics or signal accuracy.
mechanism: A continuously varying outer radius on a rotating control element's perimeter, combined with concentric visual indicators centered on the axis of rotation, encodes signal characteristics through tactile resistance and visual cues.
mechanism_raw: A continuously varying outer radius on the thumbwheel's perimeter, combined with concentric color bands centered on the axis of rotation, encodes signal characteristics through tactile resistance and visual cues.

abstract: A support block is attached to the lower end of a presser foot lifter shaft of a sewing maching to support two separately mounted sole plates of 9 presser foot. One of the sole plates is mechanically retractable by a pneumatic piston and cylinder combination at the option of the operator and this is accomplished by an extension of the piston rod which is mechanically connected to one of the sole plates.
problem: Need to selectively adjust or retract one of two supported components (sole plates) on a presser foot during operation while keeping the other component in a fixed supported position.
constraint: The mechanism must allow selective actuation of one component while the other remains supported and fixed, and the actuation must be operator-controlled and mechanically reliable during ongoing operations.
mechanism: Selective dual-component actuation with fixed support: one of two supported components is moved by an operator-controlled actuator while a separate support element maintains the position of the other component, enabling selective positioning of one element relative to a fixed counterpart during ongoing operations.
mechanism_raw: A pneumatic actuator (piston and cylinder) is mechanically linked via its extending rod to one of two separately mounted components. When activated, the piston rod directly moves the linked component (retraction) while a support block maintains the position of the other component. This allows operator-controlled selective positioning of one element relative to a fixed counterpart.

abstract: A segmenting warhead projectile has a fore section integral with an aft section. A mid section is disposed between the fore section and the aft section. Up range of a target, an explosive contained within the mid section is detonated separating the fore section from the aft section. When a desired separation distance is achieved, explosives contained within the fore and aft sections detonate, fragmenting the housing of the sections. The fragmentation patterns of the two sections overlap, providing a high dispersion of fragmentation segments along the line of flight compensating for range errors.
problem: Need to achieve wide fragmentation dispersion from a projectile to compensate for range errors and increase effective coverage area along the line of flight.
constraint: The timing between initial separation and subsequent fragmentation must be precisely controlled to achieve the desired separation distance before fragmentation occurs, and the fragmentation patterns must be designed to overlap for maximum dispersion coverage.
mechanism: Staged separation with timed independent fragmentation: an initial separation event divides a projectile into two sections creating a physical gap, followed by a delayed independent fragmentation event in each section, where the resulting fragmentation patterns overlap to produce a wider combined dispersion pattern than a single fragmentation event.
mechanism_raw: Staged separation and independent fragmentation: a mid-section explosive first separates the projectile into fore and aft sections, creating a physical gap. After a desired separation distance is achieved, explosives in each section independently fragment their housings. The fragmentation patterns from the two now-separated sections overlap, producing a wider combined dispersion pattern than a single fragmentation event could achieve.

abstract: Methods and apparatus for completely filling a fuel receiving tank with compressed natural gas under fast-fill conditions are provided. To achieve this, the methods and apparatus provide for supplying cool compressed natural gas to a fuel tank and methods and apparatus for drying the compressed natural gas to prevent the risk of water condensation, corrosion and icing up of equipment. Further, the delivery of dried compressed natural gas to the receiving fuel tank is carried out under conditions that expand the gas into the receiving tank thereby enabling complete filling of the tank. In another aspect, the methods and apparatus utilize a second independent compressor of lower horsepower, or an evacuator cylinder of a primary compressor, for circulating and cooling compressed natural gas into the storage tank.
problem: Need to completely fill a receiving tank with compressed gas under fast-fill conditions without causing water condensation, corrosion, or icing that would prevent complete filling or damage equipment.
constraint: The system must balance rapid filling speed with simultaneous moisture removal and temperature management, ensuring that gas expansion and active cooling work together to prevent condensation while achieving complete tank fill.
mechanism: Coordinated gas conditioning with expansion-driven cooling during transfer: gas is conditioned (dried and cooled) before delivery, then intentionally expanded into a receiving vessel during filling, where the expansion causes further cooling that enables complete filling while a secondary circulation system maintains temperature and prevents condensation.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated gas conditioning and expansion during transfer: the gas is dried and cooled before delivery, then intentionally expanded into the receiving tank during filling. The expansion causes further cooling that enables complete filling. A secondary cooling/circulation system (either a separate low-horsepower compressor or an evacuator cylinder) maintains gas temperature and circulation throughout the fast-fill process, preventing condensation and icing.

abstract: A two-part igniter for inflators used to inflate inflation devices such as air bags, lift rafts, slide chutes, and the like which includes a heterogeneous mixture of an ignition material and a consolidated mass of either i) a pyrotechnic component or ii) a composite propellant. The ignition material can be in a granular form or pelletized. The pyrotechnic component or composite propellant is provided as a pellet which is in immediate contact with the ignition material. The pyrotechnic component or composite propellant lowers the auto-ignition temperature of the two-part igniter. The two-part igniter can be used in inflators which generate all inflation gases from gas-generating compositions and in inflators which include a supply of stored pressurized inflation gases.
problem: Need to reliably ignite a pyrotechnic or propellant component in an inflator system at a controlled, lowered ignition temperature while ensuring intimate interaction between the ignition source and the main reactive material.
constraint: The two materials must be in immediate contact to achieve the lowered auto-ignition temperature, and the igniter must be compatible with both gas-generating and stored-pressure inflator systems while maintaining reliable ignition characteristics.
mechanism: Heterogeneous two-part ignition with intimate contact sensitization: an ignition material is placed in immediate physical contact with a main reactive material, forming a composite with lowered activation energy where the ignition material sensitizes the main component, enabling controlled initiation at a reduced temperature.
mechanism_raw: A heterogeneous two-part igniter where an ignition material (granular or pelletized) is placed in immediate physical contact with a consolidated pyrotechnic or propellant pellet. The intimate contact between the two materials creates a composite with a lowered auto-ignition temperature, as the ignition material sensitizes the main component. When triggered, the ignition material initiates combustion of the main propellant at a lower activation energy than either material could achieve alone.

abstract: Nitrogen-containing phenol compounds are biodegradable by a consortium of microorganisms. The consortium was isolated from waste sludge by successive subculturing into medium containing picric acid as the only carbon source. During the period of degradation, picric acid was seen to degrade to a colored intermediate which later disappeared. UV-Vis spectrometry, HPLC and GC-mass spectrophotometry showed that the entire ring structure was eventually destroyed. The consortium contains microorganisms from the genera Arthrobacter, Avrobacterium and Pseudomonas.
problem: Need to biodegrade persistent nitrogen-containing phenol compounds (such as picric acid) that cannot be broken down by any single microbial species, using a biological treatment approach.
constraint: No single microbial species can degrade the target compound alone, so a multi-species consortium is required. The enrichment process must use the target compound as the sole carbon source to select for the necessary cooperative community, and the degradation must proceed through intermediate steps to fully destroy the ring structure.
mechanism: Consortium-based biodegradation with selective enrichment: a mixed microbial community is developed by successive subculturing using the target compound as the sole carbon source, enriching for organisms that collectively degrade the compound through cooperative intermediate steps until the aromatic ring structure is fully destroyed.
mechanism_raw: Consortium-based biodegradation with selective enrichment: a mixed community of microorganisms from different genera (Arthrobacter, Avrobacterium, Pseudomonas) is developed by successive subculturing in medium where the target compound is the sole carbon source. This selective pressure enriches for organisms that can collectively degrade the compound. The consortium works cooperatively—individual species perform different steps of the degradation pathway—progressing through a colored intermediate until the entire aromatic ring structure is destroyed.

abstract: A knitting yarn feeding apparatus has a base body provided along the longitudinal direction of a front needle bed and a rear needle bed, and plural lace bars movable reciprocally on the base body in the longitudinal direction. Holding blocks are easily attached to and detached from the lace bars. Plural feeder tubes, are detachably fitted to each holding block. From the front end of the feeder tubes, knitting yarn is supplied to the knitting needles of the front needle bed, and the lapping motion is effected by the reciprocal drive of the lace bar in the longitudinal direction. Moreover, the knitting yarn feeding apparatus oscillates and displaces about a swing shaft by an oscillating mechanism provided beneath the front needle bed 11 and rear needle bed, and the front ends of the feeder tubes make a swing motion.
problem: Efficiently coordinating yarn feeding and lapping motion in knitting machinery while enabling modular component attachment/detachment.
constraint: Balancing ease of component attachment/detachment with precise mechanical synchronization of yarn feeding and lapping motion.
mechanism: A primary reciprocating element drives a secondary oscillating element through a mechanical linkage, synchronizing two distinct motions. A modular interface allows component replacement while maintaining the synchronized motion through a detachable coupling that preserves the mechanical relationship between the primary and secondary elements.
mechanism_raw: Reciprocal longitudinal movement of lace bars drives feeder tubes to perform a swing motion via an oscillating mechanism, synchronizing yarn delivery and lapping action. Holding blocks with detachable feeder tubes allow modular reconfiguration without disrupting the synchronized motion.

abstract: A loom reed with integral deflector heald frame is designed to prevent yarns from becoming entangled during the weaving of carpets and/or velvets, in a face-to-face or pile wire weaving loom. The reed includes dents or drop wires wherein at least one drop wire (3) is made up of a staggered or offset front and rear part which are parallel to each other. The offset between the two parts is in the weft insertion direction relative to the front part (8) of the drop wire (3).
problem: Preventing yarn entanglement during high-speed weaving of carpets and pile fabrics.
constraint: Maintaining structural parallelism of drop wires while introducing a geometric offset sufficient to separate yarns without disrupting loom mechanics.
mechanism: Parallel guiding elements are displaced in a direction perpendicular to their alignment to create a controlled path for adjacent materials, preventing crossing or tangling by introducing a geometric offset while maintaining structural parallelism.
mechanism_raw: Staggered or offset front and rear parts of drop wires, maintained parallel but displaced in the weft insertion direction, guide yarns along a controlled path to avoid crossing or tangling during weaving.

abstract: A method for recovering argon and hydrogen simultaneously from a feed mixture comprising argon, hydrogen, methane, nitrogen, ammonia, and moisture by passing a two stage adsorption separation (PSA). The feed gas including 4-6% hydrogen is sent to the first stage PSA to obtain a product hydrogen during the first period of adsorption step, and to obtain an intermediate product of argon and hydrogen mixture during the next period of adsorption step. The adsorbed gases are evacuated and sent to fuel gas. The intermediate product argon and hydrogen mixture is sent to the second stage adsorption bed. The effluent of adsorption step is recovered as another product hydrogen. After the adsorption step, the second stage adsorber is undergone concurrent blowdown, pressure equalization, argon recovery, argon purge, desorption production of argon, pressure equalization, pressurization with product hydrogen. Through such cyclic operation of two-stage PSA, high purity argon and hydrogen are recovered simultaneously.
problem: Separating and recovering high-purity argon and hydrogen simultaneously from a complex gas mixture.
constraint: Balancing adsorption/desorption timing and pressure cycling across two stages to achieve simultaneous high-purity recovery without cross-contamination.
mechanism: A multi-stage cyclic process sequentially processes a gas mixture, where each stage refines the output of the previous stage. Concurrent pressure and flow adjustments across stages optimize purity and recovery by synchronizing adsorption, desorption, and intermediate transfer steps.
mechanism_raw: Two-stage pressure swing adsorption (PSA) with cyclic steps: first stage produces hydrogen and an intermediate argon-hydrogen mixture, which is further processed in the second stage. Concurrent blowdown, pressure equalization, and purge steps optimize purity and recovery.

abstract: Using generated active intermediates or species simultaneously to remove water and organic compounds from the spent sulfuric acid catalyst of the alkylation of olefins and alkanes is disclosed in this invention. Over 90% water and 95% organic compounds of the spent catalyst can be removed by this invention under mild operating conditions, less than 20 atms and in the temperature range from -50.degree. to 250.degree. C. This invention provides a novel process instead of the traditional or commercial process by combustion and treatment of the spent catalyst at high temperature. It is significant to simplify comparing with the traditional process, and is a safe, simple, clean or pollutionless, and cheap one-stage process.
problem: Removing water and organic contaminants from spent sulfuric acid catalyst efficiently under mild conditions.
constraint: Achieving over 90% water and 95% organic removal at low pressure (<20 atm) and temperature (-50°C to 250°C) without compromising catalyst integrity.
mechanism: A reactive medium generates species that simultaneously interact with multiple contaminants in a single processing stage, using chemical affinity to remove distinct impurities without requiring high-energy input or separate treatment phases.
mechanism_raw: Using generated active intermediates or species to simultaneously react with and remove water and organic compounds from the catalyst in a single-stage process, avoiding high-temperature combustion.

abstract: A porch enclosure system for enclosing a porch having a framework including a pair of side members with vertical parallel slots, a top member for housing a motor mechanism and storing a plurality of glass panels and a bottom member for receiving a reciprocating shuttle. The plurality of glass panels each having a weatherseal either on the top edge of the preferred embodiment or on the lower edge on a second embodiment and slot engaging side edges. The motor mechanism is connected to the reciprocating shuttle by cables to raise and lower the shuttle. The shuttle carries the glass panels up and down in the slots where each panel is stopped by a pair of removable stops in each slot in a relationship to create an enclosure. The bottom member and side member slots cooperate to remove all or individual glass panels. The bottom member has a removable panel and the slotted side members have unslotted areas where glass panels are quickly and easily removed by removing the stops.
problem: Creating a modular porch enclosure system that allows rapid installation/removal of glass panels while maintaining weather sealing.
constraint: Balancing secure panel positioning via stops with the need for rapid removal, requiring precise alignment of slots, stops, and shuttle mechanics.
mechanism: A motorized linear actuator moves panels through a track system with adjustable positioning elements. Removable stops and access points in the track enable selective panel placement and rapid removal while maintaining alignment and structural integrity during operation.
mechanism_raw: A motor-driven reciprocating shuttle moves glass panels vertically in slotted side members, with removable stops in the slots to selectively position panels. Unslotted areas and removable bottom panels enable quick access for panel removal.

abstract: Steam quality is maintained substantially equal in the two outlet legs of a horizontal impact T junction, as the mass extraction ratio in each leg varies, by orifice plates fixed in each outlet leg and bypass pipes connected between a point upstream of the junction and down stream of the respective orifice plates.
problem: Maintaining equal steam quality in two outlet legs of a horizontal T-junction despite varying mass extraction ratios.
constraint: Balancing flow rates without disrupting the overall system pressure or causing instability in steam extraction.
mechanism: Adjustable flow restrictors and bypass pathways dynamically balance pressure and flow distribution between two outlet branches to maintain uniform quality despite varying extraction ratios.
mechanism_raw: Orifice plates in each outlet leg and bypass pipes connecting upstream and downstream of the orifice plates balance flow resistance and steam quality by dynamically adjusting pressure and flow distribution between the legs.

abstract: A diagnostic device for testing a false warp stop in an industrial loom caused by a failing or offending drop wire. The device provides a connector that is operably engaged with the warp bars of an industrial loom. When a drop wire becomes worn or pliable and bridges the warp bar to stop the loom, the connector assists to create a circuit that includes the affected warp bar, a power source, a rectifier and an indicator device. The indicator device is activated by completion of the circuit and remains actuated even after the loom is restarted. The apparatus is thus effective to help locate a failing drop wire as opposed to a drop wire that has fallen due to a slack or broken warp thread.
problem: Distinguishing between a failing drop wire (due to wear) and a drop wire that has fallen due to slack or broken warp threads in an industrial loom.
constraint: Ensuring the indicator persists post-restart to retain diagnostic information while avoiding false positives from transient circuit closures.
mechanism: A circuit-forming connector engages with structural elements to detect a specific failure mode, activating a persistent indicator that retains diagnostic state after system restart.
mechanism_raw: A connector engages with warp bars to form a circuit when a worn drop wire bridges the bar, activating an indicator that remains on even after restart, isolating the specific failure mode.

abstract: A fluorescent tube breaker apparatus includes a housing assembly which defines a bulb-receiving chamber for receiving a fluorescent tube. The housing assembly includes a first end portion, a body portion, and a second end portion. The second end portion is selectively removable and replaceable with respect to the body portion, and the body portion includes a spike-receiver aperture. A tube breaker assembly is connected to the housing assembly and includes a housing-connection portion connected to the housing assembly. A hinge portion is connected to the housing-connection portion. A lever portion is connected to the hinge portion, and a spike portion is connected to the lever portion. The spike portion projects from the lever portion and is in registration with the spike-receiver aperture of the body portion of the housing assembly. The spike portion includes a connected end which is connected to the lever portion of the tube breaker assembly. A main body of the spike portion is connected to the connected end. A free tip end is connected to the main body. A spring member is positioned between the lever portion of the tube breaker assembly and the body portion of the housing assembly. The spring member normally positions the lever portion with respect to the body portion such that the main body of the spike portion is normally positioned outside of the bulb-receiving chamber.
problem: Safely and controllably breaking fluorescent tubes within a housing without manual intervention during actuation.
constraint: Maintaining the spike in a safe, retracted position until deliberate actuation while ensuring sufficient force for reliable tube breakage.
mechanism: A resilient element biases a lever to maintain a tool in a retracted position; actuation overcomes the bias, driving the tool through an aperture to perform a controlled fracture.
mechanism_raw: A spring biases a lever to keep a spike retracted outside the chamber; actuation overcomes the spring force, driving the spike through an aperture to fracture the tube.

abstract: An improved susceptor for a crucible/die assembly for growing tubular crystalline structures by the EFG process is provided. The crucible/die assembly comprises a die having a substantially polygonally-shaped top end surface for supporting a film of silicon feed material that is replenished from a melt in the crucible through capillary action. A hollow crystalline body is grown from the film of silicon material on the top end surface of the die. The heat susceptor is made of graphite or similar material, and has a peripheral configuration similar to that of the die. Further, the upper surface of the heat susceptor has a central land and a plurality of circumferentially-spaced upwardly extending projections. The central land thermally contacts a central portion of the lower surface of the crucible/die, and the projections thermally contact the lower surface of the crucible/die at its corners, whereby a temperature distribution is provided that permits growth of hollow bodies having more nearly constant thickness walls.
problem: Achieving uniform wall thickness in hollow crystalline silicon structures grown via the EFG process.
constraint: Balancing thermal contact at central and corner regions to avoid localized overheating or underheating during crystal growth.
mechanism: A thermal contact element with spatially distributed contact points regulates heat transfer to create a controlled temperature profile, stabilizing growth conditions across central and peripheral regions.
mechanism_raw: A heat susceptor with a central land and circumferential projections thermally contacts the crucible/die at specific points, creating a controlled temperature distribution that stabilizes growth conditions.

abstract: Compact solar energy collector that incorporates into the same housing the collector itself and an accumulator in the shape of a parallelepiped and divided by walls to better withstand water pressure, being then complemented with the remaining conventional elements such as pump, differential thermostat, purges and valves, the housing being fitted with a transparent cover (3) and a heat exchanger inside (13) that is connected to the pump (1) and to the collector (6) and at the other end to valve (11) and lip (10), the rest of the interior of the housing containing insulating material. The water pumping rate is controlled by supplying the pump (1) with electrical power generated by a photovoltaic panel (2) in proportion to the intensity of available sunlight.
problem: Controlling water pumping rate in a solar collector system to match available solar energy intensity.
constraint: Integrating the pump control with the photovoltaic power source to avoid overconsumption of energy or insufficient circulation during low-light conditions.
mechanism: A direct energy-conversion device powers a fluid mover, creating a self-regulating feedback loop where energy availability proportionally controls circulation rate.
mechanism_raw: A photovoltaic panel directly powers the pump, with electrical output proportional to sunlight intensity, creating a self-regulating feedback loop between energy availability and fluid circulation rate.

abstract: An air balancing hoist is described having an axially movable drum reel supported on a ball nut and screw with a piston defining a pressure chamber containing regulated air pressure acting on one end of the drum reel to counter the unwinding force of a load supported on a cable wound on the drum reel. A centrifugal brake retards drum rotation when there is a sudden release of the load tending to cause too rapid wind up of the cable by the regulated air pressure applied on the piston.
problem: Controlling load dynamics during sudden release in a hoisting system to prevent uncontrolled cable wind-up.
constraint: Balancing regulated air pressure to maintain controlled unwinding while ensuring the centrifugal brake activates only when necessary to avoid over-braking or delayed response.
mechanism: A velocity-responsive mechanical feedback system engages a braking element when rotational speed exceeds a threshold, counteracting a regulated opposing force to maintain controlled motion during sudden load release.
mechanism_raw: A centrifugal brake automatically engages when drum rotation exceeds a threshold speed caused by sudden load release, counteracting the regulated air pressure's unwinding force through mechanical feedback based on rotational velocity.

abstract: A burner is disclosed having a burner chamber with heavily insulated heat retaining walls and a series of off center mixer tubes located at one end thereof. A uniform concentration gas/air mixture to 50% additional fuel above the lean flammability limit coming from the mixer tubes is ignited in the burner chamber due to the recirculation of combusting gas and air back to the end of the burner chamber above auto the ignition temperature for the mixture. The particular mixture disclosed utilizes 0.55-0.7 equivalence ratio.
problem: Maintaining stable combustion and uniform gas/air mixture in a burner while operating near flammability limits.
constraint: Operating within a narrow equivalence ratio range (0.55-0.7) to balance fuel efficiency, flammability safety, and recirculation-driven thermal stability.
mechanism: Recirculation of combusting gases back to the mixing region sustains auto-ignition temperature, creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop that stabilizes the flame front and ensures consistent mixture combustion.
mechanism_raw: Recirculation of combusting gases back to the mixer tube region sustains auto-ignition temperature, creating a self-reinforcing feedback loop that stabilizes the flame front and ensures consistent mixture combustion.

abstract: A silver halide light-sensitive material is disclosed. The light-sensitive material comprises a support and two or more layers. Silver halide, a reducing agent, an ethylenically unsaturated polymerizable compound or a cross-linkable polymer and a base precursor are independently contained in at least one of the layers. A layer containing the base precursor further contains a specific polyvinyl alcohol. The first embodiment of the specific polyvinyl alcohol (I) has such a chemical structure that a terminal alkyl group having 4 or more carbon atoms is attached to a polyvinyl alcohol. The second embodiment of the specific polyvinyl alcohol (II) is a block copolymer consisting of a vinyl alcohol unit and a hydrophobic unit, which is more hydrophobic than the vinyl alcohol unit. The third embodiment is a mixture of two polyvinyl alcohols (III) and (IV). The polyvinyl alcohol (III) has a saponification degree of not less than 95%. The polyvinyl alcohol (IV) has a saponification degree of less than 95% and a block character of not more than 0.5.
reason: The patent describes specific material compositions (polyvinyl alcohol variants with defined saponification degrees and block structures) rather than a causal functional mechanism. The focus is on material properties and formulations, not a process or system-level operation that produces an effect through a transferable principle.

abstract: An improved adjustable "L" side attachment strap means for attaching a face guard to a helmet comprises two straps: a main attachment strap and an adjustable retention strap, where the two straps are approximately orthogonal. The main attachment strap encircles the rear-most vertical bar of the guard, restricting the guard from moving in the fore and aft directions, while the adjustable retention strap encircles the lowest horizontal bar, of the rear section of the guard, restricting the guard from moving in the vertical direction. The adjustable retention strap fits into a notch in the main attachment strap, where both straps can be secured to the helmet by a single screw and T-Nut so that there is approximately a 90 degree angle between the straps, allowing for greater variability in fit.
problem: Achieving adjustable, multi-axis fit for a face guard on a helmet using minimal hardware.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and alignment between the straps and helmet attachment points while allowing sufficient variability in fit angles.
mechanism: Two orthogonal straps with a notch-and-screw interface allow independent adjustment in perpendicular directions while being secured by a single fastener, enabling variable fit through geometric constraint.
mechanism_raw: Two orthogonal straps with a notch-and-screw interface allow independent adjustment in perpendicular directions (fore/aft and vertical) while being secured by a single fastener, enabling variable fit through geometric constraint.

abstract: An apparatus (10) applies adhesive tape to workpieces. A nest plate (52) receives a workpiece (20). A clamp plate (53) holds the workpiece (20) relative to said nest plate (52). A stage (73) holds a leading portion of a continuous tape (12). A first mover (58) moves the nest plate (52) and the workpiece (20) relative to the stage (73) and the tape (12) to engage the workpiece (20) with the leading portion of the tape (12) and affix the leading portion of the tape (12) to the workpiece (20). A second mover (45) moves said nest plate (52), the workpiece (20) and the affixed portion of the tape (12) relative to the stage (73). A sever mechanism (62) severs the affixed portion of the tape from a remaining portion of the tape (12). The clamp plate (52) releases the workpiece (20). A third mover (87) moves the workpiece (20) and the affixed portion of the tape (12) relative to said nest plate (52) to remove the workpiece (20) from said nest plate (52).
problem: Automatically applying, severing, and removing adhesive tape from a continuous roll onto a workpiece in a repeatable process.
constraint: Synchronizing the timing and positional accuracy of the three movers to prevent collisions and ensure clean tape severance while maintaining workpiece stability throughout the process.
mechanism: Sequential actuation of three independent movers creates a phased workflow where each movement phase is mechanically decoupled but temporally coordinated to ensure material adhesion, cutting, and part ejection without interference.
mechanism_raw: Sequential actuation of three independent movers (engage, sever, remove) creates a phased workflow where each movement phase is mechanically decoupled but temporally coordinated to ensure tape adhesion, cutting, and part ejection without interference.
residual_terms: ["sequential actuation", "three independent movers", "phased workflow", "mechanically decoupled", "temporally coordinated"]

abstract: A paper-saving, trash-decreasing device for utilizing used standard-sized envelopes as either rigid, hand-held portable writing-paper or as rigid writing-paper stabilized on a desk-top by weight of the writing arm, said device being a stiff sheet sized to fit all the way into a standard-sized flap-sealed, one-end opened envelope and project therefrom, having projection affixed with a resilient friction pad positioned to contact the desk surface. This device has further paper-saving, trash-decreasing utility when it is attached by flexible bands to the hard back of a standard note-pad so that when the note-pad is placed on a desk, hard-back down, the resilient friction-pad of this device will be in contact with the desk top so as to stabilize the note-pad even when it is written on near its bottom edge. The note-pad, so mounted on this device, can be held in one hand with the device projecting below the bottom edge of the note-pad, so that the pad can be fully utilized by writing with the other hand down to its bottom edge while the writing wrist is resting on the projecting device. In both modes of use this device can simultaneousely be used to securely but removeably hold a writing instrument in readiness for immediate use.
problem: Stabilizing a writing surface (e.g., a note-pad or envelope) to enable full utilization of its usable area, particularly near edges, without requiring external supports.
constraint: Balancing portability (compact, hand-held use) with stability (sufficient friction and rigidity to prevent movement during writing).
mechanism: A rigid, projecting platform extends beyond the primary surface to provide a resting area for the user's hand while the main surface remains in contact with a supporting substrate. A friction-enhancing element positioned between the platform and the substrate generates sufficient resistance to prevent relative motion during use, stabilizing the primary surface without external supports. The platform's stiffness ensures minimal deflection under load, maintaining consistent contact pressure across the friction element.
mechanism_raw: A rigid, projecting sheet with a resilient friction pad positioned to contact a desk surface. The sheet's stiffness and friction pad create a stable base when placed on a desk, allowing the writing surface to remain fixed during use. The projection below the writing surface enables writing near the bottom edge while the wrist rests on the device.

abstract: The invention relates to a toothbrush (20), the brush head (22) of which can be removed from a brush handle (24). A threaded pin (26) can be moved to a limited extent out of the brush handle (24), counter to the action of a prestressing spring (32), when the brush head (22) is screwed onto the pin, until a stop catch (36) of the brush head (22) engages in a recess (38) of the brush handle (24) and locks the brush head in the rotational direction, while the prestressing spring (32) holds the brush head (22) under prestress against the brush handle (24). A firm connection can thus be established simply and rapidly between the brush handle and the brush head, irrespective of the shape of these parts.
problem: Establishing a firm, rapid, and repeatable connection between a brush handle and a removable brush head, regardless of part geometry.
constraint: Ensuring reliable locking under varying torque and wear conditions while allowing manual assembly without tools.
mechanism: A rotating interface between two components incorporates a threaded engagement that converts rotational motion into axial displacement. A resilient biasing element maintains continuous axial force between the components during engagement, ensuring sustained contact pressure. A mechanical interlock formed by a protruding catch on one component engaging a corresponding recess on the other prevents relative rotation once fully engaged, while the axial prestress from the biasing element keeps the interlock seated under varying torque and wear conditions.
mechanism_raw: A threaded pin moves axially against a prestressing spring when the brush head is screwed onto the handle. A stop catch on the brush head engages a recess in the handle to lock rotation, while the spring maintains axial prestress to keep the connection secure.

abstract: The invention relates to a guide bar for the saw chain of a motor-driven chain saw. The guide bar has a guide groove which extends about the periphery thereof wherein the saw chain runs. The guide groove is delimited by two side plates which are tightly connected to each other and are held at a spacing relative to each other. The side plates are also approximately coincident with each other. At least one of the side plates has a connecting part which projects in a direction toward the other side plate. This connecting part lies with a contact surface on a corresponding counter surface of the other side plate. The connecting part of a side plate extends through the guide groove up to the other side plate and there contacts with its contact surface the counter surface of the other side plate. The contact surface and the counter surface lie approximately perpendicular against each other. In this way, a simple manufacture of the guide bar and an easy assembly thereof is guaranteed.
problem: Maintaining precise spacing and alignment between two side plates in a guide bar while enabling simple manufacturing and assembly.
constraint: Achieving structural integrity and dimensional accuracy in a high-wear, dynamic environment (e.g., chain saw operation).
mechanism: A projecting feature on one plate extends through an elongated slot in a connecting element and makes contact with a reference surface on the opposing plate. The contact occurs along surfaces oriented substantially perpendicular to the slot's length, establishing a fixed spacing relationship between the plates. This geometric constraint ensures alignment is maintained during assembly and operation without requiring additional fasteners or adjustment mechanisms, while the slot accommodates manufacturing tolerances.
mechanism_raw: A connecting part on one side plate projects through the guide groove and contacts a counter surface on the opposing plate. The perpendicular contact surfaces ensure the plates remain spaced and aligned during assembly, eliminating the need for complex fastening or adjustment.

abstract: An improved pavement treatment apparatus and method are disclosed, for example for concrete and asphalt saws, which may include a vacuum apparatus for removing water and slag. The apparatus also may include an improved blade guard and a pump system for removing the collected water and slag solution.
reason: The abstract describes a collection of components (vacuum, blade guard, pump) without specifying a causal mechanism that integrates them to solve a problem beyond standard industrial practices. The focus is on features rather than a functional principle.

abstract: A shoelace cover incorporating an interchangeable fashion panel for covering the shoelaces of a gym shoe. The shoelace cover is secured to the shoe by a number of straps threaded through slots in the shoelace cover. A strap secured to each side of the gym shoe includes a loop and hook material such that the straps can be disengaged and the shoelace cover can be drawn back to expose the shoelaces of the shoe. The fashion panel is attached to the shoelace cover by a loop and hook material such that at the whim of the shoe wearer, the fashion panel can be replaced by other fashion panels to convey a fashion statement.
problem: Enabling rapid, tool-free replacement of a decorative or functional panel on a shoe while maintaining secure attachment during use.
constraint: Balancing ease of replacement with durability and resistance to accidental disengagement during movement.
mechanism: A separable attachment system uses complementary interlocking surfaces with opposing directional engagement characteristics—one surface providing high resistance to separation forces while allowing manual disengagement through peeling action. The attachment mechanism is functionally decoupled from the base mounting system, enabling independent replacement of the decorative element without disturbing the primary connection to the underlying structure. Multiple attachment points distribute loads to resist accidental disengagement during dynamic movement.
mechanism_raw: Loop-and-hook fasteners (e.g., Velcro) attach the interchangeable panel to the base cover, allowing the user to disengage and replace the panel at will. Straps with loop-and-hook material secure the cover to the shoe, decoupling the panel replacement from the shoe attachment.

abstract: Cable as suspension means for lifts. A synthetic fiber cable is connected with an elevator car or load-receiving means, with a sheathing, surrounding an outermost cable strand layer, consisting of synthetic material, preferably polyurethane, with the cable strands being twisted or laid up of individual aramide fibers, wherein each individual strand is treated with an impregnating medium for the protection of the fibers and a friction-reducing intermediate sheathing is interposed between the outermost strand layer and the inner strand layer, and in order to obtain an almost circularly shaped strand layer and increase the degree of filling of the strands, any gaps therein are augmented by filler strands.
problem: Creating a durable, efficient synthetic fiber cable for lifts that maintains structural integrity while minimizing friction and ensuring a near-circular shape.
constraint: Balancing the trade-off between high tensile strength (from aramide fibers), low friction (via intermediate sheathing), and geometric precision (via filler strands) without compromising cable flexibility or durability.
mechanism: Combining high-tensile-strength filaments with a low-friction intermediate layer and packing-fill elements to balance tensile load-bearing, internal friction reduction, and geometric form retention, while an outer protective sheath provides environmental isolation.
mechanism_raw: Combining aramide fiber strands with a friction-reducing intermediate sheathing and filler strands to balance strength, reduce internal friction, and optimize strand packing density, while an outer polyurethane sheath provides environmental protection.

abstract: An end release buckle. A buckle frame has a pivotally mounted pawl for lockingly engaging a buckle tongue. The pawl is urged to a locking position by a pawl spring and is released by an end release button having a ramp surface contacting and pivoting the pawl. A tongue ejector is slidably mounted within the frame and is normally urged over the pawl by an ejector spring holding the pawl in an unlocked position. The ejector moves apart from the pawl upon insertion of the tongue. A separate member slidably mounted within the frame is forced forwardly towards the buckle entrance by the button and the button spring upon insertion of the tongue with the member sliding beneath the locked pawl.
problem: Designing a buckle that allows easy manual release while maintaining secure locking under load.
constraint: Coordinating the forces of the pawl spring, button spring, and ejector spring to ensure reliable locking and release without jamming or unintended disengagement.
mechanism: A resilient locking element is automatically displaced by a moving actuator during insertion, which slides beneath the engaged locking element to release it, while a return spring ensures the locking element resets to an unlocked state when no insertion member is present.
mechanism_raw: A pawl-spring system is automatically disengaged by a sliding member forced forward during tongue insertion, which slides beneath the locked pawl to release it, while an ejector spring ensures the pawl returns to an unlocked state when no tongue is present.

abstract: An apparatus for feeding a workpiece in a machine tool, particularly in a sewing machine, comprises a main conveyor for longitudinally conveying the workpiece in a feeding direction and an auxiliary conveyor for transversely conveying the workpiece to align the same, which auxiliary conveyor comprises a conveying mechanism, which precedes or succeeds the main conveyor and is engageable with the workpiece as it is guided along a guideway and comprises conveying elements which are adapted to be driven to move transversely to the feeding direction. To ensure exact, simple and functionally reliable feeding, the conveying mechanism of the auxiliary conveyor is incorporated in a generally cylindrical rotor, which is rotatable about an axis of rotation, which is normal to the feeding direction and parallel to the direction of the guideway and is adapted to be driven at a surface speed which is related to the speed of travel of the main conveyor, the conveying elements of the auxiliary conveyor consists of a plurality of conveyor belts, which are regularly distributed about the axis of rotation of the rotor and are adapted to be driven by an adjusting drive independently of the rotation of the rotor.
problem: Achieving precise transverse alignment of a workpiece during longitudinal feeding in a machine tool.
constraint: Maintaining exact speed coordination between the rotor's rotation and the main conveyor's travel to avoid misalignment or disruption of the feeding process.
mechanism: A rotating cylindrical element with independently driven transport surfaces rotates at a peripheral speed synchronized to a primary transport system, enabling transverse correction of the workpiece position while maintaining continuous longitudinal feed.
mechanism_raw: A cylindrical rotor with independently driven conveyor belts rotates at a surface speed synchronized to the main conveyor, enabling transverse correction of the workpiece position while maintaining continuous longitudinal feed.

abstract: A geographical globe to provide geographical data about all of the continents so that a person can learn about those particular continents of interest. The geographical globe with an information base comprises an orb-shaped model assembly of the earth. A base member supports the orb-shaped model assembly. A structure in the base member supplies data about different countries on each continent of the earth.
reason: The patent describes a static integration of a physical globe with a data-storing base, lacking a causal mechanism for solving a functional problem beyond product assembly.

abstract: A filleting and skinning knife comprising a handle adapted to be positioned in the hand of a user. The handle has a generally longitudinal axis, and includes a front section and a rear section. An offset member is connected to the handle, and extends downwardly and below the front section of the handle. The offset member has a generally longitudinal axis which has an angular relationship to the longitudinal axis of the handle. The forward portion of the blade has the cutting edge and extends forwardly from the offset member. The blade member has a generally longitudinal axis and the forward part of this blade tapers at an angle to the rear of the blade. The rear of the blade is generally within the plane formed by the offset portion and the handle. The handle of the knife may include an electrical motor and drive linkage mechanism. The filleting knife provides a knife that is easier, safer and produces a thicker fillet.
problem: Designing a filleting knife that improves user control, safety, and fillet thickness during cutting.
constraint: Balancing the angular offset and blade taper to optimize cutting efficiency while minimizing user fatigue and the risk of slippage or excessive pressure on the fillet.
mechanism: An angularly offset blade-handle interface positions the cutting edge at a non-parallel angle relative to the handle axis, allowing the user to maintain a natural hand posture while applying controlled force, with a tapered blade rear reducing drag and improving precision.
mechanism_raw: An offset blade-handle geometry positions the cutting edge at an angle relative to the handle axis, allowing the user to maintain a natural hand posture while applying controlled force, with a tapered blade rear reducing drag and improving precision.
residual_terms: ["angularly offset blade-handle interface", "cutting edge", "tapered blade rear"]

abstract: The tool includes a linear housing, a thin circular fleshing blade with a cutting edge around its perimeter, and a guard member. The housing encompasses an air-driven or electric motor and serves as a handle. A rotary drive shaft projects at an angle from an end of the handle, and the free end of the drive shaft is equipped to have the blade mounted thereon. The guard member is mountable on the housing to cover a substantial portion of the blade. The angular displacement of the drive shaft and blade from the handle enables the user to conduct a fleshing operation with a backhand stroke that is easier to control than a forward thrust motion.
problem: Achieving controlled backhand fleshing motions that are difficult to manage with traditional forward thrust tools.
constraint: Balancing ergonomic control of the backhand stroke with the structural integrity and compactness of the angled drive shaft design.
mechanism: Angular displacement of a drive element relative to a handle enables a backhand stroke by aligning the tool's cutting action with the user's natural motion direction, reducing the need for awkward forward thrusts.
mechanism_raw: Angular displacement of the drive shaft and blade relative to the handle enables a backhand stroke by aligning the tool's cutting action with the user's natural motion direction, reducing the need for awkward forward thrusts.
residual_terms: ["angular displacement", "drive element", "handle", "backhand stroke", "cutting action", "natural motion direction"]

abstract: A multistand press or similar press facility for the forming of sheet metal parts, is provided with bedplate, press stand and several press slides driven by the press drive for tool top parts interacting with tool bottom parts. Gearings for deflecting the rotating movement of the motor drive into the upward and downward movement of the press slides are arranged between press stands which each form a pair of stands, and are disposed opposite one another, and above the introduction of force into the press slides. Two gearings are provided for the respective pair of stands of two press slides. This make it possible to drive the press slides assigned to a pair of press stands from one press stand area.
problem: Efficiently driving multiple press slides in a multistand press facility from a single press stand area without redundant drive systems.
constraint: Spatial arrangement of gearings to avoid interference while maintaining synchronized force distribution across multiple slides from a single drive source.
mechanism: Oppositely disposed gearings between paired stands, positioned above the force introduction point, allow two gearings per stand pair to transfer motor rotation into coordinated upward/downward motion of multiple slides.
mechanism_raw: Oppositely disposed gearings between paired press stands, positioned above the force introduction point, allow two gearings per stand pair to transfer motor rotation into coordinated upward/downward motion of multiple press slides.
residual_terms: ["oppositely disposed gearings", "paired stands", "force introduction point", "motor rotation", "coordinated motion", "press slides"]

abstract: A regulator for maintaining a constant partial vacuum in a region, such as in a piece of process equipment or a fume hood. The regulator includes a path, through which fluid passes from the region to the vacuum source, and a movably mounted piston having a frontal face, which is exposed to fluid in the path, and a distal face, which is exposed to a reference pressure, such as the pressure of the environment in which the equipment is located. The piston is disposed in the path so that the piston may constrict the path at a constriction point. Fluid in the path upstream of the constriction point exerts a pressure on the frontal face of the piston that tends widen the path at the constriction point. The piston is mounted so that the weight of the piston exerts a force on the piston in a direction that tends to widen the path at the constriction point. A force is exerted on the piston, preferably by a spring under compression, in a direction that tends to narrow the path at the constriction point.
problem: Maintaining a constant partial vacuum in a region despite fluctuations in fluid flow or external pressure.
constraint: Calibrating the spring force, piston weight, and fluid pressure sensitivity to achieve stable vacuum regulation without external power or complex feedback systems.
mechanism: A piston in the fluid path balances opposing forces: fluid pressure upstream widens the constriction, piston weight amplifies this widening, and a compressed spring counteracts both to narrow the path, creating a self-regulating equilibrium.
mechanism_raw: A piston in the fluid path balances opposing forces: fluid pressure upstream widens the constriction, piston weight amplifies this widening, and a compressed spring counteracts both to narrow the path, creating a self-regulating equilibrium.

abstract: Ceiling, sprinklers and sprinkler systems provide extended areas of coverage through a combination of extra large and super large orifices and deflectors which extend radial distributions with acceptable uniform average and absolute distribution densities all around and beneath the sprinklers. Described deflectors are circular and substantially flat, being essentially flat in pendent style and slightly fructoconical in upright style. Slots of alternating length are provided extending inwardly towards the center of the deflector from the circular perimeter to within no more than one-half inch and preferably no more than 0.6 of an inch from the center of the deflector. The upright sprinkler deflector includes central circular planar areas at least one inch and preferably at least 1.2 inch in diameter while the outer annular peripheral portion of such deflectors are coned back towards their supporting tubular bodies at an included cone angle of about one hundred forty degrees or more. Sprinkler systems of the present invention can be installed with closest adjoining pairs of sprinklers and branch lines spaced more than fifteen feet apart when the sprinklers are located within at least seven feet six inches and as close as only three feet to the protected area.
problem: Achieving uniform fluid distribution over extended areas with minimal sprinkler density while maintaining coverage consistency.
constraint: Optimizing slot length, cone angle, and orifice size to maximize coverage area without sacrificing uniformity or requiring excessive sprinkler density.
mechanism: Deflectors with alternating-length slots and frustoconical geometry redirect fluid flow radially, while large orifices and strategic spacing ensure overlapping spray patterns that balance average and absolute distribution densities.
mechanism_raw: Deflectors with alternating-length slots and frustoconical geometry redirect fluid flow radially, while large orifices and strategic spacing ensure overlapping spray patterns that balance average and absolute distribution densities.
residual_terms: ["deflectors", "alternating-length slots", "frustoconical geometry", "fluid flow", "orifices", "overlapping spray patterns", "distribution densities"]

abstract: An anchored cable sling system stabilizies and supports the rock formation above a mine tunnel roof. The system comprises a unitary multi-strand cable having a series of anchor collars on each end. The anchor collars include radially extending wings that: (1) cut and shread the resin grout material cartridges, (2) mix the resin grout material as the cable end is being inserted into the mine tunnel roof bore hole, and (3) center the anchor collars and cable in the bore hole. The anchor collars are oriented on the cable so that the wings thoroughly mix the resin grout material as it makes its way down the annulus between the cable and bore hole wall as the cable is being forced into the bore hole. The anchored cable sling system is installed in a mine tunnel roof without the necessity of spinning or rotating the cable ends in order to mix the resin grout material. The system may also include a structural beam support and a post-installation tensioning means.
problem: Stabilizing rock formations in mine tunnels using cable anchors without requiring rotational mixing of resin grout during installation.
constraint: Designing wing geometry and collar orientation to ensure thorough resin mixing and cable centering during linear insertion while withstanding high installation forces.
mechanism: Anchor collar wings mechanically shred and mix resin cartridges as the cable is inserted into the borehole, using the insertion force itself to drive mixing and centering without external rotation.
mechanism_raw: Anchor collar wings mechanically shred and mix resin cartridges as the cable is inserted into the borehole, using the insertion force itself to drive mixing and centering without external rotation.

abstract: A method and apparatus for heating a metallic material held by a holder such as a crucible which is positioned on a base using an electric furnace. The electric furnace includes a sleeve, an electric heating element disposed on the inner surface of the sleeve, a removable lid for covering a top opening of the sleeve and at least one handle disposed on the outer surface of the sleeve for lifting and removing the sleeve from the base or placing the sleeve on the base. When the sleeve is placed on the base enclosing the crucible, the removable lid is placed on the top opening of the sleeve and an electric current is applied to the electric heating element. Heat generated by the electric heating element and retained in the furnace melts the material contained in the crucible.
reason: The patent describes a specific furnace design with removable components but does not articulate a generalizable causal mechanism beyond modular hardware assembly. The problem (heating a crucible) and solution (removable sleeve/lid) are product-specific and lack a transferable functional principle.

abstract: This invention provides methods and diagnostic kits for determining the toxicity of a compound. The methods and diagnostic kits of this invention employ a plurality of E. coli hosts, each of which have been transformed with a DNA sequence encoding a unique stress promoter fused to a gene which encodes an assayable product. Each of these stress promoters is induced by exposure to a different type of cellular stress. The stress promoters utilized in this invention, in toto, comprises those which respond to redoxo stress, DNA stress, protein stress, energy stress and pH stress. The methods and diagnostic kits of this invention may be employed to characterize and quantify the toxicity of a compound, as well as to identify the cellular mechanism of its toxic action. The methods disclosed herein represent a more humane and economical alternative to the live animal testing currently employed to test the toxicity of new chemicals. Moreover, the methods of this invention, yield information concerning the action of a compound on a subcellular level. This information may be utilized to design antitoxins to compounds found to be toxic and in active drug design.
problem: Determining the toxicity of a compound without relying on live animal testing while capturing subcellular mechanisms of toxic action.
constraint: Each sensor must be specific to a unique stress pathway to avoid overlap, requiring precise genetic engineering and coverage of all relevant stress categories to ensure comprehensive detection.
mechanism: Deploy a distributed array of selective detectors, each tuned to a distinct physiological stress pathway, whose combined signals are aggregated to produce a comprehensive toxicity profile. Each detector responds to a unique stress modality (e.g., oxidative, genotoxic, proteotoxic, metabolic, acid-base) so that the collective output captures subcellular mechanisms of toxic action without requiring whole-organism testing.
mechanism_raw: Using a panel of genetically engineered biosensors, each responsive to a distinct cellular stress type (e.g., redox, DNA, protein, energy, pH), to collectively detect and quantify toxicity profiles. The combined output of these sensors provides a comprehensive map of a compound's toxic effects.

abstract: An effective phosphate free and organic solvent free aqueous acidic cleaner for soiled plastic surfaces is a low foaming aqueous solution or dispersion that consists essentially of water and: PA1 (A) hydroxycarboxylic and/or dicarboxylic acid or acids; PA1 (B) nonionic surfactant; and, optionally, one or more of the following: PA1 (C) salts including anions of hydroxycarboxylic and/or dicarboxylic acid or acids, preferably anions of the same acid or acids as specified for part (A); and PA1 (D) a sufficient amount of hydrotrope material to produce a stable homogeneous solution or dispersion of components (A) through (C) in water; and PA1 (E) a sufficient amount of a biocidal material to inhibit growth of any bacteria and/or fungi that may be present in the composition.
reason: The patent specifies a chemical formulation (acids, surfactants, hydrotropes) for a cleaner but does not describe a causal mechanism beyond ingredient blending. The problem (cleaning without phosphates/solvents) and solution (specific chemical ratios) are product-specific and lack a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A hand held vacuum cleaner portable by a user during use is disclosed. The vacuum cleaner has a housing defining a main inlet, an accessory inlet, an exhaust outlet, and a vacuum passageway interconnecting the inlets to the outlet. An impeller is driven by a motor to create a stream of air passing downstream selectively from the main inlet or from the accessory inlet to the exhaust outlet. A cover is sealingly and selectively mountable over the main inlet and the accessory inlet for selecting a stream of air passing downstream from one of the main inlet or the accessory inlet. Also, the vacuum cleaner may have a pair of clip assemblies and a strap. The clip assemblies are ideally selectively positionable between a retracted position flush with the contours of the main housing of the vacuum cleaner and an extended position wherein the strap may be attached to the clip assemblies. Also, the vacuum cleaner may have a power cord pivotally attached and selectively positionable relative to the housing to provide strain relief to the cord.
reason: The patent describes a vacuum cleaner with modular inlet covers and clip assemblies but does not articulate a generalizable causal mechanism. The problem (portability and airflow selection) and solution (mechanical covers/clips) are product-specific and lack a transferable functional principle.

abstract: An improved composting apparatus is provided which is particularly suited for use with straw-like materials. The composting apparatus includes a counter-rotating drum and paddle assembly which generates a plurality of air streams in which the composting material is entrained. The air streams rotate in a vortex like pattern within a chamber to mix and aerate the composting material. The composting apparatus is configurable for being driven sideways through fence gates and the like, and has an additional configuration for being towed without requiring a trailer.
problem: Efficiently mixing and aerating bulky, straw-like composting materials while enabling adaptable configurations for different operational contexts (e.g., narrow spaces, towing).
constraint: The system must balance rotational speed and airflow dynamics to maintain vortex stability while handling variable material densities and configurations, ensuring effective mixing without clogging or excessive energy use.
mechanism: Use opposing rotational elements to generate multiple concurrent airflow streams that establish a stable vortical circulation pattern within an enclosed chamber.
