The vortical motion entrains and continuously circulates bulk fibrous material through the chamber, achieving uniform mixing and aeration while adapting to variable material densities and spatial configurations without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Counter-rotating drum and paddle assembly generates multiple air streams that form a vortex-like pattern within a chamber. This vortex motion entrains and circulates the composting material, ensuring uniform mixing and aeration without manual intervention.

abstract: A razor that facilitates shaving effectiveness by effectively rendering the surface to be shaved taught. The razor comprises two or more surfaces wherein at least one of the surfaces is a cutting surface. The surfaces are inclined relative to each other, such that the skin and soft tissue in the area to be shaved is immobilized or pinched toward the cutting surface.
problem: Achieving effective shaving by ensuring the skin and soft tissue in the shaving area is immobilized or pinched toward the cutting surface to improve cutting precision.
constraint: The angle and spacing of the surfaces must balance sufficient immobilization of the skin against excessive pressure that could cause discomfort or injury.
mechanism: Two or more surfaces arranged at relative angles create a controlled immobilization or compression of flexible material toward a cutting edge. The geometric configuration ensures that movement of the cutting element over the material automatically tensions the material against the cutting surface, improving precision through mechanical constraint.
mechanism_raw: Two or more inclined surfaces relative to each other create a pinching or immobilizing action on the skin and soft tissue, directing it toward the cutting surface. The geometric arrangement of the surfaces ensures that movement of the razor over the skin automatically tensions the material being cut.

abstract: An electrochemical charge storage device (10) includes first and second electrodes (16) (22) with first and second current collectors (18) (24) respectively attached, an electrolyte (20) disposed between the electrodes and first and second metal foils (14) (26) to separate the electrodes (16) (22) from a packaging material. The packaging material consists of multilayered first and second polymeric packaging films (12) (28) which enclose the other components of the device (10), and are sealed to each other.
problem: Packaging electrochemical charge storage components (electrodes, current collectors, electrolyte) in a way that prevents damage to the internal components while maintaining electrical isolation and structural integrity.
constraint: The metal foils must be thin enough to minimize added bulk while thick enough to provide reliable separation and protection against chemical or electrical interaction with the packaging.
mechanism: Barrier layers are positioned between reactive internal components and external packaging films to prevent direct contact and interaction. The layered structure is sealed to enclose the components, with the barrier layers providing physical and electrical isolation while maintaining structural integrity of the enclosure.
mechanism_raw: Metal foils are positioned between the active electrochemical components and the polymeric packaging films to act as physical and electrical barriers. The multilayered packaging films are sealed to enclose the components, with the metal foils preventing direct contact between the reactive internal parts and the packaging material.

abstract: A masa handling apparatus for the continuous processing of masa type dough in conjunction with commonly available feed processing equipment, such as a masa extruder, an oven, or cooling apparatus. The masa handling apparatus includes a masa separator having a pair of opposed, endless belt conveyors having facing surfaces spaced apart to receive a generally continuous masa steam output from a nozzle on the masa extruder. When the masa stream moves between the conveyors, it is gripped by their facing surfaces and moved away from the nozzle at a faster speed, causing the masa to be separated into individual pieces, or logs. The masa handling apparatus can also include at least two masa hoppers fed by at least two endless belt conveyors arranged in upstream and downstream positions relative to each other. The masa is transported along the conveyors and is automatically diverted into one masa hopper by a diverter gate. The diverter gate is operated by a controller that receives a signal from a sensor sensing a masa level within an associated hopper. The masa handling apparatus can also include a self-feeding masa hopper that has an opening for receiving masa from its associated feed conveyor. The hopper has one or more rotating shafts having projections to remove gas bubbles from the masa and force it toward a pair of sheeter rollers.
problem: Continuously separating a viscous, cohesive material (masa dough) into discrete pieces during processing while maintaining consistent flow and preventing clogging in downstream equipment.
constraint: The speed differential between the conveyors and the incoming material must be precisely controlled to achieve separation without over-stretching or damaging the masa, while the diverter gate timing must synchronize with hopper capacity to avoid overflow or starvation.
mechanism: A pair of opposed conveying elements with facing surfaces spaced apart grip and transport a cohesive material stream at a higher speed than the incoming flow, inducing shear-induced separation into discrete units. A sensor-regulated routing element directs separated material into collection chambers based on fill levels, while rotating elements with projections remove entrapped gas and direct material toward shaping mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: A pair of opposed endless belt conveyors with facing surfaces spaced apart grip the masa stream and transport it at a faster speed than the incoming flow, causing shear-induced separation into individual pieces. A sensor-controlled diverter gate automatically routes material into hoppers based on fill levels, and rotating shafts with projections remove gas bubbles while forcing material toward sheeter rollers.

abstract: A composite material is disclosed along with the method of making the same. The material comprises a tough grade of cemented carbide granule dispersed with a hard brittle grade of cemented carbide granules to form a matrix. The quantity of hard, brittle cemented carbide granules is between 20% to 60% of the total composition. Such material functions to improve wear resistance without sacrificing toughness.
problem: Improving wear resistance in a composite material without sacrificing its toughness, which is critical for applications requiring both durability and impact resistance.
constraint: The volume fraction of hard, brittle granules (20–60%) must be optimized to maximize wear resistance while maintaining sufficient toughness to prevent fracture under stress.
mechanism: A composite structure comprises a continuous phase of tough, crack-resistant material interspersed with discrete hard particles. The tough phase encapsulates and supports the hard particles, which bear wear loads, while the tough phase prevents catastrophic failure by arresting crack propagation from the brittle particles.
mechanism_raw: A matrix of tough cemented carbide granules is interspersed with hard, brittle cemented carbide granules. The tough matrix provides structural support and crack resistance, while the hard granules bear the wear load. The brittle granules are encapsulated within the tough matrix, preventing catastrophic failure from their inherent brittleness.

abstract: An auger conveyor assembly for heating and feeding polymer coated powder from a powder supply assembly to a shuttle assembly for ultimate delivery to the die cavity of a compacting press. The auger conveyor has an auger tube having near its rearward end an inlet connected to the powder supply assembly and near its forward end an outlet for delivery of heated polymer coated powder to the shuttle assembly. A hollow tubular auger with flights on its exterior surface is rotatably mounted in the auger tube and is rotatable therein by a motor and gear assembly to advance the polymer coated powder. For the majority of its length the auger tube is surrounded by ceramic band heaters. An air heater is mounted on a manifold at the driven end of the auger. An air tube connected to the manifold extends through the length of the auger. The tube has perforations at the discharge end of the auger. Compressed air is heated and blown through the air tube and passes through the air tube perforations, returning to the manifold via the annular space between the air tube and the auger and exiting the manifold through a muffler to atmosphere. Heating the annular column of polymer coated powder from both the inside and outside, together with the mixing action of the auger provides better and more controlled heating of the polymer coated powder and increases throughput of the auger conveyor assembly.
problem: Efficiently heating and mixing polymer-coated powder during conveyance to a compacting press, ensuring uniform temperature distribution and preventing localized overheating or incomplete melting.
constraint: The balance between external and internal heating must prevent thermal gradients that could cause uneven melting, while the auger rotation speed must synchronize with the powder flow rate to avoid compaction or blockage.
mechanism: A rotating helical mixing element within a tubular chamber applies heat from both external and internal sources to achieve radial and axial thermal uniformity. The internal heat source delivers heated fluid through a perforated conduit, while the external source applies heat to the chamber exterior. The rotating element mixes the material while exhaust from the annular space is managed to maintain consistent flow dynamics.
mechanism_raw: The auger conveyor applies heat from both the exterior (ceramic band heaters surrounding the tube) and the interior (compressed air heated and blown through a perforated air tube within the auger). The rotating auger flights mix the powder while the dual heating sources ensure radial and axial thermal uniformity. Exhaust air from the annular space between the air tube and auger is recirculated or vented to maintain consistent flow.

abstract: An arrangement for towing a disabled ship comprising a wire on a wire drum having an axis extending in a longitudinal direction of a ship at the stern or stem of the ship, the wire being permanently connected with the ship at one end behind the drum and at the other end with a painter, the painter being a buoyant line stored in a magazine in which it is coiled without being twisted, the magazine being placed between the wire drum and a launching pipe for a buoy with which the other end of the painter is connected wherein the buoy is inflatable and connected with and encapsuled in a box in the form of a floating anchor, the box being launchably mounted in the launching pipe.
problem: Safe and reliable deployment of a buoyant towing line (painter) from a disabled ship without line twisting or entanglement during launch.
constraint: The storage and launching system must prevent twisting of the painter during deployment while maintaining buoyancy and structural integrity of the floating anchor under dynamic towing forces.
mechanism: A buoyant line is stored in a non-twisted configuration within a containment structure positioned between a tensioning element and a deployment channel. The containment structure is mounted for release, enabling controlled, twist-free deployment of the line under dynamic forces.
mechanism_raw: A buoyant painter is stored in a magazine coiled without twisting, positioned between a wire drum and a launching pipe. The buoy is encapsulated in a floating anchor box that is launchably mounted, ensuring controlled, twist-free deployment of the line when needed.

abstract: Apparatus and methods for providing at least one chemical composition useful to treat, e.g., clean, acidify, sanitize and the like, one or more pieces of equipment are provided. The present apparatus comprise a reservoir, at least one concentrate pump, a flow assembly and a control assembly. The concentrate pump or pumps are adapted to pump, at a controlled, preferably substantially continuously controlled, time rate and at a controlled time the concentrated form of a chemical composition from an associated reservoir. An important feature of the apparatus is the ability of the control assembly to, automatically and independently of the diluent (water) flow, control the time rate at which the concentrated form of the chemical composition exits the reservoir. This ability effectively enhances the utility of the present apparatus so that the apparatus may be used in widely varying applications, for example, to treat different pieces of equipment, without time consuming and imprecise manual adjustments of the concentrate pump or pumps.
problem: Precise and adaptable control of chemical concentrate delivery in mixing systems without manual adjustments, across varying applications.
constraint: The control system must maintain independent, continuous control of concentrate flow without relying on manual intervention or synchronization with the diluent flow, ensuring accuracy across variable operating conditions.
mechanism: A control system autonomously and independently modulates the delivery rate of a first fluid from a source, decoupled from the flow rate of a second fluid. This enables continuous, hands-free adjustment of mixture ratios across variable operating conditions.
mechanism_raw: A control assembly automatically and independently regulates the time rate of concentrate flow from a reservoir, decoupled from the diluent (water) flow rate. This allows consistent, hands-free adjustment of chemical composition ratios for diverse equipment treatment needs.

abstract: A method of removing harmful substances, particularly in the region of the earth's surface, wherewith an electrical voltage is applied to electrodes introduced into the soil. To remove the harmful substances, an electric field is established in situ by the electrical voltage, the intensity of which field is so great that harmful substances which are not electrokinetically transportable are broken up and/or degraded in place.
problem: In-situ degradation of harmful substances in soil that cannot be removed via electrokinetic transport.
constraint: The electric field intensity must be high enough to induce chemical breakdown of target substances but controlled to avoid unintended soil or environmental damage from excessive energy input.
mechanism: An electric field of sufficient intensity is applied through subsurface electrodes, generating localized energy that induces chemical breakdown of target substances directly at their location within a matrix, without requiring transport of the substances to a collection point.
mechanism_raw: An electric field of sufficient intensity is applied via subsurface electrodes, generating localized energy that breaks down or degrades non-electrokinetically transportable contaminants directly at their source within the soil matrix.

abstract: A bridge plate assembly for use in moving vehicles between rail cars for loading and unloading has sufficient length to span the space between adjacent rail cars and has sufficient width to accommodate vehicles of varying wheelbase. The plate assembly includes two relatively movable telescoping load bearing members, each of which includes a plurality of spaced tubular members and a support member at each end of each plate member joining the tubular members together.
problem: Spanning variable gaps between adjacent rail cars with a load-bearing surface that accommodates vehicles of differing wheelbases.
constraint: The telescoping design must balance adjustability in length with sufficient structural support to bear vehicle loads without buckling or excessive deflection under dynamic loading conditions.
mechanism: Telescoping load-bearing members composed of nested tubular sections and end support elements allow a bridge surface to extend or contract in length while maintaining structural rigidity and load distribution across a variable span under dynamic loading.
mechanism_raw: Telescoping load-bearing members composed of spaced tubular sections and end support members allow the bridge plate to extend or contract in length while maintaining structural rigidity and load distribution across the span.

abstract: A method for treating a fluid or gas containing contaminants wherein the fluid or gas is passed through a contactor having at least one reticulated foam structured fluid treatment element formed from metal particles bound together in an interconnected form and capable of promoting a reduction/oxidation reaction between the contaminants and the reticulated foam structured fluid treatment element. The metal particles employed in the fabrication of the reticulated foam structured fluid treatment element are selected from a group of particles comprising zinc, copper or combinations thereof.
problem: Removing contaminants from fluids or gases via redox reactions while maintaining efficient contact between reactants.
constraint: Balancing the foam's structural integrity and porosity to ensure sufficient surface area for reactions without impeding fluid flow or causing pressure drops.
mechanism: A porous scaffold with reactive elements provides a high-surface-area structure that enables direct redox interactions between contaminants and reactive sites, maintaining fluid flow while promoting simultaneous physical contact and chemical reactions.
mechanism_raw: A reticulated foam structure composed of interconnected metal particles (e.g., zinc, copper) provides a high-surface-area scaffold that promotes direct redox reactions between contaminants and the metal particles, enabling simultaneous physical contact and chemical interaction.

abstract: The specification describes articles which have a three-dimensional appearance even though they comprise a two-dimensional representation of an object. The effect can be achieved by coating the two-dimensional representation with a protective coating of a clear resin of clear plastics material, having a convex external surface. The articles may be buttons or jewellery that have the appearance of being made from gem stones such as opal.
problem: Creating a three-dimensional visual effect on a two-dimensional object without physical depth.
constraint: The coating must remain transparent and maintain adhesion to the underlying two-dimensional representation while achieving the desired optical distortion.
mechanism: A transparent medium with a curved surface profile modifies light paths across a planar substrate, generating differential optical cues (e.g., highlights, shadows) that the visual system interprets as three-dimensional form.
mechanism_raw: A convex clear resin coating alters light reflection and refraction across the surface, generating depth cues (e.g., highlights, shadows) that the brain interprets as three-dimensional form.

abstract: At least one comb-like divider (5) that is movable between an erect position and a lowered position is pivotably mounted on the basket. A pivot member (6) of the divider is pivoted in an elongate hole of at least one support member (8) which is fixed to the basket. At least one shaped projection (10) of the pivot member (6) is capable of slidably co-operating with a cam profile (14) of the member (8). The cam profile terminates upwardly with a recess (15) that is aligned with the elongate hole (9) and receives the shaped projection (10) when the movable divider (5) is in the erect position. The shaped projection (10) is disengageable from the recess (15) with a lifting movement of the pivot member (6) along the elongate hole (9) in such a way as to permit the movable divider (5) to rotate towards the lowered position.
problem: Adjustably positioning and locking a movable divider in a basket between an erect and lowered state.
constraint: The cam profile and recess geometry must balance ease of adjustment with secure locking in the erect position.
mechanism: A pivoting element with a shaped follower engages a contoured guide path, enabling controlled rotational adjustment of a movable component. The follower disengages from a retention feature via a lifting motion, permitting positional changes.
mechanism_raw: A pivot member with a shaped projection slides along a cam profile, allowing controlled rotation of the divider. The projection disengages from a recess via a lifting motion, enabling positional changes.

abstract: Metal carbide supported polycrystalline diamond (PCD) compacts having improved shear strength and impact resistance properties, and a method for making the same under high temperature/high pressure (HT/HP) processing conditions. A sintered polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) compact interlayer is provided to be bonded at a first interface to a sintered PCD compact layer, and at a second interface to a cemented metal carbide support layer comprising particles of a metal carbide in a binder metal. The supported compact is characterized as having a substantially uniform sweep through of the binder metal from the cemented metal carbide support layer, which sweep through bonds the sintered PCD compact layer to the sintered PCBN interlayer, and the sintered PCBN interlayer to the cemented metal carbide support layer.
problem: Improving shear strength and impact resistance in polycrystalline diamond (PCD) compacts for cutting tools.
constraint: The HT/HP processing conditions must be precisely controlled to ensure compatible sintering of PCD, PCBN, and carbide layers without degrading material properties.
mechanism: An intermediate sintered layer with enhanced diffusion properties promotes uniform binder migration between adjacent material strata, strengthening interfacial cohesion in a multi-layer composite structure.
mechanism_raw: A sintered polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) interlayer facilitates uniform binder metal diffusion between layers, creating stronger interfacial bonds between PCD and carbide support layers.

abstract: A method of producing heat exchangers that two heat exchangers are produced simultaneously in one assembly line, being provided with a tube element unit having a pair of intake/outlet portions on the both ends thereof, a pair of medium passages communicating between a pair of the intake/outlet portions and a cutting portion in a middle portion thereof, and a pair of tanks arranged on both sides of the tube element units, the tube element units being maintained by the tanks provisionally, after brazing, two heat exchangers being separated by cutting the cutting portion.
problem: Increasing production efficiency by manufacturing two heat exchangers simultaneously in a single assembly line.
constraint: The provisional support by tanks during brazing must maintain alignment and structural integrity until the cutting step.
mechanism: A shared structural element with paired functional channels enables simultaneous processing of two discrete units. Post-processing separation occurs along a predefined division region, reducing overall cycle time.
mechanism_raw: A shared tube element unit with paired intake/outlet passages and a central cutting portion allows two heat exchangers to be brazed together and then separated post-brazing, reducing cycle time.

abstract: A multipurpose device for marking a workpiece which has in combination a component for setting the reveal between an edge such as trim molding and the edge of a frame, a component for setting an angle from 0.degree. to 90.degree., a component for setting a space between two solid members such as deck boards or pickets in a picket fence, and a component for determining the center of a flat surface such as determining the center of the surface of a board between 2 parallel edges. Preferably the device is a three layer laminated square with the middle layer being larger in the overall dimensions i.e., length and width, which in a square, are the same dimension, are greater than corresponding dimensions of the two outer layers such that the middle layer extends beyond the edges of the outer layers.
problem: Combining multiple measurement functions (reveal spacing, angle setting, spacing between members, center-finding) into a single tool.
constraint: The lamination must ensure precise alignment of layers to maintain accuracy across all measurement functions while remaining compact and durable.
mechanism: A multi-layer laminated structure with differential geometric features provides distinct reference surfaces for multiple measurement operations, enabling modular access to each layer's functional geometry.
mechanism_raw: A three-layer laminated square with a larger middle layer provides distinct reference edges and surfaces for different measurements, enabling modular use of each layer's geometry.

abstract: A steel cord for the reinforcement of rubber articles exhibits largely different bending rigidities in two crossing directions at section of the cord and comprises a bundle of plural strands each being obtained by twisting 3 or more steel filaments and a wrapping filament helically wound around the bundle.
problem: Creating a reinforcement material with directionally dependent bending rigidity for applications requiring anisotropic mechanical properties.
constraint: Maintaining structural cohesion and durability while achieving the desired stiffness differential between the two crossing directions.
mechanism: A composite structure with directionally arranged components creates anisotropic stiffness by varying geometric configurations and twist orientations, producing differing bending rigidities in orthogonal directions while maintaining structural cohesion.
mechanism_raw: A steel cord with a bundle of multi-filament strands and a helically wound wrapping filament creates asymmetric stiffness by varying the geometric arrangement and twist direction of the components, causing differing bending rigidities in orthogonal directions.

abstract: Mutant tumor necrosis factor proteins which retain full or near full capability to bind to a TNFR-p75 receptor while retaining only a limited capability to bind a TNFR-p55 receptor are provided. Methods of inhibiting toxicity induced by tumor necrosis factor by treating cells or tissues having a tumor necrosis factor receptor with these mutant human tumor necrosis factor proteins are also provided. Pharmaceutical compositions and methods of inhibiting systemic tumor necrosis factor induced toxicity in a patient undergoing antitumor TNF-.alpha. therapy with these compositions are also provided.
problem: Inhibiting tumor necrosis factor (TNF) toxicity selectively without fully blocking its therapeutic activity.
constraint: Preserving sufficient binding capability to TNFR-p75 to maintain therapeutic efficacy while minimizing TNFR-p55 interaction to avoid systemic toxicity.
mechanism: Engineered binding proteins are designed to selectively modulate receptor interactions by retaining affinity for a target receptor associated with therapeutic effects while reducing interaction with a receptor linked to toxicity, decoupling beneficial and harmful signaling pathways.
mechanism_raw: Mutant TNF proteins are engineered to retain binding affinity for the TNFR-p75 receptor (associated with therapeutic effects) while reducing binding to TNFR-p55 (linked to toxicity), effectively decoupling beneficial and harmful signaling pathways.

abstract: A gaseous fuel compression and control system for gas turbine engine (30) comprises a screw compressor (10) driven by an electric motor (11) for feeding gaseous fuel to the gas turbine engine, and a modulating device (12) for modulating the rotational speed of the motor by controlling the frequency of electric power to the motor in response to sensed output power of the gas turbine engine.
problem: Dynamically controlling gaseous fuel supply to a gas turbine engine to match variable power demands while maintaining efficiency.
constraint: Achieving rapid and precise speed adjustments without causing fuel pressure fluctuations or motor instability under varying load conditions.
mechanism: A variable displacement pump coupled with a feedback control system dynamically adjusts fuel delivery by modulating pump speed in response to sensed engine output power, ensuring real-time adaptation to load requirements without pressure fluctuations.
mechanism_raw: A screw compressor driven by an electric motor is coupled with a feedback loop that modulates motor speed (via frequency control) in response to sensed engine output power, ensuring fuel delivery adapts to real-time load requirements.

abstract: This invention is directed to the production of a silver halide-containing glass article essentially free from silver halide crystals exhibiting a bright yellow coloration which strongly attenuates the transmission of ultraviolet radiation and radiation having a wavelength up to about 450 nm, said article having an integral reduced surface layer thereon, the depth of that layer being sufficient to effectively prevent the transmission therethrough of ultraviolet radiation and radiation having a wavelength up to about 450 nm.
problem: Producing a glass article that selectively attenuates ultraviolet and visible light (up to ~450 nm) without forming silver halide crystals that cause unwanted coloration.
constraint: Optimizing the depth and composition of the reduced layer to maximize UV/visible light attenuation without compromising the glass's transparency or mechanical strength.
mechanism: A chemically modified surface layer with depth-dependent composition creates an absorption zone that selectively attenuates harmful wavelengths while preserving bulk material transparency and mechanical integrity through controlled reduction processes.
mechanism_raw: An integral reduced surface layer is formed on the glass through controlled chemical reduction, creating a depth-dependent absorption zone that blocks harmful wavelengths while maintaining structural integrity and clarity in the bulk material.

abstract: A steam desuperheater has a body extending into a steam line and is operated by a controlled variable water pressure source responding to the amount of superheat in the steam line. As the pressure of the supply line is increased above a predetermined level greater than the steam pressure in the steam line, a piston moves up against a calibrated spring to progressively uncover a plurality of spray openings so that increasing water pressure results in an increasingly greater amount of water sprayed into the steam line.
problem: Controlling the amount of water sprayed into a steam line based on the level of superheat in the steam.
constraint: The spring calibration and pressure differential must balance to ensure progressive uncovering of spray openings without overcompensating or undercompensating for superheat levels.
mechanism: A pressure-responsive element moves against a resilient biasing element to progressively expose dispensing openings, creating a feedback loop where increasing input pressure results in proportionally greater fluid delivery into a process stream.
mechanism_raw: A pressure-responsive piston moves against a calibrated spring to progressively uncover spray openings, creating a feedback loop where increasing water pressure results in proportionally greater water spray into the steam line.

abstract: 1,1-dimethyl-2,3-benzo-1-sila-2-cyclobutene was synthesized from 2-bromobenzyl bromide through a modified Grignard procedure, which resulted in a higher (41%) than literature reported yield (35%). An alternative approach with a much less costly 2-chlorobenzyl chloride as starting material is also disclosed. In addition, new di-benzosilacyclobutene compounds were synthesized with our modified Grignard procedure. The compounds are useful as coating materials for surfaces, and when applied to metallic surfaces, can be used neat.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical synthesis method (modified Grignard procedure) to improve yield and reduce cost for a particular compound. While the problem is optimization, the mechanism is tightly tied to the chemical process and starting materials, lacking a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: Insect repellent compositions are provided comprising mixtures of: PA1 (a) from about 5 to about 95%, by weight, of an N-alkyl neoalkanamide having the formula: ##STR1## wherein R.sub.1 R.sub.2, and R.sub.3 are alkyl groups and the sum of the carbon atoms therein is from 6 to 12, and wherein R.sub.4 is either a hydrogen atom or an alkyl group having one to two carbon atoms, and wherein R.sub.5 is methyl, ethyl, or propyl; and PA1 (b) from about 5 to about 95%, by weight, of N,N-diethyl-meta-toluamide (DEET). Preferred repellent composition comprise mixtures of N-methyl neodecanamide (MNDA) and DEET which provide synergistic repellency effects against a variety of insects including cockroaches, silverfish, mosquitoes, flies and ants. The repellent compositions may be applied directly to surfaces to be treated or they may be incorporated in detergent compositions such as laundry detergents, floor and wall cleaners, rug cleaners and shampoos, hair shampoos and liquid and bar soaps.
problem: Creating an insect repellent composition with enhanced effectiveness against a variety of insects.
constraint: The ratio of the two compounds must remain within 5-95% by weight to maintain synergistic effects without antagonistic interactions.
mechanism: Combining two active agents in a controlled weight ratio to achieve a synergistic effect, where the combined action exceeds the sum of individual effects, with the ratio constrained to maintain efficacy without antagonistic interactions.
mechanism_raw: Combining two active compounds (e.g., N-methyl neodecanamide and DEET) in specific weight ratios to achieve a synergistic repellency effect, where the combined action exceeds the sum of individual effects.

abstract: A hands and arms cleaning apparatus comprised of a housing receiving a water supply line therein and having a water drain secured thereto. A pair of hand receiving holes are disposed within a front surface of the housing. A plurality of water sprayers are secured to an interior of an upper surface of the housing. The plurality of water sprayers are each coupled with the water supply line. A plurality of brushing members are rotatably positioned within a hollow interior of the housing.
problem: Effectively cleaning hands and arms using a single apparatus.
constraint: The spatial arrangement of sprayers and brushes must avoid interference while ensuring full coverage of the hands and arms within the confined housing.
mechanism: Integrating fluid delivery elements and mechanical scrubbing elements within a shared confined space, where the fluid delivery provides rinsing while the scrubbing elements mechanically agitate, enabling simultaneous or sequential cleaning actions without mutual interference.
mechanism_raw: Integrating water sprayers and rotating brushing members within a shared housing, where the sprayers provide rinsing while the brushes mechanically scrub, enabling simultaneous or sequential cleaning actions.
residual_terms: ["fluid delivery elements", "mechanical scrubbing elements", "shared confined space", "mutual interference"]

abstract: A method of photoforming a three-dimensional object, comprising the steps of transferring onto a work table a semi-hardened layer of a photohardenable resin separably supported on a base film, photoforming a hardened layer by exposing the semi-hardened layer, the hardened layer being laminated on a previously hardened layer to photoform the three-dimensional object, and when the hardened layer is photoformed, photoforming a first-region hardened layer forming the three-dimensional object and also a second region hardened layer that is adjacent to the first-region hardened layer through a predetermined space, the first-region hardened layer being supported through a portion of the semi-hardened layer by the second-region hardened layer. An apparatus for photoforming a three-dimensional object, comprising a transfer unit for transferring onto a work table a semi-hardened layer of a photohardenable resin separably supported on a base film, and an irradiation unit for photoforming a hardened layer by exposing the semi-hardened layer, the hardened layer being laminated on a previously hardened layer to photoform the three-dimensional object.
problem: Forming a three-dimensional object with structural support during layered photoforming processes.
constraint: The spacing between the first and second regions must be precisely controlled to ensure support during formation while enabling clean separation post-processing.
mechanism: Creating a primary hardened structure supported by an adjacent hardened region through an intermediate semi-hardened layer, allowing temporary structural integrity during formation while maintaining a separable interface for post-processing removal.
mechanism_raw: Creating a first-region hardened layer supported by an adjacent second-region hardened layer through a semi-hardened layer, allowing temporary structural integrity during lamination while maintaining a separable interface for later removal.

abstract: A method for conditioning sludge is disclosed which includes adding a treatment material to the sludge, the treatment material including pieces of cellulose with a hydrophobic agent applied thereto. A method for conditioning sludge is disclosed which includes adding a treatment material to the sludge, and the treatment material including pieces of cellulose with wax applied thereto, the pieces of cellulose ranging in size between one-eighth inch and seven-sixteenths inch in a largest dimension and having about 0.5% to about 3% wax by weight, and at least ninety percent of surface area of the pieces of cellulose covered with wax. A method for conditioning sludge is disclosed which includes forming a slurry of sludge and pieces of cellulose treated with a hydrophobic agent, introducing the slurry into a sludge feed stream producing a secondary stream for feeding into sludge dewatering apparatus, and feeding the secondary stream into sludge dewatering apparatus to dewater sludge in the sludge dewatering apparatus.
problem: Improving the efficiency of sludge dewatering by enhancing separation of water from solids.
constraint: Cellulose size (0.125–0.4375 inches) and wax coverage (0.5–3% by weight, ≥90% surface coverage) must balance absorption capacity, structural integrity, and flow dynamics to avoid clogging or ineffective separation.
mechanism: Introducing treated fibrous elements with controlled hydrophobic surface coverage into a slurry to form a porous matrix that promotes liquid drainage while retaining solids, enabling mechanical dewatering.
mechanism_raw: Introducing cellulose pieces treated with a hydrophobic agent (e.g., wax) into sludge to create a porous, water-absorbing matrix that facilitates drainage while retaining solids, enabling effective dewatering in mechanical apparatus.

abstract: A device for cleaning the ducts of medical instruments for internal investigation or sample-taking, the device comprising an elongate cylindrical element and a brush provided at a first end of said element, the brush comprising substantially radial brushes mounted on a longitudinal spine. The device includes a brush support member constituted by a helically wound wire whose turns define a channel suitable for receiving the spine of the brush and having a portion of length substantially equal to the length of the brush along which the turns are spaced apart axially so as to allow the bristles of the brush to pass between them.
problem: Cleaning narrow, elongated internal surfaces of medical instrument ducts without damaging the duct walls or failing to reach confined spaces.
constraint: The axial spacing of the helical wire turns must be sufficient to permit bristle passage while ensuring the brush remains centered and applies consistent pressure against the duct surface.
mechanism: Mounting flexible contact elements on a longitudinal support and using a helical guide structure with axially spaced turns to allow passage of the contact elements while maintaining consistent radial pressure against internal surfaces during movement.
mechanism_raw: A brush with radially mounted bristles on a longitudinal spine is supported by a helically wound wire with axially spaced turns, allowing the bristles to pass through gaps while maintaining contact with duct walls during movement.
residual_terms: ["flexible contact elements", "longitudinal support", "helical guide structure", "axial spacing", "radial pressure"]

abstract: A fastening device molded of a synthetic resin material and adapted to be engaged with a large number of loops on one surface of a fastener part of a mating member includes a base member having on its one surface a large number of hooks integrally molded with the base member and arranged in a plurality of rows. The hooks in each hook row generally have the same hook direction aligned with an axis of the hook row, and the hooks in one hook row and the hooks in an adjacent hook row do not always have the same hook direction. At least one hook in each hook row which is adjacent to a peripheral edge of the base member have a hook direction facing outwardly away from the peripheral edge. With this arrangement, the hooks located adjacent to the peripheral edge are capable of withstand undue force tending to fatigue and eventually break the hooks.
problem: Preventing mechanical failure (fatigue/breakage) of hooks at the peripheral edges of a synthetic resin fastening device under repeated engagement forces.
constraint: Hook directions in adjacent rows must vary to avoid uniform stress alignment, while maintaining sufficient interlocking capability across the entire fastening surface.
mechanism: Orienting interlocking elements near a peripheral edge to face outwardly away from the edge, redistributing stress concentrations and reducing localized strain during repeated engagement or disengagement cycles.
mechanism_raw: Orienting hooks adjacent to the peripheral edge to face outwardly away from the edge, redistributing stress concentrations and reducing localized strain during engagement or disengagement cycles.

abstract: Television schedule information transmission and utilization systems (50A-50D) transmit TV schedule data and associated network control messages provided by computer (54) as packets via the Video Blanking Interval (VBI) lines in the TV signal from various television program providers (51). This data is acquired by regional data processing systems and forwarded by the regional data processing systems to subscriber units (52) and used to construct an internal database. This internal database can be accessed by the subscriber unit (52) to display a TV schedule for the channels that are received by the user's TV.
problem: Transmitting TV schedule data to subscriber units without requiring dedicated bandwidth or disrupting existing television signal content.
constraint: Data transmission must fit within the limited capacity of VBI lines while ensuring compatibility with existing TV signal infrastructure and avoiding interference with primary video content.
mechanism: Embedding data packets within unused intervals of a standard broadcast signal to relay information to remote units without requiring dedicated bandwidth or disrupting primary content.
mechanism_raw: Embedding schedule data and control messages as packets within the Video Blanking Interval (VBI) lines of standard TV signals, leveraging unused bandwidth in the signal to relay information to regional processors and subscribers.

abstract: In a method for joining a thread a spindle rotor with hollow spindle shaft is rotatably supported on a machine frame. A radially outwardly extending yarn guide channel is connected to the hollow spindle shaft. Two spinning devices with upwardly open spinning rotors are supported above the spindle rotor symmetrical to the central axis of the spindle rotor. A centering point is positioned on an extension of the central axis of the spindle rotor. A spun yarn is spun in each spinning device from dissolved fiber material and led upwardly away from the spinning rotors, reversed in their direction of movement by 180.degree., and introduced into the hollow spindle axle. The spun yarns form a yarn balloon between the yarn guide channel and the centering point, and twisted yarn is removed from the centering point. The dissolved fiber material is fed to the spinning devices through the yarn balloon. For each spinning rotor a joining thread is threaded with one end into the hollow spindle axle and with the other into the spinning rotor. A thread loop is generated from each joining thread between the and guided such that a first thread branch is fed into the spinning rotor and the second thread branch is removed through the hollow spindle axle until the thread loop is resolved, the direction of movement of the first thread branch is reversed, and the joining thread is removed through the hollow spindle axle.
problem: Joining threads efficiently in a textile spinning process while maintaining consistent tension and avoiding thread breakage during the joining operation.
constraint: The rotational speed of the spindle and spinning devices, along with the thread path geometry, must be synchronized to maintain tension equilibrium and prevent slack or over-tension during the joining process.
mechanism: Forming a tensioned loop between rotating elements by twisting and reversing thread direction to create a joined yarn, with synchronized feed and removal paths ensuring tension balance during the joining operation.
mechanism_raw: Creating a yarn balloon between a rotating spindle and spinning devices, where threads are twisted and reversed in direction to form a loop that is resolved into a joined yarn, with controlled feed and removal paths ensuring tension balance.
residual_terms: ["tensioned loop", "rotating elements", "thread direction reversal", "joined yarn", "tension balance", "synchronized feed"]

abstract: A multilayer ceramic circuit substrate having therein internal conductor patterns comprising W and/or Mo as a main component and surface conductor patterns comprising Cu as a main component formed onto a surface layer of the multilayer ceramic circuit substrate, wherein an intermediate metal layer comprising 40 to 90 wt. % of W and/or Mo and 10 to 60 wt. % of at least one element selected from the group consisting of Ir, Pt, Ti, and Cr is formed in through-holes of the surface layer and on parts of the surface layer in the vicinity of the through holes on the surface layer, whereby the internal conductor patterns and the surface conductor patterns are electrically connected through the intermediate metal layer. The alumina multilayer ceramic circuit substrate provides an excellent bonding strength and electrical conductivity between the internal conductors and the surface conductors and enables high precision wiring and miniaturization of an electronic circuit part.
problem: Achieving reliable electrical and mechanical connection between internal and surface conductors in a multilayer ceramic substrate using dissimilar materials (W/Mo and Cu).
constraint: The composition must balance bonding strength and electrical conductivity while maintaining compatibility with both W/Mo and Cu systems.
mechanism: A compositionally graded intermediate layer with a controlled elemental ratio is formed between two dissimilar conductive regions, serving as a diffusion barrier and adhesion promoter to bridge internal and surface conductors while balancing bonding strength and electrical conductivity.
mechanism_raw: An intermediate metal layer with a composition gradient (40-90% W/Mo and 10-60% Ir/Pt/Ti/Cr) is formed in through-holes and adjacent surface regions, acting as a diffusion barrier and adhesion promoter to bridge the internal and surface conductors.

abstract: A method and apparatus for precision machining a surface suitable for use as a data recorder, using a scanning probe microscope (SPM) capable of observing an electrically insulating surface. The SPM includes a probe which comprises a tip having a pointed end, and also including a conductive layer applied on a surface of the tip. The tip is brought into close proximity to the surface which is to be machined and a machining voltage is applied between the tip and the surface to machine the surface.
problem: Precision machining of electrically insulating surfaces for data recording applications where conventional tools lack resolution or conductivity.
constraint: The conductive layer on the tip must maintain electrical contact without compromising the SPM's resolution or the surface's integrity during machining.
mechanism: A conductive probe tip applies a localized voltage to an insulating surface, enabling controlled material removal through electrochemical or field-assisted processes at the nanoscale while maintaining electrical contact and surface integrity.
mechanism_raw: A conductive SPM tip applies a localized machining voltage to the insulating surface, enabling controlled material removal through electrochemical or field-assisted processes at the nanoscale.
residual_terms: ["conductive probe tip", "localized voltage", "electrochemical or field-assisted processes", "nanoscale"]

abstract: A yarn heating apparatus for use in a yarn false twisting machine, which has an axial channel in which the yarn advances along a zigzagged path. To guide the yarn in the axial channel, yarn guides are provided, which are shaped as spaced apart protuberances on two metal strips. The metal strips are supported in contact with the side walls of the axial channel.
problem: Guiding yarn along a controlled axial path in a heating apparatus while maintaining consistent contact and heat transfer.
constraint: The protuberance spacing and metal strip positioning must balance yarn guidance precision with minimal friction and wear on the fiber.
mechanism: Spaced protuberances on two opposing elements create a zigzag path that mechanically constrains a filament's movement, ensuring uniform exposure to heating elements and preventing slippage while balancing guidance precision with minimal friction and wear.
mechanism_raw: Spaced protuberances on two metal strips create a zigzag path that mechanically constrains the yarn's movement, ensuring uniform exposure to heating elements and preventing slippage.
residual_terms: ["spaced protuberances", "zigzag path", "mechanically constrains", "heating elements", "friction and wear"]

abstract: A method of producing sugars and converting the sugars to ethanol in which particulate biomass resulting from hydrolysis of the hemicellulosic content of the biomass is subjected to enzymatic hydrolysis of the cellulosic content to glucose and fermentation of the glucose to ethanol. The particulate biomass resulting from hydrolysis of the hemicellulosic content of the feed stock is reduced to very fine particle size before enzymatic hydrolysis. The hydrolysis of cellulose and the fermentation of the resulting glucose may be carried out separately or they may be carried out simultaneously. The pentoses and hexoses resulting from hydrolysis of the hemicellulose may be subjected to fermentation separately to produce ethanol or they may be fermented simultaneously with the fermentation of the glucose derived from the cellulose.
problem: Efficiently converting lignocellulosic biomass into ethanol by overcoming recalcitrance of cellulose and optimizing sugar utilization.
constraint: Particle size reduction must avoid over-processing that could inhibit enzymatic activity, while process integration requires balancing reaction kinetics and contamination risks.
mechanism: Reducing pre-treated biomass to fine particles increases surface area for enzymatic hydrolysis, while flexible integration of hydrolysis and fermentation steps allows simultaneous or sequential processing of different sugar types to overcome recalcitrance and optimize sugar utilization.
mechanism_raw: Reducing hemicellulose-hydrolyzed biomass to fine particles increases surface area for enzymatic cellulose hydrolysis, while flexible integration of hydrolysis and fermentation steps allows simultaneous or sequential processing of pentose and hexose sugars.
residual_terms: ["biomass", "fine particles", "surface area", "enzymatic hydrolysis", "hydrolysis and fermentation", "pentose and hexose sugars"]

abstract: In a method for manufacturing a twisted yarn a spindle rotor is positioned in a stationary cylinder housing. At least two spinning devices are supported in a receiving chamber of the spindle rotor such that the spinning devices are located adjacent to one another and symmetrical to the central axis of the spindle rotor. A vacuum is generated within the receiving chamber. Dissolved fiber material is supplied from a fiber supply device to the hollow spindle axle of the spindle rotor. The individual fiber material is fed by the vacuum within the receiving chamber via the hollow spindle axle 6 of the spindle rotor 7 and via feed channels, connecting the hollow spindle axle to the spinning rotors, to the spinning devices. From the dissolved fiber materials spun yarns are spun in each one of the spinning devices. The spun yarns are gathered as a twisted yarn at a centering point positioned on the extension of the central axis of the spindle rotor. The twisted yarn is wound onto a spool.
problem: Manufacturing twisted yarns from dissolved fiber materials using multiple spinning devices while ensuring uniform twisting and alignment.
constraint: The vacuum pressure and feed channel geometry must ensure consistent fiber delivery to all spinning devices without causing uneven tension or misalignment during yarn gathering.
mechanism: A pressure differential within a rotating assembly draws dissolved fiber through hollow conduits and feed channels to symmetrically arranged spinning devices, where individual filaments are spun and gathered at a central point to form a twisted yarn with uniform tension and alignment.
mechanism_raw: A vacuum within the spindle rotor draws dissolved fiber through hollow axles and feed channels to symmetrically arranged spinning devices, where individual yarns are spun and gathered at a central point to form a twisted yarn.
residual_terms: ["pressure differential", "rotating assembly", "hollow conduits", "feed channels", "spinning devices", "twisted yarn"]

abstract: A method for sanitizing a fowl that has been defeathered and eviscerated by contacting the fowl with peracetic acid solution containing from 100 to 2000 ppm peracetic acid. Completely contacting the fowl with peracetic acid solution effectively reduces the bacterial level found on the fowl to a level that will not produce disease in human beings.
problem: Reducing bacterial contamination on processed poultry to safe levels for human consumption without causing harm.
constraint: Balancing antimicrobial effectiveness with safety by maintaining peracetic acid concentration within a range that avoids toxicity while ensuring thorough bacterial elimination.
mechanism: Apply a chemical oxidizing agent across the entire surface of a food product at a concentration maintained within a range that balances pathogen elimination efficacy with safety, ensuring complete surface coverage for effective microbial reduction.
mechanism_raw: Contacting the entire surface of the fowl with a peracetic acid solution at a controlled concentration (100–2000 ppm) to achieve pathogen reduction through chemical oxidation, ensuring complete coverage for efficacy.

abstract: A blade device, wherein the angling angle of a blade can be increased and the blade width at the maximum angling is smaller than the chassis width without setting the mount position of the blade too far from a chassis. The connecting position of a joint for connecting a frame and a blade deviates from the crosswise center X--X of a chassis; and an actuator for pivotally moving the blade forward or backward is attached to the frame. As such, good workability of the blade device and good transportability of an earth-moving machine to which the blade device is operably coupled can be obtained.
problem: Adjusting the angling angle of a blade on an earth-moving machine while maintaining compact transportability and avoiding excessive distance between the blade mount and chassis.
constraint: Ensuring the blade width at maximum angling remains smaller than the chassis width to preserve structural integrity and transportability.
mechanism: Use an offset mounting joint (positioned away from the central axis of the supporting structure) combined with an actuation mechanism to pivotally adjust the angle of a blade, enabling angular repositioning without increasing the lateral displacement between the blade mount and the supporting structure.
mechanism_raw: Using an offset joint (deviating from the chassis crosswise center) combined with an actuator to pivotally move the blade, enabling angle adjustment without displacing the blade mount far from the chassis.
residual_terms: ["offset mounting joint", "actuation mechanism", "pivotally adjust", "angular repositioning", "lateral displacement"]

abstract: A magnetic drain bolt comprising: a bolt body and a magnet, the bolt body comprises a male-threaded member and a head member, the male-threaded member has an axial bore formed at a bottom end thereof for receiving the magnet, the male-threaded member further has a substantially circular lip extending axially inward at a bottom edge of the axial bore; the magnet consists of a cylindrical base and a cylindrical projecting extremity, the cylindrical base is sized to fit within the axial bore and has a diameter slightly larger than an inner diameter of the circular lip, the cylindrical projecting extremity extends axially from the cylindrical base and has a diameter slightly smaller than an inner diameter of the circular lip and thereby defines an indented circular shoulder along a bottom edge of the cylindrical base and along a top edge of the cylindrical projecting extremity, wherein the cylindrical base is fitted within the axial bore and the circular lip extends over the indented circular shoulder against the top edge of the circular projecting extremity thereby securing the cylindrical base within the axial bore with the circular projecting extremity extending axially beyond the bottom end of the male-threaded member.
problem: Securing a magnet within a threaded bolt body so it remains fixed during operation without loosening or dislodging.
constraint: Matching the magnet's base diameter to the lip's inner diameter and the projecting extremity's diameter to ensure secure retention without excessive force during assembly.
mechanism: Design a magnetic element with a base and projecting extremity that interlocks with a retaining lip and shoulder feature in a hollow body through dimensional interference, creating a snap-fit retention that secures the magnet without additional fasteners during operation.
mechanism_raw: Designing a cylindrical magnet with a base and projecting extremity that interlocks with a circular lip and indented shoulder in the bolt's axial bore, creating a snap-fit retention through dimensional interference.

abstract: A process is disclosed for disposing mineral processing tailings. The process includes the step of treating the tailings to produce a flowable paste including a mass comprised of particles at least approximately 15% of which are less than 20 microns in diameter. The process further includes the step of preparing an unconfined ground surface tailings disposal site by grading a selected site to produce a substantially level paste receiving bed. The flowable paste is then deposited onto the paste receiving bed from a discharge station to flow by gravity to a natural angle of rest of between approximately 1.degree. and 10.degree. slope. The paste is allowed to consolidate from flowable to a solidified state, retaining the natural angle of rest. Overburden is then placed over the solidified paste. The process is particularly useful in ore processing using cyanidation in which cyanide destroying chemicals are used at or prior to preparation of the flowable paste.
problem: Disposing of mineral processing tailings in a stable, environmentally safe manner that prevents seepage and allows for overburden placement.
constraint: Maintaining the paste's flowability and particle composition to ensure it solidifies at a stable slope angle while retaining structural integrity under overburden pressure.
mechanism: Create a flowable paste with controlled particle size distribution, deposit it on a graded surface to form a natural angle of rest, and allow consolidation into a solidified mass before covering with overburden, maintaining flowability and structural integrity throughout the process.
mechanism_raw: Creating a flowable paste with controlled particle size distribution (≥15% <20 microns), depositing it on a graded surface to form a natural angle of rest (1–10°), and allowing consolidation into a solidified mass before covering with overburden.

abstract: Filter rod sections are transported sideways from a magazine containing a pile of parallel sections toward positions of alignment with the inlet of a pneumatic conveyor and are propelled into the conveyor at a transfer station where they continue to move sideways. In order to avoid damage to sections during propulsion into the conveyor, the duration of complete transfer of successive sections into the inlet is monitored in order to generate signals denoting the intervals of axial advancement of successive sections all the way into the conveyor. Such signals are compared with signals denoting those intervals of sidewise movement of sections past the transfer station during which the sections can move axially without being damaged by the stationary inlet of the conveyor. The evaluating circuit which compares the signals generates defect signals when the transfer of sections in unsatisfactory, and such defect signals are used to reestablish the possibility to advance undamaged sections into the conveyor or to expel the fragments of destroyed or partially destroyed sections from the conveyor and/or from those parts of the apparatus which supply articles to the transfer station.
problem: Preventing damage to filter rod sections during automated transfer into a pneumatic conveyor by detecting and correcting defective transfers in real time.
constraint: Synchronizing timing measurements of axial and lateral motion to distinguish between acceptable and damaging transfer conditions without disrupting the overall process flow.
mechanism: Monitor the duration of axial advancement and lateral movement of successive sections, compare these intervals to predefined thresholds, and generate defect signals to halt or expel damaged sections when measurements indicate unacceptable transfer conditions.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring the duration of axial advancement and sidewise movement of successive sections, comparing these intervals to predefined thresholds, and generating defect signals to halt or expel damaged sections.

abstract: A process for reducing the amount of halogenated organic materials in aqueous systems by hydrogenating the halogenated organic materials in the aqueous system in the presence of ions of a metal from the 8th secondary group of the periodic system of elements at a pH of from 7 to 14 and a temperature of from 20.degree. C. to 140.degree. C.
problem: Reducing halogenated organic contaminants in aqueous systems without degrading the catalyst or surrounding materials.
constraint: Maintaining pH and temperature within a narrow range to ensure catalytic activity while avoiding catalyst poisoning or material degradation.
mechanism: A catalytic process that breaks down harmful compounds using a catalyst under controlled environmental conditions (pH and temperature) to maintain catalyst activity and prevent degradation of surrounding materials.
mechanism_raw: Catalytic hydrogenation using a metal from the 8th secondary group (e.g., palladium) under controlled pH (7–14) and temperature (20–140°C) to break down halogenated compounds into less harmful substances.

abstract: A method of diagnosing cat scratch disease and a method of diagnosing bacillary angiomatosis in a subject by detecting the presence of Rochalimaea henselae or an immunogenically specific determinant thereof in the subject is provided. Also provided is a vaccine comprising an immunogenic amount of a nonpathogenic Rochalimaea henselae or an immunogenically specific determinant thereof and a pharmaceutically acceptable carrier. A method of diagnosing Rochalimaea quintana infection in a subject by detecting the presence of a nucleic acid specific to Rochalimaea quintana in a sample from the subject is provided. A purified heat shock protein of Rochalimaea is provided.
problem: Accurately diagnosing infections caused by Rochalimaea species and developing vaccines against them.
constraint: Ensuring specificity of detection or immune response to avoid cross-reactivity with non-target pathogens or host tissues.
mechanism: Identification of unique biological markers specific to a pathogen to enable precise detection and targeted immune response, ensuring specificity to avoid cross-reactivity with non-target agents.
mechanism_raw: Detection of pathogen-specific antigens, immunogenic determinants, or nucleic acids to distinguish target infections from others, enabling precise diagnosis and targeted immunization.

abstract: A turner holds a wood blank while positioning it adjacent a cutting bit of a router to cut the blank into a shaped cylindrical object. The turner includes a mandrel and two mandrel wheels attachable to ends of the mandrel, which each have finger gripping portions. A wood block is disposed on the mandrel and the wheels are attached to the mandrel. Spacers may be used to position the wood block. The mandrel/wood block assembly is then moved adjacent a cutting bit, such as a router bit, to remove wood from the wood block. This enables generally cylindrically shaped objects to be formed which may then be polished and finished and used in pens, mechanical pencils, handles and like holders.
problem: Shaping irregular wood blocks into precise cylindrical forms using a router without manual repositioning or loss of alignment.
constraint: Balancing clamping force and adjustability to accommodate varying wood block sizes while maintaining rotational stability during cutting.
mechanism: An adjustable clamping system that stabilizes a workpiece during cutting by applying variable gripping force, enabling consistent shaping through controlled relative motion between the workpiece and cutting element.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable mandrel with finger-gripping wheels and spacers that clamp and stabilize the wood block during cutting, allowing consistent cylindrical shaping via controlled relative motion between the workpiece and cutting bit.

abstract: Apparatus for dispensing predetermined quantities of particulate material is disclosed which includes a casing defining a dispensing chamber and an inlet tube for delivering material to the chamber. The inlet tube extends into and is surrounded by the chamber. The chamber has an outlet for discharging material from the chamber. A mechanism is provided for effecting relative movement between the tube and the casing whereby to vary the volume of material introduced into the chamber on opening of an inlet valve.
problem: Dispensing precise, repeatable quantities of particulate material without manual measurement or calibration.
constraint: Achieving precise mechanical alignment and movement control to ensure consistent volume variation without leakage or material jamming.
mechanism: A variable-volume chamber whose capacity is adjusted via controlled relative movement between components, altering the quantity of material dispensed per cycle without manual calibration.
mechanism_raw: Variable-volume chamber controlled by relative movement between an inlet tube and casing, where adjusting the tube's position alters the material volume introduced per dispensing cycle.

abstract: A spindle liner and spindle liner assembly are for use in a lathe. A quick-change feature allows the spindle liner to be readily installed and readily replaced with a new spindle liner. The spindle liner has a tubular sleeve with a set of annular bearing rings and an annular mounting flange. An adapter specially configured for mounting on a particular lathe is designed for use with the spindle liner. The adapter has an annular body with a center hole to allow the tubular sleeve of the spindle liner to be slid through it. A recessed shoulder around the hole has a diameter to accommodate the annular mounting flange of the spindle liner. The adapter also has at least one and preferably opposed retainer lugs extending inwardly from a peripheral edge of the annular body and overlying the recessed shoulder. An equal number of notches in the mounting flange of the spindle liner are positioned to align with the retainer lugs when the spindle liner is positioned in the lathe. A partial rotation of the spindle liner allows its mounting flange to abut up against the recessed shoulder. A spring-loaded pin in a retainer lug of the adapter and a keeper hole in the mounting flange of the spindle liner become engaged and hold the spindle liner in place during use. A simple set of manipulations is all that is needed to remove the spindle liner in a very quick and efficient manner.
problem: Rapidly installing and replacing spindle liners in lathes without tools or complex disassembly.
constraint: Ensuring the locking mechanism is robust enough to withstand operational forces while allowing quick manual release.
mechanism: A mechanical interlock system that engages through rotational alignment and spring-loaded retention, enabling tool-free attachment and release by balancing locking robustness with manual operability.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking retainer lugs and notches with a spring-loaded pin that engage when the liner is partially rotated, enabling tool-free attachment and release via mechanical alignment and locking.

abstract: An aqueous phosphoric bonding solution and coating composition slurry which are environmentally friendly in that they are generally free of molybdate or chromium. Yet the solution is stable with respect to inorganic metal particles, especially aluminum which are admixed to the bonding solution for the preparation of the coating slurry. The metal coated parts and the method of coating the parts with the coating composition are also described. The parts have very satisfactory properties.
problem: Creating a stable coating composition with inorganic metal particles without using environmentally harmful additives like molybdate or chromium.
constraint: Balancing environmental safety (absence of molybdate/chromium) with sufficient stability of metal particles in the solution.
mechanism: A chemical formulation stabilizes dispersed particulate matter in a liquid medium through intermolecular interactions that inhibit particle aggregation and material degradation, enabling stable suspensions without toxic stabilizing agents.
mechanism_raw: The bonding solution uses a specific chemical formulation that stabilizes metal particles (e.g., aluminum) through interactions that prevent agglomeration or degradation, enabling stable slurries without toxic stabilizers.

abstract: Products for the variable controlled release of water soluble agents are disclosed. The products have a core of water soluble agent and a first and second coating. The first coating has a permeability such that the agent can be released at a controlled rate, while the second coating has a relatively low water vapor transmission rate. Variation in the coating thicknesses and coating conditions result in nutrient release profiles which can be tailored to specific plant requirements. After application of the product, release of the agent is negligible, but after a predetermined time, e.g. one month or more, substantial release of the agent from the coated product begins. The product is particularly suitable for delayed, controlled release fertilizers.
problem: Achieving delayed, controlled release of water-soluble agents (e.g., nutrients) tailored to specific application timelines.
constraint: Balancing negligible release before a trigger time with substantial release afterward, while maintaining structural integrity of the coatings.
mechanism: A multi-layer barrier system where a first layer's permeability modulates release kinetics and a second layer's impermeability delays initial release until a threshold time, with layer thickness and material properties determining the release profile.
mechanism_raw: A dual-coating system where the first coating's permeability controls release rate and the second coating's low water vapor transmission rate delays initial release until a predetermined time, with thickness and coating conditions modulating the release profile.

abstract: A coining press is provided with a machine frame, a coining drive for slides and coining dies, an ejector coining die against which the coining die can be pressed with the interposition of the coining blank and can partially yield for this purpose, a drive for the ejector movement of the ejector coining die and one device respectively for feeding the coining blank and for removing the finished coined part. The coining drive has a coupling dwell gear which is hinged to a toggle joint gear. The coupling dwell gear has a connecting rod moved by an eccentric shaft, the longitudinal axis of the connecting rod extending substantially in parallel to the coining plane and the end of the connecting rod facing away from the coining die being hinged to a booster device. The toggle joint gear has three pressure lugs which, on one end respectively, are hinged to one another on a pin while the end of a first pressure lug is hinged to the connecting rod. The other end of a lower pressure lug is hinged to the machine frame while the other end of an upper pressure lug is hinged to the slide.
problem: Generating precise, high-force linear motion in a coining press for metal forming operations.
constraint: Managing force amplification and movement precision within a compact mechanical system without sacrificing throughput.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system converts rotational input motion into amplified linear output force through a sequence of gear ratios and pivoting lever elements, achieving high-force displacement within a constrained spatial envelope.
mechanism_raw: A coupling dwell gear connected to a toggle joint gear converts rotational motion from an eccentric shaft into controlled linear movement via a connecting rod and booster device, amplifying force through mechanical leverage.
residual_terms: ["mechanical linkage system", "rotational input motion", "linear output force", "gear ratios", "pivoting lever elements"]

abstract: An oil and oil filter recycle apparatus useful to consumers who change their own oil comprising the assembly of a receptacle for the oil and oil filter, a support within the receptacle to keep the oil filter from being immersed in dried oil, and a drain unit which is low profile to go under vehicle, invertible to empty its contents into the receptacle for transport to a recycle location, and mated to the receptacle to seal the receptacle and drain unit mutually against leakage while anchoring the support screen in the receptacle inward of the seal.
reason: The patent describes a specific structural design for an oil recycling container with an invertible drain unit and sealing mechanism. While functional, it lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond its immediate application.

abstract: A device for molding products made of glass or a synthetic resin which device has a microwave generator, a microwave oven coupled to the generator and mold parts movable relative to each other provided in the microwave oven for forming molds for holding a parison of the glass or synthetic resin to be heated dielectrically.
problem: Efficiently heating glass or synthetic resin parisons for molding without relying on traditional external heating methods.
constraint: Achieving uniform internal heating without overheating or uneven temperature distribution in the material.
mechanism: Electromagnetic field energy directly couples with material molecules to generate volumetric internal heating, enabling rapid and uniform thermal softening while external shaping elements conform the material to a desired geometry.
mechanism_raw: Microwave dielectric heating directly energizes the material internally via electromagnetic fields, enabling rapid and uniform heating while movable mold parts shape the softened material.
residual_terms: ["electromagnetic field energy", "volumetric internal heating", "thermal softening", "external shaping elements"]

abstract: An ultrasonic atomizing device comprising a piezoelectric vibrator, at least an interdigital transducer P comprising two parts P.sub.D and P.sub.F, at least an electrode G, electrode terminals T.sub.D, T.sub.F and T.sub.G formed on the parts P.sub.D, P.sub.F and electrode G, respectively, a vibrating plate connected to the piezoelectric vibrator, a self-oscillator circuit, and means for dispensing a liquid to the vibrating plate. The interdigital transducer P and the electrode G are formed on two end surfaces of the piezoelectric vibrator, respectively. When an electric signal with a frequency substantially equal to one of the resonance frequencies of the piezoelectric vibrator is applied to the piezoelectric vibrator through the electrode terminals T.sub.D and T.sub.G, the piezoelectric vibrator is vibrated acoustically. The acoustic vibration is not only transmitted to the vibrating plate, but also transduced to an electric signal between the electrode terminals T.sub.F and T.sub.G. The acoustic vibration transmitted to the vibrating plate is consumed for liquid atomization effectively. The voltage between the electrode terminals T.sub.F and T.sub.G, that arises from the piezoelectricity of the piezoelectric vibrator is fedback, and again, applied to the electrode terminals T.sub.D and T.sub.G, which is essential for supplying the mechanical vibration energy for liquid atomization. The self-oscillator circuit is confirmed to work for continuous, stable liquid atomization without special compensation, for considerably large resonance frequency deviation of the piezoelectric vibrator.
problem: Maintaining stable ultrasonic atomization despite large resonance frequency deviations in a piezoelectric vibrator.
constraint: The system must operate across a wide range of resonance frequency deviations while maintaining stable feedback without introducing instability or requiring manual tuning.
