mechanism: A closed-loop feedback system senses vibrational energy from a resonant element, converts it into a control signal, and dynamically adjusts the driving input to maintain alignment with the element's resonance frequency. This self-tuning mechanism ensures continuous energy transfer despite frequency deviations without external intervention.
mechanism_raw: A self-oscillating feedback loop uses the piezoelectric effect to sense acoustic vibration energy generated by the vibrator, converts it into an electric signal, and re-applies it to drive the vibrator. This closed-loop system dynamically adjusts the driving signal to match the vibrator's resonance frequency, ensuring continuous energy transfer for atomization without external compensation.

abstract: This invention provides a static vent unit e.g. for use on the side of an aircraft and which in operation is subjected to airflow from any direction within a wide airflow incidence range comprises a generally flat plate having an outer surface for fitment generally to flush to an outer surface of the aircraft, a vent port through the plate for connection during operation to a static vent line in the aircraft, and a bulge on the plate outer surface surrounding at least part of a circumference of the vent port and having in cross section a convex curved upper surface extending radially inwardly from an outer edge on the plate to an inner edger on the plate adjacent the circumference of the vent port and adapted during operation to promote attachment of an airflow from within at least part of the airflow incidence range to its surface and direct the airflow into the vicinity of the vent port to provide a compensating increase in ambient pressure at the vent port.
problem: Accurately measuring ambient pressure on an aircraft surface despite airflow from arbitrary directions within a wide incidence range.
constraint: The geometry must maintain airflow attachment and pressure compensation across a broad range of incidence angles without disrupting the aircraft's aerodynamics.
mechanism: A shaped geometric feature surrounding a pressure port redirects and attaches airflow to its surface, creating a compensating pressure increase at the port. This stabilizes the pressure measurement by leveraging boundary layer attachment and flow redirection across arbitrary incidence angles.
mechanism_raw: A convex curved bulge surrounding the vent port shapes and attaches the airflow to its surface, redirecting it toward the vent port. This creates a compensating pressure increase at the port by leveraging boundary layer attachment and flow redirection, stabilizing the pressure reading regardless of airflow angle.

abstract: An installation for the batchwise destruction of noxious materials is described. The noxious material is fed batchwise into a combustion furnace holding a burning coal bed which induces combustion or detonation and also serves as damper for explosion fragments. Burning combustion gases are withdrawn from the upper part of the furnace and conducted while burning to a gas/solid separator. Optionally the burnt out combustion gases are bubbled through water or aqueous solution for the absorption of poisonous gas components and an essentially clean carbon dioxide/air mixture is discharged to the atmosphere.
problem: Batchwise destruction of noxious materials while safely managing explosion risks and fragment containment.
constraint: The coal bed must balance sustained combustion temperatures with sufficient mechanical resilience to dampen explosions, while enabling batchwise material addition without interrupting operation.
mechanism: A combustible material bed serves a dual function: it induces sustained high-temperature contact to destroy noxious materials, and acts as a mechanical damper to absorb or contain transient pressure spikes. Batchwise feeding enables controlled processing while the bed's thermal mass and structural integrity manage explosion risks.
mechanism_raw: A burning coal bed serves a dual role: it induces combustion/detonation of the noxious material through sustained high-temperature contact, and acts as a physical damper to absorb or contain explosion fragments. The batchwise feeding allows controlled processing while the coal bed's thermal mass and structural integrity handle transient pressure spikes.

abstract: A fin assembly for effecting guidance of a vehicle through a fluid medium cludes an electromagnet fixed in a portion of the vehicle, and a rigid shaft fixed to a hull portion of the vehicle and extending outwardly therefrom and in alignment with the electromagnet. A fin is rotatably mounted on the shaft and is, at least in part, a permanent magnet. A switch assembly is provided in the vehicle for effecting in a first portion of the electromagnet an attractive force between the electromagnet and the permanent magnet, and in a second portion of the electromagnet a repelling force therebetween, to cause the fin to rotate on the shaft in a selected direction to effect the guidance of the vehicle.
problem: Precisely controlling the rotation direction of a vehicle's steering fin in a fluid medium using electromagnetic actuation.
constraint: The electromagnetic field gradients must be precisely controlled to ensure smooth, bidirectional rotation of the fin without mechanical backlash or hysteresis, while minimizing power consumption.
mechanism: A spatially varying magnetic field generator creates opposing attractive and repulsive forces along its length. These forces act on a magnetically responsive element mounted on a rotational axis, inducing directional torque. A switching mechanism controls the field distribution to determine force orientation and rotation direction.
mechanism_raw: An electromagnet generates spatially varying magnetic fields along its length, creating an attractive force in one region and a repelling force in another. These opposing forces act on a permanent magnet fin mounted on a shaft, inducing rotational torque in a selected direction. The switch assembly controls which portion of the electromagnet is energized to determine the force distribution.

abstract: Compositions, methods, and systems for manufacturing articles, particularly containers and packaging materials, having a fiber-reinforced, starch-bound cellular matrix. Suitable mixtures used to form the articles are prepared by first preparing a viscous preblended mixture comprising water, a gelatinized starch-based binder, and fibers having an average length greater than about 2 mm. The highly viscous preblended mixture effectively transfers the shearing forces of the mixer to the fibers. The final moldable mixture is then prepared by mixing into the preblended mixture the remaining starch-based binder, water, and other desired admixtures, e.g., mold-releasing agents, inorganic filler rheology-modifying agents, plasticizers, coating materials, and dispersants, in the correct proportions to form an article which has the desired performance criteria. The moldable mixtures are heated between molds at an elevated temperature and pressure to produce form-stable articles having a desired shape and a selectively controlled foamed structural matrix. The articles may be manufactured to have properties substantially similar to articles presently made from conventional materials like paper, paperboard, polystyrene, plastic, or other organic-based materials and have especial utility in the mass-production of containers, particularly food and beverage containers.
problem: Manufacturing fiber-reinforced starch-based articles with controlled structural properties and foam matrix uniformity.
constraint: The preblend viscosity must be high enough to transfer shear to fibers but low enough to allow subsequent mixing, while the final mixture must maintain structural integrity during forming and drying.
mechanism: A two-stage mixing process first creates a high-viscosity preblend of water, gelatinized starch, and long fibers. The preblend's viscosity transfers shear forces directly to the fibers, ensuring uniform dispersion. Subsequent addition of remaining components into the preblend allows precise control over rheology and foam formation during molding under heat and pressure.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage mixing process first creates a highly viscous preblend of water, gelatinized starch, and long fibers. The high viscosity transfers shear forces directly to the fibers, ensuring uniform dispersion. Subsequent addition of remaining binders, fillers, and additives into the preblend allows precise control over rheology and foam formation during molding under heat and pressure.

abstract: A lubricating oil for two-cycle engines, which comprises a polyoxyalkylene glycol derivative represented by the following formula as a base oil, can be used to lubricate bearing portions and frictional portions of an two-cycle engine, so that the engine can be remarkably improved in generation of smoke, starting performance, cleanliness to prevent its exhaust system from clogging with carbon, cleanliness at high- or low temperature, and anti-seizure performance. ##STR1##
reason: The mechanism is specific to the chemical composition of the lubricating oil, which directly addresses engine performance issues through its molecular structure. While effective, the causal operation is tied to the particular chemistry rather than a generalizable principle applicable across fields.

abstract: An elevator system for a multistory structure having a plurality of elevator shafts is shown which includes at least one independently movable elevator car in each elevator shaft. A digital computer with memory is used to control elevator cars including the dispatch of cars from terminal floors. A daily control parameter table in memory identifies a plurality of different methods of scheduling dispatch of elevator cars from terminal floors, groups of floors to be serviced by each elevator car, and cars in a shaft to be coupled for tandem operation. The memory is periodically read for selecting for each elevator car one of said methods of scheduling dispatch and for identifying the group of floors to be serviced by the cars. The selected method of scheduling the dispatch of cars is implemented and cars are limited to servicing the selected group of floors. One method of scheduling dispatch includes obtaining a measure of estimated passenger demand for travel in one direction that is incapable of being met by cars currently in service. A passenger loading threshold limit for travel in the one direction is selected which may range from zero to maximum capacity of the elevator car to be dispatched. When the measure of estimated passenger demand for travel in the one direction that is incapable of being met by cars currently in service equals the passenger loading threshold limit a car dispatch signal is issued for dispatch of a car from the terminal floor. Where a plurality of independently-operated cars are included in a hoistway, operation in either a coupled or decoupled manner is provided.
problem: Optimizing elevator dispatch and resource allocation in multi-car systems to meet variable passenger demand while minimizing wait times and maximizing throughput.
constraint: Balancing passenger loading thresholds (from zero to maximum capacity) against available cars to avoid over- or under-allocation of resources.
mechanism: Dynamic allocation of transport units based on real-time demand estimation, with capacity adaptation through coupling or decoupling of units. A controller selects from multiple scheduling strategies and resource groups, dispatching units when unmet demand reaches a threshold.
mechanism_raw: Dynamic scheduling of elevator cars based on real-time demand estimation, with the ability to couple or decouple cars in a shaft to adapt capacity. A computer selects from multiple scheduling methods and floor groups, dispatching cars when unmet demand reaches a threshold.

abstract: A hydrophone transducer is prepared by depositing a piezoelectric material upon a conductive substrate or support structure, and then etching the material into selected regions or segments. The center segment, which provides most of the fundamental signal, is polarized in a first direction by the introduction of a polarizing voltage. The end segments are polarized in the opposite direction by the imposition of a polarizing voltage in the opposite direction. The conductive substrate then serves as one terminal of the output of the hydrophone while the upper surfaces of the segments together serve as the other terminal. The relative strengths of the signals from the segments may tailored by adjusting the areas of the segments.
problem: Tailoring signal contributions from different segments of a hydrophone transducer to optimize sensitivity and directional response.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the substrate while enabling independent polarization of segments to achieve desired signal characteristics.
mechanism: Partitioning a sensing element into regions with opposing polarization states, where signal contribution balance is controlled by varying the relative areas of the regions. This enables adjustment of composite output characteristics through spatial configuration.
mechanism_raw: Segmenting a piezoelectric material into regions (e.g., center and end segments) and polarizing them in opposing directions. The relative signal strengths are adjusted by varying the areas of the segments, allowing control over the composite output.

abstract: A sifter frame is composed of a pair of frame elements including an outer frame and an inner frame, and the outer frame is formed from a frame member having the same height and includes a pair of fine powder dropping ports, a rough powder dropping port and a rectangular fine powder receiving plate disposed in a region surrounded by these openings and one of the outer block frame members and the inner frame is fitted with the space above the receiving plate. A pair of the outer frame members of the inner frame in contact with the fine powder dropping ports of the inner frame are projected more to the rough powder dropping port than the outer block frame members of the inner frame in contact with the rough powder dropping port of the outer frame, receiving portions are provided with the outer frame in correspondence with the above arrangement so that the projected portions of the inner frame are placed thereon as well as the surfaces where the projected portions are engaged with the receiving portions are formed to an arc shape in order to that a depressing force of an upper stage sifter frame is applied to the engaging surfaces where the inner frame of a lower stage sifter frame is engaged with the outer frame thereof as a sealing force. With the above arrangement, there is provided a novel stacking type sifter frame by which the mixture of rough powder with fine powder can be securely prevented while limiting a portion to be periodically replaced to a minimum necessary portion.
problem: Preventing cross-contamination between rough and fine powders in a stacked sifter system while minimizing replacement parts.
constraint: Ensuring the sealing force is sufficient to prevent mixing while allowing periodic replacement of only the minimal necessary components.
mechanism: Geometric interaction between nested structural elements with complementary projections and curved contact surfaces. Mechanical compression between elements generates a sealing force that isolates material streams without auxiliary sealing components.
mechanism_raw: Geometric design of nested frame elements with projected portions and arc-shaped engaging surfaces. The mechanical interaction between frames applies a sealing force when compressed, isolating powder streams without requiring additional sealing components.

abstract: An adjustable template for maneuvering a textile product. The template includes a template base with several template shoes movably mounted along the sides of the base. The position of the template shoes with respect to the template base is adjusted in response to the detection of the length and the width of the textile product such that when the template is positioned on the product, each template shoe is positioned at a predetermined distance from a lateral edge of the textile product.
problem: Adapting a textile maneuvering tool to fit varying product dimensions while maintaining precise edge alignment.
constraint: Achieving accurate shoe positioning relative to edges without manual recalibration, while accommodating a range of product sizes.
mechanism: Feedback-driven positioning of adjustable contact elements relative to detected boundaries of a target object. The elements maintain a predetermined offset from lateral edges, enabling automatic conformity to varying object geometries.
mechanism_raw: Feedback-driven adjustment of movable template shoes based on detected length and width of the textile product. The shoes are positioned at a predetermined distance from lateral edges, enabling the template to conform to the product's geometry.

abstract: An actuator comprises a housing member including a motor compartment and a gear compartment, the gear compartment having inner teeth formed on the inner periphery thereof, a motor having a rotary shaft with a motor gear mounted thereon, the motor being housed in the motor compartment in such a way as to permit the motor gear to project into the gear compartment, an output shaft projecting outwardly from the housing member, a larger diameter gear housed in the gear compartment which is rotatable about the output shaft and held in mesh engagement with the motor gear, a smaller diameter gear disposed coaxially with the larger diameter gear and rotatable in conjunction with the rotation of the larger diameter gear, a planet gear held in mesh engagement with both the smaller diameter gear and the inner teeth formed in the gear compartment so that the planet gear can shift its engagement position with respect to the inner teeth as the smaller diameter gear rotates, and a rotary member engaging the planet gear for rotation within the gear compartment, the output shaft being rotatable in response to the rotation of the rotary member.
problem: Achieving a specific output motion from a motor in a compact mechanical system while enabling variable engagement of gear components.
constraint: The mechanical arrangement must allow the planet gear to dynamically shift engagement positions while maintaining mesh with both the smaller gear and inner teeth, balancing compactness with functional variability.
mechanism: A coaxial gear arrangement where a secondary rotating element drives a planet gear to dynamically shift its engagement between an inner surface and a primary gear, transferring motion to a driven element through a connected rotary component. The shifting engagement enables variable output motion without external control systems.
mechanism_raw: A planetary gear system where a smaller coaxial gear rotates with a larger gear, causing a planet gear to shift its engagement position with inner teeth as the smaller gear turns. This shifting transfers rotational motion to an output shaft via a rotary member connected to the planet gear, enabling controlled output without complex external controls.

abstract: Polyalkylphenoxyaminoalkanes having the formula: ##STR1## wherein R is a polyalkyl group having an average molecular weight in the range of about 600 to 5,000; PA1 R.sub.1 and R.sub.2 are independently hydrogen or lower alkyl having 1 to 6 carbon atoms; and PA1 A is amino, N-alkyl amino having about 1 to about 20 carbon atoms in the alkyl group, N,N-dialkyl amino having about 1 to about 20 carbon atoms in each alkyl group, or a polyamine moiety having about 2 to about 12 amine nitrogen atoms and about 2 to about 40 carbon atoms. The compounds of formula I are useful as fuel additives for the prevention and control of engine deposits.
problem: Preventing and controlling engine deposits in internal combustion engines through fuel additives.
constraint: The molecular weight of the polyalkyl group must remain within a specific range to balance solubility in fuel and effectiveness in preventing deposits, while the amino/polyamine structure must retain sufficient reactivity to interact with deposit precursors.
mechanism: A molecular additive with a hydrophobic chain and reactive nitrogen-containing groups interacts with surfaces and deposit precursors through adsorption and solubility, disrupting their formation or adhesion. The chain length balances solubility in the medium and reactivity with target molecules.
mechanism_raw: A polyalkylphenoxyaminoalkane compound with a polyalkyl group (molecular weight 600–5,000) and an aminoalkyl or polyamine moiety interacts with engine surfaces and deposits, disrupting their formation or adhesion through molecular-level adsorption and solubility effects.

abstract: A portable frame that includes a movable support for supporting a cutting tool used for engaging a rock sample, and upon relative movement between the rock sample and the cutter, the cutter will make a constant depth cut at a constant velocity. During the cut, the forces parallel to the direction of displacement and perpendicular to the direction are measured, and both cohesion and internal friction angle, which are parameters characterizing the rock strength, the internal friction angle, which is a true measure of the rock strength, can be determined.
problem: Determining rock strength parameters (cohesion and internal friction angle) through controlled cutting and force measurement.
constraint: The system must maintain constant cutting depth and velocity despite varying rock properties, requiring precise mechanical control to ensure accurate force measurements and parameter derivation.
mechanism: A portable apparatus maintains a cutting tool at constant depth and velocity relative to a sample during displacement. Forces parallel and perpendicular to displacement are measured, and these values are used to calculate material strength parameters via mechanical equilibrium relationships.
mechanism_raw: A portable frame maintains a cutting tool at constant depth and velocity relative to a rock sample during displacement. Forces parallel and perpendicular to the displacement direction are measured, and these values are used to calculate cohesion and internal friction angle via mechanical equilibrium relationships.

abstract: An improved controller for opening and closing a venetian blind vanes over a door or window opening. A pull cord is engaged with a pulley, which is moved with a loop cord selectively engaged with a cord lock attached to a handle. A rotatable switch in the cord lock is rotated, the cord lock grasps the loop cord, and the handle is moved downwardly to pull to loop cord. Such movement operates the pulley and pull cord to raise the blind vanes. When the cord lock is disengaged, the weight of the blind returns the components to the original position. A rotatable tilt switch or combination of rotatable tilt switches are attached to a tilt rod for selectively rotating the blind vanes. All cords are completely enclosed so that looped ends of the cords are not accessible to persons adjacent the window blind.
problem: Operating venetian blind vanes safely without exposing cords to adjacent persons.
constraint: The mechanical linkage must allow both raising/lowering and tilting functions while ensuring complete enclosure of all cords, requiring precise coordination between the pulley, cord lock, and tilt switch mechanisms.
mechanism: A pull mechanism engages a pulley connected to a looped tension element, which is selectively grasped by a locking device attached to a handle. Handle movement pulls the tension element to adjust vane position, while a rotatable switch on a rod modifies vane angles. All tension elements are fully enclosed to prevent access.
mechanism_raw: A pull cord engages a pulley connected to a loop cord, which is selectively grasped by a cord lock attached to a handle. Moving the handle pulls the loop cord to raise vanes, while a rotatable tilt switch on a tilt rod adjusts vane angles. All cords are fully enclosed within the system to prevent access.

abstract: A fan shroud has side walls that wrap around the side edges of a down flow type radiator, providing both the mounting means for a condenser and side seals to direct air flow from the condenser through the radiator. The lack of direct connection between the radiator and condenser compensates for the lack of overlap between the condenser and radiator tanks, which is the usual means of interconnection. The minimization of contact between the shroud and radiator, which is secured only to the back of the radiator tanks with threaded fasteners, allows the same shroud and condenser to be packaged more easily with differing radiator designs.
problem: Packaging a condenser and radiator together in a down-flow system without direct interconnection, accommodating varying radiator designs.
constraint: The shroud must balance airflow directionality and structural support while avoiding rigid connections between the radiator and condenser, enabling flexibility in radiator design without compromising performance.
mechanism: An airflow director with side walls wraps around a primary heat exchanger, channeling flow from a secondary heat exchanger through the primary unit. The director is attached only to the primary unit's structural elements via discrete fasteners, minimizing contact and enabling modular compatibility with varying primary unit designs.
mechanism_raw: A fan shroud with side walls wraps around radiator edges, directing airflow from the condenser through the radiator. The shroud is secured only to the radiator tanks via threaded fasteners, minimizing contact and allowing modular compatibility with different radiator configurations.

abstract: A ceramic tile is mounted to the wall of an incinerator or other high temperature and/or corrosive environment with a stud assembly that includes a threaded stud and a ceramic T-nut. The ceramic T-nut thermally shields the stud to protect it from oxidation and corrosion, and reduces cracking in tile because the T-nut and the tile have similar thermal expansion. The T-nut is accessible through a small bore.
problem: Protecting a stud assembly from oxidation, corrosion, and thermal stress in high-temperature environments while preventing tile cracking due to mismatched thermal expansion.
constraint: The T-nut must balance thermal shielding effectiveness with structural integrity and accessibility through a small bore, while maintaining compatibility with both the tile and stud materials.
mechanism: A thermally matched barrier element is positioned between a high-temperature component and a substrate to reduce heat transfer and differential thermal expansion, thereby preventing oxidation, corrosion, and cracking caused by mismatched thermal responses.
mechanism_raw: A ceramic T-nut with thermal expansion properties matched to the ceramic tile is used to thermally shield the stud, reducing heat transfer to the stud and minimizing differential expansion-induced cracking between the tile and stud.

abstract: Boiler for generating steam and comprising a furnace wall defining a furnace, a casing wall concentrically encircling the furnace wall and jointly with the furnace wall defining a substantially annular interspace, steam consucting tubes positioned at the furnace wall and the casing wall and being in connection with top and bottom annular vessels and a flue gas aperture in the furnace wall for establishment of connection from the furnace to the annular interspace. At least one of the two walls, i.e. the furnace wall and the casing wall, and perferably both of the walls, i.e. the furnace wall as well as the casing wall, is constituted by steam generating tubes connected by intermediate flanges. Thus, a boiler is provided which is more stable than the prior art boilers and which is not limited to a certain maximum length, but may be provided in any length or size for obtaining the desired effect. In addition, the boiler shows other advantages in comparison with prior art boilers as e.g. a higher reliability, a compact embodiment, a leight weight and a high reliability in operation, and it requires only small space and is easy to install and to maintain.
problem: Creating a boiler that is stable, scalable to arbitrary lengths, and compact while maintaining reliability and ease of installation.
constraint: The flanged tube connections must maintain leak-tight integrity and thermal performance across variable lengths while minimizing weight and space requirements.
mechanism: Concentric structural layers formed from interconnected tubular segments with intermediate joining interfaces enable modular assembly of variable lengths while maintaining structural stability and thermal performance through distributed load-bearing and heat transfer pathways.
mechanism_raw: Concentric furnace and casing walls constructed from steam-generating tubes connected by intermediate flanges allow modular assembly of any length without compromising structural stability, enabling scalable and compact boiler designs.

abstract: A Czochralski method for producing monocrystals wherein a single crystal silicon rod is pulled from a silicon melt contained in a crucible within a chamber. After pulling the single crystal silicon rod from a silicon melt in a chamber, the chamber is cooled by flowing a gas having a thermal conductivity of at least about 55.times.10.sup.-5 g.cal./(sec..multidot.cm.sup.2)(.degree.C./cm) at 800.degree. K into the chamber. The preferred cooling gas is a helium-containing gas.
problem: Rapidly and uniformly cooling a high-temperature chamber after monocrystal pulling to prevent thermal stress and defects in the crystal.
constraint: The cooling gas must have sufficient thermal conductivity (≥55×10⁻⁵ cal/(s·cm²·K)) to achieve rapid cooling without introducing contamination or uneven thermal gradients.
mechanism: A high-conductivity fluid medium is introduced into a chamber to accelerate heat dissipation, ensuring uniform temperature reduction across surfaces and contents to prevent thermal stress-induced defects during solidification processes.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a cooling gas with high thermal conductivity (e.g., helium) into the chamber accelerates heat dissipation, ensuring controlled and uniform cooling of the silicon melt and chamber components.

abstract: The difference between the temperature of a heat exchange medium leaving the evaporator unit of a chiller and the temperature of the refrigerant in the evaporator unit is monitored relative to a real time alarm limit for this temperature difference. The real time alarm limit is computed from time to time by a microprocessor. The value of the computed alarm limit will vary with the cooling load being experienced by the chiller's evaporator unit.
problem: Detecting abnormal conditions in a chiller's evaporator unit under varying cooling loads without false alarms or missed faults.
constraint: The alarm limit calculation must adapt quickly to load changes while avoiding sensitivity to transient fluctuations that could trigger false alarms.
mechanism: A computational controller dynamically adjusts detection thresholds for operational parameters based on real-time load conditions, using feedback to distinguish between transient fluctuations and persistent anomalies to maintain accurate fault identification.
mechanism_raw: A microprocessor dynamically computes real-time alarm limits for the temperature difference between the heat exchange medium and refrigerant, adjusting thresholds based on current cooling load to maintain accurate fault detection.

abstract: The present invention relates to an improved method of manufacturing an airbag initiator. Currently, an airbag initiator is comprised of three parts made out of two dissimilar materials plus a glass to metal seal. The present method builds the same airbag initiator with the body and the pins in one piece via a process called metal injection molding. The part is then placed in a furnace to remove a wax binder, then the temperature is ramped up slowly to remove a thermoplastic layer, and the temperature is further ramped up to form a sintered part. The sintered part being equal to or better than standards of wrought material. The initiator is then removed from the furnace and a glass bead is placed in a void area in the body of the initiator. The glass is melted forming a glass to metal seal between a first pin and the body of the initiator. A top portion of the initiator is then lapped off isolating the first pin from the body of the initiator. A bridge wire is welded to the first pin and the body of the initiator yielding the completed airbag initiator.
problem: Manufacturing an airbag initiator with a glass-to-metal seal and multiple dissimilar materials while reducing part count and ensuring material quality.
constraint: The MIM and sintering parameters must achieve material properties equivalent to or better than wrought materials while maintaining dimensional accuracy for the glass-to-metal seal.
mechanism: A powder-based forming process creates integrated multi-material components with controlled densification, followed by a sealing operation that bonds dissimilar materials at interfaces to eliminate separate parts and ensure dimensional compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Metal injection molding (MIM) creates a one-piece body and pins, followed by controlled sintering and glass sealing processes, eliminating separate components and enabling precise integration of dissimilar materials.

abstract: A mill, especially an intermittently operating mill with milling bodies is emptied or filled through an opening provided with a pair of ball cocks of which a ball proximal to the opening is integrated with a sieve plate in its throughgoing bore, thereby eliminating dead zones and contamination resulting from wear of the sieve.
problem: Dead zones and contamination in intermittently operating mills due to wear of sieve plates and inefficient material flow through openings.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the sieve plate while ensuring the ball cock remains operable and sealed against wear.
mechanism: Integrate a flow-control element with a perforated surface such that the element directly governs material passage through the surface, eliminating stagnation zones and preventing debris accumulation by maintaining structural continuity and sealing against wear.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a ball cock with the sieve plate's throughgoing bore so that the ball directly controls flow through the sieve, eliminating gaps where material can stagnate or wear debris accumulates.

abstract: An emergency exhaust system is couplable to a vehicle for conducting exhaust fumes from the vehicle exhaust pipe to an enclosure ventilation system to be exhausted from the vehicle enclosure when the vehicle is normally parked when not being used. The exhaust system includes an elongated flexible hose assembly that is connected to the ventilation system and to an adaptor conduit which at its terminal end has a ring mounting electromagnets for magnetically attaching to a mount plate dependingly secured to the vehicle to have the vehicle exhaust pipe extend therethrough. An intermediate portion of the hose assembly is connected through a balancer assembly to a trolley movable along a rail in a forward direction as the vehicle moves to exit the enclosure. As the trolley moves adjacent to the rail front end, through automatic controls, the magnetic coupling to the mount plate is disengaged. As a result of not coupling directly to the exhaust pipe, the chances of damaging the vehicle exhaust system are minimized, but provision is made for safely conducting the vehicle exhaust fumes outside of the enclosure.
problem: Safely conducting vehicle exhaust fumes outside an enclosure during parking without risking damage to the vehicle's exhaust system.
constraint: Balancing secure magnetic attachment during operation with reliable, damage-free disengagement as the vehicle exits the enclosure.
mechanism: Employ a magnetic coupling that automatically decouples in response to relative motion between connected components, using a mechanical trigger to disengage before physical separation occurs, balancing secure attachment during operation with damage-free disengagement.
mechanism_raw: Using a magnetic coupling that automatically disengages as the vehicle moves away, triggered by trolley motion along a rail, decoupling the hose from the exhaust pipe before physical separation occurs.

abstract: A method and apparatus is for imparting, in a continuous sequence, a predetermined rotational movement to a warhead releasably housed in a protective canister and ejected out in ballistic ejection trajectories from the canister. The canister is spun to the desired rotational speed by flow of combustion gases through gas outlet nozzles discharging in the outer periphery of the canister and supplied from a central combustion chamber in which a propellant powder charge is combusted. The combustion gases are then led from the combustion chamber, in the final phase of the propellant charge combustion, through gas outlets facing towards the warhead and initially covered by the propellant charge and exposed as a result of the combustion, for ejecting the warhead out of the canister.
problem: Imparting controlled rotation to a warhead during ejection while ensuring reliable separation from the canister.
constraint: Timing the transition between spin-inducing gas flow and ejection gas flow to ensure full rotation is achieved before separation.
mechanism: Sequence fluid flow through two distinct pathways: first directing flow through peripheral outlets to induce rotational motion, then redirecting flow through axial outlets after an initial phase completes, ensuring full rotation is achieved before separation occurs.
mechanism_raw: Sequencing combustion gas flow: first directing gases through peripheral nozzles to spin the canister, then redirecting gases axially through outlets initially blocked by propellant to eject the warhead once the propellant is consumed.

abstract: A method and apparatus for transmitting video data over a standard personal computer bus optimizes the video data transfer rate of the bus by parsing the video data into appropriately sized and selected blocks. The video data blocks required for display are stored in a first-in first-out register, addressed, and sent over the data bus of the computer. Video data not required for display is discarded. The video data may be addressed to any location in the memory of the computer for display or further processing.
problem: Maximizing video data transfer rate over a standard PC bus while minimizing unnecessary data transmission.
constraint: Balancing block size and memory allocation to optimize throughput without overloading the bus or memory resources.
mechanism: Parse data into discrete units, buffer only units required for output in a sequential-access storage element, selectively transmit buffered units over a communication channel, and discard non-output units to reduce channel load.
mechanism_raw: Parsing video data into blocks, storing only display-required blocks in a FIFO register, addressing them for bus transmission, and discarding non-display data to reduce bus load.

abstract: An abrasive article having sheet-like structure including a major surface extending within an imaginary plane with a plurality of individual three-dimensional abrasive composites deployed in fixed positions thereto in an array, each of the composites has abrasive particles dispersed in a binder and has a substantially precise shape and a distal end, where another imaginary plane extends parallel to and is spaced from the first imaginary plane and intersects the lowest distal end among the composites, wherein any imaginary line drawn within the latter-mentioned imaginary plane in the direction(s) of intended use intersect at least one cross-section among the abrasive composites in the array. The invention also relates to methods for manufacturing such an abrasive article and its usage to refine a work surface.
problem: Efficiently refining a work surface with an abrasive article while ensuring uniform material removal across the surface.
constraint: Maintaining structural support and spacing between composites while ensuring full coverage in all intended directions of use.
mechanism: Arrange shaped abrasive elements in a fixed spatial pattern such that any trajectory along the intended direction of use intersects at least one element, ensuring continuous contact and uniform material removal while maintaining structural support between elements.
mechanism_raw: Deploying precisely shaped three-dimensional abrasive composites in a fixed array such that any line drawn in the direction of use intersects at least one composite, guaranteeing continuous abrasive contact.

abstract: An air conditioning system for vehicles prevents pressure loss in an air conditioner casing from increasing by air-conditioning a passenger compartment while detouring around an air cleaning unit when the air conditioning situation is in an irregular air conditioning range, and improves passengers' comfort by cleaning and air-conditioning air by way of the air cleaning unit when the air conditioning situation is in a regular air conditioning range. An air conditioner controller controls inlet switching dampers for switching air flowing routes in the air conditioner casing, thereby selecting an external or an internal air conditioning priority mode in which air directed to the passenger compartment passes through the air conditioning unit but makes a detour around the air cleaning unit when the air conditioning situation is in the irregular air conditioning range, and for selecting an external or an internal air cleaning mode in which air directed to the passenger compartment passes through the air conditioning unit as well as the air cleaning unit when the air conditioning situation is in the regular air conditioning range.
problem: Balancing air quality and passenger comfort in vehicle HVAC systems while minimizing pressure loss during irregular air conditioning conditions.
constraint: Trade-off between maintaining low pressure loss during irregular conditions and ensuring air cleaning effectiveness during regular conditions.
mechanism: Dynamically routing airflow through selectable paths that bypass or include an air treatment element based on detected operating conditions, enabling adaptive prioritization of external versus internal air modes while minimizing pressure loss during irregular conditions.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically switching airflow routes through inlet dampers to bypass or include an air cleaning unit based on detected air conditioning conditions, enabling adaptive prioritization of external/internal air modes.
residual_terms: ["airflow", "inlet dampers", "air cleaning unit", "air conditioning conditions", "external/internal air modes", "pressure loss"]

abstract: Apparatus and method for controlling equipment of driving a ram of a hydraulic press. Four proportional sheet valves PA, PB, TA and TB are connected with a hydraulic circuit, in which a hydraulic cylinder 2 for driving a ram 1, a hydraulic pump 3 and so on are set up, a so as to form a full-bridge hydraulic circuit. A compression proportional sheet valve PAp and a hydraulic pump 40 are connected as a hydraulic power source with high pressure and small flow rate parallel with the sheet valve PA being in the oil supply position side in the hydraulic circuit. An NC controller controls timing of turn-on of the proportional sheet valves PA, PB, TA and TB as well as change of the valves PA and Pap by PWM signal to pilot valves of the sheet valves PA, PB, TA and TB. The valves PA and TB are turned on in the down stroke of the ram 1, the valves PB and TA are turned on in the up stroke of the ram 1, and the valve Pap is turned on in the compression stroke.
problem: Achieving precise control of a hydraulic press ram's motion across different strokes (down, up, compression) with variable pressure and flow requirements.
constraint: Balancing flow rate and pressure across multiple valves to maintain precise ram control while avoiding hydraulic instability or inefficiency.
mechanism: Coordinating opposing hydraulic paths through a full-bridge circuit using independently controlled proportional valves driven by pulse-width modulation, enabling precise management of flow rate and pressure for each stroke phase while maintaining system stability.
mechanism_raw: Using a full-bridge hydraulic circuit with proportional valves controlled by PWM signals to independently manage valve timing and pressure, enabling coordinated actuation of opposing hydraulic paths for each stroke phase.
residual_terms: ["hydraulic circuit", "proportional valves", "PWM signals", "valve timing", "pressure", "ram control", "stroke phase", "hydraulic instability"]

abstract: A sizing agent is prepared from at least one specified kind of ester and at least one specified polyepoxy compound. A water-based sizing agent is prepared by emulsifying or dispersing it in water and is applied to carbon fibers at a specified ratio as sizing agent to improve lubricity, abrasion durability and spreadability of the carbon fibers at the same time.
reason: The patent describes a material composition (ester and polyepoxy compound) to achieve specific properties (lubricity, abrasion durability, spreadability) but does not describe a functional mechanism for how these properties are achieved or interact.

abstract: A carrier for electrostatic latent image developing for use in methods of developing an electrostatic latent image formed on the surface of a latent image-bearing member by transporting a developer comprising a toner and a carrier via the rotation of a developing sleeve having a built in stationary magnet roller, the carrier for electrostatic latent image developing including magnetic powder dispersed in a binder resin and having a saturation magnetization of about 50 to about 80 emu/g, residual magnetization of about 3 to about 10 emu/g, and coercive force of about 20 to about 50 oersted.
reason: The patent specifies material properties (saturation magnetization, residual magnetization, coercive force) of a magnetic carrier but does not describe a causal mechanism for how these properties enable electrostatic image development or interact functionally.

abstract: A lock is disclosed for securing merchandise products onto a hook of the type adapted for mounting onto a pegboard or other support. The lock includes a housing having an internal cavity which is formed with a cradle for seating the tip of the hook. A slot formed in the housing enables ingress and egress of the hook tip toward and away from a seated position in the cradle. A latch is pivotally mounted in the housing and the latch is moveable to a latched position at which the hook tip is captured in its seated position in the cradle. The latch is releasably held in its latched position by a nib on the housing which engages a depression on the latch. Operation of a key causes the latch to pivot toward an unlatched position at which the hook tip is enabled to be unseated from the cavity for egress out of the cavity, permitting the lock to be separated from the hook.
problem: Securing merchandise to a hook in a way that prevents unauthorized removal while allowing authorized release via a key.
constraint: Balancing secure retention of the hook tip against the need for reliable, key-activated release without mechanical jamming.
mechanism: A pivotable latch captures a hook tip in a cradle, held in place by a retention element engaging a recess on the latch. Key operation pivots the latch to disengage the retention element, enabling hook tip release.
mechanism_raw: A pivotable latch captures the hook tip in a cradle, held in place by a nib engaging a depression on the latch. Key operation pivots the latch to disengage the nib, enabling hook tip release.

abstract: A low profile trash receptacle housing carries a plurality of vertically and horizontally spaced hydraulic cylinders (A) and (B) for incrementally and simultaneously supplying a downward stroke upon a horizontally disposed compaction plate (C) so that upon retraction of the compaction plate and cylinders to a raised position following a compacting cycle adequate space is provided so that a door (D) may be opened to extend inwardly for reception of trash into a lower compacting portion of the housing with guides (E) providing stability to the compaction plate at all times during the compacting cycle.
problem: Efficiently compact trash in a low-profile receptacle while maintaining access for adding new trash.
constraint: Balancing compaction force and stroke length with the need to retract the plate fully to allow door operation in a confined vertical space.
mechanism: Multiple actuators incrementally and simultaneously drive a compaction surface downward to compress material, then retract to a raised position, creating space for an access opening to operate in a confined vertical space. Guides stabilize the surface during both compaction and retraction phases.
mechanism_raw: Multiple hydraulic cylinders incrementally and simultaneously drive a compaction plate downward to compress trash, then retract to a raised position, creating space for a door to open inward. Guides stabilize the plate during both compaction and retraction phases.

abstract: A conformable composite acoustic transducer panel including a conformable composite body having upper and lower planar faces and upper and lower thin, flexible electrodes bonded to the upper and lower faces, respectively. The composite body includes an array of individual piezoelectric or electrostrictive ceramic elements extending normal to the upper and lower faces and through the composite body from the upper face to the lower face to electrically contact the electrodes. Stiff integral face plates are bonded to the side surfaces of the elements at their upper and lower ends. Alternatively, a conformable, stiff, voided polymer matrix is bonded to the element sides over their entire length. Flexible circuit boards may be bonded to the electrodes to provide electrical contact thereto. Methods for fabricating the transducer panel are also disclosed.
problem: Creating a conformable acoustic transducer that maintains structural integrity and electrical contact while adapting to non-planar surfaces.
constraint: Maintaining stiffness at critical contact points (electrodes, element ends) while allowing global conformability through flexible matrix or voided regions.
mechanism: A composite body with energy-converting elements bonded between flexible electrodes uses stiff integral face plates or a voided polymer matrix to locally reinforce element sides, enabling flexibility without compromising performance or electrical contact.
mechanism_raw: A composite body with piezoelectric/ceramic elements bonded between flexible electrodes uses stiff integral face plates or a voided polymer matrix to locally reinforce element sides, enabling flexibility without compromising acoustic performance or electrode contact.

abstract: A belt locking device includes: a housing including a base member having a first belt end of a fastening belt fixed in the base member and having a base engaging portion formed on the base member for detachably engaging a second belt end of the fastening belt, and a cover member combinable with the base member; a primary lock resiliently slidably held in the cover member and partially protruding outwardly from the cover member and having a movable engaging portion formed on the primary lock to be engageable with the base engaging portion of the base member for locking the second belt end of the fastening belt in between the cover member and the base member of the housing, whereby upon depression of the primary lock to disengage the movable engaging portion of the primary lock from the base engaging portion of the base member, the second belt end of the fastening belt is removable from the base member; and a secondary lock secured in the housing and operatively locking and unlocking the primary lock within the housing, thereby safely enhancing a double locking of the belt locking device.
problem: Providing a belt locking mechanism that ensures secure retention while allowing safe, intentional release.
constraint: Preventing unintended disengagement of the primary lock while ensuring the secondary lock can be reliably actuated to enable release.
mechanism: A primary lock with a movable engaging portion is slidably held in a cover and operatively controlled by a secondary lock. The secondary lock physically restricts the primary lock's movement until intentionally disengaged, preventing accidental release.
mechanism_raw: A primary lock with a movable engaging portion is slidably held in a cover and operatively controlled by a secondary lock. The secondary lock physically restricts the primary lock's movement until intentionally disengaged, preventing accidental release.

abstract: A can crusher device that has a base member with an upper surface connected by linkages to a moveable plate member with a lower planar surface wherein the linkages includes levers that interconnect the forward portions of the base and plate members as well as the rearward portions of the base and plate members in a parallelogram type of linkage so that on movement of the levers the lower surface of the plate member is maintained in a parallel relationship to the upper surface of the base member during the crushing action on the can. The force exerted on the can is an endwise downward force along the full longitudinal length of the can.
problem: Crushing cylindrical containers (e.g., cans) with uniform force application while maintaining alignment between the crushing plate and base.
constraint: Maintaining parallel alignment of the crushing surfaces during motion to avoid uneven force distribution or jamming.
mechanism: A parallel-motion linkage system connects the base and moveable surface via levers at forward and rearward points, ensuring the surface remains parallel to the base throughout the crushing stroke. Force is applied endwise along the full length of the cylindrical object.
mechanism_raw: A parallelogram linkage system connects the base and moveable plate via levers at forward and rearward points, ensuring the plate remains parallel to the base throughout the crushing stroke. Force is applied endwise along the can's full length.

abstract: A hair curler with an aerated, elastic and elongated body for setting waves in wet, damp or dry hair; the aerated and elastic body is covered in whole or in part by an aerated elastic sheath provided in its-central part with protruding filament-like elements to facilitate winding hair onto the curler. The ends of the curler body are fitted with interlocking elements which allow the curler to be locked into a circular or semi-circular shape after the hair has been wound onto it.
problem: Creating a hair curler that can be shaped and locked into a specific curvature after winding hair, while remaining elastic for easy removal.
constraint: Balancing elasticity for hair retention and removal with sufficient structural rigidity to maintain the locked shape during use.
mechanism: An aerated, elastic body with protruding filaments for material winding is fitted with interlocking end elements. After winding, the ends are mechanically engaged to lock the device into a curved shape, retaining the set form until released.
mechanism_raw: An aerated, elastic body with protruding filaments for hair winding is fitted with interlocking end elements. After winding, the ends are mechanically engaged to lock the curler into a circular or semi-circular shape, retaining the set form until released.

abstract: A rotary blood pump includes a pump housing for receiving a flow straightener, a rotor mounted on rotor bearings and having an inducer portion and an impeller portion, and a diffuser. The entrance angle, outlet angle, axial and radial clearances of blades associated with the flow straightener, inducer portion, impeller portion and diffuser are optimized to minimize hemolysis while maintaining pump efficiency. The rotor bearing includes a bearing chamber that is filled with cross-linked blood or other bio-compatible material. A back emf integrated circuit regulates rotor operation and a microcomputer may be used to control one or more back emf integrated circuits. A plurality of magnets are disposed in each of a plurality of impeller blades with a small air gap. A stator may be axially adjusted on the pump housing to absorb bearing load and maximize pump efficiency.
problem: Balancing pump efficiency with minimal blood cell damage (hemolysis) in a rotary blood pump.
constraint: Trade-off between minimizing hemolysis (requiring reduced shear forces) and maintaining sufficient pump efficiency (requiring optimized fluid dynamics).
mechanism: Adjust geometric parameters of fluid-moving components in a multi-stage flow path to balance shear stress reduction against hydraulic efficiency, using sequential element shaping and stabilization mechanisms to maintain operational equilibrium.
mechanism_raw: Optimizing blade geometry (entrance angle, outlet angle, axial/radial clearances) across flow straightener, inducer, impeller, and diffuser to reduce shear stress on blood cells while maintaining hydraulic efficiency. Cross-linked blood in bearing chambers and stator adjustment further stabilize operation.

abstract: A system extracts contaminated vapors from soil or other subsurface regions by using changes in barometric pressure to operate sensitive check valves that control air entry and removal from wells in the ground. The system creates an efficient subterranean flow of air through a contaminated soil plume and causes final extraction of the contaminants from the soil to ambient air above ground without any external energy sources.
problem: Extracting subsurface contaminants without external energy input.
constraint: Reliance on ambient environmental conditions (barometric pressure changes) to generate sufficient airflow for effective contaminant removal.
mechanism: Harness ambient environmental pressure variations to cyclically actuate flow-control elements, generating directional airflow through a contaminated medium to drive contaminant transport to an external environment.
mechanism_raw: Using natural barometric pressure fluctuations to actuate sensitive check valves, creating passive subterranean airflow through contaminated soil plumes and driving vapor extraction to ambient air.

abstract: When the counter ion of hydrophilic cationic dyes is substituted with an organic anion including a sulfosuffinate anion such as diethylhexylsulfonate anion, an alkylbenzenesulfonate anion such as a dodecylbenzenesulfonate, an alkylsulfate anion such as a laurylsulfate anion, or a soap anion such as a laurylsulfate anion, the cationic dyes are imparted with hydrophobicity. An ink layer 3 containing the hydrophobic cationic dye is formed on a support 2 to provide a thermal transfer ink ribbon 10.
problem: Imparting hydrophobicity to hydrophilic cationic dyes for thermal transfer applications.
constraint: Maintaining dye functionality and color properties while achieving hydrophobicity through ion substitution.
mechanism: Modify surface interaction properties of charged chromophoric compounds by replacing their native counterions with organic anionic species, altering solubility characteristics to enable formation of a non-polar functional layer.
mechanism_raw: Substituting the counter ion of cationic dyes with organic anions (e.g., sulfosuccinate, alkylbenzenesulfonate, alkyl sulfate, or soap anions) to alter solubility and surface properties, enabling formation of a hydrophobic ink layer.

abstract: In a speech decoder which experiences frame erasure, the pitch delay associated with the first of consecutive erased frames is incremented. The incremented value is used as the pitch delay for the second of consecutive erased frames. Pitch delay associated with the first of consecutive erased frames may correspond to the last correctly received pitch delay information from a speech encoder (associated with a non-erased frame), or it may itself be the result of an increment added to a still previous value of pitch delay (associated with a still previous erased frame).
problem: Maintaining speech quality during frame erasure in speech decoding systems.
constraint: Avoiding perceptible discontinuities in pitch while minimizing computational complexity during error concealment.
mechanism: Extrapolate a temporal parameter from the most recent valid data point using iterative incremental adjustment during error intervals, creating a predictive continuity signal to mask perceptual artifacts in decoded output.
mechanism_raw: Incrementing the pitch delay value from the last correctly received frame (or a previously incremented value) for consecutive erased frames, creating a predictive extrapolation of pitch continuity to mask erasure artifacts.

abstract: A security improved credit, debit, pass, or cash card is a colorless and transparent semirigid plastic card member with non reflective faces, with no permanent imprinting on the card member to visually identify an issuer, an owner or a card number, but with temporary identification that can be removed by the owner of the card and can be visually read only when backed by an opaque sheet. The card has a bending line across a face of the card member that is a slit through the card with a hinge of flexible plastic film attached over the slit. The card has an opening cut through the card member to allow a person's finger nail to engage the opening to pull the card from a wallet or to attach the card on a shirt button.
reason: The patent describes a physical card design with structural features (slit/hinge, temporary ID) but lacks a causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through functional relationships. The innovations are product-specific configurations rather than transferable problem-solving principles.

abstract: A flowhood work station has an inspection chamber having a perforated inspection surface. An air filtration housing is in fluid communication with the perforated inspection surface. A blower is capable of directing air downwardly through the perforated inspection surface. A return air plenum is in fluid communication with the perforated inspection surface and with the air filtration housing. The return air plenum captures a substantial portion of the air passing through the perforated inspection surface and directs the air to the air filtration housing.
problem: Maintaining a controlled, clean airflow environment in a work station while efficiently recirculating and filtering air.
constraint: Balancing airflow velocity and filtration capacity to ensure consistent cleanliness without excessive pressure drop or energy consumption.
mechanism: A directed airflow source propels air through a distributed outlet surface, while a collection and redirection pathway captures the airflow and routes it through a filtration unit, forming a closed-loop system that sustains laminar flow and filtration efficiency by balancing velocity and resistance.
mechanism_raw: A blower directs air downwardly through a perforated inspection surface, while a return air plenum captures the airflow and redirects it to an air filtration housing, creating a closed-loop system that maintains laminar flow and filtration efficiency.

abstract: The subject invention involves processes for making granular compositions comprising soil release polymers, the polymers comprising at least about 10% of substantially linear esters having a backbone; the esters being uncapped or end-capped on one or both ends of the backbone; the esters comprising in their backbones oxyalkyleneoxy units and hydrophobic aryldicarbonyl units; the esters having a molecular weight of from about 500 to about 20,000; the polymers if in solid state having the tendency when exposed to moisture to spontaneously rearrange from an amorphous form which is readily soluble in water to a crystalline form which is relatively insoluble in water; the process comprising the following steps: PA1 a) taking the soil release polymers, in which are dispersed from 0% to about 25% alkylaryl or alkyl sulfonate crystallization-reducing stabilizers, in molten state at a temperature of at least about 180.degree. C., and rapidly dissolving the molten polymers in water, forming an aqueous polymer solution having a polymer concentration of up to about 50%, the average temperature of the solution being maintained below about 50.degree. C.; PA1 b) dispersing a nonionic surfactant in the molten polymers or in the water prior to step a), the surfactant being an alkylethoxy alcohol nonionic surfactant which is a condensation product of alkylalcohol and ethylene oxide, the alkyl portion being linear or branched, saturated or unsaturated, having from about 8 to about 22 carbon atoms, there being on average of from about 10 to about 100 moles ethoxy per mole surfactant, the nonionic surfactant being from about 2% to about 20% of the aqueous polymer solution, on a dry weight basis; and PA1 c) drying the aqueous polymer solution of b), thereby producing a granular composition having a water content of less than about 3%. The subject invention also involves soil release polymer granules comprising such polymers and nonionic surfactant and, optionally, stabilizers.
problem: Producing stable, free-flowing granular compositions of soil release polymers that maintain solubility and structural integrity during processing and storage.
constraint: Maintaining polymer concentration and temperature below thresholds that would degrade solubility or trigger premature crystallization during processing.
mechanism: A rapid dissolution process combines a molten polymer with a dispersion medium under controlled thermal conditions, followed by surfactant-mediated granulation and drying, leveraging a moisture-induced phase transition to form granules with tailored solubility and structural stability.
mechanism_raw: Rapid dissolution of molten polymer in water at controlled temperatures, followed by surfactant dispersion and drying, exploits the polymer's moisture-triggered phase transition to form granules with tailored solubility and crystallinity.

abstract: A hydrogen storing member which comprises at least two kinds of hydrogen storing materials comprising a first hydrogen storing material and a second hydrogen storing material capable of releasing or storing hydrogen in a range of at least one of temperature and pressure at which the first hydrogen storing material is in the .beta. phase having a high capacity for storing hydrogen.
problem: Storing hydrogen efficiently across varying temperature and pressure conditions using materials with complementary storage characteristics.
constraint: Ensuring the materials do not chemically or physically interfere with each other while maintaining their distinct phase-dependent storage capacities.
mechanism: Two storage media with overlapping operational ranges—one exhibiting high-capacity behavior in a specific phase and another active under different conditions—are combined to enable continuous storage/release without performance gaps, ensuring mutual compatibility during phase transitions.
mechanism_raw: Combining two hydrogen storage materials with overlapping operational ranges—one in a high-capacity beta phase and another active in different conditions—enables continuous hydrogen release/storage without gaps in performance.

abstract: A dental implant fixture intended for installation in maxillary and mandibular posterior regions where bone is cancellous internally and cortical externally characterized by labial and lingual cortical plates bounding a relatively large body of cancellous bone. The body of the implant fixture has a width dimension that is substantially the same as the distance between the labial and lingual cortical plates in the site of installation and has a stop flange of substantially the same width at its gingival end. When the implant is installed in that site the stop flange makes bone-to-implant contact with the coronal bone which joins the plates. The length of this implant fixture is limited so that when so installed it does not make contact with the mandibular canal or the sinus cavity.
problem: Securing a dental implant in bone tissue with a mix of cancellous and cortical structures while avoiding critical anatomical regions.
constraint: Precisely limiting implant length to avoid contact with critical anatomical structures while maximizing bone-to-implant contact for stability.
mechanism: A fixation element's transverse dimension is matched to the spacing between opposing structural boundaries, and a mechanical stop engages a reference surface to limit insertion depth, ensuring stable anchorage while preventing intrusion into sensitive regions.
mechanism_raw: Matching the implant's width to the distance between cortical plates and incorporating a stop flange for coronal bone contact ensures stable fixation without over-penetration into sensitive areas like the mandibular canal or sinus.

abstract: A spirally woven fabric as well as a prepreg and a rotary body each using the fabric therein is adapted for use as materials for high-speed rotary bodies such as flywheels for electric power storage. The fabric composed of interwoven warps and wefts is such that its warps are arranged in a spiral direction, and the warps positioned more outside in the radial (weft) direction have a higher specific elastic modulus in the warp direction than those positioned more inside in the radial direction whereby a rotary body made of the fabric is enabled to be rotated at a higher rotating speed without breakage of the wefts and consequent peeling-off between the warps.
problem: Preventing structural failure in high-speed rotary bodies (e.g., flywheels) caused by uneven stress distribution during rotation.
constraint: Balancing modulus gradients to ensure sufficient radial strength without excessive stiffness that could induce stress concentrations or manufacturing complexity.
mechanism: A composite structure incorporates reinforcement elements with a radial gradient in stiffness, where outer regions exhibit higher resistance to tensile forces, distributing stress to mitigate failure modes such as delamination or localized breakage during rotational loading.
mechanism_raw: Spirally weaving warps with radially increasing specific elastic modulus creates a composite where outer layers resist higher centrifugal forces, reducing weft breakage and delamination during high-speed rotation.

abstract: A stirrup straightener connector perpendicularly connects a stirrup having a stirrup bar to a saddle strap. The connector includes a stirrup holder and a holder bar. The stirrup holder has a first side portion, an indentation portion, an angled portion angled toward the indentation portion, and a second side portion. The holder bar has two ends, each end interconnectable with a respective side portion.
reason: The patent describes a specific mechanical connector geometry but does not articulate a causal mechanism that generalizes beyond its immediate structural application. The solution is a static arrangement of parts rather than a functional principle.

abstract: A steel cord which is suitable for reinforcing a rubber product and has excellent fatigue resistance. The steel cord has a layer-twisted structure formed by steel filaments respectively having a diameter of 0.15 mm to 0.25 mm. A core of the steel cord is formed by 1 to 4 steel filaments. A least 6 steel filaments are wound around the steel filaments of the core to form at least one layer. When the steel cord is bent from a straight state to a state in which a radius of curvature thereof is d/(17.times.10.sup.-3) wherein d is a diameter in millimeters of each steel filament in an outermost layer of the steel cord, a maximum amount of movement of each steel filament in the outermost layer in a cross-section of the steel cord is less than or equal to (-0.5454d+0.1454).times.10.sup.3 um. The steel cord preferably has a two-layer-twisted structure or a three-layer-twisted structure, and has an arrangement in which the diameters of the steel filaments gradually decrease from the core to the outermost layer.
problem: Achieving fatigue resistance in layered composite cables or cords under repeated bending stress.
constraint: Balancing filament diameter ratios and twist geometry to limit maximum filament displacement (≤ -0.5454d+0.1454 × 10³ µm) while maintaining structural integrity and manufacturability.
mechanism: Varying component dimensions in a layered structure to reduce relative movement between layers during deformation, thereby minimizing stress concentrations and enhancing durability. Controlled geometric arrangement of layers further limits displacement thresholds while preserving structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Gradually decreasing filament diameters from the core to the outer layers, combined with controlled layer-twisted geometry, reduces inter-filament movement during bending. This minimizes localized stress concentrations and wear, enhancing fatigue resistance.

abstract: A filter rod is produced by adding a water-soluble polymer in the form of an aqueous solution or dispersion, or in a particulate form, to a tow of cellulose ester fiber, with the amount of any water used being controlled within 25 parts by weight relative to 100 parts by weight of the tow, and wrapping the treated tow in wrapping paper. The water contained in the filter rod is removed or the particulate water-soluble polymer is melted by heating to bond the fiber to provide a tobacco filter. The proportion of the water-soluble polymer is 0.5 to 30 parts by weight to 100 parts by weight of the tow. To reduce the amount of water relative to the tow, a hot-melt adhesive water-soluble polymer may be employed. As the amount of water added to the tow is thus decreased, the tow can be smoothly wrapped up even at a high speed so that filter productivity is improved. This tobacco filter is highly wet-disintegratable and, hence, contributes to mitigation of the environmental pollution.
problem: Enabling high-speed production of fiber-based filters while maintaining environmental compatibility and structural integrity.
constraint: Limiting water to ≤25 parts per 100 parts tow to prevent processing delays while ensuring sufficient polymer activation for bonding.
mechanism: Controlling the ratio of a processing medium to material mass and using a soluble binding agent to enable rapid shaping without compromising adhesion. Subsequent removal of the medium bonds components, enabling fast processing and post-use disintegration.
mechanism_raw: Controlling water content relative to fiber mass and using a water-soluble polymer as a binding agent allows rapid wrapping without compromising adhesion. Heating or water removal then bonds fibers, enabling fast processing and wet-disintegration post-use.

abstract: The invention relates to a process and a device for burning oxidizable components in a vehicle gas to be purified, comprising a gas inlet (36), a burner (19) with an attached flame pipe (22) opening into a main combustion chamber (24) comprising a bottom and side walls, an annular chamber leading from the side of the main combustion chamber bottom (21), a heat exchanger (32) around which flows the purified gas and through which flows the gas to be purified, and a gas outlet (38). To obtain good combustion with a compact construction, especially to make the best possible use of the geometric dwell time in the main combustion chamber, it is proposed that the main combustion chamber be constructed in such a way and/or has such guide components (40,42,44) that the gas flowing from the bottom towards the annular chamber is distributed completely or largely uniformly over the cross-section of the main combustion chamber.
problem: Achieving efficient combustion of oxidizable gases in a compact reactor design.
constraint: Optimizing guide geometry to maintain uniform flow distribution without increasing pressure drop or reactor volume.
mechanism: Distributing a reactant flow uniformly across a reaction zone to maximize geometric dwell time and ensure complete oxidation. This balances compact construction with effective heat and mass transfer by optimizing flow distribution geometry.
mechanism_raw: Guide components distribute gas uniformly across the combustion chamber cross-section, maximizing geometric dwell time and ensuring complete oxidation. This balances compact construction with effective heat and mass transfer.

abstract: Oxide coatings are formed with a desired crystallographic texture over a large surface area. A metallic substrate is electrodeposited or vacuum deposited with a preferred crystallographic orientation, and a sol-gel/thermal process is used to form a "pseudo-epitaxial" oxide coating having crystallites that are influenced by the crystallographic orientation of the substrate. In one embodiment, p-type nickel oxide coatings with desirable electronic properties are produced by sol-gel/thermal processing on nickel substrates electrodeposited from a sulfamate nickel bath at a relatively high current density and low temperature. The electrodeposited nickel substrate has a strong Ni{100} preferred orientation. Epitaxial effects during sol-gel/thermal formation of NiO on the electrodeposited substrate enhance the extent to which the NiO{100} and NiO{111} crystal facets are aligned parallel to the coating surface, and minimize the NiO{110} orientation. This texture modification significantly improves the photoresponse of the nickel oxide coating. The method is anticipated to be useful in other metal oxide/metal substrate systems for the production of catalysts, cathodes for lithium ion and nickel-cadmium batteries, photoelectrochemical printed circuits, high-temperature electronic devices, flat panel displays, photoelectrochemical solar cells, and sensors. An advantage of the invention is that electrodeposition, vacuum deposition, and sol-gel/thermal processes are suitable for coating large surface areas.
problem: Producing oxide coatings with controlled crystallographic texture over large surface areas for enhanced functional properties.
constraint: Matching substrate orientation and processing conditions (e.g., current density, temperature) to minimize unwanted crystal orientations (e.g., NiO{110}) while scaling to large areas.
mechanism: Using a substrate with a preferred crystallographic orientation to template the growth of an oxide layer, aligning specific crystal facets parallel to the surface to enhance functional properties. Processing conditions are matched to suppress unwanted orientations while scaling to large areas.
mechanism_raw: Electrodeposition of a substrate with a preferred crystallographic orientation (e.g., Ni{100}) templates the growth of pseudo-epitaxial oxide coatings during sol-gel/thermal processing.
