This aligns specific crystal facets (e.g., NiO{100} and NiO{111}) parallel to the surface, improving properties like photoresponse.

abstract: Speech data is converted into logarithmic spectrum data and orthogonally transformed to develop feature vectors. Normalization coefficient data and unit vector data are stored. An inner product of the feature vector data and the unit vector data is calculated. The inner product may be the average of inner products for a word or a sentence, or may be a regressive average of them. A normalization vector, which corresponds to a second or higher order curve obtained by least-square error approximation of the speech data on logarithmic spectrum space, is calculated on the transformed feature vector space by using the inner product, the normalization coefficient data, and the unit vector data. Normalization of the feature vectors is performed by subtracting the normalization vector from the feature vectors on the transformed feature vector space. Then, a recognition is performed based on the normalized feature vector.
problem: Normalizing speech feature vectors to improve recognition accuracy despite speaker and environmental variations in the logarithmic spectrum domain.
constraint: The normalization must be computed efficiently using pre-stored unit vector data and normalization coefficients, and the orthogonal transformation must preserve discriminative features while enabling the least-square approximation to capture the dominant systematic variation.
mechanism: A data normalization process transforms input vectors into a feature space where a normalization vector is computed via least-square error approximation of the data distribution. This normalization vector, representing a fitted curve to the data, is derived using inner products between the input vectors and pre-stored reference vectors combined with stored coefficients. The normalization vector is then subtracted from the transformed input vectors to remove systematic bias or trend components while preserving discriminative features.
mechanism_raw: A normalization vector is computed via least-square error approximation of the speech data in a transformed feature vector space, using inner products between feature vectors and pre-stored unit vectors combined with stored normalization coefficients. This normalization vector represents a second-or-higher-order curve fitted to the data distribution. The normalization vector is then subtracted from the feature vectors in the transformed space, effectively removing systematic bias or trend components before recognition.
residual_terms: ["least-square error approximation", "inner products", "pre-stored reference vectors", "stored coefficients", "transformed feature vector space"]

abstract: A push lever activated dead-bolt lock for a door is described. The dead-bolt lock includes a dead-bolt axially mounted within a sleeve, the sleeve having a slot formed in each lateral side of the sleeve, the slots aligned parallel to each other and having a horizontal section and a vertical section; a cross member mounted within the dead-bolt in a position so that a first end and a second end of the cross member protrude through each slot; a spring mounted between the dead-bolt and the back wall of the sleeve; and an activator lever mounted so that one end of the activator lever contacts the first end of the cross member and the other end of the activator lever protrudes through to the exterior of the door, the activator lever oriented that movement of the lever by user moves the cross member from a position in a vertical section of the slot to a position in a horizontal section of the slot, the movement of the cross member releasing tension on the spring, the spring propelling the dead-bolt into a locked position. The lock is unlocked by returning the cross member to a vertical section of the T-shaped slot using a key. The key is inserted into a key acceptor, the key acceptor including an arm which contacts the first end of the cross member and is oriented such that when the key is turned, the arm propels cross member along horizontal section of the slot and into a vertical section of the slot, the first end of the cross member resting against the end of the activator lever opposite the end of the activator lever that protrudes to the exterior of the door. Thus, the user can activate the lock by simply pushing the activator lever.
problem: Providing a simple user interface (push lever) to activate a dead-bolt lock that requires significant spring force to move the bolt into the locked position.
constraint: The mechanism must reliably transition between the loaded (vertical slot) and released (horizontal slot) states, and the key-based reversal must be able to move the cross member back to the vertical position against the spring force to re-lock the mechanism for the next cycle.
mechanism: A mechanical input force is converted into a release action through a two-stage linkage system. A movable cross member transitions between a loaded state (where stored energy is retained) and a released state (where stored energy is discharged). The user input actuates the cross member to shift from the loaded to the released state, enabling a pre-loaded energy storage element to perform high-force work. A separate reversal mechanism resets the cross member to the loaded state against the energy storage element's force.
mechanism_raw: A push lever moves a cross member from a vertical slot section (where spring tension is loaded and the bolt is held in an unlocked position) to a horizontal slot section (where spring tension is released). This two-stage mechanical linkage converts the user's low-force push input into a release action that allows a pre-loaded spring to perform the high-force work of propelling the dead-bolt into the locked position. The key mechanism is decoupling the user input from the primary locking force by using the input to release stored energy rather than directly performing the locking motion.
residual_terms: ["cross member", "loaded state", "released state", "energy storage element", "reversal mechanism"]

abstract: A holding rail is useful with a storage file having stiff cover sides and an upright clip holding presentation pages. The rail may be used to hold the storage file in a presentation position or to hold the presentation pages contained in the file in a clamped-down position. The rail is also useful for linear measurement. The holding rail is substantially flat with a plurality of upwardly bent legs. At least one upwardly bent leg is located at opposing end portions of the rail. The storage file may be held in a presentation position by placing the edge of each of the stiff cover sides into one of the upwardly bent legs of the rail. The rail thereby supports the storage file with the upright clips racing outwardly and the presentation pages in the presentation position. A plurality of tapered slots or other perforations are formed within the rail. The tapered slots may engage the upright clip, thereby holding the presentation pages of the storage file in a clamped-down position. At least one of the edges of the rail has divisions such that the rail is useful for linear measurement.
reason: The patent describes a holding rail with bent legs and tapered slots as a product design. While it uses compliant bent legs for support and tapered slots for clamping, these are simple geometric features specific to the storage file application rather than a transferable problem-solving mechanism with a causal functional relationship.

abstract: A tray for supporting food and beverages relative to a back of a seat. The inventive device includes a support assembly positionable over sides of a seat and against a seat back. An upper tray is secured to the support assembly and includes lateral cup holders to support beverages and food upon the tray. A lower tray can be provided and secured to the support assembly beneath the upper tray so as to support additional food and beverages relative to the seat back.
reason: The patent describes a tray mounting system that uses a support assembly wrapped around a seat. This is a generic mounting approach (using existing structure as an anchor) without a specific causal mechanism that produces a non-obvious useful effect beyond basic mechanical support.

abstract: A centrifugal filter device includes a housing having an essentially cylindrical housing wall about an axis of the housing and an annular trough located radially inwardly of the housing wall, a cap fitted to the housing and having a lid spaced from an upper edge of the housing wall, the cap further comprising an annular side wall spaced radially outwardly from the housing wall and defining an annular catchment chamber having an annular tapered deflection surface therein, a first exit port in the side wall of the cap, a second exit port at the trough of the housing, an inner chamber situated within the housing and adapted to rotate about the axis, the inner chamber having an essentially cylindrical wall inwardly spaced from the cylindrical wall of the housing so as to define an annular space therebetween, an internal drain communicating an interior of the chamber with the trough of the housing, and an annular closure element having an opening communicating the interior of the chamber with the annular catchment chamber of the cap, and an inlet extending from outside the filter through the cap and the opening of the closure element to the interior of the chamber.
problem: Separating materials using centrifugal force in a compact device while controlling the flow of separated fractions to different exit ports.
constraint: The device must maintain rotation of the inner chamber while allowing controlled fluid communication through the annular closure element, and the geometric arrangement of the catchment chamber and deflection surface must direct separated materials to the correct exit ports without disrupting the centrifugal separation process.
mechanism: A rotating chamber generates centrifugal force to separate materials by density. A controlled communication pathway, defined by an opening in an annular closure element, allows separated materials to transfer from the rotating chamber to a stationary catchment region while maintaining rotation. The catchment region's geometric arrangement, including a tapered deflection surface, directs separated materials toward designated exit ports based on their density or trajectory.
mechanism_raw: A rotating inner chamber creates centrifugal force that separates materials by density. An annular catchment chamber, defined by the cap's side wall with a tapered deflection surface, collects the separated material. An annular closure element with an opening provides controlled communication between the rotating inner chamber and the stationary catchment chamber, allowing separated material to flow from the rotating chamber to the catchment chamber while maintaining the rotation. The tapered deflection surface directs the separated material toward the appropriate exit port.
residual_terms: ["annular closure element", "tapered deflection surface", "catchment region", "exit ports", "centrifugal force"]

abstract: A shoulder-launched multi-purpose assault weapon with a removable rocket tube and spotter barrel is provided. The rocket tube and spotter barrel assembly is a standard receiver and trigger assembly. The grouping of the tube and barrel in a single removable assembly allows quick field replacement for either repair or reconfiguration of the weapon to a different rocket size. The sight assembly is also removable by sliding the sight out of dovetail attachment points. A further benefit is that different rocket tube assemblies may be pre-boresighted at the factory, thereby also reducing field assembly time.
problem: Need for rapid field replacement and reconfiguration of weapon components (rocket tube, spotter barrel, sight) without extensive setup or recalibration time.
constraint: The module must use standard mechanical interfaces to maintain compatibility with the base weapon while being removable enough for quick field replacement.
mechanism: Grouping functionally related components into a single removable unit that maintains pre-established alignment, so that swapping the unit automatically restores correct calibration without field adjustment. Standardized interfaces ensure compatibility across different configurations.
mechanism_raw: Grouping functionally related components into a single removable module that maintains pre-calibrated alignment (factory pre-boresighting), so that swapping the module automatically restores correct calibration without field adjustment. Standardized interfaces (receiver/trigger assembly, dovetail) ensure compatibility across different configurations.

abstract: A process for cutting out decorative, artistic designs, and the three-dimensioned decorative and artistic products produced thereby which are incorporatable into articles of manufacture. The process creates relief designs by angle cutting, at predetermined and variable cut-angles and predetermined and variable cut-widths. The decorative cut-out piece, cut from a base piece, is one-directionally removable and one-directionally insertable into the aperture created when the piece is cut from the base piece. The cut-out piece inserts into the corresponding aperture a distance which is determined by a combination of cut-angle and cut-width. The maximum cut-angle and the maximum cut-width is limited by the thickness of the base piece. The cut width is substantially equal to the saw blade cut width or the width of the cut produced by any appropiate cutting device. The relief design for the three-dimensioned products is created by inserting the cut-out piece into the aperture and pushing it through the aperture until it binds. The cut-out piece forming the relief design protrudes from one surface of the base piece while it is recessed in the other surface of the base piece. The process may also be applied to articles where one or both surfaces are substantially planar, curved or actuate. The products may also be used with the decorative cut-out piece removed from the aperture, or inserted into the aperture such that the cut-out piece is flush with the surface of the base piece. The outline of the cut-out piece shows as an artistic design.
problem: Need to create three-dimensional relief designs in decorative products with controlled protrusion from one surface and recession from the other, using a single cutting operation.
constraint: Maximum cut-angle and cut-width are limited by the thickness of the base piece, and cut width is constrained to equal the cutting tool width.
mechanism: Controlled geometric cutting at variable angles and widths creates an interference fit between a cut-out piece and its aperture, where the insertion depth is determined by the combination of cut-angle and cut-width. Pushing the piece through until it binds creates a self-locking joint with a predetermined protrusion/recession profile.
mechanism_raw: Controlled geometric cutting at variable angles and widths creates an interference fit between a cut-out piece and its aperture, where the insertion depth is determined by the combination of cut-angle and cut-width. Pushing the piece through until it binds creates a self-locking joint with a predetermined protrusion/recession profile.

abstract: A turbofan, preferentially with separated-flows or short nacelle, comprises two thrust reversal doors normally housed in casings formed in the nacelle and located totally outside the inner enclosure of the nacelle. When a thrust reversal effect is sought, the doors are directed in the prolongation of the fan channel, behind the rear end of the nacelle. Thus, the doors are not submitted to the engine bypass air of the jet engine when the aircraft is in flight and the inner enclosure of the nacelle presents neither leak nor discontinuity and may be totally anti-noise treated.
problem: Need for thrust reversal capability in a turbofan engine without disrupting normal bypass airflow during flight or creating leaks/discontinuities in the nacelle inner enclosure.
constraint: The doors must be housed completely outside the inner enclosure to avoid leaks and allow full anti-noise treatment of the nacelle interior.
mechanism: Positioning deployable functional components entirely outside the primary flow enclosure so they remain inactive and sealed during normal operation, and only deploy in a specific direction when thrust reversal is needed, avoiding interference with bypass air.
mechanism_raw: Positioning deployable functional components (thrust reversal doors) entirely outside the primary flow enclosure so they remain inactive and sealed during normal operation, and only deploy in a specific direction (prolongation of the fan channel, behind the nacelle) when thrust reversal is needed, avoiding interference with bypass air.

abstract: A workbench-based interchangeable power tool mounting and operating apparatus includes a workbench frame including a base supported on an upper portion of the frame, at least one main support pallet for mounting an electrically powered tool thereon, an electrical system including a first portion mounted on the main support pallet having a first electrical connector and a second portion mounted on the base and workbench frame having a second electrical connector for connection with an external electrical power source and being matable with the first electrical connector, and a pair of alignment members mounted on the base for receiving and supporting the main support pallet on the base and slidably guiding the main support pallet into and from an installed position on the upper base of the workbench frame in which the first electrical connector of the first portion of the electrical system is electrically mated with the second electrical connector of the second portion of the electrical system for electrically connecting a power tool mounted on the main support pallet with the external electrical power source.
problem: Need for quick mounting of power tools on a workbench with simultaneous mechanical positioning and electrical connection, avoiding manual wiring or separate alignment steps.
constraint: The alignment members must guide the pallet with sufficient precision to ensure reliable electrical connector mating without manual adjustment.
mechanism: Combining mechanical alignment and electrical connection in a single guided insertion motion: alignment members physically guide a support pallet into a precise installed position where electrical connectors on the pallet and base automatically mate, ensuring both mechanical and electrical connection occur simultaneously.
mechanism_raw: Combining mechanical alignment and electrical connection in a single guided insertion motion: alignment members physically guide a support pallet into a precise installed position where electrical connectors on the pallet and base automatically mate, ensuring both mechanical and electrical connection occur simultaneously.

abstract: Apparatus for detecting dimensional information of a workpiece such as a canted log is used to control a gang saw mounted on a pivot axis to cut the log into substantially even thickness boards while moving the log past the cutting device and pivoting the gang saw to accommodate curvature in the log.
problem: Need to cut irregular workpieces (such as canted logs with curvature) into substantially even-thickness boards despite varying geometry along the length of the workpiece.
constraint: The cutting operation must continue while the tool pivots to accommodate the workpiece, requiring simultaneous motion of feed and tool adjustment.
mechanism: Using real-time dimensional sensing of the workpiece to dynamically adjust cutting tool geometry (pivot angle) during the cutting process, continuously compensating for curvature and irregularities as the workpiece moves past the cutting device.
mechanism_raw: Using real-time dimensional sensing of the workpiece to dynamically adjust cutting tool geometry (pivot angle of a gang saw) during the cutting process, continuously compensating for curvature and irregularities as the workpiece moves past the cutting device.

abstract: A rotary actuator (16) has an inner body (32) forming a rotor and at least one outer body (34) forming a stator. The inner body (32) and outer body (34) carry blades (40,44) arranged in an alternating manner and defining between them two series of variable volume chambers. The cross-section of the chambers and the height of the triangular blades (40,44) decreases from one end to the other, as a result of a substantially frustum-shape of the inner body (32). Such an actuator (16) can be used for controlling an aircraft rudder or control surface and it is then positioned along the articulation axis of the rudder or control surface.
problem: Need for a compact rotary actuator that delivers controlled, smooth torque output for aircraft rudder or control surface actuation along an articulation axis.
constraint: The taper angle and blade geometry must balance torque smoothness and chamber volume variation against structural integrity and packaging constraints in aircraft applications.
mechanism: A geometric gradient in chamber cross-section and blade height along an articulation axis creates variable-volume chambers whose progressive volume changes produce controlled, smooth rotational torque through fluid displacement.
mechanism_raw: The frustum-shaped inner rotor body creates a geometric gradient in chamber cross-section and blade height from one end to the other. As the rotor turns, the alternating inner and outer blades define two series of variable-volume chambers whose volume changes follow this gradient, producing a controlled and progressive fluid displacement that translates into smooth, continuous rotational torque.

abstract: A videoendoscopic surgery training system (10) provides training in videoendoscopic surgery techniques. A base (14) supports a simulated anatomical structure (12). A shield (20) blocks a trainee's direct line-of-sight view of the simulated anatomical structure. A reflector assembly (24, 34) reflects an image of the simulated anatomical structure past the shield. A first mirror (24) reflects an image of the simulated anatomical structure that is oriented away from the trainee. A second mirror (34) optically communicates with the first mirror to reflect an image of the simulated anatomical structure that is oriented toward the trainee.
problem: Need to train surgeons in videoendoscopic techniques where direct line-of-sight to the surgical site is unavailable, as the surgeon must rely on a video monitor during actual procedures.
constraint: The mirror arrangement must accurately reproduce the orientation, perspective, and parallax of endoscopic visualization while maintaining a complete physical barrier to direct sight.
mechanism: A physical barrier blocks direct line-of-sight to a target area, while a multi-stage reflective system redirects an image past the barrier and back to the observer, forcing reliance on the redirected image to replicate indirect visualization conditions.
mechanism_raw: A physical shield blocks the trainee's direct view of the simulated anatomy, while a dual-mirror reflector assembly redirects the image past the shield—first reflecting it away from the trainee, then reflecting it back toward the trainee. This forces the trainee to rely exclusively on the reflected image, replicating the indirect visualization experience of real endoscopic surgery.

abstract: A hot-stamping foil including a metallic layer carried on flexible carrier layer, and having a layer of heat-activated adhesive on the underside of the metallic layer and a layer of a lacquer composition coating the upper surface of the metallic layer, the lacquer being a blend of at least 50% by weight, based on the total dry weight of the lacquer composition, of a copolymer of styrene and maleic anhydride (SMA copolymer) with at least one other acrylic copolymer selected from polymethylmethacrylate copolymers, polyacrylic acid copolymers and styrene/acrylic acid copolymers. Such lacquers have an improved heat resistance.
reason: This patent describes a specific materials composition (a polymer blend with ≥50% SMA copolymer) to achieve heat resistance. The solution is achieved through material selection and formulation rather than a causal functional mechanism that operates through a process or system-level principle.

abstract: A computer system for controlling the parameters used during molecule transfer operations. The computer system includes a processor coupled to a memory. The memory stores instructions that are executed by the processor. The computer system controls the value of parameters that affect the characteristics of pulses delivered by a pulse generating circuit to a solution. The pulse generating unit delivers individual pulses during cycles. The cumulative pulse delivered during a specified number of cycles is a pulse output. The magnitude of a pulse output is determined by the number of cycles corresponding to the pulse output and the characteristics of the individual pulses delivered during the cycles. A pulse group is a series of pulse outputs. The computer system controls a molecule transfer operation by causing the pulse generation circuit to deliver one or more pulse groups to the solution. A user selects the shape and number of pulse groups to be delivered for an operation. The computer alters the operational parameters used by the pulse generation circuit to cause the pulse generation circuit to deliver pulse groups having the selected shapes.
problem: Need for precise, user-programmable control of molecule transfer operations (e.g., electrophoresis) where the delivered energy profile must be tailored to specific biological or chemical requirements.
constraint: The system must balance the granularity of individual pulse control with the flexibility of group-level user selection to achieve both precision in molecule transfer and ease of operation.
mechanism: Pulses are organized hierarchically: individual pulses accumulate into cumulative outputs, which are grouped into user-selectable units. User specifications for group shape and count are translated into operational parameters for a pulse generation circuit, which delivers corresponding pulse profiles.
mechanism_raw: Pulses are organized hierarchically: individual pulses accumulate over cycles to form a cumulative 'pulse output,' and multiple pulse outputs form a 'pulse group.' The user selects the shape and number of pulse groups, and the computer system translates these group-level specifications into specific operational parameters for the pulse generation circuit, which then delivers the corresponding pulse shapes to the solution.

abstract: The present invention relates to the use of water-dispersible and/or water-emulsifiable amphiphilic co-oligomer of fatty crotonates and radical-copolymerizable hydrophilic ethylenically unsaturated acids and/or anhydrides thereof which may also contain small quantities of other copolymerizable comonomers, for the oiling and optionally waterproof finishing of leathers and skins.
reason: This patent describes a specific chemical composition (an amphiphilic co-oligomer of fatty crotonates and hydrophilic acids) for leather finishing. The solution is achieved through chemical formulation and material properties rather than a causal functional mechanism that operates through a process or system-level principle.

abstract: A yarn feed mechanism for use with a tufting machine is disclosed. The tufting machine has a needle bar with an aligned series of spaced tufting needles disposed thereon, each of which is supplied with yarn from a yarn supply for penetrating a backing material to sew tufts of yarn therein. The yarn feed mechanism includes a support framework mounted on the tufting machine adjacent a yarn feed path extending from the yarn supply to the needles of the tufting machine, with at least one yarn feed roll assembly mounted for rotation on the support framework. The yarn feed roll assembly further includes an elongate yarn feed roll having an exterior yarn driving periphery extending along a longitudinal axis parallel to the needle bar of the tufting machine, the yarn feed roll being rotated in timed relationship with the reciprocation of the needle bar. An orbital yarn applying member spaced from the yarn feed roll is supported on the support framework and is movable about the yarn feed roll in an orbital path from a yarn receiving position to a yarn applying position. The yarn applying member is used to apply portions of selected yarns against at least a portion of the yarn driving periphery of the yarn feed roll in the yarn applying position for controlling the rate at which the yarn is fed to the needles of the tufting machine. The yarn applying member of the invention may comprise at least one concentrically orbited control rod spaced from and parallel to the yarn feed roll, or may comprise a pinch roller orbited eccentrically about the yarn feed roll, and constructed to be moved into a yarn applying position engaged with the periphery of the yarn feed roll.
problem: Controlling the rate at which yarn is fed to tufting needles in a tufting machine to ensure consistent tuft formation.
constraint: The orbital path and timing of the applying member must be synchronized with the reciprocation of the needle bar and the rotation of the feed roll to avoid disrupting the tufting process.
mechanism: A moving element interacts with a rotating surface through synchronized orbital and rotational motion to dynamically adjust contact pressure and engagement duration, thereby modulating the feed rate of a material to a downstream process. The synchronization ensures temporal alignment between the moving element's path, the surface's rotation, and the downstream process's cycle to maintain consistent material delivery without disruption.
mechanism_raw: An orbital yarn applying member moves around a rotating yarn feed roll, selectively applying portions of yarns against the roll's periphery. This orbital motion, combined with timed rotation of the feed roll, dynamically adjusts the contact pressure and engagement duration between the yarn and the roll, thereby modulating the yarn feed rate to the needles.

abstract: The method and associated apparatus of the present invention polishes the front face of a ferrule with first and second slurries such that an end portion of each optical fiber which extends through and is held by the ferrule protrudes beyond the preferentially etched front face of the ferrule by a preselected length. In order to preferentially etch the front face of ferrule as desired, the front face of the ferrule is polished with a first slurry having a plurality of suspended particulates of a first predetermined size on average which initiates the preferential etch of the ferrule relative to the optical fibers. Thereafter, the front face of the ferrule is polished with a second slurry having a plurality of suspended particles of a second predetermined size on average. The slurries are preferably selected such that the second predetermined size is less than the first predetermined size so that the polishing of the front face of the ferrule with the second slurry completes the preferential etch of the ferrule relative to the optical fibers. By preferentially etching the front face of the ferrule relative to the optical fibers, the optical fibers will protrude beyond the front face of the ferrule by a preselected length which does not vary significantly from fiber to fiber.
problem: Achieving consistent protrusion lengths of optical fibers extending through a ferrule after polishing, despite variations in material properties or fiber alignment.
constraint: The particle size difference between the two slurries must be precisely calibrated to balance etch initiation and completion without over-polishing the fibers or leaving residual ferrule material.
mechanism: Sequential application of two abrasive agents with distinct particle sizes to a workpiece, where the first agent initiates preferential material removal from one component relative to another, and the second agent completes the removal to achieve uniform protrusion. The particle size differential controls the etch initiation and completion phases to balance material removal rates.
mechanism_raw: Sequential polishing with two slurries of differing particle sizes. The first slurry (larger particles) initiates preferential etching of the ferrule material relative to the fibers, while the second slurry (smaller particles) completes the etch, ensuring uniform fiber protrusion by controlling the differential material removal rate.

abstract: A centrifuge of the type including a housing and a rotatable bowl, and including a heating jacket located therebetween. The heating jacket is established through inflatable seals which selectively seal a space located between the bowl and the housing. The seals may be inflated when the bowl is stationary. A heating fluid is then introduced into the heating jacket so that collected solids in the bowl may be heated and dried. A vacuum may be applied to the bowl to assist in the removal of moisture from the solids. A scraper assembly, including at least one scraper, is disposed within the bowl. The scraper assembly pivots between a stowed position and an operative position to remove the solid that has collected on the inside wall surface of the bowl.
problem: Drying collected solids within a rotating centrifuge bowl without interrupting the separation process or requiring manual intervention.
constraint: The inflatable seals must maintain a reliable seal during both rotation and stationary phases, and the heating/vacuum parameters must be balanced to avoid damaging the solids or compromising the bowl's structural integrity.
mechanism: A sealed rotating chamber uses inflatable barriers to create a controlled environment where heat transfer and reduced pressure accelerate moisture removal from retained solids. A mechanical scraping element, actuated independently of the chamber's rotation, removes dried solids from the chamber walls without interrupting the separation process.
mechanism_raw: Inflatable seals between the bowl and housing create a heating jacket when inflated, allowing a heating fluid to circulate and dry the solids. A vacuum is applied to the bowl to accelerate moisture removal, while a pivoting scraper assembly removes dried solids from the bowl wall.

abstract: A process and apparatus for dissolving a mixed oxide or mixture of oxides of uranium and plutonium. The powder is added with nitric acid to a chamber to dissolve uranium oxide, and the solution is circulated through a circuit of the apparatus with a portion of the solution passing through a filter. At least a portion of the filtered solution containing dissolved uranium oxide is removed from the apparatus, while returning non-filtered circulating solution containing non-dissolved plutonium oxide to the chamber. The removal of solution is then terminated, a monovalent silver salt is added and divalent silver is generated in-situ by electrolysis, the divalent silver causing dissolution of the plutonium oxide.
problem: Dissolving a mixed oxide of uranium and plutonium, where the two components have different dissolution behaviors in nitric acid.
constraint: The filtration and solution removal steps must be timed to isolate the uranium-rich solution before introducing the silver salt, and the electrolysis parameters must be controlled to avoid over-reduction or secondary reactions.
mechanism: A two-stage chemical dissolution process where a first reagent selectively dissolves one component of a mixed material, followed by isolation of the intermediate solution. A second reagent, activated via an electrochemical reduction step, then dissolves the remaining component in situ. The sequential isolation and activation steps exploit differing dissolution behaviors to achieve complete material breakdown.
mechanism_raw: A two-step dissolution process: first, nitric acid dissolves uranium oxide, with the solution filtered and partially removed. The remaining non-dissolved plutonium oxide is then dissolved in situ by generating divalent silver via electrolysis after adding a monovalent silver salt, leveraging a chemical reduction mechanism specific to plutonium oxide.

abstract: A curling iron system which, in addition to conventional mechanical elements of base, curling irons, ovens, holders and the like, utilizes an accurate temperature measurement and display capability adapted for use by salon personnel without sophisticated technical know-how. The temperature measurement is implemented by a thermocouple and the display is implemented using a plurality of light emitting diodes (LEDs) connected to the thermocouple by a thermocouple amplifier and a display driver. The combination of thermocouple, LED display and intermediate electronics, operates to provide an accurate indication of the actual surface temperature of the curling iron and thus assure that the iron will be precisely the appropriate temperature for curling or straightening the particular thickness hair being serviced. In the preferred embodiment disclosed herein, the thermocouple is mounted on a platform adjacent the oven and the display is positioned on a vertically oriented member behind the thermocouple platform. In this manner, the user can simply remove the curling iron from the oven chamber and place it on the thermocouple platform while reading the LED display.
reason: The patent describes a standard temperature measurement system using a thermocouple and LED display, which are well-known components. While the placement of the thermocouple on a platform adjacent to the oven is user-friendly, it does not introduce a novel causal mechanism for solving a problem beyond conventional temperature sensing and display integration.

abstract: A tilt and height indicator for a forklift truck including a tape reel connected to the forks of the forklift to sense their relative height. An indicator panel includes plural sets of indicators, with each set indicating when the forks are in a proper pre-programmed position, just above, or just below this position, or well above or well below this position. The plural indicators may each be programmed to independent heights which are within the range of indicated heights for another indicator, such that infinitesimal differences in shelf heights may be accounted for. All indicators may be active at the same time, or the operator may change to a separate mode in which only a chosen indicator set is active. The present invention also includes a tilt sensor in the form of a rod connected to the piston of the tilt cylinder and adjustably mounting a magnet. A sensor box is mounted on the cylinder and includes a plurality of spaced Hall-effect transistors. The location of the magnet with respect to the transistors is dependant upon the relative position of the mast and chassis, such that the magnet on the rod will be in proximity to various ones of the transistors, thus activating those transistors. The indicator panel may include a tilt display having a plurality of indicators corresponding to the transistors to provide an accurate indication of the tilt condition of the mast.
problem: Accurately indicating the height and tilt position of forklift forks relative to pre-programmed target positions, including handling infinitesimal differences in shelf heights.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise, multi-threshold positional feedback without overwhelming the operator with excessive information, while maintaining mechanical simplicity in a vibrating industrial environment.
mechanism: Using multiple independently programmable indicator sets that activate based on proximity to target positions, combined with a sensor system that translates mechanical displacement into discrete electrical states. The indicators provide real-time feedback on whether the forks are at, above, or below target positions, while the sensor maps physical displacement to electrical signals for tilt and height measurement.
mechanism_raw: Using multiple independently programmable indicator sets that activate based on proximity to target heights, combined with a magnetic sensor system that translates mechanical tilt position into electrical signals via Hall-effect transistors. The indicators provide real-time feedback on whether the forks are at, above, or below target positions, while the tilt sensor maps physical displacement to discrete electrical states.

abstract: Heat-sealable composite film having good surface slip with very good thermoforming properties based on polyamide and polyolefins, wherein the film consists of PA0 at least one layer of aliphatic polyamide (A) and PA0 at least one layer of a polymer blend (B) consisting of 10-60 wt. % of amorphous polyamide and 40-90% of aliphatic polyamide and PA0 at least one thermoplastic heat sealing layer (C) and PA0 at least one bonding layer (D), arranged in such a manner that a heat sealing layer and a layer of aliphatic polyamide are located on the outer sides of the film, and wherein the film is not stretched.
reason: The patent describes a material composition and layer arrangement (polyamide blends, heat-sealing layers) to achieve specific physical properties. The solution is a static material structure rather than a causal functional mechanism that produces an effect through a process or interaction.

abstract: A portable ladder module is provided, comprising a primary support member having a first step; a secondary support member having a second step, wherein the secondary support member is slidable relative to the primary support member. A lock is operatively disposed between the primary support member and the secondary support member for selectively locking the position of the secondary support member relative to the primary support member in an extended position and a retracted position. A strap having a quick-release buckle is secured to the primary support member for holding the ladder module to a tree, and a pair of rigid tubing members on each of the primary support member and the secondary support member are present for stabilizing the ladder module against the tree. Preferably, a third step is provided on either the primary or the secondary support member, depending upon the nature of the sliding relationship between the primary and secondary support members. Optionally, the first, second and third steps include retaining tabs, as well as upper and lower non-slip surfaces to prevent a climber's shoes from slipping off the ladder module.
problem: Creating a portable, adjustable ladder module that can be securely anchored to irregular surfaces (e.g., trees) while maintaining stability during use.
constraint: Balancing portability and adjustability with structural rigidity and stability, ensuring the ladder remains secure under load while being easy to deploy and reposition.
mechanism: Combining a sliding primary-secondary support member system with a selective locking mechanism for extension/retraction, paired with rigid stabilizing elements and a quick-release anchoring strap. The sliding and locking mechanism allows adjustable length, while the stabilizing elements and strap provide dynamic stabilization against the anchor point under load.
mechanism_raw: Combining a sliding primary-secondary support member system with a selective locking mechanism for extension/retraction, paired with rigid stabilizing tubing and a quick-release strap. The sliding and locking mechanism allows adjustable length, while the tubing and strap provide dynamic stabilization against the anchor point.

abstract: An outdoor unit of a transmitter-receiver apparatus notifies an indoor unit of normal operation by transmitting an unmodulated carrier to the indoor unit via a cable when operation is normal, notifies the indoor unit of an abnormality by transmitting a monitor signal, which is obtained by modulating a carrier by alarm data, to the indoor unit when operation is abnormal, and restores the carrier to the unmodulated state at recovery from the abnormality. Further, the indoor unit transmits an unmodulated carrier to the outdoor unit via the cable if it is unnecessary to send a control signal, and transmits a modulated control signal, which is obtained by modulating a carrier by control data, to the outdoor unit via the cable if it is necessary to send a control signal. As a result, phase noise and the characteristic of spuriousness in the vicinity of the local oscillation frequency are unaffected even if the unmodulated carrier leaks into the reference frequency signal system. As a result, no deterioration is caused in the quality of the communication system.
problem: Reliably signaling operational status (normal/abnormal) between outdoor and indoor units in a communication system without degrading signal quality or introducing phase noise.
constraint: Maintaining signal integrity in the reference frequency system by avoiding interference from modulated carriers, while enabling bidirectional communication through the same cable.
mechanism: Using modulation states of a carrier signal to encode operational status: an unmodulated carrier indicates normal operation, while a modulated carrier (with alarm data) indicates abnormality. The system restores the carrier to an unmodulated state upon recovery, ensuring phase noise and spurious signals in the reference frequency system remain unaffected.
mechanism_raw: Using modulation states of a carrier signal to encode status information: an unmodulated carrier indicates normal operation, while a modulated carrier (with alarm data) indicates abnormality. The system restores the carrier to an unmodulated state upon recovery, ensuring phase noise and spurious signals in the reference frequency system remain unaffected.

abstract: Apparatus (10) is disclosed including first and second forming rollers (18, 21) which rotatably abut with an anvil roller (20). The forming rollers (18, 21) each include a periphery forming a continuous forming surface including a plurality of axially and circumferentially spaced grooves (24) each formed as a continuous depression arranged in a serpentine and non-intersecting manner. Food (14) is simultaneously fed between a continuous strip of support material (16) and a continuous ribbon of film material (66) as they pass between a first abutment nip of the first forming roller (18) and the anvil roller (20). After extending partially around the periphery of the first forming roller (18), the materials (16, 66) and the food therebetween pass around an adjustable idler roller (70) to between a second abutment nip of the second forming roller (21) and the anvil roller (20). The food (14) compressed upon the support material (16) by the first abutment nip is in phase with the grooves (24) of the second abutment nip. The film material (66) removes the food (14) from the grooves (24) and can be discarded after passing through the second abutment nip and prior to the support material (16) being cut to longitudinal lengths and widths between the embossed shapes of food (14).
problem: Shaping and transferring food material between support and film layers with precise alignment and minimal waste during continuous processing.
constraint: Maintaining precise phase alignment between the food and grooves across multiple rollers to ensure consistent shaping and transfer, while allowing adjustable processing parameters.
mechanism: Using forming rollers with serpentine, non-intersecting grooves to compress material onto a support surface, followed by a second forming roller with grooves phased to align with the material. A separating film removes the material from the grooves after shaping, enabling continuous separation of the product from the forming surface while maintaining phase alignment across multiple rollers.
mechanism_raw: Using forming rollers with serpentine, non-intersecting grooves to compress food onto a support material, followed by a second forming roller with grooves phased to align with the food. A film material removes the food from the grooves after shaping, enabling continuous separation of the product from the forming surface.

abstract: A process for producing a silane-crosslinked polyolefin which is characterized by melt-blending (i) a polyolefinic base polymer, (ii) a carrier polymer A containing an organic unsaturated silane and a free radical generating agent and containing substantially no water and (iii) a carrier polymer B containing a silanol condensation catalyst and an antioxidant, at a temperature higher than the crystal melting point of the base polymer to effect reaction, and then contacting the resulting reaction product with water to effect crosslinking. The process can provide a silane-crosslinked polyolefin excellent in extrusion processability as well as in crosslinking property, mechanical property and heat resistance.
problem: Achieving a balance between extrusion processability and crosslinking properties in silane-crosslinked polyolefins without premature reaction or degradation.
constraint: Maintaining thermal stability and reaction kinetics during melt-blending while preventing premature crosslinking or degradation of the base polymer.
mechanism: Separating reactive components into distinct carrier matrices to control the timing and spatial coordination of crosslinking reactions. A base material is blended with carriers under elevated conditions, enabling controlled reaction initiation, followed by an external trigger to finalize crosslinking.
mechanism_raw: Separating reactive components (silane, free radical agent, catalyst, antioxidant) into distinct carrier polymers to control the timing and spatial coordination of crosslinking reactions. The base polymer is melt-blended with carriers at elevated temperatures, allowing controlled reaction initiation, followed by water contact to finalize crosslinking.

abstract: An agent for improving surface quality of paper comrising an acrylamide resin composition obtained by hydrolyzing an acrylamide resin which is obtained by polymerizing an acrylamide monomer in the presence of a urea compound, or copolymerizing an acrylamide monomer and an acrylonitrile monomer; an acrylamide monomer and a cross-linking agent; or an acrylamide monomer, an acrylnitrile monomer and a cross-linking agent in the presence of a urea compound. This agent provides paper with excellent surface strength, tensile strength and internal strength far better than conventional paper quality improving agents.
problem: Improving surface strength, tensile strength, and internal strength of paper beyond conventional agents without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing resin viscosity and cross-linking density to avoid brittleness while maximizing fiber adhesion and mechanical strength.
mechanism: Modifying a resin's molecular architecture through a mediator during synthesis to enhance adhesion and cross-linking capabilities. The mediator alters polymer structure to optimize bonding with fibrous substrates.
mechanism_raw: Modifying acrylamide resin properties through urea-mediated polymerization or copolymerization with acrylonitrile, creating a resin with enhanced adhesion and cross-linking capabilities. The urea compound alters the polymer's molecular architecture during synthesis to optimize bonding with cellulose fibers.

abstract: A process for the production of a gas-generating composition containing a redox-couple including a water soluble azide component, for example, azide of sodium, potassium, lithium, calcium or barium, and an oxidizer component, for example, sodium nitrate, sodium perchlorate, potassium nitrate, potassium perchlorate or an oxide of iron, nickel, vanadium, copper, titanium, manganese, zinc, tantalum, silicon or aluminium, said oxidizer component being capable of reacting with said azide component to generate gas, said process comprising the steps of: forming an aqueous dispersion of the redox-couple wherein the azide component is totally dissolved and the oxidizer is uniformly dispersed and stabilised in the azide solution; passing said aqueous dispersion through a spray nozzle to form a stream of droplets; and contacting said droplets with hot air whereby the water is removed to produce solid particles of gas-generating composition.
problem: Producing uniform solid particles of a gas-generating redox-couple composition with controlled stoichiometry and stability.
constraint: Maintaining dispersion stability to prevent premature reaction between azide and oxidizer while achieving uniform particle morphology during drying.
mechanism: Forming a dispersion where one reactive component is fully dissolved and another is uniformly stabilized, then solidifying the mixture into particles via controlled thermal exposure. This ensures homogeneous mixing before solidification.
mechanism_raw: Forming an aqueous dispersion where the azide component is fully dissolved and the oxidizer is uniformly dispersed and stabilized, then spray-drying the dispersion into droplets exposed to hot air. This ensures homogeneous mixing of reactive components before solidification into particles.

abstract: In a vent arrangement comprising a heating cylinder 1 containing therein a screw and provided with a vent hole 3 and a reduced pressure exhaust path 4 provided with a vacuum pump and connected to the vent hole 3 for draining volatile fractions of a material to be molded from the heating cylinder by reducing the pressure in the vent hole by means of the vacuum pump, said volatile fractions are removed by arranging in the exhaust path a filter unit 7 filled with a granular filtering material 8. The material to be molded is used for the filtering material 8. According to the above construction, it can be achieved to efficiently remove volatile matters by using the molded material as the filtering material of the filter unit arranged in the reduced pressure exhaust path of a vent arrangement.
problem: Efficiently removing volatile fractions from a heating cylinder during molding without clogging or disrupting the molding process.
constraint: Ensuring the filter material does not degrade or release contaminants under vacuum and heat while maintaining sufficient permeability for volatile extraction.
mechanism: Using the product material itself as a granular filtering medium in a reduced-pressure exhaust path. The material's physical properties enable trapping of volatile byproducts while maintaining airflow for removal.
mechanism_raw: Using the molded material itself as the granular filtering medium in a filter unit placed within the reduced-pressure exhaust path. The material's physical properties (e.g., porosity, adsorption) enable it to trap volatile byproducts while maintaining airflow for vacuum-driven removal.

abstract: An ink composition comprising a dye containing at least one group of the Formula (1): ##STR1## wherein: W.sup.1 is --F, --OR.sup.1, --SR.sup.1 or --NR.sup.1 R.sup.2 in which R.sub.1 and R.sup.2 each independently is H, optionally substituted alkyl, cycloalkyl, optionally substituted alkenyl, optionally substituted aryl, optionally substituted aralkyl or R.sup.1 and R.sup.2 together with the nitrogen atom to which they are attached form a 5 or 6 membered ring; and a medium comprising at least one of a low melting point solid, an organic solvent and a mixture of water and one more water-soluble organic solvent(s). Also claimed is a process for ink jet printing using the inks, a process for ink jet printing of textiles using the inks and a toner containing a dye with at least one group of Formula (1).
problem: Creating an ink composition with optimal solubility, stability, and jet-printing performance across diverse media (e.g., textiles, paper).
constraint: Balancing dye solubility and thermal stability in the medium while avoiding aggregation or precipitation during printing.
mechanism: Tailoring molecular substituents on a dye's structure to modulate intermolecular interactions, ensuring solubility and stability in a chosen medium. The substituents prevent aggregation and enable consistent droplet formation.
mechanism_raw: Designing a dye with specific substituents (e.g., --F, --OR, --SR, --NR groups) on its molecular structure to match the solubility and viscosity requirements of the chosen medium (low-melting solid, organic solvent, or water-solvent mixture). The substituents modulate intermolecular interactions to prevent clogging and ensure consistent droplet formation.

abstract: An efficient method for manufacturing a purified juice product from sugar beets. Untreated beet juice is initially prelimed using lime and CaCO.sub.3 to produce a prelimed juice product. Instead of subjecting the prelimed product to main liming and dual carbonation stages, the product is delivered to a porous filtration membrane which allows sugar molecules to pass therethrough which preventing the passage of solid matter and dissolved impurities. Optimum results are achieved if the prelimed product flows across the membrane from end to end. The membrane permeate is thereafter combined with CO.sub.2(g) in a single carbonation stage to remove dissolved lime. This step generates a purified juice product which can be processed to manufacture pure crystalline sugar. The membrane retentate can be combined with water and refiltered to collect residual sugar materials. The foregoing process uses less energy and raw materials (e.g. lime) compared with conventional methods.
problem: Reducing energy consumption and raw material usage in sugar beet juice purification compared to conventional liming and carbonation processes.
constraint: Maintaining optimal flow across the membrane from end to end to ensure efficient separation and minimize fouling.
mechanism: Using a selective barrier to separate target molecules from contaminants via differential permeability, followed by a secondary treatment stage to eliminate residual substances, with recirculation of unpermeated material to recover entrained targets.
mechanism_raw: Using a porous filtration membrane to selectively allow sugar molecules to pass while blocking solid matter and dissolved impurities, followed by a single carbonation stage to remove residual lime. The membrane retentate is recirculated to recover residual sugars.

abstract: A method of analyzing the sequence of a polynucleotide analyte. The method includes contacting the analyte with a position-addressable array of oligonucleotides, each anchored to a solid support and having a 5'proximal and 3'-distal orientation. The hybridized oligonucleotides are then extended by strand-directed polymerase, to produce labeled, extended oligonucleotides at positions of the array corresponding to sequence matches between the array oligonucleotides and analyte regions. The pattern of label in the array is used to analyze analyte sequence.
problem: Determining the sequence of a polynucleotide analyte efficiently and accurately.
constraint: Precise spatial addressing of oligonucleotides and controlled enzymatic extension to ensure specificity and avoid cross-reactivity.
mechanism: Employing a spatially encoded array of binding agents to capture complementary sequences, followed by enzymatic amplification of matched regions to generate detectable signals, with spatial signal patterns indicating sequence identity.
mechanism_raw: Hybridizing the analyte to a position-addressable array of oligonucleotides anchored on a solid support, extending matched oligonucleotides via strand-directed polymerase to produce labeled products, and using the spatial pattern of labels to infer sequence matches.

abstract: A method of manufacturing a pocketed coil spring assembly comprising vertically spacing two sheets of fabric apart so that the sheets are generally parallel to one another. The sheets are then attached together along one end edge and rows of coil springs are inserted between the sheets. After each row of coil springs is inserted between the sheets, the sheets are attached together along transversely extending lines of attachment in alternative planes of the pocketed coil spring assembly. These steps of inserting rows of coil springs and attaching the sheets together in alternative planes occurs sequentially until an appropriate length of the assembly is obtained.
problem: Manufacturing a pocketed coil spring assembly with controlled spacing and structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing sequential insertion and attachment in alternative planes to ensure structural coherence without misalignment.
mechanism: Building a layered structure by incrementally inserting resilient elements between parallel substrates and attaching the substrates at alternating positions to maintain alignment and spacing during assembly.
mechanism_raw: Sequentially inserting rows of coil springs between parallel fabric sheets and attaching the sheets in transversely extending lines at alternating planes, building the assembly incrementally to maintain alignment and spacing.

abstract: A steel cord (10) comprises eight or more strands (12, 14) twisted together. Each of the strands has a substantially same cord twisting direction and a substantially same cord twisting pitch in the steel cord, and each of the strands consists of two to five individual filaments (16, 18) twisted together. Such a multi-strand steel cord can be manufactured without having to twist the individual strands separately and beforehand.
problem: Manufacturing a multi-strand steel cord without pre-twisting individual strands separately.
constraint: Maintaining uniform twist direction and pitch across all strands to ensure structural consistency and strength.
mechanism: Coordinating the simultaneous twisting of multiple filament bundles such that each bundle's internal twist parameters match the overall twist parameters of the composite structure, eliminating sequential pre-twisting steps.
mechanism_raw: Twisting multiple strands together simultaneously, where each strand consists of filaments twisted in the same direction and pitch as the overall cord, eliminating the need for individual strand pre-twisting.

abstract: A drive unit (1,41,51) for a self-propelled elevator car (30) which travels along a pair of guide rails (27) is connected with a car-supporting structure (16) by rocker arms (15) and contact pressure springs (29). An electric motor (2,3,26,31) is coaxial with a wheel shaft (8) which extends therethrough and has a pair of drive wheels (10) mounted at the ends thereof. The motor housing (31) is connected to the axle tubes (11) by releasably attached motor flanges (12). The motor (2,3,26,31) drives the wheel axle (8) in rotation through a speed-reducing planetary gear (33) and a brake (32,34) which prevents rotation of the wheel axle (8) can be released selectively. An auxiliary drive (35,36,37) mounted on the motor (2,3,26,31) selectively rotates the wheel axle (8) in response to a power failure.
problem: Providing reliable drive and backup power for a self-propelled elevator car during normal operation and power failures.
constraint: Ensuring seamless transition between primary and auxiliary drives while maintaining mechanical alignment and torque transmission.
mechanism: Integrating a primary drive mechanism with a coaxial auxiliary system that automatically engages during power loss, using a mechanical coupling to maintain torque transmission and alignment between normal and backup operation modes.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a primary electric motor coaxial with a wheel shaft, connected via a planetary gear and brake, alongside an auxiliary drive system that automatically engages the wheel axle during power loss to maintain mobility.

abstract: A method for making a corrosion resistant, ferritic steel alloy, with reduced magnetic coercivity is disclosed. The process includes the step of providing an intermediate form of a ferritic alloy consisting essentially of, in weight percent, about ______________________________________ Carbon 0.02 max. Manganese 1.5 max. Silicon 3.0 max. Phosphorus 0.03 max. Sulfur 0.1-0.5 Chromium 8-20 Nickel 0.60 max. Molybdenum 1.5 max. Copper 0.3 max. Cobalt 0.10 max. Aluminum 0.01 max. Titanium 0.01 max. Nitrogen 0.02 max. Iron Balance ______________________________________ The intermediate form of the alloy is given an annealing heat treatment at a first temperature in the range of about 700.degree.-900.degree. C. for at least about 2 hours. After the penultimate annealing step, the intermediate form is cold worked to reduce its cross-sectional area by about 10-25%, thereby providing an elongated form of said alloy. The elongated form is then given a final annealing heat treatment at a second temperature in the range of about 750.degree.-1050.degree. C. for at least about 4 hours. Parts prepared in accordance with the disclosed process are fully ferritic and exhibit a coercivity significantly less than 2.0 Oe.
problem: Achieving low magnetic coercivity in ferritic steel alloys while maintaining corrosion resistance.
constraint: Balancing annealing temperatures (700–900°C and 750–1050°C) and cold work deformation (10–25%) to avoid unwanted phase transformations while achieving the desired magnetic properties.
mechanism: A sequence of thermal treatment and mechanical deformation steps is applied to a material to modify its internal structure, reducing magnetic coercivity by optimizing grain refinement and phase distribution while preserving corrosion resistance through controlled phase stability.
mechanism_raw: Controlled thermal and mechanical processing: annealing at specific temperatures followed by cold working and a final annealing step alters the microstructure, reducing coercivity by optimizing grain structure and phase distribution.

abstract: This invention relates to a method for coating leather with an anionically modified polyurethane urea prepared by PA0 (1) reacting PA1 (A) an aromatic diisocyanate, PA1 (B) a polyether polyol having a number average molecular weight greater than 1500, PA1 (C) at least one compound containing 1 to 2 isocyanate-reactive groups and at least one ionic group, and PA1 (D) a polyamine having a number average molecular weight of at least 32, PA1 wherein the average total functionality of compounds (B), (C), and (D) is 1.85 to 2.2 and the molar ratio between the NCO groups of component (A) and the NCO-reactive groups of components (B), (C), and (D) is greater than 1, thereby forming an intermediate having residual NCO groups, and PA0 (2) mixing the intermediate product with water to form an aqueous dispersion of an anionically modified polyurethane urea having 800 to 1500 mmol of urethane groups and 800 to 1800 mmol of urethane plus urea groups per kilogram of the polyurethane urea.
problem: Creating a durable, water-dispersible polyurethane urea coating for leather with controlled ionic and cross-linking properties.
constraint: Maintaining a molar ratio of NCO to reactive groups greater than 1 and controlling molecular weights (polyether polyol >1500, polyamine ≥32) to ensure proper cross-linking without over-reaction.
mechanism: Stoichiometric control of reactive chemical groups during polymerization creates an intermediate with residual reactive sites, which then interact with a secondary agent to form a stable dispersion with tailored cross-linking density and functional group composition.
mechanism_raw: Precise stoichiometric control of isocyanate-reactive groups during polymerization forms an intermediate with residual NCO groups, which then react with water to create a stable dispersion with tailored urethane/urea content.
residual_terms: ["stoichiometric control", "reactive chemical groups", "polymerization", "cross-linking density", "functional group composition"]

abstract: An improved shortening substitute for food products such as bakery products. The improved shortening substitute includes a mixture of a fruit puree, a sweetener, a preservative, water, a fat mimetic, a pH adjuster and a source of calcium ions. The shortening substitute is formulated to be used in a wide variety of food products and have a 1:1 to 0.5:1 replacement value of the improved shortening substitute to oil, butter or shortening to produce high quality baked products.
problem: Replacing traditional high-fat shortenings in food products with a healthier substitute that maintains baking quality.
constraint: Balancing ingredient ratios (1:1 to 0.5:1 replacement value) to match fat's performance while avoiding adverse effects on texture or shelf-life.
mechanism: A combination of a hydrated matrix, a functional substitute, a pH modifier, and ionic agents replicates the performance of a target substance through synergistic interactions between hydrocolloids and charged species, maintaining texture and moisture retention properties.
mechanism_raw: Combining a fruit puree, fat mimetic, pH adjuster, and calcium ions to replicate the functional properties of fat (texture, moisture retention) through synergistic interactions between hydrocolloids and ionic components.

abstract: In a baking method, a piece of dough is deposited on a substantially horizontal support surface provided with at least one perforation so that the piece of dough covers the perforation. The surface together with the piece of dough are moved into a heated enclosure, wherein the surface and the piece of dough are maintained for a predetermined period of time. During at least a portion of that period, steam is fed through the perforation so that at least some of the steam enters the piece of dough through a lower surface thereof. This method is implementable in a batch type baking process or a continuous conveyor process.
problem: Improving heat and moisture distribution during baking to enhance product quality and consistency.
constraint: Regulating steam pressure and timing to prevent over-saturation while ensuring uniform heat transfer through the dough.
mechanism: A perforated surface introduces a moisture-carrying medium directly into a product during heating, enabling controlled moisture penetration and uniform thermal processing by creating localized vaporization and heat transfer pathways.
mechanism_raw: Using a perforated support surface to inject steam directly into the dough's lower surface during heating, enabling controlled moisture penetration and even thermal processing.

abstract: An apparatus is provided for storing a multi-component cryogenic mixture as a liquid. The multi-component cryogenic mixture of interest contains at least first and second components. The first component is more volatile than the second component and the second component has a bubble point temperature atmosphere pressure, lower than that of the first component at an above atmosphere pressure. A container is provided in the apparatus for storing the cryogenic mixture. An inevitable heat leakage causes a cryogenic mixture to vaporize so that the vapor phase of the mixture is enriched in the first component and the liquid phase in the mixture is enriched in the second component. A conduit communicates between locations of the container situated above and below the head space region of the container so that vapor phase stream flows into the reservoir, opened to the atmosphere is provided in communication with the container such that a liquid phase stream, made up of the liquid phase flows into the reservoir and develops an ever increasing second component concentration. As such, the liquid phase of the mixture is able to condense the vapor phase of the mixture within the conduit. The resulting liquid will fall back into the container under influence of gravity to stabilize the concentration of the first and second components within the container.
problem: Stabilizing the composition of a multi-component cryogenic mixture during storage despite inevitable heat leakage.
constraint: Managing heat leakage rates and phase separation dynamics to maintain equilibrium between vapor and liquid phases without external energy input.
mechanism: A phase-equilibrium system uses a conduit and reservoir to redirect vapor enriched in a volatile component back to the storage container, where it condenses and returns liquid enriched in a less volatile component under gravitational force, maintaining compositional stability without external energy input.
mechanism_raw: Exploiting vapor-liquid equilibrium via a conduit and reservoir system: vapor enriched in the more volatile component flows back to condense, returning liquid enriched in the less volatile component to the container under gravity.
residual_terms: ["phase-equilibrium system", "conduit and reservoir", "volatile component", "less volatile component", "gravitational force"]

abstract: A method is specified for pitch recognition, in particular for musical instruments which are excited by plucking or striking, in the case of which method the interval between zero crossings of a signal waveform of an audio signal is used as a measure for the period length of the audio signal. Reliable pitch recognition is intended to be possible in a simple manner using such a method. The method is intended to be capable of being implemented with a low level of computation power. To this end, the magnitude of the gradient of the signal waveform is in each case determined in the region of its zero crossings, and the magnitude of the gradient is used as an assessment criterion for the selection of the zero crossings to be evaluated.
problem: Reliably determining pitch from audio signals with minimal computational resources, particularly for plucked or struck musical instruments.
constraint: Balancing computational simplicity with the need to reject spurious zero crossings caused by noise or harmonics.
mechanism: Using a signal's rate of change magnitude at crossing points as a validity criterion to filter spurious events for periodic signal reconstruction, enabling resource-efficient estimation without complex computations.
mechanism_raw: Using the magnitude of the signal waveform gradient at zero crossings as a filtering criterion to select valid zero crossings for period length estimation, thereby improving accuracy without complex computations.

abstract: A steering wheel core metal unit comprising a boss section, a boss/spoke connecting section, spoke sections and a ring section integrally die-cast, with the boss section serving as an insert. Before trimming and after being released from a die caster, the boss/spoke connecting section of the core metal unit is provided with a gate section and the ring section comprises a pair of inside and outside ribs. Overflow sections are provided along the outer periphery of the ring section at substantially the intermediate positions among the spoke sections, respectively. The sectional area of the outside rib is made larger than that of the inside rib so that a final molten metal merging portion comes to lie at the outer periphery of the ring section. Accordingly, even when the molten metal moves in the cavity of the die caster as it entrains air, the air can escape from the overflow sections and no blowhole is formed in the core metal as a die cast product.
problem: Preventing blowholes (air pockets) in die-cast metal components caused by entrapped air during molten metal flow.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the component while ensuring sufficient air venting during the die-casting process.
mechanism: Configuring flow-guiding structures with variable cross-sectional areas and designated escape zones to direct fluid displacement such that entrapped gas exits through peripheral pathways while final material convergence occurs at an outer boundary, preventing internal void formation.
mechanism_raw: Designing rib cross-sectional areas and overflow sections to direct molten metal flow such that air escapes through strategically placed overflow zones while the final metal merge point is positioned at the outer periphery, avoiding internal voids.

abstract: A piston-type, multicylinder internal combustion engine includes a cylinder block and a cylinder head mounted thereto, with a combustion chamber defined by the cylinder head and the top of the piston, with the engine being fueled by an an in-cylinder gasoline injection system which is centrally located with a spark plug such that the spark plug is closer to exhaust valves than is the injector, and with the injector being closer to the intake valves than the spark plug.
problem: Optimizing combustion efficiency in a multicylinder internal combustion engine with in-cylinder gasoline injection.
constraint: Spatial limitations within the combustion chamber requiring precise component placement to avoid interference while maximizing combustion dynamics.
mechanism: Arranging fuel delivery and ignition components in spatially separated stages within a combustion chamber to create a sequential combustion process, where fuel introduction and ignition timing are offset to enhance mixing and burn efficiency under geometric constraints.
mechanism_raw: Positioning the fuel injector closer to intake valves and the spark plug closer to exhaust valves to create a staged combustion process, where fuel is injected and ignited in a sequence that enhances mixing and burn efficiency.

abstract: The dryer section of a machine for manufacturing a paper web includes at least one and more usually a plurality of heatable drying cylinders, each of which is wrapped over a part of its circumferential surface by the web of material to be dried. A support belt is guided by guide rolls to wrap over a part of the circumference of each of the drying cylinders and over the web. A pressing device presses against the support belt to press the web of material against the drying cylinder. That pressing device may comprise a pressure box outside the support belt to which air or steam pressure is applied. The pressure box may include several zones either along the web path or transverse to the web path permitting different pressures to be applied. The pressing device may alternately comprise a plurality of pressing rolls extending transversely to the web axis and parallel to the drying cylinder axis and being biased against the support belt, e.g., by springs, and supported on a support which moves the pressing rolls toward the support belt.
problem: Efficiently drying a paper web while maintaining uniform contact pressure against heated drying cylinders.
constraint: Achieving uniform pressure distribution across the web width and path while accommodating variable drying requirements.
mechanism: Applying a flexible support element in contact with a moving substrate and using distributed pressure application devices with independently adjustable zones to maintain uniform contact force across the substrate width while enabling localized optimization of drying conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using a support belt wrapped around drying cylinders and a pressing device (pressure box or rolls) to apply controlled pressure, with zoned pressure application enabling localized adjustments to optimize drying without damaging the web.

abstract: A light-weight, portable container is provided for the stern of a boat in order to add weight to the stern and enhance the wake of the boat.
