The container is formed from an outer bag resistant to abrasion and puncture and an inner, liquid impermeable bladder positioned within the bag and protected from puncture and abrasion by the bag. The bladder is filled with water through one or more nozzles accessed through openings in the bag.
reason: The patent describes a product (a dual-layer liquid container) with specific structural features (abrasion-resistant outer bag and liquid-impermeable inner bladder) but does not disclose a causal mechanism that generates a useful effect through a functional relationship beyond the basic containment and protection of the liquid. The mechanism is merely a static design choice rather than a dynamic or transferable problem-solving principle.

abstract: A diglycerol saturated fatty acid ester mixture containing a diglycerol saturated fatty acid diester(s) having two monohydroxymonoacyloxy(iso)propyl groups, wherein the acyl groups are derived from saturated fatty acids having 10 to 24 carbon atoms and two acyl groups are the same or different from each other, in an amount of 80% by weight or more based on the total weight of the diglycerol saturated fatty acid diesters contained in the mixture, and a diglycerol saturated fatty acid diester(s) in an amount of 45% by weight or more based on the entire weight of the mixture, is used as a modifier for protein-containing materials, in particular, for the control of the stickiness on the surface of the dough during the production thereof, for the improvements of the mechanical resistance and the handleability, and for the improvements of the feelings during eating, such as softness.
problem: Controlling surface stickiness, mechanical resistance, and texture in protein-containing materials (e.g., dough) during production and consumption.
constraint: The ester composition must maintain a minimum concentration (80% by weight of specific diesters, 45% of total mixture) to ensure effective property modulation without destabilizing the material structure.
mechanism: A surfactant composition with a minimum concentration threshold modifies the physical properties of protein-containing matrices by interacting with protein structures, altering surface friction, cohesion, and mechanical integrity through controlled surfactant-like interactions.
mechanism_raw: A diglycerol saturated fatty acid ester mixture modifies the physical properties of protein matrices by interacting with protein structures, altering surface friction, cohesion, and mechanical integrity through controlled surfactant-like interactions.
residual_terms: ["surfactant", "protein", "protein structures", "surface friction", "cohesion", "mechanical integrity", "surfactant-like interactions", "minimum concentration threshold"]

abstract: The improved cable guard for a compound archery bow includes an elongated, flexible resilient rod having a rear portion and an opposite front portion, the flexibility of the rod increasing from the front portion to the rear portion. Preferably, the front portion of the rod is generally circular in transverse cross-section while the rear portion of the rod is semi-circular in such cross-section, with a flat side facing away from the bow cables and toward the bowstring. In another embodiment both the front and rear portions of the rod are generally circular in cross-section, but the diameter of the rod decreases from the front portion to the rear portion thereof. The cable guard also includes an elongated transversely extending bracket the medial end of which is adapted to be secured to the rear end of the bow riser while the distal end of the bracket extends laterally of the riser and releasably secures the rod so that its position relative to the bow riser can be adjusted. The rod and bracket can be made of metal, plastic or the like. A fitting can be provided to slidingly receive portions of the bow cables and the rod. The invention also includes a compound archery bow with the cable guard mounted thereon lateral of the bowstring and medial of the cables.
problem: Preventing cable interference and friction in compound archery bows while maintaining cable guidance and adjustability.
constraint: The rod's flexibility gradient and cross-sectional shape must balance cable guidance precision with structural resilience to avoid fatigue failure under repeated bowstring motion.
mechanism: A flexible guide element with a spatial gradient in stiffness and variable cross-sectional geometry passively directs flexible tensile members along a controlled path, reducing lateral displacement and contact with a moving element.
mechanism_raw: A flexible rod with a gradient in flexibility (increasing from front to rear) and variable cross-sectional geometry (circular to semi-circular) passively guides cables along a controlled path, reducing lateral displacement and contact with the bowstring.
residual_terms: ["flexible guide element", "stiffness gradient", "cross-sectional geometry", "flexible tensile members", "controlled path", "lateral displacement", "moving element"]

abstract: A heat recovery device is disclosed which is adapted for use in the drain conduit of standard shower installations having a hot water line, a cold water line, means for mixing water from both lines to deliver water at a suitable temperature to a shower head, and a drain conduit for disposing of waste water passing through the shower installation, the heat recovery device transferring heat from the waste water to cold water flowing to the cold water line. The heat recovery device has a first conduit connected into the drain conduit of the shower installation, and a second conduit connected into the cold water line leading into the shower installation and either wrapped around or inserted within the first conduit so that the second conduit is in operative heat transfer relationship with warm waste water passing through the first conduit, so that the incoming cold water is preheated by heat recovered from the waste water and transferred to the cold water.
problem: Recovering waste heat from shower drain water to preheat incoming cold water, improving energy efficiency.
constraint: The conduit arrangement must maintain sufficient thermal contact area and flow rates to maximize heat transfer while minimizing pressure drop in both fluid streams.
mechanism: A secondary fluid conduit is physically integrated into or around a primary fluid conduit to enable conductive heat transfer from one fluid stream to another, leveraging thermal proximity without direct fluid mixing.
mechanism_raw: A secondary conduit (cold water line) is physically integrated into or around a primary conduit (drain line) to enable conductive heat transfer from warm wastewater to cold water, leveraging thermal proximity without direct fluid mixing.
residual_terms: ["fluid conduit", "conducting heat transfer", "fluid stream", "thermal proximity", "direct fluid mixing"]

abstract: A pocket coil spring structure assembling apparatus for producing a pocket coil spring structure which includes a feeder mechanism to supply a group of pocket coil springs to a positioning transfer conveyor mechanism; a cutting mechanism between the feeding mechanism and the positioning transfer conveyor mechanism to cut the group of pocket coil springs to a predetermined length; a press holding mechanism to hold and lift the cut group of pocket coils springs on the positioning transfer conveyor mechanism by pressing the centers of opposite ends of each pocket coil springs; a pressing holding mechanism carrier mechanism to move the press holding mechanism in forward, backward, leftward, and rightward directions; a spray mechanism with a spray nozzle to apply adhesive to the cut group of pocket coil springs; a nozzle carrier to move the spray nozzle; and a controller mechanism for controlling each of the mechanisms.
problem: Automating the assembly of pocket coil springs with precise cutting, adhesive application, and positional control.
constraint: Each mechanism must operate with precise timing and positional accuracy to avoid misalignment or damage to delicate coil structures during high-speed assembly.
mechanism: A coordinated system of material handling and processing mechanisms, controlled by a central controller, synchronizes sequential operations with precise timing and positional accuracy to ensure accurate assembly of discrete components into structured arrays.
mechanism_raw: A coordinated system of feeder, cutting, pressing, and spraying mechanisms, controlled by a central controller, synchronizes material handling and processing steps to ensure accurate assembly of cut coil groups into structured spring arrays.
residual_terms: ["material handling", "processing mechanisms", "central controller", "sequential operations", "timing", "positional accuracy", "discrete components", "structured arrays"]

abstract: The present invention addresses 2-substituted aryl pyrroles, as well as compositions containing such compounds and methods of treatment. Cytokine mediated diseases refers to diseases or conditions in which excessive or unregulated production or activity of one or more cytokines occurs. Interleukin-1 (IL-1), Interleukin-6 (IL-6), Interleukin-8 (IL-8) and Tumor Necrosis Factor (TNF) are cytokines which are involved.
problem: Treating cytokine-mediated diseases by inhibiting excessive or unregulated cytokine activity (e.g., IL-1, IL-6, TNF).
constraint: The chemical structure of the pyrrole derivatives must balance target specificity and bioavailability to avoid off-target effects while achieving therapeutic efficacy.
mechanism: A chemical compound selectively interacts with biological targets involved in inflammatory signaling pathways, disrupting pathological immune responses by modulating cytokine activity.
mechanism_raw: 2-substituted aryl pyrrole compounds selectively interact with biological targets (e.g., enzymes or receptors) involved in cytokine production or signaling pathways, disrupting pathological inflammatory responses.
residual_terms: ["chemical compound", "biological targets", "inflammatory signaling pathways", "cytokine activity", "selective interaction"]

abstract: An earmuff cushion and other foam hearing protective components such as earplugs and pods for semi-aural hearing protectors and earplugs providing improved attenuation are described. The cushion and other foam hearing protective components are comprised of a dynamically stiff foam material having a low static stiffness, and a high dynamic stiffness, which produces improved attenuation in the earmuff and other hearing protective devices in which it is used. Earmuffs made from the cushion, semi-aural hearing protectors, earplugs, and improved methods of making the hearing protective devices are also described.
problem: Improving sound attenuation in hearing protective devices without sacrificing static comfort.
constraint: Balancing static comfort (low stiffness) with dynamic damping (high stiffness) to avoid material fatigue or user discomfort.
mechanism: A material system exhibiting dual stiffness behavior: low resistance to static deformation for user comfort, and high resistance to dynamic deformation to attenuate vibrational energy transfer, enabling noise reduction under dynamic conditions while maintaining static softness.
mechanism_raw: Using a foam material with low static stiffness (for comfort) and high dynamic stiffness (to resist vibrational energy transfer), enabling effective noise blocking under dynamic conditions while remaining soft when stationary.

abstract: An apparatus and method for manipulating a pole relative to a base fixed in the ground. The base is gripped and provides a rigid reference point. The pole is cradled and an actuator provides force to move the pole relative to the reference point. This can include detaching the pole from the base as well as inserting the pole on the base. As an optional feature, a pivot mechanism can be associated with the combination to allow the pole to be pivoted with respect to the base to lower the pole for inspection and maintenance, or to erect the pole to be vertically aligned and then seated onto the base.
problem: Precisely positioning and adjusting the orientation of a pole relative to a fixed base, including detachment and insertion.
constraint: Maintaining structural stability during movement while allowing sufficient flexibility for pivoting and repositioning.
mechanism: A positioning system combining a fixed reference structure with a force-applying element to generate controlled motion, integrated with a rotational joint to enable angular reorientation of a detachable component relative to the reference structure.
mechanism_raw: Combining a rigid base as a stable reference point with an actuator to apply controlled forces for pole movement, augmented by a pivot mechanism to enable angular adjustments (e.g., lowering or erecting the pole).

abstract: An apparatus and method for chemically and physically stabilizing contaminated soil is disclosed. The soil is homogenized in a homogenizer; dropped into a mixer below the homogenizer and mixed with an additive; then dropped to a processing terminus located below the mixer. The apparatus and method are useful for processing highly clumped and/or acidic soil, e.g., soil contaminated with mining waste.
problem: Stabilizing highly clumped or acidic contaminated soil through chemical and physical treatment.
constraint: Handling variable soil compositions (clumpiness, acidity) while maintaining throughput and additive distribution efficiency.
mechanism: A multi-stage treatment process involving mechanical disruption of aggregated material, controlled blending with reactive agents in a confined environment, and gravitational deposition to a processing zone to ensure uniform chemical-physical modification and separation of treated output.
mechanism_raw: Sequentially homogenizing soil to break clumps, mixing with additives in a controlled chamber, and dropping the mixture to a processing terminus to ensure uniform treatment and separation of stabilized material.

abstract: A novel polypeptide, acylglucosamine 2-epimerase as shown in FIG. 1 and derivatives thereof, DNA coding for said enzyme, a recombinant vector containing said enzyme, a transformant integrated thereinto said vector, a method for producing said enzyme and a mrthod for producing N-acetylmannosamine and N-acetylneuraminic acid using renin binding protein.
problem: Producing N-acetylmannosamine and N-acetylneuraminic acid efficiently using enzymatic catalysis.
constraint: Ensuring enzyme specificity and stability in recombinant production systems to avoid off-target reactions or low yields.
mechanism: A biological production system using a genetic delivery vehicle to express a catalytic enzyme, which facilitates a specific biochemical transformation pathway to synthesize target compounds from precursor substrates.
mechanism_raw: Employing a recombinant vector to express acylglucosamine 2-epimerase, which catalyzes the conversion of substrates into target compounds via a specific biochemical pathway.
residual_terms: ["genetic delivery vehicle", "catalytic enzyme", "biochemical transformation pathway", "precursor substrates"]

abstract: A waterborne coating composition for metal substrates comprising (a) a formaldehyde-containing resin, and (b) a formaldehyde scavenger consisting essentially of an organic compound having at least one active methylene hydrogen and a pKa of about 5 to about 13, wherein the formaldehyde scavenger is present in a sufficient amount to maintain the concentration of free formaldehyde in the composition at less than 0.1% by weight.
problem: Reducing free formaldehyde emissions in waterborne coatings while maintaining coating performance.
constraint: Balancing scavenger reactivity (to capture formaldehyde) with compatibility in the resin matrix to avoid compromising coating adhesion or durability.
mechanism: A chemical capture system incorporating a reactive agent with tunable acidity (pKa 5–13) to bind volatile byproducts through molecular interaction, preventing their release during material curing or application while maintaining matrix compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a formaldehyde scavenger with active methylene hydrogen (pKa 5–13) to chemically bind free formaldehyde, preventing its release during curing or use.

abstract: A hand operated leverage device is provided for contact with the outer surface of a roll of material, so that a relatively small amount of force applied to the device will result in a forward rotating movement of the roll of material a relatively short distance away from the user and away from the device. The support legs allow the device to be freestanding, with one of the support legs having the ability to accommodate a person's stepping force, while another support leg is pivotally connected to the body of the device and serves as a pivot point for the transmission of the force from the human operator to the roll of material. A curved, adjustable plate connected at the end of the leverage device enables it to actively engage the outer surface of the roll of material during the force-transmissive operation of the device. Operation of the device forwardly urges a roll of material away from the user and the curved plate prevents the transmitted force from damaging, marring or leaving an impression upon the outer surface of the roll of material.
problem: Moving a heavy roll of material forward (away from the operator) using only a small applied human force, while avoiding damage or marring of the roll's outer surface.
constraint: The device must balance force amplification (requiring sufficient leverage and contact pressure) against surface protection (requiring distributed, non-marring contact), while remaining freestanding and operable by a single person's stepping force.
mechanism: A leverage amplification system uses a pivotally connected support leg as a fulcrum and a stepping leg to receive human force, converting a small input force into a large rotational output that urges the roll forward. A curved, adjustable contact plate actively engages the roll's outer surface and distributes the transmitted force over a compliant area, preventing localized pressure that would damage or mar the surface.
mechanism_raw: A leverage amplification system uses a pivotally connected support leg as a fulcrum and a stepping leg to receive human force, converting a small input force into a large rotational output that urges the roll forward. A curved, adjustable contact plate actively engages the roll's outer surface and distributes the transmitted force over a compliant area, preventing localized pressure that would damage or mar the surface.

abstract: A method for a person to interact with an animal has been invented which includes a person throwing a plate on which at least one item is releasably mounted, retrieving the plate by the animal for the person, releasing of the at least one item from the plate by the person, and giving the at least one item to the animal.
reason: This is a specific animal-training/play method (throw a plate with a reward, have the animal retrieve it, release the reward) rather than a generalizable problem-solving mechanism. The core operation is a fixed interaction protocol with no underlying causal principle that transfers to other technical domains.

abstract: An automatic sample preparation system for polishing and grinding metallurgical and other samples prior to microscopic examination of the samples, including a rack which holds a plurality of abrasive platens, and platen transfer mechanism for selecting one platen from the rack and transferring the same to a platen drive plate for a polishing operation and for later returning the platen to the rack and transferring another selected platen to the platen drive plate, and a polishing head which can be rotated between a polishing position for polishing samples and a wash position where it is over a wash and dry station, the platen transfer mechanism being operated when the polishing head is rotated to its wash position.
problem: Automatically preparing multiple samples for microscopic examination using different abrasive platens for polishing and grinding, with cleaning between operations, without manual intervention.
constraint: The platen transfer mechanism must be precisely timed with the polishing head's position so that tool swapping occurs only when the head is at the wash station, preventing interference and ensuring continuous automated operation.
mechanism: A tool magazine stores multiple platens, and an automated transfer mechanism selects and swaps individual platens to a drive plate. A polishing head rotates between a polishing position and a wash/dry position, and the platen transfer is triggered in coordination with the head's rotation to the wash position, enabling seamless tool changes synchronized with workstation transitions.
mechanism_raw: A tool magazine (platen rack) stores multiple platens, and an automated transfer mechanism selects and swaps individual platens to a drive plate. A polishing head rotates between a polishing position and a wash/dry position, and the platen transfer is triggered in coordination with the head's rotation to the wash position, enabling seamless tool changes synchronized with workstation transitions.

abstract: The invention relates to a process, as well as a device which is suited for the same, for the processing of containers, particularly of bottles or the like, into which a fluid is injected for the expulsion of the air from the head room of the bottles after the filling, before the aperture of the container is closed, in a sealing manner, by means of a closure cap. After the injecting of the fluid, a closure cap is first of all moved forward to the opening of the container and held, for a certain period of time, in a position above the opening, in such a manner that the open aperture is covered by the closure cap, but that gas can exit from the container between the opening and the closure cap. After that, the closure cap is attached to the container in a sealing manner.
problem: Removing air or gas from the headspace of a filled container before permanently sealing its opening, to prevent spoilage or oxidation without introducing contamination.
constraint: The closure must maintain a vented state long enough for gas evacuation while preventing contamination ingress, then transition to a complete seal without reintroducing air or compromising the container's integrity.
mechanism: A two-stage closure process: first, the closure cap is advanced to cover the container opening but held in a non-sealing position, creating a controlled gap between the cap and opening that allows gas to escape while preventing external contaminants from entering. After a dwell period sufficient for gas evacuation, the cap is then moved into full sealing engagement with the container.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage closure process: first, the closure cap is advanced to cover the container opening but held in a non-sealing position, creating a controlled gap between the cap and opening that allows gas to escape while preventing external contaminants from entering. After a dwell period sufficient for gas evacuation, the cap is then moved into full sealing engagement with the container.

abstract: An endless power transmission belt construction, cord therefor and methods of making the same are provided, the cord having the yarns and the plies thereof respectively twisted on a 2 for 1 twister so as to cause the longitudinal axes of the fiber filaments to be disposed generally in the longitudinal direction of the cord with the denier of the fiber filaments of each yarn being approximately 1500. The twist multiplier of three plies is 3.7687 as the plies are twisted together at a rate of approximately 2.9 turns per linear inch of the cord, and the twist multiplier for the two yarns is 3.6765 as the two yarns for each ply are twisted together at a rate of approximately 4.9 turns per linear inch of that ply. The twist multiplier for five plies is 3.6986 as the plies are twisted together at a rate of approximately 1.8 turns per linear inch of the cord, and the twist multiplier for three yarns is 3.5838 as the three yarns for each ply are twisted together at a rate of approximately 3.9 turns per linear inch of that ply. The fiber filaments comprise p-aramid that comprises co-poly (paraphenylene/3,4'oxydiphenylene terephthalamide).
problem: Creating a power transmission belt with optimal fiber orientation to maximize tensile strength and load-bearing capacity along the belt's length while maintaining structural integrity and flexibility.
constraint: The twist rate at each hierarchical level must be balanced: tighter twisting improves fiber alignment but can introduce stress concentrations and reduce flexibility, while looser twisting allows fiber misalignment that reduces tensile strength. The specific twist multipliers at each level must be coordinated to achieve optimal alignment without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Hierarchical controlled twisting at multiple structural levels: individual yarns are twisted together to form plies, and plies are twisted together to form the final cord, with specific twist rates (twist multipliers) at each level chosen to progressively align the high-strength fiber filaments in the longitudinal direction of the cord. This multi-level twist control orients fibers along the primary load path.
mechanism_raw: Hierarchical controlled twisting at multiple structural levels: individual yarns are twisted together to form plies, and plies are twisted together to form the final cord, with specific twist rates (twist multipliers) at each level chosen to progressively align the high-strength fiber filaments (p-aramid) in the longitudinal direction of the cord. This multi-level twist control orients fibers along the primary load path.

abstract: To an electroless gold plating bath comprising a water-soluble gold compound, a complexing agent, and a reducing agent is added a small amount of polyvinyl pyrrodidone. The bath allows a satisfactory gold plating film to be formed on metal portions on a non-conductive substrate without plating spread.
problem: Forming a gold plating film on non-conductive substrates without lateral plating spread during electroless plating.
constraint: The concentration of polyvinyl pyrrolidone must be carefully controlled to balance inhibition of plating spread with sufficient deposition rate for practical plating.
mechanism: Introducing a kinetic modifier into a deposition medium to selectively alter growth rates, suppressing lateral expansion while enabling directional deposition on target regions through controlled concentration balancing.
mechanism_raw: Adding a small amount of polyvinyl pyrrolidone to the plating bath modifies the deposition kinetics, selectively inhibiting lateral growth while enabling vertical deposition on target metal areas.

abstract: Kit, and method for its use and construction, which includes a first plurality of vessels containing different polysubunits, each constructed from a known number of subunits. Each subunit is joined by one or more bonds and each subunit and bond can be the same or different. Each of the different polysubunits has a different sequence of subunits but has the same known subunit at one terminus. Each vessel contains polysubunits which have a different known subunit at one terminus. The kit further includes a second plurality of vessels which includes different polysubunits, each constructed from the known number minus one subunit, as described above.
problem: Systematically constructing complex molecules (polysubunits) with known structural variations for combinatorial synthesis or analysis.
constraint: Each vessel must maintain a fixed known subunit at one terminus while allowing variability in the remaining subunits to ensure systematic combinatorial exploration.
mechanism: Partitioning structural units into modular containers where each container enforces a fixed reference point at one end while allowing variable configurations in remaining positions, enabling systematic combinatorial assembly and comparative analysis.
mechanism_raw: Organizing subunits into modular vessels where each vessel contains polysubunits sharing a common terminus but varying in internal sequence, enabling controlled assembly and comparison of structural variants.

abstract: Methods are disclosed for producing substantially flat processed meat products and, more specifically, flat casingless hot dogs. In the disclosed methods a material containing substantial amounts of the meat protein is formed prior to cooking into a flat form of a predetermined thickness by pressing the uncooked material. The flat form is then heated either simultaneously with the forming or thereafter to a temperature and for a time sufficient to congeal a sufficient amount of the protein to stabilize the shape of the flat form but insufficient to cause any substantial rendering of the material. The surface of the congealed flat form is then treated by smoke, drying or both to establish its texture and flavor, and the treated flat form is then finally cooked into the food product. The flat form is cut into discrete flat shaped patties either at the beginning of the method or subsequent to cooking or chilling. The meat product formed by the method of the invention has a unique layered cross-section, and pleasantly pocked surface appearance, color and texture.
problem: Producing flat, stable processed meat products with controlled texture, appearance, and structural integrity without casing.
constraint: Heating must be precisely controlled to congeal proteins enough to stabilize the flat form but not so much as to cause fat rendering or structural collapse.
mechanism: Shaping a material into a target form prior to thermal processing, then applying controlled heat to induce structural stabilization through protein coagulation while avoiding degradation, followed by surface modification and final thermal treatment.
mechanism_raw: Pre-forming the meat into a flat shape before cooking, then heating to congeal proteins sufficiently to stabilize the shape while avoiding rendering, followed by surface treatment and final cooking.

abstract: Apparatus and method for making powder from a metallic melt by atomizing the melt to form droplets and reacting the droplets downstream of the atomizing location with a reactive gas. The droplets are reacted with the gas at a temperature where a solidified exterior surface is formed thereon and where a protective refractory barrier layer (reaction layer) is formed whose penetration into the droplets is limited by the presence of the solidified surface so as to avoid selective reduction of key reactive alloyants needed to achieve desired powder end use properties. The barrier layer protects the reactive powder particles from environmental constituents such as air and water in the liquid or vapor form during subsequent fabrication of the powder to end-use shapes and during use in the intended service environment.
problem: Producing reactive metal powders with a protective barrier layer to prevent environmental degradation during subsequent fabrication and use.
constraint: The reaction temperature and gas exposure time must be controlled to form the barrier layer without overheating the droplet core or allowing excessive penetration of reactive species.
mechanism: Disintegrating a molten material into discrete units and exposing them to a reactive environment under conditions that form a protective surface layer, creating a barrier that limits inward diffusion of reactive species into the core.
mechanism_raw: Atomizing a metallic melt into droplets and reacting them with a reactive gas at a temperature where a solidified exterior forms a refractory barrier layer, limiting further reaction penetration into the droplet core.

abstract: A magenta toner for developing an electrostatic image is formed of magenta toner particles containing at least a binder resin, a magenta pigment and a polar resin. The binder resin comprises a styrene polymer, a styrene copolymer or a mixture thereof. The magenta pigment comprises a solid solution pigment of C.I. Pigment Red 122 and C.I. Pigment Violet 19, or a solid solution pigment of C.I. Pigment Red 202 and C.I. Pigment Violet 19, and the polar resin has an acid value of 3-20 mgKOH/g. The magenta toner particles are preferably formed through suspension polymerization of a polymerizable monomer mixture including at least styrene monomer, the solid solution pigment and the polar resin. With the aid of the polar resin, the solid solution pigment can be well dispersed in the resultant magnetic toner particles to fully exhibit its coloring power.
problem: Achieving uniform dispersion of a solid solution pigment in toner particles to maximize coloring power and performance in electrostatic imaging.
constraint: The polar resin's acid value must be within a narrow range (3–20 mgKOH/g) to optimize dispersion without destabilizing the polymerization process or altering toner electrostatic properties.
mechanism: Incorporating a resin with a defined interaction parameter into a polymerization process to enhance binding between dispersed particles and the matrix, preventing agglomeration through optimized surface affinity during phase transition.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a polar resin with a specific acid value into the toner formulation during suspension polymerization, which enhances pigment-particle interactions and prevents agglomeration during polymerization.

abstract: A point-of-sale drop safe and change making mechanism employs a cash drop drawer that is movable between open and closed positions and receives money, when the cash drop drawer is open. When the cash drop drawer is closed the cash drops into receptacle in drop safe. A currency acceptor accepts and registers paper currency bills and a money dispensing mechanism in the cabinet dispenses coins in a plurality of denominations into receptacle or tray located on the exterior of the cabinet. A money selection arrangement includes a plurality of user-actuable coin select keys or switches that are disposed on the exterior of the cabinet. The keys correspond respectively to coin denominations, e.g., key #1 dispenses dollar coins, key #2 dispenses quarters, etc. A controller board coupled to the currency acceptor, the money select mechanism, and the money dispensing mechanism obtains and stores an escrow amount or money credit amount when paper currency is inserted into the currency acceptor. The user actuates the money dispenser to dispense coins in selected denominations, and the control mechanism decrements the escrow or credit amount. The drop safe can also have a bill-dispensing mechanism. The arrangement can also be configured to change money from the currency and coins of one country to that of another. In that case, the escrow amount is automatically converted from the value in one country's funds into that of the other.
problem: Managing real-time cash transactions where users insert currency and receive change in multiple denominations while maintaining accurate accounting of funds.
constraint: The system must balance accurate escrow tracking with real-time dispensing to prevent overdraft or miscalculation, while supporting multiple denominations and currencies.
mechanism: A transactional system tracks incoming and outgoing funds through an escrow mechanism, where inserting value increments a tracked balance and dispensing value decrements it, ensuring real-time reconciliation and enabling conversion between different value denominations.
mechanism_raw: A controller links a currency acceptor and coin dispenser via an escrow/credit system: inserting currency increments an escrow amount, and dispensing coins decrements it, ensuring transactional integrity and enabling cross-currency conversion.

abstract: A ground floodlight for an aircraft having a fuselage including a forward cargo door includes a generally flat lens having a first region for directing light toward the front cargo door and a second region for directing light generally forward to illuminate ground in front of the aircraft. The lens is generally flat and smooth and is adapted for flush mounting in the fuselage. A corresponding method for improving ground floodlight illumination includes directing light generated from a lamp within the fuselage in an outward direction and then redirecting first and second portions of the light toward the front cargo door and the ground in front of the aircraft, respectively.
problem: Illuminating two distinct regions (front cargo door and forward ground) from a single light source in a compact, flush-mounted aircraft installation.
constraint: The lens must maintain a smooth, flush profile to integrate with the aircraft fuselage while achieving precise light redirection for both target areas.
mechanism: A single light source is coupled to a planar optical element with spatially separated regions, each configured to redirect light toward a distinct target area, enabling simultaneous illumination of multiple zones without additional fixtures.
mechanism_raw: A flat lens with two optically distinct regions redirects light from a single internal lamp: one region directs light toward the cargo door, and another directs it forward to illuminate the ground, enabling dual-purpose illumination without separate fixtures.

abstract: This invention concerns an injection molding process for soles having a colored treading surface produced with expansible and cross-linking "EVA" compounds involving the use of colored inserts molded with the same molding material used for sole, but of a different color, fed into cups on the bottom of the mold impression and shut by caps also molded in the same material used to mold the soles.
problem: Producing a shoe sole with a colored tread surface that is integral to the sole structure without requiring post-molding assembly or adhesives.
constraint: The inserts and sole must use the same base material to ensure adhesion and structural continuity, while the colored inserts must withstand the molding process without degradation.
mechanism: Colored elements are positioned within a mold cavity prior to injecting a primary material, ensuring the colored elements bond monolithically with the primary material during a single molding process to form an integral surface.
mechanism_raw: Colored material inserts are placed into mold cups on the sole impression before injecting the primary molding material, ensuring the colored tread bonds monolithically with the sole during the same molding process.

abstract: A method and device for counting and discriminating documents including currency documents comprising a discriminating unit wherein the failure of a bill to be identified by the discriminating unit to causing the operation of the device to be suspended after the unidentified bill has been transported to an examining location for convenient examination by an operator. The device is provided with document-type selection elements. When an unidentified bill is found to be acceptable, an appropriate document-type selection element is chosen. The selection of a document-type selection element causes appropriate counters to incremented and the device to resume operation. The device is also provided with a continuation selection element. Alternatively, when an unidentified bill is found not be acceptable, the document is removed from the output receptacle and the continuation selection element is chosen. Selection of the continuation selection element causes the device to resume operation without any counters being adversely affected. In a manner similar to the handling of unidentified bills, the device may flag documents based on their forward /reverse orientation. Alternatively, the device may sort documents based on their forward/reverse orientation.
problem: Handling unidentified or misoriented documents in an automated counting/discrimination system without disrupting overall operation or corrupting counters.
constraint: The system must isolate unidentified documents for manual review while preserving the integrity of automated counters and enabling seamless resumption of operation.
mechanism: When an item fails automated classification, the system halts processing, diverts the item to a review interface, and permits manual operator input to determine its disposition, resuming operation with counters adjusted only for validated items.
mechanism_raw: When a document fails identification, the system suspends operation, transports the document to an accessible examination location, and allows an operator to classify it (accept/reject) or flag orientation, resuming operation with counters adjusted only for accepted documents.

abstract: A load bearing structure having a set of uniform voids functions to resolve the forces imposed by developing compression in the material having the voids and minimizing the amount of tension developed in the material. The voids are deployed to encompass a matrix of points arranged such that each point is spaced an equal distance from twelve and only twelve adjacent matrix points. If the structure is considered to be composed of a closely packed set of hypothetical rhombic dodecahedra (RD) and the four-edge vertices of each of those hypothetical RDs is truncated, the result will be a set of cubic voids. The center of each of those cubic voids will define the matrix referred to above and the cubic voids will serve to provide the optimum resolution of stress which minimizes the development of tension in the material. One in four of the hypothetical RDs can be eliminated achieving the same force resolution in a structure containing less material. The shape and size of the voids can be varied with only slight loss in optimum stress resolution. Some voids can be omitted with only slight loss of optimum stress resolution.
problem: Designing a load-bearing structure that minimizes tension in the material while resolving compressive forces through strategic void placement.
constraint: The void geometry must balance structural integrity with material efficiency, allowing some voids to be omitted or resized with minimal loss of stress resolution.
mechanism: A load-bearing structure incorporates a repeating void pattern derived from a geometric tessellation, where each void is equidistant from multiple adjacent voids, distributing compressive forces while minimizing tensile stress in the material.
mechanism_raw: Voids are arranged in a matrix where each point is equidistant from twelve adjacent points, derived from truncated rhombic dodecahedra geometry, creating cubic voids that optimize stress distribution and reduce tensile forces in the material.

abstract: Cigarettes and methods of making them, in which an insulated fuel element is combined with a substrate assembly comprising a substrate within a tube, combining a roll of tobacco with a plug of tobacco paper, combining the fuel element/substrate assembly with the tobacco/tobacco paper assembly, and combining the resulting combination with a filter element to produce filter cigarettes. Methods of constructing the various and preferred subassemblies are also disclosed.
reason: The abstract describes a product assembly process with specific components (fuel element, substrate, filter) but does not identify a causal functional mechanism that produces a useful effect beyond the specific product. The focus is on combining parts rather than a transferable operational principle.

abstract: A power steering apparatus in which an adjusting operation for an orifice, which is provide to optimize a steering characteristic, can be easily performed. A rotary control valve controls an amount of working oil to be supplied to a power assist cylinder in response to a relative rotation between an input member and an output member. A counter force mechanism, provided in the rotary control valve, includes a counter force plunger, a hydraulic pressure counter force chamber located on an outer side of the counter force plunger and an inside chamber located on an inner side of the counter force plunger. The counter force mechanism provides a counter force to the input member by a pressure difference between a pressure of the working oil in the hydraulic pressure counter force chamber and a pressure of the working oil in the inside chamber. A hydraulic pressure control valve is attached to the rotary control valve. The hydraulic pressure control valve includes a counter force mechanism port through which the working oil is supplied to the counter force mechanism. A connection passage connects between the inside chamber and the counter force mechanism port. An orifice is provided to a part of a connection passage located in the hydraulic pressure control valve.
problem: Optimizing steering characteristics in a hydraulic power steering system by enabling easy adjustment of an orifice that controls fluid flow and pressure distribution.
constraint: Balancing the orifice size to achieve desired steering feel without introducing excessive complexity or compromising the system's ability to maintain stable pressure differentials under varying loads.
mechanism: A variable flow restriction in a fluid circuit creates a controllable pressure differential between opposing chambers, generating a counteracting force on an input member. Adjusting the restriction size modulates the pressure difference, enabling fine-tuning of resistance and responsiveness in a mechanical system.
mechanism_raw: A hydraulic pressure control valve with an orifice in a connection passage allows modulation of pressure differences between chambers in a counter force mechanism. This pressure difference generates a controllable counter force on the input member, enabling fine-tuning of steering resistance and responsiveness.

abstract: Pads for posting removable adhesive sheets capable of receiving markings are disclosed. The pads comprise a stack of a plurality of adhesive sheets having release sheets adhered to the back of each, wherein each adhesive sheet, when applied to a surface, is removable without leaving an adhesive residue. The adhesive sheets comprise a flexible polymer film, polymer-reinforced sheet or cloth having a Taber stiffness of not less than 0.03 measured according to ASTM D747, a front side capable of receiving markings and a back side substantially covered with a pressure sensitive adhesive having an initial tack value of at least 200 g measured according to ASTM D2979 on a Polyken.TM. probe tack tester, an adhesive tack sufficient to prevent conformability failure of the adhesive sheet after 10 hours conformability testing, and an adhesive strength of at least 100N/m according to ASTM D1000 and each release sheet covers at least 50 percent of the pressure sensitive adhesive on the back of each adhesive sheet. A process for making such pads and a kit for dispensing adhesive sheet/release sheet combinations are also disclosed. The pads, processes and kits of this invention are useful for posting robust temporary and semi-permanent removable notes in an industrial or commercial setting.
reason: The abstract specifies material properties (stiffness, tack, release sheet coverage) and product features but does not describe a causal functional mechanism that produces a useful effect beyond the specific adhesive sheet design. The focus is on material selection and product specifications rather than a transferable operational principle.

abstract: A service valve for isolating the compressor of a chiller system from a flooded evaporator cooler that includes a suction pipe mounted in the top section of the evaporator that extends downwardly into the evaporator shell and a shut-off valve mounted inside the shell that is arranged to close against the bottom opening of the suction pipe. The valve is connected by linkage to a shaft that passes through the suction pipe outside the evaporator which when rotated, permits the valve to be opened and closed.
problem: Isolating a compressor from a flooded evaporator in a chiller system while enabling remote operation of an internal shut-off valve without compromising the sealed environment of the evaporator.
constraint: Maintaining a leak-proof seal along the shaft-to-pipe interface while transmitting sufficient torque to operate the valve in a high-pressure, submerged environment.
mechanism: A sealed rotary actuator transmits rotational motion through a shaft to operate a valve within a pressurized, enclosed environment. The shaft maintains a leak-proof interface while transferring torque, allowing remote actuation of the internal valve without compromising the sealed system.
mechanism_raw: A shut-off valve is positioned inside the evaporator shell and connected via a shaft that passes through the suction pipe. Rotating the external shaft actuates the internal valve, allowing opening/closing without requiring access to the sealed interior of the evaporator.

abstract: There is provided a torque control assembly for use on a continuous motion bag machine comprising torque driven means and a drive for driving a motor wherein the torque driven means is operatively connected to the motor for lowering a tension in a web prior to the web entering a sealing assembly on the bag machine. There is also provided a continuous motion bag machine comprising the torque control assembly.
problem: Controlling tension in a moving web (e.g., plastic film) prior to a sealing assembly in a continuous motion bag machine to ensure consistent sealing quality without disrupting the continuous process.
constraint: Balancing torque reduction to achieve optimal tension without causing web slippage or introducing variability in the continuous motion process.
mechanism: A torque modulation system adjusts the rotational force applied to a moving web by varying the torque transmitted from a drive motor. Reducing torque decreases tension in the web before a processing station, enabling precise control of slack to optimize performance without disrupting continuous motion.
mechanism_raw: A torque-driven mechanism is operatively connected to the motor driving the web. By lowering the torque applied to the web, the system reduces tension before the sealing assembly, allowing precise control of web slack to optimize sealing performance.

abstract: The angularly accessible head for a threaded connector comprises a spherical structure having a centered slot therein, the slot having a bottom surface or wall in the shape of an inverted V, with a center point thereof extending toward and terminating below the center of the sphere. The head is functionally accessible from a plurality of planes which are not coplanar with a center plane of the slot.
problem: Need for a connector head that allows tool access from multiple non-coplanar angles without requiring precise alignment.
constraint: Balancing multi-angle accessibility with structural integrity of the spherical head and slot geometry.
mechanism: A geometric interface with a central aperture shaped to permit engagement from multiple non-parallel orientations, where the aperture's geometry maintains structural continuity while enabling tool access without precise alignment.
mechanism_raw: A spherical structure with a centered slot shaped as an inverted V, where the slot's center point extends below the sphere's center. This geometry enables functional accessibility from multiple planes by allowing the tool to engage the slot from varying angular orientations while maintaining structural continuity.

abstract: A spinner head provides for the production of high fat content floss. The spinner head includes a base and a cover spaced from the base. A plurality of discrete spaced apart elongate heating elements are positioned between the base and the cover and define a chamber for accommodating feedstock material therein. The chamber is spun and the feedstock material is heated and is expelled through the spaces between the heating elements. Feedstock engagement surfaces are positioned in alignment with each of the spaces between the heating elements so as to engage the expelled feedstock to alter the direction of travel of the expelled product.
problem: Producing high-fat content floss with controlled texture and directional flow during spinning and heating processes.
constraint: Maintaining uniform heating and mechanical engagement to control product direction and consistency without clogging or uneven expulsion.
mechanism: A rotating containment system with internal heating elements and directional redirection surfaces, where material is heated and expelled through controlled pathways to alter physical properties during ejection.
mechanism_raw: Heating elements positioned between a base and cover create a spinning chamber where feedstock is heated and expelled through inter-element spaces. Feedstock engagement surfaces aligned with these spaces redirect the expelled material's travel direction, altering its physical properties during ejection.

abstract: A method and a structure provide emulation circuit implemented on a logic block module comprising clocked and unclocked field programmable logic devices (FPGAs). Software modules analyze the target logic circuit and impose delay constraints to require certain storage instances to be implemented on separate FPGAs so as to prevent hold time violation artifacts.
problem: Preventing hold time violations in FPGA-based emulation circuits caused by timing mismatches between storage instances.
constraint: Balancing delay constraints with FPGA resource allocation to avoid over-partitioning while maintaining timing accuracy.
mechanism: A partitioning mechanism that enforces temporal isolation between critical signal paths by distributing dependent storage elements across separate processing units, ensuring timing constraints are met through spatial separation.
mechanism_raw: Software analysis of the target logic circuit imposes delay constraints that force specific storage instances to be implemented on separate FPGAs, ensuring timing requirements are met by isolating critical paths and preventing race conditions.

abstract: A vertical movement clip for attaching a channeled beam or stud member to a horizontal building member. The clip has the advantage of easily sliding into the interior of the stud and wedging between two parallel legs of the stud member to fit securely therein. The clip also has the advantage of providing an attachment flange that securely attaches to and holds the floor to the stud and prevents most all horizontal movements and yet allows for vertical floor movement relative to the stud. A second embodiment includes a first and second arm having bent portions for increased loading capacity.
problem: Securing a floor to a vertical stud member while accommodating vertical movement (e.g., thermal expansion) and preventing horizontal displacement.
constraint: Achieving sufficient grip to prevent horizontal movement without restricting necessary vertical displacement.
mechanism: A mechanical interface that permits axial displacement while constraining lateral movement through a wedging engagement element and frictional resistance, maintaining structural connection under dynamic conditions.
mechanism_raw: A clip with a wedging body slides into the stud's interior and grips between parallel legs, while an attachment flange secures the floor. The design allows vertical sliding motion but resists horizontal forces through friction and geometric constraint.

abstract: Process and apparatus for the purification of a cryogenic fluid in liquid, diphase, gaseous or supercritical state, having boiling point Pe, with at least one of its impurities having a boiling point Pe', with Pe'>Pe. The process includes at least one step selected from the group comprised by: PA1 a filtration step of at least one impurity in solid state, PA1 and an adsorption step of at least one impurity in liquid or gaseous state; PA1 and in which there is recovered at least one portion of the cryogenic fluid at least partially purified.
problem: Purifying cryogenic fluids containing impurities with higher boiling points, which may exist in solid, liquid, or gaseous states.
constraint: Managing phase transitions of impurities (solid to liquid/gas) during purification to ensure effective separation without re-contamination.
mechanism: A multi-stage separation process that exploits phase-dependent removal mechanisms, using differential volatility to isolate contaminants while recovering the target fluid in a cryogenic environment.
mechanism_raw: Combining filtration (for solid impurities) and adsorption (for liquid/gaseous impurities) in a cryogenic environment, exploiting the boiling point differential between the fluid and impurities to selectively remove contaminants while recovering purified fluid.

abstract: Kneading device for high-consistency fiber pulp that includes at least two substantially rotationally symmetrical and coaxial kneading machines, that are movable relative to each other. The kneading machines may include teeth in ring-shaped tooth rows forming ring shaped gaps between the tooth rows and positioned relative to one another such that at least one tooth row of one of the at least two kneading machines reaches into the ring-shaped gaps of an other of the at least two kneading machines. A face side of at least a portion of the teeth may include an angled surface for diverting the fiber pulp in a transport direction, provided by a throughput of a flow of the fiber pulp through the kneading device and by relative movement between the fiber pulp and the face side. At least a portion of the teeth may include angled surfaces on a rear side. An angle .alpha.1 of a slope on the face side may differs from an angle .alpha.2 of the rear side by at least 5.degree., and at least a portion of the teeth may be mounted in a releasable fashion, so that a position of the face side and the rear side may be exchangeable by rotating the teeth.
problem: Efficiently kneading and transporting high-consistency fiber pulp through a device while maintaining controllable directional flow and allowing reconfiguration of the kneading action.
constraint: The angle difference between face and rear slopes must be at least 5 degrees to create meaningful asymmetric flow behavior, and the teeth must be releasably mounted to permit rotational reconfiguration of their directional orientation.
mechanism: Two coaxial, intermeshing rotors carry surface elements with asymmetric angular profiles: one side of each element has a slope at angle alpha1 and the opposite side at angle alpha2, where alpha1 differs from alpha2 by at least 5 degrees. The first angled surfaces divert material in a transport direction through relative movement between material and element face, while the second angled surfaces provide different flow characteristics. The intermeshing elements create ring-shaped gaps that induce shearing. The elements are releasably mounted so that rotating them exchanges the first and second side positions, allowing the directional bias of the kneading and transport action to be reconfigured.
mechanism_raw: Two coaxial, intermeshing kneading rotors have teeth with asymmetric surface angles: the face side has a slope at angle alpha1 and the rear side at angle alpha2, where alpha1 differs from alpha2 by at least 5 degrees. The face-side angled surfaces divert fiber pulp in a transport direction through relative movement between pulp and tooth face, while the rear-side angled surfaces provide different flow characteristics. The intermeshing teeth create ring-shaped gaps that induce shearing. The teeth are releasably mounted so that rotating them exchanges the face and rear side positions, allowing the directional bias of the kneading and transport action to be reconfigured.

abstract: A structure of book page for binding a book or album comprising an elongate sheet composed of a plurality of continuous sections each including a wide rectangular portion abutting a narrow rectangular portion divided by a first and a second folding lines, a pair of flap members abutting two ends of the wide rectangular portion and divided by a pair of third folding lines, a pair of trapezoidal indentations in two ends of the narrow rectangular portion engageable with the trapezoidal flap members. Both the flap members and the narrow rectangular portion are folded upward along the second and third folding lines and attached to the upper surface of the wide rectangular portions. Where the sections are folded downward along the first folding lines. So that a continuous double-layer book pages are therefore accomplished with a trapezoidal concave in the inside margin of each of the outmost pages for receiving the trapezoidal flaps of a pair of hard covers.
problem: Creating a continuous, multi-layer book page structure from a single elongate sheet that self-aligns and provides integrated connection points for hard covers without separate fasteners or alignment hardware.
constraint: The trapezoidal indentations and flaps must have complementary angles to ensure self-aligning engagement, and the fold lines must be precisely positioned so that the wide and narrow sections fold correctly to form the double-layer structure with properly aligned connection points.
mechanism: A continuous elongate sheet contains pre-defined fold lines dividing it into wide and narrow rectangular sections, with flap members at the ends of the wide sections and complementary trapezoidal indentations in the narrow sections. When folded along the fold lines, the flap members and trapezoidal indentations engage each other to form double-layer pages. The trapezoidal shapes on both the indentations and the cover flaps provide self-centering, self-aligning engagement — the trapezoidal concave inside margins of the outermost pages receive the trapezoidal flaps of the covers, creating a geometric interlock that automatically positions and secures the covers.
mechanism_raw: A continuous elongate sheet contains pre-defined fold lines dividing it into wide and narrow rectangular sections, with flap members at the ends of the wide sections and complementary trapezoidal indentations in the narrow sections. When folded along the fold lines, the flap members and trapezoidal indentations engage each other to form double-layer pages. The trapezoidal shapes on both the indentations and the cover flaps provide self-centering, self-aligning engagement — the trapezoidal concave inside margins of the outermost pages receive the trapezoidal flaps of the hard covers, creating a geometric interlock that automatically positions and secures the covers.

abstract: The invention provides a process for the protection of active reinforcements embedded in a concrete mass against the effects of oxidation, said reinforcements being possibly in the form of a bunch of cables or strands arranged in a sheath, providing also the possibility to detect imperfections of the injection grout such as voids or porosity, wherein at least one channel is first drilled in the concrete mass opening in front of the reinforcements which have to be protected, whereafter a corrosion inhibiting solution is injected into the said channel while applying a high power pulsating wave to the said solution to make it penetrate and each channel is occluded.
problem: Protecting steel reinforcements embedded in concrete from oxidation while ensuring the corrosion-inhibiting solution penetrates deeply into the concrete matrix around the reinforcement, and detecting grout imperfections such as voids or porosity.
constraint: The pulsating wave must be of sufficiently high power to overcome the flow resistance of the concrete matrix and drive penetration beyond what steady pressure could achieve, and the channel must be positioned in front of the reinforcement to direct the solution flow toward the target area.
mechanism: A channel is formed in the material mass in front of the reinforcement to be protected. A corrosion-inhibiting solution is introduced into the channel while simultaneously applying high-power pulsating pressure waves to the solution. The pulsating waves create dynamic pressure oscillations that drive the solution deeper into the porous material matrix and around the reinforcement, overcoming the static flow resistance that would prevent steady-pressure injection from reaching all areas. The pulsation also helps reveal voids or porosity in the grout by creating detectable variations in flow response. After injection, each channel is occluded.
mechanism_raw: A channel is drilled in the concrete mass in front of the reinforcement to be protected. A corrosion-inhibiting solution is injected into the channel while simultaneously applying high-power pulsating pressure waves to the solution. The pulsating waves create dynamic pressure oscillations that drive the solution deeper into the porous concrete matrix and around the reinforcement cables or strands, overcoming the static flow resistance that would prevent steady-pressure injection from reaching all areas. The pulsation also helps reveal voids or porosity in the grout by creating detectable variations in flow response. After injection, each channel is occluded.
residual_terms: ["pulsating pressure waves", "high-power", "dynamic pressure oscillations", "porous matrix", "flow resistance", "occluded"]

abstract: A crystal growth method for growing on a gallium arsenide (GaAs) substrate a gallium nitride (GaN) film which is good in surface flatness and superior in crystallinity. According to the method, a GaAs substrate having a surface which is inclined with respect to the GaAs(100) face is used. The inclination angle of the substrate surface is larger than 0 degree but smaller than 35 degrees with respect to the GaAs(100) face. The inclination direction of the substrate surface is within a range of an angular range from the 0,0,1! direction of GaAs to the 0,-1,0! direction past the 0,-1,1! direction and angles less than 5 degrees on opposite sides of the angular range around an 1,0,0! direction of gallium arsenide taken as an axis, or within another range crystallographically equivalent to the range. The GaN layer is formed on the surface of the GaAs substrate preferably by hydride vapor deposition method.
problem: Growing a gallium nitride (GaN) film on a gallium arsenide (GaAs) substrate with good surface flatness and superior crystallinity, despite lattice mismatch and different crystal structures between the two materials.
constraint: The substrate inclination angle must be greater than 0 degrees but less than 35 degrees, and the inclination direction must fall within the specified crystallographic angular range (or an equivalent range) to achieve the desired atomic step configuration that guides proper GaN growth.
mechanism: A substrate is used whose surface is inclined at an angle between 0 and 35 degrees relative to a reference crystal face, with the inclination direction within a specific crystallographic range. This controlled surface inclination creates specific atomic step configurations and surface energy distributions on the substrate that guide the nucleation and epitaxial growth of the film. The inclined surface provides a template with optimized step density and orientation that promotes two-dimensional growth mode, resulting in improved surface flatness and crystallinity of the film. The angular range and direction are chosen to optimize lattice matching and growth kinetics between the substrate and film.
mechanism_raw: A GaAs substrate is used whose surface is inclined at an angle between 0 and 35 degrees relative to the GaAs(100) face, with the inclination direction within a specific crystallographic range from the [0,0,1] direction to the [0,-1,0] direction past the [0,-1,1] direction. This controlled surface inclination creates specific atomic step configurations and surface energy distributions on the substrate that guide the nucleation and epitaxial growth of the GaN layer. The inclined surface provides a template with optimized step density and orientation that promotes two-dimensional growth mode, resulting in improved surface flatness and crystallinity of the GaN film. The specific angular range and direction are chosen to optimize lattice matching and growth kinetics between the GaAs substrate and GaN film.
residual_terms: ["0 and 35 degrees", "crystallographic range", "atomic step configurations", "epitaxial growth", "two-dimensional growth mode"]

abstract: This invention provides a premanufactured portable concrete house and efficient systems for making such a house and for providing portability to a housing site. Floor, roof, and wall components are made by casting concrete in molds with features such as electrical and water conduits being concrete-embedded during the casting. Also concrete-embedded in the various house components are steel plates used for welding to secure the components to each other during assembly of a portable house. Spaced core holes for holding lift rods are cast into the periphery of the floor/foundation component; and these are used as lift points in lifting the house onto a truck for transport to a housing site.
problem: Creating a portable concrete housing system that can be efficiently manufactured off-site, transported to a housing site, and assembled on-site without requiring additional hardware or modifications to the concrete components.
constraint: All functional features (conduits, steel plates, core holes) must be embedded during the casting process rather than added afterward, and the steel plates must be positioned to allow welding access while the core holes must be spaced appropriately around the periphery to provide balanced lifting points for safe transport.
mechanism: Structural components are cast in molds with multiple functional features embedded directly during the casting process: utility conduits are embedded within the material, connection plates are embedded for joining components during assembly, and spaced core holes are cast into the periphery of the base component to serve as lift points. By embedding all these features during casting, the same components can be lifted and transported using the core holes and lift rods, and then assembled on-site by joining the embedded connection plates — no additional hardware, brackets, or post-casting modifications are needed. The embedded features serve dual purposes: the connection plates enable structural assembly while the core holes enable transport.
mechanism_raw: Concrete components (floor, roof, and wall elements) are cast in molds with multiple functional features embedded directly during the casting process: electrical and water conduits are embedded within the concrete, steel plates are embedded for welding connections between components during assembly, and spaced core holes are cast into the periphery of the floor/foundation component to serve as lift points. By embedding all these features during casting, the same concrete components can be lifted and transported using the core holes and lift rods, and then assembled on-site by welding the embedded steel plates together — no additional hardware, brackets, or post-casting modifications are needed. The embedded features serve dual purposes: the steel plates enable structural assembly while the core holes enable transport.
residual_terms: ["embedded during casting", "core holes", "spaced", "lift points", "connection plates", "joining", "no additional hardware"]

abstract: It is an object of the present invention to reduce the abrasion at a pressure receiving portion of the cylinder block, without increasing the manufacturing cost, even when the outer rings of a bearing are jointly rotated and eccentrically fluctuated. The cylinder blocks are made of aluminum alloy comprising, by weight, 1.5 to 3.5% of Cu, 13 to 16% of Si, 0.5% or less of Mg, 1.0% or less of Zn, 1.0% or less of Fe and the remainder of Al. The matrix, except for primary Si crystal, is relatively soft. Primary Si crystals which each independently project from the pressure receiving portions tend to be pushed into the base material by the outer rings of the thrust bearings, so that the levels of primary Si crystals are easily made to be approximately uniform. As a result, the interference and thrust load from the outer rings can be appropriately supported by a large number of primary Si crystals, and a jointly rotating motion and an eccentric fluctuation can be appropriately supported by a large number of primary Si crystals under severe operating conditions.
problem: Reducing abrasion at pressure-receiving portions of cylinder blocks under joint rotation and eccentric fluctuation without increasing manufacturing costs.
constraint: Balancing matrix softness and Si crystal hardness to ensure load distribution without increasing material or processing costs.
mechanism: A composite structure combining hard discrete elements embedded in a softer continuous matrix distributes localized loads across multiple hard regions, creating a uniform load-bearing surface that accommodates dynamic mechanical fluctuations while maintaining structural integrity under severe operating conditions.
mechanism_raw: Hard primary Si crystals embedded in a relatively soft aluminum alloy matrix are depressed into the base material under load from bearing outer rings, creating a uniform surface that distributes interference and thrust loads across many crystals, enabling robust support under severe operating conditions.
residual_terms: ["Si crystals", "aluminum alloy matrix", "bearing outer rings", "interference and thrust loads"]

abstract: A method of microfinishing the edge of a die component includes polishing the edges after the die component is machined by known methods to finish the edges of the die component to a smoother finish than the rest of the die component. This eliminates the incidence of undesirable streaking defects in the coating. The polishing step can be lapping, vapor honing, or grit blasting. The edges are polished to a finish of less than 8 microinches.
problem: Eliminating streaking defects in coatings on die components caused by rough-machined edges.
constraint: Achieving a sufficiently smooth edge finish without introducing excessive processing steps or costs.
mechanism: Surface irregularities on a component edge are reduced below a critical roughness threshold via abrasive finishing processes, eliminating localized defects in subsequently applied coatings by ensuring uniform material deposition over the treated surface.
mechanism_raw: Smoothing edges to a finish below 8 microinches via lapping, vapor honing, or grit blasting reduces surface irregularities that induce coating defects, ensuring uniform coating application.

abstract: A sealable, transparent, biaxially oriented multilayer polypropylene film comprising a core layer, optionally one or more intermediate layers located on one or both sides of the core layer, and at least one top layer on the one or more intermediate layers or on one or both sides of the core layer, wherein the core layer contains a polypropylene polymer or a polypropylene mixture; the optional intermediate layers consist essentially of a polypropylene polymer or a polypropylene mixture; and wherein at least one top layer is sealable, comprises a polyolefin copolymer or terpolymer, has a thickness of .ltoreq.0.4 .mu.m, and does not contain silicon dioxide or polydimethylsiloxane. The film is suitable as a packaging or wrapping film.
problem: Creating a sealable, transparent, biaxially oriented polypropylene film for packaging without compromising clarity or sealability.
constraint: Optimizing layer thickness and material composition to balance sealability, transparency, and structural integrity.
mechanism: A multi-layer structure incorporates a thin surface layer with material properties optimized for sealing, positioned to minimize optical interference while maintaining structural continuity with underlying layers, enabling simultaneous transparency and sealability in a flexible film.
mechanism_raw: A layered structure with a thin (≤0.4μm) sealable top layer of polyolefin copolymer, free of silicon dioxide or polydimethylsiloxane, provides sealability while maintaining transparency through minimal interference with light transmission.

abstract: A cold-rolled steel sheet or a zinc or zinc alloy layer coated steel sheet containing 0.0010 to 0.01 wt % of C and having a steel composition containing one or two kinds of 0.005 to 0.08 wt % of Nb and 0.01 to 0.07 wt % of Ti in the ranges given by {(12/93)Nb+(12/48)Ti*} .gtoreq.0.0005, 0.ltoreq.C-{(12/93)Nb+(12/48)Ti*}.ltoreq.0.0015, and Ti*=Ti-{(48/32)S+(48/14)N } , in which a bake hardenability BH f the steel sheet at 170.degree. C..times.20 min after 2% tensile prestrain is 10 to 35 MPa and the BH (MPa) and a yield strength YP (MPa) of the steel sheet satisfy the ranges given by BH.gtoreq.exp(-0.115.multidot.YP+23.0) and 0.67.multidot.BH+160.ltoreq.YP.ltoreq.-0.8.multidot.BH+280.
problem: Improving bake hardenability (BH) of cold-rolled steel sheets while maintaining yield strength (YP) within specific ranges for automotive applications.
constraint: Maintaining strict compositional ranges and mathematical relationships to achieve target BH and YP without compromising formability.
mechanism: Alloying element concentrations are controlled according to predefined mathematical relationships that balance strain-induced hardening potential with yield strength requirements, enabling optimization of post-forming thermal treatment response while maintaining specified mechanical property ranges.
mechanism_raw: Precise control of Nb and Ti alloying element ratios, governed by mathematical relationships between composition, BH, and YP, enables optimization of strain-induced hardening and strength balance.

abstract: A novel protein having inhibitory activity on the protease activity of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) activator was purified and isolated, and its molecular weight (ca. 30,000 daltons) and partial amino acid sequence were determined. A gene coding for the protein was cloned, and the gene DNA was incorporated into a vector, for transforming host cells. Cultivation of the transformant gave the desired protein. The protein can be used as an in vivo or in vitro control factor for HGF or HGF activator. It is also useful as an antigen to be used in producing an antibody to be used as means for kinetic studies of the protein, or as a standard in assay systems therefor.
reason: The mechanism is highly specific to biochemical interactions (protein inhibiting HGF activator protease) and lacks a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: A centrifuge having a housing defining a chamber features a containment system with a decelerator to reduce the kinetic energy of debris traveling from the chamber toward the housing. The chamber includes an opening, and a lid is pivotally mounted to the housing to selectively cover the opening. The decelerator includes a first annular member extending from a periphery of the opening inwardly toward the chamber, terminating in a downwardly extending angled region, as well as a second annular member extending downwardly in spaced relation with respect to the housing, forming a gap therebetween.
