The second annular member, the first annular member and the annular gap define a trap adapted to preventing debris from impinging upon the gasket and the lid. An annular baffle extends downwardly from the lid and is adapted to seat proximate to the trap upon the lid being positioned to cover the opening.
problem: Debris traveling from a centrifuge chamber toward the housing, lid, or gasket during operation risks damaging components or compromising containment.
constraint: Balancing debris containment effectiveness with minimal interference to the centrifuge's rotational motion and structural integrity.
mechanism: A flow redirection and deceleration structure with annular channels and a collection zone slows and isolates particulate matter from a rotating system, while a sealing element positioned near the collection zone further isolates debris from critical components.
mechanism_raw: A decelerator with annular members and a trap redirects and slows debris through a controlled gap and angled surfaces, while a baffle on the lid seats near the trap to further isolate debris from critical components.

abstract: A method of manufacturing Construction and Demolition ("C&D") disposal debris into a substitute/alternative daily/initial cover product approved by an environmental regulatory authority for use at a solid waste disposal landfill, wherein the C&D disposal debris, before processing/manufacturing, is considered a raw material/feed stock composed of a commingled inseparable mixture of solid waste components/items which are classified based on their origin as C&D disposal debris. These components are mechanically processed by screening or shredding to a predetermined specification particle size to collectively create/form a "C&D Recovered Screen Material" ("RSM") product. This C&D-RSM product is applied as daily/initial cover material covering compacted and leveled Municipal Solid Waste ("MSW") substituting the normally used sand, dirt or earthen materials at permitted/licensed MSW disposal landfills operating with a landfill leachate containment system or other approved site location. Once applied, this manufactured MSW disposal landfill substitute C&D-RSM daily cover product is treated with a formulated solution in order to meet the required environmental regulatory authority specifications necessary for any product or material to be approved by them as a MSW disposal landfill daily/initial cover material or as a substitute daily/initial cover product.
problem: Construction and demolition debris must be converted into a regulated, usable material for landfill cover without relying on raw earth materials.
constraint: Achieving regulatory compliance while maintaining cost-effectiveness and material consistency across variable input debris compositions.
mechanism: Size reduction through mechanical comminution followed by chemical conditioning transforms heterogeneous input material into a regulated, homogeneous product suitable for substitution of traditional raw materials.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical processing (screening/shredding) reduces debris to a uniform particle size, followed by chemical treatment to meet environmental standards, enabling substitution of traditional cover materials.

abstract: A nozzle body and coupler bearing assembly for discharging a liquid material. The nozzle body consists of approximately thirty-two serially and concentrically arranged ports which receives liquid from an attached hose under high pressures. The various points of placement of the ports, combined with the rotation produce a balanced and stabilized effect on the rotating nozzle assembly which allows the nozzle assembly to be delivered to a target area, and while in operation, have the ability to be left unattended by fire-fighting personnel. The wild and natural whipping action exhibited from a fire hose under high operating pressures is nullified with the present nozzle. The body of the nozzle is a hollow paraboloid attached to a coupler bearing assembly. The nozzle body is made from a resilient and durable material with concavo-convex surfaces with a plurality of ports emitting liquid in a radial "Dandelion puff" pattern. Three of the four port groups have approximate angles which are arranged tangentially and acutely to the axis of rotation and flow. The fourth group has an approximate angle which is arranged acutely to the horizontal plane of the longitudinal axis of rotation and flow. The nozzle assembly may be transported, delivered, placed, propelled, launched, carried, or otherwise put in any mode, means, or fashion to a target to which a liquid needs to be provided or dispersed.
problem: High-pressure fire hoses exhibit unstable whipping motions that hinder precise liquid delivery and require constant manual control.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient liquid flow rate and spray pattern effectiveness while achieving mechanical stability under extreme pressure.
mechanism: Opposing fluidic forces generated by strategically oriented discharge ports counteract reactive motion, stabilizing a high-velocity liquid delivery conduit through balanced momentum exchange.
mechanism_raw: Strategically arranged ports with tangential and acute angles generate counteracting forces that stabilize the nozzle assembly, enabling unattended operation by nullifying whipping through balanced fluid dynamics.

abstract: A soft-milling wheat which produces dough having exceptionally low visco-elasticity is provided by breeding from a variety having Glu-D1 double null trait, such as the landrace "Nap Hal". The wheat can be used in the manufacture of biscuits and wafers without the need to treat the flour with agents such as sodium metabisulphite.
problem: Traditional wheat dough requires chemical additives to achieve low visco-elasticity for delicate baked goods like biscuits and wafers.
constraint: Balancing gluten reduction with sufficient dough cohesion to maintain processability during manufacturing.
mechanism: Genetic modification of a biological material reduces structural protein network formation, inherently producing a product with reduced mechanical cohesion without external chemical intervention.
mechanism_raw: Breeding wheat with a Glu-D1 double null genetic trait reduces gluten network formation, inherently producing dough with the desired low visco-elasticity without chemical treatment.

abstract: An artist's compartmented pastel case (50) and color arrangement for organizing, transporting, storing, and accessing artists' pastels, for use with computer graphics applications, and databases, as well as for use with traditional methods of painting with pastels. The case has a lid (60) which contains a removable resilient liner or pad (70) which protectively cushions and immobilizes pastels when the case is closed for transport. The color compartment arrangement (100) translates the painter's color triangle into a rectangular format by placing the three primary colors, red, yellow, and blue, in analogous locations (FIGS. 5 and 6). An empty, central compartment or current palette area (120) is provided as a place where all colors in current use can be grouped together. Empty subcompartments or holding areas (122), one located within each color compartment (FIG. 13), are also provided to hold selected pastels (172). The case's two-level construction keeps its color compartments free of dust and debris. A top layer of alignment elements on a mesh-like support grid (140) positions pastels within each color compartment, and allows pastel dust and fragments to fall into a collection chamber below. A color chart, disposed on the interior surface (130) of the lid, and viewed by removing the resilient pad, can be labeled and used to select pastel colors that have been calibrated with colors displayed on-screen in computer graphics, tutorial, or database applications (FIG. 28).
problem: Artists need an organized, dust-free system to store and access pastels while aligning physical colors with digital color references.
constraint: Optimizing accessibility and dust containment without compromising portability or the precision of color calibration.
mechanism: A multi-tiered storage and retrieval system with color space mapping elements and a containment chamber enables organized access to particulate media while maintaining cleanliness and calibration alignment.
mechanism_raw: A two-level compartment design with a color triangle-to-rectangle translation, alignment elements, and a dust collection chamber enables efficient color selection and cleanliness, while a removable pad allows calibration with digital systems.

abstract: In S2, to-be-compressed image data is encoded and thus compressed each time when using a respective one of a plurality of templates. In S4, compression rates of encoded data are compared with each other which encoded data was encoded each time when a respective one of the plurality of templates was used in S2. In S6, encoded data having the highest compression rate and template identification information of a template used when the encoded data having the highest compression rate was obtained in S2 are output. The encoding comprises entropy encoding. The to-be-compressed data comprises video game software programs.
problem: Optimizing data compression efficiency when multiple encoding methods (templates) are available, particularly for heterogeneous data types like video game software.
constraint: Balancing computational overhead of testing multiple templates against the benefit of achieving optimal compression rates.
mechanism: Apply multiple encoding strategies to the same data, evaluate the resulting compression efficiency of each strategy, and select the strategy that achieves the highest compression efficiency. This dynamically adapts to data characteristics by leveraging variability in encoding effectiveness.
mechanism_raw: Encoding the same data with multiple templates, comparing the resulting compression rates, and selecting the template that yields the highest compression rate. This leverages entropy encoding variability to dynamically choose the most effective method for the given data.

abstract: Wafer debonding of a bonded bulk wafer and a device wafer using a liquid jet to avoid scratching of the wafers is provided. The wafer debonder includes a wafer loader having a first stand with a flat upper surface and a second stand located above the first stand having a lower surface slanted with respect to the upper surface of the first stand at a predetermined angle. A first holder is connected to the first stand and a second holder is located on an imaginary surface extended from the lower surface of the second stand for holding the wafers. A liquid jetting nozzle is positioned adjacent the wafer loader to direct a jet of liquid at the interface between the wafers to separate the wafers.
problem: Separating bonded wafers (e.g., in semiconductor manufacturing) without causing physical damage such as scratches to the wafer surfaces.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient force to separate the wafers while minimizing mechanical stress or abrasion on the wafer surfaces.
mechanism: Introduce a directed fluid jet at the interface between two bonded surfaces to apply localized force that breaks the bond. The fluid jet avoids direct mechanical contact with the surfaces, which are positioned at a controlled angle to facilitate separation while minimizing surface damage.
mechanism_raw: Using a directed liquid jet at the interface between bonded wafers to induce separation. The liquid jet applies localized force to break the bond while avoiding direct mechanical contact with the wafer surfaces, which are held at a controlled angle to facilitate separation.

abstract: A method of cleaning a solid surface which is particularly effective for a surface having a complicated structure including slots and holes comprises immersing the solid surface in a cleaning slurry comprising a cleaning liquid and abrasive particles which are soluble in the cleaning liquid, the cleaning liquid comprising a saturated solution so as to greatly reduce the dissolution of the abrasive particles in the cleaning liquid.
problem: Effectively cleaning solid surfaces with complex geometries (e.g., slots, holes) where traditional cleaning methods may fail to reach or may dissolve abrasive particles prematurely.
constraint: Maintaining abrasive particle integrity and cleaning efficacy over time while ensuring the cleaning liquid remains effective in complex geometries.
mechanism: Immerse a surface in a cleaning medium containing abrasive particles suspended in a liquid, where the liquid is maintained in a saturated state. The saturation reduces dissolution of the abrasive particles, preserving their mechanical integrity during cleaning while enabling effective removal of contaminants from complex geometries.
mechanism_raw: Immersing the surface in a cleaning slurry containing abrasive particles suspended in a cleaning liquid, where the liquid is a saturated solution. The saturation reduces dissolution of the abrasive particles, allowing them to remain effective longer while mechanically abrading the surface during cleaning.

abstract: A hand support device for use with a computer pointing device relieves repetitive motion stress and includes a top surface, a bottom surface, and a perimeter surface connecting the top surface and the bottom surface. The top surface includes: a palm support region, that is an inclined planar surface; a little finger support portion extending from the palm support region; a thumb support region extending from the palm support region; a front index positioned on a side of the palm support region, and between the little finger and thumb support regions; and a side index adjacent to and extending from the palm support and thumb support regions. The bottom surface facilitates sliding of the hand support device on a work surface. The hand support device reduces stress and risk of injuries resulted from repetitive motions by encouraging the user of a computer pointing device to employ two fields of motion to control the pointing device. The user engages the fingers, the hand, and the wrist to make fine movements while holding the hand support device stationary. The user moves the computer pointing device and the hand support device in unison with the arm and shoulder when making coarse movements.
problem: Reducing repetitive motion stress and injury risk for users of computer pointing devices by optimizing hand and arm movement patterns.
constraint: Balancing ergonomic support with the need for precise and fluid control of the pointing device during both fine and coarse movements.
mechanism: Enforce two distinct motion regimes through a support mechanism: one regime restricts movement to localized body parts (e.g., fingers, hand, wrist) while keeping the controlled device stationary, and another regime moves the device in coordination with larger body segments (e.g., arm, shoulder). This distributes mechanical effort across different muscle groups to reduce repetitive strain.
mechanism_raw: Designing a hand support device that enforces two distinct motion fields: fine movements (using fingers, hand, and wrist while keeping the device stationary) and coarse movements (moving the device in unison with the arm and shoulder). This distributes motion across different muscle groups and reduces strain on any single area.

abstract: An automated speech recognition system converts a speech signal into a compact, coded representation that correlates to a speech phoneme set. A number of different neural network pattern matching schemes may be used to perform the necessary speech coding. An integrated user interface guides a user unfamiliar with the details of speech recognition or neural networks to quickly develop and test a neural network for phoneme recognition. To train the neural network, digitized voice data containing known phonemes that the user wants the neural network to ultimately recognize are processed by the integrated user interface. The digitized speech is segmented into phonemes with each segment being labelled with a corresponding phoneme code. Based on a user selected transformation method and transformation parameters, each segment is transformed into a series of multiple dimension vectors representative of the speech characteristics of that segment. These vectors are iteratively presented to a neural network to train/adapt that neural network to consistently distinguish and recognize these vectors and assign an appropriate phoneme code to each vector. Simultaneous display of the digitized speech, segments, vector sets, and a representation of the trained neural network assist the user in visually confirming the acceptability of the phoneme training set. A user may also selectively audibly confirm the acceptability of the digitization scheme, the segments, and the transform vectors so that satisfactory training data are presented to the neural network. If the user finds a particular step or parameter produces an unacceptable result, the user may modify one or more of the parameters and verify whether the modification effected an improvement in performance. The trained neural network is also automatically tested by presenting a test speech signal to the integrated user interface and observing both audibly and visually automatic segmentation of the speech, transformation into multidimensional vectors, and the resulting neural network assigned phoneme codes. A method of decoding such phoneme codes using the neural network is also disclosed.
problem: Training a neural network for speech recognition tasks (e.g., phoneme identification) in a way that allows non-expert users to iteratively refine parameters and validate results.
constraint: Balancing user-guided parameter adjustment with automated training processes to ensure efficient convergence while maintaining model accuracy.
mechanism: Segment input data into labeled units, transform each unit into multidimensional representations using user-selected methods, and iteratively train a model with these representations. Concurrent visual and auditory feedback allows users to validate or adjust parameters at each step, ensuring data quality before finalizing the trained model.
mechanism_raw: Segmenting digitized speech into labeled phoneme units, transforming each segment into multidimensional vectors using user-selected methods, and iteratively training the neural network with these vectors. Simultaneous visual and auditory feedback enables users to confirm or adjust parameters (e.g., segmentation, transformation) at each step, ensuring training data quality before finalizing the model.

abstract: Lathes for working brake rotors and other components as desired. The lathes employ a pivoting carriage which mounts a tool for working, cutting, finishing or otherwise having a desired effect on the workpiece. Control of carriage positioning is accomplished preferably using a feedscrew, hydraulic or other desired linkage which is connected, directly or indirectly, to the carriage and to the frame of the lathe (other mechanisms or linkages may also be used). Such lathes may also employ a slide carriage for working brake drums, which carriage is preferably located on the side of the lathe opposite the pivoting carriage. The slide carriage may be easily removed and sold as a separate unit to allow a number of options for buyers. This arrangement also eliminates the changeover time and effort required in conventional lathes that employ cross slide mechanisms; instead of the need to replace the tool post assembly ordinarily employed in working rotors with the boring bar assembly ordinarily used for working drums in conventional lathes, the operator simply uses the already-configured rotor or drum working unit on the desired side of the lathe. Lathes according to the present invention are mechanically simpler, and easier and less expensive to manufacture because they eliminate the need for conventional cross slide mechanisms. Because of the simplicity, however, lathes according to the present invention allow more precise control over the tool and thus a more precise finish on the workpiece.
problem: Time-consuming changeover between working on brake rotors and drums in conventional lathes due to cross slide mechanisms requiring tool post replacement.
constraint: Balancing mechanical simplicity and manufacturing cost against the precision of tool control, as the simplified design must still maintain sufficient accuracy for finishing operations.
mechanism: Two independently operable tool mounting assemblies positioned on opposing sides of a machine frame, each pre-equipped with a distinct working unit, enabling selection of a desired working unit without disassembling or reconfiguring the mounting hardware. The assemblies are mechanically decoupled so that operation of one does not require adjustment or movement of the other.
mechanism_raw: Dual independent tool carriages (pivoting and slide) positioned on opposite sides of the lathe frame, allowing pre-configured rotor/drum working units to be used without mechanical reconfiguration. The pivoting carriage and slide carriage operate independently, eliminating the need to swap tool assemblies.

abstract: A lifter device for a jacquard machine comprising a first lifter element and a second lifter element suspended from at least one hook, respectively. The hook is adapted to be selected to be carried along by one of two knives moving up and down in counterphase. A reversing roller is provided on the device. A lifter cord is provided. The lifter cord is either attached at one end to a part of the machine and is then passed over a roller of the first lifter element or is attached directly to the first lifter element. In either case the cord is passed over a reversing roller and a roller of the second lifter element. The other end of the cord is connected to at least one harness cord. The reversing roller is hingedly fixed and is disposed with its working face diagonal to the working faces of the rollers of the lifter elements.
problem: Coordinating the lifting of multiple harnesses in a jacquard machine to create complex textile patterns while maintaining synchronization between opposing motion systems.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and tension of the cord path across the reversing roller and lifter element rollers to maintain synchronization without slippage during high-speed operation.
mechanism: A tensioning element routed over a pivoting redirection point and two opposing force-applying elements moving in counterphase, transmitting controlled bidirectional forces to synchronize the motion of two driven components and their associated flexible transmission elements. The redirection point is angled relative to the driven components to maintain alignment and prevent slippage during high-speed operation.
mechanism_raw: A lifter cord routed over a hinged reversing roller (diagonally oriented relative to the lifter element rollers) and two counterphase-moving knives, enabling controlled bidirectional force transmission to synchronize the movement of two lifter elements and their associated harness cords.

abstract: Magnetic field generating apparatus comprises a pair of axially spaced coils which are so arranged that when energized, they produce a magnetic field which has a zero axial field or substantially zero axial field at an axial position midway between the coils. The annular space between the coils is filled with a material such as steel or steel with a layer of material magnetized in the radial direction, which enhances the radial field strength generated by the coils. The apparatus as application in the growth of single crystals of semiconductor material.
problem: Generating a controlled magnetic field configuration with a zero axial field at a specific midpoint for applications like single-crystal semiconductor growth.
constraint: Balancing coil spacing, material permeability, and current distribution to maintain the zero axial field at the desired position while maximizing radial field intensity for crystal growth efficiency.
mechanism: Two axially separated field-generating elements energized to produce opposing fields that cancel at a midpoint between them, combined with an annular field-shaping element positioned between the generating elements to amplify radial field intensity while preserving the axial null point at the midpoint.
mechanism_raw: Two axially spaced coils energized to produce opposing fields that cancel axially at their midpoint, combined with an annular material (e.g., steel or radially magnetized layer) between the coils to amplify radial field strength while preserving the axial null point.
residual_terms: ["field-generating elements", "annular field-shaping element", "axial null point", "radial field intensity"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for loading a film cartridge in a camera frame having a cartridge chamber, a supply chamber, and a thumbwheel extending into the cartridge chamber. The film cartridge has a case, an internal spool, and a filmstrip attached to the spool. In the method, the film cartridge is positioned in the cartridge chamber with the spool axially adjoining the thumbwheel. A quill is placed in axial proximity to the spool of the film cartridge, opposite said thumbwheel. The quill is turned in a rewind direction for the spool. Rotating of the spool in the rewind direction is deterred. During the turning, the quill is urged into axial engagement with the spool and the spool is urged into axial engagement with the thumbwheel. Following the urging, a leading portion of the filmstrip is thrust out of the cartridge.
problem: Reliably loading a filmstrip from a cartridge into a camera frame without manual intervention or risk of film damage during spool engagement.
constraint: Maintaining precise axial alignment and rotational resistance between the quill, spool, and thumbwheel to avoid slippage or over-tensioning during film extraction.
mechanism: Coordinated axial and rotational engagement of a driven shaft and a gripping element to selectively couple with a rotatable core, preventing free rotation while applying controlled rotational and axial forces to advance a flexible strip from a containment vessel through a guided path.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated axial engagement of a quill (rotated in rewind direction) and a thumbwheel to grip the spool, deterring free rotation while thrusting the filmstrip's leading end out of the cartridge through controlled rotational and axial force application.

abstract: A wax applicator for use in a depilatory waxing procedure. The wax applicator has a body portion (10) with a mounting part (11) for the mounting of the body portion to a wax container (T). A flow passage (13) leads from the mounting part (11) to a narrow elongate outlet (14). Wax can flow from the container (T) along the flow passage (13) to the outlet (14). A spreader (15) is associated with the outlet (14). The spreader (15) has a distal edge located beyond the outlet so that in use wax issuing form the outlet (14) can spill over the distal edge of the spreader (15) as the applicator is moved forwardly in the direction in which the spreader (15) projects beyond the outlet (14).
problem: Applying a viscous material (e.g., wax) evenly across a surface during depilation without manual spreading or uneven distribution.
constraint: Optimizing the outlet-to-spreader geometry and material viscosity to ensure consistent flow rate and spillover without dripping or gaps during movement.
mechanism: A dispensing applicator with a spreading surface whose distal edge extends beyond the material exit opening, allowing viscous material to spill over the edge as the applicator advances, using the applicator's motion and gravitational force to distribute the material uniformly across a target surface via contact with the spreading surface.
mechanism_raw: A spreader with a distal edge extending beyond the outlet, allowing wax to spill over the edge as the applicator moves forward, leveraging the applicator's motion to distribute the material uniformly via gravity and contact with the spreader surface.

abstract: A device and associated method for simultaneously cutting a section of laminate to be inlaid and the underlying laminate to receive the inlay, which includes a portable cradle and a router mounted on an adjustable length shaft fitted into the chuck of the router, so that the distance that the cutting blade extends below the base of the portable cradle can be adjusted, the router is held within a rectangular router box split lengthwise on each side, hingedly held together on one side and detachably secured together on the opposite side by spring tension, with the router firmly attached to the top half so that the router cutting blade may be raised from the laminate surface by rotating the top half of the case around the hinge, while the angle of the cutting blade to the laminate is adjusted by means of adjustment screws on each side of the end of the router box opposite to the cutting blade, which rotate the router box up or down around a hinge means, on the bottom of the router box adjacent to the cutting blade, by which it is attached to the base of the portable cradle, the base has a straight edge guide extending beyond the cutting blade to assist straight line cuts of the laminate and a retractable pivot means at the center of the opposite end of the base which enable precise circular cuts of the laminate sheets. This device is utilized to cut the sheets of laminate while they are still mated with double-sided polyester adhesive, with the result that the angle of the cut in the edge of the laminate section to be inlaid precisely matches the angle of the cut in the edge of the laminate section to receive the inlay.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment between two mating cuts in laminate inlay and substrate during simultaneous cutting.
constraint: Balancing adjustability of blade position with structural rigidity to maintain cut precision during operation.
mechanism: A dual-axis adjustable mounting system that enables independent control of cutting element position and orientation relative to a work surface, while maintaining structural rigidity through compliant yet constrained mechanical linkages to preserve alignment during operation.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable mechanical coupling between a cutting blade and a base, allowing independent control of blade depth and angle relative to the work surface, while maintaining rigid alignment through hinged and sliding connections.
residual_terms: ["adjustable mounting system", "dual-axis", "structural rigidity", "compliant yet constrained mechanical linkages"]

abstract: Polymeric, water soluble, quaternary ammonium compounds (F) obtainable by quaternization of PA1 (a) at least one amino-group-containing urea compound that contains one or more groups of the formula EQU --NH--CO--NH--G--L-- (.alpha.) PA2 in which G signifies a bridging group PA2 and L signifies a tertiary, quaternizable amino group with PA1 (b) (b.sub.1) an epihalohydrin and optionally PA2 (b.sub.2) at least one further quaternizing agent to a quaternized product (q) and reaction of the quaternized product (q) with PA1 (c) a dialdehyde of formula (I) ##STR1## in which Z signifies methylene or the direct bond, or a urea derivative thereof, are suitable as fixing adjuvants in particular in continuous processes under nearly neutral to acidic conditions especially for the improvement of wet fastnesses of dyeings on hydrophilic fibrous material.
problem: Improving wet fastness of dyes on hydrophilic fibers under neutral to acidic conditions in continuous processes.
constraint: Achieving effective dye fixation without requiring harsh chemical conditions or compromising solubility in water-based processing.
mechanism: A polymeric binder formed through sequential chemical reactions that creates a water-soluble matrix capable of binding dyes via multiple interaction mechanisms (electrostatic and covalent) while maintaining solubility in aqueous environments under neutral to acidic conditions.
mechanism_raw: A water-soluble quaternary ammonium compound formed via sequential reaction of a urea derivative with epihalohydrin and a dialdehyde, creating a polymeric structure that binds dyes through electrostatic and covalent interactions while remaining soluble in aqueous environments.
residual_terms: ["polymeric binder", "water-soluble matrix", "electrostatic and covalent interactions", "aqueous environments"]

abstract: A knife includes two housings having a front portion for engaging with blades. One of the housings includes a projection formed in the front portion for engaging with a depression of the other housing so as to secure the front portions of the housings together. A rod is rotatably engaged in the rear portion of one of the housings. A cap is secured to one end of the rod, and a spring biases the cap to engage with the rear ends of the housings so as to secure the rear ends of the housings together. The housings can be secured together without additional tools.
problem: Securing a blade between two tool-free housings without additional tools or complex assembly steps.
constraint: Maintaining secure blade retention under operational stress while enabling rapid, tool-free assembly and disassembly.
mechanism: A tool-free mechanical retention system using complementary interlocking features between housing components, combined with a spring-energized compression mechanism that applies locking force when the assembly is rotated to secure the blade between the housings.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical interlock system using complementary projection-depression engagement between housing halves, combined with a spring-biased cap that applies compressive force to lock the assembly when the rod is rotated.
residual_terms: ["tool-free mechanical retention", "complementary interlocking features", "spring-energized compression", "locking force"]

abstract: A cosmetic applicator such as a mascara applicator is provided including a container for the cosmetic. The container includes a constriction at its upper part, forming a wiper, and a cap fitted with a rod having at its end a brush which dips into the container as it passes through the constriction. The rod has, above the brush, an elastically deformable cleaning element whose diameter is at least substantially equal to the diameter of the constriction. The portion of the rod located between the cleaning element and the brush allows the pressures prevailing inside and outside the container to be substantially balanced before the brush engages the constriction when it is withdrawn.
problem: Balancing internal and external pressures in a container during brush withdrawal to prevent disruption of the cosmetic composition or brush function.
constraint: Ensuring pressure equalization occurs without interfering with the brush's movement or the container's sealing integrity.
mechanism: An elastically deformable pressure regulation element positioned to dynamically adjust its volume in response to pressure differentials between a container's interior and exterior, enabling equalization without impeding the movement of an adjacent component through the regulated space.
mechanism_raw: An elastically deformable cleaning element positioned above the brush, which temporarily expands or contracts to equalize pressure differentials between the container interior and exterior before the brush engages the wiper.
residual_terms: ["elastically deformable pressure regulation", "pressure differentials", "dynamic volume adjustment"]

abstract: The current paths of a plurality of floating gate type MOSFETs are series-connected to form a series circuit. The series circuit is connected at one end to receive a reference voltage, and is connected to data programming and readout circuit. In the data programming mode, electrons are discharged from the floating gate to the drain of the MOSFET or holes are injected into the drain into the floating gate. The data readout operation is effected by checking whether current flows from the other end to the one end of the series circuit or not.
problem: Storing and reading data using floating gate MOSFETs in a compact, series-connected configuration.
constraint: Maintaining reliable charge retention in floating gates while enabling efficient current-based readout in a series architecture.
mechanism: A series-connected charge storage array where data states are encoded by altering charge levels in isolated gate structures, and information is retrieved by measuring current flow through the interconnected circuit based on the programmed charge states of individual elements.
mechanism_raw: Series interconnection of floating gate MOSFETs where data programming involves electron discharge or hole injection to alter gate charge states, and readout is determined by detecting current flow through the series circuit based on the programmed charge states.
residual_terms: ["series-connected charge storage array", "isolated gate structures", "programmed charge states"]

abstract: A carrying case for hair styling equipment that includes a clamshell briefcase structure having hingedly connected upper and lower briefcase sections. The lower briefcase section has an open topped cavity formed therein that is sealed when the upper and lower briefcase sections are pivoted together and an open sided tray storage compartment having a side opening in connection with the exterior of the lower briefcase section. The upper briefcase section has an exteriorly positioned cover flap affixable in a closed position by a zipper closure. The cover flap covers a hair dryer insertion opening formed in connection with an L-shaped, thermal fabric lined hair dryer storage compartment formed within the upper briefcase section; an accordion fold upper storage compartment member affixed to an interior surface of the upper briefcase section, the accordion fold upper storage compartment member being foldable out to from an accordion fold compartment, the accordion fold upper storage compartment member including a first plurality of storage pockets formed on a surface thereof; a drop-in, molded, anti-bacterial plastic storage insert sized to drop-in fit into the open topped cavity of the lower briefcase section, the storage insert including a second plurality of storage insert cavities formed therein; and a slide-in, molded, anti-bacterial plastic storage tray that is sized to slide into the side opening of the open sided tray storage compartment, the storage tray having a third plurality of storage tray cavities formed therein.
reason: The patent describes a product with multiple storage features (clamshell structure, compartments, anti-bacterial materials) but lacks a single causal mechanism that solves a problem through a functional relationship. The design is a collection of components rather than a transferable principle.

abstract: A device and method for engaging the fill valve assembly in a water closet and maintaining the fill valve assembly in a closed condition regardless to the level of water in the flush tank of the water closet. The device includes two suspension elements that engage the walls of the flush tank on either side of the float lever portion of the fill valve assembly. A flexible element extends between the two suspension elements, wherein the flexible element passes under the float lever as extends from one suspension element to the other. As the flexible element is pulled taut, the flexible element abuts against the float lever and upwardly biases the float lever. The upward bias that is applied to the float lever causes the fill valve assembly to close. The upward bias also prevents the fill valve assembly from leaving its closed configuration regardless to the level of water in the flush tank.
problem: Maintaining a fill valve assembly in a closed state regardless of water level in a flush tank.
constraint: The upward bias must remain effective across all water levels without interfering with normal valve operation.
mechanism: A resilient element is tensioned between two anchor points to apply a constant opposing force on a mechanical linkage, overriding the system's default state regardless of external fluctuations.
mechanism_raw: A flexible element is tensioned between two suspension elements to apply a constant upward bias on the float lever, mechanically overriding the valve's position independent of water level fluctuations.

abstract: A cover for closing a divided chemical dispensing container or hopper mounted on agricultural chemical-dispensing equipment. The cover closes the top of the hopper and includes a shim that seats on the divider that divides the interior of the hopper into two compartments of approximately equal size. The hopper cover is removably mounted on the top of the hopper and engages the slotted divider shim seated on the divider, to enclose the granular chemical contents of the hopper. In a preferred embodiment the hopper cover is characterized by a conventional first opening which communicates with one of the hopper compartments designed to contain a toxic chemical such as a granular insecticide. A hinged cover opens on a raised cover lip extending from the hopper cover to access a second cover opening that communicates with the opposite compartment, typically containing a granular, non-toxic fungicide. The hopper cover is fitted with a perimeter seal for sealing the perimeter of the cover on the hopper and with a divider seal for sealing the divider shim and isolating the toxic granules from the non-toxic granules inside the hopper when the hopper cover is placed on the hopper.
problem: Preventing cross-contamination between toxic and non-toxic chemicals stored in adjacent compartments of a hopper.
constraint: The cover must be removable for refilling while maintaining a reliable seal to prevent leakage or mixing.
mechanism: A removable barrier with sealing elements engages a partitioned interface to create a physical isolation zone between adjacent compartments, maintaining separation during access or transport.
mechanism_raw: A removable cover with perimeter and divider seals engages a slotted divider shim to physically isolate the two compartments when closed, ensuring substances remain separated during transport or use.

abstract: A method for recognizing and rewarding individual contributions is disclosed as including the steps of: (1) obtaining a recognition assembly adapted to removably retain a retaining member comprising at least one award seal, the award seal having a predetermined value; (2) personalizing the recognition assembly for a qualified recipient; (3) presenting the recognition assembly to the qualified recipient; (4) removing one or more award seals from the retaining member of the recognition assembly; and (5) redeeming one or more award seals for comparably valued merchandise or services. Correspondingly, the step of formulating goals and objectives in an attempt to target certain desirable behaviors from the qualified recipient may be included. Structurally, the recognition assembly may comprise a certificate member formed of a material being sufficiently sturdy for display, an award member including at least one fastening member for removably retaining the retaining member having one or more award seals, and a detachable connection disposed between the certificate and the award member. Alternatively, the recognition assembly may comprise a greeting card having a heading or greeting field, a field for a personalized greeting or message, and/or a field for identifying the person or persons presenting the greeting card.
problem: Incentivizing and rewarding individual contributions in a way that links behavior to tangible, redeemable value.
constraint: The system must balance personalization for the recipient with standardized redemption processes for comparably valued rewards.
mechanism: A recognition system with detachable value tokens allows recipients to physically separate and exchange tokens for standardized rewards, directly linking contributions to redeemable outcomes.
mechanism_raw: A recognition assembly with removable award seals (representing value) allows recipients to physically detach and redeem seals for merchandise, creating a direct causal link between contributions and rewards.

abstract: A flat pipe includes a hollow body having a pair of upper and lower walls extending substantially parallel to each other, and opposite lateral sides joined thereto, and a plurality of spacers closely fit between the upper and lower walls of the body and interconnected by a permeable sheet. The spacers are arranged at equal intervals to define a plurality of parallel fluid passages. The spacers are fused to opposite sides of the sheet in alternating relationship so that the sheet is inclined between adjacent spacers. The spacers are resistant to compression and deformation.
problem: Creating a flat, structurally stable pipe with parallel fluid passages that resist compression and deformation.
constraint: The spacers must remain rigid to prevent collapse while the permeable sheet allows fluid flow without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Structural elements are fused to a permeable medium in alternating orientations, forming inclined pressure-distributing sections that maintain parallel fluid pathways while resisting compression.
mechanism_raw: Spacers are fused to a permeable sheet in alternating orientations, forming inclined sections that distribute pressure while maintaining parallel fluid pathways between the spacers.

abstract: A method is provided for specifying and altering the electrical properties of fibers and fabrics. This allows the prescription of filter media prepared from these constituents for consistently optimum or near optimum performance in the collection of particulate matter. The method may include the steps of determining the triboelectric properties of fabrics having other desirable filter media characteristics, modifying the triboelectric properties of these fabrics as needed to preferentially selected properties and utilizing, selectively, modified fabrics as the filter medium for optimally attracting gas entrained electrically charged particles to the surface of the filter. The modification of the triboelectric properties may be realized chemically or by dyeing the fibers and fabric. The selected fabric has triboelectric characteristics that provide maximum attraction for the dust to be filtered so that when possible, as is most common, agglomeration of the particles on the surface of the filter is promoted, and the density of the particulate on the surface of the filter is increased. Additionally, determination and modification techniques are proposed for fabrics utilized as filter media and the blending of the included fibers, filaments or yarns of selected fibers so modified. These are then combined into a medium for use in filtering particulate matter having particles of various electric charges.
problem: How to consistently optimize filter media performance for collecting particulate matter with various electric charges, ensuring maximum particle attraction and agglomeration on the filter surface.
constraint: The triboelectric modification must preserve other desirable filter media characteristics (e.g., structural integrity, porosity) while working across particles with various electric charges, requiring selective and controllable modification techniques.
mechanism: Selectively modifying the electrostatic properties of a collection surface so that its charge polarity and magnitude are matched to the charge characteristics of target particles in a flowing stream, thereby maximizing electrostatic attraction forces between the surface and particles of specific charge polarities. The modification is applied in a controlled manner that preserves the structural and flow-through characteristics of the collection surface, promoting particle agglomeration and increasing particle density on the surface.
mechanism_raw: Tuning the triboelectric properties of filter materials to match the charge characteristics of target particles, thereby maximizing electrostatic attraction. The material's surface charge behavior is chemically or physically modified (e.g., via dyeing) so that the filter medium preferentially attracts particles of specific charge polarities, promoting agglomeration and increasing particle density on the filter surface.

abstract: A grinding machine to remove markings such as painted lines from a paved surface includes a wheeled carriage to be moved over the paved surface. A grinder is positioned beneath the carriage to contact and grind the paved surface. A suspension acts between the carriage and the grinder to allow the grinder to follow the profile of the paved surface as the grinding machine is moved thereover. A drive is supported by the carriage to actuate the grinder.
problem: How to grind markings from a paved surface while maintaining consistent tool-to-surface contact despite surface irregularities and contours.
constraint: The suspension must provide enough compliance to follow surface contours while still transmitting sufficient grinding force to the surface, balancing flexibility with effective material removal.
mechanism: A compliant coupling element is positioned between a moving support structure and a working tool, allowing the tool to pivot and adjust its orientation in response to variations in the surface contour being worked on. The coupling element passively adapts the tool's angular position to surface irregularities while a drive mechanism continues to actuate the tool, ensuring continuous contact and uniform material removal across the surface.
mechanism_raw: A compliant suspension system is placed between the moving carriage and the grinder, allowing the grinder to pivot and follow the profile of the surface being worked on. The suspension passively adapts the grinder's orientation to surface variations while the drive mechanism continues to actuate the grinder, ensuring continuous contact and uniform material removal.

abstract: In a paper-making machine, a method of determining a volumetric percentage of air in a fiber suspension for delivery to a headbox. The fiber suspension is transported through a fluid conduit. A sound transmitter and a target receiver are positioned relative to the fluid conduit. A sound is transmitted through the fiber suspension from the sound transmitter to the target receiver. A speed of the transmitted sound from the sound transmitter to the target receiver is established. The volumetric percentage of air in the fiber suspension is determined, dependent upon the established speed of sound.
problem: How to determine the volumetric percentage of air in a fiber suspension during paper-making without disrupting the process flow.
constraint: The measurement must be performed in-line during continuous production without interrupting the flow of the fiber suspension, requiring the sound transmission and reception to be positioned relative to the conduit without physical contact with the suspension.
mechanism: Transmitting a wave through a flowing multiphase medium and measuring its propagation characteristics, which vary predictably with the volumetric fraction of one phase relative to another. The measured propagation parameter serves as a proxy for the medium's composition, allowing non-invasive, in-line determination of phase volume percentage based on the established relationship between wave velocity and phase content.
mechanism_raw: Transmitting a sound wave through the fiber suspension and measuring its propagation speed, which varies predictably with the air content in the suspension. The speed of sound through the medium serves as a proxy for the suspension's composition, allowing non-invasive, in-line determination of air volume percentage based on the established relationship between sound velocity and air content.

abstract: A writing instrument having an elongated barrel comprised of an outer portion and an inner portion, rotatable relative one to the other. The point or writing tip is fixed to the barrel inner portion, disposed at an angle to, and may be offset from, the centerline of the barrel outer portion. The barrel inner portion is caused to rotate relative to the barrel outer portion by pressure on the writing instrument or weights attached to the barrel inner portion to bring the point into desired alignment during the writing process.
problem: How to maintain proper writing tip alignment relative to the writing surface during the writing process, compensating for angular misalignment caused by user pressure or motion.
constraint: The self-aligning mechanism must be compact and simple enough for integration into a handheld writing instrument while providing reliable rotational movement in response to writing pressure without excessive friction or play.
mechanism: The writing tip is mounted on an inner structural element that is rotatably coupled to an outer structural element, with the tip fixed at a non-parallel angle to the central axis. Applied pressure or motion causes the inner element to rotate relative to the outer element, automatically reorienting the tip into proper alignment with the writing direction during use through a self-correcting rotational coupling.
mechanism_raw: The writing tip is mounted on an inner barrel portion that is rotatably coupled to the outer barrel, with the tip fixed at an angle to the centerline. Pressure on the writing instrument or attached weights cause the inner portion to rotate relative to the outer portion, automatically reorienting the tip into proper alignment with the writing direction during use.

abstract: An alarm clock system including an alarm clock circuit having an alarm output signal; a radio transmitter circuit responsive to the alarm output signal of the alarm clock circuit in a manner to transmit a transmitted alarm signal; and an ear insert including an audible output transducer positioned within an ear insert housing, a radio receiving and alarm generating circuit tuned to receive the transmitted alarm signal and in electrical connection with the audible output transducer, the radio receiving and alarm generating circuit generating a signal to the audible output transducer in response to receipt of the transmitted alarm signal. In one preferred embodiment the radio transmitter is electrically coupled to the alarm clock circuit. In another preferred embodiment the radio transmitter circuit includes an audio pick-up, the alarm clock circuit includes a speaker, and the radio transmitter circuit is coupled to the alarm clock circuit through the speaker and the audio pick-up. When audio coupling is used, it is preferred to provide a mechanism for muting the output of the alarm circuit speaker.
problem: How to deliver an alarm signal to a user's ear without physical wiring between the alarm clock and the earpiece.
constraint: The wireless transmission must reliably convey the alarm signal to the ear insert, and when audio coupling is used, the speaker output must be muted to prevent audible interference while still allowing the signal to be transmitted through the acoustic path.
mechanism: Wireless decoupling of signal generation from signal delivery: a transmitter sends a control signal from a source circuit to a remotely located receiver containing an output transducer. An alternative embodiment uses acoustic coupling—repurposing the source's existing output element as an acoustic transmission medium picked up by a sensor on the transmitter—effectively using the output-sensor pair as a wireless bridge for the control signal.
mechanism_raw: Wireless decoupling of alarm signal generation from alarm delivery: a radio transmitter sends the alarm signal from the clock circuit to a remotely located ear insert containing a receiver and audible transducer. An alternative embodiment uses audio coupling—repurposing the clock's existing speaker as an acoustic transmission medium picked up by an audio pick-up on the transmitter—effectively using the speaker-pickup pair as a wireless bridge for the control signal.

abstract: A stripping tool for removing thorns, excess foliage and the like from plant stems having a handle with opposed stripping blades on one end. The handle has a pivot that normally holds the handle in an open position to allow a plant stem to be inserted therebetween. Manually squeezing the handle causes the handle to pivot about the connecting pivot bringing the stripping blades into contact with a stem. The handle is of a predetermined shape so as to provide a substantially hollow interior area thereby generally enclosing the plant stem. Thus the handle becomes a barrier between the users hand and the plant stem providing protection and generally containing the stripped thorns and foliage.
problem: Safely removing thorns and foliage from plant stems while protecting the user's hand from debris and injury.
constraint: Balancing the force required to strip the stem with the need to fully enclose the stem and protect the user's hand.
mechanism: A pivoting mechanism translates manual squeezing force into controlled cutting action via opposed blades, while an enclosing structure with a hollow interior contains debris and shields the user during stem processing.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting handle with opposed blades converts manual squeezing into controlled blade contact with the stem, while a hollow interior shape encloses the stem and acts as a barrier to contain debris and shield the user.

abstract: A new electrically powered corkscrew for aiding in the removal of corks from bottles, such as wine bottles. The inventive device includes a bottle holding unit which supports a bottle thereon and a corkscrew spiral mounted on the holding unit for both rotary motion and longitudinal movement. A first electric motor is coupled to the spiral for rotating the spiral, and a second electric motor is coupled to the spiral for longitudinally moving the spiral. Operation of the motors is controlled by a control unit for operating the spiral to at least partially removing the cork from the bottle.
problem: Efficiently and precisely removing corks from bottles without manual effort or inconsistent motion.
constraint: Synchronizing the rotational and longitudinal motions to avoid over-torquing or misalignment during cork removal.
mechanism: A dual-motion actuation system uses independent rotational and axial drives coordinated by a control unit to synchronize forces applied to a spiral element, enabling automated extraction through simultaneous rotational and longitudinal motion.
mechanism_raw: Two independent electric motors (one for rotation, one for longitudinal movement) are coordinated by a control unit to apply simultaneous rotational and axial forces to the corkscrew spiral, enabling automated and controlled cork extraction.

abstract: A pressure balance or proportioning valve which comprises a disk-shaped mobile unit (10) having a pair of cylindrical shells (12) extending from each side of the mobile unit (10) which is axially movable in a bore (2) of a housing which contains hot and cold water inlet (5) and outlet (3, 4) pipes. The housing includes hot and cold water outlet pipes (3, 4), a cold water inlet (5) or supply pipe in one end of the bore, and a hot water inlet (5) or supply pipe at the other and opposite end of the bore. The hot and cold water supply pipes terminate in end walls (7) and have cylindrical side walls (13) adjacent the end walls with openings (14) extending radially through the cylindrical side walls (13). The mobile unit (10) is disposed intermediate the end walls (7) and moves axially, in response to unequal water pressure, in the bore between the end walls (7). Movement of the mobile unit (10) results in the cylindrical shells (12) either blocking or uncovering the radially extending openings (14) thereby equalizing the amount of hot and cold water entering the hot and cold water outlet pipes.
problem: Maintaining a consistent mixture of hot and cold water flow to achieve a stable output temperature despite varying input pressures.
constraint: Ensuring smooth axial movement and precise alignment of openings to maintain flow balance without leakage or hysteresis.
mechanism: A pressure-responsive element axially shifts in response to inlet pressure differentials, mechanically modulating the exposure of radially positioned openings to balance flow rates of two fluid streams into a common outlet.
mechanism_raw: A pressure-responsive mobile unit axially shifts in response to unequal inlet pressures, mechanically adjusting the exposure of radially positioned openings to balance the flow rates of hot and cold water into the outlet.

abstract: The invention provides An electrochemical zinc-air multi-cell battery, each cell being of the type provided with a housing having, two outer major surfaces, and two spaced-apart inner walls, the inner walls defining a first inner chamber for containing therein a zinc electrode, and in conjunction with the outer major surfaces defining two outer chambers for receiving reaction air; two generally planar, gas-permeable, but liquid-impermeable air electrodes, each of the electrodes being installed in a window-like opening provided in each of the inner walls, an electrolyte in contact with the zinc electrode and the air electrodes, means for directing a flow of the reaction air into a first inlet provided in a first outer side surface of the housing through both of the outer chambers substantially in a uniform flow distribution across the outer faces of both of the air electrodes, and out of a second outlet provided in an opposite outer side surface of the housing, and cooling air flow directing means for causing cooling air to flow between two adjacently positioned cells, along the outer faces of the major surfaces of two interfacing adjacent cells, the surfaces respectively being arranged to be in contact with and to cool the reaction air in each of the outer chambers bounded by the respective surfaces.
problem: Managing heat and air distribution in a zinc-air battery to maintain performance and prevent overheating during operation.
constraint: Achieving uniform airflow distribution and effective cooling without compromising the liquid-tight integrity of the electrolyte or air-electrode interfaces.
mechanism: Directed airflow through partitioned chambers distributes reaction air uniformly across active surfaces, while auxiliary cooling airflow along adjacent major surfaces dissipates heat generated during electrochemical operation.
mechanism_raw: Directed airflow through outer chambers uniformly distributes reaction air across air electrodes, while cooling air flows between adjacent cells along their major surfaces to dissipate heat from the reaction air.

abstract: The television signal recording/reproducing system digitally records and reproduces television signals composed of a luminance signal, a chrominance signal and a resolution compensation signal included in predetermined television scanning lines. The system includes a Y/C separating circuit for separating the luminance signal Y from the chrominance signal C and a decoder for decoding the color signal into color difference signals C.sub.B, C.sub.R. One of the color difference signals C.sub.B, C.sub.R is combined with the resolution compensation signal, and a digital video signal recorder digitally records the combined resolution signal and the color difference signal. In this manner, the resolution compensation signal is accurately recorded.
problem: Accurately recording a resolution compensation signal alongside color difference signals in a digital television recording system without signal degradation or loss.
constraint: Preventing interference or data overlap between the combined signals during recording and reproduction to maintain signal integrity.
mechanism: A signal combination stage merges a resolution compensation signal with a color difference signal prior to digital storage, preserving their temporal and functional relationship to maintain fidelity during playback.
mechanism_raw: Combining one color difference signal (C_B or C_R) with the resolution compensation signal before digital recording ensures both signals are stored together, preserving their relationship and fidelity during playback.

abstract: A glass composition for a substrate consisting essentially of from 56 to 72 wt % of SiO.sub.2, from 1 to less than 14 wt % of Al.sub.2 O.sub.3, from 0 to 9 wt % of MgO, from 0.5 to 11 wt % of CaO, from 0 to 4 wt % of SrO, from 0 to 3 wt % of BaO, from 6 to less than 14 wt % of MgO+CaO+SrO+BaO, from 0 to 9 wt % of Na.sub.2 O, from 6 to 20 wt % of K.sub.2 O, and from 6 to 20 wt % of Na.sub.2 O+K.sub.2 O.
reason: The patent discloses only a specific glass composition with defined weight percentages of various oxides. It does not describe a causal functional mechanism that produces a useful effect through a problem-solving operation; it is merely a formulation specification without explaining how the components interact to achieve a desired outcome.

abstract: An apparatus for protecting a worker's hand and wrist, particularly from the power saws is used in a meat cutting or lumber cutting environment. The apparatus provides a generally planar armor plate covering the back of the wrist, hand and fingers. An insulating layer covers the lower surface of the armor plate. The armor plate is segmented into hingably related wrist, hand and finger plates. The finger plate may be compound, with separately hinged index finger and outer finger plates. A glove, worn by the user, is connected to the armor plate by a plurality of adjustable straps.
problem: Protecting a worker's hand and wrist from power saws while maintaining mobility in a cutting environment.
constraint: Balancing protection against cuts with the need for natural hand and finger movement.
mechanism: Use a plurality of rigid protective segments connected by flexible joints to allow articulation of a body part while maintaining a barrier against external hazards.
mechanism_raw: Segmented armor plate with hingably related wrist, hand, and finger plates that move with the hand but provide rigid protection against cuts.

abstract: A method for manufacturing a soft magnetic steel sheet is disclosed. The silicon steel sheet is made to undergo a finish treatment so that it can be put to the practical use. The finish treatment method for an Fe-Si silicon steel sheet manufactured by a direct casting method by directly contacting a molten pool to a cooling roll according to the present invention includes the step of pickling the manufactured Fe-Si silicon steel sheet, and carrying out a cold rolling. Then the silicon steel sheet thus cold-rolled is heat-treated at a temperature above 0.5 Tm (Tm: melting temperature of the steel sheet).
reason: The heat treatment step is a standard metallurgical process. While the temperature threshold (0.5 Tm) is specific, the underlying mechanism (heat treatment to improve material properties) is not a novel or transferable problem-solving principle.

abstract: Ether compounds, which are useful as solvents, cosmetics, detergents, lubricants, emulsifiers and so on, are produced by reacting (a) a hydroxy compound with a carbonyl compound of (b) a carbonyl compound under hydrogen atmosphere in the presence of a catalyst with ease and at a low cost. The reaction is carried out while removing out produced water by using a dehydrating agent during the reaction; by distilling off the water by azeotropic dehydration and the like; or by blowing gases such as hydrogen gas to flow through the reaction system.
problem: Efficiently producing ether compounds by driving a reversible reaction to completion.
constraint: Maintaining reaction conditions that allow water removal without disrupting the catalyst or reaction environment.
mechanism: Continuously remove a reaction byproduct from a reversible chemical system to shift equilibrium toward product formation, using physical separation or chemical absorption.
mechanism_raw: Actively removing water (a byproduct) during the reaction via dehydration agents, azeotropic distillation, or gas flow to shift the reaction equilibrium toward product formation.

abstract: An aerosol can disposal apparatus having an inlet chute provided with a retractable puncturing member which punctures the side of the aerosol can and a waste container which receives the punctured aerosol can via the inlet chute. The waste container is lined with a removable refuse liner having placed therein an absorbing material for removing harmful ingredients from the evacuating contents of the punctured aerosol can. The waste container is dimensioned to accumulate therein a large number of aerosol cans before the need to remove the accumulated aerosol cans and replace the removable refuse liner.
problem: Safely disposing of aerosol cans by puncturing them and containing hazardous residual contents.
constraint: Ensuring the absorbent material effectively neutralizes contents while the container accumulates multiple cans before requiring liner replacement.
mechanism: Integrate a puncturing element with a replaceable containment module containing reactive or absorbent media to safely process multiple hazardous items within a single vessel.
mechanism_raw: Combining a puncturing mechanism with an absorbent material in a removable liner to neutralize and contain harmful contents within a single integrated waste container.
residual_terms: ["puncturing element", "replaceable containment module", "reactive or absorbent media"]

abstract: A method for constructing a laminate comprising two layers, including an acrylic homopolymer layer and a microporous PTFE layer wherein the acrylic layer is a felt and is pretreated by immersion into an adhesive solution and introduced to the PTFE layer and subjected to heat and pressure to form a laminate useful as a filtration material. A laminate useful as a filtration material is formed by the immersion process.
problem: Constructing a durable, functional laminate for filtration applications from two distinct material layers.
constraint: Achieving adhesion between dissimilar materials (acrylic and PTFE) without compromising the microporous structure of the PTFE layer.
mechanism: Bond two dissimilar material layers using a controlled process that applies energy and pressure while preserving the structural integrity of at least one layer's functional microstructure.
mechanism_raw: Using an immersion process with heat and pressure to bond a pretreated acrylic felt layer to a microporous PTFE layer, creating a cohesive composite.
residual_terms: ["dissimilar material layers", "controlled process", "energy and pressure", "structural integrity", "functional microstructure"]

abstract: A waste treatment furnace includes a first waste treatment chamber with a first burner chamber communicating therewith, and a second waste treatment chamber with a second burner chamber communicating therewith. A common bottom wall is positioned under the first and second waste treatment chambers which is inclined downwardly from the first chamber to the second chamber to facilitate transfer of waste. Each burner chamber includes a burner and a plurality of protuberances disposed across its inner surface. The protuberances effectively reflect heat from the first and second burners so that the heater air in the first and second burner chambers is homogenized.
problem: Uneven heat distribution in a multi-chamber waste treatment furnace, leading to inefficient and inconsistent waste combustion across chambers.
constraint: The protuberance geometry must reflect heat effectively without obstructing airflow or burner function, and the inclination angle must be sufficient to move waste by gravity without causing spillage or uneven loading.
mechanism: Deploy reflective surfaces distributed across the interior walls of each combustion zone to redirect radiant energy from the heat source, inducing cross-zone circulation and mixing of the heated working fluid to equalize temperature. Establish a gravity-driven transfer path via a sloped shared floor between zones so that processed material flows from an upstream zone to a downstream zone, maintaining feed continuity in both zones.
mechanism_raw: Protuberances disposed across the inner surface of each burner chamber reflect and redirect radiant heat from the burners, causing the heater air to circulate and mix between the first and second burner chambers, thereby homogenizing the temperature distribution. A common bottom wall inclined downwardly from the first chamber to the second chamber uses gravity to facilitate transfer of waste material between chambers, ensuring both chambers remain fed.
residual_terms: ["reflective surfaces", "radiant energy", "heated working fluid", "gravity-driven transfer path", "sloped shared floor"]

abstract: A golf club travel bag comprising a generally parallelpiped shaped bag body having top, bottom, side, front and back panels preferably formed from foam padding interposing a knit backing and a ballistic nylon shell. An inset shoe case recesses into the travel bag from the front panel to maintain a substantially streamline outer surface. A generally rectangular flap cut into of the front panel operably covers the shoe case and provides access to the inset shoe case. The inset shoe case preferably includes a spike guard.
reason: This patent describes a product design with static components arranged in a specific configuration (inset shoe case, flap, padding layers). The 'inset' approach is a spatial layout choice rather than a causal mechanism that produces an effect through a functional relationship. No dynamic or self-regulating process is described.

abstract: A cervical spine protective helmet and shoulder harness assembly. The helmet and shoulder-harness assembly includes a yoke or shoulder pad having a central opening for the wearer's head to pass therethrough. A protective helmet is pivotally supported over the central opening. Arcuate tracks allow the head of the wearer to be turned from side to side. Stops within the pivoting joints supporting the helmet limit neck flexion and extension. Stops at the ends of these tracks limit neck torsion. Neck compression is limited by the rigidity of the uprights supporting the helmet.
problem: Protecting the cervical spine from injury during impact or sudden movement while still allowing the wearer necessary neck mobility for normal head turning and orientation.
constraint: The mechanical stops and track geometry must limit dangerous ranges of motion without overly restricting the wearer's ability to turn their head for situational awareness, and the upright rigidity must be sufficient to resist compression without adding excessive weight or bulk.
mechanism: Mount a protective shell on articulated arcuate guides that allow controlled rotational movement of the head. Integrate mechanical end-stops within the pivot joints to restrict angular displacement in flexion-extension and torsional directions to predefined safe limits. Maintain structural rigidity in the vertical support members to resist axial compressive loads applied to the neck during impact events.
mechanism_raw: The helmet is pivotally mounted on arcuate tracks that permit controlled side-to-side head rotation. Mechanical stops integrated into the pivoting joints limit neck flexion and extension to safe ranges, while stops at the ends of the tracks limit torsional rotation. The rigidity of the uprights supporting the helmet resists compressive forces on the neck during impact.
residual_terms: ["articulated arcuate guides", "mechanical end-stops", "pivot joints", "angular displacement", "flexion-extension", "torsional directions", "structural rigidity", "vertical support members", "axial compressive loads"]

abstract: A caulking gun and cartridge combination is provided with afterflow prevention. The cartridge has a tubular body, a forward dispensing opening at a forward end of the tubular body, and a backwall movably disposed within the tubular body. The caulking gun has a trough for receiving the cartridge, and a piston movable parallel to the trough. A trigger handle is used for pushing the backwall forward within the tubular body and causing a reduction of volume within the chamber in the cartridge. The backwall slides substantially in a contact-less manner within the tubular body, preferably by way of a reduced diameter of the backwall relative the inner diameter of the tubular body, so that it is pushed backwardly when the body retracts radially after actuation. Alternatively, the cartridge body may be prevented from expanding or may even be actively squeezed so that afterflow caused by the volume reduction of the relaxing tube body is safely prevented.
problem: Afterflow in caulking guns—continued unintended dispensing of sealant after the trigger is released—caused by elastic recovery of the cartridge tube body that increases internal volume and creates suction or pressure imbalances.
constraint: The radial clearance between the backwall and tube must be large enough to allow contact-less sliding and self-correction during elastic recovery, but small enough to maintain effective sealing and dispensing pressure during normal operation.
mechanism: Dimension a movable barrier within a flexible dispensing chamber such that a radial gap exists between the barrier and the chamber wall, enabling non-contact sliding motion. Upon release of the dispensing force, elastic recovery of the chamber wall reduces the internal volume; the radial gap permits the barrier to translate axially in response to the wall motion, compensating for volume change and preventing unintended continued dispensing. Alternatively, constrain the chamber wall from expanding or apply active compression to eliminate the volume increase that causes afterflow.
mechanism_raw: The backwall of the cartridge is dimensioned with a reduced diameter relative to the inner diameter of the tubular body, allowing it to slide in a substantially contact-less manner. When the trigger is released and the cartridge body radially retracts due to elastic recovery, the clearance between the backwall and tube wall allows the backwall to be pushed backward, counteracting the volume change and preventing afterflow. Alternatively, the cartridge body may be constrained from expanding or actively squeezed to eliminate the volume increase that causes afterflow.
residual_terms: ["radial gap", "flexible dispensing chamber", "elastic recovery", "internal volume", "non-contact sliding motion", "axial translation", "active compression"]

abstract: A postage tool has three sections: A top section contains water for moistening a stamp or envelope, a second section stores postage stamps, and a third section provides a writing instrument for addressing envelopes. The three sections fit together to form a handy tool for addressing envelopes and affixing postage.
reason: This patent describes a simple product integration combining three separate functions (water reservoir, stamp storage, writing instrument) into a single multi-section tool. The sections merely fit together mechanically; there is no causal mechanism or functional relationship that produces a useful effect beyond basic physical assembly.
