It is a product feature list, not an engineering mechanism.

abstract: The present invention provides a multilayer laminated acaricidal fabric comprising: PA1 a) a bottom layer of metallized textile comprising: PA2 (i) a textile including fibers selected from the group consisting of natural fibers, synthetic cellulosic fibers, regenerated protein fibers, acrylic fibers, polyolefin fibers, polyurethane fibers, vinyl fibers, and blends thereof, and PA2 (ii) a plating including an acaricidally effective amount of ionic copper, the metallized textile characterized in that the plating is directly bonded to said fibers; PA1 b) an intermediate air and vapor permeable thermoplastic membrane having pores of up to 10 angstrom; and PA1 c) an outer fabric layer, the thermoplastic membrane serving as a bonding layer effecting the lamination between the bottom and the outer fabric layers, as well as a barrier preventing the passage therethrough of allergens from mites killed by the acaricidal fabric.
problem: Controlling allergen passage from acaricidal fabric while maintaining air/vapor permeability and ensuring sustained biocidal effectiveness against mites.
constraint: Balancing pore size to permit air/vapor exchange while blocking allergens, and ensuring the copper plating remains bonded to fibers under mechanical stress during use.
mechanism: A biocidal layer is directly bonded to a fibrous substrate to create a durable, localized antimicrobial surface. A selective barrier layer with sub-nanometer-scale pores serves dual functions: enabling vapor permeability while blocking particulate contaminants. The barrier layer also acts as an adhesive medium to bond the biocidal layer to the substrate under mechanical stress.
mechanism_raw: Directly bonding an acaricidally effective ionic copper plating to textile fibers creates a durable, localized biocidal layer. A thermoplastic membrane with sub-10 angstrom pores serves as both a lamination bonding layer and a selective barrier, allowing vapor permeability while blocking allergen particles from killed mites.

abstract: A static memory cell is described which has cross coupled pulldown transistors and dual access transistors. The memory cell is fabricated such that balanced current paths are formed through the two pulldown transistors. A single word line is used to activate the access transistors which couple the memory cell to complementary bit lines. The memory cells, as viewed in a plan view, have the single word line and gates of the pulldown transistors fabricated in parallel.
problem: Maintaining stable operation in a static memory cell by balancing current paths through pulldown transistors to reduce noise and improve reliability.
constraint: Achieving geometric and electrical symmetry in the layout to balance current paths without increasing cell area or complexity.
mechanism: Symmetric current paths are established through complementary conductive elements arranged in a cross-coupled configuration. A shared activation line controls dual access elements to couple the storage node to opposing signal lines, ensuring balanced electrical behavior and minimizing asymmetry-induced instability.
mechanism_raw: Balanced current paths are formed through cross-coupled pulldown transistors by fabricating the single word line and pulldown transistor gates in parallel, ensuring symmetric electrical behavior. A single word line activates dual access transistors to couple the cell to complementary bit lines, minimizing asymmetry-induced instability.

abstract: A mixing apparatus suitable for mixing and conveying solid, particulate, polymeric materials, comprising a barrel that can be heated and cooled, at least two co-rotatable, self-wiping extruder screws located within the bore of the barrel, the screws being connected through a laterally flexible coupling to a drive means which can reverse the direction of rotation of the screws upon the occurrence of a predetermined event. The apparatus also comprises a closeable feed port and a closeable discharge port, both of which can be made gas-tight, the shafts of the screws being provided with seals capable of withstanding elevated gas pressures inside the barrel.
problem: Efficiently mixing and conveying solid particulate polymeric materials while handling elevated gas pressures and enabling directional reversal to prevent clogging or ensure thorough mixing.
constraint: Maintaining seal integrity under elevated pressures while enabling reversible rotation without mechanical failure or leakage.
mechanism: Rotatable mixing elements connected via a laterally compliant coupling enable reversible rotation upon detecting a predetermined condition (e.g., pressure buildup). The compliant coupling accommodates mechanical misalignment during direction reversal, while pressure-sealed interfaces maintain fluid integrity during operation.
mechanism_raw: Co-rotatable, self-wiping extruder screws connected via a laterally flexible coupling allow reversal of rotation direction upon a predetermined event (e.g., pressure buildup). The flexible coupling accommodates misalignment during reversal, while gas-tight seals on screw shafts maintain pressure integrity during operation.

abstract: An apparatus and method for controlling an underground boring machine during boring or reaming operations. A boring tool is displaced along an underground path while being rotated at a selected rate of rotation. In response to variations in underground conditions impacting boring tool progress along the underground path, a control system concurrently modifies the rate of boring tool displacement along the underground path while rotating the boring tool at the selected rotation rate. The controller monitors the rate at which liquid is pumped through the borehole and automatically adjusts the rate of displacement and/or the liquid flow rate so that sufficient liquid is flowing through the borehole to remove the cuttings and debris generated by the boring tool. Sensors are provided to sense pressure levels in the rotation, displacement, and liquid dispensing pumps and an electronic controller continuously monitors the levels detected by the sensors. When the controller detects a rise in rotation pump pressure above an unacceptable level, the controller disengages the boring tool by reducing the rate of boring tool displacement along the underground path, while maintaining rotation of the boring tool at a pre-selected rate. Such disengagement reduces the load on the rotation pump and allows the pressures to recover to an acceptable level. The controller re-engages the boring tool after detecting that the rotation pump pressure has fallen below a set level.
problem: Controlling an underground boring machine to maintain cuttings removal and prevent pump overload under varying underground conditions.
constraint: Dynamically balancing displacement rate and fluid flow to avoid pump overload while maintaining effective cuttings removal in unpredictable subsurface conditions.
mechanism: A feedback control loop continuously monitors a system parameter (e.g., pressure) and dynamically adjusts two operational variables: a mechanical displacement rate and a fluid flow rate. When the monitored parameter exceeds a threshold, displacement is reduced while a secondary operation continues, lowering system load. Once the parameter recovers, displacement resumes to maintain effective material removal.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control system continuously monitors rotation pump pressure and adjusts boring tool displacement rate and liquid flow rate. When pressure exceeds a threshold, displacement is reduced while rotation continues, lowering load on the pump. Once pressure recovers, displacement resumes, ensuring sufficient liquid flow to remove debris.
residual_terms: ["rotation pump pressure", "boring tool displacement rate", "liquid flow rate"]

abstract: A sure-seal rolling pin assembly of a lapping and polishing machine for substantially eliminating friction between the sure-seal rolling pin assembly and a work carrier and for substantially reducing particle contamination between the sure-seal rolling pin assembly and the work carrier. The lapping and polishing machine has a plurality of gears operatively connected to one another by the work carrier and each gear has a counterbore which has a surface. The sure-seal rolling pin comprises a pin, a plurality of ball bearing units and a torsionally stretchable seal. The pin has a longitudinal axis, a head portion and a body portion connected to the head portion and the head portion has a diameter and an outer surface. The body portion has a lower surface located adjacent the outer surface and is removably inserted into the counterbore of one of the gears. The plurality of ball bearing units are axially retained and concentrically connected to the body portion and are also connected to the surface of the counterbore so as to allow the pin to rotate about the longitudinal axis. The torsionally stretchable seal has a relaxed state and is capable of elastic restorability. The torsionally stretchable seal creates a seal between the pin and the surface of the counterbore while in the relaxed state. The torsionally stretchable seal has an upper face, an inner diameter, and an outer diameter concentrically located around the inner diameter and the inner diameter is connected to the lower surface of the body portion so as to allow the inner diameter to torsionally stretch when dragged by the rotation of the pin about the longitudinal axis. The inner diameter maintains fall contact with the lower surface of the body portion while the pin undergoes rotational movement about the longitudinal axis. The outer diameter is connected to the surface of the counterbore and maintains full stationary contact with the surface of the counterbore while the pin undergoes rotational movement about the longitudinal axis. The torsionally stretchable seal maintains a seal between the pin and the surface of the counterbore while the pin undergoes rotational movement about the longitudinal axis and maintains the seal while the pin returns to the relaxed state.
problem: Reducing friction and particle contamination between a rotating rolling pin and a work carrier in lapping/polishing machines while maintaining a dynamic seal.
constraint: Maintaining continuous sealing contact between the rotating pin and stationary carrier despite torsional stretching and rotational motion, without introducing particle contamination.
mechanism: A torsionally elastic sealing element with an inner attachment to a rotating component and an outer attachment to a stationary component maintains continuous contact during rotational motion. The seal's elastic recovery allows torsional deformation when dragged by rotation, preserving sealing integrity. Low-friction bearing elements axially retained on the rotating component reduce resistance between the rotating and stationary parts.
mechanism_raw: A torsionally stretchable seal with an inner diameter connected to the rotating pin and an outer diameter fixed to the work carrier maintains full contact during rotation. The seal's elastic restorability allows it to torsionally stretch when dragged by rotation, preserving sealing integrity while accommodating dynamic movement. Ball bearings axially retained on the pin reduce friction between the pin and carrier.

abstract: In a method of manufacturing mold inserts by galvanic metal deposition a substrate consisting of an electrically conductive material which cannot be structured lithographically is structured by mechanical precision machining to provide different levels on the substrate which is then covered by an electrically insulating material which can be structured lithographically and which is fine structured by depth lithography to form cavities therein which are then filled by galvanic deposition of a metal layer. The metal structure so formed is then separated from the substrate and the electrically non-conductive material to provide the mold insert with projections of different heights.
problem: Creating mold inserts with projections of different heights when the substrate material cannot be structured lithographically.
constraint: The substrate material must be mechanically machinable but not lithographically compatible, while the insulating layer must allow fine lithographic structuring and serve as a sacrificial template for metal deposition.
mechanism: Combining two distinct structuring methods—one for a mechanically machinable substrate and another for a lithographically compatible layer deposited on it—to create a hierarchical template structure, where the lithographically defined layer serves as a sacrificial mold for depositing material into its cavities, thereby transferring the layered geometry to the final product.
mechanism_raw: Combining mechanical precision machining of a non-lithographically structurable substrate with lithographic structuring of an insulating layer deposited on it, enabling galvanic metal deposition into cavities formed in the insulating layer to produce the final mold insert geometry.

abstract: A secure system for Authentication information. The system includes a scanner for reading the information contained in a document, a timing mechanism for entering the time the document was read, an encryptor for encrypting the read and timed information and a counter for counting the number of documents processed.
reason: The system is a straightforward combination of existing components (scanner, encryptor, counter) without a novel causal relationship or functional principle beyond standard authentication workflows.

abstract: A flexible sealing ring is arranged at an opening roller of an open-end spinning machine which rotates in a chamber of a housing connected to a vacuum source, which sealing ring is supported concentrically to the opening roller in the housing. In order to seal the chamber against the open atmosphere, the sealing ring comprises a sealing lip, to which a sealing surface of a collar of the opening roller is arranged. The sealing ring is disposed, under the action of the pressure drop present between the open atmosphere and the chamber, on a stopping surface which determines the operational position of the sealing ring, which stopping surface is itself arranged preferably at the housing, while, however, in some embodiments, it is arranged at the opening roller itself. The sealing lip defines the smallest diameter of the sealing ring, which is larger than the diameter of the combing structure of the opening roller.
problem: Maintaining a dynamic seal between a rotating component (opening roller) and a stationary housing in a vacuum environment without manual adjustment.
constraint: The sealing ring must be flexible enough to conform to the pressure-driven positioning while maintaining structural integrity, and the stopping surface must be positioned to allow self-adjustment without binding.
mechanism: Using a pressure differential between two environments to automatically position a flexible sealing element against a fixed reference surface, ensuring continuous contact between the sealing element and a moving component under operational conditions without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: Using the pressure differential between the vacuum chamber and ambient atmosphere to automatically position a flexible sealing ring against a stopping surface, ensuring the sealing lip maintains contact with the rotating collar under operational conditions.

abstract: The "hardness" of water flowing through a pipe, and attributable to ions dissolved in the water, is reduced by producing molecular agitation in the water to transform the ions into much larger crystals, followed by filtration using a conventional filter having a mesh size much larger than the size of the ions, but smaller than the size of the crystals.
problem: Removing dissolved ions from water (water hardness) using filtration, which is impractical due to the small size of dissolved ions relative to conventional filter mesh sizes.
constraint: The agitation must be sufficient to trigger crystallization without excessive energy input, and the filter mesh must balance crystal retention with flow rate.
mechanism: Inducing aggregation of dispersed particles through controlled energy input to form larger collectives, which are then separated from a fluid medium using a barrier with openings sized to retain the collectives while allowing the fluid and smaller particles to pass.
mechanism_raw: Applying molecular agitation to induce dissolved ions to aggregate into larger crystals, which can then be physically separated by filtration using a mesh size that is too large for the original ions but small enough for the crystals.

abstract: A method and apparatus are disclosed for determining the boundaries of guard intervals of data symbols being received in a coded orthogonal frequency division multiplexed signal. Temporal samples separated by an interval of an active interval of a data symbol are associated in pairs, and difference signals obtained. The dispersion of a first comparison block of difference signals is determined, and compared to the dispersion of a second comparison block of difference signals, the second comparison block being displaced from the first comparison block by n samples. An F ratio is calculated for the dispersions of the two blocks. F ratios are iterated in a succession of comparison blocks, and a signal representing the F ratios subjected to peak detection. The peaks represent the boundaries of the symbol's guard interval. This information is utilized in synchronizing an FFT window for subsequent signal reconstruction.
problem: Accurately determining the boundaries of guard intervals in OFDM signals to synchronize FFT windows for signal reconstruction.
constraint: The method must balance computational efficiency with sensitivity to dispersion changes, and the block displacement (n samples) must align with the expected guard interval length to avoid false peaks.
mechanism: Analyzing temporal correlations between paired signal segments to identify statistical anomalies in variance patterns, which indicate boundary transitions in structured data streams through iterative comparison of dispersion metrics across successive blocks.
mechanism_raw: Comparing the statistical dispersion of difference signals between temporally paired samples across successive blocks to detect peaks in F ratios, which correspond to guard interval boundaries through iterative analysis of signal variance patterns.

abstract: An apparatus, thermal storage system and method for heat exchange using a tube-type heat exchanger. A rod or rods are propelled to moves over the inner surface of the tube. The moving rod is in contact with a first process liquid which is adjacent the inner surface as a falling film or by flooding the interior of the tube. The flooded mode is particularly useful where the tube is non-vertical or the heat exchanger is used to make an ice slurry for HVAC systems serving high-rise buildings. Multiple such rod and tube assemblies are operated simultaneously using a drive plate powered to execute an orbital motion in a plane generally orthogonal to the rods. In one form the plate is coupled via a crank to equiangularly space spaced rods in each tube. This form of orbital drive allows the use of a device to develop an auxiliary radial force, such as spring mounts extending between a central, rotating shaft mounted in each tube and the rod or rods for that tube. This auxiliary radial force supplements the centrifugal force to produce a self-alignment of the rods in a tube-parallel orientation, even when they are driven by a single drive plate positioned at one end of the tubes. Without a spring loading, the rods are preferably mounted to be movable radially, for example suspended through holes in, and driven by, a plate to executes an orbital motion or at recesses in the rod in radially directed slots in an arm rotated by a tube-mounted crank. For freezer applications, a tubular jacket surrounds the tube to form an annular thermosyphon region for a boiling refrigerant. In a thermal storage system using such exchangers, a movable warm water return nozzle return nozzle melts a floating ice mass uniformly.
problem: Maintaining alignment of moving rods within non-vertical or complex-orientation heat exchanger tubes during orbital motion, especially when driven by a single drive plate.
constraint: Balancing centrifugal force and auxiliary radial force to achieve self-alignment without overcomplicating mechanical design or introducing excessive wear.
mechanism: A motion-transmitting element generates orbital movement that propels elongated components along a constrained path. A balancing force, applied through adjustable mounting or resilient elements, counteracts inertial effects to maintain alignment of the components relative to the path axis during motion, even when driven from a single side.
mechanism_raw: Orbital motion of a drive plate, coupled via a crank to rods, generates centrifugal force that propels rods along tube inner surfaces. An auxiliary radial force (e.g., spring mounts or radially movable rod mounting) supplements centrifugal force to self-align rods parallel to the tube axis, even with a single-sided drive.

abstract: A substantially transparent and preferably textured diffuser element disposed in surmounting relation to an array of light emitting diodes intended to illuminate a legend-bearing sign panel of an exit sign or similar illuminated sign, the invention allows compact sign enclosure formation and provides even illumination of sign panels on all legend-bearing face walls of the exit sign even though multiple point light sources such as light emitting diodes comprise the illumination source. The diffuser element of the invention is preferably embodied in a tent-shaped configuration with a plurality of apertures disposed along the apex of the diffuser element with one each of the apertures being disposed immediately above each light emitting diode. The preferred diffuser element of the invention is elongated in conformation and used with a linear array of light emitting diodes, the array being preferably located along at least one interior wall of the sign enclosure adjacent at least one of the legend-bearing face walls. The diffuser element is particularly useful with relatively non-diffuse, narrow-viewing angle light emitting diodes, the aperture in the diffuser element above each diode allowing substantial portions of the light emanating outwardly from free end portions of each diode to pass undiffused therethrough and into interior portions of the sign enclosure which are spaced from the LED array to illuminate portions of one or more sign panels spaced from the array. Light emanating from lower portions of the light emitting diodes at "flat" angles is diffused through the diffuser element into portions of the sign enclosure nearmost the LED array to illuminate portions of one or more sign panels adjacent the array.
problem: Achieving uniform illumination of sign panels using multiple point light sources (e.g., LEDs) with narrow viewing angles in compact enclosures.
constraint: Optimizing aperture placement and diffuser texture to balance direct and scattered light distribution without compromising compactness or transparency.
mechanism: A structured optical element with spatially separated transmission zones directs light from discrete sources. Upper source regions emit light through unobstructed pathways to distant targets, while lower source regions emit light through scattering zones to nearby targets. This spatial separation of direct and scattered light paths balances illumination distribution across a surface.
mechanism_raw: A textured, tent-shaped diffuser with apertures positioned above each LED allows direct light from upper diode portions to pass undiffused into distant panel regions, while diffusing light from lower diode portions at shallow angles to illuminate nearby panel areas. This spatial separation of diffused and undiffused light paths balances illumination uniformity.

abstract: The present invention comprises a method and apparatus for receiving data analysis instructions from a user and for displaying results of the data analysis to the user. In one embodiment, the invention provides a series of interface windows displayed on a computer display screen. A first window allows a user to select one or more specification files comprising reference data specifying capabilities and or resources with which other data is to be compared. A second window allows the user to select one or more data files to be compared to the one or more specification files selected using the first window. A third window allows the user to interactively select the type of analysis to be performed and provides the results of the selected analysis to the user. The third window also allows the user to interactively apply one or more filters to the results and to select the manner (view) in which the results are displayed.
problem: Enabling users to interactively select data files, apply analysis methods, and visualize results in a flexible, iterative workflow without rigid procedural steps.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between windows while allowing independent interaction to avoid overwhelming the user or creating conflicting states.
mechanism: A modular interface decouples input selection, processing configuration, and output presentation into independent interactive zones. Users iteratively adjust parameters across zones, with real-time feedback between selection, processing, and visualization to dynamically refine outcomes without rigid procedural dependencies.
mechanism_raw: A multi-window interface decouples data selection (window 1), analysis type selection (window 3), and result filtering/display (window 3). Users iteratively adjust parameters across windows, with real-time feedback loops between selection, analysis, and visualization to refine outcomes dynamically.

abstract: A heat exchanger assembly with a first header, a second header, a plurality of seamed or folded type heat exchanger tubes extending between the two headers, and a plurality of heat exchanger fins. Each of the plurality of fins has between 0.01% and 0.9% magnesium to improve the braze between the header and tube joint and the tube seam to inner surface joint. Additionally, the headers have a cladded inner surface with between about 0% to about 12.6% silicon to improve the braze at the tube-to-header joint.
problem: Improving brazed joint integrity between heat exchanger tubes, seams, and headers under thermal cycling and mechanical stress.
constraint: Balancing additive concentrations to maximize joint strength without inducing brittleness or compromising base material properties.
mechanism: Graded material compositions with varying additive concentrations are applied to different joint regions. A first composition enhances flow and adhesion at seam interfaces, while a second composition optimizes wetting and bonding at connection interfaces. The localized variation creates distinct alloy layers that strengthen critical junctions under stress.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating magnesium (0.01–0.9%) into fins enhances braze flow and adhesion at tube seams and inner surfaces, while silicon-clad header surfaces (0–12.6%) optimize wetting and metallurgical bonding at tube-to-header joints. The graded material compositions create localized alloy layers that strengthen critical joint interfaces.

abstract: A drinking tube support for a beverage dispenser includes a bendable wire formed into a loop at a lower portion and a spiral at an upper portion. The beverage dispenser includes a beverage container secured on the back of a user by shoulder straps, and a drinking tube extending from the container. The drinking tube is secured to one of the shoulder straps by a clip. The drinking tube support is attached to the beverage dispenser by positioning the loop under and around the clip. The free end of the drinking tube is inserted through the spiral. An intermediate portion of the drinking tube support is long enough to enable the wire to be adjusted to position the free end of the drinking tube near the mouth of the user, who can conveniently drink by simply turning the head slightly, without having to pick up the tube. In a second embodiment, the drinking tube support includes a wire with a lower end attached to a base member, and an upper end formed into a spiral. A pair of clasps attached to the base member are clamped around the drinking tube adjacent the clip on the strap. The upper end of the drinking tube is inserted through the spiral, and the intermediate portion of the wire is adjusted to position the free end of the drinking tube near the mouth of the user. In a third embodiment, a retaining strap is provided for attaching the drinking tube to a shoulder strap of a beverage dispenser without a drinking tube clip.
problem: Positioning a drinking tube near a user’s mouth in a hands-free manner during movement, without requiring manual adjustment or fixed mounting.
constraint: Ensuring the wire’s bendability and attachment method provide stable positioning without excessive friction or slippage during dynamic motion.
mechanism: A flexible elongated element with a looped and helical configuration allows a conduit to be anchored at a fixed point while its intermediate section is manually shaped to route the conduit's free end to a target location. The helical retention and inherent flexibility maintain position during dynamic movement without manual readjustment.
mechanism_raw: A bendable wire with a loop-and-spiral configuration allows the tube to be anchored at a fixed point (e.g., shoulder strap clip) while the wire’s intermediate section is manually adjusted to route the tube’s free end to the mouth. The spiral retains the tube in place, and the wire’s flexibility maintains position during head movement.

abstract: An aroma-spraying mechanism is provided in an air conditioner to suppress unpleasant odors generated in the air conditioner. The air conditioner includes an air inlet, and an inlet opening and closing mechanism disposed at the inlet. That mechanism includes a framework and inlet opening/closing vanes rotatably mounted on the framework. The aroma spraying mechanism includes a replaceable aroma container mounted on the framework. The container includes a depressible spray head. A driver mounted on the framework includes a plunger for depressing the spray head. A user can manipulate keys on a control panel to select the spray intervals and spray duration, whereby the plunger is automatically actuated during an air conditioning operation.
problem: Suppressing unpleasant odors generated in an air conditioner during operation.
constraint: Balancing spray timing and duration to avoid disrupting airflow or over-consuming aroma material while maintaining effective odor suppression.
mechanism: Automated timed actuation of a dispensing element to release aroma from a replaceable source, synchronized with airflow generation via user-defined intervals and duration, ensuring odor suppression without disrupting airflow or over-consuming aroma material.
mechanism_raw: Automated, timed actuation of a dispensing mechanism (plunger) to release aroma from a replaceable container, synchronized with air conditioning operation via user-defined intervals and duration.

abstract: A parallel-to-serial converter based on the principle of current evaluation that, in addition having signal paths, has a reference path with intentionally generated, poorer running time properties than all signal paths, and a conversion and a deactivation of a current source in an input hold element already occurring as soon as the reference path supplies a ready message. The advantages of this converter are particularly high signal processing speed and low dissipated power, but also low line crosstalk and small chip area. A further critical advantage is that the converter is adaptive in view of technology parameters, temperature and supply voltage, i.e. these quantities have nearly no influence on the functionability of the parallel-to-serial converter.
problem: Achieving high-speed, low-power parallel-to-serial conversion with minimal crosstalk and chip area in digital circuits.
constraint: Trade-off between signal path speed and reference path timing to ensure reliable conversion without sacrificing power efficiency or chip area.
mechanism: A reference path with intentionally degraded timing triggers conversion and deactivation of current sources in input hold elements, ensuring synchronization and adaptive performance across technology parameters while balancing signal path speed and reference path timing.
mechanism_raw: Using a reference path with intentionally degraded timing to trigger conversion and deactivation of current sources in input hold elements, ensuring synchronization and adaptive performance across technology parameters.

abstract: A method and powder mixture are described for cutting a refractory body. The powder mixture comprises refractory metal oxide particles and fuel particles which burn exothermically by combining with oxygen to form a refractory oxide. The mixture is characterised in that the refractory metal oxide of the powder mixture comprises calcium oxide and/or magnesium oxide. The powder mixture enables refractory bodies to be cut more effectively than hitherto.
problem: Effectively cutting refractory bodies using a powder mixture that generates localized heat for material removal.
constraint: Balancing the refractory oxide's thermal stability and the fuel's combustion rate to ensure efficient cutting without excessive heat dissipation.
mechanism: Exothermic combustion of fuel particles with oxygen forms refractory oxides, producing controlled thermal energy to cut through refractory materials by balancing thermal stability and combustion rate.
mechanism_raw: Exothermic combustion of fuel particles with oxygen to form refractory oxides (e.g., CaO/MgO), producing controlled thermal energy to cut through refractory materials.

abstract: A method of forming a field effect transistor includes, a) providing a silicon substrate having impurity doping of a first conductivity type; b) providing source and drain diffusion regions of a second conductivity type within the silicon substrate, the source region and the drain region being spaced from one another to define a channel region therebetween within the silicon substrate; c) providing a gate relative to the silicon substrate operatively adjacent the channel region; and d) providing respective ohmic electrical contacts to the source region and the drain region, the electrical contact to the source region comprising a substrate leaking junction, the electrical connection to the drain region not comprising a substrate leaking junction. A field effect transistor is also disclosed.
problem: Forming a field-effect transistor with optimized electrical contacts for source and drain regions.
constraint: Trade-off between contact resistance and leakage current to maintain transistor performance while minimizing parasitic effects.
mechanism: Asymmetric contact design uses a substrate-leaking junction for one contact and a non-leaking junction for the other to tailor electrical characteristics, balancing contact resistance and leakage current.
mechanism_raw: Asymmetric contact design: using a substrate-leaking junction for the source contact and a non-leaking junction for the drain contact to tailor electrical characteristics.

abstract: A process and apparatus for freeze drying of liquid material in a vessel in which the vessels are moved automatically through various stages including loading vessels onto racks, washing vessels in an inverted position, sterilizing vessels and racks, filling vessels with a liquid material, rotating the vessels and the liquid material contained within each vessel at a speed that allows the liquid to form a shell against the inner surface of the vessel, subjecting the vessels and the liquid material contained therein to freezing conditions sufficient to freeze the material into the form of a shell and then moving the rack and the vessels containing the frozen material through a vacuum drying chamber in which the frozen liquid material is dried.
problem: Efficiently freeze-drying liquid materials in vessels while maintaining material integrity and process automation.
constraint: Balancing processing speed and environmental control precision to prevent material degradation while ensuring throughput.
mechanism: Automated sequential movement of vessels through discrete processing stages (loading, washing, sterilizing, filling, rotating, freezing, vacuum drying) with controlled environmental conditions at each step, balancing processing speed and environmental control precision.
mechanism_raw: Automated sequential movement of vessels through discrete processing stages (loading, washing, sterilizing, filling, rotating, freezing, vacuum drying) with controlled environmental conditions at each step.

abstract: An electrical conductor consisting of an at least partially aluminium-based central core coated by continuous electrodeposition with at least one metal layer, including pretreatment of the surface of the core, characterized in that the following are subsequently performed successively on the core, PA1 a) an electrochemical deposition of copper in an aqueous bath maintained at a temperature of between 20.degree. C. and 60.degree.C., containing KCN, CuCN, K.sub.2 CO.sub.3 and KNaC.sub.4 H.sub.4 O.sub.6 with a current intensity of between 1 and 10 A/dm.sup.2 ; PA1 b) rinsing at ambient temperature; PA1 c) an electrochemical deposition of tin in an aqueous bath maintained at a temperature of between 20.degree. C. and 60.degree. C., containing essentially tin dissolved in methanesulphonic acid and, optionally, additives, with a current intensity of between 1 and 100 A/dm.sup.2 ; PA1 d) rinsing with water at 60.degree.C.
problem: Creating a durable, conductive coating on an aluminum-based core that maintains adhesion and electrical performance across multiple metal layers.
constraint: The precise chemical compositions of the baths (e.g., KCN, CuCN, methanesulphonic acid) and temperature/current ranges must be maintained to avoid defects or delamination between layers.
mechanism: Sequentially depositing multiple conductive layers onto a substrate using controlled electrochemical processes, where each layer's deposition parameters are adjusted to ensure interlayer adhesion and electrical continuity. Intermediate cleaning steps remove contaminants between layers, and the chemical environment of each deposition stage is tailored to match the properties of the preceding and subsequent layers.
mechanism_raw: Sequential electrochemical deposition of distinct metal layers (copper then tin) using specific aqueous baths and controlled current intensities, followed by intermediate rinsing steps. Each layer's chemical composition and deposition conditions are tailored to ensure proper adhesion and conductivity while preventing degradation between layers.

abstract: A zoom lens system composed, in order from the object side, of a first lens unit which has a positive refractive power and is kept stationary during a change of a magnification, a second lens unit which has a negative refractive power and is movable for the change of the magnification, a third lens unit which has a positive refractive power and is kept stationary during the change of the magnification, a fourth lens unit which has a positive refractive power and is movable during the change of the magnification, and a fifth lens unit which has a negative refractive power and is kept stationary during the change of the magnification; and using an aspherical surface or aspherical surfaces in the lens units which are kept stationary during the change of the magnification.
problem: Maintaining image quality and correcting optical aberrations during magnification changes in a zoom lens system.
constraint: The trade-off between minimizing movement in stationary units (to reduce aberrations) and ensuring sufficient mobility in other units to achieve the desired zoom range.
mechanism: Arranging optical elements with opposing refractive characteristics such that some elements remain fixed to stabilize the optical path while others move to adjust magnification. Fixed elements incorporate non-spherical surfaces to correct optical distortions, reducing the need for complex adjustments in the moving elements and maintaining image quality across zoom ranges.
mechanism_raw: Arranging lens units with alternating positive and negative refractive powers, where movable units adjust magnification while stationary units (incorporating aspherical surfaces) correct aberrations. The fixed units stabilize the optical path, reducing the need for complex adjustments in moving components.

abstract: A ferromagnetic material can be formed in a very small size on the order of an atomic size and is capable of being stably magnetized. The ferromagnetic material comprises basic unit structures each consisting of a first atom (11), a second atom (12) of the same kind as the first atom (11), and a third atom (or atomic group) (13) of the same kind as the first atom (11) or of a kind different from that of the first atom (11). In each of the basic unit structures, the atoms are arranged on a surface of a substrate so that a chemical bond (14) is formed between the first atom or and the third atom or molecule, a chemical bond (14) is formed between the second atom and the third atom or molecule, a chemical bond or an electron path (15) not passing the third atom is formed between the first and the second atom.
problem: Forming a ferromagnetic material at atomic-scale dimensions that remains stably magnetized without external fields.
constraint: The atomic-scale geometry must precisely balance bond formation and electron path connectivity to prevent magnetic instability or loss of coherence.
mechanism: Arranging magnetic atoms into specific spatial configurations where interatomic bonding and electron pathways create localized regions of magnetic stability. The geometric arrangement ensures that magnetic moments remain aligned without external influence, even at atomic-scale dimensions, by balancing electronic interactions and structural constraints.
mechanism_raw: Structuring atoms into basic unit configurations where chemical bonds and electron paths between atoms (e.g., first and second atoms connected via a third atom or direct electron path) create localized magnetic stability. The arrangement ensures that magnetization persists even at extremely small sizes.

abstract: A pair of combined cutting and thinning shears is comprised of a pair of handles, a pair of cutting blades attached to respective front ends of the handles, and a pair of thinning blades attached to respective rear ends of the handles. The cutting blades are pivoted together at a position adjacent the handles. A guide tab on one of the thinning blades mate with the opposite thinning blade to ensure their proper alignment when closed. In a second embodiment, the handles include inside edges that are in constant engagement with each other throughout their entire range of movement to ensure alignment between the thinning blades. Both embodiments can be used to cut or thin hair by simply positioning hair between either the cutting blades or thinning blades.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment between cutting and thinning blades in combined shears during operation.
constraint: The guide and engagement mechanisms must function across the full range of motion without introducing friction or wear that compromises alignment.
mechanism: Mechanically coupling two cutting elements through complementary guide features that maintain relative positioning throughout their range of motion. One element incorporates protruding guides that interface with corresponding features on the opposing element, while handle mechanisms ensure continuous contact and alignment during operation, preventing lateral displacement.
mechanism_raw: Integrating guide tabs on one blade that mate with the opposing blade, and designing handle edges to maintain constant engagement throughout movement. These features mechanically constrain blade positions relative to each other, preventing misalignment during cutting or thinning.

abstract: Apparatus for forming a high shear strength clay liner comprising two synthetic geotextiles surrounding a semihydrated layer of swellable clay. The apparatus includes two parallel needle bars each carrying a row of needles reciprocating in opposed directions and cooperating with a reciprocating needle plate having a plurality of parallel fingers and a looper bar with a plurality of parallel looper plates rocking on an axis to form loops which can be melted to form protruding knots.
problem: Forming a high shear strength clay liner by mechanically bonding layers of geotextiles and swellable clay.
constraint: The coordination between needle reciprocation, finger movement, and looper rocking must be synchronized to ensure uniform knot formation without damaging the clay layer.
mechanism: Mechanically interlocking layered materials through a synchronized piercing and knotting process, where a reciprocating element penetrates through the layers while a complementary element forms loops that are secured to create mechanical anchors. The coordinated movement of piercing, looping, and securing elements ensures uniform attachment without compromising the integrity of sensitive intermediate layers.
mechanism_raw: Using reciprocating needle bars and a needle plate with parallel fingers to pierce through layers, while a looper bar creates loops that are melted to form protruding knots. This mechanical stitching interlocks the geotextiles and clay, enhancing structural integrity.

abstract: An energy storage device particularly suitable for use in hybrid fluid power systems and fluid systems utilizing accumulators. A piston accumulator has a primary face on one end of the piston and a series of secondary faces on the opposite end of the piston. Each face has an associated chamber, and one or more of the chambers of the secondary faces may be selectively connected to a system pressure line. Since the pressure of the system pressure line depends on (and varies with) the number of chambers connected thereto, the potential energy of the chamber of the primary face may be delivered to the system pressure line at a variety of output pressures. Similarly, the chamber of the primary face may be recharged with energy at a variety of input pressures.
problem: Delivering energy from a storage device at variable output pressures to match system requirements.
constraint: Balancing the number of secondary chambers connected to the system pressure line to achieve desired pressure levels without overcomplicating the control system.
mechanism: A pressure-regulating system uses a primary chamber and multiple secondary chambers, where selectively coupling secondary chambers to a system pressure line adjusts the output pressure. This enables variable energy delivery by leveraging pressure-dependent coupling between chambers.
mechanism_raw: A piston accumulator with a primary face chamber and multiple secondary face chambers, where selectively connecting secondary chambers to a system pressure line adjusts the system pressure. This allows the primary chamber to deliver energy at varying pressures by leveraging the pressure-dependent coupling between chambers.

abstract: The friction winding shaft is used to wind up materials in strip form onto coil cores (16). It comprises a core shaft (20) annularly surrounded by friction elements (12), as well as radially acting tension elements (24), which in the operating position bring about a frictional engagement between the coupling elements (28) slaved by the core shaft (20) and the friction elements (12), by means of which engagement torque can be transmitted with slip from the core shaft (20) to the friction elements (12). The friction elements (12) are movable outward in order in operation to establish a rotationally fixed connection between the friction elements (12) and the coil core (16). With the goal of assuring slip-free slaving of the coil core at a certain torque, it is proposed that the tension elements (24), by means of the radial forces they impose, move the friction elements (12) radially outward via the coupling elements (28) and put them in contact with the coil core. Under the radial forces of the tension elements (24) effective in the operating position, the torque transmitted by the frictional pairing of the coupling element and friction element is intended to be lower than the torque that can be transmitted by the pairing of friction element and coil core, so that a rotationally fixed slaving occurs between the friction element (12) and the coil core (16).
problem: Ensuring slip-free rotational slaving of a coil core at a specific torque during material winding.
constraint: Maintaining a precise torque differential between the two frictional pairings to prevent slippage while allowing controlled slip during torque transmission.
mechanism: Force transmission elements apply radial forces to bias friction elements into engagement with a driven component. A torque differential is maintained between the force transmission and friction interface, ensuring the driven component rotates without slippage while allowing controlled slip during torque transfer.
mechanism_raw: Radial tension elements apply forces to move friction elements outward via coupling elements, creating a frictional engagement with the coil core. The torque transmitted between the coupling element and friction element is intentionally lower than between the friction element and coil core, ensuring the coil core is driven without slippage.

abstract: Improved centrifugal decanters with a screw conveyor for the continuous separation of solids-liquid mixtures are disclosed wherein the conveyor is provided with a feed arrangement for reducing the magnitude of mechanical vibrations of the centrifuge comprising a coaxially mounted feed distributor, generally trunco-conical in form, adapted to distribute into the conveyor, a solids-liquid feed stream falling into the distributor from a short stationary feed tube. The invention includes processes which use such improved centrifuge apparatus for continuous separation of solids-liquid mixtures into separate components by centrifugal action.
problem: Reducing mechanical vibrations in centrifugal decanters caused by uneven feed distribution into the screw conveyor.
constraint: Designing the distributor geometry and alignment to ensure uniform feed distribution without introducing additional dynamic forces.
mechanism: A coaxially mounted distributor with a controlled geometry receives a feed stream and distributes it uniformly into a rotating component. This uniform distribution minimizes vibration-inducing imbalances caused by uneven loading during operation.
mechanism_raw: A coaxially mounted, trunco-conical feed distributor receives a solids-liquid feed stream from a stationary tube and distributes it evenly into the rotating screw conveyor. This controlled distribution minimizes vibration-inducing imbalances during operation.

abstract: A cooling jacket and dispenser system for a container of liquid beverage comprises a flexible sheet of thermally insulating material designed to circumferentially fit around the container to be cooled thereby. The sheet has a cooling line coil disposed in serpentine fashion upon an interior facing surface thereof for direct or indirect contact with the external side periphery of the container to be cooled thereby. The cooling line coil is operatively connected to a cooling bath fluid supplied by and recirculated to a liquid dispenser assembly.
problem: Efficiently cooling a liquid beverage container while maintaining flexibility for varying container sizes.
constraint: Balancing flexibility of the sheet with the need for consistent thermal contact between the coil and container surface across different container geometries.
mechanism: A flexible thermal interface with a serpentine flow path conforms to a target surface. The serpentine path maximizes thermal contact area, enabling efficient heat transfer through a recirculated coolant medium.
mechanism_raw: A flexible insulating sheet with a serpentine cooling coil on its interior surface conforms to the container's periphery. The coil's serpentine path maximizes thermal contact area, enabling direct or indirect cooling through recirculated coolant.

abstract: A flare stack with increased control of flow velocity of gases. The flare stack includes a pipe having a flare tip. The flare tip is provided with orifices and a sliding sleeve that opens and closes at least some of the orifices under control of an actuator. The actuator is pressure controlled. Nozzles extend from the orifices, parallel to each other. A central nozzle produces a stabilized flame. The nozzles which are controlled by the sliding sleeve are arranged in rings axially offset from each other along the pipe, so that the sleeve may open or close the nozzles in a ring as desired. The nozzles are symmetrically disposed, and terminate at the same plane, with the nozzles being disposed sufficiently close to each other that gas exiting any nozzle tends to draw in and merge with gas exiting from any adjacent nozzle.
problem: Controlling gas flow velocity and flame stability in a flare stack while enabling variable flow regulation.
constraint: Maintaining nozzle proximity and symmetry to ensure gas stream merging while allowing independent control of nozzle rings for variable flow adjustment.
mechanism: A variable-flow control system uses a sliding element to selectively open orifices arranged in axially offset rings. Symmetrically positioned outlets ensure exiting streams merge, stabilizing a flame front and regulating flow velocity through pressure-actuated adjustment.
mechanism_raw: A sliding sleeve selectively opens/closes orifices arranged in axially offset rings, with nozzles positioned symmetrically and closely enough that exiting gas streams merge. This merging stabilizes the flame and controls flow velocity through pressure-regulated actuation.

abstract: A method of preparing raw oyster meat in the shell is disclosed which employs a mild heat treatment followed by chilling for the destruction of harmful pathogenic bacteria such as Vibrio vulnificus. The oysters are captured and transported to the processing plant in a refrigerated state. The oysters are then cleaned and graded into categories according the product size. The oysters are then placed into a continuous flow of sterilized water at a sufficient temperature and duration to kill the pathogens yet leave the meat in a raw state within the shell. Different temperatures and time durations have been found to give excellent results depending on the size of the oyster. It has been found that the internal temperature of the oysters, that is, the meat within the shell, must reach a minimum of 49 degrees centigrade and not exceed 53 degrees centigrade for maximum efficacy. Depending on oyster weight and warm water temperature, the oysters will be immersed from between about 10-45 minutes. The oysters are then removed from the heated water flow and are placed in a sterilized cold water bath or air convection cooler. At this point the treated oysters are ready for shucking using standard mechanical methods. The oysters remain in a raw state and in the shell throughout the process, prior to shucking. The shucking provides a treated, raw oyster meat free from harmful bacteria. The treated, raw oyster meat may be packed and stored by conventional structure. The pathogenic bacteria are reduced to an undetectable level in the oyster meat by this process. This process may be employed with any shellfish.
problem: Pathogenic bacteria (e.g., Vibrio vulnificus) in raw oyster meat must be eliminated while preserving the meat in a raw, uncooked state within the shell.
constraint: Temperature must be high enough to kill pathogens but low enough to avoid cooking the meat (49-53°C); immersion duration must be adjusted based on oyster size/weight (10-45 minutes).
mechanism: Apply controlled thermal energy within a narrow temperature range that exceeds the pathogen lethality threshold but remains below the protein denaturation threshold of the target material, for a duration scaled to the thermal mass of the load, followed by rapid cooling to terminate the thermal exposure. The temperature-time profile selectively achieves microbial inactivation while preserving the raw state of the material.
mechanism_raw: Controlled heat treatment within a narrow internal temperature range (49-53°C) for a size-adjusted duration kills pathogens without denaturing the meat proteins, followed by rapid chilling to arrest the thermal process. The precise temperature-time window selectively targets microbial lethality while preserving the raw state.
residual_terms: ["pathogen lethality threshold", "protein denaturation threshold", "thermal mass", "microbial inactivation"]

abstract: Secondary explosive materials, particularly nitramines, are recovered from an explosive composition containing a mixture of 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT) and at least one secondary explosive by the steps of heating the explosive composition to melt the TNT, preferably using steam, separately collecting and recovering the melted TNT, treating the thus-separated secondary explosive with a material which is a solvent for TNT and a non-solvent for the secondary explosive to dissolve the TNT, removing the non-solvent from the secondary explosive, and recovering the secondary explosive.
problem: Separating secondary explosive materials from a mixture containing TNT and at least one secondary explosive, where both components have similar hazardous properties.
constraint: The solvent must be selectively soluble for TNT but non-solvent for the secondary explosive; the heating method (steam) must melt TNT without decomposing the secondary explosive.
mechanism: Perform sequential separation of components in a mixture by exploiting two distinct differential physical properties: first, apply energy to induce a phase change in one component based on a melting point difference, enabling physical collection of the phase-changed component; second, apply a selective solvent that dissolves one component but not the other, further purifying the separated material. Each step removes a component based on a different physical property.
mechanism_raw: Sequential selective separation exploiting two differential physical properties: (1) melting point difference — heating with steam melts TNT while the secondary explosive remains solid, allowing physical collection of molten TNT; (2) solubility difference — a solvent that dissolves TNT but not the secondary explosive further purifies the separated explosive. Each step removes one component based on a distinct physical property.
residual_terms: ["melting point difference", "phase change", "selective solvent", "differential physical properties"]

abstract: A crotch cushion (20) for bicycle riders includes a right buttock seat (22) having a first upwardly facing concave surface (24), and a laterally opposite left buttock seat (26) having a second upwardly facing concave surface (28). An upwardly facing trough (30) is connected between right buttock seat (22) and left buttock seat (26). In a preferred embodiment, padding (40) covers crotch cushion (20). First (24) and second (28) upwardly facing concave surfaces are contoured to accept the lower right and left medial buttocks respectively of a human, and thereby transfer the rider's weight away from the central crotch and onto the buttocks. Trough (30) provides stress relief for the perineal region of a human.
problem: Pressure on the sensitive perineal region of bicycle riders causes discomfort and potential injury during riding.
constraint: The contour geometry must balance sufficient weight transfer off the perineum with adequate overall support and stability for the rider.
mechanism: Use geometric contouring with two concave support regions to transfer load from a sensitive central area onto more robust adjacent structures, while providing a stress-relief void between the support regions for the sensitive area. The shape actively redirects applied force away from vulnerable tissue.
mechanism_raw: Geometric contouring with two concave buttock seats transfers the rider's weight from the central crotch/perineal area onto the more robust medial buttocks, while an upward-facing trough between the seats provides a stress-relief void for the perineal region. The shape actively redirects load away from sensitive tissue.

abstract: A set of footwear blocks having a set of footwear blocks has indicia, such as animal tracks or characters thereon, wherein the tracks can be interchanged between different images. The blocks also have rigid handles to support the arms of the child while walking. In a preferred embodiment the height of the rigid handles can be varied so that they can be raised so the child can walk erect while using the blocks underneath the child's shoes, or the height of the handles can be lowered so that the child, while kneeling, can use the blocks as hand-held printing imagines, for imprinting images in soft surface, such as soft ground or sand.
problem: A single device must serve two distinct functions for children: as a walking aid and as a hand-held printing/imprinting tool.
constraint: The handle height must be adjustable across a range sufficient to accommodate both the walking stance and the kneeling/hand-held printing posture.
mechanism: Provide adjustable geometry that reconfigures the device's operational mode by changing the relative position of its functional elements: in one configuration, the elements are positioned to interface with the user's support surface for upright mobility assistance; in another configuration, the elements are repositioned as hand-held implements for creating impressions in deformable media. The same base unit serves two distinct functions based on geometric reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable handle height reconfigures the device's geometry to switch between two operational modes: raised handles position the blocks under the child's feet for upright walking support, while lowered handles reposition the blocks as hand-held implements for imprinting images in soft surfaces. The same base unit functions as either a walking aid or a printing tool based on geometric reconfiguration.

abstract: Disclosed is a color ink set for ink-jet recording, which color ink set comprises a set of single-color ink, namely, cyan ink, magenta ink, yellow ink and black ink, each single-color ink containing at least a colorant, a water-soluble organic solvent and water, wherein the colorant in the single-color ink has a specific chemical structure, and which color ink set for ink-jet recording fulfills the characteristics required for ink-jet recording ink, along with the details of single-color ink constituting the ink set and an ink-jet recording method using the color ink set.
reason: The patent describes a color ink set with colorants having specific chemical structures, but this is a materials specification rather than a problem-solving mechanism. There is no novel causal operation described — it is standard formulation chemistry of selecting compatible colorants, solvents, and water to meet ink-jet performance requirements.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for recovering a crystallizable organic compound from solutions containing said compound. In accordance with the method, the compound is crystallized substantially by way of nucleation from a solution having high viscosity and high supersaturation in respect of the compound to be recovered, and the formed crystals are recovered.
problem: Efficiently recovering crystallizable organic compounds from solutions while minimizing energy or time costs.
constraint: Balancing viscosity and supersaturation levels to avoid uncontrolled crystallization or excessive energy input.
mechanism: Creating a controlled environment with elevated resistance to flow and solute concentration gradients to trigger rapid phase separation, enabling accelerated recovery of target compounds through induced nucleation dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Inducing rapid nucleation by creating a solution environment with high viscosity and high supersaturation, which accelerates crystal formation and allows recovery of the compound.

abstract: An insulated lattice is prepared with a plurality of lattice oriented atoms to create a substantially planar surface having a lattice arrangement. Any unsatisfied chemical bonds are terminated along the substantially planar surface by placing atoms at the site of the unsatisfied chemical bonds to terminate the unsatisfied chemical bonds and insulate the surface to form an insulated lattice platform. Atoms are placed at predetermined locations on the insulated lattice platform to form a first atomic chain which behaves as one of a conductor, a semiconductor and an insulator. A second chain of atoms is also placed at predetermined locations on the insulated lattice platform so that the second chain behaves as another of a conductor, a semiconductor and an insulator. These placements are made such that the second chain of atoms is electrically coupled to the first chain of atoms, and the second chain of atoms behaves differently than the first chain of atoms. That is, in the first chain the atoms are placed at a first separation distance and in the second chain the atoms are placed at a second separation distance, where the second separation distance is different than the first.
problem: Creating a platform where adjacent atomic chains exhibit distinct electrical properties (conductor, semiconductor, insulator) for nanoscale device integration.
constraint: Precise atomic placement to ensure desired electronic characteristics without disrupting structural integrity.
mechanism: Spatially organizing discrete elements at defined intervals on a supporting framework to create localized variations in charge carrier mobility, enabling selective coupling between regions with differing conductive characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Spatially arranging atoms at predetermined separation distances on an insulated lattice to modulate electronic behavior, enabling controlled coupling between chains with differing properties.

abstract: An apparatus for shredding cheese is disclosed which is capable of producing relatively precise square cross-section cheese shreds of a desired length. The apparatus is capable of simultaneously shredding multiple cheese blocks for high capacity cheese shredding. The length of the cheese shreds can be altered as desired, as well as the width and height to produce cheese shreds having a rectangular cross-section. A containment center is used to feed the blocks of cheese toward the cheese shredding apparatus. A series of horizontally mounted sectioning knives are at a front end of the containment center to section the cheese block into predefined lengths, thereby defining the length of each cheese shred. The cheese shredder includes multiple slicing and peeling assemblies mounted over a series of openings in a rotatable disk. Each slicing and peeling assembly includes a number of rakers having outwardly projecting slicing blades to vertically score a sectioned block of cheese. The slicing and peeling assemblies also includes a peeling knife arranged transversely to the slicing blades to peel the sectioned and scored cheese block. The individual cheese shreds are then fed through openings in the rotatable disk and fall into a discharge chute below.
problem: Producing uniform, precisely shaped food shreds (e.g., square cross-section) at high throughput while allowing adjustable dimensions.
constraint: Maintaining dimensional precision across multiple cutting stages while handling variable input block sizes.
mechanism: Implementing sequential material removal through aligned cutting elements arranged on a rotating platform, where each stage progressively defines geometric features while maintaining dimensional consistency across variable input sizes.
mechanism_raw: Combining sequential sectioning (to define length) with multi-stage slicing and peeling (to define cross-section) using aligned blade arrays on a rotating disk, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple blocks.

abstract: A network service system capable of providing economical services comprises a plurality of host computers connected to a network for providing services through the network and an information processing terminal connected to the network. The information processing terminal identifies a service identifier, provided in a storage medium for network service, for identifying a type of a network service when the storage medium is attached, connects the line to the host computer which corresponds to the identified service identifier and receives the network service from the line-connected host computer.
problem: Providing economical network services by dynamically routing user requests to the most appropriate host without manual configuration.
constraint: Ensuring accurate mapping between service identifiers and host capabilities to avoid misrouting or service degradation.
mechanism: Automatically correlating a resource identifier with predefined capability mappings to dynamically establish connections between requesting entities and specialized processing units optimized for specific service categories.
mechanism_raw: Automatically identifying a service type from a storage medium's identifier, then establishing a connection to a pre-mapped host computer that specializes in that service.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method for obtaining transgenic plants showing a modified fructan pattern as compared to non-transformed plants, comprising the steps of: a) preparing a DNA construct comprising one or more fructosyltransferase genes, or modified versions thereof, being operably linked to a promoter sequence active in plants and a terminator sequence active in plants; b) transforming a plant cell with the construct; and c) regenerating a transgenic plant from the transformed plant cell. Preferably, the 5' untranslated region of the fructosyltransferase gene is modified such that the expression of the fructosyltransferase is not negatively affected. The DNA construct may also comprise a targeting sequence upstream from the fructosyltransferase gene for directing the fructosyltransferase to a specific plant tissue or plant cell compartment. The fructosyltransferases produced in the transgenic plants change the fructan pattern of the plants, thus leading to different plant performance due to altered sink-source relations and yield, increased tolerance for drought, cold or other stresses, higher dry matter content, better taste and storability, and improved nutritional value. The plants are also suitable for use as raw material for fructan production.
problem: Modifying plant metabolic pathways to improve traits like stress tolerance, yield, or nutritional value through targeted genetic engineering.
constraint: Maintaining gene expression efficiency while avoiding unintended effects on plant growth or metabolic balance.
mechanism: Introducing a genetic regulatory system with compartment-specific expression control elements to direct enzymatic activity toward targeted metabolic pathways, enabling modification of biosynthetic output without disrupting core physiological processes.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a DNA construct with a fructosyltransferase gene linked to plant-active promoters/terminators and optional targeting sequences, enabling compartment-specific enzyme expression to alter fructan synthesis.

abstract: There is provided a ventilation assembly unit for a feline litter box. The unit comprises a housing containing a fan at the base thereof. A filtering medium is contained in a canister adapted for removal and insertion within the housing. The filtering medium comprises, in combination, an air dispersing mesh covered with a layer of particulate carbon.
problem: Odor and particulate control in enclosed ventilation systems while maintaining airflow efficiency.
constraint: Balancing airflow rate with filtration effectiveness to avoid restricting ventilation performance while maximizing odor and particulate removal.
mechanism: Distribute incoming flow across a cross-section using a permeable spreading element, then pass the distributed flow through a layered medium combining particulate capture and chemical adsorption, with replaceable filter modules that can be swapped independently of the main system.
mechanism_raw: Layered filtration using an air-dispersing mesh to distribute airflow evenly, combined with a particulate carbon layer to adsorb odors and contaminants. The removable canister design allows targeted replacement of the filtering medium without disrupting the entire system.
residual_terms: ["permeable spreading element", "particulate capture", "chemical adsorption", "replaceable filter modules"]

abstract: A cleaning equipment includes a brush head having a body portion formed with a dovetail groove at an opposite side thereof and a plurality of holes close to one side of the dovetail groove, an adapter having a tubular member formed with an axial outlet which is connected with a sectorial member, and a tubular handle provided with a valve assembly and a container engaged with the valve assembly, whereby the cleaning equipment can automatically dispense a mixture of water and liquid detergent as desired.
problem: Automatically dispensing a controlled mixture of water and liquid detergent during cleaning operations without manual adjustment.
constraint: Maintaining precise mixing ratios across varying pressure and flow conditions to ensure consistent cleaning performance without over- or under-dosing detergent.
mechanism: Use a fluidic control element connected to two supply sources, where the control element adjusts the relative flow rates of the two fluids based on a demand signal, producing a mixed output stream with a controlled composition delivered on-demand.
mechanism_raw: Integrated valve assembly connected to a detergent container and water supply, where the valve regulates the flow ratio of detergent to water based on user input or system demand, enabling on-demand mixing during cleaning.
residual_terms: ["fluidic control element", "demand signal", "mixed output stream", "controlled composition"]

abstract: A reversing rolling mill for rolling metal strip includes an entry side coiler and an exit side coiler and at least one mill rolling stand including a central roll, an entry side outer roll and an exit side outer roll having their respective longitudinal axes disposed in a first, horizontal, plane and parallel to a longitudinal axis of the central roll, a top outer roll in contact with the central roll, and a bottom outer roll, longitudinal axes of the top outer roll and bottom outer roll being disposed in a second, vertical, plane passing through the longitudinal axis of the central roll and parallel thereto, motors to drive the rolls and rotate the rolls about their respective longitudinal axes, devices to vertically move the central roll and the top outer roll, and devices to move the side outer rolls horizontally and to move the bottom outer roll vertically into and out of rolling contact with the central roll in a lowered position of the central roll.
problem: Controlling metal strip deformation and thickness during rolling in a reversible rolling mill configuration.
constraint: Achieving precise thickness control and material consistency while managing mechanical complexity and energy consumption across bidirectional rolling operations.
mechanism: Coordinate actuation of multiple contact elements arranged in orthogonal planes, with independent force and position control on each element to dynamically adjust contact pressure and material path geometry during bidirectional processing.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated movement of multiple rolls (central, entry/exit outer rolls, top/bottom outer rolls) in orthogonal planes, with independent vertical and horizontal actuation to dynamically adjust roll contact forces and strip path geometry during rolling.
residual_terms: ["contact elements", "orthogonal planes", "contact pressure", "material path geometry", "bidirectional processing"]

abstract: A fuel vapor vent valve for a motor vehicle is connected to an upper wall of a fuel tank in vertically depending relationship. The valve has a cover with a vapor exit passage connected to a fuel vapor storage canister and a body depending from the cover. One embodiment has a vapor exit port that communicates with the fuel tank interior adjacent the upper wall of the fuel tank. A vent tube has one end connected to the vapor exit passage and an opposite end that communicates with the vent exit port and defines a valve seat. The vapor exit port is located with respect to the valve seat so as to separate liquid fuel particles from vapor flow during fuel fill. The valve seat is closed by a valve element attached to a float when the fuel tank is full. Several further embodiments of the valve have the body connected to the cover to accommodate side impacts to the fuel tank.
problem: Separating liquid fuel from vapor during fuel tank filling and preventing vapor loss while accommodating structural impacts.
constraint: Ensuring reliable phase separation and valve closure under dynamic conditions (e.g., vehicle motion, side impacts) without compromising vapor sealing or fuel flow.
mechanism: Use a buoyant sensing element coupled to a sealing element positioned against a valve seat to close vapor pathways when liquid reaches a threshold level, combined with a flow-path geometry that separates entrained liquid from vapor during filling.
mechanism_raw: Float-actuated valve element positioned relative to a valve seat to block vapor exit ports when liquid fuel reaches a threshold level, combined with a vent tube geometry that separates liquid particles from vapor flow during filling.
residual_terms: ["buoyant sensing element", "sealing element", "valve seat", "vapor pathways", "threshold level", "entrained liquid", "flow-path geometry"]

abstract: A combustion chamber of a burner for a vehicle heater or for thermal regeneration of an exhaust gas particle filter having a frontal boundary wall, a circumferential boundary wall, a connector for fitting a glow plug and a connector for conveying combustion air which projects from the frontal boundary wall into the combustion chamber and has at least combustion air outlets through the connector wall, in which the combustion chamber with the frontal boundary wall, the circumferential boundary wall, the glow plug connector and with or without the air supply connector takes the form of a one-piece precision-cast component.
problem: Manufacturing a durable, precision-aligned combustion chamber with integrated functional features (e.g., air outlets, glow plug connectors) while minimizing assembly complexity.
