constraint: Achieving tight dimensional tolerances and material integrity in a high-temperature, high-stress environment while reducing manufacturing steps and part count.
mechanism: Form the functional structure as a single integrated unit using precision casting, embedding multiple features (boundary wall, circumferential wall, supply connector) into one component to eliminate joints, reduce alignment errors, and minimize thermal stress concentration points.
mechanism_raw: One-piece precision casting of the combustion chamber, integrating the frontal boundary wall, circumferential wall, and air supply connector into a single component to eliminate joint misalignment and reduce thermal stress points.
residual_terms: ["precision casting", "integrated unit", "boundary wall", "circumferential wall", "supply connector", "thermal stress concentration points"]

abstract: The invention relates to a coated metal surface including successively, starting at the metal, at least one layer of polyurethane and at least one layer of thermoplastic polymer, it being possible for a binder to be placed between the polyurethane and the thermoplastic polymer. It is useful for covering pipes, electrical cables, telecommunication cables and stay wires.
problem: Protecting metal surfaces from environmental degradation while maintaining structural integrity for applications like pipes and cables.
constraint: Balancing adhesion between dissimilar polymer layers while ensuring the composite structure withstands mechanical and environmental stresses.
mechanism: A multi-layer system where each layer provides a distinct functional role: a first layer ensures adhesion and flexibility, a second layer provides durability, and an intermediate layer mediates compatibility between the two to maintain structural integrity under mechanical and environmental stress.
mechanism_raw: A layered coating system where a polyurethane layer provides adhesion and flexibility, followed by a thermoplastic polymer layer for durability, with an optional binder layer to mediate compatibility between the two materials.

abstract: A gas turbine engine turbine blade squealer tip includes an airfoil tip cap having an airfoil shape and pressure and suction sides joined together at chordally spaced apart leading and trailing edges of the tip cap. The squealer tip further includes a plurality of squealer ribs extend outward from the tip cap between the leading and trailing edges and substantially parallel channels between the squealer ribs. The squealer ribs and channels may have rectangular cross-sections and may also include a trailing edge rib along a portion of the suction side including the trailing edge and/or a leading edge rib curved around an axially extending portion of the leading edge. The squealer ribs are preferably angled in an axially aft direction from the leading edge on the suction side towards the trailing edge on the pressure side. Channel ribs may be disposed between the squealer ribs and across the channels and may be arranged such that only one of the channel ribs is disposed across each of the channels. The squealer tip may be constructed with no apertures through the tip cap in the channels between squealer ribs.
problem: Reducing tip leakage and improving efficiency in gas turbine engines by managing airflow around turbine blade tips.
constraint: Optimizing aerodynamic performance without compromising the structural integrity of the blade tip under high-temperature and high-stress conditions.
mechanism: Structured ribs with angled and curved geometries are positioned to create controlled airflow paths that reduce leakage gaps while maintaining structural support through strategic placement and orientation of the ribs.
mechanism_raw: Squealer ribs and channels with angled geometries and curved edge ribs create controlled airflow paths that minimize leakage gaps while maintaining structural support through strategic rib placement and orientation.

abstract: A copper replenishment system for replenishing copper which is depleted from a copper plating solution. The replenishment is achieved by the use of a compact filter cartridge, which is inserted into a recirculating loop for the solution. The filter cartridge contains a chemical, which when reacting with the solution replenishes the copper into the solution. The filter cartridge is a compact unit which can be easily handled and reduces the amount of contaminants that could be introduced by the presence of the replenishment chemical.
problem: Maintaining consistent copper levels in a recirculating copper plating solution without introducing contaminants.
constraint: Ensuring controlled chemical reaction rates and containment of the replenishment chemical to avoid contamination while maintaining efficient copper recovery.
mechanism: A containment structure holds a reactive agent within a fluid loop, enabling controlled interaction between the agent and the fluid to replenish a component while preventing contamination through physical separation and regulated release.
mechanism_raw: A compact filter cartridge containing a reactive chemical is inserted into the solution loop, where the chemical reacts with the solution to replenish copper while the filter structure contains and controls the release of the replenishment agent.

abstract: A method for supporting image compression in a real-time graphics rendering pipeline includes sorting object geometry for a scene among image regions called chunks. The object geometry for each chunk is rendered separately, and in a serial fashion. After the object geometry is completely rendered for a given chunk, the pixel data for that chunk is compressed and stored. Each chunk of an image can be generated and stored in this manner. To assemble a display image, compressed image chunks are retrieved, decompressed, and temporarily cached. Decompressed image data in the cache is combined into a display image. The process of generating a display image with compression can be performed at real-time rates.
problem: Enabling real-time image compression in graphics rendering pipelines without sacrificing performance or visual quality.
constraint: Balancing chunk size and rendering order to maintain real-time throughput while minimizing compression artifacts and cache overhead.
mechanism: Data is partitioned into discrete segments, processed sequentially, compressed individually, and managed through a caching system to enable parallel processing and efficient memory utilization while maintaining real-time throughput.
mechanism_raw: Scene geometry is partitioned into discrete chunks, rendered serially, and compressed individually before being cached and reassembled into a display image, allowing parallel processing and efficient memory management.

abstract: Sloping water tunnels and channels interconnect existing sources of water with dry land areas to form new water basins. Turbines are installed in rapidly flowing portions of the water tunnels and channels to generate electricity. Overflow tunnels connected to the sloping water tunnels by water gates communicate with wastewater treatment plants feeding into the sloping water tunnels to open the water gates when the outflow of treated wastewater starts to back up. The water tunnels and channels are formed by removing earth and installing steel frames with sprayed on concrete which is waterproofed. The earth removed is used to fill valleys to create dams and dumped into existing lakes and ocean bays on pontoon railways to create breakwaters and islands. A number of existing sources of water and new water basins are interconnected by a number of open water channels navigable by water vessels to create a transregional navigable water transportation system. Sufficient water is transported to dry land areas creating new water basins so that the hydrological cycle is altered increasing precipitation and so that the dry land areas are supplied with water for irrigation, fire fighting, transportation, recreation, fishing, habitation uses, and other water needs.
problem: Integrating water resource management, energy generation, and land modification to create sustainable water basins and transportation systems.
constraint: Coordinating water flow rates, energy extraction, and land-use modifications to balance hydrological cycle impacts with human and environmental needs.
mechanism: Excavated channels and tunnels are integrated with energy extraction elements and overflow systems to manage fluid flow, harness kinetic energy, and repurpose excavated material for constructing barriers that balance hydrological and ecological impacts.
mechanism_raw: Sloping water tunnels and channels are constructed by excavating earth and installing steel-concrete structures, with turbines harnessing flow energy, overflow systems managing wastewater, and excavated earth repurposed to build dams and breakwaters for ecosystem and infrastructure benefits.

abstract: This invention provides a water repellant glass plate for vehicles or buildings, which shows a long-term durability. The water repellant glass plate includes a primer layer on a glass substrate, consisting essentially of silicon oxide in which oxygen atoms are partially substituted by hydroxyl groups, at a thickness between 10 nm and 100 nm, and a second layer on the first layer consisting of an organic silicon compound including a fluoroalkyl group at a thickness between about 0.2 nm and about 40 nm.
problem: Creating a durable water-repellent surface on glass that maintains performance over time.
constraint: The thickness of each layer (10–100 nm for the primer, 0.2–40 nm for the top layer) must be optimized to ensure adhesion without compromising the hydrophobic properties or structural integrity of the glass.
mechanism: A layered surface treatment uses a chemically reactive primer layer to bond to a substrate, with the primer's chemistry modified to form stable interfacial bonds. A top layer containing hydrophobic chemical groups provides water repellency. The thickness of each layer is optimized to balance adhesion strength, functional performance, and structural integrity of the substrate.
mechanism_raw: A primer layer with oxygen atoms partially substituted by hydroxyl groups forms a chemically bonded base, enabling adhesion to a top layer of organic silicon compounds with fluoroalkyl groups. The primer's modified chemistry stabilizes the interface, while the top layer's hydrophobic groups provide water repellency. The layered structure balances durability and functionality.
residual_terms: ["hydrophobic chemical groups", "chemically reactive primer layer", "interfacial bonds"]

abstract: A method for selectively applying CVD copper to metallic surfaces, that are co-located with non-metallic surfaces, is provided. The method prepares both the metal and non-metallic surfaces with a low energy ion etch of an inert gas. The etching promotes the growth of copper on the metallic surface, and inhibits the growth on the non-metallic surface. Following an application of CVD copper, the surfaces are etched again to clean any residual copper from the non-metallic surface, and to again prepare the surfaces for another deposition of copper. Through repeated cycles of etching and copper deposition, the copper overlying the metallic surface is accumulated to achieve the desired thickness, while the non-metallic surface remains free of copper. A method is also provided for the selective deposition of copper on metallic surfaces to fill interconnects in damascene IC structures. An IC with a copper layer overlying a metallic surface, co-located with a non-metallic surface, where the copper layer is grown through repeated cycles of ion etching and copper deposition, is also provided.
problem: Achieving selective deposition of copper on metallic surfaces while avoiding non-metallic surfaces in complex geometries.
constraint: The etching and deposition cycles must be precisely balanced to ensure sufficient copper buildup on metal surfaces without leaving residues on non-metallic regions, which could disrupt subsequent processing steps.
mechanism: Surface energy modification via ion-based etching creates differential nucleation receptivity between material types. Cyclic processes alternate between etching to expose reactive sites on target surfaces and deposition to accumulate material selectively. Post-deposition etching removes residual deposits from non-target surfaces, ensuring selective buildup through repeated cycles.
mechanism_raw: Low-energy ion etching modifies surface energy: metallic surfaces become more receptive to copper nucleation, while non-metallic surfaces are inhibited. Repeated cycles of etching and deposition accumulate copper selectively on metal, with post-deposition etching removing residual copper from non-metallic areas.

abstract: A beaker for a sample dyeing machine comprises a hollow beaker body and a longitudinal sliding cylinder with flanges on both its ends. The outer wall of the cylinder is uniformly perforated for wrapping of a sample yarn or cloth to be dyed. A plurality of grooves is separately formed on the periphery of either one of the flanges to guide the flow of a dye solution. An annular passage is formed in the interior of the cylinder from one end to the other for allowing a dye solution to flow between the passage and the perforated wall of the cylinder. The beaker thus constructed can dye a sample uniformly and efficiently due to sufficient contact between a sample and a dye solution. The beaker also comprises a hollow tube outside the beaker body for one-way flow of a dye solution, and/or a dispensing device screwed on the top thereof for liquid addition to the beaker. A sample dyeing machine comprises a plurality of the beakers in a fixed rack. Under the rack is a magnetic plate having a plurality of strong magnets so separately arranged on the plate that the pole of each magnet is opposite to that of adjacent magnets. The cylinders inside the beakers are moved up and down by magnetic force while the magnetic plate is slid back and forth on a screw driven by a motor.
problem: Achieving uniform dyeing of textile samples in a batch process with minimal manual intervention.
constraint: The groove and perforation design must balance fluid flow distribution and mechanical movement to avoid over-agitation or uneven dye penetration, while the magnetic system must synchronize motion to maintain sample integrity.
mechanism: A structured surface with internal fluid channels and guided pathways directs flow distribution around a sample. Synchronized mechanical actuation combines vertical and horizontal motion to create controlled agitation, ensuring consistent contact between the sample and treatment fluid. The design balances flow dynamics and mechanical movement to prevent over-agitation and uneven penetration.
mechanism_raw: A perforated cylinder with guided grooves and an internal annular passage directs dye solution flow around the sample. Magnetic actuation moves the cylinder vertically while a motorized plate slides horizontally, creating controlled agitation and ensuring consistent contact between the sample and dye solution.

abstract: A method of finishing an edge of a sheet glass is disclosed. The method includes a first grinding step for grinding an edge of a sheet glass so as to provide the edge with an outwardly convex curved shape, and a finishing step for finishing a bordering portion which has been formed by the first grinding step between the curved edge and each flat side face of the sheet glass, so as to provide this bordering portion with a greater smoothness than smoothness provided by the first grinding step. A heat-tempered sheet glass using the method and a fire-resistant construction material using this heat-tempered sheet glass are also disclosed.
problem: Creating smooth, durable edges on sheet glass without introducing stress fractures or structural weaknesses.
constraint: The grinding and finishing steps must be sequenced to avoid over-removal of material, which could weaken the edge, while achieving sufficient smoothness to prevent failure points in heat-tempered or fire-resistant applications.
mechanism: A two-stage material removal process first shapes an edge into a stress-distributing geometry to reduce concentration points, then finishes the transition zone between the shaped edge and adjacent surfaces to eliminate roughness. Controlled material removal in each stage avoids over-thinning while achieving surface continuity for structural applications.
mechanism_raw: A two-step process: first grinding the edge into an outwardly convex curve to distribute stress, then finishing the transition zone between the curved edge and flat surfaces to eliminate roughness. The convex shape reduces stress concentration, while the finishing step ensures surface continuity.

abstract: The present invention provides a splittable composite fiber having improved processability on carding and superior splitting property by a splittable composite fiber comprising at least two thermoplastic resin components, and having a structure wherein a part of at least one of the components projects from the surface of the fiber.
problem: Improving the processability and splitting behavior of composite fibers during textile manufacturing.
constraint: The extent and distribution of component projections must balance ease of splitting with sufficient fiber strength to withstand mechanical stresses during carding and downstream processing steps.
mechanism: A multi-component structure incorporates surface projections from one component to create localized weak points. These projections facilitate controlled splitting under mechanical stress during processing, while the remaining components maintain structural integrity. The extent and distribution of projections balance ease of separation with sufficient strength for downstream operations.
mechanism_raw: A composite fiber with at least two thermoplastic components is structured so that one component projects from the surface. These projections create localized weak points that facilitate controlled splitting during carding, while the remaining components maintain structural integrity during processing.

abstract: A light-emitting assembly defining a pixel comprising a series of red, green, and blue light-emitting segments in general alignment and connected by first and second electrodes. The light-emitting segments are built upon a fiber optic core. According to the preferred embodiment, the core is coated with a holographic interface material.
problem: Creating a light-emitting pixel with red, green, and blue segments that efficiently direct light from a fiber optic core.
constraint: The alignment of the segments and the optical properties of the holographic material must balance light directionality with structural integration.
mechanism: A light-modulating interface material positioned between a light-transmitting core and color-emitting segments, configured to balance directional light emission with structural integration by controlling light propagation from the core to the aligned segments.
mechanism_raw: Using a holographic interface material coated on the fiber optic core to control and direct light emission from the core to the aligned RGB segments.

abstract: A transmission for folding out the solar cell panels (3 through 7) folded in an accordion-like manner on a spacecraft (1) has cable pulleys (22 through 27) at the hinges (9 through 14), around pairs of which pulleys endless cables (29 through 33) are wound. To adapt its change in length during temperature changes to the change in the length of the panels (3 through 7) and to increase its rigidity to elongation, the cable (29 through 33) is provided with a plastic sheathing (47, 48) firmly connected to same outside the area of the cable pulleys (22 through 27).
problem: Managing thermal expansion and contraction in a spacecraft's solar panel deployment system while maintaining structural rigidity.
constraint: The sheathing must balance flexibility for thermal movement with sufficient rigidity to prevent unwanted cable stretching.
mechanism: A flexible sheath applied to tensioned cables routed through articulated joints, enabling controlled length adjustment during thermal cycles while increasing resistance to tensile deformation through distributed compliance.
mechanism_raw: Applying a plastic sheathing to cables wound around pulleys at hinges, allowing controlled length changes during temperature fluctuations while increasing resistance to elongation.

abstract: An oil absorption filter for extracting free oil from the used wash water of a laundry has platforms which extend in parallel and laterally across a tank, but do not reach across the total length of the tank so as to provide an avenue of fluid flow between the platforms.. Multiple entrances are provided into the tank to resulting in a slow flow of used wash water into the tank so as to encourage free oil to separate from the used wash water. Hydrophobic socks are vertically arranged in rows and placed through holes in the platforms. A partitioned pumping chamber is provided with an entrance proximate to the bottom of the tank which is the only avenue of entry for oil-filtered water to access the pumping chamber. A sump pump connected electrically connected to a level float pumps the oil filtered water out of the pumping chamber and out of the oil filter.
problem: Separating free oil from used wash water in a laundry system while efficiently filtering and pumping the treated water.
constraint: The flow rate must be slow enough to allow oil separation while ensuring the pumping chamber only accesses fully filtered water.
mechanism: Hydrophobic absorption elements arranged across perforated platforms to separate immiscible contaminants from a liquid stream, combined with a partitioned extraction chamber that isolates filtered liquid for removal while preventing access to untreated regions.
mechanism_raw: Using vertically arranged hydrophobic socks in rows across perforated platforms to absorb oil, combined with a partitioned pumping chamber that isolates filtered water for extraction.

abstract: A treatment method for containers of hazardous materials, including chemical and conventional weapons, is described. The method is applicable to munitions containing explosives and chemical warfare agents, and to training or test rounds. The containers are subjected to a highly corrosive fluid which dissolves all or part of the container and renders the containers useless as munitions. The highly corrosive fluid may render the hazardous material non-hazardous. The result of the treatment is a liquor which can undergo further treatment for recovery or disposal.
problem: Neutralizing or rendering hazardous material containers (e.g., munitions, chemical weapons) unusable and non-hazardous.
constraint: The corrosive fluid must effectively degrade the container and hazardous material while being manageable in terms of safety and byproduct handling.
mechanism: A corrosive agent applied to degrade container structures and neutralize hazardous contents through chemical interaction, with containment and byproduct management to ensure safe decomposition of both the container and its payload.
mechanism_raw: Subjecting containers to a highly corrosive fluid that dissolves all or part of the container and potentially neutralizes the hazardous material inside.

abstract: A process for dewaxing waxy hydrocarbonaceous materials, such as hydrocarbon fuel and lubricating oil fractions to reduce their cloud and pour points comprises reacting the material with hydrogen in the presence of a dewaxing catalyst comprising at least one metal catalytic component and ferrierite in which at least a portion of its cation exchange positions are occupied by one or more trivalent rare earth metal cations. The rare earth ion exchanged ferrierite catalyst has good selectivity for lubricating oil production, particularly when dewaxing a Fischer-Tropsch wax hydroisomerate. Preferably at least 10% and more preferably at least 15% of the ferreirite cation exchange capacity is occupied by one or more trivalent rare earth metal cations.
problem: Reducing the cloud and pour points of waxy hydrocarbon materials (e.g., fuels, lubricating oils) to improve low-temperature performance.
constraint: The catalyst must balance rare earth ion exchange levels to optimize selectivity for lubricating oil production while maintaining catalytic activity.
mechanism: A catalytic process using a rare earth-exchanged zeolite to enhance isomerization selectivity over cracking in hydrocarbon materials, optimizing molecular restructuring to reduce crystallization tendencies while maintaining catalytic activity.
mechanism_raw: Reacting the material with hydrogen in the presence of a dewaxing catalyst containing trivalent rare earth metal cations exchanged into ferrierite, enhancing selectivity for isomerization over cracking.

abstract: A solar collector having a radiation absorber (1) has a number of channels for conducting heat receiving liquid, said channels accommodating particles for capillary effect to lift the liquid to effectively sweep the sun-facing surface layer of the absorber. The solar collector is started after a prolonged operation standstill by driving a liquid pump (7) intermittently by a control unit (13) acting according to a clock-controlled program. In the intermittent start-up phase, first the pump (7) is driven for 2-4 minutes, thereafter it is shut down for a time span of about 20-60 seconds, and this is repeated two or three times before a continuous operation phase is started. Thereby air in the absorber (1) channels is expelled more rapidly.
problem: Air trapped in solar collector channels after prolonged standstill prevents efficient liquid circulation and heat transfer.
constraint: Balancing pump runtime and rest intervals to maximize air expulsion efficiency without excessive energy consumption or mechanical wear.
mechanism: Cyclic actuation of a pumping element with alternating active and idle phases generates transient pressure differentials within a fluid pathway, mobilizing and evacuating entrapped gaseous volumes more effectively than sustained unidirectional flow.
mechanism_raw: Intermittent pump operation (drive for 2-4 minutes, then shut down for 20-60 seconds, repeated 2-3 times) creates pressure fluctuations that dislodge and expel trapped air more rapidly than continuous operation.

abstract: This invention relates to a connecting pipe for a liquid-tight connection to a sewer pipe. The connecting pipe comprises a connecting-pipe body having at least two spaced apart circumferential sealing chambers, where one of the sealing chambers contains a first sealing element comprising a ring seal proximate an inside surface of the sewer pipe and facing an opening-wall surface of the branch opening. The ring seal comprises at least one sealing-lip ring extending over an outer contour of this sealing chamber to contact the opening-wall surface of the branch opening. Another sealing chamber contains a second sealing element comprising a flexible filler proximate an outer surface of the sewer pipe and facing the opening-wall surface of the branch opening, such that a slot chamber extending from this sealing chamber to the opening-wall surface of the branch opening is sealingly bridged. The connecting pipe comprises a spacing ring having a bearing flange compatible with an outside pipe surface of the sewer pipe, wherein the spacing ring is a positioning ring fastened to the connecting-pipe body by fastening means in such a manner that when the connecting-pipe body is inserted into the branch opening, the first and second sealing elements are positioned opposite the opening-wall surface of the branch opening.
reason: The invention describes a static dual-seal configuration with positioning rings, which is a component arrangement rather than a dynamic causal mechanism. The problem-solving relies on physical geometry and material placement, not a functional process that can be abstracted.

abstract: A hand held shower head and filter assembly for attachment to a waterline to remove chlorine and other substances from water. This assembly includes a reversible and reusable filter assembly for use with hot water passing through a two stage bed of ceramic-type calcium sulfite beads and a copper/zinc material. The device includes an elongated, hollow handle which holds the filter element therein in such a manner that the filter media reacts with or removes chlorine and other substances more efficiently from shower water, thereby allowing a greater volume of water to be treated, as well as the treatment of water at elevated temperatures, in a more versatile and useful device.
reason: The mechanism is limited to specific filter media (ceramic calcium sulfite beads and copper/zinc) arranged in a two-stage bed. The problem-solving is tied to material chemistry and static design, not a transferable functional process.

abstract: There is provided a heat pump system including two (4, 6), at least similar units in fluid communication with each other, each unit having a housing (8, 8'), a first air/brine heat exchanger (12, 12'), a second brine/refrigerant heat exchanger (24, 24'), a brine inlet (10, 10') for applying brine onto at least one of the heat exchangers, a brine reservoir (14, 14') and a pump (28) for circulating the brine from the reservoir to the inlet. The first and second heat exchangers are in closed loop fluid communication with each other and have a compressor (44) for circulating a refrigerant therethrough in selected directions.
reason: The heat pump system uses a conventional closed-loop refrigerant circulation with two heat exchangers. The mechanism is a standard thermodynamic configuration without a novel causal operation that can be abstracted beyond the specific heat pump design.

abstract: A waste water treating system which has an incline pipe for passing waste water therethrough by gravity flow. This aeration pipe has tuyere perforations penetrating the pipe along a portion and a sealed jacket surrounds this perforated portion of the pipe. An access conduit is connected to the jacket for access to the interior of the jacket and an air fan is mounted at the upper in the access conduit for forcing air under pressure from its inlet into the interior of the jacket and through the perforation as tuyeres for agitating and aerating waste water passing through the perforated aeration pipe. Additional aeration may be accomplished by gravity flow of the waste water by connecting the downstream end of this perforated pipe to a vertical riser pipe for flowing waste water by gravity flow from an upper open end of the riser pipe to assist in further aeration of the waste water.
problem: Inefficient aeration and agitation of wastewater in gravity-flow systems due to lack of controlled air injection.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient air pressure to overcome backpressure while ensuring uniform distribution of air through perforations without clogging or excessive energy use.
mechanism: A pressurized gas is introduced through distributed apertures along a containment boundary surrounding a sloped conduit, inducing localized flow disruption and mass transfer enhancement. Downstream gravitational movement of the working fluid through the conduit amplifies mixing and distribution of the introduced gas.
mechanism_raw: Pressurized air is forced through tuyere perforations in a sealed jacket surrounding an inclined pipe, creating localized turbulence and oxygenation. Gravity-driven flow through the pipe enhances mixing and aeration efficiency.
residual_terms: ["pressurized gas", "apertures", "containment boundary", "sloped conduit", "gravitational movement", "working fluid", "mixing", "mass transfer"]

abstract: The invention relates to a roller mill, particularly a modular air-swept mill, with a rotary grinding pan on which roll grinding rollers and having columns, on which are mounted by means of rockers the grinding rollers, the columns being in each case fixed to a foundation frame and arranged as a mill foundation frame. For the use of stable and torsionally stiff columns for relatively large roller mills, according to the invention the foundation frames of the columns, together with the connecting frame parts are arranged in a mill foundation to form a circumferential foundation frame, particularly a polygonal or U-shaped frame. A gear foundation frame is located in the mill center separately from the circumferential frame and permits the construction of a different level of the particular areas of the mill foundation.
problem: Achieving torsional stiffness and structural stability in large roller mills while allowing modular construction and variable foundation levels.
constraint: Balancing torsional rigidity of the circumferential frame with the need for localized flexibility or differential elevation in the central region.
mechanism: A load-distributing frame resists torsional forces while a separate functional frame enables independent positioning or construction, decoupling structural load-bearing from localized operational adjustments.
mechanism_raw: A circumferential foundation frame (e.g., polygonal or U-shaped) distributes structural loads and resists torsion, while a separate central gear foundation frame enables independent construction at different levels, decoupling load-bearing and functional components.

abstract: A pen holder uniquely designed for holding two writing utensils in their individual capacity, separated from adjacent writing utensils, while providing protection for the marking tips of the writing utensils. The pen holder consists of a tube casing containing two tubes. Each tube is predisposed for releasably retaining a writing utensil, particularly a pen. Separating the tubes within the tube casing and the writing utensils received within each tube is a dividing wall.
reason: The mechanism is a simple physical separation (dividing wall) within a casing to isolate two pens. No causal interaction or feedback loop generates a non-obvious effect beyond basic containment.

abstract: An exercise apparatus for exercising the entire body, but in particular the muscles of the legs and the buttocks includes a frame, a lower leg support that has a rearward facing surface for supporting a lower leg area of a user, and a yoke member. The yoke member has a rearward portion that is constructed and arranged to be gripped for lifting by a user, and a forward portion that is pivotally mounted to the frame at a location that is positioned forward of said rearward facing surface of the lower leg support. The apparatus also includes resistance structure for imparting resistance against lifting the rearward portion of said yoke member by the user. This apparatus is particularly suited for doing "lunge" exercises in a way that is both more efficient in the working of targeted muscle groups and is less stressful on the user's knee joints than conventional free weight based lunge exercises are.
problem: Performing lunge exercises efficiently while minimizing knee joint stress through targeted muscle engagement.
constraint: Balancing resistance magnitude and pivot geometry to optimize muscle engagement without overloading joints.
mechanism: A pivot point positioned ahead of a support surface redirects applied forces through mechanical advantage, enabling targeted resistance application while reducing compressive loads on a joint.
mechanism_raw: A yoke with a forward pivot point positioned ahead of the lower leg support creates a mechanical advantage that redirects lifting forces, enabling resistance to be applied in a way that emphasizes targeted muscle groups while reducing compressive forces on the knee.

abstract: A process for manufacturing a ceramic metal composite body in the case of which a dimensionally stable and porous sacrificial body is produced from ceramic initial products and is filled at a filling temperature with a softened metal, particularly under an increased pressure. The filled sacrificial body is heated to a reaction temperature and the metal to be filled in, BMe, is reacted with a metal of the ceramics. KMe, forming the ceramic metal composite body which has a ceramic phase having KMe.sub.m B.sub.x and/or KMe.sub.n C.sub.y and/or KMe.sub.o CN and BMe.sub.p O.sub.3 and has a metallic phase having an intermetallic compound which is formed of KMe and BMe, the filling temperature being lower than the reaction temperature and higher than or equal to the softening temperature of the metal.
problem: Manufacturing ceramic-metal composite bodies with controlled phase compositions and structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining the sacrificial body's structural integrity during infiltration while ensuring sufficient thermal activation for reaction without collapsing the porous structure.
mechanism: A porous sacrificial structure is infiltrated with a material at a sub-reaction temperature, then heated to trigger in situ phase formation while preserving dimensional integrity during thermal activation.
mechanism_raw: A porous sacrificial ceramic body is infiltrated with a softened metal at a temperature below the reaction temperature, then heated to trigger a reaction between the metal and ceramic components, forming intermetallic and ceramic phases in situ while preserving dimensional stability.

abstract: Molecular dispersions of rigid-rod polybenzobisazole polymer/copolymer in thermoplastic matrices in a weight ratio of about 1:99 to 50:50 are prepared by dissolving the rigid-rod polymer in an alcoholic or aprotic solvent, dissolving the thermoplastic polymer in an alcoholic or aprotic solvent, combining the two solutions and recovering the resulting molecular composite from the combined solution. These molecular dispersions consist essentially of rigid-rod polybenzobisazole polymer/copolymer having sulfonic acid groups pendant to the polymer/copolymer backbone and thermoplastic polymers selected from the group consisting of polyvinylpyridines, poly(arylene ether ketone)s with a pyridyl functionality, aromatic poly(pyridine ether)s and poly(pyridine ether sulfone) copolymers, and polyimides with a pyridyl functionality.
problem: Creating molecular dispersions of rigid-rod polymers in thermoplastic matrices with controlled compatibility and phase distribution.
constraint: Selecting solvents and polymer ratios that maintain solubility and compatibility during mixing while avoiding phase separation during recovery.
mechanism: Two polymers are dissolved in compatible solvents, combined to enable molecular-level mixing, and then solvent recovery preserves uniform dispersion of one polymer within the other matrix.
mechanism_raw: Dissolving both the rigid-rod polymer and thermoplastic polymer in compatible solvents, then combining the solutions to enable molecular-level mixing before solvent recovery, ensuring uniform dispersion of the rigid-rod chains within the thermoplastic matrix.

abstract: An automatic blade changing system of a dicing machine uses a blade which is fixed to an auxiliary stopper member provided with a thread which is engaged with a thread of a spindle. The automatic blade changing system consists of two blade holding means which hold the blade to which the stopper member is fixed and rotate the blade relatively to the spindle in the state wherein the blade is forced to the spindle, a blade accommodating means which accommodates a blade to replace the blade, a moving means for moving the blade holding means between the end of the spindle and the blade accommodating means.
problem: Automated blade replacement in dicing machines requires precise alignment and force application without manual intervention.
constraint: Maintaining alignment and consistent force during blade replacement to avoid damage or misalignment of the blade or spindle.
mechanism: A coupling mechanism combines controlled rotational and linear motion between two components to maintain alignment and force during automated replacement, using a threaded interface to translate rotational input into precise linear displacement.
mechanism_raw: Threaded engagement between the blade's stopper and spindle, combined with controlled relative rotation and linear movement of blade holding means, enables automated blade changes while maintaining alignment and force.

abstract: Compositions, methods, and systems for manufacturing articles, particularly containers and packaging materials, having a particle packed, highly inorganically filled, cellular matrix are disclosed. Suitable inorganically filled mixtures are prepared by mixing together a starch-based binder, a solvent, inorganic aggregates, and optimal admixtures, e.g., fibers, mold-releasing agents, rheology-modifying agents, plasticizers, coating materials, and dispersants, in the correct proportions to form an article which has the desired performance criteria. The inorganically filled mixtures have a predetermined viscosity and are heated between molds at an elevated temperature and pressure to produce form-stable articles having a desired shape and a selectively controlled cellular, structure matrix. The molded articles may be placed in a high humidity chamber to obtain the necessary flexibility for their intended use. The articles may be manufactured to have properties substantially similar to articles presently made from conventional materials like paper, paperboard, polystyrene, plastic, or other organic materials. They have especial utility in the mass-production of containers, particularly food and beverage containers.
problem: Manufacturing inorganic-filled articles with properties similar to conventional organic materials (e.g., plastic, paper) requires precise control over composition and processing conditions.
constraint: Balancing inorganic filler content, binder viscosity, and environmental conditions (temperature, pressure, humidity) to achieve structural integrity and desired performance without compromising material properties.
mechanism: A multi-stage process involves blending a binder with particulate fillers and additives to achieve a target viscosity, forming the mixture under controlled thermal and pressure conditions, and conditioning the formed product in a humid environment to adjust mechanical properties.
mechanism_raw: Controlled mixing of starch-based binder, inorganic aggregates, and admixtures to achieve a predetermined viscosity, followed by molding under elevated temperature and pressure, and post-processing in a high-humidity chamber to tune flexibility.

abstract: This invention pertains to a novel paint brush with inverted bristle clamping panel, a removable bristle pack and a panel hinge yield mechanism. The paint brush provides ready cleaning after use by disengaging the hinged inverted bristle clamping panel, removing the bristles and thereby exposing all of the bristles to the cleaning solution. The panel has a resilient release mechanism which yields slightly when undue force is applied to the inverted hinged panel against the bristles. A paint brush construction comprising: (a) a paint brush body and handle, the body having formed therein a cavity for receiving a group of bristles; (b) a pivotal bristle bearing member positioned proximate to the cavity, the bristle bearing member when pivoted to a closed position applying a holding force against bristles held within the cavity, and the member when pivoted to an open position enabling bristles held within the cavity to be removed; and (c) a resilient yield location associated with the paint brush body and the pivotal bristle bearing member which enables the pivotal bristle bearing member to yield when the bristle bearing member encounters an undue force when being pivoted to the closed position.
problem: Paint brushes require easy cleaning by exposing bristles to cleaning solutions without damaging the brush structure during disassembly.
constraint: Ensuring the clamping panel can open and close reliably without breaking, while maintaining sufficient holding force during use and safety during cleaning.
mechanism: A hinged panel with a compliant element enables controlled opening to release retained components, while the compliance prevents structural failure from excessive force during closure or use.
mechanism_raw: A hinged, inverted bristle clamping panel with a resilient yield mechanism allows controlled opening to remove bristles, while the yield feature prevents damage from excessive force during closure.

abstract: An apparatus for supplying, to a sewing device, a connected belt-loop material including at least one connection portion where two long materials are connected to each other, the connection portion having a width greater than a substantially constant width of a remaining portion of the belt-loop material, the apparatus including a feeding device which feeds the belt-loop material toward the sewing device, and a positioning device which positions, in a direction extending parallel to the width of the belt-loop material, at least the remaining portion of the belt-loop material being fed by the feeding device, so that the remaining portion takes a reference position in the direction of width, the positioning device including a permitting device which permits the connection portion of the belt-loop material to be fed through the positioning device by the feeding device, without lowering an accuracy with which the remaining portion of the belt-loop material is positioned by the positioning device in the direction extending parallel to the width.
problem: Accurate positioning of belt-loop material with varying widths (e.g., connection portions) during sewing operations without disrupting alignment of the uniform sections.
constraint: Maintaining positional accuracy for uniform sections while accommodating variable-width connection portions without mechanical interference or loss of precision.
mechanism: A positioning system incorporates a selective bypass mechanism that allows variable-width sections to pass through while maintaining fixed reference alignment for uniform sections, ensuring consistent processing accuracy.
mechanism_raw: A positioning device with a permitting mechanism allows wider connection portions to pass through while maintaining reference alignment for the remaining uniform-width sections, ensuring consistent sewing accuracy.

abstract: Milling/sizing apparatus which includes individual and/or nested sieves each of which may also include a quantity of beads, disks and/or other geometric or non-geometric shapes. The sieves can be rotated, vibrated or agitated in any and all combinations by various methods to achieve independently horizontal rotation and vertical reciprocation (similar to a merry-go-round) to efficiently segregate, size or mill cohesive and polydisperse powder particles to specific size ranges. The invention also contemplates a method for using the apparatus in the sizing and quantification of aggregated particles of cohesive disperse powders.
problem: Efficient segregation, sizing, or milling of cohesive and polydisperse powder particles to specific size ranges without clogging or inefficiency.
constraint: Achieving effective particle separation and milling through combined motion types and sieve geometries while avoiding clogging or uneven particle distribution.
mechanism: Independent orthogonal motions (horizontal rotation and vertical reciprocation) applied to sieves with varying surface geometries generate multi-directional agitation to disrupt particle cohesion and classify particles by size through differential passage.
mechanism_raw: Independent horizontal rotation and vertical reciprocation of sieves with geometric/non-geometric shapes (e.g., beads, disks) create multi-directional agitation to break cohesive particle aggregates and classify by size.

abstract: Cellulosic webs can be embossed using an extended nip structure with embossing means in a controlled nip dwell zone. Single and multiply wipes and towels produced by plying together two or more such webs can be embossed. Webs having common caliper and basis weight can be processed using the extended nip structure with an appropriate embossing means. The tendency of the embossed relief to relax and disappear after processing can be substantially alleviated by controlling dwell time to ensure reliable embossing.
problem: Embossed relief on cellulosic webs tends to relax and disappear after processing, reducing the effectiveness of the embossing.
constraint: Dwell time must be long enough to set the embossing but short enough to avoid material deformation or process inefficiency.
mechanism: A timed pressure application system maintains a material in a deformed state long enough for structural setting to occur, preventing relaxation-induced loss of pattern fidelity by balancing dwell duration against material integrity constraints.
mechanism_raw: Controlling dwell time in an extended nip structure ensures the embossing means applies sufficient and consistent pressure to set the relief before the material relaxes, thereby maintaining the embossed pattern.

abstract: An autonomous vehicle capable of traveling and stopping parallel to a wall includes right and left driving wheels receiving driving force to be driven independently, a dependent wheel for supporting the autonomous vehicle together with the driving wheels for a straightforward movement and a U-turn, a motor for driving the right and left driving wheels, a coupling mechanism for transmitting the rotation of the motor to the driving wheels, an encoder for detecting the rotation amount and velocity of the motor, a gyro sensor for detecting the direction of the autonomous vehicle, a distance measurement sensor for measuring the distance to a right or left object of interest, and a controller for controlling the autonomous vehicle through the motor and the driving wheels. The controller receives the output of the encoder, calculates a control value for the driving wheels based on the rotation amount and rotation velocity of the motor, and determines that the autonomous vehicle travels parallel to the wall if the ratios of a time period to turn the autonomous vehicle rightward and a time period to turn the vehicle leftward in a prescribed time period are equal based on the control value.
problem: An autonomous vehicle needs to maintain straight-line parallel travel alongside a wall despite environmental disturbances or mechanical asymmetries.
constraint: The system must balance sensor accuracy, motor response time, and environmental variability to maintain alignment without overcorrecting.
mechanism: A feedback control system adjusts actuator outputs based on differential motion measurements to maintain alignment with a reference surface, using temporal asymmetry in corrective actions to counteract disturbances.
mechanism_raw: The controller calculates control values for driving wheels based on motor rotation data and determines parallelism by comparing the ratio of rightward and leftward turning time periods, adjusting wheel speeds to balance deviations.

abstract: A process is described for producing a bonded, non-woven fibrous batt by the use of a dry, solid, particulate, latent-cross-linkable, thermosetting, fiber-binder. This fiber-binder is an intimate mixture of a solid epoxy resin and a cross-linking agent. The epoxy resin has (a) terminal epoxy groups; (b) an epoxide equivalent weight of above about 500; (c) a glass transition temperature above about 40.degree. C.; and (d) a melting point above about 70.degree. C. In the process the fiber-binder contacts the fibers to form a raw batt with the fiber-binder loosely adhering to the fibers of the batt. Then the raw batt is heated to a cross-linking temperature above the melting point of the fiber-binder but below the scorching or melting point of the fibers thereby melting the fiber-binder. The fiber-binder flows to intersections of the fibers and subsequently reacts the cross-linking agent with the terminal epoxy groups of the epoxy resin. This converts the raw batt into a hot cross-linked batt. The hot cross-linked batt is then cooled to room temperature. Batts are also described as is a process for hot molding these batts.
problem: Creating a bonded, non-woven fibrous batt without damaging the structural integrity of the fibers during the bonding process.
constraint: Temperature must exceed the binder's melting point but remain below the fibers' scorching or melting point to avoid degradation.
mechanism: A phase-changing binding agent is selectively activated at discrete contact points between structural elements, transitioning from a flowable state to a cross-linked state to create localized bonds while preserving non-contact regions.
mechanism_raw: A thermosetting fiber-binder is heated to melt and flow to fiber intersections, where it cross-links upon cooling, selectively bonding fibers at contact points while preserving the rest of the structure.

abstract: A screen used in the production of cellulose pulp mounted in a digester minimizes traditional screen problems (including clogging) without introducing new problems. The screen comprises a screen plate secured to an internal surface of the digester. The screen plate has a plurality of slots formed in it with an inclination angle, and the screen plate is positioned in the digester so that the inclination angle of the slots relative to the horizontal X axis of the X-Y plane defined by the internal surface of the digester is between 30-60.degree.. The screen plate may comprise a plurality of parallel screen bars side-by-side, or an integral metal plate with slots formed in it. The slots typically have a width between 1-5 millimeters and a spacing between them of 3-9 millimeters.
problem: Screening cellulose pulp in a digester tends to cause clogging due to fiber accumulation or uneven flow distribution.
constraint: Slot angle must balance flow efficiency and structural strength to avoid clogging without compromising the screen's durability.
mechanism: Angled flow-guiding apertures direct particulate movement along their orientation to prevent accumulation and maintain uniform distribution, with aperture angle optimized to balance throughput and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Slots in the screen plate are inclined at 30–60 degrees relative to the digester's horizontal axis, directing fiber movement along the slots to prevent accumulation and maintain consistent flow.

abstract: A method for selecting novel proteins such as growth hormone and antibody fragment variants having altered binding properties for their respective receptor molecules is provided. The method comprises fusing a gene encoding a protein of interest to the carboxy terminal domain of the gene III coat protein of the filamentous phage M13. The gene fusion is mutated to form a library of structurally related fusion proteins that are expressed in low quantity on the surface of a phagemid particle. Biological selection and screening are employed to identify novel ligands useful as drug candidates. Disclosed are preferred phagemid expression vectors and selected human growth hormone variants.
problem: Identifying protein variants with altered binding properties for therapeutic use requires efficient screening of large genetic libraries.
constraint: Expression levels must be low enough to avoid toxicity while ensuring sufficient surface display for selection efficacy.
mechanism: Biological vectors displaying variant molecules are subjected to affinity-based selection processes to isolate candidates with desired interaction properties, using expression level modulation to balance viability and detection efficacy.
mechanism_raw: Genes encoding protein variants are fused to a phage coat protein, expressed on phagemid particles, and subjected to biological selection to isolate variants with desired binding affinity for target receptors.

abstract: A machine for making a mixed yarn by combining two false-twist textured yarns is disclosed. The machine comprises drawing systems (3A, 3B; 8A, 8B) arranged on either side of the texturing area and mounted alternately on two separately controlled parallel, shafts, and heat treatment units (5A, 5B) located in the false twisting area and having a temperature controlled by two mutually separated systems. The false-twist spindles (7) are power spindles with a speed that may be varied to suit each kind of yarn. The machine comprises joining device (9) for interlacing two yarns from two different texturing positions, the device being arranged, when seen from the front, between the positions so that the two yarns (2A, 2B) follow identical paths before being joined.
problem: Ensuring two false-twist textured yarns are combined without misalignment or tension imbalance during mixed yarn production.
constraint: The joining device must maintain identical path geometry for both yarns while allowing independent control of the two texturing systems.
mechanism: A symmetric joining mechanism enforces identical path geometry for two concurrently processed elements by arranging their trajectories through a shared constraint structure, ensuring differential tension or path-length discrepancies are eliminated during interlacing.
mechanism_raw: A joining device arranged symmetrically between two texturing positions forces both yarns to follow identical paths before interlacing, eliminating differential tension or path-length discrepancies that could cause misalignment.

abstract: A water rescue device includes a flotation member, a shoulder strap, an extension strap which connects the floatation member and the shoulder strap, and a slack eliminator, which is connected to the extension material, and mechanically coils any slack extension strap between the flotation member and the shoulder strap, the slack eliminator having a torsion spring, a reel which takes up any slack extension strap under a force of the torsion spring, a plastic housing, and a selectively operable cam lever which allows the extension strap to extend a desired length against the force of the torsion spring.
problem: Managing slack in an extension strap during water rescue operations to ensure controlled deployment and retraction.
constraint: The system must balance automatic slack elimination with the ability to manually extend the strap when needed during rescue maneuvers.
mechanism: A tension-biased reel automatically eliminates slack in a flexible member via stored energy, while a selectively engageable override mechanism allows manual extension against the biasing force when controlled deployment is required.
mechanism_raw: A torsion spring-driven reel automatically coils slack extension strap under spring force, while a selectively operable cam lever allows manual override to extend the strap against the spring tension.

abstract: The method for forming an insulating film having a low dielectric constant, which is suitable for intermetal insulating film applications, by plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) includes the step of supplying a first source gas containing fluorine and carbon to a dual-frequency, high density plasma reactor. The method also includes the step of supplying a second source gas containing silicon dioxide to the reactor. In this manner a fluorocarbon/silicon dioxide film is formed on a substrate in the reactor.
problem: Forming a low-dielectric-constant insulating film suitable for intermetal applications in semiconductor devices.
constraint: The gas mixture ratio and plasma conditions must be precisely controlled to achieve the desired low dielectric constant without compromising film stability.
mechanism: A controlled gas mixture is introduced into a plasma environment with precisely regulated energy input to synthesize a composite material with tailored dielectric properties through simultaneous chemical reactions.
mechanism_raw: Co-supplying a fluorine/carbon-containing gas and a silicon dioxide gas into a dual-frequency high-density plasma reactor enables formation of a fluorocarbon/silicon dioxide composite film with tailored dielectric properties.
residual_terms: ["dual-frequency high-density plasma reactor", "fluorine/carbon-containing gas", "silicon dioxide gas"]

abstract: A fastening clasp for holding fabric or other sheet-like material in a given position. The fastening clasp includes a flexible sleeve having a first end and a second end. A ring is attached to the first end of the flexible sleeve. A flexible, transverse tab is attached to the second end of the flexible sleeve. A piece of the fabric is positioned directly over the ring while the tab is inserted within the ring. The tab and fabric are both held in place by the stiffness of the tab's perimeter. The sleeve gathers and holds the fabric in the desired position.
problem: Securing fabric or sheet-like material in a fixed position without additional fasteners or adhesives.
constraint: The tab's stiffness must be sufficient to grip the fabric but flexible enough to allow insertion through the ring during fastening.
mechanism: A flexible element inserted through an aperture and positioned over a target surface is retained by the element's inherent stiffness, which creates opposing gripping forces against both the element and the surface, while a surrounding structure gathers and secures the surface.
mechanism_raw: A flexible tab inserted through a ring and positioned over fabric is held in place by the stiffness of the tab's perimeter, which simultaneously grips both the tab and the fabric, while the sleeve gathers and retains the fabric.

abstract: A ring carrier apparatus for a round hay feeder has three spears extending horizontally from an upright post and its perpendicular crossbar base. A single long spear projects from a height on the post, while two widely separated short spears project from the crossbar. A housing is removable and adjustable in height on the upper portion of the post. The housing contains a hook which is opened by a rope leading to the farm tractor hitched to the apparatus. A roll guard on the housing prevents the feeder ring from rotating. A pivoting rocker plate attached to the crossbar base prevents the bottom of the feeder ring from excessive forward movement.
problem: Efficiently loading and unloading a round hay feeder ring onto spears while preventing rotation and excessive forward movement during tractor-based handling.
constraint: The mechanical components must coordinate with tractor movement to ensure smooth engagement and disengagement of the feeder ring without jamming or misalignment.
mechanism: A remotely actuated engagement element interacts with a ring-shaped object to secure it, while a rotational constraint and a pivoting limiter coordinate with external motion to prevent unwanted movement during loading or unloading.
mechanism_raw: A rope-actuated hook in a height-adjustable housing opens to engage the feeder ring, while a roll guard prevents rotation and a pivoting rocker plate limits forward movement of the ring's bottom during loading.

abstract: A retaining wall construction includes a lower mechanically stabilized earth bulk form with tensile members projecting from the front face of the bulk forms and connected to precast wall panels that are spaced from the front face of the bulk form. The space between the front face of the bulk form and the panels is filled with concrete. Positioned on top of the reinforced concrete and the first bulk form, as well as along the sides thereof, are additional bulk forms which include tensile members connected directly to the front facing panels.
problem: Creating a structurally stable retaining wall with spaced facing panels that can independently support loads while maintaining alignment and spacing.
constraint: Balancing the spacing between panels (to allow concrete filling and reduce material use) while ensuring sufficient tensile connectivity to prevent panel displacement under load.
mechanism: Using tension-transmitting elements embedded within a bulk material to directly link spaced-apart facing panels, transferring tensile forces between the panels and the bulk material to maintain structural integrity. Additional bulk material layers are positioned on top and along sides to distribute loads and reinforce the system.
mechanism_raw: Using tensile members embedded in a bulk form to directly connect to spaced facing panels, transferring tensile forces between the panels and the bulk form to maintain structural integrity. Additional bulk forms are layered on top and along sides to distribute loads and reinforce the system.

abstract: A transducer according to various aspects of the present invention provides high fractional bandwidth with relatively low degradation of the pulse duration and sensitivity. The transducer includes a back matching layer behind the transducer material. The back matching layer is characterized by an impedance selected to transmit a selected portion of the backwards propagating acoustic energy to an absorption layer. The remaining acoustic energy is reflected in the desired direction of propagation. As a result, the transducer provides enhanced bandwidth without excessive loss of sensitivity or increase in pulse duration.
problem: Enhancing the bandwidth of an acoustic transducer without degrading sensitivity or increasing pulse duration.
constraint: Impedance matching must balance energy reflection (for sensitivity) and absorption (for bandwidth) to avoid excessive loss in either parameter.
mechanism: A back matching layer with tailored acoustic impedance selectively transmits backward-propagating energy to an absorption layer while reflecting remaining energy in the desired propagation direction, optimizing energy directionality to broaden bandwidth.
mechanism_raw: A back matching layer with tailored acoustic impedance selectively transmits backward-propagating energy to an absorption layer while reflecting remaining energy in the desired propagation direction, optimizing energy directionality to broaden bandwidth.

abstract: A buffered emulsion blasting agent is disclosed, particularly suited for use in connection with sulfide and pyrite ores. The buffered emulsion blasting agent comprises an emulsifier, an organic fuel in continuous phase, an oxidizer salt solution in discontinuous phase, and a buffering agent comprising a low molecular weight amine. The low molecular weight amine is preferably an alkylamine or alkanolamine having carbon chain lengths of from 2 to 5 and is more preferably diethanolamine. The buffering agent is present in the buffered emulsion blasting agent in a weight percent that is preferably within a range of from approximately 0.1% to 5%, more preferably within a range of from approximately 0.5% to 1%, and most preferably approximately 0.75%.
problem: Stabilizing an emulsion blasting agent for use in reactive environments (e.g., sulfide ores) without compromising detonation performance.
constraint: Buffer concentration must be optimized to stabilize the emulsion without interfering with the oxidizer-fuel reaction kinetics during detonation.
mechanism: Incorporating a low molecular weight amine buffer to stabilize the emulsion by controlling pH and preventing premature reaction between oxidizer and fuel phases, maintaining phase separation and reactivity.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a low molecular weight amine buffer to stabilize the emulsion by controlling pH and preventing premature reaction between oxidizer and fuel phases, maintaining phase separation and reactivity.

abstract: A tortilla counter-stacker (10) having a canister (12) which has a canister side (12C) having a horizontal canister side slot (12CA) disposed therein. A stacker (16) is positioned adjacent to the canister (12). The stacker (16) has a stacker cylinder (16A) having a movable stacker cylinder piston (16AA) attached at a front distal end to a rear distal end of a horizontal stacker cylinder piston plate (16AAA) which inserts and retracts through the canister side slot (12CA). A lift (18) is positioned directly below the canister (12). The lift (18) has a lift cylinder (18A) having a lift cylinder piston (18AA) movably positioned therein. The lift cylinder piston (18AA) has a horizontal lift cylinder piston plate (18AAA) securely attached to a top distal end thereof. An upper conveyor (20) is horizontally positioned in alignment with the canister top (12T). The upper conveyor (20) has a rotatable upper conveyor belt (20A) upon which incoming tortillas (28C) are placed. A lower conveyor (22) is positioned between the lift (18) and the canister (12). The lower conveyor (22) has a lower conveyor left belt (22AL) and a lower conveyor right belt (22AR) synchronically rotatably about the lift (18). A photoelectric eye (24) and counter (26) are electrically connected thereto.
problem: Automatically counting and stacking discrete items (e.g., tortillas) in a controlled, repeatable manner during high-speed production.
constraint: Timing synchronization between the lift, conveyors, and sensor must balance speed (throughput) with accuracy (preventing misalignment or double-counting).
mechanism: Synchronizing a lift mechanism (with a piston plate) and dual conveyors to alternately receive, lift, and stack items via a photoelectric sensor-triggered counter, ensuring precise alignment and incremental stacking.
mechanism_raw: Synchronizing a lift mechanism (with a piston plate) and dual conveyors to alternately receive, lift, and stack items via a photoelectric sensor-triggered counter, ensuring precise alignment and incremental stacking.

abstract: An open-end spinning machine comprises a plurality of adjacently arranged spinning aggregates. Each spinning aggregate consists essentially of a rotor unit comprising a spinning rotor, and an opening unit for opening a fed sliver into single fibers. The opening unit and the rotor unit each comprise a plurality of components. In order to modernize the open-end spinning machine, at least one of the above mentioned components is replaced by at least one modernized component in such a way that the efficiency of the spinning aggregate is improved.
problem: Modernizing legacy industrial machinery (e.g., spinning aggregates) to improve efficiency without full replacement of the entire system.
constraint: Modernized components must maintain functional compatibility with legacy parts to avoid systemic disruption while delivering measurable efficiency gains.
mechanism: Replacing individual components of a spinning aggregate with modernized equivalents (e.g., upgraded rotors or opening units) to incrementally enhance performance while retaining compatibility with existing infrastructure.
mechanism_raw: Replacing individual components of a spinning aggregate with modernized equivalents (e.g., upgraded rotors or opening units) to incrementally enhance performance while retaining compatibility with existing infrastructure.

abstract: An indirect luminaire having a housing with a top opening and a light source in the housing is provided with an exposed lens reflector system positioned over the top opening of the housing for receiving and redirecting source light from a position above the light source. The lensed reflector system includes an outer refracting lens element having a lens surface observable from below the luminaire and a substantially diffuse reflector substrate for the lens element. This system produces a light distribution pattern substantially governed by the internal reflection and refraction characteristics of the lens element and controlled brightness characteristics on the observable lens surface substantially governed by the diffuse reflection characteristics of the reflector substrate. A lens tower is suitably provided for holding the lensed reflective system in its operative position over the top opening of the luminaire housing. Preferably, the lens tower provides the diffuse reflector substrate for the lensed reflector system, with the lens element being removably attached to the lens tower so that the lens element can be readily replaced.
problem: Controlling both light distribution pattern and surface brightness in an indirect luminaire without compromising either characteristic.
constraint: Balancing the lens element's refractive properties with the reflector substrate's diffuse characteristics to avoid trade-offs between light distribution and brightness control.
mechanism: Combining two optical elements with distinct functional roles: one element governs light distribution through controlled refraction and internal reflection, while a second element governs surface brightness through diffuse reflection, where their physical interaction enables independent optimization of each optical property without mutual compromise.
mechanism_raw: Combining a refracting lens element (governing light distribution via internal reflection/refraction) with a diffuse reflector substrate (governing surface brightness via diffuse reflection), where the two components independently control distinct optical properties through their physical interaction.

abstract: In the pulling of a single crystal, hitherto, it is difficult to reduce the OSF density while the deformation rate is held down within the tolerance, so that it is difficult to improve the quality and productivity. In the present invention, a deviation from a true circle in each part of a single crystal S.sub.n-1 which was pulled in the preceding batch is found and the pulling speed pattern f.sub.pn-1 (L.sub.1) in the preceding batch is updated (f.sub.pn (L.sub.1)) before a single crystal S.sub.n is pulled, in order to pull the single crystal as fast as possible so that the OSF density is small while the deviation is within the tolerance.
problem: Reducing OSF density in single crystal pulling while maintaining acceptable deformation rates and dimensional tolerances.
constraint: Maintaining dimensional accuracy (deviation tolerance) while maximizing pulling speed to minimize OSF density and improve productivity.
mechanism: Implementing a feedback control system that measures geometric deviations in a manufactured product, then adjusts a process parameter (e.g., speed) for subsequent production cycles to minimize defect density while maintaining dimensional accuracy within predefined tolerances.
mechanism_raw: Using a feedback loop that measures deviations from a true circle in a previously pulled crystal, then updating the pulling speed pattern for the next batch to optimize speed while keeping deviations within tolerance.

abstract: An articulated broom, comprising a joint located between a base having an attachment plane for the bristles and the end of the handle, said joint comprising a pin connected to said base and adapted to allow the rotation of a hub at the end of the handle, said hub being attached to said pin so as to provide a certain amount of friction therebetween; abutment elements of the hub being provided in a first end position in which the handle is perpendicular to the bristle attachment plane, and a second end position.
problem: Enabling a broom handle to pivot relative to the bristle base for improved cleaning access while maintaining positional stability during use.
constraint: Balancing friction torque to allow manual repositioning while preventing unintended movement during cleaning.
mechanism: A rotational joint with controlled friction torque between two connected components, combined with mechanical stops that define discrete angular positions, enabling manual repositioning while maintaining positional stability during operation.
mechanism_raw: A pin-and-hub joint with controlled friction between the handle and base, combined with abutment elements that define discrete end positions (e.g., perpendicular and angled orientations) to lock the handle in desired configurations.

abstract: A new breach filling device for plugging a hole in a structure, in particular, in a boat. The inventive device includes a container having a reservoir for holding a foaming material therein and a flexible inflatable bladder having an interior space. The interior space of the inflatable bladder is in fluid communication with the reservoir of the container to permit passage of foaming material from the reservoir of the container into interior space of the inflatable bladder. The foaming material forms a foamed material in the interior space of the inflatable bladder such that the foamed material inflates the inflatable bladder.
problem: Rapidly sealing a breach in a submerged or pressurized structure (e.g., a boat hull) without requiring manual intervention or external tools.
constraint: Ensuring the foam's expansion rate and curing time are sufficient to seal the breach before material leakage compromises the repair.
mechanism: Deploying a reactive material that undergoes volumetric expansion upon activation to inflate a flexible barrier, creating a conformal seal that adapts to irregular breach geometries through pressure-driven deformation.
mechanism_raw: Using a reactive foaming material that expands upon deployment to inflate a flexible bladder, creating a mechanical seal that conforms to the breach geometry through volumetric expansion.

abstract: A recovery device particularly useful in confined space and remote rescues. The recovery device includes a base plate, a winch coupled to the base plate, and an anchoring plate coupled to the base plate to detachably couple the base plate to an object that will support the recovery. A cord is attached to the winch to raise or lower the load to or from the recovery device or object. A guide roller assembly is coupled to the base plate to guide the cord and reduce the amount of friction on the cord that occurs when raising a load with the winch.
problem: Efficiently lifting or lowering loads in confined or remote spaces where friction and spatial constraints limit conventional winch systems.
constraint: Minimizing friction and spatial footprint while maintaining sufficient mechanical advantage for load handling in tight spaces.
mechanism: Integrating a redirection mechanism (e.g., guide rollers) into a load-handling system to alter the path of a tensioned cord, reducing frictional resistance and spatial interference while preserving mechanical advantage in constrained environments.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a guide roller assembly with the winch and base plate to redirect the cord path and reduce friction-induced resistance during load movement, enabling smoother operation in restricted environments.

abstract: A surfboard having opposed side edges disposed symmetrically about a longitudinal centerline, the surfboard including a tail section, the side edges of the surfboard along said tail section defining a generally hourglass configuration with the contours of tail section side edges approximately hyperbolic curves. In one specific embodiment, the side edges of the tail section approximate the left- and right-hand branches of a hyperbola centered on an origin lying on said longitudinal centerline. According to another aspect of the invention, the surfboard includes a pair of side fins and a tail fin attached to the bottom surface of the board. The side fins are symmetrically disposed relative to the longitudinal centerline and are so oriented that the center planes of the side fins pass through the foci of the hyperbolic side edges of the tail section.
