problem: How to coordinate the shape of a fluid boundary with the placement of control surfaces to optimize hydrodynamic interaction and flow control.
constraint: The boundary shape and control surface placement must be geometrically coupled through the mathematical properties of the curves, and the overall configuration must remain symmetric about the centerline while creating the desired flow effects.
mechanism: Using a family of curves with defined focal properties for the boundary edge shape, and placing control elements at the focal points of those curves, so that the control elements are positioned where they optimally interact with the flow patterns generated by the boundary shape. The geometric relationship between the curve's focal properties and the control element placement determines the optimal positioning of control elements relative to the flow-shaping boundary.
mechanism_raw: Using hyperbolic curves for the boundary edge shape and placing control surfaces (fins) at the geometric foci of those curves, so that the fins are positioned where they optimally interact with the flow patterns generated by the boundary shape. The mathematical properties of the hyperbola (foci) determine the optimal placement of control elements relative to the flow-shaping boundary.

abstract: An apparatus for driving an electroluminescence device by supplying an alternating current to the electroluminescence device, the apparatus having: a direct voltage source; a constant voltage control device for generating a direct current having a constant voltage on the basis of an output of the direct voltage source; a constant current control device for generating a direct current having a constant current on the basis of the output of the direct voltage source; a selecting device for selecting either one of the direct current having the constant voltage and the direct current having the constant current; and a converting device for converting the selected direct current to the alternating current to be supplied to the electroluminescence device.
problem: How to drive different types of loads that may require either constant voltage or constant current power delivery, using a single adaptable power supply architecture.
constraint: The system must be able to generate both constant voltage and constant current from a single source, and must include a selection mechanism that can switch between modes without disrupting operation.
mechanism: Providing both a constant voltage regulation path and a constant current regulation path from a common power source, then using a selection mechanism to choose which regulation mode to apply based on the load's requirements, followed by converting the selected DC output to the required AC form for the load.
mechanism_raw: Providing both a constant voltage regulation path and a constant current regulation path from a common power source, then using a selection mechanism to choose which regulation mode to apply based on the load's requirements, followed by converting the selected DC output to the required AC form for the load.

abstract: A cleaning and waste management system comprises a cleaning chamber substantially isolatable from the ambient and including at least one openable closure for accomplishing said isolation, the cleaning chamber for accommodating objects to be cleaned being connected to a collector for waste and contaminants from cleaning, and a cleaning member insertable into the chamber without substantially affecting the isolation of the interior of the cleaning chamber from the ambient. The cleaning member generates superheated vapor such as steam and to dispense such superheated vapor directed to an object to be cleaned so that the object may be hand-held in the cleaning chamber.
problem: How to perform work (cleaning) inside an environmentally isolated chamber while maintaining the isolation barrier, without requiring the chamber to be opened or broken into.
constraint: The cleaning member must be insertable and functional without breaking the environmental isolation of the chamber, and the chamber must maintain its isolation while accommodating the cleaning operation.
mechanism: Designing a chamber with isolation closures and a working member that can be inserted into the chamber through a sealable interface without substantially affecting the isolation of the chamber interior from the ambient environment. The working member generates and directs a treatment medium at the object being treated while remaining isolated from the outside.
mechanism_raw: Designing a chamber with isolation closures and a cleaning member that can be inserted into the chamber through a sealable interface without substantially affecting the isolation of the chamber interior from the ambient environment. The cleaning member generates and directs superheated vapor at the object being cleaned while remaining isolated from the outside.

abstract: A tufting needle is disclosed. The needle has a shank (1) and a stem (2). The needle has a lower eye (4) in the stem (2) which is close to the tip (3) and an upper eye (6 in FIG. 1, and 15 in FIG. 2), and a thread-guiding groove (7) on one side running along the stem (2) and connecting the eyes (4 and 6 in FIGS. 1, and 4 and 15 in FIG. 2). The needle also has a transitional segment (5 in FIG. 1, and 14 in FIG. 2) between the lower end of the shank (1) and the upper end of the stem (2). The stem is offset with respect to the shank (1) but runs parallel thereto; the upper eye (6 in FIG. 1, and 15 in FIG. 2) is in the transitional segment (5 in FIG. 1 and 14 in FIG. 2) and is aligned with the thread-guiding groove (7).
problem: How to route a flexible element (thread) through a mechanical needle structure in a controlled path that allows the element to enter and exit at different positions while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: The stem must be offset from the shank but remain parallel, and the groove must connect the two eyes while the upper eye is positioned in the transitional segment between shank and stem.
mechanism: Using an offset geometry where a secondary element is displaced from the main axis but runs parallel to it, with a first engagement point near the tip and a second engagement point in the transitional segment, connected by a guiding channel along the secondary element. The offset creates a controlled path that guides a flexible element from the second engagement point through the channel to the first engagement point, allowing the element to follow a specific trajectory through the structure.
mechanism_raw: Using an offset stem geometry where the stem is displaced from the main shank axis but runs parallel to it, with a lower eye near the tip and an upper eye in the transitional segment, connected by a thread-guiding groove along the stem. The offset creates a controlled path that guides the thread from the upper eye through the groove to the lower eye, allowing the thread to follow a specific trajectory through the needle.

abstract: A wafer polisher head drive includes a head drive housing; a head portion extending from the housing for mounting an unpolished wafer when the head drive housing and head portion are in a horizontal orientation; a pivot mechanism extending from the head drive housing for pivoting the head drive housing and the head portion from the horizontal orientation to a vertical orientation juxtaposed to a transverse vertical portion of a continuous rotating polishing belt; a drive in the housing for moving the head portion and a mounted wafer outwardly from the housing against the transverse vertical portion of the rotating polishing belt; and a drive in the housing for rotating the head portion and the mounted wafer. The head drive housing may be pivoted from the vertical orientation in a sweeping arc extending perpendicularly from the belt transverse vertical portion or in a swinging arc extending parallel from the belt transverse vertical portion. The pivot mechanism includes a hollow shaft connected to said head drive housing; and a motor, gearbox and a ball screw and nut assembly in driving connection between the gearbox and the hollow shaft for transversing in a direction parallel to the belt.
problem: How to position and operate a working head against a vertical surface from a stowed orientation, with coordinated multi-axis motion including pivoting, transverse movement, and rotation.
constraint: The pivoting, transverse movement, and rotation must be coordinated so that the head can engage the surface from the stowed position and perform work while maintaining proper contact pressure and orientation, with the sweep direction selectable between perpendicular and parallel to the surface.
mechanism: Using a pivot mechanism to swing the head from a stowed orientation to a working orientation juxtaposed to the surface, then using a drive system to move the head outward against the surface while simultaneously rotating the head and workpiece. The pivot mechanism uses a hollow shaft with actuation components to achieve transverse movement, and the head can sweep in different directional arcs for varied positioning.
mechanism_raw: Using a pivot mechanism to swing the head from a horizontal stowed orientation to a vertical working orientation juxtaposed to the surface, then using a drive system to move the head outward against the surface while simultaneously rotating the head and workpiece. The pivot mechanism uses a hollow shaft with motor, gearbox, and ball screw/nut assembly to achieve transverse movement, and the head can sweep in different directional arcs (perpendicular or parallel to the surface) for varied positioning.

abstract: In a method for eliminating residual oxygen contaminations from crucible-drawn silicon wafers, a number of trenches are etched into the front side of a crucible-drawn silicon wafer and that the silicon wafer is subsequently tempered at approximately 1100.degree. C. As a result of the extremely large surface area in the front side of the silicon wafer, oxygen contaminants can effectively diffuse out. After the oxygen drive-out has ensued, the trenches are filled bubble-free with epitaxially deposited silicon and the active structures are processed into the front side.
problem: Removing residual oxygen contaminants from silicon wafers without damaging active structures.
constraint: The trenches must be filled bubble-free with epitaxial silicon after diffusion, requiring precise deposition to avoid defects in the active structures.
mechanism: Create a textured surface with increased surface area to enhance contaminant removal via diffusion during a high-temperature treatment, followed by a deposition process to restore structural continuity.
mechanism_raw: Etching trenches into the wafer surface to create an extremely large surface area, enabling oxygen contaminants to diffuse out more effectively during high-temperature tempering. The trenches are later filled with epitaxially deposited silicon to restore structural integrity.

abstract: A plurality of tube shields interlock with each other to protect the weld of a securement s strap used to secure the shields to a tube of a power plant. The tube shield comprises a semi-cylindrical longitudinally extending tube member terminating at a first and second end. The first end is provided with a tongue portion and a stepped portion. The second end is provided with a flanged portion and a pair of longitudinally extending bayonets. A securement strap is wound about a tube to be protected and the tongue portion of the tube shield. Each end of the securement strap is then welded to the tongue portion. A second tube shield is then placed adjacent to the first tube shield. The flanged portion of the second tube shield overlaps the tongue portion, securement strap, and stepped portion to provide protection from the hostile environment of the boiler. The bayonets are inserted between the boiler tube and the securement strap and provide a wedge-like interlocking assembly to securely fasten each tube shield to one another and to the boiler tube. Successive tube shields may be utilized to protect any desired length of tubing.
problem: Protecting welds and boiler tubes from a hostile environment while allowing modular coverage of any desired length.
constraint: The interlocking design must maintain structural integrity under thermal and mechanical stress while allowing easy installation and extension along tubing.
mechanism: Use interlocking components with overlapping and self-fastening features to form a continuous protective barrier that extends modularly without additional fasteners.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking tube shields with overlapping flanges, tongues, and bayonet wedges that create a self-fastening, layered barrier. Successive shields interlock to form a continuous protective assembly without additional fasteners.

abstract: An equine saddle pad for use in direct contact with the animal's hide and hair is constructed from a mat of piled polymer filaments extruded into an elongated continuity of about 1/2 inch thickness having 65% to 80% void volume within a thermally bonded matrix of approximately 10 mil to 30 mil diameter filaments. In one alternative embodiment of the invention, a hinge band of reduced thickness and void volume is heat formed along the pad center to divide the pad into two substantially symmetric leaves. Another alternative embodiment comprises a unitized overlay of the polymer filament pad by a dissimilar material such as neoprene foam, felt, woven nylon, woven or knitted polyester, cotton, wool or linen.
problem: Providing cushioning, breathability, and structural support in a saddle pad that contacts an animal's hide directly.
constraint: The void volume and filament diameter must be optimized to maintain structural support while enabling sufficient airflow and comfort.
mechanism: Form a mat of filaments with controlled void volume and thermal bonding to balance cushioning, airflow, and structural support, with optional flexible elements for customization.
mechanism_raw: A mat of piled polymer filaments with controlled void volume (65-80%) and thermal bonding creates a balance between cushioning and airflow. Optional hinge bands or overlays allow customization of flexibility and material properties.

abstract: The present invention relates to an arrangement for a locking mechanism comprising a lock bolt spring-assisted in the intended direction of locking, which is contained inside a lock casing connected to a plate capable of attachment along the side of a door. An actuating arm projects laterally form said lock bolt and capable of actuation by means of a handle connection extending through a door of the intended kind and a handle projecting on either side of the door. A pivoting follower acts between said handle and actuating arm for the purpose of actuating the actuating arm and the lock bolt. The arrangement has a lock component capable of being caused to move in a linear direction arranged in such a way as to be capable of displacement by means of a pivotally mounted lock component carrier. This is attached to a lock cylinder connected to any side/sides of the lock and the door in question and capable of being turned by means of a key, so as to be moved between a locking position for locking the actuating arm and an opening position for releasing the actuating arm. The lock component is capable of interacting for this purpose with a stop on the actuating arm in the locking position. A spring-assisted stop component is also capable of interacting with the lick component for the purpose of retaining it in the withdrawn opening position enabling the bolt to be displaced, and in the extended locking position for the purpose of retaining the bolt in the locking position through interaction with the lock component.
problem: Creating a secure, dual-sided door lock that can be actuated from both sides while maintaining locking reliability.
constraint: The mechanism must ensure synchronized operation between the handle, lock cylinder, and bolt while preventing unintended disengagement under load.
mechanism: Implement a spring-assisted locking system with a pivoting follower and linearly displaceable component that engages stops to synchronize actuation and retain the lock in position.
mechanism_raw: A spring-assisted lock bolt interacts with a pivoting follower and a linearly displaceable lock component. The lock component engages stops on the actuating arm to lock or release the bolt, with a spring-assisted stop component retaining the lock in either position.

abstract: A timepiece for measuring the lifetime of a personal life time event (e.g., marriage, birth, the start of a career) from the moment of occurrence of the personal life time event. The timepiece comprises a housing and a timer contained in the housing. The timer is configured for measuring the elapsed time of the personal life time event from the moment of occurrence. The timepiece includes a starting mechanism for causing the timer to start measuring the elapsed time from the moment of occurrence. The timepiece includes a display for displaying the elapsed time. The timepiece may be implemented digitally, and include a processor programmed to measure the elapsed time. Memory would also be provided for storing data associated with the personal life time event, including the time of occurrence of the event. A keypad would also be provided for entering and changing the stored data. The memory may include a non-volatile memory component in which is stored the time of occurrence of the personal life time event. The non-volatile memory would ensure recovery of the elapsed times in case of a power failure or some other event which causes loss of elapsed times.
reason: The patent describes a timepiece with standard components (timer, display, non-volatile memory) for tracking elapsed time. The mechanism is a straightforward application of existing timekeeping and data storage technologies without a novel causal principle.

abstract: A steam generator comprises a chamber having an inlet for water and an outlet for steam. Disposed in the chamber are first and second sets of interleaved electrodes, connected to respective poles of an electrical supply. The electrodes have tapered planar surfaces extending adjacent one another, with a cross sectional area which increases in a direction away from the inlet for water. The electrodes also have multiple apertures formed in the planar surfaces. The chamber is tapered complementally to the shape of the electrodes, and is mounted within a primary reservoir. The inlet for water is in liquid communication with the interior of the primary reservoir and the level of the liquid in the primary reservoir is maintained constant.
problem: Efficient steam generation in a chamber with controlled water levels
constraint: Balancing electrode geometry to maximize thermal interaction without compromising structural integrity or water flow consistency
mechanism: A tapered electrode structure with progressively increasing cross-sectional area and distributed openings is positioned within a chamber to maximize thermal interaction surface area while maintaining fluid distribution uniformity and structural alignment, thereby enabling efficient energy conversion with controlled fluid levels
mechanism_raw: Tapered interleaved electrodes with increasing cross-sectional area and apertures enhance heat transfer surface area and fluid distribution, while a complementary chamber geometry maintains structural alignment and water level stability
residual_terms: ["electrode", "cross-sectional area", "apertures", "thermal interaction", "chamber geometry", "structural alignment", "water level stability"]

abstract: An athletic equipment drying rack comprises a leg assembly which is operable between an open freestanding condition and a relatively more compact closed condition, and a torso assembly adjustably connected to the leg assembly. The torso assembly includes a transversely extending shoulder member, a pair of foldable arms, and a helmet member vertically extendable from the shoulder member. In a first embodiment, the torso assembly is pivotally connected to the leg assembly by a hinge for folding along a transversely extending axis between a drying position and a storage position. In a second embodiment, the torso assembly is connected to the leg assembly by a pair of vertical side rails engaging a transversely extending upper member of the leg assembly, whereby the torso assembly may be moved vertically relative to the leg assembly between a drying position and a storage position.
reason: The mechanism is a specific mechanical design for a drying rack, relying on hinges and rails for folding/adjustment. While functional, it lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond the product's physical structure.

abstract: An applicator for temporarily masking stains on clothing includes a canister having an chamber for containing fluid, a water based, stain masking solution disposed within the chamber of the canister, and a brush or a spray head applying the stain masking solution from the chamber of the canister on a stain requiring masking. The stain masking solution covers the stain so that the stain is substantially concealed. The canister has an elongate annular wall having an open end at one end thereof, and an end wall closing the other end of the annular wall. Preferably, the stain masking solution consists of: resin--approximately 10.0 percent by weight; isopropanol--approximately 15.0 percent by weight; water--approximately 55.0 percent by weight; titanium dioxide--approximately 15.0 percent by weight; and ammonia--approximately 5.0 percent by weight.
reason: The solution is a specific chemical composition for stain masking, which is a material feature rather than a functional mechanism. No causal relationship explains how the mechanism produces the effect beyond ingredient properties.

abstract: A peripheral assembly system which can be arranged in a decentralized manner, including a basic assembly (1) and at least one expansion module. The basic assembly (1) has integrated input/output units (4, 5) of, for example, 16 or 32 bits as well as an expansion connection (7). Via the expansion connection (7), the basic assembly (1) can be expanded, in a fine-tuned manner, with expansion modules, modules having channels numbering not more than 2.
problem: Decentralized expansion of input/output capabilities in a modular system
constraint: Limiting channel count per module to ensure interoperability and prevent overloading the basic assembly's expansion interface
mechanism: A base unit provides a standardized expansion interface that accepts interchangeable modules, each containing a limited number of communication channels, allowing incremental capability scaling while preserving system-wide interoperability and preventing interface overload
mechanism_raw: Modular expansion via limited-channel modules connected to a basic assembly allows fine-tuned scalability while maintaining compatibility through standardized expansion connections

abstract: This invention relates to a fire barrier which includes a functional combination of at least one single-panel casement panel and a sliding panel which is connected or adjacent to it. The sliding panel, which can be automatically moved horizontally during normal operation, contains an auxiliary drive mechanism which, in an emergency, moves the sliding panel without an outside power source into the open position. The casement panel is moved simultaneously by a closing mechanism from its fixed or open position into the correct closed position to create or act as a barrier.
problem: Creating a fire barrier without external power during emergencies
constraint: Ensuring reliable operation without external power by relying on pre-stored energy and mechanical coordination between panels
mechanism: A mechanical energy storage element actuates a sliding barrier component to an open position while a coordinated closing mechanism simultaneously positions a secondary barrier component, using mechanical linkages to synchronize deployment and form a continuous fire-resistant seal without external power input
mechanism_raw: Stored-energy auxiliary drive moves a sliding panel to open position while a closing mechanism simultaneously positions a casement panel, using mechanical linkages to coordinate barrier formation
residual_terms: ["energy storage", "sliding panel", "closing mechanism", "casement panel", "mechanical linkages", "coordination", "fire barrier", "external power"]

abstract: A portable camp kitchen comprising a cooker unit (2) with at least one burner (3), a container member (1) adapted to contain said cooker unit (2) integrally with the latter, support means 916) rotatably mounted at ground level on said kitchen, handle means (18), container (5,10) means, lighting means (4), power supply means, movable covering means (8,9,12,13).
reason: The abstract lists components (cooker unit, container, handle, etc.) without describing a causal functional relationship that solves a specific problem. It is a static assembly of parts rather than a mechanism.

abstract: In a method of preparing soft or sticky food products for further processing, the food products are heated from below for setting a surface layer of the food products which forms a crust holding and supporting the food products during further processing. An apparatus for performing this method comprises a belt conveyor having a conveyor belt for conveying the soft or sticky food products along a path upstream of the further processing, and heating element positioned below and on both sides of the conveyor belt in the path upstream of the further processing. The heating elements heat the soft or sticky food products on the conveyor belt from below and laterally for forming a crust which is able to hold and support the food products during the further processing.
problem: Soft or sticky food products deform or lose structural integrity during processing, making them difficult to handle and shape.
constraint: The heating must be precisely controlled to form a crust without overcooking or destabilizing the internal consistency of the food.
mechanism: Controlled thermal energy applied to specific regions of a deformable material creates a rigidified boundary layer, which mechanically supports the interior during subsequent shaping or handling operations.
mechanism_raw: Heating the food from below and laterally creates a surface crust that rigidifies the exterior, providing structural support to the interior during subsequent processing steps.

abstract: An arc furnace fume collection system has a plurality of duct lines leading to a common duct that leads to a baghouse for filtering dust. The supplemental duct lines have high pressure fans, blowers, or compressors and join one of the other duct lines through a nozzle. The nozzle connection acts as a venturi to supplement the pulling power of a common exhaust fan downstream of the baghouse filter.
problem: Fume extraction systems in arc furnaces may lack sufficient suction power to effectively capture and filter particulates from high-temperature processes.
constraint: The venturi effect must be balanced with the main exhaust capacity to avoid over-pressurization or uneven airflow distribution.
mechanism: A secondary airflow system generates localized pressure differentials via fluid dynamic amplification, augmenting the primary extraction force to increase particulate capture efficiency while maintaining balanced system pressure.
mechanism_raw: Supplemental duct lines with high-pressure fans inject airflow through nozzles that act as venturis, amplifying the pulling force of the main exhaust fan to enhance overall fume collection efficiency.

abstract: An expandable intraluminal stent able to resist axial compression, comprising a body portion having a generally cylindrical structure formed by a series of interconnected bars or struts, at least one of said struts being formed of two portions having overlapping free ends; and a plurality of teeth projecting on adjacent surfaces of said overlapping free ends; whereby said stent is expanded to allow said two portions of said at least one strut to overlap at said free ends, whereby said teeth on said adjacent surfaces of said overlapping free ends of said struts engage one another to retain said stent in its expanded shape.
problem: Intraluminal stents may collapse or lose structural integrity under axial compression after deployment in a body lumen.
constraint: The teeth must engage reliably during expansion without causing tissue damage or preventing controlled deployment.
mechanism: Interdigitated structural elements with complementary engagement features self-lock upon radial expansion, creating a mechanically stable configuration that resists axial compression through positive retention.
mechanism_raw: Overlapping strut ends with interlocking teeth engage when the stent is expanded, mechanically locking the structure in its deployed shape to resist compressive forces.

abstract: A fishing reel is provided which is capable of preventing noise and rapid change in the rotational speed of the spool which take place when a casting operation is performed, controlling backlash of a fishing line by a person even if the person is not skilled in the casting operation and maintaining the distance for which the tackle can be thrown. The fishing reel having a reel body 12 having a clutch-equipped rotational-force transmission means 20 for selecting a spool free state in which the free rotation of the spool is permitted and unreeling of the fishing line is permitted and or spool operation state in which the spool is rotated and the spool winds the fishing line; a conductive member 14 provided for the spool; magnets 16 for supplying magnetic force to the conductive member provided for the reel body 12 to brake the rotation of the spool; and a spool rotational-speed control means 26 for enlarging/reducing the magnetic force of the magnets which acts on the conductive member in accordance with the rotational speed of the spool so as to control the rotational speed of the spool.
problem: Fishing reels generate noise and backlash during casting due to uncontrolled spool rotation, especially for inexperienced users.
constraint: The magnetic force must respond quickly to speed changes without introducing lag or excessive resistance that impedes casting distance.
mechanism: Variable electromagnetic damping applied to a rotating conductive element is modulated in real-time by rotational velocity feedback, producing speed-dependent resistance to stabilize uncontrolled motion and minimize energy loss.
mechanism_raw: Magnetic braking force applied to a conductive spool member is dynamically adjusted based on real-time spool rotational speed, providing variable resistance to stabilize line release and reduce backlash.

abstract: A toothbrush having an improved cleaning and abrasion efficiency, wherein the bristles are comprised of synthetic thermoplastic polymeric compositions, and contain longitudinal channels extending along the length thereof, having a depth sufficient to entrap a quantity of abrasive particles such that during brushing with a toothpaste, contact between the channel entrapped abrasive particles and the surfaces of the teeth is improved, resulting in a cleaning efficiency coefficient, CEC, above about 1.5 and, an abrasion efficiency coefficient, AEC, above about 1.5, while demonstrating suitable bristle wearability.
problem: Improving cleaning and abrasion efficiency in a toothbrush while maintaining bristle wearability.
constraint: The depth of the channels must balance sufficient particle entrapment with bristle structural integrity and wear resistance.
mechanism: Channels in flexible elements create a balance between particle entrapment and structural integrity, enhancing contact with surfaces during motion to improve cleaning and abrasion efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Longitudinal channels in bristles entrap abrasive particles, which are positioned to enhance contact with tooth surfaces during brushing, thereby increasing cleaning and abrasion efficiency coefficients.

abstract: The present invention relates to detergent compositions having a pH of at least 8.0 in a 0.5% by weight aqueous solution containing a mixture of AS and LAS surfactants and cationic surfactants of the formula: R.sup.1 R.sup.2 R.sup.3 R.sup.4 N+X.sup.- in which R.sup.1 is a hydroxyalkyl group having no greater than 6 carbon atoms; each of R.sup.2 and R.sup.3 is independently selected from C.sub.1 -C.sub.4 alkyl or alkenyl; R.sup.4 is one or mixtures of more than one of C.sub.5-11 alkyl or alkenyl; and X.sup.- is a counterion which does not substantially exchange with a hydroxide ion at 20.degree. C. in a 0.5% by weight solution of the detergent composition.
problem: Creating a detergent composition with stable surfactant interactions at high pH (≥8.0) without counterion exchange.
constraint: The counterion must remain inert under high pH conditions while the surfactant blend maintains effective cleaning performance.
mechanism: A cationic surfactant with a hydroxyalkyl group and specific alkyl chain lengths is combined with anionic surfactants, where a counterion is selected to resist hydroxide exchange under high pH conditions, maintaining formulation stability.
mechanism_raw: A cationic surfactant with a hydroxyalkyl group and specific alkyl chain lengths is combined with anionic surfactants (AS and LAS), where the counterion (X⁻) is selected to resist hydroxide exchange at 20°C, maintaining formulation stability.

abstract: A method of air jet texturing is described wherein the intensity of texturing is proposed to be increased in that an air flow exceeding Mach 2 is obtained by the design of the nozzle duct. The total opening angle of the nozzle duct (11) directly in front of the texturing zone is designed to be greater than the ideal Laval angle with an effective length which is preferably a multiple of the smallest diameter of the nozzle. This predominantly improves the quality of texturing, quite particularly at higher production rates. These can be increased into the range of 600 to 1000 m/min and higher. It has surprisingly been found that the novel nozzle core (10) can be designed so that it has all advantages of the novel invention and can be used as a substitute for prior art nozzle cores. The same applies to the complete texturing head as the novel invention can be used within the same geometric external dimensions, the same air pressure and the same quantity of air.
problem: Increasing the intensity and production rate of air jet texturing without compromising quality or requiring redesign of existing equipment.
constraint: The nozzle geometry must achieve supersonic flow while maintaining compatibility with existing air pressure, air volume, and external dimensions of prior art systems.
mechanism: A nozzle duct with an opening angle exceeding the ideal Laval angle and an effective length multiple of the smallest diameter generates supersonic airflow, enhancing fiber entanglement and texturing quality at higher speeds.
mechanism_raw: A nozzle duct with an opening angle greater than the ideal Laval angle and an effective length multiple of the smallest diameter generates supersonic airflow (Mach 2+), enhancing fiber entanglement and texturing quality at higher speeds.

abstract: A stirrup has a pair of arms, an eye on the arms for receiving a strap, and a foot on the arms for supporting the foot of a rider. The eye and the foot of the stirrup are rotatable relative to the arms. The arms define a plane and the upper surface of the foot of the stirrup is perpendicular to this plane in one terminal position of the foot of the stirrup. The foot of the stirrup can only rotate backwards from this position. The eye has an opening for a strap, and the eye is freely rotatable relative to the arms through an angle of 90 degrees to and from a position in which the opening is coplanar with the arms.
problem: Providing a stirrup design that allows controlled rotation of the rider's foot and strap attachment for safety and comfort.
constraint: Rotational movement must be directionally limited to prevent unintended disengagement while allowing sufficient adjustability for the rider.
mechanism: Rotational mounting of components on a support structure with directional constraints allows controlled movement: one component is restricted to backward rotation from a neutral position, while another rotates freely within a defined angular range to align an attachment interface coplanar with the support.
mechanism_raw: The foot and eye components are rotatably mounted on the stirrup arms, with the foot restricted to backward rotation from a perpendicular position and the eye freely rotating 90 degrees to align the strap opening coplanar with the arms.

abstract: A sewage structure in the form of a drain, inspection shaft or the like, consists particularly of one or several hollow concrete with at least one connection for a sewage pipe. The inventive sewage structure is provided at its inner wall with a contacting form region for supporting a test seal in a fluid-tight test position.
problem: Enabling fluid-tight testing of sewage structures (drains, inspection shafts) without requiring disassembly or external sealing mechanisms.
constraint: The contacting form region must maintain structural integrity of the concrete construction while providing a reliable sealing surface for test equipment.
mechanism: An integrated inner wall contacting form region provides a sealing surface within the structure, enabling fluid-tight in-situ testing without disassembly by supporting a test seal against the structure's interior.
mechanism_raw: An inner wall contacting form region is integrated into the structure to support a test seal in a fluid-tight position, allowing in-situ pressure or leak testing.
residual_terms: ["inner wall contacting form region", "test seal", "fluid-tight", "in-situ testing"]

abstract: An apparatus for and a method of bonding veneers without problems in manufacturing process even if logs, which causes disorder of veneers after dried are used. The veneer bonding apparatus for bonding veneers to each other comprises: a bonding face machining device for machining both end portions of a veneer to be bonded to bonding faces; a bonding agent applying device for applying bonding agent to at least one bonding face of the machined bonding faces; an adjusting device for adjusting a front end bonding face of a succeeding veneer to a rear end bonding face of a preceding veneer such that a face side of the preceding veneer with the applied bonding agent and a backside of the succeeding veneer with the applied bonding agent are flush with each other; and a pressurizing device for pressurizing the adjusted bonding faces to each other.
problem: Bonding veneers that become disordered after drying due to irregular log shapes, leading to misalignment and weak joints.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment of bonding faces while accommodating variable veneer geometries caused by irregular logs.
mechanism: Adjusting the relative positions of adjacent components to align their bonding surfaces before applying pressure, accommodating initial misalignment caused by variable geometries.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting the front end of a succeeding veneer to align flush with the rear end of a preceding veneer before pressing, ensuring consistent bonding surfaces despite initial misalignment.

abstract: A yarn delivery device has a casing, a delivery drum rotatably mounted on the casing, a drive belt, at least one drive wheel propelling the delivery drum, the drive wheel having a peripheral section for application of the drive belt and being provided with at least one cleaning channel extending in a peripheral direction, and at least one scrapper attached to the casing and projecting at a point of a peripheral section remaining free of the drive belt into the cleaning channel.
problem: Debris accumulation on a drive belt or wheel in a rotating system, causing slippage or wear.
constraint: Balancing scraper placement to remove debris without interfering with the drive belt's operation.
mechanism: Positioning a stationary element to engage a rotating surface's cleaning channel, removing accumulated debris during rotation without disrupting the surface's operation.
mechanism_raw: A scraper positioned to engage a cleaning channel on the drive wheel, removing debris as the wheel rotates and maintaining belt contact.

abstract: An improved method for in situ microbial filter bioremediation having increasingly operational longevity of an in situ microbial filter emplaced into an aquifer. A method for generating a microbial filter of sufficient catalytic density and thickness, which has increased replenishment interval, improved bacteria attachment and detachment characteristics and the endogenous stability under in situ conditions. A system for in situ field water remediation.
problem: Maintaining catalytic density and operational longevity of microbial filters in aquifers under dynamic environmental conditions.
constraint: Optimizing bacterial retention and replenishment rates to balance filter thickness and catalytic efficiency.
mechanism: Designing a filter with controlled microbial attachment and detachment rates to balance retention and replenishment, sustaining catalytic activity over time.
mechanism_raw: Designing a microbial filter with controlled bacterial attachment/detachment characteristics and endogenous stability to sustain catalytic activity over time.

abstract: Thermoplastic sheet comprising plasticized polyvinyl butyral has a regular pattern of ridges and channels integrally formed and arranged in each face at an angle of intersection with respect to each other of at least 25 degrees, the ridges tapering to flattened V-shaped peaks of tight radius of less than 0.0034 inch, each face of the sheet having a surface permanence of at least 70%.
problem: Creating a thermoplastic sheet with enhanced surface grip or adhesion properties for applications requiring high surface permanence.
constraint: Achieving tight peak radii (<0.0034 inch) and specific angles (≥25°) to optimize surface permanence without compromising material strength.
mechanism: Forming a regular pattern of intersecting ridges and channels with tapered peaks at specific angles to enhance surface interaction while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Forming a regular pattern of ridges and channels at intersecting angles with tapered V-shaped peaks to increase surface interaction while maintaining structural integrity.

abstract: A shaft coupling system (10) is used to connect one shaft (23) to another shaft (44). The system (10) is suited for use in the environment of a pump (11) having a motor assembly (12) and a disposable pump assembly (13). The shaft (23) is driven by a motor (15) and carries a drive coupling device (24). The shaft (44) of the pump assembly (13) carries an impeller (47) at one end and a driven coupling device (49) at the other end. The drive coupling device (24) includes lugs (55) having helical guide surfaces (57, 58) and a helical drive surface (56). The driven coupling device (49) includes fingers (64) having helical guide surfaces (66, 67) and a helical driven surface (65). When the coupling devices (24, 49) are axially engaged, the guide surfaces (57, 58 and 66, 67) may engage each other and rotate the coupling devices (24, 49) relative to each other to position the fingers (64) between the lugs (55). Rotation of the shaft (23) by the motor (15) causes the drive surface (56) to engage the driven surface (65) which not only couples the shafts (23, 44) but also axially positions the impeller (47) in the pump assembly (13). A housing (14) for the motor (15) includes pins (19) which are received in slots (39) of the pump assembly (13) to attach the motor assembly (12) to the pump assembly (13).
problem: Reliably connecting two rotating shafts in a pump system while ensuring precise axial positioning of the impeller during coupling engagement.
constraint: Ensuring helical surface geometry allows smooth engagement and disengagement while maintaining alignment under rotational forces.
mechanism: Using helical guide surfaces on interlocking components to self-align and rotate into position, enabling torque transfer and precise axial positioning under rotational forces.
mechanism_raw: Using helical guide surfaces on interlocking lugs and fingers to self-align and rotate the coupling components into position, enabling both torque transfer and axial impeller positioning.

abstract: Method for heat treating rolled stock leaving a rolling train (12), wherein the rolled stock (13) undergoes a rapid cooling treatment in a rapid cooling assembly (11) located immediately downstream of the last rolling pass, the first cooling step being followed by a temperature-equalisation step in air and at least by a second cooling treatment before being discharged and collected, the temperature-equalisation step in air and the at least second cooling treatment being set so as not to modify the surface and inner crystalline structure of the rolled stock (13) which has formed at the outlet of the first cooling treatment, the at least second cooling treatment being followed by a short segment of temperature-equalisation in air and then directly by the collection of the rolled stock (13) into compact form, such as rolls coils bundles or packs, wherein the slow cooling of the rolled stock (13) collected in compact form leads to the transformation of the crystalline structure in the stable structures. Device for heat treating rolled stock achieving the method as described above.
problem: Achieving desired crystalline structure transformation in rolled stock while preserving the structure formed during the initial rapid cooling treatment.
constraint: The second cooling treatment and intermediate temperature-equalization in air must be set so as not to modify the surface and inner crystalline structure of the rolled stock which has formed at the outlet of the first cooling treatment.
mechanism: Multi-stage thermal processing where an initial rapid cooling establishes a target microstructure, subsequent thermal steps are constrained to preserve that established structure, and a final slow cooling in a compacted configuration enables transformation to a different stable phase. The compacted arrangement reduces the cooling rate relative to earlier stages, permitting phase transformations not achievable during rapid cooling.
mechanism_raw: Staged thermal treatment where the first rapid cooling establishes a specific crystalline structure, subsequent cooling and temperature-equalization steps are deliberately constrained to not modify that structure, and final slow cooling in compact form (coils, bundles, packs) enables transformation to stable crystalline structures. The compact collection configuration slows the cooling rate sufficiently to allow different phase transformations than those occurring during the earlier rapid stages.

abstract: Several innovative systems for an aircraft, and aircraft incorporating them, are disclosed. Features include inboard-mounted engine(s) with a belt drive system for turning wing-situated propellers; compound landing gear integrating ski, pontoon and wheel subcomponents; pivotal mounting armatures for landing gear and/or propellers which provide a plurality of possible landing gear and/or propeller configurations; and a compound wing structure featuring extendable wing panels that permit the wing span of the aircraft to be nearly doubled while in flight. Aircraft incorporating such features will enjoy several safety advantages over conventional multi-engine aircraft and will be capable of modifications during flight which permit landings on any of snow, hard surfaces (runways) and water.
problem: Creating an aircraft capable of safe operation across multiple environments (snow, water, hard surfaces) without requiring separate specialized aircraft.
constraint: All configuration modifications must be achievable during flight, and the reconfigurable components must provide sufficient structural integrity and performance across all selected configurations.
mechanism: In-flight deployable and reconfigurable vehicle components using articulated mounting systems that enable selection of different operational configurations (such as landing gear and propulsion unit arrangements) during flight, combined with extendable aerodynamic surfaces that increase effective span to adapt performance across diverse operating environments.
mechanism_raw: In-flight reconfigurable aircraft components using pivotal mounting armatures that allow different landing gear and propeller configurations to be selected during flight, combined with extendable wing panels that nearly double the wing span while in flight to adapt aerodynamic performance to different operational conditions.

abstract: A method of coating a fuser member with a polymeric sheet is disclosed. Initially, the fuser member is placed in a substantially perpendicular position with respect to the polymeric sheet. The polymeric sheet is then wrapped around the fuser member such that the sheet first comes into contact with an end of the fuser member and is wrapped along the length of the fuser member from one end to the other to form a continuous layer over the fuser member. Last, the wrapped polymeric sheet is sintered to the fuser member to form a seamless coated polymer layer.
problem: Coating a fuser member with a seamless polymer layer without gaps, seams, or discontinuities.
constraint: The polymeric sheet must be wrapped continuously from one end to the other end of the fuser member to form a seamless layer without gaps or overlapping seams.
mechanism: Continuous wrapping of a polymeric sheet around a cylindrical member from one end to the other to form a seamless covering, followed by thermal bonding of the wrapped sheet to the member to create a permanent, gap-free coating.
mechanism_raw: Placing the fuser member perpendicular to a polymeric sheet, then wrapping the sheet around the member starting from one end and continuing along the entire length to form a continuous layer over the member, followed by sintering the wrapped sheet to bond it permanently to the fuser member as a seamless coating.

abstract: A solar-cell watch dial to be disposed on or above a solar cell housed in a watch, the solar-cell watch dial including an alumina of the formula Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 whose purity is at least 99.90% and exhibiting a light transmission ranging from 40 to 60%. The invention also includes a process for producing a solar-cell watch dial, which includes the steps of: mixing together an alumina of the formula Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 whose purity is at least 99.90%, an organic binder and water to thereby obtain an Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 mixture (A); drying and granulating the Al.sub.2 O.sub.3 mixture to thereby obtain a granular material (B); molding the granular material into a plate dial precursor (C); firing the dial precursor at 700 to 1500.degree. C. in atmospheric environment to thereby obtain a preliminary firing product (D); and firing the preliminary firing product at 1500 to 1800.degree. C. under a pressure of 1.times.10.sup.-2 to 1.times.10.sup.-5 torr for 1 to 10 hr to thereby obtain a solar-cell watch dial (E). The solar-cell watch dial of the present invention enables preventing the solar cell from being sighted from outside without hindering the supply of light energy to the solar cell.
problem: Creating a watch dial that conceals the solar cell from external view while still permitting sufficient light energy to reach the solar cell for power generation.
constraint: The alumina must have a purity of at least 99.90% and exhibit light transmission ranging from 40 to 60%, and must undergo specific high-temperature processing including vacuum firing at 1500-1800°C under reduced pressure.
mechanism: Use of a high-purity translucent barrier material with controlled optical transmission as a concealment layer that obscures underlying components from visual observation while permitting energy-carrying radiation to pass through, achieved through a multi-stage high-temperature processing sequence that establishes the material's optical and structural properties.
mechanism_raw: Using high-purity alumina (Al2O3, ≥99.90%) with controlled light transmission (40-60%) as a selective optical barrier that obscures visual sighting of the solar cell while transmitting light energy, achieved through a multi-step processing sequence including atmospheric firing followed by high-temperature vacuum firing that produces the required material properties.

abstract: A method to statistically process real input and output data from a color input or output device and predict the color-transfer characteristics from an arbitrary input or output signal, or from the output signal and a part of the input signal to predict the remaining part of the input signal. Real input and output data pairs and prediction-source values are prepared which are used to calculate initial values for weighted coefficients. Matrix elements and the prediction value are calculated so that the sum of the squares of a distance between the predicted output and the corresponding plurality of real output data, weighted with a weighting coefficient, is minimized. The matrix elements and the prediction value are used to recalculate the weighting coefficients.
problem: Predicting color-transfer characteristics of color input/output devices and reconstructing missing input signal components from output data.
constraint: The matrix elements and prediction values must be calculated so that the sum of the squares of the distance between the predicted output and the corresponding real output data, weighted with a weighting coefficient, is minimized.
mechanism: Iterative model refinement using paired input-output data and prediction-source values to compute initial weighted coefficients, then determining transformation parameters that minimize the weighted sum of squared deviations between predicted and actual outputs, with successive recalculation of weighting coefficients to improve predictive accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Iterative optimization using real input-output data pairs and prediction-source values to calculate initial weighted coefficients, then computing matrix elements and prediction values that minimize the weighted sum of squared distances between predicted and actual outputs, with successive recalculation of weighting coefficients to refine the predictive model.
residual_terms: ["weighted sum of squared deviations", "iterative optimization", "prediction-source values"]

abstract: A ski boot consisting essentially of a comfort liner (8), a lower shell (1) and a cuff (2) articulated to the lower shell. The cuff is provided with a strap (62) in its upper part and a lower-leg band (61) made of a material which is more rigid than the material of the cuff, these being rigidly connected to one another on the side of the boot corresponding to the inside of the foot.
problem: Providing structural support and control in a ski boot while maintaining articulation and comfort, particularly around the lower leg and inside of the foot
constraint: Balancing rigidity for support and control against articulation for comfort and natural foot movement
mechanism: Using a localized stiffening element connected to an articulating support structure so that rigidity is concentrated at high-load regions while flexibility is preserved elsewhere
mechanism_raw: Using a lower-leg band made of more rigid material than the cuff, rigidly connected to a strap on the inside of the foot, so that the rigid support is localized to the high-load inner side while the cuff can still articulate freely elsewhere

abstract: An overlock sewing machine has a movable cutter which is activated in association with rotation of a main drive shaft to cooperate with a fixed cutter provided in the same plane with an upper surface of a needle plate, to thereby cut a work while the work is being stitched. A link mechanism includes a drive link having one end rotatably connected to a mount and the other end is connected to the movable cutter and a swingable link having an arcuate guide groove extending between one end and a center axis thereof around which the swingable link is swingingly moved. The drive link has a point between opposite ends thereof operatively connected to the arcuate guide groove of the swingable link. An operating device includes an operating shaft which is operatively connected to the point of the drive shaft so that the point of the drive link may be substantially moved along the arcuate guide groove of the swingable link between said one end and center axis thereof by manipulation of an operating knob. The drive link having the point thereof moved to one end of the swingable link will be swingingly reciprocated to activate the movable cutter, and having the point thereof moved to the central axis of the swingable link will move the movable cutter to an inoperative position below the needle plate where the movable cutter is held at standstill.
problem: Need to selectively cut fabric while stitching in an overlock machine, with reliable switching between active cutting and non-cutting modes using a single drive source
constraint: The mechanism must reliably switch between cutting and non-cutting states while being driven by the same rotating main shaft, without manual intervention during operation
mechanism: Using a guided linkage system where motion of a driven element is selectively converted between reciprocating and stationary states by varying the connection point along a curved path
mechanism_raw: A link mechanism with a drive link connected to a swingable link via an arcuate guide groove; moving the connection point along the groove changes the drive link's motion from reciprocating (activating the cutter) to stationary (retracting the cutter below the needle plate)

abstract: A fire log arrangement for use in conjunction with a combustible fuel source and influences complete combustion of the combustible fuel. The fire log arrangement includes a first log and a second log. The first log and the second log define an interior face. The second log is spaced apart from the first log such that a fuel space is defined therebetween. The fuel space receives the combustible fuel therein and defines a fire chamber at a lower end thereof. The first log interior face and the second log interior face cooperate to induce the combustible fuel to fall inward between the first log and the second log thereby inducing a thorough combustion of the combustible fuel.
problem: Achieving complete combustion of combustible fuel in a fireplace or similar setting, where incomplete combustion wastes fuel and produces excess emissions
constraint: The spacing between logs must be sufficient to receive fuel and allow airflow, but close enough to induce inward fuel fall and maintain the combustion chamber geometry
mechanism: Using two cooperating surfaces with complementary interior profiles spaced to define a fuel receiving region that directs fuel inward to form a combustion chamber promoting thorough burning
mechanism_raw: Two logs with cooperating interior faces are spaced to define a fuel space; the interior faces induce fuel to fall inward between the logs, creating a fire chamber at the lower end that promotes thorough combustion through controlled fuel flow and airflow

abstract: A sorption cooling exchanger module and a process for its use in sorption cooling processes is described. The apparatus, provides high efficiency sorption cooling operations by maintaining a characteristic diffusion distance between fin plates such that the sorption cooling process can be carried out with short cycle times which increase the efficiency of the sorption cooling process and increases the specific power. The apparatus comprises an adsorption zone comprising an adsorbent layer comprising a coating of adsorbent or comprising a paper layer containing a selective adsorbent. For sorption cooling processes, the heat transfer zone is disposed in tubes disposed normal to the fin plates. The apparatus provides an opportunity to provide an adsorber/generator module having a high fin plate density per unit length of tube without the characteristic diffusion distance becoming equal to the height of the fin from the tube resulting in an improvement in efficiency.
problem: Improving efficiency and specific power of sorption cooling processes, which are limited by long cycle times and suboptimal heat/mass transfer
constraint: The diffusion distance must be optimized relative to fin geometry — short enough for fast cycles but not so short that it equals the fin height, which would reduce efficiency
mechanism: Controlling the spacing between heat exchange surfaces relative to their height to optimize mass transfer rate while maintaining thermal efficiency in cyclic sorption processes
mechanism_raw: Maintaining a characteristic diffusion distance between fin plates that is controlled relative to the fin height, enabling short cycle times for the sorption process while preventing the diffusion distance from equaling the fin height from the tube
residual_terms: ["heat exchange surfaces", "mass transfer rate", "thermal efficiency", "cyclic sorption processes"]

abstract: A miniature mosaic is disclosed that includes a support, a plurality of tesserae arranged on the support to create an image where at least a majority of the tesserae are elongate strands having cross-sectional areas of no more than 0.25 square millimeters, and an adhesive fixing the tesserae to the support. A method of making a miniature mosaic is also disclosed.
reason: This patent describes a product (miniature mosaic) made with specific materials (elongate strands with cross-sections no more than 0.25 mm²) and an adhesive. There is no causal problem-solving mechanism — it is essentially 'use small pieces to make a small image,' which is an obvious application of the basic mosaic principle rather than a novel functional relationship that produces a useful effect through a specific mechanism.

abstract: The contactless magneto-resistive angle sensing device (1) includes two sensor components (10,11) oriented at a fixed angle relative to each other, a controllable power supply (PW) to heat and maintain the sensor components (10,11) at different temperatures, a magnet (MG) producing a magnetic field (B) in which the sensor components are arranged and an evaluating device (12) to receive output signals (U1,U2) from the sensor components (10,11). Each sensor component (10,11) includes magneto-resistive resistors (MR) connected in a respective bridge (B1,B2) having input terminals (I1,I1';I2,I2') for supply of current and output terminals (O1,O1';O2,O2') for the output signal (U1,U2). In a rotating magnetic field the evaluating device (12) analyzes the output signals (U1,U2) as a function of field angle and temperature to determine a reference angle at which the output signals of the angle sensing device have a minimum temperature dependence and stores the reference angle as a zero point for subsequent angular measurements. The sensor components are then mounted on a rotatable part whose angular position is to be subsequently measured at an angular position in relation to a stationary magnetic corresponding to the reference angle.
problem: Temperature variations in magneto-resistive angle sensors introduce inaccuracies in angular measurements by altering sensor output signals.
constraint: Balancing temperature control and signal analysis to maintain accuracy while avoiding excessive power consumption or thermal stress on the sensors.
mechanism: Use multiple sensing elements maintained at distinct thermal states within a variable field, and analyze their outputs as a function of field parameter and thermal state to dynamically select an optimal reference point that minimizes environmental sensitivity, storing this as a baseline for subsequent measurements. This adaptive calibration compensates for drift by identifying a stable operating condition through comparative analysis of temperature-dependent responses.
mechanism_raw: Two sensor components are heated to different temperatures and arranged in a rotating magnetic field. The evaluating device analyzes output signals as a function of field angle and temperature to identify a reference angle with minimal temperature dependence, which is stored as a zero point for subsequent measurements. This adaptive calibration compensates for thermal drift by dynamically selecting an optimal operating point.

abstract: A knee brace for a kayak includes a structural backbone constructed of a rigid plate bent at an angle, the inside surface of the plate's curved form is lined with a resilient foam pad. The crease where the plate is bent divides it roughly into first and second portions, the first portion having a series of apertures for mounting the brace to the underside of the rearward portion of the foredeck, the second portion of the plate depending generally perpendicularly when mounted and being adapted to receive force from the inner face of the knee and lower thigh portions of a kayaker' leg. The series of apertures in the first portion of the plate is linearly arranged, but offset from the crease by 20 degrees, or so. A channel is cut out in the foam beneath the series of apertures. The first portion of the plate also includes a mating fabric patch able to be engaged with a complementary mating fabric patch which may be affixed either to the underside of the rearward portion of the kayak's foredeck, or to the underside of the tail portion of a C-shaped brace plate, if the kayak is so equipped. A round-head screw passes downward from the upper side of the rearward portion of the kayak's foredeck, and down through one of the apertures in the first portion of the brace plate to where a T-nut is engaged with the screw and holds the knee brace in place.
reason: The knee brace design is a specific product configuration for kayak mounting, relying on application-specific structural features (e.g., offset apertures, fabric patches) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism.

abstract: Disclosed is a contact structure between the bit line and the source/drain region in an EEPROM. An element region is isolated by a trench type element isolation region in a silicon substrate. The source/drain region is formed in the portion of the element region, that is surrounded by the trench type element isolation region and a multilayered gate. A silicon nitride film covers the surface of the trench type element isolation region and that of the multilayered gate, and an interlevel insulating film made from silicon dioxide is formed. A contact hole is formed in the interlevel insulating film. The source/drain region and the silicon nitride film are exposed in the contact hole. A bit line is connected to the source/drain region through the contact hole.
reason: The contact structure is a semiconductor fabrication technique specific to EEPROM devices, involving layered materials and trench isolation. It does not describe a causal mechanism applicable beyond its immediate technical context.

abstract: An apparatus for holding, organizing, selectively displaying, and storing greeting cards is generally disclosed. The apparatus provides for securing cards within an album for storage, and yet allows the recipient of the cards to selectively review the interior and exterior portions of the various cards without physically removing the cards from the album. The apparatus includes a binder having a front cover, a rear cover and a spine. The spine includes a plurality of elongated retaining members physically oriented in a parallel, opposing manner to one another, secured to the spine, and generally parallel to the longitudinal axis of the spine. The elongated retaining members are individually inserted within the interior spine of individual cards, thereby securing the cards within the binder. This arrangement allows for the selective opening of individual cards to review the interior of the cards without removing the same from the binder. Further, the binder can be closed (e.g., the front and rear covers are moved to a position wherein the two covers generally oppose one another) which provides for secure compact storage.
problem: Greeting cards need to be stored securely in an album while allowing selective review of their interior and exterior without physical removal.
constraint: Maintaining card retention and structural integrity of the binder while allowing repeated, non-destructive access to individual cards.
mechanism: Mount parallel retention elements within a binding structure, each engaging individual items to secure them while permitting independent access without disrupting adjacent items. The parallel orientation and insertion method enable selective opening by decoupling the retention of each item from its neighbors.
mechanism_raw: Elongated retaining members are mounted in parallel within the spine of a binder. These members are inserted into the interior spine of individual cards, securing them while permitting selective opening. The parallel orientation and insertion method enable independent access to each card without disrupting adjacent cards.

abstract: A seat includes a squab and a back connected to the squab. At least a substantial part of the back of the seat is arranged to undergo a rearward movement relative to an initial position of the squab of the seat. The movement comprises at least one of a pivoting movement, a sliding movement, and a bending movement. A force limiter presents a first, relatively low level resisting force to the rearward movement, at a first predetermined amount of the movement, and a second, relatively high level resisting force at a second predetermined amount of the movement.
problem: A seat back must move rearward during impact or adjustment while balancing comfort and safety through controlled resistance.
constraint: Calibrating the transition between low and high resistance to ensure safety without compromising user comfort during normal operation.
mechanism: Implement a resistance mechanism that applies a first resistance level during initial movement and transitions to a higher resistance level upon reaching a predetermined displacement threshold, dynamically adapting to the magnitude of applied force. This dual-resistance profile balances comfort and safety by modulating response based on movement intensity.
mechanism_raw: A force limiter applies a low resisting force during initial rearward movement (e.g., for comfort or minor adjustments) and switches to a higher resisting force at a predetermined movement threshold (e.g., to prevent excessive displacement during impact). This dual-resistance profile dynamically adapts to the magnitude of the applied force.

abstract: A display having a plurality of addressable pixels and a method for constructing the same. The display includes a substrate having a first conducting layer thereon. The conducting layer includes a plurality of parallel row electrodes having edges separated by insulating material. A first polymer layer constructed from one or more thin films overlies the parallel row electrodes. An insulating layer overlies the polymer layer, the insulating layer having windows therein defining pixels for the display. The insulating layer overlies the edges of the row electrodes while providing access to the first polymer layer in the area of the pixels. A second conducting layer overlies the insulating layer and includes a plurality of separated column electrodes. Each column electrode crosses a plurality of the row electrodes and is located over the windows in the insulating layer at points defining the pixels. The second conducting layer is preferably constructed by depositing a layer of photoresist over the insulating layer and patterning the layer of photoresist to provide openings extending therethrough. The openings are wider in the portion of the layer nearest to the insulating layer. This layer acts as a shadow mask for depositing a layer of conducting material. In one embodiment of the invention, a second polymer layer is located between the insulating layer and the second conducting layer. The insulating layer is preferably constructed from a layer of photoresist that is baked to cross-link the photoresist. The polymer layers include an electroluminescent material, which is preferably based on a polyfluorene.
problem: Precisely defining pixel structures in a display while ensuring proper alignment of conductive and insulating layers.
constraint: Balancing the width of shadow mask openings to ensure precise material deposition while maintaining structural integrity of the insulating layer and pixel boundaries.
mechanism: Using a patterned masking layer with variable-width openings to control selective material deposition, where the openings widen near a structural layer to balance deposition accuracy and mechanical stability of adjacent regions.
mechanism_raw: Using a photoresist layer with openings that widen near the insulating layer as a shadow mask to deposit conductive material selectively, enabling accurate electrode placement without shorting adjacent components.

abstract: An automatic debris removal system for use in combination with a pre-existing construction hoist of the type including a plurality of telescoping extension members. Such a hoist includes a carriage device which traverses the extended hoist by means of a cable/winch mechanism that is an integral component of the hoist. The present debris removal system includes a tilting dumpster or bucket which is mechanically coupled to the carriage device and is transportable from ground level to the roof under construction for carrying debris and other materials. The present system includes a detachable chute device which is attached at the base of hoist to receive debris from the dumpster which is conducted by gravity to a dump truck for disposal. The present system also includes an automatic release mechanism for dumping the contents of the bucket as it contacts the chute at the lowermost position of its travel.
problem: Automatically removing debris from elevated construction sites without manual intervention or disrupting existing hoist operations.
constraint: Integrating the system with pre-existing hoist mechanisms without requiring major modifications to the hoist's cable/winch or carriage design.
mechanism: Mechanically coupling a tilting receptacle to a lifting mechanism and using a detachable chute with a position-triggered release that disengages when the receptacle reaches a predetermined lower position.
mechanism_raw: Mechanically coupling a tilting dumpster to a hoist carriage and using a detachable chute with an automatic release triggered by physical contact between the dumpster and chute at the lowermost travel position.

abstract: A continuous furnace for baking ceramic molded parts has a heating area (14), a baking area (16) and a cooling area (18). At least one smoke gas duct (22) extends from the heating area (14) into a combustion chamber (24) and at least one hot air duct (28) leads back from the combustion chamber (24) to the heating area (14). Hot air loaded with binder fractions is extracted from the heating area at one or several spots. The combustion gases are then led into a combustion chamber where they are burned, so that a largely purified hot air may then be led back to the heating area.
problem: Efficiently managing emissions and heat recovery in a continuous furnace for baking ceramic parts with binder materials.
constraint: Maintaining consistent temperature in the heating area while ensuring complete combustion of binder fractions to avoid residual contaminants in the recycled air.
mechanism: Extracting contaminated airflow from a heating zone, combusting the contaminants in a separate chamber to purify the air, and recycling the cleaned airflow back to the heating zone to maintain thermal efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Extracting hot air laden with binder fractions from the heating area, combusting the fractions in a separate combustion chamber to purify the air, and recycling the cleaned hot air back to the heating zone.

abstract: A tool and a method employed by numismatists to extract numismatically valued coins from pockets on vinyl pages used to house and display coin collections. Tools can be machined from either plastic material or sheet steel stock, either material can be machined to identical configurations and are equal to performing desired function. Tool is machined on left segment to form a half circle, right segment is machined to a narrowed extension, on extreme right end of segment a small ridge is formed. Tool is held by placing thumb on inner surface of half circle, opposing forefinger is placed on outer surface of half circle, holding it thusly, narrowed segment is inserted into top opening of pocket, housing numismatically valued coin, engaging small ridge in recessed area of coin holder, drawing tool upward extracts coin holder.
problem: Safely extracting coins from vinyl display pockets without damaging the coins or the housing pages.
constraint: Ensuring the tool's shape and material allow precise insertion into narrow pockets while providing sufficient mechanical advantage for extraction without slippage.
mechanism: Designing a tool with a gripping portion for leverage, a narrowed insertion segment for accessing confined spaces, and a protrusion to engage recessed features of a target object for controlled extraction.
mechanism_raw: Designing a tool with a half-circle grip for leverage, a narrowed extension for insertion into pockets, and a small ridge to engage recessed areas of coin holders, enabling controlled upward extraction.

abstract: A geometrical game of strategy for two or more players in which the object of the game is to form and occupy a series of continuous adjacent polygonal areas. The game is played on a two or three-dimensional playing surface having a series of lines defined thereon. The lines define numerous polygonal areas that are occupied according to predefined rules. Players are afforded sequential turns in which they may occupy an available area or pass to the next player, with players continuing taking turns until all of the areas are occupied.
reason: The patent describes a game's rules and turn-based occupation mechanics, which are abstract strategic concepts rather than a technical problem-solving mechanism with causal functional relationships applicable to other fields.

abstract: A silicon single-crystal wafer having a diameter of 6 inches or larger and improved in the dielectric breakdown strength of oxide film especially in a peripheral part thereof is provided to thereby heighten the yield of device chips produced per wafer. This wafer has no crystal defects with regard to the dielectric breakdown strength of oxide film in its peripheral region which extends from the circumference and accounts for up to 50% of the total area, in particular which extends from the circumference to a circle 30 mm apart from the circumference.
