problem: Automatically aligning and dispensing a straw from a beverage container when the container is manipulated (e.g., tilted).
constraint: Ensuring the straw moves reliably into alignment without spilling contents, while maintaining stability during normal container use.
mechanism: A mass-responsive element coupled to a dispensing member shifts position in response to orientation changes of a container, aligning the dispensing member with an orifice. A buoyancy or gravitational force then elevates the dispensing member through the orifice once alignment is achieved.
mechanism_raw: A weighted or buoyant member attached to the straw responds to container orientation changes, moving the straw into alignment with the orifice. Buoyancy or gravity then elevates the straw through the orifice once aligned.

abstract: A fiber web is formed by the airlay technique on a web forming and transport surface by dispersing and projecting individualized fibers onto said surface by means of a flow of air, and the fibers are subjected to a carding operation prior to being inserted into the flow of air. According to an essential characteristic of the invention, action is taken on the fiber feed rate by means of one or more regulator systems between the carding operation and the insertion of the fibers into the air flow so as to make said fiber feed rate more regular. In a preferred variant of the invention, a regulator system comprises at least a combing cylinder which is designed to be rotated to have a circumferential speed that is strictly less than that of the carding cylinder and that rotates in a direction of rotation that is opposite to that of the carding cylinder, and that is coated on its periphery with a covering whose teeth or spikes point backwards, i.e. in the opposite direction to its direction of rotation.
reason: The patent describes a specific fiber web formation process using carding and a combing cylinder with tailored speed and direction. The mechanism is highly specialized to textile manufacturing and does not generalize to other fields.

abstract: A method for treating infectious organic waste material such as dewatered sewage sludge, mixed organic wastes and animal waste. The method includes mixing the infectious organic waste material with a comminuted organic fibrous material to provide a reaction mixture. An oxidizing agent is an optional additive. The reaction mixture is heated in a hyperbaric reactor vessel at an elevated pressure and temperature for a time sufficient to create saturated steam and to produce a substantially denatured product containing inactivated pathogenic agents. The denatured product is dehydrated to produce a free-flowing solid product that may be used in various agricultural, industrial or commercial applications. Odor is controlled so that malodorous compounds are not released to the atmosphere.
problem: Safely inactivating pathogenic agents in infectious organic waste while controlling odor emissions during disposal.
constraint: Balancing pressure, temperature, and duration to ensure complete pathogen inactivation without releasing malodorous compounds or degrading the structural integrity of the final product.
mechanism: Combining organic waste with a fibrous matrix to form a reaction mixture, then applying controlled thermal treatment under elevated pressure and temperature to generate saturated steam that inactivates pathogens through protein denaturation, followed by dehydration to produce a stable solid product with reduced volatile emissions.
mechanism_raw: Combining waste with fibrous material to form a reaction mixture, then heating under elevated pressure and temperature to generate saturated steam that denatures pathogens, followed by dehydration to produce a stable solid product.

abstract: A device comprises a solid support and multiple immobilized agents for protein detection is described. The immobilized agents are mainly proteins, such as antibodies and recombinant proteins. The immobilized agents can be synthesized peptides or other small chemicals. Agents are individually deposited in a predetermined order, so that each of the agents can be identified by the specific position it occupies on the support. The immobilized agents on the solid support retain their protein binding capability and specificity. Methods employing the device are extremely powerful in screening protein expression patterns, protein posttranslational modifications and protein--protein interactions.
problem: Efficiently detecting and identifying multiple proteins or protein interactions in a single assay without cross-contamination or ambiguity.
constraint: Maintaining the functional specificity and binding capability of immobilized agents while ensuring precise spatial deposition and minimal cross-reactivity between adjacent agents.
mechanism: Immobilizing distinct binding agents at predetermined spatial positions on a solid support, enabling positional encoding to identify each agent and its binding activity through spatially resolved detection without cross-reactivity between adjacent positions.
mechanism_raw: Immobilizing distinct binding agents (e.g., antibodies, peptides) at predetermined spatial positions on a solid support, enabling positional encoding to identify each agent and its binding activity.

abstract: A lightening multiple-fold automatic umbrella comprises: a central shaft consisting of a plurality of tubes telescopically engageable with one another; a rib assembly having at least a top rib and a stretcher rib pivotally secured to an upper notch on the central shaft and a lower runner slidably held on the central shaft for securing an umbrella cloth on the rib assembly; an opening spring retained within the central shaft for opening the umbrella; a drag rope retained between the central shaft and the lower runner for pulling the lower runner as upwardly moved when opening the umbrella and extending the rib assembly; and a control module embedded in a grip of the central shaft normally locking the lower runner when closing the umbrella for folding the rib assembly; and operatively unlocking the lower runner when opening the umbrella for extending the rib assembly. By these mechanisms, a multiple-fold automatic umbrella will be produced for quick assembly and convenient operation or maintenance.
problem: Enabling rapid, reliable, and maintenance-friendly deployment and retraction of a folding umbrella mechanism.
constraint: Synchronizing mechanical locking/unlocking actions with the telescoping motion of the shaft and rib assembly to ensure smooth operation without jamming or unintended deployment.
mechanism: Using a control module to selectively lock or unlock a slidably engaged component on a central shaft, synchronizing mechanical actuation with telescoping motion of a rib assembly via coordinated tension and spring forces to enable smooth deployment or retraction.
mechanism_raw: Using a control module embedded in the grip to lock or unlock a slidably held lower runner on the central shaft, which coordinates the movement of a drag rope and opening spring to extend or collapse the rib assembly.

abstract: The object of the present invention is to provide a gene of a protein having an enzyme activity which makes it possible to regulate or control the content of saturated fatty acids and unsaturated fatty acids in plant cells, and an enzyme protein as the expression product. There is disclosed a protein with a KASII enzyme activity which has a specific amino acid sequence, typically the amino acid sequence of a .beta.-ketoacyl-ACP synthetase II (KASII) enzyme protein derived from cyanobacterium (Anacystis nidulans) or substantially the same amino acid sequence as the one described above. There is also disclosed a KASII enzyme protein gene coding for the amino acid sequence of the above described protein. Furthermore, there are disclosed a recombinant vector which comprises said gene, and a cell into which said gene has been introduced.
problem: Regulating the ratio of saturated to unsaturated fatty acids in plant cells to improve nutritional or industrial properties of crops.
constraint: Ensuring the enzyme's activity is compatible with plant cellular metabolism and does not disrupt other essential lipid synthesis processes or cause toxicity.
mechanism: Introducing a recombinant gene encoding a specific enzyme to modulate a metabolic pathway, altering the ratio of product molecules in a biological system while maintaining compatibility with existing cellular processes to avoid disruption or toxicity.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a recombinant gene encoding a β-ketoacyl-ACP synthetase II (KASII) enzyme with specific activity to modulate fatty acid biosynthesis pathways in plant cells.
residual_terms: ["recombinant gene", "β-ketoacyl-ACP synthetase II", "metabolic pathway", "fatty acid biosynthesis"]

abstract: Oxides such as those commonly used in interlevel dielectrics may be removed employing a liquid composition containing a fluoride-containing compound and an organic solvent. Preferred compositions are substantially nonaqueous and include an anhydride. Improved methods for selective removal of oxides, especially for removal of silicon oxides where pre-exposed (or conductive metal - containing) features are present, where metal (conductive metal - contaimg) features are to be exposed by the desired oxide removal, or where the silcon oxide otherwise contacts metal (or conductive metal - containing) features are provided.
problem: Selectively removing silicon oxides from substrates in semiconductor fabrication without damaging adjacent conductive metal features.
constraint: Achieving high selectivity between oxide removal and metal preservation, particularly in complex multi-layer structures with pre-exposed or embedded conductive features.
mechanism: Applying a nonaqueous chemical composition containing a reactive etchant and a passivating agent to selectively remove target material layers while protecting adjacent conductive features through chemical passivation, achieving high selectivity in multi-layer structures.
mechanism_raw: Employing a nonaqueous liquid composition containing a fluoride-containing compound and an anhydride to selectively etch oxides while protecting exposed metal surfaces through chemical passivation.

abstract: The present invention provides a universal rolling mill in which rolls including width-variable rolling rolls can be replaced at a time even if the universal rolling mill is of a type in which a yoke is caused to recede upward. A concrete structure of the invention is the universal rolling mill including a pair of width-variable rolling rolls each of the rolls having a driving portion (housed in a support box) detachably joined to an end portion of a roll shaft on an operating side for varying a rolling width, the pair of width-variable rolling rolls being used as horizontal rolls, in which a receiving/passing device for receiving and passing the driving portion of an upper width-variable rolling roll from and to the rolling mill is mounted to a yoke for receiving reaction force of an upright roll on the operating side.
problem: Replacing width-variable rolling rolls (including their driving portions) in a universal rolling mill where the yoke recedes upward, making the upper roll's driving portion inaccessible for detachment and replacement.
constraint: The mechanism must operate within the limited space and movement range of the yoke as it recedes upward, while still maintaining structural integrity to handle reaction forces from the upright roll on the operating side.
mechanism: A transfer mechanism is mechanically coupled to a reciprocating structural component, enabling co-movement between the transfer mechanism and the structural component. This co-movement allows the transfer mechanism to receive and pass a removable functional element through the moving structural component, bypassing spatial constraints imposed by the component's motion path.
mechanism_raw: A receiving/passing device is mounted directly to the yoke itself, so it moves with the yoke as it recedes upward. This co-movement allows the device to receive and pass the driving portion of the upper width-variable rolling roll from and to the rolling mill, enabling replacement without complex disassembly of the yoke or mill structure.

abstract: The invention relates to a method of producing a grinding roll in which a roll tire made from a highly wear-resistant bainitic cast material is applied to the basic roll body. In order to create a roll tire with particularly high reliability against fractures and with relatively high wear resistance and compression strength, the roll tire is produced from a ductile bainitic spheroidal graphite cast material having a breaking elongation of approximately 0.1 to 2.5% and a compression strength of approximately 1,000 to 1,800 Mpa.
reason: The patent describes a material selection (ductile bainitic spheroidal graphite cast material with specific mechanical properties) rather than a functional mechanism. There is no causal operational principle described — it simply specifies material composition and property ranges to achieve desired outcomes.

abstract: A method for determining the appropriate hole parameters to achieve the desired airflow in a swirler with as-cast air jet holes includes the steps of determining the desired airflow through the holes and selecting a hole angle for the holes. Next, the ratio of the hole exit area to the hole inlet area is calculated based on the desired airflow and the selected hole angle using a regression equation. Then a value is determined for either of the hole exit area or the hole inlet area, and the other area is calculated from the known ratio. Once the hole angle, hole exit area and hole inlet area have been determined, then a swirler can be cast with as-cast holes using these hole parameters.
problem: Determining appropriate hole parameters (angle, exit area, inlet area) to achieve a desired airflow in a swirler with as-cast air jet holes, where direct measurement or iterative prototyping is impractical.
constraint: The regression equation must accurately capture the relationship between hole geometry and airflow, and the method must work with as-cast holes which have manufacturing tolerances and specific geometric constraints inherent to the casting process.
mechanism: A predictive model relates a geometric parameter ratio (e.g., exit-to-inlet area ratio) to a target performance metric (e.g., airflow) and a geometric input variable (e.g., angle). The model calculates the required ratio, from which one geometric parameter is derived and the other is computed using the known ratio, enabling parameter determination without iterative physical testing.
mechanism_raw: Using a regression equation that relates the ratio of hole exit area to hole inlet area to the desired airflow and selected hole angle. Once the ratio is calculated from the regression model, one area is determined and the other is calculated from the known ratio, enabling the swirler to be cast with as-cast holes using these parameters without iterative trial and error.
residual_terms: ["geometric parameter ratio", "target performance metric", "geometric input variable"]

abstract: A jewelry ring having a main ring with two half-ring segments, where each of the ring segments has its own design. The design of the first ring segment is more prominent than the design of the second segment and is typically displayed to an outside viewer. However, when, for security or any other reason, the wearer rotates the ring, the second half with the less prominent design is displayed, concealing the more prominent design of the first half without alerting a robber that a more prominent design is hidden.
problem: Concealing a valuable or prominent design on a jewelry ring for security purposes without alerting potential thieves that something valuable is hidden.
constraint: The concealment mechanism must be simple and non-obvious — it should not look like a security feature, and the rotation must be easy enough for the wearer but not obvious to others who might notice the ring being turned.
mechanism: A dual-sided rotatable element has two distinct surface configurations with different visual prominence. Rotation of the element switches which configuration is externally visible, allowing a less prominent configuration to conceal a more prominent configuration on the opposite side through simple manual rotation.
mechanism_raw: The ring has two half-segments with different design prominence. The wearer can rotate the ring to display the less prominent design, which physically conceals the more prominent design on the opposite side. The rotation is simple and unobtrusive, not alerting observers that a valuable design is hidden beneath.

abstract: A respirator 10 includes a compressible filter element 12, a filter element retainer 14, and a face piece 16. The respirator is unique in that the filter element 12 compresses when installed in the retainer 14, allowing a friction fit to be maintained between the filter element 12 and retainer 14. The friction fit enables the filter element 12 to be readily replaced when its service life has expired.
problem: Enabling easy replacement of filter elements in a respirator while maintaining a secure, reliable fit during use without additional fasteners or tools.
constraint: The compression must be sufficient to create a reliable friction fit during use (preventing accidental dislodging from vibration or airflow) but not so much that replacement becomes difficult or requires tools. The material must also maintain its compression properties over time and under varying environmental conditions.
mechanism: A compressible interface element is positioned between a removable component and a retaining structure. When installed, the compressible element deforms to create a friction-based retention force that secures the component during operation, while allowing manual removal by overcoming the friction force when replacement is required.
mechanism_raw: The filter element is compressible, so when installed in the retainer, it compresses and creates a friction fit through radial or axial compression against the retainer surfaces. This friction fit holds the filter securely during use but allows it to be readily removed by overcoming the friction force when replacement is needed.

abstract: An improved structure of a fitting light comprising a transparent lamp pipe integrally formed and covered with a coating, wherein, a plurality of power conductors including a common power conductor and a plurality of individual power conductors are positioned in the lamp pipe synchronically when in shaping the latter, several axial elongated grooves in same number as that of lamp strings used in the lamp pipe are disposed on the lamp pipe and are equidistantly apart from one another to each receive a lamp string; the power conductors are disposed to make every two of the power conductors including the common power conductor and one of the individual power conductors contain therebetween an axial elongated groove. The lamp pipe having been placed therein the lamp strings is shaped to have a positioning layer with a minimal diameter formed on the external periphery thereof, and to make a transparent coating of a minimal diameter cover thereon.
problem: Integrating multiple lamp strings and power conductors within a transparent lamp pipe while minimizing the overall diameter of the assembly.
constraint: The number of grooves must match the number of lamp strings, and the positioning of conductors relative to grooves must be coordinated to achieve minimal diameter for both the positioning layer and the transparent coating while accommodating all electrical connections.
mechanism: Arranging components and conductors in equidistant axial elongated grooves within a transparent structure, with each groove receiving a component and conductors positioned so that every two conductors have a groove between them, then shaping the structure to form a minimal-diameter configuration while accommodating all electrical connections.
mechanism_raw: Arranging power conductors and lamp strings in equidistant axial elongated grooves within a transparent pipe, with each groove receiving a lamp string and power conductors positioned so that every two conductors (common and individual) have a groove between them, then shaping the pipe to form a minimal-diameter positioning layer and transparent coating.

abstract: A helmet which includes a substantially rigid shell having a shell thickness defined by a substantially continuous exterior surface spaced apart from a substantially continuous interior surface. A one-piece first shock attenuating member is positioned adjacent to and in substantially in contact with portions of the interior surface of the shell. The first shock attenuating member has a first thickness and a first compression deflection. A plurality of discrete second shock attenuating members are positioned adjacent to portions of the first shock attenuating member and adjacent to and in substantially in contact with portions of the interior surface of the shell. Each second shock attenuating member has a second thickness and a second density, with the second thickness being greater than the first thickness and the second compression deflection being less than the first compression deflection.
problem: Providing effective impact protection in a helmet while managing the trade-off between initial impact absorption and distributed force attenuation.
constraint: The second shock attenuating members must have greater thickness but lower compression deflection than the first member, creating a staged attenuation profile that balances initial impact resistance with sustained force distribution.
mechanism: Implementing a staged energy absorption system with a primary member of a first thickness and compression deflection in contact with a surface, combined with secondary members of greater thickness but lower compression deflection positioned adjacent to the primary member, creating a profile where the primary member handles initial impact and the secondary members handle subsequent or distributed forces.
mechanism_raw: Using a one-piece first shock attenuating member with a first thickness and first compression deflection in contact with the shell interior, combined with discrete second shock attenuating members of greater thickness but lower compression deflection positioned adjacent to the first member, creating a staged energy absorption system where the first member handles initial impact and the second members handle subsequent or distributed forces.

abstract: An inflatable towable vehicle including a tapered hull. The hull is formed of a plurality of concentrically disposed inflatable rings with chambers which have progressively increasing diameters from the outermost ring to the innermost ring. Interior connecting webs form shared walls for the adjacent chambers, and openings in the webs allow fluid communication between the chambers so that a single inflation valve can be used to simultaneously inflate all of the chambers. When inflated, the centers of the chambers are horizontally aligned to yield a hull profile that is tapered from both the top and the bottom. The passenger cockpit is defined by the open area in from the innermost ring, and a floor including an inflatable section and a drain opening. The tapered hull acts to minimize resistance to the water or snow over which the vehicle is being towed, and results in an aesthetically appealing vehicle profile.
problem: Creating an inflatable towable vehicle with a hull profile that minimizes resistance when towed over water or snow.
constraint: The progressive diameter change from outer to inner rings must be balanced with horizontal alignment of chamber centers to achieve the desired tapered profile, while using a single inflation valve for all chambers through shared fluid communication.
mechanism: Using concentrically disposed inflatable chambers with progressively increasing diameters from outermost to innermost, connected by interior fluid pathways for shared inflation, so that a single inflation source simultaneously inflates all chambers and horizontally aligned chamber centers produce a hull tapered from both top and bottom.
mechanism_raw: Using concentrically disposed inflatable rings with progressively increasing diameters from outermost to innermost, connected by interior webs with openings for fluid communication, so that a single inflation valve simultaneously inflates all chambers and the horizontally aligned chamber centers produce a hull tapered from both top and bottom.

abstract: The system includes a confocal optical system to illuminate an object at an intended detection plane and to focus light from the object onto a pinhole. An opaque obstacle is disposed within the confocal optical system, the obstacle selected to suppress light originating outside the intended detection plane from passing through the pinhole. It is preferred that the obstacle size and location be selected to achieve a desired level of suppression. A design goal is a 100-fold reduction in background with a 10% or less loss of signal.
problem: Suppressing background light from outside the intended detection plane in a confocal optical system while preserving signal from the target plane.
constraint: The obstacle size and location must be selected to achieve a desired level of suppression (e.g., 100-fold background reduction) with minimal signal loss (e.g., 10% or less), requiring precise positioning relative to the optical path and pinhole.
mechanism: Disposing an opaque element within an optical system at a selected size and location to block light originating outside the intended detection plane from passing through a detection aperture, while allowing light from the intended plane to pass through with minimal signal loss.
mechanism_raw: Disposing an opaque obstacle within the confocal optical system at a selected size and location to block light originating outside the intended detection plane from passing through the pinhole, while allowing light from the intended plane to pass through with minimal signal loss.

abstract: A mold used for manufacturing an inorganic board and a method of manufacturing an inorganic board by employing said mold are provided in the present invention. Said mold consists of a mold part made of a fiber reinforced plastic and a metal part attached to the back of said mold part, and because of said metal part, the difference in the coefficient of thermal expansion between said mold and an inorganic board manufactured on said mold is small.
problem: Reducing thermal expansion mismatch between a mold and an inorganic board manufactured on that mold during heating processes.
constraint: The combination of fiber-reinforced plastic and metal must be engineered so that the resulting composite thermal expansion coefficient closely matches that of the inorganic board, requiring careful selection of materials and their proportions.
mechanism: Combining a first material with a second material attached to its back, where the second material adjusts the composite coefficient of thermal expansion of the combined structure to more closely match that of a target component being manufactured on the structure.
mechanism_raw: Combining a fiber-reinforced plastic mold part with a metal part attached to its back, where the metal part adjusts the composite coefficient of thermal expansion of the mold to more closely match that of the inorganic board being manufactured.
residual_terms: ["coefficient of thermal expansion", "composite structure", "first material", "second material", "target component"]

abstract: An ink jet printer with a reciprocating carriage having a circuit element with a number of electrical contacts and a fluid aperture. A print head is connected to the circuit element and has a body defining an ink inlet aperture adjacent the fluid aperture. The print head includes a number of conductive leads at least partially encapsulated by a portion of the print head body and connected to an electrical contact on the circuit element. The print head includes a die electrically connected to the leads, and connected to the body in communication with the ink inlet aperture. The leads may be formed from a leadframe, and the die may be at least partially encapsulated by the body.
problem: Maintaining electrical connectivity and fluid sealing in an ink jet print head exposed to liquid ink during operation.
constraint: Balancing fluid isolation of the electrical components with sufficient electrical connectivity and mechanical integration to the circuit element.
mechanism: Encapsulating conductive elements within a fluid-containing housing that defines an access aperture, so that the conductive elements are shielded from fluid ingress while maintaining electrical continuity through the conductive elements to an external circuit.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating conductive leads and a die within the print head body, which defines an ink inlet aperture, so that the leads are protected from fluid ingress while remaining electrically connected to the circuit element via the leads and die.

abstract: The present invention provides a dual purpose workpiece handoff station for intermediately staging a semiconductor wafer, or other workpiece, being transferred between processing stations in, for example, a Chemical-Mechanical Planarization (CMP) machine. The handoff station includes a workpiece processing surface; such as a polishing pad or buffing pad, defining a plurality of apertures for applying fluids, including water, chemicals, slurry, or vacuum, to the surface of a workpiece. In operation, a workpiece carrier moves a polished wafer from a primary polishing surface to the handoff station, and polishes, buffs, or cleans the wafer in the handoff station by rotating the wafer and oscillating the wafer across the handoff station polishing surface while pressing the wafer thereon.
problem: Intermediately staging and processing a semiconductor wafer between processing stations without interrupting its transfer or compromising its position.
constraint: Maintaining precise wafer positioning and processing efficacy during transfer while integrating fluid delivery through the apertures without disrupting the wafer's movement.
mechanism: Using a workpiece support surface with distributed apertures to apply processing fluids while simultaneously imparting multi-axis motion to the workpiece across the surface during transfer, enabling in-line processing without interrupting positional control.
mechanism_raw: Using a workpiece processing surface with apertures to apply fluids (e.g., water, chemicals, slurry, vacuum) while simultaneously rotating and oscillating the wafer across the surface during transfer, enabling polishing, buffing, or cleaning in the handoff station.
residual_terms: ["workpiece support surface", "distributed apertures", "processing fluids", "multi-axis motion", "positional control"]

abstract: A recessed canopy light having a main body positionable above an opening in a canopy sheet, a rim member in contact with the lower surface of the canopy sheet such that the sheet is sandwiched between the main body and the rim member, a lens frame below the rim member and hinged thereto, each hinge including a first member secured to the rim member and having an upwardly-open substantially semi-cylindrical female portion with an outer edge spaced below the canopy sheet by a first distance and a second member secured to the lens frame and having a truncated-cylindrical male portion engaged in the female portion, the male portion having a flat therealong such that the vertical dimension of the male portion varies between a full diameter much greater than the first distance and a truncated diameter which is at most slightly greater than the first distance, such that the male portion is non-removable from the female portion except when the lens frame is pivoted to a fully-open position beyond a vertical hanging position. Preferred embodiments include dimensioning such that deflection of the canopy sheet is necessary to allow disengagement of the hinge members.
problem: Securing a lens frame to a canopy sheet in a way that prevents accidental disengagement while allowing controlled access for maintenance or replacement.
constraint: Ensuring the hinge geometry allows secure attachment under normal use while permitting disengagement only when intentionally pivoted to a specific position, balancing accessibility with retention.
mechanism: Designing an interlocking hinge with complementary male and female geometries of varying cross-sectional dimensions, where the dimensional transition creates a retention force that prevents disengagement under normal orientation but allows release only when the attached component is pivoted beyond a threshold angle, requiring external deflection of the mounting surface.
mechanism_raw: Designing a hinge with a semi-cylindrical female portion and a truncated-cylindrical male portion, where the male portion's varying vertical dimension (full diameter to truncated diameter) creates a non-removable interlock unless the lens frame is pivoted beyond a vertical hanging position, requiring canopy sheet deflection for disengagement.
residual_terms: ["interlocking hinge", "complementary male and female geometries", "varying cross-sectional dimensions", "retention force", "threshold angle", "external deflection"]

abstract: Line coding mismatches on a transmission channel in a telecommunications network will manifest a constant error signature having a certain number of errored seconds, severely errored seconds, unavailable time and lost sync. errors upon the application of a test pattern comprising a sequence of a first, second and third octet, each repeated a prescribed number of times. The first and second octets remain constant regardless of the nature of the transmission channel, while the nature of the third octet varies according to the transmission rate of the DS0 under test and associated DS1 under test. The test pattern will reveal a line coding mismatch. In a B8ZS environment (64 Kbps clear channel capability), the pattern may be run on any DS0 channel within the DS1. In an AMI-with-ZCS environment (56 Kbps or 64 Kbps restricted), the pattern must run on either channel 1 or 24.
problem: Detecting line coding mismatches in telecommunications channels that produce consistent error signatures under specific test conditions.
constraint: Adapting the test pattern's third octet to the transmission rate and channel environment while maintaining a standardized structure for consistent error detection across different network configurations.
mechanism: Applying a structured test pattern with fixed and rate-adaptive segments to a communication channel, where the pattern's composition is configured based on channel characteristics to produce detectable error signatures that indicate coding mismatches.
mechanism_raw: Applying a test pattern composed of three octets (first and second constant, third varying with transmission rate) to reveal error signatures (errored seconds, unavailable time, etc.) that indicate line coding mismatches, with the third octet's structure adapted to the channel's environment (B8ZS or AMI-with-ZCS).
residual_terms: ["structured test pattern", "fixed and rate-adaptive segments", "communication channel", "error signatures", "coding mismatches", "channel characteristics"]

abstract: A portable device for wearing by a user and removing deposits from a surface. The device includes a first portion for delivering a fluid that is a cryogen and a second portion for overlying and dispensing the fluid onto and removing the deposits from the surface. The first portion includes a pole for hand-holding, a fitting that fluidly engages in the pole, a first valve that fluidly engages the fitting, a hose that fluidly engages the first valve, a second valve that fluidly engages the hose, a portable tank that fluidly engages the second valve and which contains the fluid which flows through the second valve when opened, through the hose, to the first valve, which when opened, allows the fluid to flow into the fitting and into the pole, and a harness that is operatively connected to the portable tank for attaching the portable tank to the back of the user or to the pole during use. The second portion includes a vessel that is inverted bowl-shaped, fluidly depends from the pole so as to allow the fluid to flow from the pole therein and be focused onto a specific and defined area, and a peripheral seal that extends around the rim of the vessel for providing temporary sealing engagement of the vessel with the surface during use so as to prevent escaping of the fluid.
problem: Delivering a cryogenic fluid to a surface in a portable device to remove deposits while maintaining controlled application and preventing fluid leakage.
constraint: Balancing portability and fluid containment by integrating the tank into a harness while ensuring the seal and vessel geometry focus the cryogen precisely without leakage during use.
mechanism: Using a delivery conduit with a controlled valve to direct fluid flow from a portable reservoir through a flexible connection to a surface-engaging vessel with a peripheral seal, where the vessel geometry focuses the fluid onto a defined area and the seal prevents escape during application.
mechanism_raw: Using a pole with a valve system to direct cryogen flow from a portable tank through a hose and fitting into the pole, which feeds an inverted bowl-shaped vessel with a peripheral seal that temporarily engages the surface to focus the cryogen onto a defined area and prevent escape.
residual_terms: ["delivery conduit", "controlled valve", "portable reservoir", "flexible connection", "surface-engaging vessel", "peripheral seal", "defined area"]

abstract: A process is disclosed for communication systems used in traffic engineering and having an earthbound transponder for each corresponding track section. The transponders transmit first data through a first path of transmission to polling machines arranged on vehicles. Based on these first data, the concerned polling machine ascertains whether second data transmitted through a second path of transmission to the polling machine are really destined for the vehicles. The signal in the second path of transmission destined for the vehicles of a section of the track is individually modulated or transmitted by a time- or frequency-multiplexing process. Depending on the selected modulation or multiplexing, coefficients are built at the emitter side which are then transmitted through the first path of transmission, extracted at the receiver side and used to demodulate or demultiplex the signal transmitted through the second path of transmission. The physical separation of the transmitted signals makes it possible to ascertain whether the signals received through the second path of transmission are destined for this section of the track or the vehicles that circulate thereon.
problem: Ensuring correct routing and demodulation of data signals in a communication system for traffic engineering, where signals must be verified as destined for specific track sections.
constraint: Physical separation of signals is required to avoid interference, necessitating dual-path infrastructure and precise coefficient synchronization between emitter and receiver.
mechanism: Employ two physically separated transmission channels: a first channel conveys control parameters and verification information, while a second channel carries modulated or multiplexed data. The control parameters are extracted from the first channel and applied to process the second channel, enabling validation of data routing and destination.
mechanism_raw: Using two physically separated transmission paths: a first path carries coefficients and verification data, while a second path carries modulated/multiplexed signals. The coefficients are extracted at the receiver and used to demodulate/demultiplex the second path, enabling verification of signal destination.

abstract: A recharge and filter assembly includes a housing with a removable recharge and filter cartridge. The housing includes a canister with a removable cover allowing access to the cartridge. The cartridge includes a filter element comprising a ring of media and upper and lower end caps. The upper end cap carries a peripheral seal which provides a fluid-tight seal with the housing canister. An annular channel is provided between an annular portion of the upper end cap and the seal. An annular support member from the cover is received in the annular channel to support the upper end cap. Latching fingers on the upper end cap and a mating ring on the cover removably couple the cartridge to the cover. The cartridge further includes a recharge canister supported by tabs on the upper and lower end caps. Fluid is recharged by inhibitor material, while particulates and other contaminants are removed by the filter media.
problem: Maintaining fluid quality in a system by simultaneously filtering contaminants and recharging with inhibitor material while allowing easy cartridge replacement.
constraint: Balancing ease of cartridge replacement with the need for a reliable fluid-tight seal and structural support during operation.
mechanism: Integrate a removable module combining a filtration component and a replenishment component within a single replaceable unit. A quick-connect interface with mechanical latching and alignment features ensures secure coupling to a housing, while sealing elements maintain fluid integrity during operation.
mechanism_raw: A removable cartridge integrates a filter element and recharge canister within a single unit. Latching fingers and a mating ring enable quick coupling to the housing cover, while an annular channel and support member ensure alignment and fluid-tight sealing during operation.

abstract: The present invention is a process for pressure treating wood and includes wood which has been pressure treated by the process. The process comprises infusion into the wood of a solution in water of an anhydride or the analogous acid of an anhydride, followed by removal of moisture from the wood and the infusion of the wood with a molten waxy solid comprising hydrocarbon paraffins or saturated fatty acids. The molten waxy solid then solidifies, filling all voids in the wood.
problem: Protecting wood from moisture ingress and environmental degradation by filling all internal voids with a solidifying protective agent.
constraint: Precise temperature control is required during wax melting and solidification to ensure complete void filling without damaging the wood structure.
mechanism: Apply a sequential treatment process: first infuse a reactive solution into a porous substrate, remove residual moisture, then introduce a molten solidifying agent. The agent solidifies upon cooling, filling internal voids and forming a continuous protective barrier against environmental exposure.
mechanism_raw: Sequential infusion of an anhydride/acid solution into the wood, followed by moisture removal and infusion of a molten waxy solid (paraffins or fatty acids). The molten material solidifies upon cooling, filling all voids and creating a moisture-resistant barrier.
residual_terms: ["anhydride/acid solution", "molten waxy solid", "paraffins or fatty acids"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for detecting improper liquid content of a metering tip of an analyzer. The method detects the content or status using radiation between 630 and 2000 nm, and comprises the steps of: a) aspirating the liquid into the tips; b) scanning the liquid; c) providing relative motion between the tip and the scanner while simultaneously scanning the liquid; d) detecting the amount of light transmitted to detector at all levels of the liquid; e) comparing the detected light with light known to be transmitted at levels of liquid free of air bubbles; and flagging the results.
problem: Detecting improper liquid content (e.g., air bubbles) in a metering tip of an analyzer to ensure accurate liquid analysis.
constraint: The wavelength range and relative motion must be precisely controlled to ensure comprehensive scanning of the liquid column and accurate comparison to baseline data.
mechanism: Illuminate a liquid column with radiation across a defined wavelength range while inducing relative motion between the liquid and a detector. Measure transmitted radiation at multiple positions and compare to reference values from bubble-free liquid, identifying deviations as indicators of improper content.
mechanism_raw: Scanning liquid in the tip with radiation (630–2000 nm) while creating relative motion between the tip and scanner. Transmitted light is detected at all liquid levels and compared to baseline values from bubble-free liquid, flagging discrepancies as indicators of improper content.

abstract: A method and device for hot-air cutting, wherein compressed air is forced into a hot-air unit in which the compressed air is heated, the hot air is then conducted through a cutting nozzle for hot-air cutting. A compressed-air unit is connected to a hot-air unit via a coupling device arranged at one end of the hot-air unit to provide the hot-air unit with compressed air. The hot-air unit is being provided at its other end with a cutting nozzle. A heating device is arranged to heat air flowing into the hot-air unit.
problem: Efficiently heating compressed air for hot-air cutting while enabling modular connection between the air supply and heating unit.
constraint: Maintaining consistent heat and airflow requires balancing thermal efficiency with the mechanical simplicity of the coupling device to avoid leaks or heat loss during operation.
mechanism: Use a modular coupling interface to connect a pressurized fluid source to a heating assembly. The heating assembly internally raises the temperature of the fluid, which is then conveyed through a delivery nozzle. A dedicated heating element maintains consistent thermal output during operation.
mechanism_raw: A coupling device at one end of the hot-air unit connects to a compressed-air unit, allowing modular assembly. The hot-air unit heats the compressed air internally, which is then conducted through a cutting nozzle. A separate heating device ensures consistent airflow temperature.

abstract: A system for instantaneously monitoring traffic congestion including a plurality of monitoring electronic devices located in motor vehicles traveling on roadways in a selected region. Each monitoring electronic device is coupled to a GPS receiver that provides physical location to a wireless modem capable of connecting to a wireless communication network. The system also includes a central computer connected to a wide area network that is able of continuously downloading physical location information from a plurality of monitoring electronic devices also connected to the wide area network. The central computer uses a traffic monitoring software program and a mapping database containing roadway information for a region and the movement information from the monitoring electronic devices to create a continuously updated traffic congestion database. Authorized users of the system are able to log onto the central computer to a portion of the database that contains specific traffic flow and congestion information. Using the system, users are also able to obtain estimated times of arrival for a specific trip, and recommendations on alternative route information. The system can also take into consideration current or anticipated events that may affect traffic congestion.
problem: How to monitor traffic congestion in real-time across a wide geographic region without dedicated infrastructure
constraint: Tradeoff between sensor density (spatial coverage and update frequency) and communication/network bandwidth costs, balanced against the need for real-time updates and the accuracy of congestion inference
mechanism: Distributed mobile sensing units (existing vehicles) continuously report their physical state (location) to a central aggregator via a communication network; the central processor combines this distributed movement data with a static spatial reference model (roadway map) to infer system-wide conditions (congestion, flow) that no single sensor could observe alone, enabling real-time database generation and user queries
mechanism_raw: Distributed mobile sensors (vehicles equipped with GPS) continuously report their physical state (location) to a central aggregator via a wireless network; the central processor combines this distributed movement data with a static reference model (roadway map database) to infer system-wide traffic conditions (congestion, flow) that no single sensor could observe alone, enabling real-time database generation and user queries

abstract: A cathode for electrolysis comprising a hydrogen-occluding material for use in an electrolytic cell partitioned by the cathode into two chambers including a reaction chamber and an electrolysis chamber. The cell is arranged so that a reactant is reduced or hydrogenated in the reaction chamber. The cathode comprises an ion exchange membrane or porous membrane. A first layer made of a hydrogen-occluding metallic palladium or a palladium alloy is formed on the reaction chamber side of the membrane. A second layer which is a porous catalyst layer made of a platinum metal black or gold is formed on the first layer. Also disclosed is an electrolytic cell using the cathode for electrolysis.
problem: How to improve electrolysis efficiency for hydrogenation or reduction reactions in a partitioned electrochemical cell
constraint: Tradeoff between hydrogen occlusion capacity (which determines how much driving gradient can be sustained) and the need for the occluding material to release hydrogen at the catalyst interface, balanced against the structural requirement of maintaining chamber separation
mechanism: A hydrogen-occluding material layer is placed adjacent to a selective barrier on the reaction side, where it selectively absorbs and concentrates hydrogen atoms, creating a concentration gradient across the barrier that drives the desired reaction forward; a catalytic interface on top of the occluding material facilitates the reaction at the interface while the occluding material prevents backflow
mechanism_raw: A hydrogen-occluding material layer (palladium) is placed adjacent to a barrier membrane on the reaction side, where it selectively absorbs and concentrates hydrogen atoms, creating a concentration gradient across the barrier that drives the desired reaction forward; a porous catalyst layer on top of the occluding material facilitates the reaction at the interface while the occluding material prevents backflow

abstract: A transducer apparatus is disclosed including a spool member having a body portion and first and second elevated regions formed on the body portion. A piezoelectric film such as a PVDF film surrounds the spool member and is spaced apart from the body portion of the spool member by an elevation of the elevated region, thereby forming a predetermined gap between the piezoelectric film and the body portion of the spool member. The predetermined gap is at least 0.1 mm and enables a predetermined resonance frequency in the piezoelectric film to control the resonance frequency of the transducer. Opposite lateral ends of the piezoelectric film are secured together such that secured ends of the piezoelectric film have substantially the same resonance frequency as a remainder of the piezoelectric film.
problem: How to control and tune the resonance frequency of a piezoelectric transducer element
constraint: Tradeoff between gap size (which determines the achievable resonance frequency range) and mechanical stability/integrity of the assembly, balanced against the need for uniform resonance frequency across the entire film including the secured ends
mechanism: A mechanical spacer with elevated regions creates a controlled gap between the piezoelectric film and the supporting body, mechanically decoupling the film from the rigid structure; this gap acts as a compliant spring element whose physical dimensions set the resonance frequency of the film independently of direct contact; securing the opposite lateral ends of the film together ensures the end portions have the same resonance frequency as the central portion
mechanism_raw: A spool member with elevated regions creates a controlled mechanical gap between the piezoelectric film and the supporting body, mechanically decoupling the film from the rigid structure; this gap acts as a compliant spring element whose physical dimensions set the resonance frequency of the film independently of direct contact; securing the opposite lateral ends of the film together ensures the end portions have the same resonance frequency as the central portion

abstract: An open-back hat (10) is provided which includes an adjustable sweatband (12), a forwardly extending bill (16), and a crown extending upwardly from the sweatband and bill in order to cover the forehead and sides of a wearer's head, while leaving a large rear open area (20). The area (20) allows pull-through of long hair and/or special hairstyles. In this manner, women or men with long hair may wear a baseball-type hat without fear of hairstyle damage.
reason: The open-back hat is a static geometric accommodation — leaving a rear opening so long hair can pass through without compression. There is no causal mechanism involving dynamic interaction, feedback, or a tradeoff between competing functional requirements; it is simply a product feature based on shape.

abstract: In order to be able to process in an economical manner different iron carriers in varying quantitative compositions, a plant for the production of iron melts (4), in particular steel melts, such as crude steel melts, is equipped with PA0 an electric are furnace vessel (1), PA0 a refining vessel (3) following upon the furnace vessel (1) via a weir (34) and including a bottom departing from the weir (34) in an at least partially downwardly inclined manner and an oxygen supply means (35, 36) as well as an iron melt tap (41) provided in its end region farther remote from the furnace vessel (1), PA0 a decanting vessel (2) following upon the furnace vessel (1) and having a common bottom (18) with the furnace vessel (1), said decanting vessel being provided with a slag tap (43) in its end region farther remote from the furnace vessel (1), PA0 a supply means (21) supplying liquid pig iron (20) and opening into the furnace vessel (1), PA0 a preheating shaft (5) supplying solid iron carries (7), said preheating shaft being arranged above the furnace vessel (1) and opening into the furnace vessel (1) via its lid (4) via a gas-permeable cooled shut-off means (6), and a charging shaft (10) arranged above the furnace vessel (1) and opening into the furnace vessel (1) via a gas-impermeable cooled shut-off means (11) (FIG. 1).
problem: How to process different iron carriers in varying quantitative compositions in an economical manner
constraint: Tradeoff between continuous throughput (flow rate) and the need for adequate phase separation time and quality, balanced against thermal efficiency of preheating and the structural complexity of multiple interconnected vessels with shared boundaries
mechanism: Multiple processing chambers are arranged in sequence where material flows from one to the next via flow control structures and shared bottom surfaces; gravity-driven flow combined with inclined bottom geometry facilitates natural phase separation (metal from slag) as material moves through the system; a separate preheating subsystem allows solid carriers to be heated before entering the main processing unit, enabling efficient use of diverse input materials
mechanism_raw: Multiple processing vessels are arranged in sequence where material flows from one to the next via weirs and shared bottom surfaces; gravity-driven flow combined with inclined bottom geometry facilitates natural phase separation (metal from slag) as material moves through the system; a separate preheating shaft allows solid carriers to be heated before entering the main furnace, enabling efficient use of diverse input materials

abstract: A pneumatically-driven, turbine device comprises a Terry turbine rotor coaxially disposed within a rigid housing equipped with a reentry port bordering an exhaust port. The rotor comprises a plurality of radially spaced-apart air buckets. An air pathway is established between an inlet and an exhaust outlet, extending through the reentry port, the exhaust port, and portions of the rotor buckets. The reentry port comprises a narrow arc defined in the race. At least a portion of the exhaust groove borders, but is separated from, the reentry port. Entering air initially impacts a first rotor bucket disposed adjacent the reentry port. Halves of the first two buckets are disposed radially adjacent the reentry port. Opposite halves of the first and second buckets adjoin the unmachined race area spaced apart from the reentry port. Halves of the third and fourth successive buckets are also disposed radially adjacent the reentry port, but opposite halves of the third and fourth buckets are disposed over the neck to complete the air path through the exhaust groove. When used as a pneumatic vibrator, the circular turbine wheel is unbalanced and lacks an output driveshaft. When configured as a fluid motor, the device's rotor is balanced, driving an output driveshaft.
problem: Efficiently converting pneumatic energy into rotational or vibrational motion while enabling dual functionality (vibrator vs. motor) in a single turbine device.
constraint: The reentry port's narrow arc and exhaust groove separation must balance airflow pressure and direction to avoid energy loss while allowing the rotor's balance state to determine the output mode.
mechanism: A fluid-driven rotary element with radially distributed impact surfaces and selectively positioned flow entry and exit ports. The spatial arrangement of the impact surfaces and ports determines whether the net force on the rotary element is balanced (producing continuous rotation) or unbalanced (producing oscillatory motion). The same physical configuration produces different output modes by altering the balance state of the rotary element and the routing of the fluid flow.
mechanism_raw: A controlled airflow path is established through radially spaced rotor buckets and strategically positioned reentry/exhaust ports. The geometry of the ports and bucket arrangement directs air impact to specific buckets, creating unbalanced forces for vibration or balanced rotation for motor operation. The same physical structure achieves different outputs by altering rotor balance and airflow routing.
residual_terms: ["rotary element", "impact surfaces", "flow entry and exit ports", "balance state"]

abstract: A chemical mechanical polishing apparatus has a rotatable platen, a generally linear polishing sheet having an exposed portion extending over a top surface of the platen for polishing the substrate, and a drive mechanism to incrementally advance the polishing sheet in a linear direction across a top surface of the platen. The polishing sheet is releasably secured to the platen to rotate with the platen, and it has a width greater than a diameter of the substrate.
problem: Achieving uniform polishing of a substrate while minimizing localized wear and ensuring consistent surface finish during chemical mechanical polishing.
constraint: The sheet width must exceed the substrate diameter to maintain full contact area during linear advancement, while the incremental drive mechanism must synchronize with platen rotation to avoid uneven polishing.
mechanism: A polishing medium wider than the workpiece is incrementally translated linearly across a rotating support surface. The combination of rotation and translation distributes contact pressure across the width of the medium, ensuring even wear and uniform surface treatment. The width of the medium relative to the workpiece ensures full coverage during incremental movement.
mechanism_raw: A polishing sheet wider than the substrate is incrementally advanced linearly across a rotating platen. The combination of platen rotation and sheet translation distributes contact pressure across the sheet's width, ensuring even wear and consistent polishing. The sheet's width relative to the substrate ensures full coverage during incremental movement.

abstract: An apparatus for enabling hands-free use of a device for magnifying a long-distance event, such as binoculars, includes a base member, a first attachment member, and a second attachment member. The first attachment member is connected to the base member and is adapted to removably attach the apparatus to an article of headgear, such as a brimmed cap. The second attachment member is connected to the base member and is adapted to removably attach the apparatus to the magnifying device. The apparatus includes adjustable portions such as hinges so that the position of the binoculars may be adjusted by the user when the apparatus is attached to the cap.
problem: Enabling hands-free operation of a magnifying device (e.g., binoculars) while allowing user-adjustable positioning and secure attachment to headgear.
constraint: The attachment mechanism must balance removability and adjustability with sufficient rigidity to hold the device steady during use, requiring careful hinge design and material selection.
mechanism: A modular coupling system uses two removable connection interfaces linked by adjustable articulation joints. The joints allow angular and positional adjustments, enabling the user to align the coupled device with their line of sight while maintaining a stable, hands-free configuration. The removability of the connection interfaces allows for detachment and reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: A modular attachment system uses two removable connection points (to headgear and device) linked by adjustable hinges. The hinges allow angular and positional adjustments, enabling the user to align the magnifying device with their eyes while maintaining a stable, hands-free configuration.

abstract: This invention relates to a Spring Water Delivery System and in particular to a system for bulk delivery of potable spring water to a customer's home. This system includes a bulk water supply truck equipped with a pumping system and an onboard ozone generator for delivery of potable tank water to a customer's supply tank. The supply tank is not pressurized, but uses an electric pump to deliver potable water to the individual faucets in the customer's home
problem: Delivering potable water to a customer's home while maintaining water quality during transport and enabling efficient distribution without pressurized storage.
constraint: The ozone dosage and contact time must be sufficient to neutralize contaminants without over-oxidizing the water, while the pump system must compensate for the lack of tank pressurization to ensure adequate flow rates.
mechanism: An onboard treatment subsystem applies a reactive agent to the fluid during transport to maintain potability, while a non-pressurized storage reservoir uses a pumping subsystem to deliver the treated fluid to end-use points. The treatment occurs in-line during delivery, ensuring continuous purification without relying on chemical additives or pressurized storage.
mechanism_raw: An onboard ozone generator treats water during transport to maintain potability, while a non-pressurized supply tank uses an electric pump to deliver water to household faucets. The ozone treatment occurs in-line during delivery, ensuring continuous purification without relying on chemical additives or pressurized tanks.

abstract: There is disclosed an aqueous formulation for pretanning leather, which formulation comprises (a) a reductive saccharide having a dextrose equivalent of 10 to 100, and (b) an aliphatic dialdehyde containing 2 to 8 carbon atoms, and which is devoid of mineral salts. The leather treated with the novel aqueous composition (wet white leather) is eminently suitable for further processing, especially for the manufacture of leathers which are devoid of heavy metals.
problem: Creating a metal-free leather pretanning formulation that effectively cross-links collagen fibers without relying on heavy metals or mineral salts.
constraint: The dextrose equivalent range and dialdehyde carbon chain length must balance reactivity and cross-linking efficiency to avoid over-crosslinking or insufficient bonding, while excluding mineral salts prevents interference with the reaction.
mechanism: A reductive saccharide reacts with an aliphatic dialdehyde to form covalent cross-links in collagen fibers. The reductive environment stabilizes the reaction, while the dialdehyde's aldehyde groups bridge collagen molecules, achieving cross-linking without mineral salts or heavy metals. The dextrose equivalent range and dialdehyde carbon chain length balance reactivity and cross-linking efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A reductive saccharide (with a dextrose equivalent of 10–100) reacts with an aliphatic dialdehyde (2–8 carbons) to form covalent cross-links in collagen fibers. The reductive environment stabilizes the reaction, while the dialdehyde's aldehyde groups bridge collagen molecules, achieving tanning without mineral salts or heavy metals.
residual_terms: ["reductive saccharide", "aliphatic dialdehyde", "covalent cross-links", "collagen fibers", "reductive environment", "dextrose equivalent", "carbon chain length"]

abstract: A blister pack, comprising at least a first and a second parallel row of blisters, and of the type in which a base foil formed with blisters is connected to a substantially flat lid foil wherein between the at least first and second rows of blisters, an intermediate part having at least one folding line parallel to said first and second rows is defined, said pack being foldable along said folding line, and that said blisters of said frist row are so offset relative to the blisters of said second row that after folding the blisters in the rows engage between each other.
problem: Creating a compact, foldable blister pack that protects contents while minimizing storage space.
constraint: Balancing the need for compactness with structural integrity to ensure the folded pack remains intact and functional.
mechanism: Offsetting adjacent rows of protective cavities relative to each other and defining a fold line between them allows the cavities to interlock when folded, enabling compact stacking without structural collapse.
mechanism_raw: Offsetting blister rows relative to each other and defining a folding line between them allows the blisters to interlock when folded, enabling compact stacking without structural collapse.

abstract: Elastomeric articles are rendered less susceptible to blow or blister defects by providing, in at least one cord reinforcement ply of an article, a plurality of gas absorbing bleeder cords with the reinforcement cords and gas absorbing cords lying in the same general plane and with the gas absorbing cords consisting of staple hollow filaments. The gas absorbing cords may be used as fill yarn in weaving fabric employing parallel reinforcement cords.
problem: Preventing blow or blister defects in elastomeric articles caused by gas entrapment during manufacturing or use.
constraint: Ensuring the gas-absorbing cords do not weaken the overall reinforcement structure while effectively mitigating gas-related defects.
mechanism: Integrating gas-absorbing elements into reinforcement plies allows localized gas absorption, reducing internal pressure and defect formation without compromising structural strength.
mechanism_raw: Integrating gas-absorbing cords (hollow staple filaments) into reinforcement plies allows localized gas absorption, reducing internal pressure and defect formation without compromising structural strength.

abstract: A machine tool has a vertical-axis tool spindle that receives a tool, and a workpiece table on whose upper side is arranged a fixture for clamping in a workpiece. The tool spindle and workpiece table are displaceable relative to one another in a working region in which the workpiece is arranged. The working region extends at least partially, in a direction transverse to the spindle axis, outside the workpiece table; the fixture projects in that direction beyond the table, holds the workpiece there, and is open at the bottom so that chips that are produced can freely fall downward in the direction of the spindle axis.
problem: Efficient removal of machining chips during tool operations without disrupting workpiece stability or requiring manual intervention.
constraint: Maintaining precise workpiece clamping and alignment while enabling unimpeded chip evacuation in the transverse direction.
mechanism: Designing a fixture that extends beyond the workpiece support surface and is open at the bottom allows chips to fall freely under gravity, avoiding obstruction and accumulation during machining.
mechanism_raw: Designing a fixture that extends beyond the workpiece table and is open at the bottom allows chips to fall freely under gravity, avoiding obstruction and accumulation during machining.

abstract: A unitary, transportable, assembled nuclear steam supply system (NSSS) with a lifetime fuel supply utilizes a fast or epithermal spectrum reactor core immersed in a pool of light water together with a plurality of steam generators through which the coolant is circulated by up to 100% natural circulation at full power, augmented by reactor coolant pumps also immersed in the pool. Redundant steam generators and reactor coolant pumps, together with the fast or epithermal spectrum reactor core and pool configuration, make it possible to operate the NSSS for 10 to 15 or more years without maintenance on the internals or refueling, thereby rendering the system proliferation resistant.
problem: Achieving long-term, maintenance-free operation of a nuclear steam supply system without refueling or internal servicing.
constraint: Balancing safety, proliferation resistance, and thermal efficiency while ensuring redundancy and passive operation over extended periods.
mechanism: Combining a sealed containment configuration with natural circulation and redundant heat exchange components enables passive heat removal and system reliability, eliminating the need for active maintenance or refueling.
mechanism_raw: Combining a sealed pool configuration with natural circulation and redundant steam generators/pumps enables passive heat removal and system reliability, eliminating the need for active maintenance or refueling.
residual_terms: ["sealed containment configuration", "natural circulation", "heat exchange components", "passive heat removal"]

abstract: A technique is described for the formation of nano and micro-scale patterns and optical wave-guides, by using Bipolar Electrochemistry. Atoms are deposited or removed from a surface by creating and moving ions into or out of a medium by the use of electric fields, currents, and induced surface charges. To improve the deposition process, lasers, electron, and ion lenses can be positioned over the surface being deposited to further define the pattern being created. This technique does not harm the surface or crystal lattice of the substrate being deposited on and is powerful enough to transport dopants completely through a substrate. The technique can be used to expose electron beam activated resist which can be used in traditional fabrication processes or to create wave-guides connecting separate optical or electro-optical devices together. As a result smaller and newer types of integrated circuits, electronic devices, and micro machines can be fabricated. The technique can also be used to improve current fabrication processes, the repair of faulty devices, and the imaging of surfaces and hidden dopants.
problem: Precisely depositing or removing atoms from a surface to create nano/micro-scale patterns without damaging the substrate's crystal lattice.
constraint: Achieving high-resolution patterning while preserving substrate integrity and enabling compatibility with existing fabrication or repair processes.
mechanism: Using bipolar electrochemistry with electric fields and induced surface charges to move ions into or out of a medium, augmented by focusing elements to direct the process and define patterns.
mechanism_raw: Using bipolar electrochemistry with electric fields and induced surface charges to move ions into or out of a medium, augmented by lenses (laser, electron, ion) to focus the process and define patterns.

abstract: A brake system for rail cars which contains an air powered fluid system, a device for providing a separate source of brake force, and a manifold connected to the air powered fluid system and the device for providing a separate source of brake force; the manifold simultaneously delivers pressurized fluid to two movable cylinders under certain conditions and in response to fluid flow from either the air powered fluid system or the device for providing a separate source of brake force; but when both the device for providing a separate source of brake force and the air powered fluid system are delivering fluid flow to the manifold, the brake system contains a device for terminating the pressure from the separate source of brake force.
problem: A brake system must deliver brake force from two independent fluid sources to two cylinders, but when both sources are active simultaneously, conflicting pressures can arise that compromise braking control.
constraint: The system must allow both sources to independently operate and deliver fluid, but when both are active simultaneously, the secondary source must be automatically deprioritized to prevent conflicting pressures from reaching the cylinders.
mechanism: A fluid distribution system allows two independent sources to deliver pressurized fluid to two output points. When both sources are active simultaneously, a priority-based override mechanism automatically deprioritizes the secondary source, ensuring only the primary source drives the outputs. This prevents conflicting pressures by dynamically selecting the dominant source based on activation state.
mechanism_raw: A manifold receives fluid flow from either of two sources and simultaneously delivers pressurized fluid to two cylinders. When both sources are delivering fluid to the manifold at the same time, a termination device automatically cuts off pressure from the secondary source, ensuring only the primary source drives the cylinders. This creates a priority-based override where one source takes precedence when both are active.

abstract: A cleaning apparatus for computer pointer devices having a standard ball contacting input rollers has an abradant ball mounted to a rotary shaft in a manner that the abradant ball may be brought into contact with rollers of the pointer device with the standard ball removed, the position of the abradant ball such that rotating the shaft will rotate the abradant ball in a manner that the abradant ball will both abrade and turn the rollers. The cleaning apparatus may be a hand-held device, built into a free-standing housing, or into a housing as a part of another computer housing, such as a computer or display. In some cases there is a variable speed drive with user settable speed, and in some cases there is a vacuuming system for removing abraded matter from a pointer device while cleaning takes place.
problem: Debris accumulates on the input rollers inside a ball-type computer mouse, degrading tracking accuracy, and the rollers are difficult to access for cleaning.
constraint: The cleaning must engage the rollers in their operational position using the same rotational motion they would normally experience, so that abrasion and roller turning occur together without disassembly.
mechanism: A cleaning element is positioned to contact rotating components in their operational orientation. The cleaning element is driven by the same rotational motion that the components experience during normal operation, combining debris removal with the components' natural movement. This ensures cleaning occurs without disassembly by leveraging existing mechanical engagement.
mechanism_raw: An abradant ball is positioned to contact the rollers (with the standard ball removed) and is rotated by a shaft. The rotation simultaneously abrades debris from the rollers and turns them, mimicking the rollers' natural operational motion. This combines cleaning action with the same rotational engagement the rollers experience during normal use.

abstract: In an exemplary embodiment, the present invention provides an exhaust constituent sensor comprising a planar sensing element securely held in place within a tubular inner shield by known methods. Improved thermal management of the sensor is provided by disposing a thermally conductive material between said planar sensing element and said tubular shield. In an exemplary embodiment, the thermally conductive material comprises a high thermal conductivity metal mesh which transfers heat within said tubular shield to said tubular shield via thermal conduction. The heat is then dissipated into the surrounding environment via thermal convection at an outer surface of the tubular shield. By optionally disposing an annular heat fin on the outer surface of the tubular shield, a greater amount of heat is dissipated into the surrounding environment via thermal convection in less time.
problem: A planar sensing element in an exhaust sensor generates heat that must be managed to maintain accurate operation, but the sensor must remain securely positioned within its protective shield.
constraint: The thermal management must not compromise the mechanical retention of the sensing element within the shield, so the conductive material serves both as a heat transfer medium and as part of the secure mounting interface.
mechanism: A thermally conductive interface is placed between a heat-generating sensing element and a protective enclosure. The interface creates a conductive heat path from the element to the enclosure, which then dissipates heat to the surrounding environment. Optional extended surfaces on the enclosure increase convective heat transfer area and rate.
mechanism_raw: A thermally conductive material (metal mesh) is disposed between the sensing element and a tubular shield, creating a conductive heat path from the element to the shield. The shield then dissipates heat to the surrounding environment via convection. Optional heat fins on the shield's outer surface increase the convective dissipation area and rate.

abstract: A machine tool is controlled through a process incorporating the steps of (1) measuring geometric and thermal errors with accurate instruments, (2) creating a global differential wet model of machine tool position, and (3) using this model to control real time compensation of machine tool operation. A controller modifies encoder-type position feedback signals used by the machine to compensate for geometric and thermal errors in the manner dictated by the global differential wet model.
