problem: Machine tools introduce geometric and thermal errors that cause the actual tool position to deviate from the commanded position, reducing machining accuracy.
constraint: The compensation must operate in real-time during machine operation, using a pre-characterized model that accounts for both static geometric errors and dynamic thermal errors without requiring continuous recalibration.
mechanism: A pre-characterized error model maps commanded positions to expected deviations caused by static and dynamic system inaccuracies. This model is applied in real-time to adjust feedback signals from position sensors, enabling the controller to preemptively correct for geometric and thermal errors before they affect the output trajectory.
mechanism_raw: Errors are first measured with accurate instruments to create a global differential wet model that maps commanded positions to expected error corrections. This model is then used in real-time to modify encoder feedback signals, so the controller compensates for both geometric and thermal errors before they affect the tool path.

abstract: A dialysis system which does not need to use a physiological saline in replenishing a solution or cleaning and priming the dialysis system, does not need a troublesome setting operation and can easily and accurately set a flow rate of a replenisher solution. The dialysis system includes a closed-type water-removal control apparatus 1, a dialyzer 2, a fresh dialysate line 3 as well as a used dialysate line 4, an RO water pressurizing line 5, an RO water pressurizing pump 51 provided in the RO water pressurizing line 5, an artery side blood line 6, a blood pump 61 provided at the artery side blood line 6 and a vein side blood line 7. According to the dialysis system, by pressurizing RO water into a communication line of the used dialysate, dialysate is made to flow from a dialysate flow path 21 into a blood flow path 22 through a dialysis membrane 23 of the dialyzer 2 and the inside of a blood circulation path can be cleaned and primed.
problem: A dialysis system needs to clean and prime the blood circulation path without using physiological saline and without complex manual setup operations.
constraint: The cleaning and priming must be accomplished using only RO water as the driving fluid, flowing through the dialysis membrane into the blood path, without requiring separate cleaning solutions or manual flow rate adjustments.
mechanism: A pressure-driven cross-flow process uses a driving fluid to transport through a semi-permeable barrier, transferring the fluid from one flow path to another. The barrier acts as both a cleaning interface and a priming mechanism, using the pressure differential to clean and prepare the receiving flow path without requiring additional solutions or manual adjustments.
mechanism_raw: Pressurized RO water is introduced into the used dialysate communication line, causing dialysate to flow from the dialysate path through the dialysis membrane into the blood flow path. This cross-flow through the membrane cleans and primes the blood circulation path using the membrane itself as the cleaning interface, driven by pressure differential rather than additional solutions.

abstract: The present invention relates to a process of coding and identifying individual members of a chemical combinatorial library synthesized on a plurality of solid supports which undergo mix and split synthesis. The process provides for tagging the solid supports with a coding identifier that is attached to the solid support and which can be decoded by infrared or raman spectroscopy when directly attached to the support.
problem: Tracking and identifying individual compounds in a combinatorial chemical library during mix-and-split synthesis without disrupting the synthesis process.
constraint: The tag must remain chemically stable and decodable while being directly attached to the support during synthesis.
mechanism: Attaching a detectable marker directly to a solid support, enabling non-invasive identification of each compound's synthesis history through spectroscopic decoding without disrupting the synthesis process.
mechanism_raw: Attaching a spectroscopic tag (decodable via infrared or Raman spectroscopy) directly to solid supports, enabling non-invasive identification of each compound's synthesis history.

abstract: The present invention relates to an apparatus and method for distributing electrical power from power substation circuits. The apparatus of the present invention is responsive to overcurrent conditions and selectively actuates a switching network so as to restore power to at least a portion of the users connected to the faulty circuit of the power distribution system.
problem: Restoring electrical power to users after an overcurrent fault in a distribution system without manual intervention.
constraint: The system must respond selectively to faults while maintaining operational continuity for unaffected circuits.
mechanism: Automatically detecting fault conditions and actuating a switching network to isolate the fault while maintaining operational continuity for unaffected circuits.
mechanism_raw: Automatically detecting overcurrent conditions and actuating a switching network to isolate the fault and restore power to unaffected portions of the system.

abstract: A combined strainer and stopper device for basins, sinks and the like. The device has a perforated cylindrical housing having an open lower end and a perforated top wall. An annular valve seat is formed in the lower end, and a handle is affixed to the top wall. A valve disc is reciprocable in the housing into and out of sealing engagement with the valve seat. An actuator stem is connected at a lower end to the valve disc and extends at its upper end through an opening in the handle. Outwardly projecting retaining lugs are on the stem for cooperation with the handle to retain the valve disc in an open position.
problem: Combining straining and stopping functions in a single device for basins/sinks without requiring separate components.
constraint: The design must balance sealing engagement with the valve seat and retention in the open position without complex actuation.
mechanism: A reciprocable valve disc with retaining lugs that mechanically engage an actuator to hold the disc in an open position, enabling dual straining and stopping functionality through controlled mechanical interaction.
mechanism_raw: A reciprocable valve disc with retaining lugs that mechanically engage the handle to hold the disc in an open position, enabling dual functionality through controlled mechanical interaction.

abstract: A circular knit blank for use in the manufacture of undergarments and the garments so manufactured comprising a tubular knit body having an elastomeric yarn on selected courses, wherein said tubular body contains at least one area of control that has a stitch pattern increasing its modulus by about 8%, to provide a balance of comfort and control. The stitch pattern is preferably a 1 by 1 alternating tuck.
problem: Balancing comfort and control in elastomeric garments by adjusting localized stiffness without compromising overall fit.
constraint: The stitch pattern must maintain compatibility with elastomeric yarns while achieving the desired modulus increase.
mechanism: Incorporating a patterned structure in selected areas of an elastomeric material to increase localized modulus, creating controlled stiffness regions while maintaining overall fit compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a stitch pattern (e.g., 1x1 alternating tuck) in selected areas to increase the material's modulus by ~8%, creating controlled stiffness regions.

abstract: A GeAs sulphide glass family of transparent glasses having transmission far into the infrared portion of the spectrum, containing a source of phosphorus ion as a co-dopant to effect dispersion of a rare earth metal ion dopant in the glass, an optical component comprising the glass, and a method of dispersing a rare earth metal ion in the glass.
problem: Achieving uniform dispersion of rare earth metal ions in GeAs sulphide glass while maintaining infrared transparency.
constraint: The co-dopant concentration must balance dispersion effectiveness with preservation of the glass's optical transmission properties.
mechanism: Introducing a co-dopant that chemically interacts with dispersed ions to prevent clustering and ensure homogeneous distribution within a glass matrix while preserving optical transmission properties.
mechanism_raw: Using phosphorus as a co-dopant to chemically interact with rare earth ions, preventing clustering and ensuring homogeneous distribution within the glass matrix.

abstract: A reservoir of the device supports, in its upper portion, a profiled flange forming a handling apparatus for the device and a trough to collect and discharge, via an opening, the water of condensation forming on a vaporization coil. The coil has turns of changing diameters, supported by support combs on the trough and enclosed in a cover provided with peripheral and upper air openings. The cover includes an element for securing a receptacle that directly coacts, by gravity, condensates.
problem: Managing condensation water generated on a vaporization coil in a heating device without manual intervention or structural complexity.
constraint: Balancing airflow through the cover openings to prevent vapor buildup while maintaining structural support for the coil and receptacle.
mechanism: A collection element positioned to receive condensed fluid from a heat exchange surface via gravitational flow, combined with a structural barrier containing airflow-regulating openings and a self-retaining containment unit, enabling passive fluid removal while maintaining mechanical support and vapor evacuation.
mechanism_raw: A trough collects condensation from the coil via gravity and discharges it through an opening, while a cover with airflow openings and a gravity-secured receptacle ensures continuous water removal and structural integration.

abstract: Disclosed is a package containing a plurality of cut lengths of fibrous casing which are moisturized to substantially soaked levels of moisture and are retained in an evacuated plastic bag wherein the moisture level of the casing is derived from free water added into the bag prior to evacuation. Also disclosed is a method of packaging cut lengths of casing which provides for the addition of soaked levels of moisture to the casing in the bag.
problem: Maintaining optimal moisture levels in fibrous casings during packaging to prevent drying or degradation.
constraint: Ensuring the moisture level remains within a range that prevents over-saturation while the vacuum preserves the casing's structural integrity.
mechanism: Introducing a controlled quantity of liquid into a sealed environment with reduced pressure, where pressure differentials and vapor-phase equilibrium between the liquid and surrounding medium maintain a target moisture content in a fibrous material without active regulation.
mechanism_raw: Introducing free water into an evacuated plastic bag before sealing, where the vacuum pressure and water vapor equilibrium retain the casing at a soaked moisture level.

abstract: An infinitely variable toroidal drive comprising a housing (1), an input shaft (3), a torque converter (34), two input discs (5, 15) with toroidal inner surfaces, two output discs (6, 16) with toroidal inner surfaces, one input disc and one output disc each forming one pair and both output discs being disposed next to each other with mirror symmetry, several friction wheels for transmitting a torque from the input disc to the corresponding output disc, one output shaft (10) and one gear wheel system (8, 9) between output discs and output shaft wherein on the transmission housing (1) is removably fastened a holding frame (2) which has: one upper frame clamp (28), one lower frame clamp (29), one cup-shaped bearing support member (7) which connects the upper frame clamp with the lower frame clamp and upon which at least one gearing (24) for the gear wheel (8) is situated in a manner such that its inner ring is stationarily arranged and its out ring rotates together with the gear wheel (8).
problem: Providing an infinitely variable torque transmission system with high efficiency and durability.
constraint: Maintaining consistent friction contact between discs and wheels to avoid slippage while minimizing wear under varying load conditions.
mechanism: A torque transfer system using opposing curved friction surfaces with adjustable normal force to create variable contact pressure, integrated with a mechanical stage that separates static and rotating elements to enable continuous torque modulation without discrete gear ratios.
mechanism_raw: Using toroidal friction discs and wheels to transmit torque via variable contact pressure, combined with a gear system that decouples stationary and rotating components for smooth speed adjustment.

abstract: A remote control vehicle comprising a body having a front end and a rear end and provided with first and second ground engageable propulsion means respectively disposed on opposite sides of the vehicle and in which the first and second propulsion means are driven by first and second transmission means respectively to permit the vehicle to be propelled and steered by driving the propulsion means on one side of the vehicle independently from the propulsion means on the other side of the vehicle, a boom assembly having carrying means for carrying an implement on the boom assembly, the boom assembly being mounted on the body for lifting movement between a raised position and a lowered position by a lifting means and wherein the ground engageable propulsion means and the lifting means of the boom assembly are operable by a receiver, of an electromagnetic signal, provided on the body.
problem: Enabling remote steering and implement lifting in a ground vehicle without mechanical linkages.
constraint: Coordinating power distribution and control signals between propulsion and lifting systems to avoid interference or overload during simultaneous operation.
mechanism: A vehicle control system using independently powered traction elements on opposing sides to achieve directional changes through speed differential, combined with a separate powered articulating member for vertical displacement, both governed by non-mechanical signal transmission to eliminate physical control linkages.
mechanism_raw: Independent propulsion of left and right ground-engageable means for differential steering, paired with a boom assembly lifted by a separate actuator, both controlled via electromagnetic signals.
residual_terms: ["independently powered traction elements", "speed differential", "non-mechanical signal transmission"]

abstract: A paper handling system includes first and second inclined conveyors. The first inclined conveyor operates at a first speed and has an output end. The second inclined conveyor operates at a second speed and is operably positioned to receive paper output from the first inclined conveyor. The second speed is greater than the first speed. The inclined conveyors are preferably inclined at an angle in the range from 15.degree. to 35.degree.. By transporting the paper up the inclined conveyors, upper layers of paper are allowed to slide down over lower layers of paper thereby creating a thinner stream of paper.
problem: Reducing the thickness of a paper stream during transport to improve handling or processing efficiency.
constraint: Optimizing the inclination angle (15–35 degrees) and speed differential to prevent layer misalignment or jamming while maximizing throughput.
mechanism: A material conditioning system using two surfaces oriented at an oblique angle relative to the transport direction, where a velocity gradient between the surfaces causes overlapping layers of a flexible medium to slide relative to each other, reducing aggregate thickness while maintaining lateral alignment through controlled friction.
mechanism_raw: Using two inclined conveyors operating at different speeds, where the faster upper conveyor causes paper layers to slide downward over slower lower layers, creating a thinner, aligned stream.

abstract: Illuminated shoes are provided with a switch having a fixed end for connection to one side of a battery and a movable end for contacting one of a plurality of selectable conducting members each connected to a separate terminal of a sub-circuit. Each sub-circuit contains a source of light or sound with a common terminal at the opposite end from the separate terminal and connected to the other side of said battery. The switch movable end moves substantially randomly or in random patterns under inertia to contact a conducting member to complete a sub-circuit.
problem: Creating variable or randomly changing lighting/sound patterns in wearable devices without complex control electronics or programming.
constraint: The inertial movement must be constrained enough to reliably contact the conducting members while remaining simple enough to function without active control or power for switching.
mechanism: Use a mechanically unconstrained inertial element that randomly selects between multiple discrete output paths through physical contact, where random motion of the element automatically triggers different functional states without requiring external control or power for switching.
mechanism_raw: A switch with a movable contact that moves randomly under inertia to selectively touch different conducting members, each linked to a separate sub-circuit, so that random physical motion automatically produces varied output patterns without active control.

abstract: An electrical connector having an improved connector shield and a multi-purpose strain relief includes an electrically insulative contact support member having a rearward cable termination end and a plurality of electrical contacts positioned on the support member forward of the termination end. An electrically conductive contact shield housing having an outer and inner walls surrounds the contact support member and extends rearward beyond the electrical contacts to shield both the contacts and the discrete conductors of a multi-conductor cable. The connector includes an electrically conductive strain relief device comprised of mirrored strain relief members which are in electrical communication with the shield housing and the cable ground thereby providing a ground path between the cable ground and the contact shield housing.
problem: Providing both electromagnetic shielding and mechanical strain relief in an electrical connector assembly.
constraint: The strain relief must maintain electrical continuity while providing sufficient mechanical retention force without compromising either the shielding effectiveness or the mechanical strain relief function.
mechanism: Integrate a single conductive component that simultaneously establishes a continuous electrical grounding path between two shielded structures while mechanically anchoring a flexible cable, where the component's dual conductivity and structural compliance satisfy both electromagnetic shielding and strain relief requirements.
mechanism_raw: Using conductive strain relief members that are electrically connected to both the connector shield housing and the cable ground, so a single mechanical component simultaneously provides strain relief and establishes a continuous ground path between cable and shield.
residual_terms: ["conductive component", "continuous electrical grounding path", "shielded structures", "structural compliance"]

abstract: An improved process for producing an atmosphere suitable for carburizing steel components by adding a small amount of oxygen to a mixture of natural gas and carbon dioxide, pre-heating the mixture to the desired reaction temperature in the presence of an inert material or a non-nickel-based catalyst that promotes the reaction between oxygen and natural gas without forming coke to avoid catalyst deactivation by coke formation, and reacting natural gas with carbon dioxide at high temperature in the presence of a catalyst.
problem: Producing a carburizing atmosphere via catalytic gas reactions without catalyst deactivation from coke formation.
constraint: The oxygen concentration must be carefully controlled to promote the desired reaction without excessive coking, and the catalyst composition must be selected to avoid coke-prone materials while still driving the target reaction.
mechanism: Control reactant gas composition by introducing a regulated oxidizing agent into a hydrocarbon stream and catalyzing gas-phase reactions using a catalyst formulation that drives target reactions while suppressing solid carbon formation, thereby maintaining catalytic activity through reduced coking.
mechanism_raw: Adding a controlled amount of oxygen to the reactant gas mixture and using a non-nickel-based catalyst that promotes the desired gas-phase reaction between oxygen and hydrocarbons while suppressing solid carbon (coke) deposition, thereby preventing catalyst deactivation.

abstract: New PB92 or Subtilisin 309 mutant serine proteases are provided having specific mutations, resulting in an surprisingly better wash performance or in an improved storage stability with at similar or even better wash performance. These PB92 or Subtilisin 309 mutants include mutations at positions 60, 87, 97, 99, 102, 116, 117, 126, 127, 128, 130, 133, 134, 154, 156, 158, 159, 160, 164, 169, 175, 180, 182, 193, 197, 198, 203, 211, and 216. The new proteases, therefore, are very suitable for use in various types of detergents, whether or not in conjunction with other enzymes, for example amylases, cellulases and lipases. Preferred embodiments are the PB92 and Subtilisin 309 mutants having a mutation at position 102 and in particular those having at least one further mutation.
problem: Improving enzyme performance (wash efficiency) and storage stability simultaneously in industrial enzymes.
constraint: Mutations must be at specific structurally significant positions to avoid destroying enzyme function, and multiple mutations may need to be combined to achieve the desired synergistic effect without compromising overall protein folding.
mechanism: Modify a protein structure through targeted amino acid substitutions at specific structural loci, where a primary substitution at a functionally critical site combined with secondary substitutions at complementary sites produces synergistic enhancements in multiple performance metrics without disrupting overall structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Introducing specific mutations at defined structural positions in the enzyme protein to achieve synergistic improvements in multiple functional properties, where a primary mutation at a key position combined with additional secondary mutations enhances both activity and stability.
residual_terms: ["amino acid substitutions", "structural loci", "functionally critical site", "structural integrity"]

abstract: A heat exchanger baffle and method by which the internal passage of a heat exchanger member is divided into two separate flow regions. The baffle includes first and second members having planar portions that define edges of the first and second members. The planar portions are connected to each other so as to form a connection region between the first and second members. The connection region is deformable to enable the planar portions to be folded onto each other. The baffle can then be installed in a heat exchanger member by installing the planar portions together into a slot in the wall of the heat exchanger member. After installation, the planar members remain substantially parallel to each other, and the connection region preferably contacts a portion of the wall opposite the slot. The manner in which the baffle is folded serves to bias the first and second members against the slot, so that the baffle is more reliably retained within the slot prior to being permanently secured by such methods as brazing. Each member of the baffle also preferably has a flange and a raised region within its planar portion. When the baffle is installed in the heat exchanger member, a portion of the wall is engaged by and between the raised region and the flange of each member, so that the baffle is securely retained within the slot prior to being permanently secured by brazing.
problem: Installing a baffle in a heat exchanger to divide internal flow passages while ensuring reliable temporary retention before permanent fixation.
constraint: The deformable connection must allow folding for insertion but provide sufficient spring-back force for retention without permanent deformation, and the geometry must ensure reliable positioning and contact pressure prior to brazing or other permanent attachment.
mechanism: Deploy a baffle assembly with a flexible coupling region between two rigid segments that can be elastically deformed for compact insertion into a confined space, then restored to an expanded configuration by stored elastic energy, where geometric engagement features between the segments and the space walls provide temporary retention force prior to permanent fixation.
mechanism_raw: A baffle with two planar members connected by a deformable region that can be folded for compact insertion into a slot, then the folded configuration creates a spring-back biasing force pressing the members against the slot walls, with geometric features (flanges and raised regions) engaging the wall for secure temporary retention.
residual_terms: ["flexible coupling region", "rigid segments", "elastic energy", "geometric engagement features"]

abstract: A propulsion system for a flying craft uses an air and water fuel source to provide propulsion thrust. The system includes two steam generating units, one attached directly to a compact turbine and the other connected to a compressor. The compressor compresses the steam from the latter steam generator, including excess steam from the turbine generator, and pumps it to a super-heated steam compression chamber. At the same time, the turbine generator powers another compressor to take in air from the atmosphere and pumps it into a super chilled compression chamber. After both the compressed super-heated steam and the compressed super chilled air have attained required pressure, volume and temperature, both gases are fed into an expansion chamber under appropriate control. The expansion chamber operates as a rocket booster and is equipped with an exhaust system made up of a main nozzle and several auxiliary thrust vectoring nozzles. Reactionary forces within the expansion chamber, caused by expansion of the chilled steam, cause thrust and generated heat. The generated heat heats the chilled compressed air within the gas expansion chamber, causing expansion of the chilled air, providing further thrust. The exhaust system controls exiting of the expanding gases to control and vector the thrust. Preferably, the heat source for the system is one or more nuclear reactors.
problem: Generating efficient propulsion thrust using a dual-temperature gas system while managing thermal dynamics and structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing pressure, temperature, and volume of both gas streams to maximize thrust while preventing structural failure or inefficient heat transfer.
mechanism: Two gas streams at contrasting thermal states are independently pressurized and then merged within a confined expansion region. The thermal energy from the high-temperature stream induces volumetric expansion of the low-temperature stream, generating a cascading pressure differential that produces directed thrust. An adjustable exhaust pathway modulates the direction of the combined expanding gases to control thrust orientation.
mechanism_raw: Two gas streams (super-heated steam and super-chilled air) are independently compressed and then combined in an expansion chamber. The heat from the steam causes the chilled air to expand, creating a cascading thrust effect. The exhaust system vectors the expanding gases to control thrust direction.

abstract: An article irradiation system includes (1) a radiation source for scanning a target region with radiation, (2) a conveyor system including a process conveyor positioned for transporting articles in a given direction through the target region, and (3) radiation shielding material defining the walls of a chamber containing the radiation source, the target region and a position of the conveyor system. The radiation source is disposed inside a loop defined by a portion of the conveyor system and is adapted to scan the articles in the chamber in a plane transverse to the given direction of the transport by the process conveyor. A shield (e.g., an intermediate wall) of radiation shielding material positioned within the loop supports a radiation shielding ceiling of the chamber, inhibits photons emitted from a beam stop in one of the chamber walls from impinging on the outer walls of the chamber and restricts flow in the chamber of ozone derived in the target region from the radiation source. A first queue is disposed outside of the chamber for transferring into the chamber articles from a loading area; a second queue is disposed in the chamber for moving the articles past the radiation source for irradiation by the source; and a third queue is disposed in the chamber for transferring articles from the chamber, after irradiation, for movement to an unloading area The operations of the first, second and third queues are synchronized. The shield inhibits radiation from the source from reaching the queues.
problem: Safely irradiating articles in a continuous process while shielding operators and equipment from radiation and ozone byproducts.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization of the three queues to ensure continuous operation without radiation leakage or ozone accumulation.
mechanism: A radiation-emitting element is enclosed within a segmented transport loop comprising synchronized processing zones (loading, treatment, unloading). Articles are conveyed through each zone in a coordinated sequence to maintain continuous operation. A barrier positioned between zones blocks harmful emissions while structurally supporting the containment system.
mechanism_raw: A radiation source is enclosed within a loop of a conveyor system, with synchronized queues (loading, irradiation, unloading) that move articles through the chamber. A shielded intermediate wall blocks radiation and ozone flow while supporting the chamber structure.

abstract: A substantially rectangular platform that has a top surface and a bottom surface. A pair of sectional tubular stanchions has one end connected to the platform. A cross-member is connected between the pair of stanchions other ends. A winch with a cable and an elongated carcass lifting member is mounted onto the cross-member. A pair of adjustable carcass leg retaining members each having one end secured to the winch's elongated carcass lifting member. The adjustable carcass leg retaining member's other ends are detachably securable to the carcass's legs. A pair of adjustable carcass skin retaining members each having one end secured to the platform by hooks. The adjustable carcass skin retaining member's other end is detachably securable to the carcass's skin. The winch is activated and lifts the legs of the carcass via the pair of adjustable carcass leg retaining members while the pair of adjustable carcass skin retaining members hold the skin in place to the platform, skinning the carcass.
problem: Lifting a carcass structure (e.g., a frame or skeleton) while preserving the integrity of its attached skin during the process.
constraint: Precisely coordinating the tension and positioning of both leg and skin retainers to avoid uneven forces or damage during lifting.
mechanism: Independent retention systems are used to selectively engage different parts of a multi-component structure during lifting. One retention system applies controlled tension to the primary structural elements via a lifting mechanism, while a second retention system anchors adjacent flexible components to a fixed platform. This separation of engagement points decouples the motion of rigid and flexible parts, preventing relative displacement and damage.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable leg retainers connected to a winch lift the carcass legs, while separate skin retainers anchored to the platform hold the skin in place. This decouples the lifting motion of the legs from the skin, preventing tearing or misalignment.

abstract: A kitchen grip or implement for kitchen use is composed of a water-resistant and stain proof material having temperature control characteristics. Such a material forms the implement from at least one sheet having a textured, recessed or irregular surface providing a non-slip contact surface while the opposite surface of the sheet is composed of a close fabricated fabric which is affixed to the sheet of non-slip contact surface material. The fabric sheet may be a sheet of nylon/polyester composition which is affixed to the non-slip contact surface sheet which may be composed of a chloride rubber. The sheets are die cut to the shape of a useful implement such as a hand mitt, a trivet, a lid holder or the like. A two-piece implement such as a hand mitt requires that two sheets of the fabric and chloride rubber composition be sewn together by means of a zigzag lock stitch employing nylon thread. One surface of the mitt may include a cross-cut textured recessed imprint providing a non-slip or gripping contact surface while the opposite exposed surface of the mitt may take the form of the smooth nylon/ polyester fabric.
problem: Creating a kitchen tool that provides a non-slip grip, temperature resistance, and durability in a single integrated design.
constraint: Selecting materials with compatible thermal expansion coefficients and bonding methods to prevent delamination under temperature fluctuations.
mechanism: A multi-layer composite structure combines a textured, moisture-resistant outer layer with a thermally insulating inner layer. The layers are bonded together to integrate functional properties: one surface provides friction-based grip while the opposing surface remains smooth for handling. Material selection ensures compatible thermal response to prevent delamination under temperature variation.
mechanism_raw: A textured, water-resistant material (e.g., chloride rubber) is bonded to a fabric layer (e.g., nylon/polyester) to combine non-slip contact with thermal insulation. The layered structure allows one surface to grip while the other remains smooth for handling.

abstract: A molded article such as a floor tile is made from recycled carpet waste which includes a polyvinyl chloride component in the backing material and fiber component having a melting point above the melting point of polyvinyl chloride. A mixture of the recycled carpet material is shredded and additional polyvinyl chloride is fed to an extruder where the polyvinyl chloride is melted without melting the carpet fibers. The resulting mixture is discharged and molded, such as by injection molding, to form a molded product. The molded product includes a continuous matrix of polyvinyl chloride having recycled carpet fibers uniformly dispersed therein. The molded article contains about 45% to about 85% of polyvinyl chloride, about 5% to about 20% of recycled carpet fibers, up to about 5% of a plasticizer and up to about 5% of an ethylene copolymer by weight based on the total weight of the product. The finished product preferably contains about 10% to about 75% by weight of recycled vinyl-backed carpet and about 25% to about 90% by weight of a flexible polyvinyl chloride based on the total weight of the product.
problem: Recycling polyvinyl chloride (PVC)-backed carpet waste into a structurally sound molded product without degrading the fibers.
constraint: Controlling the extrusion temperature to melt PVC without overheating fibers, and balancing PVC-to-fiber ratios to ensure flexibility and strength.
mechanism: Composite waste material is shredded and blended with a thermoplastic binder, then conveyed through a heated forming process where the binder melts while reinforcing fibers remain structurally intact. The molten binder creates a continuous matrix that uniformly encapsulates and binds the fibers during molding, preserving their load-bearing contribution to the final product.
mechanism_raw: Shredded carpet waste is mixed with additional PVC and processed in an extruder where PVC melts but fibers remain intact. The molten PVC forms a continuous matrix that binds the fibers uniformly during molding, preserving their structural contribution.

abstract: A nozzle for knitting machine comprises a fastening block comprising a U-shaped opening and an inlet hole; a seat under the fastening block adjacent the U-shaped opening, the seat comprising an opening in communication with the U-shaped opening; a trigger member pivotably disposed on both sides of the fastening block, the trigger member comprising a raised member in the opening of the seat; and a sliding block removably received in the U-shaped opening, the sliding block comprising a riser facing the seat, an inlet channel through the sliding block, a block member on the top of the inlet channel, a V-shaped groove on the block member, an aperture extended downwardly from the V-shaped groove being in communication with the inlet channel and the inlet hole. In blowing operation, yarn is placed on the V-shaped groove. Then move the sliding block toward the seat with the riser of the sliding block inserted into the opening of the seat. Next pivot the trigger member to cause the raised member of the trigger member to be disposed vertically. Thus, the sliding block is confined in a U-shaped opening. Hence, external high pressure air is directed to blow onto yarn. The yarn blowing or cleaning operation is made convenient. Further, the components are simplified. Thus, assembly is simple and manufacturing cost is reduced.
problem: Conveniently directing high-pressure air to blow or clean yarn in a knitting machine while simplifying component assembly and reducing manufacturing cost.
constraint: Balancing component simplicity and cost reduction while maintaining effective airflow direction and mechanical reliability during repeated actuation.
mechanism: A sliding element and a pivotable control member cooperate to mechanically constrain the sliding element within a channel-shaped cavity, forming a regulated flow conduit. The sliding element's protrusion, inlet passage, and recessed guide surface interact with the control member's projecting feature to redirect external fluid flow onto a target filament during operation.
mechanism_raw: A sliding block and pivotable trigger member interact to mechanically confine the sliding block within a U-shaped opening, creating a controlled airflow path. The sliding block's riser, inlet channel, and V-shaped groove work with the trigger's raised member to direct external air onto the yarn during operation.
residual_terms: ["sliding element", "pivotable control member", "channel-shaped cavity", "flow conduit", "protrusion", "inlet passage", "recessed guide surface", "projecting feature", "fluid flow", "target filament"]

abstract: An electrically actuated engine valve provides an armature having one or more teeth extending outward from the armature along the actuation axis to be received by corresponding sockets in the cores of opposed electromagnets. The teeth do not restrain the movement of the armature but in approaching the cores provides a magnetic flux path that produces a more constant force of attraction during actuation of the valve. This enables the valves to overcome initial opposing forces such as caused by pressure on the valve heads to which the armature is attached and provides a path of inductive coupling between the opposed coils that can reveal armature position providing a method of accurately controlling armature seating speed.
problem: Overcoming initial opposing forces (e.g., pressure on valve heads) during electromagnetic actuation while enabling accurate control of armature seating speed.
constraint: Ensuring the teeth do not physically restrain armature movement while providing sufficient magnetic flux for consistent force and position feedback.
mechanism: Projecting features on a movable magnetic component extend into magnetic core structures, establishing a magnetic flux path that sustains a substantially uniform attractive force during displacement. This flux path also enables inductive coupling between windings to detect the position of the movable component, permitting controlled actuation velocity.
mechanism_raw: Teeth on the armature extend into electromagnet cores, creating a magnetic flux path that maintains a more constant force of attraction during actuation. This flux path also enables inductive coupling between coils to reveal armature position, allowing precise speed control.
residual_terms: ["projecting features", "movable magnetic component", "magnetic core structures", "magnetic flux path", "attractive force", "displacement", "inductive coupling", "windings", "position detection", "actuation velocity"]

abstract: A faceplate light socket assembly for a light bank of the type used above vanity cabinets. The faceplate socket maintains a light bulb in substantially horizontal orientation perpendicular to the wall to which the light assembly is mounted. A pre-wired socket includes a spring clip which detachably retains the socket within a specially configured aperture of the faceplate. The aperture has an insertion slot to facilitate insertion of the spring within the aperture, a helical edge which gradually reduces the diameter of the aperture and a retaining notch to lock the socket in position. The helical edge biasingly compresses the spring clip upon rotation of the socket to maintain the socket within the aperture. An outer cylindrical surface of the socket is threaded for attaching a decorative sleeve.
problem: Maintaining a light bulb in a fixed horizontal orientation while enabling easy, secure attachment to a faceplate without additional fasteners.
constraint: Balancing ease of insertion and rotation with sufficient compression force to maintain secure retention under vibration or thermal expansion.
mechanism: A helical edge on an attachment surface progressively compresses a resilient retention element on a mounting interface during rotational insertion, securing the interface in a fixed orientation. The helical trajectory ensures gradual compression, while a detent feature locks the interface after rotation is complete.
mechanism_raw: A helical edge on the faceplate aperture gradually compresses a spring clip on the socket during rotation, locking the socket in place. The helical path ensures progressive compression, while a retaining notch secures the socket after rotation.
residual_terms: ["helical edge", "attachment surface", "resilient retention element", "mounting interface", "rotational insertion", "fixed orientation", "helical trajectory", "gradual compression", "detent feature", "rotation"]

abstract: An inbred maize line, designated PH8V0, the plants and seeds of inbred maize line PH8V0, methods for producing a maize plant, either inbred or hybrid, produced by crossing the inbred maize line PH8V0 with itself or with another maize plant, and hybrid maize seeds and plants produced by crossing the inbred line PH8V0 with another maize line or plant and to methods for producing a maize plant containing in its genetic material one or more transgenes and to the transgenic maize plants produced by that method. This invention also relates to inbred maize lines derived from inbred maize line PH8V0, to methods for producing other inbred maize lines derived from inbred maize fine PH8V0 and to the inbred maize lines derived by the use of those methods.
reason: The patent describes a specific biological product (an inbred maize line) and methods for its propagation, not a functional or mechanical mechanism that can be transferred to a different field.

abstract: A sports cap, having a stretchable pocket on the entire top surface of the visor and preferably worn on the head of a user while exercising, golfing, climbing or fishing, is disclosed. This sports cap has a visor integrated along the lower front edge of a crown into a single body through a sewing process, which a pocket provided on the entire top surface of the visor by sewing a stretchable pocket fabric along the rounded front edge of the visor. An opening is formed on the pocket at a position along the rear edge of the stretchable pocket fabric, with an elastic tape liner integrated along the rear edge of the pocket fabric and sewn to the visor at opposite ends thereof together with the pocket fabric so as to elastically tighten the opening of the pocket. The sports cap allows a user to easily and conveniently store a variety of personal necessities, such as golf tees, ball markers, a cigarette pack, a lighter, a match box, scratch papers, name cards, receipts, or score sheets, in the pocket.
problem: Storing a variety of personal items on a sports cap visor in a way that is both accessible and secure during physical activities.
constraint: Balancing stretchability for easy insertion with sufficient elastic tension to prevent items from falling out during movement.
mechanism: A compliant pocket material is affixed along the leading edge of a wearable visor, with an elastic tensioning element integrated at the trailing edge. The elastic element increases constriction around the pocket opening when stretched, allowing objects to be inserted but retained by the self-tightening action during movement.
mechanism_raw: A stretchable pocket fabric is sewn along the visor's front edge, with an elastic tape liner integrated at the rear edge. The elastic tightens the pocket opening when stretched, allowing items to be inserted but held securely by the self-tightening mechanism.
residual_terms: ["compliant pocket material", "wearable visor", "leading edge", "elastic tensioning element", "trailing edge", "pocket opening", "constriction", "objects", "self-tightening action", "movement"]

abstract: A device for producing spun yarn by means of an airflow acting in a twisting manner on the fibers of an untwisted sliver (1) as the sliver is being conducted into and through a spindle assembly (3). The spindle assembly (3) comprises a spindle head portion (5) which conically tapers toward a spindle inlet opening (2) and is rotatable independently of a spindle core portion (7) through which the yarn is withdrawn. The device suppresses any tendency of the yarn strength to decrease at high, increasing numbers of spindle revolutions.
problem: Maintaining yarn strength at high spindle speeds during spun yarn production.
constraint: Balancing the rotational speeds of the spindle head and core to ensure consistent twisting while avoiding mechanical stress that weakens the yarn.
mechanism: Decoupling rotational components to independently control twisting forces while isolating mechanical stress transmission, enabling consistent fiber entanglement without strength degradation under high-speed operation.
mechanism_raw: Independent rotation of the spindle head relative to the spindle core allows controlled airflow-induced twisting of fibers without transferring excessive rotational stress to the yarn, preventing strength degradation.

abstract: A method and machine for high speed formation of a three-dimensional woven fiber structure having at least two warp yarn systems having approximately zero crimp and at least three filling yarns having approximately zero crimp, wherein the warp and filling yarns are non-interlacing with each other, and are secured as an integral fabric via at least one vertical or Z yarn system and the warp yarn systems provided to be positioned via harness frames. The 3-D woven fabric of the present invention is fabricated on a 3-D weaving machine having rapier filling insertion that provides filling yarn insertions in unique shed openings in series to produce a complete filling insertion cycle for every movement of Z-direction yarn harnesses.
problem: Creating a three-dimensional woven structure with non-interlacing warp and filling yarns while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining zero crimp in warp and filling yarns while ensuring the Z yarns provide sufficient binding strength across all layers.
mechanism: Sequential placement of elements into discrete spatial openings combined with vertical binding elements that interlink non-interlacing layers, enabling precise three-dimensional arrangement without structural deformation.
mechanism_raw: Sequential insertion of filling yarns into unique shed openings combined with vertical Z yarns that bind the non-interlacing layers into an integral fabric, enabling precise spatial arrangement without crimp.

abstract: Metal surfaces, metal-oxide surfaces, metal-salt surfaces, silicon-comprising surfaces and/or high-molecular-weight aquoxide-comprising organic surfaces are coated. The coating is carried out with a reagent having a reactive group chosen from Si--H, Sn--H, and Ge--H. The reagent is applied in liquid, pasty, or solid form to the surface that is to be coated. Furthermore, the coating reaction requires the presence of an activator. A platinum metal in form of a compound or in metallic form is used as activator.
problem: Coating diverse surfaces (metal, metal-oxide, silicon, etc.) with a reagent that requires activation.
constraint: The necessity of platinum as an activator to facilitate the reaction, which may limit applicability in environments where platinum is unavailable or cost-prohibitive.
mechanism: Employing a catalytic activator to facilitate a chemical reaction between a reagent containing hydride-functional groups and a target surface, enabling uniform coating across chemically diverse substrates through catalytic mediation.
mechanism_raw: Use of a platinum-based activator to catalyze a reaction between a reagent containing Si-H, Sn-H, or Ge-H groups and the target surface, enabling uniform coating across chemically varied substrates.

abstract: A capacitor powered electronic emergency device retracts and parks an actuator into a resistive parking position with a crash stop barrier. Due to variations of the kinetic status of the actuator at the begin of the retraction, the actuator reaches the resistive parking position with different velocities, which can be at a level that causes the actuator to bounce off the crash stop barrier. A modulating pulsing of the energy flow extends the discharge time of the capacitor long enough to provide sufficient energy to compensate an eventual bounce-off. The use of transistors in the device keeps the internal energy consumption low. An increase of the pulsing frequency in dependence on the capacitor voltage results in a high average current flow.
problem: Preventing actuator bounce-off during emergency retraction into a resistive parking position due to variable initial kinetic energy.
constraint: Balancing pulsing frequency and capacitor voltage to ensure energy is neither depleted too quickly nor insufficient to counteract bounce-off.
mechanism: Dynamically modulating energy delivery timing and magnitude based on stored energy levels to counteract mechanical rebound, ensuring sustained force application during variable initial kinetic energy conditions.
mechanism_raw: Modulating pulsing of energy flow from a capacitor extends discharge time, dynamically compensating for bounce-off by adjusting pulsing frequency based on capacitor voltage to maintain sufficient energy delivery.

abstract: In a pull-assembling unit for automatically assembling a pull onto a slider body of a slide fastener, a slider transporting means includes a slider-body-transportation plate member having rectangular notch portions spaced at intervals of plural assembling sections along a top end edge thereof, each for accommodating the slider body. The slider-body-transportation plate member is adapted to be actuated in the slider-transportation path so as to draw a rectangular trajectory in a vertical plane. An actuation upper limit position of a top end of the rectangular notch portion is set to be above a slider-body-placing surface of the slider-transportation path and an actuation lower limit position of the top end of the notch portion is set to be at a retreat position below the slider-body-placing surface. Therefore, the slider-pull-assembling unit has a simple structure and is capable of assembling a pull onto a slider body accurately and securely at a high speed.
problem: Accurately and rapidly assembling a pull onto a slider body in an automated system.
constraint: Precise synchronization of the plate's vertical and horizontal motion to align notches with the slider body placement surface without mechanical interference.
mechanism: Controlled multi-axis motion of a component with spaced engagement features following a predefined trajectory, with positional constraints above and below a target surface to ensure precise alignment and secure assembly without interference.
mechanism_raw: A slider-body-transportation plate with spaced rectangular notches follows a controlled rectangular trajectory, with actuation limits set above and below the placement surface to ensure precise positioning and secure assembly.

abstract: A truss fabrication machine has processing circuitry for partially automating the fabrication of trusses. One or more workers place in jig stops on the tabletop a set of loose pre-cut truss members and the connector plates that get seated at the joints therebetween. The machine has a pressing head for seating the connector plates, which rides on a gantry above the tabletop in generally a Y-axis, wherein the gantry rides on a track generally along an X-axis. There are drivers to drive the gantry along the track and the pressing head along the gantry, as well an actuator for the pressing head. The processing circuitry is reliant on X- and Y-axis sensors for reckoning position on the tabletop. The processing circuitry is given control over the gantry, the pressing-head driver and actuator for coordinating movement of the gantry and pressing head between one given X and Y position to succeeding X and Y positions, and then actuating or not the actuating means. Alternatively the pressing head might pause in a standby mode following completion of a given truss sufficiently long to allow a worker to remove the completed truss and place back in the jig stops the loose pre-cut truss members and the connector plates, and so on, which will allow the fabrication of a succeeding truss, repetitively.
problem: Automating the repetitive and precise placement of connector plates at truss joints while allowing human workers to load/unload materials between cycles.
constraint: Balancing automation speed and precision with the need for human operators to safely load/unload materials between truss fabrication cycles.
mechanism: A coordinated multi-axis positioning system with automated control circuitry that sequentially directs a tool to calculated locations, actuating or bypassing operations based on positional feedback, while entering a paused state to permit human intervention between cycles.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated multi-axis (X-Y) motion control using a gantry system driven by sensors and processing circuitry to sequentially move a pressing head to calculated positions, actuating or skipping presses based on positional data, while pausing in standby mode to enable human intervention.

abstract: A line charge for deploying explosive charges across obstacles and mines to clear a safe lane has explosive charges spaced apart on a common detonating cord, and axial passageways in the explosive charges are sized to permit free longitudinal travel of the detonating cord through them. A composite strength member includes an inner fabric sleeve of high strength flexible material covered by an outer sleeve of thermoset/thermoplastic material and contains the explosive charges and detonating cord. Heat-curing the inner fabric sleeve and outer sleeve shrinks and conforms them to the outer contours of the explosive charges and combines the high strength flexible material and thermoset/thermoplastic material. Composite strength member absorbs energy during deployment of the line charge over its entire length and circumference and absorbs more energy prior to structural failure to allow the use of more powerful rocket motors to fly longer line charges from much greater and safer standoff distances. Composite strength member does not transfer self-destructive strains to the detonating cord during deployment; the detonating cord is free to longitudinally slide through the explosive charges; and composite strength member maintains proper spacing of explosive charges so that explosive effectiveness of the line charge is maximized. The cost effective and uncomplicated assembly procedure for the line charge creates a more reliable line charge having improved performance capabilities as compared to contemporary manufacturing schemes.
problem: Deploying explosive line charges across obstacles from a safe distance while maintaining structural integrity and charge spacing during high-speed deployment.
constraint: Achieving sufficient energy absorption to enable longer/more powerful deployments without compromising the detonating cord's functionality or charge alignment.
mechanism: A composite energy-absorbing structure with deformable material layers conforming to elongated charges, dissipating kinetic energy through distributed material deformation across its length and circumference, while enabling longitudinal sliding of an internal component to prevent strain transfer and maintain alignment.
mechanism_raw: A composite strength member with heat-cured inner and outer sleeves conforming to explosive charges, absorbing energy through material deformation across its entire length and circumference, while allowing longitudinal sliding of the detonating cord to prevent strain transfer and maintain charge spacing.
residual_terms: ["composite strength member", "heat-cured inner and outer sleeves", "detonating cord"]

abstract: A filter media structure, which is capable of operating in the micro- and nanofiltration regime, offers: low cost, durability, high temperature and chemical resistance, high permeability, high flow rate, low pressure drop across the filter media, high mechanical strength, separation efficiency, and biocompatibility. The filter media structure is comprised of blend of carbon or ceramic fibers and inorganic fiber whiskers generally having a diameter of from about 0.03 to about 5 microns. In one embodiment, filter media structure is comprised of blend of activated carbon-containing inorganic fibers and inorganic fiber whiskers generally having a diameter of from about 0.03 to about 5 microns.
problem: Creating a durable, high-performance filter media that simultaneously achieves high permeability, chemical resistance, mechanical strength, and separation efficiency.
constraint: Balancing fiber diameter and material composition to optimize permeability and flow rate without sacrificing structural integrity or separation efficiency.
mechanism: A composite material formed by integrating reinforcement elements with high surface area and base fibers, where the reinforcement provides mechanical strength and surface area while the base fibers contribute chemical resistance and controlled porosity for separation.
mechanism_raw: Blending inorganic fiber whiskers (0.03–5 microns) with carbon or ceramic fibers to create a composite structure where the whiskers provide mechanical reinforcement and surface area, while the base fibers contribute chemical resistance and porosity for filtration.

abstract: A transducer includes a pneumatic actuator in combination with a stepper motor lifter mechanism to which is opposed an attractive E-I core actuator for precise vertical positioning of a load with minimal transmission of vibration. A typical application is for vertical positioning of a stage in a lithography machine. The use of a stepper motor driving a lead screw and pneumatic actuator together with an attractive E-I core actuator provides a large dynamic range force actuator. The transducer has a sensor which is located spaced away from the E-I core actuator gap and which operates inductively to measure the gap. A compliant diaphragm for the pneumatic actuation allows the load to move a small amount in all six degrees of freedom.
problem: Achieving precise vertical positioning of a load (e.g., a lithography stage) with minimal vibration transmission across a large dynamic force range.
constraint: Integrating multiple actuation methods to cover a wide dynamic range while isolating vibrations and maintaining precision in a sensitive environment.
mechanism: A multi-actuator positioning system combining coarse, dynamic, and fine adjustment mechanisms with feedback sensing, where a compliant element allows limited multi-degree-of-freedom movement to isolate vibrations while maintaining precision across a wide force range.
mechanism_raw: Combining a stepper motor lead screw for coarse positioning, a pneumatic actuator for dynamic range force application, and an E-I core actuator for fine adjustments, with a spaced inductive sensor measuring gap position and a compliant diaphragm allowing limited six-degree-of-freedom movement.

abstract: A hybrid carrying truck is disclosed which has merits of both of a skid carrier and a carrying truck such that it can successively and smoothly transfer between different carrying lines to carry a work whatever the carrying lines are and can secure a removing position from the carrying line to a refuge area freely and with safety. The hybrid carrying truck includes traveling wheels mounted at front and back positions on the left and right sides of a truck body for being rolled on a pair of rails to allow the truck body to travel along a carrying line, a pair of left and right skid members mounted on a bottom face of the truck body and elongated in a carrying direction of the hybrid carrying truck, and a truck hauling engaging member mounted at a central position of the bottom face of the truck body in a widthwise direction of the truck body.
problem: Enabling a single transport vehicle to smoothly transition between different carrying lines (e.g., rails and skid tracks) while maintaining safety and positional control.
constraint: Designing a hybrid system that accommodates both wheeled and skid-based transport without compromising stability or transition smoothness between different line types.
mechanism: A hybrid transport system with dual motion interfaces (rolling and sliding) mounted on a vehicle body, enabling seamless switching between transport modes via a central coupling mechanism that interfaces with different infrastructure types.
mechanism_raw: Mounting traveling wheels for rail-based movement and elongated skid members on the truck body's bottom face, with a central hauling engaging member to interface with different transport systems, allowing seamless switching between rolling and sliding motion modes.
residual_terms: ["traveling wheels", "elongated skid members", "central hauling engaging member"]

abstract: A substantially stocking-shaped photograph album and method therefor, comprising a base portion, at least one substantially stocking-shaped leaf coupled to the base portion, and at least one sleeve coupled to the substantially stocking-shaped leaf, wherein the sleeve is dimensioned to receive a photograph in order to provide a way to store and display photographs in a festive photo album. Preferably, an audio device can be activated to play a melody while viewing the pictures.
reason: This is a product design description (stocking-shaped photo album with sleeves and optional audio) with no causal functional mechanism that solves a problem transferable to another field. It merely lists physical components and aesthetic features.

abstract: A method is disclosed for obtaining highly specific and tailored ligands suitable for purifying a particular product target or for eliminating particular target impurities in a feed stream. Engineered affinity ligands according to the invention will bind a target with high specificity at a preselected binding condition and release the target at a preselected elution condition. The ligands are isolated by contacting a target with a multiplicity of polypeptides derived through variegation of the structure of a candidate binding domain, the variants (or analogues) including polypeptides favoring binding to the target under desired binding conditions and release from the target under elution conditions, where the binding and elution conditions differ according to one or more parameters, such as pH, temperature, concentration of salt or volume % of an organic solvent.
problem: Obtaining ligands with highly specific binding and controlled release characteristics for purification or impurity elimination, where binding and elution must occur under different, preselected conditions.
constraint: The binding and elution conditions must differ by controllable parameters (pH, temperature, salt concentration, organic solvent volume), and the variants must be diverse enough to populate the desired binding/release phenotype space.
mechanism: Generating a diverse set of structural variants through systematic variation, then selecting variants whose functional behavior (e.g., binding or release) is conditionally triggered by specific environmental parameters. The conditional response emerges from the structural diversity, enabling selection of entities that activate or deactivate based on preselected thresholds of those parameters.
mechanism_raw: Creating a library of binding-domain variants through structural variegation, then selecting variants that favor binding under one set of environmental conditions (e.g., pH, temperature, salt concentration, solvent volume) and release under a different set of conditions. The conditional binding/release behavior emerges from the structural diversity of the variants, allowing selection of ligands that respond to specific environmental triggers.

abstract: A fuel assembly for a boiling water reactor comprising a plurality of fuel units (3a, 3b, 3c, 3d), stacked on top of each other, each one comprising a top tie plate (5), a bottom tie plate (6) and a plurality of fuel rods (4a, 4b, 4c) arranged between the top tie plate and the bottom tie plate. The fuel units are surrounded by a fuel channel (9) with a substantially square cross section. At least some of the fuel units comprise fuel rods with different diameters and different fuel quantities. The fuel rods are adapted such that fuel quantity and lattice space are optimized laterally and axially in the fuel assembly.
problem: Optimizing fuel utilization and reactor performance in a fuel assembly where uniform fuel distribution is suboptimal.
constraint: The fuel rods must fit within the physical lattice structure of the fuel channel, and the variation in diameters and quantities must remain compatible with reactor mechanical and thermal-hydraulic design limits.
mechanism: Spatially varying material distribution and spacing within a structured array to optimize local performance parameters (e.g., reaction efficiency, heat transfer) at each position. The multi-dimensional variation allows independent tuning of material density and geometry relative to the array's constraints, enabling localized optimization without global uniformity.
mechanism_raw: Varying fuel rod diameters and fuel quantities across both lateral and axial dimensions within the assembly, creating a heterogeneous lattice where fuel density and spacing are tuned spatially to optimize neutron economy and heat removal. The multi-dimensional variation allows local optimization of fuel quantity relative to lattice geometry at each position.

abstract: A bipolar electrolytic cell can include, as a manifold, a spiral manifold assembly. This spiral manifold assembly will comprise a first outer assembly member, a second outer assembly member and a center assembly member. The overall structure can provide reduced loss of metal or gas and minimal loss of electrical current during an electrolytic process.
problem: Reducing loss of metal, gas, and electrical current during electrolytic processes in a bipolar cell, where inefficient distribution causes material and energy waste.
constraint: The spiral manifold must maintain structural integrity under operating conditions while providing uniform distribution, and the geometry must be compatible with the bipolar cell configuration and the materials being processed.
mechanism: Using a continuous helical flow path to progressively distribute materials and energy (e.g., reactants, electrical current) along a curved trajectory, ensuring uniform delivery and minimizing stagnation zones, resistance, and leakage. The geometry enforces sequential, even distribution across the system, reducing localized inefficiencies.
mechanism_raw: Using a spiral manifold geometry to distribute reactants and electrical current along a continuous helical flow path, which promotes uniform distribution and minimizes dead zones, flow resistance, and current leakage. The spiral path ensures progressive, even delivery of materials and current across the cell, reducing localized losses.

abstract: The invention relates to a composite insulated glass assembly, comprising a pair of spaced substrates with a flexible and resilient polymeric spacing member between the substrates, at the periphery thereof. At joints in the spacer, or at corners, where small incisions may be made for ease in forming corners, and such similar discontinuities, sealing material is positioned, bonded in the space to fill any gap or opening and restore any reduction in thermal or other value of the spacer at these positions. The spacer is conveniently positioned adjacent the periphery of the assembly and is substantially free of sealing material except at the corners.
problem: Maintaining thermal and structural performance of an insulated glass assembly at joints and corners where the continuous spacer barrier is interrupted or weakened.
constraint: The sealing material must be compatible with the polymeric spacer and substrates, and must be applied only at discontinuities to avoid compromising the overall flexibility and thermal performance of the continuous spacer.
mechanism: Applying a sealing material selectively only at structural discontinuities in an otherwise continuous flexible barrier, restoring integrity at those points while preserving the barrier's inherent flexibility and thermal properties elsewhere. The selective application avoids compromising the barrier's global performance characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Applying sealing material selectively only at discontinuities (corners, joints, incisions) in an otherwise continuous flexible polymeric spacer, filling gaps and restoring barrier integrity at those specific points. The rest of the spacer remains free of sealing material, preserving its flexibility, resilience, and thermal properties.

abstract: A disposable wipe-off article having improved durability. The disposable wipe-off article includes a heat-sealable sheet and a heat-sealable wipe-off layer including an expanded bundle of continuous filaments. The wipe-off layer is bonded to the base sheet by a plurality of heat-seal lines extending to cross the continuous filaments and intermittently arranged longitudinally of the continuous filaments.
problem: Creating a durable disposable wipe-off article that maintains structural integrity during use while allowing effective wiping.
constraint: Balancing bond strength to prevent layer separation while preserving filament flexibility and wiping effectiveness.
mechanism: A bonding pattern is applied across a flexible fibrous substrate, attaching a functional layer to a backing sheet. The bonding pattern is oriented along the primary axis of the substrate, creating localized attachment points that prevent layer separation under mechanical stress while leaving intervening regions of the fibrous substrate exposed for wiping action.
mechanism_raw: Heat-seal lines cross continuous filaments and are arranged longitudinally, bonding the wipe-off layer to the base sheet. This allows the filaments to remain exposed for wiping while the cross-seal lines prevent delamination under mechanical stress.

abstract: An apparatus for securing a tag to a pair of eyeglasses is disclosed. The apparatus includes a tag having a body and at least one prong extending longitudinally across the body so as to define an aperture between the body and the at least one prong and a tube constructed from a material which shrinks when subjected to heat. The prong and the temple piece are disposed within the tube and the tube is subjected to heat, thereby shrinking the tube to secure the prong to the temple piece of the eyeglasses.
problem: Securely attaching a tag to eyeglasses without adhesives or mechanical fasteners that could damage the frame.
constraint: Ensuring the tube shrinks sufficiently to hold the tag without deforming or damaging the eyeglass temple during heating.
mechanism: An encircling shrinkable sleeve surrounds a protruding element and an adjacent structural member. Application of energy causes the sleeve to reduce in circumference, generating radial compression that creates both frictional engagement and mechanical interlocking to secure the protruding element to the structural member.
mechanism_raw: A heat-shrinkable tube encases the prong and temple piece. Heating causes the tube to contract radially, creating a tight frictional and mechanical grip that locks the tag in place.

abstract: An insulated lattice is prepared with a plurality of lattice oriented atoms to create a substantially planar surface having a lattice arrangement. Any unsatisfied chemical bonds are terminated along the substantially planar surface by placing atoms at the site of the unsatisfied chemical bonds to terminate the unsatisfied chemical bonds and insulate the surface to form a platform. In one aspect of the invention, the insulator atoms are removed at predetermined locations. Atoms to form the atomic chain are placed at predetermined locations on the insulated lattice platform to form a first atomic chain which behaves as one of a conductor, a semiconductor and an insulator. A second atomic chain is also placed at predetermined locations on the insulated lattice platform so that the second chain behaves as another of a conductor, a semiconductor and an insulator. These placements are made such that the second atomic chain is electrically coupled to the first atomic chain, and the second atomic chain behaves differently than the first atomic chain. That is, in the first chain the atoms are placed at a first separation distance and in the second chain the atoms are placed at a second separation distance, where the second separation distance is different than the first.
problem: Fabricating a nanoscale platform with spatially defined regions of varying electrical conductivity (conductor, semiconductor, insulator).
constraint: Maintaining lattice structural integrity while precisely controlling atomic placement to achieve distinct conductive behaviors in adjacent chains.
mechanism: Discrete elements are positioned at controlled intervals on a supporting framework. By varying the spacing between adjacent elements, neighboring chains of elements exhibit distinct electronic characteristics, enabling the creation of regions with different electrical conductivity properties within a single integrated structure.
mechanism_raw: Atoms are placed at controlled separation distances on an insulated lattice. By varying interatomic spacing, adjacent atomic chains exhibit different electronic properties (e.g., conductor vs. semiconductor), enabling tailored electrical coupling between regions.

abstract: An air bag gas generator has a cylindrical member that permits reliable welding of the cylindrical member with an inner surface of a ceiling portion of a housing even if the welding surface is slightly misaligned. It furthermore permits welding in such a manner (a more stable manner) that unsteadiness does not occur in the area where the inner surface of the ceiling portion of the housing and the inner cylindrical member abuts. In the air bag gas generator, which includes the inner cylindrical member in the housing, the inner cylindrical member has a peripheral wall portion bent to form a flattened surface portion as an extension of the one of that cylindrical member where it joins the inner surface of the ceiling portion.
problem: Achieving reliable welding between a cylindrical member and a housing ceiling in an airbag gas generator despite potential misalignment during assembly.
constraint: Ensuring the bent geometry does not compromise structural strength or gas generator performance under high-pressure deployment conditions.
mechanism: A deformable peripheral interface on a cylindrical component is shaped to provide a contact surface that adapts to positional variations between mating parts. This adaptive geometry ensures consistent surface engagement and joining quality between the cylindrical component and a planar housing surface despite assembly misalignment.
mechanism_raw: A bent peripheral wall on the cylindrical member forms a flattened surface that self-adjusts to compensate for angular or positional misalignment, ensuring consistent contact and weld stability between the inner cylindrical member and housing ceiling.
residual_terms: ["bent peripheral wall", "flattened surface", "self-adjusts", "angular or positional misalignment", "welding", "housing ceiling"]

abstract: Apparatus for the rolling and heat treatment of elongated metal product of relatively small cross section, such as rods and bars, is described in which the elements required for the conduct of a variety of heat treatments are arranged in in-line disposition whereby any of several heat treatment procedures can be performed on the product without need for transferring the product to remotely located heat treatment facilities. The methods of performing various heat treatments through use of the disclosed apparatus are also described.
problem: Performing multiple heat treatment processes on elongated metal products (e.g., rods, bars) without transferring the product between separate facilities.
constraint: Maintaining precise temperature and timing control across all zones to ensure consistent material properties without disrupting the continuous flow of the product.
mechanism: A series of treatment stations are arranged sequentially along a continuous conveyance path. Each station applies a distinct thermal or cooling process to the moving product as it passes through, enabling multiple sequential material treatments without interrupting the product's forward motion or requiring transfer between separate processing locations.
