mechanism_raw: Heat treatment elements (e.g., heating, cooling, quenching zones) are arranged in an in-line sequence along a single processing path. The product moves continuously through each zone, enabling sequential treatments without interruption or relocation.
residual_terms: ["heat treatment", "heating, cooling, quenching zones", "in-line sequence", "continuous processing path", "temperature and timing control"]

abstract: A bindery compactor receives and compacts simultaneously large particulate paper waste and pneumatically conveyed fine paper waste. The compactor operates with a platen cycling within a compactor chute, in which the platen is normally forward in the compacting position with a sealing plate attached to the platen extending to close the top of the chute and form the bottom of two waste paper receiving bins. A first of these paper waste-receiving bins is for large particulate paper waste loaded from a cart dumper. A second bin of these paper waste-receiving bins is for pneumatically transported fine paper waste from a cyclone separator. In the second bin, accumulation of fine particle paper waste occurs to a height where an electric eye triggers cycling of the compactor. When cycling is triggered, the compactor platen retracts from extension to the chute withdrawing the sealing plate and allowing the stored paper waste from either bin to fall into the chute ahead of the retracting platen. Upon reaching full retraction, the platen reverses direction to compact all paper waste falling from either bin in the chute. The platen then closes off the bottom of the bins with the sealing plate, and remains extended in the forward position until the next compactor cycle. Provision is made to manually cycle the compactor where the waste bin for the large particulate paper waste fills ahead of the waste bin for the small particulate paper waste.
problem: Simultaneously compacting two distinct types of paper waste (large particulate and fine) with different accumulation rates and requiring manual intervention when one bin fills faster.
constraint: Balancing the compaction cycle timing to handle two waste streams with different accumulation rates while maintaining structural integrity of the chute and bins.
mechanism: A moving compaction element cycles within a channel, triggered by a sensor when a first waste stream reaches a threshold. The element retracts to allow waste from two separate chambers to enter the channel, then reverses to compact all waste. A sealing component on the moving element alternately isolates the chambers and the channel, enabling sequential compaction of both streams. A manual override permits cycling when one chamber fills faster than the other.
mechanism_raw: A platen cycles within a chute, triggered by a sensor (electric eye) when fine waste reaches a threshold height. The platen retracts to allow waste from either bin to fall into the chute, then reverses to compact all waste. A sealing plate on the platen alternately closes the bins and the chute, enabling sequential compaction of both waste streams. Manual override allows cycling when the large-waste bin fills first.

abstract: An improvement in the structure of a worktable for a wood carving machine includes a positioning device provided with a sleeve having a U-shaped recess at the top for mounting a supporting arm of a clamping device, the supporting arm being provided with an eccentric roller close to an intermediate portion thereof and adapted for sliding on the upper edge of the positioning device, and the clamping device being replaceable with a holder which can be moved up and down along a rod and rotated with respect to a cross-shaped sleeve for holding a workpiece in place.
problem: Precisely positioning and clamping a workpiece on a wood carving machine worktable while allowing tool replacement and adjustment.
constraint: Achieving both fine positional control (via eccentric roller sliding) and modular tool replacement (via rod-and-sleeve mounting) without compromising stability during carving operations.
mechanism: A modular positioning system uses an adjustable element with a sliding contact to enable fine positional control of a workpiece. A replaceable tool mount is attached via a multi-axis coupling that allows vertical displacement and rotational orientation, securing the workpiece while maintaining stability during operation. The system decouples adjustment and clamping functions to support tool replacement without compromising positional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: A U-shaped sleeve on the positioning device accepts a supporting arm with an eccentric roller that slides along the upper edge, enabling positional adjustment. A replaceable holder is mounted on a rod and cross-shaped sleeve, allowing vertical movement and rotational orientation of the clamping device to secure the workpiece.

abstract: A system for collecting oil on water comprises an oil boom (1) and a floating collection container (2), which is connected to an opening (4) in the boom by a pumping hose (3). The pumping hose (3) is flexible so that it can follow the wave motions of the water and is provided with non-return valves, making the flow (18) in the pumping hose unidirectional. The distance between the opening (4) in the boom and the collection container (2) is adjustable by tension members (8) in order for the excess length or slack in the pumping hose (3) to be adjusted to the prevailing wave height or length conditions.
problem: Collecting oil from water surfaces in dynamic wave conditions while maintaining unidirectional flow and adapting to varying wave heights.
constraint: Maintaining effective oil collection despite wave-induced movement while preventing hose kinking or slack-induced flow disruption.
mechanism: A flexible conduit connects a floating collection vessel to a surface-skimming barrier, with tensioning elements adjusting the distance between the barrier and vessel to maintain optimal slack. Check valves ensure unidirectional flow through the conduit, while the tensioning system accommodates dynamic movement without kinking or flow disruption. The barrier and vessel move independently to adapt to varying wave heights.
mechanism_raw: A flexible pumping hose connects a floating collection container to an oil boom opening, with non-return valves ensuring unidirectional flow. Tension members adjust the distance between the boom and container, allowing slack in the hose to accommodate wave motion without disrupting flow or causing backflow.

abstract: An automated system is provided for servicing a vehicle and its occupants. A first identification signal is communicated either while the vehicle is approaching the terminal or upon arrival and a second control signal is then generated from within the vehicle beginning and terminating the requested servicing and maintaining control over the operation. Vehicle servicing, such as fueling and washing is provided robotically to the vehicle without the vehicle occupants being required to emerge from the vehicle or become physically involved in its implementation. Payment is automatically charged to the customers account.
problem: Automating vehicle servicing (fueling, washing) and payment without requiring occupant involvement or physical interaction.
constraint: Ensuring secure and reliable communication between the vehicle and terminal to coordinate servicing steps and payment without human intervention.
mechanism: A communication protocol exchanges identification and control signals between a mobile unit and a terminal to coordinate servicing steps. Autonomous actuators perform fueling and cleaning operations in response to the signals, while a payment system charges a customer account based on the exchanged data. Bidirectional communication ensures synchronization of operations and secure transaction completion without human intervention.
mechanism_raw: A first identification signal from the vehicle triggers a second control signal to begin/end servicing. Robotic systems perform fueling and washing autonomously, while payment is automatically charged to the customer's account. The system maintains control over operations via bidirectional communication between the vehicle and terminal.

abstract: A moisture-permeable waterproof fabric comprising a textile fabric and a moisture-permeable resin film containing a non-porous urethane resin layer formed on at least one side thereof, wherein the moisture-permeable waterproof fabric has a moisture permeability of 15,000 g/m2·24 hr or greater according to the potassium acetate method, a moisture condensation of no more than 5 g/m2·hr and a water pressure resistance of 20,000 mmH2O or greater, and a release-sheet attached moisture-permeable resin film comprising a release sheet and a moisture-permeable resin film formed thereon containing a non-porous urethane resin layer.
problem: Creating a fabric that is both waterproof (resists liquid water) and breathable (allows moisture vapor transport) with high performance in both metrics.
constraint: Balancing moisture permeability (≥15,000 g/m²·24hr) and water pressure resistance (≥20,000 mmH₂O) without compromising mechanical flexibility or durability of the fabric.
mechanism: A selective barrier layer is applied to a flexible substrate, creating a molecular-level filter that permits moisture vapor diffusion while blocking liquid water. The barrier's non-porous structure establishes a permeability threshold for vapor molecules but resists liquid penetration under pressure. The substrate maintains mechanical flexibility and durability despite the barrier's presence.
mechanism_raw: A non-porous urethane resin layer is formed on a textile fabric, selectively allowing moisture vapor to pass through while blocking liquid water. The non-porous structure creates a molecular-level barrier for water droplets but permits vapor diffusion, achieving simultaneous waterproofing and breathability.

abstract: A system and method are provided for the safe removal of a wet, fully-plated cathode from a silver recovery cell and its replacement by a fresh cathode. The fresh cathode is brought to the recovery cell in a transport housing, which is then docked thereto. A drip tray is unfolded from the transport housing so as to extend across and surround the top of the recovery cell. The fresh cathode is removed from the transport housing and put to one side. The used cathode is removed from the recovery cell, preferably by being attached to the lid which is unscrewed therefrom. The cathode is then transferred to the housing over the drip tray which catches any liquid falling therefrom. The used cathode is screwed into the transport housing, and the housing removed to a refiner for safe disposal, whilst the fresh electrode is screwed onto the recovery cell.
problem: Safely replacing a contaminated, liquid-laden cathode in a hazardous electrochemical recovery cell while containing spillage during the transfer operation.
constraint: The system must balance liquid containment with component access, and the transport housing must serve dual roles as both the fresh-cathode carrier and the used-cathode disposal container without cross-contamination.
mechanism: A transport housing interfaces with a work cell and deploys a containment barrier that extends across and surrounds the cell opening, creating a sealed work zone. A contaminated component is removed and transferred within this contained zone, then secured into the transport housing which serves as both the carrier and the disposal vessel, while a fresh component is installed in its place.
mechanism_raw: A transport housing docks to the work cell and deploys a containment barrier (drip tray) that extends across and surrounds the cell opening, creating a sealed work zone. The used cathode is removed and transferred within this contained zone, then secured into the transport housing which serves as both the carrier and the disposal vessel, while a fresh cathode is installed in its place.

abstract: The invention concerns a pre-vaporizing and pre-mixing burner for liquid fuels which has a fuel feed line (56), a pump which pressurizes the fuel in the feed line, a mixing region (123) and a fuel valve (119) which opens out into the mixing region and by means of which the fuel is atomized and fed to the air for combustion (127). According to the invention, the fuel is vaporized in an optimum manner in that the fuel valve opens automatically as from a given fuel pressure, and a heating device (128) is associated with the fuel valve.
problem: Optimizing fuel vaporization in a liquid-fuel burner to ensure efficient and stable combustion.
constraint: The heating must be precisely coordinated with the valve opening so that vaporization occurs only when and where the pressure threshold is met, avoiding premature or insufficient vaporization.
mechanism: A valve opens automatically when fluid pressure reaches a predetermined threshold, and a heating device associated with the valve activates in response, vaporizing the fluid at the optimal location and timing for maximum efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A fuel valve opens automatically when fuel pressure reaches a predetermined threshold, and a heating device associated with the valve activates in response, vaporizing the fuel at the optimal location and timing for maximum efficiency.

abstract: A sleeper seating unit for an aircraft, and including a primary seat having a seat frame for being stationarily-mounted to the aircraft deck, a seat back for being selectively moved by a seat occupant among fully upright, semi-reclined and fully reclined positions, a scat bottom for moving between retracted and extended positions in coordination with the seat back, and an ottoman for being positioned on the deck forward of the primary seat. The ottoman has a top cushion positioned on a top surface thereof and a leg rest cushion positioned on a side of the ottoman facing the primary seat. The leg rest cushion is movable between positions wherein when the primary seat is in an upright position, the leg rest cushion is positioned at an angle to engage and support the bottom of the feet, and when the primary seat is in a reclined position, the leg rest cushion is in a generally horizontal position adjacent to and forming an extension of the seat bottom.
problem: Providing appropriate body and leg support as a passenger seat transitions between upright and fully reclined sleeping configurations in a confined aircraft cabin.
constraint: All components must move in precise coordination to maintain ergonomic support in every intermediate position, and the leg rest must smoothly transition between foot-support and leg-extension modes without gaps or misalignment.
mechanism: The position of a primary support surface mechanically coordinates the movement of a secondary support surface and a separate leg rest cushion on a movable platform. As the primary support surface reclines, the secondary support surface extends and the leg rest cushion pivots from an angled foot-support orientation to a horizontal leg-extension orientation, continuously adapting support geometry to the system's state.
mechanism_raw: The seat back position mechanically coordinates the movement of the seat bottom and a separate leg rest cushion on an ottoman. As the seat back reclines, the seat bottom extends and the leg rest cushion pivots from an angled foot-support orientation to a horizontal leg-extension orientation, continuously adapting support geometry to the seat's state.
residual_terms: ["primary support surface", "secondary support surface", "leg rest cushion", "movable platform", "support geometry"]

abstract: Charge pump circuits are described to transfer a voltage signal in an output stage without signal level degradation. An exemplary circuit includes a transistor, complementary clock signals, and a gate controlling circuit to present a full range of voltage signal at the output stage without signal level degradation. An additional parasitic inhibitor circuit inhibits the appearance of parasitic effects associated with the operation of the transistor in the exemplary circuit.
problem: Transferring a voltage signal through an output stage without signal level degradation while suppressing parasitic effects caused by transistor switching.
constraint: The system must simultaneously preserve full signal integrity at the output while actively suppressing parasitic effects, requiring the clock signals to be precisely complementary and the inhibitor to respond without interfering with the desired signal transfer.
mechanism: Complementary control signals drive a switching circuit that operates a conductive element to transfer the full voltage range to an output stage without degradation. A separate suppression circuit actively monitors and counteracts unwanted side effects generated by the conductive element's switching operation.
mechanism_raw: Complementary clock signals drive a gate control circuit that operates a transistor to transfer the full voltage range to the output stage without degradation. A separate parasitic inhibitor circuit actively monitors and counteracts unwanted side effects generated by the transistor's switching operation.
residual_terms: ["complementary control signals", "switching circuit", "conductive element", "output stage", "suppression circuit", "voltage range"]

abstract: A method for easily and effectively preventing shattered-rim fracture in a railway wheel. Generally, the method comprises the steps of providing a railway wheel, measuring the maximum defect size within the rim of the railway wheel, and determining whether the maximum defect size is less than a predetermined maximum permissible defect size, the maximum permissible defect size being determined based on an analysis of the likelihood of Mode II crack propagation from the defect when the railway wheel has been subjected to the load. The disclosed invention also encompasses a method for grading railway wheels for maximum load suitability.
problem: Preventing catastrophic shattered-rim fracture in railway wheels caused by crack propagation from internal defects under operational loads.
constraint: The failure mode analysis must accurately model the specific crack propagation mechanism (Mode II) and the real operational loads, and the defect measurement must reliably identify the largest defect to ensure no critical flaw is overlooked.
mechanism: A specific failure mode (shear-mode crack propagation) is analyzed under actual operational load conditions to derive a maximum permissible defect size. The actual maximum defect size within each component is then measured and compared against this analytically-derived threshold to determine acceptability.
mechanism_raw: A specific failure mode (Mode II crack propagation) is analyzed under actual operational load conditions to derive a maximum permissible defect size. The actual maximum defect size within each wheel rim is then measured and compared against this analytically-derived threshold to determine acceptability.
residual_terms: ["shear-mode crack propagation", "operational load conditions", "maximum permissible defect size", "analytically-derived threshold"]

abstract: A description is given of a container closure for filling and emptying containers, in particular drum-like transporting containers, which can be inserted in an exchangeable manner into a container opening, which receives a plug head. The container closure has a riser tube, which is connected to the plug head, and a removal connection element, it being the case that the latter can be locked to the plug head by means of a stud coding system which has coding studs and matching coding recesses. According to the invention, the coding studs are provided on a first securing part and the coding recesses are provided on a second securing part. One of the securing parts is designed as an annular disc, which can separately be fitted loosely, such that it cannot slip off, onto the modular removal connection element. The other of the securing parts is integrated in the plug head. The container closure described avoids mix-up of chemicals, permits simultaneous liquid removal and ventilation, and, while complying with the regulations for licensing hazardous substances, can be connected to commercially available containers or drums.
problem: Preventing chemical mix-up and ensuring secure, regulation-compliant connections in container closures for hazardous substances.
constraint: Must comply with hazardous substance regulations while allowing simultaneous liquid removal and ventilation.
mechanism: Use complementary mechanical features on two separate parts to enforce a single correct relative orientation, preventing misalignment and ensuring secure connection between components.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical coding system using studs and recesses on separate securing parts (one as a loosely fitted annular disc, the other integrated into the plug head) to enforce correct alignment and prevent incorrect connections.

abstract: An iron-graphite composite powder having a microstructure comprising carbon clusters embedded in a ferrous matrix is disclosed. Also disclosed is a process for preparing the iron-graphite composite powder, a process for preparing sintered articles from this composite powder and the sintered articles prepared thereby.
reason: The abstract describes a material composition and its preparation process but does not specify a causal functional mechanism beyond the material's microstructure, which is too specific to metallurgy to generalize.

abstract: An array of nanowires having a relatively constant diameter and techniques and apparatus for fabrication thereof are described. In one embodiment, a technique for melting a material under vacuum and followed by pressure injection of the molten material into the pores of a porous substrate produces continuous nanowires. In another embodiment, a technique to systematically change the channel diameter and channel packing density of an anodic alumina substrate includes the steps of anodizing an aluminum substrate with an electrolyte to provide an anodic aluminum oxide film having a pore with a wall surface composition which is different than aluminum oxide and etching the pore wall surface with an acid to affect at least one of the surface properties of the pore wall and the pore wall composition.
problem: Fabricating nanowires with controlled diameter and packing density for use in arrays.
constraint: Achieving precise control over channel diameter and packing density while maintaining structural integrity of the nanowires.
mechanism: Employ a two-stage fabrication process: first forming continuous elongated structures by injecting molten material into a porous template under pressure, then modifying the template walls through selective material removal to control structural properties of the formed structures.
mechanism_raw: A two-step process: (1) melting a material under vacuum followed by pressure injection into porous substrates to form continuous nanowires, and (2) anodizing aluminum with an electrolyte to create pore walls with altered composition, then etching to modify pore properties.

abstract: A pressurized water closet operating system comprises an accumulator vessel for storing water and air under pressure. A flush valve controls the discharge of water from the vessel and comprises a cylinder having a lower end in fluid communication with the outlet of said vessel, a piston defining upper and lower chambers therein, an orifice in the piston, an aperture in the cylinder providing fluid communication between the interior of the accumulator vessel and the lower chamber in the cylinder, a valve on the piston normally closing the lower end of the cylinder so as to close the water outlet and openable upon upward movement of the piston to permit the discharge of water, and a normally closed flush valve actuator openable to effect fluid communication between ambient air pressure and the upper chamber in the cylinder whereby a fluid pressure differential across said piston effects upward movement thereof and opening of the valve.
problem: Controlling the discharge of water from a pressurized accumulator vessel in a water closet system.
constraint: Maintaining consistent pressure differentials and ensuring reliable valve actuation under varying load conditions.
mechanism: Use a differential pressure mechanism where introducing fluid to one chamber of a partitioned piston creates a pressure imbalance that drives piston movement, which in turn actuates a discharge valve through mechanical linkage.
mechanism_raw: A piston with upper and lower chambers and an orifice creates a pressure differential when ambient air is introduced to the upper chamber via a flush valve actuator, causing upward piston movement that opens the discharge valve.

abstract: A cleaning compound additive for adding to water or windshield wiper fluid to aid removal of insect splatters from a windshield. The cleaning compound additive includes the combination of effective amounts of anhydrous ammonia, alkoxylated linear alcohols sold under the trade name SURFONIC, dry particulate sodium bicarbonate, dry particulate polyvinyl pyrrolidone, dry particulate orange dye, and dry particulate citrus orange scent.
reason: The abstract lists chemical components without explaining a causal interaction or functional mechanism beyond their combined presence in a formulation, making it a product feature rather than a transferable mechanism.

abstract: This invention generally pertains to the field of psychiatry. In particular, this invention pertains to the discovery that agents which inhibit the binding of cortisol to its receptors can be used in methods for ameliorating pathologies or conditions associated with psychosis. These pathologies or conditions include psychotic major depression, schizoaffective disorders, Alzheimer's Disease and cocaine addiction. Mifepristone, a potent glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, can be used in these methods. The invention also provides a kit for the amelioration of psychosis in a human including a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist and instructional material teaching the indications, dosage and schedule of administration of the glucocorticoid receptor antagonist.
problem: Treating psychosis-related conditions (e.g., psychotic major depression, Alzheimer's) by addressing cortisol-mediated pathology.
constraint: The antagonist must be potent and selective for glucocorticoid receptors to avoid off-target effects while effectively inhibiting cortisol activity.
mechanism: Inhibiting a pathological biological pathway by selectively blocking a receptor-ligand interaction, where the blocking agent is constrained to bind specifically to a target receptor subtype to prevent downstream symptom expression.
mechanism_raw: Blocking cortisol binding to glucocorticoid receptors using a receptor antagonist (e.g., mifepristone) to interrupt the biological pathway driving psychosis-associated symptoms.

abstract: A technique for adjusting the trim of a dual electric motor marine propulsion system is provided wherein offset or calibration signal levels are determined through a calibration sequence. The propulsion units are driven in a nominal direction, such as through a “straight-ahead” command. An operator adjusts levels of drive signals to the propulsion units to compensate for deviation from the desired navigational direction, such as due to mechanical and electrical tolerances and variations, as well as due to inherent torques or moments associated with the propulsion units. When the system is determined to navigate the craft in the desired direction, the offset or calibration values are stored. The values are then used during later control of the propulsion units as an inherent trim.
problem: Compensating for deviations in marine propulsion direction caused by mechanical/electrical tolerances and inherent torque variations.
constraint: Calibration must occur during a known nominal state (e.g., 'straight-ahead' command) to isolate systematic errors from transient disturbances.
mechanism: Capturing systematic error offsets during a known reference state by adjusting control signal baselines, storing these offsets as persistent correction values to compensate for deviations during subsequent operation.
mechanism_raw: Performing a calibration sequence where an operator adjusts drive signal levels during nominal-direction operation, storing these offsets as inherent trim values for later use in correcting deviations.

abstract: Specific apparatus and associated methods are described for use in establishing the positions of locating field detectors and for path mapping within a region for the purpose of tracking and/or guiding the movement of an underground boring tool. In one aspect, an improvement is provided forming part of an arrangement for tracking the position and/or guiding the boring tool using an electromagnetic locating signal which is transmitted from the boring tool as the boring tool moves through the ground. At least two detectors are located at fixed positions within the region, each being operable in a transmit mode and in a receive mode such that each one of the detectors in the transmit mode is able to transmit a relative locating signal to the other detector for use in determining the relative position of one detector in relation to the other and such that both detectors receive the electromagnetic locating signal in the receive mode for use in determining the position of the boring tool within the region. Provisions are also described for extending drilling range by using additional detectors by moving a limited number of detectors. In another aspect, a system is provided including at least two above ground detectors for sensing the locating signal. The detectors are located at initial positions in the region. Electromagnetic data is generated by the detectors with the boring tool at multiple positions to generate electromagnetic data which is used to identify the positions of the detectors. A selected flux pathline steering technique is introduced.
problem: Tracking and guiding an underground boring tool's position within a region using electromagnetic signals.
constraint: Limited detector count is mitigated by relocating detectors to extend drilling range, requiring dynamic reconfiguration of the tracking network.
mechanism: Dynamically reconfiguring a distributed sensor network by enabling bidirectional communication between sensors to self-calibrate relative positions, while collectively receiving a target signal to map spatial trajectory.
mechanism_raw: Using detectors that switch between transmit and receive modes to self-calibrate their relative positions via inter-detector signal exchange, while collectively receiving the boring tool's locating signal to map its path.
residual_terms: ["inter-detector signal exchange", "boring tool's locating signal", "transmit and receive modes"]

abstract: A missile nose is tiltable and rotatable relative to a missile body through the action of an actuator system. In an exemplary embodiment, the actuator systems uses two electro-mechanical actuators mounted co-axially and having the output shaft of one actuator fed through the shaft of the other. One of the actuators controls a tilt angle between a longitudinal axis of the body and a longitudinal axis of the nose. The other actuator rotates the nose about the longitudinal axis of the body. A method of steering a missile includes using the actuator system to maintain the missile nose pointed at a target or other desired destination.
problem: Steering a missile nose to maintain alignment with a target or desired trajectory.
constraint: Coaxial arrangement must accommodate nested shafts to avoid mechanical interference while transmitting torque for both tilt and rotation.
mechanism: Achieving independent control of two rotational degrees of freedom using nested coaxial actuators, where each actuator adjusts a distinct orientation parameter without mechanical interference between the two motion axes.
mechanism_raw: Employing two coaxial electro-mechanical actuators—one controlling tilt angle between the nose and body axis, the other controlling rotational orientation—enabling independent adjustment of two degrees of freedom.

abstract: The invention provides a thin high-strength hot-rolled steel sheet with a thickness of not more than 3.5 mm which has excellent stretch flangeability and high uniformity in both shape and mechanical properties of the steel sheet, as well as a method of producing the hot-rolled steel sheet. A slab containing C: 0.05-0.30 wt %, Si: 0.03-1.0 wt %, Mn: 1.5-3.5 wt %, P: not more than 0.02 wt %, S: not more than 0.005 wt %, Al: not more than 0.150 wt %, N: not more than 0.0200 wt %, and one or two of Nb: 0.003-0.20 wt % and Ti: 0.005-0.20 wt % is heated at a temperature of not higher than 1200° C. The slab is hot-rolled at a finish rolling end temperature of not lower than 800° C., preferably at a finish rolling start temperature of 950-1050° C. A hot-rolled sheet is started to be cooled within two seconds after the end of the rolling, and then continuously cooled down to a coiling temperature at a cooling rate of 20-150° C./sec. The hot-rolled sheet is coiled at a temperature of 300-550° C., preferably in excess of 400° C. A fine bainite structure is obtained in which the mean grain size is not greater than 3.0 &mgr;m, the aspect ratio is not more than 1.5, and preferably the maximum size of the major axis is not greater than 10 &mgr;m.
problem: Producing a thin, high-strength hot-rolled steel sheet with uniform mechanical properties and stretch flangeability.
constraint: Cooling must initiate within two seconds of rolling completion to prevent grain coarsening, balancing cooling rate and coiling temperature to achieve the desired phase transformation.
mechanism: Controlling solidification kinetics by regulating cooling rate and terminal temperature after forming to rapidly establish a fine-grained microstructure with specified grain size and morphology.
mechanism_raw: Controlling cooling rate (20–150°C/sec) and coiling temperature (300–550°C) after hot-rolling to rapidly solidify a fine bainite microstructure with sub-3.0 µm grain size and low aspect ratio.

abstract: A combined RF-DC magnetron sputtering method stops the production of tracking arcs and promotes the consistent manufacture of thin films during the manufacture of thin films by such RF-DC magnetron sputtering. Magnets 121, 122 are placed behind the target 111. RF and DC power are simultaneously supplied to the target to produce a plasma, and sputtering is used to manufacture a thin film on a substrate 106 facing the target. The supply of RF and DC power to the target is simultaneously and periodically stopped. The time that the power is supplied is shorter than the time needed to produce tracking arcs. The RF and DC power is both supplied and stopped simultaneously, and RF and DC power is intermittently supplied to the target.
problem: Tracking arcs and inconsistent thin film production during RF-DC magnetron sputtering.
constraint: Power-on time must be precisely controlled to remain below the threshold for arc initiation while still enabling effective sputtering.
mechanism: Cyclically applying and removing energy input to a plasma generation system, where the active duration is shorter than the time required for unstable discharge formation, thereby suppressing arc initiation while sustaining plasma-mediated material deposition.
mechanism_raw: Intermittently supplying and stopping RF and DC power simultaneously, with power-on duration shorter than the time required to generate tracking arcs, thereby preventing arc formation while maintaining plasma-driven sputtering.

abstract: A plused radiation produced by an intense optical source is applied to the inner surface of a wooden container having a surface layer of organic and/or mineral deposit. Each pulse is of sufficiently short duration having sufficiently high treating energy density per unit area to bring about sublimation of the surface layer. The resulting exposed container surface is sanitized by the heat released by the radiation.
problem: Sanitizing surfaces of wooden containers with organic/mineral deposits without damaging the underlying material.
constraint: Pulse duration and energy density must be calibrated to achieve sublimation of the surface layer without excessive thermal damage to the container.
mechanism: Delivering brief, high-intensity energy pulses to a material surface to rapidly remove a thin surface layer through sublimation, using the energy released during the process to sanitize the underlying surface without excessive thermal penetration.
mechanism_raw: Applying short-duration, high-energy radiation pulses to sublimate the surface layer, using the heat released by the radiation to sanitize the exposed surface.

abstract: A chemical sampling sink and method. The chemical sampling sink typically includes an enclosure configured to contain a receptacle, and a chemical supply line extending into the enclosure, the chemical supply line including a dispenser configured to deliver a liquid chemical to the receptacle. The chemical sampling sink also includes an exhaust line attached to the enclosure, the exhaust line being configured to suction gases from the enclosure, and a filter positioned on the enclosure, the filter being configured to remove contaminants from air drawn into the enclosure as gases are suctioned from the enclosure out the exhaust line.
reason: The patent describes a system of components (enclosure, supply line, exhaust, filter) arranged to handle chemicals and gases, but does not describe a causal functional mechanism beyond standard containment and filtration principles.

abstract: A field effect floating gate transistor forming an NVRAM cell is disclosed. A substrate having field isolation structures includes therebetween a doped region forming a channel connecting a source and drain. An oxide layer is disposed over said channel forming a tunneling oxide layer for the device. A layer of polysilicon extends over the oxide layer, to each of the isolation structures and then extends upwards forming a U-shaped pillar floating gate. A second oxide layer disposed within the interior of the U-shaped floating gate supports a control gate. A second layer of polysilicon formed over the second oxide layer forms a control gate, and is connected to a conductor which is common to a row of such cells within a memory. The control gate is coupled to the floating gate through the second oxide layer to the upwardly extending layer of the floating gate as well as over the portion of the floating gate extending over the channel.
problem: Creating a non-volatile memory cell with reliable charge retention and gate coupling in a compact structure.
constraint: The oxide layer thickness and floating gate geometry must balance charge retention, tunneling efficiency, and structural integrity.
mechanism: Employing a shaped charge-storage element positioned over an isolation region and a conduction channel, with a control element capacitively coupled through dielectric layers to multiple portions of the storage element, enabling charge transfer and retention in a compact configuration.
mechanism_raw: Using a U-shaped floating gate extending over isolation structures and a channel, with a control gate capacitively coupled through oxide layers to both the upward and channel-facing portions of the floating gate, enabling charge tunneling and retention.

abstract: A novelty hat for providing headwear that may be decorated to resemble racing vehicles. The novelty hat includes a decorative hat shell resembling a vehicle. The shell is formed of a plastic and has a top wall, a front wall, a rear wall, a first lateral side wall, a second lateral side wall such that an interior of the shell is defined. The shell has an open bottom side for access into the interior of the shell. A head engaging member is positioned in the interior of the shell and is attached to the first and second lateral side walls.
reason: The patent describes a novelty hat with a decorative shell and head-engaging member, but lacks a causal functional mechanism beyond basic product design and ergonomics.

abstract: A compact core and effect yarn producing texturing machine which employs a face plate on which the core and effect yarn godets are mounted in one area of the face plate and another pair of godets are mounted in another area of the space plate. A loop breaker is mounted on said face plate between the godets of the ones mounted in another area of the face plate to break the loops of yarn produced in an air jet mounted between the core and effect yarn godets and the other set of godets.
problem: Producing core and effect yarns with controlled loops in a compact texturing machine where loops formed by an air jet must be selectively broken without disrupting the continuous yarn path.
constraint: The face plate must accommodate all godets, the air jet, and the loop breaker in a compact layout while maintaining proper yarn path geometry and tension control between the two processing zones.
mechanism: A continuous filament is guided through two spatially separated processing zones mounted on a shared support structure. In the first zone, a fluid jet induces controlled loops in the filament. In the second zone, a mechanical disruption element selectively breaks the loops. The spatial separation of loop formation and loop breaking along the filament path enables sequential processing without interrupting the continuous motion of the filament.
mechanism_raw: Godets are mounted in two spatially separated areas on a single face plate, with an air jet positioned between the two areas to form loops in the yarn, and a loop breaker positioned between the godets in the second area to break those loops. The spatial separation of processing zones on a shared mounting plate creates a sequential operation where loop formation and loop breaking occur at distinct stations along the yarn path, enabling compact integration of both functions.

abstract: Rolling stand (10) for plane products and method to control the planarity of said plane products, said rolling stand comprising a pair of working rolls (11a, 11b), a corresponding pair of back-up rolls (13a, 13b) and at least an intermediate roll (15a) located between one of said working rolls (11a) and a corresponding back-up roll (13b), axial translation means (16) and bending means (17) being associated with at least one of said working rolls (11a) to translate it axially and respectively bend it, crossing means (19) being associated with said intermediate roll (15a) to arrange it with its longitudinal axis (25a) inclined, that is, rotated, with respect to the longitudinal axes (21a, 21b, 23a, 23b) of said working rolls (11a, 11b) and of said back-up rolls (13a, 13b).
problem: Controlling the planarity (flatness) of plane products such as metal strips during rolling, where uneven thickness or warping can occur due to non-uniform roll forces.
constraint: The system must balance forces from axial translation, roll bending, and the inclined intermediate roll simultaneously while maintaining roll stability and avoiding over-correction or mechanical interference.
mechanism: A corrective force system applies multi-directional adjustments to a deformable product during processing. An intermediate element positioned between a working element and a back-up element is angled so its axis crosses the axes of the other elements, introducing a transverse corrective component. Additional axial translation and bending adjustments of the working element provide further directional correction. The combined forces balance to correct local planarity deviations while maintaining processing stability.
mechanism_raw: An intermediate roll is positioned between a working roll and its corresponding back-up roll, and is inclined (rotated) so its longitudinal axis crosses the axes of the working and back-up rolls. This inclined intermediate roll, combined with axial translation and bending of at least one working roll, applies multi-directional corrective forces to the strip. The crossing axis of the intermediate roll introduces a transverse force component that, together with axial and bending adjustments, corrects local planarity deviations.

abstract: A device for lubricating a track or a rail that is adapted to be mounted tog wheeled vehicle. The device includes a frame member adapted to be mounted to the vehicle and an arm pivotally attached to the frame member. A roller, which is adapted to ride on the rail, mounts to the arm. A lubricating nozzle is secured to the arm.
problem: Delivering lubricant to a rail or track surface from a vehicle that is in motion, where the distance and angle between the delivery point and the rail surface vary continuously.
constraint: The pivot joint and arm geometry must provide sufficient compliance to accommodate rail irregularities and vehicle motion while keeping the nozzle positioned accurately for effective lubricant application.
mechanism: A dispensing nozzle is attached to a pivotally mounted arm that carries a surface-following element. As the supporting structure moves, the surface-following element tracks the target surface, and the pivotal mounting allows the arm to self-adjust its orientation. This pivoting action maintains the nozzle in a consistent position relative to the contact point between the surface-following element and the target surface, enabling continuous dispensing despite varying distance and angle.
mechanism_raw: A lubricating nozzle is secured to a pivotally mounted arm that carries a roller adapted to ride on the rail. As the vehicle moves, the roller follows the rail surface, and the pivotal mounting allows the arm to self-adjust its orientation, maintaining the nozzle in a consistent position relative to the roller-rail contact point. The pivoting action of the arm translates the roller's surface-following motion into maintained nozzle-to-rail alignment for continuous lubrication delivery.

abstract: A process for the recovery of one or more metal values from a metal ore material comprising those of one or more values and a matrix material having a sulfur content wherein the sulfur is present in an oxidation-reduction state of zero or less comprisinga. forming particulates from particles of said ore and an inoculate comprising bacteria capable of at least partially oxidizing the sulfur content;b. forming a heap of said particulates;c. biooxidizing the sulfur content andd. recovering those one or more metal values.
problem: Recovering valuable metal values from metal ore that is trapped within a sulfur-containing matrix where sulfur is in an oxidation-reduction state of zero or less, making the metals inaccessible by conventional extraction.
constraint: The heap must maintain adequate permeability and moisture for bacterial activity while ensuring uniform distribution of the inoculant and sufficient contact between bacteria and sulfur-bearing particles throughout the biooxidation process.
mechanism: Particulate material containing a target substance within a reactive matrix is combined with a biological or chemical agent that selectively reacts with the matrix material. The combined material is arranged in a bulk configuration that allows distribution of the reactive agent throughout the mass. The agent breaks down the matrix structure, liberating the trapped target substance. The bulk arrangement ensures contact between the agent and matrix throughout the material, enabling subsequent recovery of the target substance.
mechanism_raw: Ore particles are combined with bacteria capable of oxidizing sulfur to form inoculated particulates, which are then piled into a heap. The bacteria biooxidize the sulfur in the matrix, breaking down the sulfur-containing structure and liberating the metal values. The heap configuration distributes the biological oxidation throughout the ore mass, using the bacteria as a selective oxidizing agent that targets sulfur rather than the metals, enabling subsequent metal recovery.

abstract: A conditioning composition for garments to be used before or after conventional washing and drying operations is disclosed. The compositions are suitable for conditioning dry clean only garments. The composition is an aqueous mixture containing a garment conditioning agent wherein the mixture has a fluid viscosity of from about 1 cps to about 100 cps and a fluid surface tension of from about 20 dynes/cm to about 55 dynes/cm. The conditioning composition is in fog form to improve composition deposition on the garments.
problem: Conditioning garments, particularly dry-clean-only items, with a conditioning agent that deposits effectively without conventional washing, where liquid runoff or uneven distribution would reduce efficacy.
constraint: The viscosity and surface tension must be balanced within the specified ranges to enable effective fog formation and droplet stability while ensuring sufficient wetting and deposition on garment fibers without causing damage or excessive penetration.
mechanism: A fluid composition with controlled rheological properties is delivered in dispersed phase form to a surface. The specific viscosity and surface tension ranges ensure droplet stability during delivery while promoting wetting and adhesion to the target surface. The dispersed delivery increases the surface area of the composition, allowing uniform distribution and controlled deposition without excessive runoff or pooling.
mechanism_raw: An aqueous conditioning composition with controlled viscosity (1-100 cps) and surface tension (20-55 dynes/cm) is delivered in fog form. The specific fluid properties ensure the droplets remain small and stable during fogging, while the low surface tension promotes wetting and adhesion to garment fibers. The fog delivery increases the surface area of the composition, allowing uniform distribution and controlled deposition onto the garment surface without excessive runoff.

abstract: This invention relates to a method of storing gas using gas hydrates comprising forming gas hydrates in the presence of a water-surfactant solution that comprises water and surfactant. The addition of minor amounts of surfactant increases the gas hydrate formation rate, increases packing density of the solid hydrate mass and simplifies the formation-storage-decomposition process of gas hydrates. The minor amounts of surfactant also enhance the potential of gas hydrates for industrial storage applications.
problem: Inefficient gas storage using gas hydrates due to slow formation rates, low packing density, and complex processing steps.
constraint: Surfactant concentration must remain minimal to avoid destabilizing the hydrate structure or introducing unwanted chemical interactions.
mechanism: Introducing a surface-active agent into a liquid medium reduces interfacial tension and promotes nucleation, accelerating the formation of a solid-phase material while modifying its structural matrix to increase packing density. The surface-active agent concentration is constrained to a minimal level to avoid destabilizing the solid-phase structure or introducing unwanted chemical interactions.
mechanism_raw: Adding surfactant to a water-surfactant solution accelerates gas hydrate formation by reducing interfacial tension and promoting nucleation, while simultaneously increasing solid hydrate packing density through structural modification of the hydrate matrix.

abstract: Method of electrolytically continuously treating a material of stainless steel at a current density of 0.1-3 A/cm2, wherein the material is passed through one or more electrolytic cells arranged in series. The cells contain an electrolyte selected from sulphuric acid, a salt thereof, phosphoric acid and nitric acid, and the material is passed through the electrolyte between electrodes arranged in series under the influence of a direct current with alternating polarity. The electrodes are arranged alternately anodic and cathodic and every electrode on one side of said material is matched by an electrode of the same polarity on an opposite side of the material, whereby an oxide surface layer with a thickness of at least 1 micrometer is removed from the material to produce a surface conditioning effect.
problem: Ineffective or inconsistent removal of thick oxide layers from stainless steel surfaces during electrolytic treatment.
constraint: Current density must be tightly controlled (0.1–3 A/cm²) to prevent over-etching or damage to the base material.
mechanism: Applying alternating electrical polarity across electrodes arranged symmetrically around a material creates bidirectional electrochemical dissolution, mechanically agitating the surface layer while maintaining uniform current distribution to ensure complete removal. Current density is tightly controlled within a specified range to prevent over-etching or damage to the base material.
mechanism_raw: Alternating direct current polarity across electrodes arranged symmetrically around the material creates bidirectional electrochemical dissolution, mechanically agitating the oxide layer while maintaining uniform current distribution to ensure complete removal.

abstract: Batten elements are made of plastic or metal, such as galvanized steel, galvalume, or aluminum. Several alternate embodiments of battens are shown, along with a schematic illustration of a punch process for making the metal battens of the present invention. The batten elements all include holes or tunnels for the drainage of water through the batten elements. The alternate embodiments are shown in cross section or end view.
reason: The patent describes a static structural feature (holes in battens) for water drainage, which is a straightforward design choice rather than a causal mechanism involving dynamic interactions or process optimization.

abstract: A very versatile device is proposed for high-precision machining of optical workpieces, in particular optical lenses, which comprises a horizontally displaceable gantry with at least one vertically displaceable tool spindle and a yoke with workpiece holding means mounted so as to be rotatable about a swivel axis by means of journals fitted on both sides. For swivelling of the yoke without gearing and therefore without backlash, a torque motor is provided concentrically to the swivel axis, which motor is directly connected actively with one of the journals.
problem: Mechanical backlash and imprecision in rotational systems caused by traditional gear-based actuation.
constraint: The motor must be precisely aligned with the swivel axis to maintain concentricity and avoid mechanical stress.
mechanism: Directly coupling a motor to a rotating element using electromagnetic forces enables backlash-free rotation by precisely controlling angular position through direct torque application. The motor must be precisely aligned with the rotational axis to maintain concentricity and avoid mechanical stress.
mechanism_raw: A torque motor directly coupled to a journal eliminates intermediate gearing, enabling backlash-free rotation by using electromagnetic forces to precisely control angular position through direct torque application.

abstract: A multi-layer ceramic heater for igniting fuel in a diesel engine having an electrode, an insulative layer disposed over the electrode, a resistive layer disposed over the insulative layer at the tip of the heater, and a conductive layer covering the insulative layer and extending from the resistive layer over the insulative layer to the base of heater. A substantial proportion of the volume of resistive layer is located in close proximity to the tip of heater. The resistive layer has a positive temperature coefficient (PTC) of electrical resistance and preferably a portion of the electrode is variably resistive for self regulation purposes. Due to the geometry of the resistive layer and the variable resistive characteristics of the resistive layer and the electrode, the heater is well suited to applications that require quick start heating as well as good afterglow properties or prolonged heating at high temperatures.
problem: Inability to achieve both rapid heating and sustained high-temperature operation in ceramic heaters due to fixed resistivity and thermal runaway risks.
constraint: Material composition and layer thickness must be optimized to balance PTC behavior with thermal stability and mechanical durability.
mechanism: Utilizing a positive temperature coefficient resistive layer combined with a variably resistive electrode enables self-regulation: resistance increases with temperature to limit current flow, while geometric placement of the resistive layer near the active region ensures rapid heat generation and controlled afterglow. Material composition and layer thickness are optimized to balance self-regulation behavior with thermal stability and mechanical durability.
mechanism_raw: A positive temperature coefficient (PTC) resistive layer combined with a variably resistive electrode enables self-regulation: resistance increases with temperature to limit current flow, while geometric placement of the resistive layer near the tip ensures rapid heat generation and controlled afterglow.

abstract: A method and apparatus for coating a paper or board web, wherein the web to be coated is brought to a film transfer coater and taken to a nip between the film transfer roll of the coater and its backing roll, and coating mix is applied onto the surface of the film transfer roll. The web is taken through the nip between the rolls and the rolls are turned, whereby the coating mix applied onto the applicator roll is at least partly transferred onto the surface of the web. The web is supported through the nip by means of a belt traveling at the same speed as the web, the belt having been arranged to travel on the backing roll. The web is taken onto the surface of the belt prior to the nip and separated from the belt after the nip, and it is pressed against the film transfer roll by means of the belt. The length of the path where the web and the film transfer roll are in contact with each other is controlled by varying the position of the web and the belt.
problem: Ensuring uniform coating transfer onto a moving web while dynamically controlling the contact duration between the web and the applicator roll in a film transfer coater.
constraint: Balancing belt speed synchronization with the web to maintain consistent pressure and contact time without introducing mechanical slippage or uneven coating distribution.
mechanism: A flexible belt moves in synchronization with a continuous web, supporting the web through a nip region formed between two opposing rolls. The belt's position is adjusted relative to the web to control the length of contact between the web and one of the rolls, thereby regulating the duration of interaction and the uniformity of material transfer.
mechanism_raw: A belt traveling at the same speed as the web supports the web through the nip between the film transfer roll and backing roll. The belt's position relative to the web is adjusted to control the length of contact between the web and the film transfer roll, thereby regulating coating transfer efficiency and uniformity.

abstract: A novel computer-controlled video microscopy system, features a rotatable objective lens turret. The lens turret is a rotatable cylindrical drum having an open end and closed end. A plurality of light-transmitting objective lenses are evenly spaced about the side wall of the cylindrical drum. The objective lenses are each directed perpendicularly to the axis of rotation of the cylindrical drum. A computer is used to select a desired objective lens and signal a motor to rotate the cylindrical drum about its axis of rotation, so as to move the selected objective lens into the path of an approaching light beam. When the light beam enters the drum through the objective lens, a prism or mirror inside the cylindrical drum bends the light beam at a right angle and directs it out of the drum through its open end. An image carried by the light beam is then focused onto the imaging plane of a video camera. The microscope also features a computer-controlled stage which moves a sample in any direction in the x-y plane and an illumination system using either transmitted light or incident light.
problem: Rapidly switching between multiple objective lenses in a video microscopy system without manual intervention or mechanical realignment of the entire optical path.
constraint: Achieving precise rotational alignment of the turret to ensure the selected lens is accurately positioned in the light path while minimizing switching time and mechanical wear.
mechanism: A rotatable platform with multiple optical elements arranged at discrete angular positions is rotated to align a selected element into a light path. An internal reflective element redirects the light beam at a fixed angle, allowing the image to be focused onto a detector regardless of the platform's rotational orientation.
mechanism_raw: A rotatable cylindrical turret with evenly spaced objective lenses is rotated by a motor to align a selected lens into the light path. A prism or mirror inside the turret redirects the light beam at a right angle, allowing the image to be focused onto a video camera regardless of the turret's rotational position.

abstract: A pair of refiner members comprises respective refiner bars which cooperate to refine pulp. At least one the refiner bars extends in a spiral pattern for imparting a screw-like pumping action to the pulp. The refiner bars of the cooperating refiner members have different pitch to produce a differential pumping action and increase crossovers between the refiner members in order to improve refining. A sinuous curvature can also be introduced in the spiral pattern to further increase crossovers between the refiner members.
problem: Improving the refining of pulp by increasing the interaction between refiner bars to enhance fiber separation and mixing during the refining process.
constraint: Optimizing the pitch difference and spiral curvature to maximize fiber interaction and refining effectiveness while avoiding excessive energy consumption or mechanical wear.
mechanism: Interacting surfaces are arranged in a helical pattern with differential spacing between opposing members. This creates a progressive movement and differential interaction, increasing crossover points between the surfaces. A curved helical geometry further amplifies these interactions to enhance processing efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Refiner bars are arranged in a spiral pattern with differential pitch between cooperating refiner members. This creates a screw-like pumping action and differential movement, increasing crossovers between the bars. A sinuous curvature in the spiral further amplifies these crossovers to improve refining efficiency.

abstract: A processing apparatus, method and recirculation system utilizes a level sensing probe in a filter housing of the filter assembly. The level sensing probe is adapted to provide a signal to a controller arrangement that includes at least a level sensing circuit, a central processing unit and a solid state relay. The controller arrangement is adapted to shut off a heating element of the filter assembly whenever the solution in the filter housing as defined by the level sensing probe falls below an acceptable minimum level of processing solution. With the arrangement of the present invention, it is possible to maintain re-circulated and/or replenished processing solution in the filter housing at an acceptable minimum level, and whenever the solution falls below such a level the heating element is shut off so as to prevent the overheating of the components of the filter assembly.
problem: Preventing overheating of components in a filter assembly when the processing solution level drops below a safe minimum during recirculation or replenishment.
constraint: Ensuring the level sensing probe's accuracy and response time are sufficient to trigger shutdown before overheating occurs, while maintaining reliable operation of the recirculation system.
mechanism: A sensing element continuously monitors the level of a processing medium within a containment vessel and transmits a signal to a control circuit. The control circuit automatically interrupts power to a heating element when the medium level falls below a predetermined threshold, preventing thermal damage to system components.
mechanism_raw: A level sensing probe in the filter housing continuously monitors the solution level and sends a signal to a controller. The controller, comprising a level sensing circuit, CPU, and solid-state relay, automatically shuts off the heating element when the solution level falls below the acceptable minimum, preventing component damage.

abstract: A handpiece having at least one set of piezoelectric elements. The piezoelectric elements are constructed of segments that produce both longitudinal and torsional motion. An appropriate ultrasound driver drives the set of elements at the respective resonant frequencies to product longitudinal vibration and torsional oscillation.
problem: Generating both longitudinal and torsional motion in a single handpiece for applications requiring combined vibrational and oscillatory effects.
constraint: Designing the piezoelectric segments and driver circuitry to resonate at distinct frequencies for longitudinal and torsional modes without interference, ensuring efficient energy transfer and motion coherence.
mechanism: Energizable elements are divided into segments configured to produce two distinct modes of mechanical motion. A driver applies signals at the respective resonant frequencies of the segments, causing them to vibrate in a first mode and oscillate in a second mode simultaneously.
mechanism_raw: Piezoelectric elements are segmented to produce both longitudinal and torsional motion. An ultrasound driver applies signals at the respective resonant frequencies of the elements, causing them to vibrate longitudinally and oscillate torsionally simultaneously.

abstract: An auto-controller is adapted for incorporating with a battery charger to charge a battery by using a thermo-control and current balance technology for extending a service life span of the battery while being cost effective. The auto-controller includes a resistor having a predetermined resistance for electrically connecting to the battery charger wherein the resistor generates heat when a predetermined current flows through that defines a reference temperature for the battery charger, and a thermo sensor operatively positioned adjacent to the resistor for detecting the reference temperature and selectively switching the battery charger on and off, whereby when the reference temperature is above a control temperature preset in the thermo sensor, the battery charger is switched off to not function and when the reference temperature is below the control temperature, the battery charger is maintained in a switch-on condition to continuously charge a battery.
problem: Extending battery service life while maintaining cost-effective charging control.
constraint: Balancing cost (using simple resistor/thermistor components) with precise thermal regulation to avoid battery degradation.
mechanism: A resistive heating element generates heat proportional to current flow, establishing a thermal reference. A temperature sensor detects this heat and switches the charging circuit on or off based on a preset threshold, forming a feedback loop that regulates charging to prevent overheating while using low-cost components.
mechanism_raw: A resistor generates heat proportional to current flow, creating a thermal reference. A thermo sensor detects this temperature and toggles the charger on/off based on a preset threshold, forming a feedback loop that regulates charging to prevent overheating.

abstract: A semi-automatic handgun is disclosed including a frame having a barrel housing mounted thereon. A barrel is movably mounted on the barrel housing and has a cartridge chamber at its rearward end for receiving a cartridge therein. The barrel is movable between a rearward position and a forward position with respect to the barrel housing and is normally in its rearward position. The barrel moves forwardly in a straight line from its rearward position upon firing of the cartridge in the chamber to counteract the rearward energy of discharge, thereby reducing recoil. The handgun may be fired in either a single action or double action manner. The firing hammer of the handgun is re-cocked, upon firing of the cartridge, by means of a movable piston having a firing pin positioned therein with the firing pin engaging the hammer to move the hammer to its re-cocked position.
problem: Reducing recoil energy during firing while enabling automatic re-cocking of the hammer.
constraint: Mechanical linkage must synchronize barrel movement and hammer re-cocking without compromising firing cycle timing or reliability.
mechanism: Forward motion of a barrel during discharge counteracts rearward recoil forces. A piston with an engaging element transfers energy from this motion to mechanically re-cock a striking mechanism for subsequent cycles, synchronizing movement and re-cocking without external actuation.
mechanism_raw: Barrel forward motion during discharge counteracts rearward recoil forces. A piston with a firing pin engages the hammer during this motion, mechanically transferring energy to re-cock the hammer for subsequent shots.

abstract: A padded shoe includes a shoe upper which is adjoined to a sole. The shoe upper and the sole can have padding material disposed therein. The shoe upper includes a padded tongue, which can have an inner tongue portion and an outer tongue portion. A fastening structure, which can be tightenable to maintain the shoe on the foot of the wearer, can be disposed between the inner and outer tongue portions. Alternatively, a resilient portion can be connected to the shoe upper, whereby a portion of the shoe upper can be outwardly distended to allow insertion of the foot of the wearer. The shoe can include an engagement structure to secure the outer tongue portion to at least one of the inner tongue portion and the shoe upper.
reason: The patent describes product features (padding, fastening structures) rather than a causal mechanism. The 'resilient portion' and 'engagement structure' are static design elements, not a functional principle that produces an effect through interaction.

abstract: Disclosed herein is a multi-layer golf ball having a high Mooney viscosity polybutadiene core, an inner cover layer comprising at least one ionomer (preferably at least one high flow ionomer resin) and having Shore D hardness of about 65 or less, and an outer cover layer having a different composition than the inner cover layer, comprising an ionomer, and having a Shore D hardness of more than 65. The sum of the thickness of the inner cover layer and the thickness of the outer cover layer is greater than 0.090 inches. A method for making the golf ball also is disclosed.
reason: The patent focuses on material composition and layer hardness values rather than a causal mechanism. The 'multi-layer structure' is a static architectural choice, not a dynamic functional relationship that generates an effect.

abstract: An air transducer apparatus comprising a curved piezoelectric film having a first surface and a second surface opposite the first surface, a first electrode layer disposed on at least a portion of the first surface of the film; and a second electrode layer disposed on a portion of the second surface of the film defining the second electrode layer being sized less than the first electrode layer for generating a signal in response to acoustic energy incident on the piezoelectric film.
problem: Generating an electrical signal from incident acoustic energy using a flexible transducer.
constraint: Electrode size differential must balance signal sensitivity with structural integrity of the curved film under varying acoustic loads.
mechanism: A curved piezoelectric film deforms under acoustic pressure, inducing charge displacement. Electrode layers of unequal size on opposing surfaces create an asymmetric electric field, amplifying the signal output from the mechanical deformation.
mechanism_raw: A curved piezoelectric film deforms under acoustic pressure, inducing charge displacement. Electrode layers of unequal size on opposing surfaces create an asymmetric electric field, amplifying the signal output from the mechanical deformation.

abstract: A low stretch elevator rope (10) is obtained in which a plastic core (12) has a central strength member (18) that does not increase the weight of the rope by more than 5%. Moreover, the plastic core (12) has a diameter exceeding 50% of the diameter of the rope (10), when measured prior to winding steel strands (14) onto the core (12). The steel strands (14) that are wound around the core (12) are conventional and are so wound that the plastic material of the core (12) essentially fills the inner interstices (16) between the steel strands (14).
problem: Creating an elevator rope that achieves low stretch while maintaining high strength, without adding excessive weight from the core strength member.
constraint: The central strength member must not increase rope weight by more than 5%, and the plastic core diameter must exceed 50% of the total rope diameter before strand winding. The tradeoff balances stretch reduction (plastic core) against tensile strength (steel strands) and weight minimization.
mechanism: A composite structure uses two materials with complementary mechanical properties arranged in a coaxial configuration, where one material provides compliance and the other provides tensile strength. The compliant material fills interstitial spaces between the strength-providing elements, creating intimate contact and load sharing. A geometric constraint ensures the compliant material dominates the cross-sectional area to minimize stretch, while the strength elements maintain overall tensile capacity without excessive weight addition.
mechanism_raw: A composite rope structure uses a plastic core with a central strength member, where steel strands are wound around the core such that the plastic material of the core essentially fills the inner interstices between the steel strands. This creates intimate contact and load sharing between the plastic core (providing low-stretch compliance) and the steel strands (providing tensile strength), while the geometric constraint of the core diameter exceeding 50% of the rope diameter ensures the plastic dominates the cross-section for stretch reduction.

abstract: A beaver controlling culvert attachment prevents beavers from disturbing the flow of water through a culvert. An upstream unit includes a vertical pipe having an upper grate, which prevents the entrance of beavers and debris, while allowing the entrance of water during periods of high water levels. A horizontal pipe has an upstream end attached to an upper portion of the vertical pipe and a downstream end attached to an upstream end of the culvert by an attachment plate. A basket insert is carried within the vertical pipe, and is movable between an in-use position, wherein a grate prevents entrance to the bottom of the vertical pipe, and a clean-out position wherein the grill is elevated to allow disposal of accumulated debris through the horizontal pipe and culvert. A downstream grate prevents beavers from entering the downstream end of the culvert, and from filling the culvert with debris.
problem: Preventing beavers from blocking water flow through culverts by building dams or accumulating debris, while still allowing periodic maintenance and debris removal.
constraint: The basket must be movable between two discrete positions — in-use (blocking) and clean-out (elevated/open) — and the system must maintain exclusion at both upstream and downstream ends of the culvert simultaneously. The tradeoff is between continuous flow exclusion and periodic maintenance accessibility.
mechanism: A selectively positionable barrier element within a flow channel alternates between a blocking state (preventing ingress of objects or debris at the channel inlet) and an open state (allowing accumulated material to be removed through the channel). The barrier maintains exclusion functionality at both upstream and downstream boundaries during normal operation, but can be temporarily repositioned to enable maintenance without full removal.
mechanism_raw: A selectively movable basket insert within a vertical pipe alternates between an in-use position (blocking the bottom of the pipe to prevent beaver/debris entry) and a clean-out position (elevated to allow accumulated debris to be flushed through the horizontal pipe and culvert). This creates a reversible barrier that maintains exclusion during normal operation but can be temporarily opened for maintenance without removing the entire structure.
residual_terms: ["selectively positionable barrier element", "flow channel", "blocking state", "open state"]

abstract: The invention is directed to a DNA probe set, the probe set comprising a first probe set and a second probe set, the first probe set being sufficient in length and substantially complementary to an entire breakpoint region of a first DNA and nucleotides breakpoint region but less than an entire chromosome such that the first probe set will hybridize to both sides of the breakpoint region regardless of whether the first DNA has been broken in the breakpoint region and either end fused to another DNA, and the second probe set being sufficient in length and substantially complementary to an entire breakpoint region of a second DNA and nucleotides on both sides of the breakpoint region but less than an entire chromosome such that the second probe set will hybridize to both sides of the breakpoint region regardless of whether the second DNA has been broken in the breakpoint region and either end fused to another DNA. Diagnostic kits utilizing the probe sets of the invention are also claimed.
problem: Detecting DNA breakpoints in genetic material regardless of whether the DNA has been broken and fused to another DNA, ensuring reliable diagnosis across different structural states of the target.
constraint: Each probe set must be sufficient in length to cover the breakpoint region on both sides but less than an entire chromosome, ensuring specificity while maintaining coverage. The tradeoff balances probe length (longer = more specific but harder to synthesize/manipulate) against the need to span variable breakpoint locations.
mechanism: Detection probes are designed with bidirectional sequence complementarity spanning a variable target region, where each probe set covers sufficient length on both sides of a potential breakpoint to ensure hybridization regardless of whether the target sequence is intact or structurally altered. This creates a detection system where at least one probe in each set will bind successfully across all possible structural states of the target.
