mechanism_raw: Probe sets are designed to be complementary to and span the entire breakpoint region on both sides of the breakpoint, with sufficient length to hybridize to both flanking sequences regardless of whether the DNA is intact or broken-and-fused. This bidirectional coverage ensures that at least one probe in the set will bind successfully whether the breakpoint is present or absent, creating a detection system robust to structural variation.

abstract: The invention provides an image forming apparatus having sheet supply device, image forming device for forming an image on a sheet supplied by the sheet supply device, fixing device for fixing the image formed on the sheet, a sheet guide for guiding the movement of the sheet, and a control board bearing an element for controlling the image forming device, wherein the sheet guide positioned between the sheet supply device and the fixing device is provided substantially linearly in such a manner that the sheet moves in an inclined upward direction, and the control board is provided in a space under the sheet guide and at the bottom face of the apparatus.
reason: The patent describes a static spatial arrangement of components (sheet guide positioned linearly in an inclined upward direction, control board placed under the sheet guide) without describing a causal functional relationship that produces a useful effect. It is essentially component placement optimization rather than a problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A hand tool for forming a slot between the outer cylindrical surface of a manhole frame, and the concrete in which the frame is embedded. The tool has a tool body with a bottom surface that engages the soft concrete in which the frame is embedded, and a concave lip for slidably engaging the outer surface of the manhole frame or any other circular or cylindrical object.
problem: Forming a slot or gap between the outer cylindrical surface of a manhole frame (or similar cylindrical object) and the surrounding concrete or embedding material, particularly when the concrete is still soft.
constraint: The bottom surface must engage the soft concrete while the concave lip simultaneously engages the cylindrical frame, requiring the tool geometry to accommodate both a flat/planar surface and a curved/cylindrical surface. The tradeoff is between conforming to the cylinder (concave lip) and maintaining a stable base against the concrete (flat bottom).
mechanism: A hand tool employs two geometrically complementary contact surfaces: one surface engages a planar substrate to establish a stable reference plane, while a second surface with opposing curvature conforms to a cylindrical object. Relative motion between the tool and the cylindrical object, constrained by the planar reference, creates a controlled gap between the two surfaces through differential displacement.
mechanism_raw: A hand tool uses two complementary contact surfaces: a bottom surface that engages and bears against the soft concrete (providing a stable reference plane), and a concave lip that slidably engages the outer cylindrical surface of the frame. As the tool is moved, the combination of the flat bottom pressing into the concrete and the concave lip conforming to the cylinder creates a controlled gap between the two surfaces, effectively forming the desired slot.
residual_terms: ["geometrically complementary contact surfaces", "planar substrate", "opposing curvature", "differential displacement"]

abstract: A retaining device of a scooter battery set comprises a support frame mounted on the scooter and provided with a support rod, and insertion portion, and a retaining portion, a battery box having at least one insertion portion, a hanging seat connected with the battery box and provided with a hanging portion, a retaining member pivoted to the hanging seat and provided with a wrenching portion and a retaining portion, and a handle set fastened with the insertion portion of the battery box and provided with a handle. As the handle is lifted or pressed downward, the retaining member is actuated to catch or separate from the retaining portion of the support frame.
problem: Securely attaching and detaching a battery box to a scooter while enabling easy user operation.
constraint: Balancing user accessibility with mechanical reliability to ensure secure retention without complex manual adjustments.
mechanism: A user-applied linear motion on a handle is converted into rotational movement of a pivoted retaining member, which engages or disengages with a fixed structure to selectively secure or release a component.
mechanism_raw: A handle's lifting or pressing motion directly actuates a pivoted retaining member, translating linear input into rotational engagement or disengagement with a fixed retaining portion on the support frame.

abstract: A robot system having a plurality of component units. The robot system includes a first storage device, and a second storage device. The robot system further includes a plurality of control device, with a first component control device provided with the first component and a second component control device provided with the second component wherein the first component control device controls the first component device and the second component control device controls the second component.
reason: The abstract describes a generic modular control architecture without specifying a causal relationship or novel functional principle beyond standard component-based control.

abstract: A system for modifying the surface temperature and/or relative humidity of golf greens or other grass playing fields by applying temperature controlled air and/or a water mist through pop-up nozzles. The nozzles are controlled by a central control panel which activates the nozzles based on input from temperature sensitive probes in the greens.
problem: Maintaining optimal surface temperature and humidity for grass playing fields despite environmental variability.
constraint: Precisely coordinating nozzle activation timing and output to avoid over-saturation or thermal shock while maintaining uniform field conditions.
mechanism: Environmental sensors provide real-time measurements to a controller, which selectively actuates distributed dispensers to apply conditioned fluid, forming a closed-loop feedback system that maintains target environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: Temperature-sensitive probes feed real-time data to a central control panel, which dynamically activates pop-up nozzles to apply temperature-controlled air or water mist, forming a closed-loop feedback system.

abstract: A stylized writing instrument shaped like a proprietary or familiar object. Embodiments include a housing shaped like the proprietary or familiar object, a writing implement, and internal mechanisms provided within the housing for extending the writing implement from, and retracting the writing implement into, the housing. The internal mechanisms may comprise a wide variety of actuation systems for extending and retracting the writing implement, including a cam actuation assembly, an edge slide actuation assembly, a gravity actuation assembly, a pressure actuation assembly and a push button actuation assembly.
reason: The abstract lists multiple actuation methods (cam, gravity, push button, etc.) as generic options without specifying a unique causal mechanism or functional relationship beyond standard mechanical extension/retraction systems.

abstract: An article, such as an artist's canvas (12), having at least one touch sensitive area (14) on its surface is carried in a device (10) comprising a base (16), side walls (18, 19, 20, 21), and a cross-member (22) extending across the device (10) in a position spaced from the base (16). A plurality of contact pins (24) are carried by the cross-member (22) and extend towards the base (16). The location of the contact pins (24) on the cross-member (22) can be adjusted, thereby to enable the contact pins (24) to make contact with the article (12) at positions spaced from the touch sensitive area (14).
problem: Handling or supporting a touch-sensitive article (e.g., an artist's canvas) without interfering with its sensitive surface regions.
constraint: Maintaining structural support and positional stability while ensuring no contact occurs on the touch-sensitive surface during handling or transport.
mechanism: Adjustable support elements mounted on a structural member can be positioned to contact a handled article at locations deliberately offset from sensitive surface regions, transferring support forces while avoiding contact with those regions.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable contact pins mounted on a cross-member can be repositioned to make physical contact with the article at locations deliberately spaced away from touch-sensitive areas, decoupling support forces from sensitive regions.

abstract: An extrudable black body decoy flare composition which, when combusted, provided black body radiation is disclosed. The compositions generally include from about 40% to about 70% metal such as magnesium or aluminum, from about 10% to about 40% polytetrafluoroethylene, and from about 8% to about 30% binder. Important to the operation of the invention is the production of carbon upon combustion of the composition. Accordingly, polyaromatic thermoplastics, such as polystyrene and dimethyl phthalate, serve as the binder.
reason: The mechanism is tightly coupled to specific pyrotechnic materials (e.g., metal, PTFE, polyaromatic thermoplastic binder) and their combustion chemistry. While the production of carbon via binder decomposition is a functional step, it is not a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: The present invention relates to a device and method for electrolytic deposition of metals on conducting particles. The conducting particles are completely immersed in a liquid and allowed to flow across a particle contacting surface of a cathode support. The particles flow across the surface and into a reservoir. Electrical contact is made between the negative pole of a DC power supply and the conducting particles. An anode mesh is placed above and parallel to the top face of the particle bed such that the mesh does not touch the particle bed but remains a controlled distance from it. The anode mesh is connected to the positive terminal of the DC power supply. A significant aspect of the present invention is that the device does not require a separator between the particle bed and the anode.
problem: Electrolytic deposition of metals on conducting particles without requiring a physical separator between the anode and the particle bed.
constraint: The anode-to-particle distance must be precisely controlled to balance deposition efficiency and electrical isolation.
mechanism: A spatially separated anode and particle bed are maintained at a controlled distance to enable ion-mediated material transfer while preventing direct electrical contact. Dynamic movement of the particle bed ensures continuous avoidance of shorting without requiring a static barrier.
mechanism_raw: A controlled gap is maintained between the anode mesh and the flowing particle bed, allowing ion transport and deposition while preventing direct electrical contact. This eliminates the need for a separator by leveraging spatial separation and dynamic particle movement to avoid shorting.

abstract: A composite textile fabric for wicking moisture away from the skin of the wearer and transporting moisture from its skin-side surface to the opposite surface. The fabric includes a first fabric layer which has been rendered hydrophilic in order to quickly wick perspiration and other body fluids away from the skin of the user, and includes a relative high denier; and a second fabric layer which has been rendered hydrophilic, and includes filaments which is processed by peach finish sueding. The second filaments have a relatively low denier in order to pull perspiration and other body fluids from the first fabric layer.
problem: Efficiently transporting moisture away from the skin to the opposite side of a textile fabric.
constraint: Balancing denier ratios and surface treatments to optimize absorption speed and directional transport without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A composite structure with layered elements of differing capillary properties establishes a directional transport pathway. A high-capacity absorption layer rapidly captures fluid, while a processed surface layer with reduced fiber density creates a gradient that drives fluid movement through the composite via capillary action.
mechanism_raw: A layered fabric structure uses a high-denier hydrophilic layer to rapidly absorb moisture and a low-denier hydrophilic layer with sueding to create capillary gradients that pull moisture through the composite. The denier difference and surface processing establish a directional wicking pathway.

abstract: A high-precision device for providing positioning, registration and displacement includes a two-dimensional table for providing positioning and displacement, and a registration unit for bringing markers into registration with one another. The registration unit is attached to a carriage of the table via flexible articulated supports and can be moved by several, preferably seven, drives. The device can be used as a work table for reduction projectors and scanning electron microscopes, for example for investigating structural properties of materials.
problem: Achieving high-precision positioning and registration in a multi-axis system.
constraint: Coordinating multiple actuators and flexible supports to maintain precision without introducing mechanical interference or hysteresis.
mechanism: A multi-axis positioning system uses compliant supports to allow controlled deformation while independent actuators apply coordinated adjustments across multiple degrees of freedom. The compliant supports decouple mechanical interference, enabling precise alignment through distributed actuation.
mechanism_raw: A registration unit is attached to a 2D table via flexible articulated supports and driven by multiple independent actuators (e.g., seven drives). The flexible supports allow controlled compliance while the actuators enable fine adjustments in multiple axes to align markers precisely.

abstract: An embroidering sewing machine comprising a needle vertically reciprocated to stitch a work; an embroidering frame for holding the work to be stitched; a base (2) enclosed to provide a predetermined space therein; a driver means arranged in the base (2) and including a carriage assembly operatively connected to the embroidering frame and operated in synchronism with vertical movement of the needle to move in X-direction and in Y-direction normal to X-direction, the carriage assembly including a base carriage (5) movable in X-direction, an intermediate carriage (6) operatively connected to the base carriage (5) to move therewith and being movable in Y-direction relative to the base carriage (5), a distal end carriage (7) operatively connected to the intermediate carriage (6) to move therewith; a transmission means arranged between the intermediate carriage (6) and the distal end carriage (7) and transmitting the movement of the intermediate carriage (6) to the distal end carriage (7) to move the distal end carriage (7).
problem: Synchronizing X-Y directional movement of an embroidering frame with vertical needle motion.
constraint: Ensuring precise synchronization between needle movement and multi-axis carriage motion to avoid stitching errors.
mechanism: A nested mechanical linkage system distributes motion across orthogonal axes through interconnected carriages. A base carriage provides primary axis motion, an intermediate carriage inherits and modifies this motion for a secondary axis, and a distal carriage combines both motions via transmission elements to achieve synchronized multi-axis movement.
mechanism_raw: A nested carriage system (base, intermediate, distal end) uses mechanical linkages and transmission means to convert and distribute motion across orthogonal axes. The intermediate carriage moves in Y relative to the base carriage (X), while the distal carriage inherits motion from both via the transmission.

abstract: A new approach to scabbling of surfaces of structural materials is disclosed. A layer of mildly energetic explosive composition is applied to the surface to be scabbled. The explosive composition is then detonated, rubbleizing the surface. Explosive compositions used must sustain a detonation front along the surface to which it is applied and conform closely to the surface being scabbled. Suitable explosive compositions exist which are stable under handling, easy to apply, easy to transport, have limited toxicity, and can be reliably detonated using conventional techniques.
problem: Scabbling (removing material from) surfaces of structural materials efficiently and controllably.
constraint: The explosive composition must sustain a detonation front along the surface and conform closely to the surface being scabbled, while remaining stable under handling and easy to apply.
mechanism: A conformable energetic layer is applied to a surface and initiated to propagate a reaction front along the surface, causing controlled fragmentation of the surface material through localized energy release.
mechanism_raw: A layer of mildly energetic explosive composition is applied to the surface and detonated. The explosive conforms closely to the surface and sustains a detonation front along it, causing controlled rubbleization of the surface material.

abstract: An apparatus for supporting a book or magazine for reading includes a bottom member and a top member. The top member is elevated at one end above the bottom member and is adapted to pivot from a first closed position for reading into a second open position for turning the pages. At least a portion of the top member is transparent to permit viewing of printed matter through the top member, which is adapted to press upon the book or magazine when it is disposed in the first position. A lip is attached to the bottom member and is used to further retain the book or magazine in position. A receiving member is optionally attached to a back of the bottom member and is used to attach either a leg or a handle thereto.
reason: The patent describes a specific mechanical design for a book/magazine holder (pivoting transparent top, lip, and optional leg/handle). While functional, it does not describe a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a broader class of problems.

abstract: At least one CMOS component which is configured in a semiconductor substrate is part of the inventive circuit assembly. An insulating layer is configured on the semiconductor substrate. The insulating layer covers the CMOS component. A nanoelectronic component is configured above the insulating layer. At least one conducting structure is configured in the insulating layer and serves to link the nanoelectronic component with the CMOS component. If several nanoelectronic components are provided, they are preferably grouped to nano-circuit blocks. Each of the nano-circuit blocks is so small that the RC times of their lines do not exceed 1 ns.
problem: Integrating nanoelectronic components with CMOS circuits on a semiconductor substrate while maintaining signal integrity and minimizing RC delays.
constraint: The nano-circuit blocks must be sufficiently small to keep RC times below 1 ns, requiring precise vertical integration and grouping of components.
mechanism: A dielectric medium is formed over existing circuit elements, and conductive pathways are embedded within the dielectric to establish vertical interconnects between discrete functional units. These units are partitioned into sub-components sized to maintain signal propagation delays below a specified threshold.
mechanism_raw: An insulating layer is deposited over CMOS components, and conducting structures are embedded within the insulating layer to vertically link nanoelectronic components to the CMOS. Nanoelectronic components are grouped into nano-circuit blocks small enough to ensure RC times of their lines do not exceed 1 ns.

abstract: A sanitary appliance (1) has a location space (3), which is cut out of a housing (2) and intended for a cartridge (4) containing the control elements. A base (6) closes off the location space (3) in a downward direction. A water supply pipe (11) is detachably fastened in a bore (25) of the base (6). The water supply pipe (11) is axially locked by a conical tension spring (21) disposed in a location space (19) of the base (6). The tension spring (21) is applied by its smaller-diameter end with frictional engagement against the outer surface of the water supply pipe (11). With its larger-diameter end the tension spring (21) is supported against the base of the location space (19). The conical lateral surface of the tension spring (21) widens towards the outer end of the water supply pipe (11). In said manner, smooth water supply pipes may be fastened through simple insertion into the otherwise already completely assembled sanitary appliance.
problem: Detachably fastening a smooth water supply pipe into an already-assembled sanitary appliance without requiring additional tools or complex assembly steps.
constraint: The conical tension spring must provide sufficient frictional engagement to retain the pipe while allowing insertion, and its geometry must accommodate smooth pipes without additional fittings.
mechanism: A resilient element with variable cross-sectional geometry is positioned to engage a smooth cylindrical member. The element's geometry creates a frictional grip that increases with insertion depth, while its shape allows axial insertion without rotational alignment.
mechanism_raw: A conical tension spring is positioned in a location space within the base. The spring's smaller-diameter end frictionally engages the outer surface of the pipe, while its larger-diameter end is supported against the base. The conical shape allows the pipe to be axially locked through simple insertion.

abstract: Fences and lattices are formed from a single sheet of corrugated-like plastic material comprising a pair of substantially flat sheets spaced apart by spacers that are in parallel and have the same width to form between the flat sheet a series of parallel channels. The fences include a pair of spaced apart cross supports and a series of pickets that intersect the cross supports. The cross supports and pickets all lie in substantially the same plane. The lattices include a plurality of slats intersecting each other at an angle of 90°. These slats all lie in substantially the same plane and the channels are at an angle of 45° with respect to the longitudinal axis of individual slats.
problem: Forming fences and lattices from a single sheet of material while maintaining structural integrity and enabling complex geometric configurations.
constraint: The material must be a single sheet with parallel spacers of uniform width to form channels, and the structural elements (cross supports, pickets, slats) must lie in the same plane as the channels to maintain planar geometry.
mechanism: A unitary sheet structure incorporates parallel partition elements forming enclosed channels. Structural members are co-planar with the channels, using the channel geometry to reinforce the overall structure while enabling complex planar configurations through selective material removal or shaping.
mechanism_raw: A single sheet of corrugated-like plastic material is structured with parallel spacers forming channels between two flat sheets. Cross supports and pickets (for fences) or intersecting slats (for lattices) are arranged in the same plane as the channels, leveraging the inherent channel structure for strength and design flexibility.
residual_terms: ["unitary sheet structure", "parallel partition elements", "co-planar", "selective material removal"]

abstract: A waist exerciser includes a casing supported on two support posts and two blocks are rotatably connected to two ends of a shaft in the casing. A locking member is movably received in each of the blocks and has a plurality of first holes. Each of the blocks has a plurality of second holes which are located in alignment with the first holes. A belt has two ends which of which has a pin for inserting in the aligned first hole and second hole. Each of the pins has a groove and a periphery of the first hole is movably engaged with the groove so as to prevent the pin from disengaging from the holes.
problem: Need to create an adjustable mechanical connection that allows positioning at different points along a shaft while preventing accidental disconnection under load.
constraint: The mechanism must allow smooth axial adjustment while maintaining secure retention under operational loads, balancing ease of repositioning with resistance to accidental disengagement.
mechanism: A movable element with a circumferential constraint engages aligned openings in two components, one fixed and one rotatable. The constraint walls confine the element within the openings, permitting axial sliding for repositioning while preventing radial escape, thereby creating a mechanically locked yet adjustable connection.
mechanism_raw: A pin with a circumferential groove engages the periphery of aligned holes in a locking member and a rotatable block. The groove walls constrain the pin within the holes, allowing the pin to slide axially within the groove for adjustment while preventing radial disengagement from the holes. This creates a mechanically locked but repositionable connection.

abstract: The isolation and purification of lipopolysaccharides from several related strains of eukaryotic algae is disclosed. These lipopolysaccharides have been shown to be structurally and functionally similar to the lipopolysaccharides of gram negative bacteria, or endotoxins, which have been shown to be a cause of sepsis or septic shock. The present invention also relates to the use of these algal lipopolysaccharides to inhibit the release of TNF-a from macrophages, which has been associated with the initiation and escalation of sepsis as a result of bacterial endotoxins. The present invention further relates to the use of these algal lipopolysaccharides to inhibit the innate immune system of insects and mammals.
problem: Need to inhibit harmful immune responses (TNF-a release and innate immune system activation) associated with sepsis and septic shock caused by bacterial endotoxins.
constraint: The molecular mimic must be structurally similar enough to bind to the same immune targets as the bacterial endotoxin, but functionally different enough to inhibit rather than trigger the immune response, avoiding the very sepsis it is meant to prevent.
mechanism: Structurally similar molecular analogs competitively interact with immune system receptors that would normally be activated by a harmful stimulus. Instead of triggering an inflammatory response, these analogs bind to the same targets and inhibit the release of inflammatory mediators and suppress immune system activation.
mechanism_raw: Algal lipopolysaccharides that are structurally similar to bacterial endotoxins are used as molecular mimics or decoys. These mimics competitively interact with the same immune system pathways and receptors that bacterial endotoxins would normally activate, but instead of triggering an inflammatory response, they inhibit the release of TNF-a and suppress the innate immune system activation.
residual_terms: ["molecular mimics", "competitive interaction", "immune system receptors", "inflammatory response", "TNF-a", "innate immune system"]

abstract: According to the invention, there is provided an inbred corn plant designated 6077. This invention thus relates to the plants, seeds and tissue cultures of the inbred corn plant 6077, and to methods for producing a corn plant produced by crossing the inbred corn plant 6077 with itself or with another corn plant, such as another inbred. This invention further relates to corn seeds and plants produced by crossing the inbred plant 6077 with another corn plant, such as another inbred, and to crosses with related species. This invention further relates to the inbred and hybrid genetic complements of the inbred corn plant 6077, and also to the SSR and genetic isozyme typing profiles of inbred corn plant 6077.
reason: This patent merely discloses a specific inbred corn plant variety (6077) and standard plant breeding applications. It does not describe a novel problem-solving mechanism beyond conventional genetic crossing and inbreeding techniques.

abstract: Low VOC content brake cleaner compositions useful for removing oil and particulate contamination from braking system components of vehicles such as automobiles are reported. The brake cleaner compositions comprise about 5% to about 30% by weight methyl acetate; about 25% to about 50% of a hydrocarbon according to the formula CnH2n+x, where n is 5 to 8 and x is 0 or 2; and about 25% to about 55% by weight acetone.
reason: This patent discloses a specific chemical formulation (methyl acetate, hydrocarbons, acetone) for a brake cleaner with low VOC content. It is essentially a list of components with specific concentration ranges, not a causal mechanism describing how a functional relationship produces a useful effect.

abstract: The present invention eliminates the need to stop the operation of a line even when trouble arises before, during, or after an operation of joining metal blocks in hot rolling. According to a specific solving means of the present invention, when a succeeding metal block is to be subjected to hot finish rolling in succession to a preceding metal block after the leading end of the succeeding metal block is joined to a tail end 10B of the preceding metal block on the inlet side of a finish rolling mill 26, it is determined before and after joining whether or not endless rolling is impossible. When it is impossible, joining is aborted, and the succeeding metal block 12 is temporarily stopped, is fed again after the tail end 10B of the preceding metal block moves out of the finish rolling mill 26, and is finish-rolled under the conditions set for batch rolling. When joining was not performed successfully, a joint 11 is cut between a joining unit and the finish rolling mill 26, and the rolled material is bitten by the finish rolling mill set for batch rolling.
problem: Need to maintain continuous hot rolling operations even when joining of successive metal blocks fails or becomes impossible, without stopping the entire production line.
constraint: The system must detect joining failure and seamlessly switch between endless rolling and batch rolling modes without halting the entire production line, maintaining throughput while accommodating the fault.
mechanism: A control system detects whether continuous processing between successive workpieces is possible before and after attempting to join them. When joining fails, the system aborts the attempt, temporarily halts the succeeding workpiece, waits for the preceding workpiece to clear the processing station, then feeds the succeeding workpiece under alternative processing conditions. Any failed connection between the joining mechanism and the processing station is severed to allow the station to engage the material under the alternative processing settings.
mechanism_raw: The system detects whether endless rolling is possible before and after attempting to join successive metal blocks. When joining fails or is impossible, it aborts the joining attempt, temporarily stops the succeeding block, waits for the preceding block's tail end to clear the finish rolling mill, then feeds the succeeding block again under batch rolling conditions. If a failed joint exists between the joining unit and the mill, that joint is cut so the mill can bite the material under batch rolling settings.
residual_terms: ["continuous processing", "batch processing", "joining attempt", "processing station", "severed connection", "alternative processing conditions"]

abstract: A walking beam balanced span and moment regulating oil pump having an arc, a walking beam, a support, a pitman, a base, a crank, a decelerator, a power machine, and a string device. The upper part or the lower part of the front end of a boom is articulated to the rear end of the walking beam, and between the lower part or the upper part of the boom and the rear end of the walking beam is placed a weighted arm regulator, and a weighted device is installed on the end of the boom. The walking beam balanced span and moment regulating oil pump is simple in structure, easy to operate, reliable in performance and less costly than conventional devices.
problem: Maintaining balanced operation and regulating output in a mechanical oil pump under varying load conditions.
constraint: Balancing the need for automatic regulation with structural simplicity and cost-effectiveness while maintaining reliability under variable loads.
mechanism: A feedback-driven force-balancing system uses adjustable mechanical elements to dynamically redistribute load-dependent forces, maintaining operational equilibrium through automatic compensation without external intervention.
mechanism_raw: A weighted arm regulator and weighted device on the boom automatically adjust the moment and span of the walking beam, dynamically balancing forces to stabilize pump operation without manual intervention.

abstract: A fire escape device includes first and second cable drums rotatably mounted on a mounting shaft and spaced apart from each other axially, first and second support cables respectively wound around hub portions of the cable drums, and a coupling mechanism disposed between the cable drums to interconnect releasably the same. The first support cable is unreeled to generate a jerking force to permit rotation of the second cable drum with the first cable drum. Unreeling of the second support cable can rotate the first and second cable drums to reel the first support cable. Thus, alternately lowering people one after another from an elevated floor to a safe location can be achieved.
problem: Safely lowering people sequentially from an elevated floor during emergencies without manual control of each descent.
constraint: Ensuring reliable engagement and disengagement of the coupling mechanism to prevent jamming while maintaining consistent descent speed.
mechanism: A bidirectional coupling mechanism between two rotating storage elements enables alternating transfer of rotational energy, allowing controlled sequential release of stored potential energy to lower loads in a coordinated manner.
mechanism_raw: A coupling mechanism between two cable drums allows alternating reeling and unreeling of support cables, transferring rotational force between drums to enable controlled, sequential lowering of individuals.

abstract: A paper palette for art used for mixing colors and other paints for art or arranging the point of a brush is formed by partially bundling plural pieces of paper. Each of the pieces of paper is colored in two or more tones, which enables one to match the colors delicately and accurately in relation to a color of surroundings or a color applied to a substrate. With this paper palette, one does not have to wash it after use.
reason: The patent describes a product feature (multi-colored bundled paper) rather than a causal mechanism for solving a problem. The 'mechanism' is merely the physical arrangement of colored papers, lacking a functional relationship that produces an effect through interaction or feedback.

abstract: An inverter parallel operation system includes a first inverter adapted to control the output frequency thereof by controlling a control element. The system includes the inverter, and a second inverter and subsequent inverters adapted to control the output frequency thereof by controlling control elements comprising the inverters. Power being fed to a common load after a choke coil provided on the output-side end of a first filter provided on the output side of the first inverter has been connected to a choke coil provided on the output-side end of the second filter on the output side of the second and subsequent inverters. The improvement comprising controlling effective powers output by the first inverter, and the second and subsequent inverters by detecting the effective powers output by both the inverters and controlling any one or both of the output frequencies predetermined in accordance with the effective powers.
problem: Stabilizing power distribution and preventing overload in a parallel inverter system by coordinating output frequencies.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between inverters while minimizing response lag to ensure stable power delivery under fluctuating loads.
mechanism: A distributed power coordination system detects individual output contributions and adjusts operational parameters of each unit to dynamically balance load distribution, maintaining synchronization and minimizing response lag.
mechanism_raw: Effective power output from each inverter is detected and used to adjust the output frequencies of individual inverters, dynamically balancing load sharing across the system.

abstract: The present invention relates to a novel human gene encoding a polypeptide which is a member of the TNF receptor family, and has now been found to bind TRAIL. More specifically, an isolated nucleic acid molecule is provided encoding a human polypeptide named tumor necrosis factor receptor-5, sometimes referred to as “TNFR-5” or “TR5,” and now referred to hereinafter as “TRAIL receptor without intracellular domain” or “TRID.” TRID polypeptides are also provided, as are vectors, host cells, and recombinant methods for producing the same as well as anti-TRID antibodies. The invention further relates to screening methods for identifying agonists or antagonists of TRAIL polypeptide activity. Also provided are diagnostic and therapeutic methods utilizing such compositions.
problem: Identifying and targeting a specific receptor (TRID) for therapeutic intervention in diseases involving TRAIL signaling pathways.
constraint: Ensuring specificity of TRID-targeting agents to avoid unintended effects on other TNF receptor family members while achieving therapeutic efficacy.
mechanism: A selective molecular interaction system exploits a specific binding event between a target polypeptide and its ligand to enable targeted modulation of a cellular signaling pathway via agonist or antagonist agents.
mechanism_raw: The TRID polypeptide's binding to TRAIL creates a selective interaction that can be exploited using agonists or antagonists to modulate cell death pathways, enabling targeted drug development.

abstract: Hinge-lid box for cigarettes or the like, comprising a box part (10) and lid (11) and a collar (35) which is positioned in the box part (10) and projects out of the same by way of a top collar part (39), the lid (11) enclosing the top collar part (39) in the closed position. Fastened on the inside of a lid front wall (17) is a lid inner tab (32) which, merely in the region of a (relatively long) side edge (50), has a recess (52) which ensures form-fitting interlocking with a ridge (42) in the region of a collar front wall (36) when the lid is closed.
problem: Ensuring secure closure of a hinged lid container without complex mechanical fasteners.
constraint: The recess must be localized to a side edge region to allow controlled flexibility during closure while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism: A form-fitting interlocking system where complementary geometric features (a recess and a protrusion) engage when a movable cover is closed, creating a self-locking connection through mechanical constraint that maintains closure without continuous actuation.
mechanism_raw: A form-fitting interlocking system where a recessed lid inner tab engages a collar ridge when the lid is closed, creating a self-locking connection through geometric constraint.

abstract: MnZn ferrite comprises a main component comprising iron oxide 52.5 to 54.0 mol % in terms of Fe2O3, zinc oxide 7.7 to 10.8 mol % in terms of ZnO, and manganese oxide of the remaining, and sub-components of silicon oxide 60 to 140 ppm in terms of SiO2 and calcium oxide 350 to 700 ppm in terms of CaO, and further contains nickel oxide 4500 ppm or lower (not including 0) in terms of NiO.
reason: The patent specifies a material composition with precise chemical ratios and impurity thresholds, but does not describe a functional mechanism that produces an effect through causal relationships. It is a material formulation, not a problem-solving process or system.

abstract: A process for treating an organohalogen compound-containing soil or ash of the present invention, comprises:mixing the organohalogen compound-containing soil or ash with an organohalogen compound-decomposition catalyst composed of a composite catalyst comprising an amine compound and iron compound particles, and having an average particle size of 0.01 to 2.0 &mgr;m, a phosphorus content of not more than 0.02% by weight, a sulfur content of not more than 0.3% by weight and a sodium content of not more than 0.3% by weight; and having an apparent density (&rgr;a) of not more than 0.8 g/ml and a catalytic activity capable of decomposing not less than 50% by weight of monochlorobenzene; andheat-treating the obtained mixture at a temperature of 150 to 600° C. The method for treating an organohalogen compound-containing soil or ash in order to effectively decompose dioxins and dioxin precursors such as aromatic organohalogen compounds or aliphatic organohalogen compounds, e.g., trichloroethylene and dichloromethane, which are contained in the soil or ash.
problem: Decomposing hazardous organohalogen compounds (e.g., dioxins) in contaminated soil or ash without requiring extreme temperatures or specialized equipment.
constraint: The catalyst must balance particle size (0.01–2.0 µm), impurity limits (Si, Ca, Na, S), and catalytic activity to ensure efficient decomposition without deactivation or excessive energy input.
mechanism: A catalytic system comprising a composite material with optimized physical properties (particle size, impurity content, and density) enables decomposition of target compounds at moderate thermal conditions by balancing reactivity and structural stability.
mechanism_raw: A composite catalyst combining an amine compound and iron particles with controlled particle size, low impurity content, and specific density enables catalytic decomposition of organohalogen compounds at moderate temperatures (150–600°C).

abstract: A liquid ejection device comprising: a nozzle chamber having a first aperture in one wall thereof for the ejection of the liquid and a second aperture in a wall thereof through which an actuator arm extends, the actuator arm being attached to a substrate located outside the nozzle chamber and being connected to a paddle inside the nozzle chamber, the paddle being operable by way of the actuator arm to eject the liquid through the first aperture; the system further comprising a first raised rim formed around the second aperture, the first raised rim being arranged in a manner such that, during operation of the actuator arm, a liquid meniscus is being formed along an outer surface of the liquid between the first raised rim and the actuator arm.
problem: Maintaining consistent liquid ejection from a nozzle chamber while preventing leakage or meniscus instability during actuator movement.
constraint: The rim geometry and actuator arm positioning must balance meniscus formation with minimal friction or turbulence to avoid disrupting liquid flow.
mechanism: A structural feature adjacent to an actuator entry point creates a controlled liquid interface along the actuator surface, stabilizing the fluid boundary during motion to maintain consistent ejection and prevent leakage or turbulence.
mechanism_raw: A raised rim around the actuator arm's entry point into the nozzle chamber creates a controlled liquid meniscus along the arm's surface, stabilizing the liquid interface during paddle actuation to ensure reliable ejection.

abstract: To provide a sheetlike article for laundry which is freed from the scattering or leak of the contents, facilitates arbitrary dispensing and exhibits excellent detergency even when used alone, sheetlike water-soluble substrates are arranged on both surfaces of a thin layer made of a doughy non-phosphate detergent composition which contains nonionic surfactant(s), alkaline agent(s) and sequestering agent(s) and has a penetration hardness at 25° C. of from 0.1 to 10 kg/cm2.
problem: Preventing leakage or scattering of detergent contents in a single-use laundry sheet while enabling controlled dissolution during use.
constraint: The detergent layer's hardness must balance mechanical stability (to prevent leakage) with solubility (to ensure complete dissolution during use without residue).
mechanism: A layered structure with water-soluble barriers enclosing a core material of controlled mechanical resistance maintains integrity during storage but dissolves predictably when exposed to an aqueous environment, balancing stability and solubility through hardness modulation.
mechanism_raw: Water-soluble substrates sandwich a thin detergent layer with controlled penetration hardness (0.1–10 kg/cm²), allowing the sheet to maintain structural integrity during storage but dissolve predictably when exposed to water.

abstract: The present invention, in certain embodiments, is an apparatus to indicate the presence of an under-pressurized pneumatic tire for a vehicle, including, trailers, tractors, trucks or passenger vehicles. The apparatus comprises a housing, a cap, a shaft, a probe element, a bracket, an electrical switching element an electrically powered alarm. The housing is mounted next to the axle for the wheel of the vehicle. The cap is attached to the housing and has an aperture to receive the shaft. The shaft extends through the cap, and at one end, receives the probe element, and at the other end, holds the bracket upon which the electrical switching element is attached. When a tire loses air pressure, the height of the tire, as well as the vertical distance from the axle to the travelling surface, decreases; as the vertical distance decreases, the probe element contacts the travelling surface and rotates the shaft, bracket and electrical switch. The electrical switch and bracket contact a retaining element, which in certain embodiments is either part of the cap or part of the housing. The contact of the retaining element with the bracket prevents the electrical switch from being subjected to force in excess of what is necessary to activate the switch. When the electrical switch contacts the retaining element, at least one electrically powered alarm is activated thus notifying the operator of the vehicle of the deflated tire.
problem: Detecting under-pressurized pneumatic tires on vehicles without relying on pressure sensors or complex electronics.
constraint: The retaining element must balance force limitation to prevent switch damage while ensuring activation occurs only when tire pressure drops below a threshold.
mechanism: A mechanical displacement element responds to a physical dimensional change in a monitored object, actuating a switching mechanism through a mechanical linkage. A force-limiting component ensures activation occurs only when the dimensional change exceeds a threshold while preventing excessive force on the switch.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical displacement of a probe element caused by tire height reduction directly actuates an electrical switch via a rotating shaft and bracket, converting physical tire deflation into an electrical signal. A retaining element limits force on the switch to ensure reliable activation.

abstract: A fastening device for a glass panel on a wall, a building-side substructure, or similar object, such as a building facade, using a clamp fitting that grips the glass panel and a holder that is supported on the clamp fitting that it can move to a limited extent in three dimensions. The invention teaches that the holder has a two-arm connecting bridge that can be fixed in position by means of a center retaining pivot on the clamp fitting whereby, on the outer free ends of the connecting bridge, there are connecting articulations that can be fixed in position for the connection of respective compensating shafts, which are connected on their ends farther away from the connecting bridge by means of respective articulations that can be fixed in position with an adapter for fastening to a wall, a substructure, or similar object.
problem: Securing a glass panel to a wall or substructure while accommodating misalignment or movement in three dimensions.
constraint: The system must maintain structural integrity while permitting controlled movement to compensate for installation tolerances or thermal expansion.
mechanism: A multi-segment linkage with pivot points allows controlled movement of a mounting element relative to a base, accommodating misalignment in multiple axes. Articulations at connection points enable positional adjustment while maintaining structural integrity under load.
mechanism_raw: A two-arm connecting bridge with a central pivot allows limited 3D movement of the holder relative to the clamp fitting. Articulations at the bridge ends and adapter connections enable precise positional adjustment and fixation.

abstract: A sausage link forming machine having a rotating frame secured on a drivable axle and wherein the frame has opposed parallel discs. Control cams are secured to the axle intermediate the discs. A plurality of sausage grasping head assemblies are secured between the discs and equidistantly spaced apart along a circular path. A link forming pincer mechanism is secured between each of the grasping head assemblies. These head assemblies have rotatable support rollers which are displaceable towards one another from a sausage casing receiving position to a sausage casing engaging position. A first cam follower is associated with each of the grasping head assemblies and engages a first cam portion of the control cam to displace the support rollers. A second cam follower is associated with each of the link forming pincer mechanisms and engages a second cam portion to cause the fork members to pivot to and away from one another. The support rollers are axially rotated and the forks grasp and compress a portion of the elongated sausage casing to form a sausage link twisted connection between adjacent ones of the grasping head assemblies in a portion of the rotating frame.
problem: Forming sausage links by twisting casings between adjacent grasping heads in a rotating assembly.
constraint: The cam profiles must precisely coordinate the timing of roller displacement and fork pivoting to ensure consistent link formation without jamming.
mechanism: A cam-based synchronization system coordinates the displacement of support elements and compression elements through profiled control surfaces, enabling sequential grasping, compression, and twisting motions during rotational operation.
mechanism_raw: Cam followers engage control cams to synchronize the displacement of support rollers (for casing engagement) and pincer forks (for compression), enabling sequential grasping, compression, and twisting motions during rotation.

abstract: A differential circuit is used to compare the current to the drive transducers to a matched reference circuit. With the capacitive current from the piezoelectric transducer canceled out in this manner, the resulting output current provides a direct measure of the vibration amplitude of the drop generator. By adding an appropriate inductor in parallel to the capacitive piezoelectric drive transducers, the loading of the drive electronics, or oscillator, is significantly reduced.
problem: Measuring vibration amplitude of a piezoelectric transducer while canceling capacitive current interference from the drive electronics.
constraint: The reference circuit must closely match the transducer's capacitance to ensure effective cancellation without introducing phase shifts or signal distortion.
mechanism: A differential comparison system nulls interference by matching a reference signal to the monitored signal's characteristics. A parallel reactive element reduces loading on the signal source, isolating the desired output from capacitive artifacts.
mechanism_raw: A differential circuit compares the transducer's current to a matched reference circuit, nulling capacitive effects. A parallel inductor reduces loading on the oscillator, isolating the vibration-dependent signal.

abstract: A process for the production of oriented-grain electrical steel sheet with high magnetic characteristics, and more precisely a process in which the slab obtained from continuous casting is continuously nitrided by a reaction between aluminium and nitrogen is described. Amount, size and distribution of precipitates are controlled, enabling a high-temperature continuous heat treatment during which the primary-recrystallization and a high-temperature nitriding are realized.
problem: Producing oriented-grain electrical steel with high magnetic properties by controlling precipitate formation during heat treatment.
constraint: The nitriding and heat treatment parameters must be balanced to prevent over-precipitation that would inhibit grain orientation while ensuring sufficient strengthening.
mechanism: A chemical reaction process controls precipitate characteristics (size, amount, distribution) in a material matrix, enabling simultaneous high-temperature transformation steps by balancing reaction kinetics and phase development.
mechanism_raw: Continuous nitriding via aluminum-nitrogen reactions controls precipitate size, amount, and distribution, enabling high-temperature primary recrystallization and nitriding steps to occur simultaneously.
residual_terms: ["chemical reaction process", "precipitate characteristics", "high-temperature transformation steps", "phase development"]

abstract: The present invention relates generally to depositing elemental thin films. In particular, the invention concerns a method of growing elemental metal thin films by Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) using a boron compound as a reducing agent. In a preferred embodiment the method comprises introducing vapor phase pulses of at least one metal source compound and at least one boron source compound into a reaction space that contains a substrate on which the metal thin film is to be deposited. Preferably the boron compound is capable of reducing the adsorbed portion of the metal source compound into its elemental electrical state.
problem: How to deposit elemental metal thin films with controlled, selective reduction of a metal precursor into its elemental conductive state during atomic layer deposition.
constraint: The boron source compound must be chemically capable of reducing the adsorbed metal species, and the sequential pulsing must be timed so that each precursor is introduced and purged before the next, preventing gas-phase reactions and ensuring surface-limited reduction.
mechanism: A first reactive species and a second reducing species are sequentially introduced into a reaction environment in temporally separated pulses, each followed by a purge phase. Only the portion of the first species that has adsorbed onto a surface is exposed to the second species, which chemically reduces it at the surface interface. The temporal separation prevents reaction in the bulk phase, ensuring that reduction is confined to the adsorbed layer and enabling incremental, surface-limited conversion to an elemental state.
mechanism_raw: Sequential vapor-phase pulsing introduces a metal source compound and a boron reducing agent into a reaction space in separate pulses. The boron compound selectively reduces only the portion of the metal source compound that has adsorbed onto the substrate surface, converting it from a compound state into elemental metal. The temporal separation of pulses ensures that reduction occurs only at the adsorbed interface, not in the gas phase, enabling layer-by-layer growth of elemental metal films.

abstract: A ferromagnetic material can be formed in a very small size on the order of an atomic size and is capable of being stably magnetized. The ferromagnetic material comprises basic unit structures each consisting of a first atom (11), a second atom (12) of the same kind as the first atom (11), and a third atom (or atomic group) (13) of the same kind as the first atom (11) or of a kind different from that of the first atom (11). In each of the basic unit structures, the atoms are arranged on a surface of a substrate so that a chemical bond (14) is formed between the first atom or molecule and the third atom or molecule, a chemical bond (14) is formed between the second atom or molecule and the third atom or molecule, and a chemical bond or an electron path (15) not passing the third atom is formed between the first and the second atom or molecule, wherein said third atoms or molecules consist of As atoms.
problem: How to create a ferromagnetic material stable at atomic scale (on the order of a single atom) that can retain stable magnetization despite quantum-scale dimensions.
constraint: The third atom must be an As atom (or specific kind), and the geometric arrangement must simultaneously satisfy both the indirect bonding through the third atom and the direct bonding/electron path between the first and second atoms, which requires precise atomic-scale positioning on the substrate surface.
mechanism: Three atoms are positioned on a substrate surface in a fixed geometric arrangement where a third atom mediates indirect coupling between a first and second atom of the same kind, while a direct bond or electron pathway exists between the first and second atoms that bypasses the third atom. This dual-path configuration balances competing exchange interactions, stabilizing magnetization at atomic-scale dimensions by creating a robust magnetic state resistant to quantum fluctuations.
mechanism_raw: Atoms are arranged on a substrate surface in a basic unit structure where a third atom (As) forms chemical bonds with both a first and second atom of the same kind, creating indirect coupling pathways. Simultaneously, a direct chemical bond or electron path is established between the first and second atoms that bypasses the third atom entirely. This dual-path bonding geometry—indirect through the third atom and direct between the first and second—creates a stable magnetic configuration at the atomic scale by balancing exchange interactions through multiple pathways.

abstract: The snell holder has a foundation structure on which a snell-receiving body is mounted. The foundation structure has a support shaft and an anchor solely at one end for mounting it to another object. The snell-receiving body is elongated and compressible and puncturable and at least modestly resilient. It has a central axis about which it is rotatable. The support shaft projects into one end of the snell-receiving body at the axis of the body. The opposite end of the body has an eccentric handle. Spaced catches on the body allow attachment of the non-hook end of a snell to the body so that, upon rotation of the body by the eccentric handle, the snell can be wound around the body and the hook then pressed into the body.
problem: How to efficiently store and deploy a snell (fishing lure with hook) in a compact, self-contained holder that can both wind the snell and secure the hook during storage.
constraint: The body must be simultaneously compressible, puncturable, and resilient enough to allow the hook to be pressed into it and retain it, while also being rotatable and having sufficient surface friction to wind the snell. The handle must be eccentrically positioned to generate the necessary offset motion for hook compression.
mechanism: An elongated, resilient, rotatable body is mounted on a support shaft at one end, with an eccentric actuator at the opposite end. A flexible elongated article is attached to spaced retention points on the body. When the eccentric actuator is rotated, the body rotates about its axis, and the eccentric offset causes the body to translate relative to a pointed tool, winding the article around the body while simultaneously compressing the tool into the resilient body material. The eccentric rotation converts rotational motion into both winding (via body rotation) and axial compression (via eccentric offset), achieving two functions from a single input motion.
mechanism_raw: An elongated, resilient, rotatable body is mounted on a support shaft at one end, with an eccentric handle at the opposite end. The snell is attached to spaced catches on the body. When the eccentric handle is rotated, the body rotates about its axis, and the eccentric offset causes the body to translate relative to the hook, winding the snell around the body while simultaneously pressing the hook into the compressible body material. The eccentric rotation converts rotational motion into both winding (via body rotation) and axial compression (via eccentric offset), achieving two functions from a single input motion.

abstract: An air conditioning module applicable to a partition panel is disclosed herein. The air conditioning module includes a heat exchanger and a blower mounted inside the panel. The partition panel is suitable for assembling a modular personal working compartment in an office. A heat transfer medium is provided to the air conditioning module for generating cooled or heated air for the personal working space. The operation of the air conditioning module can accommodate individual needs, as well as save energy.
reason: This patent describes a product integration—placing a standard heat exchanger and blower inside a partition panel—rather than a novel causal mechanism. The problem (personalized climate control) is addressed by spatial integration of existing components into a modular form factor, not by a transferable functional principle. There is no underlying causal operation that produces a useful effect beyond 'putting an air conditioner in a wall panel.'

abstract: A continuous-flow steam generator includes a combustion chamber with evaporator tubes for fossil fuel. The combustion chamber is followed on the fuel-gas side by a vertical gas flue through a horizontal gas flue. When the continuous-flow steam generator is in operation, temperature differences in a connecting portion, which includes an outlet region of the combustion chamber and an inlet region of the horizontal gas flue, are to be kept particularly low. For such a purpose, of a plurality of evaporator tubes capable of being acted upon in parallel by flow medium, a number of evaporator tubes are guided in the form of a loop in the connecting portion.
problem: How to minimize temperature differences in the connecting transition zone between a combustion chamber outlet and a horizontal gas flue inlet in a continuous-flow steam generator, where abrupt thermal changes would otherwise occur.
constraint: Only a number (not all) of the evaporator tubes are guided in a loop in the connecting portion, while the remainder remain in standard parallel configuration. The loop must be confined to the transition zone where temperature differences are most pronounced, balancing thermal smoothing against overall system throughput and pressure drop.
mechanism: A subset of flow channels from a parallel flow arrangement are selectively rerouted into a loop configuration specifically within a transition zone where thermal gradients are most pronounced. This loop routing of selected channels acts as a thermal buffer, distributing heat transfer across the transition region and smoothing the temperature profile between two connected sections. The loop configuration increases the residence time and heat exchange surface area in the critical transition zone, reducing thermal shock and temperature differentials.
mechanism_raw: A subset of evaporator tubes from the parallel flow medium are routed in a loop configuration specifically within the connecting transition portion. This loop routing of selected tubes in the high-gradient zone acts as a thermal buffer, distributing heat transfer across the transition region and smoothing the temperature profile between the combustion chamber outlet and the horizontal gas flue inlet. The loop configuration increases the residence time and heat exchange surface area in the critical transition zone, reducing thermal shock and temperature differentials.
residual_terms: ["thermal buffer", "residence time", "heat exchange surface area", "thermal shock"]

abstract: Gas generating compositions and methods for their use are provided. Metal complexes are used as gas generating compositions. These complexes are comprised of a metal cation template, a neutral ligand containing hydrogen and nitrogen, and sufficient oxidizing anion to balance the charge of the complex. The complexes are formulated such that when the complex combusts, nitrogen gas and water vapor is produced. Specific examples of such complexes include metal nitrite ammine, metal nitrate ammine, and metal perchlorate ammine complexes, as well as hydrazine complexes. A binder and co-oxidizer can be combined with the metal complexes to improve crush strength of the gas generating compositions and to permit efficient combustion of the binder. Such gas generating compositions are adaptable for use in gas generating devices such as automobile air bags.
problem: Producing controlled gas generation (nitrogen and water vapor) for safety devices like airbags without harmful byproducts.
constraint: Balancing the metal-ligand-anion composition to achieve efficient combustion while avoiding toxic or corrosive byproducts.
mechanism: A chemically balanced composition of a central template species, neutral molecular ligands, and oxidizing anions forms a metastable complex that undergoes controlled exothermic decomposition to release predetermined gas species. The stoichiometric ratio of ligands to anions governs reaction kinetics and product selectivity, ensuring predictable gas output without harmful byproducts.
mechanism_raw: Using a metal cation template with neutral ligands (containing H and N) and oxidizing anions to form a complex that combusts predictably, releasing specific gases. The ligand and anion balance ensures controlled decomposition products.

abstract: A tunnel thruster which is compact, quiet and can withstand the higher depth pressure encountered by a UUV. The UUV is usually a cylindrically shaped vessel and has a propulsor with control surfaces at one end. At two positions along the length of the body there are two cylindrical ports which pass through the body of the UUV. At each position one port is in the vertical plane while the other port is in the horizontal plane. These ports are four tunnel thrusters, which enable the maneuvering of the UUV. The tunnel thruster can be mounted in the ports of the UUV. The main components of the tunnel thruster includes a tunnel, motor assembly mounted in the tunnel, rotors on each end of the motor assembly and inlet ducts on each end of the tunnel. The tunnel thruster attempts to address the short comings of the commercial thrusters. The tunnel thruster is an all electrically powered thruster with all mechanical components contained within the tunnel. The rotors operate independently and are counter-rotating. Each rotor is directly driven by its own electric motor. The rotors are held in position by water lubricated fluid film journal and thrust bearings. The rotor duct assembly includes the rotor, inlet duct, bearing and seals, which can be used in other applications.
problem: Achieving maneuverability in underwater vehicles (UUVs) with a compact, quiet thruster that withstands high pressure.
constraint: Maintaining rotor alignment and bearing lubrication in high-pressure environments without mechanical complexity or noise.
mechanism: Opposing rotational elements driven by independent actuators produce opposing torque vectors to cancel net rotational forces and minimize acoustic emissions. A pressure-resistant enclosure with fluid-lubricated interfaces maintains mechanical alignment and structural integrity in high-pressure environments while enabling bidirectional thrust generation.
mechanism_raw: Counter-rotating rotors driven by independent electric motors cancel torque and reduce noise. Water-lubricated bearings and sealed ducts maintain structural integrity under pressure while enabling bidirectional thrust.

abstract: A heat shield assembly is adapted for location within a crystal puller, with respect to a crucible, above molten source material held by the crucible in the puller. The heat shield assembly has a central opening sized and shaped for surrounding the ingot as the ingot is pulled from the molten material and is generally interposed between the ingot and the crucible as the ingot is pulled from the source material. The heat shield assembly comprises an outer reflector having an inner surface and an outer surface in generally opposed, spaced relationship with a side wall of the crucible, and an inner reflector located inward of the outer reflector. The inner reflector is constructed of a material having a low emissivity and has an outer surface in generally opposed relationship with the inner surface of the outer reflector. At least one of the outer surface of the inner reflector and the inner surface of the outer reflector has a spacer projecting outward therefrom and adapted for contact relationship between the inner reflector and the outer reflector. The spacer spaces the outer surface of the inner reflector from the inner surface of the outer reflector to inhibit heat conduction from the outer reflector to the inner reflector.
problem: Controlling heat distribution in crystal growth to prevent contamination and ensure uniform material properties.
constraint: Balancing thermal reflection efficiency with mechanical spacing to avoid heat leakage while preserving structural integrity.
mechanism: A spaced dual-reflective barrier system creates a controlled thermal gradient around a material processing zone. Interposed mechanical spacers between reflective surfaces inhibit conductive heat transfer while preserving structural continuity, maintaining spatial temperature stability to prevent contamination and ensure uniform material properties.
mechanism_raw: A dual-reflector system with spacers creates a controlled thermal barrier. The spacers inhibit conductive heat transfer between the outer and inner reflectors, maintaining a stable temperature gradient around the molten material.

abstract: A baking apparatus with a toaster comprises a main body; a baking part disposed at one side of the main body, and having a lid mounted at an upper portion thereof so as to be opened and closed by a hinge, a pot mounting portion for receiving a pot, a first heat generator formed at an inside wall of the pot mounting portion, and a rotational shaft protruded at a lower center portion of the pot mounting portion so that a stirring wing is inserted thereon; a toasting part disposed at the other side of the main body, and having a toasting chamber for receiving a slice of bread, a second heat generator formed at an inside wall of the toasting chamber, a lever for applying power source to the second heat generator and guiding the slice of bread, a crumb tray for removing bread crumbs, a driving motor for driving the rotational shaft of the baking part, and an operating portion for applying the power source to the driving motor and the first heat generator.
reason: The patent describes a combination of baking and toasting functions in a single appliance but does not propose a novel causal mechanism. It lists components (e.g., rotational shaft, heat generators) without explaining a functional relationship that solves a broader problem beyond product integration.

abstract: A motor driven stapler in which there are no fears of cutting off and need for loosed part of the lead wires of photo sensor for detection of sheets to be bundled, is provided. The stapler comprises a driving out portion from which a stapler is driven out; a table 42 which forwardly and backwardly reciprocates; and a clincher which is disposed on the table 42 so as to put and hold a pile of sheets to be bundled between itself and the driving out portion when the table 42 forwardly moves and at the same time a stapler is driven out from the driving out portion against the pile of sheets, and to clinch the front end portions of the staple which penetrate through the pile of sheets, wherein a photo sensor 50 is disposed in the other side of table 42 opposite to the driving out portion; and one or more through holes 48 are arranged in the table 42 in order to guide the emitted light beam from a light emission diode 51 of the photo sensor 50 to the pile of sheets and to guide the reflected light beam from a surface of the pile of sheets to a light receiving diode 52 of said photo sensor 50.
problem: Reliably detecting sheet positions in a stapler without loose wires or mechanical failure risks.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment of light paths through the holes while maintaining durability under repeated mechanical motion.
mechanism: A light transmission pathway is established through apertures in a stationary surface to enable non-contact detection of target object positions. Light emitted from a sensor traverses the apertures to the object surface and reflects back through the same path, eliminating direct electrical connections to moving components while maintaining alignment precision during repetitive mechanical operations.
mechanism_raw: Routing light from a photo sensor through through-holes in the table to the sheet surface and back, eliminating direct wiring to moving parts. The holes act as light guides, enabling non-contact sensing during stapling operations.

abstract: This invention relates to optical fiber systems where light is launched into and propagated in the fundamental mode of graded-index multimode fiber. Generally, it is not possible to launch light exclusively into the fundamental mode of graded-index multimode fiber by butt-coupling the multimode fiber to an arbitrary fiber carrying light from a source; several other modes may be launched. By inserting a length of a special singlemode fiber between an arbitrary fiber carrying light from a source and the graded-index multimode fiber, light can be launched exclusively into the fundamental mode of the graded-index multimode fiber. The special singlemode fiber has a modal pattern that matches the fundamental Gaussian modal pattern of the graded-index multimode fiber, which permits launching of the light into only the fundamental mode of the multimode fiber. Several applications for propagation in the fundamental mode of graded-index multimode fiber arises. These include: fiber optic sensor systems, high data rate communication links, low modal noise links, high security links, etc.
problem: Launching light exclusively into the fundamental mode of a graded-index multimode fiber without exciting higher-order modes.
constraint: The modal pattern of the intermediate singlemode fiber must precisely match the fundamental mode of the multimode fiber to avoid mode mismatch losses or residual higher-order mode excitation.
mechanism: Inserting an intermediate waveguide whose mode profile matches the fundamental mode of the target multimode waveguide, thereby filtering out higher-order modes and ensuring only the fundamental mode propagates.
mechanism_raw: Inserting an intermediate singlemode fiber whose modal pattern matches the fundamental Gaussian mode of the target multimode fiber, thereby filtering out higher-order modes and ensuring only the fundamental mode propagates.

abstract: A buckle apparatus for rapid disengagement of male and female members has deformable portions of a male pull member extending into the female member and retained in openings of the female member. An elongate pull element extends from the deformable portion or portions for pulling thereon to deform the deformable portions to disengage the male and female members.
problem: Achieving rapid disengagement of male and female mechanical coupling members under tension.
constraint: The pull force must be sufficient to deform the male member's portions without damaging the female member's openings, while maintaining structural integrity during engagement.
mechanism: Using deformable portions on the male member that extend into the female member's openings, with an elongate pull element that, when pulled, deforms the deformable portions to release the mechanical interlock.
mechanism_raw: Using deformable portions on the male member that extend into the female member's openings, with an elongate pull element that, when pulled, deforms the deformable portions to release the mechanical interlock.

abstract: A closed gallery piston includes a piston body having a closed gallery for cooling oil defined in part by a bottom wall and outer wall of the piston body. At least one oil hole is formed in the bottom wall to accommodate a flow of cooling oil within the gallery. The bottom wall is locally thickened in the area bordering the oil hole with an oil hole boss to reinforce the bottom wall in the vicinity of the oil hole. The oil hole boss preferably joins with the outer wall to provide added structural integrity to the piston body at the juncture between the outer wall and bottom wall near the oil hole.
problem: Reinforcing a piston's structural integrity around an oil cooling hole without compromising the cooling flow or overall piston geometry.
constraint: The boss must be sized and positioned to reinforce the hole while maintaining sufficient oil flow area and avoiding interference with the piston's sliding motion in the cylinder.
mechanism: Locally thickening the piston wall around the oil hole with a boss structure that bridges the hole to the outer wall, distributing stress and preventing crack propagation at the hole's edges.
mechanism_raw: Locally thickening the piston wall around the oil hole with a boss structure that bridges the hole to the outer wall, distributing stress and preventing crack propagation at the hole's edges.

abstract: A method for removing non-stick coatings from cookware or bakeware products is disclosed. The method includes the step of determining the angles of the primary surfaces of a pan having a coating to be removed. The method further includes the step of configuring a high-speed, multiport, rotating cleaning head to provide at least one water jet associated with each primary surface. The method further includes the step of employing the cleaning head to deliver an ultra-high pressure water jet directed at the pan while tracking the cleaning head along a plane substantially parallel to the upper surface of the pan. Using the method of the present invention, a coating may be removed from a pan in a single pass.
problem: Efficiently removing non-stick coatings from irregularly shaped cookware surfaces in a single pass without manual reconfiguration.
