problem: Preventing loosening of a rotor-to-drive-cone connection in a centrifuge during high-speed rotation and vibration.
constraint: The spring force must be calibrated to prevent loosening without over-tightening, which could damage components or introduce excessive friction.
mechanism: A resilient element is compressed between two components via axial movement of one component caused by tightening a fastener. The resilient element maintains continuous tension, ensuring the components remain engaged even if minor loosening occurs during operation. The force of the resilient element is calibrated to prevent loosening without over-tightening, which could damage components or introduce excessive friction.
mechanism_raw: A spring is compressed between a nut and drive cone via axial movement of the nut caused by tightening a screw. The spring maintains continuous tension, ensuring the nut remains engaged with the screw even if minor loosening occurs during operation.

abstract: In a synthetic door composed of two molded skins attached to a frame composed of stiles and rails of thin wooden strips to which the skins are adhered, with the core filled with a plastic foam, the improvement comprising a insert mechanically joined to each stile along their entire length, each insert having a channel device operable to interlock with its associated stile thereby providing the approximate strength of thicker wooden stiles conventionally used in constructing such doors, as well as providing finished vertical edges of the resulting door while significantly reducing the overall costs of such doors. In addition the insert can be employed to form an interlocking frame by extending the insert beyond the ends of the stiles and milling the ends of the rails so that they interlock with the channel means of the insert.
problem: Achieving structural strength equivalent to thick wooden stiles in synthetic doors while reducing material costs and weight.
constraint: The insert must balance load transfer efficiency with cost and manufacturability, ensuring the interlocking geometry does not compromise door integrity.
mechanism: An insert with a channel mechanically interlocks with thin structural members along their entire length, transferring loads through the insert to mimic the strength of thicker material. The insert also extends beyond the structural members to form an interlocking frame with milled components, balancing load transfer efficiency with cost and manufacturability.
mechanism_raw: An insert with a channel mechanically interlocks with thin wooden stiles along their entire length, transferring loads through the insert to mimic the strength of thicker wood. The insert also extends beyond stiles to form an interlocking frame with milled rails.

abstract: The present invention provides a method and device for the acoustic ejection of fluid droplets from each of a plurality of fluid-containing reservoirs. The droplets are ejected toward sites on a substrate surface for deposition thereon. The device is comprised of: a plurality of reservoirs each adapted to contain a fluid; an ejector comprising a means for generating acoustic radiation and a means for focusing the generated acoustic radiation so as to eject fluid droplets from the reservoir fluids; and a means for positioning the ejector in acoustically coupled relationship to each of the reservoirs. The invention is useful in a number of contexts, particularly in the preparation of biomolecular arrays.
problem: Precisely ejecting fluid droplets from multiple reservoirs for controlled deposition on a substrate surface.
constraint: The acoustic energy must be precisely controlled to eject droplets without damaging the fluid or substrate, while maintaining throughput across multiple reservoirs.
mechanism: Focused acoustic radiation is generated and directed at fluid reservoirs to eject droplets via acoustic radiation pressure. A positioning system aligns the ejector with each reservoir to enable sequential droplet ejection. The acoustic energy is precisely controlled to eject droplets without damaging the fluid or substrate, while maintaining throughput across multiple reservoirs.
mechanism_raw: Focused acoustic radiation is generated and directed at fluid reservoirs to eject droplets via acoustic radiation pressure. A positioning system aligns the ejector with each reservoir to enable sequential droplet ejection.

abstract: This invention is a novelty lighting device adapted to be submersible in liquid without leakage of the liquid into the interior of the device which could damage the interior elements. The device thus generally has an outer liquid-proof case as described below. The case, if to be used in beverages, is preferably be made of food-hygiene grade plastic adapted for safety in contact with consumables. The device can be manufactured to be more or less dense than the liquid in which it is to be placed, so that the body of the device will sink or float, as the case may be.
reason: The patent describes a waterproof enclosure and material selection but does not propose a novel causal mechanism beyond standard sealing and density adjustment. The solution is a product feature rather than a transferable functional principle.

abstract: Methods of more rapidly producing aerogel products by means of a rapid solvent exchange of solvent inside wet gels with supercritical CO2 by injecting supercritical, rather than liquid, CO2 into an extractor that has been pre-heated and pre-pressurized to substantially supercritical conditions or above. Preferably, pressure waves are applied to the supercritical CO2 to enhance the solvent exchange. The rapid solvent exchange process is followed by depressurization, optionally with a gas exchange. Preferably, pressure waves are used to speed up the depressurization. The process greatly reduces the time for forming aerogel products.
problem: Rapidly exchanging solvents in wet gels to form aerogel products while minimizing processing time.
constraint: Pressure and temperature must be carefully controlled to avoid damaging the gel structure while maximizing the rate of solvent exchange and depressurization.
mechanism: A supercritical fluid is injected into a pre-heated, pre-pressurized environment to rapidly dissolve and replace solvents in a gel structure. Pressure waves are applied to enhance solvent exchange kinetics and accelerate depressurization, reducing cycle time. Pressure and temperature are carefully controlled to avoid damaging the gel structure while maximizing the rate of solvent exchange.
mechanism_raw: Supercritical CO2 is injected into a pre-heated, pre-pressurized extractor to rapidly dissolve and replace solvents in the gel. Pressure waves are applied to enhance solvent exchange kinetics and accelerate depressurization, reducing cycle time.

abstract: A roof scuttle is provided which is adapted to be easily installed on any curb on a roof which curb may be existing, pre-formed or formed on the roof at the time of installation. The roof scuttle has a rectangular frame with an outwardly extending drip flange and the bottom of the frame is placed flat on the curb and the inside wall of the frame of the roof scuttle secured to the curb. This eliminates any external fastening of the roof scuttle to the roof which can cause leakage problems and also provides a more secure and safe installation. One embodiment of the roof scuttle uses a wood frame supplied with the roof scuttle which frame is useful for transportation of the roof scuttle and also for installations requiring a wood frame curb. The roof scuttle may be installed over irregular shaped openings, existing roof scuttles, and wide or narrow concrete, wood or metal curbs.
problem: Installing a roof scuttle on varied curb types without causing leakage or compromising structural security.
constraint: Must accommodate irregular shapes, existing structures, and diverse curb materials (concrete, wood, metal) without requiring custom fitting.
mechanism: A frame with a conformal base and internal attachment interface adapts to irregular curb geometries, creating a sealed connection by eliminating external fastening paths while distributing structural loads through direct contact and embedded securing elements.
mechanism_raw: Placing the frame's bottom flat on the curb and securing the inner wall of the frame to the curb eliminates external fastening, which directly prevents leakage paths while ensuring a stable, sealed attachment.

abstract: A high pressure rubber hose has a plurality of reinforced layers. Each reinforced layer is buried by way of an intermediate rubber layer between an inner rubber layer and an outer rubber layer, in which an organic fiber reinforced layer braided from organic fiber cords into two spiral layers or one braided layer is disposed to the inner rubber layer on the outer circumference thereof. A steel wire reinforced layer braided from steel wires into two spiral layers is disposed to the organic fiber reinforced layer at the outer circumference thereof. The braiding angle of the organic fiber reinforced layer is less than braiding angle of the steel wire reinforced layer and the braiding tension of the organic fiber reinforced layer is higher than the braiding tension of the steel wire reinforced layer.
problem: Achieving optimal strength and pressure resistance in a high-pressure hose while balancing flexibility and durability.
constraint: Braiding angles and tensions must be precisely controlled to avoid delamination or uneven stress concentration between layers.
mechanism: A multi-layer composite structure uses differential angular orientations and tension profiles between adjacent layers to independently resist deformation and tensile forces, with the angular/tension relationship governing load distribution and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Differential braiding angles and tensions between organic fiber and steel wire layers create a composite structure where the inner layer resists deformation and the outer layer provides tensile strength, with the angle/tension relationship governing load distribution.

abstract: A non-linear transistor circuit uses separate signal biasing and DC biasing to improve the power efficiency while preventing thermal runaway. An improved amplifier using this circuit has a DC bias voltage supply. Using separate biasing of the DC supply voltage and the signal allows a large value resistance for the DC bias network to prevent thermal runaway and a small value resistance for the signal biasing network to improve the circuit's efficiency. A point of thermal equilibrium is reached when the voltage drop across the DC bias resistance sufficiently reduces the voltage between the transistor's base and emitter, VBE, the base current, the collector current, and the junction temperature, resulting in thermal equilibrium.
problem: Improving power efficiency in transistor amplifiers while preventing thermal runaway caused by self-heating feedback loops.
constraint: Resistance values must be tuned so that thermal feedback stabilizes rather than destabilizes the operating point.
mechanism: Independent biasing networks for DC and signal paths enable separate optimization of current limiting and efficiency, with thermal equilibrium achieved through opposing feedback effects where voltage-induced current reduction counteracts temperature-driven current increases.
mechanism_raw: Separating DC and signal biasing networks allows independent optimization: high DC resistance limits current to prevent thermal runaway, while low signal resistance maintains efficiency. Thermal equilibrium is achieved when VBE reduction from DC bias voltage drop counteracts temperature-driven current increases.

abstract: A blower having an outlet adjustably movable through a path substantially circumscribing an axis is disclosed. The blower may include an outlet formed in a housing which is coaxially aligned with an impeller. The housing and the impeller may rotate independently about the axis. Adjustable rotation of the housing may be controlled by an actuator, such as an electric motor, which is operably connected to the housing. The blower may include a wheel-mounted frame which supports the impeller and the housing. The blower may be mounted to an implement, such as a lawn mower or a tractor.
problem: Directing airflow direction in a blower system without disrupting impeller performance or requiring mechanical disassembly.
constraint: Housing and impeller must rotate independently to avoid torque transfer that would destabilize airflow or mechanical balance.
mechanism: A coaxial housing assembly with independent rotational coupling to a fixed impeller enables dynamic redirection of airflow through actuator-driven rotation, maintaining impeller stability by preventing torque transfer between components.
mechanism_raw: Coaxial alignment of an independently rotatable housing around a fixed impeller allows the outlet to sweep a full circular path via an actuator, enabling dynamic airflow redirection while maintaining impeller stability.

abstract: In a double-ended Francis turbine, shaft whip at critical speed is alleviated by pitching tappets in the housing, around the rotor. The tappets are adjusted to lie closer to the rotor than the (labyrinth) seal grooves. The tappets are of polythene, and are around twenty in number. The tappets are adjustable from outside the housing, and adjustment may be done with the turbine running.
problem: Reducing shaft whip in rotating machinery at critical speeds without halting operation for maintenance.
constraint: Tappets must be externally adjustable and made of low-friction, wear-resistant material to function under continuous operation.
mechanism: Externally adjustable damping elements positioned radially inward of sealing components provide dynamic alignment correction and vibration suppression through controlled proximity and material compliance, counteracting lateral displacement without operational interruption.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable polythene tappets positioned closer to the rotor than labyrinth seals provide dynamic damping and alignment correction, counteracting lateral vibrations through controlled proximity and material compliance.

abstract: A method for separating sucrose and a second dissolved component from a sucrose-containing solution, preferably a beet-derived sucrose-containing solution, wherein the solution is subjected to a first fractionation by a continuous or sequential chromatographic simulated moving bed process to yield a sucrose-enriched fraction and a fraction enriched with the second dissolved component. The resulting fraction enriched with the second component is subjected to a second chromatographic fractionation that is a simulated moving bed or batch type process, to yield a second sucrose-enriched fraction and a second fraction enriched with the second dissolved component wherein both fractions have an improved yield or purity.
problem: Efficiently separating sucrose and a second dissolved component from a solution while maximizing yield and purity.
constraint: Balancing the number of fractionation steps and process parameters (e.g., flow rates, temperature) to avoid excessive energy consumption or loss of product while achieving target purity and yield.
mechanism: Sequential counter-current separation using a first stage to enrich target components via differential adsorption, followed by a second stage to further refine fractions. Progressive separation is achieved by exploiting differences in binding affinity and desorption kinetics across multiple stages, with process parameters adjusted to balance throughput and purity.
mechanism_raw: Sequential chromatographic fractionation using a first simulated moving bed (SMB) process to enrich sucrose and the second component, followed by a second SMB or batch process to further refine both fractions. Each step progressively improves separation by leveraging differential adsorption and desorption dynamics.

abstract: An identification badge having a front panel and a back panel affixed to the front panel. An extended section extends from the back panel and has a perforation pattern formed thereon. The perforation pattern defines a neck strap when the perforations are separated. The front panel is formed of a transparent material. An identification card can be positioned between the front and the back panel.
reason: The mechanism is a static product design (perforation pattern for manual strap formation) without a causal functional relationship that solves a broader problem beyond the specific badge application.

abstract: A fire truck water connection cap, which has an insert installed on the outside that displays a variety of different artwork forms. It is customizable for the individual fire department. The means of retention allows for the “upright” placement of the insert regardless of orientation of the cap when it is tight to the pump inlet. The use of an elastomeric spring presses the insert against a retention ring which holds it in place after it is rotated to the correct position. The cap also uses grips on the ends of the handles to resist a firefighter's hands or a soft mallet from slipping off the end.
reason: The mechanism is a localized mechanical retention system (elastomeric spring and retention ring) tailored to a specific cap orientation problem, lacking a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: An improved twin screw extruder device (14) is provided which is capable of producing a wide variety of high quality extrudates having greatly varying final properties, without the need for extensive machine modifications. The extruder (14) includes a barrel (16) together with a co-rotating twin screw assembly (22). The assembly (22) is made up of a pair of screws (50, 52) having central, tapered shafts (54, 56) equipped with outwardly extending helical flighting (58, 60); the screws (50, 52) are non-parallel and are positioned so that the flighting (58, 60) thereof is intercalated along the length of the screws (50, 52). The fighting is of specialized configuration and tapers along the length of the screws (50, 52) preferably at an angle of taper different than that of the shafts (54, 56); moreover, the width of the outer flighting surfaces (70, 72) increases along the length of the shafts (54, 56). This screw geometry defines a series of alternating upper and lower close-clearance high-pressure nip areas (78) defined by the flighting (58, 60) which serves to propel an extrudable mixture forwardly towards the outlet end (20) of the barrel (16). However, passageways (80) and kneading zones (82) are also defined between the screws (50, 52), which assures full mixing, shearing and cooking of the material. The extruder device (14) is capable of producing high density sinking aquatic feeds as well as expanded, low density products merely by changing the rotational speed of the screws (50, 52) together with appropriate temperature control. In another embodiment, a fluid extraction extruder (138) is provided having a specialized extruder head (140) including an outer shell (144) and an inner, elongated, slotted sleeve (152).
problem: Producing a wide variety of high-quality extrudates with differing properties (e.g., density, texture) without requiring machine modifications.
constraint: Screw geometry must balance close-clearance high-pressure zones for propulsion with open passageways for mixing, while maintaining structural integrity under varying operational loads.
mechanism: Adjustable helical elements with non-parallel axes and variable pitch create alternating compression zones and mixing passageways. Dynamic control of rotational speed and thermal input modulates material transport, shear-induced mixing, and thermal processing, enabling output property variation without mechanical reconfiguration.
mechanism_raw: Non-parallel co-rotating screws with tapered shafts and intercalated helical flighting create alternating high-pressure nip zones and mixing passageways. Adjusting screw speed and temperature dynamically controls material propulsion, shearing, and cooking, enabling variable output properties.

abstract: Polymeric materials are used,to make a pliable, non-toxic, injectable porous template for vascular ingrowth. The pore size, usually between approximately 100 and 300 microns, allows vascular and connective tissue ingrowth throughout approximately 10 to 90% of the matrix following implantation, and the injection of cells uniformly throughout the implanted matrix without damage to the cells or patient. The introduced cells attach to the connective tissue within the matrix and are fed by the blood vessels. The preferred material for forming the matrix or support structure is a biocompatible synthetic polymer which degrades in a controlled manner by hydrolysis into harmless metabolites, for example, polyglycolic acid, polylactic acid, polyorthoester, polyanhydride, or copolymers thereof. The rate of tissue ingrowth increases as the porosity and/or the pore size of the implanted devices increases. The time required for the tissue to fill the device depends on the polymer crystallinity and is less for amorphous polymers versus semicrystalline polymers. The vascularity of the advancing tissue is consistent with time and independent of the biomaterial composition and morphology.
problem: Creating a biodegradable scaffold that supports vascular and connective tissue ingrowth while enabling uniform cell seeding and controlled degradation.
constraint: Pore size and polymer crystallinity must be optimized to balance tissue ingrowth rate with mechanical stability during degradation, ensuring cells remain viable and nourished throughout the process.
mechanism: A biodegradable matrix with controlled porosity and degradation kinetics allows tissue ingrowth to temporally align with structural resorption. Pore dimensions and polymer morphology are tuned to balance cellular colonization rate with mechanical integrity during degradation, with hydrolytic breakdown products maintaining cellular viability.
mechanism_raw: A pliable polymer matrix with precisely controlled pore size (100–300 microns) and degradation rate (via hydrolysis into harmless metabolites) allows tissue ingrowth to match scaffold resorption. Amorphous polymers degrade faster than semicrystalline ones, enabling tunable temporal alignment of vascularization and structural replacement.

abstract: A presetting table for preparing a system of converting tools in a stripping station of a converting press positions the following face to face, in a position simulating cantering along the machine axis and positioning at the first rule: the stripper-holder plate of an upper stripping die, a central stripping board and a replica of a pull-out frame carrying telescopic pins. The upper stripping die is prepared by using the central stripping board as a template.
problem: Preparing converting tools (stripper-holder plate, central stripping board, pull-out frame with telescopic pins) in a stripping station to match the operational configuration of a converting press without requiring the actual press to be set up.
constraint: The setup must accurately simulate the operational configuration (cantering along machine axis, first rule positioning) while remaining a separate preparation station, balancing preparation fidelity against the complexity of replicating the full operational environment.
mechanism: A preparation station positions a reference component and working components in a simulated operational configuration, using the reference component as a template to prepare the actual working component so that it matches the operational requirements of the target system without requiring the target system itself to be set up.
mechanism_raw: A presetting table positions a reference component (central stripping board) and other elements face-to-face in a simulated operational state (simulating cantering along the machine axis and positioning at the first rule). The reference component, positioned in this simulated state, then serves as a template to prepare the actual working component (upper stripping die), ensuring the prepared die matches operational requirements.

abstract: A centrifuge bucket is provided. The centrifuge bucket has a bucket body and a holder plate mounted within the body. The holder plate has a plurality of holder openings therein to receive samples. The centrifuge bucket has a bottom support member having a plurality of support openings. Each of the support openings is precisely aligned with a respective holder opening. An alignment post mechanism is affixed to the bucket. The alignment post mechanism has a mechanism base disposed on the bottom support member and an alignment post attached to the mechanism base.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment between sample holder openings and support openings in a centrifuge bucket so that samples are properly positioned and supported during centrifugation.
constraint: The alignment mechanism must maintain precise registration between the two plates while allowing for sample insertion and removal, and must remain robust under centrifugal forces without adding excessive complexity or bulk.
mechanism: A fixed mechanical reference element is attached to a base disposed on a support member, ensuring precise registration between openings on two separate plates during operation by maintaining alignment between corresponding features on each plate.
mechanism_raw: A fixed alignment post mechanism is affixed to the bucket, with a mechanism base disposed on the bottom support member and an alignment post attached to it. This fixed mechanical reference element ensures that each support opening on the bottom support member is precisely aligned with a respective holder opening on the holder plate, maintaining registration between the two components during operation.
residual_terms: ["fixed alignment post", "alignment post", "bottom support member", "holder plate", "support openings", "holder openings"]

abstract: Methods, arrays and kits are provided for rapidly and efficiently identifying and quantifying multiple different activated transcription factors in a biological sample at the same time. In one embodiment, the method includes the step of mixing a library of transcription factor probes with a sample containing activated transcription factors. The transcription factor probes that have bound to the activated transcription factors may be isolated from the complexes formed between the probes and the activated transcription factors. The bound probes can be identified, for example, by using an array of hybridization probes.
problem: Rapidly and efficiently identifying and quantifying multiple different activated transcription factors in a biological sample simultaneously, distinguishing activated from non-activated forms.
constraint: The method must selectively capture only activated transcription factors (not inactive ones) while handling multiple different factors simultaneously, requiring probes with sufficient specificity and an isolation step that preserves the bound complexes without cross-contamination.
mechanism: A library of binding agents is mixed with a sample containing target molecules in a specific state. Agents that selectively bind to the target molecules in that state form complexes, which are isolated from unbound agents and other sample components. The bound agents are then identified using a secondary detection array, enabling simultaneous detection and quantification of multiple targets.
mechanism_raw: A library of transcription factor probes is mixed with a sample containing activated transcription factors. Probes that bind to activated transcription factors form complexes, which are then isolated from unbound probes and other sample components. The bound probes are subsequently identified using a secondary array of hybridization probes, enabling simultaneous detection and quantification of multiple targets.
residual_terms: ["transcription factor probes", "activated transcription factors", "complexes", "secondary array of hybridization probes"]

abstract: A process for manufacturing a metal cord includes the steps of permanently deforming at least one wire using a substantially sinusoidal deformation lying in a plane and stranding the at least one wire together with one or more other wires by helicoidally double twisting the wires around a longitudinal axis of the metal cord. The metal cord may include at least two wires each with diameter greater than or equal to 0.10 mm and less than or equal to 0.50 mm. An associated metal cord includes at least two wires. One or more of the at least two wires is permanently deformed using a substantially sinusoidal deformation lying in a plane. The at least two wires are stranded together by helicoidally double twisting the at least two wires around a longitudinal axis of the metal cord.
problem: Manufacturing metal cord with specific mechanical properties from wires with diameters between 0.10 mm and 0.50 mm, requiring controlled deformation and stranding.
constraint: The sinusoidal deformation must be applied without damaging the thin wires (0.10-0.50 mm diameter), and the helicoidal double twisting must be performed after deformation without undoing or compromising the pre-formed geometry, requiring precise control of both deformation and stranding parameters.
mechanism: At least one wire is permanently deformed using a substantially sinusoidal deformation lying in a plane, which modifies the wire's geometry to enhance specific mechanical properties. The deformed wire(s) are then stranded together with other wires by helicoidally double twisting them around a longitudinal axis, creating a composite cord structure with combined geometric and structural enhancements.
mechanism_raw: At least one wire is permanently deformed using a substantially sinusoidal deformation lying in a plane, which modifies the wire's geometry to enhance specific mechanical properties. The deformed wire(s) are then stranded together with other wires by helicoidally double twisting them around a longitudinal axis, creating a composite cord structure with combined geometric and structural enhancements.
residual_terms: ["sinusoidal deformation", "helicoidally double twisting", "longitudinal axis", "composite cord structure"]

abstract: A container for artist's pastels which is comprised of a rectangular pad onto which is attached an elastic loop system. Pastels are inserted into the loops of the elastic. To close, the pad is rolled up from the bottom and placed into aperture of the pouch that is attached to the top of the pad. The pouch is closed with a zipper and carried by an adjustable shoulder strap.
problem: Storing and transporting artist's pastels in a way that protects them from damage, keeps them organized, and allows for compact, portable carrying.
constraint: The elastic retention must hold pastels securely without causing damage, while the rolling action must compact the items sufficiently to fit into the pouch without breaking or dislodging them, and the sealed pouch must provide adequate protection during transport.
mechanism: Items are inserted into elastic retention elements attached to a flexible substrate, which retains each item individually in place. To close and transport, the substrate is rolled up from one end, compacting the retained items and transferring them into the aperture of an attached container. The container is then sealed, containing the rolled substrate and items in a compact, protected form carried by a support strap.
mechanism_raw: Pastels are inserted into elastic loops attached to a rectangular pad, which retains each pastel individually in place. To close and transport, the pad is rolled up from the bottom, compacting the retained pastels and transferring them into the aperture of an attached pouch. The pouch is then sealed (e.g., with a zipper), containing the rolled pad and pastels in a compact, protected form carried by an adjustable shoulder strap.

abstract: It is a compact water purification/sterilization method and its device with a high electrolytic efficiency in which even though it is used continuously for a long period of time in order to purify and sterilize water with low electrical conductivity such as the water from a swimming pool, bathtub, pond, 24-hour bath, farming tank or AC, there is no deterioration or breakage of the electrodes or deformation of the plastic case for the electrolyzing device due to heat, and even if the electrical flow per electrode surface area is increased, it provides superior long-term endurance performance. Barrel-shaped (cylindrical-shaped) anodes and cathodes are arranged alternately in a concentric manner in layers at given inter-electrode intervals. The anode is a ferrite rod with a long hole along the center axis direction or a ferrite pipe, and in the hole, heating so that it has fluidity, or mercury, which is liquid at ordinary temperature, is filled, in advance, fills a low-melting point metal. Then, a conductive metal terminal body is inserted so that the contact area between the terminal and the ferrite electrode is sufficient, and, additionally, the conductivity at the contact portion is increased. This electrolyzing device is directly immersed in the water and electrolysis is carried out.
problem: Electrode degradation and heat-induced deformation in electrolytic water purification systems during prolonged use, especially with low-conductivity water.
constraint: Balancing electrical conductivity and thermal management within the electrode while maintaining structural integrity under continuous operation.
mechanism: A dual-component system combines a fluid-conductive element with a rigid structural element to maintain electrical contact and thermal stability under high current density. The fluid element accommodates thermal expansion/contraction while the rigid element preserves geometric integrity, preventing mechanical failure during continuous operation.
mechanism_raw: A fluid conductive core (e.g., low-melting-point metal or mercury) within a structurally rigid electrode (ferrite rod/pipe) maintains electrical contact and thermal stability under high current density. The fluid core adapts to thermal expansion/contraction while the rigid outer structure preserves electrode geometry, preventing mechanical failure.

abstract: A method of forming a shallow trench isolation type semiconductor device comprises forming an etch protecting layer pattern to define at least one active region on a substrate, forming at least one trench by etching the substrate partially by using the etch protecting layer pattern as an etch mask, forming a thermal-oxide film on an inner wall of the trench, filling the trench having the thermal-oxide film with a CVD silicon oxide layer to form an isolation layer, removing the etch protecting layer pattern from the substrate over which the isolation layer is formed, removing the thermal-oxide film formed on a top end of the inner wall of the trench to a depth of 100 to 350 å, preferably 200 å from the upper surface of the substrate, and forming a gate oxide film on the substrate from which the active region and the top end are exposed.
problem: Creating precise shallow trench isolation in semiconductors without damaging active regions or compromising gate oxide quality.
constraint: Achieving nanoscale depth control during oxide removal to avoid over-etching into active regions while ensuring complete isolation.
mechanism: A multi-stage material removal process uses patterned masking and timed etching steps to selectively expose regions at controlled depths. Sequential application of protective layers and removal techniques enables sub-micron precision while preserving underlying structural features.
mechanism_raw: Controlled sequential etching and selective removal of thermal oxide layers to expose active regions at precise depths (100–350 Å), enabling subsequent gate oxide formation while preserving isolation integrity. The process uses etch masks and timed removal steps to achieve sub-micron precision.

abstract: An axle assembly is provided that includes a tubular member having an outer wall and an interior cavity. The other wall includes a first interlocking feature. An axle component mounting member, such as a bearing shoulder sleeve and/or a brake flange, is arranged on a portion of the outer wall. The mounting member includes a second interlocking feature coacting with the first interlocking feature to affix the mounting member and tubular member to one anther. The axle assembly may be formed by arranging the axle mounting member into a die assembly. A tubular member may be arranged in the die assembly within an opening in the mounting member. A hydroforming process may be employed to pressurize a cavity within the tubular member. A portion of the tubular member is deformed into engagement with the mounting member to affix the mounting member to the tubular member.
problem: Securely attaching components (e.g., bearings, brake flanges) to tubular axles without welding or mechanical fasteners that weaken the structure.
constraint: Applying sufficient pressure to achieve deformation without exceeding material yield limits or compromising structural strength.
mechanism: A pressure-induced deformation process plastically reshapes a tubular member into interlocking features on a mounting component, creating a permanent mechanical bond. The process relies on controlled yielding of the tubular material to form a form-fitting joint without external fasteners or adhesives.
mechanism_raw: Hydroforming pressurizes the tubular member to plastically deform it into interlocking features on a mounting component, creating a form-fitting, permanent joint. The deformation process bonds the parts through mechanical interlocking rather than adhesives or welds.

abstract: A Ni-base heat resistant alloy excellent in weldability and strength at elevated temperatures and suited for use in manufacturing cracking furnace tubes and reformer furnace tubes to be used in ethylene plants as well as a welded joint therefor is provided. The alloy of the invention is a Ni-base heat-resistant alloy, which comprises C: not more than 0.1%, Si: not more than 2%, Mn: not more than 2%, P: not more than 0.025%, S: not more than 0.005%, N: not more than 0.04%, Cr: 10 to 30%, Al: 2.1 to less than 4.5%, and Mo: 2.5 to 15% or W: 2.5 to 9% or Mo and W: 2.5 to 15% in total, and satisfies the relation (1) given below:(104Si+1980P+1980S+9Al+15Ti+11Nb+1.8W+11600B)≦{1.1(240−20000S−1900P−30Al−10Ti−9W+17000B)   (1) In the welded joint of the invention, both of the base metal and weld metal are made of the alloy having the above composition, and the ST value of the weld metal as calculated according to the following formula (2) or (3) is larger by not less than 3 than the ST value of the base metal:in the case of Ti≦4C; ST=Mo+1.5W+100Ti   (2) in the case of Ti>4C; ST=Mo+1.5W+400C   (3).
reason: The patent specifies a material composition formula for a Ni-base alloy, which is a domain-specific solution rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The 'ST value' formula and elemental ratios are tied to metallurgical properties of nickel-based superalloys and lack a transferable functional principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: The present invention relates to an inner cushion for helmets. The inner cushion includes an shock absorbing composite sandwiched between two protecting foils. The composite includes at least one absorbing material for absorbing an impact energy, wherein the at least one absorbing material is structured and arranged to absorb the impact energy by being crushed and collapsed upon exposure to the impact energy and diffusing air through a network of pores in the absorbing material.
problem: Efficiently absorbing impact energy in protective gear while maintaining structural integrity and comfort.
constraint: Balancing pore density and material strength to ensure sufficient energy absorption without premature structural failure.
mechanism: A porous energy-absorbing layer dissipates impact forces through controlled material collapse and fluid (e.g., air) movement within a network of voids. The pore structure regulates deformation rate and energy dissipation, preventing abrupt force transmission while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A crushable composite layer with a controlled pore network absorbs energy through material collapse and air diffusion. The pores allow controlled deformation and energy dissipation via air movement, preventing sudden force transmission to the wearer.
residual_terms: ["porous energy-absorbing layer", "controlled material collapse", "fluid movement", "network of voids"]

abstract: A system for controlling ice size of an ice maker comprises: an ice size controlling means for controlling a size of ice which will be frozen in an ice maker; an ice size displaying means for displaying ice size controlled by the ice size controlling means so that a user can identify it; and a controlling means for controlling the ice size displaying means according to a signal applied from the ice size controlling means and controlling an amount of water supplied to an ice making vessel, and therefore, the ice size can be controlled easily to be the size desired by a user and the size can be identified visually.
problem: Allowing a user to easily control and visually identify the size of ice produced by an ice maker.
constraint: Balancing user input simplicity with the system's ability to dynamically adjust water supply to achieve the desired ice size.
mechanism: A system where user input for a desired output characteristic is translated into adjustments of a variable input parameter through a feedback mechanism, with a visual indicator providing real-time confirmation of the current setting.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop control system where user-adjustable ice size settings are translated into water supply adjustments via a feedback signal, with a display providing real-time visual confirmation of the selected size.

abstract: Disclosed is a novel method and system for dehairing an animal, providing a system for recycling and safely disposing of chemical and biological wastes produced during such dehairing method. Included in such method are processes for handling sodium production in waste materials, reducing and handling production of H2S, removing sulfides from animal hides, safely disposing of sulfide waste, removing solids from the waste materials, and reducing water and reagent use and disposal.
reason: The patent describes a collection of specific chemical and biological waste-handling processes tailored to dehairing operations, rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The solution is a list of domain-specific steps (e.g., sulfide removal, H2S reduction) without a unifying functional principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: A method and apparatus for mechanical strain amplification for enhanced piezoelectric transduction. The device consists of a piezoelectric element elevated above the neutral axis of a supporting, micromachined, photoetched substrate by use of castellations on the substrate. By elevating the piezoelectric element above the neutral axis, the charge sensitivity of the device is increased which facilitates the development of high-sensitivity, low-noise transducers. There is a limit to charge sensitivity because the optimal elevation is a function of the physical properties of the supporting structure and the piezoelectric element. Accordingly, a mathematical formulation and finite element analysis (FEA) are provided to define the optimal height of the castellated substrate. The recognition of limits to the castellation height has further led to the discovery of using the relaxor-ferroelectric, single crystal class of materials in the present invention. Because the modulus of these materials is an order of magnitude less than that of piezoelectric ceramics, their use in the method of strain amplification is synergistic due to enhanced piezoelectric coefficients and the ability to extend castellation height. Furthermore, the simplicity of the transducer design, and the fact that its components are selected from photoetched, micromachined parts, result in unprecedented low costs of manufacturing for industrial-grade sensors. This method and apparatus for mechanical strain amplification is integral to a diverse group of piezoelectric-based transducers and sensors, such as accelerometers, velocity sensors, mechanical impedance heads, and hydrophones.
problem: Enhancing the sensitivity of piezoelectric transducers by amplifying mechanical strain applied to the piezoelectric element.
constraint: The trade-off between maximizing strain amplification and the physical limits imposed by the modulus and geometry of the supporting structure and piezoelectric material.
mechanism: Positioning a sensing element in a region of higher mechanical strain during deformation to amplify its output, with the optimal position determined by material properties of the supporting structure and the element.
mechanism_raw: Elevating the piezoelectric element above the neutral axis of a supporting substrate using castellations, which positions the element in a region of higher strain during deformation, thereby increasing charge sensitivity. The optimal elevation is determined by material properties of the substrate and element.

abstract: An electro-hydraulic controller having a plurality of solenoid operated valves mounted in inlet and outlet ported valving cavities on a non-metallic manifold block. The manifold block has inlet and outlet ports sealed by a gasket for communication with corresponding ports in a metallic base to which the manifold block is attached. The base is sufficiently rigid to resist prohibitive deflection when exposed to the forces of fluid pressure when secured over the open hydraulic channels of an automatic transmission shift circuit deck. The non-metallic manifold may be fabricated to “Net Shape” without costly secondary operations to achieve critical dimensions.
problem: Creating an electro-hydraulic controller that resists deflection under fluid pressure while enabling cost-effective manufacturing of complex valve configurations.
constraint: Balancing the structural rigidity of the metallic base against the manufacturing simplicity and dimensional precision achievable with the non-metallic manifold.
mechanism: Combining a rigid structural element with a precisely shaped component to balance strength and manufacturing efficiency, with a sealing element at the interface between materials.
mechanism_raw: Combining a rigid metallic base to resist hydraulic forces with a non-metallic manifold block that can be fabricated to net shape, allowing precise valve cavities without costly secondary machining. The gasket seals the interface between materials.

abstract: A spreader truck having a vessel for storage of a volume of powdered material is disclosed. A dust collector is mounted on the spreader truck such that airborne particles are collected as particulate material is spread over a subgrade or roadway. Filter media in the dust collector serves a dual purpose of collecting dust through a vent opening when the vessel is being loaded and collecting dust adjacent the outlet opening when the powder is being dispensed on to a subgrade
problem: Controlling airborne particulate emissions during both loading and dispensing phases of a powdered material spreader truck.
constraint: Ensuring the filter media can handle varying dust generation patterns and particle sizes across both loading and dispensing operations without compromising efficiency.
mechanism: A single filtration system that adapts its function to different operational phases by utilizing separate pathways for each phase, with filter media handling varying particle characteristics across phases.
mechanism_raw: Using a single dust collector with filter media that serves dual purposes: capturing dust during vessel loading via a vent opening and during powder dispensing via an outlet opening, adapting its function to the operational phase.

abstract: A module housing is adapted to be inserted into an operating position in the trigger group receiving area of a firearm. The module housing includes at least one pin receiver defined by two openings formed in the module housing, one on each lateral side of the housing. A module or temporary pin is received in the pin receiver and at least one trigger group component is mounted or supported for rotation on the module pin. The pin receiver is located on the module housing so as to align with a pin receptacle of the firearm when the module housing is in the operating position. By locating the pin receiver in the module housing so as to align with a corresponding pin receptacle of the firearm when the module housing is in the operating position, the trigger group module and the trigger group components housed in the module housing may be readily supported by the OEM pin receptacle. The trigger group module, pre-assembled with one or more trigger group components, may be inserted to the operating position and then held in place using the OEM pin receptacle.
problem: Installing a pre-assembled modular component into an existing system that has fixed mounting infrastructure, without requiring additional fasteners or modifications to the host system.
constraint: The attachment receivers on the module must be precisely located relative to the module's geometry so that they align with the host's mounting points when the module reaches its operating position, requiring tight manufacturing tolerances on the module housing.
mechanism: A modular component incorporates attachment interfaces positioned at locations that align with the host system's existing mounting points when the component is inserted into its operating position. This allows the pre-assembled component and its internal elements to be directly supported by the host's existing mounting infrastructure, eliminating the need for separate fastening steps.
mechanism_raw: A module housing incorporates attachment receivers (pin receivers) positioned at locations that align with the host system's existing mounting points (OEM pin receptacles) when the module is inserted into its operating position. This allows the pre-assembled module and its internal components to be directly supported by the host's existing mounting infrastructure, eliminating the need for separate fastening steps.

abstract: In a coal preparation plant which receives a raw coal feed and separates the raw coal feed into a clean coal feed and a refuse feed, an apparatus is provided for receiving and mixing the raw coal feed with water. The inventive apparatus includes a deslime screen assembly including a feedbox, magnetic separator and a deslime screen. The feedbox receives the raw coal feed and directs the raw coal onto the deslime screen for separation into coarse and fine sized raw coal fractions. The magnetic separator is provided which is integrally formed with the feedbox. The magnetic separator receives an input slurry of magnetic solid particles and water from the coal preparation plant, and separates the magnetic solid particles from the input slurry. The overflow tailings slurry output by the magnetic separator from which magnetic solid particles have been removed is received directly by the feedbox and mixed with the raw coal feed particles received thereby.
problem: Efficiently combining a solid-liquid separation step with a solid-liquid mixing step in a material processing system, where the mixing medium is a liquid stream that also needs to have solids removed before use.
constraint: The magnetic separator must be physically integrated with the feedbox to enable direct transfer of the overflow slurry, which constrains independent optimization of the separation and mixing functions but eliminates intermediate transfer steps and reduces system footprint.
mechanism: A separation unit is integrally formed with a processing chamber. The separation unit receives an input stream containing separable solid particles suspended in liquid, removes the separable particles, and outputs a cleaned liquid stream. This cleaned stream is directed directly into the processing chamber where it is mixed with the raw material feed, using the cleaned liquid stream as the mixing medium while simultaneously recovering valuable separable particles.
mechanism_raw: A magnetic separator is integrally formed with a feedbox/mixing chamber. The separator receives an input slurry containing magnetic solid particles suspended in liquid, removes the magnetic particles, and outputs an overflow tailings slurry (liquid with non-magnetic solids removed). This overflow is directed directly into the feedbox where it is mixed with the raw material feed, using the cleaned liquid stream as the mixing medium while simultaneously recovering valuable magnetic particles.
residual_terms: ["separation unit", "processing chamber", "separable solid particles", "cleaned liquid stream", "raw material feed"]

abstract: An adjustment table for aligning a body in a horizontal plane. The adjustable table includes an external frame, an intermediate frame moveable in a first horizontal direction in the external frame along a first path, and a holding unit for the body movable in a second horizontal direction that is perpendicular to the first horizontal direction in the intermediate frame along a second path. The intermediate frame can be positioned according to the external frame via a first adjustable device pivoted/hinged to the intermediate frame at a freely definable position along the first path. The holding unit can be positioned according to the intermediate frame via a second adjustment device pivoted/hinged to the holding unit at a freely definable position along the second path.
problem: Achieving precise two-axis alignment of a body in a plane using mechanical adjustment, where the adjustment mechanism must accommodate different body sizes or positions without redesign.
constraint: The freely definable pivot/hinge positions along each path add flexibility for accommodating different bodies, but require the adjustment devices to be designed with sufficient range of motion and structural integrity at arbitrary attachment points, potentially increasing mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A nested frame system provides two perpendicular degrees of freedom: an intermediate frame moves along a first axis within an external frame, and a holding unit moves along a second perpendicular axis within the intermediate frame. Each stage uses an adjustable device that is pivoted or hinged to its respective frame at a freely selectable position along the movement path, allowing the adjustment mechanism to be repositioned to suit different alignment requirements or body geometries.
mechanism_raw: A nested frame system provides two perpendicular degrees of freedom: an intermediate frame moves along a first axis within an external frame, and a holding unit moves along a second perpendicular axis within the intermediate frame. Each stage uses an adjustable device (e.g., screw or linkage) that is pivoted or hinged to its respective frame at a freely selectable position along the movement path, allowing the adjustment mechanism to be repositioned to suit different alignment requirements or body geometries.
residual_terms: ["nested frame system", "perpendicular degrees of freedom", "adjustable device", "movement path", "alignment requirements"]

abstract: A hybrid golf club shaft set is provided that includes a composite shaft subset including shafts formed entirely of composite, a composite/metal shaft subset including shafts formed of composite/metal combination shafts, and a metal shaft subset including shafts formed entirely of metal. The composite shaft subset preferably includes the long irons with the lowest lofts such as the two, three, and four iron shafts. The composite/metal shaft subset preferably includes the middle irons with medium lofts such as the five, six, and seven iron shafts. The metal shaft subset preferably includes the short irons with the highest lofts such as the eight, nine, and wedge shafts.
problem: Optimizing the performance of a family of tools or components that share a common function but operate under different loading or performance requirements across their range of use.
constraint: The material assignment must be systematically mapped to the functional requirements of each group, which increases manufacturing complexity due to multiple material types and assembly processes, but optimizes performance across the entire product family rather than using a single material for all components.
mechanism: Different material compositions are assigned to different subsets of a product family based on the specific functional requirements of each subset. Components that experience lower loads or require specific flexibility characteristics receive one material, components with intermediate requirements receive a hybrid material, and components with higher loads or different stiffness requirements receive another material. The assignment is made according to a systematic mapping of material properties to the operational demands of each group.
mechanism_raw: Different material compositions are assigned to different subsets of a product family based on the specific functional requirements of each subset. Components that experience lower loads or require specific flexibility characteristics receive one material (e.g., composite), components with intermediate requirements receive a hybrid material (e.g., composite/metal combination), and components with higher loads or different stiffness requirements receive another material (e.g., metal). The assignment is made according to a systematic mapping of material properties to the operational demands of each group.
residual_terms: ["material compositions", "product family", "functional requirements", "hybrid material", "material properties", "operational demands"]

abstract: An apparatus and method for conditioning a pad used for chemical-mechanical planarization (CMP) are provided, that allow the conditioning to be performed in situ without stopping the polishing. A retractable pad-conditioning structure, e.g., conditioning tips, is positioned along the bottom perimeter of a wafer carrier. While polishing a surface of a wafer held in the middle of the wafer carrier, whenever the removal rate drops below a permissible value, the pad-conditioning structure, which rotates in unison with the wafer carrier, is lowered to contact the pad to condition the pad's surface. Since an area of the pad used for polishing the wafer is always surrounded by already conditioned pad areas and the area for polishing moves as the wafer carrier moves around on the pad surface, a substantially uniform removal rate is maintained. When the pad is sufficiently conditioned, the conditioning structure is retracted until the pad needs to be conditioned again.
problem: Maintaining consistent performance of a working surface during continuous operation, where the surface degrades over time and periodic restoration is needed without interrupting the process.
constraint: The maintenance tool must be retractable so it does not interfere with normal operation, and the timing of deployment must be coordinated with real-time performance monitoring, adding control complexity while enabling continuous operation without downtime.
mechanism: A maintenance tool is mounted on the perimeter of the moving work tool and can be selectively deployed to contact and restore the working surface. During operation, when performance drops below a threshold, the maintenance tool is lowered to condition the surface. Because the work tool moves across the surface, the area being worked on is always surrounded by areas that have already been conditioned by the maintenance tool, ensuring uniform performance. After conditioning, the tool is retracted to resume normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A maintenance tool (conditioning structure) is mounted on the perimeter of the moving work tool (wafer carrier) and can be selectively deployed to contact and restore the working surface. During operation, when performance drops below a threshold, the maintenance tool is lowered to condition the surface. Because the work tool moves across the surface, the area being worked on is always surrounded by areas that have already been conditioned by the maintenance tool, ensuring uniform performance. After conditioning, the tool is retracted to resume normal operation.
residual_terms: ["maintenance tool", "moving work tool", "working surface", "performance threshold", "conditioning", "uniform performance"]

abstract: A wafer plating apparatus includes a wafer clamp for holding a wafer, a wafer support member for supporting the peripheral edge of the surface to be plated, and a plating tank which circulates a plating solution while making the plating solution overflow from an upper opening of the tank. The wafer plating apparatus is arranged to perform plating, while the surface to be plated is laid face down, being in contact with the surface of the plating solution, in a state in which the wafer is clamped by the wafer clamp and the wafer support member. The wafer support member is equipped with air-vent grooves for discharging the air which remains on the peripheral edge of the surface to be plated while the surface of the plating solution and the wafer make contact. The air-vent grooves are formed at the lower end of the wafer support portion.
problem: Air bubbles forming on the surface of a wafer during plating, causing defects in the plated layer.
constraint: The grooves must be positioned to remove air without disrupting the flow or overflow dynamics of the plating solution.
mechanism: Positioned channels at a support structure's lower end facilitate air discharge from a substrate's edge as it contacts a liquid, preventing bubble entrapment during face-down processing by maintaining solution flow dynamics.
mechanism_raw: Air-vent grooves positioned at the lower end of the wafer support member actively discharge air trapped at the peripheral edge of the wafer as it contacts the plating solution, preventing bubble entrapment during face-down plating.

abstract: A method including mixing powders of at least one of MgO, Mg(OH)2, and MgCO3, and powders of Fe2O3, CuO and ZnO, pre-sintering the mixed powder at 900° or lower, milling the pre-sintered raw powder, pressing the milled powder to form a pressed body and sintering the pressed body to form a magnetic ferrite powder such as MgCuZn, MgNiCuZn, or NiCuZn.
reason: The method describes a specific chemical synthesis process with material-specific steps (e.g., pre-sintering MgO/Fe2O3 mixtures at 900°C) that are tightly coupled to the composition and properties of magnetic ferrite powders. No generalizable causal operation is present.

abstract: An apparatus and a method for detecting the tilt angle of a wafer platform in a process machine, particularly in a medium density ion implanter. The apparatus and method can be used to accurately calibrate the zero-angle position of a wafer platform in the medium energy ion implanter. The apparatus includes a process chamber that has a cavity and a wafer platform therein, a window that is substantially transparent to laser energy mounted in a top wall of the chamber, and a laser emitter and receiver positioned outside the process chamber juxtaposed to the window for emitting a laser beam onto a wafer positioned on the wafer platform and receiving a reflected laser beam to determine a tilt angle of the wafer platform by the intensity of the reflected laser beam.
problem: Inaccurate calibration of the zero-angle position of a wafer platform in a process machine, leading to misalignment during operations like ion implantation.
constraint: The window must remain transparent to laser energy, and the system must account for surface reflectivity variations to maintain measurement accuracy.
mechanism: A light beam is directed through a transparent medium onto a surface, and the reflected intensity is measured to determine angular displacement, with intensity variation correlating directly to tilt angle while compensating for surface reflectivity differences.
mechanism_raw: A laser beam is emitted through a transparent window onto the wafer surface, and the intensity of the reflected beam is measured to determine the tilt angle of the platform. The intensity variation correlates directly with angular displacement.

abstract: A mounting plate for attachment of a furniture fitting such as a hinge arm of a furniture hinge to a wall of a piece of furniture, includes a bottom plate having an end face intended for securement to an attachment surface of the wall; and a top plate configured for placement over the bottom plate and having throughholes for passage of screw fasteners and an adjustment member which is provided to allow displacement of the top plate relative to the bottom plate. The top plate has a central portion, which is in line with the end face of the bottom plate on the attachment surface, and a marginal area which is slightly set back relative to the attachment surface.
problem: Inability to adjust the position of a furniture fitting (e.g., hinge arm) relative to an attachment surface after installation, requiring precise initial alignment.
constraint: The adjustment mechanism must balance ease of movement with sufficient friction or locking to maintain the desired position under load.
mechanism: A movable plate with openings and an adjustment element allows controlled displacement relative to a base plate, enabling post-installation positional adjustments while maintaining structural engagement through friction or locking mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: A top plate with throughholes and an adjustment member allows controlled displacement of the top plate relative to the bottom plate, enabling post-installation positional adjustments while maintaining structural engagement.

abstract: For the purpose of improving monitor display condition operating ease and enabling easy display of an arbitrary site, an ultrasonic image based on an echo signal received by an ultrasonic probe 3 is produced by an image producing section 12, a display area is formed on a screen by a display area forming section 17, a displayed range of the ultrasonic image to be displayed in the display area is selected by a displayed range selecting section 14, and scrolling of a selected range and rotation of the displayed range are achieved by a displayed range moving section 15 and a displayed range rotating section 16, respectively, based on a position on the monitor screen specified by the pointing device 3.
problem: Limited flexibility in viewing ultrasonic images on a monitor, restricting the ability to inspect arbitrary regions or orientations of the scanned area.
constraint: The system must process and render image data in real-time to avoid latency during scrolling or rotation operations.
mechanism: A display region is dynamically configured to allow selection, scrolling, and rotation of image data based on user input, enabling interactive navigation of the scanned area through real-time processing of spatial relationships.
mechanism_raw: A display area is dynamically formed on the screen, and the displayed range of the ultrasonic image is selected, scrolled, and rotated based on user input from a pointing device, enabling interactive navigation of the image data.

abstract: A safety pants with removable knee pads for providing a user with a pair of pants that would incorporate pockets which could house knee protection. The safety pants with removable knee pads include a pair of pants. The pants have a lower torso portion and two legs. Each of the legs has a front knee portion. Each one of a pair of pads has a size designed for covering one of the front knee areas. Each one of the pads provides a cushioning between a horizontal support surface and knees of a user when the user is in a kneeling position. A fastening assembly is for fastening each one of the pair of pads to an associated one of the legs for covering the knees of a user.
problem: Providing knee protection that can be selectively attached or removed without permanently altering the pants' structure.
constraint: Balancing the need for secure pad attachment during use with the ease of removal and the pants' usability without the pads.
mechanism: A detachable fastening system integrates protective elements into a garment's structural region, enabling selective attachment over a target area when needed and removal without altering the garment's base structure, while preserving the garment's inherent functionality.
mechanism_raw: A fastening assembly integrates removable pads into the pants' leg structure, allowing the pads to be secured over the knee area when needed and detached when not, while maintaining the pants' basic functionality.

abstract: Devices for holding money, whether paper or plastic. One device has a clip portion having inner and outer surfaces, two arms pivotally coupled to the clip portion, an outer covering material attached to at least a portion of the outer surface, and an inner covering material attached to at least a portion of the inner surface. The device can have inserts disposed in openings of the two arms. A kit that includes a device for holding money and a wallet configured to fit within the device, and more specifically to fit within the clip portion of the device, is also disclosed.
problem: Securely holding items like money while allowing controlled access and preventing loss.
constraint: Maintaining a balance between secure retention of items and ease of insertion/removal without damaging the items.
mechanism: A flexible gripping mechanism with opposing movable elements and compliant materials creates variable clamping force to retain items between the elements, allowing controlled insertion and removal while preventing item damage through adaptive material interaction.
mechanism_raw: A clip portion with pivotally coupled arms and covering materials creates a gripping mechanism that flexes to hold items between the arms, with inserts and material layers enhancing grip and retention.

abstract: The present invention discloses a system using a conduit run into a well on a service string. In one embodiment the conduit includes outlets along its length to permit a sand control treatment to exit the conduit along the length of the conduit and distribute the sand control treatment along the length of the conduit. The conduit can have a plurality of such outlets spaced to provide an even distribution of the sand control treatment. The conduit can be attached to the delivery tubing (such as coiled tubing or service string tubing) via a releasable connector. The conduit is deployed on the delivery tubing and connector (and is in fluid communication therewith) in the well adjacent to an area to be treated. The sand control treatment is pumped into the well. Once the sand control treatment is complete, the releasable connector is released to disconnect the conduit from the delivery tubing and the delivery tubing is removed from the well.
problem: Distributing a treatment fluid evenly along a wellbore section while enabling retrieval of the distribution system after treatment.
constraint: Ensuring even distribution of the treatment along the conduit's length while enabling reliable disconnection and retrieval without leaving components in the well.
mechanism: A deployable distribution conduit with spaced discharge points is temporarily connected to a delivery system via a releasable coupling, enabling uniform fluid distribution along the conduit length during operation. After use, the coupling is disengaged to retrieve the conduit without leaving components in place.
mechanism_raw: A conduit with spaced outlets is deployed via a releasable connector to the delivery tubing, allowing the treatment to exit uniformly along the conduit's length. After treatment, the connector is released to retrieve the conduit.

abstract: CMP systems and methods provide necessary vacuum and pressure to be applied from a vacuum chuck through a carrier film to a wafer without interfering with desired wafer planarization during CMP operations. Prior low polish rate-areas on the wafer may be eliminated from an exposed surface of the wafer by structure to uniformly compress the carrier film in response to a force from the wafer on the carrier film during the CMP operations. A distance between, and diameters of, adjacent holes of the carrier film are reduced, and the locations of the holes are in an array to coordinate with passageways through the vacuum chuck. The structure significantly reduces a maximum value of compression of the carrier film during CMP operations. As a result, during the CMP operations the wafer does not deform in a manner that exactly matches the compression of the carrier film, but remains essentially flat.
problem: Applying vacuum or pressure to a wafer during CMP without causing deformation that disrupts planarization.
constraint: Minimizing carrier film compression to prevent wafer deformation while maintaining effective vacuum/pressure application for planarization.
mechanism: A perforated interface layer with coordinated openings aligned to force-transmission pathways reduces localized compression while transmitting vacuum or pressure forces, maintaining surface flatness of a workpiece during processing by distributing forces across the interface.
mechanism_raw: A carrier film with holes arranged in a coordinated array with the vacuum chuck passageways reduces localized compression, allowing the wafer to remain flat while forces are transmitted through the film.
residual_terms: ["perforated interface layer", "force-transmission pathways", "vacuum or pressure forces", "workpiece"]

abstract: By using an InP single crystal substrate of the present invention in which the oxygen atom concentration is within the range of 1×1017 to 1×1018 atoms/cm3 for vapor phase epitaxial growth such as the MOCVD method, the occurrence of protrusions referred to as hillocks on the surface of the epitaxial layer formed on the substrate can be reduced, thereby allowing the providing of an InP single crystal substrate able to accommodate reduced thickness, multi-layering and enhanced function of the epitaxial layer.
problem: Preventing surface protrusions (hillocks) during vapor phase epitaxial growth on InP substrates.
constraint: Maintaining oxygen concentration within a narrow range (1×10¹⁷ to 1×10¹⁸ atoms/cm³) to achieve defect reduction without compromising substrate properties.
mechanism: Regulating a specific atomic species concentration within a substrate within a defined range modifies crystal growth dynamics during deposition, reducing surface defect formation and enabling controlled layer thickness in multi-layer structures.
mechanism_raw: Controlling oxygen atom concentration within a specific range in the InP substrate influences crystal growth behavior, reducing hillock formation during epitaxy and enabling thinner, multi-layered functional layers.
residual_terms: ["atomic species concentration", "substrate", "crystal growth dynamics", "surface defect formation"]

abstract: A process for forming gate oxides of multiple thicknesses. Oxygen is implanted through a sacrificial oxide into selected regions of a silicon substrate according to a patterned photoresist mask. After stripping the sacrificial oxide, a thermal growth process produces a thicker oxide in the implanted regions than in the non-implanted regions. The oxygen-implanted oxide has excellent quality and thickness differentials of up to 20 å may be obtained with relatively low oxygen implant doses. In an alternative process, a thin gate oxide may be grown prior to a polysilicon layer deposition, and oxygen is then implanted through the polysilicon according to a patterned photoresist mask. After stripping the photoresist, an anneal increases the thickness of the gate oxide in the implanted regions. In another embodiment, a high dielectric constant dielectric layer is deposited on the substrate prior to polysilicon deposition to limit subsequent silicon oxide growth.
problem: Creating gate oxides with multiple thicknesses on a single silicon substrate while using relatively low oxygen implant doses and avoiding excessive substrate damage.
constraint: Balancing the magnitude of thickness differentials against low implant dose requirements and minimizing substrate damage; the sacrificial oxide must be stripped before thermal growth to avoid interference.
mechanism: A temporary layer enables selective ion implantation to create regions with differing oxidation nucleation/growth rates. A subsequent single thermal process grows a thicker material in the implanted regions than in non-implanted regions, producing a thickness differential from one processing step.
mechanism_raw: Selective oxygen ion implantation through a sacrificial oxide layer creates regions with enhanced oxidation nucleation/growth rates. A subsequent single thermal oxidation step then grows a thicker oxide in the implanted regions than in non-implanted regions, producing a thickness differential from one processing step.

abstract: Method and system are disclosed for interactively developing at least one grid pattern, such as a microarray pattern, as well as an array set of such patterns, and a computer-readable storage medium having a program for executing the method given only a few user inputs through the use of a pointing device such as a mouse or trackball on a personal computer or workstation. Each array in the set typically has an identical number of rows and columns of points.
problem: Interactively developing complete grid patterns (e.g., microarray patterns) with minimal user effort through a pointing device.
constraint: Balancing user interaction simplicity (few inputs) against the need to generate complete, consistent, and reproducible grid patterns across multiple arrays in a set.
mechanism: A small number of spatial inputs provided via a pointing device are used to automatically generate a full grid pattern with a consistent number of rows and columns. The system extrapolates from the minimal spatial inputs to populate the entire array structure, and can replicate the pattern across an array set.
mechanism_raw: A small number of user inputs provided via a pointing device are used to automatically generate a full grid pattern with a consistent number of rows and columns. The system extrapolates from the minimal spatial inputs to populate the entire array structure, and can replicate the pattern across an array set.
