abstract: An apparatus (1) is proposed for drying and heat-treating pellets with a stream of inert gas, wherein the apparatus has a cuboid base unit (2) with a feed (3) for the pellets in its upper part and an outlet (4) in its lower part, with a feed (5) on one lateral surface and with an exhaust base (6) on the opposite lateral surface of the cuboid base unit (2) for the stream of inert gas, and also with distribution and retention equipment (7, 8) in the region of the feed (5) and, respectively, of the exhaust (6) for the stream of inert gas, where each of these extends essentially over the entire vertical cross section of the cuboid base unit (2).
problem: Uniformly drying and heat-treating pellets using a stream of inert gas flowing through a bed of pellets.
constraint: Balancing uniform gas distribution across the full cross-section against the mechanical simplicity and structural integrity of a cuboid chamber design.
mechanism: A cuboid chamber has opposing lateral surfaces serving as gas inlet and exhaust, each equipped with distribution and retention equipment that spans the entire vertical cross-section of the chamber. This full cross-sectional distribution ensures the inert gas stream is spread uniformly across the entire pellet bed as it flows from inlet to exhaust.
mechanism_raw: A cuboid chamber has opposing lateral surfaces serving as gas inlet and exhaust, each equipped with distribution and retention equipment that spans the entire vertical cross-section of the chamber. This full cross-sectional distribution ensures the inert gas stream is spread uniformly across the entire pellet bed as it flows from inlet to exhaust.

abstract: The voltage translator uses a PMOS transistor connected to a positive voltage source and a wordline, an NMOS transistor connected to a voltage source lower than the earth potential and a wordline as output stages, and has a PMOS transistor having a feedback function which is connected to the positive voltage source and an NMOS transistor having a feedback function which is connected to a voltage source lower than the earth potential. In the voltage translator, not only the positive voltage but a voltage lower than the earth potential as well is supplied to a selected wordline.
problem: Translating voltage levels to drive a selected wordline to both a positive voltage and a voltage lower than earth potential.
constraint: Balancing the ability to output dual voltage levels (both above and below earth potential) against the need for stable, reliable switching through feedback control.
mechanism: Complementary output transistors are connected to positive and below-earth-potential voltage sources respectively, with additional transistors providing feedback functions. The feedback-controlled complementary pair ensures stable switching and drives the target line to whichever voltage level is selected.
mechanism_raw: Complementary PMOS and NMOS output transistors are connected to positive and below-earth-potential voltage sources respectively, with additional PMOS and NMOS transistors providing feedback functions. The feedback-controlled complementary pair ensures stable switching and drives the wordline to whichever voltage level is selected.

abstract: A side knocking-type writing instrument has a barrel having a longitudinal axis, a front end, and a rear end. A sliding member is disposed in the barrel for undergoing forward and rearward sliding movement along the longitudinal axis of the barrel. The sliding member has a shoulder comprised of a generally L-shaped side wall having a first wall portion extending along the longitudinal axis and a second wall portion extending transversely to the longitudinal axis. A knocking member undergoes pivotal movement in a direction transverse to the longitudinal axis of the barrel about a fulcrum point disposed at a rear portion of the knocking member. The knocking member has a pressing portion disposed at a front portion thereof. A linking pawl is disposed between the knocking member and the sliding member for undergoing pivotal movement therebetween and axial movement along the longitudinal axis. The linking pawl has an outward end disposed in contact with the pressing portion of the knocking member and an inward end disposed in contact with the shoulder of the sliding member.
problem: Converting a transverse side-pressing input motion into axial extension or retraction of a writing tip in a side-knocking writing instrument.
constraint: Balancing the transverse input motion (side press) with the axial output motion (tip extension/retraction) through a linking pawl that must accommodate both rotational and translational degrees of freedom.
mechanism: A pivoting input element engages a linking component that can both pivot and slide axially. The combined pivoting and axial sliding motion of the linking component converts the transverse pivoting of the input element into axial motion of a sliding output member.
mechanism_raw: A knocking member pivots about a rear fulcrum when pressed, and its front pressing portion engages a linking pawl. The linking pawl can both pivot and slide axially, and its inward end contacts an L-shaped shoulder on a sliding member. The combined pivoting and axial sliding motion of the linking pawl converts the transverse pivoting of the knocking member into axial motion of the sliding member.

abstract: The foregoing differential gloss covering comprises a backing substrate, an ink layer, and a cured top layer having a first surface portion with a first gloss and a second surface portion, made by the process comprising providing the backing substrate; depositing an ink formulation comprising a curing agent over at least a first area of a top side of the backing substrate to form said ink layer; coating the top side of the backing substrate with a radiation curable formulation to form a top curable layer; diffusing at least a portion of the curing agent into the top curable layer; curing the top curable layer to form the cured top layer and thereby forming a differential gloss covering having said first surface portion above the first area of said top of said backing substrate having the first gloss and the second surface portion having the second gloss that is different from said first gloss.
problem: Creating a surface with spatially varying gloss levels (differential gloss) where different regions have different optical reflectance properties.
constraint: The diffusion of the curing agent must be controlled so that it migrates into the top layer in the desired spatial pattern without completely homogenizing, and the curing process must produce a sufficient gloss difference between regions while maintaining structural integrity of the covering.
mechanism: A patterned agent is deposited on a base layer, then a curable layer is applied over it. The agent diffuses into the curable layer in a spatially dependent manner, creating a concentration gradient. Upon curing, regions with varying agent concentrations cure differently, producing a differential property pattern that mirrors the original pattern.
mechanism_raw: A curing agent is deposited in a patterned ink layer on a substrate, then a curable top layer is applied over it. The curing agent diffuses from the ink layer into the overlying curable layer in a spatially dependent manner, creating a gradient of curing agent concentration. When the top layer is cured, regions with higher curing agent concentration cure differently (e.g., faster or to a different degree), producing a differential gloss pattern that mirrors the original ink pattern.

abstract: The invention is directed to polyurethane foam shoe soles containing an additive comprising a mixture of polyethylene wax and PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene), and to polyol components containing the additive. The additive is produced to include the mixture at a density from greater than 0.97 to about 1.1 times the density of the polyol component.
problem: Ensuring uniform distribution of functional additives (polyethylene wax and PTFE) throughout a polyurethane foam matrix without settling, separation, or clumping during foam formation.
constraint: The density ratio must be maintained within a narrow range (greater than 0.97 to about 1.1 times the polyol density) — too great a difference causes separation, while the upper limit prevents excessive mixing difficulties or processing issues.
mechanism: The density of the additive is matched to the base material's density within a specified range to align buoyancy characteristics, preventing separation during mixing and curing, resulting in uniform dispersion throughout the matrix.
mechanism_raw: The density of the additive mixture is matched to the density of the polyol component (within 0.97 to 1.1 times the polyol density) so that the additive has similar buoyancy characteristics to the base material. This density matching prevents the additive from settling or floating during the foam mixing and curing process, resulting in uniform dispersion throughout the foam structure.

abstract: A system is described for detecting at least one event of interest. The system comprises a detector, a programmable controller, and a network. Upon detection of an event of interest, the detector communicates that information to the programmable controller through the network. The programmable controller allows a user, who may be in diverse geographic locations, to control the detector.
reason: The system uses standard network-based remote control architecture (detector → network → controller → remote user) without a novel causal mechanism. The described functionality—remote detection and control over a network—is a well-established concept with no unique problem-solving principle beyond conventional distributed control systems.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method and a device for controlling the wort flow from a lauter tun. To shorten the lautering time, according to the present invention a second increased outflow value which is to be reached within a given time interval is predetermined in the course of the total sequence of a brewing process (first wort, second worts) in at least one phase (trending phase), based on a predetermined outflow value of the wort outflow, the increase in flow rate/per time unit (increase value) as is required for attaining the second outflow value is determined on the basis of these values, and the determined increase value is used as a set value for controlling an outflow regulator.
problem: Shortening the lautering time in brewing by increasing the wort outflow rate from a lauter tun, while maintaining process control and avoiding disruption to the brewing sequence.
constraint: The increase in flow rate must be achieved within a specific time interval during a particular phase of the brewing process (trending phase), and the acceleration must be calculated based on the process sequence (first wort, second worts) to avoid disrupting the overall brewing timeline or product quality.
mechanism: A control system calculates the required rate of change (acceleration) of a process variable by dividing the difference between the current value and a target value by the time interval over which the change should occur. This calculated acceleration is used as the setpoint for the regulator, causing the system to progressively adjust the variable until the target is reached.
mechanism_raw: Instead of directly commanding a target outflow rate, the system calculates the required rate of change (acceleration) of the outflow based on the difference between the current outflow and a predetermined higher target outflow, divided by the time interval over which the increase should occur. This calculated increase value (rate of change) is then used as the setpoint for the outflow regulator, causing the system to progressively increase the flow rate at the computed acceleration until the target is reached.

abstract: A decorative craft kit and associated method of using the kit for use in decorating various objects with decorative resin is disclosed. The kit comprises a plurality of tube dispensers, a plurality of caps, and a plurality of applique tips. Each tube dispenser includes a main tubular body portion, a neck portion, a nozzle head portion, and a decorative resin wherein the decorative resin comprises water, acrylic polymer, calcium carbonate, ethylene glycol, mineral spirits and a coloring agent. Each cap of the plurality of caps is separately attached to the nozzle head portion of each corresponding tube dispenser. Each applique tip of the plurality of applique tips are separately attachable to the nozzle head portion of each corresponding tube dispenser. Another preferred embodiment of the kit consist essentially of a plurality of tube dispensers, a plurality of caps, a plurality of applique tips, a stylized logo, and a color indicia. The method of using the kit comprises the steps of aiming, allowing, identifying, obtaining, picking, putting, removing, screwing, selecting, squeezing, and un-screwing
reason: The patent describes a craft kit with various physical components (tube dispensers, caps, applique tips) and lists a sequence of manual user actions (aiming, squeezing, screwing, etc.) without identifying a genuine problem-solving mechanism. The 'method' is merely a collection of discrete manual steps rather than a causal functional relationship that produces a useful effect.

abstract: This invention provides a metallic article with a metallic substrate having a thermal barrier ceramic coating on its surface, the ceramic coating comprising a plurality of first layers of about 6 to 8 wt % yttria stabilized zirconia alternating with a plurality of second layers of about 18 to 22 wt % yttria stabilized zirconia. The alternating layers can be distinct layers or gradient layers.
problem: Thermal degradation of metallic substrates exposed to extreme temperatures in high-stress environments (e.g., turbine blades).
constraint: Balancing thermal insulation performance with mechanical durability and adhesion to the substrate under cyclic thermal loading.
mechanism: Alternating layers with compositionally distinct thermal properties create a gradient that reduces heat flux through the structure while accommodating differential thermal expansion between adjacent layers, thereby dissipating stress and inhibiting crack propagation under cyclic thermal loading.
mechanism_raw: Alternating layers of yttria-stabilized zirconia with differing compositions (6-8 wt% and 18-22 wt%) create a thermal gradient and stress-dissipating structure. The distinct or gradient layers reduce heat flux through the coating while accommodating thermal expansion mismatches between layers, preventing crack propagation.

abstract: The electronic device (1) has a layer (11) of a material comprising a first and a second element. This material has an amorphous and a crystalline state. A transition from the amorphous to the crystalline state can be effected by heating of the material to above a crystallization temperature, for example with a laser. As a result, the layer (11) has a first electrically conducting areas (21), comprising the material in the crystalline state, which are insulated from each other by the first electrically insulating area (23), comprising the material in the amorphous state. The layer (11) may be present as an interconnect layer, but also as a covering layer. Preferably, the material is aluminum-germanium. In the method of patterning a layer (11), electrically conductive areas of the layer can be strengthened by electroplating.
problem: Creating electrically conductive pathways in a material layer without traditional lithography or etching processes.
constraint: Precisely controlling the energy input to achieve sharp transitions between phases without damaging surrounding areas or causing unintended conductivity.
mechanism: A phase-change material capable of existing in insulating and conductive states is selectively energized to induce localized phase transitions, forming conductive regions separated by untransformed insulating regions. This enables direct patterning of electrical pathways through controlled energy input without material removal.
mechanism_raw: A material capable of existing in amorphous (insulating) and crystalline (conducting) states is selectively heated (e.g., via laser) to induce localized crystallization. This phase transition enables the formation of conductive regions insulated from each other by unheated amorphous regions, allowing direct patterning of electrical circuits.

abstract: Power supply apparatuses and methods of supplying electrical energy are provided. According to one aspect, a power supply apparatus includes an electrochemical device configured to store electrical energy, a first interface coupled with the electrochemical device and adapted to couple with a supply configured to provide electrical energy and a first load configured to receive electrical energy, and charge circuitry coupled intermediate the first interface and the electrochemical device, wherein the charge circuitry is configured to monitor a quantity of electrical energy supplied from the supply to the first load and to control a supply of electrical energy to the electrochemical device responsive to the monitoring and to charge the electrochemical device.
problem: Efficiently managing energy distribution between a power supply, a load, and an energy storage device to avoid overloading or underutilization.
constraint: Maintaining real-time responsiveness of the monitoring and control system to avoid delays that could destabilize the load or storage device.
mechanism: A real-time monitoring system dynamically adjusts energy distribution between a primary load and an energy storage device via a feedback loop, diverting excess energy to storage only when available. This maintains load stability while optimizing energy capture through continuous sensing and responsive control.
mechanism_raw: Charge circuitry monitors the electrical energy supplied to the load in real time and dynamically adjusts the amount of energy diverted to the electrochemical storage device. This feedback loop ensures the storage device is charged only when excess energy is available, maintaining stable operation of the load while optimizing energy capture.

abstract: A method for fitting a horse for a custom fitting saddle pad or saddle. The steps include positioning a horse in a working position, marking a first reference line and a second reference line, positioning a pad on the horse's back, securing the pad on the horse's back, forming a cast of the horse's back, and removing the cast from the horse to be transported.
problem: Creating a custom-fitted interface (e.g., saddle pad) that conforms precisely to an irregular surface (e.g., a horse’s back) to distribute pressure evenly.
constraint: Accurately capturing the surface geometry without causing discomfort or movement during the casting process.
mechanism: A molding process captures the exact geometry of a target surface while the subject is in a functional position, creating a replica that conforms to dynamic surface contours. The resulting interface adapts to movement by replicating the captured geometry, ensuring pressure distribution and positional stability.
mechanism_raw: A cast is formed directly on the target surface while the subject is in a working position, capturing its exact geometry. The cast is then used to fabricate a pad that replicates the surface contours, ensuring a tailored fit that adapts to dynamic movement.

abstract: An imaging system is disclosed for imaging and registering recordable media. The imaging system includes an input opening through which recordable media may be input to the imaging system, an imaging unit, a registration unit and an output opening through which registered imaged media may exit the imaging system. The imaging unit is for imaging the recordable media that is received through the input opening, and provides imaged media. The registration unit is for receiving imaged media from the imaging unit, and for registering the imaged media by creating registration features in the imaged media. The registration unit provides registered imaged media.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment of imaged media (e.g., photographic film, printed circuits) after imaging to enable accurate downstream processing or assembly.
constraint: Integrating registration feature creation into the imaging workflow without disrupting media transport or introducing additional alignment errors.
mechanism: Physical reference features are created on imaged media immediately after imaging to serve as alignment anchors for downstream processes. These features correct positional deviations introduced during imaging by providing fixed reference points for registration, integrating alignment into the imaging workflow without disrupting media transport.
mechanism_raw: A registration unit creates physical alignment features (e.g., perforations, fiducial marks) on the imaged media immediately after imaging. These features serve as reference points for subsequent registration steps, correcting any positional deviations introduced during the imaging process.

abstract: A system comprising a rotating device and a finger supported charging assembly for powering the rotating device. The rotating device has a housing with a base upon which the housing spins. An electric motor is contained within the housing that causes the housing to spin when the motor is activated. The finger supported charging assembly includes two contacts that are coupled to opposite terminals of a battery pack. The contacts are worn on opposing fingers and come into contact with the rotating device when the base of the rotation device is supported with the opposing fingers, when contacting the rotating device, the contacts on the opposing fingers provide electricity to the rotating device that powers the motor within the rotating device.
problem: Providing power to a rotating device without physical cables or docking stations, using only the user's fingers as both support and electrical contacts.
constraint: The contacts must only activate when the device is properly supported to avoid unintended power transfer or short circuits during handling.
mechanism: Opposing contact elements on a support structure engage conductive surfaces on a device only when the device is physically supported between them, enabling conditional power transfer to an internal actuator without external cables or docking interfaces.
mechanism_raw: Opposing finger-mounted contacts on a battery pack engage conductive surfaces on the rotating device's base when the device is supported between the fingers, directly transferring power to the internal motor.

abstract: A showerhead which automatically adjusts the outlet pressure of the water in accordance with changes in water pressure, and eliminates the operation of a faucet, thus enabling showers to be taken comfortably. The showerhead (1) spurts the water, which is flowing from a water source to the specified pipes, through the outlet holes (H) of the shower nozzle (5). The shower nozzle (5) comprises waterproof elastic materials such as silicon rubber or the like. The elastic surface of the shower nozzle (5) incorporates outlet holes (H) which can be enlarged and reduced in accordance with changes in water pressure inside the showerhead (1).
problem: Automatically adjusting water outlet pressure in a showerhead to maintain comfort despite variations in supply pressure, without manual intervention.
constraint: The elastic material must respond quickly and reversibly to pressure fluctuations while maintaining structural integrity under continuous water flow.
mechanism: Elastomeric flow-regulating elements dynamically adjust their effective aperture in response to internal pressure fluctuations, modulating flow rate to stabilize perceived output pressure despite supply variations.
mechanism_raw: Elastic outlet holes in a waterproof silicone rubber nozzle expand or contract in response to internal water pressure changes, dynamically modulating flow rate to stabilize perceived pressure.

abstract: An emergency signaling system with integrated load management functionality is provided wherein the load management circuitry is alternatively operable in programming and operating modes. The system includes a keypad, control head, control unit and a plurality of signaling features selectively activated by the control unit in the operating mode. The load management circuitry automatically sheds loads from the signaling system in response to an indication from the electrical system powering the signaling system that an energy drain is occurring at the energy source that will cause disruption to other more important systems—e.g., the ignition system in a vehicle.
problem: Preventing an emergency signaling system from draining power from critical vehicle systems (e.g., ignition) during energy shortages.
constraint: The system must prioritize critical loads (e.g., ignition) over signaling functions while ensuring emergency signaling remains operational during non-critical energy conditions.
mechanism: Load prioritization circuitry monitors energy availability at a power source and automatically disconnects non-critical loads when disruption to higher-priority systems is detected, preserving operational capacity for critical functions during energy shortages.
mechanism_raw: Load management circuitry monitors energy drain at the power source and automatically sheds non-critical signaling loads when disruption to higher-priority systems is detected.

abstract: A microelectromechanical system package has a microelectromechanical system microphone, a substrate, and a cover. The substrate has a surface for supporting the microelectromechanical microphone. The cover includes a conductive layer having a center portion bounded by a peripheral edge portion. A housing is formed by connecting the peripheral edge portion of the cover to the substrate. The center portion of the cover is spaced from the surface of the substrate to accommodate the microelectromechanical system microphone. The housing includes an acoustic port for allowing an acoustic signal to reach the microelectromechanical system microphone.
problem: Protecting a sensitive MEMS microphone while allowing acoustic signals to reach it.
constraint: Balancing acoustic signal transmission with environmental protection and structural integrity of the housing.
mechanism: A protective enclosure formed by a barrier element connected to a base, with a central region of the barrier spaced from the base to create a sealed internal volume. A controlled aperture in the enclosure allows acoustic energy to pass through while isolating the protected component from external environmental interference.
mechanism_raw: A housing formed by connecting a cover's peripheral edge to a substrate, with the cover's center portion spaced from the substrate to create a sealed cavity. An acoustic port in the housing allows sound waves to pass through while isolating the microphone from external environmental interference.

abstract: An optical detection device for use in a color sorting apparatus for granular objects includes a CCD linear sensor. The CCD linear sensor comprises a plurality of light receiving elements arranged in one row each of which is capable of detecting red, green and blue wavelengths. The CCD linear sensor receives light from a granular object and a background which are irradiated by a red light source, a green light source and a blue light source. The red, green and blue light sources are switched over while the granular object is passing within an optical detection area. The CCD linear sensor receives light from the granular object in synchronization with the above switching operation of the light sources.
problem: Accurately detecting color characteristics of moving granular objects in a sorting apparatus.
constraint: Precisely timing light source switching and sensor readout to match the object's motion without introducing detection lag or misalignment.
mechanism: Coordinated activation of multiple light sources with sensor readout timing, where each light source is energized in sequence and the sensor captures reflected energy in lockstep with the illumination, ensuring color data is acquired as the object traverses the detection zone without temporal misalignment.
mechanism_raw: Synchronized switching of red, green, and blue light sources with the readout timing of a CCD linear sensor, ensuring that light detection occurs in lockstep with illumination to capture precise color data as the object passes through the detection area.

abstract: A system and method for moving a canister of spent nuclear fuel from a first location, which may be within a nuclear power generation facility to a second location such as a storage cask that is used for short-term or long-term storage of spent nuclear fuel includes a first lifting mechanism for engaging a transfer cask and a second lifting mechanism for engaging and lifting the canister of spent nuclear fuel. Preferably, the method is practiced by first positioning a canister of spent nuclear fuel within the transfer cask and then engaging the transfer cask with the first lifting mechanism. The canister is engaged with the second lifting mechanism. The transfer cask having the canister positioned within is moved to the vicinity of a storage cask, and the canister is lowered from the transfer cask into the storage cask by the second lifting mechanism without disengagement of the first lifting mechanism from the transfer cask. Ideally, the second lifting mechanism is mounted on a portion of the first lifting mechanism that is relatively free from relative movement with respect to the transfer cask during operation. Accordingly, the lowering of the canister may be performed with a minimum of relative movement between the canister and the transfer cask, obviating or reducing the necessity for supplemental tiedowns of the transfer cask during this procedure, which is an inefficient process that if performed incorrectly can expose humans to unwanted radiation.
problem: Safely transferring a canister of spent nuclear fuel between locations while minimizing human exposure to radiation.
constraint: Maintaining minimal relative movement between the canister and transfer cask during lowering to avoid destabilization and reduce radiation exposure risks.
mechanism: A hierarchical lifting arrangement where a secondary lifting mechanism is mechanically coupled to and supported by a primary lifting mechanism, enabling independent displacement of the load relative to the primary support structure without decoupling the primary mechanism or requiring external stabilization of the support structure.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual-lifting system where a secondary lifting mechanism (engaging the canister) is mechanically mounted on the primary lifting mechanism (engaging the transfer cask), enabling independent lowering of the canister without disengaging the primary lift or requiring supplemental stabilization of the transfer cask.
residual_terms: ["lifting mechanism", "primary lifting mechanism", "secondary lifting mechanism", "support structure"]

abstract: A road-marking system comprising at least a first (1) and a second road-marking unit (2) each having an emission surface (10; 20), the first unit comprising a first light source (21, 21′ . . . ) and the second unit comprising a second light source (22, 22′ . . . ). Each unit has a shape adapted to a saw-cut recess (9) accommodating the unit.
reason: The patent describes a static physical design (road-marking units shaped to fit saw-cut recesses) without a causal functional mechanism beyond component geometry. The solution is product-specific and lacks a transferable operational principle.

abstract: The invention describes a method for the drying of a damp material (2), whereby the material (2) is treated in a treatment chamber (15) of a drying cabinet (1) in a mechanically immobile condition, in which air (10) is directed through the treatment chamber (15) and over a condenser (13) and the moisture in the air (10) can condense at the condenser (13) and be led away. The air (10) is led about the material (2) for drying at least during a period of the drying of the material (2) in a closed loop through the treatment chamber (15) in which the material (2) at increasing temperature in the treatment chamber (15) is exposed to steam or increased humidity generated at least partly from the dampness of the material (2) or the increased humidity of the air (10) circulating around and is relaxed and smoothed by the steam or the increased humidity in relation to creases, folds or similar from preceding treatments, and with an increasing dehumidify of the residual humidity of the air (10) after the beginning of the condensation at the condenser (13) the material (2) then is freed from creases, folds or similar and therefore is then dried largely without ironing. Further the invention describes a drying cabinet (1) for the drying of the damp material (2) is treated in a treatment chamber (15) of a drying cabinet (1) in mechanically immobile condition which shows flaps (21, 22) to be switched between the circulation in the closed circulation and a treatment in the open circulation which make possible an introduction and exhausting from external air.
problem: Drying damp materials (e.g., textiles) without requiring post-drying ironing to remove creases and folds.
constraint: Balancing humidity levels and temperature to ensure crease relaxation without over-saturating the material or compromising drying efficiency.
mechanism: A closed-loop environmental control system that exposes the material to elevated humidity derived from its own moisture content, followed by controlled dehumidification via condensation, creating a humidified drying environment that relaxes deformable features while removing moisture.
mechanism_raw: A closed-loop air circulation system that exposes the material to steam or increased humidity generated from its own moisture, combined with controlled condensation to gradually dehumidify the air. This creates a humidified environment that relaxes creases while drying, eliminating the need for mechanical ironing.

abstract: A garage door reinforcement arrangement for supporting and anchoring a garage door to a garage door opening includes an I-post beam assembly, a top mounting bracket, a floor plate, and a plurality of cable assemblies. The top mounting bracket is used to secure the top end of the I-post beam against vertical movement. The floor plate is used for securing the bottom end of the I-post against vertical movement. The plurality of cable assemblies are disposed at different vertical positions of the I-post beam for securing the beam immediately adjacent to the garage door so that the garage door is allowed to flex slightly as wind loads are transferred to the beam.
problem: Supporting a garage door against wind loads while allowing controlled flex to prevent structural failure.
constraint: The cables must be spaced to distribute loads evenly without over-constraining the door, which could amplify stress concentrations.
mechanism: Tensioned flexible elements positioned at multiple spaced points along a rigid structural member transfer lateral loads to the member while permitting slight deformation of the supported surface, balancing structural support with localized movement.
mechanism_raw: Cables positioned at multiple vertical points along a rigid I-post beam transfer lateral wind loads to the beam while permitting slight flexing of the door, balancing structural support with localized movement.

abstract: A composite fan consists of a first fan and a second fan located on the air outlet side of the first fan. The first fan has a plurality of first rotary vanes and a plurality of first guide vanes located on the air outlet side of the first rotary vanes. The second fan has a plurality of second rotary vanes and a plurality of second guide vanes located on the air inlet side of the second rotary vanes. Each of the second guide vanes corresponds to and is coupled with each of the first guide vanes to form a continuous curved surface.
problem: Improving airflow efficiency in a multi-stage fan system by reducing turbulence between stages.
constraint: The guide vanes must maintain precise alignment to preserve the continuous surface while accommodating rotational movement of the fans.
mechanism: Coupling corresponding guide vanes from adjacent rotary stages to form a continuous curved surface streamlines fluid flow between rotary vanes and minimizes energy loss from flow separation.
mechanism_raw: Coupling corresponding guide vanes from adjacent fans to form a continuous curved surface, which streamlines airflow between rotary vanes and minimizes energy loss from flow separation.
residual_terms: ["guide vanes", "rotary stages", "continuous curved surface", "fluid flow", "flow separation"]

abstract: An abrasive wheel is used to separate individual laminated chips from a strip by cutting through the copper bridging elements. The abrasive wheel is made up of abrasive particles bonded in a matrix having a high glass transition temperature and a cutting edge having a maximum thickness of the order of 350 micron, whereby the cut is substantially straight and free of smears and burrs.
problem: Achieving clean, burr-free cuts in laminated materials without smearing or damaging adjacent layers.
constraint: The matrix material must balance hardness for cutting with thermal stability to avoid degradation during high-speed operation.
mechanism: An abrasive cutting element with a thermally stable matrix and a precisely controlled cutting edge thickness maintains a straight cut while preventing material deformation during separation of layered materials.
mechanism_raw: Using an abrasive wheel with a high glass transition temperature matrix and a precisely controlled cutting edge thickness (≤350 microns) to maintain a straight cut while preventing material deformation during separation.
residual_terms: ["abrasive cutting element", "thermally stable matrix", "cutting edge thickness", "material deformation", "layered materials"]

abstract: In a nanostructured reactive substance and a process for producing the same, intermixing of silicon and oxidizing agent on a nanometer size scale permits virtually direct contact between the fuel and the oxidizing agent, only separated by a barrier layer. After the barrier layer is broken open, fuel and oxidizing agent are spatially directly together and can react, liberating energy. The reactive substance has a high reaction rate in comparison with conventional reactive materials.
problem: Enabling rapid, controlled energy release in reactive materials by overcoming slow reaction kinetics of conventional mixtures.
constraint: The barrier layer must be robust enough to prevent premature reaction during storage but fragile enough to rupture reliably under intended activation conditions.
mechanism: Intermixing reactive components at nanoscale dimensions with a barrier layer that, when broken, allows direct spatial contact between reactants, triggering near-instantaneous exothermic reactions.
mechanism_raw: Intermixing fuel and oxidizer at nanometer scales with a barrier layer that, when broken, allows direct spatial contact between reactants, triggering near-instantaneous exothermic reactions.

abstract: A vehicle power window and power door lock system includes a vehicle pillar adapted for use between openable and closable vehicle doors and a single lock actuation assembly in the pillar adapted for engagement with a front door lock latch assembly on a front door and a rear door lock latch assembly on a rear door for locking and unlocking the doors. The vehicle power window and power door lock system further includes a single reversible electric motor in the pillar adapted for selective engagement with a front window on an adjacent front door and a rear window on an adjacent rear door for driving the windows up and down. A vehicle side door assembly includes a door lock latch assembly, a latch rod operatively connected to the latch assembly, a window, and a driven gear operatively connected to the window. The latch rod is operably connectable to a lock actuation assembly located in a body pillar adjacent to the door when the door is positioned against the body pillar. The driven gear is operably connectable to a motor located in the body pillar.
problem: Centralizing actuation of multiple vehicle doors and windows using a single motor to reduce complexity and cost.
constraint: The motor and gear engagement must coordinate timing and force distribution across multiple doors without mechanical interference or overloading.
mechanism: A single reversible motor engages with mechanical transmission elements in adjacent doors, distributing motion to simultaneously drive window movement and door locking/unlocking.
mechanism_raw: A single reversible motor in the vehicle pillar engages with gears and latch rods in adjacent doors, distributing mechanical motion to simultaneously drive window movement and door locking/unlocking.
residual_terms: ["single reversible motor", "mechanical transmission elements", "adjacent doors", "window movement", "door locking/unlocking"]

abstract: A foldable knife. The foldable knife includes a flat handle and two opposite blades pivotably coupled to forward and rear ends of the handle respectively. The handle includes two resilient pieces on two opposite sides, each resilient piece being capable of being pressed by a hand of a user to fold or the resilient piece is urged against a rear end of the blade for locking the blade in a closed or opened position. The knife further includes a protective element disposed on the handle. The protective element has a height sufficient to prevent the cutting edges of the blades from contacting the hand of the user when the blades are in the closed position.
problem: Creating a foldable knife that is both safe for the user and functional in locking blades in open or closed positions.
constraint: Balancing blade operability (manual folding/locking) with safety (preventing hand-blade contact) through precise resilient piece placement and protective element height.
mechanism: Resilient elements integrated into a gripping region enable manual actuation to transition a cutting member between operational states, while a spatially positioned barrier prevents contact between a user's hand and the cutting member's edge during movement.
mechanism_raw: Resilient pieces on the handle allow manual pressing to fold or lock blades, while a protective element's height physically blocks the hand from contacting blade edges during closure.

abstract: The combination pendant clasp of this disclosure is suitable for a necklace or bracelet. It provides a positive locking clasp which is manipulated in front of the wearer. The pendant clasp has two principle members, both of which may be decorated with precious stones, and may symbolize a relationship between individuals. Placement of the clasp in the front of a necklace or bracelet avoids the chance that the clasp will become inadvertently and unnoticed open and the jewelry lost.
reason: The solution relies on a design choice (front placement of the clasp) rather than a causal functional mechanism that can be abstracted and applied to other fields.

abstract: The invention is directed to an apparatus made of atmospheric-pressure microwave plasma torches for elimination of toxic airborne chemical and biological warfare agents. The apparatus can purify the interior air of large volume in an isolated space such as buildings, public transportation systems, and military vehicles contaminated with chemical and biological warfare agents. The apparatus consists of several microwave plasma torches connected in series for elimination and burnout of toxic airborne warfare agents. Microwave radiation generates an atmospheric plasma torch in certain conditions. Oxidation mechanism in the torch flames eliminates the chemical and biological warfare agents.
problem: Eliminating toxic airborne chemical and biological agents in large enclosed spaces without compromising air volume or safety.
constraint: Maintaining atmospheric pressure operation while ensuring sufficient plasma intensity and series configuration to achieve complete agent burnout without excessive energy input.
mechanism: A series of atmospheric-pressure plasma stages generate progressive oxidation zones, where contaminants undergo sequential breakdown as a fluid medium passes through multiple treatment regions without requiring pressure differential maintenance.
mechanism_raw: Series-connected atmospheric-pressure microwave plasma torches generate oxidation in flame zones, progressively breaking down contaminants as air passes through multiple stages.

abstract: A sound shield is positioned between the burner chamber of a furnace and the portion of the furnace immediately in front of the burner chamber which is typically a removable door. The removable door has slotted vents that allow air to be drawn into the burner chamber. The sound shield is positioned between the slotted vents and the burner chamber in such a manner so as to prevent substantial amounts of burner noise being produced by burning fuel from escaping through the vents. This is done without unduly restricting the flow of air through the slotted vents to the burner chamber.
problem: Reducing burner noise in a furnace without restricting airflow through vent openings.
constraint: Balancing noise attenuation effectiveness with minimal airflow resistance to avoid disrupting combustion efficiency.
mechanism: A noise-attenuating barrier is positioned between a combustion source and airflow apertures to block acoustic propagation while permitting fluid flow through the apertures unimpeded.
mechanism_raw: A sound shield is positioned between the burner and slotted vents to block noise propagation while allowing air to flow through the vents unimpeded.

abstract: A method for producing hydrophobic polyolefin-containing fibers or filaments, in particular cardable staple fibers, using spin finishes applied after spinning and stretching, that comprise at least one water-insoluble ester of a mono-, di-, tri- or tetrahydric alcohol with a molecular weight not exceeding 500 and a branched or straight chain fatty acid with between 12 and 30 carbon atoms, e.g. a water-insoluble ester of ethylene or propylene glycol, glycerol, neopentyl glycol, trimethylolethane or trimethylolpropane and at least one saturated or unsaturated fatty acid residue having 12-24 carbons atoms, an anionic or nonionic antistatic agent preferably being applied after crimping; fibers produced by the method; and nonwovens produced from such fibers.
problem: Producing hydrophobic and antistatic polyolefin fibers with durable surface properties after mechanical processing.
constraint: Selecting ester molecular weight (≤500) and fatty acid chain length (12–30 carbons) to ensure water insolubility and compatibility with polyolefin substrates during processing.
mechanism: Water-insoluble chemical modifiers are applied in distinct processing stages—first during primary shaping and second during texturizing—to alter surface chemistry while preserving bulk material integrity through controlled molecular weight and chain length selection.
mechanism_raw: Applying water-insoluble esters post-spinning/stretching and antistatic agents post-crimping to modify surface chemistry without compromising fiber integrity.

abstract: A ball launching device for children that has an outer housing, an inner bowl and a launch assembly. The inner bowl has an inner surface with an outwardly curved cone shaped wall and a vertical linear wall. The launch assembly is connected to the bowl. When the bowl rotates at high speeds, the curved cone shaped wall enables balls to ascend up the inner surface and eventually propel out of the ball launching device.
problem: Propelling discrete objects (e.g., balls) outward from a rotating chamber using centrifugal force while ensuring controlled ascent and ejection.
constraint: The curvature of the cone and rotational speed must be balanced to ensure objects ascend smoothly without jamming or premature ejection.
mechanism: A curved surface combined with rotational motion creates a force gradient that moves objects along the surface until they reach an exit, where a directional element guides their trajectory outward.
mechanism_raw: A curved conical inner surface combined with high-speed rotation creates a centrifugal force gradient that lifts objects along the surface until they reach an exit point, where the vertical wall directs their trajectory outward.

abstract: A method of cleaning potable liquid flow lines employing a high pH caustic cleaning solution or a low pH acid cleaning solution with a stable dye in sufficient concentration so as to have a visible color when the solution is further diluted. The cleaning solution is pumped through the lines. The lines then are flushed with clean water until no colored solution is discharged from the lines, indicating the lines have been purged of cleaning solution. The method can be used with draft beer, soft drink or other potable liquid flow lines to prevent inadvertent consumption of caustic cleaning solution along with subsequently dispensed potable liquid.
problem: Verifying complete purging of a cleaning solution from a liquid flow line without relying on chemical sensors or complex monitoring systems.
constraint: The dye concentration must be high enough to remain visible at dilution thresholds but low enough to not interfere with the cleaning process or leave harmful residues.
mechanism: A visible indicator is introduced into the cleaning solution at a concentration detectable when diluted. The solution is flushed until the indicator is no longer visible, providing visual confirmation of purging completion.
mechanism_raw: A visible dye is added to the cleaning solution at a concentration that remains detectable when diluted. The solution is flushed until the dye is no longer visible, providing a direct visual confirmation of purging completion.

abstract: The invention relates to a helmet with retractable visors for fast day/night reconfiguration.For that, the helmet (1) is designed at the articulations of the visors to allow the use of articulations that can be disassembled without tools. The day visor (15) is thus made modular and removable and is mounted on the helmet by a translational movement in a direction (F) allowing the upper part (16) to engage in a saggital guide rail of the helmet and allowing rotation axes of the helmet to engage in the articulation part of the lateral arms (8) of the visor, locking being effected by hand using a pivoting lever (8). For night missions, the day visor is removed and replaced with a night module mounted on the helmet using the same type of articulation.The invention applies in particular to helmets for aircraft pilots, allowing unprepared ejection.
problem: Enabling rapid, tool-free reconfiguration of modular components (e.g., visors) on a wearable device while maintaining secure mechanical and rotational coupling.
constraint: The articulation design must allow tool-free engagement while ensuring sufficient mechanical stability and rotational freedom for the visor's function.
mechanism: A translational engagement system with a guide rail and pivoting lever allows modular components to be slid into place and locked via a hand-operated lever, using shared articulation points for multiple modules.
mechanism_raw: A translational engagement system with a sagittal guide rail and pivoting lever allows modular components to be slid into place and locked via a hand-operated lever, using shared articulation points for both day and night modules.

abstract: An ultrasound transducer element incorporates material of low dielectric constant to confine the electric field of a stack of piezoelectric ceramic layers. Edge segments made of material having a low dielectric constant and extending in the thickness direction are formed at opposing ends of the multilayer structure. These regions of low dielectric constant material confine the electric field to the piezoelectric ceramic material of high dielectric constant, where it remains directed vertically. In this way, when a voltage is applied between the electrodes, the piezoelectrically induced strains are almost entirely vertical. Spurious modes are therefore substantially reduced.
problem: Confining an electric field to a specific region of a piezoelectric material to suppress unwanted vibrational modes in an ultrasound transducer.
constraint: The thickness and placement of the low-dielectric edge segments must precisely balance field confinement with minimal disruption to the overall transducer geometry.
mechanism: Edge segments of low-dielectric material are placed at opposing ends of a high-dielectric component, creating a dielectric contrast that confines an electric field within the component.
mechanism_raw: Edge segments of low-dielectric-constant material are placed at opposing ends of the piezoelectric stack, creating a dielectric contrast that confines the electric field vertically within the high-dielectric piezoelectric material.

abstract: A method of flexibly mounting a gas distribution plate to the back wall of a gas inlet manifold for a plasma chamber. A perforated gas distribution plate is suspended from the back wall by flexible side walls. The flexible suspension minimizes mechanical stress due to thermal expansion of the gas distribution plate.
problem: Mounting a rigid component (e.g., a gas distribution plate) in a high-temperature environment where differential thermal expansion would induce mechanical stress and failure.
constraint: The flexibility of the suspension must be sufficient to accommodate expected thermal expansion while maintaining positional accuracy and structural integrity under operational loads.
mechanism: Flexible suspension elements connect a rigid component to a fixed structure, allowing relative movement to absorb thermal expansion-induced strain while maintaining positional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Flexible side walls suspend the component from a fixed structure, allowing relative movement between the component and its mounting point to absorb thermal expansion-induced strain.

abstract: A plant for the drying and treatment of a pourable mineral material. The plant includes a combustion apparatus, introducing smoke gases into a rotary-driven rotary drum for cocurrently with the pourable mineral material. The rotary drum is inclined in the conveying direction, has installed fittings on the inner circumference and is connected sealingly at its outlet end to a shaft. The installed fittings in a front introduction region of the drum are transport blades. The shaft is put under a vacuum by means of a fan and is set up to take over the material and gas stream emerging from the rotary drum. A Venturi fitting is arranged coaxially in the rotary drum, upstream of the outlet, and a bypass for conveying air is arranged in the drum casing in the introduction region.
problem: Efficiently drying and treating pourable mineral material in a rotary drum while managing gas and material flow dynamics.
constraint: Balancing gas flow velocity and material transport to avoid clogging or uneven drying while maintaining structural integrity of the rotary drum under vacuum.
mechanism: Using a pressure differential and airflow regulation to enhance gas-material interaction and transport, combined with a bypass system to control flow in the introduction region, enabling controlled cocurrent movement of material and gases.
mechanism_raw: Using a Venturi fitting and vacuum-induced airflow to enhance gas-material interaction and transport, combined with a bypass system to regulate air flow in the introduction region, enabling controlled cocurrent movement of material and gases.

abstract: A mounting structure for connecting detachably a saw blade guard to a worktable of a bench saw includes a first connector at the worktable, a second connector at the saw blade guard, and a fastening member for fastening the second connector to the first connector. The first connector has a block member provided with a screw hole. The second connector has a connecting block provided with a through hole and a conical hole, and a cone fitted into the conical hole and having a through hole and a socket fitted onto the block member. The fastening member has a head stopped at one end of the connecting block, and a threaded shank inserted through the through hole of the connecting block and the through hole of the cone and threaded into the screw hole of the block member to lock the second connector to the first connector.
reason: The mechanism is a standard mechanical interlock (conical socket and threaded shank) for detachable connections, which is a basic engineering solution without a unique causal relationship or transferable functional principle beyond generic mechanical fastening.

abstract: A method and apparatus for manufacturing unitary concrete blocks includes a form that defines the desired shape of the unitary concrete block. A form loading station delivers a lightweight concrete composite into the form. A station conveyor conveys the form from the form loading station through a curing oven. In the curing oven, the composite-filled form is cured into a unitary concrete block. The station conveyor conveys the form to a block removal station that removes the unitary concrete block from the form. The station conveyor returns the form to the form loading station to manufacture more unitary concrete blocks. For increased production, multiple forms can be conveyed between stations simultaneously. Additionally, a metering ingredient assembly may be used to deliver appropriate amounts of desired ingredients to a mixer for producing the lightweight concrete composite.
problem: Increasing production efficiency in manufacturing unitary concrete blocks while maintaining consistent curing and form reuse.
constraint: Maintaining uniform curing conditions across all forms during concurrent processing while ensuring reliable form handling and return to the loading station.
mechanism: Implementing a continuous conveyor system that cycles units through processing stations, allowing multiple units to be processed simultaneously in parallel, thereby reducing cycle time and increasing throughput.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a continuous conveyor system that cycles forms through loading, curing, and removal stations, allowing multiple forms to be processed simultaneously in parallel, thereby reducing cycle time and increasing throughput.

abstract: A continuous form microstructure array device is constructed as a flexible elongate film laminate containing a plurality of microstructures or arrays of microstructures arranged serially lengthwise along the laminate. The laminate can be continuously drawn from a supply roll or stack, advanced within an analytic device and, when analysis is complete, taken up in a storage roll or stack. The device provides for high throughput microfluidic processing.
problem: Achieving high-throughput microfluidic processing while preserving the structural integrity of delicate microstructures.
constraint: Ensuring the flexible laminate maintains alignment and functionality of microstructures during continuous movement and storage without damage or misalignment.
mechanism: Using a flexible, roll-based medium containing serially arranged functional elements that can be continuously advanced through a processing device, enabling scalable and continuous processing without manual handling of individual units.
mechanism_raw: Using a flexible, roll-based laminate containing serially arranged microstructures that can be continuously advanced through an analytical device, enabling scalable and continuous processing without manual handling of individual units.

abstract: A gas delivering device inside a gaseous reaction chamber capable of increasing gas flow in areas having a deficient supply of gas by forming additional holes in corresponding positions. Because a gas-delivering panel design having asymmetrical holes is employed, gas flow rate within the reactions chamber can be roughly balanced. Hence, a homogeneous stream of gaseous reactants can be maintained above the surface of a reacting wafer.
problem: Maintaining a homogeneous stream of gaseous reactants over a reacting wafer surface in a reaction chamber with uneven gas distribution.
constraint: Achieving uniform gas distribution without complex active control systems, relying instead on passive hole geometry to self-regulate flow rates.
mechanism: Employing a gas-delivering panel with asymmetrical aperture placement to dynamically balance flow rates across different regions of the chamber, compensating for spatial deficiencies in gas supply through passive flow regulation.
mechanism_raw: Employing a gas-delivering panel with asymmetrical hole placement to dynamically balance gas flow rates across different regions of the chamber, compensating for spatial deficiencies in gas supply.

abstract: A reversing automatic feed wheel assembly for wood chipper includes an infeed assembly and a rotatable cutting assembly spaced from the infeed assembly. The reversing automatic feed wheel assembly also includes at least one feed wheel disposed between the infeed assembly and the cutting assembly to feed wood material to the cutting assembly. The reversing automatic feed wheel assembly further includes a control system operatively connected to the at least one feed wheel to automatically reverse/stop/restart the infeed of the wood material in response to a reduced speed or excessive load placed on the cutting assembly.
problem: Wood chipper feed systems risk overloading the cutting assembly when material jams or slows, requiring automatic adjustment to maintain safe operation.
constraint: The system must respond quickly enough to prevent damage to the cutting assembly while avoiding unnecessary interruptions during normal operation.
mechanism: A control system monitors operational parameters of a processing element and dynamically adjusts material input mechanisms in response to detected deviations, creating a feedback loop that balances throughput with capacity constraints to prevent overload conditions.
mechanism_raw: A control system monitors load/speed on the cutting assembly and automatically reverses, stops, or restarts the feed wheel in response to detected anomalies, creating a feedback loop that dynamically balances material flow with cutting capacity.
residual_terms: ["operational parameters", "processing element", "material input mechanisms", "feedback loop", "throughput", "capacity constraints"]

abstract: The present invention comprises a series of embodiments of a swivel cheeked bridle bit wherein the cheek portion, comprising a dee and/or lower or curb rein attachment eye or ring, is separate from the purchase, with the purchase serving as a pintle for the swivel attachment of the cheek portion to the remainder of the bit structure. The upper harness attachment ring, for attaching a curb chain, nose strap, and/or cheek strap to the bit, is immovably affixed to the upper end of the purchase, which in turn is immovably affixed to the mouth bar of the bit. This ensures that the upper ring does not rotate or swivel as the cheek is turned, thus avoiding twisting the ends of the straps attached to the upper ring and precluding turning the edge of the attachment ring and any attached straps into the side of the face of the animal.
problem: Traditional bridle bits with fixed cheek attachments cause twisting of straps and discomfort to animals due to rotational forces transmitted through the bit structure.
constraint: The swivel must allow sufficient rotational freedom for the cheek while maintaining structural integrity and precise control over the bit's positioning.
mechanism: A rotational decoupling interface connects two components such that one component can rotate independently relative to the other while maintaining structural continuity, preventing torque transmission between connected elements.
mechanism_raw: Decoupling the cheek portion from the purchase via a swivel joint allows independent rotation of the cheek while keeping the upper harness attachment ring fixed, preventing torque transmission to straps and facial contact points.

abstract: A low-power illumination apparatus may be used in areas where conventional incandescent illumination would be unsafe, especially to children or small pets. The apparatus may be configured to appear as a window candle and can be safely installed in windows which are easily accessible to children. Safe application is accomplished by supplying a low-wattage bulb with a low voltage, providing a resettably-fused bulb supply within the apparatus to prohibit the use of high-wattage bulbs and an interlocking base attached to the window frame which prevents the apparatus from being inadvertently removed or tipped over.
problem: Conventional illumination devices pose safety risks in environments accessible to children or pets due to high temperatures, voltage, or instability.
constraint: Each safety mechanism must function without compromising the device's usability or requiring complex maintenance, while collectively addressing multiple failure modes.
mechanism: Multiple independent safety subsystems are integrated into a single device, each addressing distinct failure modes through separate mitigation pathways, creating redundant barriers that collectively reduce risk without compromising core functionality.
mechanism_raw: Combining low-voltage power, a resettable fuse to block high-wattage bulbs, and an interlocking base that prevents tipping creates layered safety barriers that independently mitigate thermal, electrical, and mechanical hazards.

abstract: A track guard for a sectional overhead door assembly comprises an elongate member which may be positioned between the vertical track sections of the door assembly and a wall jamb to which the vertical track sections are mounted to cover the space therebetween. The track guard has a generally C-shaped cross-section and has a width which tapers from a first end to a second end to accommodate variations in spacing between the vertical track sections and the wall jamb.
problem: Sectional overhead door tracks leave variable gaps between the vertical track and wall jamb, creating aesthetic and safety issues.
constraint: The taper must balance flexibility for variable spacing with sufficient rigidity to remain securely in place under dynamic door movement.
mechanism: A flexible, tapered structural element adapts to variable spacing between two surfaces by compressing or expanding along its length, maintaining continuous coverage while accommodating dimensional tolerances.
mechanism_raw: A tapered C-shaped member adapts to varying gap widths by compressing or expanding along its length, maintaining consistent coverage while accommodating installation tolerances.

abstract: A guard member for a fluid actuated rod and cylinder assembly of a machine having front end assembly including a dipper stick, a working implement pivotally connected to the dipper stick, an arm member pivotally connected to the dipper stick and cooperable with the implement to grapple articles therebetween and such rod and cylinder assembly for angularly displacing the arm member relative to the dipper stick, generally consisting of an elongated article mountable on the free end of the rod member and projecting along the length thereof when mounted thereon.
problem: Rod and cylinder assemblies in heavy machinery are vulnerable to damage from debris, impact, or environmental exposure during operation.
constraint: The guard must be lightweight and durable enough to withstand operational stresses without interfering with the cylinder's mechanical function or adding excessive bulk.
mechanism: An elongated protective sheath is mounted to the free end of a reciprocating rod, extending along its length to shield it from external forces while permitting unimpeded axial movement during operation.
mechanism_raw: An elongated guard mounted on the rod's free end projects along its length, shielding the rod from external forces while allowing unimpeded extension/retraction.

abstract: The present invention provides methods for producing arrays having associated modified nucleic acid structures, e.g. acid stable and/or end-blocked nucleic acids such as 2′-O—R oligonucleotides. In one embodiment, arrays produced using the methods of the invention exhibit an increased binding affinity with complementary nucleic acids, and in particular with complementary RNA. In another embodiment, the associated nucleic acids of the array produced using the methods of the invention exhibit substantial acid resistance, allowing the arrays to be treated with low pH solutions. In another embodiment, the modified associated nucleic acids of the array produced using the methods of the invention exhibit substantial resistance to nuclease degradation.
problem: Creating nucleic acid arrays that remain functional under harsh conditions (low pH, nuclease degradation) while maintaining binding affinity.
constraint: Balancing structural stability (acid/nuclease resistance) with retention of binding affinity for complementary nucleic acids.
mechanism: Modify molecular structures through chemical substitution to enhance resistance to environmental stressors (e.g., pH, enzymatic degradation) while preserving functional interaction with complementary molecular targets.
mechanism_raw: Chemical modification of nucleic acids (e.g., 2'-O-R groups) to stabilize their structure, increasing acid resistance and nuclease resistance without compromising hybridization efficiency.

abstract: A gyroscope which comprises: a driving fixed electrode (26) being fixed; a driving displacement electrode (24) being opposite to the driving fixed electrode, and being able to be displaced in a first direction; an inertial mass (23) being connected to the driving displacement electrode (24), being displaced in the first direction according to the first directional displacement of the driving displacement electrode (24), and being displaced in a second direction when an angular rate is applied; a sensing displacement electrode (22) being connected to the inertial mass (23), and being able to be displaced in the second direction according to the second directional displacement of the inertial mass (23); and a sensing fixed electrode (25) being opposite to the sensing displacement electrode and being fixed. The driving displacement electrode (24) is supported by a folded spring (31) movable in the first direction, and the sensing displacement electrode is supported by a folded spring (32) movable in the second direction.
problem: Accurately measuring angular rate in a gyroscope using mechanical displacement.
constraint: Mechanical design must enable precise, independent movement in two axes without cross-interference between displacement directions.
mechanism: Translate rotational motion into measurable linear displacements in two perpendicular directions using a compliant mechanical system that decouples movement along each axis to prevent cross-interference.
mechanism_raw: Orthogonal displacement sensing via folded springs supporting driving and sensing electrodes, translating angular motion into measurable electrostatic displacement in two perpendicular directions.

abstract: The present invention is a method of making a lithography photomask and photomask blank. The method of making the lithography photomask and photomask blank includes providing a silicon oxyfluoride glass tube having an OH content less than 50 ppm. The method further includes cutting the silicon oxyfluoride glass tube, flattening the silicon oxyfluoride glass tube, and forming the flattened cut silicon oxyfluoride glass tube into a photomask blank having a planar surface. The present invention includes a glass lithography mask preform. The glass lithography mask preform is a longitudinal silicon oxyfluoride glass tube that has an OH content ≦10 ppm, a F wt. % concentration ≧0.5 wt. %.
reason: The method is highly specific to material composition (silicon oxyfluoride glass with controlled OH/F levels) and processing steps for photomask blanks, lacking a generalizable causal mechanism applicable to other fields.

abstract: The invention concerns in one aspect, a ferrohydrostatic separation method in which a ferrofluid is used to separate materials of different density. In the method, the apparent density of the ferrofluid is controlled by means of a vertically orientated magnetic field generated by a C-dipole, open dipole (O-dipole) or split pair electromagnet or permanent magnet. Other aspects of the invention include an apparatus for use in this method and a process for separating materials of different density using the method.
problem: Separating materials of different densities using a controllable medium.
constraint: Magnetic field strength and orientation must be precisely controlled to tune the ferrofluid's density without destabilizing the separation process.
mechanism: Adjust the effective density of a responsive medium via an external field to enable density-based separation of suspended materials, where field strength and orientation control the medium's properties without destabilizing the process.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting the apparent density of a ferrofluid via a vertically oriented magnetic field, enabling density-based separation of materials suspended in the fluid.

abstract: A method and apparatus for ultrasonic assisted deposition of a release agent onto a workpiece is disclosed. The release agent can be any fluorinated or non-fluorinated phosphorous-containing organic acid. The workpiece can be any workpiece desired to be coated with the release agent, such as a surface needing an anti-stick coating required in a plastic casting or injection mold. Metal oxide workpiece surfaces strongly bond to fluorinated phosphorus-containing organic acids. In particular, the present invention can deposit anti-stick coatings onto smooth or porous surfaces, such as anodized aluminum and its alloys, using ultrasonic assisted deposition.
problem: Depositing anti-stick coatings on surfaces (e.g., metal oxides) with strong bonding requirements.
constraint: Ultrasonic parameters (frequency, amplitude) must be optimized to ensure effective coating without damaging the workpiece or causing uneven deposition.
mechanism: Apply mechanical agitation energy to promote adhesion of coating materials onto substrates by enhancing surface interaction and material distribution, with parameters optimized to avoid substrate damage and ensure uniform deposition.
mechanism_raw: Using ultrasonic energy to enhance deposition of phosphorus-containing release agents, promoting adhesion on smooth or porous substrates through mechanical agitation and surface interaction.

abstract: Disclosed is a method and solvent composition capable of removing iron oxide deposits from the surface of titanium components without substantially damaging the underlying titanium component. Iron oxide deposits may be removed from the surface of a titanium component by contacting the titanium component with the solvent composition of the invention. The solvent composition may then be removed from contact with the titanium component to obtain a recyclable solvent composition which is recycled into repeated contact with the titanium component. The solvent composition comprises an aqueous mixture of an organic acid and a hydrohalide acid.
problem: Removing iron oxide deposits from titanium surfaces without damaging the underlying titanium component.
constraint: The solvent must be aggressive enough to dissolve iron oxide deposits but not so aggressive that it attacks the titanium substrate; the ratio of organic acid to hydrohalide acid determines the selectivity window, and the solvent must remain stable and reusable across multiple cleaning cycles.
mechanism: A chemical agent with tunable reactivity selectively dissolves a surface deposit while preserving the underlying substrate's protective layer, with the agent being recovered and reused across multiple cycles to maintain operational efficiency and material integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using a solvent composition with tuned chemical aggressiveness (aqueous mixture of an organic acid and a hydrohalide acid) that selectively dissolves iron oxide while leaving titanium's passive oxide layer intact, with the solvent being recovered and recycled for repeated use.

abstract: The septic tank of the subject invention can be provided in kit form, and preferably comprises a tank lid, a tank bottom, a pair of opposing side walls, and a pair of opposing end walls having a tank flow outlet and a tank flow inlet, where a flange is affixed within the tank flow outlet and the tank flow inlet. The tank lid comprises a pair of lid openings, which are covered by hatch covers. The hatch covers comprise a hatch handle for ease of removal and are removable affixed to the tank lid with angle connection brackets. The septic tank is assembled using angle connection brackets, where the brackets are affixed to the tank lid, tank bottom, side walls, and end walls using, for example, stainless steel cap screws. A silicone sealant is interposed between the tank lid, tank bottom, side walls, end walls and the connection brackets, forming a substantially leak proof seal.
reason: This patent describes a kit-form septic tank assembled using standard mechanical techniques (angle brackets, screws, silicone sealant). It is a product design listing components and assembly steps rather than a novel causal mechanism for solving a problem.

abstract: An oven construction wherein the oven wall forms an oven cavity containing in a lower portion thereof a HTA producing device, wherein a steam generator is provided in the cavity in physically isolated relationship to the device, wherein the steam generator contains a plurality of metal balls which act as a heat sink, and wherein a water reservoir is provided on the outside of the oven and is in water flow communication with the steam generator thru a water feed line.
reason: This patent describes a specific oven configuration placing components (steam generator, heat sink balls, external reservoir) in particular locations. It is a product layout description rather than a generalizable causal mechanism that creates a useful effect through functional relationships.

abstract: A low-solids gas generating composition, which is a mixture of a fuel selected for the group consisting of cellulose, cellulose acetate, hexamine, and mixtures thereof, and an oxidizer selected from the group consisting of ceric ammonium nitrate, lithium nitrate, lithium perchlorate, sodium perchlorate, phase stabilized ammonium nitrate, a combination of ammonium nitrate with potassium nitrate, potassium perchlorate, or mixtures thereof, such that the combination is a solid solution, a mixture of ammonium perchlorate and at least one alkali metal salt, and mixtures thereof.
