The combination of ammonium nitrate with other salts in solid solution is intended to phase stabilize the ammonium nitrate. The oxidizer-fuel mixture is within about 4 percent of stoichiometric balance. Useful alkali metal salts include lithium carbonate, lithium nitrate, sodium nitrate, potassium nitrate, and mixtures thereof. The preferred oxidizers for the gas generating composition of the invention are ceric ammonium nitrate, lithium nitrate, lithium perchlorate, sodium perchlorate, a mixture of ammonium perchlorate and at least one alkali metal salt, and mixtures thereof. In addition, the gas generating composition may include an energizing agent, such as RDX or HMX. The gas generating composition of the invention may further comprise sub-micron fumed silica to reduce moisture contamination and serve as a processing and powder flow aid and/or a binder, and may be in the form of pressed pellets, grains, or granules.
problem: Creating a gas generating composition that produces minimal solid residue (low-solids) for safe and clean operation in gas-generating devices.
constraint: The fuel-oxidizer combination must be within about 4% of stoichiometric balance for clean burning; phase stabilization is required to prevent ammonium nitrate from undergoing destabilizing phase changes; and moisture contamination must be controlled (e.g., via sub-micron fumed silica) to maintain composition integrity and powder flow properties.
mechanism: A solid-phase mixture of fuel and oxidizer is formulated at the molecular level to ensure intimate mixing for complete combustion, combined with phase stabilization of a key component to prevent destabilizing transitions, and near-stoichiometric balance (within 4%) to minimize unburned solids.
mechanism_raw: Formulating a solid solution of fuel and oxidizer at the molecular level (rather than a physical mixture) to ensure intimate mixing for more complete combustion, combined with phase stabilization of ammonium nitrate to prevent unwanted phase transitions, and maintaining near-stoichiometric balance (within 4%) so that reactants are fully consumed with minimal unburned solids.

abstract: According to the method, a reactor core is shut down during the operation cycle. One or more fuel bundles of the reactor core are then moved to new positions within the reactor core to increase a total energy, output of the reactor core as compared to continuing operation of the reactor core without the shutting down and moving steps.
problem: Increasing the total energy output of a reactor core over an operating cycle beyond what is achievable through continuous operation without interruption.
constraint: The reactor must be shut down for the repositioning operation, incurring a temporary loss of power generation; the new fuel bundle positions must be carefully chosen to maximize energy extraction while maintaining safe reactor physics and thermal limits.
mechanism: Periodically interrupting operation to reconfigure the spatial arrangement of energy-generating units within a core, optimizing neutron flux distribution and burn patterns to extract more total energy from the same inventory than continuous operation allows.
mechanism_raw: Periodically shutting down the reactor core during an operating cycle, repositioning fuel bundles to new locations within the core to optimize the neutron flux distribution and burn pattern, and then resuming operation, thereby extracting more total energy from the same fuel inventory than would be possible through uninterrupted operation.

abstract: A twin float aircraft (1) which has a retractable float (4 and 5) for each side of a fuselage (3) providing buoyancy for the aircraft during take off and landing and reduced air resistance during flight with each of the floats (4 and 5) being articulated (12 and 13) to assist streamline alignment when retracted.
problem: Balancing buoyancy during takeoff/landing with reduced air resistance during flight in a twin-float aircraft.
constraint: Mechanical articulation must allow seamless transition between buoyancy mode and streamlined flight mode without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A reconfigurable structural system that transitions between a buoyancy-preserving configuration and an aerodynamically optimized configuration through articulated elements, maintaining structural integrity during mode shifts.
mechanism_raw: Articulated floats that adjust their orientation when retracted to align with the fuselage, dynamically optimizing aerodynamic profile while maintaining structural buoyancy.

abstract: A printhead cartridge for use with an ink jet printer is disclosed. The printhead cartridge includes a memory element for storing jet characteristics of the cartridge. These characteristics can be measured during fabrication, upon installation into the printer, or during the operation of the printer. The printer adjusts printing parameters to compensate for the out of specification characteristics for optimized image quality. The compensation is done through adjusting drop ejection energy, thermal control, or replacing failed jets with substitute jets in the printhead. Alternatively, the printer accesses the measured characteristics to determine if they are within specification. If the printhead cartridge does not meet specifications, the user is instructed to remove the printhead cartridge since its use may adversely affect the quality of the resulting image. The printer accesses the measured characteristics throughout the life of the cartridge to ensure the quality of the resulting image does not degrade.
problem: Maintaining consistent image quality in inkjet printers despite variations in printhead jet performance over time or across manufacturing tolerances.
constraint: Adjustments must occur dynamically during operation without interrupting printing, while ensuring stored data remains accurate and actionable.
mechanism: A dynamic feedback loop that stores operational performance data in a memory element and adjusts actuation parameters in real-time to compensate for variability, ensuring consistent output quality without interrupting operation.
mechanism_raw: Storing measured jet characteristics in a memory element and using real-time feedback to adjust drop ejection energy, thermal control, or substitute failed jets, creating an adaptive compensation loop.
residual_terms: ["memory element", "adaptive compensation loop", "jet characteristics", "drop ejection energy"]

abstract: This invention provides a conveyor and tunnel oven, where the conveyor is continuous, the tunnel oven is gas fired, having its ignited and heated gases passed through a tubular system, being attracted by one or more blowers, to generate by conduction infrared energy to furnish curing to products passing along the continuous conveyor. A control system is provided for controlling the operating parameters such as conveyor speed, regulating emitted gas, the velocity generated by the blowers, and the capacity of the BTUs created, during operations of the oven.
problem: Optimizing curing quality for products on a continuous conveyor in a gas-fired tunnel oven while maintaining throughput.
constraint: Balancing real-time parameter adjustments to avoid thermal lag or uneven curing while sustaining continuous product flow.
mechanism: A multi-variable control system that dynamically coordinates interdependent parameters to maintain consistent thermal distribution and process conditions while sustaining continuous material flow.
mechanism_raw: A control system that dynamically coordinates multiple interdependent parameters (conveyor speed, gas regulation, blower velocity, BTU output) to maintain consistent heat distribution and curing conditions.

abstract: Shoe lacing kits, laced shoes, and methods of lacing shoes. First and second lacing elements are used to create lacing loops on the exterior of the shoe body. An end of each lacing element is anchored to the shoe body. The loops are threaded through a clasp. Pulling the loops in different directions draws the clasp toward the shoe, and tightens the lacing elements on the shoe. When the tightening force is released, one or more gripping elements in the clasp grip the lacing elements and hold the lacing elements in the tightened position. Releasing the gripping elements on the clasp releases the lacing elements from the tightened position such that the lacing elements can be loosened on the shoe.
problem: Creating a secure, adjustable lacing system that maintains tension without requiring constant manual readjustment.
constraint: Gripping force must be sufficient to hold tension under load but releasable without tools, while minimizing wear on lacing elements.
mechanism: A self-locking mechanism that automatically secures flexible tensioning elements under applied force, maintaining grip without continuous manual adjustment, while allowing intentional manual release.
mechanism_raw: A clasp with gripping elements that automatically lock lacing elements in place when tightening force is applied, releasing only when intentionally disengaged.

abstract: Biomaterials are disclosed comprised of biodegradable, biocompatible, and bioabsorbable non-woven fabric materials for use in surgery for the guided regeneration of tissues. The non-woven fabric materials are comprised of threads embedded in a matrix, wherein both the matrix and the threads can be comprised of esters of hyaluronic acid, used singly or in combination, or esters of hyaluronic acid in combination with esters of alginic acid or other polymers.
problem: Providing a temporary structural scaffold for tissue regeneration that supports cell growth while gradually degrading in the body.
constraint: Material degradation rate must align with tissue growth speed, while maintaining structural integrity long enough to guide regeneration.
mechanism: A degradable scaffold structure composed of multiple components with controlled degradation rates, maintaining temporary structural support while aligning material breakdown with biological regeneration timelines.
mechanism_raw: A non-woven fabric matrix with embedded threads, where both matrix and threads are composed of bioabsorbable materials that degrade at controlled rates to match tissue regeneration timelines.

abstract: The invention is a safety fingertip toothbrush for use by persons not desiring a full length toothbrush for space conservation reasons, but still desiring their regular oral hygiene practice using a toothbrush. The safety fingertip toothbrush is also a practical solution to safety hazards presented in penal institutions, where conventional toothbrushes with hard handles can pose a risk of being converted to lethal assault weapons. The safety fingertip toothbrush has no handle, but it includes a plurality of bristles embedded in a brush head, the brush head having a depression in one end to accept the fingertip of a finger and an elastic band connected to a thumb ring within which the thumb is placed, allowing for the user to brush their teeth and other mouth tissue using the fingers as the brush handle.
problem: Need for a compact, safe toothbrush that avoids weaponization risks in constrained environments while maintaining oral hygiene functionality.
constraint: Balancing space conservation (no handle) with sufficient grip stability and safety to prevent misuse as a weapon.
mechanism: Replace a fixed rigid handle with a user's fingers as the primary grip interface, incorporating a brush head with a contoured surface and an elastic retention element to enable controlled manipulation through direct finger contact.
mechanism_raw: Replacing a rigid handle with a finger-based grip system: a brush head with a fingertip depression and an elastic thumb ring allows the user's fingers to act as the handle, eliminating the need for a fixed handle while enabling controlled brushing.

abstract: A method of and an apparatus for compressing the grinding sludge, which is effective to compress the grinding sludge to provide an intended rigid briquette even though the grinding sludge contains ground chips of hardened iron and/or steel materials and an oil-based coolant and also to facilitate reuse of the briquette (B1) as material for production of steel. The grinding sludge containing the oil-based coolant and hardened component parts such as steel component parts that are used in bearings is compressed. To this end, the grinding sludge produced from a grinding line (1) is filtered by a filtering unit (4) to provide a concentrated sludge which is subsequently compressed by squeezing by a briquetting machine (5) to provide the briquette (B1). The briquette B1 so obtained can be reused as steel material. The coolant separated from the grinding sludge during filtering and squeezing is returned to the grinding line (1) through recovery passages (7, 8).
problem: Recycling grinding sludge containing hardened metal chips and oil-based coolant into reusable steel material while recovering the coolant.
constraint: Achieving sufficient compression to bind hardened, oil-contaminated chips into a structurally sound briquette without compromising coolant recovery efficiency.
mechanism: Apply sequential concentration of particulate-laden fluid followed by high-pressure consolidation to form a rigid solid mass, with simultaneous separation of a recoverable fluid phase during both stages to enable reuse in the originating process.
mechanism_raw: Sequential filtering to concentrate sludge followed by high-pressure compression to form rigid briquettes, with coolant separation during both stages enabling reuse in the grinding process.

abstract: A bayonet locking system for vending machines is provided to lock and unlock the machine preferably with a remotely controlled electronic operating unit. It includes at least one motor driven axially and rotationally movable bayonet with an enlarged shaped head being mounted preferably on a gasketed door and at least one receptacle receiving device disposed within the machine interior positioned for engagement by the bayonet when the door is moved to an intermediate position. The bayonet advances into the receptacle and rotates to capture it in the receptacle and then axially retracts to pull the door into the closed position wherein a gasket disposed between the door and the machine is substantially uniformly compressed and sealed around its periphery. An axially rotatable pin with fins may be used with a bracket on either the door or machine to prevent prying of the door at opposite corners.
problem: Securely locking and sealing a vending machine door remotely while preventing tampering or prying.
constraint: Coordinating axial and rotational movements to ensure uniform gasket compression and tamper resistance without manual intervention.
mechanism: Coordinate axial and rotational movements via a motorized drive to engage a receptacle and compress a sealing element, with mechanical interlocks preventing external leverage-based tampering during the locking sequence.
mechanism_raw: Motor-driven bayonet motion combining axial advancement, rotational capture of an internal receptacle, and axial retraction to pull the door into a sealed position, with anti-pry fins preventing corner leverage.

abstract: A cement producing system includes a rotary kiln, a riser duct having lower portion communicably connected to the rotary kiln to pass process materials thereto, and a down draft calciner having a lower portion communicably connected to the lower portion of the riser duct. A tertiary duct is communicably connected to an upper portion of the down draft calciner to receive heated tertiary gas therefrom and a suspension burner is operably disposed in the down draft calciner in a manner to permit receipt of combustible waste and suspension of the waste therein for combustion thereof. A method of producing cement using the burner in the down draft calciner is also provided.
problem: Efficiently producing cement while utilizing combustible waste as an energy source in the process.
constraint: Maintaining optimal temperature gradients and material flow across interconnected kiln, riser, and calciner zones to ensure complete combustion and heat recovery.
mechanism: Integrate in-flight combustion of combustible materials within a downward-flow processing zone, routing heated gas through a duct to preheat feedstock in interconnected upstream and downstream zones, ensuring thermal energy recovery across the system.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a suspension burner within a down draft calciner to combust waste materials in-flight, with heated tertiary gas routed through a duct to preheat process materials in the riser and kiln.
residual_terms: ["in-flight combustion", "downward-flow processing zone", "heated gas", "upstream and downstream zones"]

abstract: A novel method for preparing fine particles comprising a transition metal and a noble metal which are monodispersed and have almost no particle diameter distribution, and are transferable to a CuAu-I type L10 ordered phase, with safety and at a low cost, wherein a salt or a complex of at least one transition metal selected from Fe and Co and a salt or a complex of at least one transition metal selected from Pt and Pd (exclusive of the combination of Co—Pd) is dissolved in an organic solvent miscible with water or an alcohol in the presence of an organic protecting agent, and the resultant solution is heated under reflux in the presence of an alcohol in an inert atmosphere, to thereby prepare a binary alloy comprising a transition metal and a noble metal, or a salt or a complex of at least one element selected from the group consisting of Cu, Bi, Sb, Sn, Pb and Ag is further dissolved in the above solvent and the resultant solution is heated under reflux in the presence of an alcohol in an inert atmosphere, to thereby prepare a ternary alloy comprising a transition metal, a noble metal and an additional element.
problem: Synthesizing monodispersed alloy nanoparticles with controlled phase ordering (e.g., CuAu-I L10) safely and cost-effectively.
constraint: Balancing solvent miscibility, reflux temperature, and inert atmosphere conditions to prevent oxidation and achieve narrow particle size distribution without hazardous reagents.
mechanism: Dissolve precursor materials in a solvent with a stabilizing agent, then apply controlled thermal energy under an inert environment to induce uniform nucleation and growth of alloy particles with ordered phase structures.
mechanism_raw: Dissolving metal salts/complexes in an organic solvent with a protecting agent, then heating under reflux in an inert atmosphere to enable controlled nucleation and growth of uniform alloy particles.

abstract: The present invention provides a double end yarn drive pattern attachment for tufting machines characterized by independent servo-motor control of yarn feed rolls capable of increased torque to carry multiple yarn ends on a single feed roll, thereby economically retaining many advantages of a single end pattern attachment. The improved attachment utilizes an intermediate gear to provide a relatively high torque drive adaptable between single and plural yarn pattern attachments.
problem: Efficiently managing multiple yarn ends in tufting machines while retaining the advantages of single-end pattern attachments.
constraint: Balancing torque capacity and control precision across variable numbers of yarn ends without sacrificing operational flexibility.
mechanism: Independent actuation of feed mechanisms with a torque amplification system that adjusts between single and multiple configurations to balance torque capacity and control precision while maintaining operational flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Independent servo-motor control of yarn feed rolls with increased torque via an intermediate gear system, enabling adaptable high-torque drive between single and plural yarn configurations.

abstract: An improved and novel method of selectively aligning and positioning nanometer-scale components using AC fields. The method provides for more precise manipulation of the nanometer-scale components in bridging test electrodes including the steps of: providing an alternating current (AC) field at a single electrode or between a plurality of electrodes to create an electric field in an environment containing nanometer-scale components. The electric field thereby providing for the aligning and positioning of the nanometer-scale components to the desired location.
problem: Precisely aligning and positioning nanometer-scale components in environments with limited physical manipulation access.
constraint: Achieving sub-micron precision while avoiding physical contact or thermal damage to delicate components.
mechanism: Applying an electric field to generate non-contact forces that align and position components at sub-micron scales without physical contact or thermal damage.
mechanism_raw: Applying an AC electric field between electrodes to generate dielectrophoretic forces that align and position components to desired locations.

abstract: A shoulder pad accessory arm pad, to protect the upper arm of a wearer from injury. The arm pad includes a tapered padded member which attaches to the shoulder pad and arm of the wearer. The arm pad remains in place during athletic activity, and does not limit the effective range of motion of the upper arm of the wearer.
reason: The patent describes a specific product design (a padded arm protector) with no underlying causal mechanism that generalizes beyond its immediate physical form and application.

abstract: A modular roller skating apparatus includes a frame having a pair of interchangeable frame portions. A plurality of wheel assemblies is axially mounted to the frame in an in-line configuration, each assembly having a pair of releasably coupled hub portions. When coupled, the hub defines a female receptacle for detachably coupling to a corresponding male structure of a tire such that worn tires may be conveniently replaced without replacing an entire wheel assembly. A boot having a lower portion for receiving a skater's foot is releasably mounted atop the frame and includes conventional lacing. An upper boot portion is provided for surrounding a skater's ankle. Laterally spaced eyelets along respective edges of upper and lower portions enable another lace to adjustably connect the boot portions and, more particularly, to provide enhanced support to a skater's ankle and leg.
problem: Enabling modular replacement and adjustment of components in roller skating equipment without compromising structural integrity or performance.
constraint: Maintaining load-bearing stability and user comfort while enabling rapid, tool-free interchangeability of parts.
mechanism: Releasable mechanical connections between structural components combined with adjustable tensioning systems enabling tool-free part replacement and customization while maintaining load-bearing stability.
mechanism_raw: Releasable mechanical couplings between hub portions and frame sections, combined with adjustable lacing systems, allowing independent replacement and customization of wear components.

abstract: The use of certain siloxane and silane materials for the conservation of organic and inorganic materials. More specifically, this invention deals with a method of impregnating organic and inorganic materials with siloxanes and silanes and ultimately curing such materials to provide preservation properties to such materials. An especially significant use of the method is to preserve and conserve ancient artifacts. The curable materials are represented by silanol containing polymers crosslinked with trialkoxysilanes.
problem: Preserving organic and inorganic materials, particularly ancient artifacts, from degradation over time.
constraint: Ensuring chemical compatibility and long-term stability of the cured material without altering the appearance or structural properties of the preserved object.
mechanism: Impregnating materials with curable polymers that crosslink to form a protective, stabilizing matrix within the substrate, preserving structural and visual properties without chemical incompatibility.
mechanism_raw: Impregnating materials with curable siloxane/silane polymers that crosslink via silanol groups and trialkoxysilane agents to form a protective, stabilizing matrix within the substrate.

abstract: A dry-etching method comprises the step of dry-etching a metal thin film as a chromium-containing film, wherein the method is characterized by using, as an etching gas, a mixed gas including (a) a reactive ion etching gas, which contains an oxygen-containing gas and a halogen-containing gas, and (b) a reducing gas added to the gas component (a), in the process for dry-etching the metal thin film. The dry-etching method permits the production of a photomask by forming patterns to be transferred to a wafer on a photomask blank. The photomask can in turn be used for manufacturing semiconductor circuits. The method permits the decrease of the dimensional difference due to the coexistence of coarse and dense patterns in a plane and the production of a high precision pattern-etched product.
problem: Achieving high-precision patterns in dry-etching without dimensional differences between coarse and dense features on a photomask.
constraint: Maintaining etch uniformity while preventing over-etching or under-etching in regions with differing pattern densities, requiring precise control of gas ratios and plasma chemistry.
mechanism: Introducing a reactive species into a processing environment to modulate reaction dynamics, balancing material removal rates across regions with differing feature densities by controlling reactive species concentrations and suppressing unwanted side reactions.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a reducing gas into the etching plasma to modulate chemical reactions, balancing etch rates across varying pattern densities by controlling reactive species concentrations and suppressing unwanted side reactions.
residual_terms: ["reactive species", "processing environment", "reaction dynamics", "material removal rates", "feature densities", "reactive species concentrations", "side reactions"]

abstract: A press has a die unit, a feed mechanism and a table unit. The feed mechanism feeds a sheet of material to the die unit. The die unit has a punch and a die for punching first and second holes in the sheet. The punching axis of the punch is inclined at an acute angle with respect to the sheet. The table unit supports the die unit and rotates the die unit with respect to the sheet to direct the punching axis in different directions to form the first and second holes in different directions.
problem: Forming holes in multiple directions in a sheet material without repositioning the material or using multiple punches.
constraint: Ensuring the punch maintains an acute angle relative to the sheet during rotation while preserving structural integrity and alignment accuracy.
mechanism: Mechanically rotating a tool assembly with an angled working element relative to a stationary workpiece, redirecting the working element's orientation to create openings in different angular directions through controlled rotational motion while maintaining alignment.
mechanism_raw: Mechanically rotating the die unit (with an inclined punch axis) relative to the stationary sheet, redirecting the punch's orientation to create holes in different angular directions through controlled rotational motion.

abstract: A method of coating an oblong shaped body (8) made of polymer material, which is intended for guiding light in the form of optical signals. In this case, a coating made of polymer material having a lower index of refraction than the shaped body (8) is applied around the shaped body (8). To generate the coating, a coating facility (A) having at least one chamber (1) is used, to which a halogenated gas (4) and/or gas mixture is supplied. The halogenated gas (4) and/or gas mixture is converted into a plasma (6) in the chamber (1) under the effect of microwaves (5) and conducted out of the chamber (1) through a nozzle (7). The shaped body (8) is moved at least one time over its entire length along the coating facility (A) in the region of the nozzle (7) and/or the plasma (6) emitting therefrom and, at the same time, provided with a coating (9) made of a halogenated polymer, which is generated by the incidence of the plasma (6).
problem: Applying a uniform polymer coating with a lower refractive index around an elongated, oblong-shaped optical waveguide.
constraint: Balancing plasma uniformity, movement speed, and gas composition to ensure consistent coating thickness and refractive index across the entire length of the body.
mechanism: Moving a shaped substrate along the length of an energy-emitting source while the energy source induces material deposition, enabling continuous coating through synchronized motion and energy exposure to achieve uniform thickness and properties.
mechanism_raw: Moving the shaped body along the length of a plasma-emitting nozzle while the plasma polymerizes halogenated gas, enabling continuous coating through synchronized motion and plasma exposure.
residual_terms: ["shaped substrate", "energy-emitting source", "material deposition", "synchronized motion", "energy exposure", "uniform thickness"]

abstract: A method of fabricating an infrared detector, a method of controlling the stress in a polycrystalline SiGE layer and an infrared detector device is disclosed. The method of fabricating includes the steps of forming a sacrificial layer on a substrate; patterning said sacrificial layer; establishing a layer consisting essentially of polycrystalline SiGe on said sacrificial layer; depositing an infrared absorber on said polycrystalline SiGe layer; and thereafter removing the sacrificial layer. The method of controlling the stress in a polycrystalline SiGe layer deposited on a substrate is based on varying the deposition pressure. The infrared detector device comprises an active area and an infrared absorber, wherein the active area comprises a polycrystalline SiGe layer, and is suspended above a substrate.
problem: Controlling internal stress in a polycrystalline SiGe layer during infrared detector fabrication to maintain structural and functional integrity.
constraint: Optimizing pressure to minimize stress without compromising layer adhesion, thickness uniformity, or the mechanical stability of the suspended active area.
mechanism: Varying a process parameter during material formation to adjust microstructural characteristics and interatomic interactions, thereby tuning internal stress levels through controlled nucleation and growth dynamics without compromising adhesion or mechanical stability.
mechanism_raw: Varying deposition pressure during SiGe layer formation to adjust grain structure and interatomic bonding, thereby tuning stress levels through controlled nucleation and growth dynamics.
residual_terms: ["process parameter", "material formation", "microstructural characteristics", "interatomic interactions", "internal stress", "nucleation and growth dynamics", "adhesion", "mechanical stability"]

abstract: To deposit optical quality films by PECVD (Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition), a six-dimensional space wherein five dimensions thereof correspond to five respective independent variables of which a set of four independent variables relate to the flow-rate of respective gases, a fifth independent variable relates to total pressure, and a six dimension relates to observed FTIR characteristics is first created. Then an optical film is deposited while maintaining three of the set of four independent variables substantially constant as well as the fifth independent variable, and varying a fourth of the set of four independent variables to obtain desired characteristics in the sixth dimension.
problem: Optimizing PECVD film characteristics (e.g., optical properties) by efficiently navigating a multi-variable parameter space.
constraint: Balancing computational and experimental efficiency by reducing dimensionality while capturing nonlinear interactions between variables that affect film quality.
mechanism: Systematically mapping a multi-dimensional parameter space and varying one independent variable while holding others constant to isolate causal relationships between inputs and output properties, enabling efficient navigation of nonlinear interactions.
mechanism_raw: Mapping a six-dimensional parameter space (gas flows, pressure, and FTIR responses) and systematically varying one independent variable while holding others constant to isolate causal relationships between inputs and film properties.
residual_terms: ["multi-dimensional parameter space", "independent variable", "causal relationships", "nonlinear interactions", "output properties"]

abstract: A water and dust-proof electric shaver head support structure that provides a wide range of movement to the floating shaver head to closely follow the contours of the skin. The floating shaver head, which contains the motor and shaving blades, freely pivots in the lateral plane and telescopically floats in relation to the shaver grip. A box-like space is formed in the shaver grip below the lower surface of the shaver head, and front and rear support walls extend upward from the shaver grip to support the shaver head in the forward/rearward direction.
problem: Achieving wide-range movement of a shaver head to follow skin contours while maintaining water/dust resistance and structural support.
constraint: Balancing multi-axis mobility with structural integrity and environmental sealing to prevent ingress of water/dust.
mechanism: A movable component with multi-axis mobility is supported by structural elements that maintain a sealed environment, allowing wide-range motion while preventing ingress of contaminants and preserving internal integrity.
mechanism_raw: A floating shaver head pivots laterally and telescopes relative to the grip, with front/rear support walls enabling controlled movement while forming a sealed box-like space to protect internal components.

abstract: A long-life bearing steel for general purpose use is provided at low cost with no use of specific secondary refining process. Specifically, a bearing material having a component composition in which C: 0.95 to 1.10 mass %, Si: 0.15 to 0.70 mass %, Mn: 1.15 mass % or less, Cr: 0.90 to 1.60 mass %, and P: 0.025 mass % or less are contained, S and O, that are elements forming nonmetallic inclusions, are contained at S: 0.025 mass % or less and O: 0.0012 mass % or less, and the rest is composed of Fe and incidental impurities, wherein the maximum diameter of the oxide-based nonmetallic inclusion is more than 10 μm, but 15 μm or less in an inspection area: 320 mm2, the number of oxide-based nonmetallic inclusions having an equivalent circle diameter of 3 μm or more is 250 or less in the inspection area: 320 mm2, while in the material, AlN is contained at 0.020 mass % or less, and or the number of sulfide-based nonmetallic inclusions having a thickness of 1 μm or more is 1,200 or less in the inspection area: 320 mm2.
problem: Producing a durable, low-cost bearing steel without secondary refining processes while controlling nonmetallic inclusions.
constraint: Balancing cost reduction (no secondary refining) with material performance by controlling inclusion formation and size distribution.
mechanism: Material properties are achieved by optimizing compositional ratios and constraining nonmetallic inclusion formation through precise elemental control, eliminating secondary processing steps while maintaining performance thresholds.
mechanism_raw: Optimizing chemical composition (C, Si, Mn, Cr, P, S, O) and limiting inclusion sizes/counts through precise elemental ratios and processing constraints to achieve desired mechanical properties.

abstract: An adjustable drum beating device, comprising at least one rotor operable to rotate a drum beater, a foot pedal driven flexible driver having a path of engagement with the rotor and operable to rotate the rotor, the driver having adjustable connection to the rotor to effectively adjust the position of the foot pedal relative to the rotor, and there being adjustably relatively movable parts associated with at least one rotor to adjust the configuration of the path of engagement of the flexible driver with the rotor.
problem: Adjusting the positional relationship between a foot pedal and a rotor in a drum beating device to accommodate user preferences.
constraint: Maintaining effective force transmission and engagement between the driver and rotor while allowing positional adjustments.
mechanism: An adjustable mechanical coupling with variable connection points modifies the engagement trajectory between a driver and driven component, enabling positional tuning while preserving force transmission efficiency.
mechanism_raw: An adjustable flexible driver with movable connection points alters the path of engagement between the pedal and rotor, enabling positional tuning without compromising mechanical coupling.

abstract: A file accessing scheme allows logical files to be processed outside of the native operating system and its logical I/O subsystem. When an application program wants to process a file outside of the native operating system, a file information block is built with a special type of file designated as “virtual.” A pointer is provided within the file information block to a handler. The handler is a library that is external to the native operating system. The library processes the file without using the native operating system. Upon completion of the processing, the handler returns the operation results to the file information block and control is transferred back to the application program.
problem: Processing logical files outside the native operating system's I/O subsystem without requiring OS-level integration.
constraint: Ensuring compatibility and control transfer between the application, virtual file structure, and external handler without native OS dependencies.
mechanism: A virtual data structure with an external handler reference bypasses native system interfaces, allowing independent processing of logical units and controlled result transfer between application and handler.
mechanism_raw: A virtual file information block with a pointer to an external handler library bypasses the native OS, allowing the handler to process files independently and return results to the application.
residual_terms: ["virtual data structure", "external handler reference", "native system interfaces"]

abstract: An apparatus for making crayons is provided. The apparatus includes a base that houses a heating component, a melt pan disposed to absorb heat from the heating component, a mold, and a cover. The melt pan receives crayon material and contains it as the heating component increases the temperature, causing the crayon material to liquefy. The liquefied crayon material can then be drained by the user of the device, into a mold with crayon-shaped cavities. A cover prevents access to the melt pan and the mold during particular operating conditions of the apparatus.
problem: Safely melting and molding crayon material while preventing user access to hazardous components during operation.
constraint: Balancing accessibility for material loading/unloading with safety interlocks that prevent contact with heated components during operation.
mechanism: A heating element liquefies material in a containment vessel, which transfers to a shaping cavity, with a safety barrier that restricts access to hazardous zones during active processing conditions.
mechanism_raw: A heating component liquefies material in a melt pan, which drains into a mold, with a cover that blocks access to the melt pan and mold during specific operating conditions.

abstract: A braiding apparatus for braiding the perforated braids with constant interval of perforations comprises a first braid section to braid one strand with a plurality of yarns, sequential braid section to braid with two strands and secondary sequential braid section to braid a final strand with the previous process of the strands. This braiding apparatus comprises a carrier guide plate (10) having a pair of core yarn holes (12), a plurality of coupling boles (13), two tracks of carrier contours (14), a base plate (40) having a plurality of carriers (20), feed gears (30), feed discs (31), feed gear shafts (32), actuators (42), carrier contour changers (50) including a main block (60), intermediate cross block (70) and inner split block (80) for performing repeated crossing and separating operations. So, the various braids with constant interval of perforations are possibly produced by differ the number of core yarns and carriers.
problem: Producing braids with constant intervals of perforations while varying the number of core yarns and carriers.
constraint: Balancing the number of core yarns and carriers to maintain structural integrity while achieving the desired perforation pattern.
mechanism: A synchronized carrier movement system dynamically adjusts the spacing and interaction of multiple yarn pathways through coordinated crossing and separation operations, maintaining uniform intervals between structural discontinuities regardless of variations in yarn count or carrier configuration.
mechanism_raw: A system of carrier guide plates, coupling boles, and carrier contour changers perform repeated crossing and separating operations to mechanically control the spacing and interaction of yarns, ensuring uniform perforation intervals through synchronized carrier movement.

abstract: An adapter for providing a concentrated beam of light over an extended distance for a flashlight. The flashlight includes a penlight with an LED light source. The adapter includes a light collecting and magnifying barrel having a reflective inner surface and a magnifying lens and is secured with the end of the penlight encasing the LED. Light rays emitted from the LED are concentrated and reflected through the lens in the form of a condensed beam of light.
reason: The mechanism relies on standard optical principles (reflective surfaces and lenses) to focus light, which is a well-known application rather than a novel causal operation.

abstract: A method and system in which a semiconductor wafer having a plurality of dies is inspected through a visual inspection and/or an electrical test. If certain of the dies on the wafer pass the inspection, then windows are mounted or affixed above those certain dies while they are still a part of the wafer.
problem: Protecting or marking semiconductor dies that pass inspection while still part of the wafer, without disrupting the wafer structure.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and adhesion of windows without damaging adjacent dies or the wafer during the mounting process.
mechanism: Real-time quality assessment is integrated with localized selective affixation of protective elements directly onto inspected targets, enabling spatially precise treatment based on pass/fail criteria without disrupting the structural integrity of the substrate.
mechanism_raw: Integrating visual/electrical inspection with selective affixation of protective windows directly onto passing dies, enabling localized treatment based on real-time quality assessment.

abstract: A process for treating animal hides includes spreading the hides (1) to be treated astride respective supporting plates (2) and introducing the plates into a container (10). Afterwards, the container (10) is closed hermetically and set under vacuum. A liquid solution is introduced into the container (10), to treat the hides, in particular to transform fresh animal hides into wet white state. The container (10) is driven into vibration, to make the solution contained in the container (10) move in a continuous and uniform way.
problem: Achieving uniform distribution of a liquid solution over animal hides during vacuum treatment to ensure consistent chemical transformation.
constraint: Maintaining vibration intensity and vacuum pressure to avoid damaging the hides while ensuring solution homogeneity.
mechanism: Hermetic containment combined with mechanical agitation induces continuous fluid circulation within a sealed environment, ensuring uniform distribution and penetration of a treatment medium across a substrate surface through synchronized pressure and motion control.
mechanism_raw: Combining hermetic vacuum sealing with mechanical vibration to induce continuous and uniform movement of the solution within the container, enhancing contact and penetration into the hides.

abstract: A method for plating electrodes of ceramic chip electronic components includes performing electroplating in a plating bath. The plating bath contains tin (II) sulfamate, acting as a tin (II) salt; a complexing agent including at least one selected from the group consisting of citric acid, gluconic acid, pyrophosphoric acid, heptoic acid, malonic acid, malic acid, salts of these acids, and gluconic lactone; and a brightener including at least one surfactant having an HLB value of about 10 or more. The tin plating adhesion of the resulting ceramic chip electronic components can be limited to a certain level.
problem: Controlling tin plating adhesion on ceramic chip electronic components to a specific level during electroplating.
constraint: Balancing the concentrations of complexing agents and surfactants to achieve the target adhesion without compromising plating efficiency or surface finish.
mechanism: Chemical interaction between a complexing agent and a surfactant with a defined surface activity parameter modulates ion availability and interfacial tension, enabling precise control of deposition adhesion through tunable molecular-level interactions.
mechanism_raw: Using a complexing agent (e.g., citric acid) and a surfactant with a defined HLB value to modulate ion availability and surface tension, thereby regulating adhesion properties through chemical interaction.

abstract: In an apparatus for the treatment of metallic workpieces (4) with cooling gas, having a cylindrical housing (3) with an opening at the end face for introducing and removing the workpieces (4), two support plates (6, 7) extending in parallel planes vertically in the housing (3) and two air-guiding plates (14, 15) are provided, the workpiece batch (4) being held between the support plates (6, 7), and the air-guiding plates (14, 15) each forming, with the adjacent support plates (6, 7) and with the respectively adjacent inner wall of the housing, shafts (16, 17 and 26, 27, respectively) through which the cooling gas conveyed by blowers held on the housing (3) flows, controlled by reversing flaps (18, 19, 20, 21) arranged at the upper and lower ends of the air-guiding plates (14, 15).
problem: Controlling cooling gas flow direction and distribution in a cylindrical treatment chamber to ensure uniform cooling of metallic workpieces while maintaining structural support for the batch.
constraint: Balancing gas flow redistribution with structural integrity of the workpiece batch and housing, ensuring flaps can reverse flow without disrupting workpiece positioning or causing uneven cooling.
mechanism: Adjustable barriers selectively redirect fluid flow through multiple predefined pathways formed between structural elements, enabling dynamic reconfiguration of flow distribution while maintaining positional stability of objects within the system.
mechanism_raw: Reversing flaps at the ends of air-guiding plates selectively direct cooling gas flow through different shafts formed between the air-guiding plates, support plates, and housing walls, enabling dynamic reconfiguration of gas pathways to optimize cooling efficiency.

abstract: A material removal optimizing system for a wood surface treating apparatus with a plurality of individual work stations arranged serially along an endless conveyor. Each station includes a working abrasive head along with an elevation adjustment mechanism for adjustably positioning the contact surface of each abrasive head at a desired working distance from the opposed surface of the workpiece traveling along the endless conveyor. An incoming workpiece dimension indicator is positioned at the infeed end, and additional workpiece dimension indicators are positioned downstream from each work station, with each dimension indicator being positioned to measure the dimensional deviation of the workpiece from a datum plane after it has passed through its preceding individual work station.
problem: Optimizing material removal across multiple sequential processing stations to minimize dimensional deviations in a workpiece traveling along a conveyor.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between sensor feedback and head adjustments while processing continuous workpieces, avoiding delays that could reduce throughput or introduce new errors.
mechanism: A feedback loop uses downstream sensors to measure deviations after each processing stage, and actuators dynamically adjust processing parameters in real time to correct cumulative errors across sequential operations.
mechanism_raw: Downstream dimension sensors measure deviations after each station, and elevation adjustment mechanisms for each abrasive head are dynamically tuned based on these measurements to correct for cumulative errors in real time.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method for utilizing soy molasses as a source for soy sugars which are of high oligosaccharaide content. The invention provides a method for purifying soy molasses comprising the following steps: (i) contacting the soy molasses with alcohol and hydrocarbon solvent mixture, thereby two layers comprising a lower aqueous-alcohol layer and an upper hydrocarbon layer are formed; (ii) collecting the lower aqueous-alcohol layer; (iii) removing coloring, off-flavor and odorous substances; and (iv) removing minerals, thereby a purified soy molasses of more than 90 wt. % sugars, on dry matter basis, is obtained.
problem: Purifying soy molasses to isolate high-value oligosaccharides while removing impurities like coloring agents, off-flavors, and minerals.
constraint: Achieving high sugar purity (>90%) without excessive loss of product during layer separation and subsequent purification stages, requiring precise solvent ratios and process timing.
mechanism: Immiscible solvent phases are used to partition target compounds into a preferred phase through selective solubility, followed by sequential purification steps to remove impurities from the partitioned phase.
mechanism_raw: Solvent extraction using an alcohol-hydrocarbon mixture creates immiscible layers, allowing selective partitioning of sugars into the aqueous-alcohol phase, followed by sequential removal of impurities through targeted purification steps.

abstract: Method and device (1) for supplying fuel to a combustion chamber that includes at least one main injector (3) and at least one pilot injector (2). The device includes a fuel tank (4), a line system (5) coupled from the fuel tank to the injectors (2, 3), a pump (6) for pumping fuel from the tank to the injectors, and a first regulator valve (7) for regulating the flow of fuel in a first line (8) in the system which is connected to the pilot injector (2). The device further includes a second regulator valve (9) for regulating the flow of fuel through a second line (10) in the system, which is connected to the pilot injector (2). The second regulator valve (9) is designed to regulate a substantially smaller flow than the first regulator valve (7).
problem: Controlling fuel flow rates to a combustion chamber's main and pilot injectors to ensure stable combustion under varying load conditions.
constraint: Ensuring the pilot injector receives a consistently smaller flow than the main injector while maintaining system responsiveness to combustion demands, avoiding cross-interference between the two regulation paths.
mechanism: Independent regulation paths with distinct flow capacities control delivery to two outlets, ensuring one outlet receives a consistently smaller flow than the other while maintaining responsiveness to demand changes.
mechanism_raw: Two regulator valves with different flow capacities independently control fuel delivery to the pilot and main injectors, enabling precise low-flow regulation for the pilot and higher-flow regulation for the main injector.

abstract: A mirror system for a vehicle comprising an exterior rearview mirror assembly, which includes a fixed portion which is configured to mount to a side of the vehicle. The movable portion includes a reflective element and a reflective element actuator. The reflective element has a generally rearward field of view when the mirror system is mounted to the vehicle. The reflective element actuator provides selective adjustment of an orientation of the reflective element to adjust the rearward field of view to a desired orientation, and the movable portion is movably mounted to the fixed portion. The movable portion actuator selectively moves the movable portion between a viewing position wherein the movable portion extends outwardly from the vehicle at an angle with respect to the side of the vehicle and another viewing position wherein said movable portion extends outwardly from the vehicle at another angle with respect to the side of the vehicle. The movable portion actuator is adapted to move the movable portion to one of the positions, and the reflective element actuator is adapted to generally maintain the rearward field of view at the desired orientation independent of the position of the movable portion.
problem: Maintaining a vehicle mirror's rearward field of view while repositioning the mirror assembly to different angular orientations relative to the vehicle side.
constraint: Achieving precise coordination between the two actuators to prevent mechanical interference and ensure the reflective element's orientation remains stable during position changes, even under vibration or external forces.
mechanism: Two independent actuators decouple positional adjustment of an assembly from orientation adjustment of a reflective element, allowing the field of view to remain fixed while the assembly's physical position changes.
mechanism_raw: Two independent actuators decouple mirror position adjustment (moving the entire assembly) from reflective element orientation adjustment, allowing the field of view to remain fixed while the mirror's physical position changes.

abstract: A method and system for reading an address of a mail piece is set out wherein the address face of the mail piece is scanned and decoded to generate an electronically recognizable or readable destination address. If the destination address is not completely decoded, the image of the address face is temporarily stored in a grouping in a database. The grouping is then forwarded to an encoding clerk who has the highest priority and is available for the grouping. The priority of the deck is based on data such as the clerk's measured professional competence. Herein, factors include experience with a particular destination region, success rate, and the like.
problem: Efficiently routing undecoded mail address images to the most competent available clerk for manual encoding.
constraint: Balancing clerk availability with their competence metrics to avoid overloading high-priority clerks while maintaining throughput.
mechanism: A dynamic task allocation system that routes undecoded data groupings to human operators based on measured performance metrics and real-time capacity, balancing workload distribution while prioritizing accuracy and throughput.
mechanism_raw: A dynamic priority-based task routing system that assigns undecoded address groupings to clerks based on measured professional competence (e.g., regional experience, success rate) and real-time availability, ensuring optimal human resource allocation for error correction.

abstract: A combustion apparatus 2 has an anti-spreading member 65 disposed below a combustion chamber 10. This anti-spreading member 65 is composed of a generally cylindrical main body 65a, an outer flange 65b and an inner flange 65c, these flanges being formed at and integral with the opposite ends of the main body 65a, respectively. A controller 40 for regulating the operation of this apparatus 2 is designed to preheat the anti-spreading member 65 at a heat generation rate ‘q’ lower than the required heat generation rate ‘Q’, before the apparatus starts its normal operation to burn a fuel.
problem: Preventing uncontrolled heat spread or flame propagation during combustion apparatus startup or operation.
constraint: Matching the preheat rate to the thermal properties of the member to avoid overheating or insufficient barrier formation.
mechanism: Preconditioning a structural barrier member at a sub-operational energy input rate before primary operation begins, forming a thermal resistance layer that limits energy propagation while preserving mechanical stability.
mechanism_raw: Preheating a structural anti-spreading member at a sub-operational heat generation rate before normal combustion begins, creating a thermal barrier that resists flame spread while maintaining structural integrity.
residual_terms: ["structural barrier member", "sub-operational energy input rate", "thermal resistance layer", "mechanical stability"]

abstract: A color OLED display includes an array of light emitting OLED pixels, each pixel having three or more gamut elements for emitting different colors of light specifying a gamut and at least one additional element for emitting a color of light within the gamut and wherein the power efficiency of the additional element is higher than the power efficiency of at least one of the three or more gamut elements; wherein all of the gamut elements for each color in the display are arranged in a first direction in a line such that no differently colored gamut element is in the line; wherein the colored gamut elements are arranged in a second direction orthogonal to the first direction in a line such that the colors of the gamut elements alternate in that line; and wherein the additional elements are arranged in lines in both the first and second directions.
problem: Improving power efficiency in color displays without sacrificing color gamut coverage.
constraint: Balancing the spatial arrangement of high-efficiency elements with the need to preserve color accuracy and pixel density.
mechanism: Integrating auxiliary energy-efficient elements with primary functional elements in a directional spatial arrangement to reduce power consumption while maintaining output quality and spatial consistency.
mechanism_raw: Integrating additional high-efficiency light-emitting elements alongside primary gamut elements, arranged in orthogonal directional lines to optimize power usage while maintaining color balance and spatial uniformity.
residual_terms: ["auxiliary energy-efficient elements", "directional spatial arrangement", "output quality", "spatial consistency"]

abstract: A vertical saw machine includes a column with upper and lower supports carrying a motor to drive a saw blade. A table is disposed between the upper and lower supports for supporting a workpiece. The saw blade intersects the table with an included angle. The column is turnable between normal and inclined positions to vary the included angle. A frame post is mounted under the table to be positioned on the ground surface. A key slot and a key member are disposed respectively in and on the frame post and the column, and confine an arcuate guiding route to retainingly guide the column to move between the two positions.
problem: Adjustably varying the angle of a saw blade relative to a workpiece table in a vertical saw machine.
constraint: Ensuring the guiding route permits smooth angular adjustment without introducing play or misalignment during operation.
mechanism: A mechanical constraint interface that defines a curved adjustment path, enabling controlled rotational positioning of a component between discrete orientations while maintaining alignment and minimizing positional drift.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical key-slot and key-member interface that confines an arcuate guiding route, allowing controlled rotation of the column between fixed angular positions while maintaining structural alignment.
residual_terms: ["mechanical constraint interface", "curved adjustment path", "discrete orientations", "positional drift"]

abstract: By providing a plurality of portals in a housing which forms a hair dryer attachment which is merely fixed to the exist portal of any conventional hair dryer, a hair dryer attachment is realized which is capable of substantially reducing the drying time required for drying the hair of any individual, while also being easily employed and comfortable. In the preferred embodiment, at least one raised, sloping panel is formed adjacent the inlet portal of the attachment with the panel sloping outwardly from the generally circular shaped inlet portal. In addition, a plurality of apertures or portals are formed in the panel for enabling ambient air to freely flow therethrough. In this way, the heated air flowing through the central portion of the attachment creates a low-pressure zone on the inside surface of the portals, drawing ambient air through the portals into the interior of the hair dryer attachment, thereby enabling the quantity of the air reaching the hair of the user is substantially increased.
problem: Reducing hair drying time by increasing the volume of airflow delivered to the hair.
constraint: Optimizing aperture size and panel slope to maximize ambient air entrainment while maintaining structural and ergonomic compatibility with conventional hair dryers.
mechanism: Generating a localized pressure differential via high-velocity fluid flow through a central conduit, inducing ambient fluid entrainment through auxiliary openings and sloped surfaces to amplify total flow rate without additional mechanical input.
mechanism_raw: Creating a low-pressure zone via high-velocity heated air flow through a central passage, which entrains ambient air through strategically placed apertures and sloping panels, thereby amplifying total airflow without additional mechanical power.
residual_terms: ["localized pressure differential", "high-velocity fluid flow", "ambient fluid entrainment", "auxiliary openings"]

abstract: An amphibious dredging vehicle includes a base including a pair of floatable pontoons linked together in essentially parallel relation; a cutterhead dredge system that is mounted on the base and that includes a cutterhead mounted on the front end portion of the base, a first directable discharge mounted to the rear end portion of the base, and a dredge pump in operative connection with the cutterhead and the directable discharge so as to develop suction at the cutterhead and to propel material from the cutterhead to the directable discharge. The directable discharge is configured so that the operator can aim the directable discharge in order to use the dredge pump to propel the amphibious dredging vehicle through water. The amphibious dredging vehicle may be used as part of a system and may be used with a method for building up land in a water-covered or water-surrounded area.
problem: Efficiently propelling an amphibious dredging vehicle through water while performing dredging operations.
constraint: Balancing the dual function of the pump (dredging and propulsion) without compromising the efficiency of either operation, and maintaining directional control of the discharge for propulsion.
mechanism: Using a single fluid-handling unit to perform two distinct functions—material transport and thrust generation—by selectively directing its output stream to create propulsive force, thereby eliminating the need for separate systems for each function.
mechanism_raw: Using the same dredge pump for both material transport and vehicle propulsion by directing the discharge outlet to generate thrust, thereby eliminating the need for a separate propulsion system.

abstract: A windsurfing catamaran with a self-stabilizing wing. The wing is moved to the correct position by counter balancing water pressure from a rotating central keel connected to a central mast. The keel rotates in the opposite direction of the wing when the wing is moved off center by wind. The keel rotates such that a greater surface area is presented to water flow striking the keel. Water pressure on the keel offsets wind pressure on the sails and returns the keel and mast back to an upright position. This increases stability, lift, driving force, and speed. A central catamaran platform provides hinged struts and shock absorbers between the rear end of the central platform and planing hulls to reduce impact damage. The hinged struts and shock absorbers reduce water drag and the braking effect of repeated hull impacts with water resulting in a further increase in speed.
problem: Maintaining stability and optimizing lift/driving force in a windsurfing catamaran under varying wind conditions.
constraint: Achieving real-time dynamic balance between wind pressure on the wing and water pressure on the keel without introducing excessive drag or mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A dynamic counterbalancing system where a movable element (opposite to an external force source) adjusts its exposed surface area in real-time to generate opposing pressure, stabilizing the primary force application point while minimizing drag.
mechanism_raw: A counterbalancing system where rotation of a central keel (opposite to the wing's movement) dynamically adjusts the keel's surface area exposed to water flow, creating opposing pressure to stabilize the wing and mast.

abstract: In a laser processing method for accurately forming a convexo-concave structure on the surface of a glass substrate, a periodic optical intensity distribution of a laser beam is obtained by an interference between diffracted light beams of +1 degree and −1 degree emitted from a phase mask, onto which the laser beam is irradiated, in the vicinity of the emission side of the phase mask, and a glass substrate, on which a thin film is formed, is set in the area where the periodic optical intensity distribution is provided. As a result, the thin film is evaporated or ablated depending on the periodic optical intensity, thereby a diffraction grating, which has the same period as that of the varying optical intensity, is formed on the glass substrate.
problem: Accurately forming periodic microstructures (e.g., diffraction gratings) on a glass substrate surface.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and coherence of the diffracted laser beams to maintain the periodicity and fidelity of the microstructure during processing.
mechanism: Creating a periodic intensity pattern through interference between two coherent light beams (e.g., +1 and -1 diffraction orders) to directly modify a target surface, replicating the pattern via controlled energy deposition.
mechanism_raw: Using interference between +1 and -1 order diffracted laser beams from a phase mask to create a periodic optical intensity pattern, which directly ablates or evaporates the thin film to replicate the pattern on the substrate.
residual_terms: ["interference", "coherent light beams", "diffraction orders", "periodic intensity pattern", "energy deposition"]

abstract: An electronic device is formed at least partially from a deflectable material that generates an electrical signal in response to contact. The first material is integrated with a display module to provide a shaped feature on the exterior surface of the display module. The shaped feature detects contact with an external object on one or more contact points, where contact with the contact points corresponds to a defined input for a processor of the electronic device.
problem: Detecting external contact on a display module to provide user input without compromising the display's structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining the display's functionality and surface quality while enabling reliable detection of contact-induced deflection across one or more contact points.
mechanism: Integrating a compliant layer with a rigid substrate such that external contact induces localized mechanical deformation, which is transduced into an electrical signal representing a defined input for processing.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a deflectable material with the display module such that physical contact causes mechanical deflection, which generates an electrical signal corresponding to a defined input for a processor.

abstract: The present invention is a clothing iron capable of lifting the iron, and thus the hot sole plate of the iron, away from a surface on which the iron rests when the iron is not in use, to reduce or prevent damage to the surface on which the iron rests. An important characteristic of the invention is that the sole plate of the iron is lifted in a direction including a vertical vector, with a plane of the sole plate remaining roughly horizontal. The elevation of the iron is accomplished through the use of an elevation mechanism including apparatus for extending at least one leg from the underside of the iron when the sensor indicates that the user's hand is not in contact with the iron.
problem: Preventing damage to surfaces (e.g., tables) when a clothing iron is not in use.
constraint: Ensuring the elevation mechanism activates reliably based on sensor input and lifts the sole plate without tilting, while remaining unobtrusive during normal use.
mechanism: A sensor-triggered actuation system that extends support elements from a device's base when user contact is removed, lifting the base vertically while maintaining its orientation to prevent surface contact.
mechanism_raw: Automatically extending legs from the iron's underside via a sensor-triggered elevation mechanism when the user's hand is no longer in contact, lifting the sole plate vertically while keeping it roughly horizontal.

abstract: An incinerator pre-fill chamber for installation on an incinerator for burning combustible material which allows the operator to continuously re-fill the container of the incinerator with new combustible material while the contents within the container is burning. The incinerator pre-fill chamber includes an elongated case having a first opening aligned in sealing relationship with a second opening disposed in the lid of the incinerator such that when said pre-fill chamber is mounted on the incinerator lid the combustible material can pass from said pre-fill chamber through said first and second openings. The pre-fill chamber further includes a plunger with a platen, at least one side door that opens for loading the material to be burned into the pre-fill chamber, and a trap door that opens when the plunger is actuated thereby permitting the material to pass through the first opening of the pre-fill chamber.
problem: Continuously refilling a burning incinerator without interrupting combustion or losing heat/seal integrity.
constraint: Balancing continuous material flow with maintaining a gas-tight seal to prevent heat loss and emissions.
mechanism: A movable barrier selectively opens a passage between a staging chamber and a processing vessel, enabling material transfer while preserving a sealed environment during operation.
mechanism_raw: A plunger with a trap door actuates to open a controlled passage between a pre-fill chamber and the incinerator, allowing material transfer while maintaining a sealed system during operation.

abstract: There are many inventions described and illustrated herein. In one aspect, there is described a thin film or wafer encapsulated MEMS, and technique of fabricating or manufacturing a thin film or wafer encapsulated MEMS employing anti-stiction techniques. In one embodiment, after encapsulation of the MEMS, an anti-stiction channel is formed thereby providing “access” to the chamber containing some or all of the active members or electrodes of the mechanical structures. Thereafter, an anti-stiction fluid (for example, gas or gas-vapor) is introduced into the chamber via the anti-stiction channel. The anti-stiction fluid may deposit on one, some or all of the active members of the mechanical structures thereby providing an anti-stiction layer (for example, a monolayer coating or self-assembled monolayer) and/or out-gassing molecules on such members or electrodes. After introduction and/or application of the anti-stiction fluid, the anti-stiction channel may be sealed, capped, plugged and/or closed.
problem: Preventing stiction (adhesion) between moving parts in encapsulated MEMS devices after fabrication.
constraint: Ensuring the anti-stiction treatment is applied uniformly without compromising the structural integrity of the sealed MEMS chamber.
mechanism: A temporary access channel allows deposition of a non-adherent coating on internal components, which is then permanently closed to preserve a sealed environment.
mechanism_raw: A temporary anti-stiction channel provides access to deposit a fluid or vapor that forms a non-stick layer on active components, which is then permanently sealed to maintain encapsulation.
residual_terms: ["anti-stiction channel", "fluid or vapor", "non-stick layer", "sealed MEMS chamber"]

abstract: A fully integrated drying or heating system utilizes forced air and electrical heaters. A solid cartridge heater is enclosed within a compact air plenum with a circuitous air path arranged within the plenum in heat transfer communication with the heater. The plenums are shaped and configured to be used in banks of plural plenums, with the operating controls and all the components of the air distribution system and air heating system fully integrated into a modular package.
problem: Achieving efficient heat transfer in a modular, scalable heating system without sacrificing compactness or integration.
constraint: Optimizing air path geometry to maximize heat exchange surface area while maintaining modularity and minimizing system footprint.
mechanism: A serpentine flow path within a compact enclosure directs air into thermal contact with a heating element, while a modular enclosure design enables scalable arrays with integrated regulation.
mechanism_raw: A circuitous air path within a compact plenum forces air into close thermal contact with an enclosed heater, while modular plenum design allows scalable banks of units with integrated controls.
residual_terms: ["circuitous air path", "compact plenum", "enclosed heater", "modular plenum", "integrated controls"]

abstract: A headwear piece has a crown defining an opening to receive the head of a wearer. The crown has (a) an inside surface having at least a portion for engaging a wearer's head to maintain the headwear piece operatively situated on a wearers head and (b) an exposed external surface. The crown has first and second openings through the external surface of the crown and spaced from each other so that an elongate object can be directed through both of the first and second openings and frictionally maintained in a stored position on the crown with the headwear piece operatively situated on a wearer's head.
problem: Securing an elongate object to headwear in a stored position while the headwear remains operatively situated on the wearer's head.
constraint: Maintaining frictional grip on the object without displacing the headwear or restricting the wearer's movement.
mechanism: Spaced apertures in a wearable structure allow an elongate object to pass through and be frictionally retained along its length, using the structure itself as a passive retention mechanism.
mechanism_raw: Two spaced openings in the crown allow the object to pass through and be frictionally retained along its length, using the headwear's structure as a passive clamping mechanism.

abstract: A tuft forming mechanism including a yarn feed mechanism and a yarn severing means (6, 18), the yarn feed mechanism including a passage (5) along which yarn (2) is guided to said yarn severing means (6, 18) and an intermittently rotatable feed disc (1) which engages the yarn (2) to advance the yarn (2) along the passage (5).
problem: Precisely advancing yarn in intermittent increments for tuft formation without continuous or uneven feeding.
constraint: Synchronizing disc rotation with severing action to ensure consistent yarn length while avoiding slack or tension irregularities.
mechanism: An intermittently rotating feed element grips and advances a filament along a guided path toward a cutting mechanism, with rotational timing determining the length dispensed per cycle.
mechanism_raw: An intermittently rotatable feed disc engages the yarn to advance it along a guided passage toward a severing mechanism, with rotation timing controlling yarn length per tuft.
residual_terms: ["intermittently rotatable feed disc", "severing mechanism", "rotation timing", "yarn length per tuft"]

abstract: A railroad e-clip removal system for efficiently and safely removing railroad e-clips from a railroad track. The railroad e-clip removal system includes an outer tube with an outer cutout, an inner tube slidably positioned within a lumen of the outer tube, an inner cutout within the inner tube having an engaging portion, and an actuator unit attached to the tubes for extending/retracting the inner tube within the outer tube. The engaging portion of the inert tube engages a portion of an e-clip when the actuator unit is extended thereby forcing the e-clip from a tubular support member attached to a rail pad. The e-clip is thereby safely and efficiently removed from the railroad track.
problem: Efficiently and safely removing a retaining component (e-clip) from a fixed position without damaging surrounding structures.
constraint: Precise alignment and force application are required to avoid damaging the rail pad or surrounding track components while ensuring reliable engagement with the e-clip.
mechanism: A coaxial dual-tube assembly where an inner member with an engaging feature is selectively extended or retracted within an outer guide tube via an actuation element, enabling controlled mechanical interaction to dislodge a retaining component from a fixed position while maintaining alignment and limiting force application to prevent damage to surrounding structures.
mechanism_raw: A coaxial sliding mechanism where an inner tube with an engaging portion is extended/retracted within an outer tube via an actuator, enabling controlled mechanical interaction to dislodge the e-clip from its support.

abstract: An optical pickup device which includes (A) a light source, and (B) an objective lens and an aberration correcting optical system which are located in a light path from the light source to an optical recording medium is so arranged that the aberration correcting optical system imparts a phase distribution to luminous flux which transmits the aberration correcting optical system, so as to correct a predetermined aberration; and an amount of phase of the aberration correcting optical system when correcting the aberration is set in such a manner that the aberration correcting optical system imparts a larger amount of phase at a position farther from a point where the aberration correcting optical system crosses an optical axis of light emitted from the light source.
