With this, it is possible to increase a tolerance for the center misalignment of the objective lens so as to reduce aberration caused by the center misalignment.
problem: Correcting optical aberrations caused by misalignment between an objective lens and an optical recording medium in an optical pickup system.
constraint: The phase correction must balance increased tolerance for misalignment against the risk of introducing new aberrations or reducing signal quality at the recording medium.
mechanism: An optical phase correction system that applies a spatially varying phase distribution to transmitted light, with progressively greater phase correction at increasing distances from the optical axis, to compensate for aberrations induced by misalignment between an optical element and a target medium.
mechanism_raw: A phase-correcting optical system that imparts a spatially varying phase distribution to transmitted light, with greater phase correction applied at positions farther from the optical axis to compensate for misalignment-induced aberrations.

abstract: A device for covering an airbag for forming an outer contour of interior trim for a vehicle with a mechanism for opening a cover into the passenger space of the vehicle and with a mechanism for moving the opened cover at least partially out of the passenger space of the vehicle, wherein the mechanism for opening including a first axis is arranged on a side of the cover facing a windshield for pivoting the cover.
problem: Safely deploying an airbag by opening and repositioning its cover to avoid obstructing the passenger compartment during inflation.
constraint: The cover must pivot and translate within tight spatial constraints while ensuring rapid, reliable deployment without interfering with airbag inflation dynamics.
mechanism: A multi-axis deployable cover mechanism that pivots about a first axis to swing open and then undergoes a secondary translational or pivoting motion to move the cover at least partially out of the deployment space, ensuring unobstructed rapid deployment of an inflatable restraint system.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting cover mechanism with a first axis on the windshield-facing side, enabling the cover to swing open and then move at least partially out of the passenger space via a secondary movement mechanism.

abstract: A unitary blade unit for an archery broadhead includes a tip structure and at least three blades inseparably connected into a single blade unit. The blade unit requires a separate ferrule in order for the blade unit to be secured to an arrow. Thus, the blade unit can be replaced while retaining a previously used ferrule, or vice versa. In a preferred embodiment, the blade unit is formed by metal injection molding.
problem: Enabling replacement of cutting blades in an archery broadhead while retaining the structural ferrule attached to the arrow.
constraint: The blade unit must maintain structural integrity during use while ensuring the ferrule-to-blade interface allows reliable attachment and detachment without compromising arrow flight.
mechanism: A modular coupling interface that decouples a replaceable blade assembly from a structural ferrule, allowing independent replacement of the blade unit while maintaining a reliable mechanical connection between the ferrule and the blade during use.
mechanism_raw: A modular blade unit design where blades are integrally formed into a single replaceable unit, decoupled from the ferrule, allowing independent replacement of either component.

abstract: A method of precisely controlling the amount of flatness or curvature in a lapping plate is disclosed. The lapping plate is formed from two layers of metal alloys, such as tin-antimony and steel. A bimetallic effect is exploited to induce a linear expansion in the plate so that the flatness or curvature of the plate is manipulated with thermal cycling. The plate is machined and charged under very specific and tightly controlled temperatures to produce a very robust, flat plate charge. As temperature cycling induces a linear expansion along a single plane across the plate, the resultant flatness change is scalar with temperature, and can be repeated and controlled. When the plate laps magnetic sliders, the plate can be thermally cycled to produce a conical surface and a high crown-to-camber ratio can be achieved.
problem: Precisely controlling the flatness or curvature of a lapping plate for high-precision surface finishing of components like magnetic sliders.
constraint: Temperature control must be tightly regulated to ensure repeatable, predictable expansion while avoiding material fatigue or thermal stress that could degrade plate performance.
mechanism: A thermally responsive two-layer structure that exploits differential thermal expansion between layers to induce controlled deformation, enabling scalar adjustment of surface flatness or curvature through regulated temperature cycling while maintaining dimensional stability and avoiding thermal stress-induced degradation.
mechanism_raw: Exploiting a bimetallic effect in a two-layer plate to induce controlled linear thermal expansion, enabling scalar adjustment of flatness/curvature through temperature cycling.

abstract: Compounds which mimic the secondary structure of helical regions of biologically active peptides and proteins having the following structure: including pharmaceutically acceptable salts and stereoisomers thereof, wherein Y, A, B, R1 and R2 are as defined herein. Such compounds have utility over a wide range of applications, including use as diagnostic and therapeutic agents. In particular, compounds of this invention, and pharmaceutical compositions containing the same, are neurokinin (tachykinin) antagonists. Libaries contaning the compounds of this invention are also disclosed, as well as methods for screening such libaries identify biologically active members.
problem: Creating therapeutic agents that can specifically modulate biological activity (e.g., as neurokinin/tachykinin antagonists) by interacting with target peptides and proteins.
constraint: The compounds must maintain sufficient structural fidelity to the target peptides to achieve specific binding while remaining stable and bioavailable enough to function as therapeutic agents in vivo.
mechanism: Designing compounds that structurally mimic the secondary structure of biologically active peptides and proteins, enabling them to bind to and block specific biological targets through molecular complementarity and shape-based recognition.
mechanism_raw: Designing compounds that structurally mimic the secondary structure of biologically active peptides and proteins, enabling them to bind to and block specific biological targets through molecular complementarity and shape-based recognition.

abstract: A method for the manufacture of micro metallic structures having high aspect ratios is provided, wherein said method comprises the step of photolithographically producing trenches in a substrate. Polymer chains are formed on the inner surface of said trenches. Thus, the critical dimensions in the photolithographical process can be reduced to any dimension down to zero. The method is quite general in its application to any process that includes the definition of a critical dimension by photolithography. Immediate applications are the reduction of the read and write dimensions in thin film magnetic heads, but the invention can be used in any technology where the manufacture of microstructures having a high aspect ratio is of interest.
problem: Creating microstructures with critical dimensions smaller than the resolution limit achievable by photolithography alone.
constraint: The polymer formation process must be compatible with existing photolithographic workflows and must achieve the desired dimensional reduction without compromising the structural integrity or aspect ratio of the final microstructure.
mechanism: Forming material on the inner surfaces of patterned recesses, which further narrows the recess dimensions beyond what the primary patterning step can directly achieve, effectively using a secondary deposition process to refine critical dimensions.
mechanism_raw: Forming polymer chains on the inner surfaces of photolithographically defined trenches, which further narrows the trench dimensions beyond what the primary photolithographic patterning step can directly achieve, effectively using a secondary deposition process to refine critical dimensions.

abstract: The present invention provides a time of flight mass spectrometer having a spiral flight path, whose mass resolution can be appropriately changed with respect to the analysis object or other factor without any complicated alteration or addition of the mechanical construction. In a specific form of the invention, the mass spectrometer includes deflecting electrodes 20-23 located between semi-cylindrical electrodes 11 and 12 for making ions fly along a spiral path. The deflecting electrodes 20-23 generate deflecting electric fields for shifting the ions in the axial direction of the semi-cylindrical electrodes 11 and 12. The voltage applied to the deflecting electrodes 20-23 is changed according to the mass resolution required. The deflecting electric fields are generated or removed with the change of the voltage, which makes the ions fly either along a spiral path or in the same loop orbit. The flight distance of the ions can be controlled as desired by regulating the voltage so that the ions fly in the loop orbit an appropriate number of times. Thus, the mass resolution can be arbitrarily controlled.
problem: Controlling mass resolution in a time-of-flight mass spectrometer without requiring mechanical modifications or hardware changes.
constraint: The voltage applied to the deflecting electrodes must be precisely controlled to achieve the desired mass resolution while maintaining stable ion trajectories and preventing ion loss or instability in the flight path.
mechanism: Using adjustable electric fields from deflecting electrodes to control ion flight path geometry — switching between a spiral path and a loop orbit — where the number of loop orbits and thus total flight distance is regulated by voltage, directly tuning the time-of-flight separation and hence mass resolution.
mechanism_raw: Using adjustable electric fields from deflecting electrodes to control ion flight path geometry — switching between a spiral path and a loop orbit — where the number of loop orbits and thus total flight distance is regulated by voltage, directly tuning the time-of-flight separation and hence mass resolution.
residual_terms: ["time-of-flight", "mass resolution", "ion flight path", "deflecting electrodes", "loop orbit", "spiral path"]

abstract: A showerhead assembly includes a filter that is removably receivable by the showerhead. The showerhead includes a receiving opening defined within the downstream face of the showerhead, which opening is functionally adapted to receive the filter within it. The opening of the showerhead is interposed between the water inlet and water outlet of the showerhead and within the flow of water through the showerhead such that, when a filter is inserted into the opening, all water flowing through the showerhead also flows through the filter. The filter is readily insertable within the opening and it is easily removable from it. The filter includes means for securing it within the opening when the filter is inserted.
reason: This patent describes a straightforward product design feature — a removable filter positioned in the water flow path of a showerhead with a retention mechanism. There is no deeper causal or functional mechanism beyond basic filtration placement and mechanical retention; it is a component arrangement rather than a problem-solving principle.

abstract: A lower barrier layer made of tantalum nitride having a thickness of approximately 25 nm is deposited by sputtering on a fourth insulating film inclusive of the sidewall surfaces and the bottom surfaces of a via hole and an upper-interconnect-forming groove. The sputtering is performed under the conditions where approximately 10 kW of DC source power is applied to a target. Thereafter, the DC source power is reduced to approximately 2 kW, and approximately 200 W of RF power is applied to a semiconductor substrate. Here, the lower barrier layer is subjected to a sputter-etching process employing argon gas at an etching amount of approximately 5 nm, so that a part of the lower barrier layer deposited on the bottom surface of the via hole is at least partially deposited on the lower part of the sidewall surface of the via hole.
problem: Ensuring proper barrier layer coverage on both the bottom surfaces and sidewall surfaces of high-aspect-ratio vias and grooves during thin film deposition.
constraint: The sputter-etching amount must be precisely controlled (approximately 5 nm) to achieve proper material redistribution without over-etching, and the power transition from high DC to low DC plus RF bias must be carefully managed to maintain process stability.
mechanism: Using a two-step deposition process where initial high-power coating applies material to all surfaces, followed by a controlled power reduction with substrate bias and sputter-etching that selectively redistributes deposited material from the bottom surface to the lower sidewall regions, improving coverage in confined geometries.
mechanism_raw: Using a two-step sputtering process where initial high-power deposition coats all surfaces, followed by a controlled power reduction with RF substrate bias and argon sputter-etching that selectively redistributes barrier material from the bottom surface to the lower sidewall regions, improving coverage in confined geometries.
residual_terms: ["sputter-etching", "DC power", "RF bias", "barrier layer", "high-aspect-ratio vias", "thin film deposition"]

abstract: An impact and fire resistant coating laminate is provided which serves as an outer protective coating for a pressure vessel such as a composite overwrapped vessel with a metal lining. The laminate comprises a plurality of fibers (e.g., jute twine or other, stronger fibers) which are wound around the pressure vessel and an epoxy matrix resin for the fibers. The epoxy matrix resin including a plurality of microspheres containing a temperature responsive phase change material which changes phase in response to exposure thereof to a predetermined temperature increase so as to afford increased insulation and heat absorption.
problem: Protecting pressure vessels from thermal damage during fire or impact events while maintaining structural integrity
constraint: Balancing structural load-bearing capacity (fiber winding and epoxy matrix) with thermal protection (microsphere volume fraction and PCM selection) so that insulation does not compromise mechanical strength
mechanism: A thermal regulation system incorporates a material with a phase-change property within a load-bearing structure, where the material absorbs heat through latent energy storage when a temperature threshold is reached, automatically activating passive cooling without compromising structural integrity
mechanism_raw: Phase-change material microspheres embedded within a structural matrix absorb heat through latent heat of fusion when temperature rises, providing passive thermal regulation that activates automatically at a predetermined temperature threshold

abstract: The Paint Brush Scrubber is a two sided device, for left and right handed use. It has a multiple notched scrub board on each side and a semicircular cutout on one edge. It cleans regulator and sponge paint brushes, paint rollers, and paint pad applicators. Can also be used to clean other types of brushes and other things including clothes etc. The size of the scrubber can vary from a size for an artist brush to the size of a house painters 4″ brush. It has a hole in handle so it can be stored with your paint brushes. It is safe to use and will never require parts or service. Paint brushes are cleaned by scrubbing action, which separates the bristles, cleaning quickly and easily, without getting your hands dirty. As the brush being cleaned it cleans the scrubber, so when the brush is clean the scrubber is also clean. The bristles are combed back into shape after cleaning using the cutout and scrub board. The scrubber also cleans paint rollers by scraping off most of paint into the paint container, using the semicircular cutout area of the scrubber, than scrubbing off the rest using the scrub board. Paint pad applicators are also cleaned using the scrub board.
problem: Cleaning paint brushes, rollers, and pads quickly and easily without manual effort or getting hands dirty
constraint: The geometry of notches and cutouts must accommodate a wide range of brush sizes (from artist brushes to 4-inch house painter brushes) while maintaining effective scrubbing action and self-cleaning behavior
mechanism: A self-cleaning interface uses a textured abrasive surface with variable geometry to mechanically separate and scrub bristles through direct contact, where the brush's motion against the surface simultaneously cleans both the brush and the interface itself via bidirectional interaction
mechanism_raw: A textured scrubbing surface with notches mechanically separates and abrades bristles through direct scrubbing contact, and the design ensures bidirectional cleaning where the brush's motion against the surface simultaneously cleans both the brush and the scrubber itself

abstract: A lightweight armor system may comprise multiple reinforcement materials layered within a single metal matrix casting. These reinforcement materials may comprise ceramics, metals, or other composites with microstructures that may be porous, dense, fibrous or particulate. Various geometries of flat plates, and combinations of reinforcement materials may be utilized. These reinforcement materials are infiltrated with liquid metal, the liquid metal solidifies within the material layers of open porosity forming a dense hermetic metal matrix composite armor in the desired product shape geometry. The metal infiltration process allows for metal to penetrate throughout the overall structure extending from one layer to the next, thereby binding the layers together and integrating the structure.
problem: Creating lightweight, strong armor with integrated reinforcement materials that are structurally bonded together
constraint: Selecting reinforcement materials (ceramics, metals, composites) and their geometries (porous, dense, fibrous, particulate) such that metal can penetrate throughout while preserving the desired mechanical properties of each layer
mechanism: A layered composite structure is formed by infiltrating a fluid medium through reinforcement layers with interconnected voids, where the medium solidifies to bind all layers into a unified dense matrix, preserving individual layer properties while enabling structural continuity
mechanism_raw: Liquid metal infiltration through layered reinforcement materials with open porosity, where the metal penetrates throughout the structure from one layer to the next, solidifying to bind all layers together and form a dense hermetic metal matrix composite

abstract: A friction device (10), applied to roll-up curtains and the like, includes a tubular roller (1), on which the curtain (2) rolls up, and which is rotatably carried on a horizontal axis. The friction device (10) includes a threaded shaft (9), situated axially inside the roller (1) and connected to the roller (1) by interposition of an angular speed reducer group (4). A body (11), mounted sliding axially inside the roller (1), is screw-coupled with the threaded shaft (9), so as to translate axially due to the shaft (9) rotation during unrolling or rolling up of the curtain (2) on the roller (1). One or more elastic members (12), subjected to pressure or counter-thrust, are compressed, on opposite ends, between abutment means (13) and a surface of the body (11), to determine a friction effect, which varies as a function of the rotation direction of the roller (1).
problem: Controlling the rolling and unrolling motion of curtains with friction that varies depending on rotation direction
constraint: The speed reducer and threading must reliably translate rotational motion into controlled axial displacement while maintaining consistent friction modulation across the operating range
mechanism: A motion conversion system translates rotational input into controlled axial displacement via a threaded interface, where the axial position of a sliding component modulates compression of elastic elements to create direction-dependent friction effects
mechanism_raw: Converting rotational motion into axial translation via a threaded shaft connected through a speed reducer, where the sliding body's axial position modulates compression of elastic elements to create a friction effect that varies with rotation direction

abstract: In a separation device for separating particles from a liquid, which is present in a container, a centrifugal rotor is rotatable around a vertical rotational axis. The centrifugal rotor has a tubular inlet member, which extends down into liquid to be treated and which upon rotation of the centrifugal rotor forms a pumping member adapted to pump liquid upwardly and into the centrifugal rotor. The rotatable inlet member is surrounded by a non-rotatable wall, a sealing device being adapted to seal between the rotatable inlet member and the non-rotatable wall. Thereby is avoided that liquid is pumped upwardly on the outside of the inlet member. Furthermore, a smallest possible part of the outside of the inlet member can be in contact with liquid, independent of the level of the liquid surface in the container.
problem: Efficiently separating particles from liquid in a centrifugal separator while preventing bypass flow around the inlet
constraint: The sealing interface between the rotating inlet member and the stationary wall must maintain a tight seal regardless of the liquid level in the container, ensuring no bypass flow occurs at any operating condition
mechanism: A dynamic sealing interface between a rotating inlet and stationary wall maintains a tight seal regardless of fluid level, where the rotating inlet acts as a pump to direct fluid into a centrifugal processing chamber while preventing bypass flow through the seal
mechanism_raw: A rotatable inlet member extends into the liquid and acts as a pump when the rotor spins, drawing liquid upward into the centrifugal rotor, while a stationary seal between the rotating inlet and non-rotatable wall prevents liquid from being pumped outside the inlet member

abstract: An improved fastener installation tool is provided of the type having a fixture pin for seated reception into a mating recess at the shank end of a threaded fastener, while a power-driven socket installs a threaded nut onto the fastener shank. The installation tool incorporates a simplified spring-loaded clutch assembly including a dual function spring member for urging the fixture pin axially forwardly relative to the power-driven socket, whereby the fixture pin slidably retracts against the applied spring force as the nut is threaded onto the fastener shank. The spring member additionally urges a cam pin into normal engagement with a lobed cam wheel carried by the fixture pin for normally preventing fixture pin rotation, but wherein the cam pin retracts to accommodate limited fixture pin rotation in response to a torque overload condition thereby protecting the fixture pin against deformation or breakage.
problem: Preventing damage to a fixture pin during torque overload in a fastener installation tool.
constraint: The spring must provide sufficient force to engage the cam normally but allow retraction under overload without compromising standard operation.
mechanism: A resilient element provides normal engagement force to maintain a mechanical interface in a fixed orientation, while a torque-responsive coupling allows controlled slippage under overload conditions to prevent component deformation. The coupling includes a lobed cam mechanism that converts rotational torque into linear retraction, enabling limited relative motion between connected parts when a threshold torque is exceeded.
mechanism_raw: A dual-function spring simultaneously urges the fixture pin forward and engages a cam pin with a lobed cam wheel to prevent rotation. Under torque overload, the cam pin retracts, allowing limited fixture pin rotation to protect against deformation or breakage.

abstract: A modular helmet system having a helmet base to protect from impacts the crown of a wearer's head and terminating basally in a rear rim and side rims; a C-shaped extension detachably connected to said rims to protect from impacts, when fitted to the helmet base, the base of a wearer's skull; and a crown comb detachably connected centrally over the crown of the helmet base. The helmet base is provided with ventilation windows centrally located over its crown. The comb covers and seals said ventilation windows. The comb is also employed to secure the extension in place, when fitted on the helmet base.
reason: The patent describes modular helmet components with multi-functional roles (e.g., a comb covering vents and securing an extension), but this is a product-specific design choice rather than a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a problem across fields.

abstract: An adjustable eddy electrostatic precipitator, including a main body, an electrode array, an adjustable opening and a precipitating device. The main body has an inner space with an air guiding plate of helical shape, an entrance for air and an exit for air. The electrode array is placed close to the entrance, ionizing air as well as particles floating therein. The adjustable opening is located at the exit, having an adjustable aperture. The precipitating device is connected with a bias high voltage for adsorbing ionized particles. Air entering the main body through the entrance is ionized, ionizing particles floating therein. Ionized particles are driven towards a single zone and are collected depending on size and charge in an adjustable manner.
problem: Efficiently collecting particles of varying sizes and charges in an electrostatic precipitator.
constraint: Balancing ionization efficiency with adjustable collection parameters to optimize particle removal across different operating conditions.
mechanism: A medium is ionized to impart electrical charge to entrained particles, followed by a variable-geometry collection zone where particle trajectories are selectively directed based on their charge-to-mass ratio and physical dimensions. An adjustable aperture modulates the collection efficiency by altering the electric field gradient or flow dynamics to optimize separation across varying particle characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Ionizing air and particles near the entrance, then using an adjustable opening at the exit to control where particles are collected based on their size and charge, enabling size- and charge-dependent separation.

abstract: In a printing apparatus or copier, a vertical portion of a paper path is formed between two flat members. To remove jammed paper from the path, one of the flat members is moved, by a hinge, from the other, releasing any sheet in the path. Released sheets drop down the path and land on a bottom structure. The bottom structure causes a sheet landing thereon to incline away from the hinge, so that a user can remove the sheet without having to reach far into the path.
problem: Removing jammed paper from a vertical paper path in a printing apparatus without requiring the user to reach into the path.
constraint: Ensuring the hinged release and inclined structure work together to safely and effectively clear jams without damaging the paper or apparatus.
mechanism: A hinged release mechanism disengages a jammed item from a constrained path, allowing gravitational or mechanical displacement toward an inclined surface that positions the item in an accessible location. The hinge axis and incline angle are coordinated to ensure the item moves away from the path without requiring manual intervention within the constrained region.
mechanism_raw: Hinged flat members release the jammed sheet, allowing it to drop to an inclined bottom structure that positions the sheet away from the hinge for easy access.

abstract: A writing utensil configurable between retracted and extended configurations is provided. The writing utensil includes a body having an interior volume and an aperture. A reciprocally movable nib assembly is located in the body and includes a nib that, when in the extended configuration, traverses the aperture. To prevent the nib from drying when in the retracted configuration, a sealing element seals the aperture. In an embodiment, the sealing element is a resilient valve element that can be opened by a sleeve slidably engaging the nib assembly. After the sleeve opens the valve, the sleeve slides with respect to the nib assembly to expose the nib. In another embodiment, the sealing element can be a sliding door that is attached to the nib assembly and overlays the aperture. When the nib assembly is moved to the extended configuration, the sliding door slides in a manner that opens the aperture.
problem: Preventing the nib of a retractable writing utensil from drying out when in the retracted position.
constraint: The sealing element must provide an effective seal when closed and open reliably when the nib is extended without interfering with the nib's movement.
mechanism: A sealing element is mechanically linked to a movable component such that the seal closes when the component is in a retracted position and opens when the component is extended. The linkage ensures the sealing element remains engaged during retraction to prevent environmental exposure while allowing unimpeded movement during extension.
mechanism_raw: A sealing element (resilient valve or sliding door) seals the aperture when retracted, opened by the movement of the nib assembly (via a sleeve or sliding door attached to the nib).

abstract: This melt-pourable explosive composition shares explosive properties comparable to those of Tritonal and is melt-pourable and castable under conditions comparable to those of Tritonal, but experiences equal or less impact, shock, and thermal sensitivity and avoids the issues of toxicity associated with trinitrotoluene. The trinitrotoluene component of Tritonal is replaced with one or more mononitro aromatic and/or dinitro aromatic melt-pourable binders, such as dinitroanisole, which can be melt poured without presenting the toxicity drawbacks experienced with the use of TNT. The melt-pourable binder can also be combined with a processing aid selected from the group consisting of alkylnitroanilines and arylnitroanilines. The composition also includes oxidizer particles, which are preferably inorganic oxidizer particles, and a reactive metallic fuel, such as aluminum.
problem: Replacing toxic and sensitive TNT in explosive compositions while maintaining performance and processability.
constraint: Balancing explosive performance, thermal/shock sensitivity, and processing compatibility of the replacement binder.
mechanism: Substitute a component with alternatives that share critical processing and performance properties, enabling equivalent functionality without the drawbacks of the original.
mechanism_raw: Substituting TNT with mononitro/dinitro aromatic binders that share melt-pourable properties, enabling equivalent casting and explosive characteristics without toxicity drawbacks.

abstract: An absorbent printed paper web and methods for making the printed web, the web having a visually discernible larger pattern, which can be a logo, on at least one surface formed essentially only of a paper web and a strengthening, colored bonding material. The printed web having the larger pattern can be made using the same bonding material and process used to print the background pattern. A double recrepe process using an improved Gravure roll may be used to print both logo and background. One method includes using a Gravure roll having deep depressions for printing a geometric background pattern, which can be a cross hatch pattern defining unprinting surface areas between the repeating deep depressions. The Gravure roll can also have shallow depressions in the reverse image of a logo to be printed, where the shallow depressions can have contiguous logo areas much larger than the size of the repeating deep depressions or unprinting surface areas in the background pattern. The shallowly printed regions add strength, and due to interaction with the creping roll and blade, also add bulk and softness to the finished web. The printed web can be printed with a Latex bonding material on one or both web surfaces, not requiring further web printing and compression on a surface after creping. The resulting printed web can carry a product or service logo or trademark, while being strengthened and expanded by the bonding material which also carries the logo or trademark.
problem: Creating a printed paper web with a logo and background pattern that enhances strength, bulk, and softness without additional compression steps.
constraint: Achieving uniform strength, bulk, and softness across the web while avoiding post-creping compression.
mechanism: Use a printing element with variable depth regions to apply material in a pattern where interaction with a subsequent mechanical process creates localized variations in material properties.
mechanism_raw: Using a Gravure roll with deep and shallow depressions to print both background and logo regions with the same bonding material, where shallow regions interact with creping to add localized strength and bulk.

abstract: The carbonization of cellulose fiber fabric comprises an initial stage of heat treatment up to 250° C. to 350° C., with a relatively high mean temperature rise speed of 10° C./min to 60° C./min, an intermediate stage up to 350° C. to 500° C. with a lower mean temperature rise speed of 2° C./min to 10° C./min, and a final stage up to 500° C. to 750° C. with a mean temperature rise speed that is again raised to 5° C./min to 40° C./min.
problem: Controlling carbonization of cellulose fibers to avoid thermal degradation while achieving desired structural properties.
constraint: Optimizing carbonization efficiency while minimizing fiber degradation through staged thermal profiles.
mechanism: Apply a multi-stage thermal treatment with variable heating rates to control decomposition rates and prevent material damage.
mechanism_raw: Applying a three-stage heat treatment with variable temperature rise speeds (high, low, high) to manage thermal decomposition rates and prevent material damage.

abstract: A closed loop dispensing system for use on a liquid container such as a bottle or the like for dispensing the liquid contents from the bottle. The outlet opening of the bottle is closed by a throat plug having a valve positioned therein which is open when the container cap is mounted on the container, but which automatically closes when the cap is removed from the container. An inlet opening is provided in the container insert so that liquid may be drawn therethrough. A closure cap is mounted on the bottle and has a dispensing tube extending therefrom for dispensing liquid from the container to a mixing machine or the like. A check valve is associated with the cap for preventing backflow from the dispensing tube to the container and for permitting liquid flow from the container to the dispensing tube in response to suction being applied to the dispensing tube. A precise discharge metering orifice is provided in the valve body as a substitution for proportioners which are normally located downstream of the dispensing system. A valve permits ambient air to enter the interior of the container as liquid is drawn therefrom. The valve prevents the flow of liquid therethrough.
problem: Enabling precise liquid dispensing from a container without backflow or contamination while maintaining system integrity.
constraint: Ensuring automatic sealing, precise flow control, and ambient air intake without liquid leakage.
mechanism: Combine a valve actuated by cap presence, a check valve for backflow prevention, and a metering orifice to control flow rate without downstream components.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a cap-actuated valve that opens/closes based on cap presence, a check valve for backflow prevention, and a metering orifice to replace downstream proportioners.

abstract: A consolidated cellulosic article of increased thickness and target face density, as well as an apparatus and method of manufacturing same, are disclosed. The apparatus includes first and second dies adapted to move toward one another with a mat of cellulosic material and a binding agent therebetween. When the dies move together, the mat is compressed under pressure and heat with forms on one of the dies forming indentations in the mat. Compression zones of increased density form between the indentations and a first face of the mat. By spacing the forms appropriately, the compression zones overlap, and the first face of the resulting consolidated board is provided with substantially uniform density. Since the entire board is not compressed to the same degree, its overall thickness is enhanced while the density of the first face of the mat is increased, and relatively little material is used.
problem: Increasing thickness and face density of cellulosic articles while minimizing material usage.
constraint: Balancing material efficiency, thickness, and uniform face density without excessive compression across the entire article.
mechanism: Use dies with structured forms to create indentations, generating overlapping compression zones that enhance face density and overall thickness through controlled localized compression.
mechanism_raw: Using structured dies with forms to create indentations, generating overlapping compression zones that enhance face density and overall thickness through controlled localized compression.

abstract: A protective structure for protecting buildings, bridges, roads and other areas from explosive devices such as car bombs and the like comprises: (a) a mesh structure having an outer surface and an inner surface, wherein the inner surface defines an annular space; (b) a concrete fill material which resides within the annular space of the mesh structure and within the mesh structure; (c) at least one reinforcement member which resides within the concrete fill material; and (d) a concrete face material which resides upon the outer surface of the mesh structure. The mesh structure may be made up of, for example, steel wire. A protective system for protecting buildings, bridges, roads and other areas from explosive devices such as car bombs and the like comprises a plurality of the above described protective structures and a plurality of support members, wherein the support members provide interlocking engagement of the protective structures to the support members.
problem: Protecting structures from explosive forces while maintaining structural integrity and adaptability to various surfaces.
constraint: Balancing blast resistance with flexibility to conform to irregular surfaces and allow modular interconnection without compromising structural continuity.
mechanism: A flexible mesh confines a rigid filler material and reinforcement elements, forming a composite that distributes explosive energy across the structure. The mesh allows controlled deformation and force redistribution, while the filler material on the outer surface absorbs and deflects blast waves. Modular interlocking elements enable assembly, transferring loads between units.
mechanism_raw: A mesh structure confines concrete fill and reinforcement members, distributing explosive energy across the mesh-concrete composite. The mesh allows controlled deformation and force redistribution, while the concrete face material on the outer surface absorbs and deflects blast waves. Interlocking support members enable modular assembly, transferring loads between units.

abstract: An apparatus for supporting milk extraction devices includes an elongated elastic strap that is adjusted to frictionally engage a woman's breasts. A pair of slits is formed in the elastic strip and each of the slits is positioned proximate the woman's breasts. The slits support the milk extraction devices therethrough. Each of the slits is a collapsible opening that alternates between a closed position when the milk extraction device is not supported by the slit and a partially opened position when the milk extraction device is supported by the slit.
problem: Supporting milk extraction devices on a wearable strap without impeding insertion/removal or causing discomfort.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient friction to hold devices in place while allowing easy insertion/removal and avoiding pressure points on the body.
mechanism: An elastic strap uses frictional engagement to stabilize against the body, while slits act as collapsible openings that self-seal when devices are removed. The elasticity of the strap and the slit geometry create a dynamic interface that alternately supports and releases devices based on their presence.
mechanism_raw: An elastic strap uses frictional engagement to stabilize against the body, while slits act as collapsible openings that self-seal when devices are removed. The elasticity of the strap and the slit geometry create a dynamic interface that alternately supports and releases devices based on their presence.

abstract: A pound or number sign shaped (#-shaped) die cast sub-frame includes first and second horizontal members and first and second vertical members. The sub-frame has four arm mounting portions provided at four corners thereof, respectively. The arm mounting portion is a die cast part obtained near a communication portion of a runner formed in a die casting machine. Generally triangular bulged portions are formed at junction portions where the first horizontal member meets the first and second vertical members. Each junction portion has increased width. The junction portion is a die cast obtained within a cavity of increased width of the die casting machine. The bulged portion is pierced to provide a hole. The bulged portion having the hole formed therein is to be mounted to a small vehicle component.
problem: Creating a lightweight, high-strength sub-frame for vehicle components using die-casting while minimizing material waste and manufacturing complexity.
constraint: Optimizing die-casting cavity geometry to maximize strength at critical junctions without increasing overall weight or manufacturing costs.
mechanism: A die-cast structure uses geometric protrusions at junctions to locally reinforce stress concentrations. The increased cavity width at junctions allows for thicker material deposition where needed, while the die-cast process enables precise geometry that balances structural support and weight reduction.
mechanism_raw: A #-shaped die-cast structure uses triangular bulges at junctions to locally reinforce stress concentrations. The increased cavity width at junctions allows for thicker material deposition where needed, while the die-cast process enables precise geometry that balances structural support and weight reduction.

abstract: A sub-assembly for a multiple bed unit having an elongate bed rail and a bed end including a pair of spaced, substantially vertical posts affixed to a side of the bed rail. Each of the posts includes a rail connector for receiving a rail of another bed. A multiple bed unit includes a first bed having a pair of bed ends, a side rail and a sub-assembly connected between and supported by the bed ends, and a second bed having a bed end and at least one side rail connected between the bed end of the second bed and the bed end of the sub-assembly of the first bed.
problem: Connecting multiple beds into a stable, modular unit while allowing independent positioning and load distribution.
constraint: Ensuring mechanical compatibility between beds of varying sizes while maintaining structural rigidity under dynamic loads.
mechanism: Vertical posts with rail connectors enable interlocking between beds. The connectors receive rails from adjacent beds, creating a continuous load path. The sub-assembly acts as a bridge between beds, transferring forces while maintaining alignment through the post-and-rail interface.
mechanism_raw: Vertical posts with rail connectors enable interlocking between beds. The connectors receive rails from adjacent beds, creating a continuous load path. The sub-assembly acts as a bridge between beds, transferring forces while maintaining alignment through the post-and-rail interface.

abstract: The present invention comprises a series of embodiments of a swivel cheeked bridle bit wherein the cheek portion, comprising a dee and/or lower or curb rein attachment eye or ring, is separate from the purchase, with the purchase serving as a pintle for the swivel attachment of the cheek portion to the remainder of the bit structure. The upper harness attachment ring, for attaching a curb chain, nose strap, and/or cheek strap to the bit, is immovably affixed to the upper end of the purchase, which in turn is immovably affixed to the mouth bar of the bit. This ensures that the upper ring does not rotate or swivel as the cheek is turned, thus avoiding twisting the ends of the straps attached to the upper ring and precluding turning the edge of the attachment ring and any attached straps into the side of the face of the animal.
problem: Controlling rotational forces in animal harness systems to prevent strap twisting and discomfort without restricting necessary movement.
constraint: Balancing rotational freedom at the swivel joint with fixed alignment at the upper ring to avoid edge pressure on the animal's face.
mechanism: A fixed upper ring immovably attached to the purchase prevents rotation of straps connected to it, while a swivel joint between the cheek and purchase allows independent cheek movement. This decouples rotational forces from the upper straps, directing motion to the swivel point instead of the animal's face.
mechanism_raw: A fixed upper ring immovably attached to the purchase prevents rotation of straps connected to it, while a swivel joint between the cheek and purchase allows independent cheek movement. This decouples rotational forces from the upper straps, directing motion to the swivel point instead of the animal's face.

abstract: This application discloses a control logic for maintaining a proper solution concentration within an absorption chiller. Further, safeguards are added to a system control to ensure robust operation when operated in a co-generation application with a heat source such as a micro-turbine, a reciprocating engine, etc. In such applications, in proper management of the heat flow into the chiller from such sources can result in crystallization of the absorption solution, which would be undesirable. Inventive control logic works to minimize such occurrences.
problem: Preventing crystallization of absorption solution in a chiller due to improper heat flow management during co-generation operation.
constraint: Balancing heat input to avoid both under-concentration (inefficient cooling) and over-concentration (crystallization), while adapting to variable heat source outputs.
mechanism: A feedback-controlled system dynamically modulates heat input from variable external sources to maintain a process fluid's concentration within a safe operating range, using real-time sensing to prevent both under-concentration (inefficient operation) and over-concentration (phase separation or solidification).
mechanism_raw: Control logic dynamically adjusts heat flow input from external sources (e.g., micro-turbines) to maintain solution concentration within safe limits, using feedback to minimize crystallization risk.

abstract: A cargo container of unitary construction surrounds a cargo hold and has an opening into the cargo hold defined by an edge. A flange extends along the edge of the opening and projects into the cargo hold to form a seat. A door having a panel defined by a border covers the opening. A bite extends along the border of the panel and projects away from the panel to contact the seat. When the door is covering the opening, the bite is positioned against the seat and is juxtaposed with the flange. In response to an explosive detonation in the cargo hold, the bite is forced against the seat and transfers the explosive force from the door to the container. If a seal is present on the seat, the bite is forced against the seal to form an airtight lock in the cargo container.
problem: Creating a secure, airtight seal in a cargo container door that can withstand explosive forces without structural failure.
constraint: Ensuring the bite-seat interface maintains structural integrity under extreme pressure while preserving airtight sealing under normal conditions.
mechanism: A structural interface transfers external pressure loads from a closure panel to a supporting frame by mechanically coupling a shaped protrusion on the panel to a complementary surface on the frame, compressing a sealing element between them to maintain airtight integrity under normal conditions while redistributing extreme forces during overload events.
mechanism_raw: A geometrically designed bite on the door panel is forced against a seat (formed by a flange) during an explosion, transferring explosive force from the door to the container structure while compressing any seal between them.

abstract: The invention relates to a pressing tool (8) provided with three or four press mandrels (12, 15) which move towards each other during the pressing process. The press mandrels (12–15) have a roof-shaped transversal profile. The lateral distance (36) between the press mandrels (12–15) is increasingly reduced during the pressing process. An extending element (37) is arranged between two press mandrels, extending from one press mandrel to another press mandrel and being inserted into the other press mandrel during the pressing process. The aim of the invention is to improve said pressing device and to improve pressing. In order to block the above-mentioned distance (36), the extending element (37) is disposed in such a way that both roof edges (38) of the corresponding press mandrels cut across said extending element (37) in an initial position.
problem: Improving pressing efficiency and material deformation control in a multi-mandrel pressing tool.
constraint: Maintaining synchronized mandrel movement and edge interaction to avoid misalignment while achieving uniform pressure distribution during deformation.
mechanism: A pair of shaped elements with overlapping edges move in a coordinated path across a deformable workpiece, mechanically constraining lateral displacement while progressively applying compressive force to ensure uniform material deformation and alignment through synchronized edge interaction.
mechanism_raw: Roof-shaped mandrels with overlapping edges progressively cut across an extending element during movement, mechanically blocking lateral distance reduction to ensure precise material compression and alignment.

abstract: A metering valve for metering dry powder material such as cement. The interior of the valve housing is expanded outward beginning at the sealing surface or lip located adjacent to the inlet opening, thereby forming an enlarged gap between the valve sleeve and housing to discourage powder accumulation in the gap and interference of large bulk particles and foreign materials with the sleeve and housing. An eccentric intermediate sleeve aligns the valve sleeve relative to the housing prior to rotation of the valve sleeve by either moving the valve sleeve away from or toward the valve inlet. The valve sleeve has a rubberized layer to seal with the housing's sealing surface or lip. A sleeve shield blocks entry of powder into the mouths of the vacuum breakers to prevent plugging of the vacuum breakers. Ball bearings are employed to suspend the valve sleeve within the housing, making the valve sleeve easier to rotate.
problem: Preventing powder accumulation and ensuring smooth valve operation in a dry powder metering system.
constraint: Balancing sealing effectiveness (via rubberized surfaces) with particle clearance to prevent clogging and maintain rotational ease.
mechanism: An enlarged internal cavity within a rotating valve body reduces particle entrapment zones, while an offset alignment mechanism and low-friction bearing system enable precise rotational positioning and continuous particle clearance to maintain sealing effectiveness without clogging.
mechanism_raw: An expanded valve housing interior creates an enlarged gap to discourage particle buildup, while an eccentric sleeve and ball bearings enable precise alignment and low-friction rotation of the valve sleeve.

abstract: An apparatus for producing a honeycomb structure having an extruder, at least one cradle and a cutting device comprising a small-gage wire for cutting the honeycomb structure and a notching member; said cradle is provided with a means capable of moving the honeycomb structure extruded from the extruder in the lengthwise direction of the honeycomb structure at nearly the same speed as the extrusion speed of the honeycomb structure, said cutting device is constructed so that the cutting small-gage wire is moved to the honeycomb structure side on the same plane as the plane of stretched small-gage wire, a cutting induction groove is formed on the outer peripheral side surface of the honeycomb structure by the notching member, and immediately thereafter the cutting small-gage wire is positioned in the induction groove, and the cutting small-gage wire is pressed into the honeycomb structure to cut the honeycomb structure.
problem: Achieving precise, synchronized cutting of extruded honeycomb structures without disrupting continuous production.
constraint: Synchronizing material movement, groove formation, and wire cutting to avoid misalignment and ensure clean, continuous cuts during high-speed production.
mechanism: A synchronized transport system moves a continuous extruded structure at matched velocity with its production rate, while a pre-forming tool creates an induction feature in the same plane as a subsequent cutting element, enabling precise, aligned severing without disrupting the production flow.
mechanism_raw: A cradle moves the honeycomb at the same speed as extrusion, while a notching member pre-creates an induction groove, allowing a cutting wire to position and cut accurately in the same plane as the groove formation.

abstract: In order to selectively reinforce portions of a material web, a cutting and laminating device efficiently produces the required reinforcing strips and then laminates them to the web. In order to efficiently and accurately produce these reinforcing strips, a cross web shear is utilized which is capable of cutting required reinforcing strips from the fairly large web of reinforcing material in an accurate manner. Once cut, a holding and positioning device is capable of grabbing onto the reinforcing strip and appropriately positioning it next to the primary material web. A separate laminator can then attach this reinforcing strip to the web at a desired location.
problem: Efficiently and accurately producing and positioning reinforcing strips on a material web without manual intervention.
constraint: Balancing cutting accuracy, positioning speed, and lamination alignment to avoid misalignment or damage to the primary web.
mechanism: A transverse cutting element severs discrete segments from a continuous supply web, a grasping and relocating element positions each segment adjacent to a primary moving web, and a bonding element affixes the segment to the primary web at a predetermined location. The process integrates severing, precise relocation, and bonding in a continuous sequence to automate reinforcement placement.
mechanism_raw: A cross-web shear cuts reinforcing strips from a large web, a holding device grabs and positions the strip adjacent to the primary web, and a separate laminator attaches it at a desired location. The mechanism integrates cutting, precise positioning, and lamination in a continuous sequence to automate reinforcement.

abstract: An embossing method and apparatus (20) comprises a rotary embossing device (32) having a radial direction (28) and an outer peripheral surface (34). The embossing device (32) includes at least one embossing-component (48) which extends at least radially outward from the peripheral surface (34), and is configured to provide for a first embossing-pattern (38). The embossing device (32) also includes a rotary shaft member (46). A base embossing-segment (50) is operatively joined to the rotary shaft member (46) and configured to carry a first base-section (40) of the first embossing-component (48). In a particular aspect, a first, supplemental embossing-segment (52) is operatively joined and selectively positionable on the rotary shaft member (46), and is configured to carry a first supplemental-section (42) of the first embossing-component (48). In other aspects, a first spacing mechanism (56) can adjust a radial position of the first, supplemental embossing-segment (52), and a first, supplemental attachment-mechanism (60) can secure the radial position of the second supplemental embossing-segment (52).
problem: Creating variable embossing patterns on a rotating surface while maintaining precise radial alignment of modular tooling components.
constraint: Maintaining radial precision and structural integrity of the embossing components during adjustment to avoid pattern distortion or mechanical failure.
mechanism: A base tooling segment is fixed to a rotating shaft, and a supplemental tooling segment is selectively positioned and secured along a radial axis via a spacing mechanism and attachment mechanism. This allows dynamic adjustment of the tooling component's radial position to form different patterns without replacing the entire tool.
mechanism_raw: A base embossing segment is fixed to a rotary shaft, and a supplemental segment is selectively positioned and secured radially via a spacing mechanism and attachment mechanism. This allows dynamic adjustment of the embossing component's radial position to form different patterns without replacing the entire tool.

abstract: In a fluid pump and cartridge assembly, a cartridge includes a material inlet port, a material outlet port, and a feed screw. The feed screw delivers fluid to be dispensed from the fluid inlet to the outlet port. The fluid inlet is preferably elongated in a direction along a longitudinal axis of the feed screw to enhance consistency in material flow through the cartridge. The feed screw is preferably driven by a closed-loop servo motor to achieve high-performance dispensing resolution. The assembly is preferably compatible with fixed-z and floating-z cartridges. A optional vented dispense tip, in combination with the fluid pump, allows for repeatable deposit of fillet patterns while maintaining optimal consistency. A dispense controller allows for reverse-compatibility such that the fluid pump of the present invention can be mounted to, and controlled by, conventional pump position controllers.
problem: Achieving high-resolution, consistent fluid dispensing while maintaining compatibility with legacy control systems.
constraint: Balancing dispensing resolution, flow consistency, and backward compatibility with existing controllers to avoid system obsolescence.
mechanism: An elongated inlet port aligned with a feed screw ensures uniform material flow, while a closed-loop servo motor provides precise rotational control of the feed screw. A vented dispense tip and reverse-compatible controller enable repeatable deposits across different systems.
mechanism_raw: An elongated fluid inlet port aligned with a feed screw ensures uniform material flow, while a closed-loop servo motor provides precise rotational control of the feed screw. A vented dispense tip and reverse-compatible controller enable repeatable deposits across different systems.
residual_terms: ["feed screw", "closed-loop servo motor", "vented dispense tip", "reverse-compatible controller"]

abstract: A method for manufacturing carbon-carbon composites includes steps of producing a mat using carbon fiber, carbon fabric, carbon sheet, or staple fiber; laminating at least three layers of mats; producing a preform using the laminated mats with a needle punching method; performing a first thermal treatment process on the produced preform at a predetermined temperature; densifying the first-thermal-treated preform; performing a second thermal treatment process on the densified preform; forming a predetermined shape out of the second-thermal-treated preform; and performing an oxidation resistant treatment process of the shaped preform.
problem: Manufacturing shaped carbon-carbon composites with structural integrity and oxidation resistance through layered material processing.
constraint: Managing thermal expansion, material density gradients, and oxidation resistance across multiple processing stages to prevent delamination or structural weakness.
mechanism: Multiple layers of fibrous material are laminated, mechanically interlocked into a preform, and subjected to sequential thermal treatments (pre-treatment, densification, shaping, oxidation resistance). Each step incrementally builds structural and chemical stability.
mechanism_raw: Multiple layers of carbon fiber mats are laminated, needle-punched into a preform, and subjected to sequential thermal treatments (pre-treatment, densification, shaping, oxidation resistance). Each step incrementally builds structural and chemical stability.

abstract: A wrist training assembly that is intended for use by releasably clamping it to a piano keyboard with a predetermined amount of clamping force. The assembly is releasably locked in place but the clamping and locking functions are separated so that the finish and structure of the piano are protected. The assembly is rapidly installed and uninstalled from a wide variety of pianos without alteration to either the pianos or the assembly. The keyslip of the piano has a first face that faces and is spaced from the keys to define a channel between the piano keys and the first face. A training bar member is mounted to a clamping unit so that it extends a predetermined distance from and generally parallel to the channel. Preferably, two spaced apart mounting hook members are pivotally mounted to the training bar member and adapted to engage with the first face of the keyslip. The clamping unit is moveably mounted to the training bar member and resiliently biased towards the mounting hook member by a predetermined amount of spring tension. The amount of spring tension is pre-selected and is not adjustable by the user. The clamping unit includes a bearing face that is opposed to the mounting hook members and is adapted to bear resiliently against the piano. The amount of spring tension is pre-set at such a level that the bearing face will not mar or distort the piano structure or finish. Once the bearing face is engaged with the piano under the urging of the predetermined spring tension, a releasable detent member is actuated to lock the clamping unit relative to the training bar member and the associated mounting hook members.
problem: Attaching a training device to a piano keyboard without damaging its finish or structure while enabling rapid installation/removal.
constraint: Ensuring the pre-set spring tension is sufficient for secure attachment without exceeding the piano's surface tolerance, while maintaining quick-release functionality.
mechanism: A clamping unit with a spring-biased bearing face applies a controlled, non-adjustable force to the surface, while a separate detent lock secures the position. The clamping and locking functions are mechanically decoupled to isolate force application from locking, preventing over-tightening or surface marring.
mechanism_raw: A clamping unit with a spring-biased bearing face applies a controlled, non-adjustable force to the piano, while a separate detent lock secures the position. The clamping and locking functions are mechanically decoupled to isolate force application from locking, preventing over-tightening or surface marring.

abstract: A two-way flow control valve for repeatedly dispensing a limited amount of liquid. A float valve is linked to a second valve and storage chamber such that one valve is closed when the other is opened, and vice versa. The chamber fills when the float valve is closed, and empties when the float valve is opened. The assembly is useful for dispensing a liquid cleaner into a toilet tank.
problem: Need to repeatedly dispense a precise, limited amount of liquid without manual intervention or external timing control.
constraint: The fill and dispense cycles are inherently linked and cannot occur simultaneously; the dispensed volume is fixed by the chamber capacity and the mechanical timing of the valve linkage, limiting flexibility in dose size.
mechanism: A coupled dual-valve system uses inverse mechanical linkage to create self-cycling fill-and-dispense operation. A level-responsive valve automatically actuates based on fluid presence, and its motion is mechanically coupled to a second valve controlling a chamber. The linkage ensures the two valves operate in complementary phases: when the level-responsive valve closes (stopping fill), the chamber valve opens (enabling dispense), and vice versa. This creates an autonomous cycle where chamber filling and emptying alternate without external control, with dispensed volume determined by chamber capacity and mechanical timing of the linkage.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical linkage couples two valves in a complementary (inverse) relationship: when one valve opens, the other closes, and vice versa. This linkage connects a float valve (which automatically shuts off based on liquid level) to a second valve controlling a storage chamber. The float valve's level-dependent operation drives the second valve, so the system automatically alternates between filling the chamber (when the float valve is closed) and emptying it (when the float valve opens), producing a self-cycling dispense mechanism.

abstract: The present invention relates to a process for the manufacture of a cereal product having an improved protein content and improved baking properties, whereby one mills cereals up to between 50 to 70% with regard to the kernel, that one from a part feed of said flour isolates native gluten and the content of water soluble constituents such as pentosans, that one add the native gluten thus isolated and constituents isolated, such as pentosans, to the remaining feed of flour, that the feed of flour being substantially freed from native protein and soluble constituents is used as such, or is further processed such as being subjected to an enzymatic hydrolysis to obtain a glucose syrup.
problem: Need to produce cereal-based products with controlled protein content and specific functional (baking) properties while maximizing utilization of all grain components.
constraint: The process requires precise control over milling fineness and isolation efficiency to achieve the right balance of recombined components; the tradeoff is between maximizing yield/utilization of the grain versus achieving specific functional properties in the final product.
mechanism: Selective fractionation and controlled recombination of milled material: a portion of milled feedstock undergoes component isolation to extract specific native constituents, while the remaining portion is depleted of those same constituents. The isolated constituents are then recombined with the depleted portion in controlled proportions to achieve target functional properties. The depleted fraction can be diverted to a separate processing path to produce a different product, enabling multi-product output from a single feedstock.
mechanism_raw: Selective fractionation and recombination: a portion of milled grain flour is processed to isolate specific native components (gluten, water-soluble pentosans), while the remaining flour portion is depleted of those same components. The isolated components are then recombined with the depleted portion in controlled proportions to achieve target functional properties. The depleted fraction can be diverted to a separate processing path (e.g., enzymatic hydrolysis) to produce a different product (glucose syrup), enabling multi-product output from a single feedstock.

abstract: This invention is a necklace or bracelet with provisions to prevent the bunching of baubles, bangles and beads which are strung on the necklace or bracelet. Bunching is prevented by keepers which are removably attached to bands fixed at intervals on the strands of the necklaces or bracelets. Two types of keepers are disclosed, one of which has internal threads which interact with a threaded bands, and one which uses a clamshell structure to secure the keeper on a band. The keepers may have a variety of shapes for decorative effects, such as cylindrical, spherical, cubical, or pyramid-shaped.
problem: Need to prevent decorative elements (beads, baubles) from bunching or sliding together into clusters on a flexible strand, while allowing adjustability.
constraint: The keepers must be removable for adjustment but secure enough to stay in place during normal use; the tradeoff is between adjustability (ease of repositioning) and retention force (preventing unintended movement).
mechanism: Removable periodic barriers are positioned at fixed intervals along a flexible strand to maintain spatial distribution of decorative elements. These barriers act as mechanical constraints that prevent elements from accumulating in clusters by physically separating them along the strand. Two attachment mechanisms are provided: one using threaded engagement with the strand, and another using a clamping structure, allowing selective placement and removal for adjustment while maintaining retention during normal use.
mechanism_raw: Removable mechanical constraints (keepers) are positioned at fixed intervals along the flexible strand to physically separate decorative elements and prevent them from accumulating in one area. The keepers act as periodic barriers that maintain distribution of elements along the strand. Two attachment mechanisms are provided: threaded engagement with a band, or a clamshell structure that clamps onto the band, allowing selective placement and removal for adjustment.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method utilizing a MEMS safe arm device for electronically arming and firing a MEMS-scale interrupted explosive train to detonate a main charge explosive. The device includes a MEMS slider assembly housing a transfer charge electrically actuated to move between safe and armed positions of the explosive train.
problem: Need to safely arm and fire an explosive device with electronic control, ensuring it cannot accidentally detonate during handling or transport.
constraint: The mechanism must be miniaturized to MEMS scale while providing reliable mechanical movement and electrical actuation; the tradeoff is between miniaturization and the reliability/force requirements for positive mechanical interlock.
mechanism: A mechanically-actuated interlock physically repositions a transfer element between a safe position (where the explosive train is interrupted, preventing propagation) and an armed position (where the train is complete and ready to fire). Electronic actuation controls the physical movement of the interlock, providing a positive mechanical barrier that must be actively overcome to arm the device. The physical separation of the transfer element in the safe state ensures that accidental electrical signals or shocks cannot complete the explosive train.
mechanism_raw: A mechanically-actuated interlock physically moves a transfer charge between a 'safe' position (where the explosive train is interrupted/disconnected, preventing propagation) and an 'armed' position (where the train is complete and ready to fire). Electronic actuation controls the slider movement, providing a positive mechanical barrier that must be actively overcome to arm the device. The physical separation of the transfer charge in the safe state ensures that accidental electrical signals or shocks cannot complete the explosive train.
residual_terms: ["mechanically-actuated interlock", "transfer element", "explosive train", "electronic actuation", "positive mechanical barrier"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for sequencing articles via a single sort pass or process includes a plurality of article receivers or collators positioned along a conveying or transport path and a plurality of carriages movable along the path. The carriages receive articles from at least one induct in a generally random manner and discharge the articles at the appropriate collators. The collators are operable to selectively receive the articles at an appropriate one of a plurality of bins of the collators, such that the articles are positioned within the bins of the collators in a sequenced manner. The articles may be unloaded to a plurality of collecting devices and/or manually unloaded and placed or stacked in a container in the desired sequence. The collecting devices may be manually unloaded while the collators simultaneously selectively receive articles during a subsequent sort wave or process.
problem: Need to sort and sequence articles efficiently in a single pass, handling random input and producing ordered output with continuous operation.
constraint: The system requires precise coordination of timing between carriages, collators, and unloading operations; the tradeoff is between throughput (single-pass efficiency) and the complexity of synchronization across multiple moving and stationary components.
mechanism: A two-stage buffering and sequencing system decouples random input from ordered output using mobile intermediate buffers and fixed sequencing stations. Mobile carriages pick up articles randomly from input stations and transport them to fixed collators containing multiple bins with selective receiving capability. The collators create a sequencing buffer that arranges articles in the desired order. The system enables overlapping operations—while one set of collators is being unloaded, another set simultaneously receives articles during a subsequent sort wave—allowing continuous processing without stopping for unloading.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage buffering and sequencing system decouples random input from ordered output: mobile carriages act as intermediate buffers that pick up articles randomly from induct stations and transport them to fixed collators. The collators contain multiple bins with selective receiving capability, creating a sequencing buffer that arranges articles in the desired order. The system enables overlapping operations—while one set of collators is being unloaded, another set simultaneously receives articles during a subsequent sort wave—allowing continuous processing without stopping for unloading.
residual_terms: ["mobile intermediate buffers", "fixed sequencing stations", "selective receiving capability", "sequencing buffer", "overlapping operations"]

abstract: A process for manufacturing a label that includes moving a web of a substrate along a first direction, placing a label upon a portion of the web, pressing the label onto the portion of the web so as to attach the label to the portion of the web and diminishing skewing of the portion of the web during the pressing.
problem: Skewing of a substrate web during label attachment in manufacturing processes.
constraint: Balancing pressing force and web movement speed to prevent misalignment without compromising attachment quality.
mechanism: Dynamically coordinating the direction of a moving substrate with a pressing force to counteract lateral displacement, maintaining alignment during attachment by adjusting the relationship between motion and force application.
mechanism_raw: Coordinating the movement direction of the web with the pressing action to dynamically counteract lateral displacement, ensuring alignment is maintained during attachment.

abstract: The present invention provides a highly sensitive screening assay for the identification of peptide binding partners to virtually any peptide or polypeptide ligand. Utilizing an expression-repression readout system, the inventors have screened libraries of peptides and identified relatively small peptide molecules that bind to the provided target.
problem: Efficiently identifying peptide or polypeptide binding partners in large molecular libraries.
constraint: Achieving sufficient sensitivity and specificity in the readout to distinguish true binding events from background noise in complex libraries.
mechanism: Employing a biological readout system where molecular binding directly modulates a detectable signal (e.g., gene expression) to enable high-throughput screening of binding interactions in complex libraries.
mechanism_raw: Using a biological expression-repression readout system where binding of a target molecule directly modulates gene expression, enabling high-throughput screening via detectable signal changes.

abstract: An adaptive saddle and support assembly for use with handicapped, disabled, or injured riders includes a saddle body having a front attachment point and a rear attachment point. The attachment points each can releasably receive a support assembly therein including a vertical support member to which can be attached a torso pad, a pair of forearm pads and a pair of handgrips depending on the needs of the rider.
problem: Providing customizable, adjustable support for riders with varying physical needs.
constraint: Ensuring secure attachment and structural integrity of supports while maintaining ease of reconfiguration for different users.
mechanism: Providing a modular framework with releasable attachment interfaces that allow interchangeable support components to be selectively coupled or decoupled based on user-specific requirements.
mechanism_raw: Implementing modular, releasable attachment points that allow interchangeable support components (e.g., torso pads, handgrips) to be dynamically configured based on rider requirements.

abstract: An even-flow tee arrangement for use with a septic system consists of a tee connector having top and bottom section cemented together. The bottom section includes a splitter plate extending from the tee-shaped exit end to two pairs of directional vanes proximate the entrance end of the tee connector.
problem: Uneven fluid flow distribution in septic system tees leading to inefficient waste processing.
constraint: Maintaining structural robustness of the tee assembly while achieving precise flow control to prevent clogging or channeling.
mechanism: Physically segmenting and redirecting an incoming flow stream using internal barriers and directional elements to enforce uniform distribution across multiple pathways while maintaining structural integrity.
