mechanism_raw: Using a splitter plate and directional vanes to physically segment and redirect incoming flow into multiple controlled pathways, ensuring uniform distribution across the system.

abstract: According to the present disclosure, a propulsion system is provided to assist a caregiver in moving a patient support about a care facility. The propulsion system is detachably coupled to patient support to permit storage of the propulsion system or use of propulsion system on multiple patient supports.
problem: Assisting caregivers in moving heavy patient supports while enabling portability and reuse of the propulsion system.
constraint: Ensuring the coupling mechanism is both secure during operation and quick-release for easy transfer, without compromising power delivery or safety.
mechanism: Designing a detachable power unit with a standardized mechanical and electrical interface that enables secure coupling during operation and rapid transfer between compatible platforms for shared use.
mechanism_raw: Designing a detachable propulsion unit with a standardized coupling interface that allows it to be transferred between multiple patient supports, enabling shared use and storage flexibility.

abstract: A mold for forming blocks with at least one textured surface, the mold comprising a structure defining a cavity open at opposite ends thereof for receiving a block forming material at one of the open ends and discharging a block formed from the block forming material at the other of the open ends; and a continuous web surrounding at least a portion of the structure and movable relative to the structure for acting on the block forming material received within the cavity to impart a texture to a surface of the block, the web being mounted to move around the portion of the structure when the block is discharged from the cavity.
problem: Creating blocks with a textured surface efficiently during molding and ejection.
constraint: The web must move relative to the cavity structure precisely during block ejection to maintain texture consistency without disrupting the forming process.
mechanism: A flexible substrate moves in coordinated motion with a forming cavity during ejection, dynamically interacting with the material being shaped to impart surface texture as the formed object exits the cavity structure.
mechanism_raw: A continuous web moves around the mold cavity structure in synchronization with block discharge, dynamically acting on the forming material to impart texture as the block exits the cavity.

abstract: A material for a shadow mask, characterized in that it has a chemical composition: C=0.0030 wt %, Si=0.03 wt %, Mn: 0.1 to 0.5 wt %, P=0.02 wt %, S=0.02 wt %, Al: 0.01 to 0.07 wt %, N=0.0030 wt %, B: an amount satisfying 0.5≦B/N≦2, and balance: Fe and inevitable impurities, and can form a shadow mask having a coercive force Hc of 90 A/m or less; and a method for producing the material, characterized in that use is made of a raw material having the above chemical composition, the finishing temperature in hot rolling is lower than Ar3 point by O to 30° C., the coiling temperature is 650 to 700° C., and the rolling reduction percentage in the final rolling (secondary cold rolling) is 30 to 45%. The material produced by the method exhibits magnetic characteristics being uniform in a coil and excellent as described above.
problem: Achieving a shadow mask material with low coercive force and uniform magnetic properties.
constraint: Balancing the B/N ratio and processing temperatures to avoid defects while ensuring uniform magnetic characteristics across the material.
mechanism: Adjusting elemental composition ratios and thermal processing conditions to modulate magnetic domain mobility and reduce energy barriers to magnetization reversal.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the chemical composition (e.g., B/N ratio) and processing parameters (hot rolling temperature, coiling temperature, cold rolling reduction) to tailor magnetic domain behavior and minimize coercivity.

abstract: A heat dissipating device incorporating heat pipes is disclosed. The heat dissipating device includes a base, a plurality of heat-dissipating fins and at least one heat pipe. The heat pipe includes an evaporating portion attached to the base, a middle-portion and a condensing portion extending through the fins. Bottoms of the evaporating portion of the heat pipe and the base are coplanar, and the condensing portion extends opposite to the evaporating portion.
problem: Efficiently dissipating heat from a localized source to ambient surroundings.
constraint: Geometric alignment of the heat pipe sections (coplanar evaporating portion, extended condensing portion) to optimize thermal contact and airflow without structural interference.
mechanism: Transferring thermal energy through a sealed two-phase medium, with heat absorption at a localized region and dissipation across an extended surface area via controlled geometric alignment.
mechanism_raw: Heat pipes transfer thermal energy via phase change, with evaporating sections attached to the heat source and condensing sections extending through fins to maximize surface area for heat rejection.

abstract: A purified preparation of primate embryonic stem cells is disclosed. This preparation is characterized by the following cell surface markers: SSEA-1 (−); SSEA-4 (+); TRA-1-60 (+); TRA-1-81 (+); and alkaline phosphatase (+). In a particularly advantageous embodiment, the cells of the preparation are human embryonic stem cells, have normal karyotypes, and continue to proliferate in an undifferentiated state after continuous culture for eleven months. The embryonic stem cell lines also retain the ability, throughout the culture, to form trophoblast and to differentiate into all tissues derived from all three embryonic germ layers (endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm). A method for isolating a primate embryonic stem cell line is also disclosed.
problem: Isolating and maintaining primate embryonic stem cells in an undifferentiated, pluripotent state.
constraint: Ensuring marker expression remains consistent over prolonged culture while preventing spontaneous differentiation or genetic instability.
mechanism: Selecting target cells via specific surface antigen recognition and maintaining cellular identity through controlled environmental conditions that suppress differentiation pathways.
mechanism_raw: Using specific cell surface markers (e.g., SSEA-4, TRA-1-60) to identify and purify target stem cells, combined with culture conditions that preserve karyotype stability and differentiation potential.

abstract: A metal catalyst carrier has a core comprising a corrugated sheet and a flat sheet with a plurality of slots in a shape elongated in a direction perpendicular to a cell passage direction. The slots are formed before a sheet metal is corrugated and have a predetermined interval apart from one another. The plural slots disposed along the direction perpendicular to the cell passage direction are arranged to form a plurality of slot arrays arranged in the cell passage direction, and an interval Y in the cell passage direction and an interval X in the direction perpendicular to the cell passage direction, between the opening peripheral edge portions of the slots adjacent to each other in the slot arrays adjacent to each other, are set under the conditions satisfying X≧0 mm and X≧−(5/2)Y+10 mm, thereby preventing the occurrence of distortions and cracks in the process of corrugating the sheet metal.
problem: Preventing distortions and cracks in corrugated sheet metal during forming processes.
constraint: Slot geometry and spacing must satisfy X ≥ 0 mm and X ≥ −(5/2)Y + 10 mm to balance material flexibility and mechanical strength during corrugation.
mechanism: Introducing precisely spaced discontinuities in a sheet prior to deformation, with geometric constraints on spacing ratios to redistribute localized stresses and prevent failure during forming.
mechanism_raw: Pre-forming elongated slots in the flat sheet at specific intervals (X and Y) before corrugation, with spacing ratios designed to distribute stress and maintain structural integrity during deformation.

abstract: Novel synthetic Arg-Gly-Asp containing peptides which have high affinity and specificity for their receptors by virtue of restrictions on their stereochemical conformation. Such restrictions can be provided by cyclization, by inclusion into a constraining conformational structure such as a helix, by providing an additional chemical structure such as an amide or an enantiomer of a naturally occurring amino acid, or by other methods. In particular, there are provided cyclic peptides having increased affinity and selectivity for the certain receptors over that of linear, Arg-Gly-Asp-containing synthetic peptides.
problem: Improving the binding affinity and specificity of synthetic peptides for their receptors.
constraint: Maintaining conformational stability without compromising other functional or pharmacological properties of the peptide.
mechanism: Constraining molecular geometry through structural restriction to stabilize a target binding configuration, thereby enhancing interaction specificity and affinity while preserving functional properties.
mechanism_raw: Restricting stereochemical conformation of peptides through cyclization, constraining structures, or chemical modifications to lock them into receptor-compatible shapes, thereby enhancing interaction.

abstract: An apparatus is adapted to centrifuge a container for separating a component, such as fibrin monomer, from blood or plasma. The container includes a cylindrical member, and a piston displaceable therein and a tubular piston rod, which extends through a top wall of the cylindrical member. The piston divides the cylindrical member into a first chamber positioned above the piston between the piston and the top wall, and a second chamber positioned below the piston. The apparatus includes a supporting turntable which releasably retains the cylindrical member. The supporting turntable is connected to a first activator for rotating the supporting turntable with the container about the central axis thereof. The apparatus also includes a rotatably journalled piston activating mechanism adapted to activate the piston by a second activator. A heat-emitting device is provided opposite the cylindrical member, and an filter is provided between the heat-emitting device and the cylindrical member to block radiation emitted by the heat-emitting device that degrades protein in the blood or plasma.
problem: Separating blood components (e.g., fibrin monomer) via centrifugation while preventing protein degradation caused by heat-emitting devices.
constraint: Balancing the need for heat (e.g., for process efficiency) with the requirement to protect temperature-sensitive biomolecules from radiation-induced damage.
mechanism: Positioning a selective attenuation barrier between an energy-emitting component and a processing chamber to reduce harmful radiation exposure while permitting the primary separation process to occur.
mechanism_raw: Using a radiation-blocking filter positioned between a heat source and the centrifuge container to selectively attenuate harmful radiation while allowing the separation process to proceed.

abstract: A low profile acoustic array (10) is configured to selectively respond to shear waves while rejecting compression wave energy in the frequency range of interest. One sensor array is configured as a linear strip with a frame segment having at least one longitudinally extending rail and a plurality of sensor elements (20) extending therefrom. These sensor elements have a resilient core and opposing PDVF outer layers configured with opposing polarities onto the core. The linear strip array also includes a pair of separate electrical signal transmission paths. The transmission lines can include a series of undulations formed thereon to help minimize undesired mechanical crossover between sensors. A carrier member can be configured to be detachably releasable carries the discrete sensors to maintain the positional alignment until they are secured to a patient.
problem: Detecting shear wave energy in an acoustic array while rejecting compression wave interference.
constraint: Achieving selective sensitivity to shear waves without sacrificing structural integrity or introducing mechanical interference between adjacent sensors.
mechanism: Using opposing polarized elements to cancel unwanted signal components, combined with mechanical decoupling structures to isolate sensor regions and suppress cross-interference.
mechanism_raw: Employing opposing polarized PVDF layers on a resilient core to cancel compression wave signals, combined with undulating transmission lines to mechanically isolate sensor elements and minimize cross-talk.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method and container for the cultivation of ornamental plants, facilitating the application of the method of drought stress to reduce cell elongation of plants grown in a slowly absorbing material such as peat moss without the use of chemical retarding agents. The invention thus discloses a container for the cultivation of plants comprising a layered structure incorporating a rapidly liquid absorbing reservoir and a body of suitable cultivation substrate. According to an advantageous embodiment a layer is furthermore inserted between said reservoir and said cultivation substrate in order to obtain a controlled flow of liquid from said reservoir to said cultivation substrate.
problem: Controlling plant growth (reducing cell elongation) without chemical retardants by applying drought stress.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient water availability to sustain plant viability while creating enough stress to inhibit excessive elongation.
mechanism: Regulating fluid delivery through a stratified medium to induce controlled stress levels that modulate biological growth responses while maintaining viability thresholds.
mechanism_raw: Using a layered container with a rapidly absorbing reservoir and a controlled-flow layer to regulate water delivery to the substrate, inducing mild drought stress that triggers growth regulation.

abstract: An injection system of a die casting machine giving the necessary casting pressure without adjusting the accumulator side, provided with an injection cylinder including an injection piston linked with the injection plunger and a booster piston arranged behind the injection piston, an accumulator for supplying a pressurized liquid of a predetermined pressure, a liquid pressure circuit for supplying the pressurized liquid from the accumulator to the injection cylinder, driving the injection piston, then driving the booster piston, a control valve for controlling a flow rate of the pressurized liquid discharged from the front side of the injection piston of the injection cylinder so as to control a flow rate of the injection piston, and controlling the pressure of the pressurized liquid at the front side of the injection piston by the timing of closing the control valve to determine the final value of the casting pressure.
problem: Achieving precise casting pressure in a die casting machine without manual adjustment of the accumulator.
constraint: Ensuring consistent pressure delivery across varying operational conditions without requiring real-time manual recalibration of the system.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting fluid control timing through automated feedback to regulate pressure delivery, ensuring consistent output without manual recalibration across varying conditions.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the timing of a valve closure to regulate hydraulic flow rate and pressure, dynamically determining the final casting pressure through automated feedback.

abstract: The present invention relates to a spray head for spreading liquid or semi-liquid products, preferably foodstuff. A product feeder (5) is provided to feed or convey a product (2) through a feed conduit (3) from a product container (4) to the spray head (1) and spraying nozzles (18) are provided to spread the product (2) when it is discharged from the spray head (1). The spray head (1) comprises three separate members, namely an upper coupling member (7), a lower coupling member (8) and a nozzle member (9) provided therebetween. The upper coupling member (7) is connected to the lower coupling member (8) and to the feed conduit (3). The nozzle member (9) and/or the upper coupling member (7) define, when the upper and lower coupling members (7, 8) are interconnected, distributing spaces (13) for distributing product (2). The spraying nozzles (18) of the nozzle member (9) are provided to open and to close. The nozzle member (9) is removable from the upper and lower coupling members (7, 8) when these members have been disconnected from each other.
problem: Enabling effective distribution of liquid or semi-liquid products while allowing easy maintenance or cleaning of the spray head.
constraint: The system must maintain structural integrity and product distribution during operation while permitting disassembly for maintenance.
mechanism: A modular fluid delivery system uses separable mechanical couplings that, when disconnected, allow a nozzle component to be removed for maintenance while interconnected couplings form internal flow channels. The nozzle's operational state is mechanically linked to the coupling connection state, ensuring flow control is coordinated with assembly status.
mechanism_raw: Modular design with separable coupling members and a removable nozzle member. Disconnecting the couplings allows the nozzle to be detached, while interconnected couplings define distributing spaces for product flow. The nozzle's open/close functionality is mechanically linked to the coupling state.

abstract: A paper dispenser includes a reel tube having a lateral opening and a cavity, a central shaft disposed inside the cavity, a set of spring for shaft with one end inserted and fixed on the central shaft while the other end is connected with the beginning end of the reel. The spring set for shaft rotates in accordance with the central shaft and can release paper through the lateral opening or furl paper back to the cavity. An annular leafspring set for the paper roll is installed between the reel tube and the spring set for shaft. When paper is released, the stretching force of the spring set for shaft along radial direction pulls the paper roll out. When the paper roll is curled back to the tube, the compressing force of the spring set for shaft along radial direction provides part of the cavity for receiving paper.
problem: Controlling the extension and retraction of a paper roll in a dispenser without jamming or uneven tension.
constraint: The spring forces must be balanced to allow smooth extension and retraction without over-tensioning or slack in the paper.
mechanism: A dual-spring biasing system applies opposing forces to control the position of a rotatable element: one spring provides outward force to extend the element during dispensing, while a second spring provides inward force to retract the element. An intermediate resilient element between the element and its mounting balances the spring forces to prevent over-tensioning or slack.
mechanism_raw: A spring set applies opposing radial forces: stretching force pulls the paper roll outward during release, while compressing force retracts the roll into the cavity. An annular leafspring between the reel tube and shaft spring balances these forces.

abstract: A method for implementing miniaturization of magnetic random access memory (MRAM) and a magnetic memory using single domain switching by direct current are provided. The magnetic memory preferably includes a half-circle or U-shaped architecture with an exchange biasing pad, such as a FeMn exchange biasing pad that effectively generates a head-to-head magnetization configuration. The magnetic memory also includes nanometer scale notches in order to minimize magnetostatic interaction between a single domain memory element and the spin current sources and to effectively trap the magnetic domain wall. Reading the bit can be carried out by anisotropic magnetoresistance, or by other means of determining the magnetization orientation through resistance measurements, such as a spin valve or a magnetic tunneling junction.
problem: Minimizing magnetostatic interaction between a single-domain memory element and spin current sources in MRAM devices.
constraint: The notches must be precisely sized at the nanometer scale to effectively trap domain walls without disrupting the magnetic state.
mechanism: Geometric constrictions in a magnetic medium physically capture magnetic domain walls, reducing unwanted magnetic interactions between memory elements and current sources. A shaped configuration with an exchange biasing region creates a stabilized head-to-head magnetization arrangement that pins the domain wall in place.
mechanism_raw: Nanometer-scale notches in the magnetic architecture physically trap domain walls, reducing unwanted interactions. The U-shaped or half-circle design with an exchange biasing pad creates a head-to-head magnetization configuration to stabilize the domain wall.
residual_terms: ["notches", "domain walls", "exchange biasing pad", "head-to-head magnetization", "U-shaped or half-circle design"]

abstract: The invention relates to a ventilation system for clothing, in particular preferably watertight sports clothing, consisting of preferably watertight fabric, in which ventilation openings are provided which are covered by shingle-like overlaps of the fabric. In accordance with the invention, the air openings are closed by a flexible, three-dimensionally cross-linked spacer material.
problem: Providing ventilation in watertight clothing while preventing water ingress through the ventilation openings.
constraint: The spacer material must balance flexibility to permit airflow with sufficient resilience to seal the openings under varying environmental conditions.
mechanism: A flexible, three-dimensionally structured material covers openings in a barrier. The material responds to pressure differentials by opening to permit fluid flow when pressure exceeds a threshold and closing to seal the openings when pressure equalizes, maintaining barrier integrity while enabling ventilation.
mechanism_raw: A flexible, three-dimensionally cross-linked spacer material covers the ventilation openings. The material dynamically opens under airflow pressure to allow ventilation and closes when pressure equalizes, maintaining watertightness.
residual_terms: ["three-dimensionally cross-linked spacer material", "ventilation openings", "airflow pressure", "pressure equalizes"]

abstract: A dynamic model of non-linear tuning behavior is used to tune a tunable device. The model quantifies a difference between a tuning characteristic of an ideal device and an actual tuning characteristic of the device. The model adjusts the tuning according to the difference. A method of compensated tuning of tunable device comprises employing a dynamic model of the tunable device to produce a compensated tuning control input to the tunable device during tuning. A tuning compensator for a tunable device comprises the dynamic model that is employed with an input tuning command to generate a compensated tuning command. A tuning-compensated YTF comprises a dynamic model-based tuning compensator and a YTF. A spectrum analyzer having a tuning-compensated preselector comprises a YTF preselector, a frequency converter, a video signal processor unit, a tuning compensator, and a controller. The tuning compensator uses the dynamic model to tune the preselector.
problem: Compensating for non-linear tuning behavior in tunable devices to achieve accurate frequency selection.
constraint: The dynamic model must accurately predict non-linearities and adapt quickly enough to maintain tuning precision under varying conditions.
mechanism: A dynamic predictive model calculates the deviation between desired and actual tuning response, generating a corrected control signal. This model operates within a feedback loop that continuously adjusts the tuning element during operation, compensating for non-linear behavior in real-time to maintain accurate frequency selection.
mechanism_raw: A dynamic model quantifies the difference between ideal and actual tuning characteristics, generating a compensated tuning command. This model is integrated into a feedback loop to adjust the device's tuning in real-time during operation.
residual_terms: ["dynamic model", "non-linear tuning characteristics", "compensated tuning command", "feedback loop", "tuning precision"]

abstract: A crucible is provided that is thermally stable at high temperatures and is suitable for use in the growth of large, bulk AlN, AlxGa1-xN or other nitride single crystals. The crucible is comprised of specially treated tantalum. During the initial treatment, the walls of the crucible are carburized, thus achieving a crucible that can be subjected to high temperatures without deformation. Once the carburization of the tantalum is complete, the crucible undergoes further treatment to protect the surfaces that are expected to come into contact with nitride vapors during crystal growth with a layer of TaN. If the crucible is to be used with a graphite furnace, only the inner surfaces of the crucible are converted to TaN, thus keeping TaC surfaces adjacent to the graphite furnace elements. If the crucible is to be used with a non-graphite furnace, both the inner and outer surfaces of the crucible are converted to TaN.
problem: Creating a crucible that can withstand high temperatures and chemical reactions during nitride crystal growth without deformation or contamination.
constraint: Balancing thermal stability (via carburization) with chemical protection (via TaN coating) while adapting surface treatment to furnace material (graphite vs. non-graphite) to avoid unwanted reactions.
mechanism: Sequential material treatment: first applying a thermal stabilization process to a substrate to enhance high-temperature resistance, then depositing a chemically protective layer to shield against reactive species. The selection of surfaces for the protective layer depends on the environmental context to balance thermal and chemical durability.
mechanism_raw: Sequential material treatment: first carburizing tantalum walls to achieve thermal stability, then coating surfaces with TaN to protect against nitride vapor corrosion. The choice of coating surfaces depends on furnace type to balance thermal and chemical resistance.

abstract: The 17β-(substituted)-3-oxo-Δ1,2-4-azasteroids (I), wherein R1 is C1–C4 alkyl, OR2, wherein R2 is a C1–C4 alkyl radical, or NR3R4, wherein R3 and R4, equal or different, represent hydrogen or a C1–C4 alkyl radical, can be obtained by means of a process comprising cleaving the oxazolidinedione ring present in a 2-(substituted)-3-hydroxyoxazolidinedione of formula (IV), wherein R5 is Br or trichloromethylsulfonyl, and removing the substituent at position 2, to form a double bond at position 1,2. Some compounds (I) are testosterone-5α-reductase inhibitors and can be used in the treatment of hyperandrogenic disorders.
reason: The mechanism is a specific chemical synthesis pathway for steroid derivatives, relying on precise reagents (e.g., Br or trichloromethylsulfonyl) and structural constraints. While the cleavage of the oxazolidinedione ring is a defined step, the process is tightly coupled to the specific molecular structure of the target compounds and lacks a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields.

abstract: In a mobile communication system, the tracking of synchronization is conducted in a stable state even in a multipath environment. A delay profile detector calculates a delay profile a(n) using a despread signal for each processing unit n. A delay profile averaging unit averages a(n) to produce Ave(|a(n)|2). A data symbol detector conducts rake combining of the despread signal using a(n) and Ave(|a(n)|2). According to a(n) and Ave(|a(n)|2, a weighting function unit calculates a representative value representing delay waves. A loop filter generates a control signal in response to the representative value. A clock controller controls a spread code generator according to the control signal.
problem: Maintaining synchronization tracking in mobile communication systems under multipath signal distortion.
constraint: Balancing noise reduction (via averaging) with responsiveness to dynamic signal changes, ensuring the weighting function adapts to varying delay conditions without over-smoothing or lagging.
mechanism: Combining signal distortion analysis, averaging of signal metrics across processing units, and adaptive weighting to compute a representative delay value. This value generates a feedback signal to adjust a signal generation mechanism, enabling synchronization stability despite multipath interference.
mechanism_raw: Combining delay profile detection, averaging of signal strength across processing units, and adaptive weighting to generate a representative delay value. This value drives a control signal to adjust the spread code generator, enabling stable synchronization despite multipath interference.
residual_terms: ["signal distortion analysis", "averaging", "adaptive weighting", "feedback signal", "signal generation mechanism"]

abstract: In a roller device (6,7) for a movable point of frog (1), including a sliding strip (18) and at least one roller (11) and at least one roller bearing (12) fixed to a stationary part of the switch, the roller(s) (11) is/are mounted on an arm (19) of a double-armed lever (10). The pivot bearing (12) of the lever (10) is arranged in a support (13) connected with a stationary part of the switch, wherein the arm (18) facing away from the roller(s) (11), of the double-armed lever (10) is pivotable against a spring (19) with adjustable spring power.
problem: Allowing controlled pivoting movement of a roller in a switch mechanism while maintaining contact and adjustable resistance.
constraint: Balancing spring power to ensure sufficient contact pressure without excessive resistance, allowing smooth pivoting while adapting to varying mechanical loads.
mechanism: A lever-based pivoting system with a central joint mounted on a fixed support. One lever arm holds a contact element, while the opposing arm incorporates an adjustable resilient element, enabling controlled pivoting motion against the resilient force while maintaining contact pressure.
mechanism_raw: A double-armed lever system with a pivot bearing mounted on a stationary support. One arm holds the roller, while the opposing arm is spring-loaded with adjustable tension, enabling the roller to pivot against the spring force while maintaining contact pressure.

abstract: Disclosed are methods for making surface plasmon resonance-capable arrays wherein molecules, such as proteins or nucleic acids, or cells, are adhered to a metal substrate. The metal substrates are modified by depositing an ω-modified alkanethiol monolayer to the substrate and then contacting the ω-modified monolayer with a heterobifunctional linking compound. Biomolecules or cells can then be attached to the heterobifunctional linking compound. Also disclosed are arrays wherein glutathione-containing molecules are immobilized on the substrate and GST-containing molecules are then specifically immobilized onto the substrate, taking advantage of the affinity between glutathione and GST.
problem: Immobilizing biomolecules or cells on a metal substrate for surface plasmon resonance (SPR) arrays without disrupting their functionality.
constraint: Ensuring specific and stable attachment of biomolecules while preserving their activity and avoiding non-specific binding that could interfere with SPR detection.
mechanism: Two-step surface functionalization: first modifying a substrate with a functionalizing agent to create reactive binding sites, then attaching a bridging compound to link the substrate to target molecules. Alternatively, employing a specific affinity interaction between a capture agent and target molecules for selective immobilization.
mechanism_raw: Two-step surface modification: first depositing an ω-modified alkanethiol monolayer to functionalize the metal surface, then attaching a heterobifunctional linking compound to bridge the surface and biomolecules. Alternatively, using glutathione-GST affinity for specific immobilization.

abstract: Processes and materials for phytoremediating water-containing sites which have been contaminated with pollutants such as arsenic, phosphorous, or other metals. Fern plants can be used to accumulate pollutants from contaminated water-containing sites having an aqueous solution, waste water, ground water, surface water, combinations thereof, and combinations of water-containing sites with soils and/or sediments. The fern plants remove pollutants from the water-containing sites, and can be harvested and readily disposed of, or can be treated to recover the pollutant.
problem: Removing pollutants such as arsenic, phosphorous, or metals from contaminated water-containing sites.
constraint: Balancing the plant's pollutant uptake capacity with its growth rate and viability, while ensuring efficient harvesting and disposal/recovery processes.
mechanism: Employing a living organism capable of bioaccumulating dissolved contaminants from a liquid medium, followed by physical removal of the organism to isolate the concentrated pollutants for recovery or disposal.
mechanism_raw: Using plants (e.g., ferns) that naturally accumulate pollutants from aqueous solutions, then harvesting or treating the plants to recover or dispose of the concentrated pollutants.

abstract: A method for creating a picture that has two sides is described. The picture has an image with a bottom layer (2), a white middle layer (3) and a top layer (4). The single image that results, when printed on a transparent medium, presents one image when seen from the front and a different image when viewed from the back, through the transparent medium. The two sided image may be printed on a transparent medium as in FIGS. (2) and (4), or it may be printed on decal material and placed on a transparent object such as a glass as in (6) and (7). Two sided text may be added as in (8), (9) and (10). The two sided image may be combined with other two sided images as in (15) and (16). Two sided decals may be placed on plastic and cut out as in (17).
problem: Creating a single image that displays different visual content when viewed from opposite sides of a transparent medium.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and material properties (e.g., transparency, white layer reflectivity) to maintain distinct images on both sides without overlap or distortion.
mechanism: Stacking a light-transmissive layer, a reflective intermediate layer, and a substrate layer such that the reflective layer enables independent visual content on opposing surfaces through controlled light transmission and reflection.
mechanism_raw: Layering a transparent top layer, a white middle layer (to reflect light for one side), and a bottom layer, such that the white layer enables distinct front/back images through controlled light transmission and reflection.

abstract: A flashing device includes a wearable band having a motion switch for sensing movement of the band and generating a trigger signal in response to the movement, a circuit responsive to the trigger signal to generate an illumination signal, and at least one light which is illuminated in response to the illumination signal.
problem: Automatically triggering illumination in response to movement for wearable or portable devices.
constraint: Balancing motion sensitivity to avoid false triggers while minimizing power consumption and ensuring reliable activation under varying movement conditions.
mechanism: Detecting movement-induced mechanical changes via a sensor, generating an electrical trigger signal that activates a power circuit to energize at least one light-emitting component.
mechanism_raw: A motion switch detects movement of the wearable band, generating a trigger signal that activates a circuit to illuminate at least one light source.

abstract: A filter making apparatus includes a positioning device having a passageway therethrough, with the passageway guiding a continuous flavor element such as a continuous strand of textile material from an inlet of the passageway to an outlet of the passageway. A liquid flavorant is introduced into the passageway at a desired flow rate and the strand of material carries the supplied liquid flavorant out of the positioning device at a rate substantially equal to the desired flow rate. A portion of the passageway can form a bath of the liquid flavorant supplied to the passageway through a separate inlet at approximately atmospheric pressure. A portion of the positioning device guides the continuous strand of material through the bath, or guides the strand to pass along the bottom of the passageway, and the saturated or partially saturated strand of material then exits from an outlet of the passageway to a point in the path of filter tow material that is being converged to form a filter rod.
problem: Applying a controlled amount of liquid flavorant to a continuous strand of material for integration into filter tow.
constraint: Maintaining precise flow rate control and ensuring uniform saturation of the strand without excess liquid that could disrupt downstream filter formation.
mechanism: Immersing a continuous filament in a liquid reservoir under ambient pressure, allowing the filament to extract liquid at a rate proportional to its transit speed, then directing the saturated filament into a converging material stream for integration.
mechanism_raw: Guiding a continuous strand through a bath of liquid flavorant at atmospheric pressure, allowing the strand to carry the flavorant out of the bath at a rate matching the desired flow, then directing the saturated strand into the path of converging filter tow material.

abstract: A waste reducing device, such as a wood chipper, having an infeed chute, a powered feed system, a powered cutting system, a discharge chute, and a safety device including an elongated structure positioned outside of and adjacent to the infeed chute of the wood chipper, the elongated structure movable vertically downward and radially inward towards the infeed chute between a plurality of positions, and an actuator operably connected to the elongated structure, the actuator having a plurality of operable positions corresponding to the plurality of positions of the elongated structure. The plurality of operable positions of the actuator permitting, interrupting, or reversing the motive operation of the powered feed and cutting systems of the wood chipper.
problem: Preventing injury or damage in machinery like wood chippers by interrupting feed/cutting operations when a hazard is detected.
constraint: Ensuring rapid and reliable actuation of the safety structure to intercept hazards while maintaining operational efficiency and avoiding false activations.
mechanism: Positioning a deployable barrier adjacent to a material intake pathway, actuating the barrier to translate into a blocking orientation that physically obstructs the pathway and interrupts powered feed/cutting operations upon hazard detection.
mechanism_raw: An elongated safety structure positioned adjacent to the infeed chute is moved vertically downward and radially inward via an actuator, physically blocking the chute and interrupting the powered feed/cutting systems.

abstract: An object of the present invention is to provide a refrigerant cycle apparatus which can reduce a production cost while hastening equalization of pressure in a refrigerant circuit after a compressor is stopped, the apparatus comprises a bypass circuit which causes an intermediate-pressure area to communicate with a low-pressure side of a refrigerant circuit, a valve device provided to this bypass circuit and a control device which controls opening/closing of this valve device, and the control device constantly closes the valve device but opens it in order to release a flow path of the bypass circuit concurrently with the stop of the compressor.
problem: Equalizing pressure in a refrigerant circuit after compressor shutdown while minimizing production cost.
constraint: Balancing cost reduction (via minimal additional components) with the need for rapid pressure equalization to avoid system inefficiencies or damage.
mechanism: A flow control element that remains closed during normal operation but opens automatically in response to a specific operational state change (e.g., shutdown), allowing a medium at an intermediate pressure to communicate with a lower-pressure region to accelerate pressure equilibration.
mechanism_raw: A bypass circuit with a valve that remains closed during operation but opens automatically upon compressor stoppage, allowing intermediate-pressure refrigerant to communicate with the low-pressure side to accelerate pressure equalization.

abstract: A dispensing device for substances including personal care, cosmetics, and medicinal substances dispenses a metered amount by actuation of a push button which indirectly contacts an advancable shaft, thereby driving a piston to push the substance from a reservoir into an applicator. The device can be operated in one hand of a person and is devoid of any twist or rotation mechanism.
problem: Dispensing a metered amount of substance in one-handed operation without requiring rotational motion.
constraint: Achieving precise metering while maintaining simplicity and eliminating rotational mechanisms for single-handed usability.
mechanism: A linear actuation system that converts direct axial force into controlled volumetric displacement via a translating shaft and piston, eliminating rotational motion to enable single-handed operation.
mechanism_raw: A push button that translates linear motion through an advancable shaft to drive a piston, converting direct axial force into controlled volumetric displacement without twisting.

abstract: A protective film transfer sheet comprises a peelable support and a protective film formed on the support, wherein the protective film comprises a protective layer and an adhesive layer formed on the support in this order and the adhesive layer has pressure-sensitive adhesiveness, the adhesiveness of the adhesive layer being increased upon heating after transferred on the image surface of photo masks, and is curable by exposure to ionizing radiation. The protective film formed by the protective film transfer sheet is excellent in adhesiveness to the image surface of photo masks, mar resistance and resistance to solvents.
problem: Creating a protective film with strong adhesion, mar resistance, and solvent resistance after transfer to a target surface.
constraint: Balancing temporary adhesion for positioning with permanent curing to ensure durability without compromising initial placement accuracy.
mechanism: A dual-stage adhesion system where a pressure-sensitive material transitions from temporary tackiness (via external energy input) to permanent bonding (via post-placement curing), enabling precise positioning followed by durable fixation.
mechanism_raw: A pressure-sensitive adhesive layer that increases tackiness upon heating post-transfer and is subsequently cured via ionizing radiation, enabling temporary adhesion during placement followed by permanent bonding.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method and apparatus for filtering and drying a product. In a preferred embodiment, the apparatus comprises a container having a plurality of porous walls and a plurality of solid walls that divide the container into a plurality of product chambers, a plurality of vacuum chambers, and, preferably, a plurality of heat transfer chambers. Each product chamber shares at least one porous wall with an adjacent vacuum chamber. Each product chamber preferably shares at least one solid wall with an adjacent heat transfer chamber. According to the method of the present invention, a product is introduced into the product chambers, where the product is held while a substance is filtered from the product through the porous walls and the product is dried by reducing the pressure in the vacuum chambers and the product chambers. In a preferred embodiment of the method, a heat transfer fluid flows through the heat transfer chambers to facilitate keeping the product frozen and/or to facilitate faster drying of the product.
problem: Efficiently filtering and drying a product while maintaining its structural integrity (e.g., keeping it frozen).
constraint: Isolating product from vacuum and heat-transfer media while allowing selective interaction (filtration/drying) through porous barriers to prevent contamination or structural degradation.
mechanism: A compartmentalized system with selective barriers (porous and non-porous) that isolates a product from external media (vacuum, heat-transfer fluids) while enabling controlled interaction (e.g., drying, thermal management) through designed permeability and fluid circulation.
mechanism_raw: A multi-chambered container with porous walls separating product chambers from vacuum chambers and solid walls separating heat-transfer chambers, enabling simultaneous vacuum-induced drying and controlled thermal management through fluid circulation.

abstract: A stencil used for printing solder paste on a contact pad of a printed wiring board has interior surfaces that define one or more apertures through the stencil. Those interior surfaces are coated with a material, such as parylene, having a lower surface tension than the interior surfaces absent the coating. The stencil can also have one or more reverse-tapered apertures passing there through, wherein the apertures have a variable cross-section that is larger at the fill side of the stencil (i.e., where solder paste enters the apertures) than at the board side of the stencil (i.e., where the stencil contacts the contact pad of the printed wiring board). Solder paste can be printed through the aperture(s) of the stencil onto contact pads on a printed wiring board.
problem: Improving solder paste deposition accuracy and consistency during stencil printing on circuit boards.
constraint: Optimizing paste release and fill efficiency while preventing clogging or uneven deposition through geometric and surface-energy modifications.
mechanism: A surface modification and geometric design approach that alters flow dynamics and release characteristics by applying a lower-surface-tension coating to aperture interiors and using reverse-tapered geometries to control material deposition and prevent clogging.
mechanism_raw: Coating stencil aperture interior surfaces with a lower-surface-tension material (e.g., parylene) and using reverse-tapered apertures (wider at the fill side, narrower at the board side) to control paste flow dynamics and release.

abstract: An automated transaction machine including an extensions for financial services (XFS) layer is provided. An application interface portion of the XFS layer is operative to communicate with an application layer of the ATM which may include terminal applications. A hardware interface portion of the XFS layer is operative to communicate with a hardware layer of the ATM which may include hardware devices of the ATM and associated service providers. A diagnostic application is operative to determine whether problems exist in the application layer or the hardware layer of the ATM by causing a plurality of hardware devices to perform predefined operations using the XFS layer and by monitoring the operations. The diagnostic application is operative to output a determination as to whether a problem with the ATM is associated with the components of the application or hardware layers of the ATM responsive to the success or failure of the operations.
problem: Diagnosing faults in a multi-layered automated system (e.g., ATM) where issues could originate in either software/application layers or hardware components.
constraint: Maintaining compatibility with existing application and hardware layers while ensuring the diagnostic process does not disrupt normal system operation.
mechanism: Using a standardized interface layer to decouple application and hardware layers, enabling independent testing of each layer by commanding hardware devices to perform predefined operations and monitoring their success/failure to isolate the source of faults.
mechanism_raw: Using a standardized interface layer (XFS) to decouple application and hardware layers, enabling independent testing of each layer by commanding hardware devices to perform predefined operations and monitoring their success/failure to isolate the source of faults.

abstract: A method for making a crystallized ceramic body containing a two phase composite comprising an alpha prime SiAlON phase that contains ytterbium and a beta prime SiAlON phase, the process includes the steps of: blending together a starting powder mixture that upon densification forms the SiAlON ceramic, the starting powder includes at least about 70 weight percent silicon nitride powder wherein the silicon nitride powder contains beta silicon nitride in an amount less than or equal to about 1.6 weight percent of the silicon nitride powder, and the starting powder further including one or more powders that contribute aluminum, oxygen, and nitrogen to the beta prime SiAlON phase and aluminum, oxygen, nitrogen and ytterbium to the alpha prime SiAlON phase; and densifying the starting powder mixture to form a densified SiAlON ceramic; and heat treating the densified ceramic body so as to form the crystallized ceramic body wherein the alpha prime SiAlON phase comprises at least about 20 weight percent of the two phase composite.
problem: Creating a two-phase SiAlON ceramic composite with controlled phase proportions (alpha prime and beta prime) to achieve specific mechanical or thermal properties.
constraint: Balancing the weight percentages of starting powders and processing parameters to achieve the desired phase distribution without compromising densification efficiency.
mechanism: Controlling the starting powder composition and applying sequential densification and heat treatment to drive phase formation, ensuring a specific phase constitutes at least a threshold percentage of the composite.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the starting powder composition (e.g., limiting beta silicon nitride content) and applying sequential densification and heat treatment to drive phase formation, ensuring the alpha prime phase constitutes at least 20% of the composite.

abstract: A vacuum cleaner includes a housing and at least one running roller operatively connected to the housing. The roller has a hub, a running ring, a wall connecting the running ring and the hub. The wall has two side surfaces and a curved cross-section between the running ring and the hub. The roller has at least one reinforcing rib extending at least from one of the two side surfaces of the wall and being in contact with neither the hub nor the running ring in a non-loaded state of the running roller. The roller forms an elastic caster with a nave and a bearing race. The nave and the bearing race are connected to another by an S or Z-shaped curved wall. Ribs are provided for reinforcing the wall or the nave.
problem: Designing a durable, elastic caster roller for a vacuum cleaner that can withstand mechanical stress while maintaining flexibility.
constraint: Optimizing rib placement and wall curvature to reinforce the structure while preserving the roller's ability to deform elastically under load.
mechanism: Incorporating a curved structural element between a central hub and bearing race to distribute stress, combined with reinforcing ribs that do not contact adjacent components in a non-loaded state to provide structural support without restricting elasticity.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating an S/Z-shaped curved wall between the nave and bearing race to distribute stress, combined with reinforcing ribs that contact neither the hub nor the running ring in a non-loaded state to provide structural support without restricting elasticity.

abstract: In the present battery apparatus for a vehicle, a temperature detecting plate 30 is fixed outside a casing 10 accommodating a plurality of secondary batteries 20. The casing 10 is provided with ventilation holes 15 for cooling the secondary batteries 20 between the secondary batteries 20 and the temperature detecting plate 30. The temperature detecting plate 30 fixes temperature sensors 50 on an insulation substrate 31. The insulation substrate 31 has air holes 33 communicated with the ventilation holes 15 of the casing 10, and a communicating portion 34 is provided between the air holes 33. The temperature sensor 50 is fixed to the communicating portion 34, and thereby the temperature sensor 50 is located so as to have access to a surface of the secondary battery 20 via the ventilation hole 15.
problem: Accurately monitoring the temperature of individual batteries in a tightly packed battery array without compromising the structural integrity or cooling efficiency of the system.
constraint: Ensuring sensor placement does not obstruct airflow or weaken the casing while maintaining reliable thermal coupling to the battery surfaces.
mechanism: Positioning temperature sensors on an external substrate with openings aligned to airflow pathways, allowing sensors to access target surfaces via the airflow paths for direct thermal contact without obstructing ventilation.
mechanism_raw: Positioning temperature sensors on an external insulation substrate with air holes aligned to the casing's ventilation holes, allowing sensors to access battery surfaces via the ventilation pathways for direct thermal contact.

abstract: According to one embodiment of the invention, a system for curing a composite material includes an oven having an inner wall defining an inner chamber, an outer wall defining an outer chamber between the inner wall and the outer wall, a hot air distribution manifold disposed within the inner chamber, a cold air distribution manifold disposed within the outer chamber, and an exhaust chimney having a cold air distribution conduit disposed therein coupled to the outer chamber. The system further includes a hot air supply system coupled to the hot air distribution manifold of the oven that is operable to supply hot air to the hot air distribution manifold, a cold air supply system coupled to the cold air distribution manifold and the cold air distribution conduit that is operable to supply cold air to them, and a plurality of hot air exhaust passages formed in the inner wall of the oven. The hot air exhaust passages are adapted to transport hot air within the inner chamber to the outer chamber.
problem: Achieving uniform temperature control during the curing of composite materials in an industrial oven, particularly managing heat distribution to avoid overheating or uneven curing.
constraint: Balancing the flow rates and temperatures of hot and cold air systems to maintain uniform curing conditions while minimizing energy consumption.
mechanism: Using a dual-chamber design with separate airflow distribution systems, coupled with transfer passages in an inner wall to move heated fluid to an outer chamber, enabling precise regulation of airflow and temperature gradients.
mechanism_raw: Using a dual-chamber design with separate hot and cold air distribution manifolds, coupled with exhaust passages in the inner wall to transfer hot air to the outer chamber, enabling precise regulation of airflow and temperature gradients.

abstract: The present invention relates to sulfur dye protection systems and compositions and methods employing same, as well as processes for making sulfur dyes, especially bleach stable sulfur dyes, processes for dying textiles with sulfur dyes and textiles dyed by such processes. More particularly, the present invention relates to modifying existing dyes and/or making newly formed sulfur dyes. Even more particularly, the present invention relates to materials that can chemically or physically interact with sulfur dyes to protect the sulfur dyes from oxidation by oxidizing agents, such as bleaching agents.
problem: Protecting sulfur dyes from degradation caused by oxidation during bleaching or other chemical exposure.
constraint: The protective interaction must not interfere with the dye's intended colorfastness or application properties while maintaining bleach stability.
mechanism: A substance forms a protective layer through chemical or physical interaction with target molecules, creating a barrier that blocks reactive agents from directly attacking the molecules while preserving their functional properties.
mechanism_raw: Materials that chemically or physically interact with sulfur dyes to form a protective barrier, preventing oxidizing agents from directly attacking the dye molecules.

abstract: A coupling device (11) between a rotor of a synchronous permanent-magnet motor and a working part (17), being advantageously able to ensure an unusual silentness, comprises a driving member (22), being eccentric with respect to the rotor rotation axis and integral with a first motion transmission component, and a driven element (24), being also eccentric with respect to the rotor rotation axis and integral with a second motion transmission component which is kinematically positioned in series with the previous one, said driving (22) and driven (24) members being placed on different non interfering parallel planes inside a tight chamber (18), said driving (22) and driven (24) members being operatively connected through kinematic connection means (25) whose axial dimension interferes with said parallel planes in said chamber (18), said kinematic connection means (25) comprising at least one elastic element (25a) being compressed in said chamber (18) between a bottom wall (19a) and a closing tight cover (19b).
problem: Achieving silent operation in a coupling device between a motor rotor and a working part without compromising mechanical transmission efficiency.
constraint: The elastic element must maintain sufficient compression to dampen vibrations while allowing kinematic connection without axial interference between the parallel planes.
mechanism: Eccentrically mounted driving and driven members on non-interfering parallel planes are connected by an elastic element compressed within a sealed chamber. The elastic element absorbs vibrational energy and converts it into controlled mechanical motion, maintaining kinematic connection without axial interference.
mechanism_raw: Using eccentrically mounted driving and driven members on non-interfering parallel planes connected by an elastic element compressed within a sealed chamber, which absorbs vibrational energy and converts it into controlled mechanical motion.
residual_terms: ["eccentrically mounted", "parallel planes", "elastic element", "vibrational energy", "controlled mechanical motion"]

abstract: A failure diagnostic device for an exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) apparatus, which can detect an intake pipe pressure at a high accuracy with a simple control and can prevent false diagnosis of an EGR system. If at least either one of first and second off-mode intake pipe pressures P1off, P2off exceeds a cancel determination value K, an ECU determines that the intake pipe pressures P1off, Pon and P2off are not properly detected, and cancels the failure diagnosis of the EGR system. Therefore, the false diagnosis of the EGR system can be avoided with a simplified process without requiring specific determinations on individual abnormal states of the various components other than the EGR system. By setting the cancel determination value K based on the intake pipe pressure P resulting when EGR off-control is executed in a state of an EGR valve being stuck in a fully-open position, each improperly-detected intake pipe pressure can be excluded with reliability.
problem: Accurately diagnosing failures in an exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system without false positives caused by sensor inaccuracies or unrelated component faults.
constraint: The cancel determination value must be derived from a specific failure state (fully open EGR valve) to ensure reliable exclusion of improperly detected pressures without requiring individual checks of all system components.
mechanism: A reference threshold is derived from a known failure state (fully open valve) and used to invalidate sensor data exceeding it. This excludes unreliable measurements from the diagnostic process by comparing real-time readings against the threshold.
mechanism_raw: Setting a cancel determination value based on known pressure readings when the EGR valve is stuck fully open, then using this threshold to invalidate sensor data that exceeds it, thereby excluding unreliable measurements from the diagnostic process.

abstract: A time-analog-to-digital converter (TAD) utilizes a time-to-digital approach for analog-to-digital conversion. The TAD includes two voltage-to-delay converters (VDCs), e.g., CMOS inverter chains, in order to increase the dynamic range of the TAD. Each VDC can handle a different range of input voltages. Comparators compare the input signal voltage to reference voltages corresponding to the different ranges of input voltage and a selector selects one of the VDC line outputs based on the range in which the input signal lies. A filter estimates the input signal voltage from a delay signal from the selected output.
problem: Extending the dynamic range of a time-analog-to-digital converter (TAD) to handle input voltages across multiple ranges without sacrificing resolution or accuracy.
constraint: Each VDC must be optimized for its specific voltage range, and the selection logic must ensure seamless transition between ranges without introducing discontinuities or requiring complex calibration.
mechanism: Two signal converters with distinct input ranges are selectively activated via comparators and a selector based on the input signal's magnitude. The selected converter's output is filtered to estimate the input voltage, enabling seamless range transitions without discontinuities.
mechanism_raw: Using two voltage-to-delay converters (VDCs) with different input voltage ranges, selecting the appropriate VDC output via comparators and a selector based on the input signal's range, then filtering the delay signal to estimate the input voltage.

abstract: A spring assist folding knife and method of biasing a blade in a folding knife. The folding knife includes a blade, liner, and handle. The blade includes a first recess for receiving a pivot pin. The blade includes a second recess offset from the axis of rotation. A latch cam having an offset pin is located relative to the second recess. The liner includes an arcuate slot in which the offset pin of the latch cam is located. The arcuate slot within the liner or handle also includes a convex extension. A spring is configured to provide a force in the direction of blade opening and provides the force throughout the entire range of blade motion. The spring applies its force to the offset pin to bias the blade in the closed position until the blade reaches a predetermined angle. Then the spring biases the blade to the open position.
problem: Providing consistent biasing force to a folding knife blade throughout its entire range of motion, transitioning from closed to open position without manual intervention.
constraint: The spring must maintain sufficient force throughout the blade's motion, and the offset pin and slot geometry must ensure a smooth transition between closed and open biasing states without binding or excessive friction.
mechanism: A spring applies force to an offset pin constrained within an arcuate slot. The geometry of the pin-slot interaction causes the spring's force direction to reverse at a predetermined angular position, biasing the moving part closed before that position and open beyond it.
mechanism_raw: A spring applies force to an offset pin on a latch cam, which interacts with an arcuate slot in the liner. The spring's force direction changes at a predetermined blade angle due to the geometry of the offset pin and slot, biasing the blade closed until that angle, then open beyond it.

abstract: Storage devices in accordance with embodiments of the present invention, and systems utilizing such storage devices, can allow for archival of various articles, particular planar articles such as electronic media, records, papers, etc. Such a storage device can comprise a sleeve having a pocket for receiving said article and one or more tabs connected with the sleeve. In some embodiments, said one or more tabs can be removably connected with the sleeve, while in other embodiments, multiple sleeves can have one or more tabs formed in various shapes, sizes, and/or colors and arranged in varying positions along an edge of the sleeve. A system utilizing such storage devices can allow for archival of various articles such that the location of an article can be readily identified by identifying one or more tabs connected with the corresponding sleeve.
reason: The patent describes a labeling system using physical tabs to identify article locations, but this is a product feature rather than a causal mechanism. The 'mechanism' is merely a direct labeling method without a deeper functional relationship.

abstract: A single bat carrier that can be used conveniently in a baseball or softball game to carry and transport a user's bat is disclosed in the present invention. The single bat carrier comprises a bat bag made of Denier nylon with a closed bottom end, a heavy-duty plastic tube inserted into the bat bag to prevent any damage to the bat, a top end cap assembly with a hinge means that fastens to the plastic tube to cover the top opening, a zipper for connecting the end cap and the nylon bat bag, another end cap glued to the bottom side of the plastic tube to hold the bat, a plurality of nylon straps for carrying purposes and for holding a baseball or softball glove, and a snap hook for fastening the single bat carrier to a fence.
reason: The patent lists components of a bat carrier (e.g., plastic tube, straps, end caps) but does not describe a causal mechanism. The solution is a product design combining parts, not a transferable functional principle.

abstract: This disclosure provides a valve which is controlled by a magnetic actuator. More specifically, the actuator is a polarized, magnetic actuator, that is, a magnetic actuator containing both a permanent magnet and an electromagnet. The actuator can be an inexpensive commercial relay having a pivoting armature that pushes a compliant diaphragm against a valve seat to close the valve. Preferably, the armature is configured as a “see-saw,” such that as the valve is opened, an opposing end of the see-saw also displaces the diaphragm. In this manner, fluid pressure in a valve chamber is relatively constant, and there are no significant pressures which prevent the valve from opening and closing. The preferred application of the valve is to actively drive printer ink supply, such that ink can be selectively drawn using the valve from a remote ink supply into a local ink reservoir, mounted near a print head. A sensor at the local reservoir is used to detect air or low pressure, and causes the valve to open and draw more ink into the local reservoir.
problem: Controlling fluid flow in a valve while maintaining pressure balance to avoid resistance during opening/closing.
constraint: The system must balance pressure across the valve chamber to ensure smooth actuation without hysteresis or pressure-induced sticking.
mechanism: Use a pivoting element with opposing ends to displace a flexible barrier against a sealing surface. As one end actuates the barrier to open a passage, the opposing end responds to fluid pressure changes, maintaining pressure equilibrium within the chamber and preventing pressure-induced resistance during operation.
mechanism_raw: A see-saw armature with opposing ends displaces a compliant diaphragm against a valve seat. As one end opens the valve, the opposing end compensates for fluid pressure changes, keeping chamber pressure constant and preventing pressure buildup that would impede operation.

abstract: This invention provides methods of retentate chromatography for resolving analytes in a sample. The methods involve adsorbing the analytes to a substrate under a plurality of different selectivity conditions, and detecting the analytes retained on the substrate by desorption spectrometry. The methods are useful in biology and medicine, including clinical diagnostics and drug discovery.
problem: Separating and detecting analytes in a sample with high resolution and specificity.
constraint: The method requires precise control over selectivity conditions to ensure distinct separation phases without cross-contamination or loss of analytes.
mechanism: Capture target substances onto a surface under varying binding conditions to exploit differential affinity, then release and identify retained substances. Sequentially altering the binding conditions enables staged separation of components with high specificity.
mechanism_raw: Adsorbing analytes onto a substrate under varying selectivity conditions (e.g., different chemical environments) to exploit differential binding, then desorbing and detecting retained analytes via spectrometry. The changing selectivity conditions enable sequential separation of components.

abstract: A drop away leaf pivot unit for use with a clamp in a manufacturing environment. The drop away leaf pivot unit includes a body having a plurality of orifices therethrough and a chamber defined therein. A base member is connected to the body at one side thereof. The pivot unit includes a cylinder extending from an end of the body with a cylinder having a piston and piston rod therein. A spline shaft is rotatably supported by the body and has a drive link engaged therewith. The drive link is also connected to the piston rod on the opposite end. At least one stop member is engaged with the shaft on an end. The drop away leaf pivot unit also includes an arm secured to the shaft on an outer portion of the shaft, outside of the body of the pivot unit. A cover plate is secured to both ends of the body to ensure an enclosed operating environment for certain components of the pivot unit.
problem: Converting linear motion from a pneumatic/hydraulic cylinder into controlled rotational motion for a pivot mechanism in manufacturing clamps.
constraint: The system must maintain an enclosed operating environment to protect components while allowing the spline shaft to rotate freely under load.
mechanism: Convert reciprocating motion into rotational motion using a linkage that engages a splined shaft. The linear actuator drives the linkage, which rotates the shaft through mechanical engagement. A limiting element constrains angular travel, and an external linkage transfers the rotational output to a clamping mechanism within an enclosed environment.
mechanism_raw: A piston rod connected to a drive link engages a spline shaft. Linear motion of the piston rotates the spline shaft via the drive link, enabling precise angular displacement. A stop member limits rotation, and an external arm transfers motion to the clamp.
residual_terms: ["splined shaft", "mechanical engagement", "reciprocating motion", "rotational motion", "limiting element", "enclosed environment"]

abstract: The present invention is a filter cartridge with integrated inhalation and exhalation valves. The exhalation valve integrated into the filter cartridge prevents unfiltered air from being inhaled. The inhalation valve(s), also integrated into the filter cartridge, effectively reduces the dead space inside the filter cartridge and thereby limits re-breathing of carbon dioxide.
problem: Preventing re-breathing of exhaled carbon dioxide and inhalation of unfiltered air in respiratory filtration systems.
constraint: Balancing valve effectiveness to ensure unidirectional airflow while minimizing dead space and maintaining filtration efficiency.
mechanism: Directional airflow control using integrated valves that minimize dead space during inhalation and block unfiltered air ingress during exhalation, ensuring unidirectional flow while maintaining filtration integrity.
mechanism_raw: Integrated inhalation and exhalation valves within the filter cartridge control airflow direction, with inhalation valves reducing dead space to limit CO2 re-breathing and exhalation valves blocking unfiltered air ingress.

abstract: A process is disclosed to treat the protein hydrolysate, prepared conventionally from a proteinous source, with alkyl halide to obtain alcohol which is subsequently oxidized to obtain aldehyde under certain specified conditions, thereby converting large protein molecules into aldehyde based industrial products of much smaller molecular size.
problem: Converting large protein molecules into smaller, industrially useful aldehyde-based products.
constraint: Controlling reaction conditions (e.g., temperature, reagent ratios) to achieve targeted molecular size reduction without over-degradation of the product.
mechanism: Sequential chemical modification through alkylation followed by oxidation to reduce molecular size of protein hydrolysates into aldehyde-containing products, with controlled reaction parameters to prevent over-degradation.
mechanism_raw: Chemical modification via alkylation with alkyl halides followed by oxidation to break down protein hydrolysates into smaller aldehyde-containing molecules.

abstract: The present invention particularly relates to a newly identified murine genomic polynucleotide that encodes an ortholog of the human P2T receptor which is expressed at high levels in the central nervous system, the use of such polynucleotides and polypeptides, as well as the production of such polynucleotides and polypeptides. The invention relates also to identifying compounds which may be agonists, antagonists and/or inhibitors of P2T, and therefore potentially useful in therapy.
reason: The patent describes a specific biological discovery (murine P2T receptor ortholog) and its use in drug screening, but does not present a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a problem outside its immediate biological context.

abstract: An integrated circuit preferably to be connected to a motor vehicle battery is selectively switchable between sleep and normal operating modes. The IC may include a useful control logic circuit, a wake-up circuit evaluating an input signal and responsively outputting a wake-up signal dependent on the input signal, and an input control and supply circuit connected between the wake-up circuit and the control logic circuit. The wake-up circuit includes at least one recognition circuit having an amplifier arrangement to selectively amplify the input signal, and an evaluation circuit having a switch arrangement controlled by the amplified signal and an amplifier producing the output signal. The wake-up circuit has a very low current consumption while monitoring the input signal, and produces the wake-up signal only if the input signal suitably exceeds or falls below a specified voltage threshold. The wake-up signal may activate the control circuit, which may activate the logic circuit.
problem: Managing power consumption in integrated circuits, particularly in battery-powered systems like motor vehicles, by enabling low-power monitoring and selective activation.
constraint: Maintaining ultra-low power consumption during monitoring while ensuring reliable activation of the main circuit when the threshold is crossed.
mechanism: Ultra-low power monitoring of an input signal using a threshold-triggered switch that decouples active operation from continuous monitoring, enabling selective activation of main circuits only when the signal exceeds a defined voltage level.
mechanism_raw: A wake-up circuit with a low-current amplifier monitors an input signal and triggers a switch arrangement to activate the main control logic only when the signal exceeds a voltage threshold, decoupling monitoring from active operation.

abstract: An ESD protection circuit includes a detection circuit for detecting an ESD current and a bypass circuit for bypassing the ESD. The detection circuit and bypass circuit are connected to a first pad and a second pad. The bypass circuit is connected to an output terminal of the detection circuit. The bypass circuit comprises a MOS transistor, a first bipolar transistor and a second bipolar transistor. The drain of the MOS transistor, the collectors of the first bipolar transistor and the collector of the second bipolar transistor are connected to the first pad. The source and the substrate of the MOS transistor and the emitter of the second bipolar transistor are connected to the second pad. The base of the first bipolar transistor is connected to the gate of the MOS transistor and the emitter of the first bipolar transistor is connected to the base of the second bipolar transistor.
problem: Protecting electronic circuits from damage caused by electrostatic discharge (ESD) events.
constraint: Balancing rapid response time and high current-handling capacity of the bypass path without introducing parasitic effects that could interfere with normal circuit operation.
mechanism: Transient voltage spike detection coupled with a low-resistance bypass path to divert electrostatic discharge current away from protected circuits, balancing rapid response and current-handling capacity without interfering with normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A detection circuit identifies ESD current, and a bypass circuit using MOS and bipolar transistors creates a low-resistance path to shunt the ESD current away from the protected circuit.

abstract: In one aspect, a food thawing cabinet includes at least one thawing chamber and one or more wall blowers and a heater for producing a controlled high volume of air flow over food product, with the heater controlled in a cyclic manner. In another aspect, various advanced control techniques for controlling heat input are provided in an effort to lower the time required to thaw frozen food products in a safe manner.
problem: Thawing frozen food products quickly while maintaining safety and preventing overheating or uneven thawing.
constraint: Balancing thawing speed against food safety requirements to avoid bacterial growth or texture degradation.
mechanism: Modulating thermal energy delivery through cyclic activation of a heating element combined with directed fluid flow across a target surface, enabling rapid yet controlled material processing by dynamically balancing energy input and preventing localized thermal damage.
mechanism_raw: Cyclic control of a heater combined with high-volume airflow over food products to modulate heat input, enabling rapid yet safe thawing by balancing thermal energy delivery and preventing localized overheating.

abstract: An improved handgrip and stirrup support device for bareback horse riding. The device comprises a handgrip having opposing arms to which are attached at an angle side members having openings therein.
