The handgrip is improved by being made generally straight and elongated and by having ridges formed into the handgrip. The handgrip is further improved by having opposing arms to increase the elevation of the handgrip over the side members. The side members are improved by having a greater surface area. The openings in the side members are improved so that a hand can enter the openings to adjust a girth and so that a breastplate can be attached to the device. The improvements enable the device to be used with any horse and increase the security and comfort of the device for both the horse and the rider. In another embodiment, the rigid handgrip is removably secured to the flexible riding pad by the stirrup straps wherein the assembled combination can be integrally manipulated as a unit like a more traditional saddle.
reason: The patent describes ergonomic and structural improvements to a handgrip and stirrup device, focusing on component geometry and adjustability rather than a causal functional mechanism that can be abstracted to other fields.

abstract: According to one exemplary embodiment, a turret-type winder is provided and includes a rotatable turret assembly having a first core and a second core supported thereby. The turret is rotatable so that the first core can be positioned at a first location while the second core is positioned at a different second location, and the web material can be wound onto either of the first and second core at either of the first and second locations. The winder includes a pack roll assembly associated with each of the first and second cores, with the pack roll assembly including one pack roll that is pivotably movable into contact with a winding roll. The present winder is configured such that each of the first and second cores is unloaded at the first location after the winding is completed thereon and a new core is loaded at the same first location, while the other of the first and second cores is continuously winding at the second location.
problem: Enabling continuous winding of web material without stopping for core replacement or reloading.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between core switching and winding operations to avoid downtime or material slack.
mechanism: A dual-position rotating mechanism holds two processing elements at distinct locations, enabling one element to remain active during material handling while the other is prepared for subsequent use, maintaining continuous operation through alternating engagement and preparation phases.
mechanism_raw: A rotatable turret assembly positions two cores at different locations, allowing one core to be unloaded and reloaded while the other remains in continuous winding operation, thereby maintaining uninterrupted production.
residual_terms: ["dual-position rotating mechanism", "alternating engagement and preparation phases"]

abstract: An acoustic driver assembly for use with any of a variety of cavitation chamber configurations, including spherical and cylindrical chambers as well as chambers that include at least one flat coupling surface, is provided. The acoustic driver assembly includes at least one transducer, a head mass and a tail mass. The end surface of the head mass is shaped so that only a ring of contact is made between the outer perimeter of the head mass of the driver assembly and the cavitation chamber to which the driver is attached. The area of the contact ring is controlled by shaping its surface.
problem: Efficiently transmitting acoustic energy from a driver to a cavitation chamber while minimizing energy loss and structural stress.
constraint: Optimizing contact area to balance energy coupling efficiency with mechanical durability and chamber compatibility.
mechanism: Shaping a contact interface to create a defined perimeter engagement between two components, concentrating energy transfer through a controlled contact area while minimizing structural stress and energy dissipation outside the target region.
mechanism_raw: Shaping the end surface of a head mass to create a controlled ring-shaped contact area with the chamber, focusing acoustic energy transfer and reducing losses by limiting contact to a defined perimeter.

abstract: The invention provides a black and white photothermographic material including, on at least one surface of a support, at least a photosensitive silver halide, a non-photosensitive organic silver salt, a reducing agent and a binder, wherein 50% or more of the total projected area of the photosensitive silver halide grains is occupied by tabular grains having an aspect ratio of 2 or more, and at least one apex portion of each tabular grain has an epitaxial junction. An image forming method is also provided, the method including bringing the photothermographic material into close contact with a fluorescent intensifying screen containing a fluorescent substance, wherein 50% or more of emission light of the fluorescent substance has a wavelength of 350 nm to 420 nm, and applying X-ray exposure. The black and white photothermographic material has high sensitivity and is superior in image storability and raw stock storability.
problem: Achieving high sensitivity and long-term storability in a black-and-white photothermographic material.
constraint: Balancing grain structure and chemical composition to maximize sensitivity without compromising raw stock or image storability.
mechanism: Structuring light-sensitive particles with high aspect ratio geometries and compositional junctions to enhance photon capture and chemical stability, combined with wavelength-specific emission from a secondary component to optimize exposure efficiency and long-term material integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using tabular silver halide grains with high aspect ratios and epitaxial junctions to enhance light capture and chemical stability, combined with a fluorescent screen emitting specific wavelengths to optimize exposure efficiency.

abstract: A marking device of a trimming apparatus includes a light source member, a lever member and a supporting member. The lever member includes a first sustaining arm, a second sustaining arm and a channel formed between the first sustaining arm and the second sustaining arm. The rear end of the light source member is fixed in the channel. The supporting member includes a sleeve for accommodating the front end of the light source member therein and an upper wing extending upwardly from the sleeve and conforming to the lever member. The upper wing includes a bolt hole corresponding to the second sustaining arm of the lever member. A resilient element is confined between the upper wing and the first sustaining arm. A screw penetrates through the bolt hole and is in contact with the second sustaining arm so as to render compression of the resilient element.
problem: Precise positioning and alignment of a light source in a marking device while maintaining structural stability under dynamic conditions.
constraint: Balancing the compression force of the resilient element to ensure stable positioning without excessive play or binding, while accommodating mechanical tolerances in the lever and supporting member geometry.
mechanism: An adjustable compression mechanism modulates the displacement of a movable component within a constrained pathway by varying the compression of a resilient element positioned between a lever arm and a structural support. The adjustment mechanism's rotation directly governs the resilient element's compression, which in turn controls the movable component's position relative to the lever and support structure.
mechanism_raw: A screw adjusts compression of a resilient element confined between a lever arm and a supporting member's wing, enabling controlled displacement of the light source within a channel. The screw's rotation modulates the resilient element's compression, which in turn governs the light source's position relative to the lever and supporting structure.

abstract: Disclosed is a variable regeneration valve of a heavy equipment in which hunting due to repeated motion of a spool does not occur in a regeneration valve that supplies a return flow of an actuator to a supply port during single operation of the actuator or its composite operation such as composite driving of arm in and swing, and a structure of the variable regeneration valve is simplified to improve process characteristics. The variable regeneration valve includes a hydraulic pump, an actuator connected with the hydraulic pump, a control valve controlling operation, stop, and direction of the actuator, a regeneration switching valve having a first piston, a switching spool, a first elastic member, and a second piston, a first damping orifice, and a second damping orifice.
problem: Preventing oscillatory 'hunting' in a hydraulic regeneration valve spool during actuator operation, while simplifying valve structure to improve control responsiveness.
constraint: Optimizing damping orifice size and elastic member stiffness to suppress oscillations without introducing excessive lag or reducing system throughput during dynamic actuator movements.
mechanism: A fluid control valve incorporates flow-restricting elements and biasing elements to regulate fluid dynamics and mechanical positioning. The flow-restricting elements dampen pressure variations, while the biasing elements return the valve to a neutral state, suppressing oscillations during single or combined operational modes.
mechanism_raw: A regeneration switching valve incorporates damping orifices and elastic members to regulate fluid flow and spool motion. The damping orifices limit pressure fluctuations, while the elastic members bias the spool to a neutral position, stabilizing movement during single or composite actuator operations.

abstract: The invention includes a system and method for managing an operation of a locomotive as a function of a location of the locomotive. The system comprises a location unit for determining the location of the locomotive and a control unit for controlling an operation of the locomotive as a function of the determined location. In another embodiment, the invention includes a system and method for receiving a security authorization input from an operator of the locomotive, comparing the received operator security authorization input to a security authorization parameter, and restricting an operation of the locomotive when the received operator security authorization input does not match the security authorization parameter. In yet another embodiment, the invention includes a system and method of sending a control command from a remote system, receiving the control command at the locomotive, and controlling an operation of the locomotive responsive to the received control command. In still another embodiment, the invention includes a system and method for controlling an operation of the locomotive as a function of the location of the locomotive, a monitored emission parameter and an emission characteristic.
problem: Coordinating locomotive operations based on multiple heterogeneous inputs (location, security authorization, remote commands, emissions) to ensure safe and compliant control.
constraint: Resolving conflicts between concurrent inputs (e.g., remote commands vs. local security authorization) while maintaining fail-safe operation and minimizing latency in critical control decisions.
mechanism: A hierarchical decision-making system integrates multiple heterogeneous input streams into a unified control framework. Each input is processed independently but prioritized according to a predefined authority structure, with conflicting or unauthorized inputs triggering operational restrictions or overrides to ensure fail-safe behavior.
mechanism_raw: A centralized control unit integrates real-time location data, operator security checks, remote command signals, and emission parameters into a unified decision-making framework. Each input is processed independently but hierarchically, with conflicting or unauthorized inputs triggering operational restrictions or overrides.

abstract: The invention provides an ink receiving medium comprising a macroporous substrate having a fluid management system and having a pigment management system in contact with surfaces of macropores of the substrate therein. In one embodiment, the pigment management system comprises water-soluble multivalent metal salt and the fluid management system comprises surfactant.
problem: Managing fluid absorption and pigment retention in a macroporous ink-receiving medium to prevent bleeding and ensure print quality.
constraint: Balancing surfactant concentration to optimize fluid transport without disrupting pigment binding, while ensuring the metal salt does not interfere with substrate porosity or long-term stability.
mechanism: A dual-component fluid management system regulates capillary-driven fluid transport within a porous medium while immobilizing particulate matter. A fluid-regulating agent controls fluid distribution through capillary action, while a binding agent immobilizes particles via chemical interactions, preventing migration and maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A fluid management system (surfactant) regulates capillary-driven fluid flow within macropores, while a pigment management system (water-soluble multivalent metal salt) binds pigment particles to pore surfaces. The surfactant controls fluid distribution, and the salt immobilizes pigment via ionic interactions, preventing migration.
residual_terms: ["capillary-driven fluid transport", "porous medium", "chemical interactions", "fluid-regulating agent", "binding agent"]

abstract: A water-repellent film that is formed on a solid substrate includes: a molecule (A) including at least one or more of siloxane bonding (—Si—O—) at both ends and a hydrocarbon chain in a middle part; and a molecule (B) including a fluorocarbon chain at one end and at least one or more of siloxane bonding (—Si—O—) at another end, wherein a polymer film is formed at least with the molecule (A) and the molecule (B). This polymer film forms a covalent bond with a surface of the substrate via siloxane bonding (—Si—O—), and the surface thereof is covered with fluorocarbon chains having high water repellency. Therefore, this film prevents the intrusion of alkali ions. Thereby, an ink jet head and an ink jet type apparatus having a water-repellent film that is not destroyed by the long-term contact with alkaline ink can be provided.
problem: Preventing alkali ion intrusion into ink jet heads while maintaining durable water repellency under prolonged exposure to alkaline inks.
constraint: Achieving sufficient covalent bonding density to prevent film degradation, while ensuring fluorocarbon chain orientation maximizes water repellency without compromising mechanical flexibility or chemical resistance.
mechanism: A covalently bonded polymer barrier with oriented hydrophobic chains forms a protective layer on a substrate. The covalent bonds ensure adhesion and structural integrity, while the oriented hydrophobic chains create a selective barrier that blocks specific ions while maintaining water repellency and mechanical flexibility.
mechanism_raw: A polymer film formed from siloxane-terminated hydrocarbon chains (molecule A) and fluorocarbon-siloxane chains (molecule B) covalently bonds to the substrate via siloxane linkages. The fluorocarbon chains orient outward, creating a hydrophobic barrier that blocks alkali ions while the siloxane bonds ensure adhesion and structural integrity.

abstract: This invention relates to methods and compositions for modulating movement of eukaryotic cells with migratory capacity. More specifically, the invention relates to methods and compositions for modulating movement of cells of hematopoietic, neural, epithelial, or mesenchymal origin, in a specific site in a subject. The foregoing are useful, inter alia, in the treatment of conditions characterized by a need to modulate migratory-cell movement associated with specific sites in a subject. More specifically, specific sites include sites of inflammation and modulation of migratory-cell movement is movement away from an agent source, or repulsion. Other sites include tumor sites, sites of pathogenic infection, and germ cell bearing sites.
problem: Controlling site-specific migratory cell movement to treat conditions like inflammation, tumors, or infections.
constraint: The agent must selectively target specific cell types (e.g., hematopoietic, neural) and anatomical sites without affecting non-target cells or regions.
mechanism: Deploy a chemical signaling source that establishes a spatially varying concentration field, where the gradient direction and magnitude bias cellular motility, thereby steering cell migration toward or away from specific locations based on chemotactic response.
mechanism_raw: Using a chemical agent source that creates a repulsive gradient, causing cells to move away from the agent's location, thereby directing their migration to or from specific anatomical sites.

abstract: A sprinkler assembly for controlling a fire situation includes at least one fluid conduit defining a flow passage including an inlet for receiving a fluid from a fluid source and at least one outlet for discharging the fluid, and a dispensing mechanism such as an open or closed sprinkler head for distributing water to a selected location. A fluid control apparatus is provided including a valve assembly having a valve seal which is moveable between a closed position blocking fluid flow through the conduit and an open position causing fluid flow through the conduit. The fluid control apparatus further includes an actuating mechanism including a valve actuator which is operatively connected to the valve assembly for causing movement of the valve seal to the open position upon release of the sealing force. A sensing mechanism is operatively connected to the valve assembly, the sensing mechanism being thermodynamically responsive to at least one of heat, smoke, infrared radiation and ultraviolet radiation emitted by a heat source.
problem: Automatically activating a fire suppression system in response to environmental threats like heat, smoke, or radiation.
constraint: The sensor must respond only to specific threat conditions to avoid false activation, while the valve must reliably transition between sealed and open states under varying pressure and temperature conditions.
mechanism: Use an environmentally responsive detection element that undergoes a physical state change when exposed to a threshold level of a target stimulus, mechanically actuating a flow control element to release a suppression medium, forming a self-regulating feedback loop that terminates when the stimulus is removed.
mechanism_raw: A thermodynamically responsive sensor detects a stimulus (heat/smoke/radiation) and triggers a valve actuator to release fluid, creating a closed-loop feedback system that converts environmental energy into mechanical action.

abstract: A wafer support device having a fixed base, a guiding device, a movable base disposed so as to move in a vertical direction with respect to the fixed base by the guiding device, a first pressing device pressing the movable base, a θ stage rotatably disposed on the movable base with the vertical direction as a rotation axis, a linear motor, a contact bar, a load control device controlling a load of pressing, and a controller controlling a pressing force by the first pressing device based on the load. The first pressing device has a cylinder and a main pressurizing chamber and a sub-pressurizing chamber, a piston rod vertically moving in the main pressurizing chamber and the sub-pressurizing chamber, respectively, a main pressure controller controlling a pressure in the main pressurizing chamber, and a sub pressure controller controlling a pressure in the sub-pressurizing chamber.
problem: Achieving precise vertical pressing force and rotational alignment in semiconductor wafer processing equipment.
constraint: The system must balance structural rigidity for support with the need for micro-scale vertical and rotational adjustments to avoid damaging delicate wafers.
mechanism: Employ two independently pressurized chambers coupled to a common actuator element, where differential pressure between the chambers produces staged displacement with coarse and fine control modes, enabling sequential application of gross force followed by micro-adjustment during precision engagement.
mechanism_raw: A dual-pressure chamber system (main and sub) independently controls piston rod movement, enabling staged force application and fine-tuned pressure regulation during wafer handling and pressing operations.

abstract: A printer driver software product is provided for execution by a computer to produce compressed page data corresponding to a page layout. The driver includes instructions to generate continuous-tone data and bi-level text and black graphics data from print data corresponding to the page layout. Data compression instructions are also included in the printer driver. Upon execution the data compression instructions cause the computer to compress the set of continuous-tone data and the set of bi-level text and black graphics data to produce compressed page data corresponding to the page layout. The compressed data is then transmitted to a printer in communication with the computer. A printer driver software product according to the invention is particularly useful where a printer is coupled to a computer by means of a relatively limited bandwidth connection.
problem: Transmitting print data efficiently over bandwidth-limited connections between a computer and printer.
constraint: The compression must maintain sufficient quality for both text/graphics and images while minimizing data size to fit within the connection's bandwidth limits.
mechanism: Partition incoming data into separate representation classes based on information type, then apply distinct encoding strategies optimized for each class's statistical characteristics, combining the encoded streams for transmission while preserving reconstruction fidelity within bandwidth constraints.
mechanism_raw: Separating continuous-tone and bi-level data into distinct streams, then applying tailored compression algorithms to each stream to optimize bandwidth usage while preserving critical visual information.

abstract: An adjustable pliers having first and second elongated members, each elongated member comprising a handle, a jaw, and a intermediate portion between the jaw and the handle. The intermediate portion of one of the elongated members includes an elongated slot, while the intermediate portion of the other elongated member includes a pivot pin that is slidingly captured in the elongated slot. A spring is captured in the elongated slot and engages the pivot pin so as to bias the jaw of one of the elongated members toward the jaw of the other elongated member. One of the handle members also includes a stop pin in its intermediate portion that abuts the intermediate portion of the other elongated member to limit the degree to which the elongated members can pivot with respect to each other about the pivot pin.
problem: Providing adjustable gripping force and jaw spacing in hand tools while maintaining alignment and preventing over-closure.
constraint: The mechanism must maintain jaw parallelism during adjustment while ensuring the spring force and stop pin work together to prevent slippage or excessive pressure on gripped objects.
mechanism: Provide a variable mechanical linkage between two gripping elements using a sliding connection within a constrained path, where a resilient biasing element maintains closing force and a mechanical stop limits the range of motion, ensuring controlled gripping pressure and parallel jaw orientation throughout the adjustment range.
mechanism_raw: A sliding pivot pin within an elongated slot allows variable jaw spacing, with a spring biasing the jaws closed and a stop pin limiting maximum pivot angle to control gripping range.
residual_terms: ["variable mechanical linkage", "resilient biasing element", "mechanical stop", "parallel jaw orientation"]

abstract: A folding knife is provided having a handle that pivotably holds a blade member adapted to be housed within the handle in a storage state, and to be deployed to a service state by swinging laterally and forwardly in a path orthogonal to the handle. The handle is constructed of facing first and second members elongated between front and rear extremities, and defining a compartment which houses the blade member. The second handle member is pivotably joined to the first handle member in a manner to permit rearward swinging movement which opens the compartment to allow deployment of the blade member. Forwardly returning movement of the second handle member secures the blade member in its service state.
problem: Need to safely store a blade in a compact handle while enabling reliable deployment and locking in a service position.
constraint: The mechanism must use a single pivoting motion to both open access to the blade and lock it in place, balancing compact storage with reliable deployment and retention without additional actuators.
mechanism: A single pivoting member that sequentially performs two functions through its motion: an initial phase that opens a storage enclosure to expose a blade, and a subsequent phase that applies a retaining force to lock the blade in a deployed position. The same rotational movement both grants access and establishes a stable locked state without additional actuators.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting handle member that, through its own rearward swinging motion, opens the storage compartment to allow blade deployment, and through forward return movement, secures the blade in its deployed service state. The same single pivoting motion serves dual sequential functions: access (opening the compartment) and locking (securing the blade).

abstract: A fixture is configured to provide external fixation of a fractured end portion of a bone by including a first number of holes for pins extending from the fixture into one or more fragments in the end portion and a second number of holes for pins extending from the fixture into the bone shaft. The second number of holes includes a hole within a sliding structure allowing a single pin to be moved with a fixture to provide extension between the fragments and the shaft. A first version of the fixture includes a sliding block through which rods extend to hold pins directed laterally into the fragments(s), and a sliding for clamping pins within the first number of holes. A second version of the fixture includes an arcuate portion in which the first number of holes extend in radial directions.
problem: Need to stabilize fractured bone fragments relative to the bone shaft while allowing controlled, adjustable extension or compression during healing.
constraint: Must maintain stable fixation of pins in bone fragments and shaft while permitting controlled, incremental adjustment of fragment position relative to the shaft, without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: A linearly adjustable fixation element that slides along a guided path within a bone stabilization structure, allowing incremental modification of the spatial relationship between bone fragments and the bone shaft while maintaining continuous fixation. The sliding motion enables controlled application and maintenance of tension or compression forces.
mechanism_raw: A sliding pin mechanism integrated within the fixation fixture that moves along a track or through a sliding structure, enabling controlled adjustment of the distance between bone fragments and the bone shaft while maintaining pin fixation. The sliding element allows incremental tension or compression to be applied and maintained.
residual_terms: ["linearly adjustable fixation element", "guided path", "bone stabilization structure", "tension or compression forces"]

abstract: A driving method of an air conditioning system is disclosed. The air conditioning system includes a first cooling device combined with a heating function and having a compressor, an outdoor heat exchanger, an expansion device, a passage control device and an interior heat exchanger, a second cooling device provided at an outlet side of the blower and having a cooling pad containing moisture and ventilating, a tank storing refrigerant, a pump, a sprayer and a filter, a control unit electrically connecting to the first and second cooling devices and a humidity sensor and alternatively driving the first cooling device and the second cooling device according to humidity of outdoor air delivered from the humidity sensor during air conditioning mode. The driving method of the present invention includes steps of measuring humidity of outdoor air at the humidity sensor when the power of the air conditioning system is on; comparing humidity of outdoor air with predetermined humidity; driving a first cooling device circulating refrigerant by using a compressor for cooling the interior when humidity of outdoor air is higher than predetermined humidity, and driving a second cooling device sucking outdoor air with low relative humidity, increasing the relative humidity through humidifying and cooling process and providing the air into the interior for cooling the interior when humidity of outdoor air is lower than predetermined humidity.
problem: Need to efficiently cool an interior space while appropriately managing humidity levels, which vary depending on outdoor air conditions.
constraint: Must balance cooling effectiveness with humidity control by switching between two different physical cooling mechanisms based on a single environmental input, ensuring optimal indoor climate without redundant or conflicting operation.
mechanism: An environmental condition-responsive selector that compares a measured parameter against a predetermined threshold and activates one of two distinct processing methods based on the comparison result. The selector uses the environmental input as a direct control signal to switch between methods, ensuring only the appropriate method operates for the current conditions.
mechanism_raw: A humidity-sensing feedback switch that compares measured outdoor air humidity against a predetermined threshold and selects between two distinct cooling methods: a refrigerant-based system for dehumidification and cooling when humidity is high, and an evaporative cooling system that adds moisture while cooling when humidity is low. The environmental condition directly determines which processing method is activated.

abstract: The present invention is a collapsible fluid container for handling liquid. The collapsible fluid container has an interior volume for storing the liquid, which defines a main chamber and an auxiliary chamber connected to the main chamber. The auxiliary chamber is positioned to receive a substance. A fitment is sealed to the collapsible fluid container that defines a port communicating with the interior volume of the fluid container.
reason: The patent describes a dual-chamber collapsible container with an auxiliary chamber for holding a substance and a fitment with a port, but does not describe any causal mechanism for how the substance interacts with the liquid, how the chambers communicate, or how the container is actively used. It is a static product feature description rather than a problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: An inkjet printer includes a resistance element with which a front end of the paper becomes in contact so that a paper on a top of the stack of papers is separated from the stack of papers and picked up from a cassette, an angle conversion unit which changes an inclination angle of the resistance element with respect to the front end of the paper, and a switching gear which is moved by a carriage to a first position to feed the paper and to a second position to drive the angle conversion unit.
problem: Need to reliably separate and pick up individual sheets from a stack of papers in an inkjet printer while coordinating paper feeding with sheet separation.
constraint: Must coordinate paper feeding and resistance element angle adjustment using only the carriage's positional movement, avoiding additional actuators while ensuring reliable sheet separation and pickup.
mechanism: A position-dependent switching mechanism that uses the movement of a carrier element to selectively engage either a feeding operation or an adjustment operation. The carrier's position determines which function is activated, coordinating two distinct operations through a single motion source without additional actuators.
mechanism_raw: A switching gear that is positioned by the moving carriage to either a first position (enabling paper feed) or a second position (driving an angle conversion unit that adjusts the inclination of a resistance element). The carriage's position thus controls whether the system is feeding paper or adjusting the resistance element angle for optimal sheet separation, using the same motion to coordinate two distinct operations.

abstract: A material handling and transport apparatus for railroad use comprises a rail car loading assembly and a deck vehicle. The rail car loading assembly comprises a loading machine having a handling arm, and means to move the rail car loading assembly forward and rearward along top edges of sidewalls of a string of gondola cars and across gaps between the gondola cars. The deck vehicle comprises a deck located at a deck end of the deck vehicle such that the deck can be maneuvered adjacent to an end gondola car of the string of gondola cars wherein the deck is located at a vertical loading position such that the means to move the rail car loading assembly is operative to move the rail car loading assembly onto the deck.
problem: Efficiently loading materials onto rail cars while navigating gaps between cars and maintaining alignment during transfer.
constraint: Maintaining structural stability and alignment of the loading assembly and deck vehicle while traversing gaps and uneven surfaces.
mechanism: Coordinated movement of a transfer mechanism along support surfaces and across physical discontinuities, combined with a mobile platform maneuvered to bridge gaps and receive the transferred load, enabling continuous material handling despite spatial interruptions.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated movement of a loading assembly along sidewalls and across gaps, combined with a deck vehicle maneuvered to bridge the gap and receive the loaded assembly, enabling continuous material transfer despite physical discontinuities.

abstract: An overhang bracket has a top member, a side member and a diagonal member. The side and top member may be connected together through a removable connecter. A guardrail post holder allows a guardrail post to be installed at a variety of angles to the top member. Rotating the side member causes the diagonal member to translate up or down the side member. A side member locator extends upwards from the overhang bracket to indicate the location of the side member. A tie rod holder holds a tie rod in an offset position relative to the side member. The side member locator may extend upwards through further parts of the shoring system or bridge overhang structure, for example a floor of a concrete form or rebar. A worker may adjust the overhang bracket in place from a standing position on a supporting structure or the floor of the form.
problem: Adjustably positioning structural components (e.g., guardrail posts) in a shoring system while maintaining structural integrity and worker accessibility.
constraint: Balancing adjustability with structural rigidity and ensuring the locator remains functional across varying configurations.
mechanism: Rotational input from an actuation element converts into linear displacement of a connected linkage, enabling angular adjustment of attached components; a position sensor provides real-time feedback to ensure alignment accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Rotational movement of a side member translates into linear displacement of a diagonal member, enabling angle adjustment of connected components; a locator provides positional feedback to ensure accurate alignment.

abstract: A system and method for preparing chalcogenide glass are provided that allow for larger quantities of glass to be produced with lower production costs and less risks of environmental hazards. The system includes a reaction container operable to hold chalcogenide glass constituents during a glass formation reaction, a stirring rod operable to mix the contents of the reaction container, a thermocouple operable to measure the temperature inside the reaction container, and a reaction chamber operable to hold the reaction container. The method includes placing chalcogenide glass constituents in a reaction container, heating the chalcogenide glass constituents above the melting point of at least one of the constituents, promoting dissolving or reaction of the other constituents, stirring the reaction melt, maintaining an overpressure of at least one atmosphere over the reaction melt, and cooling the reaction melt to below the chalcogenide glass transition temperature.
problem: Producing chalcogenide glass safely and cost-effectively while minimizing environmental risks during high-temperature reactions.
constraint: Maintaining overpressure above atmospheric levels without compromising reaction safety or material homogeneity.
mechanism: Controlled pressure within a processing vessel suppresses volatile emissions, while a mixing mechanism ensures uniform distribution of constituents, enabling consistent material formation under hazardous conditions.
mechanism_raw: Controlled overpressure in the reaction chamber suppresses volatile emissions, while stirring ensures uniform mixing of constituents, enabling consistent glass formation under hazardous conditions.

abstract: A pneumatic device selection system has a computer, first through sixth databases connected to the computer and storing data of at least pneumatic devices, a coordinate input unit and a keyboard connected to the computer, for entering input data based on an input action of an operator into the computer, and a display unit connected to the computer, for displaying information from the computer. The pneumatic device selection system functionally has a first selection processor for selecting a cylinder operating system based on input data from the coordinate input unit or the like, and a second selection processor for selecting a shock absorber based on input data from the coordinate input unit or the like and/or a selection result from the first selection processor.
problem: Selecting appropriate pneumatic devices (e.g., cylinders, shock absorbers) based on operator input and system requirements.
constraint: Ensuring database accuracy and real-time processing speed to match dynamic input conditions.
mechanism: Database-driven selection processors cross-reference input parameters against stored component specifications to recommend compatible devices, leveraging hierarchical dependencies between components to ensure system compatibility.
mechanism_raw: Database-driven selection processors cross-reference input parameters (e.g., coordinates, operational conditions) to recommend compatible devices, leveraging hierarchical dependencies between components.

abstract: System, especially for a motor vehicle, able, on the one hand, to start up an internal-combustion engine and, on the other hand, to charge an electrical circuit, including a main electrical machine able to operate, on the one hand, as a generator and, on the other hand, as an electric motor, the said electrical machine driving the internal-combustion engine by means of a belt when it is operating in motor mode, the system further including management means which drive the main electrical machine, characterised in that it includes a supplementary starter, as well as means for detecting at least one condition for triggering the activation of the said supplementary starter, and the management means drive the main electrical machine and the starter, according to a particular sequence, when the said condition is detected by the said detection means.
problem: Reliably starting an internal combustion engine and charging an electrical circuit using a shared electrical machine without compromising either function.
constraint: Coordinating the activation sequence to prevent overloading the electrical system while maintaining dual functionality.
mechanism: An auxiliary actuator activates under predefined conditions, with control sequencing means coordinating a primary electrical machine and the auxiliary actuator to prevent operational conflicts and ensure dual-function redundancy.
mechanism_raw: A supplementary starter activates under predefined conditions, with management means sequencing the main electrical machine and starter to avoid operational conflicts and ensure redundancy.

abstract: An elevator system for traveling on a rail attached to the outside of a high-rise building. One elevator has a telescopic arm attached for reaching any position on or above the building. The telescopic arm consists of two parts, which are interconnected with a pivoting mechanism. The telescopic arm has a pivot at its end attached to a cramp, by a vertical rotating mechanism. The cramp is pivoted to an outside platform with a barrier, a cabin is hung from the platform and can make a full rotation. The elevator portion has a passenger compartment with sliding doors and a vertical aperture with a staircase connecting with an autonomous rescue elevator.
problem: Accessing any position on or above a high-rise building for elevator transport without requiring multiple fixed systems.
constraint: Balancing structural stability of the telescopic arm and cabin rotation while maintaining safe load-bearing capacity during movement.
mechanism: A multi-segment extendable arm with pivoting joints and an independent rotational mechanism at its terminus enables combined rotational and translational motion, achieving full positional coverage through coordinated movement of the arm and cabin.
mechanism_raw: A telescopic arm with two interconnected parts and a pivoting mechanism enables multi-directional reach, while a vertical rotating mechanism at the arm's end allows a cabin to rotate independently, achieving full positional coverage through combined rotational and translational motion.

abstract: An automatic swimming pool cleaning robot is disclosed, comprising a body, a suction head, an unstable valve, a suction pipe having an upper end, a recuperating filter connected to the upper end, and a venturi injector, wherein the unstable valve is activated to activate the robot. The robot combines the advantages of vacuum-fed robots and pressure-fed robots.
problem: Efficiently cleaning a swimming pool by combining the benefits of vacuum-fed and pressure-fed cleaning systems in a single autonomous robot.
constraint: Maintaining consistent activation of the unstable valve to ensure seamless transitions between vacuum and pressure modes without manual intervention.
mechanism: A dynamic switching valve alternates between suction and pressure modes in response to environmental conditions, enabling adaptive operation by transitioning between debris collection and propulsion functions without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: An unstable valve dynamically switches between suction and pressure modes, activating the robot to alternate between vacuum-driven debris collection and pressure-driven propulsion, enabling adaptive operation based on environmental conditions.

abstract: An article of footwear including a shell that provides stability. The shell can include a heel cup and a wall extending forward of the heel cup and around the periphery of the forefoot, returning to the heel cup. The shell can also define a hole in the forefoot region. A cushion in the form of a midsole can be secured in the shell, with a portion extending at least partially through the shell hole. An upper can be secured to the shell with stitching passing through the upper and the shell wall in at least the forefoot region; and rearward of the stitching, the upper can be secured with cement and/or adhesives to the shell and/or the midsole. The footwear provides comfort and stability, for example toe-to-heel and lateral stability, especially during toe-off, i.e., the propulsion portion of a gait.
problem: Providing both structural stability and cushioning in footwear, particularly during dynamic movements like toe-off in gait.
constraint: Balancing rigidity of the shell for stability with flexibility of the midsole and upper attachment to avoid compromising comfort or structural integrity.
mechanism: A rigid structural frame with integrated cushioning elements interfaces with an upper component via mechanical fastening and bonding, distributing forces during dynamic movement while balancing stability and flexibility.
mechanism_raw: A rigid shell with a heel cup and forward-extending wall creates a stable frame, while a midsole cushion extends through a forefoot hole to interface with the upper, and stitching combined with adhesives secures the upper to the shell and midsole, distributing forces during propulsion.

abstract: The invention relates to a timepiece which has a resin bearing section. Moreover, the invention relates to a wheel train apparatus which has a resin bearing section. The invention is constituted by the timepiece provided with a gear wheel and supporting members which support the gear wheel, the supporting members being formed from a filler containing resin. Alternatively the invention is constituted by the wheel train apparatus provided with a gear wheel and supporting members which support the gear wheel, the supporting members being formed from a filler containing resin.
problem: Reducing weight and material costs in mechanical systems (e.g., timepieces) while maintaining functional performance of gear trains.
constraint: Ensuring the resin-filled supports can withstand repetitive mechanical stress and wear over time compared to conventional bearing materials.
mechanism: Polymer-based supports replace conventional bearing materials in mechanical systems, leveraging moldability and low density to reduce weight and cost while maintaining structural integrity under repetitive stress.
mechanism_raw: Resin-filled supporting members replace traditional materials for gear wheel bearings, leveraging the resin's moldability and low density to create lightweight, cost-effective supports without sacrificing mechanical stability.

abstract: Compact optical devices and methods of constructing the same are disclosed. The optical devices are formed with perpendicular orientations to the surface of a supporting layer (e.g., substrate), and have three-dimensional structures rather than planar structures. The optical devices can be formed with high density on supporting layers without the need for several built-up layers. Maintaining the processing temperatures within the cure profiles of polymer optical layers is readily achieved.
problem: Achieving high-density optical component integration without requiring multiple stacked layers or planar configurations.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment and structural integrity of 3D optical components during fabrication and operation without compromising performance.
mechanism: A three-dimensional spatial arrangement of optical components in perpendicular orientations relative to a substrate enables dense packing on a single layer, maintaining alignment and structural integrity during fabrication and operation.
mechanism_raw: Forming optical devices in three-dimensional perpendicular orientations relative to a supporting substrate allows dense packing of components on a single layer, eliminating the need for complex multi-layer assembly while maintaining processing temperature compatibility with polymer materials.

abstract: A trimmer includes a blade connection portion and a handle, and a blade is engaged with a recess defined in one side of the blade connection portion. A C-shaped clamp has two ridges extending from two insides thereof and the two ridges are slidably engaged with a first groove defined in the other side of the blade connection portion and a second grooves defined in an outside of the pattern block so as to sandwich the blade between the pattern block and the blade connection portion.
reason: The mechanism is a specific mechanical clamping system for a trimmer blade, which is a standard solution for securing components and lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond its immediate application.

abstract: A wind turbine with at least one blade having a pitch axis that is offset laterally so that the blade does not intersect with an axis of rotation of the wind turbine, and a center of mass and an aerodynamic center are offset from the pitch axis in the direction parallel to the axis of rotation of the wind turbine. The blade is arranged so that the blade can pitch towards stall against the action of a resilient device and also so that the centrifugal loading on at least one of the blade and one or more components optionally attached to the blade, acts against the spring in a direction to shed power by pitching the blade towards stall and also so that the torque loading provided by a power conversion device acts to pitch the blade in the opposite direction, so as to reduce the amount of load shedding whenever the power is being extracted from the wind turbine.
problem: Managing load shedding in wind turbines to reduce power extraction when torque or centrifugal forces exceed safe thresholds.
constraint: The system must balance centrifugal forces (which pitch the blade toward stall) against torque loading (which opposes this motion) to avoid excessive load shedding during power generation.
mechanism: A rotating element's pivot point is positioned offset from its aerodynamic and mass centers, creating opposing force interactions (centrifugal loading and torque from energy conversion) that automatically adjust the element's orientation toward a stall condition, self-regulating load shedding against power extraction.
mechanism_raw: The blade's pitch axis is offset from its aerodynamic and mass centers, allowing opposing forces (centrifugal loading and torque from power conversion) to automatically adjust blade pitch toward stall, balancing load shedding with power extraction.
residual_terms: ["pivot point", "aerodynamic and mass centers", "centrifugal loading", "torque", "stall condition"]

abstract: An apparatus that mass polishes a variety of fiber optic cable connectors simultaneously. The apparatus includes a plurality of polishing plates, each capable of holding its own polishing film and pad, and having a varying height. The apparatus further includes a plurality of connector fixtures that may receive a variety of connectors at varying angles. Each connector fixture communicates with a corresponding polishing pad. Thus, fiber optic cable connectors having a variety of polished end faces may be provided with the apparatus. The apparatus also eliminates the potential for contamination among polishing films, reduces polishing steps, and saves labor and maintenance costs.
problem: Efficiently mass-polishing diverse fiber optic connectors with varying geometries while minimizing contamination and labor.
constraint: The system must maintain consistent polishing quality across heterogeneous connector geometries while minimizing setup complexity and contamination risks.
mechanism: Adjustable processing surfaces with variable heights and positioning fixtures at multiple angles enable simultaneous handling of heterogeneous geometries, maintaining consistent quality while eliminating cross-contamination through isolated processing zones.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable polishing plates with varying heights and connector fixtures at varying angles enable simultaneous processing of different connector types, eliminating cross-contamination and reducing steps.
residual_terms: ["adjustable processing surfaces", "variable heights", "positioning fixtures", "isolated processing zones"]

abstract: Prior art methods for forming alt. PSMs require a relatively large number of phase assignments to avoid phase conflicts in complex arrays. This has been improved by adding dummy elements at the ends of all rows and columns of the array that is to be imaged, while initially leaving all corners open. Phases are then assigned in checker board fashion to all elements. Additional dummy elements are then placed in the open corners and assigned the same phase as their immediate neighbors. The first exposure of the photoresist is made with both the original elements and the additional dummy elements. Then additional resist is coated and exposed and the original elements are open after development. If the added elements are made somewhat smaller than the original elements, only a single exposure is used.
problem: Avoiding phase conflicts in complex photolithography arrays while minimizing the number of exposure steps.
constraint: The dummy elements must be sized and positioned to prevent phase conflicts without requiring additional exposures, balancing resolution and process efficiency.
mechanism: Auxiliary elements are strategically placed at array boundaries and corners with alternating phase assignments to resolve conflicts through spatial separation, enabling single-exposure processing by preventing overlap between original and auxiliary elements.
mechanism_raw: Dummy elements are added at row/column ends and corners, with phases assigned in a checkerboard pattern to resolve conflicts. Smaller dummy elements allow a single exposure by avoiding overlap with original elements.
residual_terms: ["auxiliary elements", "array boundaries", "alternating phase assignments", "spatial separation", "single-exposure processing"]

abstract: The present invention provides adapter-directed display systems for expressing exogenous polypeptide within a host cell and/or displaying the exogenous polypeptide on the outer surface of a genetic package. This subject systems are particularly useful for displaying a genetically diverse repertoire of monomeric and multimeric polypeptides. The invention also provides both expression and helper vectors and kits containing components of the subject display systems. Also provided are genetic packages displaying the exogenous polypeptides of particular interest. Further provided by the invention are methods of using the subject display systems.
problem: Expressing and displaying genetically diverse polypeptides (monomeric or multimeric) on the surface of host cells or genetic packages.
constraint: The adapter system must accommodate both monomeric and multimeric polypeptides while maintaining genetic stability and display efficiency in host cells.
mechanism: Linking molecules direct the fusion of diverse polypeptides to host vehicles, enabling surface display and functional screening by accommodating both monomeric and multimeric forms while preserving genetic stability through modular adapter architecture.
mechanism_raw: Adapter molecules direct the fusion of exogenous polypeptides to genetic packages, enabling surface display and functional screening of diverse repertoires.
residual_terms: ["linking molecules", "host vehicles", "surface display", "monomeric and multimeric forms", "modular adapter architecture"]

abstract: To provide an adhesive film that can be easily released leaving substantially no adhesive residue and without damaging the adherend surface when released from an adherend. A base material comprising at least a first resin film with a breaking elongation in the lengthwise direction of 300 to 1500% and a breaking strength of at least 2 kg/12 mm, and a second resin film with a lower breaking elongation and a higher flexural modulus than the first resin film is used. The second resin film can break before the first resin film when the base material is stretched.
problem: Creating an adhesive film that releases cleanly without residue or surface damage when detached from an adherend.
constraint: The mechanical properties of the two films must be precisely balanced so that the second film fails before the first, ensuring controlled delamination without compromising the structural integrity of the first film during release.
mechanism: A layered system employs two materials with contrasting mechanical properties: a first layer with high elongation and strength, and a second layer with lower elongation and higher stiffness. When stretched, the second layer fails first, allowing the first layer to elongate and release without transferring residue or damaging the adherend.
mechanism_raw: A layered base material uses two resin films with contrasting mechanical properties: a first film with high elongation and strength, and a second film with lower elongation and higher flexural modulus. When stretched, the second film breaks first, allowing the first film to elongate and release without transferring adhesive residue or damaging the adherend.

abstract: The invention relates to pre-processing of a pronunciation dictionary for compression in a data processing device, the pronunciation dictionary comprising at least one entry, the entry comprising a sequence of character units and a sequence of phoneme units. According to one aspect of the invention the sequence of character units and the sequence of phoneme units are aligned using a statistical algorithm. The aligned sequence of character units and aligned sequence of phoneme units are interleaved by inserting each phoneme unit at a predetermined location relative to the corresponding character unit.
problem: Compressing a pronunciation dictionary by reducing redundancy between character and phoneme sequences.
constraint: The statistical alignment algorithm must accurately map character-to-phoneme relationships to ensure that interleaving does not lose critical pronunciation information during compression.
mechanism: Statistical alignment of character and phoneme sequences is performed, then the aligned sequences are interleaved by inserting each phoneme unit at a predetermined location relative to its corresponding character unit. This structured interleaving reduces storage requirements while preserving the mapping between characters and phonemes.
mechanism_raw: Statistical alignment of character and phoneme sequences is performed, then the aligned sequences are interleaved by inserting each phoneme unit at a predetermined location relative to its corresponding character unit. This structured interleaving reduces storage requirements while preserving the mapping between characters and phonemes.

abstract: An apparatus and method for winding a sheet of aligned parallel yarns onto a beam is described. The beam winder utilizes a circularly arced yarn spool rack that feeds each yarn to an alignment comb through associated guide tubes. The distance between each spool of yarn and the alignment comb is substantially the same for all spools of yarn, thereby equalizing the force necessary to pull them to the comb. Next, the aligned sheet of material is preshrunk using heated rollers and wound onto a beam. Multiple speed controlled stepper motors are utilized to maintain a constant low level of tension in the sheet during the shrinking process. After shrinkage, the tension level of the yarn sheet is increased as it is wrapped onto the beam. A turntable that supports two or more beams is provided to facilitate the rapid switching of beams once one beam has become full.
problem: Maintaining consistent tension in a yarn sheet during preshrinking and winding to prevent uneven shrinkage or breakage.
constraint: The tension control system must dynamically adjust motor speeds to counteract variations in yarn elasticity during heating and winding, while the turntable design must allow seamless transitions without interrupting the winding process.
mechanism: Multiple independently controlled actuators dynamically regulate tension in different sections of the medium during processing. A dual-beam support structure enables rapid switching between beams once one is full, minimizing downtime.
mechanism_raw: Multiple speed-controlled stepper motors independently regulate tension in different sections of the yarn sheet during preshrinking and winding. A turntable with dual beams enables rapid switching between beams once one is full, minimizing downtime.

abstract: The present invention relates to a nucleic acid sequence and its corresponding protein sequence useful as a dominant selectable marker in eukaryotes. More specifically the invention relates to a nucleic acid encoding a bacterial IMPDH gene that has been engineered into a eukaryotic expression vectors, thereby permitting bacterial IMPDH expression in mammalian cells. Bacterial IMPDH expression confers resistance to MPA which can be used as dominant selectable marker in eukaryotes including mammals. The invention also relates to expression vectors and cells that express the bacterial IMPDH gene as well as gene therapies and protein synthesis.
problem: Selecting eukaryotic cells that have successfully incorporated a foreign gene into their genome.
constraint: The bacterial IMPDH must be functionally expressed in eukaryotic cells without disrupting normal cellular processes, and the MPA concentration must be calibrated to selectively kill non-transformed cells while permitting growth of resistant cells.
mechanism: A foreign gene encoding a resistance-conferring enzyme is introduced into host cells, enabling them to survive in the presence of a selective agent. Only cells with the integrated gene express the enzyme and resist the agent, allowing selective growth of transformed cells.
mechanism_raw: A bacterial IMPDH gene is engineered into a eukaryotic expression vector, enabling the host cells to produce bacterial IMPDH. This enzyme confers resistance to MPA, allowing only cells with the integrated gene to survive in MPA-containing media.

abstract: A device for treatment of an elongated medium with at least two first rotational bodies, which are pivoted around predefined rotational axes, whereby the rotational axes are essentially parallel to one another, with at least two second rotational bodies, which are pivoted around predefined rotational axes, a first treatment chamber, which is arranged in a conveying route of the elongated medium between the two first rotational bodies and the two second rotational bodies, and a second treatment chamber for the elongated medium, which is arranged in the conveying route of the elongated medium after the second two rotational bodies.
problem: Processing an elongated medium through multiple sequential treatment stages while maintaining controlled interaction with rotational elements.
constraint: The rotational axes of the bodies must remain parallel and precisely positioned relative to the treatment chambers to ensure uniform contact and consistent processing of the medium as it moves through the conveying route.
mechanism: The medium is conveyed through a route alternating between pairs of parallel rotational elements and treatment zones. The first rotational elements pre-treat the medium, the first zone applies a treatment, the second rotational elements further process it, and the second zone applies a final treatment.
mechanism_raw: The elongated medium is conveyed through a route that alternates between pairs of parallel rotational bodies and treatment chambers. The first rotational bodies pre-treat the medium, the first chamber applies a treatment, the second rotational bodies further process it, and the second chamber applies a final treatment.

abstract: A 6-high rolling mill has work rolls which have offsets, relative to the intermediate rolls, such that during operation there is a net horizontal force acting to urge the work rolls into engagement with the support rolls whereby substantially all horizontal support of the work rolls is provided by the support rolls. Support pads are located proximal the rolls' side faces, without exerting any substantial force on the work rolls during operation.
problem: Work rolls in a multi-high rolling mill require horizontal support during operation to prevent deflection and maintain alignment, but traditional support methods can introduce unwanted forces or interfere with roll function.
constraint: The offset geometry must be precisely calibrated — too much offset creates excessive forces that could overload or damage the rolls, while too little fails to provide adequate self-centering support. The support pads must also be positioned close enough to provide support without physically contacting or disturbing the work rolls during operation.
mechanism: A geometric offset between adjacent rotating elements causes operational forces to generate a net lateral force that passively maintains alignment between the elements and their supports. The offset geometry converts the forces that would otherwise cause misalignment into a self-centering effect, eliminating the need for external active alignment mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: The work rolls are geometrically offset relative to the intermediate rolls such that operational rolling forces naturally generate a net horizontal force that passively urges the work rolls into engagement with support rolls. This means the very forces that would otherwise cause misalignment are harnessed by the geometric design to maintain proper positioning, eliminating the need for active support mechanisms.

abstract: The subject matter of the invention is a heddle (1), more specifically a lifting heddle as part of a leno selvedge device, the heddle comprising a head portion and a base portion with a closed or an open eyelet for mounting to a heddle frame or to a heddle ridge bar (13), the head portion and/or base portion (2, 3) being adapted to be secured stationarily to the heddle frame or the heddle ridge bar (13), with the head portion (2) and/or the base portion (3) being adapted to be interlockingly and non-slidably fixed to the heddle frame or to the heddle ridge bar (13) by means of a detent system (11, 12, 13a).
reason: The patent describes a standard detent-based mechanical interlock (snap-fit or positive locking mechanism) for attaching a heddle to a frame. This is a well-known mechanical engineering principle with no novel problem-solving mechanism beyond basic mechanical interlocking. The specific application to textile heddles does not introduce a transferable causal operation.

abstract: An improved apparatus for filtering down-hole drilling fluids, insertable at any point in the drill string, i.e.: tool joints or within instrument subs. The filter element is a disk insertable between the two threadably connected ends of any two lengths of the drill string or adaptively placed within a tool joint containing down-hole tools such as data gathering instruments. The filter is essentially a disk having a series of expanding concentric radial slots and may be used in combination with an X collar support ring insert, combined with a sleeve having a landing ring or provided with a retrieval means.
problem: Down-hole drilling operations require filtration of drilling fluids at arbitrary points along the drill string, but the filter must fit within the existing connection geometry without disrupting the threaded connections or requiring major modifications to the drill string.
constraint: The filter disk must be thin enough to fit between connected drill string sections without altering the connection geometry, while the slot design must simultaneously provide adequate filtration, sufficient flow capacity, and structural strength to withstand high pressure and abrasive drilling fluids.
mechanism: A thin disk with expanding radial flow paths is inserted between connected sections of a tubular structure. The expanding flow path geometry increases effective filtration surface area while maintaining structural integrity under pressure, balancing filtration performance with mechanical strength. The disk form factor allows placement at any connection point without altering the connection geometry.
mechanism_raw: A thin disk filter with expanding concentric radial slots is inserted between threadably connected drill string sections. The expanding radial slot geometry increases the effective filtration surface area as fluid flows outward from the center, while the disk form factor allows it to be placed at any connection point. The expanding slots balance increased flow path length (better filtration) with structural integrity needed to withstand high down-hole pressures.

abstract: During non-use of tank (53), a connector for dispensing liquid from the tank has no portion projecting from the tank, keeps the tank in its sealed condition, and makes no disturbance. Provided in drum cap (51) threadably engaged with a neck of the tank are liquid outlet plug installation hole (55) and dual-purpose gas/liquid inlet plug installation hole (56). Siphon tube (59) extending downward to the bottom of the tank is provided inside hole. (55) of liquid plug (57) an upper surface of which does not extend beyond an upper surface of the drumcap. Dual-purpose gas/liquidplug (70) is provided inside the hole (56) not having its upper surface extend beyond the upper surface of the drum cap. Caps (62 and 75) are detachably fitted in the liquid plug and the gas/liquid plug, respectively, to seal upper openings of these plugs (57 and 70), respectively.
problem: A liquid dispensing connector for a tank must not protrude from the tank or disturb its sealed condition during non-use, while still being readily accessible for dispensing when needed.
constraint: The plugs must be recessed sufficiently to avoid protrusion while remaining accessible for connection. The sealing caps must provide reliable sealing to maintain tank integrity, and the dual-purpose plug design must handle both gas and liquid functions without cross-contamination or failure.
mechanism: Recessed access points are positioned below a surface boundary, with removable sealing elements that maintain a sealed condition when not in use. The access points are designed so their exposed surfaces do not extend beyond the boundary, preventing protrusion while allowing connection when sealing elements are removed. The design accommodates dual functional pathways without cross-interference.
mechanism_raw: The connector uses recessed plugs that sit flush with or below the drum cap surface, with removable sealing caps that maintain the tank's sealed condition when not in use. The plugs are designed so their upper surfaces do not extend beyond the drum cap, ensuring no portion projects from the tank. When dispensing is needed, the caps are removed and the plugs provide access to the siphon tube and dual-purpose gas/liquid inlet.

abstract: The invention relates to the use of polyolefin waxes as external lubricants and release agents for plastics. Said polyolefin waxes are produced by using metallocene catalysts, whereby the polyolefin waxes are homopolymerizates of ethylene or are copolymerizates of ethylene with one or more 1-olefins, and linear or branched, substituted or non-substituted olefins having 3–18 C atoms are used as 1-olefins. The processable plastic mixtures produced in this manner have a distinctively longer tack-free time and exhibit an improved behavior with regard to mold release.
problem: Plastic processing requires external lubricants and release agents that provide longer tack-free time and improved mold release behavior, but conventional waxes may not offer optimal molecular structure for these properties.
constraint: The catalyst type and monomer selection must be carefully controlled to produce waxes with the target molecular weight and structure. The wax properties must balance lubrication effectiveness with other processing requirements such as thermal stability and compatibility with the plastic matrix.
mechanism: A catalytic process produces materials with precisely controlled molecular architecture, including narrow molecular weight distribution and controlled branching. This controlled structure optimizes crystallinity and surface properties to achieve desired functional characteristics such as lubrication and release behavior. The catalyst and monomer selection directly determine the material's performance properties.
mechanism_raw: Metallocene catalysts are used to produce polyolefin waxes with precisely controlled molecular structure — narrow molecular weight distribution and controlled branching (through copolymerization with specific 1-olefins). This controlled molecular architecture creates waxes with optimal crystallinity and surface properties that provide superior lubrication and release characteristics during plastic processing.

abstract: A reinforced hydroform member having an outer structural member reinforced by a structural foam supported by the outer structural member. The structural foam extends along at least a portion of the length of the outer structural member. The structural foam is a heat-activated epoxy-based resin. As the foam is heated, it expands and adheres to adjacent surfaces. The preferred structural foam material is commercially available from L&L Products of Romeo, Mich. under the designation L5206, L5207, L5208, or L5209.
problem: Reinforcing a structural member without adding bulk or complexity to the outer structure.
constraint: The foam must be heat-activated, requiring a thermal trigger to initiate expansion and adhesion, which limits application to environments where heating is feasible.
mechanism: A material that undergoes volumetric expansion and surface adhesion when exposed to a thermal trigger, creating a bonded reinforcement that integrates with an adjacent structural element without requiring additional structural layers.
mechanism_raw: Heat-activated structural foam expands and adheres to adjacent surfaces when heated, creating a bonded reinforcement that integrates with the outer structural member.

abstract: There are disclosed a production apparatus for producing a gallium nitride semiconductor film by HVPE process, a cleaning apparatus for cleaning exhaust gas coming from the above apparatus and an overall production plant for producing a gallium nitride semiconductor by HVPE process. Therein exhaust piping for exhaust gas in the production apparatus, introduction piping for the cleaning apparatus and exhaust gas piping which connects the production apparatus and the cleaning apparatus are each composed of an electroconductive corrosion-resistant material and are each electrically grounded, thereby surely preventing electrostatic charging due to friction between ammonium chloride powders in the exhaust gas and inside walls of exhaust gas piping, and markedly enhancing operational safety.
problem: Preventing electrostatic charging caused by friction between ammonium chloride powders and exhaust gas piping in semiconductor production.
constraint: Materials must simultaneously exhibit electrical conductivity and corrosion resistance, limiting options to specialized alloys or coatings.
mechanism: A conductive pathway integrated into a system to divert electrostatic charges generated by frictional contact between particulate matter and surfaces, using materials that simultaneously provide electrical continuity and resistance to chemical degradation.
mechanism_raw: Electrically grounding conductive, corrosion-resistant piping materials to dissipate static charges generated by powder-pipe friction, thereby enhancing operational safety.

abstract: A portable powered roller screed apparatus includes a rotating roller assembly, a first operator roller controller coupled to a first end of the roller assembly, and a second operator roller controller coupled to a second end of the roller assembly. The first operator roller controller includes a rotary driver, a roller mover coupled to the rotary driver, and a speed control coupled to the roller mover, the speed control providing an input to the rotary driver to control the speed of the rotary driver.
reason: The mechanism is a standard speed-control feedback loop for a motorized roller, with no novel causal relationship or unique problem-solving principle beyond conventional mechanical engineering.

abstract: In combination, pressurized fluid contained in a storage vessel, in both liquid and vapor regions, a heat exchanger in the vapor region of the vessel, and a first pressure regulator having an inlet side in communication with liquid in the vessel, and having an outlet side in communication with the heat exchanger, whereby if pressure in the vessel rises to the setting of the regulator, it opens and admits liquid from the vessel to the heat exchanger, to vaporize in that exchanger causing vapor in the vessel to condense, and reducing pressure in the vessel.
problem: Maintaining stable pressure in a pressurized fluid storage vessel containing both liquid and vapor phases.
constraint: The system requires a heat exchanger and pressure regulator to operate in tandem, with the heat exchanger needing sufficient thermal capacity to condense vapor effectively.
mechanism: A feedback-controlled system where a pressure-sensitive valve actuates liquid flow to a thermal exchange zone when a threshold is exceeded, causing vapor phase reduction through heat transfer, thereby stabilizing pressure within a containment vessel.
mechanism_raw: A pressure regulator opens when vessel pressure exceeds a threshold, admitting liquid to a heat exchanger where vaporization causes vapor condensation, thereby reducing pressure.

abstract: A setting apparatus for a remote monitoring and controlling system allows a decrease in the size of a portable unit. The setting apparatus includes a stationary unit fixed to an installation surface and a portable unit detachably attached to the stationary unit. A battery receiving portion for receiving a battery is protruded backwardly from the rear surface of the portable unit. By receiving the battery receiving portion of the portable unit in a reception concave portion of the stationary unit and engaging a coupling convex portion with a coupling concave portion of the battery receiving portion, the portable unit is detachably attached to the stationary unit. Since the coupling concave portion for coupling to the stationary unit is formed in the battery receiving portion of the portable unit, the portable unit has a decreased size, compared with a case when the portion coupled to the stationary unit is provided independent of the battery receiving portion.
problem: Reducing the size of a portable unit in a remote monitoring system while maintaining secure attachment to a stationary base.
constraint: The coupling and battery functions must coexist in the same physical space, requiring precise geometric alignment and material compatibility to avoid interference.
mechanism: A modular interface design that co-locates mechanical attachment and power storage functions within a single geometric envelope, using complementary engagement surfaces to enable secure coupling while minimizing spatial footprint.
