mechanism_raw: Integrating the coupling mechanism (convex/concave engagement) into the battery-receiving portion of the portable unit, eliminating redundant structural elements and minimizing overall dimensions.

abstract: A flame detection system includes a plurality of sensors for generating a plurality of respective sensor signals. The plurality of sensors includes a set of discrete optical radiation sensors responsive to flame as well as non-flame emissions. An Artificial Neural Network may be applied in processing the sensor signals to provide an output corresponding to a flame condition.
problem: Accurately detecting flame conditions while distinguishing them from non-flame emissions in a sensor-rich environment.
constraint: Balancing false positives (non-flame triggers) and false negatives (missed flames) while maintaining real-time processing speed and adaptability to varying environmental conditions.
mechanism: Using a plurality of diverse sensing elements to generate distinct signal types, processed by a learning-based correlator that dynamically weights and combines the signals to identify target conditions while suppressing non-target signals. The learning-based correlator adapts its weighting over time to maintain discrimination accuracy under varying environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using a plurality of discrete optical and non-optical sensors to generate diverse sensor signals, which are processed by an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to correlate multi-modal inputs and produce an output corresponding to flame conditions. The ANN learns to weight and combine sensor signals to differentiate flame signatures from background noise or non-flame emissions.
residual_terms: ["learning-based correlator", "dynamically weights", "diverse sensing elements", "distinct signal types"]

abstract: A catadioptric projection objective which images a pattern arranged in an object plane of the projection objective into the image plane of the projection objective while generating a real intermediate image has a catadioptric objective part having at least one concave mirror and a beam deflecting device and also a dioptric objective part. The imaging system has a system diaphragm having a variable diaphragm diameter for variably limiting the cross section of the radiation passing through the projection objective. This system diaphragm is arranged in the catadioptric objective part, preferably in direct proximity to the concave mirror. The invention enables a projection objective with a simple construction.
problem: Creating a catadioptric projection objective with a simple construction while maintaining imaging quality and variable aperture control.
constraint: Maintaining image quality and minimizing aberrations while varying the diaphragm diameter, as the diaphragm's position near the mirror directly affects the optical path and beam shaping.
mechanism: Placing an adjustable aperture element in direct proximity to a focusing reflective surface within an optical system to control the cross-section of radiation passing through. This localized aperture placement allows precise modulation of the beam path without introducing additional optical elements, enabling a simplified overall design while maintaining imaging quality.
mechanism_raw: Placing a variable diaphragm in direct proximity to a concave mirror within the catadioptric objective part to control the cross-section of radiation passing through the system. This localized diaphragm placement allows precise modulation of the beam path without introducing additional complexity in the dioptric section, enabling a simplified overall design.
residual_terms: ["adjustable aperture element", "focusing reflective surface", "localized aperture placement", "cross-section of radiation"]

abstract: A track and punch SMR marking device, including a base, the base mounts for adjustment an SMR (spherically mounted retro-reflector), which in cooperation with a laser tracker beam locates the device precisely over an area where a punch mark is to be made, the base includes an upright sleeve, for holding a striker shaft, the striker shaft, at its lower end, includes a bevel, mating with the inclined surface of a cross slide, the cross slide, when it is urged forwardly, depresses a punch forcing it downwardly so as to provide a punch point or indentation upon the component to be worked.
problem: Precisely positioning a marking device over a target area and applying a controlled punch mark with mechanical accuracy.
constraint: Achieving sub-millimeter positioning accuracy via the SMR/laser tracker while maintaining sufficient mechanical force and alignment stability during the punching action.
mechanism: Using a high-precision localization system to determine the position of a marking device, coupled with a mechanical force conversion mechanism. The force conversion mechanism transforms linear motion from an actuator into a directed marking force through an inclined surface interaction, ensuring accurate application of the marking action at the located position.
mechanism_raw: Combining a laser tracker beam and spherically mounted retro-reflector (SMR) for high-precision localization of the device, coupled with a mechanical striker shaft and cross slide system. The bevel on the striker shaft interacts with the cross slide's inclined surface to convert forward motion into downward punch force, ensuring accurate indentation at the located position.
residual_terms: ["high-precision localization system", "mechanical force conversion mechanism", "inclined surface interaction", "directed marking force"]

abstract: A ventilation system for a helmet that allows for ventilation of the interior of a helmet. A ventilation system for the cheek bar portion of a helmet, including a motorcycle helmet. The ventilation system may include ribbed passageways that facilitate airflow along the interior of the helmet, and may include access openings in an intermediate portion that couple the airflow from the ribbed passageways to the area of the helmet in contact with the user.
problem: Providing effective ventilation in a helmet while maintaining structural integrity and directing airflow to areas in contact with the user.
constraint: Balancing airflow efficiency and distribution against the need for structural rigidity in the helmet, as excessive openings or poorly designed ribs could compromise safety or comfort.
mechanism: Integrating structural ribs that define internal airflow corridors along the interior of a protective shell, combined with strategically placed openings that couple airflow from the ribbed corridors to regions of direct contact with the user. The ribs provide structural support while simultaneously channeling airflow in a controlled path, and the openings ensure targeted ventilation to contact areas.
mechanism_raw: Integrating ribbed passageways along the helmet's interior to channel airflow in a controlled path, combined with strategically placed access openings that couple the airflow from the ribbed channels to regions of the helmet in direct contact with the user. The ribs act as structural supports while defining airflow corridors, and the access openings ensure targeted ventilation.
residual_terms: ["structural ribs", "airflow corridors", "protective shell", "strategically placed openings", "regions of direct contact"]

abstract: A system, comprising a plurality of slave devices collecting real time data from process stations, a master device receiving the collected data from the plurality of slave devices, wherein the master device polls the plurality of slave devices in a predetermined order and an analysis device processing the collected data and producing output data as a function of the collected data.
problem: Collecting real-time data from multiple distributed process stations and processing it efficiently to produce actionable output.
constraint: Managing polling order and timing to prevent data loss or delays, while ensuring the analysis device can process the aggregated data in real time without overwhelming system resources.
mechanism: Implementing a sequential polling architecture where a central controller queries distributed devices in a predetermined order to collect data, ensuring deterministic timing and avoiding data collisions. The collected data is then processed by an analysis device to generate output based on the aggregated inputs, enabling centralized control and decision-making.
mechanism_raw: Implementing a master-slave polling architecture where a master device sequentially polls slave devices in a predetermined order to collect data, ensuring deterministic timing and avoiding collisions. The collected data is then processed by an analysis device to generate output based on the aggregated inputs, enabling centralized control and decision-making.
residual_terms: ["sequential polling architecture", "central controller", "predetermined order", "deterministic timing", "analysis device", "aggregated inputs"]

abstract: A sliding screen frame for a closure assembly having an opening and an existing track for mounting a screen, the screen frame has framing sections with both inner and outer side edges, and a housing from which a screen is payed out and accumulated. The framing sections are adapted on the outer side edge to interfit with the existing track of the closure assembly to enable the sliding screen frame to slide across the opening of the closure assembly and the frame sections also being adapted on the inner side edge thereof to support and guide the free end of the screen between a fully payed out and a fully accumulated position. The screen frame has a mitreless corner connector for connecting adjacent framing sections without the need for mitre cuts thereof to establish continuity between the corner connector and the adjacent framing sections.
problem: Creating a sliding screen frame that can be retrofitted to an existing closure assembly with a track, without requiring mitre cuts, while simultaneously supporting and guiding the screen between payout and accumulated positions.
constraint: The frame must simultaneously provide a track-compatible sliding interface on the outer edge and a screen-guiding interface on the inner edge, while maintaining structural integrity and corner continuity without mitre cuts.
mechanism: A frame assembly uses dual-interface framing sections where one edge provides a sliding engagement with an existing track system and the opposite edge provides a guided support path for a flexible sheet material between extended and retracted positions. A corner coupling mechanism joins adjacent framing sections through complementary mechanical interlocks that establish structural continuity at junctions without requiring angled cuts or separate fastening elements.
mechanism_raw: Framing sections are designed with dual functional interfaces: the outer side edge interfits with the existing track to enable sliding motion across the opening, while the inner side edge provides a guided path that supports and directs the free end of the screen between fully payed out and fully accumulated positions. A mitreless corner connector joins adjacent framing sections without requiring mitre cuts, establishing structural continuity at corners through a mechanical interfit rather than cut-and-weld or cut-and-fasten methods.
residual_terms: ["dual-interface framing sections", "sliding engagement", "guided support path", "corner coupling mechanism", "mechanical interlocks"]

abstract: A knitted sock has an inner layer 2 comprising a toe end 4 and an outer layer 3 comprising a toe end 7. The inner and outer toe ends are aligned and joined wale stitch to wale stitch to form a composite toe end, which is closed to provide a flat toe seam 10. The layered sock is manufactured complete in a single process being knit continuously from the inner toe end to the outer toe end. It comprises reciprocated heel and toe portions. The foot portion of the inner layer is knit from a yarn with properties such as a low coefficient of friction and/or antifungal/antibacterial properties. The low friction fiber is a fluoropolymer such as polytetrafluroethylene. The outer layer may comprise a cushion structure.
problem: Manufacturing a multi-layer knitted sock with different functional properties in each layer (e.g., low-friction inner layer, cushioned outer layer) while achieving a flat, comfortable toe seam, all in a single continuous knitting process.
constraint: Must maintain distinct yarn properties in different layers while creating a flat, seamless toe closure through continuous knitting without interrupting the process or introducing separate joining steps.
mechanism: A tubular textile article is produced through continuous knitting using multiple yarn feeds with distinct material properties, creating concentric layers with different functional characteristics. The knitting process forms a closed termination at one end by aligning and joining stitch elements from opposing knitting directions, producing a flat seam without interrupting the continuous knitting operation or requiring separate joining steps.
mechanism_raw: The sock is knit continuously from the inner toe end to the outer toe end in a single process, with reciprocated heel and toe portions. The inner and outer toe ends are aligned and joined wale stitch to wale stitch to form a composite toe end, which is then closed to produce a flat toe seam. Different yarns with specific properties (e.g., fluoropolymer for low friction, antimicrobial agents) are used for the inner layer, while the outer layer may incorporate cushioning structures, all integrated during the continuous knitting process.
residual_terms: ["continuous knitting", "concentric layers", "distinct material properties", "closed termination", "flat seam", "stitch elements"]

abstract: A method for reducing the amount of mercury affixed to a sorbent and/or fly ash is disclosed. The method includes the steps of providing an amount of sorbent and/or fly ash wherein at least a portion of the amount of sorbent and/or fly ash has particulates having mercury compounds affixed to the particulates; and exposing the amount of sorbent and/or fly ash to heated flowing air until mercury compounds are liberated from at least some of the particulates. Preferably, the amount of sorbent and/or fly ash is maintained in the heated flowing air until the sorbent reaches a temperature of at least 700° F. (372° C.). When the sorbent is activated carbon, it is preferred that the amount of sorbent and/or fly ash is maintained in the heated flowing air until the activated carbon reaches a temperature in the range of 700° F. (372° C.) to 1000° F. (538° C.).
problem: Removing mercury compounds that have become affixed to sorbent or fly ash particulates, which reduces the effectiveness of the sorbent and contaminates the fly ash.
constraint: Temperature must be high enough to liberate mercury compounds from the particulates (700-1000°F for activated carbon) but not so high as to damage the sorbent structure or cause unwanted thermal degradation or secondary reactions.
mechanism: Contaminated particulate matter with adsorbed target compounds is subjected to controlled thermal energy in the presence of a flowing gas stream. The temperature is maintained within a range sufficient to break the adsorption bond between the target compounds and the particulate surfaces, causing the compounds to desorb and be carried away by the gas flow. The process continues until the target compounds are removed to a desired level.
mechanism_raw: Thermal desorption: the sorbent and/or fly ash particulates with affixed mercury compounds are exposed to heated flowing air. The elevated temperature (at least 700°F, or 700-1000°F for activated carbon) causes the mercury compounds to be liberated from the particulate surfaces, and the flowing air carries the liberated compounds away from the particulates. The process continues until the mercury compounds are sufficiently removed.
residual_terms: ["thermal energy", "flowing gas stream", "adsorption bond", "desorb", "temperature range", "particulate surfaces"]

abstract: Method and apparatus for providing high strength, low frequency tactile sensations using an inertial actuator in a haptic feedback interface device, such as an actuator driving an oscillating inertial mass. A commanded low frequency is modulated or combined with a higher frequency at which the tactile sensations feel stronger, where the resulting signal is used to output a tactile sensation at the higher frequency and convey the commanded low frequency to the user. One embodiment provides higher frequency pulse bursts at the desired low frequency wherein the higher frequency pulse bursts are at or near a resonant frequency of the actuator; other embodiments modulate or otherwise vary the amplitude of the higher frequency signal according to the desired low frequency.
problem: Producing strong, perceptible tactile sensations at low frequencies using an inertial actuator, which inherently produces weaker sensations at low frequencies due to the physics of inertial mass oscillation.
constraint: The high-frequency carrier must be at or near the actuator's resonant frequency to maximize tactile strength, while the modulation scheme must preserve the low-frequency information so the user correctly perceives the intended tactile command.
mechanism: A low-frequency command signal is used to modulate a high-frequency carrier signal that operates near the mechanical resonance of an inertial vibration source. The carrier signal produces strong tactile output due to resonant amplification, while the command signal controls the amplitude of the carrier to encode the low-frequency information. The resulting tactile output has enhanced strength at low frequencies while preserving the original command's informational content.
mechanism_raw: Frequency modulation: a commanded low-frequency tactile signal is used to modulate a higher-frequency carrier signal that is at or near the resonant frequency of the inertial actuator. The high-frequency carrier produces strong tactile sensations because the actuator operates most efficiently near its resonant frequency. The amplitude of the high-frequency carrier is varied according to the low-frequency command, so the user perceives strong high-frequency pulses whose envelope conveys the intended low-frequency information. Alternatively, higher-frequency pulse bursts are delivered at the desired low frequency rate.
residual_terms: ["low-frequency command signal", "high-frequency carrier signal", "mechanical resonance", "inertial vibration source", "resonant amplification", "amplitude modulation"]

abstract: A variable vane arrangement (36) for a compressor (26) of a gas turbine engine (10) comprises a plurality of circumferentially arranged vanes (38), a plurality of operating levers (64) and a control ring (66). Each vane (38) is pivotally mounted to a casing (30) of the compressor (26). Each operating lever (64) is pivotally mounted at a first end (68) to the control ring (66) and is mounted at second end (70) to a respective one of the vanes (38). The second end (70) of each operating lever (64) comprises a multi-sided aperture (72) and each vane (38) has a multi-sided spindle (60) which locates in the multi-sided aperture (72) of the respective operating lever (64). Each operating lever (64) has a drive member (74) located in the multi-sided aperture (72) and around the multi-sided spindle (60) of the respective vane (38). Each drive member (74) engages the respective multi-sided aperture (72) and the respective multi-sided spindle (60) to transmit drive from the operating lever (64) to the vane (38).
problem: Transmitting drive torque from a control ring to individual pivoting vanes in a compressor of a gas turbine engine, where each vane requires precise angular positioning while being pivotally mounted to the compressor casing.
constraint: The multi-sided interface must simultaneously allow pivotal rotation of the vane while transmitting torque without slippage, and the drive member must engage both the lever's aperture and the vane's spindle surfaces concurrently to ensure reliable torque transfer.
mechanism: Rotary torque is transmitted from a control element to a pivoting component through a multi-surface coupling interface. The pivoting component has a multi-faceted shaft portion that is pivotally mounted, and the control element has a corresponding multi-faceted receiving portion. An intermediate drive member engages both the receiving portion and the shaft portion simultaneously, creating multiple contact points that prevent relative rotation while allowing pivotal movement of the component.
mechanism_raw: Multi-sided torque coupling: each vane has a multi-sided (polygonal) spindle that is pivotally mounted to the casing. Each operating lever has a multi-sided aperture that receives the vane's spindle. A drive member is positioned within the multi-sided aperture around the multi-sided spindle, engaging both the aperture walls and the spindle surfaces to transmit torque from the operating lever to the vane. The multi-sided geometry prevents rotational slippage while the pivotal mounting allows the vane to pivot as the control ring moves the operating levers.
residual_terms: ["multi-surface coupling interface", "multi-faceted shaft portion", "multi-faceted receiving portion", "intermediate drive member", "multiple contact points", "pivotal movement"]

abstract: A footwear cushioning system including an insole and a midsole that define a chamber containing multiple, hollow, inverted, truncated cones. The insole includes a plate having a downwardly extending rib to define a recess. The midsole includes a midsole plate including an upwardly extending wall and multiple upwardly opening hollow, inverted frusto-conical cushion cells. The wall interfits within the rib, and the cushion cells abut against the insole plate. An outsole shell is direct-attached to the cushioning system with polyurethane. Preferably, the polyurethane pre-compresses the cushion cells and adds cushioning and energy return characteristics. To assemble the cushion system, an upper is stapled to the insole rib. The midsole is interfitted within the rib. The insole and midsole are heated to fuse the cushion cells to the insole. Polyurethane is poured into the outsole shell and the shell is direct attached to the upper/cushioning system.
problem: Creating a cushioning system that provides both impact absorption and energy return in footwear
constraint: Balancing cushioning compliance with energy return efficiency while maintaining structural stability under repeated loading
mechanism: Use compressible elements that deform under load to absorb energy and recover their shape to return energy, with structural interlocking between components to maintain alignment and integrity during repeated compression cycles
mechanism_raw: Pre-compressed hollow inverted truncated cones deform under load to absorb energy, then recover their shape to return energy, with structural interlocking between insole and midsole components to maintain alignment and integrity during compression cycles

abstract: A method to enhance grain size in polysilicon films while avoiding formation of hemispherical grains (HSG) is disclosed. The method begins by depositing a first amorphous silicon film, then depositing silicon nuclei, which will act as nucleation sites, on the amorphous film. After deposition of silicon nuclei, crystallization, and specifically HSG, is prevented by lowering temperature and/or raising pressure. Next a second amorphous silicon layer is deposited over the first layer and the nuclei. Finally an anneal is performed to induce crystallization from the embedded nuclei. Thus grains are formed from the silicon bulk, rather than from the surface, HSG is avoided, and a smooth polysilicon film with enhanced grain size is produced.
problem: Controlling grain growth in polysilicon films to enhance grain size while preventing unwanted hemispherical grain formation
constraint: Preventing surface nucleation (HSG) while enabling sufficient bulk nucleation to achieve desired grain size enhancement
mechanism: Embed nucleation sites within a material layer and suppress surface crystallization through environmental control, then induce bulk crystallization from the embedded nuclei to direct grain growth inward rather than from the surface
mechanism_raw: Embedding nucleation sites within an amorphous layer and suppressing surface crystallization through temperature/pressure control, then inducing bulk crystallization from the embedded nuclei during annealing to direct grain growth inward rather than from the surface

abstract: When electrical properties of semiconductor chips of a semiconductor wafer are inspected by bringing plural contact terminals disposed on the principal surface of a probe sheet of a probe cassette constituting a semiconductor inspection apparatus into contact with plural electrodes of the plural semiconductor chips on the principal surface of the semiconductor wafer which is disposed so as to face the principal surface of the probe sheet, the air pressure of the space formed between the facing surfaces of the principal surface of the probe sheet and the principal surface of the semiconductor wafer is reduced so as to suck the semiconductor wafer toward the side of the principal surface of the probe sheet and deform mainly the semiconductor wafer, thereby pressing the plural electrodes of the plural semiconductor chips of the semiconductor wafer against the plural facing contact terminals of the principal surface of the probe sheet.
problem: Ensuring reliable electrical contact between probe terminals and semiconductor wafer electrodes during inspection
constraint: Applying sufficient uniform pressure to achieve contact without damaging the wafer or probe terminals
mechanism: Create a pressure differential in a gap to generate a suction force that deforms a flexible element, mechanically pressing electrical contacts together through controlled elastic deformation
mechanism_raw: Reducing air pressure in the gap between probe sheet and wafer creates a suction force that deforms the wafer toward the probe sheet, mechanically pressing electrodes against contact terminals through controlled elastic deformation

abstract: An organic EL display device and a method of producing the same wherein superior connection reliability can be obtained between a thin film transistor and a lower electrode of an organic EL element even if a color-converting medium is provided adjacent light-emitting face of the organic EL element. For this purpose, in an active-driving type organic EL display device comprising an organic EL element made so as to have an organic luminous medium sandwiched between an upper electrode and a lower electrode, and a thin film transistor for controlling luminescence of the organic EL element, the luminescence of the organic EL element is taken out from the lower electrode, a color-converting medium is provided adjacent the lower electrode, and an inclined electrically connecting member is set between the lower electrode and the thin film transistor.
problem: Maintaining electrical connection reliability between thin film transistors and organic EL elements when a color-converting medium is present
constraint: Ensuring the inclined connector does not interfere with light emission or adjacent components while providing reliable electrical contact
mechanism: Position an angled conductive element between two components to bypass an intervening medium while maintaining electrical continuity through angular alignment
mechanism_raw: Positioning an inclined electrically connecting member between the lower electrode and TFT allows the connection to bypass or accommodate the color-converting medium while maintaining electrical continuity through angular alignment

abstract: Heat exchanger plates for indirect evaporative coolers, of the type having a dry side having low permeability to an evaporative liquid and formed to allow a product fluid to flow over a heat transfer area of its surface, a wet side designed to have its surface wet by an evaporative liquid, and formed to allow a working gas to flow over its surface to evaporate the evaporative liquid, further include edge extensions formed beyond the heat exchange area of the plates to facilitate removal of excess evaporative liquid. The edge extensions may slant or curve away from the wet side of the plates to assist in liquid removal. The plates may be used in a variety of configurations.
problem: Removing excess evaporative liquid from heat exchanger plates in indirect evaporative cooling systems
constraint: Maintaining effective heat transfer area while ensuring liquid removal does not disrupt working gas flow or structural integrity
mechanism: Use geometric features on edges that slant or curve to create pathways directing excess liquid away via surface tension and gravitational forces, maintaining heat transfer area while facilitating drainage
mechanism_raw: Edge extensions that slant or curve away from the wet side create a geometric pathway that uses surface tension and gravitational forces to direct excess liquid away from the heat exchange surface and facilitate drainage

abstract: A method of assigning a channel identification (ID) of an audio signal by which it is possible to follow up and select the audio channel selected by a user even though a program or an audio data stream is changed in an audio/video (A/V) device for reproducing a program including a plurality of audio data streams, a method of selecting audio channels using the same, and an apparatus suitable therefor. The method of selecting the audio channels of an A/V data stream including a plurality of programs, each program including at least two kinds of audio data streams, each audio data stream including at least two sub-audio data streams which are not repeated and having a series of IDs according to a predetermined order of precedence, the method including (a) when a program is changed to another program, searching whether there is a sub-audio data stream having a channel ID which is the same as the channel ID assigned to the sub-audio data stream of the program which was being reproduced before the program was changed, in the changed program, and (b) when it is determined that there is the sub-audio data stream having a channel ID which is the same as the channel ID assigned to the sub-audio data stream of the program which was being reproduced before the program was changed in the step (a), selecting the sub-audio data stream. According to the method of selecting the audio channels, it is possible to follow up a voice mode selected by a user (maintain the previously selected audio channel) although a program or an audio data stream is changed.
problem: Maintaining a user-selected audio channel across program or data stream changes in an A/V device.
constraint: Requires a consistent ID assignment system across all programs to ensure reliable matching.
mechanism: Preserving user-selected preferences across context changes by maintaining a consistent identifier system that enables automatic matching of equivalent data streams between prior and subsequent contexts.
mechanism_raw: Tracking and preserving user preferences by matching channel IDs between the previous and new programs, enabling automatic selection of the equivalent sub-audio data stream.

abstract: An improved escalator or moving walk construction, head elements are pre-assembled as a sub-assembly which is subsequently mounted on the truss of the escalator. The sub-assembly includes comb plate holders, one on each side, which carry a comb plate. The comb plate holder may have a C-shaped profile and may be reinforced by stiffening ribs so as to be able to bear the weight of the end-curve of a balustrade. By means of supports arranged on the truss, the height of the comb plate carrier can be adjusted to that of the truss. During pre-assembly, and until after final mounting on the truss, the comb plate serves as a connecting element between comb plate holders.
problem: Efficiently assembling complex mechanical systems (e.g., escalators) with precise alignment and structural integrity during pre-assembly.
constraint: The temporary element must be removable without compromising final structural stability.
mechanism: Using a temporary structural element to maintain alignment and coherence of sub-components during pre-assembly, allowing positional adjustment via support structures until final mounting secures the system.
mechanism_raw: Using a temporary connecting element (comb plate) during sub-assembly to maintain alignment and structural coherence until final mounting, allowing height adjustment via truss supports.

abstract: A machine for processing, in particular for cutting workpieces in the form of slabs, comprises a spindle (36) slidably supported by a beam (32) displaceable transversely with respect to the longitudinal direction of a working surface (12). The beam is in turn slidably supported at its ends by two bridge structures (22, 24) situated at the two ends of said working surface. The spindle (36) is rotatably adjustable through 360° about its vertical axis and supports a disk cutting tool (60) which may be secured thereon or picked from a tools magazine also comprising other tools and a plurality of cutting heads. When other tools are used, allows other machining operations than cutting can be performed by the machine. The working surface consists of a conveyor belt (14) made of rubber, in particular disposable rubber, and is supported at the bottom by a fixed metal surface. The machine according to the invention is suitable for insertion along a continuous processing line.
problem: Enabling versatile cutting/machining operations on a continuous processing line with multi-axis tool positioning.
constraint: Balancing tool flexibility and movement range with the need for continuous, uninterrupted processing.
mechanism: Combining multi-axis tool positioning with a continuously moving work surface to enable dynamic spatial control of processing elements while maintaining uninterrupted material flow.
mechanism_raw: Combining transverse beam movement, 360° spindle rotation, and a conveyor-based work surface to allow dynamic tool positioning and continuous material handling.

abstract: A method of operating an internal combustion engine having a combustion chamber with a piston and a spark plug, when transitioning between spark ignition combustion and autoignition combustion, creating a first mixture of air and fuel, adjusting an operating condition of the engine so that said first mixture of air and fuel in the combustion chamber approaches, but does not achieve, the autoignition temperature, and performing a spark from the spark plug so that at least a portion of said first mixture combusts to raise a remaining portion of said first mixture to said autoignition temperature.
problem: Smoothly transitioning between spark ignition and autoignition combustion modes in an internal combustion engine.
constraint: Precisely managing mixture composition and temperature to avoid premature autoignition or incomplete combustion.
mechanism: Initiating a staged reaction by triggering a controlled initial ignition of a portion of a reactive mixture, which then transfers energy to the remaining mixture to achieve a self-sustaining transition to a secondary combustion mode.
mechanism_raw: Using a controlled spark to ignite a portion of the air-fuel mixture, which then raises the remaining mixture to autoignition temperature, enabling a self-sustaining transition.

abstract: On the one hand, the invention relates to a method for weaving face-to-face fabrics on a face-to-face weaving machine, the fabrics (10),(20) consisting of weft yarns (2), ground warp yarns (3) and pile warp yarns (4), and one or several spacers (1) being provided in order to keep the fabrics (10),(20) at a distance during the weaving process, and a weaving reed being provided, comprising reed dents (A),(B),(C) through which the said ground warp yarns (3) and pile warp yarns (4) are extending, and through which the spacers (1) are extending every two or more reed dents (A),(B),(C), wherein the pile warp yarns (4) and the spacers (1) are separated from one another in the respective reed dents (A),(B),(C). On the other hand, the invention relates to a fabric woven in accordance with such a method and a face-to-face weaving machine designed to carry out such a method.
problem: Maintaining separation between two fabric layers during face-to-face weaving while allowing yarn and spacer passage through reed dents.
constraint: Ensuring spacers do not disrupt the weaving process or compromise fabric quality.
mechanism: Integrating spaced elements within a structured grid to maintain separation between adjacent layers while permitting passage of auxiliary components through the same grid, preventing interference between functional elements.
mechanism_raw: Integrating spacers into reed dents at regular intervals to physically separate the fabric layers, while isolating pile warp yarns and spacers within the same dents to prevent interference.

abstract: In a roller adjustment apparatus for an extrusion mill, comprising a cylindrical die (2) with radially extending extrusion channels and a number of rollers (1) within the die, rotatable about their axes and co-operating with the die to press material to be treated through the extrusion channels in the die wall, the adjustment apparatus comprises eccentrically journalled bearing shafts (3) for mounting the rollers (1), said eccentrically journalling of the shafts (3) providing a radial adjustment of the position of the rollers (1) relative to the die (2), the rotation of the eccentrically journalled shafts (3) is provided by means of extension arms (6) fixedly mounted on the ends of the eccentrically journalled shafts (3), and said extension arms (6) being connected to an axially movable connection element (8) by means of articulated connected linkage rods (7), and said connection element (8) being connected to a rod (9) provided with its axis in the axis of the die (2) and extending to a position outside the material flow of the extrusion mill to move the connection element (8) in the direction of the axis of the die (2), said axial movement being provided manually or by means of a suitable actuator connected to the rod (9). In this way, only simple mechanical components, such as linkage rods (7) and connection elements (8) are positioned close to the rollers and these components are moved by manual adjustment or by means of suitable actuators positioned outside the aggressive environment close to the rollers of the extrusion mill.
problem: Adjusting the radial position of rollers in an extrusion mill while operating in an aggressive environment close to the rollers.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical simplicity near the rollers while enabling precise adjustment through remote actuation outside the aggressive environment.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system converts axial displacement from a remotely positioned actuator into radial adjustment of rollers via articulated extension arms and pivotable rods, isolating sensitive actuation components from a harsh operational environment.
mechanism_raw: Eccentrically journalled bearing shafts translate axial movement from a remotely positioned actuator into radial adjustment of rollers via extension arms and articulated linkage rods, isolating sensitive actuation components from the harsh environment.

abstract: Systems and methods for processing a high-lactose aqueous fluid (HLAF), such as permeate from ultrafiltration of whey fluid, are described. The preferred process includes concentrating HLAF containing from about 1 to about 35% solids, wherein at least 50% of the solids are lactose, to form a concentrated HLAF containing from about 45 to about 65% solids; further concentrating the HLAF to form a highly concentrated HLAF containing from about 70 to about 80% solids; cooling the highly concentrated HLAF with a gaseous fluid to create a cooling, concentrating, crystallizing cascade to further concentrate the HLAF to form a partially crystallized HLAF containing from about 78 to about 88% solids; and drying the partially crystallized HLAF in an air-lift dryer to form a product rich in crystalline alpha-lactose monohydrate. An air-lift dryer having diverging sidewalls and methods of using same are also disclosed.
problem: Efficiently producing crystalline alpha-lactose monohydrate from a high-lactose aqueous fluid while managing solid concentrations during processing.
constraint: Balancing solid concentrations at each stage to optimize crystallization efficiency without excessive energy input or degradation of product quality.
mechanism: A multi-stage cascade process combines controlled cooling with gaseous fluid and progressive concentration to induce crystallization, leveraging temperature and solid content gradients to drive crystal formation.
mechanism_raw: A multi-stage cascade process combines controlled cooling with gaseous fluid and progressive concentration to induce crystallization, leveraging temperature and solid content gradients to drive crystal formation.

abstract: A device for a single-acting hydraulic cylinder (1) designed to lift or pull a load upon the existence of an oil pressure on the rod-side of a cylinder piston (7), where the cylinder bottom (15) of the hydraulic cylinder (1) is provided with a drainage outlet (27) for leakage fluid, as well as an air inlet (29).
problem: Maintaining operational integrity of a single-acting hydraulic cylinder despite leakage fluid accumulation and potential pressure imbalances.
constraint: Ensuring the drainage and air inlet do not compromise the cylinder's structural integrity or interfere with load-bearing operations.
mechanism: A drainage and air intake system at the cylinder base allows leakage fluid to escape and air to enter, preventing pressure buildup and ensuring continued functionality during operation.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a drainage outlet and air inlet at the cylinder bottom allows leakage fluid to escape and air to enter, preventing pressure buildup and ensuring continued functionality during operation.

abstract: The present invention discloses a DC-to-DC step-up converter to which a logic control unit is added in order to reduce the ripples of a DC output voltage and improve the power quality. The converter of the present invention comprises a step-up circuit, a ring oscillator, a divider circuit, a PFM (pulse frequency modulation) comparator and a logic control unit. The step-up circuit is used to step up a source voltage to generate a DC output voltage. The ring oscillator is used to generate an oscillator output signal. The divider circuit receives the DC output voltage to generate a feedback voltage. The PFM comparator compares the feedback voltage with a reference voltage to generate a comparator output signal to control outputting of the oscillator output signal. The logic control unit is used to make the conductive period of a MOS transistor in the step-up circuit identical to the high-level period of an output signal of the ring oscillator to reduce the noise and the ripple of the DC output voltage of the converter.
problem: Reducing ripples in the output voltage of a DC-to-DC step-up converter to improve power quality.
constraint: Achieving synchronization between the oscillator and transistor switching without introducing additional complexity or latency in the control loop.
mechanism: A feedback-driven control unit synchronizes the switching timing of a transistor with an oscillator signal to dynamically adjust conductive periods, minimizing output voltage ripples in a power conversion circuit.
mechanism_raw: A logic control unit synchronizes the conductive period of a MOS transistor with the high-level period of a ring oscillator signal, using feedback from the output voltage to dynamically adjust switching timing and minimize noise.

abstract: Differential amplifier includes a differential amplifier circuit, a bias circuit and an output circuit. The differential amplifier circuit includes first and second differential amplifier sections. The first differential amplifier section includes a first PMOS transistor which has a source connected with a power supply line, and a first pair of PMOS transistors which have sources connected with a drain of the first PMOS and gates respectively receiving first and second input voltages. The second differential amplifier section includes a first NMOS transistor which has a source connected with a ground line, and a second pair of NMOS transistors which have sources connected with a drain of the first NMOS and gates respectively receiving the first and second input voltages. The bias circuit activates one of the amplifier sections in response to a control signal. The output circuit outputs an output signal from an output of the activated differential amplifier section.
problem: Amplifying differential input signals while minimizing power consumption in a differential amplifier circuit.
constraint: Ensuring seamless switching between amplifier sections without introducing signal distortion or delay during transitions.
mechanism: A bias circuit selectively activates either a first or second amplifier section based on a control signal, allowing only one section to operate at a time to reduce static power dissipation in a differential amplifier.
mechanism_raw: A bias circuit selectively activates either a PMOS-based or NMOS-based amplifier section based on a control signal, allowing only one section to operate at a time to reduce static power dissipation.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for removing horn substances from animal skin. The method is characterized in that animal skins are treated in an aqueous bath containing between 0.05 and 5 wt. %, in relation to the weight of the salt, of at least one compound of general formula I or the corresponding alkali metallic salts or alkaline-earth metallic salts thereof or ammonium or phosphonium salts. The aqueous bath also comprises at least one compound which catalyses the hydrolysis of peptide compounds
problem: Removing horn substances from animal skin without damaging the underlying hide structure.
constraint: The concentration of the compound must remain within 0.05–5 wt.% to balance efficacy and avoid over-degradation of the skin; the catalyst must specifically target peptide hydrolysis without affecting other skin components.
mechanism: Apply a chemical agent in a solution to catalyze selective hydrolysis of specific molecular bonds (e.g., peptide bonds in keratin) within a substrate, maintaining a concentration within a defined range to balance efficacy and prevent over-degradation. The agent accelerates bond cleavage without affecting other components.
mechanism_raw: Using a chemical compound (or its salts) in an aqueous bath that catalyzes the hydrolysis of peptide bonds in horn substances, selectively breaking down keratin-based structures while preserving the skin. The catalyst accelerates the cleavage of specific molecular bonds, enabling targeted degradation.

abstract: A water disinfection delivery treatment system first filters the supply by a particle and then a carbon filter. The partially treated flow is split in two and a first part passes through a first cutoff valve and is fed into a disinfection (iodine) chamber, filter or feeder via a flow restricter. The chamber output passes through a second solenoid driven cutoff valve. The second part is fed to a third cutoff valve and this valve's output is summed with the second valve's output and then fed into a holding tank. The tank retain's a volume such that the water remains therein for at least a period sufficient to permit a minimum 3 log reduction of pathogenic microbes. A final carbon filter is downstream of the tank as is a meter and dispenser. A method is also provided for delivering potable drinking water.
problem: Achieving reliable pathogen reduction in water treatment while managing flow dynamics and contact time.
constraint: The retention time in the holding tank must be precisely calibrated to the flow rate and disinfectant concentration to guarantee minimum 3-log reduction; the split ratio of the flow must balance throughput and treatment efficacy.
mechanism: Split a fluid flow into two streams: one treated with a disinfectant via a flow restrictor for controlled exposure, and another bypassing treatment. Recombine the streams and hold in a retention chamber for a calibrated time to achieve a target pathogen reduction. The split ratio and retention time are adjusted to balance throughput and efficacy.
mechanism_raw: Splitting the water flow into two streams: one treated with a disinfectant (iodine) via a flow restrictor to ensure controlled exposure, and another bypassing the disinfection chamber. The treated stream is recombined with the bypass stream and held in a retention tank long enough to achieve a 3-log microbial reduction. The staged treatment and retention time ensure sufficient contact between disinfectant and pathogens.

abstract: An auxiliary scanning feed mechanism has a pair of curved feed guides for guiding a stimulable phosphor sheet along a curved feed path, and first and second roller pairs rotatable in synchronism with each other for gripping and feeding the stimulable phosphor sheet along the curved feed path. The first and second roller pairs have respective first and second drive rollers disposed inwardly of respective curved sections of the curved feed guides and respective first and second driven rollers.
problem: Feeding a flexible, fragile stimulable phosphor sheet along a curved path without misalignment or damage during scanning.
constraint: The rollers must rotate in perfect synchrony to avoid differential speeds that could cause slippage or uneven stress on the sheet; the curvature of the guides must match the sheet's flexibility to prevent mechanical damage.
mechanism: Use synchronized propulsion elements (rollers) positioned along a curved path to grip and move a flexible sheet, ensuring uniform tension and alignment. The synchronization prevents differential speeds that could cause slippage or damage, while the curvature matches the sheet's flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Using two pairs of synchronized rollers (drive and driven) positioned inwardly of curved feed guides. The synchronized rotation ensures uniform gripping and propulsion of the sheet along the curved path, maintaining tension and alignment while preventing lateral displacement or buckling.

abstract: A process of combination tannage is disclosed whereby Zirconium salt is complexed with THP salt to produce wet pink leather without using any conventional dye. The resulting leathers exhibit a shrinkage temperature of more than 100° C., and other properties comparable to those of conventionally processed leathers.
problem: Producing wet pink leather with high thermal stability without using conventional dyes.
constraint: The zirconium-THP complex must form at a specific stoichiometric ratio to achieve the desired color and thermal properties; the process must avoid precipitation or uneven distribution of the complex within the leather matrix.
mechanism: Form a metal-organic complex that binds to collagen fibers in a substrate, inducing a color change and increasing thermal stability through crosslinking. The complex forms at a specific stoichiometric ratio to avoid precipitation and ensure even distribution.
mechanism_raw: Complexing zirconium salts with THP (likely a tanning agent) to form a stable metal-organic complex that binds to collagen fibers. This interaction alters the leather's molecular structure, inducing a pink hue and increasing shrinkage temperature by crosslinking collagen without requiring external dyes.

abstract: A liquid crystal material dispensing apparatus includes a spacer height measuring unit for measuring a height of a spacer on a substrate, and a liquid crystal material dispensing system for determining an amount of the liquid crystal material to be dispensed on the substrate based upon the measured spacer height and for dispensing the liquid crystal material onto the substrate.
problem: Accurately dispensing liquid crystal material onto a substrate with spacers of varying heights.
constraint: The spacer height measurement must be precise to within micrometer tolerances; the dispensing rate must be synchronized with substrate movement to avoid over- or under-dispensing in regions with varying spacer heights.
mechanism: Measure the height of spacers on a substrate using a sensor, then calculate and dispense a material (e.g., liquid crystal) in amounts proportional to the measured height. The dispensing rate is synchronized with substrate movement to maintain uniform coverage across varying spacer heights.
mechanism_raw: Measuring the height of spacers on the substrate using a dedicated sensor, then calculating the required liquid crystal volume based on the measured height to ensure uniform coverage and cell gap consistency. The dispensing system dynamically adjusts the amount dispensed per unit area to match the spacer height profile.

abstract: The invention is an electronic circuit designed for incorporation on computer memory modules such as DDR DIMMs. It couples control signals such as address bits, bank selects, enable and even clock signals between the module input connector and the memory devices. The circuit provides low propagation delay, fast rise and fall times with no overshoot or undershoot, and significantly improves timing control compared to memory modules of the present art. Capacitive loading on the motherboard is typically much less than that provided by a single memory device input and is independent of the number of memory devices per bank or the number of banks of memory devices on the memory module. For multiple memory modules connected to the memory bus, capacitive loading is essentially N times the equivalent loading for a single memory module.
problem: Maintaining signal integrity and timing control in high-speed memory modules while minimizing capacitive loading effects that degrade performance.
constraint: Balancing low propagation delay and fast signal transitions while maintaining loading independence from device count and bank configuration.
mechanism: A fixed-impedance interface decouples signal propagation delay from the number of connected devices by maintaining a constant capacitive load, ensuring consistent timing and suppressing signal distortion through impedance matching between a connector and downstream components.
mechanism_raw: The circuit decouples capacitive loading from the number of memory devices by providing a fixed, low-capacitance interface between the module connector and memory devices, ensuring consistent signal propagation delay and eliminating overshoot/undershoot through controlled impedance matching.

abstract: A bookmark (12) uses an integrated electronic timer circuit (18) to track reading time. A flat substrate (14) marks the page of the book. A header (16) is integral with the substrate. The header has a cavity for housing the electronic timer, a display (20) for displaying the timer count value, and a plurality of control buttons (22-28) for controlling the electronic timer. A sensor (54) can sense an external condition such as light or touch to control the electronic timer. A light source (56) is provided in the header. The substrate may contain a magnifying viewing port. The electronic timer has a memory (42) for storing the timer count values for individual and cumulative reading sessions.
reason: The patent describes a product with integrated features (timer, sensor, display) but does not articulate a causal mechanism for solving a broader problem beyond the specific application of a reading timer.

abstract: A dished head header assembly for a heat exchanger having a containment body that includes a rounded, or dished, wall portion forming an interior cavity. A flange attaches to the containment body and fastens the header assembly to the heat exchanger. A plurality of refrigerant passageways are extended through an opening in the containment body into the interior cavity. At least one baffle is attached to the rounded wall portion. The baffle divides the interior cavity into a plurality of sub-cavities. At least one divider divides the sub-cavities into a plurality of chambers. The plurality of passageways includes an inlet connection and an outlet connection for a plurality of refrigerant circuits. Each passageway is disposed in a corresponding chamber of the plurality of chambers. Extensions into the headers with diffusers insure efficient operation and performance of the heat exchanger. The adjustable flow restrictor plate maintains optimum velocities to further enhance performance.
problem: Achieving efficient refrigerant flow distribution and heat transfer in a heat exchanger while maintaining structural integrity and optimal velocity profiles.
constraint: Balancing flow velocity and heat transfer performance through geometric partitioning while maintaining structural support and minimizing pressure drop.
mechanism: Internal partitioning elements segment a flow cavity into discrete sub-regions, each containing directional flow guides that regulate velocity profiles and distribute fluid uniformly while preserving structural continuity and minimizing pressure loss.
mechanism_raw: Baffles and dividers segment the interior cavity into sub-cavities and chambers, each housing a dedicated passageway with diffusers to direct flow, ensuring uniform distribution and preventing stagnation or turbulence that reduces efficiency.

abstract: Embodiments of the present invention form a weight-compensating/tuning layer on a structure (e.g., a silicon wafer with one or more layers of material (e.g., films)) having variations in its surface topology. The variations in surface topology take the form of thick and thin regions of materials. The weight-compensating/tuning layer includes narrow and wide regions corresponding to the thick and thin regions, respectively.
problem: Compensating for weight variations caused by surface topology differences (thick/thin regions) in a layered structure to achieve uniform mass distribution.
constraint: Matching the compensating layer's geometry to the substrate's topology to ensure precise weight balance without altering the functional properties of the underlying structure.
mechanism: A compensating layer with spatially varying geometry is applied in inverse correspondence to a substrate's topology, where regions of greater extent offset areas of reduced substrate thickness to achieve balanced mass distribution without altering functional properties.
mechanism_raw: A weight-compensating layer with variable widths (narrow/wide regions) is deposited inversely to the underlying topology, where wider regions offset thinner substrate areas and narrower regions align with thicker areas, balancing total mass.

abstract: Disclosed is a small-sized vibration type gyrosensor device of high sensitivity provided with a cantilevered oscillator. A cantilevered oscillator 11, provided with a lower electrode, a piezoelectric film and an upper electrode, formed on a single-crystal silicon substrate by a thin film forming process, includes, as an upper electrode, a driving electrode 6a, formed along the length of the oscillator 11 for applying the voltage for causing oscillations of the oscillator 11, and first and second detection electrodes 6b, 6c, formed on both sides of the driving electrode 6a parallel to the longitudinal direction of the oscillator, without contacting with the driving electrode 6a. With a width W0 of the driving electrode 6a, a width W1 of the first detection electrode 6b, a width W2 of the second detection electrode 6c and with W=W0+W1+W2, the condition of 0.5<(W0/W)<1 is to be met.
problem: Achieving high sensitivity in a compact vibration-type gyrosensor while minimizing cross-talk between driving and detection electrodes.
constraint: Balancing electrode width ratios to maximize oscillation amplitude and detection sensitivity without electrical or mechanical interference between adjacent electrodes.
mechanism: Electrode dimensions are optimized via a width ratio constraint between a primary actuation electrode and the total electrode span, ensuring sufficient oscillation energy while maintaining physical and electrical separation between sensing electrodes to suppress cross-talk.
mechanism_raw: The driving electrode width (W0) is optimized relative to the total electrode width (W) such that 0.5 < W0/W < 1, ensuring sufficient driving force for oscillation while maintaining adequate spacing between detection electrodes (W1, W2) to isolate sensing signals.

abstract: The operation of a doctor assembly (16) in a paper machine is monitored. In case of a malfunction, the paper machine's (10) control devices (14-14′, 15) are used to carry out the necessary measures for eliminating the malfunction and carrying out repair and/or protective measures. In addition, detector devices (20) are arranged in connection with the doctor assembly (16), to detect a malfunction. The detector devices (20) are connected to the control devices (14, 14′, 15) of the paper machine (10), in order to carry out the said measures automatically. The invention also relates to doctor assemblies in a paper machine for implementing the method.
problem: Automatically detecting and correcting malfunctions in a paper machine's doctor assembly without manual intervention.
constraint: The system must operate in real-time within the harsh industrial environment of a paper machine, requiring robust sensor integration and rapid response without disrupting production.
mechanism: Deploy a distributed sensing network integrated with a central control system to monitor operational parameters of a mechanical subsystem in real-time, automatically triggering corrective actions (e.g., repair, shutdown, or reconfiguration) when deviations exceed predefined thresholds, ensuring continuous operation without manual intervention in a high-vibration, high-moisture environment.
mechanism_raw: Integrating detector devices with the machine's control system to sense malfunctions and trigger automated corrective actions (e.g., repair or protective measures) via the existing control infrastructure.
residual_terms: ["distributed sensing network", "central control system", "corrective actions", "predefined thresholds"]

abstract: An ant sculpture is formed by removing a block of nutritious gel having with a network of ant tunnels from a formicarium container; placing the block in an p.v.c bag that serves as a release liner; and stuffing the bag containing the gel block back into the container. The tunnel network is then filled with a transparent epoxy resin which is permitted to harden in the tunnel network; the bag containing the gel body with set epoxy removed from the container and, the gel is then separated so that the hardened epoxy forms an ant sculpture replicating the network of ant tunnels. The epoxy resin is Bisphenol A epoxy resin.
problem: Creating a precise replica of a complex, naturally occurring tunnel network (e.g., ant tunnels) in a durable material.
constraint: The sacrificial material (gel) must be removable without damaging the hardened resin structure, and the barrier must allow resin penetration while containing the gel during the process.
mechanism: Form a temporary sacrificial structure with a complex internal geometry, encapsulate it within a permeable containment barrier that allows fluid ingress while retaining the sacrificial material, fill the internal voids with a hardenable medium, then remove the sacrificial structure to leave a solidified replica of the original geometry.
mechanism_raw: Using a sacrificial gel structure with the desired tunnel network as a mold, encapsulating it in a removable barrier (PVC bag), filling the tunnels with a hardenable resin, then removing the gel to leave a resin replica.

abstract: A therapeutic bra (100) for reducing breast tissue inflammation in a woman who has recently undergone breast surgery. The therapeutic bra (100) is made up of a sports bra (110), which comprises a front breast section (120), opposite bra sides (140, 160), first (180) and second (200) shoulder straps, and a rear section (220) located between the first (140) and second (160) opposite bra sides. The front breast section (120) comprises an outer layer (260) made up of hook and loop fastener material (125) such as hooks, loops, alone or in combination, and a therapeutic pouch (115). The therapeutic pouch (115) comprises front (280) and rear (300) sides, an opening (320), and an interior (330) accessible via opening (320). The rear side (300) is at least partly covered with complementary hooks, loops, alone or in combination (310) to reversibly attach to the outer layer (260).
problem: Providing adjustable, secure therapeutic support to a specific body region (e.g., breast tissue) after surgery while allowing repositioning.
constraint: The fastening system must balance secure attachment during movement with ease of repositioning, while maintaining sterility and comfort for post-surgical use.
mechanism: Implement a bidirectional mechanical coupling system between a therapeutic module and a wearable base layer, enabling repeated attachment/detachment cycles while maintaining positional stability during movement, with adjustable engagement force to balance security and repositioning ease.
mechanism_raw: Using a reversible hook-and-loop fastening system to attach a therapeutic pouch to a base garment (sports bra), enabling repositioning and secure attachment of the pouch to deliver targeted therapy.
residual_terms: ["bidirectional mechanical coupling system", "therapeutic module", "wearable base layer", "adjustable engagement force"]

abstract: A method for the supply of a constant-concentration ozonated water, employs a unit for producing ozonated water and a system for using the ozonated water at a place separated therefrom, interposing an ozonated water circulating line between the ozonated water producing unit and the place for using the ozonated water, causing the interior of the circulating line to circulate the ozonated water so that the flow rate may be constantly fixed at the outlet of the ozonated water producing unit, monitoring the ozone concentration of the ozonated water in the neighborhood of the outlet, adjusting the amount of an ozone gas supplied to the ozonated water producing unit based on the results of the monitoring, further monitoring the amount of the ozonated water used at the place for using the ozonated water, and controlling the amount of the ozonated water to be produced based on the results of this monitoring.
problem: Maintaining a constant ozone concentration in ozonated water despite variable usage rates and production demands.
constraint: The system must balance ozone dissolution kinetics (to maintain concentration) with water production rates (to meet demand) without over- or under-supplying ozone, which could degrade water quality or waste resources.
mechanism: Operate two independent feedback control loops: one regulating input of a reactive substance based on real-time concentration measurements at the production source, and another modulating output flow rate based on demand measurements at the consumption endpoint, dynamically balancing supply and usage to maintain target levels despite variable load conditions.
mechanism_raw: Implementing dual feedback loops: one to adjust ozone gas input based on real-time concentration monitoring near the production unit, and another to adjust water production volume based on usage monitoring at the point of use.
residual_terms: ["reactive substance", "concentration measurements", "production source", "output flow rate", "demand measurements", "consumption endpoint", "target levels"]

abstract: A microwave oven including: a main casing forming a component compartment and a cooking compartment and formed with a component compartment through portion communicating with the component compartment; a fan assembly coupled to the main casing, and including an exhaling fan blowing air toward the component compartment through portion to cool the component compartment and a fan motor driving the exhaling fan; and a guide unit mounted to the component compartment through portion and guiding the air blown by the exhaling fan toward a heating component accommodated in the component compartment.
reason: The mechanism is a standard cooling approach (directed airflow via fan and guide) with no novel causal principle beyond conventional thermal management techniques. It does not solve a unique problem through a transferable functional relationship.

abstract: A polyolefin plaque is made by hot compaction of an assembly of fibres of the oriented polymer. It has been found to be beneficial to subject the fibres to a prior crosslinking process. Hot compaction is then less temperature-sensitive and produces plaques with excellent hot strength properties. Preferably the fibres have been subjected to prior stages of irradiation and annealing, both in a non-oxidising environment, for example acetylene.
problem: Hot compaction of polyolefin fibers is temperature-sensitive, leading to poor hot strength in the resulting plaques.
constraint: The crosslinking process must occur in a non-oxidizing environment (e.g., acetylene) to prevent degradation, and the annealing step must balance crosslink density with structural integrity.
mechanism: Pre-treating fibers through crosslinking and annealing in a non-oxidizing environment stabilizes their structure, reducing temperature sensitivity during subsequent hot compaction and preserving hot strength.
mechanism_raw: Pre-crosslinking the fibers via irradiation and annealing in a non-oxidizing environment stabilizes their structure, reducing temperature sensitivity during subsequent hot compaction and preserving hot strength.

abstract: A method of propping at least one fracture in a subterranean formation, that comprises forming a plurality of proppant aggregates, each proppant aggregate comprising a binding fluid and a filler material, and introducing the plurality of proppant aggregates into the at least one fracture, is provided. Methods of fracturing a subterranean formation also are provided.
problem: Maintaining fracture conductivity in subterranean formations during proppant placement.
constraint: The binding fluid must degrade or dissolve over time to avoid long-term permeability loss, while the filler-to-fluid ratio must balance aggregate stability with flow capacity.
mechanism: Forming aggregates with a temporary binding agent and filler allows controlled placement into fractures, where the binding agent temporarily holds the proppant in place while enabling later fluid flow through the packed aggregates.
mechanism_raw: Forming proppant aggregates with a binding fluid and filler allows controlled placement into fractures, where the binding fluid temporarily holds the proppant in place while enabling later fluid flow through the packed aggregates.

abstract: A steam stripper (14) is provided with a support comprising a pole (16) comprised of connected sections (17, 18) and (19). The upper sections 17 and (18) are connected by a resilient spring apparatus (23), and the support is connected to a handle (20) of the stripper by a T-shaped rest (22), having a strap (21) for securing the handle to the rest. In one embodiment the support comprises an attachment (42) for a paint roller extension pole (51).
problem: Vibrations or uneven pressure during steam stripping can reduce tool effectiveness and user control.
constraint: The spring must provide sufficient compliance to absorb vibrations without compromising structural rigidity, and the T-shaped rest must securely attach the handle while permitting movement.
mechanism: A resilient element between connected support sections decouples vibrations and allows adaptive movement, maintaining consistent contact between the tool and the surface being treated.
mechanism_raw: A resilient spring between connected support sections decouples vibrations and allows adaptive movement, maintaining consistent contact between the steam stripper and the surface being treated.

abstract: A fabrication process of a conductive column suitable for a fabrication of a circuit board. The circuit board comprises a dielectric layer. A first blind hole is formed in the dielectric layer from a second surface opposite to the first surface, wherein the blind end of the first blind hole connects to the blind end of the second blind hole. The first blind hole and the second blind hole constitute a through hole. The through hole is formed in an hourglass shape such that an inner diameter of the through hole near the first or the second surface is substantially larger than an inner diameter of the through hole near a middle portion of the through hole. A conductive material is filled in the though hole to form a conductive column.
problem: Filling narrow through-holes in circuit boards with conductive material often results in voids or incomplete filling.
constraint: The hourglass geometry must balance filling efficiency with mechanical stress distribution to avoid cracking the dielectric layer during drilling or material injection.
mechanism: Shaping the through-hole into a variable cross-sectional profile (wider near surfaces, narrower in the middle) reduces flow resistance during conductive material deposition, enabling more uniform filling and stronger electrical connections.
mechanism_raw: Shaping the through-hole into an hourglass profile (wider near surfaces, narrower in the middle) reduces flow resistance during conductive material deposition, enabling more uniform filling and stronger electrical connections.

abstract: A gas bearing system comprising two opposing substantially parallel bearing surfaces (2, 3) and at least one gas duct (6) for supplying gas through an orifice (7) to the bearing gap (5) between the bearing surfaces (2, 3). At least one of the bearing surfaces (2, 3) is provided with at least one cavity (8, 9) extending over 0.3 mm2 to 3 mm2 of the at least one bearing surface (2, 3). The content of the cavity (8, 9) may be between 0.3 mm3 and 4 mm3. The gas duct (6) may supply gas to the cavity (8) through an orifice (7) in the wall of the cavity (8).
problem: Uneven gas pressure distribution in gas bearings can cause instability or wear.
constraint: Cavity size and placement must balance pressure uniformity with structural integrity, and gas ducts must supply sufficient flow to maintain cavity pressure without causing turbulence.
mechanism: Integrating cavities into bearing surfaces allows localized gas pressure regulation, stabilizing the bearing gap and reducing friction.
mechanism_raw: Integrating cavities (0.3–3 mm² area, 0.3–4 mm³ volume) into bearing surfaces allows localized gas pressure regulation, stabilizing the bearing gap and reducing friction.

abstract: This invention relates to a process for manufacturing nutritionally balanced food compositions suitable for retort sterilization which have a low pH, extended shelf life, high antimicrobial activity, and which include protein in a stable emulsion. The primary protein source for the food composition is caseinates or milk protein concentrates and isolates comprised mostly of casein. Alternately, milk protein concentrates, milk protein isolates, milk protein hydrolystates, soy protein isolates or soy protein concentrates may also be used. The process includes two homogenization steps.
problem: Creating a nutritionally balanced food composition with extended shelf life, low pH, high antimicrobial activity, and stable protein emulsion suitable for retort sterilization.
constraint: Balancing homogenization intensity to avoid protein denaturation or nutrient degradation while achieving sufficient emulsion stability for retort processing.
mechanism: Sequential mechanical shearing and stabilization of a dispersed phase through two intensity-controlled processing stages. The first stage disrupts aggregated components to achieve uniform distribution, while the second stage refines the dispersion to lock in structural integrity and functional properties during subsequent high-energy processing.
mechanism_raw: Two sequential homogenization steps that mechanically shear and stabilize the protein emulsion, ensuring uniform dispersion of caseinates/milk proteins while maintaining structural integrity during sterilization. The first homogenization breaks down protein aggregates, and the second step refines the emulsion to lock in stability and antimicrobial properties.

abstract: The present invention provides a wraparound lacing system for use in all manner of footwear. The lacing system includes a lace which encircles the upper and midsole of the article of footwear in a spiral, helical, coiled or similar wound wraparound pattern. The upper includes finger members which independently adjust to the contours of the wearer's foot while providing a snug and secure fit. The upper and midsole are integrally formed as a unitary structure. The housing of the upper and the midsole includes channels therein which receive the wraparound lace. The lace can be affixed at one or both ends to the midsole or to the upper. Removable lace end keepers on the upper permit the user to adjust the length of the lace.
problem: Achieving a snug, adaptive fit for footwear that conforms to varying foot contours without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining uniform pressure distribution across the foot while allowing independent adjustment of localized regions without over-tightening or structural failure.
mechanism: Distributed mechanical coupling via a continuous tensioning element routed through a deformable structure with independently adjustable localized regions. Selective tension application compresses specific regions to conform to variable contours while maintaining overall structural coherence.
mechanism_raw: A spiral/helical lace routed through channels in a unitary upper/midsole structure, where independent finger members on the upper adjust locally to foot contours. Tensioning the lace compresses the fingers selectively, creating a custom fit through distributed mechanical coupling.

abstract: A portable electronic apparatus includes a printer portion provided in a main body and having a printing head, a recording paper holder provided in a portion of the main body near to the printer portion, a holder cover openably attached to the paper holder, a platen provided on the holder cover and facing the printing head when the holder cover covers the paper holder, and a paper sensor provided on the holder cover, located near to the platen, and detecting the recording paper. The apparatus may includes a water-drop proof cover removably attached on the main body, covering a portion of the outer surface region of the main body which faces the printed recording paper discharged out from a recording paper discharge port formed in the portion of the outer surface region, and housing the printed recording paper discharged out from the paper discharge port.
