A single output reference XOR gate may be coupled to a latched differential input signal and the bias voltage through a second variable resistor. At least one latch may be coupled to at least one differential input of the data and reference XOR gate. The single output of the data XOR gate may be a data output of a clock and data recovery circuit (CDR) and the single output of the reference XOR gate may be a reference output of the clock and CDR. No current may flow at the data output of the data XOR gate and the reference output of the reference XOR gate when there are no transitions occurring at an input of the phase detector.
problem: Achieving pattern-independent phase adjustment in clock and data recovery circuits while minimizing power consumption during idle states.
constraint: Maintaining zero current draw during idle periods to conserve power while ensuring accurate phase detection and adjustment when transitions occur, requiring precise control of resistor values and latch timing.
mechanism: A phase detection system compares input signals against a reference using a differential comparator, dynamically adjusts alignment via a tunable impedance element, and enters a zero-current state during signal inactivity. Latching elements stabilize the detection output to maintain consistent phase alignment.
mechanism_raw: XOR gates coupled with variable resistors and latches enable phase detection by comparing input signals against a bias voltage. The variable resistors allow dynamic adjustment of phase alignment, while the absence of current flow during no-transition states ensures power efficiency. The latches stabilize the phase detection process for consistent output.

abstract: An apparatus for inserting documents (2) having at least one guide strip (13, 14) which is reciprocable between a retracted position and a projecting position in which it reaches further into the stuffing position than in the retracted position for guiding into an envelope (11) in the stuffing position at least one document (2) coming from the document transport path (1).
problem: Efficiently inserting documents into an envelope along a transport path without misalignment or jamming.
constraint: Coordinating the timing and range of the guide strip's reciprocation with the document transport speed and envelope positioning to prevent collisions or incomplete insertions.
mechanism: A reciprocating guide element extends into a transport path to direct objects into a target receptacle. The guide's motion is synchronized with the object transport speed and receptacle positioning to ensure alignment during insertion while avoiding collisions with upstream or downstream processes.
mechanism_raw: A reciprocating guide strip extends into the stuffing position to direct documents into the envelope. The strip's movement between retracted and projecting positions synchronizes with the document transport path, ensuring precise alignment during insertion while avoiding interference with upstream or downstream processes.

abstract: To obtain a small and high performance damper mechanism which reduces pressure pulsation in low pressure-side fuel in the high pressure fuel pump in a high pressure fuel supply system or a high pressure fuel pump provided with the small and high performance damper mechanism.Two metal diaphragms are welded together over the entire circumference to obtain a metal diaphragm assembly (also referred to as “double metal diaphragm damper”). The whole or part of the portion of the metal diaphragm assembly other than the weld (for example, the portion inside the weld) is clamped by a pressing member and thereby the assembly is secured in a housing enclosure. The housing enclosure may be formed integrally with the body of a high pressure pump.
problem: Reducing pressure pulsation in a high-pressure fuel pump's low-pressure side while maintaining a compact design.
constraint: Achieving sufficient damping performance in a small form factor by optimizing the diaphragm material thickness and clamping pressure to balance flexibility and durability.
mechanism: A flexible diaphragm assembly with clamped configuration absorbs pressure fluctuations by flexing in response to pulsations. The dual-layer structure and integral housing balance flexibility and structural integrity while minimizing spatial footprint under high-pressure conditions.
mechanism_raw: Two metal diaphragms welded together form a double-layer damper assembly. The clamped configuration (via a pressing member) allows the diaphragms to flex in response to pressure fluctuations, absorbing pulsations. The integral housing design minimizes space while ensuring structural integrity under high pressure.

abstract: A cardiac pacemaker programmed to pace in a demand mode with hysteresis is further programmed to recognize and correct a pacemaker mediated bradycardia. Such a pacemaker mediated bradycardia is the result of an idioventricular rhythm that occurs while hysteresis is operative and which inhibits the pacemaker from further pacing.
problem: Correcting pacemaker-mediated bradycardia caused by idioventricular rhythms that inhibit pacing during hysteresis-based demand mode operation.
constraint: Distinguishing between legitimate atrial signals and idioventricular rhythms to avoid inappropriate pacing adjustments while maintaining the benefits of hysteresis for tracking natural heart activity.
mechanism: A detection system identifies non-target rhythmic signals during a tracking mode and overrides an inhibition response to resume pacing. This recognition mechanism distinguishes between legitimate signals and spurious rhythms to maintain consistent rate support.
mechanism_raw: The pacemaker detects idioventricular rhythms during hysteresis and overrides its inhibition response to resume pacing. This recognition and correction mechanism prevents the pacemaker from being suppressed by non-atrial signals, ensuring consistent heart rate support.

abstract: The invention relates to a memory device electrode, in particular for a resistively switching memory device, wherein the surface of the electrode is provided with a structure, in particular comprises one or a plurality of shoulders or projections, respectively. Furthermore, the invention relates to a memory cell comprising at least one such electrode, a memory device, as well as a method for manufacturing a memory device electrode.
problem: Resistively switching memory devices require electrodes that can reliably and efficiently induce resistive switching states, but flat electrode surfaces may produce non-uniform electric fields that degrade switching performance and endurance.
constraint: The surface structures must be precisely formed to achieve the desired field enhancement while remaining manufacturable using standard semiconductor fabrication processes, and the geometry must not cause excessive current leakage or premature dielectric breakdown.
mechanism: Forming surface features on an electrode creates localized regions of enhanced or controlled electric field intensity and current density at specific contact points, which promotes uniform and controlled formation, rupture, and reformation of conductive pathways within a resistive switching layer, thereby improving switching reliability and endurance.
mechanism_raw: Structuring the electrode surface with shoulders or projections creates localized regions of enhanced or controlled electric field intensity and current density at specific contact points, which promotes uniform and controlled formation, rupture, and reformation of conductive filaments within the resistive switching layer, thereby improving switching reliability and endurance.
residual_terms: ["electric field intensity", "current density", "conductive pathways", "resistive switching layer"]

abstract: A semiconductor memory device (M) includes a memory array (MA) having a plurality of memory cells, a redundancy array (RA) having a plurality of memory cells, a non-volatile redundancy information memory (NVR) having a plurality of memory cells for storing redundancy information, and a redundancy control unit (RU) for selecting either memory cells in the memory array (MA) or memory cells in the redundancy array (RA). In one example, the non-volatile redundancy information memory (NVR) is connected directly to the redundancy control unit (RU) by means of at least one sense amplifier (SA).
problem: Semiconductor memory arrays inevitably contain defective memory cells due to manufacturing imperfections, and the system must be able to identify and bypass these defects to maintain reliable operation without requiring external intervention or losing stored data about which cells are faulty.
constraint: The non-volatile storage must retain defect information across power cycles and the direct connection to the control unit must provide sufficiently fast access to avoid performance degradation during normal memory operations.
mechanism: A persistent storage element retains a map of defective component locations, and this information is fed directly to a control unit via a dedicated access interface, enabling the control unit to automatically and rapidly select either normal components or redundant components based on the stored defect map, ensuring continuous operation despite hardware faults.
mechanism_raw: A non-volatile redundancy information memory stores a persistent map of defective cell locations, and this information is fed directly to a redundancy control unit via a dedicated sense amplifier, enabling the control unit to automatically and rapidly select either normal array cells or redundant array cells based on the stored defect map, ensuring continuous operation despite hardware faults.
residual_terms: ["persistent storage element", "defect map", "control unit", "dedicated access interface"]

abstract: In some embodiments, a pillow including a viscoelastic sleeve defining a cavity and filler material positioned within the cavity is disclosed. In other embodiments the pillow includes a sleeve in which is received viscoelastic filler material, or includes a viscoelastic sleeve in which is received other type(s) of filler material.
reason: The abstract describes a product combining known materials (viscoelastic sleeve and filler) in a conventional configuration without disclosing any novel causal mechanism or functional relationship that produces a useful effect beyond the inherent properties of the materials themselves.

abstract: A removable flush cap designed for use with an irrigation tube coupling or fitting, to facilitate post-installation flushing of dirt and grit from an irrigation system. The flush cap is particularly designed for use with a tube coupling of the type shown in U.S. Pat. No. 6,988,747 B2, having a plurality of retainer collets each with multiple lock fingers oriented for push-in locked reception of a tube end in engagement with a compliant seal. The flush cap includes a generally cylindrical barrel for sealed slide-fit engagement with the compliant seal within one of the retainer collets, and a recessed groove for snap-fit locked reception of the collet lock fingers. The flush cap further includes a plurality of cams for engaging and releasing the collet lock fingers from the cap groove, upon cap rotation, to permit slide-out cap removal from the retainer collet.
problem: After installation of push-fit irrigation tube couplings, it is necessary to flush dirt and grit from the system, but the coupling's lock fingers prevent easy removal of any cap or tool for cleaning without disassembling the entire connection.
constraint: The cap must maintain a fluid-tight seal with the compliant seal during flushing while the cam mechanism must reliably release the lock fingers without damaging them, and the entire operation must be achievable through simple rotational motion without additional tools.
mechanism: A removable cap with a cylindrical interface and retention feature is designed to interact with a locking mechanism via rotational motion. Integrated actuation elements on the cap mechanically disengage the locking mechanism while maintaining a sealed interface, allowing fluid flow through the coupling for cleaning without disassembly.
mechanism_raw: A removable flush cap is designed with a cylindrical barrel that slide-fits into the coupling's compliant seal and a recessed groove that snap-fits over the collet lock fingers. Upon rotation of the cap, integrated cams engage the lock fingers and mechanically push them out of the groove, releasing the cap's retention while maintaining a sealed interface with the compliant seal, allowing flushing fluid to flow through the coupling for cleaning.

abstract: A semiconductor light-emitting device includes: a semiconductor multilayer film, a substrate supporting the semiconductor multilayer film; and a phosphor layer formed on the substrate so as to cover the semiconductor multilayer film. The phosphor layer has an outer edge of a cross section taken in a direction parallel to the principal surface of the substrate having a substantially circular shape or a substantially regular polygonal shape having five or more sides. An outer edge of the principal surface of the substrate is formed in a substantially circular shape or a substantially regular polygonal shape having five or more sides. With this configuration, light obtained therefrom has less non-uniformity in color and a high luminous flux can be realized.
problem: Semiconductor light-emitting devices with phosphor conversion layers suffer from color non-uniformity and reduced luminous flux due to edge effects where light distribution becomes irregular at the periphery of the device, particularly where the phosphor layer and substrate edges create optical discontinuities.
constraint: The edge geometry must be manufacturable using standard dicing or shaping techniques while maintaining the structural integrity of the semiconductor layers, and the polygonal shape must have enough sides to approximate a smooth curve without introducing new optical discontinuities.
mechanism: Shaping the outer edges of both a light-converting layer and a substrate into forms with five or more sides eliminates sharp corners and irregular edge geometries that cause non-uniform light scattering and color mixing, resulting in more uniform light extraction and reduced color variation across the emitted light.
mechanism_raw: Shaping the outer edges of both the phosphor layer cross-section and the substrate principal surface into substantially circular or regular polygonal forms with five or more sides eliminates sharp corners and irregular edge geometries that cause non-uniform light scattering and color mixing, resulting in more uniform light extraction and reduced color variation across the emitted light.

abstract: An active balun device is provided. The active balun device includes: a differential input portion for receiving an external single input signal to output two complementary differential signals; and a differential amplifier connected to the differential input portion in cascade to amplify the two differential signals received from the differential input portion. Thus, the active balun device has a sufficient gain and a desired bandwidth in a semiconductor circuit.
problem: Achieving sufficient gain and desired bandwidth in a semiconductor-based active balun circuit.
constraint: Balancing gain and bandwidth limitations inherent in semiconductor circuits while maintaining signal integrity.
mechanism: Cascading a signal conversion stage that transforms a single-ended input into complementary differential signals with an amplification stage that increases the amplitude of the differential signals, thereby improving overall gain and bandwidth.
mechanism_raw: Cascading a differential input stage (converting a single-ended signal to complementary differential signals) with a differential amplifier stage to amplify the signals, thereby improving overall gain and bandwidth.

abstract: A metallized film and a process for making the film are disclosed. In general, the metallized film includes a polymeric film layer that is coated with a polyester coating composition. A metal layer is then formed on top of the polyester coating. The polyester coating acts as a tie layer between the metal layer and the underlying film. The polyester film composition may be formed from, in one embodiment, isophthalic acid, a sulfomonomer, and 2-methyl 1,3-propane diol. The above diol has been found to improve adhesion between the metal layer and the polymeric film layer.
reason: The patent describes a specific material composition (polyester coating with isophthalic acid, sulfomonomer, and 2-methyl 1,3-propane diol) to improve adhesion between a metal layer and polymer film. This is a material-specific solution rather than a generalizable functional mechanism.

abstract: A cooling apparatus of a cooking appliance including a cabinet having a cooking chamber located therein and an electric component chamber located outside the cooking chamber; a door installed on the cabinet for opening and closing the cooking chamber, and having a suction channel and a discharge channel communicating with the electric component chamber; and an air blower installed in the electric component chamber for sucking air to the inside of the electric component chamber through the suction channel and the discharge channel of the door and discharging the air, so that the external air having a low temperature is directly sucked through the door, cools the electric component chamber, and is then discharged to the outside, thereby increasing cooling efficiency of the door.
problem: Inefficient cooling of electric components in a cooking appliance due to limited airflow pathways.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the door while integrating airflow channels without compromising thermal isolation or mechanical sealing.
mechanism: Routing external air through dedicated suction and discharge channels integrated into a structural barrier, allowing direct airflow to a target chamber via a driving element, thereby increasing cooling efficiency.
mechanism_raw: Routing external air through dedicated suction and discharge channels integrated into the door structure, allowing direct airflow to the electric component chamber via an air blower, thereby increasing cooling efficiency.

abstract: A construction machine includes a lower traveling body on which an upper rotating body is rotatably disposed. The rotating body includes an upper frame provided with a bottom plate and a supporter acting as a perpendicular member. The bottom plate has an attachment hole extending substantially perpendicular to the bottom plate. The supporter is welded substantially perpendicular to the bottom plate while one end of the supporter is engaged with the attachment hole. Accordingly, the supporter can be easily fixed to the bottom plate while maintaining the perpendicularity and a proper height setting of the supporter.
problem: Difficulty in precisely fixing a perpendicular supporter to a bottom plate while maintaining alignment and height in a construction machine assembly.
constraint: Achieving precise alignment and structural rigidity during welding without introducing misalignment or weakening the joint.
mechanism: Using a defined opening in a base surface and joining a perpendicular element to the opening while engaging one end of the element with the opening, ensuring alignment and proper height during assembly.
mechanism_raw: Using an attachment hole in the bottom plate and welding the supporter to the hole while engaging one end of the supporter with the hole, ensuring perpendicularity and proper height during assembly.

abstract: An oxygen enrichment apparatus includes a main body including an oxygen enriching unit and a pump unit for supplying oxygen-enriched air obtained by the oxygen enriching unit to a predetermined place; a ventilating unit for suctioning exterior air into the main body and discharging the exterior air out of the main body after supplying the exterior air into the oxygen enriching unit; and a control unit for controlling the pump unit and the ventilating unit. The ventilating unit and the control unit are installed in the main body. The main body further includes therein a secondary battery serving as a power supply for supplying a power to the pump unit, the ventilating unit and the control unit.
reason: The patent describes a system integrating multiple components (oxygen enrichment unit, pump, ventilating unit, control unit, and secondary battery) into a single main body. While this addresses portability and power supply, it is a system-level design choice rather than a specific causal mechanism for solving a problem.

abstract: The present invention relates to a driving method for cholesteric liquid crystal display. A plurality of pixels of the display are controlled by a plurality of row drivers and a plurality of column drivers. According to the method of the invention, firstly, a DC input voltage or a non-symmetric AC input voltage is applied to the row drivers and the column drivers so that the voltage of the pixel is larger than a withstand voltage of the drivers. Then, an initial column signal and an initial row signal are respectively supplied by the corresponding column driver and row driver so as to initialize the corresponding pixel. The polarity of the initial column signal is different from that of the initial row signal. Because the initial row signal minus the initial column signal equals the signal of the pixel, the amplitude of the signal applied to the pixel can be increased. Therefore, according to the invention, the initial time of the pixel can be decreased, and the transferring speed of the pixel can be improved.
problem: Slow initialization and transfer speed of cholesteric liquid crystal pixels due to insufficient voltage amplitude under driver withstand limits.
constraint: The voltage applied to the pixel must remain within the withstand voltage limits of the row and column drivers while achieving sufficient amplitude for rapid pixel initialization.
mechanism: Applying opposing-polarity signals to two terminals of a load so their combined differential voltage exceeds the voltage handling capability of individual signal drivers, thereby amplifying the effective voltage across the load without exceeding the drivers' withstand limits.
mechanism_raw: Applying opposing-polarity initial row and column signals so their differential voltage across the pixel exceeds the driver's withstand voltage, thereby amplifying the effective pixel signal without overloading the drivers.

abstract: An electronics cabinet for storing a plurality of electronic devices therein is provided and includes a fan and an evaporative cooler. The fan draws a flow of air into the cabinet, circulates the flow of air through the evaporative cooler, and then across the electronic devices for removing heat produced by the electronic devices. The evaporative cooler removes heat from the flow of air by absorbing heat from the flow of air and then dissipating the heat by evaporating a liquid into a secondary airflow, which is directed out of the cabinet. The cabinet includes a cold air plenum having an actuator for adjusting a cross-sectional area of the cold air plenum to control the airflow through each of the supports.
problem: Inefficient heat removal in electronics cabinets due to fixed airflow paths that cannot adapt to varying thermal loads.
constraint: Balancing airflow rate and cooling efficiency while maintaining structural simplicity and avoiding over-engineering of the thermal management system.
mechanism: Combining a phase-change cooling medium with a variable-flow passage whose cross-sectional geometry is dynamically adjusted by an actuator to regulate airflow distribution across heat-generating components.
mechanism_raw: Combining evaporative cooling with an adjustable cold air plenum whose cross-sectional area is dynamically controlled by an actuator to regulate airflow distribution across electronic devices.

abstract: It is an object of the present invention to provide a surface protective sheet and a method for grinding a semiconductor wafer, by the use of which any dimple is not formed, nor occurs breakage and fouling of a wafer even when a wafer having high bumps which are highly densely arranged is ground to an extremely small thickness, and besides, no adhesive is left at the roots of the bumps after the surface protective sheet is peeled. The surface protective sheet of the invention is used for grinding a back surface of a semiconductor wafer, and in the surface protective sheet, one surface of a base sheet is provided with an opening portion having a diameter smaller than an outer diameter of a semiconductor wafer to be stuck, on said opening portion no adhesive layer being formed, and a portion which is provided around the opening portion and on which an adhesive layer is formed.
problem: Damage, dimpling, and adhesive residue during grinding of semiconductor wafers with high-density bumps due to direct contact or improper protection.
constraint: Ensuring the opening size and adhesive placement prevent contact with bumps while maintaining sufficient adhesion to protect the wafer during grinding.
mechanism: Placing a protective barrier with an aperture smaller than the workpiece diameter and selectively applying adhesive only around the aperture to shield the workpiece surface while avoiding contact with protruding features during material removal.
mechanism_raw: Using a protective sheet with an opening smaller than the wafer diameter and selectively placing adhesive only around the opening to shield the wafer surface while avoiding interference with bumps.

abstract: A golf club head includes a face including a bulge formed at the center of a backside thereof and having a thickness of 2.0 or more times the thickness of the thinnest part, and a plurality of ribs extended from the bulge toward a circumference of the face. Six or more ribs are provided as the plural ribs and an angle θ(°) formed between extension directions of a respective pair of adjoining ribs is less than 90°. The maximum thickness of the bulge is not more than 3.5 times the thickness of the thinnest part.
problem: Suboptimal energy transfer and structural failure in golf club faces due to uniform thickness and lack of stress distribution control.
constraint: Balancing bulge thickness (2.0–3.5x thinnest part) and rib angles (<90°) to optimize flexibility without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Incorporating a central deformable region with variable thickness and radial stiffening elements extending toward the periphery to distribute impact forces and enhance controlled elastic deformation for improved energy transfer.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a central bulge with variable thickness and radial ribs extending toward the face periphery to distribute impact stress and enhance flexible deformation for improved energy transfer.
residual_terms: ["variable thickness", "radial stiffening elements", "elastic deformation", "energy transfer", "impact forces"]

abstract: A self-adjusting goods display system maintains a proper shelf level for a display bin containing goods. An implementation has an open bin with side walls having top edges and a moveable shelf to receive a pile of goods. A light source and a light receiver are positioned on the top edges of opposing walls of the bin, and the light source generates light to be received by the light receiver. When the pile of goods is reduced so that the pile no longer obstructs the light from being received by the light receiver a signal indicates a need to raise the general level of the remaining pile contained in the bin. A controller receives the signal and controls operation of a motor to raise the height of the shelf until the remaining pile of the shelf again blocks the light, or the shelf is at a position of maximum height.
problem: Inconsistent product visibility and accessibility in retail displays as inventory levels decrease.
constraint: Ensuring accurate optical detection and motor response without false triggers or mechanical overextension, while maintaining simplicity in control logic.
mechanism: Using an optical detection pair to sense when a product pile no longer interrupts a light beam, triggering a motor to raise a support surface until the pile re-interrupts the beam or reaches a maximum position, maintaining consistent product presentation.
mechanism_raw: Using an optical sensor pair (light source and receiver) to detect when the product pile no longer blocks light, triggering a motor to raise the shelf until the pile re-blocks the light or reaches maximum height.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for producing a touch-and-close fastener element comprising a multitude of hook means, which are provided with a support as one piece and in the shape of stems with hook heads located at the ends thereof. Each of the hook heads is provided, at least in part, with an addition head part made of an additional material. A fastener system is produced from the respective head part being made from a duroplastic molding compound serving as the additional material. The fastener system can withstand a high temperature and mechanical stresses and lead to improved adhesion values and peel strength values during use.
problem: Improving adhesion and peel strength of touch-and-close fasteners under high temperature and mechanical stress.
constraint: Balancing the duroplastic material's rigidity and adhesion properties with the base material to avoid compromising flexibility or manufacturing feasibility.
mechanism: Applying a secondary material with higher thermal and mechanical resistance to specific regions of a flexible fastening structure, creating a composite that enhances adhesion and peel strength under stress without compromising overall flexibility.
mechanism_raw: Adding a secondary duroplastic molding compound as an additional head part to specific regions of hook elements, creating a composite structure that enhances thermal and mechanical resistance.

abstract: A wheel set guidance assembly is provided for suspending a wheel set bearing (10) of a wheel set (20) to a bogie frame (30), comprising separate vertical (50), lateral (70) and longitudinal (40) guidance elements for independent guidance of the movement of the wheel set in vertical, lateral and longitudinal directions wherein the stiffness of the guidance elements can be selected independently of each other.
problem: Guiding a wheel set in vertical, lateral, and longitudinal directions while allowing independent stiffness adjustment for each axis.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and load-bearing capacity while achieving independent stiffness control across all three axes.
mechanism: Separating directional guidance into independent subsystems, each with a selectively adjustable stiffness characteristic, allowing tailored dynamic response along each axis while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Decoupling the guidance system into separate vertical, lateral, and longitudinal elements, each with independently selectable stiffness, enabling tailored dynamic response per axis.

abstract: There is provided with a wireless tag reader communicating with a plurality of wireless tags each of which retains tag information piece and a bloom filter, the wireless tag reader comprising: a transmitter configured to transmit a read request signal simultaneously to the wireless tags to request the wireless tags to read out the bloom filters; a receiver configured to receive bloom filter signals simultaneously from the wireless tags to acquire a colliding bloom filter signal; a decoder configured to decode the colliding bloom filter signal to acquire a composite bloom filter which is equivalent to logic operation OR on the bloom filters; a data storage configured to store tag information pieces; and a filter verifier configured to verify each of tag information pieces in the data storage with the composite bloom filter to detect tag information pieces for which a verification result is positive or negative.
problem: Efficiently verifying tag information from multiple wireless tags in a single read operation without collisions.
constraint: Managing signal collisions and probabilistic false positives inherent to bloom filters while ensuring accurate verification across a large number of tags.
mechanism: Combining multiple probabilistic data structures into a single composite structure via logical union operations, enabling batch verification of stored information against the composite to detect matches without individual interrogation.
mechanism_raw: Aggregating bloom filters from all tags into a composite filter via logical OR operations, enabling batch verification of stored tag data against the composite filter to detect matches.

abstract: A dry cleaning process for in-home dry cleaning comprising a low-aqueous dry cleaning step of contacting a laundry article with a low-aqueous dry cleaning composition, wherein said composition comprises a non-flammable, non-chlorine containing organic dry cleaning solvent, water and surfactant, whereby the water to cloth ratio (w/w) is less than 0.45 and the water to surfactant ratio (w/w) is at most 1.5, wherein said organic dry cleaning solvent is selected from hydrofluorocarbon, hydrofluoroether and siloxane solvent.
problem: Enabling safe, effective in-home dry cleaning with minimal water usage while avoiding flammable or chlorine-based solvents.
constraint: Achieving sufficient soil removal and stain dissolution with limited water while maintaining compatibility with surfactants and avoiding hazardous solvent properties.
mechanism: Selecting a solvent system with reduced flammability and chlorine content, and controlling the ratio of water to cleaning agent to achieve soil removal and stain dissolution with minimal aqueous usage while maintaining safety.
mechanism_raw: Optimizing a low-aqueous solvent system by selecting non-flammable, non-chlorine solvents (e.g., hydrofluorocarbons) and controlling water-to-surfactant ratios to balance cleaning efficacy and safety.

abstract: The invention is to provide an aqueous ink, a recorded image and a recording method capable of improving an image fastness and a color-developing property of a recorded image, and is featured in that components of the aqueous ink are so prepared as to realize, at least on a surface portion of a recording medium, a fixed state of an ink droplet in which a contour portion of a second coloring material is formed around a central portion in which a first coloring material is fixed.
problem: Improving image fastness and color-developing properties of aqueous ink on recording media.
constraint: Balancing the solubility, particle size, and interaction dynamics of the two coloring materials to ensure proper spatial arrangement during droplet drying.
mechanism: Arranging two coloring materials in a core-shell configuration during droplet drying, where a second material forms a surrounding contour around a central first material, enhancing fixation and color stability on the recording medium.
mechanism_raw: Structuring the ink so that a second coloring material forms a contour around a central first coloring material, creating a core-shell arrangement that enhances fixation and color stability.

abstract: The invention relates to a retention device comprising a support bracket that can be moved along a filling tube, for accommodating a brake ring clasped around the filling tube to exercise a frictional force on a tubular casing to be pulled off the filling tube during filling, and further comprising a drive coupled to the support bracket for moving the support bracket back and forth parallel to the filling tube. The drive comprises a crank transmission with a crank that is connected on the driven side to the support bracket.
problem: During filling of casings (e.g., sausage casings) onto a filling tube, the casing must be pulled off the tube while maintaining controlled tension and friction to prevent slippage or damage.
constraint: The mechanism must provide controlled frictional force while simultaneously allowing reciprocating motion along the filling tube — balancing the need to pull the casing off with maintaining proper tension without stalling or over-tightening.
mechanism: A motion conversion mechanism generates reciprocating movement along a linear path. A friction element mounted on the moving support applies controlled resistance to a flexible material being advanced, maintaining dynamic contact during the reciprocating motion to ensure consistent tension without slippage or damage. The coordinated movement and friction balance pulling force with material integrity.
mechanism_raw: A reciprocating support bracket driven by a crank transmission moves back and forth along the filling tube. A brake ring mounted on the bracket applies controlled frictional force to the casing being pulled off. The reciprocating motion of the bracket, powered by the crank, allows the brake ring to maintain dynamic contact with the casing as it advances, ensuring consistent tension during the pulling-off process.

abstract: Methods and systems for facilitating the selection of alternates for hand written word. Rules select words user based on operating modes and cursor positions and sequential orderings. User interfaces can also be used to select words and to provide alternates for the selected words having alternates. Words that the recognizer believes correct to a high actual or relative probability may be skipped over in automatic processes, and the display of words that the recognizer is less confident are correct can be modified. The user can adjust such sensitivity settings for determining the probability of correctness.
problem: In handwritten word recognition, the system must efficiently present correction alternatives to the user without overwhelming them with suggestions for every word, focusing attention only on uncertain recognitions.
constraint: The system must balance between showing enough alternatives for correction while not overwhelming the user with too many suggestions — using confidence thresholds to filter which words require user attention, trading off completeness of correction against cognitive load.
mechanism: A probabilistic evaluation system assesses each recognized input's likelihood of correctness. Inputs exceeding a confidence threshold are automatically bypassed, while inputs below the threshold trigger a modified presentation state (e.g., highlighting). User-adjustable thresholds define the boundary between automatic acceptance and user intervention, with contextual factors (e.g., operating mode, position) further refining selection criteria to balance correction completeness against cognitive load.
mechanism_raw: A confidence-based filtering system evaluates each recognized word's probability of correctness. Words with high confidence are automatically skipped in processing, while words with low confidence have their display modified (e.g., highlighted or flagged). User-adjustable sensitivity thresholds determine the cutoff for what constitutes 'high' vs. 'low' confidence, and operating modes and cursor positions further refine which words are processed.

abstract: A tool for installing a metal locking tie is disclosed. The tool includes a tension mechanism and a ball set and cut-off mechanism. The tension mechanism tensions the metal locking tie wrapped around a bundle. The ball set and cut-off mechanism includes a guide block and a shear block that engages the guide block. Once the tool tensions the metal locking tie, a ball set and cut-off handle is manually activated to push the guide block and the shear block forward in the tool thereby setting a ball in a metal locking tie head and shearing a portion of the tensioned metal locking tie.
problem: Installing a metal locking tie requires both tensioning the tie around a bundle and then securing it (setting the locking ball) while cutting off the excess tail — these operations must be precisely sequenced and coordinated.
constraint: The setting and cutting operations must be precisely coordinated to occur together after tensioning is complete — ensuring the tie is properly locked before the excess is cut, while the single activation prevents premature or partial execution of either function.
mechanism: A two-stage actuation system first applies tensioning force to secure a flexible member around a target. A single activation then triggers a coordinated dual-action mechanism: one component engages a locking element while a second component simultaneously performs a severing operation. The sequential dependency ensures tensioning completes before the combined locking-and-severing action, preventing partial execution of either function.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage tool first tensions the metal locking tie around a bundle using a tension mechanism. Then, a single manual activation of a handle simultaneously pushes a guide block and shear block forward in the tool. This coordinated forward motion sets a ball in the metal locking tie head (locking it) and simultaneously shears off the excess tensioned tie. The sequential operation ensures tensioning completes before the combined set-and-cut action.

abstract: The present invention provides a method for producing negatively charged oxygen atoms comprising: placing a negative electrode (3) on a surface of a member (2) made of calcium-aluminum composite oxide, proximately placing a positive electrode (10) on a side of the member opposite to the surface on which the negative electrode is placed, supplying oxygen to the negative electrode side, and applying voltage between the negative electrode and the positive electrode so as to extract negatively charged oxygen atoms (A) from the side where the positive electrode (10) is placed. The present invention also provides an apparatus for producing negatively charged oxygen atoms which is used for the above method.
problem: Producing negatively charged oxygen atoms (useful for oxidation processes, material treatment, or chemical synthesis) requires a method to selectively extract these ions from a solid material.
constraint: The material must be conductive to oxygen ions while maintaining structural integrity, and the applied voltage must be sufficient to drive ion migration through the solid medium without causing material degradation or unwanted side reactions.
mechanism: A solid ion-conductive medium spans between two electrodes. A voltage differential applied across the electrodes drives selective migration of negatively charged ions through the medium. An ion supply is introduced at the negative electrode side, and the ions are extracted from the opposite side where the positive electrode is positioned. The medium acts as a selective transport barrier, enabling ion extraction without structural degradation.
mechanism_raw: A calcium-aluminum composite oxide member serves as a solid ion-conductive medium. A negative electrode is placed on one surface and a positive electrode on the opposite surface. Oxygen is supplied to the negative electrode side. When voltage is applied across the electrodes, negatively charged oxygen ions migrate through the composite oxide material and are extracted from the side where the positive electrode is placed. The composite oxide acts as a selective transport medium for oxygen ions.
residual_terms: ["ion-conductive medium", "voltage differential", "selective migration", "selective transport barrier", "ion extraction"]

abstract: A quick-cooling device for a refrigerator includes top, bottom and opposing side walls that collectively define an air intake/delivery housing. A plurality of air discharge nozzles are arranged about at least one wall of the housing. A blower fan is mounted to the housing for drawing an airflow from the refrigerator into the housing and thereafter expelling the airflow from the housing through the air discharge nozzles. The air discharge nozzles can be constituted by slotted or circular openings arranged in staggered rows and sized to match a particular application.
problem: Quickly cooling a refrigerator compartment requires efficient circulation and distribution of cooled air throughout the interior space from a single airflow source.
constraint: The nozzle arrangement must provide uniform coverage of the cooling airflow while maintaining sufficient air velocity — the staggered row configuration and nozzle sizing must balance between broad distribution and effective cooling, while the housing must efficiently channel airflow from intake to discharge without significant pressure loss.
mechanism: A housing structure defines an airflow channel with multiple distributed discharge points. A single airflow source draws air into the housing and redirects it through an array of nozzles positioned in staggered configurations. The nozzle arrangement and sizing balance broad spatial coverage with sufficient velocity, while the housing geometry minimizes pressure loss during redirection from intake to discharge. This ensures uniform distribution of cooling airflow throughout the target space.
mechanism_raw: A housing with top, bottom, and opposing side walls defines an air intake/delivery chamber. A blower fan draws air from the refrigerator compartment into the housing and expels it through a plurality of air discharge nozzles arranged about the housing walls. The nozzles are positioned in staggered rows and can be slotted or circular, sized to match the application. The housing captures and redirects the airflow from a single intake point to multiple distributed discharge points, ensuring uniform air distribution throughout the compartment.
residual_terms: ["distributed discharge points", "staggered configurations", "nozzle arrangement", "pressure loss", "uniform distribution"]

abstract: An upper for an article of footwear includes an upper and a sole assembly secured to the upper. The sole assembly includes an upper layer formed of a first material and a lower layer positioned beneath the upper layer and formed of a second material. At least one finger extends downwardly from at least a portion of a periphery of the upper layer.
problem: Balancing structural support and flexibility in layered sole assemblies for footwear to prevent delamination while allowing controlled bending.
constraint: The finger must be sized and positioned to allow sufficient flexibility in targeted regions while maintaining adhesion between the two material layers under dynamic loads.
mechanism: A protrusion extending from one layer engages with a complementary structure in an adjacent layer to mechanically interlock the layers, distributing applied forces across the interface while enabling localized flexure in targeted regions without compromising adhesion between the layers.
mechanism_raw: A downward-extending finger from the upper layer's periphery mechanically interlocks with the lower layer, distributing stress and enabling localized flexure without compromising overall structural integrity.

abstract: A flexible connection joint for inflatable structures such as life rafts, evacuation slides, and the like, includes a flexible connection member to join walls of the inflatable structure together. The flexible connection member includes first and second strip portions that are bonded together at one end to from three legs that can be joined to two or three walls of the structure or to other connecting elements or strips. In this manner, a tensile force acting on at least one of the walls of the structure causes generation of shear forces between the flexible legs and walls to thereby resist their separation.
problem: Resisting separation of walls in inflatable structures under tensile forces while maintaining flexibility in the connection joint.
constraint: The number and bonding configuration of legs must balance flexibility for inflation/deflation cycles with sufficient shear resistance to prevent wall separation under load.
mechanism: A flexible connector with multiple bonded segments converts applied tensile forces into shear forces between the segments and the connected surfaces, creating a self-reinforcing resistance to separation as tension increases by progressively engaging more bonding area.
mechanism_raw: A flexible connection member with bonded legs converts applied tensile forces into shear forces between the legs and walls, creating a self-reinforcing resistance to separation as tension increases.

abstract: A modeling system and process for for computer-aided, block-based modeling involving preparation of a first block diagram (1) in a first model plane (2) that relates to a first abstraction stage, in which at least one block (3) is able to be placed in the first model plane (2) and several blocks are connectable to one another by horizontal data transfer devices for horizontally exchanging data. Further more at least one other block diagram (6) can be arranged on at least one other model plane (5) which is assigned to the first abstraction stage and which is separated from the first model plane (2), so that the first block diagram (1) of the first model plane (2) and the other block diagram (6) of the other model plane (5) form an overall block diagram (7) and that by corresponding vertical data transfer devices (8, 9) which can be arranged on a selection of at least two model planes from the first model plane (2) and the other model planes (5), a vertical exchange of data between at least two selected model planes can be produced.
problem: Managing complex data exchanges in hierarchical block diagrams across multiple abstraction stages without losing coherence or scalability.
constraint: Vertical data transfer devices must selectively connect planes to avoid overcomplicating data paths while ensuring seamless integration across abstraction layers.
mechanism: A hierarchical data architecture partitions block diagrams into distinct model planes assigned to abstraction stages, with intra-plane horizontal data transfers for local processing and inter-plane vertical transfers for cross-layer communication, enabling modular scalability while preserving structural relationships.
mechanism_raw: Separating block diagrams into distinct model planes assigned to abstraction stages, with horizontal data transfers within planes and vertical transfers between planes, enabling modular data flow while preserving hierarchical relationships.
residual_terms: ["model planes", "abstraction stages", "intra-plane horizontal transfers", "inter-plane vertical transfers"]

abstract: A compound including at least one copper II complex of a material selected from the group of imidazole and imidazole derivatives is provided for use in a gas generant composition. An associated burn rate enhanced gas generant composition, in addition to such copper complex-containing compound, also includes a nitrogen-containing non-azide fuel. Additionally provided are methods for improving the combustion performance of a non-azide gas generant composition in at least one aspect selected from the group consisting of ignitability, burn rate and burn rate pressure sensitivity, through the addition of such copper complex-containing compound to the non-azide gas generant composition.
problem: Enhancing combustion performance (ignitability, burn rate, pressure sensitivity) in non-azide gas generant compositions without relying on hazardous azide fuels.
constraint: The copper complex concentration must be optimized to maximize combustion enhancement while avoiding excessive reactivity or thermal instability in the gas generant formulation.
mechanism: A catalytic agent accelerates and stabilizes combustion reactions in a gas generant formulation by lowering activation energy barriers and modulating reaction pathways, thereby enhancing burn rate and reducing pressure sensitivity without relying on hazardous fuel components.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a copper II complex of imidazole or its derivatives as a catalyst to accelerate and stabilize combustion reactions, thereby improving burn rate and reducing pressure sensitivity.

abstract: Additional information is provided to a moving object mark to enhance viewability and improve convenience. A moving object position display device has an information data obtaining part obtaining information data including an icon associated with a target, a map data obtaining part obtaining map data, a display part displaying a map corresponding to the moving object position with a moving object mark, and a moving object mark display control part reading an icon and a description associated with the target from the information data obtaining part to display it in place of the moving object mark when the moving object position has made an approach to within a predetermined distance range from a predetermined target or has entered the same screen. The target need not be searched for from a map display screen. Having made an approach to the target as well as its position and description can be easily recognized.
problem: Improving viewability and reducing cognitive load for users tracking moving objects on a map display by dynamically prioritizing relevant information.
constraint: The proximity threshold and icon selection logic must balance timely information delivery with display clutter to maintain usability during rapid movement.
mechanism: A dynamic prioritization system replaces a generic object representation with a context-specific indicator when a moving entity enters a defined proximity threshold relative to a target, reducing manual search effort and display clutter by automatically surfacing relevant information based on spatial relationships.
mechanism_raw: Replacing the generic moving object mark with a context-specific icon and description when the object enters a proximity threshold to a target, eliminating the need for manual target searching.

abstract: An article of manufacture produced by a process comprising the steps of: erecting a sediment-containment structure comprising a plurality of floating boom segments; and introducing sediment into the shape formed by the sediment-containment structure. A system for building up sediment in a water-covered area comprises: a plurality of floating boom segments connected in an essentially closed shape; a sediment source depositing sediment inside the area substantially enclosed by the essentially closed shape formed by the boom segments; and a wasteweir segment disposed so as to close the essentially closed shape formed by the floating boom segments. The wasteweir segment has two posts and a removable barrier element. A method for building up land in a water-covered or water-surrounded area comprises the steps of: erecting a sediment-containment structure comprising a plurality of floating boom; and introducing sediment into the shape formed by the sediment-containment structure.
problem: Accumulating sediment or building up land in a water-covered or water-surrounded area where water currents and waves would normally disperse the introduced sediment, preventing controlled deposition.
constraint: The barrier must be flexible enough to float and adapt to changing water levels and wave action while maintaining sufficient structural integrity to contain sediment; the enclosure must be essentially closed to prevent sediment escape, yet include a controllable opening (wastweir) for selective release.
mechanism: A flexible, segmented floating barrier is arranged into an essentially closed shape that floats on the water surface and rises/falls with water level changes. Sediment introduced inside the enclosed area is trapped because the floating barrier acts as a self-adjusting, water-level-following containment wall. A wastweir segment with a removable barrier element allows controlled opening or closing of the enclosure, enabling selective release or retention of material as needed.
mechanism_raw: A flexible, segmented floating barrier (boom segments) is arranged into an essentially closed shape that floats on the water surface and rises/falls with water level changes. Sediment introduced inside the enclosed area is trapped because the floating barrier acts as a self-adjusting, water-level-following containment wall. A wastweir segment with a removable barrier element allows controlled opening or closing of the enclosure, enabling selective release or retention of material as needed.

abstract: An internal voltage generating circuit detects a level of a back bias voltage or a pumping voltage and controls a period of an oscillating signal based on the result of counting timing when the detected voltage is lower than a reference voltage. The internal voltage generating circuit includes a back bias/pumping voltage detector for detecting a level difference between a back bias/pumping voltage and a reference voltage, a period controller for controlling a period of an oscillating signal based on the detection result of the back bias/pumping voltage detector, and a pumping unit for pumping the back bias/pumping voltage according to an activation period of the oscillating signal.
problem: Maintaining a stable internal voltage (back bias or pumping voltage) in a semiconductor circuit despite varying load conditions, temperature, and process variations that cause the voltage to drift below a desired reference level.
constraint: The system must balance response speed (how quickly it detects and corrects voltage drops) against power efficiency and stability; the counting-based timing detection introduces a delay that must be short enough for effective regulation but long enough to avoid oscillation or over-correction.
mechanism: A feedback control loop operates as follows: a detector continuously measures the back bias/pumping voltage and compares it to a reference voltage; a counter tracks the timing duration when the detected voltage falls below the reference; a period controller uses this timing information to adjust the period (duty cycle) of an oscillating signal; a pumping unit then charges or discharges the target node according to the adjusted oscillation period, thereby correcting the voltage deviation. The key causal relationship is that the duration of under-voltage conditions directly modulates the oscillation period, which in turn drives corrective pumping action.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control loop operates as follows: a detector continuously measures the back bias/pumping voltage and compares it to a reference voltage; a counter tracks the timing duration when the detected voltage falls below the reference; a period controller uses this timing information to adjust the period (duty cycle) of an oscillating signal; a pumping unit then charges or discharges the target node according to the adjusted oscillation period, thereby correcting the voltage deviation. The key causal relationship is that the duration of under-voltage conditions directly modulates the oscillation period, which in turn drives corrective pumping action.

abstract: A recycling facility includes a receptacle for receiving the ammunition to be cleaned, a gas tank for receiving a pressurized gas and coupled to the receptacle, for supplying the pressurized gas to the receptacle, and a heater coupled between the gas tank and the receptacle, for preheating the pressurized gas before the pressurized gas flowing into the receptacle, and for melting and removing the TNT material from the ammunition. The receptacle includes a control valve coupled between the heater and the receptacle, and a control valve coupled between the heater and the gas tank. A collecting casing may be coupled to the receptacle, and coupled to the gas tank via a filter.
problem: Safely removing explosive or hazardous material (e.g., TNT) from enclosed objects (e.g., ammunition casings) for recycling, where direct heating or mechanical disruption could trigger detonation.
constraint: The gas temperature must be high enough to melt the target material but below the auto-ignition or detonation threshold of the explosive; the gas pressure must be sufficient to remove molten material but controlled to prevent dangerous pressure buildup or projectile hazards.
mechanism: Pressurized gas is preheated by a heater before entering a sealed receptacle containing the objects to be cleaned. The preheated gas transfers thermal energy to the target material inside the receptacle, melting or softening it without direct flame contact. The pressurized flow of the gas then entrains and removes the molten/softened material from the receptacle. Control valves regulate gas flow between the gas tank, heater, and receptacle to maintain safe pressure and temperature. A collecting casing with a filter captures the removed material and any residual gas.
mechanism_raw: Pressurized gas is preheated by a heater before entering a sealed receptacle containing the objects to be cleaned. The preheated gas transfers thermal energy to the target material inside the receptacle, melting or softening it without direct flame contact. The pressurized flow of the gas then entrains and removes the molten/softened material from the receptacle. Control valves regulate gas flow between the gas tank, heater, and receptacle to maintain safe pressure and temperature. A collecting casing with a filter captures the removed material and any residual gas.

abstract: A micro-fluidic oscillator comprises a main body and a cover body for covering the main body. An oscillation chamber is disposed on the main body to provide an oscillation space for fluid. A sudden-expansion micro-nozzle is connected with one end of the oscillation chamber, and an outlet passage is connected with the other end of the oscillation chamber. Two fluid-separating bodies are located at the connection positions of the outlet passage and the oscillation chamber, respectively. Two feedback channels are located outside two attachment walls. The sudden-expansion micro-nozzle is used to break the viscous shear stress between fluid and the walls and to generate unstable flow and oscillation. Moreover, the two feedback channels have different lengths, inside diameters and alternate outlet positions to further enhance the oscillation of fluid.
problem: Generating and sustaining stable fluid oscillation in a micro-fluidic device, where viscous shear stress between the fluid and channel walls tends to dampen or prevent oscillatory flow.
constraint: The feedback channels must have precisely tuned dimensions (length, diameter, outlet positions) to create the correct phase relationship for positive feedback and sustained oscillation; the sudden expansion must be sufficient to break shear layers but not so large as to cause excessive turbulence or flow separation that would dampen oscillation.
mechanism: A sudden-expansion micro-nozzle creates a geometric discontinuity that breaks the viscous shear stress between the fluid and the channel walls, generating flow instability and initiating oscillation. Two fluid-separating bodies at the outlet passage and oscillation chamber connection points help direct the flow. Two feedback channels of different lengths, inside diameters, and alternate outlet positions are positioned outside the attachment walls; these asymmetric feedback paths return a portion of the fluid to the oscillation chamber with a phase relationship that reinforces and amplifies the oscillation, sustaining it over time.
mechanism_raw: A sudden-expansion micro-nozzle creates a geometric discontinuity that breaks the viscous shear stress between the fluid and the channel walls, generating flow instability and initiating oscillation. Two fluid-separating bodies at the outlet passage and oscillation chamber connection points help direct the flow. Two feedback channels of different lengths, inside diameters, and alternate outlet positions are positioned outside the attachment walls; these asymmetric feedback paths return a portion of the fluid to the oscillation chamber with a phase relationship that reinforces and amplifies the oscillation, sustaining it over time.

abstract: A cooling device for use in an electric arc furnace is provided. The cooling device provides a novel and effective method for cooling burners, lances, enclosures, and other devices used in high heat environments, such as in Electric Arc Furnaces. According to one aspect of the invention used in a steel making process in an electric arc furnace, a cooling tube is inserted into a cooling cavity in a burner. Cooling fluid is injected through the cooling tube into the cavity to cool the portions of the burner adjacent the cooling cavity. The cooling fluid is then extracted from the cavity through a concentric space between the cooling tube and the cooling cavity. According to another aspect of the present invention, a cooling fluid distribution flange is provided to distribute cooling fluid to a plurality of cooling tubes to inject cooling fluid into a plurality of associated cooling cavities.
problem: Cooling burners, lances, enclosures, and other devices exposed to extreme heat in high-temperature environments such as electric arc furnaces, where conventional external cooling cannot adequately protect internal or embedded components.
constraint: The cooling tube and cavity must maintain a precise concentric relationship to ensure uniform fluid distribution and effective heat transfer while preserving structural integrity under thermal stress; the fluid flow rate must be sufficient for cooling but not so high as to cause pressure drop or structural weakening.
mechanism: A cooling tube is inserted into a cooling cavity within the hot device. Cooling fluid is injected through the central cooling tube into the annular cavity, where it flows radially outward to absorb heat from the cavity walls. The heated fluid is then extracted through the concentric annular space between the cooling tube and the cavity wall, carrying the absorbed heat away. A cooling fluid distribution flange supplies multiple cooling tubes simultaneously, ensuring uniform cooling across the device. The concentric flow path ensures that cooling fluid contacts all hot surfaces within the cavity before extraction.
mechanism_raw: A cooling tube is inserted into a cooling cavity within the hot device. Cooling fluid is injected through the central cooling tube into the annular cavity, where it flows radially outward to absorb heat from the cavity walls. The heated fluid is then extracted through the concentric annular space between the cooling tube and the cavity wall, carrying the absorbed heat away. A cooling fluid distribution flange supplies multiple cooling tubes simultaneously, ensuring uniform cooling across the device. The concentric flow path ensures that cooling fluid contacts all hot surfaces within the cavity before extraction.

abstract: A weightlifting device includes a handle member, an adjustable member, a set of weight plates, and a restricting unit. The handle member has a tubular end portion. The adjustable member extends into the end portion of the handle member, and is movable axially relative to the handle member. The weight plates are attached removably to the adjustable member. The restricting unit is operable so as to arrest and permit axial movement of the adjustable member relative to the handle member.
problem: Adjusting resistance or load during weightlifting exercises to accommodate varying strength levels or training goals.
constraint: Balancing the need for smooth, controlled axial movement with secure locking to prevent unintended slippage under load.
mechanism: A movable load-adjustment element with removable mass components, combined with a selective engagement mechanism that alternately permits or restricts movement of the element relative to a handle, enabling dynamic modification of effective resistance during operation.
mechanism_raw: An axially movable adjustable member with removable weight plates, combined with a restricting unit that selectively arrests or permits axial movement relative to the handle, enabling dynamic adjustment of the effective weight during use.

abstract: A vacuum vessel and at least two electrodes define an internal process space. At least one power supply is connectable with the electrodes. A substrate holder holds a substrate to be treated in the internal process space. At least one of the electrodes has along a first cross section a concave profile and has along a second cross section a convex profile, the first cross section being parallel to the second cross section. Gas is provided to the space through a gas inlet. Power is provided to the electrodes and the substrate is treated.
problem: Achieving uniform or controlled treatment of a substrate in a vacuum environment using plasma or electric fields.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and electrical performance of the electrodes while varying their geometry to control field uniformity.
mechanism: A set of electrodes with alternating curvature profiles arranged in parallel, configured to spatially modulate energy field intensity across a processing region by shaping field distribution through geometric variation.
mechanism_raw: Electrodes with alternating concave and convex cross-sectional profiles (parallel to each other) that shape the electric field distribution within the process space, enabling spatially tailored energy delivery to the substrate.

abstract: A lip gloss and brush assembly includes a container, a fixed member secured in the container, a rotation member rotatably mounted in the fixed member, a brush mounted in the rotation member, and a cover mounted on the container and secured to the rotation member. Thus, the rotation member is rotated by the cover to open or close flow of the lip gloss contained in the inside of the container, so that the lip gloss and brush assembly is operated easily and conveniently. In addition, the flow of the lip gloss is controlled by rotation of the cover, so that the lip gloss is allowed to flow smoothly and constantly without being choked, thereby enhancing the working condition of the lip gloss and brush assembly.
problem: Controlling the flow rate of a viscous fluid (e.g., lip gloss) in a dispenser to ensure smooth, consistent dispensing without clogging.
constraint: Ensuring precise mechanical linkage between rotation and flow control while preventing over-tightening or leakage.
mechanism: A rotational-to-axial motion converter linking a closure member to a dispensing element, where rotation of the closure directly translates to positional adjustment of the dispensing element relative to a reservoir, thereby controlling fluid flow through mechanical displacement.
mechanism_raw: A rotational coupling between the cover and a brush-mounted rotation member, where turning the cover directly translates to axial displacement of the brush relative to the container, modulating flow via mechanical positioning.

abstract: A method of fabricating a support structure. In one embodiment, the method is comprised of forming a layer of material into the support structure. The layer of material is adapted to be attached onto a substrate surface. The method further comprises treating the layer of material. The present method is further comprised of etching said layer of material. The fabricated support structure is then implementable during assembly of a display device. In one embodiment, the support structure is attached to the substrate surface prior to the forming, treating, and etching of the layer of material. In another embodiment, the support structure is attached to the substrate surface subsequent to the forming, treating, and etching of the layer of material.
problem: Fabricating precise support structures for display devices that require integration with substrates without damaging pre-existing components.
constraint: Balancing the timing of attachment relative to processing steps to avoid damage to the substrate or support structure during etching or treatment.
mechanism: A sequential layer-processing system where material layers undergo formation, treatment, and removal steps in a configurable order relative to attachment to a substrate, allowing process steps to be temporally arranged based on structural or material compatibility requirements.
mechanism_raw: A layered fabrication process involving forming, treating, and etching a material layer either before or after attachment to the substrate, allowing selective processing steps to be sequenced based on structural or material compatibility.

abstract: An air compressor formed of a plurality of collapsible members engaged between opposing rotating side members. The collapsible members alternate between a collapsed state and enlarged state during rotation around the side members which are engaged to polygonal segments of a generally circular rotating frame. Air compressed in each of said collapsible members during rotation toward the collapsed state is communicated to a reservoir in sealed communication with each of the plurality of bellowed members. The reservoir acts to hold-compressed air for use for powering air powered devices.
problem: Compressing air efficiently in a mechanical system while maintaining continuous output despite cyclic motion of components.
constraint: Coordinating the timing of bellows compression and expansion with rotational motion to ensure seamless air transfer to the reservoir without pressure loss.
mechanism: A cyclic compression-expansion system using collapsible chambers that alternately compress and expand during rotational motion, with compressed output from each chamber communicated to a shared buffer that stabilizes and maintains continuous delivery despite cyclic input variations.
mechanism_raw: Collapsible bellows alternating between collapsed and expanded states during rotation around polygonal frame segments, with compressed air from each bellows communicated to a shared reservoir that buffers and stabilizes output pressure.

abstract: A water-resistant electric motor includes a housing for receiving an electric motor armature therein and an end cap for closing an open end of the housing. The housing includes a drive shaft aperture within a cylindrical recess that receives a journal bearing and a ring seal. The end cap includes a wire access hole for receiving power supply wires. Surrounding the wire access hole is a ridge with cut-outs. A wire cover plate is seated on top of the ridge and includes cut-outs that correspond to the cut-outs in the ridge so that the power supply wires are accommodated therein when the cover plate is secured to the ridge. The wire access hole includes a grommet to seal the hole.
problem: Maintaining environmental sealing (water resistance) of an enclosure while allowing cables/wires to pass through its wall in a serviceable manner.
constraint: The seal must be maintained around irregularly shaped or multiple wires while still allowing the cover plate to be removed for wire servicing or replacement.
mechanism: A compressible sealing interface is formed between two cooperating surfaces, each containing aligned openings that allow one or more elongated elements to pass through. The openings accommodate irregular or multiple elements, and the compressive force between the surfaces creates a sealed engagement around the elements. An additional sealing element at the entry point enhances the environmental barrier while permitting removal of the clamping surface for servicing.
mechanism_raw: A ridge surrounding the wire access hole has cut-outs, and a cover plate with corresponding cut-outs is secured on top of the ridge. The wires pass through the aligned cut-outs, and the cover plate pressing down on the ridge creates a sealed interface around the wires. A grommet at the wire entry point provides additional sealing. The cut-outs in both the ridge and cover plate accommodate the wires while the compression between the cover plate and ridge maintains the seal.
residual_terms: ["compressible sealing interface", "cooperating surfaces", "aligned openings", "elongated elements", "compressive force", "sealed engagement", "sealing element", "environmental barrier"]

abstract: Adjustable spectacles article and protection method include a novel adjustable spectacle kit positioned in the interior surface of a self contained breathing mask. In one aspect, the breathing mask covers a full face of a wearer and includes a face plate permitting a wearer to view a space outside the mask. The adjustable spectacle kit includes a bracket attached to the interior surface of the mask, a lug attached to the bracket, and spectacles connected with the lug. In one aspect, the bracket defines a slot for holding the lug. In one aspect, the slot is elongated in an anteroposterior direction. In one aspect, a resilient elastomeric grommet is inserted in the slot, and the grommet frictionally engages the lug.
problem: Positioning corrective lenses at the proper distance and orientation inside a confined, sealed breathing mask where direct manual adjustment is difficult.
constraint: The friction engagement must be strong enough to hold the spectacles in place during movement and breathing, yet allow repositioning when needed.
mechanism: An elongated adjustment channel in a mounting bracket receives a movable attachment feature connected to the corrective lens assembly. A resilient frictional element disposed within the channel engages the attachment feature, creating sufficient friction to retain the lens assembly at a selected position along the channel while permitting manual repositioning when desired. The friction engagement eliminates the need for additional fasteners while maintaining positional stability during use.
mechanism_raw: An elongated slot in a bracket allows anteroposterior adjustment of a lug connected to spectacles. A resilient elastomeric grommet inserted in the slot frictionally engages the lug, holding it at the selected position. The friction between the grommet and lug provides both adjustability and secure retention without additional fasteners.
residual_terms: ["elongated adjustment channel", "mounting bracket", "movable attachment feature", "resilient frictional element", "friction engagement", "positional stability"]

abstract: The claim over prior art is for an approach to an electronically controlled or electronically monitored breathing system that represents an improvement in electrical reliability, manufacturing cost and efficiency, user maintenance, system reliability, user cost and maintenance. These improvements are accomplished by placing the major electronic, mechanical and electromechanical control elements and sensor components in a single replaceable module.
problem: Improving electrical reliability, manufacturing cost, maintenance, and system reliability in a complex electronically controlled breathing system.
constraint: The module must be self-contained enough to function independently when replaced, while still integrating properly with the rest of the breathing system.
mechanism: A complex control subsystem comprising multiple functional elements is consolidated into a single self-contained unit. This consolidation reduces interconnect complexity between individual components and enables the entire subsystem to be manufactured, tested, and replaced as a unified module.
