The dunnage conversion machine is pivotable relative to the stand between an operating position and a servicing/loading position whereat access to internal components of the machine is simplified. A stack of sheet stock material is jacketed and/or baled for simplified loading into a packaging system or stand. An adhesive layer on the bottom or top of the stack enables the stack to be easily spliced to another stack.
problem: Time-consuming and difficult loading and servicing of dunnage conversion machines, requiring complex access to internal components and manual handling of sheet stock material.
constraint: Maintaining operational stability and alignment of the machine during use while providing unobstructed access to internal components and enabling quick consumable loading.
mechanism: A mechanical reconfiguration system that transitions between operational and service/loading configurations via pivotable mounting, combined with pre-conditioned consumables that include integrated connection features for rapid material handling and unobstructed access to internal components.
mechanism_raw: Pivotable mounting of the machine on a stand that allows transition between an operating position and a servicing/loading position, combined with pre-packaged (jacketed/baled) sheet stock that includes an adhesive splice layer for easy connection to additional stacks — a mechanical reconfiguration plus consumable pre-conditioning approach that simplifies both access and material handling.

abstract: A multiple slave logging device, or “logger” for use in a system such as an electronic blasting system. The logger is able to communicate with multiple slave devices connected to it, and preferably also is able to communicate with a slave device connected individually. The logger preferably utilizes current modulation-based talkback from the slave devices, and optionally may also be adapted to detect the presence of inappropriate slave devices connected to the system.
problem: Reliably communicating with multiple slave devices in an electronic blasting system and detecting the presence of inappropriate or unauthorized slave devices.
constraint: Ensuring reliable, safe communication in a hazardous environment (explosives) while maintaining the ability to authenticate and reject unauthorized or incompatible devices.
mechanism: A communication protocol using current modulation on a shared line for bidirectional data exchange with remote devices, combined with device-type identification that detects and flags unauthorized or incompatible devices connected to the system.
mechanism_raw: Using current modulation on a shared communication line for bidirectional talkback from slave devices — each slave modulates the line current to transmit status/data back to the logger — combined with device-type detection that identifies and flags inappropriate slaves connected to the system.

abstract: The principle use of this invention is to allow the user to safely put up and take down a pole without climbing a ladder, removing any bolts or fasteners. Conventional types of removable pole support systems can be heavy, costly and time consuming to put up and take down. The “Easy Set-Up Pole & Support System” allows the user to mount a pole, in mainly the vertical direction without clamps or a ladder. The best example of use for this mechanical invention in the use of putting up a removable flag pole on a Recreational Vehicle (RV). The RV pole application is just one of a variety of applications where a removable pole invention can be used.
problem: Need to climb ladders and remove bolts or fasteners to safely install and remove vertical poles such as flag poles on RVs.
constraint: Providing sufficient mechanical stability to securely hold the pole under load while allowing easy insertion and removal from ground level.
mechanism: A retention system that accepts a vertical load through a mounting interface relying on gravity or friction to hold the load without mechanical fasteners, enabling ground-level insertion and removal while maintaining stability under operational forces.
mechanism_raw: A support system that accepts a pole in a mainly vertical direction through a mounting interface that holds the pole without clamps or fasteners, enabling ground-level installation and removal — a gravity- or friction-based retention mechanism that eliminates the need for elevated work or mechanical fastening.

abstract: The present invention relates to a process for selectively removing undesired oligosaccharides from aqueous mixtures such as plant processing waste products, including soy whey and other vegetable wheys, using an ultrastabilized large pore, hydrophobic zeolite Y. The resulting solution, which contains isoflavones and digestible sugars such as glucose, fructose and sucrose, can serve as the basis for a nutritious new product.
problem: Selectively removing undesired oligosaccharides from aqueous mixtures such as plant processing waste products (e.g., soy whey) while retaining valuable components like isoflavones and digestible sugars.
constraint: Maintaining adsorbent structural stability and selectivity in aqueous environments while achieving efficient and selective removal of target oligosaccharides without losing valuable co-products.
mechanism: A molecular separation process using a porous adsorbent with engineered pore size and hydrophobicity to selectively capture target molecules based on size and affinity, while smaller molecules and non-target compounds pass through unaffected.
mechanism_raw: Contacting the aqueous mixture with an ultrastabilized large-pore hydrophobic zeolite Y adsorbent that selectively captures oligosaccharides based on molecular size and hydrophobicity, while smaller molecules (glucose, fructose, sucrose) and target compounds (isoflavones) pass through — a size- and affinity-based molecular separation using a engineered porous adsorbent.

abstract: A high security key blade and key for use with a lock having a cylindrical shell, a key plug which is rotatably mounted in the shell, a longitudinal key slope in the key plug, and at least one locking tumbler assembly cooperating with a key being inserted into the lock. The locking tumbler assembly includes a pair of independently movable tumbler segments which are positionable in different elevational positions in a common cavity.
problem: Preventing unauthorized access to a lock by defeating standard key-based tumbler mechanisms.
constraint: Balancing increased security complexity with the need for reliable key insertion and plug rotation without jamming.
mechanism: Independent movable elements within a shared space allow variable positioning in multiple dimensions, creating a multi-dimensional keying system that resists replication by conventional single-plane methods.
mechanism_raw: Independent movable tumbler segments within a shared cavity allow variable elevation positions, creating a multi-dimensional keying system that cannot be replicated by conventional single-plane key cuts.

abstract: A stack of 50 layers of a first pitch-base carbon fiber sheet is formed, two sets of stack each having two second pitch-base carbon fiber sheets stacked therein are fabricated. At this time, the second carbon fiber sheets have a thermal expansion coefficient larger than that of the first carbon fiber sheet. Next, the stack of the first carbon fiber sheet is then held between two sets of stack of the second carbon fiber sheets. The stack of the first and second carbon fiber sheets are then impregnated with an epoxy-base resin composition and the resin is solidified. As a result a prepreg composed of the first and second carbon fiber sheets and the resin component composed of the epoxy-base resin composition is obtained. Thereafter, interconnections and the like are then formed on the prepreg, to thereby complete a multilevel interconnection board.
problem: Managing thermal stress and dimensional stability in composite materials used for precision electronics substrates.
constraint: Achieving uniform resin impregnation and curing without delamination while maintaining precise layer alignment.
mechanism: Layering materials with differing thermal expansion coefficients in a controlled configuration allows internal stress redistribution during curing, reducing warping and improving structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Layering materials with differing thermal expansion coefficients in a controlled stack configuration allows internal stress redistribution during curing, reducing warping and improving structural integrity.

abstract: A liquefied gas dispensing nozzle having a cylinder with its axis in a vertical direction, and a plug to be inserted into the cylinder from above as its main elements. A plurality of slit portions for letting through the liquefied gas are formed in parallel in an axial direction of the cylinder from the upper end to the lower end in an inner circumferential face of the cylinder contacting to an outer circumferential face of the plug. A width of at least one or more pair of mutually opposed slit portions is generally constant from its upper end to lower end and its slit bottom is inclined so that the depth of the slit becomes gradually shallower from upper end to lower end. Each slit portion of the cylinder is closed with the plug when the plug, which is movable vertically relative to the cylinder, reaches the lowest end position. A rounded portion formed by rounding a corner portion of the lower end of the slit portion includes an inclined slit bottom.
problem: Controlling liquefied gas flow rate and shutoff timing during dispensing operations.
constraint: Maintaining a leak-tight seal across all slit positions while ensuring smooth vertical plug movement under pressure.
mechanism: Axially varying flow restriction geometries with inclined surfaces create progressive flow reduction as a component moves, enabling gradual flow control and automatic shutoff when fully seated.
mechanism_raw: Axially varying slit depths with inclined bottoms create progressive flow restriction as the plug moves downward, enabling gradual flow reduction and automatic shutoff when fully seated.

abstract: A fluid injection and removal system to inject or remove fluids from a landfill or contaminated area. The system allows for treatment of waste in the landfill or the contaminated area. The fluid injection and removal system includes a permeable layer and at least one perforated pipe. The permeable layer enables essentially uniform distribution of the fluid into the underlying waste or contaminated area. The fluid injection and removal system can be combined with a leachate collection system to create a leachate recirculation system for use in a landfill. The leachate collection system includes at least one perforated collection pipe embedded in a drainage layer. Sensors can be provided in the permeable layer to enable the change in the physical characteristics of the waste adjacent the permeable layer to be monitored.
problem: Achieving uniform fluid distribution across heterogeneous subsurface waste or contamination zones.
constraint: Balancing permeability for fluid flow with structural integrity to withstand overburden pressure and chemical degradation.
mechanism: A permeable medium with embedded sensors and distributed conduits creates a network that equalizes fluid pressure while monitoring local property changes.
mechanism_raw: A permeable layer with embedded sensors and perforated pipes creates a distributed injection/removal network that equalizes fluid pressure while monitoring local physical property changes.

abstract: A medical device includes an insertable portion capable of being inserted into an orifice associated with a body of a patient. The insertable portion comprising an automated head unit capable of being manipulated in at least two axes of motion based at least in part on one or more control signals. The medical device further includes one or more controllers coupled to the automated head unit. In one particular embodiment, the one or more controllers generate the one or more control signals based at least in part on an input signal.
problem: Precisely manipulating a medical device within confined anatomical spaces using limited external control inputs.
constraint: Miniaturizing actuators and sensors to fit within an insertable form factor while maintaining sterility and biocompatibility.
mechanism: Automated multi-axis actuation driven by sensor-based feedback control enables real-time positional adjustments without direct mechanical linkages from outside the body.
mechanism_raw: Automated multi-axis actuation driven by sensor-based feedback control enables real-time positional adjustments without direct mechanical linkages from outside the body.

abstract: One embodiment of the invention provides a method for optimizing a variety of aspects of pipeline operations by using a genetic algorithm. Generally, the genetic algorithm is used to evolve a population of feasible solutions over successive generations until a termination condition is satisfied. Each solution specifies a feasible operational state of the pipeline system. Over successive generations existing solutions are modified, and an identified solution in the population is removed at each successive generation. Over repeated generations, the solutions in the population improve. Once an optimized production solution is generated, an optimized pressure solution may be generated using a direct pressure optimization process.
problem: Optimizing complex pipeline operations with multiple interdependent variables (e.g., production rates, pressure states) under dynamic conditions.
constraint: Balancing computational efficiency with solution quality, as the algorithm must terminate within practical time limits while avoiding premature convergence to suboptimal solutions.
mechanism: Using an evolutionary search process to iteratively refine a population of candidate solutions by modifying, selecting, and eliminating candidates across iterations until an optimized state is reached. A secondary direct optimization step then refines specific parameters.
mechanism_raw: Using a genetic algorithm to iteratively evolve a population of feasible solutions by modifying, selecting, and removing candidate solutions across generations until an optimized operational state is achieved. A secondary direct optimization step then refines pressure-specific parameters.

abstract: This invention discloses a process for synthesizing a modified crosslinked elastomeric particle which comprises a two-step polymerization of a conjugated diolefin monomer and a vinyl aromatic monomer by emulsion polymerization, wherein the particle is synthesized by the steps of (1) polymerizing a conjugated diolefin monomer, alone or in combination with a vinyl aromatic monomer, and optionally a crosslinking monomer, to create a crosslinked elastomeric core having residual double bonds and an outer surface; (2) polymerizing a monomer of a vinyl aromatic monomer, alone or in combination with a diolefin monomer, to create a polymeric shell, wherein the polymeric shell is grafted to the outer surface of the polymeric core by reacting with the residual double bonds of the polymeric core; and (3) coagulating the core-shell emulsion latex solution to recover the particles.
problem: Creating a core-shell particle structure with controlled interfacial bonding between the core and shell materials.
constraint: Ensuring sufficient residual double bonds remain in the core after crosslinking to enable grafting, while maintaining core mechanical stability during shell formation.
mechanism: Forming a crosslinked core with residual reactive sites, then attaching a secondary material to the core surface via chemical reaction with those sites, enabling structural integration while preserving core mechanical integrity.
mechanism_raw: Synthesizing a crosslinked elastomeric core with residual reactive double bonds, then grafting a polymeric shell to the core surface via chemical reaction with those residual bonds, enabling precise structural integration.

abstract: An insulating assembly and method for insulating printer/copier solid ink printheads. The insulating assembly includes printhead insulators having thermal insulation capable of moving along insulator paths interposed between the printheads and an ink receiving surface for insulating the printhead front faces. The method includes moving insulating assemblies along insulator paths interposed between the printheads and an ink receiving surface for insulating the printhead front faces.
reason: The mechanism is a static mechanical arrangement (movable insulators along predefined paths) without a generalizable causal principle. The solution is tightly coupled to the specific geometry and operational requirements of printhead systems.

abstract: We disclose an elasticity-measuring device which can be inserted into a canal part of living body and which is capable of quantitatively measuring the elasticity of the biological tissue of inner side of canal part. The device consists of a probe base (5) and probes (7). The probes (7) are secured to probe base (5) and driven to press onto and return from biological tissue. According to the stress or hardness of the biological tissue measured by sensors on probes (7) and to the deviation between the probes (7) and the probe base (5), we can decide the elasticity of the biological tissue of inner side of canal part quantitatively.
problem: Quantitatively measuring the elasticity of biological tissue in confined internal body canals where direct access is limited.
constraint: Achieving accurate measurements within the spatial and mechanical limitations of a minimally invasive device, requiring precise sensor calibration and probe geometry to avoid tissue damage.
mechanism: Applying controlled pressure to tissue via calibrated probes while measuring stress response and tracking mechanical displacement between the probes and a reference point to calculate elasticity from combined force and deformation data.
mechanism_raw: Using probes with sensors to apply controlled pressure to tissue and measure stress response, while simultaneously tracking mechanical displacement between the probes and a base to calculate tissue elasticity from the combined force and deformation data.

abstract: Described herein are marine devices and methods that convert mechanical energy in one or more waves to mechanical energy that is better suited for conversion into electrical energy. The marine devices employ a mechanical energy conversion system that harnesses wave energy and converts it into limited motion that is suitable for input to an electrical energy generator.
problem: Converting irregular, low-frequency mechanical energy from ocean waves into a controlled, limited motion suitable for efficient electrical energy generation.
constraint: Matching the variable frequency and amplitude of wave energy to the fixed operational parameters of electrical generators, requiring mechanical systems that can adapt to irregular input while maintaining consistent output.
mechanism: Harnessing variable input motion from an external energy source through a mechanical conversion system that transforms irregular amplitude and direction into a constrained reciprocating or rotational motion optimized for input to an energy conversion device.
mechanism_raw: Harnessing wave-induced motion through a mechanical energy conversion system that transforms the variable amplitude and direction of wave forces into a constrained reciprocating or rotational motion optimized for input to an electrical generator.

abstract: A method and apparatus are provided for reducing the VOC, CO, and, alternatively, the NOx content of dryer offgas that is discharged into the atmosphere from a moist organic product drying process using thermal oxidizing apparatus that includes a burner, furnace, mixing chamber, thermal oxidizer, tempering chamber, and an indirect gas-to-gas heat exchanger. The dryer offgas is separated into two portions, with a larger portion being preheated by indirect heat exchange with the hot gaseous output from the thermal oxidizer. The non-preheated portion is directed to the burner in the function of flue gas recycle for NOx control. The preheated portion is separated into two portions, with one portion being directed to the furnace/mixing chamber of the thermal oxidizing apparatus. The other portion of the preheated offgas is recycled to the hot gas inlet of the dryer and serves the function of dryer heat transfer media. Ultimately, all the dryer offgas enters the thermal oxidizer, and comprises a smaller non-preheated portion directed to the burner and a larger preheated portion directed to the furnace/mixing chamber. By preheating a large proportion of the offgas directed to the thermal oxidizing apparatus, simultaneous achievement of an adequate thermal oxidizer temperature, 1600° F., and an adequate oxygen concentration of 5% by volume is achieved for optimized thermal oxidation of carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds.
problem: Achieving simultaneous optimization of thermal oxidizer temperature (1600°F) and oxygen concentration (5%) for effective VOC/CO/NOx reduction in dryer offgas treatment.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient oxygen concentration (5%) while achieving high thermal oxidizer temperatures (1600°F) without external energy input, requiring precise flow splitting and heat recovery ratios.
mechanism: Split a gas flow into multiple streams, use one stream to preheat another via indirect heat exchange, and recycle a portion of the preheated stream back to the source system. This balances thermal energy distribution and maintains optimal reaction conditions by dynamically allocating flow proportions based on system requirements.
mechanism_raw: Splitting a gas flow into multiple streams, using one stream to preheat another via indirect heat exchange, and recycling a portion of the preheated stream back to the source system. This balances thermal energy distribution and maintains optimal reaction conditions by dynamically allocating flow proportions based on system requirements.

abstract: There is proposed a security document comprising a security element, wherein the security element is of such a configuration that it can be determined by means of the sense of human touch. For that purpose either the surface nature of various surface regions can be selected differently so that the configuration and size of the different surface regions can be determined by the human sense of touch. Another possibility is for the substrate of the security document to be provided with suitably shaped openings which can be identified by means of the human sense of touch. A combination of different tactile security elements of that kind is also described.
problem: Creating a security feature that can be verified by human touch without visual inspection.
constraint: Ensuring tactile features are sufficiently distinct and durable to be reliably identified by touch while remaining compatible with standard document manufacturing processes.
mechanism: Encode information through tactilely distinguishable surface regions or shaped openings in a substrate, where the configuration and size of these regions are designed to be identifiable by the human sense of touch.
mechanism_raw: Encoding information through tactilely distinguishable surface regions or shaped openings in a substrate, where the configuration and size of these regions are designed to be identifiable by the human sense of touch.

abstract: A battery pack for a power tool of self-contained over-charge protection is proposed. The battery pack includes a battery stack composed of a plurality of series connected secondary cells, and a charge terminal connected through a charge current path to the battery stack for flowing a charge current from a charger. The battery pack includes an interrupter inserted in the charge current path, and an over-charge detector which detects a cell voltage across each of the secondary cells and actuates the interrupter to open the charge current path when any one of the cell voltages becomes higher than a predetermined threshold (VTH3). Thus, even if the charger fails to limit the charge current, the battery pack can itself protect the secondary cells from being over-charged.
problem: Protecting battery cells from over-charging even when the external charger fails to limit charge current.
constraint: Achieving independent, fail-safe operation without relying on external charger behavior, requiring per-cell sensing and rapid circuit interruption within the battery pack itself.
mechanism: Monitor individual cell voltages in a battery stack and autonomously interrupt the charge current path when any cell exceeds a voltage threshold, decoupling protection from the charger's functionality.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring individual cell voltages in a battery stack and autonomously interrupting the charge current path when any cell exceeds a voltage threshold, decoupling protection from the charger's functionality.

abstract: The present invention provides a multi-player gaming machine that enables players waiting for players now playing a game to end it, to enjoy another game during waiting. The multi-player gaming machine includes a main game section providing a main game which can be played by a plurality of main players at the same time for coins or the like and in which awards based on the bet coins or the like are paid out to the main players in accordance with an outcome of the game, and a sub-game section providing a sub-game in which sub-players bet playing values on the game outcome for the main players and in which awards based on the coins obtained or the like are paid out to the sub-players in accordance with an outcome of the game. The main game section sends main game status information indicating a status of the main game to the sub-game section. The sub-game section determines a bet acceptance period of the sub-game on the basis of the main game status information.
problem: Keeping players waiting for a main game to end engaged during idle periods.
constraint: Synchronizing the secondary game's activity with the primary game's progress to maintain engagement without disrupting the primary game's operation or fairness.
mechanism: Link a secondary game's betting window to the real-time status of a primary game, allowing waiting players to place bets on the primary game's outcome while its state drives the secondary game's timing and rules.
mechanism_raw: Linking a secondary game's betting window to the real-time status of a primary game, allowing waiting players to place bets on the primary game's outcome while its state drives the secondary game's timing and rules.

abstract: A method of treating a warm-blood vertebrate. The vertebrate may be a human being or a lower animal. The treatment method involves administering to the vertebrate in need of such treatment a pharmaceutically effective amount of a complex of halide-free glucosamine and a therapeutic drug having a pKa of less than 7. Preferably, the complex is stabilized by coating it with at least one pharmaceutically acceptable polymer comprising a water-soluble, water-immiscible and/or water-swellable homopolymer and/or copolymer. Suitable polymers include carboxypolymethylene homopolymers and copolymers; polyethylene glycol homopolymers and copolymers, povidone homopolymers and copolymers, polyacrylic acid homopolymers and copolymers; polyacrylamide homopolymers and copolymers; polysaccharides; and mixtures of two or more of the foregoing polymers. The resultant polymer-coated complex will be stable upon exposure to ambient temperature and/or the atmosphere. Suitable acidic therapeutic drugs may be found in one or more of the following classes of therapeutic drugs: α- and β-Adrenergic Agonists; Narcotic and Non-Narcotic Analgesics; Anorexics; Antiallergics; Antianginals; Antiarrhythmics; Antiasthmatics; Antibiotics; Anti-coagulants; Anticonvulsants; Antidepressants; Antidiabetics; Antihistaminics; Anti-hypertensives; Nonsteroidal Anti-Inflammatories; Antimigraines; Antineoplastics; Antiparkinsonians; Antipsychotics; Antipyretics; Antispasmodics; Antithrombotics; Anti-ulceratives; Anxiolytics; Decongestants; Diuretics; Hepatoprotectants; Sedatives; and Vasodilators.
problem: Stabilizing a pharmaceutical complex of halide-free glucosamine and an acidic therapeutic drug for ambient storage.
constraint: Selecting a polymer coating that is pharmaceutically acceptable, maintains drug efficacy, and provides stability under ambient temperature and atmospheric exposure without interfering with the drug's release or function.
mechanism: Form a stable complex between glucosamine and the drug, then encapsulate it with a polymer coating that prevents degradation by isolating the complex from environmental factors like moisture and oxygen.
mechanism_raw: Forming a stable complex between glucosamine and the drug, then encapsulating it with a polymer coating that prevents degradation by isolating the complex from environmental factors like moisture and oxygen.

abstract: The fuel nozzle support funnel comprises a top conical section and a bottom smaller opening neck section. The top conical section has a top rim configured to seat over the fuel inlet opening of a truck fuel tank with the top conical section extending into the fuel tank. The bottom smaller opening neck section depends into the tank from a bottom smaller opening edge of the top conical section and has an inner sleeve therein made of a frictional material non reactant with diesel fuel. The inner sleeve and surrounding smaller opening neck section are of a diameter sufficient to allow passage therethrough of a fuel nozzle of a fuel pump. The top conical section has a plurality of openings therein through which air can escape during fueling to maintain the pressure within the tank constant.
problem: Sealing a fuel nozzle to a tank inlet while allowing nozzle passage and maintaining pressure balance during fueling.
constraint: Balancing the seal integrity, nozzle mobility, and pressure management without compromising fuel flow or causing leaks.
mechanism: A deformable sealing interface conforms around a passing object to create a pressure-tight barrier, while a gripping element provides controlled resistance to movement, and pressure-relief pathways prevent internal pressure accumulation during operation.
mechanism_raw: A conical funnel seats over the tank opening to create a seal, a frictional inner sleeve allows the nozzle to pass while gripping it, and pressure-relief openings in the funnel prevent pressure buildup during fueling.

abstract: A document management system comprises a document management apparatus that manages a document ID by associating the document ID with a storage time of the document, and checks the storage time in response to an inquiry about a permission of destroying the document and gives a permission of destroying the document when the storage time has expired, and a document destruction apparatus including a mode selection unit that selects one of a first destruction mode and a second destruction mode and an execution unit that destroys the document according to a destruction mode selected by the mode selection unit. The execution unit destroys the document without reading the document ID in the first destruction mode, and reads the document ID to inquire the permission of destroying the and destroys the document when the document management apparatus gives the permission of destroying the document in the second destruction mode.
problem: Managing document destruction while balancing compliance with retention policies and operational efficiency.
constraint: Trade-off between destruction speed (no ID checks) and regulatory compliance (ID checks required).
mechanism: A dual-path processing system selectively applies either a bypass route for rapid execution or a verification route that enforces authorization checks, enabling a trade-off between throughput and compliance.
mechanism_raw: A dual-mode destruction system: one mode bypasses document ID checks for speed, while the other enforces permission checks via a centralized management system to ensure compliance.

abstract: The present invention relates to a durable paper or paperboard substrate containing an effective amount of synthetic fibers and having enhanced strength in the machine direction and the cross direction, as well enhanced strength through the cross section of the sheet. The present invention further relates to methods of making and using the substrate.
problem: Enhancing paper strength in multiple directions (machine, cross, and cross-section) without sacrificing structural integrity.
constraint: Maintaining uniform fiber distribution and adhesion to avoid weak spots while maximizing strength gains.
mechanism: High-tensile reinforcing elements are embedded within a base substrate to enhance mechanical strength across multiple axes, leveraging their superior load-bearing properties relative to the base material.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating synthetic fibers into the paper substrate to reinforce strength in all directions, leveraging their higher tensile properties compared to natural fibers.

abstract: Disclosed is a vacuum cleaner including a suction nozzle; a dust collecting assembly which includes a dust collecting container having a dust collecting space and an opened bottom, an inlet, a filtering device provided in the dust collecting container, and an outlet; and a cleaner body which includes a dust collecting assembly receiving recess for detachably receiving the dust collecting assembly, a polluted air outlet provided at the dust collecting assembly receiving recess and communicating with the inlet of the dust collecting assembly, a clean air inlet provided on an inner wall of the dust collecting assembly receiving recess to face the dust collecting assembly and communicating with the outlet of the dust collecting assembly, and a clean air conduit having a fan provided therein, for exhausting the clean air to the outside of the vacuum cleaner.
problem: Efficiently separating dust-laden air from clean air in a vacuum cleaner while maintaining suction and filtration performance.
constraint: Balancing airflow resistance between the dust container and clean-air path to maintain suction without overloading the filter.
mechanism: A partitioned airflow system directs contaminated flow through a containment zone with filtration, while a separate clean-flow path carries filtered air to an exhaust point, maintaining pressure differentials to preserve suction.
mechanism_raw: A dust container with a filter isolates contaminated air, while a dedicated clean-air conduit with a fan exhausts filtered air, creating a dual-path airflow system.

abstract: A control system for regulating the flow of liquid metal in a device for casting a metal. A detector measures a process variable. A control unit evaluates data from the detector. At least one process parameter is automatically varied in order to optimize casting conditions. The detector measures a characteristic of the meniscus at at least two points on the meniscus instantaneously throughout the casting process.
problem: Optimizing liquid metal flow during casting to maintain meniscus stability and casting quality.
constraint: Achieving rapid, precise adjustments without introducing instability from overcorrection or sensor lag.
mechanism: Multi-point sensing of interface characteristics provides real-time feedback to a control system that dynamically adjusts process variables, stabilizing the interface through rapid corrective action.
mechanism_raw: Real-time monitoring of meniscus characteristics at multiple points enables dynamic adjustment of process parameters (e.g., flow rate, temperature) to stabilize the casting interface.

abstract: A muffler of a vehicle includes a first muffler body so as to form a first chamber, at least a second muffler body including a housing, one end portion opened and the other end portion closed, wherein one of the second muffler bodies is fitted into the other end portion of the first member to form a second chamber and the other second muffler bodies are fitted into each other through the one end portions in series to form third chambers if more than one second muffler bodies are assembled, an inflow pipe to connect the outside with the first, second and/or third chamber by passing the one end portion of the first muffler body, and an outflow pipe to communicate the first, second, and/or third chamber with the outside by passing through the other end portion of the last second muffler body.
problem: A vehicle muffler needs to attenuate exhaust noise across multiple frequency ranges while maintaining compact packaging and adequate exhaust flow.
constraint: The design must balance acoustic attenuation effectiveness against exhaust flow resistance and spatial packaging constraints within the vehicle, requiring the chambers to be sized and arranged so that noise reduction is achieved without excessive backpressure or volume occupation.
mechanism: A cascaded multi-stage acoustic treatment system uses a series of interconnected chambers of varying volumes and geometries to attenuate sound waves across multiple frequency ranges. An input flow path routes the medium through successive chambers, causing repeated reflection, expansion, and dissipation of acoustic energy at each chamber boundary. By varying chamber sizes and inter-chamber path lengths, different resonant frequencies are selectively targeted and damped. The staged arrangement enables progressive noise reduction through distributed acoustic impedance mismatches, avoiding the need for a single large chamber while maintaining flow continuity.
mechanism_raw: A modular chamber architecture uses nested and series-connected tubular bodies to create a cascade of acoustic chambers (first, second, and third chambers) of varying volumes and geometries. The inflow and outflow pipes route exhaust gas through these chambers in sequence, so that sound waves generated in the exhaust undergo repeated reflection, expansion, and dissipation at each chamber boundary. By varying the chamber sizes and the path lengths between them, different resonant frequencies are targeted and damped, while the staged arrangement allows progressive noise reduction without a single large chamber.

abstract: A carrier device for facilitating the suspended support of a vehicle rear suspension assembly. The device includes a pair of rotatably coupled members having support legs that are adapted to pass at least partially through an existing opening in the vehicle rear suspension assembly. Projections extending from the support legs subsequently engage the vehicle rear suspension assembly structure adjacent the opening, thereby providing support for the vehicle rear suspension assembly once suspended. A suspension element such as a cable or chain is coupled to the device and to a lifting mechanism, overhead conveyor, etc., for suspending the vehicle rear suspension assembly.
problem: Supporting and lifting a heavy vehicle rear suspension assembly without modifying its existing structure.
constraint: Must utilize existing openings and structural engagement points without requiring alterations to the suspension assembly itself.
mechanism: Using adjustable support elements that interface with existing structural features through openings, creating a load path to a lifting mechanism via a flexible connector.
mechanism_raw: Using rotatably coupled support legs that pass through pre-existing openings in the assembly and engage adjacent structural features, creating a secure suspension point that transfers load to the lifting mechanism via a cable or chain.

abstract: A needle bed (1) that comprises strips (4) in order to form needle channels (5), with the strips being configured in a comb-like manner. Between the individual teeth of this comb, recesses (28 through 37) are formed, said recesses being disposed to supply fluid to the needle channel (5) and to drain said fluid. The groove (12) that accommodates the strip (4) forms a distributor space where the distribution of the fluid to be supplied to the knitting tools takes place over a section of the strip (4), which section is preferably greater than half the length of the strip.
problem: Efficiently distributing and draining fluid to knitting tools in a needle bed while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Fluid distribution must occur within the structural confines of the needle bed without disrupting knitting operations.
mechanism: Integrating fluid distribution channels within a structural component by forming recessed pathways that allow controlled fluid flow along a significant portion of the component's length.
mechanism_raw: Comb-like strips with integrated recesses and grooves form needle channels and distributor spaces, allowing fluid to flow along a section of the strip longer than half its length for controlled supply and drainage.

abstract: The invention concerns a method for feeding and removing a board to/from a gap of a periodically operating press. The board to be pressed is fed grip-supported to the gap of the press from one side and a board pressed in the previous operating cycle is removed grip-supported from the same or from the opposite side during the opening cycle of the press. The movement feeding the board to the press and the movement removing the board from the press are performed at least partially staggered with each other.
problem: Feeding and removing a board to/from a periodically operating press without mechanical interference during cyclic operations.
constraint: Timing of feed and removal motions must be precisely coordinated with the press's periodic operation to avoid interference.
mechanism: Coordinating feed and removal movements with the periodic operation of a press by staggering their timing to ensure non-overlapping actions, preventing mechanical interference.
mechanism_raw: Staggered grip-supported movements for feeding and removal, timed to align with the press's opening and closing cycles, ensuring non-overlapping actions to prevent collision.

abstract: A method of modernizing the car door system of a elevator car, which originally comprises at least one car door leaf, a door drive with a crank gear and a drive linkage displacing the car door leaf and a car door/shaft door coupling actuated by the drive linkage, with the following method steps: demounting the door drive together with the crank gear and the drive linkage, mounting a door drive with a linearly moved drive means and coupling of the drive means with the car door leaf of the original car door system, and mounting an actuating device for actuating the car door/shaft door coupling.
problem: Modernizing an existing elevator car door system with a different drive mechanism while retaining compatibility with original components.
constraint: New linear drive must interface with the original door leaf and coupling mechanism without requiring full system replacement.
mechanism: Replacing a rotational drive mechanism with a linear actuation system that interfaces with existing door components, enabling compatibility without full system replacement.
mechanism_raw: Replacing the crank gear and drive linkage with a linearly moved drive means, coupling it to the original car door leaf, and adding an actuating device for the car/shaft door coupling.

abstract: A filter for use in absorbing heat from gases generated in a gas generating system is disclosed. The filter includes a plurality of discrete, continuous gas flow passages extending therethrough. In one embodiment, the filter is incorporated into an inflator used for inflating an inflatable element of a vehicle occupant protection system. A gas generator incorporating the filter and a vehicle occupant protection system incorporating the filter are also described.
problem: Absorbing heat from gases generated in a gas-generating system (e.g., vehicle inflators) while maintaining gas flow integrity.
constraint: Filter must balance gas flow permeability with sufficient surface area for heat absorption without structural failure under high-pressure conditions.
mechanism: Designing a filter structure with discrete flow passages that permit gas movement while transferring heat to the filter material, enabling thermal management during rapid gas generation.
mechanism_raw: Discrete, continuous gas flow passages through the filter structure allow gases to pass while transferring heat to the filter material, enabling thermal management during rapid gas generation.

abstract: A device for melt spinning, treating and winding synthetic threads includes a spinning unit, a treatment unit and a winding unit. The spinning unit, the treatment unit and the winding unit are arranged in tiers one above the other and form a plurality of single-thread or multi-thread production positions along the longitudinal side of a machine. To permit a rapid, simple operation, in particular at the start of a process and during interruptions of the process, an operator walkway is located at a height between the treatment device and the winding device.
reason: The patent describes a physical layout solution (operator walkway placement) without a causal mechanism that transfers beyond the specific context of melt spinning machinery.

abstract: Many methods are provided herein including a method of providing fluid loss control comprising: providing a treatment fluid; adding to the treatment fluid an acid-generating fluid loss control additive comprising an acid-generating component wherein the acid-generating fluid loss control additive forms droplets in the treatment fluid; and placing the treatment fluid into a subterranean formation. Other methods are provided as well.
problem: Controlling fluid loss in subterranean formations during treatment operations.
constraint: The droplet size and distribution must balance controlled release kinetics with compatibility in the treatment fluid.
mechanism: Forming reactive substance-containing droplets within a treatment fluid enables localized release or reaction at a target interface, creating a barrier or seal to reduce fluid loss.
mechanism_raw: Forming acid-generating fluid loss control additives as droplets in the treatment fluid enables localized acid release or reaction at the formation interface, creating a barrier or seal to reduce fluid loss.

abstract: The invention provides an improved furnace structure and methods of melting material in furnaces, particularly aimed at reducing the start up time for such furnaces. The furnace (2) defines a container for the molten metal having a maximum depth of molten metal in that container during use. A flow generator (30) for the molten metal within the furnace is fed through a first conduit (32) and supplies material back to the furnace through a second conduit (36). The first conduit entrance is provided in the upper 60% of the maximum depth of the molten metal in the container and/or the second conduit exit is provided in the lower 25% of the maximum depth of the molten metal in the container. The flow generator may receive material preferentially from around the periphery of the container and/or direct material towards the centre of the container. The inlet and outlet to the flow generator may be angled downwards towards the container. All of these features improve heat transfer and material circulation within the furnace.
problem: Reducing furnace start-up time by improving heat transfer and material circulation in molten metal processing.
constraint: Conduit placement and flow direction must balance circulation efficiency with structural integrity and energy consumption.
mechanism: Strategically positioning flow pathways (inlet in upper region, outlet in lower region) and directing flow from periphery to center creates a circulation pattern that enhances heat transfer and material mixing.
mechanism_raw: Strategically positioning conduits (inlet in upper 60% of depth, outlet in lower 25%) and directing flow from periphery to center creates a circulation pattern that enhances heat transfer and material mixing.

abstract: A range image generating apparatus capable of preventing or reducing generation of range images with interference, which contain e.g., pixels with erroneous distance values is provided. The range image generating apparatus includes: a light source radiating a light; an image pickup element; a range image generating unit; a frequency changing unit that changes a modulation frequency for each frame rate or charge storage time; and a control unit that controls the light source and the image pickup element in synchronization with the modulation frequency changed by the frequency changing unit.
problem: Preventing or reducing interference artifacts in range images caused by erroneous distance values.
constraint: Frequency changes must be precisely synchronized with image capture timing to avoid introducing new artifacts.
mechanism: Varying the modulation frequency of a light source in synchronization with image capture timing disrupts interference patterns, ensuring accurate distance measurements across frames.
mechanism_raw: Varying the modulation frequency of the light source in synchronization with frame rate or charge storage time disrupts interference patterns, ensuring accurate distance measurements across frames.

abstract: A drill bit for drilling a borehole includes a cutter element comprising a base portion. In addition, the cutter element comprises a cutting portion extending from the base portion and terminating in an elongate crest extending between a first crest end and a second crest end, and having an intermediate portion therebetween. The first crest end has a width W1 and the second end has a width W2 that is greater than the width W1. Still further, the intermediate portion of the crest has a width W3 that is less than the width W2 and less than or equal to the width W1.
problem: Improving drilling efficiency and reducing wear in borehole drilling operations.
constraint: Crest geometry must balance cutting effectiveness with mechanical strength to prevent premature failure.
mechanism: Varying the width of a cutting element's contact surface (narrower at one end, wider at the other, with an intermediate narrower section) optimizes cutting action across different material layers and reduces localized stress concentrations.
mechanism_raw: Varying the width of the cutter element's crest (narrower at one end, wider at the other, with an intermediate narrower section) optimizes cutting action across different formation layers and reduces localized stress concentrations.

abstract: A method for making a mobile unit accompany an objective person moves the mobile unit in correspondence with movement of the objective person and executes control so that the mobile unit moves along the walking direction of the objective person by detecting the foot landing of the objective person, detecting the walking speed and the walking direction of the objective person, and predicting the predictive walking range of the objective person on the basis of the detected information of the walking direction and the foot landing.
problem: A mobile unit (e.g., robot, vehicle) needs to autonomously accompany and follow a person, moving in correspondence with their walking motion without direct control input.
constraint: The prediction must be based on real-time detected gait information and must balance prediction horizon (how far ahead to predict) against accuracy, since over-prediction can cause the mobile unit to outrun or lose track of the person, while under-prediction causes lag.
mechanism: A tracking system detects periodic motion parameters of a target (timing of repetitive events, velocity, and direction of movement) in real time, uses those detected parameters to predict the target's future trajectory over a horizon, and controls a mobile platform to move along the predicted trajectory so that it maintains proximity to the target. The prediction horizon is dynamically balanced against prediction accuracy to avoid over-prediction (which causes the platform to outrun the target) and under-prediction (which causes lag).
mechanism_raw: The system detects gait parameters (foot landing timing, walking speed, walking direction) of the objective person, uses those detected parameters to predict the person's future walking range, and then controls the mobile unit to move along the predicted walking direction so that it accompanies the person.

abstract: The current invention relates to a security element for security substrates, such as those used for banknotes and the like, having enhanced public recognition, anti-counterfeit and detection properties. A security element comprising an elongate strip of a light transmitting polymeric substrate, said substrate being provided with a magnetic feature and a metallic design, the metallic design being provided by a combination of metal and non-metallic regions and comprising indicia, characters, patterns, designs, or geometrical shapes or a combination of the aforesaid design comprising at least one repeating pattern or which one or more of the frequency, the instantaneous amplitude and/or the maximum amplitude of the pattern varies along the length of the element, said pattern being positioned relative to the magnetic feature such that it does not overlap therewith.
problem: A security element for authentication substrates (e.g., banknotes) needs to provide enhanced public recognition, anti-counterfeit, and machine detection properties simultaneously.
constraint: The optical pattern and magnetic feature must be positioned so they do not overlap, ensuring each modality remains independently detectable without interference, while the pattern variation must be controlled along the length to maintain both human recognizability and machine readability.
mechanism: A security feature combines two independent verification modalities — a first visual/optical pattern and a second magnetic or machine-readable feature — arranged in a non-overlapping spatial relationship so that each modality remains independently detectable without interference. The first pattern's characteristics (such as frequency, instantaneous amplitude, and maximum amplitude) vary along a dimension to create both human-recognizable visual distinctiveness and machine-readable encoding, while the spatial separation ensures the second modality is not obscured or degraded by the first.
mechanism_raw: The security element combines two independent verification modalities — an optical metallic design (with patterns whose frequency, instantaneous amplitude, and/or maximum amplitude vary along the length) and a magnetic feature — arranged so that the optical pattern is positioned relative to the magnetic feature without overlapping it. This non-overlapping spatial arrangement allows each modality to be independently verified by different detection methods, while the varying pattern characteristics create visually distinctive and machine-readable features.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method and an arrangement in a cardboard creasing machine performing creases on a cardboard blank web. The web has a width of at least two lanes of blanks in parallel to each other and comprise in at least one zone per pair of lanes an area where intentional creases on both are made transversally to a feeding direction of the machine. The crease-lines are on the male side interrupted to provide a longitudinal seal strip to an edge of each blank to become. The cardboard web is in a limited area of such an interruption intentionally and positively lifted and supported from the side of a female crease die to a level in between being in line with to being above an outermost surface of a female crease die roller of the machine.
problem: In a cardboard creasing machine processing a multi-lane web, crease lines need to be interrupted at specific points to create longitudinal seal strips, but the interruption creates a risk of web damage or misalignment at those points.
constraint: The lifting and support must be applied only in a limited area of the interruption, from the female die side, and to a precisely controlled level — too little lift fails to prevent damage, while too much lift disrupts the creasing process or causes web misalignment.
mechanism: A processing web is creased along predetermined lines, with selected crease lines intentionally interrupted to create seal strips at specific locations. At each interruption point, the web is locally lifted and supported from one side of the creasing tool to a controlled level between flush with and above the tool's outermost surface. This localized intervention prevents damage to the web at the interruption while maintaining proper crease formation in non-interrupted regions.
mechanism_raw: The crease-lines are intentionally interrupted to provide longitudinal seal strips at the edges of each blank. At each interruption point, the cardboard web is intentionally and positively lifted and supported from the side of the female crease die to a level between being in line with and being above the outermost surface of the female crease die roller. This localized lifting and support prevents the web from being crushed or damaged at the interruption while maintaining proper crease formation in the non-interrupted regions.

abstract: The present invention discloses an oxidized mixed cyclic phenol sulfide which is a mixture of the oxidized cyclic phenol sulfide wherein m is 8 and the oxidized cyclic phenol sulfide wherein m is an integer other than 8, the oxidized cyclic phenol sulfide being represented by the following formula (1):wherein R is a straight or branched alkyl group having 1 to 6 carbon atoms, m is an integer from 4 to 9, and n is 1 or 2; or an oxidized cyclic phenol sulfide of formula (1) wherein m is 8. The present invention also discloses a charge control agent which comprises the above sulfide(s) as the active ingredient; and a toner which comprises the charge control agent, a coloring agent and a binder resin. This charge control agent is particularly useful for color toners, and it speeds up charging risetime, and has a high charge amount and charging characteristics excellent in environmental stability. Further, the charge control agent is safe since it does not have any problem with the waste regulations.
problem: A charge control agent for toners (especially color toners) needs to achieve fast charging risetime, high charge amount, and good environmental stability while being safe from waste regulation concerns.
constraint: The mixture must include both the m=8 variant and at least one variant where m is not 8, with m ranging from 4 to 9, so that the combined charge-transfer characteristics are optimized — a single compound cannot achieve the same balance of fast risetime, high charge, and environmental stability.
mechanism: A charge control agent comprises a mixture of compounds with different structural ring sizes, including a first compound with a specific ring size and at least one second compound with a different ring size within a defined range. The mixture of compounds with varying ring sizes provides a broader distribution of charge-transfer properties than any single compound, resulting in faster charging, higher charge levels, and more stable performance across varying environmental conditions.
mechanism_raw: The charge control agent uses an oxidized mixed cyclic phenol sulfide that is a mixture of two components: one where m (the number of phenol units in the cyclic structure) equals 8, and another where m is an integer other than 8 (ranging from 4 to 9). The mixture of compounds with different ring sizes provides a broader distribution of charge-transfer properties than a single compound, resulting in faster charging, higher charge levels, and more stable performance across varying environmental conditions.

abstract: An apparatus for generating short optical pulses is provided having a storage medium capable of storing optical energy, a first module for delivering pumping optical pulses or continuous beam into the storage medium to energize the storage medium, and a second module for delivering one or more trigger optical pulses to the optical storage medium. Each of the trigger optical pulses has a rising edge which causes a cascade release of the energy stored in the storage medium in an output optical pulse having a greater power and narrower in width or duration (at full width at half maximum) than the trigger optical pulse that caused the output pulse. A control module in the apparatus controls the operation of the pump module and trigger module so as to provide the desired characteristics of output optical pulses from the apparatus.
problem: An apparatus needs to generate short optical pulses with greater power and narrower duration than the trigger pulse that initiates them.
constraint: The trigger pulse's rising edge must be sharp enough to initiate the cascade release, and the control module must precisely time the pump energy delivery and trigger pulse delivery so that the storage medium is sufficiently energized but the cascade is cleanly triggered — insufficient pump energy yields weak output, while premature or delayed triggering disrupts the pulse characteristics.
mechanism: An apparatus stores energy in a storage medium that is energized by pumping energy into it. When a trigger signal with a sharp rising edge is delivered to the storage medium, it causes a cascade release of all stored energy, producing an output pulse that has greater power and narrower duration than the trigger signal. A control module coordinates the timing of energy pumping and trigger delivery to ensure the storage medium is sufficiently energized and the cascade is cleanly initiated.
mechanism_raw: The apparatus stores optical energy in a storage medium that is energized by pumping optical pulses or a continuous beam. When a trigger optical pulse is delivered to the storage medium, its rising edge causes a cascade release of all the energy stored in the medium, producing an output optical pulse that has greater power and narrower width (at full width at half maximum) than the trigger pulse. A control module coordinates the pump and trigger operations to ensure the desired output characteristics.
residual_terms: ["storage medium", "cascade release", "rising edge", "pump energy", "trigger pulse", "full width at half maximum"]

abstract: In accordance with various aspects of the present invention, provided is an extremely compact, simple, and cost-effective approach for aligning optical fibers in an optical fiber fusion splicer. The basis of this alignment method is an “S”-Curve Piezo Bending Actuator. The device comprises a thin strip of elastically flexible material (such as spring steel, beryllium copper, or fiber reinforced polymer) that is coated in four areas with a piezoelectric material (such as barium titanate or other known compounds).
problem: Precisely aligning optical fibers in a fusion splicer using a compact, simple, and cost-effective approach.
constraint: The need for precise multi-axis alignment must be balanced with compactness and cost — a single flexible strip with multiple localized piezoelectric actuation zones replaces complex multi-component mechanical or multi-actuator systems.
mechanism: Selective activation of localized actuation zones on opposing sides of a flexible element creates controlled differential strain, bending the element into a curved configuration. This controlled multi-directional deformation enables precise multi-axis positioning of target objects through coordinated actuation of the zones.
mechanism_raw: Selective activation of piezoelectric coatings on opposite sides of a thin flexible strip creates controlled differential expansion and contraction, bending the strip into an 'S' curve. This controlled multi-directional bending enables precise multi-axis positioning of optical fibers for alignment.

abstract: An adapter that consist of a cylinder that contains three flat springs shaped to fit around a golf ball and a spring retainer. A golfer can permanently insert the adapter into the butt end of a golf putter shaft without the use of tools. The adapter is comprised of a cylinders with it's out side diameter slightly larger than the inside diameter of the butt end of a putter shaft. When the adapter is inserted into the butt end of a golf putter shaft with the springs positioned in the adapter, the springs will not interfere with the golfer while putting The three flat springs are shaped and spaced slightly smaller than a golf ball when extended to pick up a golf ball. To position the springs to pick up a golf ball, the golfer manually pulls the main spring out of the adapter to a stop that positions the three springs to the proper length to pick up a golf ball. For a golfer to pick up a golf ball, the golfer positions the springs over a golf ball. With pressure down ward over a golf ball the springs will pick up a golf ball. When the process is complete the golfer pushes the springs back into the cylinder for future use.
problem: Picking up golf balls without tools while ensuring the pickup mechanism does not interfere with putting when not in use.
constraint: The springs must be small enough to not interfere with putting when retracted, yet large enough and properly shaped to reliably grip a golf ball when deployed — balancing stowage compactness with functional grip strength.
mechanism: Elastically deformable gripping elements are configured to engage a target object when extended (sized to generate gripping force through elastic recovery under compression), and are manually retractable into a protective housing to avoid interference during non-use.
mechanism_raw: Pre-shaped flat springs are elastically deformable to grip a golf ball when extended (sized slightly smaller than the ball so downward pressure causes gripping force through elastic recovery), and can be manually retracted into a cylindrical housing for storage and non-interference during normal use.

abstract: A method for reducing the level of elemental sulfur from sulfur-containing hydrocarbon streams as well as reducing the level of total sulfur in such streams. Preferred hydrocarbon streams include fuel streams such as naphtha streams that are transported through a pipeline. The sulfur-containing hydrocarbon stream is contacted with a mixture of water, a caustic, a surfactant, at least one metal sulfide, and optionally an aromatic mercaptan. This results in an aqueous phase and a hydrocarbon phase containing reduced levels of both elemental sulfur and total sulfur.
problem: Reducing elemental sulfur and total sulfur content in sulfur-containing hydrocarbon streams.
constraint: The surfactant must enhance phase contact sufficiently to enable sulfur transfer without preventing subsequent phase separation — balancing mass transfer efficiency with phase disengagement.
mechanism: A multi-agent treatment system combines chemical reaction (via a reactive agent), interfacial enhancement (via a surface-active agent), and catalytic/reactive pathways (via a catalytic agent) to transfer target species from a first phase into a second phase for separation, with the agents acting synergistically to balance mass transfer efficiency and phase disengagement.
mechanism_raw: A synergistic multi-agent treatment system where caustic provides chemical reaction with sulfur compounds, surfactant enhances interfacial contact between the aqueous and hydrocarbon phases, and metal sulfide provides additional catalytic or reactive pathways to transfer sulfur species from the hydrocarbon phase into the aqueous phase for separation.

abstract: A water distribution plate and diffuser plate assembly for distributing a stream emitted from a sprinkler nozzle comprising: a shaft having one end attached to a sprinkler component and an opposite end supporting first and second plates in axially spaced relationship for rotation about the shaft independent of one another; the first plate located adjacent the nozzle and formed with at least one water distribution groove shaped and arranged to divide a primary stream emitted from the nozzle into a plurality of secondary streams, and the second plate located downstream of the first plate and formed with at least one diffuser element arranged to be struck by at least some of the secondary streams exiting the first plate, and wherein speed of rotation of the first and second plates is braked.
problem: Effectively distributing a stream emitted from a sprinkler nozzle into a desired pattern.
constraint: The need for even and controllable distribution must be balanced with pattern stability — independent rotation enables varied distribution effects, while braking prevents uncontrolled spinning that would randomize the desired pattern.
mechanism: Two independently rotatable elements on a shared axis: a first element subdivides an incoming flow into multiple streams via internal flow-altering features, and a second downstream element further disperses the streams via diffusion features. Independent rotation of each element and speed regulation of both elements enables controlled, patterned distribution of the fluid.
mechanism_raw: Two independently rotating plates on a shared shaft: the first plate (adjacent to the nozzle) subdivides the primary stream into multiple secondary streams via distribution grooves, and the second plate (downstream) further diffuses those secondary streams via diffuser elements. Independent rotation of each plate and speed braking of both plates allows controlled, patterned distribution of the fluid.

abstract: Methods are provided for treating suspensions of particles to improve the drainage rate and/or the solids content of flocs of the particles. The method includes the steps of (i) providing a suspension which comprises particles in a fluid; (ii) adding a cyclodextrin compound to the suspension; and (iii) dewatering the suspension by removing at least a portion of the fluid to form a cake comprising the particles. The cyclodextrin compound desirably is added in an amount effective to increase the dewatering rate of the flocs, to increase the solids content, or both, over that rate, solids content, or both, that would be obtained without the addition of the cyclodextrin compound. The suspension may be, for example, a biological or non-biological sludge, or a suspension of pulp fibers, such as in a pulping or papermaking process.
problem: Improving the drainage rate and/or solids content of flocs in particle suspensions during dewatering.
constraint: The cyclodextrin must be effective at low concentrations to improve dewatering without excessive chemical addition — balancing treatment cost and chemical load against dewatering performance gains.
mechanism: A host-guest chemistry agent is introduced to modify particle interactions in a suspension, altering floc structure and surface properties to create a more open, permeable floc network that releases interstitial fluid more readily during mechanical dewatering.
mechanism_raw: Adding a cyclodextrin compound to the suspension modifies particle interactions through host-guest chemistry — cyclodextrin molecules interact with particles or dissolved species, altering floc structure and surface properties to create a more open, permeable floc network that releases water more readily during dewatering.

abstract: A synchronous drive apparatus includes first and a second rotors. The rotors have multiple teeth for engaging sections of an elongate drive structure. A rotary load assembly couples to the second rotor. The elongate drive structure engages about the rotors. The first rotor drives and the second rotor is driven by the elongate drive structure. One of the rotors has a non-circular profile having at least two protruding portions alternating with receding portions. The rotary load assembly presents a periodic fluctuating load torque when driven in rotation. The angular positions of the protruding and receding portions of the non-circular profile relative to the angular position of the second rotor, and the magnitude of the eccentricity of the non-circular profile, are such that the non-circular profile applies to the second rotor an opposing fluctuating corrective torque which reduces or cancels the fluctuating load torque of the rotary load assembly.
problem: Fluctuating load torque in a rotary system causes unwanted vibrations or inefficiencies.
constraint: The eccentricity magnitude and angular alignment of the non-circular profile must precisely match the frequency and phase of the fluctuating load torque to achieve cancellation.
mechanism: A variable geometric element with alternating protruding and receding regions generates a counteracting force synchronized to the frequency and phase of periodic load fluctuations, dynamically canceling them through geometric and angular alignment.
mechanism_raw: A non-circular rotor profile with alternating protruding and receding portions applies a corrective torque that opposes the periodic load fluctuations, dynamically canceling them through geometric and angular synchronization.

abstract: The present invention is a device for use in cleaning a fabric surface of dust, dirt, pet hair and other debris present on the surface. The device includes a pair of cleaning members or rollers disposed on an underside of the device which can roll with respect to the device and with respect to one another. The rollers are selectively contacted with one another such that each roller can assist in removing debris picked up by the opposite roller and dispensing the debris into a collection chamber releasably positioned within the housing. The removal of the debris from each roller is also facilitated by opposed edges of a central opening in the housing that contact the rollers and direct the debris into the debris collection chamber.
problem: Efficient removal and collection of debris from a fabric surface using a handheld device.
constraint: The selective contact pressure between rollers and the geometry of the housing opening must balance debris pickup efficiency with minimal user effort.
mechanism: Two contacting transfer elements move debris between each other while a housing with directed openings channels the debris into a collection region, creating a self-cleaning transfer path through selective pressure and geometric guidance.
mechanism_raw: Two rollers in mutual contact transfer debris between each other while opposed edges of a central housing opening direct the debris into a collection chamber, creating a self-cleaning transfer path.

abstract: An apparatus and method for correcting static and dynamic imbalance with a single mass in a hard disk drive is disclosed. The method provides for determining a static imbalance of a hard disk assembly and for determining a dynamic imbalance of the hard disk assembly. A greater imbalance from the static imbalance and the dynamic imbalance is determined. A single mass is applied to the hard disk assembly to correct the greater imbalance.
problem: Static and dynamic imbalances in a rotating assembly (e.g., hard disk) cause mechanical instability or wear.
constraint: The mass must be positioned and sized to address the dominant imbalance mode without overcorrecting the secondary mode.
mechanism: A corrective mass is selectively applied to a rotating system to counteract the dominant imbalance mode, using a prioritized correction strategy that avoids overcorrection of secondary modes.
mechanism_raw: A single corrective mass is applied to the assembly to counteract the greater of the measured static or dynamic imbalance, using a prioritized correction strategy.
residual_terms: ["corrective mass", "static or dynamic imbalance", "prioritized correction strategy"]

abstract: A conversion entity and method for converting higher-rate speech parameters into lower-rate parameters including dimmed excitation parameters. The conversion entity comprises a first decoder configured to produce a target excitation from the higher-rate parameters, based on a first fixed contribution and a first adaptive contribution. The conversion entity also comprises a second decoder configured to produce a second adaptive contribution, and configured to selectably operate in a first or a second mode. In the first mode, the second adaptive component is generated based on the first fixed contribution for a previous frame, while in the second mode, the second adaptive component is generated based on a second fixed contribution for the previous frame. The second decoder operates in the second mode in response to a rate reduction request. A processing module determines the dimmed excitation parameters for generation of the second fixed contribution for the current frame, based on the target excitation and the second adaptive contribution.
problem: Reducing the data rate of speech parameters while preserving perceptual quality.
constraint: The processing module must balance computational complexity with the accuracy of dimmed parameter generation to maintain speech intelligibility.
mechanism: Two adaptive decoding pathways generate parameter contributions based on prior frame data, with mode selection between fixed and adaptive configurations driven by rate reduction requests, enabling dynamic parameter scaling while preserving perceptual quality.
mechanism_raw: Two decoders adaptively generate contributions based on prior frame data, with mode selection (fixed vs. adaptive) driven by rate reduction requests, enabling dynamic parameter scaling.

abstract: An early suppression fast response pendent-type fire protection sprinkler is suitable for use in accordance with one or more of NFPA 13, NFPA 231 and NFPA 231C to protect single row rack storage, double row rack storage and multiple row rack storage, the sprinkler having a K-factor of about 25 and flowing pressure of about 15 pounds per square inch. Preferably, the sprinkler has a body defining an orifice and an outlet for delivering a flow of fluid from a source, and a deflector mounted with a first surface opposed to flow of fluid from the outlet. The deflector defines at least one pair of generally opposed reentrant slots extending from the first surface through the deflector, the reentrant slots extending from slot openings at an outer peripheral edge of the deflector inwardly from the peripheral edge toward a deflector axis.
problem: Achieving rapid and uniform fluid distribution in fire suppression systems for rack storage.
constraint: The slot geometry and K-factor must align with pressure and flow rate requirements to meet NFPA standards for fast response.
mechanism: Shaped flow redirection elements with reentrant slot geometries create controlled fluid flow patterns that enhance coverage and penetration into target regions through pressure and flow rate alignment.
mechanism_raw: Reentrant slots in a deflector create controlled fluid flow patterns that enhance spray coverage and penetration into storage racks through shaped flow redirection.

abstract: A cooling fan for rotating machine having a sufficient cooling performance, mass production performance and easiness in mounting is provided.
