In a final position the layer is shifted to the free ends of the bristles. By shifting said hairbrush from an initial position to a final position tangled hair is gathered along the layer and easily removed from the hairbrush.
problem: Enabling easy removal of trapped debris (e.g., hair) from a brush-like tool without manual intervention.
constraint: Ensuring smooth mechanical movement of the layer without damaging bristles or compromising the brush's structural integrity during shifting.
mechanism: Shift a movable barrier with openings relative to flexible elements from a first position (elements fully extended) to a second position (barrier at element tips), causing trapped debris to accumulate on the barrier for removal.
mechanism_raw: Shifting a perforated layer relative to bristles from an initial position (bristles fully protruding) to a final position (layer at bristle tips), causing trapped debris to gather along the layer for removal.

abstract: In one aspect, the present disclosure relates to a high-strength prestressing strand having a seven-wire structure in which one core wire and six outer wires are stranded. An external diameter of the strand is from 15.0 mm to 16.1 mm, a total cross-sectional area of the strand is 135 mm2 or more, and a load at 0.2% permanent elongation is 266 kN or more. A relaxation value measured after a 1000-hour relaxation test is 2.5% or lower and a diameter of the core wire is 5.35±0.3 mm and a diameter of the outer wires is 5.15±0.25 mm. The core wire and the outer wires each have a composition of at least 0.90% carbon. The prestressing strand is manufactured by stranding the core wire and outer wires, giving a stretching treatment, and giving a bluing treatment at a temperature of 380° C. or more and 430° C. or less after or at the same time with the stretching treatment.
problem: Achieving high-strength prestressing strands with low relaxation and long-term durability under sustained loads.
constraint: Maintaining precise dimensional tolerances and material composition to balance strength, relaxation resistance, and manufacturing feasibility.
mechanism: Form a composite strand by helically arranging a central element with surrounding elements in a geometric pattern, applying mechanical stretching and surface treatments to optimize material properties, and controlling thermal processing to minimize long-term deformation under sustained loads.
mechanism_raw: Stranding a core wire with outer wires in a specific geometric configuration, applying stretching and bluing treatments to optimize material properties, and controlling thermal processing to reduce relaxation.

abstract: A method and system of establishing an offset for a receiver. In one embodiment, a method includes receiving an input signal and generating a first signal. The method can further include integrating the input signal and the first signal at a reference node. In addition, the method can include comparing the input signal to a signal at the reference node and generating an output signal, analyzing the output signal to determine whether the output signal contains noise, and modifying the first signal based on the analysis of the output signal.
problem: Establishing an accurate offset for a receiver in the presence of noise to improve signal fidelity.
constraint: Accurately distinguishing noise from signal variations without introducing latency or distortion during adjustment.
mechanism: Combine input and corrective signals at a comparison point, analyze differences to identify noise components, and dynamically modify the corrective signal based on noise characteristics to adjust a receiver's operational offset.
mechanism_raw: Integrating input and feedback signals at a reference node, comparing them to detect noise, and dynamically adjusting the feedback signal based on noise analysis to correct the offset.

abstract: A system and method for remediation of contaminated soil are provided. The system comprises a soil remediation cell of contaminated soil and a plurality of multi-functional conduits located within the contaminated soil. Each multi-functional conduit defines a reaction housing. The multi-functional conduits includes heating elements for introducing heat into the contaminated soil for volatilizing the contaminants located within the contaminated soil, without utilizing mechanically driven forced air. This produces a contaminated vapor. The system and allows for re-circulation of vapors generated during breakdown of contaminants allowing for use of the re-circulated vapor for heat production and energy use. The system may be utilized for remote access and portability to disparate locations whereby the system does not require use of a container or receptacle. A substantial portion of the contaminants in the contaminated vapor are destroyed in the reaction housing. A substantially non-contaminated vapor is produced in which at least about 80% by weight of the contaminants have been destroyed.
problem: Remediating contaminated soil efficiently without mechanically driven forced air systems.
constraint: Optimizing heat distribution and vapor recirculation to maximize contaminant destruction efficiency without requiring external containment structures.
mechanism: Deliver thermal energy through distributed channels to volatilize contaminants, recirculate generated vapors to sustain heat production, and destroy contaminants in a sealed reaction chamber while maintaining system portability.
mechanism_raw: Introducing heat via conduits to volatilize contaminants, recirculating generated vapors for heat production, and destroying contaminants in a reaction housing while maintaining portability.

abstract: A method and a device for source coding with a time advanced excitation signal. During an encoding process, a source data signal is first divided into consecutive blocks, then a first set of parameters related to a filter describing properties of a first block covering a first time period is extracted, followed by the extraction of a second set of parameters related to an excitation signal for said filter, where said second set of parameters is determined from and describing properties of both the first block and a second block following the first block within a second time period starting later than said first time period and extending outside said first time period.
problem: Improving source coding efficiency by accurately modeling excitation signals for a filter describing a current data block.
constraint: Balancing the use of future data to improve encoding accuracy without introducing excessive latency or computational overhead.
mechanism: Using parameters derived from both the current block and a subsequent block (extending beyond the current block's time period) to determine excitation signal properties, enabling more accurate prediction of the current block's characteristics by leveraging future context.
mechanism_raw: Using parameters derived from both the current block and a subsequent block (extending beyond the current block's time period) to determine excitation signal properties, enabling more accurate prediction of the current block's characteristics by leveraging future context.

abstract: In the method of using ambient air to vaporize liquefied gas, the steps include transferring heat from a stream of ambient air to a stream of liquefied gas, thereby cooling the air stream, and vaporizing the liquid; transferring heat from a source into the cooled air stream; and then discharging the heated air stream to atmosphere, sufficient heat being transferred to obviate objectionable fog production resulting from step c).
problem: Preventing objectionable fog production during the vaporization of liquefied gas using ambient air heat exchange.
constraint: Optimizing heat transfer steps to achieve fog suppression while maintaining efficient energy use and avoiding overcooling of the air stream.
mechanism: Sequentially transferring heat from ambient air to liquefied gas (cooling the air), then using the cooled air to absorb heat from an additional source before atmospheric discharge, ensuring sufficient thermal energy is removed to suppress fog formation.
mechanism_raw: Sequentially transferring heat from ambient air to liquefied gas (cooling the air), then using the cooled air to absorb heat from an additional source before atmospheric discharge, ensuring sufficient thermal energy is removed to suppress fog formation.

abstract: A locking mechanism for a pyrotechnic safe and arm interrupter 98 may be constructed with an external lock casing 2, longitudinally extending bolt 3, washer 4, spring 5, retaining ring 8 and interlocking element 9 that may be configured in various shapes and features corresponding with a safety release component. A key 10 may be constructed with key stem 11, handle 12 and two pairs of teeth 13, 14 of different diameters radially protruding from successively reduced diameters along a distal portion of key stem 11. Lock 1 may be installed with notch 19 in alignment with a corresponding feature of the safe and arm interrupter mechanism and fastened in place with mounting holes 20 so that only mounting flange 17 and the key access 18 are external to the interrupter device, panel or door.
problem: Securing a pyrotechnic safe and arm device with a key that ensures precise mechanical alignment of internal locking components.
constraint: Ensuring only a uniquely configured key can actuate the lock while maintaining mechanical robustness under pyrotechnic safety conditions.
mechanism: A key with radially varying diameter teeth engages a lock casing containing interlocking elements and a spring-loaded bolt, where the key's geometry forces the interlocking elements into alignment with the bolt to enable or block rotation.
mechanism_raw: A key with radially varying diameter teeth engages a lock casing containing interlocking elements and a spring-loaded bolt, where the key's geometry forces the interlocking elements into alignment with the bolt to enable or block rotation.

abstract: A lock device having a key and a lock cylinder. The lock cylinder includes a fixed cylinder housing and a cylinder core mounted to rotate therein. The key shaft (10.3) has an edge profile and may be inserted in a key way of the cylinder core in which displaceable tumblers (41, 42) are located transverse to the above. The key shaft (10.3) has profiled recesses running in the longitudinal direction. The recesses have a pair of follow points for each tumbler (41, 42) for coding the key, whilst the tumbler (41. 42) has a pair of counter follow points which are the basis of the corresponding counter coding. A space-saving design of the lock device is achieved with a large range of variation for the coding wherein both follow points are on the key shaft (10.3) in the form of recesses, arranged on opposing lateral surfaces to an edge (57.2; 57.3) of the edge profile of the key shaft (10.3). A web (22: 23) is thus generated in the corner region of the edge profile between both recesses. The web functions as a code web (22; 23), as the opposing web edges serve for the coding. The corresponding tumblers (41, 42) have a cut-out, which in use enclose the code web (22; 23) on opposing web edges. The lateral limits of the cut-out form the counter follow points in the tumblers (41, 42).
problem: Achieving a compact lock design with a large range of coding variations for security applications.
constraint: Maximizing coding variability while minimizing the physical space required for the key-tumbler interface.
mechanism: Using opposing recesses on a key shaft's edge profile to form a 'code web,' which interacts with corresponding cut-outs in tumblers to encode the key, allowing multiple coding configurations within a constrained spatial footprint.
mechanism_raw: Using opposing recesses on a key shaft's edge profile to form a 'code web,' which interacts with corresponding cut-outs in tumblers to encode the key, allowing multiple coding configurations within a constrained spatial footprint.

abstract: A rail joint assembly joining the ends of two rails together includes a pair of joint bars. Each joint bar having one side configured to the rail web side. Mechanical fasteners mount the joint bars to the web sides. Pairs of load bearing keys are embedded in web counter bores at predetermined depths into the webs and embedded in adjacent joint bar counter bores at predetermined depths into the joint bars. The pairs of keys in the webs and the joint bars transfer railway loads through the joint and substantially strengthen the rail joint assembly.
problem: Strengthening a rail joint assembly to transfer railway loads effectively while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Ensuring keys are positioned at optimal depths to distribute loads evenly while avoiding stress concentrations that could weaken the rail or joint bars.
mechanism: Embedding load-bearing keys into precisely machined counter bores in both the rail webs and joint bars, creating a mechanical linkage that directly transfers shear and tensile forces through the joint without relying solely on friction or surface contact.
mechanism_raw: Embedding load-bearing keys into precisely machined counter bores in both the rail webs and joint bars, creating a mechanical linkage that directly transfers shear and tensile forces through the joint without relying solely on friction or surface contact.

abstract: A new system and method for making agglomerates from material like wet chopped glass fiber strand segments is disclosed and the agglomerates so produced. Agglomerates, made by feeding wet chopped fiber strand segments into a wave chamber having a vibrating curved surface supporting a curved, dimpled liner working surface have improved density and flow characteristics compared with dry chopped strands, but it was discovered that the dimpled liner flexes during operation during vibration causing undesirable variation in properties like agglomerate size. In the invention the dimpled liner is backed up with a substantially non-compressible material and this results in agglomerates that have even better uniformity of flow and agglomerate diameters. Typical backing materials include a particulate material, an elastomer, a rididized elastomer, slurry or liquid, or wire or slivers of metal.
problem: Achieving uniform physical properties (e.g., size, density) in agglomerates formed by vibrating a dimpled surface, where surface deformation during operation causes variability.
constraint: Must maintain sufficient structural rigidity to prevent flexing while allowing the vibrating surface to impart the necessary mechanical energy for agglomeration.
mechanism: Backing a flexible working surface with a substantially non-compressible material to suppress deformation during vibration, ensuring consistent interaction between the vibrating surface and the material being processed.
mechanism_raw: Backing a flexible working surface with a substantially non-compressible material to suppress deformation during vibration, ensuring consistent interaction between the vibrating surface and the material being processed.

abstract: Hybrid composites including carbon nanotubes and a carbide-derived carbon material, electron emitters including the hybrid composites, methods of preparing the electron emitters, and electron emission devices including the electron emitters are provided. Specifically, a hybrid composite includes at least one carbon nanotube and a carbide-derived carbon material. The carbide-derived carbon material is prepared by thermochemically reacting a carbide compound with a halogen-containing gas to extract substantially all of the elements except for the carbon in the carbide compound. Since the carbon nanotubes and the carbide-derived carbon material are hybridized and composited, a screen effect that may occur when large amounts of carbon nanotubes are used can be prevented, and an electron emitter including the hybrid composite has excellent electron emission capabilities, excellent uniformity, and a long lifetime.
problem: Preventing performance degradation (e.g., electron emission screening) when incorporating high concentrations of carbon nanotubes into composite materials.
constraint: Balancing the ratio of nanotubes to matrix material to avoid screening effects while preserving the conductive and structural benefits of both components.
mechanism: Hybridizing carbon nanotubes with a carbide-derived carbon matrix to spatially separate and stabilize the nanotubes, reducing mutual interference and enabling uniform electron emission.
mechanism_raw: Hybridizing carbon nanotubes with a carbide-derived carbon matrix to spatially separate and stabilize the nanotubes, reducing mutual interference and enabling uniform electron emission.

abstract: There is provided an industrial fabric comprising a layer of batt of fibres optionally needled to a base cloth, whereby during manufacture of the fabric a dispersion of particulate, polymeric material has been applied to the layer of batt of fibres and thermally activated to provide a discontinuous layer containing a mixture of batt fibres and a polymer-baft fibre matrix.
problem: Creating a composite material with a controlled distribution of polymer and fiber phases in an industrial fabric, where uniform integration is difficult to achieve.
constraint: Requires precise thermal activation to ensure the polymer flows and integrates with the fibers without degrading the base material or causing uneven distribution.
mechanism: Applying a thermally activatable polymer dispersion to a fiber layer and activating it to form a discontinuous matrix that binds the fibers in place, creating a mixed-phase composite structure.
mechanism_raw: Applying a thermally activatable polymer dispersion to a fiber layer and activating it to form a discontinuous matrix that binds the fibers in place, creating a mixed-phase composite structure.
residual_terms: ["thermally activatable polymer dispersion", "fiber layer", "discontinuous matrix", "mixed-phase composite structure"]

abstract: Provided is a suspended nanowire sensor having good sensing characteristics and suitable for mass production, a method for fabricating the suspended nanowire sensor. The suspended nanowire sensor includes: first and second sensor electrodes formed on upper portions of a substrate and physically separated from each other; and a nanowire sensor material piece extending from the first sensor electrode to the second sensor electrode and physically suspended between the first and second sensor electrodes.
problem: Creating a suspended nanowire sensor with high sensitivity and mass production feasibility.
constraint: Balancing sensitivity (via free interaction) with structural integrity and manufacturing scalability.
mechanism: Suspending a sensing element between two contact points allows unobstructed interaction with the environment, enhancing sensitivity while maintaining structural support for scalable fabrication.
mechanism_raw: Physically suspending a nanowire between two electrodes allows unobstructed interaction with the environment, enhancing sensing characteristics while maintaining structural support for scalable fabrication.

abstract: In a method for determining a compaction degree of a surface segment, the following steps are provided: passing over the deposited layer of the surface segment to be compacted, determining positional data of a position of the compacting machine, defining a current partial surface of the surface segment of the deposited layer, the current partial surface possibly consisting of a plurality of subsegments which have already been passed over, measuring and/or picking up parameters at the position of the compacting machine, and storing the parameters together with the position data, assigning the parameters to the current partial surface or to all subsegments of the current partial surface, computing, from the parameters, a current compaction degree for the current partial surface or each subsegment of the current partial surface.
problem: Accurately determining the compaction degree of a surface segment during compaction.
constraint: Ensuring parameters are correctly attributed to specific subsegments despite overlapping machine paths.
mechanism: Mapping positional data of a mobile unit to localized regions enables spatially resolved parameter measurement, allowing precise computation of compaction degree for each region.
mechanism_raw: Mapping positional data of a compacting machine to localized subsegments enables spatially resolved parameter measurement, allowing precise computation of compaction degree for each subsegment.

abstract: A riding stirrup includes a supporting structure terminating in a solid shape and a mechanical assembly pivotably mounted on the supporting structure and around the solid shape. Additionally, the riding stirrup includes a floor assembly including at least one U-shaped profile, a floor, and one or more resilient structures, wherein the floor assembly is mounted on the mechanical assembly for vertical movement relative to an axis of the solid shape.
problem: Providing a riding stirrup that balances rider comfort with stability during motion.
constraint: Maintaining stability while enabling sufficient vertical displacement for shock absorption.
mechanism: Mounting a platform on a pivotable mounting allows vertical movement relative to a base, absorbing shocks and vibrations through resilient elements.
mechanism_raw: Mounting a floor assembly on a pivotable mechanical assembly allows vertical movement relative to the stirrup's axis, absorbing shocks and vibrations through resilient structures.

abstract: A system and method for providing a stronger lanai, area or pool enclosure. The system utilizes a beam having an interior channel that provides increased thread receiving surface for receiving one or more fasteners and an interlocking joint for further strengthening the connection between a plurality of beam members that form the beam.
problem: Increasing structural strength in modular beam systems for enclosures.
constraint: Achieving structural reinforcement without excessive weight or cost.
mechanism: An internal channel in a structural member provides increased surface area for fasteners, while mechanical interlocks between members enhance connection strength through engagement.
mechanism_raw: An interior channel in the beam provides increased surface area for fasteners, while interlocking joints between beam members enhance connection strength through mechanical engagement.

abstract: A system, method and kit for making singular applique elements, combining the singular elements on a singular pattern as an aid for quickly and repeatably creating a combined element for attachment to a quilt, tablecloth, bedspread, pillow case, and the like. Two pre-printed paper sheets are provided having outlines of the applique elements printed wherein one paper sheet is cut into singular design elements and the other pre-printed sheet is of a coated nature that remains intact as a singular pattern. The singular design elements are applied to the applique fabric of which the fabric is cut to the shape of the singular element. The singular elements are then combined using the singular pattern as an assembly template ensuring a repeatable applique design. The combined applique elements can then be attached to the desired base material in a usual manner.
problem: Quickly and repeatably creating combined applique designs for textiles.
constraint: Maintaining alignment accuracy while enabling rapid assembly and detachment of elements.
mechanism: Using one template as a cutting guide and another as an intact assembly guide ensures precise alignment and repeatable combination of design elements.
mechanism_raw: Using one pre-printed sheet as a cutting template and another as an intact assembly guide ensures precise alignment and repeatable combination of applique elements.

abstract: A wear assembly for excavating equipment which includes a wear member and a base each with upper and lower stabilizing surfaces that are offset and at overlapping depths to reduce the overall depth of the assembly while maintaining high strength and a stable coupling. The nose and socket each includes a generally triangular-shaped front stabilizing end to provide a highly stable front connection between the nose and wear member for both vertical and side loading. The lock is movable between hold and release positions to accommodate replacing of the wear member when needed, and secured to the wear member for shipping and storage purposes.
problem: Creating a compact, high-strength mechanical coupling for wear components in excavating equipment that maintains stability under multidirectional loads while minimizing assembly depth.
constraint: Balancing reduced assembly depth with sufficient strength and stability under vertical and side loading conditions.
mechanism: Interlocking offset and overlapping surfaces between a replaceable component and a base structure reduce overall assembly depth while maintaining structural integrity under multidirectional loads. Geometrically shaped stabilizing ends provide load-bearing stability in multiple directions, and a releasable locking mechanism enables component replacement without compromising coupling strength during operation.
mechanism_raw: Offset and overlapping stabilizing surfaces between the wear member and base reduce overall depth while preserving structural integrity. Triangular-shaped front stabilizing ends on the nose and socket provide multidirectional load stability, and a movable lock enables replacement without compromising the coupling's strength during operation.
residual_terms: ["offset and overlapping surfaces", "stabilizing ends", "multidirectional loads", "releasable locking mechanism"]

abstract: A combination dip and cake holder and punch bowl is readily configurable between any of three configurations. A platter member has a base with a female receiver, while a first type of receptacle has an extension that is receivable within the receiver so that when the first receptacle faces upwardly, a dip holder is formed. A second receptacle also has an extension that is receivable within the first extension of the first receptacle in order to form a punch bowl. When the first receptacle rests on its rim and the platter member receives the receptacle's extension, the device acts as a cake holder with the second receptacle being used as a cover that sits on the platter member.
problem: Designing a single apparatus that can be reconfigured into multiple functional states (dip holder, cake holder, punch bowl) without requiring separate components.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and functional utility across all configurations while minimizing the number of discrete parts.
mechanism: Nested extensions and corresponding female receivers on a primary platter and secondary receptacles enable reversible interlocking through geometric compatibility. The same physical components can be reoriented and combined to form multiple distinct functional configurations, with one receptacle serving as a closure element in a specific configuration.
mechanism_raw: Nested extensions and female receivers on a platter and receptacles allow reversible interlocking. The geometric compatibility of the extensions enables three distinct configurations by reorienting and combining the same physical components, with one receptacle acting as a cover in the cake holder mode.

abstract: The present invention relates to the discovery that specific human taste receptors in the T2R taste receptor family respond to particular bitter compounds. Also, the invention relates to the discovery of specific hT2R9 alleles and their disparate activity in functional assays with the same biter ligands. The invention further relates to the use of these T2R receptors in assays for identifying ligands that modulate the activation of these taste receptors by specific bitter ligands and related compounds. These compounds may be used as additives and/or removed from foods, beverages, cosmetics and medicinals in order to modify (block) T2R-associated bitter taste. Also T2R ligands may be used as therapeutics to treat and modulate T2R associated gastrointestinal and metabolic functions as well as treat gastrointestinal and metabolic diseases such as eating disorders, food sensing, food absorption, obesity, diabetes, Crohn's disease, celiac disease, et al.
problem: Identifying and utilizing specific molecular interactions between human taste receptors (T2R family) and bitter compounds to modulate taste perception or treat metabolic/disease conditions.
constraint: Achieving specificity in ligand-receptor interactions to avoid cross-reactivity while enabling broad therapeutic or sensory applications.
mechanism: Specific molecular receptors and their allelic variants are employed in functional assays to identify ligands that selectively block or activate target biological pathways. These ligands are then applied to modify compositional characteristics or serve as therapeutic agents targeting physiological functions.
mechanism_raw: Specific T2R receptors and their alleles are used in functional assays to detect ligands that either block or activate bitter taste pathways. These ligands can then be applied to modify food/beverage composition or serve as therapeutics targeting gastrointestinal and metabolic functions.

abstract: A variable flow pump includes: a housing with inlet and outlet chambers interconnected by a main bore and a non-rotating cylinder block positioned in the main bore. The cylinder block includes: a central bore communicating with the inlet chamber; cylinder bores arrayed around the central bore; first feed passages interconnecting the inlet chamber and the cylinder bores, defining a bypass flowpath between the cylinder bores; and at least one discharge valve disposed at the second end which permits fluid flow from the cylinder bores to the discharge chamber but prevents opposite flow; Pistons are disposed in the bores. A shaft is coupled to the pistons so as to cause them to reciprocate through an axial pump stroke when the shaft is rotated. A mechanism is coupled to the cylinder block which modulates the axial position of the cylinder block within the housing, varying the size of the bypass flowpath.
problem: Providing variable fluid flow output in a pump system while maintaining operational efficiency and control over the bypass flowpath.
constraint: Maintaining precise control over the bypass flowpath size without compromising the pump's structural integrity or introducing inefficiencies during axial repositioning.
mechanism: A non-rotating cylinder block containing multiple pistons is axially positioned within a housing to modulate the size of a bypass flowpath between cylinder bores and an inlet chamber. Adjusting the block's axial position changes the effective bypass area, thereby controlling the system's displacement and output flow rate.
mechanism_raw: A non-rotating cylinder block with pistons is axially positioned within a housing to modulate the size of a bypass flowpath between cylinder bores and the inlet chamber. Adjusting the block's position changes the effective bypass area, thereby controlling the pump's displacement and flow rate.

abstract: An apparatus for cleaning and decontaminating an air distribution system includes a sources separately containing a first fluid and a second fluid, a pressurizing system for separately pressurizing the first and second fluids, a distribution subsystem for separately conveying the first and second fluids to a plurality of injectors that convert the first and second fluids into a foam-like substance before injecting the foam-like substance into the air distribution system. The apparatus includes a control system for controlling the pressure and flow rate of the first and second fluids, and a system for removing the foam-like substance from the air distribution system after the foam-like substance has cleaned and decontaminated the air distribution system. A method for cleaning and decontaminating an air distribution system is also disclosed.
problem: Cleaning and decontaminating enclosed air distribution systems without damaging internal components or leaving residues, while ensuring thorough coverage.
constraint: Balancing the foam's cleaning effectiveness with the need to avoid residue buildup and ensure compatibility with the air system's materials and geometry.
mechanism: Two separately pressurized fluids are conveyed to injection points where they are combined to form a foam-like substance before introduction into an enclosed system. A control mechanism regulates pressure and flow rates to optimize cleaning efficacy, and an extraction system removes the foam after it has performed its cleaning function.
mechanism_raw: Two separately pressurized fluids are conveyed to injectors that convert them into a foam-like substance before injection into the system. A control system regulates pressure and flow rates to optimize cleaning efficacy, and a removal system extracts the foam after it has performed its function.

abstract: There is provided a dielectric material containing no sulfur (S), and there is provided an information recording medium that affords high signal quality and excellent recording sensitivity and repeated rewrite characteristics, even though no interface layer is provided between a reflective layer and a dielectric layer. To this end, the present invention is an information recording medium that is equipped with at least a recording layer and undergoes phase change when the recording layer is irradiated with a laser beam or when current is applied, comprising an oxide-fluoride dielectric layer that includes indium (In), an element M1 (where M1 is at least one element selected from among Zr, Hf, Y, Ti, Nb, Ta, Cr, Ga, and Si), oxygen (O), an element M2 (where M2 is at least one element selected from among La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Yb, Mg, Ca, and Sr), and fluorine (F).
problem: Achieving high signal quality and recording sensitivity in phase-change information recording media without requiring a separate interface layer between the reflective layer and dielectric layer, and without using sulfur-containing materials.
constraint: The elemental composition must simultaneously optimize multiple competing properties — optical constants (refractive index, extinction coefficient), thermal conductivity, chemical stability, and mechanical integrity — while avoiding sulfur and maintaining compatibility with adjacent layers in the recording medium structure.
mechanism: Compositional balancing of multiple elements to simultaneously optimize competing material properties (e.g., optical, thermal, chemical, mechanical) through a single integrated layer that performs the functions of multiple distinct layers, eliminating the need for separate interface or functional layers.
mechanism_raw: Multi-element composition design where a carefully selected combination of indium, a transition/rare-earth element (M1), oxygen, a rare-earth/alkaline-earth element (M2), and fluorine creates a dielectric material whose optical, thermal, and chemical properties are balanced such that the material performs the functions of both the dielectric and interface layers simultaneously, eliminating the need for a separate interface layer.

abstract: An exhaust system for a motorcycle engine including a header having an upstream end adjacent a combustion chamber of the engine and having a downstream end opposite the upstream end. The exhaust system includes a catalytic converter positioned downstream of the combustion chamber and configured to improve the emissions quality of exhaust gases discharged from the combustion chamber. The exhaust system further includes a perforated section at least partially defining an exhaust passageway, the perforated section disposed adjacent the downstream end of the header. A resonator chamber is in fluid communication with the perforated section. The resonator chamber is configured to allow expansion of the exhaust gases in the exhaust passageway through the perforated section.
problem: Improving emissions quality and controlling exhaust noise/pressure pulses in a motorcycle engine exhaust system, particularly in the compact and constrained geometry of a motorcycle.
constraint: The system must balance exhaust flow efficiency (minimizing backpressure to maintain engine performance) with acoustic damping and emissions control, all within the severe space and weight constraints of a motorcycle exhaust system.
mechanism: Controlled expansion and resonance in a flow path via perforations connected to a chamber, where pressure wave interactions tune acoustic and backpressure characteristics to balance flow efficiency, noise reduction, and emissions treatment.
mechanism_raw: Using a perforated section in the exhaust flow path connected to a resonator chamber, where exhaust gases expand through the perforations into the resonator chamber. This controlled expansion creates a pressure wave interaction that tunes the acoustic resonance and backpressure characteristics of the exhaust system, improving both emissions treatment efficiency (by optimizing gas flow to the catalytic converter) and noise reduction.

abstract: A method for driving a liquid drop ejector (1) equipped with a piezoelectric actuator (7) including a piezoelectric ceramic layer (6) having a size covering a plurality of pressurizing chambers (2). An arbitrary piezoelectric deformation region (8) of the liquid drop ejector (1) is deflected in one thickness direction and the opposite direction, respectively, by applying a driving voltage waveform including a first voltage (−VL) and an equivalent second voltage (+VL) of the opposite polarity in order to vary the volume of the pressurizing chambers (2) of a corresponding liquid drop ejecting portion (4), and a liquid drop is ejected through a communicating nozzle (3). Since gradual creep deformation of the inactive region (16) of the piezoelectric ceramic layer (6) is prevented, the ink drop ejection performance is maintained at a good level over a long term.
problem: Maintaining consistent ink drop ejection performance over a long operational lifetime in piezoelectric liquid drop ejectors, despite gradual creep deformation that accumulates in the piezoelectric ceramic layer.
constraint: The driving waveform must provide sufficient net volumetric change in the pressurizing chamber for reliable droplet ejection while ensuring that the alternating stress is balanced enough to prevent creep, all using a single ceramic layer that spans multiple pressurizing chambers.
mechanism: Bidirectional actuation using alternating stress polarities to balance mechanical strain in a deformable element, preventing cumulative unidirectional deformation and maintaining performance over repeated cycles.
mechanism_raw: Applying a driving voltage waveform with alternating positive and negative polarities to deflect the piezoelectric deformation region in both thickness directions. This bidirectional actuation applies balanced mechanical stress to the piezoelectric ceramic layer, preventing the accumulation of unidirectional creep deformation in the inactive region of the ceramic, thereby maintaining ejection performance over time.

abstract: Methods for extracting molecules of fulvic acid from a humus material such as oxidized lignite are disclosed. The humus material is mixed with water to solubilize at least some of the fulvic acid molecules. A first filtration apparatus (which may be an ultrafiltration apparatus) may be used to separate at least some of the solubilized fulvic acid molecules from the humin and at least some of the humic acid molecules. A second filtration apparatus (which may be an ultrafiltration apparatus or a nanfiltration apparatus) may be used to then separate the fulvic acid molecules from most of the water and any remaining impurities. A digestion step may also be carried out where microorganisms are brought into contact with the mixture in the presence of oxygen in order to oxidize any unoxidized organic compounds in the humus material. Iron and aluminum may be precipitated and removed by the addition of a phosphate to improve the purity of the end-product.
problem: Extracting and purifying fulvic acid molecules from complex humus materials (such as oxidized lignite) where the target molecules are intermixed with humin, humic acids, water, and various impurities including metal ions.
constraint: The process must balance extraction yield (recovering as much fulvic acid as possible) with product purity (removing humin, humic acids, metals, and other impurities), while managing the complexity of the organic mixture and the cost/energy of multiple processing steps.
mechanism: Sequential staged separation using progressively finer filtration combined with auxiliary treatments (biological oxidation and chemical precipitation) to refine a target molecule from a complex mixture while balancing yield and purity.
mechanism_raw: Sequential staged separation using progressively finer filtration — first ultrafiltration to separate solubilized fulvic acid from larger humin and humic acid molecules, then a second filtration stage (ultrafiltration or nanofiltration) to separate fulvic acid from water and remaining impurities. This is augmented by an optional biological digestion step (microorganisms with oxygen) to oxidize unoxidized organics, and chemical precipitation (phosphate addition) to remove iron and aluminum ions that would otherwise contaminate the product.

abstract: A charge system for destroying chips on a circuit board is provided. The charge system has a first substrate having a number of recesses formed therein with each of the recesses having a housing disposed therein. A high density charge is disposed within the housing. A number of recesses are formed within the high density charge. A number of low density charges are disposed within each of the recesses formed within the high density charge. A second substrate is located proximate to the first substrate. The low density charge and the high density charge are structured to destroy the second substrate after ignition. A method of destroying chips is also provided.
problem: Ensuring complete and uniform destruction of chips or circuit board substrates using explosive charges, where a single high-density charge may not reliably propagate detonation through its entire volume or may leave undisturbed regions.
constraint: The charge densities and geometric arrangement must be tuned so that the low-density charges reliably initiate and propagate the high-density charges without premature or incomplete detonation, while ensuring the combined charge system delivers sufficient energy to destroy the target substrate completely.
mechanism: Hierarchical charge structure where lower-density propagation mediators within a higher-density primary charge ensure uniform detonation wave traversal through the entire volume, enabling complete and controlled energy release for substrate destruction.
mechanism_raw: Hierarchical charge structure where a high-density primary charge contains recesses filled with low-density secondary charges. Upon ignition, the low-density charges act as propagation mediators that ensure the detonation wave travels uniformly through the entire volume of the high-density charge, creating a more complete and controlled destruction pattern that reliably destroys the target substrate.

abstract: A system is disclosed for closing the toe of a knit circular product, and particularly of a stocking, without a significant interruption of the sewing operation. In one embodiment, a circular device is inserted inside the cylinder used for producing the stocking, which, appropriately programmed, catches the knit fabric from under the needles and carries it to the sewing machine.
problem: Closing the toe of a knit circular product (e.g., a stocking) without interrupting the continuous sewing operation.
constraint: The mechanism must synchronize the catching and transport actions with the knitting process to avoid halting the main operation, requiring precise timing and spatial coordination.
mechanism: A rotating element within the production mechanism autonomously captures material from a moving surface and transports it to a processing station, synchronizing capture and transfer actions with the ongoing production cycle to maintain continuous operation.
mechanism_raw: A circular device inside the production cylinder autonomously catches the knit fabric from under the needles and transports it to the sewing machine, enabling seamless integration of the toe-closing step into the ongoing production flow.

abstract: The present invention provides a method of producing xylose from lignocellulosic feedstock. The method comprises disrupting lignocellulosic feedstock; leaching the lignocellulosic feedstock by contacting the feedstock with at least one aqueous solution for a period greater than about 2 minutes to produce a leached feedstock and a leachate; removing the leachate from the leached feedstock; acidifying the leached feedstock to a pH between about 0.5 and about 3 to produce an acidified feedstock, and; reacting the acidified feedstock under conditions which disrupt fiber structure and hydrolyze a portion of hemicellulose and cellulose of the acidified feedstock, to produce a composition comprising xylose and a pretreated feedstock. The xylose may be purified from the pretreated feedstock or it may be converted to ethanol with the pretreated feedstock.
problem: Efficiently extracting xylose from lignocellulosic feedstock while preserving other components for further use (e.g., ethanol production).
constraint: The acidity and reaction conditions must balance selective hydrolysis of target components (xylose) while maintaining structural integrity of the pretreated feedstock for downstream applications.
mechanism: A multi-stage chemical treatment applies controlled acidity and hydrolytic conditions to selectively disrupt structural components of a feedstock, releasing a target compound while preserving the integrity of remaining components for subsequent processing.
mechanism_raw: A multi-step chemical process involving controlled acidification (pH 0.5–3) and hydrolysis disrupts fiber structure and selectively breaks down hemicellulose and cellulose, releasing xylose without over-degrading the remaining feedstock.

abstract: One-time programmable (OTP) nonvolatile fuse memory cells are disclosed that do not require decoding or addressing for reading their data content. Each fuse memory cell has its content latched at its output and available at all times and can be used, for example, for code storage memories, serial configuration memories, and as individual fuse bits for ID (identification), trimming, and other post-fabrication System-on-Chip (SoC) customization needs. Means are also provided for temporary data storage for design testing, etc. In alternative embodiments, using two differentially programmed fuses in a single memory cell, the selection and programming circuitry are merged.
problem: Providing nonvolatile memory data access without requiring decoding or addressing circuitry for reading stored content.
constraint: The latching mechanism must ensure nonvolatility and data stability while minimizing power consumption and circuit complexity compared to traditional addressed memory systems.
mechanism: Each memory cell incorporates a latching element that retains its programmed state at an output terminal, making stored data persistently accessible without external addressing or decoding circuitry.
mechanism_raw: Each fuse memory cell latches its programmed state at its output, making the data immediately available at all times without external addressing, enabling direct use in applications like ID trimming or SoC customization.

abstract: A heating and cooling device for temperature conditioning an air supply for an air conditioned appliance, said heating/cooling device comprising: a first air passage for channeling a first air flow; a second air passage for channeling a second air flow; an inlet fan for drawing air into said first, air passage; an exhaust fan for drawing air through said second air passage; one or a plurality of heat exchangers for exchanging heat between air in said first air passage and air in said second exhaust air passage; wherein said first air passage comprises a tubular channel having an inlet at a first end and only one outlet, said outlet being at a second end of said passage, and said inlet fan is positioned at said inlet, such that said first air flow is channeled through said inlet fan, along the whole of said air passage, encountering all of said one or plurality of heat exchangers, and out of said outlet.
problem: Efficiently exchanging heat between two air flows in a heating/cooling device while ensuring uniform exposure to all heat exchangers.
constraint: The design must balance airflow resistance and pressure drops to maintain efficient heat exchange without requiring complex ducting or multiple outlets that could bypass exchangers.
mechanism: A single-path airflow system forces a first fluid to traverse a linear sequence of heat exchange elements via a tubular conduit with one inlet and one outlet, while a second fluid flows through an independent exhaust pathway, ensuring uniform exposure to all exchange elements.
mechanism_raw: A tubular first air passage with a single inlet and outlet forces the first air flow to traverse the entire length of the passage, encountering all heat exchangers in sequence, while the second air flow is independently channeled through a separate exhaust passage.

abstract: The invention provides methods and apparatuses that utilize mass spectrometry for preparation of a surface to have catalytic activity through molecular soft-landing of mass selected ions. Mass spectrometry is used to generate combinations of atoms in a particular geometrical arrangement, and ion soft-landing selects this molecular entity or combination of entities and gently deposits the entity or combination intact onto a surface.
problem: Depositing specific molecular entities onto a surface to impart catalytic activity while preserving their structural integrity.
constraint: The soft-landing process must minimize kinetic energy transfer to prevent molecular damage while achieving precise spatial deposition for catalytic functionality.
mechanism: A mass-selective ionization system generates and filters charged molecular species, then deposits them onto a surface with controlled kinetic energy to preserve structural integrity while achieving precise spatial arrangement for functional activity.
mechanism_raw: Mass spectrometry generates and selects mass-defined ions or molecular combinations, which are then gently deposited (soft-landed) onto a surface in a controlled geometrical arrangement, ensuring intact delivery without fragmentation.

abstract: A connection device (4) for piezoelectric actuators (3) of jacquard bars for textile machines, comprising a bearing body (32), a plurality of interconnection elements (34) inserted into the bearing body (32), which can be removably connected to a corresponding plurality of interface electric contacts (9) of a plurality of piezoelectric actuators (3), at least one interconnection terminal (33) for the interconnection elements (34) with control means of a textile machine, and at least one fastening portion (35) configured and arranged so as to removably mount the bearing body (32) onto a supporting body (7) of a jacquard thread-guide bar (2).
problem: Need to establish and break electrical connections to individual piezoelectric actuators in a textile machine without disassembling the entire system or disrupting other actuators.
constraint: Must maintain reliable electrical contact for each actuator while allowing individual access and overall removability without structural modification to the host machine.
mechanism: A modular interface assembly provides independent electrical connectivity to multiple actuators through removable interconnection elements that mate with individual actuator contacts. The assembly is removably mountable as a unit onto a supporting structure, enabling individual connection/disconnection without disrupting other actuators or requiring structural modification to the host system.
mechanism_raw: A bearing body houses removable interconnection elements that mate with individual actuator interface contacts, and the entire bearing body is removably mountable onto a supporting structure via a fastening portion. This creates a modular interface where individual actuator connections can be made or broken independently, and the whole assembly can be removed or reinstalled as a unit.

abstract: An active region is provided which includes a plurality of active region columns extending in a first direction and a plurality of active region rows extending in a second direction substantially orthogonal to the first direction and having concave portions. Floating electrodes and control electrodes are provided on the active region columns. An interlayer insulating film formed as a layer below an upper wiring is provided on the active region and the control electrodes. Conductive sections that electrically connect the upper wiring and the active region are respectively provided on the concave portions on the active region rows.
problem: Need to create selective electrical connections between upper wiring and an active semiconductor region that has complex geometry, without causing unintended shorts between different electrode types.
constraint: Must achieve electrical contact only at intended locations while maintaining isolation between floating electrodes, control electrodes, and upper wiring in a densely packed semiconductor structure.
mechanism: Precisely located placement sites on a structured surface enable selective bridging of conductive pathways to specific regions of a complex-geometry active area. Isolation between different electrode types is maintained through an insulating layer, with conductive bridges positioned only at designated contact points to prevent unintended electrical coupling.
mechanism_raw: Concave portions formed in active region rows serve as precisely located placement sites for conductive sections that bridge the upper wiring to the active region. Floating and control electrodes are placed on separate columns, and an interlayer insulating film isolates the upper wiring from the electrodes except at the designated concave contact points.

abstract: The head cooling apparatus is housed in a case removably fitted within an existing hat crown of a hat, without structural modification to the hat. The case has a plurality of air vents including an intake and a trio of vents which direct air across a hat wearer's head. The fan within the case is adjacent to the intake. The non-evaporative refreezable cooling cartridge is removably fitted within the case. The switched power source within the case is in communication with the fan and a power source. The fan forces air into the intake, across the cooling cartridge and out the vents toward a wearer's head.
problem: Need to provide active cooling to a person's head using headwear without modifying the existing hat structure.
constraint: Must fit within the confined, unmodified interior of a standard hat while delivering sufficient cooled airflow to the wearer's head.
mechanism: A self-contained cooling unit is insertable into existing headwear without structural modification. The unit generates airflow through a closed-loop path that passes air across a phase-change cooling element and directs cooled air toward the wearer's head via integrated vents.
mechanism_raw: A self-contained case is removably inserted into an existing hat crown without structural modification. Inside the case, a fan forces ambient air through a non-evaporative refreezable cooling cartridge and out directed vents toward the wearer's head, creating a closed-loop airflow path that cools the cartridge and delivers cooled air to the head.

abstract: A hopper car discharge section may be wide at the top and narrow at the bottom. Outflow is controlled by closure members, at least one of which is movable. The closure members come together to a closed condition or position for retaining lading. When apart, in an open position or condition, lading may be discharged. A seal member or seal member assembly is mounted to one or both of the closure members. The closure member may have a lading discharge encouragement feature, which may be in the nature of a tine, or blade, or knife that extends upwardly through the throat of the discharge section. Movement of the door may tend to move the blade, thereby tending to dislodge lading that may be otherwise reluctant to move.
problem: Need to fully discharge lading from a hopper car, particularly material that becomes stuck or reluctant to flow under gravity alone.
constraint: Must provide a tight seal when closed to retain lading, while the same closure movement must also actively dislodge stuck material when opening, without requiring separate actuation.
mechanism: A tapered discharge passage with a movable closure member incorporates an attached dislodging element that extends into the flow path. Movement of the closure member during opening simultaneously actuates the dislodging element to physically agitate and remove material that resists gravitational flow, while the same closure member provides a seal when closed.
mechanism_raw: A discharge section tapers from wide at the top to narrow at the bottom, with movable closure members that open to allow discharge. A blade or tine attached to a closure member extends upwardly through the throat of the discharge section, so that movement of the closure member during opening also moves the blade to physically dislodge lading that is reluctant to flow.

abstract: A connector structure securely connectable in a locked state and releasable by an easy operation, comprising a supplying connection part for supplying a fluid and receiving connection part for receiving the supply of fluid. The connector structure also comprises a securing mechanism having an operating member moving according to a connecting operation between the supplying connection part to the receiving connection part, holding the connected state of the supplying part to the receiving part in a securely locked state and releasing the locked state of the supplying part to the receiving part by movement of the operating member according to the next pressing-in operation of the supplying part and an energizing mechanism energizing the supplying part in the separating direction thereof from the receiving part. When in the locked state, the pressurized fluid can be supplied from the supplying connection part to the receiving connection part.
problem: Need a fluid connector that can be securely locked under pressure but released with a simple, single-motion operation.
constraint: Must remain securely locked under pressurized fluid flow while allowing release through the same pressing-in motion that was used for connection, without requiring additional tools or complex operations.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage couples the axial motion of a connecting operation to a locking mechanism. Initial connection motion positions the linkage to maintain a locked state under pressure. A subsequent pressing-in motion reverses the linkage position to release the lock, while a biasing mechanism automatically separates the parts once unlocked.
mechanism_raw: An operating member is mechanically linked to the connecting motion between the supply and receiving parts. During initial connection, the operating member moves to a position that holds the parts in a locked state. During a subsequent pressing-in operation, the same motion causes the operating member to move again, releasing the lock. An energizing mechanism biases the supply part in the separating direction, so that once the lock is released, the parts separate automatically.

abstract: An assembly structured to facilitate the practice of various martial art techniques by an individual such as kicks, punches and other physically delivered blows associated with various forms of the martial arts. At least one elongated stanchion is operatively supported by a base, preferably having a stabilizing assembly, in a substantially vertical, upright position. The stanchion comprises a plurality of support assemblies extending outwardly therefrom and being adjustable at various heights along the length thereof. Each or a predetermined number of the support assemblies include a mounting structure secured to an outer end thereof at a predetermined orientation. Each of the mounting structures is dimensioned, disposed and configured to have a striking target, such as a Thai pad, or like structure disposed in an exposed, accessible location to facilitate the delivery, by the individual, of different types of martial art blows.
problem: Facilitating practice of diverse martial art techniques (kicks, punches) requiring variable target positioning and orientation.
constraint: Balancing adjustability of target positions with structural stability to prevent unintended movement during use.
mechanism: A modular mounting system with adjustable components on a vertical support allows repositioning of targets at varied positions and orientations, with locking mechanisms to maintain structural stability during dynamic configuration.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable support assemblies mounted on a vertical stanchion allow repositioning of striking targets at different heights and orientations, enabling dynamic configuration for varied techniques.

abstract: In a tactile sensing array and its manufacturing method, the tactile sensing array includes first and second electrodes at different layers, conductors provided for cladding intersection positions of the first and second electrodes, and a cladding layer for cladding the first and second electrodes and conductors. Each of the first and second electrodes is a spiral conducting wire wound onto an elastic wire. During manufacture, a cladding layer solution is injected into a mold; first electrodes are installed in rows and apart, and each first electrode includes conductor solution drops; second electrodes are installed at the conductor solution drops; a cladding layer solution is injected again; and vacuum, heating and demolding process are performed. The invention has the effects of high extensibility, high elasticity and low manufacturing cost and prevents damages caused by high deformation when the tactile sensing array is used and covered onto a complicated surface.
problem: Creating a tactile sensor array that maintains conductivity and structural integrity under high deformation on complex surfaces.
constraint: Achieving high elasticity and extensibility without compromising conductivity or increasing manufacturing complexity.
mechanism: A stretchable electrode structure integrates helical conductors with an elastic substrate, combined with a coating process that applies conductive material under vacuum and heat to ensure durability and conductivity under deformation.
mechanism_raw: Spiral conducting wires wound onto elastic wires provide stretchable electrodes, while a cladding process with conductor solution drops and vacuum/heating ensures durable, low-cost integration of flexible conductive paths.

abstract: An inflator includes a generant chamber that houses a quantity of gas generant. The chamber has a plurality of gas exit holes that are positioned along the length of the generant chamber. A filter is added exterior of the chamber. In fact, the filter may be positioned on the exterior of the generant chamber. Straps may encircle the inflator. The straps are attached to studs that will operate to mount the inflator. The position of the straps may be adjusted and tailored to apportion the amount of inflation gas that is directed into each chamber of a multi-chambered or two-chambered airbag.
problem: Controlling the distribution of inflation gas into multiple chambers of an airbag to achieve tailored inflation profiles.
constraint: Balancing gas distribution across chambers while maintaining structural integrity and mounting flexibility.
mechanism: A variable flow control system uses adjustable conduits to direct gas into specific chambers by modulating exit flow through strategically positioned openings, enabling selective pressurization while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable straps encircling the inflator direct gas flow into specific chambers by modulating the amount of gas exiting through strategically positioned holes, enabling selective chamber pressurization.

abstract: According to an aspect of the present invention, there is provided a centrifuge including: a rotor rotated by a driver; a chamber housing the rotor therein; a cover openable and closable with respect to the chamber; and a lock mechanism that locks the cover in a closed state, wherein the lock mechanism includes: a motor; a first hook rotated by the motor; and a second hook connected to the first hook through a connecting member, wherein the cover includes a securing portion on which the first hook and the second hook are respectively secured when the cover is locked, and wherein, during a locking operation of the cover, primary the first hook is engaged with the securing portion and pulls the cover toward the chamber, and then the second hook is engaged with the securing portion.
problem: Securely locking a centrifuge cover during operation to prevent accidental opening under rotational forces.
constraint: Ensuring sequential engagement of hooks to achieve both initial sealing and final locking without misalignment.
mechanism: A dual-stage latching system sequentially engages a cover: the first stage applies pressure to seal the interface, and the second stage locks the position, ensuring alignment and stability under rotational forces.
mechanism_raw: A two-stage hook system sequentially engages the cover: the first hook pulls the cover toward the chamber for tight sealing, then the second hook locks it in place, ensuring alignment and stability.

abstract: A polyline tree representation of a coronary artery tree imaged in a volume data set is obtained, and its topology is extracted to give a topological representation indicating the relative positions of vessels in the tree. The topological representation is compared with a set of topological rules to find possible anatomical classifications for each vessel, and a set of candidate labeled polyline trees is generated by labeling the polyline tree with labels showing each combination of possible anatomical classifications. Each candidate labeled tree is filtered according to a set of geometric rules pertaining to spatial characteristics of vessels in arterial trees, and any labeled tree not satisfying the geometric rules is rejected A figure of merit is calculated for each remaining candidate by comparing features of the vessels measured from the polyline tree and from the volume data set with features of correctly classified vessels in other data sets to determine the probable correctness of the labeling of each candidate, and the candidate with the best figure of merit is selected as showing the proper classification of the vessels.
problem: Accurately classifying vessels in a coronary artery tree from medical imaging data despite topological and geometric ambiguities.
constraint: Balancing topological and geometric rule compliance to avoid over-filtering valid candidates while ensuring anatomical accuracy.
mechanism: A hierarchical filtering process applies topological and geometric rules to generate candidate classifications, then selects the best candidate using a figure of merit that compares features across datasets to resolve ambiguities.
mechanism_raw: A multi-stage filtering process generates candidate labeled trees using topological rules, then applies geometric rules to reject invalid candidates, and selects the best classification via a figure of merit comparing features across datasets.

abstract: A skirt assembly kit comprising a skirt panel adapted to be disposed on a trailer to route air about the road trailer is provided, a plurality of upper supports adapted to secure the skirt panel to the road trailer and a plurality of struts adapted to secure the skirt panel to the road trailer. A method of installing an aerodynamic skirt on a trailer is also provided, the method comprising providing a skirt panel, installing the skirt panel on the trailer; and performing an opening in the skirt panel. An aerodynamic skirt kit adapted to mounted to a trailer is equally provided, the aerodynamic skirt kit comprising a skirt panel adapted to define an opening therein adapted to give access through the skirt panel, and an opening closing element adapted to close the opening.
problem: Balancing aerodynamic efficiency of a trailer skirt with the need for periodic access to components behind the skirt.
constraint: The opening must be large enough for functional access but small enough to avoid disrupting airflow when closed, requiring a trade-off between accessibility and aerodynamic integrity.
mechanism: A panel with a selectively closable aperture enables temporary access to a protected region while maintaining environmental isolation during normal operation. The aperture is sealed by a dedicated closure element, preserving the panel's functional integrity when closed. The aperture size is constrained to balance accessibility requirements against performance degradation during closure.
mechanism_raw: A skirt panel with a selectively closable opening allows temporary access while maintaining aerodynamic performance when closed. The opening is sealed by a dedicated closing element, preserving the skirt's airflow management function during normal operation.

abstract: A transport apparatus for transporting articles hanging on loops or the like, in particular sausage-shaped packs, comprising a shaft which has a first axial portion on which a screw is disposed. A drive moment is applied by way of the outside periphery of the screw and the shaft is supported by way of the outside periphery of the screw.
problem: Transmitting rotational drive torque to a shaft while simultaneously providing structural support for the shaft using minimal components.
constraint: The screw must be designed to withstand both torsional loads from the drive and radial/axial loads from the shaft support without compromising either function.
mechanism: A single rotating element coaxially mounted on a shaft transmits rotational drive torque through its outer periphery while simultaneously providing structural support for the shaft. The element is designed to withstand multiple load types (torsional, radial, axial) without requiring separate drive or support components, integrating mechanical functions into a unified structure.
mechanism_raw: A screw is coaxially mounted on the shaft, with both the drive torque and shaft support applied via the screw's outer periphery. This eliminates the need for separate bearings or drive couplings by integrating drive and support functions into a single rotating element.

abstract: A liquid hand cleansing composition which has the ability to remove stubborn soils such as ink, grease, paint and the like. The composition is also able to hold water insoluble particles in suspension without separation or sedimentation because of cooperation between a special suspension system and a surfactant system. Additionally, the composition remains homogenous and viscosity stabilized even in the presence of relatively large quantities of solvent such as d-limonene.
problem: Maintaining homogeneous suspension of water-insoluble particles in a solvent-rich liquid composition without sedimentation or viscosity instability.
constraint: The suspension and surfactant systems must remain compatible across varying solvent concentrations and environmental conditions to prevent phase separation or viscosity drift.
mechanism: A colloidal stabilization system combines particulate modifiers and surfactants to form a dynamic network that counteracts destabilizing forces from solvent interactions. The system maintains particle suspension and viscosity consistency by creating reversible physical interactions that adapt to compositional and environmental variations.
mechanism_raw: A synergistic interaction between a specialized suspension system (e.g., particulate modifiers or rheology agents) and a surfactant system creates a stable colloidal network that counteracts solvent-induced destabilization, keeping particles suspended and viscosity consistent.

abstract: A portable autonomous terminal guidance system can be located in an aircraft landing zone. The terminal guidance system generates a signal indicative of the position, the terrain, and the meteorological conditions where the guidance system is located. A receiving aircraft may process the signal produced by the terminal guidance system to generate a self-contained GPS obstacle-avoidance approach path for the aircraft to the landing zone.
problem: Enabling autonomous aircraft navigation in remote or infrastructure-limited landing zones without relying on fixed ground-based guidance systems.
constraint: The terminal must be portable and self-sufficient while providing sufficient signal fidelity and coverage to support safe autonomous landing in diverse environmental conditions.
mechanism: A portable signal-generating terminal provides localized positional, terrain, and environmental data to enable autonomous navigation without fixed infrastructure. The terminal's signals are processed by the vehicle to construct a self-contained guidance path, decoupling navigation capability from centralized systems through distributed signal encoding.
mechanism_raw: A portable terminal unit generates localized signals encoding position, terrain, and meteorological data. The aircraft processes these signals to construct a self-contained GPS obstacle-avoidance approach path, decoupling navigation from centralized infrastructure.

abstract: An electrically driven entryway activation system for opening and closing two spaced swinging doors hung on spaced rotating parallel door posts comprises a base plate extending between the door posts. Levers attached to each door post rotate in a plane parallel to the base plate. A low profile actuation system spaced between the levers comprises a center post, a sector gear journaled on the center post for rotation parallel to the base plate, and a low profile gearmotor mounted between the base plate and the sector gear. A low profile emergency manual mechanism is provided for unclutching the output pinion gear of the gearmotor.
problem: Actuating two spaced swinging doors in a synchronized manner within a constrained spatial envelope while enabling emergency manual override.
constraint: The actuation system must maintain synchronization between doors despite spatial constraints, and the emergency override must function reliably without compromising the low-profile design.
mechanism: A compact drive system uses a central rotating element mechanically linked to multiple levers to synchronize movement of spatially separated barriers. An emergency disengagement mechanism allows manual operation by decoupling the drive input from the barrier linkage, preserving synchronization during normal operation while enabling override under fault conditions.
mechanism_raw: A low-profile gearmotor drives a sector gear journaled on a central post, which mechanically links to levers on each door post. The compact arrangement of gears and levers ensures synchronized door movement, while an emergency clutch mechanism allows manual operation by disengaging the gearmotor's output.

abstract: This invention comprises a method for generating functional neural networks using neural progenitor cells on microelectrode arrays (MEAs). The method involves dissociating neural progenitor cells from an embryo, propagating the neural progenitor cells, passaging the neural progenitor cells and seeding the neural progenitor cells on MEAs to produce a functional neural network. The neural progenitor cells may be continuously passaged to propagate an endless supply of neural progenitor cells. The resultant passaged progenitor cell derived neural network MEA may be used to detect and/or quantify various biological or chemical toxins.
problem: Generating a functional neural network for toxin detection requires a sustainable supply of viable neural progenitor cells.
constraint: Balancing cell viability and differentiation during repeated passaging to preserve network functionality without genetic drift or loss of responsiveness.
mechanism: A biological culture maintenance process repeatedly transfers proliferating cells through a controlled environment to preserve their functional integration and prevent genetic drift, enabling scalable and stable network formation over time.
mechanism_raw: Continuous passaging of neural progenitor cells maintains their proliferative capacity and functional integration on microelectrode arrays, enabling long-term network stability and scalability.

abstract: A memorial urn assembly for comingling remains from two containers includes a pair of containers such that each of the containers includes a perimeter wall defining an interior. The perimeter wall has an interior surface and an exterior surface. The perimeter wall of one of the containers has a mating area configured to engage with a mating area of another one of the containers. The containers are couplable together so that the interior of one of the assemblies is in fluid communication with the interior of another one of the assemblies.
problem: Combining remains from two separate containers into a single unified space while maintaining containment and accessibility.
constraint: Ensuring a secure seal at the mating interface to prevent spillage while allowing repeated coupling and decoupling.
mechanism: Reversible mechanical coupling between two containers via complementary mating interfaces creates a sealed fluid pathway, allowing repeated connection and disconnection without permanent adhesion or leakage.
mechanism_raw: Mating areas on container perimeter walls enable reversible mechanical coupling, creating fluid communication between interiors without permanent adhesion or leakage.

abstract: A method of making absorbent cellulosic sheet with increased wet/dry CD tensile ratio includes treating the fiber at high consistency with debonder in a pulper, for example. The process enables the use of large amounts of debonder in a wet-press process in order to achieve wet/dry CD tensile ratios of greater than 30%.
problem: Achieving high wet/dry CD tensile ratios in absorbent cellulosic sheets without compromising structural integrity during wet-pressing.
constraint: Optimizing debonder concentration and consistency to avoid over-treatment that weakens the sheet or disrupts the wet-press process.
