When the light-emitting diode cluster lamp is connected to a power source, the control circuit module selectively makes the light-emitting diode modules emit light. The heat generated during the light emission of each of the light-emitting diode modules is conducted and dissipated by the corresponding heat-conducting/dissipating module of each of the light-emitting diode modules.
reason: The patent describes a standard LED lamp with modular heat dissipation and control circuits. While heat management is addressed, the mechanism is specific to LED packaging and lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond component-level design.

abstract: Mobile or portable apparatus for preparing beverages comprising a module for delivering a beverage by supplying a pressurized liquid, a liquid feed tank of sufficient capacity for supplying the module with several volumes of liquid for supplying more than one beverage, gas pressurizing means suitable for supplying the module with pressurized liquid, a liquid feed chamber, of which the capacity is several times smaller than the capacity of the tank, said chamber being arranged, in a module feeding configuration, to communicate with the gas pressurizing means in order to pressurize the liquid in the chamber and to inject pressurized liquid into the module and thereby permit the delivery of the liquid through the module.
problem: Delivering pressurized liquid for beverage preparation while maintaining a compact, mobile system with sufficient liquid supply for multiple servings.
constraint: The chamber capacity must be several times smaller than the tank to balance pressurization efficiency and liquid supply volume.
mechanism: A dual-volume system where a primary liquid reservoir transfers fluid to a secondary pressurized chamber. The secondary chamber is pressurized by a compressible medium and delivers fluid to an output module via controlled injection, enabling pressurized dispensing without pressurizing the entire primary reservoir.
mechanism_raw: A two-chamber system where a large liquid feed tank supplies a smaller pressurized chamber. The chamber is pressurized by gas means and injects liquid into the delivery module, enabling controlled pressurized delivery without requiring the entire tank to be pressurized.

abstract: An automatic mask peeling apparatus 10 includes: a brushing apparatus 30 for removing solidified plugging slurry attached to the mask 24; an air injection apparatus 36 for injecting, after the removal of the solidified plugging slurry, air from the opposite end face-side of the one end face to raise a folded surplus part of the mask from the one end face; a mask peeling apparatus 50 for holding the part raised by the air injection apparatus 36 to peel the mask 24; and a carrying apparatus 55 for carrying a masked plugging honeycomb structure 200 from the brushing apparatus 30 to the mask peeling apparatus 50. This apparatus can be used to peel a mask 24 which has been used for plugging only the predetermined cells of a masked plugging honeycomb structure 200; the mask 24 having an area larger than the area of the end face of the structure.
problem: Separating a mask from a honeycomb structure without damaging the structure or causing uncontrolled movement of the mask's surplus parts.
constraint: The air injection must target the opposite end face to raise the surplus part without causing uncontrolled displacement of the mask.
mechanism: A staged separation process: first removing adhered residue via mechanical brushing, then applying directed fluid flow to lift a folded excess portion from a target surface, followed by mechanical peeling of the lifted section. The fluid flow creates controlled separation forces before physical removal.
mechanism_raw: A sequential process: first removing residue via brushing, then using air injection to lift the mask's folded surplus part from the end face, and finally peeling the lifted portion. The air injection creates a controlled separation before mechanical peeling.

abstract: An extra-large vibrating screen with duplex statically indeterminate mesh beam excitation body and plate type combined bearing beam comprises plate type flat and rigid statically indeterminate combined bearing beam (12) arranged in a screen box (1), a plurality of Y-shaped statically indeterminate combined reinforcing beams (5) arranged on the side plates (3) of the screen box alternately, duplex statically indeterminate supporting plates (22) linking a plurality of mesh beams (21) to the statically indeterminate connecting plate (4) and the side plate (3) so as to form a container made of a beam system, the vibration exciters (10) in the statically indeterminate mesh beam unit comprising eight sets of vibration exciters, which are aligned in pair horizontally and linked together through universal couplings (9), and connected to the duplex statically indeterminate mesh beam excitation body (11) to form a highly rigid integral vibrating assembly. The vibrating screen is simple and reliable in structure, can vibrate smoothly, and therefore can be widely used in coal, metallurgical, chemical, and environmental protection industries.
problem: Creating a large, rigid vibrating screen assembly that can vibrate smoothly under high loads without structural failure.
constraint: The beam and plate arrangement must balance rigidity (to prevent deformation) with flexibility (to allow vibration transmission).
mechanism: A multi-element structural framework using interconnected beam and plate assemblies with redundant load paths. The statically indeterminate connections distribute dynamic forces across multiple reinforcing elements while maintaining rigidity through geometric interdependence.
mechanism_raw: Using a duplex statically indeterminate beam and plate system to form a rigid container-like beam structure. Multiple reinforcing beams and supporting plates distribute vibration forces while maintaining structural integrity through statically indeterminate connections.
residual_terms: ["statically indeterminate connections", "beam and plate assemblies", "redundant load paths"]

abstract: In a method for detaching a charge (5) which is stuck to the inner wall of a grinding pipe (1), the grinding pipe (1) is rotated in a targeted manner such that the charge (5) that is stuck is removed from the inner wall of the grinding pipe (1) as a result of multiple modification of the rotational speed of the grinding pipe (1) and, optionally, as a result of abrupt braking of the grinding pipe (1). Generally speaking, the material-dependent maximum angle of rotation F of the grinding pipe is not exceeded in order to avoid the charge that is stuck from falling in an uncontrolled manner. The invention supercedes labor-intensive and protracted methods for detaching such charges (5) since the tasks can be carried out by the same motor of the drive device (2) which is used to drive the grinding pipe (1) during the grinding process.
problem: Detaching material stuck to the inner wall of a rotating grinding pipe without causing uncontrolled discharge of the material.
constraint: The rotational speed and braking must not exceed the material-specific maximum angle of rotation to prevent uncontrolled material fallout.
mechanism: Dynamic inertial dislodgement through variable rotational velocity and abrupt deceleration of a cylindrical surface. The speed modulation and braking are constrained by material-dependent angular thresholds to generate controlled inertial forces that detach adhered material without uncontrolled release.
mechanism_raw: Controlled rotational speed modulation and abrupt braking of the grinding pipe to generate inertial forces that dislodge the stuck material. The speed changes and braking are timed to avoid exceeding the material-dependent maximum rotation angle, ensuring safe detachment.

abstract: A method of manufacturing a composite fastener material, the composite fastener material, and products derived from the composite fastener material. The method includes providing two longitudinally continuous sheets of material, positioning the two sheets to form a longitudinal, continuous interface between the two sheets, joining the two sheets by introducing one or more molten plastic resins in at least one lane, one lane of the resin extending across the interface under conditions that cause the resin to bond to the two sheets, molding an array of stems from at least one lane of the resin, the stems extending from an exposed surface of the composite material, and forming engageable heads on the stems to form fastener elements, wherein the two sheets differ from one another by one of material composition, thickness, texture, stretchability, breathability, and compressability.
problem: Creating a composite fastener material with spatially varying functional properties (e.g., stiffness, breathability) while maintaining structural integrity and fastening capability.
constraint: Balancing the material differences between the two sheets to ensure the resin bonds both effectively without delamination, while preserving the intended functional gradients for the fastener elements.
mechanism: Joining two regions with differing material properties via an intermediate bonding agent that flows across their interface and solidifies to form discrete functional elements. The differential properties of the regions enable localized functionality (e.g., one region being compliant while the other is rigid), while the bonding agent bridges and unifies them into a cohesive structure with spatially varying characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Joining two sheets with differing material properties via a molten resin that bonds across their interface, then molding stems and heads from the resin to form fastening elements. The differential properties of the sheets enable localized functionality (e.g., one sheet being stretchable while the other is rigid), while the resin bridges and unifies them into a cohesive fastener structure.
residual_terms: ["bonding agent", "interface", "functional elements", "differential properties", "localized functionality", "spatially varying characteristics"]

abstract: A wind turbine tower, includes a first substantially tubular wall section having a tapered edge; a second substantially tubular wall section, arranged substantially coplanar with the first wall section, having a flared edge for seating against the tapered edge of the first wall section; and at least one fastener for securing the tapered edge of the first wall section to the flared edge of the second wall section. The at least one fastener includes a bolt extending through the tapered edge and the flared edge, and the bolt is arranged substantially perpendicular to a longitudinal axis of the first and second wall sections.
problem: Joining tapered and flared tubular sections of a wind turbine tower in a way that maintains structural alignment and load-bearing capacity under dynamic loads.
constraint: Ensuring the bolt's perpendicular orientation and the tapered-flared geometry maintain structural continuity and prevent stress concentration at the joint under rotational and vibrational forces.
mechanism: Using a complementary tapered-flared interface between two tubular sections, secured by a fastener arranged perpendicular to the longitudinal axis. The tapered-flared geometry ensures precise alignment and load distribution across the joint, while the perpendicular fastener provides a direct clamping force without requiring angular fastening.
mechanism_raw: Using a tapered edge on one section and a complementary flared edge on another, secured by a bolt arranged perpendicular to the tower axis. The tapered-flared interface ensures precise alignment and load distribution, while the perpendicular bolt provides a direct clamping force across the joint without requiring complex angular fastening.
residual_terms: ["tapered-flared interface", "tubular sections", "perpendicular fastener", "longitudinal axis", "clamping force", "load distribution"]

abstract: A ultrasonic probe has a plurality of piezoelectric transducers arranged in the array direction. Each piezoelectric transducer has a piezoelectric element which vibrates in the thickness direction. A signal electrode is formed on the lower surface of the piezoelectric element. An earth electrode is formed on the upper surface of the piezoelectric element. Inside the piezoelectric element, a plurality of non-piezoelectric elements are arranged along the lens direction. Each non-piezoelectric element does not come in contact with the signal electrode and the earth electrode.
problem: Controlling the vibration characteristics of a piezoelectric ultrasonic transducer array to improve signal precision and reduce unwanted mechanical interference.
constraint: Positioning the non-piezoelectric elements to avoid electrical contact with the electrodes while maintaining their mechanical influence on the piezoelectric vibration modes.
mechanism: Embedding non-active elements within an active vibratory material along a directional axis, isolating them from electrical contacts. These non-active elements act as mechanical dampers or acoustic barriers, shaping the vibration pattern of the active material to focus or direct energy waves more effectively.
mechanism_raw: Embedding non-piezoelectric elements within the piezoelectric material along the lens direction, isolating them from the signal and earth electrodes. These non-piezoelectric elements act as mechanical dampers or acoustic barriers, shaping the vibration pattern of the piezoelectric elements to focus or direct ultrasonic waves more effectively.
residual_terms: ["non-active elements", "active vibratory material", "directional axis", "electrical contacts", "mechanical dampers", "acoustic barriers", "vibration pattern", "energy waves"]

abstract: An aircraft is equipped with a spinnion coupling an inboard wing to a tilting nacelle. The spinnion is advantageously configured to extend across the nacelle from an inboard junction to an outboard junction, and terminates inside the inboard wing. This provides an efficient lightweight structure to support a nacelle and facilitate tilting of the nacelle. The spinnion, which can be configured to be at least partially disposed within the inboard wing, is advantageously concentric with the tilting axis in order to facilitate tilting of a nacelle. A cross-wing driveshaft can be included, disposed at least partly within the inboard wing, and can advantageously be configured to terminate inside the spinnion at a junction with a miter gearbox. The miter gearbox can be disposed at least partly within the spinnion but more preferably lies entirely within the spinnion, and functions to transfer power from an input shaft to the cross-wing driveshaft.
problem: Supporting a tilting aircraft nacelle with a lightweight, structurally efficient mechanism that also enables power transmission to a rotating component.
constraint: Maintaining the spinnion's structural integrity and concentric alignment with the tilting axis while integrating the gearbox and driveshaft within its interior to minimize weight and aerodynamic drag.
mechanism: Using a structural element that extends across a tilting component and is concentric with the tilting axis, terminating within a supporting structure. A power transmission shaft within the supporting structure connects to a gearbox housed entirely within the structural element, transferring power from the tilting component to the shaft while allowing the component to tilt. The concentric alignment ensures smooth rotation and load distribution.
mechanism_raw: Using a spinnion that extends across the nacelle and is concentric with the tilting axis, terminating inside the wing. A cross-wing driveshaft within the wing connects to a miter gearbox housed entirely within the spinnion, transferring power from the nacelle to the driveshaft while allowing the nacelle to tilt. The concentric alignment ensures smooth rotation and load distribution.
residual_terms: ["structural element", "tilting component", "tilting axis", "supporting structure", "power transmission shaft", "gearbox", "concentric alignment", "load distribution"]

abstract: Disclosed is a decorative material in which a metal layer (e.g., a radio-wave-transmitting metal layer) on a non-metallic-lustrous part can be removed readily and sufficiently even when the metal layer is formed partially by a process involving an etching treatment, and can decorate a molded article with a desired pattern readily and satisfactorily. Also disclosed is a method for producing the decorative material. Further disclosed is a molded article produced by using the decorative material. Specifically disclosed is a decorative material (1) which mainly comprises: a support (2) having a first main surface (S1) and a second main surface (S2) both of which are opposed to each other; a metal oxide layer (12) which is arranged on the first main surface of the support (2) and comprises aluminum oxide; a radio-wave-transmitting metal layer (14) which is arranged on the metal oxide layer (12) and contains at least one member selected from the group consisting of Sn and In as a constituent component; a mask layer (16) which is arranged on the radio-wave-transmitting metal layer (14) and comprises a synthetic resin; and an adhesive layer (20) which is arranged on the mask layer (16) and comprises a synthetic resin. In the decorative material (1), the mask layer (16), the radio-wave-transmitting metal layer (14) and the metal oxide layer (12) are so laminated that all of these layers have almost the same pattern when observed in an almost normal direction of the main surface of the support (2).
problem: Enabling selective removal of a radio-wave-transmitting metal layer from a decorative material after partial etching, while preserving pattern alignment and substrate integrity.
constraint: Ensuring the mask layer's material and thickness are compatible with the etching process to prevent over-removal or under-removal of the metal layer, while maintaining precise pattern alignment across all laminated layers.
mechanism: Laminating a protective barrier layer over a removable layer, which acts as a shield during a material removal process. The protective barrier layer, removable layer, and underlying substrate are aligned to share the same pattern. After processing, the protective barrier allows targeted removal of the removable layer without damaging adjacent regions, as the aligned layers ensure the process respects the desired pattern.
mechanism_raw: Laminating a mask layer (synthetic resin) over the metal layer, which acts as a protective barrier during etching. The mask layer, metal layer, and underlying metal oxide layer are aligned to share the same pattern. After etching, the mask layer allows targeted removal of the metal layer without damaging adjacent regions, as the aligned layers ensure the etching process respects the desired decorative pattern.
residual_terms: ["protective barrier layer", "removable layer", "material removal process", "underlying substrate", "aligned layers", "targeted removal", "desired pattern"]

abstract: A corrective method is described for processing results of transcriptome experiments obtained by differential analysis includes the following steps: obtaining the results of the level of expression of genes under a reference condition, and calculating the mean level of expression of each of such genes; obtaining the results of the level of expression of such genes under a treatment condition, and calculating the mean level of expression for each of such genes; calculating the modulation coefficient for the level of expression for each of such genes; calculating a p-value associated with each modulation coefficient; and calculating isobar curves of p-value as a function of the mean level of expression of each of such genes under the reference condition; calculating and associating a median modulation coefficient on the isobar curve of each p-value observed. The processing of results of experiments carried out on DNA chips is also described.
problem: Correcting or normalizing transcriptome data from differential gene expression experiments to account for baseline variations in expression levels.
constraint: Balancing statistical accuracy of normalization with computational efficiency when processing large-scale gene expression datasets.
mechanism: Using a reference condition's statistical relationships between significance metrics and average measurement levels to adjust observed values to a normalized baseline, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
mechanism_raw: Using isobar curves of p-values as a function of mean expression levels under a reference condition to associate median modulation coefficients, thereby adjusting observed values to a normalized baseline.

abstract: A heat-curable resin composition that yields a cured product having excellent heat resistance and light resistance, and a premolded package molded using the composition. The heat-curable resin composition comprises components (A) to (E) listed below: (A) an isocyanuric acid derivative containing at least one epoxy group within each molecule, in an amount of 100 parts by mass, (B) a silicone resin containing at least one epoxy group within each molecule, in an amount of 10 to 1,000 parts by mass, (C) an acid anhydride curing agent, in an amount such that the ratio of [total epoxy group equivalents within component (A) and component (B)/carboxyl group equivalents within component (C)] is within a range from 0.6 to 2.2, (D) a curing accelerator, in an amount within a range from 0.05 to 5 parts by mass per 100 parts by mass of the combined mass of components (A), (B) and (C), and (E) an inorganic filler, in an amount of 200 to 1,000 parts by mass per 100 parts by mass of the combined mass of components (A), (B) and (C).
reason: The mechanism is tightly bound to specific chemical components (isocyanuric acid derivatives, silicone resins, acid anhydrides) and their precise ratios, which are not generalizable beyond the chemistry of heat-curable resins. The problem-solving approach is material-specific rather than a transferable causal principle.

abstract: An FeO layer including fine crystal grains having random orientation is formed as inner layer scale on the surface of the steel wire rod containing C: 0.05-1.2 mass % (hereinafter referred to as “%”), Si: 0.01-0.50%, Mn: 0.1-1.5%, P: 0.02% or below, S: 0.02% or below, N: 0.005% or below, an Fe2SiO4 layer with the thickness: 0.01-1.0 μm is formed in the boundary face between the FeO layer of the inner layer scale and steel, and the thickness of the inner layer scale is 1-40% of the total scale thickness. In another aspect, the maximum grain size of the crystal grain of the inner layer scale is 5.0 μm or below and the average grain size is 2.0 μm or below.
problem: Improving the mechanical or thermal properties of steel wire rod by controlling the microstructure of its surface scale layer.
constraint: Maintaining a balance between the thickness of the Fe2SiO4 interlayer (0.01–1.0 μm) and the grain size of the inner layer scale (≤5.0 μm max, ≤2.0 μm average) to avoid brittleness while achieving desired properties.
mechanism: Creating a layered microstructure with controlled grain size and interlayer thickness to stabilize material properties, where a thin intermediate layer and fine-grained inner layer work together to enhance performance while avoiding brittleness.
mechanism_raw: Forming a controlled inner layer scale with fine crystal grains of random orientation and a thin Fe2SiO4 interlayer, which stabilizes the microstructure and enhances material performance through grain boundary engineering.

abstract: A food cutting and manipulating apparatus includes having an aperture extending therethrough. A gear housing is mounted on the table and includes first and second driving axles. A plurality of pairs of food manipulating members is provided. Each of the manipulating members includes a shaft, releasably engageable with the first and second driving axles, attached to an elongated base. The plurality of pairs of food manipulating members includes a plurality of pairs of cutting members. Each of the cutting members includes at least one cutting plate that is attached to the base. The at least one cutting plate extends over the aperture when the shaft is attached to the one of the first and second driving axles. Food is positionable between the food manipulating members and the motor turned on so that the food manipulating members engage the food as the food moves downwardly through the aperture.
problem: Efficiently cutting and manipulating food items using a single apparatus without manual tool changes or complex reconfiguration.
constraint: Ensuring the releasable engagement mechanism maintains precise alignment and torque transmission between the driving axles and the manipulating members during operation.
mechanism: Employing a modular tool system with interchangeable components that automatically engage and disengage from a shared actuation mechanism as an item moves through an aperture, maintaining alignment and torque transmission during operation.
mechanism_raw: Using a modular system where multiple pairs of manipulating members (including cutting plates) are releasably engaged with a common driving axle system, allowing automatic engagement and disengagement of tools as the food moves through an aperture.

abstract: A device for securing a rear seat within a cab of a vehicle, comprising a crossmember configured for attachment to a floor pan of the vehicle, the crossmember cooperating with the floor pan to provide a cavity for storing items within the cab. When the crossmember is attached to the floor pan and the rear seat is attached to the crossmember, the crossmember is contained within the space between the seat and the floor pan without extending into a passenger leg room area.
problem: Securing a rear seat within a vehicle cab while simultaneously providing storage space without encroaching on passenger leg room.
constraint: Optimizing the spatial arrangement of the crossmember and floor pan to maximize storage volume while maintaining structural integrity and passenger comfort.
mechanism: Integrating a structural element into a seat attachment framework that cooperates with a base surface to form a storage cavity, positioned entirely within the gap between the seat and base to avoid interfering with passenger space while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a crossmember into the seat attachment structure that cooperates with the floor pan to form a storage cavity, with the crossmember positioned entirely within the space between the seat and floor pan to avoid interfering with passenger space.

abstract: In accordance with the present invention, there is provided a method for producing an enhanced fertilizer, comprising the step of mixing a granular fertilizer with a ferment comprising active bacteria in a fermentation medium, to obtain an enhanced fertilizer. The ferment is used at a rate of at most 3 liters of ferment per ton of fertilizer. In accordance with the present invention, there is also provided an enhanced fertilizer comprising a fertilizer and bacteria chosen for their specific properties on crops or vegetation.
problem: Enhancing fertilizer effectiveness by introducing beneficial microorganisms in a controlled manner without overwhelming the granular structure or nutrient balance.
constraint: The ferment-to-fertilizer ratio must be capped to avoid excess moisture, structural degradation, or unintended chemical interactions that could reduce efficacy or storage stability.
mechanism: Introduce active agents into a granular medium at a precisely limited rate to ensure uniform distribution while preserving the medium's structural and chemical integrity.
mechanism_raw: Mixing a granular fertilizer with a ferment containing active bacteria at a precisely limited rate (≤3 liters per ton) to ensure uniform distribution of beneficial microbes while preserving the physical and chemical integrity of the base fertilizer.

abstract: The invention relates to a glass-metal connection, in particular for a vacuum-tube solar collector, comprising a metallic connecting part (1), which connects a heat recovery tube (3) and a enclosing tube (2) of glass in a vacuum-tight manner, one end (5) of the enclosing tube (2) being inwardly deformed in a flange-like manner in such a way that it encloses an outer edge portion (7) of the metallic connecting part (1) in a vacuum-tight manner on both sides by fusing. This edge portion (7) is expediently formed in a rotationally symmetrical manner and/or the enclosing tube (2) is produced from a soda-lime glass. The connecting part (1) is connected in a vacuum-tight manner to one or more heat recovery tubes (3). The connecting part (1) and the glass of the enclosing tube (2) have approximately the same coefficient of expansion.
problem: Creating a vacuum-tight seal between a metallic component and a glass tube in environments with significant thermal cycling, such as vacuum-tube solar collectors.
constraint: The materials must have approximately equal coefficients of thermal expansion to avoid cracking or delamination during temperature changes, and the deformation geometry must enable vacuum-tight fusion without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Mechanically deform one component to enclose another, then fuse them together using materials with matched thermal expansion coefficients to prevent stress-induced failure during temperature changes.
mechanism_raw: Inwardly deforming one end of the glass tube into a flange-like shape to mechanically enclose an outer edge of the metallic part, then fusing both materials together while ensuring their coefficients of thermal expansion are closely matched to prevent stress-induced failure.

abstract: The identification of compounds, strigolactones, having the ability to stimulate the growth and/or development of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AM fungi). Such compounds are, for example, the natural strigolactones strigol, alectrol, sorgolactone, orobanchol, or their synthetic analogs GR7, GR24, Nijmegen-1, demethylsorgolactone. New ways of developing an agriculture that is more respectful of the environment, and permits the implementation, on a small or large scale, of advanced mycorrhization techniques aimed at optimizing the production of fungic inoculum, the use of AM fungi in soils or cultivation substrates, and intensifying the symbiotic interaction between these microorganisms and cultivated plants.
problem: Stimulating the growth and symbiotic activity of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AM fungi) to enhance plant-fungi interactions in agricultural systems.
constraint: The compounds must be chemically compatible with soil conditions and plant physiology to avoid phytotoxicity or degradation before reaching target fungi, while maintaining specificity to avoid off-target ecological effects.
mechanism: Apply specific biochemical signaling compounds to trigger a target organism's response, enhancing a symbiotic relationship through targeted activation.
mechanism_raw: Applying specific strigolactone compounds (natural or synthetic analogs) that act as biochemical signals to trigger AM fungi germination and colonization, thereby intensifying the symbiotic relationship and improving inoculum production.

abstract: Devices and methods of preventing data transfer between an RFID reader and an RFID device to be protected, are provided. An example of an embodiment of an RFID signal capture device includes a container, a signal capture circuit configured to substantially disrupt the signal provided by the RFID reader when the RFID signal capture device is positioned to protect the RFID device, and an interrogation indictor configured to indicate to a user of the RFID device that an unauthorized RFID reader is attempting to interrogate the RFID device when the RFID signal capture device is positioned in close proximity to the RFID device to provide protection thereto and when the RFID reader is producing the interrogation signal.
problem: Preventing unauthorized RFID interrogation of a protected device while alerting the user to attempted data capture.
constraint: The disruption circuit must operate without permanently damaging the RFID device or its data, and the indicator must function reliably in proximity to the device without false positives from ambient signals.
mechanism: Use a portable device with an active signal disruption circuit to interfere with unauthorized communication attempts, combined with an alert system to notify the user of such attempts.
mechanism_raw: Using a portable container with an embedded signal-disruption circuit that actively interferes with the RFID reader's interrogation signal when positioned near the device, combined with an interrogation indicator that alerts the user when disruption occurs.

abstract: Sleeve and album page devices for holding flat items, in particular a compact disc such as a photo compact disc together with an associated index print, the preferred embodiment including an embedded synthetic paper strip with an exposed write-on area for identifying the subject matter of the compact disc.
reason: The patent describes a physical storage device with an integrated write-on label strip. While useful, it does not describe a causal mechanism that solves a broader problem through functional relationships or trade-offs—it is a static product design combining known elements (sleeve, synthetic paper, write-on area) without a novel operational principle.

abstract: The present invention is directed to wheat plants having increased resistance to an imidazolinone herbicide. More particularly, the present invention includes wheat plants containing one or more IMI nucleic acids such as a Teal IMI cultivar. The nucleic acids are preferably located on or derived from different genomes. The present invention also includes seeds produced by these wheat plants and methods of controlling weeds in the vicinity of these wheat plants.
problem: Developing crops with resistance to specific herbicides without cross-resistance or genetic instability.
constraint: Ensuring the nucleic acids are derived from distinct genomes to prevent genetic incompatibility or unintended interactions.
mechanism: Combining genetic elements from phylogenetically distinct sources to introduce a functional trait while avoiding cross-interference and maintaining stable expression through genetic isolation.
mechanism_raw: Introducing nucleic acids from different genomes to confer herbicide resistance, leveraging genetic diversity to avoid conflicts and ensure stable expression of the resistance trait.

abstract: There is provided a method and system for sorting mailpieces in which a mailpiece is diverted into a sorting compartment of a sorting machine as a function of a sorting code associated with the mailpiece, where several sorting code ranges are each associated with a sorting compartment. An exemplary method comprises associating at least one first sorting code range with at least another sorting code range which is a subrange of the first sorting code range and checking consecutively for the sorting code ranges associated with each other whether the sorting code belongs to the sorting code range. The exemplary method further includes diverting the mailpiece into the sorting compartment that is associated with the last sorting code range for which the sorting code belongs to the sorting code range.
problem: Efficiently sorting items into compartments based on hierarchical or overlapping code ranges without ambiguity.
constraint: Maintaining the order of range checks to ensure the most specific (sub)range is prioritized over broader parent ranges.
mechanism: Evaluating hierarchical code ranges in a prioritized sequence, where nested subranges are checked after their parent ranges, and assigning items to compartments based on the last matching subrange to ensure specificity.
mechanism_raw: Checking sorting code ranges in a nested hierarchy, where subranges are evaluated after their parent ranges, and diverting the item to the compartment associated with the last matching subrange.

abstract: A mounting device includes a vertically movable mounting table for mounting thereon a target object and a rotational driving mechanism for rotating the mounting table within a predetermined angle. The mounting table is vertically raised and rotated by the rotational driving mechanism. The rotational driving mechanism includes a driving shaft extending in a tangential direction of the mounting table and a moving body moving in the tangential direction via the driving shaft. A first cam follower is attached in perpendicular to the moving body and a second cam follower is extending horizontally from an outer circumferential surface of the mounting table so as to be in contact with the first cam follower. Also, a resilient member connecting the mounting table and the moving body brings the first cam follower and the second cam follower into elastic contact with each other.
problem: Coordinating vertical and rotational motion of a mounting table to precisely position a target object.
constraint: Balancing the resilient force to ensure continuous contact between cam followers while allowing smooth motion.
mechanism: Using a resiliently biased contact element to maintain continuous engagement between a moving body and a mounting surface, converting tangential motion into coordinated vertical and rotational displacement through mechanical coupling.
mechanism_raw: Using a cam follower system with a resilient member to maintain elastic contact between a moving body and the mounting table, translating tangential motion into coordinated vertical and rotational movement.

abstract: A multiple speed power transmission comprising: four epicylic gearing assemblies each having first, second, and third rotating elements with specified interconnections, an input shaft, an output shaft, three clutches, and two brakes. Clutches and brakes are applied in combinations of three to produce eight forward ratios and one reverse ratio.
problem: Providing multiple gear ratios in a compact power transmission system.
constraint: Managing clutch and brake combinations to avoid conflicting engagements that could damage the system or prevent ratio changes.
mechanism: Configuring selectively engageable locking and coupling elements with a multi-element gear train to create distinct power flow paths, enabling variable mechanical ratios through controlled engagement states.
mechanism_raw: Combining clutches and brakes in specific configurations with epicyclic gear assemblies to selectively engage or lock rotating elements, enabling distinct gear ratios through controlled power flow paths.

abstract: This invention provides an improvement relating to an extendable and retractable auxiliary axle suitable for supporting an end section of a telescopic conveyor system having rotatable wheel assemblies. The improvement provides for an axle assembly for a conveyor system where the axle is a transversely extending axle positioned forwardly of the rotatable wheel assemblies on the conveyor system. There is provided an axle frame operatively associated with the axle for mounting the axle relative to the conveyor system. Actuatable systems mounted on the frame are provided for displacing the axle between a first raised position and a second lowered position; also provided are a device for actuating the actuatable system to permit the actuatable system to raise and lower the auxiliary axle as desired.
problem: Supporting the end section of a telescopic conveyor system during extension or retraction.
constraint: Ensuring the axle's position and actuation do not interfere with the wheel assemblies' rotation or the conveyor's structural integrity.
mechanism: Deploying a dynamically positionable support element ahead of rotating wheel assemblies, using actuation to adjust its elevation in coordination with system extension or retraction to maintain structural support without rotational interference.
mechanism_raw: Positioning an auxiliary axle forward of the wheel assemblies and using actuation systems to raise or lower it, dynamically adjusting support as the conveyor extends or retracts.

abstract: The invention relates to a device for braiding fibers into a braided structure, the device comprising a braiding machine, comprising a continuous track plate, a forming device, comprising a forming ring, a braiding mandrel about which the braiding machine braids at least one layer of the braided structure, and positioning means to effectuate relative movement of the mandrel and the braiding machine during braiding. The continuous track plate and/or the forming ring are build up of at least two parts that may be separated and reattached to each other, the parts being arranged such as to allow the track plate and/or the forming ring to enclose the mandrel. The invention further relates to a method for braiding fibers into a braided structure.
problem: Braiding fibers around a mandrel that cannot be easily accessed or enclosed by a fixed braiding machine structure.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and alignment of the braiding components while allowing repeated separation and reattachment to enclose the mandrel.
mechanism: Using detachable and reattachable structural components that form a closed working environment around a target object, allowing the components to be separated for placement and then reconnected to resume operation, while maintaining alignment and enabling relative motion between the target and the working mechanism.
mechanism_raw: Modular separable components (track plate and forming ring) that can be detached, positioned around the mandrel, and reattached to create a closed braiding environment, enabling relative movement between the mandrel and braiding machine during operation.

abstract: In a system, an angle sensor outputs a pulse each time an output shaft of an internal combustion engine rotates by a preset angle, and a calculator calculates speed-change information indicative of a change in a speed of rotation of the output shaft based on the pulses outputted from the angle sensor. A determiner determines, based on the speed-change information, whether at least one of the pulses outputted from the angle sensor represents a proper timing for a preset of a pinion of a starter with a ring gear mounted on the output shaft. A pinion engaging unit shifts the pinion toward the ring gear so that the pinion is engaged with the ring gear when it is determined that the at least one of the pulses outputted from the angle sensor represents the proper timing for the preset of the pinion with the ring gear.
problem: Engaging a starter pinion with a ring gear on an engine output shaft at the correct rotational timing to avoid misalignment or damage.
constraint: Achieving precise timing synchronization between pinion engagement and shaft rotation without relying on continuous or complex monitoring systems.
mechanism: Monitoring rotational position through periodic signals generated per revolution, deriving speed-change metrics from temporal spacing between signals, and actuating engagement at a predetermined rotational phase determined by real-time analysis of the derived metrics.
mechanism_raw: Using an angle sensor to generate pulses corresponding to shaft rotation, calculating speed-change information from pulse intervals, and determining optimal pinion engagement timing based on real-time rotational position data.

abstract: A system and processes for the accurate measurement and control of image color values on a printing press with or without the presence of a color bar. More particularly, a universal closed loop color control system and processes for controlling the color quality of color images printed on a substrate online or offline, with or without a color bar printed on the substrate. The system may be run in a “Color Bar Mode” and scan simple rectangular color patches corresponding to each ink key in the print units, or can run in “Gray Spot Mode” and maintain overall target ink density values on the substrate as well as gray balance if the job has critical half tone images, or if the color bar is obtrusive on the job.
problem: Maintaining accurate color quality control on a printing press when a color bar is absent or obstructive on the printed substrate.
constraint: Balancing control accuracy between two distinct sensing strategies while minimizing disruption to the printing process.
mechanism: Implementing a feedback-controlled system that dynamically selects between two measurement sources—one based on dedicated reference samples and another based on integrated image content—depending on operational conditions, to maintain consistent output quality.
mechanism_raw: Adaptive closed-loop control that switches between scanning predefined color patches (Color Bar Mode) and analyzing gray balance or target ink density values directly on the printed image (Gray Spot Mode) based on job requirements.

abstract: A high-strength hot-dip galvanized steel sheet excellent in workability according to the present invention: contains C, Si, Mn and other elements; has a dual phase structure containing ferrite and martensite as the metallographic structure; and, in the ferrite structure, satisfies the expression 0.2≦(Lb/La)≦1.5 when the length per unit area of the grain boundaries of crystal grains the crystal orientation differences of which are 10 degrees or more is defined as La and the length per unit area of the grain boundaries of crystal grains the crystal orientation differences of which are less than 10 degrees is defined as Lb, and further satisfies the requirements that the average value of D is 25 μm or less and the area ratio of crystal grains satisfying the expression D≦30 μm in the ferrite grains surrounded by the grain boundaries of crystal grains the crystal orientation differences of which are 10 degrees or more is 50% or more when the circle equivalent diameter of each of ferrite grains surrounded by the grain boundaries of crystal grains the crystal orientation differences of which are 10 degrees or more is defined as D; and has a tensile strength of 980 MPa or more.
problem: Achieving high tensile strength in a hot-dip galvanized steel sheet while maintaining sufficient workability for forming operations.
constraint: Meeting minimum tensile strength (980 MPa) while ensuring grain size and orientation parameters remain within ranges that preserve formability.
mechanism: Adjusting material properties by controlling crystalline or grain structure characteristics, specifically by regulating grain boundary orientation relationships and grain dimensions within a phase, to achieve a balance between mechanical strength and plastic deformation capability.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the metallographic microstructure by regulating grain boundary orientation differences (via Lb/La ratio) and grain size (D) in the ferrite phase to balance strength and ductility.

abstract: A structural reinforcing material and method of making the same is disclosed and described. The material is prepared by coating glass reinforcing fibers with a molten epoxy-based composition. The glass fiber reinforced material can then be formed into a preform suitable for injection molding into an expandable sealing baffle.
problem: Creating a moldable preform from glass fibers that can be shaped into a complex sealing structure (e.g., an expandable baffle) via injection molding.
constraint: Ensuring the epoxy coating provides sufficient adhesion and structural integrity to the fibers while remaining compatible with injection molding temperatures and pressures.
mechanism: Applying a thermally-fusible binding agent to reinforcing fibers to form a self-supporting composite preform that maintains structural coherence during subsequent shaping under heat and pressure.
mechanism_raw: Coating glass reinforcing fibers with a molten epoxy-based composition to bind fibers into a cohesive preform structure that retains shape during subsequent molding processes.

abstract: The present invention relates to the Lactobacillus genus that have the ability to survive in high temperature environments. These thermostable microorganisms have the ability to produce viable antibacterial agents in different food products after heat 5 treatment. The thermostable microorganisms of the Lactobacillus genus may be included in food products that demand high temperature. A further object of the present invention is the ability of a food product comprising the thermostable microorganisms of the Lactobacillus genus for promoting immunotolerance in autoimmune diseases such as coeliac disease. Furthermore, two novel strains of lactobacillus 10 genus are disclosed, Lactobacillus plantarum LB3e and Lactobacillus plantarum LB7c deposited at Deutsche Sammlung von Mikroorganismen und Zeelkulturen, which have been assigned accession number 17852 and 17853 respectively.
problem: Maintaining functional viability of beneficial microorganisms during high-temperature food processing while preserving their antibacterial and immunomodulatory effects.
constraint: Balancing thermostability with the need to preserve live microbial viability and functional efficacy during processing and storage.
mechanism: Selecting organisms with inherent resistance to thermal stress that retain their functional output (e.g., metabolite production, regulatory signaling) after exposure to elevated temperatures, enabling their survival and activity in heat-processed environments.
mechanism_raw: Selecting and utilizing thermostable microorganisms (e.g., Lactobacillus strains) that retain their metabolic activity and functional properties (e.g., antibacterial agent production, immunotolerance promotion) after exposure to heat treatment, enabling their use in heat-demanding food products.

abstract: Decorative strip inlay products. Strip inlay products are used at the outer edges of stringed instruments, about the sound aperture and inwardly of the edges. Products of the invention are laser cut in the top surface of a workpiece. A bottom portion of the workpiece supports overlying cut portions. Where the strip must be flexed for insertion into curved channels, a substrate layer is resiliently flexible, and the overlying display layer is cut into segments, with spaces between the segments. The segments can move relative to each other, and/or flex, when the substrate flexes. Alternatively, the uncut bottom portion of the strip is rigid relative to an axis perpendicular to the top, and cavities in the display pattern are filled with filler and the resultant product, is sanded, resulting in display of both the filler material and the full pattern of the facing material as cut by the laser.
problem: Creating a flexible decorative strip that maintains visual continuity and structural integrity when bent or flexed for curved channels in stringed instruments.
constraint: Ensuring the segments move cohesively to preserve the visual design while maintaining sufficient flexibility for installation in curved geometries.
mechanism: Partitioning a continuous visual layer into discrete segments separated by controlled gaps, allowing relative displacement between segments when a flexible substrate deforms, preserving pattern integrity and material continuity under bending or flexing.
mechanism_raw: Segmenting the display layer into discrete pieces separated by gaps, allowing relative movement or flexing of segments when the underlying resilient substrate bends, thereby accommodating curvature without fracturing the pattern or material.

abstract: An outboard motor includes a propeller, an engine, a transmission, a casing, an engine cooling mechanism, a cooling jacket, a water intake opening, and a transmission coolant flow channel. The casing is arranged to house the transmission. The engine cooling mechanism is arranged to cool the engine by supplying the water taken into the casing from the water intake opening to the engine via an engine coolant flow channel. The cooling jacket is arranged adjacent to the transmission inside the casing. The water intake opening is provided at a predetermined position of the casing to which a dynamic pressure is applied by water flow when a marine vessel travels. The transmission coolant flow channel is arranged to connect the water intake opening and the cooling jacket. The transmission coolant flow channel is provided independently of the engine coolant flow channel.
problem: Efficiently cooling both the engine and transmission in an outboard motor without thermal cross-interference or shared flow limitations.
constraint: Optimizing channel geometry and placement to maximize cooling efficiency while minimizing space and pressure losses in the shared water intake system.
mechanism: Routing separate thermal management pathways from a shared fluid source to distinct heat-generating zones, ensuring independent flow distribution and targeted heat extraction without cross-contamination or flow competition between zones.
mechanism_raw: Providing independent coolant flow channels for the engine and transmission, each connected to a common water intake but routed separately to their respective cooling jackets, ensuring targeted heat dissipation without mixing or competing flow demands.

abstract: Textile treatment agent containing a biocidal compound, a perfume composition and a non-ionic surfactant, wherein the non-ionic surfactant has an HLB value of from 10.5 to 15 and a cloud temperature of at least 50° C. This allows production of a stable textile treatment agent which reduces the number of microorganisms on textiles treated with the agent and gives the textiles a pleasant fragrance.
problem: Stabilizing a multi-component textile treatment agent containing biocidal compounds and volatile perfumes to ensure shelf-life and functional efficacy.
constraint: Matching surfactant properties to the solubility and volatility profiles of the biocidal and fragrance components to maintain stability across varying environmental conditions.
mechanism: Matching amphiphilic compound properties (hydrophilic-lipophilic balance and thermal phase transition threshold) to the solubility and volatility characteristics of active ingredients, stabilizing the formulation against phase separation and degradation across environmental variations.
mechanism_raw: Using a non-ionic surfactant with a specific HLB range (10.5–15) and cloud temperature (≥50°C) to stabilize the formulation by balancing hydrophilic-lipophilic interactions and thermal responsiveness, preventing phase separation or degradation of active ingredients.

abstract: A method and apparatus for inhibiting the motion of a vehicle comprising a housing having a cavity, the cavity adapted to contain a net so that the net may be made available for release on command; tire engagement spikes supported by the housing, the spikes being movable to a first position to engage the tires of an oncoming vehicle, the spikes also being movable to a second position to avoid tire engagement, the spikes being positioned to grasp the net when in the first position; and an actuator for moving the spikes between the first and the second positions on command, wherein the spikes comprise at least two barbs adapted to penetrate a pneumatic tire, the spikes also having a hook for grasping a loop of the leading edge of the net. The method of the invention is a method of inhibiting the motion of a moving vehicle comprising the steps of providing a housing in the path of the vehicle, the housing being adapted to releasably contain a net having spikes arranged at a leading edge of the net; transmitting an electronic command manually to a motor that exposes the spikes to the moving vehicle; engaging the tires of the moving vehicle with the spikes by puncturing them; pulling the net from the housing by wrapping the net around the tires as the tires continue to move forward; and limiting continued forward motion by tightening the net around the axles thereby ultimately constraining the tires from further rotation.
problem: Rapidly and reliably inhibiting the motion of a moving vehicle using a deployable system that engages tires and constrains rotation without requiring direct mechanical intervention.
constraint: Timing the deployment and force application to ensure immediate tire engagement and net deployment while avoiding premature release or insufficient entanglement to stop the vehicle.
mechanism: Coordinating deployment of penetrating elements and a capturing structure via a timed actuation sequence, where the penetrating elements engage the capturing structure during initial contact, and continued motion induces entanglement and constriction around rotating components to generate resistive forces.
mechanism_raw: Coordinating the deployment of tire-puncturing spikes and a net via an actuator, where the spikes penetrate tires and grasp the net's leading edge, allowing the net to wrap around rotating tires and tighten around axles as forward motion continues, thereby creating friction and entanglement to halt movement.

abstract: A steering apparatus whereby the steering load is equal even when the left and right steering angles are large when an outboard motor is steered to the left and right via a swivel shaft. A connecting hole of a steering plate is provided at a position spaced from a center line of the steering plate so that equal angles are formed by a first straight line, joining the center of the swivel shaft and the connecting hole, and a second straight line, joining the connecting hole and a link hole formed in a steering rod.
problem: Uneven steering load distribution when an outboard motor is steered to large left/right angles via a swivel shaft.
constraint: Maintaining equal angular relationships between the swivel shaft, connecting hole, and link hole even at large steering angles to ensure uniform load distribution.
mechanism: Positioning a connection point on a movable element such that the angles formed by (1) a line from a pivot axis to the connection point and (2) a line from the connection point to a downstream link are equalized, balancing forces across varying orientations of the movable element.
mechanism_raw: Positioning a connecting hole on a steering plate at a non-centerline location such that the angles formed by (1) a line from the swivel shaft center to the connecting hole and (2) a line from the connecting hole to a link hole in the steering rod are equal, thereby balancing the steering load regardless of steering angle.

abstract: A convertible nursing bra, in an exemplary embodiment, having bra support cups releasable from straps to provide access and further including underlying support panels connected to the encircling strap or under wire support and remaining connected to the straps to provide continued support during nursing. Released portions of the cups are temporarily retained by auxiliary attachment devices on the encircling strap to reduce interference during nursing. The releasable cup-to-strap and/or cup-to-encircling strap connecting devices are easily managed for access, stowing and re-covering.
problem: Providing temporary access for nursing while maintaining continuous support and minimizing interference from released bra components.
constraint: Balancing ease of access (cup release) with retention of released components and continuous support from underlying panels during nursing.
mechanism: Releasable attachment of components to a support structure, combined with auxiliary retention devices that temporarily hold detached portions to prevent interference during access, while underlying support panels remain connected to provide continued support.
mechanism_raw: Releasable attachment of bra cups to straps, combined with auxiliary retention devices on the encircling strap that temporarily hold released cup portions to prevent interference during nursing, while underlying support panels remain connected to provide continued support.

abstract: A method and device is provided, including implanting, at an intraventricular site of a ventricle of a patient, a spool coupled to a first end portion of a longitudinal member, and coupling a second end portion of the longitudinal member to a portion of tissue facing a lumen of the ventricle. Other embodiments are also described.
problem: Providing structural support or functional enhancement to a ventricle's tissue via minimally invasive implantation.
constraint: Achieving stable coupling of the longitudinal member to both the spool and target tissue while accommodating dynamic cardiac motion.
mechanism: Implanting a tensioned structural element anchored at two points within a dynamic organ to support tissue through interaction with the organ's motion, creating a load-bearing interface that adapts to cyclic deformation.
mechanism_raw: Implanting a spool at an intraventricular site coupled to a longitudinal member, whose second end is anchored to tissue facing the ventricular lumen, creating a tensioned structural element that interacts with the heart's motion to support tissue or improve function.

abstract: A molding apparatus for making a cutting tool includes a cylindrically shaped elastic bag having an internal cavity for receiving a granulated material, such as a mixture of cobalt and carbide. The profile of the interior cavity substantially corresponds to the shape of the cutting tool being produced. The ends of the bag are open to provide access to the interior cavity of the bag. A substantially rigid tubular-shaped pressure sleeve encloses an outer circumference of the elastic bag. A pair of end caps operate to seal the open ends of the elastic bag and are engageable with the ends of the pressure sleeve. The granulated material can be formed into a solid coherent structure by placing the assembled mold containing the granulated material into a hydrostatic press for applying a substantially uniform compressive load to the outer periphery of the elastic bag.
problem: Forming granulated material into a solid coherent structure with a precise shape while applying uniform compressive force.
constraint: Balancing the elasticity of the bag to conform to the material with the rigidity of the pressure sleeve to ensure uniform compression without localized stress concentrations.
mechanism: Using a flexible container shaped to match a target form, enclosed within a rigid outer sleeve, and applying uniform external pressure to conform the container to the material, distributing compressive force evenly to form a solid structure.
mechanism_raw: Using an elastic bag with an interior cavity shaped to match the target tool, enclosed within a rigid pressure sleeve, and applying uniform external pressure via a hydrostatic press. The elastic bag deforms to conform to the granulated material, distributing pressure evenly to form a solid structure.

abstract: Disclosed are a nickel hydroxide powder and a method for producing the same. The nickel hydroxide powder comprises a particle in the form of sphere, an average particle diameter of 0.1 μm or more and 30 μm or less, and the amount of the particles having a diameter of 0.7 times or more and 1.3 times or less the average particle diameter of 80% by weight or more based on the total amount of particles. The method for producing a nickel hydroxide powder comprises the steps of (1) to (4): (1) injecting a solution containing a nickel salt through a pore into a liquid mutually insoluble with the solution to obtain an emulsion including solution as a dispersed phase and the liquid as a continuous phase; (2) gelating the emulsion; (3) separating the dispersed phase from the obtained gel to obtain a cake; and (4) drying the cake.
problem: Producing nickel hydroxide powder with a narrow particle size distribution (80% within 0.7–1.3× the average diameter) for consistent performance in electrochemical applications.
constraint: Controlling emulsion droplet size and gelation kinetics to ensure the resulting particles meet the specified size distribution while maintaining spherical morphology.
mechanism: Controlling droplet size in an emulsion and gelation kinetics to produce spherical particles with a narrow size distribution, achieved by separating the dispersed phase and drying the resulting cake to retain morphology and uniformity.
mechanism_raw: Injecting a nickel salt solution through a pore into an immiscible liquid to form an emulsion, gelling the emulsion to create a structured phase, separating the dispersed phase to obtain a cake, and drying the cake to yield spherical particles with controlled size distribution.

abstract: A tin-plated steel sheet includes a plating layer containing tin on at least one surface of a steel sheet, and a chemical conversion coating containing P and tin on the plating layer is provided. In the steel sheet, a coated amount of the chemical conversion coating per surface is 1.0 to 50 mg/m2 in terms of P, an atomic ratio Sn/P obtained from the intensity of a P2p peak and that of a Sn3d peak is 1.0 to 1.5, the intensities being measured at the surface using an x-ray photoelectron spectroscopic method, and an atomic ratio O/P obtained from the intensity of the P2p peak and that of an O1s peak is 4.0 to 9.0. The phosphoric acid-based chemical conversion coating of the tin-plated steel sheet can suppress degradation in performance, which is caused by the growth of a tin oxide layer on the surface, instead of a conventional chromate coating.
problem: Preventing degradation of tin-plated steel sheets caused by tin oxide layer growth on the surface.
constraint: The coating must maintain specific atomic ratios and thickness (1.0–50 mg/m² in terms of P) to balance oxidation resistance and coating integrity.
mechanism: A chemical conversion treatment modifies surface chemistry by forming a controlled-composition layer that suppresses oxide formation through stabilized atomic interactions, with composition and thickness constrained to balance oxidation resistance and structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A phosphoric acid-based chemical conversion coating with precisely controlled atomic ratios of Sn/P (1.0–1.5) and O/P (4.0–9.0) suppresses tin oxide formation by stabilizing the surface chemistry, measured via X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.

abstract: A non-contact, distance traveled measurement system (DTMS) to calculate speed and distance traveled by a vehicle over rails—more specifically, by trains traveling on standard railroad tracks. Preferably, a pair of short range (near field) microwave-based transmitters/sensors (transceivers) are mounted on the underside of the train and used to key on rail-bed features such as cross ties or tie plates. Preferred embodiments also include infrared sensors as a redundant channel that is less sensitive to moisture in the track bed. Data from the sensors is correlated to determine the time delay between the first and second sensors' passage over objects on the rail bed such as cross-ties or tie-plates. From this time delay, nearly instantaneous velocity can be computed at each given target such as a tie plate (metal target) or a tie (dielectric contrast target). Velocity versus time curves can be integrated over time to derive distance traveled.
problem: Accurately measuring speed and distance traveled by vehicles (e.g., trains) over rails without physical contact, even in moisture-prone environments.
constraint: Sensor placement and synchronization must account for environmental variability (e.g., moisture) to ensure reliable feature detection and data correlation.
mechanism: Multiple non-contact sensors detect periodic features on a surface and correlate their passage times to compute velocity, with redundant sensing modalities mitigating environmental interference, and temporal integration of velocity data yields distance traveled.
mechanism_raw: Two microwave sensors detect rail-bed features (e.g., cross ties) and correlate their passage times to compute velocity, while infrared sensors provide redundant data to mitigate moisture interference. Time-delay integration of velocity yields distance traveled.

abstract: A support structure for a splitter of a cutting tool includes a lock device and a moving device. The lock device can lock and unlock the splitter at a storage position. The moving device can move the splitter from the storage position to an ejected position, in which a part of the splitter extends above an upper surface of a table of the cutting tool, when the lock device unlocks the splitter at the storage position.
problem: Managing the position of a cutting tool splitter between a stowed (storage) and operational (ejected) state while ensuring secure locking during storage.
constraint: The lock and moving mechanisms must coordinate to prevent unintended deployment while allowing reliable ejection when unlocked.
mechanism: A mechanical system uses a locking mechanism to retain a component in a storage state and a separate actuation mechanism to transition it to an operational state when the lock is released, ensuring coordinated state transitions.
mechanism_raw: A lock device mechanically secures the splitter in the storage position, and a moving device (e.g., spring or actuator) deploys it to the ejected position when the lock is released, enabling controlled transition between states.

abstract: The invention is based on a device having a centering element (10) and at least one form-locking element (12) for fastening an axially mountable tool (14) to a drive shaft (16), which is drivable in an oscillating manner, of a hand-held power tool (28) in which the centering element (10) is provided for centering the tool (14) relative to the drive shaft (16), and the form-locking element (12) is provided for defining a rotary position of the tool (14) relative to the drive shaft (16).It is proposed that the form-locking element (12) is located radially outside the centering element (10).
problem: Fastening an axially mountable tool to an oscillating drive shaft in a hand-held power tool while ensuring both axial alignment and rotational positioning.
constraint: The radial placement of the form-locking element outside the centering element must maintain structural integrity while enabling precise tool attachment.
mechanism: A dual-component attachment system decouples alignment and rotational locking functions into concentric elements, where an inner element ensures axial alignment and an outer element secures rotary positioning through form-locking engagement.
mechanism_raw: A centering element aligns the tool relative to the drive shaft, and a radially outer form-locking element secures the tool’s rotary position, decoupling alignment and locking functions into concentric components.

abstract: A pocket assembly includes a major panel and a pocket panel coupled together to define a pocket between the panels. A divider is placed in the pocket to partition the pocket into two or more compartments. The divider comprises a securing element secured to at least one of the major and pocket panels.
problem: Partitioning a pocket between two panels into multiple compartments for organized storage.
constraint: The securing element must balance ease of divider placement with sufficient retention force to prevent unintended movement of the divider during use.
mechanism: A divider is attached to a panel via a retention mechanism that balances ease of placement with sufficient holding force, creating discrete compartments within an enclosed space while maintaining structural cohesion of the assembly.
mechanism_raw: A divider is secured to at least one panel via a securing element (e.g., adhesive, clip, or fastener), creating discrete compartments within the pocket while maintaining structural cohesion of the assembly.

abstract: A centrifuge has a rotor for receiving a disposable processing unit. The centrifuge is configured such that the motor is attached to an enclosure and the enclosure is supported on a base. The connection between the base and the enclosure is a vibration isolator, and the isolator is positioned such that its effective line of action aligns with the effective plane of rotation of the rotor. In accordance with another feature of the invention, the processing units are held in a decanting position by a decant ring that moves vertically but does not rotate. The ring engages the top of the processing unit during decant and the abrasion is minimal.
problem: Vibrational energy from a rotating centrifuge rotor disrupts system stability and causes abrasion during decanting of processing units.
constraint: Balancing vibration isolation with structural support while maintaining precise alignment during high-speed rotation and decanting operations.
mechanism: Align a vibrational force-canceling element's effective line of action with a rotating component's effective plane of rotation to redirect vibrational energy, and use a non-rotational engagement mechanism that moves along an axis to interact with processing units without continuous sliding contact, minimizing abrasion.
mechanism_raw: Aligning the vibration isolator's effective line of action with the rotor's effective plane of rotation to cancel or redirect vibrational forces, and using a vertically moving decant ring that engages processing units without rotational contact to minimize abrasion.
residual_terms: ["vibrational force-canceling element", "effective line of action", "effective plane of rotation", "non-rotational engagement mechanism"]

abstract: Disclosed are compositions and methods for increasing the longevity of a cell culture and permitting the increased production of proteins, preferably recombinant proteins, such as antibodies, peptides, enzymes, growth factors, interleukins, interferons, hamiones, and vaccines. Cells transfected with an apoptosis-inhibiting gene or vector, such as a triple mutant Bcl-2 gene, can survive longer in culture, resulting in extension of the state and yield of protein biosynthesis. Such transfected cells exhibit maximal cell densities that equal or exceed the maximal density achieved by the parent cell lines. Transfected cells can also be pre-adapted for growth in serum-free medium, greatly decreasing the time required to obtain protein production in serum-free medium. In certain methods, the pre-adapted cells can be used for protein production following transformation under serum-free conditions. The method preferably involves eukaryotic cells, more preferably mammalian cells.
problem: Cell cultures undergo apoptosis prematurely, limiting their longevity and reducing protein production yields in bioreactors.
constraint: Ensuring genetic modifications do not disrupt normal cellular functions or lead to uncontrolled proliferation while maintaining compatibility with serum-free media.
mechanism: Introduce a genetic modification that suppresses a programmed cell death pathway to extend a biosynthetic phase, thereby increasing product yield without reducing viable cell density.
mechanism_raw: Introducing an apoptosis-inhibiting gene (e.g., triple mutant Bcl-2) into cells to delay programmed cell death, thereby extending the biosynthetic phase and enabling higher protein yields without compromising cell density.
residual_terms: ["genetic modification", "programmed cell death pathway", "biosynthetic phase", "viable cell density"]

abstract: A system and method are presented for managing and using (e.g. for commercial or medical use) of a database. A verified database of a plurality of identified individuals is provided. The verified database comprises a plurality of individual-identifier data sets (IDSs) and relationship data. The verified database is processed in accordance with one or more parameters or conditions selected in accordance with at least one medical application, and a sub-group database is created including data records of the individuals from the verified database having said one or more selected parameters or conditions. This allows collection of data comprising the one or more selected parameters or conditions and delivery of at least part of the collected data to one or more users, and enables applying data from the verified database to provide personalized medicine service to at least one of the identified individuals.
problem: Personalized medical services require dynamic filtering of verified individual data to generate targeted subgroups for specific medical applications.
constraint: Maintaining data privacy and accuracy while enabling efficient subgroup creation and real-time data delivery across diverse medical applications.
mechanism: Apply user-defined selection criteria to a verified data repository to dynamically generate filtered subsets, then transmit the filtered data to end-user systems for personalized application delivery.
mechanism_raw: Processing a verified database by applying user-selected parameters or conditions to create sub-group databases, then delivering collected data to users for personalized medicine applications.
residual_terms: ["verified data repository", "user-defined selection criteria", "filtered subsets", "personalized application delivery"]

abstract: A tooth cleaning apparatus having a tooth scrubbing assembly and a handle through which a cleaning portion of the tooth scrubbing assembly can be placed in operative relationship to a user's teeth and borne against surfaces of a user's teeth. The tooth scrubbing assembly is configured so that at least one of a) the cleaning portion of the tooth scrubbing assembly is preformed in a curved shape to conform to a curved arrangement of inside surfaces of a user's front teeth and b) a part of the tooth scrubbing assembly is flexible to allow conforming of the cleaning portion of the tooth scrubbing assembly to the curved arrangement of inside surfaces of a user's front teeth under a pressure as applied by a user during a tooth cleaning operation.
problem: Tooth cleaning tools fail to conform to the curved internal surfaces of front teeth, reducing cleaning efficacy and increasing abrasion risk.
constraint: Balancing structural rigidity for effective cleaning with sufficient flexibility to adapt to varying tooth geometries without permanent deformation.
mechanism: Preform a cleaning element with a curved geometry and integrate compliant regions that enable dynamic shape adaptation to surface contours under externally applied pressure during contact-based cleaning.
mechanism_raw: Preforming a cleaning portion in a curved shape and incorporating flexibility in the tool assembly to dynamically conform to tooth curvature under user-applied pressure during cleaning.
residual_terms: ["cleaning element", "curved geometry", "compliant regions", "surface contours", "externally applied pressure"]

abstract: A printer that uses roll paper as the printing medium and has a manual feed button and an automatic paper cutter detects if the manual feed button was operated. If the manual feed button was operated, the paper is advanced a prescribed length, and the paper is cut by the automatic paper cutter after advancing the paper stops.
problem: Manual feed operations in printers require precise coordination between paper advancement and cutting to avoid misalignment or incomplete cuts.
