constraint: Synchronizing mechanical actions (advancement and cutting) with sensor feedback to maintain timing accuracy and prevent paper jams or misfeeds.
mechanism: Detect a manual activation signal, execute a prescribed material advancement sequence, then trigger a severing action after motion cessation, using sensor feedback to synchronize sequential mechanical operations and ensure positional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Detecting manual feed button activation, advancing paper by a prescribed length, then triggering an automatic cutter to sever the paper after advancement stops, ensuring consistent cut placement.
residual_terms: ["manual activation signal", "material advancement sequence", "severing action", "sensor feedback", "sequential mechanical operations"]

abstract: A display device having backlight and the backlight control method thereof is provided. Through the provided method, it is capable of fast determining which intensity range the intensity signal from the means for measuring the intensity of external light falls in, so that the turn-off period of backlight is reduced to avoid the decrement of brightness.
problem: Maintaining display brightness efficiently by minimizing unnecessary backlight turn-off periods in response to varying external light conditions.
constraint: Balancing power efficiency (reducing backlight activity) with maintaining consistent brightness output across varying ambient light conditions.
mechanism: A sensor detects environmental light intensity and dynamically adjusts the operational timing of a light source's activity periods to balance power efficiency with consistent brightness output. This creates a feedback loop where real-time environmental input modulates the light source's duty cycle to minimize unnecessary energy consumption while maintaining target brightness.
mechanism_raw: Fast determination of external light intensity ranges using a sensor, which dynamically adjusts the backlight's turn-off period to avoid brightness decrement. This creates a feedback loop where the system adapts its operational timing based on real-time environmental input.

abstract: Cable-stranding methods for performing SZ-stranding of strand elements about at least one core member are disclosed. One method includes passing initially spaced apart strand elements through peripheral guide holes and passing at least one core member through a generally central location of at least one guide member. The method also includes actuating a controller that controls the rotation of the at least one guide member and rotating the at least one guide member to form the SZ-stranded assembly.
problem: Creating a precisely controlled SZ-stranded assembly of strand elements around a core member with consistent spacing and alignment during rotation.
constraint: Maintaining uniform spacing and alignment of strand elements during rotation to ensure structural integrity and consistent stranding geometry.
mechanism: A guide structure with constrained pathways and a central alignment feature positions multiple flexible elements around a core member. Rotational actuation of the guide structure directly translates to a controlled twisting motion, causing the elements to form a helical configuration with uniform spacing and alignment relative to the core.
mechanism_raw: Using a guide member with peripheral holes and a central guide to constrain strand elements and the core, then actuating rotational movement of the guide member to twist the strands into a helical configuration. The controlled rotation of the guide member directly translates to the stranding pattern.

abstract: A rotary wing aircraft including a vehicle vibration control system. The vehicle vibration control system includes a rotating hub mounted vibration control system, the rotating hub mounted vibration control system mounted to the rotating rotary wing hub with the rotating hub mounted vibration control system rotating with the rotating rotary wing hub. The vehicle vibration control system includes a rotary wing aircraft member sensor for outputting rotary wing aircraft member data correlating to the relative rotation of the rotating rotary wing hub member rotating relative to the nonrotating body, at least a first nonrotating body vibration sensor, the at least first nonrotating body vibration sensor outputting at least first nonrotating body vibration sensor data correlating to vibrations, at least a first nonrotating body circular force generator, the at least a first nonrotating body circular force generator fixedly coupled with the nonrotating body, and a distributed force generation data communications network link.
problem: Reducing vibrations in a rotary wing aircraft caused by the interaction between rotating and nonrotating components.
constraint: Synchronizing force generation between the rotating and nonrotating components to avoid phase mismatches that could amplify vibrations.
mechanism: A distributed system of detectors and force applicators monitors vibrations across both a rotating component and a stationary component. The detectors sense phase and amplitude mismatches, while the force applicators generate counteracting forces in real-time, coordinated via a communication network to synchronize dynamic interactions and suppress vibration amplification.
mechanism_raw: Deploying a distributed network of sensors and force generators: sensors detect vibrations in both the rotating hub and nonrotating body, while force generators apply counteracting forces in real-time. The system uses a communications network to coordinate force application across multiple points.

abstract: The present invention provides a communication bellows including at least one external skin which has a succession of inwardly directed undulations and at least one internal skin which has a succession of outwardly directed undulations which are provided facing the inwardly directed undulations of the external skin, the two skins together delimiting an acoustic insulation space, the internal skin being connected to at least some of the inwardly directed undulations of the external skin, the external skin and internal skin being connected to each other only by some mutually facing undulations, other undulations of the two skins remaining separate from each other.
problem: Achieving effective acoustic insulation while maintaining structural flexibility in a communication bellows.
constraint: Balancing structural support (via connected undulations) with acoustic damping (via separated undulations) to prevent mechanical failure while maximizing insulation.
mechanism: Two opposing undulating surfaces are positioned to face each other, creating a sealed insulation cavity. The surfaces are selectively coupled at discrete contact points where their undulations align, allowing structural continuity at those points while isolating acoustic energy through the undulating geometry and cavity between non-contacting regions.
mechanism_raw: Designing two skins with opposing undulations (inward and outward) that face each other, creating an insulation space. The skins are connected only at mutually facing undulations, allowing selective structural coupling while isolating acoustic energy through the undulating geometry.

abstract: A refueling system including a nozzle configured to dispense fuel through a fuel path thereof into a vehicle tank. The nozzle includes a vapor path configured such that vapor recovered from the vehicle tank during refueling is passable therethrough. The system further includes a sensing valve disposed in the vapor path, wherein the sensing valve is configured to generally block the associated part of the vapor path when a sufficient vacuum from the vehicle tank is applied to the sensing valve during refueling. The system also includes a regulator valve disposed in the vapor path and arranged in series with the sensing valve, the regulator valve being configured to regulate the level of vacuum applied by a vapor pump to the sensing valve.
problem: Controlling vapor recovery during vehicle refueling to prevent over-pressurization while ensuring efficient fuel transfer.
constraint: Maintaining a vacuum level sufficient to trigger the sensing valve without exceeding safe pressure thresholds for the vehicle tank or vapor recovery system.
mechanism: A pressure-dependent switching valve blocks a flow path when a threshold vacuum level is detected, while a series regulator valve modulates the vacuum magnitude applied by a pump. The switching valve acts as a binary control based on pressure thresholds, and the regulator valve fine-tunes the system's response to maintain safe pressure ranges while enabling efficient vapor recovery.
mechanism_raw: Using a sensing valve that blocks the vapor path when a threshold vacuum is detected, paired with a regulator valve in series to modulate the vacuum level applied by a pump. The sensing valve acts as a pressure-dependent switch, while the regulator valve fine-tunes the system's response.

abstract: A method and apparatus for reducing dynamic loading of a gas turbine engine is provided. The gas turbine engine includes a rotor shaft assembly including a rotor shaft, a bearing assembly, a mounting race, and a support frame, the mounting race including a spherical surface. The method includes supporting the rotor shaft on the gas turbine engine support frame with the bearing assembly, the rotor shaft including a yield portion configured to permit bending of the rotor shaft during an imbalance operation.
problem: Reducing dynamic loading in gas turbine engines caused by rotor imbalance during operation.
constraint: Balancing flexibility in the yield portion to absorb imbalance forces without compromising structural integrity during normal operation.
mechanism: A rotating shaft with a designated flexible segment that allows controlled elastic deformation under centrifugal imbalance forces, converting dynamic loading into localized strain energy to reduce transmitted loads while maintaining structural continuity during normal operation.
mechanism_raw: A rotor shaft with a yield portion that permits controlled bending during imbalance, converting dynamic forces into localized deformation to reduce transmitted loads.

abstract: A two-stage high pressure turbine includes a second stage blade having an airfoil with a profile substantially in accordance with at least an intermediate portion of the Cartesian coordinate values of X, Y and Z set forth in Table 2. The X and Y values are distances, which when smoothly connected by an appropriate continuing curve, define airfoil profile sections at each distance Z. The profile sections at each distance Z are joined smoothly to one another to form a complete airfoil shape.
reason: The patent specifies a precise airfoil geometry defined by coordinate tables, which is a design optimization for turbine blades rather than a generalizable causal mechanism.

abstract: A method of forming a display device including source/drain electrodes on a substrate, a pixel electrode, an insulating partition wall layer, a channel-region semiconductor layer. The source/drain electrodes and the pixel electrode are formed on the substrate and in contact with each other. The insulating partition wall layer is formed on the substrate and provided with a first opening extending to between the source electrode and the drain electrode and a second opening formed on the pixel electrode and extending to the pixel electrode. The channel-region semiconductor layer is formed on the bottom of the first opening. The insulating film is formed on the partition wall layer so as to cover the first opening including the channel-region semiconductor layer. The oriented film covers the first opening from above the insulating film and the second opening from the pixel electrode.
reason: The patent describes a layered manufacturing process with specific openings for component alignment, which is a structural implementation detail rather than a transferable functional principle.

abstract: A low frequency oscillator includes a plurality of drum-shaped oscillators. Each of the drum-shaped oscillators is constructed so that a pair of disk-shaped flexural vibrators is attached on both open ends of a conductive cylinder so as to be arranged face to face. And a conductive elongated coupling member is fixed to adjacent the drum-shaped oscillators at a central portion thereof so as to electrically connect between adjacent the disk-shaped flexural vibrators and thereby coupling the drum-shaped oscillators along a central axis thereof.
problem: Creating a low-frequency oscillator system that synchronizes multiple vibrators while maintaining structural and electrical coupling.
constraint: Maintaining coupling between oscillators without interfering with their independent vibrational motion or introducing unwanted damping.
mechanism: A conductive coupling element that mechanically and electrically links adjacent vibrating bodies along a shared axis, enabling synchronized oscillation while preserving independent vibrational motion and minimizing energy loss through the coupling interface.
mechanism_raw: Coupling adjacent drum-shaped vibrators via a conductive elongated member that electrically and mechanically links their flexural elements along a central axis.
residual_terms: ["conductive coupling element", "synchronized oscillation", "independent vibrational motion", "energy loss", "coupling interface"]

abstract: A roll mill for a milling-dispersing treatment has a fixed roll fixed to a frame, and a transfer roll displaceable into and out of contact with the fixed roll in a direction perpendicular to the fixed roll by a servomotor and a ball screw. A laser sensor disposed between the fixed roll and the transfer roll measures the distance between the rolls, and a load sensor measures a pressing force between the rolls. An electronic automatic control device maintains a constant distance and a constant pressing force between the fixed roll and the transfer roll by feedback of detection signals sent from the respective sensors, wherein the servomotor is driven by the electronic automatic control device to adjust the position of the transfer roll.
problem: Maintaining consistent distance and pressing force between two rolls during milling-dispersing treatment to ensure uniform processing.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise control of both distance and force simultaneously without overloading the system or compromising throughput.
mechanism: A feedback control system measures two variables (distance and force) between interacting surfaces using sensors, and dynamically adjusts the position of one surface relative to the other via an actuator to maintain both variables within target ranges simultaneously.
mechanism_raw: Feedback control system using sensors to measure distance and load, with a servomotor and ball screw adjusting the transfer roll's position in real-time to maintain both variables within desired ranges.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for producing very fine particles by means of a jet mill (1). The relative distance a/dDüse between at least approximately concentric milling jet inlets (5) whose center lines intersect at least approximately in one point is adjusted in accordance with the pressure of the working medium, a representing the jet length and dDüse representing the nozzle diameter.
problem: Controlling particle size in a jet mill by optimizing the interaction between milling jets and the working medium.
constraint: Maintaining a precise pressure-to-distance ratio to ensure optimal jet interaction and particle size reduction without excessive energy consumption.
mechanism: A pressure-responsive spatial adjustment mechanism modulates the relative distance between fluid ejection points based on working medium pressure, thereby controlling the interaction intensity between ejected streams and material being processed to regulate output particle size.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting the relative distance between concentric milling jet inlets based on the pressure of the working medium, linking jet length and nozzle diameter to pressure to regulate particle size.

abstract: The present disclosure details a thermoacoustic driven compressor having a pressurized housing, which contains within a thermoacoustic engine and a working gas, coupled to a positive displacement reciprocating compressor. The thermoacoustic driven compressor generates scalable compressed air from a given heat source.
problem: Generating scalable compressed air from a heat source without relying on traditional mechanical engines.
constraint: Efficiently coupling acoustic wave energy from the thermoacoustic engine to the compressor's reciprocating motion while maintaining scalability and heat source flexibility.
mechanism: Thermal energy is converted into mechanical oscillations via a wave amplification process, which are then transformed into reciprocating motion to compress a fluid medium through a positive displacement mechanism.
mechanism_raw: Thermoacoustic engine converts thermal energy into acoustic waves, which drive a positive displacement reciprocating compressor to produce compressed air.

abstract: To provide a transfer tool that can be preferably used without a table such as a desk and can easily carry out the transfer operation in any places, the transfer tool includes a transfer tool main body (1) and a transferred object receiver (2) that is accompanied by the transfer tool main body (1), wherein an insertion space (AS) in which a paper slip (P) can be inserted is formed between the transfer tool main body (1) and the transferred object receiver (2); a transfer head (H) is positioned so that at least a transfer face (RTa) of the transfer head (H) is exposed in the insertion space (AS); and a tape glue (T) is transferred on the paper slip (P) by slidably moving the transfer face (RTa) in a predetermined transfer direction while bringing the transfer face (RTa) into contact with the paper slip (P) with the paper slip (P) inserted in the insertion space (AS) and the paper slip (P) sandwiched between the transfer tool main body (1) and the transferred object receiver (2).
reason: The mechanism is a specific mechanical design for portability and contact-based transfer, lacking a generalizable causal principle beyond the tool's physical structure.

abstract: A method for manufacturing a pro label book includes printing static indicia on a web of label material, applying an adhesive to each portion of the web of label material that will become a label page in a pro label book that is not the portion of the web of label material that will become a top page of a label book to be formed if the adhesive is applied to a top surface of the web of label material or a bottom page of a label book to be formed if the adhesive is applied to the bottom surface of the web of label material, printing variable information on the web of label material, sheeting the web of label material to form label pages, and batching the label pages together utilizing the applied adhesive. Certain embodiments include attaching one of a backer or a cover to the web of label material following the printing static indicia step.
problem: Efficiently assembling a pro label book with variable information and selective adhesive bonding during high-speed manufacturing.
constraint: Ensuring adhesive is applied only where needed to avoid interfering with variable information printing or final page separation, while maintaining batch integrity during sheeting.
mechanism: Selective material deposition creates temporary bonding regions on specific non-boundary areas of layered substrates, enabling automated grouping of sheets into batches while preserving separability of individual layers until final assembly.
mechanism_raw: Selective adhesive application to non-top/bottom pages enables automated batching by creating temporary adhesion points that hold sheets together until final binding.
residual_terms: ["selective material deposition", "temporary bonding regions", "non-boundary areas", "layered substrates", "separability"]

abstract: A method of manufacturing a sonar projector is disclosed. The method comprises the steps of: bonding a flat piezo-ceramic plate to a flexible conducting sheet; dicing the plate to form an assembly comprising a matrix of piezo-ceramic pegs bonded to the flexible conducting sheet, the pegs being separated by kerfs; bending the assembly to a predetermined curvature, thereby expanding the kerfs; filling the expanded kerfs with a filler material; and applying conductive material to the exposed surfaces of the pegs, such that the conductive material and the flexible conducting sheet in combination form electrodes operable to apply a voltage to the piezo-ceramic pegs. Methods of manufacturing a curved piezo-ceramic structure are also disclosed.
problem: Creating a curved piezo-ceramic structure with functional electrodes for sonar projectors while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing the curvature-induced expansion of kerfs with the need to maintain electrical connectivity and structural cohesion of the piezo-ceramic pegs during bending and filling.
mechanism: Controlled expansion of gaps during bending of a flexible conducting layer bonded to a brittle functional material allows filler material to be injected into the expanded gaps, which then forms electrodes when conductive material is applied to the exposed segments. The flexibility of the conducting layer enables curvature without fracturing the brittle material.
mechanism_raw: Controlled expansion of kerfs during bending of a flexible conducting sheet bonded to a piezo-ceramic plate allows filler material to be injected into the expanded gaps, which then forms electrodes when conductive material is applied to the exposed pegs. The flexibility of the conducting sheet enables curvature without fracturing the ceramic.

abstract: A system and method for providing autonomous and remote vehicle maintenance and repair. The system employs an on-board diagnosis and prognosis module that monitors one or more vehicle buses to identify trouble codes and other information indicating a vehicle problem. The on-board module causes a telematic device on the vehicle to broadcast a message including a problem code that identifies the problem the vehicle is having. A remote repair center may receive the message and may identify a software upgrade patch associated with the problem that can be transmitted to the vehicle to upgrade its software to correct the problem. Also, the message may be received by another vehicle that is part of a broadcast network that has previously received the software upgrade patch to fix a problem on that vehicle, where the receiving vehicle may transmit the software upgrade patch to the vehicle having the problem.
problem: Enabling autonomous vehicle maintenance and software updates without requiring manual intervention or centralized infrastructure.
constraint: Ensuring secure and accurate patch distribution across a decentralized network while preventing propagation of incorrect or malicious updates.
mechanism: A broadcast network allows nodes to share software patches peer-to-peer: a node with a problem broadcasts a diagnostic code, and another node that previously received a patch for the same issue retransmits the patch to the requesting node. This distributes updates across the network without relying solely on a central server.
mechanism_raw: A broadcast network allows vehicles to share software patches peer-to-peer: a vehicle with a problem broadcasts a diagnostic code, and another vehicle that previously received a patch for the same issue retransmits the patch to the requesting vehicle. This distributes updates across the network without relying solely on a central server.

abstract: The height adjustable toilet stand device provides for accommodating individuals of varying heights. Importantly, the housings are designed to fit typical toilet dimensions such that the front and back sides of the housing are substantially even with a front and back of a toilet. A user is thereby allowed feet placement adjacent to the toilet. In order for the device to correctly accommodate shorter statures, the bottom housing is ideally sunken within a given surface such that the toilet begins, without elevation, at a height even with the surface. The individual of greater stature has only to turn on the on/off and then use the up/down control to select a desired height for the toilet. This adjustable height feature is not only important for convenience but may be of key importance to anyone suffering from physical limitations.
reason: The patent describes a mechanical adjustment feature (height adjustment via on/off control and sunken housing) specific to toilet stands. While useful, it does not describe a generalizable causal mechanism for solving a broader class of problems beyond accommodating user height in sanitation fixtures.

abstract: An object of the present invention is to provide an inorganic board lighter in weight and excellent in strength and rigidity, and a method of producing the inorganic board. An inorganic board described in claim 1 for accomplishing the object comprises a hydraulic inorganic material, an inorganic lightweight material, a woody reinforcing material and a calcium silicate hydrate, wherein a ratio of the calcium silicate hydrate to the hydraulic inorganic material is 3-54 parts by mass: 100 parts by mass. Thus, by making an inorganic board, made of a hydraulic inorganic material, an inorganic lightweight material and a woody reinforcing material as main components, further contain a calcium silicate hydrate, an inorganic board which is lightweight and excellent in strength and rigidity can be obtained.
problem: Producing an inorganic board that is lightweight yet retains high strength and rigidity for construction or industrial applications.
constraint: Optimizing the ratio of calcium silicate hydrate to hydraulic inorganic material to balance lightweight properties with sufficient strength and rigidity.
mechanism: Combining a hydraulic inorganic material, inorganic lightweight material, and fibrous reinforcing material with a binding hydrate in a specific mass ratio creates a composite where the hydrate enhances binding and structural cohesion while the lightweight and fibrous components reduce density without sacrificing strength.
mechanism_raw: Combining a hydraulic inorganic material, inorganic lightweight material, and woody reinforcing material with a calcium silicate hydrate in a specific mass ratio (3-54 parts per 100 parts hydraulic material) creates a composite where the hydrate enhances binding and structural cohesion while the lightweight and woody components reduce density without sacrificing strength.
residual_terms: ["calcium silicate hydrate", "hydraulic inorganic material", "inorganic lightweight material", "woody reinforcing material", "mass ratio", "composite", "binding", "structural cohesion", "density", "strength"]

abstract: An authenticatable object comprises a surface having a latent hidden image embossed therein. The latent image is an encoded version of an authentication image and comprises a plurality of elements applied to the surface with a predetermined frequency. The latent hidden image is configured for optical decoding by a decoder having a decoder frequency corresponding to the predetermined frequency.
problem: Providing secure authentication of objects using a latent hidden image that is resistant to casual observation or replication.
constraint: Ensuring the predetermined frequency of the embossed elements is sufficiently precise to prevent accidental decoding by unauthorized devices while remaining compatible with the intended decoder.
mechanism: An encoded image is embossed onto a surface with elements applied at a predetermined frequency. A decoder with a matching frequency optically reconstructs the hidden image, enabling authentication. The encoding frequency acts as a key to unlock the latent image.
mechanism_raw: An encoded image is embossed onto a surface with elements applied at a predetermined frequency. A decoder with a matching frequency optically reconstructs the hidden image, enabling authentication. The encoding frequency acts as a key to unlock the latent image.

abstract: A system extends the high-frequency spectrum of a narrowband audio signal in the time domain. The system extends the harmonics of vowels by introducing a non linearity in a narrow band signal. Extended consonants are generated by a random-noise generator. The system differentiates the vowels from the consonants by exploiting predetermined features of a speech signal.
problem: Extending the high-frequency spectrum of a narrowband audio signal in the time domain, particularly for speech signals where different frequency content characteristics exist between vowels and consonants.
constraint: The classification must reliably distinguish vowels from consonants using predetermined features, and each processing technique (non-linearity for harmonic extension, noise generation for spectral extension) must be matched to the signal characteristics of the classified component to produce a coherent extended spectrum.
mechanism: A signal is analyzed to identify distinct component classes using predetermined features. A processing pathway is selected based on the classification, where each pathway applies a different spectral extension technique tailored to the characteristics of the identified component class, ensuring coherence between the original and extended spectrum.
mechanism_raw: The system classifies signal components (vowels vs consonants) by exploiting predetermined features of the speech signal, then applies different spectral extension techniques based on the classification: introducing a non-linearity to extend harmonics for vowels, and generating random noise to extend the spectrum for consonants. The classification step drives the selection of the appropriate processing path.

abstract: An apparatus and process for causing excess covering material at a workpiece corner to be gathered, folded and secured to a back side of the panel. A corner tucking apparatus includes a gathering plate positioned adjacent a positioning structure, and moves inwardly across the back side of the workpiece, from the corner, to gather and fold the corner flap. The gathering plate has a generally V-shaped notch which causes excess material to be gathered together as the plate moves inwardly. The gathered material upon reaching the apex of the notch is folded downwardly into contact with the back side of the workpiece. A securing structure which is carried inwardly with the gathering plate is then activated to fixedly secure the folded flap to the pad or workpiece.
problem: Gathering, folding, and securing excess covering material at a workpiece corner to create a clean, finished edge without loose flaps.
constraint: The V-notch geometry must be designed so that material gathering occurs progressively as the plate moves, and the apex must be positioned to create the fold at the correct location. The securing action must be timed to occur after the material has been fully gathered and folded, and the entire process must work with the specific material properties and thickness of the covering material.
mechanism: A shaped notch element moves progressively across a surface, causing excess material to accumulate as the element advances. When the accumulated material reaches a critical geometric point, it is redirected into a folded configuration. A fixing mechanism is then engaged to secure the folded material in place after the redirection is complete.
mechanism_raw: A gathering plate with a V-shaped notch moves inwardly across the back side of the workpiece from the corner. The V-notch geometry causes excess material to be gathered together as the plate advances. When the gathered material reaches the apex of the notch, it is folded downwardly into contact with the back side of the workpiece. A securing structure carried with the plate is then activated to fix the folded flap in place.

abstract: A saw blade protector for a cutting device having a table for placing thereon a workpiece, a saw blade protruding from an upper surface of the table, and a riving knife disposed in front of the saw blade in a moving direction of the workpiece for cutting the workpiece and positioned in line with the saw blade. The saw blade protector includes a guard plate constructed to cover the saw blade, a holding frame constructed to be mounted on an upper portion of the riving knife and to be able to support the guard plate, and an adjusting device constructed to be able to adjust a position of the holding frame relative to the upper surface of the table.
reason: The patent describes a component arrangement (guard plate, holding frame, adjusting device) mounted on a riving knife rather than a causal mechanism that produces a useful effect through a functional relationship. The solution is essentially mounting a guard on a nearby structure and providing manual adjustment, which is a straightforward mechanical mounting approach without a novel causal principle.

abstract: A flexure mount for economically producing pure translational motion with no arcuate or error motion in the vertical direction utilizing alignment pins and parts reducing structures including monolithic springs. A low profile embodiment utilizes a compound monolithic spring. The flexure mount may be used to translate a mirror or retroreflector in a purely linear direction of precisely controlled and known distance, useful in myriad interferometer applications including spectroscopy.
problem: Producing pure translational motion with no arcuate or error motion in the vertical direction, particularly for precision applications such as mirror or retroreflector positioning in interferometer systems.
constraint: The flexure geometry must be designed to allow motion in only the desired direction while constraining all other degrees of freedom, and the monolithic spring construction must be economical to produce while maintaining precise control over the translation distance and direction.
mechanism: Elastic elements with directional compliance are configured to permit displacement along a single axis while constraining motion in all other directions. Registration features ensure alignment of the displacement axis, and the elastic deformation of the elements eliminates parasitic motion during translation.
mechanism_raw: Alignment pins and monolithic spring structures (including compound monolithic springs) are used to constrain motion to a single linear direction. The flexure geometry of the monolithic springs allows elastic deformation in the desired direction while constraining all other degrees of freedom, eliminating arcuate and error motion. The alignment pins ensure proper registration and maintain the intended motion axis.

abstract: A flexure mount for economically producing pure translational motion with no arcuate or error motion in the vertical direction utilizing alignment pins and parts reducing structures including monolithic springs. A low profile embodiment utilizes a compound monolithic spring. The flexure mount may be used to translate a mirror or retroreflector in a purely linear direction of precisely controlled and known distance, useful in myriad interferometer applications including spectroscopy.
problem: Producing pure translational motion with no arcuate or error motion in the vertical direction, particularly for precision applications such as mirror or retroreflector positioning in interferometer systems.
constraint: The flexure geometry must be designed to allow motion in only the desired direction while constraining all other degrees of freedom, and the monolithic spring construction must be economical to produce while maintaining precise control over the translation distance and direction.
mechanism: Elastic elements with directional compliance are configured to permit displacement along a single axis while constraining motion in all other directions. Registration features ensure alignment of the displacement axis, and the elastic deformation of the elements eliminates parasitic motion during translation.

The alignment pins ensure proper registration and maintain the intended motion axis.

abstract: Ejector devices and systems are provided, that entrain ambient air within a primary stream of pressurized air, for use in a variety of applications including aircraft, buildings and other stationary structures. The ejector draws ambient air through an air treatment means such as a filter before its entrainment within the primary stream. The combined streams are then delivered to a ventilation system, an air curtain or other suitable recipient of treated, thermally conditioned air. The systems include diffusers, air curtain systems and variable air volume ventilation systems for aircraft and other vehicles.
problem: Need to entrain, treat, and deliver ambient air for ventilation systems without requiring separate treatment equipment or dedicated suction sources.
constraint: Must balance the pressure of the primary stream with the rate of ambient air entrainment while ensuring the ambient air passes through the treatment medium before mixing with the primary stream, and must maintain sufficient flow energy in the combined stream for downstream delivery.
mechanism: Using a pressurized primary fluid stream to generate a suction effect that draws ambient fluid through a treatment medium before entraining it within the primary stream, then delivering the combined treated and conditioned streams to a recipient, while balancing the pressure of the primary stream with the rate of ambient fluid entrainment and maintaining sufficient flow energy in the combined stream for downstream delivery.
mechanism_raw: Using a primary pressurized air stream to create a suction effect that draws ambient air through a treatment medium (such as a filter) before entraining it within the primary stream, then delivering the combined treated and thermally conditioned streams to a ventilation system, air curtain, or other recipient.

abstract: A pivoting, liquid cooled slag door for metallurgical furnaces is disclosed. The slag door can pivot from the top using one or more robust mechanisms that enable the door to be moved into and stopped in any position between a closed position and an open position. The slag door can also incorporate wing walls disposed in close proximity to the sides of the slag door. The wing walls can minimize air infiltration into the furnace when the slag door is in an open position. The slag door can be disposed in close proximity to the hearth of the furnace to eliminate problems associate with conventional slag door tunnels. The slag door can be fitted with a furnace apparatus such as a burner or a lance and can be used to provide access to the interior of the furnace and to control the flow of material out of the furnace.
problem: Need to control access to and material flow from a high-temperature metallurgical furnace while minimizing air infiltration and avoiding material buildup issues associated with conventional slag door tunnels.
constraint: Must pivot from the top using robust liquid-cooled mechanisms while maintaining variable positioning capability and minimizing air infiltration, all in a high-temperature environment.
mechanism: A pivoting barrier positioned close to a high-temperature processing zone with side walls disposed along its edges, allowing the barrier to be moved into and stopped at any position between closed and open states while the side walls minimize fluid infiltration into the processing zone when the barrier is open, and the close proximity to the processing zone eliminates tunnel-related problems.
mechanism_raw: A pivoting door positioned close to the furnace hearth with wing walls disposed along its sides, allowing the door to be moved into and stopped at any position between closed and open states while the wing walls minimize air infiltration into the furnace when the door is open, and the close proximity to the hearth eliminates tunnel-related problems.

abstract: A ball valve and ball valve actuator including a unique valve stem seal and mounting connection between the ball valve and actuator. The stem seal design reduces leakage issues and significantly lengthens the life span of the ball valve and actuator and the mounting connection between the actuator. The ball valve maintains the centrality of the valve stem in connection with the actuator pinion and minimizes torque and shear forces transferred to the valve stem and hence the stem seal itself.
problem: Leakage and premature wear in ball valve stem seals caused by misalignment and torque/shear forces transferred from the actuator to the valve stem.
constraint: Must reduce leakage and extend seal life while maintaining proper mechanical alignment between the valve stem and actuator pinion, and must minimize torque and shear forces without compromising the structural integrity of the connection.
mechanism: A seal and mounting connection design that maintains the alignment of a moving shaft with a driving element, thereby minimizing rotational and shear forces transferred to the shaft and hence to the seal itself, which reduces leakage and extends lifespan.
mechanism_raw: A valve stem seal and mounting connection design that maintains the centrality of the valve stem in connection with the actuator pinion, thereby minimizing torque and shear forces transferred to the valve stem and hence to the stem seal itself, which reduces leakage and extends lifespan.

abstract: A substrate processing apparatus that can reduce the number of parts. A first gas introduction hole through which the hydrogen fluoride gas is introduced into a GDP is formed in an upper lid. A second gas introduction hole through which hydrogen fluoride gas is introduced from a hydrogen fluoride gas source is formed in a processing vessel. When the upper lid engages the upper portion of the processing vessel, one end of the first gas introduction hole is joined with one end of the second gas introduction hole to form an introduction path through which the hydrogen fluoride gas is introduced into a chamber.
problem: Need to reduce the number of parts in a substrate processing apparatus while maintaining reliable introduction of process gas (hydrogen fluoride) into the processing chamber.
constraint: Must ensure precise alignment of the gas introduction holes when the parts are joined to form a continuous path, while reducing overall part count and maintaining gas-tight integrity at the mating interface.
mechanism: Forming a continuous fluid introduction path by aligning a fluid introduction port in an upper cover with a fluid introduction port in a processing vessel when the upper cover engages the upper portion of the processing vessel, thereby creating the introduction path through the mating interface itself and eliminating the need for separate connecting parts or intermediate fittings.
mechanism_raw: Forming a continuous gas introduction path by aligning a gas introduction hole in an upper lid with a gas introduction hole in a processing vessel when the upper lid engages the upper portion of the processing vessel, thereby creating the introduction path through the mating interface itself and eliminating the need for separate connecting parts or intermediate fittings.
residual_terms: ["fluid introduction path", "fluid introduction port", "upper cover", "processing vessel", "mating interface", "gas-tight integrity"]

abstract: A system for ultrasonic assisted electrical discharge machining of a component part having a longitudinal axis, a half wavelength resonant frequency along the longitudinal axis and an attachment portion, is provided. The system includes an ultrasonic horn having a longitudinal axis, a half wavelength resonant frequency along the longitudinal axis and an attachment portion. The half wavelength resonant frequency of the ultrasonic horn is the same as the half wavelength resonant frequency of the component part. Additionally, one of the attachment portion of the component part and the attachment portion of the ultrasonic horn is a male part and the other one of the attachment portion of the component part and the attachment portion of the ultrasonic horn is a female part sized and shaped to mate and engage one another when the component part and the ultrasonic horn are at generally the same temperature.
problem: Need to efficiently transfer ultrasonic energy to a component part for ultrasonic assisted electrical discharge machining without slippage, energy loss, or mechanical failure at the coupling interface.
constraint: Must match the half wavelength resonant frequencies of both the horn and component part, and the complementary attachment portions must be sized and shaped to engage reliably while accounting for thermal expansion differences between the two parts.
mechanism: Matching the half wavelength resonant frequency of an energy transmission element to that of a target component, and using complementary attachment portions on the transmission element and target component that mate and engage when both are at generally the same temperature, ensuring efficient energy transfer through resonant coupling and mechanical interlock.
mechanism_raw: Matching the half wavelength resonant frequency of the ultrasonic horn to that of the component part, and using complementary male/female attachment portions on the horn and component that mate and engage when both are at generally the same temperature, ensuring efficient energy transfer through resonant coupling and mechanical interlock.
residual_terms: ["half wavelength resonant frequency", "ultrasonic energy", "horn", "component part", "complementary attachment portions", "resonant coupling", "mechanical interlock", "thermal expansion"]

abstract: A radar system includes at least two modules, each having a phase detector and a first high-frequency source and each having an antenna output and/or each having one or more antennas. At least two modules include a device for synchronization between the first high-frequency source of a first module of the at least two modules and the first high-frequency source of a second module of the at least two modules of the radar system. The phase detector has a first input for a first reference signal. The phase detector also has a second input for a first loop signal. A module for a radar system has the design of one of the modules of the radar system described above.
problem: Maintaining phase coherence between multiple radar modules to ensure accurate detection and avoid signal interference.
constraint: Balancing synchronization accuracy with system complexity and cost, as additional synchronization hardware increases component count and potential failure points.
mechanism: Comparing reference and feedback signals to detect phase deviations, and dynamically aligning distributed signal sources through a coordination mechanism to maintain temporal coherence across the system.
mechanism_raw: Using phase detectors to compare reference and loop signals, combined with a synchronization device that aligns the high-frequency sources of separate modules, ensuring coherent operation across the distributed system.

abstract: A method for improving energy efficient operation of a vehicle includes monitoring vehicle operating characteristics, modeling operation of the vehicle by utilizing the vehicle operating characteristics to estimate energy consumption rates of the vehicle across an allowable vehicle operating range, and generating a control output to the vehicle on the basis of the energy consumption rates.
problem: Optimizing energy efficiency in vehicle operation across varying driving conditions and loads.
constraint: Ensuring model accuracy and responsiveness without excessive computational overhead, which could delay control decisions or require costly sensors.
mechanism: Continuously measuring operational parameters, constructing a predictive model of energy consumption across operating conditions, and adjusting system behavior through feedback control to minimize energy usage while maintaining performance.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring real-time vehicle operating characteristics, modeling energy consumption rates across the operating range, and generating control outputs that adjust vehicle behavior to minimize energy use based on the model.

abstract: A restoration process for restoring surface porosity defects on a component surface. The areas of a component surface having surface porosity defects are identified for restoration. The restoration surface is subsequently sprayed with a restoration spray to restore the surface porosity defects. The component surface is then finished to create a final component substantially free of surface porosity.
reason: The patent describes a specific restoration process for surface porosity defects using targeted spraying and finishing, but does not articulate a generalizable causal mechanism beyond the application-specific steps of defect identification, material application, and surface finishing.

abstract: A combustor housing includes an inlet cover plate having a central inlet configured to receive a supply of one of a high BTU content fuel or air and at least one radially-spaced, peripheral fuel inlet configured to receive a supply of a low BTU content fuel. It also includes an outlet cover plate having at least one radially-spaced, peripheral fuel outlet. The combustor housing also includes a peripheral sidewall joining the inlet cover and the outlet cover and enclosing a plenum, the at least one peripheral fuel inlet opening through the inlet cover plate into the plenum and the at least one fuel outlet opening from the plenum through the outlet cover plate. The central inlet opens into at least one conduit which extends away from the central inlet and opens into at least one high BTU content fuel conduit or air supply conduit that is axially aligned with the at least one fuel outlet.
problem: Efficiently combusting different BTU-content fuels in a single combustor while maintaining optimal mixing and combustion performance.
constraint: Maintaining uniform fuel-air mixing and combustion stability across varying fuel compositions while minimizing pressure losses in the plenum and conduits.
mechanism: Spatially partitioning input streams with distinct properties, routing them through dedicated pathways within a shared chamber, and aligning their distribution points to ensure controlled mixing prior to processing.
mechanism_raw: Spatially separating high-BTU fuel/air and low-BTU fuel inlets, routing them through dedicated conduits within a plenum, and aligning them with corresponding outlets to ensure proper distribution and mixing before combustion.

abstract: A lifting apparatus has a support structure, a frame pivotally connected to the support structure, an actuator connected to the frame so as to move the frame between a retracted position and an extended position, a lifting bar pivotally connected to the frame, and a linkage having one end pivotally connected to the support structure and an opposite end connected to the lifting bar. The lifting bar has a first strut with one end pivotally connected to the frame, a second strut with the one end pivotally affixed to the frame, and a cross member affixed adjacent to opposite ends of the first and second struts and extending thereacross. The linkage includes a first link and a second link.
problem: Achieving controlled, stable lifting motion with mechanical advantage using a compact and reliable linkage system.
constraint: Balancing mechanical advantage and load capacity against structural stability and the risk of binding or misalignment during extension and retraction cycles.
mechanism: A multi-bar linkage system where an actuator drives a frame connected to a load via articulated struts and cross members, transforming linear actuation into controlled rotational motion through coordinated pivot points.
mechanism_raw: A four-bar linkage system with an actuator driving a frame, which pivotally connects to a lifting bar via struts and cross members, converting linear actuator motion into controlled rotational lifting through coordinated pivot points.

abstract: A retrievable tool for steering through an earth formation includes a first tool assembly and a tilted antenna attached to the first tool assembly. The tool also includes a second tool assembly attached to the first tool assembly and a tilted antenna attached to the second tool assembly. The first tool assembly attaches to the second tool assembly so that the antennas are tilted in predetermined directions. The tilted antennas are transmitter antennas or receiver antennas. Each tool assembly is a tubular cylinder with a longitudinal axis running the length of the cylinder, wherein the tubular cylinder has two ends, each end including a rotational attachment mechanism. The tool assemblies attach to each other through their rotational attachment mechanisms. The rotational attachment mechanism may be a screw-on mechanism, press-fit mechanism, or welded mechanism.
problem: Achieving precise directional alignment of antennas in a downhole steering tool while maintaining mechanical reliability and retrievability.
constraint: The attachment mechanism must balance ease of assembly/retrieval with sufficient mechanical integrity to maintain antenna alignment under downhole stresses.
mechanism: Modular components connected through a rotational interface enable controlled angular orientation of directional elements relative to a primary axis. The rotational coupling allows discrete or continuous adjustment of orientation while maintaining mechanical integrity under operational stresses, ensuring alignment accuracy without continuous actuation.
mechanism_raw: Modular tool assemblies connected via rotational attachment mechanisms (e.g., screw-on, press-fit) allow independent tilting of antennas in predetermined directions. The rotational interface enables controlled angular orientation of each antenna relative to the tool's longitudinal axis, ensuring directional accuracy during operation.

abstract: Bulk storage of natural gas or methane is facilitated by absorbing and storing the gas in a liquefied medium through the interaction of moderate pressure, low temperature and a solvent medium. Systems and processes are provided that facilitate the absorption of natural gas or methane into a liquid or liquid vapor medium for storage and transport, and back into a gas for delivery to market. In a preferred embodiment, the absorptive properties of ethane, propane and butane under moderate conditions of temperature and pressure (associated with a novel mixing process) are utilized to store natural gas or methane at more efficient levels of compressed volume ratio than are attainable with natural gas alone under similar holding conditions. The preferred mixing process efficiently combines natural gas or methane with a solvent medium such as liquid ethane, propane, butane, or other suitable fluid, to form a concentrated liquid or liquid vapor mixture suited for storage and transport. The solvent medium is preferably recycled in the conveyance vessel on unloading of the natural gas.
problem: Efficiently storing and transporting natural gas at scale without requiring extreme pressures or cryogenic temperatures.
constraint: The solvent must exhibit sufficient absorptive capacity and selectivity for natural gas while remaining stable and recyclable under operational conditions.
mechanism: A reversible absorption medium selectively captures and releases a target substance under moderate conditions, forming a concentrated mixture during capture and enabling recovery of the substance during release. The medium is regenerated after release, allowing repeated cycles of absorption and desorption with improved volumetric efficiency compared to direct storage of the substance.
mechanism_raw: A solvent medium (e.g., ethane, propane) absorbs natural gas under moderate temperature and pressure, forming a concentrated liquid mixture. The solvent is recycled after gas release, enabling reversible storage and transport with higher volumetric efficiency than compressed gas alone.

abstract: Disclosed is a compound represented by the following Formula 1:The compound exhibits improved solubility and thermal stability in an organic light emitting device. An organic light emitting device including the compound, improves the driving voltage, the emission efficiency, and the color purity of an organic light emitting display.
problem: Improving solubility and thermal stability of compounds used in organic light-emitting devices (OLEDs) to enhance performance metrics like driving voltage and emission efficiency.
constraint: The molecular design must simultaneously optimize solubility, thermal stability, and electronic properties without introducing defects or inefficiencies in the device.
mechanism: A molecularly engineered compound balances competing physical and electronic properties through structural optimization. The design enables uniform deposition of the compound into thin films while resisting thermal degradation, ensuring stable performance in optoelectronic applications without introducing defects.
mechanism_raw: A chemically designed compound with a specific molecular structure (Formula 1) balances solubility in organic solvents and resistance to thermal degradation. This structural optimization enables uniform thin-film formation and stable operation in OLEDs.

abstract: The Field Testing Instrument (FTI) is designed for use in the regular maintenance and installation of airport Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI). The FTI is a self-contained and portable instrument that accurately measures the most important PAPI parameters, such as vertical aiming angle, transition angle, and light intensity. In addition to working with the current incandescent PAPIs, the FTI also measures parameters specific to the next generation LED PAPI. The FTI uses modern, efficient technology to reduce the life-cycle cost of approach lighting systems. The FTI improves on traditional PAPI testing methods by directly measuring the PAPI light beam focused to a target plate, as if seen from the pilot perspective. Due to significantly improvements in measurement accuracy and reliability, the FTI may supplement and even replace costly flight checks for PAPI maintenance with ground based operation.
problem: Accurately measuring critical parameters of airport lighting systems (e.g., PAPI) from the pilot's perspective without requiring costly flight-based checks.
constraint: The instrument must maintain measurement accuracy across varying environmental conditions while remaining compact and self-contained for field use.
mechanism: A portable measurement device replicates the optical path and angular relationships experienced by an observer by directly capturing projected radiation onto a reference surface. This ground-based approach simulates the observer's perspective, enabling accurate assessment of system performance without requiring the observer to occupy the original vantage point.
mechanism_raw: A portable instrument directly measures the light beam projected by the PAPI system onto a target plate, simulating the pilot's viewpoint. This ground-based approach replicates the optical path and angular relationships experienced during actual flight.

abstract: A modular, stackable, geothermal block system for use as a subterranean or submarine heat exchanger in a geothermal energy system which provides a heating/cooling means to an external load. The stackable blocks, which can be filled with a fluid and/or material of generally high heat retention characteristics or precast in such material, contain one or more continuous passageways that extend from the top face of the block through the opposing face, through which a rigid structural heat exchange tube, fabricated from material of high thermal conductivity, is placed. The blocks are stacked one upon another and slidably mounted on the tube(s). Each tube contains a helically wound, thermal transfer tubing comprising one leg of a U-shape configured loop. Each stackable block can contain multiple paired passageways permitting more than one U-shape loop within the system.
problem: Creating a scalable, modular heat exchanger for geothermal systems that maintains thermal efficiency and structural integrity when stacked.
constraint: The block design must balance thermal conductivity of the material with structural strength to support stacking without compromising heat transfer efficiency.
mechanism: Interconnected modular units with aligned internal channels allow thermal transfer elements to pass through multiple layers while maintaining direct thermal contact with a surrounding medium. The modular stacking enables scalable expansion, with each unit contributing to heat exchange efficiency through continuous pathways and structural support.
mechanism_raw: Stackable blocks with continuous passageways allow rigid heat exchange tubes to be slidably mounted through multiple layers. Each block contains paired passageways for U-shaped loops, enabling modular expansion while ensuring direct thermal contact between the tubes and the surrounding medium.

abstract: Presented is a system and method for disconnecting a plurality of wireline tools from a string of wireline tools while maintaining operation of the wireline tools remaining with the string of wireline tools. The disconnection is non-destructive and allows a reconnection of the disconnected tools after retrieval from the well. The system also enables testing of the disconnection mechanism before deploying the wireline tool string into the well.
problem: Need to selectively disconnect specific tools from a connected wireline tool string during well operations while keeping the remaining tools operational, without permanent damage, and with the ability to reconnect and verify functionality before deployment.
constraint: The disconnection must be non-destructive to permit reconnection, must not interrupt operation of the remaining tools in the string, and must be verifiable before deployment to avoid in-well failure.
mechanism: A selective coupling system enables individual components to be detached from an interconnected assembly without disrupting the operational continuity of remaining components. The coupling releases on command through a non-destructive mechanism, preserving both sides for post-retrieval reconnection. A pre-deployment validation interface confirms the release and reconnection capability before the assembly is committed to its operational environment.
mechanism_raw: A non-destructive coupling mechanism that allows individual tools to be selectively separated from a connected string while maintaining mechanical and operational continuity of the remaining tools. The coupling is designed to release on command without damaging either side, enabling post-retrieval reconnection. A pre-deployment test interface validates the release and reconnection function before the tool string enters the well.

abstract: There is provided a display apparatus configured by stacking a drive circuit substrate and a light-emitting substrate. Electrodes of the substrates are accurately aligned to be electrically connected to each other. A display apparatus is configured by stacking a drive circuit substrate having a drive circuit and a light-emitting substrate having a light-emitting unit including a pixel electrode to cause the drive circuit substrate and the light-emitting substrate to face each other, wherein on a stacked plane between the drive circuit substrate and the light-emitting substrate, an intermediate electrode connected to the light-emitting unit of the light-emitting substrate and a connection electrode connected to the drive circuit and the drive circuit substrate are electrically connected to each other, and the intermediate electrode is elongated in a direction parallel to or perpendicular to a longitudinal direction of the pixel electrode on the stacked plane.
problem: Need to establish reliable electrical connections between two stacked substrates (drive circuit and light-emitting) when precise lateral alignment between their electrodes cannot be guaranteed during assembly.
constraint: The elongated electrode must maintain electrical continuity across the stacked interface while accommodating manufacturing alignment variations, without introducing shorts or signal degradation in the display.
mechanism: An intermediate conductive element is positioned at the interface between two stacked substrates, elongated along an axis to create a tolerant overlap region. This element bridges the gap between connection points on opposing substrates, converting strict lateral alignment requirements into relaxed overlap tolerances while maintaining electrical continuity across the interface.
mechanism_raw: An intermediate electrode layer is placed on the stacked interface plane, elongated in a direction parallel or perpendicular to the pixel electrode axis. This elongated intermediate electrode acts as a tolerant bridge that can make electrical contact with both the connection electrode on the drive circuit substrate and the light-emitting unit on the light-emitting substrate over a range of lateral misalignment, converting a tight alignment tolerance into a relaxed overlap tolerance.

abstract: The inventions herein relate to novel forms of interaction with an electronic system, such as for games of chance, games of skill, and combinations thereof. In certain embodiments, the existing lottery infrastructure is used in conjunction with electronic remote game play. A system is provided for effecting defined game play and prizing structure parameters in an electronic entertainment environment. The system may include an input for receiving the parameters, a memory coupled to the input for storing the parameters, a processing system coupled to the storage or generating game play to effect the defined parameters, storage for recording information regarding particular game play events and an interface for at least presenting game play events to users of the electronic entertainment system.
reason: The abstract describes a configurable gaming system architecture (input → memory → processing → recording → interface) but does not disclose a specific causal mechanism that solves a technical problem. It is a list of functional components for parameter-driven game generation rather than an underlying engineering or scientific principle that can be transferred to another field.

abstract: The present invention relates to methods for removing or preventing scale formation in a liquid food processing operation. The present invention also relates to methods and compositions for increasing the solubility of insoluble calcium salts in an acidic environment. Aqueous antiscalant solutions comprising soluble magnesium salts are used to prevent the precipitation of insoluble calcium salts and/or to increase the solubility of insoluble calcium salts.
problem: Need to prevent precipitation of insoluble calcium salts (scale formation) in liquid food processing operations and to increase the solubility of already-precipitated insoluble calcium salts in acidic environments.
constraint: The antiscalant must be food-safe, effective at the operating pH and temperature of food processing, and must not introduce off-flavors or contaminate the final food product.
mechanism: A soluble ionic species is introduced into an aqueous system to competitively interact with a target precipitating ion, shifting the solubility equilibrium away from insoluble salt formation. In acidic conditions, the introduced species further destabilizes existing precipitates through ion-exchange or complexation, increasing their solubility and preventing accumulation.
mechanism_raw: Soluble magnesium salts are introduced into the aqueous processing solution. The magnesium ions compete with or sequester calcium ions, shifting the solubility equilibrium away from insoluble calcium salt precipitation. In acidic environments, the magnesium salts further increase solubility of existing insoluble calcium salts, likely through ion-exchange or complexation mechanisms that destabilize the calcium precipitate structure.

abstract: A biochemical chip in which at least the inner surface of a flow path is covered with a chemisorption monomolecular film having arbitrary surface energy, and the method includes: a step for pre-forming a chemisorption monomolecular film having arbitrary surface energy on the inner surfaces of flow path parts of first and second members which are processed to have flow paths; and a step for facing and bonding the first and second members.
problem: Need to create a biochemical chip with precisely controlled surface energy on the inner surfaces of microfluidic flow paths, where the surface properties must be established before final assembly of the chip.
constraint: The chemisorption film must be stable during the facing and bonding process, must not interfere with the bond quality, and must provide the desired surface energy uniformly across the internal flow path after assembly.
mechanism: A surface-modifying film is pre-formed on internal surfaces of separate substrate components before assembly. The components are then joined through a facing and bonding process, with the pre-formed films becoming the final internal surface. This decouples surface property engineering from the assembly process, allowing independent optimization of each step.
mechanism_raw: A chemisorption monomolecular film with arbitrary surface energy is pre-formed on the inner surfaces of flow path parts of separate substrate members before they are assembled. The two members are then faced and bonded together, with the pre-formed films becoming the internal surface of the final flow path. This decouples surface property engineering from the bonding/assembly step, allowing each to be optimized independently.

abstract: Novel 5-azaindole bisphosphonate compounds are disclosed, as well as methods of preparing the compounds, pharmaceutical compositions including the compounds, and administration of the compounds in methods of treating abnormal calcium and phosphate metabolism, including bone and joint diseases and other disorders.
reason: The patent describes a specific chemical compound (5-azaindole bisphosphonate) for treating metabolic disorders. While the compound's structure may interact with biological pathways, the abstract does not explain a generalizable causal mechanism beyond the compound's direct application. The focus is on the chemical entity itself rather than a transferable functional principle.

abstract: The present invention is directed to perform fine low-voltage control without largely increasing the circuit layout area in a low-power consumption structure. In the case of shifting a region to a low-speed mode, a system controller outputs a request signal and an enable signal to a power switch controller and a low-power drive circuit, respectively, to turn off a power switch and to perform a control so that the voltage level of a virtual reference potential becomes about 0.2 V to about 0.3V. The region operates on voltages between a power supply voltage and a virtual reference potential, so that it is controlled in the low-speed mode.
problem: Performing fine low-voltage control in a low-power circuit without significantly increasing the circuit layout area.
constraint: Balancing low-power consumption with minimal circuit layout area expansion, requiring precise voltage adjustment without additional hardware overhead.
mechanism: Adjusting an operational region to a reduced-power state by selectively disabling a power delivery path and establishing a controlled intermediate voltage potential. The region operates between a primary supply voltage and this intermediate potential, enabling voltage scaling for low-power operation while preserving control precision through regulated potential adjustment.
mechanism_raw: Shifting a region to a low-speed mode by turning off a power switch and adjusting a virtual reference potential to a controlled intermediate voltage (e.g., 0.2–0.3V). The region operates between the power supply voltage and this virtual reference, enabling voltage scaling for low-power operation while maintaining control precision.
residual_terms: ["power delivery path", "intermediate voltage potential", "voltage scaling", "regulated potential adjustment"]

abstract: A liquid crystal display (LCD) is provided that comprises a rearward LCD substrate sheet that has an array of vias formed, where the vias provide electrical conduction between both sides of the rearward LCD substrate sheet. The number of vias in the array is substantially equal to or at least equivalent to a combination of a number of column drive lines and a number of row drive lines. The respective drive lines are connected to a corresponding via, such as on one side of the rearward LCD substrate sheet, and respective patterned conductors are connected to a corresponding via, such as on the other side of the rearward LCD substrate sheet. The patterned conductors provide a connection between respective drive lines and one or more corresponding drivers. In one example, this allows a “full bleed” display to be generated.
problem: Enabling a 'full bleed' display in an LCD while efficiently routing signals between drive lines and drivers without increasing substrate complexity.
constraint: Matching via count to the total number of drive lines to ensure full signal connectivity while maintaining substrate simplicity and minimizing layout area.
mechanism: Deploying a conductive via array in a substrate layer, where the via count matches the total number of signal lines requiring inter-layer connectivity. Each via directly links a signal line on one substrate side to a corresponding conductor pattern on the opposite side, enabling full signal routing without additional routing layers or substrate complexity.
mechanism_raw: Using an array of vias in the rearward LCD substrate, with the number of vias matching the combined count of column and row drive lines. Each via connects a drive line on one side to a patterned conductor on the other side, enabling direct signal routing between drivers and drive lines without additional routing layers.

abstract: A bearing remover is configured to cooperate with a puller to remove a bearing from an axle. The bearing remover includes a claw that has an opening to receive a portion of the axle, and a lip that can be inserted between the bearing and the wall. The bearing remover also includes a centering component that fits about the axle. The claw and centering component are mechanically coupled to assist in maintaining the claw about the bearing, and to transmit a force to the claw.
problem: Removing a bearing from an axle using a puller while maintaining alignment and force transmission to the bearing.
constraint: Maintaining precise alignment of the claw relative to the bearing and axle during force application to avoid misalignment or damage.
mechanism: Mechanically coupling a force-applying tool (with a shaped aperture for an axle and a protrusion for insertion between a target component and a surface) to an alignment-maintaining interface that engages the axle. The coupling ensures the tool remains coaxially aligned with the target component during force transmission, enabling controlled removal while preventing misalignment-induced damage.
mechanism_raw: Mechanically coupling a claw (with an opening for the axle and a lip to insert between the bearing and wall) to a centering component that fits about the axle. The coupling ensures the claw remains aligned around the bearing while transmitting force from the puller to the claw, enabling controlled removal.

abstract: A cover for an anchor, particularly a fluke-type boat anchor is constructed of a cover material of a resilient rubber that includes an elongated section and side wings. An elongated opening and closing member, such as a zipper, enables the cover to be opened and closed for receipt of the anchor therein.
reason: The patent describes a protective cover for an anchor using a zipper and resilient rubber material. While the zipper enables opening/closing, the mechanism is a standard component (zipper) combined with material properties (resilience) for a specific product. There is no generalizable causal principle beyond the product's design.

abstract: A method and a device for mapping Ethernet code blocks to an optical transport network (OTN) for transmission are provided. In the method, 10G Ethernet code blocks are mapped to an OTN frame corresponding to an optical channel payload unit 2 (OPU2) as a bit stream within a justification range according to an asynchronous bit-stream mapping manner, an identifier for indicating the asynchronous bit-stream mapping manner is set at an overhead (OH) portion of the OTN frame, an offset of a certain code block in the bit stream relative to a certain position of the OTN frame is recorded, and an indicator for indicating the offset position is set. Thus, specific solutions for mapping 10G Ethernet code blocks having an encoding rate lower than a minimum payload bandwidth of the OPU2 to the OTN for transmission is provided without changing the mature OTN architecture.
problem: Mapping variable-rate data (e.g., 10G Ethernet) into a fixed-bandwidth transport structure (OTN OPU2) without altering the existing architecture.
constraint: Maintaining compatibility with the mature OTN architecture while accommodating data rates below the minimum payload bandwidth of the target frame.
mechanism: Asynchronously mapping a variable-rate data stream into a fixed-capacity frame structure by using a justification range to dynamically align the data within the frame, recording offset information to track alignment, and embedding overhead identifiers to preserve compatibility with the existing frame architecture.
mechanism_raw: Asynchronous bit-stream mapping with justification range utilization, overhead identifiers, and offset recording to dynamically align data within a fixed frame structure while preserving architectural compatibility.
residual_terms: ["justification range", "overhead identifiers", "offset recording", "fixed-bandwidth transport structure", "OTN OPU2", "10G Ethernet"]

abstract: A linear guiding mechanism includes a fixed member, a moving member, a first double parallel leaf spring mechanism and a second double parallel leaf spring mechanism arranged between the fixed member and the moving member and configured to movably support the moving member. The first double parallel leaf spring mechanism and the second double parallel leaf spring mechanism are arranged at an angle other than 180° (for example, 90°) about an axis of movement of the moving member.
problem: Providing precise linear motion while constraining movement to a single axis and allowing angular flexibility in the guiding system.
constraint: Balancing structural rigidity for linear guidance with the need to accommodate angular misalignment or external forces without compromising motion precision.
