mechanism: Using two pairs of compliant leaf elements arranged at a non-collinear angle relative to the desired motion axis, where coordinated deflection of the leaf elements enables controlled single-axis translation while accommodating angular misalignment through elastic deformation.
mechanism_raw: Two double parallel leaf spring mechanisms arranged at a non-180° angle relative to the movement axis, enabling controlled linear motion through coordinated spring deflection and angular orientation.

abstract: This invention relates generally to footwear with a shoe sole, including at least one insertable midsole orthotic. The insertable midsole orthotic is removably inserted within the shoe upper, the sides of which hold it in position. The shoe sole includes a concavely rounded side or underneath portion, which may be formed in part by the insertable midsole orthotic. The insertable midsole orthotic may extend the length of the shoe sole or may form only a part of the shoe sole and can incorporate cushioning or structural compartments or components. The insertable midsole orthotic permits replacement of midsole material which has degraded or has worn out in order to maintain optimal characteristics of the shoe sole and allows customization for the individual wearer to provide tailored cushioning or support characteristics for the purpose of orthopedic, podiatric, corrective, prescriptive, therapeutic and/or prosthetic purposes.
reason: The invention primarily describes a product feature (removable orthotic) rather than a causal mechanism. The 'insertable midsole' is a component-level solution for customization/replacement, not a functional principle that transfers to other domains.

abstract: A ram-air duct includes a ram-air inlet duct and a ram-air outlet duct arranged downstream of the ram-air inlet duct and in fluid communication with the ram-air inlet duct. At an inlet of the ram-air inlet duct, a first movable element is arranged and adapted to set an inlet parameter of the inlet. At an outlet of the ram-air outlet duct, a second movable element is arranged and adapted to set an outlet parameter of the outlet. The outlet parameter and the inlet parameter are linked together by a function, so that an outlet parameter corresponding to a value of the function is assigned to each inlet parameter. A controller implements the control function by actuating movements of the first and second movable elements.
problem: Coordinating inlet and outlet parameters in a fluid system to optimize performance under varying conditions.
constraint: Maintaining a functional relationship between inlet and outlet parameters to ensure system stability and efficiency while adapting to dynamic environmental or operational demands.
mechanism: Establishing a functional dependency between inlet and outlet parameters by linking their respective movable elements through a control function that maps each inlet parameter to a corresponding outlet parameter, enabling coordinated adjustment via a controller to maintain system stability under varying conditions.
mechanism_raw: Linking inlet and outlet movable elements via a control function that assigns corresponding outlet parameters to each inlet parameter, enabling coordinated adjustment through a controller.

abstract: A wave energy converting apparatus 44 and its associated tension mooring system 50 is described. The wave energy converting apparatus 44 comprises an elongate support structure 45 designed to extend above a mean water level in the ocean. The support structure 45 has a submerged member 46 provided in connection therewith below the mean water level. A float member 48 of positive buoyancy is slidably mounted on the support structure 45 so as to be movable in a vertical direction. The apparatus 44 also comprises a linear electric generator 49 having a stator provided in connection with the support structure 45 and a translator integrated into the body of the float member 48. Differential motion of the float member 48 relative to the support structure 45 results in the generation of electrical power by the linear electric generator 49. The tension mooring system 50 comprises a cable 51 extending from a ballast means 52 to a counterbalancing means 53 adapted to be suspended from the submerged member 46 via a pulley mechanism 54. The tension mooring system 50 allows the apparatus 44 to be “tuned” to the prevailing ocean conditions.
problem: Converting oscillatory wave motion into electrical energy while adapting to varying ocean conditions.
constraint: Balancing energy capture efficiency with structural resilience by allowing real-time tuning of mooring tension to match prevailing wave dynamics.
mechanism: Converting oscillatory mechanical motion into electrical energy using a linear generator driven by a buoyant element, while dynamically adjusting the tension of a mooring system through a pulley and counterweight arrangement to tune the apparatus to prevailing wave conditions.
mechanism_raw: A float-driven linear generator combined with a tension mooring system using a pulley and counterweight to dynamically adjust the apparatus' tension and tuning based on wave conditions.

abstract: The present invention provides a low frequency acoustic transducer for non-destructive testing of a test structure. The transducer is arranged for conversion between electrical energy and acoustic energy associated with an acoustic wave propagating through a portion of the test structure. The transducer comprises a bending actuator for generating the acoustic wave by generating a vibration from an electrical signal or for generating an electrical signal from a vibration generated by the received acoustic wave. The bending actuator has a vibration surface and a contact area surrounded by a portion of the vibration surface. The transducer further comprises a mode setting member that has a rigid portion which is in direct mechanical contact with the bending actuator at the contact area such that, within the contact area, an amplitude of the vibration is substantially suppressed. The location and shape of the contact area determine a bending mode associated with a resonance frequency of the bending actuator.
problem: Controlling the resonance frequency of a bending actuator in an acoustic transducer for non-destructive testing.
constraint: The contact area's position and geometry must be precisely defined to achieve the desired bending mode without compromising the actuator's overall structural integrity or vibration generation capability.
mechanism: A mode-setting element is placed in direct mechanical contact with a flexible actuator at a defined contact region, suppressing vibration amplitude within that region. The location and geometry of the contact region determine the bending mode and associated resonance frequency of the actuator.
mechanism_raw: A rigid mode-setting member is placed in direct mechanical contact with the bending actuator at a specific contact area, suppressing vibration amplitude within that area. The location and shape of the contact area determine the bending mode and associated resonance frequency of the actuator.

abstract: Pyrotechnic priming charge (1) intended to be used preferably for starting up one or more ignition chains, comprising a coherent porous fuel structure (2) and at least one oxidizer (4). According to the invention, the primer also comprises a moisture inhibitor (5) applied to the surface of the primer with a view to increasing the safety of the primer and reducing the risk of unintentional ignition due to breakdown of the oxidizer under the influence of ambient moisture and temperature.
reason: The patent describes a material application (moisture inhibitor) to prevent chemical breakdown, not a functional mechanism that can be abstracted to other fields.

abstract: A target parking position setting section (23) is adapted to temporarily set a target parking position (p31, p32, p33) for the vehicle for each parking mode in a predetermined stop position. A parking mode determining section (25) is adapted to determine the parking mode and the target parking position corresponding to the parking mode based on an operation of a steering wheel performed by a driver after the target parking position (p31, p32, p33) is set. A guiding section (29) is adapted to guide the vehicle (1) to the determined target parking position (P3).
problem: Guiding a vehicle to a target parking position based on driver steering input while adapting to different parking modes.
constraint: The system must interpret driver steering inputs in real-time to dynamically select the appropriate parking mode and target position without prior knowledge of the specific parking scenario.
mechanism: A target position is temporarily assigned for each operational mode. The system determines the operational mode and corresponding target position based on real-time steering inputs from the operator after the target is assigned. A guidance section then directs the vehicle to the determined target position.
mechanism_raw: A target parking position is temporarily set for each parking mode. The system determines the parking mode and corresponding target position based on real-time steering wheel operations performed by the driver after the target is set. A guiding section then directs the vehicle to the determined target position.

abstract: A magnetic element and its manufacturing method are provided. A magnetic element includes an actuation part having a first surface and a second surface, a torsion bar connected to the actuation part, and a frame connected to the first torsion bar, wherein the first surface of the actuation part is an uneven surface. The manufacturing method of the magnetic element starts with forming an passivation layer on a substrate and defining a special area by the mask method, then continues with forming the adhesion layer and electroplate-initializing layer on the substrate sequentially. The photoresist layer are formed and the magnetic-inductive material is electroformed on the electroplate area. Finally, the substrate is etched and the passivation layer is removed to obtain the magnetic element. The manufacturing method of magnetic element of the present invention can be applied in the microelectromechanical system field and other categories.
reason: The patent focuses on a specific manufacturing process for a magnetic element with an uneven surface, which is a material/structural design rather than a transferable functional mechanism.

abstract: A method of making a phosphono-substituted dipyrromethane comprises reacting an aldehyde or acetal having at least one phosphono group substituted thereon with pyrrole to produce a phosphono-substituted dipyrromethane; and wherein the phosphono is selected from the group consisting of dialkyl phosphono, diaryl phosphono, and dialkylaryl phosphono. Additional methods, intermediates and products are also described.
reason: The patent describes a chemical synthesis method for a specific compound, which is a domain-specific process rather than a generalizable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A high-precision distance measuring with a reduced error in a distance measuring system which calculates a distance from an arrival time of each pulse signal constituting a pulse sequence is provided. For an oscillator which generates pulse signals by counting the number of pulse signals constituting a received pulse sequence, a relative time difference between a transmitting device and a return device is acquired, a distance from the transmitting device to the return device is calculated, and the calculated distance is corrected based on the calculated relative time difference.
problem: Reducing error in distance measurement caused by timing offsets between a transmitting device and a return/receiving device in a pulse-based distance measuring system.
constraint: Balancing measurement precision against the need to account for and compensate timing offsets between separate devices without introducing additional measurement complexity.
mechanism: Measuring a timing offset between a signal transmission and its reception, deriving an initial distance estimate from the signal propagation time, and then adjusting that estimate by applying the measured timing offset as a corrective calibration value to reduce measurement error.
mechanism_raw: Acquiring a relative time difference between the transmitting and return devices, calculating a distance from pulse arrival times, and then correcting that calculated distance using the measured relative time difference as a calibration offset.
residual_terms: ["timing offset", "distance estimate", "signal propagation time", "corrective calibration value"]

abstract: A wearable containing element for an electronic apparatus, comparable to an ornament or pendant, comprising at least a pair of complementary shells, able to be coupled with each other so as to define a containing body with an external surface having a shape and size comparable to those of a traditional ornament, and an internal containing compartment, of a shape and size sufficiently large to house the electronic apparatus.
reason: The patent describes a static shell structure with complementary halves that couple to form a wearable ornament-like housing. There is no causal problem-solving mechanism—only a form-factor design using two shells to disguise an electronic device as jewelry.

abstract: Methods for loading a compressed fluid, such as natural gas, into and discharging the compressed fluid out of containment are provided. The compressed fluid is injected into a bottom portion of a container system for storage and/or transport until a target pressure is reached after which gas is withdrawn from an upper portion of the container system at a rate to maintain the target pressure while the compressed fluid is injected in the bottom portion. The compressed fluid is cooled through an expansion valve and by refrigerated chillers or by injecting a cold liquid of the same chemical composition as the compressed fluid, such as liquid natural gas, into the compressed fluid prior to injection into the container system. Withdrawal or discharge from the container system to a receiving facility begins with blow down from the bottom portion of the container system without a displacement fluid and continues until pressure falls below an acceptable differential pressure. The discharge stream is passed through a separator and a light gas from the separator is pressurized and injected into an upper portion of the container system to drive the compressed fluid out the bottom. The light gas is pressurized using either a compressor or a heated tank system, where two vessels operate in parallel, trapping and heating the light gas and then discharging to the container system from one while filling the other and alternating the operation between the two.
problem: Efficiently and continuously loading compressed fluid into and discharging it from a container system while maintaining target pressure and managing thermal effects.
constraint: Maintaining acceptable pressure differentials and continuous flow while cycling between parallel vessels, each of which must transition between filling/heating and discharging states.
mechanism: Operating two vessels in parallel with alternating roles—one vessel captures and pressurizes a compressible medium while the other releases it to maintain continuous flow and pressure in a target system, then switching their functions so that discharge remains uninterrupted during transitions.
mechanism_raw: Using two vessels operating in parallel in an alternating cycle—one vessel traps and pressurizes/heats a light gas while the other discharges the gas into the container system to drive fluid out, then switching roles so that continuous discharge is maintained without interruption.

abstract: Several implementations of a fan folding mechanism for folding flaps of a case into a fan fold arrangement are disclosed and described. In one implementation, the fan folding mechanism comprises four shoes, arranged to allow one shoe to contact a flap on each of four sides of the case. A finger, carried by each of the four shoes is configured for movement between a retracted position and an extended position, such that in the retracted position, each finger is in contact with a leading corner of a different flap of the case and the flaps are in an open position and in the extended position, each finger is in contact with the same leading corner of the same flap, and the flap is in the closed position. Four suction cups, each configured for releasable attachment to a trailing corner of a flap, may inhibit contention between flaps.
problem: Folding multiple flaps of a case into a fan fold arrangement simultaneously without contention or interference between the flaps during the folding operation.
constraint: Coordinating the simultaneous manipulation of multiple flaps at their leading and trailing corners to achieve synchronized folding while preventing mechanical interference between adjacent flaps.
mechanism: Simultaneously actuating multiple movable elements positioned along opposing sides of a flexible structure, where each element selectively engages a leading edge to either retain or fold a segment, while auxiliary retention elements engage trailing edges to prevent mutual interference during coordinated folding.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated movement of multiple fingers carried by shoes on each side of the case, where each finger transitions between a retracted position (contacting a leading corner to hold flaps open) and an extended position (contacting the same leading corner to fold the flap closed), combined with suction cups that releasably attach to trailing corners to inhibit contention between flaps.

abstract: A method of producing methane, an organic based fertilizer and usable water from animal waste includes the step of separating the animal waste into liquid waste and solid waste. The solid waste is subjected to anaerobic digestion to produce methane and a wet by-product. The wet by-product is pressed to into a filter cake which is pelletized into the organic based fertilizer. The liquid waste is clarified to produce a supernatant and a sludge which is pressed into a filter cake together with the wet by-product. Ammonia is extracted from the supernatant to produce ammonium sulfate and an aqueous solution. The aqueous solution is filtered to produce a concentrate and water filtrate. The water filtrate may be used as drinking or washing water. The ammonium sulfate and concentrate may be used to supplement to the solid waste which is pelletized into the organic based fertilizer. In alternative embodiments a portion of the supernatant and aqueous solution may be used as a liquid fertilizer.
problem: Producing methane, organic fertilizer, and usable water from animal waste while maximizing resource recovery from all waste streams.
constraint: Managing multiple parallel and sequential processing streams (digestion, pressing, pelletizing, clarification, ammonia extraction, filtration) while ensuring that byproducts from one process are effectively reintegrated into another to maximize overall resource recovery.
mechanism: Separating input material into liquid and solid fractions, subjecting each fraction to distinct processing stages (biological decomposition, mechanical dewatering, chemical extraction, and solidification), and reintegrating byproducts from each stage back into other stages to maximize recovery of usable outputs including fuel gas, nutrient-rich solids, and purified water.
mechanism_raw: Cascading separation and processing of animal waste into liquid and solid streams, where solid waste undergoes anaerobic digestion and liquid waste is clarified, with byproducts from each stream (wet digestion residue, sludge, extracted ammonium sulfate, concentrate) being pressed, pelletized, or recycled back into the fertilizer production stream, and filtrate water being recovered as a usable product.
residual_terms: ["liquid and solid fractions", "biological decomposition", "mechanical dewatering", "chemical extraction", "solidification", "byproducts", "recovery", "fuel gas", "nutrient-rich solids", "purified water"]

abstract: Gas-solids separator comprises a tubular housing, an inlet for introducing a gas-solids mixture at one end of said housing, which inlet is executed such that it imparts a swirl to the gas-solids mixture, a solids outlet opening at the opposite end of said housing, and a co-axially positioned tubular gas outlet conduit placed at an end of said housing, which separator further comprises a vortex stabilizer, comprising a pin placed on a stabilizing plate, in which separator the pin runs along the axis of the tubular housing and in which a passageway is provided through the stabilizer plate and the pin.
problem: Separating solid particles from a gas stream efficiently while maintaining stable vortex conditions.
constraint: Balancing vortex stability with minimal disruption to the gas-solids flow to avoid re-entrainment of separated solids.
mechanism: A rotational flow is induced in a gas-solids mixture to create centrifugal forces that separate particles from the gas, while a stabilizing element maintains the vortex structure by permitting axial flow through a central passage and constraining radial displacement of the rotational flow.
mechanism_raw: A swirl is imparted to the gas-solids mixture to induce centrifugal separation, and a vortex stabilizer with a central pin and passageway maintains the vortex structure by allowing axial flow while stabilizing the rotational flow pattern.

abstract: Methods of addressing a biomolecule to a selectively addressable electrode are described. A permeation layer overlying a plurality of selectively addressable electrodes is provided. The permeation layer includes a reactive group that is adapted to bond to a biomolecule and that requires activation through a chemical transformation before bonding to the biomolecule. At least one selectively addressable electrode is biased such that a pH change occurs in an overlying solution of the at least one selectively addressable electrode. The reactive group in a portion of the permeation layer above the at least one selectively addressable electrode is then chemically transformed to an activated reactive group as a result of the pH change. A biomolecule is then bound to the permeation layer overlying the at least one selectively addressable electrode through the activated reactive group.
problem: Selectively attaching biomolecules to specific electrodes without cross-reactivity or unintended activation.
constraint: Achieving precise spatial control of pH changes to avoid unintended activation of reactive groups in adjacent regions.
mechanism: A localized chemical environment change at a target site modifies a reactive functional group in an adjacent permeable medium, enabling selective binding of biomolecules only where the chemical transformation occurs.
mechanism_raw: A localized pH change at a biased electrode chemically transforms a reactive group in the overlying permeation layer, activating it to bind biomolecules only at the targeted site.
residual_terms: ["chemical environment change", "reactive functional group", "permeable medium", "selective binding"]

abstract: A table saw having a reaction system configured to take a predetermined action to mitigate injury upon detection of a dangerous condition is disclosed. The reaction system has a component in a predetermined orientation relative to the blade and the component is configured to maintain its orientation relative to the blade as the blade is raised and lowered.
problem: Ensuring safety mechanisms in a table saw remain functional as the blade is raised or lowered during operation.
constraint: Maintaining alignment between the safety component and the blade across all blade positions without introducing mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A safety component is mechanically linked to a cutting element such that its spatial relationship to the cutting element remains invariant during vertical displacement, ensuring consistent activation of a protective response across all positions.
mechanism_raw: A safety component is mechanically coupled to the blade such that its orientation relative to the blade is preserved during vertical movement, ensuring consistent activation of the safety response.

abstract: In the coarse and fine grinding of mineral and non-mineral materials, e.g. limestone, cement clinker, blast-furnace slag, old concrete or ashes, the grinding material, usually including new and recirculated stock, is fed as a defined and laterally bounded material layer (4) of predetermined thickness from a material feed container (3), belonging to the comminuting apparatus, by way of a roller-type or rotary-vane feeder (9), which is arranged at the outlet and can be changed in a stepless manner in respect of its rotational speed, onto the vertex of the laterally rimmed (45), driven, bottom roller (1), accelerated to the roller speed and transported continuously into the gap formed (5) with the upper roller (2), arranged in an offset manner above the driven roller (1), is subjected to hydropneumatic loading using specific compressive forces of 2 to 7.5 kN/mm and is then deagglomerated within the comminuting apparatus by a preferably high-speed rotary crusher (10). This results in good utilization of energy and in low mechanical structural, servicing and maintenance outlay. Usage over a wide spectrum for comminuting different materials is made possible, and linear throughput and speed behavior both in partial-load operation and with high mass throughputs can be realized.
problem: Efficiently grinding materials with variable feed rates while minimizing energy consumption and mechanical wear.
constraint: Balancing compressive force magnitude and material layer thickness to optimize energy use and throughput across partial-load and high-mass conditions.
mechanism: A material layer is fed into a compression zone with adjustable force application, where controlled pressure and layer thickness regulate energy transfer, followed by high-velocity impact to fragment agglomerated particles.
mechanism_raw: A controlled, laterally bounded material layer is fed into a roller gap with hydropneumatic loading, ensuring uniform compressive forces and continuous transport into a high-speed crusher for deagglomeration.

abstract: In an apparatus for folding cardboard boxes, an area of each of four top portion flaps of a corrugated cardboard box is locked by a locking member having an elastic member, and an area of each of the four top portion flaps of the corrugated cardboard box is pushed down by an overlapping folding member.
problem: Reliably folding multiple flaps of a cardboard box in sequence without jamming or misalignment.
constraint: Synchronizing the timing and force of locking and folding operations to prevent interference between flaps during the folding process.
mechanism: Temporary retention elements hold flap positions while sequential actuation elements push overlapping flaps into a folded arrangement, with timing coordination preventing mechanical interference during the folding sequence.
mechanism_raw: Elastic locking members temporarily secure flap positions while overlapping folding members sequentially push flaps into a folded configuration, coordinating locking and folding actions.
residual_terms: ["temporary retention elements", "sequential actuation elements", "folded arrangement", "timing coordination"]

abstract: A method and apparatus for plating parts like lug nuts or other metal parts that have both an easily plated outside surface as well as a recessed cavity. The invention works in combination with a standard multi-station plating process. Also, a method and apparatus for preventing areas of electrode contact on a part from being non-plated. The present invention drains and plates a part containing a cavity by moving the part from a position where the cavity is facing around 45 degrees down to a position where the cavity is facing around 45 degrees up and then back down at various times during the process. The moving is generally initiated when the rack moving along a track above the fluid tanks encounters a roller. The roller causes a depression bar to activate a mechanical mechanism that shifts the position of the part. Other embodiments of the present invention can also rotate the part on an electrode finger as a roller on the track is encountered by the rack to avoid non-plated regions on the part.
problem: Plating recessed cavities on metal parts without creating non-plated regions during multi-station plating processes.
constraint: Timing of movement must align with the plating cycle stages, and mechanical actuation must be synchronized with rack movement along fluid tanks.
mechanism: Dynamically adjusting the orientation of a recessed cavity relative to a fluid medium during processing by mechanically actuating tilting and rotational motion, synchronized with process cycle stages, to ensure uniform fluid contact and prevent stagnant zones.
mechanism_raw: Controlled tilting and rotation of the part during plating, triggered by mechanical rollers, to dynamically adjust the orientation of the cavity relative to the plating fluid, ensuring even coverage and preventing stagnant zones.

abstract: An object of the invention is to provide a polycrystalline thin film which includes an intermediate layer that is made thinner while keeping high crystal orientation so as to prevent warpage of a substrate resulting from internal stress of the film. A polycrystalline thin film according to the invention includes an intermediate layer formed by a first layer and a second layer laminated in this order and provided on a metal substrate. The first layer has a rock-salt crystal structure and the second layer has a fluorite crystal structure.
problem: Preventing substrate warpage caused by internal stress in polycrystalline thin films while maintaining high crystal orientation.
constraint: Crystal structure compatibility between layers must be maintained to prevent delamination while minimizing overall film thickness.
mechanism: Balancing internal stress distribution in a layered structure by incorporating materials with differing crystal structures to stabilize orientation and reduce warpage, enabling reduced thickness of intermediate layers without structural compromise.
mechanism_raw: Laminating a first layer with rock-salt crystal structure and a second layer with fluorite crystal structure to balance stress distribution and stabilize crystal orientation, allowing the intermediate layer to be thinner without compromising structural integrity.

abstract: The present invention aims to provide a bearing structure allowing direct adjustment between itself and an opposing bearing even after assembly and a watch equipped with the same. A bearing structure of a watch rotatably supports a forward end portion of a shaft of a wheel with respect to a base body, and includes: a bearing, a bearing support body supporting the bearing and having a male screw portion on an outer peripheral surface concentric with the shaft of the wheel, and an adjustment nut equipped with a female screw portion threadedly engaged with the male screw portion of the bearing support body, regulated in its displacement in the extending directions of the shaft of the wheel by the base body, and adapted to adjust the position of the bearing with respect to the extending direction of the shaft via the bearing support body.
problem: Enabling post-assembly adjustment of bearing position relative to an opposing bearing in a watch mechanism.
constraint: The adjustment nut must be constrained from axial displacement by the base body while permitting rotational adjustment.
mechanism: Translating rotational motion into precise axial displacement of a component via a threaded interface and adjustable nut, constrained from axial movement by a base structure, to enable post-assembly alignment correction.
mechanism_raw: Using a male screw on the bearing support body and a regulated adjustment nut to translate rotational motion into precise axial displacement of the bearing, allowing alignment correction after assembly.

abstract: A power transmission device that includes a clutch that transmits power from a motor to an axle; a first pump that is driven by power from the motor to generate and output fluid pressure; a second pump that receives and is driven by a supply of electric power to generate and output fluid pressure; a pressure regulating valve that regulates a pressure of operation fluid output from the first pump, and delivers at least a portion of operation fluid discharged in connection with the pressure regulation to a lubrication target for use as lubricant; and a switching valve that switches between a first connection state and a second connection state.
problem: Managing fluid pressure for both power transmission and lubrication in a power transmission device with dual energy sources.
constraint: Switching valve must reliably transition between connection states without disrupting pressure regulation or lubrication flow.
mechanism: Dynamically routing fluid pressure between two functional paths (power transmission and lubrication) using multiple energy-source-driven pumps and switching valves, with pressure regulation maintained during state transitions.
mechanism_raw: Combining a motor-driven pump and an electric-powered pump with a pressure regulating valve and switching valve to dynamically route fluid pressure between power transmission and lubrication paths based on operational state.

abstract: A glass substrate processing method includes irradiating laser light L onto a glass substrate 1 such that the laser light L is focused within the glass substrate 1, thereby forming a high density area 3 that has a higher density than areas where the laser light L is not irradiated around the portion where the laser light L is focused; and performing chemical etching on the glass substrate 1 using an etching solution such that at least a portion of the high density area is allowed to remain, thereby forming a projection 2 on a surface 1a of the glass substrate 1.
problem: Forming precise projections on a glass substrate surface without mechanical machining.
constraint: Laser focus depth and etching solution selectivity must be precisely controlled to ensure only the high-density regions remain intact.
mechanism: Creating localized resistant regions within a substrate via focused energy input, then selectively removing non-resistant material through chemical etching to leave intact projections.
mechanism_raw: Focusing laser light within the glass to create localized high-density regions, then chemically etching the substrate so that the high-density areas resist etching and remain as projections.

abstract: Systems and methods for weight transfer in a vehicle are provided. One system includes a plurality of springs and a plurality of movable spring seats configured to adjust a length of the plurality of springs. Additionally, a pneumatic actuator is provided that is connected to the plurality of movable springs and configured to move the movable spring seats to adjust the length of the plurality of springs. Further, a controller is provided that is coupled to the pneumatic actuator to control the pneumatic actuator to adjust the length of the plurality of springs.
problem: Dynamic adjustment of vehicle weight distribution to optimize performance or stability under varying load conditions.
constraint: Balancing adjustment speed, precision, and mechanical durability while maintaining system responsiveness under dynamic loads.
mechanism: A feedback-driven control system dynamically reconfigures mechanical elements to redistribute load-bearing forces in real time. The system adjusts the position of load-supporting components through actuation, altering force distribution paths to optimize stability or performance under varying operational conditions.
mechanism_raw: A controller modulates a pneumatic actuator to move adjustable spring seats, thereby altering spring lengths and redistributing weight. The feedback loop enables real-time mechanical reconfiguration based on operational demands.

abstract: An in-situ method for nanomixing magnesium aluminate spinel nanoparticles with a uniformly distributed controlled concentration of nanoparticles of an inorganic sintering aid, such as LiF, to produce ready-to-sinter spinel powder. The spinel-sintering aid nanomixture is formed by induced precipitation of the sintering aid nanoparticles from a dispersion of the spinel nanoparticles in an aqueous solution of the sintering aid, followed by separation, drying and deagglomeration of the spinel-sintering aid nanomixed product.
problem: Achieving uniform dispersion of nanoparticles within a matrix during material synthesis to ensure consistent sintering behavior.
constraint: Maintaining nanoparticle uniformity during processing while avoiding re-agglomeration or phase separation in the final product.
mechanism: Controlled nucleation and phase separation within a processing medium generates a uniform distribution of discrete particles. Subsequent physical separation, moisture removal, and mechanical disruption of clustered particles preserve the nanoscale dispersion without re-aggregation.
mechanism_raw: Induced precipitation of nanoparticles from a dispersion solution creates a controlled, uniform mixture. Subsequent separation, drying, and deagglomeration preserve the nanoscale distribution without re-agglomeration.

abstract: Disclosed herein is a highly-durable electrode tool for electrochemical machining, which can prevent the corrosion and abrasion of a conductive pattern at the time of electrochemical machining for forming dynamic pressure-generating grooves of a fluid dynamic bearing, and a method of manufacturing the same. The electrode tool for electrochemical machining includes: an electrode substrate on which a conductive pattern is formed to have protrusions corresponding to the fine grooves and to which negative current is applied; a nonconductive insulating layer, covering an entire top surface of the electrode substrate excluding the conductive pattern; and a conductive layer, which is formed on the conductive pattern to protect the conductive pattern, and a top surface of which is the same height as a top surface of the nonconductive insulating layer.
problem: Preventing degradation of fine conductive features during electrochemical machining processes.
constraint: Ensuring precise alignment and height matching between the conductive and insulating layers to avoid mechanical or electrical interference during machining.
mechanism: A layered structure protects a patterned conductive region during processing by encapsulating it between a non-conductive barrier and a sacrificial conductive film. The layers are mechanically aligned and planarized to maintain structural and electrical continuity during subsequent operations.
mechanism_raw: A nonconductive insulating layer covers the substrate except for the conductive pattern, while a conductive overlayer protects the pattern. The overlayer and insulating layer are co-planarized to maintain structural and electrical integrity.

abstract: The present invention aims to prevent a main drive pulse from being moved to a rank having a potential to cause a non-rotating state. A detection segment for detecting a rotating state of a stepping motor is divided into a first segment immediately after the drive with a main drive pulse, a second segment, and a third segment and, when the stepping motor is rotated by the main drive pulse, the main drive pulse is not changed when a detection signal exceeding a reference threshold voltage is detected at least in the first and second segments. When it is detected only in the first and third segments, or detected only in the third segment, the rank is moved upward and, when it is not detected in any segment, or detected only in the first segment, the rank is moved upward after the drive with a corrective drive pulse. When it is detected only in the second segment or detected only in the second and third segments, the rank is moved downward.
problem: Preventing stepping motors from entering non-rotating (stalled) states due to suboptimal drive pulse configurations.
constraint: Accurately segmenting detection intervals and correlating them with corrective actions to avoid oscillation or delayed response.
mechanism: Temporal segmentation of operational state detection enables adaptive modulation of drive signal intensity. Feedback from discrete time intervals triggers incremental adjustments to the drive signal magnitude, preventing loss of motion by maintaining rotational stability.
mechanism_raw: Segmented detection of motor rotation state informs adaptive adjustment of drive pulse 'rank' (intensity). Feedback from specific temporal segments triggers upward or downward rank shifts to maintain stable rotation.

abstract: A method for collecting tolls for location usages of an on-board unit, which has a unit identifier in a road toll system and a mobile telecommunications identifier in a mobile telecommunications network. The method includes storing the unit identifier and the mobile telecommunications identifier of the on-board unit in a control centre of the road toll system, sending the position-fix data from the on-board unit, under the mobile telecommunications identifier as sole identification, to a toll calculation server, calculating location-anonymised toll data in the toll calculation server, and sending said toll data under the mobile telecommunications identifier to a control centre of the mobile telecommunications network, charging a user account assigned to the mobile telecommunications identifier in the control centre of the mobile telecommunications network, sending a confirmation to the control centre of the road toll system under the mobile telecommunications identifier, and retrieving the unit identifier associated with the mobile telecommunications identifier and providing the confirmation in the control centre of the road toll system.
problem: Collecting location-based tolls while preserving user anonymity and preventing direct linkage between toll data and personal identifiers.
constraint: Ensuring secure, one-way mapping between identifiers to prevent re-identification while maintaining auditability for billing purposes.
mechanism: A trusted intermediary performs one-way identifier translation to decouple real-time location tracking from billing records. A temporary communication token is used for data transmission, with the trusted entity mapping the token to a permanent identifier only after anonymization to prevent re-identification.
mechanism_raw: A secondary identifier (telecom ID) is used as the sole communication token for toll data transmission. A trusted control center maps this temporary identifier back to the original unit ID only after anonymization, decoupling real-time tracking from billing.

abstract: A description is given of an endonasal filter including two essentially planar filtering components joined at their respective ends by a flexible element mounted, similar to a spring, across the cartilage between the two nostrils. The shape of the filtering components is that of a lunette as is the shape of the section at entry to the channel communicating with the nasal cavities. The filtering components are joined by a thin piece of plastic shaped to form a U-bend, the two parallel sides of which extend towards the filtering components on whose surfaces they assume the form of an oval that supports the component and to which it is made to adhere by application of heat.
problem: Maintaining a filter in a confined nasal passage while ensuring airflow and preventing dislodgement.
constraint: Balancing flexibility for conformability with structural integrity to avoid collapse or migration of the filter.
mechanism: A flexible connector element links two filtering components, enabling adaptation to anatomical contours through elastic deformation while maintaining positional stability via adhesion and structural resilience.
mechanism_raw: A flexible element (e.g., a U-bend plastic strip) connects two filtering components, allowing them to adapt to the nasal anatomy while maintaining positional stability through elastic deformation and adhesion.

abstract: A laminate is produced in which a long release sheet 2A, an adhesive layer 3A and a base material 4A are laminated together, and the base material 4A and the adhesive layer 3A are cut (half cut) so as not to penetrate through the release sheet 2A, so as to divide the base material 4A and the adhesive layer 3A into cover sheet portions 51A, bolstering portions 52A and a remainder portion 53A. The remainder portion 53A is then peeled off and removed, and an outer end portion of each of the bolstering portions 52A is half cut so as not to penetrate through the release sheet 2A, raised portions 6A being formed through the half cutting. The laminate sheet can be produced at low cost, and defects can be prevented from being formed on the adhesive sheet when the laminate sheet is wound into a roll.
problem: Producing a laminate with selectively removable and structured regions while preventing defects during rolling or handling.
constraint: Ensuring cuts do not fully penetrate the release sheet to maintain structural continuity during processing.
mechanism: Partial penetration cutting through specific layers (without fully severing a backing sheet) creates removable segments and elevated features, enabling controlled separation and forming functional geometries while preserving base material integrity.
mechanism_raw: Half-cutting through specific layers (without penetrating a release sheet) creates removable portions and raised structures, enabling controlled peeling and forming functional geometries without compromising the base material.

abstract: Provided is a measuring chip, which can spot a specimen liquid of a minute quantity for an immune agglutination easily and precisely to the measuring chip and which can prevent the flow of the specimen liquid and the contamination of the specimen. The measuring chip comprises at least two substrates, a spacer arranged between the substrates, at least one passage made of the substrates and the spacer into a hollow shape and having two open ends, counter electrodes for applying an electric field, and a specimen-spotted portion to be spotted with the specimen. The specimen-spotted portion has a structure made of a square, circular, elliptical or sector shape by that spacer. Moreover, the specimen-spotted portion has two open ends, one of which is connected to one open end of that passage.
problem: Precisely controlling fluid flow and preventing contamination in microscale specimen analysis.
constraint: Maintaining precise geometric alignment between substrates and spacer to ensure consistent fluid behavior.
mechanism: A spacing element defines a specimen-receiving region with opposing open ends connected to a hollow channel, enabling controlled capillary-driven fluid transport and isolation of the specimen within the analysis chamber.
mechanism_raw: A spacer defines a specimen-spotted region with two open ends connected to a hollow passage, enabling controlled capillary-driven flow and isolation of the specimen within the chip.

abstract: A stretchable electronic circuit that includes a stretchable base substrate having a plurality of stretchable conductors formed onto a surface thereof, with both the stretchable base substrate and conductors being bendable together about two orthogonal axes. The stretchable circuit also includes a stretchable sensor layer attached to the base substrate with a cavity formed therein which has a contact point exposing one of the plurality of stretchable conductors. The stretchable electronic circuit further includes a surface mount device (SMD) package with a conductor contact protrusion installed into the cavity, and wherein a substantially constant electrical connection is established between the conductor contact protrusion and the stretchable conductor at the contact point by tensile forces interacting between the stretchable base substrate and the stretchable sensor layer.
problem: Establishing and maintaining electrical connectivity in a stretchable circuit under mechanical deformation.
constraint: Balancing material elasticity and adhesion to prevent delamination or loss of contact under repeated stretching.
mechanism: Mechanical tension between a deformable substrate and a component with a cavity generates a self-adjusting interface, ensuring continuous electrical contact between a packaged device and conductive pathways under repeated stretching.
mechanism_raw: Tensile forces between a stretchable base substrate and a sensor layer with a cavity create a self-adjusting contact point, ensuring continuous electrical connection between an SMD package and stretchable conductors.

abstract: [Problem] To provide a thermoplastic elastomer composition for foaming, which has sufficient foamability and provides a molded article having good appearance. [Solution to Problem] A thermoplastic elastomer composition for foaming, which comprises 10 to 40% by weight of a partially or completely crosslinked ethylene/α-olefin/non-conjugated polyene copolymer rubber (A) comprising ethylene, an α-olefin of 3 to 20 carbon atoms and a non-conjugated polyene, 3 to 33% by weight of an ethylene/α-olefin copolymer (B) comprising ethylene and an α-olefin of 3 to 20 carbon atoms, 10 to 40% by weight of polypropylene (C) having a melting point, as determined by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), of 40 to 170° C., 10 to 45% by weight of a softener (D) for rubbers, and at least one substance selected from an isotactic propylene-based polymer (E-a) in an amount of 1 to 30% by weight and a syndiotactic α-olefin-based copolymer (E-b) in an amount of 1 to 20% by weight, with the proviso that the total amount of the components (A), (B), (C), (D), (E-a) and (E-b) is 100% by weight.
problem: Achieving sufficient foamability and surface quality in a thermoplastic elastomer composition.
constraint: Optimizing component ratios to prevent phase separation or incompatibility that would degrade foam properties.
mechanism: A multi-phase blend combines crosslinked elastomers, thermoplastic polymers, and compatibilizing agents to balance foam nucleation, structural cohesion, and surface quality through controlled phase interactions.
mechanism_raw: A multi-component blend combines a crosslinked rubber, ethylene/α-olefin copolymer, polypropylene, softener, and isotactic/syndiotactic polymers to balance foam nucleation, structural integrity, and surface finish.

abstract: A device to plan meals, comprising, at least one Food Item Piece corresponding to an item of food, at least one Food Item Storage Page adapted to temporarily store the at least one Food Item Piece and at least one Daily Meal Planning Chart adapted to temporarily store the at least one Food Item Piece, wherein an individual may plan a meal by selecting at least one Food Item Piece corresponding to an item of food from the at least one Food Item Storage Page and temporarily store it on the at least one Daily Meal Planning Chart.
reason: The patent describes a physical organizational tool for meal planning, which is a static product feature rather than a causal mechanism solving a technical problem.

abstract: An acoustic transducer array element includes a plurality of individual or transducer assemblies or “drivers” which are combined in a closely spaced geometry to form the array element. The respective transducer assemblies within each array element are acoustically coupled with each other. The invention utilizes such mutual coupling between the closely spaced transducers assemblies to provide improved acoustic performance.
problem: Acoustic transducer arrays suffer from degraded performance due to lack of coordination between individual transducer elements within a single array element.
constraint: The transducers must be spaced closely enough to maintain acoustic coupling, but the geometry must still allow each transducer to function as part of a coherent array element without destructive interference.
mechanism: A plurality of energy conversion elements are positioned in close proximity and mechanically coupled so that their mutual interaction enhances collective output. The physical adjacency and coupling between adjacent elements creates a cooperative effect that improves the aggregate performance compared to independently operating elements.
mechanism_raw: Multiple closely spaced transducer assemblies are acoustically coupled with each other, so that mutual coupling between adjacent transducers within the array element enhances the overall acoustic performance. The physical proximity and acoustic interaction between the transducers creates a cooperative effect that improves the array element's output compared to independently operating transducers.

abstract: A supplemental power source for a building or other structure is provided. Power is generated by converting mechanical energy derived from a fluid into electrical energy. The fluid can be, for example, in the form of air in a building air duck or water in building water lines. The invention includes a specially designed turbine enclosure through which the fluid passes. The enclosure has a Venturi area which results in movement of the fluid at a rapid speed through the turbine. An electric generator with a ratable blade also is provided within the Venturi area in order to take advantage of the faster moving fluid. The faster the fluid moves, the more energy can be converted by the generator. The generator can be constructed with a plurality of electric coils and magnets which can be arranged in series/parallel combinations depending on the power requirements of a particular application.
problem: Existing building fluid systems (air ducts, water lines) carry flowing fluids with kinetic energy that is typically wasted, and there is a need to extract usable electrical power from these flows without major system modifications.
constraint: The Venturi design must balance fluid acceleration (which increases energy extraction) against pressure drop and flow disruption, while the generator must be sized to efficiently capture energy from the accelerated flow without excessively impeding it.
mechanism: A constriction in a fluid path increases fluid velocity, and an energy conversion device positioned within this high-velocity region transforms the increased kinetic energy into electrical energy. The accelerated fluid flow through the constriction directly increases the energy available for conversion, with electrical output configurations adjustable to match power requirements.
mechanism_raw: A Venturi constriction in the fluid path accelerates the fluid velocity, and a turbine/generator positioned within this high-velocity region converts the increased kinetic energy into electrical energy. The faster fluid flow through the Venturi directly increases the energy available for conversion by the generator, with coil and magnet arrangements configurable in series/parallel to match power requirements.

abstract: An optical system is able to achieve a substantially azimuthal polarization state in a lens aperture while suppressing loss of light quantity, based on a simple configuration. The optical system of the present invention is provided with a birefringent element for achieving a substantially circumferential distribution or a substantially radial distribution as a fast axis distribution in a lens aperture, and an optical rotator located behind the birefringent element and adapted to rotate a polarization state in the lens aperture. The birefringent element has an optically transparent member which is made of a uniaxial crystal material and a crystallographic axis of which is arranged substantially in parallel with an optical axis of the optical system. A light beam of substantially spherical waves in a substantially circular polarization state is incident to the optically transparent member.
problem: Achieving a specific polarization state (azimuthal or radial) across a lens aperture typically results in significant light loss due to complex optical elements or inefficient polarization manipulation.
constraint: The birefringent element must be made of a uniaxial crystal with its crystallographic axis precisely aligned parallel to the optical axis, and the fast-axis distribution must be carefully engineered to match the desired polarization pattern without introducing excessive optical loss.
mechanism: A birefringent element with a spatially varying optical axis orientation across an aperture is combined with a polarization rotating element. The birefringent element establishes a position-dependent polarization transformation based on its axis orientation, and the rotating element then modifies the resulting polarization state to achieve a desired spatial distribution while preserving light quantity.
mechanism_raw: A birefringent element with a controlled fast-axis distribution (circumferential or radial) across the lens aperture is combined with an optical rotator positioned behind it. The birefringent element establishes a spatially varying polarization transformation based on its crystallographic axis orientation, and the optical rotator then rotates the resulting polarization state to achieve the desired azimuthal or radial distribution while preserving light quantity.

abstract: An access control system, having at least one access control unit for securing a physical area and controlling entry into and egress out of the physical area, and an Ethernet routing device, is disclosed. The Ethernet routing device includes an access controller for determining access privileges to the physical area; an Ethernet switching unit for directing network communications between multiple network devices; at least one Ethernet connector for connecting the at least one access control unit to the Ethernet routing device; and an access control message interpreter for reading messages received, by way of the Ethernet connector, from the at least one access control unit and providing access control information contained in the messages to the access controller for access privilege determination.
problem: Physical access control systems and network communication systems operate independently, creating a gap where network access cannot be dynamically coordinated with physical access decisions.
constraint: The system must maintain real-time message interpretation and privilege determination to avoid network latency, while ensuring that the integrated access controller can process both physical entry events and network communication requests without conflict.
mechanism: A network routing device integrates access control logic directly into communication switching infrastructure. Access control units send messages through network connectors to a message interpreter, which extracts access control information and provides it to an access controller. The access controller determines access privileges, and the switching unit uses these privileges to direct communications between devices, thereby converging physical security decisions with network access control at a single routing point.
mechanism_raw: An Ethernet routing device integrates access control logic directly into the network switching infrastructure. Access control units send messages through Ethernet connectors to an access control message interpreter, which extracts access control information and provides it to an access controller. The access controller determines access privileges, and the Ethernet switching unit uses these privileges to direct network communications between devices, thereby converging physical security decisions with network access control at a single routing point.
residual_terms: ["network routing device", "access control logic", "communication switching infrastructure", "access controller", "access privileges", "switching unit"]

abstract: A system and method for controlling the propagation of an email message includes defining at least a first email recipient and a second email recipient of the email message. A first email propagation policy associated with at least the first email recipient is defined, and a second email propagation policy associated with at least the second email recipient is defined. The email message is sent to the first email recipient and to the second email recipient.
reason: The patent describes defining per-recipient email propagation policies and sending messages accordingly, but this is a generic policy-based routing concept without a deeper causal mechanism. The 'mechanism' is simply applying different rules to different recipients, which is a basic conditional logic pattern rather than a transferable engineering or scientific principle.

abstract: A rope structure adapted to engage an external structure comprising a primary strength component and a coating. The primary strength component comprises a plurality of fibers. The coating comprises a lubricant portion and a binder portion that fixes the lubricant portion relative to at least some of the fibers. The coating is applied to the primary strength component such that the lubricant portion reduces friction between adjacent fibers and reduces friction between fibers and the external structure.
problem: Friction between adjacent fibers and between fibers and external structures in rope systems causes wear, inefficiency, or failure.
constraint: Balancing lubricant effectiveness with binder adhesion to maintain fiber cohesion and load-bearing capacity.
mechanism: A dual-component system where a fixing agent immobilizes a friction-reducing agent relative to a fibrous substrate, maintaining localized lubrication at contact interfaces while preserving structural cohesion through adhesion between the fixing agent and the substrate.
mechanism_raw: A binder portion in the coating fixes a lubricant portion relative to the fibers, ensuring the lubricant remains localized to reduce friction at critical contact points without compromising structural integrity.

abstract: A magnetic finger glove helps persons hold, install, and retrieve small metallic objects, such as nuts or screws, in hard-to-reach places. The finger glove is sized and shaped to sheathe and conform to an adult human index finger. A small round disc neodymium magnet is affixed to a fabric assembly in the region corresponding to the fingertip. The magnet weighs less than 0.002 pounds and is small enough to be confined within an area on the fabric assembly of less than 0.5 square inches. Yet, the magnet has a holding force of at least 1 pound.
reason: The patent describes a specific application (a magnetic glove) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The magnet's placement and strength are tailored to a narrow use case (handling small metallic objects on a finger), with no broader functional principle that transfers to other fields.

abstract: The present invention provides a method of making a laminated nonwoven fabric wherein the nonwoven fabric is a laminated one formed by integrating, through compressive bonding, a stacked nonwoven fabric structure comprising an upper and a lower thermoplastic synthetic filamentary fiber layer that have a fiber diameter from 7 pm or more to 20 pm, and an intermediate layer composed of thermoplastic synthetic fine fibers that have a fiber diameter of 5 pm or less, the laminated nonwoven fabric having an intimately mixed structure in which a portion of the fine fibers is intruded into at least one face side of the filamentary fiber layers with an intrusion index of 0.36 or more to bond, surround or interlace the filamentary fibers, a basis of weight of from 10 g or more to 250 g/m2, and a bulk density of 0.20 g/cm3 or more.
problem: Creating a laminated nonwoven fabric with controlled fiber interpenetration to achieve structural bonding and desired bulk properties.
constraint: Maintaining a balance between fiber diameter ratios, intrusion depth (intrusion index ≥ 0.36), and bulk density to ensure both structural integrity and material efficiency.
mechanism: Layered materials with differential structural element sizes are compressed to force smaller elements into adjacent layers, creating mechanical interlocks through geometric entanglement and surrounding contact, forming an integrated structure with controlled interpenetration depth.
mechanism_raw: Compressive bonding of layered thermoplastic fibers with varying diameters (coarse outer layers and fine intermediate fibers) forces fine fibers to intrude into adjacent layers, mechanically interlocking and surrounding the coarser fibers to form an integrated structure.

abstract: A field effect transistor (FET) that includes a drain formed in a first plane, a source formed in the first plane, a channel formed in the first plane and between the drain and the source and a gate formed in the first plane. The gate is separated from at least a portion of the body by an air gap. The air gap is also in the first plane.
problem: Reducing parasitic capacitance and dielectric losses in field-effect transistors to improve switching performance.
constraint: Ensuring structural stability and manufacturability of the air gap while maintaining electrical isolation and device reliability.
mechanism: A low-permittivity medium is introduced into a structural gap within an active semiconductor region, reducing capacitive coupling by replacing a higher-permittivity material while maintaining electrical isolation through physical separation.
mechanism_raw: An air gap in the gate structure replaces a solid dielectric material, leveraging air's low permittivity to minimize capacitive coupling between the gate and the channel/body.

abstract: A hybrid photovoltaic cell module includes a substrate and a photopolymer composition disposed on the substrate. The photopolymer composition includes an organic photopolymer, a plurality of nanoparticles, and a dendrimer that disperses the nanoparticles in the composition. The dendrimer has a number average molecular weight of from 300 to 10,000 g/mol and a core having a carbon atom directly bonded to X1 and X2 and two —CH2 groups. X1 is a hydrogen atom, a functional group, or a chain including a functional group. X2 is a chain including a functional group that is the same or different from the functional groups of X1. Each —CH2 group is bonded to a chain that independently includes a functional group that is the same or different from said functional groups of X1 and X2. The module is formed using a method that includes the step of disposing the photopolymer composition on the substrate.
problem: Achieving uniform dispersion of nanoparticles in a photopolymer matrix to enhance material properties without aggregation.
constraint: Optimizing dendrimer molecular weight (300–10,000 g/mol) and functional group density to balance dispersion efficacy with compatibility in the photopolymer matrix.
mechanism: A branched molecular architecture with surface-functionalized regions acts as a stabilizing agent, using steric hindrance and charge-based interactions to prevent particulate aggregation and maintain uniform distribution within a matrix through complementary physicochemical compatibility.
mechanism_raw: A dendrimer with a functionalized core and branched chains acts as a stabilizing agent, using its molecular architecture to sterically and electrostatically disperse nanoparticles within the polymer composition.

abstract: The present invention has been achieved to provide a method and apparatus for speedily and homogeneously fabricating polycrystalline silicon films or similar devices at low cost. A silicon target is attached to a water-cooled electrode, while a substrate made of a desired material is set on the other, heated electrode. When atmospheric pressure hydrogen plasma is generated between the two electrodes, silicon atoms will be released from the low-temperature target on the side and deposited on the high-temperature substrate. A doped silicon film can be created by using a target containing a doping element. Since there is no need to handle expensive and harmful gases (e.g. SiH4, B2H6 and PH3), the apparatus can be installed and operated at lower costs. In an application of the film producing method according to the present invention, an objective substance can be selectively purified from a target containing a plurality of substances.
problem: Speedily and homogeneously fabricating polycrystalline silicon films at low cost without handling expensive or harmful gases.
constraint: Balancing temperature differential between target and substrate to enable selective atom release while avoiding costly or hazardous process gases.
mechanism: Using a temperature gradient between a cooled source and a heated deposition surface to drive plasma-induced atom release and deposition, enabling selective material transfer without external process gases.
mechanism_raw: Using atmospheric pressure hydrogen plasma between a water-cooled low-temperature target and a heated high-temperature substrate to release and deposit silicon atoms via temperature-driven plasma-induced sputtering.

abstract: A mold boring apparatus including a mold boring tool having a flow passage formed inside of the mold boring tool which allows a fluid to flow therethrough, having slits and protruding portions formed on an outer peripheral portion of an outer body of a tool blade member of the mold boring tool in a circumferential direction thereof extending from a leading end to a base end of the tool blade member, and blades that are inclined inward and are formed at leading ends of the protruding portions formed between the adjacent slits.
reason: The patent describes a specific tool geometry for mold boring with slits, protrusions, and inclined blades. While the design is functional, it lacks a generalizable causal principle beyond the mechanical arrangement of cutting edges, which is too application-specific to transfer broadly.

abstract: A macronutrient sustained release composition for a plant locus containing a nanocomposite wherein a nitrogen containing macronutrient compound adsorbed on the surface of hydroxy apatite phosphate nanoparticles is intercalated within the interlayer spacing of a nanoclay. The nanocomposite containing the adsorbed macronutrient compounds is slowly released in a sustained manner when contacted with an acidic soil.
problem: Sustained release of nitrogen-containing macronutrients in acidic soil without rapid leaching or overdose.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity of the nanocomposite while enabling controlled release through pH-dependent dissolution of the clay-nanoparticle matrix.
mechanism: Embedding nutrient compounds within a layered matrix of pH-responsive nanoparticles and porous structural layers, creating a composite that releases contents selectively under acidic dissolution conditions.
mechanism_raw: Adsorbing nutrient compounds onto hydroxy apatite phosphate nanoparticles and intercalating them within nanoclay interlayers, creating a pH-responsive nanocomposite that releases nutrients slowly under acidic conditions.

abstract: A hot gas injection lance (26) for injecting hot gas into a vessel (11) is made of three modules (26A, 26B and 26C) which all fabricated separately and brought together in successive steps and connected together by releasable fastenings. Lance module (26A) is a main duct module providing an elongate duct (31) through which to direct hot gas into an upper region of the vessel. Lance module (26B) is a gas inlet module through which to direct hot gas into duct (31) of module (26A). Lance module (26C) is a central module which includes an elongate central tubular structure (33) that extends within the gas flow duct (31) and carries at its lower end a series of swirl imparting tubular structure (33) that extends within the gas flow duct (31) and carries at its lower end a series of swirl imparting vanes (34) for imparting swirl to the gas flow exiting the duct. Main duct module (26A) has a mounting flange (110) that abuts a flange (122) on vessel (11) and the flanges (110, 122) are fastened together by bolts (121). Gas inlet module has a lower mounting flange 111 which abuts a flange (103) at the upper end of module (26A) and the flanges (111, 103) are connected together by bolts (112). Central module (26C) has a mounting flange (115) that abuts a flange (114) at the upper end of inlet module (26B) and the flanges (114, 115) are fastened together by bolts (116).
problem: Injecting hot gas into a vessel while enabling modular assembly, maintenance, and replacement of components under high-temperature conditions.
constraint: Ensuring structural and thermal compatibility between modules while maintaining gas flow efficiency and swirl induction through modular alignment.
mechanism: Constructing a high-temperature gas delivery system from independently fabricated segments connected via mechanically releasable joints, enabling modular assembly, maintenance, and replacement while preserving thermal and structural alignment.
mechanism_raw: Constructing the lance from separately fabricated modules connected via releasable flange-and-bolt joints, allowing independent manufacturing, assembly, and replacement of duct, inlet, and swirl-imparting sections.

abstract: An ultrasonic transducer having a reduced cost of manufacture. The ultrasonic transducer includes a first insulative retaining layer, a second insulative retaining layer, and a vibrator film layer sandwiched between the first and second retaining layers. The first retaining layer includes a first plurality of apertures formed therethrough, and the second retaining layer includes a second plurality of apertures formed therethrough, in which the second apertures are substantially in registration with the first apertures. The ultrasonic transducer further includes a first cover portion having a plurality of spring/backplate assemblies connected thereto, and a second cover portion. The combination of the first retaining layer, the vibrator film layer, and the second retaining layer is sandwiched between the first and second cover portions of the ultrasonic transducer. The laminated construction of the ultrasonic transducer allows the formation of an array of ultrasonic film transducers using a single piece of ultrasonic vibrator film.
problem: Reducing manufacturing costs for ultrasonic transducers while enabling scalable array formation.
constraint: Achieving precise aperture registration across layers to maintain uniform transducer performance while minimizing material and assembly complexity.
mechanism: Forming an array of transducers by laminating a single active layer between insulating substrates with precisely aligned openings, compressed between opposing structural assemblies to maintain uniform aperture registration.
mechanism_raw: Laminating a single vibrator film between insulative retaining layers with aligned apertures, sandwiched between cover portions with spring/backplate assemblies, to form an array of transducers from one film piece.

abstract: A method of conducting a telephone or internet based reverse auction for selling units where the reverse auction is transmitted to users on a medium, the method comprising the steps of providing a number of units for sale and storing a preliminary available quantity in an allocation database initially indicative of the number provided for sale, providing a telephone number or web site to which calls or orders from users can be placed to enter the reverse auction, recording the time at which one or more calls or orders were received on the telephone number or at the website in a record database, placing any callers into a queue and assigning them to a call operator or system in order to sell a unit, conducting a reverse auction in which a person or system reduces the indicated price of a unit over time and in which a producer or system reduces the preliminary available quantity, the reverse auction is concluded at the time of the preliminary available quantity is reduced to a pre-determined number, such as zero, with the price at the conclusion being stored in an auction database, wherein the preliminary available quantity is reduced based at least partly on one or more preliminary indicators associated with a call/user, such as the time of the acceptance of the call or order in the record versus the timing of the auction, which indicator(s) occur before a sale of a unit is completed/confirmed.
problem: Managing the conclusion of a reverse auction by dynamically adjusting available inventory based on real-time user interactions.
constraint: Balancing the auction's end time with the number of participants to ensure fairness and prevent premature or delayed closure.
mechanism: Dynamically adjust available inventory in real-time based on user interaction timing relative to a process's progress, creating a feedback loop where user behavior directly influences resource depletion and process termination when a predetermined threshold is reached.
mechanism_raw: The preliminary available quantity is reduced in real-time based on indicators tied to user call/order timing relative to the auction's progress, allowing the system to conclude the auction when the quantity reaches a predetermined threshold (e.g., zero). This creates a feedback loop where user behavior directly influences inventory depletion and auction termination.

abstract: The present invention provides methods of introducing a polynucleotide into a target cell, wherein the method employs a light generating protein coding sequence acting as a reporter. An important advantage of the methods described herein is that drug resistant target cells or target cells having no useful auxotrophic markers can be effectively transformed. The present invention also includes transformed cells produced by the methods described herein. Also described are light generating protein coding sequence modifications, a variety of vectors, and methods of using the transformed cells of the present invention.
problem: Enabling transformation of target cells that are drug-resistant or lack useful auxotrophic markers, which are typically difficult to engineer using conventional methods.
constraint: Ensuring the reporter system functions effectively in diverse cell types while avoiding interference with the cell's native processes.
mechanism: Employ a non-destructive, direct-readout reporter system to track successful transformation without relying on traditional genetic markers, enabling functionality in diverse cell types where conventional markers may be absent or compromised.
mechanism_raw: Using a light-generating protein coding sequence as a reporter to track successful transformation without relying on traditional selection markers. The reporter provides a direct, non-destructive readout of transformation success, bypassing the need for genetic markers that may be absent or compromised in the target cells.
