abstract: An embodiment of a system for controlling loading of food products in a food mixing unit by using a loader unit, the system having: a weighing device, which is mounted on the mixing unit and has a memory for storing at least one recipe of food products to be loaded and, for each food product of the recipe, first geographic coordinates associated with the food product and identifying a stocking area of the food product; a GPS receiver associated to the loader unit to detect second geographic coordinates identifying the place in which the loader unit is located; and a processing unit configured to check the weight of the food products of the recipe as these are gradually loaded in the mixing unit, to acquire the second geographic coordinates for each food product being loaded when the loader unit takes the food product from a stocking area and to compare the second geographic coordinates with the first geographic coordinates for each food product being loaded in order to verify that the correct food product is being taken.
problem: Ensuring the correct food products are loaded in the right quantities during a mixing process, preventing errors in ingredient selection or measurement.
constraint: Achieving accurate location tracking and weight measurement in dynamic environments while maintaining operational efficiency.
mechanism: A dual-verification system cross-references location data of a loading unit with pre-stored location references for each product's designated area, combined with real-time measurement of loaded mass. This ensures both identity and quantity accuracy during dynamic loading operations.
mechanism_raw: Cross-referencing geographic coordinates (GPS) of the loader unit with pre-stored coordinates for each product's stocking area, combined with real-time weight verification. This dual-check system confirms both the identity and quantity of each product being loaded.

abstract: A side airbag device for a side collision is provided in which a first bag half body (20) on an occupant side and a second bag half body (21) on a door side are formed by sandwiching a third base fabric (19) between a first base fabric (17) on the occupant side and a second base fabric (18) on the door side, and gas supplied from an inflator (22) to the second bag half body (21) is supplied to the first bag half body (20) via a through hole (19a) formed in an end part of the third base fabric (19) that is on the side distant from the inflator (22), and therefore, after the second bag half body (21) is firstly deployed to ensure that there is the minimum necessary occupant restraint performance, the first airbag half body (20) is deployed, thereby sufficiently enhancing occupant restraint performance. When the second airbag half body (21) is deployed, due to the thickness thereof in the vehicle width direction being small, smooth deployment is possible without interfering with the occupant, and subsequently when deployment of the first airbag half body (20) is completed it is possible to protect the occupant effectively by ensuring that the thickness in the vehicle width direction of the entire airbag (16) is sufficient.
problem: Optimizing airbag deployment during side collisions to balance smooth inflation (avoiding occupant interference) with sufficient restraint performance.
constraint: Balancing deployment timing and spatial thickness to ensure smooth inflation without compromising occupant protection.
mechanism: Two components deploy in a staged sequence controlled by differential material properties and timed actuation. The first component (with reduced spatial profile) deploys initially to minimize interference, followed by the second component deploying through an opening in the first to enhance restraint. Timing and material thickness differences govern the deployment order.
mechanism_raw: Sequential deployment of two airbag half-bodies via staged gas flow. The door-side half-body deploys first (due to its thinner profile) to minimize interference, then the occupant-side half-body deploys through a through-hole to enhance restraint. Gas flow timing and fabric thickness differences control the deployment sequence.

abstract: Apparatus for detecting the presence of a flame using a UV tube which can be supplied with a DC voltage via an operating resistor, at least two UV tubes which are arranged in this manner and have substantially the same field of vision being provided, and the two UV tubes being able to be switched on and off in succession with a gap of a predefined time within a predetermined interval of time via a controller, with the result that the UV tubes are switched on for a predeterminable period of time, the number of pulses obtained from each UV tube being able to be recorded and compared with one another, the anode of the respective UV tube being able to be connected to earth potential between the operations of switching the UV tubes off and on in order to draw ionization in the discharge area.
problem: Accurately detecting a flame while distinguishing it from false UV sources (e.g., sunlight, sparks) that could trigger spurious signals.
constraint: The UV tubes must have substantially the same field of vision and be switched with precise timing gaps to ensure valid comparison, while grounding prevents residual ionization from skewing subsequent measurements.
mechanism: Activating two radiation detectors with matched sensing fields in alternating sequence, comparing their response counts over a fixed interval, and resetting their ionization states between activations. The sequential comparison and state reset ensures only consistent radiation signatures are validated while rejecting transient false sources.
mechanism_raw: Alternating activation of two UV tubes with identical fields of vision, comparing their pulse counts over a predefined interval, and grounding anodes between operations to reset ionization states. This sequential comparison and reset ensures only consistent flame signals are validated.

abstract: The teachings herein are directed to a wave forming apparatus including a bed form that may include a plurality of sections at different angles, including a base section adjacent to a wave forming channel, the base section having an exterior profile defining a first, non-abrupt angle to the direction of flow of water in the channel, and an upper section that forms an exterior profile defining a second, steeper angle to the direction of water flow. Also disclosed is a twistlock mechanism adapted to removably fasten a bed form to a water channel, and a method of use.
problem: Controlling water flow dynamics to generate predictable wave shapes in a channel while allowing adjustable positioning of the flow-modifying structure.
constraint: The angle gradients must balance flow acceleration and turbulence to form desired waves, while the twistlock must maintain structural integrity under hydraulic forces during operation.
mechanism: A flow-modifying bed with sections at varying angular gradients shapes fluid velocity and direction to generate predictable wave patterns. A removable fastening mechanism enables positionally adjustable attachment to the channel, allowing dynamic reconfiguration of flow geometry while maintaining structural integrity under hydraulic forces.
mechanism_raw: A bed form with sections at varying angles (non-abrupt base angle and steeper upper angle) shapes water flow direction and velocity gradients. A twistlock mechanism enables removable, positionally adjustable fastening to the channel, allowing dynamic reconfiguration of flow geometry.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a precious metal recovery process in which an acid sulfidic feed material is subjected to acid pressure oxidation and an alkaline sulfidic feed material is subjected to alkaline pressure oxidation, with the discharge slurries from the pressure oxidation processes being combined to reduce neutralization requirements prior to precious metal recovery.
problem: Efficiently recovering precious metals from mixed feedstocks while minimizing energy-intensive neutralization steps required for downstream processing.
constraint: The acid and alkaline slurries must be compatible in composition and volume ratios to achieve effective neutralization without destabilizing the subsequent metal recovery chemistry.
mechanism: Combining two chemical processing streams with opposing pH characteristics to partially neutralize each other through self-buffering, reducing the need for external neutralizing agents before downstream material recovery. The mixed streams achieve effective pH adjustment through mutual chemical interaction.
mechanism_raw: Combining discharge slurries from acid pressure oxidation (acidic) and alkaline pressure oxidation (alkaline) to partially neutralize each other, reducing the need for external neutralizing agents before precious metal recovery. The chemical streams self-buffer when mixed.

abstract: A preventative care recommendation engine to provide a preventative care recommendation corresponding to a patient is disclosed. Processor(s) may be coupled to network interface(s) accessible by healthcare provider(s) and/or patient(s), to execute instructions to access a set of confidential health information for an identified patient, where the set is derived from a first data source, and includes an indication of a health condition of the identified patient, a healthcare service provided to the identified patient, and/or a time when the health care service was provided to the identified patient. A second data source that includes a set of criteria specified by a third party indicating a preventative care service may be accessed. A recommendation corresponding to the identified patient may be sent, wherein the recommendation is a function of the set of confidential health information for the identified patient and the set of criteria.
problem: Generating personalized preventative care recommendations by reconciling patient-specific health data with third-party clinical guidelines or criteria.
constraint: Data confidentiality must be maintained during cross-source integration, and the criteria must be dynamically updated to reflect evolving clinical standards without compromising patient privacy.
mechanism: Integrating private patient health data with external clinical criteria through a processing system to compute personalized recommendations as a function of both datasets. Secure network interfaces enable real-time access and dissemination to stakeholders while maintaining data confidentiality during cross-source integration.
mechanism_raw: Integrating confidential patient health information (conditions, services, timing) with external criteria (e.g., clinical guidelines) via a processor to compute recommendations as a function of both datasets. Network interfaces enable real-time access and dissemination to stakeholders.

abstract: A magnetic head for data recording having a pair of heating elements that self regulate in response to temperature to distribute heat for thermal actuation. The head includes a first heating element located adjacent to the read sensor and away from the writer, and a second heating element located adjacent to the writer. The first and second heating elements have different coefficients of thermal resistance that cause the heating of the second heating element to increase relative to that of the first heating element when the overall temperature increases or when power provided by a power source increases. There, thereby prevents the read sensor from extending too much and possibly contacting the disk.
problem: Preventing thermal expansion of a read sensor in a magnetic head from causing contact with a rotating disk, which could damage the sensor or disk surface.
constraint: The thermal resistance coefficients must be precisely calibrated to ensure differential expansion compensates for temperature increases without overcooling or destabilizing the writer's thermal actuation.
mechanism: Using two thermal elements with differing thermal resistance coefficients positioned at different locations to create a self-regulating heat distribution system. As temperature increases, the element farther from the sensitive component heats disproportionately more, counteracting thermal expansion and maintaining safe clearance without external control.
mechanism_raw: Using two heating elements with differing coefficients of thermal resistance—one near the read sensor and one near the writer—to self-regulate heat distribution. As temperature rises, the second element (near the writer) heats more, counteracting expansion of the read sensor and maintaining safe clearance.

abstract: A method of operating a non-volatile memory device includes performing an erasing operation to memory cells associated with a string selection line (SSL), the memory cells associated with the SSL constituting a memory block, and verifying the erasing operation to second memory cells associated with a second word line (WL) after verifying the erasing operation to first memory cells associated with a first word line (WL).
problem: Ensuring reliable and complete erasure of memory cells across multiple word lines in a non-volatile memory device without over-erasing or under-erasing specific regions.
constraint: The order of verification must balance thoroughness with operational efficiency, as verifying all word lines simultaneously could introduce errors, while overly sequential checks may slow down the erase process.
mechanism: Staged validation of sequential operations: after completing a first operation on a primary element, the system verifies completion status of a secondary element only after confirming the primary element's status. This ordered validation prevents premature or incomplete execution of downstream operations by enforcing dependency-based verification.
mechanism_raw: Sequential verification of erase operations: after erasing memory cells associated with a string selection line, the system verifies the erase status of second word line cells only after confirming the erase status of first word line cells. This staged verification ensures that erase operations are validated in a controlled order, preventing premature or incomplete erasure of downstream cells.

abstract: A protective hood is provided for protecting a wearer's head from environmental elements. The protective hood includes a hood body having a cap section positioned to fit over a top of the wearer's head, side sections positioned to hang adjacent sides of the wearer's head, and a back section positioned to hang adjacent a back of the wearer's head. The hood body defines an interior space for receiving the wearer's head. An outlet is provided for exhausting gas from the interior space of the hood body. The outlet includes a channel defined by first and second portions of the hood body. The channel is in fluid communication with the interior space and includes an open end portion in fluid communication with the environment for exhausting gas from the channel into the environment.
problem: Managing gas flow within a protective hood to maintain a breathable environment while preventing buildup of CO₂ or other contaminants without compromising protection from external elements.
constraint: The channel design must balance sufficient airflow to prevent CO₂ buildup with minimal ingress of external contaminants, requiring precise geometry to avoid turbulence or blockage.
mechanism: Tortuous-path gas exchange: a multi-stage channel geometry creates a non-linear flow route that allows contaminated gas to exit through an open terminus while maintaining structural continuity of the enclosure. The geometry passively directs airflow without active components, balancing exhaust efficiency with ingress prevention.
mechanism_raw: A dual-chamber exhaust channel formed by overlapping sections of the hood body creates a tortuous path for gas flow. This path allows stale air to exit through an open end while maintaining structural integrity of the hood, leveraging the hood's geometry to passively direct airflow without mechanical components.

abstract: A compact exoskeleton arm support device compensates for gravity. The compact exoskeleton arm support device compensating for gravity may include at least five joints. Among the at least five joints, two joints may be driven by actuators, and the remaining joints may be driven by user force. The compact exoskeleton arm support device compensating for gravity effectively uses the actuators, thereby increasing operating efficiency and reducing production costs.
problem: Providing gravitational compensation for an exoskeleton arm support while minimizing actuator count and power consumption to reduce cost and complexity.
constraint: The system must balance actuator placement and torque requirements to ensure user comfort and effective gravity compensation without overburdening the user's input forces.
mechanism: Hybrid load distribution: primary gravitational forces are counteracted by actively driven elements at key joints, while secondary joints rely on external force input. This partitions compensation workload between powered and unpowered elements, reducing actuator count while maintaining functional support.
mechanism_raw: Hybrid actuation: two joints are actively driven by actuators to handle primary gravitational loads, while three additional joints rely on passive user force input. This distributes the compensation workload between powered and unpowered joints, reducing the number of actuators needed while maintaining functional support.

abstract: Methods and devices are provided for transforming non-planar or planar precursor materials in an appropriate vehicle under the appropriate conditions to create dispersions of planar particles with stoichiometric ratios of elements equal to that of the feedstock or precursor materials, even after selective forces settling. In particular, planar particles disperse more easily, form much denser coatings (or form coatings with more interparticle contact area), and anneal into fused, dense films at a lower temperature and/or time than their counterparts made from spherical nanoparticles. These planar particles may be nanoflakes that have a high aspect ratio. The resulting dense films formed from nanoflakes are particularly useful in forming photovoltaic devices.
problem: Creating dense, high-quality coatings or films from nanoparticles at lower processing temperatures and times compared to spherical nanoparticles.
constraint: The aspect ratio and planar geometry of the particles must be optimized to balance dispersion stability with packing density, as overly thin flakes may settle or clump, while thicker ones may not achieve sufficient density.
mechanism: High-aspect-ratio particle packing: precursor materials are shaped into planar particles with optimized geometry to increase interparticle contact area. This enhances dispersion stability in a medium and enables denser packing, accelerating fusion into cohesive films at reduced thermal energy input.
mechanism_raw: Shaping precursor materials into high-aspect-ratio planar particles (nanoflakes) that disperse more easily in a vehicle medium. These particles form denser coatings due to increased interparticle contact area, enabling faster annealing into fused films at reduced thermal budgets.

abstract: An audio decoder includes an arithmetic decoder for providing a plurality of decoded spectral values on the basis of an arithmetically encoded representation of the spectral values, and a frequency-domain-to-time-domain converter for providing a time-domain audio representation using the decoded spectral values. The arithmetic decoder selects a mapping rule describing a mapping of a code value onto a symbol code in dependence on a context state described by a numeric current context value. The arithmetic decoder determines the numeric current context value in dependence on a plurality of previously decoded spectral values. The arithmetic decoder evaluates a hash table, entries of which define both significant state values and boundaries of intervals of numeric context values, in order to select the mapping rule. A mapping rule index value is individually associated to a numeric context value being a significant state value.
problem: Efficiently decoding arithmetically encoded spectral values in audio signals while adapting to varying data contexts to maintain decoding accuracy and speed.
constraint: The hash table must balance memory usage and lookup speed, as overly granular context states increase table size, while coarse states may reduce decoding accuracy for complex signal variations.
mechanism: Context-adaptive lookup mapping: a dynamic table stores both state values and interval boundaries for input-derived context values. This enables real-time selection of decoding rules based on prior outputs, allowing rapid symbol retrieval without recalculating mappings for each context variation.
mechanism_raw: Context-adaptive hash table mapping: a hash table stores both significant state values and interval boundaries for numeric context values derived from previously decoded spectral values. This allows the decoder to dynamically select mapping rules based on real-time context, enabling rapid lookup of symbol codes without recalculating mappings for each context.

abstract: The present invention discloses a sealing system for sealing together at least a pair of flexible pouch material layers. The sealing station can have a first sealing bar, a second sealing bar and a drive system that is in contact with the first sealing bar. The drive system is operable to move the first sealing bar between an open position and a closed position such that the first sealing bar can apply a predefined pressure on the flexible pouch material layers when positioned or located between the sealing bars. A pressure sensor is also included and in communication with the drive system, the pressure sensor operable to detect if the drive system applies less or too much pressure than the predefined pressure on the flexible pouch material layers located between the first and second sealing bars.
problem: Ensuring consistent pressure application during sealing of flexible pouch materials to prevent under-sealing or over-sealing.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise pressure control with the mechanical limitations of the drive system and sensor response time.
mechanism: A closed-loop control system where a sensing element detects deviations from a target pressure and actuates a mechanical component to dynamically adjust the applied force, maintaining a desired pressure profile during a sealing process.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control system where a pressure sensor detects deviations from a predefined pressure and communicates with a drive system to adjust the sealing bar's position, dynamically maintaining the desired pressure during operation.

abstract: An image pickup apparatus which is improved in space efficiency for an optical system element, thereby reducing the apparatus size when a lens barrel is retracted. An image pickup apparatus includes a zoom lens barrel that moves between a retracted position and a shooting position in an optical axis direction to thereby change a photographing magnification. A prism bends an optical beam incident from a lens group of the lens barrel. A diaphragm-shutter element is capable of moving along the direction of the second optical axis together with a stepping motor for actuating the diaphragm-shutter element. The stepping motor is disposed, at least when the lens group is in the retracted position, at a position where the stepping motor overlaps the prism in parallel with the second optical axis.
problem: Reducing the physical footprint of an optical system when the lens barrel is retracted, without compromising functionality in the extended state.
constraint: Ensuring that overlapping components do not interfere with each other during movement between retracted and extended positions.
mechanism: Spatial arrangement of components along parallel axes to enable physical overlap in a retracted state, allowing shared volume while preserving independent motion paths during operational transitions.
mechanism_raw: Spatial overlap of components (e.g., a stepping motor and prism) in the retracted position by aligning them along parallel axes, allowing shared physical space while maintaining independent motion paths during operation.

abstract: A valve arrangement has several valve clusters which are designed for different nominal flow rates. Each valve cluster (1c) comprises a valve base (2) fitted with valve units (4), the valve units (4) respectively having a control portion (13), which is connected by way of electrical interface means (23) with internal signal transmission means (22) of the valve base (2). Irrespectively of the flow rate category the overall height of the valve bases (2), the width of the component mounting sites and of the valve units (4) and also the electrical interface means (23) are identically configured in the case of the valve clusters of all flow rate categories. The modification of the nominal flow rates is performed more especially by the choice of different overall lengths of the valve units (4).
problem: Standardizing valve cluster designs across different flow rate categories while enabling scalable flow rate adjustments.
constraint: Maintaining uniform mounting and interface compatibility across all flow rate categories despite length-based adjustments.
mechanism: A modular architecture where standardized physical interfaces and dimensions are maintained across units, while functional parameters are adjusted by varying a component's length, decoupling structural uniformity from operational variability.
mechanism_raw: Modular design where the overall dimensions (height, width, interface configuration) of valve bases and units are fixed, while flow rate is adjusted by varying the length of the valve units, decoupling physical standardization from functional variability.

abstract: The invention relates to using a lipid acyltransferase polypeptide (SEQ ID NO: 68) in the manufacture of ultra-heat treatment milk (UHT) for improving the stability, the perceptible sensory difference, the smell, and the taste; and for reducing the cholesterol content, and for eliminating or reducing creaming of the UHT milk. The invention also relates to a method of producing UHT milk, wherein the method comprises admixing a lipid acyltransferase with milk and heating the mixture to make it a UHT milk.
problem: Improving the stability, sensory qualities, and nutritional profile of ultra-heat treated (UHT) milk through enzymatic modification during processing.
constraint: Ensuring the enzyme remains active and effective under the high-temperature conditions of UHT processing.
mechanism: Introducing a catalytic agent during a high-temperature processing step to facilitate a chemical transformation of a target substance, altering its composition and stability without disrupting the thermal process.
mechanism_raw: Introducing a lipid acyltransferase enzyme during milk heating to catalyze lipid restructuring, altering fat composition and stability without compromising the UHT process.

abstract: In an imaging apparatus having a toner container, a method of periodically calibrating a back EMF constant Ke used in a speed control circuit of a DC motor used for driving for a toner metering device. To adjust the value of the back EMF constant Ke, the method uses a plurality of sampled back EMF measurements together with a calculated actual speed of rotation of the toner metering device as measured using motion sensor.
problem: Maintaining accurate speed control of a DC motor in a toner metering device despite variations in back EMF constants over time or usage.
constraint: Balancing calibration frequency and computational overhead with the need for real-time speed control accuracy.
mechanism: Periodic recalibration of a motor's operational parameter by comparing real-time sensor feedback with measured performance data, adjusting the parameter to compensate for drift or degradation in system behavior.
mechanism_raw: Periodic calibration of the back EMF constant (Ke) by comparing sampled back EMF measurements with actual motor speed data from a motion sensor, adjusting Ke to correct for drift or degradation.

abstract: A method and apparatus of monitoring security personnel in a building facility is disclosed. One example method may include storing a plurality of information records associated with each of the security personnel in a database. The method may also include compiling, via a processor, a list of the information records that may be in violation of predetermined criteria used to determine whether the security personnel are in compliance with security procedures, and automatically notifying a security supervisor of the building facility of the security personnel that may be in violation of the security procedures. Such measures may reduce security violations and increase compliance with security measures and other safety concerns.
problem: Ensuring compliance with security procedures by identifying potential violations among security personnel.
constraint: Balancing automation accuracy to minimize false positives while maintaining real-time responsiveness.
mechanism: Automated evaluation of stored data against predefined rules, followed by selective alerting of oversight entities when rule violations are identified.
mechanism_raw: Automated comparison of stored personnel records against predefined compliance criteria, followed by targeted notification of supervisors when violations are detected.

abstract: An integrated circuit for providing a differential interface for an envelope tracking signal is described. The integrated circuit includes a subtraction module having a first input for receiving a digital envelope tracking signal and a second input for receiving a second signal, wherein the subtraction module is arranged to subtract the second signal from the digital envelope tracking signal and produce an envelope tracking signal with a reduced average direct current (DC) component; a digital-to-analog converter (DAC) arranged to receive the envelope tracking signal with the reduced average DC component and produce a differential analog version thereof; and a modulator operably coupled to a differential output of the DAC, wherein the modulator comprises a DC input point arranged to insert a DC component into the differential analog version of the envelope tracking signal.
problem: Managing DC offset in envelope tracking signals to improve power efficiency and signal integrity in integrated circuits.
constraint: Maintaining signal fidelity while reducing DC offset to avoid distortion in downstream processing.
mechanism: Adjusting a signal's DC component by subtracting a secondary signal to reduce offset before conversion, then reinserting the offset via a modulation stage at the output.
mechanism_raw: Subtracting a secondary signal from the envelope tracking signal to reduce its DC component before DAC conversion, then reinserting the DC component via a modulator at the differential output.

abstract: The sound-processing apparatus of the present invention generates plural frequency data by decoding plural encoded sound data and applying inverse quantization. Each of the frequency data are subjected to sound-processing and then synthesized into one single frequency data. Transformation processing from frequency domain to time domain is applied to the synthesized single frequency data so as to generate sound data in time domain so as to reduce computation amounts of decoding process.
problem: Reducing computational load during decoding of encoded sound data while preserving audio quality.
constraint: Balancing parallel processing efficiency with the need for accurate synthesis and transformation to avoid artifacts.
mechanism: Parallel processing of multiple encoded data streams into intermediate representations, followed by synthesis into a unified dataset and transformation to a target domain.
mechanism_raw: Decoding multiple encoded sound data streams into frequency-domain data, applying parallel processing to each stream, synthesizing them into a single frequency dataset, and then transforming to the time domain.

abstract: A garment for regulating temperature includes a body having a back panel and at least one front panel made of a temperature insulating textile and partially joined along at least one common edge, the joined panels defining an inside chamber. At least one pocket is fastened to an inside surface of at least one of the front panel and the back panel. The at least one pocket is configured for accommodating a temperature regulating element.
reason: The patent describes a static garment design with specific components (chamber, pocket, insulating textile) rather than a causal mechanism for temperature regulation. The 'mechanism' is a product feature, not a functional principle that can be abstracted to other fields.

abstract: In an embodiment, a bearing assembly includes superhard bearing elements distributed circumferentially about an axis. At least one of the superhard bearing elements may include a first arcuate end portion, a second arcuate end portion, a first substantially planar face, a second substantially planar face, and a bearing surface. The first and second arcuate end portions may be generally opposite each other. The first substantially planar face may extend between the first and second arcuate end portions. The second substantially planar face may be generally opposite the first substantially planar face. The first substantially planar face may have a length greater than a length of the second substantially planar face. The bearing surface may extend between the first arcuate end portion, the second arcuate end portion, the first substantially planar face, and the second substantially planar face. The bearing assembly includes a support ring that carries the superhard bearing elements.
problem: Creating a durable, wear-resistant bearing assembly that distributes loads effectively under rotational stress.
constraint: Balancing structural support from the support ring with the need for the bearing elements to maintain precise geometric alignment under stress.
mechanism: Arranging durable elements with specific geometric configurations around a structural support to optimize contact distribution and minimize localized degradation under stress.
mechanism_raw: Arranging superhard bearing elements with asymmetric planar faces and arcuate ends around a support ring to optimize contact geometry, enabling load distribution while minimizing localized wear.

abstract: Methods and devices for fabricating tri-layer beams are provided. In particular, disclosed are methods and structures that can be used for fabricating multilayer structures through the deposition and patterning of at least an insulation layer, a first metal layer, a beam oxide layer, a second metal layer, and an insulation balance layer.
problem: Fabricating multilayer structures with precise layer integration and structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing layer thickness, material compatibility, and alignment to maintain structural support while enabling desired functional performance (e.g., electrical isolation, beam flexibility).
mechanism: Sequentially depositing and patterning distinct functional layers in a controlled stack to build a composite structure where each layer contributes to mechanical or electrical properties through its specific material characteristics and spatial arrangement.
mechanism_raw: Sequential deposition and patterning of distinct functional layers (insulation, metal, oxide, balance) in a controlled stack to build a composite structure where each layer contributes to mechanical or electrical properties.

abstract: An air cleaner device whereby the number of component parts is reduced and the filter element can be maintained and inspected without a time-consuming procedure. The air cleaner device includes: a support part provided to a cleaner case and having a fitting ingress at a region on the opposite side thereof from the cover; and a pivot provided to the cover and having a convex part capable of fitting in the fitting ingress of the support part. A hinge part for connecting the cover to the cleaner case so that the cover can open and close is formed by the support part and the pivot by fitting of the convex part in the fitting ingress.
problem: Reducing component count and enabling tool-free maintenance in enclosures requiring repeated access.
constraint: Ensuring the convex pivot fits securely into the ingress to provide both rotational freedom and retention force, avoiding looseness or unintended disengagement during operation.
mechanism: Integrating a pivot-and-receptacle joint that simultaneously provides rotational freedom and retention force, allowing a component to swing open while maintaining secure closure without additional fasteners through geometric interlocking.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a pivot-and-receptacle joint that simultaneously serves as both a hinge and a removable attachment point, allowing the cover to swing open while maintaining secure closure without additional fasteners.

abstract: A method of manufacturing a porous ceramic article is provided that includes injecting a gas into a precursor batch material. The gas is pressurized to a positive gauge pressure. Exemplary gasses that can be injected into the precursor batch material include at least one of nitrogen, helium, neon, argon, krypton, and xenon. Air can also be injected into the precursor batch material, including air in which at least a portion of CO2 and/or O2 naturally occurring in air has been removed.
problem: Creating controlled porosity in ceramic materials for applications requiring permeability or surface area optimization.
constraint: Balancing gas pressure and type (e.g., inert vs. reactive) to achieve uniform porosity without compromising structural integrity or introducing unwanted chemical interactions.
mechanism: Injecting pressurized gas into a precursor material to form discrete voids or channels during processing, where gas pressure and composition determine pore size, distribution, and material density through controlled expansion and solidification.
mechanism_raw: Injecting pressurized gas into a precursor batch to form discrete voids or channels during processing, where gas pressure and composition determine pore size, distribution, and material density.

abstract: Provided is a floor construction apparatus that includes a guide unit that is disposed on surface of a floor to be constructed, and a flattening unit that is guided by the guide unit, to then be transferred to flatten the surface of the floor to be constructed, and to thereby reduce a construction time and expense for flattening of the construction surface of the floor.
problem: Achieving uniform surface flattening in construction while minimizing manual effort and time.
constraint: Maintaining the guide unit's position and alignment relative to the surface while allowing the flattening unit to traverse without binding or uneven force distribution.
mechanism: Using a fixed guide to constrain the path of a flattening tool, ensuring consistent contact pressure and motion across a surface to be flattened, thereby automating and standardizing the process through guided traversal.
mechanism_raw: Using a fixed guide unit to constrain the path of a flattening tool, ensuring consistent contact pressure and motion across the surface to be flattened, thereby automating and standardizing the process.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a system and method for optimizing a wash procedure. Embodiments of the present invention are directed to a system for optimizing a wash procedure. In a first embodiment, a system comprises: means for collecting a sample of fouling, wherein the sample of fouling comprises one or more contaminates; means for identifying the one or more contaminates; and means for selecting one or more washing products for removing the one or more contaminates from a turbine. In an alternate embodiment, the present invention is directed to a method for optimizing a wash procedure. The method comprises: collecting a sample of fouling, wherein the sample of fouling comprises one or more contaminates; identifying the one or more contaminates; and selecting one or more washing products for removing the one or more contaminates from a turbine.
problem: Optimizing cleaning efficiency by tailoring wash procedures to specific contaminant types.
constraint: Ensuring accurate contaminant identification and product selection to avoid ineffective or damaging cleaning agents, while maintaining speed and cost-effectiveness in the wash procedure.
mechanism: Analyzing a fouling sample to identify contaminants, then selecting cleaning products based on their compatibility with the identified contaminants, creating a feedback loop that adapts the cleaning process to the actual fouling composition through iterative analysis and product selection.
mechanism_raw: Analyzing a fouling sample to identify contaminants, then selecting washing products based on their compatibility with the identified contaminants, creating a feedback loop that adapts the cleaning process to the actual fouling composition.

abstract: An arrangement and a method are disclosed for driving and steering an engine driven vehicle of the type m which left and right hand wheels 120L, 120R are respectively driven from the engine through left and right hand transmissions 122L, 122R and a steering effect is exerted by changing the ratio of one transmission relative to the other. According to the invention a follower is operatively coupled to at least one of the transmissions and is movable circumferentially about an axis by means of a driver actuable steering control to change the relative speeds of the two driven wheels and radially with respect to the axis by means of a driver actuable speed control to increase/decrease the speeds of the two driven wheels in unison.
problem: How to independently control steering (differential wheel speed) and overall vehicle speed (both wheels in unison) using a single mechanical coupling to dual transmissions
constraint: The two degrees of freedom must be mechanically decoupled so that steering input does not affect overall speed and vice versa, while maintaining mechanical simplicity and reliability in a vehicular environment
mechanism: A mechanical interface component with two independent motion axes is coupled to dual output systems. One axis translates a first control input into differential motion between the outputs to produce directional control, while a second axis translates a second control input into synchronized motion of both outputs to produce speed control. The two axes are mechanically isolated so that actuation of one does not influence the other, enabling independent regulation of directional and speed functions through a single multi-axis coupling.
mechanism_raw: A follower element is mechanically coupled to the transmissions and has two independent degrees of freedom: circumferential motion about an axis (actuated by a steering control) changes the relative speeds of the two driven wheels to produce steering, while radial motion relative to the axis (actuated by a speed control) changes both wheel speeds in unison to produce acceleration/deceleration. This decouples two control axes through a single multi-degree-of-freedom mechanical interface.
residual_terms: ["mechanical interface component", "dual output systems", "differential motion", "synchronized motion", "mechanically isolated", "multi-axis coupling"]

abstract: An air conditioning control system and method for compensating for heat gain or loss in an air conditioned space due to window area and temperature differential between outdoor temperature and indoor temperature. For predetermined amounts of window area, as a percent of total wall area defining an enclosed space, the thermostat setpoint or measured temperature is adjusted as a function of the temperature differential between the enclosed space and the outdoor ambient temperature, for example. Data may be accumulated and stored in a controller memory for various types of structures and rates of heat transfer therethrough for various amounts and type of window area as a percent of the total wall area, for example.
problem: How to adjust a thermostat setpoint to compensate for heat transfer through windows, which varies with both the geometric exposure (window area relative to wall area) and the driving thermal potential (temperature differential)
constraint: The compensation must accurately model the heat transfer coupling using the geometric factor (window-to-wall ratio) and the driving force (temperature differential), and must be adaptable to different building types and heat transfer characteristics stored in controller memory
mechanism: A control target is adjusted by computing a coupling factor derived from a geometric ratio (proportional exposure of a heat-conductive surface relative to a total boundary) multiplied by a driving potential (temperature differential across the boundary). This coupling factor is used to proactively modify the control target based on predicted heat transfer, rather than relying solely on reactive feedback. The geometric ratio and driving potential are stored as adaptable parameters to accommodate varying system characteristics.
mechanism_raw: The thermostat setpoint or measured temperature is adjusted as a function of the temperature differential between indoor and outdoor environments, scaled by the window area as a percentage of total wall area. This computes a heat transfer coupling factor (geometric ratio multiplied by driving potential) and uses it to proactively adjust the control target, rather than relying solely on reactive feedback.
residual_terms: ["coupling factor", "geometric ratio", "driving potential", "temperature differential", "heat-conductive surface", "boundary", "adaptable parameters"]

abstract: This invention relates to a method to apply waste treatment liquid to a solid waste disposal site by filing a storage tank with waste treatment liquid, connecting the liquid storage tank with a vehicle for solid waste compacting and releasing the waste treatment liquid to a portion of solid waste site in need of moisture. This invention further provided an apparatus for distributing waste treatment liquid over the working face of a solid waste disposal site includes an inflow conduit, a storage tank, an outflow conduit, a control valve that contains a remote-valve control; manifold inlet conduit attached to the control valve, and a manifold to allow the liquid received from the manifold inlet conduit to be distributed evenly over the working face.
reason: The patent describes a standard liquid distribution apparatus using a storage tank, conduit, control valve, and manifold. The manifold-based even distribution and remote valve control are routine engineering techniques with no novel problem-solving mechanism that transcends the specific waste disposal application.

abstract: A system for forming a fluid connection includes a first connector and a second connector. Both connectors include a tubular body having a membrane mounted on a distal end thereof. A support member facilitates the coupling of the connectors together so that the membranes are abutted together. Radiant energy is applied to the abutted membranes so as to first sterilize the membranes and then melt the membranes so that a passage is formed therethrough.
problem: How to form a sterile fluid connection between two systems without exposing the connection interface to contamination during the joining process
constraint: The radiant energy must be sufficient to sterilize the membrane surfaces and then melt the membrane material to form a passage, but must be controlled to avoid excessive heating or damage beyond the intended interface region
mechanism: Two sealed interfaces are brought into contact, then a single energy source is applied to the interface region in a controlled sequence: first to sterilize the contact surfaces, then to fuse the materials together to form a continuous passage. The energy input is regulated to achieve sterilization and fusion thresholds without exceeding thermal limits that would damage the interface beyond the intended region, eliminating separate sterilization and joining steps.
mechanism_raw: Two connectors with membranes are abutted together, then a single radiant energy source is applied to the interface to first sterilize the membrane surfaces and then melt them together to form a passage. The same energy input sequentially performs surface sterilization followed by material fusion at the interface, eliminating the need for separate sterilization and joining steps.

abstract: A method of assembling a turbine engine includes defining a first chamber and defining a second chamber. The method also includes forming at least one venturi device oriented with a predetermined venturi step angle greater than approximately 48°. The method further includes coupling the first chamber in flow communication with the second chamber via the venturi device therebetween.
reason: The patent describes forming a venturi device with a specific step angle (>48 degrees) to connect two chambers in a turbine engine. The venturi is a standard fluid mechanics component, and the specific angle is a design parameter for turbine engine flow characteristics, not a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A method for repairing gas turbine components, in particular gas turbine blades, including at least the following steps: a) preparing a gas turbine component to be repaired; b) removing a damaged portion from the gas turbine component to be repaired, thereby forming a plane separation surface; c) placing the gas turbine component at least partly in a process chamber in such a way that the plane separation surface extends approximately horizontally within the process chamber; d) filling the process chamber with a metal powder that is bonding-compatible with the material of the gas turbine component to be repaired, namely up to the level of the separation surface; e) building up the removed portion on the separation surface by depositing metal powder in layers onto the separation surface and by fusing the metal powder, which has been deposited in layers onto the separation surface, to the separation surface.
problem: Repairing a damaged gas turbine component (e.g., blade) by rebuilding the removed portion while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise layer deposition and fusion with the requirement to maintain the component's structural integrity during repair.
mechanism: Positioning a component relative to a reference surface, then depositing and fusing material in successive layers onto the reference surface to rebuild a removed portion. The orientation of the reference surface ensures controlled alignment and bonding between layers.
mechanism_raw: Placing the component in a process chamber with a horizontal separation surface, then depositing and fusing metal powder in layers onto the separation surface to rebuild the removed portion. The horizontal orientation ensures controlled layer alignment and bonding.

abstract: A method and an apparatus confer full superelastic properties to the active surface of a mechanical component constructed of a superelastic material prior to service. A compressive load is applied to the active surface of the mechanical component followed by removing the compressive load from the active surface whereby substantially all load strain is recoverable after applying and removing of subsequent compressive loads.
problem: Ensuring a mechanical component made of superelastic material exhibits full superelastic properties on its active surface prior to service.
constraint: The material must inherently possess superelastic properties, and the applied load must be sufficient to induce recoverable strain without causing permanent deformation.
mechanism: Applying and removing a conditioning load to a surface of a material, which stabilizes the material's inherent property so that subsequent loads produce fully recoverable deformation. The conditioning load pre-stresses the material to lock in its functional behavior.
mechanism_raw: Applying and then removing a compressive load to the active surface, which conditions the material so that subsequent compressive loads result in fully recoverable strain. This pre-stresses the material to stabilize its superelastic behavior.

abstract: The invention relates to a method in a fiber web machine. In the method, a fabric (12) included in the fiber web machine is used for supporting a web (14) produced by the fiber web machine. Moreover, in the method the location of the fabric (12) is changed in the cross direction (CD) of the fiber web machine. The location is changed by means of oscillation, the amplitude (19) of which is kept so high that the area of impact (20) of the web (14) on the fabric (12) is wider than the width (21) of the web (14) throughout the lifetime of the fabric (12). The invention also relates to an arrangement in a fiber web machine, and to a software product.
problem: Extending the operational lifetime of a fabric in a fiber web machine by distributing wear caused by repeated web impact.
constraint: The oscillation amplitude must be precisely controlled to cover the full width of the web without causing misalignment or excessive mechanical stress on the fabric.
mechanism: Moving a flexible surface in a direction transverse to the primary motion of an impacting element, with an amplitude sufficient to ensure the impact area exceeds the element's width over the surface's lifetime. This distributes wear across a larger region of the surface.
mechanism_raw: Oscillating the fabric in the cross direction with an amplitude high enough to ensure the web's impact area is wider than the web itself throughout the fabric's lifetime. This spreads wear across a larger area of the fabric.

abstract: A sampling switch circuit uses correlated level shifting. The sampling switch circuit includes: a sampling switch having a first terminal, a control terminal, and an output terminal, wherein the first terminal is connected to an input voltage node; a boosting circuit connected to first and second supply voltage nodes and coupled to the control terminal of the sampling switch; and a correlated level shifting buffer circuit. The correlated level shifting buffer circuit includes: an amplifier having first and second inputs and an output, wherein the first input is connected to the input voltage node, and the output and second input are coupled to the boosting circuit; and a level shifting capacitor coupled to the second input and output of the amplifier, to the boosting circuit, and to a level shifting voltage node.
problem: Accurately sampling an input voltage in a switch circuit while managing voltage level mismatches between the input and the circuit's supply rails.
constraint: The boosting and level shifting circuits must operate in synchronization to avoid signal distortion while maintaining low power consumption and fast switching speeds.
mechanism: Adjusting voltage levels at a switching element's control terminal using a boosting circuit, combined with a dynamically aligned buffer that synchronizes input and output voltages via a capacitive coupling. This maintains signal fidelity despite voltage mismatches between the input and supply rails.
mechanism_raw: Using a boosting circuit to adjust voltage levels at the sampling switch's control terminal, combined with a correlated level shifting buffer that dynamically aligns the amplifier's output and input voltages via a level shifting capacitor. This ensures the sampled signal retains fidelity despite voltage differences.

abstract: A device for separating ferromagnetic particles from a suspension may include a tubular reactor through which the suspension can flow and which has an inlet and an outlet, and a means for generating a magnetic field, which means is designed to generate a magnetic travelling field which acts on the reactor.
problem: Separating ferromagnetic particles from a suspension flowing through a reactor.
constraint: The magnetic field's strength and travel speed must be optimized to capture particles efficiently while maintaining suspension flow rates and avoiding turbulence.
mechanism: Generating a propagating magnetic field within a flow path that moves along its length, capturing and transporting magnetically responsive particles toward an outlet. The traveling field enables continuous particle collection without disrupting the suspension flow.
mechanism_raw: Generating a magnetic travelling field within the reactor that propagates along its length, capturing and transporting ferromagnetic particles toward the outlet. The moving field ensures continuous particle collection without clogging.

abstract: A liquid crystal display including two substrates arranged opposite to each other; a liquid crystal sealed between the substrates; and a polymer layer for regulating a pretilt angle of liquid crystal molecules and/or tilt directions at a time of driving. One of the substrates has a color filter layer formed on a side of the one substrate, and a plurality of stripe-like electrode patterns are provided on the color filter layer. The patterns are periodically arranged so that when polymerizable components mixed in the liquid crystal layer are polymerized to form the polymer layer while a voltage is applied to the liquid crystal layer between the electrode patterns and a second electrode on the other substrate, liquid crystal molecules in the liquid crystal layer are aligned in the extending directions of stripe-like electrode patterns.
problem: Controlling the alignment direction and pretilt angle of liquid crystal molecules in a display to achieve consistent optical performance.
constraint: Balancing the timing and voltage parameters during polymerization to ensure alignment without disrupting the structural integrity of the liquid crystal layer.
mechanism: Applying a spatially patterned voltage field during a polymerization process to create a structured polymer layer that imposes directional alignment on adjacent molecules through field-induced molecular orientation.
mechanism_raw: Applying a voltage between stripe-like electrode patterns during polymerization of a polymerizable component mixed in the liquid crystal layer, causing the polymer layer to form with a structure that aligns liquid crystal molecules in the direction of the electrode patterns.

abstract: Method of manufacturing a metal cord with three concentric layers (C1, C2, C3), of the type rubberized in situ, i.e. incorporating a composition made of rubber in the uncrosslinked state referred to as “filling rubber”, the said cable comprising a first, internal, layer or core (C1), around which there are wound together in a helix, at a pitch p2, in a second, intermediate, layer (C2), N wires of diameter d2, N varying from 3 to 12, around which second layer there are wound together as a helix at a pitch p3, in a third, outer, layer (C3), P wires of diameter d3, P varying from 8 to 20, the said method comprising the following steps: a first sheathing step in which the core (C1) is sheathed with the filling rubber; a first assembling step by twisting the N wires of the second layer (C2) around the core (C1) thus sheathed in order to form, at a point named the “assembling point”, an intermediate cord named “core strand” (C1+C2); downstream of the said assembling point, a second sheathing step in which the core strand (C1+C2) is sheathed with the filling rubber; a second assembling step in which the P wires of the third layer (C3) are twisted around the core strand (C1+C2) thus sheathed; a final twist-balancing step.
reason: The patent describes a specific manufacturing process with sequential sheathing and twisting steps for a multi-layered metal cord. While the process is detailed, it does not describe a generalizable causal principle beyond the specific steps themselves, making it difficult to transfer to other fields.

abstract: A superimposed voltage waveform with a predetermined cycle and amplitude is superimposed on a commanded voltage waveform for a second predetermined time after a first predetermined time elapses within an arcing period in which an arc is produced. The predetermined cycle of the superimposed voltage waveform is shorter than a short-circuit cycle and longer than a control cycle of a welding power supply unit. This suppresses a growth of a weld droplet by being pushed up toward a consumable electrode and suppresses an excessive growth of the droplet over an entire range from a low current range, characterized by frequent short-circuits, to a medium to high current range where short-circuits are less frequent. The droplet is also smoothly transferred to the weld pool in addition to preventing excessive droplet growth. This reduces the generation of spatter, giving a flatter bead appearance.
problem: Controlling weld droplet growth and transfer in welding processes to reduce spatter and improve bead appearance across varying current ranges.
constraint: Matching the superimposed waveform's cycle and amplitude to the welding power supply's control cycle and arc dynamics to avoid destabilizing the process.
mechanism: Superimposing a periodic control signal with a cycle duration intermediate between two system time scales to modulate droplet dynamics, using the signal's amplitude to counteract excessive growth and synchronize transfer timing.
mechanism_raw: Superimposing a voltage waveform with a cycle shorter than a short-circuit cycle but longer than the welding power supply's control cycle, which physically pushes the droplet upward to suppress excessive growth and ensure smooth transfer to the weld pool.

abstract: A window restrictor that may be used to limit the opening of a window. The restrictor comprises a restrictor member and a latch mechanism. Typically, the restrictor member is attached to a stile or rail of the moving window pane and the latch mechanism is attached to a part of the casing or frame surrounding the window opening. In use, the restrictor member is engaged with the latch mechanism so that as the window is opened, the extent of opening is restricted by the restrictor member length. To fully open the window, the restrictor member is disengaged from the latch mechanism. When the restrictor member and latch mechanism are disengaged, they remain in such a configuration that, when the window is closed, the restrictor member and latch mechanism automatically re-engage to prevent the window being fully opened again. The restrictor member can comprise a hinged member which includes bias means.
problem: Limiting the opening of a window while allowing full opening when needed, with automatic re-engagement after closing.
constraint: Designing the mechanical linkage and bias force to ensure reliable engagement and disengagement without manual intervention.
mechanism: Using a mechanically biased linkage system that engages a position-limiting constraint through a latching interaction, automatically re-establishing the constraint when the system returns to a default state due to stored energy in the bias element.
mechanism_raw: Using a hinged restrictor member with bias means that engages a latch mechanism to limit opening, disengages when fully opened, and automatically re-engages when the window is closed due to the bias force.

abstract: A fitting used with a container holding a pressurized beverage and adapted for connection to a filling or dispensing device has an annular and outwardly projecting collar formed unitarily with the fitting and forming a passage opening into the container and a flexible burst membrane in the fitting and blocking the passage.
problem: Creating a temporary seal for a pressurized container that can be reliably ruptured when connected to a dispensing device.
constraint: Selecting membrane material and thickness to ensure it bursts at the desired pressure without premature failure or leakage.
mechanism: Incorporating a pressure-sensitive barrier element designed to fail at a predetermined threshold when external force is applied, creating a temporary seal that ruptures upon connection to a dispensing interface.
mechanism_raw: Incorporating a flexible burst membrane within the fitting that blocks a passage into the container, which ruptures under pressure or mechanical force when the fitting is connected to a dispensing device.

abstract: A method for handling aqueous solutions of methanesulfonic acid (MSA) having a concentration from 50 to 99% by weight of MSA and a total chlorine content of less than 50 mg/kg in apparatuses in which the aqueous MSA solution is in contact with steel surfaces. The steel comprises austenitic steels having a chromium content of from 15 to 22% by weight and a nickel content of from 9 to 15% by weight.
problem: Preventing corrosion of steel surfaces in contact with high-concentration aqueous methanesulfonic acid (MSA) solutions containing trace chlorine.
constraint: The alloy composition must balance corrosion resistance with mechanical properties while operating within the specified MSA concentration (50-99%) and chlorine content (<50 mg/kg) ranges.
mechanism: Selecting a metallic alloy composition enriched in passivating elements to form a chemically stable surface layer that resists degradation in aggressive acidic and halogenated environments.
mechanism_raw: Selecting an austenitic steel alloy with a specific chromium (15-22%) and nickel (9-15%) composition to form a stable passive oxide layer that resists degradation in the harsh acidic and chlorinated environment.
residual_terms: ["passivating elements", "stable surface layer", "acidic and halogenated environments"]

abstract: A method of forming a patterned photoresist layer having a hydrophobic surface is provided. The method includes forming a photoresist layer on a substrate and image patterning. The photoresist layer may comprise a polymeric material. The imaged photoresist layer may then undergo a two-stage post-exposure bake. A surface treatment may be performed on the photoresist layer in between the two-stage post-exposure bake. The surface treatment may include applying a siloxane solution on a partially post-exposure baked photoresist layer. The post-exposure baked photoresist layer may then be developed to form the patterned photoresist layer. The method may be used to form a hydrophobic photoimageable nozzle plate of a micro-fluid ejection head having improved mechanical properties and stable hydrophobic properties.
problem: Creating a photoresist layer with stable hydrophobic surface properties and improved mechanical integrity for micro-fluid ejection nozzles.
constraint: The timing and chemical compatibility of the siloxane treatment must align with the thermal profiles of the two-stage bake to avoid disrupting the photoresist's structural integrity or patterning resolution.
mechanism: Applying a chemical surface modifier between two sequential thermal conditioning stages to alter surface properties while preserving structural integrity through staged energy input.
mechanism_raw: Applying a siloxane-based surface treatment between two sequential post-exposure bake stages, where the intermediate treatment chemically modifies the photoresist surface to enhance hydrophobicity while the dual-bake process ensures structural stability.

abstract: A system and method that enables a user of a telematics-equipped vehicle to initiate security services by activating their vehicle keyfob. If a user senses an emergency situation, such as a person breaking into their home, they can engage a panic button on their vehicle keyfob. This causes the vehicle to send a wireless warning signal to a call center which already has emergency contact numbers on file. The call center can then call the user to see if they require assistance from a police department, fire department, ambulance, etc. In one embodiment, the method also determines if the vehicle is currently located within a certain proximity of one or more designated locations (usually the user's home or work) before contacting the user. This can reduce responses to non-emergencies, such as when a user simply presses their panic button in order to locate their vehicle in a crowded parking lot.
problem: Reducing false emergency responses triggered by accidental or non-emergency activation of a vehicle keyfob panic button.
constraint: The system must balance rapid emergency response with false-positive reduction, requiring precise geofencing and low-latency communication between the vehicle and call center.
mechanism: Cross-referencing a triggered signal against real-time location data relative to predefined spatial boundaries to conditionally enable or suppress a response based on contextual validity.
mechanism_raw: Using vehicle telematics to cross-validate the panic signal against the vehicle's real-time location relative to predefined zones (e.g., home/work), delaying or suppressing the emergency response unless the vehicle is within a designated proximity.
residual_terms: ["triggered signal", "real-time location data", "predefined spatial boundaries", "contextual validity"]

abstract: A helmet and/or helmet liner having one or more internal flexibility sipes for controlling and absorbing the impact of torsional or shear forces, including, for example, at least a first bladder, chamber, or compartment having an inner surface; a second bladder, chamber, or compartment having at least one cavity or void that at least partially encloses at least one gas, and an outer surface located in the first bladder, chamber, or compartment, as viewed in a cross-section, and at least one internal sipe, which is defined by a portion of the inner surface of the first bladder, chamber, or compartment and a portion of the outer surface of the second bladder, chamber, or compartment. The surface portions defining the internal sipe oppose each other and are configured to be movable relative to each other in a sliding motion and have at least one centrally located attachment between the surface portions.
problem: Absorbing and dissipating torsional or shear forces during impact events in protective headgear without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: The sipes must enable sufficient shear deformation to absorb impact energy while retaining enough structural cohesion to prevent catastrophic failure under extreme loads.
mechanism: Integrating internal compliant structures with opposing sliding interfaces between nested chambers to enable controlled relative motion that dissipates shear energy while maintaining a central load-bearing connection.
mechanism_raw: Integrating internal flexibility sipes—defined by opposing sliding surfaces between nested chambers—that allow controlled relative motion to dissipate shear energy while maintaining a central attachment point to preserve overall helmet structure.

abstract: A recipient verification system including a band to be worn by a patient or other recipient that allows for placement of a hospital's own identification label, which is then protected from damage, an area for a permanent label, which can then be associated with the hospital label, a series of removable labels that remain with the patient, a test tube label, and a tail of labels to be removed from the band at the time of application to the patient to ensure a sufficient supply of labels. Each of the permanent label, the removable labels, the test tube label, and the tail are encoded with identical identification information. The band and label strip are separately formed from desired materials and then assembled.
problem: Ensuring accurate, durable, and synchronized patient identification across multiple labeling systems (e.g., wristbands, test tubes) while preventing label loss or damage.
constraint: The label materials and encoding methods must maintain consistency across all components while allowing selective removal of the tail without disrupting the remaining labels' integrity or readability.
mechanism: Encoding identical identification information across a series of labels integrated into a single carrier system, with a sacrificial supply segment that ensures sufficient labels remain after application without disrupting remaining label integrity.
mechanism_raw: Encoding identical identification information across a series of labels (permanent, removable, test tube, tail) integrated into a single band system, with the tail serving as a sacrificial supply regulator to ensure sufficient labels remain after application.
residual_terms: ["identical identification information", "single carrier system", "sacrificial supply segment", "label integrity"]

abstract: An integrally-rotating cylindrical sieve 1 includes a hollow rotating shaft 2, which a driveshaft 21 is inserted into and fixed to, support members 3 radially extended from the rotating shaft 2, a cylindrical sieve body 4 made from a thin plate with a large number of apertures 5 formed therein, such as punching metal, and coupled with the support members 3, and sieve frames 6a and 6b attached to axial ends of the sieve body 4. The rotating shaft 2, the support members 3, the sieve body 4, the sieve frames 6a and 6b, and the driveshaft 21 are coaxially rotated together. The sieve body 4 is a cylindrical corrugated plate having wave crests and wave troughs arranged along its circumference and has a large number of apertures 5 formed in the corrugated plate. This arrangement improves the sieving efficiency of the granular material and effectively prevents potential destruction and cracking of the granular material, thus enhancing the commercial value of the sieved granular material.
problem: Inefficient sieving of granular materials and potential damage to the material during separation processes.
constraint: Balancing structural integrity of the thin corrugated sieve body against the need for sufficient aperture density and rotational speed to achieve effective sieving without material degradation.
mechanism: A rotating cylindrical structure with a patterned surface generates controlled multi-directional motion of particulate material through the interaction of rotational movement and spatially varying surface geometry, enhancing separation efficiency while minimizing mechanical stress on individual particles.
mechanism_raw: A rotating cylindrical sieve with a corrugated sieve body creates controlled, multi-directional movement of granular material through the interaction of rotational motion and circumferential wave patterns, enhancing separation efficiency while reducing mechanical stress on individual particles.

abstract: After observing patio heaters at many events, hotels and restaurants, we, as decorators, knew they have little decorative appeal in beautiful settings.Patio heaters have gained popularity as people are enjoying more outdoor entertaining. We designed a cover to “hide” the heaters. Our cover is a tailored, box-pleat skirt design with three pleats, two side pleats are inset with fabric mesh to allow for ventilation of the tank, and detailed with a welt trim. Like a slip-cover, it fits over the neck and base of the heater, fastened with hook/loop sewn inside.All components are fire retardant. They are machine washable, hold their shape, offer protection from the elements, and have easy setup, and access to controls.
reason: The patent describes a specific product design (a decorative cover) with tailored features (pleats, mesh, fire retardant materials) rather than a generalizable causal mechanism. The solution is tied to the aesthetic and functional requirements of patio heaters, with no underlying principle that transfers to other domains.

abstract: A statically stabilized projectile may include a fixed tail boom that may be disposed in the through-bore of a sliding tail boom. The sliding tail boom may translate or extend rearward with respect to the fixed tail boom before the projectile exits a launch tube. The through-bore of the sliding tail boom may include a tapered portion. A tail boom sleeve may be fixed to a rear portion of the fixed tail boom. The tail boom sleeve may include a tapered portion that abuts the tapered portion of the through-bore when the sliding tail boom is in an extended position.
problem: Uncontrolled projectile orientation during launch, leading to instability or inaccurate trajectory.
constraint: Timing the extension of the sliding tail boom relative to launch acceleration and ensuring tapered surface engagement without jamming under high-G forces.
mechanism: A movable component extends relative to a fixed structure during launch, using tapered engagement surfaces to dynamically shift the projectile's balance point and aerodynamic characteristics, ensuring stable trajectory by adjusting center of mass and airflow interaction.
mechanism_raw: A sliding tail boom extends rearward before projectile exit, interacting with a fixed tail boom via tapered surfaces to dynamically adjust the projectile's center of mass and aerodynamic profile during launch, ensuring stable flight.

abstract: An information processing apparatus to create an arithmetic expression by combining one or more operators includes a detection unit to detect a permutation of plural operators existing in common to the plural created arithmetic expressions, and a registration unit to register the detected permutation of the operators as a new operator.
problem: Redundant computation in arithmetic expression generation due to repeated operator sequences across multiple expressions.
constraint: Identifying which operator permutations are sufficiently common to justify abstraction while avoiding overgeneralization that could obscure meaningful computational differences.
mechanism: Identifying recurring sequences of operations across multiple computational tasks and abstracting them into reusable composite operations, reducing redundant processing by enabling shared execution paths for common operator permutations.
mechanism_raw: Detecting permutations of operators common to multiple arithmetic expressions and registering them as new composite operators, enabling reuse of optimized operator sequences to streamline computation.

abstract: The embodiments disclosed herein are directed to fabrication methods useful for creating MEMS via microcontact printing by using small organic molecule release layers. The disclose method enables transfer of a continuous metal film onto a discontinuous platform to form a variable capacitor array. The variable capacitor array can produce mechanical motion under the application of a voltage. The methods disclosed herein eliminate masking and other traditional MEMS fabrication methodology. The methods disclosed herein can be used to form a substantially transparent MEMS having a PDMS layer interposed between an electrode and a graphene diaphragm.
problem: Complex and costly MEMS fabrication requiring traditional masking and patterning steps.
