constraint: Achieving precise control over release layer degradation and metal film adhesion to ensure reliable transfer while maintaining transparency and structural integrity in the final MEMS device.
mechanism: Employing a sacrificial layer with selective adhesion properties to transfer a continuous film onto a discontinuous substrate, enabling formation of mechanically movable structures through controlled degradation of the sacrificial layer without requiring patterned masking steps.
mechanism_raw: Using small organic molecule release layers to enable transfer of a continuous metal film onto a discontinuous platform, allowing formation of mechanically movable structures (e.g., variable capacitors) without masking by leveraging selective adhesion and release properties.

abstract: The present device is a detachable core for use with a cylindrical filter cartridge. The core includes a wire frame including at least two vertical struts oriented along a longitudinal direction. The wire frame includes an upper ring and a lower ring mounted to the distal ends of the vertical struts and further includes an upper flange and a lower flange mounted to the upper and lower rings respectively, wherein the lower flange is detachably mounted to the lower ring. Preferably the lower ring includes a gap in the lower ring to enable resilient compression of the ring by squeezing the lower ring in a radial inward direction prior to engagement with the lower flange. Preferably the cartridge filter includes elastomeric end caps and the cooperating rings and flanges are non-circular such that the elastomeric end caps conforms to the non-circular shape of the upper and lower flanges.
problem: Creating a detachable core for a cylindrical filter cartridge that allows easy assembly while maintaining secure engagement with the filter.
constraint: Balancing detachability for assembly with structural integrity and secure engagement during operation.
mechanism: A gap in a structural ring enables radial compression during assembly, allowing engagement with a mating component. A non-uniform cross-sectional geometry between the ring and a flange ensures alignment and prevents rotational slippage. A resilient material conforms to the geometry, maintaining a secure connection without continuous external force.
mechanism_raw: A gap in the lower ring enables radial compression of the ring during assembly, allowing the lower flange to engage. The non-circular shape of the rings and flanges ensures elastomeric end caps conform to the geometry, providing a resilient and secure connection.

abstract: A fat base is described comprising a mixture containing from 4 to 20% C12:0 lauric acid, preferentially from 5 to 17%, from 30 to 50% C16:0 palmitic acid, preferentially from 34 to 45%, and 4 to 10% C18:0 stearic acid, preferentially from 4.5 to 7.5%, and from 20 to 40% C18:1 oleic acid, preferentially from 25 to 35%, the balance being a mixture of other C4:0 to C22:0 fatty acids, having application, for example, as filling for wafer biscuits.
reason: The patent describes a specific composition of fatty acids for a food filling, which is a material formulation rather than a functional mechanism. The ratios of components are tailored to achieve desired physical properties (e.g., texture, melting point) but do not describe a causal operational principle transferable to other fields.

abstract: A spacer profile for a spacer frame of an insulating pane unit includes a hollow profile body made of plastic with a chamber defined therein. The hollow profile body extends in a longitudinal direction and includes an inner wall, an outer wall, a first side wall and a second side wall, which are connected to the inner and outer walls to form the chamber. First and second reinforcing layers made of a metallic material respectively extend on the first and second side walls and partially on the outer wall so as to be spaced apart by a first distance. A diffusion barrier layer is formed directly on the outer wall between the first and second reinforcing layers and is connected thereto in a diffusion-proof manner in order to form a heat-insulating diffusion barrier. An insulating pane unit includes at least two panes with such a spacer frame disposed therebetween.
problem: Providing thermal insulation in an insulating pane unit while maintaining structural support and preventing gas diffusion.
constraint: Balancing thermal performance (insulation) with structural support and diffusion resistance in a lightweight, durable design.
mechanism: A hollow chamber within a structural body creates an insulating region, while reinforcing layers on opposing surfaces provide mechanical strength. A barrier layer positioned between the reinforcing layers restricts gas migration, integrating thermal performance with structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A hollow plastic profile body creates an insulating chamber, while metallic reinforcing layers on the side walls provide structural strength. A diffusion barrier layer between the reinforcing layers prevents gas exchange, combining thermal insulation with structural integrity.

abstract: A fuel flow meter assembly for detecting fraud caused by tampering. The fuel flow meter assembly includes a fuel flow meter comprising a shaft and a displacement sensor operatively connected to the fuel flow meter shaft for generating information representative of an amount of fuel delivered through the fuel flow meter. At least one transponder is coupled with one of the fuel flow meter shaft and the displacement sensor. At least one interrogator electronics is coupled with the other of the fuel flow meter shaft and the displacement sensor. The at least one interrogator electronics is configured for remote electronic communication with the at least one transponder.
problem: Detecting fraud caused by tampering in a fuel flow meter without requiring physical access to the meter.
constraint: Ensuring reliable wireless communication between the transponder and interrogator while maintaining tamper resistance and operational accuracy.
mechanism: A wireless communication element coupled to a monitored component transmits operational data to a remote receiver. Discrepancies between expected and actual data patterns indicate tampering, enabling detection without physical access to the component.
mechanism_raw: A transponder coupled to the meter's shaft or sensor communicates wirelessly with interrogator electronics on the opposite component. This enables remote monitoring of the meter's operation, detecting discrepancies caused by tampering.

abstract: The present disclosure provides pre-treatment compositions and related methods. As such, a pre-treatment coating for a print medium can include a an evaporable solvent, a matrix, and a wax. The matrix can include from 5 wt % to 20 wt % of a fixer, from 5 wt % to 20 wt % of a low Tg latex, and from 30 wt % to 80 wt % of a high Tg latex. The wax can include from 5 wt % to 30 wt % of a wax. The weight percentages of the matrix and the wax are based on a total amount present in the pre-treatment coating after removal of solvent.
problem: Preparing a print medium to optimize ink adhesion and drying in printing processes.
constraint: Balancing the proportions of fixer, latexes, and wax to achieve optimal ink adhesion, drying time, and print quality without interfering with the printing process.
mechanism: A multi-component coating matrix combines a binding agent, two polymeric materials with distinct glass transition temperatures, and a volatile-regulating additive. The matrix controls ink interaction with the substrate, while the additive modulates solvent evaporation kinetics, creating a controlled environment for ink penetration and drying.
mechanism_raw: A pre-treatment coating combines a fixer, low-Tg and high-Tg latexes, and wax. The matrix (fixer and latexes) controls ink interaction, while the wax regulates solvent evaporation. The layered composition creates a controlled environment for ink penetration and drying.

abstract: A compressed air stream is cooled in an exchanger to form a compressed cooled air stream. The stream is then cryogenically compressed in a first compressor to form a first pressurized gas stream. The first pressurized gas stream is further cooled in the exchanger, cryogenically compressed in a second compressor, and then it is cooled and partially liquefied. The cooled and partially liquefied product is then fed to a system of distillation columns. A liquid product is removed from the system of distillation columns. This product is then pressurized, vaporized and warmed in the exchanger to yield pressurized gaseous product.
problem: Efficiently separating and processing gases (e.g., air) into liquid and gaseous products using cryogenic methods while minimizing energy consumption.
constraint: Balancing energy efficiency between compression/cooling stages and heat recovery during vaporization, while maintaining structural integrity of the system under cryogenic conditions.
mechanism: Progressively lowering the temperature of a gas stream through staged compression and cooling until partial liquefaction occurs, then separating components by volatility in a distillation stage. The separated liquid fraction is pressurized and passed through a heat exchange stage where it is vaporized and warmed using recovered thermal energy, producing a final gaseous output while minimizing overall energy input.
mechanism_raw: Sequential cryogenic compression and cooling of a gas stream to progressively lower temperatures, enabling partial liquefaction and subsequent distillation. The cooled and partially liquefied product is separated in distillation columns, while the liquid product is re-pressurized, vaporized, and warmed in a heat exchanger to recover energy and produce a final gaseous output.

abstract: In the case of a method for the production of punched parts in web- or sheet-like print substrates, wherein the punched parts are punched in the pass of the print substrates through a punching tool and thereafter provided in the pass through a further tool with a feature which requires a positioning within predetermined limits on them, it is suggested according to the invention that markings are punched out with the punching tool in the print substrates in each case arranged in a tolerance-free manner in terms of their position relatively to the punched parts and that these markings are used in the subsequent processing of the punched parts for guiding the feature mentioned.
problem: Ensuring precise alignment of a secondary processing tool (e.g., a feature-adding tool) relative to punched parts in a web or sheet substrate without relying on external measurement systems.
constraint: Maintaining the positional accuracy of the reference markings during the initial punching step to ensure they remain reliable guides for downstream processing.
mechanism: Creating positional reference features on a substrate concurrently with primary processing features, so that the references maintain a fixed spatial relationship to the processed elements. These references are subsequently used as alignment guides for a secondary processing tool, thereby eliminating cumulative positional errors without external measurement.
mechanism_raw: Punching positional reference markings in the substrate simultaneously with the primary punched parts, ensuring the markings are always in a fixed, tolerance-free spatial relationship to the parts. These markings are then used as guides for subsequent tool positioning, eliminating cumulative alignment errors.

abstract: A substrate processing apparatus comprises: a reaction chamber to process a substrate; a heating target object disposed in the reaction chamber to surround at least a region where the substrate is disposed, the heating target object having a cylindrical shape with a closed end; an insulator disposed between the reaction chamber and the heating target object to surround the heating target object, the insulator having a cylindrical shape with a closed end facing the closed end of the heating target object; an induction heating unit disposed outside the reaction chamber to surround at least the region where the substrate is disposed; a first gas supply system to supply at least a source gas into the reaction chamber; and a controller to control the first gas supply system so that the first gas supply system supplies at least the source gas into the reaction chamber for processing the substrate.
problem: Achieving uniform and efficient heating of a substrate within a reaction chamber while minimizing heat loss and maintaining thermal isolation.
constraint: Ensuring the cylindrical geometry of the heating target and insulator maintains structural stability and thermal efficiency under high-temperature conditions.
mechanism: Positioning a thermally conductive target element with a closed end around the substrate, and surrounding it with a concentric insulating element also having a closed end. External energy input is directed at the target element, which radiates heat uniformly inward toward the substrate, while the insulator reduces thermal loss to the surrounding environment.
mechanism_raw: Using a cylindrical heating target object with a closed end positioned to surround the substrate, combined with a concentric cylindrical insulator also with a closed end. Induction heating elements outside the chamber focus thermal energy on the heating target, which radiates heat uniformly to the substrate while the insulator reduces heat dissipation to the environment.

abstract: The present invention relates to a method for the determination of the coefficient of performance of a refrigeration machine, in particular of a heat pump, which includes a closed circuit which has a refrigerant and in which an evaporator, a compressor, a condenser and an expansion valve are arranged. In the method, at least three temperatures of the refrigerant are determined using temperature sensors arranged in the circuit. Alternatively, at least two temperatures and at least one pressure of the refrigerant is determined using sensors arranged in the circuit. Enthalpies of the circuit are calculated from the determined refrigerant temperatures and refrigerant pressures and the heat output and the taken up electrical power of the refrigeration machine are calculated therefrom to determine the coefficient of performance of the refrigeration machine from the quotient of the calculated heat output and the calculated taken up electrical power. The invention also relates to a refrigeration machine for the carrying out of such a method.
problem: Accurately determining the coefficient of performance (COP) of a refrigeration machine or heat pump without direct measurement of enthalpy or heat transfer.
constraint: Ensuring sensor accuracy and calibration to maintain reliable temperature and pressure measurements, which directly affect the precision of the derived COP value.
mechanism: Measuring temperature and pressure at multiple points in a thermodynamic circuit and deriving corresponding enthalpy values from these measurements. The enthalpy differences are used to calculate heat transfer rates and electrical power consumption, and the ratio of heat output to power input yields the coefficient of performance.
mechanism_raw: Deriving thermodynamic properties (e.g., enthalpies) from measured refrigerant temperatures and pressures at multiple points in the circuit. These calculated enthalpies are used to compute heat output and electrical power consumption, enabling COP determination via their ratio.

abstract: A portable DC power manager (400) includes an internal power bus (410) and a plurality of device ports (1150, 1160, 1170, 1180, 1190, 1200) for connecting with external power and energy sources, external power loads and other external power managers. Each device port is isolated for the internal power bus by controllable switches (A, B, C, D). Power converters (440, 442, 510) may be disposed between device ports and the internal power bus to convert voltages and attenuate current amplitude. Energy management schema operating on the power manager sums available power and allocates the available power to connected power loads according to power priority settings. A hot-change-over circuit (1300) connects additional sources to the internal bus in response to a voltage drop on the internal power bus. A compact and lightweight package (1100) enables a portability.
problem: Dynamically managing power distribution among multiple external sources and loads in a portable DC power system while maintaining stable voltage and prioritizing critical loads.
constraint: Balancing portability (compact, lightweight design) with the need for real-time power allocation and seamless source switching without disrupting connected loads.
mechanism: Monitoring available power from multiple sources and dynamically allocating it among connected loads according to predefined priority levels. When the internal bus voltage falls below a threshold, an automatic switching mechanism connects additional sources to maintain stable voltage and continuous operation during transitions.
mechanism_raw: Using an energy management controller to sum available power from connected sources and allocate it to loads based on priority settings. A hot-change-over circuit monitors the internal bus voltage and automatically connects additional power sources when voltage drops below a threshold, ensuring continuous operation during source transitions.
residual_terms: ["energy management controller", "hot-change-over circuit", "internal bus voltage", "priority settings"]

abstract: A cooling arrangement adapted to be used in a process of preparing a fine powder, and a method for using same are described. The cooling arrangement (100) comprises: a solid particles feed ingress means, a solid particles mixing means (140), a plurality of cooling air discharging devices (130) and a solid particles egress means. The cooling arrangement is characterized in that the averaged diameter of the solid particles fed the said solid particles ingress means is essentially less than 6 mm. Preferably, the solid particles are fed to the cooling arrangement and free fall (120) onto the bottom section thereof.
problem: Efficient cooling of fine powder particles during preparation
constraint: Particle size must remain below 6mm to ensure sufficient surface-area-to-volume ratio for effective cooling while avoiding airflow blockage or uneven heat dissipation
mechanism: Controlled particle size during free-fall through a cooling medium with distributed airflow to optimize convective heat transfer by maintaining optimal particle-air interaction and airflow dynamics
mechanism_raw: Free-fall of solid particles with controlled diameter (<6mm) through a cooling chamber with distributed air discharge devices, enabling enhanced convective heat transfer by maintaining optimal particle-air interaction and airflow dynamics
residual_terms: ["free-fall", "cooling chamber", "air discharge devices", "convective heat transfer", "particle size"]

abstract: The present invention relates to a heat-generating composition, comprising a hetero-structure nanomaterial which comprises (a) a first material comprising at least one component selected from the group consisting of a metal, a metal chalcogen, a metal pnicogen, an alloy and a multi-component hybrid structure thereof; and (b) a second material comprising at least one component selected from the group consisting of metal, metal chalcogen, metal pnicogen, alloy and the multi-component hybrid structure thereof; wherein the first material is enclosed in the second material; wherein at least one of the first material and the second material comprise a magnetic material. The specific loss power of the present nanomaterial is much higher than that of conventional nanomaterials (e.g., 40-fold higher than commercially accessible Feridex) and may be controlled by changing compositions or ratios of the first material and/or the second material. The heat-generating nanomaterial of the present invention may be used in a variety of application fields, for example cancer hyperthermia.
problem: Achieving high-efficiency heat generation with controllable output for applications like cancer hyperthermia
constraint: Composition and ratio of core-shell materials must be precisely controlled to balance magnetic coupling efficiency with biocompatibility and thermal stability
mechanism: Core-shell structure with a magnetic core enclosed in a secondary material to amplify specific loss power through synergistic magnetic interactions and enable tunable heating via compositional ratios
mechanism_raw: Core-shell heterostructure nanomaterial where a magnetic first material is enclosed in a second material, amplifying specific loss power through synergistic magnetic interactions and enabling tunable heating via compositional ratios
residual_terms: ["core-shell", "magnetic core", "secondary material", "specific loss power", "synergistic magnetic interactions"]

abstract: An object of the present invention is to provide an organic EL element lighting device whereby surge current can be reduced at start-up while controlling start-up variation, along with a lighting fixture using the same. Provided are a current supply part for supplying lighting current to a light source formed of one or more organic EL elements and connected between output terminals of the current supply part, a current detection part for detecting the lighting current, a target setting part for setting a target value of the lighting current, and a control part for performing feedback control of the lighting current by controlling the current supply part so that the detected value of the current detection part matches the target value of the lighting current. The target setting part has a sweep period during which the target value is gradually increased at start-up of the light source.
problem: Reducing surge current and start-up variation in organic EL lighting systems
constraint: Sweep rate must balance surge suppression with acceptable start-up time to avoid perceptible delay in lighting activation
mechanism: Feedback control system with a sweep period that gradually increases the target current during start-up, dynamically adjusting power delivery to match load conditions and suppress transient overcurrent
mechanism_raw: Feedback control system with a sweep period that gradually increases the target current during start-up, dynamically adjusting power delivery to match load conditions and suppress transient overcurrent

abstract: The resolution of a low-resolution image is made high and a stereoscopic image is displayed. Resolution is made high by super-resolution processing. In this case, the super-resolution processing is performed after edge enhancement processing is performed. Accordingly, a stereoscopic image with high resolution and high quality can be displayed. Alternatively, after image analysis processing is performed, edge enhancement processing and super-resolution processing are concurrently performed. Accordingly, processing time can be shortened.
problem: Improving image resolution and quality while minimizing processing time in super-resolution systems
constraint: Processing order and concurrency must balance computational load against resolution gains to avoid diminishing returns in image quality
mechanism: Sequential application of edge enhancement followed by super-resolution processing, or concurrent execution after image analysis, to optimize computational efficiency and output fidelity by leveraging complementary enhancement stages
mechanism_raw: Sequential application of edge enhancement followed by super-resolution processing, or concurrent execution after image analysis, to optimize computational efficiency and output fidelity by leveraging complementary enhancement stages

abstract: A device for releasably retaining a cord or flexible tube. The device includes a U-shaped yoke and a rotatable handle sized for gripping by the hand of a user. The cord or flexible tube is releasably received by a capture cap and can emanate directly therefrom or be routed to a loop located at the end of the handle in order to alter its orientation.
reason: The device is a mechanical retention solution with specific structural components (U-shaped yoke, rotatable handle, capture cap) that do not embody a generalizable causal principle applicable to other fields

abstract: A swimming pool cleaner of the type movable along an underwater pool surface to clean debris therefrom. The pool cleaner includes a body having a debris inlet and a debris outlet. A rigid debris-collection canister is secured to the body over the debris outlet to collect debris in the rigid canister and pass filtered water either back into the pool or to a remote suction system such that the collected debris remain at the pool-cleaner body for easy maintenance while allowing free flow of water through the rigid canister. The rigid canister is shaped to minimize obstructions to the pool cleaner movement in the pool by providing improved buoyancy and limiting entrapment of the cleaner by underwater pool structures. The cleaner body is adapted for securement of either a water-suction hose connected to a remote suction system or a venturi-line structure connected to a water-flow line fed by a remote pump such that the pool cleaner is interchangeably usable as a suction cleaner and as a pressure cleaner.
problem: Need to collect debris from a moving underwater cleaning device while permitting continuous water flow through the collection point and preventing the device from becoming trapped or obstructed by pool structures.
constraint: The canister must simultaneously retain debris and permit unobstructed water flow, while its shape must optimize buoyancy and movement clearance to avoid entrapment — balancing collection capacity, hydraulic throughput, and mechanical mobility.
mechanism: A flow-permeable collection chamber is positioned at a debris outlet of a moving device, creating a localized trapping zone that retains solid particles while permitting fluid to pass through the chamber walls. The chamber's geometry is configured to provide buoyancy and minimize spatial obstructions, enabling the device to navigate without entanglement. A modular connection interface allows the chamber to adapt to different operational modes of the device.
mechanism_raw: A rigid debris-collection canister is secured over the debris outlet, forming a local chamber that traps solid debris while allowing filtered water to flow through the canister walls. The canister's rigid shape is engineered to provide buoyancy and minimize geometric obstructions, so the moving cleaner is not caught or entangled by surrounding structures. An interchangeable connection interface allows the same body to operate as either a suction cleaner or a pressure cleaner.

abstract: The invention describes a system and a method for controlling an electric generator connected to the power grid during a voltage drop in the power grid, the system comprising a back-to-back converter (2) connected between the generator (3) and the power grid (4) and also, in parallel to the generator side converter (2a), rectifying means (5) connected in series between the generator (3) and the DC-link (2b) of the back-to-back converter (2), thus providing an alternative way for the energy excess at the generator side to enter the DC-link (2b).
problem: Need to manage excess electrical energy generated at the generator side when the power grid experiences a voltage drop, which constrains the normal power transfer path through the back-to-back converter.
constraint: The alternative rectifying path must activate only when the primary converter path is constrained by grid conditions, and must route excess energy into the DC-link without disrupting normal grid-connected operation or causing overvoltage.
mechanism: A primary power conversion path normally regulates energy transfer between a generator and a grid. When grid conditions constrain the primary path, a parallel conductive pathway activates to redirect excess generator energy into an intermediate energy storage node, bypassing the constrained path and preventing energy accumulation at the generator side.
mechanism_raw: A back-to-back converter normally regulates power flow between the generator and the grid. During a grid voltage drop, rectifying means connected in parallel to the generator-side converter and in series with the DC-link provide an alternative conductive path for excess generator energy to enter the DC-link, bypassing the constrained primary converter path and preventing energy buildup or instability at the generator side.
residual_terms: ["primary power conversion path", "intermediate energy storage node", "grid voltage drop"]

abstract: A capacitance-sensing device including a current-to-voltage converter and an analog-to-digital converter is described. A sense element is coupled to an input of the current-to-voltage converter. The current-to-voltage converter is configured to convert current changes in the coupled sense element to an output voltage and to maintain a constant voltage at the input. The analog-to-digital converter is configured to convert the output voltage generated by the current-to-voltage converter to a digital value.
problem: Need to accurately sense capacitance changes in a sense element while maintaining stable operating conditions at the sensing interface.
constraint: The converter must maintain a constant voltage at the sense element input (virtual ground) to ensure linear charge integration, while accurately converting small current changes to measurable voltage levels — balancing input impedance, integration accuracy, and signal-to-noise ratio.
mechanism: A signal conditioning circuit maintains a reference voltage at an input terminal of a sensing element, converting current variations caused by capacitance changes into proportional voltage signals through charge accumulation. A digitization stage then transforms the voltage signal into a digital representation of the capacitance variation.
mechanism_raw: A current-to-voltage converter (transimpedance amplifier) is coupled to the sense element and maintains a constant voltage (virtual ground) at its input terminal. Current changes in the sense element — caused by capacitance variations — are converted to a proportional output voltage through charge integration at the amplifier. An analog-to-digital converter then digitizes this output voltage to produce a digital representation of the capacitance change.

abstract: A stripper roller for use in a stripper unit subassembly is disclosed to simplify changing and replacement of parts. Brushes and batts are mounted in interlocking core segments that rotate in rigid accompaniment with a center shaft. The core segments are secured together and secured to the center shaft using retainer caps, and the retainer caps in turn are secured to the shaft to prevent lateral sliding of the stripper roller. Individual batts and brushes may be inserted into or removed from a reusable core segment, or the individual batts and brushes may be integrally affixed to replaceable core segments.
problem: Need to simplify replacement and maintenance of individual brush and batt components in a rotating stripper roller without requiring complete disassembly or replacement of the entire assembly.
constraint: The interlocking segments and retainer caps must maintain structural integrity and prevent lateral sliding during high-speed rotation, while still allowing individual components or segments to be accessed and replaced without specialized tools or complete disassembly.
mechanism: A rotating assembly comprises interlocked structural segments fastened to a central axis via retaining mechanisms, forming a rigid unitary structure. Replaceable functional elements are selectively insertable into or removable from the segments, enabling component-level maintenance. Alternatively, entire segments with pre-assembled functional elements can be substituted as modular units.
mechanism_raw: Interlocking core segments are secured together and to a center shaft using retainer caps, forming a rigid rotating assembly. Individual batts and brushes can be inserted into or removed from reusable core segments, allowing component-level replacement. Alternatively, entire core segments with integrally affixed components can be swapped out as replaceable units, enabling both granular and modular maintenance approaches.

abstract: An continuous meat grinding reclaiming system that provides a primary meat grinder unit and a secondary meat grinding unit for continuously and simultaneously processing a meat batch in a single processing run. The primary meat grinder unit is designed to grind a batch of meat by initially separating or extrapolating pure meat from the meat that contains bone; collecting the pure meat into a container; and transferring the meat that contains the bone to the secondary meat grinder unit. The secondary meat grinder unit is designed to further grind the batch of meat by separating additional pure meat from the meat that contains the bone; collecting this additional pure meat into the container with the original pure meat; and discard any remaining “undesireables”. The meat grinding reclaiming system also provides an inventive variable valve reducer for controlling the flow of the undesireables through the secondary transfer pipe.
problem: Need to continuously and simultaneously process a meat batch to maximize recovery of pure meat from bone-containing material in a single processing run, rather than through separate batch operations.
constraint: The two-stage system must operate continuously and simultaneously in a single run, with the variable valve balancing the flow of undesirables to maintain optimal separation efficiency at both stages while maximizing overall meat recovery and minimizing waste.
mechanism: A two-stage processing system operates continuously and simultaneously, where a primary separation unit isolates target material from contaminants and transfers residual material to a secondary separation unit. The secondary unit further isolates target material, combining recovered output with the primary unit's output. A flow control mechanism regulates the transfer rate of residual material between stages to balance throughput and separation efficiency.
mechanism_raw: A primary grinder performs initial separation of pure meat from bone-containing meat, collecting the pure meat into a common container while transferring the bone-containing material to a secondary grinder. The secondary grinder performs further separation, recovering additional pure meat that is combined with the original pure meat in the same container, while discarding remaining undesirables. A variable valve reducer controls the flow rate of undesirables through the secondary transfer pipe, regulating throughput and separation efficiency.

abstract: A micro spike having a three-dimensional structure made of single crystalline silicon and being capable of picking an enough amount of a tissue to examine the tissue while minimizing an examinee's pain with a minimal invasion when picking the tissue and a method of manufacturing the same are disclosed. The micro spike comprising: a main body part; extension parts inserted into a tissue when picking the tissue sample and integratedly extended from upper and lower parts of one side of the main body part; and a protrusion part integratedly protruded from at least one of side surfaces of the extension parts and inserted into the tissue to pick the tissue sample together with the extension parts when picking the living tissue sample.
problem: Picking enough tissue for examination while minimizing pain and invasion to the examinee
constraint: Balancing tissue pickup volume against invasion depth and pain — more engagement points increase sample size but also increase tissue trauma
mechanism: A distributed engagement structure with multiple micro-contact points that increase sample collection volume through spatially separated tissue interactions, where each point minimizes localized trauma by limiting individual puncture depth and area
mechanism_raw: A 3D microstructured spike with extension parts and protrusion parts that engage tissue at multiple distributed points — the protrusions on the extensions provide additional tissue pickup without increasing the primary puncture area, allowing sufficient sample collection through distributed micro-engagement while each individual point minimizes local tissue damage

abstract: According to some embodiments, a cable protection system to at least partially shield a cable from heat, fire, an impact or other potentially harmful event or occurrence comprises a first encompassing member configured for placement around the cable or cable bundle, wherein a first void is defined between the first encompassing member and an outside of the cable or cable bundle. The system additionally includes a second encompassing member positioned around the first encompassing member, wherein a second void is defined between the first encompassing member and the second encompassing member. Further, the system comprises one or more fill materials positioned within the second void. In some embodiments, the fill material comprises vermiculite, ceramic and/or one or more other materials. The first void permits the cable protection system to be slidably moved relative to the cable or cable bundle.
problem: Shielding a cable from heat, fire, impact, or other harmful events while accommodating cable movement and positioning
constraint: Balancing protection effectiveness against flexibility and sliding capability — thicker fill material improves shielding but reduces mobility
mechanism: A nested multi-layer system with an inner sliding interface permitting relative motion between protective layers and a cable, and an outer protective medium that shields against hazards while the sliding interface decouples protection from cable movement
mechanism_raw: A nested multi-layer system where an inner void between the first encompassing member and the cable permits sliding movement of the protective system relative to the cable, while an outer void filled with protective fill material (vermiculite, ceramic) shields against thermal and mechanical hazards — the sliding void decouples protection from cable motion

abstract: A musical instrument stand is disclosed that includes at least, a pair of legs pivotally secured to a support portion and disposed within a leg retention channel of the support portion when the support portion is in a closed position, and extracted from the leg retention channel when the support portion is in an open position. Preferably, the support portion includes at least a position stop that limits the extent that each the open and closed positions of the support portion may attain. The musical instrument stand further preferably includes an over center latch assembly interposed between and communicating with the pair of legs, the over center latch maintains a predetermined separation between said first and second legs when the over center latch assembly is in a locked position, and nests within the pair of legs when the pair of legs are disposed within a leg retention channel.
problem: Creating a stand that folds compactly for storage and locks securely in an open position to support a musical instrument
constraint: Balancing compact storage volume against stable open support — the over-center geometry must provide enough force for locking while allowing easy release
mechanism: A pivoting linkage system with an over-center mechanism that generates positive locking forces at both extended and retracted positions through geometric force amplification, with position stops constraining motion range
mechanism_raw: An over-center latch assembly interposed between pivoting legs that maintains a predetermined separation between the legs when in a locked open position through over-center geometry, and nests within the leg pair when in a closed/stored position — the over-center action provides positive locking at both extremes of motion while position stops limit the range

abstract: A non-volatile memory device including a variable resistance material is provided. The non-volatile memory device may include a buffer layer, a variable resistance material layer and/or an upper electrode, for example, sequentially formed on a lower electrode. A schottky barrier may be formed on an interface between the buffer layer and the lower electrode. The variable resistance material layer may be formed with a variable resistance property.
problem: Creating reliable non-volatile memory with controlled variable resistance states and stable electrical behavior
constraint: Balancing resistance state stability and reliable switching against current control and forming behavior — the barrier height must allow sufficient current for switching while preventing uncontrolled conduction
mechanism: A barrier interface between conductive layers that modulates carrier injection and current density into a variable resistance material, enabling controlled resistance state transitions through barrier height regulation
mechanism_raw: A Schottky barrier formed at the interface between a buffer layer and lower electrode, combined with a variable resistance material layer, controls current flow and electrical characteristics at the critical interface — the Schottky barrier modulates carrier injection and current density into the variable resistance material, enabling controlled resistance switching

abstract: A watertight casing includes a top cover, a transparent rubber sealing layer, a frame-shaped spacer, a loop-shaped rubber seal, and a bottom cover. The top cover defines a rib along the top cover. The bottom cover defines a receiving space and a slot surrounding the receiving space. The receiving space is to receive a portable electronic device. The slot is to receive the second rubber and the rib. The transparent rubber sealing layer is secured to the frame-shaped spacer and the top cover, and is sandwiched between the frame-shaped spacer and the top cover. When the top cover is secured to the bottom cover, the rib presses the frame-shaped rubber seal into the slot to deform the frame-shaped rubber seal, causing the slot to be filled with the deformed loop-shaped rubber seal.
problem: Creating a watertight seal for portable electronic devices that can be repeatedly opened and closed while maintaining protection
constraint: Balancing sealing effectiveness against ease of assembly and disassembly — sufficient compression is needed for watertightness but must not make opening difficult or damage the seal over repeated cycles
mechanism: A compression-based sealing system where a mechanical actuator deforms a compliant seal into a receiving cavity through applied force, converting closure motion into controlled seal deformation for repeated watertight engagement
mechanism_raw: A rib on the top cover presses a frame-shaped rubber seal into a slot on the bottom cover, mechanically deforming the seal to fill the slot volume and create a watertight barrier through compression — the rib acts as a mechanical actuator that converts the closing force into controlled seal deformation

abstract: The invention relates to a torsion sonotrode (S) having a contact surface (1, 1′) for transferring a torsional oscillation directed about a torsion axis (T) onto a component (4) to be welded. To ensure that the welded joint has a uniform strength, it is proposed according to the invention that the contact surface (1, 1′) has a flat stop surface (2, 2′) which runs substantially perpendicular to the torsion axis (T) and from which elevations (3, 3′) of insular design extend with a pointed form.
problem: Ensuring uniform strength in a welded joint when transferring torsional oscillations to a component.
constraint: Balancing the geometric design of the elevations to maintain structural integrity while achieving uniform energy distribution.
mechanism: A contact surface with a perpendicular stop and distributed energy-dissipating elements transfers torsional oscillations uniformly across a component, preventing localized stress concentrations through geometric energy distribution.
mechanism_raw: A torsion sonotrode contact surface with a flat stop surface perpendicular to the torsion axis and insular, pointed elevations distributes torsional oscillation energy evenly across the component, preventing localized stress concentrations.

abstract: A straight edge razor enables the operator to move the blade between two different settings—a first setting that hides the two sharp corners of the blade, and a second setting that exposes the two sharp corners. The first setting can make shaving a client or oneself an easy task. In the second setting, the razor can be used as a tool for easily sharpening up lines on a haircut. The razor of the present invention also allows the operator to take the device apart for cleaning and replacing a damaged part.
problem: Enabling a single razor to perform both safe shaving and precise hairline detailing without compromising functionality.
constraint: Maintaining blade stability and safety in both settings while allowing quick transitions between modes.
mechanism: A position-switching system toggles between a safety configuration (restraining sharp edges) and a precision configuration (exposing functional edges), with modular components enabling mode transitions and maintenance.
mechanism_raw: A blade position adjustment system allows switching between a first setting (hiding sharp corners for safety) and a second setting (exposing corners for precision), with a modular design enabling part replacement and cleaning.

abstract: A cowl-top cover 10 for covering a vehicle body between a front window shield and a front hood is provided with: a seal portion abutting against a rear end lower part of the front hood; and a longitudinal wall portion 1 that supports the seal portion and that is erected in a vertical direction of a vehicle, wherein the longitudinal wall 1 includes a stepped portion 3 that is extended along the vertical direction, the longitudinal wall being shaped to be wavy in a widthwise direction of the vehicle.
problem: Providing a vehicle cowl-top cover that adapts to varying body shapes while maintaining a secure seal between the windshield and hood.
constraint: Balancing flexibility for shape adaptation with structural rigidity to maintain the seal under environmental stress.
mechanism: A flexible barrier with a structured profile (stepped and undulating geometry) adapts to variable shapes while maintaining sealing integrity through controlled vertical and lateral compliance.
mechanism_raw: A longitudinal wall with a stepped portion and a wavy widthwise profile allows vertical flexibility and lateral adaptability, ensuring conformability to different vehicle geometries while preserving sealing integrity.

abstract: The present invention relates to a discharge device for discharging sausage-shaped products comprising suspension elements from the discharge end of a clipping machine to a handling device for said sausage-shaped products. The discharge device comprises a first guide for said suspension elements, having a first end and a second end as well as an upper guide surface and two side surfaces and extending from the discharge end of said clipping machine towards the handling device, and second guide arranged at said side surfaces and extending at least approximately between the first and second end of said first guide. The discharge device further comprises transportation units for transporting said suspension elements along said first guide, including transportation elements with engagement elements which engage the second guide and which are guided through said second guide in a transportation direction by said transportation elements.
problem: Reliably transporting sausage-shaped products with suspension elements from a clipping machine to a handling device without jamming or damage.
constraint: Maintaining synchronization between the transportation elements and guides to avoid mechanical interference or product deformation.
mechanism: A dual-track transport system uses interacting engagement elements between moving units and a secondary guide to enforce synchronized, directional movement of suspended objects, preventing misalignment and mechanical interference.
mechanism_raw: A dual-guide system with transportation units featuring engagement elements that interact with the second guide ensures controlled, directional movement of suspension elements along the first guide, preventing misalignment.

abstract: A new and low cost method for producing single wall nanotubes and other allotropic forms of carbon. The method uses a high electric current and 127 VAC or 220 VAC power supplies to sublimation of a solid precursor, which material can be made of graphite. The solid precursor is connected to metallic electrodes, so that an intense electric current cross the contacts to pulverize the graphite under high temperature. The carbon materials are deposited in the wall of the reactor as well as in the electrodes, in an atmospheric pressure. The obtained material is purified in acids and, then, the carbon nanotubes are separated. In general, the synthesis is characterized by the absence of a metal catalyst, the employ of a short circuit current with an agent to produce carbon materials, the low pressure into reaction, and the assembly of the apparatus involving a low voltage of operation.
problem: Producing single-wall carbon nanotubes and other carbon allotropes at low cost without metal catalysts.
constraint: Controlling electric current intensity and thermal conditions to achieve consistent nanotube formation without external catalysts.
mechanism: An electrical discharge process sublimates a solid precursor material under high current and temperature, fragmenting it into carbon-based materials that deposit on surfaces, enabling catalyst-free synthesis at ambient pressure.
mechanism_raw: A high-current, short-circuit electrical discharge sublimates a solid graphite precursor under high temperature, pulverizing it into carbon materials that deposit on reactor walls and electrodes, enabling catalyst-free synthesis at atmospheric pressure.

abstract: An exemplary embodiment of a refrigerant charge monitoring system includes first and second sensors. The first sensor is operable for sensing temperature of a liquid refrigerant line that is connected to, within, or extending from an outlet of a condenser. The second sensor is operable for sensing pressure of the liquid refrigerant line. A controller is configured to determine at least one target pressure value from the sensed temperature of the liquid refrigerant line. The controller is configured to determine if the level of refrigerant charge is at, above or below an acceptable level based on a comparison of the sensed pressure of the liquid refrigerant line to the at least one target pressure value.
problem: Determining whether a refrigerant charge in a system is at, above, or below an acceptable level without direct measurement of the charge itself.
constraint: Relies on the physical correlation between temperature and pressure in the refrigerant line, which must remain stable for accurate inference.
mechanism: Using a sensor to derive a target value based on a known physical relationship between two measurable properties, then comparing this derived target to an actual measurement of one property to infer a system state.
mechanism_raw: Using a temperature sensor to derive a target pressure value based on the thermodynamic relationship between refrigerant temperature and pressure, then comparing this target to an actual pressure measurement to infer charge level.

abstract: A fixing device includes a fixing rotator unit and an induction heating portion. The fixing rotator unit includes a heating rotary belt, a pressing member being in contact with the inner surface of the heating rotary belt, a pressurizing rotator forming a fixing nip between the pressurizing rotator and the pressing member, a belt guide member including a guide portion and an extending portion, positioning the heating rotary belt, and guiding rotation. The induction heating portion includes a magnetic-flux generating portion, a magnetic core portion, and a support member supporting the magnetic-flux generating portion. The support member includes a positioning portion that positions the belt guide member by coming into contact with or engaging the extending portion to control a distance between the magnetic-flux generating portion and the outer surface of the heating rotary belt.
problem: Maintaining precise alignment and distance between an induction heating element and a moving heating belt in a rotating fixing device.
constraint: Requires direct physical contact between the positioning feature and the belt guide to maintain consistent spacing under dynamic motion.
mechanism: Using a mechanical element with a contact feature to actively maintain a fixed spatial relationship between a stationary component and a moving surface through direct physical engagement.
mechanism_raw: Using a mechanical support member with a positioning feature that physically contacts or engages an extending portion of a belt guide to actively control the gap between the magnetic flux generator and the belt surface.

abstract: An image forming apparatus starts to change a curl correcting amount until when an upstream end in a sheet conveying direction of a preceding sheet passes through a curl correcting unit and finishes changing the curl correcting amount until when a succeeding sheet that follows the preceding sheet reaches the curl correcting unit in a case when the preceding sheet and the succeeding sheet are both guided in the curl correcting unit through a conveying path and when the curl correcting amount is changed between curl correcting amounts of the preceding sheet and the succeeding sheet.
problem: Smoothly transitioning a corrective parameter (curl correction) between two sequentially processed sheets without disrupting the correction for either sheet.
constraint: The timing of the parameter change must be synchronized with sheet positions to avoid overlap or incomplete transitions.
mechanism: Synchronizing a parameter adjustment to occur entirely within a temporal gap between sequential items, initiating the change when a preceding item exits a processing zone and completing it before a succeeding item enters.
mechanism_raw: Initiating a parameter change when the upstream end of a preceding sheet exits the correction zone and completing the change before the succeeding sheet enters, ensuring the adjustment occurs entirely within the gap between sheets.

abstract: A catheter anchoring system, apparatus and method for securing a catheter to a patient's skin, having two flexible side members and a cross-member therebetween to which a retaining assembly is mounted. The retaining assembly may hold a catheter hub at an angle for patient comfort. Gripping tabs secure to each retaining assembly side are gripped while advancing a cannula guide needle into the patient's vein and while attaching the catheter hub to a medical accessory, such as intravenous (I.V.) tubing, for increased patient comfort, reduction of the risk in contamination and patient infection, and to more easily and quickly start an I.V.
problem: Securing a catheter to a patient's skin while allowing controlled angular positioning of the catheter hub for comfort and ease of attachment to medical accessories.
constraint: Balancing flexibility for patient movement with sufficient rigidity to maintain securement and angular positioning during use.
mechanism: Using a flexible structure with adjustable gripping elements to simultaneously secure an object to a surface while permitting controlled angular reorientation of the object relative to the surface.
mechanism_raw: Using flexible side members connected by a cross-member with a retaining assembly that grips the catheter hub at an adjustable angle, combined with gripping tabs that enable controlled advancement of the cannula and attachment of accessories.

abstract: A substrate for growing carbon nanotubes capable of elongating single-walled carbon nanotubes of an average diameter of less than 2 nm is provided. The substrate for growing carbon nanotubes 1 is equipped with a reaction prevention layer 3 formed on a base material 2, a catalyst material layer 4 formed on the reaction prevention layer 3, a dispersion layer 5 formed on the catalyst material layer 4, and a dispersion promotion layer 6 formed on the dispersion layer 5.
problem: Controlling the diameter of single-walled carbon nanotubes during growth to achieve an average diameter below 2 nm.
constraint: Each layer must be optimized to perform its specific function without interfering with adjacent layers or the growth process.
mechanism: Stacking functionally distinct layers to sequentially regulate nucleation, growth environment, and product separation, thereby constraining a dimensional property through controlled material interactions.
mechanism_raw: Stacking functional layers (reaction prevention, catalyst, dispersion, and dispersion promotion) to sequentially regulate nucleation, growth environment, and nanotube separation, thereby constraining diameter through controlled material interactions.

abstract: An imprinting method forms a predetermined pattern in a resist surface of a substrate coated with a photo-curing type resist by using a mold having a pattern of projections and recesses formed in a transfer surface. The method includes an alignment step, a press step, a UV irradiation step, and a release step. The steps are performed in plural units selected from independent units, composite units, and combinations of independent units and composite units. The mold and the substrate are paired with each other and conveyed between the units. An imprinting apparatus includes plural units which perform the steps in the imprinting method and which are selected from independent units in each of which one step is executed, composite units in each of which plural of steps are executed, and combinations of independent units and composite units; and conveying devices which convey the mold and the substrate.
problem: Efficiently performing multi-step nanoimprinting processes while maintaining alignment and throughput.
constraint: Balancing throughput and process efficiency by selecting unit configurations that minimize idle time while ensuring precise alignment between steps.
mechanism: Modular processing stations that execute subsets of steps, with conveyance systems moving workpieces between stations to enable flexible workflow configurations that balance throughput and alignment precision.
mechanism_raw: Modular processing units (independent or composite) that execute subsets of steps, with conveyance systems moving the mold and substrate between units to enable flexible workflow configurations.

abstract: In order to disinfect and to detoxify a fluid, a photoreactor contains at least two light sources. One light source activates the catalytic function of a semiconductor material in the fluid to reduce the concentration of contaminants in the fluid, such as by breaking down organic contaminants into non-toxic compounds. A second light source acts directly on living biological entities to sterilize or kill them and thereby disinfect the fluid, and can also serve to activate a semiconductor photocatalyst that in turn causes further damage to biological contaminants. The semiconductor photocatalyst is desirably attached to an optically transmitting fiber substrate in the fluid. The second light source in one embodiment is external to the fluid and illuminates the photocatalyst through transmitting surfaces in a fluid containment vessel. The light sources can comprise respective sets of plural LEDs.
problem: Disinfecting and detoxifying fluids by simultaneously addressing chemical contaminants and biological entities.
constraint: Optimizing light wavelengths and spatial placement to maximize both chemical decomposition and biological sterilization without interference between the two mechanisms.
mechanism: Dual activation mechanisms: one induces chemical decomposition via a catalyst, while the second directly targets biological entities for sterilization, with the catalyst positioned on an optically transmitting substrate to enhance interaction.
mechanism_raw: Dual light sources: one activates a semiconductor photocatalyst to break down organic contaminants, while the second directly targets biological entities for sterilization, with the photocatalyst mounted on an optically transmitting fiber substrate to enhance interaction.

abstract: In an exemplary method for forming contact holes, a substrate overlaid with an etching stop layer and an interlayer dielectric layer in that order is firstly provided. A first etching process then is performed to form at least a first contact opening in the interlayer dielectric layer. A first carbon-containing dielectric layer subsequently is formed overlying the interlayer dielectric layer and filling into the first contact opening. After that, a first anti-reflective layer and a first patterned photo resist layer are sequentially formed in that order overlying the carbon-containing dielectric layer. Next, a second etching process is performed by using the first patterned photo resist layer as an etching mask to form at least a second contact opening in the interlayer dielectric layer.
problem: Forming precise contact holes in layered dielectric materials without damaging underlying structures.
constraint: Maintaining alignment and material integrity during successive etching steps while ensuring the carbon layer effectively fills and protects underlying layers.
mechanism: Sequential etching processes using a sacrificial filler material that also serves as a mask, enabling precise definition of openings while preserving alignment and structural integrity of underlying layers.
mechanism_raw: Multi-step etching using a carbon-containing dielectric layer as a sacrificial filler and mask, enabling sequential etching processes to define openings while preserving alignment and structural integrity.

abstract: A panoramic oven door which has a counter door structure which comprises a first outer section of counter door in the shape of a substantially rectangular structural frame, which has a support groove surrounding its inner perimeter border; a second inner section of counter door in the shape of a substantially rectangular structural frame, which has a coupling flange surrounding its outer perimeter border; wherein said first and second sections of counter door are coupled between each other by means of a plurality of coinciding supports or brackets formed over the same and joined by means of fastening elements; in such a way that said coupling flange of the second inner section of the counter door is made to coincide within the support groove formed in the first outer section of the counter door; and wherein additionally, an isolating thermal seal made of fiber glass thread woven in the shape of a flat hose is interposed between said coupling flange and said support groove once coupled, to avoid direct contact between both sections of the counter door creating a thermal breaking between them; said isolating thermal seal also has a seam performed in close proximity to one of its borders and parallel along the entire length of the same, thus forming a small tubular section along the length of the border of the seal within which an additional cylindrical fiber glass seal of smaller diameter woven in a braid shape is introduced, resulting in a lateral re-border which acts as an obstruction and cushioning element for the support of the ceramic glass panel over the counter door avoiding direct contact with the same.
problem: Thermally insulating a multi-section oven door while maintaining structural support and preventing direct contact between components.
constraint: Balancing thermal isolation with structural support and ensuring the seal accommodates movement while maintaining insulation performance.
mechanism: A composite thermal barrier with a flexible sealing element interposed between coupled sections to create a thermal break and cushioning, preventing direct contact and heat transfer while accommodating movement.
mechanism_raw: A composite thermal seal with a tubular section and nested braid seal, interposed between coupled door sections to create a thermal break and cushioning, preventing direct contact and heat transfer.

abstract: An endoscope cleaning/disinfecting apparatus includes: a medicinal solution storage portion; a cleaning/disinfecting tank; a medicinal solution supplying conduit having one end communicating with the medicinal solution storage portion and the other end opening toward the cleaning/disinfecting tank; a medicinal solution supplying member; a medicinal solution receiving member provided inside the medicinal solution supplying member; and a medicinal solution collecting port which is openable/closable by a lid body, and formed at a position between the medicinal solution receiving member and the opening of the other end in the medicinal solution supplying conduit.
problem: Cleaning and disinfecting endoscopes by managing fluid flow and containment in a controlled manner.
constraint: Ensuring thorough cleaning by maintaining fluid circulation and containment while preventing contamination through controlled access via the lid.
mechanism: A nested conduit system with a controlled-access collection port positioned between a fluid supply member and a receiving member to regulate fluid flow and containment during cleaning operations.
mechanism_raw: A nested conduit system with a medicinal solution supplying member containing a receiving member, and a lid-controlled collecting port positioned between the conduit opening and the receiving member to regulate fluid flow and collection.
residual_terms: ["nested conduit system", "controlled-access collection port", "fluid supply member"]

abstract: The invention relates to a method for operating a dispensing device (10, 110) for releasing an agent from the dispensing device (10, 110) in defined manner into a surrounding environment (15) of the dispensing device (10, 110), the dispensing device (10, 110) comprising: a reservoir unit (16, 116) for accommodating an agent to be dispensed and a valve unit (17, 117) for defined opening and closing of a valve passage (26, 29, 34, 126, 129, 134) from the reservoir unit (16, 116) into the surrounding environment (15) of the dispensing device (10, 110), opening and closing of the valve passage (26, 29, 34, 126, 129, 134) proceeding as a function of an ambient temperature profile of the dispensing device (10, 110) and the valve passage (26, 29, 34, 126, 129, 134) being opened when the ambient temperature falls and the ambient temperature is above a first and/or second defined minimum temperature.
problem: Controlled release of an agent into an environment based on ambient temperature conditions.
constraint: Balancing temperature thresholds to ensure agent release only occurs within desired environmental conditions while avoiding unintended activation or failure to activate.
mechanism: A thermally-actuated release system that triggers agent deployment when ambient temperature crosses a defined threshold range, using material expansion/contraction to mechanically switch between sealed and open states without external energy input.
mechanism_raw: A temperature-responsive valve system that opens when ambient temperature falls but remains above a defined minimum, using thermal expansion/contraction or material properties to mechanically trigger valve actuation without external power.

abstract: A tool-bit holder (10) for varying tool-bit shank profiles comprising a hub (12) having a longitudinal bore (28) adapted for receiving a tool-bit shank (66, 70, 80). The hub (12) has a plurality of radial slots (38) communicating with the first section (30) of the longitudinal bore (28). The tool-bit holder (10) has a collar (14) fixedly attached to the hub (12) adjacent the open (29) and disposed annularly about the hub (12). A sleeve (16) is axially slidably mounted and disposed annularly about the hub (12). The sleeve (16) has a plurality of radial bores (48), each being in communication with a respective radial slot (38) of the hub (12) with a detent ball (18) disposed within each. A spring (20) is provided for biasing the sleeve (16) towards the open end (29) wherein the detent ball (18) engages an inner ramp face (46) of the collar (14).
problem: Adapting a tool-bit holder to accommodate varying shank profiles while maintaining secure engagement.
constraint: Ensuring sufficient spring force and detent geometry to maintain secure retention across different shank sizes without excessive play or binding.
mechanism: A compliant retention system that dynamically adjusts radial engagement through mechanical compliance and ramp-based locking, using stored elastic energy to maintain secure coupling across variable geometry interfaces.
mechanism_raw: A spring-biased sleeve with detent balls that automatically adjust radial positioning based on shank geometry, using mechanical compliance and ramp engagement to lock the tool-bit in place.

abstract: A brush head, particularly a toothbrush head, may have a plurality of cleaning elements, in particular bristle tufts, which are anchored by an end section in a brush carrier, wherein the cleaning elements may be cast with positive engagement in blind-hole shaped retaining recesses. For producing such a brush head different cleaning elements may be placed successively or simultaneously in different mold cavities and may be over-molded using different plastic materials from which injection-molding sections of the bristle carrier are formed in the process. In doing so, a first cleaning element is over-molded in a first mold cavity using a first plastic material, while a second cleaning element is over-molded in a second mold cavity using a second plastic material.
problem: Manufacturing a brush head with multiple cleaning elements of different materials in precise spatial arrangements.
constraint: Maintaining alignment and material compatibility between over-molded elements and the brush carrier during sequential or simultaneous molding processes.
mechanism: A multi-material forming process that integrates distinct functional elements in precise spatial arrangements through sequential cavity-specific molding, enabling localized property variation within a unified structure.
mechanism_raw: Multi-cavity injection molding where different cleaning elements are over-molded in separate cavities using distinct plastic materials, enabling localized material properties and structural integration.

abstract: A plasma processing systems having at least one plasma processing chamber, comprising a movable grounding component, an RF contact component configured to receive RF energy from an RF source when the RF source provides the RF energy to the RF contact component, and a ground contact component coupled to ground. The plasma processing system further includes an actuator operatively coupled to the movable grounding component for disposing the movable grounding component in a first position and a second position. The first position represents a position whereby the movable grounding component is not in contact with at least one of the RF contact component and the ground contact component. The second position represents a position whereby the movable grounding component is in contact with both the RF contact component and the ground contact component.
problem: Dynamically controlling plasma processing conditions by adjusting grounding configurations.
constraint: Precise positioning of the grounding component to ensure reliable electrical contact without arcing or unintended circuit disruption during transitions.
mechanism: A dynamically reconfigurable electrical interface that modulates plasma behavior by switching between non-contact and dual-contact grounding states, using positional actuation to alter circuit paths and impedance characteristics.
mechanism_raw: An actuator-driven movable grounding component that switches between non-contact and dual-contact positions with RF and ground components, altering electrical circuit paths to modulate plasma behavior.

abstract: A headgear for a head safety product such as a face shield, hardhat or welding helmet includes a spring buffered cradle mounted on the horizontal band of the headgear to improve the fit, function, stability and comfort of the headgear. The cradle is flexible and has a concave inner surface contoured to conform to the shape of the head. A spring element is coupled between the cradle and the horizontal band to buffer the tension between the band and the head and more equally distribute pressure across the head. In a preferred embodiment, an occipital cradle includes two leaf springs coupled to the rear portion of the horizontal band.
problem: Improving fit, stability, and comfort of headgear by distributing pressure evenly across the head.
constraint: Balancing spring stiffness and cradle flexibility to provide adequate support while minimizing localized pressure points and maintaining stability during movement.
mechanism: A pressure-distributing support system that uses compliant mechanical coupling between a flexible interface and tensioned elements to dynamically balance load distribution while minimizing localized stress concentrations.
mechanism_raw: A flexible cradle with spring elements that buffer tension between the headgear band and the head, using compliant mechanical coupling to dynamically adjust pressure distribution.

abstract: An electrospray thruster and methods of manufacturing such thrusters are provided. The micro-electrospray thruster increases the thrust density of conventional electrospray thrusters by miniaturizing the individual components of the thruster thereby allowing for the increase in the number and density of the charged particle emitters.
problem: Conventional electrospray thrusters have limited thrust density due to physical constraints on the number and density of charged particle emitters that can be integrated into a given area.
constraint: The tradeoff between miniaturization scale and the functional performance of each individual emitter—components must be small enough to increase density but large enough to maintain reliable electrospray operation and structural integrity.
mechanism: Reducing the physical scale of individual functional units enables a greater number of emission elements to be integrated into a fixed area. This increased density of active elements amplifies the total output per unit area, as more simultaneous emissions occur from the same surface.
mechanism_raw: Miniaturizing individual thruster components reduces the footprint of each emitter, allowing a greater number of emitters to be packed into the same area. This increased emitter density directly increases the total thrust output per unit area (thrust density), as more charged particles are emitted simultaneously from a given surface.

abstract: A mined ore processing apparatus to process mined ores, such as oil sands ore, into granular material is disclosed. An ore processor bed receives the ore to be processed. The ore processor bed has a frame supporting several rotating elements each separately driven to provide independent rotation rate and direction from the other. The ore processing bed is operable as a sizing device to decimate mined ore supply into granular material and separating it from rocks and other large lump mineral materials found in situ. The ore processing bed may be oriented to provide an upward inclination, which, when combined with alternating rotating element rotation directions, provides a crushing action to the ore material to crush larger rock. Alternately, a rock crusher is also provided to disintegrate oversized materials.
problem: Mined ore (such as oil sands) must be processed into granular material while simultaneously separating valuable material from large rocks and lump minerals found in situ.
constraint: The tradeoff between independent rotation control complexity and the need to coordinate rotation rates and directions to achieve both effective sizing (granular production) and crushing (oversized rock reduction) simultaneously without excessive energy consumption or equipment wear.
mechanism: Multiple independently driven rotating elements with opposing rotation directions are arranged along an inclined surface. The differential motion of adjacent elements generates shearing forces and directional material transport, while the inclination lifts oversized material for repeated compressive and abrasive interaction between the rotating elements, fragmenting the material into smaller particles and separating oversized components.
mechanism_raw: Multiple rotating elements are independently driven with alternating rotation directions and combined with an upward bed inclination. The independent and opposing rotation of adjacent elements creates differential material transport and shearing forces, while the inclination causes larger rocks to be lifted and subjected to repeated crushing action between the rotating elements, decimating the ore into granular material and separating out oversized lumps.

abstract: A low-turbulent aspirating type aerator, introduced into a body of liquid, comprising of: a gas conveyance tube having a gas inlet end and a gas outlet end; a gas-liquid mixture chamber incorporating; an impeller affixed to a rotatable shaft, at the least one gas intake opening and at the least one gas-liquid discharge opening at or near bottom end of gas-liquid mixture chamber.Rotation of the impeller creates a low-pressure zone (vacuum) allowing gas conveyed via gas conveyance tube to come into contact with rotating impeller forming a gas-liquid mixture at the impeller interface wherein bubbles are formed. Gas-liquid mixture chamber confines gas bubbles thereby allowing the action of impeller and liquid shearing force to produce and discharge micro-sized gas bubbles of predominantly less than 0.85 millimeters. The micro-sized gas bubbles generated have an long residence or gas hold up time within the body of liquid, wherein gas within bubble can, based on a concentration gradient, diffuse into liquid thereby providing the capacity to provide a high gas (oxygen) transfer rate.
problem: Conventional aerators produce gas bubbles that are too large or have insufficient residence time in liquid, resulting in low gas (oxygen) transfer rates into the liquid.
constraint: The tradeoff between bubble size reduction (which increases surface area and residence time for better transfer) and the energy required for shearing, as well as the need to maintain low turbulence to preserve micro-bubble integrity while still achieving sufficient mixing for gas-liquid contact.
mechanism: A rotating element creates a pressure differential that draws gas into a mixing zone with a liquid.
