A standard retaining ring is attached to the joint to cover a portion of an enlarged head of each of the respective fasteners in order to prevent removal of the respective fasteners from the mounting openings in the joint before the respective fasteners are connected to the fan rotor.
problem: Preventing premature removal or disengagement of fasteners during assembly of rotating components in a gas turbine engine.
constraint: Ensuring the retaining ring securely blocks fastener removal during handling and assembly while allowing straightforward installation and removal once the fasteners are properly seated.
mechanism: A mechanical barrier element attached to a joint selectively blocks removal of fasteners from mounting interfaces until a connection condition is satisfied, ensuring retention during handling while permitting release upon proper engagement.
mechanism_raw: A retaining ring attached to the joint covers the enlarged heads of fasteners, mechanically blocking their removal from mounting openings until the fasteners are fully connected to the fan rotor.

abstract: A system for supplying a process gas to a processing location of a particle beam system is disclosed. The system for supplying the processing gas includes a gas reservoir, a gas conduit, a pipe located close to the processing location, a valve between the gas conduit and the pipe, and a controller configured to open and to close the valve to switch the system from a first mode of operation in which process gas is not supplied to the processing location to a second mode of operation in which process gas is supplied to the processing location. The controller can alternately open and close the valve in cycles. Each cycle can include a first duration in which the valve is open and a second duration in which the valve is closed. The ratio of the first duration to the second duration can be changed.
problem: Need to control the supply of process gas to a processing location in a particle beam system.
constraint: Balancing gas supply to meet processing requirements without over- or under-supply, ensuring stable operation.
mechanism: Periodically switching a flow control element between open and closed states with an adjustable timing ratio to dynamically regulate the rate of fluid delivery to a target location.
mechanism_raw: Cyclic opening and closing of a valve with an adjustable duty cycle (ratio of open to closed durations) to modulate gas supply dynamically.

abstract: A garment consists of a close-fitting sleeve body formed of a stretch textile, and which includes an open upper end, an open lower end, and a body-receiving volume extending through the sleeve body from the open upper end to the open lower end. Opposed, spaced-apart, surface-gripping parts are applied exteriorly to the sleeve body near the open upper end and the open lower end, respectively. The surface-gripping parts are each formed of a gripping material different from the stretch textile, and the gripping material is slightly sticky or adhesive so as to cause the surface-gripping parts to grip, and to resist slipping relative to, surfaces they come in direct contact with without leaving a resulting residue on touched surfaces.
problem: Preventing a garment from slipping on surfaces without leaving residue on touched surfaces.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient grip while avoiding residue transfer, requiring material properties that balance adhesion and cleanliness.
mechanism: Applying a controlled-adhesion surface to exterior contact points of a wearable article so that temporary grip is established through reversible surface interaction without transferring material to contacted surfaces.
mechanism_raw: Using a slightly sticky or adhesive material on gripping parts applied exteriorly to the garment, which grips surfaces through controlled adhesion without residue.

abstract: The present invention provides grain-drying facilities which can effectively use the heat energy of a biomass combustion hot-air that has been generated in a biomass combustion furnace.The grain-drying facilities adopt technical means of providing the grain-drying facilities 1 which include: a biomass combustion furnace 3 provided with a heat exchanger 24 for generating hot air on the basis of a combustion heat of a biomass fuel and an outside air which has been taken in from the outside; and a circulation type grain-drying apparatus 2 provided with a grain-drying portion 7 to which the hot air that has been generated in the biomass combustion furnace 3 is supplied through a pipe 15 for supplying the hot air, wherein the above described circulation type grain-drying apparatus 2 has a grain-heating portion 6 which has a plurality of heating pipes 6a for heating the grains in the above described grain storing/circulating tank 5, and also has an air-exhaust fan 14 that is communicated with an exhaust side opening 6c that is located in one end side of each of the heating pipes 6a, and has a pipe 11 for supplying an exhaust hot-air, which communicates the exhaust hot-air sent from the above described biomass combustion furnace 3 with a supply side opening 6b that is located in the other end side of the heating pipe 6a.
reason: The system relies on standard heat exchanger and hot-air circulation principles without a novel causal mechanism for energy efficiency or process optimization.

abstract: A bicycle saddle adapted to reduce pressure on a rider's perineum zone including a shell having a support portion for the ischial tuberosities and a narrow nose portion extending forward of the support portion. A channel of sloped depth runs substantially the length of the nose portion and follows the dimensions of the human body. The channel is depressed at a shoulder of the support portion so that little or no pressure is applied by the saddle to the central point of the perineal body. An air filled elastic member may be provided in the channel.
problem: Reducing pressure on a rider's perineum zone in a bicycle saddle.
constraint: Balancing pressure relief with sufficient support for the ischial tuberosities and overall saddle stability.
mechanism: Forming a recessed, sloped region along a forward portion of a support surface to redirect applied load away from a sensitive anatomical zone while preserving structural support at load-bearing areas.
mechanism_raw: A sloped channel running along the saddle's nose portion, depressed at the shoulder of the support area, redistributes pressure away from sensitive regions while maintaining structural support.

abstract: The present invention provides a novel production method of a cellulose nanofiber and a novel cellulose nanofiber. The method for producing a cellulose nanofiber comprises defibrating pulp by a single- or multi-screw kneader in the presence of water, the single or multi-screw kneader having a screw circumferential speed of 45 m/min. Or more.
problem: Efficiently defibrating pulp to produce cellulose nanofibers.
constraint: Achieving sufficient defibration without damaging fiber integrity, requiring precise control of mechanical energy input.
mechanism: Rotating one or more helical energy-transfer elements at a surface velocity sufficient to generate high shear forces that mechanically separate fiber bundles into smaller fibrillated structures.
mechanism_raw: Using a single- or multi-screw kneader with a screw circumferential speed of 45 m/min or more to generate high shear forces that break down fibers into nanofibers.

abstract: It is an object of the invention to provide a nonwoven fabric having projections and recesses, comprising extensible fiber and elastic fiber, which has excellent feel on the skin and elasticity, and excellent air permeability in the planar directions and the thickness direction, as well as a method of producing the nonwoven fabric.A nonwoven fabric having projections and recesses, comprising extensible fiber and elastic fiber, wherein the first surface of the nonwoven fabric has a plurality of projections and a plurality of recesses, and the proportion of extensible fiber in the projections is higher than the proportion of extensible fiber in the recesses.
problem: Creating a nonwoven fabric with region-specific properties (e.g., skin feel, elasticity, air permeability) that vary between surface projections and recesses.
constraint: Balancing fiber composition ratios to maintain overall structural integrity while achieving distinct regional behaviors without compromising bulk or air flow.
mechanism: Varying the proportion of two distinct fiber types across topographical regions of a fibrous sheet: a higher concentration of one fiber type in surface projections (to enhance tactile and mechanical compliance) and a lower concentration in recessed regions (to preserve structural continuity), thereby enabling region-specific optimization of mechanical and permeability characteristics without compromising bulk or airflow.
mechanism_raw: Differential distribution of extensible and elastic fibers across topographical regions: higher extensible fiber proportion in projections (for softness and stretch) and lower in recesses (for structural support), enabling localized optimization of mechanical and permeability properties.

abstract: A mounting device for an LED lamp has a support tube and at least one fixed unit. The support tube has an outer surface and an external engaging surface. The external engaging surface is formed on the outer surface of the support tube. Each one of the at least one fixed unit has a positioning block mounted movably and pivotally around the support tube and has a front surface and an internal engaging surface. The internal engaging surface is formed on the front surface of the positioning block and engages the external engaging surface of the support tube. Therefore, it is convenient to adjust the fixed unit to a suitable position so that the LED lamp can be installed at any location.
problem: Enabling precise, repeatable positioning of an LED lamp at arbitrary locations along a support structure without tools or complex adjustments.
constraint: Ensuring the engaging surfaces provide sufficient friction to hold position under load while allowing smooth manual repositioning.
mechanism: A rotatably mounted adjustment element with opposing contact surfaces that frictionally engage a complementary surface on a support member, allowing manual repositioning through rotational motion and self-locking fixation at a selected angular orientation under load.
mechanism_raw: A pivotable positioning block with an internal engaging surface that mates with a complementary external engaging surface on the support tube, allowing rotational adjustment and self-locking fixation once positioned.

abstract: A fiber pad having a core non-woven layer is disclosed. The core layer can have an upper surface and a lower surface. The core layer can comprise at least one fiber layer. The at least one fiber layer can comprise a plurality of parallel fibers. Selected groups of the parallel fibers can be folded into desired pleated configurations. Optionally, the core layer can comprise post-consumer carpet materials.
problem: Creating a fiber pad with controlled internal geometry (e.g., pleats) to enhance structural or functional performance while accommodating recycled materials.
constraint: Maintaining pleat stability and uniformity during processing, especially when incorporating heterogeneous post-consumer fiber inputs.
mechanism: Selective folding of grouped parallel fibers within a fibrous core layer into predefined geometric configurations, creating localized variations in stiffness, bulk, or absorption capacity while maintaining structural coherence during processing of heterogeneous fiber inputs.
mechanism_raw: Selective folding of grouped parallel fibers within a core non-woven layer into predefined pleated configurations, enabling localized stiffness, bulk, or absorption characteristics.

abstract: The invention is directed to veneer ceramics for dental restorations of framework ceramics comprising yttrium-stabilized zirconium dioxide. It is the object of the invention to make possible a translucent veneer ceramic which has high flexural strength as well as excellent adhesion to the framework ceramic of yttrium-stabilized zirconium dioxide. According to the invention, this object is met in a veneer ceramic for dental restorations made of yttrium-stabilized zirconium dioxide which is produced from the following components:
problem: Achieving a dental veneer ceramic that simultaneously exhibits high translucency, flexural strength, and adhesion to a zirconia framework.
constraint: Optimizing material ratios to avoid trade-offs between optical clarity and structural durability during high-temperature processing.
mechanism: Adjusting the relative proportions of ceramic components and additives to simultaneously achieve optical translucency, mechanical strength, and thermal expansion compatibility with a substrate material, avoiding trade-offs between light transmission and structural durability during high-temperature processing.
mechanism_raw: Tailoring the ceramic composition (e.g., specific glass-ceramic components and additives) to balance light transmission, mechanical strength, and thermal compatibility with the framework material.

abstract: We make door locks which has a receiver it can be locked or opened via receiving a password as long sequence of numbers when transmitted to it from the cellular phone where each lock when it is sold a plastic card comes with it containing password when we scratch and reveal the password and we input it in the cellular phone and save it, then the door lock will open when we press a button on the cellular phone and will be locked when we press the button again, as well the cars come with a plastic card and the same is done as explained before so by the cellular phones we can lock and unlock the car, the same can be done for the garage gate and office doors, ATM card will be replaced by a password saved in the cellular phone as explained above.
problem: Providing secure, remote access control for physical locks (doors, cars, gates) using a portable device without requiring dedicated hardware keys or cards.
constraint: Ensuring password security and reliable wireless communication while maintaining compatibility across diverse lock types and user devices.
mechanism: Storing a unique identifier on a portable electronic device and transmitting it via wireless communication to a receiver coupled to a physical lock, enabling toggle-based access control through a single actuation input without requiring dedicated hardware keys.
mechanism_raw: Storing a unique password on a cellular phone and transmitting it to a lock receiver via wireless signal, enabling toggle-based locking/unlocking through a single button press.

abstract: A contacting device for electrically contacting tensile carriers of a suspension in an elevator system includes a housing having a recess in which an exposed segment of the suspension can be received so that the housing at least partially encloses the exposed segment of the suspension. Raised areas and recesses are alternatingly disposed on an inner side of the housing, wherein a raised area and a recess face each other in a state of use. At least one contact element is disposed in a recess of the housing, wherein the at least one raised area can be pressed against a tensile carrier of the suspension, such that the tensile carrier is brought into electrical contact with the contact element.
problem: Maintaining reliable electrical contact with moving tensile carriers in an elevator suspension system without disrupting their mechanical function.
constraint: Balancing sufficient contact pressure to ensure electrical continuity while avoiding damage to the tensile carrier or housing structure.
mechanism: A dynamically textured interface with alternating protrusions and indentations on a housing surface creates intermittent contact pressure against a moving element, enabling electrical connectivity through mechanical compliance while preserving the element's tensile function.
mechanism_raw: Alternating raised areas and recesses on a housing inner surface create a dynamic interface where pressing a raised area against a tensile carrier forces it into contact with a fixed contact element, enabling electrical connectivity during movement.

abstract: A brake system includes a brake cylinder having a piston rod and a brake lever connecting the piston rod to a brake beam and a slack adjuster. An actuating lever is connected to the brake beam and the brake cylinder. A trigger of the slack adjuster is connected to the actuating lever. The actuating lever is pivotally and rotationally connected to the brake beam and swivelably connected to the brake cylinder. Also, a piston stoke indictor including an indicia positioned on a support structure of a brake cylinder to be adjacent the end of a portion of a brake piston at its extended position.
problem: Automatically maintaining proper brake adjustment in a braking system despite wear or operational changes, while providing visual feedback on piston position.
constraint: Ensuring the slack adjustment mechanism responds reliably to operational forces without introducing unintended mechanical play or binding.
mechanism: A mechanically coupled lever system translates operational movement into automatic slack adjustment via a pivotally linked trigger, while a position-sensing indicator provides real-time feedback on actuator displacement.
mechanism_raw: A pivotally connected actuating lever links the brake beam and cylinder, with a slack adjuster trigger mechanically coupled to the lever. Movement of the lever during braking actuates the trigger to adjust slack, while a piston stroke indicator provides positional feedback.

abstract: There is provided a connector capable of reducing deterioration of the noise removal capability by suppressing deformation of a ferrite. The connector includes: a housing which is provided with a plurality of connector fitting portions to be fitted in a plurality of mating connectors, respectively; a plurality of terminals which are attached to the housing to project within the plurality of connector fitting portions, respectively; a plurality of ferrites which remove noise generated from the plurality of terminals, each ferrite being provided for the respective one of the connector fitting portions and having a through hole through which each of the plurality of terminals passes; and a plurality of pressing arms which are provided in the housing, each pressing arm holding the respective one of the plurality of ferrites.
problem: Preventing deformation of noise-suppressing ferrite components in a connector that could degrade electromagnetic interference (EMI) filtering performance.
constraint: Applying sufficient clamping force to prevent ferrite deformation while allowing terminals to pass through without interference.
mechanism: Integrated clamping elements mechanically constrain a noise-suppressing component around a terminal, maintaining its geometric integrity during assembly and operation to preserve electromagnetic filtering performance.
mechanism_raw: Pressing arms integrated into the housing mechanically constrain each ferrite around its terminal, maintaining its shape and alignment during assembly and operation to preserve noise removal capability.

abstract: The invention relates to polarized cell tubulo-vesicular structure localization signals. The localization signals are utilized as research tools or are linked to polypeptides of interest or therapeutic molecules. Disclosed are methods of making and using polypeptides and modified polypeptides as signals to localize therapeutics, experimental compounds, peptides, proteins and/or other macromolecules to the tubulo-vesicular structures of polarized cells. The polypeptides of the invention optionally include linkage to reporters, epitopes and/or other experimental or therapeutic molecules. The invention also encompasses polynucleotides encoding the localization signals and vectors comprising these polynucleotides.
problem: Directing therapeutic or experimental molecules specifically to tubulo-vesicular structures within polarized cells for targeted delivery.
constraint: Achieving high specificity for target structures while avoiding off-target accumulation or degradation of the delivered molecules.
mechanism: Molecular address labels leverage cellular trafficking pathways to direct linked molecules to predefined subcellular destinations, achieving targeted delivery through sequence-specific recognition mechanisms.
mechanism_raw: Polypeptide localization signals act as molecular address labels, leveraging cellular trafficking pathways to transport linked molecules to predefined subcellular compartments.

abstract: A high-speed, high-resolution, triangulation-based, 3-D method and system for inspecting manufactured parts and sorting the inspected parts are provided. The method includes consecutively transferring the parts so that the parts move along a path which extends from a supply of parts and through an imaging station. A triangulation-based sensor head is supported at the imaging station. The sensor head is configured to generate focused lines of radiation and to sense corresponding reflected lines of radiation. The focused lines are delivered onto an end surface of each part to obtain a corresponding array of reflected lines of radiation. The sensor head senses the array of reflected lines to obtain a corresponding set of 2-D profile signals. The set of profile signals represent a 3-D view of the end surface. The set of 2-D profile signals of each part is processed to identify parts having an unacceptable defect.
problem: Rapidly and accurately inspecting manufactured parts for defects in three dimensions at high throughput.
constraint: Balancing inspection speed with spatial resolution to maintain accuracy across varying part geometries and surface textures.
mechanism: Triangulation-based optical sensors project radiation patterns onto surfaces and detect reflected signals to generate profile data, which is processed into three-dimensional surface maps for high-throughput defect identification.
mechanism_raw: Triangulation-based sensor heads project focused radiation lines onto part surfaces and detect reflected lines to generate 2D profile signals, which are processed into 3D surface maps for defect identification.

abstract: The present disclosure is directed to a device that includes a substrate and a sensor formed on the substrate. The sensor includes a chamber formed from a plurality of integrated cavities, a membrane above the substrate, the membrane having a plurality of openings, each opening positioned above one of the cavities, and a plurality of diamond shaped anchors positioned between the membrane and the substrate, the anchors positioned between each of the cavities. A center of each opening is also a center of one of the cavities.
problem: Creating a sensor with controlled mechanical response and structural integrity using a membrane and integrated cavities.
constraint: Balancing membrane flexibility for sensitivity against anchor rigidity to maintain structural stability and prevent over-deflection.
mechanism: A flexible membrane is supported by a structured framework that allows controlled lateral displacement while maintaining positional stability. The framework's geometry and alignment with internal voids ensure that membrane deformation is confined to a measurable region, enabling precise detection of pressure or displacement through localized mechanical response.
mechanism_raw: Diamond-shaped anchors positioned between the membrane and substrate provide structural support while allowing lateral movement of the membrane. The alignment of openings and cavities ensures that membrane deflection is localized and measurable, enabling precise sensing of pressure or displacement.

abstract: A discharged warm/cold heat of a refrigerant circuit is effectively utilized in order to attain high energy efficiency. Appropriate operation control is executed when a hot-water supplying operation and an air cooling operation are simultaneously performed, whereby high energy efficiency is attained.When an air cooling operation by an air temperature adjusting refrigerant circuit and a hot-water supplying operation by a hot-water supplying refrigerant circuit are executed, the air temperature adjusting refrigerant circuit, and the hot-water supplying refrigerant circuit are controlled such that a target evaporation temperature of the hot-water supplying refrigerant circuit or a target condensation temperature of the air temperature adjusting refrigerant circuit is attained, the target evaporation temperature or the target condensation temperature being set based upon an air cooling capacity and an evaporation temperature of the air temperature adjusting refrigerant circuit and a hot-water supplying capacity and a condensation temperature of the hot-water supplying refrigerant circuit.
problem: Achieving high energy efficiency when simultaneously performing hot-water supply and air cooling operations in a refrigerant system.
constraint: Maintaining stable operation of both circuits while dynamically adjusting temperatures to avoid overloading or inefficiency during simultaneous operation.
mechanism: Two interconnected thermal exchange systems dynamically adjust their operational parameters based on real-time demand signals, optimizing heat transfer between them to minimize energy consumption while maintaining stable performance across both functions.
mechanism_raw: Coordinated control of two refrigerant circuits adjusts target evaporation/condensation temperatures based on real-time capacity demands, dynamically optimizing heat exchange between the systems to minimize energy waste.

abstract: Methods of leveling ink on substrates and apparatuses useful in printing are provided. An exemplary embodiment of the methods includes irradiating ink disposed on a surface of a porous substrate with radiation emitted by at least one radiant energy source. The radiation heats the ink to at least a viscosity threshold temperature of the ink to allow the ink to flow laterally on the surface to produce leveling of the ink. The ink is heated sufficiently rapidly that heat transfer from the ink to the substrate is sufficiently small during the leveling that ink at the substrate interface is cooled to a temperature below the viscosity threshold temperature thereby preventing any significant ink permeation into the substrate.
problem: Leveling ink on porous substrates without causing ink permeation into the substrate during the leveling process.
constraint: Timing the heating and cooling rates precisely to ensure sufficient flow for leveling while preventing heat from reaching the substrate interface.
mechanism: A material is heated above a flow threshold to enable surface-level redistribution, then cooled below the threshold before reaching a porous interface, preventing penetration while achieving uniform distribution through controlled viscosity modulation.
mechanism_raw: Rapid radiant heating raises ink viscosity above a flow threshold, enabling lateral leveling. Heat transfer to the substrate is minimized so the ink-substrate interface cools below the threshold, solidifying the ink before permeation occurs.

abstract: A microwave oven includes a top wall, side walls, and a bottom wall at least partially defining a cavity of the microwave oven, and a table coupled to the bottom wall. The table has a top surface and an opposing bottom surface. The top surface is configured to support an item within the cavity. A light source directs light to the table. The table is configured to diffuse light emitted from the light source into the cavity.
problem: Providing uniform illumination within a microwave oven cavity to improve visibility during operation.
constraint: Designing the table's surface texture and material to maximize light diffusion without obstructing the microwave's primary heating function.
mechanism: A light source directs illumination to a textured surface designed to scatter light uniformly across an enclosed volume, eliminating intensity variations through controlled diffusion without obstructing primary operational functions.
mechanism_raw: A light source directs light to a table with a diffusing surface, which scatters light evenly throughout the cavity, eliminating hotspots and ensuring consistent illumination.

abstract: The source bushing assembly has a source bushing having an internal vacuum side and an external atmosphere side, a first shield of annular shape disposed at one end of the source bushing in spaced concentric relation to reduce formation of an electrically conductive coating on the source bushing, a second shield of annular shape disposed at an opposite end of the source bushing in spaced concentric relation to prevent arcing on the source bushing and an internally disposed concentric X-ray shield.
problem: Preventing conductive coating formation and electrical arcing on a source bushing in a vacuum-to-atmosphere interface, while shielding X-rays.
constraint: Positioning shields to balance electrical insulation, thermal management, and X-ray containment without compromising the bushing's operational integrity.
mechanism: Multiple shielding elements are positioned at strategic intervals along a conductive interface to regulate spacing, suppress electrical discharge, and isolate radiation paths, while maintaining thermal and electrical functionality through selective material placement.
mechanism_raw: Annular shields at both ends of the bushing create controlled spacing to reduce conductive coating buildup and suppress arcing, while an internal concentric X-ray shield isolates radiation paths without interfering with the bushing's electrical function.

abstract: A sand based jewelry and methods of making sand based jewelry is provided. The jewelry having a quantity of sand mixed with a quantity of binding medium. The binding medium and sand mixture are capable of being solidified and mounted to a jewelry setting. The jewelry setting attached to a jewelry item.
reason: The patent describes a material composition (sand mixed with a binding medium) to create jewelry, but the mechanism is a basic physical mixture without a causal functional relationship that solves a broader problem beyond the specific application. It lacks a dynamic interaction or controlled process that could be transferred to other fields.

abstract: A linear actuator includes a cylinder main body, which is provided at one end thereof with a lock mechanism capable of restricting displacement of a slide table. The lock mechanism is equipped with a lock plate and a sub-piston. The lock plate is rotatable toward a side of the slide table by an elastic force of a spring, inserted into an insertion groove, and restricts displacement of the slide table. The sub-piston is displaced by a pressure fluid supplied to a supply port, and releases a displacement restricted state of the slide table by the lock plate.
problem: Providing a fail-safe locking mechanism for a slide table that can be selectively released under controlled conditions.
constraint: Balancing the spring's elastic force with the fluid pressure required to release the lock, ensuring reliable operation without unintended disengagement.
mechanism: A resilient element biases a movable component into a receptive feature to restrict displacement, while an active force source counteracts the resilient element to release the constraint. This creates a controlled interaction between passive (resilient) and active (force) elements to toggle between restricted and released states.
mechanism_raw: A spring biases a lock plate into an insertion groove to restrict displacement, while a sub-piston uses pressure fluid to counteract the spring force and release the lock. This creates a controlled interaction between passive (spring) and active (fluid pressure) elements to toggle between locked and unlocked states.

abstract: The present invention relates to a reflector for light emission sources, having a rotational symmetry about an axis, an apex comprising a first opening of size such to accommodate a light source and a second opening, larger in size than the first opening, adapted to let out the direct light emitted by said light source and the light reflected by the internal surface of the reflector, surface which is characterized by a series of segments comprising a plurality of approximately rectangular surface segments in turn comprising a plurality of reliefs, preferably having a substantially hemispherical shape, and characterized by a convexity facing towards the inside of the reflector, said convexity being characterized by a single curvature radius.
problem: Efficiently directing and controlling light emission from a source to achieve uniform or targeted illumination.
constraint: Maintaining a consistent curvature radius across all reliefs to ensure uniform light reflection without scattering or loss of directional control.
mechanism: A reflective surface with a series of curved elements arranged in segmented regions. The curvature orientation creates a controlled light-reflection geometry, enabling precise redirection of emitted and reflected light through a uniform curvature profile.
mechanism_raw: A reflector with a series of convex reliefs (hemispherical in shape) arranged in rectangular surface segments. The convexity facing inward creates a controlled light-reflection geometry, enabling precise redirection of emitted and reflected light through a single curvature radius.

abstract: The invention provides methods of performing a sizing analysis. In the methods, a sizing ladder used in performing the sizing analysis is corrected. In one method, the sizing ladder is corrected for batch-to-batch variations in a sieving gel. In another method, the sizing ladder is corrected for a sample concentration that is different from the archival sizing ladder concentration. Methods are also provided in which the sizing ladder is corrected using a standard marker in a sample and/or using a real-time standard sizing ladder. The methods may be used individually or in combination.
problem: Accurately determining molecular sizes in gel electrophoresis despite batch-to-batch variations in sieving gels or sample concentrations.
constraint: Ensuring the reference standard is compatible with the sample matrix and provides sufficient resolution to correct for variations without introducing additional errors.
mechanism: A calibration reference with known properties is used to adjust measured values, compensating for variability in the analysis medium or sample conditions. This ensures consistent results by aligning measurements to a standardized baseline.
mechanism_raw: Using a reference standard (e.g., a known marker or real-time sizing ladder) to calibrate and correct the sizing analysis. This adjusts measured values to account for variability in gel properties or sample conditions, ensuring consistent results.

abstract: A personal stair lift to transport an individual up and down a stairway on a chair assembly supported on a rail mounted rack comprising a carriage assembly configured to support a lift mechanism including a drive member coupled to a reversible drive motor to rotate the drive member wherein the carriage assembly includes at least one pair of upper rollers and at least one pair of lower rollers movably mounted on a stationary rail disposed on each side of the carriage assembly and a rack mounted to one of the stationary rails disposed to engage the drive member to selectively move the chair assembly and person up or down the stairway when the reversible motor rotates the drive member.
problem: Transporting a person smoothly and safely along a stairway rail while maintaining stability and traction on varying stair geometries.
constraint: Balancing roller placement and drive force to ensure smooth movement without slippage, while accommodating the curvature and irregularities of stairway rails.
mechanism: A transport assembly with paired contact elements maintaining stable engagement with a guide, combined with a propulsion system that converts rotational motion into linear movement. The contact elements ensure traction while the propulsion system drives motion along the guide.
mechanism_raw: A carriage assembly with paired upper and lower rollers mounted on a stationary rail, combined with a rack-and-pinion drive system. The rollers provide stable contact with the rail, while the motor-driven drive member engages the rack to propel the chair assembly up or down the stairs.

abstract: A composition of matter comprising: a combination of a phytate and a plurality of microorganisms comprising a Trichoderma virens fungus, a Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bacterium, and one or a plurality of mycorrhizae fungi that is placed in the vicinity of a plant root in a manner that allows the microorganisms in the composition of matter to colonize said plant root; and a method for increasing plant yield comprising: placing a combination of a phytate and a plurality of microorganisms comprising a Trichoderma virens fungus, a Bacillus amyloliquefaciens bacterium, and one or a plurality of mycorrhizae fungi in the vicinity of a plant root in a manner that allows the microorganisms in the composition of matter to colonize said plant root.
problem: Increasing plant yield by enhancing root colonization and nutrient uptake efficiency.
constraint: The specific microbial consortium and phytate must be co-located near roots to enable colonization and avoid antagonistic interactions between components.
mechanism: A synergistic combination of a nutrient source and a microbial consortium that colonize plant roots, collectively enhancing nutrient availability and root health to improve plant growth. The components are co-located near roots to enable colonization and prevent antagonistic interactions.
mechanism_raw: A synergistic combination of phytate (as a nutrient source) and specific microorganisms (Trichoderma virens, Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, and mycorrhizae) that colonize plant roots, collectively improving nutrient availability and root health to boost plant growth.

abstract: In order to provide a rib structure of an umbrella, which has superior appearance without receiving unnecessary structural pressure and can contribute to the development of the industry by motivating consumers to buy, this invention features the rib structure of an umbrella which is formed with multiple ribs wherein the length of specific ribs is different from the length of other specific ribs, cloth is stretched onto the above mentioned ribs thereby changing forms of the umbrella and when the above mentioned cloth is put between the above mentioned ribs and adjacent ribs, the cloth does not expand and contract in the direction of the length of said ribs, but is expandable and contractible in any direction with the exception of the direction of the length of said ribs.
problem: Achieving controlled structural expansion in flexible materials while maintaining aesthetic and mechanical integrity.
constraint: The cloth material must be anisotropic—expandable in directions perpendicular to ribs but constrained along rib lengths—to achieve the desired form.
mechanism: A ribbed structure with varying rib lengths constrains expansion along rib axes, forcing directional expansion perpendicular to ribs. This anisotropic constraint enables controlled shape transformation while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Varying rib lengths in a ribbed structure constrain cloth expansion along rib axes, forcing directional expansion perpendicular to ribs, enabling shape control without structural pressure.

abstract: A treatment process of persistent organic pollutants contained in particles is provided. Said process includes reacting persistent organic pollutant in particles under hydrothermal conditions in the presence of Fe2+ and Fe3+. Several beneficial effects can be achieved, including 1) no other additive is needed during the reaction process; 2) Fe2+ and Fe3+ are safe, cheap and extensive sources; 3) because Fe2+ and Fe3+ are dissolved, they can fully disperse into particles, and fully contact can be achieved, thus obtaining a decomposition rate no less than 70% of the persistent organic pollutants is under subcritical conditions.
problem: Efficiently decomposing persistent organic pollutants in particulate matter without requiring additional additives.
constraint: The reaction must occur under subcritical hydrothermal conditions to maintain ion solubility and catalytic activity while avoiding secondary contamination.
mechanism: Dissolved metal ions act as catalysts under hydrothermal conditions, enabling full dispersion into particles and subcritical decomposition of pollutants via redox reactions. The conditions maintain ion solubility and catalytic activity while avoiding secondary contamination.
mechanism_raw: Dissolved Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺ ions act as catalysts under hydrothermal conditions, enabling full dispersion into particles and subcritical decomposition of pollutants via redox reactions.

abstract: Two hooking members of a hooking unit used in a device for conveying bone-in meat respectively have belt-like main body parts, blade-like pointed ends provided at ends on one side of the main body parts, and barbs provided on first sides of the main body parts to be continuous with the points. The hooking members are supported so as to be in parallel with each other with an elastically changeable interval therebetween and to be rotatable about rotation axes along longitudinal axes of the main body parts. Further, the hooking unit has an actuator which rotates the hooking members about the rotation axes.
problem: Conveying irregularly shaped, fragile objects (e.g., bone-in meat) without causing damage during transport.
constraint: The hooks must rotate about their longitudinal axes and maintain an elastically variable interval to balance grip strength and object safety.
mechanism: Adjustable, rotating gripping elements with variable spacing dynamically adapt to object geometry, gripping and releasing via rotational actuation while maintaining spacing flexibility. This balances grip strength and object safety during transport.
mechanism_raw: Adjustable, rotating hooking members with barbs and pointed ends dynamically adapt to object geometry, gripping and releasing via rotational actuation while maintaining spacing flexibility.

abstract: Each vane for an arrow is both tapered or rounded at the leading edge, and shaped to provide better adherence to the arrow. With the injection molding of each vane, a proper, rounded, smooth shape is achieved. When combined with a bottom surface of the vane having indentations therein, good adherence of the vane to the shaft of the arrow is achieved.
problem: Optimizing aerodynamic performance and attachment reliability of arrow vanes during flight.
constraint: The vane geometry must be precisely molded to balance aerodynamic shaping with surface features that ensure secure attachment without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism: Tapered/rounded leading edges reduce aerodynamic drag, while surface indentations on the base enhance adhesion to a shaft via mechanical interlocking during molding. The geometry balances aerodynamic shaping with secure attachment.
mechanism_raw: Tapered/rounded leading edges reduce aerodynamic drag, while surface indentations on the vane base enhance adhesion to the arrow shaft via mechanical interlocking during injection molding.

abstract: Techniques for constructing a solid-state lighting module that includes solid-state light emitters that emit light of different colors and are selected from separated groups of solid-state light emitters that emit light of two or more separated colors, wherein one or more solid-state light emitters are selected from each of the separated color groups of solid-state light emitters. The lighting module includes a programmable device that stores or remembers desirable optical intensities of the separated color groups of solid-state light emitters, and a control circuit that individually controls light intensity of each of the separated color groups of solid-state light emitters. The light control circuit is coupled to or in communication with the programmable device to receive the desirable optical intensities of the separated groups of solid-state light emitters and is operable to adjust the intensities of the separated color groups of solid-state light emitters based on the desirable intensities.
problem: Need to achieve and maintain desirable optical intensities across multiple separated color groups in a solid-state lighting module, where each color group must be individually controlled.
constraint: Each color group must be individually controllable while using the same stored desirable intensities, requiring per-channel control circuitry coupled to a shared memory of target values.
mechanism: A memory stores target values for each of multiple independently controlled channels, and a feedback control system adjusts each channel's output based on the stored targets, enabling coordinated regulation of discrete output groups using shared reference data.
mechanism_raw: A programmable device stores or remembers target optical intensities for each separated color group, and a control circuit individually adjusts the light output of each color group based on those stored target values, creating a multi-channel feedback control system with memory.

abstract: A transporting space of an article transport facility is divided into a first space and a second space by a wall having an opening. A first movable body that travels along a first travel rail in the first space and a second movable body that travels along a second travel rail in the second space are provided. A relay portion which can support an article without interfering with the shutter that can open and close the opening is provided in the first space. The first travel rail is arranged to extend adjacent a first space side transfer position for transferring articles between the first mobile body and the relay portion, and the second travel rail is arranged to extend adjacent a second space side transfer position for transferring articles between the second mobile body and the relay portion through the opening.
problem: Need to transfer articles between two physically separated spaces while maintaining isolation between those spaces via a shutter mechanism on a shared opening.
constraint: The relay portion must support articles for transfer while not interfering with the shutter mechanism, requiring careful geometric coordination between the relay, the opening, and the shutter.
mechanism: An intermediate transfer element in one space supports articles for movement through an opening to a second space, while a movable barrier on the opening cycles between open and closed states to maintain isolation between the spaces, with geometric coordination ensuring the transfer element does not obstruct the barrier's motion.
mechanism_raw: An intermediate relay portion in the first space supports articles for transfer and is designed to pass articles through the opening to the second space without interfering with the shutter that opens and closes the opening, enabling transfer across an isolation barrier.

abstract: A composite yarn for technical or industrial use, particularly suitable for textile webs, is uniformly coated with a polymer and exhibits improved fir behavior and improved resistance to sheath stripping. The yarn may be obtained by a process where a continuous yarn, obtained by spinning a large number of fibers, such as about 100 to 600 fibers made of an organic or inorganic material, of a suitable yarn diameter, such as between about 1 to 10 micrometers, is subjected to a process for mechanically opening the yarn by splaying, to uniformly spread out and separate the fibers, including inner layers of the fibers, without impairing functional properties of the yarn, simultaneously with or prior to coating of the fibers by a polymer material having a viscosity between 1000 and 10,000 mPa·s, and formed to have a circular cross-section and uniformly distributed fibers throughout the cross-section of the polymer material to limit desheathing of the yarn.
problem: Need to create a composite yarn with improved structural integrity (resistance to sheath stripping) and functional performance (fir behavior) while maintaining uniform fiber distribution.
constraint: The mechanical splaying must spread fibers without impairing the yarn's functional properties, requiring a balance between sufficient fiber separation and preservation of structural integrity during the coating process.
mechanism: A multi-component material strand is mechanically expanded by separating its constituent elements, and a binding agent is applied concurrently or sequentially to embed the separated elements, creating a composite structure with uniform distribution of the elements within the binding agent and reduced delamination of the outer layer.
mechanism_raw: A continuous multi-fiber yarn is mechanically opened by splaying to spread and separate fibers including inner layers, simultaneously with or prior to coating with a polymer, so that fibers become uniformly distributed throughout the polymer cross-section, limiting desheathing.

abstract: Sucker rods include end fittings having an outer wedge portion proximate to an open end, an inner wedge portion proximate to a closed end, and an intermediate wedge portion between the outer and inner wedges. Each wedge includes a leading edge, a trailing edge, and an angle between the leading and trailing edges. The triangular configuration, length of the leading edge, the length of the trailing edge, and size of the angle in each wedge portion cause distribution of force, such that compressive forces distributed to the rod proximate the closed end exceed compressive forces distributed to the rod proximate the open end.
problem: Need to distribute compressive forces along a sucker rod such that forces near the closed end exceed forces near the open end, to improve load handling and reduce stress concentration.
constraint: The wedge geometry (triangular shape, edge lengths, and angles) must be precisely specified to achieve the desired force distribution pattern, as the force redirection depends on the exact geometric relationships between the wedge portions.
mechanism: A load-bearing assembly incorporates geometrically distinct wedge sections with specified angular and linear dimensions that redirect applied compressive forces along a path, creating a gradient in force distribution where one end region experiences greater force concentration than another end region.
mechanism_raw: End fittings incorporate wedge portions (outer, inner, intermediate) with specific triangular configurations, leading and trailing edge lengths, and angles that geometrically direct and distribute compressive forces so that the closed-end region receives greater force distribution than the open-end region.

abstract: A flow control system of the present invention includes a movable riser slideably engaged with a stationary riser and having a flange. The stationary riser is interfaced to a downstream drainage system. The movable riser is made buoyant by one or more floats such that, as the water level around the flow control system changes, the movable riser follows the changes based upon the buoyancy of the float(s), thereby maintaining the flange at a constant depth. The gap between an upper edge of the flange and the inner perimeter of the stationary riser coupled with an area of the gap defines a flow rate that is constant. Vents couple an inner cavity of the movable riser to air above the fluid, the inner cavity being in communication with the drainage system as well.
problem: Need to maintain a constant flow rate in a drainage system despite changes in surrounding water level.
constraint: The buoyancy of the floats must be calibrated so the flange maintains a constant depth as water levels change, and the gap geometry must be precisely defined to set the desired constant flow rate.
mechanism: A buoyancy-driven mechanism couples a movable element to a fluid surface so the element tracks fluid level changes, maintaining a fixed geometric relationship between a flow-controlling aperture and a stationary structure, thereby regulating a constant flow rate through the aperture despite varying fluid levels.
mechanism_raw: A movable riser is made buoyant by floats so it automatically follows water level changes, keeping a flange at a constant depth relative to the water surface. The gap between the flange's upper edge and the stationary riser's inner perimeter defines a constant flow rate, while vents couple the inner cavity to air above the fluid.

abstract: According to one embodiment, a medical image processing apparatus includes a reception unit, determination unit, dividing unit, processing control unit, and storage processing unit. The reception unit receives first data including supported and unsupported tags, and individual data added to the supported or unsupported tag. The determination unit determines whether a tag included in the first data is supported or not. The dividing unit divides the first data into second data and third data. The processing control unit executes data processing by referring to the second data. The storage processing unit generates fourth data by adding second data to data acquired by the processing.
problem: Processing heterogeneous data containing both supported and unsupported elements while maintaining integrity and efficiency.
constraint: Balancing computational efficiency by avoiding processing unsupported elements while ensuring no loss of data integrity during recombination.
mechanism: Partitioning data into compatible and incompatible subsets based on compatibility criteria, processing only the compatible subset, and merging processed results with the original incompatible subset to preserve data integrity.
mechanism_raw: Separating data into supported and unsupported subsets based on tag compatibility, processing only the supported subset, and recombining processed results with the original supported data to preserve unsupported elements.

abstract: The present invention is directed to methods, for example phage display assays, for bioengineering peptides that bind to individual distinct nucleotides. Also provided are peptides engineered by such methods. Specifically, cyclic peptides that bind individual distinct nucleotides are provided herein.
problem: Engineering peptides with precise binding specificity to individual nucleotides for targeted molecular interactions.
constraint: Achieving high binding specificity and stability while avoiding cross-reactivity with non-target nucleotides.
mechanism: Iteratively selecting and amplifying molecular variants that bind to specific targets through a coupled genotype-phenotype system, enabling directed evolution of binding specificity.
mechanism_raw: Using phage display to iteratively select and amplify peptide variants that bind to specific nucleotide targets, leveraging the coupling of genotype and phenotype for directed evolution.

abstract: A sealing system for doors and windows includes a reservoir device, a sealing tube configured to expand and to contract, and a transfer valve configured to couple the reservoir device to a first end of the sealing tube. Responsive to either of a door or window closing, a medium may be transferred from the reservoir device via the transfer valve to the sealing tube. Responsive to receiving the medium, the sealing tube may expand to substantially seal a gap between an edge of either of the door or the window and a surface in proximity to the edge. Responsive to either of the door or window opening, the medium may be discharged from the sealing tube via the transfer valve. The sealing tube may contract in response to discharging the medium.
problem: Automatically sealing gaps in doors/windows without manual intervention while allowing reversible operation.
constraint: Ensuring timely and reliable medium transfer to match the mechanical movement of the door/window without leakage or delay.
mechanism: Transferring a medium into an expandable element upon closure to form a seal, and discharging the medium upon opening to retract the element, using a valve-controlled system to synchronize medium flow with mechanical movement.
mechanism_raw: Transferring a medium into an expandable sealing tube upon closure to create a seal, and discharging the medium upon opening to retract the tube, using a valve-controlled reservoir system.

abstract: Provided is an apparatus for receiving an unmanned mail capable of automatically acquiring the address information even though the user does not directly input the address information. The apparatus acquires address information of an addressee by automatically recognizing the address of the mail when the address is written on the mail, and acquires the address information of the addressee through the paper on which the address is printed or written, identification, and biometric recognition when the address is not written on the mail. The apparatus may acquire the address information of the addressee through a mail sender's voice.
problem: Automatically acquiring address information for unmanned mail without direct user input across diverse input formats.
constraint: Maintaining accuracy and reliability across heterogeneous input methods while minimizing false positives or missed data.
mechanism: Integrating multiple recognition modalities to extract address data from diverse input sources, dynamically prioritizing available sources based on reliability and availability.
mechanism_raw: Combining multiple recognition modalities (OCR, paper identification, biometrics, voice) to extract address data from mail surfaces, attached documents, or sender interactions, prioritizing available sources dynamically.

abstract: An authentication registration/invalidation apparatus is provided, which allows easy invalidation of an authentication tag when the authentication tag is lost, and facilitates management of authentication tags. When an RFID reader (2) receives an RFID signal including an instruction of invalidation, which is transmitted from an operation tag (10b) in a recognition area (A), an invalidation unit (32b) sets an operation mode to an invalidation enabled mode. If an RFID tag recognizer (31a) recognizes an authentication tag (10a) before or after the setting of the invalidation enabled mode, the invalidation unit 32b invalidates the authentication tag (10a), or invalidates all authentication tags (10a) that belong to a group to which the authentication tag belongs.
problem: Enabling rapid invalidation of authentication tags when lost or compromised, including group-based invalidation.
constraint: Ensuring secure and localized invalidation without unintended disruption to unrelated tags or systems.
mechanism: Using a proximity-triggered operation to activate an invalidation mode, which invalidates a specific authentication tag or all tags in its group via wireless communication, ensuring localized and secure invalidation.
mechanism_raw: Using a proximity-triggered operation tag to activate an invalidation mode, which then invalidates a specific authentication tag or all tags in its group via RFID communication.

abstract: An above heel lower limb orthosis comprising: an orthosis body; a support surface adapted to support a portion of a lower limb, the support surface connected to, secured to, or integral with the orthosis body; relief means adapted to relieve a portion of a lower limb from pressure; and at least one relief region connected to, secured to, or integral with the orthosis body or the support surface or the orthosis body and the support surface, the relief region depressed relative to the support surface and adapted to receive, secure, or integrate the relief means.
problem: Pressure distribution and localized relief in lower limb orthoses to prevent tissue damage or discomfort.
constraint: Balancing localized pressure relief with overall structural integrity and support for the limb.
mechanism: A localized compliant zone within a structural support system creates a controlled low-pressure region that selectively offloads compressive forces from specific areas while maintaining overall structural integrity through rigid support elsewhere.
mechanism_raw: A depressed relief region integrated into the orthosis body or support surface creates a controlled low-pressure zone that offloads specific limb portions from compressive forces, allowing targeted pressure relief while maintaining structural support elsewhere.

abstract: A method and to a device for delivering deliverable materials through a hollow chamber that is closed off from the outside air in a pressure-tight manner and that is supplied with materials via a storage container serving as a lock and that ends in the furnace chamber via a connecting tube. The delivery of the materials within the hollow chamber closed off from the outside air in a pressure-tight manner is carried out by means of depressurized mechanical conveyors.
problem: Delivering materials through a sealed environment without exposing them to external air or pressure fluctuations.
constraint: Maintaining pressure-tight isolation of the chamber while enabling continuous material transport.
mechanism: A sealed transport pathway uses controlled pressure differentials to move materials between isolated chambers, maintaining pressure-tight isolation while enabling continuous material flow through differential-driven conveyance.
mechanism_raw: Depressurized mechanical conveyors operate within a pressure-tight hollow chamber, using controlled pressure differentials to move materials from a lock-based storage container to a furnace chamber without breaching the sealed system.

abstract: A stator (1) and a method for manufacturing such a stator for an electric machine. Windings of the stator (1) protrude in the longitudinal direction beyond a cylindrical stator body (3) in the form of end windings (17, 19) on end faces (13, 15) of the stator body (3). In this case, a complementarily designed accommodating region (31) is provided on a housing (21), with the result that, when the housing (21) is assembled with the stator body (3), the windings of the end winding (17) can be pressed. As a result, good thermal contact can be effected between the end winding (17) and the housing (21), which is cooled via a cooling apparatus (25), for example.
problem: Thermal management in electric machines by improving heat dissipation from stator windings.
constraint: Achieving effective thermal contact without damaging the windings or compromising electrical insulation.
mechanism: A mechanical interface applies direct compressive force between a heat-generating component and a cooled structure, creating enhanced thermal contact through physical coupling to improve heat transfer efficiency.
mechanism_raw: End windings protruding beyond the stator body are mechanically pressed into a complementary housing cavity, creating direct thermal contact between the windings and a cooled housing structure to enhance heat transfer.

abstract: Cross-environment rendering and user interaction support provide a seamless computing experience in a multi-operating system computing environment. The multi-operating system computing environment may include a mobile operating system and a desktop operating system running concurrently and independently on a mobile computing device. The mobile operating system may be associated with a first user environment and the desktop operating system may be associated with a second user environment. Real-time display of applications running in the mobile operating system within the second user environment is provided by rendering the application through an extended graphics context of the mobile operating system. Application graphics for multiple applications are rendered into portions of a single graphics frame. The mobile computing device may be a smartphone running the Android mobile operating system and a full desktop Linux distribution on a modified Android kernel.
problem: Providing seamless user interaction and application rendering across multiple concurrent operating systems on a single device.
constraint: Synchronizing rendering and input handling between independent operating systems without performance degradation.
mechanism: A cross-environment graphics compositor merges visual outputs from independent execution contexts into a unified display frame, synchronizing rendering pipelines to enable real-time shared visual presentation across distinct systems.
mechanism_raw: Applications from a first operating system are rendered into a second operating system's environment via an extended graphics context, compositing multiple application graphics into a single frame to enable real-time cross-environment display.

abstract: A quick fastening device for fastening a guide rail to a horizontally extending rod having a bent end section on each end of the rod. The bent end sections each are fixed to a post of a grid. Each bent end section is encompassed by a clamp connected to the guide rail. The quick fastening device includes a stop abutting against the post on a side facing the guide rail. The stop is formed on the clamp.
problem: Quickly and securely fastening a guide rail to a rod with fixed bent end sections in a grid system.
constraint: Ensuring secure locking under load while permitting tool-free or rapid manual operation.
mechanism: A self-locking coupling mechanism uses a fixed reference point and compliant engagement to create positional stability under load, enabling rapid attachment/detachment through controlled mechanical interference.
mechanism_raw: A clamp with an integrated stop abuts a post on the rod's bent end section, allowing the clamp to self-lock against the post when tightened, enabling rapid attachment/detachment while maintaining positional stability.

abstract: A spring consists of, by weight %, 0.27 to 0.48% of C, 0.01 to 2.2% of Si, 0.30 to 1.0% of Mn, not more than 0.035% of P, not more than 0.035% of S, and the balance of Fe and inevitable impurities. The spring has a nitrogen compound layer and a carbon compound layer at the surface at a total thickness of not more than 2 μm. The spring has a center portion with hardness of 500 to 700 HV in a cross section and has a compressive residual stress layer at a surface layer. The compressive residual stress layer has a thickness of 0.30 mm to D/4, in which D (mm) is a circle-equivalent diameter of the cross section, and has maximum compressive residual stress of 1400 to 2000 MPa.
problem: Creating a spring that simultaneously achieves high core hardness for elastic performance and surface durability against fatigue failure, without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: The compressive residual stress layer thickness must be between 0.30 mm and D/4 (where D is the circle-equivalent diameter), and the surface compound layer must not exceed 2 μm total thickness, balancing fatigue improvement against surface brittleness and core hardness retention.
mechanism: A surface modification process creates a thin, highly stressed outer layer that resists crack initiation and propagation, while the underlying core retains high hardness for elastic function. The stressed layer thickness is scaled relative to the part's characteristic dimension, ensuring it is deep enough to intercept surface-initiated cracks but shallow enough to preserve core properties. The surface layer and core are engineered with complementary mechanical properties through controlled material treatment that establishes a stress gradient.
mechanism_raw: A surface treatment process (nitrogen/carbon compound layer formation) creates a thin surface layer with high compressive residual stress, while the core material is engineered to retain high hardness. The compressive stress layer acts as a barrier that prevents crack initiation and propagation from the surface, while the hard core maintains spring functionality. The thickness of the stress layer is scaled relative to the part diameter (0.30 mm to D/4), ensuring the stress field is deep enough to be effective but not so deep as to compromise the core properties.
residual_terms: ["compressive residual stress", "surface compound layer", "core hardness", "fatigue failure", "structural integrity", "circle-equivalent diameter"]

abstract: For controlling supply priorities, a hydraulic system includes several loads, a pump, and a tank. One load has a first-level supply priority, and optionally a second load has a second-level supply priority subordinate to the first level. A third load has a third-level supply priority subordinate to the second level. Each load can be connected to the pump by a separate supply line. The supply lines for the first and the optional second load are connected to the pump by a common load-pressure-controlled priority valve and the supply line for the third load is connected to the pump by an additional load-pressure-controlled priority valve. A first load-pressure line leading to the pump is connected to a load-pressure line of the third hydraulic load and to a second load-pressure line.
problem: Allocating limited hydraulic supply among multiple loads according to priority levels, ensuring higher-priority loads receive adequate pressure/flow before lower-priority loads, without complex electronic control systems.
constraint: The system must use purely hydraulic feedback (no electronic controllers), meaning valve response is directly tied to load pressure, limiting the speed and precision of priority switching to the mechanical response time of the valves and the pressure dynamics of the hydraulic fluid.
mechanism: A cascade of pressure-responsive control elements allocates supply among multiple loads based on priority levels. Each control element monitors the pressure state of its associated load group and restricts flow to lower-priority loads until higher-priority loads achieve their required pressure. The control elements are actuated directly by load pressure, creating a self-regulating system where supply is automatically directed to the highest-priority load still demanding it. Priority levels are established by arranging control elements in series, each responding to the pressure conditions of its designated load group.
mechanism_raw: Load-pressure feedback from each hydraulic load is fed back to priority-controlled valves. Each valve monitors the pressure demand of its associated load(s) and only allows flow to lower-priority loads when the higher-priority loads' pressure requirements are satisfied. The valve operation is directly controlled by the load pressure itself, creating a self-regulating cascade where supply is automatically diverted to the highest-priority load that still needs it. Multiple priority levels are achieved by cascading valves in series, each responding to the pressure state of its designated load group.

abstract: A method of clearing a pipe of contents with an air system. The method may include providing air by the air system at high pressure and low velocity until the contents begin to move within the pipe, providing air by the air system air at low pressure and high velocity until a majority of the contents are removed from the pipe, and continuing to provide air at low pressure and high velocity until substantially all remaining contents are removed from the pipe.
problem: Efficiently clearing the contents of a pipe using compressed air, where a single air delivery setting cannot optimally handle both the initiation of content movement and the complete removal of all residual contents.
constraint: The transition between stages must be triggered by the physical state of the pipe contents (initiation of movement, majority removal) rather than a fixed timer, requiring real-time sensing or observation of the clearing progress to determine when to switch air delivery parameters.
mechanism: A multi-stage delivery process uses different flow parameters for different phases of content removal. The first stage applies high-pressure, low-velocity flow to overcome static resistance and initiate movement. Once movement is detected, the system transitions to low-pressure, high-velocity flow to maximize transport capacity and remove the bulk of dislodged material. A final stage maintains the high-velocity flow to clear residual contents. Transitions between stages are triggered by the physical state of the contents rather than predetermined timing.
mechanism_raw: The clearing process is divided into sequential stages with different air delivery parameters. In the first stage, high pressure and low velocity air is used to generate sufficient force to overcome static friction and initiate movement of the pipe contents. Once movement begins, the system switches to low pressure and high velocity air, which maximizes flow rate and entrainment force to carry away the bulk of the dislodged contents. The final stage continues the low-pressure/high-velocity flow to remove remaining residual contents that require sustained flow rather than high impact force.
residual_terms: ["compressed air", "pipe contents", "static friction", "entrainment force", "residual contents", "flow rate", "pressure", "velocity"]

abstract: The invention relates to radiation-curable aqueous composition comprising an (meth)acrylated polyurethane prepolymer obtained from the reaction of a polyisocyanate, optionally a polyol, at least one hydrophilic compound containing at least one reactive group capable to react with isocyanate groups and which is capable to render the polyurethane pre-polymer dispersible in aqueous medium either directly or after the reaction with a neutralizing agent to provide a salt, an (meth)acrylated compound containing at least two reactive groups capable to react with isocyanate groups and an (meth)acrylated compound containing essentially one reactive group capable to react with isocyanate groups, said composition comprising an amount of (meth)acrylated and polymerizable ethylenically unsaturated groups of at least 3 meq per g.
problem: Formulating a radiation-curable aqueous coating composition that achieves sufficient crosslinking density for performance while remaining water-dispersible and processable, avoiding premature gelation or insufficient cure.
constraint: The composition must maintain at least 3 meq/g of polymerizable ethylenically unsaturated groups for adequate cure speed, while the ratio of multi-functional to mono-functional acrylated compounds must be balanced to achieve target crosslink density without causing premature gelation or loss of water dispersibility.
mechanism: A reactive composition balances network formation and chain termination by blending three functional components: a polymeric base with hydrophilic groups for dispersibility, a multi-functional reactive compound for crosslinking, and a mono-functional reactive compound for molecular weight control. The multi-functional compound forms the crosslinked network, while the mono-functional compound caps growing chains to prevent excessive molecular weight buildup that would compromise processability. A high density of reactive sites ensures sufficient crosslinking for rapid cure, while the hydrophilic base maintains compatibility with the processing medium.
mechanism_raw: The composition balances crosslinking and chain control by blending three types of reactive components: a polyurethane prepolymer with hydrophilic groups (for water dispersibility), a multi-functional acrylated compound (for crosslinking), and a mono-functional acrylated compound (for chain termination and molecular weight control). The multi-functional compound creates the crosslinked network, while the mono-functional compound caps growing chains, preventing excessive molecular weight buildup that would compromise dispersibility. The high density of ethylenically unsaturated groups (≥3 meq/g) ensures sufficient crosslinking sites for rapid UV-induced cure, while the hydrophilic prepolymer maintains water compatibility throughout the process.
residual_terms: ["radiation-curable", "aqueous coating", "crosslinking density", "water-dispersible", "ethylenically unsaturated groups", "polyurethane prepolymer", "hydrophilic groups", "acrylated compound", "UV-induced cure", "premature gelation"]

abstract: The present invention provides an engine oil composition containing polymethylacrylate, zinc alkyldithiophosphate, molybdenum dithiocarbamate, a hindered phenol antioxidant, and a fixed mineral oil. The engine oil composition of the present invention has a low-temperature viscosity The fuel efficiency of the engine oil is improved, when the engine oil composition with an improved low-temperature performance, a maintained high-temperature viscosity, an improved wear resistance, and an improved oxidation resistance is used. Further, the durability of the engine oil can also be ensured when the engine oil composition of the present invention is used.
problem: Formulating an engine oil that simultaneously delivers low-temperature fluidity, high-temperature viscosity retention, wear protection, oxidation resistance, fuel efficiency, and long-term durability, where optimizing one property typically degrades another.
constraint: The additive package must maintain chemical compatibility so that antioxidants do not degrade friction modifiers, anti-wear additives do not interfere with viscosity modifiers, and all components remain stable across the full operating temperature range without precipitation or phase separation.
mechanism: A multi-component formulation uses additives with complementary mechanisms of action, where each component addresses a distinct performance dimension without interfering with others. One component provides viscosity modification across temperature ranges. Another provides surface protection and oxidative stability. A third provides friction reduction for efficiency. A fourth provides oxidation resistance. The additives are formulated so their mechanisms are synergistic — for example, the friction-reducing component improves efficiency while the surface-protecting component operates under boundary conditions, and the oxidation inhibitor prevents degradation that would otherwise deplete other components.
mechanism_raw: The oil uses a synergistic blend of additives where each component addresses a distinct performance dimension without interfering with others. Polymethylacrylate provides viscosity index improvement (low-temp fluidity and high-temp retention). Zinc dialkyldithiophosphate provides anti-wear and antioxidant properties. Molybdenum dithiocarbamate provides friction modification for fuel efficiency and additional wear protection. A hindered phenol antioxidant provides oxidation resistance.
