The soluble mandrel serves as a temporary, removable internal support that enables the creation of large, seamless composite structures, and the method extends to embedding bosses and stiffeners directly within the composite during the over-wrap process.
residual_terms: ["temporary internal support", "composite over-wrap", "soluble mandrel", "seamless structure", "embedded features"]

abstract: A superhard structure comprises a body of polycrystalline superhard material comprising a first region and a second region. The second region is adjacent an exposed surface of the superhard structure and comprises a diamond material or cubic boron nitride with a density greater than 3.4×103 kilograms per cubic meter when the second region comprises diamond material. The material(s) forming the first and second regions have a difference in coefficient of thermal expansion, the first and second regions being arranged such that this difference induces compression in the second region adjacent the exposed surface. The first/a further region has the highest coefficient of thermal expansion of the polycrystalline body and is separated in part from a peripheral free surface of the body by the second region or one or more further regions formed of a material(s) of a lower coefficient of thermal expansion. The regions comprise a plurality of grains of polycrystalline superhard material. The second region is peripherally discontinuous with a gap therein through which a portion of the region formed of the material of highest coefficient of thermal expansion extends to the free surface of the superhard structure. There is also disclosed a method for making such a structure.
problem: Creating a superhard structure with induced compressive stress at the exposed surface to improve mechanical performance such as wear resistance and fracture toughness.
constraint: The materials must have sufficiently different coefficients of thermal expansion to induce meaningful compression, but the arrangement must be carefully designed with the peripheral gap to control where compression is induced. The gap allows selective extension of high-CTE material to the surface while preserving the compressive stress pattern, requiring precise geometric and material property coordination.
mechanism: Multiple regions of superhard material with different thermal expansion coefficients are arranged so that during temperature changes, the differential thermal expansion between adjacent regions induces controlled compressive stress in the surface region. The highest expansion material is separated from the peripheral free surface by lower expansion materials, creating a thermal stress gradient that puts the surface layer in compression. A peripheral discontinuity in the lower expansion region allows portions of the highest expansion material to extend to the free surface while maintaining the overall compressive stress pattern in the surface region.
mechanism_raw: Multiple regions of polycrystalline superhard material with different coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) are arranged so that during temperature changes, the differential thermal expansion between adjacent regions induces controlled compressive stress in the surface region. The highest CTE material is separated from the peripheral free surface by lower CTE materials, creating a thermal stress gradient that puts the surface layer in compression. A peripheral discontinuity (gap) in the lower CTE region allows portions of the highest CTE material to extend to the free surface while maintaining the overall compressive stress pattern in the surface region.
residual_terms: ["thermal expansion coefficients", "compressive stress", "superhard material", "thermal stress gradient", "peripheral discontinuity"]

abstract: A refrigeration cycle apparatus includes a refrigeration cycle formed by a first compressor, a radiator, an expander that expands a refrigerant that has passed through the radiator, and an evaporator. A bypass piping has one end connected to a discharge piping of the expander and the other end connected to a suction piping of the first compressor. A pressure sensor and a temperature sensor detect the suction pressure and suction temperature of the expander as physical quantities of the refrigerant to be sucked into the expander. A bypass valve controls the flow rate of the refrigerant. A control device determines the appropriate discharge pressure of the expander on the basis of the suction pressure and suction temperature of the expander, and opens the bypass valve when the pressure at which the expander discharges the refrigerant is higher than the determined appropriate discharge pressure.
problem: Managing the discharge pressure of an expander in a refrigeration cycle to maintain system efficiency and prevent overloading.
constraint: Balancing refrigerant flow rates to maintain thermodynamic efficiency while avoiding excessive pressure that could destabilize the cycle.
mechanism: A feedback control system monitors operating parameters of a working fluid, computes a target output pressure based on those parameters, and actuates a flow diversion element when the actual output pressure exceeds the computed target, thereby regulating system pressure to maintain efficiency and prevent overload.
mechanism_raw: A feedback control system uses sensors to detect suction pressure and temperature of the refrigerant, calculates an appropriate discharge pressure, and actuates a bypass valve to divert refrigerant flow when the actual discharge pressure exceeds the calculated threshold.

abstract: Embodiments of the present invention include a method, computer program product, and system for generating a visualization of an optimized project. The computer receives a project and a period of interest associated with the project. The computer determines a constraint status for each constraint associated with the project. The computer generates a graphical element that illustrates the constraint status. The computer generates a visualization of the project during the period of interest, wherein the visualization includes concentric geometric structures and the graphical element.
reason: The mechanism is a visualization technique using concentric geometric structures to represent constraints, which is a static architectural choice rather than a causal functional relationship solving a problem.

abstract: An electronic device may be provided with a display. The display may be a variable frame rate display capable of adaptively adjusting a frame rate at which display frames are displayed in response to information associated with the current state of operation of the device. The information may be gathered using control circuitry in the electronic device. The control circuitry may gather the information for adjusting the frame rate by monitoring the electronic device power supply configuration, other device components, the type of content to be displayed, and user-input signals. The control circuitry may adjust the frame rate based on the gathered information by increasing or decreasing the frame rate. The control circuitry may be formed as a portion of display control circuitry for the device such as a display driver integrated circuit or may be formed as a portion of storage and processing circuitry external to the display.
problem: Optimizing power consumption and performance in an electronic device by dynamically adjusting display frame rates based on operational context.
constraint: Balancing visual quality and responsiveness against power efficiency and hardware limitations.
mechanism: Control circuitry monitors multiple operational inputs representing power state, component activity, content characteristics, and user interaction, and dynamically adjusts the output refresh rate of a display by increasing or decreasing it in response to real-time data, balancing visual quality and responsiveness against power efficiency and hardware constraints.
mechanism_raw: Control circuitry monitors multiple inputs (power supply state, component activity, content type, user signals) and adjusts the display frame rate by increasing or decreasing it in response to real-time operational data.
residual_terms: ["control circuitry", "display", "frame rate", "refresh rate", "power supply state", "component activity", "content type", "user signals"]

abstract: The inventive substrate treatment apparatus includes a spin chuck which horizontally holds and rotates a wafer; a heater which is disposed in opposed relation to a lower surface of the wafer held by the spin chuck and heats the wafer from a lower side; a phosphoric acid nozzle which spouts a phosphoric acid aqueous solution to a front surface (upper surface) of the wafer held by the spin chuck; and a suspension liquid nozzle which spouts a silicon suspension liquid to the front surface of the wafer held by the spin chuck. The wafer is maintained at a higher temperature on the order of 300° C. and, in this state, a liquid mixture of the phosphoric acid aqueous solution and the silicon suspension liquid is supplied to the front surface of the wafer.
reason: The mechanism is a specific chemical process application (heating and co-application of phosphoric acid and silicon suspension) with no generalizable causal principle beyond its narrow technical domain.

abstract: The present application provides a four-bar press that includes a plurality of linkages and at least one element for maintaining at least one of the plurality of linkages in the four bar press in compression during at least a portion of a press cycle. This beneficially reduces undesirable characteristics of the press, such as jerk, which enables use of smaller and lighter components.
problem: Reducing undesirable dynamic forces (e.g., jerk) in a mechanical press to enable lighter and smaller components without compromising structural integrity.
constraint: Ensuring structural support and force transmission while minimizing component size and weight.
mechanism: A mechanical linkage system incorporates elements that maintain compressive force in at least one linkage during a portion of the operating cycle, counteracting tensile forces that cause vibration and instability, thereby reducing dynamic forces to enable lighter and smaller components without compromising structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical linkage system incorporates elements that maintain compression in at least one linkage during a portion of the press cycle, counteracting tensile forces that cause vibration and instability.

abstract: A method of manufacturing a roll of bottom gusseted pouches serially connected in a top-to-bottom end orientation is provided. The method comprises unwinding a pouch webbing in a first flow direction, the pouch webbing defining front and back panels of a respective pouch; inserting a gusset webbing between the panels in a second flow direction; attaching the gusset webbing to the panels to form the bottom gusseted end of the pouch; inserting a closure mechanism between the panels in a third flow direction; attaching the closure mechanism to the panels to form the resealable top end of the pouch; sealing the side edges of the panels to complete the pouch; winding the completed pouch onto the roll; and repeating these steps to form the other bottom gusseted pouches in the roll. At least one of the pouch webbing and the gusset webbing is formed of a supported film.
problem: Manufacturing bottom gusseted pouches serially connected on a roll while continuously moving a web through the process, requiring insertion and attachment of internal components (gusset and closure) from different directions without stopping the web.
constraint: The web must remain continuously supported and in motion throughout all insertion and attachment steps, while each component must be introduced from a different direction and properly aligned and bonded without disrupting the flow of the main web.
mechanism: Sequential multi-directional component insertion onto a continuously moving substrate: a primary substrate is advanced in a first direction, then a first component is introduced from a second direction and attached to form a structural feature, followed by inserting a second component from a third direction and attaching it to form a functional interface, all while the substrate remains in motion and supported. Each component is introduced from a direction optimized for its function and then bonded to the substrate before the completed assembly is collected.
mechanism_raw: Sequential multi-directional component insertion onto a continuously moving web: a main pouch webbing is unwound in a first flow direction, then a gusset webbing is inserted between the panels from a second (different) flow direction and attached to form the bottom gusset, followed by inserting a closure mechanism from a third flow direction and attaching it to form the resealable top, all while the web remains in motion and supported. Each component is introduced from a direction optimized for its function and then bonded to the panels before the completed pouch is wound onto a roll.

abstract: A page-turning device turning a page of a book includes a sticking part, an arm part and a drive unit. The sticking part sticks to the page of the book being opened. The arm part is provided with the sticking part on a top end and swings such that the sticking part sticks to the page at a departure position of the page and separates from the page at a destination position of the page while the sticking part goes to and fro between the departure position and the destination position over the page of the book. The drive unit swings the arm part around a drive shaft of the drive unit. The drive shaft is inclined with respect to a seam of the opened book and/or a plane on which the book is disposed.
problem: Automatically turning pages of a book without manual intervention, requiring reliable gripping of a page at one position and release at another position as the page is moved across the book's surface.
constraint: The sticking part must adhere reliably at the departure position and release reliably at the destination position, which requires the drive shaft angle to be precisely inclined relative to the book's seam and plane to ensure the correct gripping and releasing dynamics throughout the swing motion.
mechanism: Controlled adhesion and release through mechanically guided movement: an adhesion element engages a surface at a departure position and is carried by a pivotable arm to a destination position, where the relative motion between the adhesion element and the surface causes separation. The drive mechanism is angled relative to the surface's seam and/or plane, optimizing the angle of approach and departure so that adhesion occurs at the departure point and release occurs at the destination point through the geometric relationship between the arm's path and the surface's orientation.
mechanism_raw: Controlled adhesion and release through mechanically guided movement: a sticking part adheres to a page at a departure position and is carried by a swinging arm to a destination position, where the relative motion between the sticking part and the page causes separation. The drive shaft is inclined relative to the book's seam and/or the plane of the book, optimizing the angle of approach and departure so that adhesion occurs at the departure point and release occurs at the destination point through the geometric relationship between the arm's swing path and the book's orientation.
residual_terms: ["adhesion element", "pivotable arm", "drive mechanism", "surface's seam and plane"]

abstract: Apparatus and methods for a sensor system are provided. The system may be configured to detect a dispensing of cash from an automated teller machine (“ATM”). The system may be configured to orient one or more sensors to capture a first information stream that includes the dispensing of cash. The system may be configured to detect a retraction of cash by the ATM. The system may orient one or more sensors to capture a second information stream that includes the retraction. The system may be configured to determine an estimate of cash collected by an ATM customer. The estimate may be based on a comparison of the first information stream and the second information stream.
problem: Accurately estimating the amount of cash actually collected by an ATM customer, since the amount dispensed may differ from the amount taken (e.g., customer takes less than dispensed, or ATM retracts some bills).
constraint: The sensors must be oriented and configured to capture both the dispensing and retraction events as complete information streams, and the comparison must account for the temporal and quantitative relationship between the two streams to accurately determine the net cash flow to the customer.
mechanism: Differential sensing through complementary information streams: the system captures a first stream representing dispensing events and a second stream representing retraction events, then compares these two streams to determine the net amount of resource that left the system with the user. The difference between what was dispensed and what was retracted yields the estimate of resource collected.
mechanism_raw: Differential sensing through complementary information streams: the system captures a first information stream representing cash dispensing events and a second information stream representing cash retraction events, then compares these two streams to determine the net amount of cash that left the ATM with the customer. The difference between what was dispensed and what was retracted yields the estimate of cash collected.

abstract: A cosmetic brush cleaner apparatus is provided for automatically washing, cleaning, rinsing, and sanitizing a plurality of cosmetic brushes quickly, efficiently, and effectively. In particular, the cosmetic brush cleaner includes a removable lid, a base having a liquid inlet port, a removable brush holder coupled to the base, wherein the brush holder secures one or more cosmetic brushes. The cleaner further comprises a bristle plate coupled to the base, a liquid dispensing port for dispensing the liquid on to the bristle plate, a liquid drainage port for draining the liquid from the bristle plate, wherein the bristle plate is configured to engage the cosmetic brushes, and a controller for operating a motor of the brush cleaner.
reason: The patent describes a cosmetic brush cleaner apparatus that is primarily a collection of components (lid, base, brush holder, bristle plate, liquid dispensing/drainage ports, motor, controller) assembled to perform cleaning. The underlying operation—mechanically engaging brushes with a plate while dispensing and draining liquid under motor control—is a standard cleaning mechanism without a novel or non-obvious causal principle that would transfer to a different field. It reads as a product feature list rather than a transferable problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: A low pressure fogging device includes a fogging device body having a hose coupling tube formed unitarily with the lower side thereof, a screw portion formed on the upper side thereof, and a fluid flow-inducing member seating plate formed on top of the screw portion; a fluid flow-inducing member having induction wings seated on top of the fluid flow-inducing member seating plate; a nozzle body having a fitting hole open downwardly therefrom to allow the fluid flow-inducing member seating plate and the fluid flow-inducing member to be fitted thereto; and a push-up nut having a pressuring ring formed at the center thereof to be locked onto a locking projection formed from an outer lower end periphery of the nozzle body and a screw groove formed at the inner periphery thereof to be fastened to a screw portion formed on the fogging device body.
reason: The patent describes a low pressure fogging device whose operation is fundamentally a standard fluid flow system using induction wings and a mechanical push-up nut for assembly. The components (hose coupling tube, screw portion, seating plate, induction wings, nozzle body, push-up nut with pressuring ring and screw groove) are specific mechanical parts assembled in a particular configuration. While the push-up nut provides a two-mode fastening (screw engagement plus radial locking), the overall mechanism is a conventional fluid delivery and mechanical fastening design without a deeper causal principle that would generalize to other problem domains.

abstract: The present invention concerns an apparatus (1) for deployment and retrieval of a measurement system (8) on an ocean bottom, comprising devices for temporary storing the measurement system (8), movable control faces (7), software and devices for manoeuvring and at least one ballast tank (11A) for ballast (11B). The ballast (11B) comprises a slurry consisting of free soluble salt and a saturated solution of the salt in water, or a solid body or insoluble coarse or fine grained material.
problem: Precisely deploying and retrieving a measurement system on the ocean bottom while maintaining stability and buoyancy control in a dynamic underwater environment.
constraint: Balancing the slurry's solubility and density to achieve rapid buoyancy adjustments without destabilizing the system, while ensuring the ballast material remains compatible with underwater conditions and mechanical components.
mechanism: Using a controllable-density medium within a sealed chamber to dynamically adjust buoyancy forces, enabling vertical positioning and stabilization of a submerged system. The medium's density is modulated by dissolving or precipitating a solute, allowing fine-tuned buoyancy adjustments without external mechanical actuation.
mechanism_raw: Using a ballast slurry composed of free soluble salt and saturated salt solution (or solid material) to dynamically adjust buoyancy. The slurry's density can be controlled by dissolving or precipitating salt, enabling fine-tuned vertical positioning and stabilization of the measurement system during deployment and retrieval.

abstract: The present invention relates to an elastic terpolymer that can acquire good mechanical properties and elasticity (flexibility) at the same time, and a preparation method thereof. The elastic terpolymer, which is a copolymer comprising 40 to 70 wt % of ethylene, 20 to 50 wt % of a C3-C20 alpha-olefin, and 2 to 20 wt % of a diene as obtained in the presence of a catalyst comprising a vanadium compound, satisfies that: (i) the weight average molecular weight measured by GPC is 100,000 to 500,000; and (ii) in the monomer distribution of the copolymer determined by 13C NMR analysis, K given by a defined Equation 1 is 0.01 or less.
problem: Achieving simultaneous high mechanical strength and elasticity in a terpolymer material without compromising either property.
constraint: Maintaining the narrow molecular weight range and monomer distribution to prevent phase separation or uneven polymerization, which could degrade mechanical or elastic properties.
mechanism: Designing a multi-component polymer system where crosslinking agents and monomer ratios are balanced to achieve simultaneous mechanical strength and elasticity. A catalyst controls molecular weight and distribution, while specific monomer types introduce structural features (e.g., branching or crosslinks) that govern stiffness and flexibility tradeoffs.
mechanism_raw: Designing a copolymer composition (ethylene, C3-C20 alpha-olefin, and diene) with a vanadium-based catalyst to control molecular weight (100,000–500,000) and monomer distribution (K ≤ 0.01). The diene content introduces crosslinks or branching, enabling elasticity, while the alpha-olefin and ethylene balance stiffness and flexibility.

abstract: The present disclosure provides a hydrophobic and oleophobic coating composition, which comprises the following components based on weight percentage: 0.1-15% of a fluorosiloxane, 1-30% of a polyacrylic resin, 0.1-15% of a silane coupler, 33-98% of an organic solvent, and 0.05-15% of an acid. By combining the polyacrylic resin and the fluorosiloxane which exhibits hydrophobic property, the present composition not only provides good hydrophobic property but also ensures durable hydrophobic property of the coating with the help of good adhesion of polyacrylic resin. The coating composition can form hard coating which has high glossiness and high transparency under relatively low temperatures and has a contact angle of 115-120°. This coating composition can be used on surfaces of substrates, such as automotive paints, metal, plastic and glass, and it can retain long lasting hydrophobic and oleophobic property even placed outdoors for several months, and it can also prevent the surface of the substrate from being scratched.
problem: Creating a durable hydrophobic/oleophobic coating that retains adhesion and structural integrity under outdoor conditions while maintaining optical clarity and hardness.
constraint: Balancing the fluorosiloxane and polyacrylic resin ratios to avoid compromising adhesion or durability, while ensuring the acid and solvent concentrations do not degrade the coating's optical or chemical resistance properties.
mechanism: Combining a surface-modifying agent with a structural resin matrix, using an interfacial bonding enhancer to maintain adhesion and durability. The surface-modifying agent provides functional properties (e.g., repellency), while the resin ensures mechanical integrity. A curing process forms a hardened, optically clear coating.
mechanism_raw: Combining a fluorosiloxane (for hydrophobic/oleophobic properties) with a polyacrylic resin (for adhesion and mechanical strength). The silane coupler enhances interfacial bonding between the fluorosiloxane and substrate, while the acid component stabilizes the formulation. The solvent system enables low-temperature curing to form a hard, transparent coating.
residual_terms: ["surface-modifying agent", "structural resin matrix", "interfacial bonding enhancer", "curing process"]

abstract: A fracturing apparatus in a wellbore, having a housing with at least one injection port; an injection fluid supply interface to provide injection fluid for the fracturing apparatus; and at least one high pressure combustor received within the housing. The housing further includes a combustible medium interface that is in fluid communication with the at least one high pressure combustor, which is configured and arranged to provide repeated ignition cycles that include a combustion cycle that ignites the combustible medium and a fuel delivery cycle that delivers the combustible medium to the combustor, wherein pressure resulting from the combustion cycle forces the injection fluid out an injection port to cause fracturing in a portion of the earth around the wellbore.
problem: Generating controlled, high-pressure fluid pulses to fracture subterranean formations around a wellbore without relying on external hydraulic systems.
constraint: Managing thermal and pressure cycling to prevent combustor degradation, while synchronizing ignition and fuel delivery to maintain consistent fracturing pressure without overpressurization.
mechanism: Generating repetitive pressure pulses through cyclic combustion events in a confined chamber. Each combustion event forces a working fluid through an orifice to create fracturing pressure, while a replenishment cycle restores the chamber for continuous operation. Pressure and timing are synchronized to maintain consistent output without overpressurization.
mechanism_raw: Using repeated combustion cycles in a high-pressure combustor to generate pressure pulses. Each cycle ignites a combustible medium, forcing injection fluid through a port to create fracturing pressure. The fuel delivery cycle replenishes the combustor, enabling continuous operation.

abstract: A pump dispenser is arranged for dispensing solidous material under a manually-developed pressure, with the dispenser being capable of pumping and mechanically agitating the solidous material in a storage container. The resultant dispensed solidous fluid is provided with more consistent suspended solid concentrations with greater solid particle distribution homogeneity.
problem: Dispensing solidous materials (e.g., suspensions) with uniform particle distribution and consistent concentration during manual operation.
constraint: Balancing agitation intensity and pumping pressure to avoid shear-induced particle damage or excessive energy input, while maintaining compatibility with manual operation.
mechanism: Integrating continuous mechanical agitation with manual dispensing action to maintain homogeneity of a particulate-laden material during flow. The agitation prevents particle settling and clogging, while the dispensing mechanism ensures consistent output. Energy input is balanced to avoid damaging shear forces on the particles.
mechanism_raw: Integrating mechanical agitation with manual pumping to continuously remix the solidous material during dispensing. The agitation prevents particle settling and clogging, while the pumping action maintains flow, ensuring homogeneity in the dispensed output.

abstract: The present invention provides an apparatus for simultaneously producing different cannabinoids in different ratios. Specifically, the apparatus according to the invention produces tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA) and cannabichormenic acid (CBCA) or cannabidiolic acid (CBDA) in different ratios, and it comprises a bioreactor that comprises a first automated supply system configured to deliver a substrate and a cannabinoid acid synthase, and a second automated system to cease the reaction; an extractor configured to recover the cannabionoids so produced; and a controller configured to modify at least on property of the reaction.
problem: Producing specific cannabinoid ratios (e.g., THCA, CBCA, CBDA) in a bioreactor requires precise control over reaction conditions and termination timing to avoid cross-contamination or inefficiency.
constraint: Balancing real-time parameter adjustments with bioreactor stability to maintain consistent product ratios without disrupting the reaction environment.
mechanism: Dynamic parameter adjustment in a reaction system using real-time monitoring to control product composition, where a controller modifies reaction conditions (e.g., temperature, pH, timing) and terminates processes based on detected progress to steer toward target output ratios.
mechanism_raw: Automated substrate delivery and reaction termination systems, combined with a controller that dynamically modifies reaction parameters (e.g., temperature, pH, timing) to steer the biochemical process toward desired cannabinoid ratios.

abstract: A timed electrical power strip assembly allows each of a plurality of electrical outlet receptacles to be controlled by a separate timer. The assembly includes a power strip housing having a top wall, a bottom wall and a peripheral wall attached to and extending between the top and bottom walls. A plurality of electrical outlet receptacles is disposed within the housing and extends through the top wall. Each of the receptacles has a plurality of openings therein wherein each of the openings is configured to receive a male plug-in end of an external electrical cord. A plurality of individual timer switches is provided. Each of the individual timer switches is electrically coupled to an associated receptacle wherein manipulation of the individual timer switches selectively provides power to the associated one of the receptacles for a selectable period of time.
problem: Controlling power delivery to multiple electrical outlets independently on separate schedules without manual intervention or affecting other outlets.
constraint: Physically integrating multiple independent timers within a single housing while maintaining electrical isolation and user accessibility.
mechanism: Independent per-outlet scheduling using individual timer switches with electrical isolation, enabling modular power delivery control without centralized coordination or cross-interference between outlets.
mechanism_raw: Each outlet is paired with an individual timer switch that can be set to provide power for a selectable duration, enabling modular, per-outlet scheduling without centralized control.

abstract: A clock and data recovery device includes a phase detector, a quantizer, and a loop filter. The phase detector produces a phase error samples at an output representing a phase difference between a phase-adjusted clock and an input data signal. The quantizer, coupled to the output of the phase detector and responsive to high threshold and low threshold values, produces a tri-valued quantized phase error samples at an output. The loop filter filters either the quantized phase error samples or the phase error samples to control the phase-controlled clock. A frequency detector, determining the frequency of jitter present in the input data signal, addresses a look-up table to provide the jitter-frequency dependent high and low threshold values and to control which phase error samples is processed by the loop filter. The frequency detector determines the jitter frequency by taking the ratio of peak values of low pass-filtered phase error samples.
problem: Recovering a stable clock signal from a jittered input data signal in high-speed communication systems.
constraint: Balancing jitter suppression with loop stability to avoid overcorrection or loss of synchronization under varying signal conditions.
mechanism: Adaptive thresholding in a quantizer, where high/low thresholds are dynamically adjusted based on detected jitter characteristics (via peak ratio analysis of filtered phase error samples), allowing a loop filter to process either quantized or raw phase errors for optimal tracking.
mechanism_raw: Adaptive thresholding in a quantizer, where high/low thresholds are dynamically adjusted based on detected jitter frequency (via peak ratio analysis of filtered phase error samples), allowing the loop filter to process either quantized or raw phase errors for optimal tracking.

abstract: A method for determining a set of control parameters of a control sequence for a magnetic resonance device is provided. The set of control parameters is chosen from a plurality of sets of basic parameters. The method includes determining a mean flip angle for each set of basic parameters in an imaging region where an object exists using the set of basic parameters with a first measuring method. For each set of basic parameters, a signal strength of a magnetic resonance signal generated in the case of a reference flip angle of a second measuring method distinguished by a signal maximum or a signal minimum is determined, and the set of basic parameters having a signal strength that is extremal in accordance with the choice of reference flip angle is chosen as the set of control parameters.
problem: Selecting optimal control parameters for a magnetic resonance imaging device to maximize signal strength in a target region.
constraint: Trade-off between computational efficiency of parameter evaluation and the need to account for spatial variability in signal response across the imaging region.
mechanism: Parameter selection via spatial averaging and extremal signal analysis, where candidate parameter sets are evaluated by measuring mean response across a region and identifying signal extrema at a reference condition, with the set producing extremal strength selected as optimal.
mechanism_raw: Evaluating candidate parameter sets using two methods: (1) measuring mean flip angles across an imaging region, and (2) identifying signal extrema (maxima/minima) at a reference flip angle. The parameter set producing extremal signal strength is selected as optimal.

abstract: The invention relates to a replaceable die for pliers to press workpieces, such as for crimping pliers for pressing electrical connector elements. By replacing the die, the pliers can be adapted to the press operation to be performed, such as adapting a crimping pliers to different types and sizes of the connector elements to be pressed. The die according to the invention comprises a first and a second die half that can be inserted into the pliers together and removed from the pliers together. The two die halves each have a guide for this purpose. Both die halves each further have a first connecting element for releasably attaching the die to the pliers. Both die halves finally each have a second connecting element for releasably attaching the die to a storage fixture. This ensures that the die formed by the two die halves is held in the storage fixture during or after removal from the pliers, and remains therein for storage.
problem: Adapting pliers to different press operations while ensuring replaceable dies remain securely attached to storage fixtures during or after removal from the pliers.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical compatibility between the die halves, pliers, and storage fixture while enabling quick, tool-free insertion and removal.
mechanism: Dual attachment mechanisms on die halves for secure coupling to both operational and storage interfaces, ensuring the die halves remain as a unit during use and storage through separate connecting elements for each interface.
mechanism_raw: Dual connecting elements on each die half: one for releasable attachment to the pliers and another for attachment to a storage fixture, ensuring the die halves stay together as a unit during both use and storage.

abstract: Methods and apparatus for an acoustic source for directing acoustic energy to ensonify a container, a sensor to detect acoustic energy from the acoustic source affected by an object in the container without contacting the container, and a processing module to process the detected acoustic energy from the sensor to identify the object in the container.
problem: Identifying objects inside a container without physical contact or direct visual access.
constraint: Balancing the need for non-contact detection with sufficient sensitivity to distinguish objects of varying material properties and shapes.
mechanism: Directing energy into a confined space and analyzing modifications to the energy caused by an object's presence, using a sensor to detect these modifications and a processor to infer the object's characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Directing acoustic energy into the container and analyzing how the energy is altered by the object's presence, using a sensor to detect these changes and a processor to infer the object's characteristics.

abstract: A soft-sided insulated container assembly is made of a flexible wall structure that is movable between a collapsed position and a deployed position. In one variation of the deployed position it resembles a tote-bag; in another variation of folding the deployed position corresponds to a generally box-like shape. The container includes a self-inflating wall structure that has an inner layer or skin, an outer layer or skin, and a resilient, open-cell insulating layer trapped between the two skins. A valve governs the ability to take in or to expel air. The outer layer may be thicker and more robust that the inner layer, the better to resist abrasion or punctures. The inner layer may be reflective. There may be a removable internal liner. That liner may be transparent.
problem: Creating an insulated container that can switch between collapsed and deployed states while maintaining thermal performance and structural integrity.
constraint: Balancing insulation effectiveness with the ability to collapse the container for storage or transport without compromising durability.
mechanism: Employing a self-adjusting wall structure with a valve-controlled fluid intake/expulsion system and layered materials to dynamically modify the container's shape and insulation properties while maintaining structural integrity.
mechanism_raw: Using a self-inflating wall structure with a valve-controlled air intake/expulsion system and layered materials (inner reflective layer, outer abrasion-resistant layer, and open-cell insulating foam) to dynamically adjust the container's shape and insulation properties.

abstract: The present invention provides deoxynucleoside tri- or tetraphosphate comprising a 3′ nitrate and a detectable label covalently bound to the oxygen atom of an oxymethyl or oxyallyl or oxypropargyl substitution of a nucleobase. Such compounds provide new possibilities for future Sequencing by Synthesis technologies.
problem: Enabling detectable labeling of nucleotides for sequencing-by-synthesis technologies without disrupting the enzymatic or chemical processes involved.
constraint: Ensuring the label's attachment site and chemical stability do not interfere with the sequencing reaction while remaining detectable.
mechanism: Covalently attaching a detectable label to a specific chemical site on a nucleobase, enabling detection or cleavage during sequencing without disrupting base pairing or enzymatic processes.
mechanism_raw: Covalently attaching a detectable label to a specific oxygen atom of an oxymethyl, oxyallyl, or oxypropargyl substitution on a nucleobase, allowing the label to be cleaved or detected during sequencing without interfering with base pairing or polymerization.

abstract: A unitary resilient rubber finger pad for a poultry plucking machine, the finger pad having a circular base with a central aperture therethrough, an annular base plate completely embedded within the circular base; a plurality of fingers extending from one face of the base, each of the fingers being fixed to the face of said base, each of said fingers having a base, a tapered shank, and a grip pattern on a portion of said shank remote from said base; the fingers being arranged in a pair of concentric rings on the base. The method of mounting the finger pad is also disclosed.
problem: Designing a resilient, durable finger pad for poultry plucking machines that maintains consistent grip and wear resistance under repetitive mechanical stress.
constraint: Balancing flexibility and resilience to withstand repeated contact while maintaining structural integrity and effective plucking action.
mechanism: Structuring a contact surface with a tapered force-distributing shank and patterned grip elements arranged in concentric rings, combined with a resilient base and embedded reinforcement, to enhance surface interaction and withstand repetitive mechanical stress.
mechanism_raw: Structuring fingers with a tapered shank and grip patterns arranged in concentric rings, combined with a unitary rubber base and embedded annular plate, to distribute mechanical forces and enhance surface interaction with poultry skin.

abstract: A powder classifying device includes a plurality of powder classifiers that impart a whirling motion to powder with whirling gas streams to classify the powder into coarse powder and fine powder, a gas supply source that supplies the plurality of powder classifiers with gas for generating the whirling gas stream, a powder supplier that supplies the plurality of powder classifiers with powder having a particle size distribution, a fine powder collecting section that collects fine powder classified by each of the plurality of powder classifiers, a coarse powder recovery section that recovers coarse powder classified by each of the plurality of powder classifiers, and a controller that controls flow rates of gases supplied to the plurality of powder classifiers so that a classification point is substantially equal among the plurality of powder classifiers.
problem: Achieving uniform powder classification across multiple classifiers in a system to ensure consistent particle size separation.
constraint: Maintaining real-time responsiveness to flow rate adjustments while ensuring minimal cross-classifier interference and energy efficiency.
mechanism: Using a controller to dynamically adjust fluid flow rates supplied to each classifier, synchronizing their separation thresholds by compensating for variations in input or environmental conditions to ensure uniform classification.
mechanism_raw: Using a controller to dynamically adjust gas flow rates supplied to each classifier, synchronizing their classification points by compensating for variations in powder input or environmental conditions.

abstract: A printing control apparatus which discharges ink from nozzles, while moving a printing head that includes at least a first nozzle row in which a plurality of nozzles capable of discharging a same type of ink are arranged in a predetermined nozzle row direction and a second nozzle row in which a plurality of nozzles capable of discharging the same type of ink are arranged in the nozzle row direction, in a main scanning direction intersecting with the nozzle row direction, in which, when, out of a group of raster lines corresponds to odd-numbered positions in the nozzle row direction and a group of raster lines which corresponds to even-numbered positions in the nozzle row direction, one group of the raster lines is printed by discharging the ink from the nozzle row out of the first nozzle row and the second nozzle row, which precedes during the movement.
problem: Inefficient or inconsistent raster line printing due to fixed nozzle row usage during bidirectional print head movement.
constraint: Balancing print speed and quality by coordinating nozzle activation with print head movement direction to avoid misalignment or redundant passes.
mechanism: Alternating between two output elements based on positional parity to synchronize activation timing with directional movement, ensuring alignment by selecting the element that precedes during motion.
mechanism_raw: Alternating which nozzle row (first or second) is used to print raster lines based on their odd/even position in the nozzle row direction, selecting the nozzle row that precedes during movement to ensure optimal ink discharge timing and alignment.

abstract: This relates to vacuum insulated glass (VIG) window units and methods for making VIG window units. Hybrid getter(s) are utilized. In certain example embodiments, a hybrid getter for use in a VIG window unit and/or a method making same includes both evaporable getter (EG) material and non-evaporable getter (NEG) material. In certain example embodiments, the NEG material may be covered (directly or indirectly) with EG material in the hybrid getter at least prior to getter activating/flashing.
problem: Maintaining long-term vacuum integrity in vacuum insulated glass (VIG) units while ensuring rapid initial evacuation.
constraint: Optimizing the spatial and temporal interaction between EG and NEG materials to ensure initial sealing without compromising long-term stability.
mechanism: Combining two materials with distinct activation kinetics—rapidly reactive and sustained-reactivity—by layering the sustained-reactivity material beneath the rapidly reactive one to enable staged environmental response.
mechanism_raw: Combining evaporable getter (EG) material, which rapidly absorbs gases during initial activation, with non-evaporable getter (NEG) material, which provides sustained vacuum maintenance, by covering NEG with EG to enable staged activation.

abstract: A proposal is made for a cementitious system which comprises accelerator particles coated with crosslinked shellac, for the use as an additive component which comprises the accelerator particles coated with crosslinked shellac, and for a cement slurry which comprises the cementitious system and water.
problem: Premature or uncontrolled acceleration of cement setting due to unregulated release of accelerator compounds.
constraint: Designing coating integrity to prevent premature degradation while ensuring timely release under intended use conditions.
mechanism: Encapsulating active particles with a degradable barrier that remains intact until exposed to specific environmental triggers, delaying release until the barrier breaks down under intended conditions.
mechanism_raw: Encapsulating accelerator particles with crosslinked shellac coatings that degrade under specific environmental conditions (e.g., moisture, heat), delaying accelerator release until the coating breaks down.

abstract: The invention relates to a drilling unit with a carrier vehicle with a hydraulic supply, a mast, a carriage which can be moved along the mast and a hydraulic cylinder for moving the carriage which comprises a cylinder housing, in which a piston with a piston rod is mounted so that it can be displaced. The piston rod is fixed to the mast and the cylinder housing to the carriage. The carriage is connected to the hydraulic supply and comprises at least one hydraulic connection. The hydraulic cylinder is connected via the hydraulic connection on the carriage to the hydraulic supply.
problem: Inefficient or unstable hydraulic actuation for moving a drilling carriage along a mast due to complex mechanical linkages or fluid routing.
constraint: Maintaining hydraulic pressure and fluid flow through a moving carriage interface while minimizing mechanical complexity and wear.
mechanism: Fixing a linear actuator component to a stationary structure and attaching the complementary component to a moving platform, with integrated fluid pathways to enable direct power transfer without external routing.
mechanism_raw: Fixing the piston rod to the mast and the cylinder housing to the carriage, with hydraulic connections integrated into the carriage to enable direct power transfer and movement without external hoses or linkages.

abstract: A video display device is provided to achieve local control for a high-quality 3D image while reducing extraneous radiation. A video display device that receives video signals from two video signal lines with an identical frame period and is capable of displaying a stereoscopic image based on left-eye and right-eye images, the video display device including: a liquid crystal drive unit; a liquid crystal panel; an LED backlight that has a plurality of light emission areas; a combination unit that generates a composite video signal by combining the video signals with the identical frame period; a local control unit that detects a video feature quantity such as the intensity value of the composite video signal and determines the light-emission intensity value of the light emission area; and an LED driver.
problem: Poor 3D image quality or excessive extraneous radiation in video displays due to uniform backlighting across all regions.
constraint: Balancing local dimming granularity with power efficiency and response time to avoid visible artifacts or delayed adjustments.
mechanism: Analyzing composite input signals to extract feature metrics and dynamically modulating localized light emission intensity across segmented regions to match detected content characteristics.
mechanism_raw: Detecting video feature quantities (e.g., intensity) from composite signals and dynamically adjusting LED light emission intensity per localized backlight area to match image content.

abstract: A folding vehicle structure includes a frame having a plurality of members. A first member intersects a second member at a first pivot point. A third member, spaced from the first and second members, intersects a fourth member, which is also spaced from the first and second members, at a second pivot point. The frame includes a first cross-member extending between the first and second intersection points. The frame is collapsible.
problem: Creating a vehicle structure that can be collapsed for storage or transport while maintaining structural integrity when deployed.
constraint: The structure must balance collapsibility with structural rigidity — pivot points and cross-members must allow folding while maintaining enough connection to keep the structure coherent and load-bearing in use.
mechanism: Structural members connected at pivot points allow controlled folding motion, while a linking element between pivot points preserves their geometric relationship during collapse. The linking element constrains relative movement to enable predictable folding rather than uncontrolled deformation, maintaining structural coherence in the deployed state.
mechanism_raw: Frame members pivot at intersection points, with a cross-member connecting the pivot points to maintain controlled relative movement during collapse. The cross-member preserves the geometric relationship between pivot points, enabling predictable folding rather than uncontrolled collapse.

abstract: An air gun with sucking function comprises a gun body, an air intake control set and an airflow switching and controlling element. The air gun with sucking function of the present invention employs the airflow switching and controlling element disposed inside the gun tube of the gun body for switching an airflow flowing direction and converting an airflow ejection into a sucking airflow in order to meet various work requirements by switching to different functions. When it is switched for sucking airflow for cleaning, dust can be prevented from flying around and therefore is healthier for breathing.
problem: Switching between blowing and sucking functions in a single pneumatic tool to meet different work requirements (e.g., cleaning with dust containment).
constraint: The switching mechanism must be internal to the gun tube and must effectively reverse flow direction while maintaining sufficient airflow control and pressure for both blowing and sucking modes.
mechanism: An internal flow reversal element within the delivery conduit actively redirects the flow path, converting ejection direction into suction direction. The element operates within the conduit itself rather than through external reconfiguration, enabling bidirectional flow control from a single source.
mechanism_raw: An internal airflow switching element disposed inside the gun tube reverses the airflow direction, converting ejection into suction. The switching element actively redirects the flow path within the tube rather than relying on external reconfiguration.
residual_terms: ["flow reversal", "flow direction", "airflow control", "pressure", "internal switching element", "gun tube"]

abstract: Systems and methods for extracting topographic information from inspected objects to identify defects in the inspected objects. A part to be inspected is illuminated with at least two different colors emitted from an illuminator providing a gradient of light consisting of the at least two different colors. A single color image of the illuminated part to be inspected is acquired, providing a color-coded topographic mapping of the part to be inspected due, at least in part, to the gradient of light. Topographic monochrome views of the part to be inspected may be generated from the single color image. Each view of the topographic monochrome views may enhance a different type of feature or defect present in the part to be inspected which can be analyzed and detected.
problem: Extracting topographic information from inspected objects to identify defects using a single image acquisition.
constraint: Must use a single image acquisition with color gradient illumination to encode 3D topographic information into 2D color data, trading off illumination complexity for reduced acquisition time and consistent multi-view extraction.
mechanism: Multi-spectral illumination with a gradient of at least two distinct spectral components encodes surface elevation variations into color-encoded data within a single captured image. Subsequent processing generates multiple monochrome representations from the single color image, each optimized to enhance different surface features or anomalies.
mechanism_raw: Illuminating a part with a gradient of at least two different colors encodes surface topography into color variations in a single captured image. Different monochrome views are then generated from this single color image, each enhancing a different type of feature or defect.
residual_terms: ["color gradient illumination", "topographic information", "single image acquisition", "color variations", "monochrome views", "defect identification"]

abstract: A multi-stage agitation system is used for degumming vegetable oil to increase yield and reduce phosphatides. A high-shear mixing phase, that can include multiple stages, subjects an oil mixed with acid and base to a shear rate of greater than 15,000 s−1 to form a neutralized oil mixture. A low-shear mixing phase is further used to disperse water into the neutralized oil mixture. A separation step can be used to remove the phosphatides from the treated oil to form a degummed oil product.
problem: Degumming vegetable oil to increase yield and reduce phosphatide content through efficient mixing and separation.
constraint: The shear rate must transition from high to low with specific thresholds for each phase — high shear achieves rapid chemical mixing but must be followed by low shear to avoid emulsification and enable proper water dispersion for separation.
mechanism: Sequential processing with shear rate transitioning from high to low — a high-shear phase achieves rapid mixing of the reactive components, followed by a low-shear phase that gently disperses a secondary fluid into the mixed product, then a separation step removes byproduct materials. The shear rate transition prevents emulsification while enabling proper phase dispersion.
mechanism_raw: Sequential mixing with different shear rates — a high-shear phase (>15,000 s⁻¹) for rapid neutralization of the oil-acid-base mixture, followed by a low-shear phase to gently disperse water into the neutralized mixture, then a separation step to remove phosphatides.

abstract: A cellular confinement system for soil, sand or other filler material comprises a number of sub-assemblies each made up of a plurality of interconnected open cells of fabric material. The sub-assemblies are stackable one on top of the other to provide a structure having at least one generally vertical side or end wall. Each sub-assembly comprises a skirt portion which is arranged to overlap between vertically juxtaposed sub-assemblies in use. The skirt portion substantially prevents or minimizes the escape of finer aggregate material from between the stacked sub-assemblies.
problem: Containing filler material (soil, sand, aggregate) in a stacked cellular confinement structure while preventing finer aggregate from escaping between vertically stacked units.
constraint: The skirt overlap must be sufficient to prevent material escape while still allowing the sub-assemblies to be stacked — the overlap length and flexibility must balance containment effectiveness with stackability and installation ease.
mechanism: Flexible barrier extensions on each unit overlap with extensions from vertically adjacent units, creating a continuous containment wall that traps particulate material within the stacked cellular structure. The overlap length and flexibility balance containment effectiveness with stackability requirements.
mechanism_raw: Skirt portions on each sub-assembly overlap with skirts of vertically juxtaposed sub-assemblies, creating a continuous barrier that traps finer aggregate material within the stacked structure and prevents migration between cells.
residual_terms: ["skirt portions", "sub-assemblies", "vertically stacked", "aggregate material", "cellular confinement", "overlap length", "flexibility", "containment effectiveness", "stackability"]

abstract: In various aspects, systems and methods are provided for operating a molten carbonate fuel cell, such as a fuel cell assembly, with increased production of syngas while also reducing or minimizing the amount of CO2 exiting the fuel cell in the cathode exhaust stream. This can allow for improved efficiency of syngas production while also generating electrical power.
problem: Improving syngas production efficiency in molten carbonate fuel cells while minimizing CO2 emissions in the cathode exhaust stream.
constraint: Balancing syngas production efficiency with electrical power generation, ensuring that CO2 reduction does not compromise overall energy output or cell longevity.
mechanism: Modulating operational parameters of a chemical conversion system to steer reaction equilibria toward desired product formation while retaining a target byproduct within the reaction zone, thereby coupling product optimization with emission reduction.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting the fuel cell's operational parameters (e.g., temperature, pressure, reactant composition) to optimize chemical reactions that favor syngas generation and CO2 retention within the cell, rather than allowing CO2 to exit via the cathode exhaust.

abstract: Ultrasonic transmitters that can be used for ranging in mobile devices are disclosed. In some examples, an ultrasonic transmitter device can be configured to transmit ultrasonic signals in multiple frequency bands. The transmitter can include multiple sets of ultrasonic transmitters, each capable of transmitting in a different frequency band. In other examples, frequency-adjustable ultrasonic transmitters can be used. The transmitters can be configured to change one or more of a length, mass, or tension of a membrane to change a resonant frequency of the membrane. In some examples, the transmitter can include a non-uniformly shaped membrane capable of vibrating at more than one resonant frequency. The ultrasonic transmitters can be included within a housing configured to control the flow of air within and out of the housing. The transmitter membrane can further be formed on a patterned substrate configured to increase the sound pressure levels produced by the transmitter.
problem: Enabling ultrasonic ranging in mobile devices with variable frequency requirements and controlled acoustic output.
constraint: Maintaining consistent acoustic performance across frequency adjustments while minimizing power consumption and physical footprint in compact mobile devices.
mechanism: Dynamically reconfiguring the mechanical compliance of a vibrating element to shift its natural resonance across multiple frequency bands, while a structured interface enhances acoustic output by reinforcing specific vibrational modes.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically altering the physical properties (length, mass, tension) of a membrane or using non-uniform membrane geometries to shift resonant frequencies, allowing transmission across multiple frequency bands. A patterned substrate enhances sound pressure levels by optimizing vibrational modes.

abstract: An exhaust gas treatment system for an internal combustion engine may have a reductant delivery system with a controller that performs period diagnostics to determine whether there is a blockage in the reductant delivery system. The diagnostic procedure may include sampling first and second pressures at first and second operating conditions, respectively, and then comparing the first pressure differential between the first and second pressures with one or more threshold pressure differentials to determine whether system components such as a dosing line and an injector are at least partially blocked. If such a test is not conclusive, it may be repeated at a third and fourth operating conditions to provide a second pressure differential. The offset between the first and second pressure differentials may also be used to help diagnose where a blockage in the system resides.
problem: Detecting blockages in a reductant delivery system for exhaust gas treatment in internal combustion engines.
constraint: Ensuring diagnostic accuracy without false positives, requiring sufficient pressure differential sensitivity and adaptive thresholds to account for normal operational variability.
mechanism: Sampling pressure differentials across a fluid delivery pathway under varying operational states and comparing them against adaptive thresholds to detect anomalies, with repeated measurements at additional states refining the spatial localization of the anomaly.
mechanism_raw: Sampling pressure differentials at distinct operating conditions (e.g., varying flow rates or temperatures) and comparing them to thresholds to identify deviations caused by blockages. Repeating diagnostics at additional conditions refines localization of the blockage.

abstract: Systems, apparatuses, and methods are provided for actuating one or more load management devices on a wind turbine and/or a wind turbine blade. Each actuator may exhibit one or more beneficial qualities including appropriate actuation speed/force characteristics, size and/or weight characteristics, and/or increased reliability and consistent operation in a variety of operating conditions. According to some aspects, the actuator may be a direct pneumatic actuator, a ramp slide pneumatic actuator, a scissor actuator, a linear induction actuator, a belt actuator, a closed cam follower actuator, a screw drive actuator, a solenoid actuator, a rack and pinion actuator, a cylindrical cam follower actuator, a Y-belt actuator, an offset rotary drive actuator, a tape style actuator, a rigid tape actuator, a deformable membrane actuator, a memory alloy actuator, and/or a crank slide actuator.
reason: The patent lists various actuator types (e.g., pneumatic, solenoid, memory alloy) without describing a unifying causal mechanism. The solution is a catalog of options rather than a functional principle that can be abstracted to other fields.

abstract: An image forming apparatus includes a voltage application unit, a target device, a voltage application line, and an electric-current return line. The voltage application unit applies a voltage to the target device through the voltage application line made of a conductor. The electric-current return line made of a conductor connects the target device to the voltage application unit. An electric current that flows upon application of the voltage from the voltage application unit to the target device returns to the voltage application unit through the electric-current return line. The electric-current return line has a length shorter than a path by way of the casing of the image forming apparatus.
problem: Minimizing electrical resistance and interference in current return paths for image forming apparatuses.
constraint: Balancing the physical layout of the return line to ensure minimal path length without compromising structural integrity or component accessibility in compact device designs.
mechanism: Providing a preferential conductive pathway with a shorter electrical path length relative to an alternative structural path, thereby reducing resistive losses and electromagnetic interference in current return routing.
mechanism_raw: Routing the electric-current return line through a conductor with a shorter path length compared to the alternative path via the device casing, reducing resistive losses and electromagnetic interference.

abstract: A hydrogen storage container that stores hydrogen gas using a hydrogen storage material capable of storing hydrogen gas includes: a hollow liner that stores the hydrogen gas and includes a liner opening portion into which the hydrogen gas is introduced; a hollow sub-tank disposed inside the liner to house the hydrogen storage material; a heat exchange pipe which is disposed inside the sub-tank and through which a heat exchange medium passes; a sub-tank support portion that supports an end portion of the sub-tank relative to the liner opening portion and supports an end portion of the heat exchange pipe; and a heat exchange medium passage that is formed to penetrate the sub-tank support portion and leads the heat exchange medium to the heat exchange pipe.
problem: Storing hydrogen gas efficiently while managing heat generated during absorption/desorption cycles in a confined volume.
constraint: The support structure must simultaneously bear mechanical loads from the sub-tank and heat exchange pipe while allowing a fluid passage to penetrate through it to reach the internal pipe, balancing structural integrity with thermal management in a compact nested geometry.
mechanism: Nested containment with integrated load-bearing and fluid-conducting structure: a hollow liner houses a sub-tank containing a storage medium, a thermal conduit runs through the sub-tank, and a support structure simultaneously provides mechanical support for both the sub-tank and the thermal conduit while incorporating a penetrating passage that delivers a heat exchange medium directly to the conduit inside the sub-tank.
mechanism_raw: Nested containment with integrated thermal management: a hollow liner houses a sub-tank containing hydrogen storage material, a heat exchange pipe runs through the sub-tank, and a support structure simultaneously provides mechanical support for both the sub-tank and the heat exchange pipe while incorporating a penetrating passage that delivers heat exchange medium directly to the pipe inside the sub-tank.

abstract: A semiconductor device is made by forming a first conductive layer over a substrate, forming a first passivation layer over the first conductive layer, forming a first via in the first passivation layer to expose the first conductive layer, forming a second conductive layer over the first passivation layer and within the first via to electrically connect to the first conductive layer, forming a second passivation layer over the second conductive layer, and forming a second via in the second passivation layer to expose the second conductive layer. The second via is smaller than the first via. The second via is either physically separate from or disposed over the first via. The second conductive layer within the second via has a flat surface which is wider than the second via. An under bump metallization is formed in the second via and electrically connected to the second conductive layer.
reason: The mechanism is a specific semiconductor via formation process with size-graded vias and under-bump metallization, which is a fabrication technique tied to semiconductor interconnect technology rather than a generalizable causal principle applicable across fields.

abstract: A hammock suspension device for guiding a guy rope includes a base body. The base body includes upper and lower apertures, a receptacle for inserting a retaining loop formed by the guy rope, and a guide duct for introducing the guy rope into the hammock suspension device. The upper and lower apertures are arranged in a longitudinal direction of the hammock suspension device. The upper aperture is configured to be oriented toward a fastening point of the guy rope and to connect the guide duct to enable a deflection of the guy rope in the guide duct, from approximately the longitudinal direction of the hammock suspension device to approximately a transverse direction of the hammock suspension device.
problem: Redirecting tension forces from a guy rope in a hammock suspension system from a longitudinal direction to a transverse direction while maintaining proper load transfer.
constraint: The guide duct must redirect the guy rope from longitudinal to transverse direction while maintaining structural integrity of the base body and allowing the retaining loop to be properly seated and tensioned.
mechanism: Directional force redirection via a directional channel integrated into a structural body: upper and lower apertures are arranged longitudinally, and the upper aperture connects to a directional channel that deflects a tension member from the longitudinal axis of the device to a transverse direction, with a receptacle for a retaining loop to secure the redirected member.
mechanism_raw: Directional force redirection via a guide duct integrated into a base body: upper and lower apertures are arranged longitudinally, and the upper aperture connects to a guide duct that deflects the guy rope from the longitudinal axis of the device to a transverse direction, with a receptacle for a retaining loop to secure the redirected rope.

abstract: The storage tank cleaning machine is a mobile unit mounted on a trailer for towing by a suitable vehicle. The machine is positioned adjacent the access opening of the tank, e.g., a water tank, cistern, or other storage tank, and a support on the bed of the machine is raised to vertical over the opening. A multiple segment articulating arm extends from the support and is lowered through the opening to access the interior of the tank. A motorized rotary brush extends from the distal end of the arm. Distance sensors adjacent the brush detect the interior surfaces of the tank for accurately positioning the brush. An electronic control system is provided. A tank for water and/or other cleaning fluid and a disinfectant tank are also provided. Fluids used during the cleaning operation are suctioned back to the machine, where the fluids are cleaned and recycled.
problem: Cleaning the interior surfaces of storage tanks that are difficult to access through small openings, without requiring human entry or tank disassembly.
constraint: The articulating arm must be long and flexible enough to navigate through a small opening and reach interior surfaces while maintaining sufficient rigidity for brush pressure, and the fluid recycling system must clean used fluid effectively enough to sustain continuous operation without external resupply.
mechanism: Confined-space access via articulated deployment with closed-loop fluid handling: a multi-segment articulated deployment mechanism extends from a mobile base through a tank opening to position a motorized rotary brush inside the tank, positioning sensors guide precise brush positioning against interior surfaces, and used cleaning fluid is suctioned back to the base where it is cleaned and recycled for reuse.
mechanism_raw: Confined-space access via articulated deployment with closed-loop fluid handling: a multi-segment articulating arm extends from a mobile base through a tank opening to position a motorized rotary brush inside the tank, distance sensors guide precise brush positioning against interior surfaces, and used cleaning fluid is suctioned back to the base where it is cleaned and recycled for reuse.

abstract: A pencil type application tool for applying a coating material to a substrate, having a shaft and a reservoir in the shaft filled with the coating material. A tool head having an applicator, and a valve is arranged between the reservoir and the tool head, that has a valve body and, upon actuation, switches from a closed to an open position to dispense the coating material onto the substrate. In order to reduce the consumption of application tools and also permit refilling with a coating material in a reliable and clean manner, in the longitudinal extension of the application tool between the shaft and the tool head, a carrier part is arranged which receives and secures the valve body by the main part of its longitudinal extension, in a direction facing away from the applicator, and the carrier part is detachably connectable to the shaft and the tool head.
problem: Applying coating material from a handheld tool reliably while enabling clean refilling without replacing the entire tool or contaminating the coating material.
constraint: The carrier part must securely hold the valve body in proper alignment between the reservoir and applicator while being detachable, ensuring leak-free operation during dispensing and clean access during refilling without cross-contamination.
mechanism: Modular valve isolation for refillable dispensing: an intermediate coupling is positioned between the reservoir and applicator and detachably connects to both, securing the valve assembly so that the valve can be removed and refilled or replaced independently of the reservoir and applicator, while the valve switches between closed and open positions to control dispensing.
mechanism_raw: Modular valve isolation for refillable dispensing: a carrier part is positioned between the shaft (reservoir) and tool head (applicator) and detachably connects to both, securing the valve body so that the valve assembly can be removed and refilled or replaced independently of the shaft and tool head, while the valve switches between closed and open positions to control dispensing.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for processing an aqueous gel of nanofibrillar cellulose by removing water from the aqueous gel by means of an organic solvent miscible with water. In the method: aqueous gel is introduced into a volume of organic solvent miscible with water in a controlled manner so that the aqueous gel is kept as a separate phase and forms discrete physical entities containing the nanofibrillar cellulose within the phase; water is changed with the organic solvent in said discrete physical entities of nanofibrillar cellulose; and the physical entities are separated from the volume of organic solvent.
problem: Removing water from an aqueous gel of nanofibrillar cellulose without collapsing or destroying the gel's structural integrity during solvent exchange.
constraint: The aqueous gel must be introduced in a controlled manner to maintain discrete phase entities throughout the solvent exchange, preventing dispersion or structural collapse while ensuring complete water removal.
mechanism: Introduce a structured material into a secondary medium in a controlled manner so that the material remains as discrete phase entities, allowing internal exchange of one substance for another within those confined volumes, then separate the entities from the bulk medium. The confinement to discrete volumes preserves the material's structure while enabling complete replacement of the original substance.
mechanism_raw: Controlled introduction of the aqueous gel into a volume of water-miscible organic solvent so that the gel remains as discrete physical entities in a separate phase, allowing water to be exchanged with the organic solvent within those confined entities, then separating the entities from the bulk solvent. The phase-separation approach confines the exchange to discrete volumes, preserving structure while enabling solvent replacement.

abstract: A coupler for coupling an attachment to an excavator having a latching member for retaining a rear pin of the attachment and a blocking member for retaining the front pin of the attachment. A hydraulic actuator and spring are provided for holding the latching and blocking members in their closed states. In the event of a failure of the actuator, the spring, the latching member and the blocking member together hold the front and rear pins in their respective recesses to allow continued operation of the coupler, while allowing the pins to move with respect to the coupler to create a rattling movement that can indicate to the operator that a failure has occurred.
problem: A hydraulic actuator failure in an excavator coupler could cause unintended release of the attachment, creating a safety hazard and equipment downtime.
constraint: The system must balance continued operational retention of the attachment with clear indication of failure through controlled play, ensuring the backup mechanism is strong enough to hold the pins but loose enough to generate detectable rattling.
mechanism: Dual-mode retention system where an active force holds latching and blocking members in closed positions, while a passive resilient element provides backup retention.
