The sensor's state is directly driven by the closure's angular position and physical contact engagement, converting mechanical engagement into an electrical enable signal.
mechanism_raw: A mechanical switch is coupled to the closing motion such that when the closure element reaches a specific closing angle and the carcass-side and closure-side contact elements make physical contact, the switch mechanically transitions from open to closed state, thereby enabling current flow through the contact elements. The switch state is directly driven by the physical contact and angular position of the closure, converting mechanical engagement into an electrical signal.

abstract: A heat-exchanging mat to cool livestock provides for elastic water conduction channels displaced toward an upper surface of the mat and provides for cushioning placed below those elastic channels. In this way, a high degree of cushioning may be obtained without sacrificing an efficient transfer of heat into the upper surface of the mat.
problem: Providing both efficient heat transfer to the upper surface of a mat and sufficient cushioning for livestock comfort, which are typically conflicting requirements since cushioning material can insulate against heat flow.
constraint: The cushioning thickness and compliance must be sufficient for animal comfort without adding thermal resistance between the water channels and the upper surface, balancing mechanical comfort against thermal conductance.
mechanism: A composite structure spatially separates thermal conduction and mechanical compliance functions by placing heat-conductive elements adjacent to the thermal exchange interface while positioning compliant material beneath those elements. This creates a dual-path system where thermal energy transfers through the upper conductive elements in direct contact with the exchange surface, while the lower compliant material provides cushioning without introducing thermal resistance between the conductive elements and the exchange surface.
mechanism_raw: The elastic water-conducting channels are spatially displaced toward the upper surface (the heat-exchange interface) while cushioning material is placed below those channels. This separates the thermal conduction path (upper channels in direct contact with the heat-exchange surface) from the mechanical compliance path (lower cushioning), allowing heat to transfer efficiently through the upper channels while the cushioning below provides comfort without thermally insulating the active heat-transfer region.

abstract: A novel system and method for removing contaminants in a salt cavern is provided. A purge fluid is used to purge one or more contaminants from the cavern on a continuous or intermittent basis before or during operation of the cavern. The cavern can be cycled one or more times with purging operations to create a cleaner cavern less susceptible to contaminating stored hydrogen during the operational lifetime of the cavern.
problem: Removing contaminants from a confined underground storage cavern so that a subsequently stored sensitive material (e.g., hydrogen) is not contaminated during the operational lifetime of the cavern.
constraint: The purging must be effective enough to reduce contamination to acceptable levels while minimizing operational downtime and purge fluid consumption, balancing cleanliness against resource usage and throughput.
mechanism: A contaminant removal system introduces a displacement fluid into the confined space to carry away contaminants, with the space undergoing repeated cycles of fluid introduction and evacuation. Each cycle removes a fraction of residual contaminants through displacement and entrainment, progressively reducing contaminant concentration through iterative dilution and physical transport until the environment reaches a target cleanliness level.
mechanism_raw: A purge fluid is introduced into the cavern to displace and carry away contaminants on a continuous or intermittent basis, and the cavern is cycled through multiple purge operations. Each purge cycle removes a portion of the remaining contaminants, progressively reducing the contaminant concentration so that the cavern environment is cleaner before and during storage operations.

abstract: The traction system comprises a plurality of substantially parallel tendons (2) movable for pulling a load, the tendons being disposed according to a pattern in a plane perpendicular to the tendons; and at least one deviator (3) for guiding the tendons, the deviator accommodating an angular deflection of the plurality of tendons. The deviator includes a support structure (4) and a plurality of segments (5) each having an inner surface facing a convex surface of the support structure, front and rear surfaces and a plurality of channels extending from the front surface to the rear surface. The channels are disposed according to said pattern in the front and rear surfaces of each segment, each tendon being received in a respective one of the channels. At least some of the segments (5) have their inner surfaces bearing on the convex surface of the support structure (4) in response to tensile forces applied to the tendons.
problem: Guiding a plurality of parallel tendons through an angular deflection while allowing the guidance system to adapt to varying tensile loads without losing alignment or stability.
constraint: The segments must be free to slide and adjust under tension while maintaining channel alignment with the tendons, balancing load-bearing stability against smooth movement and proper tendon guidance.
mechanism: A load-adaptive guidance system uses segmented channels with internal bearing surfaces that conform to an external support geometry when tensile forces are applied. The segments self-align under load by pressing their bearing surfaces against the support, creating a stable channel array that maintains tendon alignment while allowing load-responsive positional adjustment. The system's geometry ensures channel alignment is preserved through load-induced conformal contact.
mechanism_raw: The deviator comprises segments with channels matching the tendon pattern, each segment having an inner surface that bears on a convex support structure. When tensile forces are applied to the tendons, the resulting force causes the segments to press their inner surfaces against the convex support, making the segments self-conform to the support geometry under load. This load-responsive bearing action stabilizes the segment positions and maintains proper channel alignment for the tendons as they are deflected.

abstract: The storage device comprises a storage chamber for storing objects at e.g. −80° C., a transfer chamber for intermediate object storage at e.g. −20° C. and a transport device arranged between them. The transport device comprises a pivotal and vertically displaceable carriage and is arranged in a rotatable lock chamber.
problem: Transferring objects between a storage chamber at a very low temperature (e.g., -80°C) and a transfer chamber at a higher temperature (e.g., -20°C) while maintaining thermal isolation between the two chambers.
constraint: The lock chamber must provide sufficient thermal isolation to maintain the temperature differential between chambers while allowing the carriage to move through it efficiently, balancing thermal retention against transfer speed and mechanical complexity.
mechanism: A multi-axis transfer system uses a thermally isolated intermediate chamber positioned between two temperature zones, with a carriage capable of pivotal and linear motion within the chamber. The intermediate chamber acts as a thermal barrier that maintains temperature differential between zones, while the carriage's multi-axis mobility enables object transfer between chambers without direct thermal exposure. The system decouples thermal isolation from mechanical transfer through independent rotational and translational degrees of freedom.
mechanism_raw: A transport device with a pivotal and vertically displaceable carriage is arranged inside a rotatable lock chamber positioned between the storage and transfer chambers. The carriage can pivot and move vertically, and the lock chamber can rotate, allowing the carriage to access both chambers. The lock chamber acts as a thermal barrier that isolates the temperature zones, while the multi-axis motion of the carriage enables object transfer without exposing either chamber directly to the other's temperature environment.

abstract: Methods, systems, and apparatus, including computer programs encoded on a computer storage medium, for shaping grid currents output from parallel inverters in a power distribution system with virtual impedances. In one aspect, a method includes receiving a measurement of the current output from the inverter, processing the measurement of the current to extract a first current component having a particular frequency, obtaining a second current component based on the measurement of the current and the extracted first current component, weighing the first and second current components with respective first and second impedances to obtain respective first and second component voltages, the first impedance having a lower impedance amplitude than the second impedance, obtaining a shaped voltage based on the first and second component voltages, and outputting a control signal to the inverter, the control signal causing the inverter to output the shaped voltage to the power distribution bus.
problem: Shaping grid currents from parallel inverters to meet power distribution standards while managing impedance mismatches.
constraint: Balancing impedance amplitudes to ensure effective current shaping without overloading the system or introducing instability.
mechanism: Decomposing a measured signal into frequency-specific components, applying distinct impedance weights to each component (one lower, one higher), and synthesizing a controlled output signal from the weighted components to regulate system behavior.
mechanism_raw: Decomposing the measured current into frequency-specific components, weighting each component with distinct impedances (one lower, one higher), and synthesizing a shaped voltage from the weighted components to control inverter output.

abstract: A system for horseback riding comprising an inverse stirrup which allows a horseback rider to use the top of the rider's foot to resist upward or transverse forces so as to maintain the rider's position on the horse. The inverse stirrup is attached to the horse by a circumferential or semi-circumferential strap passing beneath the horse such as the girth strap, or directly to the saddle, such that the system resists upward displacement of the inverse stirrup.
problem: Maintaining a rider's position on a horse by resisting upward or transverse forces during movement.
constraint: Ensuring the stirrup attachment resists upward displacement while allowing natural rider movement and comfort.
mechanism: Using a mechanical element attached to a support structure that allows a user's limb to apply downward or lateral resistance against the element, counteracting displacement forces through redirected mechanical force pathways.
mechanism_raw: Using an inverse stirrup attached to the horse/saddle that allows the rider's foot to apply downward or lateral resistance against the stirrup, counteracting displacement forces through mechanical force redirection.

abstract: The furnace of the present invention includes a body of a furnace having a cylindrical shape; a steel shell which is arranged at an inside surface of the furnace; and a lining refractory which is arranged at an inside of the steel shell and includes a plurality of refractory blocks, wherein: each of the refractory blocks includes a hot-face end surface which has a hexagonal shape exposed to a middle of the furnace, and a cold-face end surface which has a hexagonal shape larger than the hot-face end surface, the cold-face end surface being arranged at an outer periphery side of the furnace; the refractory blocks are arranged such that each position of the hot-face end surface is positioned along the radial direction of the furnace at a predetermined reference position; and the refractory blocks are arrayed along the circumferential direction of an inside surface of the steel shell, thereby being stacked in a honeycomb manner.
problem: Lining a cylindrical furnace with refractory blocks that accommodate thermal expansion while maintaining structural integrity.
constraint: Matching block geometry to furnace curvature and thermal gradients to prevent cracking or misalignment during heating cycles.
mechanism: Arranging shaped refractory elements with varying geometric dimensions in a tessellated pattern, aligned to distribute thermal stress and permit controlled expansion during temperature cycles.
mechanism_raw: Arranging hexagonal refractory blocks with varying hot-face and cold-face sizes in a honeycomb pattern, aligned radially and circumferentially to distribute thermal stress and allow controlled expansion.

abstract: A multi-pin hinge includes a first mounting pin, a second mounting pin, a linkage pin assembly, a first single-pin gear, a second single-pin gear and a double-pin gear assembly. The first single-pin gear is sleeved on the first mounting pin, the second single-pin gear is sleeved on the second mounting pin, and the linkage pin assembly is movably connected between the first mounting pin and the second mounting pin by the double-pin gear assembly. The multi-pin hinge connect two bodies of an electronic device to two mounting pins, thus a first body is rotatable around a second body without directly contacting the second body, thereby avoiding providing a gap or a protruding block on the two bodies. An electronic device using the multi-pin hinge can avoid providing a protruding block and/or a groove, thus the electronic device has a regular appearance and structure.
problem: Connecting two bodies of an electronic device with rotational movement while avoiding physical contact, gaps, or protrusions.
constraint: Maintaining precise gear alignment and pin spacing to ensure smooth rotation while preserving aesthetic and structural continuity.
mechanism: Mediating rotational movement between two connected bodies using a mechanical linkage system with interlocking elements that maintain alignment and spacing without direct surface contact between the bodies.
mechanism_raw: Using a multi-pin hinge with gears and linkage pins to mediate rotation between two mounting pins, enabling movement without direct contact between the connected bodies.

abstract: The present provides a secondary power system and a power supply device. The secondary power system is used for supplying power for a load equipment, and comprises: a fuse circuit, a filter circuit, a convertor circuit and an over-voltage and under-voltage protection circuit, wherein, the fuse circuit, the filter circuit, the over-voltage and under-voltage protection circuit and the convertor circuit are sequentially connected in series; the over-voltage and under-voltage protection circuit is configured to cut off power supplied to the convertor circuit when power supplied by the primary power source is an under-voltage or over-voltage; the convertor circuit is configured to convert the primary power source into a secondary power source. The secondary power system, by providing an over-voltage and under-voltage protection circuit, can not only lower the cost of the convertor circuit, but also save the space occupied by the convertor circuit.
problem: Protecting a converter circuit from over-voltage or under-voltage conditions in a secondary power system while minimizing cost and space.
constraint: Sequencing protection components to isolate faults without disrupting upstream power sources or downstream loads.
mechanism: Sequencing protective components in series, where a threshold-responsive control circuit actively interrupts power flow to a downstream load when voltage levels exceed predefined limits, isolating faults without disrupting upstream sources.
mechanism_raw: Placing a fuse, filter, over/under-voltage protection circuit, and converter in series, where the protection circuit actively cuts power to the converter when voltage thresholds are exceeded.

abstract: Systems and methods are disclosed herein for dressing centering a bearing compartment in a gas turbine engine. A nut may be inserted through an outer case of a gas turbine engine. The nut may be coupled to a strut which centers a bearing compartment. The nut may be rotated to achieve a desired tension on the strut to center the bearing compartment. A retaining plate comprising a collar may be positioned over the nut. A swaging tool comprising a swaging ramp may be positioned over the nut. The swaging tool may be forced against the retaining plate using a draw-in bolt. The swaging ramp may contact the collar and form indentations in the collar to lock the nut in place.
problem: Achieving precise centering of a bearing compartment in a gas turbine engine while maintaining structural integrity under operational stress.
constraint: Balancing the need for precise tension adjustment with the requirement for a permanent, vibration-resistant lock that does not compromise the structural alignment of the bearing compartment.
mechanism: Apply controlled tension via an adjustable element to center a component, then mechanically deform a locking element to permanently secure the position against vibration or thermal cycling.
mechanism_raw: A tension-adjustable nut is rotated to apply controlled force to a strut, centering the bearing compartment. A swaging tool then mechanically deforms a collar on a retaining plate to lock the nut in place, preventing loosening due to vibration or thermal cycling.

abstract: One object is to provide a fishing spinning reel which ensures the concentricity of the spool shaft with respect to the pinion gear and enables the spool shaft to be smoothly and accurately reciprocated back and forth without rattling during rotational operation of the handle. The fishing spinning reel includes a support member supporting the front end of the spool shaft and having a concentric fitting portion for achieving concentricity with respect to the pinion gear. The spool shaft is supported at two points, one at the support member positioned in front of a front end of the pinion gear, and the other is a slide member of an oscillation device, whereby an outer circumferential surface of the spool shaft does not contact the inner circumferential surface of the pinion gear and the gap is maintained.
problem: Maintaining concentric alignment between a rotating spool shaft and a pinion gear in a fishing reel to prevent rattling and ensure smooth reciprocation.
constraint: Achieving precise concentricity while allowing axial movement of the spool shaft for line retrieval, without introducing friction or wear from contact between the shaft and gear.
mechanism: Use dual-point support with a front and rear member to maintain concentric alignment between a rotating shaft and a gear without physical contact, ensuring a consistent gap.
mechanism_raw: The spool shaft is supported at two points: a front support member with a concentric fitting and a rear slide member. This dual-point support ensures the shaft remains aligned with the pinion gear without physical contact, maintaining a consistent gap.

abstract: A method for the treatment of waste by plasma treating the waste to destroy the hazardous organic components and to yield a slag and an off-gas by plasma treating the waste in the presence of added oxygen gas in a transferred-arc plasma treatment unit, followed by directing off-gas from the plasma treatment unit to a thermal oxidizer combustion chamber.
problem: Safely destroying hazardous organic components in waste while managing byproducts like off-gas and slag.
constraint: Ensuring complete destruction of hazardous compounds while managing energy efficiency and preventing release of untreated byproducts into the environment.
mechanism: Decompose hazardous materials using a high-energy process, then direct byproducts to a secondary treatment chamber for further destruction of residual contaminants.
mechanism_raw: Plasma treatment in a transferred-arc unit breaks down hazardous organics into inert slag and off-gas. The off-gas is then directed to a thermal oxidizer combustion chamber for further destruction of residual contaminants.

abstract: A ratchet wrench includes a head which has a through hole, a first recess, a second recess and a closed portion. A ratchet member is located in the through hole and is engaged with a pawl in the first recess. The control unit is located in the second recess and has a control member, an engaging member and a resilient member. The control member has a cylindrical rod with a slot and a notch. The engaging member is located in the slot and has a receiving recess, two contact areas and a recessed section. The resilient member is located in the notch and the receiving recess. The engaging member is restricted by the closed portion and biased by engaging member which restricts the cylindrical rod so that the control member is rotatably located in the second recess to push the engaging member to move the pawl.
problem: Controlling the engagement and disengagement of a ratchet pawl in a wrench to enable smooth directional operation.
constraint: Maintaining precise mechanical control over the pawl's movement while ensuring the system remains compact and resistant to wear under repeated use.
mechanism: A rotating control member with a slot and notch interacts with a resiliently biased engaging member to selectively move a pawl for directional operation.
mechanism_raw: A control member with a cylindrical rod, slot, and notch interacts with an engaging member biased by a resilient member. The control member's rotation pushes the engaging member to move the pawl, enabling selective ratcheting action.

abstract: A compacting auger for ground coffee has an automatic cut off that responds to either timing signals or to the torque resistance to the augur offered by the coffee that has been compacted. The automation of the cut off increases the consistency of compaction and reduces the amount of skill required to compact ground coffee for making espresso.
problem: Achieving consistent compaction of ground coffee for espresso preparation with minimal operator skill.
constraint: Balancing the need for consistent compaction with the requirement to adapt to varying coffee properties (e.g., grind size, volume) without overcompacting or undercompacting.
mechanism: Automatically halt compaction by a rotating screw based on either a timed signal or detected torque resistance to ensure uniform density without manual intervention.
mechanism_raw: An auger's compaction is automatically halted based on either a timed signal or detected torque resistance from the coffee, ensuring uniform density without manual intervention.

abstract: This invention provides novel compositions and processes for analyte detection, quantification and amplification. Nucleic acid arrays and libraries of analytes are usefully incorporated into such compositions and processes. Universal detection elements, signaling entities and the like are employed to detect and if necessary or desirable, to quantify analytes. Amplification of target analytes are also provided by the compositions and processes of this invention.
problem: Detecting and quantifying specific analytes in a sample with high sensitivity and specificity, including signal amplification for low-concentration targets.
constraint: Balancing specificity (correct analyte identification among many) with sensitivity (detection of low concentrations) while using a universal system applicable to many different analyte types.
mechanism: Using universal detection elements and signaling entities that can be paired with specific binding agents to produce detectable and amplifiable signals from target analytes. The universal elements provide the detection/amplification capability while the specific binding agents provide selectivity for the target analyte.
mechanism_raw: Using universal detection elements and signaling entities that can be paired with specific binding agents (nucleic acid arrays/libraries) to produce detectable and amplifiable signals from target analytes. The universal elements provide the detection/amplification capability while the specific binding agents provide selectivity for the target analyte.

abstract: An adjustable stock assembly includes a housing, a stock rail, a release, a key movable with respect to the release, a latch rotatable about a latch pivot between a latched position, an unlatched position and a disassembly position, and a latch cam pin coupled to the release. The housing is extendable and retractable with respect to the stock rail. The stock rail has a slot and one or more recesses adjacent to the slot that can engage the latch, thereby preventing disassembly of the rail from the housing and further securing the rail in a particular configuration. When partially depressed along with the key, the release disengages the latch from the stock rail recesses, allowing the housing to extend and retract within its adjustment range. The housing can be disassembled from the stock rail when the key and release are fully depressed.
problem: Creating an adjustable mechanical connection that can be locked in position, adjusted, and disassembled as needed, while preventing accidental disassembly during normal use.
constraint: Balancing security (preventing accidental disassembly during normal operation) with accessibility (allowing intentional disassembly and smooth adjustment) through a single control interface.
mechanism: A multi-state latch system controlled by graduated actuation of a release and key mechanism. Partial depression of both the release and key disengages the latch from the rail recesses, allowing extension/retraction. Full depression of both allows complete disassembly. The latch rotates between latched, unlatched, and disassembly positions based on the degree of actuation.
mechanism_raw: A multi-state latch system controlled by graduated actuation of a release and key mechanism. Partial depression of both the release and key disengages the latch from the rail recesses, allowing extension/retraction. Full depression of both allows complete disassembly. The latch rotates between latched, unlatched, and disassembly positions based on the degree of actuation.

abstract: A method for manufacturing a semiconductor device includes forming a fin structure having a top surface and side surfaces. A mask layer is disposed over the top surface. A doping support layer is formed to cover part of the fin structure. A first impurity is introduced into a first region of the fin structure covered by the doping support layer, by implanting the first impurity into the doping support layer so that the implanted first impurity is introduced into the first region of the fin structure through the side surfaces.
problem: Introducing impurities into specific regions of 3D fin structures where direct top-down implantation cannot reach the desired areas, particularly through side surfaces.
constraint: Achieving precise doping of specific regions in 3D structures while avoiding contamination of other areas and maintaining process control over the implantation and diffusion steps.
mechanism: Using a doping support layer as an intermediate delivery medium. Impurities are implanted into the doping support layer, which then serves as a source for diffusion through the side surfaces of the fin structure into the target region. A mask layer on the top surface prevents unwanted implantation from above, ensuring doping occurs only through the side surfaces.
mechanism_raw: Using a doping support layer as an intermediate delivery medium. Impurities are implanted into the doping support layer, which then serves as a source for diffusion through the side surfaces of the fin structure into the target region. A mask layer on the top surface prevents unwanted implantation from above, ensuring doping occurs only through the side surfaces.

abstract: A brace (200) for geometrically interlocking stringer pairs A of first stringers (106), coupled to a first panel (102), and stringer pairs B of second stringers (108), coupled to a second panel (104), of a structure (100). The brace (200) comprises a chassis (202) comprising first interlocks (204) and second interlocks (206) opposite the first interlocks (204). The first interlocks (204) geometrically engage with one of the stringer pairs A of the first stringers (106) and the second interlocks (206) geometrically engage with one of the stringer pairs B of the second stringers (108) to constrain the brace (200) in all directions along a plane (112) perpendicular to the first stringers (106) and the second stringers (108).
problem: Constraining relative motion between two panels in all directions within a plane while mechanically connecting them with a brace structure.
constraint: Constraining motion in all directions within a plane while allowing the brace to connect two separate panels that may have different stringer configurations and orientations.
mechanism: Using a chassis with opposing geometric interlocks that engage with complementary structures on two separate panels. The geometric complementarity on both sides of the chassis creates multi-directional constraint, preventing movement in all directions along the plane perpendicular to the stringers.
mechanism_raw: Using a chassis with opposing geometric interlocks (first and second) that engage with complementary structures (stringer pairs) on two separate panels. The geometric complementarity on both sides of the chassis creates multi-directional constraint, preventing movement in all directions along the plane perpendicular to the stringers.

abstract: To provide an exhaust purifying system and a method for controlling the exhaust purifying system that avoid occurrence of clogging, breakage, or the like of a reducing agent injection valve caused by the solidification of a reducing agent and prevent reduction in the efficiency of reducing agent recovery processing and exhaust gas purification.An exhaust purifying system and a method for controlling the exhaust purifying system according to an aspect of the present invention is configured to detect the injection valve temperature of the reducing agent injection valve according to detection of turn-off of an ignition switch for stopping the internal combustion engine or detection of an injection stop of the reducing agent injection valve, whichever is earlier, calculate the waiting time until reducing agent recovery processing starts based on the injection valve temperature, and permits the reducing agent recovery processing under condition of the detection of turn-off of the ignition switch and an elapse of the waiting time.
problem: Preventing clogging, breakage, or solidification of reducing agent injection valves in exhaust aftertreatment systems while maintaining exhaust gas purification efficiency.
constraint: Balancing the need for timely recovery action (to prevent solidification at low temperatures) with not disrupting normal engine operation, while accounting for varying thermal conditions that affect the required delay duration.
mechanism: A temperature-dependent delayed action system that detects the injection valve temperature upon engine shutdown or injection stop, calculates a waiting time based on that temperature, and only initiates reducing agent recovery processing when both a shutdown trigger condition and the calculated thermal-dependent delay have been satisfied.
mechanism_raw: A temperature-dependent delayed action system that detects the injection valve temperature upon engine shutdown or injection stop, calculates a waiting time based on that temperature, and only initiates reducing agent recovery processing when both a shutdown trigger condition and the calculated thermal-dependent delay have been satisfied.

abstract: A heat treatment apparatus includes: a reaction tube processing a plurality of substrates; a support member supporting the reaction tube; a flange protruding outwardly from a lower end of the reaction tube: a concave portion formed in an outer periphery of the flange; and a rotatable roller installed in a top surface of the support member. The rotatable roller engages the concave portion and positions the reaction tube in a circumferential direction.
problem: Positioning a reaction tube in a circumferential direction within a heat treatment apparatus while accommodating thermal expansion and rotational movement.
constraint: The positioning mechanism must maintain accurate circumferential alignment while accommodating thermal expansion of the reaction tube and allowing the roller to rotate freely without introducing positional play or binding.
mechanism: A rolling element engages a curved recess on a protruding feature of a thermally expanding component. The geometric constraint of the rolling element within the curved recess provides self-aligning positioning in a rotational direction, while the rolling element's rotation allows the component to be positioned without binding or positional play. The mechanical interface between the curved surface and the rolling element automatically centers and constrains the component's angular position during thermal expansion.
mechanism_raw: A rotatable roller engages a concave portion formed on a flange protruding from the reaction tube. The geometric constraint of the roller within the curved concave recess provides self-aligning positioning in the circumferential direction, while the roller's rotation allows the tube to be positioned without binding. The mechanical interface between the curved surface and the rolling element automatically centers and constrains the tube's angular position.

abstract: An electrosurgical instrument for making an end-to-end anastomosis between two hollow organ sections includes two tools movable relative to each other and each including an HF electrode by which the hollow organ sections can be fusion-welded to each other. The two tools are substantially sleeve-shaped or can at least be brought into sleeve shape so that a first tool can enclose a first hollow organ section and a second tool can enclose a second hollow organ section. Each of the electrodes is formed on an end face of each sleeve-shaped tool around which the respective hollow organ section can be everted inside out, and the two tools are movable relative to each other so that the electrodes are aligned and can clamp the everted hollow organ sections therebetween.
problem: Creating a reliable, leak-proof end-to-end anastomosis between two hollow organ sections by joining their inner luminal surfaces.
constraint: The eversion must be controlled to avoid tissue damage while ensuring precise alignment of the everted inner surfaces between the electrodes, and the welding energy must be sufficient to create a leak-proof bond without causing thermal injury to surrounding tissue.
mechanism: Enclosure tools each surround and evert a hollow organ section inside out, mechanically transforming the organ's inner surface into an accessible outer surface. The two tools are then moved relative to each other to align their end-face electrodes, which clamp the everted organ sections between them. Energy is applied through the electrodes to fusion-weld the previously internal surfaces together, creating a continuous lumen.
mechanism_raw: Sleeve-shaped tools each enclose and evert a hollow organ section inside out, mechanically transforming the organ's inner surface into an accessible outer surface. The two tools are then moved relative to each other to align their end-face electrodes, which clamp the everted organ sections between them. High-frequency energy is applied through the electrodes to fusion-weld the previously internal surfaces together, creating a continuous lumen.

abstract: A tubular flow control apparatus includes, a first screen surrounding a first tubular defining a first annular space therebetween, a second screen surrounding a second tubular defining a second annular space therebetween, and a third tubular positioned longitudinally between the first tubular and the second tubular having at least one passageway fluidically connecting the first annular space with the second annular space, the third tubular having at least one opening fluidically connecting the at least one passageway to a third space located radially outwardly of the third tubular.
problem: Controlling fluid flow between multiple radial zones in a tubular system, such as in downhole well completions, while maintaining structural integrity and selective zone communication.
constraint: The flow control system must balance desired flow rates and zone isolation with structural integrity of the concentric tubular assembly, while preventing unwanted ingress (e.g., sand or particulates) through the screens and openings.
mechanism: Concentric tubulars with surrounding screens create multiple annular spaces at different radial positions. A third tubular positioned between the first and second tubulars contains passageways that fluidically connect the first and second annular spaces. Openings in the third tubular connect these passageways to a third space located radially outward, enabling controlled fluid communication between different radial zones through the interconnected annular pathways.
mechanism_raw: Concentric tubulars with surrounding screens create multiple annular spaces at different radial positions. A third tubular positioned between the first and second tubulars contains passageways that fluidically connect the first and second annular spaces. Openings in the third tubular connect these passageways to a third space located radially outward, enabling controlled fluid communication between different radial zones through the interconnected annular pathways.

abstract: The invention relates to a method for controlling a temperature distribution in a heat exchanger, in which an actual temperature distribution in the heat exchanger is measured by means of at least one optical waveguide arranged in the heat exchanger, in particular in the form of a glass fiber, light being launched into the optical waveguide and light that is scattered in the optical waveguide being evaluated for determining the actual temperature distribution, and at least one flow of a fluid medium that is carried in the heat exchanger being controlled in such a way that the actual temperature distribution is made to approximate a pre-defined target temperature distribution. The invention also relates to a device for carrying out a method for controlling a temperature distribution in a heat exchanger.
problem: Controlling the spatial temperature distribution in a heat exchanger to match a predefined target temperature profile.
constraint: The optical sensing must provide sufficient spatial resolution and measurement accuracy, while the fluid flow control must respond quickly enough to compensate for thermal inertia and maintain the target temperature distribution despite disturbances.
mechanism: A distributed sensor is arranged throughout the heat exchanger. A measurable property is transmitted along the sensor and evaluated at multiple points, creating a spatially-resolved map of the heat exchanger's condition. This actual condition is compared to a predefined target, and at least one fluid flow is actively controlled via feedback to drive the actual condition toward the target.
mechanism_raw: An optical waveguide (glass fiber) is arranged throughout the heat exchanger. Light is launched into the waveguide and the temperature-dependent scattered light is evaluated at multiple points along the fiber, creating a distributed, spatially-resolved temperature map of the heat exchanger. This actual temperature distribution is compared to a predefined target distribution, and at least one fluid flow is actively controlled via feedback to drive the actual distribution toward the target.

abstract: A free floating wave energy converter includes a flexible pine and an inlet. The flexible pipe floats on water surface, following the wave form. Slugs of water and air enter, one after the other, through the inlet. Because the flexible pipe follows the shape of the wave, water is transported through a manifold to a pressure chamber connected to a generator. The inlet consists of hollow, inflexible pipe attached to the throat of the flexible pipe. The inflexible pipe is fixedly attached to a buoyancy tank or plurality thereof. The buoyancy tanks are arranged in a vertical plane or in tandem, with the inflexible pipe passing along the plane vertical to the fore and aft axis of the buoyancy tank and the frontward portion projecting sufficiently ahead of the buoyancy tank with the flexible pipe terminating at a singular outlet.
problem: Converting irregular wave energy from a water surface into useful electrical energy using a free-floating energy harvester.
constraint: The flexible pipe must be compliant enough to follow wave contours without breaking, while maintaining sufficient structural integrity to transport fluid slugs, and the system must efficiently convert the irregular, bidirectional wave motion into unidirectional pressure fluctuations suitable for power generation.
mechanism: A flexible conduit floats on the water surface and passively follows the contour of passing waves. As wave motion causes the flexible conduit to change shape, alternating slugs of fluid are drawn through the conduit from an inlet. The flexible conduit's wave-following motion transports these fluid slugs through a manifold to a pressure chamber, where the resulting pressure fluctuations drive a generator to produce electricity.
mechanism_raw: A flexible pipe floats on the water surface and passively follows the contour of passing waves. As wave motion causes the flexible pipe to change shape, alternating slugs of water and air are drawn through the pipe from an inlet. The flexible pipe's wave-following motion transports these fluid slugs through a manifold to a pressure chamber, where the resulting pressure fluctuations drive a generator to produce electricity.

abstract: A system, method, and computer program product are provided for combining low motion blur and variable refresh rate in a display. In one embodiment, a hold-type display is operated in a first mode of operation where the hold-type display is dynamically refreshed such that the hold type display handles updates to image frames at unpredictable times and where for each of the image frames a backlight of the hold-type display is activated for an entire duration of display of the image frame. Additionally, it is determined that at least one predefined condition has been met. Further, in response to the determination, the hold-type display is operated in a second mode of operation where the hold-type display is statically refreshed such that the hold-type display handles updates to image frames at regular intervals and where for each of the image frames the backlight of the hold-type display is flashed.
problem: Combining low motion blur and variable refresh rate in a display, which are typically conflicting requirements since variable refresh rate handles unpredictable frame updates while low motion blur requires controlled backlight flashing at regular intervals.
constraint: The fundamental tradeoff between handling unpredictable frame timing (variable refresh rate) and achieving low motion blur (which requires flashed backlight at regular intervals). Both cannot be simultaneously satisfied, so the system must switch modes based on conditions, accepting that only one optimization applies at any given time.
mechanism: Dynamically selecting between two operational modes based on detected conditions: a first mode that adapts timing to accommodate unpredictable input events while maintaining continuous output activation, and a second mode that operates at fixed intervals with pulsed output activation for optimized temporal response. The selection mechanism evaluates current input characteristics and switches modes to apply the appropriate technique, accepting that only one optimization is active at any given time.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically switching between two operational modes based on predefined conditions: a first mode using dynamic refresh with continuous backlight activation for handling unpredictable frame updates, and a second mode using static refresh with flashed backlight for regular interval updates. The mode selection is triggered by condition detection, allowing both features to coexist by applying the appropriate technique depending on the current display state.

abstract: Methods for preparing parcels for final sorting. The methods include dividing a mass flow of parcels into individual streams, separating and singulating the parcels in each stream, delivering each stream at a steady rate to a human operator that faces and culls the parcels, reading identifying indicia on the parcels, delivering the scanned parcels to a presorter in parallel lanes, and selectively discharging parcels from the lane closest to a side of the presorter off the side at multiple discharge points.
problem: Efficiently processing high-volume parcel flow from a mass stream for final sorting, where parcels arrive in bulk and need to be individually processed, identified, and routed to appropriate destinations.
constraint: Balancing throughput with accuracy: human operators require a steady, manageable rate of parcels to maintain culling accuracy, while the system must handle high overall volume through parallel processing. The selective discharge from the side-closest lane introduces a routing constraint that must be managed across multiple lanes simultaneously.
mechanism: Partitioning a bulk material flow into multiple parallel streams, individually separating items within each stream, and delivering each stream at a regulated rate to processing stations. Processed items are then distributed across parallel routing channels where selective diversion occurs based on positional proximity to discharge points, enabling high-throughput handling through parallel processing architecture.
mechanism_raw: Dividing a mass flow of parcels into individual parallel streams, singulating parcels within each stream, delivering each stream at a steady rate to human operators who face and cull parcels, then routing scanned parcels into parallel lanes of a presorter where selective discharge occurs from the lane closest to a side at multiple discharge points. The parallel lane architecture with position-based selective discharge enables high-throughput routing.

abstract: According to one example there is provided an accessory for a printing system. The accessory comprises a cylindrical core on which a web of media may be wound, and a flexible sheet having a first end attached to the core and a second free end opposite the first end having a media connector attached thereto, the media connector to connect a free end of a web of media thereto.
problem: Managing media webs in a printing system, particularly handling the free end of a web during winding or unwinding operations where the web end needs to be connected, guided, and maintained under tension.
constraint: The flexible sheet must accommodate the winding/unwinding motion and changing web diameter while maintaining a reliable mechanical connection through the connector. The flexibility of the sheet introduces a compliance that must be balanced against the need for precise web tension control during printing operations.
mechanism: A compliant linkage system connecting a rotating core to a flexible medium, where a flexible element is attached at one end to the core and extends to a connector that mechanically couples to the medium's free end. As the core rotates to accumulate or dispense the medium, the flexible element accommodates changing geometry through flexure while maintaining continuous mechanical connection, enabling controlled tension management during dynamic operations.
mechanism_raw: A flexible sheet attached at one end to a cylindrical core and extending to a free end with a media connector, where the connector mechanically links to the free end of a media web. As the core rotates to wind or unwind the web, the flexible sheet flexes to accommodate the changing geometry while the connector maintains the mechanical link between the web and the core, enabling controlled web handling.

abstract: The invention relates to a method of separating and recovering xylose from a xylose-containing plant-based solution. The method is performed in a chromatographic separation system, which comprises one or more weak base anion exchange resins and optionally one or more other resins selected from strong acid cation exchange resins and weak acid cation exchange resins, by passing the solution through the separation system, followed by recovering at least one fraction enriched in xylose. Optionally, a rhamnose fraction may also be recovered.
problem: Separating and recovering specific sugars (xylose) from complex plant-based solutions containing multiple components with similar chemical properties, where conventional separation methods lack sufficient selectivity.
constraint: The selectivity of the resins determines separation efficiency: weak base anion exchange resins must have the right binding affinity to distinguish xylose from other components, while the optional additional resins must complement rather than interfere with the primary separation. The resin selection and elution conditions must be balanced to achieve high purity and recovery of the target sugars.
mechanism: Passing a multi-component solution through a chromatographic separation medium containing selectively interactive materials that bind different components based on their chemical affinity characteristics. The differential binding allows sequential elution of fractions enriched in target components by controlling the elution conditions, with optional complementary materials enhancing separation selectivity.
mechanism_raw: Passing a xylose-containing solution through a chromatographic separation system containing weak base anion exchange resins (optionally combined with strong acid cation exchange or weak acid cation exchange resins) that selectively bind different components based on their chemical properties. The differential binding affinity allows recovery of at least one fraction enriched in xylose, and optionally a rhamnose fraction, by controlling the elution conditions.
residual_terms: ["chromatographic separation", "anion exchange resins", "cation exchange resins", "binding affinity", "elution conditions", "xylose", "rhamnose"]

abstract: A gravity-type pore pressure dynamic penetration device for exploration of shallow-layer seabed soil includes a third drop hammer, a second drop hammer, a first drop hammer, a stable empennage, and a probe rod which are sequentially arranged from top to bottom. A sidewall friction sleeve is arranged outside a probe rod lower cylinder. A friction sleeve sensor is provided on an inner sidewall of the sidewall friction sleeve. A first pore water pressure sensor, a conical tip pressure sensor, a temperature compensation sensor, and an inclinometer sensor are provided in the middle of the probe rod lower cylinder. A second pore water pressure sensor and an acceleration sensor are provided in the middle of a probe rod upper cylinder. The tail portion of the probe rod, that is, the upper portion of the probe rod upper cylinder is connected to the stable empennage.
problem: Characterizing shallow-layer seabed soil properties in situ, where multiple soil parameters (pore pressure, tip resistance, temperature, inclination, acceleration) need to be measured simultaneously during dynamic penetration to understand soil behavior under impact loading.
constraint: Multiple sensors must be positioned at specific locations along the probe rod to capture different measurements while maintaining structural integrity during high-impact penetration. The stable empennage must prevent misalignment during impact, and the sensor placement must balance the need for spatial resolution with the mechanical constraints of the probe rod design.
mechanism: Using a gravity-driven impact system with a probe containing multiple sensors distributed at different axial positions along its length. The sensors measure various physical parameters simultaneously during dynamic penetration, with a stabilizing element preventing misalignment during impact. The sequential arrangement of impact events and distributed sensor placement enables multi-parameter characterization of material response under dynamic loading conditions.
mechanism_raw: Using a gravity-driven drop hammer system with a probe rod containing multiple sensors positioned at different axial locations along the rod: pore water pressure sensors, a conical tip pressure sensor, a temperature compensation sensor, an inclinometer, and an acceleration sensor. The sequential arrangement of drop hammers and the stable empennage ensure controlled impact while the distributed sensors capture multi-parameter soil response data during penetration.
residual_terms: ["drop hammer", "probe rod", "pore water pressure sensors", "conical tip pressure sensor", "temperature compensation sensor", "inclinometer", "acceleration sensor", "empennage", "impact loading"]

abstract: A method for determining along relatively uniformly spaced apart parallel first and second wellbores situated in an underground hydrocarbon-containing formation, regions within the formation, including in particular regions between such wellbores, to inject a fluid at a pressure above formation dilation pressure, to stimulate production of oil into the second of the two wellbores, and subsequently injecting fluid at pressures above formation dilation pressures at the discrete regions along such wellbores determined to be in need. An initial information-gathering procedure is conducted, wherein fluid is supplied under a pressure less than formation dilation or fracture pressure, to discrete intervals along a first wellbore, and sensors in the second wellbore measure and data is recorded regarding the ease of penetration of such fluid into the various regions of the formation intermediate the two wellbores. Regions of the formation exhibiting poor ease of fluid penetration are thereafter selected for subsequent dilation, at pressures above formation dilation pressures. Where initial fluid pressures and/or formation dilation pressures are provided in cyclic pulses, a downhole tool is disclosed for such purpose.
problem: Optimizing fluid injection in subsurface formations to stimulate hydrocarbon production while minimizing unnecessary high-pressure treatment.
constraint: Balancing the need for accurate diagnostic data (low-pressure phase) with the efficiency of subsequent high-pressure treatment to avoid over-stimulation or wasted energy.
mechanism: A two-phase diagnostic-then-treatment approach: first, low-pressure fluid injection identifies regions with poor natural permeability by measuring ease of penetration, then targeted high-pressure injection is applied only to those regions requiring stimulation.
mechanism_raw: A two-phase diagnostic-then-treatment approach: first, low-pressure fluid injection identifies regions with poor natural permeability by measuring ease of penetration, then targeted high-pressure injection is applied only to those regions requiring stimulation.

abstract: Provided is a refrigerator including a cabinet having a storage compartment provided therein, a main door pivotably mounted at the cabinet for opening and closing the storage compartment, an auxiliary storage compartment mounted at a rear of the main door, and an auxiliary door pivotably mounted over a front of the main door for opening and closing the auxiliary storage compartment. A first hinge bracket may be fixed to an upper end of the cabinet, the first hinge bracket including a rotation shaft that is coupled to an upper portion of the main door. A second hinge bracket may be fixed to an upper portion of the sub door, the second hinge bracket including a rotation shaft that is coupled to the upper portion of the main door. The rotation shaft of the second hinge bracket may be positioned more forward than the rotation shaft of the first hinge bracket.
problem: Enabling independent opening/closing of two overlapping doors in a confined space without mechanical interference.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and smooth operation while accommodating spatial overlap between the two doors.
mechanism: Offset hinge axes: the auxiliary door's rotation shaft is positioned forward of the main door's shaft, allowing sequential or independent movement by decoupling their rotational paths.
mechanism_raw: Offset hinge axes: the auxiliary door's rotation shaft is positioned forward of the main door's shaft, allowing sequential or independent movement by decoupling their rotational paths.

abstract: A method for converting heat to electric energy is described which involves thermally cycling an electrically polarizable material sandwiched between electrodes. The material is heated by extracting thermal energy from a gas to condense the gas into a liquid and transferring the thermal energy to the electrically polarizable material. An apparatus is also described which includes an electrically polarizable material sandwiched between electrodes and a heat exchanger for heating the material in thermal communication with a heat source, wherein the heat source is a condenser. An apparatus is also described which comprises a chamber, one or more conduits inside the chamber for conveying a cooling fluid and an electrically polarizable material sandwiched between electrodes on an outer surface of the conduit. A gas introduced into the chamber condenses on the conduits and thermal energy is thereby transferred from the gas to the electrically polarizable material.
problem: Efficiently converting low-grade thermal energy (e.g., from gas condensation) into electrical energy.
constraint: Ensuring effective thermal communication between the phase-change heat source and the polarizable material while maintaining cyclic stability.
mechanism: Thermal cycling of a polarizable material sandwiched between electrodes, where heat from a condenser (gas-to-liquid phase change) drives cyclic polarization changes to generate electricity.
mechanism_raw: Thermal cycling of a polarizable material sandwiched between electrodes, where heat from a condenser (gas-to-liquid phase change) drives cyclic polarization changes to generate electricity.

abstract: A thin film composite membrane (TFC) includes an active layer on a support. The active layer includes at least 8 barrier layers of star-polymers each having at least three linear polymers attached at a central core. Each of the barrier layers has a thickness between 5 and 50 nm, and the barrier layers have alternating charge.
problem: Creating a selective barrier membrane with precise control over permeability for separation processes.
constraint: Balancing layer thickness and charge density to achieve desired permeability while maintaining structural integrity of the composite membrane.
mechanism: Alternating charged barrier layers of star-polymers (each with ≥3 linear polymers at a core) create a multi-layered structure where charge alternation and nanoscale thickness (5–50 nm) govern selective transport.
mechanism_raw: Alternating charged barrier layers of star-polymers (each with ≥3 linear polymers at a core) create a multi-layered structure where charge alternation and nanoscale thickness (5–50 nm) govern selective transport.

abstract: The invention provides a chemical compound comprising a chemical moiety (p) capable of performing a binding interaction with a target molecule, and an oligonucleotide (b) or functional analogue thereof. The oligonucleotide (b) or functional analogue comprises at least one self-assembly sequence (b1) capable of performing a combination reaction with at least one self-assembly sequence (b1′) of a complementary oligonucleotide or functional analogue bound to another chemical compound comprising a chemical moiety (q). In some embodiments, the chemical compound comprises a coding sequence (b1) coding for the identification of the chemical moiety (p) and further comprises at least one self-assembly moiety (m) capable of performing a combination reaction with at least one self-assembly moiety (m′) of a similar chemical compound comprising a chemical moiety (q). The invention also provides corresponding libraries of chemical compounds as well as methods of biopanning of for target molecules and of identifying such targets.
problem: Enabling programmable self-assembly and combinatorial reactions between distinct molecular components for targeted delivery or identification.
constraint: Ensuring specificity of self-assembly interactions to avoid unintended cross-reactions while enabling scalable combinatorial library formation.
mechanism: Modular chemical compounds with self-assembly sequences (b1/b1′ and m/m′) that selectively combine with complementary sequences on other compounds, allowing controlled linking of functional moieties (p/q) via sequence-specific hybridization.
mechanism_raw: Modular chemical compounds with self-assembly sequences (b1/b1′ and m/m′) that selectively combine with complementary sequences on other compounds, allowing controlled linking of functional moieties (p/q) via sequence-specific hybridization.

abstract: A hair barrette for securing hair is disclosed. The hair barrette includes a first, second, and third segment. The first and second segments each have a first side having teeth and a catch, and an opposing second side having an ornamental design. The third segment is positioned between the first and second segments and may have a first end, a second end, a first opening adjacent to the first end, and a second opening adjacent to the second end. The catch of the first segment is insertable into the second opening of the third segment and the catch of the second, segment is insertable into the first opening of the third segment. Further the ornamental designs are visible when said the catches are inserted into the openings.
problem: Securing hair while maintaining an ornamental appearance in a hair barrette.
constraint: The ornamental design must remain hidden until the barrette is fully secured, requiring precise alignment of catches, openings, and design placement.
mechanism: A multi-segment mechanical system uses simultaneous engagement of retention elements with corresponding openings to both secure a target object and reveal decorative features only upon full actuation, ensuring visual elements remain concealed until the locking state is achieved.
mechanism_raw: Mechanical interlocking via catches inserted into openings in a third segment simultaneously secures the hair and positions ornamental designs to be visible only when the barrette is closed.

abstract: Methods, systems, and devices are disclosed for fabricating clean, oxidation-free nanoparticles of electrically conducting metals and alloys using spark erosion techniques. In one aspect, a method includes dispersing bulk pieces of an electrically conducting material in a dielectric fluid with mechanical vibrations within a container; generating an electric field using electrodes in the dielectric fluid using by an electric pulse, in which the electric field creates a plasma in a volume existing between the bulk pieces that locally heats the bulk pieces to form structures within the volume, the dielectric fluid quenching the structures to form nanoparticles, and filtering the nanoparticles through a screen including holes of a size allowing nanoparticles of the size or smaller to pass through the screen to a region in the container, in which the dielectric fluid inhibits oxidation of the surface of the nanoparticles.
problem: Producing oxidation-free nanoparticles of electrically conducting metals and alloys using spark erosion.
constraint: Balancing electric pulse energy, dielectric fluid properties, and vibration intensity to prevent oxidation without compromising nanoparticle formation efficiency.
mechanism: An electrical discharge process occurs within a fluid medium that simultaneously cools nascent particulate structures to limit growth and suppresses chemical reactions that would degrade material purity, while external mechanical agitation breaks apart aggregated material to promote uniform particle size distribution.
mechanism_raw: A dielectric fluid both quenches plasma-formed structures to create nanoparticles and inhibits oxidation, while mechanical vibrations disperse bulk material to enable controlled erosion.

abstract: The invention relates to an ejector unit, in particular for a road milling machine, having an ejector that is replaceably mounted on a carrier. In one aspect the ejector is curved in a scoop-like fashion. In another aspect the ejector is reversible upon the carrier to allow the ejector to be reversed after one wear surface is worn, thus presenting a new second wear surface.
problem: Extending the operational lifespan of a wear-prone ejector component in a road milling machine.
constraint: The ejector must maintain structural integrity and functional alignment when reversed, requiring symmetrical design and robust mounting.
mechanism: A wear-resistant component with multiple usable surfaces is mounted in a reversible configuration so that degradation of one surface can be compensated by reorienting the component to expose an unused surface, extending operational life without replacement.
mechanism_raw: A reversible, scoop-shaped ejector is mounted on a carrier such that flipping it exposes a fresh wear surface after one side degrades, eliminating the need for full replacement.

abstract: A light steel roof truss with a structure of a double continuous beam includes structural beams (1) and structural columns (2). The structural beam (1) consists of a pair of continuous beams, and the structural column (2) is located between the two continuous beams through locating holes (4). Thereby the stability of a support structure of the roof truss is increased, and the supporting members of the roof truss can be connected conveniently.
problem: Increasing structural stability and simplifying connections in a light steel roof truss.
constraint: The beam-column interface must balance ease of assembly with sufficient rigidity to prevent loosening or misalignment over time.
mechanism: A structural framework employs two parallel load-bearing elements with intermediate vertical supports positioned and aligned via registration features, creating mutual bracing between the elements that enhances overall rigidity and maintains geometric stability under applied loads.
mechanism_raw: A dual continuous beam system with structural columns positioned between the beams via locating holes creates a self-stabilizing framework that resists deformation under load.

abstract: The disclosed technology includes a storage device including an interlaced magnetic recording (IMR) system, and a transducer head, including two writers, each writer including a write pole, wherein a width of a first write pole in a cross-track direction is substantially greater than a width of a second write pole in the cross-track direction, and wherein a down-track width of a front shield gap of the first write pole is substantially similar to down-track width of a front shield gap of the second write pole. In another implementation, the storage device includes an IMR system, and a transducer head, including two writers, each writer including a write pole, wherein a width of the first write pole in a cross-track direction is substantially greater than a width of a second write pole in a cross-track direction, and wherein a cross-track width of a side shield gap of the first write pole is substantially similar to a cross-track width of a side shield gap of the second write pole.
problem: Optimizing data writing in an interlaced magnetic recording (IMR) system to improve storage density and reliability.
constraint: The disparity in pole widths must be calibrated to avoid cross-track interference while maintaining consistent shielding for signal integrity.
mechanism: Two writing elements with different lateral dimensions but matched longitudinal and lateral spacing are arranged to enable selective data placement and reduce signal interference during sequential writing operations, where dimensional disparity controls overwrite behavior and spacing controls shielding effectiveness.
mechanism_raw: Two writers with differing cross-track pole widths but matched down-track or side-shield gaps enable selective overwriting and interference reduction during IMR operations.

abstract: A process for depositing a metal includes disposing an activating catalyst on a substrate; contacting the activating catalyst with a metal cation from a vapor deposition composition; contacting the substrate with a reducing anion from the vapor deposition composition; performing an oxidation-reduction reaction between the metal cation and the reducing anion in a presence of the activating catalyst; and forming a metal from the metal cation to deposit the metal on the substrate. A system for depositing a metal includes an activating catalyst to deposit on a substrate; and a primary reagent to form: a metal cation to deposit on the substrate as a metal; and a reducing anion to provide electrons to the activating catalyst, the metal cation, the substrate, or a combination thereof, wherein the primary reagent forms the metal cation and the reducing anion in response to being subjected to a dissociating condition.
problem: Efficiently depositing a metal on a substrate while controlling the oxidation-reduction reaction to avoid unwanted side reactions or incomplete deposition.
constraint: Balancing reaction kinetics and catalyst activity to ensure uniform deposition without over-reduction or catalyst deactivation, while maintaining compatibility with vapor-phase processing conditions.
mechanism: Using a catalytic mediator to control electron transfer between a metallic species and a reducing agent, enabling direct formation of a metallic layer on a substrate surface through regulated redox kinetics.
mechanism_raw: Using an activating catalyst to mediate the redox reaction between a metal cation and a reducing anion, enabling the formation of metallic deposits directly on the substrate surface through controlled electron transfer.

abstract: Methods, systems, and computer program products for visually representing and displaying data are described. The visual representation may be a data animation. A data query may be submitted, a time measurement for processing the query may be obtained, and a sample size of the query may be adjusted based on the time measurement and a frame refresh rate of a data animation. A data animation may be generated based on one or more results of the query.
problem: Maintaining real-time data animation performance when query processing times vary, to avoid lag or dropped frames during visualization.
constraint: Trade-off between data resolution (sample size) and processing speed, requiring adaptive tuning to preserve visual fidelity while meeting real-time display deadlines.
mechanism: Monitoring processing latency against a display refresh deadline and adaptively scaling data query resolution to maintain synchronization between animation output and real-time display capabilities.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically adjusting the sample size of the data query based on measured processing time and the target frame refresh rate, ensuring that the animation remains synchronized with display capabilities.

abstract: The present application describes a product mixing device. The product mixing device includes an ingredient combination chamber and means for agitation positioned about the ingredient combination chamber. The ingredient combination chamber includes a diluent inlet, a number of macro-ingredient inlets, a number of micro-ingredient inlets, and an outlet.
problem: Efficiently mixing ingredients with vastly different quantities (macro vs. micro) while maintaining precise proportions and avoiding cross-contamination.
constraint: Balancing agitation intensity and chamber geometry to achieve homogeneity across all ingredient types while preventing degradation of sensitive micro-ingredients.
mechanism: Routing ingredients through separate delivery pathways into a shared mixing chamber, applying localized agitation to homogenize contents while preserving proportional ratios and preventing cross-contamination.
mechanism_raw: Separating ingredient delivery into distinct inlets (diluent, macro, micro) within a single combination chamber, combined with localized agitation to ensure thorough mixing without disrupting ingredient ratios.

abstract: The present invention relates to a vane rotary compressor wherein the volume of a compression room is reduced and a fluid is compressed when a rotor rotates. According to one embodiment of the present invention, the present invention provides the vane rotary compressor for maximizing the rotational moment of a vane by extending a weight part at a front end part of the curved blade type vane so as to remove the hitting noise due to the delay of the rotational operation of the vane when the rotor is rotated, and increasing the performance by reducing the internal leak.
problem: Reducing rotational delay and impact noise in a vane rotary compressor caused by inertia mismatches during rotor operation.
constraint: Optimizing weight distribution to enhance rotational inertia without introducing excessive friction, wear, or imbalance in the rotor system.
mechanism: Adding mass to a rotating component at a strategic radial location to increase rotational inertia, smoothing motion transitions and reducing impact forces caused by inertia mismatches during cyclic operation.
mechanism_raw: Extending a weight part at the front end of the curved vane to increase rotational moment, ensuring smoother vane movement and reducing timing delays that cause hitting noise and internal leakage.

abstract: A light source device for an electronic endoscope includes a light source that emits light having a visible light wavelength region and an optical filter that has transmission peaks at a plurality of particular wavelengths in a continuous wavelength region including the visible light wavelength region. The plurality of particular wavelengths include wavelengths of around 420 nm, around 550 nm and around 650 nm. The optical filter has a constant transmissivity higher than zero and lower than a half of each of the transmission peaks in a wavelength region between the transmission peaks and the constant transmissivity in the wavelength region between the transmission peaks is higher than a transmissivity in a wavelength region other than between the transmission peaks.
problem: Providing targeted wavelength illumination for endoscopic imaging while suppressing unwanted spectral regions that degrade image quality.
constraint: Maintaining sharp spectral selectivity at target wavelengths while ensuring sufficient overall light throughput and minimizing crosstalk between adjacent transmission regions.
mechanism: Employing a spectral filter with discrete transmission peaks at selected wavelengths and controlled intermediate transmissivity to isolate desired optical bands while suppressing unwanted spectral regions.
mechanism_raw: Using an optical filter with discrete transmission peaks at specific wavelengths (e.g., 420 nm, 550 nm, 650 nm) and controlled intermediate transmissivity to isolate desired spectral bands while allowing minimal background light transmission.

abstract: Disclosed is a system and method of dynamically sorting items for delivery to diverse destinations in which at least one target location changes during the sorting process using an electronic array that correlates diverse destinations to target locations for sorting, wherein the electronic array changes based upon criteria relating to the results of the sort resulting in the removal of a first set of items from one target location while leaving a second set in the target location and placing the first set in another target location to adapt to the changed array and thereafter continuing to sort further items according to the changed array while some items remain in their initial target locations. Additionally disclosed is a system and method of sorting which electronically identifies items destined for the same address that are comingled with items to diverse destinations, and allows for their separation and bundling responsive to the electronic identification and allows for payment for delivery charges based upon a bundle rather than the individual items included in the bundle.
problem: Adapting item sorting to dynamically changing target destinations during the sorting process while maintaining partial sorted states.
constraint: Balancing adaptability to changing destinations with the need to avoid disrupting items already sorted to their initial target locations.
mechanism: Dynamically updating a mapping system that associates destinations with target locations based on real-time sorting outcomes, enabling selective relocation of a subset of items to new destinations while preserving the placement of already sorted items, and grouping items sharing the same destination for coordinated handling.
mechanism_raw: Dynamically adjusting an electronic array that maps destinations to target locations based on real-time sort results, enabling selective relocation of a subset of items to new target locations while leaving other items in their initial locations, and bundling items destined for the same address.

abstract: A method for modelling load in a power grid is provided. The method includes obtaining measurement data from a measurement device in the power grid, identifying one or more voltage adjustment events in the power grid from the measurement data, and generating a load model based on one or more voltage factors computed using the one or more voltage adjustment events.
problem: Accurately modeling electrical load in a power grid under varying voltage conditions.
constraint: Reliance on the frequency and accuracy of voltage event detection to ensure the load model remains representative of actual grid conditions.
mechanism: Detecting voltage adjustment events from real-time measurements and computing voltage-dependent factors to adjust a load model, ensuring the model reflects dynamic grid conditions through continuous recalibration based on detected voltage changes.
mechanism_raw: Identifying voltage adjustment events from real-time measurement data and computing voltage-based factors to generate a load model that reflects dynamic grid behavior.
residual_terms: ["voltage adjustment events", "voltage-dependent factors", "load model", "dynamic grid conditions"]

abstract: A needle bar case has a plurality of needle bars.
