As a main shaft is rotated by a main shaft motor (first drive source), the needle bars are driven in an up-down direction so that a sewing operation is carried out in a conventionally-known manner. Ascending/descending bars are supported on the needle bar case in corresponding relation to the needle bars, and each of the ascending/descending bars is driven in the up-down direction by a motor (second drive source). A cord guide member for guiding a cord material onto a workpiece is mounted to the lower end of any of the ascending/descending bars, in place of a conventional presser foot. Cord sewing or loop sewing of cord material can be performed selectively by changing an ascending/descending stroke of the ascending/descending bar. Thus, cord sewing and loop sewing of the chord material can be performed selectively with a simple construction.
problem: Enabling selective performance of different sewing operations (cord sewing vs. loop sewing) with a single, simple mechanical construction.
constraint: Maintaining mechanical simplicity while allowing independent control of the cord guide's motion to achieve different sewing modes.
mechanism: Using an independent drive mechanism to modulate the stroke length of a tool component, enabling switching between distinct operational modes by varying the component's motion range while maintaining mechanical simplicity.
mechanism_raw: Using a secondary drive source to independently adjust the ascending/descending stroke of a cord guide member, allowing the same tool to switch between operations by varying the stroke length.

abstract: The present invention is directed to a sink assembly that can separate particulate contaminants from a liquid in which they are suspended. The sink assembly includes a master trap and at least a first trap with a riser and valve assembly to collect particulates and prevent overflow from the master trap. The sink assembly provides a simple maintenance and cleaning solution.
problem: Separating particulate contaminants from a liquid while preventing overflow of the primary collection chamber.
constraint: Balancing effective particulate separation with the need for simple maintenance and cleaning of the trap system.
mechanism: Employing a staged separation system with a primary and secondary containment unit, where the secondary unit includes a regulated overflow pathway to collect particulates and prevent overfilling of the primary chamber during liquid filtration.
mechanism_raw: Using a master trap combined with a secondary trap equipped with a riser and valve assembly to collect particulates and regulate overflow, ensuring staged separation and containment.
residual_terms: ["staged separation system", "primary and secondary containment", "regulated overflow pathway", "particulates"]

abstract: A bladeless fluid/vapor includes: (a) three or more turbine discs disposed within a case, wherein each turbine disc has a center opening, a first set of holes substantially equally spaced from one another along a first radius, a second set of holes substantially equally spaced from one another along a second radius, and two or more of the turbine discs have a set of exhaust ports positioned annularly around the center opening; (b) the case includes a main housing, a cover and one or more fluid/vapor inlets oriented to direct a fluid/vapor onto an outer portion of the turbine discs; (c) a drive shaft passing through the center openings of the turbine discs and attached to the turbine discs; (d) a fluid/vapor outlet in the cover; and (e) a set of exhaust holes proximate to and connected to the fluid/vapor outlet that are positioned annularly around the drive shaft.
problem: Generating rotational motion from fluid or vapor flow without traditional turbine blades.
constraint: Optimizing hole placement, exhaust port geometry, and disc alignment to maximize energy transfer efficiency without blade-based turbulence.
mechanism: Directing fluid or vapor flow onto rotating discs with strategically positioned openings and exhaust ports to generate pressure differentials and momentum transfer, inducing rotation through structured fluid dynamics without blade-based interaction.
mechanism_raw: Directing fluid/vapor onto turbine discs with strategically arranged holes and exhaust ports to create pressure differentials and momentum transfer, inducing rotation through structured fluid dynamics.
residual_terms: ["rotating discs", "strategically positioned openings", "exhaust ports", "pressure differentials", "momentum transfer"]

abstract: A dryer adapted for use in an asphalt plant. The dryer comprises a drum having an inner wall and a plurality of flights, each of which is disposed on the inner wall of the drum and each of which has a proximal end and a distal end spaced apart from the proximal end. At least one of the plurality of flights comprises a V-shaped notch. A method for drying components of asphalt comprising drying the components of asphalt in the drum of such a dryer.
problem: Inefficient heat transfer and material mixing in asphalt drying due to suboptimal material movement within the drum.
constraint: Balancing material agitation intensity with mechanical durability of the flights and drum structure.
mechanism: A series of angled lifting elements create a controlled lifting and cascading motion of material, increasing surface exposure to heat while maintaining structural integrity of the containment vessel.
mechanism_raw: V-shaped notches on flights create a controlled lifting and cascading motion of material, increasing surface exposure to heat while maintaining structural integrity of the drum.

abstract: According to one embodiment, a display device includes first and second substrates, and liquid crystal layer. The first substrate includes first and second electrodes. The second electrode includes comblike electrodes extending in parallel to a first direction and tapered toward tips thereof, and a connecting portion which connects the comblike electrodes. An initial alignment direction is parallel to the first direction or a direction orthogonal to the first direction. The comblike electrode includes a first part having sides each form a first angle with the first direction, and a second part having sides each form a second angle with the first direction, the second angle being greater than the first angle.
problem: Inadequate control over liquid crystal alignment in display devices, leading to inconsistent optical performance.
constraint: Maintaining uniform alignment across the display while achieving fine-grained control over crystal orientation.
mechanism: Interdigitated electrodes with spatially varying geometries generate a spatially varying electric field gradient, enabling precise alignment of liquid crystals through differential field strength.
mechanism_raw: Comblike electrodes with varying taper angles generate a spatially varying electric field gradient, enabling precise alignment of liquid crystals through differential field strength.

abstract: A rotary press comprises a press frame and a rotor arranged thereon. The rotor has a die plate, an upper punch receiver receiving upper punches, a lower punch receiver receiving lower punches, an upper cam that guides the upper punches, and a lower cam that guides the lower punches. A rotor drive can drive the rotor rotationally. Within at least one dosing station, material is filled into receivers of the die plate for pressing. An upper pressing station has an upper pressing roller and a lower pressing station has a lower pressing roller. Coupling means couples at least one drive that operates the rotary press to the rotor such that, with movement of the at least one drive, the rotor is raised out of its operating position and into a removal position where the rotor can be removed out of the press frame in a lateral direction.
problem: Difficulty in removing or replacing a rotor in a rotary press without disassembling the entire machine.
constraint: Ensuring smooth transition between operational and removal positions without disrupting adjacent machinery or processes.
mechanism: A mechanical coupling links the rotor to a drive system such that actuating the drive raises the rotor vertically and shifts it laterally, decoupling it from the operating position for removal.
mechanism_raw: Coupling means mechanically links the rotor to a drive system such that actuating the drive raises the rotor vertically and shifts it laterally, decoupling it from the operating position for removal.

abstract: An elevator landing door arrangement for installation in a landing door opening of an elevator shaft wall includes at least one door jamb and at least one protective element fixed at the door jamb which abuts with its sealing portion against the landing door opening. The protective element has a fixing portion facing the door jamb, whereby either the fixing portion is bent around a carrier element of the door jamb or the carrier element extends around the fixing portion of the protective element.
problem: Ineffective sealing of elevator landing door openings, allowing drafts, noise, or debris infiltration.
constraint: Achieving durable sealing performance under repeated door operation and environmental exposure.
mechanism: A flexible sealing element is mechanically integrated with a door frame carrier, creating a dynamic seal that adapts to movement while maintaining contact pressure.
mechanism_raw: A protective element with a flexible fixing portion is mechanically integrated with the door jamb carrier, creating a dynamic seal that adapts to movement while maintaining contact pressure.

abstract: In a golf ball having a core and a cover, the core is formed of a rubber composition, has center and surface portions which are unfoamed regions and has an intermediate portion containing a foamed region. The core is produced by charging the rubber composition, which contains a blowing agent, into a first curing mold and curing under given conditions, then removing the molded rubber material in a semi-cured state from the first mold, transferring the semi-cured material to a second curing mold and curing under given conditions. The foamed region of the core deforms by a certain degree at the time of impact, decreasing the radius of gyration of the ball and enabling a lower spin rate to be achieved. The decrease in resilience due to expansion of the molded material can be held to a minimum.
problem: Trade-off between reducing spin rate and maintaining resilience in golf balls during impact.
constraint: Optimizing foam distribution to balance spin reduction with minimal loss of rebound energy.
mechanism: A deformable core region reduces the radius of gyration under impact to lower spin rate, while rigid regions preserve structural resilience by limiting energy absorption.
mechanism_raw: A foamed core region deforms under impact, reducing the radius of gyration to lower spin rate, while unfoamed regions preserve structural resilience by limiting energy absorption.

abstract: Screw compressor with a compression chamber that is formed by a compression housing, in which a pair of meshed helical compressor rotors in the form of a screw are rotatably mounted and with a drive motor that is provided with a motor chamber formed by a motor housing, in which a motor shaft is rotatably mounted, and this motor shaft drives at least one of the aforementioned two compressor rotors, whereby the compression housing and the motor housing are connected directly together to form a compressor housing, whereby the motor chamber and the compression chamber are not sealed off from one another and whereby the rotor shafts of the compressor rotors, as well as the motor shaft, extend along axial directions that are oblique or transverse to the horizontal plane.
problem: Need for a compact screw compressor that integrates the motor and compression stages efficiently without requiring complex sealing between chambers, while maintaining structural integrity and operational effectiveness.
constraint: The trade-off is between achieving compactness and integration versus managing cross-chamber contamination, heat transfer, and pressure dynamics that arise from not sealing the motor and compression chambers separately.
mechanism: Integrating two functionally distinct chambers (e.g., a drive mechanism and a compression mechanism) into a single shared housing without a physical barrier between them, allowing direct thermal and pressure interactions between the chambers. Orienting the primary rotating components along non-horizontal axes to optimize spatial arrangement and compactness. The unsealed interconnection enables cross-chamber energy and material exchanges to be utilized rather than isolated, while the non-horizontal orientation reduces overall footprint.
mechanism_raw: Directly connecting the motor housing and compression housing to form a single integrated compressor housing, with the motor chamber and compression chamber left unsealed from one another, and orienting the rotor and motor shafts along oblique or transverse directions relative to the horizontal plane. The unsealed interconnection allows thermal and pressure interactions between the motor and compression chambers to be leveraged rather than isolated, while the non-horizontal shaft orientation enables spatial optimization of the overall assembly.

abstract: A forming apparatus comprises: a machine bed; a tool holder mounted movably relative to the machine bed; a drive unit connected to the tool holder; a disconnector unit; a machine control for operating the drive unit; and a monitoring device to monitor movements of the tool holder and to activate the disconnector unit. The monitoring unit includes two distance measuring systems that respectively generate first and second position signals at different rates for determining a position of the tool holder relative to the machine bed. At least one radiation beam detector is deactivated in response to a different between the first and second position signals undershooting a predetermined value.
problem: Need for reliable, high-precision monitoring of tool holder position in a forming apparatus that can detect anomalies and trigger a safety disconnection before damage or unsafe conditions occur.
constraint: The trade-off is between detection sensitivity and false trigger avoidance — the threshold must be set to catch real anomalies while not being so sensitive that normal operational variations cause unnecessary disconnections, and the dual measurement system adds complexity and cost.
mechanism: Employing two independent sensing systems that sample a physical parameter at different temporal rates, generating asynchronous measurement signals. A comparator evaluates the temporal discrepancy between the signals against a predefined threshold. When the discrepancy falls below the threshold (indicating an inconsistency or anomaly), a safety mechanism is triggered to interrupt operation. The dual-rate sampling creates a temporal cross-validation that detects deviations imperceptible to single-rate monitoring.
mechanism_raw: Using two distance measuring systems that sample position at different rates, generating first and second position signals. A radiation beam detector is deactivated when the temporal difference between the two signals undershoots a predetermined threshold, indicating an anomaly. The monitoring device then activates a disconnector unit to safely interrupt operation. The dual-rate sampling creates a temporal cross-check that can detect inconsistencies that single-rate monitoring might miss.

abstract: The instant invention relates to mesogenic media comprising one or more compounds of formula Dwherein the parameters are as specified in the text, preferably to mesogenic media showing a blue phase, preferably stabilised by a polymer, and their use in electro-optical light modulation elements and their respective use in displays, as well as to such devices.
reason: The abstract describes a chemical composition (mesogenic media with a formula whose parameters are unspecified) and mentions polymer stabilization of blue phase liquid crystals, but does not explain any causal functional mechanism. It reads as a material listing with application references rather than a problem-solving mechanism.

abstract: Disclosed is an apparatus and method for capturing the hot humid gases from a gypsum board dryer and utilizing those gases in the production of a synthetic gas (referred to as “syngas”). The syngas produced can then be utilized within a gypsum board plant to reduce the amount of natural gas needed. The method utilizes the heated water vapor (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2) found within the flue gas of a board dryer. The H2O and CO2 are used in a gasification process to yield the syngas.
problem: Need to reduce natural gas consumption in a gypsum board plant by recovering and utilizing waste heat and byproduct gases from the drying process rather than venting them to the atmosphere.
constraint: The trade-off is between the energy and capital investment required for the gasification process and the amount of natural gas savings achieved, plus the need to match syngas production rates to the plant's variable energy demands.
mechanism: Capturing waste byproduct streams (e.g., heated gases and moisture) from a primary process and routing them into a secondary conversion process to generate a usable fuel. The converted fuel is then fed back into the primary process or ancillary systems to offset external energy inputs. This establishes a closed-loop energy recovery system where waste from one stage becomes the input resource for another, reducing dependency on external fuel sources.
mechanism_raw: Capturing hot humid gases (containing heated H2O and CO2) from a gypsum board dryer and feeding them into a gasification process to produce synthetic gas (syngas). The syngas is then used within the same plant as a fuel source, reducing the need for external natural gas. This creates a closed-loop energy recovery system where waste heat and byproduct gases from one process become the input fuel for another.

abstract: Methods, systems, and devices are disclosed for capturing, concentrating, isolating, and detecting molecules. In one aspect, a molecular probe device includes a molecular probe having a complimentary base pair region initially zipped and structured to include a binding agent to chemically attach the molecular probe to an outer surface of a magnetic bead, and a binding molecule to chemically attach the molecular probe to a substrate of a microfluidic device, in which the complimentary base pair region is configured to hybridize to a complementary nucleic acid sequence of a DNA or RNA molecule.
problem: Need for a system that can capture, concentrate, isolate, and detect specific target molecules (such as DNA or RNA sequences) from a sample, combining selective binding with physical separation and detection capabilities.
constraint: The trade-off is between maintaining the probe in its initial zipped conformation until target binding occurs (for specificity and stability) and allowing sufficient conformational flexibility for efficient hybridization with the target molecule.
mechanism: A molecular probe with a conformationally switchable region that transitions between a stable (e.g., zipped) state and an active (e.g., hybridized) state upon binding to a target molecule. The probe is functionalized with two distinct attachment moieties: one enabling mobile separation (e.g., magnetic coupling) and another enabling fixed positioning (e.g., substrate anchoring). Binding to the target triggers a conformational change that allows the probe-target complex to be physically isolated and concentrated via the mobile attachment, while the fixed attachment enables localized detection at a defined site.
mechanism_raw: A molecular probe with a complementary base pair region initially in a zipped conformation, structured with two distinct attachment points: a binding agent that chemically attaches the probe to a magnetic bead (enabling mobile separation and concentration), and a binding molecule that attaches the probe to a fixed substrate in a microfluidic device (enabling controlled positioning). When the complementary base pair region hybridizes to a target nucleic acid sequence, the magnetic bead allows the probe-target complex to be physically separated and concentrated from the sample, while the microfluidic attachment enables detection at a defined location.

abstract: A hot-dip galvanized steel sheet contains specific amounts of C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ti, Al, and N with the remainder being iron and unavoidable impurities. Bainitic ferrite, martensite, retained γ, and ferrite (α) are present each in a specific area ratio. The remainder γ has a specific C concentration. Sub-grains in the recrystallized α and un-recrystallized α have a specific grain diameter. The surface area ratio of α and worked α having a grain diameter of 5 μm or more is 5% or less. The average particle diameter of TiC particles inside α grains is 10 nm or less.
problem: Achieving a balance between strength, ductility, and surface quality in hot-dip galvanized steel sheets.
constraint: Balancing the area ratios of distinct microstructural phases and sub-grain diameters to avoid brittleness while maintaining formability and corrosion resistance.
mechanism: Adjusting the proportions of distinct microstructural phases and sub-grain dimensions through controlled composition and processing to balance mechanical strength, ductility, and surface integrity. Phase area ratios and grain boundary constraints are managed to prevent brittleness while maintaining formability and corrosion resistance.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the microstructure through precise alloying element ratios and phase area ratios (bainitic ferrite, martensite, retained γ, and ferrite) to optimize mechanical properties. Sub-grain size management and TiC particle size constraints further refine grain boundary strength and surface integrity.
residual_terms: ["microstructural phases", "sub-grain dimensions", "phase area ratios", "grain boundary constraints"]

abstract: Implementations relate to prioritized display of visual content in computer presentations. In some implementations, a computer-executed method includes obtaining first visual content and second visual content associated with the first visual content, where the first and second visual content include a plurality of pixels. The method provides a display of a computer presentation by a display device, where the first visual content is displayed in a presentation area of the computer presentation. The method determines that a first presentation priority of at least a portion of the first visual content is reduced based on a determination that less than a threshold amount of the at least a portion of the first visual content has changed. In response to determining that the first presentation priority is reduced, the method improves a visibility of a display of the second visual content in the computer presentation.
problem: Efficiently allocating display resources in computer presentations to prioritize dynamic content over static content.
constraint: Defining a threshold for 'change' that balances computational overhead with perceptual relevance, ensuring minimal latency in priority adjustments.
mechanism: Monitoring dynamic content changes across a visual field and dynamically reallocating display resources by reducing priority for static regions (below a change threshold) while enhancing visibility of associated secondary content to direct attention toward active areas.
mechanism_raw: Detecting changes in visual content pixels and dynamically adjusting presentation priority: reducing priority for static regions (below a change threshold) while enhancing visibility of associated secondary content (e.g., overlays or annotations) to focus user attention.

abstract: A novel maize variety designated X05K660 and seed, plants and plant parts thereof are produced by crossing inbred maize varieties. Methods for producing a maize plant by crossing hybrid maize variety X05K660 with another maize plant are disclosed. Methods for producing a maize plant containing in its genetic material one or more traits introgressed into X05K660 through backcross conversion and/or transformation, and to the maize seed, plant and plant part produced thereby. This invention relates to the maize variety X05K660, the seed, the plant produced from the seed, and variants, mutants, and minor modifications of maize variety X05K660. This invention further relates to methods for producing maize varieties derived from maize variety X05K660.
problem: Introducing specific agronomic or genetic traits into a plant variety while maintaining genetic stability.
constraint: Maintaining genetic linkage and avoiding unintended trait loss during repeated backcrossing cycles, requiring precise selection at each generation.
mechanism: Introducing a target trait into a recipient organism through iterative controlled cross-breeding with a donor, followed by selective propagation of offspring that retain the trait while preserving genetic stability via linkage maintenance across generations.
mechanism_raw: Using controlled cross-breeding and backcross conversion to introgress desired traits into a base variety (e.g., X05K660), followed by selection of progeny with stable inheritance of the target traits.

abstract: A system and a method for removing a thigh bone from a defeathered whole leg poultry product includes providing a leg product including a thigh, a drumstick and a knee joint. In the leg product, a transverse cut has been provided at the knee joint transverse to the thigh bone and the tibia bone, which extends from one side of the leg product to a cut end so that the thigh and the drumstick are connected to each other, by which transverse cut a drumstick side cut plane and a thigh side cut plane are created. While keeping the thigh and the drumstick connected to each other, changing the angle between the thigh and thereby exposing the thigh side cut plane, while keeping the thigh meat and the drumstick connected to each other, removing the thigh bone from the thigh meat via the thigh side cut plane.
problem: Removing a bone from a poultry leg product while preserving meat integrity and minimizing tissue damage.
constraint: Balancing the depth and orientation of cuts to ensure bone accessibility without severing connective tissues that hold meat to the bone.
mechanism: Creating an access plane via a transverse incision at a joint, then reorienting connected segments to expose an embedded structure for removal while maintaining physical linkage of surrounding tissues to prevent separation of the target material.
mechanism_raw: Creating a transverse cut at the joint to establish access planes, then altering the angle between connected segments to expose the bone surface for extraction while maintaining physical linkage to prevent meat separation.

abstract: The invention relates to radiation-curable aqueous composition comprising an (meth)acrylated polyurethane pre-polymer obtained from the reaction of a polyisocyanate, optionally a polyol, at least one hydrophilic compound containing at least one reactive group capable to react with isocyanate groups and which is capable to render the polyurethane pre-polymer dispersible in aqueous medium either directly or after the reaction with a neutralizing agent to provide a salt, an (meth)acrylated compound containing at least two reactive groups capable to react with isocyanate groups and an (meth)acrylated compound containing essentially one reactive group capable to react with isocyanate groups, said composition comprising an amount of (meth)acrylated and polymerizable ethylenically unsaturated groups of at least 3 meq per g.
problem: Formulating a radiation-curable aqueous coating with sufficient reactivity and water dispersibility.
constraint: Optimizing the ratio of multi-functional to mono-functional acrylated compounds to control crosslinking density and prevent premature gelation in aqueous media.
mechanism: Balancing polymerization efficiency and aqueous solubility by combining a hydrophilic base polymer with reactive groups and a blend of multi-functional and mono-functional reactive compounds, where the ratio of functional groups controls crosslinking density and prevents premature gelation.
mechanism_raw: Combining a hydrophilic polyurethane pre-polymer (with reactive groups for aqueous dispersibility) and acrylated compounds (with varying reactive group counts) to achieve a balance of polymerization efficiency and solubility during curing.

abstract: A cooling device includes an electrode unit which is arranged in a space between adjacent radiation fins and which is electrically insulated from the radiation fins, and a power supply source which applies a voltage between a heat radiation structure and the electrode unit. The cooling device is further provided with an insulation resistance detection unit which calculates an insulation resistance between the heat radiation structure and the electrode unit, and a comparison unit which compares the insulation resistance calculated by the insulation resistance detection unit with a predetermined threshold, wherein, as a result of the comparison of the calculated insulation resistance and the predetermined threshold by the comparison unit, when the calculated insulation resistance is lower than the predetermined threshold, the cooling device is adapted to judge that the radiation fins have clogged.
problem: Detecting clogging or contamination in a heat radiation structure (e.g., fins) without physical inspection or manual intervention.
constraint: The electrode must be electrically insulated from the radiation structure, and the threshold for insulation resistance must be calibrated to distinguish between normal operation and clogging conditions.
mechanism: Using a measurable electrical property between a conductive element and a heat-dissipating structure as an indirect indicator of physical obstruction. A calibrated threshold distinguishes between unobstructed and obstructed states, enabling automated detection without physical inspection.
mechanism_raw: Using electrical insulation resistance between an electrode and the heat radiation structure as an indirect measure of physical blockage. A drop in insulation resistance indicates clogging, enabling automated detection.

abstract: A stationary test device for a missile includes a retaining device for an avionics testpiece of the missile, where the retaining device enables a movement of the avionics testpiece in three rotational degrees of freedom, and a display device configured to display information on the missile surroundings, where the display device is configured to be moved inside a virtual plane by a translational carriage system. The display device can be detected by the avionics testpiece if the avionics testpiece is disposed on the retaining device. A mobile test device for the missile includes a flight platform, a carrier device mounted on the flight platform, for an avionics testpiece of the missile, wherein the carrier device enables a movement of the avionics testpiece in three rotational degrees of freedom, and a control module, where the control module is configured to control the flight platform for taking off on a specified reference trajectory, control the carrier device for orientation of the avionics testpiece, and store navigation data generated by the avionics testpiece. Finally, a test system for the missile includes the stationary test device and the mobile test device.
problem: Testing missile avionics systems in both stationary and mobile environments while simulating real-world conditions and capturing navigation data.
constraint: The system must coordinate the movement of the testpiece and display to maintain alignment and ensure accurate simulation of the missile's operational environment.
mechanism: Coordinating rotational motion of a test object with translational or positional movement of a visual output system to simulate dynamic environmental conditions. Synchronized alignment between the object and display ensures realistic replication of operational scenarios during testing.
mechanism_raw: Combining a 3D rotational retaining device for the avionics testpiece with a movable display system (via translational carriage or flight platform) to simulate environmental conditions and orientation changes, enabling realistic testing scenarios.

abstract: A vehicle video display verification system, comprising a camera carried by the vehicle; a display unit positioned in the vehicle displaying images captured by said camera; a verification sensor monitoring the status of image information from said camera being displayed on said display unit; and, a video control unit receiving said image information from said camera and outputting said image information to said display unit, and receiving feedback information from said verification sensor; wherein said video control unit records said image information from said camera and said feedback information from said verification sensor for establishing confirmation of an image display status on said display unit in the event of a vehicle accident.
problem: Verifying that a vehicle's camera-captured images are correctly displayed on a display unit, and preserving evidence of display status in the event of an accident.
constraint: The verification sensor must be synchronized with the video control unit to ensure accurate correlation between the displayed image and the feedback data.
mechanism: Monitoring a display output in real-time using a feedback sensor and correlating it with source data through a control unit. The system records both original and verified data streams to preserve evidence of display integrity during critical events.
mechanism_raw: Using a verification sensor to monitor the display output in real-time and feeding this information back to a video control unit, which records both the original image data and the verification feedback for post-accident analysis.

abstract: A method may include automatically remotely identifying at least one characteristic of an individual via facial recognition; and providing a display for the individual, the display having a content at least partially based on the identified at least one characteristic of the individual. A system may include a facial recognition module configured for automatically remotely identifying at least one characteristic of an individual via facial recognition; and a display module coupled with the facial recognition module, the display module configured for providing a display for the individual, the display having a content at least partially based on the identified at least one characteristic of the individual.
problem: Automatically personalizing displayed content for an individual without requiring explicit input or interaction.
constraint: The facial recognition module must accurately identify characteristics, and the display content must be mapped appropriately to those characteristics to avoid irrelevant or inappropriate content.
mechanism: Inferring user attributes from biometric input and dynamically mapping those attributes to content parameters. A mapping rule set ensures displayed content aligns with inferred characteristics without explicit user interaction.
mechanism_raw: Using facial recognition to infer characteristics of an individual and dynamically adjusting the content of a display based on those inferred characteristics, creating a personalized user experience.

abstract: A dice and board game. The game may comprise: a game board, a set of indicator cubes, and four or more saucers. The game board may comprise: a primary playing surface, cubbies, colored sections, an inner wall, and an outer wall. The primary playing surface may comprise a marking and may be surrounded and defined by an inner wall. The cubbies and the colored sections may be located on an outer perimeter of the game board and may be in between the inner wall and the outer wall. The cubbies and the colored sections may alternate along the outer perimeter of the game board and may be separated by partitions. The set of indicator cubes may comprise: color indicator cubes, number indicator cubes, and five sets of colored dice. Each of the color indicator cubes may comprise five colored sides and one symbol side.
reason: The patent describes a game's physical components and rules but does not present a problem-solving mechanism beyond the game's specific design. The mechanism is limited to game mechanics rather than a transferable engineering or scientific principle.

abstract: Radiator panels include two spaced-apart face-sheets including an inside face-sheet and an outside face-sheet that are constructed of a fiber reinforced composite material, a honeycomb core positioned between the two spaced-apart face-sheets, and one or more heat pipes extending through the honeycomb core. Spacecraft include a body and two radiator panels operatively coupled to the body opposite each other.
problem: Efficiently dissipating heat in spacecraft while maintaining structural integrity in a lightweight, space-constrained environment.
constraint: Balancing thermal conductivity and structural strength without adding excessive mass or compromising the mechanical properties of the composite face-sheets.
mechanism: Embedding passive thermal transport elements within a lightweight cellular core structure sandwiched between high-strength face layers, where the core provides mechanical support while the transport elements enable heat transfer across the surface.
mechanism_raw: Integrating heat pipes through a honeycomb core sandwiched between fiber-reinforced face-sheets, where the honeycomb provides structural support and the heat pipes enable passive thermal transport across the radiator panels.

abstract: The quick-fit coupling (1) for pressurized fluid comprises a valve body (3) extending along a longitudinal axis (L) and having an axial cavity (4) wherein a shutter stem (5) is axially movable with respect to the valve body in contrast to and by action of at least one elastic element (6) between a position for opening and a position for closing an axial passage of fluid through said cavity (4), the stem (5) being configured so as to be subjected by the fluid present in the cavity (4) to a resultant force having a substantially null component at least in an axial direction.
problem: Creating a pressurized fluid coupling that can open/close reliably without being actuated or disrupted by the fluid pressure itself.
constraint: Achieving a force balance on the stem so that fluid pressure does not bias the valve position, while maintaining sealing integrity under varying pressure conditions.
mechanism: Configuring a movable barrier element with a geometry that balances opposing pressure forces to achieve a net zero axial force, allowing a resilient biasing element to control position changes independently of the working fluid pressure.
mechanism_raw: Designing a shutter stem whose geometry ensures the fluid pressure exerts a net axial force of zero, allowing an elastic element to control movement between open and closed positions independently of fluid pressure.

abstract: A method and apparatus for the continuous sublimation of a substance includes cascading a material containing a substance capable of sublimation, such as water, between a plurality of trays vertically stacked within a processing zone provided within a processing chamber. A substantially atmospheric environment is maintained within the processing zone at a temperature whereby the substance sublimes forming a sublimate within the environment. The environment containing the sublimate is contacted with a drying agent such as a desiccant to maintain the environment whereby the substance sublimes at substantially atmospheric pressure and at the controlled temperature.
problem: Continuously sublimating a substance (e.g., water) at atmospheric pressure while maintaining controlled environmental conditions to sustain the sublimation process.
constraint: Maintaining a stable temperature and humidity balance in the processing zone to prevent condensation or excessive drying, which could disrupt continuous sublimation.
mechanism: Arranging vertically stacked containment layers holding sublimable material within a controlled environment, while introducing a moisture-absorbing medium to the atmosphere to maintain humidity conditions that sustain sublimation at ambient pressure.
mechanism_raw: Cascading material containing the sublimable substance between vertically stacked trays in a processing zone, while contacting the sublimate-laden atmosphere with a drying agent to maintain humidity levels that favor sublimation at atmospheric pressure.

abstract: A fan control circuit drives and adjusts a rotation speed of a fan according to operating temperatures of a plurality of heat elements. The fan control circuit includes a plurality of temperature detection units, a temperature synthesizing unit, and a driving signal generation unit. Each of the temperature detection units respectively detects the operation temperature of each of the heat elements and outputs a temperature detection signal corresponding to each of the heat elements. The temperature synthesizing unit calculates and outputs mean temperature signals according to the plurality of temperature detection signals and a plurality of predetermined weighted values corresponding to the heat elements. The driving signal generation unit generates driving signals to the fan according to the mean temperature signals.
problem: Adjusting fan speed dynamically based on the thermal states of multiple heat-generating elements to optimize cooling efficiency.
constraint: Assigning appropriate weighting values to each heat element to reflect their relative thermal importance, ensuring the fan responds to critical hotspots without overreacting to less significant sources.
mechanism: Combining temperature measurements from multiple heat sources using assigned weighting factors to produce a composite thermal signal, which modulates output device speed in proportion to the aggregated thermal load.
mechanism_raw: Using weighted temperature signals from individual heat elements to compute a synthesized mean temperature, which drives fan speed adjustments proportional to the combined thermal load.

abstract: A bug zapper includes a body, a fan and a light source. The body has a compartment, an opening, a channel arranged between the compartment and the opening, and a coupling portion arranged between the compartment and the channel. The channel is formed by an enclosed reflection wall and gradually expands from the coupling portion towards the opening. The fan is coupled with the coupling portion. The light source is mounted on a location of the body adjacent to the fan and irradiates light in the channel. As such, the efficiency in attracting the mosquitoes is outstanding, and the negative effect to the human is reduced.
problem: Attracting and trapping insects efficiently in a bug zapper while minimizing exposure to humans from the light source or electrical components.
constraint: Optimizing the channel geometry and light placement to maximize insect attraction and capture while shielding humans from direct exposure to the light or electrical elements.
mechanism: Placing an illumination source adjacent to a flow-inducing element within an enclosed, diverging flow path, where the flow draws targets toward the illumination and the expanding path guides them into a capture zone isolated from human contact.
mechanism_raw: Positioning a light source adjacent to a fan within an enclosed, gradually expanding channel, where the fan draws insects toward the light and the expanding channel directs them into a trapping compartment away from human contact.

abstract: The present invention is a tray apparatus providing mobility of a Christmas tree in a tree stand. The invention comprises a pan for placing the tree stand and a releasably attached handle. The improved mobility provided by the smooth, low-friction pan and removable handle of the present invention assists in decoration of the tree by allowing rotation for placing lights and ornaments, or other decorating tasks, as well as to present a favored side toward a desired area of the room in which it is placed. The tree may also be decorated in any convenient location and then moved laterally into the desired final position. In addition to the relatively frictionless movement provided by the pan, it also provides a basin to contain any water that spills from the stand, to catch needles, to hold presents, and to protect the floor or carpet.
problem: Moving a heavy, water-filled tree stand for decoration or positioning without spillage or floor damage.
constraint: Balancing mobility (via low friction) with containment of liquids and debris to protect surfaces and maintain usability.
mechanism: A low-friction base enables smooth movement of a liquid-containing unit, while a surrounding containment structure retains liquids and debris to protect surfaces. A removable manual interface allows repositioning without lifting the entire assembly.
mechanism_raw: A low-friction pan base enables smooth rotation and lateral movement of the tree stand, while the pan's basin structure contains water, needles, and debris. The removable handle allows manual repositioning without lifting the entire assembly.

abstract: A centrifugal separator for separation of particles from a gas stream is disclosed. The centrifugal separator includes a self-supporting frame for mounting inside an existing vessel for guiding the gas stream. The frame comprises a holder configured to hold the frame at a position inside the vessel, and a first partition for dividing the vessel into a first section and a second section. The first section is upstream of the second section. The separator includes a gas inlet communicating with the first section, and a gas outlet communicating with the second section. A centrifugal rotor is arranged to be rotatably supported in the frame around a rotational axis, the rotor having a first and a second end portion and including a plurality of separation plates defining separation passages between the plates. The centrifugal separator is configured such that the first and second sections communicate via the separation passages of the rotor.
problem: Separating particles from a gas stream within an existing vessel without requiring vessel redesign or replacement.
constraint: Achieving effective separation while maintaining compatibility with pre-existing vessel geometries and minimizing installation complexity.
mechanism: A self-supporting partition divides a vessel into upstream and downstream sections, while a rotatable centrifugal element with separation surfaces creates a flow path that forces particles outward via centrifugal force. The modular design allows retrofitting into existing infrastructure.
mechanism_raw: A self-supporting frame with a partition divides the vessel into upstream and downstream sections, while a rotatable centrifugal rotor with separation plates creates a flow path that forces particles outward via centrifugal force. The frame's modular design allows retrofitting into existing infrastructure.

abstract: The invention relates to a canal control system for controlling the water level or water flow in a canal system (2), comprising: (a) a centralized master controller (20), (b) a local slave controller (30), (c) a wireless communication system between the centralized master controller and the local slave controller, (d) a (fixed) reference point (8) or (movable) marker (11) relating to the water level in the canal system, and (e) an adjustable actuator (9) in the canal system, such as agate or pump, whereby the local slave controller comprises a mobile device (13) capable of displaying a human-readable instruction which an operator can act upon to set the adjustable actuator. The operator takes a picture of the water level and/or of the setting of the adjustable actuator. The data of the picture is used for updating a mathematical model of predictive control of the canal system and for calculating the setting of the present actuator and for determining which actuator is to be visited next by the operator.
problem: Efficiently managing water levels or flows in a canal system with distributed actuators and variable conditions.
constraint: Balancing automated predictive control with human operator input to ensure accurate, timely adjustments in a distributed environment.
mechanism: A centralized controller uses predictive models updated by real-time visual data captured by a mobile local controller. The system dynamically calculates actuator adjustments and prioritizes which actuators to visit next based on model predictions.
mechanism_raw: A centralized master controller uses predictive models updated by real-time visual data (photos of water levels and actuator settings) captured by a mobile local slave controller. The system dynamically calculates actuator adjustments and prioritizes which actuators to visit next based on model predictions.
residual_terms: ["centralized controller", "predictive models", "real-time visual data", "mobile local controller", "actuator adjustments", "prioritizes"]

abstract: A razor having an attachment portion and a shaving aid is provided. The attachment portion includes a blade body. The shaving aid is provided with a deformable portion that deforms when contacted by the skin surface. When the razor is used, the shaving aid itself deforms to decrease the frictional resistance between the shaving aid and the skin surface. This improves the tactile sensation on the skin surface and thus the shaving sensation.
problem: Reducing friction and improving tactile feedback during shaving to enhance user comfort and control.
constraint: Maintaining structural integrity and shaving effectiveness while enabling sufficient deformation to reduce friction.
mechanism: A deformable material adapts its shape in response to contact pressure, dynamically reducing frictional resistance between two surfaces. This deformation optimizes contact geometry for smoother movement and improved sensory feedback.
mechanism_raw: A deformable shaving aid material adapts its shape in response to skin contact pressure, dynamically reducing frictional resistance between the razor and skin surface. This deformation optimizes contact geometry for smoother movement and improved sensory feedback.

abstract: A deep-UV optical circuit includes a laser emitting light wavelengths (λ) below 250 nm. The circuit also includes a graphene optical cable formed of an optic core formed of a gas or vacuum having an index of refraction ranging between 1.000 and 1.002 and a cladding layer formed of a graphene cylinder made of a contiguous lattice of covalently-bonded carbon atoms surrounding the optic core. The circuit also includes an optical detector circuit configured to detect the light. The graphene optical cable optically couples the laser to the optical detector circuit, where the optical cable transmits light wavelengths (λ) below 250 nm as graphene has an index of refraction less than 1 for light wavelengths (λ) below 250 nm.
problem: Transmitting deep-UV light (below 250 nm) efficiently in an optical circuit without signal degradation or material absorption.
constraint: Selecting materials with compatible refractive indices and structural properties to support UV transmission while maintaining optical coupling efficiency.
mechanism: An optical transmission medium uses a low-refractive-index core surrounded by a cladding layer with a refractive index below that of the core for the target wavelength range. The cladding enables total internal reflection, guiding light with minimal loss.
mechanism_raw: A graphene-based optical cable uses a gas/vacuum core (refractive index ~1.000–1.002) surrounded by a graphene cladding layer. Graphene's refractive index below 1 for sub-250 nm wavelengths enables total internal reflection, guiding light with minimal loss.

abstract: Methods and apparatus of producing collectible cards are disclosed. An example method includes producing a first stack of cards including a first card type and a second card type from a single substrate sheet, separating the first stack of cards into a first sub-stack and a second sub-stack. The first sub-stack includes the first card type and the second sub-stack includes the second card type. The example method includes comparing a first top card of the first sub-stack to a first reference card and, based on the first top card being substantially similar to the first reference card, automatically transferring the first sub-stack to a first tray designated to receive the first card type.
problem: Automatically sorting and routing collectible cards of different types into designated trays without manual intervention.
constraint: The transfer is only triggered when the top card is 'substantly similar' to the reference card, establishing a similarity threshold that must be met before bulk transfer occurs.
mechanism: A threshold-based comparison gate evaluates a sample element against a reference element. When the sample meets a similarity threshold, a grouping of associated elements is transferred as a unit to a designated destination, leveraging the assumption that elements within the group share a common classification.
mechanism_raw: A single reference comparison of the top card of a sub-stack against a reference card triggers the automatic transfer of the entire sub-stack to a designated tray. The comparison acts as a threshold-based decision gate: when the top card is substantially similar to the reference, the whole sub-stack is routed as a unit, leveraging the assumption that cards in the same sub-stack share the same type.

abstract: The invention relates to a load-handling means for a tower or a tower section of a wind turbine, which load-handling means has tower-attachment means for attachment to an upper end or in the region of an upper end of a tower or a tower section of a wind turbine, and attachment points for attaching at least one anchoring means of a lifting gear unit. The invention also relates to a method for erecting a wind turbine, in particular an offshore wind turbine. The load-handling means according to the invention includes at least one oscillation damper, or at least one oscillation damper is attached, in particular releasably and/or exchangeably, to the load-handling means, the damping frequency of which oscillation damper lies in the region of a natural frequency of a clamped or freestanding tower or tower section without a gondola.
problem: Suppressing resonant oscillations in a wind turbine tower or tower section during erection, particularly when the tower is clamped or freestanding without a gondola attached.
constraint: The damping frequency must be specifically tuned to the natural frequency of the tower in its clamped or freestanding state (without a gondola), which is a different modal condition than the fully assembled turbine.
mechanism: A frequency-tuned damping element is configured to operate in the region of the natural frequency of a structure in a specific modal state. By matching the damping frequency to the structure's natural frequency, resonant energy is absorbed and dissipated rather than amplified, stabilizing the structure during dynamic operations.
mechanism_raw: An oscillation damper is tuned so that its damping frequency lies in the region of the natural frequency of the clamped or freestanding tower. By matching the damper's frequency to the structure's natural frequency, resonant energy is absorbed and dissipated rather than amplified, stabilizing the tower during lifting and positioning operations.
residual_terms: ["natural frequency", "damping frequency", "resonant oscillations", "clamped or freestanding state"]

abstract: The present application relates to perfume compositions, delivery systems comprising such perfumes products comprising such perfumes and/or delivery systems, and processes for making and using same. Such perfumes and delivery systems provide improved perfume performance under high soil conditions and in cold water washing and a shell that at least partially surrounds said core.
problem: Maintaining perfume performance and controlled release under adverse washing conditions such as high soil load and cold water.
constraint: The shell must at least partially surround the core to provide adequate protection and controlled release, balancing barrier integrity with permeability for intended release.
mechanism: A protective shell at least partially surrounds an active core, creating an encapsulated delivery system. The shell acts as a selective barrier that shields the core from premature degradation or washout under harsh conditions, while allowing controlled release of the core's contents when desired conditions are met.
mechanism_raw: A shell at least partially surrounds a perfume core, creating an encapsulated delivery system. The shell acts as a protective barrier that shields the core from premature degradation or washout under harsh conditions (high soil, cold water), while allowing controlled release of the perfume when desired conditions are met.

abstract: A method of stimulating a subterranean formation. The method begins with positioning a stimulation tool into a wellbore formed through the formation. The stimulation tool includes (i) at least one tubular segment; (ii) an outer sleeve positioned on the tubular segment and forming an annular space between the tubular segment and the outer sleeve; (iii) a propellant positioned within the annular space; (iv) at least one ignitor positioned to ignite the propellant; (v) at least one rupture disc positioned within a wall of the tubular segment; and (vi) the absence of a detonator for detonating the propellant. Thereafter, the propellant is ignited to begin deflagration of the propellant.
problem: Stimulating a subterranean formation using controlled energy release without requiring a detonator for explosive initiation.
constraint: The system operates without a detonator, relying solely on deflagration initiated by an ignitor, which constrains the energy release profile to sub-explosive combustion.
mechanism: A combustible medium is ignited to initiate controlled burning rather than explosive combustion. The resulting sub-explosive pressure buildup provides a gradual energy release profile that can stimulate a subterranean formation without requiring a detonator, using an ignitor instead of a detonating mechanism.
mechanism_raw: Propellant is ignited to begin deflagration (controlled burning) rather than detonation (explosive shock wave). Deflagration produces a slower, more controlled pressure buildup that can stimulate the formation while avoiding the need for a detonator, using an ignitor instead of a detonating mechanism.

abstract: A foldable velocipede for ease of stowage includes a bicycle that comprises a frame. The frame has a top tube and a down tube. The top tube and the down tube each comprise a front section and a rear section. Each of a pair of rotators is coupled to and extends between a respective front section and an associated rear section. The rotators are selectively positionable in extended configurations, wherein each front section extends linearly from an associated rear section and the bicycle is configured for riding. The top tube and the down tube also are selectively positionable in folded configurations, wherein each front section is positioned substantially adjacent to an associated rear section and the bicycle is configured for stowage. The improvement is the pair of rotators that is positioned singly in the top tube and the down tube such that the bicycle is reversibly foldable.
problem: Making a bicycle reversibly foldable for stowage while maintaining structural integrity and rideability in the unfolded state.
constraint: The rotators must be selectively positionable in both extended (linear, rideable) and folded (adjacent, stowed) configurations, requiring a dual-state locking mechanism that maintains rigidity in the extended position.
mechanism: Rotational coupling elements are positioned within structural members, each coupled between a front section and a rear section. These couplings allow the sections to rotate relative to each other, enabling the members to fold into a stowed configuration where sections are positioned adjacent to each other, and to extend linearly for use. A dual-state locking mechanism selectively maintains rigidity in the extended position.
mechanism_raw: Rotators are positioned singly within the top tube and down tube, each coupled between a front section and a rear section. These rotators allow the front and rear sections to rotate relative to each other, enabling the tubes to fold into a stowed configuration where sections are positioned adjacent to each other, and to extend linearly for riding.
residual_terms: ["rotators", "top tube", "down tube", "dual-state locking mechanism", "extended configuration", "folded configuration"]

abstract: There is provided a silicon single crystal producing method in producing a silicon single crystal by the Czochralski method using a pulling apparatus including a heat shield, wherein an oxygen concentration in the crystal is controlled through the adjustment of a flow velocity of inert gas introduced into the apparatus at the gap portion between an exterior surface of the single crystal and a lower-end opening edge of the heat shield, in accordance with a gap-to-crystal-diameter ratio (“the area of the gap portion”/“the area of a cross-sectional of the single crystal”). By this producing method, it is possible to appropriately control the oxygen concentration in the pulled single crystal.
problem: Controlling oxygen concentration in a silicon single crystal during Czochralski growth to ensure material quality.
constraint: Balancing gas flow rate to maintain the gap-to-crystal-diameter ratio without disrupting crystal growth dynamics or introducing turbulence.
mechanism: Modulating a process fluid flow rate in response to a geometric ratio between a gap and a target cross-sectional area, establishing a feedback loop that adjusts material incorporation into a growing structure by balancing flow dynamics against growth stability.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting inert gas flow velocity at the gap between the crystal and heat shield based on the ratio of gap area to crystal cross-sectional area, creating a feedback loop that modulates oxygen incorporation into the crystal.
residual_terms: ["feedback loop", "geometric ratio", "process fluid flow rate", "material incorporation"]

abstract: A bearing arrangement for a door, in particular for refrigerators or freezers, comprises a bearing pin for rotatably bearing the door, a closing device by means of which the door can be moved over a certain pivoting region in the closing direction through the force of a force accumulator, and a damper for damping a pivoting movement of the door over at least one pivoting region, and the closing device and the damper are oriented in a substantially perpendicular plane with respect to the axis of rotation of the bearing pin, wherein, to move the closing device, a first curved guide which can be moved by the bearing pin is provided and, to move the damper, a second curved guide which can be moved by the bearing pin is provided. As a result, the bearing arrangement can have a particularly compact design, the bearing arrangement being used in particular in a refrigerator or freezer.
problem: Achieving a compact door bearing arrangement for refrigerators/freezers while maintaining controlled closing and damping motions.
constraint: Ensuring the perpendicular orientation of components does not compromise the force transmission or damping effectiveness within the limited spatial envelope.
mechanism: Translating a single rotational input into two independent linear actuations in orthogonal directions via curved guide surfaces, enabling compact spatial arrangement while preserving force transmission and damping control.
mechanism_raw: Using two curved guides driven by a single bearing pin to independently translate rotational motion into linear actuation of a closing device and damper in perpendicular planes, enabling spatial efficiency.

abstract: A sealing element for positioning radially outwardly of aerofoil blades of a gas turbine engine is provided. A radially inner surface region of the sealing element includes a seal structure having one or more inwardly projecting walls formed by additive layer, powder fed, laser weld deposition. The walls form a plurality of curved profile shapes which are arranged in a repeating pattern across the radially inner surface region. None of the walls intersects with any other wall. The curved profile shapes have no radii of curvature less than 0.5 mm.
problem: Creating a durable, high-temperature sealing element for gas turbine blades that maintains structural integrity under stress.
constraint: Maintaining a minimum radius of curvature (0.5 mm) to prevent stress concentrations while preserving the repeating pattern's structural and sealing benefits.
mechanism: Distributing localized stress through a repeating pattern of non-intersecting curved profiles formed by layer-wise material deposition, maintaining structural integrity and sealing performance under cyclic loading without stress concentration points.
mechanism_raw: Forming non-intersecting curved profile walls in a repeating pattern via additive laser deposition, distributing stress and providing sealing without localized failure points.
residual_terms: ["repeating pattern", "non-intersecting curved profiles", "layer-wise material deposition", "stress concentration points"]

abstract: A scroll conveyor tile protection or any other material subject to wear with a weldable support and a wear resistant insert, not necessary weldable. The support is fit with a flat surface and shoulder allowing for precise positioning of tile on a scroll flight to be protected. At least one opening, preferably at its center, allows for insertion and assembly of a complementary shaped insert. The unit setting up on the scroll flight and the contact between the flight faces and the unit faces allows for creating a dove tail locking system. Welding of the support permanently insures locking of the system and insert being maintained without being otherwise fixed beyond this mechanical clamping.
problem: Protecting scroll conveyor tiles from wear while enabling secure, replaceable attachment of wear-resistant inserts.
constraint: Ensuring the mechanical clamping alone provides sufficient retention during operation while welding avoids distortion of the support or insert materials.
mechanism: Securing an insert to a support surface using complementary mechanical interlocks that provide primary retention, augmented by a permanent bonding process to prevent disengagement during operation without additional fasteners.
mechanism_raw: Using a dove tail locking system formed by complementary mechanical clamping between the support and conveyor flight faces, reinforced by welding to permanently secure the insert without additional fasteners.

abstract: A drive system for rotating one or more wheels of an aircraft landing gear for ground taxiing and/or spin-up prior to landing has a motor operable to rotate a first drive pinion via a first drive path, and a driven gear adapted to be fixed to the wheel. The drive system has a first configuration in which the first drive pinion meshes with the driven gear to permit the motor to drive the driven gear via the first drive path. One of the first drive pinion and the driven gear comprises a first sprocket and the other comprises a series of rollers arranged in two or more rows, each row of rollers being arranged to form a ring. The rollers are rotatable about pins fixed to an annular support member, and adjacent rows may be out of phase by a fraction of roller pitch.
problem: Rotating aircraft landing gear wheels smoothly during ground taxiing or pre-landing spin-up without slippage or uneven torque transfer.
constraint: Balancing phase differences between roller rows to maintain smooth engagement while avoiding excessive wear or misalignment under variable torque conditions.
mechanism: Phasing adjacent rows of engaging elements by a fractional offset of their pitch to ensure continuous load transfer across a drive path, minimizing torque ripple and uneven engagement under variable operational conditions.
mechanism_raw: Employing a sprocket and roller-row system with adjacent rows phased by a fraction of roller pitch, ensuring continuous engagement and load distribution across the drive path.

abstract: A disclosed control system and method of controlling a gas turbine engine utilizes a thrust rating schedule generated from airframe selected requirements. The system utilizes a generic logic structure for ratings combined with simple selection logic to customize rating schedules for multiple airframe customers. The use of a common generic logic structure to generate rating schedules for different airframe manufacturers reduces software design effort, memory consumption, and processor throughput requirements.
problem: Customizing control systems for multiple airframe customers without excessive software design effort, memory use, or processor overhead.
constraint: Balancing customization flexibility with reduced software complexity, memory consumption, and processor throughput demands.
mechanism: A generic logic framework generates standardized operational sequences, combined with adaptive selection logic that maps the generic framework to specific customer-defined parameters, enabling core logic reuse while accommodating customization through parameter-driven configuration.
mechanism_raw: A generic logic structure generates rating schedules, combined with simple selection logic to adapt the generic structure to specific customer requirements, enabling reuse of core logic while allowing customization.

abstract: According to an aspect of the invention, a binding device includes a first rotary member including a first serrated portion on its circumferential surface, a second rotary member including, on its circumferential surface, a second serrated portion to be engaged with the first serrated portion at an engaging position and configured to perform a binding process by rotating together with the first rotary member with a bundle of sheets pinched therebetween to form serrations in the sheet bundle in thickness direction and bring the sheets into engagement with each other while relatively moving the sheet bundle in a predetermined moving direction, and a clamping unit configured to, when the binding process is performed, clamp the sheet bundle at a clamping position upstream of the engaging position to apply a predetermined pulling force acting in a direction opposite to the moving direction to the sheet bundle.
problem: Binding a bundle of sheets into a cohesive unit with serrations while maintaining consistent engagement between sheets.
constraint: Coordinating the clamping force direction and timing with the serration-forming rotation to avoid slippage or misalignment.
mechanism: Two cooperating rotary elements with complementary surface features engage a flexible sheet bundle to form mechanical interlocks, while a tensioning mechanism applies a pulling force upstream of the engagement zone to maintain sheet alignment and ensure interlock formation during the binding process.
mechanism_raw: Two serrated rotary members rotate together to form serrations in the sheet bundle, while a clamping unit applies a pulling force upstream to maintain tension and ensure the sheets engage during the binding process.

abstract: A cable 1 comprises a first thimble 2 and a second thimble 4, at least one yarn 6, and at least a first conductive fiber 8 for monitoring the cable 1. The yarn 6 extends from the first thimble 2 to the second thimble 4, turns around the second thimble 4, extends from the second thimble 4 to the first thimble 2, and turns around the first thimble 2. Each thimble holds a stack 9 of layers 10 of turns of the yarn 6. The first conductive fiber 8 is designed to signal the wear of the yarn 6 by breaking after a predetermined portion of the turns of the yarn 6 breaks. The first conductive fiber 8 is positioned at the first thimble 2 between the turns of the yarn 6 at less than 50% of the stack height h.
problem: Monitoring wear progression in a cable's yarn bundle to signal when maintenance or replacement is needed.
constraint: Positioning the conductive fiber within the stack such that its failure accurately reflects the cumulative wear of the yarn turns without premature or delayed signaling.
mechanism: A conductive sensing element is positioned within a layered component stack at a location where cumulative degradation of adjacent layers causes the element to fail after a predetermined number of component failures, providing a threshold-based early warning signal for maintenance.
mechanism_raw: A conductive fiber is embedded within the thimble stack at a position where it breaks after a predetermined number of yarn turns fail, providing an early warning signal for wear.

abstract: Specification covers new algorithms, methods, and systems for artificial intelligence, soft computing, and deep learning/recognition, e.g., image recognition (e.g., for action, gesture, emotion, expression, biometrics, fingerprint, facial, OCR (text), background, relationship, position, pattern, and object), Big Data analytics, machine learning, training schemes, crowd-sourcing (experts), feature space, clustering, classification, SVM, similarity measures, modified Boltzmann Machines, optimization, search engine, ranking, question-answering system, soft (fuzzy or unsharp) boundaries/impreciseness/ambiguities/fuzziness in language, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computing-with-Words (CWW), parsing, machine translation, sound and speech recognition, video search and analysis (e.g. tracking), image annotation, geometrical abstraction, image correction, semantic web, context analysis, data reliability, Z-number, Z-Web, Z-factor, rules engine, control system, autonomous vehicle, self-diagnosis and self-repair robots, system diagnosis, medical diagnosis, biomedicine, data mining, event prediction, financial forecasting, economics, risk assessment, e-mail management, database management, indexing and join operation, memory management, data compression, event-centric social network, Image Ad Network.
reason: The abstract lists a broad range of AI and machine learning technologies without describing a specific causal mechanism or problem-solving principle. It reads as a collection of features rather than an underlying functional relationship.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to a system for recovering multiple kinds of ions, which includes: an ion adsorption tank that includes a plurality of adsorption channels arranged in parallel and including a first electrode unit electrically adsorbing only negative ions and a second electrode unit having an adsorbent layer for adsorbing positive ions to be recovered from positive ions, in which electricity is independently supplied to the adsorption channels; a water tank that keeps liquid discharged from the ion adsorption tank; a pump that circulates mother liquor or liquid stored in the water tank; and an ion recovering tank that keeps liquid containing positive ions to be recovered. According to the present disclosure, a series of processes make it possible to continuously recover ions to be recovered, so the operation efficiency of the system can be maximized.
problem: Continuously recovering multiple kinds of ions from a solution with high operational efficiency.
constraint: Maintaining independent control of each channel's electrical supply to ensure consistent ion adsorption while allowing other channels to undergo regeneration or recovery phases.
mechanism: Multiple parallel processing channels with independently controllable energy delivery systems enable simultaneous active-phase operations in some channels while others undergo recovery-phase operations, maintaining continuous throughput through asynchronous phase management.
mechanism_raw: Parallel adsorption channels with independent electrical supply allow simultaneous adsorption and desorption processes, enabling continuous ion recovery without interrupting the overall system operation.

abstract: The shaped composites of the present disclosure have metal powder bonded with glass powder. This feature provides the advantages of metal, metal powder, or glass composite materials, without suffering from the disadvantages. The composite is prepared with simple sintering methods, and can easily be formed into any number of desired shapes with dimensional characteristics and ingredients suited to a particular application.
problem: Combining the beneficial properties of metal and glass materials without inheriting their respective disadvantages (e.g., brittleness of glass, corrosion of metal).
constraint: The sintering process must be simple and compatible with forming complex shapes while maintaining dimensional stability and material homogeneity.
mechanism: Combining two materials with complementary properties by integrating their particulate forms into a composite structure, then using a thermal bonding process to consolidate the composite into a desired shape while preserving material homogeneity and dimensional accuracy.
mechanism_raw: Bonding metal powder with glass powder in a composite structure, then using sintering to form the composite into desired shapes. The composite leverages the strengths of both materials while mitigating their weaknesses through controlled material integration.

abstract: A capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer (CMUT) having at least two deflectable membranes. The membranes are spaced from each other, and the membranes contribute to and/or are responsive to receive or transmit an ultrasonic signal. Spacing between the at least two deflectable membranes is adjustable through application of a voltage to cause deflection of at least one of the deflectable membranes, to affect the receive/transmit properties of the CMUT.
problem: Tuning the receive/transmit properties of a capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducer (CMUT) to adapt to varying operational requirements.
constraint: The voltage-induced deflection must precisely control membrane spacing without causing mechanical failure or hysteresis in the system.
mechanism: Adjusting the spacing between two flexible elements via an applied voltage to modulate electrostatic and mechanical resonance characteristics, thereby tuning operational parameters of a transducer without inducing mechanical failure or hysteresis.
mechanism_raw: Adjusting the spacing between two deflectable membranes via applied voltage, which alters the electrostatic interaction and mechanical resonance of the transducer, thereby modulating its ultrasonic signal properties.

abstract: Various dental devices are available for cleaning the mouth, gums and teeth. However, these dental devices may also cause abrasions to the mouth and/or gums.
