Dental devices may comprise a reservoir for storing a liquid and for application of the liquid to the mouth, teeth and/or gums. The liquid may be an antibacterial liquid, such as a hydrogen peroxide solution, a salt solution or a teeth whitening solution or gel, for example. An antibacterial liquid may be applied to prevent infection of the abrasions. The reservoir may be in a hollow handle of the dental device, such that the liquid may be easily pumped or moved from the reservoir to an outlet at the functional end that may cause the abrasions.
problem: Preventing infections caused by abrasions to the mouth, gums, or teeth during dental cleaning procedures.
constraint: The reservoir and delivery system must be positioned to allow easy pumping while maintaining the structural integrity of the device and avoiding additional abrasion.
mechanism: Integrating a storage chamber within a handheld device to retain and dispense a therapeutic agent directly to a localized injury site via a fluid delivery mechanism, ensuring targeted treatment without compromising device integrity.
mechanism_raw: Integrating a reservoir within the dental device handle to store and deliver an antibacterial liquid (e.g., hydrogen peroxide) directly to the site of abrasion via a pump mechanism, ensuring localized treatment.

abstract: A pneumatic chip collector includes a free-floating head with a connector configured to be coupled to a pneumatic system. The head has a bottom with at least one slot disposed on the bottom of the head, the at least one slot parallel to the longitudinal axis of the head. The head also has at least one spacer disposed beyond the bottom of the head, the at least one spacer having a outermost surface defining a spacing relative to the bottom of the head with the outermost surface disposed on a surface.
problem: Efficiently collecting chips or debris from a surface without causing damage to the surface or requiring manual adjustment of the collector.
constraint: The head must remain free-floating to adapt to surface irregularities while the spacers maintain a precise gap to avoid damage and ensure effective suction.
mechanism: Employing a movable collection head with spacing elements to maintain a controlled gap relative to a surface, enabling debris entrainment via airflow while preventing direct contact and surface damage.
mechanism_raw: Using a free-floating head with slots and spacers to maintain a controlled distance from the surface. The spacers ensure consistent spacing while allowing the head to move freely, enabling airflow and chip collection without surface contact.

abstract: The present invention generally relates to methods for removing an organic deposit or for inhibiting deposition of deposit-forming comprising contacting a cleaning composition or an anti-coking composition with a surface. The surface can have an organic deposit or be susceptible to forming an organic deposit and the surface can be in contact with a liquid containing organics. The liquid can be produced from a thermal recovery system, and the surface can be an internal surface of a piece of steam-generating or vapor-generating equipment.
problem: Removing or inhibiting the formation of organic deposits (e.g., coking) on internal surfaces of steam- or vapor-generating equipment exposed to organic liquids.
constraint: The composition must remain effective in high-temperature, high-pressure environments typical of steam-generating systems while being compatible with the equipment materials.
mechanism: Contacting a surface with a reactive composition that chemically interacts with organic deposits to dissolve or inhibit their adhesion, maintaining effectiveness under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions.
mechanism_raw: Contacting the surface with a cleaning or anti-coking composition that chemically interacts with the organic deposits to dissolve or prevent their adhesion, leveraging reactive or solvating agents in the composition.

abstract: The invention discloses a rubber process oil and a process for manufacturing rubber process oils which are non-carcinogenic in nature. The process comprises of selectively producing Hildebrand solubility components enriched vacuum residue by selective distillation of reduced crude oil (RCO) to obtain minimum of 10 vol % boiling components in the range 490° C. to 50° C., which leads to higher solubility of rubber process oil with an aniline point of less than 70° C. and with extremely low concentration of selective polycyclic aromatics which makes the 15 product non-carcinogenic. The process comprises of selectively enriching higher Hildebrand solubility components in vacuum residue by vacuum distillation of reduced crude oil (RCO), then subjecting the enriched vacuum residue to solvent deasphalting process and subjecting the deasphalted oil to aromatic extraction process and then blending the enriched aromatic extract with Heavy Alkyl 20 Benzene (HAB) or Solvent processed base oil or hydroprocessed base oil or mixture thereof. The rubber process oils manufactured by the invented process have a polycyclic aromatics (PCA) content of less than 10 ppm, specifically benzo(a)pyrene content of less than 1 ppm. They have aniline point less than 70° C. but have high kinematic viscosity of 25 to 75 cSt at 100° C., pour point of 27° C. or less and a flash point minimum of 250° C. or more.
problem: Creating non-carcinogenic rubber process oils that simultaneously achieve low aniline point (high solvency), high kinematic viscosity, low pour point, and high flash point while eliminating harmful polycyclic aromatics.
constraint: Balancing the removal of carcinogenic polycyclic aromatics (PCA < 10 ppm, benzo(a)pyrene < 1 ppm) against maintaining low aniline point (< 70°C) and high viscosity (25-75 cSt), since aggressive purification reduces solvency and viscosity properties that are essential for rubber processing applications.
mechanism: Applying solubility-parameter-based fractionation to selectively retain components with desired solvency and viscosity characteristics while removing low-molecular-weight and harmful aromatic fractions, followed by targeted extraction stages that strip specific contaminant classes, and finally reintroducing functional property modifiers to restore performance characteristics lost during purification.
mechanism_raw: Using selective distillation based on Hildebrand solubility parameters to enrich desired solubility components in vacuum residue while removing low-boiling fractions, followed by sequential solvent deasphalting and aromatic extraction to strip out carcinogenic polycyclic aromatics, then blending the purified aromatic extract with specific base oils to restore functional properties. The selective distillation acts as a solubility-based fractionation that preserves rubber-soluble components while the downstream extraction stages remove the targeted harmful compounds.
residual_terms: ["Hildebrand solubility parameters", "aniline point", "kinematic viscosity", "pour point", "flash point", "polycyclic aromatics", "vacuum residue", "solvent deasphalting", "aromatic extraction", "base oils"]

abstract: A system and method for operating an automated aerial vehicle are provided wherein influences of ground effects (e.g., which may increase the effective thrusts of propellers by interfering with the respective airflows) are utilized for sensing the ground or other surfaces. In various implementations, operating parameters of the automated aerial vehicle are monitored to determine when ground effects are influencing the parameters associated with each of the propellers, which correspondingly indicate proximities to a surface (e.g., the ground). Utilizing such techniques, different propellers of an automated aerial vehicle may provide different sensing data (e.g., for detecting issues with an uneven landing area, a sloped ground, determining an automated aerial vehicle's location based on a unique ground surface profile, etc.)
problem: Sensing ground proximity and surface characteristics for an automated aerial vehicle without adding dedicated sensing hardware or external infrastructure.
constraint: Using only existing propulsion system telemetry as sensing input without additional sensors, while distinguishing ground effect signatures from other aerodynamic disturbances and accounting for the fact that ground effect strength varies non-linearly with height, surface texture, and propeller geometry.
mechanism: Monitoring real-time operational parameters of distributed propulsion units to detect aerodynamic perturbations caused by ground effect interference, then correlating differential response patterns across multiple spatially-separated units to infer surface proximity, texture, and topographical characteristics without dedicated sensing hardware.
mechanism_raw: Monitoring real-time operating parameters of each propeller (e.g., thrust, torque, RPM) to detect perturbations caused by ground effect interference with propeller airflow. When ground effects alter the aerodynamic loading on individual propellers, the resulting parameter deviations are correlated to surface proximity and characteristics. By comparing differential responses across multiple propellers, the system infers surface profile, slope, and unevenness from the spatial pattern of ground effect signatures.

abstract: The apparatus for water treatment using in-situ activation of a manganese dioxide catalyst includes: a reaction bath configured to give a space where aqueous organic contaminants are removed by means of reaction with permanganate (MnO4−) generated by electrochemical oxidation of manganese oxide (MnO2); a plurality of manganese dioxide catalysts provided at the reaction bath and electrochemically oxidized into permanganate (MnO4−) by a voltage applied thereto; and a power supply device configured to apply power to the manganese dioxide catalyst so that the manganese dioxide (MnO2) is electrochemically oxidized into permanganate (MnO4−).
problem: Removing aqueous organic contaminants from water using permanganate oxidation without the hazards of transporting, storing, and handling liquid permanganate at the treatment site.
constraint: Maintaining sufficient electrochemical conversion efficiency of MnO2 to MnO4− while ensuring the catalyst remains structurally stable over repeated oxidation cycles, and balancing applied voltage against energy consumption and electrode degradation rates.
mechanism: Electrochemically activating a stable solid precursor material in-situ within the reaction medium by applying a controlled electrical potential, converting it to an active oxidizing species at the point of use, whereupon the generated species reacts with and neutralizes target contaminants in the aqueous stream.
mechanism_raw: Electrochemically oxidizing solid manganese dioxide (MnO2) catalyst in-situ within the reaction bath by applying a controlled voltage, converting it directly to permanganate ions (MnO4−) at the point of use. The generated permanganate then reacts with and oxidizes organic contaminants in the aqueous stream. This eliminates the need for external permanganate delivery by activating the stable, solid precursor material only when and where it is needed.

abstract: The present invention relates to compositions and methods for generating populations of tissue precursor cells from pluripotent cells, and preferably induction of stem cells into definitive endoderm to generate anterior foregut endoderm from pluripotent cells. The anterior foregut endoderm cells can then be differentiated into an alveolar epithelial type II cell.
problem: Generating specific tissue precursor cell populations (anterior foregut endoderm and alveolar epithelial type II cells) from pluripotent stem cells in a controlled, reproducible manner.
constraint: Achieving high differentiation efficiency and purity at each stage while maintaining cell viability, since incomplete or off-target differentiation produces heterogeneous cell populations that are unsuitable for therapeutic applications, and the signaling pathways at each stage are interdependent and must be precisely timed.
mechanism: Implementing temporally-sequenced biochemical induction protocols that sequentially activate specific developmental signaling cascades, guiding pluripotent cells through a predetermined differentiation trajectory by applying stage-specific morphogenic cues that direct cells toward target lineage fates with controlled timing and pathway modulation.
mechanism_raw: Applying staged biochemical induction protocols that sequentially activate specific developmental signaling pathways: first inducing definitive endoderm formation from pluripotent cells through defined growth factor exposure, then directing those cells toward anterior foregut endoderm fate via modulation of Wnt, Nodal, and other morphogen pathways, and finally differentiating the anterior foregut endoderm into mature alveolar epithelial type II cells through further lineage-specific cues. Each stage uses temporal control of signaling inputs to guide cells through a predetermined developmental trajectory.
residual_terms: ["pluripotent stem cells", "anterior foregut endoderm", "alveolar epithelial type II cells", "definitive endoderm", "Wnt", "Nodal", "morphogen pathways", "signaling pathways", "growth factors", "differentiation efficiency", "cell viability"]

abstract: An apparatus and method is provided for generating net energy by converting the natural pressure of atmospheric air into kinetic energy, which is then converted to mechanical energy by a turbine, which can then be converted to electric energy through a generator. The method relies on natural physical phenomena such as Entrainment, Inducement and the Venturi Effect to increase the mass and velocity of air flowing through an enclosed chamber without increasing the amount of energy consumed to increase the air flow mass and velocity. A turbine-generator apparatus connected to the chamber is driven by the air flow to generate electric power which is greater than the power consumed to generate the initial air flow. Power is generated through extraction of kinetic energy from natural atmospheric air pressure energy.
problem: Amplifying natural atmospheric air pressure into usable kinetic energy flow for power generation without consuming additional energy to drive the airflow.
constraint: Achieving net energy gain (electrical output exceeding the energy consumed to initiate airflow) despite the low energy density of atmospheric pressure differentials, since the Venturi and entrainment effects must overcome system losses including friction, turbulence, and turbine inefficiencies to produce surplus power.
mechanism: Exploiting fluid dynamic pressure-differential effects within an enclosed chamber to induce ambient gas flow, where entrainment and inducement phenomena passively amplify the mass flow rate and velocity of naturally pressurized atmospheric gas, subsequently converting the amplified kinetic energy into electrical power via turbine-driven generation without external energy input for airflow generation.
mechanism_raw: Using the Venturi effect to create a pressure differential within an enclosed chamber that induces ambient air to flow through the system. Entrainment and inducement effects cause the initial airflow to draw in additional surrounding air, increasing the total mass flow rate and velocity through the chamber. This amplified airflow then drives a turbine-generator assembly, converting the kinetic energy of the naturally pressurized atmospheric air into electrical energy. The fluid dynamic effects passively multiply the energy available from the ambient pressure source.
residual_terms: ["Venturi effect", "pressure differential", "ambient air", "entrainment", "inducement", "turbine-generator", "atmospheric pressure", "kinetic energy", "friction", "turbulence", "turbine inefficiencies"]

abstract: Described is a strap pad for a shoulder strap. The strap pad includes a shoulder strap connector that is formed to wrap around and connect with the shoulder strap. Notably, a plurality of studs are affixed to and project from the shoulder strap connector. The studs are positioned to disperse the pressure and weight of the accompanying item across the muscles more evenly when the shoulder strap is positioned around the neck or shoulders of a user.
problem: Uneven pressure distribution on shoulders from a strap carrying weight
constraint: Balancing pressure dispersion effectiveness with minimal bulk and weight addition to the strap
mechanism: An array of discrete projecting elements integrated into a load-bearing connector distributes applied force across a larger surface area, converting concentrated pressure into distributed contact through spatially separated contact points
mechanism_raw: An array of studs projecting from a strap connector disperses applied load across a larger surface area of the shoulder muscles, converting concentrated pressure into distributed force

abstract: An adjustable jig for a sheet metal brake including a first arm configured to mount to the brake, and an adjustable backstop affixed on the first arm. The adjustable backstop is set at an adjustable first distance from a front face of the brake when the first arm is mounted to the brake. A first adjustable front stop can be configured to engage the first arm and retain an adjustable first front stop position relative to the first arm. A second adjustable front stop can be configured to engage the first arm and retain an adjustable second front stop position relative to the first arm. The first and second front stops are independently adjustable relative to the first arm. A sheet metal brake with an adjustable jig. A method for bending sheet metal with a sheet metal brake and an adjustable jig.
problem: Achieving precise and repeatable sheet metal bend angles with variable positioning requirements
constraint: Maintaining positional stability of each stop under bending forces while preserving independent adjustability
mechanism: Multiple independently adjustable reference points mounted on a shared structural element enable sequential or simultaneous positioning of workpiece interfaces, allowing complex geometries through controlled relative motion between adjustable stops
mechanism_raw: Independent adjustable front stops and a backstop mounted on a single arm allow sequential or simultaneous positioning of multiple reference points, enabling complex bend geometries through relative motion control

abstract: A wear pad assembly for a telescopic boom includes a wear pad having a first side for contacting an outer wall of an inner section of the boom, and a second side facing an inner wall of an outer section of the boom. At least one rigid plate is secured to the second side of the wear pad, and a stud in screw-threaded engagement with the outer section of the boom or a plate secured to the outer section of the boom is associated with each rigid plate, the end of stud and the associated rigid plate having mating formations to enable the stud to urge the first surface of the wear pad against the outer wall of the inner section while preventing the wear pad from being displaced in a plane normal to the axis of rotation of the stud.
problem: Maintaining consistent contact pressure between a wear pad and a moving inner boom section while preventing lateral displacement
constraint: Balancing applied contact pressure against wear resistance and preventing over-tightening that could damage the boom
mechanism: A threaded fastening element with mating geometric constraints converts rotational input into axial displacement, pressing a contact pad against a surface while formation geometry restricts movement perpendicular to the fastening axis
mechanism_raw: A screw-threaded stud with mating formations on a rigid plate converts rotational tightening into axial force that presses the pad against the inner wall, while the formation geometry constrains movement perpendicular to the stud axis

abstract: An electronic control device has a housing and an air breathing filter assembled to a through-hole of the housing. The air breathing filter has a filter supporting member and a filter cover member. A cylindrical portion of the filter supporting member is inserted into the through-hole from an inside space of the housing, while the filter cover member is fixed to the cylindrical portion of the filter supporting member from an outside of the housing. A pushing portion is formed in a leg portion of the filter cover member for pushing a wall of the housing in a downward direction. A water-proof sealing member is interposed between an inner wall surface of the housing and a flanged portion of the filter supporting member, so that a gap between the housing and the air breathing filter is surely sealed.
problem: Sealing an electronic housing against water ingress while maintaining air permeability for thermal management
constraint: Ensuring sufficient sealing compression without restricting airflow or damaging the filter media
mechanism: A compressible sealing member positioned between two surfaces is deformed by an actuating leg to create a compression seal, while a permeable medium integrated within the assembly allows controlled fluid flow through the sealed interface
mechanism_raw: A filter assembly with a pushing leg deforms a sealing member between the housing and filter support to create a compression seal, while the filter media itself allows controlled air flow through the sealed interface

abstract: Concepts and technologies are disclosed herein for a purlin. The purlin can include a steel structure having a pair of outer flanges flaring away from a support surface for defining outer edges of the purlin. Connected to respective inner edges of the outer flanges along bent edges can be a pair of supports. The supports can be configured to engage a support surface and define a lower surface of the purlin. Connected to respective inner edges of the supports can be a pair of support webs that extend away from the support surface.
problem: Providing structural support for loads applied to a purlin while enabling stable engagement with a support surface
constraint: Optimizing material usage and geometric angles to maximize load capacity while minimizing weight and manufacturing complexity
mechanism: Flared structural sections connected to angled load-transfer elements and internal bracing form a multi-path force distribution system, converting applied loads into tensile and compressive stresses through geometric angle optimization
mechanism_raw: Flared outer flanges connected to angled supports and webs create a load path that distributes forces across multiple contact points, with the bent edges and support geometry converting vertical loads into tensile and compressive stresses in the flanges

abstract: Provided is display panel including a substrate including a pixel area and a pad area; and a first conductive line and a second conductive line stacked on the substrate, wherein the first conductive line includes a first part disposed on the pixel area and a second part disposed on the pad area and the second conductive line includes a first part disposed on the pixel area and a second part disposed on the pad area. The first part of the first conductive line and the first part of the second conductive line are parallel to each other and the second part of the first conductive line and the second part of the second conductive line are overlapped vertically.
reason: The patent describes a static geometric layout of conductive traces (parallel in pixel area, vertically overlapped in pad area) without any dynamic causal operation that produces a useful effect. It is a structural routing arrangement rather than a functional mechanism.

abstract: A method for coalescing a disperse phase component in a primarily gas process fluid includes passing the process fluid through a structure. The structure includes an outer wall with an electrically insulating material formed on an entire inner surface of the outer wall to define an entirely insulated flow path for receiving the process fluid and the flow path is free of any portion of the structure. A plurality of planar, spaced-apart electrode plates is positioned within the entirely insulated flow path and positioned substantially parallel to one another and substantially the entirety of each of the plurality of electrode plates is coated with an insulative material. At least one insulating member disposed in a space between and spaced apart from two adjacent electrode plates. A power source is applied to the electrode plates to generate an electrical field to coalesce droplets of the disperse phase component.
problem: Coalescing dispersed droplets of a disperse phase component carried in a primarily gas process fluid so they can be separated from the gas stream.
constraint: The electrodes and entire flow path must be electrically insulated to prevent current leakage through the conductive fluid while still producing a strong enough field gradient to drive droplet migration and coalescence.
mechanism: An electric field is generated across insulated conductive elements positioned within an insulated flow channel. The field induces dispersed droplets to migrate, collide, and merge into larger droplets that can be separated from the continuous phase. Insulation of all conductive surfaces ensures the field acts on the droplets without direct current conduction through the fluid.
mechanism_raw: An electrical field is generated across multiple insulated, parallel electrode plates positioned within an entirely insulated flow path. The field induces dispersed droplets to migrate, collide, and merge (coalesce) into larger droplets that can be removed from the gas stream. The electrodes and flow path walls are fully insulated so the field acts on the droplets without direct current conduction through the fluid.

abstract: A packing system includes a conveyor configured to transport one or more containers. Two or more printers are disposed along the conveyors. The printers are configured to print printed material. Each of the printers has a tray upon which the printed material is deposited from the printer. A robotic arm is disposed proximal to the conveyor and the printers. The robotic arm has an end of arm tool configured to pick the printed material from the tray of each printer. A controller is operatively connected to the printers and the robotic arm. The controller is configured to send one or more print instructions to one or more of the printers to print the printed material. The controller is configured to instruct the robotic arm to place the printed material from the tray into the container.
problem: Efficiently collecting printed output from multiple parallel printers and placing it into containers without dedicating a separate collection mechanism to each printer.
constraint: The robotic arm must have sufficient reach to access the trays of all printers positioned along the conveyor, and the controller must synchronize print job distribution with arm availability to avoid idle time.
mechanism: A centralized coordinator distributes tasks across multiple processing units positioned along a transport path and directs a single shared manipulator to collect completed outputs from whichever unit has finished its assigned task. The coordinator tracks completion status of each unit and routes the manipulator to retrieve outputs and deposit them into containers moving along the transport path.
mechanism_raw: A centralized controller distributes print jobs across multiple printers positioned along a conveyor and coordinates a single robotic arm to collect finished print material from whichever printer tray has completed its job. The controller tracks printer completion status and directs the shared robotic arm to pick from the ready tray and place the material into the container being transported on the conveyor.

abstract: When a command for outputting a movement amount at a specific reference value is included in a command block, a numerical controller which controls a position of a control axis in synchronization with a reference value by using tabular data registers the reference value and the movement amount of the command in a shift table while associating the reference value with the movement amount. Then, when the current reference value reaches the reference value registered in the shift table, the numerical controller superposes the movement amount of the control axis that is associated with the reference value in the shift table on a distributed movement amount to the control axis, and outputs the superposed movement amount as a movement amount of the control axis.
problem: Dynamically modifying the movement amount of a controlled axis in response to reaching specific reference values during synchronized motion control.
constraint: The shift table must be pre-populated with reference-to-movement associations before the motion sequence begins, and the reference value comparison must occur in real-time during axis movement to trigger the superposition at the correct moment.
mechanism: A lookup table pre-associates specific reference values with corresponding adjustment amounts. During operation, the current reference value is compared against entries in the lookup table in real-time. When a match is detected, the associated adjustment amount is combined with the base movement command for the controlled axis, and the combined result is output as the actual movement command.
mechanism_raw: A shift table associates specific reference values with corresponding movement amounts. During operation, the current reference value is compared against registered entries in the shift table. When a match is detected, the associated movement amount is superposed (added) onto the base distributed movement amount for the control axis, and the combined result is output as the actual movement command.

abstract: An electronic device includes a pressing member having plural protruding pressing parts, a first opening-formed member having plural first openings into which the plural pressing parts are inserted so as to individually protrude, a second opening-formed member having plural second openings into which the plural pressing parts are inserted so as to individually protrude, and a positioning member positioning the pressing member, first opening-formed member, and second opening-formed member so that the plural pressing parts are disposed at positions where the plural pressing parts are inserted in the plural first openings and plural second openings.
problem: Precisely positioning multiple components relative to one another so that protruding pressing parts align correctly with openings in two separate opening-formed members.
constraint: The protruding pressing parts must be long enough to pass through and engage openings in both opening-formed members simultaneously, and the positioning member must constrain all three components with sufficient precision to maintain alignment under operating conditions.
mechanism: A common reference fixture simultaneously aligns a pressing component (with protruding engagement features) and two opening-bearing components (each with corresponding openings) so that each protrusion passes through the matching opening in both opening-bearing components. The fixture establishes a fixed spatial relationship among all three components, ensuring the protrusions are positioned at the intersection of the two opening patterns.
mechanism_raw: A positioning member simultaneously aligns a pressing member (with protruding pressing parts) and two opening-formed members (each with openings) so that each pressing part passes through the corresponding opening in both opening-formed members. The positioning member establishes a common reference frame that fixes the relative positions of all three components, ensuring the protrusions are correctly located at the intersection of the two opening patterns.

abstract: The invention concerns a bubble collector guide for use in an electrolysis process, which comprises a plurality of guide members arranged at a distance from each other, the guide members comprising a lower side. The guide members can be arranged horizontally on the vertical surface of an electrode so that the lower side of the guide member forms a downwards facing surface that is substantially orthogonal to the vertical surface of the electrode, so as to collect bubbles of gas generated at the electrode.
problem: Efficiently collecting gas bubbles generated at an electrode during electrolysis without disrupting the electrode structure.
constraint: Balancing bubble collection efficiency with the spacing and orientation of guide members to avoid obstructing electrode function or structural integrity.
mechanism: A structured pathway system with directional surfaces arranged relative to a reaction interface to guide and collect generated gas phases while preserving structural integrity of the interface.
mechanism_raw: Geometric arrangement of guide members with downward-facing surfaces orthogonal to the electrode, creating a controlled path for bubbles to be directed and collected while maintaining structural spacing.

abstract: A media binder has an inner assembly and a case assembly, The inner assembly includes inside boards pre-attached to a binding mechanism. Adhesive is placed on outward surfaces of the inside boards. The case assembly includes a cover sheet with at least one marginal edge attached to surface boards and at least one loose edge. To customize cover, a printed cover is inserted in-between the cover sheet and the surface board through an opening formed by the loose edge. The case assembly is then laminated. The laminated case assembly is combined with the inner assembly using the adhesive on the inside boards. A one-piece media binder has cover sheets wrapping around surface boards forming pockets. The surface boards are partially attached to paste downs. To customize cover, printed covers are inserted into the pockets, and the paste downs are then attached to the surface boards to seal loose edges.
problem: Customizing the appearance of a media binder's cover without permanent attachment or complex mechanical adjustments.
constraint: Ensuring the insertion and sealing process maintains structural integrity while allowing flexibility for cover customization.
mechanism: A layered insertion and fixation system where a customizable element is positioned between existing layers and then permanently bonded to retain its configuration without mechanical fastening.
mechanism_raw: Using a loose edge or pocket system to insert printed covers between layers, followed by lamination or sealing to fix the cover in place after customization.

abstract: Example computer-implemented methods, apparatuses, and systems are described for implementing split range control using Proportional-Integral (PI) control on a process. In some aspects, a feedback signal from the process is received. A proportional control is performed on the feedback signal to generate a first control output while an integral control is performed on the feedback signal to generate a second control output. A first valve of the process is controlled based on the first control output while a second valve of the process is controlled based on the second control output. The second valve has a valve diameter larger than a valve diameter of the first valve.
problem: Controlling a process with split range requirements where different control actions (proportional and integral) need to be applied to separate actuators.
constraint: Matching valve sizes to the proportional and integral control outputs to ensure smooth and stable process regulation across the entire range.
mechanism: A dual-channel feedback control system that partitions control signals into distinct response components, each actuating a separate mechanism sized to handle specific portions of the operational range.
mechanism_raw: Splitting feedback control into proportional and integral components, each driving a valve of different diameter to handle distinct portions of the control range.

abstract: A rotary cutter system for cutting a web of material being feed into the rotary cutter at a press speed that includes a cutting cylinder, an anvil cylinder and a servo motor. The rotary cutter includes a controller that controls the speed of rotations of the cylinders. Control of the speed of cutting and anvil cylinders allows for the adjustment of the cut length of the material without having to adjust the position of knives in the cutting cylinder.
problem: Adjusting the cut length of a web material without mechanically repositioning cutting blades.
constraint: Maintaining precise synchronization between cylinder speeds to ensure accurate cut lengths without introducing mechanical wear or misalignment.
mechanism: A synchronized speed modulation system that dynamically adjusts the relative rotational velocities of two cooperating surfaces to control material processing without mechanical repositioning.
mechanism_raw: Controlling the rotational speeds of the cutting and anvil cylinders via a servo motor to dynamically adjust the material feed rate relative to the cutting action.

abstract: The present invention relates to a new benzodiazepine derivative, pharmaceutically acceptable salt thereof, preparation method therefor, and use thereof. The benzodiazepine derivative and the pharmaceutically acceptable salt thereof of the present invention have obvious anesthetic effect and low toxicity in body, thereby enhancing the medication safety. The benzodiazepine derivative and the pharmaceutically acceptable salt thereof of the present invention have sedative, hypnotic, and anesthetic effect, and can be used as sedative, hypnotic, and anesthetic drugs.
problem: Developing a benzodiazepine-based drug with reduced toxicity while retaining anesthetic, sedative, or hypnotic effects.
constraint: Balancing the trade-off between therapeutic efficacy and toxicity by selecting structural modifications that enhance desired effects without introducing harmful side reactions.
mechanism: A molecular optimization framework that modifies chemical structure through targeted substitutions to enhance desired biological activity while suppressing adverse interactions.
mechanism_raw: Modifying the molecular structure of benzodiazepine derivatives to optimize pharmacological activity and minimize adverse effects through targeted chemical substitutions.

abstract: A golf shoe has an upper, a midsole, and an outsole. The outsole includes a plurality of wave-like flex channels, surrounded by a hard base material. The hard base material provides stiffness for support and stability while the flex channels allow the outsole to bend when a user walks or swings a golf club. The outsole also has a plurality of receptacles for attaching and removing cleats, providing traction between the golf shoe and a ground surface.
problem: A golf shoe outsole must simultaneously provide structural stiffness for support and stability during a golf swing while also allowing controlled flexibility for natural walking motion and club swinging.
constraint: The flex channels must be positioned and shaped so that they allow sufficient bending for natural motion without compromising the stiffness needed for support and stability during a golf swing, balancing flexibility against structural integrity.
mechanism: A composite structure integrates stiff regions and compliant regions arranged in a spatially distributed pattern. The stiff regions maintain structural rigidity where support and stability are required, while the compliant regions act as localized flexible hinges that permit controlled bending deformation when external forces are applied. The compliant regions are geometrically configured to distribute stress and enable directional flexibility, thereby balancing overall structural integrity against localized compliance.
mechanism_raw: The outsole incorporates wave-like flex channels surrounded by a hard base material. The hard base material maintains stiffness in the regions that need support and stability, while the flex channels act as localized compliant hinges that allow the outsole to bend in a controlled manner when the user walks or swings a golf club. The wave-like geometry of the channels distributes bending stresses and enables directional flexibility.
residual_terms: ["compliant regions", "stiff regions", "localized flexible hinges", "directional flexibility", "stress distribution"]
